Article.Title: A spectral framework for revealing the hidden low-dimensional structure in stochastic reaction networks
Article.Authors: Gupta A.; Khammash M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stochastic reaction networks govern noise-driven dynamics in systems ranging from gene regulation to cellular signalling and population processes. Yet their high dimensionality and sensitivity to initial states obscure transient mechanisms and limit reliable inference from experimental data. Here, we show that stochastic reaction networks in biological systems often exhibit dominant low-dimensional spectral structure that shapes their dynamics. We develop a spectral framework based on the stochastic Koopman operator that identifies these dominant dynamical modes directly from simulated trajectories, yielding reduced representations with computable error bounds. This reduction enables accurate analytical descriptions of the time evolution of moments, parameter sensitivities, and cross-spectral densities, while achieving order-of-magnitude computational gains relative to standard simulation-based methods. Applied to synthetic gene circuits, our framework reveals the spectral organisation of stochastic oscillators, enables systematic comparison of competing intracellular controllers, and facilitates inference of initial-state distributions from single-cell snapshot population data collected over time. Together, these results establish a principled spectral description of stochastic reaction dynamics and provide a foundation for analysing and inferring high-dimensional noise-driven biological systems.

Here we combine tidy data principles and embedded domain knowledge to develop a unified R programming framework for glyco-omics interpretation, called glycoverse. Glycoverse incorporates a modular ecosystem of interoperable R packages and a structure-aware computational core. This core model integrates robust statistics, glycan topology, and biosynthetic logic to programmatically parse, quantify, and visualize site-specific glycoforms from heterogeneous mass spectrometry data. Supporting both glycomics and glycoproteomics, glycoverse reduces analysis time and mechanistically interprets complex datasets to reveal structural insights inaccessible to conventional pipelines. Demonstrated by a liver disease glycomics dataset, glycoverse expands our understanding of glycosylation biosynthetic flux dysregulation in liver disease and reveals reduced activity of B4GalT and ST3/6 Gal enzymes in liver diseases. Article.Abstract: Abstract Given the large size of neurons, local maintenance of mitochondria is crucial to counteract insults to this organelle in axons and dendrites. Using live-cell imaging, we trace local PINK1 translation sites and preprotein dynamics, revealing a concerted interplay between mitochondria and the ER, with endolysosomes frequently localized adjacent to the site of translation. Upon metabolically regulated untethering from mitochondria, Pink1 mRNA relocates to ribosomes in proximity to the ER and endolysosomes for translation of the PINK1 preprotein. The ER chaperone DNAJB6 shields the PINK1 preprotein in transit to mitochondria, following the post-translational ER-SURF pathway. Consequently, loss of DNAJB6 leads to persistent ER/endolysosome-associated PINK1 precursor stores and failure of mitophagy upon mitochondrial damage. Article.Title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
Article.Authors: Jiang S.; Zhou X.; Zhan R.; Zhao J.; Li Z.; Shen Y.; Smol J.; Guo Z.
Article.Abstract: Whether the recent poleward migration of tropical cyclones (TCs) reflects anthropogenic warming or natural variability remains unresolved. This contrasting behavior indicates that internal variability can drive opposing migration responses across basins under quasi‑equilibrium conditions. In contrast, recent decades show a synchronous poleward shift in both basins. We suggest that the modern basin-wide coherence reflects increasingly dominant anthropogenic forcing that overwhelms natural, regionally specific feedbacks. Our results provide a new benchmark for attributing observed TC migration and constraining future projections of TC risk.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Achieving sub-cellular resolution in ambient, matrix-free mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because reducing the sampling area often compromises ion yield and image fidelity. Article.Abstract: Two-dimensional materials hold immense potential for memristive devices, offering a pathway to overcome the von Neumann bottleneck. We transform the conventional, densely cross-linked Si–O ring network into a low cross-linking structure containing high-density nanopores ( < 3 nm). Moreover, aerogels fabricated from these fibers synergize super-high elasticity with ultra-low thermal conductivity, showing superb extreme thermal protection property. Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Khuntia A.; Nandicoori V.; Mehra S.
Article.Abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

Article.Title: Atom-level pinning effect reinforced electrooxidative coupling of anilines into azos
Article.Authors: Wu M.; Wang K.; Zhang L.; Li H.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Electrosynthesis of azo compounds via aniline oxidation represents a sustainable alternative to conventional methods, yet its efficiency is largely limited by sequential N–H dehydrogenation and N–N self-coupling steps. Herein, a single-atom Ba-doped nickel hydroxide (C-Ba 1 Ni 1-x (OH) 2 ) with an atom-level pinning effect is engineered to tailor a robust carbonate-functionalized interface and a spatially favorable Ni–O–Ni motif for N–H dehydrogenation and N–N coupling of aniline, respectively. The C-Ba 1 Ni 1-x (OH) 2 achieves electrooxidative coupling of various anilines, with up to 95.8% yield and 98.2% Faradaic efficiency for azos, along with good tolerance. Further, single-atom Ba compresses the neighboring Ni–O–Ni distance to spatially favor *Ph-N self-coupling, overall facilitating azo electrosynthesis. Article.Title: Mitigating brittleness in ceramics via transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Chen Z.; Rostamipour K.; Hahn R.; Maier-Kiener V.; Keckes J.; Mitterer C.; Koutná N.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics.

Article.Title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
Article.Authors: Jamshidi Khameneh N.; Krüger T.; Nienaltowski P.; Kater M.; Emery Y.; Fedosov D.; Polin M.; Engstler M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Phenylethanoid glycosides are structurally diverse natural products widely found in traditional medicinal plants and display a broad range of biological activities. Article.Authors: Shi Z.; Huang J.; Li X.; Zhang H.; Peng M.; Yang X.; Liu Q.; Su S.; Zhang C.; Li P.; Gao L.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence for combinatorial optimization depends on high-quality, structured training data, yet transforming ambiguous natural-language descriptions into precise, executable formal models remains a major bottleneck, traditionally requiring extensive manual effort and domain expertise. Article.Authors: Man Y.; Zhai Y.; Gulati A.; Ji J.; Jiang A.; Bai H.; He L.; Belgur C.; Plebani R.; Mannix R.; Chen K.; Yang M.; Posey R.; Feitor J.; Tang S.; Merry G.; LoGrande N.; Sperry M.; Junaid A.; Goyal G.; Hall S.; Yin P.; Ingber D.

Article.Title: Numerosity is directly sensed and dynamically transformed in the human brain
Article.Authors: Karami A.; Castaldi E.; Eger E.; Hebart M.; Piazza M.
Article.Abstract: Humans can estimate the number of objects in a scene within a fraction of a second, suggesting that numerosity is encoded rapidly and directly by the visual system. Yet how this encoding unfolds over time and interacts with other visual features remains unclear. Here, we combined magnetoencephalography (MEG) with time-resolved representational similarity analysis (RSA) and MEG–fMRI fusion to track how numerosity is represented in the brain over time. We also used multidimensional scaling (MDS) to visualize the evolving patterns of neural activity. Two main findings emerged. First, numerosity exhibited the hallmarks of a primary perceptual attribute: its neural signature appeared very rapidly after stimulus onset, preceding the encoding of non-numeric features that could otherwise define number. Second, multidimensional scaling of the neural manifolds revealed a temporal shift in representational geometry: an early linear structure, consistent with a summation-based code and predominant in occipital regions, transitioned into a curvilinear structure characteristic of numerosity-tuned coding, emerging more prominently in associative areas along the dorsal stream. Together, these findings demonstrate that numerosity processing is encoded directly from the visual image and unfolds through a rapid hierarchical transformation, from a broad quantity signal to a finely tuned, number-specific code, linking perceptual encoding to higher-level numerical abstraction.

Article.Authors: Wang W.; Xu F.; Song S.; Liu Y.; Liu L.; Zhang D.; Zhou S.; Wu W.; Li L.; Wei Y.; Han Y.; Wang H.

Article.Authors: Barwinska-Sendra A.; Salgado P.; Sendra K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Article.Title: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
Article.Authors: Heshmati A.; Juárez S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

Article.Authors: Henry R.; Jaacks L.; Waxenberg K.; Alexander P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Article.Authors: Zhou K.; Zhou Y.; Zhou A.; Zhang Z.; Zhong J.; Teng H.; Liang C.; Zhan Q.; Cai Y.; Guo X.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Toroidal vortices in fluid and gas dynamics underpin a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, from elementary particle physics to condensed matter systems, and have recently garnered significant attention in optics because of their inherent topological stability. We further examine the impact of chaotic channels on the stability of these statistically veiled correlation topologies, demonstrating that their topological invariants remain robust under realistic environmental perturbations. Article.Authors: Li M.; Lu Z.; Wang S.; Chu T.; Li B.; Wu Z.; Huang J.; Cheng J.; Wu S.; Ren J.; Wu F.; Guo L.; Sun Z.; Zhu B.; Nie G.; Fu Y.; Li S.

Article.Authors: Barnett S.; Shade A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

Article.Title: Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores
Article.Authors: Heckenbach I.; Iversen K.; Ben Ezra M.; Andersen M.; Bundgaard H.; Scheibye-Knudsen M.; Hasselbalch R.
Article.Abstract: Rapid risk stratification is essential in the clinic, yet vital signs, laboratory tests, and triage scores often miss important risk at presentation. Here we show that a single facial photograph contains prognostic information about mortality risk. Using 27,660 smartphone facial photographs obtained from patients admitted to Danish emergency departments (median age 73 years; 52% male), we train deep neural networks to identify mortality risk. Face-derived scores show strong discrimination for mortality, with AUCs of 0.80 for 3-day mortality and 0.77 for 30-day mortality, outperforming triage level, early warning scores (EWS), vital signs, blood chemistry, and estimated face age. Patients with high EWS scores and the highest face score quartile have a thirty-fold increase in 30-day mortality compared to low-risk patients, and among low-EWS patients, the highest face score quartile identifies substantially elevated risk (OR of 13.39). These findings indicate that unstructured facial photographs encode clinically relevant prognostic information and may complement existing triage and monitoring strategies.

Article.Title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
Article.Authors: Apostol C.; Anish R.; Pham S.; Ettayebi K.; Dave J.; Neill F.; Bok M.; Sankaran B.; Crawford S.; Atmar R.; Crowe Jr J.; Parreño V.; Estes M.; Prasad B.
Article.Abstract: Virus capsids are metastable assemblies with an exquisite balance between stability and flexibility, obligatory for entry, infectivity, and immune escape. Yet the extent to which human viruses exploit capsid plasticity and how that consequently shapes antigenic landscapes remains poorly understood. Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. GII.4 HuNoVs have been evolving epochally, driving most global pandemics, and since 2012, GII.4 Sydney has been the dominant variant. The major capsid protein, VP1, is central to infectivity and immune recognition, and VP1-based virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered promising vaccine candidates. Yet, how the icosahedral HuNoV capsid responds to antibody pressure at the atomic level remains unclear. Here, we present the first atomic structure of GII.4 Sydney capsid determined by cryo-EM, revealing the structural features that likely contribute to its sustained dominance. Using focused refinement, we uncover the remarkable capsid plasticity in response to symmetry-breaking binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies. VP1 adopts 11 distinct conformational modalities to accommodate asymmetric antibody binding, and antibody-disrupted VLPs reassemble into smaller particles with five additional VP1 states. This previously unrecognized extent of conformational adaptability provides key insights for designing next-generation VLP- or mRNA-based vaccines targeting HuNoV infections.

Article.Title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
Article.Authors: Liu T.; Li N.; Tan J.; Yang X.; Zhuang J.; Dai Q.; Dong G.; Liao S.; Tan Y.; Lai Y.; Chen Z.; Wei J.; Wang Q.; Wan X.
Article.Abstract: The construction of atomically precise heterogeneous catalysts that integrate multiple distinct active sites into a synergistic architecture is highly attractive but challenging. Here, we report an Au39(PPhpy2)2(R1C ≡ C)19 (PPhpy2 = 2,2’-(phenylphosphanediyl) dipyridine, R1C ≡ CH = 4-ethynyl-α, α, α-trifluorotoluene) nanocluster. The heteroatoms (such as nitrogen) were introduced to modulate the local coordination environment and construct asymmetric coordination units on the surface of Au39 nanoclusters. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that, in addition to the symmetric R1C ≡ C-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif, Au39 features two asymmetric pyN-Au-C ≡ CR1 coordination motifs on the surface. Au39/XC-72 delivers 96.6% conversion of benzyl alcohol with 94.4% selectivity for benzaldehyde under mild conditions (40 °C, air). Mechanistic studies show that the pyN-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif facilitates O2 adsorption and activation, whereas the R1C ≡ C-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif adsorbs benzyl alcohol. The exceptional catalytic performance stems from the synergy between adjacent, functionally distinct Au sites, enabled by the asymmetric coordination strategy. This study highlights the critical role of asymmetric coordination protocols in synergistic dual-site catalysis for aerobic oxidation, providing new ideas for the rational design of synergistic catalysts. The construction of atomically precise heterogeneous catalysts that integrate multiple distinct active sites into a synergistic architecture is highly attractive but challenging. Here, we report an Au39 nanocluster with heteroatoms introduced to modulate the local coordination environment and construct asymmetric coordination units on the surface.

Article.Title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response
Article.Authors: Zhao B.; Liu Z.; Zeng D.; Li J.; Wan C.; Zhang R.; Fan D.; Li R.; Che R.
Article.Abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal borides (MBenes), boride analogues of MXenes, combine layered frameworks with tunable surface chemistry, yet high-quality MBenes remain difficult to access. Comparative thermodynamic calculations and control experiments with ZnCl 2 , ZnBr 2 , ZnF 2 , and ZnS identify molten ZnBr 2 as the preferred etchant for redox-driven Al extraction and delamination. Temperature-dependent free-energy analysis and Mo−Al−B ternary isothermal sections further define 700 °C as a processing window that suppresses Mo 2 AlB 2 formation and promotes direct conversion from MoAlB to MoB MBene. Selective Al extraction from MoAlB produces few-layer MoB MBene, retaining an ordered Mo−B framework while inducing b -axis contraction, strengthened Mo−B covalency, and enhanced electron localization. Together with O/OH and Br surface terminations, these structural and electronic features promote multiple polarizations and enable an effective absorption bandwidth of 8.7 GHz at 2.1 mm. Article.Title: Greenland ice sheet retreat intensifies the African monsoon through a polar-tropical atmospheric teleconnection
Article.Authors: Han Z.; Feng R.; Wang Z.; Li X.; Zhang Z.; He T.; Yao Z.; Tian C.; Zeng M.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Global climate forcing drives major changes in the North African summer monsoon (NASM), yet how high-latitude cryospheric changes influence tropical hydroclimate through atmospheric dynamics remains unclear. Integrating paleoclimate proxy evidence with coupled climate-model simulations, sensitivity experiments, and idealized atmospheric modeling, we show that Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) retreat acts as a dynamically important amplifier of NASM rainfall. Using the mid-Pliocene as a natural experiment for sustained global warming, we find that NASM rainfall was markedly stronger than that simulated under transient future warming for comparable global-mean temperature increases. GrIS retreat enhances Arctic warming, thereby perturbing the upper-tropospheric westerly jet and triggering a stationary Rossby wave train linking Greenland to North Africa. This polar–tropical atmospheric teleconnection strengthens monsoon circulation and moisture convergence, producing wetter conditions across the Sahara–Sahel. These results reveal a high-latitude pathway through which slow cryospheric changes modulate low-latitude monsoon variability under sustained warming.

Article.Authors: Guo Z.; Yu J.; Fang S.; Cao J.; Zhou X.; Ang Y.; Wang W.; Cheng Z.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: In this work, we introduce a class of hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics in which the spontaneous ferroelectric polarization is coupled to certain nonrelativistic spin splitting components through interlayer sliding, allowing these components to be reversibly switched in an electrical way. First-principles calculations establish bilayer VBr 2 as a representative example, demonstrating the coupled reversal of the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization and the signs of both even- and odd-parity nonrelativistic spin splitting components via an interlayer-sliding pathway. The signs of these nonrelativistic spin splitting components are locked to the sliding-switchable ferroelectric polarization and encoded in the spin-current responses, providing a signature of the coupled ferroic switching. Article.Abstract: Abstract Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Article.Authors: Chen K.; Kriftner M.; Frey M.; Vonlanthen N.; Laroche A.; Xu J.; Seeger S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nature-inspired designs for surface micro- and nanostructures have long attracted attention for their potential multifunctionality. The engineered single-scale rough surface exhibits the remarkable rose petal effect, featuring a water contact angle exceeding 150° and demonstrating extraordinary water adhesion. The wetting states of these surfaces can be easily altered through O 2 -plasma treatment with the reconstruction of secondary and tertiary hierarchical nanostructures. This approach also effectively converts petal-effect surfaces into lotus-effect surfaces, significantly enhancing their self-cleaning performance. Furthermore, the SMM coatings display extremely low adhesion to various adhesives, including tapes, hot glue, and all-purpose adhesives, with pull-off forces nearing 0. Article.Authors: Gutiérrez-Ferman J.; McFadden M.; Rayner R.; Mahajan S.; Smith H.; Aubrey A.; Chen P.; Wahba M.; Wen H.; Dubey P.; Wozniak D.; Peeples M.; Cormet-Boyaka E.; Forero A.; Deora R.

Article.Authors: Qiu S.; Xia J.; Li W.; Yu X.; Chen S.; Li Y.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Small extracellular vesicles hold immense diagnostic and therapeutic potential, yet clinical translation is hindered by inefficient separation and concentration. Current methods like ultracentrifugation and polymer-based precipitation suffer from low throughput or persistent contaminants. Article.Title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
Article.Authors: Feng S.; Wuliji H.; Liu R.; Yaer X.; Niu X.; Wang J.; Zhao K.; Baoyin H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al– x Ce powders develop an interconnected Al 11 Ce 3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al 11 Ce 3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO 2- x /CeO 2 -containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al– x Ce alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

Article.Title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Tian H.; Li J.; Li Z.; Wang J.; Sun W.; Butt H.; Xie L.; Zeng H.
Article.Abstract: Friction at solid-liquid interfaces is typically interpreted through classical contact mechanics, but molecular origins of gas-bubble friction in aqueous environments remain elusive. Oxygen bubbles generate higher friction than air, nitrogen and carbon dioxide bubbles, as supported by molecular dynamics simulations that implicate gas-specific intermolecular interactions in contact-line dissipation. Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Livingstone M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Experience-dependent plasticity in early sensory cortex is restricted to critical periods early in development. Article.Title: Chromosomally unstable cancer cells exhibit heightened dependence on the mitotic SKA complex
Article.Authors: Schoot Uiterkamp M.; Coolen E.; de Lint K.; Tarrab A.; Vukušić K.; Rockx D.; Rooimans M.; de Kleijn T.; Harmsen I.; Leite de Oliveira R.; Foijer F.; Medema R.; Tolić I.; Ben-David U.; Wolthuis R.; Vader G.
Article.Abstract: Aneuploidy and chromosomal instability are common characteristics of cancer but remain underexploited therapeutically. Chromosomally unstable cells are often selectively vulnerable to inhibition of the kinesin KIF18A, and this dependence is related to altered mitotic control. Here, we identify the spindle and kinetochore-associated (SKA) complex as a mitotic regulator that establishes a similar dependency. SKA complex loss is tolerated in cells with a defective mitotic checkpoint, but when mitosis is prolonged, it leads to mitotic errors and loss of viability. Genetic analysis reveals that the SKA complex and KIF18A are epistatic, although they function through mechanistically distinct mitotic pathways. SKA complex depletion selectively impacts chromosomally unstable cancer cells and mirrors the effects of KIF18A inhibition. We thus identify a cellular vulnerability associated with prolonged mitosis in chromosomally unstable cancers.

Article.Title: VapC40 diverts autophagic flux from xenophagy to mitophagy via ammonia-dependent metabolic toxicity
Article.Authors: Ge X.; Liu D.; Wang H.; Dong Y.; Li L.; Duan Y.; Shen P.; Li Y.; Zhang J.; Sun Y.; Huang H.; Zhou X.; Yue R.
Article.Abstract: Mycobacteria survive inside the immune cells meant to destroy them. Toxin-antitoxin systems, gene pairs that help bacteria withstand stress, are abundant in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, yet their role in infection remains unclear. Here we show that the Mycobacterium bovis toxin VapC40 disrupts host nitrogen metabolism. VapC40 redirects glutamine catabolism in infected macrophages, producing excess glutamate and ammonia. Ammonia is transported into lysosomes through the transporter RHCG, raising their pH and rupturing their membranes. Ammonia then enters mitochondria, collapsing membrane potential and triggering oxidative damage. VapC40 recruits NIX to the damaged mitochondria and activates TBK1 on their surface, inducing mitophagy. At the same time, autophagosome maturation is impaired and fewer bacteria reach lysosomes, so the pathogen escapes clearance. Mice infected with VapC40-deficient bacteria show less ammonia toxicity and lung necrosis. These findings show that mycobacteria manipulate host nitrogen metabolism, and identify ammonia-induced organelle damage as a potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
Article.Authors: Zhang W.; Wang T.; Liu G.; Zhou Z.; Kim D.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Core-mantle interactions are essential for understanding Earth’s interior dynamics and evolution. Experimental studies reveal that core-mantle reactions produce iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O (periclase‑wüstite solid solution). Here we show that Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O exhibits pronounced superionic-onset and grain-boundary premelting behavior above ~0.9 T m ( T m : melting temperature). These effects are significant in (Fe x Mg 1-x )O (x > 0.8) under core-mantle boundary (CMB) conditions, causing elastic softening, enhanced elemental transport, and ultra-low viscosity. Enhanced diffusion may facilitate core-mantle reactions and the accumulation of Fe-rich material near the CMB, potentially contributing to a dense basal assemblage. Under mantle flow and/or thermal buoyancy, the low viscosity of connected Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O could favor deformation and redistribution toward shallower depths. This process may contribute to the formation and evolution of some ultra-low velocity zones (ULVZs). The proposed scenario is consistent with the layered structures and inferred low viscosity of some ULVZs and suggests a potential role for Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O in core-mantle material exchange and heat transfer.

Article.Title: 4D printing of multi-state pH-responsive microstructures
Article.Authors: Tran H.; Mainik P.; Gomez Melo S.; Flórido Martins L.; Schwarz U.; Spiegel C.; Blasco E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep eutectic systems (DESs) are emerging as highly versatile functional materials for 3D printing, particularly in multiphoton 3D laser printing (MPLP), a powerful technique for the fabrication of complex microstructures with high spatial resolution. Here, we present a versatile strategy for the fabrication of multi-state pH-responsive microactuators based on polymerizable DESs using MPLP. By incorporating vinyl phosphonic acid and vinyl imidazole as functional monomers, respectively, we establish two actively responsive DESs that exhibit antagonistic swelling behavior across the pH range while maintaining excellent printability. The printed 3D microstructures show pronounced and reversible pH-responsive actuation with high cycling stability. Combining both materials within single architectures enables multi-state and bidirectional actuation beyond conventional bilayer systems. Complex actuator geometries further demonstrate the versatility of the platform. A hyperelastic theory implemented in a finite element framework can predict the experimentally observed actuation patterns. These results highlight the potential of polymerizable DESs as a new material platform for advanced microscale soft robotic, sensing, and adaptive systems.

Article.Title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
Article.Authors: Klein A.; Blahut J.; Vasa S.; Blokhin D.; Hyberts S.; Tošner Z.; Linser R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While conceptually, higher-dimensional approaches such as 4D and 5D correlation spectra are capable of exceeding the established molecular-weight limitations by ameliorating signal overlap, their intrinsic implications for sensitivity and measurement times required have severely limited these important prospects in practice. Here we show that in high-dimensional experiments, the extensive use of dedicated transverse-mixing optimal control pulses (TROPs) can reduce the necessary measurement time by almost an order of magnitude. TROP’ed non-uniformly sampled experiments not only benefit from a multiplicative sensitivity enhancement in each complex time point due to concomitant transfer of both components of complex signals along multi-step magnetization transfer pathways, but additionally from facilitation of reconstruction with better raw data. Aided by the processing framework provided to future users here, the combination of an extensive use of TROPs with increased dimensionality hence presents itself as highly promising to ameliorate the conventional limitations of solid-state NMR.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: solid-state NMR; non-uniform sampling; transverse mixing; magnetization transfer; protein NMR; measurement time reduction

Article.Title: Impact of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety on the Mortality among Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Luo Y.; Jiang M.; Tian S.; Huang T.; Baccarelli A.; Gao X.
Article.Abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases cause over 30% of global deaths, yet the prognostic value of depression and anxiety for individuals with cardiometabolic diseases and the modifying effects of socioeconomic environment have not been well-described. Here, among 376,713 participants from the United Kingdom and 3,973 participants from the United States, each additional cardiometabolic disease was significantly associated with a 28.5% and 33.4% higher risk of depression/anxiety, respectively. In the participants from the United Kingdom, compared with cardiometabolic disease-free individuals without depression/anxiety, the hazard ratio of all-cause mortality increased from 1.200 to 2.389 among individuals with a single cardiometabolic disease when mental disorders were identified during follow-up, and from 1.754 to 2.918 among those with two cardiometabolic diseases. Among individuals with cardiometabolic diseases, the association of depression/anxiety identified during follow-up with mortality was stronger in those with higher socioeconomic status. Replication analyses in the participants from the United States showed broadly similar patterns. These findings highlight the prognostic value of mental health in individuals with cardiometabolic diseases.

Article.Title: A spatiotemporal scaffold in the human subiculum supports episodic memory and its enhancement through navigation training
Article.Authors: Shin J.; Bingman V.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Episodic memory is grounded upon a spatiotemporal framework that binds discrete event details into a coherent structure. However, the neural mechanisms that construct this scaffold and their potential for memory enhancement through cognitive training have yet to be investigated. Here, we show a common spatiotemporal basis for human episodic memory across distinct populations, using a task in which participants remembered a sequence of objects placed in different locations in a virtual environment. Ultra-high-resolution 7-Tesla fMRI revealed that, within the hippocampal formation, the subiculum exhibited selective responses to spatiotemporal binding across sequences of spatial locations, which we attributed to its compressed, high-dimensional neural representational capacity compared to other hippocampal subfields. We then targeted this spatiotemporal framework through a two-week multi-target navigation training paradigm in a subset of participants, which led to transferable improvements in episodic memory. Critically, these behavioral gains were accompanied by enhanced retrieval-related activation and neural pattern reinstatement in the subiculum, measured using 3-Tesla fMRI. Together, these findings establish the subiculum as a core neural substrate for spatiotemporal scaffolding in human episodic memory and highlight its potential as a target for cognitive interventions.

Article.Title: Dual-functional-unit modulation enables superior energy storage in high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics
Article.Authors: Liu G.; Wang J.; Ou B.; Chen X.; Chen X.; Cheng Y.; Gao R.; Li B.; Qi H.; Dai Y.
Article.Abstract: High-performance dielectric capacitors are indispensable for next-generation pulsed power systems. However, simultaneously achieving high recoverable energy density and efficiency remains challenging because of the intrinsic trade-off between polarization and breakdown strength. Here, we develop a dual-functional-unit modulation strategy to overcome this limitation in Bi 0.47 Na 0.47 Ba 0.06 TiO 3 -based ceramics through configurational-entropy engineering combined with microstructural optimization. Specifically, configurational entropy simultaneously tailors two key local functional units, namely local polarization configurations and oxygen octahedral tilt configurations. Multicomponent substitution at the A site (Ba 2+ ) and B site (Zn 2+ /Nb 5+ ) induces fragmented heterogeneous polarization configurations together with weakened and disordered oxygen octahedral tilt, enabling strong field-induced polarization, highly reversible polarization responses, and enhanced intrinsic breakdown strength. Combined with grain refinement and improved densification achieved by high-energy ball milling, which further enhances electrical homogeneity and suppresses interfacial polarization, the optimized ceramic exhibits a breakdown strength of 94 kV mm −1 , a large recoverable energy density of 16.19 J cm −3 and a high efficiency of 91.3%. This work establishes dual-functional-unit modulation as an effective design principle for high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics and provides a general framework for overcoming the polarization-breakdown trade-off in dielectric energy storage materials.

Article.Title: Bioenergetic responses to β-adrenergic stimulation in beige adipocytes depend on actomyosin driven forces
Article.Authors: He Y.; Ling L.; Dempsey G.; Kalindjian N.; Verghese Z.; Chen E.; Liparulo I.; Cho I.; Tran V.; Kumar S.; Stahl A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Beige and white adipocytes reside within the same fat depots but differ in their responses to β-adrenergic stimulation. While both activate classical protein kinase A (PKA)-mediated pathways, only beige adipocytes show induction of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression and enhanced mitochondrial respiration, suggesting additional mechanisms that distinguish their responses. Here we uncover a parallel, non-canonical biomechanical pathway specific to committed beige adipocytes that is required for the full β-adrenergic induction of their thermogenic activity. Mechanistically, β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) stimulation induces a rapid myosin heavy chain 9 (Myh9)-mediated actomyosin contraction and stiffening in differentiated beige but not white adipocytes that activates focal adhesion kinase (FAK), which we show to be critical for the expression of oxidative and thermogenic genes including UCP1 and perilipin 5 (PLIN5). These findings reveal an alternative biomechanical Myh9-FAK signaling arm downstream of β-adrenergic activation that distinguishes thermogenic beige adipocytes from white adipocytes.

Article.Title: Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Kunze S.; Yoon K.; Hwang S.; Hwang Y.; Kim J.; Kang D.; Na I.; Pao C.; Huang W.; Lee Y.; Ku J.; Lim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anodeless all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers offer high energy density and long cycle life, yet their operation in cold environments remains limited by poorly understood failure mechanisms. Using operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy, cryogenic-cross-section electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction, we discover that Li-Ag alloying dynamics are highly temperature-dependent: rapid at 45 °C but kinetically suppressed at 5 °C. At low temperatures, suppressed alloying leads to sluggish lithium transport, internal lithium extrusion, interlayer delamination, and rapid capacity decay. We demonstrate that a brief initial charge at 45 °C permanently activates the interlayer via Li-Ag alloy formation, enabling efficient Li transport even at 5 °C. Full pouch cells following this activation protocol retain 87% of their initial capacity after 250 completed cycles following one formation cycle at 5 °C. After 250 cycles at 5 °C, AAP-treated cells delivered approximately three times the discharge capacity of cells cycled with the fixed-temperature protocol. Such in situ electrochemical alloy activation offers a practical and scalable approach to extend anodeless all-solid-state battery performance to sub-ambient temperatures without material redesign.

Article.Title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
Article.Authors: Suárez-Dou S.; Gallegos M.; Han K.; Brünig F.; Berryman J.; Tkatchenko A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: machine learning interatomic potentials; vibrational dynamics; conformational dynamics; density of states

Article.Title: A master gene for Drosophila male courtship prevents the behavior in females via a truncated protein
Article.Authors: Peng Q.; Chen D.; Wang R.; Xing L.; Li C.; Ma M.; Guan W.; Han J.; Sun Y.; Pan Y.
Article.Abstract: Decades of studies have established that a terminal gene in the sex determination hierarchy, fruitless ( fru ), controls nearly all aspects of male courtship behaviors in Drosophila and many other insects. fru is transcribed in a sex-specific manner to produce male-specific Fru proteins (Fru M ) and was considered nonfunctional in females. In this study, we identify a female-specific truncated Fru protein (Fru F ) that is specifically expressed during the pupal stage and distributed in both cell bodies and neuronal projections, in contrast to Fru M , which is expressed from larval to adult stages and localized to nuclei. We discover that Fru F cooperates with another sex determination gene, doublesex ( dsx ), to prevent male-typical courtship in females. Knocking down fru F in dsx -expressing pC1 neurons induces courtship in females. These results reveal that the master gene for male courtship prevents this behavior in females via a truncated protein, thereby refining the canonical sex determination hierarchy that controls sexual development and behaviors.

Article.Title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
Article.Authors: Sanchez-Garcia R.; Berndt A.; Apelbaum A.; Reeks J.; Williams P.; Poelking C.; Deane C.; Saur M.
Article.Abstract: Cryo-Electron Microscopy (cryo-EM) is a pivotal tool for determining 3D structures of biological macromolecules. Current workflows are computationally demanding and require manual intervention, creating bottlenecks for high-throughput applications like structure-based drug discovery. In such contexts, where all protein samples can be assumed to be equivalent at resolutions relevant for image alignment, information about particle poses from previous refinements could be reused. Existing methods, however, ignore this prior knowledge, aligning each dataset from scratch. We present cryoPARES, a deep learning pose estimation method trained on pre-aligned datasets. Our method not only provides accurate angular predictions significantly faster than traditional approaches but also introduces automated particle pruning capabilities that eliminate manual intervention. Together with its single-pass operation, these features enable near real-time reconstructions that provide feedback during data acquisition. We demonstrate cryoPARES’s effectiveness through rapid structural determination of seven ligand-bound complexes across four distinct protein targets. We also release three fragment-bound cryo-EM datasets.

Article.Title: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
Article.Authors: Kharal S.; Gao Y.; Bo L.; Damron J.; Toomey M.; Kanbargi N.; Gupta S.; Do C.; Bowland C.; Tian Z.; Kidder M.; Kearney L.; Naskar A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polymer–solvent–nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid–liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer–induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres, yet the process is often limited by coarsening of pores or collapse within the fibre core, leading to structural inhomogeneity. Here, we advance this strategy through Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer induced assembly (CAST), in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ during solvent exchange and preferentially retained within the polymer rich phase. These precipitates act as a distributed molecular retarding agent that delays domain growth, thereby preserving bicontinuity throughout the fibre cross-section to up to 250 µm. Using a poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate–ethanol–water system with a phenolic oligomer coprecipitate, we demonstrate that CAST stabilizes the hollow bicontinuous domain structure, extending the attainable specific surface area by ca. 100%. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

Article.Title: Distinct DNA-binding modes of Sp8 and Sp6 shape a hierarchical regulatory network in limb ectoderm
Article.Authors: Castilla-Ibeas A.; Moreu S.; Pérez-Gómez R.; Galán L.; Campa V.; López-Giménez J.; Rada-Iglesias A.; Ros M.
Article.Abstract: Sp8 and Sp6 are closely related transcription factors expressed in the limb ectoderm, where they control proximo-distal and dorso-ventral patterning, yet their direct targets and molecular mechanisms have remained unclear. Combining genome-wide chromatin occupancy with transcriptomic profiling in vivo, we identify shared and specific targets and reconstruct the Sp8/Sp6 gene regulatory network, establishing Sp8 as its dominant, hierarchical node. Mechanistically, the two factors diverge: Sp8 binds DNA directly at canonical GC-rich Sp motifs, regulating targets including Fgf8 and Sp6 itself, whereas Sp6 acts as a transcriptional cofactor. Via indirect binding to AT-rich motifs through Dlx, both cooperatively regulate limb-patterning pathways, including Wnt, FGF, TGF-β/BMP, and Notch. Biochemical assays confirm that both form homo- and heterodimers and interact with Dlx5 through their zinc-finger domains. Together, these findings reveal how Sp8 and Sp6 orchestrate AER formation and dorso-ventral patterning, providing a mechanistic framework for congenital limb malformations such as split-hand/foot malformation.

Article.Title: LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of exocytic RABs disrupts neurotrophin/neuropeptide secretion
Article.Authors: Murphy F.; Abramian A.; Baginska U.; Klaassen R.; Koopmans F.; van Geest N.; Saarloos I.; Smit A.; Toonen R.; Verhage M.
Article.Abstract: Neuropeptide signals such as BDNF secreted from dense-core vesicles (DCVs) are essential for neuronal development, maturation and survival. RAB3 GTPases are established regulators of DCV exocytosis, but their functional diversity remains poorly understood. Here, we use live-cell imaging and neuropeptidomics to show that distinct exocytic RABs control DCV exocytosis in a neuron type specific manner, whereas RIM1/2 is a universal effector. Striatal neurons express both RAB3A and RAB27B but, surprisingly, only the latter controls DCV exocytosis. This is explained by selective phosphorylation of RAB3A by LRRK2, preventing its recruitment to DCVs. Finally, a LRRK2 hyperactive mutation associated with Parkinson’s disease disrupts DCV exocytosis in both hippocampal and striatal neurons. These findings uncover an unexpected diversity in controlling neuropeptide secretion in different neurons and establish LRRK2-mediated inhibition of RAB recruitment to DCVs as a powerful inhibitory principle that may also contribute to neurodegeneration upon gain-of-function mutations.

Article.Title: Encoding atomic-layer thickness via spin-dependent optical differentiation
Article.Authors: Zheng D.; Liu C.; Yang Q.; Zhao Y.; Wen S.; Luo H.; Chen S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional materials exhibit pronounced layer-dependent properties, making accurate determination of atomic-layer thickness essential. Existing characterization techniques typically rely on spectroscopic signatures or scanning probes, which require complex instrumentation and often lack direct real-space interpretability. Here we introduce a spin-dependent optical differentiation approach that encodes thickness into directly observable edge features. By engineering the optical transfer function at planar interfaces, we access anisotropic and isotropic differentiation regimes governed by the spin Hall effect of light. In the anisotropic regime, the layer number is continuously encoded in the orientation of edge features. In the isotropic regime, a morphology-based transition, from disk to ring, provides a discrete and robust signature for layer identification. We experimentally demonstrate layer-resolved imaging in graphene, MoS 2 , and WSe 2 . Our results establish spin-dependent optical differentiation as a simple and versatile platform for translating atomic-scale variations into directly accessible optical features, enabling rapid and in situ characterization of two-dimensional materials.

Article.Title: Selective mTOR inhibition via FLCN drives TFE3-dependent VLDL-TG secretion and protects from MAFLD/MASH
Article.Authors: Thorsheim C.; Gosis B.; Durso G.; Zhou W.; Tanosaki S.; Jung J.; Cox A.; Boehmler D.; Axsom J.; Blair M.; Li K.; Weljie A.; Titchenell P.; Jang C.; Arany Z.
Article.Abstract: Hepatic lipid homeostasis is controlled by multiple processes, including VLDL-TG secretion. We have previously shown that the FLCN/TFE3 branch of mTORC1 signaling controls hepatic fatty acid oxidation and de novo lipogenesis to protect mice from MAFLD. We now show that the FLCN/TFE3 pathway also controls VLDL-TG secretion via direct transcriptional activation of a broad program of genes involved in VLDL-TG secretion, including PCYT1A, the rate-limiting step of phosphatidylcholine synthesis. Loss of hepatic FLCN upregulates VLDL-TG secretion and prevents MAFLD, and this protection requires TFE3 and PCYT1A. The data unveil a new pathway that orchestrates multiple steps of VLDL-TG synthesis and secretion. The data also highlight that suppressing the selective FLCN/TFE3 branch of mTORC1 signaling maximizes hepatic lipid clearance by coordinately promoting fatty acid oxidation, suppressing de novo lipogenesis, and boosting VLDL-TG secretion, providing an attractive therapeutic target for the treatment of MAFLD.

Article.Title: Ikaros transcription factors prevent the activation of an endothelial cell program in bone marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
Article.Authors: Taroni C.; Bianchi G.; El Khoury M.; Romero-Mulero M.; Cabezas-Wallscheid N.; Chan S.; Kastner P.; Kirstetter P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are generally committed to the hematopoietic lineage, but how that commitment is maintained is not well understood. We show that the Ikaros family of transcription factors is essential for HSC identity. Ikaros, alone or in combination with Helios, is required to sustain the pool of multipotent HSCs and their downstream progenitor cells in adult animals, by directly repressing a core group of genes implicated in wound healing, cell junction organization, and actin cytoskeleton organization. Remarkably, upon in vivo or in vitro deletion of Ikaros or Ikaros+Helios, nearly one-third of the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) rapidly exhibit an endothelial cell transcriptomic signature, and develop non-hematopoietic structures resembling CD144+ endothelial-like cells. These results indicate that adult HSPCs are highly plastic and prevented from activating an endothelial cell program by Ikaros family transcription factors.

Article.Title: Real estate wealth inequality and exposure to natural disasters with evidence from France
Article.Authors: Bézy T.
Article.Abstract: Most studies measuring inequalities in exposure to climate disasters rely on aggregate income data and focus on residents. By omitting dwellings owned by nonresidents, this approach overlooks half of the housing stock exposed to flooding. Using dwelling-level data covering the entire French housing market, this paper examines how natural disaster risks are distributed across tenants, owner-occupants, and owners of rental, second, and vacant properties. The results highlight large differences with the standard approach that focuses on residents. Once properties owned by nonresidents are included, flood risk disproportionately affects second homes, while subsidence mainly affects owner-occupied dwellings. These patterns have important policy implications. First, untargeted flood insurance subsidies tend to benefit second homes, whereas subsidence coverage mainly supports owner-occupied dwellings. Second, this study shows that natural disaster risks are not priced into rental, second, and vacant properties, driving at least 15% of the total overvaluation in flood-prone areas.

Article.Title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium–oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
Article.Authors: Bai T.; Hu Y.; Zhai W.; Zhong X.; Huang J.; Wang J.; Song W.; Rao T.; Du S.; Gao D.; Lu J.; Shi R.; Ci L.; Li D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium–oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Here, we report an artificial intelligence-integrated framework leveraging interpretable machine learning and density functional theory to navigate a vast chemical space of thousands of active sites. This approach identifies Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts as a better configuration among the selected elements for orchestrating multi-electron transfer. Theoretical analysis reveals that synergistic electronic coupling between the dual-sites fundamentally reconfigures the d -band center, thereby lowering the thermodynamic barriers for oxygen redox. Moreover, the catalysts enable precise regulation of the reaction pathway, inducing a controllable transition from the conventional two-electron pathway to a four-electron pathway. This shift yields a discharge capacity of ~60,000 mAh g −1 . Beyond its role as a positive electrode catalyst, this architecture functions as a multifunctional interfacial protective layer that stabilizes the lithium metal negative electrode by suppressing dendrite growth. Consequently, the lithium–oxygen system achieves stable lifespan of 2075 cycles under the four-electron pathway with reduced voltage decay. This work establishes a data-guided strategy for the rational design of atomic-scale architecture via artificial intelligence, unlocking the potential of multi-electron oxygen chemistry for lithium–oxygen batteries.

Article.Title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
Article.Authors: Cheng Y.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack .

Article.Title: Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
Article.Authors: Yan J.; Wang C.; Wu S.; Dai W.; Jia S.; Zeng Y.; Li W.; Li Y.; Zhang H.; Ren Z.; Deng B.; Gao Y.; Chu W.; Wang T.; Xu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off between achieving spatial charge separation, which is necessary for dipole formation, and maintaining sufficient wavefunction overlap to ensure efficient radiative recombination. Here, we overcome this trade-off in the two-dimensional perovskite (AE3T)PbI 4 by leveraging organic-inorganic band-edge engineering to induce frontier-state hybridization, thereby forming bright hybridized dipolar excitons with spatially indirect character and appreciable optical transition strength. These excitons combine an out-of-plane permanent electric-dipole component, room-temperature nonlinear transport consistent with long-range dipole–dipole repulsion, and finite optical transition dipole moments. Beyond addressing a key constraint in dipolar-exciton design, this work establishes frontier-state hybridization as a molecular design principle for constructing optically active, electrically polarized excitons in low-dimensional quantum materials.

Article.Title: A map of multi-omics quantitative trait loci in a Chinese population reveals regulatory variations and disease links
Article.Authors: Yang P.; Li S.; Zheng Q.; Liu X.; Pan S.; Zhang Y.; Liu T.; Lam S.; Kang H.; Zhu X.; Lin S.; Fang Z.; Wang Y.; Wang J.; Shui G.; Liu F.; Zeng C.; Jia P.
Article.Abstract: Quantitative trait loci (QTL) studies have been pivotal in mapping the genetic regulation of molecular traits but have been primarily conducted in European populations, limiting insights into diverse ethnic groups. Our study identifies 209 protein QTLs (pQTLs) for 155 proteins and 587 metabolite QTLs (metabQTLs) for 369 metabolites. By integrating these findings with cis -methylation QTL (meQTL) from our previous work, we define the shared genetic architecture across molecular layers. Colocalization analyses reveal 3,665 pairs of shared causal variants across traits, including loci such as LHPP , with mediation evidence supporting regulatory cascades linking DNA methylation, proteins, and metabolites. To link these molecular findings to health outcomes, we perform Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, identifying 497 potential causal relationships between molecular traits and diseases, including FCRL3 for Graves’ disease and deoxycholic acid 3-glucuronide for colorectal cancer. Collectively, we present a systematic genomic atlas of meQTLs, pQTLs, and metabQTLs specific to East Asian populations, providing critical insight into shared regulatory networks and candidate causal variants across molecular and disease phenotypes.

Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang L.; Lekina Y.; Hu S.; Wu X.; Huang Y.; Wang K.; Guo H.; Shen Z.
Article.Abstract: Polychromatic luminescent materials have attracted sustained interest owing to the potential applications in high-sensitivity visual optical sensing. Nevertheless, developing a rational design strategy that can simultaneously achieve a broad color gamut and tunable multicolor emission remains a highly challenging task. Here we show that a Mn 2+ -doped zero-dimensional metal halide, Mn 2+ :(TPA) 2 PbBr 4 (TPA + = tetrapropylammonium cation), demonstrates these desirable characteristics. By application of high pressure, the initial blue emission of Mn 2+ :(TPA) 2 PbBr 4 undergoes a sequential transition from cyan to yellow, then to pink-purple, and ultimately returns to blue. This polychromatic color modulation originates from the interplay between the intrinsic blue emission of the [PbBr 4 ] 2- tetrahedra and the pressure-induced green-to-red shift of the [MnBr 4 ] 2- tetrahedra, accompanied by energy transfer processes between the two luminescent centers. Concurrently, enhanced hydrogen-bonding interactions between the inorganic and organic components suppress nonradiative recombination, increasing the polychromatic emission intensity, which is further amplified at low temperatures. These findings offer new insights into the mechanisms governing polychromatic emission and provide promising strategies for developing advanced optoelectronic materials.

Article.Title: Lipid droplets amplify inflammasome-driven cytokine secretion in infection and inflammation
Article.Authors: Pedró-Cos L.; Mallet C.; Thery F.; Courrieu P.; Pichon J.; Remot A.; Eggermont D.; Bugault F.; Hehner J.; Després M.; Sánchez-Álvarez M.; Parton R.; Pol A.; Impens F.; Demangel C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipid droplets (LDs) accumulating in infected cells are traditionally viewed as passive nutrient stores exploited by invading pathogens. Proteomic and imaging analyses reveal the selective recruitment of ISGylated proteins together with caspase-1 and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) precursors to the LD surface. Comparative LD proteomics in wild-type and ISG15-deficient macrophages, combined with ISGylome profiling, identify ISGylated proteins as mediators of pro-IL-1β binding to LDs. Functionally, disruption of LD biogenesis in primary human macrophages impairs mature IL-1β secretion and compromises Mtb control. Notably, this LD-dependent amplification of IL-1β release is not restricted to microbial stimuli but also occurs in response to sterile inflammasome activation. Collectively, these findings redefine LDs as immunoactive organelles integrating microbial and danger signals to potentiate inflammasome-dependent IL-1β responses during infection and inflammation.

Article.Title: Dearomatization and cycloaddition of furans and indoles enable divergent syntheses of spirooxindole alkaloids
Article.Authors: Cheung Y.; Liu Y.; Tong R.
Article.Abstract: Dearomatization has revived recently as a key tactic in organic synthesis due to major methodological developments that allow mild chemoselective dearomatization. This synthetic strategy enables rapid collective synthesis of >30 spirooxindoles within 7 steps and 10 spirooxindole natural products within 10-14 steps with satisfactory overall yields. This work establishes a blueprint for coupling distinct dearomatization manifolds in complex molecule synthesis, with immediate implications for medicinal chemistry and natural product-inspired drug discovery.

Article.Title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict
Article.Authors: Headley T.; Shay C.; Tozan Y.
Article.Abstract: Humanitarian emergencies test the resilience of global health systems, yet policy is constrained by limited empirical evidence on the magnitude and timing of service delivery disruptions. Here, we assess the association between measured childhood vaccination-as a proxy for health service delivery-and forced displacement, armed conflict, and natural disasters. Across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023, sudden increases in displaced populations were associated with declines in vaccination coverage of approximately 3 to 6 percentage points, persisting for 2 to 3 years before recovery. Dose-response analyses revealed a nonlinear relationship: coverage fell steeply at low displacement levels and plateaued at extreme exposure. Conflict intensity followed a similar nonlinear pattern that plateaued near 3000 annual battle-related deaths while mortality from natural disasters showed no detectable association with coverage. Displacement's association was largely independent of armed conflict, indicating that displacement may act as a distinct, additive shock rather than a proxy for violence.

Article.Title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites
Article.Authors: Louca P.; Khan Mirzaei M.; Kouraki A.; Khamespanah E.; Lin Y.; Peng X.; Pope R.; Visconti A.; Asnicar F.; Kirk D.; Costeira R.; Segata N.; Falchi M.; Bell J.; Spector T.; Edwards L.; Deng L.; Valdes A.; Menni C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacteriophages, viruses infecting bacteria, are abundant in the human gut, but their population-level structure and metabolic associations remain unclear Here we present a foundational characterisation of the gut phageome using deep shotgun metagenomic data in a large population-based cohort ( n = 1,069: TwinsUK). Phageome diversity was mostly driven by environmental factors, with modest heritable components. We detected 4 significant vOTU diet associations. These results identify structured population-level associations between phage-associated genomic elements, bacterial communities, and microbial metabolites, motivating future experimental and mechanistic studies.

Article.Title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Popov T.; Beilner T.; Fearns N.; Vollmar C.; Kaufmann E.; Remi J.; Staudigl T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neural activity and eye movements are well-established predictors of human memory performance. Article.Title: Author Correction: A machine learning model reveals expansive downregulation of ligand-receptor interactions that enhance lymphocyte infiltration in melanoma with developed resistance to immune checkpoint blockade
Article.Authors: Sahni S.; Wang B.; Wu D.; Dhruba S.; Nagy M.; Patkar S.; Ferreira I.; Day C.; Wang K.; Ruppin E.
Article.Abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was a coding error that originated in our single-cell RNA-seq cell-cell interaction tool, SOCIAL, in which cell-type-specific ligand-receptor interactions were not calculated correctly from the single-cell data. As SOCIAL is integrated into our spatial transcriptomics tool, SPECIAL (also introduced in this article), the downstream spatial transcriptomics analyses were also affected. We have corrected the error in SOCIAL and regenerated the affected single-cell and spatial transcriptomics results (Fig. 2I-J; Fig. 5; Supplementary Figs. 7–10 and associated figure legends and text). The conclusions are not affected. We have updated the SOCIAL code deposited in GitHub. The HTML and PDF versions of the article have been updated. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

Article.Title: Mapping redox networks in cardiomyocytes reveals non-overlapping response pathways for cytosolic versus mitochondrial H₂O₂ signaling
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Cárdenas-Arciniegas J.; Vergel Leon A.; Maurer W.; Ibrahim A.; Zieseniss A.; Kurschat L.; Hillemann A.; Bauer L.; Nanadikar M.; Guo J.; Berecic B.; Gorshkova A.; Cyganek L.; Vikram Vamsi P.; Mondal S.; Brügmann T.; Wagdi A.; Tiburcy M.; Urlaub H.; Lenz C.; Rehling P.; Brandenburg S.; Katschinski D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are essential redox messengers, yet their effects depend on concentration, localization, and duration. Here, we investigate how compartment-specific hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) production influences cardiomyocyte redox signaling and function. Using human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CM) expressing the H₂O₂ biosensor HyPer fused to D-amino acid oxidase (DAO), we achieve chemogenetic control of H₂O₂ generation in the cytosol, mitochondria, or nucleus. Cytosolic H₂O₂ propagates throughout the cell, whereas mitochondrially generated H₂O₂ remains spatially restricted, reflecting compartmentalized antioxidant buffering. Cytosolic H₂O₂ impairs contractility and relaxation in both 2D and 3D engineered heart tissue models, accompanied by preferential oxidation of Z-disc–associated and actin-binding proteins and by altered sarcomere organization. Antioxidant treatment attenuates these effects. In contrast, mitochondrially produced H₂O₂ is better tolerated and associated with adaptive redox remodeling, with preserved contractile performance that is antagonized by conoidin A-induced inhibition of cytosolic peroxiredoxin activity. These findings demonstrate that the subcellular source of H₂O₂ shapes redox propagation, oxidation patterns, and functional responses, highlighting redox compartmentalization as a determinant of cardiomyocyte performance and stress resilience.

Article.Title: Identification of translation events that drive nonsense-mediated mRNA decay reveals functional roles for alternative RNA isoforms
Article.Authors: Young D.; Wang Y.; Guydosh N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway targets mRNAs undergoing premature translation termination for degradation. Previously, RNA-seq of yeast lacking NMD revealed that most genes targeted by NMD lack obvious premature termination codons (PTCs). We develop a combined approach using RNA-seq and 40S ribosome profiling to identify cryptic premature termination events that could account for NMD on nearly all these transcripts, including many alternative RNA transcript isoforms associated with annotated genes. Many NMD-targeted transcripts appear to be involved in two-promoter gene regulatory systems and share properties with long un-decoded transcript isoforms (LUTIs). In particular, we show that the DAL5 LUTI regulates expression of the DAL5 protein-coding mRNA in response to changes to environmental nitrogen. Our work expands the functional roles for LUTIs and establishes the importance of NMD in their regulation.

Article.Title: Ligand-Mediated Long-Range Interactions Enable Selective Activation of H2O2 for Efficient Water Decontamination
Article.Authors: Cai T.; Li Y.; Shi W.; Wang X.; Ren L.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Steering hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) activation to selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2•−) offers a potent solution for water decontamination, especially under neutral or even alkaline conditions. However, the practical potential of this approach has long been constrained by inefficient O2•− generation due to non-selective O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation. Here, we develop a biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) strategy to synthesize a meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin iron (TCPP-Fe) catalyst that directs heterolytic O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation, leading to predominant O2•− generation with an apparent O2•− generative selectivity of 90.3% among the quantified reactive oxygen species. The TCPP-Fe catalyst exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a normalized apparent rate constant of $$40.6\,{{{{\rm{L}}}}}^{2}\,{\min }^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{{\rm{H}}}}}_{2}{{{{\rm{O}}}}}_{2}}}^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{\rm{cat}}}}.}}^{-1}$$, which is approximately 2.1-fold higher than the next-highest value in the compiled dataset of representative Fe-based, Fe-alloy, and related catalysts. This remarkable reactivity and selectivity arise from BSCSE-induced modulation of the electronic structure of Fe sites, which facilitates efficient electron transfer between H2O2 and Fe centers while electrostatically stabilizing the Fe–*OOH intermediate to steer O2•− generation. Integrated into a continuous-flow catalytic membrane filtration system treating real secondary effluent, TCPP-Fe enables >96% bisphenol A removal with negligible Fe leaching and sustained removal performance during 120 h of operation. This work bridges biomimetic principles with heterogeneous catalysis, providing a generalizable design strategy for next-generation catalysts toward sustainable water decontamination. Biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) steers H2O2 activation toward superoxide generation, enabling efficient and durable contaminant removal in complex water matrices.
