Article.Title: Hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring steers CO electroreduction toward ethanol
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Wang X.; Wang D.; Liu N.; Chu S.; Wu W.; Yang B.; Li Z.; Zhang Q.; Lei L.; Wang Y.; Hou Y.
Article.Abstract: Electrochemical conversion of carbon monoxide (CO) to ethanol is challenged by competing pathways that remove oxygen from reaction intermediates and form ethylene. Here we show that strontium (Sr)-modified copper (Cu) promotes ethanol formation and propose hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring as a mechanism for oxygen-retention. Sr-derived sites are proposed to host hydroxyl adjacent to Cu reaction sites, creating a site-differentiated interface that shift hydroxyl from site-competing spectators to selectivity-directing components. In situ spectroscopy reveals Sr-dependent changes in signals associated with adsorbed CO and oxygen-containing intermediates. Calculations suggest that nearby Sr–OH groups can stabilize the oxygen-ends of selected intermediates through non-covalent interactions, mitigating C–O bond weakening. The resulting Sr(1.0%)-Cu catalyst achieves an ethanol Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65.4% at 1.0 A cm −2 , with an ethanol-to-ethylene FE ratio of ~18.7, compared with a maximum of ~2.0 for pristine Cu. It also operates for over 200 hours in a membrane-electrode assembly and retains ethanol selectivity under syngas feeds. These findings highlight the spatial organization of interfacial hydroxyl species as a strategy for oxygen-retaining electrosynthesis.

Article.Title: Upcycling of polyolefin and polyester mixtures via a single-atom alloy
Article.Authors: Zhang G.; Liu S.; Duan Z.; Zheng S.; Liu T.; Liang Y.; Yang F.; Li S.; Qi D.; Zhang K.; Wang Y.; Li J.; Tian J.; Xiong H.
Article.Abstract: Upcycling of mixed plastic waste is challenging due to the complex compositions and high sorting costs, lacking robust catalysts for simultaneous conversion of polyolefins and polyesters. Herein, guided by machine learning, we design a Ru 1 Cu/CeO 2 -GR single-atom alloy catalyst that enables one-pot hydrogenolysis of mixed plastics into fuel-range hydrocarbons. Ru single atoms anchored on Cu nanoparticles lower C–C bond cleavage barriers, while Cu suppresses benzene ring overhydrogenation. Under mild conditions (280 °C, 30 bar H 2 ), the catalyst delivers ~75% liquid yield (C 5 –C 22 ) with 59.5%–62.7% C 8 –C 16 fraction and ~15% aromatic products yield from five-component mixed plastics. Life cycle and techno-economic analyses confirm that this direct upcycling route outperforms traditional sorted recycling with lower environmental impacts and higher economic benefits. This work provides a sustainable and economically viable strategy for mixed plastic waste valorization.

Article.Title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
Article.Authors: de Graaf F.; Thornalley D.; Wilson D.; Hewett Z.; Rosenthal Y.; Woodard S.; Ford H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). Here we present high-resolution neodymium isotope (ε Nd ) records from a depth transect in the equatorial Atlantic over the iNHG. We find a persistent latitudinal and depth gradient in neodymium isotope values in the deep Atlantic during the Late Pliocene, absent in the Early Pleistocene, indicating an expansion of NADW extent over the iNHG. In contrast, our reconstruction suggests very little glacial-interglacial variability in NADW extent during both the Late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene. These results suggest deep-water circulation was substantially different during a warm climate state, with implications for the role of NADW formation during major climate transitions and its future stability.

Article.Title: Staggered cryo-plasma FIB milling enables high-throughput cryo-ET
Article.Authors: Lisicki E.; Taubitz T.; Wagner T.; Raunser S.; Tacke S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cryo-focused ion beam (cryo-FIB) milling combined with cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a crucial technique for studying macromolecules in their native environment. To mill thick samples, plasma ion sources are used. However, the practicality of high plasma currents, which offer the greatest potential for increasing throughput, and their possible damaging effects on the sample have not yet been investigated. Here, we systematically examine high-current xenon plasma-FIB (PFIB) milling and quantify the current-dependent damage in over 4700 tomograms by preparing a total lift-out volume of 9000 µm³. We find that currents of up to 2500 nA can be used in cryo-ET lamella preparations, enabling increased milling speeds and sample volumes that can be examined while maintaining sample integrity. We demonstrate this using a newly developed high-throughput staggered milling routine for waffle-like preparations, in which we achieve high-resolution reconstructions of yeast ribosomes, and for tissue serial lift-outs, enabling a complete experiment within 24 hours. Our results and approach provide a strong foundation for future in situ structural investigations of medically relevant protein complexes in organoids, tissues, or entire organisms.

Article.Title: In vivo dynamics of ovulation and oocyte entrance into the oviduct in mice
Article.Authors: Umezu K.; Faubert A.; Wang S.; Behringer R.; Larina I.
Article.Abstract: Ovulation is a dynamic multistep process essential for female fertility. Although central to reproductive success, the real-time behaviors of oocytes, ovarian tissues, and oviducts during the ovulatory process in vivo remain unknown. Here, we use intravital microscale volumetric imaging to reveal the in vivo spatiotemporal dynamics of key stages of ovulation associated with follicle opening, oocyte release, and the subsequent transport of the ovulated oocyte into the oviduct in mice. Unexpectedly, we find a time lag between follicle opening and subsequent abrupt changes in follicular volume and oocyte position, followed by the release of the cumulus-oocyte complex (COC). Remarkably, oocytes deform into an elliptical shape as they squeeze through a relatively small opening of the follicle but regain a spherical shape shortly after being released. We also discover repetitive pulses of fluid emitted from the oviduct that inflate the periovarian space, increasing fluid flow required for COC movement into the oviduct. These findings uncover previously unrecognized cellular, tissue, and organ-level mechanisms that coordinate ovulation and oocyte transport, offering potential insights into the etiology of ovulatory disorders and female infertility.

Article.Title: Stepwise transitions unlock three spin states and diverse SHG in a polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Zhang Z.; Wu S.; Ishikawa R.; Mishima A.; Yan Z.; Xu G.; Dai J.; Sato O.; Yamashita M.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multifunctional spin-crossover materials are promising for information storage and nonlinear optics, yet stepwise spin-crossover coupled with controllable second harmonic generation switching is hindered by poor thermal stability of non-centrosymmetric lattices. Herein, we report an air-stable polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex displaying cooling-induced two-step spin-crossover but one-step transition during heating, delivering a wide thermal hysteresis of 75 K (199 K cooling / 274 K heating) via intense intermolecular cooperativity. Sequential phase evolution ( P 1 → P 1 → Pn ) creates three discrete spin configurations with c -axis cell duplication followed by a symmetry-increasing transition to full low-spin phase upon cooling. Second harmonic generation tests verify three separable nonlinear optical states consistent with magnetic responses. Crystal stacking analysis and density functional theory calculations validate that spin ordering-phase transition synergy rearranges molecular dipoles to realize stepwise second harmonic generation modulation. This study offers an original route toward dual spin-optic functional materials for optical storage applications.

Article.Title: Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
Article.Authors: Leroy C.; Laurencin D.; Valenza D.; Montels P.; Gaveau P.
Article.Abstract: Mechanochemistry is an expanding and generally green synthetic route, which is attracting more and more chemists in academia and industry. Yet, its applicability is often still limited by the lack of information on the mechanochemical processes. Therefore, to help elucidating reaction pathways in the solid state, we need to develop new real time monitoring techniques. Here we present an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando (i.e., real-time in situ) mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this original technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in ball-milling (BM). Lastly, we show that our NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution, during a reaction, directly inside the milling jar. This method, BM-NQR, represents a promising functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling syntheses.

Article.Title: Single-cell mass accumulation reveals copiotrophic bacterial growth rates in native seawater
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Roller B.; Hellerschmied C.; Sichert A.; Gomez A.; Bartlau N.; Séneca J.; Danilyan E.; Wolfram M.; Mußmann M.; Miettinen T.; Polz M.; Manalis S.
Article.Abstract: The growth of marine microbial communities drives ocean biogeochemical cycles, yet the growth rates of individual species remain poorly understood. Copiotrophic bacteria, such as Vibrio species, are thought to live a feast-and-famine existence, as their capacity for rapid growth contrasts with their typically low abundance. Here we use a microfluidic mass sensor adapted to directly measure subtle and otherwise undetectable mass accumulation of individual marine bacteria in native seawater. We observe growth of several copiotrophic bacteria and find that Vibrio species consistently grew across diverse temporal conditions and had higher buoyant mass than co-occurring species. Remarkably, their growth rates were similar across samples collected over days to months and followed a well-known nutrient growth law previously established in laboratory cultures. Overall, our findings suggest that low-abundance species may play a disproportionately large role in the marine carbon cycle, with rapid biomass turnover driven by high growth rates balanced by intense predation.

Article.Title: STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis links innate immune activation to tau pathology
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Fan L.; Wong M.; Ambaw Y.; Zhu J.; Norman K.; Ye P.; Foxe N.; Zhu D.; Wan Y.; Srinivasan M.; Mok S.; McIntire L.; Walther T.; Farese R.; Gan L.; Luo W.
Article.Abstract: Genetic risk for Alzheimer’s disease and related tauopathies is strongly enriched in pathways governing microglial activation and cholesterol metabolism, yet how these processes converge to drive neurodegeneration remains unclear. Here, we identify the oxysterol 25-hydroxycholesterol (25-HC) as a pathogenic lipid downstream of the cGAS-STING–Interferon (IFN) pathway. In models of tau pathology, interferon signaling induces microglial expression of Cholesterol 25-hydroxylase (CH25H), the enzyme responsible for 25-HC production. Ch25h deletion in female P301S mice suppressed tau aggregation, preserved synapses, prevented brain atrophy, and rescued memory. Mechanistically, loss of CH25H disrupted STING trafficking, attenuated IFN activation, and dampened self-perpetuating microglial inflammation. Strikingly, 25-HC directly accelerated tau propagation in human iPSC-derived neurons. It also disrupted lysosomal and mitochondrial lipid composition, driving cholesteryl ester accumulation and promoting neuronal death under tau-induced stress. These findings define a STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis that bridges innate immune activation to tau pathology and toxicity, offering a tractable therapeutic pathway for inflammation-driven neurodegenerative conditions.

Article.Title: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation of mediodorsal thalamus disrupts decision flexibility during reward learning
Article.Authors: Mackenzie G.; Gilmour W.; Barnard I.; Yang S.; Suveges S.; MacFarlane J.; Kanodia A.; Manfield J.; Khan S.; Osman Farah J.; Macerollo A.; Steele J.; Gilbertson T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract When learning to find the most beneficial course of action, the prefrontal cortex guides decisions by comparing estimates of the relative value of the options available. Basic neuroscience studies in animals support the view that the thalamus can regulate this activity within and across the prefrontal cortex. We studied a group of patients (n = 37) undergoing unilateral MR-guided focused ultrasound for essential tremor, performing the restless bandit, a reward reinforcement learning task, immediately before and after thalamotomy. Thalamotomy significantly impaired the proportion of switch choices during the task without affecting overall performance. This effect was observed when the task was delivered to co-incide with maximal vasogenic thalamic oedema but not in a control group tested on the same day of their treatment. A reinforcement learning model fitted to the patients’ choices replicated the effect of thalamotomy when the model increased exploitation of the bandits’ learnt value estimate. This shift in the explore-exploit trade-off, manifesting as reduced choice flexibility, co-varied with the pattern of post-operative oedema extension into the mediodorsal nucleus. These findings confirm a causal role of the thalamus and specifically the mediodorsal nucleus in regulating the extent to which value estimates are used to guide decisions and learning from reward.

Article.Title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
Article.Authors: Yavorskiy D.; Hagenmüller D.; Charrouj N.; Ivonyak Y.; Kazakov A.; Todorov Y.; Knap W.; Białek M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A 2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A 2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

Article.Title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
Article.Authors: Smit S.; Bluschke M.; Moen P.; Heinsdorf N.; Zavatti E.; Bellomia G.; Giuli S.; Dufresne S.; Suen C.; Zimmermann V.; Au-Yeung C.; Zhdanovich S.; Dadap J.; Dosanjh P.; Zonno M.; Gorovikov S.; Lee H.; Kuo C.; Lee J.; Song D.; Ishida S.; Eisaki H.; Keimer B.; Michiardi M.; Elfimov I.
Article.Abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures ( T c ), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi 2 Sr 2 Ca 2 Cu 3 O 10+ δ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO 2 plane – as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) – and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record T c of Bi2223.

Article.Title: Morphogenesis of the muscular ventricular septum is driven by retinoic acid signalling to myocardium
Article.Authors: Bønnelykke T.; Coulon C.; Sturny R.; Couderc M.; Cortés C.; Rousset C.; Saha D.; Marchese D.; De Bono C.; Miquerol L.; del Monte-Nieto G.; Zaffran S.; Kelly R.
Article.Abstract: The mammalian heart is divided into four chambers by septa that isolate systemic and pulmonary circulation and are hotspots of congenital heart defects (CHD). The muscular ventricular septum develops between left and right ventricular cardiomyocytes derived from the first and second heart fields. Despite its clinical importance, mechanisms underlying development of the ventricular septum are poorly understood. Here we show that myocardial reception of retinoic acid (RA) signalling regulates formation of the compact septal core. Activation of a dominant negative RA receptor in second heart field-derived myocardium during septal morphogenesis results in a deep interventricular cleft and bifid cardiac apex. This phenotype is preceded by ectopic trabecular contributions to a RA-independent septal primordium. Molecular analysis identifies defective cardiomyocyte maturation and impaired RAC1 activation in mutant hearts. These results support an infolding and RA-dependent fusion model of septal morphogenesis, providing new insights into ventricular development and the origins of CHD.

Article.Title: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy
Article.Authors: Charles M.; Romero Ferrufino S.; Ramelli S.; Gallogly S.; Kwe Yinda C.; Ahuja D.; Hayes E.; Pizzuti M.; Vannella K.; Martens C.; Kaiser F.; Platt A.; Quezado M.; Morris C.; Munster V.; Hewitt S.; Chertow D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb caused an outbreak of >100,000 cases globally, with highest disease burden in people living with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), those with CD4 count <200 cells/mm 3 . However, we detected replication-competent MPXV in multiple CNS tissues and confirmed neuronal and glial cell infection using RNA-scope in situ hybridization. MPXV sequencing from body and brain tissues revealed widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated variants. Article.Title: Whole-brain modeling of dynamic causal circuits in human cognition using amortized variational inference
Article.Authors: Lee B.; Rouillard L.; Diniz L.; Jiang L.; Ambrogioni L.; Ryali S.; Branigan N.; Mistry P.; Cai W.; Wassermann D.; Menon V.
Article.Abstract: Understanding dynamic mechanisms underlying cognition remains a major challenge in human neuroscience. Here, we develop, validate, and apply Multivariate Dynamical Systems Identification with Amortized Variational Inference (MDSI-AVI), a computational framework designed to address critical challenges in capturing asymmetric, context-dependent, whole-brain directed interactions while accounting for regional hemodynamic response variability in fMRI data. MDSI-AVI leverages simulation-based inference through forward and reverse variational inference to address the limitations of conventional variational methods in high-dimensional settings. By averaging over uncertainty in hemodynamic response parameters using forward simulation, MDSI-AVI provides well-calibrated posteriors of directed connectivity that scale efficiently to networks with hundreds of nodes. Applied to Human Connectome Project data ( N = 728), MDSI-AVI provides insights into working memory mechanisms, identifying the dorsal anterior insula as a critical hub influencing activity at the whole-brain level. We demonstrate task-dependent modulation of causal influences, where the salience network drives frontoparietal network activity, which differentially influences the default mode and sensorimotor networks depending on working memory load. These whole-brain causal interactions distinguish task conditions with high accuracy and predict working memory performance. Our framework demonstrates reproducible results across whole-brain parcellations, establishing MDSI-AVI as a robust tool for advancing our understanding of circuit dynamics in cognition and disease.

Article.Title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C(sp3)−H bond oxygenation
Article.Authors: Huang L.; Cai J.; Guo Q.; Ding B.; Liu M.; Ma C.; Duan C.
Article.Abstract: The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues faces marked challenges. By encapsulating a non-heme FeIII-complex into the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule, herein we report a light-responsive allosteric catalysis for activating O2 and metabolizing C(sp3)−H bonds. Light irradiation initially triggers the bridged FeIII-porphyrins switching into unbridged FeII/O=FeIV-porphyrin pair for substrate oxygenation. Parallelly exciting the anthraquinone groups sensitizes O2 to 1O2 via energy transfer, meanwhile exciting the non-heme FeIII-complexes generates the chlorine radicals via ligand-to-metal charge transfer. The capsules enforce heme and non-heme FeII fragments into proximity, forming an Fe−O − O−Fe intermediate with the reactive 1O2 species for O − O bond cleavage. Synergistic hydrogen abstraction by chlorine radicals and O=FeIV-porphyrin by combining multiple photons selectively and fleetly oxygenates thioxanthene to thioxanthen-9-one within the capsule pocket, therefore reshaping oxygenase for selective metabolism in a supramolecular approach. The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues is challenging. Here, the authors report the allosteric catalysis of a non-heme Fe(III)-complex encapsulated in the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule.

Article.Authors: Herr L.; Dhar S.; Rossi M.; Schaffer E.; Biswas K.; Burkett S.; Keskin E.; Datta A.; McNeill D.; Mukhopadhyay S.; Butcher D.; Calvo-Rubio M.; Camandola S.; Abdelmohsen K.; Nicolae C.; Dunn C.; Stumpo D.; Gorospe M.; Moldovan G.; de Cabo R.; Blackshear P.; Branzei D.; Sharan S.; Brosh R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The mechanistic basis for chromosomal instability characteristic of RECQ helicase disorders remains poorly understood due to their molecular-genetic complexity. Article.Title: Structurally guided wavefront neural encoder for broad-range generalizable 3D holography
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Yan X.; Li J.; Shi Z.; Yu Y.; Zhang Y.; Jing T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep learning has advanced computer-generated holography, but learned models remain coupled to fixed wavelengths and distances, limiting generalization. Here we present the structurally guided wavefront neural encoder (SGWN-Encoder), which integrates diffraction physics with neural networks and employs a structural propagation strategy that analytically strips the parameter-sensitive global phase. Article.Abstract: Agitation combines motor restlessness with negative affect, yet the neural circuits coordinating these features remain unclear. Article.Title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
Article.Authors: Ohta M.; Lee C.; Sietses V.; Kostylev I.; Ball J.; Moroshkin P.; Hamamoto T.; Kobayashi Y.; Onoda S.; Ohshima T.; Isoya J.; Takahashi H.; Kubo Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

Article.Authors: Sîmpetru R.; G. Molinari R.; Rohlf D.; Batichotti R.; Watanabe R.; Elias L.; Del Vecchio A.

Article.Title: Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
Article.Authors: Horwood J.; Oglic D.; Hernández-Lobato J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We explore diffusion-based training as a flexible approach to molecular property prediction in settings shaped by chemical, biophysical, and latent heterogeneity. To address this, we build on score-based generative diffusion models and introduce a conditional diffusion module for predictive tasks, equipped with a joint training and sampling guidance scheme and an optional gated residual mechanism that regulates feature- vs target-driven information flow across noise levels. The module acts as a plug-in learning block for existing molecular encoders, making it complementary to advances in representation learning. Across diverse feature extractors and graph neural networks, diffusion-based training improves over conventional maximum-likelihood objectives on small-molecule regression benchmarks and matches or exceeds strong baselines on multitask regression and classification datasets. It also produces well-calibrated predictive uncertainty as measured by prediction interval coverage, enables confidence-guided ranking, and performs well in challenging settings including activity cliffs and class-imbalanced multitask prediction. Overall, these results position diffusion as a promising representation-agnostic approach for effective molecular property prediction.

Article.Authors: Tang S.; Duan Z.; Tian Z.; Du W.; Qian F.
Article.Abstract: Characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of complex chemical reactors, especially localized engineering-critical points or regions, remains challenging in process engineering. Although data-driven methods offer computational advantages, the incorporation of domain-specific physical knowledge can further enhance their predictive performance. Here, we present a physics-informed machine learning framework that systematically embeds coking mechanisms and heat transfer principles into neural network architecture and training constraints. Using a coke-accumulating cracking reactor as a prototypical case, the proposed approach reproduces the spatiotemporal distributions of key operational parameters obtained from conventional simulations with high fidelity and achieves a 10 5 -fold computational acceleration. Crucially, the incorporation of mechanistic knowledge enhances prediction fidelity for critical safety indicators, particularly the maximum external wall temperature (error < 0.5%), enabling precise identification of optimal decoking intervals. This paradigm bridges data efficiency with domain-informed modeling, providing a useful reference for developing real-time monitoring and optimization models for complex industrial systems.

Dt1, which confers stem-growth habit, physically interacts with RIN2, attenuating RIN2-mediated transcriptional regulation. STF1 / 2 act downstream of Dt1 and RIN2 . Article.Title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
Article.Authors: Hu F.; Huang Q.; Chaw S.; Xia C.
Article.Abstract: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are two types of biogenetically related polycyclic monoterpenoid alkaloids with distinct structural features. Article.Title: A redox-coupled ROMO1–LONP1–SIRT3 axis controls hepatic lipid catabolism
Article.Authors: Peng K.; Qiu S.; Ren Y.; Xu F.; Zhang W.; Xu Y.; Wang Y.; Fu L.; Zhang X.; Duan X.; Cheng H.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Disturbed balance between lipid anabolism and catabolism drives hepatic steatosis. Mitochondria play a central role in lipid clearance through free fatty acid (FFA) oxidation, yet the molecular mechanisms governing this metabolic process remain incompletely understood. Hepatocyte-specific ablation of ROMO1 impairs mitochondrial FFA oxidation and causes hepatic lipid accumulation. Mechanistically, ROMO1 loss induces sulfenylation of the mitochondrial protease LONP1, resulting in excessive degradation of SIRT3 and consequent hyperacetylation of mitochondrial proteins involved in FFA oxidation. Moreover, spontaneous fatty liver in aged rhesus macaques is associated with reduced ROMO1 expression and concomitant loss of SIRT3 protein. Collectively, our findings establish the ROMO1–LONP1–SIRT3 axis as a redox-coupled signaling cascade that links mitochondrial redox regulation to hepatic lipid catabolism, providing potential therapeutic targets for steatotic liver diseases.

Article.Title: 4D mitochondrial network assumes distinct and predictive phenotypes through human lung and intestinal epithelial development
Article.Authors: McMahon G.; Agarwal D.; Arora M.; Wang Z.; Arkfeld E.; Hakozaki H.; Schöneberg J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mitochondria form dynamic three-dimensional networks that exhibit a wide range of morphology and motility depending on cell state, cell type, and cell fate. Article.Abstract: Halide-based Na-ion conductors have attracted intense attention due to their favorable (electro)chemical compatibility with oxide positive electrodes. Among these, zirconium (Zr)-based halide solid electrolytes (SEs) offer a cost advantage over halide SEs based on rare metals, but the relatively low ionic conductivity has limited their application in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Here, we report employing soda ash (Na 2 CO 3 ) as a low-cost precursor to introduce an aliovalent carbonate polyanion and produce a family of Na-Zr-Cl-CO 3 conductors with nominal compositions of (2- x )NaCl- x Na 2 CO 3 -ZrCl 4. This substitution increases structural disorder and amorphization, creating structural environments that facilitate Na + transport. At the optimal composition, its ionic conductivity reaches 1.02 mS cm −1 at 25 °C. The optimized Na-Zr-Cl-CO 3 SE also exhibits stable electrochemical behavior and favorable mechanical properties. When paired with NaCrO 2 positive electrode, the assembled ASSBs deliver an initial discharge capacity of 117 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and demonstrate a long-term cycling stability at 0.3 C for 850 cycles. Article.Title: Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
Article.Authors: Xing E.; Zhang J.; Wang S.; Cheng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract AlphaFold2 (AF2) has transformed protein structure prediction by harnessing co-evolutionary constraints embedded in multiple sequence alignments (MSAs). MSAs not only encode static structural information, but also contain evolutionary signatures linked to protein dynamics and conformational heterogeneity, which are central to biological function. However, the subtle co-evolutionary signals that bias proteins toward distinct conformational states are often obscured by noise within MSA data and remain challenging to decipher. Here, we introduce AF-ClaSeq, a systematic framework that enriches and purifies state-specific evolutionary signals through iterative sequence classification and selection. By identifying sequence subsets that preferentially encode distinct conformational states, AF-ClaSeq enables robust predictions of alternative conformations across diverse protein systems. Our findings indicate that the accuracy of alternative-state prediction depends more on the purity of the evolutionary signal within an MSA than on sequence depth. Notably, purified sequences encoding specific structural states are distributed across phylogenetic clades and superfamilies, rather than being confined to individual lineages. By extending AF2 beyond single-state structure prediction, AF-ClaSeq provides a promising approach for exploring protein structural plasticity, establishing a foundation for future studies of the sequence determinants underlying conformational switching and allosteric regulation.

Article.Abstract: Recent advances in soft electronics have enabled the conformal integration of epidermal sensors on skin, significantly improving performance, long-term stability, and user comfort. However, achieving perfect conformability between conventional planar devices and three-dimensional skin surfaces remains a major challenge due to possible Gaussian curvature mismatch. In this study, we propose in situ fabrication of conductive nanofibres to achieve conformal epidermal sensors on arbitrary surfaces. We develop a stable and uniform carbon nanotube-based hybrid precursor for the fabrication of sub-1-μm intrinsically conductive nanofibres directly on skin, achieving conformability on both developable surfaces and non-developable surfaces. The porous nanomesh exhibits excellent gas-permeability, radiative heat dissipation efficiency, biocompatibility, and long-term stability, making it suitable for user-friendly epidermal electronics. Article.Title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
Article.Authors: Beaven R.; Fafinska M.; Dai J.; Halberg K.; Denholm B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Countercurrent exchange describes the crossover of some property between two bodies flowing in opposite direction. Countercurrent circuits, which work more efficiently than concurrent circuits, are common in nature and mimicked in human engineering. An example is the beetle cryptonephridial complex (CNC)—a multi-organ water conservation system which makes key contributions to the water budget in a vast number of species. It is even used by some to harvest water from the atmosphere. The system evolved by a radical reorganisation of insect internal anatomy bringing the renal/Malpighian tubules and rectum into countercurrent configuration, and their isolation in a chamber by an unusual tissue of unknown origin—the perinephric membrane. The CNC is richly supplied with tracheae to meet the high metabolic demands of the system. How the CNC is assembled during development is unknown. Here we characterise CNC development in the model beetle Tribolium castaneum and discover the molecular signals orchestrating its assembly. We find that dynamic crosstalk between the developing precursor cells of the rectum, Malpighian tubules, perinephric membrane, and trachea rely on a single, differentially spliced fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor and two FGF pathway ligands. We also map the origin of the perinephric membrane to a previously uncharacterised population of mesodermal cells, providing clues to its evolutionary origin. This work illuminates the developmental processes underpinning the reorganisation of the insect internal body plan to assemble a natural countercurrent system, one which is fundamental to beetle physiology, ecology and evolutionary success.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Heat stress events pose a major threat to global agriculture due to elevated air and soil temperatures. Our findings reveal an interesting pathway for plant adaptation to heat stress, linking pH, ROS and root thermomorphogenesis, with major implications for improving plant resilience in warming climates.

Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Cui H.; Zhou C.; Xie C.; Zhao R.; Liao W.; Li H.; Zhang Y.; Li L.; Su Z.; Chen Y.; Li J.; Simchi A.; Bai J.; Zhou B.; Liu M.

Article.Title: Kinetic balancing for near-equilibrium growth of defect-suppressed lead bromide perovskite single crystals
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Li Z.; Zhou T.; Hao Y.; Wang S.; Meng G.; Xu Y.; Fang X.
Article.Abstract: Controlling crystallization pathways for solution-grown lead-bromide perovskites remains a major unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a ligand-regulated crystallization strategy that achieves near-equilibrium growth for lead-bromide perovskite single crystals. Such regulation mitigates kinetic imbalance during crystal growth, thereby suppressing non-equilibrium defect incorporation, improving lattice coherence, and facilitating spatially uniform crystal growth. This strategy is applicable to a representative set of lead-bromide perovskites. Specifically, the resulting CsPbBr 3 single crystals exhibit a high resistivity of 5.1 × 10 10 Ω·cm and carrier mobility up to 93.95 cm 2 ·V −1 ·s −1 . Reduced electron-phonon coupling weakens optical-phonon scattering and raises the effective thermally activated conduction barrier from 0.43 to 0.71 eV, extending stable bias operation from 40 to 200 V·mm −1 . These advances enable sensitive and stable ionizing-radiation detection under both photon-counting and charge-integrating modes. Article.Title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Shin C.; Bae S.; Kim K.; Park H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bound states in the continuum (BICs) support high-quality-factor resonances embedded in extended spectra, and their radiation properties can be tailored through perturbative symmetry breaking and chiral engineering. However, because BICs are intrinsically delocalized states of infinite periodic structures, they typically require large spatial footprints. Achieving localized BIC modes while preserving radiation suppression and topological singularities, and simultaneously enabling chiral responses, remains a challenge. Here, we experimentally realize low-threshold BIC lasers localized at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains with identical bulk BIC characteristics but opposite chirality. The resulting interfaces and junctions host spatially localized states that exhibit optical spin–momentum-locked emission governed by the assigned chirality, while retaining intrinsic BIC properties, including narrow far-field divergence and pump-selective lasing localization. In addition, polarization singularities confirm the topological nature of these low-dimensional BICs, particularly the well-defined topological charge of the zero-dimensional junction mode. Coupling two zero-dimensional BICs further gives rise to bonding and antibonding supermodes, enabling non-Hermitian, chirality-locked behaviors. These results establish a route to compact, high-quality-factor photonic states with engineered chirality through dimensional reduction of BICs, without relying on defect confinement or band inversion.

Article.Title: Sensory cortical disinhibition underlies long-term fear memory in humans
Article.Authors: Brown J.; Ma Y.; Wang Y.; Massa J.; Cheng P.; Chen C.; Ding M.; Schmidt N.; Milad M.; Soares J.; Dolan R.; You C.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract How transient threats turn into persistent, long-term fear memories is a fundamental problem in neuroscience, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Early sensory cortex, traditionally viewed as a passive feature analyzer, is increasingly recognized as an active participant in fear processing. These findings establish sensory cortical disinhibition as a necessary mechanism for long-term fear memory in humans and identify early sensory cortex as crucial node for intervention of persistent maladaptive fear.

Article.Title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
Article.Authors: Yao Y.; Shu S.; Feng J.; Hu H.; Yang W.; Liu R.; Wang X.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Classical theory predicts that environmental improvement intensifies competition and increases forest structural heterogeneity (variation in tree radial size). On the Tibetan Plateau, warmer and wetter conditions are associated with homogenization via enhanced radial growth and reduced climate sensitivity. These findings challenge the classical expectation that environmental improvement inevitably increases structural heterogeneity, revealing a shift from stress-driven convergence to decoupling under low stress and providing a unified framework for predicting forest responses to climate change.

Article.Authors: Bhandari K.; Chen P.; Havlin S.; Gao J.
Article.Abstract: Identifying pivotal components in complex networks—such as key intersections in transportation systems, influential actors in social networks, or keystone species in ecosystems—is essential for improving the resilience and mitigating catastrophic failures of these systems. However, existing methods for critical node detection are typically tailored to specific network types and objectives, limiting their generalizability. To overcome this limitation, we propose a machine learning framework that combines reinforcement learning with an attention-based graph neural network. By leveraging multi-topology training, our model learns to adapt and generalize across diverse network structures and objective functions. Experiments on real-world and synthetic networks uncover distinct topological features that are important for identifying critical nodes. Notably, our method applied to personalized gene networks, prioritizes genes that are significantly enriched for cataloged cancer drivers. This work provides a robust critical node detection model with a comprehensive multi-topology training approach, suitable for a broader range of real-world applications.

Article.Title: Agricultural economic responses to ecoclimate teleconnections induced by forest loss
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Zhao L.; Fei C.; McCarl B.; Wang X.; Liu M.; Breshears D.; Feng X.; Baldwin E.; Cheng H.; Derbridge J.; Golding J.; Lien A.; López-Hoffman L.; McLaughlin D.; Swann A.; Soto J.
Article.Abstract: Forest disturbances are increasing globally, altering vegetation in ways that can affect distant agricultural systems through ecoclimate teleconnections. We examine how large-scale U.S. regional forest loss with C3 grass replacement affects agricultural production and markets. We integrate climate simulations, econometric yield models, and an agricultural sector model to trace impacts from vegetation change through climate anomalies to yields, land allocation, prices, and welfare, while isolating vegetation-driven effects from greenhouse-gas forcing. Teleconnection-induced yield responses are spatially heterogeneous. Soybean yields decline, particularly in the Southern Plains, while wheat gains occur there and corn responses are muted. This shifts regional crop mixes and increases total production by 1–3%, lowering crop prices, increasing consumer surplus, and reducing producer surplus, with small positive net agricultural welfare effects. Our study excludes forest-sector impacts and ecosystem-service losses and therefore does not imply that forest loss is beneficial.

Article.Title: Geophysical conditions favoring precursory slip before major earthquakes
Article.Authors: Dong P.; Xia K.; Kato A.; Obara K.; Peng Z.; Peng J.
Article.Abstract: Precursory slow slip holds potential for reliable earthquake forewarning, yet the conditions conducive to it remain elusive. While quite a number of large earthquakes on smooth megathrust faults are preceded by precursory slow slip, laboratory experiments suggest such slip is inhibited on smooth faults. Here we capture diverse preseismic slow slip behaviors through laboratory experiments, and show that the occurrence pattern of precursory slow slip is dictated by both fault roughness and stress. We find that energetic slow slip producing pronounced acceleration in preseismic moment release prevails on smooth faults under low stress but diminishes as stress increases. For rougher faults, multiple slow slips yield moderate to pronounced acceleration depending on stress. Our results extend previous observations by showing that under lower normal stress, precursor signals on smooth faults can be more pronounced than those on rougher faults, reconciling the contradiction between field and laboratory observations. Our findings provide a mechanism for the prevalence of precursory phase for large earthquakes on smooth, fluid-rich megathrust faults.

Article.Title: Functional diversity of GPCR–Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways
Article.Authors: Jaime Arce V.; Lettmann M.; Tögl M.; Bonn Garcia S.; Bauer M.; Neukirch M.; Kleinstück O.; Langolf A.; Kaczmarek I.; Hilger D.; Schihada H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gustducin (G gust ), the G protein mediating taste receptor signaling, is expressed not only in sensory taste cells but throughout the human body alongside numerous non-taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Whether and how these receptors engage G gust , and the functional consequences of such interactions, remain poorly understood. Here, we develop two complementary biosensors that enable direct monitoring of GPCR–G gust interaction and downstream signaling in living cells, allowing pharmacological characterization of G gust activity induced by non-taste GPCRs. We find that several non-taste GPCRs do not activate G gust but instead stabilize the G protein heterotrimer and suppress basal signaling by forming unproductive GPCR–G protein complexes, whereas others induce conventional G gust activation and signal transduction. We further show that these unproductive GPCR–G gust complexes suppress the activation of alternative signaling pathways by sequestering receptors from other G proteins. This mode of interaction functionally partitions GPCRs into activators and inactivators of G gust and represents a mechanism for balancing concurrent signaling pathways within a cell.

Article.Title: Sunflower pollen microgels enable sonication-free dispersion of carbon nanotubes for bio-based conductive inks
Article.Authors: Gao C.; Yang D.; Liang J.; Wang Z.; Zhao M.; Zhao Z.; Deng H.
Article.Abstract: Sustainable, high-performance conductive inks are crucial for wearable electronics. While biopolymer-based dispersants offer renewable and biocompatible routes for CNT inks, a paradox persists: biopolymers require energy-intensive extraction, high-power ultrasonication, and lack the rheological strength for precision extrusion printing. Here we show that a sonication-free strategy utilizing sunflower pollen microgels in their native granular state, leveraging their amphiphilic spiky architecture, achieves CNT debundling through a mild-stirring-driven capture-collision-friction integrated process, while alginate provides electrostatic stabilization. The resulting pollen-alginate-CNT (PAC) inks exhibit rapid thixotropy and high viscoelasticity, enabling high-fidelity 3D extrusion and screen printing. Drying induces a lamella-like assembly, forming anisotropic conductive networks. These features unlock multifunctional performance, including humidity sensing via interlayer-spacing modulation, direction-dependent strain sensing, and electromagnetic interference shielding. This work establishes a scalable, energy-efficient framework that overcomes the processing and rheological limitations of conventional bio-based inks, advancing sustainable, adaptive printed electronic systems.

Article.Title: Bright and stable near-infrared tin-perovskite LEDs enabled by efficient optical and thermal management
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Liu Y.; Pu C.; Yu Q.; Feng X.; Chen D.; Niu W.; Ye Y.; Wang X.; Yu T.; Gao F.; Zou Z.; Bao C.
Article.Abstract: Invisible near-infrared (NIR) light sources are central to optoelectronic and bioelectronic systems including night-vision imaging, facial recognition, and non-invasive biomedical sensing. However, realizing planar NIR emitters with high output optical power remains a major challenge. Here we demonstrate lead-free CsSnI 3 perovskite light-emitting diodes (LEDs) that achieve simultaneous breakthroughs in efficiency, radiance and operational stability. The devices deliver high radiances of 6304 W sr −1 m −2 under DC and 21,633 W sr −1 m −2 under pulsed driving, together with a half-lifetime (T 50 ) of 64.3 h at 100 mA cm −2 , representing record performance for NIR tin-based perovskite LEDs and a substantial advance for solution-processed NIR optoelectronics. These advances are enabled by the spontaneous formation of discrete hemispherical perovskite microstructures, which synergistically enhance optical and thermal management. We further demonstrate the effectiveness of large-area planar LEDs for red-glow-free night-vision surveillance, biomedical imaging and sensing. Our work establishes a viable route toward high-radiance, stable and lead-free NIR light sources, advancing the development of scalable perovskite-based optoelectronic and bioelectronic technologies.

Article.Title: An electrically driven multimodal soft robot enabled by a monolithic heterolayer elastomer
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Ji H.; Wang Z.; Zhuo J.; Jiang L.; Xu N.; Shi M.; Dong H.; Peng J.; Normahmedov O.; Jiang S.; Zhao X.; Wang Z.; Chen F.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: Soft robots powered by active materials can navigate complex environments through multimodal locomotion. However, prevailing designs typically rely on a single active material within multi-component architectures, which often leads to high structural complexity and “soft-stiff” interfacial challenges. Here, we present an electrically driven, entirely soft robot based on a monolithic heterolayer elastomer integrating a processable high-performance dielectric elastomer and a liquid crystal elastomer. In this “soft-soft” structure, the liquid crystal elastomer functions as a reconfigurable compliant skeleton to program the equilibrium states, while the dielectric elastomer serves as a fast-responsive artificial muscle driving dynamic motion. Through independent control of the two active materials, the robot demonstrates bidirectional crawling at 2.3 cm·s −1 , leaping over 2.5 body lengths, climbing on a 20° slope, and controlled rolling. Our approach establishes a paradigm for creating soft robots with high structural integrity, payload‑to‑weight ratio, and controllability for deployment in unstructured environments.

Article.Title: TRIM47 drives cardiac ischemia/reperfusion injury by impairing mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism in male mice
Article.Authors: Hu C.; Wang L.; Sun W.; Song Y.; Li X.; Zhang Z.; Zhang X.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: E3 ubiquitin ligase Tripartite motif-containing 47 (TRIM47) is integral in modulating metabolic processes and cellular homeostasis. However, its pivotal role and underlying molecular mechanisms in cardiac ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that TRIM47 is markedly upregulated in cardiomyocytes during cardiac I/R injury in an early growth response 1-dependent manner, and that its expression positively correlates with the severity of cardiac I/R injury. Gain- and loss-of-function studies reveal that cardiomyocyte-specific TRIM47 overexpression exacerbates, while TRIM47 knockout attenuates I/R-induced cardiac injury, structural remodeling and functional impairment in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, upregulated TRIM47 facilitates K63-linked ubiquitination of forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) at K210 site to induce its nuclear translocation, where it interacts with and inhibits the transcriptional activity of hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha (HNF4α), thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, fatty acid oxidation defects and cardiac I/R injury. Moreover, therapeutic knockdown of TRIM47 after I/R injury is highly effective in preventing cardiac remodeling and dysfunction. Our findings identify the role of the TRIM47/FOXO1/HNF4α axis in I/R-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic disorders and cardiac injury, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting TRIM47 to treat cardiac I/R injury in male mice.

Article.Title: Anion manipulation for breaking through 3.0 V of aluminium–graphite batteries
Article.Authors: Guo K.; Huang Z.; Wang W.; Song W.; Jiao S.
Article.Abstract: Aluminium-graphite batteries offer low cost and intrinsic high safety. However, the voltage window mostly remains limited because conventional chloroaluminate ionic-liquid electrolytes with Lewis-acidic Al 2 Cl 7 − ([AlCl 3 –AlCl 4 ] − ) anions are intrinsically moisture-sensitive and unstable beyond 2.5 V. To extend the voltage window, a polytetrafluoroethylene/AlF 3 framework‑confined, fluorine-rich chloroaluminate ionic-liquid composite quasi-solid-state electrolyte cosolvated with 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl ether is designed for constructing stable aluminium-graphite batteries with a cut-off voltage of 3.0 V. With the presence of AlF 3 , the Al 2 Cl 7 − is regulated through AlF 3 -associated chloroaluminate interactions, which reduces its activity and suppresses its electrochemical decomposition in the range of 2.5–3.0 V. Meanwhile, the fluorinated ether coordinates with the AlCl 3 units in Al 2 Cl 7 − and promotes the formation of a fluorine-rich artificial interface on the graphite, essentially improving the electrochemical stability via alleviating electrochemical decomposition of AlCl 4 − up to 3.0 V. Furthermore, ion transport channels could be well maintained during large mechanical deformation induced by anion-intercalation/deintercalation of graphite interlayer. Therefore, the Al|electrolyte|graphite cells deliver discharge capacity beyond 137 mAh g −1 up to 3.0 V (specific current: 5.0 A g −1 ) (compared to 64 mAh g −1 , charged up to 2.5 V at 5.0 A g −1 ) along with stable cycles beyond 35,000, demonstrating long-term high-voltage operation in rechargeable aluminium–graphite batteries.

Article.Title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
Article.Authors: Zhou B.; Li H.; Hu B.; Zhou J.; Li C.; Zhou J.; Huang Y.; Duan X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising laser-gain media for their direct bandgap and strong excitonic effects. However, existing TMD lasers typically rely on mechanically exfoliated or high-temperature chemical-vapor-deposition-grown materials, with their atomic-scale thickness inherently limiting the available optical gain volume. Here, we report room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 (BM-MoS 2 ) thin films in whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) cavities. Using solution exfoliation and spray coating under ambient conditions, we produce area- and thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films composed of electronically decoupled MoS 2 monolayers separated by organic spacers. This layered architecture preserves the intrinsic monolayer excitonic properties while providing a tunable gain volume beyond that of an isolated monolayer. Integrated with WGM cavities, the thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films enable a balance between the quality ( Q ) and optical confinement ( $$\varGamma$$ Γ ) factors. Power-dependent measurements reveal key lasing signatures, including a threshold-like input-output crossover accompanied by linewidth narrowing at a pump power of approximately 1.4 nW, and pump-induced polarization selection. Solution-processable BM-MoS 2 thus offers a scalable gain medium for thin-film laser photonics.

Article.Title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
Article.Authors: Wu Q.; Cui J.; Wu A.; Meng Y.; Chen D.; Wang Y.; Yan L.; Ma L.; Taniguchi T.; Watanabe K.; Lin S.; Shi S.; Cui Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Kondo insulators are paradigmatic strongly correlated materials, traditionally found in f-electron compounds. They originate from the hybridization between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, which opens a gap in the electronic spectrum. Two-dimensional moiré systems provide a new route to flat bands with strong electron correlation, which host localized moments at half filling. Here we report signatures, based on local conductivity measurements using microwave impedance microscopy, of a Kondo insulator in a moiré superlattice of monolayer WS 2 / bilayer WSe 2 , in which one WSe 2 layer carries flat moiré bands and the other dispersive ones. When both layers are partially doped with two holes per moiré unit cell in total, an insulating state appears when the moiré band contains less than one hole. The insulator becomes metallic above a certain threshold magnetic field, evidence for the singlet nature of the Kondo insulator, and the observed behavior is reproduced by a periodic Anderson model. Our results open a route to simulating Kondo physics in tunable moiré systems.

Article.Title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
Article.Authors: Zheng J.; Wang Z.; Lin J.; Huang C.; Pan G.; Xu D.; Hu X.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: Notable differences between histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch have been extensively researched at peripheral and spinal levels. However, the way in which the brain processes histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch remains unknown. We discovered that the posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (pPVT)→the nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcMed) circuit exhibits reverse response patterns to histamine-dependent or histamine-independent itch and serves as a central anti-pruritic role. Mechanistically, histamine-dependent itch activates excitatory inputs from the lateral hypothalamus (LH) to mobilise the anti-pruritic centre, thereby buffering its intensity. In cases of chronic itch, however, there is a decrease in the efficiency of the anti-pruritic circuit’s postsynaptic transmission, thereby promoting itch sensitisation. Our research reveals that histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch are processed differently in the mouse brain, offering insights into the neural mechanisms underlying chronic itch sensitization.

Article.Title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
Article.Authors: Gong Q.; Lan H.; Zhao H.; Zhang W.; Li X.; Chen M.; Huang T.; Si J.; Huang H.; Zhao H.; Hu Y.; Yang X.; Wang J.; Yan X.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Systematic and precise regulation of coordination environments in single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains challenging due to thermodynamic constraints and kinetic traps. Herein, we report a thermodynamic-guided strategy to tailor the local coordination of Fe single atoms on CoWO 4 support by regulating oxygen chemical potential. Via fine-tuning hydrogen partial pressure during pyrolysis, a series of Fe 1 O x SACs is synthesized with well-defined Fe-O coordination numbers ranging from 3 to 6. Combining operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations, Fe 1 O 4 is identified as the optimal configuration for hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) electrosynthesis, which delivers balanced kinetics by moderating free water dissociation for *NH 3 generation and strengthening HCHO chemisorption via pronounced Fe 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization near the Fermi level. As a result, the Fe 1 O 4 SAC achieves a HMTA yield of 0.21 mmol h −1 cm −2 with 83.04% Faradaic efficiency at 1.75 V and stability over 200 h in a flow cell. This work establishes a universal thermodynamic approach for precise coordination engineering of single-atom electrocatalysts and provides a general paradigm for kinetically balancing complex multi-intermediate electrocatalytic systems.

Article.Title: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
Article.Authors: Xing A.; Ng H.; Lin J.; Ye Q.; Tong H.; Li Y.; Liang J.; Ma Y.; Jiang G.; Li K.
Article.Abstract: Relaxation of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions was followed by a global resurgence of respiratory infections, yet how accumulated population susceptibility interacts with environmental forcing and human mobility remains unclear. Here we analyse ~1.88 million clinical influenza tests from Macau (2010-2025) alongside meteorology, air quality, digital information-seeking, and independent surveillance and time-resolved viral genomes from Hong Kong, benchmarked against global surveillance data. Counterfactual inference indicates a post-pandemic excess in influenza activity consistent with immunity debt, mirroring global resurgence patterns, and an independently parameterised susceptible–exposed–infectious–recovered–susceptible model reproduces this excess (best-fit debt fraction 42%; approximate Bayesian computation posterior 58%, 95% uncertainty interval 32-77%). Susceptibility rises disproportionately in adults rather than children, whereas vaccination coverage in high-risk groups does not decline, arguing against reduced uptake as the driver. Time-varying models and convergent cross mapping reveal environmental decoupling, whereby high susceptibility weakens meteorological constraints and sustains influenza A transmission, and asymmetric suppression of influenza B. Spatiotemporal and phylogenetic evidence supports travel-linked reintroduction from ports of entry into dense neighbourhoods, and digital information-seeking shifts from lagging to leading clinical burden. These findings indicate a post-pandemic regime shift in influenza dynamics rather than a return to historical baselines, motivating adaptive, multi-source surveillance in high-density cities.

Article.Title: Epithelium stratifies via nucleation and growth induced by foam-geometric instability
Article.Authors: Fukamachi S.; Datta R.; Wuergezhen D.; Ichikawa T.; Yagasaki R.; Leeaw P.; Arai M.; Teranishi A.; Horiguchi S.; Omachi K.; Sada A.; Imayoshi I.; Kajiwara K.; Hiraiwa T.; Oshima M.; Fukuma T.; Fujiwara H.; Okuda S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Epithelial stratification, the transition from a monolayer to a multilayer structure, occurs across a wide range of phenomena. Recent studies have identified several cell behaviors as triggers, including junctional tension, cell density and geometry, and topological defects. However, how these factors drive stratification throughout the entire epithelium remains poorly understood. Here, we show that epithelial stratification proceeds through a nucleation-and-growth mechanism. Combining cell culture with three-dimensional vertex modeling, we demonstrate that multilayer origins emerge in a dispersed manner and expand across the epithelium through disordered intermediate states. This transition is induced by a mechanical instability inherent in the foam-like geometry of the epithelium. Moreover, the nucleation-growth concept applies to embryonic skin development and intestinal cancer transformation. These findings conceptualize epithelial stratification as a form of structural transition governed by foam mechanics, offering a physical perspective on various epithelial developments.

Article.Title: Sublevel-selective electron spin hyperpolarization of triplet radical pairs in metal–organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Hamachi T.; Huang Y.; Eckvahl H.; Carella A.; Peinkofer K.; Young R.; Krzyaniak M.; Ito T.; Kurashige Y.; Yabuki R.; Wasielewski M.; Yanai N.
Article.Abstract: Molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies because their electronic structures can be synthetically tailored and integrated into higher-order assemblies. Photogenerated radical pairs can exhibit spin hyperpolarization under ambient conditions, yet extending such spin dynamics from isolated molecules to structurally organized materials remains challenging. Here, we report a metal-organic framework that regulates the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within locally well-defined donor-acceptor arrangements. N,N'-di(4-pyridyl)-1,4,5,8-naphthalenetetracarboxdiimide is introduced into a zinc tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin-based framework. Dense donor-acceptor packing promotes efficient quenching of the porphyrin singlet excited state and selectively forms strongly coupled triplet radical pairs polarized in the zero-spin projection sublevel. These radical pairs exhibit narrow electron paramagnetic resonance signals and long spin-lattice relaxation times. Their spin-lattice relaxation dynamics persist in various guest solvents and vary with guest identity, demonstrating a route to chemically responsive spin materials based on porous, locally organized donor-acceptor frameworks.

Article.Title: Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS2
Article.Authors: Suzuki S.; Nakayama K.; Yanagizawa K.; Sugawara K.; Souma S.; Ozawa K.; Takano S.; Takahara R.; Hara T.; Wakabayashi Y.; Takahashi T.; Nojima T.; Ueno K.; Sato T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS 2 has long been considered a prime example of a Mott insulator driven by strong electron correlations. However, this view has been recently challenged by proposals which favor a band insulating state arising from interlayer dimerization. This ongoing debate opens a frontier in 1T-TaS 2 research focusing on stacking order, and raises a fundamental question with broad implications for two-dimensional materials: can electronic phases be engineered by actively tuning interlayer coupling? Here, using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that uniaxial strain drives 1T-TaS 2 from its insulating charge-density-wave phase into a stable metallic phase. This metallic phase, distinct from hydrostatic-pressure-induced or non-equilibrium hidden phases, emerges via a strain-induced rearrangement in the interlayer stacking of the Star-of-David charge order, effectively disrupting interlayer dimerization. Furthermore, the emergent metallic phase exhibits a significant quasiparticle mass renormalization, a hallmark of strong electron correlations, indicating its correlated nature and proximity to a Mott instability. This finding necessitates a re-evaluation of the interplay between structural and strong correlations in 1T-TaS 2 . The present results establish uniaxial strain as a powerful method for tuning the interlayer coupling, opening pathways for exploring quantum phases inaccessible under ambient conditions.

Article.Title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
Article.Authors: Cherrad N.; Foustoukos G.; Fernandez L.; Osorio-Forero A.; Buron J.; Eliasson N.; Emmenegger Y.; Milanese P.; Ferreira Morais J.; Mansuy-Aubert V.; Franken P.; Lüthi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Parasympathetic nervous system activity, vital for restorative sleep, is influenced by vagal sensory afferents, but how these shape brain-body correlates of sleep remains open. Here we combined vagal sensory neuron (VSN) stimulation in the mouse with EEG/EMG, heart rate, brain-body temperature, noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC) neuron population activity measures and in vitro synaptic physiology to investigate the effects of VSN activation on sleep-wake states. We show that chemogenetic VSN stimulation during the resting phase induced a non-rapid-eye-movement sleep (NREMS)-like state with enriched, but homeostatically regulated, low-frequency (0.75–4 Hz) EEG activity, yet suppressed REMS. Simultaneously, brain-body temperatures dropped while LC activity increased. The gradual recovery towards normal NREMS-REMS-cycles was accelerated by external warming, identifying cooling as key contributing factor. We conclude that VSN activation can promote brain-body correlates as a continuum of normal NREMS while engaging wake-promoting forebrain neuromodulation, revealing a coexistence of classically incompatible sleep- and wake-associated signatures.

Article.Title: Photonic-assisted ingenious agile non-periodic oscillator (PIANO)
Article.Authors: Hao T.; Yang T.; Cen Q.; Wang L.; Xiao S.; Li M.; Wang A.; Li W.; Hao P.; Steve Yao X.; Capmany J.; Zhu N.; Dai Y.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: The development of high-performance frequency-agile microwave signal generators has long been constrained by the inherent limitations of electronic technology. To overcome this challenge, researchers have increasingly turned to photonics, leveraging its high-frequency and broad-bandwidth capabilities. Here, we introduce and demonstrate a Photonic-assisted Ingenious Agile Non-periodic Oscillator (PIANO), which enables high-performance frequency-agile microwave signal generation with flexible frequency agility, ultra-low phase noise, rapid switching speed, and large time-bandwidth product (TBWP). The key innovation of PIANO lies in incorporating a dynamic frequency-shifting module into an optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) cavity, thereby extending the conventional delay-based OEO framework by decoupling frequency-agility behavior from the cavity-delay constraint. During experiments, PIANO successfully generated various flexible frequency-agile waveforms, with a frequency-switching time of 27 ns, phase noise as low as −134 dBc/Hz@10 kHz, and TBWP up to 1,440,000. This work offers a promising approach to high-performance frequency-agile microwave signal generation for applications such as radar and communication systems.

Article.Title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking

Article.Abstract: Cracking of polyolefins is a prerequisite for their selective conversion over microporous zeolites to value-added small molecules such as monocyclic aromatics. However, cracking and aromatization often proceed concurrently, creating an intrinsic accessibility-selectivity conflict that limits aromatic yield and productivity. This paper describes a strategy that temporally decouples polyolefin cracking from selective aromatization in one-pot with tandem catalysts. This strategy delivers an aromatic yield of ca. 60.3 wt% within 0.5 h at 380 °C from postconsumer polyolefins over 40 consecutive cycles, corresponding to an aromatic space-time yield of 11 g gcat −1 h −1 , more than twofold higher than reported values of ≤ 5 g gcat −1 h −1 . Article.Title: Failure of TSPO-dependent metabolic compensation marks the loss of mitochondrial bioenergetic adaptation in parkin-deficient neurons
Article.Authors: Cho J.; Cho S.; Kim E.; Jo M.; Choe J.; Lee S.; Hyeon D.; Kim T.; Chung C.; Kim M.; Lee Y.; Park H.; Lee W.; Hwang D.; Seo J.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neurons require mitochondrial bioenergetic flexibility to withstand chronic mitochondrial quality control failure, yet the compensatory safeguards that preserve mitochondrial functional output during neurodegenerative progression remain unclear. Substrate-specific mitochondrial respiration and ATP assays showed impaired pyruvate-supported bioenergetic capacity but preserved glutamate-supported bioenergetic capacity, supporting a transient glutamate-linked compensatory state before neurodegenerative deterioration. Article.Authors: Keomanee-Dizon K.; Clenman Y.; Duran A.; Ryabichko S.; Hansen P.; Borjigin T.; Thornton R.; Toettcher J.; McNamara H.

Article.Authors: Krätschmer I.; Hegemann L.; Pálsson G.; Hofmeister R.; Richmond A.; Hayward C.; Andreassen O.; Jugessur A.; Sønderby I.; Askelund A.; N/A N/A.; Metspalu A.; Milani L.; Esko T.; Mägi R.; Nelis M.; Hudjashov G.; Kutalik Z.; Marioni R.; Hardarson M.; Stefansson Ó.; Jónsson H.; Kharchenko P.; Stefánsson K.; Halldórsson B.

Article.Authors: Small C.; Kumar D.; Abbas A.; Sánchez Fructuoso A.; Yamanaga S.; Pérez González V.; Karakizlis H.; Nissen M.; Gyun Choe P.; Paloschi V.; Chadban S.; Hailemariam H.; Gerard C.; David M.; Descamps D.; Vandermeulen C.; Oluwayi K.; Hulstrøm V.; N/A N/A.

Article.Title: Percolation and site energy distribution jointly control Li+ transport in disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
Article.Authors: Liao J.; Li Z.; Chen H.; Xie Y.; Man Z.; Tan S.; Qu Y.; Zhao S.; Lun Z.; Hou T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Disordered rocksalt positive electrodes are promising candidates for high-energy batteries, yet their ion transport kinetics is constrained by an incomplete understanding of Li transport in disordered environments. We reveal a trade-off whereby increasing cation disorder enhances topological connectivity but concurrently broadens the site energy distribution, inducing a rugged energy landscape that suppresses overall diffusion. To reconcile these conflicting factors, we construct a design map spanning the full Li–Mn–Ti–O composition space, establishing a Li-site energy rectified percolation metric that transforms their interaction into a quantifiable descriptor. This framework enables the identification of Li 1.3 Mn 0.4 Ti 0.3 O 2 , which delivers a specific capacity of 294 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we demonstrate that inducing a phase transition toward a partially disordered spinel-like state simultaneously enhances percolation connectivity and narrows the energy landscape, achieving a specific capacity of 316 mAh g −1 . This work provides insights into the ion transport mechanisms in disordered electrode materials and offers practical design principles for battery systems.

Article.Title: Non-equilibrium resonance scattering in intramolecular charge transport drives conformational changes
Article.Authors: Park Y.; Kim T.; Baek J.; Park S.; Kim D.; Shin C.; Sam S.; Kim W.; Dongbang S.; Kim D.; Choi Y.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intramolecular charge transport is conventionally described as proceeding along a static ground-state potential, with the carrier acting as a passive probe of a fixed electronic landscape. Combined electrical and in situ structural measurements resolve a threshold-activated transition to a gauche-defect state coincident with the onset of orbital-mediated transport. We rationalize this coupling through a quantum resonance scattering framework in which accessible orbitals act as scattering potentials that transiently host the injected charge, depositing energy into nuclear motion with an efficiency set by molecule–electrode coupling and Franck–Condon overlap. The framework quantitatively reproduces the measured response and predicts the enhanced behavior of amide-containing junctions. Together, these results suggest that charge-transport–structure feedback can be understood in terms of microscopic parameters governing resonance-mediated energy transfer, and that these parameters may be tuned through chemical design.

Article.Title: Dynamic chlorine vacancies enable X-ray-specific afterglow
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Shang Y.; Zhao Q.; Li D.; Gao P.; Hao S.; Zhou J.; Yang C.
Article.Abstract: Afterglow luminescence in inorganic materials is conventionally attributed to pre-existing static defects that trap and gradually release charge carriers. Here we show that Bi 3+ doped Cs 2 ZrCl 6 crystals exhibit afterglow exclusively under X-ray excitation, with no such effect under ultraviolet illumination. We demonstrate that this behavior arises from the in-situ generation and self-healing of metastable chlorine vacancies (V Cl ) specifically driven by X-ray irradiation, directly correlating with afterglow kinetics. Advancing beyond previous vague attributions to Frenkel defects, our multimodal evidence unambiguously pinpoints V Cl as the operative defect species. This discovery challenges the paradigm that afterglow requires static pre-existing traps, establishing a dynamic mechanism where metastable defects are created by the probing radiation and gradually disappear when radiation is removed. We further manipulate the afterglow kinetic through Sn 4+ induced modulation of vacancy formation energy, extending the afterglow duration to multiple hours while maintaining a high light yield of 55670 photons MeV −1 and a low detection limit of 30.81 nGy air s −1 . Finally, we integrate these crystals into a flexible PDMS composite film for X-ray imaging, achieving a high spatial resolution of 23.6 lp mm −1 that enables high-fidelity imaging of curved objects via time-resolved readout. Our findings open an avenue for designing smart scintillators with programmable, radiation-specific responses, with implications for flexible radiography and beyond.

Article.Title: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Yu J.; Xu J.; Zhang Y.; Chen H.; Ho M.; Kam K.; Young A.; Ip P.; Pang C.; Tham C.; Yam J.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early-life nutritional conditions may influence biological aging and age-related health, but the long-term associations of early exposure to sugar rationing remain unclear. Here we investigate the associations of early-life exposure to sugar rationing with biological aging and age-related diseases among 54,201 participants in the UK Biobank, taking advantage of the abrupt end of post-war sugar rationing as a natural experiment. Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life is associated with lower biological age acceleration, with stronger associations observed among participants with longer exposure durations. Article.Authors: Tae H.; Choe Y.; Jiang D.; Gnanasekaran L.; Park S.; Zhu J.; Bazan G.; Zhdanov V.; Parikh A.; Cho N.

We hypothesize that crystallite motilities arise from local cholesterol depletion in the underlying bilayer, generating gradients in composition, rigidity, and thus adhesion, which induce directional forces analogous to those involved in haptotaxis and/or durotaxis. Article.Title: LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish luteal cell identity

Article.Title: A hierarchical metabolic flux orchestrates cell cycle transitions in bacteria

Article.Abstract: Soil microbial activity, and the balance of anabolic (carbon assimilating) and catabolic (CO 2 -releasing) processes, control the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes.
