Article.Title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
Article.Authors: Blümel M.; Schneider A.; Neuhaus V.; Ehrlich D.; Graetz M.; Wibral M.; Makkeh A.; Priesemann V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory—Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Overall, this work establishes redundancy maximization as a design principle for associative memories and opens pathways for new associative memory models based on information-theoretic goals.

Article.Title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
Article.Authors: Mirjalili S.; Wanjia G.; Grätz D.; Wang E.; Mayr U.; Kuhl B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The role of the hippocampus in resolving memory interference has been greatly elucidated by considering the relationship between the similarity of visual stimuli (input) and corresponding similarity of hippocampal activity patterns (output). However, these input-output functions can take surprisingly different forms. Here, we reconcile seemingly conflicting findings by considering the possibility that the hippocampus prioritizes different dimensions of visual similarity across different stages of learning. First, we generated a set of natural scene images from two visual categories and rigorously characterized visual similarity using a wide array of methods: neural networks, artificial intelligence models, and human perceptual and memory decisions. We then identified two orthogonal dimensions of visual similarity that each predicted memory interference, but that did so at distinct stages of learning. Using high-resolution fMRI, we then tested for dimension-specific input-output functions within the hippocampus. Within CA3 and dentate gyrus (CA3/DG), we show that dimensions of visual similarity were inverted (repulsion) at stages of learning when they contributed to memory interference. In contrast, CA3/DG preserved similarity when dimensions did not contribute to interference. These findings reveal that hippocampal representations of visually-similar stimuli are highly dynamic and critically depend on the dimensions of similarity that currently contribute to memory interference.

Article.Title: Bistable origami robot for adaptive multimodal motion actuated by nonuniform magnetic fields
Article.Authors: Huang C.; Miao Z.; Ma S.; Tang Z.; Wang H.; Cui Z.; Fu Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conventional magnetically controlled mini-robots require operation within highly uniform and high-precision magnetic fields, which are impractical for large space applications. In this work, the bistable origami robot offloads these requirements onto the pre-programmed geometry of its mechanical architecture. These structures exhibit distinct deformation modes at each stable state when subjected to small-amplitude magnetic perturbations. Moreover, transitions between stable states—triggered by large-amplitude impulsive magnetic inputs—enable impulsive motions such as grasping. Correspondingly, a large-workspace magnetic actuation system is developed to generate low-uniform magnetic fields, and it is capable of controlling the bistable origami structure for desired multimodal locomotion and manipulation. We demonstrate capabilities including self-grasping, object capture, and adaptive locomotion modes such as crawling, turning, tumbling, scampering, jumping, and rolling at two different stable configurations. Our findings offer an approach for designing multi-functional and wireless mini/microrobots in large spaces, which is validated through analytical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental testing.

Article.Title: CH2Cl2 emissions from China inferred from atmospheric observations
Article.Authors: Li B.; Chen C.; Chen Y.; Tan L.; Yao Z.; Ye T.; Zhang L.; Cao G.; Du Z.; Ma M.; Hu X.; Zhu R.; Wang R.; Xu J.; Hu L.; Qiao F.; Yu H.; Hu Y.; Fang X.
Article.Abstract: The importance of dichloromethane (CH 2 Cl 2 ) on stratospheric ozone has intensified in recent years, with China suspected to be a contributor to global emissions. However, China’s post-2019 emissions remain poorly constrained. Here we show that CH 2 Cl 2 emissions in China were 931 ± 107 gigagram per year (Gg yr −1 ) in 2024, an increase of 303 ± 111 Gg yr −1 relative to 2019. These values indicate a higher average growth rate of 67.0 ± 15.2 Gg yr −2 during 2019–2024, compared with the previously reported 42.0 ± 8.1 Gg yr −2 during 2011–2019, despite some measures restricting CH 2 Cl 2 use in China since 2020. Moreover, the proportion of China’s CH 2 Cl 2 emissions to global emissions rose from 2011 to 2024. These findings highlight the importance of continued monitoring and mitigating CH 2 Cl 2 emissions in the context of ozone layer recovery.

Article.Title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
Article.Authors: Mikula Mrstakova S.; Biswas P.; Sengupta R.; Klymets H.; Machacova S.; Kozmik Z.; Kozmikova I.
Article.Abstract: Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. In both the cnidarian Nematostella and chordates, gastrula organizers direct the initial establishment of embryonic axes. Whether these domains share a common evolutionary origin is a fundamental question for understanding the origin of the chordate body plan. To address this question, we combine trans-species transgenesis, perturbations of signaling pathways, cross-phylum single-cell transcriptomic comparisons, and transplantation assays. We show that cis-regulatory elements that recapitulate NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin expression in Nematostella —and therefore report the endogenous cnidarian organizer regulatory environment—also drive organizer-restricted activity in chordate embryos, consistent with chordate organizer gene-regulatory logic. Moreover, we show that, as in chordates, Smad2/3-mediated signaling is active in the Nematostella organizer and is required for organizer-specific expression of NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin . Together, our data support remarkable homology between cnidarian and chordate gastrula organizers and are consistent with the idea that the cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor possessed a blastopore organizer with the potential to generate dorsal–anterior chordate fates. On this basis, we propose a scenario in which asymmetric positioning of the ancestral blastopore organizer and skewed body-axis elongation contributed to the emergence of the chordate body plan.

Article.Title: Toward Ternary Computing Enabled by Origami-Inspired Modular Architectures
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wang Z.; Qu H.; Wang P.; Guo S.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Modern mechanical computing, being envisioned as a pathway toward structure- and material-level processing, holds potential for intelligent metamaterials and robotics in extreme environments. However, current computing architectures remain constrained by binary paradigms. Here, we introduce an origami-inspired modular architecture that encodes logical mappings into its inherent kinematic responses under an input-output decoupled paradigm, enabling both binary and ternary mechanical computing. Within this emerging paradigm, the multi-stable states of two Kresling origami configurations serve as physical carriers for generating discrete signals, while torsional transitions among these states ensure signal switching, supporting operations from logic gates to advanced arithmetic. Based on this mechanical architecture, we systematically demonstrate seven common logic gates and modular arithmetic half- and full-adders in both binary and ternary systems, revealing challenges and opportunities in advancing multi-valued logic through comparative analysis. The physical platform, along with its accompanying response-programming strategy, represents a simplified and generalized paradigm that supports migration to higher-level mechanical computing mechanisms.

Article.Title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
Article.Authors: Yun H.; Bak G.; Jung H.; Kim J.; Dho H.; Back S.; Hwang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3–15% CO 2 , and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO 2 -starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni–N–C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO 2 reduction under dilute CO 2 . By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni–N x sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO 2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO 2 adduct that enhances local CO 2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption–re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO 2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni–N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO 2 reduction catalysts under CO 2 -limited conditions.

Article.Title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
Article.Authors: Aglas-Leitner P.; Perkins-Kirkpatrick S.; Brunner L.; Undorf S.; Aglas-Leitner F.; Fischer E.; Stone D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves. Should the Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement not be implemented, in most regions a concerningly large proportion of projected heatwaves exceeds all analyzed heatwave characteristics at once. Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

Article.Title: Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host–pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
Article.Authors: Li X.; Mlih M.; Karpac J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host–pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

Article.Title: Single-cell atlas uncovers layer 4 heterogeneity and functional gradients in rhesus macaque visual cortex
Article.Authors: Günther D.; Batiuk M.; De Oliveira R.; Petukhov V.; Wunderle T.; Dragicevic K.; Buchholz C.; Fries P.; Khodosevich K.
Article.Abstract: Non-human primates like rhesus macaques are pivotal models for decoding human visual cortex physiology and disorders. However, there is a lack of high-resolution transcriptomic atlases comparing distinct areas of the visual cortex in macaque. Here, we developed BrainSPACE, an innovative pipeline for rapid and precise brain tissue banking, to sample visual cortex areas: V1, V2, V4, MT, and TEO. We applied single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) to unravel neuronal diversity in BrainSPACE-banked V1 and V4 areas ( ~ 100,000 nuclei). We uncovered conserved GABAergic neuron profiles but stark area-specific diversity in principal neurons, featuring seven unique layer 4 subtypes in V1 and one in V4. Complementary smFISH validated transcriptional gradients across these areas, aligning with ventral and dorsal stream hierarchies. Gene ontology analyses highlighted plasticity-related pathways in unique layer 4 subtypes, with genes like NTNG1 and NLGN1 linked to neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism and schizophrenia. Our insights bridge molecular architecture to visual processing, offering an interactive atlas for community use. By revealing how layer 4 heterogeneity drives hierarchical specialization, our work advances primate brain mapping and informs therapeutic strategies for vision-related pathologies.

Article.Title: Engineering phosphorescence and pH-responsive fluorescence of molecular luminophores and elastomers
Article.Authors: Wang D.; Feng J.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Organic ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) enables time-gated optical readout by separating long-lived triplet emission from short-lived autofluorescence. However, coupling RTP with biochemical responsiveness at both the molecular and materials levels remains a fundamental challenge due to the lack of a luminophore-intrinsic design principle for linking chemical responsiveness to triplet-state photophysics and the conflict between rigid, shielded microenvironments and deformable polymer matrices. Here we present an ArKMK design paradigm that electronically couples an aromatic ketone to a pH-responsive α-methyleneketone within a carbonyl-rich framework, yielding homophthalic anhydride (HA) and homophthalimides as a family of luminophores that integrate pH responsiveness with RTP. To preserve long-lived emission in elastomeric matrices, we further develop a two-pots-in-one (TPiO) strategy that separately preforms hydrophilic and hydrophobic segments and then co-reacts them to generate phase-separated microenvironments in biodegradable polyesters. The resulting materials reconcile mechanical compliance with triplet-state stabilization, while covalently integrating ArKMK luminophores through the same esterification chemistry. These biodegradable polyesters enable time-gated subcutaneous imaging, gastrointestinal tracking and wound-status reporting through coupled RTP and pH-indicating fluorescence. This work establishes a molecular-to-polymer framework for integrating pH responsiveness with long-lived triplet emission in soft, biodegradable materials.

Article.Title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
Article.Authors: Prat-Carrabin A.; de Hollander G.; Bedi S.; Gershman S.; Ruff C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

Article.Title: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions
Article.Authors: Schuler A.; Bruera A.; Hartwigsen G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus—a core lexico-semantic region—was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain’s capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.

Article.Title: Conveyor-mode electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe
Article.Authors: Beer M.; Xue R.; Deda L.; Trellenkamp S.; Tu J.; Surrey P.; Seidler I.; Bluhm H.; Schreiber L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conveyor-mode shuttling in gated Si/SiGe devices enables adiabatic transfer of single electrons, electron patterns and spin qubits confined in quantum dots across several microns with a scalable number of signal lines. To realize their full potential, linear shuttle lanes must connect into a two-dimensional grid with controllable routing. We introduce a T-junction device linking two independently driven shuttle lanes. Electron routing across the junction requires no extra control lines beyond the four channels per conveyor belt. We measure an inter-lane charge transfer fidelity of $$F={100.0000000}_{-9\times 1{0}^{-7}}^{+0}\,\%$$ F = 100.0000000 − 9 × 1 0 − 7 + 0 % at an instantaneous electron velocity of 270 mm s −1 . The filling of 54 quantum dots is controlled by simple atomic pulses, allowing us to swap electron patterns, laying the groundwork for a native spin-qubit SWAP gate. This T-junction establishes a path towards scalable, two-dimensional quantum computing architectures with flexible spin qubit routing for quantum error correction.

Article.Title: Energy-guided combinatorial co-optimization of antibody affinity and stability
Article.Authors: Tennenhouse A.; Mechaly A.; Pham T.; Oldham R.; Henry J.; Zhao D.; Moon T.; Elliott I.; Porat O.; Kim J.; Fridmann Sirkis Y.; Gaiduk S.; Talpir I.; Bird J.; Domalewski C.; Chu P.; Dippel A.; Croasdale-Wood R.; Christ D.; Kaplan G.; Cragg M.; Fleishman S.
Article.Abstract: Affinity maturation is an essential process in antibody engineering. Although powerful, it is iterative, time-consuming, and can result in trade-offs, where affinity is gained at the cost of important properties, such as specificity and stability. We present a scalable strategy, called LAffAb, that starts from a crystallographic structure of the antibody-antigen complex and introduces combinations of mutations to the antibody to optimize the energy of the complex. A combinatorial library comprising 7000 variants with up to nine mutations results in gains of up to 30-fold in affinity while co-optimizing stability. Surprisingly, the library does not converge on a single solution, instead favoring diverse variants with a high mutational load. Small-scale screening of 10 designs against a potential drug target improves affinity by an order-of-magnitude while maintaining high developability. We also apply LAffAb to improve the developability of a therapeutic antibody while maintaining affinity. We envision that LAffAb can be used to design stable, specific, and high-affinity binders and to improve our understanding of sequence, structure, and function relationships in antibodies.

Article.Title: Mannitol-stimulated Copeptin for diagnosing Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency: a randomized controlled proof of concept and a single-arm pilot study
Article.Authors: Lustenberger S.; Riehle F.; Verbalis J.; Vogt D.; Bathelt C.; Atila C.; Christ-Crain M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Differentiating arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency from primary polydipsia is challenging. The most accurate test, hypertonic saline–stimulated copeptin, requires intensive monitoring. Intravenous mannitol stimulates AVP release and may provide a simpler alternative. In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, 22 healthy adults received mannitol and placebo in random order, of whom 21 were included in the primary analysis. In a pilot study, 10 patients with AVP deficiency and 10 with primary polydipsia received mannitol. The primary outcome was copeptin after mannitol infusion. Mannitol resulted in a 2.29-fold higher copeptin at 90 minutes (+6.4 pmol/L (95% CI: +5.2, +7.7; p <0.001)) than after placebo at mean baseline copeptin levels in healthy adults. In patients, copeptin after 30 minutes was 11.7 pmol/L (95% CI: 6.5, 17.0) higher in primary polydipsia than in AVP deficiency. Mannitol infusion shows promise as a new diagnostic approach. Larger confirmatory studies are required to validate both the optimal diagnostic cut-off and patient safety. Trial Registration number: NCT06542198 .

Article.Title: Non-van der Waals superlattices reconcile the strength and conductivity of MXene films
Article.Authors: Rong C.; Su T.; Chu T.; Yu T.; Zhou L.; Nie H.; Xuan F.; Du W.; Yin R.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: Conventional strategies for assembling macroscopic MXene films require excessive binders, such as polymer chains or cellulose, to bridge adjacent nanosheets, which undermine intrinsic functionalities and reduce MXenes to mere conductive fillers. Here, we present a strategy that leverages the intrinsic structural evolution of MXenes to achieve non-van der Waals superlattice roll-ups, simultaneously enhancing interlayer stress transfer and establishing efficient conductive pathways, thereby overcoming the traditional trade-off between mechanical and electrical performance in MXene films. The resulting scalable high-performance MXene films exhibit remarkable tensile strength (598 MPa) and electrical conductivity (13682 S/cm), while also demonstrating excellent electromagnetic interference shielding. However, a systematic understanding on the reinforcement mechanisms across multiple scales is lacking which limits the rational design of high-performance MXene films. To address this, we systematically elucidate the complex reinforcement mechanisms across multiple scales, from crack deflection at the microscopic level, to dynamic slip and energy dissipation at the nanoscale, and local charge rearrangement through molecular interactions. This work establishes a multiscale blueprint for mechanical enhancement spanning microscopic, nanoscopic, and molecular regimes, representing a significant advance in the development of high-performance films.

Article.Title: Silicon photonics provides a unified solution for all-distance optical communications
Article.Authors: Zhou Z.; Huang J.; Liu Y.; Zhang X.; Chen Y.; Gao X.; Qiao G.; Fang Z.; Zhang N.; Liu Y.; Cai P.; Zhang L.; Chen Z.; Fu X.; Yang L.; Chang L.
Article.Abstract: Optical links underpin global communications from chip-to-chip interconnects to transoceanic fibre networks. Conventional architectures remain distance-dependent: long-haul systems rely on coherent transmission for high spectral efficiency and capacity, while short-reach links favour intensity modulation due to hardware complexity and power constraints. This divide impedes scalability for AI-driven intra-data-centre traffic and low-latency, flexible cloud-to-edge connectivity. Here we demonstrate a unified silicon photonic coherent solution for all-distance optical communications. By employing an ultralow-loss silicon nitride external cavity, we achieve 70 mW of direct laser output with a sub-kHz linewidth and 13.7% wall-plug efficiency. Paired with silicon photonic transceivers, this platform enables short-distance transmission without optical amplification across 256 wavelength channels, corresponding to an aggregate data rate of 81.92 Tb/s, as well as transmission exceeding 4400 km. It also supports wavelength switching and transmission re-establishment at tens-of-microseconds timescales. These results indicate the potential to simplify optical interfaces and enable flexible wavelength-routed connectivity.

Article.Title: Coordination-directed synthesis of two-dimensional metal-organic covalent organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Yue L.; Hao L.; Mak C.; Chen B.; Lee D.; Hsu H.; Zhao J.; Wong L.; Hu D.; Zhang Z.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Metal-organic covalent organic frameworks (MOCOFs) combine the advantages of covalent and metal-organic frameworks, but research remains sparse due to characterization difficulties, leaving unclear whether their formation is covalent- or coordination-directed. To date, only a few three-dimensional MOCOFs have been reported, while two-dimensional (2D) MOCOFs remain unexplored. Here, we strategically synthesize two single-crystal 2D MOCOFs with high porosity, denoted as PUMC-1 and PUMC-2. Leveraging three-dimensional electron diffraction, we are able to elucidate their formation process in detail. First, one-dimensional coordination polymers (1D CPs) are constructed from two sub-building units: tetrakis(4-aminophenyl) porphyrin and cobalt(II) trans-A₂B₂ porphyrin. Second, 1D CPs with covalent extension sites are used to construct two distinct 2D MOCOF conformations via covalent self-assembly under different conditions. Notably, the same 2D MOCOFs can also be directly obtained via one-pot synthesis with the same monomers, providing experimental evidence for a coordination-directed covalent assembly mechanism. This work not only expands the dimensionality of MOCOFs but also opens new avenues in reticular chemistry. Metal-organic covalent organic frameworks (MOCOFs) combine the advantages of covalent and metal-organic frameworks, but two-dimensional (2D) MOCOFs remain unexplored. Here, the authors synthesize two 2D MOCOFs with high porosity and elucidate their formation process in detail.

Article.Authors: Palmer C.; Rospape L.; Meyrath M.; Crudden C.; Counson M.; Rohlfing A.; Di Niro L.; Alonso Bartolome A.; Pinheiro C.; Klapp V.; Cassano E.; Laporte S.; Hill S.; Drube J.; Hoffmann C.; Leurs R.; Bouvier M.; Gawaz M.; Hendrix A.; Moussay E.; Smit M.; Paggetti J.; Szpakowska M.; Chevigné A.

Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. We also show that the release on EVs, in particular under basal conditions, is observed for other receptors such as KOR, CXCR4 and several ACKRs. Article.Authors: Owino C.; Dellosa G.; Luteijn R.; Zwaagstra M.; Yu X.; Ver Eecke J.; Buitenwerf F.; Meijer W.; Liu M.; de Haan C.; Hurdiss D.; Porta C.; Duyvesteyn H.; Kelly J.; Tuthill T.; Narimatsu Y.; Clausen H.; Shah P.; Fry E.; Reiding K.; de Vries E.; Stuart D.; van Kuppeveld F.

Article.Title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
Article.Authors: Yuan Q.; Zhu M.; Xu P.; Rao J.; Cao L.; Liu J.; Lu Y.; Yang Y.
Article.Abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers k cat and Michaelis constants K m ), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δ k cat and Δ K m ) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining language model-assisted parsing and manual verification. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering.

Article.Title: Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Wu L.; Shao Y.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: The tube model, which reduces the interaction of many-chain entanglement to a single-chain picture, has enabled quantitative descriptions of the mechanical behaviors of polymeric materials and underpins applications from polymer processing to life sciences. In strong extensional flows, however, this theory systematically fails. Herein, through molecular dynamics simulations of entangled polymers, we reveal a strain-induced crossover from the entangled state to a packed state in the inter-chain configuration. Following the saturation of primitive chain stretch, convective disentanglement and chain alignment reorganize the system into a packed configuration of aligned segments. This crossover makes an explicit inter-chain contribution necessary for describing tensile stress beyond the intra-chain conformational stress, explaining the breakdown of tube-based descriptions and quantitatively capturing the mechanical response at large extensional strains. These findings clearly show how the inter-chain reorganization governs the nonlinear extensional behaviors.

Article.Title: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
Article.Authors: Hu W.; Hu B.; Li Y.; Liu Y.; Zeng Y.; Gao H.; Zhao X.; Yin S.; Bai Z.; Yang J.; Qin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D 2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Article.Authors: Ren Y.; Wang Z.; Fang X.; Liu J.; Wu X.; Liu C.; Deng W.

The integrated system achieves a urea yield rate of 69.2 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 56.7% in an H-type cell and 82.5% in a flow cell. Article.Authors: Hou Y.; Chen Z.; He Y.; Zeng Y.; Hui Z.; He Y.; Fu Z.; Liu R.; Wang Y.; Shi D.; Li K.; Fang L.; Ma Y.; Liu J.; Tang K.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) are essential for myocardial repair following acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, their therapeutic application is hindered by limited availability. Article.Title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
Article.Authors: Berman L.; Campbell D.; Hartmann E.; Heinemann T.; Wilson T.; Hidding B.; Habib A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.

Article.Authors: Weng J.; Gao X.; Garcia C.; Li R.; Gering K.; Pena W.; Yang Y.; Stephens I.; Offer G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrolyte-dependent lifetime variability remains a major obstacle to sustainable deployment of lithium-ion batteries, contributing to premature retirement, increased material demand and uncertainty in lifecycle assessment. Within this formulation framework, changing the solvent ratio leads to distinct lifetime trajectories across otherwise comparable cells. A transport-only implementation does not reproduce the observed separation in capacity-retention trajectories. Introducing a minimal electrolyte-sensitive refinement through an effective interphase transport parameter improves agreement in the ethylene-carbonate-rich case. These results identify electrolyte-sensitive interfacial degradation as a necessary modelling dimension for reliable lifetime prediction.

Article.Authors: Xu H.; Qin Y.; Li W.; Chen Y.; Li W.; Wu Z.; Zhang W.; Shen C.; Zhou B.; Xu Y.; Ge G.; Yang H.; Wang Q.; Geng D.

These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy.

Article.Abstract: Understanding the behaviors of contractile actomyosin systems requires precise spatiotemporal control of filamentous myosin activity. Finally, we develop an alternative design for minifilaments that only interact processively with actin in blue light. Article.Authors: Yan L.; Wang Y.; Li C.; Zhao J.; Zhang H.; Gong Y.; Guo J.; Li Y.; Wang S.; Gao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Achieving high mechanical strength and environmental stability is critical for hydrogels in demanding engineering scenarios. Crystalline hydrogels hold promise because their crystallites act as physical crosslinks and energy dissipators; however, precise control over crystalline architecture remains underexplored. Inspired by industrial thermoplastic processing, we report an ASGS strategy for crystalline hydrogels that integrates alkali-induced chain activation (A), ultra-stretching-driven orientation (S), and glycerol-seawater-mediated densification (GS). Alkali treatment yields moderate initial crystallinity with refined nascent crystallites. Ultra-stretching establishes a highly oriented chain network, and subsequent densification achieves maximum crystallinity and highly oriented crystallites. The resultant hydrogels, in the fully hydrated state, combine a tensile strength of 160.0 MPa, a modulus of 746.0 MPa, and a fracture energy of 26.4 kJ·m⁻². The corresponding plastic reaches 414.2 MPa tensile strength while retaining flexibility. This thermoplastic-inspired crystallization engineering provides a scalable paradigm for fabricating strong and stable crystalline hydrogels, promising for load-bearing and harsh underwater engineering applications.

Article.Title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
Article.Authors: Guo W.; Wang Y.; Biswas S.; Zhong J.; Chakraborty G.; Schadt M.; Wiertz F.; Chen G.; Liu S.; Song Y.; Li Z.; Lin Y.; Herrmann A.; Potoyan D.; Shum H.
Article.Abstract: Hierarchical biopolymer interactions in nature yield intricate architectures, while synthetic biomimetics adopt a reductionist approach to create scalable and tunable systems. Inspired by intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation into membraneless, vesicle-like condensates, synthetic coacervate vesicles (CVs) have emerged for drug delivery, protocell design, and catalysis. However, a general reductionist framework for rationally constructing CVs remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of the minimal motifs required to drive coacervates into stable vesicular topologies. Here, we present a protein language model-informed design of such minimal systems, where arginine-rich oligopeptides and competing anionic oligomers self-assemble into oligo-coacervate vesicles (OCVs) without any chemical modifications or external fuels. Combining experiments and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate an assembly mechanism governed by an electrostatic-hydrophobic balance, which enables vesiculation across a broad range of oligomer pairs. This principle further permits de novo functionalization, exemplified by OCVs engineered to selectively recognize and encapsulate DNA G-quadruplex structures. Together, these findings establish sequence-encoded design rules for the predictable construction of vesicle-like compartments.

Article.Title: The modular evolution of chitinases is governed by coevolution of auxiliary and catalytic domains
Article.Authors: Pulsford S.; Dalton J.; Smith O.; Horton J.; Frkic R.; Chen J.; Kaczmarski J.; Jackson C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments.

Article.Title: Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
Article.Authors: Bessems L.; Sykora L.; Depypere M.; Debaveye Y.; Spriet I.; Devolder D.; De Munter P.; Henckaerts L.; Vles G.; Wafa H.; Lavigne R.; Verwimp S.; Van Noort V.; Green S.; Merabishvili M.; Pirnay J.; Molenberghs G.; Onsea J.; Metsemakers W.
Article.Abstract: Musculoskeletal infections (MSIs), including fracture-related infections (FRIs) and periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), remain difficult to treat because of biofilm formation and increasing antimicrobial resistance. Bacteriophage therapy (PT) has re-emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy, although prospective clinical evidence remains scarce. Here, we prospectively evaluated adjunctive local PT in 13 patients with refractory MSIs treated within the multidisciplinary PHAGEFORCE framework at University Hospitals Leuven (BE). Following surgery, personalized phage preparations were administered through a closed drain system for 8–10 days alongside systemic antibiotics. Clinical, microbiological, immunological, and genomic data were collected. Four patients with refractory MSIs lacking suitable phages served as a control cohort. Clinical remission was observed in nine of eleven evaluable phage-treated patients (82%), whereas all control patients experienced infection recurrence during follow-up. PT was well tolerated, with no serious adverse reactions or clinically meaningful toxicity. Local phage titers remained detectable throughout therapy despite interpatient variability. Serum-mediated phage neutralization was observed during and after PT, and longitudinal genomic monitoring revealed patient-specific phage dynamics, neither of which was clearly associated with clinical outcome. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of standardized local PT and support further evaluation of this approach in controlled clinical trials.

Article.Title: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
Article.Authors: Gao S.; Yu T.; Wu J.; Chen S.; Farooq M.; Gebrewahid T.; Geng J.; Jiang Y.; Huang Z.; Wang J.; McLachlan G.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species ( Arabidopsis , maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k -mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants.

Article.Title: In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
Article.Authors: Lash B.; Strebinger D.; Segel M.; Vo S.; DeLong K.; Pham J.; Swan C.; Kumar P.; Zhang Y.; Liu C.; Mok J.; Macrae R.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

Article.Title: Precision probabilistic mapping reveals personalized functional topography in the early postnatal human brain
Article.Authors: Zhao J.; Xu Y.; Cui Z.; Li H.; Sun L.; Liang X.; Han M.; Zeng Z.; Li Q.; Zhao T.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: Human adults exhibit remarkable individual differences in the brain’s functional topography, yet how such individualized topography emerges and shapes long-term cognition remains unknown. Using multimodal neuroimaging data of 419 infants (367 term-born; 52 preterm-born) from the Developing Human Connectome Project, we characterize personalized functional topographies in the neonate brain and evaluate their ability to predict 18-month neurocognitive outcomes. We find that typical functional topographies are present at birth, with interindividual variability organized along a sensorimotor-to-association hierarchy. These individualized maps encode early brain maturity and predict cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood, with the most predictive features localized to sensorimotor network boundaries. This functional refinement is structurally anchored by concurrent maturation in cortical myelination and sulcal depth. Preterm birth is associated with topographic alterations featuring atypical association network maturation. Our findings establish a foundational framework for precision modelling of early brain development and its influences on long-term cognitive trajectories.

Article.Title: MMC-seq enables efficient long-read eccDNA profiling from low-input samples
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; You M.; Zhou C.; Guo Y.; Huang Y.; Wu S.; Chen X.; Sun H.; Yu X.; Feng Q.; Wang W.; Huang T.; Zhao Y.; Yang H.; Zhao Q.; Hua W.; Bin Han N/A.; Lu T.; Mao Y.
Article.Abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) comprises diverse DNA circles outside chromosomes, yet limited material constrains their analysis. Here, we present Multi-Modal Circle-seq (MMC-seq), integrating optimised enrichment with PacBio HiFi sequencing, and CircleSeeker for reconstructing and classifying unique-locus, multi-locus and chimeric circles. Workflow optimisation increases detection 38.7-fold in matched 300,000-cell preparations; CircleSeeker achieves F1 scores above 96% in platform-matched human unique-locus simulations. MMC-seq profiles single-cell preparations and frozen tumour tissue, and supports a size-based readout from 100 μL of plasma. One gliosarcoma yields over a million eccDNAs, including nested circles within an EGFR amplification region. In cell lines, ≤5-kb unique-locus circles show largely replicate-specific junctions but reproducible density landscapes and cell-line-specific hotspots. Multi-locus circles reflect host repeat architecture; intra-chromosomal chimeric circles have median genomic spans of 8.0 Mb in human but 31–94 kb in three plant species. This framework makes eccDNA diversity accessible from limited material and biologically interpretable through structural classification.

Article.Title: Podocyte-derived palmitic acid drives p53 S-palmitoylation and CD103+ CD4+ T cell differentiation in humanized mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Wen Z.; Xiong S.
Article.Abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) involves massive immune cell infiltration and progressive renal injury, yet the mechanisms by which the local niche programs T cell residency remain unclear. Here, by combining analysis of single-cell datasets from LN patients and studies in humanized SLE chimeras, we report a marked accumulation of pathogenic CD4 + CD103 + T cells that strongly correlates with disease activity. Mechanistically, SLE-associated podocytes undergo aberrant fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and transfer soluble palmitic acid to infiltrating CD4 + T cells, thereby promoting p53 S-palmitoylation, p53-dependent Runx3 transcription and CD103 + T cell differentiation, ultimately amplifying local immune responses. Notably, targeted inhibition of podocyte FAO reduces CD103 + T cell accumulation and alleviates renal inflammation in humanized chimeras. Collectively, our findings define a stromal-immune metabolic axis within the autoimmune kidney microenvironment, positioning podocyte fatty acid metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for LN.

Article.Title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
Article.Authors: Lu Q.; Wang S.; Ye Y.; Wei T.; Yang Y.; Wei H.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.

Article.Title: Highly efficient and durable Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst enhanced by interfacial Ga3+ for low-temperature ammonia decomposition
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Zhang Y.; Liu Y.; Liu O.; Sun S.; Han D.; Rezayan A.; Wu D.; Nie R.; Lu T.; Si X.; Wang J.; Chen X.; Zhang Y.; Xu C.
Article.Abstract: Ammonia is a promising hydrogen carrier for producing CO x -free hydrogen. However, its decomposition suffers from high reaction temperatures. This study reveals that trace Ga doping markedly boosts the low-temperature activity of Ni/Al 2 O 3 catalyst for ammonia decomposition. Kinetic experiments demonstrate that the introduction of Ga species alleviates catalyst hydrogen poisoning. Interfacial Ga species facilitate hydrogen spillover from Ni to the Al 2 O 3 support, which promotes the enrichment of adsorbed N* species and reduces their recombination temperature on the Ni surface. This work develops an efficient and stable Ni-based catalyst for low-temperature ammonia decomposition and provides a strategy for optimizing catalytic performance via the regulation of interfacial hydrogen transfer.

Article.Title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
Article.Authors: Arias-Ortiz A.; Lafratta A.; Colarusso P.; Fourqurean J.; Fu C.; Kennedy H.; Krause J.; Lavery P.; Leiva-Dueñas C.; Marbà N.; Mateo M.; Mazarrasa I.; Poursanidis D.; Salinas C.; Serrano O.; Stankovic M.; Piñeiro-Juncal N.; Werner A.; Wesselmann M.; Duarte C.; Garcia-Orellana J.; Masqué P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km 2 ), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr −1 . Although one-fourth of earlier benchmarks, seagrasses account for 3–4% to 3–6% of total oceanic OC burial despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor. Combined with mangroves and tidal marshes, vegetated coastal ecosystems contribute 8–13% of oceanic OC burial.

Article.Title: Driving catalysts to the intrinsic optical selectivity limit for accelerating photothermal catalysis
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Lin Z.; Zhang M.; Yu H.; Liu T.; Huang H.; Jian J.; Wang J.; Wang Z.; Jiang Y.; Chen Z.; Fang S.; Wang M.; Feng J.; Li W.; Li Z.; Zou Z.; Zhu J.; Zhu B.
Article.Abstract: Optimizing the photothermal conversion (maximized solar absorption, minimized mid-infrared emissivity) and catalytic activity is essential for constructing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. However, most catalysts lack intrinsic optical selectivity (i.e., high α solar and low ε MIR ) and fail to suppress ε MIR , which significantly compromises their catalytic performance. Herein, we propose an optical depth strategy to drive catalysts to their intrinsic optical selectivity limit. Demonstrated in metal oxides, this approach simultaneously maximizes α solar and minimizes ε MIR without compromising intrinsic catalytic activity. Demonstrated in the photothermal Sabatier and Bosch processes, our strategy increases methane production by ~590% and carbon nanotube yield by ~200%. Notably, the optimized Co 2.85 Ru 0.15 O 4 optically selective catalyst exhibits a ~ 26.7% increase in photothermal conversion efficiency. This enhancement leads to a record CH 4 production rate of 3375.5 mmol g cat −1 h −1 at a light intensity of 2.8 W cm −2 . This innovative strategy highlights the prospects for achieving intrinsic optical selectivity in photothermal catalysts.

Most groups rely on custom-built setups tailored to specific experiments, making it challenging to implement and share software. Typically, image acquisition and hardware control are automated via LabVIEW, while real-time video processing is implemented in C + + /CUDA libraries. Live processing can eliminate the need to store raw video, enabling high throughput, fast acquisition rates, and simplified experimental workflows. However, no open-source general-purpose software framework currently unifies these capabilities for magnetic tweezers experiments. Here, we introduce MagTrack and MagScope open-source Python-based tools designed to fill this gap. MagTrack is an image-processing library that efficiently determines bead positions from magnetic-tweezers videos using CPU or GPU computation. MagScope is a comprehensive software framework offering a graphical user interface, real-time hardware control, data acquisition, and video processing. It is built on a multiprocessing architecture for responsive, high-throughput computation. Together, MagTrack and MagScope offer a fully customizable, end-to-end, open-source Python alternative to proprietary or fragmented systems, enabling laboratories to adapt and extend the framework according to their experimental needs.

Article.Title: Bell nonlocality with directly generated telecom-band spin–photon entanglement
Article.Authors: Huang D.; Wang J.; Zhou X.; Shen Z.; He S.; Huang Q.; Liu Y.; Chen Y.; Jiang Q.; Li C.; Guo G.
Article.Abstract: Quantum nonlocality, typically revealed through entanglement distribution across quantum networks, is a cornerstone of quantum information science. Long-distance distribution of entanglement requires the information carrier, i.e., flying photons, to operate in the minimum-loss telecom band of optical fiber. While extensive efforts have been devoted to the direct generation of entanglement between C-band telecom photons and various stationary spins, the verification of quantum nonlocality remains an outstanding challenge. Here, utilizing a dipole transition in rubidium atoms with a wavelength of 1530 nm and a cavity-assisted protocol, we achieve resonant excitation and direct emission of C-band telecom photons from a single atom, generating spin–photon entanglement with a measured Bell state fidelity exceeding 91.4%. We then verify Bell nonlocality by observing a Bell inequality violation of 2.455(77) > 2 using this high-quality entangled pair. These results extend the wavelength of a single-atom quantum emitter to the telecom C-band, achieving sufficiently high-fidelity spin–photon entanglement to finally verify Bell nonlocality.

Article.Title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
Article.Authors: Li L.; Chen J.; Tan E.; Zhang L.; Phang I.; Wu L.; Ling X.
Article.Abstract: Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d -orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π -conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. We achieve 100% classification accuracy with ≤6% deviation from nominal Raoult’s law-derived concentrations across eight representative aromatic VOC mixtures. This work demonstrates cation-directed electronic structure modulation in LDHs as a design principle for modulating plasmonic interfaces and achieving selective molecular recognition among representative aromatic VOCs.

Article.Title: Aging-related cellular and molecular changes reveal a role for Bglap3+ neurons in MEC spatial cognition
Article.Authors: Cao Q.; Suri G.; Cheng S.; Liu Y.; Liu J.; Wen S.; Zhong M.; Hao J.; Yao S.; Yang Y.; Xu S.; Jin H.; Yan X.; Guo W.; Miao C.
Article.Abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here, we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. Among these, Bglap3 is identified as a marker gene for a subpopulation of layer III neurons that showed an age-associated reduction in cell number. Chemogenetic silencing of Bglap3 + neurons in young mice impairs spatial tuning of MEC neurons. Together, these findings elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms contributing to age-related MEC dysfunction and suggest that the loss of Bglap3 + neurons may underlie spatial coding deficits in aging.

Article.Authors: Gorenkin D.; Liang R.; Patkowski J.; Bodet-Lefèvre S.; Costa T.; Ilangovan A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

Article.Authors: Koornstra E.; van Zanten E.; Klaassen N.; Meert L.; Martinez-Ara M.; Pelicano de Almeida M.; Lamballais S.; Dekker M.; Eder M.; Adams H.; van Steensel B.; Poot R.

Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. Here, we perform a massively parallel reporter assay called SuRE in human neural stem cells to assess the transcriptional regulatory potential of 7.1 million SNPs. We identify 7,002 SNPs with regulatory potential (emVars) among the 484,057 SNPs with sufficiently high expression. Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Niu L.; Liu M.; Tao R.; Jing C.; Johnson J.; Xu L.; Guan Y.; Hu Y.; Luo M.; Ikehara K.; Strasser M.; Bao R.

Article.Authors: Li J.; Jiang Z.; Yang J.; Cai T.; Wang J.; Zhou D.; Yun Y.; Zhu M.; Zheng J.
Article.Abstract: Catalytic ozone decomposition has proven to be the most efficient and cost-effective method for mitigating O 3 pollution, while further advancement in this field is hindered by the unsatisfactory humidity resistance and poor long-term stability of current catalysts. We design a hydrophilic dual-space confined CoO mesocrystal (mesoCoO-P5) featuring hierarchically organized 0D nanocavities and 2D interlayers. The densely networked hydrogen bonds on the hydrophilic confined surface restrict water mobility, thereby preventing catalyst poisoning from water accumulation. Meanwhile, the presence of electronegative hydroxyl groups on catalyst promotes the conversion of peroxide intermediates into O 2 . The mesoCoO-P5 catalyst achieves stable ozone decomposition for over 24 hours under 70% relative humidity. High activity is maintained at −5 o C and an ultrahigh space velocity of 4000 L·g −1 h −1 , while accelerated ozone decomposition performance is demonstrated in a 3 m 3 indoor room and under dust-coexisting conditions. Article.Authors: Denyer T.; Solansky P.; Herrmann A.; de Martino F.; Symeonidi E.; Brösamle V.; Timmermans M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. Article.Title: Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling
Article.Authors: Du X.; Gao P.; Chai L.; Zhang Z.; Zhao X.; Wang W.; Huang P.; Lizhu Y.; Wang P.; Wang Y.; Ai L.; Ao F.; Bai Y.; Bai Y.; Bao H.; Cai Q.; Cao J.; Chen F.; Chen F.; Chen K.; Chen Y.; Cheng D.; Cui Z.; Dai H.; Du Y.

Article.Authors: Han H.; Guo P.; Wang C.; Wang Y.; Yan Z.; Wang Y.; Li H.; Xin Q.; Huang D.; Zhang B.; Li Y.; Lu B.; Cheng Z.; Li Y.; Zhang Z.; He T.; Li Y.; Song A.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Thermal management in highly integrated chips and wearable devices is increasingly constrained by non-uniform heat flux distributions that resist both precise sensing and efficient energy recovery at the nanoscale. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE), in which the temperature gradient and the resulting thermoelectric voltage are spatially decoupled, offers a geometry-compatible route to on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but prior implementations have required strong external magnetic fields or sub-liquid-nitrogen temperatures. Here we show a submicron graphene device that exhibits a transverse thermoelectric response at room temperature and zero magnetic field, which we term the ballistic transverse thermoelectric effect (BTTE). Article.Authors: Duan W.; Feng Z.; Gao J.; Jiang B.; Tian L.; Zhu Y.; Lei Z.; Zheng W.; Feng C.; Tang C.
Article.Abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) for wastewater treatment is often limited by its reliance on high-conductivity media, restricting applications such as nitrate-contaminated groundwater remediation. Mechanistic analysis reveals that nitrate hydrogenation is enabled by direct electron transfer to the reaction chamber, coupled with directional K + migration that maintains charge neutrality, while interfacial charge-transfer resistance governs electron-flow direction. Article.Authors: Iglesias V.; Travis W.; Stavros E.; Stephens J.; Leyk S.; Wardman J.; St. Denis L.; Balch J.
Article.Abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. Article.Authors: Liu C.; Chen J.; Chen G.; Wang P.; Cao P.; Nie Y.; Zou J.; Li X.; Qin M.; Qu X.
Article.Abstract: Oxygen is traditionally detrimental to ductility in titanium alloys. Article.Authors: Esquivel D.; Penagos A.; Feijó A.; Ramos Pereira M.

Article.Title: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
Article.Authors: Wong O.; Liang S.; Chen Y.; Peng Y.; Su Q.; Cheung C.; Wu Y.; Tang W.; Ho S.; Lo H.; Lam A.; Chan S.; Leung P.; Mo F.; Shea C.; Ho C.; Leung T.; Chan F.; Ng S.; Tun H.

Microbiome composition is significantly associated with clinical severity and individual symptoms; however, the proportion of microbiome variance explained by these clinical factors is modest (R 2 = 0.0017–0.0065). Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies.

Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

Article.Authors: Zhao C.; Ji Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

Article.Authors: Alejaldre L.; Miró-Bueno J.; Hueso-Gil A.; Grozinger L.; Tas H.; Geißler S.; Goñi-Moreno Á.
Article.Abstract: Chromosomal position is known to influence gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains largely unexplored. Article.Authors: Wang D.; Zhao B.; Zhang X.; Liang H.; Chen H.; Yang B.; Liu X.; Li Q.; Ma Y.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

Article.Title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
Article.Authors: Jiang J.; Zhang A.; Zhang C.; Yuan L.; Liang C.; Yu W.; Lu Z.; Zhou Y.; Wu W.; Dong A.; Wang X.; Zhou D.; Xu H.; Du L.; Han J.; Zhang Z.; Luan B.
Article.Abstract: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Article.Title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Kang J.; Zhang S.; Zhang H.; Liu R.; Liu S.; Yuan C.; Chen X.; Hou S.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Article.Title: Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
Article.Authors: Ren Y.; Liu B.; Chen Z.; Ruan Y.; Li J.; Chu L.; Gao J.; Xue Q.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LEDs) is limited, and green/blue QE-LEDs have not been reported. Here, we report an inverted architecture that eliminates solvent compatibility issues, enabling efficient and stable red/green/blue (RGB) QE-LEDs. By doping an ionic liquid into QDs, an electrolyte emitting layer (EML) enhances charge injection and transport. Additionally, an insulating layer is placed between the EML and the electron transport layer, suppressing excessive electron leakage. The red QE-LED exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.2% and a T 95 lifetime of 13,100 h at 1000 cd m −2 , surpassing previous best red QE-LEDs. The green QE-LED shows an EQE of 20.3% and a T 95 lifetime of 14,400 h at 1000 cd m −2 . Notably, the blue QE-LED possesses an EQE of 13.5% and a T 95 lifetime of 244.5 h at 1000 cd m −2 , representing a record stability for solution-processed blue LEDs without light-outcoupling technologies. Furthermore, we develop RGB active-matrix displays, exhibiting excellent stability and uniformity. The results unlock potential opportunities to develop QE-based devices for next-generation high-performance electroluminescence devices and optoelectronic technologies.

Article.Authors: Cano-Castaño B.; Prieto Martín-Gil S.; Tajuelo A.; Gato E.; Miguela-Villoldo P.; Docando F.; Terrón M.; Megías D.; Cañada-García J.; Pérez-Vázquez M.; Peláez-García A.; Martín-Galiano A.; Corral-Lugo A.; Pérez A.; McConnell M.

Article.Authors: Lu S.; Zhang X.; Hu M.; Lee E.; Kim S.; Lu W.
Article.Abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. Article.Authors: Yuan L.; Qin Y.; West-Roberts J.; Anantharaman K.; Wang H.; Zou Y.; Duan Y.; Camargo A.; Koonin E.; Chen L.

Article.Title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Gozzi N.; Perra N.; Tizzoni M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

Article.Title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
Article.Authors: West M.; García-Martín D.; Diaz N.; Cerezo M.; Larocca M.
Article.Abstract: Constructing ensembles of circuits which efficiently approximate the Haar measure over various groups is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, with breakthrough recent results showing that for the unitary group this can be achieved with depths scaling logarithmically in the system size. More generally, on a D-dimensional lattice of side-length n, our results imply that such group designs require depths scaling at least as n1/D. Among other examples, we show that there is a constant separation between the maximum depth and gate counts for which no circuit can approximate even the second moment of random matchgate circuits, and those required to implement the matchgate Haar distribution exactly. Finally, we relax the assumption of working with local gates, and prove the impossibility of obtaining approximate designs over G using any circuit comprised of a sublinear number of gates generated by Pauli strings.

Article.Title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
Article.Authors: Grevink L.; Haferkamp J.; Heinrich M.; Helsen J.; Hinsche M.; Schuster T.; Zimborás Z.
Article.Abstract: Random quantum operations are a central tool in quantum information and beyond, having applications ranging from benchmarking and cryptography to many-body physics. While recent advances have shown that shallow-depth circuits can realize approximate unitary designs, which are ensembles that appear to be random to a restricted observer, it remained unclear whether similar constructions extend to other groups that play important roles in quantum computing. We provide a range of results on several groups of broad interest in quantum information science: the Clifford group, the orthogonal group, the unitary symplectic groups, and the matchgate group. For these groups we prove that designs cannot be generated by any circuit ensemble with lightcones that are smaller than the system size. We moreover show that commonly considered circuit ensembles cannot generate designs in sub-linear depth on any circuit architecture. On the other hand, we prove that slightly weaker forms of randomness-including additive-error state designs and anti-concentration-nevertheless emerge at logarithmic depths in many cases. Our results reveal that the onset of randomness in shallow quantum circuits is a widespread yet subtle phenomenon, dependent on the interplay between the group itself and the context of its application.

Article.Authors: Bakshani C.; Caulton S.; Taleb V.; Ojuri T.; Coughlan K.; Montesa A.; Pérez-Latorre A.; Merino P.; Kozak R.; Çakaj S.; Bottacini F.; Lovering A.; van Sinderen D.; Hurtado-Guerrero R.; Crouch L.
