Article.Title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Immunotherapy: A Review of the Emerging Uses and Current Challenges
Article.Authors: Nangoli S.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide despite major therapeutic advances, including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Although a subset of patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) experiences durable long-term responses, currently available predictive biomarkers, including programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression, have limited ability to reliably distinguish responders from non-responders. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as powerful approaches for extracting clinically meaningful patterns from complex, high-dimensional datasets spanning pathology, liquid biopsy, imaging, and integrated multimodal data. This narrative review examines current applications of AI in NSCLC immunotherapy across these complementary data modalities and evaluates the evidence supporting their clinical translation. Particular attention is given to the methodological limitations of existing studies and to the emerging shift from single-modality biomarkers toward dynamic and multimodal prediction. Although AI-based approaches show potential to complement established biomarkers, limitations in validation, generalizability, and prospective evidence currently restrict their clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Piperlongumine Targets Triple-Negative Breast Cancer by Inducing Paraptosis Through Elevated ER Stress, Autophagic Flux Impairment and ALIX Downregulation
Article.Authors: Hanson S.; Nedungadi D.; Binoy A.; Bhutia S.; Nair A.; Nair B.; Mishra N.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains an aggressive malignancy, largely due to its resistance to conventional apoptosis-inducing therapies and induction of survival autophagy, making the identification of novel cell death mechanisms critical. Piperlongumine (PL), an alkaloid derived from Piper longum, has shown promising anti-cancer activity, yet its ability to induce paraptosis and inhibit autophagy in TNBC has not been explored. In this study, PL-induced cell death was investigated through morphological analysis, cell viability assays, Annexin-V/PI staining, ER stress marker assessment, autophagic flux using a tandem fluorescence construct, and pharmacological inhibition with NAC, chloroquine, cycloheximide, and MAPK inhibitors, alongside ALIX knockdown and overexpression studies to clarify the regulatory mechanism. Survival analyses based on ALIX expression were also conducted using three independent public transcriptomic datasets. PL induced higher cytotoxicity in TNBC cells than in MCF-10A, through cytoplasmic vacuolation-mediated paraptosis, with vacuoles originating from the ER alongside elevated ER stress, polyubiquitinated protein accumulation, Bip/CHOP upregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, increased ROS, and reduced ATP. PL-induced cell death was suppressed by NAC, implicating sulfhydryl disruption. PL impaired late-stage autophagy, evidenced by LC3-II/p62 accumulation, and downregulated ALIX, whose overexpression restored survival and reduced paraptosis. High ALIX expression predicted poor basal/TNBC prognosis in two of three cohorts, suggesting therapeutic significance.

Article.Title: Carnosic Acid Attenuates Lipotoxicity-Mediated Myocardial Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury by Suppressing Complex I ROS and Modulating the SIRT1–UPRmt Axis
Article.Authors: Shi X.; Wang M.; Zhou X.; Diao Y.; Fu Y.; Li G.; Ma C.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: The growing prevalence of high-fat diets and sedentary lifestyles has contributed to a marked rise in metabolic disorders and a concomitant increase in cardiovascular disease (CVD). High-fat diet-induced lipotoxicity is a key pathological driver that exacerbates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Carnosic acid (CA), a natural bioactive compound, shows promise for cardiovascular protection through anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. However, the protective effects of CA against lipotoxicity-aggravated myocardial I/R injury and the molecular mechanisms involved remain incompletely understood. In this study, an isolated mouse heart was perfused with a high oleic acid (0.8 mM) solution to create a metabolic stress model of lipotoxicity. Metabolomics was applied to characterize metabolic changes in lipotoxicity-induced myocardial I/R injury. Additionally, the same model was used to investigate the potential mechanisms of action of CA (5 μM). Metabolomic analysis identified pronounced metabolic differences in isolated hearts from the normal and high-fat groups during perfusion, ischemia and reperfusion. Differential metabolites clustered primarily in energy metabolism pathways, consistent with lipotoxicity-driven metabolic derangements that worsen myocardial I/R injury. High-fat perfusion amplified the ischemic accumulation of free fatty acids and succinate in mouse myocardium, thereby aggravating I/R injury. Carnosic acid treatment markedly reversed the lipotoxicity-exacerbated cardiac I/R damage. Mechanistically, CA potentially binds to subunits adjacent to the Q site of mitochondrial complex I, decreasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production from reverse electron transport (RET). The Sirtuin 1 (Sirt1) inhibitor selisistat (EX527) abolished CA’s protective effect, indicating that CA also modulated the Sirt1-UPRmt pathway to preserve mitochondrial homeostasis and mitigate myocardial injury.

Article.Title: Hydrogen Sulfide Pathways and Zinc-Containing Proteins in Human Diseases: A Systematic Review and Evidence Map
Article.Authors: Munteanu C.; Bembea V.; Manolaki Y.; Rotariu M.; Galaction A.
Article.Abstract: Hydrogen sulfide can regulate protein function, but interactions with zinc-containing proteins and their relevance to human disease remain uncertain. We assessed recent human evidence linking sulfur exposure or endogenous sulfur-pathway alterations to zinc-containing proteins and disease-associated outcomes. Article eligibility covered the last five years: 2021–2026. PubMed and ScienceDirect records were searched. Human findings were classified by protein target, zinc function, measured endpoint and mechanistic attribution. The assessed reports described modification-sensitive signals, gene expression, protein abundance and localization involving epigenetic regulators, metalloproteinases, alkaline phosphatase, superoxide dismutase and metallothioneins. Bone-specific alkaline phosphatase concentration increased following uncontrolled sulfurous-water inhalation, whereas total alkaline phosphatase activity showed no significant change. Descriptive co-profiling did not establish sulfur-dependent protein regulation. No assessed human report demonstrated direct sulfide coordination at protein-bound zinc or zinc-site-mediated clinical benefit. Differences in study designs, exposures and endpoints did not support quantitative pooling of the assessed findings. Recent human findings identify candidate sulfur–protein relationships whose functional and therapeutic relevance requires validation. Progress depends on chemically specific exposure measurements, target-specific functional assays and controlled clinical outcomes. Systematic Review Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261535243.

Article.Title: Composition-Dependent Structure and Electrochemical Performance of MXene/Polypyrrole/ZnO Ternary Nanocomposites for Supercapacitor Electrodes
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Shin K.
Article.Abstract: The development of high-performance supercapacitor electrodes requires optimizing charge storage, electron transport, and active-site accessibility. In this study, MXene/polypyrrole/zinc oxide (MXene/PPy/ZnO) ternary nanocomposites were fabricated through in situ polymerization followed by hydrothermal synthesis, systematically varying PPy content and ZnO precursor concentration. Structural and morphological analyses revealed that composite composition influenced ZnO crystal growth and distribution, with excessive precursor concentrations promoting aggregation. M-3P-1Z exhibited uniformly distributed ZnO nanorods and the lowest charge-transfer resistance (0.4713 Ω), achieving the highest CV-derived specific capacitance of 888.01 F g−1 at 1 mV s−1. In contrast, M-1P-0.5Z, featuring ZnO nanorods with an aspect ratio of 10.1, achieved the highest GCD-derived specific capacitance of 1548.75 F g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and a maximum estimated energy density of 161.2 Wh kg−1 at 160 W kg−1. Furthermore, its specific capacitance increased from 56.3 to 306.25 F g−1 after 1000 cycles at 5 A g−1, indicating progressive electrochemical activation. These findings highlight the importance of balancing ZnO morphology, accessible charge-storage sites, and MXene/PPy conductive networks, providing a composition-guided strategy for developing ternary nanocomposite electrodes with improved electrochemical energy storage performance.

Article.Title: From Phage Signatures to Prophage Portrait: Rhizobiophage Sequences in the Genomes of Sinorhizobium spp.
Article.Authors: Roumiantseva M.; Saksaganskaia A.; Muntyan V.; Kozlova A.; Gorbunova M.; Vladimirova M.
Article.Abstract: Prophages shape bacterial evolution, yet their distribution and domestication in symbiotic bacteria remain largely unexplored. We screened 182 rhizobiophage genomes against 105 strains of the genus Sinorhizobium, with S. meliloti and S. medicae comprising the majority (80 strains). Six phages with the highest coverage (25–72%) were selected for analysis, and 34 corresponding intact prophages were identified. Proteome- and distance-based phylogenetic analyses of these prophages revealed three congruent evolutionary clades. Striking interspecies differences emerged: S. meliloti acts as the main recipient of phage material, accumulating less ameliorated prophages (mean ΔGC = −2.62%) with a broader spectrum of integration sites, whereas S. medicae maintains a more closed, vertically inherited pool characterized by higher synteny and greater GC amelioration (ΔGC = −1.12%). We identified distinct integration mechanisms targeting conserved tRNA hotspots and three patterns of phage-prophage recombination: classical, homology-driven, and non-homologous. Furthermore, two types of prophage-to-prophage exchange were identified: recent modular-cassette transfers and ancient recombination events. A broader arsenal of abortive infection systems in S. meliloti (e.g., Pycsar) likely acts as a selective filter rather than an absolute barrier. Such divergent domestication and exchange strategies likely reflect different evolutionary ages of the two species. These findings provide a basis for assessing the risk of stress-inducible prophages in inoculant strains.

Article.Title: Morphological and Molecular Characterization of Tissue, Cellular, and Spheroid Models of the Astrid-17 (10-17-2) Rat Glioma Strain
Article.Authors: Alekseeva A.; Sentyabreva A.; Arutyunyan I.; Gerasimov A.; Melnikova E.; Soboleva A.; Shpakova K.; Skribitsky V.; Finogenova Y.; Kosyreva A.
Article.Abstract: Adult type diffuse gliomas are malignant neoplasms with a high mortality rate and low therapeutic efficacy. The lack of relevant models hinders the search for and development of new therapeutic and diagnostic methods. The rat glioma tissue strain 10-17-2 was obtained through chemical induction. Through in vitro cultivation, cell and spheroid models were obtained for it, reproducing the features of glioma when implanted intracranially in rats. The study involved a comparative analysis of the morphological and molecular-genetic characteristics of the tissue, cell, and spheroid models of Astrid-17 (10-17-2) rat glioma to identify relevant models for human gliomas. This paper presents a morphological characterization of the models, an assessment of the level of mRNA expression of the Cdkn2a, Trp53, S100b, Pten, Vegfa, Pdgfra, Sox2, Abcb1b, and Mgmt genes, and an assessment of the level of expression of the p53, ATRX, PDGFRA, and MGMT proteins. A significant increase in the expression of Sox2 and Vegfa was observed in all models, along with an increase in Pdgfra, Mgmt, Abcb1b, and Tp53 in the tissue model; a decrease in the expression of Tp53, Abcb1b, and Mgmt was noted in the spheroid model. At the same time, an increase in the expression of the p53 and ATRX proteins was observed in all three models. All models were visualized using MRI and PET-CT. It is shown that the tissue model has the most pronounced morphological similarity, while the spheroid model exhibits moderate morphological similarity to high-grade human gliomas. The molecular profile is individual for each model; however, based on the combination of markers, the spheroid model is the most relevant to human glioma compared to the tissue and cell models.

Article.Title: Proposed Grammatical Rules for the Redox Code
Article.Authors: Andrés C.; Pérez de la Lastra J.; Munguira E.; Juan C.; Lebeña E.
Article.Abstract: Oxidative stress biology has long worked within a framework in which reactive species cause damage and antioxidants supply the remedy. Large antioxidant trials have returned null or harmful results, and systemic redox biomarkers such as malondialdehyde and 8-oxo-dG show only modest diagnostic performance. We propose that both disappointments become more tractable once redox signalling is treated as a local, competitive and compartmentalised information system rather than a global balance, formalised here as the system G = {Σ, M, R, E, L, C, T, Φ}, where G denotes the grammar of the redox code and the eight symbols name its element classes. Reactive signallers (Σ) write post-translational marks (M) that editors (E) reverse or repair, effectors (L) read, and compartments (C) and temporality (T) contextualise, with disease outputs (Φ) completing the architecture. Its predictive core is five operative rules, R.S1 to R.S5, stated in terms of kinetic dominance rather than absolute concentrations, each giving a condition under which one modification should prevail on a contested residue. Three worked applications develop PKG1α Tyr247 nitration in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, DJ-1 Cys106 overoxidation in Parkinson’s disease and ApoA-I modification in sepsis, each as a testable hypothesis. G asks which mark dominates, whether it is reversible and what it does functionally, so that intervention is directed at the right level. G is proposed as a complement to quantitative redox modelling and not as a replacement for it, since it generates testable hypotheses where kinetic parameters are incomplete and does not attempt quantitative simulation.

Article.Title: Thiazolidine-2,4-dione Conjugated with Aryl/Benzyl Piperazines: Design, Synthesis, Tyrosinase Inhibitory Activity, and In Vitro and In Vivo Anti-Melanogenic Effects
Article.Authors: Romagnoli R.; De Ventura T.; Romagnoli E.; Germanò M.; Mirabile S.; De Luca L.; Pitasi G.; Corallo D.; Bortolozzi R.; Viola G.
Article.Abstract: Tyrosinase is a key enzyme in melanogenesis and a target for the development of agents against hyperpigmentation. In this study, fifteen thiazolidine-2,4-dione derivatives conjugated with aryl- or benzylpiperazine moieties were designed and synthesized using a molecular hybridization strategy. Their inhibitory activity against mushroom tyrosinase was evaluated together with molecular docking, and selected compounds were further tested in SK-MEL-31 human melanoma cells and wild-type AB/TU zebrafish embryos. Ten derivatives inhibited mushroom tyrosinase more potently than kojic acid. Linker length and aromatic substitution strongly influenced activity, with TDP10 and TDP2 showing the highest potency (IC50 = 0.41 and 0.79 μM, respectively). Kinetic studies revealed inhibition profiles consistent with a non-competitive mechanism for both compounds. The selected derivatives reduced α-MSH-induced intracellular tyrosinase activity at 50 μM, with TDP7 producing the greatest effect. In zebrafish embryos, TDP2, TDP7, and TDP10 reduced pigmentation to different extents, with TDP7 showing a marked effect at 100 μM. Developmental toxicity assessment revealed concentration-dependent adverse effects at 100 μM, particularly for TDP10, whereas no adverse endpoints were observed at lower concentrations. These findings identify the thiazolidine-2,4-dione-aryl/benzylpiperazine scaffold as a promising starting point for the development of new tyrosinase inhibitors, while highlighting the importance of further efficacy and safety evaluation.

Article.Title: An Antimicrobial Peptide-Loaded Electrospun Polymeric Nanofiber Coating for Preventing Biofilm Formation on Orthopedic Implant Surfaces
Article.Authors: Campoccia D.; Sotgiu G.; Bottau G.; De Donno A.; Ravaioli S.; Navacchia M.; Lo Re A.; Capponi E.; Cantelli A.; Columbaro M.; Bua G.; Arciola C.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent an important alternative to conventional antibiotics, conferring bactericidal and anti-biofilm properties to biomaterial surfaces to address the challenge of antibiotic resistance. KSL-W is a decapeptide with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. This study focused on the development and characterization of a novel anti-infective coating for orthopedic titanium prostheses, consisting of electrospun poly(ε-caprolactone)(PCL)/poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)(PLGA) nanofibers loaded with KSL-W (PCL/PLGA@KSL-W). Pure titanium discs were coated with PCL/PLGA coatings, either loaded with KSL-W or peptide-free, and their antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities were evaluated against two bacterial strains representative of etiological agents frequently isolated from orthopedic implant-associated infections: the Gram-positive Staphylococcus epidermidis and the Gram-negative Escherichia coli. Furthermore, the cytocompatibility of coated discs was investigated by seeding osteoblast-like MG63 cells and assessing cell metabolism (by both ATP luminescence and Alamar blue) and alkaline phosphatase activity. PCL/PLGA@KSL-W coating was found to reduce of over 3 Logs biofilm formation of S. epidermidis and E. coli, and of 2 and 3 Logs, respectively, the growth of planktonic bacteria with respect to the peptide-free PCL/PLGA coating. Despite the potent antibacterial activity, no difference in osteoblast viability was observed between PCL/PLGA and PCL/PLGA@KSL-W coatings. Interestingly, PCL/PLGA@KSL-W coating combined strong antibacterial activity with desirable osteocompatibility properties, favouring bone cell differentiation.

Article.Title: Sex-Stratified Regulatory Landscapes of Pancreatic β-Cells in Type 2 Diabetes: Single-Cell and Donor-Level Transcriptomic Analysis
Article.Authors: Niu X.; Feng Y.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) exhibits sex-dependent differences in islet β-cell dysfunction, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. By integrating two independent single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, we performed sex-stratified analyses at both the single-cell and donor levels to identify sex-prioritized candidate genes and candidate therapeutic interventions. At the single-cell level, differential expression and network analyses nominated AKT2 as a male-prioritized candidate and ALDOA and GAPDH as female-prioritized candidates; virtual gene knockout of these candidates indicated that they impair β-cell function through diffuse regulatory-network remodeling rather than through single marker genes; and female β-cells formed a discrete T2D-enriched functional state (T2D proportions of 32.5%, 56.8%, and 80.0% across the three states; p < 0.0001), whereas no disease-associated functional stratification was detected in males. Pathway-enrichment and CytoTRACE2 analyses revealed, at the cell level, correlation structures that differed between sexes for 6 pathways (e.g., Insulin_Secretion, r = +0.206 male vs. −0.103 female, cell-level p = 4.8 × 10−4), although these differences were not confirmed in donor-level sensitivity analyses and are presented as descriptive. Pseudobulk analysis across 24 donor units identified a significant signature of seven genes in the female-stratified analysis, dominated by glycolytic downregulation, with SPP1 upregulation reaching nominal significance; in males, four genes reached significance but rested on only two male T2D donors in the pseudobulk subset and are presented as descriptive, so no robust male disease signature was detected given limited statistical power. Machine-learning models with donor-grouped cross-validation yielded donor-level ROC-AUC values at or below 0.52 in both sexes, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals spanning 0.5 in all cases, consistent with chance-level performance. Drug screening nominated ten candidate compounds, and molecular docking predicted favorable binding of SB-431542 with AKT2 (−8.10 kcal/mol) and triamterene with ALDOA (−7.71 kcal/mol).

Article.Title: Activity of Protective Blends Comprised of Cinnamon, Clove, Rosemary, Eucalyptus and Lemon Essential Oils Against Clinical Escherichia coli Strains Isolated from Poultry
Article.Authors: Zych S.; Adaszyńska-Skwirzyńska M.; Dzięcioł M.; Konieczka P.; Kozłowski K.; Witkowska D.; Szewczuk M.
Article.Abstract: Poultry colibacillosis is a common bacterial disease caused by pathogenic strains of Escherichia coli. The growing drug resistance of these strains is driving the search for new phytobiotics that are effective against this bacterium. A medieval recipe, the “Thieves” protective blend, shows promising results in this regard. This blend contains essential oils (EOs) from cinnamon bark (cinnamaldehyde chemotype), clove buds (eugenol chemotype), rosemary and eucalyptus (both eucalyptol chemotype) and lemon (limonene). The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) method was used to determine the activity of a total of 12 selected EOs (5 single EOs and 7 protective blends) against fifty clinical isolates of E. coli and the reference strain ATCC 25922. The detailed chemical composition of all EOs and their blends was determined using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Cinnamon bark EO showed the strongest activity (mean MIC = 0.14% v/v), followed by two mixtures containing 50% and 20% of this EO (mean MICs of 0.22% and 0.25% v/v, respectively). The second most active EO was clove bud EO (mean MIC = 0.28% v/v) and the related blend (mean MIC 0.27% v/v). Rosemary, eucalyptus, and lemon EOs appear to have low activity against E. coli (MIC > 4% v/v). However, typical MIC values for their mixtures ranged from 0.34 to 0.5% v/v, indicating a possible synergy between the individual components of the “Thieves” blend. If additional synergistic effects with antibiotics can be identified in the future, it will be possible to use this type of protective blend in the adjunctive treatment of colibacillosis in poultry.

Article.Title: NAA-Param: Automated De Novo Parameterization of Non-Canonical Amino Acids for Molecular Dynamics Studies
Article.Authors: Carotenuto G.; Menconero E.; Botta L.; Saladino R.; Bottoni P.; Castrignanò T.
Article.Abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are key determinants of protein function and play an increasingly central role in rational drug design. These modifications involve the presence of non-canonical amino acid residues (nAA) within the affected proteins. Force fields typically used in molecular dynamics studies contain parameters for the 20 canonical amino acids; the lack of specific parameters for the nAAs makes it impossible to apply standard molecular dynamics (MD) protocols to proteins with PTMs, as these protocols often fail to generate accurate topologies for proteins featuring such modifications. In this work, we present a robust computational framework designed to parameterize the force fields required to perform MD simulations on proteins with PTMs. We introduce NAA-Param, a tool that derives high-quality, specific force field parameters for nAA on demand. The system automatically replicates the original protocol used to calculate parameters for the Amber99sb-ildn force field, a widely used force field in MD. Output files for the nAA are generated in a GROMACS-compatible format; furthermore, NAA-Param can be executed on HPC platforms.

Article.Title: Research Advances on Gut–Brain Axis in Parkinson’s Disease Pathogenesis and Prodromal Prediction
Article.Authors: Huang L.; Du W.; Zhai J.; Zhu W.; Wu J.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) is a common chronic progressive neurodegenerative disorder. Traditionally, it has been considered to be a disorder confined to dopaminergic neuronal injury in the substantia nigra of the central nervous system. However, increasing evidence from epidemiology, clinical imaging, and molecular biology suggests that the pathological process of PD may begin in the gut, with the gut–brain axis participating in disease initiation and progression. This review systematically summarizes the structural and physiological regulatory mechanisms of the gut–brain axis, focusing in particular on the aggregation of α-synuclein in the gut and its prion-like propagation, features of gut microbiota dysbiosis, leaky gut and systemic inflammatory cascades, and vagus nerve–related transmission mechanisms. Centering on prodromal PD, we discuss in depth early biomarkers based on this framework and propose a multi-dimensional combinatorial strategy integrating gut microbiota, barrier-related molecules and prodromal clinical phenotypes, to provide new perspectives for the prodromal prediction of PD.

Article.Title: Diagnostic Yield and Variant Spectrum in 375 Patients with Segmental Overgrowth and Vascular Malformations: Implications for Panel Design and Molecular Testing Strategies
Article.Authors: Bychkova E.; Semenova N.; Sagoyan G.; Alimov S.; Zhigulin A.; Somsikov G.; Khagurov R.; Guseva D.; Volodin I.; Kutsev S.; Strelnikov V.
Article.Abstract: Segmental overgrowth and vascular malformations comprise a group of diseases caused by postzygotic variants in genes that regulate cell growth, proliferation, and angiogenesis. The best-characterized group is the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS), which includes syndromes sharing variants in the PIK3CA gene. Beyond PIK3CA, the genes involved fall into two mechanistically distinct groups, with gain-of-function (GNAQ, GNA11, TEK, AKT1, AKT3, MTOR, PIK3R1) and loss-of-function (RASA1, GLMN, PTEN) causative variants. What remains poorly established is how effectively a molecular diagnosis is actually achieved in routine practice, and how this depends on the referral clinical diagnosis. By targeted panel deep sequencing in patients with segmental overgrowth and/or a vascular malformation, we have identified at least one pathogenic / likely pathogenic (P/LP) genetic variant in 266 of the 375 successfully tested patients, giving an overall diagnostic yield of 70.9%. The yield was 63.5% in patients with isolated overgrowth (94 of 148), 75.0% in patients with an isolated vascular malformation (111 of 148) and 77.2% in patients with a combined or syndromic phenotype (61 of 79). The 277 P/LP variants identified were distributed across 17 genes; PIK3CA accounted for 141 variants (50.9%), GNAQ for 44 (15.9%), TEK for 31 (11.2%), RASA1 for 15 (5.4%) and GNA11 for 11 (4.0%); these five genes together accounted for 87.4% of the variants. The spectrum was highly concentrated: the ten most frequent variants accounted for 57.0% of the P/LP variants, with GNAQ variant p.Arg183Gln (15.2%) and PIK3CA hotspot variants p.Glu542Lys (8.7%), p.Glu545Lys (6.9%), and p.His1047Arg (7.6%). In several genes, variants were restricted to specific regions: in GNAQ and GNA11 to two codons, 183 and 209 (98.2% of all findings), and in TEK to the 3′-terminus. Considered together with the referral diagnosis, the distribution of variants, their allele fractions and their mechanisms of pathogenicity suggest molecular testing strategies.

Article.Title: Circulating CD39+ Regulatory T Cells from Patients with Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: Exploratory Assessment of Neuroprotective and Regenerative Activity in Pooled Preparations
Article.Authors: Ye C.; Jiang Q.; Cai B.; Jiang B.; Xie L.
Article.Abstract: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss and irreversible visual impairment. The potential involvement of regulatory T cells (Tregs) in glaucomatous neurodegeneration remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated Mendelian randomization (MR), peripheral blood immunophenotyping, and experimental functional assessments to investigate CD39+ Tregs in POAG. Functional experiments using pooled donor-derived preparations showed that CD39+ Treg-conditioned medium and adoptively transferred CD39+ Tregs exerted a degree of protective activity. In vitro, healthy control-derived conditioned medium exhibited greater neurite-supporting activity than POAG-derived conditioned medium in the preparations tested. In vivo, both healthy control- and POAG-derived preparations exhibited neuroprotective effects; healthy control-derived conditioned medium yielded a higher RGC density than POAG-derived medium, and short-distance axon regeneration was numerically greater following treatment with healthy control-derived preparations. Together, these proof-of-concept findings highlight the potential neuroprotective and regenerative properties of CD39+ Treg-derived preparations and support further investigation of their involvement in retinal neurodegeneration.

Article.Authors: Yi X.; Zhu Y.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Urticaria is a common and heterogeneous inflammatory skin disorder with a complex pathogenesis, and effective treatment options remain limited for some patients. This study employed an integrative multi-omics framework combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based MR (SMR), Bayesian colocalization, and mediation analysis to identify candidate genes and inflammatory mediators associated with urticaria susceptibility. Furthermore, C4A expression was significantly downregulated in lesional skin from patients with chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), and a consistent reduction was observed in ear skin from mice subjected to IgE/DNP-induced passive cutaneous anaphylaxis. Collectively, these findings support potential associations of C4A and CCL19 with urticaria risk and provide preliminary statistical evidence for a possible mediating role of CCL19 in the association between genetically predicted C4A expression and urticaria risk. Although this study cannot establish causality or directly inform clinical translation, it identifies candidate genes and a potential C4A–CCL19 relationship warranting experimental validation.

Article.Title: Dendritic Cells Undergo Cytoskeletal, Adhesive, and Inflammatory Remodeling During Productive Infection with Vaccinia Virus Western Reserve
Article.Authors: Biernacka Z.; Markowska M.; Wróblewski M.; Niedzielska A.; Zawadzka K.; Koper M.; Gregorczyk-Zboroch K.; Lasocka I.; Gieryńska M.; Struzik J.; Mielcarska M.; Wierzbicki M.; Toka F.; Szulc-Dąbrowska L.
Article.Abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) are professional antigen-presenting cells (APCs) that regulate key aspects of innate and adaptive immunity. Their functions rely on dynamic cytoskeletal remodeling and specialized adhesive structures, including podosomes and focal adhesions (FAs), which coordinate cell–matrix interactions, antigen sampling, and migration to lymphoid organs, where DCs initiate T-cell responses. Non-pathogenic or attenuated vaccinia virus (VACV) strains can modulate DC functions despite undergoing abortive infection in these cells. However, the capacity of VACV Western Reserve (VACV-WR), a pathogenic and highly mouse-adapted strain with pronounced virulence in murine models, to productively infect DCs and its effects on their cytoskeletal organization, adhesive properties, and immune functions remain poorly characterized. Here, we demonstrate that VACV-WR completes its replication cycle and produces infectious progeny virions in murine GM-CSF-derived bone marrow DCs (BMDCs). Such productive infection promotes the phenotypic maturation of BMDCs with a limited pro-inflammatory response and induces rapid podosome disassembly accompanied by increased FA number and length. Consequently, podosome-dependent extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation was abolished in infected cells. Despite pronounced morphological and adhesive remodeling, VACV-WR infection did not significantly alter mean BMDC migration distance or speed in the two-dimensional assay, although time-lapse analysis revealed a significantly increased proportion of stationary cells. These findings indicate that VACV-WR induces the coordinated cytoskeletal, adhesive, and immunological reprogramming of BMDCs, with functional consequences for ECM remodeling but not basal motility.

Article.Title: Genotypic and Phenotypic Spectrum of Pediatric β-Thalassaemia: Insights from a 30-Year Single-Center Experience
Article.Authors: Adramerina A.; Goulas I.; Tritou M.; Gkimprixis C.; Malontziki L.; Aidinidou L.; Teli A.; Theodoridou S.; Vrettou C.; Traeger-Synodinos J.; Economou M.
Article.Abstract: Thalassaemia was the first human disease for which a genetic basis was elucidated. The marked clinical heterogeneity of this monogenic disorder has attracted research interest, particularly towards the identification of genetic and other modifiers of disease phenotype. The aim of the present study was to investigate genotype–phenotype correlations in pediatric patients with thalassaemia followed at a Pediatric Thalassaemia Unit. All 36 patients carrying homozygous β0/β0 or β+/β+ variants, or compound heterozygous β0/β+ mutations were transfusion-dependent, whereas the remaining TDT patients carried β0 or β+ and silent β-globin variants or α-globin gene triplication. Four genotypes found in 16 patients were associated with both transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent phenotypes. Notably, two pairs of related patients carrying the same genotype exhibited discordant clinical phenotypes. The clinical heterogeneity of β-thalassaemia is further highlighted by the discordant phenotypes observed among patients carrying the same genotype, underscoring the need to identify additional factors that influence clinical expression. Characterization of these factors is important, not only for more accurate genetic counseling and prognostic assessment, but also for individualization of treatment strategies and appropriate selection of candidates for emerging therapeutic approaches.

Article.Title: Cell-Penetrating TLR Inhibitor Peptide Ameliorates Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis and Promotes Efferocytosis in Microglia and Macrophages
Article.Authors: Lee Y.; Park H.; Pak S.; Kim M.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling contributes to inflammatory activation during autoimmune neuroinflammation. Pharmacological inhibition further implicated LXR signaling in this response, while cpTLR-i altered SOCS/STAT3 signaling, revealing an unexpected association between modulation of TLR signaling and signaling networks involved in the regulation of efferocytosis. These findings demonstrate that cpTLR-i not only suppresses inflammatory responses but also promotes pro-resolving functions of microglia and macrophages, suggesting that selective modulation of TLR signaling represents a potential therapeutic strategy for neuroinflammatory diseases.

At day 28, no paired comparison remained FDR-significant; however, H3/H4 showed a significant overall temporal change across the six complete serial trajectories (q = 0.0334). Exploratory day-28 trajectories showed concordant decreases in all three four-marker-positive populations in patients achieving complete remission, with opposite changes in residual disease; however, the response-stratified comparisons were not statistically significant. These findings support disease- and treatment-associated redistribution of circulating histone populations across myeloid neoplasia.

Article.Title: Life After Catalytic Death: Pseudopeptidases as Key Regulators in Health and Disease
Article.Authors: Dunaevsky Y.; Tereshchenkova V.; Zhiganov N.; Zamyatnin A.; Elpidina E.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, researchers have increasingly focused on a special class of proteins—pseudopeptidases—that have lost their catalytic activity while retaining the ability to bind targets with high specificity. The evolutionary transition from an active enzyme to a pseudopeptidase is often driven by point mutations in the active site that “switch off” hydrolysis, paradoxically increasing affinity for substrates or regulatory partners. This process of “functional exaptation” allows the cell to create complex regulatory networks by repurposing existing domains rather than synthesizing new structures. This review analyzes the mechanisms underlying the emergence of pseudopeptidases across all major peptidase families and their roles in signaling cascades as molecular scaffolds, allosteric modulators, or competitive inhibitors. Particular attention is paid to their contribution to pathophysiology: the loss of proteolytic function does not render these proteins “silent”; on the contrary, their dysfunction is critical in the development of cancer, as well as neurodegenerative and inflammatory diseases. The shift from catalytic inertness to active regulation opens new horizons in understanding the molecular mechanisms of pathologies, positioning pseudopeptidases as promising targets for therapeutic intervention.

Article.Title: Oxyresveratrol and Related Stilbenes in Retinal Diseases: Current Preclinical Evidence, Mechanistic Rationale, and Research Priorities
Article.Authors: Kang B.; Lee D.; Vitiello L.; Lim S.
Article.Abstract: Oxyresveratrol is a naturally occurring stilbene known for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic activities. However, its relevance to retinal disease requires careful distinction between direct ocular findings and evidence obtained with related compounds or non-ocular models. This narrative review critically examines direct retinal evidence for oxyresveratrol, comparative retinal studies of resveratrol, and non-ocular findings for mulberrosides and oxyresveratrol-containing botanical preparations. The literature search used PubMed and Google Scholar, supplemented with reference-list screening. The direct oxyresveratrol evidence discussed here includes pretreatment studies in hydrogen peroxide- or sodium iodate-exposed ARPE-19 cells and a sodium iodate-induced mouse retinal injury model. Reported improvements in cellular viability and retinal structure support further investigations of RPE oxidative injury, but methodological limitations and the predominantly preventive treatment designs preclude conclusions regarding efficacy in human age-related macular degeneration or other retinal diseases. The reported NRF2-silencing experiments did not establish that NRF2 activation was required for protection. Effects on retinal mitochondrial function, SIRT1/SIRT3 signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and adipose–retina interactions remain hypotheses requiring direct validation. Findings for resveratrol, mulberrosides, or phytochemical combinations should not be treated as interchangeable evidence of oxyresveratrol efficacy. Priorities include independent replication, post-injury treatment studies, quantitative ocular exposure assessment, and evaluation of safety and disease-specific functional outcomes. Oxyresveratrol therefore warrants further preclinical evaluation, while its translational relevance remains to be established.

Article.Title: Dietary Protein or Amino Acid Supplementation and Its Impact on Sarcopenia and Frailty: A Narrative Review
Article.Authors: Mercado Nieves F.; Lopez I.; Fulzele S.; McGee-Lawrence M.; Johnson M.; Hamrick M.; Bollag W.; Isales C.
Article.Abstract: Nutrition and physical activity are crucial determinants of age-related frailty, an increasingly common condition that can coexist with sarcopenia. Since protein and amino acid supplements are relatively cheap and accessible, determining the usefulness of this intervention in treating frailty/sarcopenia would be valuable. Several clinical trials have examined the effects of protein and amino acid supplementation on frailty and sarcopenia, and results suggest that adequate dietary protein intake/supplementation can improve muscle mass, strength, and function in older adults. An English literature search was conducted using the PubMed (NLM) database from June 2002 to June 2024, and 458 studies were identified. Of these, 410 were excluded after review of their titles, abstracts and the population studied or identification as duplicate references. The remaining 48 studies investigated a variety of protein or essential amino acid (EAA) supplements in a range of settings. Reported positive results were mostly in combination with exercise, specifically resistance training. However, any overall positive effect remains unclear. More high-quality studies are needed to better understand protein/amino acid supplementation’s role in preventing or treating frailty. Amino acid supplementation may be a more practical approach to increasing dietary protein content for older adults, but beneficial effects may require that it be accompanied by exercise.

Article.Title: Ion Homeostasis Disturbances and Their Cellular Consequences in Metabolic Syndrome
Article.Authors: Topcu A.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is increasingly understood as a network disorder in which disturbances across multiple cellular systems converge to promote metabolic and cardiovascular dysfunction. Although ion homeostasis is essential for cellular function, researchers have often considered its contribution to MetS separately for individual ions or within specific disease contexts. In this narrative review, we propose an integrated framework in which disturbances in calcium (Ca2+), magnesium (Mg2+), sodium (Na+), potassium (K+), zinc (Zn2+), and iron (Fe) homeostasis are viewed as interconnected components of metabolic dysfunction rather than isolated abnormalities. We examine how altered ion gradients, transport processes, buffering mechanisms, and intracellular compartmentalization interact with mitochondrial and endoplasmic reticulum function, redox balance, inflammatory signaling, and metabolic pathways. Particular attention is given to the crosstalk between ion-dependent processes and insulin–AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)–mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling, as well as to their links with mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and regulated cell death pathways. We further distinguish interactions between ionic systems that have been directly demonstrated from links inferred only through shared downstream effectors, specify the level at which ion status was assessed, and separate ionic effects on insulin secretion from those on insulin action. Rather than providing a descriptive catalog of ion abnormalities, this review synthesizes the available evidence into a systems-level model of ion–metabolism interactions in MetS and identifies major unresolved mechanistic questions. This framework highlights the interconnected ion–metabolism network as a relevant feature of metabolic dysregulation in MetS and provides a basis for future studies integrating ionomics with metabolic, molecular, and spatially resolved approaches.

Article.Title: Genetics of the Leading Causes of Death in Human Aging
Article.Authors: Martignoni A.; Cai W.; Calderon V.; Aguinaldo C.; Park K.; Murakami S.
Article.Abstract: The relationship between age-related genetic factors and health conditions is crucial in aging research, particularly with respect to the leading global causes of mortality identified by the World Health Organization (WHO). To investigate the direct impact of these genes, we conducted a disease association analysis that compared 307 age-related genes with multiple control gene sets. Our results showed that the age-related gene set was significantly enriched with 113 disease categories compared to the controls, achieving a stringent false discovery rate (FDR) of less than 1 × 10−5. Interestingly, the disease ontology categories did not align directly with the WHO’s primary causes, leading us to reclassify them using the ICD-11 framework. Our analysis revealed that age-related genes are enriched among leading causes of death, particularly those affecting the cardiovascular system, brain, and lungs. We identified 15 recurring genes, including TNF, AKT1, IL6, and CDKN2A, with no evident publication bias, except for TP53, which may have a modest effect. These genes are associated with cancer, inflammatory diseases, and metabolic disorders, highlighting protein–protein networks in nitric oxide regulation and insulin signaling. This study provides a comprehensive analysis and reclassification of the genetic factors linked to human aging and health outcomes, generating key hypotheses in human aging.

Article.Title: Molasses-Assisted Green Combustion Synthesis of LaFeO3 Perovskites: Structural and Interfacial Insights for the Simultaneous Electrochemical Determination of Acetaminophen and 4-Aminoantipyrine
Article.Authors: Alfonso-Gonzalez J.; Paredes-Cuarán A.; Toro-Corrales V.; Renteria-Moreno L.; Hernández-Herrera C.; Morales-Morales J.
Article.Abstract: Sugarcane molasses-assisted combustion was employed to synthesize two LaFeO3 perovskite formulations (ELF-4 and ELF-6). X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement supported the formation of the orthorhombic Pnma structure, while vibrational spectroscopy and electron microscopy revealed formulation-associated differences in surface-related features and aggregate morphology. Cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy demonstrated distinct interfacial responses without establishing a generalized enhancement in electron-transfer kinetics following LaFeO3 modification. At pH 3.5, ELF-4-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes (ELF-4/SPCE) exhibited distinguishable oxidation signals for acetaminophen (AC) and 4-aminoantipyrine (4-AAP). Differential pulse voltammetry of equimolar mixtures provided concentration-dependent responses over 20–180 µM, with sensitivities of 0.0969 µA µM−1 for AC (R2 = 0.997) and 0.0192 µA µM−1 for 4-AAP (R2 = 0.927). Cross-concentration experiments revealed asymmetric analyte interactions, indicating that peak discrimination does not necessarily ensure independent quantitative responses. Exploratory measurements in diluted and fortified campus garden fountain and tap water samples yielded distinguishable signals, although joint standard additions did not establish reliable individual quantification. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of molasses-derived LaFeO3 as an electrochemical sensing modifier while identifying limitations that must be addressed for accurate simultaneous analysis.

Article.Title: The Chemistry of Ash Dieback: Fungal Metabolites, Host Defence and Endophytes
Article.Authors: Pawłowicz T.
Article.Abstract: Ash dieback combines fungal chemical activity with tissue-specific host defence and interactions with associated microorganisms. This structured narrative review integrates the constituents of Hymenoscyphus fraxineus, ash tissues and fungal associates, and reanalyses public leaf metabolomics data at the genotype level. The fungal repertoire includes furanosteroids, glycosides, a tetramic acid, volatile lactones and extracellular carbohydrates. Fraxetin shows recurring associations with lower-susceptibility bark and has experimentally demonstrated antifungal activity; recent evidence of pathogen-mediated depletion adds a dynamic dimension to host chemistry. Secoiridoid associations depend on candidate identity and sampling context, with the strongest support for several matched candidates concentrated in the Danish panel. Reanalysis of 13 European ash genotypes detected no susceptibility-category association in the primary 54-feature leaf profile (R2=0.047, p=0.915); alternative prevalence filters gave consistent results, with feature-dependent precision. Mature-tree phenolics varied with site and year, while crown-damage coefficients remained near zero in the selected endpoints. Phomopsidin, PF1140, CJ-17,572 and mycorrhizin A inhibited the pathogen in compound assays, and plant observations distinguished antagonism from host compatibility. The synthesis identifies tissue, chemical state and environmental context as essential coordinates of ash chemical phenotyping, connecting molecular evidence with the interpretation of forest disease and host survival.

Article.Title: Lipid Droplet Remodeling at the Glia–Neuron Interface: Metabolic Sinks, Flux Traps, and Therapeutic Pitfalls in Neurodegeneration
Article.Authors: Fu M.; Su Y.; Hu G.; Luo X.
Article.Abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neurological decline, metabolic dysfunction, and chronic neuroinflammatory changes. Dysregulated lipid handling has emerged as an important component of these processes, but the functional significance of lipid droplets (LDs) remains strongly context-dependent. Here, we review LD biogenesis, turnover, and cell type-specific functions in the central nervous system (CNS) and critically evaluate evidence linking LD remodeling to neurodegeneration. Transient LD formation can buffer excess or oxidation-prone lipids and support metabolic adaptation, whereas persistent lipid retention in the setting of impaired lysosomal, mitochondrial, or lipid-export capacity is associated with cellular dysfunction. We compare human tissue data, genetic evidence, LD-specific perturbations, pharmacological studies, and experimental models across Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and Huntington’s disease (HD). Particular attention is given to microglial lipid-associated states, neuron–glia lipid transfer, monogenic disorders of lipid handling, and apparently opposing outcomes of LD manipulation in different disease contexts. Rather than treating LD accumulation as a universal pathogenic mechanism, we propose LD remodeling as a candidate metabolic–inflammatory convergence state whose functional consequences depend on cell type, lipid composition, turnover capacity, and disease stage. Translational strategies should therefore prioritize direct measurements of LD flux, demonstration of CNS target engagement, and biomarker-guided patient and disease-stage selection. We further define experimental findings that would support or falsify the proposed convergence model.

Article.Title: Astragaloside IV Attenuates Arsenic-Induced Myocardial Injury and Reduces Galectin-3 Expression: A Network Toxicology and In Vivo Study
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Dong R.; Xie Y.; Zhan L.; Zhu X.; Chen S.; Lu T.; Cai T.
Article.Abstract: Arsenic-induced myocardial injury (AIMI) is a cardiovascular consequence of arsenic exposure. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV), a primary bioactive compound from Astragalus membranaceus, is known for its cardioprotective properties, yet its efficacy against AIMI remains unexplored. This study combined network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vivo experiments to assess AS-IV’s protective effects and potential mechanisms in AIMI. We identified 101 overlapping targets between AS-IV and AIMI. Functional enrichment implicated apoptosis-related processes and inflammatory pathways in AS-IV’s actions. Five hub genes—LGALS3, MMP9, IL2, AR, and BCL2L1—were identified. Docking and simulations predicted potential interactions of AS-IV with MMP-9 and galectin-3 (encoded by MMP9 and LGALS3). In vivo, AS-IV ameliorated arsenic-induced histopathological damage and reduced cTnI levels. Arsenic exposure decreased myocardial GSH-Px activity but increased T-SOD activity, whereas MDA levels showed no statistically significant changes across groups. AS-IV restored GSH-Px activity and further increased T-SOD activity without significantly altering MDA levels. In addition, AS-IV attenuated cardiomyocyte apoptosis, as evidenced by reduced TUNEL positivity and cleaved caspase-3 expression. Notably, arsenic upregulated galectin-3, which AS-IV dose-dependently reduced, while MMP-9 remained unchanged in this early-stage model, consistent with minimal fibrosis. Further bioinformatic analyses linked galectin-3 to early immune-inflammatory and extracellular matrix remodeling signals. In conclusion, AS-IV attenuated arsenic-induced myocardial injury and cardiomyocyte apoptosis in mice. The protective effects were accompanied by changes in oxidative stress-related enzyme activities and reduced myocardial Galectin-3 expression. These findings suggest that galectin-3 may represent a candidate target associated with AS-IV treatment, although its causal involvement in the cardioprotective effects of AS-IV requires further investigation.

Article.Title: Implementing Measurable Residual Disease Assessment in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Methods, Clinical Decisions, and a Tiered Framework for Resource-Limited Settings
Article.Authors: Abusalim E.; Harb M.; Shamieh A.; Kamal N.; Barakat F.; Almasri N.; Abdel Rahman Z.
Article.Abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) is a well-established prognostic biomarker in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), although randomized evidence that MRD-guided monitoring improves overall survival is so far limited to prespecified molecular subgroups. This review compares current MRD methods (multiparameter flow cytometry, polymerase chain reaction, and next-generation sequencing), outlines their benefits and drawbacks, and discusses the prognostic significance of MRD at different time points during treatment. We summarize the 2025 ELN-DAVID recommendations, which address the integration of MRD status into decisions on treatment escalation or de-escalation and on the timing of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. We discuss the time points at which MRD should be assessed, including after intensive chemotherapy, after hypomethylating agents combined with venetoclax, and around transplantation. We also discuss open questions in FLT3-mutated and NPM1-mutated disease, including low-level MRD and treatment cessation. Factors affecting the accuracy of MRD assessment are also covered, such as sample hemodilution, peripheral blood testing, and the uneven standardization of flow cytometric and molecular assays. Finally, we consider how to implement MRD assessment when infrastructure, reagents, or downstream interventions are limited, and propose a tiered framework that matches modality to local capability.

Article.Title: SPNS2 in Cancer: From Sphingosine-1-Phosphate Transport to Tumor Progression
Article.Authors: Bassi R.; Giussani P.
Article.Abstract: Spinster homolog 2 (SPNS2) is a membrane transporter that regulates sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) export and tissue S1P homeostasis. By controlling extracellular S1P availability, SPNS2 influences immune-cell trafficking, vascular and lymphatic function, inflammation, and cellular metabolism. Increasing evidence implicates SPNS2 in cancer, although its effects are highly context-dependent. In tumor cells, SPNS2 can regulate survival, apoptosis, proliferation, migration, invasion, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, and metastatic behavior through mechanisms involving S1P signaling and potentially additional metabolic effects. Divergent effects across and within tumor types highlight the importance of S1P receptor expression, intracellular versus extracellular S1P pools, downstream signaling, and tumor genetic and microenvironmental context. Beyond cancer cell-intrinsic functions, SPNS2 modulates the tumor microenvironment through S1P-dependent immune-cell trafficking and may influence metastatic colonization. Recent structural studies have provided insights into SPNS2-mediated S1P transport, while the development of selective and orally bioavailable inhibitors has demonstrated the feasibility of pharmacologically targeting this pathway. Here, we review the emerging role of SPNS2 in cancer, focusing on its molecular mechanisms, context-dependent functions, and therapeutic perspectives.

Article.Title: Targeting DNA Ligase III Addiction in T-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia by the Natural Flavonoid Rhamnetin
Article.Authors: Signorelli S.; Juli G.; Ascrizzi S.; Polerà N.; Gaetano M.; Squillacioti S.; Altomare E.; Gagliardi A.; Tassone P.; Tagliaferri P.; Grillone K.; Pensabene L.; Caracciolo D.
Article.Abstract: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is an aggressive malignancy with dismal outcomes in relapsed/refractory settings, where nelarabine remains the sole approved agent with limited frontline efficacy. Genomic instability in T-ALL is sustained by a rewired DNA repair network, yet the functional reliance on DNA Ligase III (LIG3)-dependent alternative non-homologous end joining remains largely unexplored. By interrogating public transcriptomic cohorts, functional DepMap datasets, and siRNA-mediated knockdown, we evaluated LIG3 expression and essentiality in T-ALL. Pharmacological targeting was evaluated using Rhamnetin (RHM), a previously characterized LIG3-binding flavonoid, alone or combined with nelarabine across T-ALL cell lines and healthy peripheral blood mononuclear cells. LIG3 mRNA was uniformly expressed across T-ALL oncogenic subgroups. Functional assays confirmed LIG3 essentiality in T-ALL models. RHM dose-dependently reduced viability and clonogenic potential while sparing healthy cells. Mechanistically, RHM triggered a canonical DNA damage response with CHK1/CHK2 phosphorylation and γH2AX accumulation, driving CDC25A down-regulation, cell cycle perturbation, and apoptosis. Furthermore, RHM enhanced the anti-leukemic efficacy of nelarabine, displaying synergistic to additive interactions. These findings suggest LIG3 as an actionable dependency in T-ALL cells and support LIG3 inhibition, alone or combined with nelarabine, for therapeutic development.

Article.Title: Accelerating MAPK1 Inhibitor Discovery Through Stacking Ensemble Learning with Graph Neural Networks
Article.Authors: Srisongkram T.; Duy H.; Paiboon S.; Piyasawetkul T.; Zetta D.; Kampaengsri S.; Weerapreeyakul N.
Article.Abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1) plays a central role in cancer cell proliferation and survival. In this study, we developed an ensemble graph neural network framework integrating graph convolutional neural networks, graph message-passing neural networks, and attention-based graph neural networks to predict MAPK1 inhibitory activity using large-scale quantitative high-throughput screening data. Our models achieved recall ranging from 79.5% to 92.3%, areas under the precision–recall curve ranging from 80.4% to 90.3%, and Matthews correlation coefficients ranging from 0.523 to 0.725 on the independent test set, demonstrating a strong ability to identify MAPK1 inhibitors. The Y-randomization test further confirmed a true relationship between molecular graph structure and MAPK1 inhibitory activity. We also defined the model’s applicability domain to establish clear boundaries for confident prediction. To experimentally validate this approach, we evaluated the approved MAPK1 inhibitor ulixertinib and tested multiple FDA-approved kinase inhibitors, which underscored the model’s predictive ability in the drug development pipeline. Furthermore, we applied the developed models to predict and experimentally validate natural products as potential novel MAPK1 inhibitors. Finally, we developed a web server to deploy this model, enabling rapid and cost-effective identification of MAPK1 inhibitors for hit screening experiments prior to substantial in vitro testing.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic Profiling Pre- and Post-Dupilumab Treatment in Atopic Dermatitis Using Minimally Invasive Microneedle Sampling: A Pilot Study
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Hong N.; Kim J.; Gwag H.; Kim J.; Jeong D.; Ahn J.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: Individual differences in dupilumab treatment response remain an unmet need. This pilot study aimed to explore transcriptomic changes and candidate molecular signals that may reflect disease activity and treatment response by analyzing gene expression changes in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) using a minimally invasive microneedle-based skin sampling method (MISSM). Lesional and non-lesional skin samples were collected from six patients with moderate to severe AD before and 16 weeks after dupilumab treatment, and only samples exceeding a predefined complementary RNA (cRNA) yield threshold following pico-scale RNA amplification were analyzed by microarray. Transcriptome profiling identified several genes, including immunoglobulin variable-region and T-cell receptor genes, that showed correlation trends with clinical improvement (change in Eczema Area and Severity Index, ΔEASI) and significant changes after treatment in the responder group. Baseline expression of other immune-related genes, such as chemokines and immunoglobulins, differed between responders and non-responders. As these findings were derived from a small, non-independent cohort, they should be regarded as exploratory signals rather than validated biomarkers. We also demonstrated that MISSM is a feasible platform for multi-layered analysis of molecular changes in AD, supporting its potential utility for longitudinal treatment response monitoring and molecular profiling in chronic inflammatory skin disease.

Article.Title: Terminalia chebula Retz. Ethyl Acetate Fraction and Chebulagic Acid Attenuate IL-6/IL-1β-Driven Migration and Invasion of Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Cells and Modulate AKT/GSK3β Signaling
Article.Authors: Srisawad K.; Semmarath W.; Arjsri P.; Intanil I.; Thippraphan P.; Dejkriengkraikul P.
Article.Abstract: Chronic inflammation within the prostate tumor microenvironment drives disease progression, in part because locally released cytokines make malignant cells more motile and better able to invade surrounding tissue. Plant-derived bioactive compounds may offer a potential strategy for attenuating inflammation-associated tumor aggressiveness. This study investigated the effects of the ethyl acetate fraction of Terminalia chebula Retz. (TC-EA) and its major constituent, chebulagic acid, on inflammation-stimulated migration and the invasion of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) cells. TC-EA was obtained by solvent-partitioning and chemically characterized using the Folin–Ciocalteu method and high-performance liquid chromatography. DU145 and PC3 cells were pretreated with TC-EA or chebulagic acid and subsequently exposed to conditioned medium derived from LPS-exposed THP-1 M1-like macrophages (M1-THP-1-CM), which contained elevated levels of IL-6 and IL-1β. Cell migration and invasion were assessed using wound-healing and Transwell invasion assays, respectively, while gelatin zymography, RT-qPCR, and Western blotting were used to evaluate invasion-associated molecular changes. TC-EA contained 511.12 ± 33.02 mg GAE/g extract of total phenolics and 264.34 ± 13.26 mg/g extract of chebulagic acid. M1-THP-1-CM significantly enhanced the migration and invasion in both cell lines, whereas neutralization of IL-6 or IL-1β attenuated these effects. TC-EA (10–40 μg/mL) and chebulagic acid (5–20 µM) significantly reduced M1-THP-1-CM-enhanced migration and invasion (p < 0.05). These effects were associated with reduced MMP-2 and MMP-9 activities, decreased expression of the invasion-associated proteins uPA, uPAR, and MT1-MMP, increased E-cadherin expression, and decreased N-cadherin and MT1-MMP mRNA expression (p < 0.01), and attenuated phosphorylation of AKT and GSK3β. These findings suggest that TC-EA and chebulagic acid may attenuate inflammation-driven migration and invasion of CRPC cells, potentially involving modulation of cytokine-associated AKT/GSK3β signaling.

Article.Title: Divergent Roles of LBD16 and LBD18 Transcription Factors During Lateral Root Primordium Initiation Within the Parental Root Meristem of Cucurbits
Article.Authors: Kiryushkin A.; Ilina E.; Kukushkin V.; Kuznetsov S.; Samukha M.; Guseva E.; Pawlowski K.; Demchenko K.
Article.Abstract: The LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN (LBD) transcription factors LBD16 and LBD18 are master regulators of lateral root (LR) initiation in Arabidopsis thaliana, but their conservation in Cucurbitaceae, where LRs initiate within the parental root meristem, remains poorly understood. Here, we identified the cucumber (Cucumis sativus) orthologs of AtLBD16 and AtLBD18, investigating their roles via phylogenetic analysis, RT-qPCR profiling of auxin-dependent gene regulation, spatial expression visualization, and functional CRES-T analysis. Comparative analysis of spatial expression patterns revealed an evolutionary reprogramming of transcriptional networks governing root organogenesis in Cucurbitaceae. Native CsLBD16 promoter activity was detected in the quiescent center and root cap but was absent during early LR initiation, whereas CsLBD18 expression was confined to the central cylinder and developing primordia. Notably, unlike in Arabidopsis, where LBD16 is essential for the earliest steps of LR initiation, functional analysis confirmed that CsLBD16 is dispensable for this process in cucumber. Furthermore, CsLBD18 occupies a unique, essential position in the genetic cascade regulating cucumber adventitious root development, whereas CsLBD16 and CsLBD30 play no role in this pathway. Together, our findings demonstrate a significant functional divergence of LBD genes between Arabidopsis and cucumber, necessitating further investigation into the specific role of CsLBD18 in cucumber root development.

Article.Title: Comprehensive Analysis of Protein Expression Profiles in Seeds of the Gene-Edited High Oleic Acid Soybean Variety P16
Article.Authors: Guo C.; Wang R.; Yang Z.; Liu W.; Jin W.
Article.Abstract: This study systematically characterized seed proteome dynamics across three consecutive generations (T5–T7) of the fad2-1 (encoding Δ-12 fatty acid desaturase, catalyzing the conversion of oleic acid to linoleic acid) gene-edited high-oleic acid soybean variety P16 using data-independent acquisition (DIA)-based quantitative proteomics. Functional enrichment analysis revealed significant representation of these DEPs in Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways related to “protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum (ER)” and/or “peroxisome.” Furthermore, eight proteins were consistently differentially expressed across all three generations—hereafter referred to as consistently differentially expressed proteins (coDEPs). The preliminary in silico evaluation of the toxicity, anti-nutritional properties, and allergenicity of the coDEPs indicated that all identified coDEPs were predicted to be non-toxic and non-allergenic, and to lack anti-nutritional activity—except for the STI1 domain-containing protein, which was computationally predicted to exhibit allergenic potential. Mass spectrometry (MS) analysis demonstrated a significant and consistent decrease in the abundance of the FAD2-1-associated peptide in P16 seeds across all three generations relative to the wild-type soybean cultivar ZH42.

Article.Title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the Bromodomain Gene Family in Olive (Olea europaea) and Its Association with Salt Stress Responses
Article.Authors: Alotaibi H.; Alsaadi N.; Siraj H.; Almalki S.; Alsaieb S.; Albishi S.; Alrasheed M.
Article.Abstract: Bromodomain (BRD) proteins are evolutionarily conserved epigenetic readers that bind acetylated lysine residues on histone tails, linking chromatin remodeling to transcriptional regulation and abiotic stress adaptation. Although salinity is among the most economically damaging abiotic stresses worldwide, the bromodomain-level epigenetic mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in the perennial crop olive (Olea europaea L.) remain unstudied. This study aimed to identify and characterize the complete Olea europaea bromodomain (OeBRD) gene family in olive, resolve its evolutionary relationships with Arabidopsis thaliana, and identify candidate genes potentially associated with salt-stress responses. Genome-wide identification, physicochemical characterization, promoter cis-regulatory element analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, orthogroup clustering, conserved-motif and gene-structure analysis, AlphaFold3 structural modeling, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data (BioProject PRJNA841838) from control, primed (75 → 150 mM NaCl) and non-primed (150 mM NaCl) plants, and Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING)-based protein–protein interaction (PPI) and Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analyses were performed. Twenty-one non-redundant OeBRD genes were identified in the O. europaea genome (GCF_002742605.1), with molecular weights of 43,076–242,620 Da, isoelectric points of 5.05–9.67, and universally negative grand average of hydropathicity (GRAVY) values. Phylogenetic analysis resolved four clades, including olive-specific paralog groups, and orthogroup clustering against A. thaliana identified 16 orthogroups, eight of which are strict 1:1 orthologs, five show copy-number differences between the two species (more copies in olive in three groups, including OeBRD6a/6b/6c, and more copies in Arabidopsis in two), one is a balanced 2:2 group and two contain only Arabidopsis genes. Multiple Em for Motif Elicitation (MEME) analysis identified 10 conserved motifs. Promoter analysis revealed abundant abscisic acid (ABA)-, myeloblastosis (MYB)/myelocytomatosis (MYC)- and jasmonate-responsive cis-elements. DESeq2 differential expression analysis of primed (75→150 mM NaCl) and non-primed (150 mM NaCl) plants relative to untreated controls identified four of the 21 OeBRD genes as significantly differentially expressed (adjusted p < 0.05): OeBRD6b, OeBRD6c, OeBRD10 and OeBRD26 were up-regulated in primed roots, OeBRD26 was also up-regulated in non-primed roots and non-primed leaves, and no gene was significant in primed leaves; STRING PPI analysis identified OeBRD24 and OeBRD13 as the most connected nodes in a network inferred from Arabidopsis orthologues, with chromatin, chromatin remodeling and histone acetyltransferase activity among the most significantly enriched GO terms. Ten proteins—OeBRD26, OeBRD6c, OeBRD6b, OeBRD10, OeBRD13, OeBRD24, OeBRD11, OeBRD16, OeBRD28 and OeBRD29—were prioritized as candidates for future experimental validation of a possible role in salt-stress responses in olive.

Article.Title: Physiological, Reproductive, and Molecular Responses of Perna viridis to Aquaculture Wastewater Bioremediation
Article.Authors: Noor Z.; Tang Y.; Huang W.; Shi Y.; Gu Z.
Article.Abstract: Mussels are considered active biofilters that filter suspended and dissolved components of water and can be used in aquaculture. We studied the role of green mussels (Perna viridis) in filtering aquaculture effluent and its effects on gametogenesis and physiological processes. We established four experimental groups: G1, G2, G3, and G4. Groups G1 and G2 received fish-cultured wastewater and shrimp-cultured wastewater, respectively. Group G3 received low-nutrient seawater, whereas G4 served as a mussel-free control and received low-nutrient seawater under otherwise identical experimental conditions. The impact of biofiltration was evaluated by analyzing gonad morphology, gene expression, and physiological energetics. The results show a significant change in the gonadal structure, with low spermatozoa and spermatid content characterizing G1, and adipogranular cells becoming more prominent. G2 showed a comparatively high number of sperm cells, with spermatozoa becoming more prominent in the gonads. G3 is characterized by elevated sperm volume. CASA semen analysis showed low sperm counts and reduced motility and other kinematic parameters in G1 and G2. The Gonadosomatic Index (GSI) and Condition Index (CI) indicated better physiological condition in G2 and G3, with the highest survival rate in G2. Quantitative real-time PCR results revealed the expression of genes in the hepatopancreas, with high expression (p < 0.05) of Glutathione S-transferases (gst-o1), Heat shock protein 60 (hsp60), Heat shock protein 70 (hsp70), Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), superoxide dismutase (SOD1), and a key sensor of oxidative and electrophilic stress-1 (KEAP1). Ammonia excretion was high in the G1 and G2 groups, and oxygen consumption was initially high in G1 and G2, later declining until the 21st day, while in G3 a stable trend was observed. Despite P. viridis’s positive role in bioremediation, aquaculture effluents negatively impact reproductive functions; moreover, P. viridis filtration augmented the decrease in nutrient content along with other abiotic components in the recirculating aquaculture in the G1 and G2 groups, confirming its role as a biofilter and helping with the reuse of aquaculture effluents.

Article.Title: Morroniside in Ischemic Stroke: Preclinical Evidence and a Proposed Stage-Dependent Framework for Neurovascular Repair
Article.Authors: Zhu L.; Sun F.; Ma Y.; Li D.; Liu T.; Tian X.; Zheng W.; Zhu Z.; Wang Y.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability. Although thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy have improved reperfusion, secondary neurovascular injury and incomplete tissue repair remain important challenges. Morroniside (MOR), an iridoid glycoside from Cornus officinalis, has shown neuroprotective and repair-associated effects in experimental stroke models. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical evidence from 11 eligible in vivo cerebral ischemia or post-stroke recovery studies identified through searches of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus. Reported findings associate MOR treatment with changes in neuroinflammation, pyroptosis, oxidative stress, apoptosis, blood–brain barrier (BBB) integrity, angiogenesis, and neural progenitor responses. On this basis, we propose a hypothesis-generating, stage-dependent framework that organizes injury-associated and repair-associated outcomes according to their reported post-ischemic timing. These outcomes may represent complementary aspects of MOR activity, but because the findings derive from separate experiments, they do not establish a validated temporal sequence or stage-specific treatment regimen. Inconsistent methodological reporting and unresolved questions about brain exposure, target engagement, treatment timing, and safety also limit translational interpretation. MOR therefore merits further investigation as a potential adjunct to reperfusion and rehabilitation, although its efficacy and therapeutic window require rigorous validation before clinical application.

Article.Title: Genome-Wide Identification and Population-Based Genetic Dissection of Amino Acid Transporter (AAT) Gene Family in Maize
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Shen J.; Li X.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Long-term yield-oriented breeding reduces maize kernel protein content, whereas excessive nitrogen fertilization raises cultivation costs and causes environmental pollution. Amino acid transporters (AATs) are key regulators of plant nitrogen allocation, governing crop nitrogen-use efficiency and grain quality. Here, we systematically identified 98 ZmAAT genes from the latest B73 RefGen_v5 maize genome and classified them into 12 subfamilies. Furthermore, pangenome-wide analysis across 26 diverse maize inbred lines and 8 wild relatives revealed extensive structural polymorphisms, presence/absence variations (PAVs), and core–shell–cloud orthogroup classifications. Segmental duplication primarily drove AAT superfamily expansion; pangenome-level duplication and selection pressure analyses confirmed that all duplicated paralogs experienced strong purifying selection to preserve conserved amino-acid-transport functions. Using metabolite-based genome-wide association study (mGWAS) on 378 diverse maize inbred lines, we uncovered a major pleiotropic hotspot on chromosome 5 containing ZmCAT7 and ZmCAT8 as key candidate genes. Their natural variations are significantly associated with accumulations of glutamine, phenylalanine, and glutamic-acid derivatives. These results highlight ZmCAT7 and ZmCAT8 as promising targets for future functional validation and potential genetic improvement of maize grain quality.

Article.Title: Increased Relative Abundance of Lactobacilli Species in the Gut Microbiota of Patients with Crohn’s Disease and Ulcerative Colitis
Article.Authors: Khusnutdinova D.; Markelova M.; Senina A.; Siniagina M.; Boulygina E.; Abdulkhakov S.; Grigoryeva T.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), are associated with gut microbiota alterations. While lactobacilli are traditionally considered beneficial probiotics, recent studies report their increased abundance in IBD, suggesting a more complex role. This study aimed to assess the species diversity and representation of lactobacilli in CD and UC patients compared to healthy volunteers. Fecal samples from 40 CD patients, 40 UC patients, and 42 healthy controls were analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing, shotgun metagenomic sequencing, and qPCR. Over 28% of IBD patients harbored six or more lactobacilli species versus only 2% of controls. Species-level analysis identified Ligilactobacillus salivarius, Lactobacillus gasseri, and Limosilactobacillus mucosae as having significantly higher relative abundances in IBD patients. The increased occurrence of specific species with known virulence potential challenges the traditional view of lactobacilli as universally beneficial, indicating that certain lactobacilli may be associated with dysbiosis in IBD.
