Article.Title: Where to improve the European protected areas network to represent threatened fungi?
Article.Authors: Copoț O.; Runnel K.; Lõhmus A.
Article.Abstract: To set a global example in biodiversity conservation, the European Union aims to protect 30% and strictly protect 10% of its land by 2030 and to invest in ecosystem restoration. Comparing distributions of predicted habitats with existing protected-area networks provided robust evidence of large, uneven protection gaps among species and countries. Article.Authors: Tao S.; Wang L.; Zhu Z.; Lee D.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid advancement of general-purpose AI, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to simulate human decisions in structured environments. Article.Title: An integrated framework for agroclimatic, salinity, and groundwater assessment in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan
Article.Authors: Amanov B.; Ghirardelli A.; Sherov A.; Gafarova A.; Gulomov D.; Tarolli P.
Article.Abstract: Climate change, salinization, and water scarcity increasingly threaten irrigated agricultural landscapes in arid regions. This study developed an integrated framework combining hydro-climatic, soil, and groundwater indicators to assess agricultural landscapes in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan. Integrated assessment scores ranged from 11 to 16 points, classifying most districts as unsatisfactory in 2021 and satisfactory during 2022-2024. Zafarabad and, occasionally, Sh. Rashidov exhibited the lowest overall scores. The framework provides a practical tool for monitoring landscape vulnerability and supporting irrigation, reclamation, and salinity-management decisions.

Article.Title: Revolutionizing drought defense: The water-plant-microbe synergy in climate-smart agriculture
Article.Authors: Wang W.; He Z.; Chen J.; Ding R.; Wang L.; Chen M.; Kang J.; Tong L.; Du T.
Article.Abstract: Global warming-induced water scarcity threatens agricultural sustainability. While precision irrigation and microbial inoculants are recognized as effective individual strategies, their synergistic potential remains under-explored. This review synthesizes recent advances in the "water-plant-microbe" synergy to propose a bidirectional regulatory mechanism for climate-smart agriculture. We demonstrate that irrigation regimes function as a primary filter for rhizosphere microbial assembly, thereby defining the hydraulic niche for colonization. Conversely, functional microbes actively engineer the soil environment via exopolysaccharide production and hormonal modulation, thereby enhancing plant hydraulic status and water use efficiency (WUE). In contrast to previous reviews focusing on single factors, this review constructs an integrated framework linking soil hydrology with microbial ecology, supported by emerging comparative evidence. We conclude that future agricultural water management must shift from solely regulating water supply to managing the holobiont's hydrological interactions, offering a promising systems-level strategy to safeguard food security under climate stress.

Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents a critical window for dementia prevention, yet the comparative efficacy of diverse exercise modalities remains unclear. Article.Abstract: 6-Phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3 (PFKFB3), a key regulator of glycolysis highly expressed in many tumor cells, has a critical role in promoting glycolysis and tumor progression. Article.Abstract: During the 70-million-year Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity over 3-fold. Article.Title: Context shapes action understanding in social interactions
Article.Authors: Keck J.; Sato K.; Cañal-Bruland R.
Article.Abstract: In social interactions, individuals anticipate what others are about to do next, enabling smooth social interactions and coexistence in daily life. Article.Title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies
Article.Authors: Farhadzadeh F.; Borji A.; Aram C.; Alishvandi A.; Kamali M.; Rahimi M.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

Article.Title: Key genes and pathways of pulmonary hypertension identified by integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing

These effects emerged well after stimulus onset and generalized to earlier time points, indicating a modulation of visual processing during continuous input. Our findings demonstrate that visual information is represented more accurately at specific alpha phases. Carcass-mediated transmission, wild boar density, movement, habitat conditions, and seasonal variation were important factors influencing ASF occurrence and spread. Article.Title: Senescence and tumor immunology: A multifaceted interplay of influence
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zhang J.; Wang S.; Rao D.; Zhang J.; Ao Y.
Article.Abstract: Medical advances and global population aging have propelled aging and cancer research into a new period of discovery. Senescent cells, which exert context-dependent tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects, are central to this progress and engage in complex crosstalk with tumor proliferation. This review critically examines the multidimensional interplay between aging and cancer by synthesizing genetic, cytokine signaling, and tissue microenvironment evidence. We discuss how senescent cells influence immune surveillance, therapy response, tumor progression, metastasis, and age-related cancer risk, while cellular diversity, molecular complexity, immune balance, tumor heterogeneity, treatment resistance, and individual aging variability further complicate this relationship. We conclude that aging and cancer are intertwined through dynamic, context-specific mechanisms. By integrating these insights, this review aims to inspire novel research directions and transformative advances in cancer therapy and healthy longevity.

Article.Abstract: Conscious visual phenomenology comprises multiple representational levels, from basic features to integrated percepts, raising the question of how the neural correlates of consciousness (NCC) differentiate accordingly. Event-related potential (ERP) studies identified early occipitotemporal negativities as reliable NCC; yet, it remains unclear whether these capture conscious content beyond low-level features and extend to higher-order representations. Article.Title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
Article.Authors: Paraskevopoulos E.; Bamidis P.
Article.Abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Article.Authors: Krapf P.; Heidbreder P.; Bruijning M.; Meirmans P.; Stankowski S.; Kulmuni J.

Article.Title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice
Article.Authors: Tomita K.; Nakano T.; Morozumi S.; Okahashi N.; Arita M.
Article.Abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. The levels of sitosterol sulfate (SIS), campesterol sulfate, and stigmasterol sulfate, the three major phytosterol sulfates, along with coprostanol sulfate, were reduced in the feces of germ-free mice compared with those of specific pathogen-free mice. We characterized a series of Bacteroidota species and their sterol sulfotransferases that produced phytosterol sulfates more efficiently than mammalian enzymes. Article.Abstract: The mechanical tumor microenvironment critically influences colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis, yet the underlying molecular mediators remain poorly defined. Article.Title: Linking nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal microbiota to immune responses during influenza-like illness in an aging population
Article.Authors: Kool J.; Konstanti P.; van Dijken H.; Chu M.; Nanlohy N.; Bijvank E.; van Woudenbergh E.; van Beek J.; van Baarle D.; Fuentes S.
Article.Abstract: Older adults are vulnerable to influenza-like illness (ILI). Article.Abstract: A substantial percentage of surgical patients develop persistent postsurgical pain, and sleep disruption is an established, modifiable contributor. Article.Authors: Deng C.; Jin Z.; Wu H.; Fang Z.; Yang Y.; Zhao Q.; Hang J.; Zhang Z.; Jiang H.

Article.Title: A linear calibration method for scattering semiconductors using the Kubelka-Munk function
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Luo L.; Zhang F.; Jiang B.; Jaroniec M.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Absorption spectroscopy of solids is hindered by strong scattering, which violates assumptions underlying the Beer-Lambert (BL) law. In contrast, KMF increases linearly with mass fraction within a low-loading regime, and the relation persists across distinct morphologies. This work underscores a simple, rapid, and non-destructive calibration strategy for scattering semiconductors that uses KMF as a linear axis for composition.

Article.Abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) has a high mortality rate, creating an urgent need to identify novel therapeutic targets. Aberrant expression of bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) is associated with the progression of several cancers. Previous reports demonstrated that BMP2 is highly expressed in tumor tissues and serum of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the pathological roles and mechanisms of BMP2 in LUSC progression, and the mechanism underlying the overexpression of BMP2 remain to be elucidated. In this study, we found that a high level of BMP2 is correlated with poor prognosis in patients with LUSC, and that BMP2 promotes the growth and metastasis of LUSC cells in vitro and in vivo by activating the MAPK-ERK1/2 signaling pathway. Article.Title: StrokeTime: A comprehensive longitudinal scRNA-seq atlas of the ischemic mouse brain
Article.Authors: Anrather J.; Garcia-Bonilla L.
Article.Abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers profound, dynamic changes in the brain's cellular landscape. Myeloid cells showed the greatest plasticity, including disease-associated microglia/macrophage programs shared across resident and infiltrating cells, whereas lymphocytes featured activation and regulatory signatures within lineage constraints. Vascular and mural cells shifted from early inflammatory and barrier-disruptive programs to later fibrotic and angiogenic states. Article.Authors: Xu H.; Gu R.; Serville Torvund A.; Grønlien I.; Xomalis A.; Nguyen H.; Yu Z.; Zhao Z.

Article.Authors: Lingemann M.; McGee T.; Sidoti Migliore G.; DeLuca J.; Whitehead S.; Bonsignori M.

Article.Authors: Hirsch E.; Koren I.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial ecoregions represent coherent ecological units shaped by shared environmental conditions and biological communities. Many of these occur in regions with low direct human modification, suggesting a strong role for large-scale environmental drivers. This framework provides a scalable approach for identifying ecosystems at risk and supports targeted monitoring and conservation planning.

Activated neutrophil supernatants cleaved 5,166 peptides, and inhibition of serine proteases caused 95% reduction in signal. Deconvolution algorithms identified protease signatures for elastase, cathepsin G, and PR3 proportional to their levels in neutrophils. Article.Title: A longitudinal study of rotenone-induced Parkinsonism in mice
Article.Authors: Joshi P.; Fan F.; Lou X.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. Article.Title: A single arm phase II trial of chidamide plus cisplatin in advanced adenoid cystic carcinoma
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Chen G.; Xue K.; Zhang Q.; Xia Z.; Ji D.; Jin J.; Lv F.; Liu X.; Wang Y.; Hong X.; Cao J.
Article.Abstract: Systemic therapy for recurrent or metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma remains limited, and durable disease control is difficult to achieve. Article.Title: Diatom-based treatment of geothermal brines to selectively remove silicon, retain lithium for downstream recovery, and produce omega-3 fatty acids
Article.Authors: Rehmanji M.; Skeffington A.; Hudson-Edwards K.; Newsome L.
Article.Abstract: Silica (SiO2) scaling in geothermal brines processing can hinder energy production and downstream lithium (Li) recovery. Here, we investigate diatom-based selective silicon (Si) removal from brines to support downstream recovery of lithium (Li) and generating biomass for valorization. When cultivated in geothermal brine supplemented with urea, Halamphora sp. removed 34 mg L-1 of Si (97.14%) within 48 h, while retaining over 99% of Li (75 mg L-1) in solution. Urea supplementation also enhanced biomass production, reaching 0.45 g L-1. The resulting biomass contained the omega-3 fatty acids eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; 47 mg g-1) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; 24 mg g-1). These results demonstrate the potential for coupling biological Si removal and Li retention with production of value-added biomass during geothermal brine processing.

Article.Title: NR2F6 functions as a key transcriptional checkpoint enforcing dysfunction of human CD3+ T cells and limiting CAR-T cell potency
Article.Authors: Koutník J.; Gruber T.; Freimark D.; Humer D.; Schreiber D.; Hölzl I.; Lang V.; Tokic N.; Sajinovic T.; Wolf D.; Thuille N.; Siegmund K.; Klepsch V.; Baier G.

In an anti-EGFR CAR-T cell-A549 co-culture model, enforced NR2F6 expression, mimicking its upregulation in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, markedly impairs killing under repeated tumor challenge. Article.Title: Frequency-dependent thalamocortical transfer limits sustained cortical expression of sensory drive
Article.Authors: Yu Z.; Wang H.; Zhuo Y.; Zuo Z.
Article.Abstract: Frequency-dependent sensory drive must pass through thalamocortical pathways before cortical expression, yet how high-frequency input is transformed into sustained cortical activity remains unclear. Peripheral forepaw stimulation revealed intermediate-frequency cortical tuning, whereas thalamic nuclei remained responsive at high frequencies. Direct S1FL activation evoked sustained high-frequency blood-oxygen-level-dependent responses, indicating that cortex can express high-frequency drive when upstream relay is bypassed. These findings identify a frequency-dependent bottleneck in VPL-to-S1FL transfer, rather than local cortical responsiveness, as a constraint on sustained cortical expression of temporally dense sensory input.

Article.Title: Expanding the galactose oxidase substrate repertoire via a multi-modal computational strategy
Article.Authors: Miyajima J.; Tay D.; Yeo W.; Koo Y.; Supekar S.; Chen A.; Chia C.; Muthaliff N.; Teh T.; Fan H.; Lim Y.; Maurer-Stroh S.; Ang E.
Article.Abstract: Biocatalysis offers a greener alternative to chemical processes, yet industrial adoption is bottlenecked by the prohibitive cost of enzyme engineering. Here, we report a multi-modal computational framework that integrates synergistic descriptors of substrate binding, protein stability, and aggregation traits. Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Li S.; Xie L.; Li J.; Wang C.; Li Z.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Hearing loss, a highly prevalent global disease with complex pathogenic mechanisms, poses significant challenges due to limited treatment options and secondary complications. Article.Authors: Chen D.; Kong X.; Zhong H.; Zhang Y.; Si C.; Kasimu A.; Qiao R.; Song Y.; Li B.

Article.Authors: Wang X.; Tan G.; Ni M.; Li J.; Gao F.
Article.Abstract: Lipids are central to membrane organization, signaling, myelination, and metabolic homeostasis in the central nervous system (CNS), where their abundance, turnover, and spatial distribution are tightly regulated. Article.Authors: Vigil-Escalera J.; van Baar J.; Molleman L.; van Duijvenvoorde A.; Ma I.
Article.Abstract: Understanding and predicting others' behavior is a key developmental task in adolescence as social interactions become more complex. Article.Title: The structure of technological learning: Insights from water electrolysis for cost forecasting, policy, and strategy
Article.Authors: Atouife M.; Jenkins J.
Article.Abstract: Forecasting the cost evolution of emerging clean technologies is crucial for informed policy, investment, and decarbonization decisions, yet it remains deeply uncertain. Learning curves, which link cost declines to cumulative deployment, are widely used for technological cost forecasting. However, applying them to emerging technologies is challenging due to parametric uncertainty in learning rates, which are scarce and highly uncertain, and structural uncertainty stemming from multiple plausible learning frameworks. Using water electrolysis as a case study, we evaluate how different learning structures, from shared to fragmented learning across technology variants and regions, alter expected cost paths. We interrogate model assumptions that represent contrasting industrial realities, including competition among electrolyzer variants and supply chain fragmentation associated with protectionism and industrial policy. We find that plausible modeling choices generate widely different trajectories, with materially different implications for policy design and technology strategy. We argue for routinely applying multiple learning frameworks to explore decision spaces and stress-test conclusions for scale-up planning, national industrial strategy, and energy systems modeling.

Article.Title: Working memory gating across sensory modalities reveals modality-specific maintenance mechanisms
Article.Authors: Limburg R.; Beste C.; Prochnow A.
Article.Abstract: The flexible resolution of the conflict between updating and maintenance demands in working memory is thought to rely on a selective gating mechanism. While gating of visual information has been extensively studied, gating of multisensory information remains poorly understood. We addressed this gap by contrasting task performance and accompanying neuro-oscillatory modulations across a purely visual and two audiovisual variants of a working memory gating task. Task-dependent performance differences emerged specifically for gate closing. Across tasks, gate closing was consistently associated with alpha band activity modulations supporting the integration of task-relevant information and beta band activity modulations controlling the reconfiguration of the gate state, while theta band activity modulations were overall negligible. Article.Authors: Tawfik Y.; Diekmann Y.; Orlando L.; Burger J.; Blöcher J.
Article.Abstract: Age-at-death estimation of archaeological human remains is central to paleodemographic research yet remains particularly challenging for adults, where osteological methods often produce imprecise age ranges. Article.Title: Unrealized optimal designs challenge models of constraint in early vertebrate evolution
Article.Authors: Leflaëc E.; Ballell A.; Sanisidro O.; Ferrón H.

Consequently, autophagy is elevated in TGF-β/activin signaling-blocked muscle which in turn has a protective role against the threats to PQC. Hierarchy strengthens near criticality, where slow oscillatory modes dominate and reflects long-range anatomical scaffolding of whole-brain activity. Our decomposition provides the first EC eigenmode-based multiscale representation of temporal irreversibility, revealing dual counterpropagating streams along the unimodal-transmodal axis at distinct frequencies and identifying slow-mode individual-specific signatures, with unimodal networks contributing disproportionately to subject identifiability. Article.Authors: Kallapura G.; Prakash A.; Prasad R.; Josphine I.; Maurya M.; Dhar D.
Article.Abstract: The transition from traditional foraging lifestyles to modernized urban environments is associated with reduced human gut microbiome diversity. Article.Title: Photocatalytic strategies for mitigating microplastic pollution and greenhouse gas emissions
Article.Authors: Salari M.; Lai C.; Saber A.; Akhoundi B.
Article.Abstract: Microplastics contaminate water, soil, and air, and their persistence is linked to greenhouse gas emissions. Photocatalysis can break down these polymers via reactive oxygen species but particle shrinkage alone does not prove complete mineralization. Recent photocatalytic systems are examined, including TiO2-based materials, S-scheme and Z-scheme heterojunctions, laddered architectures, metal-organic frameworks, and g-C3N4 composites. These systems improve charge separation and visible-light harvesting, with some achieving high mineralization under optimized conditions. Verifying true breakdown requires TOC, LC-MS, and GC-MS because incomplete oxidation can produce toxic intermediates. Photocatalysis may also shorten plastic residence times and reduce methane and nitrous oxide emissions, though this depends on carbon fate, catalyst stability, energy inputs, and water chemistry. Combining photocatalysis with renewable energy and water treatment could offer a practical route to microplastic management, provided catalyst recovery, toxicity, and scale-up challenges are addressed.

Article.Authors: Shan Q.; Li J.; Wang Y.; Gupta S.; Song L.; Zhang W.; Su F.; Guo Y.
Article.Abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60-70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. This growing disease burden, together with the progressive loss of cognitive, motor, and communicative functions, highlights the need for more precise approaches to early detection, functional assistance, and individualized intervention. Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

The developed hydrogel demonstrated temporal mechanical reinforcement and prolonged stability, with in vitro studies demonstrating enhanced chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells. Additionally, hemostatic and in vivo studies demonstrated the potential of the DNA-Silk fibroin hydrogel as a promising biomaterial for rapid hemostasis and accelerated wound healing. Article.Title: Connectome analysis reveals brain-wide visual processing in Drosophila
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Kim A.
Article.Abstract: Sensory processing relies on a brain-wide network that integrates specialized sensory circuits with the rest of the brain. Article.Title: Quantum-enhanced trusted execution with dynamic policy optimization for zero-trust edge computing
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Zero-trust edge computing faces escalating security challenges from quantum threats, heterogeneous resources, and dynamic operational conditions. Article.Title: Geographic and thematic gaps in wildfire resilience research

Article.Abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent and destructive around the world, threatening lives, homes, and natural landscapes. Our review of over 1,500 wildfire resilience studies shows that while research is growing, it is unevenly distributed across regions and topics, often focusing on habitats while paying less attention to human communities, infrastructure, and other aspects that matter for people's lives and well-being. Article.Title: Consequences of climate-driven relocation in the Prehispanic US Southwest
Article.Authors: Ortman S.
Article.Abstract: As humanity copes with a warming planet, there is a growing recognition that in some situations entire communities may be forced to relocate. This perspective paper summarizes an especially well-understood episode of climate-driven relocation that took place in the Four Corners region of the US Southwest in the 13th century CE. This episode is well understood due to an exceptional archaeological record with high temporal resolution, oral traditions that have been maintained in descendant communities, a long history of research, and significant investment in synthesis of both archaeological and paleoclimatic records. The account is also well established in that it is based on a robust quantity and quality of evidence and high agreement among experts. Article.Title: Space-number association in zebrafish
Article.Authors: Potrich D.; Zanon M.; Rugani R.; Sovrano V.; Vallortigara G.
Article.Abstract: Spatial-numerical associations reflect the tendency to map small numerosities to the left and larger numerosities to the right. Although widely documented in humans and some non-human species, its presence in teleost fish has remained unclear. Here, we investigated whether zebrafish exhibit a spatial-numerical association by presenting fish with a left-right numerical discrimination task in a controlled behavioral assay. Zebrafish exhibited systematic magnitude-dependent spatial choices, showing a significant spatial shift toward the left for smaller relative to larger numerosities across experimental conditions. These results provide evidence for a number-space association in zebrafish and suggest that number-space mapping may extend to basal vertebrate lineages. This highlights zebrafish as a promising model for investigating the neurobiological mechanisms underlying number-space associations.

Article.Title: Biogeography and monsoon-associated climatic trait evolution in true frogs Rana
Article.Authors: Othman S.; Litvinchuk S.; Maslova I.; Dujsebayeva T.; Chen Y.; Zhang X.; Kohler D.; Hoti J.; Chuang M.; Purevdorj Z.; Bae Y.; Messenger K.; Skorinov D.; Amin H.; Um T.; Min M.; Jang Y.; Borzée A.
Article.Abstract: Climatic variation across latitude shapes lineage diversification and niche evolution. Biogeographic reconstruction supported a northward expansion of the Rana amurensis lineage into Siberia, c. 7.67 Mya, coinciding with relatively warm Arctic conditions. Across lineages, broad latitudinal ranges evolved independently in Eurasian Pelophylax ridibundus, R. amurensis, R. dybowskii, and R. temporaria (c. 30.00 Mya), with additional origins in Nearctic Lithobates catesbeianus and L. sylvaticus (c. 12.00 Mya). Article.Title: AI optimized fertilization and irrigation improve wheat yield and quality in semi-arid calcareous soils
Article.Authors: Hadad M.; Gholami A.
Article.Abstract: Traditional wheat farming in calcareous, low-organic-carbon, semi-arid environments relies on blanket fertilization and calendar-based irrigation, causing low nitrogen use efficiency and poor grain quality. The AI system reduced water use by 12.5% and nitrogen fertilizer by 28% while increasing grain yield by 8.5%. Water productivity improved by 24%, nitrogen use efficiency rose from 43% to 72%, grain protein increased by 13%, zinc by 43%, and iron by 33%. Soil organic carbon increased from 0.42% to 0.48%, microbial biomass carbon increased by 68%, and net greenhouse gas emissions fell by 43%. These findings show that simple, affordable AI tools can support sustainable intensification in semi-arid wheat systems.

Article.Title: Ovarian function via gut microbiota-driven serotonin dysregulation in zebrafish
Article.Authors: Wang N.; Dong T.; Yu K.; Qiu Y.; Lyu D.; Li B.; Yu X.; Jing C.; Jiao X.
Article.Abstract: Ciprofloxacin (CIP) is frequently detected in aquatic environments, yet its effects on reproduction through gut microbiota-mediated pathways remain unclear. Multi-omics analyses revealed gut dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism, including increased serotonin (5-HT) and indole-3-lactic acid associated with Cetobacterium and Plesiomonas shigelloides. Brain transcriptomics showed suppressed hormone signaling and elevated 5-HT, consistent with hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis disruption. FMT from CIP-exposed donors reproduced hormonal and ovarian abnormalities in microbiota-depleted recipients. This study underscores the need to integrate microbiota-host interactions into the risk assessment of emerging aquatic contaminants and highlights the broader implications of environmental exposures for reproductive and endocrine health in both aquatic organisms and potentially humans.

Article.Authors: Barquero-González J.; St. J. Read V.; Montiel-Parra G.; Contreras-Félix G.; Tartara A.; Villagomez F.; Heethoff M.; Mayer G.; de Sena Oliveira I.

Article.Authors: Guo X.; Liu J.; Yang G.; Shang J.; Qiao S.; Dai W.; Ren Y.
Article.Abstract: Stand density is a key management factor affecting vegetation and soil recovery in desert plantations. Compared with higher densities and bare sand, low density improved shrub morphology, aboveground biomass, understory herbs, soil structure, water content, and nutrients. Article.Title: Van der Waals heterojunctions: An emerging pathway toward high-performance perovskite solar cells
Article.Authors: Wei P.; Gao Y.; Fei C.; Hu X.; Yan Z.; Wang S.; Shen X.
Article.Abstract: Metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved impressive power conversion efficiencies, yet poorly controlled crystallization, interfacial recombination, ion migration, and operational instability continue to impede further progress. Van der Waals heterojunctions (vdWHs) from two-dimensional materials provide a distinctive interface engineering platform. Their atomically smooth surfaces, weak interlayer coupling, high tolerance to lattice mismatch, and tunable electronic structures enable simultaneous structural and electronic regulation. This review examines the roles of vdWHs in PSCs through the lens of synergistic regulation at multifunctional interfaces. We first contrast conventional heterojunctions with vdWHs to clarify their unique interfacial features, and then trace how interfacial structure and coupling regulate perovskite crystallization while simultaneously governing band alignment, carrier transport, and degradation pathways under operating conditions. Finally, persistent challenges related to mechanistic understanding, interfacial diagnostics, operando studies, and scalable manufacturing are outlined to guide the development of efficient, durable, and manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics.

Article.Title: Survival and laryngeal preservation with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in hypopharyngeal carcinoma: A multicenter study
Article.Authors: Wang R.; Wang L.; Lei D.; Liu S.; Zhou Y.; Bai Y.; Zhong Q.; Zhang Y.; He Y.; Shi Y.; Ma H.; He S.; Shi Q.; Zhao Y.; Fang J.
Article.Abstract: Optimal neoadjuvant therapy for resectable locally advanced hypopharyngeal carcinoma (LAHC) remains clinically important. In this multicenter retrospective cohort of 517 patients, taxane-platinum-fluorouracil (TPF), TPF plus targeted therapy, and taxane-platinum (TP) plus immunotherapy were compared before surgery-based multimodal therapy or radical (chemo) radiotherapy. TP plus immunotherapy achieved superior overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62), progression-free survival (HR 0.65), and laryngectomy-free survival (HR 0.59), with the highest pathologic complete response (25.4%) and laryngeal preservation rate (83.7%). Article.Title: Notch-mediated thyroid hormone regulation of skin development in the zebrafish caudal fin
Article.Authors: Uemoto-Hayashi T.; Autumn M.; McMenamin S.
Article.Abstract: Thyroid hormone (TH) is a systemic regulator of vertebrate development. Although TH is known to be involved in the maturation of stratified skin, this role has remained incompletely understood. Using the skin at the peripheral-most edge of the zebrafish caudal fin, we characterized the trajectory of epidermal maturation during the transition from juvenile to adult. We found that TH regulates the allometric expansion of the peripheral edge (PE) by stimulating both cell proliferation and hypertrophy of the epidermis. We further demonstrated that TH acts upstream of the Notch pathway to mediate this expansion. While TH signaling machinery was broadly expressed throughout the fin, effectors of the Notch pathway were specifically enriched in the PE. Inhibiting Notch activity prevented PE expansion, while upregulating Notch partially rescued the effects of TH deficiency. Identifying Notch as a highly region-specific effector of TH-driven growth, our findings reveal a mechanism by which systemic endocrine signals may be translated into local tissue-level skin morphogenesis.

Article.Title: Learning societies as catalysts for climate resilience: A systematic review and meta-analysis of community-based environmental education models
Article.Authors: Ampofo J.; Li J.; Zou W.; Zhu W.
Article.Abstract: Climate change demands social responses beyond technical fixes. Community-based environmental education (CBEE) embeds climate learning within communities, aligning with the learning-society emphasis on distributed knowledge and adaptive governance. We synthesized global evidence to characterize CBEE models, quantify their associations with resilience outcomes, and examine mediators and moderators. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched six databases (2014-2024) and analyzed 127 studies (48,592 participants, 42 countries) using random-effects meta-analysis, meta-regression, and meta-analytic structural equation modeling. Three models emerged: Participatory Learning Networks, Place-Based Learning Communities, and Transformative Learning Partnerships. CBEE showed large associations with social cohesion, environmental stewardship, and adaptive capacity, exceeding traditional education, although heterogeneity was substantial. Social capital, collective efficacy, knowledge integration, institutional capacity, and adaptive learning mediated these associations, which cultural relevance and collaboration strengthened. These patterns clarify how community education can support climate resilience and inform the design of context-sensitive, equitable programs. Registration: This review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261411683).

Article.Authors: Serrano J.; Martine L.; Charvet L.; Manière G.; Grosjean Y.; Acar N.; Masson E.; Alves G.

Article.Authors: Kuttiatt V.; Sundararajan T.; Anandan M.; Gnanasekaran V.; Paranthaman S.; Manavalan S.; Periyathambi M.; Balakrishnan V.; Sadhasivam A.
Article.Abstract: Lymphatic filariasis remains a leading cause of chronic, debilitating lymphedema. Article.Authors: Xiao T.; Chen Y.; Kimbrough A.
Article.Abstract: Binge drinking is a prevalent and clinically significant behavior contributing to alcohol use disorder. CoA activation did not alter alcohol intake in either sex but increased locomotor activity in females but not males, although the corresponding sex interaction was not significant. CoA inhibition was associated with distinct brain-wide network configurations, including differences in CoA-associated module composition, hub-like node distribution, and co-activation patterns involving alcohol-relevant limbic and hypothalamic regions. Article.Authors: Herz S.; Khan A.; Betancourt-Toscano I.; Tiron C.; Ton V.; Selley D.; Damaj M.

Article.Abstract: The rising global burden of depression necessitates novel mechanistic insights and therapeutic targets. Voltage-gated sodium channel β2-subunit (Navβ2, coded by SCN2B) has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, yet its role in depression remains unexplored. Here, we identify SCN2B as a previously unrecognized driver of depression-like pathophysiology. Using SCN2B-overexpressing (SCN2B-OV) mice across different ages (1, 12, and 20 months) and CRISPR-engineered Navβ2V173A,V175K mice with selective reduction of the Navβ2 intracellular domain (NICD), we combined behavioral phenotyping, electrophysiology, neurotransmitter profiling, and molecular analyses, with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) as an environmental challenge. SCN2B-OV mice exhibited accelerated depression-like phenotypes, including anhedonia (sucrose preference 52.42% reduction, P < 0.05), behavioral despair (forced swim test immobility 67.42% increase, P < 0.05), and cognitive deficits (Y-maze alternation 50.90% reduction, P < 0.05), independent of natural aging. Electrophysiologically, SCN2B overexpression induced a striking prefrontal-hippocampal imbalance: prefrontal cortex (PFC) became hyperexcitable (glutamate release increased by 64.7%; sEPSC amplitude increased 2.05-fold, P < 0.05), whereas the hippocampus showed synaptic suppression (GABA release reduced by 32.65%; sIPSC frequency reduced by 66.67%, P < 0.05). Mechanistically, SCN2B overexpression suppressed BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/AKT signaling axis (BDNF reduced by 53.17%; p-TrkB reduced by 63.62%, P < 0.05), accompanied by decreased synaptic proteins (PSD95 43.45%, synapsin I 40.31%, P < 0.05). Remarkably, NICD-reduced Navβ2V173A,V175K mice were fully resistant to CUMS-induced behavioral and neurotransmitter deficits, establishing NICD as a critical mediator of stress vulnerability. Collectively, these findings unravel a causal pathway in which SCN2B overexpression drives NICD-dependent suppression of BDNF signaling, leading to region-specific excitatory/inhibitory imbalance, synaptic disintegration, and depression-like phenotypes. Targeting Navβ2 proteolysis to block NICD generation may thus represent a novel therapeutic strategy for mood disorders.

Article.Title: 3,4-Dimethoxyacetophenone ameliorates epileptogenesis by suppressing BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 expression in a pentylenetetrazole-induced kindling model of epilepsy
Article.Authors: Ali S.; Jamal M.; Ayub M.; Nisar U.; Malhi S.; Faizi S.; Simjee S.; Iriti M.
Article.Abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological condition that affects approximately 50 million individuals worldwide. Current treatments mainly alleviate symptoms and have substantial adverse effects, with about 1/3 of patients not responding to existing medications. This underscores the urgent need for new drugs that can overcome these challenges. According to recent studies, the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) pathway play an important role in epileptogenesis. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and c-fos are also involved in neuronal excitability and seizure-induced neuronal changes. The purpose of the present study was to examine the anticonvulsant and antiepileptogenic activities of 3,4-dimethoxyacetophenone (3,4-DMA) in the acute seizure and pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced kindling models of epilepsy and to elucidate related molecular changes of BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 signaling pathways. 3,4-DMA was first evaluated in an acute seizure model, followed by a kindling model of epilepsy in mice. The effects of 3,4-DMA on BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 were assessed by quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). The results showed that 3,4-DMA significantly reduced seizure scores in a PTZ-induced kindling model. BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 were significantly upregulated in both the cortical and hippocampal tissues in PTZ-control mice. Conversely, treatment with 3,4-DMA attenuated this overexpression in the cortex and hippocampus. In conclusion, 3,4-DMA has antiepileptogenic effect as evidenced by a reduction in the expression of BDNF, c-fos and the JAK-2/STAT-3 pathway components. So, it can be a promising therapeutic candidate in the treatment of epilepsy. However, future studies measuring p-JAK-2 and p-STAT-3 will be required to confirm pathway activation status.

Article.Title: Melatonin ameliorates anxiety-like behavior and intestinal barrier dysfunction induced by high-fat diet in BTBR mice
Article.Authors: Cai Y.; Yang Q.; Song J.; Liang Z.; Liu B.; Yang X.; Xie Z.; Li S.; Xiao X.
Article.Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is often accompanied by severe gastrointestinal symptoms, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear, and effective treatments are lacking. This study investigate whether melatonin ameliorates ASD-related behaviors and intestinal dysfunction in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed BTBR mice, focusing on intestinal Treg/Th17 balance and its underlying pathway. BTBR mice were divided into four groups: (1) normal-diet (ND) + 0.9% NaCl (VEH); (2) ND + melatonin (MEL); (3) HFD + VEH; (4) HFD + MEL. After eight weeks of HFD or ND, melatonin was were administered for two weeks. Body weight, blood glucose, behavior, intestinal barrier protein, inflammatory cytokine, CD4+ cell, and AMPK/SIRT1 pathway were assessed. To confirme the role of Treg/Th17 balance, recombinant IL-17 (rIL-17) and anti-CD25 monoclonal antibody (aCD25mAb) were co-administered. This study observed that melatonin treatment significantly improved metabolic disorders and autism-related behaviors in HFD BTBR mice. It concurrently improved intestinal barrier integrity, reduced intestinal inflammation, restored the Treg/Th17 balance, which was associated with the activation of AMPK/SIRT1 pathway. Crucially, the beneficial effects of melatonin on behavior, intestinal barrier integrity and inflammation were all attenuated by rIL-17 or aCD25mAb co-administration, demonstrating a dependence on Treg/Th17 balance. Our study demonstrated that melatonin improves ASD-related behaviors and intestinal barrier integrity in HFD BTBR mice. The mechanism involves the restoration of intestinal Treg/Th17 balance, likely mediated through the AMPK/SIRT1 pathway, highlighting a novel gut-immunological mechanism for melatonin in ASD.

Article.Title: Repeated swim exposure and PKN1a knockout enhance group I mGluR-dependent excitability associated with reduced EAAT3 expression in mouse dentate granule cells
Article.Authors: Yasuda H.; Kubouchi K.; Hanamura K.; Kurihara T.; Nakasone Y.; Mukai H.
Article.Abstract: Stress-related experiences alter glutamatergic signaling and neuronal excitability, but the mechanisms that couple experience to dentate granule cell function remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined how protein kinase N1a (PKN1a), a protein kinase C-like serine/threonine kinase, and repeated swim exposure regulate mouse hippocampal dentate granule cell excitability, with a focus on the neuronal glutamate transporter excitatory amino acid transporter 3 (EAAT3) and group I metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs). Five days of repeated swim exposure increased spike firing in mature dentate granule cells from wild-type mice. PKN1a knockout produced a similar increase, and repeated swim did not further enhance firing in knockout mice. The enhanced firing observed after repeated swim exposure and in PKN1a knockout mice was reduced by co-application of an mGluR1 antagonist (LY367385) and an mGluR5 antagonist (MPEP). Inhibition of glutamate transporters with DL-TBOA increased granule cell firing in control wild-type mice but did not further increase firing in repeated-swim wild-type or PKN1a knockout mice, suggesting occlusion of transporter-dependent regulation of excitability. Repeated swim exposure and PKN1a knockout also reduced total and surface expression of EAAT3 in the hippocampus, whereas expression of the glial glutamate transporter EAAT2 was not significantly altered. Finally, PKN1a knockout and repeated swim exposure reduced anxiety-related behavior in the elevated plus maze test. Thus, PKN1a-dependent regulation of EAAT3 may restrain group I mGluR-dependent excitability in dentate granule cells, whereas repeated swim exposure and PKN1a knockout shift this system toward a lower-EAAT3, higher-excitability state accompanied by reduced anxiety-related behavior.

Article.Title: Brain CYP2D alters orally administered oxycodone induced conditioned place preference in rats
Article.Authors: Okhuarobo A.; Funk D.; Lê A.; Fletcher P.; Miksys S.; Tyndale R.
Article.Abstract: Oxycodone is an opioid analgesic metabolized by the CYP2D enzyme to oxymorphone. We investigated in rats the impact of CYP2D metabolism in the brain on oxycodone-induced reward and aversion, assessed by conditioned place preference (CPP). During conditioning rats were confined to one compartment for 60 min after gavage with oxycodone (or oxymorphone) or with water; treatment and compartments were alternated daily for six days. Rats then underwent 60 min of posttests for five days where CPP was assessed. Pretreatments with the CYP2D inhibitor propranolol, or vehicle, injected intracerebroventricularly 24 h - prior to first and third of six conditioning sessions blunted CPP and with a trend for increased aversion to the oxycodone paired compartment. Pretreatment with the brain CYP2D enzyme inducer nicotine, for 12 days prior to oxycodone conditioning, did not change CPP to oxycodone but tended to reduced aversion to oxycodone paired compartment. Oral oxymorphone induced a CPP with no observed aversion; it was unaffected by CYP2D inhibitor pretreatment. Together this indicates that oral oxycodone and oral oxymorphone both induce CPP. Inhibiting brain CYP2D, previously shown to reduce the relative concentrations of oxycodone to oxymorphone, reduces CPP and tended to increase aversion suggesting that variation in CYP2D activity in the brain could be a source of interindividual differences in oxycodone induced reward and abuse liability.

Article.Title: Cannabidiol alleviates anxiety-like behaviors via α3-containing glycine receptors in the lateral habenula
Article.Authors: Yao Q.; Hu C.; Zhang T.; Yu M.; Sun Y.; Wu J.; Chen Q.; Gao Z.; Zou G.
Article.Abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) exerts potent anxiolytic effects, yet the brain nuclei and molecular targets mediating these effects remain poorly defined. Here, using behavioral and electrophysiological approaches, we identify glycine receptors (GlyRs) in the lateral habenula (LHb) as a key mediator of CBD's anxiolytic action. Pharmacological blockade of LHb GlyRs by intra-LHb strychnine induces robust anxiety-like behaviors, whereas both systemic and intra-LHb CBD administration alleviate them. However, CBD failed to reverse the anxiety-like behaviors induced by prior intra-LHb strychnine. Consistent with this, whole-cell recordings reveal strychnine-sensitive tonic currents in LHb neurons, implicating extrasynaptic GlyRs. To define the responsible subtype, we generated conditional knockouts and found that deletion of α3-containing GlyRs (GlyRα3 cKO), but not α1-containing GlyRs (GlyRα1 cKO), in the LHb produces robust anxiety-like behaviors. Notably, CBD exerts no anxiolytic effect in GlyRα3 cKO mice, establishing GlyRα3 as the subtype required for CBD's action. Furthermore, CBD elevates the action potential threshold and reduces the firing rate of LHb neurons, effects abolished in GlyRα3 cKO mice, thereby linking GlyRα3 activation to reduced LHb excitability. Collectively, these findings identify LHb GlyRα3 as a novel molecular target underlying CBD's anxiolytic effects and support CBD as a promising therapeutic for anxiety disorders.

Article.Title: Female ddY mice show a weaker diazepam-induced reduction in aggressive biting behavior toward inanimate objects and lower hypothalamic KCC2 expression than males do
Article.Authors: Igarashi K.; Kuchiiwa S.; Kuchiiwa T.; Tomita K.; Sato T.
Article.Abstract: Anyone may engage in aggressive behavior under the influence of stress. Animal models have been used to elucidate the mechanisms underlying aggression. Herein, we studied aggressive behavior in chronically isolation-reared male and female mice using an Aggressive Response Meter (ARM) device. The ARM device induces aggressive biting behavior (ABB) in mice toward inanimate objects, and measures its intensity and frequency, hereafter referred to as ABB intensity and ABB frequency, respectively. We characterized ABB intensity and frequency compared with open field test (OFT), social interaction test, and elevated plus maze (EPM). ABB intensity and frequency were increased and the time in the center zone in OFT was decreased in isolation-reared male and female mice compared with group-reared counterparts. No statistically significant correlation was detected between ABB intensity and other behavioral features in OFT, social interaction test, and EPM, indicating that ABB intensity reflects behavioral characteristics not fully explained by these behavioral characteristics. As the effects of GABA-targeting agents are poorly characterized, we examined the effect of diazepam on ABB. At higher doses (4 mg/kg), diazepam effectively reduced ABB levels in both males and females, with males showing higher sensitivity than females at lower doses (2 mg/kg). The number of c-Fos-expressing cells in the dmVMH and dlPAG was high in mice with high ABB. We next analyzed KCC2, a K+-Cl- co-transporter that maintains inhibitory GABA transmission. Low KCC2 expression in the hypothalamus of female was detected using qPCR and immunoblotting. Testosterone supplementation enhanced female responsiveness to diazepam at lower doses.

Article.Title: Genetically predicted cocaine addiction vulnerability is associated with elevated GABAergic transmission in the central amygdala of drug-naïve rats
Article.Authors: Qiao R.; Johnson B.; Doyle M.; Palmer A.; de Guglielmo G.; Kallupi M.
Article.Abstract: A central unresolved question in addiction neuroscience is whether the cellular differences that distinguish vulnerable from resilient individuals precede drug exposure or arise as its consequence. Because addiction-like phenotypes are conventionally assigned only after drug exposure, existing evidence cannot readily separate predisposition from neuroadaptation. Here we used RATTACA, a genome-wide prediction method developed for heterogeneous stock (HS) rats, to select drug-naïve rats with high or low genetically predicted cocaine addiction severity and characterized synaptic transmission by whole-cell recording before any drug exposure, in three independent cohorts. Rats with a high predicted addiction severity showed elevated spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic current (sIPSC) frequency in the medial subdivision of the central amygdala (CeM), and sIPSC frequency scaled continuously with the predicted severity across rats. Amplitude and kinetics were unchanged, a pattern consistent with greater presynaptic GABAergic input. In separate cohorts, GABAergic transmission in the nucleus accumbens core (NAc core) and glutamatergic transmission in the CeM did not differ between groups, suggesting that, among the measures examined, the association was specific to CeM inhibitory transmission. Bath-applied cocaine reduced CeM sIPSC frequency by a similar proportion in both groups and increased CeM glutamatergic transmission. Because high-predicted rats started from a higher baseline, the absolute reduction in spontaneous inhibitory input was larger in these rats. Groups did not differ in locomotor activity. These findings identify elevated spontaneous GABAergic transmission in the CeM as a pre-existing correlate of polygenic cocaine addiction risk and show that genome-wide prediction can dissociate innate cellular predisposition from drug-induced adaptation.

Article.Title: CMKLR1 contributes to diurnal variation in brain injury after cardiac arrest by promoting lactate production in microglia
Article.Authors: Li T.; Fan Z.; Wang H.; Fan D.; Peng F.
Article.Abstract: Previously, the results of our clinical study have suggested that circadian rhythm have an impact on neurological outcomes following cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CA/CPR), but the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, using a mouse model of CA/CPR, we aimed to unravel the underlying mechanisms of the diurnal variation in CA/CPR-induced brain injury. The mice received 5 min of CA either in the active phase or in the inactive phase. To identify novel therapeutic targets for the impact of circadian rhythm on CA/CPR-induced brain injury, we applied high throughput RNA-seq analysis to profile mRNAs with differentially expression in the hippocampus of the two groups. Since it has been reported that CMKLR1 is beneficial for inhibiting neuroinflammation and improving neurological outcomes among many neurological diseases, we centered on this gene and clarified that its main cellular source is microglia. The correlation between CMKLR1 expression in hippocampus and neurological outcomes after CA/CPR was elucidated by CMKLR1 activation and knockout in microglia. The impact of CMKLR1 on microglial function, especially glucose metabolism, was clarified using BV2 microglia cell line by glucose uptake analysis, seahorse analysis and carbon 13 tracing. As a result, CA/CPR happening at active phase leads to better neurological outcomes with upregulation of microglial CMKLR1 in the hippocampus of mice. Our findings suggest that elevated microglial CMKLR1 expression in the hippocampus contributes to improved neurological outcomes after CA/CPR by promoting lactate production in microglia.

Article.Title: Prelimbic cortex CRHR1 regulates Parkinson's disease-related anxiety through a PrLGlu-avBNSTGABA-VTADA pathway
Article.Authors: Gao S.; Yang J.; Bai Y.; Song M.; Guo Y.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Anxiety is a common non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD). Due to the unclear mechanism, treatment becomes challenging and significantly impacts the quality of life of patients. Although corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 1 (CRHR1) is abundantly expressed in the prelimbic cortex (PrL) and have been implicated in PD and anxiety, the role and mechanism of PrL CRHR1 in PD-related anxiety remain unclear. By combining neuropharmacological, chemogenetic, neuroanatomical, and molecular approaches, the present study were performed to investigate the role of PrL CRHR1 in PD-related anxiety and to explore its neural pathways. In this study, unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine lesions of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) in male Sprague-Dawley rats induced anxiety-like behaviors and decreased CRHR1 expression in the PrL compared to sham rats. In sham and the lesioned rats, pharmacological blockade of PrL CRHR1 induced anxiety-like behaviors, whereas its activation produced anxiolytic-like effects, with both effects attenuated in the lesioned rats. CRHR1 blockade was accompanied by increased c-Fos expression in the anterior ventral bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (avBNST), while selective knockdown of CRHR1 in avBNST-projecting PrLGlu neurons similarly enhanced anxiety-like behaviors. Activation of the PrL-avBNSTGABA-ventral tegmental area (VTA) pathway or the avBNST-VTADA pathway induced anxiety-like behaviors, whereas inhibition of either pathway produced anxiolytic-like effects. Together, these findings suggest that PrL CRHR1 regulates PD-related anxiety, at least in part through the PrLGlu-avBNSTGABA-VTADA pathway, thereby providing new insights into the neural mechanisms underlying PD-related anxiety.

Article.Title: α7 nicotinic receptors in the ventral tegmental area gate the acute ethanol effects on aversive memory formation
Article.Authors: Urrea F.; Medina J.; Pastor V.
Article.Abstract: Acute ethanol intoxication is classically associated with impairments in memory formation, yet the circuit and receptor mechanisms through which it modulates aversive memory formation remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of a single post-training injection of different binge-like doses of ethanol on memory formation using an inhibitory avoidance task in young adult male rats. An intermediate dose of ethanol (1.5 g/kg) induced the expected memory impairment, whereas a higher dose (2.5 g/kg) produced a long-lasting enhancement of aversive memory formation that persisted for at least 21 days. Both effects depended on α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (α7nAChRs) within the ventral tegmental area (VTA). Intra-VTA antagonism of α7nAChRs with methyllycaconitine prevented ethanol-induced memory enhancement, while intra-VTA positive allosteric modulation of α7nAChRs with PNU-120596 prevented the memory impairment produced by the lower dose. In addition, pharmacological activation of prefrontal cortical D1 dopaminergic receptors restored ethanol-induced memory enhancement following intra-VTA α7nAChR antagonism, suggesting that prefrontal cortical D1 receptor signaling is involved in the enhancement pathway. Together, these findings identify VTA α7nAChRs as key regulators of the dose-dependent effects of acute ethanol on aversive memory formation, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how acute alcohol exposure can produce opposing mnemonic outcomes.

Article.Title: Activation of GLP-1 receptors in the middle part of the paraventricular nucleus of thalamus suppresses alcohol-related responses
Article.Authors: Aranäs C.; Witley S.; Zhang Q.; Edvardsson C.; Jerlhag E.
Article.Abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) remains a major public health challenge, and identifying the brain circuits through which pharmacological interventions act is central to developing more effective treatments. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists suppress alcohol-related behaviors in rodents and reduce alcohol consumption in clinical populations with AUD, yet the neuroanatomical substrates mediating these effects remain only partly mapped. One candidate region implicated in addiction is the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT), particularly its middle part (mid-PVT), which modulates mesolimbic dopamine signaling, has been implicated in addiction-related processes including alcohol use, and expresses GLP-1R. Whether activation of GLP-1R in the mid-PVT influences alcohol-related responses had not been examined, and that was the aim of the present study. Here, we found that local GLP-1R antagonism in the mid-PVT with exendin-3(9-39) (Ex9) attenuated the suppressive effect of systemically administered GLP-1R agonist exendin-4 (Ex4) on alcohol-induced locomotor stimulation, implicating this region in the central actions of GLP-1R agonists. Intra-mid-PVT Ex4 also attenuated alcohol-induced locomotor stimulation and accumbal dopamine release in male mice, without altering the expression of alcohol-induced conditioned place preference. We further showed that Ex4 into the mid-PVT reduced alcohol intake in male and female rats, although a higher dose was required in females. In a separate cohort of alcohol-consuming, treatment-naive rats, Glp1r mRNA in the PVT did not differ between the sexes. Together, these findings indicate that GLP-1R in the mid-PVT contributes to alcohol-related responses, extending the neuroanatomical map of circuits through which GLP-1R agonists may suppress alcohol intake.

Article.Title: HDAC6 inhibition promotes peripheral nerve development and regeneration via neurofilament acetylation
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Zhang X.; Wu Y.; Luo K.; Shen M.; Ji Y.; Ding F.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Peripheral nerve injury remains challenging due to limited neuronal regeneration. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) regulates microtubule dynamics, but its role in peripheral nervous system (PNS) development and repair is incompletely understood. This study investigates the expression, function, and mechanism of HDAC6 in PNS maturation and regeneration. HDAC6 was abundantly expressed in dorsal root ganglia and sciatic nerves. During postnatal development (P1-P28), HDAC6 expression progressively declined, inversely correlating with increased α-tubulin K40 and global acetylation. Pharmacological HDAC6 inhibition with Tubastatin A (Tub A) or suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA) accelerated nerve maturation, evidenced by enhanced conduction velocity, myelination, and cytoskeletal integrity. In a sciatic nerve crush model, HDAC6 inhibition promoted functional recovery, axonal regeneration, and remyelination. In vitro, HDAC6 inhibition or siRNA knockdown enhanced neurite outgrowth and growth cone expansion in both motor and sensory neurons. Mechanistically, acetylome identified neurofilament light chain (NEFL) as a novel HDAC6 substrate. Among several hypoacetylated lysine residues post-injury, K316 showed the greatest decrease. Direct HDAC6-NEFL interaction was confirmed by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation. Expression of an acetylation-mimetic NEFL (K316Q) mutant promoted neurite outgrowth and growth cone maturation compared with wild-type or acetylation-deficient (K316R) mutants. Collectively, HDAC6 acts as a key negative regulator of PNS development and regeneration, and NEFL K316 acetylation serves as a critical molecular switch for axonal growth. Targeting HDAC6 represents a promising strategy for peripheral nerve repair.

Article.Title: MasR agonist AVE0991 ameliorates EAE: potential involvement of the Nrf2-dependent TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway
Article.Authors: Fang X.; Ma X.; Ma L.; Liu X.; Li D.; Ma X.; Liu Y.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system (CNS). Mas receptor (MasR) constitutes the counter-regulatory arm of the renin-angiotensin system. Despite well-established anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects of MasR, its functional roles and regulatory mechanisms in MS remain elusive. Herein, we established an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model in female C57BL/6 mice by immunization with MOG35-55, and prophylactically treated the mice with the selective MasR agonist AVE0991 starting on day 8 post-immunization for 14 consecutive days. The results showed that AVE0991 treatment reversed the downregulated MasR expression in the spinal cord of EAE mice, effectively alleviated neurological functional impairments, and mitigated excessive inflammatory infiltration in the CNS. MasR was verified to be expressed in IBA1+ cells, and transcriptomic profiling indicated its close association with immune regulation. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV2 cells, AVE0991 significantly inhibited inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, MasR activation by AVE0991 facilitated Nrf2 nuclear translocation, thereby suppressing the TLR4/MyD88 signaling cascade and NF-κB nuclear translocation, and eventually inhibiting NLRP3. Consistently, the anti-inflammatory effects of AVE0991 were fully abolished by the MasR inhibitor A779, TLR4 agonist Neoseptin 3 or Nrf2 inhibitor ML385. And the protein-level alterations of the above molecules were also recapitulated in spinal cord homogenates from EAE mice. Collectively, our data suggest that AVE0991-mediated MasR activation ameliorates neurological deficits and neuroinflammation in EAE, possibly via Nrf2-dependent regulation of the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 cascade. These findings identify a MasR-associated regulatory axis linked to neuroinflammation, which may provide a potential therapeutic strategy for MS.

Article.Title: Nicotine increases dopamine signaling in the nucleus accumbens in male Wistar rats
Article.Authors: Tan X.; Ding Z.
Article.Abstract: Nicotine is the primary tobacco alkaloid that reinforces tobacco use. Increase in extracellular dopamine levels within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) is believed to mediate the reinforcing effects of nicotine. Historically, microdialysis and in vivo voltammetry have been commonly used to monitor nicotine-induced dopamine increase with different temporal resolution and dopamine specificity. Fiber photometry coupled with GPCR-based dopamine sensors recently emerged as a versatile tool for monitoring dopamine signaling linked to drug and drug-related behaviors at a subsecond time scale and with high dopamine specificity. Studies with this technique have begun to uncover rapid dopamine dynamics induced by nicotine aerosol exposure and subcutaneous injection. Intravenous self-administration (IVSA) remains a commonly used behavioral assay for assessing the reinforcing effects of nicotine. However, dopamine dynamics associated with nicotine IVSA remains to be determined. The current study investigated nicotine effects on rapid dopamine dynamics in the NAc following both passive and volitional IV nicotine administration and pharmacological regulation of these effects by nicotine-related compounds. Passive IV infusion of nicotine at 0.06 mg/kg significantly enhanced rapid dopamine signaling in the NAc and such effects were abolished by pretreatment with mecamylamine, varenicline, or bupropion. Volitional nicotine IVSA at 0.06 mg/kg/infusion also increased dopamine signaling in the NAc that was time-locked to active lever press and cue light presentation for nicotine infusion. These results suggest that increase in rapid dopamine signaling in the NAc may underlie the effects of nicotine and that inhibition of such effects may contribute to the pharmacological effects of nicotine-related compounds.

Article.Title: ATDP33605, a selective NOP receptor agonist, reduces cocaine self-administration in rhesus monkeys
Article.Authors: Teshima K.; Paronis C.; Minoguchi M.; Hashimoto T.; Kaneko S.; Fukudome D.; Bergman J.
Article.Abstract: The selectivity and efficacy of a small-molecule NOP receptor agonist, 2,3-Dihydro-N-methyl-2-oxo-3-[1-[(1R)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-5-methyl-1-naphthalenyl]-4-piperidinyl]-1H-benzimidazole-1-acetamide (ATDP33605) were characterized in vitro. Next, its effects on operant behavior maintained by food pellets or self-administered cocaine were evaluated in a group of 4 male nonhuman primates. ATDP33605 showed high affinity for human NOP receptors expressed in HEK293 cells (Kᵢ = 0.59 nM) and exhibited approximately 240-fold selectivity for binding NOP over MOP receptors. ATDP33605 also stimulated [35S]GTPγS binding to human NOP receptors expressed in HEK293 cells in a concentration-dependent manner, with an EC50 of 2.39 nM and a Hill coefficient of 0.85. The efficacy of ATDP33605 was comparable to N/OFQ, indicating that it functions as a full agonist at NOP receptors. In behavioral studies, acute intramuscular treatment with ATDP33605 dose-dependently reduced the self-administration of a peak unit dose of cocaine, albeit with some variability among individual monkeys. Doses of ATDP33605 that significantly decreased cocaine-maintained behavior (0.32 or 0.56 mg/kg) had little or only transient effect on food-maintained behavior in individual monkeys. Subsequent studies revealed that the effects of ATDP33605 were apparent over a range of cocaine unit doses. These findings demonstrate that selective activation of NOP receptors effectively suppresses cocaine self-administration in primates, supporting a critical role of NOP signaling in cocaine-reinforced behavior. Variability among individual subjects highlights the need for studies with larger sample sizes and female subjects. Importantly, this study provides the first evidence that a selective NOP receptor agonist can reduce IV cocaine self-administration in nonhuman primates, suggesting its potential therapeutic value for cocaine use disorder.

Article.Title: Adolescent ethanol exposure reduces central amygdala GABA transmission but preserves noradrenergic signaling in adulthood
Article.Authors: Marsland P.; Penta P.; Towner T.; Coleman H.; Liss A.; Varlinskaya E.; Werner D.; Varodayan F.
Article.Abstract: Early initiation of alcohol use is a risk factor for developing alcohol use disorder (AUD) later in life, yet the long-term neuronal consequences of adolescent drinking remain poorly understood. The central amygdala (CeA) drives the negative emotional states that promote excessive drinking, and its overactivation is a hallmark of AUD in adults. Moreover, alcohol releases the stress signal norepinephrine (NE) into the adult CeA, leading to sex-dependent changes in its GABA transmission. Whether similar alcohol-induced changes in the adolescent CeA contribute to later-life vulnerability to AUD is unknown. In the present study, we used an intragastric gavage model of adolescent intermittent ethanol (AIE) exposure in Sprague-Dawley rats to examine the long-lasting effects on CeA synapses and noradrenergic regulation. AIE reduced basal GABA transmission via pre- and postsynaptic mechanisms in adults of both sexes, a response that deviates from the typical increased inhibition found in subjects only exposed to ethanol during adulthood. We observed similar NE-induced increases in CeA GABA release in adult males and females regardless of AIE exposure, and no differences were observed in CeA adrenergic receptor gene expression. Collectively, our data reveal that AIE produced a long-lasting reduction in adult CeA inhibitory tone, and this change is likely independent of the noradrenergic system. This developmental-specific shift in CeA activity reflects the heightened vulnerability of the adolescent brain to ethanol-induced neuroadaptation and may represent a neural substrate underlying the increased risk of AUD following adolescent alcohol use.

Article.Title: Profiling the effects of alcohol history on cognitive performance during abstinence: an examination of proenkephalin-A-derived peptides in the medial prefrontal cortex
Article.Authors: David E M.; Meera A.; Laura A A.; Stan B F.; Luis A N.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairments during abstinence may complicate recovery from alcohol use disorder, but their persistence across executive domains and accompanying cortical adaptations remain unclear. Neuropeptides are candidate mediators of persistent alcohol (ethanol; EtOH) effects, and emerging evidence implicates endogenous opioid peptides in cortical processing. Here, we examined cognitive function and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) enkephalin profiles in rats with a history of chronic EtOH exposure. Using a longitudinal operant-based approach, we assessed cognitive flexibility during early abstinence and delay-dependent working memory during protracted abstinence. We then quantified methionine-enkephalin (Met-ENK) and leucine-enkephalin (Leu-ENK) and profiled the proenkephalin-A (PENK)-derived peptide pool in the mPFC. EtOH history did not alter overall trials or errors to criterion during strategy set-shifting or reversal learning. During reversal, however, EtOH rats showed greater perseverative bias, with response adjustments less aligned with recent feedback and more strongly influenced by prior reinforcement. During initial testing at the longest working memory delay, EtOH rats also showed lower accuracy. Performance across these tasks was correlated in EtOH rats, suggesting individual differences in cognitive susceptibility were maintained across abstinence. Targeted analyses showed comparable levels of Met-ENK and Leu-ENK between groups. Although individual PENK-derived sequences did not differ in abundance, compositional analysis showed a greater summed relative contribution of C-terminal fragments in EtOH samples. These findings indicate that EtOH history produces lasting cognitive vulnerabilities that emerge under greater task demands, with some animals remaining more susceptible than others. C-terminal PENK profiling may reveal novel targets associated with enduring mPFC adaptations during abstinence.

Article.Title: SV2A attenuates interictal anxiety in pharmacoresistant epilepsy via the SYT3–GluA2 axis
Article.Authors: Li C.; Pan T.; Ren M.; Wang X.; Shi Y.; Ren S.; Wu G.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: Objective: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) is an established target of antiseizure therapy; however, its role in excitatory synaptic function and downstream postsynaptic machinery remains poorly defined. This study examined whether SV2A limits excitotoxic signaling by recruiting synaptotagmin-3 (SYT3), thereby modulating the α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor subunit GluA2. Methods: A multilevel strategy was used to define the contribution of SV2A to anxiety in a pharmacoresistant epilepsy (PRE) model. The phenobarbital/phenytoin-resistant PRE phenotype was established in rats using the lithium-pilocarpine paradigm. Lentiviral vectors were delivered to the hippocampal CA1 region for bidirectional manipulation of SV2A expression. Protein abundance and molecular interactions were examined using western blotting, immunofluorescence, co-immunoprecipitation, and molecular docking. Synaptic plasticity was assessed using long-term potentiation (LTP) recordings, and anxiety-related behavior was evaluated using the elevated plus maze and open field test. Results: A special interaction between SV2A and SYT3 was confirmed at the protein level. PRE rats exhibited pronounced anxiety-like behavior, increased seizure frequency, reduced SV2A expression, and aberrantly potentiated LTP in the CA1 region. Hippocampal SV2A overexpression reduced SYT3 levels, suppressed GluA2 internalization, and attenuated both exaggerated LTP and anxiety-like behavior. Conversely, SV2A knockdown increased SYT3 expression, promoted GluA2 endocytosis, and further aggravated aberrant LTP and anxiety-like behavior. Conclusion: SV2A plays a pivotal role in interictal anxiety associated with PRE. PRE downregulates SV2A and weakens the SV2A-SYT3 interaction, thereby driving aberrant LTP and the emergence of anxiety-like behavior.

Article.Title: Molecular mechanism of the interaction between kaempferol and human nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Moon M.; Yun J.; Yeom H.; Kamau V.; Lee M.; Lee G.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Kaempferol has been investigated for its potential neuroprotective properties and its ability to modulate mood-regulating pathways through the regulation of neurotransmitter systems. Evidence suggests that it may inhibit the reuptake of selective neurotransmitters, thereby enhancing their synaptic availability. Here, using two-electrode voltage-clamp recordings in Xenopus oocytes expressing five human nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) subtypes, we found that kaempferol selectively and potently inhibits α3β4 nAChRs, with weaker inhibition of α3β2 receptors and no effect on α7, α4β2, or α4β4 subtypes. This inhibition was reversible, voltage-independent, and non-competitive with acetylcholine, indicating an allosteric mechanism of action rather than direct competition at the orthosteric binding site. To identify the structural basis of this subtype selectivity, molecular docking of kaempferol onto the α3β4 nAChR structure was performed, and candidate binding residues at the α3-β4 interface were prioritized based on binding energy for site-directed mutagenesis. The results showed that the inhibitory effect of kaempferol was abolished in the α3 W55A and β4 R151A double mutant. These findings confirm that kaempferol selectively and effectively inhibits the α3β4 nAChR subtype via an allosteric site formed by residues W55 (α3) and R151 (β4), supporting the hypothesis that it interacts with a specific region of this receptor distinct from the acetylcholine-binding site.
