Article.Title: How Habitual Language Mode Shapes Self-Stigma Perception Process in Deaf Individuals: Evidence from an Event-Related Potentials Study
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Li Y.; Wang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deaf individuals often experience public stigma from the hearing majority due to communication barriers, which may further evolve into internalized self-stigma. However, how habitual language mode shapes self-stigma-related processing remains unclear. In the present study, 20 signing deaf and 21 oral deaf individuals completed a semantic priming task while event-related potentials (ERPs) were recorded. Deaf-identity (“I am deaf”) primes were presented subliminally or supraliminally before positive and negative trait words. Among oral deaf participants, negative words elicited a larger N400 than positive words under supraliminal priming, while a negative-over-positive LPC effect emerged in the no-priming and subliminal conditions but disappeared under supraliminal priming. Signing deaf participants showed no N400 valence effect but exhibited a negative-over-positive LPC effect across all conditions. These findings provide no clear evidence of self-stigma in either group. Instead, they suggest that habitual language mode and conscious accessibility of deaf identity jointly shape the temporal dynamics of self-evaluative processing, potentially reflecting different ways of resisting the internalization of negative societal evaluations. Signing deaf individuals may derive protection from a culturally and collectively grounded Deaf identity, whereas oral deaf individuals may rely more on individualized, self-protective processing to prevent negative evaluations from being incorporated into the self.

Article.Title: mPFC-Dependent Valuation Shapes Information Sharing: Causal Evidence from tDCS and a Dyadic Social Media Paradigm
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Information sharing drives the spread of both accurate and misleading content, yet its psychological and neural mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated whether perceived self- and social relevance influence sharing through downstream content evaluations, and whether this process depends on medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) function. In a dyadic social media paradigm, 186 participants were assigned to anodal, cathodal, or sham tDCS over the mPFC. Senders judged 30 science news items (15 true and 15 false) on truthfulness, self-relevance, social relevance, interestingness, and importance before deciding whether to share each item with a real receiver. Structural equation modeling showed that self- and social relevance predicted sharing indirectly through evaluations of interestingness, importance, and truthfulness. mPFC stimulation did not reliably change sharing rates, but altered evaluative processing: it reduced perceived interestingness, and anodal stimulation produced a significant negative indirect pathway to sharing through reduced interestingness. Multi-group analyses indicated that these valuation pathways were invariant across true and false news. On the receiver side, social endorsement increased reading of shared items but had little effect on post-reading evaluations. Together, these findings support a causal contribution of mPFC-targeted neuromodulation to evaluative processing relevant to sharing, with limited evidence for a direct effect on sharing behavior.

Article.Title: Disentangling weather from season in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment: a nationwide time-series and simulation study
Article.Authors: Kim E.; Nam S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Seasonal variation in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) has prompted many studies of meteorological risk factors, but these analyzed monthly counts without adjusting for season, an approach that cannot separate the effect of weather from the calendar. In a nationwide analysis of 55,880 surgically confirmed RRD cases in Korea (2014–2023; six regions × 522 weeks), weekly incidence was modeled by negative binomial regression, contrasting an unadjusted design with one adjusting for week of year, and characterized against data simulated under a known null. Without seasonal adjustment, ten of eleven exposure–incidence correlations fell within the range produced by data sharing only the calendar. After adjustment, temperature associations greatly attenuated and no longer significant and most exposures showed no association—relative humidity reversing direction—indicating that the reported effects of weather largely reflect season rather than weather itself. Only a few prespecified measures of clear, dry weather became associated after adjustment—led by sunshine duration (1.026; 1.011–1.042)—but the signal was confined to the week of diagnosis, consistent with either a true effect or earlier floater recognition, which this design cannot distinguish. In simulations, the conventional design recovered a true effect in 24% of replicates and reversed its sign in 12%. Conventional analyses can generate associations season explains and obscure ones adjustment reveals; for temperature, an effect cannot be excluded rather than shown absent.

Article.Title: A machine learning framework for human activity recognition and confidence-based atypical pattern assessment for remote physiotherapy monitoring
Article.Authors: Banu S.; Bhardwaj A.; Kaabi A.; Vishnoi A.; Narooka P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has emerged as a critical aspect of digital healthcare, especially for remote physiotherapy monitoring and support for rehabilitation. Current HAR systems are, however, mainly concerned with activity classification and offer a few ways to handle the representation of prediction uncertainty and detection of potentially atypical activity patterns. This research introduces a machine learning approach based on simulation that combines activity recognition, atypical pattern recognition based on confidence, and confidence-based evaluation. A HAR publicly available dataset from the smartphones was used, with six activity classes and 561 features extracted in the dataset, and the training/testing partition was set, the default one. Because there is no ground truth information of correct and incorrect movements, prediction confidence is only used as an indicator of the uncertainty of the classifiers and potentially unusual activity patterns. Confidence-derived atypicality score $$ S(x) $$ is computed as $$ (1 - C(x)) \times 100 $$ ; prediction score $$ C(x) $$ is categorized as Good, Moderate and Needs Improvement and interpreted computationally. The multi-class ROC-AUC of the Random Forest model is 0.995 and it is achieving 93% accuracy. Approximately 0.20 s are needed for the full test set in the evaluated environment under the condition of inference, while threshold analysis can be accomplished by analyzing the number of samples below the different prediction-confidence thresholds. The results show the computational feasibility of confidence-based activity assessment and further clinical validation is needed when using physiotherapy-specific datasets and labels of movement-quality, which were also manually annotated by experts.

Article.Title: Microstructural changes in radiochromic film and dosimetry in magnetic field
Article.Authors: Soni V.; Keidar M.; Das I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiochromic film (RCF) dosimetry in magnetic resonance-guided linear accelerator systems requires validation due to conflicting reports regarding dosimetric accuracy in magnetic fields (MF). This study quantitatively evaluated microstructural changes and dosimetric response of EBT-3 RCFs exposed to ionizing radiation in a 0.35 T magnetic field. Films from a single batch were irradiated with 2, 5, 8, 10, and 16 Gy using a 6 MV flattening filter-free photon beam from a ViewRay magnetic resonance-linear accelerator unit, with and without magnetic field activation. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at 2500× magnification analyzed microstructural features, while quantitative measurements of needle-like crystal structures assessed length and angular orientation using ImageJ software. Optical density measurements employed standard RCF protocols with red-green-blue to grayscale conversion. Results demonstrated that crystal lengths remained consistent across all radiation doses regardless of magnetic field presence, with no statistically significant variations observed. However, magnetic field exposure produced dramatic angular alignment effects, with crystal structures clustering within ± 80 to ± 100 degrees compared to random 360-degree distribution without magnetic field. This alignment became progressively pronounced at higher doses, particularly at 8–16 Gy. Despite significant microstructural reorientation, optical density analysis revealed negligible dosimetric differences between magnetic field conditions, with variations remaining within experimental uncertainty. The findings indicate that magnetic fields influence topochemical polymerization directionality without affecting total polymerized material quantity, explaining why structural changes do not compromise dose measurement accuracy. These results resolve previous conflicting literature by demonstrating that EBT-3 RCFs maintain dosimetric reliability in magnetic field environments, supporting their continued use for accurate dose measurements in magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy applications.

Article.Title: A quinoa-associated Pantoea isolate displays salinity-responsive auxin production and promotes plant growth under salt stress
Article.Authors: Murata Y.; Kashiwa T.; Dangjarean H.; Kobayashi Y.; Fujita Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plant-associated bacteria can promote plant growth under saline conditions, but salinity-dependent changes in bacterial physiological traits remain insufficiently understood. Here, we isolated bacteria from surface-sterilized seedlings of the quinoa Kd line and evaluated their activity under saline conditions. A quinoa-associated Pantoea isolate, strain 6PN, promoted primary root elongation and whole-plant dry weight of Arabidopsis thaliana under salt stress, whereas no significant effect was observed under non-saline conditions. Comparative analyses with reference Pantoea agglomerans strains showed that strain 6PN exhibited salinity-responsive indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) production. Genome analysis identified a putative ipdC gene and additional genes related to stress responses, nutrient acquisition, polysaccharide biosynthesis and export, flagellar biosynthesis, and chemotaxis. Phylogenomic analysis indicated that strain 6PN was genomically distinct from representative Pantoea species examined here. In an Arabidopsis trench-plate assay, GFP-labeled strain 6PN was recovered from spatially separated plant tissues at higher levels than a GFP-labeled reference strain under saline conditions. These results identify strain 6PN as a quinoa-associated Pantoea isolate with salinity-responsive IAA production and plant growth-promoting activity under defined salt-stress conditions.

Article.Title: Quantitative evaluation of single-grating phase-contrast imaging with a femtosecond laser–plasma K$$\alpha$$ X-ray source
Article.Authors: Giakoumakis G.; Ferré A.; Gudz D.; Saliji M.; Primot J.; Utéza O.; Clady R.; Stolidi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We present the first implementation of an X-ray phase-contrast imaging approach using single 2D-grating phase retrieval and a quasi-monochromatic hard K $$\alpha$$ X-ray source generated via high-intensity femtosecond laser—plasma interaction. To highlight its pertinence, we demonstrate quantitative phase-contrast measurements of a known canonical physical object, retrieving phase distribution with high-fidelity, under varying experimental conditions. As a marker of such performance, a correlation score of up to 0.922 ± 0.008 is obtained between theoretical and experimental phase images. The consistency of the retrieved phase gradients is further quantitatively evaluated using the Confidence Map, a self-consistency metric derived directly from the acquired data. This framework supports a systematic parametric study aimed at quantifying the influence of X-ray source characteristics on phase retrieval and thus optimizing imaging performance by balancing exposure time and spatial resolution. Two operating regimes are investigated: fixed integrated photon-count conditions with varying spatial coherence of the X-ray source, and fixed acquisition-time conditions with varying X-ray photon flux. This work establishes a pathway toward minimizing exposure times while preserving accurate phase retrieval, with the long-term objective of enabling short-time exposure of time-resolved phase-contrast imaging.

Article.Title: Ensemble learning-based surrogate modeling of a four-port self-isolated MIMO antenna for V2X and X-band wireless applications
Article.Authors: Sharma M.; Harikaran M.; Kumar S.; Singh H.; Baliyan A.; Saini K.; Sharma G.; Poojary R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This article presents an ensemble learning-based surrogate model of a compact monopole/four-port self-isolated multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for Vehicle-to-Anything (V2X), X-band, and partial Ku-band wireless communication. The proposed single-port antenna is printed on a compact substrate with an overall dimension of 12.0 × 15.0 × 0.80 mm³. The structure consists of a circular monopole radiator loaded with an internal slot and a modified curved/defected partial ground plane to improve impedance matching and generate the desired multiband response. The optimized antenna provides resonance around 5.90 GHz for V2X communication and additional operating points around 7.90 GHz, 10.0 GHz, and 12.96 GHz, supporting X-band and partial Ku-band applications. The single-port design is further transformed into a four-port MIMO configuration by arranging four identical radiators orthogonally, with optimized inter-element spacing of D 1 = 20.50 mm and D 2 = 19.0 mm, to reduce mutual coupling and improve diversity performance, and occupies a space of 50 mm×50.0 mm. The measured isolation remains better than 23 dB in Band A and better than 20 dB in Band B for adjacent elements, while S31 reaches more than 30 dB and 35 dB in Band A and Band B, respectively. An equivalent RLC circuit model, rooftop V2X validation, specific-absorption-rate (SAR) evaluation, radiation-pattern analysis, and gain/efficiency comparison are also presented. The SAR values remain below the 1.60 W/kg safety limit for both single-port and four-port configurations. Additionally, an ensemble learning-based surrogate modeling framework is evaluated using 93,149 electromagnetic simulation records grouped by antenna geometry. The stacking ensemble was tested on 9,505 samples corresponding to unseen geometries and achieved a Root-Mean-Square-Error (RMSE) of 0.464, Mean-Absolute-Error (MAE) of 0.198, and an R² (Coefficient of Determination) of 0.99561, demonstrating accurate S 11 prediction and rapid design-space exploration.

Article.Title: Comparative investigation of various optical properties, birefringence, and order parameter of pure 5CB and its fully and partially deuterated samples, 5CB-d19 and 5CB-d8 liquid crystals
Article.Authors: Iram N/A.; Choudhury S.; Herman J.; Bhattacharjee D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This article investigates the temperature-dependent optical properties of pure 5CB, deuterated 5CB- d 19 , and 5CB- d 8 liquid crystals. The 5CB liquid crystal is widely studied, but the systematic comparative study of various optical and orientational properties of its fully and partially deuterated variants, 5CB- d 19 and 5CB- d 8 , remains limited. This is the motivation for this systematic comparative study, in which the four-parameter model method is used to calculate the theoretical refractive indices from experimentally measured data in the nematic phase. The temperature-dependent order parameter S(T) was also calculated using different experimental and theoretical approaches. To validate the four-parameter model in the aforementioned liquid crystals, the values of the four unknown parameters, i.e. A, B, $$\:\beta\:$$ and $$\:{\left(\varDelta\:n\right)}_{o}$$ were determined using the two-step fitting method, thereby validating the four-parameter model. The crossover temperature $$\:{T}_{CO}$$ was also calculated, and the values were 271.42 K for 5CB, 271.66 K for 5CB- d 19 , and 292.24 K for 5CB- d 8 . Additionally, this study indicates that all the theoretical models used in this article are justified and in agreement with the experimental results. The preceding investigation explains the distinct optical features of these compounds for enhanced use.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning for genomic prediction, subgroup classification, and optimal parent cross ranking in rice breeding using 1k-RiCA SNP data
Article.Authors: Singh G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genomic selection can accelerate rice breeding by predicting agronomic performance directly from genomic markers, but its adoption is limited by the black-box nature of many machine-learning models and the lack of tools that translate predictions into actionable parent-cross recommendations. We developed an explainable machine-learning framework using the publicly available 1,000 Rice Core Accessions (1k-RiCA) SNP panel (353 indica rice accessions genotyped at 965 loci) to (i) predict flowering time (FLW) and plant height (PH) from SNP genotypes, (ii) classify accessions into subspecies subgroups, and (iii) rank all pairwise parent crosses by predicted offspring performance. Ridge regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated for regression, while random forest and XGBoost were compared for subgroup classification. XGBoost produced the best FLW predictions (test R² = 0.69, RMSE = 2.52 days). For PH, a random forest model incorporating FLW as a covariate with univariate feature selection achieved the best performance (test R² = 0.55, RMSE = 5.94 cm). Random forest also achieved the highest subgroup-classification performance (76.7% accuracy; macro-AUC = 0.82). Grain yield was excluded from genomic prediction because formal genomic predictive ability analysis (rrBLUP R² = 0.115 ± 0.061) confirmed near-zero marker signal, consistent with strong genotype-by-environment (G×E) interaction; grain yield was retained as a descriptive input in the composite cross-ranking score. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified markers driving each prediction. All 62,128 pairwise parent crosses were scored and ranked to generate a prioritized breeding shortlist. The pipeline was deployed as an interactive web application supporting dataset upload, automated preprocessing, SHAP-based explanations, and ranked cross export, providing transparent, statistically robust decision support for rice breeding using mid-density SNP panels without whole-genome sequencing.

Article.Title: Landslide directionality reveals fault-influenced valley-slope geometry in the northern Xiaojiang Fault Zone
Article.Authors: Liu R.; Jia H.; Zhang J.; Li C.; Su T.; Yuan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Regional landslide inventories commonly describe where landslides occur, but they rarely capture the directional organization of slope failure. We compiled a remote-sensing-derived geomorphic inventory with 3,442 landslides along the northern Xiaojiang Fault Zone, southeastern Tibetan Plateau, and defined the principal runout direction as the plan-view vector from the highest point along the rear boundary to the centroid of each landslide polygon. Circular statistics, fault-distance zoning and the angle between landslide direction and local fault strike (ΔF) were used to evaluate regional landslide directional patterns. Landslide directions show a clear multimodal distribution, dominated by east-southeast and west-southwest sectors. Directional concentration varies spatially, with the lowest value in the 0–1 km fault-distance zone (0.1149) and the highest value beyond 5 km (0.3898). ΔF is strongly concentrated at high angles, indicating that the principal direction vectors are not parallel to the fault. Instead, their directions are more consistent with local valley–slope geometry that may result from the combined effects of prolonged fault activity and fluvial downcutting. Principal runout direction therefore provides information complementary to conventional inventory metrics and offers a regional-scale indicator for examining tectonic–geomorphic organization in active-fault mountain landscapes.

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning with modified red fox optimizer based task scheduling scheme for human–robot collaboration
Article.Authors: Sivalingam C.; Rao G.; Gowroju S.; Vemanaboina H.; Kantipudi M.; Paramasivam P.; Yusuf M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human–Robot Collaboration (HRC) is transforming modern industrial environments by combining human flexibility with robotic precision. However, real-time task scheduling (TS) in HRC systems remains challenging due to large state-action spaces and reliance on expert knowledge. This study proposes a novel Deep Reinforcement Learning with Modified Red Fox Optimizer (DRL-MRFO) approach for optimal TS in HRC systems. The DRL-MRFO model integrates a Deep Q-Network (DQN) to learn effective scheduling strategies autonomously, while the MRFO algorithm fine-tunes hyperparameters for improved performance. Experimental validation under various scenarios shows that the DRL-MRFO outperforms traditional methods like DP, Nash-Q, and DQN-MARL. For instance, on Product-1 with 1000 min of training, DRL-MRFO achieved the lowest CT of 74 min, compared to 109, 115, 100, and 82 min for DP, Nash-Q, DQN-SARL, and DQN-MARL, respectively. Similar improvements were observed across multiple human–robot configurations, with DRL-MRFO consistently achieving reduced completion times and higher robot utilization, reaching up to 92.87% in 1H-1R scenarios. These results demonstrate the model's effectiveness and scalability in handling complex assembly tasks. The proposed DRL-MRFO framework offers a promising solution for real-time, adaptive task scheduling in dynamic HRC environments.

Article.Title: Limited emission reduction from China’s low-carbon city pilot: evidence from 112 Yangtze River Economic Belt Cities
Article.Authors: Tang Z.; Qin J.; Zhang R.; Nie X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract China’s Low-Carbon City Pilot (LCCP) program covers 72 of 112 prefecture-level cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB) across three staggered cohorts (2010, 2012, 2017) and is among the world’s largest subnational climate experiments. Using a balanced panel of 1,870 city-year observations (2007–2023) and two-way fixed effects with city-clustered standard errors, we find no statistically significant effect of LCCP on CO₂ emissions ( β = 0.032, p = 0.256). Event-study estimates find no strong evidence against parallel pretreatment trends (joint Wald χ²=7.316, p = 0.120), while post-treatment coefficients turn significantly negative only after seven to nine years (k = 7: −0.120, p = 0.011; k = 8: −0.111, p = 0.038; k = 9: −0.142, p = 0.015). A dose–response analysis confirms this pattern: each additional exposure year is associated with a 1.1% reduction in CO₂ emissions ( β =−0.011, p = 0.043). Heterogeneity across cohorts, regions, and city size is imprecise, and a descriptive decomposition attributes part of the association to carbon intensity, a near-definitional channel that cannot support causal claims. An interaction analysis finds no evidence that carbon trading amplified the effect (interaction β = 0.010, p = 0.878). After 17 years, the LCCP program has produced no detectable emission reduction across YREB cities, although delayed, dose-dependent reductions may materialize over a decade or more, calling for extended evaluation timelines.

Article.Title: Trust-adaptive participation in fog-based SplitBFT: a communication–liveness trade-off study
Article.Authors: Saxena T.; Chacko N.; Bhat K. V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fog and edge computing environments have begun to rely heavily on blockchain systems to coordinate untrusted devices. However, the consensus mechanisms deployed on these systems must balance security and communication costs while dealing with unreliable and resource-limited conditions. This work considers the existing SplitBFT consensus algorithm, which improves the scalability of Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus by dividing participating nodes into smaller cooperating groups. However, it has a major drawback: it operates with a fixed configuration and cannot respond to changing node behaviour. The aim of this study is to determine whether making SplitBFT adaptively select nodes based on trust metrics, such as observed reliability measured from uptime, voting history, responsiveness, and detected misbehaviour, can reduce communication cost without affecting the security of the algorithm. For this, we conducted over 11,000 controlled experiments spanning a range of conditions, including network sizes, adversarial intensities, and loss conditions. Our findings suggest that adjusting the number of confirmations a group requires offers no benefit, whereas restricting participation to a trusted subset of nodes reduces communication by roughly 46.5–49.1% while preserving safety and liveness. A smaller trusted subset further lowers overhead under attack, as it keeps malicious nodes out of the decision-making set. However, this advantage holds only in near-stable networks and diminishes once packet loss exceeds a low, size-dependent threshold, after which full participation is preferable. These results characterise when trust-adaptive participation benefits fog-based consensus, and serve as a caution when deploying such systems in edge environments, particularly where network reliability is low.

Article.Title: A multilingual vision-language retrieval-augmented assistant for smallholder farmer decision support
Article.Authors: Alotibi Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Smallholder farmers in low-and-middle-income countries lack access to timely, language-inclusive, and evidence-grounded crop advisory, a gap that existing vision-language models fail to close due to English-centric training, ungrounded generation, and absent calibration. To address this, we propose AgroVLM-RAG, a multilingual vision-language retrieval-augmented assistant, which integrates a cross-lingual aligned encoder with an evidence-gated retriever, and a faithfulness-calibrated generator. The design is based on three mechanisms: a multilingual cross-lingual alignment module that allows the mapping of imagery and queries from nine languages to a common space; a confidence router that will abstain and re-query when a learnt confidence low; and an evidence gate which only retains retrieved passages where the support score exceeds a learnt threshold. Compared to the best baseline models, AgroVLM-RAG achieves 78.9% accuracy on PlantDoc-VQA (field-captured images, the most deployment-relevant setting), 91.4% on PlantVillageVQA, and 63.1% on AgroBench, improving the strongest baseline by 5.3, 3.5, and 3.9% points respectively. The cross-lingual accuracy is at most 8.9 points away from the optimum accuracy, against 22.6 points for a strong generalist encoder, and the expected calibration of the error ranges between 0.121 and 0.031. The assistant responds in about 395 to 402 milliseconds when deployed with an embedded accelerator, allowing the deployment of advisories on the device. When confident guessing is converted to evidence-gated and calibrated abstention, these results show that it becomes auditable and language-inclusive crop decision support.

Article.Title: Systemic immune and metabolomic responses to oral hyaluronic acid in a randomized placebo-controlled clinical study
Article.Authors: Šínová R.; Berka V.; Kubala L.; Ovesná P.; Šimek M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oral hyaluronan (HA) supplementation has shown clinical benefits, but its systemic effects remain insufficiently characterized. We focused on the systemic effects of oral HA. (1.8 MDa) at 60 mg/day (SH60), 120 mg/day (SH120), or placebo for 12 weeks in 150 healthy donors. Within this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, plasma samples were analyzed to assess changes in immune and metabolic markers, as well as alterations in lipid metabolism, using high-quality, untargeted omics approaches with high information depth. The SH120 group significantly reduced pro-inflammatory markers, including CRP, IL-1b, and precursor of inflammatory mediators such as arachidonic acid, compared with placebo. Together with selective modulation in metabolic biomarkers, including fetuin-A, adipsin, mannopyranosyl tryptophan, 1,16-hexadecanedioic acid, and 3-hydroxydecanoic acid, support the hypothesis that oral HA may promote an immune homeostasis and a “metabolically healthy” profile, exerting protective effects even in otherwise healthy individuals. Correlations between plasma markers and previously reported skin outcomes were generally weak, suggesting that modulation of systemic biomarkers can explain only partially the cutaneous effects of supplementation. Overall, oral HA was associated with selective changes in plasma biomarkers in healthy adults, which should be considered when evaluating the mechanisms underlying its clinical effects. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07065110 (retrospectively registered on 15 Jul 2025) EFSA (European Food Safety Authority) registry EFSA202400027979 (prospectively filed on 06 Jun 2024).

Article.Title: Region-aware CT-to-PET image synthesis using deep learning models for accurate lung cancer localization
Article.Authors: Sayed M.; Rahman A.; Rahman G.; Islam M.; Chowdhury M.; Park J.; Kadir M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate functional imaging remains a major challenge in medical diagnostics, particularly in regions with limited access to positron emission tomography (PET). We propose a modular, tumor-aware pipeline that learns PET-associated representations from computed tomography (CT) images using paired CT–PET data as supervisory information. The computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system consists of four stages: (i) field-of-view alignment using YOLOv11, (ii) synthetic 18 F-FDG PET generation via a ResNet-9 based generator with a patchGAN discriminator (CPGAN), (iii) tumor segmentation with SegResNet to guide region-specific synthesis, and (iv) tumor-aware PET enhancement through tumor superimposition and PET-CT fusion. Experimental evaluations indicate strong performance across multiple tasks. Thoracic region detection achieved mAP50 scores of 99.50% (CT) and 98.50% (PET), while lung segmentation reached 99.20%. 18 F-FDG PET synthesis with CPGAN yielded PSNR 20.94 dB, SSIM 72.94%, and MAE 0.036. Incorporating tumor superimposition substantially improved 18 F-FDG PET quality within tumor regions (SSIM 83.47%, PSNR 25.99 dB, MAE 0.017). After peripheral padding, full-image metrics further improved (SSIM 96.35%, PSNR 33.66 dB, MAE 0.0036). For the segmentation, SegResNet model achieved the highest performance (Dice: 97.06%, IoU: 93.65%). The proposed framework provides an anatomically grounded visualization that can highlight CT regions associated with metabolically active tumors and may assist radiologists in identifying areas warranting further assessment.

Article.Title: Economic and technical optimal sizing and placement of the hybrid energy resources in the electrical grid considering uncertainties
Article.Authors: Lin M.; Kamol K.; Kamola I.; Bakhodir E.; Radjabova L.; Saidov M.; Farrux Q.; Abdullayeva M.
Article.Abstract: The integration of hybrid energy resources in the electrical grids is essential for improving sustainability and reducing dependence on conventional fossil-fuel generation. Hence, installation of these energy resources is required to maximize their technical and economic benefits while maintaining secure and stable grid operation. This paper focuses on a multi-objective optimization framework to identify the best installation and sizing of hybrid energy resources, considering the stochastic characteristics associated with renewable generation, such as photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine (WT) systems. The stochastic aspects of renewable generation are represented using the point estimate method, enabling the framework to account for variations in renewable resource availability. The multi-objective functions for the optimal installation and sizing of hybrid energy resources are developed with a focus on operational costs, Voltage Stability Index (VSI), and power losses. Two case studies are provided to validate the proposed algorithm, examining different configurations of hybrid energy resources in IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 118-bus test systems. The optimal sizing of hybrid energy resources in the IEEE 33-bus test system result in a 3.68% reduction in operating costs, a 42.89% decrease in power losses, and a 0.19% improvement in the VSI. Also, minimization rate of the operational costs and power losses, and improvement of VSI for IEEE 118-bus test system are equal to 9.3%, 13.23% and 0.3%, respectively.

Article.Title: Theta-band EEG network topology during semantic processing differs between children and adolescents
Article.Authors: Behboudi M.; Schneider J.; Maguire M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Language comprehension relies on the integration of semantic information across distributed brain networks, yet how the organization of these networks changes across childhood and adolescence remains poorly understood. This study used electroencephalography (EEG) connectivity and graph theory to examine theta-band (4–8 Hz) network organization in 28 children aged 8–10 years and 31 adolescents aged 12–14 years as they listened to correct sentences and sentences with a semantic violation, created by pairing an agent with an implausible action. Functional connectivity was computed using the imaginary part of coherency. Global efficiency, local efficiency, and modularity were extracted from theta networks during the N400 time window. Network density was selected by efficiency-cost optimization. All three metrics showed a significant Age Group × Condition interaction. During correct sentences, children had higher global efficiency, local efficiency, and modularity than adolescents, but the groups did not differ significantly during semantic violations. Among children, those with stronger online sentence processing skills showed lower theta-network modularity during semantic violations. These findings suggest that children may rely more on organized theta networks to integrate meaning, whereas the lower theta-network values in adolescents during correct sentences may reflect a broader combination of frequency bands supporting comprehension at this age.

Article.Title: Understanding parental experiences before pediatric cochlear implantation in Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Ivasenko A.; Yousef E.; Almassad A.; Almuhawas F.; Yousef M.
Article.Abstract: Pediatric cochlear implantation (CI) is routinely offered in infancy, yet parents may face an unexpected diagnosis, difficult treatment decisions, and a pathway shaped by access to specialist care. This qualitative interview study used reflexive thematic analysis to examine pre-implantation experiences of nine parents (eight mothers and one father) representing eight families and ten children who received CI at a tertiary center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Semi-structured interviews, conducted between April 22 and May 15, 2025, were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated from Arabic to English with back-translation, and reviewed by participants for transcript accuracy. Two researchers developed inductive, semantic, cross-case themes through collaborative reflexive discussion. Six themes described life before CI; receiving the news; decision-making; diagnosis and access; preparing for surgery; and doctors and hospitals. Parents described communication difficulties and perceived developmental and school-related consequences before implantation; shock and gradual acceptance after diagnosis; deliberation informed by clinicians, other families, and relatives; access barriers; fear and hope before surgery; and trust in clinicians and hospital transparency. Pre-implant counseling should anticipate the emotional impact of diagnosis, address informational and access barriers, and facilitate family-centered discussion of peer support, communication options, and faith where parents wish to raise it.

Article.Title: Risk and benefit perceptions asymmetrically shape wearable health monitoring device adoption in India
Article.Authors: Jadhav B.; Misra S.; Adtani R.; Mishra A.
Article.Abstract: Wearable health monitoring devices (WHMDs), which include smartwatches, fitness trackers, continuous glucose monitors, and cardiac patches, are an important innovation in the personal management of health, but their uptake is not even, and dropout rates are well-documented. Based on the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB; 1 ), this research hypothesizes and empirically tests an extended model that implements benefit perceptions and risk perceptions as parallel antecedents of attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control. In addition to the traditional TPB variables of subjective norms, perceived behavioural control and behavioural intention, benefit perceptions and risk perceptions were added as parallel antecedents of attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control. Path coefficients were estimated by using Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped inference on a sample of 235 respondents. Findings show that risk perceptions had a significantly larger impact on attitude toward WHMD adoption (β = − 0.540, p < 0.001) than benefit perceptions (β = 0.192, p = 0.001), which is consistent with a loss-aversion dynamic in prospect theory 2 ,notably, risk's influence was confined to attitude and did not extend to perceived behavioural control or subjective norms, both of which were driven significantly by benefit perceptions instead. Subjective norms and perceived behavioural control were, in turn, significant predictors of adoption intention (β = 0.380 and β = 0.374, respectively), and behavioural intention significantly predicted actual use of the device (β = 0.645, p < 0.001). The implications of the findings are relevant to device manufacturers, healthcare providers, and policymakers aiming to understand risk concerns and to bring about sustained WHMD adoption in different groups.

Article.Title: A Bayesian-evolutionary game framework for robust multi-agent workforce scheduling in resilient supply chains
Article.Authors: Yu S.; Cui F.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a Bayesian–Evolutionary Hybrid Game with Robust Stochastic Optimisation (BEHG-RSO) framework for coordinated workforce allocation under supply-chain disruptions. Bayesian partner-reliability estimates and evolving cooperation shares enter a two-stage mean–worst-case mixed-integer scheduling model through effective productivity and reserve-sharing capacity. The evaluation combines public benchmark data, multi-agent simulation and a paired 30-seed comparative analysis. The experiments report 93.6% workforce utilisation, a 9.9% reduction in scheduling cost relative to the multi-agent reinforcement learning comparator and a 25.5% reduction in recovery time. Component-ablation, paired uncertainty and computational-scaling analyses further characterise performance under the evaluated disruption scenarios. The results demonstrate the framework’s operational trade-offs and computational requirements.

Article.Title: Robust microseismic arrival picking for hydraulic fracturing monitoring using a deep orthogonal collaborative ensemble network
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Zhang Y.; Chen F.
Article.Abstract: Accurate microseismic arrival picking is critical for hydraulic fracturing monitoring and subsequent fracture characterization. In recent years, deep learning-based pickers have achieved promising performance by automatically learning complex waveform features. However, these pickers still face challenges in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments and in changing monitoring scenarios. These challenges are closely related to the restricted feature representation capability of individual network architectures, which may hinder their ability to capture diverse waveform features. To overcome this issue, we propose a deep orthogonal collaborative ensemble network (DOCE-Net) for robust microseismic arrival picking in hydraulic fracturing monitoring. DOCE-Net employs three heterogeneous base learners, including U-Net, Res-LSTM, and TransNet, to capture complementary waveform representations from multi-trace microseismic data. An orthogonality constraint is introduced to reduce feature redundancy and enhance diversity among different learners. The outputs of these learners are further combined through a semblance-based decision-level fusion strategy, which exploits prediction consistency to improve picking reliability. The proposed method is evaluated using two field hydraulic fracturing microseismic datasets. In the in-domain tests, DOCE-Net consistently outperforms the three individual base learners, particularly under low SNR conditions, and achieves higher accuracy than its single-trace counterpart, confirming the contribution of multi-trace spatial coherence. In the cross-domain tests, DOCE-Net also achieves superior performance after fine-tuning with limited labeled samples from an unseen monitoring domain. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DOCE-Net for robust microseismic arrival picking and cross-domain generalization. This study indicates that DOCE-Net can provide a reliable strategy for developing robust and transferable microseismic phase arrival pickers.

Article.Title: Physics-informed neural surrogate learning predicts cervical cancer progression with mechanistic interpretability
Article.Authors: Sridharan P.; Ghosh M.
Article.Abstract: Deep learning models achieve high predictive accuracy in oncology but operate as black boxes, while mechanistic models offer biological interpretability but fail to capture patient heterogeneity. Prior work has explored hybrid approaches combining these paradigms, yet fundamental challenges remain in ensuring biological consistency and clinical trustworthiness. We developed a Physics-Informed Neural Surrogate Learning (PI-NSL) framework that incorporates a system of biophysical partial differential equations (PDEs) governing tumor-immune-viral dynamics as soft constraints within a deep neural network, guiding learned representations toward biological plausibility. The framework comprises a variational physics encoder that infers patient-specific PDE parameters from routine clinical data, a differentiable PDE solver for efficient spatiotemporal simulation, and a dynamic risk operator for survival prediction. We applied PI-NSL to a longitudinal cohort of \(\text{20,287}\) cervical cancer patients treated at Apollo Proton Cancer Centre (Chennai, India, \(2018-2023)\) . The development cohort was partitioned \(70/15/15\) . All \(\text{2,663}\) patients enrolled in \(2023\) were assigned to the held-out test set to enable temporal internal validation; the \(2023\) subset is therefore nested within the \(\text{3,043}\) -patient test set, not additional to the \(\text{20,287}\) -patient analytical cohort. External validation used two independent institutions: Tata Memorial Centre (TMC, \(n=\text{8,432})\) and AIIMS \(\left(n=\text{7,535}\right)\) ; total external \(n=\text{15,967}\) . PI-NSL achieved a time-dependent AUC of \(0.91\pm 0.03\) for \(2-year\) progression-free survival prediction, with a C-index of \(0.89\pm 0.04\) . Unsupervised analysis of the model’s latent representations identified three clinically distinct clusters with significantly different survival outcomes \(\left(log-rank p<0.001\right)\) : Cluster 1 (high immune activity, \(34\%\) , \( 84\%, 2-year PFS\) ), Cluster 2 (peripheral immune accumulation, \(41\%, 45\%\) ), and Cluster 3 (high proliferation, \(25\%, 28\%\) ). Model calibration demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed survival probabilities (integrated Brier score \(=0.082\pm 0.015\) ). On the \(2023\) temporal subset nested within the test set \(\left(n=\text{2,663}\right)\) , performance was stable (time-dependent AUC \(0.89\pm 0.05; \Delta AUC=-0.01\) versus the non- \(2023\) test subset, \(p=0.72)\) . External evaluation provided evidence of generalizability within the Indian healthcare context, with time-dependent AUC values of \(0.87\pm 0.05\) at TMC and \(0.86\pm 0.05\) at AIIMS. PI-NSL demonstrates that incorporating mechanistic biological knowledge as soft constraints within neural architectures can achieve strong predictive performance while providing clinically interpretable outputs. The identified clusters generate hypotheses about mechanisms of treatment resistance that warrant prospective validation. This framework represents a step toward AI systems that are both accurate and mechanistically grounded for clinical oncology applications.

Article.Title: Risk of low energy availability among Indian athletes in weight-dependent sports: ​Phase I multicentre study
Article.Authors: Santhiya B.; Kawale P.; Kalpana K.; Chakraborty A.; Tiwari H.; Kshetrimayum K.; Tiwari K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low energy availability (LEA) is a concern among athletes, particularly in weight-dependent sports, where high training demands and weight-management practices are associated with LEA risk. This multicentre cross-sectional study estimated LEA risk and examined its associations with exercise dependence, disordered eating, sleep quality, and sleep behaviour among Indian athletes. A total of 271 athletes in five weight-dependent sports (174 males and 97 females; aged 15–23 years) completed the Low Energy Availability in Females Questionnaire (LEAF-Q), Low Energy Availability in Males Questionnaire (LEAM-Q), and validated questionnaires. Overall, 38.7% of athletes were classified as being at risk of LEA, including 51.1% of males classified using the LEAM-Q and 16.5% of females classified using the LEAF-Q ( P < 0.001). LEA risk exceeded 40% among athletes from Delhi andHaryana, junior athletes, those participating in grappling sports, and the middle-weight category. Among female athletes, LEA risk was associated with exercise dependence, disordered eating, sleep quality, and sleep behaviour. Female athletes with disordered eating had 4.4-fold higher odds of LEA risk (OR = 4.42, ​95% CI: 1.08–18.21; P = 0.039), whereas no significant associations were observed among male athletes. These findings suggest considering disordered eating, exercise dependence, and sleep in LEA risk screening.

Article.Title: A complete-coverage path-planning algorithm based on local path cost
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zhu Y.; Tang J.; Dai Z.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Complete coverage path planning (CCPP) is a core enabling technology for autonomous operation and navigation of mobile robots and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). However, in large-scale and complex environments, due to the lack of directional guidance in population evolution, existing heuristic path planners often suffer from slow convergence, premature trapping in local optima, and excessive turning maneuvers along the planned tour. To mitigate the blindness of conventional mutation operators, this paper proposes a complete-coverage path-planning algorithm based on local path cost (CCPP-LPC). First, a local path cost evaluation model is constructed to adaptively quantify the possible impact that each node may have on the overall path length, thereby identifying nodes with high optimization potential. Second, an adaptive dual-guided perturbation node selection strategy is designed, which derives both optimization-oriented and diversity-oriented probability distributions from local costs, guiding the population to preferentially refine high-cost segments while preserving gene diversity. To assess the performance of CCPP-LPC, comprehensive comparisons against six state-of-the-art heuristic algorithms on four simulated grid maps of varying scales and complexity are conducted, as well as four simulation maps from real environment. Experimental results show that CCPP-LPC not only improves computational efficiency, but also achieves the best performance across key metrics, including path length, and repeated coverage ratio. These outcomes highlight CCPP-LPC as a practically valuable approach for complete-coverage optimization under multi-constrained, complex environments.

Article.Title: Functional time series forecasting of air temperature using a functional autoregressive model with electricity demand as an exogenous variable
Article.Authors: Jan F.; Alshanbari H.; Assar G.; Tahir M.; Shafee A.; Iqbal N.
Article.Abstract: Short-term air temperature (AT) forecasting is crucial for climate monitoring, integration of renewable energy, agricultural management, and environmental decision-making. The inherent complexity of the temporal structure of AT (nonlinear dynamics, high diurnal periodicity, the interactions between various meteorological variables) makes the conventional statistical and machine learning models (which typically view AT observations as discrete time series and do not make effective use of the continuous functional structure of AT) less effective in predicting AT. This study proposes a functional autoregressive model with exogenous variable (FARX(1)) for predicting daily AT curves in a functional time series (FTS) context, overcoming these limitations. The proposed model is an extension of the classical functional autoregressive model of order one (FAR(1)), which maintains the time dependence and smooth functional structure of the daily temperature measurements; while additionally incorporating electricity demand as the exogenous variable, given its established association with diurnal temperature dynamics. The hourly AT data is approximated by smooth functional curves that enable efficient modeling of the diurnal temperature dynamics and observational noise in the data, and is obtained by an approximation of the data with Fourier basis functions. The ability of the proposed framework to forecast the performance is evaluated by comparing it with five widely used benchmark models: ARIMA, VAR, ANN, ARNN, and FAR(1) over extensive overall forecasting, hourly forecasting, weekly forecasting and monthly forecasting scenarios, employing the Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE), Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (sMAPE), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed FARX(1) model in minimizing the conventional FAR(1)’s forecasting error for all the evaluation scenarios, highlighting the significance of using the exogenous variable of electricity demand in the model for forecasting accuracy. The results also highlight the potential of representing AT as functional observations to obtain a flexible and statistically sound representation of complex temporal variations, which enhances the reliability and robustness of short-term AT forecasts. The concept is proposed as a solution for the meteorology community in operational forecasting to the weather community and as climate monitoring and decision support to weather dependent applications such as renewable energy management.

Article.Title: Regional sediment characterization and curve reconstruction for hydropower infrastructure design and turbine wear management
Article.Authors: Oğulcan Marangoz H.; Süme V.; Daneshfaraz R.; Yılmaz E.; Aliyev E.
Article.Abstract: Hydro-abrasive turbine wear caused by sediment passage is a severe operational and economic threat to run-of-river hydropower plants (HPPs) in steep, mountainous regions, leading to rapid efficiency decline and high turbine maintenance costs. This study investigated the spatial and seasonal variability of sediment grain-size distributions (GSD) across 11 HPPs in Rize, Türkiye, to establish a regional baseline and a sediment characterization and GSD reconstruction framework relevant to sediment management. A total of 53 GSD curves were evaluated from regulator sediments during winter and summer periods. Samples were analyzed using conventional granulometric parameters, compositional data analysis (CoDa), principal component analysis (PCA), unsupervised clustering, and paired seasonal tests. The representativeness of composite mixed samples was also assessed at the HPP level to evaluate cost-efficient sampling protocols. Ridge, partial least squares, and Gaussian process regression were compared with regional median and logarithmic interpolation benchmarks under three partial-measurement scenarios using leave-one-HPP-out cross-validation to evaluate reconstruction accuracy at unmeasured sieve sizes. No statistically significant seasonal differences were detected in sediment compositions ( p = 0.650). This result indicates that a consistent winter–summer contrast was not established in the sampled dataset; it does not identify the processes controlling sediment variability or erosive hazards. PCA and clustering identified four exploratory sediment groups with contrasting gravel, sand, and fine-material proportions, providing a descriptive basis for comparing deposited sediment among the sampled locations. Crucially, Under Scenario 2, using measurements at five sieve sizes, logarithmic interpolation reconstructed the unmeasured GSD values with high accuracy (R 2 = 0.978; MAE = 1.706 percentage points), outperforming the evaluated machine-learning models. These findings support a five-sieve reconstruction approach for preliminary sediment screening, although its benefits in terms of testing time, labour, and cost require direct evaluation.
