Article.Title: Stability analysis of networked control systems using three-layer delay modelling
Article.Authors: Chowdary G.; Azad S.; Priyanka S.
Article.Abstract: Networked Control Systems (NCS) play a vital role in industrial process automation by enabling communication among sensors, controllers, and actuators through shared communication networks. However, delays caused by field devices and multi-layer protocol stacks significantly influence closed-loop stability and transient performance. This paper investigates the dynamic effects of delay in a three-layer network structure within industrial process control. A systematic delay assessment model is developed to evaluate the significance of delay within each layer and to include these delays in closed-loop stability analysis. Unlike existing lumped-delay models, the proposed methodology explicitly decouples deterministic intra-device processing delays from multi-layer protocol communication delays. The paper derives the exact Maximum Allowable Communication Delay (MACD) using frequency-domain Phase Margin criteria and validates closed-loop stability margins. Furthermore, an industrial layer-aware Smith Predictor architecture is developed to compensate for network transport delays, demonstrating that while communication latencies can be effectively eliminated from the closed-loop characteristic equation, uncompensated internal device execution delays establish an ultimate physical performance boundary. Benchmark simulations across Open-Loop, Closed-Loop, and Cascade-Loop configurations validate that the proposed co-design framework enhances stability margins, mitigates phase erosion, and minimizes transient lag in industrial automation.
Article.Topic: Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Advanced Control Systems Design; Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Teleoperation and Haptic Systems

Article.Title: The relationship between SARS-CoV-2 infection history and persistent symptoms in a rural Wisconsin community cohort
Article.Authors: Sundaram M.; Alonge O.; King J.; Petrie J.; Saydah S.; Feldstein L.; Rolfes M.; Belongia E.; Nguyen H.
Article.Abstract: Some individuals experience persistent symptoms after COVID-19 (“Long COVID”). We assessed persistent symptoms consistent with Long COVID by SARS-CoV-2 infection history. Participants of a longitudinal, community-based cohort completed a survey about new persistent symptoms starting on/after January 2022. Cox models assessed relative hazards of symptoms among those with Omicron-only infection, or Omicron plus pre-Omicron infection, versus no infection. Models controlled for age group (18–49 versus ≥ 50 years), sex, and chronic health conditions as time-fixed effects and vaccination status as time-varying. Of 646 respondents, 61% were female; 66% were ≥ 50 years old. The presence of ≥ 1 new persistent symptom was 37% (107/287), 41% (124/303), and 43% (24/56) among individuals with no infection, Omicron-only infection, and Omicron plus pre-Omicron infection, respectively. Individuals with Omicron-only infection had increased, non-significant hazards of new persistent symptoms (aHR: 1.23, 95% CI: 0.94–1.61) compared to individuals with no infection. Individuals with Omicron plus pre-Omicron infection had increased, statistically significant hazards of new persistent symptoms (aHR: 1.94, 95% CI: 1.33–2.83) compared to no infection. During the Omicron variant period, SARS-CoV-2 reinfection was associated with new persistent symptoms in adults. Primary infection was not statistically significantly associated with new persistent symptoms compared to those not infected.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Clinical Neurology > Long-Term Effects of COVID-19; Medicine > Infectious Diseases > COVID-19 Clinical Research Studies; Medicine > Infectious Diseases > SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19 Research

Article.Title: Identification and characterization of unique plastic degrading bacteria from the east Kolkata wetlands
Article.Authors: Ghosh S.; Chaudhuri S.; Ghosh S.; Mitra A.; Choudhury S.; Chandra A.; Uti D.; Dhara B.
Article.Abstract: Plastic pollution is an environmental issue that has been highlighted by scientists and activists for years. While most definitely being cheap to produce and having a myriad of uses, these polymers take anywhere from 20 to almost 500 years to effectively decompose, thus, continuing to remain in the environment for decades when carelessly discarded. As a consequence of weathering forces, they erode into microscopic particles in the environment, eventually contaminating water and food sources, and entering living tissues. This study was aimed towards reducing the pollution caused by these particulates in soil used for cultivation. Accordingly, soil samples were collected from the East Kolkata Wetlands (EKW) municipal waste dumping ground and the presence of microplastics in them was analysed and demonstrated using FT-IR Spectroscopy. Bacteria were isolated from the soil sample, and assays for the production of microplastic degrading enzymes were conducted for these strains. They were identified using 16S rRNA sequencing as Bacillus paramycoides , Bacillus siamensis , Bacillus velezensis and Bacillus altitudinis, which were further used to develop a consortium. This consortium was added to pre-weighed Polyethylene (PE) and Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) in nutrient broth, and minimal salts media devoid of any carbon source separately. Another set-up involved adding the bacteria to soil polluted with microplastics. The applied consortium was found to be effective in breaking down plastics since, at the end of the 45-day incubation period, the weight of PE was reduced by 9.180% in nutrient broth, and by 11.870% in minimal salts medium. The weight of PET was reduced by 3.050% in nutrient broth, and by 6.280% in minimal salts media. Scanning Electron Microscopy of the plastics revealed the extent and type of degradation in each of these cases. In the soil sample set-up, microplastics per 0.05 g of soil decreased by almost 70.78% at the end of 45 days upon addition of the consortium. Therefore, this study provides an insight into the impacts of unique plastic degrading bacteria in the EKW and their futuristic impacts upon reducing plastic pollution in other contaminated soils used for agriculture.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Pollution > Microplastics and Plastic Pollution; Environmental Science > Pollution > Microbial bioremediation and biosurfactants; Materials Science > Biomaterials > biodegradable polymer synthesis and properties

Article.Title: Association between the neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio and 30-day mortality in intensive care unit patients: a retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Yang Y.; Lu J.; Xiu J.; Wang L.; Zhao Y.; Zou K.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: We examined the association between the neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) and mortality in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients. Methods: The primary analysis used albumin and neutrophil-percentage measurements obtained 0–24 h after ICU admission and no more than 2 h apart. Patients had to be alive at hour 24; follow-up began at that landmark and ended at day 30. A four-knot restricted cubic spline logistic model adjusted for age, sex, selected comorbidities, first-day SOFA score, and sepsis. Results: The primary cohort included 5,130 patients, of whom 1,082 (21.1%) died between hour 24 and day 30. The spline fit better than the linear model (AIC 4,451.4 vs. 4,475.3; likelihood-ratio chi-square = 27.85, df = 2, p < 0.001). The adjusted linear OR was 1.15 (95% CI, 1.10–1.19) per 5-unit increase in NPAR. NPAR alone had modest discrimination (AUC 0.627) and did not outperform albumin alone (AUC 0.631; p = 0.639). Conclusions: Temporally aligned, paired NPAR was associated with subsequent mortality, but evidence of curvature depended on distribution tails and incremental discrimination was small. Residual selection bias, covariate-timing uncertainty, confounding, and lack of external validation preclude clinical use.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Critical Care and Intensive Care Medicine > Sepsis Diagnosis and Treatment; Medicine > Oncology > Inflammatory Biomarkers in Disease Prognosis; Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Inflammation biomarkers and pathways

Article.Title: Effects of rice bran protein hydrolysate and sweetener addition levels on Hom Nil rice drink with honey or sucrose syrup
Article.Authors: Pakakaew P.; Chaisan W.; Singh K.; Utama-ang N.
Article.Abstract: Hom Nil rice drink (HNRD) fortified with rice bran protein hydrolysate (RBPH) was developed as a functional beverage promoting agricultural sustainability. Response surface methodology (RSM) was used for optimization. Two independent 3-level factorial designs evaluated RBPH concentration (0.5–2.5 g/100 g base mixture) and sweetener addition level (0–15% w/w of the base mixture) in honey- and sucrose syrup-based formulations. Physicochemical, sensory, and antioxidant properties were evaluated. In both systems, increasing RBPH enhanced protein content and antioxidant capacity but reduced sensory acceptability, whereas increasing sweetener addition levels improved overall liking, flavor, and aftertaste. Principal component analysis (PCA) associated sweetener addition levels with sensory acceptance and higher RBPH concentrations with ABTS, FRAP, viscosity, and color development. The honey-based optimum contained 0.55 g RBPH/100 g base mixture and 13.91% honey (w/w of base mixture), whereas the sucrose syrup-based formulation contained 0.70 g RBPH/100 g base mixture and 11.85% sucrose syrup (w/w of base mixture). The optimized sucrose syrup-based formulation had higher rice aroma and flavor liking scores ( p ≤ 0.05), whereas the honey-based formulation had higher protein content and FRAP antioxidant capacity. Acceptance and purchase intent did not differ significantly between formulations. These findings indicate trade-offs between sensory, nutritional, and antioxidant characteristics.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Protein Hydrolysis and Bioactive Peptides; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Food Nutrient Composition and Product Development; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Food Quality and Safety Studies

Article.Title: Trigonometric cubic $$\mathscr {B}$$-spline collocation approach for system of singularly perturbed turning point problem with integral boundary conditions
Article.Authors: Karanam C.; Maroju P.
Article.Abstract: This study focuses on a system of singularly perturbed turning point problems (SPTPPs) with integral boundary conditions (IBCs). When a turning point is present, boundary layers arise at both ends of the domain, making numerical approximation of the problem more difficult. To effectively address this difficulty, we propose a trigonometric cubic \(\mathscr {B}\) -spline collocation method (TCBSCM) constructed on a Shishkin mesh, which is specifically designed to accurately capture the layer behavior. The trapezoidal rule is used to discretize the IBCs, and the discrete maximum norm is used to assess the accuracy of the method. It is demonstrated that the proposed approach achieves close to second-order convergence. Numerical experiments are carried out to validate the theoretical findings, and a comparative study with the existing FDM and the cubic B-spline collocation method (CBSCM) by Geetha et al. 1 provides evidence of the accuracy and its favorable convergence behavior of the proposed approach.
Article.Topic: Singular Perturbation, Asymptotics and Difference Schemes
Article.TopicFields: Mathematics > Numerical Analysis > Singular Perturbation, Asymptotics and Difference Schemes; Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Advanced Numerical Methods in Computational Mathematics; Mathematics > Modeling and Simulation > Fractional Differential Equations Solutions

Article.Title: Antiviral activity of Clinacanthus siamensis Bremek ethanolic extract against dengue virus serotype 2 infection
Article.Authors: Fungfueang S.; Boonsatit N.; Thongyim S.; Inta A.; Baillie G.; Limjindaporn T.; Yenchitsomanus P.; Panya A.
Article.Abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) infection causes dengue fever and can progress to severe, life-threatening diseases. Currently, no specific antiviral therapy is available, and although vaccines exist, their variable efficacy across DENV serotypes raises safety concerns. Therefore, the identification of effective antiviral agents remains critical for reducing disease severity and limiting viral transmission. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of the Thai medicinal herb Clinacanthus siamensis against DENV infection. An ethanolic extract of C. siamensis was evaluated using in vitro DENV infection assays and demonstrated significant antiviral activity, with an IC₅₀ value of 19.32 µg/mL. The inhibitory mechanism of the extract was evaluated across multiple stages of the viral life cycle using time-of-addition experiments, including pre-treatment, co-treatment, and post-infection conditions, in which the virus was exposed to the extract before, during, and after viral entry, respectively. The pre-treatment condition demonstrated the highest level of inhibition, with the extract reducing viral protein levels to 92.79 ± 7.74%, 60.30 ± 9.79%, and 12.52 ± 10.18% at concentrations of 15.625, 31.25, and 62.5 µg/mL, respectively. These findings suggest that the extract exerts its antiviral activity predominantly at an early stage of infection. This observation was further supported by virus-binding assays, which demonstrated that pretreatment of viral particles with the extract impaired their subsequent ability to bind to host cells, suggesting a direct effect on viral particles that may contribute to reduced viral infectivity. In addition, the bioactive constituents of the extract were characterized using LC–MS/MS analysis, which identified two compounds with reported antiviral activity, including isoferulic acid and luteolin, that may contribute to the observed anti-DENV effects. These findings demonstrate that C. siamensis possesses potent anti-DENV activity by reducing viral infectivity at an early stage of infection and highlights the potential of C. siamensis for future development as an affordable therapeutic candidate against DENV​ infection.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Complementary and alternative medicine > Medicinal Plant Studies; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Medicinal Plant Research; Medicine > Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health > Mosquito-borne diseases and control

Article.Title: Forecasting weekly influenza-like illness counts in chongqing using a temporal attention-based multisource network (TAM-Net)
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Zhou J.; Ni L.; Wang J.; Yuan Y.; Long J.; Peng B.
Article.Abstract: Routine ILI surveillance can be complemented by internet search and meteorological data, but integrating these data streams with different temporal patterns is an important consideration for multi-horizon forecasting. This study developed and evaluated a Temporal Attention-Based Multisource Network (TAM-Net) for 1- to 4-week-ahead forecasting of weekly ILI case counts in Chongqing using ILI surveillance, Baidu Search Index, and meteorological data. Weekly ILI surveillance, Baidu Search Index, and meteorological data from Chongqing (2015–2024) were integrated and chronologically divided into training, validation, and test sets (70%, 15%, and 15%, respectively). Using a 26-week input window, TAM-Net employed branch-specific LSTM and TCN encoders to extract temporal features from ILI and exogenous data, respectively. Multi-head self-attention and forecast-horizon-wise adaptive gating were incorporated to refine temporal representations and dynamically adjust branch contributions across the 1- to 4-week forecasting horizons. TAM-Net achieved an overall RMSE of 1,418.06 ± 104.93 and an R² of 0.754 ± 0.037, demonstrating favorable forecasting performance compared with the evaluated baseline models. Ablation experiments highlighted the contributions of heterogeneous data sources and architectural components. The forecast-horizon-wise adaptive gating mechanism dynamically adjusted the contributions of historical ILI and exogenous information across different forecasting horizons, while rolling-origin validation further supported the model’s predictive performance. TAM-Net combines branch-specific temporal encoding with forecast-horizon-wise adaptive fusion for short-term ILI forecasting. However, its evaluation was limited to a single region and retrospective data; external and prospective validation is needed to establish its generalizability.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Epidemiology > Data-Driven Disease Surveillance; Computer Science > Signal Processing > Time Series Analysis and Forecasting; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Forecasting Techniques and Applications

Article.Title: FP-TTFNet: fourier periodic embedding enhanced multi-scale deep learning for monthly runoff prediction at contrasting hydrological stations
Article.Authors: Xu D.; Li J.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Reliable monthly runoff forecasts are essential for reservoir operation, water allocation, and flood–drought preparedness, but their robustness across contrasting basins is limited by multiscale periodicity, nonlinear catchment response, and spatiotemporal heterogeneity. This study develops FP-TTFNet, an end-to-end forecasting framework that couples explicit periodic priors with adaptive nonlinear mapping and collaborative local–global dependency modeling for monthly runoff prediction. Fourier periodic embedding encodes seasonal and interannual phase information; a parametric nonlinear feature processor adapts to heterogeneous catchment responses; multiscale temporal convolution and Transformer self-attention jointly capture short-term fluctuations and long-range dependencies; and an operationally weighted hybrid loss emphasizes peak flows and long-horizon stability. The framework is evaluated on three climatically distinct stations—monsoon-dominated Manwan, arid Jiayuguan, and alpine-transition Hongshanhe—against LSTM, GRU, RNN, TCN, and Transformer using ten repeated runs and significance testing. FP-TTFNet consistently achieves the lowest errors and highest efficiency: at Manwan, MAE is reduced by 22.0% to 176.06 m 3 /s with KGE = 0.9591; at Jiayuguan, RMSE is reduced by 43.1% to 2.99 m 3 /s; at Hongshanhe, NSE reaches 0.9508 despite the 117 km 2 catchment. Across all sites, NSE exceeds 0.92, and KGE exceeds 0.95. The results show that integrating interpretable periodic priors, nonlinear adaptation, multiscale dependency fusion, and operation-oriented optimization provides robust monthly runoff forecasts for engineering decision-making.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Hydrological Forecasting Using AI; Environmental Science > Water Science and Technology > Hydrology and Watershed Management Studies; Environmental Science > Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law > Environmental Monitoring and Data Management

Article.Title: Deep neural network-controlled autonomous laser oscillation
Article.Authors: Ikeya Y.; Sekine T.; Tani S.; Endo T.; Otsu T.; Morita T.; Tamaoki Y.; Kato Y.; Kawashima T.; Kobayashi Y.
Article.Abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success in data-rich domains, but applying it to physical systems remains challenging because labelled datasets are difficult to acquire and model predictions must be converted into fast, repeatable hardware interventions. Laser-cavity alignment in solid-state lasers is one such problem that still relies heavily on skilled operators. Here, we demonstrate an autonomous solid-state-laser feedback system in which a programmable liquid-crystal-on-silicon spatial light modulator acts as an intracavity mirror and an image-based deep neural network predicts alignment and curvature corrections from pre-lasing amplified-spontaneous-emission images. In the original optical configuration, the system initiated laser oscillation from unseen non-lasing states after a single feedback update. After manual removal and coarse reinstallation of the modulator, the same trained model recovered laser oscillation from non-lasing starting conditions within two feedback updates in three independent tests, without retraining. These results show that weak pre-lasing spatial emission patterns contain actionable information about the latent cavity state, enabling reproducible, electronically programmable initiation of solid-state laser oscillation with practical tolerance to alignment perturbations introduced by manual reinstallation.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Solid State Laser Technologies; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Semiconductor Lasers and Optical Devices; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Neural Networks and Reservoir Computing

Article.Title: Advanced pollen-based nanoplasmonic biosensing platforms for salivary TNF-α monitoring: toward point-of-care oral disease diagnostics
Article.Authors: Annunziata M.; Cennamo N.; Stampone E.; Arcadio F.; Bencivenga D.; Cecoro G.; Pasquardini L.; Della Ragione F.; Guida L.; Zeni L.; Guida A.; Borriello A.
Article.Abstract: Saliva is a readily accessible, non-invasively collected biofluid, increasingly recognized as a potential liquid biopsy for the diagnosis and monitoring of oral diseases. However, reliable assessment of disease biomarkers remains challenging, as their concentrations often lie at or below the analytical detection limits, and available volumes may be insufficient for accurate analysis. Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) is a key cytokine of several oral diseases, with concentrations that vary widely depending on their nature. This research introduces a pollen-based nanoplasmonic biosensor for highly sensitive detection of TNF-α in saliva. The biosensing platform exploits the natural nanostructures of sunflower pollen covered with a gold nanofilm to improve biosensor performance by hybrid plasmonic phenomena, reaching a limit of detection of 3.4 × 10⁻ 19 M. Through appropriate sample dilution, this capability significantly extends the platform’s potential applicability across the widely varying TNF-α concentrations typically encountered in clinical settings. As a preliminary proof of concept, distinct TNF-α salivary concentrations were measured from a healthy subject and two patients with an inflammatory and a neoplastic oral disease, respectively. While further clinical validation on larger patient and healthy cohorts, as well as the comparison with gold-standard reference assays are required, these initial results support the feasibility of pollen-derived nanoplasmonic biosensors as potential tools for the salivary biomarkers assessment.
Article.Topic: Gold and Silver Nanoparticles Synthesis and Applications
Article.TopicFields: Materials Science > Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials > Gold and Silver Nanoparticles Synthesis and Applications; Physics and Astronomy > Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics > Plasmonic and Surface Plasmon Research; Engineering > Biomedical Engineering > Biosensors and Analytical Detection

Article.Title: Post-flood contrasts in soil properties and enzyme activities in a karst riparian zone: a paired-block comparative study
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Yang F.; Liu Q.; Yang J.; Tan S.; Yang K.; Ruan H.
Article.Abstract: Flooding is a primary riparian disturbance, yet the short-term biogeochemical consequences of rare, extreme floods remain poorly characterized in karst floodplains. After a 1-in-50-year flood in a karst reach of the Qingshui River (Guizhou, China), we compared soil physicochemical properties, carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) contents, and potential extracellular enzyme activities between three flood-affected locations covered by freshly deposited silt and three adjacent reference locations. Each flood–reference pair formed one block, yielding 72 observations (three blocks × two conditions × two layers × six dates). In mineral soil, flood-affected locations had higher moisture, organic C, total N, total P, and dissolved organic C, and lower nitrate and nitrite. Potential activities of C-, N-, and P-acquiring hydrolytic enzymes were lower, whereas peroxidase and polyphenol oxidase potentials were higher in both layers. Because cover-layer materials differed (flood silt versus native litter), primary inference uses mineral soil. PLS-SEM path coefficients had 95% bootstrap confidence intervals that included zero, so the path models describe association structure. Vector angles were 37.6° with urease alone and 59.7° with denitrification reductases included, indicating N and P limitation, respectively. These contrasts apply to the studied reach; broader inference requires replicated reaches.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Soil Carbon and Nitrogen Dynamics; Environmental Science > Environmental Chemistry > Soil and Water Nutrient Dynamics; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Soil erosion and sediment transport

Article.Title: Traffic signs recognition for advanced driver assistance systems using deep learning
Article.Authors: Hesham M.; Abdrabou M.; Shawky M.; ShamsEldin T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traffic accidents remain a major global cause of death, motivating the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). Within ADAS, traffic sign recognition (TSR) is essential for interpreting road environments and improving driving safety. However, challenges such as changes in lighting, poor weather conditions, and blocked signs continue to limit recognition accuracy. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have substantially improved TSR performance. This study evaluates deep learning architectures for TSR on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset across three research pathways. First, a benchmarking study reproduces the Custom CNN and VGG16 architectures proposed by the existing paper under a closely matched experimental protocol, with the reproduced Custom CNN achieving a validation accuracy of 97.82%, surpassing the 94–96% reported in the baseline. Second, three newly introduced architectures AlexNet, Xception, and YOLOv11 are evaluated, with Xception achieving 92.95% validation accuracy and YOLOv11 achieving a test mAP50 of 97%, suggesting a potential advantage of detection-based frameworks for real-time ADAS applications in this single-run, single-dataset evaluation. Third, two transformer-based architectures ViT-B/16 and DeiT-Tiny are developed and evaluated, achieving test accuracies of 96.96% and 96.61% respectively, with DeiT-Tiny delivering superior precision, recall, and F1-score despite being 15 times smaller. Results demonstrate that transformer-based and detection-based models offer compelling advantages over traditional CNN baselines, with DeiT-Tiny emerging as the most parameter-efficient architecture and YOLOv11 providing the strongest real-time spatial localization capability for ADAS deployment.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Engineering > Automotive Engineering > Autonomous Vehicle Technology and Safety; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning

Article.Title: Frequency-specific intersubject phase synchrony reveals network reconfiguration during emotional processing
Article.Authors: Tamimi M.; Daliri M.
Article.Abstract: Emotional processing (EP) involves coordinated responses across distributed brain systems. Although intersubject functional connectivity (ISFC) can characterize shared stimulus-related responses, the frequency-specific organization of intersubject phase coordination during EP remains insufficiently understood. We analyzed task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from 100 healthy adults from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) who performed a controlled face–shape matching task. Intersubject phase synchrony (ISPS) was estimated across four predefined low-frequency bands (Slow-5 to Slow-2). Regions of interest (ROI) - level ISPS time series were used to characterize the temporal organization of intersubject phase coordination, and ROI-to-ROI correlations were examined to assess frequency-specific network-level differences between the face and shape conditions. ISFC was additionally analyzed as a complementary reference measure. Condition-related differences in ISPS exhibited frequency- and network-dependent patterns. In Slow-5, face > shape differences prominently involved visual and limbic interactions, whereas shape > face differences primarily involved temporal-parietal and visual interactions. Slow-4 showed a broader pattern of face > shape differences involving visual interactions with temporal-parietal and frontoparietal networks, as well as within-visual-network connectivity differences. Only a small number of significant differences were observed in Slow-3, involving visual, frontoparietal, and default-mode network interactions. No significant condition-related differences were detected in Slow-2. ISFC revealed complementary condition-dependent patterns of intersubject functional coordination involving visual, limbic, and higher-order networks. Frequency-resolved ISPS revealed distinct network-level patterns of intersubject phase coordination across low-frequency bands during a controlled face–shape matching task. These findings support the utility of frequency-specific analyses for characterizing condition-related differences in intersubject network organization and provide a complementary perspective to conventional ISFC measures.
Article.TopicFields: Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > Functional Brain Connectivity Studies; Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > Neural dynamics and brain function; Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > Neural and Behavioral Psychology Studies

Article.Title: Systematic evaluation of machine learning and explainable AI for NOx emission prediction in gas turbine systems
Article.Authors: Prabhu O.; Navada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for improving environmental sustainability, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency in gas turbine systems. However, the complex nonlinear interactions among environmental and operational variables make reliable emission forecasting challenging using conventional modeling approaches. This study presents a comprehensive machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework for NOx emission prediction using the Gas Turbine CO and NOx Emission dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Ten regression algorithms, including linear, tree-based, ensemble, and gradient-boosting models, were systematically evaluated and optimized using Grid Search, Random Search, and Bayesian Optimization. Model performance was assessed using multiple regression metrics, including R², MAE, MSE, RMSE, MAPE, EVS, and MedAE. Among all evaluated approaches, Bayesian-optimized LightGBM achieved the best predictive performance with an R² score of 0.8928 and an RMSE of 3.7694. To enhance model transparency, multiple complementary XAI techniques, including SHAP, Permutation Feature Importance, Partial Dependence Plots, Individual Conditional Expectation, LIME, surrogate modeling, and residual analysis, were employed. The explainability results consistently identified ambient temperature, turbine inlet temperature, gas turbine exhaust pressure, and turbine after temperature as the dominant factors influencing NOx emissions. The proposed framework demonstrates that high predictive accuracy and interpretability can be achieved simultaneously, providing a promising and transparent approach for NOx emission prediction in gas turbine systems.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI); Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Air Quality Monitoring and Forecasting; Energy > Energy Engineering and Power Technology > Advanced Power Generation Technologies

Article.Title: CFD-guided aerodynamic redesign of an electric bus for lower drag and energy demand
Article.Authors: Kahsay B.; Tirfe A.; Nallamothu R.; Fisha A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electric buses face range and battery-temperature limits, and aerodynamic drag is a major part of their energy demand at higher speeds. This study examines how three features of an electric bus, the windshield inclination, the ground clearance and the roof transition angle, affect its aerodynamics, using steady computational fluid dynamics simulations of a 1:10 model of the BYD K9. Each feature was varied in turn, and the final combined design was simulated directly. Grid convergence was confirmed on four meshes, and the normalized flow fields did not depend on Reynolds number over the simulated range. Inclining the windshield to 27° reduced the drag coefficient by 5.7%. Raising the ground clearance from 370 to 430 mm reduced it by a further 2.3%, while lowering the estimated underbody convective heat transfer by 1.2%. A 45° roof transition gave the largest single reduction and brought lift close to neutral. The final design lowered the drag coefficient from 0.603 to 0.501, a 16.9% reduction, which cuts the aerodynamic energy demand at 100 km/h from 0.70 to 0.58 kWh/km. The results come from steady, zero-yaw simulations without experimental validation.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Aerodynamics and Fluid Dynamics Research; Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Computational Fluid Dynamics and Aerodynamics; Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Fluid Dynamics and Vibration Analysis

Article.Title: Microfluidically fabricated purpurin microparticle-thermosensitive hydrogel hybrid system reduces inflammation and alveolar bone loss in rat periodontitis
Article.Authors: Shim G.; Shin S.; Choi E.; Kim H.; Kitagawa H.; Imazato S.; Oh S.; Bae J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Periodontitis is a dysbiotic, host-mediated inflammatory disease in which locally applied agents are rapidly cleared from the periodontal pocket, so sustaining a therapeutic concentration at the diseased site remains an unmet formulation problem. We addressed it by using purpurin-loaded calcium alginate microparticles incorporated in a thermosensitive hydrogel. Freeze-dried microparticles measured 21.5 μm with a drug-loading content of 8.37%, and all formulations gelled below 34 °C at pH 6–7. The purpurin content of the microparticle-containing gels was adjusted so that P3, MP and P3MP delivered the same total purpurin dose of 3.0 mM, equivalent to 38.4 µg per 50 µL application. Purpurin release followed Korsmeyer–Peppas kinetics, lasting 9 days from the solution formulation (P3), 16 days from microparticles (MP) and 11 days from the combination (P3MP), the free and encapsulated molecules producing a two-stage release profile. Purpurin inhibited Porphyromonas gingivalis with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 20 µM and a minimum bactericidal concentration of 50 µM, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages and, as P3 or P3MP, reduced viable counts in a human saliva-derived multispecies biofilm by approximately 2 log. In rat ligature-induced periodontitis under a repeated daily-dosing regimen, every treatment reduced cemento-enamel junction to alveolar bone crest distance relative to untreated disease, bone mineral density was raised only by P3MP, and gingival Il1b, Il6 and Spp1 were downregulated and Il10 upregulated in the two microparticle-containing formulations.
Article.TopicFields: Dentistry > Periodontics > Oral microbiology and periodontitis research; Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics > Pharmaceutical Science > Advanced Drug Delivery Systems; Dentistry > Periodontics > Periodontal Regeneration and Treatments

Article.Title: Layer-by-layer antibacterial coating encompassing silver nanoparticles for infection-resistant BioHole buttonHole device
Article.Authors: Wouters M.; Van Moll L.; Vandecasteele F.; Bendimouan Z.; De Vooght L.; Van Campenhout L.; Cos P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most patients in nephrology units require hemodialysis three times per week. Among the available vascular access techniques, the buttonhole method offers distinct advantages, including improved patient comfort and consistent cannulation. However, its clinical adoption remains constrained by a markedly increased risk of access-related infections. In this study, we present a novel and biocompatible coating strategy for the BioHole buttonhole medical device based on in-house produced silver nanoparticles. These particles were uniform, nanosized and had a narrow size distribution, exhibiting strong and reproducible antibacterial activity. Following mild aqueous amination of the BioHole device surface, a layer-by-layer assembly was applied to deposit a polyelectrolyte multilayer composed of cationic poly-L-lysine and anionic citrate- or citrate/tannic acid-capped silver nanoparticles. The coating demonstrated a strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , while maintaining excellent biocompatibility with L-929 fibroblasts. Overall, this technique provides a versatile strategy for developing antimicrobial surfaces on polycarbonate-based medical devices and establishes a preliminary proof of concept for further research into infection-resistant BioHole devices for buttonhole cannulation.

Article.Title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals novel stem cell markers for corneal limbal epithelium homeostasis
Article.Authors: Zhou Q.; Guaiquil V.; Zappia M.; Chang J.; Tang G.; Oyarzun M.; Cho M.; Sarkar J.; Wang X.; Frolov M.; Benevolenskaya E.; Rosenblatt M.
Article.Abstract: Sox9 is a well-established marker of skin epithelial hair follicle stem cells and has been observed in the corneal limbus of Sox9-EGFP transgenic mice. Using Sox9-EGFP as a reference marker, this study characterized the transcriptomic atlas of corneal limbal epithelial cells during homeostasis and identified novel markers of limbal stem cells (LSCs) by single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). A total of 20,351 viable cells were profiled, revealing 13 distinct cell clusters with unique molecular signatures. The cluster enriched with EGFP-positive cells was identified as the putative LSCs population during corneal epithelial homeostasis. Comparative analysis of corneal LSCs and early differentiated cells revealed several differentially expressed genes (DEGs) strongly associated with stemness-related pathways, including Gabrp , Fmo1 , Fmo2 , and Alcam , which were identified as potential novel LSC markers. Among these DEGs, Gabrp , and Alcam were exclusively expressed in the limbus, as confirmed by quantitative PCR (qPCR), Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. This study delineated the heterogeneous cellular composition of the limbal epithelium and uncovered several novel candidate markers that may be critical for maintaining corneal epithelial homeostasis.

Article.Title: Structural insight into dynamic switching mechanism o​f the SAM-IV riboswitch revealed by molecular simulations
Article.Authors: Uppuladinne M.; Korrapati N.; Sonavane U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-responsive riboswitches regulate essential metabolic pathways in many bacteria and represent attractive structured-RNA targets for chemical modulation. Among these, the SAM-IV riboswitch remains comparatively less explored at the level of ligand-dependent conformational dynamics despite the availability of apo and SAM-bound cryo-EM structures. Here, we investigated four structural states of the SAM-IV riboswitch—6UES-Apo, 6UET-bound, 6UES-Docked and 6UET-NoLig—using two independent 4 µs molecular dynamics simulations for each system, providing an aggregate sampling time of 32 µs. Structural stability, regional flexibility, hydrogen-bond persistence, clustering, combined principal component analysis, free-energy landscape mapping, dynamic cross-correlation analysis, pairwise residue-contact analysis, MM-GBSA calculations and ensemble docking were integrated to compare the conformational ensembles sampled in the presence and absence of SAM. Across the replicate simulations, the SAM-bound state generally displayed a comparatively restricted ensemble and lower local fluctuations, whereas ligand removal was associated with broader structural variability and redistribution of tertiary contacts. Ensemble docking further showed that several conformations sampled by the apo and ligand-removed trajectories remained capable of accommodating SAM; however, docking-score differences were interpreted qualitatively and native-pose agreement was evaluated by ligand RMSD because empirical scoring functions have limited energetic resolution. MM-GBSA calculations likewise indicated more favorable SAM stabilization in the experimentally resolved bound state than in the apo-derived docked state. Together, the results support an ensemble-based model in which ligand occupancy is associated with stabilization of a subset of SAM-IV conformations, while ligand removal permits broader conformational sampling. The proposed switching interpretation remains a simulation-derived mechanistic hypothesis that will require experimental and kinetic validation.

Article.Title: Multidimensional cognitive assessment of preservice middle school mathematics teachers’ proportional reasoning skills
Article.Authors: Avcu R.; Arıcan M.; Kaya T.
Article.Abstract: Proportional reasoning is a crucial yet challenging skill for preservice middle school mathematics teachers (PSTs) to develop. This study investigates PSTs’ mastery of three critical skills (attributes) underlying proportional reasoning: understanding ratios, understanding proportions, and understanding nonproportional relationships, as well as their difficulties with problems involving these skills. We designed a diagnostic test with 45 items (31 multiple-choice and 14 open-ended) and administered it to 747 PSTs from six public universities across Türkiye. We applied the Hierarchical Diagnostic Classification Model (HDCM) to analyze the PSTs’ responses to the diagnostic test. The results showed that nearly one-fifth of the PSTs had not mastered any attribute, while only about one-third had mastered all three attributes of proportional reasoning. Moreover, they found it particularly challenging to compare numerically complex ratios, use ratios to measure different real-world attributes, and distinguish between problems requiring additive and multiplicative reasoning. The implications for improving PSTs’ proportional reasoning skills are discussed.

Article.Title: Nitrogen fertilisation reveals contrasting nitrogen-use efficiency and greenhouse gas emission intensity responses in linseed and oilseed rape
Article.Authors: Walthall C.; Girkin N.; Kevei Z.; Warner H.; Johnston A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Break crops vary in nitrogen (N) demand, yet direct comparisons of their nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity are limited. We compared four linseed ( Linum usitatissimum ) genotypes with one oilseed rape (OSR; Brassica napus ) genotype in a controlled glasshouse experiment across four N fertiliser rates (0–120 kg N ha − 1 ). Plant growth traits, NUE, daily and cumulative GHG fluxes (N 2 O, CO 2 , CH 4 ) and emission intensity (kg CO 2 e kg − 1 biomass) were quantified. OSR produced greater biomass, chlorophyll content, and NUE than linseed at all N rates. Absolute GHG emissions rose more steeply with increasing fertiliser in OSR. Consequently, CO 2 e emission intensity increased with N rate in linseed but decreased in OSR, consistent with biomass dilution. Fertiliser rate was the dominant driver of GHG fluxes; crop type had no independent effect on cumulative emissions once N rate was accounted for. Genotypic variation within linseed was negligible compared with crop- and fertiliser-driven effects. These results highlight a yield-emission trade-off: OSR maximises productivity but requires careful N management to control emissions while linseed maintains lower emission intensity under reduced N inputs. Linseed offers potential as a lower-intensity break crop in diversified, low-N rotations. Further field-scale evaluation needed to support agricultural decarbonisation.

Article.Title: Zein–zinc oxide nanofibrous coating containing a cumin essential oil pickering emulsion: effects on the quality of Kurdish cheese during refrigerated storage
Article.Authors: Javidi Pezhman I.; Sani A.; Mahdian E.; Hakimzadeh V.
Article.Abstract: Kurdish cheese is a traditional dairy product whose microbial and physicochemical quality may change during refrigerated storage. This study evaluated electrospun zein/zinc oxide nanoparticle (ZnO-NP) nanofibers (NFs) prepared with a cumin essential oil (CEO) Pickering emulsion (PE). The selected PE (1.00% w/v ZnO-NPs; 0.50% v/v CEO) showed a droplet size of 210 ± 12 nm, zeta potential of − 34.8 ± 1.5 mV, and day-30 creaming index of 3.5 ± 0.8%. The final NFs contained 0.280 ± 0.030 mg CEO/g and released 61.8 ± 4.5% of measured initial CEO loading after 48 h in aqueous buffer at 25 °C. After 21 days at 4 °C, the PE-containing coating was associated with total viable and yeast/mold counts 2.30 and 2.80 log CFU/g lower, respectively, than in uncoated cheese. Coliform counts differed by only 0.30 log CFU/g and the control comparison was not statistically significant. Coated cheese also showed less acidification and higher measured moisture than the control. The findings indicate formulation-dependent quality differences in Kurdish cheese, but do not establish antimicrobial synergy, a validated shelf-life extension, or the safety of direct food contact; these require additional studies.

Article.Title: Comparing AMMI and REML/BLUP approaches for grain yield stability in bread wheat
Article.Authors: Amini A.; Asadi A.; Pirahani A.; Chaichi M.; Alaa M.; -Ahmadi M.; Kalkhoran M.; Ghadiri A.; Bay S.; Salehi P.; Monirifar H.
Article.Abstract: Genotype × environment interaction (GEI) is a major source of variation in multi-environment trials (METs) and complicates the identification of wheat genotypes with high yield and stable yield across diverse environments. Although the Additive Main Effects and Multiplicative Interaction (AMMI) model is widely used to investigate GEI, its interpretation may be limited when the first interaction principal components explain only a small proportion of the total interaction variance. This study compared the conventional AMMI model with a Restricted Maximum Likelihood/Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (REML/BLUP) approach for evaluating grain yield stability and adaptability of bread wheat genotypes grown under irrigated conditions in the cold regions of Iran. Twenty bread wheat genotypes were evaluated across nine locations during two growing seasons (18 environments) using a randomized complete block design with three replications. Combined analysis of variance, AMMI analysis, and mixed-model analyses were performed, and stability was assessed using conventional AMMI statistics together with the WAASB and WAASBY indices. Environmental effects, genotype × environment interaction, and genotype effects were all significant (P < 0.01), with the environment accounting for 61.3% of the total variation, followed by GEI (18.4%) and genotype (2.9%). The first two AMMI interaction principal components explained 47.3% of the total interaction variance, indicating that a substantial proportion of GEI remained in higher-order components. Consequently, BLUP-based stability statistics, which incorporate all significant interaction principal components, provided a more comprehensive assessment of genotype yield than conventional AMMI biplots. Among the evaluated genotypes G9, G3, G15 and G18 consistently combined high grain yield with broader adaptation and stable yield across environments. Overall, the integration of AMMI and REML/BLUP improved genotype discrimination and provided a framework for selecting superior wheat genotypes in multi-environment trials.

Article.Title: Experimental and numerical analysis of damage, stability, and seepage in underground anti-scour walls
Article.Authors: Wang K.; Zhang M.; Yao N.; Huang D.; Tang K.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the damage evolution and seepage control performance of underground anti-scour walls under complex hydraulic environments, concrete damage tests were conducted to elucidate the damage deterioration process. Subsequently, a numerical model of the anti-scour wall construction was established to analyze its structural stability and anti-seepage effectiveness under varying degrees of concrete damage and different water levels. The results indicate that the presence of prefabricated cracks reduces the peak strength of the specimens by 40% to 70% compared to intact specimens, and the degree of deterioration exhibits anisotropy. The established damage constitutive model effectively describes the complete stress-strain process of fissured concrete. Numerical simulations reveal that the anti-scour wall effectively blocks the horizontal seepage path of groundwater, forcing water to flow around it. This creates a hydraulic head difference between the inner and outer sides of the wall, demonstrating its excellent seepage control capability. Further analysis shows that even under extreme conditions involving elevated flood levels and wall damage, the H-shaped anti-scour wall effectively inhibits pore pressure transmission without experiencing seepage instability, proving its substantial structural safety redundancy.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Dam Engineering and Safety; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Geotechnical Engineering and Underground Structures; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Geotechnical Engineering and Soil Stabilization

Article.Title: Transcriptional responses of white-tailed deer to SARS-CoV-2 challenge
Article.Authors: Petry B.; Boggiatto P.; Buckley A.; Davila K.; Palmer M.; Putz E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract White-tailed deer are susceptible hosts for SARS-CoV-2, exhibiting robust viral replication, active shedding, efficient deer-to-deer transmission, and widespread natural infection across the United States. However, the molecular level host responses remain poorly defined. In this study, we describe whole blood transcriptomes from experimentally infected deer and compare their responses with other previously published wildlife hosts such as elk and bison, to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying infection. Over time, deer exhibited a regulated antiviral response, with rapid activation of innate immune pathways and Coronavirus Pathogenesis signaling as early as day 2 post infection (pi), followed by prevalent transcriptomic remodeling and inhibition of cytokine storm associated pathways at day 5 pi, and a reduction in differential expression by day 7 pi. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis highlighted early induction of interferon associated networks and hypercytokinemia related signaling. Comparative analysis with elk and bison revealed 22 conserved upregulated genes at day 2 pi, including antiviral regulators such as ADAR and STAT1 . At day 5 pi, a mere five downregulated genes and 20 upregulated genes remained conserved between the species, highlighting a lack of shared molecular responses across species, in line with divergent infection susceptibilities. Together, these findings define the temporal architecture of the deer immune response and identify conserved host defense mechanisms serving as molecular markers of SARS-CoV-2 infection in wildlife.

Article.Title: Even Jacobi-Fourier phase in intraocular lens for presbyopia correction
Article.Authors: Cvarch B.; Acosta E.; Arines J.; Amador E.; Bog M.; Kim H.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: An intraocular lens (IOL) was designed with an even Jacobi-Fourier phase (JFP) for the purpose of producing an extended range of object vergences over which there is little change in image quality. Evaluations of the IOL inside a Liou Brennan model eye were done with polychromatic light and tested entrance pupil diameters ranging from 2.5 mm to 5.0 mm. The metrics used to evaluate the IOL’s performance included Optical Transfer Function (OTF), simulated Visual Acuity (sVA) based on area under OTF (aOTF), the appearance of simulated Sloan letters, and Hilbert Space Angle (HSA). Excepting HSA, these metrics were all used to determine the range of object vergences over which the image quality is acceptable (logMAR ≤ 0.2). All pupil sizes were shown to have a range that was greater than 1.5D, and for pupils ≤ 4.0 mm, this increased to at least 2D. The HSA results were used to show that image quality remains remarkably steady within this range. Also, preliminary dysphotopsia simulations indicated that the IOL performed acceptably. Lastly, as an experimental proof of concept, a JFP plate was fabricated and used to photograph letter charts at different object vergences. The experimental findings demonstrate that JFP can be successfully applied in a defocus-resistant imaging system.

Article.Title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance patterns of Salmonella enterica serotypes in dairy products from Central Oromia, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Bedassa H.; Sisay T.; Zewdu W.
Article.Abstract: Salmonella in dairy products poses a global public health threat, yet serotype data remain limited in Ethiopia, hindering surveillance and intervention. This study examined prevalence, serotype distribution, and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella enterica in dairy products from Central Oromia, Ethiopia, based on secondary analysis of archived isolates; of the 71 isolates, 41 (57.7%) were from raw milk, 24 (33.8%) from pasteurized milk, and 6 (8.5%) from cottage cheese. PCR-confirmed S. enterica isolates from raw and pasteurized cow milk and cottage cheese were serotyped and tested against 12 antibiotics via disk diffusion; 62 (87.3%) were serotyped, while nine (12.7%) were untyped. Salmonella Heidelberg predominated (35.2%), followed by Salmonella Enteritidis (28.2%) and Salmonella Typhimurium (23.9%). Raw milk (36.6%) and cottage cheese (33.3%) showed highest contamination; pasteurized milk had lowest prevalence (25%). Resistance was high to ampicillin (60.6%) and tetracycline (59.2%), with resistance to trimethoprim (25.4%) and ciprofloxacin (15.5%). High susceptibility occurred with cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, and aztreonam. Multidrug resistance was detected in 48.4% of serotyped isolates, commonly ampicillin–tetracycline–ciprofloxacin and ampicillin–tetracycline–trimethoprim–ciprofloxacin. These findings highlight public health risks from Salmonella contamination and antimicrobial resistance in Ethiopian dairy, emphasizing improved hygiene, prudent antimicrobial use, and regular monitoring.

Article.Title: An integrated multimodal neural network framework for early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment combining genomic, neuroimaging, and behavioral modalities
Article.Authors: Cui Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the field of biomedical informatics and the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, the swift and precise detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and its early stage, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), presents a considerable obstacle in precision medicine. Traditional diagnostic techniques generally rely on singular data sources, thus failing to adequately capture the complex biological and behavioral interrelations that influence disease advancement. This study presents a novel multimodal deep learning architecture designed to amalgamate genetic information, neuroimaging techniques, and behavioral assessments to improve early detection proficiency. The suggested framework consists of three simultaneous analytical pathways: a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) designed for the extraction of morphological characteristics from MRI data, a densely interconnected neural network focused on the analysis of genetic variants, and a non-diagnostic longitudinal assessment of behavioral trajectories and cognitive measurements. To efficiently integrate these diverse data streams, an attention-driven adaptive modality gating mechanism is utilized, which dynamically adjusts the impact of each modality. Validation employing harmonized multimodal data from ADNI and UK Biobank demonstrates that the integrated multimodal model exceeds unimodal alternatives regarding predictive efficacy and resilience. Furthermore, the modality gating mechanism provides comprehensible results by pinpointing significant multimodal biomarkers that signify early stages of Alzheimer’s disease. This framework collectively highlights the potential of integrative multimodal data fusion techniques in improving early diagnostic accuracy and enabling personalized risk assessment for Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Psychiatry and Mental health > Dementia and Cognitive Impairment Research; Neuroscience > Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience > Alzheimer's disease research and treatments; Health Professions > Health Information Management > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

Article.Title: Mechanical and microstructural behavior of ASTM A588 weathering steel following a prolonged bridge fire
Article.Authors: Sajid H.; Slein R.
Article.Abstract: Assessing the residual capacity of fire-damaged structural steel is critical for guiding rehabilitation decisions, as prolonged fire exposure and subsequent fire extinguishing can degrade mechanical properties of steel. However, realistic fire-induced mechanical degradation data remain limited, particularly for weathering grades of structural steels. This study investigates the post-fire mechanical, microstructural, and surface patina behavior of ASTM A588 weathering steel using specimens from a VT-14 bridge steel that suffered severe deformation during a 36-h vehicular fire involving an overturned propane semi-trailer. To assess the ASTM A588 uncoated weathering steel’s post-fire behavior, the following series of tests were conducted: metrology of the deformation fields, mechanical testing (uniaxial tension, impact toughness, and hardness), chemical analysis of the patina, and metallographic evaluations. Post-fire mechanical testing revealed up to a 22% reduction in yield strength within the zone of maximum thermal exposure, relative to steel extracted from an unaffected, ambient-temperature baseline region of the same bridge girder, alongside a minor reduction in tensile strength (by 10%) and an increase in ductility (by 8%). The macrohardness and microhardness of the fire-damaged steel reduced by 9% and 18%, respectively, correlating with the yield strength reduction. Impact toughness experienced nominal changes across the girder regions and remained well above AASHTO limits. Microstructural results indicated that the metallurgical phase composition remained consistent, though experienced coarsening in ferrite grain and pearlite colony sizes dictated by the fire's thermal history and cooling rate. Direct fire exposure partially transformed the patina’s goethite to magnetite and hematite and increased the protective layer thickness by approximately eightfold, introducing new considerations for long-term durability. Despite some mechanical degradation and altered patina morphology, the steel largely retained its material-level viability, suggesting that localized repair could be pursued for the fire-affected steel, provided that global deformations and site constraints permit.

Article.Title: Treatment patterns and clinical outcomes in hospitalized adults with discordant Clostridioides difficile results: a multihospital cohort study
Article.Authors: Tsai S.; Noble O.; Pasupuleti P.; Paez-Mayorga J.; Fan C.; Alsafadi M.
Article.Abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a common gastrointestinal infection in hospitalized patients. A two-step testing algorithm comprised of a nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) followed by a specific toxin assay may be used to improve diagnostic accuracy of infection testing. Discordant results (NAAT+/Toxin-), however, create clinical uncertainty regarding the administration of CDI antimicrobial therapy. The purpose of this retrospective cohort study was to identify predictors of adverse clinical outcomes, including administration of CDI antimicrobial therapy as a primary predictor of interest, and evaluate treatment patterns among hospitalized adults with discordant C. difficile test results. This study included hospitalized adults with discordant (NAAT+/Toxin-) C. difficile test results between December 2023 and June 2025 across a nine-hospital tertiary-care health system. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint of 30-day all-cause mortality and colectomy attributable to C. difficile. Secondary outcomes included receipt of CDI antimicrobial therapy and 30-day all-cause readmission to an acute-care facility. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with clinical outcomes and antimicrobial therapy. Among 1,256 patients with discordant C. difficile testing, the primary composite outcome occurred in 59 (5%) patients. Factors associated with the primary outcome included older age (65–99 years; odds ratio (OR) 2.95, [1.53–6.20], p < 0.01), immunocompromised status within 30 days prior to the discordant test (OR 2.08, [1.10–4.15], p = 0.03), white blood cell counts ≥ 15,000 cells/µL (OR 1.86, [1.05–3.26], p = 0.03), and intensive care unit (ICU) status at the time of the C. difficile discordant test (OR 3.49, [1.91–6.29], p < 0.01). Overall, 879 (70%) patients received antimicrobial therapy; in exploratory analyses, ICU status was associated with treatment receipt (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.02–2.24). Thirty-day readmission was associated with immunocompromised status (OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.25–2.26), elevated creatinine levels (OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.12–1.96), and higher comorbidity index (OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.34–3.14), and older age was associated with lower odds of readmission (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57–0.99). Patient-level clinical characteristics and markers of acute illness, rather than discordant CDI test results alone, are more strongly associated with short-term clinical outcomes. CDI antimicrobial therapy was not independently associated with the primary composite outcome among patients with discordant C. difficile test results after adjustment for measured confounders. Future studies are needed to determine whether specific groups of patients with discordant results benefit from treatment.

Article.Title: Workplace ergonomics, self-reported musculoskeletal symptoms and sedentary behaviour among desk-based office employees in Islamabad, Pakistan: a cross-sectional survey of employees and human resources officers with an embedded qualitative component
Article.Authors: Rehman U.; Ashraf M.; Ajaib S.; Ahmed A.; Sana S.
Article.Abstract: Poor workplace ergonomics is a growing yet under-investigated occupational health concern in Pakistan’s expanding corporate sector. This study estimated the prevalence of self-reported musculoskeletal symptoms; described perceived workplace ergonomic conditions and sedentary behaviour among desk-based employees in Islamabad; examined their correlates; and documented organisational ergonomic practices as reported by human resources (HR) officers. A cross-sectional survey with an embedded qualitative (free-text) component was conducted in Islamabad between 2024 and 2025 among a purposive sample of 251 respondents: 179 desk-based office employees and 72 HR officers. Employees and HR officers were recruited independently and could not be linked to one another at the organisational level, so the two strands are reported as complementary perspectives and never as a paired organisational comparison. Two distinct instruments were used. The employee instrument, informed by the item content of the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ) and the Rapid Office Strain Assessment (ROSA) checklist, captured self-reported symptoms, workstation characteristics and sedentary patterns; neither tool was administered as a scored assessment. The HR instrument captured organisation-level ergonomic policy and practice. The two instruments shared no items in common, so the two groups are reported separately and not pooled. Qualitative data came from open-ended items embedded in the employee survey; we conducted no in-depth interviews. Analyses in SPSS version 21 comprised frequencies with 95% confidence intervals, chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. We conducted inductive thematic analysis of open-ended responses, integrating themes through a joint display. Associations are cross-sectional and are reported as adjusted odds ratios; they describe associations, not prediction or causation. Among the 179 employees, 124 (69.3%) had never received ergonomic training, although 156 (87.2%) believed ergonomic improvement would reduce workplace fatigue. An adjustable chair supporting the back was available to 106 (59.2%) and a screen at eye level to 120 (67.0%). At least one musculoskeletal symptom was reported by 127 (70.9%, 95% CI 64.3–77.6), and 102 (57.0%) reported symptoms at two or more body sites. Back pain was the most prevalent single symptom (100, 55.9%), followed by shoulder discomfort (98, 54.7%), eye strain or headaches (92, 51.4%), neck discomfort (90, 50.3%) and wrist pain (70, 39.1%). Persistent pain developing over time was reported by 84 (46.9%), and 62 (34.6%) had sought medical treatment. Sixty-eight employees (38.0%) sat for seven hours or more daily, and 53 (29.6%) rarely took movement breaks. A screen positioned at eye level was independently associated with lower odds of neck discomfort (adjusted OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.15–0.70), shoulder discomfort (0.33, 95% CI 0.15–0.73), and back pain (0.32, 95% CI 0.15–0.69). Female employees reported substantially higher symptom prevalence than male employees at every site (any symptom 86.6% versus 61.6%; adjusted OR for male sex 0.22, 95% CI 0.09–0.53). Among HR officers, 44 (61.1%) reported a formal ergonomics policy; only 24 (33.3%) reported that their organisation provided ergonomic training; 25 (34.7%) tracked discomfort reports; and 44 (61.1%) allocated under 5% of the budget to ergonomic improvements. Thematic analysis identified five organisational barriers: budgetary constraints, managerial knowledge gaps, organisational inertia, spatial limitations and reluctance to raise complaints. Self-reported musculoskeletal symptoms were common among desk-based employees in this Islamabad sample, and basic ergonomic provisions and training were frequently absent. Screen height was the workstation characteristic most consistently associated with symptoms, and female employees carried a markedly higher symptom burden. HR officers commonly reported formal ergonomic policies, while employees commonly reported a lack of training and monitoring; because the two respondent groups were not linked at the organisational level, these are complementary perspectives on ergonomic provision and do not demonstrate organisation-level discordance. Workstation review, ergonomic training and accessible reporting channels are plausible low-cost priorities; prospective and intervention studies are required to establish causation and effectiveness.

Article.Title: Exploring relationships between attitudes toward reducing mental illness stigma and help-seeking on a major Taiwanese online discussion forum: a machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Lien Y.; Feng H.; Koh J.; Chen C.; Cian S.; Huang H.
Article.Abstract: Mental health literacy is critical to improving timely access to mental health care, but persistent stigma and negative attitudes toward seeking help remain significant barriers. Social media platforms offer real-time insights into how users express such attitudes and behaviors. This study examined the associations of stigma-reduction attitudes and help-seeking attitudes with subsequently reported help-seeking behaviors. We analyzed 1,506,333 posts from eight mental health–related boards on PTT, a Taiwanese online forum, from January 2018 to January 2024. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) models trained on manually annotated posts scored stigma reduction attitudes, help-seeking attitudes, and help-seeking behaviors (help-seeking behavior detection: F1 = 0.84, accuracy = 0.87; attitude scoring: macro-F1 = 0.67–0.78, accuracy = 0.87–0.93). Logistic regression was used to examine associations between user-level attitude scores derived from posts within a 3-month observation window and subsequent help-seeking behavior. Each one-point increase in stigma reduction attitudes was associated with 1.33-fold higher odds of subsequent help-seeking, whereas continuous help-seeking attitudes were not significant. In dichotomized analyses, stronger stigma reduction and more positive help-seeking attitudes had 1.66- and 1.72-fold higher odds, respectively, although the latter warrants caution. These findings inform culturally sensitive strategies to enhance mental health service utilization.

Article.Title: Species-agnostic tools for Influenza A H5 antibody and NP antigen detection in dairy cows, chickens, and humans
Article.Authors: Ahlers L.; Sammons N.; Lane B.; Wang Y.; Dzantiev L.; Mathew A.; Abraham J.; Shittu I.; Marushchak L.; Gray G.; Harrington W.; Kercher L.; Kandeil A.; Wohlstadter J.; Sigal G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza (HPAI) A (H5N1) circulates in wild birds, causing outbreaks in domestic poultry, but recently became enzootic in the United States spilling over into various mammals, including cattle. The zoonotic potential of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b emphasizes the need for tools for surveillance in mammalian and avian species. We developed two species-agnostic assays using the Meso Scale Discovery (MSD) platform to enhance current surveillance methods: a sandwich immunoassay for influenza A nucleoprotein (NP) antigen, and a bridging serology assay for influenza A/H5 specific antibodies. We assessed the assays by testing milk and serum from cattle herds experiencing H5N1 incursions, serum from H5N1-vaccinated humans and chickens, and negative control samples from cattle, chickens, and humans. Antibodies and antigen were detected in milk and serum from H5-exposed cattle herds, but not in samples from putatively naïve herds. The number of identified exposed animals increased by combining antigen and antibody testing. The bridging serology assay accurately differentiated serum from H5-vaccinated chickens and humans, relative to H5-naïve controls. Blocking with H1 hemagglutinin improved discrimination between H5-vaccinated and presumed-negative human samples by reducing potential cross-reactivity. The studies demonstrate the applicability of these methods to diverse species and facilitate their use in surveillance studies.

Article.Title: Dynamic tracking of N2O and CO2 associated with Fusarium and soil using mid-IR QCL sensing
Article.Authors: Yumoto M.; Kawata Y.; Miyajima S.; Ono Y.; Matsuyama T.; Wada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, nitrous oxide (N 2 O), a major greenhouse gas predominantly emitted from agricultural soils via microbial activity, was investigated using a real-time detection approach. Real-time monitoring of microbially derived N 2 O is crucial for elucidating soil microbial dynamics and visualizing soil ecosystem conditions. A simultaneous N 2 O and CO 2 detection system was developed by integrating a mid-infrared quantum cascade laser operating at ~ 4.47 μm with a multipass gas cell (MGC). Detection limits of 12 ppb and 66 ppm were obtained for N 2 O and CO 2 , respectively. By maintaining the MGC at low internal pressure throughout gas sampling and measurement, continuous-flow monitoring of N 2 O and CO 2 concentrations in gases released from Fusarium oxysporum and agricultural soil (leaf mold) was successfully conducted. This system enabled, for the first time, real-time observation of dynamic fluctuations in N 2 O and CO 2 concentrations in response to environmental changes. These results provide enhanced visualization of microbially derived N 2 O concentration changes and offer valuable insights for advancing analyses of microbial N 2 O dynamics.

Article.Title: Circulating Resolvin D1 and Resolvin E1 and carotid atherosclerotic burden in type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Uyanık T.; Demir C.; Çınar M.; Ersoy G.; Kocatürk İ.; Şenol Ç.; Reis B.; Küçüksayan H.; Gülten S.; Taşkıran Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Failure to resolve inflammation may contribute to accelerated atherosclerosis in type 2 diabetes. We investigated whether circulating Resolvin D1 (RvD1) and Resolvin E1 (RvE1), measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), are associated with carotid atherosclerotic burden and improve discrimination of prevalent carotid stenosis beyond carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT). In this single-center cross-sectional study, 139 adults with type 2 diabetes underwent carotid ultrasonography and serum resolvin measurement. The prespecified primary endpoint, ≥ 50% carotid stenosis, was present in 59 participants (42.4%). After adjustment for prespecified confounders, the association of ELISA-immunoreactive RvD1 with the primary endpoint was not statistically significant (prevalence ratio per 1-SD increment 0.72, 95% CI 0.49–1.03; p = 0.074). In exploratory secondary analyses, each 1-SD higher ELISA-immunoreactive RvD1 was associated with an adjusted 6.92%-point lower maximum stenosis (95% CI 2.79–11.05; p = 0.001) and with lower cIMT; ELISA-immunoreactive RvD1 also differed across plaque phenotypes in unadjusted comparisons ( p < 0.001), although phenotype overlapped with stenosis severity. Adding ELISA-immunoreactive RvD1 to the clinical model with cIMT increased the C-statistic by 0.010 (bootstrap 95% CI − 0.003 to 0.038). ELISA-immunoreactive RvE1 showed no statistically significant adjusted association with stenosis, cIMT, or plaque presence. These exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation with validated mass spectrometric measurements.

Article.Title: Multi-label bridge damage segmentation with topology supervision and conformal calibration
Article.Authors: Rafiei S.; Dabouri Farimani G.; Yusufbay Y.; Kamol K.; Kenjayev S.; Sayfiddinov D.; Sodikova N.
Article.Abstract: Reliable automated bridge inspection requires accurate masks, preservation of defect geometry, and uncertainty estimates. This study combines a pretrained ViT-S/16 encoder, a rank-48 residual adapter, progressive decoding, dual-view appearance regularization, boundary and clDice supervision, and label-conditional conformal calibration. DACL10K v2 supplies 19 non-exclusive channels: 13 damage and six component/object classes. Group-disjoint subdivision of its 6935 training images yielded 5202 training, 693 calibration, and 1040 locked internal-test images; 975 official validation images supported model selection and ablation. Native-image evaluation on the internal test yielded Macro-IoU 0.758, Macro-Dice 0.861, Micro-IoU 0.817, and Boundary F1 0.792. ECE was 0.016 and the Brier score was 0.094. Five-seed validation ablation yielded Macro-IoU 0.803 ± 0.003 for the full model. Seventeen controlled perturbations identified haze and occlusion as major failure conditions; stronger compound corruptions reduced positive-label conformal coverage to 0.793–0.849. Matched five-seed retraining gave Macro-IoU 0.757 ± 0.003 for Full and 0.766 ± 0.004 for Mask2Former/Swin-T, showing no overlap superiority of the proposed backbone. These results support a joint internal assessment of overlap, geometry, and uncertainty. External-domain transfer and field robustness remain unvalidated.
