Article.Title: Source-dependent patterns in microbial communities and resistance-associated features of PE-associated biofilms in laboratory wastewater influent microcosms
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Li W.; Lei Y.; Hu H.; Zhuang Z.; Gao X.; Wang Z.; Liu X.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Plastic-associated biofilms formed from wastewater influent provide a laboratory microcosm model for investigating wastewater-associated plastisphere communities. However, it remains unclear whether they broadly enrich resistance-related features or instead show source-dependent patterns in wastewater-derived microbial and functional features. Here, we analyzed source-matched polyethylene (PE)-biofilm samples and PE-free water-phase controls established in separate microcosms from raw influent wastewater collected from four wastewater treatment plants using 16 S rRNA gene sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and 16 S-normalized qPCR targeting selected antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic element (MGE) markers. Bacterial communities in PE-associated biofilm samples differed from those in source-matched PE-free control microcosms, with the magnitude and direction of differences varying among wastewater sources. Several taxa showed higher representation in PE-associated biofilm samples, whereas Shannon diversity values overlapped and showed no consistent difference across the four source-matched comparisons. At the annotation level, ARG-associated features showed source-dependent compositional differences, some source-matched comparisons showed relatively higher signals for multidrug, disinfectant/biocide, and efflux-related categories. Targeted quantitative PCR further showed a marker-specific pattern: tet(39) and floR exhibited higher 16 S-normalized abundances in PE biofilms, whereas the Integrall-derived marker Int02 showed no consistent PE-associated enrichment. MGE-associated profiles were likewise source and marker dependent. Assembly-level analysis further identified a limited subset of predicted plasmid contigs carrying both high-confidence ARGs and candidate mobility-related ORFs; however, these sequence contexts were source- and sample-dependent and were not consistently associated with PE. Integrated module analysis further revealed that pathogen- and virulence-related, resistance, and MGE-marker annotations formed distinct source-specific profiles rather than a single coordinated pattern of enrichment on PE. These findings indicate that ARG-associated abundance did not show a consistent increase across the four source-matched PE–water comparisons. Instead, they showed source-dependent, particle-associated differences in bacterial communities, resistomes, MGE-marker profiles, and pathogen- and virulence-related features. These observations suggest that characterization of wastewater plastisphere-associated resistance should consider not only ARG abundance but also the multidomain organization of microbial, resistance, MGE-marker, and virulence-associated traits, while these source-dependent patterns require validation in independently replicated experiments that include non-plastic particle controls and same-flask water-phase sampling.

Article.Title: Changing seasonality and trends of other infectious diarrhea and norovirus across the pandemic era in Shenzhen China
Article.Authors: Cheng Y.; Xiong H.; Chen Z.; Ren J.; Liu T.; Zhang J.; Deng Y.; Su Y.; wen Y.; Lu Y.; Song L.; Ci R.; Wang H.; Zhang Y.; Zhang J.; Lv Z.; Yao X.; Du C.; Li Y.; Hu Q.; Lv Q.; Zhang Z.; Zou X.
Article.Abstract: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is a heterogeneous surveillance syndrome whose temporal patterns may change with transmission, pathogen composition, care seeking and reporting. We analyzed 578,222 OID reports from Shenzhen, China, from 1 January 2013 to 31 July 2025, together with monthly norovirus GI-positive, GII-positive and mixed GI + GII-positive series. Calendar-month distributions differed across pre-COVID-19, during COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 periods for all four series. Autocorrelation-aware breakpoint profiling with adjustment for temperature, relative humidity and wet-day frequency favored February 2020, whereas independent-error profiling favored January 2022. In the primary climate-adjusted ARMA(2,0) model, OID reports fell 48.1% at February 2020, then increased by 2.15% per month. The slope change was 1.13% per month, with a confidence interval spanning zero. A January 2022 sensitivity model estimated a positive post-break trend of 3.28% per month, but its slope change also included zero. A three-segment model found no additional acceleration in January 2022 relative to 2020–2021. Available meteorological covariates did not explain the positive later trend. These findings support changing surveillance dynamics across the COVID-19 era, but not a unique or causal 2022 acceleration.

Article.Title: Function, activity and participation limitations in patients with post-COVID condition: a multicenter analysis from two prospective German cohorts
Article.Authors: Nürnberger C.; Steinmetz A.; Appel K.; Balzuweit B.; Bahmer T.; Kraus T.; Krawczak M.; Polidori M.; Neumann C.; Bröhl I.; Butzmann J.; Dahl E.; Dashti H.; Deckert J.; Fiedler K.; Frank S.; Hanses F.; Heuschmann P.; Pütz S.; Illig T.; Jensen B.; Kobbe R.; Koehler P.; Raquib S.; Reese J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Based on the WHO definition of post-COVID condition (PCC), its symptoms can cause limitations in activity and participation of daily living. However, studies investigating this association are rare. This study aims to examine relevant activity and participation impairments in PCC patients as well as determinants for said impairments using established cohort studies in Germany. Data from patients included in the two inpatient cohorts of the National Pandemic Cohort Network (NAPKON) were used. Within the two cohorts, patients from 32 hospitals were included and evaluated at 3 and 12 months follow up (3MFU, 12MFU) after baseline examination. The previously developed PCC score (PCCS) was used for measuring PCC severity. To assess activity and participation impairment, the PROMIS-29 domain ‘ability to participate in social roles and activities’ was used. Defined other deficits in different areas of life were assessed by defined PROMIS domains. Overall, 655 patients with available information on PCCS and PROMIS at 3MFU and 374 patients at 12MFU were included between 2020 and 2023 , of whom 76% and 70% had at least a mild PCC, respectively. At 3MFU, 43% of patients with at least mild PCC had evidence for activity and participation impairment. 17% of these still had at least mild PCC and activity and participation impairments at 12MFU. They further had significantly lower quality of life, higher PCCS and more comorbidities than patients without PCC at 3 and 12 MFU (3MFU/12MFU: p<.001/p<.001, p<.001/p<.001, p=.004/p=.025, respectively). ​Even when multiple symptoms are present, PCC is not always associated with limitations in activity and participation. As such restrictions are important for rehabilitation planning, further studies should specifically address the risk of PCC patients to develop an impairment in activity and participation. Trail registration: The NAPKON SUEP is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT04768998). The NAPKON HAP is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT04747366).

Article.Title: A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-attention model optimized by an improved sparrow search algorithm for identity authentication and anomaly detection in electricity markets
Article.Authors: Yang C.; Hu Y.; Tan Z.; Huang K.; Xu K.
Article.Abstract: Conventional rule-based and signature-based approaches struggle to identify sophisticated cyber threats in increasingly digitalized electricity markets, such as identity spoofing, replay attacks, and data tampering, while existing deep learning models often suffer from suboptimal hyperparameter configurations and limited feature representation capability. This work proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a convolutional neural network, bidirectional long short-term memory, and an attention mechanism for identity authentication in electricity market environments. A bimodal feature engineering scheme is constructed by combining user behavioral characteristics with network traffic statistics, providing complementary information for attack discrimination. To address the sensitivity of deep models to hyperparameter selection, an improved sparrow search algorithm is developed, which incorporates Tent chaotic mapping for population initialization, an adaptive inertia weight for balancing exploration and exploitation, and a Cauchy-Gaussian hybrid perturbation strategy for escaping local optima. Experimental evaluations are conducted on the NSL-KDD and CICIDS2017 benchmarks together with a simulated electricity market dataset built on the IEEE 30-bus test system. On the simulated electricity market dataset, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 98.71% and an F1 score of 98.43%; averaged across the three datasets it attains 98.31% accuracy, consistently outperforming representative baselines including bidirectional long short-term memory, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, convolutional neural network, and long short-term memory. Ablation studies confirm the individual contribution of each component, and robustness analyses show stable performance under the simulated noise levels and attack ratios considered.

Article.Title: Coherent state sampling for molecular vibronic spectra
Article.Authors: Konyshev I.; Pradip R.; Page O.; Ünlüer C.; Nasibullin R.; Sundholm D.; Pernice W.; Ferrari S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electronic spectroscopy is today among the most powerful methods for studying chemical systems, and state-resolved (line-assigned) simulations are essential for attributing spectral features to specific vibrational excitations. The standard time-independent sum-over-states (SOS) route provides line assignments; while effective with truncation and prescreening, it can become computationally demanding as the number of modes increases. Vibronic boson sampling (VBS) offers an event-based alternative, but scaling photonic implementations remains challenging and the required vibronic inputs can be demanding for larger systems. Here we introduce coherent-state sampling (CSS), a sampling scheme for the Linear Coupling Model (LCM), where vibrational modes are independent. This enables a photonic architecture based on a single reconfigurable optical channel with essentially fixed hardware complexity; increasing system size is handled by additional measurement iterations rather than additional optical modes. Using pentacene as a test case, we demonstrate an end-to-end workflow—electronic-structure input, sampling strategy, hardware validation, and comparison to experiment—showing that both a laptop implementation and a superconducting-detector photonic implementation reproduce reference spectra with high fidelity and yield band shapes in good agreement with experiment. While not targeting quantum advantage, CSS provides a practically scalable, state-resolved tool for LCM vibronic spectroscopy and a controlled displacement-dominated complement to more general VBS schemes.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: pentacene; line assignment; vibronic spectra; superconducting detectors; photonic quantum computing

Article.Title: Genomic epidemiology of a colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii outbreak in a South African tertiary hospital
Article.Authors: Adelabu O.; Skosana Z.; Dube S.; Glover E.; Potgieter S.; Wadula J.; Musoke J.
Article.Abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is a critical-priority healthcare-associated pathogen associated with extensive multidrug resistance. Outbreaks of colistin- and carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii in oncology populations pose profound clinical and infection control challenges, severely restricting remaining last-line therapeutic options. Despite this growing threat, genomic characterization of colistin-resistant outbreaks within these specialized cancer care environments remains highly limited in South Africa. A retrospective, single-centre outbreak investigation was conducted at Universitas Academic Hospital, Free State, South Africa, between 18 and 31 July 2025. Four colistin- and carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii isolates recovered from patients in a specialised haematology ward were identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption ionisation time of flight (MALDI-TOF) Mass spectrometry, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) performed on the automated VITEK ® 2 system. Colistin resistance was confirmed by broth microdilution (BMD) in accordance with clinical and laboratory standards institute (CLSI) guidelines. Subsequently, all four isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing (WGS) using an Illumina MiSeq platform. Genomic analyses included de novo assembly, resistome and virulome profiling, pan-genome analysis, plasmid replicon screening, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), and core-genome single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based maximum-likelihood phylogenetic reconstruction. All four isolates were assigned to sequence type 2 (ST2), consistent with international clone 2, and formed a single terminal phylogenetic clade. Pairwise core-genome SNP distances ranged from 2 to 13 before recombination filtering and 0 to 4 after filtering. Carbapenem resistance was universally mediated by co-carriage of bla NDM-1 and bla OXA-23 alongside the intrinsic bla OXA-69. The isolates carried nucleotide variants in the lipid A biosynthesis-associated genes lpxA , lpxC , and lpxD . However, the functional contribution of these variants to colistin resistance was not established. A conserved virulome encompassing biofilm formation, Type IV pili, Type VI secretion system components, and acinetobactin iron acquisition was identified across all isolates. The pan-genome comprised 3,904 gene clusters, with a core genome of 3,886 genes. Our study describes a clonal outbreak of extensively drug-resistant ST2 A. baumannii harbouring convergent colistin and carbapenem resistance mechanisms in a tertiary hospital ward, underscoring the urgent need for genomic surveillance and strengthened infection prevention and control strategies in high-risk clinical settings.

Article.Title: Peripheral neuropathy among HIV patients on antiretroviral therapy at Kayunga Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda
Article.Authors: Hassan Adan A.; Jeyte M.; Amon B.; Mukisa R.; Dubad Abdi F.; Kassahun Bekele H.; Ali Hassan A.; Farah Ismail M.; Hakizimana T.; Ali Araye F.; Mohamud Hirsi A.
Article.Abstract: HIV/AIDS remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa. Peripheral neuropathy is a common complication among people living with HIV, contributing to disability, reduced quality of life, and increased economic burden. This hospital-based cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence, disability patterns, and factors associated with peripheral neuropathy among HIV patients on antiretroviral therapy at Kayunga Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda. We enrolled 384 participants aged ≥ 18 years on ART. Peripheral neuropathy was diagnosed using the Clinical HIV Associated Neuropathy Tool (at least one symptom and one sign). Disability was assessed using the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0). Logistic regression was performed to identify associated factors. The prevalence of peripheral neuropathy was 23.4% (90/384, 95% CI 19.5–27.3%). Among participants with neuropathy, mobility and self-care were the domains most affected (78.9% each). Independent factors associated with neuropathy included: age > 60 years (aOR = 2.963, 95% CI 1.730–5.427), poor ART adherence (aOR = 4.576, 95% CI 2.110–10.694), HIV duration > 10 years (aOR = 1.906, 95% CI 1.115–3.723), underweight (aOR = 2.138, 95% CI 1.412–5.788), overweight/obese (aOR = 3.333, 95% CI 1.669–6.767), unsuppressed viral load (aOR = 2.134, 95% CI 1.258–4.105), and low CD4 count (aOR = 2.641, 95% CI 1.184–5.890). Peripheral neuropathy is common among HIV patients on ART in Uganda, with significant associated disability. Routine screening should be integrated into HIV care, with targeted assessment for high-risk patients.

Article.Title: Grandparent-grandchild relationship quality and adolescent sexual risk-taking: the moderating role of socioeconomic status
Article.Authors: Kamal S.; Mozaffar A.; Basakha M.
Article.Abstract: Adolescent sexual risk-taking is a pressing public health concern shaped by family and socioeconomic conditions. This study explored whether supportive relationships between grandparents and grandchildren protect Iranian adolescents from sexual risk behaviors, and whether this protective role varies by socioeconomic status (SES). A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 640 adolescents aged 15–20 years in Malekan, Iran. Participants completed validated questionnaires on grandparental relationship quality, SES, and sexual risk behaviors. Analyses included correlation, regression, and moderation tests while controlling for demographic and behavioral factors. Results showed that closer grandparent–grandchild relationships were associated with reduced sexual risk-taking, with the strongest protective effect observed among adolescents from low-SES backgrounds. The association weakened in medium-SES groups and was negligible in high-SES groups. Additionally, female gender, urban residence, private schooling, and other risk behaviors increased vulnerability. Findings highlight the cultural and protective role of grandparents, particularly for socioeconomically disadvantaged youth.

Article.Title: Dual-layer directional hydraulic fracturing for pressure relief of thick hard key strata in a deep longwall top-coal caving face: mechanism and field validation
Article.Authors: Cao X.; Chen X.; Yun M.; Shi K.; Yan T.; Fan Z.; Liu B.; Liu M.; Jia G.; Ren J.
Article.Abstract: Thick hard roofs in deep longwall top-coal caving faces can develop large suspended spans, leading to stress concentration and strong dynamic loading during sudden failure. This study investigates the pressure-relief mechanism and field performance of dual-layer directional hydraulic fracturing at the 4301 working face of Jianxin Coal Mine. In-situ stress measurements, key-stratum analysis, UDEC simulations, and multi-source field monitoring were integrated to identify critical roof strata, optimize fracturing horizons, and evaluate the resulting mechanical response. The maximum horizontal principal stress ranged from 18.82 to 20.87 MPa, with a predominantly northeast orientation. A 13.8 m-thick coarse sandstone layer, with a calculated fracture span of 24.8 m, was identified as the principal key stratum. Based on mechanical analysis and field geological investigations, a dual-layer staged hydraulic fracturing scheme using underground directional long boreholes was developed to target sandstone horizons approximately 20 and 44 m above the coal-seam roof. UDEC simulations showed that fracturing promoted earlier roof movement, expanded the displacement and stress-relief zones, and facilitated a transition from continuous load bearing and delayed failure to segmented failure and progressive stress redistribution. Field monitoring provided complementary evidence of these predicted trends. Comparisons between the selected pre- and post-fracturing monitoring periods showed that the recorded microseismic event number and cumulative energy were 12.4% and 11.6% lower, respectively, in the post-fracturing period. Considering the differences in mining stages, these changes are interpreted as supplementary evidence of the post-fracturing response rather than effects attributable solely to hydraulic fracturing. Deep and shallow roof separations remained within approximately 30 and 20 mm, respectively, while bolt-and-cable loads increased without pronounced abrupt surges. These findings indicate that coordinated weakening of near-field and high-level key strata reduces roof structural continuity and effective spanning capacity, providing a practical basis for pressure-relief design and evaluation under similar deep mining conditions.

Article.Title: An age calculator for high-latitude Quaternary foraminifera using amino acid racemization
Article.Authors: Kaufman D.; Hunt S.; Smith J.; Bright J.; Hillenbrand C.; Klages J.; McKay N.; O’Regan M.; Risebrobakken B.; West G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dating deep-sea cores from polar regions is challenging because sedimentation rates can be variable and oxygen-isotope stratigraphy can be ineffective, making amino acid racemization an important alternative. We calibrated the rate of racemization in Neogloboquadrina pachyderma , the dominant high-latitude planktic foraminifer, using 140 independently dated samples from 21 Arctic, Nordic Seas, North Atlantic, and Southern Ocean sites spanning 2 ka to 1.4 Ma. Racemization rates among these ocean basins differ less than among individual sites. Ages are based on aspartic acid, a more precise chronometer than glutamic acid, which, however, provides an independent check on the analysis. A publicly available age calculator returns formal uncertainty intervals incorporating calibration and measurement errors. Ages carry a realistic uncertainty of roughly ± 32% (66% level), insufficient to assign a sample to a specific Marine Isotope Stage but still useful for many polar marine sediment cores. A single age picks correctly between two candidate ages 90% of the time when they differ by a factor of 2.3 (e.g., 100 versus 230 ka). An independently dated horizon in the same core can reduce the uncertainty to ± 28%. Because comparisons are more precise than absolute ages, amino acid geochronology is best applied as a down-core series.

Article.Title: Effect of posterior longitudinal ligament resection on biomechanical characteristics in cervical disc arthroplasty: a finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Sang D.; Lu K.; Ding G.; Ren W.; Wu H.; Du C.; Sang H.; Zhou F.
Article.Abstract: The posterior longitudinal ligament (PLL) plays a critical role in maintaining the biomechanical integrity. However, the biomechanical impact of PLL resection on the cervical spine remains a subject of debate. This study aimed to use finite element analysis (FEA) to determine the effects of PLL resection versus preservation on the biomechanics after cervical disc arthroplasty (CDA). A validated finite element model of the cervical spine (C3-C7) was developed based on computed tomography data from a patient with mild degenerative changes at C5-C6. At this level, a CDA model was constructed and implanted with three cervical disc prostheses (Bryan, Mobi-C, and Prodisc-C). For each prosthesis, both PLL-preserved and PLL-resected surgical models were established. Two distinct mechanical loading protocols were applied, namely identical axial preload with 1.0 Nm moment and displacement loading. The analyzed parameters encompassed range of motion (ROM), intervertebral disc stress (IDS), facet joint stress (FJS), bone-implant interface stress (BIS), prosthesis stress (PS). Compared with the preoperative condition, ROM increased at the operative segment (C5-C6) following all three disc replacements, indicating increased segmental ROM. Regarding the comparison between PLL resection and preservation, the majority of biomechanical parameters remained largely unchanged. However, a few notable exceptions were observed. Among them, the Bryan artificial disc exhibited the most pronounced change, with a 10.08% reduction in BIS during extension following PLL resection. The Prodisc-C demonstrated the greatest variation at the operative segment (C5-C6), where PS increased by 6.77% during extension while BIS decreased by approximately 3.5% during lateral bending, while changes during flexion (− 0.41%) and rotation (− 0.16%) were negligible. Aside from these isolated instances, all other parameter changes between PLL resection and preservation were minimal, generally remaining below 1%. Under the simulated quasi-static loading conditions, resection of the PLL during CDA did not meaningfully alter postoperative biomechanical outcomes. ROM at the operative segment was consistently increased regardless of the prosthesis type or PLL management strategy, and the few parameter variations observed between resection and preservation were minor under the simulated conditions. These findings suggest that biomechanical considerations alone need not drive the decision to resect the PLL; rather, the decision should be individualized based on the need for adequate decompression and patient-specific pathology.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Surgery > Cervical and Thoracic Myelopathy; Medicine > Orthopedics and Sports Medicine > Spine and Intervertebral Disc Pathology; Medicine > Surgery > Spinal Fractures and Fixation Techniques

Article.Title: Machine learning analysis of serum ATR-FTIR spectra for colorectal cancer discrimination
Article.Authors: Spagnolo D.; Picciariello A.; Pesole P.; Donghia R.; Ancona A.; Grassi I.; Vincenti L.; Giannelli G.; Giglio M.; Brunetti A.; Bevilacqua V.; Zifarelli A.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, highlighting the need for complementary minimally invasive approaches able to support early CRC detection. This study investigated serum attenuated total reflection Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning analysis for discriminating CRC cases from non-cancer controls. ATR-FTIR spectra were acquired from dried serum samples of 100 CRC cases and 100 non-cancer controls and analyzed in the fingerprint and high-wavenumber spectral regions. Second-derivative spectra were used to enhance spectral resolution and to perform variable importance in projection analysis, which guided the selection of discriminant spectral regions before classification. The most relevant variables were mainly assigned to protein-related vibrations, phosphate-containing biomolecules, and carbohydrate-associated molecular structures. A PCA–ANN classifier was developed to reduce spectral dimensionality while preserving model parsimony. In internal validation, the model achieved 87.5% accuracy, 90.0% sensitivity, 85.0% specificity, and an AUC of 0.941. Preliminary evaluation on an independent external dataset of 28 subjects yielded 85.7% accuracy and an AUC of 0.920. These findings support the feasibility of serum ATR-FTIR fingerprints combined with interpretable machine learning for CRC/control discrimination, although larger prospective and demographically balanced external cohorts are required to assess its potential utility for CRC early detection.

Article.Title: A prediction–optimization–decision framework for logistics network design under demand and disruption uncertainty
Article.Authors: Zhao T.; Chen G.; He N.; Phoophiwfa T.; Li L.; Gu Y.; Busababodhin P.
Article.Abstract: Aiming at the problem of the separation of logistics network design prediction and optimization under the double uncertainty of dynamic demand and disruption risk, this paper proposes a prediction-optimization-decision integration framework with deep integration of machine learning and system optimization. The framework adopts a three-layer architecture: the prediction layer constructs a hybrid model combining spatial-temporal graph neural network and multi-head attention mechanism and uses deep ensembles and quantile regression to quantify epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. The risk layer identifies disruption risks through attention-based multi-label classification and deep support vector data description and generates a representative risk scenario set combining multi-layer network propagation model and importance sampling. The optimization layer establishes a multi-period mixed integer programming model and introduces resilience service level constraints and conditional value-at-risk measurement to realize the synergy between cost and resilience. In order to solve large-scale problems, a learning-enhanced large-scale neighborhood search algorithm is designed, and reinforcement learning agents are embedded in the operator selection process. The experimental results show that the MAE of the proposed prediction model is reduced by 8.2% to 15.6% compared with Transformer in each step. The average F1 of risk classification reached 0.847, 6.2% higher than that of XGBoost. The total cost of the optimization algorithm is 13.4% lower than that of stochastic programming on large-scale instances, and the optimality gap reaches 0.8% within 600 s. The total cost of the framework in 12 months decreased by 16.9%, the service level improved by 5.6% points, and the interruption recovery time shortened by 62%.

Article.Title: Photocrosslinked gelatin hydrogel-mediated IGF-1 delivery promotes early cartilage-like tissue formation in a rabbit auricular defect model
Article.Authors: Kushibiki T.; Mayumi Y.; Nakayama E.; Yamashiro T.; Azuma R.; Ishihara M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Auricular cartilage has a limited capacity for self-repair. Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) promotes chondrocyte proliferation and extracellular matrix synthesis; however, its therapeutic efficacy is constrained by rapid diffusion and a short in vivo half-life. In this study, we investigated whether IGF-1 delivered in a previously developed visible-light photocrosslinked gelatin hydrogel could promote cartilage repair. In a mouse subcutaneous model, ex vivo fluorescence imaging over 14 days showed that the hydrogel prolonged the local retention of fluorescently labeled IGF-1 compared with IGF-1 solution. In a rabbit auricular-cartilage defect model, defects were treated with saline, IGF-1 solution, hydrogel alone, or IGF-1-loaded hydrogel ( n = 5 per group) and evaluated 1 month later. The IGF-1-loaded hydrogel group formed cartilage-like tissue with rounded cells within lacunae, proteoglycan-rich matrix, and type-II collagen, which occupied 83.8% of the defect length compared with 6.4% in the hydrogel-only group. This group also showed higher COL2A1 , ACAN , SOX9 , and COL1A1 expression, more Ki-67-positive cells, and increased peripheral angiogenesis, without calcification. IGF-1 delivery using photocrosslinked gelatin hydrogels, which prolonged local IGF-1 retention, is thus a promising strategy for promoting early cartilage-like tissue formation, although long-term maturation and mechanical function remain to be established.

Article.Title: Multimorbidity patterns, disease networks, and phenotype clusters in Vietnamese children
Article.Authors: Ho N.; Hermiston M.; Nguyen M.; Van Nguyen Q.; Dao A.; Tran C.; Nguyen P.; Nguyen Q.; Do C.; Pham A.
Article.Abstract: Multimorbidity in children remains poorly characterized in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), with no prior large-scale network-analytic study in Vietnam. We aimed to describe the prevalence, structure, and demographic determinants of pediatric multimorbidity using a population-level school health database. We analyzed 283,926 annual school health visits from 72,909 children aged 0 to 18 years attending a private school system in Vietnam (2020 to 2025). Multimorbidity was defined as ≥ 2 ICD-10 diagnoses per child. A six-layer multiplex network was constructed to identify disease hubs via betweenness centrality. Temporal trajectories were assessed with directed binomial tests, and multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios for comorbidity pairs. Association rules were extracted via Apriori and phenotype clusters were derived using Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) followed by Leiden community detection. Multimorbidity was present in 53.7% of children, with higher burden in males (55.7% vs. 51.5%) and the 6 to 11-year age group (65.7%). The strongest co-occurrences involved blindness/low vision with protein-energy malnutrition (OR 6.71) and hyperalimentation (OR 8.73), constituting a visual-nutritional double burden. Acute tonsillitis and dental caries emerged as the top universal disease hubs (hub scores 1.10 and 0.95, respectively). Hyperalimentation preceding obesity was the highest-risk temporal sequence (RR 2.45). Seven phenotype clusters were identified (multimorbidity prevalence 39.3% to 69.5%), with disorders of refraction and dental caries present across all groups. Multimorbidity is highly prevalent in this urban Vietnamese pediatric population. A nutritional-ophthalmological cluster and an upper airway-oral health cluster support integrated school-based screening and interventions in Vietnam and comparable LMICs.

Article.Title: Assessing model transferability to predict the state of battery health across independent datasets
Article.Authors: Seixas Leal A.; Deo R.; Prasad S.; de Castro Santos L.; Ali M.; Berton L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Data-driven battery prognostic models are usually evaluated within the dataset on which they were trained. This study evaluates the zero-shot transfer of six state of health forecasting models, from regularized linear regression to recurrent and attention-based networks, across three public lithium-ion datasets, together with uncertainty estimates and alarm policies. Dataset separability, measured by classifier AUC and maximum mean discrepancy, did not explain transfer error: the pair with the largest distributional distance included the easiest transfer. Error depended primarily on target domain characteristics rather than source-target separability. The most regularly degrading dataset (ZHU) exhibited the lowest transfer error for every model, supporting target degradation regularity as a leading hypothesis for cross-dataset predictability. At a 10-cycle horizon, however, a persistence forecast that assumes no change had the lowest average cross-dataset error; learned models outperformed it only marginally on a few transfers and were significantly worse on others. Monte Carlo Dropout reached nominal coverage in all but one scenario, but its intervals were often an order of magnitude wider than the forecast error, so a risk-aware alarm policy based on them warned earlier within a dataset yet alarmed almost continuously under transfer. Cross-dataset prognostic benchmarks should therefore report a persistence reference and target-domain predictability alongside model accuracy.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Automotive Engineering > Battery Modeling and Management; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advancements in Battery Materials; Engineering > Safety, Risk, Reliability and Quality > Reliability and Maintenance Optimization

Article.Title: Large language model surrogates for Bayesian optimization of antibody sequences
Article.Authors: Huh E.; Choi S.; Shin H.
Article.Abstract: Enhancing therapeutic antibody properties typically requires iterative sequence engineering and experimental validation, such as binding assays, making antibody optimization time-consuming and resource intensive. To address these challenges, we introduce AbL2BO, a Bayesian optimization (BO) framework integrating a large language model (LLM) with Bayesian fine-tuning. AbL2BO leverages prior knowledge embedded in an antibody-specific LLM and efficiently updates model parameters using Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with approximate inference, including the Laplace approximation or MC dropout. The fine-tuned LLM serves as a surrogate model within the BO framework. Our results show that AbL2BO achieves superior sample efficiency compared to conventional BO methods that rely on Gaussian process regression to model black-box functions. Across experimental and simulated benchmark datasets, AbL2BO consistently demonstrated competitive or superior optimization performance with better-calibrated uncertainty estimates than kernel-based BO approaches. Integrating LLMs into BO offers three key advantages: (1) warm-starting the optimization with pretrained knowledge; (2) easy adaptation to new domains; and (3) bypassing the complexities of kernel design choices, kernel computation, and sequence alignment to handle sequences of varying length. Overall, AbL2BO improves both optimization efficiency and uncertainty estimation, particularly for complex antibody sequence landscapes, with the potential to reduce time and resource requirements in therapeutic antibody development.
Article.TopicFields: Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Advanced Bandit Algorithms Research; Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Monoclonal and Polyclonal Antibodies Research; Computer Science > Computational Theory and Mathematics > Advanced Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithms

Article.Title: Digital proxy practices in Singapore compared with the United States
Article.Authors: Zakaria C.; Wu Y.; Phua A.; Pakianathan P.; Koh G.; Foong P.
Article.Abstract: While design and deployment of digital services are predicated on a model for independent and autonomous use, populations requiring caregiving support are increasingly relying on interdependent engagement to maintain personal care, including digital use. As a result, proxy-mediated access is no longer a peripheral workaround but a core component of daily navigation, requiring caregivers to act as digital proxies to manage online accounts on behalf of their care recipient. Yet, little is known about who these proxies are or how they gain access to digital accounts. This study surveyed 304 Singaporean adults to examine the prevalence, predictors, and methods of digital proxy behavior, revealing comparable motivations and use of informal access methods to those reported in the United States. Our cross-national comparison between two developed, aging nations, one Western and one Asian, highlights shared challenges and context-specific differences in digital caregiving. Despite high ‘Smart Nation’ maturity, our results reveal a strong trend of older adult digital proxies frequently relying on informal, unsecured methods of digital access. For both countries, the current ‘one-user, one-account’ paradigm creates a structural barrier to health and financial equity, compelling digital proxies to resort to informal workarounds that may compromise the delegators privacy and data integrity. Our findings provide actionable evidence for medical and financial service providers to design digital systems that accommodate socio-digital interdependence, specifically for those requiring caregiving support.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Geriatrics and Gerontology > Technology Use by Older Adults; Social Sciences > Life-span and Life-course Studies > Aging, Elder Care, and Social Issues; Social Sciences > Human Factors and Ergonomics > Digital Accessibility for Disabilities

Article.Title: Assessing the relationship between industrialization and CO2 emissions in Somalia
Article.Authors: Abdihamid M.; Sabrie H.; Mohamed M.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the relationship between industrialization and CO 2 emissions in Somalia via annual data from 1990–2024. The autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) approach is employed to investigate the short-run dynamics and long-run relationships among CO 2 emissions, industrialization, GDP per capita, primary energy consumption, population growth, and institutional quality. The bounds test confirms the existence of a long-run relationship among the variables. The results indicate that industrialization, GDP per capita, primary energy consumption, and institutional quality are positively and significantly associated with CO 2 emissions in the long run, whereas population growth is statistically insignificant. The error correction term is negative and significant, indicating that approximately 61.91% of deviations from long-run equilibrium are corrected within one period. Robustness checks via dynamic ordinary least squares and canonical cointegrating regression confirm the direction and statistical significance of the long-run relationships. These results highlight the importance of integrating cleaner energy, energy efficiency, and environmental considerations into Somalia’s industrial development strategies.

Article.Title: Exploring the potential of phygital bone as a synthetic surrogate for forensic bone trauma
Article.Authors: Rzymelka V.; Crespo-Santiago J.; Gesualdo M.; Álvarez A.; Andreu C.; Mallafré H.; Garrido X.; Schwab N.; Otero-Viñas M.; Galtés I.; Jordana X.
Article.Abstract: Mechanical trauma analysis is vital in forensic investigations to determine causes of death, yet current synthetic bone surrogates inadequately replicate human bone’s biomechanical and microstructural properties. Here we explore the potential of the Phygital Bone (PHyB) model, a 3D-printed synthetic femur reproducing human bone macro- and microarchitecture, against fresh human femora and commercial surrogates (SYNBONE, Sawbones) via compression, three-point bending, and gunshot trauma tests. PHyB matched human femora in compressive stiffness and maximum stress and shared specific fracture traits with human bone, while Sawbones better approximated bullet energy loss; no surrogate, including PHyB, was distinguishable from the others under three-point bending. These findings suggest PHyB offers a promising condition-dependent surrogate for forensic trauma reconstruction, though further validation across diverse loading conditions is needed before widespread forensic application.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: Sawbones; three-point bending; fracture patterns; compressive stiffness

Article.Title: Effect of growth hormone on euploid blastocyst rate in advanced-age women: a prospective, randomized, controlled trial
Article.Authors: Shunji Z.; Yi T.; Yangqin P.; Xiaoyi Y.; Yurong Z.; Change H.; Ruyi G.; Liqing L.; Qin N.; Ge L.; Fei G.
Article.Abstract: Older women exhibit an increased incidence of chromosomal abnormalities in preimplantation embryos. At present, it remains uncertain whether growth hormone (GH) administration can improve embryonic ploidy status in this population.This study aimed to investigate whether GH administration can improve the euploid blastocyst rate in older women undergoing preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A). This is a prospective, randomized, controlled trial.We included 316 advanced-age infertile women (≥ 35 years) undergoing PGT-A.Participants in the GH group received subcutaneous GH injection at a dose of 2 IU/day starting from the mid-luteal phase of the two menstrual cycles preceding the initiation of ovarian stimulation. Between the initiation of ovarian stimulation and the day of human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) trigger, GH was administered at an increased dose of 4 IU/day.The control group did not receive additional interventions. The primary endpoint was the euploid blastocyst rate which was calculated as follows: number of euploid blastocysts/total number of blastocysts × 100%. The number of euploid blastocysts per patient was 0.98 ± 0.99 in the GH group and 0.89 ± 0.99 in the control group ( P = 0.534; absolute difference [95% CI]: 0.00 [− 0.00, 0.00]). Further, there was no significant difference in the euploid blastocyst rate between the GH group (37.78% ± 36.77%) and the control group (31.55% ± 33.99%; P = 0.325; absolute difference [95% CI]: 0.01% [-0.00%, 16.67%]). Our findings indicated that GH supplementation did not significantly improve the euploid blastocyst rate in advanced-age women undergoing PGT-A. These findings suggest that routine GH co-treatment may not increase the euploid rate in this population. Trial registration: ChiCTR2100052433; http://www.chictr.org.cn , Oct 26, 2021.

Article.Title: Numerical investigation of rock damage characteristics during combined perforation-controllable shock wave fracturing
Article.Authors: Tang K.; Huang C.; Li B.; Ren G.; Yu L.; Zhao P.; Zhou J.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Controllable shock-wave fracturing combined with perforation offers a potential approach for unconventional reservoir stimulation, yet the effects of perforation configuration, in-situ stress, and shock-wave loading parameters on rock damage remain unclear. In this study, a three-dimensional finite element model incorporating wellbore and perforation cavities was established using the Holmquist-Johnson-Cook (HJC) constitutive model. The model was validated against large-scale shock-wave fracturing experiments, showing qualitative agreement with the experimentally observed acoustic emission event distribution. Rock damage was quantified in terms of effective damage volume and maximum damage radius. Compared with the non-perforation case, the 6-perforation configuration increased the maximum damage radius from 0.743 to 1.276 m, while the effective damage volume changed from 0.334 to 0.310 m 3 , indicating that perforations primarily promote directional damage extension rather than increase the overall damage volume. For 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 perforations, the effective damage volumes were 0.332, 0.305, 0.310, 0.300, and 0.290 m³, respectively, while the corresponding maximum damage radii were 0.956, 1.027, 1.276, 1.015, and 0.915 m. The effective damage volume exhibited an overall decreasing trend with increasing perforation number, whereas the maximum damage radius varied non-monotonically, reaching its highest value at six perforations. This behavior may be attributed to the combined effects of perforation orientation, stress distribution, and interactions between adjacent damage branches. Repeated shock-wave loading promoted cumulative damage, but increasing the pulse number from seven to nine produced negligible additional damage. Increasing the peak pressure from 200 to 240 MPa enlarged the effective damage volume from 0.310 to 0.411 m 3 , while the maximum damage radius remained nearly unchanged. Increasing the horizontal stress difference enhanced preferential damage propagation along the maximum horizontal principal stress direction. Furthermore, a lower-pressure, longer-duration loading mode produced greater damage volume and radial extension than a higher-pressure, shorter-duration mode. These findings suggest that perforation number and orientation should be selected according to the reservoir stress state and the desired balance between near-wellbore stimulation and far-field damage extension, while shock-wave peak pressure, pulse duration, and pulse number should be jointly adjusted to improve stimulation efficiency.
Article.TopicFields: Energy > Fuel Technology > Hydraulic Fracturing and Reservoir Analysis; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Rock Mechanics and Modeling; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Geotechnical and Geomechanical Engineering

Article.Title: A lightweight defect grading detection method for quick-frozen dumplings based on improved YOLOv11n
Article.Authors: Xiong D.; Wang Y.; Guo B.; Ma X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fine-grained defect grading and differentiated quality management of quick-frozen dumplings remain challenging in complex industrial environments. To support fine-grained quality evaluation, a defect grading dataset containing four quality levels (normal, minor defect, moderate defect, and severe defect) was constructed. Based on this dataset, a lightweight defect grading detection model, SCSL-YOLO, based on YOLOv11n is proposed. StarNet and the C3k2_Star module are introduced into the backbone network to enhance multi-scale feature representation. A cascaded group attention mechanism (C2CGA) is adopted in the feature fusion stage to improve feature discrimination under complex backgrounds. In addition, a lightweight shared detail-enhanced detection head (Detect_LSDECD) is designed by integrating detail-enhanced convolution and group normalization to improve bounding box prediction and fine-grained quality classification while reducing computational complexity. Experimental results show that SCSL-YOLO achieves superior detection accuracy and efficiency compared with YOLOv11n. Precision, recall, and mAP@0.5 reach 95.7%, 94.5%, and 98.6%, respectively. Compared with the baseline model, precision is improved by 2.4 percentage points, while recall and mAP@0.5 are increased by 1.3 percentage points and 0.5 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, the number of parameters, model size, and GFLOPs are reduced by 40.38%, 30.91%, and 25.40%, respectively, and the inference speed reaches 316.6 FPS. The proposed method achieves a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an effective solution for frozen dumpling defect grading detection and intelligent food quality inspection.
Article.Topic: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering > Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Smart Agriculture and AI

Article.Title: Multimodal emotion recognition and feedback adaptation for personalized music therapy
Article.Authors: Chen K.
Article.Abstract: Effective music therapy depends on dynamic matching among an individual’s emotional state, music emotion attributes, and intervention feedback. Existing intelligent music therapy studies have focused mainly on system implementation or recommendation performance, while paying insufficient attention to how emotion recognition informs therapeutic decision-making, how music features map onto regulation goals, and how user feedback revises subsequent interventions. Based on the valence-arousal emotion model, this study develops a personalized music therapy framework driven by multimodal emotion recognition. The framework maps the user’s current emotional state, target therapeutic state, and music emotion features into a unified space, and models the relationships among current-state congruence, target-state approach, user preference, and historical feedback through a therapeutic utility function. In implementation, a cross-modal Transformer is employed to fuse facial, speech, and physiological signals for user emotion representation; VGGish with dual-task learning is used to extract music valence and arousal features; and a hybrid strategy integrating content matching, collaborative filtering, and DQN-based feedback optimization is used to generate personalized music intervention plans. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieved 90.1% emotion-recognition accuracy and an F1 score of 89.6%. For music emotion prediction, the valence and arousal MAEs were 0.096 and 0.101, respectively, with a correlation coefficient of 0.861. The recommendation module achieved HR@10 and NDCG@10 values of 84.2% and 80.5%, respectively. In the short-term affective evaluation, the mean reduction in distance from the current state to the predefined target state was 0.214 for the proposed estimator, compared with 0.186 for Tensor Fusion. These results support the computational feasibility and adaptability of the framework, while not constituting evidence of clinical therapeutic efficacy.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Emotion and Mood Recognition; Psychology > Social Psychology > Music Therapy and Health; Computer Science > Signal Processing > Music and Audio Processing

Article.Title: LENS: localized updates facilitate patient-level unlearning in clinical large language models
Article.Authors: Kim M.; Han J.; Kim Y.; Park S.; Jun T.
Article.Abstract: Large language models fine-tuned on clinical records can reproduce patient information that a patient may ask to have removed. A deletion request applies only to the patient who made it, so outputs for other patients in the same fine-tuning data should remain unchanged. Unlearning studies typically check general medical knowledge but rarely examine these non-deleted patients. Restricting updates to a subset of model components has been reported to reduce side effects on untargeted knowledge, but its effect on non-deleted patients remains unclear. We propose layer-wise evidence-based neural suppression (LENS), which confines the unlearning update to a single four-layer window of the fine-tuning adapter. We fine-tuned MedGemma-4B-IT on MIMIC-III notes with synthetic patient names. After fine-tuning, ROUGE-L on deleted and non-deleted patients was 0.98–0.99, and a reference model trained without the deleted patients scored 0.33 on them. Existing methods that brought the deleted patients to this level (0.29–0.39) lowered the non-deleted patients to 0.47–0.69. LENS brought the deleted patients to 0.34 and kept the non-deleted patients at 0.90. External medical benchmark accuracy changed by less than 0.02 for every method and did not distinguish these outcomes. These results suggest that unlearning should also be evaluated on the non-deleted patients.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Medicine > Health Informatics > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Machine Learning in Healthcare

Article.Title: A novel framework for automated volume quantification of subretinal fluid in central serous chorioretinopathy
Article.Authors: Xu J.; Liu Y.; Shen J.; Xu J.; Tian S.; Yan Z.; Zhou F.
Article.Abstract: Conventional quantification approaches of subretinal fluid (SRF) not only necessitate time-consuming frame-by-frame processing but also struggle with accurate fluid segmentation within the initial and terminal segments of linear optical coherence tomography (OCT) B-scan images. Therefore, a novel radial scanning OCT image-driven framework consisting of three modules is proposed for SRF volume quantification. The contour extraction module facilitates the extraction of SRF contour information from individual B-scan images through image cropping, cross-sectional annotation, and edge detection. The three-dimensional reconstruction module unifies the spatial relationships of radial OCT B-scan images through spatial alignment, achieving structured representation of cross-sectional contours via contour point serialization and accomplishing SRF reconstruction through subsequent spatial mapping. The volume quantification module develops an adjacency relationship construction technique to compensate for missing data between adjacent scanning frames and, through microelement subdivision and discrete integration approximation, enables volume quantification of SRF. Besides, an interpolation strategy is further designed to explore the feasibility of accurate SRF volume quantification by the framework under sparse scanning conditions. The quantification results of the proposed framework are in close agreement with the gold standard. The absolute error (AE) metric reaches a minimum of 0.0011 mm 3 , while the relative error (RE) metric ranges from 0.16 to 7.82%, with the majority concentrated around 6% and the lowest value recorded as low as 0.16%. Moreover, with the interpolation strategy’s sampling factor set to 2, the framework achieves a minimum mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.30%. These extensive experiments demonstrate the significant advantage and competitive strength of the proposed framework for SRF volume quantification, while also suggesting that the interpolation strategy possesses substantial potential to maintain the framework’s quantification accuracy even with a limited number of radial OCT B-scan images.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging > Retinal Imaging and Analysis; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Medical Image Segmentation Techniques; Medicine > Ophthalmology > Retinal Diseases and Treatments

Article.Title: Acute psychological and neuroendocrine responses to a single whole-body cryotherapy session in an uncontrolled pilot study of healthy men
Article.Authors: Javidi E.; Gröninger J.; Wiltfang J.; Hristova D.; Wedekind D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) is established in rheumatology and sports medicine, but acute psychological and neuroendocrine responses to a single session in healthy individuals remain poorly characterised. In this prospective, non-randomised, uncontrolled, single-arm experimental pilot study, 52 healthy men underwent one WBC session (− 110 °C, 3 min); 50 were analysed (mean age 26.9 ± 6.9 years). Mood, concentration, and self-rated physical condition were rated on numerical rating scales (0–10) at baseline, shortly after WBC, and at 4 h; the Trail Making Test A and B were administered at the first two timepoints; and cortisol, testosterone, interleukin-6, creatine kinase and full blood count were measured pre- and post-session. All three subjective domains were significantly higher shortly after WBC (estimated increases: mood + 1.0, concentration + 0.9, self-rated physical condition + 1.1; all p < 0.001), with the physical-condition gain persisting at 4 h ( p = 0.0036). Shorter Trail Making Test times probably reflect practice. Cortisol was approximately 15% higher ( p = 0.0026; Wilcoxon p = 0.008, above the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold), creatine kinase rose modestly, and testosterone and haematological parameters were unchanged; interleukin-6 was largely undetectable. This uncontrolled design precludes causal inference; these hypothesis-generating findings may inform randomised controlled trials of WBC in psychiatric conditions.

Article.Title: Quantification and classification of carbon nanotubes in electron micrographs using vision foundation models
Article.Authors: Pradeep S.; Wang C.; Dahm M.; Eldredge J.; Tsai C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of carbon nanotube morphologies in electron microscopy images is vital for exposure assessment and toxicological studies, yet current workflows rely on slow, subjective manual segmentation. This work presents a unified framework that leverages vision foundation models to automate the quantification and classification of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) in electron microscopy images. First, an interactive quantification tool built on the Segment Anything Model segments particles with near-perfect accuracy using minimal user input. Second, a classification pipeline uses the resulting masks to spatially constrain a DINOv2 vision transformer, extracting features exclusively from particle regions while suppressing background noise. Evaluated on a dataset of approximately 1800 TEM images, the architecture achieves 89.5% cross-validated accuracy and 92.7% on a held-out test set in distinguishing four CNT morphologies, outperforming the previous baseline while using a fraction of the training data. Instance-level processing enables the framework to resolve mixed samples, correctly classifying distinct particle types co-existing within a single field of view. These results demonstrate that integrating zero-shot segmentation with self-supervised feature learning enables high-throughput, reproducible nanomaterial analysis, transforming a labor-intensive bottleneck into a scalable, data-driven process.

Article.Title: The evolution and transmission dynamics of H3N2 influenza virus identified in a respiratory disease outbreak in companion dogs in Alabama, USA
Article.Authors: Kazemian S.; Tamim S.; Neasham P.; Kanwar S.; Zhong K.; Chenoweth K.; Perkins A.; Criado M.; Walz P.; Wang C.; Trovao N.; Kyriakis C.
Article.Abstract: H3N2 Canine influenza virus (CIV)​, initially of avian origin, emerged in Asia around 2005–2007 and subsequently spread globally, reaching the USA in 2015. Despite initial containment efforts, H3N2 CIV re-emerged in several USA states in 2023. This study investigates the evolution and transmission dynamics of H3N2 CIV identified in companion dogs during an outbreak in Alabama, USA, between August and October 2022. We performed whole-genome sequencing on five H3N2 CIV isolates and conducted phylodynamic modeling, incorporating 100 global H3N2 CIV genomes per segment. Phylogenetic reconstruction showed the Alabama strains formed distinct, tightly clustered groups, suggesting recent common ancestry and localized evolution. Phylogeographic inference revealed discordant origins for different gene segments. The Hemagglutinin (HA), Matrix Protein (MP), Nucleoprotein (NP), Non-structural Protein (NS),​ and Polymerase Acidic (PA) genes traced ancestry to California strains, the Neuraminidase (NA) gene to Florida strains, and the Polymerase Basic1 (PB1) and Polymerase Basic2 (PB2) genes to Illinois strains. This genomic incongruence strongly indicates that the Alabama outbreak strain emerged through a reassortment event involving viruses from these three geographically distinct regions. The findings highlight reassortment as a mechanism driving H3N2 CIV evolution and spread, likely facilitated by the movement of infected dogs. Low vaccination coverage in dogs requires continued surveillance and shelter-focused vaccination to control CIV outbreaks and monitor adaptation.

Article.Title: A predictive and reinforcement learning-driven framework for adaptive cybersecurity training and behavioral risk mitigation
Article.Authors: Samoo M.; Syed D.; Almansour H.; Al Reshan M.; Alqhtani S.; Alsulami M.; Shaikh A.
Article.Abstract: Phishing attacks continue to become more sophisticated and employee behavior is still a major part of the organization’s cyber security strategy. This study introduces a behavior-aware framework to predict the phishing susceptibility through supervised learning, clustering (unsupervised learning techniques), and reinforcement learning and to provide the customized cybersecurity training. The framework was created based on an augmented dataset, which takes into account phishing simulation data along with Human Resource (HR) data, such as demographic, behavioral, and organizational attributes. The accuracy, F1 Score, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrix were used to assess the accuracy of the five ensemble learning algorithms (Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), Extra Trees (ET), LightGBM (LGBM) and soft Voting Ensemble). Among the baseline classifiers, ET outperforms as compared to other by achieving accuracy (80%), and F1-score (79%) with ROC-AUC (0.88) which was good for discriminative power over decision thresholds. To identify various behavioral personas of employee ‘s behaviour, K-Means clustering algorithm was applied. The optimal clustering solution was determined using silhouette analysis, which was followed by one-way ANOVA that revealed a significant difference in the groups’ phishing risk and their engagement and participation in training. These behavioral profiles create interpretable basis to create specific cybersecurity interventions. The framework is designed to build on these insights and uses Q-learning to adapt training approaches based on the user’s behavior response instead of using fixed training programs based on awareness. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first framework to integrate phishing susceptibility prediction, behavioral segmentation, and adaptive based reinforcement training within unified human-centered cybersecurity architecture.

Article.Title: Remimazolam–propofol combination versus standard-dose propofol-based sedation in elderly outpatients undergoing colonoscopy: a randomized, double-blind trial
Article.Authors: Ma S.; Gao X.; Guan J.; Gao W.; Lin J.; Chen L.; Chen S.; Pan X.
Article.Abstract: Older adults undergoing outpatient colonoscopy are susceptible to sedation-related hypotension. We compared remimazolam plus reduced-dose propofol with standard-dose propofol-based sedation. In this prospective, randomized, double-blind trial, 156 outpatients aged 65–80 years were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive remimazolam 0.1 mg/kg plus propofol 0.5 mg/kg or propofol 1.0 mg/kg. Both regimens included sufentanil 0.05 µg/kg. The primary outcome was intraoperative hypotension, defined as a ≥ 30% decrease in mean arterial pressure from baseline. In the intention-to-treat analysis using multiple imputation, the estimated incidence of hypotension was 26% in the combination group and 59% in the propofol group (risk ratio, 0.43; 95% confidence interval, 0.28–0.66; p < 0.001). Nonprimary analyses were exploratory, without adjustment for multiple comparisons. Among the prespecified secondary outcomes, median propofol consumption was 60 mg lower, and median recovery and discharge-readiness times were 4 and 5 min shorter, respectively, with the combination. Bradycardia and hypoxemia were numerically less frequent, whereas no between-group differences were observed in body movement or satisfaction. No adverse events requiring hospitalization or unblinding occurred. The combination regimen was associated with a lower incidence of intraoperative hypotension than standard-dose propofol-based sedation. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111696.

Article.Title: Assessing the interplay between yeast cell wall supplementation and oral Salmonella vaccines in poultry immunity
Article.Authors: Bobe E.; Maupin C.; Verhaeghe L.; Marquis V.; Pineau L.; Schulthess J.
Article.Abstract: Due to the increasing concerns over antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains, implementing alternative strategies has become crucial for poultry health. The use of Mannan-oligosaccharides (MOS) from Yeast cell wall (YCW), and the administration of oral vaccines, are strategies that can be leveraged to help reduce the incidence of Salmonella . When MOS enhances gut innate immunity, live attenuated Salmonella vaccines promote the development of a specific humoral response. However, studies have demonstrated the binding between MOS and Salmonella pathogenic strains, thereby raising questions about the effect of a YCW-supplemented diet on the live attenuated strains and the efficiency of these vaccines. Here, we show that despite this phenomenon, Salmonella vaccination is at least as effective among chickens fed with YCW as in the control group. No major differences were found in the circulating antibody titer, nor in the cytokines’ activation potential between the two groups. Furthermore, antigen-presenting cells’ class II major histocompatibility was overexpressed by 59.9%, and an increased frequency of 70.6% in mature B-cells among the treated animals was detected. Our results demonstrate that a YCW-supplemented diet has a time-specific but positive effect on the animal’s effective vaccine-induced protection. Therefore, even though binding between MOS and the vaccine may occur, it does not negatively impact the chicken’s immune protection.

Article.Title: Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles using complex polysaccharide-rich sulphated extract (CPSE) from Gracilaria tenuistipitata and its broad-spectrum antimicrobial and catalytic activity
Article.Authors: Nath R.; Raisa M.; Kona U.; Sarkar S.; Kabir S.; Jahan T.; Hossain T.; Mondal S.; Karim M.
Article.Abstract: The dual global crises of escalating antimicrobial resistance and the environmental hazards of chemical synthesis demand the creation of advanced nanomaterials through sustainable and precisely controlled methodologies. While “green” synthesis offers a promising alternative, it is often limited by a lack of control over key nanoparticle attributes such as crystallinity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that a complex polysaccharide-rich sulphated extract (CPSE) from the red alga G. tenuistipitata serves as an effective biofunctional reducing and stabilizing matrix, facilitating the controlled synthesis of silver nanoparticles with desirable physicochemical properties. This one-pot, hydrothermal strategy leverages the CPSE’s intrinsic chemical architecture to direct the synthesis of stable and, critically, crystalline Ag/AgCl NPs with sizes ranging from 61 to 94 nm. The formation and reduction of the NPs were confirmed through UV-visible spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and HRTEM. Furthermore, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and ¹H NMR analyses provided mechanistic insights, revealing the dual functionality of CPSE: its electron-rich groups facilitate the reduction of Ag⁺ ions, while the polysaccharide matrix simultaneously forms a stabilizing layer, imparting inherent biofunctionality to the nanoparticle surface. The resulting bio-functionalized Ag/AgCl NPs exhibit potent, broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against a panel of clinically relevant Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens. In addition, the synthesized Ag/AgCl NPs were employed as effective catalysts for the degradation of two representative dyes, methyl orange (MO) and methylene blue (MB), in aqueous systems. Their excellent catalytic performance was confirmed by UV-visible spectroscopy, which revealed a rapid and significant decrease in the absorbance maxima over a short period of time. Overall, this study demonstrates that marine biopolymers can serve as effective reducing and stabilizing matrices for the green synthesis of crystalline nanomaterials, offering a sustainable platform for developing materials with potential biomedical and environmental applications.

Article.Title: Exploring conjugation between Streptomyces as a tool to mobilize biosynthetic gene clusters
Article.Authors: Bahriichuk K.; Rudenko V.; Botserovska A.; Melnyk S.; Rebets Y.; Luzhetskyy A.; Ostash B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Streptomyces bacteria harbor conjugative plasmids and integrative conjugative elements that employ a unique mode of DNA transfer. It minimally requires a single FtsK-like motor protein, TraB, and a cis -acting sequence recognized by TraB, clt . Notably, clt -like sequences ( clc ) are also scattered over Streptomyces chromosomes, driving the co-transfer of their macrofragments along with the plasmid. This could be used to facilitate the exchange of genetic material between different streptomycete strains and even species, thus creating new opportunities for natural product discovery. Here we explored several possible avenues of use of conjugation in the context of the popular chassis strain Streptomyces albidoflavus J1074, such as plasmid and chromosomal marker mobilization, and ability to transfer across species. First, among several clc types being screened in silico, the one for TraB encoded by plasmid pIJ101 was the most abundant. Second, TraB-mediated transfer of replicative (pIJ101-based) plasmid occurred at a frequency of 10% of recipient spore titer. The efficiency of inheritance of the chromosomal marker, distant to the conjugative plasmid location within the genome, was about four orders of magnitude lower. The developed methods might be useful to produce novel J1074 genotypes. Finally, we show that the removal of native plasmid-encoded clt site and repressor gene korA led to further drop (down to 10 − 6 ) in conjugation efficiency, albeit did not abrogate it completely. Hence, the prospects of chromosomal clc sites for gene transfer across species deserve more attention. We discuss the challenges associated with this genetic system and possible avenues for improvement, in the context of ongoing chassis-centered natural product discovery endeavors.

Article.Title: Time-in-range correlation with the primary patency of diabetic femoropopliteal artery occlusion after endovascular therapy: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Chang H.; Li Y.; Qiang W.; Lin Y.; Chen Z.; Gao Y.; Guo H.; Yang L.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to assess the correlation between time in range (TIR) and the primary outcome of diabetic femoropopliteal artery occlusion (DFO) after endovascular therapy. In this prospective cohort study, 162 patients with DFO were divided into two groups according to their seven-point glucose profiles within 7 days: those with a TIR below 70% (TBS) and those with a TIR above 70% (TAS). The clinical and follow-up data were analyzed. The TIR value in TBS was lower than that in TAS (58.84 ± 7.72% vs. 78.34 ± 6.13%) and duration above the range (34.79 ± 8.39% vs. 15.92 ± 5.89%; P < 0.001) were greater in TBS group. The primary patency rate in TBS group was lower than that in TAS group at 12-month (71.67% vs. 88.54%, P = 0.006). The restenosis (28.33% vs. 11.46%; P = 0.007) and clinical-driven target lesion revascularization (23.33% vs. 8.33%; P = 0.009) were greater in TBS group. Severe calcification (hazard ratio (HR): 4.08, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.86–8.97; P < 0.001) and TIR (HR: 0.025, 95% CI: 0.001-0.70; P = 0.03) were confirmed to be independent risk factors for restenosis. Our results suggested that TIR > 70% was associated with greater primary patency after endovascular therapy, which might be a potential indicator of DFO revascularization.

Article.Title: Theoretical design and structure–property relationship of symmetric and asymmetric benzoheterocycle-based triphenylamine hole-transport materials for n–i–p perovskite solar cells
Article.Authors: Shabani S.; Ghadari R.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: The molecular design of hole-transport materials (HTMs) is critical to charge extraction in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, fourteen triphenylamine-based small molecules containing symmetric or asymmetric benzoheterocyclic acceptor cores with O, S, N, or Se atoms were investigated as potential HTMs for n–i–p MAPbI₃ devices using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations. Ground-state properties were calculated at the B3LYP/6-311G(d) level, while excited-state optical properties were evaluated using CAM-B3LYP/6-311G(d). The predicted absorption maxima span 313.43–460.73 nm, and the hole reorganization energies range from 0.136 to 0.270 eV. Among the investigated structures, the symmetric benzoselenadiazole derivative ( Se-Sym ) has the smallest uncorrected DFT HOMO–LUMO gap (2.27 eV) and the longest predicted absorption wavelength (460.73 nm). O-Asym exhibits the lowest hole reorganization energy (0.136 eV), whereas Py-Sym has the lowest adiabatic ionization potential (5.26 eV) and the most negative solvation free energy (− 0.57 eV) in dichloromethane. These results show that the heterocyclic core and molecular symmetry jointly influence the calculated properties. Se-Sym emerges as a candidate for further study; however, experimental measurements and device-level testing are required to establish its practical performance.

Article.Title: FedBISINDO: edge-based federated cross-domain sign language recognition on non-IID data
Article.Authors: Sampedro G.; Cheng Y.; Caballero A.; Putra M.; Karna N.; Fauzi M.
Article.Abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has accelerated the development of automatic sign language recognition (SLR) systems for inclusive communication. However, centralized architectures require continuous raw video transmission, resulting in substantial communication overhead and increased privacy risks. Although federated learning (FL) preserves data privacy, conventional FL approaches experience performance degradation under statistical non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions and cross-domain environmental variations. To address these limitations, FedBISINDO is proposed as a privacy-preserving cross-domain SLR framework. A hybrid edge pipeline integrating a YOLOv11-Pose spatial engine with a Convolutional Neural Network-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) sequential network is employed to extract lightweight joint-coordinate representations, while a trajectory-matching aggregation layer is incorporated to mitigate non-IID client drift. Based on distributed simulations using 8,010 augmented frames across 36 vocabulary classes under label-skew conditions ( \(\alpha = 0.5\) ), a validation accuracy of \(87.0 \pm 0.8\%\) and an F1-score of \(86.9 \pm 0.7\%\) were obtained. The proposed framework achieved absolute accuracy improvements of 13.4% compared with FedProx and 24.9% compared with standard FedAvg. In addition, on-device hardware profiling indicated that a compact model footprint of 110,564 parameters and a computational complexity of 0.003310 GFLOPs were maintained. On-device profiling across the 10 Raspberry Pi edge clients indicated a per-frame inference latency ranging from 12.81 to 23.65 ms, satisfying the real-time processing constraint ( \(T_{\text {inf}} < 33.33\) ms). These results indicate that the proposed framework can support real-time sign gesture translation on resource-constrained mobile edge devices.

Article.Title: Qualitative dynamics and a positivity-preserving implicit scheme for a reaction-diffusion rotavirus model with breastfeeding and vaccination
Article.Authors: Fadhal E.; Shahid N.; Samreen N.; Raza A.; Ahmed N.; Alfwzan W.
Article.Abstract: Rotavirus remains a leading cause of severe diarrhoea in children under five, and its spread depends on how long breastfeeding and vaccination protect a child and on how children move between neighbouring communities. We extend a breastfeeding–vaccination rotavirus model to a reaction–diffusion system and ask two practical questions: how much do vaccine coverage and the duration of vaccine protection reduce transmission, and how fast does a newly introduced strain spread in space? We first show that the model is well posed, that infection dies out when the basic reproduction number \(\mathcal {R}_0\) is below one, and that a unique endemic state exists and is locally stable when \(\mathcal {R}_0>1\) . We then construct a semi-implicit finite-difference scheme that keeps all compartments nonnegative for every time and space step, and prove that it is stable and convergent in the maximum norm without the usual restriction \(\Delta t\lesssim (\Delta x)^2\) . With parameters taken from the rotavirus literature and transmission calibrated so that 95% of children are infected before age five in the absence of vaccination, the model gives a pre-vaccination \(\mathcal {R}_0\) of 22.1, inside the range reported by published transmission models. Under these parameters, increasing infant vaccine coverage alone changes \(\mathcal {R}_0\) only slightly when protection wanes within months, whereas longer-lasting protection lowers it markedly; interrupting transmission would require a vaccine that reduces the risk of infection by about 96%. A new strain spreads as a travelling front whose speed agrees with the linear prediction \(2\sqrt{d\,(\iota +\tau +\gamma )(\mathcal {R}_0-1)}\) to within 0.2%. The code is openly available.
