Article.Title: System dynamics and deep learning driven optimization of new product development lifecycle a smart stage-gate decision engine architecture
Article.Authors: Faridnia R.; Zarei A.; Nikabadi M.; Ebrahimi S.
Article.Abstract: New Product Development (NPD) in the automotive sector combines technical, quality, cost, schedule, resource, supplier and regulatory variables that evolve through feedback and delay. This study presents a Smart Stage-Gate Decision Engine architecture that integrates data-driven structure learning, dynamic-state modelling, Deep Learning (DL), System Dynamics (SD), dynamic-programming/optimal-control concepts, and policy learning. The architecture is explicitly organized as :Data → Structure → State/Dynamics → Prediction → Optimization → Decision → Learning/Decision Memory. The computational release implements a temporal Transformer and an Actor–Critic policy learner over a fixed-seed synthetic benchmark of 3,000 program-state records, together with an executable nonlinear state transition, numerical Jacobian, Hamiltonian evaluation, finite-horizon Pontryagin reference solver and System-Dynamics-compatible trajectory simulation. The primary run uses a 70/15/15 train/validation/test split. The Transformer reached 0.8578 validation accuracy and 0.8644 held-out test accuracy against the synthetic decision kernel. Mean utility change was 0.03268 under the code-defined synthetic utility. These results demonstrate computational execution and reproducibility rather than industrial performance. The architecture therefore provides a testable methodological bridge between predictive learning, dynamic state analysis and gate decision support, while empirical calibration with longitudinal industrial data remains necessary.

Article.Title: GATA6 modulates cellular metabolism to influence chemotherapy sensitivity in non-small cell lung cancer
Article.Authors: Ju W.; Yu S.; Lin L.; Lv X.; Bai S.; Zheng L.
Article.Abstract: As a key transcription factor, GATA binding protein 6 (GATA6) has recently emerged as a critical regulator in tumorigenesis and cancer progression. However, its functional role in chemotherapy resistance, particularly in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), remains poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanistic link between GATA6 expression and chemosensitivity in NSCLC cells. The chemoresistant phenotype was modeled using chemoresistant NSCLC cell lines. GATA6 expression was genetically modulated to assess its impact on chemosensitivity via cell viability assays and in vivo xenograft experiments. Cellular metabolic phenotypes were profiled using cellular energy metabolism analyzers, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection assays were used by fluorescent probes. Mechanistic investigations included qPCR and western blotting to dissect the GATA6/c-Myc regulatory axis. GATA6 expression was found to be lower in chemoresistant lung cancer cells compared to their parental counterparts, and overexpression of GATA6 was able to partially reverse chemotherapy resistance. We observed that GATA6 regulates the metabolic phenotype of lung cancer cells, particularly affecting oxidative phosphorylation in chemoresistant lung cancer cells. This regulation of metabolism was associated with GATA6-mediated suppression of c-MYC mRNA expression. Furthermore, through reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection assays, we identified that GATA6 predominantly influences ROS production, ultimately affecting the chemosensitivity of lung cancer cells. In summary, this study demonstrates that GATA6 expression is associated with chemotherapy sensitivity in NSCLC cells, potentially through the modulation of metabolic phenotypes and steady‑state ROS levels. Our data suggest that GATA6 may regulate c‑Myc expression, which in turn influences mitochondrial respiration and ROS homeostasis, ultimately affecting cellular responses to cisplatin.

Article.Title: Influence of train speed on ground surface vibrations in urban rail tunnels
Article.Authors: Etemadi S.; Boroujerdi S.; Nejati H.; Moosavi S.; Nateghi R.; Goshtasbi K.; Abedini M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As underground rail networks expand, train-induced vibrations increasingly affect nearby structures, disturbing residents and sensitive equipment. One of the critical aspects of this research is the investigation of ground vibrations induced by train movements within tunnels. To address this issue, Line 6 of the Tehran Metro has been selected as a case study. A numerical approach was employed to simulate the dynamic loads exerted by trains operating at various speeds. The modeling process was conducted in two phases using finite element analysis. First, the dynamic loads resulting from wheel–rail interaction were determined. Then, the finite element method was applied to evaluate the ground vibration levels caused by underground train movements. Vibration velocity levels were analyzed at train speeds of 40, 60, and 90 km per hour. Given the double-track configuration of the Tehran Metro, nine distinct scenarios were considered. The results reveal that the scenario involving the simultaneous movement of two trains at 90 km/h produces the highest ground surface vibrations. The vibration velocity level in this case reaches 84 decibels, which may be disruptive to nearby residents. Overall, the findings indicate that increasing train speed leads to higher peak particle velocities, thereby intensifying ground vibration levels.

Article.Title: Gut microbial enrichment of Blautia and elevated serum butyrate in IgA nephropathy: an integrated multicenter analysis
Article.Authors: Park J.; Koh J.; Kim H.; Cho H.; Kim J.; Lee J.; Park S.; Kim D.; Lee J.; Kim Y.; Kim B.; Song W.; Lee W.; Kim D.; Nam H.; Li M.; Park S.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is increasingly linked to gut mucosal immune dysregulation, but the associated microbial and metabolic features remain inconsistently characterized. In this multicenter cross-sectional study, fecal samples from 187 participants (100 IgAN, 30 membranous nephropathy, 57 controls) and a replication cohort (96 IgAN, 46 controls) across six tertiary hospitals underwent 16S rRNA sequencing. Controls comprised healthy living kidney donors who passed standard donor screening. Differential abundance analysis was performed for genera and PICRUSt2-predicted pathways. Functional validation included short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) quantification and ex vivo SCFA stimulation of patient-derived B cells. IgAN patients differed from controls in beta diversity ( P = 0.001) but not alpha diversity. Among eight genera and 31 pathways associated with IgAN, Blautia , Ruminococcus gnavus group, and pyruvate metabolism (ko00620) were consistently enriched in IgAN in the replication cohort ( P = 0.008, 0.011, and 0.005, respectively). Blautia abundance positively correlated with blood pressure, serum creatinine, and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio in IgAN ( P < 0.05). Serum lactate ( P < 0.001) and butyrate ( P = 0.017) were elevated in IgAN, and butyrate stimulation increased CCR9 + and decreased IL-10 + B cell proportions ex-vivo ( P < 0.05). These findings suggest a potential role for circulating butyrate in mucosal immune dysregulation in IgAN, mediated through altered B-cell homing and impaired regulatory function.

Article.Title: Multi-prototypical contrastive mean-teacher with multi-granularity feature pyramid fusion for domain adaptive object detection
Article.Authors: Chen F.; Tao J.
Article.Abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptive object detection (UDA-OD) transfers detectors from labeled source domains to unlabeled target domains, yet mean-teacher methods still suffer from noisy pseudo-labels and cross-domain feature misalignment. Existing prototype-enhanced approaches retain three limitations: single centroids cannot model intra-class multi-modal feature dispersion; discrete fixed-scale extraction causes detection blind spots for extreme-size objects; and coarse prototype matching is vulnerable to degenerate pseudo-label predictions. We propose the Multi-Prototypical Contrastive Mean-Teacher (MPCMT) with three key designs. First, a bottom-up progressive nested multi-scale fusion (NMSF) module constructs a five-level dense scale pyramid and adaptively aggregates cross-granularity features via a lightweight channel-wise SE-Fuse operator, decoupling object scale variation from cross-domain appearance shift. Second, a category-wise multi-modal Gaussian prototype bank replaces the single-centroid paradigm, and symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence is adopted for distribution-level fine-grained prototype matching. Third, a hierarchical dual-level contrastive paradigm jointly enforces intra-domain compactness and inter-domain distribution alignment, complemented by a prototype prediction consistency loss that suppresses degenerate predictions. All modules operate only during training; an optional adaptive prototype ensemble strategy can further boost accuracy at deployment with about 1.3% extra latency. Extensive experiments on benchmarks covering three typical domain shift scenarios demonstrate that MPCMT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods with zero extra inference overhead in its default configuration.

Article.Title: Individual treatment effects of transcranial direct current stimulation on sustained attention
Article.Authors: Heo J.; Lee Y.; Yun S.; Jung M.; Kim H.; Seo H.; Kim H.; Oh B.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sustained attention is essential for daily functioning, yet the optimal parameters for transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) remain unclear because treatment responses vary across individuals. This study examined whether tDCS effects on sustained attention varied across individuals and stimulation intensities, and whether individual differences in treatment effects were associated with baseline cognitive function or EEG connectivity. In a randomized within-subject crossover study, 16 healthy participants received 0, 1, 2, and 3 mA tDCS. Electroencephalography (EEG) and response times during an auditory continuous performance task were measured before and after stimulation. No dose-specific improvement beyond sham was detected at the group level. However, a causal machine-learning model estimated heterogeneity in treatment effects. Cross-validated descriptive analyses showed larger response-time reductions in held-out prediction instances classified as responders than in those classified as non-responders or sham. Baseline EEG connectivity contributed more predictive information than demographic and neuropsychological measures. These findings suggest that baseline EEG connectivity may help identify likely responders and provide a framework for prospective validation of responder identification and treatment-parameter selection.

Article.Title: Seasonal sea ice formation re-establishes the cold halocline layer on the Northeast Greenland Shelf
Article.Authors: Ruiz-Castillo E.; Rysgaard S.; Rosing-Asvid A.; Dietz R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydrographic changes of the Northeast Greenland Shelf, located along the cold branch of the AMOC pathway, can alter the thermohaline circulation and global climate system. Regardless, the hydrography of the Northeast Greenland Shelf has been historically overlooked. Intra-annual variability remains poorly understood as scarce observations from ice-free periods depict a persistent Cold Halocline Layer (CHL) with near freezing temperatures overlying warmer waters. However, measurements from free-ranging ringed seals equipped with CTD satellite transmitters and casts taken through ice-covered to -free periods show large intra-annual variability. This consists of seasonal sea-ice melt and atmospheric heat input freshening and warming. Subsequently, surface fresher and warmer waters deepen into the CHL core. Afterwards, seasonal ice formation and associated brine release counteract warming and freshening, re-establishing the near freezing temperatures and more saline waters. Our findings highlight the vital role of local sea ice and brine formation in maintaining interannually the shelf CHL near freezing temperatures. Current predictions foresee shorter ice-covered periods. Reductions in sea-ice formation could decrease brine release formation and the cooling efficiency of the Northeast Greenland Shelf, turning the CHL into a warm and fresher halocline layer system.

Article.Title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of the Pfmdr1 N86Y mutation among malaria patients at Our Lady of the Apostles Hospital, N’Djamena, Chad
Article.Authors: Saleh B.; Cedric Y.; Raoul S.; Nadia N.; Pacome T.; Edna G.; Formotar V.; Kevin T.; Deborah D.; Ismail I.; Hervé M.; Ngaryedji T.; Mbida M.; Hu H.; Luyten W.
Article.Abstract: Malaria, an endemic parasitic disease caused by the Plasmodium genus, remains a major public health problem in Chad. The aim of this study is to assessed the frequency of the N86Y mutation in the pfmdr1 gene associated with antimalarial resistance amongst patients at Our Lady of the Apostles Hospital in N’Djamena, Chad. A cross-sectional study was conducted at Our Lady of the Apostles Hospital in N’Djamena, Chad. Samples were collected from consenting patients for the rapid diagnostic tests and thick blood smears to determine the presence and intensity of Plasmodium infection respectively. Positive samples were spotted on Whatman paper for molecular analysis. Plasmodial DNA was extracted using the Chelex-100 method and amplified by nested PCR. Mutations were detected using Afl III enzyme and restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis. The statistical analysis was carried out using SPSS software. Fifty-one (51) out of the 217 recruited participants were tested positive, with an overall prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum infection of 23.5%. Participants were aged from 0 to > 35 years and the prevalence of P. falciparum infection was higher among participants between 0 and 5 years and among students, with a significant difference ( p < 0.05). Females had a higher mean parasite density than men (419 ± 282.81). At the molecular level, the pfmdr1 gene was successfully amplified in 94.11% of positive samples; 90.2% for wild-type N86 alleles and 3.9% for mixed N86Y alleles. No pure 86Y mutant alleles were detected. Mixed allele frequency was comparable between male and female. This study assessed the frequency of the pfmdr1 N86Y antimalarial-resistance mutation among malaria patients attending Our Lady of the Apostles Hospital in N’Djamena, Chad. The pfmdr1 wild-type N86 allele overwhelmingly predominated among isolates (90.2%) with only low-frequency mixed N86Y alleles (3.9%) and an absence of pure 86Y mutant alleles. These findings underline the value of ongoing molecular surveillance to monitor antimalarial drug resistance markers and sustain treatment efficacy in Chad.

Article.Title: Activation of differential brain regions after sensing and eating a high-fat diet in mice
Article.Authors: Yamada S.; Kojima K.; Tsuneoka Y.; Watanabe Y.; Tanida T.; Matsuda K.; Tanaka M.
Article.Abstract: Food intake behavior is induced by factors such as low energy and pleasure/reward. To examine the brain mechanisms regulating pleasure/reward-induced food intake behavior, we investigated brain regions that were activated after eating or exposure to a high-fat diet (HFD), a palatable food for mice, using c-Fos immunohistochemistry. After exposure to HFD without eating, the number of c-Fos-immunoreactive (ir) cells significantly increased in the basolateral amygdala (BLA), paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN), and lateral hypothalamus (LH). After eating HFD, the number of c-Fos-ir cells significantly increased in the LH, nucleus accumbens (NAc), ventral tegmental area (VTA), and central amygdala (CeA). Using an in situ hybridization chain reaction, we found that 70% of activated cells after exposure to HFD in the BLA were vesicular glutamate transporter 1-positive. In conclusion, these data provide new findings showing that PVN neurons and BLA glutamatergic neurons are activated by sensing HFD without eating, whereas NAc, VTA, and CeA neurons are activated by eating HFD and LH neurons are activated by both sensing and eating HFD.

Article.Title: In utero exposure to high temperature-humidity index and its association with neonatal plasma metabolites in female dairy calves
Article.Authors: Dewulf M.; Plekhova V.; Vynck M.; Meesters M.; Van Eetvelde M.; Vanhaecke L.; Opsomer G.
Article.Abstract: Early-life environmental conditions during gestation can influence fetal development and induce long-term physiological adaptations. Prenatal heat stress has been associated with impaired health, survival, and productive performance in dairy cattle offspring. Metabolomics can reveal whether such exposures are reflected in the neonatal metabolome, offering insight into biological pathways linked to future performance and resilience. Plasma samples from 164 neonatal Holstein-Friesian calves from three Belgian dairy farms were analyzed using UHPLC-HRMS metabolomics. Prenatal factors (gestational exposure to elevated THI, maternal parity and season of birth) and later-life outcomes (age at removal from the herd, reproductive and productive parameters) were linked to the neonatal metabolome using partial Spearman correlations adjusted for herd and age at sampling. Exposure to elevated THI during mid- and late gestation was associated with 27 and 55 molecular features, respectively (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05, |ρ| > 0.3). Putatively annotated features were mainly eicosanoid-like, with opposite directions of association for mid- and late-gestational THI. Glutathione- and arachidonic acid metabolism were enriched for both trimesters. These observational findings indicate that gestational thermal conditions are associated with measurable differences in the neonatal plasma metabolome of dairy calves, with exploratory evidence implicating lipid mediator metabolism alterations.

Article.Title: A secure service-oriented framework for electronic health record management using blockchain
Article.Authors: Banerjee K.; Chowdhury S.; Saha S.; Mazumdar H.; Singh S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems remain a frequent target of cyberattacks, and storing patient data in one central place continues to put privacy and safety at risk. This paper presents eMediBlock, a service-oriented blockchain framework for EHR management in which patient data management, service booking, monitoring and recovery are exposed as loosely coupled services composed through smart contracts, and in which patients retain ownership of their records and decide who may read them. Records are kept off-chain and only a cryptographic fingerprint is written to the Ethereum blockchain, so the system stays affordable while any change to a record can still be detected. Building on this design, the paper adds six improvements and tests each one. Withdrawal of consent now takes effect immediately and completely, so a patient who changes their mind cannot be read by anyone in the gap between one withdrawal and the next. An emergency access path lets a doctor reach the record of an unconscious patient, but only in a way that is always recorded, expires by itself, and must be countersigned by a second doctor. Fingerprints are written in batches to cut cost, records are stored using an error-correcting code so they survive server failures, the fingerprint is computed over the standard HL7 FHIR form of the record so other hospital systems can check it, and routine transactions are scheduled into cheaper periods without ever delaying urgent ones. Testing every possible ordering of transactions found no case in which access survived a withdrawal of consent, whereas the usual design leaks access in 25 to 38 per cent of orderings. Batching cuts the cost of recording a document from 96,449 to 1,126 gas, the storage scheme keeps records available 9.8% points more often than simple copying at the same storage cost, and 2078 FHIR resources passed validation with no errors. The framework is designed to support HIPAA and GDPR principles; formal regulatory approval and hospital deployment remain future work.

Article.Title: A postmortem effect plays an important role in mineral formation
Article.Authors: Polgári M.; Bérczi S.; Gyollai I.
Article.Abstract: Igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary forms of the mineral genesis of main mineral-rock types are mature categories in terrestrial mineral lithology. In recent decades, the presence of a further large category, biomineralization, has been outlined. Questions regarding small-scale mineral assemblages have been partially answered by the processes found in large-scale sedimentary ore deposits. A question that arises for the creation of large-scale rock bodies is whether a post-decay, postmortem life effect of mineral-rock formation occurs widely, and not only in terrestrial geology but also on the rocky planetary bodies of our solar system. This postmortem effect we introduce as the Cell and EPS (extracellular polymeric substance)-induced Element POol (reservoir), or the CEEPO concept, including CEEPO-based mineralization. Manganese and iron ores have a special formation environment that allows us to formulate the CEEPO concept. The formation of Fe–Mn ore deposits can be interpreted in terms of large material transformations that took place with microbial mediation. Evidence from 390 samples from 14 Mn and Fe ore deposits and other metal indications of variable geological ages and geographical sites, studied by routine methodologies and complex interpretation supports a widespread and significant postmortem effect. We propose the positioning of this CEEPO concept among mineral precipitation types based on two important aspects that justify classifying this mineralization as an independent category: (1) precipitation of enormous mineral masses and (2) the fact that false interpretations can result when this mechanism is ignored.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based reconstruction of finite element thermal fields induced by microwave heating: a comparative study
Article.Authors: Milyani A.; Abu-Hamdeh N.
Article.Abstract: Microwave thermal therapy produces spatially localized heating whose numerical representation depends on energy deposition, conduction and blood perfusion. We investigated how accurately three compact coordinate-based regression families reconstruct withheld portions of one published steady-state finite-element bioheat field from sparse samples. Ridge-regularized tensor-product B-splines, a Fourier-feature multilayer perceptron and Chebyshev Elastic Net were evaluated with matched 20-evaluation differential-evolution and dual-annealing searches. Five spatially blocked test folds, a separate validation fold, 0.5-mm exclusion buffers, three sampling seeds and training budgets of 649 (1%) or 3,243 (5%) nodes reduced immediate-neighbor leakage. The spline achieved mean held-out MAE of 0.701 K at 649 nodes and 0.450 K at 3,243 nodes in its best optimizer configurations; at the larger budget, its 345-K node-mask Dice score reached 0.899 in hot-bearing folds. Sensitivity analyses with a wider buffer and an alternative block layout also favored a spline configuration in aggregate, although rankings were layout-dependent. These findings identify effective sparse-reconstruction representations and highlight regional error behavior within this solved thermal field, without assuming transfer to untested therapy configurations.

Article.Title: Optimal actor-critic learning-based cooperative control of nonlinear multi-agent systems subject to communication delays
Article.Authors: Niroomanesh R.; Alipour K.; Tarvirdizadeh B.; Ghamari M.
Article.Abstract: Multi-agent systems have attracted considerable attention due to their wide-ranging applications in robotics and search and rescue operations. Cooperative control in such systems requires designing protocols that facilitate effective communication among agents to achieve shared objectives, while ensuring consensus in the presence of nonlinear dynamics and communication delays, and optimizing performance to minimize energy consumption and convergence time. This research proposes a novel consensus-based cooperative control framework for a multi-agent system following a leader-follower approach. The framework addresses nonlinear dynamics and time-varying heterogeneous communication delays through the design of a near-optimal distributed controller. The controller is developed and simulated using online actor-critic reinforcement learning with a neural network architecture, ensuring near-optimal performance and minimal error. Its performance under uncertainties and large time-varying delays is also evaluated, with the simulation results demonstrating the high delay tolerance and robustness of the proposed approach, as well as its scalability to larger agent networks. Furthermore, the stability of the system is rigorously proven using a Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, confirming its effectiveness in handling these challenges.

Article.Title: A novel topology-guided adaptive strategy for automated nuclear-cytoplasmic H-score quantification in immunohistochemistry
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Lin M.; Zou F.; Yang Z.; Huang M.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Automated quantification of immunohistochemistry (IHC) supports reproducible biomarker assessment, but routine use remains limited by cellular crowding and staining variability. We present a workflow for batch quantification of nuclear and cytoplasmic IHC staining using H-scores, without task-specific model training. It integrates StarDist nuclear detection, a Voronoi-based Cell Distance (VCD) topology-guided segmentation strategy and user-guided reference-calibrated grading. VCD constrains nuclear expansion using Voronoi-derived boundaries to maintain separation between adjacent measurement regions. Reference-calibrated grading uses user-selected reference regions from a representative calibration image to derive batch-specific staining-intensity thresholds. In the segmentation benchmark, 99.7% of matched objects had a mean boundary distance from manual ground-truth contours to predicted contours of no more than 2 pixels. Across 752 IHC images representing diverse staining conditions, reference-calibrated grading showed close agreement with pathologist-assigned reference H-scores (Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient = 0.997), with a mean Bland–Altman bias of − 2.35 H-score units. In Human Protein Atlas datasets, automated H-scores correlated with categorical expression annotations for Timeless ( n = 330; Spearman’s ρ = 0.760), CDK1 ( n = 290; ρ = 0.660) and p53 ( n = 152; ρ = 0.765). This open-source plugin provides an accessible workflow for batch quantification of nuclear and cytoplasmic IHC staining in selected image fields.

Article.Title: QUANTUM-IDS: a quantum-inspired deep learning framework with multi-scale temporal analysis and meta-learning for network intrusion detection
Article.Authors: Sudhakar K.; Mishra V.; Mayasala P.; Krishna B.; Narayana S.
Article.Abstract: Network intrusion detection systems currently face key challenges in detecting advanced cyber-attacks that have non-linear feature relationships, various scales of temporal relationships, and enhanced evasion techniques. This study investigates the applicability and empirical value of five concepts for network intrusion detection by embedding them in a deep learning architecture called QUANTUM-IDS: Quantum Feature Entanglement (QFE), a classical feature-mixing mechanism that uses feature expansion and repeated learned pairwise interactions; a Multi-Scale Temporal Convolutional Network (MS-TCN) for representing traffic at multiple temporal resolutions; an Adversarial Robustness Module (ARM) combining adversarial training with certified robustness guarantees; a Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Detection module (MFD) intended to support efficient few-shot adaptation within the evaluated attack-category distribution using a handful of labelled examples and a Causal Inference Attribution module (CIA) intended to support explainability of the decision process. Evaluated under a leakage-controlled protocol on a five-class subset of CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (248,347 de-duplicated flows; Benign, DoS, DDoS, Infiltration, Bot; Timestamp excluded), QUANTUM-IDS reached 85.76% ± 1.31% test accuracy and 73.02% macro-F1 over five seeds, below an MLP (88.12%) and gradient-boosted trees (90.62%). Without adversarial training (clean-accuracy variant), it reached 88.83% ± 1.07%. With adversarial training, it kept accuracy at 81.8% under PGD-20 attacks (ε = 0.1) and 81.5% under AutoAttack, against 62.8% and 49.0% for an undefended MLP. Ablations over five paired seeds showed no significant contribution of the quantum-inspired, multi-scale, few-shot or causal modules, and an equally robust adversarially trained MLP indicates that robustness stems from the training procedure. The principal limitation is that attack classes absent from training were not detected reliably, even with labelled examples. A leakage audit showed that including the Timestamp field would raise accuracy from 85.0 to 94.9%.

Article.Title: Mapping citizen-sourced urban perceptions to guide health-directed interventions
Article.Authors: Nishii S.; Sato T.; Kataoka K.; Deguchi R.; Luo Y.; Wang B.; Nakashima Y.; Nagahara H.; Fujimori M.; Murata N.; Suzuki N.; Takebe T.
Article.Abstract: The urban environment is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of human health, yet planning tools rely on static, low-resolution surveys that fail to capture people’s granular experience of local environments. We ask whether citizen-sourced, high-resolution data on urban experience can be translated into design-relevant hypotheses for healthier behavior. We developed Enabling City Walk (ECW), a smartphone platform that collects geotagged submissions linking real-time perceptions of “happiness” and “healthiness” to specific urban visual features. Across 28 sessions in ten urban and suburban areas of seven Japanese municipalities, 648 participants contributed 8,225 posts. Combining citizen science with computer vision, we identified environmental correlates of positive and negative experience, from greenery and social spaces to neglect and disorder. We introduce the Enabling Index, which locates mismatches between perceived healthiness and happiness and identifies candidate sites for targeted improvement. We then implemented low-cost pilot interventions; pre-post observation showed increases in positive perceptions and in observed stair use, with the reach of the change tracking the affective content of the design rather than the presence of an installation. This citizen-and-AI methodology gives planners a scalable way to generate and prioritize design hypotheses for happiness-oriented, health-enabling design, which can then be tested prospectively.

Article.Title: Sustainable microcrystalline cellulose matrix for cisplatin binding: a bioinorganic and spectroscopic evaluation
Article.Authors: Abd Kadir N.; Lenga Gururuloo S.; Poobalan C.; Mohammad M.; Alam M.
Article.Abstract: This research explores the formulation of cisplatin tablets utilizing microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) derived from coconut coir as a sustainable matrix material. The successful incorporation of cisplatin into the MCC-based tablet was confirmed through analytical techniques, including SEM, FT-IR, TGA, and XRD. XRD analysis revealed an apparent crystallinity index of 80.40% for the whole tablet formulation, and TGA showed that the tablet remains largely stable below 250 °C, with the first major degradation event beginning around 250 °C, indicating structural robustness for further interaction studies. The binding interactions of the MCC-cisplatin complex with bovine serum albumin (BSA) and human serum albumin (HSA) were investigated using fluorescence spectroscopy and molecular docking. Fluorescence analysis revealed predominantly static quenching ( K SV decreased with increasing temperature and K q exceeded the diffusion-controlled limit). Binding parameters were calculated: for BSA, the number of binding sites ( n ) = 0.82, Stern–Volmer constant ( K SV ) = 0.128 (µg/mL)⁻¹, and binding constant ( K b ) = 5.97 × 10 5 M − 1 ; for HSA, n = 0.5, K SV = 8.45 × 10 − 3 (µg/mL)⁻¹, and K b = 1.02 × 10 4 M⁻¹. These results indicate stronger interaction of the MCC-cisplatin complex with BSA compared to HSA. Molecular docking of cisplatin identified hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions at specific amino acid residues, with similar PLANTS​ (Protein-Ligand ANT System) scores of − 39.9189 for BSA and − 39.5462 for HSA. A comparative study with commercial MCC revealed differences in protein-binding behavior, suggesting that the MCC source may influence protein-binding behavior. This work suggests the potential of coconut coir-derived MCC as a green, functional matrix for formulating metal-based compounds in biophysical interaction studies.

This study evaluated the effects of incorporating Citri-Fi 200FG fiber (0, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 g/100 g) into batter mixes on the physicochemical properties of deep-fried chicken strips. Samples were fried in an oleogel made with carnauba wax-canola oil (10 g/100 g). Citri-Fi 200FG significantly enhanced batter viscosity and pick-up and reduced fat-uptake while improving moisture content ( p < 0.05). However, it did not affect ash, protein, color, texture, pH, or sensory attributes. SEM of the defatted, freeze-dried crust–core interface showed a smoother structure with fewer voids in Citri-Fi-battered samples. Fatty acid analysis showed Citri-Fi-battered samples had lower saturated fatty acids and higher monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids than controls ( p < 0.05). The oleogel showed the ability to immobilize oil and solid-like rheological behavior, as evidenced by its oil binding capacity and viscoelastic properties. Overall, using Citri-Fi 200FG in batter and oleogel as the frying medium improved the nutritional profile of fried chicken strips without compromising quality.

By the end of the five-day evaluation, biochemical markers largely normalized and our macroscopic observation using a digital caliper, revealed a significant enhancement in the wound closure rate in the nanoparticle-treated groups These findings highlight the exceptional architecture of this nanocomposite, identifying it as a potent nanoplatform for alleviating oxidative stress, stabilizing cellular activity and accelerated wound healing in diabetic oral wound models.

Article.Title: Behavioural responses to simulated phishing across organizational roles in higher education
Article.Authors: Jasinska H.; Jasinski A.
Article.Abstract: Phishing remains one of the most effective forms of social engineering, exploiting not only technical vulnerabilities but also organizational and behavioural factors. While individual susceptibility has been widely examined, comparatively little empirical research has investigated how organizational roles shape real-world responses within a single institution. This study reports findings from an observational field experiment conducted at a large technical university (N = 600), examining behavioural responses to simulated phishing messages among administrative staff, academic staff, and students. Participants received contextually relevant phishing scenarios within their routine email environment, and observable behaviours were recorded, including link interaction, reporting, and non-response. Behavioural responses differed significantly across organizational groups (χ 2 (4, N = 600) = 272.03, p < .001, Cramér’s V = 0.48). Administrative staff exhibited the highest interaction rate (93.5%), compared with 44.0% among academic staff and 22.5% among students. Logistic regression analysis indicated that administrative staff were substantially more likely to interact with the phishing link than students (OR = 49.87, 95% CI [20.55, 121.01]). The findings demonstrate substantial differences in behavioural responses across organizational groups under realistic phishing conditions. While the role-specific phishing scenarios employed in the study were designed to maximize ecological validity, the results suggest that organizational context, communication practices, and role-specific interaction environments may influence phishing-related behaviour. These findings support the development of role-sensitive and context-aware cybersecurity interventions within higher education institutions.

Article.Abstract: This study investigates the effects of magnetised sodium dodecylbenzene sulphonate (SDBS) solution on coal pore structure and wettability. With increasing magnetisation flow rate, the aromatic-layer spacing first increased and then decreased, whereas the planar extent of aromatic structural units, aromatic-layer stacking height, number of stacked layers, and degree of coalification first decreased and then increased. The average pore diameter first increased and then decreased, whereas total pore volume and specific surface area first decreased and then increased. The limiting occupied area of SDBS molecules at the gas–liquid interface was positively correlated with both aromatic-layer spacing and average pore diameter, whereas the Gibbs free energy of adsorption at the gas–liquid interface was negatively correlated with these parameters. Increasing magnetisation flow rates altered the interfacial behaviour of SDBS, as reflected by the increase in its limiting occupied area. These changes loosened aromatic-layer arrangement, reduced coalification, and improved pore connectivity, facilitating solution penetration and enhancing coal wettability. The findings provide a theoretical basis for regulating coal-seam gas desorption and mitigating gas-related disasters.

Article.Title: Moderating role of religiosity in islamic banking intentions and behaviours within the decomposed theory of planned behaviour

Article.Abstract: While Islamic banking is becoming more important in Türkiye its market share is still small compared to many other Muslim majority countries. Survey data from 790 individuals were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The results show that attitude is the strongest predictor of intention, while perceived behavioral control also has a positive and significant effect; subjective norm, however, does not significantly predict intention. Intention is the strongest predictor of Islamic banking behavior, with perceived behavioral control also exerting a positive effect. The moderation results further indicate that religiosity does not operate uniformly across the DTPB relationships: it positively moderates the attitude–intention relationship, negatively moderates the subjective norm–intention relationship, does not significantly moderate the PBC–intention or intention–behavior relationships, and shows a weaker moderating effect on the PBC–behavior relationship. These findings extend DTPB-based Islamic banking research by showing that religiosity operates in a path-dependent manner across intention formation and behavioral enactment.

Article.Title: Identification of stable RT-qPCR reference genes for hypoxia-driven transcriptional studies in oesophageal adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Das B.; Robb H.; Kwan Hung Leung P.; Brooks E.; Bristow R.; Hanna G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oesophageal adenocarcinoma (OAC) is an aggressive malignancy with poor clinical outcomes. Tumour hypoxia contributes to treatment resistance and disease progression, highlighting the need for accurate quantification of hypoxia-regulated gene expression. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) remains the reference method for precise gene expression analysis; however, its accuracy depends on reference genes with stable expression across experimental conditions. Because hypoxia induces extensive transcriptional remodelling, many commonly used reference genes become unsuitable for normalisation. We therefore sought to identify and validate stable reference genes for RT-qPCR studies of hypoxia in OAC. Candidate reference genes were identified using RNA sequencing datasets from three widely used OAC cell lines (FLO-1, OE33, and OE19) cultured under normoxic and hypoxic conditions. Genes exhibiting minimal transcriptional variation across oxygen tensions were shortlisted. Thirteen candidates were then evaluated by RT-qPCR across multiple oxygen levels (21%, 1%, and 0.2% O 2 ) and exposure durations (24 and 48 h). Expression stability was assessed using the geNorm algorithm to determine the optimal normalisation strategy and independently validated using NormFinder. Transcriptome-wide screening identified thirteen candidate genes with highly stable expression across cell lines and oxygen tensions (maximum log 2 FC 0.081–0.145; CV ≤ 0.006). RT-qPCR validation demonstrated that DDX6 and EFCAB14 exhibited the lowest expression stability values across all experimental conditions. Pairwise variation analysis indicated that two reference genes were sufficient for accurate normalisation (V 2/3 < 0.15). NormFinder analysis independently confirmed the stability of these genes, with concordant rankings across both algorithms supporting their robustness. Normalisation using the geometric mean of DDX6 and EFCAB14 produced consistent quantification of hypoxia-responsive transcripts, whereas commonly used reference genes such as GAPDH and ACTB substantially altered the apparent magnitude of VEGFA and SLC2A1 induction. DDX6 and EFCAB14 are highly stable reference genes for RT-qPCR normalisation in hypoxia-exposed OAC cell lines. These findings provide a validated normalisation framework for transcriptional studies of tumour hypoxia in OAC and improve the accuracy and reproducibility of gene expression analyses in this disease.

Article.Title: Preoperative subtalar joint stiffness predicts poor functional outcomes after supramalleolar osteotomy in an internally validated prognostic model
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Chen D.; Liu Y.; Zheng L.; Liu P.
Article.Abstract: In this TRIPOD Type 1a study, we analyzed 108 consecutive patients who underwent computer-navigated SMO for varus ankle arthritis (2019–2024). STJ function was preoperatively stratified via a three-domain assessment (clinical range of motion, stress radiography, and CT) into Compensated (mobile, n = 88) or Decompensated (stiff, n = 20). The primary outcome was a composite of poor functional outcome (AOFAS < 80) or revision surgery. We developed a Firth-penalized logistic regression model and performed internal validation using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) and bootstrap resampling (B = 100) to estimate the optimism-corrected AUC. Multivariable Firth-penalized logistic regression identified subtalar joint (STJ) decompensation as the single independent predictor of poor outcome (OR 62.23, 95% CI 8.70–812.53, P < 0.001); preoperative talar tilt (TT) angle > 7.5° (OR 3.40, 95% CI 0.28–29.03, P = 0.293) and Takakura stage Ⅲ (OR 1.69, 95% CI 0.11–16.22, P = 0.675) did not reach significance after adjustment. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.957 with a LOOCV AUC of 0.880 (optimism 0.078; bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC 0.947). Calibration was adequate (LOOCV calibration slope 0.96, in-the-large − 0.06, Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.634). The primary outcome occurred in 90.0% (18/20) of the Decompensated group versus 2.3% (2/88) of the Compensated group ( P < 0.001). A sensitivity analysis with continuous preoperative TT angle recovered a significant per-degree effect (OR 3.62, 95% CI 1.43–9.19, P = 0.007). In this preliminary, single-center cohort, preoperative STJ stiffness emerged as a potentially important independent predictor of poor functional recovery despite successful radiographic correction. The internally validated nomogram offers a preliminary risk-estimation tool that may assist preoperative counseling.

Article.Title: Open-data critical-access screening for compound heat–flood infrastructure risk in low-data cities
Article.Authors: Al-Azazi S.; Ali A.; Qasem F.; Alawag A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-data and conflict-affected cities need infrastructure-access screening that uses public data without turning proxies into predictions. We rebuilt a four-city Yemen analysis from archived raw sources using a topology-preserving road graph, WorldPop, SRTM, HydroSHEDS, regional NASA POWER, CHIRPS, UCDP GED and UNOSAT flood observations. Population inside 30-km analytical frames was routed on a 45-km road-and-facility halo to reduce boundary truncation. Network distances increased mapped education remoteness beyond 5 km to 57.81% of population in Taiz and 48.11% in Al Hudaydah. Exact clipping placed 0.59–2.54% of road length within 100 m of mapped waterways. CHIRPS independently indicated higher recent annual rainfall in Taiz (+ 109.0 mm) and Al Hudaydah (+ 78.2 mm), while regional POWER cells exposed substantial within-frame climate variability. A transparent road-link screening priority was evaluated with alternative aggregation, three weight-perturbation families, boundary, snapping and conflict-impedance sensitivities, and 400 link-removal experiments. UNOSAT comparison was restricted to observable cloud-free coverage and did not validate the composite score as an inundation classifier. The framework is therefore an auditable triage tool for field verification, not a flood, closure, travel-time or investment model.

Article.Title: A physics-encoded transformer for fast three-component borehole transient electromagnetic forward modeling
Article.Authors: Tang Y.; Yu J.; Su B.
Article.Abstract: Three-dimensional forward modeling of three-component borehole transient electromagnetic responses is computationally expensive, severely limiting “Long-Heading Long-Detection” technology in coal mines. We construct a physics-encoded Transformer surrogate that takes a 3D conductivity volume as input and predicts response nodes across all stations, components, and time gates. A 3D convolutional encoder compresses the conductivity structure. Physical descriptors explicitly encode station position, observation time, dimensionless time, component attributes, and sampling indices. A multi-layer, multi-head self-attention Transformer allows interactions among response nodes along the borehole, across components, and across time gates. Training data are generated by batch 3D finite volume method simulations over homogeneous conducting backgrounds, layered media, and typical mine anomalous bodies. Single-factor studies of normalization and hyperparameters are supplemented by seven baseline and ablation configurations trained with three random seeds under a common protocol. The proposed model achieves a pooled $$\:R^2$$ of 0.9846 ± 0.0012 across three training seeds on a fixed, held-out test set of 400 cases. The pooled score is strongly influenced by the early-time axial response. Component-wise scores, decay curves, and zero-crossing diagnostics characterize agreement with the FVM reference for the weaker transverse responses. Single-inference latency is reduced to milliseconds, with a reported model-only online speedup of 30,080-fold, excluding preprocessing, database generation, and training. Within the sampled geological family and fixed observation layout, the surrogate provides a fast forward approximation and a computational basis for future inversion studies.

Article.Title: Quantum inspired adversarial learning with transformer driven context modeling for breast cancer characterization in ultrasound imaging
Article.Authors: Shankar Ganesh V.; Purushothaman A.
Article.Abstract: Although breast ultrasound has the potential to become a powerful imaging tool in the diagnosis of breast cancer, it remains a difficult modality to use in the clinic, owing to its low contrast, indistinct tumor boundaries, and speckle noise, which masks fine tissue structures and complicates interpretation. To address these challenges, this study introduces a hybrid end-to-end diagnostic framework combining quantum-inspired learning and transformer-based classification for breast lesion segmentation and malignancy prediction. First, anisotropic diffusion filtering is used as a preprocessing step to successfully reduce the speckle noise while retaining important edge information. Subsequently, the tumors are segmented using a quantum-inspired generative adversarial network (QI-GAN), which is improved by entanglement-inspired quantum feature attention, channel attention modules (CAM), and multi-scale feature fusion (MSFF) to precisely capture the complex lesion morphology and precise boundary details. Simultaneously, a vision transformer (ViT) is directly integrated with the segmentation network’s encoder to capture long-range spatial relationships and global context for the purpose of training the network to classify the malignancy of the lesion.At the same time, a vision transformer (ViT) is directly coupled to the segmentation network’s encoder to capture long-range spatial relationships and global context to allow training of the network for lesion level malignancy classification. To obtain better performance, key hyperparameters are optimized via the sharpbelly fish optimizer (SFO), a bio-inspired optimization method that is aimed at maximizing segmentation accuracy and classification robustness. Two publicly available datasets were used for extensive validation: Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) and Ultrasound Diagnosis in Ambulatory Tumors (UDIAT). Because the class imbalance is an intrinsic property of ultrasound images owing to highly present background regions compared to the foreground, the evaluation was performed using metrics more resistant to imbalanced data distributions. The experimental results show that the proposed model can obtain Dice similarity coefficients of 97.85% on BUSI and 98.85% on UDIAT, which proves that the model can accurately delineate the tumor boundary with noisy imaging data. The framework achieves F1-scores of 99.08% and 99.27% on BUSI and UDIAT, respectively, for the classification of lesion-level malignancy, which represents good discriminative ability. This study corroborates the strength and effectiveness of the proposed framework for using quantum technology to accurately segment and classify breast lesions in ultrasound images.

Article.Title: Sirtuin mRNAs and NBR2 emerge as candidate biomarkers and contribute to the progression of prostate cells via secreted extracellular vesicles
Article.Authors: Onyiba C.; Scarlett C.; Weidenhofer J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Late detection remains a major challenge to the successful treatment of prostate cancer (PCa), as current biomarkers show low sensitivity and specificity for the early detection of the disease. Given that extracellular vesicles (EVs) secreted by cells contain a wide range of bioactive molecules with biomarker potential, we determined the biomarker potential and functional contributions of SIRT1–7 mRNA, NBR2 , and PCGEM1 in prostate cells via their secreted EVs. EVs were isolated by ultrafiltration and characterised by nanoparticle tracking analysis and Western blotting. Expressions of SIRT1–7 mRNA, NBR2 , and PCGEM1 were quantified by qRT-PCR assays. The functional contributions of these molecules via EVs were determined by apoptosis, necrosis, proliferation, and migration assays. We identified diagnostic and prognostic molecular signatures of sirtuin mRNAs and NBR2 , which differed between the PCa cells and their secreted EVs. Among the potential biomarkers identified, SIRT2 , 3 , 4 , and 7 mRNA showed the highest biomarker potential in PCa-derived EVs. Through functional assays, we demonstrated that sirtuin mRNA-rich PCa-derived EVs increased apoptosis, long-term proliferation, and migration of PNT-2 cells. Overall, we demonstrated, for the first time, that sirtuin mRNAs and NBR2 serve both biomarker and functional purposes for prostate cells via secreted EVs.

Article.Title: Comparison of practical efficiencies of solar pv panels used for solar pv power plants and solar powered electric vehicles
Article.Authors: Koyuncu T.; Lule F.
Article.Abstract: In this work; the efficiencies of solar PV panels used in two different applications were investigated. One of these applications is fixed solar PV power plant and the other is solar powered electric vehicles. The application of solar PV power plant has three similar fixed solar PV power plants consisting of 1.025 MW each power. The other application is solar powered electric vehicles consisting of an automobile and a minibus called “Firat Force” and “Commagene”, respectively. The main purpose of this study is to determine the practical efficiencies of solar PV panels used in these two different applications and to compare them with their efficiencies both in STC conditions and in different applications. Thus, the practical efficiencies of fixed and mobile solar PV panels and the differences between them has been determined. As a result of this work; It was determined that the peak efficiency of solar PV panels used in fixed solar power plants is 16.32% under Standard Test Conditions (STC) and is 15% in practice. In addition, the peak efficiency of solar PV panels used in solar powered automobile and minibus was found as 18% under STC and was determined as 13% in practice.

Article.Title: Assessment and mapping of soil moisture at field capacity using machine learning methods in the Central Chernozem Belt of Russia
Article.Authors: Shirali M.; Hatamiafkoueieh J.; Poddubsky A.; Rezaeian N.
Article.Abstract: Soil moisture at field capacity (SM FC ) is a key soil hydraulic property for assessing water-storage capacity, irrigation requirements, and crop-water availability, yet its regional distribution is difficult to characterize because it is controlled by interacting soil, climatic, topographic, and land-surface factors. To address the logistical constraints of direct regional matric potential measurements, this study applied an indirect, pedotransfer function (PTF)-augmented digital soil mapping framework to estimate and map SM FC at 0–30 cm depth and a matric potential of − 33 kPa across the Central Chernozem Belt of Russia using an explainable machine learning framework. A total of 2157 geo-referenced soil samples collected between 2023 and 2025 were combined with remote-sensing, terrain, climatic, geological, and spatial covariates defined within the SCORPAN framework. SM FC was estimated from van Genuchten water-retention parameters derived using pedotransfer functions, and three machine-learning algorithms, namely artificial neural network (ANN), support vector machine (SVM), and random forest (RF), were trained and independently evaluated using a 70:30 calibrations–validation design. The RF model provided the most accurate predictions in both datasets, achieving R 2 = 0.81, RMSE = 1.93, and PRD = 3.17 during calibration and R 2 = 0.89, RMSE = 1.45, and PRD = 3.25 during independent validation. ANN showed intermediate performance, whereas SVM produced the lowest accuracy. RF-based predictions revealed substantial and spatially heterogeneous variation in SM FC , with values ranging from 13.68 to 43.34, and no simple regional gradient. Variable-importance analysis identified NDVI, TWI, SAVI, and NDWI as the leading predictors, highlighting the relevance of vegetation condition and topographic moisture redistribution to the spatial pattern of soil water retention. Lower and upper prediction-limit maps further demonstrated that predictive uncertainty varied across the region. These findings indicate that explainable machine-learning methods, particularly RF, can support regional assessment of SM FC in environmentally heterogeneous agricultural systems, while uncertainty information remains necessary for cautious interpretation and responsible application in irrigation planning and soil–water management.

Article.Title: Fault-tolerant IoT sensing and attention-based bidirectional LSTM forecasting enable day-ahead groundwater quality early warning in a semi-arid alluvial aquifer
Article.Authors: Dhaka R.; Khurana M.; Lamba S.
Article.Abstract: Real-time wireless sensor network (WSN) deployments for groundwater monitoring face two intertwined reliability problems that have been addressed only in isolation: link-layer packet loss under realistic low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) conditions, and the silent propagation of resulting data gaps and sensor faults into downstream predictive models. Existing IoT groundwater deployments report monitoring results without engineered fault tolerance, while existing recurrent water-quality forecasters are evaluated on laboratory-curated time series and not as components of an operational WSN. This paper contributes a networked-systems framework in which the WSN reliability layer and the temporal prediction layer are co-designed and jointly validated on an empirical 30-node, 15-minute field dataset spanning 1445 days (4.16 million records) in a semi-arid alluvial aquifer, with electrical conductivity (EC) as the directly-measured salinity sensor (total dissolved solids derived as TDS \(=\,0.64\times\) EC, \(R^{2}=0.96\) ). The framework combines (i) a single-hop LoRa star in the WPC-delicensed 865–867 MHz band with sensor-node-side buffering and a dual-mode gateway; (ii) a two-stage anomaly screen and a parameter-stratified imputation pipeline: Ordinary Kriging for the spatially-coherent parameters (DO, temperature) and within-node temporal imputation for the rest, the split decided from measured nearest-neighbour correlation; and (iii) a Hybrid Bidirectional LSTM with Attention Mechanism (HBiLSTM-AM) with conformally-recalibrated uncertainty. Groundwater signals at this site vary slowly and are strongly autocorrelated. The honest figure of merit is therefore day-ahead (24 h) forecasting skill above a strong persistence baseline, and above all fault tolerance. At the 24-hour horizon HBiLSTM-AM attains a mean \(R^{2}=0.953\) , the strongest of the recurrent forecasters across a nine-baseline comparison that spans naive persistence, kernel, support-vector, regularised-linear, feed-forward, transformer, and domain state-of-the-art dual-attention encoder–decoder references, and \(+1.8\) points above naive persistence. On clean data the strongest non-recurrent references are statistically level with it, an outcome this evaluation was built to expose. Robustness is where the separation appears. The data-layer imputation holds day-ahead \(R^{2}\) within 0.001 (absolute) under up to \(40\%\) packet loss (uniform and bursty), whereas the same model without imputation collapses to \(R^{2}=0.804\) , and a simulated worst-case outage of an entire six-node spatial cluster over the full 24-hour input window, an event never observed in the 1445-day record, bounds the degradation at \(-0.026\) mean \(R^{2}\) with every channel above 0.90. Chronologically calibrated split-conformal \(95\%\) prediction intervals achieve near-nominal coverage (PICP 0.946–0.961), and a day-ahead EC salinity-threshold alert reaches \(88.5\%\) precision at \(88.8\%\) recall with a 24-hour lead time. The EC sensor is laboratory-anchored at \(R^{2}=0.996\) ( \(n=1461\) paired samples), and the site is salinity-stressed (EC exceeds the WHO-permissible level in \(65\%\) of laboratory samples). The networked-systems co-design, and the imputation-driven fault tolerance in particular, is the principal contribution. We do not claim generalisation beyond the present semi-arid alluvial aquifer, and identify it as future work.

Article.Title: Association of fruit and vegetable intake with traditional lipid profile and atherogenic indices: cross-sectional evidence from the isfahan cohort study 2
Article.Authors: Kakavand N.; Mahmoudi Azar M.; Hashemi Chaleshtori N.; Boshtam M.; Dianatkhah M.; Bateni M.; Arefianjazi M.; Hosseini A.; Mohammadifard N.; Sarrafzadegan N.
Article.Abstract: While fruit and vegetable intake is widely linked to improved cardiometabolic health, evidence connecting it to traditional lipid measures and atherogenic indices remains limited. This study investigated the association between fruit and vegetable consumption and lipid-related cardiovascular risk markers in Iranian adults. This cross-sectional study used data from 2,188 participants aged 35 years or older enrolled in the Isfahan Cohort Study 2 in 2018. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), and participants were categorized into tertiles based on their fruit and vegetable consumption. Fasting lipid parameters were measured, and atherogenic indices, including Atherogenic Index of Plasma (AIP), Atherogenic Combined Index (ACI), Castelli Risk Indices (CRI-I/II), Atherogenic Coefficient (AC), Lipoprotein Combined Index (LCI), Remnant Lipoprotein Cholesterol (RLPC), Triglyceride to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (TG/HDL-C), non-HDL-C/HDL-C ratio (NHHR), and non-HDL-C (NHC), were calculated. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were applied to examine these associations. In the fully adjusted linear regression models, none of the associations between fruit and vegetable intake and the lipid parameters or atherogenic indices were statistically significant. However, in the logistic regression analysis, participants in the highest tertile of fruit and vegetable intake had significantly lower odds of elevated NHC compared with those in the lowest tertile (OR: 0.77; 95% CI 0.60, 0.99; P = 0.039). Higher fruit and vegetable intake was associated with a more favorable NHC profile, but not with most other lipid parameters or atherogenic indices in the fully adjusted analysis. These findings should be interpreted cautiously, given the cross-sectional study design, and prospective studies are needed.

Article.Title: QTL-seq reveals two heading date QTLs with contrasting associations on chromosomes 3A and 3D in allohexaploid wheat
Article.Authors: Abraha H.; Choi C.; Kim K.; Kadam S.; Choi J.; Jung H.; Oh E.; Jeon D.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bread wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) is a major cereal crop, but South Korea produces less than 2% of its wheat demand. Developing early-heading cultivars for wheat–rice double-cropping is a key breeding goal, although the genetic basis of heading date (HD) remains challenging because of its polygenic inheritance and allohexaploid genome. This study identified HD-associated quantitative trait loci (QTLs) using QTL-seq, linked markers, and candidate-genes. Phenotypic evaluation revealed an asymmetric bimodal distribution with transgressive segregation. QTL-seq identified two significant loci on chromosomes 3A ( qHdtm-3A.1 ; 746–762 Mbp) and 3D ( qHdtm-3D.1 ; 627–639 Mbp), both exceeding the 99% confidence threshold. Genotype and concordance analyses revealed contrasting genotype–phenotype associations, with qHdtm-3A.1 and qHdtm-3D.1 showing contrasting allele-enrichment patterns relative to the parental phenotypes. Comparative analysis supported their homoeologous relationship through conserved gene relationships and local collinearity, while limited sequence alignment indicated substantial sequence divergence. Candidate-gene analysis identified both shared F-box/FBD/LRR-repeat genes and QTL-specific candidates, supporting the hypothesis of distinct genetic contributions from the A and D subgenomes. These findings provide candidate genomic regions and linked markers that may contribute to early-heading wheat breeding, pending validation at the individual-plant level across multiple environments and in independent populations.

Article.Title: Changes in tobacco product use and risk of depression and suicide in a regional cohort of Korean male smokers
Article.Authors: Park S.; Chung J.; Park S.; Kim H.; Jeong S.; Lee S.; Kim K.; Ko A.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: Smoking is associated with depression and suicide, but the mental health implications of quitting or of switching to alternative nicotine products remain uncertain. Using Korean National Health Insurance Service data from Chungcheongnam-do, we followed 157,745 men aged 19 years or older who smoked combustible cigarettes in 2014–2015 and underwent a second health screening in 2018–2019. Tobacco product use at the second screening was categorized as continued combustible cigarette use, complete cessation, switching to e-cigarette or heated tobacco product use, or dual use. Over a mean follow-up of 3.6 years, 1452 incident depression diagnoses and 169 suicide deaths occurred. Compared with continued combustible cigarette use, complete cessation was associated with a higher risk of depression (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.18; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04–1.34) and a lower risk of suicide (aHR, 0.63; 95% CI 0.40–0.996). Both associations were attenuated when outcomes in the first year were excluded (depression aHR, 1.10; 95% CI 0.94–1.28; suicide aHR, 0.71; 95% CI 0.45–1.13) and are therefore not conclusive. Dual use was associated with a higher risk of depression (aHR, 1.20; 95% CI 1.01–1.42), whereas estimates for switching were imprecise. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence against smoking cessation.

Article.Title: Hardware-aware SRP-assisted aerial edge computing for low-latency mining IoT under cognitive spectrum sharing
Article.Authors: Darem A.; Karali S.; Alsini R.; Alghushairy O.; Almalki K.; Thanoon M.; Alhashmi A.; Alghawli A.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) in hazardous and topologically constrained environments, such as deep-pit mining, requires low-latency, reliable, and spectrum-aware communication and computing infrastructures. In such environments, terrestrial networks often suffer from severe non-line-of-sight (NLoS) blockage, while spectrum reuse with legacy primary systems imposes cognitive coexistence constraints. This paper proposes a simulation-driven optimization framework that integrates an aerial edge machine (AEM) with a smart reflecting panel (SRP) to support autonomous mining robots. Unlike ideal reflecting-surface models that assume lossless unit-modulus phase shifting, the proposed framework adopts a hardware-constrained SRP model whose phase-dependent amplitude response is fitted to measured varactor-tuned element data, and optimizes the reflection coefficients directly on the resulting non-convex manifold. We formulate a worst-case safety-response-time minimization problem by jointly optimizing quasi-static AEM placement, SRP passive beamforming, uplink transmit-power allocation, AEM computation-frequency allocation, and task-partitioning ratios under statistical interference-temperature-limit (ITL) constraints. The problem is solved by a two-level decomposition in which an outer bisection searches the target latency and an inner block coordinate descent (BCD) loop combines closed-form task and computation updates, primal-dual weighted MMSE power allocation, Riemannian manifold optimization (RMO), and a trust-region successive convex approximation (SCA) for placement. Each surrogate step is accepted only if it does not increase a common violation function, so the monotonicity of the inner loop holds by construction; no global optimality is claimed, and the returned latency is achieved by an explicitly verified feasible configuration that upper-bounds the optimum. At a workload of 3.0 Mbits the framework attains 1.05 s against 6.00 s for local execution, an $$82.5\%$$ reduction, while maintaining Jain’s fairness index above 0.9 and a fading-averaged cognitive safety headroom of 2.5–12.5 dB below the ITL threshold. The achieved latency lies within 0.05 s of the ideal-reflection bound; the analysis attributes this narrow gap not to near-optimal beamforming but to the deployment being edge-computation-limited, with uplink transmission accounting for roughly $$5.5\%$$ of the offloading time, so that the panel’s practical role is insurance against blockage rather than latency reduction. These results delimit the conditions under which hardware-aware and cognition-aware SRP-assisted aerial edge computing benefits mining digital ecosystems and industrial digital-twin deployments.

Article.Title: Assessment of the MOMENTUM sport earbud for multi-parametric physiological tracking and exploratory lactate modeling during incremental exercise
Article.Authors: Camargo D.; Zellhuber I.; Weber M.; Schönfelder M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Continuous monitoring of heart rate (HR) and core temperature ( $$T_c$$ ) is essential for optimizing athletic performance and preventing heat-related illness. However, traditional monitoring methods like chest straps and wrist-worn trackers often face accuracy challenges during exercise due to sweat, motion, and signal interference. Furthermore, few devices offer validated, synchronized HR and $$T_c$$ monitoring during physical exertion. This study validates the MOMENTUM Sport (MSPORT) earbud, a novel multisensor wearable for synchronized HR and $$T_c$$ tracking and investigates its utility in non-invasive blood lactate prediction. Thirty-six healthy adults (19 males, 17 females) performed an incremental cycling ramp test under controlled laboratory conditions. MSPORT HR and $$T_c$$ were validated against Polar H10 and Braun ThermoScan 7 references. Predictive lactate modeling was implemented via a Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) framework, with physiological significance assessed through Linear Mixed Models (LMM) and temporal coupling via cross-correlation analysis. MSPORT showed good inter-device agreement for HR (MAE: 0.89 bpm; RMSE: 1.10 bpm) compared to the Polar H10, and good ear-canal temperature agreement with the Braun ThermoScan 7 (MAE: 0.35 $$^{\circ }$$ C; MAPE: 0.92%). The lactate prediction model achieved a correlation of $$R = 0.84$$ ( $$p < 0.05$$ ), with LMM confirming $$T_c$$ as a highly significant independent predictor ( $$\beta = 11.63$$ , SE = 1.00, $$z = 11.65$$ , $$p < 0.001$$ , 95% CI [9.68, 13.59]), while HR also contributed significantly ( $$\beta = -1.94$$ , SE = 0.29, $$z = -6.78$$ , $$p < 0.001$$ ). The negative HR coefficient likely reflects collinearity or a suppression effect: once cumulative $$\Delta T_c$$ accounts for the metabolic trend, HR becomes a corrective term. Sex was a significant covariate ( $$\beta = -1.25$$ , $$z = -2.00$$ , $$p = 0.046$$ ). The random intercept variance was 1.909, indicating substantial between-participant variability in baseline lactate (model converged; REML). An exploratory cross-correlation analysis suggested a preliminary temporal association between lactate and ear-canal temperature; the precise lag magnitude cannot be reliably estimated from three-minute lactate sampling intervals. Absolute lactate magnitude showed significant sex-based differences ( $$p < 0.05$$ ). The MSPORT earbud provides reliable HR tracking and good ear-canal temperature agreement with a co-located tympanic reference during laboratory cycling. The exploratory lactate model demonstrates group-level association ( $$R = 0.84$$ ) and supports the feasibility of thermal-cardiac signal fusion for metabolic monitoring, though individual-level accuracy remains insufficient for clinical use. Further research is required to assess performance across diverse exercise protocols, environments, and populations.

Article.Title: PAFTI-Net predicts termite infestation risk levels from multivariate gas monitoring data
Article.Authors: Wu S.; Wang H.; Lu W.
Article.Abstract: In response to the problems that traditional termite monitoring is difficult to quantify the degree of invasion and that there are noise interference in multi-temporal data as well as difficulties in jointly modeling local–global patterns, this paper proposes and implements Parallel Adaptive Fusion and Temporal Interaction Network (PAFTI-Net) based on the self-built gas monitoring platform. The model’s front end adopts adaptive feature fusion to dynamically weight CO2, CH4, temperature and humidity, and temporal features; the middle layer constructs three parallel paths: multi-scale convolution, cross-temporal global dependency modeling, and factor-level nonlinear interaction; the back end outputs low, medium, and high risk levels through dynamic fusion. On a structured dataset containing 89 independent experimental batches and 26,820 window samples, the test accuracy of PAFTI-Net reaches 91.50%, and the F1-score is 91.03%. Compared with the optimal baseline model ESD-TripleStream, it has achieved absolute improvements of 2.95% and 2.40% respectively, and a 3.69% increase in recall rate. The results indicate that PAFTI-Net has significant advantages in discriminating termite invasion risk levels under controlled conditions, providing a feasible technical path for intelligent prevention and control based on gas monitoring.

Article.Title: Physician-level variation and concentration of low-value thyroid function testing in german ambulatory care
Article.Authors: Hildebrandt M.; Hueber S.; Schübel J.; Voigt K.; Vogt V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract According to recent guidelines, the measurement of free triiodothyronine (fT3) and free thyroxine (fT4) in the routine monitoring of patients with known hypothyroidism does not offer added value beyond thyrotropin (TSH) testing and is considered low-value care. Understanding variation in low-value testing is essential for informing targeted de-implementation strategies. This study examines physician-level variation and concentration in low-value thyroid function testing in Germany using nationwide ambulatory statutory health insurance data from 2020, comprising 48.2 million cases of common blood tests in 22.2 million patients. We analysed ordering patterns of thyroid function tests (TSH, fT3, fT4) across specialties and individual physicians and assessed the distribution of testing volumes to identify concentration among high-utilising physicians. In total, 12.8 million patients received thyroid function tests (19 million cases), most commonly single TSH measurements (74%) and complete thyroid panels (17%). Among patients with hypothyroidism, 1.3 million TFTs were classified as low-value (0.9 million patients, 84% female), with 80% ordered by general practitioners. Low-value testing was highly concentrated: 27% of physicians accounted for 80% of all low-value thyroid function tests. Higher physician-level volumes of low-value testing were associated with an increased use of complete thyroid panels. These findings indicate substantial unwarranted variation in care and suggest that interventions targeting high-utilising physicians may be particularly effective in reducing unnecessary testing and improving the efficiency of healthcare delivery. The analytic approach used in this study can be applied to administrative data in other healthcare systems.

Article.Title: Beach and coastal structure impacts of infragravity waves during the late december 2023 swells in Southern California
Article.Authors: Stehno A.; Lynett P.; Wesley M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A late December 2023 swell in the Pacific impacted Southern California, generating near-record wave heights in the Santa Barbara Channel. We analyze wave conditions and resulting coastal impacts of this event using offshore buoy data, tide gage records, field observations, and numerical modeling. The storm produced significant infragravity (IG; <0.04 Hz) within local harbors. A “sneaker” wave was observed at Ventura on 28 December, overtopping a beach and seawall during high tide and causing sudden flooding over nearby infrastructure. Post-event surveys documented ~25 m of shoreline retreat and 2 m-high erosion scarp near the Ventura Harbor entrance, as well as damage to the Ventura Harbor breakwater and groin. This event was among the largest events on record at buoy measurements in the Santa Barbara Channel, with a significant wave height of 7.8 m and peak wave height of ~13 m. A Boussinesq wave model revealed resonant oscillation modes in Santa Barbara between 16-21 minutes and Ventura between 16-20 minutes. Modeled amplification of IG waves likely contributed to extreme runup and observed coastal damage, highlighting the effects of long-period wave energy hazard during the extreme swell from this case study event.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: infragravity waves; shoreline retreat; Santa Barbara Channel; Boussinesq wave model; coastal flooding; beach erosion; wave run-up

Article.Title: A lightweight and efficient model for fall-related human movement detection based on improved YOLOv10
Article.Authors: Ma C.; Li M.; Mi J.; Yao J.; Su P.; Zuo Y.
Article.Abstract: Vision-based fall detection is increasingly relevant to assistive healthcare, rehabilitation, and older-adult monitoring; however, practical deployment requires a favorable balance among detection accuracy, model complexity, and inference efficiency. The current study proposes FGLD-YOLO, a lightweight fall detection model derived from YOLOv10. FasterNet replaces the original backbone to reduce computational overhead, while a Generalized Feature Pyramid Network (GFPN) is incorporated into the neck to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion. The modified backbone and neck are further combined with the YOLOv8 detection head to form a hybrid detection architecture. Feature-based knowledge distillation is then applied, using the optimized hybrid detector as the teacher and YOLOv10n as the student, to transfer learned representations to a smaller deployment model. Experiments were conducted on 5,000 images derived from the UR Fall Detection Dataset (URFD) and Fall Detection Dataset (FDD), with training, validation, and test sets partitioned at a ratio of 7:2:1. Compared with YOLOv10, the optimized full FGLD-YOLO model improved mAP50, precision, and recall by 4.2, 4.7, and 8.3% points, respectively, and showed competitive performance against YOLOv8 and YOLOv12. The distilled deployment-oriented student achieved 91.9% mAP50, 87.9% precision, and 85.1% recall, corresponding to gains of 3.1, 4.1, and 3.2% points over YOLOv10. Relative to the optimized full model, the distilled student reduced parameters by 53.2%, GFLOPs by 42.0%, and per-image processing latency by 56.0%. These results indicate an improved accuracy-efficiency trade-off for fall detection on the evaluated datasets and support further investigation of FGLD-YOLO for resource-constrained monitoring and assistive-care applications. Validation in real-world settings and older-adult populations remains necessary before clinical use.
