Article.Title: Functional changes of testicular Sertoli cells induced by prenatal caffeine exposure and their mechanisms
Article.Authors: Kong Z.; Zhang Q.; Cheng P.; Liu Y.; Liu Y.; Jiang P.; Li M.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Our previous studies have shown that prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) can impair the function of testicular Leydig cells in offspring, but its effect on Sertoli cells remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to investigate the changes of inhibited WT1 expression in testicular Sertoli cells induced by PCE in offspring rats and its underlying mechanisms. Pregnant Wistar rats were orally administered with caffeine at doses of 30, 60, and 120 mg/kg·d from gestational day (GD) 9 to 20. The results showed that PCE led to abnormal testicular morphology and decreased expression of Sertoli cell development marker genes (Wt1 and Sox9) in offspring. After birth, the Sertoli cells’ secretory function was impaired (reduced levels of ABP and INH-β), and the expression of blood-testis barrier constituents (Cx43) was decreased. PCE increased sperm deformity and reduced sperm motility at PW12, whereas chronic stress additionally reduced sperm count and further aggravated sperm abnormalities. Under the conditions tested, corticosterone reduced the expression of several Sertoli cell markers in TM4 cells. Caffeine treatment did not significantly change the mRNA levels of these markers. The molecular and cell intervention experiments support a potential role for GR/P300/miR-199a-5p/WT1 signaling in the Sertoli cell changes associated with prenatal caffeine exposure.

Article.Title: HC-MFT: a hierarchical cross-modal fusion transformer for robust and explainable thoracic disease diagnosis
Article.Authors: Imran S.; Ullah K.; Khalid S.; Hussain I.; Karpulevich E.; Markin Y.; Romanov S.
Article.Abstract: Chest radiography (CXR) and computed tomography (CT) provide complementary views of thoracic disease, yet most automated diagnostic models use a single modality. We present HC-MFT, a hierarchical cross-modal fusion transformer that encodes radiographs with a Vision Transformer and CT slices with an EfficientNet-B3–Transformer hybrid, exchanges information between the two token sequences through stacked bidirectional cross-attention, and combines them with a sample-adaptive, dimension-wise gate. Because no public dataset offers patient-matched CXR–CT examinations for the four classes studied, we evaluate the method on class-matched pseudo-pairs built from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and the SARS-CoV-2 CT-Scan Dataset; both image pools are split into training, validation and test partitions before pairing and audited for near-duplicates, and the CT branch is supervised only with the binary label it carries. With an identical training protocol for all models, HC-MFT reached 96.3% accuracy (95% CI [94.7, 97.7]), a macro AUC of 0.989 and a macro F1 of 0.963 on 600 test pairs covering COVID-19, lung opacity, viral pneumonia and normal radiographs, and a macro F1 of 0.957 ± 0.004 across 5 random splits. HC-MFT was the most accurate and most stable model, but its advantage over the strongest fusion baselines was not statistically significant. Pairing controls showed that the trained model relies almost entirely on the radiograph, and a quantitative saliency analysis revealed substantial attention outside the lung fields, which suggests source-related shortcuts. HC-MFT is therefore a competitive computational fusion framework; clinical use requires validation on genuinely paired, multi-centre cohorts

Article.Title: Advancing coral reef ecology and restoration by understanding the ecological mechanisms that generate resilience
Article.Authors: Strychar K.; Studivan M.
Article.Abstract: Coral reef science has entered a defining decade in which accelerating environmental change is reshaping both reef ecosystems and the scientific approaches used to understand and conserve them. Climate warming, ocean temperature changes, ocean acidification, emerging diseases, declining water quality, and other anthropogenic pressures are altering biodiversity, ecosystem function, and the capacity of coral populations to recover naturally. In response, coral reef ecology and restoration have become increasingly integrated disciplines, with ecological understanding providing the foundation for more predictive and adaptive interventions. The studies presented in this Scientific Reports Collection illustrate this transformation through three interconnected themes: understanding the ecological mechanisms that generate resilience, applying ecological knowledge to strengthen those mechanisms through restoration, and measuring restoration success through ecosystem recovery rather than coral survival alone. Together, these contributions demonstrate that successful restoration depends on rebuilding the processes that sustain biodiversity, structural complexity, ecosystem function, and adaptive capacity under continued environmental change. Integrating ecological theory, restoration practice, technological innovation, and adaptive management will be essential for sustaining resilient reef ecosystems in an increasingly uncertain future.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: coral reef restoration; coral reef resilience; coral disease; ecosystem functioning; ocean acidification; climate change impacts on coral reefs; ecosystem recovery; adaptive management

Article.Title: Classical baselines match spatio-temporal graph neural networks for groundwater quality index prediction under matched tuning budgets
Article.Authors: Shehab Z.
Article.Abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks (ST-GNNs) have been proposed for predicting the Water Quality Index (WQI) of groundwater, but published comparisons rarely control task formulation, tuning effort or evaluation uncertainty. A gated ST-GNN, recurrent networks and classical baselines were therefore benchmarked on 352 monitoring stations observed in three annual post-monsoon campaigns. An analytic sanity check first confirms that the same-season task common in this literature reconstructs a known formula, ordinary least squares recovering the index from contemporaneous hydrochemistry at R² = 0.99997. With every model given an identical budget of 100 random-search trials inside each of 25 station-grouped cross-validation folds, and all preprocessing fitted on training stations only, a tuned Random Forest, a recurrent network and the ST-GNN were indistinguishable in classification (macro-F1 0.856, 0.844 and 0.848) and in hazardous-class recall, and a tuned support vector machine attained the lowest regression error; hazardous-class comparisons rest on only 16 stations. Within the three campaigns available, prior campaigns gave at most small gains, smaller than the variation between resamples, and only when current laboratory chemistry was incomplete. No graph constructible from the monitoring data, whether geographic, hydrochemical or combined, significantly improved on the same model without message passing, although dependence within 10 km was detectable. In a deployable laboratory-triage scenario, no model improved significantly on ranking wells by their previous laboratory result, which captured 2.4 times as many fluoride exceedances as random ordering in the first fifth of analyses. Attribution rankings followed the weighting of the chosen index, fluoride leading only under inverse-limit weighting. These conclusions are specific to a short, sparse panel and to the graphs and tuning protocol evaluated; they define the comparisons required before architectural advantages can be claimed rather than showing that spatio-temporal learning lacks value for groundwater quality.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: spatio-temporal graph neural networks; groundwater quality index; support vector machine; recurrent neural networks; groundwater quality classification

Article.Title: Research through evaluation for large language models in patient-clinician communications
Article.Authors: Hao Y.; Holmes J.; Hobson J.; Bennett A.; McKone E.; Ebner D.; Routman D.; Shiraishi S.; Patel S.; Yu N.; Hallemeier C.; Ball B.; Kalantari S.; Ghassemi M.; Waddle M.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to draft replies to patient messages, but the methods available for evaluating such drafts were developed for other kinds of systems, and expert evaluators are difficult to recruit at the scale that LLM output requires. We propose Research through Evaluation (RtE), an iterative approach in which the evaluation metrics and the grading rubric are developed together with the clinicians who apply them. We applied RtE in a retrospective comparative study of 158 prostate cancer patient inquiries, comparing replies written by the clinical care team with replies generated by a GPT-4-based in-basket bot. Three rounds of human evaluation with clinical professionals (Rounds 1–3) were followed by a fourth round in which four LLM graders scored the same responses with the final rubric. Across the human rounds, the design moved from disclosed-source comparison to randomized single-blind grading, Conciseness was replaced by Clarity and Trustworthiness by Empathy, and items on editing effort and time to answer were added. In the final clinician evaluation, clinical care team replies scored higher on Completeness, Correctness and Clarity, in-basket bot replies scored higher on Empathy, and in-basket bot replies more often needed major editing. All four LLM graders rated the in-basket bot replies more favourably than the clinical care team replies, and their absolute agreement with one another was low (Krippendorff's alpha 0.07–0.18) compared with that of the clinician graders (0.53–0.81). RtE produced a documented evaluation instrument in which every revision can be traced to the round that prompted it, and the results indicate that zero-shot LLM graders cannot yet replace clinician evaluation in this setting.
Article.Topic: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

Article.Title: Sensory reweighting and proximal muscle reorganization underlie postural control after unilateral lower limb amputation
Article.Authors: Krauskopf T.; Ott C.; Herget G.; Kubosch E.; Häberlin M.; Maurer C.; Stieglitz T.; Pasluosta C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Individuals with lower limb amputation face substantial challenges in maintaining postural stability, leading to an increased risk of falls and injury. However, the compensatory sensorimotor adaptations developed following limb loss remain poorly characterized. We quantified sensory reweighting and motor compensation strategies via postural modeling and neurophysiological measurements. We conducted perturbed standing experiments to model postural control in transfemoral (TFA) and transtibial (TTA) unilateral amputees. The model quantified proprioceptive weighting ( W p ) and neural controller parameters ( K p and K d ) using a single inverted pendulum. Transfer function analysis was used to describe gain and phase shifts in the relationship between the external perturbations and the Center of Mass (CoM) responses. Non-negative matrix factorization assessed muscle synergies of lower body muscles. We observed a pronounced reduction in the proprioceptive contributions to postural control in the TFA group with eyes open ( W p ≈ 30% in TFA vs. W p ≈ 70% in able-bodied controls). Despite sensory re-weighting, the motor system gain was preserved in both amputee groups, while TFA showed frequency-dependent phase differences mainly when vision was unavailable. We further observed altered muscle synergies in the amputee groups, with increased proximal leg (rectus femoris) contributions, a redistribution of trunk muscle contributions between synergies and condition-specific reductions of intact-side soleus contributions. Yet, the relative activation of synergies was comparable across groups. These findings suggest that postural instability in unilateral lower limb amputees arises from sensory deficits compensated by a proximal shift in muscle recruitment, preserving the amplitude of the motor responses but introducing temporal coordination constraints.

Article.Title: Enhancing the optical properties of chitosan using natural dye extracted from purple radish peels (Raphanus sativus L.): a non-destructive spectroscopic study
Article.Authors: Ahmed B.; Mamand D.; Aziz D.; Muheddin D.; Hussein A.; Aziz S.
Article.Abstract: In the current work natural dyes extracted from radish peels were used to improve the absorption properties of chitosan (CS) biopolymer. Non-destructive technique such as FTIR and UV-vis were used to study the structural and optical properties, respectively. The Urbach and Taucs regions were identified from the absorption coefficient versus photon energy. The refractive index was enhanced in the dye-doped CS films. The energy gap dropped for the doped films compared to neat CS film. The UV-shielding efficiencies of pure CS, CS4, and CS8 were calculated as 16.71%, 44.12%, and 52.96%, respectively, demonstrating enhanced UV-blocking performance with increasing radish peel extract dye concentration. The optical dielectric properties were used to identify some of the significant optical parameters like N/m and optical energy band gap. The steepness (beta) and the electron-phonon interaction strength ( \(\:{E}_{e-ph}\) ) parameters were determined. The W-D model provided the dispersion energy ( \(\:{E}_{d}\) ) and effective single oscillator energy ( \(\:{E}_{o}\) ). Optical dielectric properties were determined to study SELF (surface energy loss function) and VELF (volume energy loss function). Linear electric susceptibility and electronic polarizability were examined with the help of the parameter of refractive index. Basicity and electronegativity optical errors Pure and dye-doped CS films were considered to calculate optical electronegativity and optical basicity. The nonlinear optical susceptibility of second order which deals with the generation of second harmonics and nonlinear optical susceptibility of third order were theoretically estimated to determine the NLO refractive index. The phase velocity ( \(\:{v}_{p}\) ) associated with the decrease in light speed inside the material in the CS-doped films. The sheet resistance ( \(\:{R}_{s}\) ), thermal emissivity ( \(\:{\epsilon\:}_{th}\) ), and figure of merit (φ) were theoretically estimated using Kirchhoff-based equations rather than measured directly.

Article.Title: Regularized population proportion estimation under ranked set sampling: a ridge logistic regression approach
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Sinha R.; Singh H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ridge regression is an effective approach for addressing multicollinearity in statistical estimation by stabilizing regression coefficients when multiple auxiliary variables are highly correlated. This article proposes a hybrid ridge logistic regression-assisted model for finite population proportion estimation under concomitant-based Ranked Set Sampling (CRSS). The proposed model combines observed responses with predictions from a ridge logistic regression, thereby exploiting multiple auxiliary variables while mitigating the effects of multicollinearity. A bootstrap resampling scheme designed for Ranked Set Sampling is adopted for variance estimation and statistical inference. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations under varying sample sizes, correlation structures, and dimensions of auxiliary variables, including additional moderate levels of multicollinearity. Applications to the Body Fat and Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer datasets are presented to demonstrate its practical utility. The results generally show lower bias and mean squared error and higher relative efficiency than existing estimators, particularly under severe multicollinearity. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating ridge-regularized logistic regression with CRSS for finite population proportion estimation using multiple auxiliary variables.

Article.Title: An artificial intelligence–driven predictive model for EPclin risk assessment (ENDOPREDICT test) in HER2-negative luminal breast cancer
Article.Authors: Lembege N.; Le V.; Alran L.; Brunet M.; Larmonier C.; Sentis J.; Truffaux N.; Andrieu M.; Velasco V.; Ulliel D.; Chakiba C.; Auriol S.; Haik L.; Blaye C.; Saut O.; MacGrogan G.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prognostic stratification is essential for guiding adjuvant treatment decisions in HER2-negative luminal breast cancer. Artificial intelligence applied to digital histopathology offers an opportunity to extract complementary information for molecular risk assessment. We developed a multimodal deep learning model combining whole-slide histopathological images, tumor size, and nodal status to predict ENDOPREDICT EPclin risk groups in 768 patients, including an Internal cohort (n = 256) and a multicenter External cohort (n = 512). Cross-cohort testing yielded AUCs of 0.74 for the Internal-trained model tested on the External cohort and 0.77 for the External-trained model tested on the Internal cohort, compared with 0.715 and 0.702 for the clinical-only model, respectively. Improvement was significant in the Internal test cohort (paired DeLong p = 0.0079), but not the External test cohort (p = 0.145). Pooled 10-fold cross-validation yielded AUCs of 0.787 and 0.789 for patients originating from the Internal and External cohorts, respectively, demonstrating moderate and relatively consistent discrimination. High-risk predictions had PPVs of 88.8–93.4%, sensitivities of 56.7–64.9%, and NPVs of 37.3–47.8%. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of EPclin risk prediction from digitized histopathological slides and clinical variables. The potential incremental contribution of image-derived features warrants further investigation and prospective multicenter validation.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic modulation of biofortified spinach through foliar application of lemon-derived vesicles and nanoencapsulated selenium
Article.Authors: Gomez-Molina M.; Yepes-Molina L.; Olmos-Ruiz R.; Carvajal M.
Article.Abstract: Selenium biofortification of crops is an effective strategy to address micronutrient deficiencies, although its efficiency is often limited by suboptimal uptake and phytotoxicity. In this study, we investigated the use of lemon-derived vesicles as nanocarriers for the foliar delivery of selenate in spinach ( Spinacia oleracea L.), aiming to enhance selenium accumulation while determining its effects on plant physiology. Plants were treated with free or nanoencapsulated selenate, and physiological, metabolic, and transcriptomic responses were evaluated. Nanoencapsulation of selenium in vesicles significantly improved Se accumulation in leaves, resulting in more than twofold increase compared with free selenate application. Molecular analyses revealed that selenium enrichment was associated with the activation of glutathione-related pathways and reduced proline levels. In addition, vesicle application also induced phenylpropanoid metabolism and nutrient reservoir-related genes, alongside changes in redox-related responses. Notably, vesicles alone promoted plant growth, increasing both fresh and dry weight, whereas selenium-loaded vesicles only increased fresh weight. Vesicle application also modulated secondary metabolism, including hesperidin accumulation. These findings suggest that lemon-derived vesicles could serve as an efficient selenium delivery system, offering a promising approach for foliar selenium biofortification of spinach. However, further studies are needed to assess the scalability of this approach, its field performance, and formulation shelf life.

Article.Title: Cinnamaldehyde against hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: in vitro and in silico insights into antibacterial, anti-biofilm, and gene expression modulating effects
Article.Authors: Chegini Z.; Kareem Tuama F.; Kashi M.; Akbari M.; Shariati A.
Article.Abstract: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) has emerged as a concerning global pathogen. hvKp is more virulent than classical K. pneumoniae (cKp) and capable of causing community-acquired infections, often in healthy individuals. The increasing prevalence of biofilm-forming, carbapenem-resistant hvKp (CR-hvKp) has created an urgent need for alternative antimicrobial agents. This study investigated the antibacterial, antibiofilm, and underlying mechanisms of cinnamaldehyde against CR-hvKp isolates. Antibacterial activity was evaluated using disk diffusion and broth macrodilution assays. Antibiofilm activity was assessed by crystal violet biofilm biomass quantification and biofilm metabolic activity assays. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was performed to examine ultrastructural changes. The expression of biofilm-associated genes was analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), and molecular docking was conducted to evaluate the interaction of cinnamaldehyde with key biofilm-related proteins. Cinnamaldehyde exhibited potent antibacterial activity against CR-hvKp isolates, producing a mean inhibition zone diameter of 34 ± 1 mm and a mean MIC of 48 ± 18.4 µg/mL. The biomass of mature biofilms decreased by 53% and 73% following treatment with cinnamaldehyde at 2× and 4× MIC, respectively, while metabolic activity decreased by approximately 48% and 65%, respectively. SEM analysis revealed severe cell envelope damage, membrane disruption, and marked biofilm structural deterioration. qRT-PCR demonstrated significant downregulation of the biofilm-associated genes mrkD and fimH . Molecular docking predicted favorable binding affinities ranging from − 6.8 to − 4.9 kcal/mol across the tested targets, with the strongest affinity observed for the type 3 fimbrial adhesin MrkD (− 6.8 kcal/mol). Its observed mechanism of action highlights its promise as a potential component of future therapeutic formulations and supports further investigation for combating antimicrobial resistance.

Article.Title: Fetal fraction of cell-free DNA in ART pregnancies: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Neelakandan A.; Kamath V.; Chacko M.; Kunjummen A.; Chinta P.; Rani N.; Beck M.; Navaneethan P.; Kamath M.
Article.Abstract: The effect of assisted reproductive technology (ART) and related treatment parameters on fetal fraction (FF) remains unclear. This cross-sectional study evaluated FF in pregnant women with singleton gestations at 10–11 weeks who conceived spontaneously, through ovulation induction, or via ART at Christian Medical College and Hospital, Vellore (July 2023 - June 2025). Associations between FF, mode of conception, and ART parameters were assessed using univariate and multivariable regression. The mean Bioanalyzer-estimated FF did not differ significantly between ART and non-ART groups (6.76% vs. 6.09%; P = 0.123) in the unadjusted analysis. After adjustment for maternal age, body mass index (BMI), and gestational age, ART pregnancies showed a significantly higher log-transformed FF compared with non-ART pregnancies (β = +0.17, P = 0.019). Within ART, frozen embryo transfers (FET) were associated with higher log-transformed FF (β = +0.19, P = 0.010). The strongest association was noted in modified natural FET cycles (β = +0.332, P = 0.002). No significant associations were observed with the number or day of embryos transferred. Although a higher mean FF was observed following blastocyst transfer, the difference did not reach statistical significance. Preliminary findings from the current study demonstrate associations between mode of conception and FF.

Article.Title: DFlee: a scalable agent-based framework for simulating flood-induced population displacement across multiple flood scenarios
Article.Authors: Jahani A.; Puma M.; Harbach L.; Ghorbani M.; Suleimenova D.; Xue Y.; Groen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural disasters displace millions of people each year, and effective disaster response requires accurate models of population movement. This study presents DFlee, an agent-based model for flood-induced evacuation built on the Flee framework for conflict-driven displacement. DFlee introduces three key extensions: (i) dynamic integration of evolving, location-specific flood conditions into agent decision-making; (ii) risk-sensitive destination selection accounting for flood severity, shelter inundation risk, and accessibility; and (iii) recession-driven short-term return-to-origin. Synthetic scenarios with recurrence intervals ranging from 10 to over 100 years represent minor and major riverine floods, coastal storm surges, and compound flooding. Validation combines empirical comparison against the 2022 Bauchi flood in Nigeria with behavioural validation of three stylised facts: preference for nearby safe destinations, short-term return to origin as flood conditions improve, and heterogeneous evacuation timing. Across scenarios, approximately 84–91% of evacuees select the nearest safe destination, while returns to origin begin promptly as flood conditions recede, with cumulative returns within the simulated window limited by late-peaking displacement dynamics. These behaviours persist across a tenfold increase in population size, and ARCHER2 experiments simulate 16 million agents in under one minute on a single compute node and around five seconds on 32 nodes, supporting uncertainty quantification, scenario exploration, and humanitarian planning.

Article.Title: Determinants of quality of life and pulmonary function decline in Pseudomonas aeruginosa-colonised bronchiectasis: a longitudinal study
Article.Authors: Bueno-Freire L.; Alcaraz-Serrano V.; Oscanoa-Huamán P.; López-Aladid R.; Vázquez N.; López-Gavin A.; Scioscia G.; Gabarrús A.; Ceccato A.; Cabrera R.; Ferrer M.; Soler N.; Fernández-Barat L.; Torres A.
Article.Abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) colonisation is a key prognostic factor in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (BE), associated with pulmonary exacerbations (PE), lung function decline, and poorer health-related quality of life (HRQoL). We aimed to identify clinical and microbiological determinants of HRQoL and pulmonary function decline over one year in PA-colonised BE. We followed sixty-eight PA-colonised BE adults assessing HRQoL (QoL-B v3.1) and spirometry quarterly. Linear mixed-effects models and logistic regression examined body mass index (BMI), colonisation status, PA sputum phenotype, frequency of PE/previous year, and pulmonary function phenotype. Lower BMI was associated with early decline across Physical (β 1.52 [0.69], p = 0.029), Health Perceptions (1.67 [0.59], p = 0.005), and Respiratory Symptoms (1.26 [0.56], p = 0.025) HRQoL domains. Chronic colonisation contributed to early Physical (-17.58 [6.99], p = 0.013) and Social Function (-13.73 [5.86], p = 0.020) decline, while mucoid PA predicted early Physical Function worsening (-15.60 [6.53], p = 0.018). Non-obstructive BE was linked to six-month deterioration in Vitality (-17.17 [8.61], p = 0.047), Social Function (-21.02 [8.69], p = 0.017), and Respiratory Symptoms (-13.28 [6.00], p = 0.028). Mucoid PA and ≥1PE/year were the most consistent predictors of multidomain HRQoL deterioration. These determinants were also associated with forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁)/forced vital capacity (FVC) decline. These findings identify factors associated with deterioration in PA-colonised BE, which may inform closer clinical follow-up.

Article.Title: Reliability improvement of distribution networks through optimal recloser placement considering photovoltaic resource allocation and sizing with protection coordination constraints
Article.Authors: Hajiabadi M.; Ramezani H.; Tarsa R.; Lotfi H.; Nejad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated optimization framework for the optimal placement of reclosers and the simultaneous determination of the location and capacity of photovoltaic (PV) units in distribution networks. Unlike conventional approaches that treat the placement of protection devices and PV allocation as separate planning problems, the proposed method addresses both problems simultaneously and evaluates the impact of PV integration on protection performance and network reliability. Within this framework, recloser placement aims to improve reliability indices, including SAIFI, SAIDI, and ENS, while the locations of PV units and the maximum hosting capacity are determined subject to network voltage constraints. In addition, the coordination constraint between the recloser and cut-out fuse is incorporated into the objective function as a penalty term to ensure proper protection coordination and maintain the fuse-saving strategy. The optimization problem is solved using a search algorithm, and the proposed method is evaluated on the IEEE 33-bus test system. In Scenario 2, Bus 29 is identified as the optimal location for a PV unit with a capacity equivalent to 70% of the total network load, resulting in an improved voltage profile. In Scenario 3, with the recloser optimally placed on Line 1, the ENS, SAIFI, and SAIDI values are 36.82 (MWh/yr), 5.58 (int/cus/yr) and 9.12 (h/cus/yr), respectively. Furthermore, the short-circuit analysis of faults downstream of the cut-out fuses confirms that the recloser–fuse coordination constraint is satisfied both with and without PV integration. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can simultaneously optimize recloser placement and PV allocation while maintaining proper protection coordination and the fuse-saving strategy. It also enables an increase in PV hosting capacity subject to voltage constraints and improves network reliability.

Article.Title: Mandibular bone dimensions for miniscrew placement in different facial biotypes assessed by cone-beam computed tomography
Article.Authors: Cuji Paguay A.; Vaca Zapata M.; Aguirre Balseca M.; Freitas K.; Arias N.
Article.Abstract: To assess mandibular buccal cortical thickness, buccolingual alveolar thickness, and interradicular distance across facial biotypes, interradicular sites, and measurement depths using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). This cross-sectional study included 150 patients aged 15–35 years classified by the Ricketts VERT index as mesofacial ( n = 50), dolichofacial ( n = 40), severe dolichofacial ( n = 11), brachyfacial ( n = 24), or severe brachyfacial ( n = 25). Bilaterally averaged measurements were obtained at four mandibular interradicular sites and at 4, 6, and 8 mm apical to the alveolar crest (1,800 observations per outcome). Three linear mixed-effects models included patient-level random intercepts and fixed effects for biotype, depth, site, age, and biotype-by-depth interaction. Compared with 4 mm, measurements at 8 mm showed significantly greater interradicular distance (β = 0.449 mm; p < 0.001), buccal cortical thickness (β = 0.136 mm; p = 0.001), and buccolingual alveolar thickness (β = 0.704 mm; p = 0.001). Compared with the canine–first premolar region, the first–second molar region exhibited greater interradicular distance (β = 2.157 mm), buccal cortical thickness (β = 1.435 mm), and buccolingual alveolar thickness (β = 3.413 mm; all p < 0.001). Mandibular bone dimensions vary by anatomical site and depth, with depth-related differences across facial biotypes for cortical and buccolingual thickness. These anatomical findings support individualized miniscrew site assessment; clinical stability and success were not evaluated.

Article.Title: Combined association of sedentary time and gait speed with falls and fractures in older Chilean adults
Article.Authors: Ferrero-Hernández P.; Farías-Valenzuela C.; de Victo E.; Poblete-Aro C.; Ferrari G.
Article.Abstract: Falls are a major public health concern among older adults, frequently leading to fractures, hospitalization, and reduced quality of life. This study examined the combined association of sedentary time and self-reported gait speed with past-year falls and lifetime fracture history in older Chilean adults. Cross-sectional data from the 2016–2017 Chilean National Health Survey included 1517 older adults. Sedentary time (≥ 4, < 4 h/day), gait speed (slow, medium, fast), falls, and fractures were self-reported. Participants were grouped into six combined sedentary time and gait speed categories. Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for sex, age, marital status, and financial stress, estimated combined associations; sedentary time × gait speed interactions were tested. No significant sedentary time × gait speed interaction was found for falls ( p = 0.243) or fractures ( p = 0.433). Lower sedentary time with medium gait speed was associated with higher odds of falls (OR = 1.99, 95%CI 1.40–2.82). For fractures, lower sedentary time combined with fast (OR = 2.49, 95%CI 1.46–4.26) or medium gait speed (OR = 1.53, 95%CI 1.06–2.21) was associated with higher odds, although this estimate showed limited precision. Combined sedentary time and self-reported gait speed profiles, rather than a statistical interaction, may help characterize falls and fracture risk in older Chilean adults.

Article.Title: Clinical biomarker profiles of adults attending private health screening in the UK and Ireland
Article.Authors: Watt J.; Irvine A.; Kurth M.; Mooney L.; Rice C.; Lamont J.; Fitzgerald P.; Dowey L.; Ruddock M.
Article.Abstract: Private health screening is increasingly used by adults who consider themselves well, yet how often it detects out-of-range results is poorly characterised. In this retrospective observational study, clinical, anthropometric, questionnaire and laboratory data were analysed for 18,042 adults aged 18 or older who attended Randox Health Clinics between January and December 2025. Results were classified against predefined thresholds; missing data were not imputed. Overall, 66% of attendees reported no known disorders. However, 20% had blood pressure in the hypertensive range, 58% had elevated total cholesterol, 16% were obese, and 15% met criteria for metabolic syndrome. Iron deficiency (13.0%) and anaemia (5.9%) were frequent, particularly in younger females, and 18.0% of those tested had raised lipoprotein(a). Obesity, diabetes and hypertension were less common than in national survey data, whereas raised cholesterol was more common. Participants were self-selected and not followed up, so the clinical significance of these results is unknown. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish whether early detection improves outcomes. We describe the prevalence of abnormal biomarkers and early risk states among adults attending private health screening in the UK and Ireland.

Article.Title: Acquisition-related variability in widefield circumferential limbal OCT angiography
Article.Authors: Hafner M.; Kessler C.; Reinstein U.; Priglinger S.; Priglinger C.; Gerhardt M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantitative anterior segment optical coherence tomography angiography (AS-OCTA) may provide biomarkers of limbal ischemia, inflammation, and treatment response, but acquisition variability may obscure biological change. We quantified differences in widefield circumferential limbal vascular metrics across ocular-surface exposure techniques. In this prospective repeated-measures study, 26 healthy right eyes underwent duplicate scans under six sequential conditions: natural viewing, lower-lid retraction, topical anesthesia immediately and after 2 and 7 min, and speculum-assisted imaging. Vessel area density (VAD) and vessel length density (VLD) were prespecified primary outcomes within a 1.5-mm annular limbal region. Lower-lid retraction did not differ from natural viewing. Immediately after anesthesia, VLD was 0.14 mm $$^{-1}$$ higher than during natural viewing (simultaneous 95% CI, 0.02–0.25; Holm-adjusted $$P=0.008$$ ), while VAD increased by 1.22 percentage points ( $$P=0.046$$ ). Both remained stable through 7 min. During final speculum-assisted imaging, VAD and VLD were 3.59 percentage points and 0.57 mm $$^{-1}$$ higher than during natural viewing (both $$P<0.001$$ ), corresponding to within-eye increases of 10.1% and 19.1%. Quantitative limbal AS-OCTA therefore differs materially by acquisition state. Standardizing anesthetic protocol, exposure technique, timing, and limbal sector is essential for longitudinal and multicenter biomarker studies.

Article.Title: Association between forward head posture and neck and upper-back stiffness
Article.Authors: Shibasaki S.; Sei Y.; Harashima K.; Ohnishi H.; Watanabe T.; Sakata K.; Kishino T.
Article.Abstract: Trapezius muscle (TM)-related neck and upper-back stiffness has been attributed to forward head posture (FHP), but the association remains uncertain. Subjects with stiffness-related symptoms exhibit decreased transverse cervical artery (TCA) flow into the TM and increased intermuscular length between the sternocleidomastoid and levator scapulae muscles around the accessory nerve. This cross-sectional study examined whether FHP is independently associated with symptom presence, and also investigated TCA hemodynamics, TM hardness and intermuscular length on sonography. The study population comprised 67 healthy men (mean age, 22 ± 3 years). FHP was diagnosed based on craniovertebral angle (CVA). Symptom presence was determined from questionnaires. Comparisons were performed concerning the presence or absence of FHP and neck and upper-back stiffness. Multiple logistic regression analysis was used to confirm factors contributing to stiffness-related symptoms. Greater intermuscular length was associated with a higher likelihood of symptoms ( p = 0.006, odds ratio [OR] 4.00, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47–10.80), whereas higher peak systolic velocity in the TCA was associated with lower likelihood of symptoms ( p = 0.036, OR 0.95, 95%CI 0.91–1.00). CVA was not significantly associated with neck and upper-back stiffness. FHP was not independently associated with the presence of neck and upper-back stiffness in this cohort.

This post hoc exploratory analysis compared outcomes by age at avelumab initiation (<​75 vs. ≥​75 [main] and <​80 vs. ≥​80 years [supportive]). Article.Authors: Hoseyniniya S.; Khosravifard N.; Shahmalekpour A.; Babaee Hemmati Y.; Dalili Kajan Z.; Ghaffari M.
Article.Abstract: This cross-sectional study assessed the association between soft palate morphology and Need’s ratio across operationally defined sagittal skeletal groups. Leaf-shaped and Crooked morphologies were the most and least frequent configurations, respectively. Neither morphology distribution nor Need’s ratio differed significantly among skeletal groups ( p = 0.204 and p = 0.971, respectively). Among morphology subgroups with n ≥ 3, Need’s ratio differed by morphology in skeletal Class II and Class III ( p < 0.001 and p = 0.041, respectively); these associations persisted after age adjustment ( p < 0.001 and p = 0.044). Across the full sample, age showed a weak positive correlation with Need’s ratio ( r = 0.145, p = 0.008). No statistically significant between-group difference in Need’s ratio was detected within the study’s operational skeletal definitions. Morphology-related differences were observed within Class II and III groups. These findings characterize static anatomical variation and do not establish velopharyngeal dysfunction, airway impairment, speech abnormalities, or sleep-disordered breathing.

Article.Title: Imbalance aware modelling of road crash severity for transport safety policy
Article.Authors: Mohd Azami M.; Misro M.; Hamidun R.
Article.Abstract: Road traffic crashes remain a major safety and sustainability challenge in Malaysia. Fatal and serious crashes impose a disproportionate burden in terms of mortality and long-term social costs. Identifying these high-severity outcomes is difficult due to the strong imbalance in crash severity data and the tendency of conventional models to prioritise overall accuracy. This study analyses Selangor crash database covering the period 2012–2020 to examine how imbalance-aware modelling strategies affect the identification of severe crash outcomes. Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machine models are evaluated using different class balancing approaches, including random undersampling, synthetic oversampling, and class weighting. Model performance is assessed using both overall and class-specific metrics, with particular attention to sensitivity to fatal and serious crashes. The application of class-balancing techniques improved the detection of serious-crash cases across all machine learning models. Among the balanced configurations, the Random Forest model with class weighting achieved the highest overall accuracy (81.66%) while improving the recall of serious-crash cases to 20.53%, compared with the initial model performance. Feature analysis indicates that collision type and road surface type are key factors associated with crash severity. Motorcycles below 250 cc, widely used in shared and informal mobility services, are found to be overrepresented in fatal and serious crashes. The findings highlight the limitations of accuracy-focused modelling for policy analysis and underscore the need for evaluation approaches that prioritise high-risk outcomes when designing targeted road safety interventions.

Article.Authors: Hashemi Soudmand B.; Mohsenzadeh R.
Article.Abstract: Generating dense periodic representative volume elements (RVEs) with prescribed particle sizes challenges random sequential adsorption (RSA) as admissible insertion space becomes fragmented. A Void-Guided Particle Packing (VGPP) workflow was proposed for two-dimensional monodisperse disks combining periodic distance-transform void mapping, stochastic insertion and rearrangement, fixed-final-radius densification, collective relaxation, and periodic overlap auditing. Across 20 realizations per target, VGPP attained area fractions from 0.40 to 0.70, whereas periodic RSA reached targets only through 0.50 and saturated near 0.54. Focused experiments generated valid configurations at an area fraction of about 0.76; the maximum attainable fraction remains undetermined. Controlled comparisons showed that distance-transform-weighted and uniform random candidate-sampling variants also reached every target investigated when the shared growth-and-relaxation procedure was retained. A collision-driven Lubachevsky–Stillinger (LS) benchmark independently demonstrated dense packing, with two realizations at 0.74 reaching computational budgets before completion. All 140 realizations in a domain-size, particle-radius, and grid-resolution sensitivity study achieved their prescribed targets. Increasing particle concentration was associated with lower local area-fraction heterogeneity and stronger short-range order, with relatively small structural differences among candidate-selection strategies. All accepted configurations satisfied a 10⁻⁸ model-length-unit periodic overlap tolerance. The framework provides geometrically verified periodic microstructures and quantified spatial descriptors for subsequent micromechanical analysis.

Article.Title: PEN: balancing energy and performance in NVM-based systems via DVFS with minimal wear-out
Article.Authors: Tobar M.; Siddhu L.; Wedeck P.; Bauer L.; Nassar H.; Hölscher N.; Hakert C.; Chen J.; Henkel J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Edge devices are highly resource-constrained, requiring careful management of both energy efficiency and latency. Dynamic Voltage-Frequency Scaling (DVFS) is widely used to balance this trade-off and improve system performance. However, when Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) serves as the main memory, offering high density and low power consumption, DVFS can accelerate memory wear and reduce the useful lifetime. To address this, we propose PEN : a p olicy for e nergy–performance –efficient operation of N VM-based systems via DVFS while respecting memory lifetime constraints. PEN minimizes refreshes caused by system deceleration and takes advantage of acceleration to enable faster write modes, enhancing both lifetime and performance beyond what DVFS alone can achieve. Unlike previous approaches, PEN accounts for multicore-induced non-deterministic slowdowns and incorporates a low-overhead fallback refresh mechanism to preserve data integrity. Our results show that PEN improves Energy Delay Product (EDP) and NVM lifetime by 24.5% and 33%, respectively, compared to the state of the art.

Article.Title: Quality-screened GNSS benchmarking finds limited distance-graph gains for landslide displacement forecasting
Article.Authors: Zhong B.; Tan Q.; Zhang Y.; Yuan J.; Wu L.; Huang M.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Ground-based Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) networks can track landslide motion at hourly resolution, but missing records and uneven station quality complicate multi-station forecasting. We used a long-term Huangtupo landslide monitoring record to test whether a distance-graph prior improves displacement-increment forecasts after retrospective station admission. Shared temporal baselines and graph models were trained with identical inputs, rolling-origin splits, and random seeds. The Shared GRU achieved a mean absolute error of 0.2755 mm, slightly below 0.2774 mm for the Graph-fusion GRU; this 0.0019 mm difference is much smaller than the 0.1 mm record resolution and estimated increment-noise scale. Expanding the quality-screened node set narrowed the branch gap but did not reverse the ranking, and the small early 12 h gap did not persist in later folds. Leave-one-station-out, topology, and coherence controls showed heterogeneous station effects but no stable evidence that admission eligibility or distance proximity ordered graph-specific predictive value. A secondary GNSS/InSAR correspondence screen also found no station clearly separated from stable-ground and permutation controls. For this single slope, retrospectively admitted node set, and distance-graph protocol, the results support quality-screened benchmarking before deploying graph-based landslide forecasting models.

Article.Title: Low-altitude UAV logistics network planning for complex urban environments: a case study of Wuhan
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Wang H.; Yang S.
Article.Abstract: To address insufficient coordination between transfer-node deployment and risk-aware route planning in complex urban environments, this study proposes a two-stage collaborative optimization framework integrating an improved Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) with a risk-weighted Theta* algorithm. First, altitude-specific risk maps are constructed by incorporating population density, building height, and no-fly zones. In the upper stage, DDQN enhanced with NoisyNet and prioritized experience replay (PER) optimizes transfer-node selection and service allocation. In the lower stage, risk-weighted Theta* generates flight routes and feeds path distances and risk costs back to upper-level decisions. A case study in Wuhan is conducted to validate the framework. Compared with baseline DDQN, the complete model increases the mean final reward by 22.3% and reduces the mean number of episodes to convergence by 23.8%. Compared with conventional A*, risk-weighted Theta* reduces total service distance, risk cost, and total cost by 10.5%, 20.1%, and 16.6%, respectively. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively coordinates network layout and risk-aware route planning while balancing economic efficiency, service-load balance, and flight safety, providing methodological support for UAV logistics network planning in complex urban environments.

Article.Title: Mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride fibers: a comparative study
Article.Authors: Tomaszewska-Rolla D.; Szewczyk O.; Martynkien T.; Sotor J.; Kowalczyk M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We present a comparative study of mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride optical fibers driven by a low-noise, Kerr-lens mode-locked Cr:​ZnS laser oscillator delivering ultrashort 35-fs pulses centered at 2300 nm. By investigating three commercial fluoride fibers with varying core geometries, numerical apertures, and chromatic dispersion profiles, we characterize how the magnitude of anomalous dispersion affects the dynamics of spectral broadening and the homogeneity of the supercontinuum. In fibers exhibiting high and steep anomalous dispersion, temporal pulse stretching triggers higher-order soliton fission, resulting in deeply modulated and fragmented spectra. However, combining a flat, near-zero anomalous dispersion profile with tighter spatial mode confinement supports efficient soliton dynamics and prevents early pulse walk-off. This results in the generation of a smooth, octave-spanning supercontinuum. Our experimental results, supported by numerical simulations based on the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation, demonstrate an ultrabroadband mid-infrared spectrum spanning 1600 nm to 5350 nm, with an average output power of 140 mW. These results highlight low-dispersion fluoride fibers pumped by femtosecond solid-state oscillators as a compact, robust platform for high-brightness, broadband mid-infrared light sources well-suited for molecular spectroscopy and trace-gas sensing.

Article.Authors: Kim K.; Kim C.; Choi W.; Hong S.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: In patients with acute hip fracture, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is frequently impractical due to pain and immobility, despite the high prevalence of sarcopenia in this population. In many countries, including the Republic of Korea, pelvic computed tomography (CT) is a standardized diagnostic workup for hip fracture, requiring no additional imaging burden and making psoas muscle volume (PV) an accessible surrogate. This prospective cohort study included 140 patients with hip fracture (28 males, 112 females; aged 49–98 years) who underwent surgery. We evaluated the relationship of PV and appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) with handgrip strength (HGS), and determined whether PV shows a comparable association with HGS relative to ASM. PV showed a stronger correlation with HGS in men ( r = 0.663, p < 0.001) and the total cohort ( r = 0.711, p < 0.001) than ASM, whereas ASM showed a slightly higher correlation in women ( r = 0.438 vs. r = 0.355, p < 0.001). AUC values for discriminating low HGS were comparable between PV and ASM in both sexes, with no statistically significant differences (Steiger’s Z-test and DeLong’s test, all p > 0.05). PV shows an association with HGS comparable to that of ASM, supporting its utility as a feasible alternative muscle mass indicator when DXA is unavailable.

Article.Title: Deep temporal modeling of grain growth and recrystallization kinetics during thermo-mechanical processing
Article.Authors: Shaikh S.; Fu Y.; Frazier W.; Li L.; Choi K.; Xu Z.; Joshi V.; Soulami A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Grain growth and recrystallization are essential microstructural transformations that directly influence the mechanical properties of materials subjected to thermomechanical processing. The processing often involves undertaking several steps which need to be tightly controlled to achieve optimal performance. While physics-based simulations provide valuable insights into processes, and enable predictive control, their reliance on high-throughput experimentation to explore a wide range of processing routes is prohibitively costly due to significant computational demands. To address these challenges, this study introduces a data-driven approach based on Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) to accurately predict the temporal evolution of final grain size, specifically the average (FGS avg ) and maximum (FGS max ) grain size, and the recrystallization fraction (Recry), in an alloy undergoing thermomechanical processing. The proposed TCN model was trained on a dataset compiled from the results of Finite Element Method–Kinetic Monte Carlo (FEM-KMC) simulations, performed under varied process parameters to capture the temporal evolution of critical microstructural features. Under ten-fold cross validation, with performance metrics averaged across all folds, the average R 2 ranged from 0.885 to 0.933, with average NMAE (normalized mean absolute error) of 0.122 for FGS avg , and 0.175 for FGS max , and an average MAE of 0.043 for Recry. These results highlight the potential of integrating machine learning with Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) frameworks for advanced nuclear applications.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: recrystallization fraction; recrystallization kinetics; temporal convolutional network; integrated computational materials engineering; thermomechanical processing; grain growth
Article.TopicFields: Materials Science > Materials Chemistry > Machine Learning in Materials Science; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Metallurgy and Material Forming; Materials Science > Metals and Alloys > Microstructure and mechanical properties

Article.Title: Engineering validation of analytical predictions for strength of equal and unequal legged reinforced concrete L-columns
Article.Authors: Shetty S.; Shetty T.; Marathe S.; R. M S.
Article.Abstract: Structural engineering frameworks frequently demand reinforced concrete (RC) columns capable of resisting complex coupled axial compression and uniaxial flexure. While standard design aids (such as IS 456 and SP 16) provide ultimate load-moment interaction diagrams for symmetric cross-sections, a distinct research gap exists regarding asymmetric, special-shaped L-columns. This study addresses this research gap by developing a simplified, strain-compatibility-based analytical framework to generate non-dimensional design interaction charts for short RC L-columns. These charts are strictly bounded to the specific geometric leg-length ratios, thickness ratios, and reinforcement topologies investigated herein, featuring both equal (450 mm × 450 mm × 210 mm with 12 bars) and unequal (450 mm × 330 mm × 210 mm with 10 bars) leg geometries under varying cross-sectional orientations. The analytical model was evaluated experimentally by subjecting full-scale structural specimens (1.36 m in height) cast with M20 grade concrete (mean 28-day compressive strength of 27.85 MPa) and longitudinal Fe-500 rebar arrays (12 bars of 12 mm diameter for equal-legged; 10 bars of 12 mm diameter for unequal-legged profiles) to eccentric loading within a 200-t loading frame. Investigational results revealed that orienting equal-legged columns with the flange as the highly compressed edge (ELP-1) achieved a balanced moment capacity (Mu) of 117.04 kN-m at an axial load (Pu) of 524.49 kN (neutral axis depth xu = 0.37D), compared to Mu = 102.62 kN-m at Pu = 203.40 kN (xu = 0.50D) for the web-compressed orientation (ELP-2). For unequal legs, orientation UELP-4 yielded a balanced moment capacity of 102.36 kN-m (Pu = 527.62 kN), approximately 92% higher than the corresponding balanced moment capacity of UELP-1 (Mu = 53.35 kN-m, Pu = 414.93 kN), with the comparison made at their respective axial loads; this difference may partly reflect the greater geometric depth along the bending axis. ​ The proposed limit-state analytical framework was compared with empirical results, showing positive experimental-to-analytical differences of approximately 5% to 27% in four of the eight reported L-column comparisons, while the remaining four showed negative differences, discussed with reference to possible local bearing failure. These non-dimensional charts provide a computationally efficient, limit-state-based design aid for optimizing specific asymmetric vertical structural elements in building infrastructure.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: M20 grade concrete; flexural capacity; eccentric loading; IS 456

Article.Title: Identification of language difficulties using explainable AI and multimodal EEG-fMRI brain network biomarkers
Article.Authors: Li H.; Zhong R.; Zhang Q.; Zuo M.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: The Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals identifies language difficulties in children and adolescents. However, the neurobiological underpinnings remain unclear, partly because traditional single-modality neuroimaging fails to capture the multi-scale dynamics of brain function. This study targets individuals aged 5–21 years exhibiting language difficulties identified by low scores on the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals (CELF). It proposes a multimodal spatiotemporal fusion analysis method based on EEG microstates and fMRI brain networks. First, group-level statistical analyses were conducted on the full sample and three age-stratified subgroups of CELF individuals and typically developing controls, to identify significant between-group differences in EEG microstate and fMRI functional connectivity features. Subsequently, based on the selected features, models incorporating all pairwise combinations of seven base algorithms were constructed, and extensive hyperparameter optimization was performed for each architecture, resulting in 4,221 machine learning models. Leave-one-out and five-fold cross-validation were employed to evaluate classification performance in the 173-participant sample. Finally, SHAP, an explainable AI (XAI) technique, was utilized to interpret the core neural features underpinning the optimal model. Under strict nested cross-validation, the fusion model achieved balanced accuracies of 78.4% in the full sample and 86.0%, 87.9%, and 88.1% across the three age subgroups (5–9, 10–13, and 14–17 years); non-nested estimates were higher. Furthermore, statistical and SHAP analyses consistently revealed significant EEG microstate and fMRI connectivity anomalies in the CELF group. This study presents an ensemble model demonstrating high discriminative performance for CELF-identified individuals. More significantly, by integrating statistical and XAI approaches, it elucidates the underlying key neural correlates, thereby providing objective, multimodal evidence for understanding the neurobiological mechanisms of language difficulties.

Article.Title: Preceding meteorological conditions and machine-learning identification of salinity anomalies in the Yangtze Estuary
Article.Authors: Kong Y.; Xin F.; An B.; Ding Y.; Xu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Salinity anomalies in the Yangtze Estuary threaten freshwater supply, but associations with antecedent meteorological conditions remain poorly characterized. Using daily salinity observations from four stations (2021–2024) and ERA5 reanalysis, this study characterizes the seasonal variability of salinity anomalies, examines associated antecedent meteorological conditions, and develops machine-learning models for their retrospective identification. We found that salinity anomalies clustered from September to the following March and were least frequent from May to July. Training-period composites showed warmer conditions and reduced precipitation over the Yangtze River basin 45–90 days before anomalies. At shorter lead times, salinity anomalies were associated with near-surface and lower-tropospheric northerly and easterly wind anomalies and reduced 850 hPa specific humidity. XGBoost and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) models using ten meteorological factors were evaluated on independent 2024 data under single-station and multi-station labels. XGBoost achieved higher recall and F1-score under both schemes, whereas TabPFN had higher precision but detected only about half of anomaly days. SHAP analysis identified precipitation, near-surface temperature, and wind-related factors as important contributors to model-estimated anomaly probabilities. These findings support retrospective identification of salinity anomalies using antecedent meteorological conditions, an approach that remains relatively underexplored in studies of estuarine salinity anomalies.

Article.Title: Between AI usage and academic procrastination among college students through anxiety, self-control, and ai guilt
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: The increasing integration of AI tools in higher education has raised questions about how AI usage is associated with students’ academic behaviors. While AI can enhance efficiency, it may also be associated with greater academic procrastination. Existing studies have explored AI use and learning outcomes, but the psychological pathways underlying this association remain underexamined. Drawing on Self-Regulated Learning Theory and Moral Emotion Theory, this study examined the indirect roles of academic anxiety and self-control in the relationship between AI usage and academic procrastination, while also assessing whether AI guilt moderated these associations. In this cross-sectional survey, 782 students were recruited from two public universities in Guangxi, China, which were selected based on accessibility. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses were performed using PROCESS Models 4 and 7 in SPSS. The results showed that AI usage was positively associated with academic procrastination. Academic anxiety and self-control both showed significant indirect associations, with completely standardized estimates of 0.129 and 0.119, respectively. Together, these indirect associations accounted for approximately 54.87% of the total association. In addition, AI guilt moderated the associations between AI usage and academic anxiety and self-control. Specifically, the positive association between AI usage and academic anxiety was weaker at higher levels of AI guilt, as was the negative association between AI usage and self-control. Within the scope of the variables examined, these findings provide context-specific evidence concerning selected emotional, behavioral, and moral-evaluative processes relevant to the associations among AI usage, academic anxiety, self-control, and academic procrastination among students at the participating universities.

Article.Title: Establishment of a conditional knock-in mouse model for SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase Nsp12
Article.Authors: Naka K.; Ooshima A.; Edyanto A.; Koide T.; Sakaguchi T.; Sotomaru Y.; Koike K.; Sakamoto N.; Wang T.; Ishikawa T.; Kim S.; Sawa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) plays an essential role in replication of RNA viruses, the pathogenic effects of the Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) RdRp Nsp12 remain poorly understood. Here, we generated a conditional knock-in mouse model enabling inducible expression of SARS-CoV-2 Nsp12 in vivo (hereafter referred to as Nsp12 mice). In Nsp12 mice, detectable Nsp12 expression required co-treatment with the integrated stress response (ISR) inhibitors both in vitro and in vivo. Nsp12 induction did not cause overt pneumonia or significant alterations in major immune cell populations, while inhibiting ISR. Intriguingly, a machine learning-based behavioral analysis revealed reduced locomotor activity in female, but not male, Nsp12 mice. This behavioral phenotype was markedly improved by treatment with the RdRp inhibitor EIDD-2801. In the same vein, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed mitochondrial abnormalities in the heart and cerebellum of Nsp12 mice, while Nsp12 expression was not detectable in these organs. These abnormalities were attenuated by EIDD-2801 treatment, suggesting that the RdRp activity of Nsp12 may contribute to mitochondrial dysfunction. Taken together, these results suggest that the viral RdRp Nsp12 may induce systemic tissue dysfunction through inter-organ communication. Although further studies are required to clarify the precise mechanisms underlying these inter-organ effects and to identify the mediators released from Nsp12-expressing cells, our findings open up a novel avenue for the replication-independent pathogenic effects of a single viral factor, SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Nsp12, in vivo.

Article.Title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals sex-specific microglial responses to simulated galactic cosmic radiation without broad inflammatory activation
Article.Authors: Osabutey M.; Calcines-Rodríguez L.; Trojanczyk L.; Olschowka J.; O’Banion M.
Article.Abstract: Long‑duration deep space missions expose astronauts to galactic cosmic radiation (GCR), a complex mixture of high‑ and low‑LET ions that can compromise central nervous system (CNS) health. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, are highly sensitive to radiation, yet their cell‑state adaptations to space‑relevant mixed‑field exposure remain poorly defined. Here, we performed single‑cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of hippocampal and cortical microglia isolated from male and female C57BL/6 J mice 53 days after acute 100 cGy 5‑ion simulated GCR (GCRsim). Behavioral testing showed no overt deficits, but scRNA‑seq revealed subtle, sex‑specific transcriptional remodeling. Male microglia engaged a stress‑adaptive program characterized by upregulation of Fkbp5 , Ddit4 , Adrb1 , and metabolic regulators, with concurrent downregulation of ER chaperone genes. Female microglia displayed a transcriptionally blunted phenotype with selective induction of Fkbp5 , Ccnd3 , Tsc22d3 and Tnfaip2 , and broad downregulation of inflammatory and Nucleotide-binding Oligomerization Domain (NOD)/Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) pathways. Notably, canonical inflammatory or disease‑associated microglia (DAM) signatures were absent, and homeostatic markers ( P2ry12 , Cx3cr1 ) were preserved. FKBP5 immunoreactivity within Iba1 + microglia was significantly increased in both the dentate gyrus and cortex after GCRsim, without any change in total microglial volume. These findings define a non‑inflammatory, sex‑specific microglial response to space‑relevant GCR. This refined understanding of microglial adaptation provides a cellular framework for sex‑informed CNS risk assessment and countermeasure development for deep space travel.

Article.Title: Triglyceride-glucose composite indices and frailty progression in Chinese middle-aged and older adults
Article.Authors: Hu S.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Evidence on the prospective associations between triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-related composite indices and frailty progression remains limited. This study examined five TyG-related indices in relation to frailty and longitudinal trajectories of frailty index (FI). In total, 4,148 baseline nonfrail adults aged at least 45 years had FI assessed at Wave 4 and 4,510 participants had at least three FI assessments for trajectories in China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Five baseline indices including TyG-WHtR, TyG-WWI, TyG-ABSI, TyG-BRI, and TyG-CVAI were examined in tertiles and per 1-standard-deviation increase. Survey- and inverse-probability-weighted modified Poisson models, restricted cubic splines, discrimination assessment, subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. Latent class mixed models were used to identify FI trajectories. Among 4,148 participants, 779 were frail at Wave 4 (134/2,080 initially robust; 645/2,068 initially prefrail). After FDR correction, highest-tertile TyG-WHtR, TyG-WWI, TyG-BRI, and TyG-CVAI were associated with frailty overall [RRs:1.30-1.41, all FDR-adjusted P <0.05]. In prespecified stratified analysis, significant associations with frailty were observed for TyG-WWI and TyG-ABSI in the robust group, whereas for TyG-WHtR, TyG-BRI, and TyG-CVAI in the prefrail group (all FDR-adjusted P <0.05). Besides, TyG-WHtR was associated with the rapidly increasing FI trajectory versus other classes [RR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.17-2.26; FDR adjustedP= 0.028]. The main findings remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. However, adding any single index did not significantly improve model discrimination. Overall, The findings indicated association between TyG-related composite indices and frailty among middle-aged and older Chinese adults without frailty at baseline. Moreover, TyG-WHtR was associated with a rapidly increasing FI trajectory.

Article.Title: Automated spinal abnormality detection using multi-modal medical imaging: a deep learning paradigm
Article.Authors: Jain R.; Dubey S.; Khan V.; Nandan D.; Dubey S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spinal disorders, like herniated discs, spinal stenosis and spondylolisthesis, affect over 540 million people worldwide. However, these disorders are determined based on a manual interpretation of MRI and X-ray images. This is challenging because of the inter-observer variability of (10-30%) and the laborious process involved in the analysis undertaken. This investigation exhibits a consolidated Deep Learning framework that automates the diagnosis of lumbar spine anomalies in medical images taken from multiple modalities, overcoming the limitations of manual diagnosis and single modality approaches. We collected a dataset of 2847 images (1542 MRI and 1305 X-ray) of anonymous patients from four medical centres comprising of four classes, namely Normal, Herniated Disc, Spinal Stenosis, and Spondylolisthesis. The system consists of (1) advanced preprocessing (Gaussian & Bilateral filtering followed by CLAHE), (2) modified U-Net architecture for accurate spinal segmentation with Dice=0.91, (3) Hybrid feature extraction with combination of custom design CNN Layers with transfer learning (ResNet50, VGG19) by feature level fusion, (4) Multi-class Classification. Segmentation is interpretable through attention maps. The proposed method produced 95.2% accuracy (95% CI: 94.1-96.3%), 93.8% Precision, 94.5% Recall, and 94.1% F1 Score with extensive augmentation and 5-fold cross-validation. Our method outperforms standard CNN baselines (+3.7%) and non-segmented methods (+4.1%). The framework consistently performed well on both MRI (96.1%) and X-ray (94.3%) modalities, demonstrating that explicit spinal segmentation merged with hybrid deep learning classification can robustly detect abnormality across multi-modality. The system detects abnormalities in different imaging modalities robustly. Performance is encouraging on MRI (96.1%) and X-ray (94.3%) modalities.

Article.Title: Endometriosis classification using blood plasma through data fusion of Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and high-performance liquid chromatography
Article.Authors: Pavithran M.; Mathew C.; Upadhya R.; Anjali M.; D’Souza J.; Pai M.; Chidangil S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A minimally invasive detection method is highly desirable for endometriosis due to its long diagnostic delay, non-specific symptoms, and invasive diagnostic procedures. This study explored the synergetic application of vibrational spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) and protein profile (HPLC-FLD) analysis of blood plasma samples for the detection of endometriosis. The different feature selection tools, such as genetic algorithm (GA), variable importance in projection (VIP) and random forest variable importance (RFVI), were adapted to screen the most significant variables among the whole data. The machine learning models, such as support vector machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) and shallow neural network (NN), were applied to the data for the classification of endometriosis from control. The protein profile data with common features selected out of feature selection tools such as GA and VIP, and KNN as a classifier resulted in a sensitivity of 73% an area under the ROC curve of 0.77. Furthermore, the explainable AI tool SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) values was used to identify the blood plasma fractions responsible for classifying endometriosis relative to controls. The untargeted mass spectrometry analysis of these blood plasma fractions revealed a panel of proteins that were responsible for the classification of endometriosis and probable protein biomarkers of endometriosis. The Mid-level data fusion (extracting PLS-DA score) was applied on the ATR-FTIR and HPLC-FLD data set with feature selection algorithms, which resulted in an 80% sensitivity and AUC of 0.80. This study suggests that a multimodal analytical approach with suitable data fusion can be a promising tool for minimally invasive endometriosis detection.

Article.Title: True triaxial experimental study on the 3D morphological evolution of multi-cluster fractures in tight sandstone
Article.Authors: Xinghao G.; Jian Y.; Ji Z.; Lei X.; Fei L.; Xu L.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Nonuniform cluster activation and complex three-dimensional fracture growth are major challenges in horizontal-well multi-cluster fracturing. To investigate their evolution, large-scale true triaxial hydraulic-fracturing experiments were conducted on 300 mm natural tight-sandstone cubes containing four simulated clusters. Pump-pressure evolution, cluster-initiation efficiency, fluorescent-tracer observations, and three-dimensional fracture reconstructions were jointly analyzed. The 30, 40, and 50 mm-spacing specimens exhibited initiation efficiencies of 75%, 50%, and 100%, respectively. At 30 mm spacing, strong inter-fracture interaction produced localized and tortuous fracture growth, corresponding to the smallest reconstructed area of 1.14 $$\times$$ 105 mm2 and the highest Dexcess of 19.85. At 50 mm spacing, reduced near-wellbore competition allowed all four clusters to propagate over the largest reconstructed area of 3.43 $$\times$$ 105 mm2. The 40 mm specimen developed a fracture-interaction interval, the largest pressure range, and preferential growth of fewer dominant fractures. Increasing the nominal injection rate from 10 to 30 mL/min reduced the number of activated clusters from three to two, while the reconstructed area changed by only 1.15%; the three-dimensional morphology consequently shifted from distributed multi-surface growth to edge-dominated propagation. The two viscosity conditions had the same initiation efficiency, but the higher-viscosity specimen had a 29.7% smaller area and a 124% larger Dexcess, indicating more localized and tortuous growth, whereas the lower-viscosity fluid promoted broader spatial extension. These results demonstrate that spacing, injection rate, and viscosity control the three-dimensional evolution of multi-cluster fractures through stress interference, preferential fluid allocation, and pressure retention. This study provides experimental evidence for explaining the competitive propagation of fractures and optimizing multi cluster completion designs.

Article.Title: A retrieval-augmented local large language model for ICD-10-CM terminology mapping of clinical signs and symptoms
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Finkelstein J.
Article.Abstract: Accurately mapping clinical signs and symptoms (S&S) from free text to ICD-10-CM codes is essential for early cancer detection, phenotyping, and risk-prediction modeling. However, manual coding is labor-intensive, and automated models often generate invalid or hallucinated codes. This study evaluates whether grounding a large language model (LLM) in the full ICD-10-CM catalog through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves accuracy and reliability compared with an LLM operating without retrieval. Using 200 clinical notes containing 545 human-labeled S&S, we compared an LLM-only baseline, a retrieval-only voting baseline, and a RAG-LLM model. Eight domain-specific and general embedding models produced dense vectors for all 98,186 ICD-10-CM codes. For each symptom, up to 40 candidate codes were retrieved by cosine similarity and incorporated into the model prompt for final selection. Performance was evaluated at the three-character ICD-10 block level against human annotations, with expert adjudication of non-matching cases. Code validity and raw description consistency were evaluated using the official ICD-10-CM reference. The RAG-LLM model achieved 85.87% three-character ICD-10-CM match accuracy, outperforming the LLM-only baseline (72.11%) and the retrieval-only voting baseline (55.60%). After exploratory adjudication, 98.90% of RAG-LLM outputs were considered clinically acceptable S&S mappings. Paired McNemar tests showed significant improvements over both baselines. The RAG-LLM model also reduced invalid ICD-10-CM code generation from 9.91% in the LLM-only baseline to 1.10%. This proof-of-concept study shows that retrieval-guided LLM candidate selection can improve symptom/sign-level ICD-10-CM terminology mapping on MTsamples. The RAG-LLM model improved both three-character and full-code matching while reducing invalid ICD-10-CM code generation. These findings support further evaluation of retrieval-guided LLM mapping as a preprocessing approach for symptom-based phenotyping research, but additional validation is needed before use in real-world EHR workflows, billing-grade coding, or downstream disease-prediction models.

Article.Title: Clinicopathological features and prognostic risk factors for isolated and ANCA-positive anti-GBM disease
Article.Authors: Liang Q.; Liu Y.; Ning W.; Qi Y.; Zhao Z.
Article.Abstract: Anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) disease is a rare, rapidly progressive autoimmune disorder. Approximately 30% of patients concurrently test positive for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), constituting the double-positive (DP) subgroup, while those with isolated anti-GBM disease are classified as single-positive (SP). This study aimed to compare the clinicopathologic phenotypes, renal outcomes, and prognostic risk factors between SP and DP patients. We enrolled a total of 117 SP patients and 63 DP patients admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University from January 2015 to June 2025. A retrospective analysis was conducted on the baseline clinicopathological data and follow-up information for these patients to identify factors affecting their survival and renal prognosis. Cox regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were used to assess the association between prognostic risk factors and clinical outcomes. Compared to the SP group, DP Patients were diagnosed at a more advanced age ( P < 0.001) and experienced a longer duration of symptoms before presentation ( P < 0.001). The DP cohort exhibited more pronounced anemia ( P < 0.001), reduced lymphocyte counts ( P = 0.038), and lower serum complement C3 levels ( P = 0.025). The SP group had lower levels of serum globulin ( P = 0.006) and serum IgG compared to the DP group ( P = 0.002). DP patients exhibited a higher incidence of tubular atrophy than those with SP patients ( P = 0.043). Additionally, the DP patients demonstrated a greater likelihood of recovering from dialysis dependence within one year post-treatment ( P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, the independent predictors for poor patient survival included advanced age, diffuse alveolar haemorrhage at the time of diagnosis, and the need for renal replacement therapy at presentation. The independent predictors for end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in patients included high serum creatinine at presentation and oliguria/anuria. RCS analysis showed nonlinear associations between serum creatinine and ESRD ( P < 0.001).
