Article.Title: Predicting the antioxidant capacity of lignin from high- and low-field NMR spectra using chemometric methods
Article.Authors: Burger R.; Rumpf J.; Diehl B.; Monakhova Y.; Schulze M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lignin is a complex heterogeneous natural polymer with promising antioxidant properties. A chemometric method for the prediction of the antioxidant capacity of organosolv lignins ( n = 55) based on high-field (500, 600 MHz) and low-field (43, 60 MHz) 1 H NMR spectroscopy is presented. Partial least squares regression (PLS-R) models were trained ( n = 38) and externally validated ( n = 17) for ABTS (2,2’-Azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid), DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl), FRAP (Ferric ion reducing antioxidant power), and Folin–Ciocalteu. Robust models were achieved at all field strengths for ABTS (validation: R 2 = 0.84–0.95, relative error (RE) = 5.2-9.0%), FRAP (validation: R 2 = 0.84–0.91, RE = 5.4–7.5%), and Folin–Ciocalteu (validation: R 2 = 0.92–0.95, RE = 4.8–5.7%), indicating that the relevant predictive information is encoded in the overall 1 H spectral profile, with little dependence on field strength. In contrast, DPPH was not predictable from the 1 H NMR spectra, it showed significantly higher errors and lower correlation coefficients (validation: R 2 = 0.26–0.62; RE = 19–24%) than the models for other parameters. The generally high DPPH assay imprecision, lower reactivity, and steric constraints impede successful modeling. To enable cross-platform deployment of the method, a calibration transfer across the NMR spectrometers was performed using 10 transfer samples. Transferred models showed comparable performance to the original models for ABTS, FRAP, and Folin–Ciocalteu, including transfers from high-field 600 MHz to benchtop NMR (validation: R 2 = 0.73–0.96; RE = 5–14%). These results demonstrate that benchtop and high-field 1 H NMR, coupled with PLS-R provide a rapid approach for screening lignin antioxidant capacity, reducing reliance on laborious wet-chemical testing.

Article.Title: Classifying morphologically unidentifiable leukemia blast cells using quantum neural networks and ResNeXt
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Md A.; H S.; Padmavathy T.
Article.Abstract: Accurate classification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) blast cells remains challenging when morphological differences between malignant and normal cells are weak or visually ambiguous. This study presents a proof-of-concept hybrid classical–quantum framework for the binary classification of morphologically unidentifiable leukemia cell images. The proposed model combines ResNeXt-101-32 × 8d as a fixed feature extractor with a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) as the trainable decision module. The full dataset, obtained from a public cancer imaging repository, contains 7,272 cancer-cell images and 3,389 normal-cell images, indicating substantial class imbalance. To avoid bias toward the majority class and to enable controlled comparisons across models, a balanced subset was created, with 100 images used for training (50 per class) and 200 images used for testing (100 per class). Three hybrid QNN variants with 6, 10, and 12 qubits were evaluated under different quantum hyperparameter settings and compared against classical neural-network baselines with matched structural depth. Across the experiments, the hybrid models achieved up to 88.9% validation accuracy, recall above 0.90 for the best-performing variants, and ROC–AUC values of approximately 0.95, while showing slightly better sensitivity than comparable classical dense-layer baselines. The main novelty of this work lies in integrating transfer learning with a custom VQC employing even–odd entangling layers for leukemia-image classification under morphologically ambiguous conditions. Although limited by simulator-based training and a small balanced experimental subset, the results suggest that hybrid quantum-classical learning is a promising direction for challenging medical image classification tasks.

Article.Title: The acoustic environment is structured more by place and fine particulate matter more by time across Rhode Island communities
Article.Authors: Walker E.; Mandalapu S.; Lefebvre S.
Article.Abstract: Environmental comfort in cities is shaped by several exposures at once, yet noise and air pollution are often combined into a single index of environmental quality. We measured the acoustic environment, fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and nighttime illuminance at 144 sites across eight Rhode Island municipalities, sampling each in four day and night session types over 39 measurement days (531 site-sessions). Sound level and PM2.5 were uncorrelated and had different predictors. Sound was associated mainly with the built environment, rising near industrial land, and most of its variance lay between sites. PM2.5 was associated chiefly with day-to-day weather, falling with wind and rising with temperature and precipitation, and most of its variance lay between measurement days. Sound fell at night while PM2.5 rose. These patterns held under penalized regression and after accounting for spatial clustering, which itself reflected shared weather. Applying the same models to every measured quantity separated them consistently: the acoustic metrics and nighttime light were structured mainly by place, and every air-quality metric mainly by time. In this setting the acoustic environment behaved more as a feature of place and PM2.5 more as a feature of time, suggesting the two are better characterized separately than combined.

Article.Title: Effects of kaempferol-loaded niosomes on apoptosis and the expression of BAX, BCL2, TP53, and MMP2 in A549 lung cancer cells
Article.Authors: Ehsani rad F.; Kavousi M.; Jamshidian F.
Article.Abstract: Kaempferol is a naturally occurring flavonoid with reported anticancer properties; however, its limited aqueous solubility may restrict its therapeutic application. Non-ionic niosomes represent a potential delivery platform for poorly soluble bioactive compounds. This study evaluated the physicochemical properties and in vitro biological effects of kaempferol-loaded niosomes in A549 human lung adenocarcinoma cells, with HLF cells included as a non-malignant cellular model. Kaempferol-loaded niosomes were prepared using the thin-film hydration method and characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta-potential analysis. Cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay after 24, 48, and 72 h of treatment. Wound closure was evaluated using an in vitro scratch assay, and apoptosis-associated cell populations were analyzed by Annexin V–FITC/propidium iodide flow cytometry. The mRNA expression levels of BAX, BCL2, P53, and MMP2 were evaluated by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in A549 and HLF cells. FESEM revealed predominantly spherical structures measuring approximately 60–87 nm, whereas DLS showed a bimodal hydrodynamic size distribution, with peaks at approximately 242 and 765 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.422. The mean zeta potential was approximately − 9.2 mV. In A549 cells, kaempferol-loaded niosomes produced concentration- and time-dependent reductions in cell viability, with lower estimated IC₅₀ values than free kaempferol across the tested treatment durations. Flow-cytometric analysis showed a higher proportion of apoptotic cells following treatment with kaempferol-loaded niosomes than with free kaempferol. The scratch assay revealed a larger remaining wound area in the niosome-treated group, indicating reduced wound closure; however, contributions from cytotoxicity and altered cell proliferation could not be excluded. In A549 cells, treatment with kaempferol-loaded niosomes was associated with increased BAX and P53 mRNA expression and decreased BCL2 and MMP2 mRNA expression. The corresponding expression patterns differed in magnitude in HLF cells; however, cancer-selective activity was not established. Under the conditions investigated, kaempferol-loaded niosomes were associated with greater apparent cytotoxic and apoptosis-associated effects in A549 cells than free kaempferol. The observed changes in wound closure and gene expression provide preliminary evidence of altered cellular responses following treatment. Further studies incorporating appropriate statistical comparisons, protein-level validation, migration assays that account for cytotoxicity and proliferation, and in vivo evaluation are needed to establish the reproducibility, selectivity, and therapeutic potential of this formulation.

Article.Title: Physics-inspired smoke segmentation via heterogeneous feature modeling with a Kolmogorov–Arnold-inspired activation head
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Wang Y.; Zheng A.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Smoke segmentation systems often use general-purpose backbones with predefined pointwise activations, which may limit channel-specific modeling of nonlinear variations in smoke appearance and apparent density. Differences between black and white smoke, together with interference from clouds and fog, further complicate feature extraction. We propose the smoke KAN-inspired dual-stream SegFormer (SKD-SegFormer), a lightweight framework guided by these smoke characteristics. Its KAN-inspired channel-adaptive activation head applies learnable B-spline mappings to individual feature channels after multi-scale fusion, enabling flexible nonlinear responses across feature-value ranges. Two modules developed in this work address complementary challenges. The dual-stream smoke discrimination module adaptively fuses diffuse patterns and localized details through branches with different receptive fields. The smoke-oriented suppression module combines appearance-dependent confidence with a spatial prior motivated by the typical buoyancy-driven morphology of rising fire smoke to reduce false responses to environmental distractors. On the self-built real smoke dataset, SKD-SegFormer achieves a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of $$82.85\% \pm 1.14\%$$ over three random seeds (best run 84.03%). Its single-run IoU on the synthetic dataset is $$83.46\%$$ . With 6.45 M parameters and 52 frames per second on an NVIDIA A40 GPU, the model offers a favorable balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

Article.Title: LAR-Net: a lightweight adaptive receptive field network for point cloud segmentation of pharmaceutical deposits on reactor inner walls
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Wang H.; Ma Z.; Shi Y.; Chen B.; Wu S.; Zhang T.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent cleaning of chemical reaction vessels is an inevitable trend in equipment operation and maintenance, and its implementation highly depends on high-precision perception of the residual amount and spatial distribution of pharmaceutical deposits on vessel inner walls. However, conventional inspection methods suffer from three major limitations: high labor intensity, low efficiency, and weak morphology reconstruction capability. Therefore, these methods are insufficient for supporting refined, demand-driven, and quantitative cleaning strategies. Although point cloud deep learning has been widely applied to 3D semantic segmentation, specialized networks for reactor inner-wall pharmaceutical deposit detection remain limited. Existing general-purpose models are poorly adapted to the small scale, weak boundaries, and irregular adhesion patterns of deposits, resulting in insufficient local detail representation and incomplete boundary delineation. To address these problems, this study proposes LAR-Net, a lightweight adaptive receptive field network for point cloud segmentation of pharmaceutical deposits on reactor inner walls. Built upon the lightweight hybrid backbone LitePT, LAR-Net dynamically adjusts the receptive field according to local geometric complexity, models local inter-voxel relationships through Adaptive Relation Convolution (AR-Conv), and recalibrates channel features within local patches to enhance the feature representation of small-scale deposits. A reactor inner-wall pharmaceutical deposit point cloud dataset was constructed for model evaluation. On the test set, LAR-Net achieved an mIoU of 0.8326, an mAcc of 0.8827, a deposit-class IoU of 0.6781, and a deposit-class accuracy of 0.7713, outperforming LitePT by 1.11, 1.49, 2.18, and 2.99 percentage points, respectively. Furthermore, LAR-Net achieves a favorable balance among segmentation accuracy, boundary preservation, geometric consistency, and computational efficiency, demonstrating improved capability for fine-grained pharmaceutical deposit segmentation and providing support for automated deposit detection and intelligent cleaning of chemical reactors.

Article.Title: Decreased mechanosensing properties and altered gene expression in hiPSC-cardiomyocytes carrying a lamin A/C mutation
Article.Authors: Kuusela E.; Lönnrot A.; Thusberg S.; Prajapati C.; Heliö T.; Taimen P.; Milicevic N.; Cherian R.; Kesseli J.; Ihalainen T.; Nykter M.; Aalto-Setälä K.; George Abraham B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mutations of the LMNA gene are the second most common genetic cause for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and significant cause of non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). Lamins A and C, both encoded by the LMNA , have a role in maintaining nuclear architecture, DNA replication, transcription, and apoptosis, but the molecular mechanisms by which LMNA mutations drive DCM remain poorly understood. Previous studies have shown that the p.S143P mutation increases mobility and nucleoplasmic pool of lamin A/C, suggesting that it is less tightly bound to the intranuclear elements and to the nuclear envelope. We utilized patient-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) and investigated the impact of p.S143P mutation on lamin structure, nuclear mechanics, electrophysiological properties, and gene expression to understand the mechanisms linking the mutation to DCM. A dual lamin A/C labeling approach revealed increased N-terminal and decreased rod-domain epitope accessibility of patient line compared to the control line indicating changes in nuclear lamina organization. Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer analysis using fluorescent protein-based strain sensor showed a shift in lamin strain towards a relaxed state in patient-derived cardiomyocytes compared with healthy controls. Transcriptomic profiling supported the impact of these results, showing dysregulation of genes involved in cytoskeleton and mechanosensitive pathways. Electrophysiological analysis of CMs revealed increased calcium densities in calcium currents and increased number of delayed after depolarizations in mutant CMs. In conclusion, the findings indicate that the p.S143P LMNA mutation directly disrupts nuclear lamina organization leading to impaired mechanotransduction, alters expression of genes related to cytoskeleton organization and mechanosensation, and perturbs calcium signaling, providing an integrated mechanobiological route to DCM pathogenesis.

Article.Title: Optimization of water chestnut starch-based encapsulation systems for improved probiotic survival under simulated gastrointestinal stress
Article.Authors: Saeed F.; Ahmed A.; Mohammed N.; Raza N.; Shoukat L.; Ateeq H.; Ali S.; Afzaal M.; Islam F.; Ndagire C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to improve the viability and stability of probiotic bacteria under adverse environmental and gastrointestinal conditions through encapsulation in water chestnut starch-based micro- and nanoparticles prepared by the gelation method. The resulting particles were characterized and evaluated for their ability to protect Bifidobacterium bifidum during storage, thermal exposure, and simulated gastrointestinal conditions. Both encapsulation systems demonstrated high encapsulation yields, with values of 95% and 97% for microcapsules and nanocapsules, respectively. During storage, encapsulated probiotics exhibited significantly greater viability than free cells. After 20 days, viable counts decreased from approximately 9.50 log CFU/g to 7.29 log CFU/g in microencapsulated cells, and 8.94 log CFU/g in nanoencapsulated cells. Encapsulation also enhanced thermal stability compared with free probiotic cells. Under simulated gastric conditions, free cells showed the greatest loss in viability, decreasing to 4.74 log CFU/g after 120 min, whereas microencapsulated and nanoencapsulated cells retained viable counts of approximately 7.62 and 8.55 log CFU/g, respectively. Similarly, under simulated intestinal conditions, free cells showed the lowest survival, 3.65 log CFU/g, while encapsulated cells maintained substantially higher viability. Nanoencapsulated cells exhibited the highest survival (8.13 log CFU/g), demonstrating the protective effect of starch-based encapsulation against gastrointestinal stress. In contrast, free probiotic cells showed substantially greater losses in viability under all tested conditions. Statistical analysis demonstrated significant differences among treatments where applicable (p < 0.05). In conclusion, water chestnut starch-based encapsulation enhanced the stability and survival of B. bifidum during storage, thermal, and simulated gastrointestinal conditions. Nanoencapsulation showed greater retention of viability than microencapsulation under the storage, simulated gastric, and simulated intestinal conditions evaluated. These findings support the potential of starch-based encapsulation as a strategy for improving probiotic protection, however, validation in food matrices and in vivo studies is required before practical applications can be established.

Article.Title: Microwave photonic crystal plasma source
Article.Authors: Magarotto M.; Schenato L.; Santagiustina M.; Galtarossa A.; Capobianco A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient electromagnetic coupling is a central requirement in low-temperature plasma sources, particularly in applications involving kilowatt-class or higher input powers, where power reflected toward the microwave generator or transmitted beyond the plasma region can limit performance and reliability. Here, we introduce Photonic Crystal Plasma (PCP) sources, a novel class of microwave plasma sources that exploit Bragg-like field localization to enhance plasma production. The concept is investigated through theoretical modal analysis and full-wave numerical simulations in cylindrical geometries. Two implementations are proposed: a plasma-only configuration, based on a periodic modulation of the static magnetic induction field, and a plasma-dielectric configuration, in which the plasma acts as a defect embedded in a dielectric photonic crystal. For representative low-pressure microwave plasma conditions, the plasma-only source is estimated to couple more than 96% of the incident power to the plasma, with reflected and transmitted powers below 2% and 3%, respectively. The plasma-dielectric configuration maintains plasma absorptivity approaching 90% while reducing the source footprint by more than a factor of five, achieving lengths as short as 0.35 m with a metallic front termination. These results establish PCP sources as a promising design paradigm, with potential applications in tunable microwave loads and protection devices, plasma-assisted processing, and plasma sources coupled to grid-extraction systems.

Article.Title: A machine learning prognostic prediction model for primary tinnitus patients using large real world data
Article.Authors: Ji D.; Lan H.; Zhang Y.; Zhou S.; Deng A.
Article.Abstract: Primary tinnitus exhibits significant prognostic heterogeneity and lacks early prognostic prediction tools currently. This study aimed to construct a prognostic prediction model for primary tinnitus by leveraging real-world big data through machine learning-based analytical methods. A total of 1850 patients diagnosed with primary tinnitus were retrospectively assigned to a training cohort and a validation cohort at an 8:2 ratio. Five key features were selected through the random forest algorithm, and predictive models were subsequently constructed using random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), support vector machine (SVM), and CatBoost. Model performance was compared across multiple standard metrics via 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap validation on the training set. The final model was further evaluated on the held-out test set using standard binary classification metrics including receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and area under the ROC curve (AUROC), accuracy, recall, specificity, precision, F1-score, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Model stability was assessed using calibration curves, calibration slope, calibration-in-the-large (CITL), Brier score, and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals. The study employed a comprehensive suite of analytical techniques to assess a predictive model for tinnitus patients. A feature importance plot underscored "Course" as the paramount predictor, with "Treatment methods," "Continuous," "Age," and "THI" (in that order) rounding out the top five most critical features. Among the multiple modeling approaches examined—CatBoost, decision tree, random forest, and SVM—CatBoost emerged as the better-performing model when its results from 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap validation were considered jointly, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.715. Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) further highlighted CatBoost’s superior net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities, reinforcing its substantial clinical utility. The calibration curves indicated acceptable concordance between the predicted probabilities and the observed outcomes, which was especially evident for the CatBoost model. SHAP analysis elucidated the model’s decision-making process, reaffirming "Course," "Treatment methods," and "THI" as pivotal determinants. The clinical usability assessment confirmed that CatBoost exhibited greater overall strength in accuracy (0.6865), recall (0.6585), and F1 score (0.6506). Although its performance did not differ substantially from that of random forest under bootstrap validation, it achieved an AUC of 0.7152 and a specificity of 0.7087. Although CatBoost demonstrated relatively better predictive performance compared to other models in predicting primary tinnitus outcomes, its overall AUROC remains modest. While it shows potential as a predictive tool, further optimization and validation are needed to enhance its clinical utility and reliability.

Article.Title: Spectroscopic and magnetic studies of 0.9Bi0.80Sr0.20FeO3–0.1CoFe2O4 composite
Article.Authors: Sharma O.; Singh J.; Lim W.; Chae K.; Jaiparkash N/A.
Article.Abstract: In this study, perovskite-spinel based composite, 0.9Bi 0.80 Sr 0.20 FeO 3 –0.1CoFe 2 O 4 ceramic, has been synthesized using solid-state reaction method. X-ray diffraction study confirms the presence of both perovskite Bi 0.80 Sr 0.20 FeO 3 (BSFO) and spinel CoFe 2 O 4 (CFO) phases in the composite, and no secondary phase formation. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy shows the presence of an absorption band around 551 cm -1 , which signifies the presence of the stretching mode associated with metal–oxygen vibrations in CFO. The broadening of the absorption band around 551 cm -1 in the composite indicates the overlap of wave numbers associated with Fe–O and Bi–O vibrations. The bands corresponding to the BSFO and CFO phases were detected in the Raman spectrum of the composite. The field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) micrographs reveal that the particles in all the synthesized materials exhibit a spherical morphology. 57 Fe Mössbauer spectroscopic study exhibits the presence of Fe 3+ in a high spin state. Fe L -edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) measurements show the presence of Fe 3+ ions in the composite. O K -edge NEXAFS measurements revealed a change of metal–oxygen interaction in the composite with respect to CFO and BSFO. Magnetic study confirms that the magnetization (M) and coercivity (H c ) in the composite sample are 9.54 emu/g and 0.45 kOe, respectively. The energy band gap is 2.16 eV for the composite. The correlation between the magnetic property and local electronic structural study in the 0.9Bi 0.80 Sr 0.20 FeO 3 –0.1CoFe 2 O 4 system contributes to the development of multifunctional composites with tunable magnetic properties for data storage and spintronic device applications.

Article.Title: SpecEvaluator enables structured multi-expert quality assessment of speech dialogue systems with specialized large audio models
Article.Authors: Wang R.; Zhang H.; Qu D.
Article.Abstract: We investigate automatic evaluation for spoken dialogue systems and propose SpecEvaluator, a structured multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Existing methods either rely on ASR transcription or produce a single holistic score, which hinders the preservation and discrimination of key aspects of speech dialogue such as semantic content, emotional expression, and speech quality. To address this, SpecEvaluator decomposes the evaluation task into three dimensions—content coherence, emotional appropriateness, and speech quality—each judged by a dimension-specific audio-language model. A zero-shot aggregation module then generates the final score and explanation. We further construct a multi-dimensional evaluation dataset with controllable quality gradients and generate dimension-level supervision signals using a teacher model. Experiments demonstrate that SpecEvaluator consistently outperforms strong baselines across ranking accuracy, correlation, and grade classification.

Article.Title: Composition–structure–optical characteristics of V–Ti co-doped zircon pigments
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Zhou C.; Wang Y.; Wang J.; Manzalat J.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a reproducible secondary-data reanalysis of five V–Ti co-doped zircon pigment formulations. No new synthesis, diffraction, reflectance, or colorimetric measurements were performed. Nominal oxide compositions and archived structural, Kubelka–Munk-response, and CIELAB values were processed through a common computational workflow. The normalized tetragonality deviation, Δ(c/a), ranged from − 1.197 × 10⁻⁴ to − 6.847 × 10⁻⁴ and varied non-monotonically across the formulation series. Ten archived optical-response values per formulation were evaluated on their native non-uniform wavelength grid using a three-point derivative for unequal intervals. The sampled minimum occurred at 645.161 nm for all samples, whereas the steepest sampled negative slope occurred at 487.805 nm and increased in magnitude from 0.003981 to 0.005454 nm⁻¹. Recalculated chroma ranged from 6.708 to 9.000, and hue angle increased from 135° to 180°, indicating a yellow-green-to-green shift. Correlations were descriptive because only five formulations were available. The contribution is an auditable integration and consistency assessment of archived measurements, not generation of new experimental data or causal composition–property inference, and identifies testable hypotheses for future controlled validation.

Article.Title: A digital intervention targeting multiple dimensions of well-being in existing friendship dyads and groups in a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Turóczi H.; Szabó Z.; Verebélyi L.; Prohászka B.; Kun Á.; Salamon J.
Article.Abstract: Emerging adulthood is associated with increased vulnerability to mental health difficulties, lower well-being, and heightened loneliness, highlighting the need for scalable digital interventions. Positive psychology models, particularly the PERMA model, provide a multidimensional framework for promoting well-being. The present preregistered study examined a six-week, PERMA-based, chatbot-delivered intervention designed to mobilize existing friendship networks through structured interaction in dyads and small groups. In this preregistered cluster randomized controlled trial, pre-existing friendship groups were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or waitlist control condition. The final analytic sample included 251 participants (intervention: n = 124; waitlist control: n = 127). Outcomes included PERMA well-being and its dimensions, perceived social support from friends, loneliness, and interpersonal closeness. Participants in the intervention condition reported higher post-intervention perceived social support from friends and higher scores on the relationships and accomplishment dimensions of PERMA. Within the intervention group, interpersonal closeness also increased across the intervention period. No significant intervention effects were observed for overall well-being, loneliness, positive emotion, engagement, or meaning. These findings suggest that the effects of the intervention were relatively specific rather than broad, with the clearest pattern emerging for participants’ relational experiences. More generally, the study highlights the potential value of considering not only intervention content but also the social context in which digital positive psychology activities are delivered.

Article.Title: Development and characterization of wafer creams using soybean oil oleogels structured with monoglyceride and carnauba wax as shortening replacers
Article.Authors: Habibzadeh A.; Kermani R.; Nematollahi S.; Roufegarinejad L.; Alizadeh A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the use of soybean oil oleogels to partially replace shortening in wafer creams. Soybean oil was structured either with 7% monoglyceride (MG) or 6% carnauba wax (CW) to obtain monoglyceride-based oleogels (MGO) and carnauba wax-based oleogels (CWO), respectively. The oleogels were then examined for their thermal behavior, oil-binding capacity (OBC), crystal morphology, crystal structure, and FTIR spectral characteristics. Notably, the MGO-based oleogel exhibited a denser, spherical crystal network, resulting in a significantly higher OBC (99.19 ± 0.72%) compared to the CWO-based oleogel (92.8 ± 0.9%), which displayed needle-like crystals. The oleogels were incorporated into wafer creams at 25% and 50% replacement levels, and the resulting formulations were evaluated for textural properties, oxidative stability, oil loss, specific gravity, and color. MGO-containing creams showed lower oil loss and better oxidative stability than CWO-containing creams during storage. As the oleogel substitution level increased, the hardness and adhesiveness of the creams decreased; however, MGO-containing samples maintained superior structural integrity and aeration compared to CWO-based formulations.

Article.Title: Optimizing energy efficiency in IoT enabled wireless sensor networks via Gegenbauer graph neural network
Article.Authors: S. S. A.; Mary A.; Rajendran A.; Arumugam P.
Article.Abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have been widely studied because of their data collection and observation across diverse applications. However, the restricted energy resources of sensor nodes (SNs) remain a major challenge for prolonging the network lifetime. To address this issue, this study proposes an Energy Efficient IoT-Enabled WSN framework based on a Gegenbauer Graph Neural Network (EE-IoT-WSN-GGNN). Initially, clusters are generated using Multi-Kernel Collaborative Fuzzy Clustering (MKCFC) method. For each cluster, an efficient Cluster Head (CH) is selected with the help of Elite Opposite Sparrow Search algorithm (EOSSA), facilitating WSN development to accommodate a large amount of SNs. The multi objective fitness dependent optimizer algorithm (MOFDOA) then optimizes the candidate routing configurations generated by the trained GGNN to find the most energy efficient data transmission using the Adam optimizer. The proposed framework can simultaneously optimize energy consumption, delay, congestion, QoS, and network stability by combining the topology-aware routing from GGNN with multi-objective routing optimization. The proposed EE-IoT-WSN-GGNN framework was implemented in the python environment. The performance of the proposed EE-IoT-WSN-GGNN approach attains 20.65%, 25.81% and 31.21% higher energy efficiency, 21.58%, 25.15% and 30.15% higher network stability compared with existing methods like efficient energy management in WSN depending on optimized explicit feature interaction-aware graph neural network (MEE-WSN-DT), cluster-basis routing protocol design utilizing Gated Fusion Adaptive Graph Neural Network in WSN (EE-MPDP-WSN), energy efficient clustering for dense WSN using graph neural networks with coverage metrics (LMNN-EE-WSN), multi-hop graph-based approach for an energy-efficient routing protocol in wireless sensor networks (QoS-ASR-GNN), Lightweight reinforcement learning for energy efficient communications in wireless sensor networks (ONS-PO-GNN), energy-efficient optimization-based routing technique for wireless sensor network using machine learning (GAT-EER-WSN) and Graph convolutional networks and deep reinforcement learning in IoT environs for intelligent edge routing (GCN-SRL-ER) respectively

Article.Title: A hybrid mutation-guided adversarial evolution framework for adaptive web intrusion detection systems
Article.Authors: Alhwikem F.; Mohd Saqib S.
Article.Abstract: Contemporary Web Intrusion Detection Systems (WIDS) remain vulnerable to zero-day, polymorphic, and adversarial attacks that evade signature-based and traditional Machine Learning detection. Existing approaches lack the capacity to proactively stress-test detection boundaries and evolve defensive models against previously unseen threat morphologies. This paper introduces MutaShield-Net, a software-testing-grounded hybrid framework that synergistically integrates software mutation testing principles and verification with adversarial evolutionary learning to continuously harden web intrusion detection models. The proposed architecture comprises three interdependent novel components: (1) Spectral Mutation Operator Engine (SMOE), which generates semantically valid traffic mutations across seven taxonomic attack families; (2) Cross-Domain Attention-Gated Recurrent Transformer (CA-GRT), a novel detection backbone that fuses temporal recurrence with multi-head cross-attention over both raw packet features and application-layer semantic embeddings; and (3) Adversarial Mutation Fitness Evolutionary Loop (AMFEL), a co-evolutionary algorithm wherein mutant generators and detection classifiers engage in a min-max optimization game governed by a novel mutation survival score metric. Extensive experiments on the CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 benchmark datasets demonstrate that MutaShield-Net achieves 99.47% detection accuracy, 98.92% F1-score, and 99.21% AUC-ROC while reducing the false positive rate by 40.4% compared to the strongest single baseline (FL-WGAN-IDS, from 0.52% to 0.31%).

The new configuration is applied to realistic drone to verify the feasibility and technical capabilities of the pentacopter. The hardware is built using the Pixhawk autopilot control and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller. Finally, the pentacopter is tested along with quadcopter to validate the CFD analysis. Using the flight log of pentacopter and quadcopter graphs are produced and the results are interpreted.

Article.Title: Aye-aye percussive foraging integrates frictional gliding and percussive tapping: kinematic and acoustic evidence
Article.Authors: Masurkar N.; Nemati H.; Dehghan-Niri E.
Article.Abstract: The aye-aye ( Daubentonia madagascariensis ), an endangered nocturnal lemur, employs a unique percussive foraging strategy in which its elongated third digit taps tree surfaces to acoustically locate wood-boring insect larvae. Despite the recognized importance of this adaptation, the precise biomechanical dynamics of the digit during foraging remain poorly understood, largely due to limitations in capturing detailed motion under low-light conditions. We developed a dual-sensing approach integrating high-speed thermal imaging with acoustic recording to quantify digit movement, thermoregulation, and muscle excitation during percussive foraging. Our analysis reveals that the behavior traditionally described as simple tapping is, in fact, a compound motion: the third digit performs a frictional gliding motion across the surface immediately before the majority of percussive taps. The high-frequency acoustic components generated during this frictional gliding phase closely match the elevated sensitivity of the aye-aye’s external auditory structures, suggesting a tightly coupled sound-production and reception system. To our knowledge, this is the first documented observation of this compound motion in aye-ayes. These findings reframe our understanding of aye-aye foraging mechanics and have direct implications for the development of bio-inspired, nondestructive evaluation technologies that emulate this multi-modal sensing strategy.

Article.Title: Re-examining the relationship between artificial intelligence development and urban per capita carbon emissions within a government–market–public framework
Article.Authors: Yao H.; Wang Y.; Wang B.; Xiang M.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) development may be associated with urban emissions through technological applications and interactions among government, market, and public actors, yet city-level evidence remains limited. This study develops a government–market–public (GMP) framework using panel data for 279 Chinese cities from 2013 to 2021. A city-level AI development index combines government policy support, AI-related firms and patents, and public attention. Two-way fixed-effects models with city-clustered standard errors assess its association with urban per capita carbon emissions, supplemented by sensitivity, spatial, pathway-consistency, and heterogeneity analyses. AI development is negatively associated with urban per capita carbon emissions in the baseline model and under alternative controls, lagged controls, province-by-year fixed effects, most leave-one-out tests, and the spatial model. The relationship is not sustained with city-specific linear trends or first differences, and a significant lead term complicates its temporal interpretation. Spatial estimates show a significant local association but no significant cross-city spillover. GMP regressions yield exploratory patterns involving government intervention, population agglomeration, and household income rather than verified transmission processes. Interaction tests indicate stronger negative associations in coastal cities and provincial capitals or centrally administered municipalities; city-size results remain exploratory. Overall, the findings reveal a context-dependent and specification-sensitive relationship between AI development and lower urban per capita carbon emissions.

A rat model of endothelial cell senescence was used to produce EVs senescent . HF was induced in rats using doxorubicin (DOX) and treated with EVs senescent , EVs miR-503 antagomir , and DAA. Cardiac function, tissue fibrosis, and NT-proBNP levels were assessed using echocardiography, histological staining, and ELISA, respectively. Mitochondrial markers TOM20 and LC3B were analyzed. DOX-treated H9C2 cells were developed as a cell model, with mitophagy, mitochondrial function, cell viability, and the levels of marker proteins and miR-503 measured. Total m6A was quantified, and m6A methylation sites on MST1 mRNA were predicted and subsequently validated. EVs senescent showed high miR-503, inhibiting mitophagy and promoting mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby worsening HF in rats. These effects were partially reversed by miR-503 antagomir. EVs senescent miR-503 repressed mitophagy and increased mitochondrial dysfunction in DOX-treated cardiomyocytes. Mitophagy activation reduced the adverse effects of EVs senescent . An m6A methylation site on MST1 was identified. miR-503 delivered by EVs senescent was correlated with MST1/m6A modification and mitochondrial dysfunction. EVs senescent miR-503 to modulate MST1 expression in an m6A modification-dependent manner, thereby suppressing mitophagy, aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, and exacerbating HF in rats.

Article.Title: Car-to-car injury risk functions for real-time emergency decision-making in highly automated vehicles
Article.Authors: Vichi G.; Gulino M.; Fiorentino A.; Chauvel C.; Bigi L.; Cuny S.; Vangi D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional active safety systems focus on collision avoidance, but unavoidable impacts require real-time occupant injury risk (IR) mitigation. Existing car-to-car injury risk functions (IRFs) rely on crash-phase metrics requiring computationally intensive simulations that violate millisecond on-board decision budgets. Furthermore, most lack geographical transferability. To bridge this gap, this study proposes a novel methodological framework to derive omni-directional, continuous IRFs designed for real-time on-board execution using exclusively pre-crash variables known at the first instant of contact. Optimal predictors are identified via a two-stage feature selection process, and the resulting functions are cross-tested across three geographically distinct accident databases (IGLAD, NASS-CDS, VOIESUR). Rather than providing definitive standalone models, the derived IRFs serve as empirical case studies demonstrating the framework’s validity. This proof-of-concept reveals excellent cross-dataset discrimination for severe ( $$MAIS \ 3+$$ ) injuries (AUC>0.82). The fatal ( $$MAIS \ 6$$ ) model acts as an exploratory baseline for rare events, whilst minor injury prediction remains limited by occupant-intrinsic parameters. Application to a real-world crash test illustrates straightforward model applicability and validates viability under imperfect data regimes. By omitting crash-phase simulations entirely, this approach permits purely kinematic evaluations of autonomous steering and braking interventions at each sensor update, selecting the manoeuvre that minimises occupant IR. Ultimately, this framework provides a concrete technological foundation for real-time injury mitigation in automated vehicles.

Article.Title: Diagnosed and undiagnosed depression among undergraduate medical students in Pakistan: a multi-provincial cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ahmad A.; Sadia Z.; Khalid R.; Khalid M.; Akhtar S.; Zulfiqar R.; Abdullah A.; Javaid M.; Aminpoor H.; Rehan R.; Shahab M.; Ullah M.; Muzdah W.; Malik T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depressive symptoms can adversely affect students’ psychological well-being and academic functioning, while barriers to mental health care may delay recognition and treatment. Evidence distinguishing students with a previous clinical diagnosis from those with clinically significant depressive symptoms but no prior diagnosis remains limited in Pakistan. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of diagnosed and undiagnosed depression among university students across four provinces of Pakistan. This multi-provincial cross-sectional study included 987 university students aged 18–25 years from Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan. Convenience sampling was used, and 903 participants (91.5%) were undergraduate medical students. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), with a score of ≥ 10 indicating clinically significant depressive symptoms. Diagnosed depression was defined by a self-reported prior clinical diagnosis, while undiagnosed depression was defined as a PHQ-9 score ≥ 10 without a reported prior diagnosis. Demographic characteristics and perceived barriers to mental health care were examined using descriptive and appropriate inferential statistics. The overall prevalence of depression, defined by a prior clinical diagnosis and/or clinically significant depressive symptoms without a prior diagnosis, was 32.3% (95% CI: 29.4%–35.2%). A prior clinical diagnosis was reported by 9.2% (95% CI: 7.4%–11.0%), while 23.1% (95% CI: 20.5%–25.7%) screened positive without a prior diagnosis. The overall prevalence varied across provinces, from 25.1% in Punjab to 56.4% in Balochistan. Undiagnosed depressive symptoms were more prevalent among females than males (27.2% vs. 17.9%; p = 0.002). Depression status was associated with monthly household income ( p = 0.042). Participants with a prior diagnosis had higher median PHQ-9 scores than those without a prior diagnosis (16 vs. 14; p < 0.001). Approximately one-third of participants had a prior diagnosis or screened positive for clinically significant depressive symptoms, and most participants meeting the study’s criteria for depression had no reported prior clinical diagnosis. The findings support strengthening access to mental health screening and assessment in university settings. Because the sample was predominantly composed of medical undergraduates and recruitment used convenience sampling, the findings should be generalized to the wider university-student population with caution.

Article.Title: Association between physical activity and loneliness among Chinese university students mediated by basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration
Article.Authors: Fu D.; Zhang P.; Yang T.; Li B.; Jia M.
Article.Abstract: Loneliness has emerged as a growing concern among Chinese university students, and physical activity may represent a modifiable behavioral factor associated with loneliness; however, the psychological factors underlying this association remain largely underexplored. The purpose of this study was to examine the association between physical activity and loneliness, and to assess the mediating role of basic psychological needs among Chinese university students. A convenience sample of 1,195 university students in Zhejiang Province was surveyed to assess physical activity, loneliness, and basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration using the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire, the UCLA Loneliness Scale, and the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 29.0 and PROCESS macro version 5.0. Results revealed that physical activity was negatively correlated with loneliness ( r = -0.374, p < 0.001) and basic psychological need frustration ( r = -0.402, p < 0.001) and positively correlated with basic psychological need satisfaction ( r = 0.297, p < 0.001). Mediation analyses indicated that both basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration independently mediated the relationship between physical activity and loneliness. Higher physical activity was associated with lower loneliness, with significant indirect effects through basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration. These findings suggest that basic psychological needs may help explain the association between physical activity and loneliness and may inform campus-based strategies aimed at addressing loneliness and supporting student mental health.

Article.Title: Energy minimization for RIS-assisted aerial-terrestrial multi-tier MEC under strict latency constraints
Article.Authors: Alshahrani H.; Mengash H.; AlAqil M.; Nemri N.; Almubarak H.; Alharbi E.; Yahya A.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of computation-intensive and latency-critical applications continues to outpace the hardware evolution of mobile user devices. While Mobile edge computing (MEC) offers a viable solution, traditional terrestrial access points are often constrained by signal blockages and rigid deployment constraints. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a unified optimization framework for an RIS-enabled multi-tier MEC system that synergistically integrates a rotary-wing Aerial Edge Node (AEN) and a Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). Operating under a cross-tier OFDMA protocol, the architecture facilitates a hierarchical computation flow across local devices, a Terrestrial Access Point (TAP), and an AEN. We formulate the problem as a Mixed Integer Non-Convex Program (MINCP) to minimize the total system energy encompassing device transmission, local computation, and edge server processing, subject to strict heterogeneous latency deadlines. To solve this intractable problem, we design a mathematically rigorous Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) algorithm that converges to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point. The framework systematically (i) optimizes the UAV 3D positioning and RIS passive beamforming via Semidefinite Relaxation (SDR) and Successive Convex Approximation (SCA), (ii) decouples cross-tier user scheduling and power allocation through Big-M constraints and first-order Taylor expansions, and (iii) determines globally optimal partial offloading fractions and CPU resource distributions from a strictly convex cubic subproblem. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significant energy reductions of up to 68.4% compared to total edge migration and 87.9% compared to standalone local processing. More importantly, compared with the optimization-based Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) baseline, the proposed structured BCD framework achieves a 31.2% lower energy consumption while providing stable and deterministic convergence. Furthermore, the proposed joint optimization outperforms unoptimized surface reflection and fixed aerial deployment by 55.0% and 64.0%, respectively, while ensuring strict deadline feasibility. Our analysis further uncovers fundamental system insights, including a coherent $$\mathcal {O}(L^2)$$ RIS array gain, a convex U-shaped altitude trade-off for the AEN, and the algorithm’s ability to dynamically adapt offloading decisions to avoid edge computational bottlenecks. These findings establish a robust blueprint for the design of energy- and delay-efficient aerial-terrestrial networks in future 6G ecosystems.

Article.Title: Facial self-resemblance does not uniformly increase liking
Article.Authors: Kasahara S.; Claggett E.; Shirado H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social evaluation increasingly unfolds in digital environments where visual cues can be computationally altered, yet it remains unclear whether facial self-resemblance increases positive evaluations of others in naturalistic social interactions. Here, we conducted a preregistered online experiment using a yoked-stimulus design—in which morphed faces were shown to both self-relevant and matched control viewers—to isolate the effects of facial self-resemblance from morphing artifacts. Sixty participants viewed eight two-person conversational videos in which speakers’ faces were morphed to resemble either the viewer or a different participant, yielding 480 evaluations of morphed speakers. We found that facial self-resemblance did not produce a consistent increase in positive evaluations across participants. Exploratory analyses further suggested substantial heterogeneity in responses: participants with higher self-esteem evaluated self-resembling speakers more positively, whereas participants with lower self-esteem showed the opposite tendency. These patterns were observed across both binary and continuous measures of evaluation and were absent in yoked control analyses designed to remove self-relevance. Together, our findings suggest that self-referential visual cues do not exert a fixed social effect. Instead, their consequences may depend on how individuals view themselves, suggesting that digitally altered appearance interacts with self-concept in shaping social evaluation.

Article.Title: Geraniol exerts hormetic effects on proteostasis through SKN-1/Nrf2 and DAF-16/FOXO activation in neurodegeneration models
Article.Authors: Romussi S.; Lacour A.; Veuthey T.; Rayes D.; De Rosa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) are fundamentally linked to proteostasis failure and the accumulation of toxic protein aggregates. Identifying compounds capable of activating endogenous defense systems represents a critical therapeutic priority. In this study, we demonstrate that geraniol, a natural monoterpene, exerts hormetic effects with potent protective outcomes in Caenorhabditis elegans models of Parkinson’s disease (PD). Geraniol treatment significantly mitigated locomotor deficits, reduced α-synuclein-associated fluorescence, and preserved the structural and functional integrity of dopaminergic neurons. Mechanistically, we show that geraniol enhances cellular responsiveness to autophagy-inducing stimuli, suggesting a “priming” effect that facilitates the efficient clearance of misfolded proteins. In parallel, genetic analyses reveal that these beneficial effects are dependent on the conserved transcription factors SKN-1/Nrf2 and DAF-16/FOXO, key regulators of the cellular stress response. Importantly, we found that the effects of geraniol extend beyond PD, also mitigating proteotoxicity in C. elegans muscle models of β-amyloid and polyglutamine aggregation. However, geraniol produces dose- and model-dependent effects, with beneficial effects at lower concentrations and toxicity at higher concentrations, particularly in the β-amyloid and polyglutamine models. These findings support a hormetic response in which the biological outcome of geraniol exposure depends on both concentration and proteotoxic context. Overall, our results provide evidence that geraniol may modulate proteostasis through the hormetic activation of endogenous stress-response pathways, contributing to its beneficial effects in models of protein aggregation.

Article.Title: Determination of l-ascorbic acid and total vitamin C in cosmetic products using ion-pair RP-HPLC-DAD
Article.Authors: Kurpet K.; Serdeń W.; Chwatko G.
Article.Abstract: Reliable determination of vitamin C in cosmetic products remains analytically challenging because of the susceptibility of l-ascorbic acid (AA) to oxidation and the complexity of cosmetic matrices. In this study, an ion-pair reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography method with diode-array detection (IP-RP-HPLC-DAD) was developed and validated for the determination of AA and total vitamin C after quantitative reduction of dehydroascorbic acid (DHAA) with tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP). Validation according to ICH Q2(R2) and Eurachem guidelines confirmed method specificity without matrix interference at the AA retention time. The limits of detection and quantification were 0.7 and 2.2 mg/g for AA and 0.9 and 2.8 mg/g for total vitamin C, respectively. The method showed excellent linearity over concentration ranges of 2.2–200 mg/g for AA (R 2 = 0.9999) and 2.8–200 mg/g for total vitamin C (R 2 = 0.9999). The method demonstrated good accuracy (recoveries of 95.99–110.31%) and precision (RSD ≤ 4.73%). Processed samples remained stable in the autosampler at 4 °C for at least 9 h, with signal changes not exceeding 4.5%. The validated workflow was successfully applied to ten commercially available cosmetic products, demonstrating its suitability for routine compositional analysis and quality control of vitamin C-containing formulations.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of Ghana’s greenhouse gas emission data across national and international databases
Article.Authors: Sokama-Neuyam Y.; Kusi C.; Dzikunu-Bansah N.; Darkwah-Owusu V.; Kemausuor F.
Article.Abstract: Greenhouse gas estimates for the same country can differ substantially across national inventories and international datasets, complicating their use in research and climate assessment. This study reconciled Ghana’s national greenhouse gas inventory (NGHGI; 1990–2022) with three independent datasets (EDGAR, IEA, and FAOSTAT) and three compilations (World Bank WDI, Climate Watch, and Our World in Data) by harmonizing system boundaries, sector definitions, and global warming potentials. Once the boundaries were matched, the national totals converged: EDGAR was within 10% of the NGHGI in 29 of 33 years and only 2.2% lower in 2022 (46.9 versus 48.0 Mt CO₂e). This agreement masked large offsetting sectoral differences whose absolute values totalled 18.8 Mt CO₂e in 2022, dominated by waste, fugitive emissions, industrial processes, and agriculture. Land-use estimates diverged most strongly, with 2022 net LULUCF ranging from − 55.1 Mt CO₂e in FAOSTAT to + 47.7 Mt CO₂e in EDGAR, compared with + 6.8 Mt CO₂e in the NGHGI. Differences arose from system boundaries, category allocation, activity data, emission factors, release cycles, and population denominators. International datasets therefore provide valuable independent checks and cross-country comparability, but require explicit reconciliation with national inventories before interpretation.

Article.Title: Animal welfare concerns regarding water-based foam used for depopulation of livestock
Article.Authors: Reyes-Illg G.; Kolus C.; Carlin E.; Brelje K.; Mitchell H.
Article.Abstract: Farm animal depopulation, i.e., mass killing in response to urgent circumstances, is an increasingly common occurrence in animal agriculture. Water-based foam (WBF) is one such method that kills by smothering animals with a wet foam that results in airway occlusion (obstructive asphyxia). Used in the United States as a method of poultry depopulation, the severely negative subjective experience associated with dying from airway occlusion has led numerous expert panels to reject WBF as a depopulation method 1 , 2 , 3 . However, a recent study published in Scientific Reports that evaluated WBF’s utility in sheep and goats recommends it as “a strong candidate for small ruminant depopulation” 4 . Despite including the term “welfare” among the article’s keywords, Park et al. neglect to examine fundamental welfare harms associated with WBF and downplay the duration of animals’ suffering. Accurately characterizing WBF’s animal welfare impacts would demonstrate that the circumstances in which its use would be ethically justified are exceedingly rare.

Article.Title: Rigorous multi-seed evaluation of domain generalization strategies for multi-center tuberculosis detection in chest radiography
Article.Authors: Almisned F.; Shuaibu I.
Article.Abstract: Deep-learning models for tuberculosis (TB) screening on chest radiographs often lose accuracy at new sites, yet domain generalization (DG) methods are usually compared using a single training run. We built a multi-seed leave-one-domain-out benchmark of seven training objectives (empirical risk minimization (ERM), MixStyle, CORAL, a feature-mixing variant (AdaMix), IRM, GroupDRO and a proposed hyperspherical prototype entropic assignment regularizer (HP-EAR)) across four public chest-radiograph cohorts (1,280 images after near-duplicate removal). Each configuration was trained with five seeds (140 runs), giving 20 matched evaluations per method. Mean AUROC ranged only from 0.752 (ERM, CORAL, HP-EAR) to 0.767 (MixStyle). No method differed from ERM in paired tests or in mixed-effects models accounting for repeated seeds and cohorts (likelihood-ratio p = 0.59). Rankings were unstable: three different methods ranked first across the five individual seeds. AdaMix produced markedly better-calibrated probabilities (expected calibration error 0.232 versus 0.286–0.327; all Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.048), driven by less over-confident predictions. Extending training from 12 to 30 epochs changed no conclusion. At the default threshold, mean sensitivity was 0.55–0.60 at unseen cohorts. Multi-seed testing, calibration and operating-point reporting should be minimum standards for DG claims in medical imaging.

Article.Title: The carbon stable isotope canopy effect extends beyond the edges of temperate forest
Article.Authors: Krajcarz M.; Drucker D.; Borowik T.; Hofman-Kamińska E.; Kamiński T.; Bocherens H.; Kowalczyk R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The canopy effect—the relative depletion of 13 C isotope in plants under closed canopies—is a phenomenon used for interpreting stable isotope data in ecological and palaeoecological studies of herbivore foraging behavior. However, the horizontal extent of this effect near forest boundaries or within forest clearings is still poorly understood, in particular in high-latitude ecosystems. We investigated the distribution of the canopy effect across a gradient from dense forest to open areas in and around the Białowieża Primeval Forest (Eastern Europe) through analysis of δ 13 C values in 10 plant species commonly foraged by large herbivores. Our results demonstrate a significant canopy effect of around 3.7‰ VPDB in the Białowieża Forest. We found that the canopy effect is not confined to the dense forest, but it extends beyond forest edges, significantly affecting plants within approximately 200 m of dense forest.The mechanism beyond is likely the lateral dispersal of 13 C-depleted CO₂ from the forest. To quantify this phenomenon, we propose the parameter “Canopy Impact Distance”, representing the zone around dense canopies where the canopy effect remains measurable. These findings have implications for interpreting isotopic data from herbivores. Low δ 13 C values in herbivore tissues may reflect foraging in dense forests, as well as in forest-adjacent contexts, such as ecotones or near forest edges. This observation challenges simplified forest-versus-grassland models in palaeoecology.

Article.Title: Structural basis and biochemical characterization of the Dicistroviridae 3C protease substrate specificity
Article.Authors: Veeremaa A.; Tamm T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proteolytic processing of viral polyproteins by virus-encoded proteases is a prerequisite for successful infection and viral replication. In this study, we investigated the substrate specificity and potential cross-selectivity of Dicistroviridae 3C proteases by coupling in silico modeling of protease-substrate complexes with in vitro proteolytic assays. Structural bioinformatic analysis across distinct Dicistroviridae genera ( Cripavirus , Triatovirus , and Aparavirus ) highlighted dissimilarities in substrate accommodation. Despite structural divergences in the substrate binding cleft, a common mechanism for substrate stabilization near active site among 3C proteases was identified, explaining the prominence of glutamine at the P1 position. Feature analysis further revealed variations in the length of the β-ribbon, which likely acts as an additional determinant for substrate selection. To validate these structural models, we developed an in vitro test system utilizing active cricket paralysis virus (CrPV) 3C protease and engineered DnaK-based model substrates. Experimental validation confirmed that the residues at positions P2 and P4’ are critical determinants of catalytic efficiency and substrate specificity for CrPV 3C protease. These findings demonstrate that while the P1-stabilization mechanism remains conserved, structural variations in the β-ribbon and distal interactions dictate strict species-specificity, preventing substrate cross-processing within the Dicistroviridae family. Together, our work provides a structural and experimental framework for understanding variations in substrate selection among viral proteases.

Article.Title: Association between allergic conditions and mental health among Japanese university students: a cross-sectional study using the CCAPS-Japanese
Article.Authors: Montano Santoyo L.; Masood A.; Kawamoto M.; Kawamoto N.; Kumagai C.; Horita R.; Tajirika S.; Aiba M.; Fukao T.; Ohnishi H.; Yamamoto M.
Article.Abstract: Although allergic diseases are common worldwide and may affect quality of life and mental health, limited information is available on young adults. This study examined the association between allergic diseases and mental health in Japanese university students. Of 5,657 students undergoing health checkups, 4,010 Japanese students completing the Health Questionnaire on allergy status and the Counseling Center Assessment of Psychological Symptoms-Japanese (CCAPS-Japanese) were included (female/male = 1,849 (46.1%)/2,161 (53.9%); mean age = 20.07 ± 1.833 years). CCAPS-Japanese subscale scores (depression, generalized anxiety, social anxiety, academic distress, eating concerns, family distress, hostility, and alcohol use) were compared by allergy status and related difficulties. The prevalence of self-reported allergic disease in this single-university sample was 44.8%. After adjustment for age and sex and correction for multiple comparisons, no significant differences in subscale scores were observed by allergy status or type. Among 1,616 students with allergies who answered whether their allergy symptoms interfered with their academic or daily life, 157 (9.7%) reported such difficulties. These students had significantly higher generalized anxiety scores than students without allergies and higher family distress scores than both students without allergies and allergic students without difficulties. Assessing allergy-related difficulties in academic or daily life may help identify students who could benefit from mental health support.

Article.Title: Elevation-dependent reorganization of seasonal vegetation greenness dynamics and climate constraints across an arid mountain–oasis–desert system
Article.Authors: Zhuang Z.; Wei X.; Xi Z.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Elevation gradients are associated with pronounced differences in temperature, water availability, and energy conditions, potentially contributing to spatial variation in vegetation responses to climate variability. Previous regional-scale analyses have shown that long-term greening can coexist with contrasting month-to-month greenness changes within the growing season. However, the elevational organization of these seasonal changes and their climatic associations remains insufficiently resolved. Here, we investigated how the magnitude of seasonal greenness dynamics, their climatic associations, and selected temporal response windows vary along an elevational gradient. We integrated SPOT/VEGETATION NDVI observations from 2000 to 2018, MODIS observations during their overlapping period, and CHELSA climate data to examine seasonal vegetation greenness dynamics across the Tarim River Basin (TRB), China. Using trend analysis, partial correlation analysis, Lindeman–Merenda–Gold (LMG) relative-importance decomposition, and lagged climate association analysis, we characterized month- and elevation-dependent patterns in vegetation greenness dynamics and their relationships with temperature, precipitation, and radiation. Long-term monthly NDVI trends were generally positive during the growing season, whereas trends in month-to-month greenness changes differed between early and late seasonal stages. The magnitude of the early–late seasonal contrast exhibited a pronounced non-monotonic relationship with elevation, with a minimum around 1500–2000 m and stronger contrasts at lower and middle-to-high elevations. Climatic associations and relative contributions also varied across months and elevation bands, with differing roles of temperature, precipitation, and radiation. Antecedent climatic conditions were selected more frequently in some higher-elevation combinations, indicating elevation-dependent differences in the statistical temporal windows of climate–vegetation associations. These findings extend previous regional-scale observations of intra-seasonal greenness asymmetry by characterizing its non-monotonic elevational structure and the associated month-by-elevation variation in climatic relationships within the TRB. Elevation therefore provides a useful organizing dimension for describing seasonal vegetation–climate relationships, although the observed patterns may also reflect differences in vegetation composition, land management, and other environmental factors. Joint consideration of seasonal stage, elevation, and antecedent climatic conditions may improve the interpretation of vegetation responses to climate variability in topographically heterogeneous drylands.

Article.Title: Physicochemical properties of Juncao grass (Cenchrus fungigraminus) feedstock and biochar
Article.Authors: Mgoyana S.; Muchaonyerwa P.; Dlamini L.; Vilakazi S.; Mkhonza N.
Article.Abstract: Juncao ( Cenchrus fungigraminus ) is a rapidly growing perennial grass, generating high biomass, and its production ​is expanding in South Africa, and its conversion to biochar remains uncharacterised. This study examined the physicochemical properties of Juncao grass ​and its biochar produced at 350 (J350) and 550 °C (J550). The feedstock and biochar were analysed for proximate and ultimate composition, pH, calcium carbonate equivalent (CCE), mineral concentration, surface functional groups, morphology and surface area. Total carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) were higher in biochar (> 60% C and > 1% N) compared to feedstock (45.5% C and 0.86% N). Pyrolysis at 550 °C increased fixed C, nutrient concentrations, and pH, while volatile matter decreased. The H/C decreased from 1.34 (feedstock) to 0.47 (J350) and 0.27 (J550), and the O/C ratio declined from 0.76 to 0.10 and 0.03. FTIR indicated disappearance of O–H, C–H, and C = O groups and an increase in aromaticity with pyrolysis temperature, whereas scanning electron microscopy (SEM) validated the transformation from dense plant tissue to a more porous biochar structure, particularly at 550 °C. However, the BET surface area remained relatively low (4.66 and 5.54 m 2 g − 1 for 350 and 550 °C, respectively). The findings imply that Juncao grass biochar exhibits increased C, alkalinity, mineral content, and structural porosity as pyrolysis temperature increases, suggesting potential C sequestration.

Article.Title: Operating-condition-decoupled sparse order-domain gear fault monitoring for range-extended hybrid agricultural machinery in hilly and mountainous areas
Article.Authors: Xie X.; Dong J.; Ma H.; Wang S.; Wang P.; Liu Z.; Tan T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vibration signals from range-extended hybrid agricultural machinery in hilly and mountainous areas are strongly nonstationary under variable conditions. Gear-fault components drift and broaden with rotational speed, causing normal fluctuations to overlap fault responses and increasing false alarms and missed detections. This study proposes a operating-condition-decoupled sparse order-domain monitoring (OCD-SOM) method. An operating-condition-powertrain-vibration simulation model and paired-sample strategy ensured that normal and fault samples shared identical slope, vehicle speed, load, battery state of charge (SOC), powertrain state, and speed trajectory, differing only in gear health. Variable-speed vibrations were transformed to the order domain; local amplitude, energy, and prominence features were sparsely selected before support vector machine classification. For 1000 normal and 1000 simulated fault samples, the method achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.9337 ± 0.0181 across five parent-cycle-grouped splits, exceeding frequency-domain and decomposition-based filtering methods by 2.60 and 5.74% points, respectively. Leave-one-level-out validation using mean speed, mean load, slope root mean square, and drive-shaft speed variability achieved 0.9364 across 12 unseen levels. Sensitivity analysis showed that the model maintained good classification performance under the specified limited fault-induced rotational-speed perturbations. The proposed method can mitigate the influence of operating-condition variations on gear fault identification, supporting its algorithmic feasibility for gear condition monitoring under variable-speed conditions and providing a methodological basis for subsequent real-machine validation.

Article.Title: Annual hospital volume and mortality after open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair: a systematic review and dose–response meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Kanemaru E.; Sasaki K.; Miyake T.; Noma H.; Goto T.; Mihara T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Centralisation of open surgical repair of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) has been advocated to improve outcomes, but the potential hospital volume thresholds remain uncertain. This systematic review aimed to quantify the association between annual hospital volume and mortality after open AAA repair and to explore potential volume thresholds. PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were systematically searched for retrospective cohort studies. In-hospital and/or 30-day mortality was analysed using pairwise and dose–response meta-analyses. Thirty-four studies comprising 42 cohorts (259,764 patients) were included. Mortality was significantly lower in high-volume than in low-volume hospitals (relative effect, 0.64; 95% confidence interval, 0.58–0.70). A significant nonlinear relationship was observed for unruptured AAA repair ( p < 0.001), with an estimated threshold of 40–42 annual repairs, whereas no evidence of nonlinearity was found for ruptured AAA repair ( p = 0.270). For the overall cohort, the estimated threshold was 33–46 annual repairs and decreased to 12–18 repairs in analyses restricted to the endovascular aneurysm repair era (from 2005 onwards). Higher hospital volume was associated with lower short-term mortality, although the certainty of evidence was low. These findings characterise the volume–mortality relationship but do not establish a universal minimum-volume threshold.

Article.Title: Green power consumption scheduling via CatBoost–LightGBM forecasting and hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Li J.; Shi M.; Su R.; He G.; Liu K.; Wu K.
Article.Abstract: The increasing penetration of wind and photovoltaic generation creates uncertainty and coordination challenges for power-system operation. This paper develops an integrated green-power scheduling framework that combines a CatBoost–LightGBM forecasting ensemble with hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning. Feature-specific routing, weighted fusion, and residual correction are used to represent heterogeneous meteorological and temporal information. A regional deep Q-network (DQN) agent coordinates distributed virtual power plant (VPP) agents based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm. A constrained multi-objective formulation links renewable-energy utilization, operating cost, carbon emissions, and power balance. Forecast intervals are retained as uncertainty descriptors, although calibrated scenario-based reinforcement learning remains to be validated. Adaptive penalties and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) are used to explore feasible scheduling trade-offs. The framework is evaluated using operational data from an industrial-park VPP in Yunnan, China. The results indicate that forecast quality, coordinated control, storage flexibility, and weather conditions influence scheduling performance. Computational cost, static objective weighting, limited extreme-weather coverage, and scalability to larger VPP populations remain important deployment considerations.

Article.Title: A modular deep learning framework with exact Shapley attribution for explainable stock market forecasting and risk-aware decision support
Article.Authors: Gupta V.; Rathi G.; Sharma R.; Upadhyay R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Explaining a fused trading decision usually requires an approximation. Agentic-Forecast is a modular architecture in which the explanation is exact: forecasting, technical, fundamental, sentiment and risk components each compute a bounded signal, a decision layer fuses these signals into a discrete call, and the small coalition lattice is enumerated in full, so that every Shapley attribution is exact for an explicitly stated cooperative game. The architecture specifies five modules, but the sentiment module produced no usable signal, so the system evaluated empirically fuses four signals. The second contribution is an integrated validation protocol for financial machine learning, comprising a purged walk-forward of the complete pipeline, dependence-aware inference, a leakage audit, a multi-seed study and an analysis of Shapley reference sensitivity. On two years of S&P 500 and DJIA data, and in an extended nested walk-forward over ten years and three indices (about 1,800 out-of-sample decisions per index), the protocol gives a largely negative predictive verdict. Across four purged folds the fused layer averages 38.70% accuracy against a 44.92% majority-class rate. In the extended evaluation its balanced accuracy exceeds chance for two of three indices (0.378 and 0.392), but no fusion model beats a no-skill prior after multiplicity correction and no strategy beats buy-and-hold. Exact attribution is inexpensive, but exactness belongs to the computation, not to the stability of the explanation: baseline and conditional games agree on the dominant signal in only 66–81% of decisions. Neither ablating the components of the forecaster nor replacing the four signals with raw, technical or distance-based inputs changes the verdict, which places the bottleneck in signal construction for these indices rather than in the fusion model.

Article.Title: CDAI and DAS28-CRP agreement in rheumatoid arthritis: a tertiary-care cross-sectional study with exploratory machine learning
Article.Authors: Ghimire S.; Paudyal B.; Ghimire D.; Sharma L.; B. K. K.; Samad M.; Sanwar Hosen A.
Article.Abstract: Accurately evaluating disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis is crucial for guiding treatment decisions and monitoring patient outcomes. The Disease Activity Score based on 28 joints and C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP) is widely used but requires laboratory testing and calculation, which can limit immediate use in resource-constrained settings. The Clinical Disease Activity Index (CDAI) offers a simpler alternative based entirely on clinical assessment. In this cross-sectional tertiary-care study, we examined same-visit agreement between CDAI and DAS28-CRP among 139 treated patients from Nepal and explored internally validated machine-learning (ML) models as a secondary exploratory analysis. CDAI distinguished remission/low from moderate/high DAS28-CRP activity with sensitivity of 88.1%, specificity of 97.2%, and ROC-AUC of 0.983. CDAI and DAS28-CRP were strongly correlated (Spearman \(\rho =0.955\) ; Pearson \(r=0.938\) ), and four-level disease-activity categories showed 71.9% observed agreement with substantial weighted agreement. Exploratory ML models showed high internal performance, but predictors overlapped substantially with DAS28-CRP, the sample was small, and these analyses should not be interpreted as evidence for routine clinical use. Discordant cases, particularly patients classified as remission/low activity by CDAI but moderate/high activity by DAS28-CRP, highlight the need for clinical judgment and laboratory assessment when indicated. These findings support CDAI as a practical assessment tool in this setting, while emphasizing that CDAI should complement rather than replace clinician assessment and that ML findings require external validation.
