Article.Title: Assessing satellite-derived bathymetry across optically complex coastal lagoons using explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Shalby A.; Mohsen A.; Elasbah R.; Fayad S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) offers a cost-effective approach for spatially continuous monitoring of shallow waters, but reliable depth retrieval remains challenging in highly turbid coastal lagoons. This study evaluates a standardized machine-learning SDB workflow across Egypt’s two largest coastal lagoons, Lake Manzala and Lake Burullus, using Sentinel-2 A imagery and field-measured depths. Eight spectral predictors were used to train a multiple linear regression baseline and five machine-learning models: Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, CatBoost, support vector regression, and multilayer perceptron. Performance was evaluated using an independent validation subset comprising 30% of the observations, together with spatial residual analysis, longitudinal bathymetric profiles, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Linear regression performed poorly in both lagoons (R² < 0.30), whereas ensemble models substantially improved depth retrieval. XGBoost performed best in Lake Manzala (R² = 0.75), followed by RF and CatBoost (R² ≈ 0.73). In Lake Burullus, RF and CatBoost were the most stable models (R² = 0.79 and 0.76, respectively), while XGBoost exhibited overfitting. Residual maps and longitudinal profiles confirmed spatial consistency while revealing localized underestimation in channelized zones. SHAP analysis revealed visible-reflectance dominance in Lake Manzala and spectral-ratio control in Lake Burullus, demonstrating site-dependent optical relationships. The results support workflow-level transferability under lagoon-specific calibration and establish pre-rehabilitation bathymetric baselines for future assessment of sedimentation, morphological change, and rehabilitation effectiveness.

Article.Title: Efficacy of nano-formulated Nitazoxanide compared with tablet-derived free Nitazoxanide against human oral squamous cell carcinoma cells
Article.Authors: Elkholy M.; Kishta M.; Moharib B.; Ali S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a therapeutic challenge. This study compared the in-vitro anticancer activity of tablet-derived free Nitazoxanide (NTZ) and Nitazoxanide-nanostructured suspension (NTZ-NS) against SCC-9 cells, using HaCaT keratinocytes as non-malignant controls and Cisplatin as a reference chemotherapeutic drug. Cytotoxicity was assessed by MTT assay, apoptosis and cell-cycle distribution by flow cytometry, and BCL2 and VEGF levels by ELISA. Both formulations of NTZ reduced SCC-9 viability in a dose-dependent manner, with NTZ-NS showing greater potency (IC₅₀ 2.628 µM versus 5.934 µM). HaCaT keratinocytes exhibited lower sensitivity to all treatments, maintaining higher viability than SCC-9 cells across tested concentrations, demonstrating a broader in-vitro selectivity margin rather than complete absence of toxicity at elevated concentrations. NTZ increased late apoptosis to 28.3 ± 0.3% and sub-G1 to 15.00 ± 0.30%; NTZ-NS further increased late apoptosis to 35.6 ± 0.3% and sub-G1 to 19.00 ± 0.30%, while altering S- and G2/M-phase distributions ( n = 3, P < 0.05). Both treatments lowered BCL2 and VEGF, with stronger effects after NTZ-NS. Nano-formulation enhanced the in-vitro activity of NTZ against SCC-9 cells. These findings support further preclinical evaluation; therapeutic applicability cannot be inferred from the present cell-culture data alone.

Article.Title: QuanTCN-SE: a quantum-inspired temporal convolutional network for real-time speech enhancement on edge devices
Article.Authors: Indrakanti R.; Kumar K.; Kasarla S.; Sree P.; Reddy C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Additive noise degrades speech intelligibility in most real-world recording conditions, which creates a need for enhancement systems that remain robust while operating on resource-constrained hardware such as hearing aids, voice-interface modules, and IoT nodes. We present QuanTCN-SE, a compact speech-enhancement network that combines quantum-inspired channel processing with a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) backbone with 2.8 M trainable parameters. The network takes complex short-time Fourier transform (STFT) features, encodes them through a four-stage strided 2-D convolutional encoder, routes them through four cascaded Quantum-TCN blocks, and reconstructs the enhanced waveform through a symmetric decoder that predicts a complex ratio mask. Within each Quantum-TCN block, dilated causal convolutions run in parallel with a Quantum-Inspired Bottleneck (QIB), a classically simulated module that compresses global channel statistics through angle encoding and propagates them through a learned row-stochastic mixing matrix whose role is modelled on, but not equivalent to, the entangling layer of a parameterized quantum circuit. The design follows the structure of parameterized quantum circuits but relies entirely on standard floating-point operations. It therefore runs on any GPU or CPU. The QIB output modulates the convolutional branch through a dense mixing of four encoded angles, each formed from all sixteen pooled channel descriptors, in place of the ReLU bottleneck of a squeeze-and-excitation layer of similar size. An Adaptive Gating Module with separate channel and temporal gates further refines the latent features along both the frequency and time dimensions. Across five independently trained seeds on the VoiceBank-DEMAND benchmark, QuanTCN-SE attained a mean PESQ of 2.76, STOI of 0.94, and SI-SNR of 20.06 dB. A squeeze-and-excitation gate of matched size, trained under the same protocol, reached the same PESQ, STOI, and SI-SNR, so the quantum-inspired module does not raise these metrics. It does change background-noise suppression: the CBAK composite score was 3.19 with the QIB against 2.45 with the squeeze-and-excitation gate, and 3.38 in the four of five seeds in which the effect developed. A four-variant ablation traced this gain to an interaction between the QIB and a small residual path that passes a scaled copy of the noisy spectrum to the output; neither component raised CBAK on its own. In a zero-shot evaluation on a DNS Challenge test subset that was not used in training, the CBAK advantage persisted at a smaller margin (2.17 against 1.79). Because the QIB uses a row-stochastic rather than a unitary mixing matrix and runs entirely in classical arithmetic, these results concern a quantum-inspired inductive bias and do not demonstrate any quantum computational advantage.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial resistance and emerging ESBL-producing uropathogens in children with community-acquired urinary tract infections in cyprus
Article.Authors: Koliou M.; Vassiliadou G.; Ioannou C.; Savva A.; Georgiou E.; Charalambous E.; Papamichail A.; Marcou M.; Tryfonos A.; Mendris M.; Mazeri S.
Article.Abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common bacterial infections in children and a major cause of antibiotic use. Increasing antimicrobial resistance among community-acquired uropathogens complicates empirical therapy. Data from Cyprus are limited. We conducted a retrospective study of children < 16 years hospitalised with a first episode of community-acquired UTI between January 2013 and December 2023 at two tertiary hospitals in Cyprus. Demographic, clinical, microbiological, and antimicrobial susceptibility data were analysed. Resistance trends were compared between 2013 and 2017 and 2018–2023 and extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production was assessed. A total of 489 children were included (47.0% female; median age 4 months). Escherichia coli was the most common pathogen (71.6%), followed by Klebsiella spp . (12.7%) and Enterococcus faecalis (4.1%). High resistance rates were observed to ampicillin (49.7%) and first-generation cephalosporins (33.7%). E. coli resistance to commonly used empirical agents increased significantly over time, including amoxicillin–clavulanate, cefuroxime, ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, and gentamicin ( p < 0.05). Among the 412 E. coli and Klebsiella spp. isolates tested, 13.1% were ESBL-producing, with a significant increase in 2018–2023 ( p = 0.002). ESBL production was identified in 11.7% of E. coli and 21.0% of Klebsiella spp ., and was more frequent in infants < 12 months ( p = 0.019). ESBL isolates showed high co-resistance but remained susceptible to amikacin. Uropathogens in pediatric community-acquired infections in Cyprus, even in first episodes, appear to display higher antimicrobial resistance and ESBL-production rates in later years. Ongoing surveillance is essential to guide empirical therapy and support antimicrobial stewardship.

Article.Title: Distribution and human use shape popularity of threatened plants on Wikipedia
Article.Authors: Pal A.; Brown M.; Bachman S.
Article.Abstract: Increased public awareness is crucial to mitigating the ongoing loss of biodiversity worldwide, and conservation culturomics offers a way to quantify this awareness and its implications for conservation. Large online data repositories provide an opportunity to measure awareness, even for groups such as plants, which receive less attention in global conservation analyses. We used Wikipedia page views in vascular plants across ten language editions (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish) as a proxy for public awareness and quantified differences across extinction risk, documented human use, and geographic range size. We found that overall, threatened species tend to have fewer page views, contrary to expectations. However, after accounting for the covariates of range size and human use, this effect reverses: threatened species receive more page views than non-threatened species. Unsurprisingly, useful species and those with larger ranges tend to receive more page views than those without documented use, suggesting that people are inclined to search online for plants that provide ecosystem services. In addition, our results strongly suggest that there is heightened public awareness of threatened plants in their local-language (Wikipedia language used in each ‘botanical country’ region). We present the first global study of vascular plants using Wikipedia page views as a proxy for public awareness through conservation culturomics to understand human-plant relationships.

Article.Title: Research on the influence of gas components on the measurement values of optical interference methane detector and correction methods
Article.Authors: Xue S.; Liu J.; Lou L.; Liu F.; Yang Z.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: To investigate how gas components affect the measurement error of an optical interference methane detector, the detector’s measurement principle was analyzed, and a model was established to quantify the influence of gas composition on methane readings. O₂ and CO₂ were selected as the main influencing factors because they are the major variable components affecting the refractive index of mine gas, whereas other interfering gases are usually present only at trace levels under normal mine conditions. The quantitative relationships between variations in O₂ and CO₂ volume fractions and the indicated methane concentration were derived and experimentally validated. Based on the experimental results, an O₂-based correction model was developed and evaluated in a field case at an underground coal mine. The results show that the detector reading decreases linearly with increasing O₂ volume fraction and increases linearly with increasing CO₂ volume fraction. A 1% decrease in O₂ volume fraction results in a 0.1927% increase in the indicated CH₄ concentration, whereas a 1% increase in CO₂ volume fraction results in a 1.0776% increase, indicating a stronger theoretical influence of CO₂. The experimental relationships for O₂ exhibit good linearity, with R 2 > 0.97. However, because the CO₂ concentration in underground coal mines is usually below 0.5% and varies only slightly, O₂ variation is the dominant practical factor affecting the measurement result. The proposed correction method brings the readings within the allowable error range, providing a practical approach for enhancing methane monitoring accuracy in underground coal mines.

Article.Title: Assessment of model uncertainty based on model level and application method
Article.Authors: Radwan M.; Kövesdi B.
Article.Abstract: The present study explores the influence of different numerical modelling approaches on the determination of model factors for global buckling, adopted in this work as a representative structural stability phenomenon. Beam, shell and solid element models are investigated through both deterministic analyses and stochastic Monte Carlo simulations. The performed simulations take into account the variability in material and geometrical properties, enabling a more realistic representation of the global buckling behaviour. Three reliability-based methods are employed to evaluate the corresponding model factors and to assess the influence of the modelling approach and the selected reliability-based method on the resulting design buckling resistance. The results indicate that the evaluated model factors are generally consistent across the different modelling approaches, suggesting a limited sensitivity to the adopted formulation of finite elements. However, this insensitivity holds true for the studied case, in which all three models can lead to consistent global buckling resistance, with local instabilities prevented. In contrast, the choice of the reliability-based method has a pronounced effect on the resulting design buckling resistance, providing a more improved estimation of the design resistance while reducing the conservative estimation, and maintaining consistency with the Eurocode standards. The provided results aid the designer in the process of selecting an appropriate modelling approach and reliability-based method for the assessment of the resistance.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: global buckling; structural stability; model uncertainty; Monte Carlo simulation; reliability-based design; Eurocode

Article.Title: Wearable ear-EEG can record brain activity during auditory tasks in hyperacusis
Article.Authors: Das A.; Rivera Rosario E.; Zhong Y.; Bo W.; Gherardi A.; Sun W.; Xu W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hyperacusis, characterized by physical discomfort from everyday sounds, lacks an objective measure, so clinicians rely on questionnaires and loudness discomfort levels, which give inconsistent diagnoses. Ear electroencephalography (ear-EEG) could fill this gap but, to our knowledge, is untested in hyperacusis. We recorded cEEGrid ear-EEG in 21 adults with hyperacusis and 13 controls during loudness, speech-in-noise, aversive-sound and visual fixation tasks. All participants completed the tasks, data quality was similar between groups, and most showed alpha peaks and stimulus-locked phase coherence. Onset power during speech in noise, the primary outcome, was higher in hyperacusis in every planned sensitivity analysis (Hedges’ $$g = 0.86$$ ) and absent in the visual task. Further analyses found no relation to hearing thresholds, but its source is not yet identified, because it spanned $$\theta $$ to , appeared before the sound and shrank when single epochs were down-weighted. Between-ear $$\delta $$ synchronization in this task was lower in hyperacusis and passed correction at ages 18–40 without hearing loss, although at this sample size none of 29 hypotheses from an exploratory analysis survived study-wide correction. Ear-EEG during auditory tasks is therefore feasible, and both effects are candidates for confirmatory testing, which for onset power needs 47–104 per group.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: hyperacusis; ear-EEG; speech perception in noise; phase coherence

Article.Title: An efficient high voltage gain DC–DC converter with reduced switch voltage stress
Article.Authors: Gholami M.; Hajilou M.; Farzanehfard H.; Adib E.
Article.Abstract: This paper introduces a high step-up DC–DC converter derived from a modified quasi-Y-source structure, aiming to achieve high voltage gain while maintaining low voltage stress on power switches. The proposed topology integrates a switched-capacitor cell with a reconfigured basic structure to improve the converter specifications. In this converter, diodes conduction losses are effectively mitigated, and zero-voltage switching (ZVS) at turn-on is achieved for all switches. In addition, all diodes turn off under zero-current conditions, which significantly reduces reverse recovery losses. The leakage inductance energy is properly managed and transferred to the load, while capacitive turn-on losses are inherently avoided which have improved the overall converter efficiency. The topology also features a continuous input current and a common ground between the input and output terminals, making it suitable for a wide range of power conversion applications. The proposed converter operating principles and steady-state characteristics are analyzed in detail. Experimental results obtained from a 200W laboratory prototype confirm the theoretical analysis.

Article.Title: High-isolation 18-element multiband mMIMO antenna system for 5G smartphones using metallic side frames
Article.Authors: Jaglan N.; Parthasarathy H.; Kishk A.
Article.Abstract: An 18-element multiband massive MIMO slot antenna system has been developed for 5G-enabled smartphones. The proposed design operates in LTE bands 42 (3.4–3.6 GHz), 43 (3.6–3.8 GHz), and 46 (5.15–5.925 GHz), thereby covering a wide range of global 5G frequency allocations. Each antenna element is excited through a U-shaped feedline coupled to an inverted T-shaped slot, enabling compact integration within the limited space of a smartphone chassis. To reduce mutual coupling between adjacent antenna elements, etched isolation slots are introduced on the metallic frame of the device. Both full-wave electromagnetic simulations and experimental measurements confirm the stable performance of the proposed system, achieving an envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) below 0.07 and a radiation efficiency exceeding 87% across all operating bands. In addition, the channel capacity analysis based on the Kronecker model shows that the maximum achievable throughput is 99.5 bps/Hz. The practical feasibility of the antenna system was confirmed with realistic smartphone conditions, such as user interaction, display module influence and battery placement. Furthermore, an information-theoretic approach that relates the electromagnetic coupling between the transmitting and receiving antenna surfaces to the mutual information between the two surfaces is introduced.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: envelope correlation coefficient; 5G smartphones; channel capacity; mutual information; mutual coupling reduction; Kronecker channel model
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Antenna Design and Analysis; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Antenna Design and Optimization; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Electromagnetic Compatibility and Measurements

Article.Title: A Gamma–Power Ailamujia Hybrid Distribution for Bayesian and likelihood inference under progressive Type-II censoring
Article.Authors: Almetwally E.; Gomaa R.; Tolba A.; Magar A.
Article.Abstract: We develop a flexible hybrid lifetime modeling framework for censored data with complex hazard-rate behavior, termed the Gamma–Power Ailamujia Hybrid Distribution (GPAHD). The proposed model integrates generalized gamma and power Ailamujia mechanisms to accommodate a wide range of hazard shapes and to enhance the analysis of lifetime and economic-type duration data, particularly under censoring. Key theoretical properties are derived, including moments, entropy measures, and structural characteristics of the hazard rate. For inference under progressive Type-II censoring, we construct maximum likelihood estimators and a Bayesian MCMC procedure under both squared-error and LINEX loss functions, enabling symmetric and asymmetric decision settings. Extensive Monte Carlo experiments across multiple sample sizes and censoring schemes demonstrate the finite-sample behavior of the proposed estimators and highlight the benefits of Bayesian estimation with informative priors in small and censored samples. The empirical utility of the GPAHD is illustrated using two real datasets on economic growth determinants and polyester fiber tensile strength, where the proposed model yields competitive–and often superior–fit relative to standard alternatives.

Article.Title: Numerical investigation of wrapped-face back-to-back reinforced soil walls: wall separation and the mobilized earth pressure
Article.Authors: Malekmohammadi K.; Dias D.; Lajevardi S.
Article.Abstract: Back-to-back reinforced soil walls (RSWs) are widely used for bridge approaches and narrow embankments, but the available numerical evidence derives mostly from rigid or modular facing systems. Unlike rigid facing, a geosynthetic wrap provides negligible flexural rigidity, so lateral earth pressure is resisted only by soil–reinforcement interaction. Plane-strain finite element analyses simulate the staged construction of 6 m high wrapped-face back-to-back RSWs, evaluating wall separation, reinforcement continuity, vertical spacing, foundation stiffness, reinforcement creep and constitutive soil model. The largest change in response occurs when the two reinforced zones lose contact, rather than at the boundary between interacting and independent walls defined in design guidance. Separation increases displacements and tensile loads and lowers the factor of safety. Reinforcement continuity mainly reduces facing deformation, whereas vertical spacing controls both deformation and stability. Softer foundations reduce facing displacement while lowering the factor of safety, so facing displacement alone is an unreliable performance indicator. Over the design life, reinforcement creep increases facing displacement by about 26–30% but relaxes tensile loads. The mobilized earth pressure remains close to the at-rest state with the Hardening Soil model and vertical spacings up to 0.4 m, including after creep, but close to the active state with Mohr–Coulomb.

Article.Title: Characterisation of marsupial oviductal fluid during oestrus: a metabolite and protein profile for the fat-tailed dunnart
Article.Authors: Hutchinson A.; Fenelon J.; Cook L.; Beilby K.; Pask A.
Article.Abstract: Many Australian marsupial species are endangered, yet assisted reproductive technologies (ART), including in vitro fertilisation (IVF), remain largely undeveloped. Successful IVF requires media that supports gametes and embryos, and in particular, facilitates sperm capacitation. Here, we used the fat-tailed dunnart as a model to characterise the composition of oviductal fluid at oestrus, with the aim of identifying candidate factors for in vitro support of marsupial spermatozoa. Using LC/MS, we profiled 132 metabolites, 3002 proteins, and sex steroids—progesterone, oestradiol, and oestrone—generating the first comprehensive dataset for marsupial oviductal biology. The oestrus oviduct exhibited heightened energy metabolism through glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, abundant amino acids, fatty acids, and nucleosides, and protein enrichment associated with cilia growth, sperm motility, oocyte maturation, fertilisation, and embryogenesis. Biochemical and macromolecular factors supporting extended sperm storage were identified, with fructose, glucose, and citric acid as potential substrates. Shared proteins with placental mammals, such as CAPS and NME5, suggest conserved roles in sperm-oocyte interactions, while marsupial-specific proteins, including conceptus-coat mucin and vitellogenin, provide insight into viviparity evolution. This novel dataset offers a foundation for optimising ART in marsupials.

Article.Title: System-level multi-objective co-optimization of an MPPT boost converter and DTC motor for photovoltaic water pumping system
Article.Authors: Alzamil A.; Kechida R.; Gacem A.; Naoui M.; Touil S.; Khechekhouche A.; Albaker A.; Alateeq A.; Chughtai M.; Marouani I.; Guesmi T.
Article.Abstract: Photovoltaic water pumping systems (PWPSs) represent a promising solution for sustainable irrigation in remote areas. However, their overall performance strongly depends on the coordinated operation of the photovoltaic (PV) generator, power converter, motor drive, and hydraulic load under highly variable solar conditions. Conventional design approaches typically optimize each subsystem independently, which may lead to suboptimal global performance. This paper proposes a system-level multi-objective co-optimization framework for a PV water pumping system based on direct torque control of an induction motor. The proposed framework integrates an adaptive Incremental Conductance (AD-INC) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) to jointly optimize the boost converter parameters (L, Cin and Cout) and PI speed controller gains (Kp and Ki), thereby improving energy conversion, speed regulation, torque-ripple performance, and hydraulic operation. The AD-INC algorithm employs a variable step-size mechanism with stability-aware adjustment to improve tracking dynamics and reduce steady-state oscillations around the maximum power point. The optimization framework combines power mismatch, torque and speed regulation, and hydraulic flow into a unified weighted objective function. MATLAB/Simulink simulations are conducted under different irradiance levels to assess the electrical, electromechanical, and hydraulic performance of the optimized system. Compared with conventional DTC, the GWO-based configuration achieves up to 83.6% reduction in torque ripple, 95.45% reduction in steady-state speed error, and 64.3% reduction in speed settling time. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system-level co-optimization framework in improving the dynamic and overall operating performance of the PV-driven water pumping system.

Article.Title: Transitioning from opportunistic to organized cervical precancer and breast cancer screening using a community register model in Ghana
Article.Authors: Effah K.; Tekpor E.; Wormenor C.; Goka E.; Legbedze G.; Kpodo C.; Appiah E.; Kemawor S.; Danyo S.; Sesenu E.; Tay G.; Koranteng J.; Glover R.; Zigah M.; Essel N.
Article.Abstract: Breast and cervical cancer impose a high burden on women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Ghana, where opportunistic screening is the status quo. This paper evaluates a pilot program aimed at transitioning Ghana from opportunistic to organized screening for these cancers by utilizing community-based registers to systematically identify and invite eligible women for screening and foster community ownership for acceptability and continuity. The paper presents the framework, participation rates, and outcomes of the pilot, offering insights critical for future efforts in similar contexts.​ This retrospective cross-sectional study details the development and implementation of a transition model piloted in two rural communities in the North Tongu District of Ghana, Fodzoku and Torgorme between June 2022 and April 2024. Cervical cancer screening involved high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV) DNA testing and Visual Inspection with Acetic acid (VIA) while breast cancer screening involved clinical breast examination (CBE). Local health workers trained at the Cervical Cancer Prevention and Training Centre (CCPTC) conducted the screenings. Firth penalized binary logistic regression models were fitted to explore factors associated with hr-HPV infection and VIA positivity.​ This pilot program registered 577 eligible women, representing a registration rate of 63.6% (95% CI, 60.4 − 66.8) among ≥ 25-year-old women in both towns. The screening uptake among women registered was 42.4% (95% CI, 38.4 − 46.6) and 42.8% (95% CI, 38.7 − 47.0) in the Breast and Cervical arms, respectively, whereas the screening uptake among all eligible women based on the latest census was 27.0% (95% CI, 24.1 − 30.0) and 27.2% (95% CI, 24.4 − 30.3), respectively. CBE revealed clinically significant masses in 2 (0.8%), lymphadenopathy in 1 (0.4%), and nipple discharge in 4 (1.6%) women. The overall hr-HPV prevalence among 246 women tested was 36.2% (95% CI, 30.2 − 42.5), disaggregated as 4.9% (95% CI, 2.5 − 8.4) for HPV16, 2.8% (95% CI, 1.2 − 5.8) for HPV18, and 34.1% (95% CI, 28.2 − 40.4) for other hr-HPV types. VIA positivity was 4.5% (95% CI, 2.3 − 7.9) among 244 women screened. A higher number of lifetime pregnancies (aOR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.77–0.98) was associated with lower odds of hr-HPV infection, whereas prior gynecological surgery (aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 0.96–5.47) and current contraceptive use (aOR, 1.95; 95% CI, 0.96–3.97) showed elevated but imprecise odds.​ The CCPTC model, piloted over nearly two years in these two rural communities, provides valuable insights for transitioning to organized screening in LMICs. Screening uptake, especially in the Cervical arm relative to the WHO 90-70-90 targets, remains low despite community-level implementation and service provision at no cost to the women. Further studies are required to address these participation gaps in organized screening efforts.

Article.Title: Human expert-generated flexibility program versus single-attempt AI (Gemini 2.5 Pro)-generated flexibility program for office workers: a quasi-randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Sönmez M.; Akaras E.
Article.Abstract: Sedentary office environments contribute to flexibility loss and musculoskeletal disorders. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers scalable rehabilitation, its clinical reasoning and biomechanical safety remain scrutinized in academic literature. This study compared the efficacy of 15-minute home-based flexibility exercises designed by human experts versus those generated by AI (Gemini 2.5 Pro) on flexibility, lower back health, and muscle stiffness. In this quasi-randomized controlled trial, 30 male participants were allocated to a Human Expert Group ( n = 15) or an AI Group ( n = 15) using a random start (single coin toss) followed by alternating allocation, which differed from the wording of the ethics-approved application (simple random method, coin toss) and carries a risk of selection bias. Interventions lasted 4 weeks (3 days/week). Assessments included Sit-and-Reach tests, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and MyotonPRO stiffness measurements. Initially, the groups exhibited similar characteristics ( p > .05). In the Sit-and-Reach test, a measure of flexibility, the average score for the human expert group increased from 14.93 ± 10.67 cm to 22.60 ± 11.49 cm, while in the artificial intelligence group, this value reached only from 16.23 ± 7.91 to 17.53 ± 7.60 cm; a statistically significant Time × Group interaction with a large effect size was detected between the groups (F(1,28) = 28.26, p < .001, ηp² = 0.502). A significant Time × Group interaction was also found for the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) (F(1,28) = 7.49, p = .011, ηp² = 0.211). Following Benjamini–Hochberg False Discovery Rate (BH-FDR) multiplicity adjustment across the eight interaction tests, statistically significant Time × Group interactions robustly survived for Sit-and-Reach flexibility ( p < .001), Oswestry Disability Index ( p = .011), dominant biceps femoris stiffness (F(1,28) = 11.01, p = .003, ηp² = 0.282), and non-dominant gastrocnemius stiffness (F(1,28) = 11.16, p = .002, ηp² = 0.285) in favor of the human expert group. In contrast, the Time × Group interaction for dominant erector spinae stiffness was nominally significant prior to adjustment only (F(1,28) = 4.41, raw p = .045, ηp² = 0.136) and did not survive FDR correction. No significant interactions were observed for the remaining muscle groups ( p > .05). Based on the observed Time × Group interaction effects, human expert-generated programs containing dynamic and static flexibility exercises yielded significantly greater improvement over time in flexibility and lower-back health than the single-shot static stretching program generated by Gemini 2.5 Pro. These findings highlight the short-term efficacy of the specific expert-designed dynamic protocol rather than demonstrating a generalized limitation of generative AI in exercise prescription. Trial registration : The study was registered on Clinicaltrials.gov under the number NCT07242287. (Date of Registration 11/17/2025)

Article.Title: Dietary diversity and associated factors among women of reproductive age in Banja District, Northwest Ethiopia: a mixed–method study
Article.Authors: Eshetu D.; Molla M.; Molla H.; Agezew Y.
Article.Abstract: Adequate dietary diversity is essential for the health and nutrition of women of reproductive age. Evidence on factors influencing dietary diversity among non-pregnant, non-lactating women in Ethiopia is limited. This study assessed dietary diversity and its sociocultural determinants among women in Banja District, Northwest Ethiopia. A concurrent embedded mixed-methods design was employed to quantify dietary diversity and identify associated factors, while the qualitative component provided contextual insights into the sociocultural influences on women’s dietary practices. The quantitative component was a community-based cross-sectional study among 497 women selected using multistage and systematic random sampling techniques. Dietary diversity was assessed using a 24-hour dietary recall, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify associated factors. The qualitative component comprised 17 key informant interviews and 10 in-depth interviews, with participants selected through purposive sampling. Quantitative data were analyzed using Stata version 17, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically using ATLAS.ti version 9. The prevalence of minimum dietary diversity was 34.4% (95% CI: 30.2–38.6%). Women with a college education or above (AOR = 3.2; 95% CI: 1.8–5.7), merchant occupation (AOR = 2.0; 95% CI: 1.2–3.4), high food and nutrition knowledge (AOR = 6.0; 95% CI: 3.0–12.0), and fruit and vegetable consumption at least twice weekly (AOR = 3.0; 95% CI: 1.7–5.3) were more likely to achieve adequate dietary diversity, whereas women from food-insecure households were less likely (AOR = 0.35; 95% CI: 0.20–0.60). Qualitative analysis generated three major themes: structural and household barriers to dietary diversity; cultural beliefs and perceptions regarding food and nutrition; and food taboos, household restrictions, and cultural eating norms. These themes highlighted the influence of economic constraints, women’s workload, food and nutrition knowledge, cooking skills, perceptions of nutritious foods, cultural and religious beliefs, food taboos, household food restrictions, and social and gender-based eating norms on women’s dietary practices. Dietary diversity among women of reproductive age in Banja District was low. It was influenced by education, income, nutrition knowledge, fruit consumption, household food security, and sociocultural factors. Interventions should target nutrition education, economic empowerment, and culturally sensitive strategies.

Article.Title: Mechanisms underlying Ginsenoside Rg1-mediated promotion of angiogenesis via regulation of microvascular endothelial cells following spinal cord injury
Article.Authors: Yin S.; Wu Z.; Xia F.; Shen K.; Zou W.; Lu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ginsenoside Rg1 (GRg1), a predominant bioactive ingredient in Panax ginseng , has therapeutic potential for spinal cord injury (SCI). This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying GRg1-mediated regulation of angiogenesis in spinal cord microvascular endothelial cells (SCMECs) following SCI. In vitro, primary SCMECs were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation to mimic the ischemic-hypoxic microenvironment after SCI. Western blotting (WB) was utilized to investigate the effect of GRg1 on vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression in SCMECs. Network pharmacology was utilized to predict potential signaling pathways involved in GRg1-induced pro-angiogenesis. Subsequently, a pathway-specific inhibitor was administered to GRg1-treated SCMECs. Key pathway protein expression, cell proliferation, and angiogenic capacity were evaluated via WB, immunofluorescence staining, and tube formation assays, respectively. In vivo, rat and mouse SCI models were established, followed by intraperitoneal GRg1 administration. VEGF protein levels were measured by WB. Angiogenesis and neurorepair at the injury site were assessed by immunofluorescence staining. Hindlimb motor function recovery was evaluated using footprint analysis. The results showed that GRg1 significantly upregulated VEGF expression in SCMECs. Network pharmacology analysis identified the JAK2/STAT3 pathway as a key potential target of GRg1. AG490 markedly inhibited GRg1-induced VEGF upregulation, cell proliferation, and tube formation in SCMECs. In vivo, GRg1 increased VEGF expression in rat spinal cord tissue, augmented angioneural repair at the lesion site in mice, and promoted hindlimb motor function recovery in both species. These findings suggest that GRg1 promotes angiogenesis after SCI by modulating SCMEC function, which may contribute to neurological recovery.

Article.Title: Developing a hybrid framework for intermodal terminal planning in Uzbekistan
Article.Authors: Mukhamedova Z.; Mukhamedova D.; Fayzibayev S.; Turdiev O.; Kasimov O.; Shoisaeva M.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid decision-support framework, the first developed specifically for Uzbekistan, that incorporates a statistical binary logit model with an AnyLogic-Python hybrid simulation to optimize intermodal terminal site selection within the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan. The statistical stage uses a binary logit model to examine the relationship between station characteristics and expert-defined terminal suitability and to rank expert-eligible stations according to their fitted probabilities. The three highest-ranked eligible locations-Chukursay, Sergeli, and Angren-are subsequently transferred to the second stage for comparative operational evaluation using an AnyLogic-Python hybrid simulation, with GIS-based routing and Python-supported analysis. The simulation compares the candidate-terminal scenarios under a common operational framework using key performance indicators (KPIs), including journey time, modal split, terminal utilization, and freight flows. The simulation stage provides a cross-stage operational assessment rather than independent external validation of the statistical model. The integrated framework provides central policymakers with an evidence-based decision-support approach for investment planning, policy design, and long-term development of intermodal terminal infrastructure in the Tashkent region.

Article.Title: Urinary tobacco-specific nitrosamines and cotinine are associated with early childhood caries
Article.Authors: Patil S.; Cardenas A.; Pillarisetti A.; Steenland K.; Patil S.; Amare S.; Balakrishnan K.; Waller L.; Jabbarzadeh S.; Peel J.; Clasen T.; Barr D.; Gota V.; Puttaswamy N.
Article.Abstract: Urinary cotinine is a well-established biomarker of nicotine exposure and has been associated with an increased risk of early childhood caries (ECC). However, the role of tobacco-specific nitrosamines remains unclear. We concurrently measured urinary cotinine, 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanol (NNAL), and N′-nitrosonornicotine (NNN) among 167 Indian preschoolers (mean age: 4.08 ± 0.5 years) in the Household Air Pollution Intervention Network cohort. Exposure was stratified using the NEG–TEG–MEG framework to capture gradations of environmental tobacco smoke intensity. Dental caries were assessed clinically, and biomarkers were measured via liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Negative binomial hurdle models examined associations between biomarker concentrations and ECC. Each log-unit increase in cotinine (IRR:1.15; 95% CI:1.02–1.30) and NNN (IRR:1.11; 95% CI:1.01–1.23) levels corresponded to higher ECC incidence in the count component. Children in the highest quartile of cotinine and NNN exhibited 49% (β: 0.40) and 39% (β: 0.33) greater caries incidence, respectively. In zero model, children in the second quartile of NNN had 71% lower odds of being caries-free, suggesting that even moderate exposure increases ECC susceptibility. The NNAL/cotinine ratio was suggestive of potential thirdhand smoke exposure. Significant associations between tobacco-derived toxicants and ECC highlight the need for targeted interventions to reduce secondhand and thirdhand smoke exposure in early childhood.

Article.Title: Soil and environmental gradients driving riparian vegetation structure on two Nile River islands, Luxor Governorate, Upper Egypt
Article.Authors: Nadi A.; Mohamed E.; Kasem A.; Ghanem A.; Badry M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Documenting, updating, and evaluating the phytoremediation potential of natural riparian plants are essential for plant conservation. As part of ongoing floristic surveys on the Nile River islands in Upper Egypt, the present study investigates vegetation–environment relationships across three ecologically distinct sites on two Nile River islands in Luxor Governorate (Armant Island: sites 1 and 2; Aqalata Island: site 3); and to evaluate phytoremediation efficiency of some macrophytes ( Setaria geminata (Forssk.) Veldkamp, Ceratophyllum demersum L., Myriophyllum spicatum L., Persicaria senegalensis (Meisn.) Soják, and Ludwigia adscendens subsp. diffusa (Forssk.) P.H. Raven) in these islands for non essential heavy metals lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd). Cd and Pb concentrations in the water at all three sites were within safe limits for irrigation water. While Pb in sediments is within the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) safe limit, Cd levels in the sediments exceeded those limits. In contrast, Pb and Cd levels in all studied species fell within the permissible limits during all seasons. The bioaccumulation factors (BAFs) exceeded one for Pb in the submerged species C. demersum and M. spicatum , while the value for Cd exceeded one in M. spicatum only. Translocation factors (TFs) for both metals, Pb and Cd, were less than one, except for Pb in S. geminata and L. adscendens . These results suggest that submerged species, particularly C. demersum , are suitable for phytoextraction, while emergent macrophytes are suitable for biomonitoring. For vegetation analysis, a total of 80 species from 30 families (52 annuals and 28 perennials) were recorded. Poaceae, Fabaceae, Asteraceae, and Brassicaceae are the most diverse families, accounting for 47.50% of the total flora. Therophytes (53.75%) were the most common life form, with a strong cosmopolitan affinity, indicating that widespread species dominate the studied islands. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) ordination reveals distinct environmental gradients and species distributions across the sampled sites. CCA axis 1 (58.5% variance) clearly separated site 1, characterized by sandy sediments, high pH, and elevated Cd, from the finer-textured, nutrient- and ion-rich sites 2 and 3. The sandy, low-retention environment of site 1 supports a distinct flora adapted to disturbance. CCA axis 2 (41.5% variance) further partitioned site 2 (clay-rich, waterlogged, high organic matter) from site 3 (disturbance-driven). Our findings show that sediment texture, nutrient content, waterlogging, and localized anthropogenic impacts (agricultural runoff, tourism, and related heavy metals) act as cooperative filters, assembling distinct floristic communities on each island. The study expands our understanding of riparian biodiversity in human-influenced arid-region river systems, emphasizing that even small riparian islands serve as sensitive indicators of the interactions between natural and anthropogenic gradients.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a multi-omics model for early glaucoma diagnosis and prediction in high-risk populations
Article.Authors: Meng J.; Huang X.; Yang M.; Yuan C.
Article.Abstract: To develop and validate a multi-omics integration-based predictive model for early glaucoma diagnosis in high-risk populations, thereby providing a quantitative tool for early clinical screening and intervention. A total of 342 consecutive participants with high-risk factors for glaucoma were enrolled and randomly allocated into a training set and a validation set at a 7:3 ratio. Clinical, imaging, and multi-omics indicators—including intraocular pressure (IOP), vertical cup-to-disc ratio (vCDR), retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFLT), ganglion cell complex thickness (GCCT), latent transforming growth factor beta binding protein 2 (LTBP2), and D-glucose-6-phosphate—were collected. Univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression was applied to identify independent influencing factors (vCDR was entered into the model per 0.1-unit increment). Three machine learning models—Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine, and logistic regression—were then constructed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under curve (AUC) the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, and decision curves. Furthermore, SHAP analysis was applied to interpret feature contributions. Univariate analysis revealed significant differences between the early glaucoma and non-glaucoma groups for all six indicators ( P < 0.05). And all six factors as independent predictors of early glaucoma in high-risk individuals ( P < 0.05). RF demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.863 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.803–0.923) in the training set and 0.785 (95% CI 0.670–0.900) in the validation set. SHAP analysis ranked feature contributions in descending order as: RNFLT, vCDR, IOP, D-glucose-6-phosphate, GCCT, and LTBP2. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. Additionally, decision curves confirmed a high net clinical benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. A multi-omics integration-based predictive model for early glaucoma diagnosis was successfully constructed and validated, which serves as an objective, quantitative auxiliary tool for identifying early glaucoma in high-risk populations.

Article.Title: Large language model diagnostic performance across informant sources in child and adolescent psychiatry: a prospective multicenter study
Article.Authors: Kayış H.; Tahıllıoğlu A.; Hira Selen A.; Gedizlioğlu Ç.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for mental health assessment, yet child and adolescent psychiatric diagnosis depends on information from multiple informants. It remains unclear how the source and richness of clinical information influence LLM diagnostic performance. This study evaluated diagnostic accuracy across child, parent, combined, and clinician-enriched information conditions and compared performance across three widely used LLMs. This prospective multicenter study included 220 children and adolescents aged 1–17 years presenting to two university child and adolescent psychiatry clinics in Turkey. Presenting complaints were obtained separately from children and parents. Four input conditions were created: child only, parent only, child plus parent, and child plus parent supplemented with physician-derived clinical information. Three LLMs were evaluated using independent single-turn API queries, followed by two repeat runs to assess reproducibility. Clinician-established DSM-5 diagnoses served as the reference standard. Performance was assessed using Top-1 and Top-3 accuracy, mean reciprocal rank, Cohen’s kappa, F1 scores, and sensitivity and specificity for detecting any psychiatric diagnosis. Models and conditions were compared with paired tests and generalized estimating equation models. Top-1 accuracy was lowest in the child-only condition (35.5–44.1% across models), increased to 65.9–69.1% with parent information, and was highest when physician-derived information was added (78.6–83.2%). Adding the child narrative to the parent narrative did not significantly improve accuracy (69.1–71.8%). Full-information Top-3 accuracy ranged from 88.2 to 91.8%. Model differences were significant only in the child-only condition. With parent narratives, sensitivity for any psychiatric diagnosis exceeded 93%, but specificity was 14.3–42.9%; physician-derived information increased specificity to 52.4–61.9%. Age was associated with higher accuracy only in the child-only condition (OR = 1.164 per year, 95% CI 1.071–1.264). Two repeat runs reproduced the main information-condition findings; between-model differences were less consistent. LLM diagnostic performance varied with the available clinical information, with the highest accuracy observed when physician-derived findings were included. Adding child narratives to parent reports did not significantly improve accuracy, and the models frequently assigned diagnoses to children without a psychiatric disorder. These observational findings are based on routine clinician-established diagnoses and do not demonstrate improvements in clinical decision-making or patient outcomes.

Article.Title: Resource-aware device-level control of air-conditioning load clusters for load shaping
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Wang H.; Yan S.; Zhao Z.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Aggregated air-conditioning (AC) loads can support load shaping, but cluster requests must be translated into discrete device actions as resources and thermal margins change. We present a resource-aware device-level control method with two mechanisms: online resource-aware admissible-target correction, which filters the request using predicted and online resources and aggregate stress; and paced device-level setpoint dispatch, which uses action budgets, safeguards, and thermal-laxity ordering for 0.5 \(^{\circ }\) C updates. We evaluated 1004 residential AC units over 28 days in 1-min closed-loop simulations. Nominally, E4 achieved mean peak reduction and peak-valley-difference (PVD) improvement of 3.154% and 3.521%, with 9.266 actions per device and 0.347% control-induced thermal violation. A representative constrained MPC-QP achieved higher mean peak reduction and PVD improvement (3.590% and 3.967%) with fewer actions (3.669 per device), but had a 2.415% control-induced thermal-violation rate. This comparison revealed load-shaping–execution–thermal-risk operating points. Parameter sensitivity and degradation under four uncertainty models were evaluated. Under an uncompensated 5-min actuation delay, E4’s PVD improvement fell to 0.715% and actions rose to 74.770 per device. Conclusions are limited to the simulated population and load-shaping metrics; field operation and feeder-level power flow were not evaluated.

Article.Title: Parkinson’s disease awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, and intended practices among adults in Palestine: an online cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Hassouneh D.; Al-Hasanat A.; Dodeen M.; Arafat M.; Qawasmi E.; Hajahja R.; Raed S.; Hasan A.; Altell J.; Sowaity O.; Deeb S.; Amro A.
Article.Abstract: Evidence on community understanding of Parkinson’s disease (PD) in Palestine is limited. The mean score was 8.11 ± 4.17. Tremor was recognized by 77.5%, compared with 8.7% for reduced smell and 8.5% for constipation. These findings suggest educational needs among respondents, especially for non-motor manifestations and support resources. Article.Title: Reservoir properties and their controls on oil accumulation in the Chang7–Chang9 members, southern Zhouchang area, Ordos Basin
Article.Authors: Sun B.; Bai J.; Zhao X.; Li C.; Wu W.
Article.Abstract: Reservoir properties and their controls on tight oil accumulation constitute a key component of tight oil enrichment mechanisms. This study focuses on tight sandstone reservoirs of the Chang7–Chang9 members in the southern Zhouchang area of the Ordos Basin. By integrating well-logging, drilling, core, formation-testing and production-test data, we characterize reservoir attributes, including sand-body thickness, lithology, pore space, and petrophysical properties, classify reservoir types, and discuss how reservoir conditions govern tight-oil distribution. The results indicate that the dominant cumulative sand-body thickness for each oil group of the Chang7–Chang9 peaks at 15–30 m, while individual sand-bed thickness is dominantly 2–6 m, accounting for 62.0% of the total. The reservoirs are predominantly fine-grained arkose, with calcite and chlorite as the major interstitial materials. Intergranular dissolution pores and primary intergranular pores constitute the dominant reservoir space. The reservoirs have a mean porosity of 6.9% and a median permeability of 0.33 × 10 − 3 µm 2 , classifying them as tight reservoirs, which are further grouped into three categories: Type I, Type II and Type III. Shielded by mudstone and siltstone, tight oil occurs in lenticular bodies with coexisting oil and water during production, exhibiting quasi-continuous distribution in clusters and belts. Porosity and shale content are the primary controls on tight oil enrichment, followed by permeability, whereas sand-body thickness exerts a relatively weak control. Based on the current data analysis, Combined with the oil-bearing signatures of these tight sandstones, sand bodies with thickness = 10–15 m, with porosity > 7%, permeability > 0.5 × 10 − 3 µm 2 and shale content < 12%, are favorable for tight oil accumulation and high productivity. This study improves the understanding of tight oil accumulation in the Chang7–Chang9 members and offers practical guidance for tight oil exploration and horizontal well deployment in the southern Zhouchang area of the Ordos Basin.

Article.Title: Condylar morphology and CBCT grayscale values differ between combined dental–vertical skeletal class II phenotypes
Article.Authors: Deng X.; Xia W.; Xiao C.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: The mandibular condyle is responsive to occlusal and skeletal loading conditions, but differences between combined dental–vertical Class II phenotypes remain insufficiently quantified. This study compared condylar morphology and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) grayscale values (GSV) between adult females with combined dental–vertical skeletal Class II phenotypes. This retrospective single-centre cross-sectional study screened 120 archived CBCT records. After 20 records were excluded, all 100 eligible records were included and classified according to the prespecified dental and vertical skeletal phenotype criteria, yielding 50 participants in each phenotype group. Both right and left condyles were segmented, and patient-level means were analysed. Three-dimensional reconstruction was performed in Mimics Research 20.0. The primary outcomes were mean condylar GSV, volume, and surface area. Group comparisons used independent t-tests, with additional age- and BMI-adjusted sensitivity analyses. Because FMA angle formed part of the phenotypic contrast and masticatory muscle data were not standardized primary outcomes, FMA and muscle-related variables were not included as primary covariates. The combined dental–vertical phenotype classified as Class II/2 showed higher mean condylar GSV than the phenotype classified as Class II/1 (687.10 ± 158.68 vs. 558.89 ± 161.05; mean difference 128.21, 95% CI 64.76–191.66; P < 0.001). Condylar volume was also greater in the Class II/2 phenotype than in the Class II/1 phenotype (646.59 ± 168.64 vs. 500.23 ± 228.85 mm³; mean difference 146.36, 95% CI 66.58–226.14; P < 0.001), as was surface area (1712.13 ± 309.39 vs. 1322.92 ± 322.87 mm²; mean difference 389.21, 95% CI 263.71–514.71; P < 0.001). The direction of the findings remained unchanged in age- and BMI-adjusted sensitivity analyses. In this adult female cohort, the combined dental–vertical Class II phenotype classified as Class II/2 was associated with larger condylar dimensions and higher CBCT GSV than the combined dental–vertical Class II phenotype classified as Class II/1. These findings describe phenotype-associated imaging differences and do not establish deviation from a Class I reference or a causal mechanism. Studies including Class I controls, both sexes, adolescents, and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

Article.Title: Pro-tumorigenic effects of Capnocytophaga leadbetteri and Capnocytophaga gingivalis isolated from oral squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Yu M.; Yu X.; Yu M.; Guo Q.; Gong L.; Dong Q.; Yuan R.; Zhou J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Capnocytophaga species are oral commensal bacteria that have been found to be associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). This study aimed to investigate the carcinogenic potential of C. leadbetteri and C. gingivalis isolated from OSCC patients. A total of 72 patients with OSCC and 31 healthy controls (HC) were included in the study. Samples from patients with OSCC were collected both from cancerous tissues (CT) and paired adjacent normal tissues (PT). QPCR revealed that the Capnocytophaga load was significantly elevated in CT (log value: 6.16 ± 1.03) compared with HC (5.76 ± 0.54, adjusted P = 0.023). Furthermore, it was significantly higher in TNM stage I than in stage IV tumors ( P < 0.05). Clinical isolates C. leadbetteri N95 and C. gingivalis F53 were cultured and used to infect OSCC cell lines CAL27 and SCC15. Both strains were capable of adhering to OSCC cell, promoting proliferation, invasion, and migration, upregulating the expression of IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-α. Furthermore, the JAK2/STAT3 pathway appeared to be activated (increased expression of p-JAK2, p-STAT3, and c-Myc) in response to the infection. Treatments with the JAK2 inhibitor AG490 significantly suppressed the bacteria-induced upregulation of IL-6 and IL-8, as well as the enhanced migration and invasion of OSCC cells. Genomic analyses revealed the presence of predicted VI/IX secretion systems and multiple virulence-related genes in both strains. These findings indicate that C. leadbetteri N95and C. gingivalis F53 are overgrown in OSCC and exhibit pro-tumorigenic potentials.

Article.Authors: Centner A.; Park G.; Khalili L.; Ukhanov V.; Kadyan S.; Hwang H.; Nagpal R.; Salazar G.
Article.Abstract: The role of sex in the effects of vaping and individual aerosolized e-liquid constituents on atherosclerosis, vascular aging, and gut microbiome remodeling remains poorly characterized. Menthol reduced nicotine-induced plaque burden compared with nicotine alone in both sexes, but this reduction was not correlated with improved lipid profiles. Novel findings show that e-liquid exposure also altered gut microbial composition in a sex- and exposure-dependent manner, with nicotine causing the greatest dysbiosis and the addition of menthol exerting modulatory, but not restorative, effects. While sex stratification reduced statistical power, the pooled analysis identified Alloprevotella as a key discriminating genus associated with reduced plaque burden, supporting a potential role for gut microbial remodeling in vascular protection that warrants experimental validation.

Article.Title: Seismic performance of RC beam-column joints with stepped column geometry retrofitted using steel haunches
Article.Authors: Kim M.; Lee Y.
Article.Abstract: This study experimentally investigated the seismic performance of reinforced concrete (RC) beam–column joints with stepped columns, focusing on the effect of the stiffness discontinuity between the upper and lower columns and the effectiveness of a bolted steel haunch retrofit. Relative to the un-retrofitted specimens with the same stiffness ratio, the retrofit increased the peak lateral load by 28–34% and 54–67% in the positive and negative loading directions, respectively, the initial effective stiffness by 17–31%, and the cumulative energy dissipation at the same drift ratio by 23–50%, and it relocated damage from the joint core to the beam. The displacement ductility index of the retrofitted specimens was 16–18% lower than that of their un-retrofitted counterparts, because the yield displacement increased more than the ultimate displacement, and the equivalent hysteretic damping ratio was essentially unaffected. H-U0.6-L0.45, with the smallest stiffness difference between the columns, showed the most favorable overall response, although no un-retrofitted counterpart was tested. These results indicate that the proposed retrofit improves joint performance mainly through strength, stiffness and energy dissipation rather than displacement ductility.

Article.Title: Moslosooflavone promotes diabetic wound healing via TrkB/PI3K-Akt signaling and macrophage polarization: in vitro and in vivo validation
Article.Authors: He R.; Yu Y.; Xue S.; Wu P.; Chen A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) represent a severe and refractory diabetic complication characterized by persistent inflammatory activation, disordered macrophage phenotypic transformation, and impaired neurotrophic signaling. Although moslosooflavone (MOS) has been verified to possess anti-inflammatory and pro-healing bioactivities in multiple disease models, its underlying multi-target regulatory mechanisms in DFU wound repair remain poorly elucidated. Two public transcriptomic datasets (GSE134431, GSE199939) were integrated through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), protein–protein interaction(PPI) networks, and consensus machine learning (XGBoost (XGB), random forest (RF), LASSO regression, Boruta feature selection) to screen and validate core DFU-related targets. Potential MOS targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, and TargetNet databases. Binding modes and stability were evaluated by molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Immune cell infiltration was quantified using CIBERSORT. In vitro, high-glucose-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were used to assess cell viability, cytokine secretion, phenotypic transformation, and pathway activation using CCK-8, ELISA, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and Western blotting. TrkB (K252a) and PI3K (LY294002) inhibitors were employed to confirm pathway dependency. In vivo, a streptozotocin-induced diabetic mouse full-thickness wound model received topical MOS-loaded Carbopol hydrogel. A five-gene diagnostic signature consisting of CYP1A1, MAOB, NTRK2, ESR2, and KIT exhibited high efficacy in distinguishing DFUs from normal skin tissues. Among these, CYP1A1, MAOB, and NTRK2 were prioritized as candidate MOS targets, displaying stable binding (-5.05 to -6.62 kcal/mol), sustained hydrogen bonds, RMSD < 0.5 nm, and favorable MM/PBSA free energies. These targets were functionally linked to M0/M2 macrophage homeostasis. In high-glucose-stimulated macrophages, MOS improved cell viability, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines, and promoted M2 polarization. Pharmacological blockade of TrkB and PI3K largely abrogated these protective effects, supporting an important role for the TrkB/PI3K-Akt axis in the observed effects of MOS. Topical MOS hydrogel dose-dependently accelerated diabetic wound closure, accompanied by increased infiltration of CD206 + M2 macrophages and elevated phospho-TrkB in F4/80 + wound macrophages. MOS facilitates diabetic wound repair via a dual regulatory mechanism. Specifically, MOS alleviates pathological oxidative damage and activates the TrkB/PI3K-Akt pro-healing signaling cascade.This synergistic dual regulation restores neurotrophic signaling homeostasis, resolves wound inflammatory microenvironment imbalance, and drives macrophage transformation into a reparative M2 phenotype, ultimately ameliorating DFU pathological progression and accelerating diabetic wound regeneration.

Article.Title: Biofiltration: a hotspot for antibiotic resistance genes
Article.Authors: Samadhiya K.; Look J.; Düker U.; Schulz D.; Wallner M.; Nogueira R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) play a central role in limiting the environmental dissemination of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet their performance can fluctuate following operational disturbances. Samples from influent, secondary clarifier, biofiltration and effluent, were cultivated on chromogenic agar CHROMagar ESBL and CHROMagar mSuperCARBA plates. Phenotypic profiling of isolates combined with colony PCR of key extended spectrum ß-lactamase (ESBL) encoding genes, namely, bla- TEM, bla- CTX-M, and bla- SHV, and carbapenemase (CARBA) encoding genes, namely, bla- NDM and bla -Oxa-48 was performed. Along with the relative abundance of the genes co-occurrence patterns of targeted gene profiles of ESBL producing isolates was also investigated. Removal of Gram-negative bacteria stabilized within 3 months, however, removal of ESBL- and CARBA-producing bacteria did not. The relative abundance of ESBL-producing bacteria increased 3.7-fold and CARBA-producing bacteria 6.7-fold from influent to effluent in May, with additional proliferation in the biofiltration stage from the secondary clarifier (2.3-fold ESBL; 5.1-fold CARBA). Genotypic screening of the isolates revealed that the most prevalent ESBL genes, bla -SHV, bla -CTX-M and bla- TEM, frequently co-occur, with a particularly strong co-association between bla- SHV and bla- TEM and striking persistence of bla -NDM, which was detected in up to 87% of the effluent isolates in May. Sampling at four different stages in WWTP sampling further enabled the identification of resistance hotspots, pin-pointing biofiltration as a key zone of gene exchange and ARG persistence. Together, these findings highlight the critical need for targeted monitoring strategies in engineered water environments.

Article.Authors: Yaman M.; Sümbül A.; Uğur R.; Gönültaş M.; Tunç Y.; Köse M.; Demirel S.; Demirel F.; Say A.; Yıldız E.; Uzun A.; Pınar H.

Total phenolic content ranged from 102.61 to 192.57 mg GAE 100/g FW, total flavonoid content from 30.63 to 46.34 mg QE/100 g FW, and antioxidant activity from 44.00% to 69.50%. Multivariate analyses further elucidated the relationships among morphological, biochemical, and mineral traits and effectively characterized the diversity among genotypes and cultivars. Overall, the findings demonstrate substantial diversity within the evaluated apricot germplasm and highlight apricot leaves as an underutilized, low-cost, and potentially valuable source of bioactive compounds and mineral elements. These results provide preliminary information that can support further research into the potential use of apricot leaves in functional foods, herbal products, and natural preservatives; and can provide useful basic information for the future characterization and use of apricot genetic resources in breeding programs.

CRF decoding improves every encoder, whereas multilingual pretraining alone does not outperform monolingual pretraining of the same size. Five-shot GPT-5.4 (0.724) matches a fine-tuned base-size model but remains 6.8 points below the best system, with the largest gap on informal symptom expressions. Article.Title: SPMNet: shape-prior guided progressive decoding for camouflaged marine animal segmentation
Article.Authors: Chen H.
Article.Abstract: Complex underwater backgrounds and biological camouflage often weaken target semantics, while low contrast and non-rigid morphologies lead to ambiguous boundaries and incomplete structures. To address these issues, we propose SPMNet, a shape-prior guided network for marine animal segmentation. Built upon SAM2, SPMNet introduces a Progressive SAG-CCS Decoder (PSD) for progressive semantic and structural reconstruction. Within PSD, a Spatial Attention Gate (SAG) suppresses camouflage-induced background responses during cross-level feature fusion, providing more reliable decoding features. An Iterative CCS Refinement (ICCS) mechanism based on the Convex Combination Star Shape (CCS) prior then imposes explicit geometric constraints to improve boundary continuity and structural completeness. We further design a Hybrid Shape-Aware Loss (HSAL), which combines pixel-level region supervision with gradient-direction consistency. A frozen SAM2 Hiera backbone with lightweight adaptation and contextual enhancement modules is used for underwater feature representation. Experiments on MAS3K, RMAS, UFO120, and RUWI demonstrate competitive performance. Article.Title: PALMD supports spheroid integrity and survival in ovarian cancer cells
Article.Authors: Kikuoka M.; Miyagawa Y.; Takasaki K.; Watanabe R.; Shigekawa K.; Kosaka T.; Watanabe S.; Nishizawa M.; Takahashi Y.; Nishida H.; Hirano M.; Hiraike H.; Osuga Y.; Nagasaka K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peritoneal metastasis of ovarian cancer involves multicellular spheroids that survive under anchorage-independent conditions. This study investigated the role of palmdelphin (PALMD), a paralemmin-family protein implicated in membrane dynamics, in ovarian cancer spheroid integrity and survival. An ascites-derived ovarian cancer cell culture (OVCSC) displayed spheroid-forming and cancer stem-like features. RNA sequencing of MESOV cells under two-dimensional and three-dimensional (3D) conditions identified 3,764 differentially expressed genes, including higher PALMD transcript abundance in 3D culture. In OVCSC cells, PALMD protein abundance increased after attachment of preformed spheroids. PALMD depletion was associated with increased p53 and vimentin protein abundance, disrupted spheroid morphology, and increased apoptosis-related readouts in the original spheroid experiments. Additional attached and suspension comparisons showed assay-dependent responses: transient knockdown increased the caspase 3/7 signal in suspension culture without significant Annexin V differences, whereas stable populations showed an increased caspase signal under both conditions and significant Annexin V differences in attached culture. Exploratory microarray comparisons showed a larger numerical PALMD transcript increase after 6 h of endothelial co-culture than after attachment alone, although neither comparison met Q < 0.05. These findings support a role for PALMD in spheroid integrity and survival and motivate investigation of its context-dependent relationship with cell adhesion and the microenvironment.

Article.Title: Median-pi-sigma artificial neural network for time series forecasting
Article.Authors: Yücesoy E.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a novel robust artificial neural network architecture, called the Median–Pi-Sigma Neural Network, for time series forecasting problems. Unlike conventional neural network approaches that rely primarily on additive neuron structures and external robustness techniques, the proposed architecture incorporates robustness directly into the computational structure of the network. In the proposed model, a median-based hidden layer is employed to suppress the propagation of anomalous observations and reduce the sensitivity of the network to noise. To compensate for the potential loss of representational capability caused by median processing, a second hidden layer composed of multiplicative product-unit neurons is integrated into the architecture. This hybrid structure enables the model to simultaneously achieve robustness and high-order nonlinear representation capability within a unified framework. Due to the non-differentiable nature of the median operator and the highly nonlinear error surface generated by multiplicative neurons, the network parameters are optimized using a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The forecasting performance of the proposed architecture was evaluated using ten different Financial Times Stock Exchange (FTSE) time series datasets and compared with several important neural network models in the literature, including multilayer perceptron, Pi-Sigma, multiplicative neuron, recurrent, gated recurrent neural network, long short-term memory deep artificial neural network, and dendritic neural network architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Median Pi Neural Network achieved the lowest average RMSE values in many of the datasets and generally outperformed competing methods in terms of forecasting accuracy and robustness. Statistical analyses based on the Friedman test further confirmed the superiority of the proposed approach. The findings indicate that integrating median-based robustness with multiplicative nonlinear modelling provides an effective and powerful framework for financial time series forecasting under noisy environments.

Article.Title: Lightweight multi-modal fault diagnosis via self-supervised pre-training and knowledge distillation for industrial devices
Article.Authors: Han W.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Predictive maintenance in the Industrial Internet of Things is constrained by scarce labeled fault data and limited edge computing resources. This study proposes a lightweight multimodal fault diagnosis framework integrating self-supervised pre-training and knowledge distillation (SSL-KD). An early-fusion architecture combines one-dimensional vibration signals with Short-Time Fourier Transform, Continuous Wavelet Transform, and Gramian Angular Field representations. A high-capacity Teacher is contrastively pre-trained without class annotations and then fine-tuned for supervised four-class diagnosis. Its diagnostic knowledge is transferred to a simplified Student using soft predictions and ground-truth labels. Experiments on synthetic signals and two public bearing datasets, CWRU and PU, demonstrate that the Student retains performance comparable to the Teacher while reducing deployment costs. On the CWRU datasets, the Teacher and Student achieved accuracies of 1.0000 and 0.9963, respectively, while the Student reduced inference time, model size, and parameter count. Under limited-label conditions on CWRU, self-supervised pre-training improved accuracy from 0.939 to 0.985 with 10% labels and from 0.972 to 0.978 with 20% labels, although improvements were not uniform across all label fractions. An 11-configuration ablation study further supports the contribution of multimodal fusion to known-fault diagnosis.

Article.Title: Reduced fertilization sustains ecosystem multifunctionality and economic benefit in a temperate agroforestry system
Article.Authors: Manu R.; Hollmann M.; Beule L.; Choe S.; Schmidt M.; Bischel X.; Niu D.; Rettie F.; Langhof M.; Paul C.; Corre M.; Veldkamp E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Agroforestry as a sustainable agricultural intensification strategy aims to optimize resource use and enhance the provision of ecosystem services when compared to treeless open croplands. Here, we evaluated the effects of fertilization rates and land use management on ecosystem functions, based on 37 ecological indicators, measured over five years (2019–2023). Reduced fertilization did not significantly affect overall ecosystem multifunctionality in either agroforestry or open cropland, although some indicators differed. This lack of reduced fertilization effect likely reflects a legacy effect of chronic over-fertilization in this agroecosystem. Compared to open cropland, agroforestry enhanced carbon sequestration but was associated with reduced water filtration likely due to spatially unadjusted fertilization rates in shade-affected, low-yielding crops near the trees. Economic performance indicators were collectively comparable among fertilization and land use management systems. Our results suggest that optimized fertilization in agroforestry can sustain food production, while promoting resilient, resource-efficient agriculture.

Article.Title: Green-engineered copper oxide nanosheets: synthesis, characterization, antimicrobial efficacy, and toxicity assessment
Article.Authors: Wrońska N.; Mucha J.; Kisielewska A.; Piwoński I.; Lisowska K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Eco-friendly, sustainable nanomaterial synthesis has gained attention as an alternative to conventional chemical and physical methods. In the present study, copper oxide nanosheets (CuO NS) were synthesized using the fungal strain Fusarium oxysporum . The obtained nanomaterials were characterized by UV-ViS spectroscopy, FTIR, DLS, EDAX and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The biological activity, cytotoxicity and environmental safety of the biosynthesized CuO nanosheets were evaluated. The antibacterial activity was assessed against selected bacterial strains, with significant growth inhibition, particularly against Gram-negative strains (in the concentration range 1-0.015 mg/L). Cytotoxicity assessment using fibroblast cell cultures showed dose-dependent responses, while no significant reduction in cell viability was observed within the concentration range of 0.0005–0.015 mg/L. The ecotoxicological potential of biogenic CuO NS was also tested. Organisms representative of aquatic ecosystems were selected for ecotoxicological evaluation. The 48-hour EC₅₀ value for the marine crustacean A. franciscana exposed to CuO NS was determined to be 30 mg/L. In addition, toxicity testing using Spirodela duckweed toxkit demonstrated concentration-dependent biphasic responses to CuO NS, characterized by both growth inhibition and growth stimulation. The estimated EC₅₀ value for Spirodela was 30 mg/L. F. oxysporum -mediated synthesis represents a promising green route for producing CuO NS, although toxicity evaluation remains essential for future biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Immediate changes of microperfusion during angioplasty of the lower limb arteries
Article.Authors: Eissele L.; Zeidan Y.; Gerdes L.; Reißfelder C.; Stellos K.; Schwenke K.; Sigl M.; Gerken A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The success of lower-limb revascularization in peripheral artery disease (PAD) is usually assessed by vessel patency, while tissue-level perfusion is not routinely monitored during the procedure. We examined whether continuous microcirculatory monitoring could detect immediate perfusion changes during angioplasty. In this prospective single-center observational study, 25 patients with symptomatic PAD undergoing technically successful percutaneous revascularization were evaluated. Microvascular blood flow (Flow), postcapillary oxygen saturation (SO₂), and relative hemoglobin content (rHb) were continuously measured at the forefoot using combined laser Doppler flowmetry and white-light spectrophotometry (O2C). All three parameters peaked during reactive hyperemia after balloon deflation ( P < 0.001 for changes over time). Flow and SO₂ remained significantly elevated at the end of the procedure, while rHb returned to baseline. By the next day, all three parameters were comparable to baseline despite a significantly improved ankle–brachial index ( P < 0.001), patent treated lesions, and improved Rutherford category on follow-up ( P < 0.001). Successful revascularization was thus associated with immediate but transient changes in resting, supine microcirculatory measurements. Continuous O2C monitoring captures transient intraprocedural microcirculatory responses that complement conventional postprocedural assessments of vessel patency and macrocirculatory hemodynamics. Larger studies are needed to determine whether these dynamic responses can guide revascularization or predict clinical outcomes.
