Article.Title: An operational risk assessment framework for landslide mitigation projects with a case study in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area
Article.Authors: Cheng J.; Chen Z.; Wu J.; Sang Y.; Qiu X.; Wu L.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Large-scale landslide mitigation projects face complex environmental forces and long-term performance degradation. Existing risk assessments for landslide mitigation projects tend to focus primarily on structural limit states, often neglecting operational management factors and the distinction between risk probability and consequences. To address these gaps, this study develops an operational risk assessment framework integrating the Hierarchical Holographic Model (HHM), Best–Worst Method (BWM)–improved CRITIC game-theoretic weighting, and a bivariate normal cloud model. The system evaluates 18 indicators across four dimensions: hazard source, retaining structures, environment, and management. Critically, the bivariate cloud model simultaneously quantifies risk probability ( \(E{x}_{x}\) ) and consequence severity ( \(E{x}_{y}\) ). Applied to the Huangtupo landslide mitigation project in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (TGRA), which has been in service for over 20 years, the framework yields an overall operational risk of Level III (General Risk) with a closeness similarity of \({\lambda}_{III}=0.6582\) . Cumulative displacement ( \({w}^{*}=0.1485\) ) and structural stress overload ( \({w}^{*}=0.1145\) ) are identified as primary physical drivers, exhibiting high consequence expectations ( \(E{x}_{y}=6.50\) and \(7.20\) ). The case study shows that an overall Level III classification can coexist with elevated risks associated with individual indicators, particularly cumulative displacement and stress overload. The framework brings these local concerns into the interpretation of project-level risk and provides a basis for setting monitoring and maintenance priorities.

Article.Title: Blind spot minimization through optimized LiDAR placement
Article.Authors: Arukgoda M.; Samarakoon S.; Muthugala M.; Hwang K.; Elara M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The placement of Light Detection And Ranging (LiDAR) sensors considerably influences the perception of large autonomous robots. Where precise navigation and obstacle detection are required, optimizing LiDAR placement is crucial to maximize coverage while minimizing blind spots. Existing studies have largely focused on coverage improvement without addressing application-specific prioritization of critical regions. This research proposes a novel method to optimize the placement of 2D LiDAR sensors on large robots with complex shapes, improving perception in high-priority areas while minimizing blind spots. A custom simulation environment is used to evaluate coverage performance, and a new scoring method is introduced to prioritize important perception areas. The optimization process employs three metaheuristic algorithms to find the optimum LiDAR configurations: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA). Five blind-spot metrics (uncovered area ratio, high-priority-region coverage rate, overlap/redundancy rate, angular coverage, and maximum blind gap) are introduced alongside the priority score, and configurations are judged by the blind spots they leave. The method is validated on five robot platforms of markedly different geometry and on sensor counts from two to five, each optimized over 10 independent runs. Two control experiments isolate the contributions of the sensor count and of the simulation resolution, showing that the score rises monotonically with the count when the field of view is held fixed and that doubling the grid resolution leaves every metric within its run-to-run spread. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in achieving improved perception.

Article.Title: SpineFusion for local and global feature fusion in two dimensional MRI image classification
Article.Authors: Özçelik S.; Kılıç E.; Güler H.
Article.Abstract: We assessed the feasibility of combining local and global features for classification of two-dimensional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) exports. SpineFusion couples ConvNeXt-Tiny and Swin-T encoders through bidirectional cross-attention, with an optional plane embedding. Separate models were trained on three public image collections: spinal MS–myelitis (MSM), binary brain MS/healthy (BT-MS), and eight-class neurological MRI (MCND). Duplicate audits identified 46 redundant decoded-pixel copies in MSM and 50 in MCND. Removing these before stratified image-level 10-fold cross-validation left 2,700 and 11,905 images. On cleaned MSM, SpineFusion achieved 94.89 ± 1.09% accuracy, compared with 94.63 ± 1.12% for ConvNeXt-Tiny and 95.26 ± 1.06% without the plane embedding. On cleaned MCND, the corresponding SpineFusion and ConvNeXt-Tiny accuracies were 98.99 ± 0.42% and 99.20 ± 0.25%. The original 3,427-image BT-MS experiment achieved 97.78 ± 0.85%. Exploratory matched-fold analyses did not establish a statistically supported performance advantage for the fusion architecture or the plane embedding. Perceptual-hash screening identified remaining cross-fold similarity candidates. Reliable subject and source mappings were unavailable, so these image-level estimates do not establish patient-level generalization. The study provides a reproducible feasibility evaluation; patient-grouped external validation remains necessary for clinical interpretation.

Article.Title: Self-reported injury, sport injury anxiety, and psychological symptoms in recreational athletes
Article.Authors: Çelik E.; Eskiyecek C.
Article.Abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the associations of previous-year sports injury and injury-specific anxiety with depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms among young recreational athletes. Participants ( N = 211) completed a sports injury information form, the Sport Injury Anxiety Scale (dimensions: Loss of Athleticism, Being Perceived as Weak, Experiencing Pain, Letting Down Important Others, Reinjury, and Loss of Social Support), and the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21). Overall, 142 participants (67.3%) reported a previous-year sports injury. All six sport injury anxiety dimensions were positively correlated with DASS-21 total scores (Spearman’s rho = 0.252–0.543; all false-discovery-rate-adjusted P <.001). After multiple-testing correction, participants reporting an injury had higher depression, anxiety, stress, and total DASS-21 scores, whereas no sport injury anxiety dimension differed significantly. In an HC3-robust multivariable model, female sex and previous-year injury were associated with higher DASS-21 total scores; Loss of Athleticism, Being Perceived as Weak, and Reinjury also retained independent associations after covariate adjustment and multiple-testing correction. The final model explained 39.5% of the variance. Athletes with greater concerns about reinjury, appearing weak, or losing athletic ability reported more psychological symptoms. Psychological screening may therefore be useful during injury rehabilitation. Longitudinal studies with clinically verified injuries are needed.

Article.Title: Association of salivary cortisol, dehydroepiandrosterone, and chromogranin A levels with orthodontic malocclusion severity and related anxiety in adolescents
Article.Authors: Kose T.; Yorgancilar N.; Uygun S.; Arpa M.; Kose O.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the possible relationship between malocclusion severity and anxiety levels in adolescents and to examine the potential role of salivary cortisol, dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), and chromogranin A (CgA) levels in this possible relationship. 164 adolescent participants were divided into 4 groups based on the severity of malocclusion according to their Dental Aesthetic Index (DAI) scores: DAI-I, -II, -III, and -IV. Anxiety levels in all participants were determined using the Social Appearance Anxiety Scale (SAAS) and Rosenberg’s Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) psychosocial assessment scales. Additionally, current anxiety markers cortisol, DHEA, and CgA levels were determined in unstimulated saliva samples using ELISA. The cortisol/DHEA ratio was calculated. Correlational relationships between DAI scores, anxiety questionnaire scores, and biochemical findings were comprehensively analyzed. Psychosocial assessments indicated greater social appearance anxiety among adolescents with severe (DAI-III) and very severe (DAI-IV) malocclusion than among those with mild (DAI-I) and moderate (DAI-II) malocclusion. Salivary cortisol and CgA levels were found to be higher in DAI-III and especially DAI-IV adolescents ( p < 0.001, p = 0.005, respectively). DHEA levels and the cortisol/DHEA ratio did not differ significantly across DAI severity categories in unadjusted comparisons. However, adjusted regression analysis revealed a significant positive association between continuous DAI scores and DHEA levels. Positive correlations were found between DAI and cortisol, CgA, and SAAS, while a negative correlation was found between DAI and RSES. Salivary cortisol and CgA levels may be indicators of anxiety levels associated with malocclusion severity (or the need for orthodontic treatment).

Article.Title: Adversarial prompt detection via contrastive dual-encoder transformer for zero-day jailbreak defense based on AdverSentinel-LLM model
Article.Authors: Alshammri G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have become core elements of current artificial intelligence applications yet are highly susceptible to adversarial prompt attacks such as jailbreaks that compromise safety alignment. Current defense mechanisms rely predominantly on fixed rule-based filters or single-encoder classifiers with limited generalizability to new, zero-day jailbreak signatures. This paper presents AdverSentinel-LLM, a novel adversarial prompt detector based on a Contrastive Dual-Encoder Transformer (CDET) architecture trained to identify malicious prompts in real time, including zero-day jailbreak attacks. The CDET architecture maintains two independent representation spaces—one encoding prompt semantics and one encoding structured threat patterns—trained jointly under a supervised contrastive objective that explicitly pushes adversarial embeddings away from benign clusters, enabling zero-day generalization to unseen attack vectors via contrastive disentanglement. The framework comprises two parallel transformer encoders: a Prompt Semantic Encoder (PSE) that learns deep contextual representations of input prompts and a Threat Pattern Encoder (TPE) that learns discriminative representations of known adversarial attack patterns. A supervised contrastive learning objective encourages separation between adversarial and benign embeddings, enabling zero-day generalization to unseen attack vectors. We additionally incorporate a Dynamic Threat Memory Bank (DTMB) with prototype pruning and rejuvenation to prevent stagnation, and an Anomaly-Aware Gating Mechanism (AAGM) for context-sensitive detection threshold modulation. Extensive experiments on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, ToxicChat, and PromptSafety-Bench demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with an F1-score of 0.967, detection accuracy of 97.3%, and a zero-day detection rate of 94.8%, with the contribution of every architectural element verified by ablation studies and preliminary evidence of cross-model transferability demonstrated across adversarial prompt distributions independently curated against GPT-4, LLaMA-3, Claude-3, and Gemini-Pro backends; a controlled matched-prompt evaluation is deferred to future work.

Article.Authors: Shaban H.; Medhat M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Thermally tunable multi-stage optical filters were presented by employing thermotropic liquid crystal (LC) materials. The filter design was characterized by Jones matrices based on optical dispersions of birefringence, Δ n , via combining Haller’s temperature-dependent order parameter model with the Cauchy wavelength-dispersion equation including the LC clearing temperature. The smooth thermal tuning of the LC-based filter was explored that enabled scanning within the visible spectrum, 400–800 nm, with a narrow single band or more, under different ranges of operating temperatures according to the used LC material. Results showed that increasing the LC stage thickness can contribute to widening the spectral transmission range by a percentage reaching 558.33%, as in the case of E7 material. LCs like E48 and E44 showed a pronounced thermal stability represented in the thermal shift of the wavelength, d λ m /dT, that reached 2.4–15 nm/K and 2.2–21 nm/K, respectively, compared to that of 5CB, which ranged from 6 to 146 nm/K. The spectral resolution of the proposed design was thermally tuned for E44, as an example, from ~ ~ 12.5–25 nm at the first mode, while varied from ~ 3.12–3.20 nm at the fourth mode. A pure single-mode filter in the case of E44 showed a thermally tunable wavelength range from 400 to 593 nm, under operating temperatures of 366 to 297 K, with a line width spanning 12.5 to 18.57 nm. This work primarily contributes widely to developing hyperspectral imaging for agricultural monitoring, biomedical diagnostics, and remote sensing, supporting SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), and innovating compact photonic devices for integrated sensing, on-chip spectroscopy, and portable optical systems, supporting SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure).

Article.Authors: Farías A.; Mendizabal-Ruiz G.; Chavez-Badiola A.; Acosta-Gómez F.; Aleriano K.; Bixon B.; Millán C.; Rico-Botero V.; Matia-Algué Q.; Costa-Borges N.; Sánchez-González D.; Murray A.; Silvestri G.; Alikani M.; Cohen J.

The ADPS produced dishes with a weight coefficient of variation ranging from 0.6% to 2.2%, and bicarbonate buffered media remained within acceptable pH ranges at 24 h of incubation. Rapid and simultaneous automated oil overlay application reduced evaporation, preserving osmo​lality. Mean preparation times ranged from 17.1 ± 4.8 to 126.0 ± 3.6 s per dish, depending on complexity and volumes. Three biocompatibility experiments (laser-marked dishes, media exposed to the ADPS environment, and fully automated preparation) showed expanded blastocyst formation rates above the acceptance threshold of 80%. Optical coherence tomography imaging found no dish surface changes after laser marking, and air quality parameters (volatile organic compounds, formaldehyde) within the unit remained within recommended thresholds, though particle counts exceeded targets in the workshop testing environment. Article.Title: Petrographic and geochemical characterization of Oba Ile granitoids and their implications for magma source and chemical weathering in southwestern Nigeria
Article.Authors: Abeiya S.; Alimi S.; Yusuf K.; Ayodele O.
Article.Abstract: The Oba-Ile area and environs in Akure, southwestern Nigeria, are underlain predominantly by granitoids of the Precambrian Nigerian Basement Complex. This study integrates field mapping, petrography, whole-rock major and selected trace element geochemistry, chemical weathering indices, and multivariate statistical analysis to constrain their geological evolution and petrogenesis. Major and selected trace elements were determined using Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (AAS). Field investigations identified a heterogeneous basement assemblage comprising migmatite gneiss, granite gneiss, porphyritic granite and fine-grained granite, with subordinate pegmatite, aplite, dolerite, and quartz to quartzofeldspathic veins. The granitoids comprise mainly quartz, feldspar, biotite, and hornblende, with minor zircon and pyroxene. SiO₂ contents range from 58.23 to 78.40 wt%, defining intermediate to felsic compositions. Decreases in Fe₂O₃, CaO, MgO, P₂O₅, and MnO with increasing SiO₂ indicate progressive magmatic differentiation dominated by fractional crystallization. The granitoids are predominantly calc-alkaline and metaluminous to peraluminous, suggesting heterogeneous crustal sources, substantial crustal involvement, and possible metasedimentary contributions, consistent with crustal reworking and felsic magmatism during convergent to post-collisional Pan-African tectonothermal evolution. Predominant N–S joints and NE–SW veins record post-emplacement brittle deformation and localized fluid movement. CIA values of 57.70–77.60 indicate slight to moderate chemical weathering, while PCA defines Co–Mn–Cr–Ni, Zn–Cu–Fe–Cd, and Zr–Pb associations, reflecting primary mineral partitioning, magmatic differentiation, and weathering modification rather than hydrothermal mineralization. Overall, the granitoids record multistage magmatic evolution, crustal reworking, structural modification, and tropical weathering. However, interpretation of trace-element behaviour is constrained by the use of acid-leachable AAS methods, particularly for refractory elements, and the absence of high-resolution whole-rock, isotopic, and mineral-chemical datasets. Consequently, the results provide a first-order petrogenetic framework, while future XRF, ICP-MS, and isotopic analyses are recommended to refine source, timing, and crustal evolution models.

Article.Title: Associations between circulating neuregulin 4 and diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ma K.; Wei Y.; Liu Y.; Hou Y.; Li X.; Zhao K.
Article.Abstract: Neuregulin 4 (Nrg4) is being increasingly recognized as being involved in diabetes biology and vascular injury. Among a cohort of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), we evaluated whether serum Nrg4 concentrations were related to T2DM and diabetic retinopathy (DR) risk. Serum Nrg4 was assayed by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 302 adults, including 78 healthy controls and 224 patients with T2DM. DR was evaluated by optical coherence tomography angiography, and T2DM participants were categorized as having non-DR, nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR), or proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). We modeled the association between the Nrg4 level and DR using multivariable logistic regression. The predictive ability was summarized with receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Serum Nrg4 levels in the T2DM group were lower than those in the control group. Compared with that in the NDR group, serum Nrg4 levels were lower in both the NPDR and PDR groups and decreased as DR severity increased. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that decreased Nrg4 levels and increased fasting insulin and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) were risk factors for T2DM. In the adjusted logistic regression, higher fasting plasma glucose levels and hs-CRP levels and lower Nrg4 levels remained independently associated with DR. When Nrg4 was dichotomized at 3.695 ng/ml in a multivariable model, values above this threshold were associated with a lower DR risk (OR, 0.376; 95% CI, 0.196–0.702; P < 0.01), supporting an independent correlation between Nrg4 and DR. Decreased serum Nrg4 levels are associated with the development of T2DM and DR, and serum Nrg4 levels decrease as DR becomes more severe. This trend suggests that Nrg4 may play a protective role in the development and progression of DR.

Article.Title: Plant-eating machines: cranial performance and feeding behaviour in sauropodomorpha
Article.Authors: Barbosa G.; Silva Junior J.; Zhang Q.; You H.; Montefeltro F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evolution of sauropodomorph skulls involved major shifts in cranial architecture, feeding mechanics, and ecological strategies. Here, we integrate finite element analysis, safety-factor estimation, relative bite force, and gape modelling within a standardised framework to compare the early sauropodiform Yizhousaurus sunae , the diplodocid Diplodocus carnegii , and the macronarians Camarasaurus lentus and Sarmientosaurus musacchioi . Y. sunae exhibited the highest relative bite force but also high extrinsic stresses and the most restricted gape, indicating that force transmission and structural robustness were partly decoupled. D. carnegii produced a high absolute bite-force output but the lowest relative bite force and showed pronounced sensitivity to vertical and lateral loading. The two sampled macronarians generally exhibited lower stresses and higher safety margins, although their gape capacities differed. These broad performance differences persisted after surface-area scaling and recalculation of taxon-specific bite forces, indicating that model size alone does not explain the recovered patterns. Rather than supporting a linear progression towards greater robustness, the results reveal distinct functional configurations and a broader diversification of the sauropodomorph feeding apparatus.

Article.Title: Investigating the antitumor potential of Karakilçik wheatgrass juice against prostate and lung cancer cells through in vitro and in silico
Article.Authors: Demirag A.; Bicak B.; Akman G.; Kecel Gunduz S.; Yildirim M.
Article.Abstract: Triticum aestivum L. (Wheat grass juice) exhibits various therapeutic effects, including anti-cancer, antioxidant, and anti-ulcer properties, due to the compounds present in its content. In this study, the anticancer potential of grass juice powder obtained from Triticum aestivum L. species on prostate and lung cancer lines was investigated using theoretically and experimentally methods. Cytotoxic activity study performed with wheat grass juice powder was performed using human prostate cancer cell line (PC-3), human lung carcinoma cell line (A549), human non-small cell lung cancer cell (H1975) and epithelial cell line (BEAS-2B), and dose-dependent antiproliferative effects were observed on all cells. In order to elucidate potential molecular mechanisms, major compounds found in wheat grass juice powder were evaluated by molecular docking analysis against cancer-related targets (androgen receptor, PSMA, mTOR, Akt1, PI3K). It was determined that some major compounds showed high binding affinity and could inhibit cancer-related signaling pathways. Furthermore, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations performed on selected major phytochemical–target complexes confirmed the structural stability, binding persistence, and favorable dynamic behavior of the most promising interactions under physiological conditions. Additionally, in silico ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Elimination, and Toxicity) analysis was performed to evaluate the drug-like properties of the major compounds. The obtained results showed good oral bioavailability and a low estimated toxicity profile. Moreover, taste activity estimations were performed for the major compounds in the study, and the potential bitter, sweet, and sour profiles of these compounds were determined, with their evaluation presented to support the development of oral supplement formulations. In conclusion, wheatgrass juice powder obtained from wheat grass juice powder shows potential as a natural therapeutic agent against prostate and lung cancers. Further studies are required to support its clinical validity.

Article.Title: CABRIA: contrastive attribute preference bridge for personalized image aesthetic assessment
Article.Authors: Tao Z.; Xu C.; Mahmood A.
Article.Abstract: Personalized Image Aesthetic Assessment (PIAA) aims to predict an individual user’s aesthetic ratings from a small set of images scored by that user. Generic aesthetic predictors are able to provide useful population-level knowledge, but they collapse the user-specific deviations that define personal taste. Direct few-shot adaptation can also entangle shared image quality with sparse user evidence, making it difficult to identify what should be personalized. To address this problem, we introduce CABRIA , a support-residual-conditioned framework that casts personalization as a user-specific correction over a global aesthetic prior. CABRIA first learns the generic prior and contrastively pretrains the representation used for support retrieval, then converts support-rating residuals into positive and negative preference memory. A Cross-Attention Bridge provides a structured route that connects positive and negative support evidence with query attribute tokens, and per-user gradient adaptation estimates the final residual correction. Under the 37-user FLICKR-AES protocol, CABRIA with ResNet-101 achieves SROCC scores of 0.694 and 0.760 for 10-shot and 100-shot personalization, respectively. A strict user-disjoint control that excludes validation- and test-user ratings from Stage 1 shows a statistically significant 10-shot improvement over the frozen prior and all matched adaptation baselines, while the multiplicity-corrected 100-shot comparisons do not establish an advantage for the complete pipeline. The code is available at CABRIA’s GitHub repository .

Article.Title: Tectonic coupling indicated by bi-modal stress regimes revealed from moment tensors of ML ≥ 4 intermediate-depth Vrancea earthquakes (2022–2025)
Article.Authors: Vavryčuk V.; Lukešová R.; Hrubcová P.; Fojtíková L.; Borleanu F.
Article.Abstract: We determine highly accurate full moment tensors for 40 intermediate-depth earthquakes (M L ≥ 4) that occurred in the Vrancea seismic region between 2022 and 2025, using recordings from the Romanian Seismic Network and from the mobile AdriaArray broadband network. The retrieved moment tensors contain not only double-couple (DC) components but also significant non-double-couple (non-DC) components. The non-DC components are dominated by CLVD, ranging from −40% to 40%, and are likely caused by seismic anisotropy within the source region. The focal mechanisms derived from the DC components are classified into four types, which can be grouped into two datasets. Dataset A is characterized by fault strikes of 230–240°, whereas dataset B exhibits strikes of 320–345°. The coexistence of focal mechanisms with two markedly different strike orientations indicates a bi-modal stress state within the focal zone. Consequently, the two stress regimes must be analyzed separately; otherwise, stress inversion yields biased results. Separate stress inversions of datasets A and B produce azimuths of maximum compression of 320° and 75°, respectively. These directions correspond, respectively, to the predominant maximum compression in the upper mantle, oriented perpendicular to the Carpathian Arc at its bend, and to the maximum compression in the overlying crust, oriented parallel to the Carpathian Arc at its bend. This correspondence suggests tectonic coupling between the seismically active slab segment and the overlying lithosphere.

Article.Title: Mechanical and multi-radiation shielding performance of concrete optimized with activated carbon and silica fume
Article.Authors: El-Rahman H.; Mohsen M.; Yousef M.; Abdelmonem A.; Ramadan W.; Kora H.; Galahom A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Concrete plays a critical role in nuclear reactors by providing structural support and serving as a primary barrier against ionizing radiation. This study investigates the effects of activated carbon (AC) and silica fume (SF) as partial cement replacements on the fresh properties, mechanical performance, and gamma-ray shielding efficiency of concrete cured for 28 and 56 days. AC was incorporated at 1–6% by cement weight, while SF was used at a fixed dosage of 10%. Slump tests showed reduced workability for all modified mixtures due to the high surface area and water demand of AC and SF. Mechanical testing revealed that compressive strength increased with AC addition up to an optimum range of 2–4%, with further enhancement achieved in hybrid AC–SF mixtures; the highest gains were observed for combinations of AC and SF, while SF alone significantly improved both compressive and splitting tensile strengths. Gamma-ray attenuation was evaluated experimentally (0.1218–1.408 MeV) and validated using both XCOM theoretical data and MCNPX simulations based on Linear Attenuation Coefficient (LAC) and Mass Attenuation Coefficient (MAC), which showed good agreement with experimental data (relative deviation < 7%). Following model validation in the experimental energy range, these simulations were extended up to $$15 MeV$$ to generate theoretical predictions for complex shielding parameters ( $${Z}_{eff}$$ , $${N}_{eff}$$ , $${Z}_{eq}$$ ) and fast neutron removal cross-sections ( $${\Sigma}_{R}$$ ) without requiring additional costly experimental setups. Results indicate that optimized AC–SF mixtures, particularly the 2% AC + 10% SF hybrid, successfully balance structural integrity with superior multi-radiation shielding efficiency. The results demonstrate that optimized AC–SF concrete mixtures can simultaneously enhance mechanical integrity and gamma-ray shielding efficiency, making them promising candidates for structural radiation-shielding applications in nuclear facilities.

Article.Title: An explainable AI framework for integrated authentication, intrusion detection, and adaptive data transmission in IoMT networks
Article.Authors: G N.; G N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Real-time monitoring, remote diagnostics, and automated medical treatments are all made possible by the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), this has revolutionised healthcare. However, due of their improved connectivity, IoMT devices are more exposed to a range of cybersecurity attacks, such as malware insertion, spoofing, man-in-the-middle attacks, and distributed denial-of-service assaults. Traditional black-box AI models provide robust security mechanisms but lack transparency, making it difficult to identify and mitigate cyber threats effectively. This work introduces an explainable AI (XAI)-driven cybersecurity framework for IoMT applications to enhance trust, interpretability, and resilience against cyber threats. The proposed framework integrates deep learning networks with local model networks for authentication, employs a enhanced deep Q-Network for secure data transmission, and leverages XAI-based techniques for real-time attack detection and resistance. The model incorporates SHAP and LIME to provide interpretable security decisions, ensuring that IoMT stakeholders can understand and act on AI-generated security insights. In addition, this paper discusses a detailed attack resistance study using XAI, which shows the degree to which the proposed framework withstands various cyber threats.The paper evaluates security effectiveness metrics such as false positive rate, attack detection rate, response time, and the explainability score to judge the performance of XAI in IoMT security. Compared to conventional AI models, XAI-based detection accuracy has been proved to be significantly better experimentally, the reaction time was shortened, and the system was more transparent.

Article.Title: Dual-encapsulated liposomal vitamin C increases comparative oral exposure in a randomised crossover study in healthy adults
Article.Authors: Andalattu Vijayan N.; Saji A.; Erezhath Sarun S.; Gopalakrishnan S.; Mohan G.; Balakrishnan K.
Article.Abstract: This study characterised DELT, a rice-protein-associated dual-encapsulation vitamin C powder, and compared its in vitro properties and short-term pharmacokinetic profile with conventional liposomal and reference vitamin C formulations. Physicochemical characterisation included particle size, polydispersity, surface charge, morphology and solid-state analysis. Vitamin C content, operational encapsulation efficiency, in vitro release and accelerated stability were also evaluated. An exploratory, randomised, double-blind, three-treatment, three-period crossover study was conducted in 12 healthy adults following a single oral dose containing 350 mg vitamin C. Re-dispersed DELT had a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 210.0 ± 33.4 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.025. Measured vitamin C content was 71.3 ± 1.0% w/w, and operational encapsulation efficiency was 87.8%. In phosphate buffer at pH 6.8, DELT released 35.0 ± 3.5% of its vitamin C by 8 h, compared with 78.8 ± 4.6% for unformulated vitamin C. During 8 months of accelerated storage at 40 °C/65% relative humidity, vitamin C content changed from 71.23% to 71.17% w/w. In the clinical study, mean baseline-corrected maximum plasma concentrations were 16.90 ± 1.90 µg/mL for DELT, 9.92 ± 1.10 µg/mL for conventional liposomal vitamin C and 2.62 ± 0.76 µg/mL for reference vitamin C. Corresponding areas under the concentration–time curve up to the last measured time point were 126.32 ± 19.60, 68.11 ± 8.46 and 11.43 ± 2.60 µg·h/mL, respectively. Pairwise comparisons were statistically significant ( p < 0.0001). These exploratory findings demonstrate differences in formulation characteristics, release behaviour and measured short-term plasma exposure. Larger studies with longer sampling, validated analytical procedures and compositionally matched comparators are required to confirm the pharmacokinetic findings and investigate the contribution of individual formulation components. Article.Title: The influence of storage temperature on platelet toll-like receptor 2 integrity in platelet concentrates
Article.Authors: Vaz D.; Kobsar A.; Kuhn S.; Koessler A.; Zeller-Hahn J.; Gittel J.; Stigloher C.; Koessler J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Platelet concentrates (PC) are used for the treatment of thrombocytopenia or platelet-dependent hemorrhage. In addition to hemostasis, platelets are also involved in immunological processes. In this context, platelet toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) mediates important responses to bacterial antigens. Since storage temperature of PC storage essentially interferes with platelet reactivity, it was the aim of this study to investigate TLR2 expression, distribution and function in platelets from PC either stored at room temperature (RT, 20–24 °C) or cold temperature (CT, 2–6 °C). For this purpose, apheresis-derived PC were initially stored at RT before splitting into two parts on day 1. Then, one part was stored at RT and the other part at CT until day 5. On day 1 and 5, samples were drawn for comparative analysis. Flow cytometry was used to analyze TLR2 surface expression, induced uptake of fibrinogen or TLR2 ligand Pam3CSK4, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and CD40L expression. Transmission electron microscopy and high-resolution fluorescence microscopy were performed to visualize TLR2 distribution. TLR2-stimulated secretion of platelet chemokines RANTES, NAP-2, PDGF, PF4 and sCD40L was measured by immunoassays. Regardless of storage temperature, TLR2 surface expression and its subcellular distribution were not substantially changed until day 5. TLR2 was able to stimulate CD40L expression, the uptake of fibrinogen and the internalization of TLR2 ligand Pam3CSK4 likewise at CT or RT. TLR2-induced ROS production was remarkably reduced on day 5 accordingly at both temperatures. The potential for TLR2-mediated release of PF4 and PDGF showed some slight variations over the storage period at CT and at RT. In conclusion, TLR2 integrity and associated functions may be variably influenced by storage time and temperature. It is therefore essential to further address platelet immune functions, in addition to hemostatic functions, to optimize storage conditions of PC.

Article.Title: A CGM-derived late-phase glycemic response phenotype during fasted moderate-intensity running
Article.Authors: Park W.; Ju S.; Shong M.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: This exploratory study evaluated whether late-phase glycemic responses during fasted moderate-intensity running summarize continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) responses and relate to skeletal muscle index (SMI). Thirty healthy adults (19 men, 11 women) completed two or three 60-min treadmill runs (76 trials) at 40–60% heart rate reserve, calculated using age-predicted maximal heart rate. Glucose Increase ( \(\Delta G\) ) was defined as mean glucose during the final 30 min minus fasting baseline. The first principal component explained 67% of time-series variance; its scores correlated with \(\Delta G\) ( R 2 = 0.92). Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.424 (95% CI, 0.139–0.663) for single trials and 0.642 (0.275–0.830) for repeated-trial averages. Overall, \(\Delta G\) was not significantly associated with SMI ( R 2 = 0.10, nominal p = 0.084). Post hoc, a negative association in recreational runners ( R 2 = 0.24, nominal p = 0.024) was non-significant after sex adjustment (p = 0.67; SMI–sex VIF = 5.06) or, separately, Holm correction across three SMI– \(\Delta G\) regressions (adjusted p = 0.072); trained runners showed no significant association. Given post hoc stratification, a small sample, and multiple comparisons, this finding remains hypothesis-generating. These findings support \(\Delta G\) , averaged across repeated sessions, as a candidate CGM-derived glycemic response phenotype, but do not establish it as a muscle-mass biomarker.

Article.Title: Room-temperature consolidated calcium phosphate bioceramics as drug delivery systems
Article.Authors: Dauge L.; Ernestsons G.; Ernestsons G.; Locs J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bioceramic vehicles for localized drug delivery are well established, but the ceramic sintering temperatures limit the means of drug incorporation and surface-bound drugs are often released rapidly into the surrounding environment. Room-temperature consolidation (RTC) opens a possibility to create bioceramic drug delivery systems, where the drug is distributed within the entire volume of the carrier, potentially achieving higher control over the release profile. In this study, strontium ranelate (SR) containing nanocrystalline hydroxyapatite (nHAp), amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) and octacalcium phosphate (OCP) bioceramics were produced, using RTC. The low-temperature, high-pressure approach preserved the metastable, low-crystalline calcium phosphates, but minor pressure-induced deterioration of the drug’s ranelic acid residue was present. Ultimately, by varying the consolidation pressure, drug content and calcium phosphate matrix, drug delivery lasting from three to 58 days was achieved.

Article.Title: Computational workflows for neoantigen identification in non-small cell lung cancer: a scoping review and meta-analysis of neoantigen vaccine trials
Article.Authors: Akurut E.; Nabisubi P.; Namugamba B.; Semawule S.; Odur W.; Babirye S.; Ogenrwot J.; Walugembe J.; Kakembo F.; Nabukeera K.; Isiagi M.; Richard E.; Kabbale K.; Sabakaki P.; Kyomukama R.; Adera D.; Aweco E.; Nakabiri G.; Namuswe M.; Nyanzi J.; Nagaba R.; Nabakooza H.; Agasi H.; Kebirungi G.; Kawalya H.
Article.Abstract: Computational identification of tumor-specific neoantigens is central to personalized vaccine development for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, variation in sequencing, HLA typing, epitope prediction, candidate prioritization, and reporting may limit reproducibility and clinical translation. A scoping review with an embedded random-effects meta-analysis of vaccine-induced T-cell responses was conducted to evaluate computational workflows for neoantigen identification in NSCLC and examined progression towards functional validation and vaccine development for studies between 2005 and 2025. Computational workflow methods and reporting completeness were assessed across eight workflow computational domains. Clinical studies were quantitatively pooled only when explicit patient-level post-vaccination responder numerators and immune-evaluable denominators were available. The primary meta-analysis used a random-effects binomial-logit generalized linear mixed model (GLMM). Twenty-five unique studies published between 2005 and 2025 were identified, and their contributions included: 22 to the computational workflow synthesis, 5 to human clinical vaccine synthesis; 1 study contributed to translational evidence. Whole-exome and RNA sequencing were used in 86.4% and 63.6% of computational studies, respectively. All studies performed MHC class I prediction, whereas only 22.7% incorporated MHC class II prediction, and 31.8% reported clonality assessment. Reporting completeness was 85.8%, with the greatest variability occurring in downstream neoantigen candidate prioritization and validation. Four clinical studies provided extractable patient-level immunogenicity data, with 35 of 46 immune-evaluable patients demonstrating a vaccine-induced T-cell response. The primary GLMM yielded a pooled response estimate of 92.53% (95% CI 42.71–99.52%), although alternative random-effects models yielded estimates of approximately 81–82%, indicating substantial uncertainty in the magnitude of the pooled response. Alternative random-effects sensitivity analyses yielded estimates of approximately 81–82%. All five human clinical vaccine studies were judged to have an overall serious risk of bias. Vaccination was generally well tolerated, although clinical efficacy remains uncertain because of small early-phase cohorts, concomitant therapies, and heterogeneous outcome assessment. The study incompleteness and variability in neoantigen downstream analysis call for standardization of computational workflows, and larger cohort studies may give better insights into long-term vaccine-specific T-cell responses compared to small cohort clinical trials.

Article.Title: Quantum correlations on living temporal exclusivity graphs
Article.Authors: Darvish M.; Eshaghi Gordji M.
Article.Abstract: Exclusivity graphs encode classical, quantum, and generalized-probabilistic bounds through graph invariants. We study a temporal extension in which the active event set and the exclusivity relation may vary with time. We distinguish two operational regimes. In the snapshot regime, exclusivity is imposed only within individual time slices, and the resulting time-weighted score is bounded by the corresponding weighted average of static graph parameters. In the global regime, exclusivity relations may also connect events occurring at different times, so the appropriate graph-theoretic description is a single graph on time-stamped events. A three-slice example based on \(C_5\) , \(P_5\) , and \(K_5\) illustrates the distinction. For independent snapshots, the classical, quantum, and fractional bounds are respectively \(2,\qquad \frac{\sqrt{5}+4}{3}\approx 2.079,\qquad \frac{13}{6}\approx 2.167.\) After one inter-temporal exclusivity edge is introduced, the corresponding global weighted graph satisfies \(\alpha (G_{\mathcal {T}},\omega )=\vartheta (G_{\mathcal {T}},\omega )=\alpha ^{*}(G_{\mathcal {T}},\omega )=2.\) Thus, in this example, the additional inter-temporal exclusivity constraint leaves the classical bound unchanged while tightening the quantum and fractional graph-theoretic bounds to the same value. This first example shows that a cross-time constraint can remove a snapshot-level quantum-classical gap. A second, explicitly branch-gated protocol yields a different global graph, \((C_5\vee K_5)\sqcup P_5\) , with weighted bounds 5/3, \((\sqrt{5}+3)/3\) , and 11/6, respectively. Its strict quantum-classical separation is attainable in the stated idealized protocol, but originates in the familiar \(C_5\) subexperiment rather than a new temporal quantum effect. The two examples establish that the effect of cross-time constraints depends on their operational definition.

Article.Title: Integrating GC-MS compositional profiling with ATR-FTIR spectral fingerprinting of Melissa officinalis L. and Thymus vulgaris L. essential oils obtained by supercritical CO2 extraction
Article.Authors: Nejatzadeh-Barandozi F.
Article.Abstract: Essential oils of Melissa officinalis L. (lemon balm) and Thymus vulgaris L. (common thyme) are valued for antioxidant, antimicrobial and antispasmodic bioactivities linked to their monoterpenoid and phenolic content. In this study, oils were isolated from dried leaves by supercritical carbon dioxide extraction (SC-CO 2 ; 40 °C, 10 MPa) and benchmarked against conventional n-hexane maceration, then characterized in parallel by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR, 4000–400 cm⁻¹). Triplicate independent extractions (three extraction batches per species, each prepared from a single commercial plant batch and analysed once) gave yields (mean ± SD) of 0.90 ± 0.03% (SFE) and 1.03 ± 0.07% (n-hexane) for M. officinalis , and 0.97 ± 0.03% and 0.95 ± 0.04% for T. vulgaris . Yields of the two methods did not differ significantly for either species (Welch’s t-test, p = 0.068 for M. officinalis and p = 0.53 for T. vulgaris ), although with three replicates per group these tests have little power and cannot establish equivalence of the methods. GC-MS resolved the T. vulgaris oil as a thymol/γ-terpinene/p-cymene chemotype (23.0%, 29.0% and 20.3% of normalized peak area, respectively; raw means 22.4 ± 0.4%, 28.1 ± 1.1% and 19.8 ± 0.2%) and the M. officinalis oil as a geranial/neral/geranyl acetate profile (23.9 ± 0.3%, 22.5 ± 0.6% and 18.6 ± 0.7%). All percentages derive from manually re-integrated chromatograms (per-replicate resolved-area totals 95.5–99.7% for T. vulgaris and 95.5–97.5% for M. officinalis ). All GC-MS percentages are area-normalized, semi-quantitative relative abundances obtained without compound-specific calibration and, owing to partial co-elution among the major monoterpene hydrocarbons, should be regarded as approximate. ATR-FTIR spectra corroborated these compositions: the composite aromatic C–H wagging band at ~ 808 cm⁻¹ in thyme oil scaled with the combined thymol/p-cymene/γ-terpinene aromatic load, while the 1671 cm⁻¹ α,β-unsaturated carbonyl band in lemon balm oil tracked the pooled geranial/neral fraction. Spectral correlation coefficients between SFE and n-hexane extracts were ≥ 0.99 for both species, consistent with closely similar bulk chemical selectivity of the two non-polar media; because GC-MS was applied only to the SC-CO 2 extracts, this similarity refers to bulk spectral fingerprints rather than compound-resolved composition. Under the mild condition tested (40 °C, 10 MPa), SC-CO 2 extraction retained the diagnostic chemotype of both species. Once anchored to GC-MS reference data, ATR-FTIR fingerprinting may therefore serve as a rapid, solvent-minimal, chromatography-free screening tool for chemotype assessment and essential oil quality control; this application should be regarded as preliminary until it has been tested on independent samples covering different geographical origins, production batches and chemotypes.

Article.Title: Screen-based behaviors over 3 years and executive function and brain-derived neurotrophic factor in adolescents
Article.Authors: de Freitas M.; Romanzini M.; da Costa J.; Romanzini C.; Cossio-Bolaños M.; de Lucena Martins C.; Mota J.; Ronque E.
Article.Abstract: To examine associations of baseline and 3-year changes in screen-based behaviors with executive function and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) in adolescents. The study included 141 adolescents (51% girls) assessed at baseline (2016; mean age 12 years) and follow-up (2019; mean age 15 years). Screen behaviors was assessed at both time points, while executive function and plasma BDNF were assessed at follow-up. Sex-stratified linear and quadratic regression models were fitted. Among boys, higher baseline cellphone use was associated with lower Stroop congruent accuracy (B = − 0.552; 95% CI − 1.035 to − 0.069), while baseline video viewing showed a quadratic association with congruent accuracy (B 2 = −0.445; 95% CI − 0.870 to − 0.020). Among girls, baseline videogame use showed quadratic associations with several executive function outcomes, including incongruent accuracy (B 2 = −3.761; 95% CI − 5.707 to − 1.815) and interference (B 2 = 0.035; 95% CI 0.009 to 0.061), both of which remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. Three-year changes in cellphone, leisure computer, and videogame use showed nominal quadratic associations with executive function outcomes, but none remained significant after correction. No statistically detectable associations were observed with plasma BDNF. Overall, baseline videogame use showed the most consistent associations with Stroop incongruent accuracy and interference among girls, highlighting the importance of considering specific screen-based behaviors and nonlinear patterns when examining executive function.

Article.Title: A two-phase flow model for low-permeability reservoirs coupling imbibition–displacement dynamics with water-injection-induced fractures
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhang H.; Wang N.; Xia W.; Xu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-pressure water injection into low-permeability tight sandstone reservoirs generates cyclic dynamic fractures that enhance flow capacity but risk inducing water channeling. Existing models assume static fractures and a single capillary-pressure curve, and so cannot capture the imbibition-displacement competition operating throughout water injection. Here we combine an embedded discrete fracture model with dual capillary-pressure and relative-permeability models that distinguish imbibition from displacement, yielding an oil-water two-phase flow model coupled to dynamic fracture evolution. Fracture initiation follows the Irwin stress-intensity-factor criterion, fracture geometry and flow properties are updated through an exponential stress-sensitivity equation, and the matrix-fracture equations are solved by a fully implicit finite-difference method. Validation against three core experiments reproduces the multi-peak fluctuation and multi-stage breakthrough of the injection pressure, with a computed breakthrough pressure of 3.0–4.5 MPa matching measurements. Induced fractures shorten the injection-production balance time from 153 to 68 min. An optimal fracture-length interval exists: displacement recovery reaches 61.58% at two-thirds of the fully penetrating length but falls to 40% once the fracture fully penetrates and induces channeling, while the shut-in imbibition oil increment rises from 1.97% to 5.89% as fracture length increases. This work clarifies the synergistic-competitive mechanism between dynamic fracture evolution and matrix imbibition-displacement.

Article.Title: Sustainable low-carbon concrete evaluation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and data-driven modeling
Article.Authors: Kumar B.; Sai A.; Padavala S.; Gashe A.; Nagaraja K.
Article.Abstract: The research paper examines the performance of a low-clinker blended binder system including calcite, bentonite and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) in M30 grade concrete. The main aim of the research is to explore the effect of a combination of calcite, bentonite, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) on the strength and durability properties of M 30 grade of concrete. The cement content was set at 50% with all mixes. A combination of calcite and bentonite, in equal proportions, was used to replace cement at levels of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 15%. The GGBS content was varied to 50%, 45%, 40% and 35% keeping a constant water to cement ratio of 0.45. This study will include an investigation into the fresh concrete properties such as slump and compaction factor, the chemical and mechanical properties, with and without CO 2 sequestration. Moreover, microstructural properties have been taken as a subject of X-Ray Diffraction (XRD). The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and the measurement of alternating current (AC) conductivity is further used to analyze the pore structure of the concrete. Autoregressive and tabular prior data fitting machine learning models were used to predict compressive, split tensile, and flexural strength using only experimental mechanical strength dataset. The models were highly accurate in the testing data with the highest results observed on compressive strength with the use of autoregressive model (R² = 0.9688), split tensile strength with the use of tabular fitting (R 2 = 0.9748) and flexural strength with the use of the autoregressive model (R 2 = 0.9657). These findings prove the possibility of the data-driven method to optimize concrete mix design and improve the sustainability performance. The designed blended binder system is believed to lower the embodied CO 2 emission by about 35–40% relative to traditional M 30 concrete, which is consistent with decarbonization of the world and a sustainable infrastructure objective.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of biochemical and genomic approaches to newborn screening for lysosomal storage disorders in a Chinese cohort
Article.Authors: Mu J.; Zou H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs) are severe inherited metabolic diseases for which early diagnosis through newborn screening (NBS) enables timely initiation of disease specific therapies and improves long term outcomes. However, the comparative performance of biochemical screening, genetic screening, and their combination in Chinese populations remains poorly characterized. This prospective, real-world implementation study was conducted at Jinan Maternity and Child Care Hospital between May 2023 and June 2026. A total of 6204 newborns were allocated to three screening strategies based on parental preference: only biochemical screening (NBS, n = 2581), only newborn genetic screening (NBGS, n = 3193), and combined screening (n = 430). Positive predictive value (PPV), disease specific performance, carrier frequency, and minor allele frequency (MAF) were analyzed. NBS identified 27 initial screen positive cases (0.90%), 5 remained positive on repeat testing, of which 2 were confirmed (1 Fabry disease, 1 Krabbe disease), yielding an overall PPV of 7.4% at initial screening. NBGS identified 2 confirmed cases (1 Fabry, 1 Krabbe). Combined screening identified 1 Fabry case. Carrier frequency analysis revealed that 3.78% carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant. GALC c.1901T > C (1.71%), GALC c.2041G > A (0.69%), and GAA c.761 C > T (0.19%) accounted for 68.6% of all carriers. MAF comparison with ExAC-EAS showed enrichment of GALC c.2041G > A in the northern Chinese population, suggesting a regional founder effect. Biochemical screening for LSDs achieves high sensitivity but is limited by low specificity. Genetic screening offers superior specificity but requires enzymatic confirmation for clinical actionability. The combined strategy effectively provides a high diagnostic accuracy while reducing false positive recalls. Population specific carrier frequency and MAF data from this study provide essential reference information for designing LSD screening programs in Chinese populations.

Article.Title: A study on the spatiotemporal evolution and spatial pattern optimization of Hefei urban ecosystem sustainability based on the emergy-carbon footprint-GIS framework
Article.Authors: Pang Y.; Zhang J.; Asutosh A.; Song G.
Article.Abstract: Rapid urbanization has made assessing urban ecosystem sustainability a critical issue for regional sustainable development. Using five-period land use data from 2000 to 2020, this study constructed an integrated framework combining emergy analysis, carbon footprint accounting, and GIS spatial analysis to systematically diagnose the spatiotemporal evolution of Hefei’s urban ecosystem sustainability and propose spatial optimization strategies. Results show that construction land expanded by 76.5% to 1,370 km², while cropland decreased by 406 km², with 648.55 km² converted during 2010–2015 alone, accounting for 64.8% of the total transition. Total emergy usage increased from 1.85 × 10 22 sej to 4.21 × 10 22 sej, renewable resource share dropped from 8.7% to 4.1%, and the emergy sustainability index fell from 0.112 to 0.085, far below the threshold of 1.0. Carbon emissions surged 14.6-fold from 3.96 to 61.72 million tons, with construction land’s share rising from 9.9% to 92.9%, while net carbon sink surplus shrank by 57.4%. The severely unsustainable zone expanded from 5.2% to 34.4%, and the centroid of carbon emission hotspots shifted 11 km southwestward, consistent with Hefei’s urban development strategy. A core ecological protection area of 425 km² and a low-carbon industrial suitability zone of 1,650 km 2 were identified, with multi-scenario simulations showing the low-carbon scenario could raise the emergy sustainability index to 0.097. This study innovatively integrates emergy analysis, carbon footprint accounting, and GIS into a unified framework, enabling sustainability assessment from aggregate diagnosis to spatial identification. The findings provide scientific support for territorial spatial planning, ecological redline adjustments, and carbon neutrality action plans in Hefei, with the methodological framework serving as a reference for other rapidly urbanizing regions.

Article.Title: Dual loop neural Lie derivative estimation enhanced PSO tuned super-twisting control for maximum power point tracking in PMSG wind systems
Article.Authors: Ullah S.; Yessef M.; Hafeez G.; Alsafran A.; Algethami A.; Kraiem H.
Article.Abstract: A robust nonlinear control methodology is developed for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of wind energy conversion systems (WECS) utilizing permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs). The control framework merges a generalized super-twisting sliding mode controller (Gen-STSMC) with a dual-loop recursive emotional neural network (DLRENN) estimator, enhanced through PSO-based gain optimization. Through its recursive structure, the DLRENN enables online estimation of nonlinear Lie derivative functions, avoiding the necessity of analytical modeling for aerodynamic and electrical uncertainties. PSO is also applied to the optimal tuning of the controller parameters, achieving a desirable trade-off among tracking accuracy, robustness, control effort, and chattering attenuation to further improve controller performance. The stability of the closed-loop system is ensured by the input-output linearization and the zero-dynamics analysis. Simulation results on a 3 kW benchmark show that the proposed method and the three benchmark controllers–feedback-linearization control (FLC), the real-twisting algorithm (RTA), and conventional sliding mode control (CSMC)—all reach an MPPT efficiency of about 99.97% under a highly turbulent wind profile, while the proposed method yields the lowest power-coefficient ripple and chattering. The combination of neural approximation and optimization-based gain tuning provides a practical and efficient solution for practical WECS applications.

Article.Title: Corrosion detection and inversion imaging of buried natural gas pipelines via transient electromagnetic method
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Yang W.; Luo D.; Wei Y.; Yang Q.; Hao L.; Hu B.; Jiao J.
Article.Abstract: Buried metal pipelines operate for extended periods in complex and changeable underground environments, making them susceptible to pipeline corrosion and to weakening of their strength, resulting in pipeline leakage accidents and serious threats such as economic losses, casualties and environmental pollution. At present, the trenchless detection technology for in‑service natural gas pipelines has problems such as strong interference of detection signals and single signal interpretation methods. Based on the theory of transient electromagnetic methods, this paper designs the TEM detection model of buried pipelines and gives the principle and applicability analysis of TEM detection. The numerical simulation of the inversion shows that the resistivity of the pipeline and the surrounding medium obtained by the inversion are consistent with the real model. The measured data sets show that when the buried metal pipeline is corroded, the local induced electromotive force is enhanced on the transient electromagnetic multi‑channel map, and the abnormal characteristics become evident.

Article.Title: PVminer: a domain-specific tool to detect the patient voice in patient generated data
Article.Authors: Fodeh S.; Ma L.; Wang Y.; Talakokkul S.; Puthiaraju G.; Khan A.; Hagaman A.; Lowe S.; Roundtree A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patient generated text such as secure messages, surveys, and interviews contains rich expressions of the patient voice (PV), reflecting both communicative behaviors and social determinants of health (SDOH). Traditional qualitative coding methods are labor intensive and do not scale to the large number of patient-authored messages produced across health systems. Existing machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) approaches provide partial solutions for analyzing patient generated text. However, most methods treat patient generated text and SDOH as separate tasks, ignoring overlapping expressions within the same message. Some of them rely on pre-trained models that are not well suited to patient-facing language. These limitations highlight the need for scalable, domain-adapted approaches that jointly model the linguistic and social dimensions of patient generated communication. We introduce PVminer, a domain-adapted NLP tool for structuring patient voice in secure patient-provider communication. PVminer formalizes PV detection as a multi-label, multi-class prediction task and integrates three components: pre-training of patient-specific BERT encoders (PV-BERT-base and PV-BERT-large), unsupervised topic modeling for thematic augmentation (PV-Topic-BERT), and fine-tuned classifiers of Code, Subcode, and Combo-level labels. Topic information derived from a PV-Topic-BERT model is appended during both fine-tuning and inference to enrich input representations with high-level semantic cues. PVminer with our proposed domain-adapted pre-trained models achieves strongest performance across all three hierarchical tasks and outperforms biomedical and clinical pre-trained baselines. For Code-level classification, PV-BERT-large attains an F1 of 82.25%. At the Subcode level, PV-BERT-base achieves the highest F1 of 80.14%. For the more challenging Combo-level task, PV-BERT-base and PV-BERT-large obtain F1 of 77.58% and 77.87%. An ablation study further shows that author identity and topic-based augmentation each contribute meaningful gains. The training and evaluation code is available at https://github.com/Data-Mining-Lab-Yale/PVBERT .

Article.Title: A data-driven framework for identifying innovation pathways in rice abiotic stress research
Article.Authors: Lin Q.; Wu D.; Yang L.; Hu Z.; Xian G.; Zhang X.; Sun T.
Article.Abstract: Research on abiotic stress-related traits in rice—particularly salt tolerance, drought tolerance, and cadmium accumulation—is important for understanding environmental constraints on crop performance and supporting trait improvement. However, scientific innovation in this field still relies heavily on expert experience, and existing research data remain fragmented and dispersed across pathways, making it difficult to systematically integrate experimental technologies, biological entities, environmental factors, and phenotypic traits into traceable innovation pathways. To address this gap, this study develops a data-driven methodological framework that integrates multi-source data fusion, knowledge-base enhancement, multilayer heterogeneous-network construction, multidimensional innovation-feature measurement, and innovation-pathway identification. A curated literature dataset was first constructed by integrating full-text research articles with domain knowledge bases. A knowledge-base-enhanced entity–relation extraction model (KB-EREM), combining Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) with Lightweight Retrieval-Augmented Generation (LightRAG) was subsequently developed. A technology-data heterogeneous network was then built, comprising nine categories of scientific data and technical entities together with eight types of association relationships. On this basis, an innovation-feature measurement indicator system was established across five dimensions—data-drivenness, interdisciplinarity, connectivity, frontier orientation, and breakthrough potential—and the entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method was employed to quantify innovation characteristics along scientific research chains. An iterative depth-first search (DFS) algorithm was further used to identify innovation pathways within the heterogeneous network, thereby identifying potential innovation pathways in rice abiotic-stress research. The framework extracted 10,409 entity instances and 13,034 relation instances, with F1-scores of 87.58% for entity extraction and 75.03% for relation extraction. Empirical results show that innovation pathways in rice abiotic-stress research exhibit a characteristic “technological support → gene-related association → phenotypic realisation” structure, and the associations among molecular breeding technologies, environmental factors, and target traits occupy central positions in the network. Using salt-tolerance research as an example, pathways associated with SHMT3, HOG1, and OsVTC1-3 display high innovation-feature values, identifying these genes as literature-derived, computationally prioritised candidates associated with rice salt tolerance, whose biological roles require further experimental validation. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies traceable innovation pathways in rice abiotic-stress research, providing methodological support for literature-based candidate prioritisation, research-pathway tracing, and hypothesis generation in data-intensive crop research.

Article.Title: A novel hybrid fuzzy membership function-based feature transformation for cardiovascular disease prediction
Article.Authors: Pathak A.; Chaubey M.; Marisha N/A.; Gupta M.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular disease portrays a critical health issue due to its huge numbers of morbidity and mortality rate. Stable, accurate prediction and diagnosis are important for early intervention, monitoring, and treatment. The area of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) significantly enhanced the healthcare sector, providing early detection of diseases, diagnosis, monitoring, and personalized care. Despite the advancement in AI-based diagnosis system existing methods often struggle with handling uncertainty, complexity, discreteness in datasets which leads to model overfitting, poses a significant challenge to develop a generalized model. This study proposes a novel hybrid fuzzy membership function-based feature transformation technique. The proposed technique combines gaussian function to capture localized precision in high-confidence region and sigmoid functions ensure smooth transition in area with greater certainty. Subsequently, the proposed hybrid fuzzy membership function (F-MF) integrated with gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) and bagging Fuzzy-GBDT for heart disease prediction. The proposed approaches reduce overfitting, adapt to complex, nonlinear decision boundaries and improve predictability of individual features, resulting in improved model generalization and overall prediction performance. The validation of the proposed methodology is carried out on two publicly available benchmark datasets: (1) UCI Heart Disease dataset and (2) a publicly available Kaggle version of the Framingham dataset for cardiovascular risk prediction. The proposed model on Dataset 1 achieved accuracy of 98%, precision of 98%, recall of 98%, F1 score of 99% and AU-ROC (Area Under- Receiver Operating Characteristics) score 0.99. The model achieved an accuracy of 84.23%, precision of 88.86%, recall of 70.49%, F1 score of 78.62% and AU-ROC of 0.91 on Dataset 2. Furthermore, 10-fold cross-validation confirms the model’s generalizability, with minimum variance in performance across all folds. These results highlight the potential of hybrid fuzzy membership functions with GBDT models for reliable, interpretable CVD prediction subject to further external and clinical validation.

Article.Title: Explainable artificial intelligence for prehospital identification of endovascular thrombectomy candidates: a retrospective real-world study
Article.Authors: Eder P.; Moser O.; Rashid A.; Schlemm E.; Hessler J.; von Jouanne-Diedrich H.; Ziegler V.; Soda H.
Article.Abstract: Acute ischaemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion requires rapid endovascular treatment (EVT). Prehospital stroke scales, though widely used, have not achieved an optimal balance of sensitivity, specificity, and overall discriminative performance, underlining the need for evaluation of machine learning (ML) approaches to improve early identification of EVT candidates. We conducted a retrospective development and internal validation study based on digital real-world data from consecutive EMS-transported patients with suspected stroke ( n = 1,435, 94 EVT events [6.6%]) from the Stroke Angel initiative in a rural region in Germany (Rhön-Grabfeld), covering the period from January 2015 to June 2021. Predicted probabilities of six ML models were recalibrated using Platt scaling, and clinical relevance was evaluated using decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were computed to quantify individual feature contributions to model predictions. Among 287 patients (24 EVT events) in the evaluation cohort, Random Forest achieved the highest AUROC (0.85 [95% CI, 0.78–0.90]), with sensitivity of 0.92 [0.74–0.99], specificity of 0.66 [0.60–0.72]. The 4I-SS (score > 2) yielded an AUROC of 0.82 [0.72–0.89], sensitivity of 0.87 [0.67–0.96], and specificity of 0.69 [0.64–0.74]. Bootstrapped intervals overlapped across all metrics and platt scaling probabilities, suggesting no statistically significant superiority.

Article.Title: Sensitivity analysis and physics-aware deep learning for aluminum mirror coatings: when network architecture outweighs loss-function design
Article.Authors: Ghapanvari E.; Salahshoor M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aluminum is the most prevalent material for broadband mirror coatings, yet the design parameters affecting its specular performance, such as film thickness and surface roughness, are not well quantified. Additionally, the pace of developing surrogate models for metallic reflectance has been slower than for dielectric models. This study addresses these gaps by implementing a numerically validated transfer-matrix framework for a single absorbing aluminum layer on a glass substrate, accompanied by an optical sensitivity analysis. The engine agrees with an independent transfer-matrix implementation to machine precision over 400–1200 nm, and its conclusions are robust to the choice among five aluminum optical-constant datasets. Results indicate reflectance saturates past an opaque thickness of approximately 40 nm, and the p -polarized response shows a pseudo-Brewster minimum that does not reach zero. Surface roughness decreases specular reflectance due to the Debye–Waller factor, with a characteristic $$1/\lambda ^{2}$$ scaling affecting the blue end of the spectrum. We then present a physics-informed deep-learning surrogate model that links thickness and roughness to the reflectance-deficit spectrum, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.9999 with held-out data. Our findings suggest that the architecture of the neural network is crucial for addressing metallic reflectance, contrasting with traditional approaches, provided that the loss function constrains the magnitude of the spectrum. A surrogate-driven search of the bounded design space, verified by exact transfer-matrix calculations, recovers the physically expected boundary optimum (an opaque, smooth film with a band-averaged reflectance of 91.5%), which we use as an end-to-end consistency check of the pipeline; the same calculations show that 36.5 nm of aluminum already reaches within 0.5 percentage points of this value.

Article.Title: One-point versus three-point botulinum toxin type A injection for masseter reduction: a randomized controlled trial in a Thai population
Article.Authors: Khwanngam E.; Tantipoj C.; Arunakul K.
Article.Abstract: Botulinum toxin type A injection is widely used for lower facial contouring, particularly in Asian populations. However, there is no consensus regarding the optimal injection technique. While multi-point injection is often advocated to enhance toxin distribution, single-point injection is favored for its procedural simplicity. This study aimed to compare the longitudinal effects of one-point and three-point injection techniques on lower facial volume reduction and patient satisfaction. This triple-blind randomized controlled trial included 24 participants, randomly assigned to one-point or three-point injection groups. All participants received 25 U of prabotulinumtoxinA (Nabota ® ) per side of the masseter muscle. Lower facial volume was assessed using three-dimensional facial scanning, and patient satisfaction was evaluated using the FACE-Q™ questionnaire at baseline and at 1, 2, 3, and 6 months post-injection. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Significant time-dependent changes were observed in both lower facial volume reduction and patient satisfaction ( p < 0.001). No significant technique-by-time interaction was detected for either outcome, providing no evidence of differences in the longitudinal response patterns between the two injection techniques. Both one-point and three-point injection techniques were associated with longitudinal changes in lower facial volume and patient satisfaction. No statistically significant differences in longitudinal response patterns were detected between the two techniques. The one-point technique may represent a simpler injection approach worthy of further investigation. Thai Clinical Trials Registry: TCTR20251016020 (registered October 16, 2025).

Article.Title: A sclerostin-targeting polydopamine nanoplatform promotes osteogenesis and attenuates ovariectomy-induced bone loss by reducing ferroptosis-like injury
Article.Authors: Sun D.; Chen J.; Ge S.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass, disrupted trabecular microarchitecture and increased fracture risk. Although sclerostin inhibition is an established bone-anabolic strategy, systemic blockade may raise safety concerns and conventional drug delivery to bone remains inefficient. Here, we developed a sclerostin-targeting, lipid-coated polydopamine nanoplatform loaded with N-oleoyl-L-serine (OS) and modified with the sclerostin-targeting aptamer Aptscl56 (PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56). The formulation showed a uniform nanoscale morphology, negative surface charge, favorable colloidal stability, efficient N-oleoyl-L-serine loading, measurable Aptscl56 conjugation and sustained release behavior. In primary bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56 exhibited good biocompatibility and enhanced osteogenic differentiation, as indicated by increased alkaline phosphatase activity, matrix mineralization and upregulation of osteogenic markers including ALP, RUNX2, OSX and OPN. Single-component controls demonstrated that PDA alone and free Aptscl56 had limited osteogenic effects, whereas OS alone and non-targeted PDA@NLipo-PEG produced moderate effects; the complete PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56 formulation exerted the strongest osteogenic activity. In ovariectomized mice, PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56 improved femoral trabecular bone parameters and histological mineralization. Proteomic analysis suggested treatment-associated changes in ferroptosis- and mitochondrial respiratory-chain-related proteins, with Uqcrfs1 emerging as a high-degree candidate protein within a mitochondrial protein interaction network. Mechanistically, PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56 reduced ferroptosis-like injury in OVX bone tissue and RSL3-treated osteoblasts, as reflected by restored GPX4/FTH1/FTL expression, reduced ACSL4 expression, and decreased Fe 2+ and 4-HNE levels. Uqcrfs1 overexpression partially attenuated these protective effects, supporting its involvement in the anti-ferroptotic response to PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56. Representative fluorescence biodistribution and safety analyses further supported the bone-targeting tendency and preliminary biosafety of the formulation. These findings indicate that PDA@NLipo-Aptscl56 is a promising bone-targeted nanoplatform for promoting osteogenesis and attenuating OVX-induced bone loss, partly through suppression of ferroptosis-like oxidative injury.
