Article.Title: Intestinal goblet cell defect is linked to immune dysregulation in multiple sclerosis
Article.Authors: Montini F.; Cencicchio M.; Schwerdtfeger L.; Palmieri V.; Massimino L.; Tonino S.; Asnicar F.; Ungaro F.; Segata N.; Martinelli V.; Weiner H.; Falcone M.
Article.Abstract: Modifications of the gut environment including dysbiosis, immune dysregulation, and impaired barrier integrity have been documented in multiple sclerosis (MS). The mucus layer is an important component of the gut barrier that regulates host-microbiota interactions. Mucus-secreting goblet cells and mucus-associated immune pathways are crucial to promote tolerance and regulatory T-cell differentiation, thus maintaining immune homeostasis in the gut but also in extra-intestinal tissues such as the central nervous system (CNS). Here we investigated the integrity of the mucus layer and mucus-associated immune regulatory pathways in multiple sclerosis patients. We analyzed the integrity of the duodenal mucus layer and its association with microbiota composition and immune regulation in intestinal biopsies and fecal samples from multiple sclerosis patients and healthy controls. Duodenal biopsies and fecal samples were analyzed using histology, flow cytometry, qPCR, and fecal metagenomic whole-genome sequencing. Multiple sclerosis patients have evidence of goblet cell dysfunction measured as a significant reduction of Alcian Blue-positive and UEA-1-positive goblet cells in intestinal crypts. Fecal metagenomic analysis was associated with higher relative abundance of species with reported mucin-degrading capacity, including A. muciniphila , (A) glycaniphila , (B) cellulosilyticus , and P. coprophilus . Further, there was reduced relative abundance of species reported to support goblet cell differentiation and maturation, such as B. breve and (C) butyricum . Immunophenotyping demonstrated a reduction of intestinal FoxP3-positive regulatory T cells. In EAE-immunized mice, enzymatic disruption of the mucus barrier worsened CNS autoimmunity, supporting a functional link between mucus barrier integrity and neuroinflammation. These data indicate that mucus barrier integrity is associated with regulation of CNS autoimmunity and suggest that restoring mucus integrity may represent a therapeutic strategy in MS. The intestine is protected by a mucus layer that helps keep gut bacteria separated from the body and supports balanced immune responses. In multiple sclerosis, changes in the gut environment influence immune cells that attack the brain and spinal cord. We studied intestinal samples, stool bacteria, and immune cells from people with multiple sclerosis and healthy individuals. People with multiple sclerosis had evidence of goblet cell dysfunction, and lower abundance of bacterial species reported to sustain mucus regeneration, and reduced intestinal differentiation of regulatory T cells that are essential to prevent autoimmune attack of the brain. In a mouse model of multiple sclerosis, damaging the mucus layer made disease worse. These findings suggest that protecting or restoring the intestinal mucus barrier integrity may help support immune balance and prevent disease relapses in multiple sclerosis.

Article.Title: Pre-forceps intrapartum ultrasound measurements are associated with difficult forceps delivery in nulliparous women
Article.Authors: Pei Y.; Tian Y.; Chen Y.; Li Y.; Yu J.; Hou J.; Su Z.; Wu Q.; Jiang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Forceps-assisted vaginal delivery can avert second-stage cesarean delivery, but how difficult the procedure will be is hard to anticipate from digital examination alone. We prospectively studied 120 nulliparous women with singleton term cephalic pregnancies undergoing Simpson forceps-assisted delivery. Transperineal ultrasound was performed after the decision for forceps delivery and before instrument application. Difficult forceps delivery, defined as two or more traction attempts or failed forceps delivery requiring cesarean delivery, occurred in 25 women (20.8%). A smaller angle of progression and a non-upward fetal head direction were independently associated with difficult delivery, whereas digitally assessed fetal station was not. The ultrasound model had an apparent area under the curve of 0.845 (95% CI, 0.751–0.939) and an optimism-corrected value of 0.834; adding clinical variables did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC, 0.045; P = 0.19). An exploratory two-marker stratification separated women across a risk gradient, from 5.3% with neither unfavorable marker to 70.6% with both ( P for trend < 0.001). Pre-forceps transperineal ultrasound measurements were therefore associated with procedural difficulty in this cohort. This single-center study had 25 outcome events and the risk threshold was derived from these data; external validation and evaluation of clinical impact are required before these measurements inform management.

Article.Title: Compact SWB monopole antenna with an SWB frequency selective surface for radiation performance enhancement
Article.Authors: Zadehparizi F.; Barzegar-Parizi S.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a super-wideband (SWB) monopole antenna and frequency-selective surface (FSS) layers to enhance its radiation characteristics. The monopole antenna consists of a radiating patch featuring triangular strips along with both triangular and rectangular cuts. The feed line also incorporates triangular cuts. The partial ground plane includes rectangular and triangular cuts at its lower and upper edges, respectively, as well as a rectangular notch connecting two triangular strips at the center of the ground plane’s upper edge. To improve radiation performance, SWB FSS sheets with different array sizes (4 × 4, 6 × 6, and 8 × 8) are designed and placed behind the antenna to reflect backward radiation. The final antenna with the 4 × 4 array achieves an operating bandwidth from 2.9 to 48 GHz and a peak gain of 8.3 dBi, while occupying a compact size of 28 × 28 × 29.2 mm 3 . Owing to its compact size, super-wide operating bandwidth, and enhanced radiation characteristics and gain, the proposed antenna is a promising option for broadband and SWB wireless applications.

Article.Title: A unified graph neural network framework for artery labelling across multiple vascular territories
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Singh S.; Gharleghi R.; Moses D.; Sowmya A.; Beier S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vascular disease is a major public health challenge, with coronary artery disease the leading cause of death worldwide. Improved diagnostics through vascular imaging, including computed tomography coronary angiography, depend on accurate anatomical labelling of arteries. However, manual labelling is labour-intensive because arterial trees are complex and variable. Traditional rule-based methods lack adaptability across protocols, while convolutional neural networks often fail to capture the spatial and topological relationships required for accurate labelling. We propose an adaptable graph neural network (GNN) framework for automated artery labelling across coronary, intracranial, and abdominal anatomies. Artery centrelines are represented as graphs, with anatomically informed node features, including hierarchical depth and segment orientation, capturing structural patterns shared across vascular regions. By learning from anatomical connectivity rather than fixed geometric templates, the framework reduces reliance on manual feature engineering and supports cross-domain application. To our knowledge, this is the first study to evaluate GNN-based artery labelling across multiple anatomical domains. Graph Convolutional Networks achieved F1-scores of 0.895 and 0.870 on two independent coronary datasets, while GraphSAGE performed best for intracranial and abdominal arteries, achieving F1-scores of 0.967 and 0.992. These results demonstrate a practical, adaptable, and generalisable approach to automated artery labelling in medical image analysis.

Article.Title: Electroglottographic and acoustic metrics of vocal technique in trained lyric sopranos: a descriptive cross-dataset study
Article.Authors: Niu Q.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: Vocal technique in lyric sopranos is a central topic in voice science and vocal pedagogy, yet existing studies are commonly limited by small samples, the lack of systematic physiological–acoustic comparison, and weak ecological validity. In this study, electroglottographic (EGG) and acoustic signals were recorded simultaneously from 24 trained lyric sopranos, yielding 1,104 valid tasks across three vowels and four pitch points for four techniques—vibrato, straight tone, breathy, and trill—and a cross-dataset comparison was performed within the acoustic feature space using the female subset of VocalSet (154 segments). Between-technique comparisons were descriptive, summarised as group means with 95% confidence intervals and effect sizes rather than by hypothesis testing. Breathy tasks were descriptively lower in the contact quotient at a 25% threshold (CQ 25 ), the dEGG closing-to-opening peak amplitude ratio (dEGG C/O ratio), cepstral peak prominence (CPP), and the harmonics-to-noise ratio (HNR), and higher in the first-to-second-harmonic amplitude difference (H1 − H2) and shimmer, whereas trill tasks were descriptively higher in EGG-jitter, the standard deviation of the fundamental frequency (F0 SD), modulation rate, and modulation extent than vibrato, an elevation consistent with intended F0 modulation rather than cycle irregularity. Within-subject Spearman correlations indicated consistent associations between EGG and acoustic measures, the strongest being between EGG-jitter and acoustic jitter ( r = 0.864 pooled across techniques; within-technique median r = 0.575). Random forest classification trained on the experimental data and tested on VocalSet reached an accuracy of 0.961 and a macro-averaged ROC-AUC of 0.966, whereas reverse transfer from VocalSet to the experimental data was lower (accuracy 0.889); trill was the least reliably recovered technique in the forward direction (recall 0.848). These results indicate asymmetric segment-level transfer across the two datasets examined, but do not establish singer-independent generalization because singer composition, recording conditions, equipment, and task format differed simultaneously. This study proposes, as a descriptive framework requiring further validation, a two-level EGG–acoustic metric structure covering glottal contact, closing dynamics, cycle stability, source-spectrum quality, and resonance focusing, which may serve as a candidate set of variables for the objective description of lyric soprano techniques and for cross-dataset research.

Article.Title: Evaluation of key parameters affecting gasifier roof subsidence under thermal damage conditions
Article.Authors: Jianhua W.; Lin X.; Jun M.; Huan W.
Article.Abstract: Aiming at investigating the gasifier roof subsidence and variations with the related parameters under thermal damage conditions (TDC), this study established the fixed beam model of the rock beam (RB) and constructed the propagation equation of the temperature field in the rock under TDC. Using static equilibrium theory, the differential equation of the deflection curve of the RB was derived and solved to obtain the RB deflection under particular thermal damage conditions. The time-dependent variations in bending moment, deflection, position of the neutral layer, thermal flexural rigidity, and limit span of the RB were compared and examined in depth. The results show that when the elastic modulus dropped with increasing temperature, compared with the values at normal temperature, the deformation of the RB under TDC was greater, the maximum positive bending moment was smaller, and the maximum negative bending moment was greater. The position of the neutral layer first rose and then dropped slowly but was always located above the neutral layer at normal temperature. Thermal flexural rigidity determined the RB’s deformation and the bending moment’s distribution. A larger thermal flexural rigidity indicated smaller subsidence of the key stratum and vice versa. The limit span in the middle of the RB was subjected to the combined effect of the bending moment and the position of the neutral layer. Compared with the measured surface subsidence curves in the Huating Underground Gasification Project, the deflection curves under TDC conditions were more consistent with the actual conditions than those under thermal-mechanical coupling conditions (TMC) regarding the variation characteristics. Based on the calculated results, the maximum surface subsidence of the project was approximately 65 mm.

Article.Title: Person-centred care, outdoor restorative experiences, and well-being in Lithuanian residential long-term care facilities: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zlibinaite L.; Nilsson A.; Mazeike L.; Matukyniene K.; Engström M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multimorbidity, functional impairment, and depressive symptoms are common among long-term care residents. Person-centred care and restorative green spaces may be relevant to well-being, but have rarely been examined together using residents’ own reports. This cross-sectional study examined associations of resident-rated person-centred care and perceived restorativeness of facility gardens/patios with life satisfaction and depressive symptoms. Data were collected from 219 residents in 14 facilities across Lithuania. Analyses accounted for facility clustering and adjusted for sex, age, frailty, and the staff-to-resident ratio. Nearly half had minimal depressive symptoms (49.3%), 31.5% mild and 19.1% moderate to severe. Person-centred care and perceived restorativeness correlated positively with life satisfaction and negatively with depressive symptoms. In adjusted models, higher scores of person-centred care and perceived restorativeness were associated with higher life satisfaction and fewer depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that interpersonal care processes and restorative experiences of green spaces may both be relevant to residents’ well-being. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify these associations.

Article.Title: Associations between breastfeeding duration and blood pressure in children and adolescents: evidence from a cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen L.; Cheng X.; Zheng S.; Tahir M.; Wang Y.; Luo S.; Zhong H.; Huang D.; Chen L.; An X.; Liang X.
Article.Abstract: Breastfeeding is widely recognized as beneficial for child health, yet the relationship between breastfeeding duration and long-term cardiovascular outcomes, particularly blood pressure (BP), remains incomplete. This study aimed to examine the association between breastfeeding duration and blood pressure (BP) among school-aged children in southwest China. A cohort of 15,007 children aged 6-13 years from the Chongqing Health Children Cohort was analyzed. Participants were stratified by breastfeeding duration. Mixed-effects linear regression models were used to investigate the associations between breastfeeding duration and BP parameters; while mixed-effects logistic regression was applied to evaluate the associations with prehypertension and hypertension, adjusting confounding variables. Longer breastfeeding (> 10 months) was observed to be statistically associated with elevated diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and mean arterial pressure (MAP), but not systolic blood pressure (SBP), particularly in males, children under 9.3 (50th percentile) years old, and those with birth weight below 3000 g or over 3600 g ( P < 0.001). Further, statistical associations between breastfeeding duration and blood pressure varied by residential region and sex. Statistically significant associations were observed for DBP (β(95%CIs) = 1.18(0.40, 1.97), P = 0.044) among urban children and for SBP (β(95%CIs) = 0.82(0.14, 1.50), P = 0.007) and DBP (β(95%CIs) = 0.99(0.39, 1.60), P = 0.001) among males. This study preliminarily identified observed statistical association between longer breastfeeding duration (> 10 months) and elevated DBP/MAP within certain pediatric subpopulations, highlighting the need for population-specific breastfeeding guidance informed by further evidence related to children cardiovascular health.

Article.Title: Integrated genetic association and computational analysis of ATM variants rs189037 and rs227091 in lung cancer susceptibility among the Bangladeshi population
Article.Authors: Zim A.; Mahmud Z.; Raj K.; Tamanna S.; Rahman T.; Ansari F.; Howlader M.
Article.Abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its increasing incidence in Bangladesh highlights the need for population-specific genetic studies. The ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) gene, a key regulator of the DNA damage response, contains regulatory variants that may influence cancer susceptibility. This study investigated the association of ATM single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) rs189037 (5′UTR, G > A) and rs227091 (3′UTR, C > T) with lung cancer risk in a Bangladeshi population and evaluated their potential regulatory functions using in silico approaches. A case-control study was conducted in a total of 250 individuals comprising lung cancer patients and healthy controls. Genotyping was performed using polymerase chain reaction–restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) analysis. Genetic associations were evaluated under codominant, dominant, and recessive inheritance models, while Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, linkage disequilibrium, and haplotype analyses were performed using SHEsisPlus. Functional predictions were assessed using PolymiRTS, miRNASNP, MicroSNiPer, RegulomeDB, rSNPBase, and RNAfold. Compared with controls, lung cancer patients exhibited significantly lower body mass index, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and reduced red blood cell counts ( p < 0.0001). Under the recessive model, the rs189037 AA genotype was nominally associated with an increased risk of lung cancer (OR = 2.09, 95% CI = 1.22–3.53, p = 0.01, uncorrected for multiple comparisons), with a stronger effect observed among males (OR = 2.19, p = 0.0097). No significant associations were detected in age- or smoking-stratified analyses. In contrast, rs227091 showed no significant association with lung cancer under any genetic model. Both SNPs conformed to Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium and exhibited linkage disequilibrium. Haplotype analysis revealed that the AT haplotype was potentially associated with increased lung cancer risk (OR = 1.445, p = 0.046), whereas the GT haplotype conferred a protective effect (OR = 0.297, p < 0.0001). Bioinformatic analyses predicted that rs227091 may alter multiple miRNA binding sites, while rs189037 received a RegulomeDB score of 1a, indicating strong regulatory potential. These exploratory findings suggest that the ATM rs189037 AA genotype may contributes to increased lung cancer susceptibility, particularly among males, whereas rs227091 appears to have limited functional relevance despite predicted regulatory effects. The rs189037 AA genotype should be regarded as a candidate signal requiring independent replication. Further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is warranted to confirm these associations and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

Article.Title: A deep learning–based CNN approach for accurate islanding detection in microgrids using droop-controlled signal behavior
Article.Authors: Elgamasy M.; Ibrahim E.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes an approach that leverages a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) as a classifier for islanding detection. The proposed method is distinguished by monitoring the individual response of each DG in the system, making it suitable for multi-DG systems. The method monitors the behavior of droop-controlled signals within distributed generation (DG) controllers, analyzing their deviations from expected droop characteristics under various operating conditions. These responses are formatted into two-dimensional images representing droop behavior and fed into the CNN for classification. The approach demonstrates high accuracy of 98.68% in distinguishing between intentional islanding, unintentional islanding, and other normal disturbances. The performance of the model is capped by an outstanding Area Under the Curve (AUC) value of 0.99. Simulation results validate the robustness of the method in accurately detecting islanding events in microgrids.

Article.Title: Thermal enhancement mechanisms in a heat exchanger installed with gear-ring turbulence promoters
Article.Authors: Samruaisin P.; Chokphoemphun S.; Promthaisong P.; Pimsarn M.; Chuwattanakul V.; Naphon P.; Kumar M.; Eiamsa-ard S.
Article.Abstract: The heat transfer enhancement and pressure loss characteristics of a tube fitted with two novel gear-shaped turbulators, namely the gear ring inner (GRI) and gear ring outer, were experimentally and numerically investigated. This study addresses a research gap by systematically evaluating the effects of gear geometry on thermal performance over a wide range of turbulent flow conditions (Re = 6000–20,000). The investigated parameters included three numbers of teeth (N = 4, 6, and 8) and three pitch ratios (PR = 2, 3, and 4). The results demonstrate that the insertion of gear-ring turbulators substantially intensifies fluid mixing and disrupts both the thermal and hydrodynamic boundary layers compared to a smooth tube, thereby enhancing convective heat transfer. Depending on the gear configuration, tooth number, and pitch ratio, the Nusselt number increases by 1.82–2.67 times relative to the smooth tube. This enhancement, however, is accompanied by an increase in pressure loss, with the friction factor rising by 8.37–12.53 times. Among the investigated configurations, the GRI insert with N = 8 and PR = 2 at Re = 6000 achieves the highest thermal performance factor of 1.16.

Article.Title: A non-canonical metabolic link between PCSK9 and ENO1 K71 lactylation in colon cancer
Article.Authors: Meng J.; Ding H.; Dong Z.; Su G.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: Lactylation modification regulates tumor metabolism and malignant progression. Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) modulates lactylation and intracellular lactate levels, but its role in glucose metabolism remains unclear. The 4D label‑free lactylproteomics was performed on PCSK9‑knockdown colon cancer cells to screen lactylation targets. Enolase 1 (ENO1) lactylation were verified by immunoprecipitation and Western blot (WB). Site‑directed mutagenesis was used to generate the ENO1 K71R mutant, which abolishes the K71 lactylation acceptor site and serves as a lactylation‑deficient surrogate. Lactate levels and ENO1 enzymatic activity were measured, and core Kla‑regulatory enzymes were assessed by WB. A total of 1128 differential lactylation sites (614 proteins) were identified, mostly downregulated and enriched in glycolytic pathways. Among three glycolytic candidates (ENO1, ALDOA, PGK1), ENO1 showed reduced Kla upon PCSK9 knockdown, accompanied by decreased enzyme activity and lactate production-without altering total ENO1 protein. The ENO1‑K71R mutant, which eliminates the K71 lactylation acceptor site and functions as a lactylation‑deficient surrogate, displayed diminished ENO1 Kla, compromised enzymatic activity, and lowered lactate production. PCSK9 knockdown did not affect canonical Kla‑regulatory enzymes (HDAC1, HDAC2, p300/CBP) protein levels. PCSK9 knockdown is associated with decreased ENO1 K71 Kla and reduced glycolytic activity, independent of canonical Kla‑regulatory enzymes. These findings uncover a non‑canonical metabolic function of PCSK9 in colon cancer.

Article.Title: Effects of holographic, video-based, and text-based feedback on cognitive load, motivation, and perceived learning transfer in virtual EFL classrooms
Article.Authors: Al Shathri A.; Allehyani F.; Ismail S.; Alsaleem A.
Article.Abstract: This study compared holographic, video-based, and text-based feedback in virtual EFL classrooms by examining learners’ cognitive load, motivation, and perceived transfer and by exploring how they experienced the cognitive, motivational, and interactional characteristics of the three modalities. An embedded mixed-methods design with a randomized three-group pretest–posttest quantitative component was used with 95 intermediate-level male Jordanian EFL learners recruited through convenience sampling and subsequently randomly assigned to a Holographic Feedback Group ( n = 32), a Video-Based Feedback Group ( n = 31), or a Text-Based Feedback Group ( n = 32). Across a three-month intervention, all groups followed the same instructional curriculum, but the feedback they received differed in representational format, feedback source, immediacy, and opportunities for reciprocal interaction. Cognitive load, motivation, and perceived transfer were assessed before and after the intervention. The quantitative data were analyzed through MANCOVA and follow-up ANCOVAs, and semi-structured interviews with 32 learners were examined through qualitative content analysis. The quantitative analyses revealed significant between-condition differences across the combined outcomes and each individual outcome. The holographic group showed the lowest cognitive load and the highest motivation and perceived transfer, the video-based group generally occupied an intermediate position, and the text-based group showed the least favorable adjusted outcomes. Four interconnected qualitative themes characterized learners’ experiences: perceived realism and social presence; cognitive immersion and mental effort regulation; feedback immediacy, agency, and self-regulation; and motivational enjoyment, engagement, and emotional resonance. Across the two strands, the pattern suggests that learners associated the holographic feedback package with spatially represented guidance, rapid correction, perceptual clarity, and opportunities for active self-repair; these interconnected features were not manipulated separately. The findings support feedback designs that prioritize pedagogically purposeful immediacy, multimodal clarity, responsiveness, and learner action when immersive technologies are used in virtual EFL instruction.

Article.Title: Life cycle assessment and environmental life cycle costing of nanoscale spintronic energy harvesters at the early design stage
Article.Authors: Gulotta T.; Salomone R.; Saija G.; Primerano P.; Le D.
Article.Abstract: Emerging nanoscale spintronic devices, such as spin rectifiers based on magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), offer a promising solution for harvesting ambient electromagnetic energy for low-power applications. However, previous studies evaluating the environmental and economic benefits of this technology are still limited. This research aims to fill that gap by assessing the environmental, energy, and economic impacts of 15 different laboratory-scale spin rectifier configurations, combining five surface areas and three series arrangements of MTJs, through life cycle assessment and environmental life cycle costing. Hotspot and sensitivity analyses of the most energy-efficient design are included, along with a comparative evaluation of all configurations. Results show that platinum and ruthenium are the primary contributors, accounting for about 5.71 to 93.21% of environmental impacts, followed by copper, which contributes between 3.00 and 86.10%. Fabrication processes, like sputtering and lithography, significantly impact certain categories, with fabrication energy accounting for up to 48.19% of these impacts. Sensitivity analysis indicates that impact results can vary by ± 20% based on assumptions about material losses and energy consumption during manufacturing. Comparing all configurations helps identify which prototype design could reduce environmental and economic impacts more effectively without compromising energy performance. Then, payback time analysis reveals that these devices could offset production impacts through electric energy savings, ranging from 8.5 to 16,800 h, depending on the specific design and impact category. Overall, the study provides insights into the sustainable development of nanoscale spintronic energy harvesters, highlighting areas for material and process improvements to enhance environmental, energy, and economic sustainability.

Article.Title: Generative pre-trained transformer NEOX large language model driven predictive maintenance system in industrial IoT with hybrid deep learning
Article.Authors: Araujo S.; Kamble A.; Patil D.; Hatti D.
Article.Abstract: Predictive maintenance is a crucial approach in the industrial sector, and the utilization of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensors is becoming popular to detect faults and monitor the equipment’s condition. Still, the gathering, processing, and transmission of a large volume of data in predictive maintenance is highly challenging. To tackle such issues, this paper develops the Recurrent Radial Basis Long Short-Term Memory (RRBLSTM)-based predictive maintenance system using IIoT. The IIoT simulation is the primary process for a predictive maintenance system. The input time series data is subjected to the Box-Cox transformation for data transformation. The interval features, Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) features are extracted. The RRBLSTM is developed to label the issue. Using the predictive labels, the prompt is generated. The prompt is converted into a sentence by the utilization of the Generative Pre-trained Transformer NEOX Large Language Model (GPT-NEOX LLM) model. In addition, metrics like Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), R-Square, Mean Square Error (MSE), and Root MSE (RMSE) are used to estimate the efficacy of the model, and the corresponding outcome of 0.325, 0.901, 0.098, and 0.313.

Article.Title: Surface adsorption and phase-selective electronic modulation of monolayer TaSe$$_2$$
Article.Authors: Jeong D.; Alghifari A.; Yeom H.
Article.Abstract: Surface adsorption doping is a powerful way to tune two-dimensional electronic structures of surfaces and monolayers in van der Waals materials, but its impact often goes beyond simple charge transfer. Here, we investigate using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy how different adsorbates, such as alkali metal (K), transition metal (Fe), and simple diatomic molecules (CO and O 2 ), modify the electronic structures of monolayer 1 T - and 1 H -TaSe 2 , prototypical transition-metal-dichalcogenide monolayers featuring distinct electronic phases. While K adsorption induces a rigid band shift consistent with electron doping on both 1 T and 1 H monolayers, Fe adsorption produces spectral broadening without an apparent rigid shift in the 1 T monolayer, indicating distinct local interactions. In contrast, CO and O 2 adsorptions lead to unexpectedly strong rigid band shifts in the 1 T monolayer but leave the 1 H band essentially unchanged. The unusual band shift on the 1 T monolayer is attributed to the formation of an interfacial dipole layer, whose details are revealed by density functional calculations. These results highlight the rich diversity of adsorbate interactions on transition-metal-dichalcogenide monolayers, which can be a versatile knob controlling the electronic properties of van der Waals materials.

Article.Title: A kidney–brain-axis machine-learning framework for predicting 28-day mortality in chronic kidney disease with acute brain injury: derivation and external validation
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Dong G.; Liao S.; Wei W.; Zhou Y.; Li Z.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and acute brain injury (ABI) frequently co-exist in the ICU, yet no dedicated prognostic instrument has been validated for this population. Using MIMIC-IV ( n = 1,887) for derivation and eICU-CRD ( n = 791) for external validation, we derived three decision-oriented tools from a common 43-feature set: a calculator-free 10-feature bedside score (CKD-BI), a 10-variable LASSO-logistic nomogram, and seven machine-learning models benchmarked against SOFA, SAPS-II, APS-III and OASIS, with SHAP interpretability. The CKD-BI score stratified 28-day mortality (Low 3.0%, Intermediate 13.9%, High 36.9%; OR 18.92) and outperformed all four legacy scores (internal CV AUC 0.7937; external 0.7310). The nomogram enabled hand-computable probabilities (external AUC 0.7445), close to the ensemble model (0.7768). Random forest achieved the highest internal test AUC (0.8011; ΔAUC + 0.117, P < 0.001). Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) total minimum was the dominant predictor (mean |SHAP| 1.04). The kidney–brain axis operated through parallel additive pathways; magnesium lacked independent prognostic value after adjustment (OR 0.87/SD, P = 0.226) whereas sodium retained a directionally reversed association (OR 1.21/SD, P = 0.002). These complementary tools offer transparent risk stratification and individual probability estimation with performance comparable to ensemble models; prospective validation with local recalibration is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Nonlinear neutralization of the Bohm potential
Article.Authors: Ourabah K.
Article.Abstract: Quantum particles may behave as classical free particles when they are subjected to suitable nontrivial potentials, as made particularly transparent by the Madelung–Bohm formulation. Here, we discuss a self-consistent counterpart of this mechanism, in which the spatially varying part of the Bohm quantum potential is compensated by nonlinear terms in the Schrödinger equation. Such nonlinearities may appear at a fundamental level, but they are especially relevant in many-particle settings, where the wave function is interpreted as a collective field. We establish a systematic correspondence between representative density profiles and the local nonlinearities required for this compensation, resulting in classical-like dynamics in the Hamilton–Jacobi sense. In the simplest one-dimensional case, hyperbolic-secant, Gaussian, and Lorentzian density profiles recover the established cubic, logarithmic, and cubic–quintic correspondences, respectively, while stretched-exponential and algebraic families lead to broader logarithmic-type and power-law responses. We further extend the construction to radially symmetric states, where dimensional geometry may change either the coefficients or the functional form of the required nonlinearity. In particular, the cubic contribution vanishes for a three-dimensional radial Lorentzian density, whereas a radial hyperbolic-secant profile generates a non-polynomial response involving the inverse hyperbolic secant. Finally, requiring the balance to persist during norm-preserving ballistic expansion recovers the established mass-critical dependence $$F(\rho )\propto \rho ^{2/d}$$ through a direct hydrodynamic scaling argument.

Article.Title: Language comprehension and social cognition in deaf children
Article.Authors: Mejía C.; Cardona J.; Baez S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social cognition (SC)—including emotion recognition, theory of mind (ToM), and empathy—is essential for children’s socioemotional development. Deaf children, particularly those with hearing parents, often experience early language deprivation, which may impact SC. This study examined SC and its association with language comprehension in 83 children aged 6–14 (32 deaf, 51 hearing) using a culturally adapted SC battery and an adapted Token Test. Deaf children showed lower performance in language comprehension and overall SC, with the largest differences observed in ToM and symbolic emotion recognition. No group differences were found in contextual emotion recognition or total empathy, although hearing children showed greater sensitivity to others’ distress. For deaf children, language comprehension mediated both ToM and emotion recognition, but not empathy. These results suggest a dissociation between language-based and nonverbal components of SC. Enhancing early language access in deaf children may be key to supporting their socioemotional development and long-term social integration.

Article.Title: AI-assisted curriculum mapping for competency-based dental education: a comparative study
Article.Authors: Hassanein F.; Alsaeed S.; Abou-Bakr A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Curriculum mapping is essential for competency-based dental education but is often time-consuming and dependent on faculty interpretation. As dental schools undergo digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools may enhance curriculum quality assurance and alignment processes. Large language models (LLMs) may support curriculum alignment tasks; however, evidence in dental education remains limited. This study compared the accuracy, quality, efficiency, and faculty acceptance of ChatGPT-assisted versus manual curriculum mapping. A fixed-order, repeated-measures comparative study included 90 dental faculty members from Periodontology, Oral Medicine, and Oral Diagnosis. Participants completed manual mapping followed by ChatGPT-assisted mapping after a seven-day washout period, aligning course-level Intended Learning Outcomes with Program Learning Outcomes. Mapping accuracy against an independent, Delphi-derived reference standard was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included rubric-based mapping quality, task completion time, error patterns, and faculty perceptions assessed using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The primary comparison used participant-level paired t-tests, with participant-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations used to assess incorrect mapping occurrence. Mapping accuracy was significantly higher with ChatGPT assistance than with manual mapping (78.8% ± 7.9% vs. 74.3% ± 8.2%; mean difference = 4.5% points, 95% CI 2.81–6.19; Cohen’s d_z = 0.56; p < 0.001). A secondary participant-clustered analysis supported this finding, showing lower odds of incorrect mapping (OR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.62–0.98; p = 0.035). ChatGPT-assisted mapping yielded higher rubric-based quality scores (25.67 ± 0.26 vs. 20.96 ± 0.36; p < 0.001) and shorter completion times (14.0 ± 1.5 vs. 27.8 ± 2.9 min; p < 0.001). The participant-clustered analysis found no statistically significant difference in the relative distribution of error types between methods ( p = 0.053). Faculty reported favorable technology acceptance, with all three TAM constructs rated significantly above the neutral midpoint (all p < 0.001). ChatGPT-assisted mapping was associated with significantly higher mapping accuracy, higher rubric-based quality scores, and shorter completion times than manual mapping. However, the fixed-order, non-randomized design precludes attributing these differences exclusively to AI assistance, as practice and familiarity effects may have contributed to the observed results. These findings support further evaluation of LLMs as faculty-supervised decision-support tools for curriculum alignment, particularly through randomized, counterbalanced, multicenter studies.

Article.Title: Influence of solitary and combined foliar spray of iron and zinc on fruit-micronutrient biofortification, functional quality and yield of cherry tomatoes
Article.Authors: Kumar P.; Barupal S.; Kumar M.; Jaajpera T.; Panwar N.; Singh A.; Singh D.; Khapte P.
Article.Abstract: The present study evaluated the effects of supplementary fortnightly foliar applications of iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn), applied individually and in combination (Fe + Zn), on cherry tomatoes. The experiment was conducted under net house conditions in an arid region using a factorial randomized block design with three replications. Responses were assessed in red cherry tomato (cv. Pusa Cherry Tomato 1) and yellow cherry tomato (cv. Pusa Golden Cherry Tomato 2) with respect to micronutrient biofortification, growth, yield, and fruit quality. The combined application of Fe and Zn was the most effective treatment, increasing fruit Fe and Zn concentrations by 4.9- and 1.7-fold, respectively, in red cherry tomato, while approximately twofold increases in micronutrient concentrations were observed in yellow cherry tomato (mg/kg DW basis). Foliar application also improved fruit quality parameters, including titratable acidity, soluble solids content, electrical conductivity, and functional quality traits. Shoot dry mass and fruit yield increased by 9% and 16%, respectively, compared with the control. In addition, Fe and Zn application enhanced the accumulation of other nutrients, including potassium, manganese, and copper, indicating synergistic nutrient interactions. Significant fruit type × spray treatment interactions for fruit and leaf micronutrient concentrations indicated differential responses between red and yellow cherry tomatoes. These findings demonstrate the potential of foliar Fe and Zn application as an agronomic biofortification strategy to improve the nutritional and functional quality of cherry tomatoes, thereby contributing to dietary micronutrient enrichment.

Article.Title: Conspiracist attributes differentiate pro- and anti-vaccine online discourses about data
Article.Authors: Cheng R.; Shaw A.; Hill B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The public frequently and increasingly participates in discussions about vaccines and data on social media. However, such public engagement often includes claims and rumors that misuse data to support anti-vaccine perspectives and lead to negative public health impacts. Often, people expressing anti-vaccine views use the same rhetorical strategies as vaccine advocates to engage with data and evidence. Prior work finds that machine learning systems can distinguish pro- and anti-vaccine content as well as other types of misinformation and conspiracy theories. However, prior classification approaches prioritize predictive performance over human-interpretable features that explain why content differs. We propose a theory-driven approach to distinguish anti-vaccine social media discussions of data by identifying textual characteristics of conspiracy discourses, including mentions of authority figures, expressions of certainty, and causal claims. We conduct statistical analyses to evaluate this approach using a dataset of public Twitter posts containing pro- and anti-vaccine discourse on data about COVID-19 vaccines during the first six months after the beginning of Phase 3 clinical trials. We identify pro- or anti-vaccine Twitter posts using hashtags and keywords. Compared to pro-vaccine data discourses on Twitter, we find that anti-vaccine data discourses are less likely to mention authority figures but more likely to express certainty and make causal claims. The findings can inform ongoing vaccination and public health interventions.

Article.Title: A safety-constrained AI framework for CAR-T design in solid tumors
Article.Authors: Tastan C.; Aydin B.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy has transformed the treatment of hematological malignancies, but its translation to solid tumors remains limited by antigen heterogeneity, poor tumor infiltration, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, and on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we present a safety-constrained artificial intelligence framework for rational CAR-T design in solid tumors. The workflow integrates four linked stages: CD-antigen prioritization, safety-by-design CAR architecture mapping, constrained large language model (LLM)–assisted reasoning, and statistical feature-structure analysis. Curated CD-antigen functional annotations and tumor-associated expression descriptors were encoded into a multi-criteria scoring system that stratified targets into high-confidence, conditional, and unsafe classes. Across the analyzed CD-antigen space, 38% of markers were classified as high-confidence candidates, 34% as conditional targets requiring logic-gated or controllable architectures, and 28% as unsafe targets because of predicted off-tumor risk. External benchmark analysis using MSLN, HER2/ERBB2, EGFR/EGFRvIII, CEA/CEACAM5, GD2, B7-H3/CD276, and CD47 supported the framework’s ability to distinguish direct targets from safety-constrained or unsuitable candidates. An updated four-model LLM benchmark, including GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.5, Grok 4.5, and Claude Sonnet 5, showed convergence toward dual-antigen logic-gated, trafficking-enhanced, and armored CAR designs, while revealing model-dependent differences in safety awareness, traceability, and hallucination risk. Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol showed the strongest safety-oriented performance, whereas Grok 4.5 required greater expert oversight. Correlation and clustering analyses further identified redundant safety-liability features and candidate antigen combinations for logic-gated CAR design. This study provides a reproducible, human-in-the-loop decision-support framework for generating safety-aware CAR-T hypotheses. The framework is computational and hypothesis-generating and does not constitute experimental validation of CAR-T efficacy or safety.

Article.Title: Development and characterization of α-Mangostin-loaded polymeric nanoparticles for intranasal brain delivery: pharmacokinetic evaluation and preliminary in-vitro neuroprotective assessment
Article.Authors: Pardeshi C.; Potdar M.; Shinde P.; Ansari A.; Agrawal Y.; Belgamwar A.; Siddique M.; Hussain A.; Rafiq Z.; Altamimi M.; Khuroo T.
Article.Abstract: α-Mangostin (αM) belongs to a bioactive xanthone derivative, having antioxidant​ and potential neuroprotective properties. However, its therapeutic applications are restricted due to limited aqueous solubility and limited penetration across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) of the brain. The present study aimed to develop αM-loaded polymeric nanoparticles for a intranasal delivery and improved brain availability. αM was initially selected through a multiscale in-silico studies. The optimized αM-PNPs (polylactide-co-glycolide as PLGA nanoparticles) were characterized using the physicochemical, in-vitro , and ex - vivo evaluations, followed by long-term stability studies. I n vivo pharmacokinetics were conducted in rats and a preliminary neuroprotective activity was evaluated in OGD/R-induced BV-2 cells. The in-silico analysis showed a favorable docking score (-9.980 kcal/mol) for αM and formed a stable complex with the PPAR-γ receptor throughout a 200ns MD simulation, supporting its predicted interaction with PPAR-γ. The optimized αM-PNPs exhibited a mean particle size of 232.63 ± 5.03 nm, a zeta potential of -20.9 ± 2.27 mV, an encapsulation efficiency (%EE) of 84.7 ± 3.57%, a drug loading (%DL) of 14.5 ± 1.08%, and a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.191 ± 0.024. The αM-PNPs exhibited a biphasic drug release profile, with approximately 88% cumulative drug release over 12 h. However, based on the reported regression coefficients​, the release profile was best fitted to first-order and Hixson-Crowell models (r² = 0.9976). The steady state permeation flux value ( J ss ) of αM-PNPs (573.98 ± 17.1 µg/h.cm 2 ) was relatively higher than αM-SUS (316.8 ± 10.6 µg/h.cm 2 ), demonstrating an intense modulation of the BBB for improved penetration into the brain. The optimized αM-PNPs demonstrated a satisfactory long-term stability under the controlled storage conditions. αM-PNPs showed enhanced brain drug availability and improved in vitro cytoprotective activity (BV-2) as compared to αM-SUS. Overall, the developed intranasal αM-PNPs represent a promising non-invasive strategy for enhancing nose-to-brain delivery of αM.

Article.Title: Rational design of neuroactive biomolecule functionalized silicon doped graphdiyne for apomorphine delivery: a DFT study

Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s disease requires efficient therapeutic systems with targeted drug delivery applications; however, the absence of drug-loading capability and physiological stability remains a key challenge. Overall, the results suggest that OA-Si-GDY@APO provides a favorable balance between adsorption stability and drug-release accessibility, identifying it as a computationally promising candidate for further experimental investigation.

Article.Title: Comparative cost-effectiveness of HPV mRNA and DNA testing for anal cancer screening in MSM living with HIV: a model-based study
Article.Authors: Diaz M.; Silva-Klug A.; Gómez-Guillén D.; Montoliu A.; Torres M.; Podzamczer D.; Trenti L.; Baixeras N.; de Sanjosé S.; Alemany L.; Paytubi S.; Saumoy M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anal cancer incidence is increasing among men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV, driven by persistent high-risk (HR) HPV infection. HPV mRNA testing may offer higher specificity for detecting high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) than cytology or HPV DNA testing, with potential economic implications. We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of screening strategies combining HPV biomarkers and post-high-resolution anoscopy (HRA) management. A Markov model simulated a cohort of MSM living with HIV to assess 45 screening strategies varying by algorithm (cytology, co-testing, HPV reflex), HPV assay (DNA-hybridization, DNA-PCR, mRNA), and post-HRA management (follow-up, infrared coagulation [IRC], trichloroacetic acid [TCA]). Outcomes included HSIL and anal cancer cases, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), costs, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs). Strategies involving treatment reduced anal cancer incidence by 43–69% compared with no screening, with greater reductions for co-testing. Cytology was the most cost-effective option at €25 per test. At €6, co-testing became competitive, particularly with HR-HPV assays—DNA-hybridization (€13,203/QALY) and mRNA (€14,482/QALY). All optimal strategies included TCA. Anal cancer screening in MSM living with HIV is effective and cost-effective. Co-testing with cytology and HR-HPV assays—whether DNA or mRNA—combined with post-HRA treatment provided the greatest health benefits, while its cost-effectiveness depended strongly on HPV test cost and became favorable at lower HPV test costs. HPV mRNA-based approaches provided a comparable and viable alternative to HPV DNA.

Article.Title: A drift-adaptive learned index with knowledge-graph-enhanced hybrid retrieval improves metadata management for large-scale scientific computing data
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Metadata from large scale scientific computing grows rapidly, and its high dimensional heterogeneity, continuous evolution and domain semantics strain both traditional index structures and keyword based retrieval, which have developed in isolation. This paper proposes MetaSciX, a metadata management and hybrid semantic retrieval framework built on four techniques: a multidimensional learned index that combines adaptive quantile quantization with a z-order curve and absorbs distribution drift by statistically triggered incremental fine-tuning; a knowledge graph enhanced pipeline that encodes domain relations with a graph attention network and fuses sparse, dense and graph signals under query aware weights; consistent hashing with virtual nodes for distributed consistency; and a version aware provenance scheme that folds record versions into the composite key and keeps PROV compatible lineage in the knowledge graph. On real high energy physics and climate metadata, MetaSciX lowers point query latency by at least 30.5% relative to the PGM-Index, uses at most 15.4% of the K-D tree memory, and raises Recall@10 by at least 8.1% over the best single channel retriever and 4.1% over static fusion. On 100 M synthetic records, 8 nodes reach 12,420 queries per second at a scaling efficiency of 0.84, and ablation confirms the contribution of each component.

Article.Title: SECNet: a self-evolving attention network with uncertainty-driven residual refinement for breast ultrasound cancer classification
Article.Authors: Pasha S.; Abed F.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer diagnosis from ultrasound imaging remains a challenging task due to low image contrast, speckle noise, heterogeneous tissue appearance, and significant overlap between benign and malignant lesion characteristics. These factors often lead to diagnostic uncertainty and limit the reliability of conventional deep learning models that rely on static feature representations and fixed attention mechanisms. Improving both classification accuracy and prediction reliability is therefore essential for the development of clinically applicable computer-aided diagnosis systems. In this work, we propose SECNet, a self-evolving cross-domain cancer intelligence network that explicitly addresses diagnostic ambiguity by jointly modeling dynamic attention evolution, uncertainty estimation, and uncertainty-guided residual refinement within a unified end-to-end framework. a unified end-to-end framework. SECNet integrates an Adaptive Attention Evolution Unit that persistently recalibrates both spatial and channel-wise attention throughout training iterations, allowing the model to adapt to varying feature saliency in diverse imaging contexts. Additionally, an uncertainty-driven residual refinement module selectively modifies unstable feature regions based on assessed epistemic uncertainty, thereby enhancing robustness and mitigating overconfident predictions. The suggested technique is assessed using a publicly accessible breast ultrasonography dataset using a stratified and reproducible experimental design. Performance is evaluated by various clinically pertinent parameters, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Cohen’s kappa, Micro-F1 score, AUROC, and AUPRC. SECNet attains an overall classification accuracy of 91.8 ± 0.7%, a Micro-F1 score of 91.4 ± 0.8%, and an average AUROC of 98.5%, achieving the best average performance among the evaluated convolutional, transformer-based, and ensemble benchmarks. Statistical analysis further confirms that the observed performance differences are significant for several baseline comparisons, while SECNet remains statistically comparable with some strong ensemble-based approaches. These results demonstrate that integrating attention evolution with uncertainty-aware residual refinement leads to more reliable and interpretable breast ultrasound cancer classification, highlighting SECNet’s potential for real-world clinical decision support.

Article.Title: An explainable hybrid machine learning framework for predicting rapid chloride permeability in durable concrete
Article.Authors: Kharkan Ghahjavarestani M.; Hanif H.; Ghafourivayghan M.
Article.Abstract: Chloride penetration is a critical factor influencing the durability of reinforced concrete structures because it initiates reinforcement corrosion and significantly shortens service life under aggressive environmental conditions. Although the Rapid Chloride Permeability Test (RCPT) is widely adopted to evaluate concrete resistance against chloride ingress, its experimental implementation is laborious, costly, and time-intensive, making it unsuitable for large-scale investigations. To provide an efficient alternative, this study presents an interpretable hybrid machine-learning framework for accurate prediction of RCPT values in concrete mixtures. A comprehensive dataset containing 483 concrete samples compiled from published literature was used for model development. The predictive capability of the models was enhanced by constructing ratio-based and interaction-derived features, followed by feature optimization using a Supervised Concrete Autoencoder (SCAE) and Variational Transformer-based Feature Selection (VTFS). Four hybrid learning models were subsequently established and comparatively assessed, including LightGBM–SSO, RF–OO, TabNet–MFO, and SAINT–PSO. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM–SSO exhibited the best predictive performance, achieving an R 2 of 0.9631, an RMSE of 46.75, and an MAE of 36.58. To improve model transparency, SHAP analysis was employed to quantify the contribution of individual variables, identifying the fly ash-to-water ratio (F/W) as the dominant factor governing chloride permeability. Residual-based bootstrap analysis provided a descriptive comparison of prediction-error dispersion and interval coverage, without establishing independent predictive calibration. The findings indicate that the developed framework provides an accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient approach for estimating chloride permeability, offering valuable support for durability-based concrete mixture design and reducing reliance on extensive laboratory testing.

Article.Title: Automated measurement of rhythm in stereotyped animal vocalisations
Article.Authors: Jancovich B.; Rogers T.
Article.Abstract: Many non-human animals produce vocal displays with rhythmic stability. For animals that sing or call underwater, measuring inter-call intervals (ICIs), the time between the starts of consecutive song or call emissions, can be complicated. Sound travels greater distances in the ocean than in air, so underwater recordings often simultaneously capture the vocal displays of multiple individuals. To accurately measure each individual’s ICI, it’s necessary to disentangle their interleaved call sequences. Complex ocean propagation conditions complicate matters further by introducing indirect arrivals into recordings; phantom copies of songs that arise from reflection and refraction. ICI estimations in underwater bioacoustics tend to be constrained to conservative manual processes which are time-consuming, offer substantial room for human error, and limit studies to small sample sizes. We developed an automated ICI estimation method that includes multi-caller separation and multi-path suppression. Our method takes the output of an existing automated call detector and constructs single-caller sequences using TDOA (time difference of arrival) bearing estimation, phase dispersion minimisation, and directed-acyclic longest path optimisation. This pipeline then feeds each single-caller sequence to our ICI estimation algorithm that uses epoch folding and the harmonic $${Z}_{2}^{2}$$ statistic to measure periodicity. We demonstrate the method on a 25-year dataset of audio recordings of the Chagos pygmy blue whale song and show that this population’s ICI is decreasing over time, while individual animals have strong rhythmic consistency within each calling bout. Our new method allows more robust estimation of ICI, with mechanisms for quantifying typical individual rhythmic consistency, and the degree of a population’s ICI stereotypy, facilitating the broader study of long-term change in baleen whale song and other stereotyped animal vocal displays.

The synthesized material was characterized using FTIR, 1 H NMR, DSC, SEM–EDS, XPS, TEM and TGA–DTG. Fortification recovery mean values were 88.6–103.0% at the examined levels (n = 3 per level), and recovery mean value remained 91.0% after five reuse cycles. Application was examined in ten market vegetable extracts. These results data support AuPLA–Lip as a reusable extraction platform for the selected panel; sample-based reporting limits and quantitative residue conclusions require complete whole-method validation.

Article.Title: Evaluation of heavy metal contamination and carcinogenic risks in the tropical catchment: evidence from the Kok River Basin, Thailand
Article.Authors: Kaewlom P.; Udomkun P.; Pripdeevech P.; Khruengsai S.; Sripahco T.; Fakkaew K.; Tipmanee D.; Haemanwichian D.; kanchanaratchataphong W.; Wannapaiboon S.; Thumanu K.; Sirimongkonlertkun N.; Aekakkararungroj A.; Kunpradid T.; Pongpiachan S.
Article.Abstract: Heavy metal (HM) contamination in tropical river systems poses increasing risks to ecosystems and human health, yet integrated assessments of water, sediments, and associated risks remain limited. This study evaluated HM contamination in the Kok River Basin, Thailand, using physicochemical characterization, multi-index analysis, and human health risk assessment. Water quality showed low biochemical oxygen demand (BOD: 0.6–2.3 mg/L), favorable dissolved oxygen (DO: 6.8–7.0 mg/L), and slightly alkaline pH (8.0–9.0). However, turbidity was extremely high (397–1006 NTU), exceeding Thai standards (> 25 NTU) by more than 20-fold. Dissolved metals exhibited clear spatial gradients, with cadmium (Cd), nickel (Ni), copper (Cu), uranium (U), and chromium (Cr) decreasing downstream by 20–50%, while iron (Fe) increased by ~ 10%. Sediments showed substantially higher contamination, particularly for arsenic (As) (contamination factor, CF: 17.5–20.2), lead (Pb) (CF: 2.8–3.2), and uranium (U) (CF: 5.2–6.5), with greater accumulation in the central channel than riverbanks. Water-based indices, including the metal index (MI < 1), water quality index (WQI: 19.7–26.2), and heavy metal pollution index (HPI: 75.1–86.5), indicated generally acceptable conditions. In contrast, indices incorporating cumulative and sediment-associated contamination, such as the heavy metal evaluation index (HEI: 73.2–88.7) and potential ecological risk index (PERI), revealed moderate to high contamination, particularly upstream. This difference reflects the distinct environmental compartments assessed, where water-based indices capture short-term dissolved conditions, whereas sediment-based indices indicate cumulative contamination and long-term ecological risk. Non-carcinogenic risks from water ingestion were negligible (hazard index, HI < 1), whereas sediment exposure posed potential health risks, particularly for children. Carcinogenic risks (incremental lifetime cancer risk, ILCR) were within or slightly above the acceptable range (10⁻ 6 –10⁻ 4 ), with children showing higher exposure levels. Overall, although water quality appears acceptable based on conventional indices, sediment-associated contamination represents a significant and underrecognized risk. These findings highlight the need for integrated water–sediment monitoring and targeted management of pollution sources and depositional hotspots to protect environmental and public health in tropical river systems.

Article.Title: Sex-specific age prioritization of epidemic interventions under alternative equality objectives: a case study of COVID-19
Article.Authors: Zsichla L.; Müller V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resource scarcity necessitates prioritization during epidemics, and equity is often used as a main guiding principle. However, alternative operational definitions of equity may yield different priorities. We developed a framework to investigate how equality objectives translate age- and sex-specific COVID-19 infection fatality ratio (IFR) estimates into prioritization strategies. IFR estimates were combined with demographic data from the UK to derive sex-specific age thresholds under Individual Risk Equality, Benefit Equality, Mortality Equality, and Life-year Equality. Male IFR at a given age approximated female IFR 7 years older. The four objectives produced different age thresholds, with differences ranging from a few years to several decades. In addition, we evaluated these objectives in a counterfactual reconstruction of the UK vaccination campaign, incorporating detailed empirical data but varying prioritization. In the reconstruction, prioritization based on Benefit, Mortality, and Life-year Equality yielded vaccination age thresholds that were 3.49/3.12, 4.92/3.75, and 6.62/4.47 years lower for males compared with females for first/second doses. Relative to sex-neutral allocation, total deaths changed by − 0.20%, + 0.48%, and + 2.61%, respectively, despite reductions in male mortality. These findings demonstrate that allocation outcomes depend on operational definition of equity and that achieving parity does not necessarily minimize total mortality.

Article.Title: Mitigation of DC-link ripples in smart converters under asymmetric grid conditions via stationary-frame dual-vector control
Article.Authors: Tlili F.; Slimene M.; Khlifi M.; Bacha F.
Article.Abstract: Asymmetric grid faults induce second-order harmonics in the DC-link voltage of three-phase AC/DC converters, leading to increased capacitor stress, reduced power quality, and compromised system stability. While sequence-decomposition-based control strategies effectively mitigate these effects, their practical adoption is often hindered by the computational overhead of synchronous reference frame transformations. Here, we propose and validate a Dual-Vector Current Control (DVCC) scheme operating primarily in the stationary reference frame for current regulation and reference generation, while employing minimal rotational transformations for sequence extraction. The control architecture employs a parallel arrangement of resonant filters to extract positive- and negative-sequence components, coupled with a notch-filter-based harmonic isolation stage to eliminate 100 Hz ripple without compromising transient response. Through analytical modeling and time-domain simulations under balanced and severely unbalanced grid conditions (voltage sag down to 0.85 p.u.), we demonstrate that under grid voltage sags down to 0.85 p.u., the proposed controller achieves a 92% reduction in DC-link voltage ripple compared to conventional PI control, and maintains input current total harmonic distortion below 7% under moderate unbalanced conditions (15% voltage sag) and below 3% under balanced conditions. Under severe single-phase loss (100% sag), THD increases to 37%, highlighting current limitations and the need for derating strategies. The bidirectional power transfer capability is preserved during fault transients, with settling times under 50 ms. These findings establish DVCC as a computationally efficient and robust alternative for grid-interfaced converters in distributed generation, electric vehicle charging, and microgrid applications, offering a practical pathway to enhanced grid resilience with minimal hardware modifications.

Article.Title: A multi-rotor UAV classification and recognition method based on RCSB-Net
Article.Authors: Peng S.; Xing J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the issue of low accuracy in target classification and recognition caused by the difficulty in extracting micro-Doppler time-frequency features from multi-rotor UAVs in complex low-altitude environments with strong clutter, this paper proposes a high-precision classification and recognition framework for multi-rotor UAVs, termed the RSPWVD, CBAM, Swin Transformer, and BiFPN based Network (RCSB-Net), which integrates RSPWVD-based time-frequency representation, CBAM-enhanced Swin Transformer feature extraction, and BiFPN-inspired bidirectional multi-scale feature fusion. This algorithm employs the Reassigned Smoothed Pseudo-Wigner–Ville Distribution (RSPWVD) to perform time-frequency processing on radar echo signals. Through an energy center-of-gravity reassignment mechanism, it suppresses cross-term interference and enhances time-frequency concentration, thereby preserving fine-grained micro-Doppler characteristics of the multi-rotor UAVs; Based on the Swin Transformer backbone network, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is embedded to enable the extraction of micro-Doppler features from targets in both the channel and spatial dimensions; a BiFPN-inspired bidirectional multi-scale feature fusion module is adopted to facilitate complementary interaction between shallow detailed features and deep semantic features ; A global feature aggregation and classification head is designed to predict target categories by combining multiscale features, thereby completing the classification of multi-rotor UAVs; Testing was conducted using the LSS-FMCWR-1.0 dataset. Experimental results show that RCSB-Net achieves a classification accuracy of 99.5%, a recall of 98.6%, and an F1-score of 91.3%. Compared with ResNet-50, the classification accuracy is improved by 6.1% points, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for multi-rotor UAV classification.

Article.Title: Multiple wearable digital biomarkers for AI-based diagnosis of major depressive disorder defined by self-reported and clinician-rated scales
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Kang S.; Lee S.; Kim K.
Article.Abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is traditionally assessed using clinician-rated and self-reported scales. However, repeated assessments are challenging, and discrepancies between these scales may limit their suitability as ground truth for wearable-based diagnosis. This study developed machine learning models using wearable-derived digital biomarkers to diagnose the presence and severity of MDD, comparing the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) as ground-truth labels. A total of 111 patients with depression and 50 healthy controls were recruited. Sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), and physical activity data were collected over 6 weeks using a wrist-worn device. The BDI was assessed at weeks 0, 2, 4, and 6, while HAMD was assessed at weeks 0 and 6. Logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting models were developed for binary and multiclass classification and evaluated using participant-level nested cross-validation. The HAMD-based model achieved peak area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.84 for diagnosis and 0.72 (macro-averaged) for severity classification, outperforming the BDI-based model (AUCs: 0.71 and 0.64); the advantage of HAMD persisted when both scales were compared on identical participants and time points (weeks 0 and 6). Key features in the HAMD-based models included low-frequency power, entropy, root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep latency, deep sleep duration, total active minutes, and weekday distance. While RMSSD, entropy, deep sleep duration, and activity were negatively associated with the predicted probability of depression, REM sleep latency showed a positive association. Wearable-derived multimodal biomarkers are effective for MDD diagnosis, and the clinician-rated HAMD may provide a more suitable ground truth than the BDI. This approach supports continuous monitoring and early detection in digital mental health management.

Article.Title: Interaction mechanism of tunnel excavation and overlying building loads in shallow-buried coastal urban tunnels
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Guo Z.; Kong F.
Article.Abstract: Shallow coastal tunnels excavated beneath buildings can deform under the combined effects of excavation, groundwater and structural loading, but their coupled response remains unclear. We investigated the onshore section of the Second Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Subsea Tunnel using a hydro-mechanical physical model, finite-element simulations and field monitoring. The model test and simulations identified upper-bench excavation of the right pilot tunnel beneath the building as a stage of pronounced deformation. Field settlement profiles showed a similar overall pattern, although peak magnitudes and locations differed; they could not establish the timing of the peak response. In the zero-offset, 0°numerical configuration, seepage increased maximum crown displacement from 22.7 to 28.9 mm (27.3%) relative to the no-seepage reference. Building loading deepened and narrowed the settlement trough, while building offset shifted the trough and altered differential settlement. At zero offset, increasing crossing angle raised peak ground-surface settlement and narrowed the trough. These findings identify excavation stage, groundwater and tunnel-building geometry as joint controls on deformation in this case and inform monitoring of comparable coastal tunnels.

Article.Title: In silico screening of FDA-approved drugs for elimination of senescent cells via senescence-associated anti-apoptotic pathway inhibition
Article.Authors: Manni E.
Article.Abstract: Senescent cells activate senescence-associated anti-apoptotic pathways to evade apoptosis, leading to irreversible cell cycle arrest. Here, an in silico screening strategy was used to identify FDA-approved drugs that cause senescent cells to lose their ability to evade apoptotic pathways by targeting senescence-associated anti-apoptotic pathway (SCAP)-related genes. Absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) parameters (reduced to 80), StopTox filtering (reduced to 15), and ProTox 3.0 classification were used to screen over 1500 chemicals obtained from the ZINC database. Three compounds, ZINC000000057255, ZINC000096006009, and ZINC000001530803, were selected for further examination based on their favorable LD 50 values. ZINC000001530803 was predicted to be non-toxic across the computational toxicity endpoints evaluated in this study. Twelve overlapping candidate targets were identified by intersecting PharmMapper-predicted compound targets with GeneCards-derived SCAP-related genes. For protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, these 12 overlapping targets were combined with BCL2, MCL1, and BCL2L1 as anti-apoptotic pathway anchors, resulting in a 15-node network in which EGFR and AKT1 emerged as key hub genes. ZINC000000057255 had the best docking score and electronic stability but it was predicted to be toxic to the eye. ZINC000001530803 demonstrated a favorable predicted ADMET profile and established robust hydrogen-bond interactions with significant residues of EGFR and AKT1. Overall, ZINC000001530803 shows promise as a lead candidate for SCAP inhibition and warrants further refinement and experimental verification.

Article.Title: Meaning-making amid existential uncertainty: a hermeneutic phenomenological study of parents of children with trisomy 18
Article.Authors: Minami K.; Tanaka K.; Ota Y.; Nagata K.; Takeuchi M.
Article.Abstract: Advances in medical care have transformed the management of trisomy 18 while posing increasingly complex ethical and psychosocial challenges for parents. This study aimed to explore and interpret the lived experiences of parents of children with trisomy 18. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 25 parents of children with trisomy 18. Data were analyzed using a hermeneutic phenomenological approach based on van Manen’s “Phenomenology of Practice.” Three themes emerged: (1) Existential uncertainty about the child’s future, (2) Ambivalence between social isolation and recognition of the child, and (3) Living a meaningful life through the child’s enduring presence. Although parents experienced profound existential distress, interactions with their children enabled them to reexamine the values that mattered most and reconstruct their identities. These findings suggest that parents’ experiences cannot be understood solely in terms of suffering. Meaningful parent–child interactions fostered ongoing meaning-making that was not constrained by the child’s lifespan and continued beyond the child’s death, providing new insights for family-centered care.

Article.Title: Theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling reveals differential neural correlates of error processing and symptom severity in generalized anxiety disorder
Article.Authors: Camenzind M.; Korsapathy S.; Guirguis V.; Li W.; Carlton C.; Pupillo F.; Park J.; Schwippel T.; Townsend L.; Stewart Z.; Ali S.; Feldman Z.; Meltzer-Brody S.; Frohlich F.

Spatially distinct PAC–symptom clusters emerged (p cluster < 0.035). PAC between the right prefrontal seed and parieto-occipital sensors, topographically consistent with frontoparietal cognitive control networks, tracked autonomic hyperarousal symptoms. However, descriptive post-hoc decompositions revealed distinct statistical drivers: “Somatic Sensory” symptoms were linked to elevated coupling exclusively during correct trials. In contrast, “Insomnia” and “Unable to Relax” were characterized by opposite-direction effects, with increased PAC during correct trials and a decrease during errors. Conversely, a frontocentral cluster linked to “Fear of Dying” showed the reverse pattern, with PAC increasing specifically during errors. These effects were observed using the right prefrontal seed during the post-response window; exploratory control analyses using left/middle PFC seeds or a pre-response window did not yield significant symptom-cluster associations. Results suggest anxiety symptom severity within this population involves specific, state-dependent differences in oscillatory coupling. Rather than a singular mechanism, these symptom-associated coupling patterns offer exploratory insights into how early error-processing dynamics vary with individual anxiety profiles.

Article.Authors: Kim D.; Kang H.
Article.Abstract: Cross-dataset generalization remains difficult in deepfake detection, and the placement of parameter-efficient adaptation within pretrained vision models remains insufficiently controlled. A common-rank contrast showed that Attn-Out used 49.9% fewer trainable parameters than Attn-Q/V at \(r=16\) , while its source-validation frame-level AUC was lower by 0.000659. Models were trained on FaceForensics++ C23, and configurations were frozen using source validation before evaluation on six reporting-only external datasets. In the exact-budget comparison, Attn-Q/V achieved the highest observed mean Macro-6 AUC ( \(0.9432\,\pm\,0.0010\) ), whereas Attn-Out led numerically on three targets and required less measured training memory and model-compute time. All family-balanced crossed-bootstrap intervals included zero, so the AUC ordering is descriptive. Explicit merging removed placement-specific low-rank operations, and inference measurements did not support a deployment-speed ranking. Together, these comparisons separate adapter size and training-resource requirements from merged inference behavior.

Positive attitude (β = 0.310), negative attitude (β = −0.215), and the post-truth index (β = 0.425) had significant conditional associations. Negative attitude had an essentially null zero-order association ( r = .021). The post-truth index uniquely accounted for 13.4% points beyond the other measured predictors. Exploratory structure analyses supported a dominant common dimension but also revealed residual item clustering; content-domain sensitivity analyses localized the association mainly to devaluation of factual truth. These self-report associations do not establish causality, objective misinformation susceptibility, or a validated unitary post-truth disposition.

Article.Title: Noninvasive methods for laboratory animal health assessment during tick-borne encephalitis
Article.Authors: Alzheeva А.; Belov A.; Rogova A.; Andrianova A.; Romanova L.; Gadzhikurbanov M.; Averyanova А.; Karganova G.
Article.Abstract: Noninvasive methods for monitoring laboratory animal health are essential for improving welfare and enhancing the reliability of scientific data. This study evaluated two approaches—daily body weight measurement with mathematical analysis of weight dynamics, and urine qPCR—for monitoring young BALB/c mice infected with tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV). In the initial BALB/c cohort, a diagnostic threshold of − 0.6 (derived from control animals as mean − 2 × SD) showed high discriminatory performance. However, when the method was tested on independent cohorts of C57BL/6, CBA, and aged BALB/c mice, the absolute threshold values were found to be strain- and sex-dependent, underscoring the need for context-specific calibration. Urine qPCR detected viral RNA at the group level as early as day 2 post-infection, peaking on day 7, supporting its feasibility for cohort-level monitoring. These noninvasive approaches, combined with mathematical analysis of body weight, provide an objective and refinement-oriented tool for health assessment in virology research, contributing to the 3R principles.
