The dataset comprises 765 physical holes from 85 plates, partitioned at plate level into mutually exclusive training, validation and test sets in a 6:2:2 ratio. Model and parameter selection use the training and validation partitions. Joint success requires valid dual profiles and all four center and radius errors relative to separately annotated visual references to be strictly below 5.0 pixels. Held-out test success is 78.43% overall, including 88.89% for clean and 66.67% for contaminated surfaces. Controlled refinement comparisons distinguish balancing from confidence weighting. Paired errors and threshold responses reveal parameter-specific trade-offs. Article.Authors: Ferede M.; Terefe A.; Mwema M.; Philipo M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adoption of climate-smart agricultural (CSA) practices has been widely recognized as a promising and effective approach to minimize the adverse impacts of climate change. However, their adoption among smallholder farmers remains low in developing countries, including Tanzania. This study examined the impact of climate-smart maize production on the nutritional security of smallholder households and the determinants in the Arumeru District, Tanzania. The study employed a two-stage multinomial endogenous switching regression model. The results revealed that farmers’ adoption of CSA practice combinations was significantly influenced by the education of the household head, land size, frequency of extension contact, cooperative membership, access to credit, and CSA training. The study also found that adoption of the comprehensive package comprising improved seed, integrated soil fertility management, and small-scale irrigation (I 1 E 1 S 1 ) was associated with the largest gains, with average treatment effects on the treated of 3.975 for the Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS) and 16.782 for the Household Food Consumption Score (FCS); adopters’ mean HDDS and FCS were 6.638 and 45.397, respectively. In conclusion, the findings indicate that the largest estimated nutrition security gains among smallholder farmers are associated with adopting a comprehensive package encompassing all three practice categories, although the cross-sectional design warrants caution in causal interpretation. Thus, the study highlighted that district government, farming entities and local authorities should establish phased CSA support initiatives, encourage the leasing of irrigation equipment, and that rural development banks and credit institutions should provide funds to farmers at affordable rates.

Article.Title: Listening with others: fostering empathy and relationships with nature through immersive soundscape experiences
Article.Authors: Carruthers-Jones J.; Eriksson M.; Giusti M.; Kondakova M.; Raymond C.
Article.Abstract: Empathy and nature connectedness provide a key motivational basis for positive conservation behaviour, yet dominant framings treat ‘nature’ as a generalised, abstract category rather than attending to relationships with specific species. Multispecies thinking offers a more relational alternative, but how it might be cultivated in practice remains underexplored. We examine whether immersive listening via an urban soundwalk and an immersive dome theatre can foster (1) human-nature relationships, (2) empathy towards nature, and (3) the perceived importance of sound to humans and other species, and whether the importance of sound mediates these effects. Using a pre-/post-treatment survey with 116 high-school students from Tampere Finland (aged 16–18), the soundwalk guided participants on a perspective-taking exercise centred on listening to another species, while the dome presented diverse local urban and natural soundscapes from across Finland. Participants showed strengthened human-nature relationships and increased empathy towards nature and the perceived importance of sound; however, the importance of sound did not significantly mediate these relationships. These findings suggest that immersive listening can shift participants’ relationship with nature and move their evaluation of why sound matters away from an anthropocentric framing towards a more relational, multispecies understanding of their acoustic environment.

Article.Title: A Caputo fractional tuberculosis model with saturated incidence: stability analysis, optimal control, and machine learning forecasting
Article.Authors: Alyobi S.; Shafee A.; Zahir A.
Article.Abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is still the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, and high-burden settings need models that are biologically faithful, analytically tractable, and usable for forecasting and intervention planning. Most fractional-order TB studies address only one of these aspects. We formulate a Caputo fractional-order TB model with vaccination, a saturated (Holling type-II) incidence that combines person-to-person and environmental transmission, and an explicit isolation compartment. Every transition follows the natural history of TB: latently infected individuals can only progress to active disease or die; isolated individuals are active cases who either start treatment, leave isolation untreated, or die; and recovery occurs only through treatment completion or documented spontaneous self-cure, with relapse. We prove positivity and boundedness, derive the reproduction number \({\mathcal {R}}_0\) in closed form with the next-generation method, verify the Matignon stability condition with computed Jacobian eigenvalues, and prove global stability of the disease-free equilibrium with an explicitly constructed linear Lyapunov function. We also prove well-posedness of the Caputo system and the existence of an endemic equilibrium when \({\mathcal {R}}_0>1\) , and we give an explicit condition for the bifurcation at \({\mathcal {R}}_0=1\) to be forward. We then pose an optimal-control problem with four controls (awareness, vaccination, active case finding with isolation, and environmental decontamination), derive the exact adjoint system and control characterisations from Pontryagin’s maximum principle, and couple the mechanistic model with a NARX neural network trained by the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. For a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa-scale parameterisation ( \({\mathcal {R}}_0\approx 3.79\) ), \({\mathcal {R}}_0\) is most sensitive to the transmission rate, the progression rate from latency and the treatment-initiation rate. Isolation at rate \(q=0.2\) \(\hbox {year}^{-1}\) lowers \({\mathcal {R}}_0\) from 4.72 to 3.79 and almost halves the active TB burden after 70 years. Memory effects ( \(\alpha <1\) ) markedly slow the epidemic. Combining all four controls minimises the objective functional and reduces active TB at 50 years by about \(92\%\) ; omitting awareness is the most costly omission. The NARX surrogate achieves 1.4– \(2.3\%\) one-step-ahead error on noisy synthetic data, whereas fully recursive multi-step forecasts drift by \(12\%\) on average over a 10-year horizon. A biologically consistent model structure, rigorous threshold results and a clearly delimited data-driven layer together give a transparent tool for TB control planning. The results identify early case detection, treatment initiation and contact reduction as the most effective levers.

Article.Title: Genome-wide characterization of the integrin gene family reveals environment-associated expression patterns of the laminin–integrin axis in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
Article.Authors: Zoghly H.; El-dine B.; Khaled M.; Rashed M.; Elian S.; Grana Y.; Nofal A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Integrins are essential transmembrane receptors that help cells interact with the extracellular matrix (ECM) and coordinate various signaling pathways. While well-studied in model organisms, how the integrin family is organized and expressed in Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) under different environmental conditions is not yet fully clear. To address this gap, we conducted a genome-wide characterization of the tilapia integrin gene family and evaluated the expression of key laminin–integrin axis members, including four integrin beta subunit genes ( On_ITGB1a , On_ITGB3b , On_ITGB4 , and On_ITGB6 ) and laminin beta 2 ( On_lamb2 ), normalized to elongation factor 1a ( On_ef-1a ) across three ecologically distinct Egyptian habitats: the relatively pristine Rosetta branch of the Nile River, the moderately impacted Edfina Barrage, and the heavily polluted Burullus Lake. We identified 46 integrin genes ( α and β ) displaying conserved structural domain architectures, signatures of purifying selection (Ka/Ks < 1), and evidence of teleost-specific gene duplications. Water quality variations across anthropogenically stressed aquatic habitats directly matched tissue-specific transcriptional shifts. In brain tissue, all tested genes exhibited a clear spatial gradient: expression was at baseline levels in the Rosetta branch (reference site), intermediate in Edfina Barrage, and highest in Burullus Lake. Conversely, hepatic expression showed moderate, non-significant variations across all locations. These findings demonstrate that the laminin–integrin profile exhibits site-specific transcriptional plasticity across wild environments, suggesting the potential of selected laminin–integrin components as molecular indicators of environmental stress in Nile tilapia.

Article.Title: Pharmacological evaluation of tannic acid–based chelation therapy in ferric citrate–supplemented rats
Article.Authors: Kittilukkana A.; Intakhad J.; Pilapong C.
Article.Abstract: Tannic acid is recognised as a natural iron chelator; however, its in vivo applicability may be constrained by non-specific interactions with amino- and thiol-containing biomolecules, potentially altering its bioavailability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. In the present study, several formulations of tannic acid (TA)–based chelators, including unmodified TA, oxidised TA (TAox), phenylalanine-combined TA (TAphe), lysine-combined TA (TAlys), or cysteine-combined TA (TAcys), were synthesized and evaluated for chelation therapy in ferric citrate–supplemented rats. Animals fed a ferric citrate–enriched diet for eight weeks, followed by an eight-week chelation regimen with distinct TA-based formulations, exhibited chelator-dependent alterations in hepatic iron accumulation and liver enzyme activity, without significant changes in reactive oxygen species (ROS) production or lipid peroxidation. Notably, TAlys exhibited the greatest reduction in hepatic iron, while TAcys exhibited the greatest attenuation of serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activities. In plasma, selected chelation treatments, particularly TAphe, reduced plasma ROS levels without affecting systemic iron accumulation. In contrast, none of the TA-based chelation treatments produced statistically significant changes in brain iron levels or oxidative stress markers, although some trends in specific behavioral performance were observed. Collectively, these findings indicate that TA-based chelation therapy predominantly modulates iron homeostasis and function. Specific TA-based formulations may therefore represent promising candidates for further pharmacological development in targeted iron chelation and related therapeutic or nutraceutical applications.

Article.Title: Deep-water choruses originate from slope-associated biological aggregations
Article.Authors: Duane D.; Caspers P.; Freeman L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evening biological chorusing of unknown origin has been reported near pelagic waters around the world, including the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. While vertically migrating deep scattering layers have been suggested as a possible source of the chorus, this is difficult to confirm without measurements of the spatial distribution of the bioacoustic sources. Here we deployed a directional acoustic sensing system to localize the chorus using multipath backpropagation in deep water near Bermuda, and the sources were found to be emanating from the 800-900 m depth contour along the slope edge of the Bermuda Rise. Two simultaneously active aggregations were tracked over the chorusing interval with no evidence of vertical migration. Directional isolation of individual sounds within the chorus enabled estimation of source level and call-rate density, with measured source levels within the range reported for fish sounds. These findings rule out a vertically migrating open-ocean scattering layer as the source of the chorus observed here, and instead suggest a slope-associated origin within the lower mesopelagic zone, potentially involving aggregations of larger demersal fish. Although the taxonomic identity of the vocalizing fauna remains unresolved, these results substantially narrow the range of candidate taxa and demonstrate the value of passive acoustic sensing for localizing and tracking soniferous biological aggregations in the deep ocean.

Article.Title: Milk and milk substitute consumption and hepatocellular carcinoma risk: the mediating role of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
Article.Authors: Akhtar S.; Almohaid S.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for approximately 75% of primary liver cancers. Evidence on HCC risk factors in Middle Eastern countries, including Kuwait, remains limited. We previously reported that heavy alcohol consumption, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and high consumption of milk and milk substitute were significant risk factors for HCC. This study examined the mediating role of MASLD in the association between milk and milk substitute consumption and HCC risk. Fifty-three histopathologically confirmed HCC cases were identified from the Kuwait Cancer Control Center Registry, and 196 controls (1:4 ratio) were recruited from medical and surgical outpatient clinics at six public hospitals. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a standardized questionnaire. Causal mediation analysis within the counterfactual framework was conducted to estimate the marginal total effect (MTE), natural direct effect (NDE), and natural indirect effect (NIE) of milk and milk substitute consumption on HCC risk mediated through MASLD. Effects were reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A higher proportion of HCC cases were aged ≥ 60 years compared with controls (79.2% vs. 45.9%). The milk and milk substitute consumption showed significant MTE (OR MTE = 5.97; 95% CI 1.69, 21.12; p = 0.006), and NDE (OR NDE = 4.45; 95% CI 1.27, 15.53; p = 0.019) on HCC risk. In addition, a significant NIE mediated through MASLD was observed (OR NIE = 1.34; 95% CI 1.14, 1.57; p < 0.001). Based on the OR scale, the proportion of MTE mediated (PM) through MASLD was 16.4% (PM = 16.4%; 95% CI 14.1%, 35.4%; p = 0.049), suggesting that this proportion of the effect could potentially be prevented through interventions targeting MASLD. Dietary modification, alongside systematic screening and management of MASLD, may help reduce HCC risk. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the relatively small E-value and its lower bound for the NIE suggest that an unmeasured confounder could potentially explain the observed NIE. Prospective studies are therefore warranted to confirm these findings .

Article.Title: Daily links between rumination and physical activity in major depression and borderline personality disorder
Article.Authors: Balder T.; Schulze L.; Wilbertz G.; Bohländer J.; Renneberg B.; Zetsche U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Response Styles Theory proposes that rumination interferes with behavioral engagement, yet few studies have simultaneously tracked objectively measured physical activity and momentary rumination in daily life. We combined seven days of ecological momentary assessment (eight prompts/day assessing rumination frequency) with continuous hip-mounted accelerometry in female participants with major depressive disorder (MDD; n = 43), borderline personality disorder without comorbid MDD (BPD; n = 46), and healthy controls ( n = 43). Bayesian multilevel models with person-mean centering examined group differences and prompt-to-prompt cross-lagged associations. Both clinical groups reported higher momentary rumination than controls, and participants with MDD, but not BPD displayed lower physical activity and higher sedentary time. Cross-lagged analyses did not identify a consistent pattern of associations between rumination and subsequent activity, or in the reverse direction. Two small BPD associations in the primary models were not consistent across all sensitivity analyses, and no clear differences in lagged associations were detected between diagnostic groups. Everyday hypoactivity appears specific to MDD rather than a general feature of psychopathology. We discuss possible reasons why lagged associations were not detected, including the measurement of rumination and physical activity and the temporal resolution of the design.

Article.Title: Adaptive memory-augmented Artificial Protozoa Optimization with competitive operator control for complex numerical and constrained problems
Article.Authors: Elsabagh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable optimization of complex numerical and constrained problems requires algorithms that can exploit accumulated search experience without sacrificing population diversity. This paper proposes MAO-APO-RC, an enhanced Artificial Protozoa Optimizer that couples memory-augmented learning with adaptive competitive control. The method combines historical-solution guidance, quasi-oppositional sampling, Lévy-flight exploration, stagnation-triggered rescue, success-history parameter adaptation, and feedback-based operator scoring within a unified multi-candidate search framework. At every iteration, alternative candidates are produced by complementary operators, evaluated under a common selection rule, and reinforced according to their recent contribution, enabling dynamic regulation of exploration and exploitation. The performance was assessed in 30 independent runs on 15 benchmark functions including shifted, rotated, ill-conditioned, multimodal, hybrid and composition landscapes in 30 and 50 dimensions, and four constrained engineering design problems. The comparisons were made to APO, PSO, DE, GWO, WOA, SCA, CMAES-lite, and SHADE-lite. MAO-APO-RC achieved the best overall Friedman mean rank of 2.3667 on the numerical benchmark suite. Six of the eight competing algorithms were statistically significantly different with Wilcoxon–Holm analysis, whereas APO and SHADE-lite were statistically comparable. For the engineering problems, MAO-APO-RC obtained a joint-best mean rank of 1.875 with DE. Ablation analysis revealed the APO + QOD as the best reduced configuration with a mean rank of 1.8500 compared to 1.9167 for MAO-APO-RC whereas the complete framework significantly outperformed the Memory and Energy variants. Despite measurable constant-factor runtime overhead, MAO-APO-RC preserves APO’s asymptotic time and space complexity. These findings demonstrate that MAO-APO-RC provides competitive aggregate performance across the evaluated numerical and engineering problems, while its statistical advantage remains competitor- and problem-dependent.

Article.Title: The regulatory effects of astaxanthin on immune function and gut microbiota in a fatigue model of rats
Article.Authors: Bai R.; Wang J.; Wu L.
Article.Abstract: Exhaustive exercise (EE) may impair immune function and alter gut microbiota composition. We investigated the effects of astaxanthin (ASTA) supplementation on immune parameters and gut microbiota in rats subjected to EE. Thirty male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control (C), EE (E), and EE plus ASTA (EM) groups (n = 10 per group). Rats in the EM group received ASTA (25 mg/kg) by oral gavage daily for 28 days. Serum immunoglobulins and cytokines, splenic histology, and cecal microbiota were assessed using ELISA, histological examination, and 16S rRNA gene sequencing, respectively. Compared with the E group, the EM group showed significantly higher serum IgG and IgM levels and IFN-γ/IL-4 ratios, lower IL-4 levels, and less pronounced splenic histopathological alterations. The relative abundances of Verrucomicrobiota, Actinobacteriota, and Akkermansia were also significantly higher in the EM group. PICRUSt2 analysis indicated differences in predicted microbial functional categories between the E and EM groups. Spearman correlation analysis revealed a positive association between Akkermansia abundance and the IFN-γ/IL-4 ratio ( r = 0.555, P = 0.011). Overall, ASTA supplementation was associated with improvements in immune parameters and beneficial changes in gut microbiota composition following EE. Further studies are needed to establish whether these changes are causally related.

Article.Title: Acute stress is associated with rapid sex-dependent epigenetic changes in the human intestinal mucosa
Article.Authors: Rodiño-Janeiro B.; Martinez C.; Pigrau M.; Rodriguez-Casanova A.; Costa-Fraga N.; Jacome Pumar M.; Salvo-Romero E.; Nieto A.; Exposito-Fernandez E.; Fortea M.; Camacho C.; Albert-Bayo M.; Gonzalez-Castro A.; Guagnozzi D.; Lobo-Alvarez B.; Niesler B.; Vicario M.; Diaz-Lagares A.; Santos J.; Alonso-Cotoner C.
Article.Abstract: The intestinal barrier is essential for gut homeostasis, regulating immune responses, digestion, and nutrient absorption. Psychological and physical stress can rapidly alter barrier function, showing marked sexual dimorphism. Although epigenetic mechanisms are proposed to mediate these changes, it remains unclear whether acute stress is associated with changes in the human intestinal epigenome in vivo . We aimed to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation and microRNA (miRNA) changes in the human jejunal mucosa following acute stress and to assess sex-specific effects. DNA methylation and miRNA expression were analyzed in intestinal mucosa from healthy subjects at baseline and after 15 min of cold pain stress (CPS). DNA methylation (850,000 CpGs) was assessed using the Infinium MethylationEPIC array (Illumina), and 25 IBS-related miRNAs were quantified using an nCounter miR a-la-carte codeset. Comparison of biopsies obtained before and after CPS identified 4,116 differentially methylated CpGs. Sex-stratified analysis increased this number to 94,075, highlighting a marked sex-dependent epigenetic response. Enriched pathways included cell adhesion, cytoskeletal organization, neurodevelopment, cytokine signaling, and MAPK/Wnt pathways. CPS was also associated with reduced expression of miR-125b-5p and miR-145-5p. Acute stress is associated with rapid, sex-dependent epigenetic changes in the human intestinal mucosa, providing evidence for a potential role of epigenetic regulation in stress-associated intestinal barrier dysfunction, and disease vulnerability.

Article.Title: A novel common-ground single-input 7-level grid-tied inverter with lower number of switches
Article.Authors: Hosseini S.; Ghassemzadeh S.; Sharifian M.; Babaei E.
Article.Abstract: In this study, a novel common-ground single-input 7-level grid-tied inverter with a lower number of switches is proposed. The new design, by maintaining a common ground between the input and the grid, helps reduce both differential and common-mode voltages, which in turn minimizes leakage current from solar panels. Additionally, it reduces the size of the output filter and the harmonic content. Furthermore, the proposed topology is capable of tripling the input voltage using a single input. It utilizes a lower number of switched-capacitor cells to decrease the current spikes of the power switches during switching. The topology of the conventional buck-boost configuration is also integrated into the design to boost the low input voltage. Furthermore, the presented converter employs fewer power switches than other conventional topologies at the same voltage level. These features make the presented converter more cost-effective and efficient. A 330 W experimental prototype has been developed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design. The overall efficiency achieved is approximately 97.33%. Additionally, the proposed 7-level inverter is compared with other topologies reported in the literature.

Article.Title: Landscape genetics reveals the role of watercourses in driving gene flow in Chioglossa lusitanica
Article.Authors: Aguilar F.; Tarroso P.; Segurado P.; Velo-Antón G.
Article.Abstract: Riparian ecosystems are increasingly affected by human activities that alter habitats and reduce landscape connectivity. Riparian amphibians are particularly vulnerable because they depend on both aquatic and terrestrial environments. In this study, we examined how landscape features influence genetic connectivity in Chioglossa lusitanica , an endemic stream salamander from the western Iberian Peninsula, using a high-resolution watershed-scale landscape genetic approach in the Ceira River basin. Microsatellite data from 248 individuals sampled at 88 sites were analysed to evaluate isolation-by-distance and isolation-by-resistance models incorporating environmental, geographical, and topographic variables. Genetic analyses identified two main genetic clusters with extensive admixture in the Lousã Mountains, revealing fine-scale genetic structuring within a single drainage system. Patterns of genetic differentiation were strongly associated with the river network, indicating that watercourses play a key role in maintaining connectivity across the watershed. However, the observed genetic structure likely reflects the combined influence of contemporary connectivity and historical population processes. Lowland areas were associated with increased landscape resistance, consistent with reduced habitat suitability in human-modified landscapes. These findings highlight the importance of riparian landscapes for population connectivity and suggest that conservation efforts should prioritize the maintenance and restoration of riparian corridors, particularly in mountainous regions, to support long-term persistence of C. lusitanica and other riparian-dependent species.

Article.Title: Design and analysis of an integrated structure for a spatial camera aluminum alloy mirror based on topology optimization
Article.Authors: Ren J.; Yin L.; Zhang W.; Pei Z.; Yu H.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To meet the critical demand for large-aperture, lightweight, and high-surface-accuracy mirrors in thermally stable space cameras, this study proposes a design method for a Φ294 mm aluminum alloy mirror based on topological optimization. First, using (RSA-6061) aluminum alloy as the base material, a topological optimization mathematical model was established by combining the SIMP model with a substructure method. This model uses weighted compliance minimization as the objective function and comprehensively considers axial and lateral gravity loads, polishing load, and thermal load conditions, while adhering to volume fraction constraints. Topological optimization was used to achieve optimal material distribution. Second, the topological optimization contour was used to design the structure with manufacturability considerations, followed by parametric optimization of key dimensions. Finally, finite element simulation and experimental validation were conducted. Simulation results show that the mirror achieved a weight reduction of 72%. Under self-weight in the X, Y, and Z directions, the RMS surface profile accuracy of the primary mirror was 7.02 nm, 7.099 nm, and 2.353 nm, respectively. At a temperature rise of 6 °C, the primary mirror’s surface profile accuracy was 4.571 nm. The fundamental frequency was 360.543 Hz. Experimental verification showed that the RMS surface profile accuracy was 0.0206λ, with a fundamental frequency of 356.78 Hz. All tested metrics met the technical specifications for the space camera.

Article.Title: Research on a CNC machine tool machining error analysis and prediction method based on digital twin and ISSLO-CNN
Article.Authors: Cao Z.; Chen L.; Lin Z.; Zhuo Y.
Article.Abstract: To address the insufficient hyperparameter optimization accuracy and low convergence efficiency of the stochastic social learning optimization algorithm (SSLO) in CNC machine tool machining error prediction, caused by the fixed distribution of learning factors, lack of elite guidance in learning targets, and static knowledge exchange rate, an improved stochastic social learning optimization algorithm (ISSLO) and digital twin-driven CNN error prediction model are proposed. First, physical measurement signals and virtual simulation signals are synchronously acquired based on a digital twin quadruple model, and a multisource fused feature matrix is generated using a linear fusion strategy as the input samples of the convolutional neural network (CNN). Subsequently, a new improved SSLO algorithm is designed. On the one hand, an elite-guided adaptive learning factor mechanism based on iterative cosine decay and fitness ranking is introduced to dynamically regulate the search step size and guide individuals toward elite solutions. On the other hand, an adaptive perturbation strategy based on historical successful-direction memory and a dynamic knowledge exchange rate adjustment mechanism based on the update success rate are constructed to enhance the improvement efficiency of disadvantaged individuals and information exchange within the population. Finally, ISSLO is employed to iteratively optimize key CNN hyperparameters, including convolution kernel size, number of kernels, learning rate, number of neurons in the fully connected layer, and batch size, and the CNN is trained using the optimal configuration to perform error prediction. Experimental results on the NCMT-DT-Error dataset show that ISSLO-CNN achieves a root mean square error of 3.84 ± 0.16 μm, a mean absolute error of 2.72 ± 0.12 μm, and a coefficient of determination of 0.979 ± 0.003, while its physical consistency metrics comprehensively outperform those of comparison models such as SSLO-CNN. The proposed method has 1.97 M parameters and a single-sample inference time of 3.62 ms, and ablation experiments verify the effectiveness of the two improvement strategies. The results demonstrate that ISSLO-CNN improves prediction accuracy while maintaining low model complexity and inference latency, indicating its potential for online machining error monitoring and intelligent quality control. Its practical closed-loop compensation performance requires further validation.

Article.Title: The calibration method coupled with registration errors of secondary imaging spectral polarimetric remote sensing system
Article.Authors: Song M.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The secondary imaging optical configuration requires precise registration between the mosaic spectral filter array and the focal plane array of the polarization camera. Micrometer-level registration errors between these two components can cause spectral crosstalk among adjacent pixels, thereby reducing the accuracy of target characteristic measurements. To address this issue, this article proposes a polarimetric–radiometric joint calibration method coupled with registration errors. This method introduces registration errors into the mapping relationship between incident spectrum polarization information and imaging detector output. Based on this relationship, a system energy transfer and response model coupled with registration errors is established. Designs a calibration equation using spectral polarization superpixels as calibration units and provides its least squares solution method. Calibration and inversion experiments are conducted to compare and analyze the calibration matrix and inversion error under two conditions: ideal registration assumption and coupled registration error. The experimental results show that the relative error of radiance inversion is ≤ 1.81%, that of the degree of linear polarization is ≤ 2.69%, and the error of the angle of polarization is ≤ 1.1092°. This method can effectively improve the calibration and inversion accuracy, providing a high-precision and reliable calibration framework for remote sensing applications of secondary imaging spectral polarimetric imaging systems.

Article.Title: ROME (INAFM2) expression is required for mouse parturition and postnatal survival
Article.Authors: Molotkova A.; Knoll N.; Taskintuna K.; Stablewski A.; Ozdemirli M.; Jayatilake M.; Bansal S.; Cheema A.; Ayhan A.; Bassel L.; Edmondson E.; Karim B.; Lee Y.; Rodriguez O.; Albanese C.; Toretsky J.; Golestaneh N.; Üren A.
Article.Abstract: We previously characterized the biochemical properties of the ROME protein and discovered its essential role in cancer cell metastasis and zebrafish development. To study the function of ROME in mammalian development and homeostasis, we created an inducible Rome knockout mouse model with tet-o-cre, M2-rtTA at the Rosa26 locus, and loxP sites inserted outside the 5’ and 3’ ends of the entire Rome gene. When Rome was deleted during embryogenesis by providing doxycycline in the feed to pregnant animals, phenotypically normal looking pups were born at the expected Mendelian ratio, but 86% of the pups with homozygote Rome deletion died within 72 h. Early postnatal mortality was primarily dependent on the genotype of the pregnant female as Rome deletion caused impaired parturition. In the F1 generation, Rome knockout mice surviving to adulthood exhibited unilateral or bilateral microphthalmia with 23% penetrance and a trend for the right eye being affected more frequently in the unilateral cases. These findings suggest that ROME expression during embryogenesis is critical for normal parturition and subsequent survival of pups in early postnatal life.

Article.Title: Adaptive Structural Interaction Guided Fractional Perona–Malik Diffusion for Medical Image Enhancement
Article.Authors: A P.; S K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite these developments, image enhancement remains a challenging task, because it requires effective noise removal while preserving edges, textures, and fine structural details. Existing diffusion-based techniques may cause excessive smoothing, which can result in the loss of important image information. To address this issue, the present study proposes an image enhancement framework that integrates the Caputo fractional derivative, Hausdorff Fractal Derivative (HFD), and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) within the Perona–Malik anisotropic diffusion model. A fidelity term is incorporated to maintain structural consistency and improve the reconstruction accuracy during the enhancement process. The mathematical properties of the proposed model are established through convergence and stability analyses. The proposed framework is evaluated using two-dimensional and three-dimensional benchmark datasets, as well as medical images corrupted by Gaussian noise. A parameter sensitivity analysis is performed to identify suitable fractional and fractal orders. The results show that parameter values within the range (0, 1) enhance the image while effectively preserving important structural details. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better quantitative and visual performance than the existing image enhancement methods, with higher Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) values and reasonable computational time. Under Gaussian noise, the proposed method demonstrates improved performance compared with deep learning-based methods, including DnCNN, SU-Net, and RED-CNN. To further assess its generalization capability, the proposed framework is evaluated under Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, speckle, Poisson, and mixed noise conditions. The results show that the proposed method provides effective enhancement under different noise conditions, although its performance varies with the type of noise. Multiple realizations of Gaussian noise, together with statistical analysis based on the mean and standard deviation, further confirm the consistency and reliability of the proposed method. In addition, ROI-based comparative analysis demonstrates improved preservation of fine structures and important image details. Overall, the integration of fractional-order diffusion, fractal-based feature preservation, and multiscale wavelet analysis provides an effective and versatile framework for image enhancement.

Article.Title: Multidimensional evaluation of bacterial inoculants for modulating growth, physiology, soil biochemical functioning and productivity of Zea mays under contrasting water regimes
Article.Authors: Khati P.; Mishra P.; Parihar M.; Meena R.; Ghasal P.; Pandey B.; Kant L.
Article.Abstract: The aim of the present study was to evaluate five PGP bacterial inoculants (T1–T5) and an uninoculated control (T6) for drought stress mitigation in maize ( Zea mays L. cv. V-412) through indicators such as plant water status, physiological and biochemical processes, nutrient acquisition, soil enzymatic activities and yield. A factorial randomized block experiment was conducted with six treatments under well-watered (80% field capacity) and water-deficit (40% field capacity) conditions. Under water deficit, T2 recorded the highest relative water content (91.5%), along with higher proline accumulation, grain N concentration (1.33%) and Fe concentration (47.5 ppm). T5 maintained comparatively higher chlorophyll and carotenoid contents and showed relatively higher alkaline phosphatase activity (~ 160 μg pNP g −1 soil h −1 ) and seed number per cob (~ 180) under water deficit. Soil dehydrogenase and fluorescein diacetate hydrolysis activities also differed among treatments, indicating variation in soil enzymatic responses to bacterial inoculation. Yield-related traits, including seed number per cob, 100-seed weight, seed weight per cob and grain yield varied across treatments and water regimes. Principal component analysis showed associations among physiological, growth and yield-related traits with the first two principal components accounting for 52.6% of the total variation. Among the ten stress-tolerance indices evaluated, T5 and T3 showed relatively favourable index values across the measured traits. The results indicate treatment dependent effects of bacterial inoculation on plant and soil responses under water deficit with T5, T3 and T2 showing comparatively favourable responses across selected physiological, nutritional and yield-related attributes.

Article.Title: Bicarbonates extracted from coffee silverskin biochars remediate bacteria from contaminated water
Article.Authors: Rayner J.; Scettri A.; Salgado J.; Miara T.; Krishnan S.; Ali A.; Ojkic N.; Volpe R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Disinfection of water is essential to ensure access to safe drinking water, especially in the rural areas of developing countries. However, conventional methods of water remediation often generate toxic byproducts, or are highly energy-intensive and technologically advanced, and therefore not always sustainable in the developing countries. Here we show a novel approach for water decontamination from bacteria which uses biochar derived from Coffee Silverskin. We demonstrate that potassium carbonates, which concentrate on the biochar surfaces during biomass pyrolysis, easily dissolve in water to form bicarbonates with significant bacteriostatic and bactericidal activity. We found an optimal pyrolysis temperature for the preparation of biochar that is effective against highly contaminated water, reducing the number of bacteria by 97%. Furthermore, we showed that biochar-derived bicarbonates reduce bacterial cell elongation rate, disrupt bacterial proton-motive force, and induce deadly cell lysis. Therefore, we established a novel mechanism of bacterial elimination from contaminated water using biochar-derived bicarbonates.

Article.Title: More than evidence—the science of forensic dentistry in pursuit of justice
Article.Authors: Fonseca G.; Merdietio Boedi R.; Angelakopoulos N.; Franco A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Science is not inherently obliged to solve immediate practical problems. Forensic science, however, carries an additional responsibility by bringing scientific knowledge to bear on questions posed by law and justice. Forensic dentistry is undergoing a profound methodological transformation, with established morphological, radiographic, and comparative approaches increasingly complemented by artificial intelligence, three-dimensional imaging, molecular biomarkers, and advanced evidence synthesis. The 12 papers in this Scientific Reports Collection capture this convergence between longstanding forensic questions and methodological change. Together, they show that innovation must remain inseparable from validation, transparent communication of uncertainty, and practical relevance to forensic research and legal and humanitarian practice, so that scientific progress can be translated into sound and humane responses to matters affecting identity, rights, and human dignity.

Article.Title: Survival rates and challenges of mobilized tree planting seedlings in Wadla Woreda, Northeastern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Sisay B.; Merso D.; Abegaz A.
Article.Abstract: The main purpose of this study was to assess the level of seedling survival and associated challenges under community mobilization tree planting practices in Wadla Woreda, North Wollo Zone, Ethiopia. A descriptive survey design with a mixed approach was used, which included both quantitative and qualitative data collected from households, leaders of kebeles, development agents, and forestry experts. Primary data was gathered through questionnaires, interviews, focus groups, and transect walks, while secondary data, including reports and official records, was also reviewed. Based on transect walk data, the average seedling survival rate was 51.77% with a wide range of variations among the kebeles. Among sample kebeles, Meley recorded the highest (81.3%) survival rate, and Kuana registered the lowest (31.86%) survival rate. Woreda Agricultural Office records further showed that, seedling survival fluctuated between 2018 and 2022, declining from 89.4% in 2018 to 49.4% in 2020 before recovering to 84.6% in 2022. Participants associated the low survival in 2020 with the COVID-19 pandemic and the disruption of planting and monitoring in 2021 with unrest in northern Ethiopia. Based on household responses, descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression identified improper planting technique, inappropriate planting time, competition by weeds, predation by animals, lack of replacements, and local instability as the major factors associated with reduced seedling survival in the study area. The findings suggest that improving the success of mobilized tree-planting programs requires greater emphasis on post-planting management, including capacity building, timely replacement planting, and sustained institutional support to enhance seedling survival and achieve long-term restoration outcomes.

Article.Title: Putative lethal and unfavorable haplotypes associated with reproductive performance and chick viability in broiler chickens
Article.Authors: Padilha S.; Ibelli A.; Cantão M.; Peixoto J.; Coutinho L.; Dias L.; Ledur M.; Schenkel F.
Article.Abstract: Breeding structure and intensive selection can increase inbreeding and the frequency of recessive alleles, some of which may reduce fertility and cause offspring mortality. This study aimed to identify prospective lethal and putative unfavorable haplotypes associated with the number of incubated eggs (NIE), fertile eggs (NFE), hatched chicks (NHC) and viable chicks (NVC) in a paternal broiler line. Data from 902 genotyped chickens were used for phasing and haplotype block construction with findhap.f90 . Haplotypes were considered lethal when frequency was > 5%, no homozygotes were observed, expected numbers of homozygous individuals ≥ 2 and probabilities of observing zero homozygotes ≤ 0.15. Putative unfavorable haplotypes were analyzed as pseudo-SNPs using BLUPF90. Genes were identified using biomaRt and subjected to enrichment analysis with clusterProfiler. Twenty-one candidate lethal haplotypes were identified, harboring 240 genes enriched for embryonic, morphogenesis, nervous and DNA processes. GWAS identified haploblocks containing unfavorable haplotypes associated with all traits, harboring 479 genes enriched for metabolic, embryonic, morphogenesis, immune, nervous, genetic and cellular processes. Two haplotypes (1908_1 and 351_17) were identified as both lethal and unfavorable. Given the biological processes in which genes located within these haplotypes are involved, their presence may negatively affect reproductive traits and chick viability. Thus, monitoring and preventing the propagation of these haplotypes could mitigate their negative impacts.

Article.Title: Seeing red: avian fatality rates reduced by red-blade patterning at a species-rich African wind farm
Article.Authors: Simmons R.; Martins M.; Cervantes F.
Article.Abstract: Renewable energy wind facilities designed to reduce fossil fuel impacts will increase avian collision rates as they are rolled out in biodiverse nations, without additional mitigation. One such mitigation is to increase blade visibility with high contrast colours. Three field experiments with single black blades reduced fatalities by 72% in Norway, 74% in Spain, but showed no effect in The Netherlands. We undertook the first field-test using patterns and colours at a species-rich South African wind farm using fatality data from 24 months before and 32 months after treatment. The Before-After-Control-Impact (BACI) approach revealed that two broad red stripes on single blades at four of the most lethal turbines reduced fatalities by a median 83% for both the (4) un-patterned nearest-neighbour controls and all 16 controls across the farm. Bayesian models revealed wide confidence limits but strong statistical support for the reduced fatalities effect. There was weak support for the collateral fatalities idea that birds avoiding patterned turbines might veer into un-patterned nearest neighbours. The patterning was particularly effective for raptors, the most impacted group, with an estimated 87% reduction in fatalities. We surmise that patterns increase the contrast of the blades while red may additionally act as a warning (aposematic) deterrent for approaching birds. Our results suggest a new cost-effective pathway to reduce avian-turbine collisions, across biodiverse regions.

Article.Title: Experimental and first-principles investigation of NO2 sensing behaviour in tetragonal ZrO2 nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Bhoye L.; Zoting K.; Sonawane L.; Mandawade A.; Kim H.; Jadhav O.; Patil G.; Gholap H.; Kim J.; Bulakhe R.; Shinde M.
Article.Abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a hazardous oxidizing gas that requires reliable detection for environmental and industrial safety applications. In this work, nanocrystalline tetragonal ZrO 2 nanoparticles were fabricated into thick-film sensors and systematically investigated using structural, surface, optical, and first-principles approaches to establish comprehensive structure–property correlations. X-ray diffraction and HRTEM confirmed phase-pure tetragonal ZrO 2 with an average crystallite size of 8–9 nm, while Raman spectroscopy validated structural symmetry. Mesoporous properties with an average pore diameter of 3.49 nm were found by BET analysis. UV-visible spectroscopy showed an optical band gap of 3.8 eV, consistent with the DFT-calculated indirect band gap of 4.03 eV. Density of states analysis indicated dominant Zr 4d contributions in the conduction band and O 2p states in the valence band. The experimental optical behavior was supported by the computed dielectric function, absorption coefficient, and optical conductivity, which showed substantial interband transitions in the UV range. Gas sensing studies demonstrated a high NO 2 response of 87.5% at 200 °C, with rapid response (12 s) and recovery (21 s) times, linear sensitivity from 20 to 160 ppm, and stable performance over 50 days. The enhanced sensing performance is associated with adsorption-induced electronic modulation at the nanoparticle surface, confirming tetragonal ZrO 2 as a promising NO 2 sensing material.

Article.Title: A gFET-based sensor equipped with a focused polyclonal aptamer library derived from FluMag-SELEX for specific quantification of the hormone-like anti-aging protein klotho in human serum
Article.Authors: Li R.; He S.; Gruber D.; Krämer M.; Stürmer A.; Hasler R.; Kleber C.; Knoll W.; Kissmann A.; Rosenau F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Klotho (KL) gene encodes a single-pass transmembrane protein that functions as a regulator associated with aging-related physiology. In humans, reduced Klotho expression is associated with aging, diabetes, Alzheimer’s disease and other age-related disorders, correlating with increased all-cause mortality. The full-length α-Klotho protein consists of two extracellular domains, KL1 and KL2, which are proteolytically cleaved to generate the soluble form – the predominant species in circulation, which is difficult to detect in plasma. Among these, KL1 is the key functional domain, mediating most of Klotho’s enzymatic and signaling activities, including the modulation of fibroblast growth factor (FGF) pathways and glycan processing, making it a critical target for biomarker development. In this study, a polyclonal ssDNA aptamer library was enriched through nine rounds of FluMag-SELEX against human α-Klotho. The selection process was monitored by qPCR, while fluorescence microscopy and fluorometric microtiter plate assays were used to characterize the binding properties of the enriched library. The resulting aptamer library exhibited preferential recognition of α-Klotho and was further evaluated for recognition of its KL1 domain. We developed an Aptamer-Linked Fluorescence Assay (ALFA), demonstrating Klotho-associated fluorescence responses in 50% and undiluted human serum. Furthermore, integration of the enriched aptamer library into a graphene field-effect transistor (gFET) enabled label-free, concentration-dependent electrical detection of recombinant α-Klotho and KL1 in buffer and 1% human serum. Together, these complementary approaches demonstrate the potential of the selected polyclonal aptamer library for fluorescence-based and electronic detection of Klotho, providing a foundation for further biosensor development and analytical validation in biological samples.

Article.Title: Enhanced flying-capacitor boost multilevel inverter with improved capacitor voltage balancing and minimized current spikes
Article.Authors: Awadelseed A.; Lewicki A.; Jaderko A.; Iqbal A.
Article.Abstract: Flying-Capacitor-based multilevel inverters, MLIs, provide high output voltage levels through their charging-discharging topological concept of inserted capacitor banks. But high component-count, capacitor voltage imbalance, and pronounced current spikes in the charging paths of the constituting capacitor banks are major drawbacks of this class of multilevel inverters. This paper proposes a single-phase, eleven-level flying-capacitor boost multilevel inverter (11 L-FCMLI) topology configured to overcome the said drawbacks. The proposed configuration synthesizes an 11-level output voltage from a single DC source by integrating a conventional H-bridge with an auxiliary flying-capacitor cell. The auxiliary cell not only provides voltage boosting capability, but also ensures robust and precise capacitor voltage balancing. Such operational control suppresses voltage drift and mitigates transient current surges that adversely affect inverters’ performances and reliability. The 11 L-FCMLI achieves a high voltage gain with significantly reduced semiconductor devices; thereby lowering system cost, complexity, and devices’ voltage stresses. A hybrid sinusoidal pulse-width modulation, SPWM, scheme with an in-built advanced capacitor voltage balancing algorithm is presented for the control of the 11 L-FCMLI. This control approach entrenches effective voltage regulation, reduced switching losses, and improved harmonic quality. Comparative evaluation against recently developed Capacitor-switched-based MLIs demonstrates the superior performances of the proposed inverter configuration. Theoretical analysis is validated through detailed experimental verification, demonstrating strong agreement with predicted results.

Article.Title: An initial investigation into a low-complexity adaptive transparency framework for hearables using spectral analysis and loudness control
Article.Authors: MENON A.; SHANMUGAM K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transparency mode is an important feature of modern hearable devices, enabling real-time reproduction of environmental sounds while preserving perceptual comfort and situational awareness. Conventional transparency pipelines rely on static filtering and fixed loudness control, which perform poorly in highly non-stationary acoustic environments and often produce perceptual harshness, clipping, and unstable loudness behaviour. This paper presents an initial, proof-of-concept investigation into a low-complexity hybrid adaptive transparency architecture that integrates statistically driven loudness control, content-aware filtering, and lightweight acoustic feature analysis. Short-time energy and spectral centroid are jointly used to detect perceptually harsh high-frequency events and classify incoming acoustic frames. Based on this classification, harsh events are selectively attenuated through targeted band-stop filtering, while benign ambient sounds are preserved through gentle low-pass filtering. Loudness stability is addressed using an adaptive RMS-based limiter that dynamically updates its threshold via a combination of exponential moving average and percentile-based ambient estimators; this is a statistically driven loudness control strategy rather than a validated psychoacoustic loudness model. The proposed system is implemented in a real-time MATLAB framework that reflects the constraints of hearable-class digital signal processing. On a limited set of real-world environmental recordings, the proposed system shows lower peak-to-average ratio, improved transient handling, faster recovery, and smoother loudness trajectories compared to three static transparency baselines implemented for this study, alongside computational characteristics compatible with embedded hearable devices: an estimated per-hop cost of approximately 9000 multiply-accumulate operations. These findings are indicative rather than conclusive. This is a preliminary framework: perceptual evaluation was conducted informally by the two authors only, without an independent listener panel or a formal psychoacoustic loudness/sharpness model beyond the offline metrics reported, and the evaluation corpus was limited in size and diversity. Formal subjective validation and larger-scale, independently annotated evaluation are identified as essential next steps before broader claims can be supported.

Article.Title: Homogeneous liquid–liquid microextraction using low-density solvents for BHA and BHT extraction from artificial tears followed by GC–FID
Article.Authors: Ghoreishizadeh M.; Farajzadeh M.; Barazandeh S.; Afshar Mogaddam M.
Article.Abstract: An efficient homogeneous liquid–liquid microextraction approach was established for the extraction of butylated hydroxy anisole and butylated hydroxy toluene from artificial tear samples prior to gas chromatography–flame ionization detection. The proposed approach was designed to combine high analytical performance with procedural simplicity, short extraction time, and minimal organic solvent consumption. In the extraction procedure, a few µL of toluene was first added to the aqueous solution of the analytes to form a homogeneous solution. Subsequently, a few µL of di- n -butyl ether was introduced as a phase-separating solvent, resulting in the formation of a turbid system. After centrifugation, the low-density organic phase containing the enriched analytes was accumulated in the capillary section of a specially home-made glass extraction tube, allowing convenient removing and injection into the separation system. The influences of critical experimental parameters, such as type and volume of extraction solvents, vortexing time, centrifugation conditions, and pH were systematically investigated and optimized to achieve maximum extraction efficiency. Under the optimized conditions, enrichment factors of 2454 and 1607 were obtained for butylated hydroxytoluene and butylated hydroxy anisole, respectively. The method presented satisfactory linearity over the concentration range of 10–5000 µg L −1 , with coefficients of determination higher than 0.99. The limits of detection were 0.70 µg L −1 for butylated hydroxytoluene and 2.3 µg L −1 for butylated hydroxy anisole while the intra- and inter-day relative standard deviations were below 10%. Also, extraction recoveries were 65% for butylated hydroxy anisole and 98% for butylated hydroxytoluene. Key advantages of this approach included simplicity, rapidity, cost-effectiveness, reliability, and high enrichment factors. The proposed method provided a rapid and economical approach for the determination of phenolic antioxidants in ophthalmic formulations.

Article.Title: A systematic review and dose response meta-analysis of dietary fat intake and liver cancer risk
Article.Authors: Mokhtari A.; Heshmatipour H.; Zeydi M.; Rezazadegan M.; Sadeghi O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Data on the association between dietary fat intake and liver cancer risk are inconclusive. Therefore, the present meta-analysis was conducted to examine the associations between dietary fat intake, different types of fatty acids, and liver cancer risk. A comprehensive literature search was conducted to identify eligible studies through June 2026. We included 14 prospective cohort studies. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale, and data were synthesized using a random-effects model. Total fat intake was not significantly associated with liver cancer risk (RR: 1.14, 95% CI 0.95–1.36). Dose–response analyses showed that each 20 g/day increase in plant fat intake was associated with a 20% lower risk of liver cancer (RR: 0.80, 95% CI 0.67–0.96), whereas each 20 g/day increase in saturated fat intake was associated with an 18% higher risk (RR: 1.18, 95% CI 1.02–1.37). Higher MUFA/SFA (RR: 0.80, 95% CI 0.72–0.89) and (PUFA + MUFA)/SFA (RR: 0.87, 95% CI 0.77–0.97) ratios were associated with a lower risk of liver cancer, whereas the PUFA/SFA ratio showed a borderline inverse association (RR: 0.82, 95% CI 0.68–1.00). Overall, these findings suggest that dietary fat quality, rather than total fat intake, may be a more relevant indicator of a dietary target for liver cancer prevention. Article.Title: Rapid quantification of patchouli alcohol in patchouli oil (Pogostemon Cablin) using near infrared spectroscopy with multivariate and machine learning approaches
Article.Authors: Ainina N.; Nurjanah S.; Sinniah U.; Hidayat R.; Julaeha E.; Nanda M.; Muhaemin M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patchouli oil ( Pogostemon Cablin ) is an essential oil primarily used as a fixative ingredient in the perfumery and cosmetic industries. Its major component, patchouli alcohol (PA), is recognized as a key quality parameter, with higher contents being desirable. However, the conventional method for quantifying PA, namely gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), is relatively expensive, time-consuming, and destructive. Therefore, this study aimed to explore near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with multivariate and machine learning algorithms, including partial least squares regression (PLSR), support vector regression (SVR), and a hybrid method, partial least squares-support vector regression (PLS-SVR). The best-performing models was obtained using PLSR combined with Savitzky-Golay 2nd derivative (SG 2nd) preprocessing in a single-split evaluation, achieving R 2 CV = 0.9094, RMSECV = 2.3471, R 2 P = 0.9251, RMSEP = 2.3099, and RPD = 3.676. The robustness of this model was further confirmed using Monte-Carlo double cross-validation (MCCV-DCV), yielding a mean of R 2 P and RMSEP at 0.8909 ± 0.0417 and 2.4329 ± 0.4402, respectively, across thirty repeated iterations. A paired statistical comparison between PLSR and PLS-SVR further showed no significant difference in RMSEP (Wilcoxon singed-rank test, p-value = 0.1347), while SVR performed significantly worse ( p < 0.05). In conclusion, NIR spectroscopy using PLSR method, could be used as a rapid, simple, low-cost alternative method for estimating PA content in patchouli oil.

Article.Title: Phylogeography and population genetic structure of Ehrlichia canis based on 16​S rRNA gene sequences
Article.Authors: Nehra A.; Kumari A.; Panda R.; Moudgil A.
Article.Abstract: Ehrlichia canis is a globally distributed tick-borne pathogen of dogs, but its phylogeographic patterns and population structure remain incompletely understood. In this study, 16S rRNA ( n = 67) gene sequences from multiple geographic regions, including 17 newly generated sequences from India, were analyzed to assess genetic diversity and population structure. Phylogenetic analysis revealed high conservation of the partial 16S rRNA gene. Nine haplotypes were identified, with low overall haplotype diversity (Hd = 0.302 ± 0.073). A predominant haplotype was shared among geographically distant populations, while India showed the highest observed number of haplotypes and Mexico comparatively high nucleotide diversity. Significant negative Tajima’s D and Fu and Li’s F values, together with a star-like haplotype network, were compatible with demographic expansion or other departures from neutrality, although selection, population structure, and uneven sampling may also contribute. AMOVA indicated that 93.23% of genetic variation occurred within populations, while overall differentiation was low and non-significant (F ST = 0.06765, P = 0.27664). These findings indicate weak geographic structuring at the conserved 16S rRNA locus but do not demonstrate genome-wide homogeneity or contemporary transcontinental gene flow. The study provides a comparative baseline for E. canis population genetics and highlights the need for balanced sampling and higher-resolution genomic approaches.

Article.Title: DCAF7 downregulation as a potential prognostic biomarker in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: tissue-based and in vitro evidence
Article.Authors: Liao Y.; Li D.; Chen S.; Shao Q.; Zhou G.; Qin L.; Liao S.
Article.Abstract: DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor 7 (DCAF7) has been demonstrated in protein degradation, transcriptional regulation, and signal transduction in various cancers. However, its prognostic value and celluar function in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain to be explored. This study assessed DCAF7 expression and its clinicopathological and prognostic implications in ccRCC utilizing bioinformatics, immunohistochemistry and western blot analysis. Analysis of three independent cohorts (TCGA-KIRC, GSE40435, and the combined dataset GSE53757 and GSE66272) consistently revealed that DCAF7 is downregulated in ccRCC. Further validation through immunohistochemistry and Western blot analysis confirmed the downregulation of DCAF7 protein in samples from ccRCC patients, as well as in ACHN and OS-RC-2 cell lines. Correlation analysis revealed a significant association between decreased DCAF7 expression and higher pathological grades, suggesting that low expression may serve as a predictor of poor prognosis in patients. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) based on these public tissue cohorts confirmed that DCAF7 mRNA expression discriminates ccRCC tumors from adjacent normal tissue. Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified distant metastasis, lymph node metastasis, and age as independent risk factors, whereas high DCAF7 expression served as an independent protective factor. A nomogram incorporating these prognostic factors effectively predicted overall survival at 1-, 3-, and 5-years. At the CpG-island level, methylation was not significantly correlated with DCAF7 mRNA expression. However, several individual CpG sites showed significantly associations with patient survival. Immune infiltration analysis suggested a positive correlation between DCAF7 expression and the extent of immune cell infiltration. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) further revealed significant enrichment of pathways, including WNT signaling negative regulatory module (SOST/LRP4 axis), RTK-CBL-mediated ubiquitination, and Hippo signaling in the high DCAF7 expression group. In vitro functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of DCAF7 significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of ACHN and OS-RC-2 cells, suggesting a potential tumor-suppressive role of DCAF7 in ccRCC. Collectively, DCAF7 may serve as a prognostic biomarker for ccRCC, and future research is required to validate its translational potential as a therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Model-based assessment of thoracic load transmission and local cortical bone stress under posterior manual loading: a whole spine–thorax finite element study
Article.Authors: Li J.; Yu Y.; Tang L.; Meng J.; Hu Z.; Liao W.; Liang Z.; Wang Y.; Zhang F.; Zhang J.; Yang J.; Ye Y.; Li Y.; Feng Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The thoracic spine and rib cage form a coupled load-bearing system, but internal thoracic stress transmission under posterior manual loading remains difficult to quantify experimentally. This preclinical computational study aimed to evaluate thoracic load transmission, whole-model stress and​ deformation, and local cortical bone stress under controlled posterior manual thoracic loading conditions. Finite element simulations were performed using a previously developed whole spine–thorax model with consistent boundary conditions and quantified mechanical inputs. Six palm-based posterior thoracic loading patterns were simulated under T6 spinous-process loading using experimentally measured mean peak loads and mean equivalent contact areas. Under the superimposed palm–palm-root loading condition, T6 spinous-process loading was compared with left paravertebral loading at T6 under identical loading parameters. Progressive loading was then performed under the representative left paravertebral condition to evaluate local cortical-bone stress concentration and identify the external load at which the predefined 90 MPa reference criterion was reached. Different experimentally defined posterior thoracic loading scenarios produced different whole-model stress and deformation responses. The double-palm condition had the highest measured peak load and also produced the largest whole-model maximum von Mises equivalent stress and maximum total deformation. Compared with T6 spinous-process loading, left paravertebral loading produced a more loaded-side-concentrated stress distribution and lower whole-model maximum von Mises equivalent stress and maximum total deformation. Under progressive loading, high-stress cortical bone regions were mainly concentrated in the upper ribs. The predefined 90 MPa cortical-bone reference criterion was reached at an external load of approximately 730 N. Posterior manual thoracic loading produced distinct whole-model and local cortical bone responses across experimentally defined loading scenarios and force-application sites. The differences among loading patterns were observed under experimentally defined combinations of peak load, contact area, and loading geometry and should not be interpreted as independent effects of these individual parameters. These findings provide model-specific biomechanical evidence for interpreting thoracic stress distribution and regional osseous stress concentration under posterior manual loading.

Article.Title: Environmental enrichment exerts neuroprotective effects on cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury with the ALK5/Smad2/3/Gadd45β pathway involved in the inhibition of apoptosis
Article.Authors: Liu G.; Xiao H.; Zou Y.; Jiang X.; Liao L.; Liu L.; Lu Q.; Song Y.; Lv L.; Zhang K.; Gao C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reperfusion therapy is the primary treatment for ischemic stroke; however, it can induce cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury (CIRI), often leading to suboptimal neurological recovery. Combining reperfusion with neuroprotective interventions such as environmental enrichment (EE) to suppress reperfusion-induced cellular damage holds significant therapeutic promise. This study mainly focused on the activin receptor-like kinase 5 (ALK5) signaling pathway to explore the potential regulatory mechanism of EE in mediating neuroprotection and functional repair following CIRI. In vivo experiments were performed using transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (tMCAO/R) rat models. In vitro validation was conducted in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) treated SH-SY5Y cells. Combined genetic interventions, including ALK5 overexpression, ALK5 knockdown, and growth arrest and DNA damage-inducible 45 β (Gadd45β) silencing, were applied to verify the potential molecular mechanism. The results showed that EE significantly upregulated ALK5 expression in the ipsilesional cerebral cortex (M1 region) within the ischemic penumbra, reduced neurological deficits, and reduced the abundance of apoptosis-related markers and TUNEL-positive cells. Mechanistically, ALK5 overexpression was associated with increased phosphorylation of downstream Smad2/3 and elevated Gadd45β expression. Further intervention experiments demonstrated that ALK5 knockdown aggravated neurological deficits, whereas ALK5 overexpression recapitulated the neuroprotective phenotypes observed with EE. Moreover, Gadd45β silencing reversed the modulation of apoptosis-related markers induced by the EE/ALK5 signaling axis. In conclusion, this study reveals a novel potential neuroprotective mechanism in which the ALK5/Smad2/3/Gadd45β signaling cascade may contribute to EE-mediated amelioration of CIRI. It provides theoretical support for the clinical translation of EE as an adjuvant rehabilitative strategy for stroke, and suggests that the ALK5 signaling pathway may serve as a promising therapeutic target for improving neurological recovery following CIRI.

Article.Title: Manganese superoxide dismutase mimetic attenuates doxorubicin-induced myocardial injury via antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms involving Nrf2/HO-1 signaling
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Liu J.; Xue L.; Dang C.; Zhang X.; Tai X.; Zhang L.; Da D.; An Y.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a highly effective anticancer agent, but its clinical application is severely limited by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. Despite its widespread use, effective strategies for preventing DOX-induced cardiac injury remain limited. In this study, we investigated the cardioprotective effects of an engineered manganese superoxide dismutase mimetic (MnSODm) against DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. MnSODm showed no significant cytotoxicity in H9C2 rat cardiomyocytes and dose-dependently alleviated DOX-induced cytotoxicity and morphological alterations, with optimal effects observed at 20 and 40 mg/L. MnSODm also reduced DOX-induced apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses in vitro. In a DOX-induced mouse model, MnSODm significantly improved cardiac index and reduced serum CK and LDH levels, histopathological abnormalities, and cardiac fibrosis. Moreover, MnSODm enhanced antioxidant defenses, as indicated by increased SOD, glutathione peroxidase, and catalase activities and reduced MDA levels. Mechanistically, MnSODm increased Nrf2 and HO-1 expression while reducing Keap1 expression, supporting the involvement of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway in its cardioprotective effects. MnSODm also attenuated inflammatory responses and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure in DOX-treated cardiac tissue. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that MnSODm protects against DOX-induced cardiac injury, primarily through attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation and modulation of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway, highlighting its potential as a cardioprotective strategy during DOX-based chemotherapy.

Article.Title: Cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with task-embedded time perception during exercise
Article.Authors: Edwards A.; Wong A.; Sun F.; Chow C.; Jones A.; Kuo C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subjective time is an emerging dimension of exercise experience, but whether cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with temporal judgements during exercise remains unclear. Twenty-five adults completed a 20-min cycling bout prescribed at 55% of individual peak power output during an externally guided power-and-cadence task. Passage of time (PoT), dynamic time progression estimation at 75% of the bout (DTPE) and 30-s interval production (IPT30) were assessed, alongside heart rate variability (HRV) before and after exercise. V̇O₂max was examined as the principal continuous predictor of PoT and DTPE in sex-adjusted models. Higher V̇O₂max predicted lower DTPE (B = − 0.377, p = .016; Holm-adjusted p = .032), whereas the corresponding association with PoT was directionally consistent but less precise (B = 0.505, p = .075). Secondary sample-relative fitness comparisons showed lower DTPE ( p = .027) and faster PoT ( p = .029) in the higher-fitness subgroup, while IPT30 did not differ between subgroups ( p = .355). Exploratory HRV associations with temporal outcomes did not survive false-discovery-rate correction after controlling for V̇O₂max. Cardiorespiratory fitness was therefore associated most clearly with perceived temporal progress during exercise, indicating that adults with lower fitness may experience the temporal demands of exercise differently even when workload is scaled to individual capacity. This may have implications for how exercise is evaluated and sustained, particularly when supporting less-fit individuals towards independent and lasting exercise participation.

Article.Title: Hydrodynamic simulation-derived training images to improve braided-river reservoir architecture characterization
Article.Authors: Jiang C.; Lin C.; Ren L.; Zhang X.; Liu H.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multiple-point geostatistics (MPS) can reproduce complex geological patterns, but its performance depends on representative training images (TIs). We developed a workflow that converts forward hydrodynamic simulations of braided-river deposition into three-dimensional TIs for reservoir-architecture modeling. Five candidate TIs were reconstructed from time-resolved erosion–deposition increments and classified into channel, mid-channel-bar, floodplain, and bar-margin elements. They were evaluated using cross-sectional architecture, fractal dimension, vertical transition probability, and vertical facies thickness, with interpreted well sequences providing quantitative constraints. The selected TI was used for MPS modeling and compared with sequential indicator simulation (SIS) and object-based modeling (OBM) across ten realizations per method. MPS preserved TI-consistent channel–bar geometries and target proportions, whereas SIS produced fragmented architectures and OBM generated excessive vertical amalgamation. Maximum connected mid-channel-bar thickness was 17.45–20.64 m for MPS, compared with 9.89–22.87 m for SIS and 31.18–50.02 m for OBM. At two held-out wells excluded from conditioning and TI selection, ensemble modal architectural-element accuracy was 76% and 78% for MPS, exceeding SIS (70% and 63%) and OBM (63% and 65%). The workflow links physically based TI construction, quantitative TI selection, and independently tested reservoir prediction, providing a reproducible approach for characterizing interwell architecture while avoiding unsupported inference about dynamic-flow performance in braided-river reservoirs.

Article.Title: Development and characterisation of lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) stem powder-enriched functional rusk using response surface methodology
Article.Authors: Ghodki B.; Rakhita N/A.; Dobhal A.; Rawat K.; Kaur G.; Kumar S.; Kumar V.; Hussain A.; Joshi S.; Kaur R.; Mishra R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to optimise lotus stem powder-enriched rusk (L SP R) using response surface methodology (RSM) and a Box-Behnken design. Lotus stem ( Nelumbo nucifera ) powder level (20–45%), proofing time (90–110 min), and baking time (40–50 min) were selected as independent variables. Their effects were evaluated on key response parameters, including total colour difference, total ash content, crude fiber content, overall acceptability, iron content, and calcium content. The optimised rusk (O-L SP R) was formulated with 36.08% lotus stem powder, a proofing time of 102.91 min, and a baking time of 41.45 min. Comparative evaluation revealed that O-L SP R had higher fiber content (5.65%), total phenolic content (25.30 mg GAE/100 g), iron (11.75 mg/100 g) and calcium (82.05 mg/100 g) than the control rusk (C R ). These findings indicate the potential of lotus stem powder to enhance the nutritional profile of rusk and support its use as a plant-based ingredient in the development of value-added bakery products.

Article.Title: Machine learning and molecular validation reveal the PI3K/AKT/mTOR inflammatory axis for therapeutic targeting in severe COVID-19
Article.Authors: Samsami S.; Alipanah H.; Ghodrat A.; Naghizadeh M.; Ashrafmansouri S.; Ghanbariasad A.
Article.Abstract: Dysregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis contributes to COVID-19 severity by amplifying hyperinflammatory responses. This pilot study integrates molecular biology and explainable machine learning to characterize this pathway, emphasizing its negative regulator PTEN , in stratifying disease severity. RT-qPCR gene expression profiles from 83 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients were merged with clinical data of lung involvement in three severity classes (mild: n = 40, moderate: n = 24, severe: n = 19). Molecular analysis revealed significant upregulation of IL-6 , PI3K , mTOR , and AKT1 in severe and fatal cases, alongside progressive downregulation of PTEN ( P < 0.001) and Cyclin D1 , suggesting impaired pathway inhibition and disrupted cell-cycle regulation. MMP-2 levels correlated with lung involvement. Eight machine learning classifiers were evaluated using Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation for multiclass severity stratification. Random Forest achieved the highest performance (Accuracy: 0.879 ± 0.041; F1-score: 0.874 ± 0.045; AUC-ROC: 0.978 ± 0.007), with robust per-class discrimination including the Severe class (F1: 0.727). Crucially, SHAP-based explainable AI independently validated the molecular findings by identifying PI3K (mean |SHAP| = 0.0984) as the most discriminative feature, followed by AKT1 (0.0838), IL-6 (0.0537), Cyclin D1 (0.0327), and PTEN (0.0287), confirming the canonical PI3K → Akt → mTOR signaling hierarchy. These findings demonstrate that integrating explainable AI with molecular validation can identify biologically coherent prognostic biomarkers, offering a transparent, hypothesis-generating framework for future targeted immunomodulatory research in severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.
