Article.Title: Dynamic response and empirical correction method for shaft structures in layered geotechnical media under lateral blast loading
Article.Authors: Shanzheng S.; Yuan L.; Zeng L.; Linjian M.
Article.Abstract: To address the difficulty in predicting the deformation of shaft structures in layered geological media under lateral blast loading, this study investigates their dynamic response characteristics and develops a correction-based deformation calculation method. An integrated approach combining physical model tests and numerical simulations is adopted to analyze the deformation behavior of shaft structures within a three-layer geotechnical media (sand, soft rock, and hard rock). Comparative analysis with homogeneous media reveals that layered geotechnical media drastically modify the dynamic surface pressure distribution and impose distinct boundary constraints, thereby fundamentally changing the structural deformation mechanism. The results indicate a dual deformation mechanism comprising local shell-type along with global beam-type deformations, which is significantly affected by the constraints of the soft rock layer. Notably, deformations in layered media were consistently smaller than those in homogeneous media under identical loading conditions. An empirical formula for calculating the correction factors was established by dimensional analysis and parametric studies on the influence of charge position and soil-rock parameters. The formula is governed by relative burial depth, layer thickness ratio, and modulus ratio. The correction-factor fitting yields R-squared values above 0.97, and the deformation error compared with the validation cases remains below 20%. The proposed method provides a practical reference for the engineering design and deformation-based assessment of shaft structures under lateral blast loading in layered geological sites.

Article.Title: Ship detection using RSE-YOLOv12 with enhanced feature extraction and fusion
Article.Authors: Wen J.; Wan X.; Du Y.
Article.Abstract: Ship detection in complex maritime scenes is challenged by substantial scale variation, limited details of small targets, and interference from sea surfaces and shoreline backgrounds. Preserving target features during feature extraction and fusion while maintaining inference efficiency remains important for maritime monitoring. To address these challenges, this study proposes RSE-YOLOv12, an enhanced ship detection model based on YOLOv12. Receptive field coordinate attention convolution is incorporated into C3k2 to strengthen local feature representation. A Spatial Perception Informed Feature Extraction module replaces A2C2f to combine local features with contextual information. An efficient upsampling convolution block refines upsampled features for cross-scale fusion. Experiments on SeaShips and LEVIR-Ship show that RSE-YOLOv12 achieves mAP@0.5:0.95 values of 0.805 and 0.316, respectively, exceeding the YOLOv12 baseline by 1.6 and 8.1 percentage points. Inference takes 5.2 ms and 5.4 ms per image on the respective datasets under the experimental settings. These results indicate that the proposed modifications improve ship detection accuracy while maintaining millisecond-level inference in shore-based and remote sensing scenarios.

Article.Title: Structural design and integrated tracking control simulation of a heavy duty dual axis solar tracking turntable
Article.Authors: Wang K.; Zhao C.; Zhang G.; Zhao Y.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: An azimuth and elevation tracking turntable carrying a 1 m aperture primary mirror and a 700 kg class optical payload was designed for cryogenic absolute irradiance measurement. The static response and modes of the elevation support were calculated using an equivalent beam finite-element model. A dual-axis dynamic model incorporating eccentric gravitational torque, low-speed friction, transmission backlash, and three-component wind disturbances was developed to simulate multirate integrated control and the optical power response at the receiver plane. The design offset of the elevation assembly’s center of mass was reduced from 18.4 mm to 3.8 mm, lowering the corresponding maximum eccentric gravitational torque from 167.51 N·m to 34.59 N·m. The first-mode frequency of the equivalent beam increased from 25.21 Hz to 33.45 Hz. At mean wind speeds of 2.0, 9.6, and 10.0 m/s, the combined dual-axis root mean square (RMS) optical axis errors under full control were 1.505″, 1.533″, and 1.539″, respectively. At a mean wind speed of 2.0 m/s, the relative standard deviations of direct irradiance were 4.1047% under baseline control and 0.0738% under full control. At a nominal visibility of 60 km, the relative standard uncertainty of the retrieval was 4.39%.

Article.Title: The effect of a sports-based cognitive game development program on attention level and frontal-midline (Fz) EEG theta/beta ratio
Article.Authors: Eroğlu Eskicioğlu Y.; Pepe Ş.; Baba Kaya H.; Koç G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aims to examine the effects of a 12-week sports-based cognitive game development program on selective attention performance and frontal-midline (Fz) EEG theta/beta ratio in active athletes. The research was conducted using a pre-test–post-test control group randomized experimental design; 100 sport sciences students from Düzce University who were actively engaged in sport (self-reported) were randomly assigned to experimental (n = 50) and control (n = 50) groups; five participants in the experimental group were excluded for non-adherence (absence from more than two sessions), and 95 participants (45 experimental, 50 control) were included in the analysis. The experimental group participated in a sports-based cognitive game development program for 12 weeks, two days a week, totaling 24 sessions, with each session lasting 45 min. The program was designed based on a five-stage and gradual cognitive load principle, including adaptation and basic cognitive infrastructure, attention and reaction development, decision-making and strategy, concentration and multitasking performance, and reinforcement and transfer to sports. The control group received no intervention and continued their daily lives. As measurement tools, the d2 Attention Test (TN-E score; primary outcome) and, as an exploratory neurophysiological measure, the EEG theta/beta ratio obtained from the Fz electrode using the NeXus-10 Mk II device were used; the data were analyzed using a 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVA and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons. The Group × Time interaction was significant for the primary outcome (d2 TN − E) and for the exploratory outcome (theta/beta ratio). Compared with the control group, the experimental group showed a greater improvement in selective attention performance (difference in change: 40.73 points, 95% CI [26.02, 55.45]; dppc2 = 0.81, 95% CI [0.53, 1.16]) and a greater reduction in the theta/beta ratio (difference in change: − 3.19, 95% CI [− 3.89, − 2.48]; dppc2 = − 1.01, 95% CI [− 1.29, − 0.79]). At post-test, the between-group differences were d = 0.84 (95% CI [0.42, 1.26]) for attention performance and d = − 0.88 (95% CI [− 1.29, − 0.45]) for the theta/beta ratio. The change in the control group was not statistically significant for either outcome, although the confidence intervals did not exclude small changes. However, the achieved sample (N = 95) was smaller than the planned sample (N = 128), and the a priori sample size calculation was not based on the primary (Group × Time) analysis; the effect estimates are therefore imprecise, and their confidence intervals are compatible with effects ranging from small-to-medium to large. In a sensitivity analysis including all 100 randomized participants, with conservative assumptions for the five participants without post-test data, both between-group effects remained (difference in change: TN − E 36.06, 95% CI [21.56, 50.56]; TBR − 2.90, 95% CI [− 3.61, − 2.19]). The findings suggest that, compared with no intervention, participation in the sport-based cognitive game program as a whole was associated with a greater improvement in selective attention performance and with a reduction in the resting frontal-midline (Fz) theta/beta ratio in active athletes. Changes were observed in both the behavioral outcome and the exploratory neurophysiological outcome; however, individual changes in the two outcomes were not correlated (partial r = .04, 95% CI [− .16, .24]), and the functional meaning of the change in the theta/beta ratio was not established. Because the control group received no intervention, the effects cannot be attributed specifically to the cognitive game component rather than to the additional activity, contact and attention received by the experimental group, and, because only the ratio was recorded at a single electrode (Fz), the change in the theta/beta ratio is considered exploratory and does not indicate specific neurophysiological adaptations. The main limitations of this study are the practice effect due to the repeated application of the d2 test, the impossibility to carry out a blind application, the lack of a follow-up measurement and an active control condition, the use of only the Fz electrode the lack of participant-level information on sport discipline, training experience and physical activity outside the intervention, and the fact that the sample is specific to a single university. Article.Title: Multi-frequency phase-difference microwave sensing for moisture detection in fiberglass insulated pipelines
Article.Authors: Gacem M.; Akbar M.; Dabous S.
Article.Abstract: Moisture ingress in insulated pipelines can promote corrosion under insulation and increase operational and safety risks, while early detection remains challenging because the affected region is concealed beneath the insulation. This study presents a non-invasive multi-frequency phase-difference microwave sensing framework for assessing localized moisture conditions in fiberglass-insulated steel pipelines. The system operates over the 2.40–2.42 GHz band using an IEEE 802.11 OFDM structure with 64 subcarriers and a dual-receiver configuration. Differential phase responses are extracted across the subcarriers, combined using circular-mean aggregation to account for phase periodicity and exploit frequency diversity, and subsequently processed using exponential moving average (EMA) filtering. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations were used to evaluate the sensing principle under controlled variations in standoff distance, insulation thickness, pipe radius, and moisture condition. Ablation analysis demonstrated a progressive reduction in response ambiguity from 16 ambiguous points for the amplitude-based benchmark, to 11 for single-frequency phase difference, 9 following multi-frequency circular averaging, and only 3 using the complete circular-mean-plus-EMA method, corresponding to approximate discrimination performances of 84%, 89%, 91%, and 97%, respectively. The simulations further showed preserved separation among the dry and moisture conditions for insulation thicknesses of 1–5 cm and pipe radii of 0.5–4 cm. Experimental proof-of-concept measurements were conducted using a dry reference and localized water volumes of 1, 40, and 120 ml, corresponding to nominal volumetric moisture fractions of approximately 0.031%, 1.228%, and 3.684%, respectively. Measurements were performed at 5, 15, and 30 cm standoff distances with ten repeated acquisitions per prepared condition. At 5 and 15 cm, the dry, low-, medium-, and severe-moisture conditions exhibited non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals, indicating clear separation of their estimated mean responses. At 30 cm, the 1 ml and 40 ml responses substantially overlapped, while the severe-moisture condition remained more distinguishable, demonstrating reduced discrimination between lower moisture levels at increased standoff distance. Overall, the results demonstrate the proof-of-concept feasibility of multi-frequency differential-phase sensing for reducing response ambiguity and distinguishing localized moisture conditions under the investigated configuration, while identifying standoff distance as an important practical factor governing discrimination performance.

Article.Title: A guideline-based artificial intelligence system for hypertension in primary care: a single-arm pre–post study
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Liu Y.; Gou Z.; Xiao Y.; Zhang X.; Zhou B.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension control remains suboptimal in primary care, particularly in resource-constrained settings lacking clinical decision support. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the real-world changes associated with a Guideline-based Digital System (GDS) implemented in a primary care network in Chengdu, China. Data from 515 hypertensive patients with complete baseline and 12-month follow-up data were analyzed. The primary outcome was office blood pressure control rate (< 140/90 mmHg, or < 130/80 mmHg for patients with diabetes); secondary outcomes included changes in systolic/diastolic blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, lipid profiles, and medication adherence (MMAS-8). After 12 months, systolic blood pressure decreased by 8.86 mmHg (95% CI: -10.67~-7.04; P < 0.001) and diastolic by 3.42 mmHg (95% CI: -4.60~-2.26; P < 0.001). The control rate increased from 60.39% to 76.70% (+ 16.31% points; P < 0.001). MMAS-8 score changed from 4.98 to 6.18 ( P < 0.001). Significant changes were also observed in fasting blood glucose and lipid profiles (all P < 0.05). Implementation of the GDS system was associated with pre-post changes in blood pressure control, cardiovascular risk factors, and medication adherence, supporting the potential scalability of AI-based guideline-digitalized systems in resource-constrained primary care settings. However, due to the lack of a control group, high exclusion rate, and potential selection bias, these findings cannot establish causality and should be presented as preliminary associations.

Article.Title: Cholelithiasis and cholecystectomy show modest associations with incident type 2 diabetes and limited predictive value beyond metabolic risk factors
Article.Authors: Kim N.; Kim M.; Jung K.; Lee K.; Baik S.
Article.Abstract: Whether cholelithiasis or cholecystectomy meaningfully increases long-term risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains unclear. We quantified their independent associations with incident T2DM and whether gallstone-related variables add predictive value beyond established metabolic risk factors. Using Korean National Health Insurance Service data (2008–2019; follow-up until 2022), this retrospective matched cohort study included participants with incident cholelithiasis, stratified by cholecystectomy status, propensity score-matched to each other (1:1) and to gallstone-free controls (1:4; total N = 419,250). Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using multivariable logistic regression, and six machine learning models were trained on 24 predictors using Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). During follow-up, 31,441 participants (7.5%) developed T2DM. Cholelithiasis (OR = 1.14) and cholecystectomy (OR = 1.12) were significantly associated with T2DM, though far more weakly than metabolic syndrome (crude OR = 2.76); cholecystectomy was not associated with additional risk compared with unoperated gallstones (OR = 0.98). eXtreme Gradient Boosting achieved the highest discrimination (area under the curve = 0.800). In SHAP analyses, gallstone-related features added minimal predictive value, whereas fasting glucose, body mass index, and triglycerides were the strongest predictors. Both associations were marginal, suggesting that gallstone history adds little to T2DM risk assessment beyond conventional metabolic risk factors.

Article.Title: SViT-UAV: energy-efficient spiking vision transformer for remote sensing scene classification in UAV scenarios
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Zha K.; Ding Y.; Fan L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate scene classification is critical for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) perception, yet achieving high accuracy under strict energy constraints remains challenging for conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs). Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide an energy-efficient event-driven computation paradigm, existing SNN-based methods for remote sensing scene classification still face limitations in capturing both local spatial details and global contextual information. We present SViT-UAV, a hybrid spiking vision transformer that addresses this limitation by integrating convolutional feature encoding with transformer-based global reasoning under a unified spiking paradigm. A spatio-temporal gating block (STGB) is incorporated to enhance spike representations along spatial and temporal dimensions with negligible parameter overhead. Experiments on four widely used UAV-oriented remote sensing scene benchmarks—WHU-RS19, UC-Merced, AID, and NWPU-RESISC45—show that SViT-UAV achieves ANN-competitive classification accuracy with an energy consumption of only 9.58 mJ, substantially outperforming existing SNN methods. These results highlight the effectiveness of SViT-UAV for accurate and energy-efficient remote sensing scene classification in UAV scenarios.

Article.Title: Trajectories of calculated serum osmolality associated with 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Hao S.; Zhang W.; Guo Y.; Hu C.
Article.Abstract: Although calculated serum osmolality is a recognized prognostic marker in critical illness, the clinical relevance of its temporal changes in patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) remains unclear. This study therefore investigated the association between longitudinal calculated serum osmolality trajectories and 28-day mortality in patients with SIC. Using the MIMIC-IV database, we calculated daily serum osmolality values during the first three intensive care unit (ICU) days in patients with SIC. Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was employed to identify distinct calculated serum osmolality trajectories. In a landmark analysis framework, multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied to examine the associations between trajectory groups and 28-day mortality after the 72-hour landmark. To assess the incremental predictive value of calculated serum osmolality trajectories beyond a base model containing conventional baseline clinical covariates, and to compare this incremental value with that of baseline sodium, glucose, and BUN levels, we calculated the C-index, continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Subgroup analyses, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and doubly robust Cox regression were conducted to test the robustness of the findings. Using GBTM, we identified four distinct calculated serum osmolality trajectories: normal-ascending, normal-stable, low-ascending, and high-persistent. Compared with the normal-stable group, the normal-ascending group (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.18–1.52), the low-ascending group (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.25–1.89), and the high-persistent group (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.43–1.99) were associated with a higher 28-day mortality risk after the 72-hour landmark. Adding the trajectory groups modestly improved model performance beyond conventional baseline covariates. However, the comparison used baseline sodium, glucose, and BUN levels, not their dynamic trajectories. Early calculated serum osmolality trajectories are associated with mortality in ICU patients with SIC. Such dynamic calculated serum osmolality patterns may aid in identifying patients at elevated risk. Longitudinal calculated serum osmolality profiles may provide modest incremental predictive value beyond conventional baseline clinical variables.

Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning for predicting residual cancer burden following neoadjuvant therapy in HER2 positive breast cancer: A real-world study
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Lin J.; Zheng C.; Chen Y.; Li C.; Chen Y.; Zhuang J.; Chen Z.; Guo L.; Huang J.; Liu S.; Han H.; Lin S.; Fu C.; Xu C.; Han Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate early prediction of response to neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in HER2-positive breast cancer could support pre-treatment risk stratification. We conducted a retrospective real-world study of 692 patients treated between November 2018 and May 2025 at a tertiary center to develop interpretable machine-learning models for pre-treatment prediction of residual cancer burden (RCB; favorable: RCB 0–I vs. poor: RCB II–III). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator identified nine routinely available predictors, and ten algorithms were trained with 10-fold cross-validation and grid search. Among them, a gradient boosting machine (GBM) achieved the best discrimination in the independent test set (AUC 0.796) with superior calibration and net clinical benefit. SHAP highlighted HER2 status, hormone-receptor status and clinical nodal stage as the strongest contributors, consistent with biological expectations. We implemented a Shiny web application for research and educational use. In a propensity score–matched comparison of trastuzumab–pertuzumab versus trastuzumab– pyrotinib regimens, no significant difference in achieving favorable RCB was observed. This interpretable GBM model shows potential for pre-treatment risk stratification in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer; however, its current predictive performance does not support stand-alone clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: All-dielectric TiO₂ and Poly-Si grating RGB color filters for CMOS image sensor
Article.Authors: El-Metwally A.; Obayya S.; Areed N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract CMOS image sensors require compact color filters, but conventional dye-based filters face fabrication and long-term reliability constraints, while plasmonic designs incur Ohmic loss that limits transmission efficiency. This work numerically investigates an all-dielectric RGB filter set, with no metal in the optical path, combining TiO₂ (blue) and Poly-Si (green, red) gratings on Si₃N₄/SiO₂ spacer stacks. TiO₂ avoids short-wavelength silicon absorption in the blue channel. Fano-lineshape and phase-matching analysis shows that the spacers tune the leaky guided-mode resonance while partially participating in it. Coupled multi-parameter optimization by response-surface modeling defines the blue and green designs. With wavelength-dependent material dispersion, the final designs reach peak transmittances of 83.3% (blue), 83.7% (green), and 79.01% (red), with FWHM of 70.9, 96.1, and 91.6 nm (Q = 6.3, 5.7, and 6.8). The peak wavelength stays within 5 nm of its normal-incidence value for both TE and TM polarization up to 15° (blue) and 20° (green and red). With silicon-photodiode weighting, the filter set covers 21.6% of the sRGB gamut, against 14.7% for the Horie et al. baseline under the same procedure, and gives a mean CIEDE2000 of 2.48 over 24 ColorChecker patches. A potentially CMOS-compatible fabrication route using localized excimer laser annealing and unannealed sputtered TiO₂ is proposed. All results are simulated for infinite periodic arrays.

Article.Title: Multidimensional symptom burden and its associated factors among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a multicenter cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Jabareen M.; Alhroub W.; Fasfoos A.; Amarin H.; Al Ubra R.; Issa J.; Qanaeer B.; Jubran M.; Jbour M.; Dawada H.; Hamoudah I.; Amayra Q.; Al-Sweity M.; Alra’e M.; Hroub M.; Hammad M.
Article.Abstract: Symptom burden is common among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis and can substantially affect physical and psychological well-being. However, evidence on the multidimensional symptom burden and its associated factors among Palestinian hemodialysis patients remains limited. This study assessed symptom burden and its demographic, clinical, and socioeconomic correlates among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis in the West Bank, Palestine. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 418 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis at four dialysis centers in the West Bank between June 1 and August 1, 2026. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and a modified 30-item Chronic Kidney Disease Symptom Burden Index (CKD-SBI), assessing symptom prevalence, distress, severity, and frequency. Internal consistency and known-groups validity were assessed. Multivariable linear regression models were used to examine adjusted associations with total symptom burden and its dimensions. Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors were used in the regression analyses. The mean number of reported symptoms was 10.28 ± 5.90. Fatigue or lack of energy was the most frequent symptom (72.7%), followed by bone or joint pain (53.6%), numbness or tingling (50.2%), difficulty falling asleep (49.0%), and difficulty staying asleep (48.8%). Mean scores were 62.99 ± 41.98 for distress, 62.95 ± 42.49 for severity, and 57.81 ± 37.38 for frequency. The modified 30-item CKD-SBI demonstrated good internal consistency across symptom prevalence, distress, severity, and frequency domains (Cronbach’s α = 0.849–0.872). Symptom dimensions were strongly correlated (ρ = 0.917–0.993; all p < 0.001). In the adjusted total symptom-burden model, older age, previously married status, living with a partner, heart disease, and other comorbid diseases were associated with higher symptom-burden scores, whereas an income of 2,000–4,000 NIS was associated with lower scores. The graft-versus-fistula contrast was attenuated in sensitivity analysis. Palestinian patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis experienced substantial and multidimensional symptom burden, with fatigue, pain, sensory symptoms, and sleep disturbances being particularly common. Older age, selected social and clinical characteristics, and comorbid diseases were associated with greater burden, whereas moderate income was associated with lower burden. Routine multidimensional symptom assessment using reliable instruments may help identify patients requiring targeted clinical and psychosocial support.

Article.Title: Satellite-free BLoS UAV communication using HF skywave and airborne relay networks
Article.Authors: Roy K.; Singh S.; Kumar M.; Deb S.; Das H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-range beyond-line-of-sight (BLoS) communication for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks is challenged by ionospheric variability, fading, and electronic and cyber attacks. This paper develops a satellite-independent architecture for 500–1000 km UAV command and control (C2) that combines high-frequency (HF) skywave propagation with cooperative airborne relays, usable-band-adaptive frequency hopping, direct-sequence spreading, an HF-adapted authenticated-encryption profile, and a zero-trust relay gateway. A system-level simulator couples a physics-guided ionospheric model, which derives the maximum and lowest usable frequencies (MUF and LUF), with correlated relay fading, geometry-based barrage and reactive jamming, direction-finding (DF) exposure, and deadline-aware C2 traffic. Compared with the International Reference Ionosphere, the propagation model is plausibility-checked rather than validated: its MUF deviates by 15.1% by day and 35.9% at night. Over ten independent seeds, the secure configuration under reactive jamming delivers 0.933±0.031 (two relays) and 0.955±0.029 (three relays) of C2 packets within their deadlines, against 0.423±0.049 for a single-relay legacy baseline; for emergency-abort commands the corresponding values are 0.894, 0.937, and 0.456. The secure configuration reduces the modeled DF exposure by 90.1% and accepts no spoofed frames and at most $$7\times 10^{-5}$$ of the replayed frames, whereas the unauthenticated baseline accepts approximately 21% and 23% of them under the modeled adversary. A MUF-aware sliding-window bandit selector improves rate-oriented reward, regret, and delay-tolerant throughput under reactive jamming, with at most a small effect on deadline-compliant C2 delivery, whereas a delayed-CSI greedy selector performs better without jamming and under barrage jamming. The absolute reliability is sensitive to the external-noise level: with 10 dB higher noise, the supported rate falls below the offered C2 load and the two-relay timely delivery drops to 0.263, although the secure configuration remains better than the baseline. The results therefore support low-rate, satellite-independent UAV C2 under the stated model assumptions.

Article.Title: Designing mRNA vaccine against porcine getah virus using E2 protein with molecular dynamics simulation
Article.Authors: Sapkota S.; Al Arian T.; Bhandari P.; Chalise R.; Hossain D.; Ahmed M.
Article.Abstract: Getah virus is a mosquito-borne alphavirus that can infect multiple hosts, affecting animal well-being and public health because of its zoonotic potential. The main objective of this study was to target the E2 protein, to design an mRNA vaccine as there is no USDA-approved vaccine. In this study, the E2 protein was selected to predict B and T cell epitopes. Molecular docking and Post docking MMGBSA analyses were then conducted between Getah_Vax and TLRs. Codon optimization and immune simulation was also performed. Finally, MD simulation was performed to evaluate the stability of the complexes. The novel vaccine construct (Getah_Vax), consisting various epitopes were selected relying on immunogenic, non-allergenic and non-toxic properties. The Ramachandran plot (94.5%), ERRAT (74.737) and z-score (​-5.38) indicated the good structural quality of Getah_Vax. Molecular docking and post docking MM-GBSA revealed favorable binding scores. According to MD simulation, vaccine, receptors and complexes showed conformational dynamics and stability. Immune simulation indicated the stimulation of adaptive and innate immune systems following immunization. Codon optimization indicated excellent codon usage with CAI (0.9695767653650869). Finally, the vaccine was successfully cloned into the pET-60-DEST™ vector. Getah_Vax is a promising and stable vaccine candidate, but further confirmation through experimental validation is required.

Article.Title: HMCKD-Net: hybrid machine learning for chronic kidney disease screening and probability calibration assessment
Article.Authors: Suman N/A.; Singh Y.; Gulati N.; Moreira F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) can remain undetected until renal damage progresses. HMCKD-Net combines training-only preprocessing, six principal components, four PCA-compressed autoencoder components, and logistic stacking of XGBoost, random forest and LightGBM for CKD classification. The development dataset contains 400 records (320 training; 80 hold-out). On the hold-out, HMCKD-Net achieved AUROC 0.9973 (95% confidence interval 0.9880–1.0000), accuracy 0.9875 and Brier score 0.0146. Hybrid-feature LightGBM achieved the same accuracy and AUROC 0.9967; the additional stacking stage did not establish a meaningful discrimination advantage. The frozen model was separately assessed against the time-to-event-derived EventCKD35 endpoint in 491 Abu Dhabi records. Its reported AUROC was 0.6786 and Brier score 0.3133. Seven of ten selected predictors were unavailable as measured external inputs. An independent assessment of baseline eGFR on the same public external records gave AUROC 0.8370 and average precision 0.4159, exceeding the reported transported discrimination. The external test involves predictor and endpoint shift and is not conventional external validation of the CKD classification model. The results emphasize leakage control, transparent comparisons, calibration assessment and the need for same-task prospective evaluation before clinical application.

Article.Title: Structural and functional connectivity change of cerebellum in Parkinson’s disease with cognitive impairment: a multimodal MRI study
Article.Authors: Qiao Y.; Ren Y.; Chen X.; Wang Y.; Yu M.; Ma X.; Qiao B.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a prevalent and disabling non-motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD). While the role of the cerebellum in cognition is increasingly recognised, its specific contribution to Parkinson’s disease with cognitive impairment (PD-CI) remains poorly defined. This study investigates alterations in cerebellar subregion architecture and cerebellar-cortical connectivity in patients with PD-CI.We enrolled 35 PD-CI patients, 31 cognitively normal PD patients (PD-NC), and 33 healthy controls (HCs). Grey matter volume (GMV) of 28 cerebellar subregions was quantified using voxel-based morphometry with the SUIT atlas. For cerebellar regions showing differences in GMV, dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) with the cerebral cortex was calculated using the sliding window method.Compared to PD-NC, PD-CI patients exhibited pronounced reductions in GMV in posterior cerebellar ‘cognitive’ hubs, including the right Crus I and left Crus II. DFC analysis revealed abnormal connections between these key nodes within the default mode network (DMN) and subcortical nuclei (SBN). Further correlation analyses revealed that abnormal GMV and dFC indices in these regions were significantly correlated with cognitive-related rating scale scores.Our research reveals focal cerebellar atrophy and impaired cerebellum-cortex dynamic connectivity in patients with PD-CI. This provides a preliminary, circuit-level model of the potential pathophysiological mechanisms of PD-CI. It identifies potential neuroimaging targets that could be useful for future validation and therapeutic development.

Article.Title: Integrated multi-omics analyses reveal candidate astrocytic signalling responses shared across pharmacologically distinct psychoactive compounds
Article.Authors: Greener M.; Horder J.; Martin S.; King M.; Martínez‐Jarquín S.; Kim D.; Finelli M.; Sheridan G.; Benest A.; Storr S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Astrocytes are increasingly recognised as contributors to the neuroadaptations that underlie substance use disorders, but most studies examine single drugs, and it remains unclear whether pharmacologically distinct substances engage a common astrocytic response. Here, we apply an integrated multi-omic approach to two human astrocyte-like cell lines, KNS-42 and SVG-A, exposed to ethanol, Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol, cocaine, morphine or psilocin, to profile the transcriptome in both cell lines and the phosphoproteome and metabolome in KNS-42. Both cell lines expressed transcripts for several canonical targets of these compounds, including opioid (OPRM1, OPRD1) receptors and serotonin receptors and the astrocytic glutamate transporter SLC1A3, with the cannabinoid receptor CN1 and the glutamate transporter SLCA2 detected in KNS-42 cells only. KNS-42 and SVG-A diverged transcriptionally, as expected for developmentally distinct astrocytes. Despite this, the chemically distinct psychoactive compounds converged on a small set of candidate molecular features: seven phosphoproteins (including vimentin, MAP1B and AHNAK) and thirteen putatively annotated metabolite features, each representing greater overlap than expected by chance. The shared response across multi-omic layers implicated cytoskeletal and Rho-GTPase signalling, cell-cycle regulation and, putatively, nucleotide catabolism. Our findings indicate that distinct psychoactive compounds may converge on a small number of astrocytic processes and we provide an interactive data application for exploring astrocytic responses to psychoactive compounds.

Article.Title: Soil physicochemical heterogeneity and bacterial community patterns across depths and sites at the Erhongqu check dam on the ​ Loess Plateau
Article.Authors: Jia B.; Han Y.; Zhang J.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: To address the unclear relationship between soil physicochemical properties and microbial community characteristics in check dams on the Loess Plateau, this study took the Erhongqu medium-sized check dam in Ordos City, Inner Mongolia, as the research object, and revealed the soil physicochemical properties, microbial community structural characteristics, and their interactions at different depths across seven sampling sites in the upper, middle, and lower reaches of the dam. The results showed that particle size, electrical conductivity (EC), soil water content (SWC), soil organic carbon (SOC), total nitrogen (TN), and available phosphorus (AP) differed significantly with depth, and that multiple physicochemical properties, especially EC, SWC, SOC, and TN, exhibited significant positive correlations. Soil pH ranged from 7.17 to 8.49. Electrical conductivity, water content, organic carbon, and total nitrogen in the surface soil were higher than those in the middle and deep layers, showing a decreasing trend with increasing depth. The bacterial community was mainly composed of Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Acidobacteriota. Although the bacterial community showed no significant depth- or position-related differences or environmental correlations, this study provides a comprehensive perspective on the links between physicochemical gradients and bacterial community patterns. Based on this single-dam case study, the associations among hydrodynamic sedimentary sorting, soil physicochemical gradients, and bacterial community structure along horizontal and vertical gradients were revealed, providing a basis for exploring microbial responses to sediment heterogeneity in check dam systems.

Article.Title: Changes in academic procrastination and engagement following assertiveness training among nursing students during pediatric clinical education
Article.Authors: Soltanian M.; Keyhanmehr S.; Shirazi Z.; Ghaemmaghami P.; Tavakoli P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nursing students often experience fear and anxiety during pediatric clinical placements, which may increase academic procrastination and reduce engagement in learning activities. This single-group, uncontrolled pre-post study examined changes in academic procrastination and academic engagement following an assertiveness training program among undergraduate nursing students during pediatric clinical education. A single-group clinical trial was conducted with 36 students selected through convenience sampling. After providing informed consent, students with low assertiveness were identified using the Gambrill and Richey Assertiveness Questionnaire. Participants completed Solomon and Rothblum’s Academic Procrastination Questionnaire and Gunuçe and Kuzu’s Academic Engagement Questionnaire, then attended two four-hour assertiveness-training workshops. Academic procrastination and engagement were assessed before the intervention, immediately afterward, and one month later. The mean procrastination score decreased from 85.4 ± 11.3 at baseline to 77.6 ± 11.4 immediately afterward and to 74.4 ± 11.9 at one month ( P < 0.001). The mean engagement score increased from 152.5 ± 35.3 to 165.9 ± 33.8 and 175.0 ± 33.5 at the same time points ( P < 0.001). These findings indicate that participation in the assertiveness training program was temporally associated with reductions in procrastination and increases in engagement. Because the design lacked a control group, randomization, and blinding, these changes cannot be confidently attributed to the intervention alone, and causal claims are not warranted at this stage.

Article.Title: A configurable VR spacecraft simulator enhanced with HMI data in microgravity
Article.Authors: Krishnan A.; Kharsade M.; Saren S.; Vishwakarma H.; Thalal S.; Saluja K.; Mitra M.; Biswas P.
Article.Abstract: Simulators play a crucial role in the aerospace industry, ranging from simple desktop models to advanced Level D simulators used for pilot training. While most non-gaming simulators focus on crew training and client illustration, there is a notable deficiency in simulators that assist with cockpit design. Current methods primarily utilize standard CAD/CAE software alongside Digital Human Models, which often lack adequate functionality for comprehensive human factor evaluation for design optimization. This paper introduces a configurable Virtual Reality Spacecraft Simulator that is calibrated with data from microgravity studies from the International Space Station collected from two astronauts. The VR simulator is also integrated with human factor evaluation suit like eye gaze and EEG trackers. The proposed VR simulator implements immersive task execution in scenarios such as deorbiting manoeuvres, emergency responses, and robotic arm operations, while also comparing task completion times in microgravity conditions. Three applications of the VR spacecraft simulator are presented to highlight prospectives uses for informed design decisions.

Article.Title: Glycemic control and associated factors among adults with type 2 diabetes managed in primary care in Vietnam: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Tuan T.; Nguyen D.; Nguyen P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Good blood glucose control reduces the risk of complications in type 2 diabetes, but how often it is achieved in primary-level hospitals in Vietnam, where most patients are managed, is unclear. We studied 802 adults with type 2 diabetes attending follow-up visits at a primary-level hospital in Ho Chi Minh City between May and December 2023, and collected clinical, behavioral, and treatment data by interview and from medical records. Factors associated with poor control, defined as glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) of 7.0% or above, were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Only 38.3% of participants reached the HbA1c target. After adjustment, poor control was more likely in women (adjusted odds ratio 1.74, 95% confidence interval 1.18–2.57), in participants with a diabetes duration of 5– < 10 years (1.86, 1.27–2.72) or ≥ 10 years (2.54, 1.71–3.78) compared with < 5 years, in those who had missed a medication dose in the preceding week (1.71, 1.15–2.55), and in those treated with oral agents plus insulin (3.82, 2.29–6.37); it was less likely in participants aged 60 years or older (0.68, 0.48–0.96). Body mass index, family history, smoking, and alcohol use showed no association. Since missed doses are modifiable, supporting medication adherence may be a priority for primary care.

Article.Title: Solar UV-induced space weathering of volatile-rich C-complex asteroids suggested by rapid spectral changes in carbonaceous chondrites
Article.Authors: Furukawa S.; Okada T.; Yasuda Y.; Hiroi T.; Sasaki S.; Egashira Y.; Kaiden H.; Yada T.; Ishizaki T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation has been proposed as a potentially important driver of early-stage space weathering on airless bodies. Here, we investigate near- to mid-infrared reflectance spectral changes induced by UV irradiation equivalent to several days to months at 1 AU using three carbonaceous chondrites: the hydrated Tagish Lake (C2-ung.) meteorite, the particularly fresh Oued Chebeika 002 (CI1) meteorite, and the relatively anhydrous Allende (CV3) meteorite. Tagish Lake (C2-ung.) and Oued Chebeika 002 (CI1) exhibit weakening of the 2.7 μm OH absorption band and a long-wavelength shift and broadening of the Reststrahlen Band (RB), indicating that solar UV irradiation could modify OH-bearing phases and mineral structures in hydrated carbonaceous materials on relatively short timescales. In contrast, Allende (CV3) shows comparatively limited spectral changes, suggesting that the magnitude and nature of UV-induced alteration depend on hydration state. These results suggest that solar UV radiation could modify the surface spectral properties of volatile-rich carbonaceous asteroids on much shorter timescales than other space weathering processes at 1 AU. Our findings highlight the importance of considering UV-induced alteration when interpreting remote-sensing observations and returned samples. Further systematic experiments using diverse carbonaceous materials and complementary analytical approaches are needed to constrain its physicochemical mechanisms.

Article.Title: Associations of physical activity and frailty with nutritional status among community-dwelling older adults in Southern Vietnam: a community-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Doan Duy T.; Le Thi Thanh H.; Pham Nhat T.; Truong Thanh A.; Le Thi H.
Article.Abstract: Malnutrition, low physical activity, and frailty are interrelated geriatric conditions that may contribute to functional decline among older adults. Evidence from community settings in Vietnam remains limited. This study examined the associations of physical activity and frailty with nutritional status among community-dwelling older adults in southern Vietnam. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 660 adults aged ≥ 60 years in Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Nutritional status was assessed using the full Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA). For regression analyses, the binary outcome was defined as an MNA score < 24 (at risk of malnutrition or malnourished), combining participants at risk of malnutrition (MNA 17–23.5) and those with established malnutrition (MNA < 17). Physical activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire–Short Form, and frailty was assessed using a modified Fried phenotype. Poisson regression with robust variance was used to estimate prevalence ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for sociodemographic and health-related covariates. The mean age was 66.8 ± 4.6 years, and 67.0% of the participants were women. Among all the participants, 44.4% had an MNA score < 24 (at risk of malnutrition or malnourished), 48.5% had low physical activity, 59.5% were prefrail, and 30.0% were frail. In the adjusted models, compared with low physical activity, moderate physical activity was associated with a lower prevalence of an MNA score < 24 (adjusted prevalence ratio 0.83, 95% confidence interval 0.70–0.99). Prefrailty and frailty were associated with a higher prevalence of MNA score < 24 (at risk of malnutrition or malnourished), with adjusted prevalence ratios of 2.01 (95% confidence interval 1.19–3.38) and 3.17 (95% confidence interval 1.87–5.37), respectively. An MNA score < 24 (at risk of malnutrition or malnourished) was common among community-dwelling older adults in southern Vietnam and was strongly associated with frailty. Integrating nutritional assessments with simple evaluations of physical activity and frailty may help identify older adults who are at risk of malnutrition or malnourished at the primary care level.

Article.Title: Fuzzy logic-based safety integrity level determination for multi-initiating-event scenarios: a case study of an ammonia primary reformer
Article.Authors: Haghgoo M.; Shasadeghi M.; Safarinejadian B.
Article.Abstract: The conventional Risk Graph method, widely used by technology licensors for Safety Integrity Level (SIL) allocation, often yields ambiguous or erroneous results when applied to scenarios involving multiple independent Initiating Events (IEs). This study validates a quantitative fuzzy Risk Graph framework through an industrial case study, demonstrating its ability to correct specific miscalculations inherent in traditional licensor assessments. Probabilistic input intervals are fuzzified and processed via a Mamdani inference system calibrated to reproduce conventional SIL assignments at category centers while explicitly aggregating multi-IE Demand Rates. Applied to 13 Safety Instrumented Functions (SIF) in a 3000-TPD ammonia plant’s synthesis-gas unit, the framework was benchmarked against the original licensor’s baseline. Results show that the conventional method misallocated SIL in four critical cases: underestimating SIL from 2 to 3 for two SIFs exposed to seven and eight IEs. These findings confirm that the proposed fuzzy approach provides a more accurate, discriminative, and uncertainty-aware basis for SIL determination in complex multi-IE scenarios where traditional qualitative methods fail.

Article.Title: Instruction-related neural predictors of placebo and nocebo efficacy
Article.Authors: Lambertz L.; Heeren S.; Wittkamp C.; Wolf M.; Rose M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Verbal instructions about treatments shape placebo and nocebo effects across experimental and clinical contexts. In experimental paradigms, they are routinely followed by conditioning procedures to enhance treatment expectations. Yet, the neural effects following verbal instructions and their relation to learning during conditioning are frequently overlooked. We investigated how nocebo-placebo instructions shape the neural processing of corresponding visual cues and how these neural responses relate to subsequent conditioning efficacy. In an fMRI paradigm, participants ( n = 51) received verbal instructions linking visual cues to sham assessments of low (placebo) or high (nocebo) pain sensitivity, thereby evoking expectations. Following instructions, participants viewed these visual cues in the explicit absence of pain prior to a conditioning phase. The neural processing of the different cues in the visual system was directly related to the individual conditioning learning rate, in line with instruction-based allocation of meaning and salience. This emphasizes that instructions extend their influence beyond initial expectations, shaping learning processes throughout the course of treatment. Comparing the cue processing before and after the treatment revealed altered neural processing of visual cues across several areas, consistent with experience-based updating of cue meanings. These distinct neural responses persisted outside the context of pain, suggesting that placebo and nocebo cues retain their expectation-evoking capacity beyond the original treatment context.

Article.Title: Squamous cell carcinoma involving the uropygial gland region in related captive budgerigars: a clinicopathological case series
Article.Authors: de Castro Eloy L.; Linhares M.; dos Santos A.; Pequeno W.; Silva J.; Quillas L.; Ubiali D.; Carvalho L.; Lucena R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) involving the uropygial gland region is an uncommon epithelial malignancy in birds, and detailed descriptions in budgerigars remain limited. This study describes uropygial gland region lesions in six full-sibling captive budgerigars maintained under the same husbandry conditions. All birds had proliferative, nodular, verrucous, ulcerated or exudative lesions in the uropygial gland region. Fine-needle aspiration cytology was performed in all six birds and supported an epithelial neoplasm, showing atypical epithelial cells with anisocytosis, anisokaryosis, perinuclear vacuolation, atypical keratinization and mitotic figures. Radiographs obtained from four birds showed soft-tissue opacities in the dorsocaudal body region, consistent with enlargement of the uropygial gland region, without detectable mineralisation or bone involvement. SCC was histologically confirmed in five sampled birds, including one necropsied bird and four surgically excised lesions; one additional bird had compatible clinical and cytological findings but died before tissue sampling. Histology revealed infiltrative, non-encapsulated neoplasms composed of pleomorphic squamous epithelial cells forming keratin pearls and invading adjacent dermis and skeletal muscles. Cytokeratin AE1/AE3 immunolabeling supported epithelial differentiation. Three surgically treated birds were followed for up to eight months without owner-reported or clinically detected local recurrence. These findings highlight the value of integrating clinical examination, cytology, imaging, histopathology and immunohistochemistry for diagnosing SCC involving the uropygial gland region in budgerigars.

Article.Title: Evaluation of sensing response of H2S sensing materials toward H2S molecules using artificial neural network and response surface methodology
Article.Authors: Hamidipour F.; Masoumi H.; Rahbar-Kelishami A.
Article.Abstract: In this work, temperatures of 25 to 275 °C, times of 6.5 to 4091 s, concentrations of 0.0001 to 400 ppm, and surface areas of 17.11 to 223.6 m 2 /g were simulated through artificial neural network (ANN) and response surface methodology (RSM) for predicting the H 2 S sensor response. The number of collected data points was 548. The optimum values of each parameter were calculated using RSM. The optimized variables were 97.11 ℃ of temperature, 2785 s of response time, 259.77 ppm of H 2 S concentration, and a surface area of 197.78 m 2 /g. Regarding RSM, the dependency of sensor response on the parameters is quadratic. The multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and radial basis function (RBF) models were used in the ANN. Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation algorithm (trainlm) was used. The numbers of neurons of 49 and 29 were considered for the first and second hidden layers for the MLP network, respectively. The number of neurons was calculated as 198 for the RBF model. The R 2 values of MLP, RBF, and RSM models were attained at 0.9897, 0.9894, and 0.9821, respectively. Also, the % AARD values of the MLP and RBF models are 17.33 and 66.20, respectively. It is concluded that the MLP model could predict the sensor response better than the RBF model. The transfer function for the first and second hidden layers was tansig in the MLP model. The best MSE validation performance of the MLP and RBF networks was 0.001061 and 0.001486 at 69 and 198 epochs, respectively. The MLP 3D diagram also proved that H₂S sensing materials such as Fe 2 O 3 -Ba 0.99 Ce 0.01 TiO 71 , SnCl 2 , and Fe-600 are good candidates for sensing the H 2 S molecules.

Article.Title: Research on precursory signal identification and strength prediction of granite failure under uniaxial compression
Article.Authors: Hu J.; Zhuang Y.; Li C.; Yan P.; Li E.; Zhang E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aiming at the problems of strong suddenness of brittle failure of granite, difficulty in identifying precursor signals, and insufficient generalization ability of strength prediction models, granite from Longchang, Sichuan Province is taken as the research object, and a coupled stress-acoustic monitoring test under uniaxial compression is carried out. Based on the test results, the sensitivity of acoustic emission (AE) characteristic parameters in warning rock failure is quantitatively evaluated by the defined dimensionless parameter precursor response ratio (PRR). Then, the grey relational analysis (GRA) method is used to optimize the strength influencing factors, and compressive strength prediction models are constructed based on LSBoost, Transformer, and KELM algorithms, respectively. The model accuracy, robustness, and generalization ability are evaluated by multiple indicators, and the full-range local dependence method is introduced to conduct parameter sensitivity analysis. The results show that the PRR value of AE absolute energy is the highest (the maximum, average, and cumulative values are 309.77, 246.12, and 349.21, respectively), indicating that absolute energy is the most sensitive precursor indicator for identifying granite failure. A two-level early warning threshold based on sliding-window average PRR is preliminarily established, which provides a quantitative reference for damage state identification of granite specimens. Duration and rise time are precursor indicators with moderate sensitivity and can be used as auxiliary verification parameters, while the signal-to-noise ratios of ringing count and amplitude are low and thus should not be used alone as warning parameters. Under small-sample nonlinear datasets, the LSBoost model shows the best accuracy and robustness, with a test set coefficient of determination ( R ²) of 0.84 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.34. In contrast, the Transformer model demonstrates good anti-overfitting ability, while the KELM model is prone to overfitting. Young’s modulus is identified as the core driving factor determining the uniaxial compressive strength of granite, with a resulting strength fluctuation range of 22.59 MPa. Local dependence analysis shows that Young’s modulus has a positively correlated step effect. The research findings provide methodological reference and theoretical support for rapid strength assessment and failure precursor warning of granite rock masses, and lay a foundation for the transformation from laboratory research to engineering non-destructive testing scenarios.

Article.Title: Associations between cumulative physical activity and dementia risk in middle-aged and older adults
Article.Authors: Kim E.; Jang Y.; Kim H.; Hurh K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical activity is associated with lower dementia risk; however, most studies do not capture cumulative volume, long-term duration, or longitudinal activity changes. This nationwide nested case–control study used data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service–Health Screening Cohort (2002–2019). Adults aged 40–79 years without dementia were followed for incident dementia from 2009 to 2019. Physical activity was measured as metabolic equivalent task-minutes per week (MET-min/week) at each health examination and accumulated across repeated examinations. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression with multivariable adjustment and lag periods of 2–10 years to evaluate reverse causation. Included were 28,653 dementia cases and 143,265 matched controls (mean age, 76.7 years). Greater cumulative physical activity volume (odds ratio [OR] per 100,000 MET-min, 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.95–0.96) and longer active duration were associated with lower dementia risk. Associations were clearest for Alzheimer’s dementia and, for cumulative volume, persisted across lag periods, although some estimates were imprecise at the 10-year lag. Sustained, or even intermittent, physical activity in midlife and later adulthood was associated with lower dementia risk; residual confounding and reverse causation cannot be excluded.

Article.Title: Deep karst systems as indicators of transtensional deformation: evidence for a releasing step-over geometry in the Alburni Massif (Italy)
Article.Authors: Cafaro S.; Schiattarella M.
Article.Abstract: In the southern Apennines, neotectonic evolution is driven by the interaction between strike-slip and extensional regimes. These processes fragmented the Mesozoic carbonate platforms into structurally distinct massifs. Within this regional framework, the Alburni Massif is a key area for investigating tectonic controls on deep speleogenesis. We focus on the massif’s Central Zone, which hosts the highest concentration of cave entrances and the most developed cave systems. Our analysis combines a previously established map-scale morpholineament dataset with outcrop-scale fracture characterisation, spatial statistics, and multi-parameter cave morphometry. The datasets indicate heterogeneous brittle deformation across the massif, with local clusters of morpholineaments and spatially variable fracturing within the Central Zone. Spatial statistical analyses reveal a significant association (p < 0.001) between cave distribution and sectors marked by high morpholineament intensity. The interpolated Karst Intensity Index (KII) provides complementary information on cave-system development, with several high-KII nuclei occurring within the Central Zone. Underground conduits display predominantly E-W to WNW–ESE orientations that only partly correspond to the dominant NW–SE structural trend. This mismatch suggests that deep speleogenesis did not simply follow the dominant surface structural trend, but may reflect the combined influence of faults, joints, and stratigraphic discontinuities. Site-scale structural survey documents multimodal fracture networks and local variations in brittle deformation, suggesting that the Central Zone pattern is consistent with a transtensional releasing step-over interpretation. In this sector, distributed brittle deformation may have enhanced rock-mass permeability and groundwater circulation. Deep karst systems may therefore preserve evidence of the deformation architecture of the massif.

Article.Title: The relationship between perceived organizational support and occupational stress: a cross-sectional study among clinical nurses in China
Article.Authors: Sun L.; Chen X.; Li Z.; Hu H.; Zhu P.; Sheng Y.; Chen Y.; Cao J.; Kou J.
Article.Abstract: Clinical nurses experience long-term high occupational stress, which has been associated with burnout and turnover and may be associated with impaired nursing quality. Perceived organizational support has been associated with lower stress, while psychological capital and emotional intelligence have been proposed as internal psychological resources. To examine the association between perceived organizational support and occupational stress among clinical nurses, and to test the serial mediating roles of psychological capital and emotional intelligence in this association, thereby providing empirical evidence that may inform future longitudinal or interventional studies aimed at examining factors associated with nurses’ occupational stress and optimizing nursing management. A cross-sectional descriptive design was used. From September to November 2025, 511 clinical nurses from a tertiary hospital in Henan were recruited by convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Perceived Organizational Support Scale, Nurse Psychological Capital Scale, Emotional Intelligence Scale, and Core Occupational Stress Scale. SPSS and Model 6 of the PROCESS v4.1 macro were used for data analysis and serial mediation analysis. Perceived organizational support was significantly positively correlated with psychological capital and emotional intelligence ( r = 0.701, 0.519, P < 0.01) and significantly negatively correlated with occupational stress ( r = -0.661, P < 0.01). The direct association between perceived organizational support and occupational stress was significant ( β = -0.348, P < 0.001), accounting for 59% of the total effect. Psychological capital and emotional intelligence mediated the association between perceived organizational support and occupational stress both independently and sequentially, with a total indirect effect of 41%. Psychological capital and emotional intelligence play a serial mediating role in the association between perceived organizational support and occupational stress among clinical nurses. Perceived organizational support was associated with occupational stress both directly and indirectly through the serial mediating pathways of psychological capital and emotional intelligence. These constructs may represent potential targets for future longitudinal or interventional studies.

Article.Title: Predicting and interpreting the irradiation-induced tensile behavior of fast reactor cladding using explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Kim D.; Yeo S.; Kim J.; Jeon W.; Oh J.; Lee Y.
Article.Abstract: HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels are promising candidates for advanced nuclear fuel cladding. In this study, 1,590 tensile test data points of 9–12Cr ferritic/martensitic (FM) steels were collected to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting irradiation-induced changes in the tensile properties of HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod). Regression models were evaluated after Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization using test-set evaluation and k -fold cross-validation (CV). Extreme gradient boosting (XGB) exhibited the best predictive performance; however, an artificial neural network (ANN) was selected for its continuous response, physical consistency, and stable representation of irradiation-dependent trends. Using independent experimental data, the ANN yielded mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 6.26 ± 0.47% for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and 10.69 ± 0.46% for yield strength (YS). The ANN model predicted the YS across irradiation conditions and showed that the irradiation-induced increase in YS for HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels saturated at 5–10 displacements per atom (dpa). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) method, quantified the contributions of dpa and irradiation temperature, revealing that irradiation temperature has a greater overall influence on the predicted YS. These results provide both reliable property predictions and physical insights into the effects of irradiation conditions.

Article.Title: Approval is not session binding in identity-provider-mediated push authentication
Article.Authors: Jubur M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract National-scale digital identity systems increasingly use push-based authentication across multiple relying parties. This study examines single sign-on–style, identity-provider-mediated push authentication, in which a relying party delegates authentication to an external identity provider and the user approves a request on a registered device. Using Nafath, Saudi Arabia’s national authentication platform, we introduce a channel-separated assessment framework that distinguishes approval/assertion security from session establishment. We analyzed 1,782 valid Select-and-Confirm notifications from 1,820 controlled captures. The results showed high entropy, balanced option placement, and slight exact-value deviation from uniformity, but no tested offline prediction model met a predefined improvement over baseline attacker strategies. We then conducted a two-phase controlled reverse-proxy relay assessment using researcher-controlled accounts and devices. In Phase 1, approval of a current request number enabled attacker-side session establishment when post-approval artifacts were transferable across browser environments. In a later post-disclosure reassessment, Phase 2 no longer reproduced cross-browser artifact transfer, and approval notifications displayed additional requester and context information; the internal cause could not be determined. These findings show that identifier-based initiation, approval context, and session binding are distinct security problems. Number matching should therefore be combined with origin-bound or sender-constrained mechanisms, including WebAuthn/passkeys, OAuth 2.0 mutual TLS, and DPoP.

Article.Title: DALightNet achieves real time rain and haze removal on edge devices
Article.Authors: Li J.; Liang Y.; Yuan M.; Deng F.; Fang K.; He G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Rain and haze degrade image visibility and contrast, while computationally intensive restoration methods remain challenging to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices. Aims: This study proposes DA-LightNet, a lightweight image restoration framework designed to balance restoration quality and computational efficiency for unified rain and haze removal. Methods: DA-LightNet integrates degradation-aware feature modulation with an efficient restoration backbone. The degradation-aware feature modulation (DAFM) module adaptively recalibrates intermediate feature representations, while the lightweight architecture reduces computational requirements. The model is evaluated on the LHP-Rain and LMHaze datasets and compared with representative CNN-based, transformer-based, all-in-one, and state-space restoration methods. Results: DA-LightNet achieves a PSNR of 33.28 dB and an SSIM of 0.9267 on LHP-Rain, and a PSNR of 17.61 dB and an SSIM of 0.7536 on LMHaze. Its average PSNR and SSIM across the two datasets are 25.45 dB and 0.8402, respectively. With 4.6 million parameters and 21.5 GFLOPs, DA-LightNet achieves an inference speed of $$34.8 \pm 3.1$$ FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano at an input resolution of 512 × 512 pixels and a batch size of 1. Under the evaluated configuration, the model meets the 30-FPS real-time inference criterion. Conclusion: DA-LightNet provides a favorable balance between restoration quality and computational efficiency. Its low computational complexity and measured inference speed demonstrate its potential for real-time rain and haze removal on the evaluated edge platform.

Article.Title: Combined effects of Co and Mo contents on precipitation behavior and creep resistance in 9Cr-based martensitic steels
Article.Authors: Park B.; Seok W.; Kim S.; Park I.; Shin J.; Ramachandran D.; Jang J.; Kang N.
Article.Abstract: The combined effects of Co and Mo contents on the microstructural evolution and creep resistance of two 9Cr-based martensitic steels were investigated. The 1.0Co–0.1Mo and 2.0Co–0.7Mo alloys were subjected to identical heat treatments and creep testing at 630 °C and 145 MPa. One long-term creep-rupture specimen was tested for each composition, and the measured rupture lives were 5,979 and 10,384 h for the 1.0Co–0.1Mo and 2.0Co–0.7Mo specimens, respectively. After solution treatment, local transmission electron microscopy observations revealed differences in the residual carbide populations of the two alloys. After tempering, the M₂₃C₆ area fractions were 2.46% and 3.25%, with average particle sizes of 70.3 and 75.2 nm, respectively. During prolonged creep, M₂₃C₆ in the 1.0Co–0.1Mo alloy coarsened to 101.5 nm, whereas that in the 2.0Co–0.7Mo alloy remained comparatively stable at 78.1 nm. A similar difference was observed for the Laves phase, which increased from approximately 80.0 to 157.3 nm in the 1.0Co–0.1Mo alloy but only from 98.2 to 102.2 nm in the 2.0Co–0.7Mo alloy. These observations indicate greater long-term stability of the precipitate microstructure in the higher-Co/Mo composition. Because Co and Mo contents were varied simultaneously, their individual contributions cannot be independently separated, and the observed behavior is therefore interpreted as a combined compositional effect.

Article.Title: Cross-platform analysis of endothelial transcriptomic changes associated with diabetes
Article.Authors: Luo Y.; Huang K.; Sun J.; Law K.; Malhi N.; Chen M.; Qi M.; Tang X.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is an early hallmark of diabetes and a key driver of diabetic vascular complications. However, the transcriptional responses of endothelial cells (ECs) to diabetic stress across different vascular beds and the extent to which cultured ECs recapitulate these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we profiled transcriptomes of mesenteric arterial intima from non-diabetic, pre-diabetic, and type 2 diabetic donors and compared diabetes-associated differentially expressed genes with those identified in five cultured human EC subtypes, including umbilical vein, aortic, dermal microvascular, lymphatic microvascular, and liver sinusoidal ECs, exposed to high glucose and TNF-α. Human arterial intima and cultured ECs shared multiple diabetes-associated stress-response and vascular remodeling programs, with metabolic alterations more prominent in human donor ECs and inflammatory and immune pathways more pronounced in cultured ECs. Despite these context-dependent differences, we identified a subset of genes, including GGT5 , HTR1B , SLC25A34-AS1 , and LINC01235, consistently downregulated in both human donor samples and multiple cultured EC subtypes under diabetic conditions. Functional analyses demonstrated that suppression of these genes impaired angiogenesis while promoting endothelial inflammation and senescence, recapitulating key features of endothelial dysfunction. Together, our findings reveal both shared and context-dependent endothelial responses to diabetes and provide a transcriptomic resource for studying disease-associated EC changes and identifying candidate regulators of diabetes-associated endothelial dysfunction.

Article.Title: Seasonal mismatch between bottlenose dolphin abundance and vocal activity reflects prey dynamics in southeastern U.S. estuaries
Article.Authors: Marian A.; Blake L.; Miller A.; Willford G.; McClellan W.; Jones P.; DuBois I.; Dunning H.; Ballenger J.; Montie E.
Article.Abstract: Tamanend’s bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops erebennus ) are apex predators whose abundance and behavior may reflect seasonality in estuarine food webs. We investigated relationships among primary productivity, prey dynamics, and dolphin abundance and vocalizations using nine years of data from two estuaries in Beaufort County, South Carolina, United States. Datasets included (i) chlorophyll a and nutrient concentrations, (ii) fish abundance and community composition from seines and trammel nets, (iii) fish calling intensity scores from passive acoustic monitoring, (iv) dolphin abundance from visual surveys, and (v) dolphin vocalizations. Primary productivity, fish abundance, fish calling intensity scores, and dolphin abundance generally increased with water temperature and peaked during spring and summer, accompanied by seasonal restructuring of the fish community. In contrast, dolphin vocalizations peaked during winter, despite lower dolphin abundance. Elevated winter vocalizations suggest dolphins increase echolocation and social signaling when prey is scarce, likely reflecting greater foraging effort and coordination. These findings demonstrate that seasonal prey dynamics influence dolphin acoustic behavior, and acoustic detections should not be interpreted as a simple proxy for dolphin numbers without ecological and behavioral context.

Article.Title: Risk factors of adverse drug reactions in surgical and critical care patients at adverse drug reaction monitoring centre in South India
Article.Authors: Nair D.; Chintalapati A.; Ramesh M.
Article.Abstract: Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) accounts for 5% of hospital admissions with problems related to drugs, and 10–20% of inpatients. Risk factors of ADRs in surgical and critical care patients remain inadequately characterized although they are vulnerable due to several factors including polypharmacy, physiological stress, and complex treatment regimens. Therefore, this study aimed to determine Risk factors of ADRs in these patients. A prospective observational study was carried out at adverse drug reaction monitoring centre, tertiary care hospital, Mysuru, India. Patients aged ≥ 18 years admitted to general surgery and critical care units were enrolled for a period of 1 year. Association of ADR with population characteristics such as patient demographics, clinical factors, disease severity, hospital course, and type of admission, were assessed. Among 4,548 admissions, 376 patients were screened and 223 patients were included, of whom 70 (31.4%) patients experienced ADRs. Geriatric (47.08%) and male (68.2%) patients were predominant. A significant association with ADR was seen with elective surgery (OR 13.6, 95% CI 6.8–27), females (OR 3, 95% CI 1.6–5.4), one comorbidity (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3–4.4)) total LOS of 4–7 days (OR 3.5, 95% CI 1.9–6.5) patients undergoing > 2 procedures (OR 23.5, 95% CI 8.6–64.5), and those with ICU length of stay (LOS) 4–7 days (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.2–3.8). The multivariate model with these Risk factors demonstrated fair to good discrimination (AUC 0.85, 95% CI: 0.71–0.89). The multivariate analysis identified female gender (AOR 3.0, 95% CI 1.4–6.4), elective surgery (AOR 5.2, 95% CI 2.1–12.8), and undergoing more than two surgical procedures (AOR 8.2, 95% CI 2.0-33.6) as independent predictors of ADRs in surgical and critical care patients. Although one comorbidity and LOS categories showed significant associations in univariate analyses, these did not remain statistically significant after multivariable adjustment. The model showed fair to good discrimination, supporting targeted pharmacovigilance strategies.

Article.Title: Training and validation of an expected goals (xG) model in elite women’s football: a comparison with the data provider’s model
Article.Authors: Iván-Baragaño I.; Niu Z.; Casal C.; Ardá A.; Maneiro R.
Article.Abstract: The objective of this work was to train and validate a probabilistic model of expected goals (xG) in elite women’s football using event records and to compare the model’s performance with that of the data provider. Specifically, the study aimed to identify the variables that show a positive association with an increase in xG. To this end, a total of 3,542 shots (133 matches) from the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2019 and 2023 and the UEFA Women’s EURO 2022 were analysed. The algorithm (Logistic Regression or Random Forest) and its hyperparameters were selected with the Brier Score within a nested, match-grouped 5-fold cross-validation, and an independent leave-one-tournament-out validation was also carried out; Logistic Regression was selected in every case. Penalties were assigned the conversion rate observed in the training data only. Both models were compared on identical shots, and the paired difference in Brier Score (ΔBrier = trained model − provider) was estimated with a match-level bootstrap. For non-penalty shots, the model showed a good correlation with the original StatsBomb data provider model ( r = .800; p <.001) and a Brier Score 0.0736 (95% CI: 0.0659, 0.0815), higher (i.e., worse) than that of the data provider, which was equal to 0.0677 (95% CI: 0.0605, 0.0751), with ΔBrier = + 0.0059 (95% CI: 0.0039, 0.0079; p < .001). The provider’s model also obtained a lower Brier Score in each held-out tournament (ΔBrier from + 0.0032 to + 0.0106) and in the full dataset including penalties (0.0778 vs. 0.0723). The features with the largest contribution to the model output (SHAP values) were distance to goal and shooting angle, followed by body part used, shooting technique, and play pattern. These results support the feasibility, but not the superiority, of an xG model trained exclusively on women’s football data; external validation in other competitions and direct comparisons of female-, male- and mixed-trained models are still required.
