Article.Title: Comparative apoptosis induction by hydatid cyst fluid and laminated layer antigens in HepG2 and A549 cancer cells
Article.Authors: Radfar M.; Tavakoli-Yaraki M.; Jafari M.; Bahreini E.; Alipour M.; Razmjou E.; Rafiei-Sefiddashti R.
Article.Abstract: Identifying novel anti-cancer agents is a major focus of current research. Several studies have reported an inverse association between certain parasitic infections and cancer development, potentially due to shared antigens and cross-reactive immune responses. This study investigated the anti-cancer effects of hydatid cyst fluid (HCF) and laminated layer (LL) antigens from Echinococcus granulosus in human lung (A549) and liver (HepG2) cancer cell lines. Crude HCF and LL antigens were isolated from hydatid cysts collected from naturally infected sheep. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay following treatment with varying antigen concentrations and exposure times. Apoptosis, necrosis, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production were analyzed by flow cytometry, and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were measured to assess oxidative stress. The scratch assay was performed to evaluate the migratory capacity of A549 cells. HCF antigen significantly reduced the viability of A549 and HepG2 cells at 400 µg/mL after 48 h, and flow cytometric analysis confirmed increased apoptosis. This effect was associated with increased ROS generation and decreased SOD activity. LL antigen also inhibited cell growth at 660 and 1100 µg/mL after 48 h; however, only HepG2 cells showed a significant increase in apoptosis. Oxidative stress markers showed variable responses depending on cell type and antigen concentration. Both HCF and LL antigens demonstrated anti-proliferative activity against cancer cells, albeit through divergent underlying mechanisms. These findings underscore the potential of hydatid cyst-derived antigens as promising reservoirs for novel anti-cancer therapeutics and warrant further investigation into their precise molecular pathways and clinical applications.

Article.Title: Environmental impacts and lighting energy use efficiency of hydroponically grown leafy greens under different light intensities and nutrient solution concentrations
Article.Authors: Simonavičiūtė A.; Vaštakaitė–Kairienė V.; Savickas D.
Article.Abstract: Hydroponic production under artificial LED lighting requires a balance between biomass yield and resource inputs. We evaluated radish, fennel and basil microgreens, and lettuce and basil at baby-leaf and technical-maturity stages, under three photosynthetic photon flux densities (200, 250 and 300 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; 12 h photoperiod) and three mineral nutrient-solution concentrations (base, 1.5-fold and approximately two-thirds of the base). For the microgreen experiments, biomass and lighting energy use efficiency (LEUE) were analysed using two-way ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD test, whereas treatment differences in DWC-grown lettuce and basil were evaluated descriptively. A restricted life cycle assessment quantified lighting-electricity and macronutrient-fertilizer burdens per kilogram of fresh biomass. Within individual crop–stage experiments, maximum-to-minimum fresh-yield ratios ranged from approximately 1.24 to 2.46, and fresh-weight-based LEUE ratios from 1.72 to 3.89. Radish microgreens grown at 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ with a 1.5-fold nutrient-solution concentration had the highest observed fresh-weight-based LEUE and lowest modelled global warming potential (GWP) among the assessed systems. Lettuce and basil at technical maturity had lower GWP per kilogram than at the baby-leaf stage, without establishing lower total burdens per cultivation cycle. The findings indicate treatment-specific productivity–electricity trade-offs under the tested conditions rather than a universal cultivation optimum.

Article.Title: Line curvilinearity–masculinity associations on packaging influence expected taste intensity of green tea
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Zhang H.; Hu B.; You S.; Thoo A.; Spence C.; Wang M.; Zheng L.
Article.Abstract: Visual cues on product packaging play an important role in shaping consumers’ sensory expectations before they consume. Although line curvilinearity is commonly used in green tea packaging, little research has examined how angular versus rounded lines influence expected taste intensity or the psychological mechanisms. This research aims to examine how line curvilinearity ​(Angular vs. Rounded) affects expected taste intensity in green tea packaging. It also investigates the roles of perceived femininity and masculinity in this relationship. Three online experiments were conducted with 458 participants recruited through the Credamo platform in China. Participants viewed green tea packaging featuring angular or rounded lines and rated expected taste intensity, perceived masculinity and femininity, and willingness to purchase. Across three studies, angular lines (vs. rounded lines) were associated with higher expected taste intensity. They were also associated with higher perceived masculinity ( B = 1.66, p < .001 in S1; B = 2.21, p < .001 in S2; B = 1.76, p < .001 in S3) and lower perceived femininity ( B = -1.32, p < .001 in S1; B = -1.72, p < .001 in S2; B = -1.25, p < .001 in S3). Perceived masculinity consistently accounted statistically for the relationship between line curvilinearity and expected taste intensity, whereas perceived femininity did not. Expected taste intensity was also positively associated with willingness to purchase. This research offers insights into how tea enterprises can optimize their packaging design. This research examines how a common design element in green tea packaging (Angular vs. Rounded lines) influences consumers’ expected taste intensity and highlights the unique mediating role of perceived masculinity.

Article.Title: Combination of FGF13 and THBS4 expression in PBMCs as a novel screening biomarker for prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Bhummaphan N.; Pumpong P.; Chinnakarn T.; Mutirangura A.; Watcharanurak P.; Puttipanyalears C.
Article.Abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most frequent cause of death from cancer among men. Despite advances in screening for early detection, many patients continue to present with advanced stage. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive, and highly accurate diagnostic platform for screening. This study aimed to identify potential novel biomarkers for prostate cancer screening by analyzing PBMC gene expression profiles. Gene expression datasets of prostate cancer patients, including GSE153514, GSE16120, and GSE46602, were collected from the NCBI-GEO database. Quantitative RT-PCR was performed to observe FGF13 and THBS4 expression in PBMCs. FGF13 and THBS4 expression levels were significantly higher in the prostate cancer group than in the healthy group ( p < 0.0001). FGF13 combination with THBS4 had the greatest discriminative capacity with 99.1% sensitivity 84.8% specificity. The mRNA expression of FGF13 and THBS4 in PBMCs cocultured with prostate cancer cells ( N = 10) was significantly increased at 72 h ( p = 0.047 and p = 0.0063, respectively). We also performed a gene expression analysis correlated with cancer stages and found that FGF13 and THBS4 were highly expressed in the early stages of cancer ( p < 0.0001). FGF13 ( p < 0.0001) and THBS4 ( p = 0.0011) exhibited highly specific mRNA expression in prostate cancer among various types of cancers. Our study found that FGF13 in combination with THBS4 revealed higher efficiency than current screening tools and should be pursued as a potential screening biomarker.

Article.Title: Role of precursor pH in structural ordering, surface evolution, and magnetic behavior of glycine-assisted auto-combustion synthesized Li–Cr ferrite nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Kondhare R.; Atkare S.; Dhage V.; Labis J.; Shirsath S.; Fulari A.; Mane M.; Bhosale A.
Article.Abstract: Nominal Li 0.5 Cr 0.5 Fe 2 O 4 nanoparticles were synthesized by a glycine-assisted sol-gel auto-combustion route at precursor pH values of 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 to determine how pH-dependent precursor chemistry affects phase ordering, microstructure, porosity, and magnetism. Thermogravimetric analysis and differential scanning calorimetry (TGA/DSC) showed that the principal nitrate-glycine decomposition occurs between approximately 200 and 400 °C. The gradual high-temperature upturn in several TG traces was treated cautiously as an apparent mass gain arising mainly from baseline/buoyancy drift, while minor oxidation by residual oxygen could not be excluded. Rietveld refinement using the ordered lithium-ferrite structural model P4 3 32 described a predominant ordered cubic spinel phase; the weak (210) superstructure reflection was consistent with cation ordering rather than a separate impurity. The Scherrer crystallite size varied non-monotonically from 16.19 to 35.65 nm, while the Williamson-Hall slopes yielded apparent compressive microstrain magnitudes of 14.5–49.3 × 10 − 4 . Field-emission scanning electron microscopy showed strongly agglomerated particles with image-derived mean sizes of approximately 33.00–37.50 nm. The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area decreased overall from 25.243 to 10.301 m 2 g − 1 despite the smaller high-pH crystallites, indicating that aggregation and loss of accessible pore volume dominated the nitrogen-accessible surface area. All samples exhibited soft ferrimagnetic behavior, with M s = 20.09–21.09 emu g − 1 and H c = 89.93–124.1 Oe. The pH 7 sample showed the highest M s , whereas pH 9 produced the smallest crystallites, largest microstrain magnitude, lowest surface area, and highest H c . Electron spin resonance linewidths varied non-monotonically from 161.8 to 212.0 mT. Overall, precursor pH acts through coupled changes in combustion, nucleation, defect structure, surface accessibility, and A-B sublattice interactions; however, the post-calcination lithium content and exact cation occupancies were not independently determined.

Article.Title: Levels of Nogo-B in patients with diabetic foot infection: a retrospective study
Article.Authors: Irakoze L.; Manirakiza A.; Bizimana P.; Nduwayezu J.; Niyomugisha C.; Banderembako P.; Manirakiza M.; Nisubire D.; Nkengurutse L.; Chen G.; Cheng Q.
Article.Abstract: Nogo-B has been implicated in many metabolic diseases including diabetes mellitus. It is still unclear whether the levels of serum Nogo-B decrease in patients with diabetic foot infection (DF). We retrospectively collected sera of T2DM patients with or without DF from the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University. Human Nogo-B ELISA Kit (Jiubang Biotechnology Cat number: QZ-17338) was used to determine serum Nogo-B levels in all the samples. Graphpad and SPSS version 27 software were used for statistical analyses. T2DM patients with DF displayed lower levels of Nogo-B than those without DF (18.66 ± 4.16 ng/ml versus 26.77 ± 3.27 ng/ml, respectively; P < 0.001). In addition, lower levels of Nogo-B were associated with DF [OR (95% CI) = 0.528 (0.436–0.640), P < 0.001]. This association was independent of other factors associated with DF [OR (95% CI) = 0.413 (0.244–0.702), P = 0.001). The results of our study highlight the association of lower levels of Nogo-B with DF. Our findings describe associations and cannot establish causation. Future studies should be conducted to verify or confirm our findings.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence-based cyber-resilient architecture of wearable fitness and sports performance monitoring under adversarial sensor attacks
Article.Authors: Bi F.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled wearable systems provide continuous activity, physiological, and sports-performance monitoring; however, their increasing dependence on connected sensors, wireless communication, edge computing, and learned decision models introduces vulnerabilities to sensor spoofing, data tampering, poisoning, unauthorized access, communication disruption, and adversarial manipulation. This study proposes a cyber-resilient edge–cloud AI architecture for wearable fitness and sports monitoring in which security is incorporated into the sensing-to-decision pipeline rather than treated as an external network-level component. A reproducible adversarial threat-modelling procedure is further introduced in which malicious samples are generated only after participant-level partitioning, preventing leakage between clean and attacked observations. The threat model covers sensor spoofing, data tampering, replay, packet-loss/denial-of-service, training-data poisoning, unauthorized access, and gradient-based FGSM and PGD adversarial perturbations. The framework is evaluated on the PAMAP2 multimodal wearable dataset and the real-world WISDM activity dataset using subject-independent validation. Activity-recognition accuracy reaches 96.8% on PAMAP2 and 95.9% on WISDM, compared with 93.4% and 92.1%, respectively, for the reported baseline. For cyber-threat detection, the framework achieves 97.1% overall accuracy, 0.97 precision, 0.97 recall, and 0.97 F1-score, with a false-positive rate of 0.02 and approximately 24 ms detection latency. The hybrid edge–cloud configuration reduces mean processing latency from 128 ms for cloud-only processing to 87 ms, corresponding to an approximately 32% reduction, while maintaining scalability beyond edge-only execution. Under severe simulated tampering at 70% data integrity, activity accuracy remains 93.8% and threat detection 95.2%, with only a 2.5% performance reduction.

Article.Title: Development of a web-based prediction model for depression risk among caregivers of disabled older adults
Article.Authors: Bai T.; Ma L.; Yang Y.; Luo S.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Efforts to look after disabled older adults are frequently physically exhausting and psychologically distressing. This may result in depressive symptoms in the caregivers. Help can be given earlier if the recognition of those at risk is performed. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 1370 caregivers from three tertiary hospitals. Depressive symptoms were measured using the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9). To identify candidate predictors, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm were applied. Variables identified by both methods were entered into multivariate logistic regression analysis to construct the final model. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Thirteen predictors were included in the final model. Alcohol use, insomnia, extended caregiving hours, family conflict, and a low poverty–income ratio increased the odds of depression, whereas higher educational attainment and stronger social support appeared to be protective. The model showed strong discriminatory ability (AUC 0.945, 95% CI 0.929–0.960 in the training set; 0.945, 95% CI 0.923–0.966 in the test set). Calibration was good (Brier = 0.074 and 0.077; Hosmer–Lemeshow, P = 0.470 and 0.914), and DCA demonstrated a clear net clinical advantage. The nomogram provides a practical approach for identifying caregivers at risk of depression. Its use in clinical and community settings may facilitate early detection and prevention of depressive symptoms.

Article.Title: Early post-stimulus posterior parietal connectivity is associated with response time during visual object categorization
Article.Authors: Arun Y.; Soni S.; Priya M.; Kumar S.; Tayade P.; Kaur S.; Sharma R.; Muthukrishnan S.
Article.Abstract: Visual object categorization is a rapid and complex cognitive process involving hierarchical processing across distributed cortical networks. However, the role of pre-stimulus and early post-stimulus network dynamics on behavioral performance remains unclear. The present study aimed to investigate the role of directed interactions among cortical regions before and during the early stages of visual processing in determining behavioral performance during a complex visual categorization task. Cortical interactions were examined in 50 healthy participants using high-density 128-channel electroencephalography (HD-EEG) and compared with baseline resting-state activity with eyes open. To maintain the consistent 100 ms window length required for robust frequency-domain cross-spectral estimation via the Phase Slope Index (PSI), effective connectivity was evaluated across two overlapping task windows: a peri-stimulus window (–50 to + 50 ms) centered at stimulus onset, and a post-stimulus window (0 to + 100 ms). Source localization and effective connectivity were analyzed using exact low-resolution electromagnetic tomography (eLORETA) and phase slope index (PSI), respectively, and visualized with BrainNet Viewer. During the peri-stimulus period, a significant outflow from visual, default-mode, and somato-motor networks to the limbic network was observed. Subsequently, sustained interactions of somato-motor network with limbic and other higher-order neural networks were evident. Participants with higher category-pooled PSI estimates for BA5 outflow within the somatomotor network tended to exhibit longer response times during inanimate object trials. Sustained interaction of regions of somatomotor network support the higher-order processing during visual object categorization.

Article.Title: Dual-energy CT for differentiating gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors from leiomyomas
Article.Authors: Wu L.; Liu S.; Chen X.; Zhang Y.; Wei L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To evaluate the diagnostic value and reproducibility of quantitative dual-source dual-energy CT (dsDECT) parameters for differentiating 0.5–4.0 cm gastric GISTs from leiomyomas. This prospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed gastric GISTs (n = 61) or leiomyomas (n = 42) measuring 0.5–4.0 cm who underwent contrast-enhanced dsDECT between August 2025 and June 2026. Quantitative parameters, including IC, NIC, λHU, and Z, were compared between the two groups. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to determine whether VP IC remained independently associated with GIST after adjustment for relevant clinical and conventional imaging characteristics. VP parameters showed the most consistent discriminatory differences. VP IC, VP NIC, VP λHU, and VP Z were significantly higher in GISTs than in leiomyomas after false discovery rate correction. Among all evaluated dsDECT parameters, VP IC exhibited the highest diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.809; 95% CI, 0.723–0.894). At an optimal cutoff of 1.45 mg/mL, VP IC achieved an accuracy of 72.8%, a sensitivity of 62.3%, a specificity of 88.1%, and a positive predictive value of 88.4%. VP IC remained independently associated with GIST after adjustment for age, sex, CT maximum diameter, and growth pattern (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 9.86; 95% CI, 3.73–33.65; P < 0.001). Interobserver agreement for VP IC was excellent (ICC, 0.962; 95% CI, 0.945–0.974). Addition of VP Z did not significantly improve discrimination compared with VP IC alone (AUC, 0.816 vs. 0.809; DeLong P = 0.510). Quantitative dsDECT parameters, VP IC provide reproducible noninvasive information for differentiating gastric GISTs from leiomyomas. VP IC showed moderate sensitivity and high specificity and remained independently associated with GIST after clinical adjustment. External validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Epigenetic biomarkers identify premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle
Article.Authors: Hantsoo L.; Lee R.; Epperson C.; Kaminsky Z.; Payne J.
Article.Abstract: Reproductive depression includes postpartum depression (PPD) and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). We tested whether epigenetic biomarkers predictive of PPD are also associated with PMDD. Female participants completed prospective daily rating of symptoms over two menstrual cycles to confirm control or PMDD status. Whole blood samples were obtained in the follicular or luteal phase. Women with PMDD received the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) sertraline 50 mg during the luteal phase of a subsequent menstrual cycle. Targeted pyrosequencing was carried out at the TTC9B and HP1BP3 genes; we applied our published PPD biomarker linear model to DNA methylation at these genes. The epigenetic biomarkers were assessed in 55 participants ( n = 26 control, 29 PMDD). Luteal but not follicular phase samples generated an AUC of 0.71 (95% CI: 0.49–0.93) to distinguish N = 10 PMDD from N = 18 controls. Model application to luteal phase samples distinguished N = 5 SSRI responders from N = 5 non-responders (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.57–1.00). There was a significant association of follicular phase TTC9B methylation with change in allopregnanolone levels from follicular to luteal phases ( p = 0.02), and the ratio of allopregnanolone to progesterone ( p = 0.040). These analyses indicate that epigenetic biomarkers of PPD are also associated with PMDD, another type of reproductive depression, and are associated with more severe, SSRI-responsive PMDD. Given the small sample sizes in the predictive analyses, these findings should be considered preliminary, but they suggest that epigenetic biomarkers of PPD may also be associated with PMDD and with more severe, SSRI-responsive PMDD.

Article.Title: Growth stages dependent changes in oxalate and nitrate contents as major antinutritional factors in winter leafy vegetables
Article.Authors: Archana G.; Jat G.; Yadav R.; Choudhary H.; Bharadwaj R.; Tomer A.; Sunartiya V.; Singh D.; Saha S.; Mishra G.; Tomar B.
Article.Abstract: Green leafy vegetables (GLVs) are important sources of essential nutrients and bioactive compounds; however, the accumulation of nitrate and oxalate content may influence nutritional quality and dietary safety. The experiment was carried out to assess the variability in nitrate and oxalate contents among 14 varieties of 7 GLVs at three stages (S1, S2, S3) of harvest and to identify genotypes with lower accumulation. Analysis of variance revealed highly significant effects of variety, harvest stage, and variety × stage interaction, whereas replication effects were non-significant. Nitrate content ranged from 25.64 to 364.99 mg/100 g DW, fenugreek cv. Pusa Kasuri (56.16 mg/100 g DW) and Pusa Early Bunching (58.15 mg/100 g DW) showing the lowest mean values, whereas palak cv. Pusa Bharti (299.82 mg/100 g DW) and All Green (289.69 mg/100 g DW) recorded the highest values. Mean nitrate content increased from 129.35 mg/100 g DW at stage 1 to 210.39 mg/100 g DW at stage 3. Oxalate content showed greater variability, ranging from 13.26 to 735.37 mg/100 g DW. Lettuce cultivars, Great Lakes (24.29 mg/100 g DW), Pusa Green Lettuce (25.78 mg/100 g DW), and Pusa Red Lettuce (32.87 mg/100 g DW) exhibited the lowest mean oxalate contents, whereas spinach cv. Virginia Savoy (429.99 mg/100 g DW) and palak cv. Pusa Bharti (411.42 mg/100 g DW) showed the highest accumulation. Mean oxalate content increased from 65.05 mg/100 g DW at stage 1 to 367.84 mg/100 g DW at stage 3. The significant variety × stage interaction emphasized the importance of genotype and harvest stage in nitrate and oxalate accumulation. Early harvesting, at stage 1 and selection of low-accumulating genotypes provide an effective strategy for improving the nutritional quality and dietary safety of GLVs.

Article.Title: LncRNA495810 promotes mitochondrial function and podocyte damage in diabetic nephropathy podocytes by impairing TFAM mRNA stability through hnRNPA2B1-dependent m6A modification
Article.Authors: Li X.; Hao Z.; Wang P.; Du J.; Wu H.; Guo H.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is one of the most common complications of diabetes mellitus. Podocyte injury is tightly linked to the pathogenesis of DN. Recently, increasing evidence suggests that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play key roles in podocyte injury. In this study, we explored the underlying mechanism of a novel lncRNA495810 on podocyte injury in DN. Our results demonstrated that lncRNA495810 was highly expressed in various organs of DN mice, especially in kidney tissue, as well as mouse podocytes induced by high glucose. More importantly, knockdown of lncRNA495810 alleviated high glucose-induced podocyte injury, as evidenced by improved podocyte survival, reduced apoptosis, enhanced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and decreased lipid accumulation. In addition, TFAM may be proved to participate in podocyte injury induced by lncRNA495810. Mechanistically, lncRNA495810 could bind to hnRNPA2B1, thereby preventing m 6 A modification of TFAM mRNA mediated by hnRNPA2B1 and reducing the stability of TFAM mRNA, which may contribute to mitochondrial dysfunction and podocyte injury. In summary, these data reveal a new mechanism of TFAM mRNA expression, provide a novel target and new insight for the treatment of diabetic nephropathy in the future.

Article.Title: Women’s empowerment and maternal–newborn continuum of care completion through timely antenatal care initiation in conflict-affected Tigray region, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Abebe G.; Bayray A.; Medhanyie A.; Gebregziabher M.; George M.; Gebrehiwet T.
Article.Abstract: Women’s empowerment is a core priority principle of the World Health Organisation (WHO) to improve access to and coverage of maternal health services and ensure a continuum of care. The study aimed sto assess the status of Maternal–Newborn Continuum-of-Care Completion (COC) and to investigate the relationship between women’s empowerment and completion of the entire continuum of Maternal–Newborn care, accounting for the potential mediating effect of timely antenatal care. A prospective follow-up study design was implemented involving 1,258 pregnant women between August 2024 and May 2025. A multistage cluster sampling techniques was used to select study participants. Mediation analysis was performed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the direct, indirect and total effect of women’s empowerment through timely initiation of antenatal care on completion of the continuum of maternal health services. In this study, we found that only 14.97% (95% CI: 12.99%–17.1%) of women completed all stages of the maternal continuum of care. When the latest WHO recommendation of eight antenatal care (ANC) contacts was applied, the proportion of women who achieved full completion of the continuum dropped sharply to 1.93% (95% CI: 1.23%–2.85%). Women’s empowerment also demonstrated significant direct and total effects on CoC completion. Compared with low empowerment, average and high empowerment were significantly associated with higher odds of CoC completion, with direct effects of Exp(β) = 2.32 (95% CI: 1.17–3.48) and 1.67 (95% CI: 1.01–2.41), respectively, and total effects of 2.62 (95% CI: 1.13–4.12) and 2.07 (95% CI: 1.01–3.13), respectively. However, the indirect effects through timely initiation of the first ANC contact were not statistically significant for either average (Exp[β] = 1.13; 95% CI: 0.75–1.50) or high empowerment (Exp[β] = 1.24; 95% CI: 0.92–1.54), providing insufficient evidence of mediation. The study highlights the need for maternal and newborn health programmes to prioritise women’s empowerment alongside timely ANC initiation to improve the completion of the continuum of care, recognizing that early ANC initiation alone does not explain this association.

Article.Title: Quantity and quality of AI innovation drive renewable energy consumption in Chinese cities
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Gan J.; Liu B.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Renewable energy is central to the green transition and to UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 11, and 13. Using a balanced panel of 279 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2007–2021, this study distinguishes AI quantity innovation (AI1, AI patent applications, capturing the rate of knowledge creation) from AI quality innovation (AI2, authorized AI patents, capturing inventions that pass substantive examination for novelty, inventiveness and industrial applicability) and examines how each relates to renewable energy consumption. Two-way fixed-effects models are combined with instrumental-variable (IV) identification, two-step mediation, formal cross-group tests, and moderation analysis. Both AI1 and AI2 are positively associated with renewable energy consumption, and the association survives alternative IPC-based patent measures (AI3/AI4), logarithmic specifications, lagged predictors, place-based policy controls, and IV strategies. Three channels-public science-and-technology effort, R&D investment, and energy utilization efficiency-transmit part of the relationship. Effects differ across regions, resource endowments and city sizes, and are amplified by government support and market competition. The results inform differentiated, SDG-oriented AI-renewable policy.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of soil and sediment nematode communities across fluvial and lacustrine environments in a Mediterranean coastal Wetland, Central Chile
Article.Authors: Bastidas B.; Sulbaran-Bracho Y.; Morales-Montero P.; Gaete-Toro J.; Aponte H.; Rojas C.; San-Blas E.
Article.Abstract: Mediterranean coastal environments are increasingly exposed to environmental pressures, yet their ecological responses remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the structure and functionality of nematode communities in fluvial and lacustrine soils and sediments from a coastal wetland and its tributary in central Chile. Nematode communities responded to spatial gradients and seasonal variation, primarily associated with changes in pH, water content, total organic carbon, and available phosphorus. An interannual decline in richness, evenness, and functional integrity was detected, together with a shift toward stress-tolerant and generalist guilds, suggesting increasing ecosystem degradation associated with nutrient depletion and potential agricultural inputs from surrounding areas. Functional indices, including the Sigma Maturity Index (ΣMI), together with metabolic footprints, effectively captured both immediate and cumulative community responses to environmental disturbance, revealing pronounced functional transitions and trophic simplification in fluvial systems. These changes were characterized by the collapse of fungal-mediated decomposition channels and the increasing dominance of opportunistic taxa, indicating reduced ecological redundancy and resilience. Overall, the results highlight the value of nematodes as effective bioindicators for monitoring ecological processes and support the integration of biological indicators into restoration and sustainable management strategies for Mediterranean coastal ecosystems under environmental change.

Article.Title: Association between serum eosinophil cationic protein and coronary artery calcification burden: an observational study
Article.Authors: Gao F.; Tian R.; Hu G.; Zhang B.; Xu H.; Wu J.; Gao B.; Liu Q.; Ye J.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of global mortality, and coronary artery calcification (CAC) is a key marker of atherosclerotic burden. Eosinophil cationic protein (ECP), a granule protein released by activated eosinophils, has been implicated in inflammatory processes. However, its role in CAC and cardiovascular events (CVE) remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the expression of eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) between patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and healthy controls, and to explore the correlations of ECP levels with coronary artery calcification (CAC) and cardiovascular events (CVE). This analysis included 151 participants, comprising 86 patients with coronary artery calcification (CAC) and 65 non-CAC controls. ECP, IL-4 and IL-13 were measured by ELISA; CAC burden was quantified by Agatston score. Cardiovascular events (CVEs) and follow-up durations were available only in CAC patients. We compared clinical characteristics, examined Spearman correlations, fitted prespecified ordinary least-squares models, and assessed CVE using Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier/log-rank methods. The normality of continuous variables was assessed by histogram and Shapiro-Wilk test. Non-normally distributed variables were described as median (IQR) and non-parametric tests were applied. ECP was higher in CAC patients than controls (median [IQR] 11.09 (8.50, 28.69) vs. 3.81 (3.06, 5.95) ng/mL; P < 0.001). IL-4 ( P = 0.915) and IL-13 ( P = 0.128) were not different. Among CAC patients, ECP correlated strongly with CACS (Spearman rho = 0.984, P < 0.001). In robust multivariable analysis of log(1 + CACS), ECP (β = 0.547, P < 0.001) and age (β = 0.375, P = 0.006) remained associated with CACS. Thirty-nine of 86 CAC patients experienced recorded cardiovascular events. In the adjusted Cox model ( N = 81, events = 36), ECP was not associated with event hazard (1.063 (95% CI 0.830–1.361; P = 0.629)), whereas NT-proBNP (1.026 (95% CI 1.002–1.051; P = 0.032)) and hypertension (0.457 (95% CI 0.219–0.954; P = 0.037)) showed exploratory adjusted associations. Primary log-rank tests for ECP median and the three CACS categories were not significant ( P = 0.070 and P = 0.096). The level of ECP is closely associated with the CAC burden, however, in the pre-set Cox regression model after adjusting for covariates, no independent prognostic value of ECP was found for cardiovascular events. The exploratory study conducted post-hoc in this study revealed that there was a statistically significant difference in cardiovascular events between the severe and non-severe CAC subgroups.

Article.Title: Rock burst prevention and control method for irregular section coal pillars under thick hard roof with multiple mining disturbances
Article.Authors: Gao F.; Chen J.; Wu X.; Shi K.; Hao X.; Zhang L.; Ma X.; Hu H.; Yin D.; Dong W.
Article.Abstract: Regarding the prevention and control of rock bursts in irregular coal pillars in thick coal seams, with the No. 5316 working face of Shandong Mine as the engineering background, a combination of on-site investigation, theoretical analysis, numerical simulation and on-site industrial tests was adopted to systematically study the stress and impact instability evolution law of irregular coal pillars in working faces with thick and hard roofs. The rock burst risk in the irregular coal pillar area under mining influence was systematically evaluated, and a coal pillar rock burst prevention and control method coordinating overlying strata structure optimization and stress control was proposed. The results show that the expressions of vertical stress and horizontal stress borne by coal pillars with different widths are derived, and the evolution law of stress in irregular coal pillars is studied through examples; the stability of irregular coal pillars under mining disturbance is systematically analyzed, and the energy-induced mechanism of impact instability of coal pillars is discussed and analyzed. Based on the Dempster-Shafer evidence Theory, an overall evaluation method for coal pillar rock burst risk is proposed, which integrates monitoring information from microseismic, online stress and drill cuttings methods within the same time window, and the early warning values for rock burst risk in irregular coal pillars are determined. In combination with the characteristics of rock burst risk areas in irregular coal pillars, a coal pillar rock burst prevention and control method that coordinates the optimization of overlying strata structure of thick and hard roof with stress control is proposed. The results of on-site industrial tests show that after the implementation of comprehensive prevention and control measures, there were no abnormal conditions in stress and working resistance of hydraulic supports in the irregular coal pillar area during the mining process of the working face. The rock burst prevention and control effect is good, which ensures the safe and efficient mining of the working face.

Article.Title: Intelligent selection of UAV based robotic sensing systems for precision agriculture a CRITIC SYAI decision framework
Article.Authors: Li M.; Qi Y.; Niu J.
Article.Abstract: The selection of sensing configuration for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) application in precision agriculture is a critical decision-making problem since available systems have varying spatial resolution, geolocation accuracy, spectral responses, payload capacity, and availability of data products. In this study, an integrated multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) framework called the CRITIC-SYAI framework is developed to evaluate the UAV-based robotic sensing configurations quantitatively by using the quantitative information of the MuST-C agricultural dataset. The four sensing configurations are evaluated against six criteria: ground sampling distance, mean geolocation error, spectral band richness, sensor payload weight, native sensor resolution and diversity of data products released. CRITIC method is applied to compute data-driven criterion weights, and the SYAI method is applied to rank the alternatives in relation to each other. The baseline results indicate that the configuration A1 (UAV1-RGB) is the best, with a SYAI score of 0.548802, followed by A4 (UAV3-MS), A3 (UAV3-RGB), and A2 (UAV2-RGB). The ranking agreement and stability are studied through comparative analyses with TOPSIS, VIKOR and WASPAS, alternative weights and parameter-sensitivity analysis. The results show that the ranking results are sensitive to the weighting and aggregation method used, but that the original ranking preference remains constant for the tested parameter of the SYAI. The proposed framework provides a structured approach on agricultural UAV sensing configuration comparison. The results are limited to four alternatives and six evaluation criteria; however, further validation is needed to make the results more widely applicable to other sensing technologies and to other agricultural applications.

Article.Title: Superheated steam processing preserves phytochemicals in turnip greens (Brassica rapa subsp. rapa) while conventional thermal processing differentially affects their bioaccessibility
Article.Authors: Narra F.; Di Matteo G.; Scioli G.; Moreno D.; Ceccanti C.
Article.Abstract: Turnip greens ( Brassica rapa subsp. rapa ) are a source of health-promoting phytochemicals whose retention and bioaccessibility can be affected by thermal processing. This study aimed to assess the retention of phytochemicals and their in vitro bioaccessibility in turnip greens subjected to superheated steaming, boiling, and steaming, providing a comparative evaluation of the effects of heat treatments on the nutritional and nutraceutical properties of this vegetable. Moreover, the application of superheated steaming as a cooking technique for edible leafy vegetables represents the main novelty of the present study. Although superheated steaming has been primarily investigated for food preservation purposes, its potential as an alternative cooking method for leafy vegetables remains relatively unexplored. Compared with S and other thermal treatments, superheated steaming can provide a low-oxygen processing environment, potentially limiting oxidative degradation and promoting the retention of nutritional and nutraceutical compounds. Boiling caused the greatest phytochemical losses, reducing total phenols by 75%, total flavonoids by 69%, and glucobrassicin by 61%. Steaming induced intermediate losses, including a 25% reduction in total phenols, while preserving antioxidant capacity. Conversely, superheated steaming maintained total phenols, total flavonoids, and antioxidant capacity at raw-sample levels, while increasing concentrations of individual flavonoids and the aliphatic glucosinolate gluconapin. Despite its lower phytochemical retention, B increased the bioaccessibility of total phenols (+ 8.9%) and ascorbic acid (approximately threefold compared with raw samples). NMR metabolomics distinguished raw from processed samples and showed that boiling treatment increased the levels of free amino acids compared with raw samples. Overall, superheated steaming was the most effective treatment for preserving the nutraceutical quality of turnip greens, whereas boiling promoted the release of selected compounds during in vitro gastrointestinal digestion. These findings demonstrate that phytochemical retention after thermal processing does not necessarily predict their subsequent bioaccessibility, highlighting the importance of considering both parameters when comparing thermal processing technologies.

Article.Title: Uncertainty quantification reveals the limits of lattice thermal conductivity prediction
Article.Authors: Rayka M.; Naghavi S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of lattice thermal conductivity ( \(\kappa _\textrm{L}\) ) drives thermoelectric materials discovery, yet existing machine learning models rarely quantify the reliability of their predictions. Here, we use evidential neural networks to quantify predictive uncertainty and split it into aleatoric uncertainty (data noise) and epistemic uncertainty (model ignorance). Our analysis reveals that predictions of very low lattice thermal conductivity are inherently unreliable as aleatoric noise dominates the uncertainty, and this noise can rival or even exceed the predicted value itself. High- \(\kappa _\textrm{L}\) materials, by contrast, carry higher epistemic uncertainty, indicating room for improvement by additional training data. Consistent with this observation, adding out-of-distribution samples improves model accuracy by reducing model uncertainty. We further develop an uncertainty-aware screening method that prioritizes predictions with low total uncertainty rather than relying solely on the absolute value of \(\kappa _\textrm{L}\) . This approach recovers a wide range of compositional classes with low \(\kappa _\textrm{L}\) from the Starrydata experimental repository at nearly twice the rate of random selection, thereby narrowing the search space needed to identify promising materials. These results establish evidential neural networks as a practical uncertainty-aware tool for \(\kappa _\textrm{L}\) prediction, enabling reliable candidate screening and guiding data-collection to accelerate materials discovery.

Article.Title: When sensory timing loses precision across sensory modalities in multiple sclerosis
Article.Authors: Bollini A.; Campus C.; Podda J.; Cuturi L.; Bellosta A.; Pedullà L.; Brichetto G.; Tacchino A.; Gori M.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive slowing is a disabling feature of multiple sclerosis (MS), yet the perceptual factors contributing to reduced processing speed remain poorly understood. Multisensory temporal integration supports coherent perception, and reduced temporal precision could increase decisional demands in everyday contexts. We tested cross-sensory temporal order processing in 19 people with MS (PwMS) and 19 healthy controls using three temporal order judgment tasks (audiovisual, audiotactile, visuotactile). Temporal sensitivity was quantified by the just noticeable difference (JND) and point of subjective simultaneity (PSS) from psychometric fits. Trial-level reaction times and binary choices were modelled with hierarchical drift diffusion modelling, with drift rate depending on stimulus onset asynchrony in each sensory pairing. Processing speed was assessed with the Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT). PwMS showed larger JNDs across all modality pairs, indicating reduced temporal precision, while PSS values were comparable between groups. PwMS showed lower sensitivity of drift rate to temporal asynchrony, the computational counterpart of their larger JNDs, whereas the other decision parameters did not differ between groups. Within PwMS, neither temporal precision nor sensitivity to temporal evidence was associated with processing speed, whereas higher SDMT scores were associated with lower boundary separation in exploratory analyses. These findings suggest reduced temporal precision across cross-sensory TOJ conditions in PwMS, whereas the relationship between temporal precision and processing speed requires further investigation.

Article.Title: SAGE-VR: state-aware semantic tile streaming for networked virtual art museums
Article.Authors: Luo H.
Article.Abstract: Networked virtual art museums must preserve fine detail and visual continuity as viewing shifts between navigation and inspection under fluctuating bandwidth. A fixed-horizon gaze policy does not by itself distinguish viewing states or scene roles, or control temporal and cross-tile quality variation. We present SAGE-VR, a state-aware semantic tile-streaming framework that translates causal head–gaze predictions into feasible enhancement requests. Predicted transit, overview, and detail-inspection states determine request horizons; authored scene roles and texture energy combine with future visibility and eccentricity to prioritize artwork and labels. The allocator subtracts outstanding transmission commitments from throughput and decoding budgets before selecting tile levels, with penalties for temporal quality changes and spatial discontinuities. A resident base remains renderable when enhancements arrive late. Paired evaluation comprised 3,750 runs across five methods, five galleries containing Met Open Access artworks, and 30 generated network traces, using held-out predictions on synthetic gaze–head trajectories. At equivalent average decoded application-payload bitrate, SAGE-VR increased viewport peak signal-to-noise ratio from 35.6 to 37.8 dB and reduced late deadline frames from 6.9% to 3.8% relative to predictive gaze foveation. In a separate trajectory-matched ablation collection, removing the temporal penalty increased quality switches from 7.70 to 13.25 per minute, and removing the spatial penalty increased seam energy from 0.266 to 0.441. These controlled replay results support coordinating viewing state, content priority, and outstanding commitments to deliver inspection-relevant detail while controlling continuity; effects on real visitors’ experience require subsequent validation.

Article.Title: Exploring the association between adolescents’ interpersonal competence and loneliness: a parallel mediation analysis of physical activity and positive psychological capital
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Qiu W.; Liu Y.; Guo Y.; Feng L.; Wang Z.; Luo L.; Liu C.; Xiao H.
Article.Abstract: Adolescent loneliness is a complex phenomenon influenced by multiple factors. This study aims to examine the direct and indirect associations between interpersonal competence and loneliness among adolescents. Physical activity and positive psychological capital are included in the model as parallel mediators in a statistical mediation analysis. This study adopted a cross-sectional design. A total of 473 adolescents aged 13 to 18 years were recruited from middle schools in Jiangxi Province, China, using stratified cluster random sampling. The instruments included the Interpersonal Competence Scale (ICS), the Physical Activity Rating Scale-3 (PARS-3), the Positive Psychological Capital Scale (PPCS), and the Loneliness Scale (LS). Data analysis, including correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and mediation analysis, was performed using SPSS 29.0 and AMOS 29.0 software. Correlation analysis revealed that interpersonal competence was significantly correlated with loneliness, physical activity, and positive psychological capital. After we statistically controlled for gender and grade, interpersonal competence showed significant regression relationships with loneliness, physical activity, and positive psychological capital. Parallel mediation analysis revealed that the direct statistical association between interpersonal competence and loneliness was not significant, whereas its indirect statistical association was significant: the indirect association via physical activity was β = -0.023 (95% CI [-0.045, -0.004]), and the indirect association via positive psychological capital was β = -0.387 (95% CI [-0.471, -0.308]). Although the direct statistical association between adolescents’ interpersonal competence and loneliness may be weak, physical activity and positive psychological capital have significant indirect effects on this association. This finding provides a theoretical basis for exploring potential intervention strategies that target loneliness in this population. Future research may consider examining comprehensive approaches that focus simultaneously on the development of habits related to physical activity and the cultivation of positive psychological resources to explore their statistical associations with alleviating loneliness among adolescents.

Article.Title: A two-class clinical signature of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury is recovered in a Chinese intensive care cohort and in MIMIC-IV
Article.Authors: Lu Z.; Yang S.; Li X.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury is heterogeneous, and whether its subphenotypes reflect transferable biology or local case mix is unclear. We analysed adults with Sepsis-3 and sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in a discovery cohort from Zigong, China (n = 282) and in MIMIC-IV v3.1 (n = 14,949). Subphenotypes were derived from eighteen first-day variables by consensus clustering; K = 2 was prespecified in the discovery cohort, whereas in MIMIC-IV the number of classes was left free. A clinically similar two-group partition emerged in MIMIC-IV and, in that cohort, the rule chose K = 2 without prespecification. We therefore describe the classes as a clinical and prognostic signature rather than as discrete biological subphenotypes. The high-risk class showed higher lactate and bilirubin and lower platelet count, and higher 28-day mortality in both cohorts, with adjusted hazard ratios of 2.65 (1.70–4.15) and 1.70 (1.57–1.84). The association was strongest in the first 7 days (2.05, 1.88–2.23) and remained significant in every SOFA stratum. Discrimination improved only modestly when subphenotype was added to age, sex and SOFA (ΔAUC + 0.0154, 95% CI 0.0102–0.0208 at 28 days). Peak temperature was the only discordant variable. The signature was recovered across two health systems but adds little beyond measured severity.

Article.Title: ProactiMate: evaluating LLM-based chatbots for behavior change interventions
Article.Authors: Chen B.; Dethlefs N.
Article.Abstract: This paper explores the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in promoting sustainable behavior, specifically in overcoming procrastination. Despite widespread recognition of the need for sustainable behavior change, individuals often struggle to break free from entrenched, unsustainable habits. LLMs, such as OpenAI’s GPT-4, represent a significant breakthrough in artificial intelligence and are increasingly used in behavior change interventions. This study introduces ProactiMate, a chatbot built using Motivational Interviewing (MI) principles and a Chain of Models approach for prompt engineering, designed to help users combat procrastination. Our research compares four LLMs (GPT-3.5 Turbo, LLaMA-3.2-11B, Qwen-2.5-32B, and SmolLM-1.7B) for output influence on procrastination avoidance, and assesses the impact of hyperparameters (temperature and top-p values) on procrastination avoidance. The findings reveal that GPT-3.5 outperforms other models across various evaluation metrics, and higher temperature and top-p values lead to more effective procrastination avoidance from automatic evaluation. According to expert evaluations, Qwen-2.5 and GPT-3.5 Turbo demonstrated notable effectiveness in fostering user engagement and motivation for addressing procrastination, with GPT-3.5 Turbo particularly distinguished by its capacity to provide strategies that help maintain long-term motivation. The results indicate that GPT performed strongly according to the automatic evaluation metrics, while Qwen achieved the highest average expert evaluation score. This discrepancy highlights that automatic and expert evaluations may capture different aspects of conversational quality and suggests the importance of combining both evaluation approaches when assessing LLM-based conversational behaviour change support. The results provide insights into the most effective ways to use LLMs in chatbot design, offering solutions for future usability testing.

Article.Title: Future dynamics of water-related ecosystem services and their vegetation relationship under climate and land-use changes in the Poyang Lake Basin
Article.Authors: Emiru K.; Wu X.; Ren Y.; Zuo S.; Khan G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Improving water-related ecosystem services (WESs) is vital for sustainable development in regions vulnerable to climate and land-use changes. Integrating PLUS and InVEST models under SSP-RCP scenarios, we project that water yield (WY) will increase by 31.77–52.37% across scenarios, driven primarily by climatic factors, particularly precipitation. Carbon storage (CS) rises by 19.2% under SSP1-2.6 (2080–2100) but declines by 21.28% under SSP5-8.5. Forests and croplands consistently show high NDVI with low WY, reflecting known hydrological differences between forested and non-forested land. In contrast, shrublands and grasslands combine moderate-to-high NDVI with high WY, most favorable under SSP1-2.6. Under the high-emission SSP5-8.5, forests show reduced WY despite sustained high NDVI, while shrublands and grasslands show declining NDVI by the late century, suggesting vegetative stress. WY and CS also diverge spatially across land-use types, with land-use change driving this spatial divergence even as basin-wide WY magnitude remains climate-dominated; forests show the highest carbon density but lowest WY, most pronounced under SSP1-2.6 and comparatively muted under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. As NDVI and carbon density were derived from land-use-specific parametrizations, these patterns are presented as descriptive land-use associations rather than statistically inferred trade-offs. Coordinated land-use and water management strategies are needed to safeguard ecosystem services, particularly under high-emission trajectories.

Article.Title: Pozzolanic, filler, and biomineralization effects in lightweight foamed concrete bricks for optimizing compressive strength and carbonation resistance using definitive screening design
Article.Authors: Alhudaibi M.; Alshalif A.; Al-Shaeer H.; Amran M.; Abkar M.; Alqurashi A.; Alruwaythi O.; Rashid R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Foamed concrete (FC) is widely recognized for its low density and thermal insulation properties; however, its high porosity and limited durability restrict broader structural applications, while the environmental burden associated with Portland cement production necessitates the development of sustainable construction materials. This study developed bio-foamed concrete (B-FC) incorporating rice husk ash (RHA; 1%, 3%, and 5%), eggshell powder (ESP; 1%, 3%, and 5%), coffee waste (CW; 1%, 2%, and 3%), and Bacillus tequilensis (3 × 10⁵, 3 × 10⁶, and 3 × 10⁷ cells/mL) to enhance mechanical performance and carbonation resistance through the combined effects of biomineralization and pozzolanic mechanisms. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on Definitive Screening Design (DSD) was employed to evaluate and explore the effects of bacterial concentration, RHA, ESP, and CW on compressive strength and carbonation depth. The microstructural characteristics and phase characteristics of the developed B-FC were investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) after 28 days of atmospheric curing. The highest experimentally measured compressive strength of 37.77 MPa was obtained at 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL of B. tequilensis, 3% ESP, 3% RHA, and 2% CW, representing a 75.37% improvement compared with FC. The minimum experimentally measured carbonation depth of 1.11 mm was obtained at 3 × 10⁵ cells/mL of B. tequilensis, 5% ESP, 5% RHA, and 1% CW, corresponding to a 50% reduction relative to FC. The RSM models predicted a maximum compressive strength of 44.45 MPa and a minimum carbonation depth of 0.3072 mm at the selected factor combinations. These values were model predictions rather than experimentally measured results, as the optimized combinations were not included among the 13 experimental runs. SEM observations showed differences in pore morphology and matrix continuity among the investigated specimens, together with visible solid deposits of different morphologies. XRD analysis revealed differences in diffraction patterns, indicating variations in the crystalline characteristics of the specimens. The improved compressive strength and reduced measured carbonation depth may be associated with the combined contributions of pozzolanic reactions, filler-related effects, and biomineralization in the developed B-FC under the investigated conditions. Furthermore, the partial replacement of Portland cement with RHA and the valorization of agricultural by-products, including ESP and CW, demonstrate the potential for agricultural-waste valorization and reduced reliance on conventional cementitious materials. Overall, integrating microbial technology with agricultural waste-derived supplementary materials shows promise for enhancing the mechanical and carbonation-related performance of B-FC under the investigated conditions.

Article.Title: Rheological characteristics of fine-grained tailings slurry paste
Article.Authors: Xianqing W.; Ze L.; Ruicheng W.; Yujie T.; Yanchuan R.; Ze Z.; Peng L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract During the pumping procedure of fine-grained tailings slurry, its rheological properties are crucial for flow regime analysis and pipeline transmission pressure loss calculation in pipeline transportation. This paper employs a variable shear rate loading method to experimentally investigate the rheological characteristics of fine-grained tailings slurry at different concentrations. The results indicate that the plastic viscosity of fine-grained tailings slurry decreases with increasing shear rate following a negative exponential function, while the yield stress increases with increasing shear rate following a positive exponential function; both tend to stabilize after acting for a certain period. The minimum plastic viscosity μ min occurs when the internal structure of the slurry reaches dynamic equilibrium; the maximum plastic viscosity μ max is observed when the internal structure is undisturbed by external load, corresponding to the yield stress τ 0max associated with the dynamic equilibrium of structural breakdown and reformation. All three parameters gradually increase with the mass concentration of the slurry. An improved exponent Bingham model applicable to fine-grained tailings slurry under variable shear rate flow conditions was established and verified. This model can serve as the rheological equation for fine-grained tailings slurry under variable shear rate loading to describe its rheological behavior and provide a reference for slurry pipeline transportation design.

Article.Title: An augmented reality and robotic rehabilitation platform with prognostic modeling for post-stroke hand spasticity
Article.Authors: Syringas P.; Kakkos I.; Papagiannis G.; Triantafyllou A.; Zestas O.; Tselikas N.; Miloulis S.; Vezakis I.; Matsopoulos G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Post-stroke hand impairment can limit manual dexterity and daily activities. We evaluated Rehabotics, an integrated augmented reality (AR) and robotic finger-stretching platform, in a 5-week single-arm intervention. Eighty patients with hand spasticity (time since stroke, 4.53 ± 1.04 months; baseline Ashworth Scale (AS), 2.28 ± 0.62) completed three supervised 30-minute sessions per week, consisting of AR serious-game training followed by robotic finger stretching. Clinical outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention using the AS, Box and Block Test (BBT), and Active Range of Motion (AROM), expressed as Total Active Motion (TAM). We developed a novel exploratory prediction framework using linear mixed-effects models to derive task-specific features from first-session AR task performance, relative to patterns learned from repeated training-cohort data. These AR-derived digital markers were combined with baseline clinical variables in ridge regression to predict post-intervention outcomes. Internal validation used patient-level 5-fold grouped cross-validation (CV), with leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) CV performed as a sensitivity analysis. Following the intervention, AS scores decreased from 2.28 ± 0.62 to 1.34 ± 0.48 ( p = 3.22·10 − 15 ), BBT scores increased from 39.14 ± 2.45 to 45.14 ± 1.57 blocks ( p = 3.47·10 − 50 ), and AROM increased from 147.98 ± 19.27° to 224.61 ± 7.58° ( p = 3.37·10 − 62 ). Our findings reflect within-group pre–post changes in a single-arm cohort and do not establish superiority over conventional physiotherapy. The prediction model achieved R² = 0.615 ± 0.397 for BBT and 0.661 ± 0.271 for AROM, while AS classification achieved 0.850 ± 0.034 accuracy and quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.608 ± 0.187. LOSO CV yielded pooled R² values of 0.636 for BBT and 0.750 for AROM, with AS accuracy of 0.900 and QWK of 0.768, suggesting that early AR-derived markers may provide short-term prognostic information.

Article.Title: Removal of organophosphorus pesticides from aqueous solution using Fe3O4@SiO2/Chitosan nanocomposite functionalized with pomegranate peel extract as a bioadsorbent
Article.Authors: Rezagholizade-shirvan A.; Salehi A.; Nasirifar S.; Abdi-Moghadam Z.; Shamloo E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water contamination by organophosphorus pesticides (OPPs) poses serious threats to both the environment and human health. In this study, Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 /Chitosan–Pomegranate Peel Extract (Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 /Cs–PPE) was synthesized by ionic gelation (0.2% chitosan), followed by ultrasonic-assisted functionalization with 0.5 g SiO 2 , 50 mL pomegranate peel extract (PPE), and 0.2 g Fe 3 O 4 . Comprehensive physicochemical analyses, including FTIR, XRD, FE-SEM, BET, and VSM, supported the formation of a nanoporous, magnetically separable composite structure. Under optimal conditions (pH 7, an adsorbent dose of 0.2 g L -1 , an initial pesticide concentration of 10 mg L -1 , and a contact time of 40 min at room temperature), the nanocomposite demonstrated adsorption capacities of 166.7–200 mg g -1 . The findings showed removal efficiencies of 96%, 94%, 90%, and 90% for diazinon, malathion, parathion, and ethion, respectively, when tested individually. The kinetic study revealed that the adsorption data were best fitted by the pseudo-second-order model (PSO), without being used as independent evidence of a specific adsorption mechanism. The Langmuir isotherm indicated monolayer adsorption, with a favorable monolayer adsorption capacity. Furthermore, after seven regeneration cycles, the adsorbent maintained measurable adsorption performance, with the removal efficiency decreasing from 95% in the first cycle to 60% in the seventh cycle using a mixture of the four pesticides. Overall, Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 /Cs–PPE exhibits promising adsorption performance and acceptable reusability under the experimental conditions studied for the removal of pesticides from water. Future studies should emphasize large-scale production and testing in real-world wastewater applications.

Article.Title: Evaluating explanation methods by the predictors they induce
Article.Authors: Selbæk J.; Hammer H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Explanations of machine learning models are usually judged by criteria that are hard to compare. We propose a simpler test: if an explanation really describes how a model uses its features, it should be possible to rebuild the model’s predictions from it. We turn each explanation into a predictor by reading each feature’s effect and adding them up, and measure how well that predictor reproduces the model on unseen data. Nothing is fitted, so the score reflects the explanation itself. The test applies to any explanation that can be written as a function of the features; we demonstrate it on partial dependence plots (PDP), accumulated local effects (ALE), SHAP and LIME. We prove that summing partial dependence curves gives the best possible additive summary of a model when its features are independent, and that this fails when they are dependent. Across 13 real datasets and 9 synthetic designs and four model families, which method scores best depends entirely on feature dependence: where features are independent SHAP is slightly worse than PDP, exactly as the theory predicts; on dependent real data SHAP leads. Some widely used quality metrics can even prefer a randomly permuted explanation to an intact one.

Article.Title: Community perceptions of glacier ecosystem service dynamics in the Baspa basin using a DPSIR, FCM and FLM framework
Article.Authors: Arya A.; Santhanam H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Montane glaciers are climate-vulnerable socio-ecological systems (SES) vital for sustaining water resources, ecosystem services (ES), and livelihoods in the Indian Himalayan Region subject to high anthropogenic pressures. The present study used the Drivers–Pressures–State–Impact–Response (DPSIR) framework along with Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM), and Fuzzy Logic Modelling (FLM) methods to systematically analyse and unravel local community perceptions of glacier ES and SES dynamics in the Baspa Basin. The DPSIR framework was used to organize perception-based indicators and then normalized DPSIR scores were subsequently analysed through two complementary and computationally independent approaches: FCM to quantify perceived directional interactions and feedback mechanisms, whereas and, FLM to evaluate nonlinear response behaviour and uncertainty through fuzzy rule-based inferencing. Primary data were collected through household surveys captured community perceptions of glacier change and adaptation practices towards climate change. These were consistent with the results of the present study as well as previously documented regional and basin-specific glaciological changes, providing clear evidence of ongoing hydro-climatic transition DPSIR analysis revealed dominant downstream linkages, with strong positive relationships among pressures, state, impacts, and responses, and indirect influence in the case of drivers. FCM simulations highlighted the central role of impact-driven responses to pressures in climate adaptation, while FLM revealed greater nonlinear system behaviour under highly resource-stressed conditions. The findings suggest that the SES operates in a predominantly reactive mode, whereas adaptation is primarily triggered by the impacts experienced at community-level. The present framework provided complementary insights into directional system interactions, feedbacks, nonlinear response behaviour, and uncertainty, with FCM illustrating perceived network dynamics and FLM capturing a fuzzy rule-based response behaviour. The results illustrate the need for anticipatory ‘glocal’ SES governance integrating traditional knowledge with modern practices to enhance climatic resilience and sustain glacier ES.

Article.Title: Oleanolic acid potentiates the antileukemic activity of​ elesclomol​ by​ promoting FDX1-mediated cuproptosis
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Teng H.; Sun L.; Gao X.; Li W.; Song L.; Zhao H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cuproptosis is a programmed cell death in leukemia cell therapy. Elesclomol(ES) as a copper ion carrier, triggers cuproptosis in malignant cells and displays antitumor potential. Oleanolic acid(OA) has garnered attention in hematologic malignancies recent years. The two compounds can synergistically regulate cuproptosis remains unclear. The present study aimed to determine whether OA augments ES-induced cuproptosis in leukemia cells. The functional relevance of the FDX1/DLAT axis was interrogated through FDX1 knockdown and DLAT overexpression. In vivo was assessed in nude mice. Proliferation assays demonstrated that OA reinforced the growth-inhibitory action of ES on leukemia cells. Molecular analyses revealed that FDX1 silencing or DLAT overexpression markedly attenuated the effects elicited by OA, supporting the involvement of the FDX1/DLAT axis in OA-mediated potentiation of cuproptosis. In the K562 xenograft model, co-administration of OA and ES yielded greater reductions in tumor size, volume, and weight. By upregulating FDX1 and promoting protein lipoylation, OA synergistically induces cuproptosis in K562 and HL-60 cells, offering a candidate target and therapeutic strategy for leukemia.

Article.Title: Climate-aware photovoltaic technology selection using hybrid BWM–CRITIC, MARCOS, and explainable surrogate modeling
Article.Authors: Tunca S.
Article.Abstract: Selecting photovoltaic (PV) technology for a specific location requires consideration of both local operating conditions and technology-specific characteristics. This study proposes a climate-aware Multi-criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework integrating the Best–Worst Method (BWM), Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC), and Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to COmpromise Solution (MARCOS) for PV technology selection. Ten years of hourly NASA POWER data (2015–2024) for Kütahya, Türkiye, were combined with commercial module specifications to evaluate Mono-PERC, TOPCon, heterojunction (HJT), bifacial n-TOPCon, and CdTe technologies. Four criteria were considered: expected energy production, temperature performance, long-term reliability, and low-irradiance performance. BWM represented literature-supported engineering priorities, whereas CRITIC quantified the discriminatory information contained in the decision matrix. Under the reference hybrid weighting scheme, MARCOS ranked HJT first with a utility of 0.6877, followed by bifacial n-TOPCon (0.6832) and TOPCon (0.6761). Robustness was examined through weighting sensitivity, TOPSIS, and VIKOR comparisons, leave-one-criterion-out analysis, and 60,000 Monte Carlo realizations across three perturbation levels. Under the ± 5% reference scenario, HJT had a 53.90% probability of ranking first, while HJT, bifacial n-TOPCon, and TOPCon remained among the top three in 98.32%, 97.45%, and 91.14% of realizations, respectively. A Random Forest surrogate achieved a held-out R 2 of 0.9435, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified expected energy production as the dominant contributor to surrogate-predicted MARCOS utility. Overall, the results support a robust leading group rather than an unequivocal single-technology winner and demonstrate the importance of combining site-specific climatic information, engineering priorities, and uncertainty analysis in PV technology selection.

Article.Title: Mapping tryptophan metabolites from skin bacteria identifies tryptophol as a regulator of keratinocyte barrier function
Article.Authors: Adel Aldehalan F.; Mercer S.; Colette A.; Basill N.; Elias A.; Taylor G.; McBain A.; O’Neill C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The skin barrier is regulated, at least in part, by tryptophan metabolites produced by the skin microbiota. However, the contribution of individual microbial species to barrier function has not been systematically addressed. Mass spectrometry revealed that only strains capable of producing tryptophol enhanced TEER. Notably, the S. hominis strain that failed to augment TEER carried mutations in a gene involved in tryptophol biosynthesis. Supplementing supernatants from this strain with low concentrations of exogenous tryptophol led to enhancements in TEER, while adding tryptophol to keratinocytes in isolation was only able to enhance TEER at high concentrations. Together, these findings demonstrate that bacterial effects on keratinocyte barrier function are both species-and strain-dependent and highlight tryptophol as a microbial metabolite that contributes to the barrier-enhancing effects of bacterial secretions.

Article.Title: Macro- and meso-scale study of the lateral bearing mechanism of a single pile with a cap under pure lateral loading
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Luo K.
Article.Abstract: Single piles with caps frequently bear pure lateral loads induced by wind, waves, ship impact and adjacent soil movement, yet quantitative studies on the meso-scale deformation and load transfer of the surrounding soil remain scarce. Focusing on zero vertical load, a visualized model test of a single pile with a cap in sandy ground was conducted using particle image velocimetry (PIV), obtaining the load–displacement curve, pile bending moments and the progressive soil displacement field. A three-dimensional coupled discrete–continuum model was established, with meso-scale parameters calibrated by flexible-membrane-boundary numerical triaxial tests and the variable-particle-size method improving efficiency. Upon verification, the displacement field, particle rotation field, contact force chains and stress distribution of the soil were quantitatively analyzed at the meso-scale. The load–displacement curve enters the nonlinear stage at about 100 N; the ultimate lateral capacity from the second inflection point of the load–displacement gradient curve is about 187 N at 8.6 mm pile-top displacement. The bending moment is parabolic along the depth with its maximum at 100–200 mm; with increasing load, the maximum moment moves towards the pile tip, and the pile rotates rigidly about a center roughly 378 mm below the ground surface. The soil within the rotation depth participates in resisting the lateral load. The loading-side soil heaves while the opposite side collapses, and the disturbance zone concentrates within nine pile diameters around the middle–upper pile shaft. At the ultimate state, strong force chains form an arch-shaped transfer path coinciding with the shear bands, and the horizontal stress within six pile diameters on the passive side peaks at about 66 kPa at 340 mm depth. The lateral bearing behavior is therefore interpreted as the combined result of shear strength mobilization in the passive-side soil and the embedment restraint of the soil below the rotation center, which provides a meso-scale reference for the design of laterally dominated pile-cap foundations.

Article.Authors: Shariffar A.; Tohidi A.; Zanganeh Ranjbar P.; Negahdar H.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the stabilization of clay soil for cold climates using industrial by-products and recycled materials. The WCF provided effective crack control by bridging micro-cracks, significantly increasing toughness, ductility, and energy absorption capacity (reaching 213.9 kJ/m³). In conclusion, this sustainable composite not only substantially enhances the mechanical performance and F-T durability of clay soil but also offers a promising eco-friendly solution for geotechnical engineering in cold regions.

Article.Authors: Klier K.; Beres Y.; Renner K.; Meyer-Nieberg S.; Gebhardt T.; Weber S.; Eder M.; Küsel C.

Article.Authors: Patri-Alcalde D.; Muñoz-Poblete C.; Stumfol M.; Rodríguez-Coloma M.; Astudillo R.; Carranza-Leiva J.; Bascour-Sandoval C.
Article.Abstract: Rotator cuff-related shoulder pain (RCRSP) is associated with serratus anterior (SA) dysfunction. No statistically significant between-condition difference in the percentage increase in SA thickness was detected (mean paired difference = 9.80 percentage points [95% CI − 3.97 to 23.57]; p = 0.145). In a single session, SA thickness increased following both RUSI and manual feedback during a motor control exercise in individuals with RCRSP. No statistically significant between-condition difference in the percentage increase in SA thickness was detected. These findings suggest that both feedback strategies may be used during the early stages of motor control-based rehabilitation in individuals with RCRSP, providing clinicians with flexibility depending on the context and available resources. Further studies with repeated sessions and under conditions that more closely reflect clinical practice are needed to confirm these findings.

Article.Authors: Abdulkader Mohamed R.; Abdul Rahim N.; Mohamad S.; Ahmad Yusof H.

Article.Title: CFAP298 governs dynein arm protein homeostasis to ensure motile cilia function
Article.Authors: Lee R.; Sub Y.; Lee S.; Lee M.; Gee H.
Article.Abstract: Motile cilia drive directional fluid flow essential for mucociliary clearance, cerebrospinal fluid circulation, and left–right body patterning, and their dysfunction causes primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a disorder often linked to defective axonemal dynein arms. CFAP298 (C21orf59) has been implicated in ciliary motility in unicellular organisms and non-mammalian vertebrates, but its mechanistic role in mammalian motile cilia remains poorly understood. Here we generated mice carrying a homozygous Cfap298 gene-trap allele and found that Cfap298 disruption resulted in severe developmental abnormalities and PCD-like phenotypes, including hydrocephalus, respiratory defects, and laterality abnormalities. Ciliogenesis and overall axonemal architecture were largely preserved, whereas Cfap298 mutant cilia showed partial depletion of outer and inner dynein arms and increased variability in central pair orientation. Multiple dynein-arm subunits exhibited reduced abundance and impaired ciliary localization, while several dynein-arm assembly-associated were largely preserved. Transcriptomic profiling revealed no broad reduction in cilia-related gene expression, suggesting that transcriptional suppression alone does not account for the observed protein-level defects. Proteomic interactome analysis of CFAP298 immunoprecipitates identified candidate CFAP298-associated proteins enriched in molecular chaperones, ubiquitin-related factors, and RNA-binding proteins, pointing to a post-transcriptional regulatory network. These findings indicate that CFAP298 is required for dynein-arm integrity and motile cilia function in mice, and suggest that it acts at a post-transcriptional level, potentially through protein networks involved in dynein-arm protein homeostasis.
