Article.Title: Weight-stratified analysis reveals context-specific association between dietary diversity and hypertension among minority populations in Southern China
Article.Authors: Yao M.; Su H.; Chen S.; Zeng X.; He S.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension is a major global public health burden, and dietary factors play a key role in its development. However, evidence on the association between dietary diversity and hypertension among ethnic minority populations in China remains limited. This cross-sectional study included 13,356 Zhuang adults aged 35–74 years in Guangxi, China. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire, and the dietary diversity score (DDS) was calculated from nine food groups. Blood pressure and anthropometric measurements followed standard protocols. Binary logistic regression and mediation analyses were employed. The prevalence of hypertension was 33.46%. In the total population, DDS showed a significant protective total effect on hypertension (OR = 0.96, P < 0.01), which remained after adjusting for BMI (direct effect OR = 0.95, P < 0.001). Stratified analysis revealed that this protective association was significant only in overweight individuals (total effect OR = 0.93, direct effect OR = 0.92, both P < 0.001), with no significant mediation or interaction by BMI. A linear dose-response relationship was observed, with DDS ≥ 6 as a key threshold. Higher dietary diversity was associated with a reduced risk of hypertension specifically in overweight populations, independently of BMI, suggesting that tailored dietary interventions could help prevent hypertension in overweight adults from minority populations.

Article.Title: A deep learning-enhanced cryptographic framework for intelligent traffic blocking in secure networks
Article.Authors: Srilatha K.; Khekare G.
Article.Abstract: The rise of encrypted communications, the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, autonomous infrastructures, and the distributed cloud-edge environment has created a challenging set of issues for cybersecurity management today. Expanding encrypted payloads, shifting attack patterns, and diverse network conditions are becoming a major challenge for conventional intrusion detection and rule-based traffic-filtering mechanisms. While many machine learning and deep learning algorithms can classify traffic and detect intrusions, few integrate risk-aware security enforcement, adaptive cryptographic protection, and intelligent traffic control. Building on this, this paper presents SecureBlockNet, a deep-learning-assisted cryptographic framework for intelligent traffic blocking and adaptive secure communication management. This architecture combines spatial feature extraction via a 1D-CNN, temporal dependency modelling using BiLSTM, attention-based feature prioritisation, calibrated risk assessment, adaptive cryptographic policy selection, and context-aware traffic enforcement in a single cybersecurity pipeline. The framework considers the predicted attack class, malicious confidence level, severity, and historical behaviour to dynamically choose actions such as allow, monitor, block, and encrypted quarantine. SecureBlockNet’s performance is evaluated through experiments on CICIoT2023, CSE-CIC-IDS2018, and CIC-IDS2017, achieving 98.87% classification accuracy, 98.64% F1-score, 99.13% ROC-AUC, and a false-positive rate of 1.02%, outperforming conventional machine-learning and CNN-LSTM-based baselines. Cross-dataset experiments also show consistent generalisation across diverse traffic scenarios, and ablation and cryptographic-overhead analyses validate the contributions and viability of the built-in security components. These results show that SecureBlockNet offers a scalable basis for smart cybersecurity management in IoT, enterprise, smart-grid, vehicular and cloud-edge communication systems. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/srilatha-178/SecureBlockNet .

Article.Title: One Health seroepidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 and associated risk factors at the human–animal interface in Central Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Tufa T.; Eberhardt K.; Tufa T.; Behnke K.; Hunstig F.; Debela N.; Shimelis A.; Rabl D.; Massion P.; Schwarz-Cadeddu M.; Orth H.; Worku A.; Mueller L.; Luedde T.; Eggers Y.; Feldt T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The epidemiological role of agricultural livestock in SARS-CoV-2 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa where human-animal interactions are deeply integrated into daily life. This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence and risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 exposure among parallel livestock and human populations across four districts (Bishoftu, Lume, Boset, and Fantale) in Central Ethiopia. A cross-sectional One Health investigation (February–June 2021) was conducted across two peri-urban hubs (Bishoftu and Lume) and two rural pastoral/agro-pastoral districts (Boset and Fantale). Serum and nasal swabs were collected from 114 livestock (49 cattle, 22 sheep, 20 goats, and 23 camels) and serum from 115 humans. Active viral shedding in livestock nasal swabs was assessed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), while serological screening used spike- and nucleocapsid-specific electrochemiluminescence immunoassays (ECLIA) in livestock and rapid IgM/IgG lateral flow assays in humans, with biological validation in livestock via full-virus neutralization tests (NT). Risk factors were assessed using Firth’s penalized logistic regression. Overall SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence was 12.3% (14/114) in livestock and 23.5% (27/115) in humans, with no active viral shedding detected in animals by RT-PCR. Species-level seropositivity ranged from 20.4% (10/49) in cattle, 10.0% (2/20) in goats, and 9.1% (2/22) in sheep to 0.0% (0/23) in camels. Seropositive small ruminants exhibited the highest neutralizing titers (up to 1:40). Sedentary extensive farming systems were associated with increased odds of seropositivity compared to mobile pastoral herds (OR = 13.98, 95% CI: 2.57–95.42, p = 0.002). Similarly, humans in the peri-urban hub of Bishoftu faced higher odds of exposure compared to residents of the rural pastoral district of Boset (OR = 3.84, 95% CI: 1.18–12.99, p = 0.026). This study provides serological evidence of prior SARS-CoV-2 exposure among livestock and humans in Central Ethiopia. The elevated risk in sedentary extensive and peri-urban management systems underscores the critical need for proactive, serology-based One Health surveillance at the human-animal interface beyond symptom-triggered detection.

Article.Title: WBRCNet for respiratory sound classification using continuous wavelet scalograms and blank region cropping
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Gu T.; Luo C.; Zhang Y.; Wen W.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: Respiratory sounds are non-stationary biomedical signals, and automatic classification remains challenging because of limited samples, variable cycle lengths and complex abnormal acoustic patterns. This study aimed to improve cycle-level respiratory sound classification by optimizing continuous wavelet time-frequency representations. A Wavelet-based Blank Region Cropping Network (WBRCNet) was developed on the ICBHI 2017 dataset. Respiratory cycles were resampled, length-normalized using Smart Padding, transformed into continuous wavelet scalograms, and processed by Blank Region Cropping for Wavelet (BRCW) to remove low-energy redundant regions. ResNet34 was used as the classification backbone, and comparative experiments were conducted for time-frequency representation, BRCW, boundary artifact suppression and mother wavelet selection. Continuous wavelet scalograms achieved a higher ICBHI Score than Mel spectrograms in the evaluated comparison. With CWT and class-balanced augmentation held constant, replacing conventional BRC with BRCW increased specificity, sensitivity, and the ICBHI Score. The final model achieved Se of 48.88%, Sp of 76.90%, and an ICBHI Score of 62.89%. WBRCNet provides a scalogram preprocessing strategy for respiratory sound classification on ICBHI 2017. However, limited sensitivity and the absence of external validation prevent conclusions about reliable clinical screening or deployment readiness.

Article.Title: A bio-digital circular framework for sustainable duck feed production using agro-industrial side-streams and aquatic biomass
Article.Authors: Elgingihy S.; Abdelrahman R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIREEM framework, a bio-digital circular approach for the valorization of Snack Food Industry By-products (SFIB) and aquatic biomass ( Azolla pinnata and Spirulina platensis ) in poultry feed production. The framework integrates IoT-assisted process monitoring, computational feed optimization, machine-learning prediction, and circular resource-utilization principles. An IoT-assisted pelleting system incorporating a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and real-time sensors was used to monitor and control processing conditions, while a Python-based Least-Cost Ration (LCR) model optimized feed formulations under predefined nutritional and economic constraints. Under the simulated conditions, the optimized formulation reduced the estimated feed production cost from approximately 22,000 to 12,450 EGP ton⁻¹ (43.4%) and reduced logistics-related CO₂ emissions by 93.8% within the defined assessment boundary. Machine-learning models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with Gradient Boosting providing the best prediction of body weight and Extra-Trees providing the best prediction of feed conversion ratio among the evaluated models. Feature-importance analysis indicated that age and metabolizable energy were major predictors of growth-related performance, whereas Azolla inclusion showed a greater contribution to feed conversion ratio than to body weight prediction. In addition, 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation indicated that the economic performance of the optimized system remained feasible across the majority of the simulated uncertainty scenarios, with SFIB cost and transportation expenditure identified as important cost drivers. Overall, the results support the potential of SHIREEM as an integrated computational framework for circular feed-resource utilization and localized production. However, the findings represent a computational proof-of-concept and require experimental and commercial-scale validation before biological, environmental, and economic performance can be generalized to practical poultry production systems. To support regional adoption, agricultural policymakers could consider developing appropriate quality-certification frameworks for bio-based feed resources and supportive policy mechanisms that facilitate the responsible upcycling of locally available agro-industrial residues into animal feed.

Article.Title: Assessing spatial genetic resilience and enhancement strategies for traditional villages in Liping County, Guizhou, China
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Xiang Y.; Gong L.; Zhou X.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Resilience stands as a central theme within sustainability science, and the resilience of traditional villages and their spatial genes constituting a vital facet of “rural resilience”. This paper applies resilience theory to the study of spatial genetic resilience in traditional villages within China’s ethnic regions. Taking the traditional Dong ethnic villages in Liping County, Qiandongnan Prefecture, Guizhou Province, China as a case study, it constructs an assessing indicator system for the spatial genetic resilience of traditional ethnic villages based on the ‘Pressure-State-Response’ (PSR) model. It comprehensively employs the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Entropy Weighting method, and Composite Index method to measure the spatial genetic resilience of the traditional Dong ethnic villages. An Obstacle Degree Model(ODM) was employed to diagnose the primary factors hindering the enhancement of spatial genetic resilience in the sampled traditional villages, thereby proposing optimisation strategies to elevate their spatial genetic resilience levels. Results indicate: (1) The comprehensive spatial genetic resilience of traditional Dong ethnic villages in Liping County remains at a low-to-medium level overall, with weak systemic capacity to withstand risk disturbances. (2) Regarding resilience levels across the three criterions layer: the pressure-layer exhibits low resilience, with ‘rapid urbanisation’ being the primary systemic stressor; the state -layer, traditional dwellings spatial genes exhibited high resilience; the response-layer reveals higher resilience in local department responses compared to villager responses. (3) In identifying obstacle factors to enhancing system resilience, ‘system state’ constitutes the primary criterion-level impediment to improving spatial genes resilience in the sampled traditional villages; ‘whether local department possess disaster information and issue timely warnings’ represents the key indicator-level obstacle factors. Building upon this, this paper proposes resilience enhancement strategies for the inheritance and development of traditional villages and their spatial genes. This study explores resilience enhancement strategies based on spatial genetic resilience assessing for traditional villages, aiming to provide theoretical references and methodological insights for the preservation and transmission of traditional villages and their spatial genetic heritage in ethnic regions of China and other country worldwide. This contributes to the sustainable conservation and utilisation of traditional villages cultural heritage.

Article.Title: SPD-YOLO: a reliable model for imported supermarket products detection
Article.Authors: Du C.; Liu L.; Zhang X.; Tang L.
Article.Abstract: Accurate detection of imported supermarket products is essential for automated retail management and intelligent inventory inspection. However, in practical supermarket scenarios, detection performance is often affected by dense product arrangements, highly regular vertical layouts, scale variation, partial occlusion, and complex background interference. To address these challenges, we propose SPD-YOLO, a lightweight detector for accurate and efficient imported product detection. First, the backbone incorporates a C3K2-CSSC feature enhancement module, which integrates column attention, spatial attention, and a self-calibration branch to strengthen column-wise consistency modeling and spatial feature representation for vertically arranged products. Second, we introduce a C2DA feature processing module between the backbone and the feature fusion layer. By embedding deformable attention into the C2PSA structure, C2DA enables adaptive feature sampling and enhances the representation of fine-grained and partially occluded products. Third, we adopt Slim-Neck, a lightweight feature fusion architecture that combines GSConv and VOVGSCSP to promote efficient multi-scale feature interaction while reducing computational redundancy. Finally, we replace the original detection head with EfficientHead, a lightweight decoupled head that uses grouped convolutions for efficient feature processing and Distribution Focal Loss for more accurate bounding box regression. Experiments on the self-constructed imported supermarket product dataset show that SPD-YOLO achieves 91.4% mAP50 and 75.8% mAP50-95 with only 2.7 M parameters and 5.9 GFLOPs, outperforming the YOLO11n baseline and other compared detectors. Compared with YOLO11n, SPD-YOLO reduces GFLOPs from 7.0 to 5.9 and improves inference speed from 330.1 FPS to 358.6 FPS while maintaining the same parameter size, demonstrating clear computational and speed advantages. Furthermore, on the public Locount Dataset, SPD-YOLO achieves 69.2% mAP50 and 52.8% mAP50-95, demonstrating its competitive generalization performance. These results indicate that SPD-YOLO achieves a favorable balance among detection accuracy, model complexity, and inference efficiency.

Article.Title: Eggshell-supported iron oxide composite for As(III) removal via response surface optimization
Article.Authors: Olika Desisa T.; Wakuma Duke B.; Dereje Mekonin N.; Abdisa Feyisa M.; Fufa Feyessa F.; Tadesse Gameda T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Arsenic contamination of water poses a serious environmental and public health challenge, particularly where affordable treatment technologies are limited. In this study, an eggshell-supported iron oxide composite was synthesized by precipitation-calcination and evaluated for As(III) removal from aqueous solution. The composite was characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface-area analysis, and particle-size analysis. The specific surface area was 9.79 m 2 g −1 , and particle-size analysis indicated a nanoscale size under the specified measurement conditions. Adsorption conditions were optimized using response surface methodology with a Box–Behnken design, considering pH (4–9), adsorbent dosage (0.2–1.5 g L −1 ), initial As(III) concentration (5–35 mg L −1 ), and contact time (30–120 min). The optimum conditions were pH 7.10, adsorbent dosage 1.2879 g L −1 , initial As(III) concentration 16.1834 mg L −1 , and contact time 89.3404 min, yielding a predicted removal efficiency of 95.7528%. Experimental validation gave 95.0 $$\pm $$ 0.17% removal. After correcting the adsorbent mass used in adsorption-capacity calculations, the pseudo-second-order model provided a better fit than the pseudo-first-order model (R 2 $$=$$ 0.997 and 0.696, respectively), although kinetic fitting alone does not establish chemisorption. Equilibrium data were better described by the Langmuir model than by the Freundlich model (R 2 $$=$$ 0.998 and approximately 0.74, respectively). The findings demonstrate the potential of eggshell-supported iron oxide as a waste-derived adsorbent for As(III) removal and eggshell waste valorization. Further studies using environmentally relevant arsenic concentrations, competing ions, and regeneration cycles are required to assess practical water-treatment applicability.

Article.Title: Isolation and characterization of lytic bacteriophages targeting multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from Bar-headed Goose (Anser indicus) and environmental sources
Article.Authors: Chawre M.; Ghonse K.; Koratkar S.; Pawar S.; Kulkarni P.; Keng S.; Waghchaure R.; Ushir V.; Bhatt A.; Sheth J.; Puvar A.; Patel J.; Pande S.; Velayudhan A.; Joy S.; Gupta N.
Article.Abstract: The global emergence of multidrug- resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae has become a major public health challenge due to the limited availability of effective treatment options. In this view, three lytic bacteriophages, KPAФ-04, KPAФ-05, and KP84Ф-06, were isolated from a fecal dropping from a Bar-headed Goose and surface water from a waterbody frequented by wild and migratory birds and characterized for their potential application against clinical multidrug resistant K. pneumoniae. KPAФ-04 and KPAФ-05 phages were classified within the family of Autosignataviridae , while KP84Ф-06 belonged to the family Drexlerviridae . The genome size ranged from 43.6 kb to 51.7 kb with GC contents of 50.2–51.6%. Phage genome annotation identified genes associated with DNA replication, structural assembly, host lysis, and packaging, including holin-endolysin systems, while no lysogeny, virulence, or antibiotic resistance-associated genes were detected. Phages remained stable at temperatures up to 50 °C, across pH 5 to 9, while UV exposure for 40 min. Phages showed antibacterial activity against clinical multidrug resistant (MDR) K. pneumoniae , and exhibited low toxicity in Vero cells, supporting their safety in therapeutic application. The isolation of therapeutically relevant phages from migratory bird and environmental sample highlights significance of One Health surveillance in identifying alternative antimicrobial agents and understanding pathogen–phage dynamics across human, animal, and environmental interfaces. Collectively, these findings highlight the antibacterial efficacy, genomic safety, and therapeutic potential of KPAФ-04, KPAФ-05, and KP84Ф-06, supporting their further development as phage-based interventions for the treatment of MDR K. pneumoniae infections.

Article.Title: A feature fusion network with time-frequency cross-attention for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
Article.Authors: Tang Z.; Zhai Y.; Bian A.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: To address the limitations of existing rolling bearing fault diagnosis methods in time-frequency feature coordination, cross-domain information interaction, and fault feature extraction under noise interference, a Time-Frequency Cross-Attention Network (TFCANet) is proposed. The proposed method employs a dual-branch architecture to extract complementary features from raw vibration signals and their Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectra, capturing transient fault impulses, dynamic response patterns, and spectral characteristics. Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) modules are incorporated into both branches to adaptively emphasize fault-sensitive channels and suppress redundant information. Furthermore, a multi-head time-frequency cross-attention mechanism is developed, using temporal features as queries and spectral features as keys and values to facilitate explicit cross-domain interaction and adaptive feature fusion. Experiments conducted on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset demonstrate that TFCANet achieves an accuracy of 0.9954, precision of 0.9951, recall of 0.9948, and F1-score of 0.9949, outperforming the compared methods under the original evaluation protocol. Additional cross-load evaluations, attention-direction comparisons, extended ablation studies, and repeated training experiments are performed to assess diagnostic performance and stability. Across 20 cross-load tests, TFCANet achieves an overall accuracy of 0.980 ± 0.036 and a macro-F1 score of 0.979 ± 0.039. In the extended ablation experiments, the complete model achieves an accuracy of 0.982 ± 0.020 and a macro-F1 score of 0.981 ± 0.022. These results demonstrate that the proposed time-frequency fusion framework effectively extracts discriminative bearing fault features and maintains favorable diagnostic performance across different load conditions, while revealing variations in model performance and stability under different operating conditions.

Article.Title: Significant offshore rainfall trends during sea-land breeze transition hours
Article.Authors: Zhang A.; Zhang H.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: The understanding of coastal precipitation changes is critical for climate adaptation, yet their diurnal-scale responses to global warming demand robust observational constraints. In this manuscript, using 25 years (2000–2024) of high-resolution IMERG satellite precipitation data, we systematically investigate globally averaged behavior of precipitation trends in coastal and offshore regions, with a focus on diurnal variations and physical drivers. Our results reveal a pronounced “offshore precipitation minimum” zone located 20–30 km from coastlines. Paradoxically, this climatologically dry zone exhibits the strongest precipitation increase over the past two decades, with trends peaking at 7.5 mm/yr. This enhancement is not diurnally uniform but concentrates during morning (~ 0900 LST) and evening (~ 2100 LST) transition periods of the sea-land breeze circulation, when > 80% of samples show statistically significant increases. Mechanistically, while sea-land thermal contrast weakens, the offshore skin temperature gradient increases significantly, accompanied by significant modest rise in CAPE, slight decline in boundary layer height and enhancement of moisture convergence. These thermodynamic and moisture changes collectively create favorable conditions for convection and drive the significant offshore precipitation trends. The findings reveal a fundamental reorganization of coastal precipitation under climate change, with critical implications for flood risk management and climate model improvements in coastal zones.

Article.Title: An enhanced equivalent magnetic network model for electromagnetic analysis of a counter-rotating dual-rotor PM-reluctance motor
Article.Authors: Nadri P.; Rezaeealam B.; Mikhak-Beyranvand M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate electromagnetic analysis of Counter-Rotating Dual-Rotor Synchronous Motors (CRDRSMs) is challenging because of severe magnetic field modulation, multidirectional leakage flux paths, and the coexistence of dual air gaps. Although Equivalent Magnetic Network (EMN) method have been successfully applied to various electrical machines, an EMN-based analytical model for CRDRSMs has not yet been reported. To address this gap, this paper proposes a comprehensive EMN model for the electromagnetic analysis of CRDRSMs. The proposed model employs a distributed permeance formulation to accurately represent complex magnetic flux paths in critical regions, while a quadrilateral permeance mesh is adopted for the air-gap region to discretize the non-uniform magnetic field distribution. In addition, a modular Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) solution algorithm is developed to improve numerical stability and convergence during nonlinear network analysis. The proposed analytical model is validated by finite-element analysis (FEA) through comparisons of air-gap flux density, flux linkage, back-EMF, inductance, and electromagnetic torque. The obtained results demonstrate close agreement between the proposed EMN model and FEA, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed approach for accurate and computationally efficient electromagnetic analysis of CRDRSMs.

Article.Title: Trichoderma virens strain Ir. 11 neutralizes the challenge of Phytophthora infestans infection in potato by augmenting plant defense mechanisms and modulating defense-related genes
Article.Authors: Akbari A.; Davari M.; Torabi Giglou M.; Estaji A.; Azarmi R.; Heydarnajad Giglou R.; van Diepeningen A.
Article.Abstract: Late blight of potato, caused by Phytophthora infestans , is the most significant and dangerous disease of potatoes, leading to annual losses of billions of dollars worldwide. Two Trichoderma strains were investigated for their use as biological control organisms of this disease under both in vitro and greenhouse environments. On the basis of these results, the Trichoderma virens strain AY154945 Ir. 11 presented a more specific response to P. infestans than did the other strain AY154931, a T. koningii Ir. 502 strain. Moreover, the T. virens Ir. 11 AY154945 exhibited the highest activity in inhibiting P. infestans growth, reaching up to 86.6% reduction under in vitro conditions. Additionally, the results indicated that treatment with T. virens Ir. 11 significantly reduced hydrogen peroxide levels. In greenhouse-grown potato plants challenged with P. infestans , treatment with T. virens Ir. 11 reduced H 2 O 2 levels by 48.07% and 31.37% in Agria and Jelly, respectively, compared with P. infestans -infected plants. The treatment also increased total phenolic content by 60.13% in Agria compared with P. infestans -infected plants. PAL activity increased by 20.77% and 21.59% in Agria and Jelly, respectively, compared with P. infestans -infected plants. Furthermore, compared with plants treated with P. infestans alone, treatment with T. virens Ir. 11, increased the expression of StuPR1 by 3.27-fold and 1.72-fold in Agria and Jelly, respectively; StuMAPK4 by 3.07-fold and 3.19-fold; StuPPO9 by 2.08-fold and 1.80-fold; and StuPAL by 2.89-fold and 1.91-fold, respectively. Overall, T. virens Ir. 11 induced stronger defense-related responses, whereas the other Trichoderma strain showed different responses. The results showed that potato cultivars differed in their precise responses to Trichoderma treatments. On the basis of these findings, a comprehensive evaluation of the impact of Trichoderma as a biological fungicide on each potato cultivar before its utilization in commercial fields is imperative.

Article.Title: Adaptive severity-aware educational content recommendation for autistic learners using a LinUCB-based contextual bandit framework
Article.Authors: Rathod V.; Goudar R.; Sangani S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the rapid growth of digital learning technologies, many existing educational platforms remain insufficiently adaptive to the diverse behavioural and cognitive characteristics exhibited by autistic learners. To address this challenge, this study proposes a LinUCB-based contextual bandit framework for personalized educational content recommendation using learner-specific contextual representations. The proposed proof-of-concept framework constructs severity-aware and age-aware learner profiles from publicly available Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) screening datasets obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and Kaggle and complements them with controlled synthetic educational interaction variables to investigate adaptive recommendation strategies. The resulting contextual representation integrates demographic information, behavioural indicators, severity-related characteristics, and educational interaction attributes to support recommendation across multiple learning modalities. Experimental evaluation using stratified 10-fold cross-validation demonstrates that the proposed framework consistently outperforms conventional supervised learning algorithms and alternative bandit-based approaches, achieving a recommendation accuracy of 87.3%. Comparative benchmarking and feature ablation analyses further highlight the contribution of contextual learner attributes to recommendation performance and model interpretability. Owing to its computational efficiency and interpretable contextual bandit formulation, the proposed framework provides a promising foundation for future research on explainable, privacy-conscious, and context-aware personalized educational recommendation systems for autistic learners. Future work will focus on validation using authentic learner interaction data together with the incorporation of multimodal behavioural information to further improve recommendation quality and generalizability.

Article.Title: Full-range flexural modelling of hybrid-reinforced steel fibre recycled aggregate concrete beams
Article.Authors: Shi K.; Bai B.; Meng J.
Article.Abstract: Hybrid FRP-steel reinforcement and steel fibre-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (SFRAC) can improve crack control and deformation capacity, but the full-range flexural response of hybrid SFRAC beams remains insufficiently quantified. This study developed a four-stage semi-analytical model for the load-mid-span deflection response of hybrid FRP-steel-reinforced SFRAC beams. Nine beams, comprising eight hybrid specimens and one all-steel reference, underwent four-point bending. Parameters included steel-fibre volume fraction, lower-to-upper bottom-reinforcement area ratio and lower-layer reinforcement type. A nonlinear finite-element model with explicitly embedded steel fibres interpreted pre-peak response, reinforcement-strain development, and damage distribution. The semi-analytical model defines cracking, yielding, ultimate, and post-peak reference states through sectional equilibrium, strain compatibility, an equivalent fibre-bridging force, ultimate-curvature correction, and calibrated post-peak secant stiffness. Compared with the identically reinforced fibre-free beam, steel-fibre volume fractions of 0.5%, 1.0%, 1.5%, and 2.0% increased the ultimate load by 8.9%, 12.6%, 13.6%, and 16.4%. Increasing lower-layer BFRP bar diameter from 10 to 14 and 18 mm increased ultimate load by 4.9% and 13.8%, respectively. Lower-layer BFRP and CFRP beams exceeded the all-steel reference’s ultimate load by 15.5% and 21.1%, respectively. Lower-layer FRP bars’ sustained elastic tensile contribution governed post-yield hardening. The fibre-bridging coefficient, ultimate-curvature coefficient, and post-peak secant stiffness were calibrated using five identically reinforced hybrid beams with steel-fibre volume fractions of 0–2.0% and held fixed thereafter. Internal assessment using three held-out hybrid specimens gave MAPE values of 3.7%, 10.5%, 10.4%, and 8.2% for \(P_{{{\text{cr}}}}\) , \(P_{{\text{u}}}\) , \(\delta_{{\text{u}}}\) , and \(\delta_{{\text{f}}}\) respectively. An external literature assessment gave a 7.3% MAPE for \(P_{{\text{u}}}\) . The all-steel reference specimen identified the applicability boundary, indicating that the model is intended for beams with linearly elastic FRP reinforcement in the lower layer of bottom reinforcement. Further independent validation is needed before the calibrated coefficients are generalised.

Article.Title: Consistent time-varying association between ctDNA and post-resection colon and rectal cancer recurrence: The β-CORRECT study
Article.Authors: Hashimoto T.; Nakamura Y.; Young G.; Flake II D.; Abbasi M.; Hall D.; Palomares M.; Subramaniam S.; Frederick J.; Wallace M.; Oki E.; Kotani D.; Mishima S.; Watanabe J.; Ebi H.; Kotaka M.; Yamazaki K.; Taniguchi H.; Suwa Y.; Hirata K.; Akazawa N.; Kataoka K.; Bando H.; Takemasa I.; Kato T.
Article.Abstract: In this retrospective study of 468 patients with Stage II, III, or resectable Stage IV colorectal cancer (CRC), the association between circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detected with a tumor-informed molecular residual disease (MRD) assay and recurrence was evaluated. Tumor DNA and RNA sequencing of tumors were also performed to assess associations of tumor genomic alterations and expression with ctDNA status, DFS, and site of recurrence. Among 417 patients with a median follow-up of 1.9 years, ctDNA detection was strongly associated with shorter DFS during surveillance (HR 36.6), post-surgery (HR 7.5) and post-definitive therapy (HR 24.0), independent of clinicopathological factors. Each 10-fold increase in ctDNA level was associated with a two-fold increase in recurrence risk. Median lead time between ctDNA detection and clinical recurrence was 97 days. Among ctDNA-positive patients, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved DFS (HR = 0.3), whereas no benefit was observed among ctDNA-negative patients (HR = 1.8). Significant interactions were observed between ctDNA status and RAS/BRAF alterations and WNT and MAPK pathway alterations. RNA sequencing identified distinct expression patterns associated with the epithelial-mesenchymal transition. These findings support ctDNA as an independent prognostic marker in resected CRC and identify molecular features associated with MRD and recurrence risk.

Article.Title: Energy-efficient hybrid stochastic arithmetic design in quantum-dot cellular automata
Article.Authors: Bahar A.; Wahid K.
Article.Abstract: This work proposes a hybrid stochastic number (HSN) system based on quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) majority logic. Unlike traditional single-bit stochastic encoding, HSN uses multiple bit streams with different weights to enhance numerical accuracy while preserving stochastic computing’s inherent error tolerance. A QCA-based encoder is proposed to convert classical binary numbers into stochastic sub-streams, and two arithmetic units are designed on this basis: a majority-logic adder and a multiplier. This architecture minimises sub-stream correlations, hardware cost, and facilitates parallel processing. The proposed 2-, 4-, and 8-bit HSN adders and multipliers were functionally simulated using QCADesigner, and their energy dissipation was estimated using QCAPro. The system was also evaluated in an image denoising experiment in which zero-mean Gaussian noise was added to a grayscale image. The experimental results show that the PSNR increased from 22.20 dB to 27.87 dB and the SSIM from 0.4663 to 0.7408. The proposed QCA-based HSN design combines numerical accuracy, small size, and noise tolerance, which makes it a candidate for low-energy computing systems.

Article.Title: A multiscale analysis of the TNBC immune landscape
Article.Authors: Akins A.; Brooks J.; Harrington M.; Geier M.; Bridges W.; Dunn H.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive and heterogeneous subtype of breast cancer (BC). Women of African ancestry (WAA) tend to receive more severe and frequent diagnoses of TNBC. The majority of TNBC research is conducted on patients of European descent, with a limited number of studies including cell lines or patients of African descent. We investigated four cell lines from these two patient groups using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) to determine the expression of immune-related genes. Additionally, six patient samples were analyzed using spatial transcriptomics to determine the expression levels and tumor localization of our genes of interest in TNBC cell lines. We curated a group of 26 immune-related genes that were differentially expressed between WAA and women of European ancestry (WEA) TNBC and mammary epithelial cells (MEC) cell types using qPCR. After comparing the genes with TNBC tumor samples from WAA and WEA, we elected to investigate six genes of interest in more depth using spatial transcriptomic analysis, eventually narrowing our gene pool to three primary genes: NFATC4 , CD68 , and SMAD7 . From the integrated analysis of cell line and spatial transcriptomic datasets, we identified NFATC4 , CD68 , and SMAD7 as candidate immune-associated genes associated with TNBC tumor heterogeneity. These findings suggest that ancestry-associated differences in the TNBC immune microenvironment may involve distinct immune regulatory programs, although larger studies and further investigation are required to fully validate these observations.

Article.Title: CryoEDNet: an edge-enhanced deep convolutional network for detail-preserving denoising of cryo-EM particle images
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Xu Y.; Han J.; Zou L.; Lin X.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has revolutionized structural biology by enabling near-atomic reconstruction of biological macromolecules without crystallization. However, the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of cryo-EM particle images limits the accuracy of downstream three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction. Existing denoising algorithms may blur structural boundaries, remove fine details, or provide limited benefits for 3D reconstruction. To address these problems, we propose CryoEDNet, an edge-enhanced deep convolutional neural network for cryo-EM particle image denoising. CryoEDNet includes a multi-scale feature extraction module, an edge enhancement module, and a detail preservation module. The network is trained using a multi-constraint loss that considers pixel-level reconstruction, perceptual similarity, structural similarity, and frequency-domain consistency. Experiments on synthetic projections with Gaussian white noise at SNR=0.1 show improvements in image quality, projection orientation estimation, and 3D reconstruction results. Tests on three experimental cryo-EM datasets (EMPIAR-10028, EMPIAR-10219, and EMPIAR-10330) show that CryoEDNet improves particle representation, 2D class averaging, and reconstruction-related outcomes under the evaluated conditions. These results support the transferability of CryoEDNet across the evaluated experimental datasets, while broader validation across more diverse cryo-EM specimens and imaging conditions remains necessary.

Article.Title: Effects of risedronate on volumetric bone mineral density and CT-derived muscle–bone associations after sleeve gastrectomy: a pilot randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Greene K.; Beavers K.; Beavers D.; Reed K.; Knapp R.; Flores L.; Ard J.; Fernandez A.; Weaver A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) is an effective surgical treatment for severe obesity but is associated with bone mineral density (BMD) loss. This analysis investigates postoperative bisphosphonate effects on computed tomography (CT)-derived compartmental volumetric BMD (vBMD) and associations with CT-derived muscle outcomes. The 6-month pilot study randomized 24 SG patients to once-monthly 150 mg risedronate (n = 11) or placebo (n = 13). CT scans were collected at baseline, and 6- and 12-months postoperatively to assess hip and spine vBMD. Treatment effects were estimated using a mixed linear model adjusted for sex and baseline measures, and Pearson correlations with CT-derived muscle outcomes were assessed. There were no significant vBMD differences between risedronate vs. placebo groups after SG, but 6-month trends suggest vBMD losses [mg/cm 3 ] with risedronate were potentially attenuated in the trabecular compartment of the total hip [− 8.8 vs. − 9.6], femoral neck [− 3.6 vs. − 7.3], and L1–L4 vertebrae [− 8.4 vs. − 11.1]. Muscle–bone correlations were not significant but trends suggest larger and less fat infiltrated trunk muscles may protect against spine vBMD loss. This pilot study did not find a significant treatment effect of risedronate on vBMD in SG patients, but exploratory findings in relation with muscle measures warrant additional investigation in a larger study.

Article.Title: Multiomics investigation of iron-responsive idiopathic anemia in hybrid (Ictalurus punctatus × I. furcatus) catfish
Article.Authors: Older C.; Yamamoto F.; Richardson B.; Kirby M.; Reifers J.; Goodman P.; Wood M.; Byars T.; Griffin M.; Wise D.; Camus A.; Waldbieser G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Idiopathic catfish anemia (ICA) is an important cause of protracted mortalities in pond-cultured channel ( Ictalurus punctatus ) and hybrid ( I. punctatus × I. furcatus ) catfish. Herein, fish and water samples from spontaneous outbreaks in two non-adjacent identically managed ponds were utilized to investigate potential roles of environmental and intestinal microbiomes, and host transcriptome profiles in ICA. Microbiome profiling was performed on posterior intestinal samples from affected pond fish, healthy fish from an unaffected pond and raceway, and water samples from the three ponds. All fish were derived from the same original cohort. Head kidney, liver, and intestinal samples were used for transcriptomic analyses. Characterization of microbial communities did not provide strong evidence for a bacterial role (e.g., iron sequestration) in ICA. Anemic fish demonstrated upregulation of genes involved in erythropoiesis and iron transport/storage in the head kidney and liver but lacked compensatory upregulation of iron absorption genes in the intestine and corresponding downregulation of hepcidin, a key regulator of iron metabolism, in the liver. Results support previous research suggesting ICA is due to an inability to absorb sufficient iron from typical feed formulations. Findings suggest dysregulation of host iron metabolism and provide novel molecular targets for further investigation.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a clinical nomogram for predicting sarcopenia risk in elderly patients with chronic heart failure
Article.Authors: Han F.; Zhai Y.; Wu Y.; Li M.; Du X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To identify risk factors for sarcopenia in elderly chronic heart failure (CHF) patients and develop a predictive nomogram. Cross-sectional study with random split-sample (7:3) derivation and internal validation. Tertiary hospital in Shanxi, China. 317 elderly CHF patients (July 2023–June 2024); 221 in derivation cohort, 96 in validation. The primary outcome was sarcopenia. Primary evaluation metrics included the area under the ROC curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Secondary measures included sensitivity, specificity, and the Kappa coefficient. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess model robustness, including exclusion of grip strength from the model and reclassification of sarcopenia according to the AWGS 2025 criteria. Five independent risk factors for sarcopenia were identified: fatigue, physical activity level, calf circumference, body mass index (BMI), and grip strength (all p < 0.05). The model showed good performance, with a C-index of 0.951. The AUC was 0.955 (95% CI: 0.929–0.980) in the derivation cohort and 0.951 (95% CI: 0.907–0.995) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA confirmed the model’s clinical utility. Sensitivity analysis excluding grip strength yielded an AUC of 0.949 (95% CI: 0.925–0.973). Reclassification using AWGS 2025 criteria resulted in an AUC of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.946–0.982), confirming model robustness across different diagnostic frameworks. Fatigue, low physical activity, reduced calf circumference, low BMI, and low grip strength are independent risk factors for sarcopenia in elderly CHF patients. The validated nomogram has strong predictive performance and may help clinicians identify high-risk individuals. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the model’s robustness across different variable compositions and diagnostic frameworks.

Article.Title: Luteolin mitigates thiamethoxam-induced hepato-intestinal injury and impaired growth in Nile tilapia by modulating oxidative stress, inflammation, and intestinal barrier integrity
Article.Authors: Abuzaied H.; Yasin N.; Hashim A.; Rashad M.; Mabrouk M.; Elnakeeb M.; El-Habback H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated the toxic effects of thiamethoxam (TMX) on the liver and intestine of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) during a 14-day exposure and evaluated the protective potential of dietary luteolin. A total of 180 fish were randomly assigned to six groups (3 replicate aquaria per treatment, 10 fish per aquarium), with n = 7 fish/group sampled for biochemical and histological analyses: a control group, luteolin-treated groups (200 and 400 mg/kg diet), a TMX-exposed group (100 mg/L), and combined TMX plus luteolin groups. After 14 days, growth performance and oxidative stress indices were evaluated. The expression of genes related to xenobiotic metabolism (cytochrome P450 1A1, CYP1A1), cellular stress (heat shock protein 70, HSP70), immune signaling (Toll-like receptor 2, TLR-2), barrier integrity (occludin), and growth regulation (ghrelin and insulin-like growth factor 1, IGF-1) was assessed to provide an integrated molecular evaluation of TMX-induced hepato-intestinal injury and luteolin-mediated protection, along with histopathological alterations. TMX significantly reduced daily weight gain, length gain, and final body weight, increased malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, decreased glutathione (GSH) content, and downregulated glutathione peroxidase (GPX) ( P < 0.001). It also upregulated CYP1A1, HSP70, and TLR-2, while downregulating occludin, ghrelin, and IGF-1 ( P < 0.001), and was accompanied by hepatocyte degeneration, vascular congestion, reduced hepatic glycogen, villus atrophy, inflammatory cell infiltration, and goblet-cell hyperplasia. Co-supplementation with luteolin (200 and 400 mg/kg diet) increased final body weight by 8.1% and 6.6%, respectively; reduced MDA and restored GSH and GPX; downregulated CYP1A1, HSP70, and TLR-2; upregulated occludin, ghrelin, and IGF-1; and reduced hepatic and intestinal lesions ( P < 0.05). Collectively, these molecular and histological improvements demonstrate luteolin’s hepato-intestinal protective potential against TMX toxicity and, to our knowledge, provide the first evidence supporting its potential use as a functional dietary additive in Nile tilapia aquaculture.

Article.Authors: Aldelemy A.; Al-Dulaimi A.; Abd-Alhameed R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Healthy-reference information may improve radiofrequency fracture-sensing representations under anatomical domain shift, but its benefit must be separated from noise dependence and threshold transfer. For early healing, independent same-SNR referencing increased mean macro AUROC from 0.7935 to 0.9725; the matched difference was 0.1790 (multiplicity-adjusted 99.5% H2 interval 0.1343–0.2072), conditional on fixed anatomy and fitted models. All six matched endpoint contrasts favoured reference assistance. Equal-budget comparison favoured same-SNR over cross-SNR referencing; a second same-SNR reference provided no clear additional early-healing benefit. Early-healing pooled AUROC was 0.8567; locked sensitivity-targeted thresholds transferred with mean sensitivity 82.83% and specificity 20.00%. Saved-model replay on ten selected configurations across twelve numerical/noise settings changed 1,266 of 9,600 Youden and 539 sensitivity-targeted decision instances relative to baseline. These repeated instances are not independent patients or new cohort performance. The framework separates reference-information benefit, noise variation and decision transfer. These simulation-only findings do not estimate human diagnostic accuracy or electromagnetic continuum accuracy.

Article.Title: Effects of olanzapine, crocin, and their combination on PTSD-like behaviors and hippocampal BDNF/CREB expression in male rats
Article.Authors: Barmake M.; Ghorbani Yekta B.; Sari S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Post-traumatic stress disorderr (PTSD) is a psychiatric disorder that may develop following traumatic events. In rodents, fear conditioning is widely used to model PTSD-like behavior. This study evaluated the effects of olanzapine, crocin, and their combination on freezing behavior, locomotor activity, rearing, hot-plate response latency, forced-swim-test immobility, passive avoidance memory, and hippocampal brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and cAMP-response element-binding protein (CREB) mRNA expression in male rats subjected to fear conditioning. Olanzapine and olanzapine + crocin reduced freezing, whereas crocin alone had no significant effect. Rearing behavior was increased in the olanzapine and olanzapine + crocin groups, while locomotor activity was unchanged. Hot-plate response latency was decreased in the olanzapine and olanzapine + crocin groups. Importantly, forced-swim-test immobility duration was significantly decreased in all treatment groups, including crocin alone ( P < 0.001 versus the PTSD group). Passive avoidance memory was unaffected. Hippocampal BDNF mRNA expression was increased in all treatment groups, with a greater increase in the combination group, whereas CREB mRNA expression was increased in the crocin and olanzapine + crocin groups. These findings suggest that olanzapine, alone or combined with crocin, ameliorated several PTSD-like behavioral alterations, while combined treatment was associated with broader hippocampal transcriptional changes.

Article.Title: Modality-adaptive learning for glaucoma diagnosis with incomplete availability of fundus photographs and visual field data
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Chen J.; Zheng Y.; Ye J.; Si K.; Gong W.
Article.Abstract: Multimodal diagnostic models often assume that all input modalities are available, whereas clinical datasets commonly contain incomplete examination records. We developed CGMA-Net to evaluate glaucoma diagnosis under three modality-availability conditions: fundus photography only, visual field testing only, and paired fundus and visual field data. CGMA-Net combines modality-specific encoders, an explicit availability mask, and gated adaptive fusion to prevent absent inputs from contributing to the fused representation without imputing missing examinations. The model was evaluated in a retrospective two-center cohort comprising 5,181 samples from 3,262 participants, with participant-level separation of training, validation, and test sets. On the internal test set, CGMA-Net achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.997, with 97.6% accuracy, 98.9% sensitivity, and 94.9% specificity, and maintained high discrimination across modality-availability conditions. In ablation analyses, removing gated fusion produced a larger performance decrease than removing cross-attention. Post hoc temperature scaling improved probability calibration without changing classification metrics. Both learned uncertainty and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty were higher for misclassified than correctly classified samples. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of modality-adaptive glaucoma classification across CFP-only, VF-only, and paired CFP–VF settings in a selected retrospective cohort, but do not establish performance in an unselected clinical population. Validation in a consecutive cohort that includes diagnostically ambiguous cases, relevant differential diagnoses, and examinations of variable quality is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Geometric control of maximal entanglement via bound states in the continuum
Article.Authors: Legón A.; Rojas M.; Orellana P.; Norambuena A.
Article.Abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) suppress emission into a waveguide through destructive interference, but do not eliminate independent environmental losses. We study two giant atoms coupled at spatially separated points to a coupled-resonator waveguide and characterize the spectral conditions for BICs with maximally entangled normalized atomic components. An exact compact-state construction establishes a degenerate BIC subspace at band centre, distinguishing BIC existence from state selection. Within a family defined by an additional slope-cancellation condition at both reciprocal resonances, the connection-length ratio determines the conditional concurrence and the propagation phase determines the Bell-like sector. The physical atomic concurrence also depends on the photonic dressing. Full finite-mode dynamics and a mixed-state loss calculation quantify retention of initially prepared entanglement under calibration errors, atomic relaxation and dephasing, and resonator loss. We also discuss effective-coupling compensation for unequal connection lengths within a spectrally admissible family. These results connect analytical BIC design with the control requirements and environmental limitations of entanglement retention.

Article.Title: Amendment of a drug utilization study protocol based on results from a real-world pilot study of liraglutide use in Europe
Article.Authors: Major-Pedersen A.; Aberle J.; Sbraccia P.; Rathor N.; Olsen A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Economic and time constraints may incite researchers to avoid formalized pilot studies. Here, we report results of a pilot study that amended the ensuing drug utilization study (DUS) protocol, thus ascertaining fit-for-purpose data availability and quality, to better support regulatory decision-making. This retrospective, multicenter medical chart review in Germany and Italy, 6 months after Saxenda® (liraglutide 3.0 mg, a once-daily human glucagon-like peptide-1 analog for weight management) launch, ahead of a full DUS, collected patient data. The target study population included 100 initiators (25 Saxenda® and 25 Victoza® initiators in both Germany and Italy). Written informed consent was obtained before medical chart data extraction. Overall, 218 sites were contacted, with 39 Saxenda® initiators (33 in Italy; six in Germany) and 52 Victoza® initiators (31 in Italy; 21 in Germany). Patient records were obtained for all enrolled Saxenda® and Victoza® initiators in Italy and Germany; however, availability of individual study variables varied, with follow-up body weight showing the greatest degree of missingness among Saxenda® initiators. The pilot study indicated a poor enrollment feasibility of Saxenda® initiators in Germany and an unfit-for-purpose dose-related data quality. Based on these findings, refinements were implemented in the ensuing DUS protocol to improve the collection of fit-for-purpose real-world data for regulatory decision-making.

Article.Title: Polylactic acid (PLA)/Polycaprolactone (PCL)/Hydroxyapatite (HA) three-dimensional porous scaffolds for bone tissue engineering
Article.Authors: Nazari M.; Zebarjad S.; Sherafat Z.; Sani M.; Falamarzi K.
Article.Abstract: Bone tissue engineering requires three-dimensional scaffolds that mimic the extracellular matrix, support cell behavior, and degrade at an appropriate rate. This study fabricated polylactic acid/polycaprolactone/hydroxyapatite (PLA/PCL/HA) composite scaffolds via solvent casting/particle leaching and systematically investigated the effects of PLA:PCL weight ratios (0:100, 25:75, 50:50, 75:25, 100:0) and HA concentrations (1, 3, and 5 wt%) on wettability, biodegradability, bioactivity, cytocompatibility, and osteogenic potential. Results demonstrated that increasing PLA content in the PLA/PCL blend had only a modest effect on hydrophilicity, with contact angles of unfilled scaffolds remaining in the range of approximately 110–113° due to the polar ester groups of PLA. In contrast, the incorporation of HA nanoparticles markedly improved wettability through both chemical (polar hydroxyl and phosphate groups) and physical (surface roughening) mechanisms, reducing the contact angle from 112.76° (pure PCL) to 84.34° for the 75PLA/25PCL-5HA formulation. Bioactivity assessment in simulated body fluid for 28 days showed calcium phosphate layer formation on all HA-containing scaffolds. The 75PLA/25PCL-5HA and 50PLA/50PCL-5HA samples achieved Ca/P atomic ratios of 1.77 and 1.58, respectively, both of which fall within the apatite range and are close to the stoichiometric HA value of 1.67 (deviations of 0.10 and 0.09, respectively). MTT assays showed maintained MG-63 cell metabolic activity across all scaffold formulations during the 7-day culture period MTT assays showed maintained MG-63 cell metabolic activity across all scaffold formulations during the 7-day culture period. Alizarin Red staining demonstrated that HA-containing scaffolds significantly promoted calcium deposition compared to HA-free samples, with the 75PLA/25PCL-5HA sample exhibiting the highest mineralization capacity. These findings establish that PLA/PCL/HA composite scaffolds fabricated by solvent casting/particle leaching, particularly the 75PLA/25PCL-5HA formulation, represent promising candidates for bone tissue regeneration applications.

Article.Title: Assessment of eco-label properties criteria from ceramic sludge industry incorporated into fired clay brick
Article.Authors: Detho A.; Jufri I.; Hassan M.; Alanazi A.; Ahmed A.; Rassem H.; Mesalam Y.; Kadir A.
Article.Abstract: An assortment of manufacturing procedures, including but not limited to water treatment, effluent treatment, and on-site sanitation systems, generate sludge, which is a semi-solid mixture. With the disposal of sludge posing a significant challenge, researchers have explored innovative methods that involve incorporating ceramic sludge as a raw material in brick production. The fundamental goal of this research project is to determine the most effective ratio of fired clay bricks to ceramic sludge, taking into account the bricks' physical and mechanical properties. Moreover, the study seeks to evaluate how these properties align with the eco-label standards for brick manufacturing. The research involved combining six different concentrations of ceramic sludge (0%, 1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, and 30%) with fired clay bricks, subsequently subjecting them to firing at 1050°C in a monitored furnace. The results showed that incorporating ceramic sludge improved the compressive strength of the fired clay bricks, with the 30% ceramic sludge brick achieving the highest compressive strength of 25 N/mm 2 compared with 15.22 N/mm 2 for the control brick. The density of the 30% ceramic sludge brick decreased to 1789.48 kg.m 3 , while the shrinkage remained below the specified limit. Furthermore, the 30% ceramic sludge brick satisfied the evaluated requirements of British Standard (BS 3921:1985) and the SIRIM ECO SIRIM ECO 023:2016 for the properties investigated. Consequently, as long as appropriate mixing and manufacturing processes are employed, ceramic sludge can be utilized efficiently as part of the material in the construction of bricks. This practice not only offers an eco-friendly disposal solution for ceramic sludge but also presents a viable alternative for the substitution of conventional materials in brick production.

Article.Title: Extracorporeal norepinephrine filtration is associated with increasing norepinephrine requirements during percutaneous hepatic perfusion with melphalan
Article.Authors: Ebel S.; Struck M.; Peitzsch M.; Kirsten H.; Bösemann D.; Denecke T.; Gößmann H.; Berg T.; Hempel C.; Matz-Soja M.; van Bömmel F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chemosaturation with percutaneous hepatic perfusion (CS-PHP) using melphalan is frequently associated with profound hypotension, necessitating high-dose norepinephrine support. We investigated the potential of the extracorporeal chemofilter to remove circulating norepinephrine. In this prospective observational study, paired blood samples were obtained upstream and downstream of the extracorporeal filter during CS-PHP at predefined procedural timepoints. Norepinephrine was quantified using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Transfilter concentration reduction was assessed in conjunction with temporal changes in norepinephrine administration during the procedure. A total of ten CS-PHP procedures in eight patients were analyzed. This included the main test, for which one procedure was performed on each patient (n = 8), as well as an additional test on one patient, for which two additional procedures were performed to enable an intra-individual assessment of three consecutive procedures. Circulating norepinephrine concentrations increased during treatment, peaking upstream of the filter during active filtration. The filter reduced norepinephrine concentrations by a median of 91.3% after bypass closure and 91.9% during melphalan perfusion (both p = 0.008). Norepinephrine infusion rates increased from a median of 0.2 μg/kg/min after inferior vena cava occlusion to 0.6 μg/kg/min immediately after filter activation ( p < 0.01). These rates remained elevated throughout filtration before decreasing after completion of the procedure. The temporal relationship between transfilter concentration reduction of norepinephrine and a significant increase in norepinephrine administration suggests an association with hemodynamic effects during CS-PHP.

Article.Title: Monte Carlo assessment of a D–T neutron generator-based beam shaping assembly for BNCT: moderator effects on neutron spectrum and dose
Article.Authors: Asghari S.; Ghapanvary M.; Alavi A.; Ghalehasadi A.; Dehghani V.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a Monte Carlo parametric assessment of a multilayer beam shaping assembly (BSA) for boron neutron capture therapy using a 14.1 MeV D–T neutron source. A validated reference calculation was retained for the principal beam-quality quantities, while additional controlled calculations were used to reassess material substitution, finite-source and aperture effects, and one-at-a-time layer-thickness sensitivity. Under a common computational framework, AlF 3 provided the highest epithermal response and the lowest fast-to-epithermal ratio among the tested moderator substitutions. Paraffin and light water reduced the epithermal component by approximately 74% and 73%, respectively, relative to AlF 3 , whereas D 2 O and polystyrene produced intermediate and similar responses. The validated reference configuration yielded an epithermal neutron flux of 1.1×10 9 n cm⁻ 2 s⁻ 1 and a beam directionality of 0.78; however, its fast-neutron dose per epithermal flux, 2.4×10⁻ 13 Gy·cm 2 /n, remained about 20% above the historical IAEA-TECDOC-1223 design benchmark. Additional calculations showed that the finite 1 cm-radius source did not produce a statistically resolved change relative to the point-source reference, whereas increasing the aperture from 10 to 24 cm increased the aperture-averaged epithermal response. Thickness variations revealed substantial transmission trade-offs and did not establish a unique global optimum. The 36 cm AlF 3 , 4 cm Fe, and 2.6 cm Cd dimensions are therefore reported as the reference geometry of the existing assembly. The results support continued computational refinement but do not constitute clinical qualification.

Article.Title: Resilient UAV formation tracking using hybrid fractional-order terminal sliding mode control
Article.Authors: Saeed Bin Gaufan K.; Alyazidi N.; El-Ferik S.; Saif A.; Al-Dhaifallah M.; Mysorewala M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) formations are increasingly deployed in surveillance, transportation, and search-and-rescue operations; however, precise cooperative coordination remains challenged by severe nonlinearities, underactuation, stochastic perturbations, and parametric uncertainties. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an adaptive fractional-order nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control (AFONFTSMC) framework, evaluated across both integer-order and fractional-order leader-follower quadrotor architectures. In the proposed hybrid architecture, fractional-order modeling is incorporated exclusively into the leader’s translational subsystem, whereas the followers retain computationally efficient integer-order dynamics. This structural asymmetry facilitates a rigorous assessment of leader dynamics while preserving a unified control law across all agents. A Lyapunov-based analysis demonstrates finite-time convergence and global closed-loop stability in the presence of random disturbances and parametric variations. Comprehensive simulation results on a complex helical trajectory demonstrate that the fractional-order leader achieves convergence within 0.15 s and yields an 85–92% reduction in integrated tracking error metrics (IAE and ITAE) compared to the integer-order configuration under nominal conditions. Under severe parametric uncertainties (including up to a 65% mass variation) and continuous stochastic disturbances, the proposed hybrid framework restricts peak transient horizontal position errors to within $$\pm 0.01$$ m and reduces vertical tracking deviation by more than 80%, accompanied by rapid disturbance recovery in under 1.5 s and chatter-free control effort. These findings, established through comprehensive numerical simulations under realistic quadrotor physical parameters and continuous stochastic perturbations, demonstrate that integrating fractional-order dynamics into the leader vehicle provides a resilient mechanism for multi-UAV cooperative control, offering a verified analytical foundation for future experimental flight testing.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Active genomic surveillance is increasingly needed to detect the emergence and spread of arboviruses before outbreaks become apparent. Usutu virus ( Orthoflavivirus usutuense , USUV) has expanded across Europe during the last three decades, but molecular confirmation of its circulation in Portugal has been lacking. Within an active surveillance program for orthoflaviviruses in hunted red-legged partridges ( Alectoris rufa ), we screened vascular growing feathers from 249 apparently healthy birds collected in southern Portugal during the 2021–2023 hunting seasons. Article.Authors: Manikandan D.; Swarna M.; Nivetha D.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid growth of video content on platforms such as Instagram and YouTube, the spread of harmful and illegal material by unauthenticated users has become a serious concern, particularly for children, youth, and other vulnerable audiences. The system integrates DeepLabV3 + for semantic segmentation and Faster R-CNN for object detection to analyze visual elements, while Wav2Vec 2.0 and a CNN are used to identify abusive speech and ambient threats such as gunshots and screams. BERT is employed to detect toxic and hate speech in video-related text. A priority-based Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) scheduler orchestrates these models for efficient execution and load balancing, and Firefly Optimization is used for hyperparameter tuning to enhance accuracy. The implemented multimodal system achieves an overall detection accuracy of 98.33%, and includes a customizable Content Sentinel module that enables real-time actions such as skipping flagged segments. This solution promotes ethical video sharing and offers a scalable approach to content moderation across social media platforms.

The elemental composition of the plant ash was identified by means of energy dispersive x-ray fluorescence (edxrf) to evaluate the elemental composition. The surface wettability of the composite sheet was measured by water contact angle analysis whereas water absorption and thickness swelling were investigated after immersion in distilled water for short periods of time to understand their moisture affinity. The findings showed good result by using fiber treated with plant ash alkali treatment composites compared to the untreated composites in terms of wettability through several tests which are contact angle, water absorption, density and thickness swelling tests. Meanwhile, APBRPLA-5 exhibited highest contact angle, APBRPLA-20 exhibited lowest density value (1.516 ± 0.029 g/cm 3 ). Moreover, there were moderate improvements in Izod impact strength and scanning electron microscopy (sem) images showing morphological characteristic of the modified BR and PLA matrix.

Article.Title: Geomicrobiology of iron rich stalactites and implications for habitability of Martian iron deposits
Article.Authors: Mansor M.; Višić H.; Dreher C.; Zirner A.; Markl G.; Mentzer S.; Duda J.; Escudero C.; Kappler A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exploration of Earth’s subsurface environments continues to expand our understanding of microbial diversity and associated mineral deposits, providing valuable analogues for the search for life on other worlds. Here, we investigate Fe-rich stalactites (up to 1 m long; ~51.7 wt% Fe) from the abandoned Segen Gottes mine (Germany) as an analogue for Fe-rich deposits on Mars. Acidic drip waters (pH 2.7 to 6.3) produced by sulfide oxidation are enriched in dissolved Fe, S, Si, and trace metals. Mineralogical and petrographic analyses show porous cores dominated by akaganeite and goethite, surrounded by a jarosite-rich crust with spatially variable As-rich laminations. Microbial communities are dominated by acidophilic aerobic heterotrophs (~ 98%), with Fe(II)-oxidizing Leptospirillum comprising only 1.4 to 1.7%. Micro-CT reveals isolated pores (~ 1.33% of pore volume) that may support anoxic microhabitats for Fe(III)- and sulfate-reducing microorganisms. We propose a three-stage formation model involving microbial Fe(II) oxidation, precipitation of poorly crystalline As-rich Fe(III) phases, and transformation into akaganeite, goethite, or jarosite depending on geochemical conditions. These findings suggest that porous Fe-rich deposits can host diverse redox metabolisms and that akaganeite-goethite-jarosite assemblages can form under ambient near-surface conditions, without requiring volcanic-derived fluids, broadening the range of terrestrial conditions capable of producing Martian-relevant Fe-mineral assemblages.

Article.Authors: Li Y.; Liu C.; Zhao Z.; Liang F.; Ma H.; Xue T.; Wang C.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health challenge. While "inflammation-lipid imbalance" is implicated in renal injury, the association between the high-sensitivity C-reactive protein to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (hs-CRP/HDL-C) and rapid kidney function decline (RKFD) remains under-investigated. To investigate the longitudinal association of the hs-CRP/HDL-C ratio with RKFD and incident low eGFR in Chinese older adults. This longitudinal study utilized data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). We analyzed the association between the baseline hs-CRP/HDL-C ratio and subsequent renal outcomes, including RKFD and incident low eGFR, in older adults free of CKD at baseline. Multivariable regression models were employed to adjust for potential confounders. During the follow-up period, participants in the highest quartile of the hs-CRP/HDL-C ratio exhibited a significantly increased risk of both RKFD and incident low eGFR compared to the lowest quartile. An overall positive correlation was observed for both outcomes, independent of traditional metabolic risk factors. An elevated hs-CRP/HDL-C ratio is an independent associative indicator for RKFD and incident low eGFR in Chinese older adults. This composite marker may assist in identifying individuals at elevated risk of renal progression.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is one of the most accessible vibrational probes in materials laboratories, but its forward problem (structure to spectrum) is bottlenecked by the cost of density functional perturbation theory, and its inverse problem (spectrum to structure) typically relies on retrieval against curated references. We introduce RamanGPT, a deep-learning framework that addresses both directions for crystalline inorganic materials. The forward model, an Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network (ALIGNN), is trained on the 5,099-material Computational Raman Database and predicts 200-bin spectra over 50–1000 $$\hbox {cm}^{-1}$$ with 53.8% of the 509 held-out materials reaching an active-region cosine similarity of at least 0.354, capturing qualitative features of the target spectrum. The model also shows qualitative agreement with an experimental measurement of metallic 1T $$\hbox {VSe}_{2}$$ , a system absent from the training set. The inverse model fine-tunes DiffractGPT, a large language model already trained for diffraction-to-structure generation, via Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation on Raman-plus-formula prompts, recovering lattice parameters with mean absolute errors of 1.13–2.14 Å and reduced-formula consistency of 92.1% on 508 held-out materials, compared to 17.1% for a formula-conditioned retrieval baseline given identical inputs. A cosine-similarity matcher and an inverse $$\rightarrow$$ relax $$\rightarrow$$ forward consistency loop are deployed at https://atomgpt.org/raman .

Article.Authors: Akçay S.; Akkurt M.
Article.Abstract: Robot-assisted rehabilitation is increasingly used after stroke, but no instrument evaluates whether YouTube videos convey guideline-based clinical content. In this cross-sectional study, 150 YouTube videos were screened and 37 meeting eligibility criteria were scored by a primary rater using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmark criteria, and the Stroke Robotic Rehabilitation Guideline-Based Evaluation Criteria (SRR-GEC), a 10-item checklist of guideline-derived clinical-content domains; a second rater independently re-scored the sample for reliability. Most videos (81.1%) were rated moderate-to-high quality by GQS but showed limited reliability on mDISCERN and JAMA; SRR-GEC completeness averaged 7.97 of 10, not directly comparable in absolute terms given the instruments’ differing item difficulty. GQS correlated significantly with mDISCERN and SRR-GEC but not JAMA. Explicit reporting of treatment parameters and safety/feasibility content showed the strongest exploratory association with GQS, although which specific item remained associated with GQS after adjustment depended on which rater’s scores were used. Raw engagement metrics were unrelated to quality. Videos narrated by a narrator with a verified clinical credential showed numerically higher quality, not surviving multiple-comparison correction, and video age was not associated with quality. These videos showed meaningful limitations in reliability and transparency, came mostly from sources whose clinical background was unverified, and their comparatively higher guideline-based content coverage reflects the presence rather than the accuracy of guideline-derived information; they should not replace clinician-provided guidance for this technically demanding intervention.

Article.Authors: Singh S.; Singh N.; Tandon D.; Kumar S.; Singh R.; Singh V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mental health problems, such as depression, anxiety, stress, bipolar disorder, and thoughts of suicide are a serious health issue in the world today. Because users of social media platforms generate vast amounts of text, these data can provide researchers with insight into their emotional and psychological condition. However, owing to linguistic variability, contextual ambiguity, and the complex language of emotions, extracting meaningful indications of mental health from noisy, unstructured social media data is challenging. In this study, the authors propose a hybrid deep-learning framework, called FBert-GRU, which combines the fine-tuned Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) with Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) to learn the contextual semantic information and sequential emotional patterns. The framework was evaluated on a public mental health dataset comprising social media posts that were labeled for several mental health conditions. The experimental results showed an accuracy of 96%, a precision of 87%, a recall of 82%, an F1-score of 81% and an AUC-ROC of 94%. The experimental results showed that the proposed method using contextual embeddings and sequential learning improved the detection of mental health-related signals from social media text compared with the benchmark models. The suggested framework offers a promising strategy for conducting mental health evaluations and behavioral trend analysis at a large scale and for the digital monitoring of mental health.

Article.Abstract: Running times across sprint and middle-distance events may be related in physically trained students, but the extent to which participant profiles reflect overall performance level or distance-specific specialization remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the relationships among 100-m, 200-m, 400-m, and 800-m running performances and to explore whether participant-level clusters with distinct running-performance patterns could be identified using hierarchical cluster analysis. A pooled cross-sectional observational study included 196 male third-year students from the Faculty of Physical Education and Sport, University of East Sarajevo, representing 10 annual academic cohorts assessed between January 2012 and December 2023. Descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation analysis, and participant-level hierarchical cluster analysis using Ward’s method were applied. All four running times were positively correlated, with the strongest association observed between the 100-m and 200-m events ( r = 0.799, p < 0.001). Participant-level clustering identified two broad performance profiles. Cluster 1 comprised 124 participants (63.3%) and had faster mean times across all four events, whereas Cluster 2 comprised 72 participants (36.7%) and had slower mean times. Descriptive between-cluster effect sizes ranged from 1.13 to 5.24. The two-cluster solution had a median adjusted Rand index of 0.949 (IQR 0.876–0.974) across repeated subsamples. These internal comparisons and stability estimates do not constitute independent validation of the profiles. In this sample of physical education and sport students, participant-level clustering primarily reflected overall running-performance level rather than distinct sprint- and middle-distance specialization. not applicable.
