Article.Authors: Fuchs S.; Kuhn T.; Meyn K.; Kihara T.; Garbe-Schönberg D.; Klischies M.; Freitag R.; Schwarz-Schampera U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We report the discovery and characterization of fourteen hydrothermal vent fields around the Rodrigues Triple Junction, including the first fields characterized in detail on the Southeast Indian Ridge. The fields occur in the axial valley, on ridge flanks, on an off-axis volcanic plateau and at non-transform offsets. Most are basalt-hosted, but four at non-transform offsets and near the triple junction are ultramafic-hosted, on gabbro and peridotite exhumed along large faults. Brine-type fluids are vented in fields of both host-rock types, vapor-type fluids only in basalt-hosted fields with young volcanism. Ultramafic-hosted fields vent cooler, metal-poorer brines, but the host rock is recorded more clearly in their sulfides, enriched in Sn and Au and depleted in As, Tl, Sb, Mo and Se. Inactive sites outnumber active ones in most fields; their degree of oxidation records a relative sequence from active venting to long-inactive mounds. Indian Ocean vent taxa dominate the megafauna. Repeated near-bottom survey show that sulfide occurrences are not rare, even 16 km off-axis.

The Langmuir adsorption isotherm model fits the adsorption behavior, suggesting strong and spontaneous adsorption of molecules on the steel surface. Molecular dynamics simulations on the Fe (110) surface give insight into the adsorption geometry and energy on an atomic scale, showing stronger interaction of PMH than PDM, in agreement with the experimental findings. The experimental and simulation results underline the influence of molecular structure on the adsorption strength and protective performance of pyrazole-based inhibitors and provide insights for the development of more effective pyrazole-based inhibitors in acidic environments.

Article.Abstract: Interactions among ore fragments (OF), interfacial transition zones (ITZ), and weakly cemented matrix (WCM) govern impact response in weakly cemented fractured orebodies, yet phase-specific responses and internal-energy partitioning remain insufficiently quantified. From 10 to 80 J, peak force rose from 18.0 to 25.2 kN, maximum penetration from 0.380 to 0.615 mm, and the high-response volume fraction from 16.59 to 28.25%. Response preferentially localized in ITZ, propagated and coalesced through continuous WCM, and increasingly involved OF. WCM carried the largest internal energy, ITZ the highest phase-averaged internal-energy density, and OF's energy share increased from 22.0 to 29.7%. Despite an eightfold increase in input energy, summed phase internal energy rose only from 3.161 to 5.371 J, while the peak three-phase internal-energy ratio fell from 31.61 to 6.71%, showing internal-energy accumulation was not proportional to input energy. These results reveal overlapping ITZ localization, WCM propagation, and OF involvement, supporting joint evaluation of mechanical, phase-specific spatial, and energy-partitioning metrics rather than reliance on peak load or affected extent alone.

Article.Title: Lateral-torsional buckling of steel beam with clamped ends
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Wang F.; Yang J.; Shu X.; Zhang G.; Pan J.
Article.Abstract: A multitude of studies have been conducted on the overall stability of steel beams. Elastic linear analytical solutions for the global stability of simply supported steel I-beams subjected to transverse loads have been comprehensively developed. However, the buckling behaviour under the fixed end conditions with the non-linear material and geometric properties is not adequately studied. To address this problem, both theoretical and numerical investigations are performed in this study to understand the lateral-torsional buckling (LTB) behaviour of the steel I-beams with fixed ends. A comprehensive series of parametric investigations are conducted to scrutinize the influencing factors of the critical buckling load. The analysis results suggest that the span length and the flange width are proven to be the key influencing factors on the overall stability. Moreover, a modified design model is put forward based on the energy method and regression analysis to verify the numerical results. It is demonstrated that the outcomes of the proposed model are consistent with those obtained through numerical analysis.

Article.Title: Association between renal vascular index from microvascular flow imaging and corpus callosal length Z score in fetal growth restriction
Article.Authors: Li C.; Li L.; Yang Y.; Fan H.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the association between the near-field renal microvascular flow imaging (MV-Flow) vascular index (VIMV) and corpus callosal length (CCL) Z score in fetuses with fetal growth restriction (FGR). This prospective single-center study included 110 fetuses with FGR and 161 appropriate-for-gestational-age controls. Near-field renal VIMV and midsagittal CCL were assessed cross-sectionally during a single ultrasound examination; CCL Z scores were derived from an internal gestational-age-specific reference based on controls.Within the FGR cohort, multivariable linear regression evaluated the VIMV–CCL association after adjustment for gestational age, FGR subtype, head circumference (HC) Z score, and abdominal circumference (AC) Z score.FGR-control VIMV and subtype analyses were supportive or secondary. Within the FGR cohort, each 1-percentage-point increase in VIMV was independently associated with a 0.28-unit higher CCL Z score (95% CI, 0.15–0.40; P < 0.001), with consistent findings across sensitivity analyses. Renal VIMV was also lower in FGR than in controls (26.85% [23.63–28.50] vs. 37.90% [36.00–40.10]; P < 0.001). Early-onset FGR had lower VIMV than late-onset FGR even after gestational-age adjustment, whereas CCL Z scores were similar between subtypes; secondary interaction analysis showed a steeper VIMV–CCL association in early-onset FGR (interaction P = 0.028). Within FGR, near-field renal VIMV was independently associated with CCL Z score; this cross-sectional association does not establish causality.Combined assessment of renal microvascular imaging characteristics and gestational-age-standardized CCL may provide complementary quantitative ultrasound information in FGR.

Article.Title: Prediction of single-pile bearing capacity in high-fill areas from O-cell tests using L-BFGS-B inversion
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; Chen M.; Wang J.; Zhi C.; Wei H.; Zhao H.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: In O-cell pile load tests conducted at high-fill mine spoil-dump sites, testing is often terminated before the pile reaches its ultimate bearing state owing to the loading-capacity limitation of the O-cell and the requirement to avoid destructive loading of engineering piles, making it difficult to directly determine the ultimate vertical bearing capacity of the pile. To address this issue, a prediction method based on the limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno algorithm with box constraints (L-BFGS-B) is proposed. Based on load-transfer theory, a depth-dependent ideal elastoplastic model for shaft resistance and a bilinear hardening model for toe resistance are established. The soil-layer-specific coefficients governing the depth-dependent shaft stiffness and the corresponding pile–soil interface elastic-limit displacements, together with the pile-toe initial stiffness, hardening stiffness, and elastic-limit displacement, are back-analyzed within prescribed bounds by minimizing the mean squared displacement residual between the measured and calculated O-cell responses. The complete load–displacement responses of the upper and lower pile segments are then reconstructed and converted into an equivalent conventional pile-head load–displacement curve using the equal-displacement method, from which the ultimate bearing capacity is determined. Finally, ABAQUS numerical models of the O-cell test and conventional static load test are established for comparative analysis. The results show that the proposed method effectively reproduces the measured O-cell responses, and the back-analyzed axial-force distributions are in good overall agreement with the numerical simulation results. The predicted ultimate vertical bearing capacity of the single pile agrees well with the conventional static-loading simulation result, with a relative deviation of approximately 5.9%. The proposed method provides an efficient approach for back-analyzing load-transfer parameters from incomplete O-cell test data and predicting the bearing capacity of single piles in high-fill mine spoil-dump sites.

Article.Title: A comparative expert evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini on urolithiasis: clinical accuracy versus citation reliability
Article.Authors: Aktaş Y.; Tunçekin A.
Article.Abstract: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) presents opportunities and risks, including ‘hallucination’, for urological practice. This study compares the performance of ChatGPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro in answering urolithiasis queries, and evaluates the discrepancy between clinical accuracy and citation reliability. In this cross-sectional study conducted between January and February 2026, 65 clinical questions based on the 2025 European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines were administered to both models. Two blinded, board-certified urologists independently evaluated the 130 generated responses. The outputs were scored on three separate dimensions. These were medical accuracy, guideline adherence and citation quality. Each dimension was scored on a 1–5 scale. Gemini 3 Pro demonstrated statistically higher scores compared to ChatGPT 5.2 Pro in terms of medical accuracy and guideline adherence (both p < 0.001). Gemini 3 Pro provided responses that were rated as clinically appropriate by experts at a rate of 98.5%, compared to 81.5% for GPT-5.2 Pro ( p = 0.001). However, both models had critically flawed citation reliability. At the overall response level, ChatGPT generated high-risk responses in 95.4% of cases, compared to 69.2% for Gemini ( p < 0.001). At the individual citation level, 45.8% of GPT-5.2 Pro’s citations and 24.8% of Gemini 3 Pro’s citations were entirely fabricated (score 1a). Meanwhile, 30.3% and 31.4% of citations, respectively, were real publications with incorrect or mismatched DOIs (score 1b). Notably, there was no statistical correlation between medical accuracy and citation quality (ChatGPT 5.2 Pro: rho = 0.033, p = 0.793; Gemini 3 Pro: rho=-0.195, p = 0.120). While Gemini 3 Pro provides highly accurate, guideline-adherent clinical information for urolithiasis, neither model currently serves as a reliable primary tool for academic literature retrieval. There is a stark discrepancy between the models’ high clinical accuracy and their critically poor citation reliability. Therefore, it is unsafe to rely on AI-generated medical content without strictly and independently verifying the underlying references for clinical practice.

Article.Title: Safety-constrained multi-agent AI for emergency department disposition decisions
Article.Authors: Tsafrir L.; Arama L.; Ben Haim G.; Saban M.
Article.Abstract: Emergency department disposition decisions integrate measurements, narratives and contextual risk. We developed SMARTriage AI, a multi-agent system combining role-specialized language-model agents with deterministic rules, intended as safety gates, to recommend admission or discharge. In a retrospective, single-center development study of 469 valid-label adult internal medicine and geriatric encounters from one 24-h period (468 analyzed; 154 admitted), prompts and rules were refined over about 30 cycles on the same cohort, without a held-out set. Apparent accuracy was 88.2% (95% CI, 85.0–90.9%) and admission recall 96.1%. Accuracy was 97.2% with physician summary or recommendations text (n = 248) and 78.2% without it (n = 220); with the text withheld it was 65.0%. After peer review, a redesigned system (v2), evaluated on all 469 encounters under a protocol locked before the runs, discriminated worse than a single language-model agent (Setting A AUC 0.794 vs. 0.821–0.823). At the pre-specified thresholds, accuracy was 76.3% for v2 versus 67.0% for discharging everyone. The multi-agent design did not outperform a single agent, and apparent performance was optimistically biased by development on the evaluation encounters and by disposition information in physician documentation. Evaluation on unseen encounters, and external and prospective validation, are required before any conclusion about clinical utility.

Article.Title: Quantitative strengthening and corrosion correlation for partial and full substitution of nickel by nitrogen on AISI 316 stainless steel via VIM
Article.Authors: Shehata M.; Ghali S.; Ahmed A.; Al-Ganainy G.; Ibrahim M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nickel stabilization of the austenitic phase in stainless steels faces economic and supply-chain pressures, motivating partial or near-complete nickel substitution through nitrogen alloying as an alternative alloy-design strategy. This study systematically evaluates partial (0.24 N, 6.56 wt% Ni retained) and near-complete (0.52 N, 0.01 wt% Ni) nitrogen substitution in AISI 316 stainless steel, produced via vacuum induction furnace (VIM) under controlled-nitrogen-pressure melting at 18 and 32 bar, respectively. Nitrogen addition refined austenite grain size by 53.4% (from 29 to 13.5 μm) and increased dislocation density from 0.13 × 10 14 to 1.97 × 10 14 m −2 , with the 0.52N alloy developing a duplex (γ + α) microstructure. A phase-resolved strengthening model decomposed yield strength contributions into grain refinement, solid-solution, and dislocation mechanisms, achieving good agreement with experimental results. Nitrogen shifted corrosion potential positively, reduced corrosion current density from 9.1 to 2.4 µA cm −2 , and EIS analysis showed the passive film’s charge-transfer resistance rising from 121.5 to 193.5 kΩ cm 2 with a corresponding fall in effective capacitance, while the electrical-equivalent film thickness recalculated from these parameters increases only modestly, from 0.10 to 0.12 nm. Dilatometry revealed a thermal instability window (780–840 °C) unique to the 0.52N alloy, consistent with thermally activated phase evolution within its γ + α duplex microstructure. The 0.24N alloy provides the most balanced combination of strength, ductility, corrosion resistance, and thermal stability among the investigated conditions, while the 0.52N alloy provides the highest strength but also exhibits greater phase complexity and a thermal-instability window; therefore, both alloys require application-specific validation of processing, weldability/forming behaviour, and long-term service performance before industrial deployment.

Article.Title: Phenological and meteorological determinants of herbaceous pollen dynamics in a subtropical urban basin
Article.Authors: Calderón-Ezquerro M.; Guerrero-Guerra C.; Martínez-López B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Herbaceous pollen dynamics in subtropical urban systems remain poorly characterized relative to temperate frameworks. We analyzed 18 years of daily pollen records from four stations of the Mexican Aerobiology Network in the Mexico City Basin, characterizing their intraannual regime, interannual trends, meteorological determinants, and inter-station differences. Because conventional methods for defining the pollen season do not apply here, we complemented standard metrics (Annual Pollen Integral) with circular statistics, Colwell indices, and harmonic analysis. All three converged: herbaceous pollen shows weak seasonality, with a stable circular mean date but high day-to-day dispersion ( r ≈ 0.2–0.4), rather than a temperate-style season. Despite lower concentrations than arboreal taxa, herbaceous pollen reached up to 50% of total airborne pollen during August–October. Water governed the system through four pathways: seasonal rainfall promoted flowering; irrigation sustained baseline pollen in the dry season and likely dampened interannual climate signals; and daily rainfall reduced same-day concentrations through washout. Land-use and tree-cover gradients further modulated pollen contribution, about threefold higher in the most urbanized station. Pollen exposure in subtropical urbanized systems thus depends on multiple forms of water availability and land management rather than a fixed calendar, with direct implications for allergen exposure assessment and urban environmental management.

Article.Title: Chitosan gelatin coatings enriched with Satureja essential oil improve rainbow trout fillet quality and shelf life during superchilled storage
Article.Authors: Molaee-aghaee E.; Isvand A.; Safarzadeh H.; Mirmotahari S.; Heidarzadeh S.; Amini M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Edible coatings enriched with essential oils are a sustainable approach to preserving highly perishable foods, especially fish. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a chitosan–gelatin coating containing Satureja essential oil (SEO) in maintaining the quality and extending the shelf life of rainbow trout fillets during superchilling storage. Fillets were immersed in sterile distilled water (control), chitosan–gelatin solution, or chitosan–gelatin with 1% or 2% SEO, then stored at − 1.4 °C for 30 days. Microbiological parameters (mesophilic, psychrophilic, lactic acid bacteria, Enterobacteriaceae), physicochemical properties (total volatile basic nitrogen, conjugated dienes, TBARS, protein carbonyls, pH, electrical conductivity, freshness index), and sensory characteristics were evaluated on days 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30. The results demonstrated that CH-GEL-SEO treatments significantly preserved the quality of samples during refrigerated storage. By day 30, TVN levels reached 32.5 mg N/100 g in the control group, while they remained substantially lower in CH-GEL-SEO1% and CH-GEL-SEO2% groups (17.1 and 18.0 mg N/100 g, respectively). Similarly, conjugated diene (CD) values were significantly reduced in the SEO-treated groups (0.17 and 0.15 mmol/g) compared to the control (0.42 mmol/g). Furthermore, the coatings effectively suppressed microbial growth (TMB, TPB, and LAB) and maintained superior sensory attributes throughout the storage period. Combining chitosan–gelatin coating with SEO under superchilled storage effectively improves preservation and extends the shelf life of rainbow trout fillets.

Article.Title: A machine learning framework for parkinson’s disease classification using digitized spiral drawings: markov-based feature selection and ensemble evaluation
Article.Authors: Yadav P.; Aroba O.; Vijarania M.; Awotunde J.; Haruna H.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder associated with progressive degeneration of dopaminergic neurons, resulting in motor and non-motor impairments. Digitized spiral drawings provide a non-invasive means of assessing motor abnormalities, but manual evaluation can be subjective and time-consuming. This study presents a machine-learning framework for classifying PD and healthy controls using features extracted from digitized spiral drawings. Six spatial and image-derived features are scaled using Min–Max normalization and ranked using a steady-state Markov chain feature selector, whose transition matrix combines absolute feature correlations with variability-based weights. Classification is performed using a stacking ensemble comprising a Decision Tree, a radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM), and a Random Forest, with Logistic Regression as the meta-learner trained on out-of-fold predictions. Scaling, feature selection, and stacking are fitted within the training folds, while duplicate-linked files are assigned to the same split group. The stacking model had a five-fold cross-validation accuracy of 86.46 ± 17.17% and balanced accuracy of 84.23 ± 20.15% on the development set of 62 files. Sensitivity in out-of-fold pooling was 95.92%, while the specificity was 38.46%, implying that there were few healthy control identifications. However, on the hold-out set where all 15 files were classified, there were just two controls, and the 95% Wilson confidence interval for accuracy was 79.6–100%. Ablation experiments showed that stacking did not outperform a single RBF-SVM and that Markov-based feature selection did not outperform the use of all six features. The results prove the viability of the proposed method but do not indicate its diagnostic ability. More independently collected datasets would be required for assessing its generalizability.

Article.Title: Mechanistically informed statistical modeling of hydraulic performance for bentonite construction liners: long-term mechanistic insights from real-time data, ANOVA, and regression analysis
Article.Authors: Al-Mahbashi A.; Dafalla M.; Abbas Y.
Article.Abstract: Sand–bentonite liners (SBLs) play a pivotal role in geotechnical and environmental engineering as hydraulic barriers designed to minimize contaminant migration and safeguard subsurface soil and groundwater. This study presents a comprehensive statistical investigation into the key operational, field, and climatic factors influencing the long-term durability and hydraulic efficiency of compacted SBLs under sustained flow conditions. A long-term laboratory permeability test was conducted to maintain continuous flow through the specimen while systematically monitoring the effects of aging, hydraulic head variation, cumulative flow, and ambient temperature. Quantitative evaluation using one- and two-way ANOVA, interaction plots, and a quadratic regression model (F = 324.20, p < 0.001) revealed that cumulative flow and aging, along with their interaction, exerted the most pronounced influence on hydraulic conductivity. Specifically, hydraulic conductivity increased by approximately 38% after 90 days of sustained flow, which highlights the critical role of cumulative seepage in permeability evolution. These findings provide valuable quantitative insights into mechanisms governing the long-term behavior of SBLs and offer a data-driven foundation for designing more sustainable and efficient barrier designs.

Article.Title: Immunophenotyping of end-stage lung disease patients on the transplant waiting list
Article.Authors: Berezhinskiy O.; Cho A.; Auner S.; Alemanno S.; Jevtić M.; Spittler A.; Hoetzenecker K.; Aigner C.; Wekerle T.; Jaksch P.; Shirazi S.; Benazzo A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Circulating immune features distinguishing end-stage fibrotic from obstructive disease remain poorly characterized. We sought to define the peripheral immune landscape across these conditions relative to healthy individuals and to test whether it predicts outcome after transplantation. Whole blood from 134 lung transplant candidates and 53 healthy controls was analyzed by flow cytometry. Major immune populations and B-cell, T-cell, dendritic-cell, and regulatory T-cell (Treg) subsets were profiled by manual gating and with unsupervised FlowSOM/UMAP clustering as qualitative confirmation. In the 114 candidates who subsequently underwent, the baseline immune state was tested against chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD)-free survival and overall survival by Cox proportional-hazards regression. Both diseases shared a signature of lymphoid contraction against a background of leukocytosis. Total leukocytes were increased in both (p < 0.0001) and higher in fibrosis than obstruction (p = 0.002). CD8⁺ T cells, including CD57⁺ and PD1⁺ populations, were expanded in both diseases (p < 0.0001), and Tregs (FoxP3⁺, CD39⁺, CD45RA⁻) were enriched in both obstruction and fibrosis (p < 0.0001). Fibrosis was distinguished by a more pronounced CD4⁺ contraction and by selective enrichment of Helios⁺ Tregs and CD8⁺CD57⁺populations. This pre-transplant immune state did not predict CLAD-free or overall survival. End-stage lung disease is marked by a convergent reprogramming of peripheral immunity.

Article.Title: Association between sex-specific waist-defined central obesity and blood pressure abnormality among undergraduate, master’s and doctoral students in Shanxi, China
Article.Authors: Hu M.; Yang L.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: Although central adiposity and elevated blood pressure often emerge during early adulthood, evidence regarding waist-defined central obesity across diverse university training levels remains scarce. We investigated the association between central obesity and blood pressure abnormality and evaluated potential effect modification by sex, educational stage, and body mass index (BMI) among university students in Shanxi, China. We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2025 Shanxi provincial student physical fitness and health survey. Records with implausible waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure or body mass index (BMI) values were excluded. Central obesity was defined as waist circumference ≥ 90 cm in men or ≥ 85 cm in women. Blood pressure abnormality was defined as systolic blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 90 mmHg. Robust Poisson regression with sandwich standard errors was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) as the primary effect measures; logistic-regression odds ratios (ORs) were secondary estimates. Among 2132 students (1065 women and 1067 men), 254 (11.9%) had central obesity and 401 (18.8%) had blood pressure abnormality. The prevalence of blood pressure abnormality was 38.6% among students with central obesity and 16.1% among those without. In robust Poisson regression, central obesity was associated with blood pressure abnormality in the crude model (PR 2.39; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.98–2.88) and after adjustment for demographic and school-related covariates (PR 1.82; 95% CI 1.52–2.18). This association was partially attenuated yet remained statistically significant upon further adjustment for BMI (PR 1.30; 95% CI 1.01–1.67). Secondary logistic regression yielded concordant results (covariate-adjusted OR 2.68; 95% CI 1.95–3.69; BMI-adjusted OR, 1.60; 95% CI 1.05–2.43). Interaction tests did not indicate heterogeneity by sex ( P = 0.318), training level ( P = 0.326) or BMI category (< 28.0 versus ≥ 28.0 kg/m 2 ; P = 0.102). In this cross-sectional sample of university students in Shanxi, China, sex-specific, waist-defined central obesity was associated with a higher prevalence of blood pressure abnormality, and the association persisted after BMI adjustment. These findings support the complementary use of waist circumference and BMI in routine university health monitoring to identify students who may benefit from standardized repeat blood-pressure assessment.

Article.Title: System dynamics simulation of green transformation risks in China’s Northern Greater Bay Area
Article.Authors: Zeng X.; Zhou M.; Li J.; Guan Y.
Article.Abstract: Since 2011, China has enforced mandatory clean production policies in historically polluted regions, triggering complex socioeconomic and ecological transitions. Against the backdrop of China’s 2024 national strategy for comprehensive green transformation, understanding regional green transition dynamics has become more important. Taking the Northern Greater Bay Area as a case study, this research constructs a system dynamics model integrating ecological resources, green technology innovation, market feedback, and policy regulation subsystems. Validated against 2010–2025 historical data, with core variables showing acceptable average relative errors except for policy-induced outliers in 2012–2014. The model identifies four systemic risks and their coupling pathways: R&D investment traps, economic collapse, ecological stock depletion, and fiscal subsidy dependence. Threshold and scenario analyses reveal a critical transition window during 2026–2030, where the system may evolve toward a self-reinforcing virtuous cycle, persistent oscillation, low-level equilibrium, or collapse. We propose a state-dependent switching control strategy to maintain system stability within a safe operating range. This study contributes a quantitative simulation tool and a governance-oriented framework for managing green transformation risks.

Article.Title: A hybrid structure based on polycaprolactone nanofibers and propolis-loaded gelatin/hyaluronic acid hydrogel as a cartilage scaffold
Article.Authors: Shavandi N.; Gholipour-Kanani A.; Eslahi N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Articular cartilage has a low self-healing capacity due to the lack of blood vessels and nerves. Hybrid structures based on nanofibrous layer incorporating hydrogels can effectively mimic the structure of articular cartilage and stimulate tissue repair. In this study, the electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofibers was used to improve the mechanical properties of the hybrid structure. Gelatin was blended with hyaluronic acid at different ratios and loaded with propolis extract as an antibacterial agent to form a hydrogel that served as a substrate for the PCL nanofibrous layer. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) showed that the PCL nanofibers had a uniform, bead-free morphology with an average diameter of 141 ± 25 nm. The images also revealed a strong attachment between the nanofibrous layer and the hydrogel. Contact angle measurements indicated that the presence of hydrophobic PCL nanofibers did not significantly reduce the hydrophilicity of the hybrid. Swelling profiles indicated a swelling ratio of 510 ± 28% for propolis-loaded hybrid. Mechanical testing demonstrated that the incorporation of the PCL web significantly reinforced the hydrogel, with compressive modulus of 67.1 ± 2.36 kPa for the hybrids. The release study showed that approximately 90% of the propolis content was released from the hybrid scaffold containing 10% propolis within 48 h. Antibacterial testing demonstrated high activity of the propolis-loaded scaffolds against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The MTT assay showed excellent cell viability when cells were exposed to both propolis-loaded and unloaded hybrid scaffolds, especially at concentrations of 5 and 10 µg/mL. In conclusion, the hybrid PCL nanofiber/propolis-loaded gelatin–hyaluronic acid hydrogel represents a promising material for cartilage repair.

Article.Title: Injection strategy optimization for engineered water enhanced oil recovery in carbonate reservoirs
Article.Authors: Al Alwan A.; Khamehchi E.
Article.Abstract: Carbonate reservoirs commonly exhibit limited oil recovery because of strong heterogeneity, complex pore structures, and unfavorable wettability. This study presents an integrated experimental-numerical framework for evaluating engineered-water flooding and optimizing injection strategies in the heterogeneous WQ1-57 carbonate reservoir. Laboratory core-flooding experiments were combined with geochemical modeling, multiphase-flow calibration, scale-up, reservoir simulation, and sensitivity analysis. Engineered-water injection consistently enhanced oil displacement, yielding incremental recoveries of 11.7–22.8% across the investigated cores. The calibrated numerical model reproduced the experimental recovery and pressure responses and was subsequently used to evaluate radial, line-drive, and conformance-controlled injection configurations. Among these strategies, conformance-controlled injection provided the most favorable reservoir response, increasing oil recovery by 18.1%, delaying water breakthrough by 0.30 pore volumes, improving areal and vertical sweep by 17% and 20%, respectively, and reducing water cut by 15%. Sensitivity analysis identified horizontal permeability as the dominant control on incremental recovery, followed by residual oil saturation and relative-permeability behavior, whereas engineered-water ionic composition, vertical permeability anisotropy, and injection conditions showed comparatively smaller effects. These findings demonstrate that engineered-water performance is governed by the coupled effects of fluid-rock interactions, reservoir heterogeneity, and injection management.

Article.Title: Occurrence and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Staphylococcus aureus and MRSA in milk, milkers’ hands, and farm environments in Sheger City, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Elias M.; Yitayew B.; Tekola B.; Abunna F.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), particularly involving Staphylococcus aureus and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), is an increasing One Health concern in low- and middle-income countries, where weak antimicrobial regulation and inadequate AMR surveillance practices exacerbate the problem. This study aimed to assess the occurrence and antimicrobial resistance profiles of S. aureus and MRSA in dairy farms in Sheger City, Ethiopia, using a One Health approach. A cross-sectional study was conducted from December 2024 to May 2025 on dairy farms in Sheger City, Oromia Region, Ethiopia, using a One Health approach. Four districts, Gelan, Sida Awash, Wadesa, and Tulu Dimtu, were selected by simple random sampling from the two sub-cities. Gelan and Tulu Dimtu were selected from Gelan Sub-city, while Sida Awash and Wadesa were selected from Koye Fache Sub-city. A total of 312 samples were collected, comprising milk samples ( n = 212), hand swabs from milkers ( n = 40), and environmental swabs ( n = 60). Isolation and identification of bacterial isolates were performed using conventional bacteriological methods and MALDI-TOF MS. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines. Overall, 20.83% (65/312) of samples were positive for S. aureus and 9.9% (31/312) were phenotypically identified MRSA. The highest prevalence of S. aureus was observed in hand swabs (27.5%), followed by udder milk (23.11%) and environmental samples (8.3%). MRSA was detected exclusively in milk samples (14.62%). All isolates exhibited multidrug resistance, with 100% resistance to penicillin, tetracycline, clindamycin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and cloxacillin. All isolates were susceptible to ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, and norfloxacin. All 65 isolates exhibited multidrug resistance (MDR), with 26 (40.0%) resistant to three antimicrobial classes, 25 (38.5%) to four classes, and 14 (21.5%) to five classes. The findings highlight the public health risk of MRSA in dairy systems and emphasize the need for improved hygiene, prudent antimicrobial use, and integrated One Health AMR surveillance strategies.

Article.Title: Predicting under-five mortality in Bangladesh through comparative survival analysis using traditional, machine learning, and deep learning models
Article.Authors: Amin R.; Bristi W.; Asgar A.; Mobin M.
Article.Abstract: Under-five mortality (U5M) remains a persistent public health challenge in Bangladesh, where 36.6 deaths per 1,000 live births separate the country from the SDG 3.2.1 target of 25. Standard survival models have shaped our understanding of this burden for decades, but their rigid structural assumptions limit how much of the underlying predicted risk architecture they can recover. Using data on 13,119 children from the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS), this study systematically compares eight survival models across three methodological paradigms: traditional Cox proportional hazards and its penalized variants (Lasso, Ridge, Elastic Net), ensemble methods (Random Survival Forest (RSF) and Gradient Boosting Survival Analysis (GBSA)), and deep learning architectures (DeepSurv and DeepHit). A two-stage feature selection procedure: univariate Cox screening followed by Random Survival Forest permutation importance identified 15 predictors for model development. Performance was evaluated across discrimination, probabilistic accuracy, time-dependent AUC, and calibration, with stability confirmed across six k-fold configurations ( \(k = 5\) -30) via Friedman’s test ( \(p = 0.223\) ), while external validation was performed using an independent Nepal Demographic and Health Survey cohort processed with an identical analytical pipeline. DeepHit achieved the strongest joint performance: concordance index (C-index) of 0.977, Integrated Brier Score (IBS) of 0.016, mean time-dependent Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.987, and calibration slopes of 0.99–1.04 across three follow-up years, the only model in this comparison to approach ideal calibration. RSF led on C-index (0.978) but showed systematically inflated calibration slopes (1.42–1.45), while Cox-family models were competitive on discrimination but severely miscalibrated. Pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests further demonstrated that the performance differences between the best-performing models and conventional survival approaches were statistically significant ( \(p < 0.05\) ) with large effect size. In the Nepal cohort, DeepHit maintained its performance without retraining, with a C-index of 0.9663 and a mean AUC of 0.9811. The relative rankings of the other models also carried over. Number of living children, total children ever born, and antenatal care intensity consistently dominated feature importance, locating the strongest mortality signal in maternal reproductive history rather than socioeconomic status alone.

Article.Title: Effects of heat stress on honey bee physiology and gut microbiome under laboratory conditions
Article.Authors: Baugus L.; Walt H.; Gautam A.; Yang L.; Chakrabarti P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heat stress affects individual honey bees, and this may compromise overall colony performance and health. As the frequency, intensity, and duration of heat waves increase due to climate change, it is crucial to understand the impacts of heat on honey bees. This study investigates how heat stress impacts honey bee physiology and gut microbiome. Honey bees were subjected to three temperature conditions (control, heat stress and heat shock) for two weeks. Half of all experimental cages received multifloral pollen supplementation. The acute heat shock group, both with and without pollen, exhibited the highest mortality, followed by control groups (with and without pollen) and chronic heat stress groups (with and without pollen). The honey bee microbiome adapted to the effects of heat stress, with temperature stress exerting selective, taxon-specific effects on gut microbiome rather than broad community disruption. Specifically, changes occurred in Bombella intestini, Bifidobacterium asteroides , Lactobacillus apis, and Gilliamella apicola . Additionally, there was an absence of a strong effect of heat stress on the honey bee proteome, suggesting that the honey bee proteome adequately adapts to heat stress in the measured temperature range. This study highlights the value of focusing on individual taxon and specific protein functions when evaluating environmental stressor impacts.

Article.Title: Urine-based liquid biopsy markers for diagnosis and treatment response monitoring in higher-stage bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Jeong M.; Eum D.; Baek S.; Park S.; Jung S.; Kim G.; Song J.; Chung S.; Cho J.; Choi Y.; Choi S.; Ku J.; Heo K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urine is in direct contact with bladder tumors, making it an ideal biofluid for non-invasive biomarker discovery. This study aimed to identify urine-based protein biomarkers for bladder cancer diagnosis and treatment response monitoring. By analyzing transcriptomic data from bladder cancer cell lines with differential sensitivity to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, we identified four secreted proteins associated with treatment resistance: collagen type I alpha 1 chain (COL1A1), microfibrillar-associated protein 5 (MFAP5), dipeptidyl-peptidase 4 (DPP4), and extracellular matrix protein 1 (ECM1). Urinary concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in 57 bladder cancer patients and 22 cancer-free controls. All four markers were significantly elevated in patients, and a combined four-marker panel outperformed individual markers (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.916, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.858–0.975), with discrimination driven primarily by stage T1 or higher disease. In a treatment-monitoring cohort of 13 patients receiving systemic chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy, changes in urinary COL1A1, MFAP5, and ECM1 from baseline were concordant with CT-based response, with COL1A1 showing the highest concordance (92.3%). These exploratory findings suggest that urinary secreted proteins may reflect disease status during treatment. However, their added value over imaging was not assessed, and their utility in surveillance settings warrants future investigation.

Article.Title: Ontology-grounded nanotoxicity data federation with a provenance-aware knowledge graph and conformal prediction for antimicrobial hazard screening
Article.Authors: Singh P.; Pandey P.; Chandrasekar V.; Singh A.; Kumar M.
Article.Abstract: Nanomaterials are increasingly used across industrial, therapeutic, and consumer applications, while their interactions with biological and environmental systems can produce adverse effects. Although nanotoxicological evidence is abundant, it remains fragmented across curated repositories, computational archives, and datasets extracted from the scientific literature. Inconsistent terminology, measurement units, and identifier schemes limit interoperability and reuse. This study presents an ontology-grounded pipeline that federates two complementary public sources against the eNanoMapper ontology, harmonises records into a canonical schema, preserves evidence in a provenance-aware knowledge graph, and applies gradient-boosted classification with split conformal prediction to a relative antimicrobial hazard-screening task based on MIC/MBC records. The integrated dataset contains 6588 records spanning thirteen material classes and seven harmonised endpoint types, and the knowledge graph contains 2279 nodes and 32,940 typed edges in one weakly connected component. Under five-fold stratified cross-validation, the strongest classifier achieved an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC) of \(0.819 \pm 0.020\) . On a disjoint test set, split conformal prediction achieved empirical marginal coverage of 0.955, 0.929, and 0.825 against nominal targets of 0.95, 0.90, and 0.80, respectively. A material-grouped cross-validation stress test reduced AUROC to \(0.609 \pm 0.098\) , demonstrating limited generalisation to unseen material classes. Feature attribution and ablation show that categorical experimental context carries most of the discriminative signal, whereas measured physicochemical descriptors contribute comparatively little. The resulting framework therefore combines semantic data integration, explicit provenance, and uncertainty-aware antimicrobial hazard screening while making the limits of cross-material generalisation explicit.

Article.Title: Comparative XLRS phenotyping in two rodent models of Rs1 exon-1 knockout
Article.Authors: Salamone G.; Sieving P.; Strettoi E.
Article.Abstract: X-linked retinoschisis (XLRS; MIM 312700) from RS1 gene mutations is the most common genetic retinal dystrophy affecting young males. XLRS causes retinal structural disorganization and progressive visual dysfunction. Cellular mechanisms underlying XLRS remain unclear and effective therapies are not available. As Rs1-deficient rodent models recapitulate key features of human XLRS disease, they provide valuable tools to investigate disease mechanisms and therapeutic strategies. We compared XLRS disease in rat and mouse transgenic models with the same Rs1 exon-1 knockout (KO). Rs1-KO mice had outer nuclear layer thinning and photoreceptor degeneration, outer plexiform layer synaptic disorganization, macroglia and microglial activation. The Rs1-KO rat exhibited more severe disease; retinal development appeared normal at P12, but by P14 schisis cavities had formed in the inner nuclear layer and then collapsed by P30. The Rs1-KO rat showed rapid XLRS progression with severe photoreceptor degeneration, outer retinal remodeling and glial activation. Although Rs1 was present in the inner plexiform layer, immunohistochemistry failed to detect it at junctions between bipolar and amacrine or ganglion cells in either model. Both species displayed a similar XLRS pathogenic sequence but with different temporal dynamics, highlighting species-specific modulation of disease progression while underscoring shared mechanisms relevant to the timing and design of therapeutic interventions. Regarding abnormal retinal cystic fluid homeostasis in XLRS, the retinal pigment epithelium of Rs1-KO rat up to P30 showed no disruption in ZO-1 staining integrity, albeit the hexagonal profiles of ZO-1 staining pattern appeared altered. This was beyond what was observed in the KO mouse.

Article.Title: Intramuscular versus intravenous naloxone for the reversal of methadone overdose in hospitalized patients: a randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Jangjou A.; Kolahi A.; Taheri M.; Hassani A.; Deravi N.; McDonald R.; Buckley N.; Hassanian-Moghaddam H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Methadone, a synthetic long-acting opioid, is commonly used in maintenance therapy for opioid addiction. Naloxone is the standard treatment for methadone overdose, capable of reversing opioid effects in both the central and peripheral nervous systems. Continuous naloxone infusion may be required to prevent re-sedation after initial treatment. Given the challenges associated with intravenous administration, alternative delivery methods are under investigation. We aimed to compare the effectiveness of intramuscular (IM) naloxone with intravenous (IV) naloxone in opioid-dependent patients with methadone overdose. A randomized clinical trial was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Tehran, Iran, involving patients with methadone overdose aged 19–59. Patients received either IM or IV naloxone following basic life support and an initial naloxone bolus. In the IV group, approximately two-thirds of the initial effective dose was administered hourly. In the IM group, the dose was adjusted every 4 h based on the calculated hourly requirement: 0.4 mg, 0.8 mg, 1.2 mg, or 1.6 mg, corresponding to calculated needs of < 0.2 mg/h, 0.2–0.4 mg/h, 0.4–0.6 mg/h, or > 0.6 mg/h, respectively. The primary outcome was the occurrence of withdrawal syndrome, assessed using COWS criteria. Naloxone dosing adjustments were guided by venous blood gas analysis and level of consciousness. Treatment response and episodes of apnea were monitored during hospitalization. A total of 160 patients with suspected methadone overdose, randomly assigned to IM or IV naloxone. Normalization of respiratory rate and level of consciousness was comparable between the IM (50.8%) and IV (49.2%) groups ( P > 0.05). COWS scores were significantly higher in the IV group. However, apnea occurred in 20 (25%) cases in the IM group and 18 (22.5%) cases in the IV group during hospitalization, each requiring a single rescue dose of naloxone. IM naloxone resulted in a significantly lower median [IQR] pulse rate (76 [70, 80] vs. 98 [88, 110] in the IV group) at four hours post-intervention. Oxygen saturation and pCO 2 levels post-naloxone were similar between the two groups. IM naloxone was associated with less severe opioid withdrawal, reflected by lower COWS scores and may represent a reasonable alternative to intravenous naloxone in selected clinical settings. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of the single-center design, potential variability in naloxone dosing, concomitant substance use, and the lack of confirmatory toxicological testing. Trial registration: IRCT20120629010133N6. Registered 01 January 2023.

Article.Title: Automated perimetry in children with suspected and known glaucoma: virtual reality versus tabletop
Article.Authors: Tillit S.; Piryani N.; Liu J.; Saleem Z.; El-Dairi M.; Wang B.; Freedman S.
Article.Abstract: Humphrey visual field (HVF)-equivalent virtual reality fields (VRFs) have shown promise in adult glaucoma. Research comparing HVF-equivalent VRF to standard automated perimetry (SAP) in pediatric glaucoma is limited. We aimed to evaluate association and agreement between HVF-equivalent VRF and SAP for children with glaucoma. This prospective study enrolled children with known or suspected glaucoma. Participants completed HVF, then VisuALL HVF-equivalent VRF at one visit. A masked ophthalmologist graded visual fields for defects and location. Global parameters were compared between devices. A point-by-point deviation plot analysis was performed. A total of 60 patients (116 eyes) were included, mean age 13.1 ± 2.93 years. Mean retinal nerve fiber layer thickness was 86.1 ± 21.20 μm. Average mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and foveal sensitivity significantly differed for HVF versus VRF. There was moderate association between HVF and VRF for MD ( P < 0.001) and PSD ( P < 0.001). Concordance by region for any defect was 76.2%; point-by-point match rate for total deviation plots was 75.8%. Test duration was longer for HVF versus VRF (4.17 ± 1.19 vs. 2.10 ± 0.18 min, respectively, P < 0.001). Most children (43/44, 97.7%) preferred VRF over HVF. HVF and HVF-equivalent VRF testing modalities yielded moderate association. HVF-equivalent VRF offers a shorter test that children preferred and may supplement SAP.

Article.Title: Differences in core muscle surface electromyographic activity during static unilateral and bilateral carries
Article.Authors: Busch A.; Tuttle M.; Bias S.; Ulm R.
Article.Abstract: Strength and conditioning programs often utilize carriage exercises to challenge postural stability with the intent of improving abdominal muscle endurance and grip-strength. This study examined differences in surface electromyography (sEMG) within core musculature during static bilateral and unilateral carries of different loads based on body weight (BW). Thirty-one healthy male, Division III collegiate athletes (age = 19.54 ± 1.06 years, height = 178.62 ± 5.58 cm, weight = 83.11 ± 13.27 kg) completed three different types of static carries including a bilateral (BL), contralateral (CL) and ipsilateral (IL) hold in random order using two different weights: 12.5% BW and 25% BW. Unilateral sEMG was recorded for the dominant-handed rectus abdominis (RA), external oblique (EO), and erector spinae (ES) muscles. For all three muscles recorded, there were statistically significant two way interactions between the weight held and carry type. All carry types demonstrated greater sEMG activity in the RA, EO, and ES during 25% BW compared to 12.5% BW carries. When comparing carry type, CL carries elicited significantly greater sEMG activity for all muscles compared to BL and IL carries for both 25% BW and 12.5% BW. Unilateral carries held on the CL side elicited greater sEMG activity in the dominant side core-muscles under these static holding conditions.

Article.Title: Unified sliding-mode control of a flexible excitation system with lightweight stator/rotor dual-channel damping injection
Article.Authors: Weng J.; Xiao S.; Zhang Y.; Qin H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power systems are increasingly exposed to broadband and strongly coupled disturbances. Under large disturbances, parameter perturbations, and operating-point variations, flexible excitation system (FES) may exhibit aggravated DC-link voltage fluctuations, sluggish excitation response, and insufficient damping of electromechanical oscillations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a unified sliding-mode control framework for a FES consisting of a three-level neutral-point-clamped voltage-source converter (NPC-VSC), a DC link, and a DC/DC excitation chopper. An adaptive-gain second-order sliding-mode (AG-SOSM) controller is introduced into the VSC outer loop to ensure finite-time convergence of the DC-link voltage and enhanced disturbance rejection. In the VSC current inner loop and the chopper control loop, band-pass-filter (BPF)-enhanced sliding surfaces are combined with the super-twisting algorithm (STA) to achieve fast tracking of the excitation variable with reduced chattering. In addition, lightweight stator-side reactive power damping and rotor-side damping-torque components are injected through the reference path, enabling coordinated dual-channel damping enhancement without modifying the main controller structure. Time-domain simulation results under network disturbances, mechanical-power perturbation, excitation-related parameter variations, and converter-current harmonic evaluation show that, compared with CES, PID-FES, and CSMC-FES benchmarks, the proposed strategy improves electromechanical damping, accelerates dynamic recovery, maintains DC-link voltage regulation, and reduces converter-current harmonic distortion.

Article.Title: Alterations in homologous recombination repair genes and impact on survival among Chinese pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients detected using next-generation sequencing
Article.Authors: Du J.; Duan N.; Wang L.; Zhu Y.; Ma Q.; Li H.; Ma Y.; Jin B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Detection of homologous recombination repair (HRR) deficiency in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is advancing, yet germline HRR mutation landscapes and survival impact remain poorly characterized in Chinese patients. In this study, we undertook next-generation sequencing among 126 Chinese PDAC patients using a 32-gene panel. Pathogenic and likely pathogenic (P/LP) germline mutations were diagnosed according to the ACMG variant classification categories. Mutation frequencies of HRR-related genes were analyzed statistically, and hotspot genes with high mutation prevalence were identified. Simultaneously, we compared the differences in demographic information, tumor characteristics, and clinical outcomes between P/LP mutation carriers and non-carriers. Germline P/LP variants were identified in 11.1% of the 126 patients, most frequently involving ATM and BRCA2. VUS were detected in 31.7% of patients, with ATM, BRCA2, and BRIP1 being the most commonly involved genes. Survival analysis of 103 patients showed longer overall survival in carriers of germline P/LP variants than in non-carriers ( P = 0.032). In the platinum-treated subgroup ( n = 20), overall survival was numerically longer in P/LP variant carriers than in non-carriers, but the difference was not statistically significant. SMAD4 loss was associated with shorter survival in the 39 patients with complete pathological data. These findings characterize the distribution of germline HRR variants in this cohort and suggest an association between P/LP variants and overall survival that warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Article.Title: Development and external validation of a risk stratification model for hyperuricemia in adolescents: a multicenter clinical study
Article.Authors: Wu Z.; Liu D.; Li X.; Tang Y.; Min R.; Mu Y.; Feng G.
Article.Abstract: Hyperuricemia is prevalent among adolescents and is associated with metabolic abnormalities and cardiometabolic risk; however, the secondary use of routinely collected health examination data for HUA risk stratification remains underexplored. We developed and externally evaluated a multivariable risk stratification model for adolescent hyperuricemia using such data. Among 903 adolescents aged 12–18 years from two Chongqing centers, 747 formed the development cohort and 156 the external validation cohort. Predictors were selected using multivariable logistic regression with Akaike information criterion-based backward selection. Eight predictors were retained: body mass index, alkaline phosphatase, urea, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, γ-glutamyl transferase, absolute monocyte count, and absolute neutrophil count. The model demonstrated acceptable discrimination, with AUCs of 0.831 and 0.804 in the development and external validation cohorts, respectively, although external calibration was weaker. Decision curve analysis suggested net benefit at lower threshold probabilities. When the required predictors are already available but SUA has not been measured, the model generates a model-based probability of current HUA from the existing data. This output is intended to support HUA risk stratification and the prioritization of adolescents for subsequent direct SUA measurement. The model is intended as a complementary risk stratification tool and requires prospective evaluation before implementation.

Article.Title: Perceived social support relates to career adaptability in middle school students through sequential mediation and cross-lagged effects
Article.Authors: Kang Y.; Liu S.; Chen C.; Wu J.; Yang J.; Chen Y.; Tian M.
Article.Abstract: To examine how perceived social support, career decision-making self-efficacy, and career exploration are associated with career adaptability among adolescents, and to investigate the prospective relationship between career decision-making self-efficacy and career exploration. A total of 1,080 secondary-school students in Beijing completed the Perceived Social Support Scale, Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy Scale, Career Exploration Scale, and Career Adapt-Abilities Scale at Time 1 after multivariate outlier removal. A longitudinal subsample of 265 students in grades 10 and 11 completed follow-up measures of career decision-making self-efficacy and career exploration three months later. We conducted cross-sectional latent path analyses and a two-wave cross-lagged panel model. Study 1 examined two theoretically plausible chain mediation models: one starting with self-efficacy beliefs (perceived social support → career decision-making self-efficacy → career exploration → career adaptability) and the other with exploratory behavior (perceived social support → career exploration → career decision-making self-efficacy → career adaptability). Both models yielded statistically significant indirect pathways, with different patterns of specific indirect effects. In the primary analysis of Study 2, career exploration significantly predicted later career decision-making self-efficacy after multivariate outlier removal; however, this association was not statistically significant in the sensitivity analysis that retained all eligible participants. Perceived social support was associated with adolescents’ career adaptability through multiple theoretically plausible cognitive-behavioral pathways. The longitudinal findings provide only tentative evidence of a prospective association between career exploration and subsequent self-efficacy beliefs; this preliminary pattern emerged only after multivariate outlier removal and requires replication in larger longitudinal samples before stronger temporal inferences can be made. These findings extend the application of Social Cognitive Career Theory to Chinese secondary-school students and highlight the potential relevance of supportive environments and career exploration for future longitudinal and intervention research on career adaptability.

Article.Title: Sports participation and reduced obesity incidence among Chinese adolescents in a nationwide multi-source cohort study
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Chen X.; Jiang J.
Article.Abstract: Adolescent obesity has emerged as a critical global public health concern, yet large-scale longitudinal evidence examining the protective role of sports participation remains scarce. To examine the association between sports participation and obesity incidence among Chinese adolescents, drawing upon multi-source integrated data from a nationally representative monitoring platform. We conducted a cohort study using the National Adolescent Health Monitoring Big Data Platform (2015–2023), an integrated research database assembled from China’s national school-based health surveillance systems. A total of 3,892,741 non-obese adolescents aged 10–17 years were followed for 18,647,293 person-years. Sports participation was assessed through questionnaires, wearable accelerometers, and administrative records. Propensity score matching (1:2, nearest-neighbor, without replacement, caliper = 0.2 SD) and Cox proportional hazards models were employed to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). E-value sensitivity analysis quantified robustness to unmeasured confounding. During follow-up, 412,847 incident obesity cases occurred (incidence rate: 22.1 per 1,000 person-years). After comprehensive adjustment, adolescents with high sports participation demonstrated significantly lower obesity risk compared with low participation (HR = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.63–0.65). A dose-response relationship was observed with modest nonlinearity (P nonlinearity = 0.024), with each standard deviation increase in composite participation score associated with 15% reduced hazard. The E-value for the primary estimate was 2.50 (E-value for the confidence interval limit closest to the null: 2.45). Protective associations were consistent across sex, age, and geographic subgroups, though statistically significant effect modification by sex (P interaction = 0.003) and age (P interaction = 0.018) was detected. Sustained sports participation is associated with substantially reduced obesity risk during adolescence. Although our observational design precludes definitive causal conclusions, the consistency, dose-response gradient, and robustness of these findings support prioritizing physical activity promotion in youth obesity prevention strategies.

Article.Title: A vision transformer framework with multi-scale temporal attention for automatic highlight detection and semantic understanding in large-scale sports broadcast video
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Geng H.
Article.Abstract: Automatic highlight detection in sports broadcasting requires models that can localise brief impact events and longer narrative arcs at the same time, and produce meaningful semantic descriptions across sports with markedly different broadcast grammars. Hand-crafted pipelines and single-scale deep architectures struggle on all three fronts, and the difficulty compounds when a system is asked to transfer from one discipline to another. We propose a framework that couples a hierarchical vision Transformer backbone with a three-branch multi-scale temporal attention module and a contrastively aligned semantic decoder, optimised end-to-end under uncertainty-weighted multi-task losses. The backbone equips tube embedding with a learned shot-grammar prior tailored to broadcast footage; the attention module operates at short, medium and long temporal scales fused through a content-dependent gate that adapts to event duration without any explicit duration supervision. A hierarchical decoder emits three semantic axes—action category, participating subjects and event nature—trained jointly with detection through a shared representation. Experiments on SoccerNet-v2, NCAA Basketball and a tennis benchmark report 51.7 ± 0.4 mAP@0.5 and CIDEr 1.42 ± 0.02 over three random seeds, outperforming six competitive baselines including ActionFormer and MViTv2 at p < 0.01. Component-wise ablations isolate the contribution of the shot-grammar prior, the learned duration-aware gate and the shared decoder, and confirm that the gains do not follow from added parameters alone. A qualitative captioning and failure-mode analysis identifies replay overlays, amateur fixed-camera footage and severe occlusion as the three residual weaknesses. Inference runs at 47 ms per 96-frame clip on a single A100 GPU under batch size 1; sustained streaming on a full 90-minute broadcast reaches roughly 2.1× real time once buffering and causal masking are accounted for. Present evidence covers three sports categories only, so we treat the cross-sport claim as encouraging rather than proven; extending it to gymnastics, motorsports and combat sports remains open.

Article.Title: Valorization of compressed biogas digestate into biodegradable nursery pots through process optimization and performance characterization
Article.Authors: Sharma H.; Singh T.; Sharma A.; Singh J.; Kumar A.
Article.Abstract: The rapid expansion of compressed biogas (CBG) production has increased the generation of digestate, creating an urgent need for sustainable valorization pathways beyond its conventional use as fertilizer. This study investigated the conversion of CBG digestate into biodegradable nursery pots as a sustainable alternative to high-density polyethylene (HDPE) grow bags. Twelve formulations were prepared using digestates derived from cattle dung, press mud, and municipal solid waste combined with four natural binders (soil, lime, starch, and guar gum). The bio-pots were characterized for their physical, mechanical, chemical, biodegradation, and agronomic properties following ASTM standards and the fertilizer control order (FCO-1985). Among the formulations, the press mud–guar gum blend (50:50) exhibited the best overall performance, with a compressive strength of 1.04 MPa, shattering resistance of 73.5%, water absorption of 14.8%, and favorable nutrient composition (TOC 16.7%; N–P–K 1.18–0.72–1.32%). The optimized bio-pots remained stable during storage for over 180 days, biodegraded within 56 days in soil, and achieved 100% seed germination with enhanced seedling vigor of Amaranthus viridis plants compared with HDPE grow bags. These findings demonstrate the potential of CBG FOM-based biodegradable pots as a waste-valorization pathway that can simultaneously reduce dependence on HDPE nursery bags and facilitate nutrient recycling within a circular agricultural system.

Article.Title: Factorized coordinated double deep Q-learning for multi-user computation offloading and resource allocation in mobile edge computing
Article.Authors: Oukissou Y.; Amzil M.; Meddaoui M.; Ouyidir A.; Ait Omar D.; Zougagh H.
Article.Abstract: Efficient computation offloading in Multi Access edge-computing (MEC) requires joint decisions on whether tasks should be processed locally or remotely and how limited edge-computing resources should be allocated among simultaneously active users. Such coupling produces a challenging sequential decision problem because independently selected offloading actions may generate competing resource requests under a shared MEC capacity. This work proposes Factorized Coordinated Double Deep Q-Learning (FC-DDQN), a value-based multi-agent framework that separates the binary local/offloading decision from the discrete MEC CPU request decision using dedicated value heads. A lightweight MEC-side coordination mechanism ranks simultaneous offloading proposals according to their learned Q-value advantage and admits resource requests subject to the shared server-capacity constraint. Importantly, coordinated actions are applied during policy learning, ensuring consistency between the behavior executed in the environment and the transitions stored for training. The proposed approach is evaluated using independently trained models, validation based checkpoint selection, and held-out test scenarios. Across ten training seeds, FC-DDQN achieves a mean normalized constraint-aware system objective of 0.02005 with low inter-seed dispersion and zero mean MEC overload. Relative to conventional DDQN, the proposed architecture reduces the mean system objective by approximately 25%, while also reducing queue backlog and maintaining low deadline-violation rates. FC-DDQN approaches the performance of a strong Weighted Earliest Deadline First scheduler under the nominal configuration, with an objective gap of approximately 4%, while a model-based myopic controller remains the strongest reference when explicit analytical system knowledge is available. Ablation experiments show that training-time coordination and factorization of the offloading and CPU allocation decisions are responsible for most of the observed performance improvement. These findings indicate that explicit coordination and structured action representations can substantially improve value based multi-agent reinforcement learning for constrained MEC resource management, while also clarifying the operating regimes in which model-based scheduling remains advantageous.

Article.Title: A robust machine learning framework for multitemporal bare soil monitoring with high temporal transferability
Article.Authors: Avila-Lorduy L.; Mercado V.; Jiménez-Caldera J.; Vélez J.; Pacheco C.
Article.Abstract: Accurate monitoring of land degradation is critical for achieving land degradation neutrality, yet multitemporal assessments often suffer from low temporal transferability and threshold-related biases. Here, we present a robust machine learning framework to quantify long-term bare soil dynamics (1985–2020) across tropical drylands in Sucre, Colombia. Using Landsat time series, we evaluated Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and Logistic Regression (LR) ML models under three experimental strategies: year-specific assessment, interannual cross-validation, and combined multitemporal training. A total of 11,308 labeled samples were used for model calibration, and vegetation and soil indices were used as ancillary layers for sample support and quality control. SVM maps were additionally validated with 22,000 independent samples. Our results show a marked expansion of bare soil between 1985 and 2001 (+ 25,504 ha; + 53%), followed by a further increase from 2001 to 2010 (+ 53,351 ha; + 71.7%) and a subsequent reduction by 2020 (–28,475 ha; –22%). Although all models achieve high within-year accuracy, SVM showed the most consistent temporal generalization and external validation performance, with accuracy above 98% and Kappa values close to 1 across decades. Spectral contribution analysis identified Red, Green, and shortwave infrared (SWIR2) bands as the most informative predictors. In contrast, NDVI-based reclassification underestimated persistent bare soil by more than 96% relative to the multivariate ML approach. By integrating interannual validation, threshold-sensitivity analysis, and GIS-based persistence mapping, the proposed framework effectively distinguishes transient seasonal exposure from chronic degradation hotspots. These findings provide a scalable and transferable Earth observation workflow to support evidence-based territorial planning and soil conservation in vulnerable tropical landscapes.

Article.Title: Analysis of critical success factors for exoskeleton implementation in emerging economy context
Article.Authors: Kumar P.; Virmani N.; Agarwal S.; Bhandari D.; Garza-Reyes J.; Kumar H.; Pandey S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exoskeletons have received increasing attention in recent years due to their potential to reduce physical strain and the risk of musculoskeletal disorders, particularly in repetitive manufacturing tasks. However, the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing their successful implementation remain underexplored. This study therefore identifies and evaluates the CSFs for exoskeleton implementation in the automotive industry. A questionnaire was developed, and data were collected from four automotive manufacturing companies. The identified CSFs were analyzed using the fuzzy-Analytic Hierarchy Process (fuzzy-AHP) to develop a decision-making framework. The results indicate that “quick reconfigurability for easy switching between different manufacturing processes” and “ease of cooperative operations” are the two most important CSFs. The findings highlight the importance of human–machine interaction in dynamic and complex manufacturing environments and provide practical guidance for managers, practitioners, and decision-makers when selecting and implementing exoskeletons. The study contributes to the literature by developing a structured decision-making framework for exoskeleton implementation in the automotive industry.

Article.Title: Enhancing tropical cyclone intensity estimation via multi-scale spatial feature correlation
Article.Authors: Han J.; Zhu Z.
Article.Abstract: Tropical cyclones pose significant threats to coastal regions, necessitating accurate intensity estimates for effective disaster management. Traditional methods that rely on manual feature extraction suffer from subjectivity and limited scalability. This study introduces a multi-scale spatial feature correlation network for tropical cyclone intensity estimation. The model combines a deformable input block, residual feature extraction, squeeze-and-excitation channel recalibration, and strip pooling to represent irregular cloud morphology, inter-channel dependencies, and long-range spatial context. On the TCIR test set, the proposed model achieved a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 8.46 kt, compared with 8.68 kt without channel-specific smoothing. In the comparison experiments, SATCON and 3DAttentionTCNet yielded RMSEs of 9.21 and 9.48 kt, respectively.

Article.Title: The neural correlates of virtual bus following across adult age: an fMRI study
Article.Authors: Menze F.; Churchill N.; Fischer C.; Schweizer T.; Graham S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recent advances in virtual reality technology permit complex naturalistic behaviour to be studied in a safe, well-controlled manner with concurrent functional neuroimaging. One important application is driving a vehicle, a complex activity associated with substantial safety risks for old adults. Towards managing these safety concerns, improved understanding is needed of the driving-related changes in behaviour, cognition, and brain activity that occur with healthy aging. A cross-sectional study was thus conducted of individuals who performed an immersive bus-following task during fMRI (N = 41, 29 – 79 years). The distance between vehicles, response time, and performance variability each showed a positive association with age. Brain activity was evaluated for three participant-specific behavioural regressors (based on relative speed and relative velocity between the bus and car, and speed of lateral lane adjustments) revealing engagement of widespread visual, attentional, and motor regions. Positive associations between age and brain activity were found for prefrontal, temporal, and insular regions. These findings agree with the posterior-anterior-shift-in-aging and dedifferentiation models predicting the engagement of additional anterior brain regions when the elderly perform challenging tasks. This interpretation is consistent with older drivers requiring increased executive control to engage in safe driving behaviour compared to middle-aged drivers.

Article.Title: Frequency-domain ResNet-34 with stochastic augmentation enhances detection of AI-generated images
Article.Authors: Dorotík L.; Kopřiva A.; Oplatková Z.
Article.Abstract: Nowadays, diffusion-based generators such as Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, or DALL-E have made AI-generated visual content indistinguishable from authentic media, while online platforms often spread such material with inconsistent flagging of synthetic media, contributing to misinformation risks. To address this gap, a lightweight frequency-domain detector combining ResNet-34 with Advanced Stochastic Augmentation (ASA) was proposed, operating exclusively on the Fourier magnitude spectrum. Input images are converted to luminance, transformed via the fast Fourier Transform (FFT), log-scaled, and classified by a ResNet-34 trained on 53,988 class-balanced images from diffusion and GAN sources. ASA combines mobile ISP simulation, variable JPEG compression, blur, scaling, and Gaussian noise injection during training. Evaluation is performed on the SPAI cross-dataset benchmark covering 13 generators, with robustness assessed under compression, resizing, blur, and noise; an ablation study additionally confirms the contribution of ASA. Across 30 independent training runs, ResNet-34-FFT ASA achieves a mean SPAI benchmark AUC of 92.4% (95% CI [92.1%, 92.8%]), compared with 91.0% (SPAI), 85.5% (RINE), and 83.5% (DMID); the best observed run (seed 626) reaches 95.7%. On the internal test set, the best model attains 95.6% accuracy with sustained robustness under common image degradations (AUC $$\ge$$ 91% at JPEG Q = 50).

Article.Title: ColoPath-Mamba: a stain-aware pathology foundation–Mamba framework for six-class colorectal histopathological image classification
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Anandaram H.; Gupta N.; Sagar P.; Raghtate G.; Paliwal S.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal histopathological image classification plays a critical role in computer-aided diagnosis. However, discrimination between visually similar tissue types is often difficult due to the presence of various subtypes of glands, epithelial abnormalities, and staining patterns in hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained images. This study proposes ColoPath-Mamba, a stain-aware pathology foundation–Mamba framework for six-class colorectal histopathological image classification using the EBHI-Seg dataset. The proposed framework first applies stain-aware preprocessing and then extracts pathology-oriented representations using a pretrained pathology foundation encoder. A task-specific pathology adaptation layer is introduced to align the extracted features with EBHI-Seg diagnostic categories. To capture long-range tissue dependencies, a Vision Mamba-based tissue-context block is incorporated, followed by class-aware attention pooling for diagnostic feature aggregation. In addition, a stain-consistency regularization strategy is used to reduce sensitivity to controlled stain perturbations by enforcing representation similarity between stain-normalized and stain-augmented views of the same image. The model classifies images into six diagnostic categories. Experimental evaluation using a five-fold protocol shows that ColoPath-Mamba achieves 97.60% accuracy, 98.28% weighted precision and 97.72% weighted F1-score. Comparative and ablation analyses demonstrate that pathology foundation features, Mamba-based tissue-context modelling, class-aware attention, and stain-consistency learning jointly improve classification performance.

Article.Title: Employee’s previous rationalized knowledge-hiding and counterproductive work behavior toward the organization through the lens of the moral licensing mediation-moderation model
Article.Authors: Zada S.; Abdalla A.; Zada M.; Manzoor S.; Ali S.; Vega A.
Article.Abstract: Organizational success depends on skilled employees, who drive growth and innovation. However, employees may engage in seemingly well-intentioned actions, such as rationalized knowledge hiding (RKH), that can inadvertently harm the organization. Based on moral licensing theory (MLT), this study examines the effect of RKH on counterproductive work behavior toward the organization (CWB-O) through three distinct moral mechanisms: Moral Credits (MC), Moral Credentials (MCr), and Moral Pride (MP). The study further investigates whether past, present and future temporal focus conditions these relationships. We collected survey data from employees in Pakistan telecommunication sector and analyzed it using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings show that MC, MCr, and MP significantly mediate the relationship between RKH and CWB-O. Past, and present temporal focus strengthen the link between all three moral mechanisms and CWB-O. In contrast, future temporal focus weakens the effects of MC and MCr, but strengthens the effect of MP towards CWB-O. The study findings extend moral licensing research by showing that RKH can stimulate distinct moral self-regulatory processes and that their behavioral consequences vary according to employees’ temporal orientation.
