Article.Title: Integrated fungal-mediated tannin biodegradation and green synthesis of hematite (α-Fe₂O₃) nanoparticles using Trichoderma citrinoviride
Article.Authors: Alnhlaoui M.; Alghoraibi I.; Arnous M.; Ali-Nizam A.; Daghestani M.; Dagher W.; Zein R.
Article.Abstract: Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) have gained significant attention due to their wide-ranging applications across environmental, agricultural, biomedical, and industrial sectors. In this study, a sustainable dual-stage green synthesis approach was developed by coupling fungal-mediated tannin bioconversion with the biosynthesis of nanoparticles. Five species of Trichoderma were screened for their ability to degrade tannins extracted from Quercus coccifera leaves and to generate bioactive metabolites suitable for nanoparticle formation. Among them, Trichoderma citrinoviride showed the highest performance, achieving up to 90% tannin degradation at a 6% substrate concentration, along with tannase activity reaching 37.9 U/mg. The biodegradation products were subsequently utilized as natural reducing and stabilizing agents for the green synthesis of iron oxide nanoparticles using ferric chloride as a precursor. UV–Vis spectroscopy confirmed nanoparticle formation through a characteristic absorption peak at 256 nm. FTIR analysis indicated the presence of Fe–O bonds alongside hydroxyl and carbonyl functional groups, which contributed to both reduction and stabilization processes. XRD results verified the formation of well-crystallized hematite (α-Fe₂O₃) nanoparticles, with an estimated crystallinity of about 84% and an average crystallite size of approximately 10 nm. Morphological analysis via FESEM revealed predominantly quasi-spherical nanoparticles with sizes 19 ± 2.3 nm. AFM images indicated the presence of dendritic and branched surface patterns, likely resulting from particle aggregation and rearrangement during sample deposition and drying. Elemental analysis by EDX confirmed iron as the major constituent (53.52 wt%), while elemental mapping demonstrated a uniform distribution of iron and oxygen throughout the nanostructures. These findings indicate that tannin degradation products generated by Trichoderma fungi can act as supporting agents in the green synthesis of α-Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles. The integration of biodegradation with nanoparticle formation provides a practical route for utilizing tannin-rich biomass in material preparation. Overall, the results highlight the usefulness of fungal processes in nanoparticle synthesis under environmentally mild conditions.

Article.Title: Remote Ischemic PreConditioning (RIPC) enhances perfusion and pro-angiogenic activity of free microsurgical flaps in a randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Sogorski A.; Kurbacher A.; Behr B.; Reinkemeier F.; Drysch M.; Schmidt S.; Puscz F.; Steubing Y.; Wallner C.; Fiedler A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intraoperative ischemia and Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury (I/R) are indivisibly associated with free flap reconstruction. Representing a still unsolved problem of potential postoperative microvascular disturbance and consecutive tissue damage. Remote Ischemic PreConditioning (RIPC) can interfere with such harmful mechanisms by attenuating I/R and improving microvascular perfusion. We conducted this randomized controlled study in patients scheduled for autologous breast reconstruction who received RIPC to systematically examine postoperative perfusion characteristics and molecular changes within transferred flaps. Flaps were randomized to receive either No RIPC, Early RIPC (18-24 h prior to surgery) or Late RIPC (1 h before surgery). Comprehensive analysis of flaps’ microcirculation (microvascular Blood Flow, Tissue Oxygen Saturation) was carried out for 4 consecutive days. Additionally, consecutive tissue samples were taken at different times (incision, closure, 5th postoperative day) to determine the course of HIF1-a, VEGF and CD31/PECAM1 levels perioperatively. Compared to No RIPC, postoperative microcirculation in conditioned flaps improved significantly (p < 0.05) within the first 4 postoperative days (POD), resulting in a significantly higher tissue oxygenation in Early RIPC flaps by POD 4 (64.62% vs. 47.03% StO2 (p < 0.05)). HIF1-α levels in both conditioning groups were found reduced by POD 5 compared to No RIPC flaps (p < 0.05), whereas angiogenetic activity was significantly increased (CD31/PECAM1: p < 0.0001). RIPC is a safe technique that can improve postoperative microcirculation and tissue oxygenation in free microsurgical flaps. Beyond attenuating effects on I/R, Early RIPC improves postoperative angiogenetic potential including HIF1-a and VEGF modification resulting in superior perfusion capabilities compared to unconditioned flaps.

Article.Title: Molecular characterization of Plasmodium falciparum MSP-2 allelic diversity and infection complexity in patients attending Bamenda regional hospital, Cameroon
Article.Authors: Anangmo C.; Yamssi C.; Sah M.; Djeussi D.; Mba G.; Tsague M.; Nkadeu G.; Vershiyi B.; Tsopdjou R.; Ndjebet P.; Djimta S.; Ngouemo P.; Medjouyo S.; Haroun-Abdoulaye I.; Nguimbou E.; Hu H.; Luyten W.
Article.Abstract: The control of malaria in sub-Saharan Africa remains threatened by the emergence of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains and the high genetic polymorphism of the parasite. This study aimed to determine the genetic diversity of the merozoite surface protein 2 ( msp2 ) gene and the complexity of P. falciparum infections among patients attending Bamenda Regional Hospital, Cameroon. This was a hospital-based cross-sectional study conducted among 299 consenting participants attending Bamenda Regional Hospital. Malaria was diagnosed using rapid diagnostic tests. Samples that tested positive were selected for molecular analysis. DNA was extracted from dried blood spots using Chelex-100, and msp2 allelic families (FC27 and 3D7/IC) were genotyped by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Genetic diversity was assessed using expected heterozygosity (He), and family-specific mean allele count was estimated from the number of alleles detected per isolate. Data were analyzed using SPSS. The malaria test-positivity of P. falciparum infection was 32.12% (96/299). In univariate analysis, it was significantly associated with age ( p = 0.003), occupation ( p = 0.006), marital status ( p = 0.04), insecticide use ( p < 0.001), and the presence of stagnant water ( p = 0.005). The FC27 allelic family was detected in 86 isolates, comprising 32 alleles, with a heterozygosity of 0.94 and a mean allele count of 2.10. The 3D7/IC family was detected in all isolates, with 35 alleles, a heterozygosity of 0.96, and a mean allele count of 2.42, indicating high genetic diversity and predominantly polyclonal infections. Plasmodium falciparum isolates circulating in Bamenda exhibit high genetic diversity and a high proportion of polyclonal infections, reflecting sustained malaria transmission. These findings provide valuable baseline molecular epidemiological data to guide malaria surveillance and reinforce control efforts.

Article.Title: Responses of macrofauna communities to changes in physicochemical elements in the southern Caspian coastal waters (Anzali Lagoon and Gorgan Bay, two sites of Ramsar convention)
Article.Authors: Jamshidi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Over the past 5 years, the Caspian Sea shrinkage has had a detrimental impact on two significant Ramsar sites along the Caspian Sea coast: the Gorgan Bay in the east and the Anzali Lagoon in the west. The present results show that reduction of the Caspian Sea size can have notable effects on physicochemical factors like water depth, salinity, temperature, and nutrient levels in both mentioned ecosystems which in turn influencing the aquatic environment as well as density, biodiversity and community structure benthic fauna. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the current status of macrofauna communities in response to recent environmental changes and reduced water levels in these two Ramsar wetlands. To achieve this, field sampling was conducted at 11 stations in the Anzali Lagoon and eight stations in the Gorgan Bay during February 2023. At each station, physicochemical parameters (depth, temperature, salinity, pH, dissolved oxygen, nutrients, sediment organic matter, and grain size) were measured, and benthic macrofauna samples were collected using a Van Veen grab (250 cm²). Multivariate statistical analyses were applied to examine the relationships between environmental variables and macrofauna community structure. In the Anzali Lagoon, a decrease in depth and salinity was observed compared to previous records, while in the Gorgan Bay, a decrease in depth along with a substantial increase in salinity (about three times higher than 2010–2013 levels) was recorded. In the Anzali Lagoon, nine species of macrofauna, predominantly freshwater taxa, were found. In the Gorgan Bay, the study revealed ten species of macrofauna, primarily comprising brackish-water species. In both ecosystems, spatial differences in macrofauna density and community structure were observed, which were significantly correlated with physicochemical factors. While these findings suggest that recent environmental changes may be influencing benthic communities, the single sampling event limits our ability to attribute these patterns definitively to long-term climate-driven trends. Long-term monitoring is therefore recommended to better understand the temporal dynamics of these ecosystems.

Article.Title: Hierarchical and local detail enhancement for small object detection in aerial images
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Bie Y.; Jia X.; Wang B.; Gao G.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Accurate small object detection in aerial images is important for vision-based applications. Detecting unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and birds in airport clearance zones is particularly important for aviation safety. Nevertheless, existing approaches still suffer from pronounced semantic inconsistencies between high-level semantic representations and low-level structural cues during multi-scale feature fusion. Furthermore, local structural information of small targets is prone to degradation during deep semantic modeling and cross-scale feature aggregation, leading to compromised detection performance. To mitigate these issues, we introduce HLD-DETR, a Hierarchical and Local Detail Enhancement framework for small object detection in aerial images. In particular, the Hierarchical Detail Complementation Module (HDCM) selectively integrates low-level structural details into deep semantic features via a cross-level cross-attention mechanism. Thereafter, the Local Detail Refinement Module (LDRM) combines multidirectional local structural modeling with channel attention to explicitly refine the local structural features of small objects. Collectively, HDCM and LDRM systematically address cross-level interaction and local structural enhancement, synergistically improving small object feature representation. Additionally, we construct the UB-SOD dataset, specifically for detecting small UAVs and birds in airport clearance zones. Extensive experiments on both UB-SOD and the publicly available VisDrone2019 datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of HLD-DETR for small object detection in aerial images, while further validating its applicability to airport clearance zone scenarios.

Article.Title: Salmonella species shedding in the feces of healthy horses in Jordan: prevalence, antimicrobial resistance, virulence genes, and associated risk factors
Article.Authors: Alzuheir I.; Aljarrah A.; Abutarbush S.; Gharaibeh M.; Alekish M.; Al Majali A.; Alguzo A.
Article.Abstract: Salmonella is an important zoonotic pathogen that affects both animals and humans. In horses, infection is often subclinical, and infected animals may act as carriers that intermittently shed the organism, contributing to environmental contamination and transmission. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of Salmonella. spp. fecal shedding in horses in Jordan, identify associated risk factors, evaluate antimicrobial resistance profiles, and detect selected virulence-associated and antimicrobial resistance genes. A total of 900 fecal samples were collected from 100 horses from different regions of Jordan over a nine-month period (May 2023–January 2024), with nine serial samples collected from each horse. The samples were examined via enrichment culture followed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to target the invA gene. The PCR positive isolates were subjected to antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the disk diffusion method according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Selected antimicrobial resistance- and virulence-associated genes were detected via PCR, and risk factors associated with fecal shedding were assessed via univariate analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Overall, 37/900 (4.11%) fecal samples were positive for Salmonella spp . following enrichment-PCR analysis and culture-based prevalence as 23/900 (2.6%). Twenty-four horses (24%) were identified as fecal shedders, and five horses (20.8%) showed repeated shedding over multiple sampling periods. Salmonella was cultured from 23/37 (62.2%) PCR-positive samples. All the isolates exhibited multidrug resistance. High resistance rates were observed against doxycycline, tetracycline, ampicillin, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, and chloramphenicol (100%). The most frequently detected antimicrobial resistance genes were blaTEM (91.3%), aph(3)-III (82.6%), floR (82.6%), and tetA (78.3%). Among the virulence genes investigated, ompA was the most prevalent (95.7%), followed by ompF and spvC (91.3% each). Logistic regression analysis revealed that training was a significant risk factor associated with increased fecal shedding (OR = 5.225, 95% CI 1.765–15.467, p = 0.003). The findings from this study demonstrate that healthy horses in Jordan can serve as carriers of multidrug-resistant Salmonella spp . and contribute to environmental contamination. Improved biosecurity practices and antimicrobial stewardship are recommended to reduce transmission risks among animals and humans.

Article.Title: Hydrogeological and redox controls on trace metal(loid) mobilization in a Himalayan multi-aquifer system
Article.Authors: Dar T.; Jahan A.; Rai N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Groundwater in Himalayan intermontane basins represents a critical freshwater resource, yet the hydrogeological and geochemical controls governing trace metal(loid) mobilization remain poorly understood. This study investigates the occurrence, distribution, and potential sources of twelve trace metal(loid)s in the Upper Jhelum River Basin (UJRB), Kashmir Himalaya, comprising shallow groundwater (SGW; n = 51), deep groundwater (DGW; n = 103), and springs (SPR; n = 80). Hydrogeological characterization, groundwater-flow analysis, geochemical indicators, and positive matrix factorization (PMF) were integrated to examine trace metal(loid) distributions across contrasting aquifer environments. Several trace metal(loid)s exceeded drinking-water guideline values, with maximum As and Cr concentrations reaching 147 and 4334 µg L⁻ 1 , respectively, in DGW. Spatial patterns and redox indicators suggest that aquifer architecture, lithological heterogeneity, groundwater-flow conditions, and redox variability influence trace metal(loid) occurrence. The co-occurrence of elevated Fe, Mn, and As in fine-grained, relatively low-Eh aquifer environments is consistent with reductive dissolution of Fe–Mn-bearing phases as a potential mobilization mechanism. In contrast, localized Cr enrichment may reflect interactions between Cr-bearing lithological materials and diffuse anthropogenic inputs. PMF resolved four factors interpreted as geogenic/weathering–redox (25.4–37.3%), predominantly agricultural (11.9–29.7%), combustion-related (12.7–34.3%), and mixed-source contributions (16.6–32.0%). Their relative contributions varied among groundwater environments, indicating the combined influence of natural processes and anthropogenic activities. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of integrating aquifer architecture, groundwater-flow characteristics, and hydrogeochemical conditions when evaluating trace metal(loid) occurrence and potential contamination sources in complex Himalayan groundwater systems.

Article.Title: Risk assessment of heavy metals in popular toothpaste brands in central area of Iran
Article.Authors: Mohammadzadeh M.; Zarajabad A.; Rahimi H.; Mirzaei N.; Mostafaii G.
Article.Abstract: Toothpaste is a widely used oral care product valued for its ability to clean and polish teeth, remove plaque, reduce oral bacteria, and combat dental diseases. However, microbial or chemical (heavy metals) contamination can cause severe health effects. In the present study, nine adult toothpaste brands (five Iranian and four foreign) and four children’s toothpaste brands with high sales were investigated for assessing their heavy metal content. Comprehensive Quality Assurance (QA), Quality Control (QC), and validation procedures were employed to ensure accuracy. Samples were processed and digested for analysis using ICP-OES. The results indicated that no brand exceeded the permissible limit of arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd) and antimony (Sb). Significant variability was observed in heavy metal concentrations across brands. Based on risk assessment results, Arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), nickel (Ni), and lead (Pb) fell within the acceptable risk range, indicating very low cancer risk. Copper (Cu) had a mean Lifetime Cancer Risk of 1.48 \(\times \) 10 −6 , within the possible risk range. The Hazard Index (HI) for these metals was also below 1, indicating no significant non-carcinogenic risk. The estimated carcinogenic risk of Cu in children’s toothpastes fell within the 10 −6 –10 −4 range, whereas Pb risk estimates were below 10 −6 ; all HQ values remained below 1, with Zn exhibiting the highest HQ. The composition of toothpaste, particularly concerning heavy metals, requires continuous monitoring and stringent control to ensure consumer safety.

Article.Title: An interpretable machine learning framework for automated screening of patient-facing LLM consultations: a comparative evaluation in medical aesthetic consultation
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Sun X.; Lei S.; Geng J.; Shao Z.; Si X.
Article.Abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into patient-facing clinical decision support systems (CDSS) has outpaced the development of automated quality assurance mechanisms. In medical aesthetic consultation—where patient safety and informed decision-making are paramount—no validated framework exists for pre-deployment screening of LLM-generated content. To develop and evaluate an interpretable machine-learning framework that screens LLM-generated patient-facing consultations using automatically computable generation metadata and readability features—as a triage aid for prioritising expert review—and to comparatively evaluate DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi in medical aesthetic consultation. We generated 600 responses from 25 standardized queries across five aesthetic topics using DeepSeek-V3 (DeepSeek-AI, Hangzhou, China) and Kimi (Moonshot AI, Beijing, China) under six prompt strategies and two conversational modes. Two blinded dermatologists rated quality on six dimensions (accuracy, relevance, comprehensiveness, empathy, falsehood, safety). Readability was quantified using Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, and SMOG Index. Four machine learning models were trained to predict high-quality responses (composite score ≥ 4.0, pre-specified threshold) and evaluated with question-level grouped 5-fold cross-validation—in which all 24 responses of each seed question were confined to a single fold to prevent information leakage—with SHAP analysis to identify key predictive features. Between-model quality comparisons used paired tests reflecting the matched design. To align evaluation with the triage purpose, performance was additionally assessed with low-quality responses as the positive class (precision–recall analysis and review-burden operating points), and robustness was examined using alternative quality thresholds and an applicability-adjusted composite score. DeepSeek-V3 achieved higher composite quality than Kimi (3.89 ± 0.45 vs. 3.70 ± 0.38, paired Wilcoxon P < 0.001; robust under applicability-adjusted scoring). Prompt strategy was the dominant quality determinant (Friedman test, Kendall’s W = 0.376), with sixth-grade reading level prompts paradoxically yielding the lowest scores (3.25 ± 0.40). All ML models achieved moderate discrimination under question-level grouped cross-validation (AUC 0.714–0.732; response-level sensitivity analysis: 0.758–0.773), with findings robust to alternative quality thresholds (AUC 0.749–0.797 at cutoff 3.5 and 0.725–0.838 at cutoff 4.5) and to applicability-adjusted labelling (AUC 0.679–0.702); prompt strategy, sentence length, and model identity were the strongest SHAP-identified predictors. Aligned with the triage purpose, average precision for low-quality detection reached 0.802 (Logistic Regression), and capturing 90% of low-quality responses required flagging 83.2% of responses for expert review. The proposed framework demonstrates feasibility as an explainable triage aid that flags potentially low-quality LLM consultations for expert review using generation metadata and readability features; it does not assess semantic or clinical content, and expert review remains indispensable. Findings underscore that prompt engineering—not model selection alone—drives output quality, and that readability optimization must be decoupled from clinical completeness to ensure safe deployment in aesthetic medicine information systems.

Article.Title: Design and optimization of high-density calcium nitrate completion fluids for HPHT applications: an integrated experimental and machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Ahmadi A.; Khamehchi E.; Saffar S.; Mahdavi Kalatehno J.
Article.Abstract: Exploring hydrocarbon resources in High-Pressure/High-Temperature (HPHT) environments requires advanced, solids-free completion fluids to maximize productivity and mitigate formation damage. This study presents an integrated approach combining laboratory experimentation and machine learning (ML) to design high-density, thermally stable completion fluids. The experimental phase evaluated the incorporation of polyols (MEG, DEG, TEG) into calcium nitrate brines. Results established that while all polyols enhanced density and thermal stability, MEG provided the optimal equilibrium between density, rheology, and clarity, avoiding the excessive viscosity induced by heavier glycols. Leveraging the experimental dataset, predictive ML models were subsequently developed to forecast critical fluid properties. A comparative analysis of five algorithms revealed a task-specific optimal hierarchy: the Random Forest algorithm best captured the complex non-linearities of viscosity, whereas the Extra Trees algorithm demonstrated superior precision in modeling deterministic, thermodynamic density variations. Ultimately, this research delivers a validated fluid formulation for HPHT operations and establishes robust computational frameworks to streamline the future design and optimization of advanced completion fluids.

Article.Title: Altered CAV1 expression correlates inversely with DCN level, and CAV1 is associated with the progression of endometriosis
Article.Authors: Lu Z.; Wang Y.; Gao Y.
Article.Abstract: Endometriosis is a disorder that significantly impairs women’s quality of life and reduces pregnancy rates. Its pathogenesis remains unclear, and effective treatment options are lacking, making the investigation of its molecular mechanisms and the development of therapies particularly challenging. Single-cell transcriptome datasets downloaded from the NCBI database were analyzed to screen caveolin-1 ( CAV1 ) as a hub gene linked to endometriosis. Bioinformatics analysis was performed to evaluate the potential expression association between CAV1 and decorin ( DCN ). Subsequent verification was conducted at clinical tissue, cellular and in vivo animal levels. CAV1 participates in angiogenesis, migration and adhesion of endometrial stromal cells. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence verified markedly upregulated CAV1 expression in ectopic endometrial lesions. Functional experiments in immortalized human endometrial stromal cells (THESCs) validated that CAV1 enhances stromal angiogenesis, migratory and adhesive capacities. Correlation analysis uncovered an inverse expression pattern between CAV1 and DCN . RT‒qPCR and immunofluorescence assays further verified their interaction and opposite expression tendency. CAV1 aggravates endometriosis progression by accelerating stromal angiogenesis, migration and adhesion. Moreover, CAV1 interacts with DCN and presents an inverse expression trend with DCN in endometriotic lesions, implying a potential functional linkage between the two molecules during disease progression.

Article.Title: A computer-vision-driven dynamic color rendering algorithm for virtual reality and its application in remote art creation systems
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Huang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Remote art creation in virtual reality continues to be undermined by three coupled problems: color distortion under transient illumination, tail latency during rapid brushwork, and chromatic divergence across heterogeneous headsets. This study develops a computer-vision-driven dynamic color rendering algorithm and embeds it within a working remote art creation platform. The algorithm consists of three loosely coupled stages: a chroma-preserving feature encoder that reads scene context, a hypernetwork-conditioned non-linear mapping module weighted by spatial and channel attention, and a saliency-driven scheduler that applies per-terminal correction within a sub-frame budget. Color is treated as a first-class replicated quantity through a CRDT-based synchronization layer, with bandwidth-adaptive quantization preserving consistency under degraded networks. Experiments on a mixed HTC Vive Pro and Oculus Quest platform across 240 painted scenes show cross-terminal CIEDE2000 values near 2.1 under high-bandwidth conditions, against five to twelve for current platforms, with 95th-percentile latency held below 20 ms. A user study with thirty practicing artists across paired painting, mural construction, and instructor-led demonstration scenarios returned composite experience scores of 6.18 against 4.79 for the strongest baseline, with the gap concentrated in the color consistency and coordination dimensions. Robustness tests under cycling illumination, HDR scenes, and concurrent collaboration up to thirty-two peers confirmed graceful scaling, with logarithmic convergence growth and material-class generality across painting, sculpture, and installation work. Limitations remain at sub-5 Mbps bandwidths and on 8K-class panels, pointing toward multimodal sensing and aesthetic-quality optimization as next steps.

Article.Title: A dual-center radiological and clinical model for predicting invasive pulmonary fungal infections in the elderly
Article.Authors: Pang X.; Wang X.; Zeng M.; Zhang Q.; Xiong W.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early identification and risk stratification of invasive pulmonary fungal infection (IPFI) are crucial for timely antifungal evaluation and management in elderly patients with pulmonary infection. At present, there is a lack of clinical-radiological risk stratification model for estimating IPFI risk in the elderly. Data from 364 patients aged ≥ 60 years, comprising an IPFI group and a comparison group, were used to identify predictors through binary logistic regression analysis and develop the prediction model. Model performance was subsequently evaluated in an independent validation cohort of 104 patients. Diabetes mellitus, acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, malnutrition after admission, pre-admission broad-spectrum antibiotic use, right lower lobe involvement, left upper lobe involvement, left lower lobe involvement, ground-glass opacity, air bronchogram sign, and consolidation were retained as final model predictors. In the independent validation cohort, the combined clinical-image model, clinical model, and image model achieved AUCs of 0.808 (95% CI, 0.723–0.892), 0.821 (95% CI, 0.740–0.902), and 0.704 (95% CI, 0.604–0.804), respectively. The clinical-radiological prediction model may serve as a practical risk stratification tool to assist clinicians in early identification and timely management of elderly patients at high risk of invasive pulmonary fungal infections.

Article.Title: Perceived social support, self-compassion, and substance use cravings in patients receiving methadone maintenance treatment
Article.Authors: Heidarian P.; Jalali A.; Ezzati E.; Khaledi B.; Salari N.
Article.Abstract: Managing drug cravings is a critical component of successful addiction recovery. Psychological and interpersonal resources, such as perceived social support (PSS) and self-compassion, may relate to craving intensity. This study examined the relationships between PSS, self-compassion, and drug cravings among patients receiving methadone maintenance treatment (MMT). In this cross-sectional correlational study, 300 patients were recruited from MMT clinics in Kermanshah, Iran (2023–2024). Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Neff Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), the Community Assessment Inventory (CAI), and the Desires for Drug Questionnaire (DDQ). Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman rank-order correlations, and two-step hierarchical multiple linear regression adjusting for sociodemographic covariates. The mean scores for PSS, self-compassion, and drug cravings were 103.32 ± 12.12, 78.57 ± 12.24, and 54.93 ± 16.86, respectively. Bivariate analyses revealed a robust negative correlation between self-compassion and craving (r s = − 0.599, P < 0.001) and a weak positive correlation between PSS and craving (r s = 0.134, P = 0.021), whereas PSS and self-compassion were not significantly correlated (r​ s = 0.048, P = 0.405). In the final hierarchical multiple regression model (R 2 = 0.427, adjusted R 2 = 0.409, P < 0.001), self-compassion emerged as the strongest independent protective predictor of craving (β=−0.567, P < 0.001). PSS retained a modest positive association with craving (β = 0.118, P = 0.012), alongside older age (β=−0.243, P = 0.001) and higher education (β=−0.195, P < 0.001). Self-compassion demonstrates a robust, inverse association with craving intensity among patients undergoing MMT, highlighting the primacy of intrapersonal emotional regulation over external support networks in managing substance cravings. Compassion-focused interventions should be integrated into standard MMT protocols to help mitigate craving and prevent relapse.

Article.Authors: Chahir R.; Hammani N.; Khaali W.; Chakir S.; Baghtoul M.; Hboub H.; Benmrid R.; Bouchmaa N.; Elfatimy R.; Oukkache N.
Article.Abstract: We developed an in-house indirect ELISA for relative measurement of IgG binding to the SARS-CoV-2 Spike receptor-binding domain (RBD; Omicron BA.1). Within-run OD-based coefficients of variation were 4.1–6.5%, and between-run AU-based coefficients of variation were 2.4–8.8% across three days with one operator. In a pilot panel of 10 sera from patients with RT-PCR-confirmed infection and 10 pre-pandemic sera, the cut-off (0.134 OD₄₀₅; mean + 3 SD of the pre-pandemic sera) gave a sensitivity of 90.0% (95% CI 59.​6–98.2%). The same negative sera were used to set the cut-off, thus the specificity was estimated by leave-one-out analysis and was 90.0% (59.6–98.2%), with an accuracy of 90.0% (69.9–97.2%). Apparent specificity at the fixed cut-off was 100%. The ROC AUC was 0.99 (95% CI 0.94–1.00). These findings support further development of a research serology platform, with independent clinical validation and calibration harmonisation needed before broader quantitative or diagnostic use.

Article.Title: Enhanced oil recovery via foams featuring various nanoparticle and polymer formulations
Article.Authors: Mirgaloye Bayat D.; Esfandyari Bayat A.
Article.Abstract: This study comprehensively investigated how various additives affect the stability of nitrogen (N 2 ) foam at 25, 60, and 90 °C, focusing on both the fundamental mechanisms that influence foam behavior and its practical applications in enhanced oil recovery (EOR) processes. The methodology utilized involved silica nanoparticles (SiO 2 -NPs) and Polyethylene Glycol (PEG). To determine the most effective approach for enhancing foam stability, two stabilization methods were assessed. The initial approach focused on coated SiO 2 -NPs, while the subsequent method investigated the synergistic impact of PEG and SiO 2 -NPs. Incorporating PEG into the base formulation enhanced foam stability more effectively than simply adding SiO 2 -NPs. Moreover, the foam formulation that included both SiO 2 -NPs and PEG exhibited the highest stability compared to the other formulations across all temperatures. Characterization at the bubble level revealed that foams with greater stability featured smaller, more uniformly distributed bubbles and thicker lamellae. SiO 2 -NPs + PEG formulation resulted in the most substantial improvement in foam structure, achieving the smallest bubble sizes and the thickest lamellae. Furthermore, SiO 2 -NPs + PEG foam increased oil recovery by as much as 43.2% by amplifying viscous forces while diminishing capillary forces. Our findings suggest that the combination of PEG with NPs can produce long-lasting, heat-resistant foams suitable for EOR applications.

Article.Authors: Sabei L.; Parada Sarmiento M.; Correa G.; Lima S.; Nogueira S.; Parsons T.; Zanella A.
Article.Abstract: The environment of male parents can alter their offspring’s development through epigenetic mechanisms, potentially influencing their coping behaviors and emotional states. This study aimed to assess the emotionality of piglets sired by boars housed in crates (C), pens (P), or enriched pens (E). Male piglets born from these matings were behaviorally tested at 25 days of age, and treatment was identified using a post hoc paternity test. As vocalizations can provide insight into an animal’s emotional state, acoustic recordings were conducted during open field (OF), novel object (NO), and elevated plus maze (EPM) tests. A total of 46,685 piglet vocalizations were categorized into four types: low-grunts (LG), high-grunts (HG), low-squeals (LS), and high-squeals (HS). Generalized linear mixed models were used to identify differences ( p < 0.05). Treatment C piglets exhibited a greater overall tendency to vocalize than the other treatments. They vocalized more HS calls than P or E piglets across all behavioral tests. C piglets vocalized more HG than E piglets in NO, more HG than P in EPM, more LS than E piglets in NO, more LG than P piglets in EPM, but vocalized fewer LG than E piglets during OF. Our results showed that the boar’s environment alters the vocalizations of its offspring during behavioral tests and suggest that C piglets’ experience in these tests was more aversive than those sired by boars housed in other treatments. Our findings support the possible intergenerational inheritance of behavioral traits that help cope with unfamiliar surroundings and advance the use of vocalization to assess animal welfare.

Article.Authors: Abdelrahman M.; Emam M.; Alsharif A.; Almohammadi B.; Refaey H.

The PVT-PCM system incorporated encapsulated RT35 paraffin wax within a water-cooling channel, while the PVT-water system employed three different copper absorber configurations. Both systems were tested at flow rates of 2 and 3 L/min under insulated and non-insulated conditions. The results showed that both cooling approaches significantly improved photovoltaic performance compared with the reference uncooled PV module. However, the PVT-PCM system consistently achieved superior thermal regulation through the combined effects of active water cooling and latent heat storage. The maximum PV temperature reduction reached 6.5 °C for the PVT-PCM system compared with 4.9 °C for the PVT-water configuration. Consequently, the PVT-PCM system improved electrical power generation by up to 23.6%, while the PVT-water system achieved improvements of approximately 11%. The highest thermal and overall efficiencies obtained for the PVT-PCM system were 62.5% and 76.5%, respectively, compared with 59.3% and 72.4% for the PVT-water system. In addition, exergy analysis confirmed improved thermodynamic performance for the PCM-assisted configuration due to enhanced thermal regulation and reduced thermal irreversibility. The findings demonstrate that integrating encapsulated phase change material with active water cooling provides an effective hybrid thermal management strategy for photovoltaic thermal systems operating in hot climates, resulting in significant improvements in thermal regulation, energy recovery, and overall system performance.

The method was successfully applied to human urine and plasma samples, providing recoveries above 90% with RSDs below 5.2%. Integrating of G-EME with electrochemical detection eliminated the need for a separate desorption step and reduced the total analysis time to less than 20 min. Furthermore, the greenness of the method was evaluated using the Analytical GREEnness (AGREE) metric, yielding a score of 0.81, which confirms its environmental compatibility.

Article.Authors: Maleki A.
Article.Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

In this new framework, a combination of fuzzy logic system, convolutional neural network (CNN) and local binary pattern (LBP) has been used to increase the contrast and improve the quality of the images. The first part of the framework consists of a parser network based on fuzzy logic and LBP, which decomposes the image into illumination and reflectance components. In the next step, the CNN-based adjustment network balances the exposure level by correcting the brightness component and reconstructs the colors with high fidelity. The meta-heuristic SWO algorithm guides the optimization steps of both parts and reduces noise and improves resolution in real time. The results of the experiments showed that the proposed method has a superior performance compared to the traditional methods, so that while obtaining better clarity and contrast in the images, the radiation dose received by the body was reduced by 72.15%. This approach can be effective in cardiac angiography to increase the quality of imaging and reduce the risk of radiation for patients and doctors.

Article.Title: Toona sinensis attenuates lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment alongside coordinated hippocampal metabolic shifts
Article.Authors: Shon W.; Jung C.; Putra H.; Cho I.; Youn J.; Yoon Y.; Kim S.; Park H.; Jang H.; Kwon S.
Article.Abstract: Neuroinflammation is a major contributor to cognitive decline, yet effective interventions remain limited. Toona sinensis (TS), an edible medicinal plant widely consumed in East Asia, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its potential to counter neuroinflammation-associated cognitive impairment and the accompanying hippocampal metabolic alterations remains unclear. We investigated whether sustained TS supplementation attenuates lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced cognitive impairment and characterized the accompanying hippocampal metabolic profiles under inflammatory challenge. RNA sequencing of 50 medicinal plant extracts in LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia identified TS as a potent suppressor of inflammatory gene expression. In LPS-challenged mice, chronic TS supplementation improved spatial learning and recognition memory and attenuated LPS-associated increases in hippocampal IBA1 immunoreactivity, MHC-II abundance, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. Untargeted LC–MS/MS metabolomics revealed LPS-associated alterations in purine metabolism, amino acid and tricarboxylic acid (TCA)-linked pathways, and glycerophospholipid metabolism, whereas TS supplementation was accompanied by shifts toward control-like metabolite profiles, including higher adenosine and lower lysophosphatidylcholine levels than in the LPS group. Chemical profiling annotated multiple flavonoids and phenolic acids in the TS extract. Together, TS supplementation attenuated cognitive impairment and hippocampal inflammatory responses during LPS challenge, alongside coordinated hippocampal metabolic shifts, supporting further mechanistic and translational investigation.

Article.Title: EAKD-CFND: continual fake news detection through adaptive knowledge distillation with external verification
Article.Authors: Jolly A.; Kumar S.; Paliwal S.
Article.Abstract: Fake news spreads faster than detection models can adapt, and models updated on new data tend to forget what they learned before, an effect severe enough to make naive deployments impractical for continuous, streaming fake-news detection (FND). Continual-learning methods address this either by storing real past examples for replay, which is accurate but carries a memory and privacy cost many streaming deployments cannot accept, or by staying exemplar-free, which avoids that cost but can degrade badly under severe task drift; a deployer is typically forced to commit to one property or the other before knowing which their data will actually require. We introduce EAKD-CFND, a class-incremental continual-learning framework built around one mechanism, per-instance uncertainty-adaptive knowledge distillation with external fact-checking verification, offered in two configurations that share that mechanism: an exemplar-free default (EAKD-CFND) that never stores a past instance, and a rehearsal-augmented configuration (EAKD-CFND-R) that adds a small reservoir buffer for settings where storage is available and drift risk is high. We evaluate both configurations against five baselines (fine-tuning, EWC, LwF, the rehearsal-based DER, and the category-level adaptive-KD method LUD) under one identical protocol on three real class-incremental splits built from PHEME and FakeNewsNet, and measure calibration, hyperparameter sensitivity, and verification cost end to end. The exemplar-free configuration is statistically indistinguishable from every baseline tested, including rehearsal-based DER, on both FakeNewsNet splits, at zero storage cost. On PHEME’s more demanding five-task sequence, the exemplar-free configuration collapses to near-random accuracy alongside every other exemplar-free method tested, while DER’s stored exemplars carry it to 84.8%; switching to the rehearsal-augmented configuration closes that gap (85.5% on PHEME-Event, matching DER within noise), giving a working option for exactly the regime where the exemplar-free default falls short. The rehearsal-augmented configuration is not a single-benchmark fix: on FNN-Poli-Time it adds a further, measured gain over both the exemplar-free default and DER, while on FNN-Gossip-Time it adds nothing, a benchmark-specific split traced directly to how much genuine task drift each benchmark actually contains. The uncertainty signal itself is poorly calibrated in absolute terms (Expected Calibration Error 0.80–0.84 across four estimators), but the framework’s accuracy is robust to its two governing hyperparameters across a wide sweep, and its API cost is quantified rather than assumed. Together these results give practitioners a working choice between the two configurations, made on measured grounds rather than a qualitative argument: exemplar-free by default, rehearsal-augmented when storage is available and drift risk is severe.

Article.Title: Synonymous codon usage bias in Rhododendron: unveiling the roles of mutational pressure and natural selection across eight species
Article.Authors: Ma W.; Chen H.; Yu H.; Liu T.; Ji H.; Wang X.; Yu T.
Article.Abstract: Codon usage bias (CUB), the non-random usage of synonymous codons, influences gene expression and protein synthesis. This study conducts an investigation into CUB in eight Rhododendron species. By analyzing nucleotide composition, neutrality, synonymous codon usage, and interspecies correlations, it aims to characterize the contributions of mutational pressure and non-mutational evolutionary forces, including, but not limited to, natural selection. The total GC showed limited variation across species, with values ranging from 45.62% ( R. griersonianum ) to 47.19% ( R. vialii ), while GC content at different codon positions (GC1, GC2, GC3) varied significantly. Neutrality plots indicated that mutational pressure weakly influences CUB, suggesting that factors beyond mutational pressure contribute to the observed bias. ENC-GC3s analysis revealed that most genes clustered below the expected curve, further supporting the contribution of factors beyond mutational pressure, although this deviation is not diagnostic of any single mechanism and could also reflect other non-mutational factors such as mRNA stability. A consistent bias towards A < T and G > C at the third codon position was observed across all species using PR2 plot analysis. Pairwise RSCU correlations were extremely high across all eight species (Pearson’s r = 0.9991–0.9997). The RSCU-based dendrogram groups the species solely according to the similarity of their codon-usage profiles; it is a descriptive ordination of RSCU vectors, not a phylogenetic or taxonomic tree, and neither agreement with nor deviation from reported taxonomic groupings should be interpreted as evidence of evolutionary relationships. Compared to other plant lineages, Rhododendron exhibits a constrained GC content range, which may reflect either a constrained mutational landscape or stabilizing selection, although the present data cannot distinguish between these alternatives. This study provides valuable insights into the evolutionary forces shaping CUB in Rhododendron , indicating that mutational pressure alone is insufficient to explain CUB, while a contribution of natural selection (including possible translational selection) remains plausible but is not established here because tRNA-abundance, gene-expression, and translational-efficiency data were not examined.These findings provide a genome-wide descriptive baseline of synonymous codon usage in this ecologically and economically important genus; broader evolutionary or adaptive conclusions would require additional functional, expression, and tRNA data, and this study therefore provides a foundation for such future studies.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: mutation pressure; Rhododendron; natural selection; GC content; codon usage bias; synonymous codons; stabilizing selection; plant genomics; mRNA stability

Article.Title: Spectra-Scope: a toolkit for automated and interpretable characterization of material properties from spectral data
Article.Authors: Johnson A.; Fajardo C.; Sansguiri L.; Ye W.; Torrisi S.
Article.Abstract: Spectroscopy is a central pillar of materials characterization, providing useful information on properties like structure, composition, or excited state dynamics of a system. However, many spectroscopic techniques present challenges in the development of interpretable, performant, and reliable supervised learning models due to the wide range of possible nonlinear correlations that can exist between the signal and the response variable (target) of interest. Here, we present Spectra-Scope, an open-source AutoML framework for automatic characterization of material properties from spectroscopy data using interpretable machine learning (ML) models. The software is implemented in Python and a no-code web application. It comprises tools for data preprocessing, nonlinear feature extraction, machine learning model training, and feature selection. Users can easily train different types of simple, interpretable ML models on a set of feature transformations quickly and with modest computational resources. In this work, we outline the methods of Spectra-Scope and its effectiveness across diverse datasets, with applications to materials and agricultural spectroscopy data. We show that Spectra-Scope can reproduce performance of comparable models in the literature, and highlight how our emphasis on interpretability can be used to rationalize the behavior of individual models and understand the physical processes behind spectral features.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: nonlinear feature extraction; model interpretability; feature selection; automated machine learning; material characterization; materials property prediction; spectroscopy; open source software

Article.Title: Study on transport and escape characteristics of particles in a combustion-heat-driven gas flow in fracture channels
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Wang K.; Liu S.; Tang Y.; Lu F.; Liu P.
Article.Abstract: To reveal the dust generation characteristics of different-sized coal particles and the dust transport and escape behavior within fracture channels during coal combustion, the heat released at the coal fracture channel wall was incorporated into the gas-phase momentum equation via the equation of state and the continuity equation. The simultaneous solution of these governing equations produced an analytical formulation for the pressure gradient within the fracture channel under combustion-induced heating. This pressure gradient served as the driving force for gas flow, and the particle motion equations—accounting for drag, gravity, pressure-gradient forces, and thermophoresis—were solved using the discrete phase model (DPM) to simulate the transport and escape behavior of particles across different size ranges. Experimentally, coal particles of four distinct sizes (2 cm, 1 cm, 0.5 cm, and 0.1 cm) were combusted, and the dispersity of the resulting dust was quantified using a dust dispersity analyzer. The findings indicate that the ability of particles to escape is inversely proportional to the square of their size, with smaller particles preferentially escaping alongside the gas flow, while larger particles exhibit reduced escape propensity. Dust generated from coal particles of all sizes predominantly consists of fine particles; notably, larger coal particles yield a finer dust generation spectrum, whereas smaller coal particles produce a coarser yet more uniform distribution. The observed skewness of the measured spectra toward finer particles supports the preferential transport of fine particles, resulting in an escaping dust population that is further enriched in fine particles relative to the initial generation spectrum. These results offer a foundational framework for assessing dust exposure and informing dust suppression strategies in combustion settings involving coal particles of diverse sizes.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: particle escape; particle size effects; thermophoresis; coal combustion; pressure gradient; dust formation

Article.Title: Exploratory analysis of human serum albumin Cys34 redox profiles in paired serum samples collected before and after diagnostic CT examination
Article.Authors: Yamaguchi M.; Tatara Y.; Sato Y.; Tsujiguchi T.; Naraoka M.; Ito K.; Hanada H.; Kashiwakura I.
Article.Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) involves exposure to ionizing radiation, but limited information is available on changes in circulating redox-related molecules following diagnostic CT examinations. Human serum albumin (HSA) contains a reactive free thiol at cysteine 34 (Cys34), which undergoes various redox modifications and may serve as a potential indicator of systemic redox status. This exploratory study investigated HSA-Cys34 redox profiles in paired serum samples collected before and after clinically indicated CT examinations in 21 emergency patients. Eight Cys34 redox forms were analyzed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with their signals expressed as normalized peak areas. The cumulative effective dose from CT examinations performed between the paired blood collections ranged from 8.8 to 48.1 mSv. After correcting for multiple comparisons, the relative MS signals assigned to Cys34-sulfenic acid and Cys34-S-nitrosylation were significantly higher in post-CT samples, whereas the other Cys34 forms showed no significant differences. Post-CT signals for reduced Cys34, cysteinylated Cys34, and their signal ratio showed significant correlations with cumulative effective dose. However, these dose associations did not remain significant after adjustment for baseline measurements and multiple comparisons. These findings demonstrate measurable differences in HSA-Cys34-related MS signals between paired serum samples collected before and after CT examinations, providing new insights into serum albumin redox profiles in the clinical setting and a basis for further investigating the potential relevance of HSA-Cys34 profiling to low-dose radiation exposure assessment.

Article.Title: Physics-informed offline reinforcement learning reduces worst-case fuel risk in maritime routing
Article.Authors: Bora A.; Chalfant J.; Chryssostomidis C.
Article.Abstract: International shipping produces approximately 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet voyage routing remains dominated by heuristic methods that adapt poorly to varying ocean conditions. Here we present Pier (Physics-Informed, Energy-efficient, Risk-aware routing), an offline reinforcement learning framework that learns fuel-efficient, safety-aware routing policies from physics-calibrated environments grounded in historical vessel-tracking and ocean-reanalysis data, requiring no online simulator. Validated on one full year (2023) of Automatic Identification System data across seven Gulf of Mexico routes, Pier reduces mean fuel consumption and, more strongly, its variance and worst-case tail. Across five routes, mean per-voyage CO 2 is 10.2% lower than great-circle routing (bootstrap 95% CI [2.9%, 16.7%]; Monte Carlo [9.3%, 11.0%]). Per-voyage CO 2 variance is 3.7 \(\times\) lower (Levene’s test \(p = 0.0020\) ), and voyages exceeding 2 \(\times\) the median CO 2 fall from 3.0% to 0.3% (2 of 577), with the worst single voyage reduced by 65%. Pier is forecast-independent: in an exploratory experiment, classical path optimization’s wave protection degrades as forecast noise grows ( \(\sim\) 2.2 \(\times\) at \(\sigma = 0.25\) ), while Pier maintains constant performance from local observations alone. Pier demonstrates that physics-informed offline reinforcement learning enables stable, risk-aware decision-making in safety-critical transportation domains where online simulation is unavailable.

Article.Title: Synergistic protective effects of minoxidil and black soybean extract via modulation of androgen receptor and β-catenin signaling in human hair follicle dermal papilla cells
Article.Authors: Kim M.; Hong S.; Hwang I.; Lee J.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is a prevalent hair loss disorder driven by dihydrotestosterone (DHT)-induced dysfunction of human hair follicle dermal papilla cells (HFDPCs). Although minoxidil (MNX) is a first-line therapy, its long-term or high-dose use is limited by reduced efficacy and adverse effects. Black soybean extract (BSE) contains bioactive compounds with potential hair-protective activity. This study investigated the synergistic cytoprotective effects of MNX–BSE against DHT-induced HFDPC dysfunction and explored underlying mechanisms. Synergism was assessed using combination index and isobologram analyses to determine an optimal ratio. A 5:5 MNX–BSE combination showed strong synergistic cytoprotection (CI < 1), reducing oxidative stress markers and restoring antioxidant enzyme activity. It activated Akt/ERK/GSK-3β signaling, enhanced β-catenin nuclear fluorescence intensity, increased growth factor expression, and suppressed androgen receptor activation and inflammatory cytokine production. These findings suggest MNX–BSE may offer an improved therapeutic strategy for AGA.

Article.Title: Eye gaze direction influences the perceived believability of dynamic facial expressions in computer-generated characters
Article.Authors: Haile J.; Dawel A.; Palermo R.; Linden B.; Sutherland C.; Krumhuber E.; Bell J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Eye gaze is a central feature of human communication, yet it is often overlooked in research on facial expressions, especially when dynamic stimuli are used. This omission limits our understanding of how expressions are interpreted in real-time interactions and how to design believable computer-generated (CG) characters. Critically, gaze direction may shape the believability of an expression, as reflecting genuine emotion. Across two studies (Study 1 N = 131, Study 2 N = 63), we systematically tested the effect of eye gaze direction on the perceived believability and intensity of CG facial expressions. In line with predictions, happy expressions were most believable with direct gaze and sad expressions with downcast gaze. Gaze-related changes in the perceived believability of dynamic expressions were not explained by changes in perceived expression intensity. Study 2 directly compared dynamic and static expressions across gaze direction, replicating the effect of gaze on expression believability in both levels of stimulus dynamism, with no mediating effect of intensity in either. These findings emphasise the importance of eye gaze in communicating believable emotion in dynamic interactions and provide guidance for designing CG interfaces that can interact more effectively with humans.

Article.Title: Wettability-tailored recycled pet nanofibrous membranes for efficient oil/water emulsion separation
Article.Authors: Esmaeili S.; Moslehi M.; Movahedi B.
Article.Abstract: In this study, recycled polyethylene terephthalate was electrospun into nanofibrous membranes and surface-modified to develop super-hydrophilic and super-hydrophobic membranes for oil/water emulsion separation. To this end, two chemical modification strategies were employed: a sol–gel method based on tetraethyl orthosilicate to impart super-hydrophilicity, and they used of methyltrichlorosilane to induce super-hydrophobicity. FTIR and EDS analyses provided complementary evidence of silicon- and oxygen-containing species associated with the modified membrane surfaces. FESEM analysis revealed distinct surface morphologies after modification, including silica-associated surface structures in the super-hydrophilic membrane and hierarchical roughness in the super-hydrophobic membrane. Contact angle measurements showed that the pristine PET nanofibers were relatively hydrophobic, with a water contact angle of about 87° ± 1.12; after surface modification, the super-hydrophilic membrane showed a near-zero contact angle, while the super-hydrophobic membrane reached approximately 162° ± 2.8. Additionally, the team measured the underwater oil contact angle for the super-hydrophilic membrane at approximately 165–167°± 3.3, demonstrating its strong oil repellency in aqueous environments. Filtration tests showed that the super-hydrophilic membrane exhibited higher water flux, consistent with its enhanced surface hydrophilicity, whereas the superhydrophobic membrane showed lower water permeability. Mechanical tests further revealed that surface modification improved tensile strength; notably, the super-hydrophobic membrane exhibited a higher Young’s modulus due to the formation of stiffer surface layers. Ultimately, this study demonstrated that targeted surface modification of recycled PET nanofibers can significantly enhance wettability properties, filtration performance, and water/oil separation efficiency, leading to high-value recycled membranes suitable for environmental and industrial applications. Moreover, Both the super-hydrophilic and super-hydrophobic membranes achieved an oil/water separation efficiency of approximately 97 ± 2.4%.

Article.Title: WDQAR: a weighted double Q-learning based adaptive routing protocol for flying ad hoc networks
Article.Authors: Ni Q.; Bai Y.; Yu D.; Zhang Q.; Meng F.
Article.Abstract: Reliable routing in flying ad hoc networks (FANETs) faces challenges such as frequent topology changes and unstable links, which are caused by the rapid mobility of UAVs. Existing Q-learning-based protocols still suffer from biased Q-value estimation, slow convergence, and high control overhead. This paper proposes WDQAR, an adaptive routing protocol based on weighted double Q-learning. WDQAR consists of two stages: neighbor discovery and routing. In the neighbor discovery phase, each UAV dynamically adjusts the HELLO message broadcast interval based on link duration and speed, promptly perceiving topology changes and reducing control overhead. In the routing phase, WDQAR applies a sector-based candidate neighbor filtering mechanism to narrow down the next-hop candidate set, thereby accelerating the selection of the optimal path. The reward function comprehensively considers residual communication energy, link duration, geographical progress, and valid neighbor ratio. Then, a weighted double Q-learning framework is adopted during Q-value update to mitigate the estimation bias of Q-learning towards future values, thereby enhancing the stability of routing strategies. In addition, the protocol adopts two optimization methods, namely Q-value initialization and adaptive learning parameters, to accelerate the learning process. Simulation results based on NS-3 demonstrate that WDQAR outperforms the comparative protocols in terms of packet delivery rate, end-to-end delay, energy consumption, and routing overhead.

Article.Title: Synthesis and characterization of copper-containing polyoxovanadate immobilized on layered double hydroxide nanocatalyst for efficient CuAAC and A3 coupling reactions
Article.Authors: Fakhri P.; Amini M.; Ahadi A.; Hosseinifard M.
Article.Abstract: In this study, a novel heterogeneous nanocatalyst, denoted as POV-Cu@LDH, was successfully synthesized via a co-precipitation method, in which a copper-containing polyoxovanadate (POV-Cu) species was immobilized within the layered double hydroxide (LDH) framework. The structural, morphological, and compositional features of the synthesized nanocatalyst were comprehensively characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), elemental mapping, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The characterization results confirmed the successful formation of the hybrid POV-Cu@LDH structure and the uniform distribution of the active polyoxovanadate species throughout the LDH matrix. The catalytic activity of the prepared nanocatalyst was investigated in two important multicomponent transformations, namely the azide–alkyne cycloaddition click reaction and the A 3 coupling reaction. In the click reaction, the POV-Cu@LDH nanocatalyst efficiently promoted the synthesis of 1,2,3-triazole derivatives under mild and environmentally friendly conditions, affording the desired products in good to excellent yields ranging from 58% to 97%. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable performance in the A 3 coupling reaction of aldehydes, amines, and terminal alkynes, providing the corresponding propargylamines in yields of 54–99% under optimized reaction conditions in acetonitrile. A notable advantage of the POV-Cu@LDH nanocatalyst is its heterogeneous nature, which allows easy separation and recovery from the reaction medium. Recycling studies demonstrated that the catalyst maintained high activity during the initial runs, followed by a gradual decrease in subsequent cycles, primarily due to structural changes in the layered support and active site loss. Reusability studies demonstrated that the catalyst could be readily recovered and reused for multiple consecutive cycles with sustainable performance, while post-reaction XRD and FT-IR analyses confirmed the remarkable retention of its structural integrity. Overall, the combination of high catalytic efficiency, broad substrate compatibility, operational simplicity, and recyclability highlights the potential of POV-Cu@LDH as an effective catalyst for sustainable and green organic transformations.

Article.Title: Discrepancies between airborne BTEX exposure, clinical outcomes, and risk perception in informal waste management setting, Indonesia
Article.Authors: Rahman I.; Rahardyan B.; Oginawati K.; Santoso M.; Ramadhani A.; Purnama D.; Aurelia C.; Yudhiantara M.; Mulyana N.; Fahimah N.; Amin M.
Article.Abstract: Open dumpsites are persistent sources of airborne pollutants. However, BTEX exposure, clinical outcomes, and perceived health risks remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated discrepancies between airborne BTEX exposure, objective health indicators, and risk perception in an informal waste management setting. Ambient BTEX concentrations were quantified from 56 air samples collected across multiple landfill zones, while health outcomes were evaluated through clinical examinations and spirometry. Risk perception and self-reported symptoms were assessed using structured questionnaires administered to landfill workers, scavengers, and nearby residents (n=150). Benzene was the predominant compound, with the highest concentrations observed in active dumping areas (70.09 ± 22.29 µg m −3 ), influenced by local meteorological conditions. Landfill workers reported a higher prevalence of respiratory (76.7%) and neurological symptoms (83.3%). Although no acute clinical abnormalities were detected, spirometry indicated mild to moderately severe impairment in lung function, with no significant differences between exposure groups ( p > 0.05). Lung function impairment was significantly associated with body mass index and household ventilation. Risk perception varied across groups, with scavengers exhibiting the highest BTEX exposure (30.71 ± 24.62 µg m −3 ), but lower perceived environmental and health risks than nearby residents, indicating a marked exposure–perception discrepancy ( p < 0.05). These findings provide a comprehensive understanding of how environmental exposure, clinical outcomes, and risk perception interact, reinforcing the importance of integrated environmental health management and risk communication strategies in informal waste management settings.

Article.Title: A critical analysis of semantic attribute leakage in compositional text-to-image generation
Article.Authors: Kakde Y.; Dash S.; Das R.
Article.Abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models suffer from a persistent and under-examined failure: semantic attribute leakage , wherein a visual attribute specified for one object—color, texture, or shape—erroneously manifests on a co-occurring object in the generated image. Distinct from catastrophic neglect and attribute swapping, leakage is a directional, cross-object contamination arising from three independent sources: entangled CLIP token representations, spatially unbound cross-attention maps, and training-data priors learned during pretraining. Despite its prevalence, leakage has never been subjected to a dedicated critical analysis as a standalone phenomenon with its own taxonomy, mechanistic framework, and benchmark critique. We address this gap by introducing a three-axis taxonomy (source, attribute type, severity) that unifies the fragmented terminology across the literature. We critically analyse the mechanistic roots of leakage, evaluate existing mitigation methods against the taxonomy, and assess whether current benchmarks actually isolate leakage from compositional failure broadly. Our analysis reveals that reported performance on texture and shape binding consistently lags color across every method with published scores on all three, that attention-manipulation methods offer limited gains at disproportionate cost, and that the transition to Diffusion Transformer architectures has shifted but not resolved leakage’s structural origin.
Article.Topic: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

Article.Title: Experimental investigation and multi-criteria assessment of drilling in SiO₂-reinforced AZ91 magnesium composite under bio-based and cryogenic cooling conditions
Article.Authors: Moinuddin S.; Ponnarengan H.; Kamaraj L.; Kannan S.; Nagallapati V.; Khan M.; Niaz A.; Hodhod M.
Article.Abstract: Magnesium (Mg) alloys are attractive for biodegradable and lightweight applications, yet drilling-induced surface integrity remains sensitive to machining and cooling conditions. This study investigates the drilling behaviour of a 6 wt% silica (SiO₂) – reinforced AZ91 Mg composite fabricated by ultrasonic-assisted casting. Thirty distinct drilling conditions were evaluated using a structured mixed-level matrix by varying cutting speed (30–110 m/min), feed rate (0.05–0.15 mm/rev), tool type, and cooling/lubrication environment comprising vegetable oil, coconut oil, and liquid nitrogen (LN₂). Thrust force (F z ), torque (M z ), and surface roughness (R a ) were measured and ranked using MEREC–DNMA and LOPCOW–EDAS multi-criteria decision frameworks. Across the investigated matrix, higher cutting speed and feed rate were generally associated with increased F z , M z , and R a ; these trends are interpreted at the level of the complete drilling condition because the design does not independently separate coolant, tool, and interaction effects. Run 1 (30 m/min, 0.05 mm/rev, vegetable oil, HSS) was the best-ranked investigated condition, with F z = 118 N, M z = 0.23 N·m, and R a = 0.13 μm. Targeted macroscopic and SEM-EDS examination of retained Run 1 burr material revealed segmented and serrated morphology, lamellar shear ridges, plastic-flow bands, microcracks, and localized matrix tearing. The analyzed region was Mg-dominant and did not establish SiO₂ particle pull-out. The ranking identifies the best compromise within the tested domain, not a global process optimum. Vegetable and coconut oils remain candidate bio-based lubricants within the investigated domain; superiority over conventional mineral oil cannot be inferred without matched reference experiments.

Article.Title: Metadata relationship mining and intelligent bloodline tracing system empowered by graph neural networks
Article.Authors: Xu J.; Gao X.; Lv L.; Lv F.
Article.Abstract: Metadata serves a vital function in assuring data transparency, traceability, and accountability throughout digital ecosystems. With the ever-growing amount of data and metadata produced, intelligent systems are increasingly demanded to mine the subtle latent relations of metadata entities and accurately trace lineage over time. Existing rule-based solutions and early graph- based models ignore the temporal semantic, heterogeneity, and hierarchical structure inherent to metadata environments. Recent advances in GNNs have been promising, but current implementations face difficulties incorporating heterogeneous or temporal data. In this research an innovative intelligent system, Temporal-Heterogeneous Hierarchical Graph Neural Network for Metadata Mining and Bloodline Tracing (TH-HGNN-MMBT) that analyse temporal, heterogeneous, hierarchical metadata data to achieve lineage traceability and discover relationships of metadata have been proposed. This model builds a hierarchical graph in which every entity such as dataset, file, user, step in metadata environment is taken as node, and their dependences such as ownership, latency, association is represented as time-aware heterogenous edges. The proposed TH-HGNN-MMBT model achieves a 12.8% gain in temporal consistency and a 7.5% gain in bloodline completeness filtering, processes metadata 34.2% faster, and has 6.8% better scaling for large-scale lineage analysis. The architecture enables discovering hidden relationships, inferring missing links, and rebuilding heterogenous metadata bloodline between layers of abstraction.

Article.Title: Marine-derived Planococcus citreus as a source of bioactive metabolites acting as dual-action agents against biofilms and quorum sensing
Article.Authors: Bukhari S.; Shah L.; Nazir N.; Abbasi S.; Khalil S.; Faheem M.; Alshehri F.; Shami A.; Tombozara N.; Sajjad W.
Article.Abstract: Marine sponges host diverse symbiotic bacteria that produce bioactive secondary metabolites with potential therapeutic applications. The rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens and biofilm associated infections needs new antimicrobial and antibiofilm agents. This study explores the culture-dependent diversity of bacteria associated with the marine sponge Callyspongia fibrosa from the coastal region of Karachi, Pakistan, and evaluates their antimicrobial, antibiofilm and anti-quorum sensing (anti-QS) activities to prioritize isolates with dual functionality. Sponge-associated bacteria were isolated by culture-based methods and characterized by colony morphology and 16 S rRNA gene sequencing. Anti-QS activity was assessed using reporter strain ( Chromobacterium violaceum CV026) and validated by high-performance liquid chromatography with N-Butanoyl-L-homoserine Lactones (C4-HSL). LC-MS analysis suggested the presence of diketopiperazine (DKP)-like compounds in methanol-soluble fraction. In silico analyses were performed to investigate bioactive metabolites and their interactions with quorum-sensing (QS) regulators. Isolates belong to Bacilli and Gammaproteobacteria. The methanol-soluble fraction of Planococcus citreus demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (MIC 32 µg/mL; MBC 128 µg/mL) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , (MIC 64 µg/mL; MBC 256 µg/mL). Biofilm inhibition and eradication reached 70% and 58% respectively ( p = 0.003 and p = 0.0001). QS inhibition was confirmed by a 35 mm inhibition zone and HPLC verified signal reduction in peak intensity (95%). LasR and AgrC were selected as the master QS regulators controlling virulence and biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa and MRSA, respectively. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations predicted stable interactions with these targets. Sponge associated bacteria from C. fibrosa produce metabolites with antimicrobial, antibiofilm and ​QS inhibitory properties, indicating potential for developing alternative therapeutics against MDR pathogens.

Article.Title: Vision-driven retrieval-augmented decision support for plant disease diagnosis using EfficientNetV2 and large language models
Article.Authors: Kaya F.; Aslan S.; Tümen V.; Akın E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate and timely plant disease diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production and precision farming. However, most existing agricultural decision support systems treat visual disease diagnosis and agronomic recommendation generation as separate processes, either providing image classification results alone or generating recommendations with large language models that are not grounded in domain-specific knowledge. To address this limitation, this study introduces EffiToRag, an end-to-end decision support framework that integrates an EfficientNetV2-based visual diagnosis module with a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. Rather than relying solely on free-text queries for disease-level retrieval, the proposed approach uses the disease class predicted by EfficientNetV2 as the primary key for retrieving the corresponding record from a structured agronomic knowledge base constructed from peer-reviewed scientific publications and official phytopathological guidelines. The visual diagnosis module was trained using Progressive Training and Class-Aware Tiered Augmentation (CATA) to account for differences in class representation. On a held-out test set comprising 11,621 images across 60 plant health classes, EfficientNetV2-M achieved 99.13% accuracy and a Macro F1 score of 0.9889, with an inference time of 4.39 ms per image on the evaluated GPU. For 500 user queries, the system selected query-relevant knowledge fields with a precision of 0.972 and a recall of 0.985. The factual-consistency assessment combined GPT-4-based evaluation and manual expert review of a random sample of 100 diagnostic reports and yielded a mean factual-consistency score of 0.99. The experts also assigned these reports a mean applicability score of 4.85/5.0. These findings show that visual disease classification, structured agronomic knowledge retrieval, and LLM-based recommendation generation can be integrated within a single decision support pipeline for precision agriculture.

Article.Title: Taxon-specific ontogenetic trajectories of brain endocast shape in birds
Article.Authors: Ohnishi Y.; Izawa E.; Shiomi K.; Sano M.; Koyama S.; Yoda K.; Kawabe S.
Article.Abstract: Ontogenetic changes in avian brain shape have been intensively studied in precocial birds, with three-dimensional analyses revealing global changes in brain morphology. However, it remains unclear whether altricial species also show the same pattern. In this study, we investigate three-dimensional ontogenetic changes in brain shape using geometric morphometrics in a precocial species, Gallus gallus , and in three non-precocial taxa, including a Procellariiform seabird and passerines. Our results show that size-associated changes in brain endocast shape differ among the sampled taxa, with distinct patterns of landmark displacement in the chicken, shearwater, sparrow, and crows. Ontogenetic brain shape change in chicken is consistent with previous studies. However, the most conspicuous taxon-specific differences involved the anterior olfactory-bulb landmark in the shearwater and telencephalic landmarks in passerines. These taxon-specific trajectories may reflect a combination of developmental mode, phylogenetic history, and ecological or functional specialization, which cannot be disentangled with the present sampling design. These findings also provide a developmental framework for paleoneurological studies, highlighting the importance of considering developmental mode, phylogenetic history, and ecological or functional specialization when interpreting fossil brain endocasts.
