Article.Title: A hybrid visual state-space model with progressive depth modulation for single image dehazing
Article.Authors: Xie Z.; Zhao H.
Article.Abstract: Single image dehazing at high resolution must propagate scene-wide haze statistics efficiently while exploiting depth-related geometry without destabilizing training. Convolutional networks restore local detail but lack large-scale consistency, Transformer-style global modeling is computationally expensive, and geometry-aware methods can degrade when unreliable depth is injected too aggressively. We propose SSMDehazeNet, a hybrid visual state-space model with progressive depth modulation. A state-space branch propagates global haze statistics with linear complexity while a parallel local branch reconstructs structure at full resolution; the two are coupled inside a Parallel Hybrid State-Space Module so that both paths remain available at the same feature layer. Geometry is introduced progressively: a zero-initialized Spatial Depth Modulator gives it negligible influence early in training and lets its contribution be learned from data, and the depth-consistency objective is modulated by the current reconstruction residual. On the RESIDE SOTS benchmark, SSMDehazeNet achieves 42.48 dB/0.9968 (indoor) and 36.18 dB/0.9931 (outdoor) with favorable no-reference quality, and at $$512 \times 512$$ resolution it runs in 80.62 ms on an RTX 4090, substantially faster than heavy Transformer-based dehazing. Zero-shot evaluation on O-HAZE and NH-HAZE, a branch-level analysis, and a controlled geometry-corruption study further characterize its generalization and its reliance on the learned geometry cue.

Article.Title: A structural and energetic model of phosphatidylserine recognition by the scavenger receptor CD36 from docking, dynamics and conservation analysis
Article.Authors: Mukala P.; Menon R.; Mohan G.; Balakrishnan K.
Article.Abstract: Phosphatidylserine (PS) is an anionic glycerophospholipid that, when externalised to the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane, functions as an “eat-me” signal recognised by structurally diverse receptors that drive efferocytosis and immune homeostasis. Although the class B scavenger receptor CD36 is an established mediator of PS-dependent phagocytosis, the atomic basis by which it reads out the PS molecule has remained undefined. Here we combine comparative molecular docking, focused re-docking, a 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, end-state binding free-energy analysis and cross-species conservation analysis to build a structural and energetic model of CD36–PS recognition. A panel of eight PS-associated proteins (CD36, ABCA1, Annexin V, Synaptotagmin I, TIM-4, SR-B1, protein kinase C and the dopamine D2 receptor) was first screened by docking with 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-L-serine (POPS); among the cofactor-independent targets, CD36 presented the most complete recognition interface. CD36 was re-docked into its crystallographic fatty-acid pocket, and the top pose (− 7.8 kcal/mol) was advanced to MD using the AMBER99SB-ILDN and GAFF2 force fields. The ectodomain remained structurally invariant across the trajectory (Cα RMSD 1.30 ± 0.14 Å; radius of gyration 22.78 ± 0.09 Å), while POPS was continuously retained through extensive van der Waals burial of its acyl chains (mean 6,704 contacts within 6 Å) and a dynamic head-group hydrogen-bond network (mean 3.0 simultaneous bonds). Per-residue energy decomposition, computed independently on both trajectories, identified Asp270, Tyr212 and Ser268 as the principal head-group anchors. Phe383, Phe201, Phe266, Ile271, Leu295, Val339, Leu371 and Leu387 as the dominant hydrophobic contributors, the interaction being energetically dominated by van der Waals rather than electrostatic terms. A further, independent 500 ns simulation retained POPS bound to CD36 throughout and left the ectodomain backbone stable (backbone RMSD approximately 0.15–0.17 nm). Its MM/PBSA binding energy was − 78.92 ± 4.03 kcal/mol (entropy not included), dominated by van der Waals interactions (ΔE vdW = − 107.67 ± 0.38 kcal/mol), whereas the net electrostatic contribution, after polar desolvation, opposed binding (+ 39.08 kcal/mol). The ligand RMSD, the number of protein–POPS hydrogen bonds and the binding energy each changed once, at about 240 ns (ΔG bind −67.9 kcal/mol before and − 89.1 kcal/mol after). All ten pocket-lining residues were completely conserved across six mammalian orthologues. These convergent analyses define an amphipathic, cofactor-free recognition mode — polar anchoring of the head group, which fixes its orientation without contributing net favourable electrostatic free energy once desolvation is accounted for, coupled to hydrophobic tail sequestration within a geometrically permissive, evolutionarily constrained tunnel — and yield specific, experimentally testable hypotheses for mutagenesis and biophysical validation.

Article.Title: A hierarchical resilient tri-level energy management for islanded multi-energy system with risk-aware learning-in-the-loop RL algorithm
Article.Authors: Tan W.; Liao H.; Alwan A.; Seyyedi A.
Article.Abstract: Coordinated energy management is crucial for the effective operation of integrated multi-energy systems (IMESs), which integrate water, heat, and electricity networks. The primary objectives of this coordination include reducing operational costs, minimizing hazards, and ensuring a reliable supply of energy. Traditional methodologies tend to address these objectives within a singular optimization framework, which often constrains their capacity to accommodate the distinct operational requirements associated with economic scheduling, vulnerability assessment, and service restoration. This study investigates the potential for enhancing system performance by dispersing these objectives into three interconnected decision-making tiers and coordinating their outputs throughout the operational phase. At the highest level, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is utilized to facilitate operational decisions that improve energy supply and service restoration during disruptions. The intermediate level employs a sensitivity-based risk assessment to pinpoint vulnerable system components and evaluate their effects on operational performance. At the foundational level, resources pertaining to power, heat, water, storage, and energy conversion are scheduled through Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), which integrates resilience and risk outcomes as operational constraints and decision-making priorities. Furthermore, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent manages real-time operations by coordinating the outputs from these three levels, dynamically adjusting operational choices based on prevailing system conditions. This hierarchical flow of information enables resilience requirements and vulnerability assessments to inform economic scheduling without conflating all objectives into a single optimization problem. Simulations conducted on an IMES reveal that the proposed framework enhances energy supply during disruptions by 35.14% and reduces daily operating costs by 13.79% when compared to traditional benchmark approaches. These findings suggest that the proposed structure improves supply continuity and economic efficiency while effectively addressing operational vulnerabilities and network limitations.

Article.Title: Prediction-sealed risk routing limits negative transfer in cross-workflow translation of two-dimensional material properties
Article.Authors: Talaat A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Computational databases can assign different electronic properties to equivalent two-dimensional materials because their density-functional workflows differ. These inconsistencies can change screening decisions and can make flexible cross-database corrections fail after transfer. We present FidelitySwitch-2D, a prediction-sealed framework that combines structure matching, material-group-disjoint development, candidate-specific risk estimation, adaptive routing and group-level conformal triage. Development used 4,540 directed pairs from 1,056 material groups across C2DB, JARVIS-DFT and 2DMatPedia. In sealed external audits, the nonlinear Residual Bridge transferred negatively; on 490 independent MC2D groups, the frozen switch reduced Residual Bridge error by 0.0557 eV. In a target-sealed hybrid-perovskite audit, RiskArgminRouter achieved the lowest observed band-gap and conduction-band-minimum errors and consistently enriched low-error subsets across band gap, CBM and VBM. These results support FidelitySwitch-2D as an auditable reliability layer for workflow-dependent materials labels, while broader validation across properties, routes and experimental cohorts remains necessary.

Article.Title: Folate-functionalized chitosan nanocarriers of an iron nitrosyl nitric oxide donor for dual antileukemic and antibacterial activity in acute myeloid leukemia cells
Article.Authors: Dowidar D.; Elshami F.; Elmehasseb I.; Shaban S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treatment is frequently complicated by severe bacterial infections resulting from chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, creating a need for therapeutic platforms that address both leukemic progression and infection-related complications. In this study, folate-functionalized chitosan nanocarriers loaded with an iron nitrosyl nitric oxide donor, FA-CS@FeNOTSP, were developed as a dual-action platform for antileukemic and antibacterial evaluation. The nanocarriers were obtained by carbodiimide-mediated folate conjugation followed by FeNOTSP encapsulation and characterized by FT-IR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, zeta-potential analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and dynamic light scattering. FA-CS@FeNOTSP exhibited high encapsulation efficiency (approximately 85–92%), SEM-derived particle dimensions of approximately 210 nm, hydrodynamic diameters of approximately 250–327 nm in aqueous suspension, and a marked surface-charge shift consistent with folate functionalization. The formulation showed pH/GSH-responsive release, with limited FeNOTSP liberation under physiological conditions (approximately 20% at pH 7.4 after 24 h) and enhanced release under acidic, reductive conditions (approximately 40% at pH 4.5 with 10 mM GSH). DNA-binding and stopped-flow studies indicated moderate ctDNA interaction (K b = 4.31 × 10 4 M − 1 ) through a reversible two-step mechanism involving rapid electrostatic association followed by slower structural binding. FA-CS@FeNOTSP displayed low hemolytic activity (< 1%), reduced cytotoxicity toward WI38 fibroblasts (IC 50 =162.07 ± 1.89 µg mL − 1 ), retained activity against Kasumi-1 AML cells (IC 50 = 84.99 ± 1.11 µg mL − 1 ), and exerted broad-spectrum antibacterial effects (21–32 mm inhibition zones, comparable to gentamicin). Pre-exposure of Kasumi-1 cells to excess free folic acid increased the IC 50 of FA-CS@FeNOTSP by 35.4%, providing preliminary functional support for the contribution of folate-sensitive cellular interactions to the in-vitro response. Collectively, these findings support FA-CS@FeNOTSP as an in-vitro proof-of-concept multifunctional platform with responsive release, antileukemic activity, and antibacterial effects.

Article.Title: Learning a density-guided adaptive spiking network for remote sensing image dehazing
Article.Authors: Wu B.; Luo Y.; Hu R.; Lei S.
Article.Abstract: Remote sensing images are often degraded by atmospheric haze, resulting in reduced visibility and structural information loss. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) have shown potential for efficient image restoration, existing approaches have not explicitly incorporated spatial haze density into neuronal dynamics, limiting their adaptability to non-uniform haze degradation. In this paper, we propose DASNet, a Density-Guided Adaptive Spiking Network for remote sensing image dehazing. Different from existing SNN-based restoration approaches, DASNet introduces haze degradation awareness into neuronal dynamics through a lightweight Haze Density Estimation (HDE) branch, which predicts spatial haze density distributions from hazy observations. Based on the estimated density map, we design an Adaptive Haze-aware Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (AH-LIF) neuron that dynamically adjusts membrane potential evolution according to different haze levels, enabling region-specific temporal information aggregation. Specifically, heavily degraded regions can preserve more historical information through enhanced membrane integration, while lightly degraded regions maintain rapid responses for detail preservation. Furthermore, a pseudo haze density supervision strategy is introduced using paired hazy and clear remote sensing images to improve density estimation accuracy. Extensive experiments on public remote sensing image dehazing benchmarks demonstrate that DASNet achieves competitive restoration performance while preserving the efficiency advantages of spiking neural networks.

Article.Title: Coupled carrier transport and fractional-order thermoelastic dynamics in porous semiconductors with spatial–temporal nonlocality
Article.Authors: M. K V.; Dutta R.; Das S.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a unified analytical framework to investigate the coupled thermoelastic response of porous semiconductor material under the fractional-order Lord–Shulman thermoelastic model. A spatiotemporal nonlocal elasticity theory, introduced and systematically developed by Lazar and Agiasofitou 59 by taking into account one dynamical scalar nonlocal kernel, is employed. In line with this theory, the isotropic nonlocal elasticity model of Klein–Gordon type, incorporating both a characteristic internal length scale and an essential internal time scale parameter, is adopted 59 , 60 . The primary objective is to examine how nonlocal interactions, thermal memory, carrier transport, and porosity collectively influence the thermo-mechanical behavior of semiconductor media under thermal loading. A two-dimensional semi-infinite porous semiconductor subjected to mechanical loading and thermal shock is formulated. The governing equations describing displacement, temperature, carrier density, void volume fraction, equilibrated stresses, and mechanical stresses are derived using the Klein–Gordon nonlocal framework and the fractional-order Lord–Shulman heat conduction model. The resulting system is solved analytically using the normal mode technique, while numerical simulations for silicon are performed to investigate the effects of spatial and temporal nonlocality. Heat-map visualizations are also employed to illustrate the spatial evolution of the physical fields. The numerical results reveal that spatial nonlocality redistributes stresses, modifies displacement fields, enhances carrier diffusion, and attenuates thermal responses through long-range interactions, whereas temporal nonlocality governs memory-dependent thermal relaxation, delayed energy transport, and wave propagation characteristics. Heat-map visualizations effectively identify regions of maximum thermo-mechanical concentration and demonstrate the coupled influence of nonlocality and fractional-order effects on the semiconductor response. The proposed model successfully unifies nonlocal elasticity, fractional thermoelasticity, porosity, and carrier transport within a single analytical framework while recovering several established thermoelastic theories as limiting cases. The formulation provides a robust theoretical basis for the analysis and design of advanced porous semiconductors, nanoelectronic devices, MEMS/NEMS, thermal sensors, and other microscale engineering systems operating under coupled thermo-mechanical environments.

Article.Title: Biosynthesis and characterization of exopolysaccharide from Lactiplantibacillus plantarum RSM51 with antioxidant and antidiabetic potential
Article.Authors: El Halfawy N.; Masoud A.; Abdelmonaem S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing demand for innovative biotherapeutics requires comprehensive characterization of novel probiotic strains with desirable health-promoting attributes and established safety profiles. This study provides genomic and physicochemical analyses of the exopolysaccharide (EPS) producing strain Lactiplantibacillus plantarum RSM51, evaluating its probiotic potential and biopolymer characteristics. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of isolate Lb. plantarum RSM51 was performed, and the assembled genome comprises 3.37 Mbp with a GC content of 44.35%. To investigate the genetic basis of EPS production, the genome was systematically screened for gene clusters associated with EPS biosynthesis. The in silico analysis predicted a complement of genes encoding glycosyltransferases, polymerization enzymes, and transport machinery potentially involved in heteropolysaccharide assembly and export. Furthermore, the crude EPS yield of Lb. plantarum RSM51 was approximately 410 mg/L. Physicochemical characterization of the crude biopolymer, designated EPS-RSM51, by Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicated a polysaccharide structure. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of the EPS exhibited an irregular, porous, and amorphous morphology. Elemental analysis via Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy showed the polymer was primarily composed of carbon and oxygen, with minor amounts of nitrogen and phosphorus. Moreover, crude EPS-RSM51 exhibited moderate antioxidant activity, with an IC 50 of 5.84 mg/mL in the DPPH assay, 1.70 mg/mL in the FRAP assay, and 3.64 mg/mL in the NO assay. Additionally, crude EPS-RSM51 revealed potent inhibition of α-amylase (IC 50 = 3.28 mg/mL) and α-glucosidase (IC 50 = 3.12 mg/mL). Therefore, this study provides insight into the predicted EPS biosynthetic capacity and the experimentally determined physicochemical properties of EPS-RSM51, thereby supporting the evidence-based integration of crude EPS-RSM51 into functional food and nutraceutical applications.

Article.Title: SWCNTs thin film transistor circuits fabricated on flexible substrates with inkjet-printed silver electrodes for photodetectors
Article.Authors: Singh S.; Ranjan P.; Sambandan S.
Article.Abstract: We demonstrate thin film transistors (TFTs) and PMOS inverter circuit using drop casted single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) as active semiconductor and spin-coated poly(4-vinylphenol) (PVP) dielectric on a flexible polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) substrate of 125-µm-thick. All the electrodes were inkjet-printed using silver ink. The fabricated TFTs exhibit a linear field-effect mobility of 2.43 cm 2 V −1 s − 1 , while the saturated-load PMOS inverter achieves a voltage gain of 1.2 at a supply voltage of -15 V. The optoelectronic characteristics of these TFTs are systematically investigated under white-light illumination by monitoring drain-current (I D ) transients at different gate voltages (V GS ). The transfer characteristics reveal a reversal in hysteresis direction between dark and illuminated conditions, indicating that photo-induced charge-carrier recombination governs the device response. Under positive gate bias, the TFTs exhibit a pronounced and fully reversible photoresponse, with the drain current recovering completely after the light is switched off. In contrast, under negative gate bias, illumination suppresses the drain current, and the stretched-exponential transient decay becomes progressively faster with increasing negative V GS , reflecting Fermi-level-dependent carrier dynamics.

Article.Title: Dual-mode Meta-MXene utilizing moiré and quasi-bic resonances for terahertz biosensing applications
Article.Authors: EL-Wasif Z.; Obayya S.; Hameed M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study introduces a dual-mode computational framework that utilizes twisted Moiré-integrated metamaterials to achieve high-precision terahertz refractive-index sensing of normal and pathological brain tissues. The Moiré Supercell Meta-MXene architecture relies on rotational spatial symmetry breaking—induced by an 11.4° interlayer rotation and a 1 μm coupling gap—as the key physical trigger driving strong dipole-BIC hybridization. This mechanism confirms the evolution of a non-radiating dark state into an accessible, highly localized quasi-Bound State in the Continuum (q-BIC), displaying a sharp reflection minimum of -40.147 dB at 9.948 THz. Concurrently, the Meta-MXene layer folding inherent to the twisted supercell creates an emergent Moiré-signature resonance at 8.524 THz—a spectral feature entirely absent in unrotated geometries. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that the primary q-BIC sensing channel achieves a peak Quality Factor (Q) of 28.62, whereas the induced Moiré mode acts as a stable reference benchmark with a peak Q of 42.66 and a baseline sensitivity of 208.6 GHz/RIU across the full refractive index span of brain tissue (1.333–1.483). For targeted pathological brain refractive-index sensing demonstration to discriminate healthy Gray Matter ( n = 1.395) from highly aggressive Malignant Glioblastoma ( n = 1.4470), the q-BIC resonance yields a localized diagnostic sensitivity of 462.4 GHz/RIU, supported by a 154.1 GHz/RIU sensitivity along the reference Moiré channel. Further, the heterostructure exhibits remarkable tolerance under realistic fabrication deviations, restricting perturbations to $$\:{\Delta\:}\text{f}=0.072\:\text{T}\text{H}\text{z}$$ and $$\:{\Delta\:}\text{Q}=5.146$$ for the Moiré mode and $$\:{\Delta\:}\text{f}=0.12\:\text{T}\text{H}\text{z}$$ and $$\:{\Delta\:}\text{Q}=\:3.09\:\:$$ for the q-BIC mode, confirming robust electromagnetic field confinement. By combining the high-gain sensitivity of the q-BIC state with the spectral resilience of the Moiré feature, this dual-mode framework overcomes single-resonance limitations, providing a label-free THz diagnostic pathway for early-stage brain pathologies.

Article.Title: Enhanced Congo Red adsorption by chitosan graft polyacrylamide hydrogel incorporating diatomite supported Fe–Ni layered double hydroxide
Article.Authors: Peighambardoust S.; Mardani M.; Akbari A.; Peighambardoust N.
Article.Abstract: This research aimed to enhance the adsorptive properties of chitosan-grafted-polyacrylamide Poly(AAM) copolymeric hydrogels through the incorporation of Fe–Ni layered double hydroxide (LDH)-loaded diatomite. The synthesized adsorbents were characterized using various analytical techniques, including BET, FTIR, XRD, SEM–EDS, and elemental mapping. The results confirmed the successful immobilization of diatomite–LDH within the hydrogel network. Furthermore, BET analysis revealed enhanced porosity of the composites after modification. The adsorption performance of the prepared adsorbents was assessed for the removal of Congo Red (CR), an anionic dye, using batch adsorption experiments. The effects of key parameters—namely temperature, contact time, adsorbent dosage, initial dye concentration, and pH—on the adsorption efficiency were systematically evaluated. The maximum experimental adsorption capacity for CR removal was found to be 9.702 mg·g⁻¹ under the following conditions: 25 °C, pH = 5, initial dye concentration of 10 mg.L⁻¹, contact time of 150 min, and adsorbent dosage of 1 g.L⁻¹. Kinetic studies indicated that the adsorption process followed the pseudo-first-order kinetic model. Isotherm analysis showed that the Langmuir model provided the best fit for CS-g-Poly(AAM) and CS-g-Poly(AAM)/Diatomite, consistent with monolayer adsorption, whereas the Freundlich model gave a slightly higher R² value (0.982) than the Langmuir model (0.971) for CS-g-Poly(AAM)/Diatomite/Ni–Fe LDH, suggesting that adsorption onto this composite may be governed by multilayer adsorption on heterogeneous surfaces. The favorable nature of CR adsorption onto all adsorbents was supported by the dimensionless separation factor (R L ) and the Freundlich n values. The mean adsorption energies obtained from the Dubinin–Radushkevich isotherm (0.418, 0.249, and 0.365 kJ.mol⁻¹) indicated that physical adsorption interactions contributed substantially to CR uptake. Thermodynamic investigations demonstrated that the adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic in nature. The influence of interfering ions revealed that the presence of Na⁺ and Ca²⁺ cations in the solution decreased the adsorption efficiency. Moreover, the synthesized adsorbents exhibited excellent reusability, maintaining their adsorption performance over six consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles.

Article.Title: Multimodal conflict-aware and generative-enhanced AI for early-stage startup risk prediction
Article.Authors: Xi J.
Article.Abstract: Early-stage startups are central to innovation-driven economies, yet their failure rates remain persistently high, with more than half of new ventures not surviving their first three to five years. Accurately assessing the risk of young ventures is challenging because relevant signals are dispersed across heterogeneous sources, including entrepreneurial narratives, early financial indicators, and founders’ positions in entrepreneurial networks. Most existing models either focus on a single modality or treat multimodal features as independent inputs, overlooking whether cross-source discrepancies contain additional information and struggling with small, imbalanced datasets. This paper proposes a conflict-aware, generative-enhanced multimodal framework for predicting startup risk within 36 months after the initial institutional evaluation. The model jointly encodes business plan and interview text, structured financial features, and founder-centric social network information via transformer, multilayer perceptron, and heterogeneous graph neural network encoders. Cross-modal contrastive learning aligns the three modalities into a shared representation space, while a modal conflict attention module computes representation-level discrepancies between textual, financial, and network signals as candidate features for further inspection. To mitigate data scarcity and class imbalance, we further introduce a conditional GAN operating in the fused latent space to generate label- and conflict-conditioned synthetic representations that expose the classifier to both typical and strategically conflictual patterns. Experiments on a real-world dataset of 4,500 early-stage startups show that the proposed framework outperforms structured, text-feature, network-feature, and multimodal baselines. Compared to the best multimodal fusion baseline, our model improves AUROC from 0.82 to 0.87 and AUPRC from 0.53 to 0.62, with consistent gains in positive-class F \(_1\) and balanced accuracy. Ablation studies confirm the incremental contributions of contrastive alignment, modal conflict attention, and generative augmentation. A held-out construct-validity analysis further shows that the learned conflict representation tracks independently derived cross-domain discrepancy measures, while its non-monotonic outcome gradient supports using it as an inspection signal rather than a stand-alone diagnostic.

Article.Title: Exposure to biological hazards and associated factors among nurses and midwives working in Bale zones public hospitals, Southeast Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Usleyman B.; Zenbaba D.; Bekele G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Occupational exposure to biological hazards is an important occupational health concern among healthcare workers, particularly nurses and midwives who frequently perform procedures involving blood, body fluids, and sharp instruments. However, evidence on the broader range of biological hazard exposures among nurses and midwives in public hospitals of Bale and East Bale Zones is limited. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the prevalence of exposure to biological hazards and associated factors among nurses and midwives working in public hospitals of Bale and East Bale Zones, Southeast Ethiopia. An institution-based cross-sectional study design was conducted involving 407 Nurses and Midwives working in public hospitals of Bale zones. Participants were selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using the Kobo Android application and analysed using SPSS statistics version 27. Binary logistic regression analysis was performed to identify variables associated with biological hazard exposure. Adjusted odds ratio (AOR) with a 95% confidence interval were used to assess associations, and statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05. Overall, 68.6% (95% CI: 63.6–73.0) of nurses and midwives reported at least one occupational exposure to a biological hazard during their professional lifetime career. Recapping needles after use (AOR = 2.08, 95% CI: 1.16–3.74), lack of training on infection prevention (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.61–4.79), working > 40 h per week (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 2.41–8.67), lack of safety guideline at working unit (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI: 1.91–7.58) and having work experience of less than five year (AOR = 2.21, 95% CI: 1.16–4.24) were significantly associated with exposure to biological hazards. The findings of this study revealed the high prevalence of exposure to biological hazards among nurses and midwives in the study area compared to previous studies conducted in the country. Therefore, providing training on infection prevention, establishing clear safety guidelines, and effectively managing working hours are crucial steps for enhancing occupational safety and improving healthcare outcomes.

Article.Title: First-in-human feasibility study of a portable low-field pulsed-gradient-free MR device in acute stroke
Article.Authors: Barker J.; Tzeng Y.; Teal P.; Thomas D.; Churilov L.; McDonald A.; Moed T.; Rivet S.; Swarup O.; Anderyas P.; Pierce S.; Stilwill F.; Mulligan L.; Obruchkov S.; Cowell K.; Romero J.; Alexandrov A.; Alexandrov A.; Goldstein J.; Zaidat O.; Liebeskind D.; Loquet G.; Parsons M.; Campbell B.; Donnan G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We conducted the first-in-human evaluation of a novel portable low-field 0.1 T pulsed-gradient-free magnetic resonance (MR) device (~ 100 kg) that acquires regional MR biomarkers for bedside stroke assessment. We aimed to evaluate its safety, tolerability and feasibility in acute stroke. This single-centre non-randomised observational cohort study prospectively recruited healthy controls and consecutive stroke patients within 72-h of hospital presentation. Participants underwent conventional 1.5–3 T MRI and two consecutive device scans (DWI, T2). The primary outcomes were feasibility with the proportion of scans where an interpretable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was obtained, safety, and tolerability via survey. Forty of forty-nine participants with acute stroke (34 ischemic and 6 hemorrhagic) had successful scans; median age 71 (years[IQR 58.5–76.5]); median NIHSS 4.5 [IQR 2.0–12.0]) and 20 healthy controls were enrolled. No device-related safety concerns were identified, and the scanner was generally well tolerated. SNR ≥ 3 for algorithm-based analysis were obtained in 36/40 (90.0%) stroke participants and 12/40 (30.0%) achieved the higher threshold for heatmap visualisation (SNR ≥ 12). This first-in-human study demonstrates the safety, tolerability, and technical feasibility of operating the device within an inpatient stroke workflow and generate interpretable MR-derived signals in most patients. These findings justify larger prospective studies to evaluate diagnostic performance and clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Comparative metagenomic survey of gut microbiome composition and metabolic potential in wild and conservation-area saiga antelopes (Saiga tatarica)
Article.Authors: Katkenov N.; Kushugulova A.; Kozhakhmetov S.; Jarmukhanov Z.; Vinogradova E.; Mukhatayev Z.; Nurgaziyev M.; Kovenskiy A.; Mukhanbetzhanov N.; Kushaliyev K.; Taubaev U.; Radojicic B.; Sansyzbay A.
Article.Abstract: The gut microbiome of saiga antelopes ( Saiga tatarica ) under captive conditions remains poorly characterized. We used shotgun metagenomics to compare fecal microbiomes of wild Ural saiga from steppe habitats ( n = 54) and captive saiga from a conservation area in western Kazakhstan ( n = 43). Captive-group samples showed lower bacterial species richness and evenness and a higher relative abundance of Fibrobacter- classified sequences, a finding not independently corroborated by an alternative taxonomic profiling approach and therefore interpreted cautiously. ANCOM-BC2 (compositionality-aware) was consistent with enrichment of Fibrobacter and Faecalimonas in captive-group samples, whereas several taxa identified by relative-abundance testing were not consistently supported. Median relative abundances (wild vs. captive) of predicted pathways were higher in wild-group samples for L-rhamnose degradation I (0.33% vs. 0.20%; Cliff’s δ = 0.91) and pyruvate fermentation to propanoate I (0.33% vs. 0.19%; δ = 0.89), and in captive-group samples for inosine-5′-phosphate biosynthesis II (1.30% vs. 1.60%; δ = 0.87) and L-lysine biosynthesis VI (0.64% vs. 0.90%; δ = 0.99); pathway differential analysis was not compositionality-aware and requires cautious interpretation. Differences between groups cannot be attributed specifically to captivity because geographic, dietary, and other group-level factors are confounded. These findings provide a baseline for future studies.

Article.Title: PT-LGBM: an end-to-end interpretable cross-domain model for high-speed train bearing fault diagnosis under class imbalance
Article.Authors: Liao H.; Wang F.; Li N.; Chen Y.; Li R.; Liu X.; Xiu X.
Article.Abstract: Generalizing the high diagnostic accuracy achieved under laboratory conditions to high-speed train bearings operating in real-world environments is critical. Existing methods remain limited in their ability to address fault-class imbalance, domain shift, and insufficient interpretability simultaneously, leaving the reliability of cross-domain diagnosis inadequately validated. This study proposes PT-LGBM, an interpretable cross-domain fault diagnosis model for high-speed train bearings, comprising four components: PICFS, a geometry-partition-based intelligent sampling method; TFRO-Align, a cross-domain feature-alignment method; an NSGA-II-optimized LightGBM classifier; and an interpretability module integrating t-SNE and SHAP. PICFS reconstructs minority-class samples near decision boundaries to reduce classification bias and boundary blurring caused by conventional interpolation. TFRO-Align combines feature reweighting, orthogonal mapping, and optimal-transport constraints to reduce discrepancies between the CWRU laboratory source domain and the in-service train target domain. The aligned features are classified using the optimized LightGBM model, while t-SNE and SHAP examine the transfer process and diagnostic decisions. On the labeled CWRU source-domain dataset, PT-LGBM achieved 94.12% accuracy, 93.45% Macro-F1, and 100% recall for the normal class. On 16 in-service target-domain records whose labels were blinded during the modeling stage, PT-LGBM achieved an Accuracy of 0.750 (12/16), providing a traceable analytical pathway from laboratory diagnosis to the in-service train environment.

Article.Title: A comparative study of convolutional neural networks and vision transformers for human identification from ante-mortem panoramic dental radiographs
Article.Authors: Moros Morales L.; Sabourin C.; Dunoyer C.; Baccino E.; Inquimbert C.
Article.Abstract: Identifying deceased individuals is a critical component of forensic investigations, particularly following mass casualty events or in cases involving advanced decomposition, where traditional identification methods such as fingerprint analysis may no longer be applicable. Dental records provide a valuable alternative; however, their comparison remains a challenging and time-consuming task for forensic experts. In this study, we investigate the use of deep learning for human identification from panoramic dental radiographs. We employ triplet loss to learn discriminative image embeddings and evaluate six modern neural network architectures, including convolutional and transformer-based models, using panoramic radiographs collected at Montpellier University Hospital (CHU Montpellier). Performance was assessed on two tasks: verification, which determines whether two images belong to the same individual, and identification, which consists of retrieving the identity of an unknown image from a database of known individuals. Among the evaluated architectures, the best verification performance was achieved by ConvNeXt-S, with an accuracy of 0.9908. For identification, the best-performing model was ConvNeXt-L, achieving a Rank@1 accuracy of 0.9877 and a Rank@5 accuracy of 0.9983. These results demonstrate the potential of deep metric learning for forensic dental identification and suggest that semi-automatic systems could substantially assist practitioners during the identification process.

Article.Title: Genome-wide association analysis and genomics-assisted prediction of seed productivity traits in Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.)
Article.Authors: Joshi V.; Colley M.; Shi A.; Ierlan K.; Formiga A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the genetic basis of reproductive traits can help improve spinach ( Spinacia oleracea L.) seed productivity. We evaluated a diversity panel in Chimacum, Washington, during the 2023 season using genome-wide association analysis and genomic prediction. Analyses used 86,049 single-nucleotide polymorphisms, with 227 accessions for days to flowering and gender distribution and 195 for seed yield per female plant. The strongest associations were at SOVchr3_49591612, SOVchr2_3481334, and SOVchr3_1006345, with maximum − log₁₀(P) values of 11.95, 12.04, and 12.80, respectively. Positional candidates included SAP18 for flowering, a BURP domain-containing protein, and pollen-specific SF21 for yield, and a TPX2/importin domain-containing protein for gender distribution. Across 100 repeated holdouts, the highest reported mean predictive correlations were 0.636, 0.641, and 0.478 for the respective 20-, five-, and seven-marker panels. Because marker selection preceded resampling, these estimates describe predictive ability conditional on fixed panels rather than independent validation of marker discovery. Together, the associations, candidate annotations, and compact marker panels provide a focused framework for investigating reproductive timing, female seed productivity, and field gender balance, prioritizing genomic targets for fine mapping and marker validation in spinach breeding.

Article.Title: Radiological and adding‑on outcomes of L3 versus L4 lowest instrumented vertebra for Lenke 5/6 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a meta‑analysis
Article.Authors: Liu W.; Wen C.; Zhu W.; Tang X.; Bao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The optimal lowest instrumented vertebra (LIV) selection in Lenke 5/6 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is controversial. We aimed to compare radiographical outcomes and the incidence of the adding-on phenomenon with L3 versus L4 as the LIV, the two most frequent selections. This research included studies comparing outcomes of L3 versus L4 as the LIV in Lenke 5/6 AIS published from August 2001 to June 2025 in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. An updated search from July 1, 2025 to manuscript submission was subsequently performed, with no additional eligible comparative studies identified. The Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool and the Newcastle‒Ottawa Scale were used to assess the quality of randomized controlled trials and retrospective cohort studies, respectively. Meta-analysis of coronal parameters, sagittal parameters, and the adding-on phenomenon was performed. Data were pooled using random-effects or fixed-effect models to obtain mean differences (MD) for continuous variables and relative risk for categorical variables, with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI). Six studies with 228 patients in the L3 group and 184 patients in the L4 group were included. The preoperative thoracolumbar/lumbar curves were 46.95° (95% CI: 40.82 to 53.08) in the L3 group and 46.81° (95% CI: 40.00 to 53.62) in the L4 group. The L3 group had significantly shorter fused segments than the L4 group (MD = -0.81, 95% CI: -1.15 to -0.48, P < 0.001). There was no difference in correction of thoracic curve (MD = 0.58, 95% CI: -1.00 to 2.27, P = 0.50), C7-central sacral vertical line (MD = 2.16, 95% CI: -0.29 to 4.61, P = 0.08), thoracic kyphosis (MD = -0.39, 95%CI: -2.49 to 1.71, P = 0.72), lumbar lordosis (MD = 0.18, 95% CI: -3.46 to 3.83, P = 0.92) and sagittal vertebral axis (MD = 1.01, 95% CI: -3.47 to 5.50, P = 0.66) between L3 group and L4 group. L4 group showed a slightly better effect in correcting the thoracolumbar/lumbar curve (MD = 3.72, 95% CI: 0.96 to 6.49, P = 0.008) than the L3 group. Regarding the adding-on phenomenon, the L3 group had a higher incidence than the L4 group (relative risk = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.20 to 5.45, P = 0.02). In summary, in patients with mild to moderate Lenke 5/6 AIS, L3 represents a safe distal fusion segment. In contrast, L4 may be recommended as the LIV for individuals with a younger age, skeletal immaturity, or a rigid curve. Future large‑scale randomized controlled trials or well‑adjusted propensity‑score‑matched multi‑center studies with long-term follow-up are required to validate our conclusions and disentangle the true effect of LIV selection from patient confounders.

Article.Title: Quality-controlled synthetic oversampling for imbalanced tabular classification using large language models
Article.Authors: Yuksel A.; Karabiyik M.; Turkoglu B.; Asuroglu T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many tabular classification tasks involve imbalanced classes, but synthetic oversampling can produce rows that violate feature constraints or duplicate existing observations. We present QualSynth, a training-free framework that prompts a large language model to make sparse edits to real minority-class rows under data-derived feature constraints and a machine-readable output contract. A deterministic validation layer checks each candidate’s structure, values, and duplication before admitting it to the training set. We evaluated QualSynth on eight benchmark datasets with ten seeds against four synthetic oversamplers, including the widely used SMOTE, and class-weighted learning without augmentation. QualSynth achieved the highest F1 score among the synthetic oversamplers on four datasets, while SMOTE had the best average ranks. In equivalence tests, QualSynth and SMOTE differed by less than prespecified margins of 0.03 in F1 score and 0.02 in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). After correction for multiple comparisons, the only pairwise difference was higher ROC-AUC for QualSynth than for the diffusion model TabDDPM. Class weighting alone had the best overall ranks, and no augmentation strategy improved aggregate ROC-AUC over the unweighted reference. QualSynth is therefore a controlled, inspectable option for minority-class augmentation, with predictive utility comparable to SMOTE’s.

Article.Title: An improved RT-DETR algorithm for surface defect detection integrating state space model and feature recalibration
Article.Authors: Lu W.; Wei X.; Li J.; Diao L.; Wei Y.; Wan G.; An R.; Zhao P.
Article.Abstract: Industrial surface defect detection requires accurate localization of scale-varying defects under complex background interference while maintaining real-time inference efficiency. Additional comparisons with Le-DETR-M and evaluations on GC10-DET and an automotive filter dataset further support its detection performance under the investigated conditions. Controlled illumination and input-resolution experiments provide additional evidence of detection stability and accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. These findings indicate the potential of RT-DETR-MLS for real-time industrial surface defect inspection.

Article.Authors: Zhao Z.; Niu X.; Li Q.; Wu S.; Kong C.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the mechanism of drilling energy consumption under complex in-situ stress conditions. The drilling work coefficient exhibits a piecewise functional relationship with the lateral pressure coefficient, with deviations up to 30% at a coefficient of (2) Experimental and theoretical results differ by 0.66%~8.76%. Unlike previous models assuming uniform confining pressure, this study reveals a nonlinear non-monotonic relationship between drilling work and lateral pressure coefficient (κ), and introduces a dimensionless coefficient (C E ) to quantify the deviation from hydrostatic conditions. Article.Title: A phenotypic-transport model of selection and therapy-associated phenotypic redistribution in the VC-Resist glioblastoma state
Article.Authors: Romero-Rosales J.; Reveilles J.; Ortega-Sabater C.; Jiménez-Sánchez J.; Pichol-Thievend C.; Seano G.; Calvo G.
Article.Abstract: Glioblastoma recurrence is sustained by tumour cells that survive chemoradiation and infiltrate the peritumoural brain. We previously identified VC-Resist, a Nestin-high, vessel-co-opting and therapy-resistant state induced by DNA-damaging therapy and vascular cues. Whether its short-term enrichment reflects selection of pre-existing cells, phenotypic redistribution, or both remains unclear because death, proliferation and state transitions co-occur. We formulate a phenotypic-transport model for glioblastoma-cell density along a continuous Nestin-reporter axis. The model separates phenotype-dependent net growth from conservative transport and is calibrated to seven-day flow-cytometric Nestin distributions after irradiation of MGG4 cells, with Sytox measurements informing treatment-associated death. It reproduces dose-dependent Nestin-high enrichment and is consistent with a graded association between higher Nestin expression, reduced proliferation and greater radiation resistance. Under the specified uncertainty ranges, transport parameters are among the strongest determinants of the modelled day-7 mean Nestin coordinate. Because the velocity field is inferred from the distributions being fitted, independent longitudinal data and transition-specific perturbations are needed to establish whether the redistribution depends causally on therapy-induced reprogramming. Counterfactual simulations compare attenuation of phenotypic transport with reduction of Nestin-associated protection. Our framework provides an interpretable, data-constrained basis for designing experiments that directly test therapy-induced plasticity in glioblastoma.

Article.Title: The associations between bilateral limb length asymmetry and AI-derived movement symmetry in young adult multi-sport athletes
Article.Authors: Moganan H.; Sankaravel M.; Thung J.; Gao J.; Elumalai G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pre-participation screening often assumes that bilateral anatomical inequality is reflected in functional movement asymmetry, a correspondence rarely tested in training-adapted athletes. Seven bilateral limb segments were tape-measured to the nearest 0.5 cm; HoloMotion markerless screening yielded two proprietary composite and three range-of-motion symmetry indices. Spearman correlations and hierarchical regression (adjusting for gender, sport cluster, dominant side) with bootstrap intervals were Bonferroni-corrected. Of 18 correlations and 18 anthropometric regression coefficients, no association survived correction, and every bootstrap interval included zero. A correlation with uncorrected p < .05 between Femur Length Asymmetry and the Lower Limb Symmetry Score (ρ = −0.189, p = 0.015) did not survive correction or reach significance after adjustment (β = −0.177, p = 0.062). Supplementary Mann–Whitney tests showed a Bonferroni-significant gender difference in Shoulder Limb Symmetry Index favouring males ( p = 0.001, r = 0.26). Tape-measured limb length asymmetry was not associated with HoloMotion-derived symmetry indices, whose composites are proprietary and not independently validated; this does not establish that the constructs are unrelated.

Article.Title: Approximate analytical solution for steady seepage and hydraulic gradient containment safety criterion of an underground water-sealed oil storage cavern
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Qiao L.; Wang S.; Liu X.; Wang C.; Li Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Seepage analysis of the surrounding rock masses is crucial for evaluating the containment property of underground water-sealed oil storage caverns (UWOSCs). Due to the complexity of theoretical derivation, analytical solutions for the seepage field and containment property evaluation of UWOSCs remain lacking, and relevant theoretical research remains insufficient. In this study, an analytical solution for the seepage field of an UWOSC is established based on Darcy’s law and the mirror image method under the assumption of homogeneous, isotropic rock mass and steady-state Darcy flow, considering the rock mass permeability coefficient and key water curtain system parameters (borehole spacing, elevation, and pressure). Taking the vertical hydraulic gradient as the evaluation criterion, a theoretical model for evaluating the containment safety of an UWOSC is established. The rationality of the theoretical model is verified via numerical simulations, field monitoring data, and engineering application in a representative UWOSC project. Furthermore, the influences of rock mass permeability and water curtain system parameters on containment safety are analyzed. The study shows that water curtain system parameters have a significant influence on the containment safety of the UWOSC: containment safety decreases with increasing borehole spacing and elevation but improves with higher pressure. Optimized parameters for the water curtain system are proposed for the representative UWOSC. Under the stated equivalent-continuum assumptions, the proposed analytical solution and theoretical evaluation model provide references for the preliminary design and containment property assessment of UWOSCs, as well as benchmarks for laboratory model tests and numerical simulations.

Article.Title: Deep learning-based prediction of close proximity between the mandibular third molar and the inferior alveolar canal using panoramic radiographs
Article.Authors: Jang M.; Lee H.; Byeon J.; Kim D.; Kim Y.; Jeong I.; Lim H.; Hwang B.; Song I.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Assessment of the relationship between the mandibular third molar and the inferior alveolar canal is essential for preoperative treatment planning. This retrospective study evaluated whether panoramic radiographic regions of interest (ROIs) contain sufficient information to predict close proximity, defined as a minimum root–canal distance of 1 mm or less on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). We analyzed 110 mandibular third molars from 63 patients. CBCT images were used only to establish ground truth and define ROIs, whereas model training and inference used panoramic ROI images exclusively. EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet121, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet18 were compared using patient-level five-fold stratified group cross-validation, and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping was used for model interpretation. ResNet18 achieved the numerically highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) (0.829 ± 0.022), with an accuracy of 0.800 ± 0.027, sensitivity of 0.817 ± 0.029, and specificity of 0.780 ± 0.045. The model primarily focused on regions corresponding to the third molar root and inferior alveolar canal. These preliminary findings, derived from folds also used for model selection, suggest that panoramic ROIs contain information associated with CBCT-defined close proximity but cannot determine buccolingual canal position due to the two-dimensional nature of panoramic radiography; independent validation is needed.

Article.Title: Research on agricultural and forestry waste-based deodorizing fillers for rural domestic sewage treatment facilities and their application
Article.Authors: Wei S.; Lu H.; Guo C.; Ni Y.
Article.Abstract: Decentralized rural domestic sewage treatment facilities in China often emit ammonia-rich odours. Conventional media are costly and have poor microbial affinity. Farm and forestry wastes are inexpensive, but their mechanisms and field performance remain underexplored. In this study, loofah sponge and pine bark were compared against an activated carbon–ceramsite control. The reactor was stabilized for 30 days and then tested at gas loads of 4–14 L/min, inlet ammonia concentrations of 10–90 ppm, and temperatures of 20–35 °C. Pine bark maintained an ammonia removal efficiency of 97–99% across the tested range. The optimized pine bark–ceramsite composite formed a layered porous structure and enriched Nitrospira to a relative abundance of 19.25%, suggesting a potentially nitrifying community. Loofah sponges performed well only under low-load and moderate-temperature conditions. A two-year field trial revealed that the composite reduced the capital cost to CNY 92.14 per ton of daily capacity, and the effluent met local discharge standards. The composite can be constructed from locally available waste materials, making it a practical option for odour control in rural domestic sewage treatment facilities.

Article.Title: Three dimensional analysis of corneal reflectivity following cultivated oral mucosal epithelial transplantation using optical coherence tomography
Article.Authors: Ogino R.; Mori-Ogiwara Y.; Shijo T.; Kasamatsu H.; Ibrahim O.; Shirane M.; Yagi-Yaguchi Y.; Tomida D.; Noma H.; Dogru M.; Yamaguchi T.
Article.Abstract: Limbal stem cell deficiency (LSCD) is a debilitating condition that impairs corneal transparency and visual function due to damage of the limbal niche. Traditional treatments often fall short in bilateral cases or severe opacity. Cultivated oral mucosal epithelial transplantation (COMET) has recently emerged as a regenerative approach to restore the ocular surface in LSCD. Here, we evaluated changes in visual acuity, corneal reflectivity, and higher-order aberrations after COMET. Using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), we quantified reflectivity in the epithelial, stromal, and endothelial layers over time. Visual acuity improved significantly after COMET, whereas epithelial reflectivity showed only a transient reduction at 1 month, with no sustained significant changes in corneal reflectivity thereafter. In linear mixed-effects models accounting for repeated measurements and bilateral eyes, both epithelial and stromal reflectivity were significantly associated with visual acuity. Higher-order aberrations showed significant reductions at 12 months. These findings indicate that the sustained visual improvement after COMET was not accompanied by corresponding sustained reductions in corneal reflectivity, suggesting that changes in corneal backscatter alone do not explain visual recovery. Quantitative AS-OCT reflectivity analysis may provide complementary information for characterizing corneal structural and optical properties in patients with LSCD.

Article.Title: Effects of cocoa pod husk fermented with Saccharomyces cerevisiae and lactic acid bacteria on feed utilization and performance of meat goats
Article.Authors: Chaipetch S.; Seephueak W.; Maliwan P.; Sangkaew B.; Cherdthong A.; Supapong C.
Article.Abstract: Cocoa pod husk is an abundant agricultural by-product with potential as an alternative feed resource for ruminants. Fermentation with beneficial microorganisms may improve its nutritive value and enhance nutrient utilization. Therefore, this study investigated the effects of replacing soybean meal with yeast-fermented cocoa pod husk (YFCPH) on feed intake, nutrient digestibility, rumen fermentation characteristics, and blood metabolites in goats. Twenty female Thai Native × Boer crossbred goats (0.5-1 years old; 16.5 ± 0.3 kg body weight) were assigned to a completely randomized design and fed for 90 days. Five dietary treatments were formulated in which YFCPH replaced soybean meal at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. Cocoa pod husk was fermented with Saccharomyces cerevisiae (1.0 × 10 8 CFU/g) and lactic acid bacteria (1.0 × 10 8 CFU/g) for 21 days before inclusion in the concentrate diet. Rice straw was provided ad libitum, and concentrate was offered at 0.5% of body weight. Fermentation reduced plant secondary compounds, including phenolics, tannins, theobromine, caffeine, and saponins, while improving the amino acid profile of cocoa pod husk. Increasing levels of YFCPH significantly increased rice straw intake ( p < 0.01), whereas concentrate intake and growth performance were not affected ( p > 0.05). Apparent digestibility of dry matter, organic matter, crude protein, neutral detergent fiber, and acid detergent fiber decreased linearly with increasing YFCPH inclusion ( p < 0.05). Rumen protozoal and bacterial populations were influenced by dietary treatments, with increased microbial counts observed in supplemented groups. Total volatile fatty acid concentrations showed moderate variation among treatments, indicating stable rumen fermentation. Blood biochemical and hematological parameters were not significantly affected by dietary YFCPH supplementation. In conclusion, YFCPH can be used as an alternative feed ingredient to partially replace soybean meal in goat diets without negative effects on growth performance or animal health. Fermentation improved the nutritional quality of cocoa pod husk and reduced anti-nutritional factors, supporting its utilization as a sustainable feed resource for smallholder goat production systems. However, high inclusion levels may reduce nutrient digestibility due to increased dietary fiber.

Article.Title: Improved deep reinforcement learning based on virtual inertia control in islanded microgrids
Article.Authors: Amiri F.; Sadr S.; Shalbafian A.
Article.Abstract: One of the most important fundamental challenges in islanded microgrids (IMs) is frequency stability. The reduction in inertia and damping in this system is due to the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources. Virtual inertia control (VIC) is a solution to improve frequency stability in IM. Control methods that have been used for VIC in IM have problems with parameter uncertainty and disturbances and are not adaptable. In this paper, a new method based on improved deep reinforcement learning (IDRL) has been used in the VIC structure, which is obtained by combining three components: (1) The TD3 algorithm has been used to train frequency stability in IM, (2) The hierarchical attention mechanism has been used to focus on the microgrid frequency deviation and reduce the impact of disturbances on it, (3) Meta-learning has been used to quickly adapt to changes in system parameters and disturbances. The proposed method (IDRL) has been compared in several scenarios with the ANN-PI controller and BEL controller in terms of performance against disturbances and parameter uncertainty. The results indicate that the proposed method has achieved an average improvement of 42% in the microgrid frequency deviation and 52% in the settling time of the frequency deviations.

Article.Title: Automatic recognition and assessment of students’ high-order thinking skills in online learning environments based on multimodal deep learning
Article.Authors: Li H.; Zhou G.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Scalable prediction of rubric-consistent proxy indicators related to students’ high-order thinking skills in online learning environments is important for supporting process-oriented learning analytics and personalized educational intervention. However, existing assessment methods often rely on manual scoring, single-source learning evidence, or shallow multimodal fusion strategies, which makes it difficult to capture the complex relationships among students’ textual expression, learning behavior, task performance, and interaction patterns. To address these limitations, this paper proposes MHTA-Net, a multimodal network for predicting rubric-derived high-order thinking proxy targets through multimodal encoding, Mamba-based selective fusion, and KAN-based multi-task prediction. Specifically, the multimodal learning feature encoder extracts heterogeneous representations from textual expressions, behavioral sequences, assessment records, and interaction features. The Mamba-based selective fusion module models cross-modal dependencies and selectively retains informative evidence states from heterogeneous learning traces, while the KAN-based multi-task module maps the fused representation to an overall rubric-derived proxy level and dimension-specific proxy scores for analysis, evaluation, and creation. Experiments are conducted on the constructed MOOCCubeX-HOTS benchmark, which contains 12,486 learner-course instances derived from public MOOC data. The proposed MHTA-Net achieves the best overall performance, with an Accuracy of 0.876, a Macro-F1 of 0.862, an AUC of 0.923, an MAE of 4.96, an RMSE of 6.42, and a PCC of 0.842. Ablation experiments, dimension-level analysis, missing-modality robustness evaluation, visualization, and case studies further demonstrate the predictive effectiveness, robustness, and output transparency of the proposed model. The results indicate that MHTA-Net provides a feasible framework for multidimensional prediction of rubric-derived proxy indicators related to high-order thinking in online learning environments, rather than an independently validated measurement of latent cognitive ability.

Article.Title: Rainfall redistribution and water use patterns of four planted forest types in a small watershed in the exposed pisha sandstone region of the loess plateau
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Liang C.; Yang Z.; Yue Z.; Guo J.; Zhao J.; Gao Y.
Article.Abstract: Water availability is a key limiting factor for vegetation restoration and ecosystem stability in the Pisha sandstone region of the Loess Plateau. However, quantitative evidence on how different planted species partition rainfall, modify soil infiltration, and differentiate their vertical water-uptake niches under water-limited conditions remains scarce for this lithologically unique region. This study addressed three questions: (i) how the four species partition rainfall into interception, throughfall and stemflow; (ii) how they modify soil infiltration; and (iii) how their water sources shift vertically across the growing season, and what this implies for species selection in vegetation restoration. Four dominant planted species ( Caragana korshinskii , Hippophae rhamnoides , Pinus tabuliformis , and Prunus sibirica ) were investigated in a representative small watershed, with three replicate plots established for each species. Field observations included canopy rainfall redistribution, double-ring infiltration experiments, continuous soil moisture monitoring across the 0–60 cm soil profile, sap flow measurements, and hydrogen and oxygen isotope tracing of soil and xylem water during the growing season. The MixSIAR Bayesian mixing model was applied to quantify seasonal variations in plant water sources, and linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate interspecific differences. The results showed that H. rhamnoides and C. korshinskii exhibited strong canopy interception capacity (averaging 76.5% and 59.4%, respectively), whereas P. sibirica produced the highest stemflow volume. C. korshinskii showed the highest initial (9.80 mm min − ¹), steady-state (4.42 mm min − ¹) and average (5.70 mm min − ¹) infiltration rates, while H. rhamnoides showed the lowest infiltration capacity (steady-state rate of 1.05 mm min − ¹). All species displayed distinct diurnal sap flow patterns, reflecting different water regulation strategies. Isotope analysis revealed clear seasonal and vertical differentiation in water source utilization: C. korshinskii primarily relied on shallow soil water, with its contribution increasing from 16.85% in June to 38.10% in September; P. tabuliformis and P. sibirica shifted toward deeper soil water during rainy periods, which accounted for over 50% of total uptake in August; and H. rhamnoides showed flexible water uptake strategies. These findings demonstrate species-specific ecohydrological adaptations of planted forests in water-limited environments and provide insights into plant functional responses and sustainable vegetation restoration in fragile ecosystems.

Article.Title: Grid-forming energy storage capacity configuration strategy considering economic and stability constraints
Article.Authors: Li C.; Liu Y.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: To address the stability requirements of power systems with high renewable energy penetration, an optimal capacity configuration method for grid-forming energy storage systems (GFM-ESS) is proposed. The optimization model is first established with the objective of maximizing the average daily comprehensive profit of GFM-ESS, considering energy arbitrage revenue, ancillary service compensation, and investment, operation, and maintenance costs under typical operating scenarios. To simultaneously ensure system stability, nonlinear frequency stability and small-signal stability constraints are incorporated into the model. Data-driven approaches, namely hyperplane fitting and Bayesian linear regression, are employed to linearize the two types of stability constraints and construct a multi-type stability-constrained optimization framework. The proposed method is validated using a modified IEEE 39-bus system and a large-scale practical power system in northwestern China. The results suggest that the optimized GFM-ESS configuration helps reduce the risks of frequency instability and small-signal oscillations within the investigated test cases, while achieving coordinated improvements in both economic performance and operational efficiency. Furthermore, the case study on the practical large-scale power system confirms the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed method in renewable-rich power grids.

Article.Title: Prediction of anemia among pregnant women in Ethiopia using explainable ensemble machine learning models
Article.Authors: Atnaf A.; Abebaw D.; Gebeyehu M.; Getie Z.; Amare Y.; Beyene S.; Mengistie M.; Mengistu A.; Tizie S.; Anteneh A.; Tadele M.
Article.Abstract: Anemia during pregnancy remains a major public health concern in Ethiopia, contributing significantly to maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an ensemble machine learning–based model for predicting anemia among pregnant women in Ethiopia using nationally representative survey data. A total of 2699 pregnant women with complete hemoglobin measurements and covariate information were included from the Ethiopian Demographic and Health Surveys (EDHS) of 2005, 2011, and 2016. Six machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Gradient Boosting, CatBoost, and stacking ensemble) were trained and evaluated using performance evaluation metrics. Gradient Boosting demonstrated the highest overall discriminatory ability, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.65, followed closely by CatBoost and the stacking ensemble model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed that media exposure, history of pregnancy termination, pregnancy intention, religion, and iron supplementation were among the most influential predictors of anemia among pregnant women. An ensemble machine learning model showed moderate potential for predicting anemia among pregnant women in Ethiopia and may serve as a supportive decision-making tool in antenatal care settings. However, improvements in sensitivity, incorporation of longitudinal and clinical data, and external validation are required.

Article.Title: Men show larger cardiorespiratory responses than women to paced breathing at 0.1 and 0.25 Hz in trained athletes
Article.Authors: Romanchuk O.; Guzii O.; Abreu R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Controlled breathing is a standard probe of cardiovascular autonomic and baroreflex function, yet whether the magnitude of the cardiorespiratory response differs between the sexes is insufficiently characterised. We compared sex differences in the responses of autonomic, haemodynamic and respiratory indices to paced breathing at the cardiovascular resonance frequency (0.1 Hz) and at 0.25 Hz in 134 trained athletes (89 men, 45 women) using spiroarteriocardiorhythmography. For each index we computed the within-participant increment from spontaneous breathing and compared increments between sexes with the Mann–Whitney U test and Welch’s t-test, controlling the false discovery rate within each manoeuvre family and reporting rank-biserial correlations with bootstrap confidence intervals. At rest, women had longer QTc and higher cardiac index, and men had higher blood pressure and peripheral vascular resistance; general physical working capacity did not differ. Sixteen increments differed between the sexes after correction, and fifteen of the sixteen were larger in men: at 0.1 Hz the differences involved spectral redistribution and vascular resistance, and at 0.25 Hz they involved ventilation and respiratory-flow variability. Minute ventilation rose in both conditions and, at 0.25 Hz, rose more in men in absolute and relative terms, so the ventilatory differences reflect greater ventilatory recruitment, not body size.

Article.Title: Soil-building cluster dynamic interaction affects the seismic demands of urban buildings
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Guo T.; Knappett J.; Xie Y.; Lin X.; Xie T.; Du Z.; Yu S.
Article.Abstract: Soil-building cluster dynamic interaction (SBCI) can influence the seismic demands of buildings in densely built environments, yet it remains underexplored and absent from current seismic design practices. Here, by integrating shaking table tests, analytical derivations, and advanced numerical simulations, we systematically quantify the governing mechanisms and engineering implications of SBCI. We find, through complementary experimental, analytical, and numerical investigations, that SBCI effects are considerably influenced by a set of coupled factors, including earthquake intensity and frequency content; building number, spacing, configuration, natural frequency, and foundation embedment; and soil type and shear wave velocity profiles. SBCI is particularly significant under near-resonant conditions and, within the investigated parameter space, generally becomes negligible (i.e., the influence on seismic demand is less than 5%) when inter-building spacing exceeds twice the building width or soil shear wave velocity exceeds 300 m/s. For the investigated building clusters on non-liquefiable soils, SBCI is generally beneficial, whereas it may amplify the seismic force of a building with a fundamental period exceeding the site period. For the investigated building clusters on liquefiable soils, SBCI increases the post-earthquake tilt of edge buildings and lateral forces of all buildings, highlighting its potential to increase seismic demands of building clusters. These findings support further consideration of SBCI in future seismic design provisions for urban building clusters.

Article.Title: Leg preference affects mental representation of single-leg hopping in healthy female adolescents
Article.Authors: Ron Baum A.; Taragin T.; Gutman I.; Tenenbaum G.; Schack T.; Vogel L.; Franklin E.; Abraham A.
Article.Abstract: Single-leg hopping (SLH) is a fundamental motor skill in daily activities that is stored as a mental representation. A mental representation is an internal depiction of an action based on prior experience and task comprehension. It is organized through Basic Action Concepts (BACs) and underpins motor planning, execution, and control. This research examines the role of leg preference (either right or left) in the mental representation of SLH among healthy female adolescents. In study 1, we describe the development and validation of the BAC method by using SLH through comparisons between mental representations of children (N = 9; 8–15 years) and young adults (N = 4; 18–24 years). In study 2, we examine the role of leg preference on mental representation through a cross-sectional analysis of 38 healthy female participants ( M age = 16.07 ± 0.33 years; range = 15.6–16.6). Mental representations of SLH were analyzed by using structural dimensional analysis of motor mental representation (SDA-M). The results of study 1 confirmed the developmental process of BACs by showing that young adults maintain a more structured (i.e., functionally organized) mental representation than children ( p < 0.05). The results of study 2 revealed more structured mental representations for the preferred leg than for the non-preferred-leg and for the right leg than for the left-preferred leg ( p s < 0.05). These preliminary findings support age-related cognitive-motor development and may suggest that left hemisphere motor superiority comprises cognitive spheres, namely, enhanced mental representation. Future research into the associations between side preference, cognitive characteristics and motor planning, execution and control is warranted.

Article.Title: Multi-performance optimization of CO2-MQL burnishing process considering surface properties
Article.Authors: Bui H.; Van A.; Nguyen T.
Article.Abstract: In this work, process parameters of the CO 2 -based minimum quantity lubrication burnishing (CMB) process, including the spindle speed ( S ), feed rate ( f ), and penetration depth ( D ) are optimized to maximize the Vickers hardness ( VH ) and reduce the maximum height roughness in the defined area ( Sz ). A set of CMB experiments was conducted on SKD61 steel. The Gaussian process regression (GPR) and ensembles of trees (ET) approaches were used to propose predictive models of the CMB responses. The criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC), elite-guided adaptive Cauchy-zebra optimization algorithm (ECZOA), and multi-attributive ideal-real comparative analysis (MAIRCA) are utilized to compute the weights, generate feasible solutions, and determine the best point. The findings showed that the optimal S , f , and D were 1600 rpm, 100 mm/min, and 0.20 mm, respectively. At the optimal point, the improvements in the VH and Sz were 5.5% and 30.0%, respectively. Moreover, the average coefficient of friction ( COF ) and final wear depth ( Z ) were reduced from approximately 0.704 to 0.581 and from 0.17 to 0.08 mm, respectively, demonstrating the improved tribological performance of the optimized CMB process. The GPR approach outperformed the ET model in predicting the CMB responses. The integrated GPR-ECZOA-MAIRCA procedure successfully identified a beneficial operating condition for simultaneously improving Sz and VH within the investigated parameter domain. Microstructural observations revealed that higher S and D promoted more extensive subsurface deformation. The compressive residual stress (CRS) of − 412.48 MPa was obtained, demonstrating the development of substantial compressive stresses and improved surface integrity in the burnished SKD61 steel.

Article.Title: SatForensics: a transformer-based multi-modal framework for cyber-attack detection, attribution, and chain-of-custody forensics in low-earth-orbit satellite communication networks
Article.Authors: Kaushik K.; Al-Zyoud M.; Gaur P.; Rajput G.; Singh M.; Joshi R.
Article.Abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite networks lack public records of labelled cyber-attacks, which makes it hard to evaluate detection, attribution and forensic tools for them. We present SatForensics, a gated multi-modal Transformer that scores each satellite observation for anomalies, attributes injected RF attacks to one of five archetypes (broadband, continuous-wave, swept and pulsed jamming, and Doppler-following spoofing), and records every event in a SHA-256 hash-chained ledger together with a calibrated posterior, a confidence margin and an ambiguity flag. The model fuses RF features of the recorded waterfall, orbital geometry propagated from the observation’s own orbital elements, and link context. We evaluate it on 5,408 real SatNOGS observations from 573 satellites and 379 stations, using satellite-grouped splits, attacks injected after splitting, and 5 runs reported as mean ± standard deviation. SatForensics reaches a detection F1 of 81.0 \(\pm \) 1.4% and an attribution macro-F1 of 96.1 \(\pm \) 0.7%. It outperforms SVM, CNN and LSTM baselines in detection but not Random Forest (83.5 \(\pm \) 1.4%) or an RF-only Transformer (84.3 \(\pm \) 1.6%), and ablations show no reliable contribution of gating, geometry, context or mutual-information alignment on this data. Natural labels are SatNOGS vetting outcomes, not attacks, and attack labels are synthetic. Ledger appends take a median of 10.0 \(\mu \) s and inference takes 0.47 ms on one CPU thread. The code and dataset construction scripts are released.

Article.Title: Hyperintense acute reperfusion marker sign in patients with diffusion weighted image-negative transient ischemic attack
Article.Authors: Kim T.; Heo S.; Kim B.; Lee K.; Park S.; Woo H.; Kim W.; Kim K.; Jeon P.; Chang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The hyperintense acute reperfusion marker (HARM) sign on postcontrast fluid-attenuated recovery inversion images reflects blood-brain barrier disruption and is associated with cerebral ischemic injury. However, its clinical significance in transient ischemic attack (TIA) remains unclear. We included 329 consecutive patients with diffusion-weighted imaging-negative TIA and divided them into two groups according to the HARM sign. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with the HARM sign, and Cox regression evaluated predictors of stroke recurrence. The HARM(+) patients were older and had higher systolic blood pressure, shorter symptom duration, more frequent recent TIA or stroke history, and symptomatic arterial steno-occlusion. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that recent TIA or stroke within 12 months (OR 6.623), symptom duration < 1 h (OR 2.735), and symptomatic artery steno-occlusion (OR 2.761) were independently associated with the HARM sign. During follow-up, the recurrence of ischemic stroke was higher in the HARM(+) group (13.3% vs. 3.0%, p = 0.023). However, in multivariable Cox analysis, the ABCD2 score and symptomatic arterial stenosis or occlusion independently predicted stroke recurrence. In DWI-negative TIA, the HARM sign is associated with recent cerebrovascular events, shorter symptom duration, and large artery stenosis or occlusion, but not an independent predictor for recurrent stroke.
