Article.Title: Walking participation as a potential pathway between neighborhood urban forest coverage and all cause mortality across Korean administrative districts
Article.Authors: Kim G.; Kim Y.; Eom S.
Article.Abstract: Urban green space has been associated with health benefits, yet links with mortality remain unclear. This study examined whether walking participation represents a potential pathway in the association between neighborhood urban forest cover and age-standardized all-cause mortality in Korea. An ecological study was conducted using data from 228 Korean administrative districts. Walking participation rate was assessed as a potential mediator between neighborhood urban forest coverage and age-standardized all-cause mortality using multivariable linear regression and mediation analysis. Neighborhood urban forest coverage was positively associated with walking participation (β = 3.69, p < 0.001), whereas walking participation was inversely associated with all-cause mortality (β = −0.89, p < 0.001). In the total-effect model, neighborhood urban forest coverage showed a negative, but non-significant, association with mortality (β = −2.37, p = 0.220). For the contrast between the 25th and 75th percentiles of neighborhood urban forest coverage (0.78% vs. 4.89%), the average indirect association through walking participation was statistically significant (ACME = − 6.07, 95% CI: −10.40 to − 2.76), whereas the average direct and total associations were not statistically significant; however, under CR2 small-sample-corrected inference, neither the exposure–walking interaction nor the indirect association remained statistically significant. Adjustment for categorical city size attenuated but did not eliminate the indirect association through walking, whereas additional adjustment for population density attenuated it to the null. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the estimated indirect associations were attenuated to the null at approximately ρ = −0.20 for δ(t₀) and ρ = −0.40 for δ(t₁). These ecological findings are statistically consistent with walking participation as one potential behavioral pathway but do not establish causal mediation.

Article.Title: Transforming rainfed smallholder farming through typology-based climate-efficient pathways in the lower Shivalik foothills of India
Article.Authors: Dhillon B.; Sandhu P.; Singh M.; Khokhar A.; Singh K.; Yousuf A.; Bhat M.; Kaushik P.; Bhargavi B.; Gopinath K.; Chary G.; Prasad J.; Singh V.
Article.Abstract: Smallholder rainfed farming systems in India face declining landholdings, yield stagnation, and income insecurity. This study applied a typology-driven Rainfed Integrated Farming System (RIFS) approach to 240 farm households in Punjab, categorizing them into five farm types based on landholding, livestock composition, and income sources. Tailored interventions including improved crop varieties, diversified cropping (cereals, pulses, oilseeds, sugarcane, fodder, vegetables), livestock integration (small and large ruminants), resource-conservation practices (vermicomposting, farm ponds, in-situ moisture retention), and value-added enterprises (sugarcane processing, mushroom cultivation, kitchen gardening) were implemented over five years. Economic outcomes revealed substantial net income gains: Type 1 (+ 557%), Type 2 (+ 431%), Type 3 (+ 638%), Type 4 (+ 437%), and Type 5 (+ 184%). Soil fertility improved significantly, with soil organic carbon increasing by 11.5% and available N, P 2 O 5 , and K 2 O by 10.7–14.1%. Greenhouse gas intensity per unit income was lowest in small-ruminant rainfed systems, demonstrating climate-efficient productivity gains. The study empirically validates the effectiveness of typology-specific RIFS interventions in enhancing farm income, resource-use efficiency, and environmental sustainability, providing a scalable framework for smallholder rainfed agro-ecosystems.

Article.Title: Randomized noninferiority trial of VasoClip versus WeckClip in robotic urologic surgery
Article.Authors: Choi J.; Suh H.; Hwang T.; Lee D.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Polymer ligating clips are widely used for vessel and tissue ligation in robotic surgery. This prospective, randomized, phase III noninferiority trial evaluated the efficacy and early safety of VasoClip, a polymer clip with a Z-groove and elastic notch, compared with WeckClip. Forty patients undergoing robotic urologic surgery were randomized 1:1 to VasoClip ( n = 20) or WeckClip ( n = 20). The primary endpoint was ligation success assessed per clip, with patient-level clustering accounted for using generalized estimating equations. A total of 573 clips were applied (300 VasoClip and 273 WeckClip). Overall success was 96.0% versus 92.4%, with a clustering-adjusted absolute risk difference of 3.6% (95% CI, -1.5% to 8.7%). The estimate met the prespecified − 10% noninferiority criterion; however, because the trial included only 40 patients and the original sample-size calculation did not account for within-patient clustering, this result should be interpreted cautiously. In the exploratory body-structure subgroup, success was numerically higher with VasoClip (94.9% vs. 86.1%), but the difference was not statistically significant ( P = 0.078). No Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher complications occurred, and no early device-related safety signals were observed during the two-week follow-up.

Article.Title: Quantitative evaluation and prediction of hydrocarbon generation potential in saline lacustrine mixed sedimentary rocks of the Lucaogou Formation, Junggar Basin
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Zhu R.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Mixed sedimentary rocks in saline lacustrine basins have become key targets for unconventional hydrocarbon exploration due to their unique integrated source-reservoir characteristics. Understanding these systems is crucial for expanding exploration frontiers. Focused on the Lucaogou Formation in the Jimsar Sag, the Junggar Basin, a combined petrophysics-geochemistry workflow was established to resolve lithological complexity and the interference from retained hydrocarbons. Core observations, thin-section analysis, and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were integrated to define lithology, and a Random Forest algorithm was applied to predict lithofacies across the wellbore. An innovative comparison of Rock-Eval pyrolysis parameters pre- and post-extraction with organic solvent was also employed. This method strips the influence of retained mobile hydrocarbons (S 1 and partial S 2 ), allowing for an accurate assessment of the intrinsic generation potential of solid kerogen. Three distinct source-reservoir assemblages were identified: (1) Mudstone (Efficient Supply Model): characterized by dominant generation and strong expulsion, mudstones exhibit the highest post-extraction residual generation potential. Most generated hydrocarbons are expelled into adjacent reservoirs, making this the primary source rock. (2) Dolostone (Generation/Storage Model): characterized by intercrystalline generation and in-situ sealing, dolostones contain the highest quality organic matter (highest original Hydrogen Index (HI)). Intercrystalline pore networks formed by dolomitization provide a unique in-situ encapsulation mechanism for generated hydrocarbons. (3) Siltstone/Tuff (Migrationand Accumulation Model): characterized by early generation but limited source potential, these rocks develop primary intergranular or dissolution pores that facilitate high expulsion efficiency. Consequently, they serve primarily as carrier beds with excellent reservoir transport capacity. Ultimately, a lithology-specific quantitative model for generation potential was established, providing a geological basis for selecting shale oil sweet spots in the Jimsar Sag.

Article.Title: Multi-scale graph attention multi-head aggregation autoencoder for electricity theft detection
Article.Authors: Ai Y.; Zheng K.; Lin G.; Li S.; Dai H.; Wu M.; Zheng Q.
Article.Abstract: Unsupervised analysis of multivariate electricity consumption time series based on machine learning has become a core technical approach for electricity theft detection. Without relying on manually labeled theft samples, such methods can mine the inherent correlation and anomaly patterns hidden in electricity consumption data, thereby supporting the identification of theft behaviors under relaxed supervised conditions. However, mainstream unsupervised detection methods rarely consider the multi-temporal fluctuation characteristics of electricity data and the coupling relationships among multiple consumption variables, which to some extent weakens the generalization ability of algorithms across different data sources. As a result, it is difficult to effectively identify stealthy theft behaviors such as meter-tampering electricity theft. To tackle the above challenges, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Graph Attention Multi-Head Aggregation Autoencoder (MSGME). The model extracts electricity consumption features at multiple temporal scales through multi-scale modules and constructs them into multi-scale graphs. On this basis, a contrastive graph attention network is designed to strengthen the correlation modeling between multiple consumption variables, and multi-head attention aggregation is integrated to improve feature representation capability. Under the unsupervised learning paradigm, the proposed MSGME realizes an effective unsupervised training and detection workflow by combining reconstruction loss and contrastive loss. Experimental results on real-world electricity consumption datasets verify the effectiveness and superiority of the MSGME model in electricity theft detection.

Article.Title: Factors influencing exercise adherence among pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation recipients: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhi Y.; Zhang C.; Wen F.; Wang M.; Xu L.; Yao W.; Bai Z.
Article.Abstract: Exercise adherence is crucial for rehabilitation in pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) recipients, yet remains challenging. This study investigated the current status and influencing factors of exercise adherence, focusing on symptom distress, exercise self-efficacy, and kinesiophobia. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 429 pediatric HSCT recipients. Sociodemographic Questionnaire, Exercise Adherence Scale (EAS), Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale (ESES), the Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale (MSAS10-18), and Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia-11 (TSK-11) were administered. The mean EAS score was 35.77 ± 3.82. Multiple linear regression revealed that prior hospital-supervised exercise (β’ = 0.106, P = 0.003), pre-existing exercise habits (β’ = 0.147, P < 0.001), and daily screen time of 3–6 h (β’ = 0.081, P = 0.045) were protective factors. Daily screen time ≥ 6 h (β’ = -0.103, P = 0.023), fatigue (β’ = -0.169, P = 0.011), difficulty sleeping (β’ = -0.154, P = 0.001), nausea (β’ = -0.133, P = 0.013), and kinesiophobia (β’ = -0.171, P = 0.004) were negative predictors, while exercise self-efficacy (β’ = 0.156, P = 0.004) was a positive predictor. Pediatric HSCT recipients exhibit moderate exercise adherence. Individualized interventions targeting psychological and symptom-related barriers, along with structured screen time management, are needed.

Article.Title: Nanopore epitranscriptomic profiling of influenza A infection in differentiated primary human airway epithelial cells
Article.Authors: Islam M.; Pharo E.; Knox B.; Heyward M.; Ord L.; Williams S.; Alexander M.; Stewart C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses reshape host gene expression and exploit RNA modifications to fine‐tune replication and evade innate immunity. In this study, we used Oxford Nanopore Technologies' (ONT) direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) combined with the CHEUI algorithm to simultaneously map N 6 ‑methyladenosine (m 6 A) and 5‑methylcytidine (m 5 C) modifications and measure poly(A) tail lengths during influenza A/H1N1pdm09 (pandemic strain, 2009) virus infection in normal human bronchial epithelial (NHBE) cells differentiated on transwells (well-differentiated; wdNHBE) in situ at the air–liquid interface (ALI). We profiled the transcriptome at early (6 h post‑infection; hpi) and late (24 hpi) stages and integrated methylome and transcriptome dynamics with polyadenylation. H1N1pdm09 infection elicited strong viral replication and cytokine induction, accompanied by widespread host gene down‑regulation and selective induction of interferon‑stimulated genes. We detected 11,448 unique m 6 A sites and 9,900 unique m 5 C sites, with a stable gene-level overlap between time points (66% of genes differentially methylated at 6 hpi were also modified at 24 hpi), but minimal site-level overlap (< 3% of sites differentially modified at both time points), indicating locus-specific remodelling over time. Crucially, we identified a biphasic remodelling of the host epitranscriptome. Early infection was characterised by decreased m 6 A and increased m 5 C stoichiometry which reversed by 24 h. This late-stage m 6 A hypermethylation converged heavily on translational machinery, such as EEF1A1 . Poly(A) tails were broadly similar between conditions. However, at 24 h post-infection, wdNHBE cells exhibited modest global shortening and transcript‑specific changes, with genes encoding epithelial secreted proteins (e.g., BPIFB1 and SLPI) and antigen presentation machinery (e.g., HLA-C) showing longer tails and mitochondrial mRNAs shorter tails. We provide these multi‑modal data through an interactive Shiny application to facilitate interrogation of epitranscriptomic regulation during infection. Our study demonstrates that influenza virus infection reprograms the host epitranscriptome, with dynamic changes in m 6 A and m 5 C methylation and polyadenylation.

Article.Title: Reconstructing sudden ambient temperature changes in death time estimation from temperatures in two closed compartments using a Bayesian double-exponential approach
Article.Authors: Subramaniam J.; Hubig M.; Schenkl S.; Muggenthaler H.; Springer S.; Sudau J.; Shah F.; Mall G.; Weiser M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional methods of time of death estimation in forensic casework mostly assume a constant ambient temperature $$T_a$$ , which can lead to significant errors. Reconstructing ambient temperature changes at a crime scene a posteriori can therefore be an important task. As a first step, we reconstruct a single sudden drop in $$T_a$$ at unknown time $$t_0$$ using a posteriori temperature measurements $$T_Z(t)$$ , $$Z \in \{X, Y\}$$ , in two closed compartments X , Y (boxes, cupboards,..) at the crime scene. As a reliable reconstruction based on a simple Newtonian cooling model turned out to be not straightforward in a previous study, we apply a Bayesian framework with a double-exponential cooling model for $$T_Z(t)$$ . The approach is tested in two experimental scenarios in a climate chamber under controlled conditions. The results show a reduced reconstruction error in either $$T_a$$ , or $$t_0$$ , or both, compared to a simpler approach using Newtonian cooling and maximum likelihood estimation. The study thus represents a proof of concept giving hints for further research.

Article.Title: Porosity estimation of construction materials from computed tomography images using image segmentation and adaptive thresholding techniques
Article.Authors: Kim B.; Natarajan Y.; Preethaa K.; Park S.; Pyo S.
Article.Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) enables non-destructive examination of pore structures, but image-based porosity estimates depend on preprocessing, segmentation, and imaging resolution. This study compares four filtering–thresholding configurations for estimating porosity from 6,840 CT slices representing six construction-material classes: CM0, CM5, CM10, CM20, geopolymer mortar, and ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC). Median and Gaussian filtering were paired separately with adaptive mean-C and adaptive Gaussian thresholding. Pore-area fractions were calculated from segmented images and compared with available vacuum-pycnometer (PYC) reference values. Three specimens per class were prepared from one batch and tested using PYC, with one specimen subsequently selected for CT scanning. Median filtering with adaptive mean-C thresholding (MB_AMCT) showed promising agreement with the supplied reference values for most investigated classes. In the UHPC comparison figure, all four configurations exceeded the PYC reference value, indicating that unresolved fine pores alone cannot explain the discrepancy. Contributions from noise, local intensity variations, threshold settings, pore misclassification, and physical-reference uncertainty may also contribute, and differences in pore accessibility and spatial coverage mean that CT and PYC cannot be directly equivalent. An additional qualitative comparison looked at candidate pore boundaries in five available CT crops, including UHPC, without independent segmentation ground truth. Agreement in total porosity does not establish accurate pore localization or morphology. Independent CT specimen replication, parameter-sensitivity analysis, and unfiltered comparisons were unavailable. The findings therefore describe performance within the investigated dataset. Further evaluation with documented parameters and independently prepared specimens is required to establish reproducibility, ranking stability, and broader applicability.

Article.Title: Risk assessment and strategic decision support to enhance preparedness and minimize human and economic losses in managing natural disasters
Article.Authors: Shen H.; Fang H.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the impacts of natural disasters is essential for effective risk management, emergency response, and policy planning. However, the complex, nonlinear, and highly irregular nature of disaster-related data poses significant challenges for traditional modeling approaches. This study proposes a comprehensive machine learning and deep learning framework for economic loss prediction, integrating advanced preprocessing, optimization, and validation strategies to enhance predictive accuracy and robustness. Multiple predictive models, including deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks, and gradient boosting, are systematically evaluated and optimized using a Turbulent Flow of Water-based Optimization algorithm. To address data irregularities, Isolation Forest is used for outlier detection, and statistical tests are applied to assess distributional assumptions before normalization. Model performance is rigorously assessed using 5-fold cross-validation and a diverse set of evaluation metrics that capture accuracy, bias, and agreement. In addition, ensemble learning is employed to improve predictive reliability further, while runtime analysis provides insights into computational efficiency. The statistical significance of performance differences is verified using ANOVA and the Wilcoxon test, and an ablation study is conducted to examine model stability and sensitivity. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust, statistically significant improvements in predictive performance, highlighting its suitability for reliable economic loss modeling. This study contributes a validated, generalizable, and decision-oriented modeling approach that can support data-driven disaster risk reduction and management strategies.

Article.Title: Visible dental conditions are associated with peer preferences among preschool children
Article.Authors: Benke B.; Zsido A.; Basler J.; Marada G.; Radnai F.; Fonai F.; Sandor B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Visible dental conditions may influence children’s social perceptions, but evidence in preschool populations remains limited. This cross-sectional study examined hypothetical friendship preferences among 139 children aged 3–7 years (mean ± SD:4.63 ± 0.92) recruited from two kindergartens. Children completed 12 paired comparisons of digitally modified photographs depicting healthy dentition, or a fractured, missing, or a carious incisor. Each pair depicted the same facial identity. Trial-level binary choices of peer preference were analysed using a Bradley–Terry mixed-effects logistic regression model. Healthy dentition was selected most frequently, followed by fractured, missing, and carious teeth. All pairwise differences were statistically significant (Holm-adjusted p < .001) and remained significant after including kindergarten, data-collection period, and their interaction. Girls were more likely than boys to select missing rather than healthy dentition (OR = 3.85, p < .001), whereas older children were less likely to select carious rather than healthy dentition (OR = 0.59 per year, p = .048). Dental status and clinically evident previous treatment were not significantly associated with preferences ( n = 81). These findings suggest dental appearance-based judgements may emerge early. Larger, more diverse studies in naturalistic settings should examine whether these experimental preferences translate into real-world peer interactions.

Article.Title: Thermo-mechanical mechanisms in induction-assisted hard turning of SKD61 steel revealed by experimental benchmarking and archived FEM reanalysis
Article.Authors: Do D.; Kien H.; Vi N.; Huy T.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a mechanism-centered thermo-mechanical reanalysis of induction-assisted hard turning of hardened SKD61 steel with high-speed steel tools using a previously published, center-weighted 27-run campaign as the experimental benchmark. No new authenticated cutting simulations were performed; the numerical contribution comprises reanalysis of archived FEM outputs, Johnson–Cook constitutive-sensitivity calculations, and verification-oriented post-processing. At the condition-matched 475 °C reference, the archived FEM cutting force differed from the experimental mean by 1.43%. Sensitivity screening identified the initial yield parameter \(A\) and thermal-softening exponent \(m\) as the dominant local constitutive influences, with the effect of \(m\) increasing with temperature. From 350 to 600 °C, the archived flank-contact-pressure indicator decreased from 920 to 680 MPa, whereas predicted average tool-zone temperature increased from 430 to 525 °C. Under matched cutting parameters, \({R}_{a}\) , \({R}_{q}\) , and \({R}_{z}\) decreased by about 29%, while terminal \(V{B}_{\text{m}\text{a}\text{x}}\) remained broadly overlapping and non-monotonic across the three temperatures. The limited wear subset supports endpoint comparison only, not wear-rate or tool-life inference. The 475 °C condition is therefore interpreted as an intermediate thermo-mechanical state, not a renewed optimum. Conclusions are limited by the archived 2D plane-strain formulation and the absence of independent tool-temperature validation.

Article.Title: Physical fitness, weight status and cardiovascular changes following school-based HIIT in adolescents: implications for the fat but fit concept
Article.Authors: Koźlenia D.; Domaradzki J.
Article.Abstract: The “fat but fit” concept suggests that higher physical fitness may attenuate the adverse health consequences of elevated adiposity. However, it remains unclear whether combinations of weight status and physical fitness are associated with differences in cardiovascular changes over time among adolescents participating in exercise programmes. This study examined whether baseline weight status and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) were associated with cardiovascular pre-to-post changes among adolescents participating in an 8-week school-based high-intensity interval training (HIIT) intervention. This exploratory secondary pre-to-post analysis was restricted to the plyometric HIIT arm of a previously reported school-based cluster-randomized controlled trial. Ninety-eight 15-year-old adolescents were classified using age- and sex-specific body mass index (BMI) thresholds and sex-specific CRF thresholds into four weight status–CRF categories: Non-overweight–high CRF ( n = 27), Non-overweight–low CRF ( n = 49), Overweight–high CRF ( n = 9), and Overweight–low CRF ( n = 13). No participants met the criteria for obesity. Post-intervention outcomes were analyzed using ANCOVA with baseline values as covariates. Observed individual changes were classified using smallest worthwhile change (SWC) thresholds, and multiple linear regression models tested whether sex, baseline BMI, and baseline estimated VO 2 max predicted changes in performance, cardiovascular outcomes, and body fat percentage. Mean estimated VO 2 max increased by 1.17–1.91 mL kg −1 min −1 across the four categories, although the 95% confidence interval included zero in the Overweight–low CRF category. ANCOVA showed no statistically significant BMI status × CRF status interactions for any outcome ( p > 0.05). BMI status significantly differentiated post-intervention systolic blood pressure (F = 7.978, p = 0.006, η 2 p = 0.079), but not diastolic blood pressure or mean arterial pressure ( p > 0.05). Responder analyses showed no significant associations between weight status–CRF category and responder status for any outcome ( p > 0.05). Regression models explained 1.4–8.2% of the variance in change scores. Although mean estimated CRF increased across all categories, no statistically significant evidence was found that baseline weight status and CRF interacted in relation to cardiovascular pre-to-post changes. However, the small numbers of adolescents in the categories with overweight, limited precision, and absence of a concurrent control comparison preclude firm conclusions about differences in changes between categories or their attribution to HIIT.

Article.Authors: Nwarunma E.; Miari K.; Papadopoulou A.; Corradini S.; Watt G.; Hurwitz S.; Fourfouris T.; Lee K.; Bubnova X.; Briggs R.; Goodyear C.; Simakou T.; Doohan M.; MacDonald L.; Elmesmari A.; Kurowska-Stolarska M.; Humpton T.; Campbell V.; Forrester L.; Mills K.; Lappin K.; Ferro V.; Kim Y.; Wheadon H.; Williams M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interactions between acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) cells and the bone marrow microenvironment can reduce responses to chemotherapy. Macrophages are abundant in AML bone marrow, but how macrophage-associated mitochondrial trafficking relates to drug tolerance remains incompletely defined. Using AML cell lines, primary AML specimens and monocyte-, iPSC- and mouse bone marrow-derived macrophage models, we found that M-CSF-differentiated macrophages attenuated daunorubicin-induced AML apoptosis, with the strongest protection during direct co-culture. AML cells acquired macrophage-derived MitoTracker Deep Red signal, which increased with daunorubicin and was reduced by transwell separation, cytochalasin B and LIMK inhibition. Cross-species co-culture provided orthogonal molecular support through species-specific measurement of murine mitochondrial DNA, with murine nuclear DNA measured in parallel as a control. Macrophage co-culture was also associated with increased AML respiratory capacity and reduced reactive oxygen species. Exploratory proteomic analysis and interrogation of public transcriptomic datasets nominated RHOC/LIMK/cofilin signalling for follow-up, while TH-257 and metformin reduced the transfer-associated signal and macrophage chemoprotection. These findings support an association between acquisition of macrophage-derived mitochondrial material and daunorubicin tolerance in AML models and identify LIMK-dependent actin regulation as a candidate mechanism for further investigation.

Article.Title: Event-triggered distributed STW-RBFNN control of PV-battery DC microgrids under uncertainty and delays
Article.Authors: Fetanat Fard Haghighi H.; Moattari M.; Izadneshan H.
Article.Abstract: Voltage regulation in PV-battery DC microgrids is challenging because of nonlinear converter dynamics, uncertain operating conditions, changes in PV generation and load demand, and communication delays. This paper presents a distributed smooth super-twisting radial basis function neural network (STW-RBFNN) controller for DC-link voltage regulation. The RBFNN estimates uncertain nonlinear dynamics online, while the super-twisting term deals with estimation errors and bounded disturbances. Directed pinned coordination is used for voltage regulation, and a two-stage event-triggered scheme reduces communication between units. The controller is tested on a six-node PV-battery DC microgrid under nominal conditions, 40 stochastic Monte Carlo runs, and communication delays. Under nominal conditions, the RMSE is 0.0089 V, the MAE is 0.0074 V, and the settling time is 0.601 s. The controller requires 3228 network-wide transmissions, 91.03% fewer than 1 ms periodic communication. Across the Monte Carlo runs, the mean RMSE is 0.00704 V with a standard deviation of 0.00027 V. Tests with delays from 0.5 to 10 ms show small changes in voltage error and communication. The analysis establishes conditional practical boundedness for the reduced continuous-time model. Simulations evaluate the complete digital implementation with sampling, saturation, and delayed communication; no analytical delay margin is established.

Article.Title: Research on optimal control of green credit risk based on four-party evolutionary game
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Zhao X.
Article.Abstract: The rise of green credit has strongly promoted the green economy, but green credit risk affects the orderly development of environmental, economic, and social systems. The optimal control of green credit risk can support sustainable economic growth. This study examines how changes in the strategies of different stakeholders affect green credit risk by comparing the factors that influence the balance of interests. It integrates the behavioral strategies of government departments, environmental protection departments, financial institutions, and enterprises into a unified theoretical framework, considering environmental, economic, and social factors such as credibility, support, punishment, and violation. Next, a four-party game model is constructed, the evolutionary stable strategies under various scenarios are analyzed, and the impact of credibility, support, punishment, and violation on participant behavior is examined. The results show that credibility strongly influences government department and environmental protection department behaviors; increased support has a greater incentive for the government department; higher punishment from the environmental protection department restrains the enterprise more than the government department; and the violation degree has a limited effect on the enterprise. Deep participation by all stakeholders is essential for resource sharing, complementary advantages, and coordinated development. Simultaneously, green credit markets, products, services and platforms can provide a conducive environment for risk reduction.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of seven Buxus (Buxaceae) species provides insight into plastid genome evolution, ndh pseudogenization, and inverted repeat dynamics
Article.Authors: Abdullah N/A.; Riaz F.; Sammad A.; Ashfaq S.; Latif S.; Shah S.; Heidari P.
Article.Abstract: Buxus L. (Buxaceae) comprises 101 accepted species distributed across Europe, Asia, Africa, Madagascar, and the Caribbean. Despite their ecological, pharmacological, and horticultural significance, plastome resources for South Asian Buxus taxa have remained unavailable. Here, we de novo assembled five Buxus plastomes ( B. papillosa , B. wallichiana , B. harlandii , B. sempervirens , and B. austroyunnanensis ) and compared them with two published genomes ( B. microphylla and B. sinica var. parvifolia ), providing the first plastome resources for the South Asian species B. papillosa and B. wallichiana . The seven plastomes exhibited the typical quadripartite structure, with lengths ranging from 150,915 to 161,655 bp. Inverted-repeat (IR) dynamics revealed four distinct genome types, with B. sempervirens showing the most contracted IR (17,860 bp) and B. wallichiana the most expanded (32,284 bp). Simple sequence repeats (SSRs) were mainly AT-rich mononucleotides localized in noncoding regions, and codon usage and amino acid frequencies were highly conserved across species, reflecting stable translational constraints. Nucleotide diversity analysis identified the intergenic spacers rps16–trnQ-UUG , ycf4–cemA , ccsA–ndhD , and trnE-UUC–trnT-GGU as the most variable candidate regions for future DNA barcoding. Phylogenetic analysis of the complete plastomes, rooted with Pachysandra terminalis , recovered two strongly supported lineages: B. papillosa + B. wallichiana (SH-aLRT/UFBoot = 100/100) and B. sempervirens + B. harlandii + B. sinica + B. microphylla (100/100). The unrooted tree strongly supported a bipartition separating these six species from P. terminalis + B. austroyunnanensis (99.7/100), but this value did not independently support the sister relationship between B. austroyunnanensis and the six-species group seen in the rooted tree. Consistent with this uncertainty, analysis of 74 shared protein-coding genes recovered the same two groups with high support (100/100 and 98.9/100) but placed B. austroyunnanensis with B. papillosa + B. wallichiana with weak support (83.8/79), leaving its position unresolved. Within the sister pair B. wallichiana and B. papillosa , the shared absence of ndhF is consistent with, although not conclusive of, a single loss in their common ancestor, whereas the additional pseudogenization of ndhD , ndhG , ndhH , and ndhI is restricted to B. wallichiana . These findings provide a crucial genomic foundation for future studies on Buxus evolution, diversification, and conservation.

Article.Title: PVP/HPMC-stabilized silver nanoparticle coatings balance antibacterial activity, silver mobility, breathability, and cytocompatibility in commercial face masks
Article.Authors: Karatas E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are widely used to impart antibacterial activity to face masks; however, post-manufacturing finishes should not compromise breathing resistance or filtration, and the mobility and biological effects of the incorporated silver need to be controlled. In this study, AgNPs were synthesized at room temperature by L-ascorbic acid reduction in an aqueous poly(vinylpyrrolidone)/hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (PVP/HPMC) matrix, which served as a stabilizing and film-forming medium, and were immobilized on commercial three-layer polypropylene medical masks by dip-coating at nominal Ag concentrations of 50 and 100 ppm (M50 and M100). The spherical, face-centered cubic AgNPs had a mean diameter of 24.8 ± 2.4 nm, and ICP-OES revealed Ag loadings of 8.63 ± 0.25 and 17.03 ± 0.32 µg cm − 2 for M50 and M100, respectively. Under limited-moisture conditions (1–2 µL PBS cm − 2 , 37 °C, 24 h), less than 10% of the loaded Ag was mobilized. Particle filtration efficiency was preserved (95.0% for the pristine mask versus 96.1% and 97.3% for M50 and M100) and was unaffected by moisture. M50 retained 93% of the original air permeability and remained within the EN 14683 Type I/II differential-pressure limit after moisture challenge, whereas M100 exceeded this limit. In direct-contact assays, viable counts of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus were reduced by 78.8–83.4% for M50 and 95.9–97.4% for M100 (log reductions of 0.68–1.59, below the 2-log efficacy threshold of standardized tests), whereas the silver-free coating showed no antibacterial activity. Both formulations were non-cytotoxic to L929 fibroblasts according to ISO 10993-5, although M100 induced a modest decrease in metabolic activity and a transient intracellular oxidative response. Increasing the Ag loading thus enhanced antibacterial activity at the expense of breathability and cellular compatibility, identifying M50 as the more balanced formulation.

Article.Title: Bioprocessing of coconut husk to produce second-generation bioethanol using Zymomonas mobilis ZM4
Article.Authors: Kumar V.; Mishra S.; Babbal N/A.; Yazdani S.; Lal P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coconut husk is an abundant lignocellulosic residue generated by the tropical coconut processing industry and remains largely underutilized despite its considerable carbohydrate content. This study developed an integrated strategy involving sequential alkaline, dilute-acid, and bleaching pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, and fermentation with Zymomonas mobilis for the valorization of coconut husk into bioethanol. The sequential pretreatment enhanced cellulose accessibility and resulted in substantial removal of lignin and extractive components while retaining a considerable proportion of the carbohydrate fraction. Enzymatic hydrolysis using a cellulase–hemicellulase cocktail released approximately 230 mg glucose g⁻¹ and 161.25 mg xylose g⁻¹ of raw coconut husk, corresponding to overall sugar recovery efficiencies of approximately 50–60% following pretreatment and hydrolysis. Fermentation of the hydrolysate by Z. mobilis resulted in an ethanol yield of 0.0975 g g⁻¹ raw biomass, corresponding to approximately 83% of the theoretical ethanol yield based on the available fermentable sugars. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of coconut husk as a feedstock for second-generation bioethanol production and highlight the integrated approach as a promising strategy for efficient lignocellulosic biomass conversion and agricultural waste valorization.

Article.Title: Addiction treatment providers’ perspectives on barriers to accessing addiction treatment in Scotland in the context of gender and age
Article.Authors: Ciesluk B.; Inglis G.; Parke A.; Troup L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Drug related deaths continue to cause an unprecedented public health crisis in Scotland. Addiction treatment services remain most effective at reducing these deaths, however there are still many individuals who stay hidden from this essential support. This vulnerability is especially found for women and older individuals. Therefore, this study aims to find the most prominent addiction treatment barriers in Scotland perceived by treatment providers, especially for those most vulnerable. Data were drawn from a large cross-sectional survey exploring views and experiences of 64 addiction treatment providers currently working in Scotland. Analyses of Variance (ANOVAs) were conducted using an adapted version of the Barriers to Treatment Inventory (BTI) to compare participants’ ratings of perceived barriers to treatment, identifying which were most prominent, and which varied by group (women vs men, older vs younger). To capture any further barriers, 22 open-ended responses were analysed using content analysis. Fear of treatment and privacy concerns were perceived as the most prominent barriers. Stigma was also perceived to hinder treatment access, with participants highlighting how biased views create limited options for harm-reduction services and service user’s lack of choice over their own care. Although most barriers were thought to affect both women and men, some gender differences emerged with women being perceived to experience more challenges overall, especially around gender-specific barriers (limited gender-specific programmes, limited childcare, gender-based trauma). Men were perceived to avoid treatment due to denial or avoidance, which was not found for women. Limited differences were found for age, but older individuals were perceived slightly more vulnerable to fear of treatment and time conflict. These findings help to establish the most prominent barriers to addiction treatment in Scotland, as perceived by treatment providers, and highlight targets for future research and developments in addiction treatment. Gender and age should be considered in future investigations to ensure development of targeted interventions, and focus should be on expanding gender-specific support, enhancing data protection and client centred care. This could limit fear, increase trust, options and choice of treatment among those seeking help, in turn improving treatment access for those most vulnerable.

Article.Title: A semi-discrete calibration-prediction framework for deposition uniformity in magnetron sputtering under complex magnetic fields
Article.Authors: Bian G.; Han B.; Deng B.; Gao F.; Zhang X.; Yang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uniform film thickness is an important requirement in magnetron sputtering, while achieving the desired deposition uniformity in practice often requires repeated adjustment of magnet positions followed by experimental deposition tests. To reduce such trial-and-error iterations, a semi-discrete calibration-prediction framework is developed to predict film-thickness distributions for different magnetic-field configurations. The horizontal magnetic flux density on the target is used to represent the spatial variation of the effective sputtering source, while sputtered-atom transport is described by an experimentally calibrated Gaussian deposition kernel. A key feature of the framework is that the calibration experiment does not require optimized deposition uniformity: a single deposition experiment under a convenient, non-optimized magnetic-field configuration can be used to determine the effective spreading parameter σ , after which alternative magnet configurations can be evaluated computationally before further experiments are performed. The framework is validated using Al magnetron sputtering experiments at 8 kW and 0.7 Pa under four magnetic-field configurations. The predicted thickness distributions agree well with the measurements, with a maximum relative error of 1.79% and MAPE values remaining below 1%. The proposed approach provides a rapid engineering tool for screening magnet configurations and reducing experimental iterations during magnetron sputtering system development and process optimization.

Article.Title: Quantum entanglement-assisted adaptive firewall intelligence for next-generation cybersecurity
Article.Authors: Senthil Kumar P.; Asha V.; Albalawi A.
Article.Abstract: Signature- and rule-based firewalls score packets one at a time against a fixed threshold, which leaves them weak against multi-stage attacks and drifting traffic. We present the final design and a complete re-evaluation of QEAFIS, a quantum-inspired architecture that places three modules around a simulated 7-qubit quantum neural network (QNN). Entanglement-Guided Inter-Packet Correlation (EGIPC) scores a session with the entropy of a dephased register qubit. Behavioral Fingerprint Memory (BFM) matches traffic against confirmed threats. Dynamic Threshold Adaptation (DTA) moves the decision threshold by stochastic-approximation descent on an explicit cost. Every result was regenerated on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 under de-duplicated, leakage-free partitions with up to ten seeds. The evaluation covers the end-to-end pipeline, a ten-configuration ablation, classical and neural sequence baselines, withheld attack categories, poisoning and drift tests, and per-stage latency. BFM with an admission guard and DTA on rank-calibrated scores gave practically meaningful gains: DTA lowered the post-shift error cost by 0.104 and 0.047, and on NSL-KDD the guard held the BFM false-positive rate at 1.0% with 20% of memory poisoned, against 68.7% without it. The quantum-inspired parts did not. We show that the EGIPC score is a classical sequential statistic. It matched a transition-weighted CUSUM, trailed LSTM, GRU, Transformer and TCN models by 0.23–0.28 AUROC on evasive NSL-KDD attacks, and saturated under distribution shift. The QNN detected no better than a classical network at about thirty times its per-event cost (about 1 ms), and withheld categories were detected unreliably. Earlier shadow-mode results are retained only as provisional.

Article.Title: Analytical interpretation and numerical assessment of vertical placement of repeated pressure-relief windows in a high-stress coal roadway rib surface-support layer
Article.Authors: Niu M.; Yan K.; Zheng X.; He Z.; Zhao Y.; Qin X.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Vertical placement of openings in passive rib surface support changes the local restraint on a deforming roadway rib. This study examines periodically repeated pressure-relief windows using a symmetry-based analytical interpretation and a layered FLAC3D model. Archived monitoring profiles cover six window-bottom elevations, while matched-control calculations compare four elevations on coarse, baseline and refined meshes, with an additional ultrafine no-window control. Spatial stress, displacement and coal plastic-state maps are reported alongside volume-based indicators. On the baseline mesh, changing the window-bottom elevation from 0.5 to 2.0 m gives model-wide maximum displacements of 57.48–65.21 mm and coal yielded fractions of 27.54–27.56%. The corresponding host-rock mean XX-stress changes relative to the no-window control range from $$-1.146$$ to $$-0.019$$ MPa, indicating stress shifts toward compression in the sampled slabs. Refinement produces larger changes in the global response than elevation adjustment, and the ultrafine control retains sensitivity in yielded fraction and near-rib mean stress. The results distinguish the local response to support-layer openings from the host-rock response and provide a basis for evaluating window placement together with mesh resolution and support stiffness.

Article.Title: DGS-CF: a DSM and sparse-view 3DGS co-optimization framework for georeferenced 3D building reconstruction
Article.Authors: Song J.; Dong Y.; Fan D.; Ji S.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Satellite-based DSMs enable large-scale 3D reconstruction but lack facade geometry. Existing methods rely on dense close-range images, incurring high costs and limited applicability. Addressing the challenge of facade geometry recovery for DSMs under sparse close-range images, we propose a DSM and Sparse-View 3DGS Co-Optimization Framework for Georeferenced 3D Building Reconstruction (DGS-CF). DGS-CF leverages DSMs to provide spatial priors that enhance Gaussian initialization quality. It augments the training samples through controllable view derivation, and employs a 3DGS that combines a depth-augmented view joint optimization with a dual‑Gaussian pruning strategy to achieve high fidelity recovery of the missing facade from extremely sparse-views. The completed 3D‑DSM preserves the georeferenced attribute of the original DSM, leading to georeferenced 3D building reconstruction. Experiments on public and self-collected data demonstrate that under only four views, our method outperforms the mainstream approaches with an average improvement of 21.73–27.91% in SSIM. Under the same initialization, the PSNR is increased at least 2.953 dB in the self-collected datasets with poorer DSM quality, while the restored 3D-DSM achieves improvements of at least 273.8% in quantity and 48.2% in accuracy. This research provides an effective technical pathway for 3D building reconstruction and facade geometry completion of DSMs from sparse-views.

Article.Title: KAYA identity-based modelling of carbon emissions in West Africa using interpretable quantum-optimised support vector regression
Article.Authors: Mati S.; Ismael G.; Ahmed A.; Usman A.; Ozsahin D.; Nadarajah S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions is vital for shaping sustainable environmental policies and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those linked to climate action. Guided by the KAYA-identity, which links emissions to population, economic activity, energy use, and technology, this study examines seven forecasting approaches for West Africa. It applies univariate methods such as the Autoregressive model (AR) and the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), alongside multivariate techniques including Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and SVR combined with Quantum Particle Swarm Optimisation (SVR-QPSO). For interpretability, Shapley values are used to assess the contribution of each variable within the models. Among all approaches, SVR-QPSO delivers the strongest predictive performance. In the training sample, SVR-QPSO lowers the forecasting error of AR by 95.81% for Côte d’Ivoire, 93.34% for Ghana, 97.05% for Nigeria, and 92.55% for Senegal. In the testing sample, it improves on AR by 96.67% for Côte d’Ivoire, 95.15% for Ghana, 97.82% for Nigeria, and 93.37% for Senegal. SVR-QPSO is identified as the leading model for Ghana and Nigeria, SVR performs best for Côte d’Ivoire, and MLP is the strongest for Senegal. The findings show that SVR-QPSO and MLP offer valuable support for future climate policy design aimed at strengthening environmental resilience.

Article.Title: Heterogeneous multimodal driver assistance using a Jetson Nano–ESP32 architecture
Article.Authors: Ali W.; Saleh H.; Eid H.; Fathi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-cost embedded advanced driver-assistance systems must combine heterogeneous perception and control functions within limited compute and memory budgets. We present a five-function robotic ADAS prototype that partitions vision and RGB-D association to an NVIDIA Jetson Nano while assigning ultrasonic blind-spot sensing, warnings and actuation to an ESP32. A single Astra Pro Plus RGB-D camera supplies forward color and depth for vehicle, traffic-sign, speed-bump and lane processing; two lateral HC-SR04 sensors provide the blind-spot path. The final 44-epoch ACC validation on 1,126 images (3,517 vehicle instances) produced precision 0.869, recall 0.823, mAP@0.5 = 0.889 and mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.684. The selected traffic-sign YOLOv5s configuration recorded 95.9% precision and 92.5% recall. For speed-bump detection, YOLOv5s recorded 94.2% precision, 91% recall and mAP@0.5 = 0.843 while using 91.7% fewer parameters and requiring 91.6% less storage than YOLOv5x. Lane and blind-spot tests provide functional demonstrations of sensing-to-warning and sensing-to-actuation paths. The study establishes architectural feasibility and subsystem-level experimental validation on a low-cost robotic prototype, not a road-certified vehicle; synchronized concurrent throughput, latency, processor utilization, memory, frame drops, power and thermal behavior remain unmeasured.

Article.Title: Molecular authentication of tobacco in complex processed matrices through short-amplicon SSR profiling
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Wang Y.; Luo A.; Feng X.; He S.; Zhang X.; Liu N.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Accurate identification of Nicotiana -derived materials in complex industrial degraded samples is critical for quality control, market regulation, and forensic authentication. However, conventional approaches based on sensory and chemical profiling are limited by subjective bias and exogenous interference, while most molecular marker systems are developed under high-quality genomic DNA, resulting in poor applicability to degraded industrial matrices. In this study, a molecular identification profiling based on short-amplicon simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers was developed through genome-wide mining and cross-species negative screening, enabling rapid and specific discrimination between Nicotiana -derived DNA from non- Nicotiana samples, while a washing pretreatment effectively eliminated interference from exogenous DNA and artificial additives. The robustness and practical applicability of the method were confirmed through validation across multiple sample matrices of different physical forms and taxonomic categories, including heated tobacco products, tobacco seeds, and tobacco-like materials, thus providing a reliable framework for screening and authentication of Nicotiana -derived materials in degraded industrial matrices.

Article.Title: Assessing Ga9N9 and In9N9 nanorings as toxic gas adsorbents: a comprehensive DFT analysis
Article.Authors: El-Tahawy M.; Abodom S.; Abdelghany A.; Garavelli M.; Aboelnga M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen oxide (NO) and ammonia (NH 3 ) are harmful gases that can adversely affect the environmental quality and human health, so it is important to find effective materials to detect and remove them. Here, we have investigated the interaction of gallium nitride (Ga 9 N 9 ) and indium nitride (In 9 N 9 ) nanorings with such toxic gases and their potential as gas sensing or capture materials using density functional theory (DFT). We find that the nature of the interaction is substantially affected by the type of gas. The NH 3 chemisorbs strongly to the two nanorings with adsorption energies of −1.46 eV on Ga 9 N 9 and − 1.13 eV on In 9 N 9 . This strong binding is manifested in pronounced structural changes, short adsorption distances, and a large charge transfer. In contrast, CO and NO interact only weakly through physisorption, with low adsorption energies and minimal effect on the nanoring structure. However, when we examined the electronic properties, three non-trivial insights emerged. First, although NO exhibits the weakest adsorption energy (− 0.19 to − 0.34 eV), it induces the largest electronic perturbation (HOMO-LUMO gap reduction from 3.74 to 2.63 eV) due to its unpaired electron and spin-polarization effects, demonstrating that strong binding is not required for high detectability. Second, water counterintuitively enhances NH 3 adsorption on Ga 9 N 9 (from − 1.46 to − 1.60 eV) due to differential solvation effects and electrostatic stabilization of the polar molecule. Third, the α and β spin channels of NO show dramatically different sensing responses (differing by ~ 10 4 ), suggesting potential for spin-selective gas detection. Thermodynamic calculations confirm that NH 3 adsorption is spontaneous and stable, while recovery time analysis shows that NH 3 desorbs very slowly at room temperature, making the nanorings more suitable for ammonia capture and storage than for reusable sensing. CO and NO, on the other hand, desorb quickly, which is ideal for reversible sensor applications. Overall, Ga 9 N 9 performs better than In 9 N 9 , showing stronger interactions and more pronounced electronic responses. These results position III-nitride nanorings as versatile materials that can be tailored either for capturing ammonia or for sensitively detecting NO, with the latter benefiting from NO’s strong electronic footprint despite weak binding, its anomalous solvation behavior, and its spin-selective response channels. Selectivity screening against common atmospheric gases (H 2 O, CO 2 , N 2 , O 2 ) confirms that NH 3 is preferentially adsorbed over all interferents on both nanorings and further reveals that singlet O 2 reacts destructively with In 9 N 9 , inserting into the ring via a new N–O bond, while leaving Ga 9 N 9 structurally intact, identifying Ga 9 N 9 as the more chemically robust and overall superior candidate material. Future computational studies should extend this framework by exploring larger nanoring sizes (e.g., X 12 N 12 , X 18 N 18 ), investigating the effects of heteroatom doping and edge functionalization on selectivity, and employing machine learning-accelerated DFT screening to identify optimal compositions for specific target gases.

Article.Title: RAG-LegalAssist: a retrieval-augmented framework with adaptive hybrid legal chunking for high-precision legal retrieval
Article.Authors: Gurusamy B.; Sathwik N.; Balaji T.; Koushik V.; Reddy N.
Article.Abstract: Legal documents are long, structurally complex, and semantically dense, which makes manual analysis and information retrieval time consuming and prone to error. Traditional keyword based retrieval methods often fail to capture the hierarchical and contextual dependencies of legal text. At the same time, standalone large language models are limited by context constraints and may generate unsupported or hallucinated outputs when processing long documents. To address these challenges, this paper proposes RAG LegalAssist, a retrieval augmented generation framework for legal question answering that incorporates an Adaptive Hybrid Legal Chunker. The proposed chunking method combines structure aware rule based segmentation, semantic similarity based splitting, and length constrained chunking. This design preserves legal boundaries while ensuring compatibility with model context limits. The system is evaluated on the European Court of Human Rights dataset containing about 11,000 legal judgments. Document segments are embedded using BGE embeddings and indexed with FAISS. Response generation is carried out using the Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct model. Experimental evaluation across multiple phases, including large scale query testing, query type analysis, prompt comparison, paraphrase robustness, and chunking strategy evaluation, shows strong performance. The system achieves a Precision@5 of 0.40, Recall@5 of 0.82, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) of 0.84, and nDCG@5 of 0.85. Generation evaluation shows Groundedness of 0.8749, Faithfulness of 0.9664, and a hallucination rate of 0.0000 under the adopted evaluation criterion.

Article.Title: Exploring the applicability of pix2pix for firing effect prediction of Jingdezhen high-temperature colored-glaze porcelain panels
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Guan J.; Zhang J.; Ning Y.
Article.Abstract: High-temperature colored-glaze ceramics are distinguished by their kiln-transformation, glaze-transformation, and flow effects. However, complex stochastic firing processes make their final appearance difficult to predict, hindering craft transmission and industrial development. This study investigated a pix2pix-based simulation framework for estimating the fired appearance of Jingdezhen high-temperature colored-glaze porcelain panels. Panels produced with fixed glaze combinations were represented by semantic segmentation maps as conditional inputs. VGG perceptual loss and instance-noise regularization were incorporated into pix2pix. Performance was assessed using five panel-level holdout validation splits, SSIM, LPIPS, and color-histogram correlation. The baseline model generated relatively realistic fired appearances within the training domain. Among combined-constraint configurations, L1 = 30, perc = 10, and noise enabled achieved the lowest LPIPS (0.2011) and a relatively high SSIM (0.5229), while suppressing some GAN texture artifacts. Nevertheless, performance deteriorated substantially on unseen samples, and generated images remained far below practical requirements. These findings indicate that pix2pix’s deterministic mapping struggles with the complex stochastic relationships involved in ceramic firing. Future work should investigate multimodal generative architectures integrated with materials-mechanism modeling to support reliable tools for craft transmission and industrial development.

Article.Title: Correlation of structural distortion with electrical and magnetic properties in Ho-doped BiFeO3
Article.Authors: Hredy T.; Hassan M.; Saha T.; Khan M.; Rashid R.; Alam M.
Article.Abstract: Holmium (Ho) doping is a promising strategy to tailor the multiferroic properties of bismuth ferrite (BiFeO 3 ). Here, we report a systematic study of Bi 1–x Ho x FeO 3 bulk ceramics (x = 0 to 0.10) synthesized by solid-state reaction. X-ray diffraction confirms that all samples retain the rhombohedral R3c perovskite structure, with only evidence of Bi 25 FeO 39 impurity. Increasing Ho content causes the unit cell to contract and the grain structure to refine. Magnetic measurements reveal that the room-temperature saturation magnetization rises dramatically from 0.143 emu g − 1 (x = 0) to 0.984 emu g − 1 (x = 0.10), indicating an enhancement of weak ferromagnetism via Ho substitution. The ferroelectric Curie temperature (T C ) of pure BiFeO 3 (~ 1000 K) decreases to 945 K at x = 0.10, reflecting a weakening of ferroelectric order. Dielectric spectroscopy shows Maxwell–Wagner interfacial polarization; all compositions exhibit a high dielectric constant and loss at low frequency, which diminish with increasing frequency. Notably, a Cole–Cole analysis for x = 0.06 reveals a single semicircular arc, consistent with grain-boundary–controlled conduction. Accordingly, Ho doping can improve the physical properties of BFO, providing profound insights into the design of low-loss multiferroic devices.

Article.Title: Longitudinal association between AI dependence and pre-service teachers’ critical thinking disposition: the role of AI self-efficacy and perceived stress
Article.Authors: Zhu M.; Yang Y.; Long Q.; Zhou Q.; Hu Z.
Article.Abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into teacher education has brought both opportunities and challenges. While AI tools are increasingly accessible to pre-service teachers, excessive dependence on AI may inadvertently undermine their critical thinking disposition—a key competency in professional development. Based on social cognitive theory, this study investigates the influence of AI dependence on pre-service teachers’ critical thinking disposition, with a particular focus on the mediating role of AI self-efficacy and the moderating role of perceived stress. A three-phase longitudinal design was employed. The study tracked 461 pre-service teachers from Jiangxi Province, China. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the hypothesized relationships, including the mediation effect of AI self-efficacy and the first-stage moderating effect of perceived stress. Results showed that AI dependence significantly and negatively predicted pre-service teachers’ critical thinking disposition. AI self-efficacy partially mediated this negative association. Furthermore, perceived stress significantly moderated the first stage of the mediation process, such that the negative association between AI dependence and AI self-efficacy was stronger among pre-service teachers with higher levels of perceived stress. The conditional indirect effect was stronger at higher levels of perceived stress, and the index of moderated mediation was significant. The second-stage moderation was not significant. These findings highlight the potential risks associated with excessive AI dependence in teacher education: over-reliance on AI may undermine pre-service teachers’ critical thinking disposition partly through reduced AI self-efficacy. Moreover, perceived stress amplifies the negative indirect effect by moderating the first stage of the mediation process. This study extends social cognitive theory to the context of AI use and provides practical implications for promoting balanced AI engagement and critical thinking development in teacher training programs.

Article.Title: Physiological and yield responses of cassava (Manihot esculenta Crantz) to irrigation
Article.Authors: Malik A.; Youabee L.; Oudthachit S.; Eberhard J.; Scobie M.; Seton S.; Newby J.; Nhan P.; Hung N.; Tung N.
Article.Abstract: Efficient irrigation is crucial for agriculture to boost crop production while reducing water use. Cassava ( Manihot esculenta Crantz) is known for its adaptability to water-limited environments but can produce markedly higher yields with supplemental irrigation. This study explored the physiological and yield responses of three cassava varieties to irrigation. Four field experiments were conducted in two countries (Lao PDR, Vietnam) over two growing seasons (2019–20 and 2021–22). Plots were arranged in a block design with four replicates. The varieties tested were KU50 and Rayong11 in Lao PDR, and KU50 and D7 in Vietnam, with treatments including irrigated and non-irrigated rainfed plots harvested at three stages: start of starch accumulation stage (1H, 6 to 9 months), end of starch accumulation stage (2H, 9 to 10 months), and starch accumulation completed and plant starts to shed leaves (3H, 10 to 13 months). With irrigation, both varieties in Lao PDR showed higher total biomass (20% to 60%), starch yield (20% to 35%) and greater harvest index (7% to 17%) compared to non-irrigated rainfed plots. Stomatal conductance, NDVI and chlorophyll fluorescence measured in Lao PDR in the 2021–22 season was 1.6 to 5.2-fold higher in irrigated plants compared to plants from non-irrigated rainfed plots leading to significant yield increase in the irrigated plots. Similar yield increase were observed in the irrigated plots compared to rainfed plots in Vietnam. Efficient irrigation increases tuber yields in cassava as the plants mature, highlighting the need for effective water management. Research on genotypes under different irrigation levels can inform better farming practices, enhancing productivity and resilience in changing climates.

Article.Title: Latent class analysis of oral frailty and associated factors among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Zhou Y.; Kang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) may exhibit different patterns of oral functional risk that may not be fully captured by total-score-based assessments of oral frailty. A three-class model was retained, comprising the low-risk/relatively preserved oral function class (54.2%), moderate-risk/denture-related masticatory impairment class (27.2%), and high-risk/multiple oral function impairments class (18.6%). Older age and a greater number of dentures were associated with membership in both higher-risk classes, whereas educational attainment and self-rated oral health showed associations that varied across latent classes. These patterns may inform more targeted oral health assessment and preventive oral health care in dialysis settings.

Article.Title: Divergent DSF-mediated quorum sensing responses in strains of the Stenotrophomonas maltophilia complex are independent of RpfF-RpfC REC domain structural association
Article.Authors: Ortiz J.; Conchillo-Solé O.; Bravo M.; Sánchez-Alba L.; Pons J.; Huedo P.; Coves X.; Gómez A.; Reverter D.; Gibert I.; Daura X.; Yero D.
Article.Abstract: In the Stenotrophomonas maltophilia complex (Smc), DSF-mediated quorum sensing regulates diverse behaviours through the Rpf system. In these species, the DSF/Rpf system occurs as two genetic variants, rpf-1 and rpf-2 , associated with distinct phenotypes. The first crystal structure of S. maltophilia RpfF-1 revealed a conserved crotonase-like architecture. Structural comparisons with an AlphaFold2-predicted model of RpfF-2 and modelled complexes with the RpfC receiver (REC) domain revealed a highly conserved RpfF–RpfC interaction interface across variants. Consistently, bacterial two-hybrid assays showed comparable RpfF–RpfC REC domain interaction signals in both variants. In contrast, RNA sequencing of rpfF and rpfC mutants revealed variation in downstream regulatory responses. While the rpf-1 strain displayed transcriptional profiles consistent with the canonical DSF/Rpf signalling pathway, the rpf-2 strain showed divergent transcriptional responses between mutants, suggesting an alternative RpfF-dependent regulatory axis. Motility-associated genes emerged as a major source of regulatory divergence. Together, our findings indicate that differences between the rpf-1 and rpf-2 variants are not readily explained by RpfF–RpfC REC domain association alone and may involve divergent downstream regulatory responses and additional RpfF-dependent functions.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a prediction model for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in young and middle-aged adults: a population-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Yan B.; Li Y.; Xiao J.; Zhu M.; Gao X.; Zhang Y.; Han T.; Zhou J.
Article.Abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is now the most common chronic liver disease, affecting 38% of adults worldwide. This study aimed to establish and validate a prediction model for NAFLD in the young and middle-aged Chinese adults, and provide a basis for early screening and timely intervention. A total of 966 healthy subjects, aged 18–59 years, were recruited for physical examination at our health management center within a tertiary hospital. The subjects were randomly divided into a training set ( n = 676) and a validation set ( n = 290) in a 7:3 ratio. A multiple logistic regression model was utilized to identify independent risk factors for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and to develop a nomogram prediction model. The predictive performance of the nomogram was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis (ROC), the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The developed nomogram incorporated five clinical variables: body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), triglycerides (TG), and serum uric acid (SUA). The area under the ROC curve (AUROC) for the training set was 0.903 (95% CI 0.881 to 0.925), while the validation set yielded an AUROC of 0.907 (95% CI 0.872 to 0.942). Calibration curves demonstrated a significant agreement between predicted and actual outcomes, indicating that the nomogram possesses excellent accuracy. DCA curve analysis further confirmed the clinical utility of the developed prediction nomogram. Our validated prediction nomogram, based on physical examination and laboratory indicators, effectively predicts NAFLD. It serves as a rapid screening tool for assessing NAFLD in young and middle-aged individuals.

Article.Authors: Shirkey G.; Yokoyama G.; Fu L.; Agatep A.; Camacho-Umaña M.; Dauber G.; Deering C.; Doughty C.; Espeleta J.; Hatch H.; Jia M.; Nelson K.; Pivovaroff A.; van Riper S.; Schwandner F.; Snyder M.; Terrer C.; Vargas Murillo J.; Zalman C.; Goldsmith G.; O’Connell C.; Fisher J.

Neither in-situ nor CLM5 R d were correlated with elevated CO 2 . CLM5 underestimated stem CO 2 and CH 4 efflux by 141% and 200%, respectively, whereas it underestimated R d by 14–34%. Article.Authors: Labra A.; Retamales K.; Rojas I.; Aliaga A.; Souper R.; Otaola H.; Bernier P.; Pinochet R.; Orvieto M.; Eltit I.

Article.Title: Innovative contactless dual-coupled microwave sensor for non-invasive blood glucose monitoring
Article.Authors: Elgeddawy R.; El-Hameed A.; Eldamak A.; Elhenawy H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, a novel non-invasive blood glucose monitoring system based on microwave sensing using a compact, contactless and sensitive dual-coupled sensor configuration is proposed. The proposed sensor consists of two electromagnetically coupled resonators, configured as a bandpass filter centered around 2.2 GHz. The sensor is fabricated on a 40 × 40 mm 2 Rogers RO3003C substrate with a 20 mm gap between the resonators to accommodate different finger sizes and incorporates a dedicated mechanical isolation structure to minimize measurement variability caused by direct contact, applied pressure, and positioning uncertainty. The operation of the sensor is based on near-field electromagnetic coupling between the resonators and biological tissue, enabling detection of glucose-correlated variations in dielectric properties without direct skin contact. The experimental trials for glucose concentrations from 76 to 201 mg/dL showed a monotonic decrease in the transmission coefficient with increasing glucose concentration with a sensitivity of 0.031 dB/mg/dL and frequency shift sensitivity of 0.41 MHz/mg/dL. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed sensor and indicate the feasibility of sensitive contactless glucose monitoring using a microwave-based sensor.

Article.Title: Magnetized drainage water and nano-NPK improve sugar beet productivity and water-use efficiency in saline clayey soils
Article.Authors: Abou El-Enin M.; Elgamal I.; Abd El-Razek U.; Badawy A.; El-Safy N.; Abou Tahoun A.; Shaghaleh H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sugar beet ( Beta vulgaris L.) cultivation under saline conditions in the Egyptian Nile Delta faces persistent yield penalties from both irrigation water quality and soil ionic load. This study examined whether magnetized agricultural drainage-blended water (MDBW) and foliar nano-NPK fertilization could jointly address these constraints. The MDBW × 600 mg L −1 nano-NPK combination reached the highest root yield (72.98 t ha −1 ) and sucrose content (19.71%), while cutting the blue water footprint by 35.4% and returning a benefit–cost ratio of 6.53. Significant Water × Nano-NPK interactions were detected for some response variables. The combined treatment produced the highest observed values, but the present design does not establish biological synergism. These results indicate that MDBW combined with foliar nano-NPK may improve sugar beet productivity under the conditions evaluated here.

Article.Title: Pro/Ala/Ser (PAS) peptides as an alternative to polyethylene glycol (PEG) for the surface shielding of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) carrying therapeutic mRNA
Article.Authors: Makbul C.; Friedrich L.; Binder U.; Skerra A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), comprising a mixture of cationic lipids, neutral phospholipids, cholesterol and, in particular, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-conjugated lipids on their surface, have emerged as a powerful technology to encapsulate and deliver protein-encoding mRNAs as modern vaccines or for therapeutic intervention. However, the common use of PEG for surface shielding of mRNA-LNPs has raised concerns, especially in the light of a growing prevalence of anti-PEG antibodies in the healthy population. PASylation offers a biological alternative to the chemical PEG polymer, employing recombinant or synthetic (poly)peptides made of the small natural L-amino acids Pro, Ala and Ser which, in contrast to PEG, are biodegradable. PAS sequences are conformationally disordered, fully uncharged but strongly solvated and, thus, closely match the biophysical properties of PEG chains. Based on this notion, we synthesized a novel PASylated lipid, Pga-PAS 40 -ditetradecylamine (PAS-DTA), by replacing the PEG moiety in a clinically approved PEG-lipid (ALC-0159) with a 40mer PAS peptide N-terminally protected with pyroglutamate (Pga). mRNA-LNPs were formulated with this PASylated lipid, adopting a published procedure for conventional LNPs, and their properties were compared with those prepared using common PEG-lipids. In addition, cultured HepG2 and HEK293E cells transfected with the PASylated mRNA-LNPs encoding either enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) or PAS 200 -mIFNα11 showed robust expression of both recombinant proteins. Furthermore, in a side-by-side experiment with HepG2 cells transfected with mRNA-LNPs that were prepared using PAS-DTA or two different PEG-lipids, comparable or slightly higher amounts of secreted PAS 200 -mIFNα11 were detected in the culture supernatant both by western blotting and ELISA. Taken together, our in vitro data indicate that PAS-lipids offer a viable alternative to PEG-lipids for the preparation of mRNA-LNPs, without immunochemical cross-reactivity but with potentially better tolerability for the transfected target cells.

Article.Authors: Fouda S.; S. Alnasser A.; Abbas M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract One of the biggest challenges in wastewater restoration is the creation of effective, stable, and environmentally safe photocatalysts for the breakdown of persistent organic pollutants. Electron microscopy demonstrated the uniform dispersion of graphene sheets throughout the silica network, while XRD and FTIR investigations verified the effective integration of graphene into the silica matrix without the formation of secondary crystalline phases. Optical studies showed that the electronic structure of silica was successfully altered by graphene inclusion, resulting in increased degredation of visible light and decreased band-gap energy. Under the same experimental settings, the photocatalytic capabilities of the produced nanocomposites were assessed in relation to the degradation of amoxicillin and Eosin dye. The silica@(2 g graphene) nanocomposite (S 7 ) had the best photocatalytic effectiveness and the biggest apparent pseudo-first-order rate constants of 1.966 × 10⁻ 2 min⁻ 1 for amoxicillin and 3.116 × 10⁻ 2 min⁻ 1 for eosin dye among all produced samples. The enhanced activity is explained by the synergistic interaction between conductive graphene and amorphous silica, which accelerates the production of reactive oxygen species, inhibits electron–hole recombination, and encourages effective charge separation. These results show that sol–gel-synthesized silica@ graphene nanocomposites are potential photocatalysts for the effective removal of dye molecules and new pharmaceutical pollutants from aqueous environments.

Article.Authors: Mutailifu M.; Sailaijiang M.; Wang X.; Zhang Y.; Chen D.; Xie K.

These findings demonstrate that BmATG5/6/8 participate in Pb-induced autophagy and apoptosis, and that proteolytic processing of BmATG5/6 may serve as a regulatory node associated with the transition from cytoprotective autophagy to pro-apoptotic signaling under escalating Pb stress. This study provides new mechanistic insights into heavy metal toxicity in insects and supports the silkworm as a valuable model for environmental toxicology.

Article.Abstract: Postoperative complications occur in 30–60% of patients after esophagectomy and are poorly predicted by conventional staging. Dual-Hit was associated with overall (OR 2.63, 95% CI 1.09–6.33, P = 0.031) and severe complications (OR 2.86, 95% CI 1.21–6.79, P = 0.017) after adjustment for six clinical covariates. The prediction models had apparent C-indices of 0.763 and 0.777, with bootstrap-corrected values of 0.721 and 0.735. Adding Dual-Hit to the clinical models yielded small apparent AUC increases, with confidence intervals that included zero. The Dual-Hit phenotype was associated with postoperative complications in this cohort, but its incremental predictive value beyond clinical variables was small and uncertain. These exploratory findings require independent validation before clinical application.

These results indicate that NeuroNet-X is a technically sound decision-support framework for brain tumor categorization. However, the model was evaluated solely on retrospective 2D public benchmark datasets, and clinical deployment would require external multi-center validation, patient-level splitting, volumetric analysis, and clinician-in-the-loop reader studies.

Overlap in the 0–60 min zone exceeded two spatial null models; the zone ranking held under alternative baseline nights, most implementation settings and most alternative metrics, whereas the level of the index depends on the smoothing radius and on the set of input cells. The event night had 22–24% more stays per cell than the baseline night, with spatially clustered net population. These aggregate patterns are consistent with a staging role of districts within about one hour of transit travel, although the mechanism itself cannot be confirmed with aggregate data; 60 min is proposed as an operational reference range, not an optimum.
