Article.Title: A shifted gamma–logistic transmuted distribution with properties and applications to process monitoring via CUSUM control charts
Article.Authors: Hasaballah M.; Braimah J.; Nnamdi E.; Bakr M.; Tashkandi N.; Tashkandy Y.
Article.Abstract: We introduce the shifted gamma–logistic transmuted (SGLT) distribution, obtained by applying the quadratic rank transmutation map (QRTM) to a shifted, power-transformed logistic baseline that coincides with the power half-logistic law. Closed-form expressions are derived for the cdf, pdf, reliability and hazard functions, quantile function, moments, moment generating function and order statistics. The three parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood; the score equations were re-derived and checked against finite differences, and standard errors come from the observed information. A Monte Carlo study ( N = 1000 replications) shows that mean squared errors decrease with the sample size, but that the transmutation parameter is poorly determined for n ≤ 100. A two-sided likelihood-ratio CUSUM chart for SGLT observations is constructed, with the decision interval calibrated by simulation to an in-control average run length of 370. On two industrial datasets the SGLT attains the lowest AIC and BIC among the eight models of the original comparison (Tables 2 and 3), but its λ = 0 sub-model attains lower values still, the likelihood-ratio test does not reject λ = 0, and bootstrap-calibrated KS, CvM and AD tests reject the SGLT fit for the glass-fibre data while not rejecting it for the carbon-fibre data. The results delimit what the added transmutation parameter does and does not contribute.

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving, low-annotation pregnancy status classification from obstetric ultrasound reports using on-premises small language models
Article.Authors: Neveditsin N.; Patil S.; Patil S.; Lingras P.; Mago V.
Article.Abstract: Ultrasound reports in obstetric care provide information about the status of the pregnancy which is essential for clinical informatics purposes. This information, however, is buried in free text. We evaluated seven frozen small language models with 3–4 billion parameters, run on-premises, on 628 MIMIC-IV reports and 340 reports processed with OCR from one Indian clinical site. The models were used to classify the reports as early active pregnancy, late active pregnancy, or no active pregnancy with a 14-week operational boundary and a labeling scheme based on management status. With 12 in-context exemplars, a seven-model committee achieved a macro F1 of 0.9622 on MIMIC-IV and 0.9814 on the Indian OCR cohort. When MIMIC-IV exemplars were transferred to the Indian OCR cohort, performance did not differ detectably from that obtained with Indian OCR cohort exemplars in a paired bootstrap test. We also investigated how to reduce labeling burden and introduced a probability-guided exemplar selection procedure. The procedure converted 95–98% of annotation effort into usable balanced prompt exemplars, compared with 52–66% under random sampling. These retrospective results support pregnancy-status extraction with human review in low-annotation settings where data remain on-premises, without fine-tuning or offsite data transfer.

Article.Title: Limosilactobacillus reuteri KUB-AC5 partially attenuates metabolic disturbance but has limited effects on submandibular gland alterations in obese rats
Article.Authors: Chunchai T.; Pintana H.; Aroonsingkarat N.; Kittikunkanyakit P.; Wongcharee P.; Prommetjit P.; Thiennimitr P.; Chattipakorn N.; Chattipakorn S.
Article.Abstract: Obese​ insulin resistance (OIR) is associated with submandibular gland pathology, fibrosis, and molecular alterations. Although probiotics have shown protective effects on the gut and other vulnerable organs, their impact on submandibular gland pathology under OIR conditions remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether administration of the probiotic, Limosilactobacillus reuteri ( formerly Lactobacillus reuteri) KUB-AC5, reduces metabolic disturbance and attenuates submandibular gland pathology in OIR rats. Thirty-two male Wistar rats were acclimated for one week (week 0–1). Thirty male Wistar rats were included in the final analysis, as two rats assigned to the NDV group were excluded before initiation of the experimental protocol. Then, all rats were fed either a normal diet or a high-fat diet for 24 weeks (week 1–25). From week 13, rats were subdivided to receive PBS or Limosilactobacillus reuteri KUB-AC5 (1 × 10⁸ CFU/day in 1 mL of PBS by oral gavage for 12 weeks) until week 25 (week 13–25). Next, metabolic parameters and submandibular gland (SMG) pathology were evaluated. Limosilactobacillus reuteri KUB-AC5 administration reduced body weight and insulin resistance, but did not significantly decrease total cholesterol levels in OIR rats. The high-fat diet-fed rats treated with vehicle (HFV) displayed SMG pathology, characterized by decreased antioxidant levels, altered expression of selected mitochondrial-related genes, elevated proinflammatory cytokine, and increased fibrotic area. At the dose and treatment duration used in the present study, Limosilactobacillus reuteri KUB-AC5 improved selected systemic parameters but was not associated with statistically significant improvements in the major molecular and histological alterations evaluated in the SMG of OIR rats. In conclusion, Limosilactobacillus reuteri KUB-AC5 partially reduced systemic metabolic disturbances in OIR rats. However, these effects were not accompanied by statistically significant improvements in SMG pathology, fibrosis, or associated molecular alterations under the present experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Vibration characteristics of light goods vehicles during second-echelon pharmaceutical wholesale distribution in Japan
Article.Authors: Hashimoto K.; Tamura M.; Inomata T.; Mawaribuchi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transportation-induced vibrations can cause product damage and failure. Although vibration environments under real transportation conditions have been investigated using large vehicles employed in first-echelon distribution, studies focusing on light goods vehicles (LGVs) used in second-echelon distribution remain limited. This study aimed to characterize the vibration levels and frequency characteristics of LGVs under real transportation conditions in Tokyo, Japan. Under real transportation conditions, vibration data were collected using three types of LGVs (NV100, NV200, and NV350) on two pharmaceutical distribution routes from wholesalers’ offices to medical institutions in Japan (five runs per vehicle per route). Vibration levels and frequency characteristics were evaluated using root-mean-square acceleration ( G rms ), empirical cumulative distribution functions (ECDFs), probability density functions (PDFs), and power spectral density (PSD) analysis. The vibration levels of LGVs were lower than those previously reported in other countries. NV100, a kei car unique to Japan and widely used in second-echelon distribution, exhibited higher vibration levels than NV200 and NV350 in all directions. Furthermore, route-specific differences in vibration frequency characteristics were observed for NV100. These differences may be associated with vehicle structural characteristics, including lower body weight, shorter wheelbase, and narrower tread width. The results suggest that both vibration magnitude and vibration frequency characteristics should be considered when evaluating transportation environments. These findings provide repeated field-derived vibration data for second-echelon LGV distribution, characterize route-dependent variability under routine transportation conditions, and may support future transportation-environment assessments and the development of transportation testing protocols.

Article.Title: SEC23B variants and mRNA expression defects in congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type II: comprehensive analysis in an Indian cohort
Article.Authors: Saptarshi A.; Nemani S.; Aggarwal M.; Jain S.; Seth B.; Dongerdiye R.; More T.; Kamble P.; Kedar P.
Article.Abstract: Congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type II (CDA II) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the SEC23B gene, characterised by moderate to severe anaemia, jaundice, and splenomegaly, primarily due to ineffective erythropoiesis and haemolysis. Complications include iron overload and gallstone formation. This study aimed to characterise the clinical, haematological, and molecular features of CDA II patients and to evaluate the impact of SEC23B variants on mRNA expression as supportive evidence of pathogenicity. A total of 29 CDA II cases were identified. Clinically, patients presented with pallor, icterus, splenomegaly, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia. Haematological analysis revealed hypochromic microcytic anaemia with spherocytes in peripheral smears, with a mean haemoglobin level of 7.54 ± 2.00 g/dL, indicating moderate to severe anaemia. Bone marrow examination showed erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoiesis, including > 10% binucleated erythroblasts and karyorrhexis. Serum ferritin was elevated in the majority of patients, consistent with iron overload. Targeted next-generation sequencing identified 13 SEC23B variants. The most frequent mutation, c.1385 A > G (p.Tyr462Cys), was observed in 19 patients in the homozygous state. Two novel variants, including a splice-site mutation (c.2148 + 1G > T) and a nonsense mutation (p.Gln220Ter), were identified and supported by in silico analyses. Quantitative real-time PCR demonstrated reduced SEC23B mRNA levels in all patients, with greater reduction in compound heterozygous patients. One patient underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, three underwent splenectomy, and others were managed with transfusion support. This study expands the mutational spectrum of SEC23B in Indian CDA II patients and highlights the value of gene expression analysis in strengthening variant interpretation and improving diagnostic precision in rare inherited anaemias.

Article.Title: Routine blood-derived inflammatory and metabolic indices in diabetic patients with and without documented cardiovascular comorbidities: a large retrospective exploratory study
Article.Authors: Kovács–Deák B.; Kovács B.; Boda F.; Mikes I.; Kolcsár M.; Fülöp I.; Kelemen P.; Nagy E.
Article.Abstract: Routine blood-derived inflammatory and metabolic indices are increasingly investigated as accessible markers of cardiometabolic status in diabetes. However, their clinical interpretation in large retrospective datasets remains challenging, particularly when statistically significant differences may not correspond to meaningful discrimination. This study evaluated cross-sectional differences in routinely available laboratory indices between patients with diabetes with and without documented cardiovascular comorbidity (CVC) and explored their ability to distinguish the two existing clinical groups. A retrospective exploratory analysis was performed using laboratory and diagnostic data from 7034 patients. Patients were classified as diabetes mellitus without documented CVC (DM, n = 5114) or diabetes with documented CVC (DM + CVC, n = 1920). Routine laboratory variables and derived indices, including triglyceride/glucose index (TyG index), monocyte-to-HDL ratio (MHR), triglyceride-to-HDL ratio (THR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), pan-immune inflammation value and its haemoglobin normalised index (PIV, PIV/Hb), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were evaluated using univariable comparisons, robust effect-size estimates, FDR-adjusted multivariable linear and logistic regression, exploratory threshold-based odds ratios, and cross-validated machine-learning classification. Exploratory classifiers were evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation with fold-specific preprocessing and class-imbalance-aware performance measures. Given the predominance of primary hypertension within the heterogeneous DM + CVC group, a complementary primary analysis excluded patients whose only documented cardiovascular comorbidity was hypertension. Several parameters differed significantly between DM and DM + CVC groups; however, most effect sizes were negligible or small. MPV and PDW showed comparatively larger haematological differences than the other parameters, but their limited effect sizes indicated substantial overlap between the groups. In adjusted analyses, higher PDW, TyG, MHR, THR, and MLR were associated with higher odds of existing DM + CVC status, whereas higher MPV, SIRI, and NLR were associated with lower odds. Most effect sizes remained negligible or small. After exclusion of hypertension-only patients, MHR, THR, SIRI, NLR, and MLR retained the same direction and statistical interpretation, whereas TyG was attenuated and PIV/Hb became significant. Machine-learning discrimination was poor to modest, with ROC AUC values of 0.544–0.668 and balanced accuracy of 0.526–0.599, with Naïve Bayes modelling being the most balanced among the evaluated models, although still insufficient for individual-level classification. Routine blood-derived indices provide useful population-level information on inflammatory and cardiometabolic laboratory patterns in diabetes, but most markers showed limited stand-alone discriminatory value for documented CVC. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation using longitudinal outcomes, complete clinical and medication data, and formal assessment of incremental clinical utility.

Article.Title: Dragon fruit peel waste-derived iron nanozyme with peroxidase-like activity for smartphone-assisted colorimetric detection of urinary uric acid
Article.Authors: Saithongksam N.; Sirivatanapa J.; Thongkliang Y.; Bunchuay T.; Kannasoot P.; Duangiad P.; Morales N.; Hemstapat R.; Ojida A.; Wongkongkatep J.
Article.Abstract: Uric acid monitoring is important for the early identification and management of hyperuricemia, which is linked to gout and an increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Turning agricultural and food-processing waste into useful functional materials also offers a more sustainable path for developing low-cost analytical tools. Here, we developed a simple colorimetric method for detecting uric acid using a nanozyme made from dragon fruit peel, an abundant agricultural waste material. This nanozyme mimics the activity of natural peroxidase enzymes, converting a colorless substrate into a blue-colored product in the presence of hydrogen peroxide. Uric acid was found to inhibit this colorimetric reaction, with the intensity of the blue color decreasing as uric acid concentration increased. The colorimetric assay exhibited a linear response over a uric acid concentration range of 0–100 µM, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.49 µM. The method was applied to uric acid detection in rat urine samples using a smartphone camera for colorimetric readout. High concentration of calcium and magnesium ions were found to cause some interference with uric acid detection. These findings support the use of dragon fruit peel-derived nanozymes as a practical platform for affordable, point-of-care uric acid monitoring.

Article.Title: Multi-modal machine learning for real-time quality monitoring in smart medical logistics production
Article.Authors: Arif M.; Tanvir M.; Nadia N.; Rabby H.; Aung Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient and reliable medical logistics systems are vital for ensuring the timely delivery of life-saving resources such as medicines, vaccines, and emergency supplies. However, existing monitoring frameworks often treat operational, environmental, and behavioral data streams in isolation, limiting their ability to capture the complex interactions that drive delays. This paper proposes a novel multi-modal machine learning framework for real-time quality monitoring in smart medical logistics production. The approach integrates heterogeneous data sources, including IoT sensor measurements, categorical shipment descriptors, and temporal event sequences, within a unified deep learning architecture that combines embedding layers, temporal encoders, and attention mechanisms. To ensure trustworthy decision support, the framework incorporates calibration strategies, cost-sensitive evaluation, and regularization techniques, yielding reliable probability estimates and accurate predictions. Experimental evaluation on two real-world logistics datasets shows that the model achieves 88.9% accuracy, an F1-score of 0.823, and well-calibrated probability estimates (Brier score 0.131, expected calibration error (ECE) 0.041), with reduced false alarms (0.072/h) and a longer predictive lead time (15.9 min). It also provides accurate regression-based delay estimation (MAE 8.9 min, RMSE 14.7 min) and strong cross-dataset generalization (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.832). These results highlight the predictive superiority and practical value of the framework in reducing false alarms, extending predictive lead times, and providing actionable insights for high-stakes medical supply chains. This work establishes the potential of multimodal learning to enhance resilience and responsiveness in healthcare logistics, offering a pathway toward more intelligent, adaptive supply chain management.

Article.Title: Fuel efficiency gains, market restructuring and rising fuel consumption in global passenger aviation (1996–2025)
Article.Authors: Dobruszkes F.; Mattioli G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fuel or GHG emission efficiency improvements are a key part of aircraft manufacturers’ narratives about their commitment to climate mitigation. However, climate impact depends on absolute emissions, and therefore on the amount of fuel burnt. The latter depends on several parameters, including traffic volumes, distances flown, fleet mix and seat density aboard. This calls for a joint assessment of the combined effect of technological progress, fleet renewal, market restructuring and traffic growth on the fuel consumption. Considering the global provision of regular passenger air services in 1996 and 2025, we find that fuel efficiency improved by 44% (as fuel intensity declined by 31%, from 32 to 22 g/available seat- kilometre), thanks to the introduction of newer aircraft, as well as changes in aircraft size, distance flown and seat density. Meanwhile, air traffic tripled (+ 8,037 billion available seat-kilometres), mostly due to more second/latest-generation aircraft being operated on medium-/long-haul routes. Consequently, the modelled amount of fuel burned has doubled (+ 139 million tonnes). This suggests that fuel savings from the phase-out of older aircraft were more than offset by the traffic increase associated with the deployment of newer aircraft, a dynamic that is insufficient to reduce the climate impact of passenger aviation.

Article.Title: Assistive technologies on safety monitoring for community-dwelling persons living with dementia
Article.Authors: Lee K.; Cho A.; You J.; Lee J.; Choi Y.; Lee S.; Yang E.
Article.Abstract: Individuals with dementia face safety-related incidents at home. However, research predicting such incidents using assistive technologies is limited. This observational study explored the feasibility of a machine learning approach using penalized logistic regression to predict safety-related incidents among community-dwelling persons living with dementia. From July 2021 to October 2022 in South Korea, 67 dyads of persons with dementia and their caregivers provided surveys, a 14-day safety diary, Actiwatch2 actigraphy, and smart motion sensor data. As the target was whether a dyad had experienced any incident during the window, the analysis was conducted at the participant level, with each dyad contributing one observation. A penalized logistic regression model was trained using cross-validation grouped by participants. Discrimination was summarized by the area under the curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CI). A clinical baseline model predicted which dyads experienced an incident (AUC 0.726, 95% CI 0.591–0.845); adding sensor summaries, sleep (actigraphy) summaries, or both did not improve discrimination (all AUC ≤ 0.703). Neuropsychiatric symptoms and the number of medications were the strongest predictors, whereas technology-derived features contributed little. These exploratory findings suggest potential feasibility rather than clinical readiness, and require confirmation in larger, properly powered, externally validated studies.

Article.Title: Design and additive manufacturing of nonlinear graded joints between austenitic and ferritic-martensitic steels
Article.Authors: Nandwana P.; Kannan R.; Nayir S.; Jordan B.; Wang H.; Sridharan N.; Srivastava A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Welds between austenitic stainless (SS347H) and ferritic-martensitic (P91) steels are commonly used in power-generation systems. However, differences in their properties, such as thermal expansion coefficients and carbon chemical potentials, often lead to premature failure. While additive manufacturing (AM) of compositionally graded transition joints (GTJs) offers a promising solution, most prior efforts have relied on linear composition gradients, which can be suboptimal. In this work, we use thermo-kinetic modeling to design, and blown powder directed energy deposition (BP–DED) to fabricate, a nonlinear GTJ between the two steels. The CALPHAD calculations show that nonlinear composition gradients reduce carbon chemical potential gradients across the joint compared to linear composition gradients thereby enhancing thermal stability of the joint. The fabricated nonlinear joint exhibited an average yield strength of $$\:478\pm\:16\:\text{M}\text{P}\text{a}$$ , comparable to or exceeding that of the two base materials. Pressurized creep testing on a tubular assembly comprising of GTJ welded to SS347H and P91 on either side showed failure after $$\:967$$ hours in the P91 region, while the nonlinear GTJ remained intact. This approach provides a pathway for designing high-performance nonlinear GTJs for other technologically critical material systems.

Article.Title: Reconfigured boundaries: the dynamics of emotion expression in social-media users reporting a depression diagnosis
Article.Authors: Bucur A.; Koosha T.; Cosma A.; Flek L.; Shariatpanahi B.; Thanarajah S.; Bernhard F.; Rosso P.; Jamalabadi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emotions are multidimensional and dynamic: emotions persist, interact, and change in relation to everyday events. Depression-related differences may therefore emerge both in ongoing emotional dynamics and in responses to particular experiences. Here, we examined both levels using more than 400,000 social-media posts from 1,690 users, including 871 users reporting a depression diagnosis and 819 comparison users without an observed depression-related disclosure. A transformer-based language model inferred normalized probability distributions across 28 emotion-expression dimensions from each post. We then fitted user-specific linear dynamical models using Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control to characterize post-to-post dynamics and estimate the modeled influence of detected positive life events. Our analyses revealed distinct, emotion-specific patterns of persistence and propagation across the broader emotional landscape. In users reporting a depression diagnosis, these ongoing dynamics were fundamentally reconfigured: the distinct roles of several emotions blurred, while others shifted in opposing directions. This points to a reorganization of emotional boundaries rather than a simple increase in negativity or a uniform flattening of affect. In contrast, immediate responses to positive life events remained largely preserved after correcting for post count. Together, these findings suggest that depression-related differences manifest primarily as a structural reconfiguration of baseline emotional dynamics rather than a dampened capacity to respond to positive events.

Article.Title: Progressive Whole-body vibration plus exercise is associated with quality-of-life gains without detectable inflammatory changes in sarcopenic older adults
Article.Authors: Altaf S.; Malmir K.; Mir S.; Olyaei G.; Aftab A.; Rajput T.
Article.Abstract: Sarcopenia is associated with reduced quality of life and chronic low-grade inflammation. Whole-body vibration (WBV) training offers a gentler alternative to strenuous exercise for older adults, but its effects on sarcopenia-specific QoL, inflammation, and potential sex-specific differences remain unclear. This study examined whether progressive WBV combined with active exercise could improve these outcomes in older adults with sarcopenia. In this assessor-blinded trial, 60 sarcopenic adults (≥ 60 years) were randomized into control and intervention groups, stratified by sex. Four participants withdrew after the baseline assessment, leaving 56 participants in the final analysis. The intervention group (14 men, 14 women) performed active exercises combined with vibration at increasing frequencies (15–40 Hz) over 8 weeks. The control group (14 men, 14 women) performed the same exercises without vibration. Sarcopenia Quality of Life (SarQoL), IL-6 (Interleukin-6), and ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) were measured before, after 8 weeks of intervention, and at 8 weeks follow-up. No time × group × sex interaction remained significant after Holm adjustment (largest unadjusted effect: ADLs, F(1.576, 81.962) = 3.83, p = 0.035; Holm-adjusted p = 0.352; ηp² = 0.069). Overall time × group effects remained significant for Physical and Mental Health (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), Locomotion (0.042), Functionality (< 0.001), ADLs (< 0.001), Leisure Activities (< 0.001), Fears (0.001), and Total SarQoL (< 0.001), but not for Body Composition, IL-6, or ESR. In sex-stratified analyses, significant effects remained in men for Physical and Mental Health (0.032), Functionality (< 0.001), and Total SarQoL (0.008), and in women for Physical and Mental Health (0.001), Locomotion (0.008), Functionality (0.006), ADLs (< 0.001), Leisure Activities (< 0.001), Fears (0.014), and Total SarQoL (< 0.001). These findings were descriptive and did not establish a sex-dependent treatment effect. At post-intervention and follow-up, 100% of WBV participants versus 78.6% and 64.3% of controls, respectively, achieved the selected 9-point Total SarQoL responder threshold. No significant intervention effects were detected for IL-6 or ESR. Progressive WBV combined with active exercise was associated with greater improvements in several sarcopenia-specific quality-of-life outcomes than active exercise alone, while the primary analysis did not demonstrate a statistically significant sex-dependent differential response. No statistically significant additional change in IL-6 or ESR was detected. The 9-point threshold was used as a responder threshold rather than as a universally established MCID. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to clarify the added value of WBV, the durability of quality-of-life changes, and possible biological effects on inflammation in older adults with sarcopenia.

Article.Title: Expanding the genetic spectrum of hereditary polyposis syndromes: a multicenter study from Argentina
Article.Authors: Soarez J.; Olkinuora A.; Mayordomo A.; Coraglio M.; Collia Ávila K.; Piñero T.; Kalfayan P.; González M.; Yonamine K.; Garona J.; García-Rivello H.; Vaccaro C.; Nieminen T.; Peltomäki P.; Pavicic W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hereditary polyposis syndromes (HPS) predispose to colorectal cancer, yet their genetic landscape in Argentina remains underrepresented. We analyzed 177 individuals from 163 unrelated families recruited through three Argentine reference centers, including 169 index cases and eight affected relatives evaluated for segregation analyses. Genetic testing included APC and MUTYH analysis by Sanger sequencing and MLPA, complemented by multigene panels and whole-exome sequencing (WES). Variants were classified following ACMG/AMP guidelines. Germline APC variants were identified in 75/177 individuals (42.4%), biallelic MUTYH variants in 8 (4.5%), and alterations in BMPR1A and SMAD4 in two index cases each. Within the APC -positive subset, 52 unique germline variants were detected, including seven novel truncating frameshift mutations and six large genomic rearrangements. Segregation analysis supported pathogenicity in available families. Genotype–phenotype analyses showed a descriptive enrichment of truncating variants within the mutation cluster region (MCR) in classic FAP, whereas distal variants predominated in attenuated forms. This first large-scale Argentine study characterizes APC - and MUTYH -related polyposis in the region. The identification of novel APC alleles and regionally recurrent MUTYH variants broadens the national reference framework, providing critical evidence to improve genetic diagnosis and clinical management in this specific population.

Article.Title: Ecology, population structure, and habitat vulnerability of Trachomitum venetum s. l. in the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve, Romania
Article.Authors: Chirilă S.; Doroftei M.; Bănescu A.; Attila M.; Sîrbu C.; Oprea A.
Article.Abstract: Trachomitum venetum is an endangered plant species in Romania. Overgrazing and associated trampling pressure represent the main identified threats to the species. The distribution area of this species is very limited in Romania, as it is found only on the Perișor sandbank in the Danube Delta. The study was conducted from 2024 to 2026 and aimed to analyse the environmental preferences, plant associations, and habitat vulnerability of T. venetum in the Danube Delta. For the vegetation analysis, 38 plots were recorded, applying the Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering method. A site-level condition assessment was conducted using categories guided by Article 17 of the Habitats Directive. Soil samples were collected and subsequently analysed in the laboratory to determine the environmental conditions. Ecological indices were also calculated. The HEC-RAS hydraulic model was used to assess the flood risk affecting the habitat of the analysed species. The investigated population of Trachomitum from the Danube Delta, Romania, was provisionally referred to as T. venetum , in accordance with the treatment adopted in Flora Europaea. However, the Romanian material showed deviations from published descriptions in some morphological features, suggesting that further comparative studies using herbarium material and molecular markers are needed to clarify the taxonomic status of this plant in Romania. Soil analyses showed that the soils are strongly alkaline, with high organic carbon and humus content and a predominance of organic nitrogen. A direct field census across the entire 25 ha occupied area recorded 10,119 above-ground shoots, of which 284 were flowering (2.81%); total shoot abundance remained broadly stable during 2024–2026. The highest total shoot abundance in the 2026 association-level census was recorded in the Secali sylvestris – Brometum tectori and Artemisio santonici-Juncetum maritimi associations. The phytocoenological analysis identified six plant associations. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) showed that the soil water-regime indicator (Hd) was the strongest vegetation-derived correlate of floristic composition, although it individually explained only 9.9% of the variation. The most frequent EUNIS habitat among the analysed records was A2.5 Coastal salt marshes and saline reedbeds. The indicative site-level assessment classified population condition, habitat condition and future prospects as U1, local occupancy and spatial distribution as U2; and the overall local condition as U2. Hydraulic modelling indicated increasing potential flood exposure of the occupied habitat under the more severe modelled scenarios. The biological consequences of such flooding were not measured. In conclusion, the restricted distribution, unfavourable site-level condition, and modelled exposure to flooding highlight the need for targeted conservation measures and further studies to better understand the morphological variability of the Romanian population.

Article.Title: Time-dependent evolution of mechanical properties of surrounding rock in roadways within fractured rock masses and determination of optimal support timing
Article.Authors: Ou R.; Yin T.; Jiang K.; Lin W.; Zhu H.; Li Z.; Gong Y.
Article.Abstract: To reveal the time-dependent deterioration of surrounding rock in deep roadways excavated in fractured rock masses and determine a reasonable support timing, the track inclined roadway in the II₃ mining district of a certain mine was investigated in this study. Ultrasonic testingUltrasonic testing and sequential core drilling were employed to obtain the time-dependent expansion characteristics of the surrounding-rock damage zones, and a time-series mechanical testing system was used to determine the time-dependent changes in strength and deformation parameters. The results show that the crushing zone and plastic zone of surrounding rock expand rapidly within the first 20 days after excavation, while mechanical parameters exhibit exponential degradation. Cohesion, internal friction angle, and elastic modulus decrease significantly, whereas Poisson’s ratio increases gradually. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulation indicate that the optimal support timing is approximately 10 days after excavation, and the latest support time should not exceed 20 days. Based on this finding, a coordinated support system consisting of shotcrete–bolt–mesh combined with long anchor cables was proposed. Field application results show that the roof–floor convergence and sidewall convergence of the roadway were effectively controlled within 32.5 mm and 28.3 mm, respectively. The study demonstrates the practical feasibility of determining support timing based on the time-dependent evolution law of surrounding rock damage and provides theoretical and practical guidance for stability control of deep underground roadways.

Article.Title: Small language models are agentic but not autonomous in greenhouse climate control
Article.Authors: Penica M.; Bhattacharya M.; Dooley A.; O’Connell E.
Article.Abstract: Agentic large language models (LLMs) are proposed for cyber-physical control, yet evidence on how reliably small open-weight models turn sensor context into actuator commands is scarce. We present a reproducible benchmark grounded in an operational ESP32-based greenhouse controller: ninety-six generated test cases run against the production tool schema and prompts, scored deterministically, with the controller’s rule-based fallback ported verbatim as baseline. Four quantized models (3–14 B) ran on a pinned llama.cpp stack in two locked environments two months apart (12,000 scored runs). Three findings dominate. Autonomous self-initiation is far less reliable than command execution: models executing 65–100% of chat commands fall to 0.4–64.6% when acting unprompted. Model rankings are environment-conditional: one environment favoured Qwen2.5-7B over the 14B (McNemar p = 0.016; cluster-robust GEE p = 0.084), the other decisively reversed it at identical seeds ( p < 0.001; 77.5% cross-environment agreement), requiring re-benchmarking on the deployment stack. The rule baseline matches the second-best model with the best refusal behaviour: the LLM’s measured value is language-mediated actuation, knowledge capture, and auditability, not superior regulation. Field telemetry and thermal replay show the hybrid controller running unattended through the growing season, rules holding the safety-critical floor. All instruments and both environments’ traces are released.

Article.Title: Higher insulin sensitivity estimated by SPISE is associated with lower odds of incident knee osteoarthritis in Chinese adults
Article.Authors: Cui X.; Li M.; Wu J.; Qi Q.; Zhao K.; Liang J.; Huang W.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the association between insulin sensitivity estimated using the Single Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator (SPISE) and knee osteoarthritis (KOA) among Chinese middle-aged and older adults. We conducted a longitudinal analysis using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). KOA was the outcome and SPISE was the exposure. Feature selection was performed using Boruta, and selected variables were included in multivariable logistic regression models. Dose–response patterns were assessed using restricted cubic splines, and prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted to examine consistency across strata.To contextualize SPISE’s clinical utility, we compared its predictive performance against the triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio (TG/HDL) and body mass index (BMI) using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, with between-marker comparisons performed using DeLong’s test and Holm correction for multiple comparisons), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). To complement the observational findings, we additionally conducted a rat experiment (12 male Sprague-Dawley rats, blank vs. model group) to explore the metabolic phenotype associated with altered SPISE, acknowledging that this experiment does not directly validate the SPISE-KOA association. A total of 2,709 participants were included, of whom 252 had KOA (9.30%). In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in SPISE was associated with lower odds of KOA (odds ratio 0.7939, 95% confidence interval 0.6826 to 0.9203; P = 0.0025). Compared with SPISE Q1, SPISE Q4 was associated with lower odds of KOA (0.5973, 0.3944 to 0.8982; P = 0.0139); however, Q2 and Q3 did not differ significantly from Q1, and the significant trend test (P for trend = 0.0093) was driven primarily by this extreme-quartile contrast, so a graded dose-response relationship could not be confirmed. Restricted cubic splines supported an overall association ( P = 0.011) with no evidence of nonlinearity ( P = 0.84). Subgroup analyses showed no significant interactions by age, sex, hypertension, or smoking.In head-to-head comparisons, the AUC of SPISE for incident KOA was 0.5606 (95% CI 0.5241 to 0.5972): discrimination was significantly higher than that of TG/HDL (0.5065, 95% CI 0.4699 to 0.5431; AUC difference 0.0541, 95% CI 0.0279 to 0.0804; DeLong P < 0.001) but not superior to BMI (0.5805, 95% CI 0.5435 to 0.6175; AUC difference − 0.0199, 95% CI -0.0399 to 0.0001; P = 0.0512), with conclusions unchanged after Holm correction; the incremental gain was small and non-significant (NRI 0.04, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.11; IDI 0.008, P = 0.12), indicating that SPISE did not significantly improve discrimination or reclassification beyond conventional metabolic markers and that its standalone discriminative ability is limited.In the rat experiment, the model group showed significantly lower SPISE than the blank group (28.63 ± 1.35 vs. 31.40 ± 1.68, P = 0.010), consistent with the human data. The negative correlation between SPISE and BMI in rats ( r = -0.744, P = 0.006) is mathematically expected because BMI is a denominator term in the SPISE formula and was not interpreted as an independent biological finding. Higher SPISE was associated with lower odds of KOA in a nationally representative Chinese cohort. The association appeared approximately linear and was broadly consistent across key subgroups. However, the association was primarily driven by the extreme quartile contrast (Q4 vs. Q1), and SPISE showed no statistically significant incremental predictive value over BMI and TG/HDL. The exploratory rat experiment supported metabolic phenotype consistency but did not validate the SPISE-KOA association directly, owing to the lack of histological KOA confirmation and the absence of a lean surgical control group. These findings suggest that SPISE is an insulin-free metabolic correlate of KOA; because it provided no significant incremental predictive value over BMI or TG/HDL, its practical advantage lies in its physiological specificity and freedom from insulin assays rather than in superior predictive performance, and its clinical translation requires further validation against imaging-confirmed outcomes.

Article.Title: Background selection behavior follows ontogenetic color change in Nessus sphinx moth caterpillars (Amphion floridensis)
Article.Authors: Lopez T.; Forkner R.; Lowell M.; Vasas V.; de Alcantara Viana J.; Hanley D.
Article.Abstract: Animals have evolved an array of strategies for maximizing background matching camouflage in complex and colorful environments, including color change and background selection. Here we investigate background selection in Nessus sphinx ( Amphion floridensis ) caterpillars, which change color as they grow. Caterpillars transition from green to brown, with some individuals expressing a rare pink phenotype before changing to brown. We found that these three developmental color phases are visually distinct in the eyes of their natural avian predators, impacting the caterpillars’ ability to camouflage against host plant colors as they age. We also performed a dichotomous choice experiment to test whether caterpillars prefer either green or brown backgrounds. We found that they preferentially move across surfaces which maximize their current camouflage and that they adjust their preferences as they grow, choosing green model leaves while green and preferring brown model leaves after becoming brown themselves. Pink caterpillars did not prefer either color. These findings provide strong evidence that behavioral crypsis is plastic in Nessus sphinx caterpillars and used to maintain crypsis as their coloration changes over time.

Article.Title: Integrating chaotic encryption with a quantum-inspired nonlinear feature mapping for privacy-aware image intelligence
Article.Authors: Barati K.; Hamidi A.; Farmani A.
Article.Abstract: Recent advances in intelligent visual systems have created a growing need for frameworks capable of simultaneously protecting sensitive image content and supporting reliable machine-based interpretation. Here, we present a unified privacy-aware visual intelligence framework that integrates chaotic image encryption, statistical security assessment, hybrid feature extraction, and a classical nonlinear feature mapping inspired by quantum feature-space representations. The encryption stage employs pseudo-random key generation, permutation–diffusion dynamics, and dual-key XOR transformations to disrupt spatial structure and obscure the visual content of plaintext images. Statistical analyses demonstrate strong randomness and differential-sensitivity characteristics, achieving a mean NPCR of 99.8709%, a mean UACI of 33.4629%, and a mean ciphertext entropy of 7.9972 bits. In the learning branch, deep and handcrafted features are combined and transformed using a quantum-inspired nonlinear mapping before classification. Using the selected Proposed-QINNFM-SVM model, the independent held-out test achieved 100.0000% accuracy, 1.0000 Macro-F1, and 100.0000% balanced accuracy, while repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation across the five evaluated models on the training data identified Proposed-QINNFM-SVM as the strongest repeated-validation configuration, with 91.03 ± 0.20% accuracy, 0.8894 ± 0.0026 Macro-F1, and 87.10 ± 0.24% balanced accuracy. These results are evaluated separately to distinguish independent-test performance from variability across training-data partitions. The proposed framework provides an integrated computational architecture for privacy-aware image protection and downstream visual classification, with potential applications in medical imaging and other sensitive visual-analysis scenarios.

Article.Title: Ultrasound-assisted forward osmosis for enhanced flux in pomegranate juice concentration
Article.Authors: Gunashree B.; Nagesh K.; Nayak C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Forward osmosis (FO) presents a non-thermal method for concentrating heat-sensitive fruit juices, with concentration polarization and fouling limiting membrane transport when processing complex feeds. Despite the potential of ultrasound (US) for process intensification, its application in FO has largely been confined to model solutions or limited acoustic conditions, leaving the influences of membrane orientation, frequency, and acoustic mode on real juice matrices underexplored. This study examined pomegranate ( Punica granatum L.) juice concentration using 40 kHz and 1.7 MHz US in both continuous and pulsating modes, evaluating membrane transport, reverse salt diffusion, product quality, and energy characteristics evaluated. Membrane orientation showed a feed-dependent response, with the active layer facing the juice offering superior performance. Under this setup, 40 kHz and 1.7 MHz US increased flux by 29% and 20%, respectively, although they also elevated reverse salt diffusion. Pulsating US halved energy input with minimal flux reduction, and 1.7 MHz produced negligible bulk heating. US-assisted FO enhanced concentration and anthocyanin content while largely maintaining physicochemical and antioxidant qualities after reconstitution. The resulting performance–energy–quality relationships identify pulsating US as an energy-efficient approach and highlight frequency selection as crucial for optimizing FO concentration of heat-sensitive liquid foods.

Article.Title: Machine learning based bottom hole temperature prediction using well log data in the Taranaki Basin New Zealand
Article.Authors: Singh S.; Anand S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of bottom hole temperature (BHT) is essential for optimizing drilling operations, reservoir characterization, and petrophysical assessments. This study focuses on the development of various machine learning (ML) models for predicting BHT. The well log data from the Taranaki Basin, New Zealand, is used for the model development. After data acquisition and preprocessing, a feature selection process using correlation analysis identified the most relevant input feature logs. Six ML models—Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and a Voting Regressor—were developed and evaluated using blind-test data. This study compares the machine learning models to predict the BHT using well log data from the Taranaki Basin, providing one of the first basin-specific assessments of model performance and prediction refinement through exponential smoothing. Model evaluation was conducted on three datasets: (1) 20% random test split, (2) unseen data from the Goldie-1 well (blind-test well), and (3) the same well (Goldie-1) after exponential smoothing of the predicted values. The Random Forest consistently delivered significant accuracy, an R 2 score of 0.990 on blind testing, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.38 °C, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.77 °C, a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.01%, and a maximum error of 8.94 °C. After applying exponential smoothing on predicted data, the error further decreased with an MAE of 0.33 °C, an RMSE of 0.45 °C, a MAPE of 0.01%, and a maximum error of 1.31 °C. The ensemble methods, particularly Voting Regressor, demonstrated comparable performance, achieving an R 2 score of 0.974 on blind test data, an MAE of 1.09 °C, an RMSE of 1.27 °C, an MAPE of 0.02%, and a maximum error of 3.23 °C. The findings of this study indicate the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms and the workflow for predicting subsurface temperature (BHT) with significant accuracy.

Article.Title: Removal of protein-bound uremic toxins using amine-functionalized silica nanocomposite–polyethersulfone membranes via combined adsorption and diffusion
Article.Authors: Farmani M.; Ranjbaran N.; Fathollahzadeh F.; Salmani S.; Yegani S.; Yegani R.
Article.Abstract: Removal of protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUTs) remains a major challenge in hemodialysis. The elimination of these toxins is difficult due to the formation of toxin-protein complexes during hemodialysis. In this study, we functionalized silica nanoparticles (SNPs) with amine groups and incorporated them into a polyethersulfone (PES) membrane matrix. The modified membrane exhibited enhanced hydrophilicity, increasing the pure water flux from 29.39 to 52.62 L m − 2 h − 1 . To evaluate the adsorption behavior and performance, three adsorption isotherms -Langmuir, Freundlich, and Sips- as well as kinetic models including pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and Elovich were investigated. The fabricated membrane achieved highest adsorption capacities of 29.75 mg g − 1 for Hippuric acid (HA) and 37.55 mg g − 1 for p-cresol (PC), as predicted by the Sips isotherm and Elovich kinetic model confirming monolayer adsorption of both PC and HA onto the heterogenous surface of modified nanocomposite membrane. Hollow fiber membranes were tested in membrane separation modules to simulate the hemodialysis process under equal hydrodynamic dimensionless numbers and similar mass transfer condition with practical dialysis modules. The results showed that the neat membrane had limited efficiency in removing PBUTs, whereas the developed nanocomposite membrane substantially improved the removal of HA and PC. The modified nanocomposite membrane increased the HA and PC removals from 28.59% to 6.62% of the neat membrane to 59.22% and 35.75%, respectively. These findings demonstrate the significant potential of functionalized NPs for enhancing dialysis membrane performance.

Article.Title: Assessing the transferability of urban relations from large to small cities using spatial–temporal and anatomic-statistical analyses with GIS and KBS
Article.Authors: Chen Q.; Liu Y.; Zhou L.; Wang B.; Wu J.; Shen G.
Article.Abstract: Urban planning and studies increasingly rely on explicit-tacit knowledge derived from large cities, yet whether these relations hold for small cities remains underexplored. Using 161 years of parcel-level data for Corvallis, Oregon, a small American city, we test whether quantified urban measures and professional heuristics established for large cities transfer to small-city settings. We compute 32 urban measures of form, land-use mix, accessibility, and socio-economics at 5-year intervals (1853–2014), examine 496 pairwise relations fitted with linear, power, exponential, and polynomial functions, and estimate multivariate regressions linking urban measures to socio-economic factors. Of the 496 pairwise relations, 317 were positive (mean r = 0.84) and 179 negative (mean r = − 0.59); non-linear functions provided the best fit for most pairs (292 third-order polynomial, 87 power, 38 exponential or logarithmic, and 78 s-order polynomial relations), whereas only one pair was best described by a linear function. Multivariate regressions yielded high explanatory power (adjusted R 2 = 0.570–0.999) with theoretically expected coefficient signs. These findings indicate that commonly accepted explicit-tacit urban relations for large cities largely hold for small cities, supporting the transferability of GIS-KBS, anatomic-statistical, explicit-tacit frameworks to small-city planning practice and urban studies.

Article.Title: Assessing non-linear socio-spatial dynamics in urban resilience using interpretable machine learning: evidence from aging communities
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Zhou X.; Wang B.
Article.Abstract: Aging residential communities face compound socio-ecological risks, yet renewal programs may prioritize physical retrofits over social conditions associated with resilience. We examine non-linear associations between social participation and physical infrastructure using data from four aging communities in Dalian, China (687 baseline surveys, spatial audits, and stakeholder interviews). We constructed a 48-indicator Comprehensive Resilience Index (CRI) and analyzed it with Random Forest (RF), Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and panel threshold regression. Permutation importance assigned the largest relative share to social participation (31.2%). SHAP estimates showed larger model-specific contributions for selected social factors than for static physical attributes. The panel threshold model estimated a context-specific threshold of 54.80 on the normalized social participation scale (0–100). Below the threshold, the infrastructure coefficient was not statistically significant ( β = 0.062, p = 0.168); above it, the estimated coefficient was 0.485 ( p < 0.001). These observational results are consistent with a thresholded association between participation and infrastructure-resilience relationships; they do not establish a causal multiplier mechanism or a universal readiness cutoff.

Article.Title: Robust and stable detection of visual features from objects with depth-axis motion against variable scenes: locust-inspired visual neural pathway modeling
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Xu M.; Zheng S.; Ruan Y.
Article.Abstract: Currently, Locust-inspired visual models based on the Lobula Giant Movement Detector 1 (LGMD1) have achieved significant advances in the field of intelligent obstacle avoidance. However, the decision-making reliability of obstacle avoidance systems is highly dependent on the robust detection of visual features of moving objects. Specifically, substantial excitation from translating moving objects and variable scenes pose challenges for robust (i.e., resilience under variable low-contrast scenes) and stable (i.e., consistency despite spatial-contrast variations) detection of visual features from moving objects in the LGMD1-based model. To address this challenge, we present a Locust-inspired motion-object depth-axis vision-feature-detection (MODAVFD) model that integrates ON and OFF pathway competition and contrast neural computation, which shows a preference for objects with depth-axis motion (i.e., motion along the depth axis) and enables robust and stable detection of visual features against variable scenes. The MODAVFD model integrates successive neural computational layers from the retina to the lobula complex. First, changes in luminance are captured by the photoreceptor cells and divided into parallel ON and OFF pathways. Second, the lateral inhibition (LI) mechanism is employed as early visual preprocessing to enhance the selectivity of motion boundaries, and the non-linear instantaneous feedback divisive contrast normalization mechanism is adopted to reduce sensitivity to local contrast. Third, the parallel contrast pathways are activated to inhibit the parallel motion pathways, suppressing high-spatial-contrast optical flow. Finally, neural competition between the ON and OFF pathways is conducted and the winner is transmitted to the LGMD1. Notably, the MODAVFD model does not discriminate between approaching and receding motion, and a downstream mechanism is therefore required before its use in collision avoidance. Through extensive comparative experiments with state-of-the-art (SOTA) bio-inspired models, the MODAVFD model demonstrates a preference for objects with depth-axis motion and responds robustly to low-spatial-contrast inputs. Moreover, the performance of the MODAVFD model was evaluated under three object velocities. First, regarding the sum of the coefficient of variation, it decreased by 40.91%, 74.03%, and 92.36% on the synthetic pure dataset; by 78.56%, 74.95%, and 85.26% on the semi-synthetic cluttered dataset; and by 12.11%, 8.77%, and 17.96% on the semi-synthetic real-world dataset, respectively. Notably, the improvement of the MODAVFD model on the semi-synthetic real-world dataset is smaller than that on the other datasets, which is primarily attributed to the multi-class objects in the backgrounds of this dataset, introducing inter-class interference. Second, regarding the inter-quartile range (IQR) of the coefficient of variation, it changed by − 46.36%, 26.75%, and 44.65% on the semi-synthetic cluttered dataset, and by 7.99%, 5.19%, and 15.38% on the semi-synthetic real-world dataset, respectively. Importantly, the aforementioned improvement is not consistent across object motion velocities and baselines, but the response stability is improved overall. However, the model exhibits a known limitation when processing bisected black and white rectangular stimuli: because such stimuli carry both contrast polarities in balanced proportion, the ON and OFF responses offset at the integration stage, producing no usable output.

Article.Title: Rapid postural control adaptations to repeated virtual reality stimulation in older adults
Article.Authors: Hansson E.; Nae J.; Östlind E.; Röijezon U.; Fransson P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vision plays a crucial role in postural control, and age-related conditions can increase reliance on visual input for balance, making older adults more susceptible to instability in distorted visual environments. Virtual Reality (VR) may help mitigate disruptive visual information by promoting a shift in sensory reliance. This study investigated how older adults respond to challenging visual environments presented through immersive VR, focusing on postural stability, muscle activity, and adaptation over repeated exposures. Thirty-two older adults participated, with 25 included in posturography/EMG measurements (mean age 74.8 ± 3.5 years) and 31 included when studying occurrence of incidences requiring fall-preventing support. Participants completed two control tests (quiet stance with eyes open and closed) before undergoing five repetitions of a 120-second VR roller-coaster simulation, with about 10 min rests between sessions. Postural stability and muscle activity in four postural leg muscles were recorded simultaneously. Co-contractions indexes were calculated according to agonist muscle pairs contributing to postural stability over ankle and hip joints. VR exposure significantly increased energy use for postural stability (p < 0.001) and muscle co-contractions (p ≤ 0.001) compared to eyes-open control tests. Initially, 45% of participants required support to prevent falls, but repeated sessions reduced incidents to 10%. These improvements were accompanied with decreases in stability energy use (p ≤ 0.002) and muscle co-contractions (p < 0.001) indicating postural adaptations to visual stimulation. Strong correlations between postural stability responses and muscle activity emerged especially during VR-stimulations. This finding indicates increased reliance on co-contraction (stiffening strategy) of postural muscles during more challenging balance tasks. In conclusion, visual stimulation through VR can challenge balance control on older adults inducing increased stability measures and co-contractions of postural muscles. However, repeated VR exposures may rapidly enhance sensorimotor control, reduce visual dependency, improve postural stability and reduce muscular co-contractions.

Article.Title: Mechanical performance analysis and construction technology of novel sealing walls in coal mine connecting roadways
Article.Authors: Gong S.; Dong Y.; Wang X.; Lin D.; Zhang D.; Huang J.; Wu R.
Article.Abstract: To address the deficiencies of traditional sealing walls, such as low construction efficiency, susceptibility to failure, and poor airtightness, this paper proposes a novel sealing wall with equivalent thickness. Based on elastic thin-plate theory, their load-bearing mechanisms are compared; through numerical simulation, their mechanical responses under mining conditions are analyzed; relying on a self-developed vehicle-mounted integrated backfilling system, process linkage tests and underground industrial practices are carried out to evaluate the feasibility of the innovative construction method and the service reliability under mining conditions. The results show that the novel sealing wall achieves collaborative load bearing, with maximum bending moment reduced by 89% and maximum shear force reduced by 66.67%; the overlying roof transitions from a tensile to a compressive stress state; the high-stress (>10 MPa) zone shrinks by approximately 84%, and the low-stress (<5 MPa) zone expands by about 107.7%. The self-developed vehicle-mounted integrated backfilling system enables material delivery from surface mixing to continuous underground pouring, and the new construction method integrates innovative processes: “full-section mechanical slotting and embedding, flexible-formwork support and suspension, micro-pressurized roof contact, and flexible-formwork backfilling”. These achieve multiple engineering objectives: structural stability, air-tightness, and low cost (reduced by 52%), demonstrating favorable economic benefits and engineering prospects, and providing an effective solution for rapid sealing in roadways subjected to intense mining pressure and sudden emergencies.

Article.Title: Performance analysis of scalable posit processing element with accelerated arithmetic units
Article.Authors: Susithra N.; Rajalakshmi K.; Sumant B.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a posit processing element (PPE) that integrates optimized posit adder, multiplier and Multiply Accumulate (MAC) units suitable for matrix workload aimed at ML and Deep Neural Network accelerators in the signal processing domain. The proposed architecture targets Posit (N, es) formats, with a component-partitioning stage having a leading zero counter–based regime extractor, followed by structurally modelled arithmetic cores built from Kogge–Stone, Han–Carlson adders, Modified Booth and Wallace tree multipliers. Parameterized Verilog HDL generators are developed and instantiated for 8‑, 16‑, and 32‑bit posits, with synthesis performed on a Zynq‑7000 and 90 nm ASIC flow to enable a fair comparison with existing posit cores. For a <32,3> posit adder on F​PGA, the proposed Han–Carlson–based design reduces the maximum datapath delay by 1.5%, and on ASIC it reduces cell area by around 32%. The Modified Booth–based 32-bit posit multiplier achieves up to 63% lower ASIC delay but with 48% higher cell area, highlighting the speed–area trade‑off. The 32‑bit PPE and a 4‑tap FIR filter realized with the proposed posit modules achieves 23.1% lower critical-path delay. The hardware overhead in posits are amortized by the better accuracy. Evaluating rounding schemes reveals that Posit {32, 2} under truncation retains 100% accuracy up to 4 decimal places and 98.8% at 6 decimal places with a negligible Mean Relative Error of 1.0e−6, proving that rounding logic can be safely bypassed to save hardware cost in noise-tolerant DSP and ML applications. The target domain applications are MAC-dominated DSP/ML accelerator datapath involving FIR/convolution filtering and matrix–vector multiplication.

Article.Title: Interactive effects of planting date and mulch type on tomato growth and yield in Makurdi, Nigeria
Article.Authors: Akaazua W.; Aboyeji C.; Ige S.; Okunlola F.; Olofintoye T.
Article.Abstract: The timing of planting and the application of some agronomic practices are very important in the production system of tomatoes. This study investigated the effects of planting time and mulch type on the growth and yield performance of the UC 82B tomato variety in Makurdi, Nigeria. A 3 × 4 factorial experiment (three planting times: January, May, September; and four mulch types: silver plastic, black plastic, grass mulch, no mulch) in a split-plot arrangement was conducted in the years 2023 and 2024 fitted in a Randomised Complete Block Design (RCBD). Data from the study were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA) using the SAS package. Treatment means were separated using Duncan’s Multiple Range Test at 5% probability level. The study results revealed that the interaction between planting time and mulch type (PT × MT) significantly ( P ≤ 0.05) affected growth and yield. The interaction effect was pronounced, with September × silver mulch producing the highest yield (39.9 t/ha in 2023; 43.2 t/ha in 2024), representing about 100–133% increase over January with no mulch. May × silver mulch produced the highest fruit weight (103.9 g in 2023; 95.5 g in 2024) and vigorous vegetative growth (plant height up to 90.9 cm). No mulch consistently gave the lowest performance across planting times. Mulch benefits were greatest under favourable conditions (May and September) but reduced under January stress. Trends were consistent across years, though yields were generally higher in 2024. The study recommends that planting UC 28B variety with favourable climatic windows (September) and applying reflective (silver mulch) or organic mulch significantly improves tomato productivity in the Southern Guinea Savannah.

Article.Title: Multifunctional spacecraft radiation shield based on an HBGPE composite with modelled scintillation-based energy conversion and boron-10 neutron capture
Article.Authors: Patel K.
Article.Abstract: Deep-space missions require substantial shielding mass, yet conventional shields dissipate absorbed particle energy as wasted heat. Here we present RADIANT, a six-layer composite combining a hydrogen-boron-graphene polyethylene (HBGPE) layer, a cerium oxide-loaded scintillation layer, and a graphene-polycaprolactone layer intended for charge collection. Geant4 11.2.2 simulations across 35 configurations show 2.14-fold higher neutron attenuation than equivalent-thickness aluminium at 1 MeV, driven by hydrogen moderation rather than boron-10 capture at fast-neutron energies; at equal areal density this rises to 2.53-fold. Boron-10 was modelled at both 95% enrichment (an optimisation scenario) and the natural abundance (~ 19.9% ¹⁰B) of the prototype, giving 19.02% attenuation. Infrared testing showed stable electrical output spanning 0.69 to 131.05 W·m⁻² under controlled thermal input, with the transduction mechanism uncharacterised. A model-based calculation combining Geant4 energy deposition with literature-derived scintillator parameters projects particle-driven conversion efficiencies of 0.00–0.0107%, pending ionising-radiation validation. In bench tests, the outer tungsten surface reached a pyrometer-estimated 545 °C with output retention above 93%, and the prototype withstood 100 N of compressive load with partial structural compromise, no fracture, at 14.9% lower areal density than equal-thickness aluminium. These results establish simulated neutron-shielding gains and an unconfirmed pathway toward radiation-to-electrical conversion in shielding mass.

Article.Title: A scFv-based immunotoxin for selective targeting and cytotoxicity against c-Met-overexpressing cancer cells: an integrated in silico and in vitro study
Article.Authors: Poordad Z.; Dabirmanesh B.; Khajeh K.
Article.Abstract: C-Met receptor is frequently overexpressed in multiple cancers, driving tumor invasiveness, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Although amivantamab has received clinical approval as a c-Met inhibitor, its large molecular size and lack of intrinsic cytolytic activity limit its broader therapeutic application, underscoring the need for next-generation dual-mechanism agents. To address this, we designed, produced, and characterized a novel immunotoxin, SM1, comprising an anti-c-Met scFv derived from amivantamab fused to the cytolytic peptide melittin via flexible (G 4 S) 3 linkers. Among four computationally designed models, SM1 exhibited the most favorable binding free energy toward c-Met and was selected for experimental validation. SM1 was successfully expressed in Escherichia coli C41 (DE3) as a SUMO fusion protein, while the scFv without melittin (S1) was expressed in BL21 (DE3). Both proteins were overexpressed as inclusion bodies, solubilized using sarcosyl, and purified for functional characterization. Cell-ELISA showed stronger apparent cellular binding of both constructs to c-Met-overexpressing MKN-45 cells than to HT-29 cells, consistent with c-Met expression levels, while indicating that melittin fusion did not substantially affect scFv binding. To assess whether the melittin domain retained its lytic activity after fusion, the antibacterial activity of SM1 was evaluated against E. coli JM109, and the observed growth inhibition confirmed the retention of melittin-associated lytic activity in the fusion construct. In cytotoxicity assays, SM1 exhibited greater activity than S1 against both MKN-45 and HT-29 cells, with the strongest response observed in MKN-45 cells, while HEK-293 viability remained above 80% under the tested conditions. This selective cytotoxicity was accompanied by limited hemolytic activity, with both constructs showing less than 10% hemolysis at the highest concentration tested of 200 µM. Flow cytometry analysis further revealed potent apoptosis induction (97.03%) and extensive Sub-G1 accumulation in MKN-45 cells, with markedly lower effects in HEK-293 cells (9.22%), confirming target-dependent cytotoxicity. These findings demonstrate the preferential cytotoxicity of SM1 toward c-Met-expressing cancer cells and support its potential as a dual-mechanism immunotoxin for targeted therapy of c-Met-driven malignancies.

Article.Title: Influence of light pollution and atmospheric conditions on twilight sky brightness at the Kottamia Astronomical Observatory
Article.Authors: Aboushelib M.; Morcos A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Twilight sky brightness provides valuable information on the combined effects of solar illumination, atmospheric conditions, and artificial light pollution, making it an important parameter for astronomical site characterization and environmental monitoring. In this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of twilight sky brightness based on continuous observations obtained over a 15-month period using a Sky Quality Meter (SQM) at the Kottamia Astronomical Observatory (KAO), Egypt. Morning and evening twilight measurements were acquired between November 2021 and January 2023 to investigate the influence of atmospheric conditions and anthropogenic light pollution on the temporal evolution of sky brightness. Monthly averages of zenith sky brightness (ZSB) were determined as a function of solar elevation, revealing clear seasonal variations during both morning and evening twilight. On average, astronomical twilight was darker in the morning than in the evening. The mean brightness increase from astronomical to nautical twilight was 0.65 ± 0.06 mag SQM /arcsec 2 , while the transitions from nautical to civil twilight and from civil twilight to sunrise or sunset were 5.44 ± 0.18 and 5.54 ± 0.14 mag SQM /arcsec 2 , respectively. The ZSB began to increase at a solar depression of approximately 14.5° during morning twilight and stabilized at approximately 15.1° during evening twilight. To investigate the observed seasonal variations, Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV), and Ozone Total Column (OTC) data were analyzed over the same period. The results indicated that variations in aerosols contributed significantly to the observed changes in twilight sky brightness, whereas water vapor provided a secondary contribution and ozone had only a minor influence on the broadband SQM measurements. Simultaneous observations toward the zenith, eastern horizon, and western horizon demonstrated a pronounced directional dependence of twilight sky brightness. During evening twilight, the zenith darkened first, followed by the eastern and western horizons approximately 19 and 27 min later, respectively. During morning twilight, the eastern sky brightened approximately 8 min before the zenith, whereas the western horizon responded about 19 min later. Persistent sky glow produced by nearby urban areas significantly increased the brightness of the western horizon, even during astronomical and nautical twilight. These results demonstrate that twilight sky brightness is controlled primarily by solar depression, while atmospheric conditions and artificial light pollution introduce measurable seasonal and directional variations. The long-term observations presented in this study provide valuable constraints for astronomical site characterization, long-term monitoring of light pollution, and investigations of atmospheric variability.

Article.Title: Ensemble-based assessment of projected hazard risk: Identification of regions exposed to extreme precipitation in North-Central Europe
Article.Authors: Fakour P.; Ustrnul Z.; Messori G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accelerated transformations in the European hydrological cycle during the early 21st century call for a rethinking of approaches used to detect regions susceptible to precipitation extremes. This work provides a risk map for extreme precipitation events, categorizing areas into four risk levels: from no risk to high risk. These were defined based on the direction, magnitude, and statistical significance of trends in extreme precipitation indices, with the highest category representing significant positive trends within the upper percentiles of the precipitation distribution. The study includes 70 years of historical data from E-Obs (1951–2020) and 13 bias-adjusted CORDEX models under two future scenarios, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, for 80 years (2021–2100). To ensure reliable detection of long-term changes, the analysis employs the Mann-Kendall test with an iterative pre-whitening procedure. The historical risk assessment derived from seven decades of E-Obs observational data shows a heterogeneous pattern across Europe. Elevated risk zones are predominantly concentrated along the western coastal regions of Scandinavia, particularly in Norway’s Atlantic-facing territories. In contrast, continental interior regions (Central European lowlands) generally exhibit lower risk levels. Under the RCP4.5 scenario, some areas, particularly in Scandinavia, show increased risk, although model agreement remains variable. The RCP8.5 scenario presents a noticeable increase in risk levels, with widespread agreement among climate models. Almost the entire study domain transitions into medium to high-risk categories. This broadly shift represents not merely an intensification of existing patterns but a fundamental reorganization of the region’s extreme precipitation climatology. The changes are especially pronounced across the Scandinavian countries, with almost the entire region falling into the high-risk category. The contrast between the two emissions scenarios emphasizes the strong sensitivity of extreme precipitation patterns to greenhouse gas concentration pathways. Overall, the results emphasize the urgency of mitigation and inform adaptation planning in regions likely to face higher extreme precipitation risk.

Article.Title: Mediating roles of resilience, anxiety, and pain in the association between hope and cancer-related fatigue among oncology patients
Article.Authors: Hemati M.; Momtazian Z.; Khorashadizadeh S.; Shaygan M.; Hosseini F.; Haghighat S.; Karimi-Haghighi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is one of the most prevalent and debilitating symptoms among oncology patients. Psychological factors such as hope, resilience, anxiety, and pain have been associated with CRF; however, the factors underlying the association between hope and CRF remain insufficiently understood. This study examined whether resilience, anxiety, and pain mediate the association between hope and CRF in oncology patients. A cross-sectional, multi-center study was conducted among 500 oncology patients in five affiliated centers of Shiraz University of Medical Sciences, Iran. Participants completed the Snyder Hope Scale, CD-RISC-10, GAD-7, VAS for pain, and the Okuyama CRF Scale. Path analysis was performed using Mplus (version 8.3) to examine direct and indirect associations, with mediation interpreted statistically rather than causally; descriptive statistics were conducted using SPSS (version 22). Hope was significantly associated with lower anxiety (β = −0.429, 95% CI [− 0.505, − 0.353]) and pain (β = −0.187, 95% CI [− 0.282, − 0.092]), and higher resilience (β = 0.224, 95% CI [0.146, 0.302]). Resilience (β = −0.268, 95% CI [− 0.359, − 0.178]) and anxiety (β = 0.357, 95% CI [0.262, 0.453]) were significantly associated with CRF, whereas pain was not (β = 0.042, 95% CI [− 0.045, 0.128]). The direct effect of hope on CRF was not significant (β = 0.025, 95% CI [− 0.068, 0.117]). Significant indirect effects were observed through resilience (β = −0.060, 95% CI [− 0.089, − 0.031]) and anxiety (β = −0.153, 95% CI [− 0.203, − 0.103]), as well as a significant sequential indirect effect through resilience and anxiety (β = −0.009, 95% CI [− 0.018, − 0.001]). The total effect of hope on CRF was significant (β = −0.213, 95% CI [− 0.300, − 0.126]). Hope was indirectly associated with reduced CRF through resilience and anxiety. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as statistical associations and do not establish temporal or causal relationships. The findings may inform future research on interventions targeting resilience and anxiety, while longitudinal studies incorporating biological and psychosocial factors are needed to further examine the temporal relationships underlying these associations.

Article.Title: A hybrid bio-inspired and machine learning framework for adaptive congestion control and multi-objective QoS optimization in heterogeneous network
Article.Authors: Jagadish S.; Kumar T.
Article.Abstract: Heterogeneous communication networks, that is, the integration of wireless access networks (IoT, Wireless Sensor Networks, Mobile Ad Hoc Networks, Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks, and 5G/6G terrestrial networks), software-defined and cloud-edge infrastructures, and satellite-assisted non-terrestrial networks (NTN), present a serious challenge to adaptive congestion control because of the diversity of technologies, topologies, mobility patterns, and QoS requirements. Although there are various solutions to this problem, such as bio-inspired optimisation, machine-learning prediction, and reinforcement-learning control, none of them addresses the whole problem by considering a combination of global path exploration, proactive congestion forecasting, and adaptive routing control. We propose a 4-layer hybrid framework, CAIRES-Arterial, which combines a genetic algorithm (GA) for Global Path Exploration, Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO) for Pheromone-Guided Path Refining, CatBoost Gradient Boosting for Proactive Congestion State Prediction, and Q-learning for Decentralised Node-level Adaptive Forwarding. The confidence-weighted Hybrid Decision Engine combines GA fitness score, ACO pheromone strength, CatBoost prediction confidence, and Q-learning state-action values to make composite routing decisions in response to real-time network conditions. Extensive simulations with synthetic and real traffic traces (MAWI/CAIDA), using NS-3, GNS3 and Mininet, random, grid and scale-free topologies, show that CAIRES-Arterial outperforms both GA-ACO, CatBoost-Q-learning, DQN and OSPF baselines by 8–15% in terms of throughput, > 92% packet delivery ratio, up to 18% energy saving and up to 35% faster congestion recovery (statistically significant, p < 0.01), while being containerised and deployed in an 512-node topology.
