Article.Title: WCIP-based modeling and deep neural network–driven optimization of a terahertz sensor for IoT-enabled green hydrogen monitoring
Article.Authors: Alsirhani K.; Hlali A.; Sahbani A.; M. Alanazi T.
Article.Abstract: Reliable hydrogen monitoring is a critical requirement for the safe deployment of emerging green hydrogen infrastructures. In this work, a compact terahertz (THz) hydrogen sensor combining physics-based electromagnetic modeling and data-driven optimization is proposed. The sensing platform consists of three laterally cascaded spiral resonators functionalized with graphene, black phosphorus (BP), and vanadium dioxide (VO \(_2\) ), enabling strong near-field confinement and tunable electromagnetic interaction with the surrounding gas medium. The device is analyzed using an extended Wave Concept Iterative Process (WCIP), which provides an efficient full-wave framework for modeling planar structures incorporating ultrathin conductive and anisotropic materials without volumetric discretization. Hydrogen sensing is evaluated through concentration-dependent resonance-frequency shifts associated with the modeled hydrogen-induced perturbation of the VO \(_2\) sensing region, while the intrinsic refractive-index sensitivity is evaluated separately. The investigated concentrations range from 500 ppm to 40 000 ppm H \(_2\) , covering ppm-level concentrations up to approximately the lower explosive limit (LEL). The optimized configuration achieves sensitivities ranging from 1.22 to 1.39 THz/RIU while maintaining sharp spectral responses and quality factors between 22.2 and 25.8. To accelerate the design exploration process, a deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model is developed to learn the nonlinear relationship between material parameters and sensing performance. Comparative evaluation against several machine-learning algorithms demonstrates the superior predictive accuracy of the proposed DNN, enabling rapid multi-parameter optimization beyond conventional full-wave simulations. Finally, the proposed sensing platform is discussed as a potential component of a 6G-enabled Internet-of-Things (IoT) monitoring architecture for distributed hydrogen-safety monitoring. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach for high-resolution THz hydrogen sensing in next-generation smart energy systems.

Article.Title: Performance of an alkali-activated binder derived from recycled glass fiber reinforced plastic under high-pressure CO2 exposure
Article.Authors: Bakri O.; Mahmoud A.; Elkatatny S.; Abd El Fattah A.; Al Ramadan M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the durability of glass fiber reinforced plastic (GFRP) geopolymer cement exposed to high pressure CO 2 . The relationship between mechanical performance, microstructural evolution and leachate chemistry is studied in the setting of CO 2 storage. GFRP was produced from GFRP rebar production waste. The geopolymers were exposed to 1500 psi (10.3 MPa) of CO 2 saturated brine at 125 °F for 90 days and benchmarked against conventional Class G cement. The mechanics of the GFRP-derived binder are a key finding as it maintained mechanical performance for the duration of the study compared to the Class G cement which showed significant degradation. The scratch test results showed that the GFRP binder scratch-derived strength increased from 14.5 MPa at day 1 to 17.9 MPa at day 90, an increase of 23.4%, and the tensile strength remained stable at about 1.5 MPa. However, Class G cement lost 42.3% of its scratch-derived strength (from 12.3 to 7.1 MPa) with a minor loss in tensile strength. The non-destructive computed tomography (CT) analysis revealed a more homogenous internal damage of the GFRP binder in comparison to Class G cement. Brine chemistry after exposure showed moderate alkalinity (pH 8.0), a large increase in dissolved inorganic carbon and a significant leaching of potassium (from 19 to 12,690 ppm). These results suggest a potential for GFRP derived alkali-activated binders in CO 2 -rich wellbore applications.

Article.Title: Upregulation of calmodulin exacerbates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury via regulation of the MLCK/NOX2/NOX4 signaling axis
Article.Authors: Shen D.; Tian J.; Xiang R.; Mao L.; Dai Z.; Tan L.; Li T.; Ali Sheikh M.; Yang Z.
Article.Abstract: The calmodulin (CaM) implicates in the pathological process of Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains unclear. This study aims to explore the role of CaM in oxidative stress injury during CIRI. The correlation analysis between plasma CaM and cerebral infarction of ischemic stroke patients was conducted. In vivo and in vitro models were established to simulate ischemic stroke. Gene function was validated by transfection with CaM- or myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK)-specific siRNA or via luciferase activity experiments. Protein-protein interactions were investigated via bioinformatics analysis and co-immunoprecipitation assays. Protein expression levels, intracellular calcium and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were detected.Plasma CaM levels positively correlated with infarct size in ischemic stroke patients. In in vivo or in vitro model, the expression of CaM, MLCK, NADPH oxidase 2/4 (NOX2/4) and cytochrome c (cyt-c) increased, accompanied by calcium overload and ROS overproduction. Bioinformatics analysis reveals interactions among CaM, MLCK, NOX2, and NOX4. CaM or MLCK knockdown significantly downregulates the expression of CaM, MLCK, NOX2/4, and cyt-c in MCAO rats and H/R-treated SH-SY5Y cells, as well as ROS. However, CaM knockdown not significantly decrease intracellular Ca²⁺ and MLCK knockdown has no effect on CaM expression. CaM or MLCK siRNA can significantly reduce the luciferase activity of SH-SY5Y cells transfected with MLCK-P plasmid, or NOX2-P or NOX4-P plasmids.Our findings demonstrate that CaM promotes oxidative stress in CIRI via the CaM/MLCK/NOX2/NOX4 axis, indicating that CaM acts upstream of MLCK and has potential as a therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

Article.Title: The mosaic genetic ancestry of Rohingya
Article.Authors: Singh P.; Sultana G.; Pathak A.; Montinaro F.; Ongaro L.; Desai S.; Mishra R.; Tamang R.; Nandineni M.; Metspalu M.; van Driem G.; Chaubey G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract South and Southeast Asia represent geographic crossroads of immense ethnic, cultural, and genetic diversity. However, the Rohingya, an ethnic group primarily indigenous to the Rakhine State of Myanmar and speakers of an Eastern Indo-European language closely related to the Chittagonian dialect of Bengali, remain one of the least genetically characterized populations in the region. While recent massive displacements driven by regional policies have drawn significant global attention to their socio-political and public health challenges, the deep biological history and evolutionary trajectory of the Rohingya have remained largely unexplored. To address this critical gap, we generated the first high-resolution, genome-wide dataset for 25 Rohingya individuals and 45 individuals from neighbouring regions, contextualizing them against 2,217 reference samples from across Eurasia. Our comprehensive genomic analyses reveal that the ancestry of the Rohingya aligns robustly with their linguistic affinity, comprising a major South Asian foundational lineage admixed with a minor but significant Southeast Asian component. Specifically, following the historical settlement of their ancestors in the Arakan region, the Rohingya experienced localized gene flow from surrounding Tibeto-Burman-speaking communities. This introgression resulted in a significantly elevated East Eurasian ancestry compared with neighbouring Bangladeshi populations. Furthermore, we identified unique signatures of genetic adaptation and putative disease associations specific to the Rohingya genome. These findings provide unprecedented insights into the admixture dynamics and biological history of a highly marginalized population, underscoring the critical value of genomic data in illuminating both the evolutionary narratives and the ancestry-informed health profiles of vulnerable communities.

Article.Title: Design, modeling, and decoupled control of a fully-actuated pentacopter UAV with a central 2-DoF gimbaled thruster
Article.Authors: Kabiri P.; Sadati H.
Article.Abstract: Recent advancements in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) demand higher maneuverability and stability in complex missions. However, traditional quadcopters, due to their under-actuated nature, suffer from strong coupling between translational and rotational degrees of freedom, which limits independent trajectory tracking and degrades performance in aggressive maneuvers. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel fully-actuated architecture termed the Center-Gimbal Pentacopter, in which a centrally mounted rotor on a 2-DoF gimbal augments a conventional four-rotor layout. The resulting actuator redundancy enables the generation of independent forces and torques, effectively mitigating the drawbacks of under-actuated systems. By employing a baseline hierarchical cascaded PID control framework, this study demonstrates that the the proposed mechanical architecture together with the cascaded controller achieves effectively decoupled translational and rotational dynamics in the reported simulations, facilitating independent control of the degrees of freedom without requiring complex control algorithms. The inner loop stabilizes roll, pitch, and yaw, while the outer loop regulates position, thereby separating attitude and position dynamics and facilitating independent control of the degrees of freedom. The proposed architecture and control scheme are evaluated through comprehensive numerical simulations and compared against a conventional quadcopter under identical reference trajectories. Results demonstrate that the Center-Gimbal Pentacopter significantly enhances trajectory tracking performance and improves overall stability. Quantitative analysis shows that the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) in altitude control is reduced by up to 40% compared with traditional platforms, while maintaining a nearly level attitude during horizontal motion. These findings highlight the high potential of the proposed system for executing highly precise and complex spatial maneuvers in advanced aerial missions.

Article.Title: Application of [18F]NaF PET/CT imaging in renal osteodystrophy in MHD patients
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Chen L.; Wen X.; Wu W.; Kang T.; Huang Z.; Ou S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Renal osteodystrophy (ROD) is an abnormal bone metabolism accompanying chronic kidney disease. Although bone biopsy remains the gold standard for ROD diagnosis and classification, its invasiveness, complexity, and high cost limit its clinical utility. Fluorine-18 labelled sodium fluoride ( 18 F-NaF) PET/CT is a high-resolution bone imaging technique that incorporates functional information with anatomical images. We evaluated 18 F-NaF PET/CT and biomarkers as as noninvasive assessments of ROD in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients. This retrospective study was performed on 21 MHD patients with ROD and 23 individuals with normal renal function who underwent 18 F-NaF fused PET/CT scans. We examined bone metabolic markers in MHD patients, such as intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), beta-C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (β-CTX), and total procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide (t-P1NP). The standard uptake value (SUV) was calculated from the anterior superior spine, lower lumbar spine and femoral neck as the intake of 18 F-NaF. In 71.4% of MHD patients, images revealed abnormal tracer concentration in multiple skeletal sites, indicative of super bone scan characteristics. Among the signs, concentrated radioactivity manifested as a “hot skull sign” in the skull and mandible, a “tie sign” in the sternum, and beadlike signs at the junction of the ribs and costal cartilage. Lumbar spine SUV showed a positive correlation with alkaline phosphatase ( r = 0.477, P = 0.029), while femoral neck SUV correlated positively with iPTH ( r = 0.623, P = 0.003), t-P1NP ( r = 0.637, P = 0.002), and β-CTX ( r = 0.507, P = 0.019). In conclusion, 18 F-NaF PET/CT may serve as a non-invasive adjunctive imaging tool for evaluating ROD in MHD patients by identifying the distribution and extent of skeletal lesions and by providing semi-quantitative information associated with bone turnover markers.

Article.Title: Tourism demand concentration exposes ecological carrying-capacity mismatches in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Gan H.; Zhu Y.; Liu Q.
Article.Abstract: Tourism growth and ecological protection increasingly overlap in large river-basin corridors, but available visitor statistics rarely provide a continuous, cross-regional series and within-city spatial detail at the same time. We therefore used a long-term tourism-demand/service-concentration proxy (TD) as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, observed visitation. Across 129 administrative analytical units in the Yangtze River Economic Belt in 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2023, we combined entropy-weight TOPSIS TD and ecological resource-pressure/capacity (ECC) indices with coupling co-development, a directional relative mismatch index (MI), spatial statistics, GeoDetector and 5-km management zoning. TD increased from 0.041 to 0.147, the main-specification ECC averaged 0.131 in 2023, and CCD increased from 0.240 to 0.341. In 2023, 35 units were TD-dominant and 30 were ECC-dominant; global Moran’s I was 0.170 ( p = 0.003), with 26 significant local clusters. MI rankings were highly similar under min-max scaling (Spearman rho = 0.997), and city TD was strongly associated with the area-weighted mean grid tourism-intensity proxy (Pearson r = 0.918; Spearman rho = 0.888; n = 129). ECC rankings remained sensitive to weighting and water-wetland specification. Rail accessibility had the largest single-factor GeoDetector q value (0.202), and potential-cultivation zones covered 54.83% of the study area. The results provide a relative spatial diagnosis for differentiated management, not an estimate of biophysical visitor-capacity thresholds.

Article.Title: Dual-mode plasmonic nanosensor with high sensitivity and RBF neural network-assisted lactate detection
Article.Authors: Darabi A.; Malekshahi M.
Article.Abstract: Refractive index (RI) sensing is an important technique for biomedical diagnostics, environmental monitoring and chemical analysis. However, most of the current plasmonic sensors are single-mode, have low sensitivity and use linear calibration models that are unable to describe the complex non-linear behavior of real systems. Here, we propose a new dual-mode plasmonic nanosensor for high performance RI sensing based on metal-insulator-metal (MIM) waveguide structure. Different dielectric models are studied for silver, being the Drude-Debye model with an enhancement of the transmission and a decrease of the losses in the whole range of operation the one that provides the best performance. The systematic optimization was carried out to customize the sensor for two different passbands of 950 nm and 1465 nm with high transmission rates of 0.96 and 0.94, respectively. The proposed sensor shows ultrahigh sensitivities of 1580 nm/RIU and 2420 nm/RIU and high figure of merit and quality factor in both operation regimes. To enable accurate and robust RI prediction, a dual-input Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network was used to successfully model the non-linear sensor response with high accuracy (RMSE = 0.0092, R 2 = 0.9987). The sensor was further utilized for lactate detection, demonstrating its great potentials for rapid label-free biomedical sensing. In comparison to the latest plasmonic sensors, the presented design outperforms them in overall performance due to the synergistic integration of advanced structural optimization, precise material modeling, and intelligent data processing. This work offers a promising platform for next-generation high-sensitivity RI sensors.

Article.Title: HFPnet: a hybrid feature perception network for high-quality low-light light field enhancement
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Liu X.; Wang D.; Liu Y.; Yan S.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Existing algorithms for low-light light field enhancement (L3FE) generally suffer from detail loss, severe noise interference and poor cross-view consistency, which greatly degrade the reconstruction quality of L3FE. To solve these problems, the hybrid feature perception network (HFPnet) is proposed for high-quality L3FE. Firstly, a hybrid decoupling module (HDM) is designed to extract spatial features, angular features and omnidirectional EPI geometric features of light field (LF) images. Based on HDM, three dedicated optimization modules are constructed, including a reflection estimation module (REM), a gradient prior module (GPM) and an illumination estimation module (IEM). These modules collaboratively compensate for missing texture details, suppress image noise and restore distorted illumination information to achieve high-fidelity L3FE and stable cross-view consistency. Extensive experimental results verify that the proposed HFPnet outperforms current state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms.

Article.Title: Quantum criticality correlations in a transverse-field anisotropic cluster-XX chain
Article.Authors: Abbasi M.; Mahboob N.; Mahdavifar S.
Article.Abstract: We investigate the spin-1/2 XX chain with an anisotropic three-spin interaction in a transverse magnetic field, a model in which cluster interactions provide a tunable route to unconventional quantum phases and low-energy spectral reconstructions. We focus on how the anisotropy of the three-spin coupling modifies the field-driven evolution of gapless phases and their quantum correlations beyond the conventional gap-closing scenario. We find a rich phase structure containing both gapped and gapless regimes, including a Lifshitz-type gapless–gapless transition associated with a reconstruction of the low-energy Fermi points while the excitation gap remains closed. For the anisotropy parameter \(\beta <0\) , the field can drive a sequence of two gapless phases followed by a gapped phase, whereas for the anisotropy parameter \(\beta>0\) the system is gapless at zero field, becomes gapped immediately upon applying a finite field, and undergoes a further transition at the transverse magnetic field \(h=1\) between distinct gapped regimes. The anisotropy also produces distinct chiral and chiral-nematic correlation patterns, while concurrence and quantum discord reveal qualitatively different distributions of bipartite entanglement and more general nonclassical correlations across the phase diagram. These results show that anisotropic three-spin interactions provide a distinct extension of previously studied cluster-XX chains, in which external fields can reorganize the topology of gapless excitations and the associated correlation structure. The model therefore offers an exactly solvable framework for studying unconventional quantum criticality arising from the interplay of cluster interactions, field control, and quantum correlations.

Article.Title: Occupational solvent exposure and Parkinson’s disease: evidence from PPMI online
Article.Authors: Martinez H.; Luna-Rangel F.; Gutierrez-Treviño O.; Armengol-Garcia C.; Luna J.; Gonzalez-Bedolla B.; Martinez B.; Figueroa-Sanchez J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Occupational exposures are increasingly implicated in Parkinson’s disease (PD), but the role of specific organic solvents remains unclear, and solvents are rarely encountered alone. To examine whether occupational solvent exposure is associated with PD and whether individual solvents can be distinguished from one another. We analyzed 41,315 PPMI Online participants who completed an occupational chemical exposure questionnaire, 33,709 of them in fully adjusted models. Exposure to 13 organic solvents was ascertained by self-reported occupational use of at least 100 days. Logistic regression with false discovery rate correction estimated adjusted odds ratios (aOR), adjusting for sex, education, household income, caffeine intake, smoking status, and severe head injury; age was not recorded for controls. Solvents were modeled individually and then simultaneously, and cumulative exposure by the number of solvents reported and by ten-year age bands before age 50. Seven solvents were associated with PD in single-solvent models: trichloroethylene, kerosene, carbon tetrachloride, mineral spirits, methyl ethyl ketone, toluene, and jet fuel. With all 13 modeled simultaneously, associations persisted for trichloroethylene (aOR 1.65, 95% CI 1.39–1.96), kerosene (1.50, 1.30–1.74), mineral spirits (1.27, 1.13–1.42), and carbon tetrachloride (1.28, 1.05–1.55), but not for methyl ethyl ketone, toluene, or jet fuel. Odds rose monotonically with the number of solvents reported (1.16 per additional solvent, 1.13–1.20), but showed no gradient across age bands before 50. Reported occupational solvent exposure was associated with higher odds of PD, with positive associations confined after mutual adjustment to four solvents. Given the cross-sectional design and self-reported exposure, these findings are hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Metasurface-integrated multiband arrow-shaped antenna with spoof signals suppression for GNSS applications
Article.Authors: Kumar G.; Zaidi A.; Kumar S.; Srivastava K.; Kanaujia B.; Rengarajan S.; Kumar O.; Mainuddin N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, an arrow-shaped dual-band monopole antenna array designed specifically for the L1 GNSS and ISM-band applications is presented. The designed antenna operates at the bandwidths of 1.54–1.97 GHz and 2.74–3.45 GHz, covering GNSS and mid-band 5G (sub-6 GHz) spectrum. A dual-band metasurface is employed to improve the antenna radiation pattern and gain over the resonant bands. The directional radiation pattern of the antenna helps the receiving system to identify spoofed signals that affect receiver timing and positional accuracy. The proposed antenna gain varies from 3 to 7 dB throughout the resonant bands, thus providing a reliable solution for both secure GNSS and broader wireless communication, and this architecture provide spatial diversity that can be directly exploited for spoofing identification and mitigation. In addition, improvement in time to first fix (TTFF) in GNSS system is implemented. To the authors’ best knowledge, this is the first reported design of an array of arrow-shaped monopole antennas integrated with a microstrip line for spoof signal suppression along with TTFF evaluation.

Article.Title: Residual effects of combining bone char with some amendments on phosphorus availability and coriander growth in calcareous sandy soil
Article.Authors: Barakat A.; Usman A.; Roshdy N.; Amin A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bone char is a promising phosphorus-rich fertilizer for recycling phosphorus-containing wastes. However, the phosphorus in bone char has relatively low solubility, which can be improved by modifying bone char or combining it with other materials. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the residual effects of twelve treatments applied to a previous spinach crop, including control (CK), bone + sulfur (B + S), bone + humic acid (B + HA), bone char + sulfur (BC + S), bone char + humic acid (BC + HA), modified bone char (MBC), modified bone char + humic acid (MBC + HA), acidified bone char with 0.1 N H₂SO₄ (0.1ABC), acidified bone char with 1 N H₂SO₄ (1ABC), rock phosphate (RP), rock phosphate + sulfur (RP + S), and rock phosphate + humic acid (RP + HA), on soil chemical properties, phosphorus availability, apparent phosphorus recovery efficiency, and coriander growth in calcareous sandy soil. The experiment was conducted in a sequential cropping system using a completely randomized design with three replicates. The residual effect of applying B + S, B + HA, BC + S, BC + HA, MBC, MBC + HA, 0.1ABC, 1ABC, and RP + S treatments significantly improved phosphorus availability in calcareous sandy soil. The concentration of available phosphorus increased from 8.86 mg kg − 1 (control treatment) to 14.39, 12.09, 17.94, 12.79, 18.34, 19.11, 13.93, 16.38, 11.85 and, 10.61 mg kg − 1 for B + S, B + HA, BC + S, BC + HA, MBC, MBC + HA, 0.1ABC, 1ABC, RP + S, and RP + HA respectively. Compared to the control, the residual effect of adding BC + S caused a significant increase in the weight of fresh shoots of coriander plants grown in sandy calcareous soil. The weight of fresh coriander shoots increased from 21.77 g pot − 1 for the control treatment to 33.65 g pot − 1 for the BC + S treatment. However, the residual effect of B + HA and BC + S significantly enhanced coriander dry weight. Dry weight increased from 2.66 g pot − 1 in the control to 3.33, 4.21, 4.78, 3.93, 3.87, 3.81, 3.43, 3.78, 3.19, and 3.12 g pot − 1 under B + S, B + HA, BC + S, BC + HA, MBC, MBC + HA, 0.1ABC, 1ABC, RP + S, and RP + HA treatments, respectively. The highest values of fresh and dry shoot weights of coriander were recorded with the residual effect of BC + S. Our results indicate that the residual application of bone char, especially when combined with sulfur and modified bone char, effectively improves phosphorus availability and coriander growth in calcareous sandy soil.

Article.Title: Assessment of Wuchereria bancrofti infection among the migrant populations in South India
Article.Authors: Balasubramaniyan R.; Abraham P.; Vasuki V.; Krishnamoorthi R.; Saravanan C.; Kumar B.; Raju K.; Hoti S.; Kumar A.; Rahi M.; Shanthakumar P.; Shabura M.; Dahiya D.; Selvavinayagam T.; Vadivelan P.; Sriramulu G.; Venkateswarlu B.; Kumari R.; Vinoth P.
Article.Abstract: Lymphatic filariasis (LF) is one of the major public health problems in India and in spite of existence of the national filaria control programme since 1955. It is currently being interrupted the LF transmission in twelve states through a mission-mode mass drug administration by Diethyl Carbamazine (DEC) and Albendazole / DEC, Albandazole and Ivermectin (IDA). The major challenge of elimination is migration of human population is the reservoir of local transmission of infection. The study aims to assess the LF infection among migrants in two different migrant settlement areas by night blood survey (NBS) and Molecular Xenomonitoring (MX) and also socioeconomic status of migrants. It is essential to prevent the introduction of new infection / resurgence of further transmission and this result will be helpful for ongoing elimination efforts. Microfilariae (Mf) survey was carried out in two different migrant settlement areas of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Migration information based on a questionnaire-based survey of migrants (Out-migrants and Internal migrants), along with a microfilariae survey, was conducted by collecting night blood samples, which were then stained with Giemsa stain and examined under the microscope for the presence of microfilariae. Female Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes were collected using gravid traps, morphologically identified, and pooled separately for molecular xenomonitoring (MX) to detect filarial infection. Genomic DNA was extracted from pooled Cx. quinquefasciatus mosquitoes using a simple extraction protocol and analyzed by long DNA repeat (LDR) based real-time PCR assay for detection of Wuchereria bancrofti DNA in vector mosquitoes. A total of 278 migrants was enrolled, comprising 52 individuals from the Thirukovilur block, Kallakurichi district of Tamil Nadu, and 226 from, the Puducherry localities of Sedarapet, Thuthipet, Thondamanatham, Koodappakkam (Villianur), and Vadamangalam. All participants belonged to lower- and middle-income socioeconomic groups, and were aged 18 to 75 years. The participants had attained primary to lower secondary levels of education, and most were unaware of lymphatic filariasis and mass drug administration (MDA) program. No microfilariae were detected among migrants from Tamil Nadu, whereas the microfilaria prevalence was 3.1% among migrants from Puducherry. A total of 2047 Cx. quinquefasciatus mosquitoes were collected from Puducherry and grouped in to 94 pools (1–25 mosquitoes per pool). Five pools tested positive for W. bancrofti DNA, corresponding to an overall infection rate of 2.50% (95% CI:0.93–5.51). One pool of 11 mosquitoes was dissected, and parasite larvae at different developmental stages were detected in two individual mosquitoes. This study highlighted the presence of LF infection among migrants and their socioeconomic status and the pattern of the migrants in the study area. It indicates a risk of transmission to the local population and leads to the risk of resurgence. Hence, future surveillance may be focused on migrant areas with vigilant monitoring and vector surveillance. Molecular Xenomonitoring is a potential tool for the detection of current / residual infection status, which is essential for successful / sustainable LF elimination.

Article.Title: Alpha-1 antitrypsin in follicular and seminal fluids and exploratory associations with IVF parameters in unexplained infertility
Article.Authors: Zyguła A.; Jezela – Stanek A.; Godek B.; Grzechocińska B.; Knap-Wielgus W.; Marianowski P.; Chorostowska - Wynimko J.; Kosiński P.
Article.Abstract: To characterize alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) concentrations in follicular and seminal fluids, provide exploratory reference values, and examine potential associations between AAT levels and selected IVF-related parameters in couples with idiopathic infertility. Prospective observational exploratory study. Thirty couples (n = 60) undergoing IVF treatment for idiopathic infertility. Quantification of AAT concentrations in follicular fluid and seminal fluid using immunonephelometry, followed by exploratory correlation analyses with clinical and embryological parameters. Associations between AAT concentrations and embryological parameters related to oocyte maturation, fertilization, and pregnancy outcome. Mean AAT concentrations were significantly higher in follicular fluid than in seminal plasma (98.15 mg/dL vs. 16.95 mg/dL; p < 0.0001). Follicular fluid AAT concentration was not associated with pregnancy outcome. Additional analyses using normalized embryological outcomes demonstrated no significant association between follicular fluid AAT concentration and MII rate, whereas a positive association was observed with fertilization rate. In seminal fluid, lower AAT concentrations were associated with a higher number of fertilized oocytes. An inverse association between seminal AAT concentration and progressive sperm motility was observed, although it did not reach conventional statistical significance (Rs = − 0.36, p = 0.05). No associations were identified between AAT concentrations and pregnancy achievement. This exploratory study provides one of the first integrated descriptions of AAT concentrations in follicular and seminal fluids in the context of IVF. While AAT levels were not associated with pregnancy achievement, observed associations with fertilization-related parameters suggest a potential relationship between AAT concentration and selected reproductive processes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies incorporating predefined endpoints, serum measurements, and functional analyses.

Article.Title: HCAN: a hierarchical CNN–attention network for multi-class malicious URL detection using dual-input feature fusion
Article.Authors: Devika S.; Kaur A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malicious URL detection is a challenging task due to the lexical ambiguity between different threat classes and lack of URL representation learning in previous works, which motivates us to design HCAN (Hierarchical CNN–Attention Network) for classifying benign, phishing, defacement, and malware URLs given their raw character sequences and handcrafted structured features. The presented approach utilizes hierarchical convolutional neural networks with multi-scale convolution, residual convolution, and multi-head self-attention modules to learn sequential patterns in the character-sequence input at different levels of abstraction. The character-based representation is combined with another sub-network processing 64 handcrafted lexical, statistical, entropy, IP, HTTPS and phishing keyword features to yield a joint embedding for downstream classification. Experiments were carried out on 629,822 pre-processed URLs from the Malicious-Phish dataset, employing leakage-aware pre-processing and five-fold out-of-fold validation. On the main dataset, HCAN achieved 92.56% accuracy, 90.61% macro-F1 and 93% weighted-F1, with phishing URLs being the hardest class with an F1 of 79%. An independent performance evaluation on external URL dataset without any re-training or fine-tuning demonstrated that our approach achieved 87.43% accuracy and 82.48% macro-F1, highlighting the ability of our approach to generalize across different URL datasets, while also uncovering some performance gaps in the face of distribution shifts. The results show the potential of the hierarchical architecture using dual-branch design for four-class malicious URL identification.

Article.Title: Rapid and visual detection of the invasive pest Lobesia botrana using an RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a-LFD system
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Zhao J.; Meng C.; Li Y.; Chen X.; Xu F.
Article.Abstract: Lobesia botrana is a major invasive pest of global viticulture, causing significant yield and economic losses. It has a broad host range, including stone fruits and berries, and was first detected in China in 2014. Morphological identification of Lobesia botrana is challenging, particularly at larval stages, necessitating a rapid and reliable molecular approach. In this study, we developed a rapid and visual detection method based on recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) coupled with the CRISPR/Cas12a system and a lateral flow dipstick (LFD) readout. The assay specifically distinguished Lobesia botrana from four closely related orchard pests. The key parameters for RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a were systematically optimized. Under optimized conditions, the complete RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a platform achieved a limit of detection of 1 × 10 − 3 ng/µL for Lobesia botrana genomic DNA. The whole assay was performed under low-temperature isothermal conditions at 37–38 °C (RPA at 38 °C and CRISPR/Cas12a at 37 °C). When combined with rapid on-site DNA extraction, the total sample-to-result time was approximately 45 min. The assay was further validated using field-collected Lobesia botrana samples from different geographical origins and different developmental stages, including egg, 1st–5th instar larvae, pupa, and adult, and all tested samples produced positive results. This RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a-LFD system provides a rapid, sensitive, and visual detection platform for Lobesia botrana , demonstrating potential for field application.

Article.Title: A hybrid GWO-PSO-based MPPT controller for high-efficiency grid-connected PV-assisted EV charging under dynamic conditions
Article.Authors: Saif H.; Mnati M.; Fayadh R.; Aldahmashi J.; Emara A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems with electric vehicle (EV) charging is challenging because conventional MPPT algorithms perform poorly under changing weather conditions. To improve the performance of a grid-tied PV-EV charging system, this paper proposes and validates a hybrid Grey Wolf Optimizer–Particle Swarm Optimization (GWO-PSO) algorithm for MPPT control. An integrated system model comprising a PV array, a boost converter, a 3-level voltage-source converter (VSC), and a battery-charging subsystem was developed in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed GWO-PSO algorithm, which combines the exploration capability of GWO with the exploitation capability of PSO, was compared with conventional GWO, PSO, and INC algorithms under step-change and variable-weather operating conditions. For the step-change irradiance case, the simulation results show that the proposed GWO-PSO method achieved a tracking efficiency of 97.979%, an average steady-state PV power of 100.15 kW, and a harvested energy of 41.121 Wh over the post-step interval from 1.00 s to 2.50 s. It also exhibited a post-convergence PV power ripple of 54.31 W and reached the steady-state MPP region within 0.0876 s based on a ± 2% convergence criterion. Under variable irradiance and temperature conditions, the proposed controller achieved a tracking efficiency of 91.57%, an average PV power of 70.543 kW, and a harvested energy of 48.988 Wh over the selected evaluation interval, outperforming the conventional PSO and GWO methods in terms of energy extraction and tracking accuracy. Under grid-only operating conditions, the controller also maintained stable DC-link regulation and effective battery charging performance. This improved MPPT performance contributes to effective battery charging, while the VSC maintains a regulated 500 V DC-link throughout the tested cases. Overall, the hybrid GWO-PSO controller improves PV energy extraction and supports stable PV-assisted EV charging operation under the tested simulation conditions.

Article.Title: Ternary choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents for continuous gas dehumidification: performance benchmarking against triethylene glycol
Article.Authors: Aliasgari M.; Shahin H.; Rezaeiyan Z.; Keshavarz P.
Article.Abstract: This research evaluates deep eutectic solvents (DES) as potential alternatives to conventional glycol-based desiccants for gas dehydration, highlighting their low volatility, tunable composition, and strong water-binding abilities. However, experimental studies on novel ternary hygroscopic DESs designed for gas dehydration remain limited. In this study, we synthesized and tested a series of ternary choline chloride-based DESs for air moisture absorption and potential use in gas dehydration systems. We characterized their physical properties by measuring density, viscosity, and pH, and confirmed molecular interactions using FTIR and ¹H NMR spectroscopy. Air dehumidification experiments at room temperature with a controlled humidity system assessed the hygroscopic properties of these DESs. Water absorption rates and relative humidity were monitored throughout the tests. All six ternary DES formulations remained stable as single phases for 72 h. The ChCl: Lactic Acid: TEG and ChCl: Lactic Acid: MDEA systems achieved minimum relative humidity values of 1.3% and reduced the dew point temperature to − 35 °C. The ChCl: Acetamide: MeOH and ChCl: Citric Acid·H₂O: MeOH systems showed the highest water absorption capacities at 12.28 wt% and 12.39 wt%, respectively. These findings demonstrate a correlation between DES composition, physicochemical properties, and hygroscopic performance, highlighting the potential of these ternary DESs for dehumidification under the investigated laboratory conditions and their prospective application as liquid desiccants for natural-gas dehydration, subject to further validation under representative pressurized gas conditions.

Article.Title: Impact of implementation of an antifungal stewardship program in a surgical intensive care unit at a tertiary care hospital in a developing country: a quasi-experimental study
Article.Authors: Negm E.; Gouda A.; Shahin M.; Refky M.; Soliman S.; Eldeen S.; Naser E.; Shahin M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bloodstream infections (BSIs) caused by Candida species are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. While early antifungal therapy is crucial, inappropriate use drives resistance and escalates costs, necessitating structured Antifungal Stewardship (AFS) programs. To evaluate the impact of implementing an AFS program on the incidence of fungal infections, the quality of antifungal prescribing, antifungal consumption and costs, and clinical outcomes in a surgical Intensive Care Unit (ICU). A prospective, quasi-experimental study was conducted over 18 months in a 25-bed surgical ICU at Zagazig University Hospitals. The study comprised three 6-month phases: baseline (observational), implementation (interventional education and policy), and programme continuation (prospective audit and feedback). A total of 270 patients with risk factors for fungal infection were enrolled (135 per phase). The primary outcome was the change in Candida infection incidence. Secondary outcomes included prescription quality scores, antifungal consumption in Defined Daily Doses (DDD), costs, and clinical outcomes. Physician knowledge was assessed via pre- and post-intervention questionnaires. The incidence of Candida infection showed a non-significant numerical reduction from 22.2% to 20.0% ( p = 0.997). However, the AFS program significantly improved the global quality of antifungal prescribing, with the total prescription adequacy score increasing from 6.1 ± 1.5 to 7.8 ± 1.5 ( p = 0.007). Physician knowledge and attitude scores improved markedly from 12.7 ± 3.9 to 21.0 ± 2.8 ( p < 0.001). Favorable but non-significant trends were observed in antifungal costs, ICU length of stay (LOS), and mechanical ventilation duration. In-hospital mortality remained stable (55.6% vs. 54.8%; p = 1.000), confirming the intervention’s safety. Implementation of a multifaceted AFS program in a resource-limited surgical ICU significantly enhanced the quality of antifungal prescribing and physician knowledge without compromising patient safety. While immediate reductions in infection incidence were not statistically significant, the improvements in key process measures are essential prerequisites for long-term clinical and economic benefits. The findings strongly support the integration of routine AFS into critical care practice.

Article.Title: Integrated placental metabolomic and lipidomic profiling reveals class-specific lipid remodelling in severe preeclampsia
Article.Authors: Han H.; Baek M.; Yang S.; Han S.; Kim D.; Kim N.; Lee H.; Jung S.; Kim M.; Ryu H.; Lim J.
Article.Abstract: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity, yet the placental metabolic changes associated with disease severity remain poorly defined. We combined untargeted metabolite profiling with targeted quantification of 173 lipid species across 12 classes in placentas from normotensive ( n = 9), non-severe preeclamptic ( n = 5) and severe preeclamptic ( n = 7) pregnancies. Of 43 preselected metabolite features, four differed between control and severe preeclampsia, three of them lipid-related, whereas metabolites of central carbon metabolism were unchanged. In the lipidome, 87 species differed between control and severe preeclampsia after false-discovery-rate correction, but none between control and non-severe preeclampsia. The pattern was class-specific and bidirectional: all 42 membrane phospholipid species that differed were reduced, as were five of six ceramide species, whereas all 28 differing triacylglycerol and cholesteryl ester species were increased. Triacylglycerol was the most extensively affected class and the only class that also differed between non-severe and severe preeclampsia. Most class-level differences persisted after adjustment for gestational age at delivery. Severe preeclampsia is thus accompanied by a coordinated loss of membrane phospholipids and ceramide together with neutral lipid accumulation in the placenta; because severe disease and fetal growth restriction coincided, their contributions could not be separated.

Article.Title: Lightweight dynamic graph reinforcement learning for adaptive stock portfolio optimization
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Chen S.
Article.Abstract: Traditional graph neural network based portfolio optimization methods rely on fixed topological structures to model stock correlations, which fail to capture the structural changes in stock linkages during industry rotation and market style shifts. Moreover, full-scale dynamic graph approaches incur prohibitive computational overhead, making them inefficient for the iterative training of deep reinforcement learning on large-scale asset pools. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a lightweight dynamic graph reinforcement learning (LDGRL) framework for adaptive stock portfolio optimization. The framework first constructs a dynamically evolving stock correlation graph based on rolling return correlations, capital flow patterns, and market sentiment signals. A dual pruning mechanism including adaptive edge filtering and node screening is adopted to generate sparse topology, enabling dynamic updates of graph connections. Notably, the global asset pool remains fixed to ensure consistent reinforcement learning action dimensions. We propose a unified triple lightweight design strategy: dynamic topology dual pruning, local consistent subgraph sampling, and shallow sparse graph convolution combined with principal component analysis feature dimensionality reduction. This design reduces computational complexity while preserving critical correlation information. The dynamic graph embeddings are then fed into an improved twin trust region policy optimization agent to generate dynamic position allocation decisions. A unique topology-decision closed-loop mechanism is introduced to dynamically adjust key hyperparameters of graph reconstruction using investment returns and risk feedback. Extensive experiments on the CSI 300 index constituent stocks show that LDGRL achieves higher cumulative return and lower maximum drawdown than state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning approaches, with a competitive Sharpe ratio.

Article.Title: The numerical investigation of the design, analysis, and validation of a screw-compressor with the Rack-profile method
Article.Authors: Shafiei E.; Heidarian Shahri M.; Madadi A.
Article.Abstract: Screw compressors are classified as a type of positive displacement compressor, which currently constitutes a significant portion of the sales of operational positive displacement compressors. The increasing popularity of this type of compressor in recent years can be attributed to new designs with complex geometries that have led to reduced leakage flow and increased pressure ratios. Additionally, advancements in machining tools and manufacturing processes have enabled the production of rotors with intricate geometries and design tolerances down to the micrometer level, all at a competitive cost and high performance. Due to the rotary nature of all moving parts, these compressors exhibit lower weight and higher reliability compared to similar-capacity reciprocating compressors. These factors have contributed to the widespread use of screw compressors across various industries, particularly in the oil and gas sector. Despite significant advancements in the design and simulation of screw compressors, the knowledge surrounding their design remains proprietary, held by a limited number of companies. Therefore, this research begins with a comprehensive examination of screw compressors, including their history, operational principles, types, advantages, and disadvantages. Following the literature review and terminology used, as well as common methods in the design of these compressors, the design of a screw compressor using the rack profile method is detailed. With an understanding of the screw compressor design methodology, the SCORG software for generating screw compressor meshes is introduced, and a sample screw compressor is meshed using this software. The generated mesh is then coupled and transferred to ANSYS CFX software for a complete three-dimensional transient model solution within its geometric domain. By increasing the number of mesh elements in the leakage path region, a comparison is made between the numerical results and experimental results. The findings indicate that this increase in mesh density has reduced the discrepancy between the numerical solutions and experimental outcomes.

Article.Title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
Article.Authors: Fici A.; Casiraghi C.; Monticelli B.; Accardi S.; Bilucaglia M.; Rossi C.; Corsaro D.; Zito M.; Russo V.
Article.Abstract: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

Article.Title: FBBDL: flow-aware benign-behavior deviation learning for leakage-controlled unseen-family DoS detection
Article.Authors: Purohit S.; Pradhan S.; Nigam N.
Article.Abstract: Detecting previously unseen denial-of-service (DoS) attack families remains challenging because conventional random or stratified splits may allow family-specific information to influence model development, while imbalanced attack distributions can bias detection toward dominant families. This study proposes Flow-Aware Benign-Behavior Deviation Learning (FBBDL), a leakage-controlled framework for unseen-family DoS detection using aggregated network-flow statistics. FBBDL excludes every bin containing a target-family flow from all development stages and integrates duplicate-group-disjoint cross-fitted benign-deviation estimation, tempered family-frequency weighting, nested pseudo-unseen-family validation, and development-only false-positive-rate (FPR) control. Experiments on 692,692 eligible flows from the Wednesday CIC-IDS2017 capture evaluated four independently withheld DoS families over 20 matched seeds. FBBDL achieved a macro recall of 95.64%, a macro geometric mean (G-mean) of 0.975, and a worst-family G-mean of 0.958, with a mean benign FPR of 0.62%. Compared with class-weighted XGBoost (CW-XGB), the strongest evaluated baseline, FBBDL improved macro and worst-family G-mean by 0.016 and 0.033, respectively; the paired differences remained significant after Holm correction (( p < 0.001)). Ablation experiments identified multi-flow temporal aggregation as the dominant contributor, with additional gains from benign-reference deviation, family-frequency weighting, and nested family withholding. Sensitivity analyses further indicated stable performance across the evaluated aggregation and balancing settings. The frozen detector required 0.81 ms per aggregated bin, corresponding to approximately 1,235 bins per second. An independent Wednesday-to-Friday transfer evaluation revealed important limitations: although DDoS score ranking remained strong (normalized pAUROC@1% = 0.997), the frozen threshold produced a benign FPR of 30.23%, exceeding the 1% operating target, while PortScan recall was only 0.14%. These findings support the effectiveness of FBBDL under the evaluated within-capture family-withheld setting, while demonstrating that reliable cross-capture operation cannot be inferred from score-ranking performance alone.

Article.Title: Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance
Article.Authors: Willinger D.; Wunderl S.; Stieger S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Research has shown that SARS-CoV-2 infection can impact cognition in adulthood. Less is known about its cognitive impact in adolescence, a critical neurodevelopmental period. Based on data from N = 3,860 adolescents in Lower Austria ( M age = 13.5 years), we used multivariate regression and machine learning analyses to examine how self-reported COVID-19 history (infection occurrence, symptom severity) was related to performance on cognitive and (psycho)motor performance tests. While infection occurrence was not linked to performance, more severe COVID-19 symptom courses were significantly associated with lower logical reasoning and numerical ability without significant gender differences, as well as lower verbal ability specifically among girls. The machine learning models corroborated the regression findings for reasoning and verbal ability and additionally identified fine finger dexterity and long-term memory as showing non-linear associations with symptom severity relative to their linear regression coefficients. The observed effect sizes are practically meaningful, corresponding to an estimated 3- to 7-point performance deficit on standardized cognitive scales for the least and most severe symptom courses. Our findings indicate that adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. The results underline the need to investigate whether and how COVID-19 affects adolescents’ neurocognitive development, which may be specific for gender.

Article.Title: Associations of Epstein–Barr virus DNA and transcriptional activity with interferon signaling, pyroptosis, and microRNA signatures in oral lichen planus
Article.Authors: Aghdam H.; Najafi A.; Enjilelahi D.; Pakdel F.; Eslami H.; Nahand J.
Article.Abstract: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disorder, but the molecular factors shaping its immune response remain unclear. Here, we explored associations of Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) positivity with interferon, inflammasome, and microRNA expression in OLP. Public datasets lacked sample-level EBV status and informed OLP-associated pathway analysis and target prioritization. Separately, we examined oral tissues from 35 patients with OLP and 35 controls for EBV DNA; LMP1, BZLF1, and BRLF1 transcripts; genes involved in inflammation, interferon responses, and pyroptosis; and seven mature miRNAs. Transcriptomic analysis revealed consistent enrichment of interferon-γ, interferon-α, inflammatory response and TNF–NF-κB pathways in OLP. EBV DNA was detected in 8 of 35 OLP samples and 4 of 35 controls, although this difference was not significant. Among EBV-positive tissues, LMP1 was the most frequently detected viral transcript; the observed BZLF1 and BRLF1 differences were based on very few detectable specimens. OLP tissues displayed broad upregulation of genes involved in inflammation, interferon responses, and pyroptosis. The primary molecular signature was OLP-associated; after adjustment for disease status, no host marker retained a significant EBV association following correction for multiple testing. miR-155-5p, miR-146a-5p, miR-21-5p and miR-142-3p were increased in OLP, while miR-27b-3p was reduced. Overall, OLP was characterized by interferon and inflammatory responses, altered miRNAs, and transcriptional priming of pyroptosis-related pathways. EBV-associated findings are exploratory because the positive subgroups and transcript-detectable subsets were small, and pooled comparisons may be confounded by disease status. These data do not establish that EBV drives a distinct inflammatory program in OLP.

Article.Title: Non-invasive MRI-based assessment of early radiation-induced normal tissue effects in the in ovo chicken embryo model
Article.Authors: Monti S.; D’Alterio C.; Licenziato L.; Sarnella A.; Terlizzi C.; Ferrara Y.; Prinster A.; Albanese S.; Buono M.; Oliviero C.; Maruccio L.; Borrelli L.; Ambrosio T.; Scala S.; Pacelli R.; Cella L.
Article.Abstract: Emerging radiation therapy modalities require robust preclinical models to characterize normal tissue effects. We evaluated the feasibility of longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for detecting radiation-induced alterations in the in ovo chicken embryo model. Twenty-four fertilized chicken eggs were incubated under standardized conditions. At Embryonic Development Day (EDD) 5, 12 embryos received 4 Gy using a 6-MV linac, and 12 served as controls. Six embryos per group underwent longitudinal 7T MRI at EDD9, 12, and 15. T2-weighted imaging was used to measure brain biparietal diameter (BPD), whole-brain, heart, and liver volumes, and normalized liver signal (nLS). Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) was also performed. Histopathology in the target organs and digital quantification of hepatic vascular stasis were performed at EDD 15. Survival at EDD15 was 83% (20/24), with no significant difference between irradiated and control groups. EDD12 was the earliest developmental time point at which all target organs could be consistently visualized and quantitatively assessed by MRI. Irradiation significantly affected longitudinal changes in whole-brain and heart volumes. BPD and whole-brain volume showed the strongest discrimination between groups at EDD12 and EDD15 (adjusted p < 0.05). At EDD15, heart volume and nLS values were lower in irradiated embryos, with large effect sizes, although the differences between-group were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Histopathology showed increased hepatic vascular stasis in irradiated embryos ( p = 0.002), consistent with the lower nLS values observed on MRI. DTI data were limited by image quality constraints. These findings demonstrate for the first time the feasibility of longitudinal MRI for investigating radiation-induced tissue alterations in ovo , identify potentially informative imaging readouts and developmental time points, supporting further evaluation of this ethically acceptable model in comparative radiobiological studies.

Article.Title: A robust and interpretable hybrid SunAFNet framework for sunflower classification with adversarial resilience and mIoU-validated explainability
Article.Authors: Hossan M.; Riyad T.; Assaduzzaman M.; Bijoy M.; Hasan M.; Samad M.; Ohidujjaman N/A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate and reliable monitoring of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) developmental phases and health status is fundamental for optimizing agricultural yields and ensuring global food security. Manual diagnostics are subjective and time-consuming, and most stand-alone deep learning architectures are limited in their ability to accurately model the fine-grained spatial texture and long-range relationships between the various parts of the capitulum. For this study, we introduce a novel dual-stream hybrid framework: SunAFNet which combines a frozen DenseNet201 backbone with a selectively fine-tuned Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16). The key component of the architecture is a flexible Attention Fusion Module, which dynamically weights local spatial descriptors and global contextual features based on input complexity with an MLP-Softmax mechanism. SunAFNet has been evaluated on a large image dataset of 5,111 images of capitula of five growth and health classes and resulted in a diagnostic accuracy of 97.26%, which is better than the existing CNN and Transformer baselines. The framework showed very high generalization capability, achieving 94.26% accuracy on an independent secondary dataset, and remained very close to the optimal Robustness Index of 0.9899 despite various environmental and digital perturbations. A low value of the Expected Calibration Error (ECE 0.0675) was found, and the model achieved near-perfect selective prediction (accuracy 1.000) on clean data. Furthermore, SunAFNet demonstrated pronounced defensive resilience across a multi-level FGSM adversarial spectrum ( \(\:\epsilon\in\:\left\{0.01,0.05,0.10,0.20,0.30\right\}\) ), maintaining 71.71% accuracy at \(\:ϵ=0.10\:\) and retaining 42.35% diagnostic capability even under extreme perturbation ( \(\epsilon = 0.30\) ), well above stochastic chance. Moreover, a multi-layered Explainable AI (XAI) suite was validated empirically to ensure that the model’s logic is based on biologically relevant floral markers with a statistically significant mIoU of 0.7487 ( p = 0.0098), ensuring grounded diagnostic decisions. SunAFNet can provide a platform to support real-time precision agricultural monitoring, which is both fast and efficient in terms of both computing and inference speed, with an inference latency of merely 38.35 ms.

Article.Title: Global warming extends boreal fire seasons into uncharted territory
Article.Authors: Ruiz D.; Netherton S.; Weaver A.; Whaley C.; Abraham C.; Goldblatt C.; Flannigan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recent wildfire disasters in communities such as Fort McMurray and Jasper in Canada, and across Siberia, highlight the growing vulnerability of boreal regions to prolonged fire-conducive conditions under a warming climate. Here, we use 5000-year Earth system model simulations to quantify how quasi steady-state global warming alters the boreal fire-season length across North America and Eurasia. We find that the simulated area-weighted boreal fire season lengthens by $$\sim $$ 12 ± 2 days per $$^\circ $$ C of global mean warming, driven primarily by higher near-surface temperatures and reduced snow cover. Under present-day warming, the mean boreal fire season is already extended by approximately two weeks relative to pre-industrial conditions. The fire-season length spatial pattern remains broadly conserved, but warming shifts the entire boreal domain toward earlier onset and later termination, with the largest proportional increases in high-latitude regions where historical fire seasons were shortest. The area of the boreal forest experiencing fire seasons outside the range of pre-industrial variability increases with warming, leading to increasingly widespread unprecedented fire seasons. Above 2 $$^\circ $$ C of global warming, much of the boreal forest faces unusually long fire seasons. Keeping warming below 2 $$^\circ $$ C could significantly limit the geographic extent and consequences of unprecedented boreal fire seasons.

Article.Title: Electroporation outcomes in human Jurkat cells are affected by exposure to simulated microgravity
Article.Authors: Conway M.; Sedelnikova A.; Sander E.; Worthington K.; Steelman Z.
Article.Abstract: Electroporation (EP) is commonly used to permeabilize cell membranes to deliver nucleic acids and other biomolecules. EP-based methodologies have the potential to support in-space biomanufacturing; however, it is currently unclear whether cellular adaptations to microgravity influence EP outcomes. To investigate this, human T-lymphocyte (Jurkat) cells were exposed to simulated microgravity (SµG) in a rotating wall vessel (RWV) bioreactor prior to EP to deliver exogenous fluorescent molecules or plasmid DNA. We observed that 2 h of SµG exposure led to a 20% decrease in fluorophore uptake and a 31% decrease in transfection efficiency compared to standard gravity controls for several voltages. To explore underlying mechanisms, the effects of SµG on actin organization were assessed using a phalloidin stain, which revealed increased cell area and cortical actin thickness following SµG. Actin targeting drugs jasplakinolide and latrunculin B were used to promote or destabilize F-actin, respectively, and modulated cell area and cortical actin thickness. Promoting F-actin also led to decreased transfection efficiency, mimicking the effect of SµG, while destabilizing F-actin in SµG showed a small non-significant increase in transfection efficiency, slightly reversing the impact of SµG. Our results indicate that cellular adaptations to altered mechanical environments, such as SµG, can influence transfection efficiency.

Article.Title: Electrical stimulation combined with exercise therapy for chronic neck pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Mollazadeh M.; Ramezanpour S.; Zarei H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the additional therapeutic benefits of combining electrical stimulation modalities with structured exercise therapy compared with exercise alone in adults with chronic nonspecific neck pain. A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and Web of Science from inception to June 25, 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating electrical stimulation combined with exercise therapy in chronic neck pain (≥ 3 months) were included. Two independent reviewers screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool and methodological quality using the PEDro scale. Hedges’ g effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals were computed using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Eight studies involving 375 participants were included. The combined intervention significantly improved pain intensity (Hedges’ g = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.60 to 1.08, p = 0.001 across eight intervention arms, with low heterogeneity (I² = 19.49%). Disability showed large improvements (Hedges’ g = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.54 to 0.98, p = 0.001 across seven intervention arms, with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 48.11%). Cervical range of motion significantly improved (Hedges’ g = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.19 to 0.91, p = 0.001 across three intervention arms, with low heterogeneity (I² = 22.49%). Exploratory subgroup analyses by electrical stimulation modality revealed consistent benefits across tDCS, IFC, TENS, and NMES; however, these analyses are limited by the small number of studies per subgroup. No publication bias was detected; however, publication bias tests are underpowered with the limited number of studies included. Combining electrical stimulation with exercise may provide short-term benefits for pain and disability in adults with chronic nonspecific neck pain, with moderate-to-large pooled effect sizes. However, the certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate, and the pain MCID conclusion was sensitive to standard-deviation assumptions. Current evidence is insufficient to recommend routine integration of electrical stimulation into exercise programs, and the concept of exercise nonresponders was not directly evaluated. Adequately powered trials with complete outcome reporting and longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Design and evaluation of indole-based hydrazones targeting heparanase with cytotoxic activity in human breast cancer cells
Article.Authors: Padmapriya M.; Manjunath R.; Thompson E.; Toh A.; Beeraka N.; Kempasiddegowda M.; Lobie P.; Nikolenko V.; Basappa B.; Sinha R.; Gandhi N.; Gaonkar S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heparanase, an endoglycosidase implicated in tumour growth, invasion, and metastasis,​ remains an attractive target for anticancer drug discovery. In this study, a series of indole-based hydrazones was designed to target heparanase with potential anticancer inhibition in breast cancer cells. Structure-based analyses, including molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, suggested that several derivatives can interact with residues in the heparanase binding region, including recurrent contacts involving GLU 225, GLN 270, HIS 296, TYR 298, and TYR 348. In silico ADME profiling indicated generally acceptable drug-like properties for the designed series. The designed compounds were synthesized and characterized by FTIR, 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, and HRMS, and conformational features were further examined by DFT studies. Among the synthesized compounds evaluated for heparanase inhibition using the HTRF assay, derivative E showed the highest apparent inhibitory response; however, its activity remained substantially weaker than that of the reference inhibitor PG545 and lacked a clear dose-dependent trend, indicating only modest inhibitory potential. Furthermore, cytotoxicity testing in MCF-7 breast cancer cells identified compound A as the most active compound, with an IC 50 value of 2.078 µM. Overall, these results identify indole-based hydrazones as preliminary scaffolds for further optimization toward heparanase-related anticancer applications.

Article.Title: Syntax-guided multi-granularity fusion for multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Xiao L.; Gao Y.; Cui B.; Tan P.; Tan Z.
Article.Abstract: Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (MABSA) aims to predict the sentiment polarity toward a given aspect term from social-media image–text pairs. Prior approaches often under-exploit hierarchical visual cues and do not explicitly leverage syntactic constraints to bind aspect terms with their sentiment-bearing opinion expressions, which weakens aspect-specific cross-modal alignment under noisy visual content. To this end, we propose a Multi-Granularity Gated Fusion Network (MGGFN) that couples syntax-aware evidence modeling with multi-granularity visual–text representation learning. MGGFN constructs a weighted graph by combining probabilistic dependency weights with semantic similarities between visually enhanced textual nodes. Scene-level captions and face-level descriptions provide global visual-semantic context. An adaptive gating mechanism then integrates global context and local evidence for aspect-level sentiment prediction. Experiments on Twitter-2015 and Twitter-2017 show that MGGFN achieves mean macro-F1 scores of 73.2 and 69.6, respectively, across three runs. Among the compared methods, MGGFN demonstrates competitive performance on both datasets, supporting its effectiveness for aspect-level multimodal sentiment prediction. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/BlackHand12138/MGGFN-MABSA.git .

Article.Title: Dynamic attention-based multimodal fusion for audience emotion analysis in interactive media
Article.Authors: Li J.; Yang H.; Lei Z.
Article.Abstract: The interactive film and television (FAT) system urgently requires real-time audience emotion understanding, but existing methods inadequately capture subtle emotional variations in dynamic audiovisual contexts. This study proposes a multimodal emotion recognition model for FAT scenarios, integrating facial expressions, vocal prosody, and audiovisual contextual features under real-time interaction constraints. It incorporates the Temporal Context Synchronization Attention (TCSA) mechanism to align user response sequences with audiovisual content features and capture stimulus–response causal associations, and the Dynamic Weighted Routing (DWR) strategy to adaptively adjust visual, auditory, and contextual fusion weights across FAT genres. On IEMOCAP and LIRIS-ACCEDE, the jointly trained model achieves 87.9% and 87.2% accuracy, with F1-scores of 87.8% and 87.0%. Under the same joint training setting, the overall accuracy and F1 score on the combined IEMOCAP+LIRIS-ACCEDE test set (approximately 2,310 samples) are 87.6% and 87.4%, respectively. These values represent the sample-size-weighted averages of the results from the IEMOCAP and LIRIS-ACCEDE test sets. Under the specific six-class relabeling scheme of IEMOCAP, recognition of Low-Arousal Sadness (LAS), a non-clinical state, improves from 62.3% with the two-stream baseline (without TCSA/DWR) to 74.2% with the jointly trained full DWR-TCSA model. This represents a 19.1% relative improvement over the two-stream baseline under the same relabeling scheme, calculated as (74.2%−62.3%)/62.3%. The 74.2% result is obtained by the jointly trained full DWR-TCSA model on the IEMOCAP test set, whereas LAS recognition further increases to 75.8% (i.e., 0.758) on the combined IEMOCAP+LIRIS-ACCEDE test set. Recognition of Surprise also improves from 82.3% to 84.9%. Across five random seeds, DWR-TCSA achieves an accuracy of 0.879 ± 0.004 (95% CI [0.874, 0.884]) and an F1 score of 0.878 ± 0.005 (95% CI [0.872, 0.884]). Under leave-one-session-out (LOSO) cross-validation, its advantages over the two-stream baseline are statistically significant. Five-fold paired t-tests (df = 4) yield t(4) = 25.16, p < 0.001, for accuracy and t(4) = 30.10, p < 0.001, for LAS recall. Both differences remain significant after Holm–Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. The model also achieves a higher mean accuracy across the five random seeds than the cross-modal attention baseline (0.879 ± 0.004 vs. 0.857 ± 0.009). After lightweight optimization, the model achieves an inference speed of 72 frames per second (FPS), with a latency of 186 ms. In a real-world experiment involving 96 participants, the system achieves a mean real-time accuracy of 86.2%. This accuracy refers to the agreement between the model’s window-level predictions and the reference labels. The reference labels are primarily derived from participants’ self-reports, supplemented by consensus judgments from blinded annotators. Therefore, they represent subjective rather than independently objective labels. The experiment also yields a mean interaction satisfaction score of 4.19 out of 5.00. In a separate online questionnaire survey involving 300 valid respondents, 91.7% (275/300) report being satisfied or very satisfied with the system’s emotion recognition accuracy. The 96 participants in the aforementioned real-world experiment were recruited from this pool of 300 respondents. The framework supports intelligent interactive media experiences.

Article.Title: A geomorphic process-informed machine learning strategy for interpretable soil thickness mapping in the subtropical hilly regions of Southern China
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Huang J.; Zheng M.; Wan J.; Guo X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil thickness exhibits strong spatial heterogeneity in hilly regions, and its predictive mapping is hindered by the complexity of geomorphic processes and limited model interpretability. We develop an interpretable, process-informed framework integrating variable construction, multi-algorithm comparison, uncertainty quantification and slope-zone interpretation, and apply it in Xunwu County, subtropical China. Using 513 profiles and 35 variables spanning terrain, climate, erosion, vegetation, spectral and composite information, we compared five machine learning models—Random Forest, quantile regression forest (QRF), XGBoost, CatBoost and LightGBM—and selected the final model on held-out test data. Process information entered through process-informed features (three terrain core variables and six interaction composites) and slope-stratified interpretation and uncertainty evaluation. The composites supported interpretation, but removing them changed the mean R² from 0.418 to 0.443 (paired 95% CI − 0.015 to + 0.060), so their predictive benefit remains unproven. CatBoost achieved the highest mean R² under repeated random splits (0.418 ± 0.056; RMSE 22.94 cm; MAE 16.65 cm), followed by XGBoost (0.416 ± 0.065); the difference was not significant. This accuracy reflects local interpolation within the sampled domain: under spatial blocking and leave-quadrant-out validation, R² was − 0.84 to − 0.91 and − 0.03, respectively. The 90% QRF intervals achieved 85.4% coverage, increasing to 87.7% after conformal calibration, with a mean width of 70.4 cm. The applicability domain covered 92.9% of the area. SHAP showed that climate and topographic position dominated the gentle and transitional zones, whereas slope, spectral variables and vegetation were more prominent in the steep zone. These results support local, slope-stratified soil thickness mapping and interpretation rather than prediction in spatially independent areas.

Article.Title: Associations of managers’ AI literacy with innovative work behavior and work well-being through AI job crafting and psychological needs satisfaction
Article.Authors: Jun Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Learning to use AI is not the same as benefiting from it. As artificial intelligence becomes embedded in knowledge work, its implications are often discussed in contrasting terms—potential productivity gains and risks to well-being—raising the question of whether AI literacy is associated with both performance-related behavior and well-being. Conceptualizing AI literacy as a learnable competence, this study examines how AI literacy is associated with what managers achieve and how they experience their work. Managers here are examined as adult learners whose roles may provide opportunities to apply AI-related competence in their work. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources perspective and Self-Determination Theory, survey data from 322 managers experienced with generative AI were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. AI literacy was positively associated with AI job crafting, and AI job crafting was positively associated with psychological needs satisfaction (autonomy and competence satisfaction). AI literacy, AI job crafting, and psychological needs satisfaction were also significantly associated with innovative work behavior and work well-being, and the proposed indirect associations were statistically significant.

Article.Title: Reduced three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index in macular telangiectasia type 2 and its association with multimodal disease stage
Article.Authors: Hafner M.; Deschler D.; Mueller S.; Brunner B.; Priglinger S.; Gerhardt M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) primarily affects the retina, but choroidal involvement remains incompletely characterized. We compared three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index (3D-CVI) in 70 MacTel eyes from 35 participants and 66 healthy eyes from 33 controls using swept-source OCT angiography. Linear regression adjusted for age, sex and axial length; participant-clustered CR2 covariance and Satterthwaite inference accounted for fellow-eye dependence and limited sample size. Total 3-mm CVI was the primary endpoint. Additional analyses examined numeric and pooled disease grades, choroidal volumes, outer retinal volume and vascular–functional profiles. MacTel eyes had lower CVI (adjusted control-minus-MacTel difference, 0.119; P = 0.0013) and a negative average grade association (− 0.050 per grade; P < 0.001). Grades 3–5 had lower CVI than controls after multiplicity correction. Total choroidal volume and total choriocapillaris flow share did not differ significantly; choroidal vascular volume was lower in MacTel. Greater outer retinal volume and better acuity were associated with higher CVI after Holm correction. These cross-sectional findings suggest retinal–choroidal covariation and warrant longitudinal evaluation; prognostic and treatment-monitoring validity remain unestablished.
