Article.Title: Cyclodextrin encapsulation enhances the stability, anticancer, antimicrobial, and antibiofilm activities of chios mastic gum essential oil
Article.Authors: Lababidi J.; Alabrahim O.; No author name N/A.; Fytory M.; Abou-Shanab A.; Emad A.; Abdeldayem A.; El-Badri N.; Azzazy H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, mastic gum essential oil ( Pistacia lentiscus var. Chia; PL) was encapsulated within 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (CD). This formulation aimed to improve the limited compatibility, volatility, and stability of PL, while enhancing its biological performance. PL-CD nanoparticles were characterized using FTIR, ¹H NMR, 2D NOESY, thermal analysis, DLS, SEM, and TEM. These analyses confirmed successful encapsulation, with a high entrapment efficiency of 91.04 ± 0.76%. TEM analysis showed PL-CD nanoparticles ranging in size from 28.18 to 135.26 nm. In contrast, DLS showed a larger hydrodynamic diameter. Encapsulation also improved the thermal stability of PL and produced favorable degradation behavior. Short-term storage and photostability assessment showed no detectable changes in weight, color, clarity, or odor for up to 105 h under light or dark ambient conditions. Biological evaluation of PL-CD showed enhanced antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity. PL-CD exhibited MIC values of 2.5–5 mg/mL, representing up to an eight-fold improvement compared with free PL. It also inhibited biofilm formation by more than 92% across the tested bacterial strains. Biocompatibility studies using HSF cells showed that PL-CD showed a safe profile under the tested conditions. Anticancer evaluation using MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells showed concentration- and time-dependent reductions in MTT-derived metabolic activity after PL-CD treatment. Annexin V/PI flow cytometry further showed increased apoptotic cell populations following PL-CD exposure. These findings indicate that the observed cytotoxic response was associated with apoptosis. The developed PL-CD nanostructures represent a promising platform for further investigation in antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anticancer applications.

Article.Title: Parametric overturning-stability assessment of a compact construction transport vehicle equipped with a crane boom
Article.Authors: Dai Y.; Zhao F.; Cui H.; Wang Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Compact transport vehicles fitted with crane booms require stability assessment beyond nominal payload ratings. This study implements a fully specified rigid-body screening model for 200 kg at 3.60 m, 310 kg at 2.70 m, 450 kg at 1.95 m and 800 kg at 1.13 m horizontal payload reach. A node-consistent piecewise-linear boom-CoG model replaces an inconsistent single-line approximation, and all scenario figures are recomputed using declared support-centred coordinates, force heights and gravity projections. For 1000 kg deck mass, 3° outward slope and 15.5 m s⁻¹ wind, the minimum stability indices are − 0.110, -0.143, -0.079, 0.090 for Cases I–IV. At 1500 kg deck mass and the same environment, the longitudinal stability-only payload bounds for SI ≥ 0.10 are 191.4, 276.2 and 437.1 kg at the first three rated reaches; the fourth reaches the 1000 kg numerical search ceiling. A specified PCG64 Monte Carlo implementation uses 100,000 samples per case with seed 20,260,809 and wind draws clipped to 0–20 m s⁻¹. The resulting conditional probabilities of SI < 0 are 17.79%, 22.30%, 15.90%, 2.70%. A 1,000,000-sample check changes those estimates by at most 0.0761% points. Source code, configuration and sampled inputs are provided for reproduction. The completed model is a computational screen based partly on declared assumptions; it is not hardware validation or a certified capacity chart.

Article.Title: PreVAP: an explainable machine learning model for early prediction of ventilator-associated pneumonia using electronic health records and near-real-time clinical dashboards
Article.Authors: Berrueta J.; Rodríguez A.; Gómez J.; García-Martínez A.; Orts P.; Manrique S.; Claverias L.; Guardiola J.; Ausso-Trias S.; Bodí M.
Article.Abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) affects up to 20% of critically ill patients, prolonging hospital stay, increasing costs and contributing to mortality, yet its diagnosis remains challenging. Most machine-learning models for VAP rely on administrative codes or microbiological surrogates and provide a single static prediction. We conducted a retrospective single-centre study of 2,817 adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation for at least 48 h (2014–2025), 334 of whom developed VAP, using physician-documented diagnoses with exact onset dates and hourly electronic health record data. Twelve algorithms, multiple feature-selection strategies and three prediction horizons (1, 24 and 48 h before onset) were compared. The final CatBoost model, based on 18 routinely collected variables, predicted VAP 24 h before clinical diagnosis with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.86 and a sensitivity of 0.76 in the held-out test set. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified antibiotic administration, maximum positive end-expiratory pressure, maximum temperature, maximum fraction of inspired oxygen and purulent secretions as the main predictors. The model has been deployed in silent mode, generating hourly, explainable risk estimates with full traceability. External and prospective validation are needed before its clinical impact can be established.

Article.Title: Deep learning assisted blunt liver injury diagnosis with ultrasound: an animal study
Article.Authors: Zhong Z.; Liu T.; Zhang T.; Zhang X.; Hua S.; Zhu Y.; Zhou G.; Lv F.
Article.Abstract: Blunt liver injury usually needs fast and accurate diagnosis for timely rescue, which can be achieved through ultrasound scanning. However, the recognition of liver injury from ultrasound images is highly dependent on subjective judgment, especially when there is no bleeding in the viscera. In this study, we explore animal models for validated standards of blunt liver injury, thereby evaluating the feasibility of the deep learning network in assessing indirect (hemoperitoneum) and direct (trauma focus) ultrasonographic traumatic signs for objective and reliable diagnosis. 54 healthy New Zealand rabbits were used to establish animal models with different levels of blunt liver injury. We collected ultrasound images before and after their modeling, then calculated the hemoperitoneum index, i.e., the sum of the maximum depth, to establish the corresponding anatomical standard. A deep-learning-based model, ResNet50, was then utilized to automatically detect the presence of hemoperitoneum or trauma focus and further grade the injury based on ultrasound images. There is a significant positive correlation between a hemoperitoneum index and the weight of the hemoperitoneum after animal modeling ( r = 0.788, p < 0.001). In addition, the difference in the hemoperitoneum index is positively correlated with the grade of blunt liver injury ( r = 0.413, p = 0.007). The accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of the ResNet50 model were 0.842, 0.901, and 0.712 for determining the presence or absence of hemoperitoneum and 0.864, 0.852, and 0.881 for trauma focus. Furthermore, the model could discriminate the degree of liver injury with an accuracy of 0.732. This study demonstrates the feasibility of developing a validated standard for liver injury using animal models. The results also suggest the potential and feasibility of using a deep learning-based model to identify liver injury beyond the detection of hemoperitoneum from ultrasound images.

Article.Title: A hybrid graph-convolutional moving average framework for spatio-temporal voltage prediction in smart microgrids
Article.Authors: Anas M.; Adnan M.; Alghamdi S.; Tariq M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate voltage forecasting is critical for maintaining the operational stability and reliability of smart microgrids under dynamic load and generation conditions. This paper proposes a novel Hybrid Graph Convolution Moving Average (Hyb-GCMA) spatio-temporal deep learning framework that synergistically integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Seasonal AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average with eXogenous variables (SARIMAX) for dynamic voltage prediction in an IEEE 14-bus truncated microgrid. The proposed framework very well encompasses spatial correlations between interconnected buses by graph-based learning while sequential learning of temporal dependencies due to time-varying load patterns. To increase the robustness and generality of the model, historical load-flow data under various operating scenarios are preprocessed by normalizing and generating sliding-window sequences. To prevent overfitting, adaptive learning rate strategies and early stopping mechanisms are used to further optimize the model training. The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) per-bus accuracy metrics, along with \(R^2\) , show that the proposed Hyb-GCMA framework makes a significant improvement over conventional standalone deep learning baselines. The RMSE and MAE obtained are 0.0049 p.u and 0.0047 p.u, in squared and absolute error respectively. \(R^2\) value calculated is 0.999993, which suggests the model explains the proportion of variance best fit. The results show that spatio-temporal deep learning methods are providing great potential for real-time voltage stability assessment, anomaly detection and predictive control of next generation smart microgrid systems.

Article.Title: Native biocontrol agents for the suppression of clubroot disease in rapeseed (Brassica napus) and mustard (Brassica juncea) in Nepal
Article.Authors: Devkota S.; Ghimire A.; Timila R.; Adhikary D.; Manandhar H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clubroot disease caused by Plasmodiophora brassicae is a major constraint to the production of cruciferous crops worldwide, including Nepal. This study evaluated the efficacy of native biocontrol agents ( Trichoderma and Bacillus ) against clubroot in rapeseed and mustard under screenhouse conditions for two consecutive years (2024/25 and 2025/26). Initial screening of 22 native Trichoderma isolates in a pot culture experiment identified seven which showed promise for suppressing P. brassicae in rapeseed. Those isolates were subsequently evaluated individually and as a consortium, along with two Bacillus isolates and Nebijin (flusulfamide) as a chemical check. Across both growing seasons, application of the Trichoderma consortium resulted in lower disease severity (29% and 33%, respectively) than bacterial and chemical treatments. Most of the Trichoderma treatments positively increased plant growth traits, including plant height, leaf number, and plant rigidity, and the plants treated with Bacillus isolates had more fibrous and robust stems. Enzyme assays revealed significant variation among the 22 Trichoderma isolates in cellulase and amylase production. The superior performance of the consortium compared to individual isolates may therefore be attributed to the combined enzymatic activities of multiple isolates, as each isolate possesses different levels of enzyme production capacity, resulting in a complementary and enhanced effect in managing clubroot disease in crucifer crops.

Article.Title: Integrating explicit loading/unloading times and horizontal–vertical movements into multi-level puzzle-based storage optimization
Article.Authors: Al Jneid R.; Yiğit V.; Keskin M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growth of e-commerce has increased demand for compact, responsive automated storage systems. Multi-level puzzle-based storage systems with autonomous shuttles offer high storage density, yet models that treat loading and unloading as instantaneous may underestimate retrieval times and misrepresent movement-handling interactions. This study develops a time-indexed optimization framework representing horizontal and vertical movement, explicit handling, collision avoidance, and completion at final unloading. A Time-Indexed Integrated Movement-Manipulation (TIMM) heuristic combines priority-based construction, local search, and independent schedule-replay validation. TIMM reproduced all seven proven optima and generated replay-valid schedules in 489 of 522 runs. All 60 runs for the tested low-density M200R20 configuration on the 10 × 10 × 10 grid were replay-valid. Across nine paired cases, one-period loading and unloading increased mean makespan from 5.56 to 7.67 (38.0%) relative to instantaneous handling. In five matched mobility cases, unrestricted vertical movement reduced mean makespan from 8.2 to 6.6 (19.5%). Shuttle scarcity increased makespan and reduced throughput. Closest-First outperformed Furthest-First under full shuttle availability, whereas neither rule dominated under scarcity. TIMM also matched the adapted ALNS-IP method in makespan on ten jointly solved instances while reducing median runtime from 13.836 to 0.415 s.

Article.Title: Chronic HIV infection modulates the cargo of plasma exosomal ncRNAs associated with non-AIDS-defining cancers
Article.Authors: Ureta A.; Restrepo C.; Pedregal M.; Callata H.; Nistal S.; Peinado H.; Gómez M.; Sánchez-Cabo F.; García-Gil M.; Cabello A.; Estrada V.; Górgolas M.; García-Foncillas J.; Benito J.; Rallón N.
Article.Abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are key regulators of gene expression, and their dysregulation has been described in the context of both HIV-1 pathogenesis and tumor development. This signature was not observed in cancer-free PLWH and HIV-negative individuals with cancer, suggesting that the coexistence of persistent HIV infection and cancer may be associated with specific features of the plasma exosomal ncRNA profile. Our findings provide evidence of distinct exosomal ncRNA profiles associated with NADCs in PLWH, laying the basis for further investigation of ncRNAs as candidate circulating biomarkers and as potential indicators of cancer-associated biological processes in PLWH, supporting future efforts toward improving the understanding and clinical management of HIV-associated malignancies.

Article.Title: Deep learning classifies calcium imaging dynamics using time-series representations
Article.Authors: Alves C.; Hufgard S.; Campanharo A.; Sallum L.; Kalbasi A.; Mayer M.; Däsch H.; Rodrigues F.; Thielemann C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Calcium imaging data are challenging to analyze reliably because signal extraction and segmentation can vary across recordings and acquisition settings. This study aims to develop a segmentation-agnostic deep learning framework for classifying neuronal dynamics across different spatial resolutions and acquisition frequencies. Fluorescence time series were transformed into compact, fixed-size matrices based on quantile transition patterns. These standardized representations were classified using convolutional neural networks. Performance was evaluated using stratified hold-out testing and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Multiple quantile-based representations were evaluated under whole-image and grid-based preprocessing strategies, and robustness was assessed under reduced temporal resolution and controlled noise perturbations. Across all preprocessing strategies and representation variants, the framework achieved strong and consistent classification performance, achieving precision = 0.99, sensitivity = 0.99, and specificity = 0.99 in independent validation. Classification performance remained high under moderate noise perturbations but declined progressively as perturbation magnitude increased. The proposed segmentation-agnostic framework provides a robust, scalable, and generalizable strategy for analyzing calcium imaging dynamics, enabling efficient characterization of neuronal activity in pharmacological and systems neuroscience applications.

Article.Title: In vitro antioxidant activity, quantitative phytochemistry, metabolite profile of endemic Indian Pogostemon speciosus Benth. and Pogostemon gardneri Hook.f
Article.Authors: Momin S.; Gurav R.; Jadhav M.
Article.Abstract: Endemic plant species represent an important yet underexplored source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites with potential therapeutic significance. Although members of the genus Pogostemon (Lamiaceae) are widely recognized for their ethnomedicinal and pharmacological properties, phytochemical and bioactivity data on endemic taxa remain limited. In the present study, the phytochemical composition and antioxidant potential of two unexplored endemic species, Pogostemon speciosus Benth. and Pogostemon gardneri Hook.f., were comparatively investigated. Fresh and dried plant parts were extracted using methanol, acetone, and distilled water through ultrasonication. Antioxidant activity was evaluated using multiple in vitro assays, including DPPH, ABTS, FRAP, superoxide anion scavenging, ferrous ion chelation, phosphomolybdenum, and hydroxyl radical scavenging assays. Among the tested extracts, acetonic leaf extracts exhibited the highest antioxidant activity in both species. Quantitative analyses revealed higher accumulation of phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, tannins, and saponins in acetone- and methanol-based extracts. Furthermore, comprehensive metabolite profiling using UHPLC–QTOF-MS/MS enabled the tentative identification of 66 metabolites in P. speciosus and 42 metabolites in P. gardneri , representing the first detailed metabolomic characterization of these endemic taxa. Significant correlations between phytochemical contents and antioxidant activities highlight the role of secondary metabolites in the observed bioactivity. These findings provide valuable insights into the chemical diversity and pharmacological potential of endemic Pogostemon species.

Article.Title: An auditable framework for ranking movement tasks in skeleton-derived autism intervention data
Article.Authors: Cai R.
Article.Abstract: We conducted a secondary computational analysis of the public MMASD autism intervention dataset to examine how movement tasks are ranked using skeleton-derived evidence. The analysis comprised 1,693 traceable derived logical segments from 32 autistic children across 11 activities; paired native-24/native-71 representations were collapsed. The 1,315 clips reported in the source study were retained as a historical reference, not equated with the derived segments. A seven-dimension Deployment Suitability Score (DSS) was examined using single-criterion rankings, TOPSIS, weight and proxy-score perturbations, participant-balanced aggregation, and approximate degradation tests. Under the primary configuration, Arm Swing, Chest Expansion and Body Swing ranked first to third (DSS 0.892, 0.839 and 0.829); Squat ranked fourth (0.759). Participant balancing moved Squat to second and Chest Expansion to fourth, changing top-three membership. Severe derived-table degradation preserved the top-three set but not exact full ranking. These findings demonstrate that apparent ranking stability depends on which uncertainty and representation choices are tested. The study evaluates task-level measurement and ranking behaviour, not clinical relevance, smartphone recording feasibility or a service workflow. No diagnosis, screening, child-level prediction or clinical benefit was assessed.

Article.Title: Comparison of pharmacokinetic properties of mitomycin C-based regimens for hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy in a rat model
Article.Authors: Joo S.; Moon K.; Baek S.; Ahn S.; Park E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mitomycin-C (MMC) is the most widely used agent for hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) in colorectal peritoneal metastases, though dosing and intervals vary across institutions. This study aimed to compare the pharmacokinetic profiles of three MMC-based HIPEC regimens. Eighteen male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomized into three groups for 90 min of HIPEC at 41–42℃. Group 1 received 35 mg/m² in three divided doses at 0, 30, and 60 min; Group 2 received 40 mg/m² in two divided doses at 0 and 60 min; Group 3 received a single bolus dose of 35 mg/m² at HIPEC initiation. Peritoneal fluid and plasma concentrations were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. MMC concentrations differed significantly across groups over the 90-minute perfusion period ( p < 0.001). Peritoneal concentrations at 90 min were comparable among groups (73.63 vs. 75.92 and 79.58 ng/mL), whereas the plasma concentration was lower in Group 1 (1.59 vs. 2.45 and 2.02 ng/mL; p = 0.043). The peritoneal-to-plasma AUC ratios were comparable among groups (52.1 vs. 47.7 vs. 47.1, respectively; p = 0.849). In conclusion, the three MMC-based HIPEC protocols showed no significant differences in the peritoneal-to-plasma AUC ratio, although Group 1 demonstrated lower plasma MMC concentrations.

Article.Title: Microstructure and texture evolution in functionally graded AA6014 aluminium tubes processed by tube roller compression
Article.Authors: Zayed E.; Alateyah A.; El-Garaihy W.; Mohamed A.; Zein H.; El-Mahallawy N.; Zedan Y.
Article.Abstract: Tube Roller Compression (TRC) was used to study the relationship between the through-thickness deformation gradient, the microstructural evolution, crystallographic texture and hardness of AA6014 aluminium alloy tubes. In the most highly strained areas, the average grain size was refined from about 19.5 μm in the annealed condition to 3–4 μm by the application of non-uniform strain due to TRC, highest at the outer surface and decreasing towards the inner wall. The higher the severity of processing, the more elongated the grains became and the more heterogeneous the microstructural organization. Analysis of {111} pole figures and orientation distribution functions at φ₂ = 45° indicated an initially weak texture, with Goss as the dominant pole figure with a minor Cube component, that evolved as a result of condition-dependent redistribution of the Copper, Brass, and Goss components. As a result of this evolution, local orientations with higher texture intensities or relatively diffuse orientation distributions were obtained depending on the processing parameters. Consistent with the microstructural gradient, the hardness increased from approximately 48–52 HV near the inner region to 58–70 HV at the outer surface, depending on the processing condition. Using an objective hardened threshold defined from the annealed condition (mean + 2SD, ~ 53 HV), the effective hardened-layer depth ranged from approximately 0.2 to 1.6 mm, while Sample 5 remained above the threshold throughout the measured depth (> 1.8 mm). Based on these results, a quantitative correlation between TRC-induced strain gradient, grain refinement, texture evolution and strengthening of the local material is established. TRC therefore offers a potential pathway to achieve functionally graded aluminium tube that is hard on the outside while retaining a comparatively less-deformed core.

Article.Title: DSC-Mamba: a lightweight dual-attention network for real-time driver behavior detection
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Xu C.; He S.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents DSC-Mamba, a lightweight model for abnormal driving behavior detection from in-vehicle camera images. The model reduces computational load through depthwise separable convolution and designs two key interaction mechanisms: in the DAEDC module, channel attention generates weights to modulate multi-scale spatial attention; in the HEMamba module, the global modeling output of Mamba is normalized and re-injected into local tokens, allowing global context to calibrate local representations. On the SFD3 dataset, using driver-level five-fold cross-validation as the primary protocol, DSC-Mamba achieved an average accuracy of 93.12% ± 0.19% with only 0.421 M parameters and 0.1053 G FLOPs. This is 0.08 percentage points higher than the competitive MVim baseline under the same partition. Under random image-level partitioning, the accuracy reached 99.89%, though this is noted as overly optimistic and for reference only. On the AUCv2 dataset, the model achieved 92.75% accuracy. Furthermore, PyTorchSim-based NPU simulation estimates an INT8 single-frame latency of 12–18 ms and power consumption of 0.9–1.4 W. These results indicate that DSC-Mamba achieves a favorable balance among parameter count, FLOPs, and accuracy, though real-vehicle hardware verification remains future work.

Article.Title: Physiological responses of potato leaves to nitrogen stress at the early stage of tuber formation
Article.Authors: Ding K.; Shan Y.; Wang L.; Zhang Y.; Wang L.; Sun X.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Nitrogen is a key macroelement that regulates potato growth, stress resistance and yield, but the physiological mechanism of potato response to different nitrogen levels is still unclear. This study investigated the effects of three nitrogen treatments (N0: nitrogen deficiency, N1: normal nitrogen, N2: excessive nitrogen) on potato growth, photosynthesis, reactive oxygen species (ROS) metabolism, antioxidant defense system, osmotic adjustment and their internal correlation. Nitrogen deficiency reduced plant height, net photosynthetic rate, chlorophyll content, nitrogen accumulation and tuber yield, whereas excessive nitrogen enhanced vegetative growth and leaf photosynthesis but markedly reduced tuber weight per plant and the commercial rate. Compared with excessive nitrogen, nitrogen deficiency induced more severe oxidative stress, manifested as the accumulation of superoxide anion (O 2 − ), hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) and malondialdehyde (MDA). Nitrogen deficiency severely inhibited the activity of antioxidant enzymes, while excessive nitrogen caused a moderate decrease in enzyme activity and AsA-GSH cycle imbalance. In addition, nitrogen deficiency and excess reduced the accumulation of osmotic adjustment related substances. Correlation analysis showed that there was a synergistic relationship between antioxidant system and osmotic regulation system, both of which were positively correlated with growth and photosynthesis, and negatively correlated with oxidative damage. This study characterized the physiological responses of potato leaves to nitrogen stress under pot conditions with a single cultivar, and provided a reference for scientific nitrogen management in potato production under similar conditions.

Article.Title: Seismic fragility of geopolymer concrete pile supported wharves under exposure zone dependent chloride deterioration and nonlinear soil pile interaction
Article.Authors: Hu B.; Zhou L.; Fazli A.; Khairy Y.; Ghoniem R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pile supported wharves in seismic coastal regions experience earthquake loading while undergoing progressive chloride deterioration, yet the influence of spatially varying marine exposure on the seismic fragility of geopolymer concrete wharves remains insufficiently quantified. This study develops an exposure zone resolved framework linking chloride ingress, reinforcement corrosion, bond degradation, cyclic pile response, nonlinear soil pile interaction, and seismic fragility for geopolymer concrete and ordinary Portland cement concrete wharves. Marine exposure produced substantially lower deterioration in the investigated geopolymer concrete system. At 365 days, chloride penetration and reinforcement mass loss were 22.8% and 40.9% lower than the corresponding Portland cement concrete values, while displacement ductility was 24.6% greater. Service life analysis showed that the median DS3 seismic capacity at 60 years retained 81.2% of its initial value for geopolymer concrete compared with 71.2% for Portland cement concrete. Uniform deterioration assumptions overestimated the 60 year DS3 median capacity by 20.5% and 23.0%, respectively, and failed to identify the tidal zone as the governing response location. The results demonstrate that spatial marine deterioration can materially alter both seismic fragility and critical damage location, supporting exposure zone resolved assessment of aging pile supported wharves.

Article.Title: Deep learning for multiuser detection in UAV communications using RIS and orthogonal time sequency multiplexing with circular pulse shaping
Article.Authors: Hossain M.; Shimamura T.; Kaniz A.; Ullah S.
Article.Abstract: This paper addresses reliable multiuser signal detection and perceptual-level physical-layer confidentiality for circular pulse-shaped orthogonal time-sequency multiplexing (OTSM) transmission over reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) delay–Doppler channels. To improve multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detection under doubly dispersive propagation, a feedforward deep neural network (DNN) trained using 12-fold cross-validation is employed. The proposed learning-based detector achieves lower mean square error (MSE) than the considered minimum mean square error (MMSE), zero-forcing (ZF), orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP), and OAMP-Net baselines, and provides improved bit error rate (BER) performance particularly at moderate and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels, while maintaining stable convergence and validation behavior across users. To provide lightweight physical-layer confidentiality, a nine-dimensional (9D) eighth-order chaotic encryption mechanism with random signal insertion is incorporated into the transmission chain, and perceptual confidentiality is evaluated using the Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) metric. Block diagonalization (BD) precoding is used to mitigate multiuser interference, while repeat–accumulate (RA) coding improves detection reliability. Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves 30–40 dB out-of-band (OOB) power reduction and a peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of approximately 11 dB at a complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) of \(10^{-3}\) . Under the idealized simulation setting with perfect channel state information (CSI), BD-based interference suppression, and no pilot or RIS-control overhead, the system attains an upper-bound aggregate block-normalized spectral efficiency of approximately 227 bps/Hz. This value is reported as a system-level benchmark for the considered model and should not be interpreted as a practical per-subcarrier or per-antenna spectral efficiency. Encrypted image transmission yields LPIPS values above 1.19 for all users, indicating strong perceptual dissimilarity prior to reception. Overall, the results indicate that the proposed RIS–UAV-assisted circular pulse-shaped OTSM framework can improve spectral containment, signal detection reliability, and perceptual-level physical-layer confidentiality in highly dynamic wireless environments.

Article.Title: Arctic Puffin Algorithm with local escaping operator for feature selection in high-dimensional datasets
Article.Authors: Selim M.; Fahim A.; Elmanakhly D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large datasets might make data mining more difficult due to their high dimensionality. To minimize the dimensionality of large datasets, feature selection is an essential step that maximizes classification accuracy by choosing the most informative features. In this study, a binary adaptation of the enhanced Arctic Puffin Optimization (EAPO) algorithm, which builds on the Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO) algorithm, is introduced within a wrapper-based framework to identify the optimal subset of features for classification tasks. To improve the search performance of APO, a local escaping operator is incorporated to effectively balance exploration and exploitation and enhance its ability to escape local optima. Furthermore, a key aspect of EAPO is the design of the transfer function, which facilitates the transformation of the continuous search space into a binary domain. To evaluate its effectiveness, three transfer functions, S-shaped, V-shaped, and U-shaped, are investigated. The proposed EAPO method is assessed on 14 benchmark datasets using the k-Nearest Neighbor classifier as the evaluation metric. To control overfitting, k-fold cross-validation employs a partitioning strategy in which the dataset is divided into k folds, and each fold is used as the test set once while the remaining folds form the training set. Comparisons are made with state-of-the-art methods, including the beluga whale optimization, sine cosine algorithm, kepler optimization algorithm, grey wolf optimizer, coati optimization algorithm, salp swarm algorithm, arithmetic optimization algorithm, and bat optimization algorithm. The results obtained from the experiments show that the EAPO technique is better in terms of consistency, feature reduction, and classification accuracy. Statistical analysis further confirms the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

Article.Title: Research on Bayesian network probabilistic assessment model for soil seismic liquefaction considering small-sample and incomplete SPT data
Article.Authors: Fan M.; Yang Z.; Li J.; Liu X.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: Liquefaction assessment is a critical task in seismic geotechnical engineering; however, existing methods are often limited by their reliance on complete datasets and inability to effectively handle missing information. This study proposes a Bayesian network-based framework for probabilistic liquefaction assessment under conditions of small sample size and incomplete Standard Penetration Test ( SPT ) data. Causal logical relationships derived from liquefaction mechanisms are incorporated to construct interpretable network structures. A systematic experimental framework integrating different parameter learning algorithms, training strategies, and missing-data handling schemes is developed to evaluate model performance under varying conditions. The results illustrate that small-sample models show limited performance, whereas incorporating incomplete information significantly improves prediction accuracy. Under the optimal combination of the real-sample-based training strategy (Method-1) and the maximum a posteriori probability (MAP)-based missing-data handling scheme (Scheme II), the five-factor Bayesian network model achieved an Overall Accuracy ( OA ), Precision ( Pre ), Recall ( Rec ), and F 1 -score ( F 1 ) of 80.56%, 74.00%, 97.37%, and 84.09%, respectively, on the independent validation dataset. It demonstrates the reliable predictive capability of the proposed model for unseen liquefaction cases. The proposed framework expands the applicability of probabilistic liquefaction assessment across different depth ranges, seismic loading conditions, and soil properties. Moreover, it provides an interpretable and robust solution for engineering scenarios where data incompleteness is unavoidable, offering practical value for seismic hazard assessment.

Article.Title: Integrated hydrogeological characterization and flow modelling for sustainable management of a regional multilayer aquifer system
Article.Authors: Pinardi R.; Artoni A.; Avanzi R.; Celico F.; Chelli A.; Ducci L.; Fagandini C.; Luceri M.; Molino L.; Pesente G.; Rizzo P.; Zaghini M.; Zanini A.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a multidisciplinary and integrated approach for the characterization and modelling of a multilayered confined aquifer system in the Mantova sector of the Po Plain (northern Italy), combining three-dimensional geological reconstruction, hydrogeological analysis, hydrochemical, isotopic and biomolecular data and numerical groundwater flow modelling. The proposed framework aims to overcome the limitations of single-discipline approaches when dealing with complex fluvio-glacial and alluvial aquifer systems intensively exploited for water supply at the regional scale. A three-dimensional geological model was developed using subsurface data and field surveys to reconstruct the spatial architecture of aquifers and aquitards. Hydrogeological observations, natural tracers and pumping-test data were jointly used to constrain hydraulic properties and define a robust conceptual model. On this basis, a regional three-dimensional groundwater flow model was implemented using MODFLOW-USG and calibrated against regional piezometric maps. The model successfully reproduces regional hydraulic gradients, groundwater levels and the response of confined aquifers to pumping stresses, with normalized root mean square errors below 2% for deep aquifers. Estimated hydraulic parameters are consistent with independent field measurements. Application examples, including capture zone delineation and drawdown assessment, demonstrate how the integrated modelling framework can support groundwater management and protection strategies. The proposed approach provides a transferable methodology for the sustainable management of complex aquifer systems under increasing water demand and climatic variability.

Article.Title: CARMA: contention-aware retransmission management for energy-efficient medium access over lossy wireless sensor links
Article.Authors: Dhaka R.; Singar S.; Sharma M.
Article.Abstract: The medium-access-control (MAC) layer decides how a battery-powered sensor node spends its scarcest resource, energy, yet the IEEE 802.15.4 carrier-sense access in most deployments retransmits with a fixed retry limit that treats every acknowledgment failure alike. Failures have two distinct causes: a collision, cured by backing off, and a channel fade on a lossy link, which backing off does not cure, so that on a dead link repeated attempts merely burn energy the first-order radio model never counts. The obstacle is that plain 802.15.4 has no collision detection. CARMA, the contention-aware retransmission manager introduced here, sidesteps this: from only the fraction of its clear-channel assessments that find the medium busy and the fraction of its transmissions left unacknowledged, each node splits its failure rate into collision and channel components. CARMA prices its retry budget by the channel component, abandoning dead links after a single probe, and scales the contention window with the collision component. On a model that follows the 2450 MHz physical layer, frame format and timing of the standard and counts the energy of every radio state, reproduced by a second, separately written simulator, it delivers 17 to 42% more frames per joule than standard 802.15.4 across the load range at equal or higher delivery, and 14% more than a grid-tuned 802.15.4 at the nominal load. A paired ablation attributes the gain to the abandon rule. The decomposition, the contention scaling of the budget and a per-failure refinement have no measurable effect, and the contention-scaled window helps slightly at saturation only if backoff is cheap. CARMA falls behind the tuned baseline under strong hidden terminals and behind Idle Sense on a saturated channel when waiting is cheap, and it stays 19% below a perfect-information threshold rule. On measured Intel-Lab link qualities its 16% gain over the standard comes with a delivery ratio 5.5 percentage points lower.

Article.Title: Timing of de novo vaccination during pregnancy impacts maternal and newborn immunity
Article.Authors: Nziza N.; Lopez P.; Kellman B.; Roy V.; Chen T.; Lawler S.; Lakudzala A.; Ilan S.; Jasset O.; Yinger R.; Ibanez-Pintor L.; Cao Y.; Balazs A.; Alter G.; Elovitz M.; Lauffenburger D.; Edlow A.; Julg B.
Article.Abstract: Maternal immunity is essential for protecting both the pregnant individual and fetus, balancing immune tolerance with defense against infection. While maternal vaccination enhances protection, the impact of gestational timing on antibody responses and transplacental antibody transfer remains unclear. The COVID-19 pandemic provided a unique opportunity to study primary SARS-CoV-2 vaccine-induced humoral responses in individuals without documented prior SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination. To investigate how vaccination timing shapes maternal and fetal immunity, we performed comprehensive serological profiling in 263 individuals, including 96 maternal–neonatal dyads, sampled across pregnancy and at delivery. Leveraging natural variation in SARS-CoV-2 vaccine timing, we assessed antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and 13 additional pathogens using Systems Serology, analyzing isotypes, subclasses, FcγR binding, glycosylation, neutralization, and Fc-mediated functions. Pregnant individuals maintained stable immunity to previously encountered antigens (from past infections or vaccinations) and mounted expected responses to pertussis and tetanus boosters. Initial responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccination were attenuated in third-trimester vaccinees but reached comparable levels after the second dose. Enhanced responses to unrelated antigens, such as poliovirus and measles, were observed, particularly in later gestation, potentially due to cross-reactivity. Antibody transfer was most efficient following late second to early third trimester vaccination, with decreased transfer in the late third trimester. Fetal sex also influenced antibody transfer efficiency, favoring male fetuses in the third trimester. These findings underscore the importance of vaccine timing to optimize maternal and neonatal immunity.

Article.Title: Resilience and secondary traumatic stress in relation to work engagement and job satisfaction among polish police officers exposed to indirect trauma
Article.Authors: Bąk G.; Ogińska-Bulik N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to examine the significance of psychological resilience and secondary traumatic stress (STS) for work engagement and job satisfaction, including the mediating role of STS. The study involved 220 Polish police officers. The majority of participants were male (n = 183, 83.18%). The sample also included 35 females (15.91%), and two participants (0.91%) did not disclose their gender. Regarding professional assignment, 120 officers (54.5%) were employed in the preventive division, while 100 officers (45.5%) represented the criminal division. Length of service in the police ranged from 2 to 32 years (M = 14.55; SD = 6.27). For the purposes of this study and the psychological instruments employed, special approval was obtained from the General Police Headquarters of Poland (Approval No. GAK-1591/1561/24/AK). All experimental protocols were approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the University of Lodz (Resolution No. 95 KEBN-UŁ 2025–26). Participation was voluntary and anonymous, and the study was conducted in accordance with applicable regulations and guidelines. Informed consent was obtained from all participants involved in the study. For the purposes of this study, a dedicated questionnaire was developed. In addition, the following standardized research instruments were administered: the UWES-9, the Job Satisfaction Scale, the Resilience Measurement Scale, and the Secondary Traumatic Stress Inventory. The participating police officers demonstrated moderate levels of work engagement and average job satisfaction. They were also characterized by high psychological resilience and low levels of STS. Resilience was positively correlated with both work engagement and job satisfaction, and negatively associated with STS. STS was also negatively related to job satisfaction. STS (including its two symptoms) demonstrated a modest indirect effect in the relationship between resilience and job satisfaction. The findings suggest that psychological resilience may play an important role in the occupational functioning of police officers, being associated with higher levels of work engagement and job satisfaction, as well as lower levels of secondary traumatic stress (STS) symptoms.

Article.Title: Physics-guided deep learning for high resolution X-ray free-electron laser imaging
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Mishra A.; Arnott A.; Berboucha M.; Boiadjieva N.; Chatterjee G.; Cunningham E.; Czapla N.; Dyer G.; Ehni J.; Ettelbrick R.; Grassi A.; Grech M.; Hart P.; Khaghani D.; Lee H.; McGehee P.; Nagler B.; Neumayer P.; Riconda C.; Welch M.; Zabala A.; Galtier E.; Nguyen Q.
Article.Abstract: Imperfections in X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) imaging systems can limit their performance, especially in High Energy Density (HED) or Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE)-relevant experiments that are typically single shot, by introducing structured, non-stationary features that overlap with the signal of interest. When the X-ray transmission is reconstructed by typical flat-field normalization, even small shot-to-shot drift of structured features imprints residual patterns onto transmission maps, degrading signal visibility and biasing measurements such as electron density, velocity and feature sizes. We investigate this limitation by modeling the artifacts as a separable feature layer and training a U-Net architecture to estimate and infer them directly from the experimental data. We compare our method against Fourier filtering, phase cross-correlation (PCC), and more advanced procedures like Dynamic Flat-Field Normalization (DFFN) to evaluate artifact suppression capability and signal preservation in the reconstructed transmission maps. In multiple synthetic injection tests, our Physics-Guided Deep Learning approach is able to obtain an improvement in mean Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) from 0.345 to 0.906 and from 0.0679 to 0.945, while better preserving filament profiles and reducing degradation of the filament signal during artifact suppression. Additionally, we utilize deep ensembles to obtain predictive epistemic uncertainty estimates for the U-Net based reconstruction, to ensure Out Of Distribution (OOD) robustness for this procedure.

Article.Title: Triglyceride glucose body mass index and incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity among middle and older adults in China and England
Article.Authors: Zheng J.; Wang X.; Lv Z.; He W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) substantially reduces life expectancy, and the triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI) is a simple marker of insulin resistance. We examined the prospective association between TyG-BMI and incident CMM in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; primary cohort, n = 6,426) and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; replication cohort, n = 2,221). CMM was defined as at least two of diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and stroke in CHARLS, and of diabetes, heart disease, and stroke in ELSA, where harmonized hypertension data were unavailable. Incident CMM occurred in 17.8% of CHARLS and 2.9% of ELSA participants. In fully adjusted logistic models, the highest versus lowest TyG-BMI quartile was associated with higher odds of CMM in CHARLS (OR = 5.72, 95% CI 4.52–7.22) and ELSA (OR = 4.03, 95% CI 1.70–11.16). In CHARLS, the association persisted after adjustment for the number of baseline CMM components (OR = 4.02, 95% CI 3.15–5.14), among participants with zero or one baseline component, and after restriction to complete baseline ascertainment; the corresponding risk ratio was 3.91 (95% CI 3.23–4.73). Discrimination was modest (AUC 0.655). The direction of association was replicated across cohorts, but effect magnitudes are not directly comparable, and clinical predictive utility requires dedicated evaluation.

Article.Title: RAFT-MAC reverse asymmetry aware failure tolerant MAC for heterogeneous wireless mesh access networks
Article.Authors: Mathiyalagan P.; Mahalakshmi A.
Article.Abstract: Heterogeneous Wireless Mesh Access Networks built on MANET infrastructure often include nodes with unequal transmission ranges. When this happens, a node may reach its neighbour in one direction but the neighbour cannot reach back, so acknowledgements never return. MAC and routing protocols in common use treat every link failure the same way, with no distinction between a broken forward path and a broken reverse path. They are particularly ill-suited to the case where the reverse link collapses during an ongoing data session. This paper describes RAFT-MAC, a two-state cross-layer MAC protocol that handles these two scenarios separately. When no session is active, the Proactive Idle-State Handler (PIH) watches reverse-link health through a per-node Reverse Link State Table and pre-selects an alternate next-hop, so recovery needs no search time when a session later starts. When a session is running, the Reactive Active-Transmission Handler (RATH) catches a mid-session reverse-link failure, holds in-flight packets in a buffer, and re-routes traffic with one MAC-layer PATH_UPDATE without the source application noticing under CBR/UDP traffic. Both handlers fit inside an 8 to 10-byte extension of the standard Hello message. NS3 experiments across 50 to 150 heterogeneous nodes, run against six baselines under varied mobility, density, and asymmetry, show a 12.4 percentage-point PDR improvement and 39.3% lower delay relative to LDTR 33 , together with 25.5% lower control overhead relative to AI-QoS 38 . Wilcoxon signed-rank tests showed p = 0.0625 for all RAFT-MAC versus AOMDV 37 comparisons. Against LDTR 33 , only recovery time reached the 10% significance threshold; the remaining metrics did not.

Article.Title: Climate change threatens projected habitat suitability and phytochemical quality of Stachys pilifera Benth: a dual-projection modeling approach
Article.Authors: Tavan M.; Piri Sahragard H.; Jahantab E.
Article.Abstract: Climate change poses substantial risks to biodiversity, species distributions, and both the compositional consistency and the concentration of bioactive constituents in medicinal plants. Stachys pilifera Benth., valued for its antioxidant and antimicrobial constituents, may experience shifts in both habitat suitability and chemical quality under future climatic regimes. This study integrates ecological niche modeling with chemotypic analysis to assess how climate change could reshape the geographical distribution and secondary-metabolite composition of S. pilifera . Habitat suitability was modeled using MaxEnt under current conditions and CMIP6-based future climates across multiple Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). Essential oil constituents were quantified using GC FID and GC MS, based on 11 populations sampled across the species’ distribution range, and chemometric and multivariate statistical analyses were applied to identify relationships between ecological variables, compound-specific patterns, and overall quality classes. Random Forest models were further used to evaluate the environmental predictability of key metabolites, enabling the generation of climate-sensitive quality zoning maps. The MaxEnt model showed high discriminatory performance, with elevation and seasonal temperature parameters emerging as the dominant predictors, alongside apparent population-level compositional variation. While total suitable habitat is projected to undergo spatial redistribution rather than decline, high-quality chemical zones exhibit narrower environmental optima and stronger sensitivity to future climatic scenarios. Under several SSPs, moderate warming is associated with an increased probability of medium-quality compositional classes, whereas high-quality zones showed more variable responses. These findings provide a preliminary basis for conservation prioritization, climate-resilient cultivation strategies, and sustainable utilization of S. pilifera and other medicinal plants in regions undergoing rapid environmental change.

Article.Title: BIABooster-based characterization of the cell-free DNA fragmentome in healthy adult blood donors reveals stable reference profiles and pre-analytical influences
Article.Authors: Sebastian A.; Sibra G.; Boutonnet A.; Mano M.; Denis J.; Boissan M.; Fina F.; Picard C.; Serres S.; Ginot F.; Pedini P.
Article.Abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a versatile biomarker in oncology, prenatal testing, and organ transplantation. Although cfDNA concentration and genomic markers are widely used, its fragment size distribution (fragmentome) offers additional diagnostic potential. However, robust reference profiles for healthy individuals—particularly for fragments exceeding 300 bp—remain lacking. We used the BIABooster system to analyse cfDNA from 240 healthy adult blood donors, collected in two French cities of different climate at four different time points over a one-year period. cfDNA concentration and size distribution up to 1650 bp were measured and synthesised in 10 concentration and size descriptors. Potential correlations with demographic and haematological parameters were assessed. For selected samples, cfDNA was also analysed up to 10 kb, and the impact of an end-repair step was investigated. cfDNA size profiles were highly consistent across collection sites and time points and were not significantly affected by the demographic and haematological parameters investigated. In particular, the relative abundances of mono- and di-nucleosomal cfDNA fractions were remarkably stable across individuals. Analysis of longer cfDNA fragments revealed an unexpected peak around 3.2 kb that appeared to depend on pre-analytical conditions. This study establishes a detailed characterisation cfDNA fragmentation profiles in healthy adult blood donors and highlights their limited variability across geographic, temporal, demographic and common haematological parameters. It also demonstrates that pre-analytical conditions, particularly blood collection procedures, can influence specific fragmentome features and should therefore be carefully considered when developing cfDNA size profiling for clinical applications.

Article.Title: Methylomic analysis of nasal brushings in pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome: a pilot study
Article.Authors: Williams J.; Elmadany N.; Joshi R.; Jones R.; Gregor N.; Lahni P.; Standage S.; Varisco B.
Article.Abstract: Pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) is a significant cause of mortality in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and supportive care remains the mainstay of treatment. A better understanding of the biological heterogeneity within PARDS, which has resulted in numerous negative interventional trials, is required to develop new therapies. One understudied source of heterogeneity is the epigenetic regulation of gene expression via methylation. We hypothesized that PARDS patients could be classified into at least two subgroups defined by differential methylation of immune-related genes. We conducted a prospective, single-center cohort study of PARDS and control subjects under 18 years of age admitted to the PICU. Nasal brushings were obtained on day 1 in PARDS (n = 21) and control (n = 3) subjects for methylomic analysis, and clinical information and outcomes were recorded until discharge. Principal component analysis (PCA) showed that the first principal component (PC) explained an inordinately large portion of the variation in the data set. Cellular deconvolution showed that PC1 was strongly positively correlated with the epithelial cell fraction and strongly negatively correlated with the neutrophil fraction. After adjustment for cell-type composition, dimensional reduction revealed no subgroup structure (mean silhouette width 0.233 at k = 2). A sensitivity analysis including only the PARDS subjects showed worse subgroup structure (mean silhouette width 0.138 at k = 2) compared to the full cohort. In conclusion, no robust methylomic subgroup structure was identified in nasal brushings from PARDS subjects at this sample size.

Article.Title: Fire evacuation strategies for hospital inpatient wards under different fire source locations
Article.Authors: Zhang P.; Liu S.; Wang X.; Bao Y.; Gao Y.; Chen Y.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Due to patient vulnerability and the diversity of personnel, hospital inpatient evacuations are more prone to congestion and even stagnation, making fire evacuation in hospital wards more complex and hazardous than in other buildings. Most existing studies focus solely on evacuation, neglecting the impact of fire scenarios on the evacuation process. To provide more comprehensive insights into high-rise hospital ward fire evacuations, this study takes the inpatient department of a secondary hospital in China as a case study. Multiple fire scenarios were simulated using PyroSim software, and parameters including temperature, visibility, and CO concentration were analysed to determine the available evacuation time. Based on the building layout and occupant distribution, several evacuation strategies were designed and compared through simulations using Pathfinder software, ultimately identifying the optimal evacuation strategy. The results indicate that evacuation efficiency can be significantly improved by rationally adjusting exit selection, setting occupant priority, and implementing refuge areas. Moreover, evacuation strategies should be appropriately modified and optimised according to the location of the fire source. The findings of this study provide practical strategies for fire evacuation in high-rise hospital wards, effectively reducing casualties and contributing to the safety management of such facilities.

Article.Title: Distinct body temperature trajectories during general anesthesia in pigs undergoing interventional and surgical procedures
Article.Authors: Yoshida K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Temperature trajectories during general anesthesia in pigs remain poorly characterized. We retrospectively examined 735 anesthesia sessions in 715 female pigs, comparing fluoroscopy-guided interventional procedures (657 sessions) with surgical procedures involving body cavity exposure (78 sessions). Rectal temperatures from 20 to 540 min after probe insertion were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models; maximum temperature was assessed over the full monitoring period. Rectal temperature increased progressively during interventional procedures but decreased during surgical procedures, with a significant procedure-by-time interaction that persisted in covariate-adjusted analyses. Maximum recorded rectal temperature was higher in the interventional group and occurred later (median 230 vs. 15 min from probe insertion). At least one temperature measurement ≥ 39.5 °C occurred in 11.9% of interventional sessions and none of the surgical sessions; the corresponding proportions for ≥ 40.0 °C were 4.4% and 0%. Cooling interventions were documented only during interventional sessions. Differences in heat loss associated with body cavity exposure may contribute to these contrasting patterns, although causal mechanisms could not be established. These findings highlight the importance of procedure-specific temperature monitoring during prolonged anesthesia in pigs.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: pigs; surgical procedures; fluoroscopy-guided procedure; rectal temperature; general anesthesia; body temperature; heat loss; interventional procedures; hypothermia

Article.Title: A two-stage MPPT controller with energy-regret coordination and transition memory for PV systems under complex partial shading conditions
Article.Authors: Ye M.; Shi L.; Luo P.; Chen J.; Guo L.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Partial shading creates multiple photovoltaic power peaks and makes online maximum power point tracking (MPPT) costly in harvested energy. ER-ISSA-IVY combines improved sparrow search (ISSA) with contracting Ivy (IVY) refinement. A best-so-far-referenced rule balances estimated exploration gains against measured probing costs; transition memory reuses measured peaks while retaining globally initialized alternatives. Simulations in Python with NumPy use a five-module engineering PV model and a time-domain PWM boost converter. For ER-ISSA-IVY, baseline static and step-irradiance efficiencies are \(100\%\) and \(94.35\%\) , respectively. The controller achieves \(99.99\%\) efficiency in the historical satellite-profile summary and \(99.911\%\) mean daily efficiency in a separate continuous 14-hour simulation. Its switching-level overshoot and ripple are \(0.77\%\) and \(0.07\%\) , respectively. ER-ISSA-IVY has the lowest mean number of first-hit evaluations in static scenarios S1–S3. ER-ISSA-IVY ranks highest or joint-highest in eleven of twelve combinations of array size and profile for ten- and twenty-module arrays. Memory improves whole-profile mean efficiency in all three mismatch tests. Comparisons with six hybrid algorithms show that ER-ISSA-IVY achieves higher mean dynamic efficiency and faster re-tracking under the tested protocols.

Article.Title: Physics-guided machine learning for leakage-aware prediction and temporal extrapolation of concrete carbonation
Article.Authors: Aldosari H.; Shaik N.; Abdul Rasheed M.; Alqahtani S.; Naveed Q.; Alasmari A.; Aldahwan N.; Abdulerahim M.
Article.Abstract: Machine learning models for carbonation depth are usually validated on random splits of multi-source compilations and seldom asked to predict beyond their training ages. We re-evaluated 17 model configurations on 8,120 natural carbonation depths from 71 sources (7 days to 20 years) under five protocols, separating forecasts for series already observed early from forecasts for new sources. Within-series time exponents were 0.52 indoors, 0.46 sheltered and 0.32 unsheltered; only the unsheltered exponent stayed below 0.5 under source resampling, alternative weightings and a censored likelihood, and the outdoor exponents rose at later ages. Random-row testing overstated accuracy: R 2 of about 0.93 fell to 0.63 to 0.67 on unseen sources, where a physics-normalised learner gained little, and only in a few sources. Training gradient boosting on the coefficient d/ \({\text{t}}^{{{\text{n}}_{{\text{e}}} }}\) restored extrapolation in time: R 2 = 0.87 against 0.17 for later ages of observed series, and 0.57 against at most 0.03 for new sources at late ages. Nested hyperparameter tuning did not change these results. Source-grouped residual bands covered 91.8% of new-source depths, unevenly across sources. Service-life values beyond 20 years are power-law extrapolations and are illustrative only.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: concrete carbonation; carbonation depth prediction; temporal extrapolation; physics-guided machine learning; gradient boosting

Article.Title: Comprehensive device optimization and thermal stability investigation of mixed-cation (FAPbI₃)₀.₉₅(MAPbBr₃)₀.₀₅ perovskite solar cells using SCAPS-1D
Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Singh J.; Pachauri R.; Gupta V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nowadays, lead halide perovskite material has gained considerable interest among researchers because of its outstanding properties like excellent absorption coefficient, abundant availability and extreme defect tolerance. Perovskite solar cells are made up of an absorber layer inserted between the electron transport layer (ETL) and hole transport layer (HTL). Previously, the scientists had announced power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.48% in lead halide based perovskite solar cells (PSCs). But the thickness of the absorber layer, the density of defect at the interface, the doping density and operating temperature of the device influence the performance of PSC. Narrow-bandgap halide (NBH) based perovskite solar cell with the absorber layer of (FAPbI3)0.95(MAPbBr3)0.05, TiO2 (electron transport layer) and P3HT (hole transport layer) are designed and simulated in this work. Firstly, the device is analyzed by varying the thickness of the absorber layer from 250 nm to 550 nm, which yields a maximum Jsc of 28.08 mA/cm2 and a PCE of 16.94% at 550 nm. Further results have been analyzed by varying the interface defect density at the ETL/NBH and NBH/HTL interfaces from 1 × 10 9 cm − 2 to 1 × 10 14 cm − 2 , yielding J sc of 24.08 mA/cm2 and PCE of 16.56% at 1 × 10 9 cm − 2 on the NBH/HTL interface. Moreover, the analysis was carried out by varying the doping densities of both the electron transport layer (ETL) and the hole transport layer (HTL) from 1 × 10 14 cm − 3 to 1 × 10 18 cm − 3 , yielding a J sc of 24.09 mA/cm 2 and a PCE of 15.64%. Furthermore, the effect of operating temperature on the NBH-based PSC absorber layer is also examined over the range of 270 K to 300 K to assess the environmental impact. The overall examination of NBH-based PSC enhanced the device’s efficiency by 16.13%. These observations can also be applied to lead-free halide perovskite solar cells and tandem applications.

Article.Title: Treatment of steel slag leachates and the synthesis of calcite via carbon dioxide micro-pressure circulating aeration technique: a pilot study
Article.Authors: Ai S.; Hao R.; Wang Y.; Zeng S.; Cao J.; Sun X.; Li L.; Gao Y.; Bian D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Steel slag leachate poses significant pollution risks to the surrounding environment. This study proposes a CO 2 -based micro-pressure circulating aeration technique for treating strongly alkaline steel slag leachate. By optimizing experimental research and pilot tests in engineering devices, the calcium-containing wastewater was well treated and met the emission standards. The results show that the effluent of this leachate wastewater treatment project reaches Ca 2+ concentrations of ≤ 80 mg/L, with a pH range of 7.0–7.3. Moreover, the process produces mineral carbonation products of pure calcite particles, with sizes ranging from 5 to 100 μm in an aggregated state. The application of this technology not only solves the environmental pollution problem of steel slag leachate but also facilitates CO 2 reduction and resource recovery of calcium carbonate products. This protocol can be applied to the treatment of high-calcium wastewater and the storage of carbon dioxide in the future.

Article.Title: Effects of neem-mediated CuO nanoparticles and nutrient amendments on rice (Oryza sativa L.) performance, soil microbial processes and metal accumulation
Article.Authors: Igiebor F.; Egboduku O.; Ngwoke U.
Article.Abstract: This study explored the synergistic effects of plant-based copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) and organic amendments on the yield and soil microbial dynamics of rice ( Oryza sativa L . ). As global agricultural systems faced increasing challenges related to soil degradation and food security, the application of CuO NPs synthesized using Neem ( Azadirachta indica ) leaf extracts offered a promising solution for enhancing crop productivity. In this study, CuO NPs were applied in combination with organic amendments (cow dung and NPK fertilizer) to assess their impact on rice growth, yield, and soil health. The tested soil amendments impacted soil properties, microbial enzyme activities, and overall rice development in noticeably different ways. Cow dung yielded the highest grain mass at 168.2 g plant −1 , with the CuO-NPs + NPK fertilizer blend following at 153.42 g plant −1 . In contrast, combining CuO-NPs with cow dung produced the lowest output at 113.36 g plant −1 . Interestingly, nanoparticle applications excelled in panicle productivity; the CuO-NPs + cow dung and CuO-NPs + NPK mixes generated 750.4 and 711.42 grains g −1 , respectively. The variations observed in soil dehydrogenase, urease, and phosphatase activities further confirm that soil microbial functions responded uniquely to each specific amendment group.

Article.Title: Associations of body composition and obesity with retinal microvascular and ocular biometric parameters in children
Article.Authors: Mazaheri-Tehrani S.; Amani-Beni R.; Arabi S.; Pourazizi M.; Pourmahdi-Boroujeni M.; Heidari-Beni M.; Kelishadi R.
Article.Abstract: Limited evidence is available regarding the potential ocular complications of childhood obesity. This study aimed to investigate the associations of multiple anthropometric and body composition indices with retinal microvascular characteristics and ocular biometric parameters in children. This cross-sectional study was conducted from July 2023 to December 2024 in Isfahan, Iran. The analytical dataset comprised 223 children aged 5–17 years, including 9 with thinness, 115 with normal weight, 39 with overweight, and 60 with obesity; categorical comparisons included the latter three groups ( n = 214). Anthropometric and body composition measurements, ocular biometry, and optical coherence tomography angiography were assessed. Associations were examined using linear mixed-effects models, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for fully adjusted exposure contrasts. Several central and overall adiposity indices were associated with higher whole-image, parafoveal, and perifoveal superficial vessel density (SVD) after multiplicity adjustment. Higher skeletal muscle mass index was associated with lower whole-image deep vessel density (DVD) (β=-0.839 per 1 kg/m², 95% CI -1.453 to -0.225; adjusted P = 0.033). Obesity was associated with higher SVD in three regions, while overweight was associated with lower parafoveal and perifoveal DVD. The principal vessel-density patterns were maintained after additional axial-length adjustment. No ocular-biometry association remained significant after multiplicity adjustment. Adiposity and body composition showed region-specific associations with retinal vessel density in children, whereas ocular-biometry associations did not remain significant after multiplicity adjustment. These exploratory cross-sectional findings require confirmation in longitudinal studies that account for pubertal development.

Article.Title: Seed transitioning to seedling: a genome wide association study on trade-off between seed maturity indices and osmopriming response in quinoa
Article.Authors: Razzaq M.; Aslam M.; Ahmad R.; Afzal I.
Article.Abstract: Quinoa seed retains residual amounts of chlorophyll after maturation, affecting germination performance. Seed priming is a promising pre-sowing treatment to enhance seed germination under sub-optimal conditions. This study evaluated the response of quinoa seeds (immature and mature) to osmopriming. We further dissected the genetic components of that response through a genome-wide association analysis approach. We subjected a diverse panel of 95 quinoa accessions to osmopriming followed by pre-assessment of seed chlorophyll fluorescence, final germination, seedling length, seedling vigor index, abnormal seedlings and their respective colors. Association studies identified 57 marker trait associations (MTAs), out of which 18 were identified for seed traits before priming while other 39 were identified for enhanced seed performance after priming treatment. Contrary to the positive impact of seed priming on germination, abnormal seedling proportion was relatively higher in seeds with increased initial chlorophyll fluorescence. We annotated novel putative candidate genes associated with seedling anomalies that might be involved in chlorophyll degradation or retention pathways. Other putative candidate genes identified included those related to stress signaling, membrane stabilization, and hormonal regulation. The findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of mature and immature seed response to osmopriming and offer potential genomic targets for the development of climate-resilient quinoa cultivars with improved seed quality traits.

Article.Title: From phytochemical profile to skin-related bioactivity: an in vitro study of onobrychis oxyodonta boiss
Article.Authors: Şentürk T.; Uysal A.; Nath E.; Barak T.; Yılmaz M.; Celep E.
Article.Abstract: The Fabaceae family ranks among the largest groups of flowering plants, encompassing species that are both economically significant and nutritionally valuable. Several Onobrychis species have been traditionally used for skin-related conditions and have shown promising phytochemical and biological properties. However, no detailed phytochemical quantification or skin-related enzyme inhibitory evaluation has been reported for Onobrychis oxyodonta Boiss. In this study, an 80% aqueous-ethanolic extract prepared from the aerial parts of O. oxyodonta was investigated for its antioxidant capacity, phytochemical composition, and inhibitory activity against tyrosinase, collagenase, and hyaluronidase. Antioxidant activity was assessed by DPPH, FRAP, CUPRAC, and TOAC assays. Phytochemical characterization involved total phenolic and flavonoid content assays, LC-MS/MS screening of 53 phytochemicals, GC-MS profiling, and HPTLC quantification of arbutin. The study findings revealed the presence of arbutin, a compound that aids in the treatment of hyperpigmentation, in ethanol extract. The extract showed inhibitory effects against tyrosinase, hyaluronidase, and collagenase at the tested concentration, with the highest inhibition observed against tyrosinase (39.6 ± 1.2%) and collagenase (28.01 ± 0.50%). These findings provide preliminary evidence that O. oxyodonta is a source of phytochemicals with antioxidant and skin-related biological activities, warranting further investigation.

Article.Title: Vehicle-external screening of persistent fuel-intensive operation using remote OBD data
Article.Authors: Liu T.; Li T.; Yue D.
Article.Abstract: Fleet environmental management needs scalable ways to identify fuel-intensive operation in dense telematics streams. We analyzed 464,936 hot-engine observations from 14 heavy-duty diesel tractor units monitored by OBD-interface networked terminals and GNSS through cooperation with a Nanjing-based transport company. We asked whether patterns defined in ten development vehicles could support screening in four unseen vehicles. Maximal persistent episodes occupied 10.62% of support but carried 29.17% of the time-integrated OBD fuel-rate signal. Development-defined spatial cells retained excess holdout burden after exposure adjustment, and relative-history profiles remained recognizable in the unseen vehicles. At natural prevalence, operational and fuel histories provided similar ranking information, while their combination yielded a modest improvement. A daily rank cap translated scores into a fixed review workload without overwhelming users with repeated alerts. The findings position remote OBD as a vehicle-external screening tool for prioritizing vehicle–time–location contexts for fleet review and targeted confirmatory measurement.

Article.Title: Socio-cultural and health system barriers to male participation in antenatal care in somaliland
Article.Authors: Abdiwali S.; Hashi M.; Omar O.; Ahmed A.; Keise A.; Nur N.; Geta T.
Article.Abstract: Antenatal Care (ANC) is a critical intervention for reducing maternal morbidity and mortality. While global health strategies increasingly emphasize the role of male partners in improving maternal health outcomes, male involvement remains significantly low in Somaliland. This study explores the socio-cultural, economic, and institutional barriers and opportunities for male participation in ANC, aligning the findings with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 3 (Good Health), 5 (Gender Equality), and 17 (Partnerships). The study employed a robust qualitative methodology involving a total of 31 participants to ensure a multi-dimensional perspective on the research topic. Data collection was triangulated through three focus group discussions (FGDs) comprising six women in antenatal or postnatal care, eight urban married men, and six rural married men, alongside eight individual in-depth interviews (IDIs) with both men and women. To incorporate professional and community oversight, three key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with a healthcare provider, a health center head, and a community leader. The findings reveal a complex interplay of barriers. Primary socio-cultural obstacles include the perception of ANC as a “woman’s domain” and the fear of social stigma among men. Economically, the pressure of providing for the household often prioritizes work over clinical attendance. Institutionally, participants highlighted long waiting times, lack of male-friendly spaces in MCH centers, and a lack of clear communication from healthcare providers regarding the importance of male presence. Conversely, opportunities identified include the influential role of religious leaders in reframing male involvement as a family responsibility and the potential for digital health reminders to engage fathers. This study demonstrates that while men acknowledge the value of antenatal care (ANC), their active participation is frequently hindered by deeply rooted patriarchal norms, healthcare facility designs that exclude men, and significant economic or informational gaps. However, when these systemic barriers are mitigated through the implementation of male-friendly health policies, targeted educational initiatives, and proactive community engagement, male involvement significantly increases. Enhancing male participation serves as a catalyst for achieving the SDGs and ensuring a holistic approach to reproductive health.

Article.Title: Multispectral camouflaged object detection using a boundary-driven guidance network
Article.Authors: Ding B.; Liu D.; Ni H.; An J.
Article.Abstract: Camouflaged object detection remains difficult when targets share similar colors and textures with their surroundings, particularly when only RGB imagery is available. This study examines whether non-visible spectral information can improve detection under such conditions. We propose a Boundary-Driven Guidance Network (BDGNet) for multispectral camouflaged object detection. BDGNet combines spectral-spatial prior estimation, prior-guided hierarchical feature modulation, and progressive boundary-aware decoding to use spatial and spectral information while reducing background interference. Experiments on the MCOD benchmark show that BDGNet outperforms the compared methods. Band-subset analysis also shows a clear benefit from information beyond RGB: the $$F_\beta$$ score increases from 0.776 with RGB input to 0.791 with Red Edge/NIR input and to 0.845 with the full multispectral input. These results indicate that multispectral observations can complement RGB imagery and improve target delineation in visually ambiguous scenes.
