Article.Title: Circadian eating-related drives in Parkinson’s disease patients with restless legs syndrome
Article.Authors: Marques A.; Pereira B.; Lestra P.; Beal C.; Vidal T.; Rieu I.; de Chazeron I.; Durif F.; Fantini M.
Article.Abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS), both idiopathic and associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD), has been linked to impulse control disorders (ICDs), particularly compulsive eating. In idiopathic RLS, eating-related symptoms may occur preferentially in the evening or at night, but whether this pattern extends to PD-associated RLS remains unknown. To compare compulsive eating and the temporal distribution of eating-related features in PD patients with and without RLS. Fifty-four non-demented PD patients with ( n = 27) and without RLS ( n = 27), matched for age and sex, were prospectively recruited. ICDs, including compulsive eating, were assessed using the Ardouin Scale of Behavior in Parkinson’s Disease. Night Eating Syndrome (NES) and Sleep-Related Eating Disorder (SRED) were diagnosed clinically. The Night Eating Questionnaire (NEQ) assessed evening–night eating-related behaviors and cognitions, while a seven-day diary recorded the timing of eating episodes. Compulsive eating was more frequent in RLS+ than RLS− patients (40.7% vs. 3.7%, p = 0.001), as was the presence of at least one ICD (59.3% vs. 25.9%, p = 0.01). NEQ scores were higher in RLS+ patients ( p = 0.004), but no patient fulfilled criteria for NES or SRED, and diary-recorded nocturnal eating did not differ between groups. RLS in PD was strongly associated with compulsive eating and ICDs. Higher NEQ scores suggest a greater evening–night orientation of eating-related behaviors and cognitions in PD patients with RLS, although no corresponding shift in the timing of eating episodes or clinically defined nocturnal eating disorders was observed. The circadian significance of this association therefore remains uncertain and requires further chronobiological investigation. Registration number : NCT03818243.

Article.Title: Changes in thyroid function during and after non-severe acute ınfections in children: a prospective longitudinal study
Article.Authors: Dörtkardeşler B.; Özalp Kızılay D.; Örsdemir Hortu H.; Azarsız E.; Öztürk Atasoy T.; Darcan Ş.; Kurugöl Z.; Gökçe Ş.
Article.Abstract: Thyroid function tests obtained during acute illness are difficult to interpret. In this prospective longitudinal study, we examined changes in thyroid function in 90 otherwise healthy children aged 2–18 years with non-severe acute infections. TSH, free thyroxine (fT4), free triiodothyronine (fT3) and reverse T3 (rT3) were measured at presentation and on days 14 and 30, and changes over time were analysed using linear mixed-effects models. At presentation, TSH was below the age-specific reference range in 6.7% and above it in 2.2% of children, and fT4 was low in 6.7%; these values normalized during follow-up in all children with available data, mostly by day 14. From presentation to day 14, fT3 increased by 1.07 ng/L (95% CI 0.78–1.35) and TSH by 23% (95% CI 5–44%), with no further change by day 30, whereas fT4 remained stable. Higher C-reactive protein concentrations were associated with lower fT3. Reverse T3 was undetectable in 81.1% of children. Non-severe acute infections in children are associated with mild, transient changes in thyroid function, consistent with a partial adaptive response within the spectrum of non-thyroidal illness syndrome. Abnormal results obtained in this setting should be interpreted cautiously and reassessed after recovery, with timing individualized to the clinical context.

Article.Title: Patient profiles, treatment patterns and biomarker use in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer in Greece: the retrospective real-world INFINITY study
Article.Authors: Sofia A.; Giannis M.; Anna K.; Ioannis B.; Ηelena L.; Georgios G.; Christos C.; Vasileios R.; Christos E.; Paris K.; Ippokratis K.; Dimitrios B.; Flora Z.; Davide M.; Stamatia D.; Andreas D.; Ioannis D.; Eleni I.; Konstantinos S.
Article.Abstract: This retrospective chart review study captured real-world initial management strategies and patient characteristics among those diagnosed with early-stage (stages I–IIIC) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) between January 2016 and December 2020 at participating hospitals in Greece. This study describes management practices prior to the era of immuno-oncology therapy (IO) and targeted therapy (TT) in ES NSCLC. 300 patients were included, with equal representation of stages I, II, and III, excluding patients enrolled in clinical trials. Observation period extended from diagnosis until development of distant metastasis, withdrawal of consent, or death. Data was collected across 16 oncology clinics between October 2021 and May 2022. Median age at diagnosis was 67 years; 74% were male and 89% had a history of smoking. Most patients (96%) had a performance status of 0–1, and 62% had non-squamous histology. Biomarker testing was limited: 46% underwent any testing, including programmed death-ligand 1 (33%), epidermal growth factor receptor (31%), and anaplastic lymphoma kinase (28%). All but three patients received treatment. Surgical resection was performed in 75% of cases and systemic treatment in 74%, predominantly chemotherapy (91%). Radiotherapy was given to 29%. Overall, 68% received ≥ 2 treatment modalities. Among stage III patients, treatment appeared variable: 42% received definitive chemoradiotherapy without surgery, while among those who underwent surgery, 71% received adjuvant systemic treatment, 20% neoadjuvant, and 5% both. Most patients were treated with guideline-concordant modalities. These findings provide an essential historical baseline for evaluating evolving management patterns as novel systemic therapies are adopted into routine practice.

Article.Title: Long-term spatiotemporal assessment of PM₂.₅ in a semi-urban region of Bangladesh using CAMS and MERRA-2 reanalysis data
Article.Authors: Paul R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is poorly characterised outside South Asia’s major cities, where monitoring is sparse. We assessed PM₂.₅ in Habiganj, a semi-urban district of north-eastern Bangladesh, from 2016 to 2025 using two atmospheric reanalyses, CAMS and MERRA-2. Annual district means ranged from 70.4 to 84.9 µg m⁻³ in CAMS and from 35.0 to 44.2 µg m⁻³ in MERRA-2, 7–17 times the World Health Organization guideline of 5 µg m⁻³ in every year. The two products agreed on the seasonal cycle (R² = 0.80) and on year-to-year variation ( r = 0.70, p = 0.023) but differed systematically in magnitude (mean difference 39.9 µg m⁻³); a 1-km satellite-derived product placed the 2016–2023 district mean (51.8 µg m⁻³) between them. Neither reanalysis showed a significant annual trend; a seasonal Mann–Kendall test indicated a modest increase in CAMS only (+ 0.57 µg m⁻³ yr⁻¹, p = 0.019). In MERRA-2, organic matter (33%), sulfate (30%) and dust (23%) dominated PM₂.₅. An illustrative health-impact assessment suggests roughly 2300–4000 premature deaths per year, depending on the concentration–response function. These results indicate that severe, persistent PM₂.₅ exposure extends beyond Bangladesh’s large cities and that several products should be compared where ground monitoring is lacking.

Article.Title: Burden of menstrual disorders and its associated risk factors among young adult women in West Bengal, India
Article.Authors: Das P.; Jungari S.
Article.Abstract: Menstrual health is a vital component of women’s reproductive well-being, yet menstrual disorders remain highly prevalent and contribute substantially to reproductive ill health worldwide. In this context, this community-based cross-sectional study investigates the burden of menstrual disorders and their associated risk factors among young adult women in West Bengal, India. A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted in West Bengal, involving 420 women aged 15-34 years. Descriptive statistical techniques were used to estimate the prevalence of menstrual disorders and related symptoms, and logistic regression was used to identify key determinants. Results show that the prevalence of menstrual disorders was 75%, among all disorders, dysmenorrhea (58.1%) was highest, followed by PMS (47.1%) and Oligomenorrhea (38.3%). The study further found that occupation [OR=3.40, 95% C.I, (1.08-10.7)] place of residence [OR=1.80, 95% C.I, (1.04-3.13)], Obesity [OR=10.29, 95% C.I, (1.85-56.95)] depression status [OR=8.39, 95% C.I, (2.99-23.53)] and eating out [OR=3.22, 95% C.I, (1.70-6.07)] were significantly associated factors with menstrual disorders among young adult women. The study found that 75% of the women studied had experienced at least one menstrual disorder. Results highlight the importance of identifying health complications and suggest that early detection and treatment can promote healthier lifestyles and reduce menstrual disorders.

Article.Title: A machine learning algorithm facilitates treatment selection for up to three hepatocellular carcinomas ≤ 3 cm in size
Article.Authors: Kokudo T.; Yamada Y.; Asaoka Y.; Tateishi R.; Hasegawa K.; Kabeya Y.; Kamada A.; Yoshida S.; Nakamura Y.; Yoshimitsu K.; Yano H.; Murakami T.; Fukumoto T.; Hatano E.; Shimada M.; Kato N.; Iijima H.; Kurosaki M.; Sakamoto M.; Kudo M.; Kokudo N.
Article.Abstract: Liver resection (LR) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) are recommended for patients with up to three hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs) measuring ≤ 3 cm and preserved liver function. Nevertheless, treatment allocation is decided according to the preference of the treating doctor. This study aimed to develop a predictive model to guide treatment decisions based on survival outcomes. A total of 18,958 patients with HCC with up to three nodules measuring ≤ 3 cm were included from the nationwide survey of Japan. Deep survival analysis was performed using the Recurrent Deep Survival Machines (RDSM) model. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation, concordance index (C-index), and overall survival (OS). A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model using the same covariates was constructed as a conventional reference analysis. Survival curves were compared using the log-rank test. Potential confounding was adjusted for using 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). Patients who underwent LR showed significantly longer OS than those who underwent RFA (5-year survival rate 81.4% vs. 73.1%; P < 0.005). The trained RDSM model achieved a C-index of 0.68, comparable to that of the multivariable Cox proportional hazards model (0.69). In the deep learning (DL) model, patients who received the recommended treatment exhibited significantly longer survival than those who did not (5-year survival rate 81.2% vs. 73.9%; P < 0.005; PSM, 81.9% vs. 76.7%; P < 0.005). The DL model recommended LR in 6,966 (84.5%) patients who received RFA, especially those exhibiting typical imaging patterns (early enhancement and washout in the computed tomography (CT) images [85.9% vs. 61.7% and 84.1 vs.74.3%, respectively]). The proposed DL-based treatment recommendation model may help guide treatment allocation for patients with HCC with up to three nodules measuring ≤ 3 cm. These findings suggest the potential utility of individualized DL-based treatment recommendations.

Article.Title: Re-examining cognitive abilities and sustainability in fragile ecotourism ecosystems: the silence of uncertainty and the power of self-regulated action
Article.Authors: Mohammadi A.; Azareh A.; Alambeigi A.; Rafiei-Sardooi E.; Ansari A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transitioning toward sustainable ecotourism destinations requires a profound understanding of how individual cognitive mechanisms scale up to macro-level socio-ecological outcomes. While structural linear models often treat sustainability as a mechanical output, capturing the dynamic, organic flow of socio-cognitive energy and how human agency is systematically channeled within fragile ecological regions remains a critical theoretical omission in sustainable tourism governance. Grounded in Entrepreneurial Cognitive Theory and Personal Initiative Theory this study addresses this critical gap by investigating the complex structural pathways through which local actors’ cognitive capabilities and opportunity recognition drive environmental and economic sustainability in a developing ecotourism destination. Data were gathered from a purposive sample of ecotourism managers, local entrepreneurs, and regional development experts. Structural Equation Modeling via Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) and Multi-Group Analysis (PLS-MGA) were employed to validate the hypothesized structural pathways. The empirical findings demonstrate that cognitive capabilities and opportunity recognition serve as the foundational metabolic energy the sunlight and nutrient-rich soil that triggers behavioral agency and synthesizes service innovation. The model’s key theoretical originality lies in revealing the dual-pillar mechanism required for ultimate sustainability: synthesized innovations must be simultaneously amplified through experiential staging (customer experience design) and rooted via social license (social trust and local acceptance). Furthermore, the multi-group analysis identifies professional tenure as a vital boundary condition that significantly optimizes the metabolic efficiency of converting cognitive potential into robust ecotourism innovations. The primary scientific contribution of this research is the paradigm shift it introduces to ecotourism modeling, moving away from rigid, mechanistic, and linear frameworks toward a living, adaptive system perspective. By proving that socio-ecological sustainability is not a static endpoint but an emergent, metabolic outcome of structured human agency, experience design, and community trust, this study offers a novel theoretical blueprint for managing sustainable regional tourism ecosystems under boundary conditions of professional experience.

Article.Title: Bias-resilient ECG waveform modeling for rapid differentiation of stanford type-A aortic syndrome from STEMI
Article.Authors: Xu Y.; Li Y.; Ren Y.; Wang J.; Xu Z.; Wu D.; Guo Z.; Song X.; Tian H.
Article.Abstract: Stanford type-A aortic syndrome (TAAS) and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are time-critical cardiovascular emergencies that can show overlapping electrocardiographic findings but require fundamentally different treatment strategies. Differentiation at the first ECG assessment is therefore critical, yet labeled ECG resources for this task remain scarce, especially for physician-confirmed TAAS cases from emergency-care settings. Here, we introduce the Anzhen Dataset, a paper-based 12-lead ECG cohort comprising 728 first-admission records from 344 TAAS and 384 STEMI patients, providing a clinically grounded resource for this underexplored differential diagnosis task. We also identify a shortcut-learning risk in direct paper-ECG image classification, in which visual models exploit non-physiological image cues rather than electrophysiological morphology, limiting their reliability in real-world application scenarios. To reduce this risk, we propose a bias-resilient waveform modeling framework that converts paper ECGs into standardized 12-lead one-dimensional signals through perspective correction, lead localization, grid and noise removal, waveform digitization, and interpolation-based compensation. A lightweight ConvNeXt-Femto model then combines morphological analysis, low-rank feature compression, and lead-region relational attention to capture local waveform differences and cross-lead pathological consistency. In the TAAS–STEMI task, the model achieved 0.900 accuracy and 0.906 F1-score with 61,850 trainable parameters and a classifier inference latency of 4.010 ms per sample. Multi-class experiments, ablation studies, and visualization analyses further supported the model’s representation ability, module contribution, and physiological interpretability. These proof-of-concept findings support waveform-centered modeling as a lightweight approach that reduces image-related bias in TAAS–STEMI differentiation from paper-based ECGs; the model is intended only for preliminary risk stratification and cannot replace confirmatory imaging.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: ST-elevation myocardial infarction; shortcut learning; differential diagnosis; perspective correction

Article.Title: Machine learning detects mild cognitive impairment in cerebral small vessel disease via retinal vascular–structural–morphologic metrics
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ma S.; Li L.; He H.; Yuan L.; Lu Q.
Article.Abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major cause of vascular mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but early recognition of CSVD-related MCI and individuals at risk of its development remains challenging. The retina offers a non-invasive window into cerebral microvasculature and neurodegeneration, and advances in swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA) now allow quantitative assessment of retinal vascular, structural, and morphologic alterations in vivo. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model that predicts MCI in patients with CSVD based on SS-OCTA-derived retinal biomarkers. We retrospectively enrolled 309 consecutive patients with CSVD, of whom 256 met the inclusion criteria, including 101 patients with MCI and 155 without MCI. An initial feature pool comprising clinical variables and SS-OCTA-derived retinal vascular, structural, and microvascular topological metrics was constructed. A leakage-free feature-selection workflow was implemented within the training cohort. After final refitting on the complete training cohort, the Boruta algorithm retained 22 features, which were subsequently reduced by Akaike information criterion-guided backward stepwise logistic regression to seven key retinal predictors: superficial capillary plexus vessel density in the inner ring, inner superior macular retinal nerve fibre layer thickness, inner nasal ganglion cell complex thickness, foveal ganglion cell–inner plexiform layer thickness, inner superior and inner inferior ganglion cell–inner plexiform layer thickness, and vascular bifurcation number. Logistic regression, decision tree, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were trained on 70% of the cohort and evaluated on the remaining 30%. XGBoost achieved the highest numerical area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.908 and showed favorable overall validation performance, including high specificity and precision, a favourable F1-score, good calibration, and greater clinical net benefit on decision-curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) confirmed that inner-ring superficial microvascular rarefaction, inner macular neuroretinal thinning, and reduced vascular bifurcation complexity were strongly associated with increased MCI risk. These findings demonstrate that SS-OCTA-derived retinal biomarkers, integrated through an interpretable machine-learning model, can non-invasively identify CSVD patients at high risk of MCI and may support earlier, targeted intervention pending external validation.

Article.Title: A multi-layer deep feature selection and meta-ensemble learning framework for cross-platform malware detection
Article.Authors: Maqsood A.; Mirza H.; Rashid J.; Jamel L.; Sarwar N.
Article.Abstract: Malware: Malicious programs damage or compromise computer networks, systems, and devices. Identifying these threats represents a key challenge within common hybrid platforms, Windows and Android. Standard security measures like signature-based systems pass over modern complex viruses. To mitigate this, researchers recommend modern technical options like static analysis, dynamic analysis, supervised algorithms, ensemble frameworks and deep computing logic for advancing virus removal efficiency on desktop and mobile environments. Still, current solutions often confront massive obstacles concerning model interpretability, insufficient logic transparency, alongside a troubling rate regarding erroneous alerts appearing when users run heavy scans upon compromised files or suspect background operations affecting clean targets. Existing studies mostly address Android or Windows separately, rely on a single feature type, and evaluate a single classifier or a single-layer ensemble on one dataset. This study proposes a multi-level stacking ensemble framework for cross-platform malware detection that combines static and dynamic features from Android and Windows under one unified preprocessing pipeline (standardization, PCA and min-max scaling). A deep feature selection stage (autoencoder, 1D-CNN and attention) is applied before stacking. Twelve heterogeneous base learners feed a logistic-regression meta-classifier. The framework is evaluated on six public datasets in three experimental settings (static, dynamic and combined) and compared with traditional machine-learning, tree-ensemble and deep-learning baselines. It reaches 99.93% accuracy (FPR 0.07%) on static data and 96.19% accuracy (FPR 3.73%) on dynamic data, and 99.03% accuracy (FPR 0.90%) on the pooled hybrid setting. The study also discusses its limitations, including leakage risk and cross-domain transfer.

Article.Title: Flexural strengthening techniques for ultra-high-performance fiber-reinforced concrete beams: experimental study
Article.Authors: Abadel A.; Alqarni A.
Article.Abstract: This paper aims to investigate the various strengthening techniques for restoring the flexural performance of ultra-high-performance fiber-reinforced concrete (UHPFRC) beams with a simulated reduction in tensile reinforcement, represented by removing one or two steel bars to model a simplified condition of reinforcement loss due to corrosion. The strengthening techniques include near-surface mounting (NSM) of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) bars, glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) bars, and a CFRP plate. In addition, a CFRP sheet was used as an externally bonded layer on the tension side of the beam. Six beams were fabricated, which had a cross-section measuring 120 mm in width and 185 mm in depth, with an overall length of 1500 mm. All the beams were tested using a four-point flexural test. The results indicate that the strengthening techniques used significantly improved the load-carrying capacity. The B-2-CFRP beam exhibited the highest ultimate load, representing a 55.6% increase over the control beam (B-CS). In addition, the B-2-CFRP beam demonstrated superior serviceability performance with the highest energy absorption capacity, with 228.2%, compared to the B-CS beam. The predicted-to-experimental capacity ratios ranged from 0.95 to 1.17.

Article.Title: Student mental health patterns in the REALISE cohort show four trajectories over one academic year
Article.Authors: Kahle A.; Jusepeitis A.; Croy I.; Krull F.; Ahrendt L.; Rottstädt F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract University students experience high levels of psychological distress, often exceeding those observed in other young adult populations. Despite growing evidence that students are at increased risk for psychological distress, its development across the academic year remains insufficiently understood. Additionally, for early identification of highly distressed students, understanding heterogeneous patterns is crucial. This longitudinal study investigated trajectories of psychological distress among N = 458 students from a German university using the Depression , Anxiety , Stress Scale with monthly assessments across one academic year. Latent class growth analysis identified distinct trajectory classes. In addition, a random forest model predicted class membership based on baseline measurements. Four trajectory classes were identified: low psychological distress (36.9%), moderate psychological distress (32.1%), moderate-high psychological distress (23.8%), and high psychological distress (7.2%). The high-distress class showed persistently elevated distress, whereas the other three classes revealed decreasing distress over time. Baseline measures of depression, anxiety, stress, and well-being best predicted trajectory class membership with moderate average accuracy (61.4% [95% CI 56.7, 65.8%]), demonstrating best accuracy for extreme trajectory classes (low and high distress). Including two additional within-year measurement points slightly increased accuracy to 66.4% (95% CI 61.8, 70.7%), but notably improved the differentiation of moderate distress trajectories. These findings suggest that baseline screening enables early risk stratification, whereas subsequent within-year assessments could serve as ongoing monitoring for adaptive risk refinement and targeted resource allocation in university settings.

Article.Title: Screening and reporting of occupational noise related hearing disorders using MySmartOH—a cloud-based analytics solution
Article.Authors: Pathmanathan P.; Yew S.; Yusoff H.; Husin S.
Article.Abstract: This study was aimed to evaluate the validity and agreement of MySmartOH (a novel cloud-based analytical software), as compared to conventional audiometric test, for screening of occupational noise–related hearing disorders (ONRHDs) among Malaysian workers. Subsequently, the time taken for screening and reporting between MySmartOH and the conventional paper-based approach was compared. This cross-sectional study involved 16 occupational health doctors and 320 audiograms. For each hearing condition, sensitivity and specificity tests were used to determine the software’s validity while Cohen’s kappa coefficient was used to assess its agreement. The time taken to screen and report ONRHDs between MySmartOH and the conventional method was analysed. The sensitivity of MySmartOH ranged from 55.6 to 99.1% while specificity ranged between 70.0 and 99.2%. Cohen’s kappa values for MySmartOH ranged between 0.41 and 0.92. For the left ear, screening and reporting were faster with MySmartOH (0.93 and 0.48 min) than with the conventional method (1.25 and 0.87 min). For the right ear, MySmartOH also shortened screening (0.87 vs. 1.15 min) and reporting times (0.47 vs. 0.83 min). MySmartOH reduced screening time by 24.3–25.6% and reporting time by 43.3–44.8%. MySmartOH demonstrated variable diagnostic performance, with moderate-to-high agreement for screening ONRHDs compared with conventional audiometric assessment. It also offers a faster alternative to the conventional method.

Article.Title: Seafood intake and urinary total mercury in children: dose–response in three national samples and a paired urine–blood comparison in adolescents
Article.Authors: Yun J.; Kim D.; Lee I.; Lee J.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Urinary mercury is read as a marker of inorganic exposure, and urinary elimination of dietary methylmercury is treated as negligible. Whether urine carries a measurable seafood signal in children is unresolved, and national programs rarely draw blood from young children. The Korean National Environmental Health Survey (Cycle 5, 2021–2023) provided three probability samples: preschoolers ( n = 648), schoolchildren ( n = 780), and adolescents ( n = 901). We fitted survey-weighted log-linear models of habitual seafood intake with a Rao–Wu bootstrap. Each doubling of animal seafood intake was associated with 13.5%, 11.8%, and 15.0% higher creatinine-corrected total mercury in spot urine, pooling to 13.2% (95% CI 11.0, 15.5) with no detectable heterogeneity. Seaweed, the internal negative control, showed no positive association. In 812 adolescents, dietary slopes did not differ detectably between urine and blood (ratio 0.99; 0.72, 1.28), category profiles were similar, and adjustment for blood total mercury halved the urinary dietary slope. Agreement within individuals ( n = 872) stayed moderate (weighted Spearman ρ = 0.50, κ = 0.33). Spot urinary total mercury tracks seafood-related mercury exposure at population scale; without speciation, the signal cannot be assigned to methylmercury or inorganic mercury. It cannot stand in for blood mercury in one child.

Article.Title: Environmental conditions associated with the occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in agricultural landscapes affected by intensive livestock production farming
Article.Authors: Kupiec J.
Article.Abstract: Intensive livestock production is associated with increased pressure on aquatic environments in agricultural landscapes. The occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in waters exposed to intensive livestock production was analysed in relation to selected physicochemical parameters. The study was conducted at two locations characterized by high livestock density and included precipitation, surface, groundwater, and well waters. The alga was detected in surface and precipitation waters, but was absent from groundwater. The occurrence of H. pluvialis was associated with moderately nutrient-enriched waters characterized by elevated conductivity and slightly alkaline pH. Elevated nutrient concentrations were recorded in waters influenced by intensive livestock production. The results suggest that H. pluvialis may represent a potential candidate indicator of aquatic environments exposed to intensive agricultural pressure. However, the observed relationships are associative rather than direct causal effects, and further studies are required to evaluate the broader indicator potential of this species under different environmental conditions.

Article.Title: Estimation of individual-tree DBH and allometry-derived biomass of Korean red pine using mask-based multimodal deep learning from UAV imagery
Article.Authors: Kwon K.; Kim S.; Lee Y.; Cha S.; Kwon C.; Im S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of individual-tree biomass is important for forest inventory, carbon assessment, and fuel management. In this study, we proposed a mask-based multimodal deep learning framework for estimating diameter at breast height (DBH) and allometry-derived tree biomass (TB) using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. Field measurements and UAV imagery were collected from two Korean red pine plots in South Korea. Crown metrics obtained from Mask R-CNN delineation were combined with crown-specific image features in a fully connected prediction head. Leave-one-plot-out evaluation was used to compare the framework with image-only and metric-only neural networks, least squares regression, random forest, and XGBoost. In the baseline comparison, the multimodal model showed the lowest test relative root mean square error (rRMSE) in both evaluation directions: 10.93% and 11.09% for DBH and 26.24% and 25.90% for allometry-derived TB. However, paired comparisons did not consistently support lower multimodal error against every model. Model performance also varied with image resizing and alternative masks. These results support combining crown metrics and image features for individual-tree estimation within the conditions examined. Further evaluation is required for other forest conditions.

Article.Title: Weather-aware contrastive state-space learning for probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasting under high irradiance variability
Article.Authors: Asiri J.; Alyahya T.; Elmaleeh M.; Arishi A.; Alawad W.; Ali E.; Alromithy F.
Article.Abstract: Accurate probabilistic photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential to reliable operation of power systems with high renewable penetration. The rapid changes in the weather lead to strong non-stationarity in PV generation and degrade both prediction accuracy and uncertainty estimation. We propose a weather-aware contrastive state-space learning framework for probabilistic forecasting of PV power. Our framework integrates a selective state-space encoder for efficient long-range temporal modeling, a contrastive learning module that structures representations according to irradiance-ramp-based weather regimes, and a quantile forecasting head for direct uncertainty estimation. This design does not explicitly generate weather scenarios but adapts the learned representations to varying atmospheric conditions. The framework was validated using 118,865 operational measurements collected from a 350 kWp grid-connected photovoltaic system under real operating conditions. The experimental task is formulated as a short-term one-step-ahead PV power forecasting problem using a historical input window of 24 consecutive observations. On the full evaluation set, the proposed model achieved an RMSE of 0.318, an MAE of 0.251, a MAPE of 11.02%, and a CRPS of 0.244 on the original PV power scale after inverse transformation from the normalized training representation, outperforming the persistence, recurrent, Transformer-based, and state-space baselines that were evaluated. Under high irradiance-variability conditions on the evaluated photovoltaic installation, the RMSE was 36% lower than that of LSTM and 17% lower than that of the independent Mamba baseline. Ablation experiments also showed the complementary contributions of selective state-space modeling and weather aware contrastive learning. These results demonstrate the potential of weather-aware state-space representation learning for efficient probabilistic PV forecasting under non-stationary operating conditions.

Article.Title: Association of MMP9 (rs17576 and rs3787268) genetic variants with breast cancer susceptibility: integrating molecular and bioinformatics approaches
Article.Authors: Zidan N.; Almutairi F.; Sakran M.; Alalawy A.; Shaman A.; Omran A.; Albalawi M.; Albalwi R.; A-Elgadir T.; EL-Ezaly F.; El-Ghany M.; Keshk A.; Alatawy R.; Toraih E.; Elshazli R.
Article.Abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP9) plays an important role in extracellular matrix remodeling and has been implicated in tumor invasion and metastasis in several cancers, including breast cancer (BC). This study aims to elucidate the genetic factors influencing breast cancer risk by analyzing the role of MMP9 (rs17576 and rs3787268) variants in cancer susceptibility. We employed a holistic methodology that integrates genetic analysis with sophisticated bioinformatics techniques to elucidate their potential influence on the progression of breast carcinoma using multi-platform functional evidence. A case–control study was conducted including 120 breast cancer patients and 120 age-matched healthy controls. Genotyping of rs17576 and rs3787268 was performed using TaqMan allelic discrimination assays. Logistic regression models were applied to evaluate genotype, allele, and haplotype associations with breast cancer susceptibility. Complementary bioinformatic analyses (GEPIA2, GTEx, TNMplot, muTarget, STRING, I-Mutant, and 3DSNP) were performed to investigate gene expression patterns, eQTL effects, protein stability, and potential molecular interactions. The missense variant MMP9*rs17576 showed a significant association with breast cancer susceptibility under several genetic models (A/G: OR = 2.31, 95% CI = 1.24–4.29, p = 0.007; and G/G: OR = 2.46, 95% CI = 1.16–5.22, p = 0.017). The G allele frequency was higher in patients than in controls (52.5% vs. 41.2%; OR = 1.57, 95% CI = 1.10–2.26, p = 0.013). In contrast, the intronic variant MMP9*rs3787268 showed no independent association with breast cancer susceptibility. Bioinformatic analyses suggested that rs17576 may influence MMP9 function and regulation, including predicted protein destabilization (ΔΔG = − 0.34 kcal/mol), breast-tissue eQTL effects, and potential involvement in tumor-related molecular pathways. Expression analyses also indicated increased MMP9 expression in breast cancer tissues and association with disease progression. These findings suggest that the MMP9*rs17576 variant may contribute to breast cancer susceptibility in Egyptian women, whereas MMP9*rs3787268 showed no independent association. Given the single-population design, these results should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, ethnically diverse cohorts together with functional investigations.

Article.Title: Seasonal decoupling of local climate zone thermal responses in three cold-climate cities of Northeast China
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Dong Y.; Tai H.; Ma X.; Wang Q.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Urban thermal environments are strongly influenced by urban morphology and land cover, yet the seasonal stability of Local Climate Zone (LCZ)–land surface temperature (LST) relationships in cold-climate cities remains insufficiently understood. In regions with long winters and seasonal snow cover, LCZ-specific surface thermal responses may differ substantially from those observed in temperate cities. This study investigates seasonal thermal responses across LCZ types in three major cold-climate cities in Northeast China—Shenyang, Harbin, and Changchun. LST was retrieved from Landsat 8 imagery on the Google Earth Engine platform, and LCZ maps were produced following the World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT) framework. Seasonal differences in LCZ thermal responses were examined through intra- and inter-city comparisons of mean LST, LCZ-referenced LST contrasts, and mixed-effects model estimates. To further isolate structural thermal effects from background climatic variability, a linear mixed-effects model was applied with LCZ type, season, and their interaction as fixed effects and city as a random effect. Auxiliary snow-cover and solar-radiation indicators were also incorporated to support the interpretation of seasonal mechanisms. The results show that summer LST patterns are strongly controlled by urban morphology and surface radiative properties. Compact built-up zones (LCZ 1–3), industrial or large impervious areas, and exposed hard surfaces exhibit pronounced warming effects, with Changchun showing the highest mean summer LST among the three cities. In winter, inter-LCZ thermal contrasts become substantially weaker, and low-vegetation, open, or exposed surfaces tend to show stronger cooling under snow-covered and low-radiation conditions. Shenyang maintains the warmest winter condition, whereas Harbin exhibits the strongest winter cold background. The mixed-effects model reveals a significant LCZ × season interaction, indicating a seasonal shift in the mechanisms controlling urban surface temperature. Summer thermal patterns are primarily governed by radiative absorption and urban surface structure, whereas winter thermal dynamics are jointly modulated by snow cover, reduced solar radiation, and heating-season urban energy processes. These findings demonstrate that LCZ–LST relationships in cold-climate cities exhibit pronounced seasonal variability and should not be directly generalized from studies conducted in warmer regions. The results provide a scientific basis for seasonally differentiated, LCZ-specific climate adaptation and thermal environment management in high-latitude cities.

Article.Title: Assessing pertussis control strategies: a mathematical modeling approach incorporating vaccination and asymptomatic infection
Article.Authors: Raza A.; Ali K.; Jeeva N.; Mensah K.; Acheneje G.; Abbas M.; Jawo E.
Article.Abstract: Pertussis is a highly contagious respiratory disease caused by Bordetella pertussis , which continues to pose a significant public health challenge worldwide. In this study, we develop a deterministic model for pertussis transmission comprising six compartments: susceptible, vaccinated, exposed, symptomatic infectious, asymptomatic infectious, and recovered individuals ( SVEIAR ). Using the next-generation matrix method, we derive the basic reproduction number \(\mathcal {R}_0\) of the model without vaccination and the vaccination-adjusted reproduction number \(\mathcal {R}_v\) at the vaccinated disease-free equilibrium. The disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if and only if \(\mathcal {R}_v<1\) and globally asymptotically stable if \(\mathcal {R}_0<1\) ; a unique endemic equilibrium exists whenever \(\mathcal {R}_v>1\) , and an exact quadratic criterion shows that the bifurcation at \(\mathcal {R}_v=1\) is forward for all parameter values sampled from the literature ranges, although an imperfect vaccine can produce backward bifurcation outside them. Local stability of the endemic equilibrium is established near the threshold (at the baseline values of the other parameters) by centre-manifold analysis and verified numerically away from it. Sensitivity analysis revealed that vaccination, recovery rates, asymptomatic infectiousness, and the proportion of asymptomatic infections were the primary drivers of \(\mathcal {R}_v\) . The transmission rate and a reporting fraction were calibrated to eleven annual counts of reported US cases (CDC, 2014–2024). These parameters are not identifiable from the data: the objective has several local minima, the reported baseline ( \(\mathcal {R}_v=0.80\) ) is a local optimum, and parameter sets with \(\mathcal {R}_v>1\) fit at least as well. The calibrated model does not reproduce the 2017–2019 plateau or the 2023–2024 resurgence ( \(R^2<0\) ) and is used here as a reference scenario, not for forecasting. Furthermore, the uncontrolled SVEIAR model is extended into an optimal control framework by incorporating four time-dependent intervention strategies, with explicitly stated, assumed cost weights, control bounds and horizon. Under these assumptions, strategies that include transmission reduction gave the lowest objective values, and this ranking was unchanged when each weight was halved or doubled; the size of the benefits, however, depended mainly on the assumed control bounds and on the calibration scenario. These rankings are model-based findings under stated assumptions, not predictions of real-world intervention effectiveness. By integrating imperfect vaccination, breakthrough infections, asymptomatic transmission, and temporary immunity, the model offers a framework for exploring the persistence of pertussis in highly vaccinated populations; age structure, seasonality, stochasticity, richer surveillance data and economic evaluation are needed before the results can inform policy.

Article.Title: Cardiovascular complications and cardiovascular death are rare in severe COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury or failure
Article.Authors: O’Brien C.; Gunturkun F.; Deng Y.; Ruaysungnoen R.; Chang D.; Khanijo S.; Barnett C.; Kapil S.; Daly A.; Goffi A.; Stavi D.; Carrier F.; Ennehas Y.; Fiza B.; Patterson A.; Daubert T.; Moll V.; Castellucci C.; Zekhtser M.; Burgara N.; Mayette M.; Courchesne K.; Thompson S.; Parikh R.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SARS-COV2 infection has been linked to cardiovascular complications. Published data suggest that cardiac injury may be a common disease feature and contribute to morbidity and mortality in severe COVID-19. Since early in the pandemic, little data has emerged describing what cardiovascular complications arise from myocardial injury in severe COVID-19 and whether these complications contribute to mortality. We set out to describe the incidence and nature of cardiovascular complications in patients with severe COVID-19 infection and biochemical or imaging evidence of myocardial injury. We analyzed consecutive patients admitted for severe COVID-19 and presenting with biochemical or echocardiographic evidence of myocardial injury across 16 centers within the CARDIO-COVID investigator-initiated consortium. A light-GBM machine learning model was used to identify variables associated with mortality. Our study included 1,328 patients. ICU mortality was 29.4%. Factors most associated with mortality were age, SOFA Cardiovascular score, elevated troponin, intubation, high vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), high PEEP, and high FiO2. Individual cardiovascular (myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, VT/VF, new onset heart failure) complications were rare (all < 5%) but common in sum (17.6%), and did not present significant association with mortality. Patients with high VIS and SOFA Cardiovascular scores had a significantly higher incidence of secondary bacterial pneumonias suggesting septic shock played a role in their physiology. Investigator-adjudicated cause of death data identified respiratory failure and septic shock as primary causes of mortality. Though cardiovascular complications of severe COVID-19 are common, they do not seem to contribute significantly to mortality. Elevated cardiac enzymes and myocardial dysfunction carry prognostic value likely reflecting myocardial strain in the setting of multisystem organ dysfunction rather than direct myocardial injury by SARS-CoV2.

Article.Title: Human adipose derived mesenchymal stem cell extracellular vesicles ameliorate ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 expression in premature ovarian insufficiency mice
Article.Authors: Arjmand F.; Mirsanei J.; Mehdizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a major cause of infertility and long-term health complications in young women and can result from gonadotoxic chemotherapy. Current management alleviates symptoms but does not restore ovarian reserve. Human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (hAD-MSC-EVs) have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical POI models. Human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAD-MSCs) were expanded and characterized by morphology and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) were isolated from conditioned medium by sequential centrifugation and ultracentrifugation and characterized using dynamic light scattering, transmission electron microscopy, the Bradford assay, and Western blotting for CD63, TSG101, and calnexin. POI was induced in mice using cyclophosphamide and busulfan. Animals received hAD-MSC-EVs via tail vein injection. Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and estradiol (E2) levels were measured, and ovarian histology was evaluated using hematoxylin and eosin staining. Ovarian messenger RNA (mRNA) levels of Bmp15 , Gdf9 , Foxo3 , and Mapk3 , encoding bone morphogenetic protein 15 (BMP15), growth differentiation factor 9 (GDF9), forkhead box O3, and mitogen-activated protein kinase 3, respectively, were quantified, together with ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 protein levels. EV treatment partially ameliorated POI-associated endocrine alterations, reducing FSH and increasing LH and E2 levels compared with untreated POI mice. Histological analysis showed improved ovarian architecture and reduced stromal abnormalities. Ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 protein levels were higher in EV-treated mice than in untreated POI mice and did not differ significantly from control levels. However, Bmp15 and Gdf9 mRNA levels increased only modestly and remained below control levels, whereas Foxo3 and Mapk3 mRNA levels did not differ significantly among groups. hAD-MSC-EV treatment was associated with partial endocrine and histological improvement and increased ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 protein levels in mice with chemotherapy-induced POI. These findings support further investigation of hAD-MSC-EVs as a potential approach to ovarian recovery, while the mechanisms underlying these associations remain to be established.

Article.Title: Optimization of asymmetric conical flow channels for efficient yarn conveying via numerical method
Article.Authors: Liu T.; Huang Q.; Lu B.; Zhou L.; Li X.; Yan Y.
Article.Abstract: During pneumatic yarn conveying process through an asymmetric conical channel, the channel structural parameters have a significant effect on conveying performance. To balance the computational accuracy and efficiency, an efficient two-way fluid-structure interaction method is employed to establish a dynamic model of the yarn in airflow. Weakly coupled simulations are performed through two-way projection to efficiently capture the interaction between the airflow and yarn motion. The effects of the cone angle, connection tube diameter, and connection tube length on yarn conveying performance are investigated through single-factor and multi-parameter analyses. The results show that the yarn velocity first increases and then decreases with increasing cone angle and connection tube length, whereas increasing the connection tube diameter enhances yarn conveying efficiency. The deviation between the experimental and simulation results is less than 5%, and the optimized structure improves yarn conveying velocity by 35% compared with the original structure. The optimized structure provides a useful reference for the structural optimization of pneumatic yarn conveying devices.

Article.Title: Lifelong vehicle re-identification via ResNet50 with depthwise spatial attention
Article.Authors: Rong L.; Han L.; Bai L.
Article.Abstract: The core task of vehicle re-identification is to recognize vehicles with the same identity across different scenes. Existing methods, relying on fixed-dataset training, struggle to cope with continuously updating multi-domain vehicle data in real-world scenarios, and thus suffer significant performance degradation under data distribution shifts. While lifelong learning techniques can gradually accumulate multi-domain knowledge, they suffer from catastrophic forgetting of historical discriminative features and adapt inefficiently to new domains, particularly in preserving cross-domain spatial cues (e.g., component structure, contour details). To address this, this paper proposes a lifelong vehicle ReID model based on ResNet50, which embeds the depthwise spatial attention module. By leveraging depthwise separable convolution to dynamically focus on cross-domain invariant spatial regions such as the grille, headlights and vehicle contours, the model enhances local discriminative features to mitigate feature drift. The model couples two mechanisms: the depthwise spatial attention module preserves historical discriminative spatial features and curbs catastrophic forgetting, while the feature alignment loss maintains consistent multi-domain representations and balances old and new knowledge. Extensive experiments on VeRi-776, VRIC, and VehicleID show that, among the lifelong methods compared under a common protocol, the proposed method attains the highest accuracy—77.0% mAP and 78.7% R1 on average—while storing no historical images and requiring the lowest peak training memory of 7.2 GB.

Article.Title: Time-series field phenotyping and GWAS reveal QTL underlying yield potential in Amaranthus tricolor
Article.Authors: Hung C.; Ezura K.; Lin C.; Schafleitner R.; Hoshikawa K.; Lin Y.
Article.Abstract: Amaranthus tricolor is a climate-resilient, nutrient-rich crop, but its genetic improvement is hindered by a lack of systematic phenotypic and yield trait data. In this study, 362 genetically diverse accessions were evaluated over two seasons under field conditions using a high-throughput phenotyping platform equipped with the PlantEye F500 multispectral sensor, enabling daily, non-invasive 3D imaging of plant development. Scanner-derived plant height, leaf area, digital biomass, and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were quantified throughout growth. Two accessions, VI056855A and VI047897, consistently exhibited superior performance and are potential breeding materials. A genome-wide association study (GWAS) revealed 52 significant SNPs for yield-related traits and 6 for NDVI. ATR1.0CH10_6710679 (yield-related traits) and ATR1.0CH06_11239836 (NDVI) were each detected in both seasons. Accessions carrying the high-NDVI allele of ATR1.0CH06_11239836 exhibited both high- and low-yield performance, suggesting that variation in leaf pigmentation may complicate the interpretation of NDVI as an indicator of plant performance in A. tricolor . By integrating high-throughput phenotyping with GWAS, this study provides a foundation for dissecting the genetic basis of yield-related traits in A. tricolor and a framework that may be applicable to other underutilized crops.

Article.Title: Environmental threat classification from mel-spectrograms using an augmented 2D CNN with sub-second CPU inference
Article.Authors: Bhargav Teja P.; Sree Chathurya L.; Ragavan K.
Article.Abstract: Illegal logging threatens biodiversity, carbon storage and ecological stability, yet ranger patrols and camera networks are costly, spatially limited and rarely provide timely alerts. This paper presents ForestEar, a proof-of-concept framework that classifies 2-second audio clips as Safe, Illegal Activity or Environmental Risk using a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) applied to log-mel spectrograms. In the absence of a labelled forest-threat corpus, classes from the public ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K datasets were remapped as proxy labels, and stochastic augmentation was applied to minority classes. On a held-out test partition, a binary Safe-versus-Illegal-Activity evaluation ( n = 338) reached 92.9% accuracy, with recall of 0.95 (Safe) and 0.90 (Illegal Activity). A three-class configuration that adds the Environmental Risk class is demonstrated in a preliminary evaluation, which identified Environmental Risk as the most difficult class. Per-clip inference took approximately 250 ms on a laptop CPU. Because the results derive from proxy benchmark data, a single data split that was not grouped by source recording, and single training runs, they demonstrate feasibility under benchmark conditions rather than field performance. Validation on forest recordings and on embedded hardware remains future work.

Article.Title: Hybrid MPC for dual three-phase PMSMs under open-phase and short-circuit faults
Article.Authors: Rahmani-Fard J.; Mohammed M.; Ridha A.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a unified, constraint-preserving polynomial hybrid model predictive control (MPC) strategy for dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors (DT-PMSMs) under open-phase faults (OPFs) and short-circuit faults (SCFs). For OPFs, a cubic polynomial mixing coefficient approximates the full-range minimum-loss (FRML) optimal solution, guaranteeing rated current limits. For SCFs, a two-stage Lagrange-based compensation cancels the short-circuit magnetomotive force (MMF) and applies the open-phase hybrid strategy. Both fault modes are integrated into a finite control set MPC (FCS-MPC) framework with 12 virtual voltage vectors (VVs) that produce zero harmonic voltage. Experimental validation on a DT-PMSM prototype shows that under healthy conditions the currents are sinusoidal and balanced. Under an uncompensated OPF, the currents become severely distorted and unbalanced (peak > 1.75 p.u.). The proposed OPF controller restores sinusoidal balanced currents within the rated limit (1 p.u.) and suppresses harmonic currents, as seen from the z 1 z 2 trajectories collapsing to a small cluster near the origin. Under an SCF, the controller maintains sinusoidal αβ currents matching the torque reference (0.5 p.u.) while keeping the non-sinusoidal phase currents within the rated limit. Dynamic tests show that under OPF, a load torque step of 6 Nm causes a speed drop of < 6% with recovery in 150 ms and a torque overshoot of 7%; a speed step from 500 to 700 r/min has a rise time of 70 ms with negligible overshoot. The algorithm runs in 80 µs on a TMS320F28335 DSP, confirming real-time feasibility.

Article.Title: Reproducible laboratory evaluation of speaker independent speech command recognition with an artificial neural network for humanoid robot control
Article.Authors: Shrivastava S.; Banerjee S.; Srivastava M.; Khalid S.; Nishad D.
Article.Abstract: Voice-controlled humanoid robots can take over hazardous tasks in defence and field scenarios where direct human intervention is risky. Most reported prototypes couple an Android front end to an Arduino through Bluetooth, which restricts on-board signal processing, obscures end-to-end timing, and is seldom evaluated under speaker-independent conditions. This work reports the design, implementation and evaluation of an artificial neural network based speech-command recognition system that controls a humanoid robot prototype from within a single integrated development environment. A custom corpus of 5,000 utterances covering five motion commands was recorded from ten speakers (five male, five female) at 16 kHz under controlled laboratory conditions with a signal-to-noise ratio of at least 30 dB. A six-stage cleaning pipeline retained 4,728 utterances. Two speakers, one male and one female, were held out in full before any frame-level processing; the remaining eight speakers formed a development pool of 3,771 utterances that was further divided by speaker into six training and two validation speakers. Fourteen Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were extracted from every 25 ms frame with a 10 ms hop and mean-pooled over the voiced frames of an utterance, yielding one 14-dimensional vector per utterance. A 14-50-5 feedforward network with rectified linear hidden units and a softmax output was trained with MATLAB scaled conjugate gradient backpropagation (trainscg) using speaker-defined index partitioning and validation-based early stopping. On a class-balanced speaker-independent test set of 750 utterances (150 per command) the network classified 651 utterances correctly, an overall accuracy of 86.8% with a 95% Wilson confidence interval of 0.842 to 0.890 and macro-averaged precision, recall and F1 score of 0.87. Per-command recall ranged from 84.0% for turn right to 91.3% for stop, the directional pair being hardest to separate because of a shared phonetic prefix. The classifier holds 1,005 parameters and needs about 2.0 kFLOP per utterance, some 33 and 53 times fewer parameters than the one-dimensional convolutional and long short-term memory baselines evaluated here. Command latency, measured from end-of-speech detection to actuator acknowledgement, averaged 149.7 ms with a standard deviation of 3.9 ms. The same feature extraction and classifier framework, with cleaning thresholds adapted to that corpus, was additionally applied to the public Google Speech Commands v0.02 corpus, with the released words forward, backward, right, left and stop standing in for the five commands and with the release’s own speaker-disjoint partition; on a class-balanced test set of the same size it reached 67.5% (95% Wilson interval 0.640 to 0.707) against 95.2% for the convolutional baseline, which indicates that the accuracy reported above is specific to this corpus and suggests that the loss of temporal information caused by utterance-level mean pooling may be an important limitation when the distinguishing material is short, although the present experiments do not isolate it as the sole cause. The contribution is a transparent, reproducible, speaker-independent laboratory baseline for small-vocabulary humanoid robot voice control; it is not evidence of readiness for operational deployment, which would require validation under realistic acoustic and mission conditions.

Article.Title: Clinical significance of recurrently mutated genes in VHL wild-type clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Liu P.; Glennon K.; Najmabadi A.; Vasudev N.; Tanguay S.; Riazalhosseini Y.
Article.Abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the most common subtype of kidney cancer, is characterized by its genomic heterogeneity and high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy. While the majority of ccRCC tumors harbor somatic mutations in VHL tumor suppressor gene (VHLmut), approximately 20–25% lack VHL mutations (VHLwt), and may exhibit different progression patterns. VHLwt tumors remain significantly underrepresented in genomic studies. Our objective was to compare prognostic significance of somatic mutations in ccRCC-associated genes between patients with VHLmut and VHLwt tumors. We analyzed genomic and clinical data of 914 ccRCC patients (720 VHLmut and 194 VHLwt) from the Cancer Genomics of the Kidney (CAGEKID) cohort. Prognostic impacts of individual and co-occurring mutations in 12 RCC-related genes as well as chromosomal copy number variations (CNVs), associated with survival, were evaluated in VHLmut and VHLwt groups through survival analyses. Findings were compared between the two groups. Prognostic significance of somatic mutations in BAP1, SETD2 and PBRM1, is dependent on VHL mutational status. Co-occurring mutations in PBRM1 and SETD2 were significantly associated with poorer clinical outcomes in VHLmut tumors, but not in VHLwt tumors. TP53 mutations were associated with poorer survival in VHLwt tumors. The differing prognostic effects of somatic mutations by VHL status suggest distinct underlying mechanisms of disease progression in VHLwt ccRCCs, highlighting the need to consider VHLwt separately from VHLmut tumors in prognostic and predictive models. Further investigations of these observations in independent cohorts are warranted.

Article.Title: Antitumor activity and immune-related gene expression changes following recombinant Mycobacterium smegmatis treatment in a mouse model of bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Song D.; Park J.; Choi G.; Kim B.; Han H.; Choi Y.
Article.Abstract: Bladder cancer requires additional therapeutic strategies because of frequent recurrence and progression risk. We evaluated recombinant Mycobacterium smegmatis expressing a human macrophage migration inhibitory factor–interleukin-7 fusion protein (rSmeg-hMIF-hIL-7) in a syngeneic subcutaneous MBT-2 bladder cancer model. Among mice that developed measurable tumors, intraperitoneally treated mice showed reduced tumor growth and longer endpoint-free survival, defined as time to death or humane-endpoint euthanasia. RNA sequencing of four control and three treated tumors identified 116 differentially expressed genes at a fold-change magnitude ≥ 2 and false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05. Enrichment analyses highlighted immune-related transcriptional differences, although tissue-collection timing and tumor burden limited their attribution to treatment. Cross-species expression comparison identified five exploratory candidates: CCL15, CCRL2, ST3GAL5, SIGLEC6, and TMEM255A. Four showed FDR-significant survival associations in exploratory unadjusted Cox analyses within the same TCGA-BLCA cohort. Expression patterns concordant with those in treated mouse tumors were also associated with papillary histology. RT-qPCR using the same biological samples supported increased Ccl6 and St3gal5 expression after multiple-testing correction. These findings support the antitumor potential of rSmeg-hMIF-hIL-7 and provide exploratory links between murine tumor transcriptional differences and human bladder cancer characteristics.

Article.Title: Integrated core-based calibration of the lower Bahariya reservoir in the Shahd and Shahd SE fields, Western Desert, Egypt
Article.Authors: Arafa F.; Hafeez T.; Fathy M.; Ayyad H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable petrophysical evaluation is essential for reservoir characterization and hydrocarbon resource assessment, particularly in heterogeneous sandstone reservoirs where uncertainties in log interpretation, core measurements, and reservoir cutoffs can affect reservoir-property estimates. This study presents an Integrated Core-Based Calibration (ICC) Workflow for the Lower Bahariya reservoir in the Shahd and Shahd SE fields, Western Desert, Egypt. The workflow integrates conventional wireline logs, routine core analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), thin-section petrography, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and reservoir-engineering data through a structured sequential framework comprising wireline-log quality control and normalization, core–log depth matching and overburden correction, core-based petrophysical calibration, geological validation and reservoir-quality rock typing, integrated reservoir characterization, and independent reservoir validation. The calibration established a consistent basis for estimating clay volume, effective porosity, and water saturation from calibrated wireline responses. Integrated reservoir characterization identified 32.0 ft of net pay in Shahd-1, with an average effective porosity of 14.3% and average water saturation of 25.4%, compared with 194.5 ft of net pay in Shahd SE-5, with an average effective porosity of 21.4% and average water saturation of 9.7%. Independent well-scale and reservoir-scale validation using Shahd SE-63 and XPT pressure-gradient data provided supporting evidence for hydraulic differentiation between the interpreted Lower Bahariya intervals and distinct oil–water contact depths. The proposed workflow provides a structured sequential framework for integrating multi-scale geological and petrophysical information and progressively constraining interpretation uncertainty in heterogeneous sandstone reservoir characterization.

Article.Title: Factors associated with unmet patient care, sexual health, and health system needs among cancer patients at an oncology center in Southern Ethiopia, 2024
Article.Authors: Debebe A.; Amenu A.; Jemebere W.; Borie Y.; Bore M.
Article.Abstract: Unmet health care needs refer to the gap between patients perceived need for services and the care they receive. These needs may occur during the course of cancer diagnosis and treatment and can cause psychological distress, ineffective coping, and reduced quality of life. Evidence on patient care/support, sexuality, and health system needs among cancer patients in Ethiopia is limited. To assess the prevalence and factors associated with unmet patient care/support, sexuality, and health system needs among cancer patients at the Oncology Center of Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Hawassa, Ethiopia, in 2024. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 321 cancer patients selected via simple random sampling. Data were collected using an interviewer-administered structured questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS 26. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with unmet needs; p < 0.05 was considered significant. Of 311 participants (response rate 96.9%), the mean age was 45.16 years. Unmet needs were highest in the health system and information domain (72.3%), followed by patient care/support (43.4%) and sexuality (27.7%). Low Income (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR] = 5.96; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 2.29–14.13) and middle income (AOR = 4.64; 95% CI: 1.48–14.50) predicted unmet health system needs. Co-existing illness was associated with unmet patient care/support needs (AOR = 1.87; 95% CI: 1.09–3.52), and time since diagnosis predicted unmet sexuality needs (AOR = 1.05; 95% CI: 1.01–1.11). Unmet supportive care needs are high, particularly in the health system and information domain. Interventions addressing income, co-existing illnesses, and disease duration are recommended to improve supportive care and patient quality of life.

Article.Title: Optimization of ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction of volatile oil from Gardenia jasminoides flowers and evaluation of antioxidant activity
Article.Authors: Pei W.; Xu L.; Yang F.; Wang Z.; Ma Y.; Hou M.; Feng X.
Article.Abstract: This study developed and optimized an integrated enzymatic pretreatment and ultrasound-assisted extraction (EPUAE) process for volatile oil recovery from Gardenia jasminoides flowers. Pectinase was selected over cellulase through enzyme-type screening. Flower powder underwent enzymatic hydrolysis, enzyme inactivation, and ultrasonic treatment prior to steam distillation. Using Box-Behnkel response surface methodology, hydrolysis temperature, pH, and ultrasound time were optimized at 55 °C, pH 4.6, and 29 min, respectively. The optimized process yielded 0.85% ± 0.03%, representing a significant improvement over steam distillation (0.52%), ultrasound-assisted steam distillation (0.68%), and enzymatic extraction alone (0.63%). The volatile oil demonstrated concentration-dependent radical scavenging activity, with IC 50 values of 0.44 mg/mL for DPPH and 0.50 mg/mL for ABTS• + . These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of the combined EPUAE approach and provide preliminary evidence for the oil’s antioxidant potential. This study provides experimental evidence and technical support for the efficient preparation and application of volatile oil from Gardenia jasminoides flowers.

Article.Title: Context-aware tooth instance segmentation and missing-tooth localization in panoramic radiographs
Article.Authors: Bajpai S.; Shafiq H.; Lee B.
Article.Abstract: Reliable localization and segmentation of individual teeth are fundamental for automated dental diagnostics and computer-aided treatment planning. However, panoramic radiographs pose persistent challenges due to anatomical variability, overlapping structures, and inconsistent image quality, thereby keeping clinical workflows heavily dependent on manual interpretation. This study introduces DentAll, a framework that integrates tooth instance segmentation with contextual estimation of anatomically expected missing-tooth locations. The proposed segmentation with Contextual Spatial Attention Blocks (S-CSAB) integrates dilated convolutions and ROI-based positional encoding to enhance fine-grained boundary delineation while maintaining anatomical coherence across adjacent teeth. Building upon these contextual features, the Missing-Tooth Localization Predictor (MTLP) estimates missing-tooth locations via patient-conditioned coordinate regression, using the target tooth’s identity together with the geometry of its nearest same-arch neighboring teeth, without requiring explicit missing-tooth annotations. DentAll was evaluated on 1,325 panoramic radiographs using instance-level segmentation metrics, COCO-style mask average precision, comparative baselines, and controlled pseudo-missing localization experiments. Under an all-ground-truth evaluation protocol, the framework achieved a DSC of 88.21% (92.74% among successfully matched instances), AP50 of 97.34%, AP75 of 87.20%, and mAP50:95 of 68.58%, while contextual MTLP localization improved the IoU ≥ 0.5 rate from 25.20% (index-only formulation) to 72.58%. These findings demonstrate that integrating instance segmentation with patient-specific anatomical context provides an effective and computationally practical framework for structured analysis of panoramic dental radiographs under anatomical variability.

Article.Title: Hybrid app-based motivational interviewing to prevent excessive gestational weight gain and improve health-promoting lifestyle: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Mohammadi S.; Nasiri-Amiri F.; Adib-Rad H.; Faramarzi M.; Nikbakht H.; Omidvar S.; Ghanbarpour A.
Article.Abstract: Excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) is a major risk factor for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Identifying effective interventions to prevent excessive weight gain while promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors and psychological well-being during pregnancy is essential. This study evaluated the effects of hybrid app-based motivational interviewing on preventing EGWG, improving health-promoting lifestyle behaviors, and enhancing psychological health among pregnant women. This randomized controlled trial was conducted from August 2024 to May 2025 among 188 pregnant women at less than 14 weeks of gestation attending prenatal clinics in Babol, Iran. Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention or control group using block randomization ( n = 94 per group). Follow-up was completed by 88 participants in the intervention group and 83 in the control group. The primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle, with missing data handled using multiple imputation. The intervention consisted of six individual motivational interviewing-based counseling sessions over six consecutive weeks (weeks 15–20 of gestation). Sessions 1, 3, and 5 were conducted in person, whereas sessions 2, 4, and 6 were delivered remotely via a mobile application. Psychoeducational materials were provided through the application following each remote session. The control group received routine prenatal care. Maternal weight was measured at baseline, 28 weeks of gestation, and before delivery. Excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) was defined according to the 2009 Institute of Medicine guidelines. The Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP-II) and the 28-item General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-28) were administered at baseline, 28 weeks of gestation, and six weeks postpartum. Independent-samples t-tests were used for unadjusted between-group comparisons, repeated-measures ANOVA for within-group comparisons over time, and ANCOVA for adjusted between-group comparisons. By delivery, excessive weight gain was lower in the intervention group (23.4%) than in the control group (40.4%) ( P = 0.039). Mean weight gain was 2.06 kg lower at week 28 (95% CI: −2.75 to − 1.37, P < 0.001) and 1.56 kg lower at delivery (95% CI: −2.30 to − 0.82, P < 0.001) in the intervention group. For HPLP-II, a marginally statistically significant between-group difference was observed at baseline ( P = 0.049), with higher scores in the intervention group. The intervention group had significantly higher scores at week 28 (127.38 ± 19.43 vs. 107.00 ± 11.52, P < 0.001) and six weeks postpartum (128.78 ± 16.98 vs. 100.31 ± 10.16, P < 0.001). For GHQ, there was no baseline difference ( P = 0.308), but the intervention group had lower scores at week 28 (16.44 ± 3.11 vs. 21.55 ± 4.10, P < 0.001) and six weeks postpartum (17.99 ± 3.47 vs. 22.88 ± 3.59, P < 0.001), indicating better general health. The hybrid app-based motivational interviewing intervention was associated with a lower incidence of excessive gestational weight gain (23.4% vs. 40.4%; absolute risk reduction, 17.0% points) and a lower gestational weight gain at delivery (between-group difference, − 1.56 kg; 95% CI: −2.30 to − 0.82), as well as improved HPLP-II and GHQ-28 scores compared with routine prenatal care. The intervention may be considered for routine prenatal care, pending further evaluation of its cost-effectiveness and implementation feasibility. Trial registration The trial was prospectively registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20200122046228N6) on 21 April 2024, before participant enrollment began.

Article.Title: Integrating geometry-aware radial-angular perturbation and topology-aware contrastive learning for heterogeneous graphs
Article.Authors: Sun M.; Luo X.; Hu M.; Huang E.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: Heterogeneous information networks (HINs) model multiple node types and semantic relations, but existing heterogeneous graph contrastive learning methods still face two limitations. Random perturbations may disturb fragile cross-type structures, and local message-passing encoders may be limited in capturing long-range dependencies and broader structural cues. To address these limitations, we propose Geometry-aware radial-angular perturbation and Topology-aware contrastive learning (Geo-Top), a heterogeneous graph contrastive learning framework that combines topology-aware encoding with geometry-aware radial-angular latent perturbation. Geo-Top uses an SVD-inspired learnable low-rank topology factorization to model meta-path-induced adjacency relations and injects the resulting structural factors into attention computation through gradient decoupling. This design enables topology-aware attention to couple local semantics with non-local structural cues. Geo-Top further introduces radial-angular perturbations in the latent tangent representation to generate structured augmented samples. Together with shallow feature masking, cross-view contrastive learning, and momentum target encoders, these modules support semantic-view consistency and topology-aware representation learning. Experiments on five public heterogeneous graph datasets show strong node-classification performance. Geo-Top leads the reported clustering metrics on DBLP, AMiner, and Freebase, while the results on ACM and IMDb show that clustering benefits depend on the dataset. Component ablations characterize the contributions of topology-aware encoding and latent augmentation across classification and clustering.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: heterogeneous graphs; node classification; cross-view contrastive learning; graph contrastive learning; data augmentation; graph clustering

Article.Title: Lon protease modulates bacterial morphology, stress tolerance, and virulence in Riemerella anatipestifer
Article.Authors: Liang C.; Tang F.; Ding X.; Lu C.; Cheng L.; Cai X.; Zheng C.; Ouyang Z.; Liu W.; Chen R.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Riemerella anatipestifer ( R. anatipestifer ) is an important avian pathogen that causes severe economic losses in the poultry industry, yet its molecular pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Lon protease has been reported to regulate virulence in several bacterial pathogens, but its role in R. anatipestifer has not yet been defined. In this study, a R. anatipestifer lon deletion mutant was constructed by natural transformation and homologous recombination to investigate the role of lon . Phenotypic analyses showed that deletion of lon did not affect bacterial growth but resulted in a shorter cell length and reduced tolerance to heat, acidic, and oxidative stresses. Adhesion and invasion assays using RAW264.7 murine macrophages revealed that the lon mutant exhibited significantly reduced adhesion and invasion abilities compared with the parental strain. In vivo infection experiments further demonstrated attenuated virulence of the mutant, with an LD 50 approximately 50-fold higher than that of the parental strain and less severe pathological lesions in ducklings. RNA-seq analysis identified 54 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the lon mutant, including 29 upregulated and 25 downregulated genes. These DEGs were mainly enriched in metabolic pathways, including nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism, pyrimidine metabolism, ribosome-related pathways, and microbial metabolism in diverse environments. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that lon contributes to the stress tolerance and virulence of R. anatipestifer and provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying its pathogenicity.
