Article.Title: Passivity-aware reactive diffusion policy for stable contact-rich manipulation
Article.Authors: Yang H.; Yu J.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Contact-rich manipulation demands stable, low-impact interaction with uncertain environments. Reactive diffusion policies (RDP) achieve strong task success, yet their high-frequency corrective actions can inject energy into the contact, producing large contact forces and instability under disturbance. We propose PaRDP (Passivity-Aware Reactive Diffusion Policy), which augments a slow-fast visual-tactile diffusion base with three lightweight, provably passivity-bounded modules: (i) a Passivity-aware Interaction Frame & Hybrid Force-Position (PIF-HFP) module that selects free-motion degrees of freedom in an estimated interaction frame; (ii) a Passivity-Bounded Fast Force Correction (PB-FFC) shell that projects out energy-increasing corrections through an energy tank with a bounded injection allowance; and (iii) Stability-Conditioned Training (SCT), a training-time regularizer that penalizes net energy injection. We prove that the closed-loop system remains stable whenever the environment is passive. On RDP/TactAR, our primary benchmark, PaRDP improves the All score by $$+0.02$$ to $$+0.05$$ over RDP(Force) and reduces peak contact force by up to $$34\%$$ while adding under $$7\%$$ inference overhead; we additionally list published ForceVLA-Data and RH20T baselines as external reference context for force-aware and cross-dataset settings. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm the contribution of each module.

Article.Title: Protective effects of molsidomine on oxidative stress, inflammation, and VEGF/P-selectin expression in CLP-induced sepsis
Article.Authors: Kose A.; Ozhan O.; Gul M.; Kurucay E.; Dogru F.; Yasar S.; Keser Z.; Balkar M.; Ulutas Z.; Parlakpinar H.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, inflammation, and vascular activation. We investigated whether molsidomine pretreatment modifies hepatic injury in rats subjected to cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Forty male Wistar rats were randomized to sham surgery, molsidomine alone, CLP, or molsidomine plus CLP. Molsidomine (10 mg/kg/day) was administered orally for 14 days before surgery. Four rats in each septic group died before the 24-hour assessment, leaving eight survivors per group. Liver histology, vascular endothelial growth factor and P-selectin immunoreactivity, tissue redox and inflammatory markers, and serum hepatic indices were evaluated. Compared with CLP alone, pretreatment was associated with lower median hepatic damage scores (2 versus 5), lower vascular endothelial growth factor and P-selectin immunoreactivity, higher hepatic reduced glutathione and total antioxidant status, and lower hepatic tumor necrosis factor-α. Other measured hepatic redox indices did not differ significantly between septic groups. Serum albumin, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, and lactate dehydrogenase did not differ significantly, whereas total bilirubin was higher with pretreatment. In this shared experimental cohort, prophylactic molsidomine was associated with reduced structural injury and selective tissue biochemical changes. These exploratory findings do not demonstrate improved hepatic function, a causal vascular mechanism, or clinical efficacy when treatment begins after sepsis onset.

Article.Title: Neuronal cell line expressing full-length mutant huntingtin displays alteration of proteasome activity
Article.Authors: Gotmanova N.; Bobik T.; Ezhov A.; Valyaeva A.; Zvereva M.; Rubtsova M.; Bacheva A.
Article.Abstract: Polyglutamine diseases are incurable genetic neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation of extended polyglutamine fragments-containing mutant proteins, which are prone to the formation of poorly soluble aggregates. The adequate cellular model is crucial in uncovering the pathological mechanisms responsible for neurotoxicity in Huntington’s disease (HD), screening for therapeutic molecules and elucidation of the molecular mechanisms impacted by particular compound. In the present study, genetic constructs based on the Sleeping Beauty system were created for the stable inducible expression of full-length normal and mutant huntingtin (HTT) in eukaryotic cells. These constructs were then employed to develop model neuronal cells using Neuro-2a cell line. The expression of HTT as well as the accumulation of HTT-immunopositive intracellular aggregates (most characteristic features of HD) was demonstrated, and these aggregates showed colocalization with the proteasome. The activation of the proteasome, as well as changes in the expression of proteasome regulators, components of the autophagy system, and the neuronal proteases cathepsins B and D, reflect the versatility of cellular responses to the mutant pathological forms of HTT.

Article.Title: Pedagogical incorporation of generative AI in university visual effects courses and its implications for learning assessment and institutional support
Article.Authors: Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is entering university visual effects courses, but how students’ informal uses become part of teaching and assessment remains unclear. This interpretivist multiple-case study examined practices at three Chinese universities through 45 interviews with 36 teachers, students, and staff, 15 observations, course documents, student work, and available GenAI-use records. Within-case and cross-case analysis developed four themes: uneven movement from student experimentation into course workflows; the use of generated alternatives in comparison and revision; reported uncertainty about technical competence and creative control when outputs appear polished; and attempts to make student decisions and contributions visible. Across the cases, participants’ accounts and available records suggest that the meaning of GenAI use depended on task objectives, teacher guidance, assessment requirements, and institutional support. Process visibility offers a way to examine the boundary between assistance and substitution through students’ intentions, selections, revisions, and explanations. Because the study did not directly measure learning or competence, these are contextual interpretations rather than demonstrated educational effects.

Article.Title: Prospective associations of urinary bisphenol A and phthalate metabolites in early and school-aged childhood with liver function in adolescence
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Lee H.; Park B.; Hong Y.; Kim H.; Park H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract People are simultaneously exposed to multiple endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs). We prospectively evaluated the associations of the mixture of urinary bisphenol A (BPA) and phthalate metabolite concentrations measured at 3–5 and 7–9 years of age with liver function in adolescence, as a surrogate indicator of metabolic disease. We analyzed 126 children whose urinary BPA and phthalate metabolite concentrations were measured at 3–5 and 7–9 years of age; their liver enzyme levels were measured in adolescence. The overall association of the urinary biomarker mixture with liver enzyme levels and the variable importance of the biomarker groups—BPA and metabolites of high- and low-molecular-weight phthalates (HMWPs and LMWPs)—were evaluated using Bayesian kernel machine regression. We investigated sex-specific associations and bivariate interactions between urinary biomarkers. In each measurement period, phthalate metabolite concentrations were generally strongly correlated within the HMWP and LMWP groups. Additionally, there were correlations between BPA and several phthalate metabolites at 3–5 years of age but not at 7–9 years of age. For biomarkers measured at 3–5 years, estimated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels and the AST/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ratio tended to increase when mixture components were jointly set above their respective medians. For biomarkers measured at 7–9 years, estimated AST, ALT, and gamma-glutamyltransferase (γ-GTP) levels tended to increase as mixture concentrations increased jointly. However, the overall effect was not statistically significant; only an overall trend was detected. LMWPs, particularly monoisobutyl phthalate (MiBP), had the highest variable importance for AST. We evaluated the associations of the mixture of urinary BPA and nine phthalate metabolite concentrations in childhood with liver function in adolescence. The results provide epidemiological evidence on associations between urinary EDC biomarkers and liver enzyme levels, indicating a need for further research.

Article.Title: Optimal multi-objective configuration of a hybrid walker-star/delta navigation satellite constellation in LEO via MOPSO and reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Hesari A.; Bakhtiari M.; Daneshjou K.
Article.Abstract: Optimal design of satellite constellations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) for global navigation and positioning applications is of significant importance. This study presents a design framework for LEO satellite constellations based on hybrid Walker-Star/Delta geometric configurations, with the objective of simultaneously minimizing Geometric Dilution of Precision (GDOP) and deployment costs. A multi-objective optimization approach is employed by integrating Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to adaptively tune key optimization parameters and the resulting RL-MOPSO algorithm is validated against conventional MOPSO and NSGA-II on standard benchmark problems. Satellite manufacturing and launch costs are estimated using a combined SSCM/USCM8 cost model and the design tool is further validated against the operational GLONASS constellation. The proposed hybrid configuration is evaluated against conventional Walker-Delta and Walker-Star configurations across multiple orbital altitudes. Results show that the optimized hybrid configuration achieves a notable improvement in mean GDOP compared with both Walker-Delta and Walker-Star configurations, while maintaining a comparable number of satellites and avoiding any significant increase in deployment cost. These findings demonstrate that the proposed RL-MOPSO based hybrid configuration is an effective approach for designing high-accuracy, cost-efficient LEO navigation constellations for future global navigation and precise positioning applications.

Article.Title: Experimental data-based analysis and intelligent prediction of smoke production characteristics for typical PMMA fire loads in substations
Article.Authors: Jin M.; Zhu W.; Zhang Y.; Liu Q.; Meng T.; Jiang C.; Tang Z.; Li Y.; Wang H.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Accurate characterization and early prediction of smoke production are essential for fire-risk assessment in substations, where polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) is a typical fire load. Cone-calorimeter tests were conducted on 5 and 25 mm PMMA specimens, with three replicate trials each. Seven time-resolved combustion variables, including smoke production rate (SPR), heat release rate, and gas concentrations, were recorded throughout the full combustion cycle. Using a 30 s historical window, K-nearest-neighbor (KNN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and Transformer models were trained to forecast SPR at horizons of 5, 15, and 30 s, with one complete trial held out for independent cross-trial testing. The 5 mm specimens showed a short, concentrated smoke-production process, whereas smoke production from the 25 mm specimens persisted for more than 1800 s; despite a 26.8% lower peak SPR, their total smoke production (68.73 ± 15.88 m²) was approximately 10.3 times that of the 5 mm specimens. Among the three PMMA smoke models developed from the experimental data, Transformer achieved R² greater than 0.8 under both scenarios and was the better performing of the three models. Error analysis revealed an increasing tendency to underpredict SPR at longer horizons, and SHAP analysis showed that model reliance shifted from historical SPR toward material consumption and combustion-state features.

Article.Title: Timbre variation in weakly coupled multiple-metronome network encourages integrative beat perception and enhances individual differences
Article.Authors: Lem N.; Fujioka T.
Article.Abstract: Auditory textures can emerge from large-scale ensembles of rhythmic sound sources, such as insects’ percussive clicks or birds’ vocal calls. These “swarms” of overlapping events are sometimes identified by listeners as a single texture, or perceived as containing certain rhythmic structures, depending on different levels of embedded synchrony. Our previous study demonstrated that even within the same synchrony level, individual listeners’ ability to extract beat-like rhythmicity widely varies. The present study further investigates how introducing timbral variation into such textures affects their perception. Using a generative model of forty phase-coupled oscillators, we presented participants with metronome sounds under varying coupling strengths, either with identical or slight timbre differences and asked them to tap along however they feel the ‘beat.’ Results revealed that slight timbral heterogeneity encouraged more regular tapping responses in weaker coupling conditions in a subset of participants, particularly those who were already able to elucidate regular beats without timbre variation. We suggest that, for some listeners, timbre may serve as a perceptual anchor that facilitates integrative, rather than sequential, rhythm processing. These findings shed light on the interaction between timbre and individual differences in temporal perception.

Article.Title: An anatomy aware Mamba framework for video based 3D human pose estimation
Article.Authors: Song J.; Chen F.; Zhong L.
Article.Abstract: Video-based 3D human pose estimation suffers from depth ambiguity and faces great challenges in modeling long‑range spatial and temporal dependencies. Diffusion models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for this task. However, their denoisers commonly rely on Transformer backbones, where quadratic self-attention complexity limits computational efficiency. We propose AnatoMamba, an anatomy-aware Mamba framework for diffusion-driven 3D human pose estimation. AnatoMamba employs Articulated Pyramid Pooling to aggregate multiscale body context, Kinematic Wave Scanning to serialize joints according to skeletal topology, and Anatomical Signature Injection to explicitly encode body-part membership. The derived anatomy-aware features are further refined through bidirectional spatial and temporal state space modeling to capture inter-joint dependencies and cross frame motion patterns. With 243-frame inputs and 10.44 million trainable parameters, AnatoMamba-L achieves an MPJPE of 38.5 mm on Human3.6M. In cross-dataset evaluation on MPI-INF-3DHP, it achieves 98.9% PCK, 87.5 AUC, and 14.7 mm MPJPE. These results demonstrate competitive pose estimation accuracy with a compact parameter footprint.

Article.Title: Effect of plant-based compost on the growth and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage under salt stress in peat-based growing media
Article.Authors: Alkaç O.
Article.Abstract: Soil salinity is one of the major abiotic stress factors limiting the growth, ornamental quality, and performance of ornamental plants. This study investigated the effects of different compost application rates on plant growth, morphological characteristics, phytochemical composition, and antioxidant defense mechanisms in ornamental cabbage ( Brassica oleracea var. acephala ‘Pigeon Red F1’) under salt stress. The experiment was conducted as a two-factor factorial design consisting of three compost rates (0, 20, and 40%) and four NaCl concentrations (0, 25, 50, and 75 mM). Morphological traits, chlorophyll content (SPAD), root characteristics, antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, POD, and SOD), oxidative stress indicators (MDA and H₂O₂), total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, DPPH radical scavenging activity, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) were evaluated. Compost significantly affected plant height, plant diameter, leaf number, plant fresh weight, root length, root fresh weight, and root dry weight. Increasing compost rates generally reduced plant height, plant diameter, and leaf number, whereas mean root length increased. Salinity significantly affected plant height, leaf number, and SPAD values. Compost × salinity interactions were significant for plant height, leaf length, SPAD values, and catalase activity, indicating that responses to salinity depended on the compost rate. Neither compost nor salinity nor their interaction significantly affected plant dry weight or central coloration diameter. The 20% compost treatment improved maintenance of total flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity under moderate salinity conditions, while the 40% compost treatment increased total phenolic content under non-saline conditions. Salinity significantly altered antioxidant enzyme activities and oxidative stress markers, whereas catalase activity, root length, root dry weight, and central coloration diameter were not significantly affected. Overall, compost application modified the physiological and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage to salt stress in a dose-dependent manner. These findings indicate that compost application may help maintain ornamental quality and improve stress tolerance under saline cultivation conditions, providing a sustainable strategy for ornamental cabbage production.

Article.Title: Improved MGLR control charts based on Klein’s sensitizing rules for joint mean and dispersion monitoring under measurement error
Article.Authors: Maleki M.; Jafari M.; Eghbali H.; Nikoogoftar M.
Article.Abstract: Shewhart-type control charts, despite their simplicity and satisfactory performance in detecting large shifts, are not sufficiently sensitive to small process changes. On the other hand, in many real-world applications, an assignable cause simultaneously affects both the location and dispersion parameters of the process. Furthermore, despite advances in data-collection technologies, measurement errors remain unavoidable, and their effects on control-chart performance should therefore be considered. Motivated by these considerations, this paper has two objectives. First, two enhanced versions of the multivariate generalized likelihood ratio (MGLR) control chart are developed by incorporating Klein’s 2-of-2 and 2-of-3 sensitizing rules to accelerate the detection of small shifts in the process mean, dispersion, or both. Second, the improved charts are modified under an additive covariate model to account for the effect of measurement error. The effectiveness of the proposed monitoring schemes, and the adverse effects of measurement error are evaluated through extensive simulations, considering various out-of-control scenarios and error variance levels using average run length ( ARL ), standard deviation of the run length ( SDRL ), and median run length ( MRL ). Additionally, an extensive sensitivity analysis is conducted to evaluate the effects of subgroup size ( \(n\) ) and process dimensionality ( \(p\) ), revealing that increasing the sample size substantially improves the detectability of all charts, whereas process dimensional growth degrades their detection sensitivity. The results indicate that measurement error diminishes the sensitivity of all control charts to process changes, even at low levels of error variance. Nevertheless, the 2-of-2 and 2-of-3 schemes substantially outperform the classical MGLR chart across all shift scenarios and error variance levels, with the 2-of-3 scheme performing slightly better than the 2-of-2 counterpart.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: median run length; measurement error; standard deviation of run length; average run length; small shift detection; subgroup size

Article.Title: Multi-agent dual federated learning for intelligent task offloading in hierarchical edge–fog–cloud 6G networks
Article.Authors: Ambika B.; Pandian S.; Sundaravadivel P.; Vinothkumar E.
Article.Abstract: The rapid emergence of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks is driving the need for intelligent task offloading frameworks capable of simultaneously satisfying stringent latency, energy efficiency, scalability, and privacy requirements. Existing task offloading approaches are constrained by centralized learning architectures, binary offloading decisions, inadequate handling of heterogeneous non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, and limited awareness of wireless interference dynamics, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization in hierarchical Edge–Fog–Cloud (EFC) environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes MADFL-6G, a Multi-Agent Dual Federated Learning framework for intelligent task offloading in hierarchical 6G networks — ‘Dual’ referring to MWFA’s two-component aggregation weighting, which jointly combines data-volume proportionality and KL-divergence-based distribution-similarity penalization (Sect. 3.5, Eq. 9). The proposed framework integrates distributed Dueling Deep Q-Network (Dueling DQN) agents with Prioritized Experience Replay (PER), a Mobility-Weighted Federated Averaging (MWFA) strategy for robust aggregation under heterogeneous data distributions, an interference-aware seven-dimensional state representation, and a five-action adaptive partial task offloading mechanism that dynamically distributes computational workloads across edge, fog, and cloud resources. The task offloading process is formulated as a set of coupled, independently learning agents operating within a shared, non-stationary Edge–Fog–Cloud environment, incorporating stochastic wireless channel conditions and queueing dynamics to accurately model realistic 6G environments. Extensive experiments conducted on more than 200,000 real task execution records demonstrate that MADFL-6G achieves an average latency of 61 ms, energy consumption of 0.31 J, and a 98.7% task success rate, outperforming conventional federated deep Q-learning by 28.2%, 31.1%, and 2.6%, respectively, while substantially exceeding heuristic and centralized baselines. Additional analyses, including scalability evaluation, component ablation, statistical significance testing, robustness under non-IID settings, and SHAP-based explainability, confirm the effectiveness, interpretability, and reliability of the proposed framework. These findings demonstrate that MADFL-6G provides a scalable, privacy-aware, raw-data-preserving, and explainable solution for intelligent resource management in emerging 6G applications, including autonomous transportation, industrial Internet of Things, smart cities, and extended reality services.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: prioritized experience replay; non-IID data; edge-fog-cloud architecture; 6G; task offloading; dueling deep Q-network; multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Software-Defined Networks and 5G; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Wireless Network Optimization

Article.Title: Proposed new words and collective identity in human and language model agent groups
Article.Authors: Ito K.; Nagai H.; Wakamiya S.; Aramaki E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Groups develop distinctive words even when ordinary expressions are sufficient. Such words can symbolize collective identity, and observational studies link language use to community attachment. We examined identity change in temporary groups of one human and four disclosed large language model (LLM) agents, comparing discussions with and without a neologism proposal across recruitment waves. We recruited 100 Japanese participants in two sequential waves; an agent proposed a new word only in the first wave. Mean collective identity change did not differ significantly between waves. Within the proposal wave, favorable ratings of the proposed word were associated with change in identity, but this association did not survive correction for multiple testing (adjusted $$p=0.229$$ ). The three-way interaction among recruitment wave, message count, and team impression had a nominal $$p=0.027$$ but did not survive correction (adjusted $$p=0.082$$ ). In a sensitivity analysis, the interaction was not significant after adjustment for midpoint identity (nominal $$p=0.078$$ ; adjusted $$p=0.624$$ ). The nonsignificant between-wave comparison and exploratory associations that did not survive correction, together with wave confounding and post-discussion evaluations, limit causal inference and motivate randomized studies with repeated measures to test whether proposed group language affects identification.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: LLM agents; collective identity; neologisms; community attachment; group languages; personal transformation

Article.Title: Effects of motor imagery training on landing kinematics in female volleyball players: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Niziplioğlu A.; Uysal Ö.; Ergun N.; Fırat T.
Article.Abstract: Although the effectiveness of motor imagery (MI) in improving performance in sports is known, there is no research on its effect on jumping and landing in female volleyball players. Thirty female volleyball players were randomized into three groups and followed up for 12 weeks. Participants in the Solo training (ST) and Group training (GT) groups received the motor imagery intervention individually or in a group setting, respectively, whereas the Control group (CG) continued routine volleyball training only. Jump landing was recorded, and hip, knee, and ankle joint angles were measured using the Dartfish Analysis System. Neurocognitive functions were measured using the Computerized Neurocognitive Tests Vital Signs (CNSVS). Initial contact knee varus–valgus and ankle plantarflexion showed significant group × time interactions (right knee: p = 0.024; left knee: p = 0.005; ankle plantarflexion: p = 0.001). Post hoc analysis revealed that for the right knee, the GT group showed greater changes in the varus–valgus angle than the CG (GT vs. CG: p = 0.024). For the left knee, both the ST and GT groups showed greater changes in the varus–valgus angle than the CG (ST vs. CG: p = 0.011; GT vs. CG: p = 0.013). A significant group × time interaction was observed for initial-contact plantarflexion angle; the pre-to-post change was greater in the ST group than in both the GT group ( p = 0.002) and the CG ( p = 0.008), whereas the GT and CG did not differ. During full contact, hip flexion ( p = 0.004), knee flexion ( p = 0.027), left knee valgus/varus ( p = 0.003), and ankle flexion ( p = 0.041) also showed significant group × time interactions. Post hoc analysis revealed greater reductions in hip flexion (ST vs. CG: p = 0.004), knee flexion (ST vs. CG: p = 0.023), and greater changes in ankle flexion (ST vs. CG: p = 0.049) in the ST group, whereas both the ST and GT groups demonstrated greater changes in left knee valgus/varus than the CG (ST vs. CG: p = 0.008; GT vs. CG: p = 0.007). Most neurocognitive outcomes did not show significant group × time interactions. Significant interactions were observed for processing speed and simple attention; however, these findings were not supported by Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc interaction contrasts, which showed no significant pairwise differences in pre-to-post changes between groups. Motor imagery training was associated with changes in selected laboratory-based landing kinematics in female volleyball players. However, no clear evidence was found for meaningful improvements in neurocognitive performance. Further studies including kinetic analyses, injury incidence, and sport-specific landing assessments are needed to determine whether these kinematic changes translate into clinically meaningful reductions in injury risk. Participants were randomly allocated into three groups. This trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07009080). The trial record was initially submitted on May 27, 2025, met the registry’s quality-control criteria on May 29, 2025, and was publicly posted on June 6, 2025. Participant enrolment commenced on June 9, 2025.

Article.Title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of a human-centric AI tutoring and human-in-the-loop assessment system in advanced STEM education
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang Z.; Zhou R.; Xiao C.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education, yet most deployments of large-language-model tutoring and automated grading target introductory courses and pay limited attention to the transparency, trust, and equity concerns that become acute in advanced, safety-critical technical domains. This paper presents a human-centric AI-assisted instructional system and evaluates it in a postgraduate hardware-security course on electromagnetic protection and side-channel analysis. The system couples three human-centric components: (i) a retrieval-augmented tutoring assistant whose answers are grounded in citable course materials to curb hallucination and preserve traceability; (ii) a human-in-the-loop assessment pipeline in which a language model drafts rubric-based feedback that instructors verify item by item; and (iii) an adaptive, tiered project-based learning path that offers differentiated entry points. We evaluated the system in a quasi-experiment with 47 postgraduates (24 experimental, 23 control) taught concurrently by the same instructors in parallel class sections. The experimental group’s competency score rose from 62.4 to 84.7, against 61.8 to 70.2 for the control group, a difference in gains that was statistically significant and associated with a large effect size ( \(t(41.2)=4.55\) , \(p<0.001\) , Cohen’s \(d=1.32\) ), while its score dispersion contracted from a standard deviation of 14.5 to 7.2. A baseline-by-group interaction indicated significantly stronger differential improvement among initially lower-scoring students in the experimental section, although this distributional finding is interpreted cautiously given the non-randomised design. Human-in-the-loop grading was associated with a 35.7% reduction in marking time while reaching an AI–instructor agreement of quadratic-weighted Cohen’s \(\kappa =0.95\) ; because this agreement measures consistency rather than correctness, we interpret it accordingly. We examine how human oversight, citation grounding, and adaptivity may have jointly contributed to these outcomes, treating the intervention as an integrated bundle whose individual components remain to be isolated, and we set out the responsible-AI safeguards that such deployments require.
Article.Topic: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

Article.Title: Chattering-attenuated sensorless hybrid PMSM drive using integral hyperbolic sliding backstepping control and EKF: real-time co-simulation on dSPACE DS1104
Article.Authors: Bekkour E.; Sakhri Z.; Mahfoud S.; Boulal A.; Hussien S.; Mosaad M.; Larguech S.; Bossoufi B.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a Sensorless Hybrid Integral Hyperbolic Sliding Backstepping Control strategy with an Extended Kalman Filter (SH-IHSBSC-EKF) for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drives. The proposed strategy is developed to enhance the dynamic response, disturbance rejection, and current quality of the drive without mechanical position and speed sensors. The controller is designed through a recursive backstepping procedure, in which the virtual control inputs are derived from Lyapunov theory to guarantee the global exponential stability of the speed and current tracking error dynamics. In the outer speed loop, an integral sliding surface with an exponential reaching law and a hyperbolic tangent switching function ensures fast convergence and attenuates chattering. In parallel, the EKF reconstructs the rotor position and speed from stator current and voltage measurements. The designed strategy is evaluated against the Proportional-Integral (PI-EKF) and Integral BackStepping Control (IBSC-EKF) sensorless strategies under three simulation scenarios using MATLAB/Simulink. Under low-speed operation, the settling time is reduced by 95.68% and 48.00% compared with PI-EKF and IBSC-EKF, respectively, and the load rejection time by 96.41% and 64.37%. Moreover, the stator current Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) is reduced from 2.68% with PI-EKF and 0.56% with IBSC-EKF to 0.24% with SH-IHSBSC-EKF. In all three scenarios, covering variable speed and load, low-speed operation, and parameter variations, stable speed tracking with near-zero steady-state error is preserved. The proposed strategy is further validated through real-time co-simulation on a dSPACE DS1104 platform. Although the EKF remains sensitive to inductance mismatch and assumes a known initial rotor position, the overall performance demonstrates the potential of the proposed strategy for high-performance sensorless PMSM drives.

Article.Title: GreenSense: controlled predictive, computational, and carbon-aware evaluation of efficient neural models for fraud detection
Article.Authors: Sathya K.; Pandiyan M.; Tamilselvi S.; Kaliyamurthy N.; Taterh S.; Agarwal S.; Kant S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Green artificial intelligence requires model quality to be evaluated together with computational cost, model size, and estimated environmental impact. This study presents GreenSense as a controlled benchmarking framework for energy-aware fraud detection. Seven configurations are compared on two imbalanced transaction datasets: Compact Nonlinear Dense (CND), full-precision and dynamically quantized tabular CNNs and MLPs, an LTC-style state-refinement network, and a sparse NCP-CfC-style network. All training, quantization, and inference measurements were repeated on a single dedicated workstation (Intel Core i5-13500, Windows 11) under one fixed software stack, thread and CPU-affinity setting, and measurement protocol. Each model–dataset configuration is evaluated over five independently seeded training runs, and each inference measurement is repeated five times in fixed-work windows of at least 30 s. CPU-package energy is measured with CodeCarbon and cross-checked against a second software readout of the same hardware energy counter; CO $$_2$$ is derived from a cited national grid-emission factor. Predictive evaluation emphasizes precision–recall area under the curve (PR-AUC), $$F_1$$ , recall, precision, and ROC-AUC. On FraudTrain, the LTC-style model achieved the highest mean PR-AUC (0.8015, 95% CI 0.7947–0.8082), followed by MLP-FP32 (0.7679) and NCP-CfC-style (0.7654). On the ULB Credit Card benchmark, MLP-FP32 (0.7554) and CND (0.7528) had the highest mean PR-AUC with overlapping intervals, while CNN-FP32 had the highest mean $$F_1$$ (0.1889). Training accounted for more than 99.9% of lifecycle-equivalent energy for every configuration. Dynamic INT8 quantization reduced MLP storage size by 1.94 $$\times $$ (FraudTrain) and 2.09 $$\times $$ (ULB) but increased inference energy per transaction in all four FP32–INT8 pairs (by 43–47% for the MLP and 4–6% for the CNN; all paired intervals excluded zero). Its predictive effect was dataset-dependent: FraudTrain MLP PR-AUC decreased by 0.301 (95% CI $$-0.358$$ to $$-0.247$$ ), whereas the ULB change was only $$-0.003$$ . The PR-AUC/lifecycle-energy Pareto sets were CND, MLP-FP32, and LTC-style on FraudTrain and CND and MLP-FP32 on ULB. GreenSense provides a reproducible, task-specific basis for comparing predictive, computational, and estimated environmental operating points; all code, configurations, raw energy logs, and manifests are archived with a DOI.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: fraud detection; green AI; credit card fraud; CO2 emissions
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Imbalanced Data Classification Techniques; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Green IT and Sustainability; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications

Article.Title: Amplification-free detection of antibiotic resistance in Enterococcus faecium using PNA-FISH
Article.Authors: Im J.; Yun S.; Choi B.; Kim S.; Kim C.; Nho S.; Campbell N.; Kang J.; Kwon T.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) is a major nosocomial pathogen, with antibiotic resistance mediated by the vanA and vanB operons. Rapid and accurate detection of antibiotic resistance is critical for the timely treatment of bacteremia and sepsis. Although imaging-based approaches using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) provide a potential diagnostic solution, detecting mRNAs of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in individual cells remains particularly challenging due to their low copy number and transient expression. Here, we present a peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-FISH method for direct detection of vanA- and vanB -associated resistance in individual VREfm cells. A universal probe targeting the conserved region across vancomycin resistance genes and a set of probes exclusively targeting the vanB gene were designed. The universal probe showed increased fluorescence in the vanA -genotype strain upon vancomycin or teicoplanin treatment, and in the vanB -genotype strain upon vancomycin treatment. In contrast, vanB -specific probes showed increased fluorescence exclusively from the vanB -genotype strain upon vancomycin treatment, confirming their specificity to the vanB gene. Efficient cellular penetration and high target specificity of PNA probes enabled efficient and reliable detection of antibiotic-resistant bacterial cells, even under a wide-field fluorescence microscope. Negligible signals above background were observed in other major bacterial species associated with bacteremia and sepsis, suggesting the potential detection of antibiotic-resistant strains in mixed microbial samples. When integrated with microbe-capturing techniques, this method may enable culture-independent detection of antibiotic resistance without nucleic acid amplification or sequencing, with the potential to reduce diagnostic turnaround time.

Article.Title: Adaptive Japanese language instruction using behaviorally inferred learner states and multimodal contrastive reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent tutoring systems for second-language acquisition have long aspired to deliver instruction that mirrors expert human pedagogy, yet existing approaches rely either on static knowledge-tracing models that ignore real-time cognitive signals or on large language models fine-tuned with fixed curricula that cannot adapt to individual learner trajectories. In the specific and linguistically complex context of Chinese speakers learning Japanese, cross-lingual phonological and orthographic transfer introduces an additional layer of challenge that general-purpose systems fail to address systematically. We identify three core obstacles: (i) the absence of a unified representation that jointly captures acoustic pronunciation quality and lexical comprehension, (ii) the inability of current curriculum planners to reason about latent cognitive load, and (iii) the lack of principled cross-lingual prior injection during feedback generation. To overcome these, we propose CogAdapt, a novel end-to-end framework that fuses a contrastive cross-modal encoder with a reinforcement-learning-based curriculum planner conditioned on continuous cognitive-state estimates, and generates error-aware natural language feedback through a cross-lingual knowledge-grounded decoder. On three public benchmarks—JLPT-Learn, CALL-SJ, and EduLLM-JA—CogAdapt achieves 82.6%, 80.1%, and 78.9% accuracy, outperforming the best baseline by up to 5.5 percentage points, and improves BLEU-4 by 4.7 points, demonstrating that cognitive adaptivity and cross-lingual transfer awareness are jointly essential for robust AI-assisted language learning.
Article.Topic: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

Article.Title: ​​QSVQ-Net: A morphology-conditioned spiking–variational quantum network for interpretable brain tumour MRI classification
Article.Authors: Abinash P.; Krishnamoorthy N.
Article.Abstract: Accurate, interpretable classification of brain tumours from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to treatment planning, yet high-performing deep models are often poorly calibrated and rarely tested beyond a single dataset. We present QSVQ-Net, a hybrid quantum-classical framework that couples an EfficientNet-B0 backbone and a complex-valued spiking neural network to a morphology-conditioned variational quantum circuit, in which eighteen morphological and radiomic descriptors parameterise the qubit rotations through a learnable mapping. Evaluation covers five-fold cross-validation with confidence intervals, calibration, a matched multi-seed ablation, intrinsic circuit characterisation, auxiliary localisation for mask-free inference and external validation against classical baselines. On the BRISC-2025 test partition, QSVQ-Net attains 98.8% accuracy with an expected calibration error of 0.006; under five-fold cross-validation it reaches 99.48% (95% CI 98.91–100.0), statistically indistinguishable from EfficientNet-B0 (99.57%; paired t-test p = 0.59). The quantum branch performs within confidence-interval overlap of a parameter-matched classical control, so we claim no quantum accuracy advantage. On an independent mask-free dataset, accuracy falls to 72.6% while classical baselines retain 90–93%, a limitation we trace to the morphology branch. QSVQ-Net thus offers a reproducible, transparently characterised quantum-classical design and a candid account of where morphology-conditioned quantum encoding helps and where it does not.

Article.Title: Genetic heterogeneity of Plasmodium falciparum across three areas of varying transmission intensity in Ethiopia based on merozoite surface protein (msp) genes msp1 and msp2
Article.Authors: Reda A.; Aseffa A.; Golassa L.; Mamo H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plasmodium falciparum malaria continues to be a significant threat in Ethiopia. This study aimed at assessing the genetic heterogeneity of this malaria parasite. Understanding the genetic diversity of P. falciparum is crucial for informing public health strategies, including vaccine development, diagnostic accuracy, treatment efficacy, and targeted control interventions. Samples for this study were collected from three malaria-endemic sites in Ethiopia with varying transmission intensities—Metema (northwest), Wondogenet (south), and Metehara (central-east). A consecutive convenient sampling technique was employed to recruit outpatients initially enrolled in an uncomplicated malaria therapeutic efficacy study in 2015 from these sites, along with additional samples collected from malaria suspects attending the Metehara health centre in 2019. Overall, 661 finger-prick blood samples were collected for malaria microscopy and rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), while dried blood spot (DBS) samples were obtained on Whatman 903® filter paper for molecular analysis. This study specifically utilized selected 150 quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR)-confirmed P. falciparum monoinfection-positive samples from the previously reported total of 661 samples to investigate previously unreported merozoite surface protein ( msp1 and msp2 ) genes-based genetic heterogeneity. Genotyping of P. falciparum msp1 and msp2 genes was conducted using nested PCR, and the mean multiplicity of infection (MOI), polyclonal infections and expected heterozygosity index (He) were assessed. Out of the 150 samples analyzed, successful genotyping rates of 45.3% were revealed for msp1 and 43.3% for msp2 across the sites. Notable variations in allele frequencies were observed, with the K1 allele predominating for msp1 and the FC27 allele for msp2 . Metema exhibited the highest complexity of infections, with mean MOI values of 1.53 for msp1 and 2.14 for msp2 , alongside the greatest genetic diversity. The analysis indicated that polyclonal infections were prevalent, particularly in Metema and Wondogenet. The overall pooled mean MOI across all study sites was 1.26 for msp1 and 1.59 for msp2 , with an overall polyclonality rate of 35.3% and 44.6%, respectively . Important differences in allele frequencies and a slight reduction in both mean MOI and He were observed over time between samples collected in 2015 and 2019 in Metehara. This study highlights the genetic diversity and regional variations of P. falciparum in Ethiopia, and shifts in population dynamics.

Article.Title: Research on super-resolution reconstruction technology of atmospheric turbulence phase screens based on deep learning
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Zhao M.
Article.Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence phase screens are commonly utilized to calculate the transmission of light in the atmosphere. The key to accurately generating an atmospheric turbulence phase screen is to satisfy the statistical characteristics of atmospheric turbulence. Traditional methods for generating turbulence phase screens are limited by high computational complexity. Therefore, enhancing the image quality of turbulence phase screens is of utmost importance. This paper presents a super-resolution reconstruction algorithm for atmospheric turbulence phase screens based on deep learning. The proposed model integrates the statistical properties of atmospheric turbulence into the neural network and incorporates the wavefront phase structure function to modify the loss function. Experimental results demonstrate that the atmospheric turbulence phase screens generated by the improved super-resolution convolutional neural networks (ISRCNN) are substantially consistent with theoretical values in terms of statistical characteristics. The proposed method achieves a modest improvement over bicubic interpolation and super-resolution convolutional neural networks (SRCNN) models with respect to statistical properties.

Article.Title: AI-assisted ultrasonography for noninvasive detection of moderate-to-severe interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy in chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Yin W.; Lan Y.; Kao C.; Lin Y.
Article.Abstract: Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA) is a common pathway of irreversible kidney damage. Although renal biopsy remains the standard for IFTA assessment, its invasive nature limits repeated monitoring. Ultrasonography (US) assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a potential noninvasive alternative, but its diagnostic performance for IFTA remains to be systematically evaluated. PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Wanfang Database, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched through October 2025. Studies evaluating AI-assisted B-mode ultrasonography, shear wave elastography (SWE), or combined US + SWE for detecting moderate-to-severe IFTA (≥ 25%), with renal biopsy as the reference standard, were included. The primary outcomes were AUROC, sensitivity, and specificity. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly synthesized using a bivariate random-effects model, with estimation of the summary operating point and corresponding 95% confidence and prediction regions. AUROC was separately pooled using a random-effects model. Diagnostic accuracy and other diagnostic measures were evaluated as secondary outcomes. Fourteen studies including 3,776 participants were eligible, of whom 1,244 contributed to pooled diagnostic performance estimates. The bivariate random-effects model yielded a summary sensitivity of 0.821 and summary specificity of 0.828. The pooled AUROC was 0.880 (95% CI, 0.815–0.924). SWE and deep learning models showed numerically higher performance, but subgroup findings were exploratory because of limited study numbers and wide confidence intervals. AI-assisted ultrasonography serves as a reliable, noninvasive diagnostic tool for identifying moderate-to-severe IFTA, demonstrating balanced sensitivity and specificity. While SWE and DL architectures exhibited favorable numeric trends, these subgroup observations remain exploratory and warrant further large-scale prospective validation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy; chronic kidney disease; deep learning; shear wave elastography; B-mode ultrasound; diagnostic accuracy; renal biopsy

Article.Title: Brain tumor classification from contrast-enhanced T1 MRI, a patient-wise deep learning study
Article.Authors: Asiri A.; Soomro T.; Ali A.; Siddiqui R.; Alelyani M.; Alshuhri M.; Alghamdi A.; Alamri S.; Alateeq K.; Awais M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate classification of intracranial tumors on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1) is challenged by heterogeneous enhancement patterns and strong correlations among multiple slices from the same patient. We propose a compact CE-T1 MRI analysis framework that standardizes image intensities, enhances local CLAHE (contrast using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization), and applies a lightweight convolutional classifier whose slice-level probabilities are aggregated to obtain a single patient-level prediction. An independent optional U-Net-based pathway provides binary tumor segmentation when spatial delineation is required. Evaluation was performed using a strictly patient-wise, leakage-controlled protocol with stratified five-fold cross-validation on 233 subjects (3,064 slices) comprising glioma, meningioma, and pituitary adenoma. The classifier achieved 99.4% patient-level accuracy, with macro-averaged sensitivity and specificity of 99.3% and 99.0%, respectively. The optional segmentation pathway achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 97.3%. Post-hoc temperature scaling reduced the patient-level expected calibration error from 3.0% to approximately 1.2%, although larger independent cohorts are required to determine the stability of this estimate. The classifier contains 7.8 million parameters and requires approximately 15.9 GFLOPs per $$256\times 256$$ slice, with an end-to-end inference latency of approximately 0.41 s per slice under the evaluated hardware configuration. These findings demonstrate strong patient-level performance within the evaluated retrospective cohort. The framework is intended as a research-stage approach for reproducible evaluation rather than a clinically validated diagnostic system for routine radiology practice. However, no independent quantitative external validation was performed; therefore, multi-centre evaluation across different scanners, acquisition protocols, institutions, and patient populations is required before generalizability or clinical applicability can be established.

Article.Title: DATE: domain-aware transformer ensembles for reliable extremism detection in social media
Article.Authors: Ali Z.; Qasim M.; Raza ur Rehman H.; Jhandir M.; Villar M.; Garay H.; Ashraf I.
Article.Abstract: Extremist content spreads quickly on social media, so moderation needs classifiers that are accurate and whose confidence can be trusted. We study the Domain-Aware Transformer Ensemble (DATE): a BERTweet-base classifier (pre-trained on 850M English tweets), contextual-substitution and random-edit augmentation applied only inside each training fold, and a soft-voting ensemble of ten fold models. We evaluate on the Social Media Extremism Detection dataset (2,250 training posts, 749 labelled test posts) with a leakage-controlled protocol and report three kinds of evidence separately. (i) Cross-validation: single DATE models reach 0.822 accuracy (±0.027) on held-out folds. (ii) Held-out test posts: the ten-model ensemble reaches 0.843 accuracy (95% CI 0.814–0.868), macro-F1 0.744 and ROC-AUC 0.863, and its expected calibration error is 0.030 against 0.064 for single models (paired bootstrap difference \(-0.029\) , CI \(-0.046\) to \(-0.010\) ); over five training seeds, the ensemble is better calibrated than its members in every run (mean ECE 0.037 against 0.061). (iii) Competition: the submitted DATE ensemble scored 0.8507 on the private leaderboard of the Kaggle challenge ( \(\approx\) 375 posts), tied for first place with two other teams among 164 teams; this margin is within sampling noise. Controlled ablations repeated over five seeds show that augmentation, class weights and the cosine schedule do not improve accuracy at full data size, although augmentation helps when training data is scarce; BERTweet beats RoBERTa-base in all five seeds (1.9 points on the test posts), and a TF-IDF baseline reaches comparable test accuracy. The study is limited to one English dataset whose annotation details (number of annotators, agreement) are not reported, and the test set has a different class balance from the training set.

Article.Title: EPFH-Net: efficient pyramid forward harmonic network for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease detection
Article.Authors: Sekhar C.; Rao K.; Moka S.; Ponnada S.
Article.Abstract: Detecting Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) involves identifying fat accumulation in the liver but not linked to excessive alcohol consumption. NAFLD is a common liver disorder where fat builds up in liver cells, potentially leading to inflammation, liver damage, or liver cancer. Liver biopsy is the therapy used to detect NAFLD in the olden days, which consumed more time and provided inaccurate results. Therefore, the new framework named Efficient Pyramid Forward Harmonic Network (EPFH-Net) is introduced to detect NAFLD effectively. First, the ultrasound liver image sourced from the B-mode fatty liver ultrasound images dataset is fed as the input. Next, the extraction of the region is done by the Region of Interest (ROI) and the features, such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), Pyramid Histogram of Oriented Gradients (PHOG), and Center Symmetric-Local Binary Patterns (CS-LBP), are extracted. Then, Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is detected using EPFH-Net, which is a combination of Efficient Network (EfficientNet), Pyramid Network (PyramidNet), and harmonic analysis. Finally, the detected outputs are fatty or normal. The experimental outcomes attained by EPFH-Net are 92.12% of accuracy, 92.52% of TPR, and 91.88% of TNR for the k-value of 9.

Article.Title: Comparison of aluminum and iron electrodes for electrocoagulation of automotive cataphoresis wastewater: removal performance and operating cost
Article.Authors: Erol Nalbur B.; Kasaplar M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the applicability of the electrocoagulation (EC) process to wastewater generated by the electrocoating (cataphoresis) process used in the painting of vehicle bodies. Samples were obtained from an automotive factory in Bursa, Türkiye. In a laboratory-scale EC reactor equipped with Al–Al or Fe–Fe electrodes, the operating parameters that govern the removal of chemical oxygen demand (COD) and total phosphorus (TP) — inter-electrode distance, current density, and reaction time — were optimized. A Box–Behnken response surface design (Design-Expert 12.0) was used to construct mathematical models, whose adequacy was assessed by analysis of variance (ANOVA). Under the optimum conditions for Al electrodes, removal efficiencies of 74.88% (COD) and 95.37% (TP) were achieved individually, and 74.72% (COD) and 79.28% (TP) simultaneously. With Fe electrodes, the highest measured COD removal was 83.3%, and the TP removal was 61.42% individually and 83.30% (COD) and 46.20% (TP) simultaneously; the quadratic model fitted to the Fe–COD data was not statistically significant and was therefore used only descriptively. Operating costs at current (July 2026) unit prices were 63.8 TL/m³ (US$ 1.35) for Al electrodes and 72.6 TL/m³ (US$ 1.54) for Fe electrodes.

Article.Title: SMFFX: a signal processing-inspired feature extraction framework for viral genomic sequences classification
Article.Authors: Khodaei A.; Mahmoudi Y.; Shahriardoust A.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, the coronavirus and other viral diseases increasing rate have attracted significant attention. Viral data can be analyzed at the intracellular level in the form of genomic sequences. This study introduced a signal processing approach applied to the corresponding signals of viral genomic sequences. The Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) algorithm, based on windowing techniques, enabled examination of genetic samples for feature extraction. Various statistical features were extracted from the resulting feature space, enabling classification algorithms to accurately identify and distinguish among the different virus types with high efficiency. The proposed approach was evaluated on 173,228 samples across 30 types of viruses using both binary and multi-class classification tasks. In the binary classification test, the proposed approach achieved accuracy and F1-scores of more than 0.99 using a decision tree classifier. In the multi-class classification mode, an accuracy of 0.99 and an F1-score exceeding 0.98 were achieved. In the one-versus-rest classes analysis, most classes achieved more than 99% F1-score, and AUC values. The high classification performance indicates the reliable predictive capability of the proposed approach. The feature-importance analysis provides the potential applicability to similar classification tasks involving other viruses or viral variants.

Article.Title: Real-time embedded control and performance evaluation of BLDC motors for electric vehicle applications
Article.Authors: Torad M.; Zahran M.; El-Mokadem S.; El-Mokadem E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are central to modern electric vehicle (EV) drivetrains, yet achieving high efficiency and stable torque under dynamic conditions remains a significant engineering challenge. This study presents the design and real-time embedded implementation of a motor control system realised on the STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller, together with a hardware-parameterised performance characterisation used to evaluate and cross-validate its behaviour. Two established control strategies—Trapezoidal Commutation and Field-Oriented Control (FOC)—were implemented independently on the same hardware platform under identical load conditions to enable a direct, unbiased comparison. The system incorporates Hall-effect sensor-based rotor position detection, closed-loop PI control (speed for Trapezoidal, d/q current for FOC), Direct Memory Access (DMA) for high-speed data acquisition, and a Controller Area Network (CAN) / Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART) framework for real-time parameter transmission to a driver-facing display. Characterised performance results, derived from the implemented hardware's own rated parameters, show that FOC achieves a peak efficiency of 92% versus 86% under Trapezoidal Control, with torque ripple reduced by approximately 40% and peak current lowered from 50 to 44 A. The characterised thermal behaviour indicates that FOC maintains motor temperatures below 70 °C at full load, whereas Trapezoidal Control approaches critical thresholds under equivalent conditions. The modular architecture supports scalability across microcontroller tiers and EV configurations, providing a validated and deployable reference for energy-efficient BLDC drive systems.

Article.Title: Broadband amplification of organ of Corti vibrations in the mouse cochlear apex
Article.Authors: Dewey J.
Article.Abstract: Mammalian hearing depends on the active amplification of sound-evoked waves as they travel along the basilar membrane within the cochlea. This amplification is mediated by the outer hair cells (OHCs), which generate force to enhance the vibrations of the surrounding structures. While OHCs at a given location only amplify basilar membrane motion for a narrow frequency range, recent measurements show that the amplification of motions deeper within the organ of Corti is much more broadband. However, the extent to which this broadband amplification influences the motions that are most relevant to inner hair cell stimulation – i.e., at the organ’s apical surface – remains uncertain. Here, optical coherence tomography was used to demonstrate that OHCs nonlinearly amplify the motions near the top of the organ of Corti, including at the reticular lamina and tectorial membrane, over a wide frequency range in the mouse cochlear apex. Responses at all frequencies were physiologically vulnerable and grew compressively with stimulus level. Low-frequency responses also exhibited non-monotonic features that were due to interference between amplified motion and the underlying traveling wave. The data suggest that broadband amplification of motions at the top of the organ of Corti likely explains certain phenomena observed in auditory nerve responses.

Article.Title: CROWN-UAV: world-model-based planning for risk-aware and auditable UAV navigation
Article.Authors: Farkh R.; Khayyat M.; Alsaig A.; Khayyat M.; Eshmawi A.; Jambi E.; Omri K.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous UAV navigation in cluttered warehouses requires anticipation of dynamic and occluded hazards, explicit risk attribution, and recovery-aware action selection. CROWN-UAV integrates an object-centric encoder, a retrained action-conditioned dual world model, stochastic future hypotheses, a calibrated structured risk graph, candidate-level runtime filtering, discrete receding-horizon planning, and planner-grounded audit traces. A frozen, leakage-controlled revision campaign evaluated five implementations on 120 paired NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1.0 PhysX cases per method across three warehouse layouts, four hazard families, five disturbance conditions, and two independent scenario seeds. CROWN-Full achieved 59.2% success (95% CI 50.2–67.5%), identical to Greedy and slightly below MPPI (60.8%). Relative to Greedy, CROWN reduced near collisions from 51.7% to 30.8% (paired difference − 20.8% points, Holm-adjusted p = 0.00346) and increased mean minimum clearance by 0.241 m (adjusted p = 5.40e-9), while successful paths were 2.50 m longer and completion was 3.90 s slower on 53 jointly successful cases. At 4.5 s, the DualWorldModel improved UAV ADE (0.313 versus 1.314 m) and occupancy IoU (0.527 versus 0.392) relative to constant velocity, but object ADE was worse (0.772 versus 0.547 m). Full-loop p95 latency was 101.95 ms, with 150/15,170 deadline misses. The evidence supports an implementation-specific proximity-safety trade-off and auditable decision records, not higher task completion, universal predictor superiority, formal safety, or human-validated explainability.

Article.Title: Chitosan-intercalated FePS3 as novel and efficient adsorbent for Congo-red dye removal from aqueous solution
Article.Authors: El-Shafey O.; El-shafey S.; Abdel-Karim A.; El-Meligi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates surface adsorption of Congo red dye (CR) by iron phosphorus trisulphide (FePS 3 ) before and after chitosan (CS) intercalation. The novel intercalation of CS into the layered nanomaterial FePS 3 was processed to obtain FePS 3 -CS. The materials of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS were characterized by XRD, FTIR, SEM–EDX, and BET techniques. These tests verified the effective intercalation of the chitosan into the layered nanomaterial FePS 3 with improved characteristics for applications involving adsorption. XRD measurements show a slight shift and partial intercalation of CS into FePS 3 layers, and some diffraction peaks have disappeared. This behavior may be due to CS as a polymer interacting with FePS 3 through electrostatic interactions between the amino/hydroxyl groups of CS and S-containing FePS 3 , surfaces, and hydrogen bonding. IR and SEM–EDX confirm the presence of CS functional groups and main elements after intercalation with FePS 3 . FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS exhibited notable removal of Congo-Red from artificial aqueous solutions. The best adsorption circumstances of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS were found in the presence of a dye concentration of 50 mg/L, a dose of (0.05 g and 0.025 g), and pH 5 and 6, respectively, and a contact time of 90 min. Under these conditions, the maximum adsorption efficiencies of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS are 91.4 and 99%, respectively. The results of the kinetic study indicated that a pseudo-second-order kinetic model described the adsorption process with a high degree of agreement between the experimental data and the kinetic model. Moreover, the best kinetic model describing the equilibrium data is the Freundlich isotherm, and this model demonstrates multilayer adsorption behavior. These results highlight the proper effectiveness and promise of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS as novel adsorbents for CR dye removal applications.

Article.Title: Composite approach to quantifying regulating soil-based ecosystem services using multiple indicators
Article.Authors: Pindral S.; Coblinski J.; Wnuk A.; Smreczak B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The spatial evaluation of soil functions and soil-based ecosystem services (SES) is a key challenge and demand nowadays. SES can provide a scientific background to the decision and policy-making. We define them as benefits that humans and the environment derive from soils and their functions. In our studies we presented the first maps of SES on a national scale for Poland. The research was focused on evaluation of regulating SES, which plays a crucial role in the crop production and circulation of matter and processes in the entire environment. Regulating SES contribute to CO 2 fluxes and sequestration, nutrient cycling, water cycle regulation, control of erosion and mass movements, among others. In this research we develop the multi-indicators index, grouping four SES and 11 separate indicators. For this reason, we used geometric means for calculating regulating SES and their final integrated index. For the nutrients provision, and carbon sequestration we used digital soil mapping approach with quantile regression forest algorithm, while for the water regulation and erosion control, mechanistic and empirical models were applied. Our results showed that regulating SES in Polish agricultural areas is relatively low, indicating serious limitations for Polish agriculture. In particular, 84% agricultural soils were classified as having very low or low status of regulating SES especially due to natural limitations, whereas only 2% showed high status, mainly due to the limited capacity for erosion control and high water retention capacity. This is an important step in the agricultural studies indicating the main soil health problems and areas of improvement to increase the natural potential of soils. The presented approach, due to the applied statistical and point bonitation methods, can be applied to other SES evaluation, and also allows to implement different indicators that may be more important for different regions in the world.

Article.Title: Underwater dielectric elastomer actuators with large bending deformation for soft robots
Article.Authors: Murata C.; Shibuya T.; Yoshizaki S.; Uemura N.; Kusama K.; Nakane D.; Shimizu M.; Shintake J.
Article.Abstract: Soft robots are promising platforms for underwater exploration and biological sampling because of their compliance and adaptability. Dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs), particularly bending DEAs, are appealing for underwater soft robots because they enable diverse robotic architectures. However, existing underwater bending DEAs are limited in deformation magnitude and speed. Here, we present an underwater DEA comprising a layered elastomer with an encapsulated water electrode, an inextensible layer, and transverse reinforcing frames. The inextensible layer restricts deformation on one side of the actuator to induce bending, while the transverse frames further constrain lateral deformation, enabling larger and faster bending deformation. The resulting actuator achieves a maximum bending angle of 308.5° (corresponding to a curvature of 82.8 m − 1 ), and its voltage dependence is captured by an analytical model. It further attains maximum bending speeds of 161.1°/s and 245.0°/s upon voltage application and removal, respectively, and a blocked force of 57.2 mN, while maintaining stable actuation over 10,000 cycles. The actuator was further demonstrated as an electrically driven biohybrid luminescent device incorporating Pyrocystis lunula and as a soft gripper capable of manipulating a live jellyfish. These results highlight the potential of the proposed DEA for advancing underwater soft robotic systems.

Article.Title: Physics-anchored fault-cell localization in electric vehicle battery packs with variable cell counts
Article.Authors: Fang F.
Article.Abstract: Identifying a faulty cell from battery-management records is difficult when operating trends affect all cells and different diagnostic indicators favour different candidates. Here we present PhyFuseCell, a physics-anchored ranking method for packs with variable cell counts. Both branches reference cell voltages to the pack median: one characterizes charge-residual magnitudes and trends, while the other learns normalized discharge patterns. A shared cell encoder and scorer, together with valid-cell masking, accommodate different pack sizes. The evidence scores are standardized within each pack and combined with equal weights. On CH-BatteryGen packs with 28 or 124 cells, the compact implementation achieved the highest mean Top-1 localization accuracy among the evaluated methods, at 98.0 ± 2.7% across five vehicle-held-out splits, 7.0 percentage points above a validation-tuned clustering baseline. Paired predictions showed how complementary evidence corrected competing cell rankings. In self-discharge transfer without target-group training, adding target-pack charge evidence increased mean accuracy from 61.0 to 83.8% for 28-to-124-cell transfer and from 66.3 to 94.7% in reverse. These results support organizing physical and temporal evidence at the cell level to improve fault localization across the evaluated pack sizes.

Article.Title: Determination of suitable reference genes for RT-qPCR analysis in Gryllodes sigillatus (Orthoptera: Gryllidae)
Article.Authors: Ben-Miled H.; Bonhomme R.; Renois F.; Deschamps M.; Benoit-Biancamano M.; Meurens F.
Article.Abstract: The tropical house cricket Gryllodes sigillatus is an emerging species in edible insect farming; however, molecular resources for this species remain limited. In particular, the absence of validated reference genes hinders accurate RT-qPCR normalization and reliable gene expression analyses across different tissues. To address this limitation, we evaluated the expression stability of six candidate reference genes ( ACTB , EF1α , GAPDH , HisH3 , RPL5 , and 18 S rRNA ) in four tissue types (abdomen, head, legs, and whole body). Gene stability was assessed using geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, the comparative ΔCt method, and RefFinder, while the optimal number of reference genes was determined by pairwise variation (Vₙ/Vₙ₊₁) analysis. Candidate genes were identified from the G. sigillatus genome and annotated by BLAST and reciprocal BLAST analyses, and all experimental procedures complied with the MIQE 2.0 guidelines. ACTB , RPL5 , and EF1α were identified as the most suitable reference genes for abdominal samples; ACTB , GAPDH , and RPL5 for head samples; EF1α , RPL5 , and ACTB for leg samples; and EF1α , ACTB , and RPL5 for whole-body samples. In contrast, GAPDH and His H3 exhibited relatively unstable expression across most tissues, with the exception of GAPDH in the head. Although 18 S rRNA consistently ranked among the most stable reference genes, its high transcript abundance suggests that its suitability should be carefully evaluated, particularly for the normalization of low-abundance target genes. This study provides the first validated reference gene panel for G. sigillatus , enabling reliable tissue-specific RT-qPCR normalization and supporting future gene expression studies, although validation under additional experimental conditions is still required.

Article.Title: Identification of 1H-pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridines as potential inhibitors of Leishmania arginase
Article.Authors: Camargo P.; de Sousa Ribeiro J.; Soares J.; dos Santos C.; Albuquerque M.; Muri E.; Rodrigues C.; Dias L.; Lima C.
Article.Abstract: Leishmaniasis, a parasitic disease transmitted by sandflies, remains a significant global health concern, particularly in tropical regions. The arginase enzyme ( La Arg) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in Leishmania amazonensis . This study employs a computer-aided drug design approach to identify novel La Arg inhibitor candidates. A series of 38 compounds featuring a 1 H -pyrazolo[3,4- b ]pyridine nucleus was evaluated using 3D-QSAR (Py-CoMFA), molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict pIC 50 values and investigate molecular interactions within the La Arg active site. Our results identified 14 compounds with promising predicted activity (pIC 50 ≥ 5.00). Molecular docking analysis revealed that 10 compounds establish strong interactions with key catalytic residues (His127 and His142) and Mn 2+ ions, which are crucial for La Arg binding. Molecular dynamics further characterized compounds 1b and 1e as potential arginase inhibitors, though they exhibited distinct thermodynamic profiles. Compound 1b , featuring a nitrile group, demonstrated initial stability and a balanced molecular profile. However, it failed to maintain its binding mode throughout the entire simulation trajectory. Conversely, while 1e remained stable at the site, its bromine substituent incurred a significant solvation penalty, leading to a less favorable binding free energy than 1b . These findings provide significant insights into the structural requirements for arginase inhibition and establish a framework for developing novel therapeutic compounds against leishmaniasis.

Article.Title: Integrating sustainable technological interventions for cleaner fertilizer production and occupational ammonia exposure reduction
Article.Authors: Elhadad S.; Omar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Egypt's fertilizer industry is a major component of the petrochemical sector and relies heavily on ammonia during nitrogenous fertilizer production, creating potential occupational exposure risks for workers. Over the past decade, sustainable technological interventions and pollution-control measures have been implemented to reduce ammonia emissions and improve workplace safety. This study assessed occupational ammonia exposure among workers in a modern nitrogenous fertilizer plant in Alexandria, Egypt, and evaluated the effectiveness of these interventions. Ammonia concentrations were measured at representative operational stations using a MIRAN gas analyzer, and a structured questionnaire was administered to assess workers' occupational characteristics, use of personal protective equipment, health complaints, and awareness of occupational hazards. Ammonia concentrations ranged from 0.70 to 1.06 ppm, remaining approximately 95.8–97.2% below the occupational exposure limit of 25 ppm recommended by the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH) and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH). These low exposure levels were completed through the implementation of cleaner production technologies, including the Uhde ammonia synthesis process, replacement of conventional urea melting and prilling with environmentally friendly granulation technology, acidic scrubbing systems, condensate stripping, ammonia recovery and recycling, emission capture systems, and preventive maintenance practices. The findings demonstrate that integrating cleaner production technologies, Best Available Techniques (BAT), continuous environmental monitoring, ammonia detection systems, emergency response measures, and targeted occupational health training can effectively minimize occupational ammonia exposure, enhance worker safety, ensure compliance with international occupational health standards, and promote environmentally sustainable and economically efficient fertilizer production

Article.Title: Efficient color image encoding using chroma-subsampled hybrid quantum representation
Article.Authors: Nikam V.; Motghare M.; Gupta R.; Panchal V.; Dey B.; Nirkhi S.; Patel R.
Article.Abstract: Quantum image representation (QIR) is a fundamental component of quantum image processing, but existing color-image encoding approaches often require substantial qubit resources, gate counts, and circuit depths. This work presents CS-HQR (Chroma-Subsampled Hybrid Quantum Representation), a hybrid quantum classical framework that integrates YCbCr color space transformation and 4:2:0 chroma subsampling with quantum state preparation. The proposed framework preserves the luminance component at full spatial resolution while encoding chrominance components at reduced resolution, thereby reducing the amount of color information requiring quantum encoding. CS-HQR employs a dual circuit architecture in which the luminance component is encoded using 16 qubits and the subsampled chrominance components use 15 qubits including a channel selection qubit. The framework was evaluated using 6097 medical brain MRI images, with circuit level analysis performed across the complete dataset and reconstruction-quality analysis conducted on a representative subset. Compared with MCQI, CS-HQR requires 16 rather than 18 qubits and achieves approximately 54.0% reduction in transpiled gate count and 72.2% reduction in transpiled circuit depth, while maintaining high reconstruction quality. To assess generality beyond grayscale derived medical images, additional experiments were conducted on the Kodak, BSD500, and USC-SIPI natural colour benchmarks, obtaining mean SSIM values of 0.987, 0.981, and 0.984, respectively, with approximately 50% gate reduction. These results indicate that classical perceptual redundancy reduction can be incorporated into quantum image encoding to reduce state preparation resources while maintaining high reconstructed-image quality. The study provides a simulation-based evaluation of CS-HQR and establishes a basis for further investigation on hardware-aware and noise-resilient quantum image processing systems.
