Article.Title: Theory of mind inspired mental state reasoning with large language models for empathetic response generation
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As conversational AI expands into emotionally sensitive domains such as mental health support and counseling, empathetic response generation has become a key research challenge. Existing empathetic dialogue systems either reflect the user’s surface level emotions or, when relying on external commonsense knowledge bases, capture only generic patterns. We propose a Theory of Mind inspired framework in which a large language model first infers the speaker’s five mental states of Belief, Desire, Emotion, Intent, and Knowledge from the multi turn dialogue history and then uses them as conditioning signals for empathetic response generation. A preliminary study on a theory of mind benchmark indicates that the LLMs employed perform reasonably on mental state inference in both multiple choice and free form settings. On an empathetic dialogue dataset, injecting the self generated inferences improved response quality under both automatic metrics and LLM as judge evaluation. In the LoRA fine-tuned setting, the ToM condition performed comparably to COMET, an external commonsense knowledge baseline, with higher ROUGE-L point estimates for all four backbones and a significant advantage for one. Shuffled and corrupted descriptions consistently degraded response quality, whereas the ToM condition and a context-grounded factual-summary control performed similarly, indicating that contextual grounding is the primary source of the benefit. These findings suggest that speaker grounded mental state reasoning can be an effective strategy for empathetic dialogue systems.

Article.Title: Unsupervised neural clustering and seismic attribute analysis for gas channel delineation in the Scarab field
Article.Authors: Khalifa T.; Eleslambouly A.; Khalil A.; Ismail A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The western offshore Nile Delta of Egypt represents a significant hydrocarbon province, characterized by complex stratigraphy and challenging reservoir connectivity. This study investigates two vertically stacked, unconnected channel systems, Channels 1 and 2, which serve as the primary reservoirs in the Scarab Field. Conventional seismic interpretation techniques often fall short in delineating subtle stratigraphic features and reservoir architecture. To overcome these limitations, we employed an integrated machine learning workflow combining Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to enhance reservoir characterization. After data conditioning and the calculation of seismic attributes, PCA was applied to reduce dimensionality and extract the most informative seismic attributes. The resulting principal components were input into SOMs, an unsupervised neural network approach used to classify seismic meta-attributes into meaningful lithological facies. The SOM successfully identified six distinct facies classes: siltstone, clayey sand, clayey limestone, gas-bearing sandstone, water-bearing sandstone, and interbedded siltstone, validated through well log calibration. In particular, the technique delineated gas-water contacts and subtle stratigraphic trends that are critical for both exploration and development planning. The results and quantitative analysis through classification accuracy and GWC misfit assessments using different data types demonstrate that unsupervised machine learning, supported by multi-attribute seismic analysis, offers important improvements over traditional interpretation methods in detecting Direct Hydrocarbon Indicators (DHIs), refining stratigraphic resolution, and reducing exploration risk.

Article.Title: Healthcare provider’s perceptions of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings
Article.Authors: Suwanbamrung C.; Asgai A.; Endrias E.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a key public health concern globally, especially in resource-limited settings, where health system limitations contribute to poor antimicrobial stewardship. Digital health solutions present an opportunity to improve antimicrobial stewardship through better prescribing, surveillance, and clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, there is limited evidence on healthcare providers’ perceptions and contextual factors that affect the implementation of digital antimicrobial stewardship in low-resource settings. The objective of this study is to explore healthcare providers’ perceptions of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited primary hospitals. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted in public primary hospitals in the Wolaita Zone of Southern Ethiopia, utilizing in-depth interviews with purposively chosen healthcare providers. Data collection was done until thematic saturation was reached. The interviews were recorded on tape, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed through inductive thematic analysis using Opencode version 4.02 software. Fourteen participants were included in the study. Five key themes emerged: infrastructure-related issues, training and digital competency, organizational support and leadership, perceived usefulness of digital tools, and opportunities to enhance antimicrobial stewardship. Respondents identified the possibilities of digital tools to improve the accuracy of prescribing and monitoring; inappropriate digital infrastructure, insufficient training, and lack of institutional support were identified as barriers to successful implementation. The facilitators were leadership dedication, capacity-building efforts, and the incorporation of digital systems in daily clinical operations. Technological, human, and organizational factors are mutually dependent and influence the implementation of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings. Although healthcare providers have good perceptions about digital antimicrobial stewardship, there is a need to bridge the gap in infrastructure and capacity. Digital readiness and institutional support are needed to facilitate the successful implementation and sustainability of digital health interventions to fight antimicrobial resistance.

Article.Title: Safe and efficient positioning control of an offshore wind turbine installation vessel
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Li X.; Chen X.; Liu Q.
Article.Abstract: This article proposes a safe and efficient positioning control method for offshore wind turbine installation vessels (OWTIVs), addressing the challenges posed by unmeasured multi-source disturbances and thruster constraints. First, a prescribed-time composite disturbance observer (PTCDO) is developed to accurately estimate multi-source disturbances. Building on this, an adaptive robust prescribed performance control (PPC) law is designed to enhance the dynamic performance of the OWTIV and ensure operational safety. Additionally, a finite-time auxiliary dynamic system is introduced to address the effects of input magnitude and rate constraints. To further improve positioning accuracy, the control framework integrates finite-time command filtered backstepping (FTCFB) technology with PTCDO and PPC, forming a finite-time DP control law with prescribed performance. The finite-time stability of the positioning system is rigorously proven using Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, the proposed positioning control strategy is validated through numerical simulations, including performance assessments under partial failure conditions of the disturbance observer, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of load transfer and coupling techniques for soil–structure interaction in 3D building models
Article.Authors: Felić H.; Langarudi A.; Tschuchnigg F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The distinct separation of structural and geotechnical numerical modelling often results in inadequate representation of soil–structure interaction (SSI), with simplified coupling methods such as the subgrade reaction approach neglecting nonlinear and time-dependent soil behaviour. This study evaluates a methodological framework for SSI analysis by comparing decoupled modelling approaches against holistic three-dimensional benchmark models developed in SOFiSTiK and PLAXIS for an eight-storey high-rise building on a raft foundation. The framework systematically examines five foundation load transfer approaches (ranging from smeared surface loads to discrete nodal force extraction) and three structural–geotechnical coupling strategies, assessing their accuracy in reproducing benchmark foundation settlements and raft bending moments. The results show that simplified smeared load approaches yield settlement deviations exceeding 15 %, whereas discrete nodal forces with explicit superstructure stiffness achieve near-perfect benchmark agreement. Conventional subgrade reaction moduli, whether constant or variable, exhibit error margins from $$-40$$ to $$+40$$ %, while the exchange of imposed settlement troughs reproduces benchmark results with deviations below 1 %. These findings demonstrate that replacing stiffness-parameter exchange with nodal-displacement transfer substantially reduces settlement and bending moment deviations, providing a practicable and more accurate basis for SSI analysis in structural and geotechnical engineering practice.

Article.Title: Secrecy-aware sequential RIS selection for energy efficient user-assisted cooperative NOMA in 6G networks
Article.Authors: R D.; Albert S.; K G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology for achieving ultra-reliable and inherently secure connectivity by enabling software-defined control of the electromagnetic environment in sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, most existing RIS-assisted Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) frameworks assume static user positions or rely on simple nearest-RIS selection (NRS) criteria, which fail to account for the security risks posed by spatially distributed eavesdroppers along a mobility path. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a secrecy-aware, RIS-enabled user-cooperative NOMA framework, where a near-user acts as a cooperative relay to assist a mobile far-user in the presence of localized eavesdropping threats. A novel Sequential-Action Secrecy-aware RIS Selection (SA-SRS) algorithm is introduced, utilizing a security-constrained hysteresis margin to optimize handovers and proactively bypass “danger zones” where eavesdropping risk is high. The framework integrates a partitioned RIS architecture with Singular Value Decomposition-based (SVD-U) precoding and artificial noise (AN) injection to maximize the secrecy gap while effectively suppressing inter-user interference without the need for high-complexity iterative phase tuning. Extensive simulations along a dynamic mobility path demonstrate that the proposed SA-SRS scheme maintains a superior and stable secrecy sum-rate by strategically avoiding compromised RIS units, effectively mitigating the rate degradation observed in traditional NRS methods. Furthermore, the analysis of secrecy outage probability (SOP) and energy efficiency (EE) confirms that the proposed framework achieves a robust trade-off between physical layer security and sustainable power consumption, proving its suitability for high-mobility secure 6G communications.

Article.Title: Evaluating large language models for public patient education on levodopa therapy in Parkinson’s disease: accuracy, empathy, reliability, and readability
Article.Authors: Zuo H.; Tang Q.; Wang C.; Zuo X.; Cheng C.; Wang L.; Zhu L.
Article.Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based chatbots are increasingly used for health information, but their performance in Parkinson’s disease (PD) patient education remains unclear. This study evaluated five widely used LLM-based chatbots in answering public questions about levodopa therapy. In this cross-sectional comparative study, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, and Doubao were assessed using a structured set of levodopa-related patient education questions. In the primary analysis, 265 responses were evaluated by five blinded raters for safety, accuracy, empathy, and information quality using predefined criteria, including DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark criteria, and the Global Quality Score. Readability was assessed using six established indices. An additional 265 responses were generated in an independent repeat-generation analysis using the same question set to assess response stability. Inter-rater agreement was high. Safe-response rates ranged from 86.8% to 94.3%. Accuracy differed significantly, with Copilot and DeepSeek showing the highest median scores, whereas empathy differences were modest and closely clustered. Doubao had the highest DISCERN and EQIP scores, while ChatGPT had the lowest information-quality scores. Gemini showed the best readability profile and Doubao the poorest. Repeat-generation analysis showed generally high stability, with 97.0% exact safety agreement and largely preserved model rankings. Current LLM-based chatbots generated generally informative English-language responses about levodopa therapy, but safety gaps, variable information quality, and poor readability remained. These findings reflect expert-rated output quality rather than demonstrated patient education effectiveness, and patient-centered validation is warranted.

Article.Title: Development and internal validation of a 12-month recurrence nomogram for non-puerperal mastitis: a two-center retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Wang N.; Wu G.; Ma T.; Qin J.; Zhang R.; Tian X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To construct and internally validate a recurrence risk prediction model for non-puerperal mastitis (NPM) by integrating sociodemographic, clinical, pathological, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data. A retrospective study was conducted on 517 patients with first-diagnosed NPM admitted to two hospitals from January 2020 to August 2024. Of the 764 initially assessed patients, 83 were excluded for insufficient follow-up, leaving 681 patients who completed the 12-month follow-up. Among these 681 patients, 164 were further excluded due to predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria or incomplete data, resulting in 517 patients in the final analysis. The index date was the documented resolution of clinical symptoms and active imaging abnormalities after initial treatment. LASSO regression was used to select predictors, and multivariate Logistic regression was applied to construct a nomogram model. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis. Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method. During the 12-month follow-up, 56 patients (10.8%) experienced recurrence. LASSO regression identified five predictors: age, white blood cell count, monocyte proportion, axillary lymphadenopathy, and surgical procedure. Multivariate Logistic regression showed that elevated white blood cell count (OR = 1.449), axillary lymphadenopathy (OR = 4.513), and minimally invasive surgery (OR = 14.390) were independent risk factors for recurrence, while increasing age (OR = 0.941) and elevated monocyte proportion (OR = 0.716) were protective factors. The apparent AUC was 0.921 (95%CI: 0.894–0.948); the optimism-corrected AUC after 5,000 bootstrap resamples was 0.897. At the Youden-optimal threshold, sensitivity was 0.82, specificity 0.87, positive predictive value 0.43, and negative predictive value 0.98. The calibration curve indicated good agreement between predicted and actual probabilities (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, P = 0.147). Decision curve analysis demonstrated clinical net benefit within the threshold probability range of 0.05–0.80. This exploratory nomogram shows good apparent discrimination in the development cohort, but the surgical-procedure coefficient should be interpreted as a predictive marker rather than a causal effect due to confounding by indication. External and center-specific validation are required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Applied research on a seismological method for coal mine blasting safety
Article.Authors: Song S.; Shi Y.; Zhang L.; Li Z.; Jiao X.; Xing Y.
Article.Abstract: The magnitudes of coal mine blasts are generally low, and the yield estimation of which faces significant challenges. In this study, based on measured ground motion data from coal mine blast experiments, the time–frequency characteristics of the signals and the attenuation law of ground motion are analyzed in depth. On one hand, a local magnitude dataset is obtained by establishing a near-field calibration function model, and rapid quantitative yield estimation is achieved through a near-field magnitude-yield empirical formula. On the other hand, drawing on a far-field seismic wave energy calculation model, the physical chain of the radiated energy method and yield is inverted through source spectrum integration and explosive seismic efficiency is elaborated, and a blast yield estimation model based on near-field seismic radiated energy is established. In view of the practical limitations imposed by the monitoring system bandwidth and the signal analysis time window, the systematic underestimation of radiated energy estimates caused by frequency truncation is quantified, and a semi-theoretical, semi-empirical method for analyzing and calculating explosive seismic efficiency is introduced. In this study, the calculated frequency-band compensation coefficient ranges from 0.140 to 0.191, and the seismic explosive efficiency ranges from 0.013 to 0.017. The data from blasts 3–7 were utilized to calibrate all model parameters, including the attenuation coefficients of displacement and velocity, the seismic explosive efficiency, and the parameters for the calibration function and empirical formula in the magnitude-yield relationship, and the data from blasts 1–2 were used for validation. The results show that the radiated energy method provides a physically more explicit approach to yield estimation for small-magnitude coal mine blasts, while the constraints of bandwidth truncation and efficiency dispersion must be acknowledged. A cross-checking framework is recommended, in which the magnitude method serves for rapid preliminary estimation and the energy method provides physical constraints, offering a reference for related yield estimation.

Article.Title: Evidence of expanding range and environmental suitability for Culex perexiguus in Northern Italy (Emilia-Romagna, 2025)
Article.Authors: Calzolari M.; Grisendi A.; Scremin M.; Dalmonte G.; Callegari E.; Casano A.; Severini F.; Antolini G.; Albieri A.; Dottori M.
Article.Abstract: Culex perexiguus , a mosquito typically associated with hot and semi‑arid environments across North Africa, the Middle East, and southwestern Asia, has recently emerged as a potential public health concern in parts of southern Europe due to its demonstrated vector capacity for multiple arboviruses, particularly West Nile virus (WNV). In 2025, 84 specimens of this mosquito were collected across 22 sites in Emilia‑Romagna, northern Italy, within the regional WNV entomological surveillance program; DNA barcoding of 21 individuals confirmed morphological identification. Comparison with entomological data from 2009 revealed a concurrent decrease of another mosquito, Culex modestus , suggesting a possible northward shift in suitable areas for both species. Ecological niche modelling based on presence records of Cx. perexiguus indicated an estimated distribution primarily linked to the availability of suitable breeding habitats, and the meteorological anomalies recorded in 2025 (compared to 2001–2020) likely favoured its presence. The unexpected expansion of Cx. perexiguus into Emilia‑Romagna, in an area characterised by a temperate continental climate, underscores the broader changes in mosquito distribution potentially linked to climate change. Its presence may have significant implications for public health, vector surveillance, and control strategies, and will therefore require careful monitoring in the coming years.

Article.Title: Physical activity and sedentary behavior are longitudinally associated with diurnal cortisol rhythms up to 1 year after colorectal cancer treatment
Article.Authors: Frenken K.; Scheer F.; Qian J.; Bours M.; Breukink S.; Janssen-Heijnen M.; Konsten J.; Keulen E.; Bons J.; Meijer K.; Steindorf K.; de Vos-Geelen J.; Weijenberg M.; Buffart L.; van Roekel E.
Article.Abstract: Less robust diurnal cortisol rhythms are hypothesized to be associated with fatigue, depressive symptoms, psychological distress, sleep disturbances and poorer quality of life. Sedentary behavior and physical activity may influence cortisol rhythmicity, providing mechanistic leads for intervention strategies. We examined longitudinal associations of accelerometer-assessed sedentary behavior and physical activity with diurnal cortisol patterns among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) up to 12 months post-treatment. Among 74 CRC survivors, total and prolonged sedentary time (in bouts ≥30 min), total physical activity (TPA), and relative amplitude of physical activity reflecting day-night contrast in activity were determined with 7-day thigh-worn accelerometry at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after cancer treatment. Salivary cortisol was sampled five times daily over two consecutive days at each follow-up timepoint. As a comprehensive assessment of diurnal cortisol rhythms, the relative amplitude of cortisol concentration (RA_cort), diurnal slope, area under the curve and cortisol awakening response (CAR) were derived as comprehensive measures of diurnal cortisol rhythms. We used confounder-adjusted linear mixed models to estimate overall longitudinal associations, with coefficients (β) reflecting differences in SD units of the cortisol parameters per 2 h/day of sedentary time, per 1 hour/day of physical activity, or per 1 SD of the RA of physical activity. More total sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a weaker decline in cortisol over time and thus a flatter slope (β = 0.19; 95% CI = 0.06,0.33). More prolonged sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a lower RA_cort (β = − 0.12; 95% CI = − 0.23, − 0.01) and flatter cortisol slope (β = 0.16; 95% CI = 0.04,0.27). More TPA (per 1 h/day: β = 0.23; 95% CI = 0.03,0.43) and a higher relative amplitude of physical activity (per SD: β = 0.15; 95% CI = 0.00, 0.29) were associated with a higher RA_cort. More total sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a higher CAR (β = 0.14; 95% CI = 0.01, 0.27). Higher physical activity levels, a larger RA of physical activity, and less sedentary time were associated with more robust diurnal cortisol rhythms, mainly driven by inter-individual associations. Intervention studies are needed to determine whether modifying these behaviors may improve cortisol rhythmicity after CRC. Registration : EnCoRe study ( https://www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl/ ).

Article.Title: Federated dual-attention temporal convolutional networks for privacy-preserving intrusion detection in EV charging infrastructure
Article.Authors: Ragab M.; Alhussian H.; Abdulkadir S.; Eltahir M.; Alwadain A.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure has increased exposure to cyberattacks, while conventional centralized intrusion detection remains poorly suited to distributed and privacy-sensitive EVSE environments. This study proposes a federated learning framework based on a Dual-Attention Temporal Convolutional Network (DA-TCN) for collaborative cyberattack detection without centralized data sharing. The model combines dilated causal convolutions with channel and temporal attention to capture complex dependencies in multimodal EVSE telemetry. To improve federated optimization, we introduce Federated Stochastic Weight Averaging (FedSWA) and client-local mixup augmentation, which together enhance generalization and robustness across distributed clients. Evaluated on the CICEVSE2024 dataset, the proposed framework achieved 99.29% accuracy and 99.10% macro F1-score, outperforming a centralized baseline (98.79% accuracy) while maintaining perfect recall for benign and cryptojacking traffic. With an inference latency of 8.26 ms per batch and a model size of 4.07 MB, the framework is well suited for real-time edge deployment. A complementary Isolation Forest module provides unsupervised zero-day anomaly detection. These results demonstrate that federated learning can deliver accurate, lightweight, and deployment-ready intrusion detection for privacy-preserving EV charging infrastructure.

Article.Title: High intensity interval training modulates autophagy and apoptosis related markers in the liver of D galactose induced aged rats
Article.Authors: Shahouzehi B.; Fallah H.; Najafipour H.; Rostamzadeh F.
Article.Abstract: Aging deregulates autophagy and apoptosis, leading to progressive liver dysfunction. This study examined the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on autophagy and apoptosis-related markers in a D-galactose (D-gal)-induced aging model, focusing on the AMPK signaling pathway. Male Wistar rats were allocated into four experimental groups: Control (CTL), HIIT, D-gal, and D-gal+HIIT. Experimental aging was induced by D-galactose administration for eight weeks, while HIIT was performed using a treadmill running protocol. mRNA expression and protein levels of AMPK, Beclin1, NF-κB (p65), ATG9, and caspase-3 were assessed by real-time PCR and Western blotting, respectively. Total antioxidant and total oxidant status were determined using colorimetric methods. Pro-inflammatory indices were measured by ELISA. AMPK mRNA expression and p-AMPK protein levels were higher in the D-gal+HIIT group than in the D-gal group. HIIT upregulated Beclin1 and ATG9 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels and reduced caspase-3 mRNA expression and cleaved caspase-3 protein levels in the D-gal group. HIIT was associated with a reduction in NF-κB mRNA expression and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β levels, along with restoration of oxidant/antioxidant balance in D-gal-treated rats. These findings suggest that HIIT is associated with coordinated molecular changes that may help maintain liver homeostasis during experimental aging.

Article.Title: Bent ommatidia in apposition eyes
Article.Authors: Yamahama Y.; Hariyama T.; Jafrancesco D.; Ugolini A.; Ciattini S.; Mercatelli L.
Article.Abstract: The compound eyes of arthropods are typically composed of ommatidia with straight dioptric apparatus and rhabdoms all aligned along the optical axis, a configuration assumed to maximize light capture. Through comparative morphological analyses carried out on 12 species of crustacean amphipods belonging to 9 genera and 7 families, we reveal an unexpected deviation from the canonical architecture: the rhabdoms are markedly bent. This is not found only in Talitrus saltator but in other supralittoral beach-dwelling amphipods with a similar style of life: they rest under the damp sand during the day and perform migrations along the sea–land axis of the beach at night or in dim light. However, occasionally they are forced to leave the damp belt of sand and quickly return to it even during the day, for example due to predation attempts or changes in sea state. This bent organization of rhabdoms, absent in marine and terrestrial amphipods, indicates a new habitat-specific optical specialization and, from an optical point of view, points to a role of the rhabdoms beyond that of simple light guides. Moreover, bent ommatidia are embedded in interommatidial cells filled with a white substance, observed in all amphipods possessing bent rhabdoms. Ray-tracing simulations and optical modelling evoke enhanced light collection by scattering compared with straight ommatidia lacking this substance, albeit at the cost of reduced spatial resolution. We propose that this arrangement improves visual sensitivity in dark, dim, or rapidly changing twilight conditions. Our findings thus reveal a novel structure and mechanism for light harvesting in apposition compound eyes, highlighting a distinct optical strategy for maintaining visual performance in supralittoral and intertidal dwelling amphipods.

Article.Title: SSG-GAN: spatial-spectral guided generative adversarial network for hyperspectral reconstruction from RGB images
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Quan S.; Cao X.; Liu J.; Tang X.; Zhang T.; Wang Z.; Peng Y.; Li H.; Xiao X.
Article.Abstract: Hyperspectral reconstruction from a single RGB image provides a practical and low-cost solution for spectral imaging with conventional cameras. However, the task is highly ill-posed because three broad RGB channels must be mapped to multiple continuous narrow spectral bands. Existing methods, including convolutional, Transformer-based, multi-scale, and adversarial reconstruction models, have improved reconstruction accuracy, but many of them still learn RGB spatial structures and hyperspectral reconstruction features in a coupled reconstruction stream, while adversarial constraints mainly focus on spatial distributions. To address these issues, we propose SSG-GAN, a spatially guided hyperspectral reconstruction framework. The generator explicitly decouples RGB spatial-prior extraction from hyperspectral reconstruction through a dedicated multi-scale guidance branch. At corresponding decoding stages, a Cross-Branch Spatial-Spectral Attention (CB-SSA) module uses guidance-derived spatial weights to modulate reconstruction features and further refines them through feature-channel modulation and channel recalibration. Moreover, the discriminator incorporates a dedicated pixel-wise spectral-vector branch to evaluate joint band responses, providing complementary adversarial supervision alongside the multi-scale spatial branches. Experiments on CAVE, Harvard, and ICVL demonstrate the competitive performance of SSG-GAN. Specifically, it achieves MRAE/SAM/RMSE values of 0.0605/0.0734/0.0177 on CAVE, 0.0393/0.0294/0.0041 on Harvard, and 0.0303/0.0309/0.00101 on ICVL.

Article.Title: First application of a ball-pen probe for direct measurements of plasma potential and nonlinear fluctuation dynamics in a linear helicon plasma
Article.Authors: Di Matteo D.; Yamada T.; Nagashima Y.; Adamek J.; Cavalier J.; Namimatsu R.; Chung H.; Moon C.
Article.Abstract: Direct measurements of the plasma space potential and electron temperature are essential for characterizing plasma dynamics and fluctuations, particularly in magnetized plasma systems. Here, a ball-pen probe (BPP) is assembled and installed for the first time on a linear helicon plasma device, enabling direct and fast measurements of the plasma space potential and, in combination with a Langmuir probe, estimation of the electron temperature. A comparative study between BPP and Langmuir probe measurements demonstrates the success of the BPP in simultaneously resolving radial profiles and temporal fluctuations of the plasma potential and electron temperature. The BPP floating potential approximates the plasma potential directly in the edge and peripheral regions, whereas a finite correction is required in the core. Preliminary measurements further reveal low-frequency instabilities and nonlinear plasma potential dynamics that are not directly accessible through Langmuir probe measurements. These results demonstrate for the first time the potential of BPPs for direct investigation of plasma potential dynamics and turbulence in linear helicon plasmas.

Article.Title: Evaluating large language models for quality control in research ethics review
Article.Authors: Maghsoudlou P.; Fennelly-Barnwell J.; Abraham A.; Kapacee Z.; Allen C.; Totenhofer A.; Mamtora S.; Keane P.; Denniston A.; Liu X.; Kolstoe S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) could streamline research ethics and governance review by automating routine quality control checks. This study assessed Claude 3.5 Sonnet, ChatGPT4o, and Microsoft CoPilot in evaluating participant information sheets against Health Research Authority standards. Six clinical trial applications were processed using 32 standardised queries, with accuracy, processing time, error rates, and response quality assessed by two blinded reviewers. Claude showed the highest accuracy, detected more deviations from guidance, and had the fastest processing time (7.17 ± 0.68 min vs. ChatGPT 13.58 ± 2.2 min, CoPilot 23.25 ± 6.21 min). Hallucination rates were lowest in Claude, followed by ChatGPT and CoPilot. Claude also received the highest response quality ratings (77.6% “very good” vs. ChatGPT 56.7%, CoPilot 45.2%). While all three models were capable, Claude consistently outperformed the others, demonstrating the potential of LLM-assisted quality control while emphasizing the need for human oversight.

Article.Title: Enhancing the sensitivity of fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance sensors using nanostructured metamaterials
Article.Authors: Afroozeh A.
Article.Abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) optical fiber sensors represent a prominent technology for label-free biochemical diagnostics; however, conventional single-layer metallic configurations suffer from an inherent trade-off between sensitivity and spectral linewidth. In this study, we propose and numerically demonstrate a high-performance refractive index sensor based on a side-polished (D-shaped) optical fiber functionalized with an engineered two-dimensional array of gold Split-Ring Resonator (SRR) metamaterials atop a continuous \(\:50\text{\:nm}\) gold base film. The underlying physical mechanism is elucidated using a lumped-element inductive-capacitive ( \(\:LC\) ) circuit framework, where the near-field hybridization between propagating surface plasmons (SPPs) and localized magnetic/electric resonances (LSPRs) generates an intense \(\:15.2\) -fold local electric field confinement within the \(\:20\text{\:nm}\) capacitive subwavelength split gap. Rigorous numerical simulations are executed using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method and cross-validated with the Finite Element Method (FEM), yielding mutual agreement above \(\:99.9\%\) with an absolute discrepancy below \(\:0.4\text{\:nm}\) . Across the standard biological refractive index regime ( \(\:{n}_{a}=1.330-1.390\) ), the proposed sensor achieves a high wavelength sensitivity of \(\:{S}_{\lambda\:}=933.3\text{\:nm/RIU}\) , an ultra-narrow full width at half maximum of \(\:\text{FWHM}=18.0\text{\:nm}\) , an elevated Figure of Merit of \(\:\text{FOM}=51.8{\text{\:RIU}}^{-1}\) , a peak amplitude sensitivity of \(\:{S}_{A,max}=68.4{\text{\:RIU}}^{-1}\) at \(\:\lambda\:=776.5\text{\:nm}\) , and a limit of detection of \(\:\text{LOD}=1.07\times\:{10}^{-5}\text{\:RIU}\) . Furthermore, comprehensive tolerance analyses demonstrate robust spectral stability against dimensional fabrication perturbations ( \(\:\pm\:10\text{\:nm}\) ) and negligible thermal cross-sensitivity ( \(\:0.012{\text{\:nm/}}^{\circ\:}\text{C}\) ). With its high spectral resolution, planar lithographic feasibility, and dual-interrogation versatility, this metamaterial-assisted fiber architecture offers a robust platform for real-time, trace-level chemical and biological sensing applications.

Article.Title: The first genome of the Italian hare (Lepus corsicanus) and new insights into Lepus phylogenesis
Article.Authors: Buglione M.; Scala G.; Rivieccio E.; de Filippo G.; Drinkwater R.; Troisi S.; Fulgione D.
Article.Abstract: The Italian hare ( Lepus corsicanus ) is a Mediterranean endemic species, restricted to Southern and Central Italy, Sicily, and introduced historically in Corsica. It is currently classified as Vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, mainly due to habitat loss, population fragmentation, and the widespread introduction of the European hare ( L. europaeus ). Despite the urgent need of conservation, knowledge on its ecology and genetic traits remain unexplored which weakens the tools for proper species management. Here, we report the first high-quality de novo assembly of L. corsicanus genome, generated using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing and a co-assembly approach supported by the existing reference genome. The final assembly has a total length of 2.84 Gb, with scaffolds (N50 = 129 Mb) anchored to 23 autosomes and X, Y chromosomes, and a BUSCO completeness of 98.2%. Genomic annotation uncovered 22,159 protein-coding genes, with an average gene length of 50,882 bp, mean exon length of 223 bp, and repetitive elements account for approximately 40% of the genome. A preliminary investigation on phylogenetic position of L. corsicanus relative to other Lepus species present new insights into the evolutionary history of the group. The topology recovered a strongly supported sister relationship between L. corsicanus and L. castroviejoi , as well as L. europaeus and L. timidus . L. capensis and L. tolai formed a clade, which was strongly related to L. yarkandensis with high statistical support, and all together grouped with the L. europaeus - L. timidus clade. These results underline that reference genome for L. corsicanus provides a valuable resource for future research on the evolution studies and conservation.

Article.Title: G protein–coupled receptor 41 deficiency exacerbates dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis and is associated with altered gut microbiota composition
Article.Authors: Tomikawa A.; Ito T.; Kageyama T.; Meguro K.; Tanaka S.; Iwata A.; Suto A.; Suzuki K.; Kimura I.; Nakajima H.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease comprises chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract. G protein-coupled receptor 41 (GPR41), a receptor for short-chain fatty acids, has been implicated in intestinal immune regulation, but its contribution to colitis and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the susceptibility of GPR41-deficient ( Gpr41 -/- ) mice to dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis. Gpr41 -/- mice exhibited more severe colitis, including greater body weight loss and greater colon shortening, than littermate controls. Under antibiotic treatment, no statistically significant differences in colitis severity were detected between Gpr41 -/- mice and littermate controls. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene amplicon analysis revealed differences in gut microbial diversity and composition between Gpr41 -/- mice and littermate controls at steady state, with compositional differences also observed after DSS treatment. GPR41 deficiency was also associated with reduced fecal levels of the iron-binding proteins lipocalin-2 (LCN2) and lactoferrin (LTF) at steady state. Prophylactic administration of recombinant LCN2 was associated with numerically lower colitis severity in Gpr41 -/- mice, although the differences were not statistically significant. Together, these findings support a protective role for GPR41 in DSS-induced colitis and identify associated changes in iron-binding protein levels and gut microbiota composition.

Article.Title: Endocrine, clinical and oxidative stress profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a cross-sectional case-control study
Article.Authors: Ikram J.; Batool A.; Riaz N.; Tabassum T.; Aslam M.; Rehman M.; Haque M.; Naveed N.
Article.Abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a prevalent cause of infertility worldwide. This study aimed to assess endocrinological and biochemical alterations and analyze oxidative stress in women with PCOS. A cohort of PCOS patients was examined for various clinical manifestations. We investigated the levels of several key parameters, including antioxidants, hormones (Luteinizing Hormone, Follicle Stimulating Hormone, Estradiol, and Testosterone), and hematological parameters. The study revealed that PCOS patients showed significantly higher levels of testosterone, while LH levels were lower in the non-PCOS group. FSH concentration was reduced in the PCOS group. Antioxidant levels demonstrated statistically significant differences between PCOS and non-PCOS females. A majority of PCOS patients experienced symptoms such as hair loss, hirsutism and menstrual irregularities. Menarche occurred at an early age, with PCOS females experiencing it at 13 years. A substantial portion of the population (84%) reported experiencing pain during periods, yet only a small fraction (14%) were using medication for pain relief. Ultrasonography revealed findings of a thickened endometrium and multiple cysts ranging from 5 to 7 mm. The findings reveal substantial hormonal imbalances, elevated testosterone levels, and significant differences in luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone dynamics, underscoring the endocrinological complexity of PCOS. The high prevalence of distressing clinical manifestations and the underutilization of pain relief medication among PCOS patients emphasize the need for improved symptom management and healthcare interventions.

Article.Title: Quantum annealing for customer segmentation: a proof-of-concept QUBO framework for supply chain clustering
Article.Authors: Bouchet R.; Puchkova A.
Article.Abstract: This article investigates the potential of quantum clustering, specifically through quantum annealing, to enhance supply chain segmentation compared with classical K-Means. Using a proof-of-concept framework, clustering is translated into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimisation formulation, tested on customer datasets via both classical Simulated Annealing and D-Wave’s Leap hybrid solver, with penalty parameter optimisation introduced to address solver sensitivity. Performance is benchmarked against K-Means on runtime, accuracy metrics, and scalability, across dataset sizes from 200 to 5,000 points. Results show that while K-Means maintains superior inertia and stability, the hybrid quantum approach achieves faster solver-reported runtimes and, on a simplified 200-point, two-feature benchmark, delivers improved silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, Calinski-Harabasz, and Dunn scores once penalties are optimised — metrics which, it is noted, reward the balanced partitions structurally favoured by the pairwise QUBO objective. However, scalability remains constrained by current qubit capacity and solver access, limiting practical deployment beyond mid-sized datasets. The study concludes that classical methods remain dominant for industrial-scale segmentation; the demonstrated framework, penalty-optimisation pipeline, and objective-level analysis nonetheless provide a documented foundation, grounded in a customer segmentation case study, upon which future quantum-assisted supply chain clustering can build as hardware matures.

Article.Title: Aspect-grounded heterogeneous graph learning for explainable cross-domain recommendation
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Liu X.; Xu Z.; Ang M.; Ng K.; Kor A.
Article.Abstract: Personalized recommender systems are essential for mitigating information overload. However, existing approaches face challenges in fine-grained preference modeling, behaviorally relevant explanations, and cross-domain transfer. We propose Aspect-Grounded Heterogeneous Graph Learning (AGHGL), a recommendation framework that uses aspect-level sentiment semantics as a common basis for preference modeling, explanation, and cross-domain transfer. AGHGL constructs a heterogeneous sentiment graph integrating users, items, aspects, and opinion expressions, enabling relation-aware message passing and aspect-mediated preference modeling. A margin-based intervention-sensitivity objective couples attention-derived aspect importance with prediction changes under aspect masking, aligning explanations with prediction behavior. A dual-level aspect alignment mechanism facilitates cross-domain transfer by aligning aspect representations at semantic and graph-structural levels. Experiments on real-world datasets show that AGHGL consistently outperforms the evaluated baselines in recommendation accuracy, with larger relative gains under sparse and cold-start conditions in the target domain. Human evaluation indicates improved perceived explanatory quality, while intervention-based analysis shows that higher aspect importance is associated with larger prediction changes. These results suggest that the aspect-grounded framework provides a useful basis for jointly modeling recommendation, explanation, and cross-domain transfer within the evaluated settings.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cross-domain recommendation; heterogeneous graph learning; explainable recommendation; cold-start recommendation; personalized recommendation systems; preference modeling

Article.Title: His-tag-directed, stable conjugation of proteins via [CoIII(NTA/IDA)(CO3)]2−/− reagents
Article.Authors: Benk A.; Seneca S.; Comba P.; Spatz J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Site-selective conjugation of proteins remains an important tool in biological research, medical engineering as well as the production of biopharmaceutical products and biosensors. However, current methodologies still suffer from one or more drawbacks such as a potential reduced protein functionality, lack of stability, or laboratory simplicity and versatility. Here we report a stable, His-tag-directed and physiological system for the conjugation of His-tagged proteins or an antibody by cobalt(III)-carbonate-mediated functionalization with nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA)-based or iminodiacetic acid (IDA)-based reagents ([Co III (NTA/IDA)(CO 3 )] 2−/− ). In comparison to the well-established metal(II)-NTA/IDA-mediated interactions, the application of low-spin octahedral dia​magnetic complexes of cobalt(III) results in a stable complex formation that is chemically inert towards various chelators and reduction agents. Thus, the usage of carbonatocobalt(III) complex reagents helps overcome current limitations by obviating the present H 2 O 2 -dependent oxidation step and was associated with an increase in coupling efficacy by about 200% and 100% for NTA-reagents and IDA-reagents, respectively. This allows for a simple and His-tag-directed protein or antibody conjugation under physiological conditions within a reasonable time without compromising conjugate stability, function, or protein binding efficacy.

Article.Title: A Wavelet-Change-Point framework for sequence-stratigraphic controls on reservoir quality and geomechanical evaluation: a case study of the Asmari-Ghar succession, SW Iran
Article.Authors: Falahatkhah O.; Serajamani M.; Jalilian P.; Kadkhodaie A.
Article.Abstract: The Oligo-Miocene Ghar-Asmari interval of the Dezful Embayment (SW Iran) is a proven reservoir, but its field-scale sequence-stratigraphic framework is poorly documented. We apply a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) multi-resolution analysis (Meyer wavelet, detail levels D1-D4) to gamma-ray logs of four wells in the Bahregansar and Hendijan fields. Combining D3-D4 local-wavelet-energy maxima with gamma-ray character and member boundaries, eight maximum flooding surfaces (MFS1-MFS8) were interpreted as depth-domain correlation surfaces. The number of surfaces is not an intrinsic output of the transform: energy-peak counts range from about 6 to 34 per well depending on the threshold, and eight emerges at the 90th-95th percentile. Two change-point algorithms were used as independent checks. Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection (BOCPD) matched 71.9% of the 32 surfaces within ± 8 m, which exceeds the agreement expected from random change points (47%, p = 0.001); Pruned Exact Linear Time (PELT) matched 43.8%, which is not distinguishable from chance (38%, p = 0.27). Reservoir quality, based on delivered effective porosity (PHIE) and water saturation (Sw) curves, ranks A > C > D > B (mean PHIE 0.159, 0.131, 0.099, 0.091) and this ranking is unchanged across 81 alternative cut-off combinations. Well A is the most ductile (Brittleness Index, BI = 36.5), whereas wells B, C and D are more brittle (BI = 53.1–61.5). Within the framework, the best reservoir quality and lowest BI occur in the upper packages (MFS5-MFS8, Ghar clastics) and deteriorate downward into the Asmari carbonates; this pattern persists when the MFS depths are perturbed by ± 4 m. Pore pressure from the Eaton sonic method is statistically indistinguishable from hydrostatic and cannot be calibrated, so a first-pass overburden-bounded mud-weight window of about 9.8 ppg (hydrostatic pore pressure) is given with a sensitivity range. The workflow is a screening tool for mixed siliciclastic-carbonate reservoirs of the Zagros foreland; its picks, petrophysical cut-offs and geomechanical values are uncalibrated against core, biostratigraphy or leak-off data.

Article.Title: Nutrients and consumer pressure influence coral and microbiome recovery following sequential marine heatwaves
Article.Authors: Vompe A.; Draney C.; Speare K.; Castañeda N.; Epstein H.; Silva D.; McLachlan R.; Kawahara M.; Adam T.; Burkepile D.; Sharpton T.; Thurber R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Current and projected ocean conditions under climate change necessitate an understanding of coral holobiont resilience, factors contributing to host survival during marine heatwaves (MHWs), and how corals can recover after MHWs subside. It is especially important to understand how MHWs may interact with local stressors such as nutrient pollution and overfishing. Here, we used a five-year field experiment to investigate the effects of nutrient enrichment and consumer exclusion on host mortality (percent dead tissue) and microbiome stochasticity (beta dispersion) of three coral species, Acropora retusa , Porites lobata , and Pocillopora spp., following MHWs in Moorea, French Polynesia. Our experiment tracked resident coral colonies and their microbiomes through time and captured two MHWs. The interaction of nutrient enrichment with consumer pressure played a significant, yet coral-specific role in host and microbiome recovery from sequential MHWs. Specifically, after the MHWs and under reduced consumer pressure, A. retusa and P. lobata experienced lower host mortality when subjected to ambient nutrient levels. Under high consumer pressure, A. retusa had lower host mortality when nutrient levels were elevated. However, under low consumer pressure, corals with a history of elevated nutrient exposure experienced higher mortality and microbiome stochasticity. On the other hand, Pocillopora spp. microbiomes were more homogenous under elevated nutrients and consumer pressure. Additionally, a reduction in a dominant P. lobata bacterial symbiont, Parendozoicomonas haliclonae , was strongly associated with increased host mortality during and after the MHWs. Overall, these results suggest that local nutrient inputs and fishing pressure can significantly alter reef recovery from MHWs, despite heat stress masking the impacts of these local-scale factors during MHWs.

Article.Title: Evaluating canine hip analysis: NANet model for norberg angle prediction
Article.Authors: Yao Y.; Li J.; Hansen G.; Yueh S.; Todhunter R.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: The Norberg angle (NA) plays a crucial role in evaluating hip joint conformation in canines by quantifying femoral head subluxation within the hip joint. It is a key metric for assessing hip joint quality and diagnosing canine hip dysplasia (CHD), a multifactorial orthopedic disease influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. While contemporary tools offer automated NA quantification, they still rely on substantial manual labeling and verification by trained veterinarians. Rather than focusing on workflow efficiency, the objective of this study is to develop a fully automated system capable of predicting the NA directly from radiographs, thereby reducing dependence on manual annotation and enabling consistent and reproducible assessment. To address the limited availability of diverse, high-quality annotated radiographs, our previous work incorporated diffusion-based generative models to augment the training dataset from 1,168 images to 2,693 images. Training with this expanded dataset resulted in substantial performance gains, with an average improvement of 35.3% across evaluation metrics. Our proposed NANet model outperformed state-of-the-art alternatives, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy. In particular, the predicted Norberg angle fell within 5 degrees of the reference measurement in 81.30% of test cases, approaching or surpassing the consistency observed among human annotators.

Article.Title: User interaction, perceived narrative quality and perceived spatiotemporal organization are associated with user experience in virtual reality museums
Article.Authors: Hu X.; Xu Y.
Article.Abstract: This study examined associations among user interaction (UE), perceived narrative quality (PNQ), perceived spatiotemporal organization (PSO), sensory experience (SA), and user experience (UX) in virtual reality (VR) museum exhibitions. The stimulus–organism–response framework and embodied cognition informed a model positioning UE, PNQ, and PSO as perceived exhibition attributes, SA as a multisensory organismic state, and UX as an overall evaluation. Cross-sectional survey data from 398 respondents with prior VR museum experience were analyzed using second-order structural equation modeling. The model showed acceptable overall fit (χ²/df = 1.592, CFI = 0.945, RMSEA = 0.039). UE, PNQ, and PSO were positively associated with both SA and UX, and SA was positively associated with UX. UE had the largest standardized direct coefficient for UX (β = 0.658), while PSO had the largest coefficient for SA (β = 0.400). The indirect estimates through SA were 0.116, 0.131, and 0.136, respectively; all bootstrap confidence intervals excluded zero. This study refines the application of the stimulus–organism–response framework to VR museums by distinguishing sensory experience from overall UX. The findings provide an empirical basis for evaluating interaction, narrative quality, spatiotemporal organization, and multisensory presentation as related aspects of exhibition design.

Article.Title: Analytical investigation of the fractional Gilson-Pickering equation: a study of bright and dark solitons
Article.Authors: Kumar R.; Jhala D.; Chouhan V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this article, we investigates about the fractional Gilson–Pickering equation by employing the Sine-Gordon expansion method (SGEM) in the framework of the beta derivative. This is a useful tool for analyzing complex nonlinear systems. The classical Gilson–Pickering equation is extended to its fractional form using the beta derivative to capture more realistic dynamics of nonlinear wave propagation. The obtained solutions include solitary wave (soliton), periodic, dark, bright soliton and complex combined dark-bright soliton solutions, which demonstrate the rich dynamical behavior of the fractional model. The influence of the fractional parameter are analyzed, showing that it significantly affects wave amplitude, width, and propagation characteristics. Furthermore, the obtained solutions are illustrated graphically through two-dimensional (2D), three-dimensional (3D), and contour plots, which provide clear insight into the physical behavior and evolution of the wave profiles. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of SGEM and highlight the impact of the fractional parameter on wave dynamics.

Article.Title: Age-dependent effects of titrating anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) intensity on motor sequence learning
Article.Authors: Frese A.; Ungureanu R.; Ghasemian-Shirvan E.; Melo L.; Xiong Y.; Beaupain M.; Kuo M.; Meesen R.; Nitsche M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Optimising the currently heterogenous efficacy of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) interventions for motor learning requires identifying stimulation parameters facilitating performance while accounting for age-related differences in baseline performance and mechanisms underlying neuroplasticity. We systematically explored anodal tDCS intensity effects on implicit motor sequence learning (IMSL) in young and older adults. The study utilised a randomised, double-blind, counterbalanced crossover design. Ninety-six healthy participants (48 young adults, 48 older adults) completed a serial reaction time task (SRTT) with online sham or anodal tDCS over M1 at intensities of 1, 2, and 3 mA. The next day, memory retention and consolidation were assessed in a recall test. Both age groups demonstrated IMSL across conditions. While 1 mA tDCS improved IMSL in young adults by reducing reaction times, higher intensities had no significant benefit compared to sham. In older adults, anodal tDCS did not affect general task performance compared to sham, but selective sequence learning was lower with 1mA tDCS. Young adults’ performance remained unchanged between learning and recall, indicating motor memory retention, but following anodal tDCS conditions, older adults showed faster reaction times in sequence blocks at recall compared to learning, indicating offline consolidation. The results demonstrate age-dependent and non-linear dose-dependent effects of anodal tDCS on IMSL. This underscores the necessity for age-adapted protocols for experimental and clinical tDCS applications. Future research should explore neurophysiological reasons for altered tDCS efficacy in older adults found in the present study.

Article.Title: Deep generative design and structure-based evaluation of celecoxib-inspired PTGS2/COX-2 ligands: a computational study in the context of adenomyosis-associated inflammation
Article.Authors: Üstünel S.; Ali N.
Article.Abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic inflammatory gynecological disorder in which cyclooxygenase-2 (PTGS2/COX-2)-derived prostaglandin signaling contributes to inflammation. This study asked whether deep learning-based generative modification of the celecoxib scaffold yields compounds with a more favorable predicted interaction profile at PTGS2. A generative platform combining a three-dimensional convolutional neural network with a conditional variational autoencoder returned twelve analogues, all carried forward without post hoc selection and examined by substructure analysis, docking at the experimentally defined ligand-binding site, pharmacophore comparison, ADMET and toxicity prediction, density functional theory, and 200 ns molecular dynamics with MM/GBSA estimation. The benzenesulfonamide group of celecoxib was retained in five of twelve analogues and the trifluoromethyl-pyrazole core in none, so the compounds are better described as scaffold-hopped analogues than as close derivatives. AI Analogue 2 returned the most favorable predicted binding energy (− 10.024 kcal/mol; celecoxib − 7.748 kcal/mol) and formed a persistent complex with an effective binding energy of − 51.89 kcal/mol. Its predicted pose lies along the main cyclooxygenase channel rather than the COX-2 side pocket occupied by celecoxib, so the two energies are not comparable as affinities. Redocking of the co-crystallized ligand gave a deviation of 1.924 Å and the celecoxib trajectory did not converge, indicating a rigid-receptor starting-pose artifact rather than a property of the generated compounds. Predicted blood–brain barrier permeability coincided with an active neurotoxicity call, identifying central exposure as the principal predicted liability. The study does not establish COX-2 inhibition, selectivity over COX-1, improved safety, or therapeutic activity in adenomyosis .

Article.Title: Adaptive EWMA control charts for monitoring dispersed count data: a COM-Poisson-based self-adjusting framework and applications
Article.Authors: Huda N.; Raza M.; Nawaz T.; Tahir M.; Emam W.; Hussain M.; Algahtani A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Control charts for count data are based on the Poisson (equi-dispersed), Negative Binomial (over-dispersed), or Binomial (under-dispersed) distributions. However, the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (COM-Poisson) distribution can flexibly model data with varying dispersion levels (under-, over-, and equi-dispersion). Over the past few years, adaptive control charts have gained attention compared to traditional Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) charts because of their ability to dynamically adjust the smoothing constant in response to process shifts. Existing adaptive EWMA charts are primarily restricted to Poisson-based models and therefore fail to provide a unified monitoring framework for under-, equi-, and over-dispersed count data. To overcome this gap, this study is the first to develop two Adaptive Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (AEWMA) control charts for the COM-Poisson distribution, allowing the smoothing constant to dynamically adjust estimated process shifts for a fixed rate parameter under-, equi-, and over-dispersed settings. The COMP-AEWMA-I chart is constructed using either of the two given smoothing strategies, whereas the COMP-AEWMA-II chart utilises dispersion-specific upper-tail quantiles for the COM-Poisson distribution to define intervals that govern the adaptive selection of the smoothing constant. The primary objectives of this study are to detect shifts promptly and to enhance process monitoring accuracy across various dispersion levels. Using the Monte Carlo simulation method, the performance of the proposed control charts is evaluated using key measures, including the average, standard deviation, and percentiles of run lengths for both zero- and steady-state cases. To assess the practical applicability, validity, and robustness of the proposed charts, real-life datasets from different fields are also used.

Article.Title: A dual-branch keypoint Transformer for continuous Korean Sign Language recognition
Article.Authors: Kim D.; Kang H.
Article.Abstract: Continuous Korean Sign Language recognition requires practical models that capture manual and non-manual articulation. We propose KDS-Former, a compact dual-branch keypoint Transformer that encodes hand and body–face motion, fuses the temporal representations, and predicts gloss sequences using connectionist temporal classification. On KSL-Guide, KDS-Former-S achieved word error rates (WERs) of \(6.33 \pm 1.68\) % and \(7.61 \pm 2.09\) % under seen-signer/unseen-sentence and unseen-signer/unseen-sentence protocols, respectively, using 2.59 million parameters and 1.91 model-compute GFLOPs. KDS-Former-M achieved \(5.68 \pm 1.98\) % and \(6.27 \pm 2.24\) % using 14.75 million parameters and 9.93 model-compute GFLOPs. The larger systems of Min et al. and TEMPO achieved lower mean WERs across three runs, whereas KDS-Former required fewer parameters, lower model-compute GFLOPs, and lower peak GPU memory usage. Under both primary protocols, the full KDS-Former-S achieved lower mean WER than all five controlled ablation variants, although the unseen-signer/unseen-sentence single-branch result showed substantial between-run variability. Under controlled input corruption, both KDS-Former variants showed smaller mean WER degradation than ST-GCN. These results position KDS-Former as an efficiency-oriented, model-level alternative rather than an accuracy-leading method. Signer-generalization results are limited by evaluation on only two held-out signers, and the reported latency was measured on an RTX 4090 without upstream keypoint extraction, preprocessing, or CTC decoding; broader signer-disjoint and hardware-specific validation is therefore required.

Article.Title: Gradient affinity from a shared encoder guides multitask grouping of ADMET endpoints measured on largely disjoint compounds
Article.Authors: Koo S.; Ko S.; Seong S.
Article.Abstract: Multi-task learning can improve ADMET prediction, but choosing which endpoints to learn together often relies on trial and error. Existing task-compatibility measures compare tasks on shared compounds, an assumption rarely met in ADMET data, where endpoints are measured on different compounds. TAG-lite, a gradient-based workflow, estimates task compatibility even when tasks share no compounds. Across 27 Therapeutics Data Commons endpoints, whose pairs shared a median 0.99% of compounds, affinities from one shared AttentiveFP encoder, averaged over three seeds, defined seven endpoint groups. Measured after a brief warm-up, before group-wise training, affinity tracked group-level transfer ( r = 0.881, permutation P = 0.006); in an exploratory task-level analysis it predicted transfer direction (area under the curve 0.745, 95% CI 0.515–0.945). Below approximately 5% compound overlap it no longer tracked magnitude, while task-level direction discrimination was preserved. Affinity-guided grouping outperformed single random, anti-affinity, pharmacokinetic-category and task-type partitions. The only large negative-transfer case among affinity-admitted endpoints shared almost no compounds with its partners, motivating a screening rule combining affinity and compound overlap; after this post-hoc exclusion, gradient surgery numerically improved every endpoint in the admitted groups.

Article.Title: Implementation challenges of eliminating preferential currency in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector
Article.Authors: Mojtabaeian S.; Bayati M.; Delavari S.; Khoshnoud M.; Lotfi F.
Article.Abstract: Before the implementation of Darooyar, Iran’s pharmaceutical sector relied heavily on preferential foreign-exchange allocation for imported medicines and pharmaceutical inputs, while the system faced broader challenges related to financing, affordability, and medicine supply. In this context, the Darooyar plan was introduced to eliminate preferential currency and replace it with a targeted pharmaceutical subsidy mechanism intended to improve the sustainability and transparency of pharmaceutical financing. This study aimed to explore the challenges associated with eliminating preferential currency in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector, with particular attention to financing, governance, stakeholder relationships, and pharmaceutical supply-chain pressures. A qualitative study employing descriptive content analysis was conducted in 2025 to explore the challenges associated with eliminating preferential currency in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector, with particular attention to financing, governance, stakeholder relationships, and pharmaceutical supply-chain pressures. Participants included policymakers, executive managers, insurance specialists, pharmacy technical officers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers. Purposive sampling with a snowball approach was applied, yielding 27 participants. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews using an interview guide. Data collection and analysis were performed concurrently using Atlas.ti software. Five overarching themes, 21 subthemes, and 73 codes were identified regarding the challenges of implementing the policy. The main themes comprised: (1) Weaknesses in policy design, management, planning, and implementation; (2) Reported irregularities, misconduct, and inadequate oversight within the pharmaceutical system; (3) stakeholder dissatisfaction and constraints; (4) financial problems across the pharmaceutical supply chain; and (5) Macroeconomic and policy pressures on pharmaceutical system sustainability. Recommendations include strengthening technological infrastructure (integrated insurance systems and reliable internet), targeted education and communication, establishing independent expert oversight, ensuring sustainable budget allocation with timely online payments, and conducting pilot implementations with continuous evaluation prior to nationwide rollout.

Article.Title: A federated learning framework for cyber-resilient defense in EV-integrated microgrids
Article.Authors: Gholami J.; Yousefi B.; Shirazi A.; Yazdani A.
Article.Abstract: Continuous deployment of moving target defense in modern power grids is often limited to intermittent use in practice because deliberately perturbing the network to expose stealthy cyber attacks pushes the dispatch away from its economic optimum and inflicts an operating-cost penalty that is paid with certainty in every hour of operation, whereas the attacks it prevents are sporadic. In the cluster studied here this penalty amounts to about 298 dollars per hour, roughly 1.4 percent of the base operating cost and 6.2 percent in the most congested microgrid, or about 2.6 million dollars per year. This paper proposes a unified cyber-physical architecture that absorbs most of this penalty while enforcing a minimum subspace-separation margin for attack exposure and preserving the data sovereignty of every participant. The defense layer selects each reactance reconfiguration through a decision-based multi-objective optimizer that simultaneously maximizes the geometric separation needed to expose hidden attacks, minimizes the induced operating cost, and minimizes the physical actuation effort of the flexible-transmission devices. The cost penalty created by the reconfiguration is then absorbed by mobilizing the bidirectional flexibility of electric vehicle fleets, which are dispatched precisely at the buses where the defense creates artificial congestion. Detection of the exposed attacks is delegated to a federated detector that is trained collaboratively across the cluster by exchanging only model parameters, so that raw measurements never leave a local microgrid. The framework is evaluated on a cluster of five interconnected IEEE 30-bus microgrids, each hosting five charging stations with one hundred electric vehicles. The results show that full participation of the vehicle fleet reduces the cluster defense penalty from about 298 to roughly 16 dollars per hour, a reduction close to 95 percent that leaves a small residual cost, while the federated detector reaches a detection area under the curve of about 0.92 and outperforms an isolated, data-scarce local detector. The exposed attacks raise the detection statistic far above its alarm threshold, supporting reliable and economically sustainable protection.

Article.Title: Multimodal Sentiment-Symptom Disentanglement network for interpretable mental health classification from text and visual data
Article.Authors: Reddy K.; Gantayat S.
Article.Abstract: Mental health disorders manifest through intertwined affective and symptomatic signals that are difficult to separate using unimodal or naively fused multimodal models, often producing classifiers that conflate general sentiment polarity with clinically meaningful symptom markers and offer little insight into their own decision process. This paper proposes a Multimodal Sentiment-Symptom Disentanglement Network (MSSD-Net) that explicitly decomposes textual and visual representations into two orthogonal latent subspaces — a sentiment-affect subspace capturing general emotional tone and a symptom-specific subspace capturing clinically relevant behavioral and linguistic markers (e.g., psychomotor cues, facial action units, negation and rumination patterns in text). Modality-specific transformer encoders first extract joint text and visual embeddings, which are passed through a disentanglement module trained with a combination of mutual-information minimization, orthogonality regularization, and adversarial subspace classifiers to enforce separation between the two latent streams. A cross-modal attention fusion layer then recombines the disentangled symptom subspaces from both modalities for downstream mental health classification (e.g., depression, anxiety severity levels). At the same time, the sentiment subspace is retained only as an auxiliary, interpretability-supporting signal. To ensure clinical transparency, the framework incorporates a post-hoc and intrinsic explainability layer that projects attention weights and subspace activations back onto input tokens and facial regions, yielding symptom-attributed saliency maps rather than sentiment-confounded heatmaps. Experiments on benchmark multimodal mental health datasets demonstrate that MSSD-Net achieves 89.4% F1-score over E-DAIC and state-of-the-art multimodal baselines, while substantially improving the faithfulness and clinician-rated interpretability of the generated explanations. Ablation studies reveal that disentangling sentiment and symptom is responsible for the performance gain and improved interpretability in joint entangled fusion. The findings indicate that disentangled multimodal architectures can serve as promising, clinically sound methods for automated mental health screening from naturalistic, real-world data.

Article.Title: Global prevalence of the double burden of malnutrition among adults in 80 countries using WHO STEPs data
Article.Authors: Hasan M.; Biswas T.; Kohlberg S.; Niki A.; Musavi Z.; Momtahin A.; Mostari S.; Chowdhury M.; Townsend N.
Article.Abstract: The double burden of malnutrition (DBM), the coexistence of underweight and overweight/obesity within the same population, is a growing global health challenge, yet its population-level scale has not been comprehensively quantified. We analysed individual-level data from 80 nationally representative WHO STEPS surveys conducted between 2004 and 2024 among adults aged ≥ 18 years across seven WHO regions ( n = 283,426). Prevalence estimates were survey-weighted, age-standardised, and pooled using a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis; sex disparities and temporal trends were also examined. Global pooled DBM prevalence was 59.5% (95% CI 54.6–64.2%), ranging from 23.6% in Rwanda to 93.7% in American Samoa, and was driven mainly by overweight/obesity (51.0%) rather than underweight (4.1%). DBM prevalence was higher in women than in men in 70 of 80 countries (88%), with a median absolute sex gap of 10.4% points. Regional prevalence ranged from 40.9% in sub-Saharan Africa to 83.3% in Oceania, and rose monotonically with national income, from 37.3% in low-income to 77.6% in high-income countries; no significant temporal trend was observed. These findings show that population-level DBM affects most adults worldwide, is driven predominantly by excess weight, and disproportionately burdens women, underscoring the need for integrated, sex-disaggregated nutrition policies that address both extremes of malnutrition simultaneously.

Article.Title: Activated platelets release extracellular vesicles with a distinct thromboinflammatory protein signature
Article.Authors: Guerreiro E.; Latysheva N.; Bhandari S.; Wikan V.; Brodin E.; Brækkan S.; Hansen J.; Snir O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) from activated platelets possess a shifted biomolecular profile and enhanced procoagulant activity. However, the specific EV proteome and surface antigens characterizing these vesicles in acute thrombotic events remain poorly defined. We aimed to identify a thromboinflammatory PDEV surface signature and evaluate its diagnostic potential in deep vein thrombosis (DVT). PDEVs from control or TRAP6-activated washed platelets were analysed by mass spectrometry (MS). Candidate protein markers were validated on the surface of washed platelets PDEVs and plasma EVs from DVT patients, symptomatic non-DVT patients, and healthy controls using an in-house immunocapture bead-based flow cytometry assay. Platelet activation enriched 129 proteins in the PDEV proteome, primarily mediators of coagulation and inflammation. While MS identified high levels of vWF and Factor V, flow cytometry confirmed that CD41, CD62P, CCL5, and CD9 are specifically enriched on the PDEV surface. An integrated multi-marker panel (CD41, CD9, CD151, PF4, FV, CD62P) successfully discriminated DVT patients from healthy controls, but not between DVT and symptomatic non-DVT patients. In conclusion, activation reconfigures the EV proteome and surface into a distinct thromboinflammatory signature. While this signature captures systemic platelet activation in symptomatic patients, further refinement is required to achieve clot-specific diagnostic utility.

Article.Title: Uncovering the virome of sweet cherry using VANA-based high-throughput sequencing and RT-PCR in Türkiye
Article.Authors: Tunç B.; Çağlayan K.; Roumi V.; Rynard J.
Article.Abstract: In the last decade, high-throughput sequencing approaches have been increasingly applied in plant virology. In this study, virion-associated nucleic acid (VANA)-based high-throughput sequencing (HTS) was performed on a pooled sample of 29 sweet cherries ( Prunus avium L.) exhibiting virus-like symptoms in Osmaniye Province, Türkiye. Based on viruses detected by VANA-based sequencing, 259 samples collected from major cherry-growing provinces were tested by virus-specific RT-PCR analyses to confirm the presence and prevalence of these viruses. HTS and RT-PCR analyses confirmed the presence of Prune dwarf virus ( Ilarvirus PDV , PDV), Cherry green ring mottle virus ( Robigovirus viridiavii , CGRMV), Little cherry virus 1 ( Velarivirus nanoavii, LChV-1), Cherry necrotic rusty mottle virus ( Robigovirus necroavii, CNRMV), Cherry latent virus 1 (CLV-1), and Cherry virus Turkey (CVTR). Among the samples tested, CNRMV and CLV-1 were detected in Türkiye for the first time, and CLV-1 was the most widespread of the three viruses surveyed, followed by CGRMV and CNRMV. Prunus virus F was detected only by HTS and requires further confirmation. VANA-based HTS followed by targeted RT-PCR confirmation proved useful for virus detection in sweet cherry and provides data for virological surveys and certification programs.

Article.Title: Study on the deformation characteristics and fracture development laws of the shaft coal pockets inner wall
Article.Authors: Liu M.; Wen Z.
Article.Abstract: The shaft coal pocket is a critical component of the transportation system in underground coal mines, its deformation or structural damage poses a direct threat to the safety and continuity of mine operations. As the shaft wall are semi-hidden structures, the deformation and damage are difficult to detect, so the research about the mechanisms of deformation and damage lags behind the development of the coal industry. During the load and unload of coal (gangue) in the shaft coal pocket, the repeated load-unload and dynamic impact of loose granular particles on the bunker wall lead to a complex and variable deformation and damage process. This paper employs comprehensive research methods, including theoretical analysis, mechanical experiments, similarity simulations, and numerical analysis. Study the deformation and damage mechanisms of the shaft wall in underground coal mines. Reveal the deformation and failure mechanism of the shaft coal pocket inner wall. The research indicate that deformation and damage of shaft wall under combined load can be divided into four stages: elastic deformation, plastic deformation, crack propagation and structural instability. The damage mechanisms of shaft wall are primarily related to the applied loads. Once under prolonged external load, the mechanical state of the shaft wall changes, initially cause localized damage. As the damage progresses, cracks and fissures develop. When the stress on the shaft coal inner wall exceeds the allowable stress of the concrete material, structural instability and failure occur. When the primary load on the shaft walls is from internal loose granular particles, the failure type is predominantly shear failure. When the primary load comes from weak rock layers on the exterior, the failure type is primarily tensile failure. When both factors act simultaneously, it results in combined tensile-shear failure.
