Article.Title: A heterogeneous deep-learning ensemble for assistive 11-class classification of kidney diseases using transmission electron microscopy
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Liu J.; Zhang Q.; Li X.; Liu Z.; Li J.; Wang H.; Wang W.; Wang H.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) aids glomerular disease diagnosis. However, single-image classification under patient-independent evaluation remains uncertain. We classified 11 kidney diseases using 60,509 quality-controlled TEM images from 8,250 patients, partitioned by patient into training (5,940 patients), meta-calibration (Meta-Cal; 661), and held-out test (1,649) sets. Five backbones (EfficientNet-B4, ViT-B/16, Swin-B, ConvNeXt-B, and DeiT-B) were trained using patient-grouped nested folds. Training-set out-of-fold predictions were used to fit weighted soft voting and logistic-regression stacking with eightfold test-time augmentation. Meta-calibration compared these two prespecified candidates and supported calibration and referral-rule assessment. Single-image accuracy, macro-F1 score, balanced accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient, and macro-AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) were 0.444, 0.361 (bootstrap mean: 0.360; 95% confidence interval: 0.344–0.379), 0.354, 0.345, and 0.793, respectively. Averaging probabilities across images of 1,642 single-diagnosis patients yielded an accuracy of 0.610 and macro-F1 score of 0.507; 7 patients with discordant labels were excluded only from this aggregation. These results were not comparable with image-level-split estimates, including our original submission. Temperature scaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.059 to 0.028. The prespecified referral target (Meta-Cal autonomous accuracy ≥ 0.90) was not reached, and therefore no operating threshold was selected. The results provide a patient-independent benchmark, not evidence for autonomous diagnosis.

Article.Title: Outcomes of Carlevale-type scleral-fixated intraocular lenses as a stable platform in silicone oil-filled eyes: a multicenter study
Article.Authors: Wolfram L.; Wahib E.; Nasyrov E.; Bodenbender J.; Kunzmann B.; Januschowski K.; Dimopoulos S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To evaluate functional, refractive, and morphological outcomes, and silicone oil (SiO)-related complications of Carlevale-type scleral-fixated intraocular lens (C-IOL) implantation with SiO tamponade. This multicenter case series included nine eyes that underwent C-IOL implantation combined with SiO tamponade, either simultaneously during primary retinal detachment surgery (56%), or sequentially, with the C-IOL already in place before retinal detachment repair and SiO tamponade (44%), across three centers. SiO tamponade consisted of standard 5000 cSt silicone oil (78%) or heavy fluorinated silicone oil (Densiron 68, 22%). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), spherical equivalent (SE), intraocular pressure (IOP), SiO position, C-IOL stability, and adverse events were recorded preoperatively and at follow-up. Median age was 75.0 years (IQR 67.0–79.0); 67% were male. Median follow-up was 36.7 weeks (IQR 25.4–55.0). BCVA improved from 2.3 logMAR (IQR 1.3–2.3) preoperatively to 0.9 logMAR (IQR 0.9–1.8) at last follow-up (median ΔBCVA − 0.6) in 67% of eyes. Median SE remained near emmetropia, though with individual variability and available in only 6/9 eyes at ≥ 36 weeks. No IOP measurement exceeded 21 mmHg. Anatomical success was achieved in 78% of eyes. No clinically documented C-IOL decentration, tilt, or dislocation occurred. SiO was explanted in 33% of eyes at a median of 25.4 weeks (IQR 16.7–31.1); the remaining eyes retained tamponade through last follow-up. C-IOL opacification occurred in 22% (one explantation). Anterior SiO migration occurred in 44%, mostly limited to a small, clinically non-significant bubble; diffuse migration occurred in one eye only after explantation. Anterior-chamber irrigation was required in 22%. The combined surgical management of vitreoretinal surgery, SiO tamponade, and C-IOL fixation was associated with visual improvement, high anatomical success, and no clinically documented C-IOL decentration, tilt, or dislocation, although C-IOL opacification and anterior SiO migration warrant further prospective, comparative evaluation.

Article.Title: Influence of service life and system boundary modelling on the life cycle environmental performance of SCM-based concrete
Article.Authors: Mishra A.; Mishra L.; Gaur A.; Raj A.
Article.Abstract: Cement-intensive concrete production contributes significantly to global emissions, prompting wide use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) to reduce clinker content. However, the long-term environmental performance of SCM-based concrete is strongly governed by durability, which directly influences service life and maintenance requirements. Life cycle assessment (LCA) of concrete is often limited to cradle-to-gate boundaries, neglecting these durability-driven effects, and the combined influence of service life and system boundary modelling on environmental performance remains insufficiently explored for reinforced concrete (RC) infrastructure under Indian coastal conditions. To address this, four M50 grade concrete mixes (OPC, GGBS50, FA30, and SF11.9) are comparatively assessed by integrating chloride-induced service life prediction with LCA under cradle-to-gate, cradle-to-service life, and cradle-to-grave system boundaries. The predicted service life follows the order SF11.9 > FA30 > GGBS50 > OPC. Under the cradle-to-gate boundary, SCM-based concretes show 1–23% lower environmental impacts than OPC across midpoint categories due to reduced clinker content. Incorporating service life through the cradle-to-service life boundary yields substantially higher reductions of 48–63%, highlighting the strong influence of durability on environmental performance. Under the cradle-to-grave boundary, which accounts for repair interventions over a 100-year period, reductions decrease to 17–33% due to additional maintenance-related material consumption. These findings show that cradle-to-gate assessment alone inadequately represents long-term environmental performance, as durability governs both impact distribution and maintenance demand. Cradle-to-service life and cradle-to-grave approaches thus provide a more relevant basis for durability-oriented design and lifecycle decision-making in RC infrastructure under coastal exposure.

Article.Title: Foliar phenylalanine application modulates biochemical traits and antioxidant enzyme activities in strawberry under reduced nutrient solution supply
Article.Authors: Fazli F.; Hassanpour H.; Manda-Hakki K.
Article.Abstract: Strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) productivity and biochemical fruit attributes can be adversely affected by reduced water and nutrient solution supply. Phenylalanine (Phe), a precursor of the phenylpropanoid pathway, may modify these responses. This study investigated foliar Phe effects on fruit yield, biochemical attributes, and antioxidant-related responses of strawberry cv. ‘Sabrina’ under greenhouse soilless conditions. The experiment used a factorial completely randomized design with three Phe concentrations (0, 500, and 1000 µM) and two nutrient solution regimes (200 and 160 mL plant − 1 every other day), with three biological replicates. The interaction between Phe and nutrient solution regime significantly affected several biochemical and antioxidant traits. The highest total phenolic content (4.75 mg GAE g − 1 FW), total flavonoid content (2.22 mg QE g − 1 FW), DPPH radical-scavenging activity (82.25%), and FRAP value (27.44 mg Fe 2+ g − 1 FW) occurred at 500 µM Phe under 200 mL. In contrast, the highest total anthocyanin content (0.797 mg C3G g − 1 FW) occurred at 1000 µM Phe under 160 mL. Phe and nutrient solution regime independently affected fruit yield: the highest mean yield was at 1000 µM Phe (650.19 g plant − 1 ), and yield under 160 mL was 560.14 g plant − 1 versus 620.30 g plant − 1 under 200 mL (9.7% lower). PPO activity was lowest (0.035 U g − 1 FW) at 500 µM Phe under 200 mL and highest (0.15 U g − 1 FW) in untreated plants under 160 mL. SOD activity was affected independently by Phe and nutrient solution regime, whereas CAT, APX, and POD depended on their interaction. Overall, foliar Phe modified biochemical traits and antioxidant-related responses, but effects varied with trait, Phe concentration, and nutrient solution regime. Under the tested conditions, 500 µM Phe was associated with the highest values for several biochemical traits, whereas 1000 µM Phe produced the highest mean yield. These findings suggest potential applications of Phe in soilless strawberry production under reduced nutrient solution supply. However, the study was limited to one cultivar and one greenhouse environment, and mechanisms were not directly measured; therefore, validation across cultivars and growing conditions is required.

Article.Title: Adaptive robust fractional-order sliding mode fault-tolerant control for quadrotor UAV inspection
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Gu Y.; Yu Z.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents an adaptive robust fractional-order sliding mode fault-tolerant control strategy for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles subject to external disturbances, partial actuator effectiveness loss, and input constraints. The position and attitude sliding variables combine regularized integral feedback with finite-band fractional memory. A velocity-based observer estimates the lumped effects of disturbances and effectiveness loss without requiring the effectiveness values. Bounded adaptation regulates the robust gains, while integral-state conditioning uses force-projection and command-clipping information to constrain integral accumulation. These mechanisms are incorporated into a thrust–attitude cascade with reference filtering and continuous input shaping. Under the stated operating-domain and complete-residual bounds, the distance of the sliding variables to an invariant neighborhood decays exponentially, and the tracking errors are ultimately bounded. In the considered 130-s inspection simulation, the position root mean square errors are 0.02904, 0.02190, and 0.01500 m along the x , y , and z axes, respectively. The simulations illustrate tracking performance under the specified disturbances and effectiveness-loss schedule; comparisons concern the explicitly stated controller configurations.

Article.Title: Interactive effects of seed priming and salinity stress on growth, yield, and nutrient dynamics in wheat genotypes (Triticum aestivum L.)
Article.Authors: Monalisa N/A.; Tasnim M.; Mannan M.; Shohel M.; Abusor M.; Baque M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Salinity severely constrains wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) productivity in salt-affected environments. A split-split plot field experiment at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, Dhaka (November 2017–March 2018) evaluated three wheat genotypes (ESWYT 5, ESWYT 6, and BARI Gom 28), three NaCl-imposed irrigation-solution salinity levels (0, 10, and 15 dS m⁻¹), and three seed-priming treatments (no priming, 5% PEG-6000, and 2% mannitol). Salinity at 15 dS m⁻¹ reduced grain yield by 29%, filled grains spike⁻¹ by 45%, 1000-seed weight by 17%, and post-harvest soil available phosphorus by 40% relative to the non-saline control. ESWYT 5 consistently outperformed BARI Gom 28 across the measured growth, yield, and nutrient traits. Based on the directly analysed salinity × priming marginal means, 5% PEG-6000 increased grain yield by 118% over the unprimed treatment at 15 dS m⁻¹ (4.572 vs. 2.10 t ha⁻¹), while S0P1 produced the highest salinity × priming grain-yield mean (5.45 t ha⁻¹). PEG-6000 osmopriming combined with a salt-tolerant genotype therefore represents a promising strategy warranting validation under naturally saline coastal field conditions.

Article.Title: Prediction of flavonoid components and antioxidant activity in tangerine peel based on machine learning
Article.Authors: Chi C.; Yang C.; Cui D.
Article.Abstract: Tangerine peel is a valuable citrus by-product enriched with flavonoids and antioxidant compounds, possessing considerable potential for applications in the functional food and nutraceutical industries. Conventional analytical techniques for flavonoid determination are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for high-throughput quality evaluation. This study developed a machine learning-based prediction framework for the rapid assessment of major flavonoid components and antioxidant activity in tangerine peel using physicochemical characteristics and near-infrared spectral information. A total of 320 tangerine peel samples were analyzed, incorporating moisture content, soluble solids, color parameters, total phenolic content, and spectral variables as predictors. Hesperidin, nobiletin, and tangeretin concentrations were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography, while antioxidant activity was determined using the DPPH radical scavenging assay. Three machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were evaluated and compared. The results demonstrated that XGBoost exhibited the highest predictive accuracy, achieving coefficient of determination (R²) values of 0.945, 0.921, and 0.907 for hesperidin, nobiletin, and tangeretin, respectively. Antioxidant activity prediction achieved an R² of 0.959, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.73%, which demonstrates the reliability and generalization capability of the model. Feature importance analysis revealed that total phenolic content (24.8%), absorbance at 1450 nm (18.6%), and peel color parameter a* (12.9%) were the most influential predictors. Compared with conventional laboratory analysis, the proposed framework reduced analytical time from approximately 51.6 min per sample to less than 2.5 s while maintaining prediction accuracy above 95%. These findings confirm that machine learning integrated with spectral sensing technologies provides an efficient, accurate, and non-destructive strategy for predicting flavonoid composition and antioxidant capacity, offering substantial potential for intelligent quality control and high-value utilization of citrus processing by-products.

Article.Title: Comparing concurrent associations between health behavior theory constructs and mask wearing during and after a mask mandate
Article.Authors: Arthur K.; Eksin C.; Pandit A.; Ndeffo-Mbah M.; Smallman R.; Fields S.
Article.Abstract: While studies have used health behavior theories to examine COVID-19 preventive behavior, few have examined which theoretical framework’s constructs best predict mask-wearing behavior across contexts (e.g. mask mandate versus no mandate; public setting versus private setting). The current study evaluates the relative concurrent predictive performance of construct sets associated with four health behavior theories (Theory of Planned Behavior, Health Belief Model, Social Cognitive Theory, and Transtheoretical Model) for mask-wearing during and after a mask mandate in Texas. Social Cognitive Theory constructs were consistently among the strongest-performing individual theory-based construct sets and yielded the lowest prediction error in all but one context, although Transtheoretical Model constructs often performed comparably. An integrative model composed of constructs from all four theories provided the lowest prediction error across contexts. Further analysis of the Social Cognitive Theory construct set suggested that, relative to context-specific behavioral baselines, these constructs provided greater predictive information post-mandate than during the mandate. Our findings highlight the importance of social and policy context in understanding the predictive information provided by health behavior constructs and suggest that multiple theoretical frameworks may contribute complementary information for understanding preventive behavior.

Article.Title: Comparison of perceived clinical leadership needs among staff nurses and nurse managers in Iran: a cross-sectional correlational study
Article.Authors: Taghizadeh N.; Mehri S.; Mirzaei A.; Habibi Soola A.
Article.Abstract: Clinical leadership is essential for ensuring quality patient care and optimizing healthcare outcomes. However, perceptions of leadership needs may vary by organizational role. This study compared perceived clinical leadership needs between staff nurses and nurse managers and identified associated socio-professional factors. We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional study in 2024 across five teaching hospitals in Ardabil, Iran. Participants included 374 staff nurses (selected via proportional stratified random sampling) and 76 nurse managers (recruited via census). We collected data using a demographic questionnaire and the Persian version of the Clinical Leadership Needs Analysis (CLeeNA) instrument. We analyzed data in SPSS v.26 using ANCOVA and separate dummy-coded multiple linear regression models. Nurse managers reported significantly greater perceived clinical leadership needs than staff nurses (Adjusted Mean: 302.32 vs. 258.18; F = 165.39, p < 0.001). In the staff nurses’ model (R2 = 0.239, p < 0.001), holding a Master’s degree or higher was the only significant categorical predictor (β = 0.465, p < 0.001). In the nurse managers’ model (R2 = 0.668, p < 0.001), being married was associated with higher perceived needs (β = 0.194, p = 0.047), whereas non-permanent employment statuses (Contractual and Commitment) were associated with significantly lower perceived needs than permanent employment ( p ≤ 0.009). Perceived clinical leadership needs differ substantially between staff nurses and nurse managers. Rather than reflecting objectively assessed leadership competence, these differences likely arise from role-specific organizational responsibilities. Professional factors—including nurses’ education and managers’ employment security—are statistically associated with these perceptions. Leadership development programs should be tailored to account for these distinct organizational roles.

Article.Title: Evolution, convergence, and determinants of tourism eco-efficiency in Hainan Province and six ASEAN economies, 2010–2022
Article.Authors: Zheng L.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Tourism eco-efficiency benchmarks rarely place Chinese provincial destinations alongside ASEAN sovereign economies despite overlapping carbon footprints and divergent policy regimes. We assemble a balanced panel of Hainan Province and six ASEAN economies (Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam) over 2010–2022 (91 observations) and combine Super-SBM, rolling-window Malmquist, panel MLE/Tobit, and synthetic control. The seven units settle into three persistent efficiency tiers: Hainan and Singapore at or above the frontier, Thailand and the Philippines in a volatile middle band, and Malaysia, Vietnam, and Indonesia well below. Sigma-divergence and conditional beta-convergence coexist (β = −0.0691, p < 0.05; half-life about 10 years), pointing to convergence toward heterogeneous steady states rather than a common one. Malmquist decomposition attributes most pre-2020 productivity improvement to operational catch-up rather than frontier innovation; pandemic-era estimates are interpreted with caution given an asymmetric floor correction. Free-trade-zone presence is negatively associated with eco-efficiency on average; the interaction with internet penetration is directionally consistent with a digital-infrastructure complementarity reading but imprecisely estimated under wild cluster bootstrap at G = 7. After a difference-in-differences adjustment for imperfect pre-treatment fit, the Hainan-specific advantage post-2020 is approximately + 0.43 on the super-efficiency score; given the cross-border donor pool, the synthetic control evidence should be read as suggestive rather than conclusive. The findings indicate that Hainan Free Trade Port-type regimes carry short-run efficiency frictions and that digital infrastructure and trade liberalisation are best built in parallel.

Article.Title: Cross-sectional study of facial bone wall thickness of maxillary incisors in healthy and periodontitis populations based on CBCT analysis
Article.Authors: Hu Z.; Liu Q.; Guo J.; Abulizi A.; Liu Z.; Jin S.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the differences in facial bone wall thickness (FBT) of maxillary incisors between healthy and periodontitis populations and to explore potential influencing factors, providing a theoretical basis for immediate implant placement. A retrospective study was conducted using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) to analyze the facial bone wall thickness of 300 patients. According to the alveolar bone loss (ABL) level, patients were classified into healthy, mild, moderate, and severe groups. FBT was measured at three positions: alveolar crest (FBT1), mid-root (FBT2), and root apex (FBT3). The sagittal root position was classified into three types. Multiple linear regression analysis was performed to identify influencing factors. A total of 300 patients were enrolled, including 177 males (59.0%) and 123 females (41.0%). The median FBT1 values for the healthy, mild, moderate, and severe groups were 1.03 mm, 0.93 mm, 0.63 mm, and 0.55 mm, respectively ( P < 0.001); the median FBT3 values were 1.88 mm, 1.54 mm, 1.38 mm, and 1.24 mm, respectively ( P = 0.002). For root positions, the median FBT3 values for Type 1 (palatal/central), Type 2 (slightly labial), and Type 3 (obviously labial) were 2.47 mm, 1.81 mm, and 1.00 mm, respectively ( P < 0.001). Multiple linear regression showed that ABL had a significant negative effect on FBT1 (beta=−0.165, P = 0.004), root angle alpha had a significant negative effect on FBT3 (beta=−0.426, P < 0.001), and gender had a significant effect on FBT3 (beta = 0.198, P < 0.001). Significant differences exist in facial bone wall thickness of maxillary incisors between healthy and periodontitis populations. Periodontitis patients generally have thinner facial bone walls than healthy populations, and bone wall thickness is significantly affected by the level of alveolar bone loss. Higher alveolar bone loss is associated with thinner bone walls. Gender, age, and root position also influence bone wall thickness to a certain extent.

Article.Title: Association between social networks and central sensitization-related symptoms among residents of a Japanese community: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Abe Y.; Endo M.; Kono K.; Iwata N.; Haruyama Y.; Kobashi G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social networks may be associated with central sensitization-related symptoms, but community-based evidence is limited. We examined associations of total, family, and friend network scores with elevated symptom burden among 1813 residents of Mibu Town, Japan, in a cross-sectional study. The Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) and six-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6) were used; CSI ≥ 40 indicated elevated symptom burden rather than a clinical diagnosis. Overall, 135 participants (7.4%) met this threshold. Participants with CSI ≥ 40 had lower social network scores than those with CSI < 40. In multivariable analyses, higher total network scores were associated with lower odds of CSI ≥ 40 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85–0.92), as were family (aOR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.76–0.87) and friend scores (aOR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.82–0.93). All three networks showed inverse trends across score categories (P for trend < 0.001). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses excluding self-reported CSI Part B conditions from the adjustment set. These findings highlight the relevance of family and friend relationships to symptom burden but do not establish causality.

Article.Title: RCE-YOLO: receptive-field attention and content-aware feature enhancement for aerospace transparent-component defect detection
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; He Z.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Aerospace transparent components are safety-critical optical structures whose surface integrity directly affects visual quality, environmental isolation and maintenance reliability. Single-image detection is particularly difficult when defects are weak, small or elongated and when reflections and illumination changes produce strong background responses. This study develops RCE-YOLO, a compact YOLOv11n-based detector organized around three staged operations: receptive-field-aware feature extraction, content-aware feature reconstruction and multi-scale feature recalibration. RFCBAMConv and C3k2_RFCBAMConv strengthen channel-selective and receptive-field spatial responses; CARAFE replaces fixed top-down interpolation with content-dependent feature reassembly; and efficient multi-scale attention (EMA) recalibrates the final P3, P4 and P5 features before prediction. Experiments use the Aircraft Glass Defect Dataset (AGDD) as a representative aerospace glazing benchmark. The 219 selected single-view source images are split into 197 training and 22 validation images before offline augmentation, yielding 1,379 training and 154 validation images under the current protocol. RCE-YOLO achieves 89.77% precision, 88.29% recall, 93.80% mAP@0.5, 77.27% mAP@0.75 and 71.60% mAP@0.5:0.95. Relative to YOLOv11n, mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.75 improve by 1.47 and 2.11 percentage points, respectively, with 2.80 M parameters and 7.40 GFLOPs. The eight-configuration ablation includes the three pairwise variants \(A+B\) , \(A+C\) and \(B+C\) ( A = C3k2_RFCBAMConv, B = CARAFE, C = EMA). The \(A+B\) configuration attains the highest mAP@0.5 (93.96%) and mAP@0.5:0.95 (73.53%), whereas the full \(A+B+C\) model yields the highest mAP@0.75 (77.27%). Pairwise interaction contrasts are 0.00 percentage points at the reported precision for these three mAP metrics; the three-way contrast varies by metric. These point estimates do not demonstrate reproducible synergy or establish that all three stages are necessary. At the class level, contusion AP@0.5:0.95 declines by 3.44 percentage points despite a 0.42-point gain at IoU 0.5; the full model therefore does not improve every defect class or IoU criterion. All performance figures are single-run point estimates, without multi-seed standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. Because the 154 augmented validation images originate from only 22 source images, the small numerical differences must not be interpreted as statistically established improvements. No independent external dataset or untouched real-image test set was evaluated; therefore cross-material and cross-acquisition generalization remains unverified.

Article.Title: Enhancing the performance of multi-access edge computing based intelligent transportation system
Article.Authors: Dana B.; Woldesenbet M.; Zerihun B.; Mishra S.
Article.Abstract: Vehicle-based Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSs) utilize connected vehicles to enhance our driving experience and optimize traffic flow. However, most vehicles do not have the processing capability necessary to support the expanding number of increasingly complex technologies associated with ITS. Examples of this include real-time traffic analysis and autonomous driving features. Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) provides a possible solution to the issue of offloading computation from vehicles by utilizing minicomputer servers located at the edge of the network, where the action is happening. This enables vehicles to offload large computations onto these MEC servers and increase their available resources, thereby improving overall system performance. In addition, caching of frequently used data within the MEC servers can also alleviate the processing burden on vehicles. The optimization of the strategy to fully implement MEC applications is critical. The proposed paper presents a combined optimization of service caching and computational offloading strategies for MEC-based Intelligent Transportation Systems that are located within Small Cell Networks. This methodology utilizes a Best-Score Server Selection Algorithm (BSSSA) approach, which assesses MEC servers to determine server scores based on pre-cached tasks, available resources, latency from the operator to the server, and proximity to the operator (vehicle). The server with the highest score is utilized for the physical offload of tasks. With Least Recently Used as the cache replacement policy on MEC servers, the content in these servers can be efficiently managed to maintain a maximum cache hit ratio, resulting in reduced overall system latency and energy consumption by the mitigation of duplicate tasks executed by the same MEC servers. By utilizing existing server capabilities, latency, and proximity of the operator (vehicle) through BSSSA, a significant increase in Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) will be provided, which allows for reliable transmission of packets. In addition, the overall performance of the MEC networks can be improved, as the use of Software Defined Network (SDN) technology will provide efficient information collection and centralized management of the vehicular network, as the primary purpose of an MEC network is to support high-speed data transportation. To benchmark the effectiveness of this proposed methodology, real-world vehicle-to-network scenarios will be created and tested by utilizing the OMNeT + + network simulation tool in conjunction with the Simu5G modules for 5G vehicular communication and the OpenFlow protocol, which facilitates the use of SDN technologies. The proposed methodology is expected to result in high cache hit ratios, low computing energy use of MEC servers, low latency in offloading tasks, and overall improved system performance and reliability.

Article.Title: GLP-1R in JBMMSCs suppressed mandibular injury via modulating PKA/STAT3/TET3/SHP2/β-catenin signaling induced osteoblast differentiation
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Bao X.; Ge S.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the specific molecular mechanisms of GLP-1R in jaw bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (JBMMSCs) under the influence of semaglutide on mandibular osteoporosis in rats. Rat osteoporosis samples were chosen for bioinformatics analysis from the GEO database. Additional single‑cell RNA‑seq, pseudotime trajectory, and cell‑cell communication analyses were also performed. Rat mandibles were used to harvest JBMMSCs, which were then identified using flow cytometry. CT was used to measure the degree of osteoporosis in a rat osteoporosis model. The therapeutic benefits of semaglutide-intervened JBMMSCs on osteoporosis and the function of SHP2 in semaglutide’s treatment effectiveness were assessed using H&E staining. JBMMSCs were cultivated in vitro at the optimum semaglutide concentration for osteogenic and adipogenic induction. Osteogenic and adipogenic-related protein expression levels were found using Western blot, and osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation capacities were evaluated by ARS and Oil Red O staining. Additionally, ChIP-qPCR was performed to assess direct transcriptional regulation, and immunofluorescence was used to evaluate β-catenin nuclear translocation. To further investigate the molecular processes by which JBMMSCs ameliorate osteoporosis under semaglutide intervention, the expression levels of GLP-1R, p-PKA, p-STAT3, TET3, t-SHP2, p-SHP2, and β-catenin were evaluated. CT observations revealed that semaglutide-intervened JBMMSCs had a therapeutic effect on osteoporosis, with SHP2 playing a critical role in enhancing semaglutide’s efficacy. Rats treated with semaglutide-intervened JBMMSCs had much less osteoporosis, according to H&E staining. Bioinformatic analysis further revealed that MRONJ‑derived BM‑MSCs exhibited impaired osteogenic potential, enhanced adipogenic predisposition, and dysregulated TGFB1‑driven cell‑cell communication. Semaglutide improves osteoporosis by promoting osteogenesis and inhibiting adipogenesis in JBMMSCs via the PKA/STAT3/TET3/SHP2/β-catenin axis, according to Western blot analysis of associated protein expression levels, which was further corroborated by RT-qPCR at the transcriptional level. Mechanistically, ChIP-qPCR confirmed that p-STAT3 directly binds the TET3 promoter, and TET3 directly binds and demethylates the SHP2 promoter; immunofluorescence further demonstrated that this axis promotes β-catenin nuclear translocation. These results were validated by rescue studies. GLP-1R in JBMMSCs inhibits osteoporosis by regulating osteoblast differentiation induced by the PKA/STAT3/TET3/SHP2/β-catenin signaling pathway.

Article.Title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
Article.Authors: Ueno K.; Yomogida T.; Kumagai Y.; Kitagaki T.; Ikeuchi H.; Mizokami M.; Mizokami S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The powdered fuel debris sample, prepared via a vibratory mill, was analyzed using micro-Raman spectroscopy and was compared with simulated debris synthesized under controlled conditions. The average Raman spectrum revealed characteristic bands corresponding to tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides originating from stainless-steel structural components, and a cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution. The Raman spectrum of the retrieved fuel debris differed significantly from that of uranium-containing particles (UP1) previously sampled from stagnant water at torus room of Unit 2 of the FDNPS, indicating that further sampling and analysis are required to fully understand the overall chemical complexity of the fuel debris. Raman spectroscopy proved effective for identifying oxidative products in the fuel debris, requiring only minimal sample amounts and no vacuum or coating pretreatments. This study highlights the method’s potential as a valuable tool in nuclear decommissioning efforts, especially for the characterization of uranium bearing compounds in fuel debris.

Article.Title: Efficacy of amlodipine as an adjunct to iron chelation therapy in reducing iron overload in thalassemia patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Hetta H.; Alanazi F.; Alattar A.; Alshaman R.; Albarqi H.; Qedir B.; Alkazm M.; Ahmed A.; Alquzi I.; Kaabi R.; Aljuaid M.; Almrwani S.; Merdad S.; Selim T.; Sayad R.
Article.Abstract: Iron overload remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with thalassemia, particularly due to cardiac siderosis. Although iron chelation therapy (ICT) is the cornerstone of management, it may be insufficient to prevent progressive iron accumulation. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs), such as amlodipine, have been proposed as adjunctive therapy to reduce myocardial iron uptake. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy of amlodipine combined with standard ICT in thalassemia patients. This study followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. A comprehensive search of Embase, PubMed, Medline, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted up to August 2025. We included RCTs evaluating amlodipine plus ICT versus ICT plus placebo or non-CCB supplements in patients with thalassemia. Primary outcomes were serum ferritin, liver iron concentration (LIC), myocardial iron concentration (MIC), myocardial T2*, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Pooled analyses were performed using random- or fixed-effect models based on heterogeneity. Seven RCTs (2013–2022; n = 15–64) were included. At 6 months, combination therapy significantly reduced serum ferritin (MD = − 689.03 ng/ml; 95% CI − 1001.45 to − 376.61; P < 0.0001) and MIC (MD = − 0.22; 95% CI − 0.42 to − 0.03; P = 0.02). At 12 months, serum ferritin (MD = − 303.30; 95% CI − 513.92 to − 92.68; P = 0.005) and MIC (MD = − 0.42; 95% CI − 0.56 to − 0.28; P < 0.00001) remained significantly reduced, with no heterogeneity. Myocardial T2* improved significantly at 12 months (MD = 4.29; 95% CI 1.58 to 7.01; P = 0.002), whereas LIC and LVEF showed no significant changes at either time point. Adjunctive amlodipine combined with standard iron chelation therapy may provide additional benefits in reducing systemic and myocardial iron burden and improving cardiac T2* in patients with transfusion-dependent thalassemia. Although these findings support the potential role of amlodipine in mitigating cardiac siderosis, they should be interpreted with caution because the available evidence is based on a limited number of relatively small RCTs with clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

Article.Title: Techno-economic optimization of a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system with an EV charging station at a university campus​
Article.Authors: Nazir K.; Biswas B.; Shimul A.; Solre G.; Al-Humaidi J.; Aljazzar S.; Benghanem M.; Elboughdiri N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EV) adoption in developing economies, combined with the growing imperative to decarbonize campus energy systems, necessitates novel planning frameworks that reconcile grid-interactive microgrid design with probabilistic economic validation. This study presents a techno-economic planning framework for a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) co-designed with an EV charging station at university campus​. Unlike prior studies that treat EV loads as static inputs, this work constructs a behaviorally-informed, regulated-charging EV load profile by characterizing the actual EV fleet accessible within the study area, yielding a demand model grounded in local mobility patterns. Four HRES configurations integrating PV arrays, WT, a Bio-Gen, BESS, and utility grid support are optimized through HOMER Pro. The optimal configuration achieves a NPC of $2,403,816 and a COE of $0.069/kWh at a RF of 70.04%, while attaining significantly reduced emissions of CO 2 , NO x , SO 2 , and CO compared to the more grid-reliant configurations (Cases III and IV), and demonstrating environmental performance akin to Case II. Critically, this study couples system-level optimization with a probabilistic Monte Carlo simulation framework consisting of 10,000 stochastic trials over uncertain techno-economic parameters to produce probabilistic financial performance distributions. The analysis yields a 99.03% probability of achieving a positive NPV, a mean payback period of ~ 11.5 years, and a mean IRR of 10.98%, closely aligned with the project discount rate, collectively indicating favorable financial performance under the considered uncertainty. A local multivariate sensitivity analysis further indicates that, within the evaluated parameter ranges, solar irradiance exhibits the greatest influence on system performance, followed by wind speed, whereas Bio-Gen availability demonstrates comparatively low sensitivity. These findings provide useful guidance for technology prioritization in climate-variable south-central region.

Article.Title: DSG-BDF: a design semantic graph-guided bidirectional diffusion framework for controllable clothing pattern generation based on ControlNet and CLIP ViT-L/14
Article.Authors: Pan G.; Fang Y.; Zhang Y.; Wen L.; Xu Z.; Sun X.
Article.Abstract: Diffusion models have shown promise in clothing theme pattern generation, but the lack of a stable cross-modal coupling mechanism between structural constraints and textual semantics leads to semantic drift and style fluctuations under complex design conditions. This paper proposes the Design Semantic Graph Guided Bidirectional Diffusion Framework (DSG-BDF). Design theme text is encoded via the CLIP ViT-L/14 encoder and organized into a design semantic graph capturing pattern element relationships and style attributes, which a graph neural network encodes into structured semantic vectors. These vectors are fused with CLIP features and injected into the UNet cross-attention layer as a semantic conditional path, while ControlNet encodes contour and layout features as a structural constraint path. A bidirectional collaborative module enables mutual modulation between the two paths during denoising, and a joint loss covering semantic consistency, structural preservation, and style stability supervises training. Experiments show that DSG-BDF achieves a CLIP-Score of 0.347 ± 0.003, FID of 19.8 ± 0.4, and SCI of 0.912 ± 0.012, outperforming the strongest baseline (FashionDiff: CLIP-Score 0.341, FID 20.9) and improving over the Stable Diffusion baseline (CLIP-Score 0.289, FID 28.6) by 20.1% and 30.8% respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves stable semantic-structural co-generation under complex design conditions.

Article.Title: Frequency-aware and depth-guided neural radiance fields for 3D reconstruction of complex disaster scenes
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Tang D.; HM L.; Chen J.; Chen X.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Smoke occlusion, weak textures, non-Lambertian reflectance, and structural fragmentation in complex disaster scenes undermine multi-view photometric consistency and exacerbate depth ambiguity under sparse-view settings, resulting in geometric floaters, blurred boundaries, and the loss of fine details in neural radiance field reconstruction. To address these challenges, we propose a neural radiance field reconstruction method that integrates frequency-aware gating with depth-guided geometric priors. The proposed method constructs a hierarchical spatial representation using multi-resolution hash encoding, adaptively fuses low-frequency geometric features with high-frequency residual features through frequency-aware gating, and incorporates cross-level geometric consistency regularization and dynamic residual learning to suppress structural drift caused by hash collisions and enhance local responses in spectral transition regions. To mitigate geometric degradation under sparse-view conditions, monocular depth priors are further introduced, together with scale-and-shift alignment and an uncertainty-aware spectral consistency constraint, to reduce the adverse influence of erroneous priors on geometry optimization. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves the PSNR by 1.865 dB over the baseline model. Compared with the model using only depth priors, the proposed method reduces the depth MSE by 88.99%, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving pixel-level reconstruction accuracy, structural similarity, and depth consistency in complex disaster scenes.

Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Liu C.; Zheng W.; Wang Y.; Du Y.; Jin J.; Yu M.; Sha J.
Article.Abstract: To address the issue of rolling bearing vibration signals being obscured by noise, leading to unclear fault characteristics and low fault diagnosis accuracy, a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on the Multi-scale Temporal Attention Liquid Neural Network (MTA-LNN) optimized by multi-scale temporal attention mechanism is proposed. Firstly, the original vibration signals are constructed into multi-scale time series samples through different scale windows. Secondly, the temporal attention mechanism is introduced to perform adaptive weighting on fault signal features at different scales. Finally, the liquid neural network is introduced to construct a fault diagnosis model to achieve the fault diagnosis task. Experimental results show that the liquid neural network optimized by the multi-scale attention mechanism can still achieve a high fault diagnosis rate under complex working conditions, with a fault diagnosis accuracy of up to 98.99%.

Article.Title: Detection and classification of failed fiber reinforced polymer composite samples under mechanical loading using YOLO11 on microscopic SEM images
Article.Authors: Aboobacker S.; Pallavi J.; Roopa B.; Sandeep B.; Vamshi A.; Khan T.; Jazaa Y.; Khan W.
Article.Abstract: The fracture surfaces of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and are slow to conduct. The fracture surfaces of FRP composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and slow to conduct. This proof-of-concept study compares an anchor-free single-stage detector, YOLO11n, to localize and classify six fractographic features: fiber breakage, fiber pull-out, fiber–matrix debonding, delamination, voids and matrix debris, in SEM images of carbon- and glass-fiber/epoxy specimens failed in tension, three-point bending and short-beam shear. The data consists of 125 images with 37 specimens, with 1318 labelled boxes following written labelling criteria. The weights for the model were initialized from COCO and were updated using the Adam optimizer. YOLO11n was able to obtain mAP@0.5 = 0.821 with 6.5 ms per image on a preliminary image-level split, but the number of images per subset is not consistent with 125 images and the results may be optimistic due to the fact that images from one specimen can be split into multiple subsets. Multiple seeds, a controlled comparison between it and YOLOv5n, YOLOv8n and YOLOv9t, per-class ablations and an error analysis were performed at the level of the specimen and the groups. The study shows that it is possible to apply the method of detector-assisted laboratory fractography. It does not provide any structural-health-monitoring or safety-critical capability, and is not tested on other material systems or imaging conditions.

Article.Title: Association between social determinants of health, lifestyle behaviors, and health outcomes in Saudi Arabia: An exploratory cross-sectional online survey study
Article.Authors: Jazieh C.; Ajam A.; Alhusseini N.; Cahusac P.; Sajid M.
Article.Abstract: Social determinants of health (SDH) and lifestyle factors significantly influence chronic disease burden and healthcare access. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of 411 adults residing in Saudi Arabia (January–April 2024) to examine associations between SDH (education, income, financial strain), lifestyle behaviors (diet, physical activity, smoking), chronic conditions, and healthcare access. The sample (mean age 29.4 ± 11.2 years, 60.1% female, 38.2% Saudi nationals) showed prevalences of obesity (10.2%), asthma (7.5%), diabetes (7.1%), hypertension (6.6%), and dyslipidemia (6.1%). In adjusted models, age (β = 0.21, partial η²=0.042, p < 0.001) and financial strain (β = 0.14, partial η²=0.018, p < 0.01) were statistically associated with multimorbidity (associational findings; causal inferences cannot be drawn). Food insecurity was associated with higher chronic disease burden (OR = 1.45, 95% CI 1.12–1.88), while higher education was associated with increased healthcare access (OR = 1.67, 95% CI 1.23–2.27). Financial hardship was associated with reduced healthcare access odds (OR = 0.61, 95% CI 0.42–0.88). In this exploratory sample of adults residing in Saudi Arabia (predominantly young, female, and non-Saudi nationals), socioeconomic factors and lifestyle behaviors were associated with health outcomes and healthcare access. Financial strain and food insecurity showed unfavorable associations (higher chronic disease burden), while higher education showed favorable associations (better healthcare access). Addressing financial strain and promoting education may help reduce chronic disease burden and improve healthcare equity; however, given the cross-sectional design and sample limitations, causal inferences cannot be drawn, and findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Centrifuge vs. laboratory: the usability of touch sensitive screens under g-load
Article.Authors: Schmidt A.; Aulenbacher C.; Daum O.; Hecht H.
Article.Abstract: Touchscreens have become rather sophisticated and well-designed in road vehicles. In contrast, in aviation contexts, existing touchscreens leave room for improvement. In particular, the challenge of using such displays in high-performance aircraft is of great interest due to the effects of extreme g-forces on usability. The study aimed to determine the effects of g-forces on touch input during flight and to assess how best to simulate these effects. Two lab experiments and a run in the human centrifuge of the German Air Force Centre of Aerospace Medicine in Königsbrück were conducted. The experiments were designed to test the usability of touch input under an increased g-load along the vertical body ( $$g_z$$ ) axis. The first lab experiment utilised a large panoramic screen for the primary task of flying a simple plane through virtual gates in the sky. The secondary tasks (pointing at a target, zooming, dragging, and following an object) were presented alternately on four touch screens. Attaching weights to the arms to make them twice as heavy as normal, simulating a $$g_{z}$$ load of 2, initially produced minor performance decrements that could be quickly compensated. For practical reasons, only a subset of touch screens could be used on the centrifuge. A $$g_z$$ load of 2.2 g and above produced major loss in speed and/or precision. Finally, a control experiment was conducted to replicate the same conditions with weighted arms. This showed a similar effect to the first lab experiment, with only minor initial performance decrements for $$g_{z}$$ loads of 2.2 g and 3.0 g. In conclusion, the effects of g-load on touchscreen interaction performance are detrimental and cannot be simulated in standard lab environments. Further centrifuge experiments are required to optimise touch displays in high-performance aircraft.

Article.Title: Computational exploration of Hemidesmus indicus phytochemicals targeting HSP90 in ovarian cancer through molecular docking, structural dynamics and free energy landscape
Article.Authors: Sivaprakasam B.; Jayaraman M.; Kulandhaivel S.; Arun M.; Antony S.; Jeyaraman J.; Muthuramalingam P.; Shin H.; Jesudass J.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian cancer is a leading cause of death in all gynecological cancers, as recurrence, drug resistance, and limited therapeutic options remain critical clinical challenges despite advances. Heat Shock Protein 90 (HSP90) is a molecular chaperone and validated as an attractive therapeutic target in cancer drug discovery, as it supports many oncoproteins that act as critical regulators of the cell cycle, apoptosis, and signalling pathways. In this current study, a computational pipeline was used to evaluate bioactive phytochemicals from Hemidesmus indicus (L.) R. Br. ex-Schult as potential HSP90 inhibitors relevant to ovarian cancer. Among 87 phytochemicals screened, rutin, isoquercetin, and indicine were prioritized based on receptor-based molecular docking, exhibiting favorable docking scores of −14.99, −13.17, and −11.73 kcal/mol, respectively, compared with −5.07 kcal/mol for the reference HSP90 inhibitor geldanamycin. The corresponding MM-GBSA binding free energies were −80.93, −74.61, and −77.47 kcal/mol for rutin, isoquercetin, and indicine, respectively, compared with −80.02 kcal/mol for geldanamycin. In silico ADMET analysis predicted comparatively favorable pharmacokinetic characteristics for isoquercetin and indicine, whereas rutin showed predicted physicochemical limitations that may require further optimization. The stability of the HSP90-ligand complexes was investigated by performing 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) with stable and persistent behavior in RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration, and hydrogen bond parameters across the entire simulation trajectory. Principal component analysis (PCA)-based free energy landscape (FEL) mapping demonstrated well-defined low-energy conformational states, and MM-PBSA calculations affirmed strong interactions with active-site residues. Together, these in silico findings suggest that rutin, isoquercetin, and indicine may represent promising candidate HSP90-targeting compounds from H. indicus for further experimental validation to evaluate their anticancer potential. In vitro studies targeting HSP90 binding and ATPase activity together with ovarian cancer cell line testing, followed by in vivo experiments, are needed to confirm their therapeutic efficacy and anticancer effects.

Article.Title: Development of flax/kenaf hybrid epoxy composites incorporating sugarcane biochar with enhanced fire performance for potential electrical conduit applications
Article.Authors: Velmurugan G.; Chohan J.; Abraar S.; Velusamy K.; Raja D.; Maranan R.; Arunprasath K.; Kumar A.; Sembeta R.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the effect of sugarcane biochar on the structural, mechanical, thermal, and fire-related behaviour of flax/kenaf/flax hybrid epoxy composites with different weight contents of biochar (0–6 wt%). FTIR analysis shows that chemical structure changes may occur and that there might be interactions between the biochar and the epoxy matrix. Mechanical characterisation revealed that the measured mechanical properties improved with biochar contents up to 4.5 wt%, but decreased at 6 wt% biochar loading, where changes in filler distribution may have occurred. At 4.5 wt% biochar, the composite exhibited a tensile strength of 38.01 ± 0.55 MPa, flexural strength of 76.12 ± 0.90 MPa, impact strength of 9.62 ± 0.45 kJ/m 2 , hardness of 86 ± 1 Shore D, and ILSS of 13.24 ± 0.35 MPa. Additionally, TGA/DTG results revealed that the thermal degradation resistance was enhanced, as the onset degradation temperature rose to 317 °C and the residual char content was 28% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The fire-performance evaluation revealed that the LOI of neat epoxy increased from 19.5 ± 0.5% to 28.4 ± 0.8% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The same formulation showed a lower PHRR of 300.10 ± 9.28 kW/m 2 and THR of 54.03 ± 1.74 MJ/m 2 , with delayed ignition and a lower horizontal burning rate. Morphological support for the proposed condensed-phase protective mechanism was obtained from SEM analysis of the post-flammability residues. A cylindrical prototype was fabricated as a proof-of-concept demonstration of the feasibility of forming the composite into a conduit-like geometry, with a length of 300 mm and a wall thickness of 3 mm .

Article.Title: Optimization of gum arabic powder content in Kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites for enhanced mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related performance
Article.Authors: Arunkumar A.; Venkataramanan A.; Kumaravelan R.; Manoj Kumar P.; Somasundaram K.; Parthipan N.; Vannan R.; Prabhu P.; Gebreyohannes D.
Article.Abstract: The use of sustainable multifunctional composites made from renewable sources is gaining momentum in the field of advanced engineering. A constant kenaf fiber content of 20 wt% was maintained, while gum Arabic powder loading was varied from 0 to 20 wt% (KEG0–KEG20) in the proposed in kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites. The effects of gum Arabic incorporation on mechanical, thermo-mechanical thermal dielectric, and moisture absorption properties were systematically investigated. The addition of fillers increased the composites’ performance and the effects were the highest at 15 wt%. The enhancement of mechanical properties may be attributed to the improved filler dispersion, improved interfacial interaction, improved stress-transfer conditions and lower microstructural defects in the composite. KEG15 composite demonstrated the best tensile strength of 55.3 MPa, Young’s modulus of 3.12 GPa, flexural strength of 88.9 MPa, flexural modulus of 4.48 GPa, impact strength of 28.6 kJ m⁻², Shore D hardness of 83.2, dielectric strength of 29.8 kV mm, storage modulus (~ 4500 MPa), glass transition temperatures of around 105 °C and residual char content of 23.7%. Despite the individual properties showed different responses to the gum Arabic powder loading, KEG15 was found to be the optimum formulation based on the highest overall multifunctional performance index representing the most balanced combination of the selected mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related properties. One-way ANOVA based on independent specimen level observations revealed statistically significant differences between the formulations ( p < 0.001). FTIR and SEM observations supported the corresponding interfacial and morphological changes. This study has effectively combined the synergistic action of kenaf fiber and gum Arabic powder to make multifunctional epoxy composites with excellent mechanical, thermal, electrical insulation, and environmental durability properties being achieved. 15 wt% gum Arabic powder was the optimum filler level.

Article.Title: Rasch analysis of the physical activity questionnaire for children in Spain supports a candidate three-item short form
Article.Authors: Lizoain P.; Gambra L.; Magallón S.; Martínez M.
Article.Abstract: The Physical Activity Questionnaire for Children (PAQ-C) is widely used to assess habitual physical activity in youth, although its psychometric properties have shown variability across cultural contexts. This study aimed to examine the internal structure and measurement properties of the PAQ-C in Spanish primary-school children using Rasch analysis, explore a candidate short-form version, and derive sample-based percentile thresholds for describing physical activity scores. A cross-sectional exploratory study was conducted involving 259 children aged 6–12 years from two schools in Navarra, Spain. Parents or guardians completed the questionnaire for children in Grades 1–3, whereas children in Grades 4–6 completed it themselves. Item-level analyses and Rasch modeling were used to examine response functioning, scale structure, reliability, and differential item functioning (DIF) by sex and school grade. The original nine-item PAQ-C showed significant overall Rasch model misfit, disordered response thresholds in several items, and evidence of multidimensionality. An exploratory three-item version comprising Items 7–9 demonstrated improved Rasch model fit (χ² = 12.76, df = 9, p = 0.173), ordered thresholds, and acceptable person separation reliability (PSI = 0.76). No statistically significant DIF was detected by sex or school grade. Sample-based percentile thresholds were derived to describe the distribution of three-item scores, without establishing clinical or health-related cut-off values. Overall, the findings suggest that the candidate three-item short form shows more favorable Rasch measurement properties than the original questionnaire in this sample, although independent validation, assessment of temporal reliability, and comparison with external physical activity measures are needed before broader application.

Article.Title: Multilayer feed-forward neural network-based mobile app for photovoltaic module parameter estimation
Article.Authors: Taibin M.; Islam M.; Hussan M.; Rahman M.; Al-Subhi A.; Shafiullah M.; Hossain M.; Islam A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate parameter estimation of photovoltaic (PV) cells and modules is essential for the modeling, simulation, and optimization of PV systems. However, this task involves solving a complex nonlinear optimization problem, which often suffers from slow convergence and entrapment in local minima. The objective of this research is to contribute finding an efficient and software-independent approach to predict the parameters of the single diode model for polycrystalline and monocrystalline PV cells and modules from only the datasheet parameters at Standard Test Conditions (STC). To accomplish this task, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) approach is used, which resulted in the ability to estimate instantly without the need of commercial software. The developed model is additionally implemented in an Android application, which offers a user friendly and accessible instrument for PV system designers. The model was further evaluated through comparisons of reconstructed I–V and P–V characteristics with available reference characteristics, Simulink library modules, manufacturer datasheet values, and recently published algorithms. The results demonstrate high reliability, with RMSE, MAE and U95 values of 1.3610e−04, 6.8160e−05 and 2.659820e−04 respectively. Furthermore, the model reliably reproduced P–V and I–V characteristics under varying environmental conditions, closely aligning with the datasheet specifications of the four modules.

Article.Title: Culturomics complements 16S rRNA gene sequencing in the characterization of the urogenital microbiome of asymptomatic reproductive-age women
Article.Authors: Villenave C.; Dahyot S.; Leoz M.; Roussel G.; Santini A.; Charbonnier C.; Pestel-Caron M.
Article.Abstract: Culturomics and 16S rRNA gene sequencing offer complementary views of the genitourinary microbiome (GUM) but are rarely compared in well-phenotyped cohorts. Here, we characterized the GUM of 100 prospectively enrolled asymptomatic, non-pregnant, premenopausal women (18–45 years). Community structure types (CSTs) were defined by hierarchical clustering of genus-level relative abundances identified by culturomics and 16S V3-V4 sequencing. Correlations with clinical and behavioural host metadata collected were assessed based on sequencing. Culturomics and sequencing respectively identified 139 species from 59 genera, and 138 species from 144 genera. Per-sample richness at the genus level was higher by sequencing, but mean Shannon diversity was similar. Lactobacillus -dominated communities were common (37% by culturomics; 53% by sequencing), followed by Gardnerella -dominated and mixed Lactobacillus – Gardnerella profiles. Seven CSTs were defined from culturomics and six from 16S rRNA gene sequencing, which were concordant in only 31 of 98 samples (31.6%). Regarding metadata, none correlated with CST profiles, and only the menstrual cycle was significantly associated with variation in the beta diversity indices. This study revealed a well-structured and diverse GUM in asymptomatic women of reproductive age. However, longitudinal studies involving larger cohorts are needed to further our understanding of the host factors potentially associated with GUM.

Article.Title: Microbiological contamination in an anatomy laboratory: comparison of cadaveric materials and environmental surfaces
Article.Authors: Emre E.; Toraman Z.; Ogeturk M.; Ustundag Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the distribution of microbial contamination in an anatomy laboratory to determine whether contamination was primarily associated with cadaver-related materials or with the general laboratory environment. Although cadaver dissection is an essential component of medical education, anatomy laboratories may represent potential sources of biological exposure because microorganisms can persist on cadavers, laboratory equipment, and frequently touched surfaces. The study aimed to compare microbial growth among human tissues, cadaver-related surfaces, and commonly used laboratory areas. A total of 88 swab samples were collected from human tissues, cadaver-contact surfaces, and areas without direct cadaver contact. Samples were cultured using standard microbiological techniques, and microbial identification was performed with an automated identification system. Microbial growth was detected in more than half of the collected samples. The highest contamination levels were observed on laboratory surfaces without direct cadaver contact, particularly laboratory coats, student desks, door handles, and electrical switches. Lower contamination rates were identified in samples obtained from formaldehyde-preserved cadavers and frozen cadavers, suggesting that preservative methods reduce but do not completely eliminate microbial survival. Dry bone materials demonstrated comparatively higher microbial colonization. Frequently isolated microorganisms included Staphylococcus aureus , Staphylococcus epidermidis , Bacillus subtilis , Enterococcus faecalis , and several enteric bacteria, while fungal species such as Candida albicans and Aspergillus flavus were also identified. These findings demonstrate that microbiological contamination in anatomy laboratories extends beyond cadavers and may spread through environmental surfaces and shared materials. Regular disinfection, appropriate ventilation, and consistent use of personal protective equipment are therefore critical for maintaining biosafety in anatomy education environments.

Article.Title: Maintenance and termination of the embryonic diapause in the univoltine damselfly Lestes sponsa Hansemann
Article.Authors: Norling U.; Sniegula S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Embryonic diapause and its termination are key to seasonal timing in the univoltine damselfly Lestes sponsa , ensuring that eggs overwinter and hatch in spring. Following summer oviposition—typically in plants above water—diapause begins after 2–3 weeks. We investigated diapause termination in eggs from southern Sweden (~ 55°N) using combinations of chilling in darkness and subsequent exposure to photoperiods at elevated temperatures. Diapause development—a physiological process underlying termination—was fastest at 10 °C, slower at 5 °C, and slowest (possibly stagnating) at 20–21 °C. Longer chilling enhanced the terminating effects of long photoperiods and high temperatures, resulting in faster, more synchronous hatching and a shorter critical photoperiod. At immediate 21 °C and solstice-like photoperiods (LD 19.5:4.5), hatching began 1–2 weeks after diapause initiation and continued for weeks, but synchrony improved with prior exposure to diapause-maintaining conditions (< LD 17:7). LD 18:6 was only weakly effective in terminating diapause without chilling. After 19–21 weeks at 5 °C, virtually complete hatching occurred within 2–4 days independently of photoperiod. If diapause was not terminated immediately at 21 °C after chilling, diapause development appeared to reverse, restoring pre-chill photoperiodic responses. In contrast, 10 °C post-chill accelerated diapause development and reduced late outliers, but some effects of photoperiod on hatching time still persisted after 19–21 weeks chilling. Post-diapause development was 3-3.5 times slower at 10 °C and ~ 20 times slower at 5 °C compared to 21 °C. Hatching was successful at 5 °C, and larvae survived two weeks near 0 °C, suggesting potential for winter hatching under a warmer climate. Eggs from Poland (~ 54°N) and northern Sweden (~ 66°N) differed in critical photoperiods, with a weaker diapause at higher latitudes. This system, adapted to latitude, ensures early and synchronous spring hatching, with hatchlings resistant to cold spells and prevents premature hatching during untimely warm periods via short-day inhibition.

Article.Title: Integrating UAV-assisted blow sampling and photo-identification in common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus)
Article.Authors: Ceolotto L.; Fiore E.; Ferraresso S.; Andrés-Hervías C.; Genov T.; Gonzalvo J.; Lokar K.; Pesce G.; Dugény E.; Mazzariol S.; Centelleghe C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-invasive genetic sampling can improve the study and conservation of cetaceans by reducing disturbance while providinsg information on population structure, connectivity, and other parameters. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of UAV-assisted blow sampling for obtaining DNA from free-ranging common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in two Mediterranean areas: The Gulf of Ambracia (Greece) and the Gulf of Trieste (off Piran, Slovenia). Blow samples were linked to photo-identified individuals and assessed through UAV video review. Mitochondrial DNA amplification was successful for at least one mitochondrial locus in 78% of Greek and 100% of Slovenian samples, whereas a nuclear marker amplified only in samples of animals under human care, used as a control, indicating that the mitochondrial assays used here performed more consistently than the single nuclear assay tested for blow-derived low-template DNA. Fifteen individuals were sequenced for up to six mitochondrial loci, and 13 were retained in the final concatenated dataset. Phylogenetic, haplotype network, and multivariate analyses showed that the recovered mitochondrial sequences could be used for genetic comparisons between the two study areas. Video-assessment categories were associated with molecular success, suggesting that UAV video assessment is particularly useful for identifying sampling attempts with a low likelihood of molecular success. Overall, our results support UAV-assisted blow sampling integrated with photo-ID as a promising approach for individual-based molecular monitoring of small cetaceans.

Article.Title: From waste to worth: Green valorization of food waste into a sustainable fluorimetric nanoprobe for chemical and bioanalytical sensing
Article.Authors: Abdel-Monem M.; Eid M.; Aly F.; Abdallah N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Overripe plant materials represent a major source of organic agricultural waste and are highly susceptible to rapid microbial decomposition due to their high moisture and sugar content. Improper disposal of such waste leads to the release of greenhouse gases and contributes to environmental pollution. Therefore, adopting sustainable recycling approaches is essential to minimize their environmental impact and promote efficient resource utilization. Herein, overripe goldenberry fruits, typically discarded as waste, have been successfully recycled and utilized for the first time as a convenient, renewable eco-friendly carbon source for engineering multi-doped CQDs that exhibit outstanding fluorescence characteristics (λex/em of 340/420 nm). These naturally derived nanodots were fabricated in only two min using a straightforward, one-pot microwave-assisted process offering rapid, and eco-friendly aspects arising from the utilization of bio-based carbon material and preparation strategy. The fabricated nanosensor was utilized for quantification of the veterinary NSAID Flunixin (FXN). The studied drug induced fluorescence quenching of these CQDs via both inner filter effect and dynamic quenching. This work showcases transforming discarded biomass into profitable nanomaterials. Beyond introducing the first CQD-based fluorescent assay for FXN, this study demonstrates an innovative strategy for converting discarded biomass into high-value nanomaterials. The method exhibited outstanding performance, including remarkable selectivity, a broad linear range, and a low detection limit, highlighting its sustainability, and applicability to pharmaceutical, food, and environmental water samples.

Article.Title: Postoperative evaluation of Achilles tendon using short echo time MRI and artificial intelligence
Article.Authors: Ciszkowska-Łysoń B.; Borowiec A.; Witkowska J.; Paśnik M.; Śmigielski R.; Borucki B.; Kapiński N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The objective was to identify the optimal MRI sequence to evaluate postoperative Achilles tendon (AT) healing. A total of 45 patients (mean age 36 ± 6 years; 36 men, 9 women) underwent nine consecutive MRI examinations at intervals from 1 to 52 weeks after surgery. SI in all postoperative MRI examinations was measured in AT in TE4, TE16 and PD. SI in the operated AT appears normal in PD and TE16 sequences around week 39. However, TE4 still shows high signals, indicating ongoing remodeling. Significant correlations were found between biomarkers and SI in the TE4 sequence ( p < 0.001 for structural changes and tendon edema, and p = 0.002 for tissue edema). High SI values were associated with poor biomarker outcomes. The mean absolute errors (MAE) between AI model scores, obtained using only axial TE4 scans, and radiologist evaluations ranged from 0.12 to 0.63. In conclusion, TE4 demonstrated greater sensitivity to persistent postoperative signal and structural abnormalities and may be useful in postoperative assessment of AT. AI scores showed relatively small absolute differences from the reference radiologist scores.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal analysis and machine learning prediction of road traffic crash hotspots: a case of Amhara region, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Fetene A.; Zelelew H.; Juremalani J.; Tola A.
Article.Abstract: Road traffic crashes remain a major public health and development challenge in Ethiopia. While previous studies in the Amhara region have examined crash trends, contributing factors, or specific road corridors, there is limited evidence on spatiotemporal hotspots and on predicting population-adjusted crash rates. This study aimed to investigate the spatial and temporal distribution of road traffic crashes in the Amhara region and to build machine learning models to estimate crash rates across administrative zones. The dataset comprised police-reported crash records from 2013 to 2022 along with spatial, demographic, traffic exposure, and school-related variables. Spatial clustering was assessed using the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic. Machine learning approaches were evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation. The North Shewa zone consistently emerged as a statistically significant cluster of reported crash burden, and the East Gojam zone appeared as an emerging hotspot during the later years of the study period. Of the models evaluated, Random Forest achieved the strongest cross-validated performance (RMSE = 0.866 ± 0.205; R 2 = 0.678 ± 0.266). The GIS and machine learning findings are complementary: GIS identifies geographic clustering of reported crashes, whereas machine learning estimates population-normalized crash rates. These results can support regional road safety planning by helping prioritize zones for enhanced monitoring, enforcement strategies, data quality improvements, and targeted corridor-level assessment. Future work should incorporate geocoded crash records and road segment-level data to enable the design of site-specific interventions.

Article.Title: Numerical investigation of the influence of pile-cap configuration on hydrodynamic interactions and mean vortical structures in complex bridge piers
Article.Authors: Pezeshki A.; Beheshti A.; Modaresi M.; Ziae A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate characterization of the intricate flow field around complex bridge piers is paramount for mitigating local scour and ensuring the structural integrity of transportation infrastructure under hydrodynamic loading. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation into the complex hydrodynamic interactions around multi-component bridge piers. The numerical framework is rigorously validated against high-resolution experimental data obtained via Acoustic Doppler Velocimeter (ADV) measurements, demonstrating excellent agreement in mean velocity contours and profiles. Beyond validation, the simulations provide high-fidelity insights into the near-field coherent flow structures that govern the erosive potential of complex piers. By evaluating diverse pier geometries, this research elucidates the synergistic effects between columns, pile caps (PC), and pile groups on flow topology and bed shear stress distribution. For foundations with a bed-level PC, the results identify a prominent horseshoe vortex at the leading edge, while the interplay between separated shear layers and downward flows generates distinct secondary side vortices. In the wake region, an arch-like vortex emerges as the primary mechanism for bed material entrainment due to significantly intensified turbulence. Notably, the exposure of the pile group induces a secondary corner vortex at the PC trailing edge. The findings reveal that increasing the PC elevation not only curtails the downstream recirculation length but also shifts the scouring dominance from the pile cap to the pile group as the PC’s influence on near-bed hydrodynamics progressively diminishes.

Article.Authors: Heinke S.; Schürmann O.; Andraszewicz S.; Rieskamp J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract It is essential for researchers and practitioners advising decision-makers to understand and measure precisely individual risk preferences. Behavioural risk- preference elicitation tasks have several advantages over self-report measures, including reducing biases and providing objective assessments. However, their low test–retest reliability limits their predictive value and overall measurement quality. This study investigates whether increasing the number of decisions within behavioural risk-elicitation tasks can improve their reliability. We hypothesise that adding multi-items to behavioural tasks can reduce decision noise and improve test–retest reliability. To test this hypothesis, we compared an enhanced multi-item behavioural risk elicitation task with standard behavioural- and self-report risk measures. Our results show that, although increasing the number of decisions improves reliability relative to traditional behavioural risk-preferences elicitation tasks, well-established multi-item self-report psychological questionnaires still demonstrate superior test–retest consistency.

Article.Title: LLM-agent-based cross-modal retrieval method for detecting clues of ecological environment damage
Article.Authors: Zhao M.; Bai L.; Lu S.; He X.; Chen L.; Ben F.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Within Ecological Conservation Redline zones, ecological environmental damage caused by non-compliant production and construction activities has become increasingly severe. Existing methods typically leverage remote sensing imagery and deep learning techniques to automatically identify unauthorized construction, or retrieve clues of ecological environmental damage from textual information such as public complaints and official circulars. The former often relies on professional experiential knowledge, while the latter remains at the level of passive retrieval; both rely on predefined rules and professional experience and suffer from a time lag. Recently emerging Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents, which possess both natural language understanding and multi-step task execution capabilities, make it possible to acquire and fulfill users’ retrieval demands in a fast and flexible manner through human–machine dialogue. Inspired by this, this paper constructs a multimodal clue retrieval agent for ecological environmental damage based on a multi-agent framework. The agent interacts with users who lack computer professional and technical backgrounds through natural language via LLMs to clarify their retrieval demands regarding specified regions, time periods, and damage types. It then orchestrates different sub-agents to automatically retrieve textual clues and remote sensing image clues within the corresponding spatiotemporal scope in a cross-modal manner, and aggregates and presents textual and image evidence to users to support the review and analysis of problem clues. Testing and evaluation conducted by researchers in the field of procuratorial case handling show that the proposed method achieves satisfactory retrieval performance and usability, and is simple and easy to learn. It can provide technical support for the screening and assessment of ecological environmental damage issues.
