To explore EMP1 roles, overexpression and knockdown experiments were conducted using human peripheral blood neutrophils, with migration assessed via transwell assays. Neutrophil abundance was notably increased in tumor tissue. Among eight neutrophil subtypes, neutro4 showed highest migration-related activation. Through comprehensive analyses, we identified 28 candidate genes associated with neutrophil migration. The stepCox + RSF composite model was selected as optimal (average C-index = 0.7, AUC > 0.7), incorporating EMP1 and RBP7 biomarkers involved in specific biological processes with complex non-coding regulatory networks. These biomarkers correlated with bladder cancer clinical phenotypes. RT-qPCR confirmed RBP7 and EMP1 were significantly downregulated in tumors ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, functional experiments revealed that EMP1 overexpression significantly enhanced neutrophil migration. This study provides a better understanding of neutrophil roles in bladder cancer. The identified biomarkers and constructed prognostic model offer potential clinical value for diagnosis and prognosis assessment, which may contribute to more effective treatment strategies. Functional experiments validate EMP1’s biological significance in neutrophil migration, supporting its potential as a therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Self-motion perception influences postural sway more than environmental motion perception
Article.Authors: Anson E.; Critelli K.; Chen E.; Staab J.; Carpenter M.; Crane B.
Article.Abstract: Motion of the visual field can alter postural sway and cause illusions of self-motion. The relative perceptual sensitivity of self-motion versus visual field motion induced by virtual reality (VR) stimulation and whether observable sway differs based on perceptual task is unknown. Methods to quantify sway perception while concurrently measuring sway do not exist. We measured head sway and motion perception (self or world) in healthy adults who stood with feet together wearing a VR headset while experiencing adaptive staircases of virtual sinusoidal pitch rotation about the ankle axis. In separate conditions of randomly ordered blocks, subjects were asked to indicate (yes/no) if the room moved (regardless of perceived postural sway) or if their postural sway increased (regardless of perceived room motion). Head sway area was measured by tracking movement of the VR headset. Yes/No responses were fit with psychometric curves to determine points of subjective equality (PSEs) for room motion and postural sway. PSEs were compared between conditions. Effects of motion perception (binary responses) on head sway area before, during, and after visual stimulation were examined. Article.Title: Deep learning analysis of echo signals from a single piezoelectric element for breast mass detection: a proof-of-concept study

On additional validation, ultrasound pre-training gave higher region-level AUCs than ImageNet initialization (ResNet-50, 93.6% versus 91.7%; ViT-B/16, 96.3% versus 93.2%) and more mass-focused Grad-CAM heatmaps. For ViT-B/16, the advantage grew as training data decreased. Conventional spatial augmentation gave most of the gain (ViT-B/16, 96.8% versus 93.2%), and VSPA added little. Article.Title: A technical framework for HR-driven imbalanced classification: pipeline architecture, oversampling algorithms, ablation analysis, and threshold engineering for data scientist job-change prediction
Article.Authors: Mazumdar A.; Ahmed M.; Btissam C.; Shil H.; Khan N.; Jamali M.; Bashir M.; Aurin M.; Rabby S.; Ray S.; Azad M.; Haque M.; Mamoon I.
Article.Abstract: Predictive modelling of employee job-change propensity from HR survey data presents a canonical cluster of machine-learning engineering challenges: structured mixed-type inputs with systematic missingness, moderate class imbalance, and self-reported labels susceptible to noise. This paper presents the technical design and implementation of an end-to-end HR analytics pipeline applied to the HR Analytics: Job Change of Data Scientists dataset ( \(N = 19{,}158\) ; positive rate \(\approx 24.9\%\) ). We formalise the leak-safe imbalanced-learn Pipeline architecture that confines synthetic oversampling strictly to training folds and empirically quantify—via a controlled leaky-versus-clean experiment—that naive pre-split oversampling inflates 5-fold cross-validated AUC by 0.014–0.018 units for SMOTE-family methods, a margin sufficient to reverse configuration rankings. Nine oversampling algorithms are instantiated and evaluated across 90 model \(\times\) sampler configurations. A systematic ablation study of the feature engineering pipeline identifies missingness indicator construction ( \(\Delta \textrm{AUC} = -0.008\) when removed) and out-of-fold smoothed target encoding ( \(\Delta \textrm{AUC} = -0.009\) ) as the two highest-value components. HistGradientBoosting on the unaugmented training distribution achieves the highest holdout ROC-AUC of 0.816 [95% CI 0.800, 0.832]; all pairwise sampler AUC differences fall within this \(\pm 0.016\) estimation band and are not statistically significant. With threshold optimisation applied uniformly across configurations, performance differences between the best unresampled and best oversampled alternatives are within the confidence interval (F1 \(= 0.644\) vs. 0.648; \(\Delta = 0.004\) , overlapping bootstrap CIs), though oversampled configurations achieve meaningfully higher recall (73.6% vs. 78.1%). Article.Title: Source informed dual expert machine learning combining Gaussian and Boltzmann representations for sequential twin tunnel settlement prediction
Article.Authors: Rostami A.; Mahdevari S.; Shahriar K.; Rostami J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sequential excavation of twin tunnels creates a staged settlement problem because the second drive acts on ground already affected by the first. In nested five fold evaluation of 52 staged HSsmall numerical scenarios, VF predicted ΔS with R 2 = 0.839 and RMSE = 0.2315 cm, nearly identical to the Gaussian expert (0.2324 cm) and lower than the Boltzmann expert (0.2578 cm). Additional conventional baselines showed that a raw design ExtraTrees model achieved lower RMSE for S1 and S2 (0.9492 and 1.0592 cm) than VF (1.0761 and 1.1856 cm), whereas VF retained the lowest ΔS RMSE among the added baseline set (next lowest 0.2379 cm for gradient boosting). Thus, the evidence supports response dependent representation use rather than universal ensemble dominance. Blocked family testing exposed poor extrapolation for Isfahan S1 and S2 when complete response families were absent from training. VF is supported as a leakage controlled numerical surrogate within the audited HSsmall domain; independent field validation remains required before physical predictive use.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal analysis of shoreline changes in Mobile Bay, U.S.A.
Article.Authors: Nourin F.; Dey H.; Shao W.; Munasinghe D.
Article.Abstract: Shoreline changes affect coastal communities by altering ecosystems and storm buffers. With the growth of coastal populations, the societal impact of shoreline change is expected to increase. Understanding the past and present shoreline positions is thus essential for managing coastal hazards and supporting population as well as ecosystem services. This study quantifies shoreline change rates and evaluates the persistence and variability of shoreline behavior in Mobile Bay, U.S., over the past 25 years (2000​–2024 inclusive). CoastSat, an open-source Python software toolkit built on the cloud computing platform Google Earth Engine (GEE), is used to detect shoreline positions and analyze change rates. Furthermore, the Hurst exponent analysis is applied to the shoreline change rate of 396 shore-normal transects to assess the persistence or randomness of shoreline change behavior. The findings reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity in shoreline dynamics across Mobile Bay, with Dauphin Island exhibiting the highest erosion rate (−5.4 m/yr), the greatest shoreline variability between the northern and southern shore, and the strongest responses to major hurricane events. In contrast, the more sheltered estuarine shorelines towards the riverine delta experienced smaller shoreline displacements and more localized variability. The integration of persistence analysis with conventional erosion-accretion assessments enabled the distinction between persistently erosional, persistently accretional, and highly variable shoreline segments, providing additional insight into long-term and short-term shoreline behavior. The findings contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of shoreline dynamics and support site-specific coastal management, hazard mitigation, and the implementation of nature-based solutions.

Associations between demographic characteristics and double-locus-variant clonal complex membership were assessed using binary logistic regression. The 24-locus scheme showed high discriminatory power (HGDI = 0.9896). Among genotyped isolates, LAM was predominant (29.1%), followed by Beijing (9.7%), Ghana (3.9%), S (2.9%), Haarlem (1.9%), West African 1 (1.9%), and West African 2 (1​%); 49.5% of isolates were unassigned. UPGMA identified five identical-profile clusters comprising 17 isolates (16.5%), corresponding to an estimated recent transmission rate of 11.6%. Article.Title: Aversive conditioning prevents perceptual habituation, but not cortical adaptation to odors
Article.Authors: Oleszkiewicz A.; Riedel F.; Sinding C.; Hummel T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To save attentional resources, the human brain learns to decrease its response to non-threatening stimuli. The decreased behavioral response is known as habituation, while the decreased peripheral and central neural response is called adaptation. In this investigation, we were interested in whether initially non-threatening olfactory stimuli, when paired with aversive shock, may become less prone to habituation and adaptation. To this end, in 46 individuals (24 females; M age =24.8 ± 5.7 years), we examined changes in cortical response and perceptual assessments of three odors, of which one was conditioned (i.e. paired with electric shock) and the remaining two were unconditioned. The conditioned odor was randomized across the participants. We report that aversive conditioning can prevent odor habituation, but we did not find support for the hypothesis that aversive conditioning prevents odor adaptation. We propose that aversive conditioning can be a method of maintaining olfactory alertness in those, who remain at risk of malodor exposure and may unintentionally get used to it, inflating the risk of negative consequences of this exposure.

Article.Title: The sulfur budget and composition of arc magmas and cumulates
Article.Authors: Hehn P.; Keith M.; Strauss H.; Kutzschbach M.; Haase K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subduction zones play an important role in the global S cycle, because recycling of altered oceanic crust and overlying sediments transfers different S species, particularly sulfide and sulfate, into the mantle. These affect the S contents, the S isotope composition and possibly the redox conditions in the mantle, as reflected by arc magmas along subduction zones. We compiled S and Cu contents together with ​ δ 34 S data of arc magmas and associated sulfides and show that ascending magmas in arcs typically become sulfide-saturated at Mg# ~ 55, evidenced by decreasing S and Cu concentrations. This effect may promote Ni-Cu sulfide deposit formation by removing > 70% of the S and Cu budget of mafic magmas in the deep arc crust. Sulfur isotope data of sulfide-bearing cumulates imply that most primitive magmas in Phanerozoic and Precambrian arcs have low δ 34 S values (− 2 to + 3‰) that overlap with mid-ocean ridge basalt (− 0.9 ± 0.5‰). Sulfide segregation drives positive δ 34 S shifts in residual melts by preferentially sequestering isotopically light S into magmatic sulfides, particularly in relatively oxidized magmas. Greater S isotope variability in Phanerozoic than Proterozoic arc magmas probably reflect the more variable δ 34 S of subducted sediments, whereas slab-derived sulfate has little effect on magma redox state.

Article.Title: Assessment of potential bias mechanisms in the analysis of large electronic medical record datasets
Article.Authors: Janssens A.; Crèvecoeur J.; Libin P.; Van Pottelbergh G.; Vaes B.; Neyens T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electronic medical records aid general practitioners in the follow-up of their patients. The vast amounts of patient data that are being collected through such electronic medical records offer opportunities to use them for other purposes such as epidemiological and (pre)clinical research. But the use of electronic medical record data for research purposes raises concerns about potential biases, since these data are typically not collected within a study design specifically developed to address a predefined research question, which may instead emerge during or after data collection. In addition, data collection practices and reporting behaviours can vary between general practitioners, while patients themselves differ in their likelihood of seeking care or reporting symptoms. Although a large patient population may mitigate some of these random variations through the law of large numbers, systematic biases related to the non-randomized sample of the participating practices and heterogeneity in patient characteristics may persist. If not appropriately accounted for, these sources of heterogeneity and potential bias can lead to different or potentially conflicting research findings. Using a large electronic medical records dataset from Flanders, Belgium, we assess how simple statistical approaches, such as adding practice-level random effects and changing the analytical entity, can help identify potential bias mechanisms and assess the sensitivity of estimated associations to them.

Article.Title: The joint association of glycated haemoglobin and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol with type 2 diabetic neuropathy
Article.Authors: Lv N.; Gao S.; Li K.; Ru Z.; Liang N.; Wang L.; Zhang X.; Wang M.; Han T.; Qiao H.
Article.Abstract: Neuropathy is highly prevalent and has a poor prognosis in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients. T2DM is accompanied by abnormal glucose and lipid metabolism. After adjustment for confounding factors, compared with HbA1c < 7%, both HbA1c 7–9% and ≥ 9% were associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy [HR = 1.62 (1.31–2.01); P < 0.001; HR = 2.44 (1.76–3.38); P < 0.001] in the UKB; compared with LDL-C < 2.6 mmol/L, LDL-C ≥ 2.6 mmol/L did not increase the risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy [HR = 1.06(0.81–1.40); P = 0.675]. Compared with LDL-C ≥ 2.6 mmol/L combined with HbA1c < 7%, LDL-C ≥ 2.6 mmol/L combined with HbA1c ≥ 9% increased the risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy [HR = 2.80 (1.76–4.48); P < 0.001]. LDL-C is not associated with type 2 diabetic neuropathy. Article.Title: SRSF3-mediated post-transcriptional regulation of SERPINH1 promotes tumor growth and immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Yan H.; Zhu L.; Liu B.; Liu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by aggressive progression and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Gain- and loss-of-function approaches were used to evaluate the effects of SRSF3 on HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and cytokine secretion in vitro. RNA immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the interaction between SRSF3 and SERPINH1 mRNA. Tumor growth, immune cell infiltration, and fibrosis were analyzed in mouse tumor models with SRSF3 manipulation or overexpression of distinct SERPINH1 isoforms using flow cytometry, histology, and immunofluorescence. Among SERPINH1 isoforms, the short isoform exerted the strongest pro-tumorigenic and pro-fibrotic effects, promoting collagen deposition, tumor proliferation, and immune exclusion. Our findings identify SRSF3 as a critical driver of HCC progression by orchestrating tumor growth, fibrosis, and immune evasion through regulation of SERPINH1, particularly its short isoform. Targeting the SRSF3–SERPINH1 axis may represent a promising strategy to simultaneously inhibit tumor progression and improve antitumor immune responses in HCC.

Article.Authors: Bacha T.; Ali U.; Belissa S.; Tolani T.; Mendera J.; Barwant M.; Ogidi O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is a vital source of dietary protein and income for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia, yet productivity is severely limited by strong genotype × environment interaction (G×E). AMMI stability value (ASV) and Yield Stability Index (YSI) were computed to rank genotypes. The overall mean yield was 3115.88 kg/ha⁻¹. The first interaction principal component (IPCA1) captured 64.25% of the G×E sum of squares. Based on ASV, the most stable genotypes were Dinkinesh (ASV = 16.30), Nasir (16.86), and SCR 15 (17.89). However, Nasir combined the highest mean yield (3807.25 kg/ha⁻¹) with excellent stability, while Awash 2 (3206.25 kg/ha⁻¹) showed above-average yield and moderate stability (ASV = 24.37). The AMMI1 biplot confirmed Nasir and Awash 2 as high-yielding, stable genotypes, whereas Tole and Dabo Hana were identified as highly interactive, high-yielding environments. The single-year data underscore the necessity of multi-season validation before large-scale deployment. These findings provide a basis for enhancing common bean productivity and food security in western Ethiopia.

Article.Authors: Liao X.; Du Y.; Yi S.; Zhang W.; Wang W.; Liu X.; Cai J.; Yang X.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Landslide susceptibility models are strongly influenced by the spatial scale at which conditioning factors and landslide inventories are represented. A regional model was developed using six conditioning factors derived from 30 m DEM and Landsat imagery, while a segment-scale model incorporated 12.5 m ALOS PALSAR DEM-derived geomorphic indices and GF-2 interpreted landslide polygons. The segment model achieved the best overall performance (AUC = 0.9375; F1-score = 0.8566), whereas the transfer model showed high precision (0.9167) but lower recall (0.6667). Its recall further decreased from 0.818 for large landslides to 0.477 for small landslides, indicating limited transferability of the regional factor system to fine-scale landslide identification. Feature-importance analysis showed that the dominant conditioning factors varied with assessment scale, with river-related factors being more influential at the regional scale and tectonic and local hydrological/topographic factors becoming more important at the segment scale. These results indicate that increasing spatial resolution alone cannot compensate for the loss of process-relevant information in a scale-inappropriate factor system. Landslide susceptibility assessment should therefore match the spatial resolution, conditioning factors, and geomorphic processes to the target assessment scale.

Article.Authors: Abecia J.; Campo M.; Martínez Á.; Palacios C.
Article.Abstract: The sudden reduction in daylight during a total solar eclipse provides a unique natural setting to investigate how animals respond to an unexpected transition towards darkness. Responses differed markedly among species and populations. Sheep exhibited a pronounced but transient reduction in LA around totality, followed by a rapid recovery. Activity during the early post-totality period was lower than on reference days (P = 0.039), although this difference was not consistently supported by broader statistical analyses. In laying hens, the eclipse coincided with changes in evening activity, including an earlier transition towards sustained inactivity in Zaragoza and pronounced activity suppression in Burgos. In contrast, free-ranging mares showed no consistent group-level response. Physiological measurements revealed no uniform changes in body T or HR associated with the eclipse. These findings indicate that a late-day total solar eclipse can coincide with short-lived changes in livestock behaviour, particularly in species exhibiting pronounced evening activity transitions. However, the diversity of responses and the proximity of the eclipse to natural sunset suggest that its behavioural effects cannot be separated entirely from normal dusk-related processes.

Four metaheuristics did not improve on rule-based valley filling, harmonic-aware and harmonic-blind schedules coincided, and vehicle-to-grid lowered the hourly objective only when battery throughput was weighted below 0.08–0.14, without network benefit at one-minute resolution. With non-linear household loads the households dominated the distortion and no filter was needed for any schedule.

Article.Abstract: Despite increasing policy attention to aesthetic education, college students’ responses to aesthetic education courses remain a concern in China. This study examined students’ perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement and its associations with creativity and attitude in an optimised course integrating Chinese literati painting. A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design involved 793 students from six intact classes across three higher education institutions in Shanxi Province, China. Individual-level analyses indicated both a pre-post increase in perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement in the experimental group and higher baseline-adjusted post-test scores than in the control group. Neither finding was statistically supported after accounting for class-level clustering. Within the experimental group, primary and baseline-adjusted structural equation models used individual-level and class-clustered inference. The positive associations of creativity with attitude and of attitude with perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement retained statistical support across these analyses. Statistical support for the direct creativity-outcome association and the indirect association through attitude was less consistent. Based on the findings, the proposed model offers a framework for further investigation of the relationships among creativity, attitude, and perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement rather than an established causal explanation.

Article.Title: A generative approach for synthetic image-response in surface plasmon resonance sensors
Article.Authors: Saraiva J.; Fernandes S.; Oliveira L.; Lima A.
Article.Abstract: A generative approach for the automatic generation of surface plasmon resonance (SPR) image-responses is presented. The modern development of SPR sensors is driven by machine learning (ML) interventions that require data related to the sensors’ operation, with the intention of anticipating behaviors, predicting responses, and accelerating the design, optimization, and utilization of this type of sensor. The cost to produce SPR data in terms of time, material consumption, and experimental complexity associated with the absence of a public dataset of SPR images, makes it difficult to develop effective intelligent solutions for SPR sensors. The methodological proposition is based on a generative adversarial network (GAN) model to generate​ synthetic SPR images, reducing experimental data dependence, accelerating research workflows, and supporting intelligent biosensor advancement through complementary synthetic data. Manual​ creation of Fresnel images based on Kretschmann-configuration experimental SPR images of aqueous solutions was employed as training data. The results of synthetic images were quantitatively and qualitatively evaluated, in particular for a deep-convolutional GAN (DCGAN), indicating the feasibility of the model to generate two-dimensional SPR images. The latent space generated by DCGAN was explored in different scenarios of image generation, and the utility of the generative approach is attested in the substance classification task, leading to a model improvement of the main performance metrics.

Article.Title: Traumatic PVR prevention and treatment via composite drug film
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Liu Y.; Liu J.; Zhu T.; Nan K.; Chen M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to develop a composite sustained-release drug film by incorporating triamcinolone acetonide (TA) and daunorubicin (DNR) into a poly-L-lactide caprolactone (P(LLA-CL)) matrix, and to evaluate its in vitro release characteristics, in vivo biocompatibility, and therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of traumatic proliferative vitreoretinopathy (TPVR). P(LLA-CL) was dissolved in hexafluoroisopropanol, weighed TA and DNR powder, and added it to the P(LLA-CL) solution, and then electrospinning was performed on these materials to prepare P(LLA-CL)-TA, P(LLA-CL)-DNR, and P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR composite drug films. In vitro release experiments were performed on drug films (4 × 8 mm) and corresponding drug powders placed in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). At fixed time points, samples were collected and drug content was calculated by HPLC to record the cumulative drug release curve. The in vivo safety of the drug films was evaluated by suturing the drug films onto the rabbit eyes sclera, 5 mm away from the limbus, and then observing slit-lamp biomicroscopy, intraocular pressure (IOP), and histopathological changes at fixed time points from 1 week to 6 months after suturing. TPVR was constructed by scleral injury and autologous blood injection, and the rabbits were randomly divided into model, control, P(LLA-CL)-TA, P(LLA-CL)-DNR, and composite drug film groups. The observation indices were fundus photography, HE staining, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) analysis of inflammatory factors TNF-α and TGF-β. In vitro release experiment results showed that the P(LLA-CL)-TA and P(LLA-CL)-DNR drug films released the drugs for 156 and 135 days, and the cumulative drug release rates reached 88.41% and 92.68%, respectively. The composite P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR drug film released TA and DNR for 141 days (91.54%) and 129 days (89.31%) respectively, which were greatly prolonged compared with the release time of the drugs powders (48 days and 4 days for TA and DNR, respectively). In vivo experiment results showed that no ocular toxicity or IOP elevation was induced by the drug films. The gradual degradation of drug films was observed during the six-month observation period. In therapeutic application, the composite drug film reduced the retinal folding, preretinal membrane formation and TNF-α mean optical density at 2 weeks [(0.426 ± 0.036) vs. (0.518 ± 0.043) in the model group, P < 0.0001] and at 4 weeks [(0.460 ± 0.040) vs. (0.537 ± 0.029), P = 0.0003], and improved the vitreous hemorrhage ( P = 0.0402). P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR composite drug film can achieve sustained release of therapeutic agents for up to five months. The drug film exhibits a good safety profile, and showed preliminary therapeutic potential to attenuate TPVR progression via suppressing inflammatory response and cellular proliferation. Compared with single-drug films, the composite film showed marginal improvement of vitreous hemorrhage absorption and reduced retinal proliferation.

Article.Title: A unified aperture-based framework for modeling fracture capillary pressure and relative permeability in multiphase flow
Article.Authors: Golsefatan A.; Shadizadeh S.; Behbahani H.
Article.Abstract: Fracture capillary pressure and relative permeability strongly influence multiphase flow in fractured porous media, yet fracture-flow representations commonly assume zero capillary pressure and linear relative permeability. This study develops a unified aperture-based constitutive framework for fracture capillary pressure and relative permeability from statistical fracture-aperture characteristics. Fracture aperture is represented by a lognormal distribution parameterized by its mean and log-space standard deviation. Capillary pressure is formulated using a local Young–Laplace capillary-equilibrium relationship and an aperture-based phase-occupancy criterion, while relative permeability is obtained by integrating aperture-dependent phase flow with a saturation-dependent tortuosity closure. The framework is intended primarily for quasi-static and capillary-dominated conditions and does not explicitly resolve dynamic capillary effects, fracture deformation, network topology, disconnected pathways, or directional/tensorial network-scale behavior. Model assessment distinguishes cases with independently specified aperture-distribution parameters from calibration cases in which the aperture parameter is inferred from target data. Comparisons with published analytical and experimental datasets reproduce the principal trends of the investigated capillary-pressure and relative-permeability relationships. The framework provides a compact aperture-based constitutive representation, while its applicability beyond the investigated conditions requires further independent experimental assessment.

Article.Title: Biliary bile acid profiling reveals diagnostic signatures for cholangiocarcinoma and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Arif M.; Braadland P.; Larsson E.; Darwich L.; Natali L.; Burza M.; Hedenström P.; Hov J.; Henricsson M.; Sadik R.; Molinaro A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The early diagnosis of biliopancreatic cancers, including cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), remains challenging because currently available serum biomarkers have limited diagnostic accuracy. Bile acids are bioactive signaling molecules implicated in carcinogenesis and may reflect disease-specific alterations within the biliary microenvironment. We aimed to characterize biliary bile acid profiles in patients with PDAC and CCA and evaluate their diagnostic potential. Bile samples were prospectively collected from the common bile duct during endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) in 71 individuals, including noncancer controls (CTRL, n = 41), patients with PDAC ( n = 14), and patients with CCA ( n = 16). Quantitative bile acid profiling was performed with ultra-performance liquid chromatography‒tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC‒MS‒MS/MS). Random forest, stability selection, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and elastic net algorithms were used as feature-selection methods to identify diagnostic bile acid signatures, which were evaluated using five-fold cross-validated receiver operating characteristic analysis. PDAC was associated with higher total and primary bile-acid concentrations than CCA, including higher cholic acid concentrations. Compared with controls, CCA was associated with lower total secondary bile-acid concentrations ( p = 0.009), including lower deoxycholic acid ( p = 0.013), lithocholic acid ( p = 0.021), and ursodeoxycholic acid ( p = 0.023) concentrations. After adjustment for bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase, glycocholic acid, taurochenodeoxycholic acid, and taurohyocholic acid were selected by all four feature-selection methods. Their combined model achieved a cross-validated area under the curve of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.79–0.90), compared with 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58–0.76) for CA19-9 and 0.61 (95% CI, 0.51–0.71) for CEA. A separate bile-acid model distinguished CCA from PDAC with an area under the curve of 0.87 (95% CI, 0.72–0.99), 85.7% sensitivity, and 87.5% specificity. CCA and PDAC patients exhibit distinct biliary bile acid profiles. Bile acid signatures identified after adjustment for cholestasis may complement conventional serum biomarkers during ERCP-based evaluation of indeterminate biliary strictures.

Article.Title: The systemic immune-inflammation index is associated with prevalent chronic kidney disease in adults with hypertension
Article.Authors: Duan H.; Zhao Z.; Zhang J.; Li M.; Lou T.; Yin Y.; Ma S.; Zhao M.; Zhang Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypertension and chronic kidney disease (CKD) interact bidirectionally, forming a vicious cycle, while chronic low-grade inflammation represents a central pathway mediating hypertensive renal injury. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), calculated from routine complete blood count parameters, comprehensively reflects systemic inflammatory and immune imbalance. However, evidence from large-scale stratified analyses and robust validation remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between SII and prevalent CKD in adults with hypertension in a nationally representative sample and to assess the consistency of the findings across multiple propensity score weighting approaches. This cross-sectional study included 18,675 adults with hypertension from the 2001–2020 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Analyses accounted for NHANES examination weights, strata, and primary sampling units. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and stratified interaction analyses were performed. The consistency of the findings was assessed using propensity score weighting approaches targeting the average treatment effect (ATE), the average treatment effect among the treated, and the average treatment effect in the overlap population. After full adjustment, each 1-standard-deviation increment in log1p-transformed SII was associated with higher odds of CKD (OR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.04–1.17, P = 0.002). Compared with the lowest SII quartile, the highest quartile had higher odds of CKD (OR = 1.23; 95% CI, 1.03–1.47, P = 0.023). The fully adjusted spline showed a significant overall association ( P = 0.002), whereas the test for nonlinearity was not significant ( P = 0.267). The association was stronger among participants younger than 60 years ( P for interaction = 0.017). Overlap weighting yielded an OR of 1.192 (95% CI, 1.064–1.334, P = 0.002) for high versus low SII. Higher SII was associated with greater odds of CKD among individuals with hypertension. SII may serve as an auxiliary inflammatory biomarker associated with CKD in individuals with hypertension.

Article.Title: Alzheimer’s disease fMRI image classification and hippocampal region detection using faster R-CNN deep learning algorithm
Article.Authors: Wei X.; Huang R.; Cai X.; Liu X.; Li J.; Ban Y.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by early hippocampal degeneration and microvascular alterations preceding overt neocortical atrophy. Accessible, automated, and interpretable screening from non-invasive neuroimaging remains a clinical challenge. To develop and benchmark a multi-task Faster R-CNN framework for simultaneous AD classification and bilateral hippocampal localization on resting-state fMRI. This retrospective study analyzed 200 participants (100 AD, 100 cognitively normal [CN]) from institutional and public (ADNI, OASIS-3) cohorts. The cohort was partitioned at the participant level into training (70%, n = 140), validation (15%, n = 30), and held-out test (15%, n = 30; 15 AD, 15 CN) sets. Crucially, to preserve steady-state T2* susceptibility contrast and structural hippocampal boundaries without zero-frequency signal loss, voxel-wise temporal-mean functional volumes were calculated from realigned and spatially normalized resting-state fMRI data prior to nuisance regression and band-pass filtering. ComBat harmonization was fitted exclusively on training data. Six contiguous axial slices spanning the bilateral hippocampi (1,200 slices total; 2,400 expert-adjudicated bounding boxes) were extracted. A multi-task Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50 backbone was trained under a unified loss combining proposal regression, objectness, and a dual-hippocampal disease classification head. Subject diagnosis was determined via probability averaging across slices. On the independent held-out test cohort (N = 30), the model achieved 93.3% accuracy (28/30; 95% CI 78.7–98.2%), 93.3% sensitivity (14/15; 95% CI 70.2–98.8%), 93.3% specificity (14/15; 95% CI 70.2–98.8%), and an AUC of 0.95 (95% CI 0.87–0.99). In exploratory subgroup evaluations, test accuracy was 91.3% in mild AD (n = 8 AD, n = 15 CN; 95% CI 72.0–98.9%) and 95.5% in moderate AD (n = 7 AD, n = 15 CN; 95% CI 77.2–99.9%). Accounting for within-subject clustering across the 360 test bounding boxes, a Linear Mixed-Effects Model confirmed that hippocampal localization significantly surpassed fixed Harvard–Oxford atlas templates (IoU 0.87 ± 0.04 vs. 0.72 ± 0.06; beta = + 0.155, SE = 0.0034, Wald z = 45.18, p < 0.001; subject-level paired t(29) = 45.15, p < 0.001). On non-hippocampal axial slices (n = 60), the detector yielded 59 true negatives and 1 false positive, demonstrating 98.3% slice specificity (95% CI 91.1–99.7%). The framework surpassed baseline CNN (80.0%, p = 0.046), SVM (76.7%, p = 0.031), and Random Forest (76.7%, p = 0.031) classifiers. The multi-task Faster R-CNN provides accurate AD classification and interpretable hippocampal detection on temporal-mean resting-state fMRI, demonstrating encouraging preliminary feasibility for automated computer-aided screening. However, given the broad confidence intervals inherent to the small independent test sample (N = 30), prospective validation in larger, multi-center prodromal cohorts is required prior to clinical translation.

Article.Title: Machine-learning-based landslide susceptibility mapping using an InSAR-Refined Inventory in the Mandi district, Northwestern Himalaya, India
Article.Authors: Manocha A.; Hieu T.; Pawlik Ł.; Kroh P.; Quan N.
Article.Abstract: Landslides triggered by intense monsoon rainfall and active tectonics pose a persistent threat to transportation corridors and settlements in the Mandi district of the Northwestern Himalaya. Most existing susceptibility assessments for this region rely on historical inventories that do not include currently moving. This study tests whether refining a historical landslide inventory with Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) improves machine-learning susceptibility mapping in Mandi district. Sentinel-1A data from January 2023 to December 2024 (59 ascending and 43 descending acquisitions) were processed with Persistent Scatterer (StaMPS) and Small Baseline Subset (MintPy) interferometry. Active deformation areas were used to refine the Geological Survey of India’s Bhukosh inventory of 968 landslides, which consists mainly of slides, by adding 1,685 InSAR-derived landslide points, including 36 field-verified new landslides. Twelve uncorrelated topographic, hydrological, geological, climatic, and anthropogenic conditioning factors were selected using Pearson correlation and variance inflation factor analysis. Four machine learning algorithms, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Multilayer Perceptron, were trained and compared using a nested spatial block cross-validation framework across block sizes of 1,000–10,000 m. XGB achieved the best performance at an optimal block size of 2000 m, and the InSAR-based XGB model generally showed higher ROC-AUC and PR-AUC, along with lower ECE and Brier scores, indicating improved discrimination, calibration, and probabilistic accuracy across spatial validation scales (at 2 km: ROC-AUC 0.887 vs 0.878; expected calibration error 0.067 vs 0.097). SHAP and Mean Decrease Accuracy (MDA) plots identified distance to roads and slope as the dominant predisposing factors. . The map was categorized into five susceptibility zones using a curvature-based break-point detection approach, with a success rate of AUC of 0.909, indicating very good discrimination of areas with different susceptibility levels. The map represents susceptibility to slide-type landslides. Areas outside the AOA accounted for only 1.1% of the study region, indicating that the model can be reliably applied across most of the study area. These results demonstrate that coupling InSAR-derived deformation with machine learning substantially improves the completeness and calibration of the model of landslide susceptibility mapping, offering a scalable approach for hazard mitigation and land-use planning in tectonically active Himalayan terrain.

Article.Title: Knowledge attitudes and risk perceptions of herbal remedies among Palestinian adults in a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Abu basha A.; Dahdooh A.; Mokhaimar T.; Altell O.; Malhis D.
Article.Abstract: Herbal remedies are widely used, but perceptions of safety may differ from knowledge of potential harms. The aim of this study was to examine herbal remedy use, risk knowledge, attitudes, and perceived safety among surveyed Palestinian adults. A cross-sectional convenience survey recruited 303 adults in the West Bank between March and April 2026. Respondents were predominantly younger adults, women, university-educated individuals, and students. Risk-related knowledge was assessed using a nine-item score (range 0–9), while perceived safety was measured using a five-category ordinal response. Knowledge and perceived safety were analyzed as separate outcomes, and their association was assessed using Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient. Prior herbal or natural remedy use for health purposes was reported by 88.4% of respondents. The mean knowledge score was 5.5 ± 2.5 out of 9, with item-level correct-response proportions ranging from 44.9% to 84.8%. Regarding perceived safety, 56.4% selected a neutral rating, 28.1% considered herbal remedies safe or very safe, and 15.5% considered them dangerous. Knowledge was inversely associated with perceived safety (Spearman’s ρ = −0.286, p < 0.001). In the adjusted linear regression, male respondents had lower knowledge scores than female respondents (B = − 1.41, 95% CI − 2.05 to − 0.77, p < 0.001). Self-reported herbal or natural remedy use for health purposes was common among surveyed respondents, while knowledge of possible harms and perceived safety varied. Higher knowledge scores were modestly associated with lower perceived safety ratings. Because the sample was recruited by convenience and predominantly comprised younger, female, and student respondents, the results should not be generalized to the Palestinian population or interpreted as evidence of actual clinical harm.

Article.Title: Theoretical study on the in-plane vertical and rotational coupled vibration of a shield cutter head
Article.Authors: Zhou F.; Liu S.; Deng T.; Xie Z.; Yang H.; Lin Z.; Zhou W.; Cao K.
Article.Abstract: During shield tunnelling, cutter head vibration not only affects face stability but also accelerates structural fatigue and cutter wear. To address the coupled vibration effect induced by the combined action of gravity and drive torque, this paper presents a comprehensive theoretical method for analysing the in-plane vertical-rotational coupled vibration response of the shield cutter head. First, the cutter head is modelled as a thin elastic circular plate with clamped edges, which is discretised using the localized radial basis function (LRBF) method, and its free vibration characteristics are obtained via the modified QR algorithm. Second, a two-degree-of-freedom mass-spring-damper model is established to simulate the cutter head system, and a coupling stiffness is introduced to account for the interaction between vertical displacement and rotational angle. Subsequently, the multi-scale perturbation method is applied to separate fast and slow time scales and eliminate secular terms, thereby enabling a reduced-order solution of the coupled vibration equations and yielding the amplitude and phase evolution equations as well as the frequency response functions. Finally, a case study indicates that the vertical-rotational coupling causes a shift in the natural frequencies of the cutter head, resulting in two new coupled frequencies. This frequency splitting is attributed to energy exchange between the vertical and rotational modes: the low-frequency mode is dominated by rotational vibration, whereas the high-frequency mode exhibits stronger modal coupling. Within the assumptions of harmonic excitation and linear coupling, the frequency splitting amount ΔΩ increases nonlinearly with increasing coupling stiffness and cutter head diameter, suggesting that the modal coupling becomes more intensive. Thus, the vertical-rotational coupling effect should be carefully considered for ultra-large diameter shields. Design should prioritise cutter layout optimisation to reduce coupling stiffness, or increase rotational stiffness to separate the natural frequencies, thereby weakening the risk of coupled vibration. This paper elucidates the energy transfer mechanism between the two modes and provides a theoretical basis for vibration control.

Article.Title: Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
Article.Authors: Park D.; Kwon Y.; Han S.; Yoo P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology firms, the framework uncovers asymmetric competitive momentum, contested market leadership, and emerging challenger dynamics. By bridging relational time-series forecasting with structured multi-agent deliberation, this study advances competitive dynamics analysis from purely accuracy-centric prediction toward context-aware, uncertainty-informed strategic intelligence.

Article.Title: Study on similar materials for the asphalt concrete impervious layer of the pumped-storage upper reservoir in a karst area
Article.Authors: Xu C.; Chen S.; Du Q.; Zhang Y.; Han X.; Long Z.; Zhang C.; Gou Y.; Yuan S.
Article.Abstract: Groundwater–air pressure may break the full-basin impervious systems in pumped-storage reservoirs built in karst depressions. This study developed polyurethane-based similar materials for asphalt concrete impervious layers. An L9(3 4 ) orthogonal design was used to evaluate the formulation factors. Mechanical and permeability tests, weighted grey relational analysis, uplift loading, and SEM–EDS were used for formulation screening and validation. Across the nine formulations, elastic modulus, flexural modulus, flexural strength, and maximum flexural tensile strain ranged from 1.47 to 5.07 MPa, 2.10 to 12.42 MPa, 0.11 to 1.02 MPa, and 4.12% to 13.69%, respectively. Results showed that the curing ratio had the greatest effect on flexural modulus and maximum flexural tensile strain, whereas talc powder increased stiffness and DOP enhanced deformation capacity. The novel mechanical uplift tests were carried out, and result showed that the deformation and cracking processes broadly similar to those of the asphalt concrete prototype. The material group X5 also exhibited more uniform talc dispersion and matrix encapsulation than material groups X1 and X9. This study provides a method for preparing similar materials with adjustable deformation and strength properties for physical model studies of asphalt concrete impervious structures.

Article.Title: Hill-based reformulation of the Hodgkin-Huxley model for mapping gating changes to neuronal excitability
Article.Authors: Saab B.; Fahs J.; Daou A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conductance-based models link ion-channel gating to neuronal excitability, but mutation reports often provide steady-state voltage shifts without sufficient kinetic measurements to specify a unique model. We introduce a Hill-based reformulation of selected Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) gating relationships and evaluate its usefulness under this low-information constraint. The hybrid formulation retains canonical HH-like spike waveforms and frequency–current behavior after a modest remapping of applied current, while providing an explicit mapping from reported activation descriptors to model parameters under specified assumptions. An A863P kinetic-sensitivity analysis shows how steady-state constraints and kinetic assumptions jointly shape excitability predictions in both classical HH and Hill-based implementations. The Hill formulation makes this mapping reproducible through explicit parameter relations, whereas refitting classical HH rates requires additional fitting choices; both approaches still require kinetic assumptions. Retrospective benchmarks using the Nav1.7 mutations A863P, F1449V, and A1632G show that the Hill-based model captures the qualitative increase in excitability but overestimates the magnitude of threshold reduction. Classical HH comparisons for A863P demonstrate that similar qualitative predictions can also be obtained under specified kinetic assumptions. These findings support the Hill formulation as a reproducible framework for mapping reported gating changes onto HH-like excitability, without establishing superior quantitative prediction of mutation effects. Quantitative transfer to mutation-specific neuronal behavior requires additional kinetic and cellular constraints.

Article.Title: Cost-effectiveness and carbon footprint of cystoscopic surveillance schedules in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Yu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Repeated cystoscopy for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer incurs costs and greenhouse-gas emissions, but fewer examinations may delay recurrence detection. We compared nine surveillance schedules in a 15-year monthly cohort model stratified by European Association of Urology risk group. We used 2021 United States costs and an international emissions inventory. In low-risk patients, ending scheduled surveillance after the three-month examination, while retaining investigation of symptoms, reduced modelled costs by 24.0% and inventoried emissions by 13.0% compared with guideline follow-up. Time spent with undetected recurrence increased. In 5,000 paired simulations, the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years for this low-risk comparison was 0.009 per patient (95% uncertainty interval, -0.260 to 0.291). Clinical results depended on progression before recurrence detection and diagnosis prompted by symptoms; less favourable assumptions increased progression and bladder-cancer deaths. Recurrence treatment accounted for most inventoried emissions, limiting the carbon savings from fewer cystoscopies. Selected reductions in low-risk surveillance warrant prospective evaluation, but the model does not establish the safety of stopping scheduled surveillance after one examination.

Article.Title: A stabilized abdominal imaging platform for intravital interrogation of preclinical omental metastatic niche models
Article.Authors: García-Fuentes R.; de Aguileta N.; Pinci B.; Moreno-Luqui D.; Bella Á.; Zheng Y.; Salgado-Pascual A.; Juárez-Curiel E.; Risson A.; Chiclana-Valcarcel M.; Llorente-Ortega M.; Ederra C.; Urbiola A.; Ruiz-Guillamón D.; Fernández S.; Melero I.; Berraondo P.; Teijeira Á.; Aranda F.
Article.Abstract: The omentum is a highly specialized immunological and metabolic tissue that frequently acts as a permissive niche for metastatic dissemination within the peritoneal cavity. Despite its central role in metastatic progression and therapeutic response, real-time interrogation of the omental microenvironment in preclinical in vivo models remains technically challenging because of respiratory motion, tissue drift, and the fragility of abdominal tissues. Current methodologies largely rely on endpoint analyses or invasive tissue externalization procedures that disrupt physiological tissue dynamics and limit longitudinal investigation. Here, we present a mechanically stabilized abdominal imaging platform that enables high-resolution longitudinal intravital imaging of the omentum in live mice. The system combines a custom abdominal imaging window with a lift-support stabilization structure that mechanically isolates the omentum from respiratory motion while preserving tissue architecture and physiological immune cell behavior. Using fluorescent reporters, we demonstrate stable, long-term visualization of tumor progression, immune cell recruitment, and adoptive cell transfer targeting within the omental niche. As a proof-of-concept application, the platform was validated using an omentum-tropic model of peritoneal ovarian cancer dissemination, enabling longitudinal monitoring of metastatic engraftment and spatiotemporal immune dynamics during locoregional immunotherapy. Importantly, imaging through the stabilized window preserved lymphocyte motility significantly better than conventional tissue externalization approaches, thereby supporting the physiological relevance of the system. Overall, this platform provides a robust, adaptable framework for studying immune and metastatic processes in the peritoneal cavity and may facilitate preclinical evaluation of intraperitoneal therapies, cell-based immunotherapies, and microenvironment-targeted interventions.

Article.Title: Multi-horizon wind speed prediction with physics-embedded state space neural operator learning
Article.Authors: Parikibandla S.; Hota C.; Sreenivas A.; Nuthalapati C.; Karna V.
Article.Abstract: Accurate and repeatable long-range wind-speed prediction is required for the integration of renewable energy into power grids, and these models will need to reconcile a number of contradictory requirements: high accuracy, low computational effort, physical plausibility, and quantified prediction uncertainty. In this paper, Physics-Embedded State-Space Operator Learning (PESO-Net) is proposed for multi-site, multi-horizon forecasting. The framework comprises a selective state-space encoder, gated cross-site mixing, a validation-controlled vertical shear regularizer, direct quantile decoding, and chronological conformal calibration. Observations from five years of 1-h synchronization at four anonymous sites were split chronologically into training, validation, calibration, and test sets, and one 168-h forecast trajectory was assessed over the 1–24 h, 1–72 h, and 1–168 h prefixes. The primary validation-weighted PESO-Net achieved MAE 2.080 m/s, RMSE 2.622 m/s, R² 0.176, 95.56% empirical coverage, 10.489 m/s mean interval width, and interval score 12.048. The primary validation-weighted PESO-Net had lower observed point errors and interval scores than the compared baselines. Among the four added model variants, PatchTST was closest by RMSE (2.727 m/s), with an interval score of 12.513. Mean predicted shear exponents ranged from 0.229 to 0.235, compared with observed means near 0.222; correlations of 0.287–0.302 support only limited physical agreement. The primary paired block-bootstrap RMSE contrast with Transformer was − 0.0185 m/s (95% CI − 0.0390 to 0.0042; p = 0.096), so statistical superiority was not established. The test period was used in earlier experiments, which limits the validity of claims of independent generalization. Thus, PESO-Net is not necessarily state-of-the-art for the four sites studied, but according to the data, it is competitive.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial activity of apramycin formulated with dextran-based single-chain polymeric nanoparticles against Acinetobacter baumannii
Article.Authors: Ibáñez J.; Movellan J.; Loinaz I.; Dupin D.; Marimón J.
Article.Abstract: The global emergence of antimicrobial resistance is driving the development of novel strategies for treating bacterial infections. In this context, dextran-based single-chain polymeric nanoparticles (DXT-SCPNs) have been developed as antibiotic delivery systems for the treatment of pulmonary infections. A series of DXT-SCPNs were formulated with apramycin with different physicochemical properties, namely three degrees of substitution (with a low degree of crosslinking in all cases): low (L-DS a ), medium (M-DS a ), or high (H-DS a ), and two degrees of crosslinking (with a medium degree of substitution in both nanoparticles): low (M-DSa) or high (H-CL a ). Their in vitro activity against eleven Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates was assessed compared to the free drug, using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) and time-kill kinetic (TKK) assays. Overall, no statistically significant differences were observed between the antimicrobial activity of free and formulated apramycin. Nevertheless, a slight trend towards higher activity was observed in the cases of M-DS a and H-CL a .

Article.Title: Cortical activation during hand grasping in Parkinson’s disease with different motor onset sides: an fNIRS study
Article.Authors: Wang K.; Guo J.; Liu D.; Wu Q.; Qiao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Motor symptom asymmetry is a key feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), but how onset side affects cortical activation during motor tasks remains unclear. This study used functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to investigate cortical activation and task-related lateralization during hand grasping in left-onset PD (LPD, n = 29), right-onset PD (RPD, n = 35), and healthy controls (HC, n = 14). During the left-hand task, both PD groups showed lower mean ΔHbO in the right primary somatosensory cortex than HC (LPD vs. HC: pFDR = 0.027; RPD vs. HC: pFDR = 0.022), with altered peak timing in the right frontal eye field (pFDR = 0.004 and 0.011). During the right-hand task, the RPD group showed lower activation in the right somatosensory association cortex (vs. HC pFDR = 0.039; vs. LPD pFDR = 0.024) and reduced peak activation (pFDR = 0.021), with shortened full width at half maximum in bilateral S1, M1, and SMA (all pFDR < 0.05). Lateralization analysis showed reversed task-related lateralization in the right primary somatosensory cortex in LPD (deltapeak: pFDR = 0.047) and altered task-related lateralization of timing in the right frontal eye field in both PD groups (pFDR = 0.034). In an exploratory analysis, longer disease duration was associated with shorter R-SAC time-to-peak in RPD but not LPD ( p = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵, q = 2.4 × 10⁻³ globally). Motor onset side is associated with distinct sensorimotor cortical dysfunction, with RPD showing more widespread deficits, whereas delayed FEF timing is a shared alteration independent of onset side. Temporal-domain metrics were more consistently affected than amplitude-based measures and may capture cortical changes missed by intensity indices.

Article.Title: From media to meals: intergenerational transmission of food-based media literacy and its association with food security in Iran
Article.Authors: Pakravan-Charvadeh M.; Flora C.
Article.Abstract: Food insecurity remains a major global challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In this context, food-based media literacy has emerged as an important skill that enables individuals and families to critically evaluate food-related media messages and make healthier dietary decisions. This study examined the intergenerational dynamics of food-based media literacy and its associations with food choices, dietary habits, and household food insecurity among Iranian families. Using a cross-sectional parent–young adult dyadic model, data was collected from 250 dyads ( n = 500) and analyzed using Dyadic PLS-SEM. The findings showed that food-based media literacy operates as a shared family resource rather than an individual competency. Both parents and young adults significantly influenced each other’s food choices and dietary habits, highlighting the importance of intergenerational dialogue. Critical thinking, self-efficacy, and food heritage preservation emerged as significant predictors of healthier dietary behaviors. Food choices and dietary habits also mediated the relationship between media literacy constructs and household food insecurity. Higher levels of food-based media literacy were associated with lower food insecurity, particularly through healthier dietary practices. Young adults’ constructs showed stronger overall associations than those of parents, emphasizing the importance of youth empowerment in strengthening household food security. The findings suggest that family-centered interventions promoting critical thinking, self-efficacy, and cultural food heritage may contribute to reducing food insecurity and improving dietary resilience.

Article.Title: Industrially promising probiotic candidates, Lacticaseibacillus paracasei strains from artisanal fermented camel milk, with no detected antibiotic-resistance genes
Article.Authors: Kochetkova T.; Lukina A.; Sokolyanskaya L.; Elcheninov A.; Avakyan M.; Khandyshanova M.; Strukova E.; Grabarnik I.; Ganina V.; Ravin N.; Karnachuk O.
Article.Abstract: Antibiotic resistance (AR) in industrial strains of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) poses a critical safety concern, as these microorganisms can serve as reservoirs and vectors for AR within the food chain. LAB isolates obtained from human or animal samples may harbor AR genes as a result of selective pressure from antibiotics. Traditional products derived from pasture-raised animals that do not receive feed additives serve as a possible source of AR-free LAB. We isolated six strains of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei from shubat — a traditional Asian fermented camel milk beverage, obtained from free-grazing camels in the high-altitude pastures of the Altai Mountains — and evaluated their probiotic potential, antimicrobial features and some technological characteristics. Whole-genome sequencing did not reveal any known AR genes in novel LAB. The strains exhibited variable tolerance to gastrointestinal stressors in vitro, grew in the presence of up to 6–8% NaCl, and efficiently fermented milk, reaching final counts of ≥ 10⁶–10⁹ CFU/mL, supporting their technological suitability as potential starter or adjunct cultures. Several biosynthetic gene clusters encoding putative secondary metabolites, including bacteriocins, were identified, suggesting the potential for bacteriocin production. The strains also exhibited in vitro antagonistic activity against the tested pathogenic and opportunistic bacteria, supporting their further evaluation as probiotic candidates.

Article.Title: Decoding MMP9 allosteric inhibition by ​​ Ocimum sanctum bioactives via network pharmacology and molecular dynamics for treating diabetic foot ulcers
Article.Authors: Hemal M.; Chandni F.; Polash M.; Talukder M.; Rahman M.; Sarkar B.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) represent a global health crisis characterized by chronic inflammation and a failure to transition into the proliferative phase of wound healing. This delay is mostly caused by the abnormal overexpression of matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), leading to indiscriminate destruction of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and essential growth factors. Conventional orthosteric inhibitors often fail due to lack of specificity and dose-limiting toxicities. This study aims to identify potential allosteric inhibitors of MMP-9 derived from Ocimum sanctum using a systemic computational framework. We employed an integrated approach combining GC–MS profiling and database mining of O. sanctum phytocompounds with transcriptomic analysis of the GSE199939 dataset. Network pharmacology was used to identify hub genes and shared targets between O. sanctum and DFU. High-precision molecular docking and 100 ns multivariate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations including RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration (Rg), and SASA were performed to evaluate the stability of the phytocompound binding at the allosteric hemopexin-like (PEX) domain of MMP-9. Binding free energies were quantified using MM/GBSA calculations. GC–MS and database mining collectively identified 19 lead bioactive compounds with favourable ADME/drug-likeness profiles, including retinal and eugenol. Transcriptomic integration revealed 11,570 DFU-associated genes, with 52 common targets shared with O. sanctum . MMP-9 was identified as a critical structural hub (degree = 29) within the interactome, closely linked to inflammatory nodes like STAT3 and BCL2. MD simulations and FEL analysis confirmed that O. sanctum bioactives establish stable and energetically favourable interactions within the MMP-9 allosteric PEX domain. This study highlights the potential of the O. sanctum -derived phytocompounds as selective allosteric modulators of MMP-9, offering a focused, multi-target, multi-pathway approach to restore the wound microenvironment and presenting a cost-effective and safe therapeutic solution for chronic diabetic wound management.

Article.Title: Salt chemistry regulates liquid environments and microsphere distribution in brinicles
Article.Authors: Garner M.; Feduschak M.; Perl S.; Smith H.; Foreman C.
Article.Abstract: Brinicles are dynamic ice structures that have been proposed as chemically active systems on Ocean Worlds, potentially serving as habitable niches for life. However, experimental studies of their internal microstructures and implications for habitability remain limited. This study examined how brine composition influences the formation of liquid habitats within brinicles and how differences in liquid fraction distribution impact the transport and location of fluorescent microspheres representing cellular proxies. Flow cytometry and cryo-Raman spectroscopy were used to quantify the spatial distribution of cellular proxies, liquid brine, and hydrated salts across the radial and vertical axes of brinicles grown under two salt compositions (NaCl and CaCl 2 ). Our findings demonstrate fundamental differences in brinicle microstructure between the two salt compositions. CaCl 2 grown brinicles exhibited confined localization of liquid brine towards the inner channel, whereas NaCl brinicles showed a more homogeneous distribution of the liquid fraction.​ Ultimately, these differences in liquid fraction and microstructure provide a physical mechanism for cellular surrogate localization in the ice. CaCl 2 brinicles resulted in the entrapment of microspheres near the brine channel while the NaCl brinicles produced uniform distribution of microspheres throughout the ice. These results demonstrate that brine chemistry can control habitat structure and the entrapment of cellular proxies within brinicles, highlighting the importance of ocean composition when assessing habitability on Ocean Worlds.

Article.Title: Machine learning maps multiplanar spinal surface alignment and patterns of change across heterogeneous cohorts
Article.Authors: Moustafa I.; Khowailed I.; Abdelrahman F.; Canıaz E.; Oakley P.; Harrison D.
Article.Abstract: Surface-derived thoracolumbar-pelvic alignment measures span sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes, but their multivariate organization remains incompletely characterized. This retrospective pooled analysis comprised a baseline cross-sectional sample of 468 participants from four cohorts (CGH, n = 200; FMS, n = 120; LSR, n = 80; AIS, n = 68) and a separate paired sample of 268 participants from the three intervention cohorts (FMS, n = 120; LSR, n = 80; AIS, n = 68). The CGH cohort was a matched cross-sectional study with one baseline assessment and was excluded from all post-treatment, change-score, and multiplanar change-magnitude analyses. In the primary cohort-centered baseline analysis, the first two PCA components explained 83.3% of variance, and CCA yielded Rc = 0.926 (95% cohort-stratified bootstrap CI 0.915–0.939; within-cohort permutation p < 0.001). In the cohort-centered paired analysis, PCA of post-minus-baseline changes explained 81.2% and 6.7% of variance in PC1 and PC2, respectively (87.9% cumulative), and CCA yielded Rc = 0.917 (95% cohort-stratified bootstrap CI 0.898–0.935; within-cohort permutation p < 0.001; repeated cohort-stratified cross-validated Rc = 0.912 ± 0.022). Exploratory K-means clustering yielded two partially overlapping descriptive profiles; an alternative Gaussian mixture analysis did not support two discrete latent subgroups. The profiles were not validated against independent clinical outcomes. Three-class classification using change scores alone was modest (balanced accuracy 0.418 ± 0.072; macro-AUC 0.610 ± 0.035). The paired findings describe multiplanar covariance of observed within-participant change across different interventions and follow-up intervals. They do not establish a shared adaptive mechanism or a common treatment effect, and they do not apply to the baseline-only CGH cohort.

Article.Title: BALANCE-ST: distilling deep reinforcement learning policies into PLC logic for multi-VFD load balancing
Article.Authors: Li L.; Zhang G.
Article.Abstract: Industrial multi-VFD load balancing on programmable logic controllers (PLCs) requires control policies that are accurate, transparent, and fast enough for deterministic scan cycles. Deep reinforcement learning can learn effective balancing strategies, but neural policies are difficult to inspect and deploy as IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (ST). We propose BALANCE-ST, a simulation-to-PLC pipeline that trains a deep Q -network (DQN) teacher, distils it into a depth-2 decision tree selected by held-out validation parsimony, renders the tree as PLC-oriented ST, and wraps the resulting policy with a deterministic guard enforcing command-bound, ramp-rate, dwell-time, and overload checks. In an in-distribution post-training evaluation across eight demand families and ten seeds, BALANCE-ST achieves mean load-imbalance coefficient of variation 0.0697 versus 0.0696 for the ten-teacher DQN aggregate, while reducing imbalance by \(34.4\%\) , \(52.6\%\) , and \(15.0\%\) relative to equal-share, threshold-staging, and PI baselines, respectively. On the interquartile mean, the reduction versus threshold staging is \(43.2\%\) . A guard ablation and hard-stress evaluation show that the runtime guard reduces realised violations at the cost of higher imbalance under actuator dropout. Compared with beam-search model predictive control, BALANCE-ST yields higher imbalance but much lower online decision cost and a compact policy with four leaves and three effective actions. These results support BALANCE-ST as a practical trade-off between control performance, inspectability, and deployment-oriented simplicity for PLC-based multi-VFD control.

Article.Title: Broadband sensor-level EEG power dynamics differentiate anticipation, observation, imitation, and execution of hand actions
Article.Authors: Hashemi N.; Beal D.; Pranjić M.; Tou J.; Chau T.
Article.Abstract: To understand how perceived actions translate to neural processes relevant for learning, planning, and adaptation, it is important to study how sensory inputs and intentions are interpreted within the mirror neuron system (MNS) framework. Although execution, observation, and imitation are commonly studied within the MNS framework, prior reports on cortical activity differences—particularly hemispheric lateralization between left- and right-hand actions and the temporal progression of activity across perceptual, cognitive, and motor cortical regions—remain unclear. Here, we analyzed electroencephalography data from 15 right-handed adults as they anticipated, executed, imitated, and observed right- and left-hand squeezes to characterize task-, hand-, and phase-specific temporal, spectral, and spatial patterns of sensor-level EEG oscillatory power, and to evaluate the within-sample reliability of these patterns. We found that low- and high-frequency EEG power differed by task and hand. EEG oscillatory power patterns were predominantly bilateral, whereas contralateral power modulations emerged during anticipation. Differences in the temporal profile of sensor-level EEG activity were consistent with top-down organization during observation (early frontal EEG power modulation) and bottom-up organization during cue-driven execution and imitation (early visuoparietal EEG power modulation). These findings demonstrate that a single within-subject EEG design can resolve task-, hand-, and phase-specific sensor-level dynamics within MNS-related action paradigms with adequate within-sample reliability, establishing an empirical basis for future hypothesis-driven investigations of sensorimotor integration and perception–action mapping.

Article.Title: Low-frequency noise reduction in laser-induced graphene devices by noble metal nanoparticles decoration
Article.Authors: Drozdowska-Czubek K.; Smulko J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We exploited the surface-modified laser-induced graphene (LIG) resistors decorated with gold, silver, or platinum nanoparticles (AuNPs, AgNPs, or PtNPs) to reduce their low-frequency noise. The resistors can be used to prepare sensors or contact paths in wearable electronics due to their elastic properties, and their inherent noise impacts their performance. The simple NPs modification of the LIG surface resulted in a noise-reduction effect, which increased in the following order: Pt<Ag<Au for the devices investigated here.​ Au-decorated LIG exhibited a 32-times reduction of normalized voltage noise. This result was observed independently of photoactivation or plasmonic resonance induction in the NPs. The most significant effect was observed for Au-decorated LIG. We propose the interpretation that AuNPs occupy the LIG surface, which may create a damping effect on phonon vibrations, thereby decreasing the intensity of mobility fluctuations responsible for flicker noise generation as reported for other materials. The weaker effect observed for Ag-/Pt-decorated LIGs can be ascribed to differences in contact forces existing between these nanoparticles and graphene compared to AuNPs. Our work points out that Au-decorated graphene has high potential for use in low-noise electronics and that low inherent noise is required to employ graphene and graphene-like structures in practical sensing applications.

Article.Title: Multi-step-ahead forecasting of highway slope displacement using adaptive feature decoupling and an attention-enhanced Bi-LSTM ensemble
Article.Authors: Rao P.; Duan R.; Chen Y.; Cui J.; Li X.; Chun P.
Article.Abstract: GNSS monitoring data for highway slopes exhibit strong non-stationarity and high-frequency noise, making traditional deep learning models prone to error accumulation in long-sequence forecasting. This paper proposes a highway slope displacement forecasting model based on Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) and a weighted ensemble of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) networks. OC-SVM and Simple Moving Average (SMA) are employed for outlier removal and noise reduction, while CEEMDAN decomposes the displacement sequence into a multi-channel feature matrix to suppress environmental interference. A Bi-LSTM incorporating a self-attention mechanism and Global Average Pooling (GAP) is then developed, and an inverse-error-based homogeneous weighted ensemble strategy is adopted for prediction. The model is validated using three-dimensional GNSS displacement data from a highway slope in Qingxiu District, Nanning, Guangxi. A total of 9000 E-W displacement samples (2-min interval) are used for evaluation. As the forecasting horizon increases from 1 to 12 h, prediction accuracy gradually decreases (R2 = 0.9577, 0.9122, and 0.8717) but consistently outperforms baseline models. When applied without retraining to the N-S and U displacement components recorded at the same GNSS monitoring station, the model also achieved R² values above 0.86. The proposed model effectively mitigates long-sequence forecasting divergence and provides technical support for dynamic highway slope monitoring.

Article.Title: Prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension among older adults in China
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Tang W.; Du H.; Xu R.; Huang C.; Zhang W.; Luo Q.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract China contributes to approximately 20% of the global burden of hypertension; however, a nationwide epidemiological survey on the prevalence of hypertension among older adults is lacking. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension among older adults in China. The data were derived from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) in 2015. We included 7,733 participants aged 60 years and older. The prevalence of hypertension was 53.1% (95% CI 51.7–54.6%), which is equivalent to 140 million adults aged 60 years or older with hypertension in China. Among the participants with hypertension, 74.1% (95% CI 72.5–75.8%) were aware of their condition, 54.5% (95% CI 52.5–56.5%) were treated, and only 33.7% (95% CI 31.8–35.6%) were controlled. Systolic blood pressure increased with age ( r = 0.504, P < 0.001), whereas diastolic blood pressure decreased with age ( r = − 0.175, P < 0.001). The prevalence of hypertension increased with age (P for trend < 0.001). The prevalence of hypertension was observed to be higher in urban areas (57.0%, 95% CI 53.7–60.3%) than in rural areas (51.2%, 95% CI 49.8–52.6%) ( P = 0.002), along with the prevalence being higher in northern areas (56.8%, 95% CI 54.7–58.8%) than in southern areas (50.7%, 95% CI 48.8–52.7%) ( P < 0.001). Spanning from the western provinces to the central provinces to the eastern areas, the prevalence of hypertension was 50.8% (95% CI 48.6–53.1%), 52.6% (95% CI 50.4–54.8%), and 55.6% (95% CI 52.7–58.5%) (P for trend < 0.001), respectively. Multivariable analysis revealed that older age (65–69 years group: OR = 1.292, 95% CI 1.105–1.512; 70–74 years group: OR = 1.482, 95% CI 1.235–1.779; 75–79 years group: OR = 1.922, 95% CI 1.569–2.355; ≥ 80 years group: OR = 2.192, 95% CI 1.739–2.764), living in northern areas (OR = 1.197, 95% CI 1.054–1.360), drinking more than once a month (OR = 1.187, 95% CI 1.000–1.410), obesity (OR = 2.568, 95% CI 1.977–3.336), diabetes (OR = 1.694, 95% CI 1.443–1.989), and dyslipidaemia (OR = 1.378, 95% CI 1.218–1.559) were positively correlated with hypertension, whereas being married (or cohabitating) (OR = 0.772, 95% CI 0.668–0.892) was negatively correlated with hypertension. The prevalence of hypertension was high in people aged 60 years or older in China; however, the rates of control of hypertension remain low. Efforts are needed to prevent hypertension and improve the treatment and control of hypertension.
