Article.Title: Prognostic value of triglyceride-glucose glycemic variability index in critically ill unstable angina patients via machine learning with independent hospital validation
Article.Authors: Zheng Z.; Qiu J.; Qian Y.; Xu S.; Jiang Y.; He K.
Article.Abstract: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is associated with outcomes in critical illness, but the prognostic value of combining it with glycemic variability, the TyG-glycemic variability index (TyG-GVI), has not been evaluated in critically ill patients with unstable angina. In this study we examined the association between TyG-GVI and ICU and in-hospital mortality and developed an interpretable machine-learning model for mortality risk. We retrospectively analyzed 1,444 adult patients with unstable angina from the MIMIC-IV 3.1 database (2008–2022) as the development cohort, dichotomized at the median TyG‑GVI. Associations with ICU and in-hospital mortality were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards and logistic regression, and the dose-response relationship was modelled with restricted cubic splines. Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM classifiers were developed with Boruta confirmatory importance analysis and SHAP-based interpretation, and the optimal model was externally validated in an independent retrospective cohort of 340 ICU patients with unstable angina from the Quzhou Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University. A total of 108 ICU deaths (7.5%) and 190 in-hospital deaths (13.2%) occurred. Compared with the low TyG-GVI group, high TyG-GVI was associated with ICU mortality in the fully adjusted Cox model (HR 2.29, 95% CI 1.43–3.66) and with in-hospital mortality (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.11–2.15), although the latter did not reach statistical significance in every model specification. The dose-response relationship was non-linear (P for non-linearity < 0.01 for ICU mortality and < 0.05 for in-hospital mortality), with a data-derived nadir at a TyG-GVI of approximately 3.135. Random Forest achieved the numerically highest discrimination in the development cohort (AUC 0.830) and in the external validation cohort (AUC 0.874). High TyG-GVI was independently associated with ICU mortality and was also associated with in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with unstable angina. An interpretable machine-learning model incorporating TyG-GVI showed consistent discrimination performance in the development and external validation cohorts and has been deployed as a web-based research prototype. Prospective validation and formal assessment of calibration and clinical utility are required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Explainable IoT intrusion detection via bio-inspired encoding and interpretable AI models
Article.Authors: AL Ibaisi T.; Kazim M.; Ur Rehman M.; Kaiiali M.; Kuhn S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We introduce an explainable Internet of Things (IoT) intrusion detection framework built on a bio-inspired Amino Acid encoding of network flows. The flow features are first transformed with the Yeo–Johnson transformation, the most informative ones are selected, and their values are encoded as Amino Acid sequences, which are then summarized by ten protein structural properties (e.g., $$\beta $$ -Turn, Isoelectric Point and Molecular Weight). In this way every flow is described by the same compact set of ten properties, whatever the feature set of the original dataset. The models are explained with SHAP, LIME and ELI5, complemented by Captum Integrated Gradients and Alibi anchors for the neural models, and the attributions are linked back to the raw traffic features through measured correlations. On a balanced 50,000-flow subset of CICIoT2023 that covers all 33 attack classes, most of the 12 classical and 5 deep models reach 98.4–98.5% accuracy on a held-out test set (MCC up to 0.97). The recurrent neural network (RNN), used for the in-depth explainability study, reaches 98.5% accuracy with a false-alarm rate of 0.02%, has fewer than 15,000 parameters and needs about 0.1 ms per flow on a CPU. An ablation experiment shows that encoding the selected features keeps detection close to the full 39-feature raw representation (MCC 0.970 against 0.979), while giving a fixed ten-property input that can be explained. All explanation methods agree that $$\beta $$ -Turn and Isoelectric Point drive most decisions, and both properties correlate strongly with the packet count and packet size of the flows.

Article.Title: Geotechnical characterization and foundation competence evaluation using shallow seismic refraction: a case study from Ain Sokhna, Gulf of Suez, Egypt
Article.Authors: Farag M.; Shebl S.; Soliman S.; Shazly T.; Abed M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evaluation of subsurface conditions and foundation competence is essential for sustainable infrastructure development in the Ain Sokhna area along the Gulf of Suez, Egypt. This study applies shallow seismic refraction surveys to characterize the geotechnical properties of near-surface materials and assess their suitability for engineering and construction. Seismic P-wave (Vp) velocities obtained from twenty survey sites were integrated with measured S-wave (Vs) velocities and density values to derive a comprehensive set of dynamic geotechnical parameters, including Poisson’s ratio, shear modulus, Young’s modulus, bulk modulus, material index, concentration index, stress ratio, ultimate bearing capacity, and allowable bearing capacity. Results reveal pronounced spatial variations in subsurface engineering characteristics. P-wave velocities range from 677 to 2330 m/s, while S-wave velocities vary between 376 and 1355 m/s. Velocity distributions show a systematic decrease from the northeastern to the southwestern sector, reflecting reduced density, stiffness, and rock-mass competence. This trend is corroborated by elastic parameters: shear modulus ranges from 224 to 3954 MPa, Young’s modulus from 571 to 9842 MPa, and bulk modulus from 427 to 6420 MPa. The northeastern sector exhibits higher velocities and moduli, indicating compacted, mechanically competent foundation materials, whereas the southwest shows lower values, suggesting increased fracturing, weathering, and diminished geotechnical quality. Bearing-capacity analyses are consistent with this zonation, with ultimate values between 2.0 and 85.4 kg/cm 2 and allowable values from 0.7 to 28.5 kg/cm 2 . The highest capacities occur in the northeast, while progressively weaker conditions dominate toward the southwest. The integrated results delineate two broad geotechnical zones, with comparatively competent materials in the northeastern, eastern, and central sectors and moderately competent materials toward the southwest.

Article.Title: Quantification and micro-costing analysis of healthcare waste generated in a pre-clinical simulation laboratory
Article.Authors: Akarsu A.; Yilmaz A.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to evaluate the comprehensive environmental and financial burden—specifically, the amount, type, per-student waste load, and micro-costs—of medical, sharps, and packaging waste generated during the practical examination process for first-year midwifery students. In this descriptive, cross-sectional study, the clinical skills practical examination (including parenteral applications, catheterization, and venipuncture) of 67 students was audited. Waste generated during examination stations was audited and classified in accordance with World Health Organization guidelines and national health waste management standards, adapted for a non-biological simulation environment. Waste was segregated at the source, weighed using precision scales, and inventoried. A micro-costing approach was used to calculate consumable procurement and waste-disposal costs, which were converted to US Dollars (USD) based on June 2026 market rates. The examination generated a total of 28,450 g of non-hazardous medical consumables, 597 g of sharps waste, and 2,621 g of packaging waste, consuming 1,521 needles, 536 ampoules, and 1,675 gloves. On average, each student produced 120.5 waste items, including 40.7 sharps materials. Financially, the total institutional expenditure for the single examination session was 18,301.85 TRY ($396.83 USD), which includes both consumable procurement costs ($368.01 USD) and waste disposal/management fees ($28.82 USD), translating to an overall operational expense of $5.92 USD per student. Pre-clinical laboratory training imposes a substantial, hidden eco-financial burden on institutions while exposing students to high occupational safety risks due to the density of sharps. Integrating waste minimization strategies and green curriculum protocols could significantly lower institutional procurement and disposal costs while minimizing injury risks. University administrations are urged to adopt sustainable laboratory infrastructures to achieve both fiscal efficiency and environmental stewardship.

Article.Title: A controlled evaluation of objective-responsive genetic-operator adaptation for variable-length 3D UAV path planning
Article.Authors: Oszczypała M.; Betkier I.; Lęgas A.; Ziółkowski J.
Article.Abstract: Three-dimensional UAV path planning requires simultaneous satisfaction of obstacle-clearance, altitude, and turning constraints. This study evaluates objective-responsive genetic-operator control within a variable-length waypoint representation. A common signal derived from the best penalized objective and a geometric lower bound adjusts selection, crossover, mutation, and elitism separately or jointly. Eight GA variants were compared in 960 runs across four synthetic environments using 30 matched seeds per environment and 100,000 objective evaluations per run. Fixed-length GA, particle swarm optimization, differential evolution, and a Dubai urban case extended the evaluation. Adaptation of individual operator families achieved the highest observed feasibility in three synthetic environments, although its pairwise feasibility advantages over the balanced GA did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Full adaptation produced significantly worse final objectives than the balanced GA and three variants adapting individual operator families in Environment 3. In the two larger environments, median feedback signals remained near 0.21–0.22 as infeasibility penalties dominated, limiting changes in operator settings. Differential evolution with the minimum fixed waypoint count achieved full feasibility in all synthetic environments; selection, mutation, and elitism adaptation each yielded 10/10 feasible outcomes in Dubai. These results connect adaptation outcomes with the measured feedback response and demonstrate the importance of evaluating operator control jointly with feasibility and trajectory dimension.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: particle swarm optimization; UAV path planning; differential evolution; 3D trajectory optimization; obstacle avoidance

Article.Title: Proximo-distal muscle modulation as a function of hand orientation in a reach-and-grasp task
Article.Authors: Chambellant F.; Hilt P.; Cronin N.; Thomas E.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to improve our understanding of muscle contractions in the arm as a function of object orientation for grasp. While there have been several reports on arm kinematics for reach and grasp adjustments for object orientation, little has been done at the muscular activity level. To this end, we analyzed the modulation of Shoulder, Elbow and Hand muscle groups for a reach and grasp task involving a target in either Horizontal or Vertical orientation. We hypothesized that unlike what has been observed for kinematics, that at the muscular activity level, we would see less correlation between the three muscle groups. A decoding approach with Machine Learning (AdaBoost) revealed adaptation patterns that were not visible using classical statistics methods. Reach-and-grasp has traditionally been treated as being made of two components – the reach and the grasp components. Our dynamic decoding approach revealed a more complex picture with very different adaptation dynamics in the activity of the Shoulder and Elbow muscle groups during reach. All muscle groups showed peak accuracy for predicting target orientation before the start of grasp and followed the ubiquitous proximo-distal organization. The patterns of muscular modulation for target orientation were strongly perturbed by the ‘Eyes Closed’ and ‘Slow movement’ conditions, potentially decreasing the available degrees of freedom for adaptation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: elbow muscles; reach and grasp; hand muscles; slow movement; degrees of freedom; hand orientation; shoulder muscles

Article.Title: Human milk composition data for healthy growing, breastfed infants: analysis from 9 countries in Europe and Asia
Article.Authors: Monnard C.; Popovic D.; Lavalle L.; Giuffrida F.; Austin S.; Affolter M.; Kratzer G.; Vassallo I.; Gimenez E.; Dubascoux S.; van der Beek E.; Binia A.
Article.Abstract: Human milk (HM) is the gold standard for infant nutrition, but, currently – beyond the macronutrients – there is limited knowledge on the composition of milk fed to infants growing within the WHO growth reference standards. This study aims to provide HM composition values for energy, macronutrients, fatty acids, and gangliosides for breastfed infants growing within the WHO growth reference standards. A pooled analysis of previously collected HM data from the mothers of healthy growing infants from 9 countries across Europe and Asia was performed using meta-analysis techniques to identify average values for energy, protein, lactose, total fat, fatty acids, and gangliosides. Healthy infant growth was defined according to the WHO growth standards. The pooled mean for energy in HM was 71.2 (95% confidence interval 66.27–76.22) kcal/100 mL, total fat was 4.21 (3.73–4.69) g/100 mL, protein was 1.26 (1.12–1.40) g/100 mL and lactose was 7.18 (6.91–7.44) g/100 mL. Pooled means for saturated​ and monounsaturated fatty acids were similar to previously reported values (mean, 95% CI: 42.2%, 39.12–45.29 and 41.3%, 39–43.66, respectively). Total polyunsaturated fatty acids showed considerable between-country heterogeneity, with the highest country-specific mean of n-3 PUFA in HM from Norway (2.49, 2.04–2.95) %. Pooled mean (95% CI) for HM gangliosides were 0.88 (0.7–1.05) mg/100 mL and 0.24 (0.21–0.27) mg/100 mL for GM 3 and GD 3 species, respectively. This analysis provides values for HM macronutrients, fatty acids and gangliosides from healthy mothers breastfeeding healthy, term infants from 9 countries across Europe and Asia. These data may be used to inform nutrient intake recommendations and guide nutritional interventions to support infant health and development. Clinical Trial Registry : NCT01894893 (25/04/2013); NCT01805011 (04/03/2013); NCT03387124 (21/12/2017).

Article.Title: Machine-learning-assisted prediction and optimization of tensile strength in particulate-filled polymer composites
Article.Authors: Fuxian Z.; Wen Z.; Bailiang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Particulate-filled polymer composites (PFPCs) are characterized by high specific strength, good formability, and considerable design flexibility, making them key materials for rapid tooling in aerospace equipment manufacturing. In this study, metal-powder/resin composites were investigated, and a tensile-strength dataset comprising 45 independent experimental conditions was established. Three machine-learning regression algorithms, namely linear least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR), were employed to develop tensile-strength prediction models. A fixed outer five-fold cross-validation procedure was used to obtain out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, while hyperparameters were selected through inner five-fold cross-validation within each outer training fold; a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently used to further optimize the SVR hyperparameters. The OOF RMSE, MAE, and R² values of SVR were 1.67 MPa, 1.32 MPa, and 0.882, respectively, and those of GA-SVR were 1.54 MPa, 1.21 MPa, and 0.901. With increasing particle volume fraction and particle size, the tensile strength initially increased and then decreased, whereas ball-milling time had a relatively limited effect. Single-parameter analysis yielded predicted peak positions of approximately 34.80%, 30.92 μm, and 2.68 h for particle volume fraction, particle size, and ball-milling time, respectively. Continuous searching within the experimental domain identified a high-strength parameter combination of f = 34.63%, D = 30.67 μm, and t = 2.65 h, corresponding to a predicted tensile strength of 61.33 MPa. The measured strengths of three independent validation specimens prepared using a nominal particle size of 31 μm were 61.12, 60.93, and 60.56 MPa, with a mean of 60.87 ± 0.28 MPa, a coefficient of variation of 0.47%, and a relative deviation of 0.75% between the experimental mean and model prediction. Within the current experimental domain, the proposed framework can provide a quantitative reference for PFPC tensile-strength prediction and formulation/process-parameter screening, and offers an efficient strategy for accelerating formulation design and optimization while reducing experimental cost. Its implementation also provided students with practical experience in applying machine-learning algorithms to material-strength prediction and parameter design.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: particle size; ball milling time; genetic algorithm hyperparameter optimization; support vector regression; k-nearest neighbors regression; tensile strength prediction; particle volume fraction; rapid tooling; LASSO; process parameter screening

Article.Title: A transformer defect detection method based on state space model and cross-domain feature fusion
Article.Authors: Zhou W.; Wang N.; Li Y.; Lou J.; Zheng P.
Article.Abstract: Power transformers serve as critical equipment in power systems, and appearance defect detection is essential for ensuring grid safety. This paper proposes a power transformer defect detection method based on state space model and cross-domain feature fusion. First, a multi-scale wavelet frequency enhancement module is designed, which extracts multi-scale frequency domain features through three-layer Haar wavelet decomposition and achieves adaptive complementary fusion of frequency-domain and spatial-domain features via cross-domain gating mechanism. Second, a dual-branch state space modeling module is proposed, which captures global long-range dependencies through multi-directional selective scanning of the Mamba architecture, combined with multi-scale convolution and ECA channel attention to extract local detail features, achieving complementary enhancement of global context and local information. Finally, a multi-scale linear attention module is introduced based on a dual positional encoding mechanism to enable efficient global context modeling. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an mAP50 of 84.7%, representing an improvement of 12.9 percentage points over the baseline method, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cross-domain feature fusion; Haar wavelet decomposition; state-space model; multi-scale feature extraction; linear attention

Article.Title: Coupled exposure–response assessment and regulation of multi-source ecological risks in coastal wetlands of Guangxi
Article.Authors: Qin W.; Shen X.; Lao Y.; Nong G.; Chen X.; Chen F.; Pan T.; Fu L.; Zhang K.
Article.Abstract: Coastal wetlands serve as ecological security barriers and provide important ecosystem services. They are now under combined pressure from multiple human activities. To address the diverse risk types, complex impact pathways and heterogeneous ecological responses in the wetlands of the Beibu Gulf, Guangxi, this study extended the conventional Relative Risk Model (RRM) by incorporating an explicit exposure–response pathway framework linking risk sources, habitat receptors and ecological endpoints. The extended framework integrates four indicators: relative risk density, habitat abundance, exposure coefficient and response coefficient. The model integrates four indica-tors, namely relative risk density, habitat abundance, exposure coefficient and response coefficient. Remote sensing interpretation, field investigation and AHP-based weighting were combined to support quantitative, pathway-based and zoning-oriented assessment of coastal ecological risks. The results show clear spatial differences among the five assessment subregions. The Maowei Sea and Qinzhou Bay region (Q4) had the highest comprehensive risk value, reaching 7.58. This was mainly driven by the combined effects of port expansion, pollutant discharge and waterway construction. Tieshan Port (Q1) and Pearl Bay (Q5) had risk values of 4.14 and 3.90, respectively. These two areas were classified as medium-high risk zones. The Nanliu River Estuary (Q2) and Sanniang Bay (Q3) showed lower risk values, at 2.24 and 2.73, respectively. Among all ecological receptors, mangrove wetlands had the highest exposure and response coefficients. They therefore represented the most sensitive areas with concentrated ecological risks. The model identified the pathway from urban construction to mangrove wetlands and then to biodiversity degradation as an important risk transmission pathway. Based on the assessment results, differentiated ecological regulation strategies are proposed for different zones. High-risk zones should implement ecological red-line protection and risk monitoring and management mechanisms. Medium-risk zones should strengthen pollution control and industrial restructuring. Low-risk zones should promote green ecological use and preventive management. The proposed model can jointly represent multiple risks, multiple receptors and multiple endpoints. It provides spatially precise and regulation-oriented decision support for coastal wetland conservation. It also extends the application boundary of the relative risk model (RRM) in complex ecosystems. The results showed clear spatial differences among the five assessment subregions, mainly associated with differences in port and urban construction, waterway disturbance, aquaculture intensity and pollution pressure.

Article.Title: Polygenic associations with COVID-19 severity across two danish cohorts: relationships with pre-infection health
Article.Authors: Quinn L.; Geller F.; Feenstra B.; Vestergaard L.; Hjalgrim H.; Kaspersen K.; Didriksen M.; Dinh K.; Nissen J.; Hindhede L.; Schwinn M.; Saekmose S.; Werge T.; Bruun M.; Aagaard B.; Sørensen E.; Erikstrup C.; Ullum H.; Schork A.; Ostrowski S.; Christoffersen L.; Pedersen O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract COVID-19 severity varies widely between individuals, reflecting a combination of demographic, clinical, and genetic risk factors. Although polygenic scores (PGS’s) are increasingly used to study susceptibility to infectious disease, it remains unclear to what extent these associations are sensitive to health characteristics present before infection. We examined PGS associations across four disease domains with COVID-19 severity outcomes in two complementary Danish cohorts: 14,364 participants from the Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS), with self-reported bedridden COVID-19, and 115,515 participants from the Copenhagen Hospital Biobank (CHB), with register-defined COVID-19 severity among individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. PGSs surviving false-discovery-rate correction were examined across sequential models adjusting for pandemic period, measured pre-infection health and vaccination status at infection. Associations were quantified using population-standardised risk differences with 5,000 bootstrap iterations used to generate 95% CIs for risk estimates. Eight PGSs were associated with bedridden COVID-19 in DBDS and nine with register-defined COVID-19 severity in CHB, with seven associations shared across cohorts and showing concordant directions. In our nested sequential adjustment models adjustment for pre-infection health resulted in heterogeneous changes across PGSs. In DBDS, the risk difference per 1-SD higher ADHD PGS decreased from 1.75% points after adjustment for pandemic period to 1.31 after additional adjustment for pre-infection BMI and physical and mental health, whereas the corresponding influenza PGS association changed from 2.00 to 1.83% points. In CHB, ADHD PGS decreased from 0.49 to 0.40% points following adjustment for pre-pandemic comorbidity, while the COVID-19 severity PGS remained stable (0.19 to 0.19% points). Vaccination adjustment generally produced comparatively little additional attenuation. In our study, polygenic liabilities across multiple disease domains were associated with COVID-19 severity outcomes, but their associations showed varying sensitivity to adjustment for measured pre-infection health across two distinct cohort settings and two distinct pre-infection health measures. These findings suggest that cross-trait polygenic associations with COVID-19 differ in their relationships with pre-existing health highlighting the importance of pre-existing health when interpreting genetic associations with infectious disease outcomes.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: COVID-19 severity; polygenic risk score; vaccination status
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Genetics > Genetic Associations and Epidemiology; Medicine > Infectious Diseases > COVID-19 Clinical Research Studies; Medicine > Infectious Diseases > SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19 Research

Article.Title: Resting-state aperiodic EEG activity exhibits regional differences and behavioral associations in mild-to-moderate age-related hearing loss
Article.Authors: Wu S.; Jiang M.; Wang Y.; Xue L.; Li X.; Zhu Y.; Luo Y.; Guo M.; Jiang Q.; Sun J.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Age-related hearing loss is associated with cognitive decline, yet its underlying neural changes remain poorly understood. Resting-state EEG offers a clinically feasible approach to investigating these changes. Eighty adults aged 50–70 years were classified by pure-tone average (PTA) into normal-hearing (NH; n = 40) and hearing-impaired (HI; n = 40) groups. Resting-state 128-channel EEG was recorded during eyes-closed (EC) and eyes-open (EO) conditions. Power spectra were parameterized using FOOOF to characterize the aperiodic spectral background. Alpha-band functional connectivity was quantified using the weighted phase lag index, with regional analyses conducted across six electrode-based regions of interest (ROIs). No significant between-group differences in alpha-band total power were detected in either condition. During EC rest, the HI group showed a lower aperiodic exponent in the Frontal ROI at nominal significance ( p = 0.032, Cliff’s δ = 0.280). During EO rest, lower exponents were observed in the TemporalCore, TemporalExtended, Occipital, and Parietal ROIs. Exponent–alpha power correlations were numerically weaker in the HI group in several ROIs. During EC rest, the Frontal exponent was positively correlated with Frontal connectivity strength in the NH group (Spearman’s ρ = 0.53, p < 0.001), whereas the HI correlation was not significant (ρ = −0.19, p = 0.24). Within the HI group, the Frontal exponent during EO rest was negatively associated with speech-in-noise threshold after adjustment for PTA, age, sex, and education (partial ρ = −0.386, p = 0.020). PTA remained positively associated with speech-in-noise threshold after adjustment for the Frontal exponent and the same demographic covariates (partial ρ = 0.691, p < 0.001). These exploratory findings suggest that aperiodic spectral measures may complement conventional alpha-power analysis in characterizing hearing-related EEG differences. The cross-sectional, sensor-level findings require replication and do not establish underlying physiological mechanisms.

Article.Title: A cue-locality audit framework for attributing spurious temporal shortcuts in deep sequence models
Article.Authors: Cho Y.; Kim D.; Kim Y.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High accuracy on independent and identically distributed (IID) test data does not reveal which temporal cue a sequence model uses. A directional process can leave a cue in individual frames, so out-of-distribution (OOD) failure alone does not establish temporal-order use. We propose a six-gate audit that attributes failure to a nuisance and distinguishes frame-local, order-invariant multi-frame, and order-encoded cues. A companion controlled benchmark provides the factor-level probes and interventions the audit requires. Applied to this benchmark, the audit revealed that a variant designed to encode temporal order was instead solvable from individual frames. In the strict order-encoded variant (OE-Strict), direction is readable only from interior frame order. With nuisance direction aligned with the label with probability 0.97 during training, a gated recurrent unit (GRU) trained by empirical risk minimization (ERM) selects the shortcut in thirty of thirty seeds (0.970 IID and 0.030 OOD accuracy). Channel-selective interventions attribute the collapse to nuisance frame ordering. The audit distinguishes which process supports a prediction and whether using that process requires temporal order.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: empirical risk minimization

Article.Title: Sociodemographic correlates of physical literacy among urban adults aged 20–59 years: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; He J.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical literacy (PL) is widely regarded as a cornerstone of lifelong physical activity (PA) participation. However, empirical research on PL and its sociodemographic correlates in adult populations remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the sociodemographic correlates of PL among Chinese urban adults aged 20–59 years. We used convenience sampling to recruit 731 participants, of whom 80.4% held a bachelor’s degree or higher. PL was measured using a previously developed assessment tool for Chinese adults, covering three domains: PA cognition, PA-related behavior, and physical competence. Univariate analyses and hierarchical multiple linear regression were conducted to identify correlates of PL. Univariate analyses showed significant differences in the total PL scores across age, health status, city, education level, personal monthly disposable income, and frequency of health checkups ( P < 0.05). After controlling for city, the final regression model revealed that PL was significantly associated with age ( β = -0.15, P < 0.001), health status ( β = 0.11, P = 0.002), holding a bachelor’s degree or higher (β = 0.15, P = 0.007), a personal monthly disposable income exceeding 9000 yuan ( β = 0.08, P = 0.05), and undergoing annual or biennial health checkups ( β = 0.26, P = 0.001; β = 0.10, P = 0.04). Notably, the models explained a modest proportion of variance in total PL (adjusted R² = 0.27) and a very small proportion for the PA cognition domain (adjusted R² = 0.02). PL among urban Chinese adults with relatively high education levels is associated with age, health status, education, income, and regular health checkups. However, the limited explanatory power of these sociodemographic factors suggests that future research should incorporate broader psychosocial and environmental determinants to inform more effective intervention design.

Article.Title: GRACE-AI: a governance-centric MLOps framework for risk-tiered control, continuous assurance, and explainability in high-stakes AI systems
Article.Authors: Kamireddy R.; Bijjam P.; Eraganeni S.; Reddy A.
Article.Abstract: The recent successful adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in several important applications has made it imperative to integrate operational machine learning with governance frameworks to facilitate regulatory alignment, structured accountability mechanisms, and risk-based decision-making. Current MLOps frameworks are good at controlling the technical lifecycle of AI models, but are less likely to support governance needs in regulated environments. This paper introduces a governance-oriented MLOps framework to support healthcare and financial AI systems, namely GRACE-AI (Governance, Risk, Assurance, Compliance, and Explainability for Artificial Intelligence). The proposed framework is composed of four interconnected layers, (i) Regulatory Alignment Layer: mapping regulatory requirements into pipeline constraints that incorporate information about governance; the Regulatory Alignment Layer is presented as a proposed architectural component for automated obligation extraction; its clause-level classification performance was not independently benchmarked in this study (ii) Dynamic Risk-Tiering Engine: assigning adaptive governance risk levels based on composite risk scores; (iii) Continuous Assurance Pipeline: drift detection, monitoring, automated recalibration, and anomaly tracking; and (iv) Explainability-by-Design Module: generation of stakeholder-oriented and interpretable explanations. The proposed framework was evaluated using three benchmark datasets supporting four prediction tasks across the healthcare and financial domains, achieving an average accuracy of 96.38% and an unweighted cross-task mean AUC of 0.973; this is 2.78 percentage points above the strongest evaluated standalone baseline (Transformer, 93.60%) and 6.06 percentage points above the mean of the five evaluated standalone baselines. In addition, GRACE-AI could cover 94.7% of the risk, reduce compliance overhead by 38.6%, and detect drift with an average latency of 1.8 s. The findings suggest that the proposed governance model is effective in a controlled experimental setting and could be used to enable trustworthy, governance-aware deployment of AI in regulated environments. In the future, the framework will be validated under operational, real-world conditions with human involvement and at production scale.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: financial AI; AI governance; MLOps; regulatory compliance; artificial intelligence in healthcare; drift detection; continuous assurance; model monitoring; explainability

Article.Title: Multitrophic interactions between endophytic Metarhizium anisopliae and the predatory mite Amblyseius swirskii and their effects on predator population growth and predation rate
Article.Authors: Safavi S.; Jarrahi A.
Article.Abstract: Endophytic entomopathogenic fungi offer promising opportunities for integrating microbial and arthropod biological control agents, yet their effects across multiple trophic levels remain insufficiently understood. This study evaluated the compatibility of endophytic Metarhizium anisopliae with the predatory mite Amblyseius swirskii in a strawberry– Tetranychus urticae –predator system. Strawberry plants were inoculated with M. anisopliae , and the biological performance, population growth, predation capacity, and prey preference of A. swirskii were assessed when feeding on T. urticae developed on fungus-colonized or control plants. Endophytic colonization of strawberry plants did not compromise predator performance. The intrinsic rate of increase, finite rate of increase, and pre-adult survival of A. swirskii were not significantly affected by prey origin. However, predators feeding prey reared on fungus-colonized plants showed prolonged deutonymphal and adult periods, higher fecundity and gross reproductive rate, and increased consumption during the immature stages. Lifetime prey consumption was 41.43% higher, resulting in a 20.27% increase in the net predation rate ( C 0 ). Other predation parameters and prey preference did not differ significantly between treatments. Under controlled, short-term conditions within a single generation, endophytic M. anisopliae did not adversely affect the measured performance of A. swirskii , suggesting potential compatibility. However, long-term and multigenerational effects, performance under mixed-prey conditions, and efficacy under greenhouse and field conditions require further investigation. These findings are specific to the fungal isolate tested.

Article.Title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy across acute and post-acute phases after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a multi-cohort randomized controlled pilot study (HOT-RESUS 1)
Article.Authors: Schnaubelt S.; Snijders E.; Strouven C.; Janssens E.; Verdonck P.; Lateur J.; Peeters M.; Vermeersch G.; De Paep R.; Saenen J.; Snoeckx A.; Sulzgruber P.; De Maeyer C.; Schlager O.; Jorens P.; Monsieurs K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains untested in humans despite promising preclinical evidence. We thus evaluated feasibility, tolerability, observed treatment-related adverse events, and early biological signals of HBOT across three distinct clinical cohorts and exposure subgroups. This prospective, single-centre, randomized, controlled, open-label pilot study enrolled (i) Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients with sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) within the preceding 24 h, (ii) long-term OHCA survivors, and (iii) healthy volunteers. Within each cohort, participants were randomized to no HBOT, one HBOT session, or five HBOT sessions. Assessments included serial laboratory biomarkers, vascular function, neurocognitive testing, and patient-reported outcomes. Analyses were primarily descriptive, with additional between-group comparisons considered exploratory. The prespecified recruitment target was achieved (45/45 participants), all assigned HBOT sessions were completed (90/90; 100%), and all scheduled blood samples were obtained. No HBOT-related adverse events occurred. In ICU patients, serial biomarkers demonstrated pronounced temporal changes during the acute post-cardiac-arrest phase across inflammatory, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, neuronal injury, and myocardial injury domains, whereas direct comparison of trajectories between HBOT groups were generally inconclusive. In long-term OHCA survivors and healthy volunteers, exploratory analyses suggested reductions in arterial stiffness and, particularly among survivors, favourable changes in neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes, with several favourable numerical patterns observed in HBOT-exposed groups. Given the small subgroup sizes, extensive multiplicity, and generally inconclusive direct between-group comparisons, these findings remain exploratory. HOT-RESUS 1 demonstrated that the prespecified recruitment and HBOT procedures could be completed as planned, including treatment of selected acute post-ROSC ICU patients in a specialised hyperbaric centre, with no HBOT-related adverse events observed. Exploratory analyses showed dynamics of inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, arterial stiffness, and neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes, with several favourable numerical patterns observed in HBOT-exposed groups. Although the small pilot sample, extensive multiplicity, and largely inconclusive direct between-group comparisons preclude attribution of these changes to HBOT or conclusions regarding biological or clinical efficacy, the findings identify possible biological and functional outcomes for further investigation in adequately powered randomized trials.

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving federated analysis reproduces multicentre alteplase compared to tenecteplase (AcT) stroke trial
Article.Authors: Bao Y.; Saad Z.; Duarte K.; Abbas F.; Sajobi T.; Holodinsky J.; Menon B.; Drew S.
Article.Abstract: Cross-jurisdictional clinical trials face increasing barriers from data privacy regulations and governance restrictions that limit centralized individual patient data (IPD) transfer. Federated analysis, where standardized statistical scripts execute locally and only aggregate outputs are shared, offers a privacy-preserving alternative. We evaluated whether a federated analytical framework could reproduce the non-inferiority findings of the Alteplase Compared to Tenecteplase (AcT) randomized controlled trial. We developed Starfish-FL, a general-purpose federated analysis platform, and applied it to AcT IPD from 21 stroke centres across 8 Canadian provinces (n = 1577). The dataset was partitioned by site to emulate a federated environment. Each site computed treatment effect estimates (proportion difference and standard error) for tenecteplase versus alteplase, combined using a fixed-effects federated meta-analytic framework. The primary outcome was excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0–1 at 90–120 days), with a non-inferiority margin of − 5%. Data from 21 sites comprising 1577 patients (806 tenecteplase, 771 alteplase) were included. Reproducing AcT's crude estimation from the same site partition yielded a risk difference of 2.14% (95% CI − 2.61 to 6.88%) for the primary outcome against 2.1% (95% CI − 2.6 to 6.9%) in the original centralized analysis, matching on the estimate and both interval bounds. The site-stratified federated estimator yielded 2.12% (95% CI − 2.53 to 6.77%). Non-inferiority was met under both. All four outcomes reproduced the published result at the published precision, so mRS 0–2 at 0.80% against 0.8%, symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage at 0.23% against 0.2%, and 90-day mortality at − 0.11% against − 0.1%. Non-inferiority held under all ten sensitivity specifications examined, with the lower confidence bound between − 2.95 and − 2.09% throughout. A federated analytical framework reproduced the non-inferiority conclusions of a large multicentre randomized stroke trial without cross-border IPD transfer. Validated federated infrastructures offer a scalable, privacy-preserving paradigm for future global clinical research.

Article.Title: Nano-curcumin-mediated antibacterial photodynamic therapy activated by blue diode laser or blue LED against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms in infected root canals
Article.Authors: Sherif H.; Abdelgawad L.; Zaki D.; Sherief M.; Eissa S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of nano-curcumin activated by a 450-nm diode laser or a blue light-emitting diode (LED) against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms in infected root canals. Sixty-six extracted human single-rooted teeth were prepared, sterilized, inoculated with Enterococcus faecalis , and incubated at 37 °C for three weeks. Six specimens were used to confirm biofilm formation by scanning electron microscopy (SEM; n = 3) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM; n = 3). The remaining 60 specimens were randomly allocated into six experimental groups ( n = 10 per group): Group 1, 2.5% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl); Group 2, diode laser alone; Group 3, LED alone; Group 4, nano-curcumin; Group 5, nano-curcumin + diode laser; and Group 6, nano-curcumin + LED. Antibacterial efficacy was evaluated by colony-forming unit (CFU) counts and CLSM-based live/dead biofilm assessment. Data were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s post hoc test ( p < 0.05). Significant reductions in Enterococcus faecalis CFU counts were observed in all treatment groups compared with baseline ( p < 0.05), except for Groups 2 and 3. Group 1 exhibited the greatest antibacterial efficacy (99% CFU reduction), followed by Group 5 (70.02%) and Group 6 (68.29%), whereas Group 4 demonstrated a modest antibacterial effect (27.86% CFU reduction). CLSM findings were consistent with the CFU results, with Group 1 exhibiting the greatest reduction in biofilm viability, followed by Groups 5 and 6. Within the limitations of this in vitro study, activation of nano-curcumin with either a 450-nm diode laser or a blue LED enhanced its antibacterial activity and may have potential as an adjunctive approach to conventional root canal disinfection.

Article.Title: Digital literacy and teaching innovative behavior among physical education teachers: a cross-sectional moderated mediation study
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Zhu B.; Gu J.; Guo P.; Xiang Y.; Luo L.; Li R.; Xie T.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Although digital literacy is critical for physical education teachers, the indirect pathways linking it to teaching innovative behavior remain unclear. Guided by Social Cognitive Theory and Conservation of Resources Theory, this study tested a moderated mediation model in which teaching self-efficacy mediates the digital literacy–teaching innovative behavior association, and perceived organizational support moderates the teaching self-efficacy–teaching innovative behavior association. A cross-sectional survey included 984 primary and secondary physical education teachers in Jiangsu, Hubei, and Sichuan, China. Digital literacy was positively associated with teaching innovative behavior (c = 0.351, p < 0.001). Teaching self-efficacy partially mediated this association (indirect effect = 0.056, 95% bootstrap CI [0.030, 0.084]). Perceived organizational support moderated the teaching self-efficacy–teaching innovative behavior association (B = 0.057, p < 0.001). The index of moderated mediation was significant (0.042, 95% bootstrap CI [0.019, 0.065]). Conditional indirect effects were significant at mean and high support but not low support. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested the moderated mediation pathway was significant in primary and junior secondary teachers but not senior secondary teachers, although most between-group differences were not statistically significant. The moderation model explained 14.9% and the full model explained 18.6% of variance in teaching innovative behavior. Findings are correlational, not causal.

Article.Title: Distribution and genetic relatedness of multidrug-resistant E. coli in poultry farms: a One Health perspective
Article.Authors: Wafa A.; Bakr W.; Omran E.; Elsenduony M.; ElSayed N.; Reda O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The prevalence of pathogens, including multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, especially extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli (ESBL-EC), in poultry farms is a matter of public health and One Health significance. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the distribution and genetic relatedness of MDR and ESBL-producing E. coli from different reservoirs in poultry farms. A total of 90 samples were collected from five poultry farms: 60 chicken samples (66.7%), 15 farm-worker stool samples (16.7%), and 15 pooled environmental samples (16.7%), comprising five pooled litter samples, five pooled farm-soil samples, and five pooled agricultural-soil samples. Chickens were selected using a simple random technique (12 samples from each of the five farms), and all available farm workers were included. E. coli was isolated and identified, and the antimicrobial susceptibility profile of the isolates was determined. All isolates were genotyped using Enterobacterial Repetitive Intergenic Consensus polymerase chain reaction (ERIC-PCR) to assess similarity and genetic relatedness among isolates from the different compartments. Out of the total 90 samples, 52.2% ( n = 47) were MDR and 40.0% ( n = 36) were ESBL-producing E. coli . Among the 60 chicken samples, 63.3% ( n = 38) were MDR and 50.0% ( n = 30) were ESBL producers. Among the 15 pooled environmental samples, 46.7% ( n = 7) were MDR-positive and 26.7% ( n = 4) were ESBL-positive. Relatively lower ESBL positivity was observed among farm workers (2/15; 13.3%). Similar ERIC-PCR fingerprint patterns were observed among isolates from chickens, workers, and environmental compartments. Chicken isolates showed higher observed MDR and ESBL positivity than isolates from the pooled environmental samples and farm workers. Similar ERIC-PCR profiles across sources suggest genetic relatedness and potential epidemiological connectivity. These findings underscore the value of integrated One Health surveillance strategies.

Article.Title: The Cdh23tm2a mouse allele causes progressive hearing loss that is not improved by postnatal Cdh23 gene expression
Article.Authors: Pentland D.; Blackburn J.; Altiti B.; Ingham N.; Kirwin D.; Steel K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cdh23 encodes cadherin related 23, a cadherin which is an essential component of the tip link of stereocilia on the sensory hair cells of the inner ear. Mutations in human CDH23 lead to either non-syndromic deafness or Usher syndrome, while mutations in mouse Cdh23 lead to hearing impairment with or without balance defects. Here we characterise the Cdh23 tm2a mouse mutant and show that the mutation causes reduced transcription of Cdh23 and early-onset progressive hearing loss in Cdh23 tm2a/tm2a homozygotes. Cdh23 +/tm2a heterozygotes also exhibit progressive hearing loss but only at high frequencies, and this was dependent on the presence of the Cdh23 ahl allele which is present in the background C57BL/6N strain. Scanning electron microscopy revealed stereocilia bundle defects in homozygous mutants but stereocilia appeared normal in heterozygotes. To investigate whether hearing loss could be reversed by inducing expression of the gene, we removed the transcription disruption cassette within the Cdh23 tm2a mutant allele using tamoxifen-inducible Flp recombinase at either 4 days or 21 days old, but no improvements in Auditory Brainstem Response thresholds or stereocilia bundle appearance were detected. These findings suggest that any treatments for Cdh23 -associated hearing loss would probably need to applied very early in development, before stereocilia are fully formed.

Article.Title: Scale-dependent associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM2.5 concentrations across contrasting landscape backgrounds in Beijing
Article.Authors: Wang G.; Liu H.; Zhou J.; Yu Y.; Sun C.; Yu P.; Kang J.; Liu Z.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM 2.5 concentrations may vary with spatial scale and landscape background, yet these variations remain insufficiently understood. We examined these relationships using annual mean PM 2.5 concentrations from 13 monitoring stations in Beijing during 2021–2025 and high-resolution urban landscape data. We fitted XGBoost models using eight predictors, including five two-dimensional landscape indicators and three three-dimensional morphological indicators, within 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 km buffers. SHAP analysis was then used to assess the relative importance of these predictors in model predictions. A dominance-ratio approach was used to classify the surroundings of each station into blue-, green-, or grey-space backgrounds. The highest-ranked predictor changed across scales, from frontal area index ( FAI ) at 1.0 km (mean absolute SHAP = 0.824 µg m −2 ) to building height ( BH ) at 1.5 km (0.813 µg m −2 ) and street canyon height-to-width ratio ( HW ) at 2.0 km (0.756 µg m −2 ). At each scale, the single station classified as blue-space had the lowest PM 2.5 concentration, whereas grey-space backgrounds generally showed the highest. Under the 1.0 km classification, the 2023 increase was 1.1 µg m −2 at the blue-space site, compared with mean increases of 3.3 and 3.5 at green- and grey-space stations, respectively.

Article.Title: Intraspecific differentiation in metabolite diversity of a monotypic endemic Indianthus in the Western Ghats
Article.Authors: Bhat K.; Pandi V.; Gayathri R.; Mahim B.; Udupa S.; Muthusamy A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Indianthus virgatus (Marantaceae), a monotypic genus endemic to the Western Ghats–Sri Lanka Biodiversity Hotspot, represents an evolutionarily distinctive lineage for which intraspecific metabolomic variation remains poorly documented. Such variation can provide insights into biochemical differentiation among populations and potential environmental interactions. We used untargeted high-resolution liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (HR-LC-MS) to characterize metabolomic diversity across nine geographically distinct populations of I. virgatus in the Western Ghats. A total of 3,673 metabolite features were detected, of which 214 putative plant-derived metabolites were annotated and retained for downstream analyses following quality filtering. Multivariate analyses revealed differences in metabolomic profiles among the sampled population composites. Principal component analysis showed that the first two components explained 51.2% of the total variation. Variable importance in projection analysis highlighted glutamyl derivatives, amino acid intermediates, and phenolic compounds as important contributors to the observed separation. Distance-based redundancy analysis identified precipitation during the coldest quarter as the only individually significant environmental predictor ( P < 0.05), although the overall model was not statistically significant ( P > 0.05). KEGG pathway analysis indicated nominal enrichment of pyrimidine metabolism, which did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction (FDR = 0.0539). This preliminary metabolomic characterization provides a biochemical foundation for future multi-omics investigations integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic data to elucidate the ecological and evolutionary processes underlying intraspecific diversity in I. virgatus . It also suggests a basis for further research into its phytochemical composition, bioactive compounds, and potential pharmacological applications.

Article.Title: Multifunctional isoliquiritigenin-loaded chitosan/alginate hydrogels with antibacterial and antifibrotic potential for wound dressing applications
Article.Authors: Tymetska S.; Wnuk D.; Bernasik A.; Brzychczy-Włoch M.; Drożdż K.; Targosz‐Korecka M.; Ozimek J.; Szajna K.; Krok F.; Raczkowska J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic wounds present complex healing challenges due to bacterial infection, persistent inflammation, and dysregulated extracellular matrix remodeling. Although isoliquiritigenin (ISL) exhibits potent anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifibrotic properties, its low aqueous solubility hinders direct hydrogel incorporation. Here, alginate (Alg)- and chitosan/alginate (Cht/Alg)-based hydrogels were developed for localized ISL delivery, using Tween 20 (Tw20) or decyl glucoside (DecGlu) as non-ionic surfactants to enhance compound release. Polymer composition and surfactant addition significantly influenced hydrogel morphology, swelling, surface chemistry, micromechanical properties, and porosity. Surfactant-enriched Alg formulations increased ISL release by 52–76% within 24 h. In vitro assays demonstrated high cytocompatibility for Cht/Alg systems (>80% viability in MTT and >90% in crystal violet/LDH assays at 144 h), whereas the Alg/Tw20 formulation exhibited cytotoxicity. ISL-containing extracts significantly attenuated TGF-β 1 induced fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, reducing α-SMA-positive cells by 50% for Alg and 29% for Cht/Alg, with DecGlu further reducing them to 15.0% and 20.0%, respectively. ISL also reduced total collagen I and fibronectin protein levels. Furthermore, Cht/Alg hydrogels exhibited marked antibacterial activity, achieving 4- and 5-log reductions in Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , respectively. Overall, ISL-enriched Cht/Alg-DecGlu hydrogels represent a promising multifunctional wound-contact platform combining localized bioactive delivery, excellent cytocompatibility, antibacterial efficacy, and potent modulation of profibrotic responses.

Article.Title: A highly reliable, self-healing photovoltaic cell-level dynamic reconfigurable architecture based on software-defined energy flow management
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Wang D.; Sun S.; Zhu Q.; Liu F.
Article.Abstract: Traditional crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules employ irreversible laminated packaging. Once individual cells fail or become obstructed, the entire string’s output power declines significantly, and repairs cannot be made without damaging the module—this constitutes a fundamental limitation of “static packaging.” This paper proposes a cell-level dynamic reconfigurable photovoltaic architecture that encapsulates each cell as a standardized “power generation cell,” integrating chip-level power optimizers, microfluidic active cooling systems, and high-speed industrial communication networks. Through a matrix backplate, the system enables online hot-swapping of cells and millisecond-scale electrical reconfiguration. This architecture redefines photovoltaic systems from static “power panels” into self-healing energy networks with physically maintainable components and software-defined energy pathways. A joint electrical-informatics-reliability simulation model was developed, comparing the proposed architecture with traditional modules under local failures, non-uniform shading, and long-term degradation conditions using Python simulations. Results demonstrate that during single-cell failure, the proposed architecture isolates the faulty cell and switches to backup cells within 5 ms, achieving power loss below 2%; over a 25-year lifecycle, the system’s rated output availability approaches 100%, whereas traditional modules show annual declines to approximately 82%. Active liquid cooling maintains cell temperatures at 45 ± 2 °C, thereby substantially reducing thermal hotspot risks under the simulated conditions. This study establishes a novel system paradigm and quantitative benchmark for next-generation high-reliability, intelligent photovoltaic power systems. The reported performance metrics are derived from numerical simulation; experimental validation through hardware-in-the-loop testing and outdoor prototyping remains necessary and is outlined as future work.

Article.Title: Engagement phenotypes for a sample of 102,684 AI mental health chatbot (ash) users and dose-response associations with clinical outcomes
Article.Authors: Wolfe E.; Su T.; Tieleman O.; Hull T.; Malgaroli M.; Stamatis C.
Article.Abstract: Conversational AI chatbots are emerging as scalable mental health tools, but little is known about real world engagement or its relationship to clinical outcomes. To characterize engagement phenotypes among users of Ash, a purpose-built AI mental health chatbot, and examine associations with clinical change and working alliance. K-means clustering across eight behavioral features identified engagement phenotypes among 102,684 users. Subsamples completed the PHQ-9 ( n = 298), GAD-7 ( n = 298), and MSPSS (social support; n = 194) at baseline and 3 weeks; 11,437 users completed baseline Working Alliance Inventory (WAI). Five engagement phenotypes emerged: Early Dropouts (52.2%), Power Users (1.6%), Intensive Users (4.1%), Weekly Users (25.3%), and a novel Concentrated User pattern (16.8%); across users, 66.9% had at least one overnight session (9pm-5am). Significant pre-post improvements occurred in depression ( d = -0.51), anxiety ( d = -0.57), and social support ( d = 0.22). An observed dose-response gradient in self-reported depression improvement was replicated in a larger sample using model-predicted PHQ-9 ( n = 23,813), with the largest improvements among high-engagement Power and Intensive Users ( d = -0.57 and -0.50) and the smallest among Early Dropouts ( d = -0.22). Higher working alliance predicted depression improvement and moderated the engagement-social support relationship. Engagement with AI mental health tools is multidimensional, and different clinical outcomes respond to different dimensions of use. Findings caution against treating session counts as a primary engagement metric and offer naturalistic, correlational evidence consistent with clinical benefit of purpose-built conversational AI, pending confirmation in controlled designs.

Article.Title: Antifungal bioprotective effect of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum against Aspergillus niger and Penicillium notatum in set yogurt during refrigerated storage
Article.Authors: Mirzalou Z.; Homayouni-Rad H.; Aval M.; Bonyadi N.; Nami Y.; Homayouni-Rad A.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the antifungal bioprotective potential of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PTCC 1058 in set yogurt during 28 days of refrigerated storage (4 ± 1 °C). Four distinct formulations were evaluated: regular yogurt (Y1), yogurt containing L. plantarum (Y2), pre-acidified yogurt with L. plantarum (Y3), and chemically acidified milk prepared with glucono-δ-lactone (GDL) without cultures (Y4). Samples were monitored for mold counts ( Aspergillus niger and Penicillium notatum ), viable counts of L. plantarum , physicochemical properties, and sensory attributes. Viable cell counts of L. plantarum changed during storage ( P < 0.05), but reached approximately 9 log CFU/g by day 28. In fungal challenge assays, L. plantarum -containing yogurts (Y2 and Y3) demonstrated pronounced antifungal activity, whereas regular yogurt (Y1) and chemically acidified milk (Y4) showed no noticeable fungal suppression. Specifically, viable counts of P. notatum decreased significantly by ~ 1.8 log CFU/g from day 14, and A. niger was reduced by ~ 1.67 log CFU/g from day 21 through day 28 ( P < 0.05). This indicates that the antifungal effect was biologically mediated by the active culture rather than non-specific bulk acidity. Concurrently, post-acidification in formulations containing L. plantarum contributed to a pH decline to 3.94, which significantly lowered flavor and overall acceptability scores by day 28, whereas color, texture, total solids, and syneresis remained technologically stable. Overall, L. plantarum PTCC 1058 exhibits strong potential as a clean-label bioprotective adjunct against post-processing mold spoilage in set yogurt, although formulation optimization is required to balance bioprotection with long-term sensory quality.

Article.Title: Aligning clinical decisions with patient values: a quantitative analysis of patient and physician preferences in liver cancer treatment decisions
Article.Authors: Winkelmann C.; Bengart P.; Vogt B.; Wacker F.; Neumann T.; Dewald C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract When several liver-directed treatments are feasible, patients and physicians may weigh survival benefit, treatment-related risk, and short-term physical burden differently. We used choice-based conjoint analysis with hierarchical Bayes estimation and preference-share simulations to compare preferences of 69 patients with hepatic malignancies and 40 gastroenterologists in Germany across three scenarios describing early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (Case 1), an isolated colorectal liver metastasis (Case 2) and metastatic uveal melanoma with diffuse hepatic involvement (Case 3). Lifetime extension was the most important attribute for both groups in all scenarios. Patients assigned greater relative importance to well-being after the intervention in Cases 1 and 2 (25.2% vs 10.9% and 22.3% vs 12.1%, posterior probability of direction [pd] ≥ 99%), whereas gastroenterologists assigned greater importance to tumor-removal probability in Case 1 (24.3% vs 17.2%, pd 95.8%). In Case 2, the simulated ablation share was higher among patients (86.6% vs 71.8%, p < 0.01), with the complementary resection share higher among gastroenterologists. In Case 3, simulated shares did not differ significantly. Whether and in which attributes the two groups differed thus depended on the clinical scenario. Patient priorities should therefore not be inferred from general assumptions but addressed explicitly during shared decision-making.

Article.Title: A causal decision framework for selecting industry 4.0 technologies to overcome open innovation barriers in construction
Article.Authors: Shojaei P.; Nikbakht A.
Article.Abstract: The construction industry has long struggled to embrace open innovation, not for lack of intent, but because of deeply embedded financial, organizational, and cultural barriers that resist change. This study responds to that challenge by building an integrated decision-support framework that identifies which Industry 4.0 technologies are best positioned to address these barriers. The research followed a three-stage design. Following a systematic literature review and expert content validation, 11 open innovation barriers and 7 technologies were retained. Then, a two-method analytical sequence combining Pythagorean Fuzzy DEMATEL (PF-DEMATEL) with Grey MABAC applied. PF-DEMATEL mapped the causal structure among the barriers, identifying inadequate support from top management and their risk attitude (C2; weight = 0.1119, D + R = 4.566) as the central systemic mediator, while difficulty in finding suitable human resources for R&D (C6; D − R = 1.730) and market uncertainty regarding innovative products (C4; D − R = 1.023) emerged as the dominant root causes driving the broader barrier network. Grey MABAC then ranked the seven technologies by their weighted mitigation potential, placing Building Information Modelling well ahead of the field, followed by the Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence. The findings offer construction practitioners a sequenced, evidence-based roadmap for digital transformation that targets the most influential barriers first and builds collaborative innovation capacity from the ground up.

Article.Title: Crop-specific vegetation indices and phenological windows for spectral separability of 46 United States crops
Article.Authors: Rahimi E.; Jung C.
Article.Abstract: Vegetation indices designed for greenness are routinely applied to crop discrimination, yet searches for better indices rarely control for redundant candidates, selection bias or spatial dependence. We quantified one-versus-rest spectral separability for 46 crops on 16,647 parcels across the contiguous United States in 2019, 2021 and 2023, using 36 dekadal Sentinel-2 composites. A generative grammar produced 985 index expressions, of which 563 were distinguishable to rank-based methods; each was scored at every dekad against spatially matched neighboring parcels, and leading candidates were re-evaluated with selection confined to training folds. Optima were largely crop-specific (38 different best indices for 46 crops), with median held-out separability of 0.846 across years. Once candidate-family size was equalized, no index family dominated. Held-out separability fell from 0.872 in training to 0.835 when years were withheld and to 0.734 when spatial blocks were withheld, a gap that persisted after removing test parcels near training parcels. Thinning clear observations left a fixed index essentially unchanged but degraded re-selection; nevertheless, re-selection within a withheld region outperformed, on average, indices transferred from other regions at every observation density tested. Index atlases should therefore report sets of near-equivalent indices, calendar windows and the domain over which separability was validated.

Article.Title: An experimental study on enhancing learning motivation and academic performance through AI literacy training
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Song G.; Zhen H.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in higher education, creating opportunities to support personalized learning. However, the educational value of AI depends not only on access to AI tools but also on students’ motivation, academic self-efficacy, and learning progress. This study presents the Motivation–Performance Adaptive AI Literacy Optimization Framework (MP-AILOF), a conceptual framework designed to integrate AI literacy instruction with learner-related indicators to inform adaptive instructional decisions. The framework combines learner profiling, motivational assessment, academic performance monitoring, and a proposed feedback-based instructional optimization process. Its empirical evaluation used a two-group pre-test–post-test dataset comprising 80 undergraduate students, with 40 students in the experimental group and 40 in the control group, from one higher-education institution. The experimental group received MP-AILOF-supported AI literacy instruction, whereas the control group received conventional classroom instruction. Academic self-efficacy, learning motivation, and grade point average (GPA) were assessed before and after the intervention. Paired-sample t-tests were used to examine within-group changes, and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to compare post-test outcomes while adjusting for baseline scores. In the supplied dataset, the experimental group showed statistically significant increases in all three outcomes. The ANCOVA analyses also indicated higher adjusted post-test scores for the experimental group than for the control group. These findings describe the observed results in the available sample and should be interpreted in light of the study design and the need to verify the recorded GPA values against the institutional grading scale. The implementation package reproduces the principal descriptive and inferential analyses; it does not independently validate the framework’s proposed GBR prediction and adaptive optimization components. Further research using verified data, documented allocation procedures, validated measurement instruments, and follow-up assessments is required to evaluate generalizability and the persistence of any observed changes.

Article.Title: The brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge for establishing correspondence between pre-operative and follow-up MRI scans of diffuse glioma patients
Article.Authors: Baheti B.; Chakrabarty S.; Akbari H.; Bilello M.; Wiestler B.; Schwarting J.; Calabrese E.; Rudie J.; Abidi S.; Mousa M.; Villanueva-Meyer J.; Fields B.; Kofler F.; Shinohara R.; Iglesias J.; Mok T.; Chung A.; Wodzinski M.; Jurgas A.; Marini N.; Atzori M.; Müller H.; Großbröhmer C.; Siebert H.; Hansen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Registration of longitudinal brain MRI scans containing pathologies remains a challenging problem, due to substantial changes in tissue appearance. While medical image registration methods have advanced considerably, they often lack the required precision and robustness. To address this gap, we introduced the brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge, the first public benchmark specifically designed for deformable registration between pre-operative and follow-up scans of patients with adult-type diffuse gliomas. Conducted in conjunction with ISBI-2022 and MICCAI-2022, BraTS-Reg provides de-identified, multi-institutional, multi-parametric MRI data accompanied by expert-annotated landmark points across time. Training data with ground truth annotations were publicly released for algorithm development, while validation data without annotations enabled pre-testing. Submitted containerized algorithms were evaluated on hidden testing cases. Quantitative evaluation was based on median Euclidean error (MEE), Robustness, and the determinant of Jacobian of the displacement field. Top-ranked methods demonstrated comparable performance and shared key features, including pre-alignment of scans, deep neural networks, inverse consistency analysis, and per-case test-time optimization. The best method achieved MEE comparable to inter-rater variability for 63% of landmarks, underscoring the need for further improvements in accuracy and robustness relative to human experts. BraTS-Reg serves as a three-fold active resource for research on image registration, providing a publicly available dataset, a framework for a community benchmark, and online evaluation tools, accessible at https://bratsreg.github.io/ .

Article.Title: Process evaluation showing the importance of co-located, high-intensity and person-centred smoking cessation support in a lung cancer screening setting
Article.Authors: McCutchan G.; Quinn-Scoggins H.; Tong H.; Smith P.; Quaife S.; Callister M.; Thorley R.; Baldwin D.; Beeken R.; Copeland H.; Crosbie P.; Lewis S.; Rogerson S.; Wu Q.; Murray R.; Brain K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evidence regarding optimal integration of smoking cessation is needed to inform implementation of lung cancer screening (LCS) and reduce smoking-related inequalities. The Yorkshire Enhanced Stop Smoking Randomised Controlled Trial tested opt-out, co-located standard best practice (SBP) smoking cessation support (control) versus SBP enhanced with theory-informed, personalised risk information derived from participants’ lung scan results to boost quit motivation (intervention). The intervention was tailored to degree of lung/heart damage, and designed to optimise self-efficacy and response-efficacy for quitting smoking 1 . Smoking cessation practitioners (SCPs) received bespoke intervention training in delivering theory-informed behaviour change techniques (BCTs). We conducted a nested process evaluation to evaluate the implementation of optimised smoking cessation support compared to SBP. Semi-structured interviews were carried out with 45 trial participants and eight SCPs at 4-, 12- and 52-weeks after screening (participants) or training (SCPs). Interviews were analysed thematically to assess intervention fidelity, exposure, context, contamination and theory. Observations of SCP consultations on the mobile screening unit (n = 84; 4%) and 4-weeks after screening (n = 132; 13%) were analysed to test fidelity, context and contamination. Intervention context was paramount: participants in both trial arms described benefits of co-located and ongoing high-intensity smoking cessation support, with immediate provision of pharmacotherapy. Tailored, non-judgemental care was considered key to initiating and sustaining quitting, particularly for participants at various points along their quit pathway and awaiting a possible lung cancer diagnosis. Fidelity was high (97%) on the screening unit and moderate (75%) 4-weeks after screening, and moderate for the enhanced intervention (77%) 4-weeks after screening. SBP and the intervention was flexibly delivered according to time constraints, participant motivation to quit, anxiety about screening and screening and/or booklet results. There was variation in how participants used and shared their booklets (exposure). Contamination of SCP intervention training was observed, with SCPs delivering theory-informed BCTs across both trial arms e.g. using the LCS context to boost response-efficacy beliefs. Provision of co-located, high intensity and person-centred smoking cessation support was vital, irrespective of trial arm. Investment in specialist LCS smoking cessation practitioners may harness the benefits of LCS as a teachable moment for cessation. Article.Title: Broad-spectrum antimicrobial white light preserves cellular and tissue homeostasis without detectable cytotoxic or genotoxic damage in primary human skin models
Article.Authors: Bartolocci V.; Capone A.; Di Meo E.; Arcano S.; Dellambra E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has stimulated the development of non-pharmacological approaches for microbial control in healthcare and other occupied environments. Antimicrobial white light (aWL) inactivates microorganisms through photoexcitation of endogenous chromophores while providing environmental illumination, but its photobiological effects on human skin require characterization. Here, we evaluated the acute photobiological effects of a broad-spectrum aWL source (peak 400–420 nm) under a conservative close-proximity exposure scenario using primary human keratinocytes, dermal fibroblasts, and reconstructed three-dimensional skin equivalents, with UV-B irradiation as a phototoxic reference. Cellular responses were assessed by clonogenic survival, tissue architecture, intracellular ROS generation, antioxidant enzyme modulation, oxidative DNA damage, cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs), and p53/p21 pathway activation. Unlike UV-B, which reduced clonogenic ability, increased ROS, induced CPDs, and activated p53/p21 signaling, aWL preserved cell survival and tissue structure without detectable DNA damage or stress-pathway activation. Acute aWL exposure did not induce detectable ROS accumulation, although modulation of antioxidant enzyme expression was observed, consistent with a possible redox-regulatory response. Overall, broad-spectrum aWL preserves cutaneous cellular and tissue homeostasis without detectable cytotoxic or genotoxic effects under the acute conditions investigated. These findings support further evaluation, including long-term and cumulative exposure studies, to define the broader safety profile.

Article.Title: Real-time predictive control of fusion plasmas with an adaptive digital twin
Article.Authors: Morishita Y.; Kenmochi N.; Murakami S.; Funaba H.; Osakabe M.; Motojima G.; Mizuno Y.; Nagahara K.; Okuno A.; Ueno G.; Nakanishi H.; Tokunaga S.; Ishii Y.; Yokoyama M.; Sakamoto R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fusion plasma control requires real-time coordination of multiple actuators under partial observations and model uncertainty. Here we demonstrate predictive control of a fusion plasma on the Large Helical Device using an adaptive digital-twin system that combines data assimilation with physics-based integrated modeling. The digital twin was dynamically synchronized with experimental observations, while heating and fueling inputs were optimized from its predictions to drive the plasma toward target states. Real-time adaptation and control estimation were performed on a remote supercomputer located approximately 1,000 km from the experimental device, using up to 10,000 CPU cores. Multivariate control of electron density, electron temperature, and ion temperature was demonstrated in five representative target cases. These results establish a closed loop between an adaptive digital twin and a physical fusion plasma. They provide a route toward digital-twin-based control of fusion reactors and other partially observed complex systems.
