Article.Title: Region-guided cross-attention and view-GCN for interpretable multi-view echocardiographic classification of common left-to-right shunt lesions
Article.Authors: Chen L.; Zhang X.; Li Q.; Guo J.; Zhang P.
Article.Abstract: Echocardiography is the primary imaging modality for screening common congenital left-to-right shunt lesions; however, accurate diagnosis requires systematic integration of multiple standard views by experienced sonographers. Existing deep learning approaches typically analyze single views or rely on simple concatenation of multi-view features, which fail to capture anatomical relationships across imaging planes. Moreover, echocardiographic models are prone to shortcut learning, attending to background artifacts rather than clinically meaningful cardiac structures. We developed an interpretable end-to-end multi-view fusion framework integrating spatial region-guided cross-attention (RG-CA) and a view graph convolutional network (View-GCN). The framework was developed using a retrospective single-center cohort comprising 2,205 patients and 27,535 cine clips across four diagnostic categories: normal, atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). All dataset partitioning was performed at the patient level. The cohort was stratified into a development cohort of 1,764 patients (564 Normal, 576 ASD, 360 VSD, and 264 PDA) and an independent test cohort of 441 patients (141 Normal, 144 ASD, 90 VSD, and 66 PDA). All cine clips, sampled frames, and echocardiographic views from the same patient were retained within the same partition, and five-fold cross-validation was conducted exclusively within the development cohort. Five standard echocardiographic views were included: subcostal, apical four-chamber, parasternal short-axis, parasternal long-axis, and suprasternal long-axis. Cine clips were processed as frame-based multi-view image sets: representative frames were sampled from each clip, frame-level features were aggregated within each cine clip to obtain clip-level representations, clip-level representations belonging to the same echocardiographic view were further aggregated into a single view-level representation, and missing views were handled using zero-padding together with a view-availability mask. Zero-padding and the availability mask specify how the model processes missing views, but this architectural mechanism is not itself an empirical demonstration of missing-view robustness. The retained analysis did not include a controlled stress test in which one or more of the five views were systematically removed. View-GCN generated one final patient-level prediction per patient. No explicit temporal sequence model was used in the current implementation. Physician-annotated lesion masks were used only during model training as anatomical supervision for the mask-guided attention penalty (MGAP); no manually annotated mask is required during validation, testing, or clinical inference. Stratified five-fold cross-validation within the 1,764-patient development cohort yielded a reported mean patient-level AUC of 0.976 ± 0.015 for distinguishing normal cases from common left-to-right shunt lesions. In the independent test cohort, the model correctly classified 428 of 441 patients, yielding an overall multiclass diagnostic accuracy of 97.05%. The test cohort comprised 141 Normal, 144 ASD, 90 VSD, and 66 PDA patients. No ASD, VSD, or PDA cases were misclassified as normal, and the normal class achieved a precision of 1.0000. All reported test-set diagnostic-performance analyses were based on one aggregated patient-level prediction per patient rather than frame- or clip-level observations. Quantitative t-SNE/clustering and ablation performance claims are not made because the corresponding data partition, evaluation subset, denominator, and unit of analysis could not be verified. Attention maps are presented as qualitative illustrations only; quantitative Dice, IoU, and attention-mass measures are not reported. An exploratory L1-regularized analysis of 13 handcrafted grayscale intensity and texture descriptors ranked GLCM dissimilarity, homogeneity, and energy highest. This post hoc analysis was not based on a separately locked training-only subset and was not used as an input to the deep-learning classifier. The fold-specific configurations underlying the reported AUC could not be linked to a single defined training setup, and the exact configuration associated with the checkpoint used for the independent test predictions could not be verified. The proposed framework combines lesion-aware attention and graph-based multi-view reasoning to support automated diagnosis of common left-to-right shunt lesions using echocardiography. By using physician-defined anatomical regions as training-stage supervision rather than inference-stage inputs and integrating diagnostic evidence across multiple views, the training strategy was designed to encourage attention toward clinically relevant anatomical regions while supporting clinically oriented interpretability. The present results do not establish that reliance on non-anatomical artifacts or shortcut learning was quantitatively reduced. The model demonstrated high internal diagnostic accuracy, perfect normal-class precision, and qualitative attention visualizations and exploratory handcrafted intensity/texture-feature findings, suggesting its potential as an AI-assisted screening tool for common left-to-right shunt lesions.

Article.Title: Micron-precision depth control in automated volumetric laser ablation with ultrashort laser pulses
Article.Authors: Holder D.; Buser M.; Weber R.; Onuseit V.; Graf T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altered laser-material coupling caused by the formation of Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS). This work presents an industrial-grade setup for closed-loop volumetric ablation that integrates an ultrafast laser, a galvanometer scanner, and coaxial Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for real-time depth control. To overcome measurement artifacts arising from the evolving surface morphology and local fluctuations of the OCT depth signal, two complementary correction strategies were implemented. First, a morphology-dependent initial OCT depth offset is determined by extrapolating the stabilized depth progression and subsequently compensated. Second, a pixel-wise moving average of the OCT depth measurements provides a robust termination criterion for local laser processing. The developed processing system with the advanced control software enabled precise and reproducible laser ablation of volumetric structures in AISI 304 stainless steel with a depth accuracy of 1 μm to 2 μm regardless of the investigated initial surface states and process parameters for target depths ranging from 50 μm to 500 μm.

Article.Title: Disinformation-aware decision-making in supply chains using support vector machines
Article.Authors: Dolly B.; Jindal S.; Kumar N.; Kumar V.; Dwivedi S.; Nandal A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Supply chain decision-making is increasingly vulnerable to disinformation—false or misleading information that triggers demand forecasting errors, inventory mismanagement, and procurement disruptions. This study presents a systematic evaluation of five machine learning classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost—for automated supply chain disinformation detection. A hand-verified dataset of 141 labeled statements spanning 12 supply chain topic areas was constructed from professional fact-checking organizations. All classifiers were evaluated using nested stratified 5-fold cross-validation with TF-IDF feature extraction. Linear classifiers substantially outperform ensemble tree methods: LR achieves the highest F1-score (82.2%) and precision (89.0%); SVM achieves the highest AUC-PR (0.925) and ROC-AUC (0.918); NB achieves the highest recall (84.2%). RF and XGBoost lag on F1 (72.4% and 72.5%). A Friedman test (χ 2 (4) = 7.435, p = 0.115) finds no statistically significant difference at the current dataset size; however, Cohen's d effect sizes up to 2.16 indicate a practically meaningful advantage for linear classifiers. A sensitivity analysis on the 104-row supply-chain-only subset confirms results are robust to source-domain confounding. SVM is recommended when threshold flexibility is required; LR when minimising false positives is the priority.

Article.Title: Development of an anti-GM1 antibody-specific glycomimetic for Guillain-Barré syndrome and multifocal motor neuropathy
Article.Authors: Bialic A.; Aliu B.; Pang L.; McGonigal R.; Seydoux E.; Demeestere D.; Salhi S.; Boucraut J.; Delmont E.; Steck A.; Herrendorff R.; Willison H.; Ernst B.; Hänggi P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multifocal motor neuropathy (MMN) is a chronic autoimmune neuropathy predominately affecting motor neurons, caused by IgM antibodies that target the ganglioside GM1. These pathogenic autoantibodies trigger complement-mediated nodal disruption and axonal injury at paranodes and neuromuscular junctions. Similar anti-GM1 antibodies also drive acute forms of peripheral neuropathy, such as Guillain-Barré-Syndrome (GBS), in which molecular mimicry following infection induces cross-reactive immune responses. Antibodies generated against microbial GM1-like glycans bind endogenous GM1, leading to severe neurological symptoms which requires intensive care. Current therapies, such as plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG), can be effective, however, they lack selectivity and can cause adverse effects. We hypothesize that selective depletion of autoreactive anti-GM1 antibodies could provide a targeted therapeutic strategy. This antibody removal can be achieved through multivalent presentation of carbohydrate mimetics of pentasaccharide on a biodegradable poly- l -lysine scaffold. Here we report the development of a lead compound that successfully inhibits binding of anti-GM1 antibodies from patients’ sera to GM1 and effectively prevents binding of anti-GM1 antibodies on terminal axonal networks in vitro and ex vivo.

Article.Title: AI-based non-destructive food screening for detecting calcium carbide (CaC2)-treated bananas
Article.Authors: Alam E.; Hossain M.; Islam M.; Mahmud A.; Tariq F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial fruit ripening using calcium carbide (CaC 2 ) poses a significant food safety concern because prolonged consumption may expose consumers to harmful chemicals. Existing detection methods typically require destructive laboratory analysis, specialized equipment or expert interpretation, limiting their use for rapid on-site screening. Although several AI-based approaches have recently been proposed, they are generally evaluated on individual banana images under controlled conditions, with limited investigation of robustness, computational efficiency and realistic deployment scenarios. This study presents an AI-based framework for the non-destructive detection of calcium carbide-treated bananas using conventional smartphone captured images. Two complementary AI frameworks, Deep Classification with a Frozen Backbone (DCF) and Deep Feature-Based Shallow Classification (DFS), were systematically compared using seven state-of-the-art convolutional and transformer backbones. Unlike previous studies, the proposed framework was evaluated under realistic inspection scenarios containing multiple bananas with different proportions of naturally ripened and calcium carbide-treated fruits, together with comprehensive robustness, explainability and computational efficiency analyses. The DCF-based MobileNet-v2 achieved the highest hold-out classification accuracy of 99.74%, whereas the DFS-based MobileNet-v2​ + Logistic Regression (LR) framework provided the best trade-off between predictive performance and computational efficiency. The MobileNet-v2 + LR framework achieved 95.46% hold-out accuracy, 95.40% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy and correctly classified all 20 images (99.9% mean prediction confidence) in realistic multi-banana inspection, while requiring only 0.65 Giga Floating-Point Operations (GFLOPs) and 0.177 seconds per image. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirmed that the model learned meaningful fruit-specific representations. These findings demonstrate that DFS models combined with smartphone imaging provide an efficient and practical solution for non-destructive food adulteration screening.

Article.Title: Environmental DNA captures ecological communities' dynamics along natural and anthropogenic gradients in a mediterranean lagoon ecosystem
Article.Authors: Zangaro F.; Ismailaj M.; Mercuri E.; Sota D.; Bakaj A.; Specchia V.; Pinna M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mediterranean lagoons are vital ecosystems that provide essential services such as water filtration, carbon sequestration, and habitat support. Despite their high ecological and socio-economic value, transitional waters naturally experience strong environmental variability, including atmospheric phenomena like sea level rise and temperature fluctuations, and are vulnerable to human pressures such as invasive species, pollution, and human activities, emphasising the need for effective conservation strategies. In this study, we employed multiple marker genes and eDNA metabarcoding to characterise the micro-eukaryotic and zoobenthic community structure of lagoon ecosystems and to assess its variation in relation to natural and anthropogenic gradients. Our research focused on a large Albanian lagoon, which, like other Mediterranean lagoon systems, plays a significant role in mitigating climate change. Given the importance of effective management and conservation strategies for these ecosystems, our findings highlight the potential of eDNA metabarcoding as an innovative tool for monitoring biodiversity and informing sustainable practices in Mediterranean lagoon environments. Furthermore, this study demonstrated that analysis through eDNA, simultaneously investigating multiple marker genes and targeting benthic and micro-eukaryotic communities, indirectly highlights the potential influence of an urbanised area on their structure, opening up possibilities for the use of this approach in monitoring and prevention activities.

Article.Title: Systematic identification of bedaquiline-anchored regimens with cross-species efficacy for nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease
Article.Authors: Whittel N.; Guglielmi V.; Cummings J.; Slayden R.
Article.Abstract: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), particularly Mycobacterium avium and Mycobacterium abscessus , are increasingly recognized causes of chronic pulmonary disease, yet current therapies remain prolonged treatment, are frequently associated with adverse effects, and often achieve suboptimal clinical outcomes. To identify therapeutic regimens active against both slow- and rapidly growing NTM species, we systematically evaluated 11 tuberculosis (TB) standard-of-care drugs using a tiered preclinical screening framework comprising minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing, intracellular macrophage infection assays, and species-matched murine lung infection models. Initial susceptibility screening demonstrated substantial differences in drug activity between M. avium and M. abscessus , with cell wall-directed agents generally exhibiting limited cross-species activity. Bedaquiline (BDQ), an FDA-approved antimycobacterial agent, demonstrated the greatest activity among the compounds evaluated in our screening panel and was therefore selected as the foundation for subsequent combination studies. Azithromycin (AZI), clarithromycin (CLA), and ofloxacin (OFL) also emerged as promising agents for further evaluation. Following extended incubation, CLA and AZI MICs increased 2- to 4-fold in M. abscessus , consistent with inducible erm (41)-mediated macrolide resistance, whereas BDQ and OFL retained unchanged activity, supporting BDQ as a candidate therapeutic anchor. Intracellular macrophage studies confirmed BDQ as the most consistently active single agent and demonstrated enhanced bacterial clearance with BDQ + AZI; BDQ + OFL was advanced based on complementary mechanisms and favorable cross-species activity. Subsequent murine lung infection studies confirmed BDQ as the principal driver of antibacterial efficacy against both species. The BDQ + AZI and BDQ + OFL combinations emerged as two-drug therapeutic backbones with activity in both species-matched models, while optimizing the dose and schedule of the three-drug BDQ + AZI+OFL regimen produced cross-species efficacy and the greatest bacterial clearance observed in the M. abscessus model. Treatment performance was examined using complementary measures with distinct purposes: Δlog10 CFU quantified absolute bacterial clearance, Hedges’ g described standardized effect magnitude, quartile classification provided relative within-model ranking, and MACI provided secondary normalization for species-specific in vitro susceptibility. Collectively, these studies establish a systematic translational framework that down-selected 11 TB standard-of-care drugs to 3 prioritized therapeutic agents (BDQ, AZI, and OFL) and ultimately to three BDQ-anchored regimens with activity across both species-matched models. Further, these findings identify BDQ as a candidate therapeutic anchor whose activity is maintained despite inducible erm (41)-mediated macrolide resistance and support the development of modular BDQ-anchored therapeutic platforms that can be optimized for species-specific susceptibility while maintaining a common therapeutic architecture across clinically important NTM species.

Article.Title: Tunable surface functionalities in coffee-waste–derived carbon enable high-capacity antibiotic adsorption
Article.Authors: Hamza W.; Khitouni M.; Almindrej F.; Benzina M.
Article.Abstract: Agro-waste valorization into functional materials represents a sustainable strategy for mitigating emerging water contaminants. In this study, spent coffee waste collected was converted into activated carbon (AC) via two distinct chemical activation routes: phosphoric acid activation (AAC) and alkaline activation (BAC). The materials were comprehensively characterized using BET surface area analysis, pH P ZC determination, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM, and SEM, and EDX. AAC exhibited a higher specific surface area, pore volume, and abundance of surface functional groups than BAC, resulting in a superior adsorption performance toward the antibiotic Cephalexin. Batch adsorption experiments revealed maximum removal efficiencies of 88.0 ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for AAC and 70.0 ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for BAC at pH 6.3. The adsorption equilibrium was best described by the Langmuir isotherm, which predicted a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of 78.47 ± 2.1 mg g⁻¹, indicating monolayer adsorption. The kinetic data were best fitted by the pseudo-second-order model, suggesting that chemisorption was the predominant adsorption mechanism. Batch adsorption experiments revealed maximum removal efficiency of 88% ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for AAC and 70% ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for BAC at pH = 6.3. The adsorption equilibrium was best described by the Langmuir isotherm, which predicted a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of 78.47 ± 2.1 mg. g -1 , indicating monolayer adsorption. The kinetic data were best fitted by the pseudo-second-order model, suggesting that chemisorption was the predominant adsorption mechanism. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed that the adsorption process is spontaneous and exothermic, with an activation energy of 91.6 kJ.mol -1 , suggesting that chemisorption plays a significant role in the adsorption process. Article.Title: Unlocking high photocatalytic H2 generation and tetracycline eradication over 2D/2D/2D nanocomposite of P-doped g-C3N5/WO3/B4C
Article.Authors: Sareshkeh A.; Rasoulifard M.; Dorraji M.
Article.Abstract: The imperfections of g-C 3 N 5 cause some photocatalytic weaknesses. Herein, we prepared the 2D P-doped g-C 3 N 5 (PCN x ) photocatalysts via one-pot protocol; then, the 2D materials (i.e., Tungsten Oxide (WO 3 ), and Boron Carbide (B 4 C)) coupled to PCN 0.25 , which extended visible-light-adsorption domain, attenuated charge complexation rate, and hastened charge carriers’ transportation rate compared to the pristine g-C 3 N 5 (CN). Thereby, the Tetracycline (TC) elimination increased to ~ 95% through H 2 O 2 -assisted photocatalysis, which evinced the abatement rate of TC enhanced to 578% than the primary photocatalysis. The maturation rate of green gram corroborated that the protocol of PCN 0.25 /35WO 3 /10B 4 C//H 2 O 2 //visible-light alleviated the negative impacts of TC. In addition to these, the presence of Pt and a double S-Scheme electron transfer mechanism synergistically increased the values of the Solar-to-Hydrogen (STH (%)) and the Apparent Quantum Yield (AQY (%)), which fortified the H 2 production rate (13.484 mmol g −1 h − 1 ) over the 2D/2D/2D nano-heterostructure of PCN 0.25 /35WO 3 /10B 4 C. This nanocomposite preserved its photo-sustainability after consecutive cycles. The outcomes could divulge new perspectives for improving the photocatalytic activity of g-C 3 N 5 for producing green fuel and treating wastewater.

Article.Title: Carcass traits and sensory properties of five different strains of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) reared in brackish water ponds
Article.Authors: Moses M.; Chauka L.; Palaiokostas C.; Mtolera M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Five introduced strains of Nile tilapia O. niloticus in Tanzania were evaluated to gain insights regarding their carcass quality and sensory properties and used as basis for setting up a breeding program. One-year-old tilapia strains, identified as BIG NIN, Chitralada, GIFT, ¨Ruvu Farm¨ and Silver YY harvested from brackish water lined ponds with mean live average weight (±standard deviation) of 634.89 ± 107.34, 601.56 ± 144.90, 687.13 ± 161.46, 535.80 ± 123.49 and 466.56 ± 134.01, respectively were used in this experiment. To estimate the carcass traits, fish body offal were removed and then each individual fish was separated into three sections namely; front cut, interior cut and rear cut. The 9-point Hedonic Scale was used to assess the sensory properties of the fish. Overall, the total edible fillet yields (%) were 42.5, 40.2, 40.0, 36.2 and 34.7 for the Chitralada, GIFT, BIG NIN, ¨Ruvu Farm¨ and Silver YY strains, respectively. The higher muscle area was recorded at interior cut, followed by the front cut and the rear cut. The Silver YY, BIG NIN and GIFT scored significantly higher ( p < 0.05 ) than Chitralada in overall acceptability of sensory properties. All of these disparities are likely to be related to each strains breeding and farming history. Therefore, any future breeding design could benefit from the studied traits.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery provides all weather, day and night Earth observation but lacks the spectral richness of optical imagery, which limits interpretability in many applications. The proposed configuration outperformed the evaluated baseline U-Net, transformer-augmented, and diffusion-refined variants in terms of SSIM and PSNR. However, comparisons with literature-reported methods revealed metric-dependent trade-offs, and uniform superiority across all metrics is not claimed. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed local–global–adversarial configuration for SAR-to-optical translation under the reported resource-constrained setting.

Article.Title: ModCon-ARMA for modularity-aware contrastive biomedical graph clustering with uncertainty analysis
Article.Authors: Abburi V.; Shigwan S.; Kumar N.
Article.Abstract: Accurate early diagnosis of biomedical and neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging due to limited labeled data and complex imaging patterns. We introduce ModCon-ARMA , an unsupervised graph learning framework for node clustering that jointly optimizes a Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD)-based contrastive objective and a modularity-based structural loss within a single principled formulation. By modeling subjects as graph nodes and leveraging inter-sample similarities, the method learns structurally meaningful representations without using any diagnostic labels. Extensive experiments on three clinically relevant datasets—Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), BreastMNIST, and PneumoniaMNIST—demonstrate that ModCon-ARMA consistently outperforms existing graph-based and classical clustering baselines in terms of accuracy, recall, and F1 score. Furthermore, Monte Carlo dropout with feature and edge perturbations provides predictive cluster-assignment uncertainty estimates that characterize sensitivity to stochastic model, feature, and graph perturbations. Code is available at github.com/tejaswi-abburi1083/ModCon-ARMA_2026 .

Article.Title: Triglyceride-glucose index and multiple diseases with systemic inflammation as a potential mediator in a phenome-wide association study
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Liu Y.; Han S.; Liu Z.; Yu J.; Wang X.; Ping F.; Xu L.; Li W.; Li Y.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) is associated with metabolic dysregulation and may increase the risk of diseases across multiple systems. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a validated surrogate marker for IR but does not measure IR directly. This study aimed to comprehensively assess the associations of TyG index with a broad spectrum of diseases and explore the potential mediating effects of systemic inflammation. We tested associations between TyG index and incidence of 1,127 diseases in the UK Biobank prospective cohort. Cox proportional hazards models were adjusted for multiple covariates and P values were corrected for multiple comparisons. For diseases showing statistically significant positive associations, mediation analyses were performed to estimate the proportion mediated by the low-grade chronic inflammation (INFLA) score. The study included 361,175 participants (mean age 56.5 years; 53.2% female) with a median follow-up of 13.5 years. The TyG index was significantly associated with an increased risk of 283 distinct diseases (25.1% of those tested, hazard ratios [HRs] up to 4.61), including a subset of positive associations with limited prior evidence. The INFLA score showed statistically significant indirect effects in 76.7% (217/283) of these associations, with 42 demonstrating a mediation proportion exceeding 30%, 136 showing a proportion of 10–30%, and 39 exhibiting a proportion of 0–10%. The targeted sensitivity analysis of anemia and urinary calculus produced directionally consistent estimates under stricter outcome definitions and additional outcome-specific covariate adjustment. The TyG index was positively associated with 283 diseases, and statistically significant indirect effects through the INFLA score were observed for 217 phenotypes, although the estimated mediation proportions were small for many outcomes. These findings suggest that TyG-related metabolic dysregulation may have broad health implications. The analyses were exploratory rather than evidence of an established mechanism.

Article.Title: Benchmarking the reliability of frozen Code LLMs for smart-contract vulnerability decisions
Article.Authors: Le T.; Park J.; Heo S.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Frozen language models can produce plausible smart-contract reports despite generation failures and weak discrimination. We benchmark three approximately 7-billion-parameter models on SmartBugs-Curated, ScrawlD, and balanced BCCC under a fixed prompt family and documented recovery procedures. Across 75,957 model–record outputs, final validity is 100%, but native first-attempt record validity ranges from 3.7% to 85.3%; all three datasets fail a declared recovery-sensitivity criterion. The reported scores are conditional on the evaluated model snapshots, prompt, and recovery protocol rather than estimates of general Code-LLM performance on these benchmarks. The best raw micro-F1 is 0.961 on SmartBugs-Curated and 0.108 on ScrawlD; the best BCCC balanced accuracy is 0.520. We examine the Taxonomy-Aware Calibrated Ensemble (TACE) using nested cross-fitting with prevalence-only and logistic-stacking controls. On ScrawlD, their micro-F1 values are 0.5985, 0.5978, and 0.5986; 80.1% of TACE’s positive decisions occur when all three models predict negative. Source-family-grouped analysis gives qualitatively similar conclusions. Confidence-based abstention can retain mostly negative decisions while discarding almost all true positive alerts. These findings support TACE as an interpretable reliability diagnostic, not evidence of superior semantic detection or model complementarity. The study separates native validity, recovery dependence, prevalence effects, calibration, discrimination, and selective positive-alert utility; prompt robustness and cross-dataset transfer remain untested.

Article.Title: Age- and stage-specific competing mortality after colorectal cancer resection
Article.Authors: Li W.; Xu G.; Sun W.; Zheng M.; Yin F.; Ren B.; Ma W.; Dou X.; Ping Y.; Yao N.; Sun D.
Article.Abstract: Mortality after colorectal cancer (CRC) resection reflects cancer and competing health risks. We analysed 231,248 resected stage I–III adenocarcinomas diagnosed during 2004–2017 in SEER using cumulative-incidence functions, Fine-Gray models and separate survivor landmark cohorts. Exploratory stable crossover times were estimated on a monthly grid with 2,000 bootstrap replicates. In stage I, other-cause mortality predominated within 1–5 months; among patients aged ≥ 90 years, the estimate was 5 months (95% CI, 1–12; n = 1,091). In stage II, crossover occurred at 7.0 years (6.3–7.5) at ages 65–74 and 2.6–2.9 years at ages ≥ 75; no crossover was observed below age 65. No stage III age group crossed within 10 years under recorded cause-of-death classifications. Age-by-stage interactions were significant for both outcomes ( P < 0.001). Among separate 5-year survivor cohorts, subsequent 5-year CRC/other-cause incidences were 4.1%/17.6%, 8.1%/19.6% and 12.8%/13.0% in stages I–III. Cause-of-death reallocation changed some crossover conclusions. These population-level descriptions require external validation and do not define individual treatment or surveillance thresholds.

Article.Title: Neurophysiological correlates of interoceptive compassion training for depression
Article.Authors: Anzolin A.; Ellis S.; Kim E.; Joss D.; Marin F.; Gawande R.; Comeau A.; Bumpus C.; Phillips J.; Cahn B.; Kim M.; Napadow V.; Schuman-Olivier Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depression is often linked to interoceptive dysfunction and self-critical thinking. The Heart-Smile Training-Intensive Introduction Program (HST-IIP) integrates interoceptive attention training with compassion-based practices to support emotional well-being. This pilot study randomized 23 individuals with depression to either HST-IIP or a waitlist control group. Participants completed EEG recordings and clinical assessments before and after a 4-week intervention. The primary outcome was heartbeat-evoked potentials (HEPs), while depression severity was our main clinical outcome, assessed using the Computerized Adaptive Test-Mental Health (CAT-MH). Exploratory outcomes included Delta power spectral density (PSD) during guided meditation, as well as psychological measures of interoceptive awareness (MAIA-2) and self-compassion (SCS). Compared to the control group, participants assigned to HST-IIP showed greater improvements in depression scores (Hedges’ g = –1.422, p = 0.028) and increases in interoceptive awareness. EEG analyses revealed attenuated (less negative) HEP amplitude in right frontal electrodes during attention-focused meditation and reduced Delta power during compassion-focused meditation. Changes in these neural markers were associated with improvements in depression outcomes. This exploratory pilot study provides preliminary evidence that HST-IIP is associated with improvements in depressive symptoms together with changes in HEP and Delta activity. These findings suggest that interoceptive compassion training may influence neurophysiological processes relevant to depression and support further research into interoceptive compassion training as a treatment for depression.

Article.Title: Molecular subtypes of breast cancer in the Aljouf region of Northern Saudi Arabia: insights from a five-year retrospective analysis
Article.Authors: Shalabi M.; Alzahrani B.; Almarshad H.; Nour N.; Sah A.; Ullah M.; Abbas A.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a major cause of cancer morbidity and mortality among women worldwide. Advances in diagnosis have contributed to a substantial burden of breast cancer in the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia. Molecular characterization is crucial for understanding tumor heterogeneity and informing clinical management. This retrospective study aimed to investigate the proportion and epidemiological characteristics of molecular subtypes among BC patients from the northern areas of Saudi Arabia. This retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using breast tissue samples from newly diagnosed cases between January 2020 and December 2024 at regional hospitals in Aljouf, Saudi Arabia. Clinicopathological parameters and molecular subtypes determined by immunohistochemistry were evaluated. Among 874 cancer cases, 212 (24.3%) were diagnosed with breast cancer. The mean age was 54.05 ± 13.3 years, and 50.5% of BC cases occurred in patients aged ≥ 50 years. Female patients accounted for 95.3% of cases, yielding a female-to-male ratio of 20.2:1. Molecular characterization showed that luminal A was the most frequent subtype (50.5%), subsequent subtype was the HER2-positive (26.9%). Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) accounted for 16.0% of cases, whereas luminal B was the least common subtype (6.6%). Molecular subtypes showed significant association with tumor grade, lymphovascular invasion, and distant metastasis ( p < 0.05), but not with histological type. In conclusion, luminal A and the HER2-positive molecular subtype were the most common among BC cases in the northern region of Saudi Arabia. The observed associations between molecular subtypes and clinicopathological characteristics highlight the clinical relevance of subtype-based assessment and support the need for targeted screening strategies.

Article.Title: Enhancing illness communication between patients with stroke and their spouses: a dyadic coping intervention programme
Article.Authors: Lv X.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To develop a dyadic coping intervention program tailored to illness communication between patients with strokes and their spouses, with the aim of enhancing their ability to communicate effectively while coping with the disease together. Following an evidence-based approach, relevant domestic and international literature was reviewed. Guided by the Systemic-Transactional Model, an initial draft of the dyadic coping intervention program was developed through group discussions. The final version of the program was established after two rounds of expert consultations using the Delphi method. A total of 15 experts from two regional medical centres participated in two rounds of consultation, with a 100% response rate for both rounds. The authority coefficient of the experts was 0.933. The coefficient of variation for all items ranged from 0 to 0.116. The Kendall’s coefficient of concordance was 0.299, indicating low to moderate agreement among the experts ( P < 0.001). The finalized intervention program comprised 8 primary indicators, 19 secondary indicators, and 24 tertiary indicators. The dyadic coping intervention program developed in this study was systematically constructed and refined through expert consultation. The final program reflects a moderate level of expert agreement and may provide a structured reference for future clinical practice and empirical evaluation in supporting illness communication among patients with stroke and their spouses.

Article.Title: Quantitative investigation of hybridized plasmonic resonances in graphene-coated nanocylinder chains for multiplexed dual-mode SERS/ SEIRA applications
Article.Authors: Raad S.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the hybridized plasmonic resonances in graphene-coated nanocylinder chains for multiplexed dual-mode surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) sensing applications. To this end, nanocylinder chains with different numbers of elements are numerically analyzed, and it is observed that as the number of elements in the chain increases, the number of intense plasmonic resonances increases under specific plane-wave excitation. The scattering and absorption cross-sections, as well as near-field distributions at the plasmonic resonances, are investigated to ensure the presence of adequate field intensities for single-molecule detection at the multiple hot spots provided by the chains. The spectral features of the resonances are investigated by calculating their linewidth and quality factor. Importantly, the boundary conditions play an essential role in the absorption efficiency, where finite-length nanocylinders are better suited for low-scattering sensing applications in comparison to the infinite-length ones. The multiband optical absorption provided by the proposed device can be passively and actively tuned, respectively, by the geometrical parameters and by employing the two-dimensional nature of graphene material to coincide the multiple observed resonance frequencies with the vibrational modes of the analytes in complex mixtures.

Article.Title: Robust low-light object detection and classification via hybrid feature fusion and synthetic data augmentation
Article.Authors: S K.; Sethi S.; J S G.; Vasudevan A.; Manimaran S.; Raj R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Robust visual navigation in low-light environments remains a fundamental challenge for autonomous systems due to severe illumination degradation, low signal-to-noise ratio, reduced texture information, and loss of discriminative visual cues. These primary conditions significantly impact the reliability of conventional handcrafted descriptors to detect objects on training on well-illuminated datasets through deep learning models. To improve low-light image object detection and classification by overcoming above limitation, we proposed a low-light visual recognition framework that combines image enhancement, complementary handcrafted and pretrained deep feature representations, dimensionality reduction, and synthetic low-light data augmentation. In the pre-processing stage, we had applied Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), followed by gamma correction, to enhance local contrast while preserving structural information. To improve generalization across varying illumination levels, a pseudo low-light image synthesis pipeline was introduced, combining gamma-based exposure reduction, Poisson photon noise modeling, and intensity bias simulation. The resulting pseudo low-light images provide realistic illumination degradations for data augmentation. Feature extraction was done using Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), which captures local edge and gradient structures that are comparatively robust to intensity variations, followed by deep convolutional embeddings that provide high-level semantic representations. For image classification, HOG descriptors and pre-trained features of ResNet-18 model was evaluated both individually and as a fused representation with PCA-based dimensionality reduction, using Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers. Separately, for object detection, synthetic low-light images generated from COCO images were used to augment ExDark training images, and their effect is evaluated with YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 object detection models. Extensive experiments were performed on the ExDark benchmark dataset to evaluate the proposed hybrid feature fusion strategy in terms of feature discriminability, detection accuracy, recall, and robustness across varying illumination conditions, in comparison with conventional handcrafted and deep feature baselines. The results show that complementary feature representations and synthetic low-light augmentation improve classification and detection performance under challenging low-light conditions, supporting improved robustness to illumination variation of low-light images.

Article.Authors: Li W.; Shi J.; Mo X.; Xu S.
Article.Abstract: Anti-carbamylated protein (anti-CarP) antibodies are part of the anti-modified protein antibody repertoire in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but their relationship with systemic inflammatory burden and osteoporosis (OP) remains insufficiently defined. This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated the complementary serological value of anti-CarP antibodies and their associations with systemic inflammation, osteoarticular damage, and OP in RA. A total of 182 patients with RA and 100 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were included. Serum anti-CarP antibodies were measured by ELISA. Associations with conventional autoantibodies, inflammatory markers, disease activity indices, radiographic damage, bone mineral density and OP were evaluated using non-parametric tests, correlation analyses and multivariable regression models. Nested logistic models assessed the incremental value of anti-CarP for OP-associated model performance. Anti-CarP levels were higher in RA patients than in controls ( P < 0.0001), with positivity rates of 41.2% and 4.0%, respectively. Anti-CarP correlated more strongly with RF than with anti-CCP antibodies and was detected in 12.5% of double-seronegative RA patients. After multivariable adjustment, anti-CarP remained significantly associated with ESR, CRP, and OP, but not with structural joint damage. Adding anti-CarP significantly improved model fit, but the improvement in overall discrimination was minimal. Anti-CarP antibody concentrations remained associated with systemic inflammatory markers and OP after multivariable adjustment in this Chinese RA cohort. These findings suggest that anti-CarP antibodies may provide complementary serological information regarding inflammatory and skeletal manifestations of RA. However, given the cross-sectional design, these associations do not establish causality or the ability of anti-CarP to predict future outcomes. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and prognostic significance of these associations and their potential clinical applications.

Article.Title: Contactless radar-based ECG waveform estimation with morphology-​ and spectral-aware learning
Article.Authors: Babu G.; Sharma L.
Article.Abstract: Electrode-based electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical standard for cardiac monitoring, but it is not practical for long-term unobtrusive use. Contactless radar sensing can capture chest-wall micromotions; however, ECG waveform estimation from radar in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) signals remains an inherently challenging problem due to noise, motion interference, and the lack of direct electrical measurements. This paper proposes a morphology and spectral aware learning framework for ECG waveform estimation from contactless radar signals. The approach aims to improve the preservation of ECG morphological characteristics, particularly QRS-related features, as well as spectral components, using a composite loss that combines time-domain reconstruction, short-time spectral alignment, band-limited energy constraints, and temporal smoothness. We evaluate the method on a publicly available radar-ECG benchmark dataset with 30 subjects across multiple physiological scenarios, including resting, valsalva, apnea, tiltup, and tiltdown. In the resting scenario, the method achieves high spectral correlation (0.9864 ± 0.0084) and R-peak detection F1 score (0.9826 ± 0.0100), indicating effective preservation of spectral and event based characteristics. Under more challenging conditions, such as motion and low-amplitude scenarios (apnea), performance decreases; however, the framework still partially preserves waveform morphology and temporal structure while maintaining R-peak detection and temporal alignment. Performance under cross-subject evaluation was substantially lower than in the within-subject evaluation, highlighting the challenges of generalizing radar-to-ECG waveform estimation across unseen individuals. Overall, the results suggest that the morphology and spectral aware method shows promise for consistent ECG waveform estimation from contactless radar signals.

Article.Title: Thermoelastic dynamics with memory: A $$\psi$$–Atangana–Baleanu fractional model and its semi-analytical solution by the homotopy perturbation method
Article.Authors: Zidan A.; Ahmed S.; Salameh W.; Sanaee H.; Iqbal N.
Article.Abstract: We formulate a one-dimensional nonlinear coupled thermoelastic model in which the inertia of the displacement u and the heat capacity of the temperature \(\theta\) carry hereditary memory described by \(\psi\) -Atangana–Baleanu (AB) operators with a nonsingular Mittag–Leffler kernel. The displacement equation has order \(\alpha \in (1,2]\) , the temperature equation has order \(\beta \in (0,1]\) , and the scale function \(\psi\) acts as an intrinsic material clock. The novelty is threefold. (i) We give a consistent \(\psi\) -framework, in which all time derivatives are taken with respect to \(\psi\) , together with the exact inversion formulas, the compatibility conditions and the initial layer that are specific to the AB kernel. (ii) We derive a transform-free \(\psi\) -AB homotopy perturbation method (HPM) and prove an explicit convergence criterion: the series converges when the spectral radius of an “instantaneous” operator, proportional to \((1-\beta )/B(\beta )\) and \((2-\alpha )/B(\alpha -1)\) , is below one, and it generically diverges otherwise. We also prove convergence to the classical model as \(\alpha \rightarrow 2\) , \(\beta \rightarrow 1\) . (iii) We validate the method against exact fractional solutions, fixed-point residuals and an independent time-stepping solver. The method is applied to four problems, including an unforced thermal-grating problem with no known solution, for which a Laplace-domain modal analysis quantifies how \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) change the frequency and attenuation of the thermoelastic mode. A comparison with the Caputo model and with a non-trivial scale function shows where the AB kernel differs from the power-law kernel.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of antioxidant, antibacterial activity of methanol solvent extract and ZnO nanoparticle synthesized using Hydrolea zeylanica (L.) Vahl
Article.Authors: Roy M.; Boruah N.; Nath M.; Kakati K.; Rongphar A.; Roy D.; Sharma R.; Bhattarai S.; Borbora D.; Nath N.; DasMahapatra S.
Article.Abstract: In the present study, the whole plant of Hydrolea zeylanica was used to prepare a crude methanolic extract, which was then used as a bioactive capping agent for the synthesis of nanoparticles using zinc oxide metal ions. Formation of nanoparticles was confirmed using an UV–Vis spectrophotometer at the absorption peak of 320 nm, FESEM revealed the nanoparticles form aggregation after long storage; EDX confirmed ZnO elemental composition of the nanoparticles, XRD analysis revealed hexagonal crystalline nanoparticles with size 35.4 nm ±17.31, DLS analysis showed single peak at 420.6 nm with PDI 0.384 and FT-IR data revealed presence of functional groups like phenols and flavonoids. After characterisation, the bioactivity of both the methanolic extract and nanoparticle sample was evaluated for comparative bioactivity assessment using DPPH and H 2 O 2 free radical scavenging tests in vitro. The DPPH test revealed IC50 value of 86.11 mg/mL for the methanolic extract and 29.34 mg/mL for the ZnO nanoparticle solution and 80.07 mg/mL for the plant extract. The antibacterial assessment was performed against two bacterial strains, Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus and the nanoparticle solution showed better activity in both disc diffusion and MIC tests. A viable colony count assay has also been performed to determine the antibacterial efficiency of the nanoparticles. Overall, the results show that nanoparticle synthesis is an effective way to enhance the bioactivity potential of the plant’s natural metabolites compared with raw plant extracts.

Article.Title: A leakage-controlled multimodal framework for depression detection using audio, visual, and text features
Article.Authors: Kallem M.; Aluvala S.; Singh P.
Article.Abstract: Depression is one of the most prevalent mental health disorders that can be addressed using objective computational screening that may be used in conjunction with clinical screening, but should not be used to replace it. The present research proposes a clear multimodal approach combining the acoustic, visual and textual behavioural data of a structured interview. The speech is represented by Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients and COVAREP descriptors, the facial behaviour is represented by constrained local neural fields landmarks and the semantics of the text is represented by BERT embeddings. The standardized training-fold statistics, the fixed weighted feature-level concatenation, the principal component analysis and the L2-regularized Logistic Regression are used to standardize, concatenate, reduce and classify modality specific features. The accuracy when evaluated on the DAIC-WOZ corpus, using a participant-independent, stratified five-fold cross validation was 91.2%, macro-precision 88.5%, macro-recall 90.7%, macro-F1 score 89.5%, specificity 91.7%, depressed-class sensitivity 89.7%, and ROC AUC 0.94. Improvements of unimodal and multimodal representations were found in the ablation analysis, with text proving the most effective representation, and acoustic and facial features adding complementary improvements in the multimodal context. The framework focuses on the aspects of methodological transparency, training-fold leakage control and low-parameter classifiers. External validation must be done prior to clinical use.

Article.Title: Short term effects of ambient air pollution exposure on influenza: a multi-city study in Shandong, China
Article.Authors: Su M.; Wu J.; Sun L.; He Q.; Zhang R.; Su W.; Duan Q.; He Y.; Zhang S.; Li W.; Liu T.; Xing W.
Article.Abstract: Ambient air pollution is a recognized risk factor for influenza-like illness (ILI). However, it remains unclear how city-specific characteristics modify these associations. This study evaluated the short-term associations between six major air pollutants and ILI incidence in Shandong Province, China, and investigated the modifying effects of seasonal, spatial, and socioeconomic factors. Daily air pollutant concentrations and ILI surveillance data from 16 cities in Shandong Province (2015–2019) were analyzed using a two-stage approach. City-specific associations were estimated using quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), followed by a multivariate random-effects meta-analysis to calculate pooled cumulative relative risks (CRRs). Meta-regression and stratified analyses were used to assess effect modification by demographic, geographic, and macroeconomic indicators. A total of 2,145,543 ILI cases were included. Except for O 3 , short-term exposure to all evaluated air pollutants was significantly associated with increased ILI incidence. NO 2 (CRR: 1.041, 95% CI: 1.031–1.052) and SO 2 (CRR: 1.040, 95% CI: 1.023–1.058) exhibited the strongest positive associations, whereas O 3 was inversely associated with ILI. The risks were higher in children aged 5–14 years, during transition seasons (spring and autumn), and in coastal areas. Meta-regression indicated that higher gross domestic product and healthcare resource density mitigated the adverse impacts of particulate matter and carbon monoxide, whereas basin. Basin topography exacerbated pollution-induced ILI risks during severe pollution episodes. Short-term exposure to major air pollutants increases ILI risk, but the magnitude of this risk is significantly modified by city-level socioeconomic and geographic characteristics. These findings highlight the need to develop localized, resource-adjusted air quality early warning systems to protect vulnerable populations.

Article.Title: Heterogeneous genetic sharing between inflammatory bowel disease and allergic phenotypes: genome-wide and targeted regional analyses
Article.Authors: Yin H.; Cao H.; Guo Y.; Wang Y.; Han L.; Liu Q.; Yu X.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and allergic diseases share genetic liability, but subtype and regional patterns remain uncertain. We analysed European-ancestry summary statistics for Crohn’s disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), combined IBD, and four allergic phenotypes using genetic correlation, Mendelian randomization (MR), Causal Analysis Using Summary Effect estimates (CAUSE), targeted colocalization, fine-mapping, and gene and functional follow-up; UK Biobank analyses served as cross-dataset consistency checks. Genetic sharing was detected more consistently for CD than for UC, without a formal subtype difference. Reference inverse-variance-weighted MR associations of genetically predicted CD log odds with atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and allergic conjunctivitis passed within-family false-discovery-rate correction; CD–asthma did not, whereas secondary discovery-only combined-IBD associations passed correction for all four outcomes. Three CAUSE comparisons had nominal model-comparison P values, but none survived within-family correction. Regional architectures were heterogeneous: targeted 5q31 CD–asthma colocalization support was high but specification dependent; 2q12 remained unresolved, and 17q12–21 supported distinct IBD and asthma signals. Regulatory and functional follow-up did not establish a stable target-specific mechanism, and SLC22A5 remained a 5q31 regional candidate. Resolving these signals requires ancestry- and linkage-disequilibrium (LD)-matched fine-mapping with estimable regulatory data and direct perturbation in disease-relevant models.

Article.Title: Deep learning-based computer-aided detection of cerebral microbleeds achieves high sensitivity with a low false-positive rate in a confirmatory clinical trial
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Lee E.; Yoon J.; Yeo I.; Lee J.; Lee M.; Jo S.; Song D.; Jang H.; Kim D.; Lee K.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are small, focal brain lesions recognized as critical biomarkers of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive decline. Despite advances in MRI technology, detecting CMBs remains challenging, highlighting the need for automated tools. This study aimed to evaluate the standalone performance of Neurophet SCALE MRI for automated CMB detection. The model was trained on 201 SWI and phase examinations. Neurophet SCALE MRI employs a two-stage deep learning pipeline with preprocessing steps, including reorientation, resampling, and data augmentation. In the first stage, CMB candidates are generated using a multiscale backbone and bidirectional convolutional Long Short-Term Memory. The second stage reduces false positives through a Squeeze-and-Excitation ResNet-based classifier and brain tissue segmentation. In this retrospective, single-center clinical trial, the model was tested on 457 MRI examinations. The primary endpoints were lesion-wise sensitivity (> 85.7%) and false positive rate (< 2.35 per patient). In addition, patient-wise and group-wise analyses were conducted. A total of 456 participants (224 CMB-positive, 232 CMB-negative) with 515 CMB lesions were included for the statistical analysis. The device exceeded all predefined performance criteria, demonstrating a lesion-wise sensitivity of 88.35% (95% CI: 86.61–90.17) and a false positive rate of 0.95 per patient (95% CI: 0.83–1.07). Patient-wise sensitivity and specificity were 1.0 (95% CI: 0.98–1.0) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.81–0.90), respectively. For group-wise classification (0–4 vs. ≥5 CMBs), sensitivity and specificity were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.88–0.93) and 0.95 (95% CI: 0.74–1.0). Neurophet SCALE MRI demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity along with a low false-positive rate, supporting its potential clinical utility. Further validation by expert readers in a broader population is warranted.

Article.Title: Design and analysis of a CPW-Fed truncated patch MIMO Antenna for Wi-Fi applications
Article.Authors: Begum M.; Yuvaraj T.; Krishnamoorthy R.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes the design and evaluation of a compact coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed multi-band MIMO antenna specifically optimized for contemporary Wi-Fi applications, encompassing IEEE 802.11b/g/n as well as the latest Wi-Fi 6 and 6E (802.11ax) standards. The proposed antenna comprises a CPW-fed circular patch radiator with a strategically embedded truncation to enable multi-band operation. The design evolution—from a basic circular patch with truncation configuration—demonstrates how resonant modes in the 2.4 GHz, 5–7.1 GHz bands are efficiently excited within a compact planar footprint. The final single-element antenna achieves effective impedance matching across the target bands with reflection coefficients better than − 10 dB, making it suitable for integration in compact wireless systems. A four-port MIMO configuration is realized by optimizing element placement and incorporating spatial and polarization diversity to ensure low mutual coupling (< − 20 dB) and high isolation. The proposed antenna achieves high diversity gain (> 9.9 dB) and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC < 0.005), confirming its suitability for robust multi-band MIMO performance. Simulated and measured results validate that the design meets the requirements for next-generation Wi-Fi communication systems in terms of bandwidth, compactness, isolation, and diversity performance.

Article.Title: Long-term trends and COVID-19 pandemic–era changes in the incidence of cancers with established screening strategies in the United States: a population-based SEER study
Article.Authors: Mali B.; Mali A.; Mali A.; Abdulrazzak M.; Jobran A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer screening and prevention constitute essential components of cancer control, although their influence on population-level incidence varies across cancer types and is shaped by patterns of healthcare access and utilization. Large-scale public health emergencies can disrupt the delivery of routine preventive, diagnostic, and oncologic services. The present study examines long-term incidence trends and evaluates changes in cancer incidence patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data were sourced from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) 21 registries database. Age-adjusted incidence rates for lung and bronchus, colon and rectum, breast, and cervix uteri cancers among adults aged 40 years and older were analyzed separately from 2000 to 2022. Joinpoint regression analysis was conducted to assess long-term incidence trends. Pre-pandemic trends from 2000 to 2019 were extrapolated to estimate expected incidence rates for 2020–2022, which were compared with observed rates. Long-term incidence declined significantly for lung and bronchus (AAPC, − 1.81%), colorectal (AAPC, − 1.94%), and cervical cancers (AAPC, − 1.48%) from 2000 to 2022, whereas breast cancer incidence showed no significant overall change (AAPC, − 0.32%). Descriptive subgroup analyses demonstrated heterogeneous patterns across age, sex, race/ethnicity, and stage. Stage distribution among diagnosed cases showed only modest year-to-year variation across the four cancer sites. Over the past two decades, lung and bronchus, colorectal, and cervical cancer incidence declined, whereas breast cancer incidence remained relatively stable among adults aged ≥ 40 years. During 2020–2022, observed incidence rates for several cancer types deviated from those expected based on pre-pandemic trends, with the largest reductions generally observed in 2020 and variable patterns thereafter. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining accessible and resilient cancer screening and diagnostic services during future public health emergencies to minimize potential disruptions in timely cancer detection and care.

Article.Title: A novel three stage passive particle swarm optimization algorithm for the p-median problem
Article.Authors: An M.; Xiang W.; Lu Y.; Zhu W.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: The p-median problem (PMP) is a classical NP-hard problem in location science. To solve it, many methods have been developed, including a novel discrete particle swarm optimization (NDPSO). To further improve comprehensive performance of NDPSO, a novel three stage passive particle swarm optimization algorithm (TSPPSO for short) is proposed. In TSPPSO, first, an integer encoding scheme and random particle generation method are employed to form swarm particles. Second, a three-stage evolution strategy with single point crossover, single point mutation and a dynamic probability mechanism is developed. Third, a passive strategy for passive particles is also integrated into TSPPSO. To validate its effectiveness and advantage, a lot of experiments on 40 PMP instances are carried out. Related experimental results including comparisons with eight representative methods demonstrate the performance, simplicity, superiority and robustness of TSPPSO.

Article.Title: An integrated machining performance framework considering tool wear and hole integrity attributes during drilling via indexable drilling inserts using entropy-weights and TOPSIS
Article.Authors: Ijaz M.; Afzal M.; Ishtiaq S.; Khan S.; Farooq M.; Anwar S.
Article.Abstract: Quantification of machinability is challenging, especially with the development of new materials like DC 53 steel and new tooling, such as the fabrication of indexable inserts. In this context, an integrated machining performance framework named the Integrated Hole Integrity Index (IHII) is proposed. An indexable drilling setup with peripheral wiper inserts and central stepped carbide inserts was employed. The drilling tests were conducted at 20 m/min and 30 m/min cutting speeds while employing feed rates of 0.05 mm/rev, 0.075 mm/rev, and 0.10 mm/rev to assess the effect of microstructure on tool wear, surface integrity, diametric error, machining temperature, and burr formation. The microstructural examination revealed that D2 steel contained large carbides that were not evenly distributed, but DC53 steel displayed a martensitic structure with small carbides that were evenly spaced. The D2 steel performed better than DC53 steel such that the minimum flank wear value of 49 μm was recorded when drilling the former material at 20 m/min and 0.05 mm/rev, with surface roughness values being in the range of 1.0–4.8 μm. However, tool wear was almost in the same vicinity, but roughness values were substantially higher, ranging from 1.9 to 5.4 μm with the latter material at the same machining parameters. The SEM analysis revealed that surface damage occurred through three main mechanisms, which included adhesion, material side flow, and plastic deformation. For a more holistic drilling performance assessment, an IHII model/performance metric is calculated using entropy weights and subsequently TOPSIS analysis was conducted to overcome the limitations of individual output responses. Hereafter, the best drilling condition is suggested, which indicates the best compromise among all output responses. A value of 0.743 for IHII was calculated for Test 4, performed on D2 material, showing a better performance index, while a 23% lower IHII was determined for DC53 steel.

Article.Title: GKB202 suppresses malignant phenotypes of circulating tumor cells in non-small cell lung cancer by modulating adaptive oxidative stress responses
Article.Authors: Hu Y.; Li T.; Chen Y.; Lin T.; Chen C.; Lu L.; Chou R.
Article.Abstract: Antrodia cinnamomea is a Taiwan-endemic medicinal fungus with reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) contribute to metastasis and therapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study investigated whether stress-adaptive programs supporting CTC survival can be pharmacologically disrupted by GKB202, a purified derivative of A. cinnamomea . Patient-derived NSCLC CTCs were isolated and treated with GKB202 followed by RNA sequencing. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, and rank-rank hypergeometric overlap (RRHO) analyses were performed using a public NSCLC bone metastasis dataset (GSE175601). Functional assays in A549 cells assessed proliferation, migration, and invasion. MT1E protein expression was examined by Western blotting, and metabolomic profiling was conducted using UPLC-QTOF/MS. Untreated CTCs showed enrichment of migration- and lipid metabolism-related programs, whereas GKB202 treatment was associated with enrichment of stress-adaptive and detoxification pathways. Metallothionein-1E (MT1E) expression increased following GKB202 treatment. GKB202 reduced CTC viability and its combination with cisplatin produced a greater reduction in viability than either treatment alone in patient-derived CTC cultures. In A549 cells, GKB202 reduced proliferation and migration, accompanied with time-dependent changes in MT1E protein expression. Exploratory metabolomic profiling showed alterations in lipid-associated metabolic pathways consistent with stress-responsive regulation. These findings suggest that GKB202 is associated with changes in stress-adaptive molecular and metabolic programs in NSCLC models, together with reductions in selected malignant phenotypes and modulation of MT1E-associated responses. By potentially modulating compensatory stress responses in CTCs, GKB202 may increase their vulnerability to therapeutic stress, a possibility that warrants further investigation in the context of CTC-associated metastatic progression in NSCLC.

Article.Title: Incidence and determinants of malaria recurrence in Andabiet district, Northwest Ethiopia: implications for malaria elimination
Article.Authors: Abate A.; Yirsaw B.; Abebe D.; Gedamu H.; Demssie T.; Angaw D.
Article.Abstract: Malaria remains a significant public health burden, with recurrent infections posing challenges for control and elimination efforts. Evidence on the incidence and determinants of malaria recurrence in Ethiopia is limited. This study assessed the incidence of malaria recurrence and its contributing factors among patients in the Andabiet district, Northwest Ethiopia. A retrospective follow-up study was conducted among 649 malaria patients treated in public health facilities between July 2022 and June 2023. A two-stage sampling technique was used to select patients to be interviewed using systematic random sampling. Data were collected through pretested and structured questionnaires and analyzed using the Weibull regression model to determine recurrence predictors. Survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier curves, and significance was set at p-value < 0.05. The overall incidence rate of malaria recurrence was 1.79 per 1,000 person-days. The median time to recurrence was 239 days. Key predictors of recurrence included male sex (AHR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.04–2.95), larger family size (AHR = 1.76, 95% CI = 1.10–2.79), delayed diagnosis and treatment (AHR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.32–0.71), lack of primaquine treatment (AHR = 3.91, 95% CI = 2.66–5.76), poor medication adherence (AHR = 0.52, 95% CI = 0.34–0.80), and not sleeping under insecticide-treated nets (AHR = 0.55, 95% CI = 0.37–0.82). The high incidence of malaria recurrence highlights the need for enhanced interventions, including timely diagnosis, adherence to treatment protocols, and proper utilization of bed nets. Strengthening these measures is crucial to reduce recurrence rates and advance malaria elimination goals in Ethiopia.

Article.Title: Environmental and innovation outcomes following China’s Zero-Waste City program
Article.Authors: Niu L.; Wu Q.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract China’s Zero-Waste City (ZWC) program bundles source reduction, resource utilization, controlled disposal, hazardous-waste compliance and public disclosure in a city-level solid-waste governance framework. Using a balanced panel of 297 prefecture-level cities from 2005 to 2023 and a corrected designation map, we estimate two-way fixed-effects, cohort-specific, and group-time difference-in-differences models. The baseline ln(PM 2.5) is -0.012 and statistically indistinguishable from zero in all specifications with year effects. Baseline associations for industrial ln(CO 2 ), ln(SO 2) and the municipal harmless-treatment rate lose significance under province-by-year effects, pretreatment covariate by year controls, or city-specific trends. The coefficients of ln(invention-patent) grants is significantly higher than ln(utility-model) grants. But this contrast is fragile that the invention estimate is concentrated in the 11 cities designated in 2019, whose pre-designation test is borderline, and a group-time DID gives an aggregated invention ATT of 0.026. Invention applications do not increase and science spending does not change. Industrial solid-waste utilization and broad city science and technology spending outcomes are also null. Because city-level waste-source effects are likely masked by the broader atmospheric setting, these null estimates do not imply policy ineffectiveness. The results might be interpreted as a provisional difference in observed patent-grant composition across patent types.

Article.Title: Social jetlag, sleep duration and clinically significant fatigue among Chinese college students from health-related majors
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Luo J.; Lin S.
Article.Abstract: Evidence on the relationship between social jetlag (SJL) and fatigue is limited among college students from health-related majors. This study aimed to examine the association between SJL and clinically significant fatigue among Chinese college students from health-related majors and assess the extent to which sleep duration mediates this association. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1764 Chinese college students from 10 health-related majors. Fatigue was assessed using the shortened fatigue questionnaire, with scores ≥ 18 indicating clinically significant fatigue. SJL was calculated as the absolute difference between mid-sleep on weekdays and weekends. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline were used to assess the relationship between SJL and fatigue. Mediation analysis was used to explore the potential mediating role of sleep duration. Among participants, 8.3% met criteria for clinically significant fatigue. A non-linear association between SJL and fatigue was observed, with odds of fatigue increasing sharply when SJL exceeded 1.1 h. In the fully adjusted model, participants with higher SJL (≥ 1.1 h) had elevated odds of fatigue (OR = 1.51, 95%CI: 1.05–2.17). Similar results were found using literature-based SJL categories, with the highest risk in those with SJL > 2 h (OR = 2.01, 95%CI: 1.24–3.27). Subgroup analyses showed that elevated SJL was associated with higher odds of fatigue among females and freshmen, although no significant interactions were observed between SJL and sex or academic grade. Exploratory mediation analysis suggested that sleep duration may partially account for the observed association between SJL and fatigue ( -18.1% of the total effect). Higher SJL was associated with greater odds of clinically significant fatigue among Chinese college students from health-related majors. Sleep duration may play a potential mediating role in this association. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationships and underlying mechanisms.

Article.Title: Distributed $$H_\infty $$ leader–following control of nonlinear heterogeneous multi-agent systems via an alternating LMI iterative approach
Article.Authors: Xu L.; Zhang X.; Zhang H.; Ye F.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates distributed $$H_{\infty }$$ leader–following control for nonlinear heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMASs) subject to external disturbances. A compact tracking-error model is formulated by introducing a lumped nonlinear mismatch term, and a detailed derivation of this term is provided to clarify the components induced by heterogeneity and nonlinearity. Sufficient conditions for stability and prescribed $$H_{\infty }$$ disturbance attenuation are derived via Lyapunov stability theory and a structured weighted quadratic constraint on the mismatch. For controller synthesis, a bilinear matrix inequality (BMI) condition is established, and a verification-based alternating linear matrix inequality (LMI) iterative approach is proposed to address it, together with an analysis of its relation to the original BMI problem and of the initialization sensitivity. Numerical examples, including a nonlinear HMAS and a leader–following unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) network, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Article.Title: Association between ultrasonographic diaphragm thickness and pulmonary function in children with pectus excavatum
Article.Authors: Karakullukcuoglu Z.; Oke D.; Gulec M.; Ozkan C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between ultrasonographic diaphragm thickness and pulmonary function in children with pectus excavatum compared with healthy controls. In this prospective study, 32 children with pectus excavatum and 29 healthy controls were included. Diaphragm thickness was measured ultrasonographically at functional residual capacity (FRC) and total lung capacity (TLC). Spirometry assessed forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV 1 ), and FEV 1 /FVC ratio. Correlations between diaphragm thickness and spirometric parameters were analyzed using Pearson’s test, with significance set at p < 0.05. In the pectus group, inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive correlation with FVC % predicted ( r = 0.421, p = 0.016), while no correlation in the controls ( r = 0.070, p = 0.719). In the pectus group, inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive correlation with FEV 1 % predicted ( r = 0.421, p = 0.016), whereas no significant correlation between these parameters was observed in controls ( r = 0.070, p = 0.719). Mean expiratory thickness at FRC was 1.60 ± 0.38 mm versus 1.64 ± 0.47 mm, respectively ( p = 0.709). Regarding spirometric values, mean FVC % predicted was 82.62 ± 9.00 vs. 87.10 ± 10.58 ( p = 0.079), mean FEV 1 % predicted was 83.31 ± 11.16 vs. 88.72 ± 11.64 ( p = 0.069), and mean FEV 1 /FVC ratio was 88.28 ± 8.52 versus 91.34 ± 6.42, respectively ( p = 0.121). Inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive association with FEV 1 % predicted in children with pectus excavatum. Given the cross-sectional design, small sample size, and multiple exploratory comparisons, this finding requires confirmation in larger studies. Article.Title: Risk-aware hybrid reinforcement learning and robust optimization for reliable PV-battery scheduling under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Ahmed B.; Hagh M.; Hosseini S.
Article.Abstract: High photovoltaic penetration makes residential battery scheduling sensitive to forecast error, tail cost, and model mismatch. This work present a closed-loop interface linking chronological residual-based conformal intervals, cardinality-budgeted receding robust dispatch, distributional cost critics in Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), an uncertainty- and margin-aware fusion/fallback rule, and final safety projection. Evaluation uses chronological household demand from the UCI Individual Household Electric Power Consumption dataset and NASA POWER hourly irradiance and ambient temperature. The processed series is split without shuffling into 23,544 training, 5040 validation/calibration, and 5066 test hours. The final benchmark uses 80 non-overlapping internally contiguous 24-h reserve episodes per method and scenario, with 12 controllers; learned policies are trained independently with seeds 11, 29, and 47 under a common maximum 15,000-step budget with validation early stopping, while the primary five-scenario tables use seed 11. On the executed case study, Proposed obtains the lowest observed mean cost and risk-adjusted CVaR90 in all five scenarios. Nominal mean cost is EUR 2.8058/day and both economic and risk-adjusted CVaR90 are EUR 8.0981. No physical SOC event is observed for Proposed in 1920 audited nominal decisions (0/1920; one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound 0.1559%), although 39.2188% boundary exposure and zero minimum margin show that this is feasible boundary operation rather than a perfect-safety guarantee. Validation selects the robust-action endpoint w = 1.0 for all three seeds, so the final gain is not attributed to active SAC/RO mixing and the conclusions are restricted to the stated data, reserve, seeds, tariff, and perturbations.

Article.Title: Causal admissibility of earthquake triggering laws
Article.Authors: D’Alessandro A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Statistical earthquake-triggering models allow previous events to influence later seismicity immediately across space, satisfying temporal ordering but not finite-speed physical reachability. Here I show that causal admissibility can be imposed by restricting triggering probability to the domain reached after the earliest permitted arrival from a point source or evolving finite rupture, and define causal leakage as the excluded pre-arrival probability. Dimensionless analysis identifies the propagation-to-triggering timescale ratio and the temporal and spatial kernel exponents as its controls. Synthetic experiments show that timing uncertainty can erase the distance–time dependence distinguishing retarded from instantaneous formulations and induce compensating parameter bias. In the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence, causal leakage is $$2.31 \times 10^{ - 5}$$ and enforcement produces negligible predictive change. Across four selected Southern California earthquake families, predictive gains vary in sign without exhibiting a consistent monotonic relationship with leakage magnitude. Physical admissibility and predictive superiority are therefore distinct model properties.

Extraction of selected compounds was quantified by HPLC after 1, 2, 4, 8, and 20 weeks in 75% ethanol/water. These findings show marked material-dependent variation in both outcomes and indicate that conventional and bulk-fill classification alone does not predict compressive-property changes after prolonged saline storage.
