Article.Title: Biological sex influences the biodistribution and absorbed dose of 131I (iodide) in mice
Article.Authors: Elvborn M.; Ytterbrink C.; Shubbar E.; Spetz J.; Langen B.; Forssell-Aronsson E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biological sex can influence radiation response, but sex is rarely considered in biodistribution studies of radionuclides. 131 I is used clinically and may be released at nuclear accidents. The aim was to investigate differences in biodistribution and dosimetry of 131 I (iodide) between male and female mice. C57BL/6N mice received 170 kBq 131 I i.v. and separate groups were euthanised at seven time points from 1 h to 7 days after administration. 131 I concentration was determined in various collected organs and tissues, and mean absorbed dose per injected activity, D/A inj , was calculated. Results showed higher 131 I concentration and D/A inj in most organs in females than males except for kidneys, where males received fourfold higher D/A inj after 7 days (120 versus 31 mGy/MBq). The D/A inj in most organs in females was about up to approximately twofold higher than in males, while thyroid D/A inj was also higher in females, at 180,000 versus 140,000 mGy/MBq. In conclusion, sex-related differences in 131 I biodistribution between males and females were found in all investigated tissues at one or more time points, but the magnitude and timing of these differences varied between tissues. These findings support consideration of biological sex as a variable in preclinical biodistribution and dosimetry studies of radionuclides.

Article.Title: An empirical study on factors influencing digital technology adoption among primary and secondary school physical education teachers
Article.Authors: Ouyang J.; Li L.; Ren Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the acceleration of educational digital transformation, the adoption of digital technologies by primary and secondary school physical education teachers has become crucial to improving teaching effectiveness. Existing research has focused predominantly on general academic subjects, while in the field of physical education—characterised by embodied practice and dynamic interaction—there has been insufficient in-depth analysis of the mechanisms through which multiple factors operate synergistically. Drawing on the UTAUT model and incorporating Digital Technology Proficiency(DTP))as a moderating variable, this study employs a mixed-method approach combining Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling(PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to systematically investigate the key determinants and configurational pathways of digital technology adoption among primary and secondary school physical education teachers.The findings show that performance expectancy(PerfE༉, effort expectancy༈EE༉, social influence༈SI༉ and facilitating conditions(FC)all significantly and positively predict teachers’ Willingness for Digital Physical Education Teaching (WDPET) and enhance their Digital Physical Education Teaching Competenc (DPETC). DTP significantly strengthens only the pathways from performance expectancy and community influence to willingness. fsQCA identifies several equivalent configurational pathways leading to high willingness and high competence. By innovatively integrating net-effect analysis with configurational analysis, this study moves beyond a single linear perspective, confirms the applicability of UTAUT in physical education, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for the digital transformation of physical education.Accordingly, education authorities should promote the balanced allocation of digital infrastructure across urban and rural areas and establish assessment standards for physical education teachers’ digital literacy. At the school level, efforts should be made to foster a culture of mutual support in digital teaching research, improve equipment maintenance and management, and implement differentiated and category-specific teacher training, thereby creating a transformation framework in which policy guidance and school-level implementation advance in coordination. Teacher-training institutions should provide targeted, differentiated training based on authentic physical education classroom scenarios. Through multi-stakeholder collaboration, the application of digital technologies by physical education teachers can become more professional and more deeply integrated with subject-specific teaching practice.

Article.Title: Psychotropic medication-induced movement disorders among patients with mental illness on regular follow-up in northwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Fasil B.; Kelebie M.; Fanta B.; Shumet S.; Demelash D.; Getnet M.; Shitie A.; Yiglet Z.
Article.Abstract: Psychotropic medication-induced movement disorders represent an important clinical burden in psychiatric treatment. These adverse effects are associated with significant patient burden, including subjective distress, stigma, reduced medication adherence, and impaired quality of life, yet they remain under-recognized and frequently overlooked in routine clinical practice. They may occur with both first- and second-generation antipsychotics and other psychotropic medications. However, evidence on their prevalence and associated factors remains limited, particularly in low-resource settings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of psychotropic medication-induced movement disorders and their associated factors among patients receiving regular psychiatric follow-up care. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted from October 1 to November 30, 2025, among patients receiving regular psychiatric follow-up at the University of Gondar Hospital. Study participants were selected using a systematic random sampling technique. Psychotropic medication-induced movement disorders were assessed using the Extrapyramidal Symptom Rating Scale (ESRS). Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Bivariable logistic regression analysis was initially performed, and variables with a p -value ≤ 0.25 were entered into the multivariable logistic regression model. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and statistical significance was declared at a two-sided p -value < 0.05. The prevalence of psychotropic medication-induced movement disorders was 38.6% (95% CI 33.7–43.5%). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, being single (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.95; 95% CI 1.08–3.52), having a diagnosis of schizophrenia (AOR = 2.62; 95% CI 1.03–6.67), and an illness duration of more than 10 years (AOR = 3.65; 95% CI 1.05–12.70) were associated with higher odds of movement disorders. Compared with antidepressant use, first-generation antipsychotic use (AOR = 5.42; 95% CI 1.47–19.95) and second-generation antipsychotic use (AOR = 3.22; 95% CI 1.19–8.68) were also associated with higher odds of movement disorders. Psychotropic medication-induced movement disorders were common, affecting more than one-third of patients receiving regular psychiatric follow-up. Being single, having a diagnosis of schizophrenia, an illness duration of more than 10 years, and treatment with first- or second-generation antipsychotics were associated with higher odds of movement disorders. These findings underscore the importance of routine monitoring, early detection, and appropriate management of movement disorders in psychiatric care, particularly among patients with prolonged illness and those receiving antipsychotic treatment.

Article.Title: Policy-gated firmware trust and anti-rollback resilience for autonomous UAV edge platforms: a software validation study
Article.Authors: Shagor M.
Article.Abstract: Firmware integrity and version control are important safeguards during the initialization of autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, the effectiveness of firmware-admission mechanisms depends not only on their security policies but also on whether those policies consistently enforce integrity requirements, rollback restrictions, and persistent-state protection. This study investigates the gap between stated security assumptions and actual admission behavior in a GPS-denied UAV environment. A fail-closed firmware-admission approach is examined through formal policy analysis and controlled experimental validation. The investigation identifies two critical weaknesses: acceptance of inadequately verified integrity metadata when a required secret is absent, and acceptance despite unsuccessful preservation of the previously trusted state. The revised mechanism addresses these weaknesses by enforcing mandatory trust configuration, independently evaluating firmware-version and rollback-counter constraints, and preserving accepted-state integrity when admission is rejected. Experimental findings demonstrate consistent rejection behavior under the evaluated conditions. The study contributes a more clearly defined and experimentally assessed software-level security boundary for UAV firmware admission. Its conclusions remain limited to the evaluated policy assumptions and do not establish hardware-backed firmware authenticity or resistance to privileged compromise.

Article.Title: ParkMultiNet combines MRI and speech data for multimodal Parkinson’s disease classification
Article.Authors: Jia G.; Li P.; Hao L.; Wang Z.; Yang X.
Article.Abstract: Early Parkinson’s disease (PD) classification requires jointly reasoning over structural imaging and behavioral signals, yet existing methods remain limited in modeling long-range spatial dependencies in 3D medical images and in effectively integrating heterogeneous modalities, making it difficult to fully exploit subtle structural abnormalities and cross-modal complementary information. To address this issue, we propose ParkMultiNet, a multimodal framework for PD classification that integrates MRI and speech information. ParkMultiNet adopts a four-stage hierarchical architecture and contains three key modules: a multi-view spatial attention (MVSA) module for modeling long-range 3D spatial dependencies through decoupled convolutional paths, a group-enhanced channel recalibration (GECR) module for suppressing feature redundancy and improving modality-aware feature refinement, and a cascaded atrous spatial pyramid module (CASPM) for extracting multi-scale contextual features while maintaining parameter efficiency. Experiments were conducted on PubPDdataset, a pseudo-paired multimodal dataset constructed from multiple public data sources, and on PativePDdataset, an independent clinical dataset evaluated in a label-consistent pseudo-paired multimodal setting. Results show that ParkMultiNet achieves the highest observed mean accuracy among the compared methods in multimodal classification. In particular, it attains an accuracy of 0.9385 and an F1-score of 0.9457 on PubPDdataset. On PativePDdataset, its observed mean accuracy was 0.8417. Further unimodal comparisons and ablation studies verify the effectiveness of multimodal integration and the complementary contributions of MVSA, GECR, and CASPM. These results indicate that ParkMultiNet provides an effective multimodal solution for PD classification.

Article.Title: V-shaped folded flexible patch antenna for conformal 5 GHz applications: static electromagnetic characterization
Article.Authors: Kishore Ajay kumar A.; Srinivas K.; Shah O.; Rangi S.; Tipu R.; Sreenivasulu V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Flexible antennas are attractive for conformal wireless platforms because they can be integrated onto curved or space-constrained structures. This work investigates the electromagnetic response of a Kapton-based microstrip patch antenna subjected to localized V-shaped folding in forward-folding and backward-folding configurations. The antenna was modeled using full-wave electromagnetic simulation and experimentally characterized under controlled static fold angles. The analysis includes the input reflection coefficient, resonant-frequency shift, impedance bandwidth, gain, radiation patterns, surface-current distribution, and simulated power losses. The results show that the antenna retains a resonance near 5 GHz over the investigated fold-angle range, although the impedance response, gain, and loss distribution depend on both folding direction and angle. The forward-folded configurations generally provide higher simulated gain, whereas the backward-folded configurations exhibit a different resonance and loss response. Surface-current distributions indicate that the principal current path remains active after folding, which is consistent with the observed resonance retention. The measured and simulated results show similar trends, with deviations attributed to fabrication tolerance, SMA-connector effects, material-property uncertainty, and fold-angle control. The study demonstrates static electromagnetic performance under controlled V-fold configurations; it does not establish mechanical fatigue life or long-term structural durability.

Article.Title: Rendezvous optimization method for addressing long-job burst problem in industrial internet of things
Article.Authors: Alghuson M.; Alghuried A.; Abuhasel K.
Article.Abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) cells suffer long-job bursts when arrival surges and interdependent tasks push jobs past their time limit. This article presents ROM-RS, a Rendezvous Optimization Method with rule-based Recommendation Scheduling for adaptive task scheduling and resource reallocation. ROM-RS matches a resource to a waiting task at the moment the resource is released, reallocates released resources across jobs, and applies three runtime rules that favour the jobs that can still finish within the limit. The method is evaluated on a discrete-event simulation of a CNC cell whose task types, precedence and processing times are taken from a public machining dataset, with 1,080 jobs per 8-hour shift and arrival surges, against first-come first-served dispatching, PSO- and GA-tuned priority rules and a DQN rule-selection scheduler. ROM-RS yields the lowest burst ratio of the five methods (0.125 against 0.150 for the tuned rules and 0.301 for FCFS; paired p < 0.001) with 0.25 s of computation per shift, while the tuned rules complete about 0.5% points more jobs at roughly 600 times the computation. An ablation attributes the result to the recommendation rules, the event-driven matching and the reallocation of released resources. The simulator and all outputs are deposited.

Article.Title: Trends in deaths involving melanoma and cardiovascular disease among older US adults from 1999 to 2020
Article.Authors: Shakil R.; Mughees M.; Ehtesham S.; Anwar S.; Khan S.; Khan M.; Bhatti A.; Fawad Z.; Qamar I.; Sajjad W.; Najam F.; Qureshi S.; Ashraf D.
Article.Abstract: Malignant melanoma (MM) is an aggressive skin cancer with rising incidence and improved survival. However, trends in U.S. deaths involving both MM and cardiovascular disease (CVD) among older adults are not well characterized. We aimed to describe age-adjusted mortality trends and disparities for these deaths among U.S. adults aged 65 years or older from 1999 to 2020. We used the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess US mortality trends from 1999 to 2020 among adults aged 65 years or older whose death certificates listed MM (ICD-10 C43) and CVD (ICD-10 I00–I99) as underlying or contributing causes. We calculated age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 and annual percent changes (APCs) using Joinpoint regression, with results stratified by sex, race, place of death, region, state, and metropolitan status. This analysis describes deaths involving both conditions in the population; it does not estimate cardiovascular mortality risk among patients with melanoma. Between 1999 and 2020, 39,190 deaths involving MM and CVD were recorded among adults aged 65 years or older, 36.8% at home. AAMR increased from 3.8 to 5.0 (APC 0.95%, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.31). Men had higher AAMRs than women (7.0 vs. 2.5). AAMRs were highest in NH Whites (5.0), followed by Hispanics (1.3), and lowest in NH Blacks (0.8). Final-segment APCs were 10.38% for nonmetropolitan counties (2018–2020) and 3.44% for metropolitan counties (2016–2020); these segments are not directly comparable. AAMRs across states ranged from 1.4 (District of Columbia) to 6.1 (California, Oklahoma, Nebraska), with overlapping CIs. The West had the highest regional AAMR (5.1). The rate of deaths in which both MM and CVD were listed as underlying or contributing causes is rising among older adults, with notable disparities by sex, race, and geography, highlighting the need for targeted, region-specific interventions to reduce this burden.

Article.Title: Cooperative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for robust frequency regulation in renewable-integrated power systems
Article.Authors: Krishnaveni S.; Muniraj R.; Sambath R.; Aruna R.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient with prioritized experience replay and cooperative gradient sharing (MADDPG-PER-Coop) framework for automatic generation control (AGC) in renewable-integrated interconnected power systems. The proposed approach integrates prioritized experience replay, adaptive exploration noise, cooperative gradient sharing, State-of-Energy observation augmentation, and a composite multi-objective reward function to improve frequency regulation and tie-line power control under varying operating conditions. The framework is investigated using a three-area thermal–hydro–wind–solar photovoltaic interconnected power system and further examined in an extended five-area configuration to assess its performance under increased system dimensionality. Under the nominal benchmark condition, the proposed controller achieves a settling time of 8.0 s, an overshoot of 2.1%, an integral squared error (ISE) of (8.6\times10^{-3}), and an integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of 0.21. Compared with the conventional proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller, these results correspond to reductions of 68.4%, 85.2%, 80.9%, and 76.4% in settling time, overshoot, ISE, and ITAE, respectively. In a separate stochastic evaluation involving 30 independent simulation runs, the proposed method achieves a mean ITAE of 0.248 with a standard deviation of 0.015 and a mean settling time of 5.94 s. The ablation analysis examines the contribution of the individual framework components to the observed control performance. In addition, real-time implementation using a dSPACE DS1104 platform yields a mean execution latency of 1.86 ms and a maximum latency of 2.47 ms, with peak frequency deviations of approximately 0.010–0.012 Hz across the evaluated areas. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides effective frequency regulation under the investigated simulation conditions and demonstrates real-time execution feasibility on the tested platform. The findings are limited to the evaluated system configurations and operating scenarios, and further assessment is required to establish its applicability to larger and more diverse power systems.

Article.Title: Structure-controlled accessibility and mechanistic insights into the antimicrobial activity of one-dimensional Cd(II) and Mn(II) coordination polymers
Article.Authors: Alzard R.; Dahman N.; Alshehhi M.; Alblooshi M.; Poulose V.; El-Maghraby H.; Labata F.; Munawar N.; Alzamly A.; Abdellah M.
Article.Abstract: In this study, we report the synthesis and antibacterial evaluation of two 1D-metal-coordination polymers (M-CPs), one of which is the Cd(II)-based polymer (Cd-CP), which represents a new crystal structure determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), while the Mn(II) analogue (Mn-CP) is used for comparative evaluation. Cd-CP crystallizes in a triclinic structure with a chemical formula of [Cd(Phen)(5-NIP).H 2 O)] n [5-NIP = 5-nitroisophthalate, Phen = 1,10-phenanthroline] with coordinated water molecules. Comprehensive characterizations, including PXRD, FT-IR, TGA, XPS, and SEM/EDX, confirmed both M-CPs’ structural, chemical, and morphological features. M-CPs were evaluated against Lactococcus sp., Escherichia coli (E. coli) , and Burkholderia sp. using complementary biological assays, and their antibacterial mechanisms were investigated and compared through multiple experimental approaches to establish a plausible mode of action. For Gram-positive bacteria, Cd-CP showed high susceptibility, with an MIC of 15.625 µg/mL, followed by Mn-CP (125 µg/mL). Mn-CP also exhibited potent antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria, with MIC values of 31.25 µg/mL against E. coli and 500 µg/mL against Burkholderia sp. Agarose gel electrophoresis demonstrated that both M-CPs cause membrane disruption and DNA damage, consistent with ICP-based metal release data that showed minimal release of Cd 2+ compared to Mn 2+ . Mechanistic studies using Ellman’s reagent (DTNB, 5,5′-dithiobis(2-nitrobenzoic acid)) assay and Terephthalic acid (TA) assays revealed that Mn-CP induces oxidative stress via redox processes, whereas the new Cd-CP operates through labile ligand exchange, facilitating Cd–thiol coordination that mimics enzymatic inhibition in the bacteria. This work highlights the advantage of structure-controlled design in CPs to tailor metal bioavailability and antibacterial pathways, which establishes M-CPs as promising platforms for selective and next-generation antimicrobial strategies.

Article.Title: Feasibility assessment of Exhaled breath condensate (EBC) as a source of lung microbiome of NSCLC patients, based on metabarcoding analysis
Article.Authors: Machnicki P.; Czarnecka-Chrebelska K.; Kordiak J.; Lewandowski K.; Bielec F.; Płoszaj T.; Brzeziańska-Lasota E.; Pastuszak-Lewandoska D.
Article.Abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely because its early symptoms are non-specific and diagnosis often occurs at advanced stages. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in the lung microbiome contribute to NSCLC development and progression. This study evaluated the feasibility of using exhaled breath condensate (EBC) as a non-invasive source of lung microbiome profiles. We performed 16 S rRNA gene metabarcoding on 32 EBC samples and compared their microbial composition with matched tumor and adjacent control lung tissues. EBC provided sufficient bacterial sequence data for 16 S rRNA gene-based microbiome analysis. We found that a limited but detectable proportion of the EBC microbial profile could be attributed to lung-tissue sources, while seven genera were common across all analyzed sample types. Escherichia - Shigella , predominant genus previously linked to lung malignancy, was consistently detectable in EBC. EBC also showed a higher bacterial sequence retention rate suggesting a lower relative impact of host DNA interference. These findings offer a preliminary signal of the feasibility of EBC as a non-invasive material for pulmonary microbiome research. Further studies including healthy controls are required before EBC can be considered for biomarker development or clinical applications.

Article.Title: WHtR identifies higher ultrasound-detected fatty liver prevalence below the BMI overweight threshold but adds little beyond BMI and TyG
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Gan L.; Lu X.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) may identify a central-adiposity phenotype with a high prevalence of fatty liver among adults whose body mass index (BMI) is below the Chinese overweight threshold (< 24 kg/m²). Whether this information improves individual-level discrimination beyond metabolic measures remains uncertain. We evaluated the phenotyping value of WHtR, its incremental contribution beyond BMI plus the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index, and the performance of TyG-derived anthropometric composite indices. We retrospectively analysed 3469 adults who attended routine health examinations at Fusui County People’s Hospital. We first compared the prevalence of ultrasound-detected fatty liver across four BMI–WHtR phenotypes and then examined the joint BMI–WHtR association using a continuous generalized additive model. For the secondary classification analysis, unpenalized logistic models were evaluated with 20 repeats of outcome-stratified 10-fold cross-validation. All models included age, sex, systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure; additional terms comprised BMI, waist circumference, WHtR, TyG, prespecified combinations or TyG-derived composite indices. Ultrasound-detected fatty liver was present in 839 participants (24.2%). Among the 1933 participants with BMI < 24 kg/m², those with WHtR ≥ 0.5 represented 11.0% of the BMI stratum but accounted for 31.4% of its cases of ultrasound-detected fatty liver. The prevalence of ultrasound-detected fatty liver was 23.0% in this group, compared with 6.2% among participants with both low BMI and low WHtR. After adjustment for age, sex and TyG, the prevalence ratio for the low-BMI/high-WHtR phenotype was 2.63 (95% CI, 1.90–3.63). Prevalence rose gradually across the joint BMI–WHtR distribution, with no abrupt change at BMI 24 kg/m² or WHtR 0.5. Adding TyG to BMI increased the cross-validated ROC AUC from 0.837 to 0.865. Adding WHtR to BMI plus TyG increased the ROC AUC to 0.867, a paired difference of 0.00163 (95% CI, − 0.00009 to 0.00337). The corresponding differences were − 0.00008 (95% CI, − 0.00424 to 0.00416) for precision–recall AUC and − 0.00053 (95% CI, − 0.00132 to 0.00023) for the Brier score. ​WHtR identified a high-prevalence phenotype of ultrasound-detected fatty liver among adults below the Chinese BMI overweight threshold. Its addition to BMI plus TyG, however, yielded little further discrimination, with no clear improvement in precision–recall performance or overall prediction error. TyG-derived composite indices showed no clear overall advantage over the simpler BMI-plus-TyG model. Waist and height measurements may support low-cost phenotypic stratification in routine county hospital health examinations, but these single-centre cross-sectional data do not support using WHtR alone as a screening threshold to guide liver ultrasound referrals.

Article.Title: Collision detection in polishing robots based on self-supervised learning
Article.Authors: Xing Y.; Zhang F.; Liu D.; Mu D.
Article.Abstract: Polishing robots are widely used in industrial surface-finishing tasks, but collision detection remains challenging because labeled collision data are costly and potentially hazardous to collect. This paper proposes a self-supervised collision-detection framework that learns temporal representations from unlabeled robot interaction data without requiring collision labels during pre-training. A modality-specific dual-encoder architecture based on Gated Recurrent Units separately models joint motion and current-related signals, while intra-modal contrastive objectives and cross-modal alignment capture temporal consistency and complementary dynamic information. After pre-training, both encoders are frozen and only a lightweight probe classifier is trained for downstream collision detection. Task-oriented signal augmentations are further introduced to improve robustness to polishing-related disturbances. On a highly imbalanced simulation benchmark, the proposed method achieves an Area Under the Precision–Recall Curve (PR-AUC) of \(94.02\%\) , a Best F1-score of \(93.88\%\) , and a Recall of \(94.77\%\) under a false-positive-rate constraint of 0.5% (R@FPR \(\le\) 0.5%), outperforming the compared methods across the four reported metrics. In controlled real-world proof-of-concept experiments on an RM65 robotic arm, few-shot probe adaptation improves window-level Recall from 73.44% to 86.08% and trial-level Recall from 60.00% to 79.20%. These results demonstrate the potential of self-supervised multimodal representation learning for collision detection under polishing-related conditions, while indicating that further validation is needed for practical deployment.

Article.Title: A novel dual-switched inductor and switched capacitor converter with low ripple current and high voltage gain for a low-voltage fuel cell stack
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Arun N.
Article.Abstract: In this paper a non-isolated dual switched inductor-switched capacitor (DSI-SC) converter is proposed. This converter is designed for high-efficiency power conversion in applications using a low-voltage fuel cell stack. The topology is developed to reduce the input current ripple, component voltage stress, enhance the voltage gain and thereby improve the performance of the system. The proposed DSI-SC converter is specifically designed to boost the output voltage of a fuel cell electric vehicle. Fuel cell technology is an important energy source for electric vehicles. The fuel cell stacks are the fundamental components of this technology. A high-voltage fuel cell stack requires additional fuel cells to produce enough power for an electric vehicle. But the heavier you make the electric vehicles, the more fuel cells you put in the stack. Moreover, fuel cells have a problem with loads with abrupt changes. The impact of the input ripple current is noticeable at high load currents. The proposed DSI-SC converter is therefore well suited for a low-voltage fuel cell stack, as it can provide high voltage gain with low current ripple at the input. The DSI-SC converter has been verified by hardware testing and modelling at a 400 V/400 W load.

Article.Title: The effect of electric-acoustic stimulation on hair cell response in a neural-silenced mouse model
Article.Authors: Fankhauser V.; Geys M.; Bertschinger R.; Kunut A.; Schär M.; Bächinger D.; Dalbert A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Combined electric-acoustic stimulation (EAS) can improve hearing outcomes in cochlear implant users with residual hearing, yet electrical stimulation may interfere with acoustically driven cochlear responses. Where exactly in the auditory pathway this interaction happens remains controversial. To our knowledge, no previous study has examined purely hair-cell-derived cochlear microphonics (CMs) during EAS. We isolated hair-cell-derived CMs in C57BL/6 mice by using kainic acid to suppress neural responses while preserving hair-cell activity. After cochlear implantation with a custom-made electrode array, extracochlear ECochG was recorded during acoustic stimulation alone and simultaneous EAS using two electrical phase durations (60 and 200 µs) and four acoustic frequencies (2, 4, 6, 8 kHz). During EAS, CM amplitudes were reduced compared with acoustic stimulation alone, with mean reductions of 1.10 dB for 60-µs stimulation and 1.79 dB for 200-µs stimulation. This attenuation was transient, maximal within the first milliseconds after stimulus onset, and largely resolved by 5 ms. No significant interaction between phase duration and acoustic frequency was detected. These findings show that electrical stimulation transiently suppresses hair-cell responses during EAS, but the small and short-lived effect suggests that additional neural mechanisms are required to explain perceptual electric-acoustic interference.

Article.Title: Independent control of volatile fugacity and redox state using Ag–AgXy equilibria
Article.Authors: Thomas R.; Matzen A.; Gorojovsky L.; Rusiecka M.; Wood B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The solubility and speciation of volatile elements in silicate melts strongly influence magmatic processes, from redox evolution to fluid exsolution and metal transport. Experimental investigation of these behaviours requires precise control of volatile fugacities at high pressure and temperature, yet existing approaches, including mixed-gas systems, volatile-bearing fluids, and classical oxide buffers all have limitations. We present an alternative approach based on rarely exploited equilibria between silver metal (Ag) and its binary compounds (AgX y ), where X is any element forming a stable silver phase. These equilibria fix the fugacity of X-bearing molecular species directly in contact with silicate melt at high pressure and temperature. Because silver and its compounds have low solubilities in silicate melts under most conditions, Ag-AgX y buffers impose predictable, composition-independent volatile fugacities. The method is compatible with some internal and external oxygen buffers, enabling simultaneous control of volatile fugacity and redox state. We outline the thermodynamic basis of the Ag–AgX y approach, describe its high-pressure implementation and demonstrate its applicability across multiple volatile element groups, including halogens and chalcogens. We conclude that Ag-AgX y buffering provides a valuable addition to the experimentalists’ ‘toolkit’ , a robust and flexible means of controlling chemical potentials in high-pressure experiments.

Article.Title: Disparities in COVID-19 challenges among people with a history of injection drug use in the RADx-UP initiative
Article.Authors: Walters S.; Brewer R.; Payne G.; Leonard S.; Bouris A.; Wruck L.; Stebbins A.; Schneider J.
Article.Abstract: Structural vulnerability underlies significant inequities in access to resources and outcomes in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. In particular, people who inject drugs (PWID) or people with a history of injection drug use (PWHID) face health and social challenges such as unstable housing, limited healthcare access, and increased prevalence of comorbidities, which are associated with increased risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Despite these vulnerabilities, there is limited research on the factors underlying COVID-19-related challenges and the specific challenges PWID/PWHID face. The RADx Underserved Populations (RADx-UP) initiative aims to address COVID-19-related disparities by improving testing in underserved populations. RADx-UP sites reported standardized data across diverse geographic, racial, and socioeconomic groups, with a particular focus on vulnerable communities such as racial minorities, PWID/PWHID, people with disabilities, and those with limited access to healthcare. Data examined in this study includes 24,808 participants from 31 RADx-UP projects across the United States (US). A total of 952 participants identified as people with a history of injection drug use by selecting “intravenous drug use” from a list of health conditions. The primary outcome was challenges experienced during COVID-19 in six domains: healthcare access, housing, food security, water access, medication access, and transportation. Participants ranked factors as being “no challenge,” a “minor challenge,” or a “major challenge.” GEE logistic regression models were used to assess the association between injection drug use and COVID-19 challenges. PWHID were significantly more likely to experience at least one COVID-19-related challenge compared to those without a history of injecting drugs (AOR = 2.00 [95% CI 1.36–2.94]). PWHID had higher prevalence of unstable housing, food insecurity, and lack of access to healthcare. Structural vulnerabilities such as insufficient access to personal protective equipment (PPE) and chronic health conditions were also associated with elevated risk of severe outcomes. Equitable public health interventions, including efforts to prioritize resource distribution to PWID/PWHID and other marginalized populations, are critical to prevent exacerbation of inequities in the context of crises.

Article.Title: Estimating the transmission dynamics of Mpox in Saudi Arabia using case surveillance and a Bayesian SEIR model
Article.Authors: M.S. Althobaity Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to estimate the population-level transmission dynamics of the 2023–2024 Mpox outbreak in Saudi Arabia, using surveillance data from 13 May 2023 to 8 February 2024, and to estimate key epidemiological parameters to inform targeted interventions and containment strategies. Case-based surveillance was integrated with dynamic modeling, and the 92% of confirmed cases with complete data were analyzed using a Bayesian SEIR model to estimate the effective reproduction number ( $$R_e$$ ), the observation-scaling parameter ( $$\rho $$ ), and the overdispersion parameter ( $$\phi $$ ). At the onset of the modelled period (13 May 2023), $$R_e$$ was estimated at 2.04 (95% CrI: 1.47–2.64), rose to a peak of 2.08 (95% CrI: 1.55–2.66) on 16 May 2023, and declined below the epidemic threshold ( $$R_e < 1$$ ) by 8 September 2023. The observation-scaling parameter, which links modelled incidence to reported cases, was estimated at $$\rho = 0.561$$ (95% CrI: 0.351–0.786). The overdispersion parameter was $$\phi = 3.141$$ (95% CrI: 2.479–3.877), with stable estimates. Cases were reported among individuals with travel histories and reported exposure to social settings, and the case series showed a concentration among men. The observed dynamics were consistent with the global Clade IIb outbreak context, connecting imported cases to local transmission. These findings underscore the role of human mobility and local transmission in Mpox dissemination within Saudi Arabia, emphasizing timely epidemiological monitoring to inform targeted interventions, containment strategies, and resource allocation.

Article.Title: Phylogenetic analysis of a rare SAT1 foot-and-mouth disease virus incursion in Iran in 2025 reveals genetic association with African lineages and suggests potential transboundary connectivity
Article.Authors: Saeidi B.; Azimi M.; Binayi F.; Sharif‐zak M.; Azimi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) serotype Southern African Territories 1 (SAT1) has historically been restricted to sub-Saharan Africa, where wildlife-livestock interfaces sustain endemic transmission. Its recent incursion into non-endemic regions highlights critical gaps in global biosecurity surveillance. Here, we characterized the VP1 sequence of a 2025 Iranian SAT1 isolate (accession PX608395.1) and assessed its phylogenetic placement and relationship to available global reference sequences using maximum likelihood analysis, alongside spatial mapping of SAT1 detections reported in 2025 by the World Reference Laboratory for Foot-and-Mouth Disease (WRLFMD; https://www.wrlfmd.org/2025-quarter-4-oct-dec ). Rather than representing an independent regional variant, the Iranian isolate clustered within established Southern African Topotype III lineages, exhibiting a close sister-group relationship with Botswana reference strains. Researchers identified the Iranian isolate when SAT1 topotype III detections were also reported in Lebanon, Azerbaijan, and Türkiye. Spatial analysis revealed a marked geographic disjunction between these newly affected West Asian countries and active Southern African viral reservoirs, highlighting substantial genomic surveillance gaps that may obscure intermediate viral circulation. These findings show that exotic FMDV strains can travel long distances despite substantial geographic separation, underscoring the need for connectivity-informed risk-assessment frameworks. Strengthening cross-border data sharing, expanding diagnostic capacity, and enhancing baseline genomic surveillance are essential to anticipate and contain future transboundary viral incursions.

Article.Title: Biosynthesis and characterization of arsenic trioxide (As2O3) nanoparticles and evaluation of their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Ghaderi M.; Pajavand H.; Satarzadeh N.; Dousari A.; Karbalaei M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli are very dangerous pathogens because they are the cause of hospital infections on the one hand and natural flora in the digestive system of people on the other hand and are easily transmitted to other people and are associated with high mortality. Therefore, the present study aimed to develop a green synthesis method for arsenic trioxide (As 2 O 3 ) nanoparticles using pink rose petals as a biological source and to characterize their physicochemical properties. Furthermore, the antibacterial activity of the synthesized As 2 O 3 nanoparticles was evaluated against multidrug-resistant E. coli strains. Pink rose petals were used as a reducing agent for As 2 O 3 NPs. XRD, EDX, FTIR, SEM, and DLS analyses were used to identify As 2 O 3 NPs and the microplate approach was utilized to examine the antibacterial effects of As 2 O 3 NPs on multidrug-resistant E. coli . Characterization analyses showed that the biosynthesized As 2 O 3 NPs were spherical, with an average dry particle size of 17.74 nm determined by SEM and a hydrodynamic diameter of 19.01 nm determined by DLS. The results of antibacterial effects demonstrated that the lowest MIC of As 2 O 3 NPs was 50 μg/mL on the standard strain of E. coli and 100 μg/mL against clinical strains of multidrug-resistant E. coli . Biosynthesized As 2 O 3 NPs showed notable antibacterial activity against the tested standard and multidrug-resistant E. coli strains. The use of pink rose petals represents a simple, rapid, and low-cost approach for the synthesis of these nanoparticles; however, further studies are required to evaluate their biosafety and broader antibacterial spectrum.

Article.Title: Revealing the generation characteristics of China’s household food waste by provinces by year
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Liao X.; Fan L.; Zhao Z.; Li Y.; He T.; Fan J.; Su D.; Zhang G.; Jia M.
Article.Abstract: Household food waste (HFW) lies at the intersection of food security, resource efficiency, and climate mitigation, yet robust regional-scale generation data remain scarce in rapidly urbanizing developing countries. We compiled 274 data points covering 38 cities to quantify the proportion of HFW in total municipal solid waste (PHFW_MSW) and the HFW across 31 Chinese provinces during 2001–2024. A socioeconomic-driven backpropagation neural network model is constructed to project HFW trajectories up to 2050 under three scenarios, and facility operational data are adopted to assess economic and carbon reduction benefits of large-scale anaerobic digestion. Our analysis reveals substantial spatial heterogeneity in PHFW_MSW, ranging from 14 to 76% across provinces, with East China generating nearly half of national HFW. National HFW rose from 62.12 ± 8.34 to 139.11 ± 19.39 Mt yr -1 and its projects to peak at 150–160 Mt around 2030 before declining. Scenario analysis indicates that, under the optimistic scenario, cumulative carbon reductions can reach 738.05–828.05 Mt CO 2 -eq by 2050, and that anaerobic digestion can yield cumulative economic benefits of 177.30–219.86 billion USD by 2040. This study provides baseline data for differentiated regional HFW governance (e.g., the formulation of future regional coordinated waste reduction strategies), and the modelling framework is globally applicable.

Article.Title: Qualifying LPA generated electron beams to free electron laser applications
Article.Authors: Ghaith A.; Labat M.; Espinos D.; LaBerge M.; Schöbel S.; Ufer P.; Chang Y.; Herrmann F.; Valléau M.; Roussel E.; Loulergue A.; Schramm U.; Irman A.; Couprie M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Laser plasma accelerators (LPAs), capable of producing ultra-short, high peak current electron beams with low emittance, offer a promising path toward next-generation compact free-electron lasers (FELs). However, their large energy spread, high divergence, and shot-to-shot fluctuations present major challenges for stable FEL operation. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the Coxinel phase-space manipulation beamline in mitigating these limitations for 196 MeV LPA-generated electron beams, with beam transport validated through experiments and Elegant simulations. FEL performance at 270 nm is analyzed using Genesis code, with additional studies extending to shorter wavelength (64 nm, 41 nm, 28 nm), revealing strong sensitivity to beam parameters at the LPA source. Article.Title: Tissue eosinophilia in oral leukoplakia, erythroplakia, oral lichen planus, and conventional oral squamous cell carcinoma: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Srijunkat H.; Poomsawat S.; Kosanwat T.; Pankam J.; Khovidhunkit S.
Article.Abstract: Eosinophils have been implicated in tumor-associated inflammation and may contribute to carcinogenesis. However, evidence regarding their role in oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains limited. This study aimed to compare tissue eosinophilia among three OPMDs, namely, oral leukoplakia (55 cases), oral erythroplakia (27 cases), oral lichen planus (OLP) (22 cases), conventional OSCC (23 cases) and normal oral mucosa (NOM) (20 cases). All cases were stained with hematoxylin and eosin. Eosinophils were counted and recorded as number of eosinophils per10 high-power fields. Differences in eosinophil counts among groups were evaluated using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by Dunn’s post hoc test with Bonferroni correction. Associations between tissue eosinophilia, clinicopathological variables and risk factors for OPMDs and OSCC were analyzed using univariable followed by multivariable logistic regression. No significant differences in eosinophil counts were observed among leukoplakia, erythroplakia, OLP and NOM. In contrast, OSCC demonstrated significantly higher eosinophil counts than NOM and all OPMDs ( p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression revealed that tissue eosinophilia was associated with OSCC (adjusted OR = 18.14; 95% CI: 2.50-131.69; p = 0.004) and alcohol consumption (adjusted OR = 5.52; 95% CI: 1.47–20.69; p = 0.011). In conclusion, tissue eosinophilia was more frequent in OSCC than in NOM or the three OPMDs examined. This suggests that eosinophil infiltration is associated with invasive carcinoma rather than with oral leukoplakia, erythroplakia or OLP. The association between tissue eosinophilia and alcohol consumption raises the possibility of alcohol-related eosinophil recruitment, warranting further investigation. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings and clarify the role of eosinophil infiltration in oral carcinogenesis.

Article.Title: Fast time-domain near-infrared spectroscopy for investigating human skeletal muscle microvascular control mechanisms
Article.Authors: Re R.; Quaresima V.; Contini L.; Amendola C.; Contini D.; Spinelli L.; Ferrari M.; Torricelli A.
Article.Abstract: Microcirculatory oscillations of the small arteries and arterioles, known as vasomotion, are a documented feature of blood flow that reflects the functional state of the vascular system. These oscillations modify blood flow and contribute to periodic flow fluctuations known as flowmotion. Reliable techniques for noninvasive in vivo study of microvascular control mechanisms in human skeletal muscles during rest and/or exercise are lacking. Here, we introduce a combined approach using fast (20 Hz) time-domain near-infrared spectroscopy, a noninvasive optical measurement, and power spectral density analysis, via fast Fourier transform, to investigate microvascular control mechanisms in vivo and during exercise. We identified six characteristic frequency intervals (bands), ranging from 0.005 to 2 Hz, in the tibialis anterior muscle of 8 healthy participants (27.4 ± 1.4 y; 5 males: 27.4 ± 1.8 y; 3 females: 27.3 ± 0.6 y) during rest, prolonged isometric contraction at 40% of maximal voluntary contraction, and recovery. Each band, extensively investigated in cutaneous blood flowmotion studies, has been proposed to reflect a specific physiological influence modulating the microcirculatory response. For band VI, there were differences in oxyhemoglobin (O 2 Hb) and total hemoglobin (tHb) between rest and contraction, and between contraction and recovery. Recovery differed from rest for deoxyhemoglobin (HHb) and oxygen saturation (rSmO 2 ). In contrast, band V showed a difference only between recovery and contraction for tHb. In band IV, rest differed from contraction for all tests. It also differed for recovery for HHb and rSmO 2 . Band III showed differences between rest and contraction, and between contraction and recovery for all parameters. In conclusion, this work establishes a new methodology, utilizing all four hemodynamic parameters, useful for elucidating the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle microvascular oscillations across diverse diseases and conditions, such as training and aging.

Article.Authors: Dhanda A.; Thulluru L.; Chowdhury S.; Dubey B.; Chakraborty D.; Jadhav G.; Ghangrekar M.; Sfirloaga P.; Duteanu N.
Article.Abstract: As the global shift toward circular economy accelerates, recovering nutrients and energy from waste streams has become increasingly critical. This investigation explores electroconcentration (EC) as a strategy for recovering multiple nutrients and hydrogen (H₂) from hydrolysed urine. During continuous operation, the system achieved a NH₄⁺–N removal efficiency of 79.8% and a recovery efficiency of 69.1% in the concentrate. Removal efficiencies of 82.2, 92.7, 87.2, 56.7 and 70.2% were obtained for Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻, PO₄³⁻ and SO₄²⁻, with corresponding recovery efficiencies of 75.6, 85.9, 81.8, 52.1 and 63.2%, and up-concentration factors ranging from 3.29 to 5.42. A peak NH₄⁺–N concentration of 24.6 g/L was obtained in the concentrate. Simultaneously, H₂ was recovered at 5.40 m³/m³·​d, offering an energy offset of 4.4 kWh/kg·N recovered. The system maintained stable performance over 168 h of continuous operation. These results highlight EC as a viable platform for integrated nutrient and energy recovery, offering strong potential for decentralised wastewater treatment and circular resource management.

Article.Title: Source transparency and accuracy warnings support more selective reliance on generative-AI answers in a randomized online experiment
Article.Authors: Xing Y.; Zhang Z.; Zhang Y.; Zhang M.; Lu X.
Article.Abstract: Generative-AI systems increasingly provide answers to everyday questions, but users need to decide not only whether to accept an answer, but whether acceptance should depend on answer correctness. This randomized online experiment tested whether visible source information and an accuracy warning supported more selective reliance on AI-style answers. A final analytic sample of 800 adult participants was assigned to one of four between-subjects cue conditions in a 2 × 2 × 2 mixed design crossing source transparency (absent vs. present), accuracy warning (absent vs. present), and answer correctness (incorrect vs. correct, within participant). Each participant evaluated 24 AI-style answers, yielding 19,200 trial-level observations. The primary analysis used all trials and modelled acceptance as a function of source transparency, accuracy warning, answer correctness, and their interactions. Participants accepted correct answers more often than incorrect answers, and the correct-incorrect acceptance gap was largest in the source-plus-warning condition. In the applied-risk model restricted to incorrect-answer trials, acceptance of incorrect answers was highest in the control condition (1080/2400, 45%) and lower in the source-only (864/2400, 36%), warning-only (672/2400, 28%), and source-plus-warning conditions (504/2400, 21%). Verification behaviour was highest in the combined condition (2496/4800, 52%). These results indicate that brief on-screen cues lowered erroneous-answer acceptance and encouraged verification in low-risk information-evaluation tasks, while the distinction between response bias and sensitivity remains an important boundary condition.

Article.Title: Paeoniflorin attenuates high-fat diet-induced obesity by promoting white adipose tissue browning via the regulation of the AMPK/SIRT3 pathway
Article.Authors: Sun M.; Wang M.; Ni Y.; Wang W.; Zhang L.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Obesity is a major global public health challenge. Induction of white adipose tissue (WAT) browning has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance energy expenditure and improve metabolic homeostasis. Paeoniflorin (PF), a natural monoterpene glycoside, exhibits diverse pharmacological activities; however, its effects on WAT browning remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether PF alleviates high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity and associated metabolic abnormalities by promoting WAT browning. Obesity was induced in C57BL/6 mice by HFD feeding, followed by oral administration of PF (100 or 200 mg/kg). Body weight, adipose tissue mass, blood glucose, serum insulin, and lipid profiles were evaluated. Adipocyte morphology and the expression of thermogenesis-related markers, including UCP1, PGC-1α, and PRDM16, were assessed by histological analysis, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. Lipid accumulation was evaluated by Oil Red O staining. In vitro, 3T3-L1 cells were treated with PF during adipocyte differentiation to assess lipid accumulation and the expression of browning-related markers. The potential involvement of the AMPK/SIRT3 signaling pathway was further investigated using pharmacological inhibition of AMPK. PF treatment significantly attenuated HFD-induced obesity and metabolic abnormalities in a dose-dependent manner. Compared with the HFD group, final body weight was reduced by 5.6% and 9.8% following treatment with PF at 100 and 200 mg/kg, respectively. Fasting blood glucose levels were decreased by 22.3% and 35.3%, while fasting insulin levels were reduced by 34.2% and 62.6%, respectively. PF also markedly improved dyslipidemia, with serum TG, TC, and LDL-C levels reduced by 27.1%, 25.8%, and 25.0%, respectively, in the 100 mg/kg group and by 41.1%, 49.5%, and 42.6%, respectively, in the 200 mg/kg group. PF further reduced adipocyte hypertrophy and increased the expression of the browning-related markers UCP1, PGC-1α, and PRDM16 in inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT). In differentiated 3T3-L1 adipocytes, PF reduced lipid accumulation, enhanced browning-related marker expression, and activated AMPK/SIRT3 signaling, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK attenuated these effects. PF alleviates HFD-induced obesity and associated metabolic abnormalities, accompanied by enhanced iWAT browning and reduced lipid accumulation. These effects may be associated with activation of the AMPK/SIRT3 signaling pathway.

Article.Title: Optimizing Cu content in TiN/Cu Coatings on NiTi for biomedical performance
Article.Authors: Rahimi M.; Kianvash A.; Memar M.; Rezvani M.
Article.Abstract: TiN/Cu composite coatings containing 2.7, 4.1, and 6.8 at% Cu were deposited on NiTi substrates by RF magnetron sputtering to investigate the effect of Cu content on their multifunctional performance. The microstructure, phase composition, hardness, corrosion resistance, ion release, antibacterial activity, bioactivity, and cytocompatibility were systematically evaluated. Increasing Cu content enhanced antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , while a reduction in hardness, corrosion resistance, apatite-forming ability, and cellular response was observed. The coating containing 2.7 at% Cu (S 1 ) exhibited the highest hardness (≈400 HV) and charge-transfer resistance (90.18 kΩ·cm 2 ), indicating superior mechanical and electrochemical performance. All coatings significantly reduced Ni 2 ⁺ release from the NiTi substrate, while Cu 2 ⁺ release remained below the reported cytotoxic level. S 1 also exhibited the most favorable bioactivity, with dense apatite formation and a Ca/P ratio of 1.58. MTT analysis using MG-68 cells showed cell viabilities of 86%, 72%, and 66% for S 1 , S 2 , and S 3 , respectively, consistent with fluorescence microscopy observations. Although S 3 exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, its electrochemical and biological performance decreased. Overall, S 1 provided the most balanced combination of mechanical, electrochemical, bioactive, and cytocompatibility properties, while S 3 showed superior antibacterial performance.

Article.Title: Finite element modeling of cutting forces and surface integrity in milling of GFRP and CFRP composites with acoustic emission monitoring
Article.Authors: Ciecieląg K.; Różyło P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of cutting forces and surface integrity during machining of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites remains challenging because of their heterogeneous architecture, anisotropic behavior and complex damage mechanisms. This study proposes an integrated numerical–experimental framework based on Continuum Shell finite element modelling and Progressive Failure Analysis for predicting the machining performance of woven fabric glass fiber reinforced plastic (GFRP) and woven fabric carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) composites during milling. The proposed approach employs continuum shell elements combined with progressive damage modelling to represent the machining response of composites. The numerical model was validated through milling experiments by comparing the predicted cutting forces and three-dimensional surface topography with experimental measurements. Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring was further employed to characterize the machining process. The results showed that the AE energy generated during CFRP milling was significantly higher than that recorded for GFRP, indicating differences in the acoustic response of the two composite materials during machining. The proposed framework combines continuum shell based numerical modeling, predictive capability and experimental validation, providing a useful tool for analyzing machining performance and surface integrity of FRP composites while demonstrating the potential of acoustic emission for real time monitoring of the machining process.

Article.Title: Spatial pattern variations in AI-generated urban park layouts under retained urban constraints
Article.Authors: Ni B.; Liu C.; Zhang Y.; Shao Z.; Wang P.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: How generated urban park layouts respond to different conditional spatial constraints remains unclear. There are three research gaps in current research: (1) Most studies examine individual spatial elements separately and provide limited comparisons among different retained constraint types; (2) Existing park cases differ in site conditions, making it difficult to compare constraint-related spatial responses under comparable conditions; (3) How combined retained constraints modify the spatial responses associated with individual constraints remains unclear. To address these problems, we construct a constraint-conditioned comparative generative framework for urban park layouts: (1) First, establish a common environmental baseline condition and construct single- and multi-constraint generation conditions by progressively introducing internal roads, building footprints, and water bodies; (2) Secondly, use conditional GANs to generate park layouts under different constraint conditions; (3) Finally, evaluate the generated layouts using 15 Spatial Pattern Indicators and use statistical comparisons and effect-size estimation to characterize spatial responses across constraint conditions. The research results show that: (1) Differences among single-constraint configurations were most pronounced in the connectivity of walkable spaces and landscape pattern, particularly in RCC, ED, and SHEI. (2) Indicator sensitivity varied across constraint types, with some indicators showing limited responses under individual constraints but greater responses under selected combined conditions. (3) Responses to combined constraints depended on the baseline configuration, with some additional constraints producing limited changes under already constrained conditions.

Article.Title: When do e-commerce prediction models fail over time? cross-task evidence on temporal reliability and model maintenance
Article.Authors: Lan Z.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Machine-learning models in e-commerce are often evaluated on randomly partitioned historical data, whereas deployment requires prediction on future observations under changing populations and information availability. We examine temporal reliability and model maintenance across four public dataset–task settings: late-delivery prediction among eventually delivered Olist orders, matched 24-h cart-to-purchase prediction in Retailrocket and Synerise RecSys 2025, and 30-day repeat-purchase prediction in Online Retail II. Sequential analyses restrict historical features, model updating, and recalibration to information and labels available at each prediction or deployment time. Random-to-future differences varied substantially: Olist showed pronounced deterioration, whereas the other settings showed smaller or qualitatively different changes. In the primary Olist XGBoost analysis, cumulative retraining improved ranking and modestly improved Brier accuracy, while sliding-window retraining improved ranking but worsened probability reliability. Cross-model, matched-exposure, and sensitivity analyses showed that maintenance effects depended on setting, period, model family, and design. Post-hoc recalibration did not provide a consistently reliable repair, and same-base calibration effects differed from net maintenance-policy effects. The matched comparisons do not identify causal task or duration effects. These findings support forward-in-time evaluation that assesses ranking, probability quality, label availability, and maintenance effects separately rather than inferring future reliability from offline performance or task identity.

Article.Title: Prenatal, perinatal, and neonatal factors associated with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a case-control study in Iranian children and adolescents
Article.Authors: Eslamiyeh H.; Emarati A.; Karimi M.; Karimi N.; Akbarian E.
Article.Abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder with multifactorial origins. Evidence regarding early-life risk factors from Middle Eastern populations is limited. This case-control study examined demographic, parental, prenatal, perinatal, and neonatal factors associated with ADHD among Iranian children and adolescents. A total of 247 children aged 6–15 years (123 ADHD cases and 124 controls) were recruited from pediatric neurology and psychiatry clinics in Yazd, Iran, between 2015 and 2023. Data were collected via structured maternal interviews supplemented by medical records. Multivariable binary logistic regression using a parsimonious, pre-specified set of ten covariates was performed to identify independent correlates. Neonatal jaundice requiring hospitalization showed the strongest independent association with ADHD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.37, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.00–9.52; p < 0.001). Term birth (aOR 3.01, 95% CI 1.26–7.15; p = 0.013) and male sex (aOR 1.84, 95% CI 1.03–3.29; p = 0.040) were also independently associated with higher odds, while NICU admission showed an inverse association (aOR 0.37, 95% CI 0.16–0.86; p = 0.022) that should not be interpreted as a protective effect. Lower paternal educational attainment showed a borderline association (aOR 1.80, 95% CI 0.99–3.26; p = 0.054). ADHD subtype (inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, or combined presentation) was incompletely documented and could not be analyzed. These preliminary findings from a single-center, clinic-based sample in Yazd, Iran are consistent with a multifactorial etiology of ADHD; the term-birth and NICU findings in particular should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger, population-based studies across multiple settings are needed to confirm these associations, assess their generalizability, and explore causal pathways.

Article.Title: Evaporation and kinetic characteristics of soybean oil-ethanol secondary droplets during micro-explosion
Article.Authors: Zhang W.; Meng K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soybean oil is one of the important sources of sustainable aviation fuel, and the study of soybean oil mixed with ethanol can provide important data support for the development and utilization of soybean oil. In this experiment, the evaporation, micro-explosion and the number and distribution characteristics of four kinds of mixed fuel droplets made of soybean oil and ethanol under different temperatures were studied by controlling the nitrogen flow rate (7.9 L/min) and the oxygen flow rate (2.1 L/min) to simulate the air atmosphere by using the test platform of micro-explosion characteristics of mixed fuel and the moving droplet tracking technology. No combustion occurred during the experiment. It took 10 ms, 1ms, 5ms and 1ms for S80E20, S70E30, S60E40 and S50E50 droplets to expand from the beginning to fully form secondary droplets, respectively. The evaporation rate of droplets is mainly affected by the temperature and micro-explosion intensity of two factors. The S80E20 droplet was distorted repeatedly before micro-explosion, and the secondary droplet distortion formula was established. Through calculation, it was found that the maximum distortion of S80E20 droplet before micro-explosion had exceeded 0.7, and the secondary droplet distortion produced after micro-explosion of S80E20 droplet was all above 0.05, with the maximum value exceeding 0.25.

Article.Title: Concentration variations and risk characteristics of volatile organic compounds and nitrochlorobenzenes in groundwater at a retired pesticide site under risk control
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Du J.; Li J.; Yang L.; Sun L.; Li W.; Peng L.; Meng W.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Retired pesticide sites are an important category of contaminated land, and groundwater pollution at these sites remains a major environmental concern. Understanding groundwater pollution characteristics and the effectiveness of containment measures is essential for site management and safe reuse. This study investigated a retired pesticide site under risk control in Jiangsu Province, China to characterize the spatio-temporal distribution patterns, source relationships, and ecological and human health risks of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and nitrochlorobenzenes (NCBs) in groundwater from 2019 to 2021. The results showed that chlorobenzene (CB) and NCBs were the dominant pollutants. Spatial distribution of pollutants exhibited marked heterogeneity, with two distinct contamination hotspots identified. Historical storage and handling facilities in the southern part of the site suggest potential localized sources of contamination. Time-series monitoring showed that groundwater pollutant concentrations fluctuated but declined overall after containment implementation. In particular, the mean concentration of ΣNCBs decreased sharply from 6846 μg/L in 2019 to 1025 μg/L in 2020, with a slight rebound to 1109 μg/L in 2021, indicating that the containment measures effectively reduced pollutant migration and the overall contamination level. Risk assessment results indicated that the target compounds posed high ecological (RQ T range: 140 ~ 219) and human health risks under conservative generic exposure scenarios, with CR T ranging from 2.80 × 10 –5 to 1.77 × 10 –1 and HQ T ranging from 5.15 × 10 –1 to 5.08 × 10 3 (i.e., 0.515 ~ 5080). However, site-specific actual risk evaluation under industrial land use showed that the groundwater risk outside the controlled zone was generally acceptable. These findings provide a scientific basis for evaluating risk-control effectiveness, supporting dynamic management, and informing safe land-reuse decisions for pesticide-contaminated sites.

Article.Title: Comparative effectiveness of aerobic, resistance, and combined exercise interventions for obesity management: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Alhammad A.; Alfayyadh A.; Alanazi S.; Almulhim L.; Alghadier M.; Osailan A.; Muteesasira E.
Article.Abstract: Obesity is a critical global public health challenge characterized by an excess accumulation of body fat that severely compromises systemic health. Although the therapeutic efficacy of exercise on individual body composition parameters varies, structured physical activity is universally recommended as a foundational, non-pharmacological strategy for long-term weight mitigation and cardiometabolic risk reduction. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the comparative effectiveness of structured exercise interventions on absolute body weight, body mass index (BMI), body fat percentage (BFP), waist circumference (WC), and absolute fat mass in adults with overweight or obesity. A comprehensive, systematic search was conducted across 4 major electronic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and CENTRAL) in strict accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. Parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) meeting pre-specified PICO criteria were included. Quantitative data synthesis was executed using a random-effects model to calculate pooled Mean Differences (MD) and 95% Confidence Intervals (CI). Between-study variance was estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML); Hartung-Knapp-adjusted CIs and 95% prediction intervals were added as sensitivity analyses. Methodological quality was independently evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and the absolute certainty of the generated evidence was appraised via the GRADE framework, with detailed modality-specific subgroup analyses. Twenty RCTs involving 1,504 participants (946 in exercise groups and 558 in control groups) met the eligibility criteria. The number of studies contributing data varied across individual meta-analyses: 20 RCTs evaluated absolute body weight, 18 evaluated BFP, 7 evaluated BMI, 2 evaluated WC, and 2 evaluated absolute fat mass. Structured exercise interventions were associated with statistically significant reductions in absolute body weight (MD = − 2.53 kg, 95% CI −3.69 to − 1.37; Moderate certainty), BFP (MD = − 2.60%, 95% CI −3.72 to − 1.47; Moderate certainty), and BMI (MD = − 0.97 kg/m², 95% CI −1.88 to − 0.06; Hartung-Knapp 95% CI −2.11 to 0.17; Low certainty). Conversely, pooled reductions in WC (MD = − 1.93 cm, 95% CI −5.49 to 1.63; Very low certainty) and absolute fat mass (MD = − 2.12 kg, 95% CI −6.09 to 1.84; Very low certainty) were not statistically significant. Modality-specific subgroup analyses demonstrated significant anthropometric improvements following aerobic exercise (AE) and combined training (CT) regimens, whereas resistance training (RT) exhibited non-significant trends. Formal testing for subgroup interactions revealed no statistically significant differences between the competing exercise modalities. The body weight and BFP estimates remained statistically significant after Hartung-Knapp adjustment, whereas the BMI estimate and the aerobic-exercise subgroup effect on body weight did not. Among adults with overweight or obesity, structured exercise interventions drive statistically significant reductions in absolute body weight and body fat percentage with moderate certainty, alongside smaller BMI reductions carrying low certainty that were not robust to Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Evidence remains insufficient and carries very low certainty regarding distinct impacts on absolute fat mass and waist circumference. These findings support the clinical integration of structured exercise not as a standalone treatment, but as a foundational adjunct to dietary and behavioral interventions to optimize cardiometabolic management. Article.Title: Design and testing of a rotating airflow-type banana fiber impurity removal device
Article.Authors: Zeng W.; Fu W.; Liang D.; Liu J.; Yu S.; Yang Z.
Article.Abstract: Banana stem fiber has broad application prospects, but mechanical extraction suffers from significant fiber damage and incomplete separation of impurities. To address this, this paper presents the design of a rotating airflow impurity removal device that applies gentle impact to composted and kneaded banana stem material using periodic rotating airflow. This approach effectively separates impurities such as pectin while significantly reducing mechanical damage to the fiber. Based on critical velocity analysis and mathematical modeling, the airflow velocity range, nozzle motion trajectory, and airflow velocity distribution were determined. CFD numerical simulation was used to perform dynamic flow field simulations of the rotating airflow components and CFD-DEM fluid-structure interaction analysis. Parameter optimization was conducted using a Box-Behnken experimental design, with cylinder rotation speed, airflow velocity, and conveyor speed as influencing factors. Under the optimized conditions of cylinder rotation speed 33 rpm, nozzle outlet airflow velocity 15 m/s, and conveyor speed 0.3 m/s, the fiber extraction rate reached 89.35%, the fiber impurity content was only 5.09%, and the fiber integrity rate was 84.41%. This study validated the feasibility of using rotating airflow impurity removal technology for low-damage purification of banana stem fiber, providing a new solution and a basis for equipment R&D for processing of various agricultural bast fiber raw materials.

Article.Title: Causal reliability-gated GRU sensor reconstruction for a reduced-order floating offshore wind turbine under false-data injection
Article.Authors: Abbas N.; Hao L.; Ayoubi M.; Bano N.; Rehman S.
Article.Abstract: Sensor reconstruction under false-data injection (FDI) is investigated on a control-oriented, reduced-order nonlinear floating offshore wind turbine inspired by the NREL 5-MW rated scale. The model combines empirical aerodynamic maps, surge–pitch platform dynamics, a single-mass drivetrain and constrained actuators. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) predicts six sensor outputs causally from trusted environmental inputs and previously applied commands. Distinct trajectories are used for training, validation, detector calibration and testing. Offline prediction-confidence weights blend received measurements and predictions after channel-wise residual detection; global detection and full-replacement variants are compared. Across 27 held-out attack/noise scenarios, channel-gated compensation reduces the dimensionless sensor-error metric by 19.02% with a mean paired rotor-speed RMSE reduction of -0.15% relative to the unprotected benchmark. Scenario reductions range from -4.04% to +6.46%, with improvement in 11 of 27 cases; near-zero mean change does not imply scenario-wise performance preservation. Channel improvements range from -3.28% for power to 78.65% for generator torque in the base condition. Reliability gating yields lower rotor-speed RMSE than full replacement in 22 of 27 matched comparisons, but superiority over fixed partial replacement or independent predictors is not established. Single-channel tests reveal limited rotor-speed attack detection: recall is 4.42% for a rotor-speed-only attack, and the clean rotor-speed false-alarm rate is 12.48%. Reliable feedback-channel protection and guaranteed post-attack recovery are not established. Vector error identities, a conditional mean-square benchmark, controller-command sensitivity, and a finite-horizon perturbation bound explain the relationship between reconstruction and regulation. The study establishes a reproducible evaluation framework for reconstruction and controller-aware assessment; its internal ablations do not separately establish advantages of the GRU architecture and the confidence-weighting rule.

Article.Title: Dimethyltryptamine improves early graft hemodynamic performance in a heterotopic rat heart transplantation model
Article.Authors: Csonka M.; Damenija G.; Stengl R.; Bálint T.; Nagy D.; Budai A.; Erőss B.; Șulea C.; Frecska E.; Merkely B.; Szabó G.; Radovits T.; Nardai S.; Benke K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Preserving donor organ viability during cold storage is critical for successful heart transplantation, as ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI) adversely affects graft function. N, N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT), an endogenous sigma-1 receptor ligand, has demonstrated cytoprotective effects under hypoxic and oxidative stress. This study evaluated the effects of DMT on graft recovery in a rat model of heterotopic heart transplantation. Hearts from male Lewis rats were preserved for 1 h at 4 °C in either Custodiol solution or Custodiol supplemented with DMT. Both donors and recipients in the treatment group also received DMT. After transplantation, graft function was assessed 60 min into reperfusion using preload-dependent pressure measurements, complemented by molecular and histological evaluations. DMT-treated grafts exhibited higher left ventricular systolic pressure, enhanced myocardial contractility and improved diastolic relaxation compared with controls. Gene expression analysis revealed significant modulation of Ddit3 , Hif1a and Vldlr , with trends in apoptotic and metabolic markers. A strong trend toward increased cleaved caspase-3 expression and significantly higher p62 immunohistochemical scores were observed, whereas cardiac troponin I and TNF-α levels remained unchanged. Overall, these findings indicate that DMT treatment improves early post-transplant graft contractile performance under the experimental conditions tested. The mechanisms underlying the observed functional improvement remain to be further elucidated.
