Article.Title: Serum proteomics in newborns reveals a multi-pathway molecular panel for neonatal sepsis, encompassing pathogen sensing, leukocyte recruitment, and endothelial injury
Article.Authors: Roger K.; Coly N.; Metatla I.; Agne F.; Basse I.; Gueye P.; Chhuon C.; Guerrera I.
Article.Abstract: Neonatal sepsis is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Senegal, where incidence is 78–104 per 1000 live births and mortality exceeds 20 per 1000, with case fatality rates around 36%. Diagnosis is difficult due to non-specific clinical signs and lack of molecular biomarkers, highlighting the need for improved early diagnostic molecular panel that could be applied even outside hospital settings. Our aims are to ompare neonatal and adult serum proteomes to establish a reference and to identify serum protein biomarkers of neonatal sepsis. Serum samples from Senegalese neonates and adults were analyzed using data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics on neat serum (Evosep-timsTOF HT platform). The cohort comprised 22 neonates with confirmed sepsis (CS), 6 neonates with non-confirmed sepsis (NCS), 17 healthy newborn controls (HC), 6 unclassified, 9 outliers and 20 healthy adults. Downstream analyses included differential protein abundance testing, unsupervised clustering, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and correlation analyses with clinical parameters. We identified 979 ± 20 proteins in newborns versus 718 ± 40 in adults. Newborns showed reduced immune-response related proteins, a narrower dynamic range, and increased structural proteins such as collagens, consistent with immune immaturity and tissue development. Unsupervised WGCNA analysis led to a 53-protein cluster discriminated CS from NCS/HC. Some of these dysregulated proteins identified have already been reported in independent studies using different approaches in neonatal and/or adult sepsis. Our larger panel however of identified markers maps to three major biological processes involved in sepsis: (i) pathogen sensing (LBP, CD14), and acute-phase inflammation (e.g. CRP, SAA1/2, ORM1/2); (ii) innate immune activation and leukocyte recruitment (e.g., FCGR3A, CSF1R, CD163, CD206) and final platelet exhaustion, (e.g., PF4, PPBP, THBS1, GP5); (iii) endothelial injury and microvascular dysfunction with tissue remodeling (e.g., ICAM1, VCAM1, VWF, SPARC) with simultaneous loss of protective lipoproteins and serpins (e.g., APOA1, APOA2, APOM, SERPINA4, SERPINA5). This study provides a very comprehensive neonatal serum proteome characterization and identifies a protein panel of proteins mapped to three major processes in sepsis.

Article.Title: GC–MS metabolite profiling, elemental composition, and molecular docking analysis of camel milk extracts: insights into antioxidant and antibacterial activities
Article.Authors: Nigussie G.; Zaib S.; Dekebo A.; Abebe M.; Tegegn M.; Zegeye A.; Meressa A.; Negassa T.; Woldemariam M.; Hunsen M.; Endale M.; Chanyalew M.
Article.Abstract: Despite its rich nutritional value and diverse therapeutic properties, camel milk remains poorly studied in Ethiopia. Therefore, this study investigated the chemical profile, elemental composition, ATR-FTIR characteristics, antioxidant and antibacterial activities, and molecular docking interactions of lyophilized camel milk extracts. GC–MS metabolite profiling of camel milk revealed solvent-dependent variations in chemical composition, with cholesterol (32.4–40.92%), palmitic acid (24.53–30.91%), and stearic acid (12.69–18.84%) as the major constituents of the n -hexane, chloroform, and ethyl acetate extracts, whereas the methanol extract was enriched in palmitoleic acid (40.22%), elaidic acid (27.38%), and heptadecanoic acid (14.59%). The DPPH radical scavenging assay revealed strong antioxidant activity for the methanol extract (IC 50 = 3.54 µg/mL) and lyophilized camel milk (IC 50 = 2.33 µg/mL), showing activities comparable to ascorbic acid (IC 50 = 1.25 µg/mL). The n -hexane and CHCl 3 extracts exhibited the highest antibacterial activity against Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus with MIC values of 2.5 mg/mL, whereas the methanol extract and crude lyophilized camel milk were most active against Escherichia coli at the same MIC value. ATR-FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates in lyophilized camel milk, indicating preservation of major bioactive constituents after lyophilization. Elemental analysis using MP-AES revealed the presence of essential macro- and microelements with varying concentrations. Potassium (2237.45 ± 22.10 mg/L) was the most abundant element, followed by calcium (1507.71 ± 26.54 mg/L), phosphorus (757.09 ± 28.02 mg/L), and sodium (714.80 ± 3.19 mg/L). Toxic heavy metals, including Pb, Cd, Cr, Ni, Co, and Mo, were below detectable limits. Molecular docking analysis showed that major camel milk phytochemicals exhibited notable binding affinities against key targets. Palmitoleic acid showed slightly higher predicted binding affinity (− 4.3 kcal/mol) than ascorbic acid (− 4.2 kcal/mol) against Human Peroxiredoxin 5 (PDB ID: 1HD2). Cholesterol demonstrated a strongest predictable binding affinity against S. aureus topoisomerase IV subunit A (− 7.1 kcal/mol; PDB ID: 2INR) and L. monocytogenes InlA protein (− 8.8 kcal/mol; PDB ID: 1O6T), with higher affinity than ciprofloxacin. These findings suggest that camel milk is a promising source of bioactive compounds, and the analyzed milk samples are safe for consumption due to the absence of harmful heavy metals.

Article.Title: Depth of penetration prediction in atmospheric and submerged abrasive water jet machining of Nimonic-90 using hybrid cohort intelligence modelling
Article.Authors: G D.; Jambagi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the influence of machining environment—atmospheric versus submerged—on the performance of Abrasive Water Jet Machining (AWJM) of Nimonic-90, focusing on depth of penetration (DOP) and surface quality. Experiments were conducted using a Taguchi L27 design considering water pressure (WP), traverse speed (TS), abrasive flow rate (AFR), and stand-off distance (SOD) as control parameters. Atmospheric machining achieved a maximum DOP of $$37.46 \pm 3.01$$ ​ mm at 275 MPa, whereas submerged machining produced smoother surfaces ( $$R_a = 1.91$$ – $$4.45\,\upmu $$ m) due to the damping effect of the surrounding water medium. TS was identified as the most influential parameter ( $$\Delta = 6.36$$ ), with an increase from 50 to 150 mm/min reducing DOP by approximately 54.6%. The optimal parameter combination for maximum DOP was WP = 275 MPa, TS = 50 mm/min, AFR = 300 g/min, and SOD = 2 mm. The Hybrid Cohort Intelligence (HCI) model incorporating polynomial regression demonstrated strong predictive capability, achieving $$R^{2} = 0.9812$$ and MSE = 1.106 for AWJM, and $$R^{2} = 0.9900$$ and MSE = 0.520 for Submerged Abrasive Water Jet Machining (SAWJM). Overall, atmospheric AWJM is suitable for higher material removal, while SAWJM provides superior surface integrity, offering a useful framework for process optimisation of Nimonic-90 within the investigated parameter range.

Article.Title: Live reptile imports into Republic of Korea and their implications for conservation and global health
Article.Authors: Hwang J.; Jeon S.; Kim Y.; Jung H.; Yoo J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The international reptile trade has expanded significantly, raising global concerns regarding biodiversity and biosecurity. We analyzed 14 months of national reptile quarantine data ( n = 164,139 individuals) from South Korea, integrating trade records with a global environmental risk index for emerging infectious diseases (EID). While the USA and China accounted for 52.8% of total import volume, the majority of top 10 exporting countries—both by total and CITES-listed import volume—were nations from biodiversity hotspots in Southeast Asia and Africa. These nations were primary exporters of non-captive individuals, comprising 100% of CITES-listed exports from Madagascar and Togo and 87.0% from Indonesia. A statistically significant positive correlation between EID risk index values and non-captive sourcing among major exporters ( r = 0.66, p = 0.038) indicates that high-pathogen-risk regions tend to rely on extractive harvesting. The non-CITES category comprised 73.8% of total imports and included 15 IUCN-threatened species, highlighting a significant conservation blind spot. Moreover, 73.2% of imported species were sourced exclusively from a single country, indicating concentrated harvesting pressure on specific wild populations. Our findings provide an empirical basis for risk-prioritized monitoring strategies focusing on high-risk trade routes, and underscore the need for global data-sharing frameworks to address converging risks of wildlife exploitation and EID threatening One Health.

Article.Title: Temporal deep learning and multitask learning offer no advantage over tree ensembles for early warning of student course outcomes
Article.Authors: Qin H.; Zhang C.; Qi L.
Article.Abstract: We ask whether either temporal deep learning or multi-task learning improves early-warning prediction of pass/fail and withdrawal from virtual learning environment (VLE) logs, and find that neither does. Using 14-day interaction sequences from the first weeks of enrollment for 22,848 Open University students, we compare single-task and multi-task BiLSTM architectures, a GRU variant, and four tabular baselines across 10 runs, evaluating differences with equivalence testing rather than significance testing alone. All eight models fell within a narrow F1 band (0.574–0.583): the recurrent networks did not outperform well-tuned gradient-boosted trees, and on the academic task the single-task, hard-sharing, and cross-attention variants were statistically equivalent within a two-point bound, a result that also held under student-level bootstrap resampling. Multi-task sharing conferred no advantage despite moderate task correlation ( r = 0.589), and this null result was robust to excluding withdrawn students. The contribution is a boundary condition for multi-task and deep sequence models in educational data mining: when the predictive signal in early click logs is limited, task correlation does not translate into transfer, and added model capacity does not translate into accuracy. Predictive information was instead governed by the behavioral features measured, chiefly cumulative and rolling engagement, pointing practitioners toward simpler, interpretable models and richer signals rather than more complex architectures.

Article.Title: Evolutionary game driven adaptive sliding mode control for high-reliability PMSM Systems with d–q axis cooperative strategy under electrical parameter perturbation
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Li W.; Lv T.; Song D.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) in high-power-density applications face simultaneous perturbation of stator resistance, d- and q-axis inductances and rotor flux linkage due to temperature rise, magnetic saturation and demagnetisation. Existing adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC) schemes treat the d-axis and q-axis current loops independently, leaving cross-axis coupling unaddressed and causing conservative gain selection, chattering and current ripple. We propose an evolutionary game driven adaptive sliding mode control (EG-ASMC) framework that recasts the two current loops as cooperating populations in an evolutionary game. Controller gains evolve online via a replicator dynamic whose fitness function couples tracking error, cross-axis coupling residual and torque smoothness. We prove that the cooperative game admits a unique evolutionary stable strategy coinciding with the Pareto-efficient gain pair, that the closed-loop system reaches the sliding manifold in fixed time with uniformly ultimately bounded tracking under simultaneous parameter perturbation, and that cooperative tuning attenuates chattering by a factor scaling with the cross-axis coupling strength. A finite-time disturbance observer is co-designed with its residual embedded into the game payoff. Monte Carlo simulations under five perturbation scenarios show that EG-ASMC reduces q-axis tracking RMSE by 41.6%, torque ripple by 36.7% and chattering index by 50.9% relative to non-singular fast terminal SMC. Hardware-in-the-loop verification on a 7.5 kW interior PMSM platform confirms real-time feasibility at 10 kHz. The per-cycle computational overhead of the replicator dynamic is approximately 7 microseconds, enabling deployment on cost-constrained embedded processors.

Article.Authors: Alabdullah A.; Kosik O.; Leverington-Waite M.; Mitchell R.; Prins A.; Brett J.; Griffiths S.; Shewry P.; Lovegrove A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dietary fibre intake remains below recommended levels, and increasing fibre content of widely consumed white wheat flour (derived from the starchy endosperm) represents a scalable strategy to improve public health. In wheat starchy endosperm, arabinoxylan (AX) is the dominant fibre component, with the water-extractable (WE) fraction being particularly beneficial to health. We assembled an Elite Fibre Panel (EFP) of 384 elite modern wheat genotypes from ​Western European commercial breeding programmes and quantified the content of WE-AX in wholemeal, as a proxy for soluble AX in white flour, across two UK field environments. Wholemeal WE-AX, showed substantial quantitative variation, with an approximate broad-sense heritability of 0.67 on a genotype-mean basis and a moderate positive correlation between sites (r = 0.51). Genome-wide association analyses using 6,791 Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) identified seven loci associated with WE-AX content. The strongest and most stable effects were mapped to major loci on chromosomes 1B and 6B, previously implicated in AX regulation, while additional loci of smaller and sometimes environment-dependent effect were detected on chromosomes 3A, 5B, and 7A. The favourable alleles were associated with higher WE-AX content, and genotypes carrying more favourable alleles generally had higher mean WE-AX. Linkage disequilibrium (LD)-defined intervals contained PER1, which has published functional evidence for a role in AX cross-linking, and putative candidates annotated as UTP-glucose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase, trichome birefringence-like proteins and xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolases. Their annotations and developmental expression profiles support prioritisation for functional investigation. These findings highlight favourable alleles already segregating within elite germplasm as potential targets for breeding wheat with enhanced soluble dietary fibre content and improved nutritional quality.

Article.Title: Spatial coherence and input uncertainty in AutoML-tuned gradient-boosting predictions of depth to groundwater as an indicator of groundwater potential
Article.Authors: Shehab Z.; Faisal R.; Al-Ansari N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Groundwater in the semi-arid Zagros foreland of northern Iraq is being withdrawn faster than it is replenished, and identifying where groundwater is most accessible is a precondition for managing that deficit. This study maps groundwater potential in the Karma Soor basin, Kurdistan Region, and compares three gradient-boosted ensemble learners, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost, tuned under identical settings with the Train Using AutoML tool in ArcGIS Pro. Depth to groundwater served as the response variable, interpreted as an indicator of groundwater accessibility rather than of recharge, and twelve conditioning factors spanning the topographic, hydrological, geological, pedological and land-cover domains served as predictors. Under a random hold-out, XGBoost returned the lowest errors (MAE 5.21 m, RMSE 7.90 m, R² 0.905), but the bootstrap confidence intervals of the three models overlapped widely, and under four-fold spatial block cross-validation CatBoost generalized best (RMSE 6.89 m); the three models are therefore broadly comparable, with their ranking dependent on the validation design. Stream order dominated both impurity-based (38.62%) and SHAP importance, acting largely as a proxy for topographic position, whereas removing rainfall did not reduce accuracy. Perturbing the predicted surface by ± 5%, ± 10% and ± 20% across one hundred simulations and re-running the hot-spot analysis left 90.25%, 80.16% and 66.12% of the basin in its original category. Instability grew sub-linearly and concentrated at cluster margins, and it consisted mainly of shifts between adjacent confidence levels (e.g., from 95% to 90% hot spot) rather than jumps between hot-spot and cold-spot categories, while the cores of the high-potential channel corridors remained stable. By evaluating spatial generalization, spatial coherence and stability alongside conventional accuracy, the study shows that hold-out error statistics alone are an insufficient basis for selecting a groundwater potential model.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based diabetes risk classification using clinical and lifestyle indicators
Article.Authors: Kadir D.; Khudhur A.; Taher H.; karim S.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a major global health challenge associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. This study presents an internally validated machine-learning framework for multiclass classification of current diabetes-risk strata using concurrent clinical and lifestyle indicators. The dataset comprised 825 observations with nine predictors: age, gender, body mass index (BMI), systolic and diastolic blood pressure, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting blood sugar (FBS), physical activity level, and family history of diabetes. Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers were evaluated using an 80:20 stratified train-test split, stratified ten-fold cross-validation, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Model differences were assessed using the Friedman test followed by Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons. XGBoost achieved the highest internal test performance, with an accuracy of 98.18%, precision of 98.22%, recall of 98.18%, F1-score of 98.18%, and ROC-AUC of 0.99970. Cross-validation showed stable internal performance, and the Friedman test indicated an overall difference among classifiers (χ² = 10.1786, p = 0.0171), although Holm-adjusted comparisons showed that XGBoost differed significantly from SVM but not from RF or MLP. Global feature-importance analysis identified FBS, systolic blood pressure, BMI, and HbA1c as the most influential predictors within the fitted models. Because the study used a modest, single-center cohort and did not include external validation, the findings should be interpreted as proof-of-concept evidence for classifying existing, source-defined diabetes-risk strata rather than predicting future diabetes onset or establishing clinical readiness. Independent multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

Article.Title: A spectral-domain multi-strategy Fourier transform optimizer for numerical optimization and robot path planning
Article.Authors: Lan S.; Xiang J.; Yang G.; Ye H.; Shi H.; Niu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Fourier Transform Optimizer (FTO) provides a frequency-domain search framework for metaheuristic optimization, but its original spectral operations do not explicitly consider spectral-energy distribution, amplitude–phase-aware information exchange, or multi-resolution spectral manipulation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Spectral-Domain Multi-Strategy Fourier Transform Optimizer, termed MIFTO. Three complementary mechanisms are introduced. First, Spectral Energy Redistribution (SER) adaptively regulates the relative contribution of spectral components through normalized spectral energy and bounded energy redistribution. Second, Cross-Spectral Alignment (CSA) performs phase-reference-preserving cross-individual spectral recombination while maintaining the conjugate symmetry required for real-valued reconstruction. Third, Multi-Resolution Spectral Search (MRSS) partitions the spectrum into low-, middle-, and high-order subspaces and applies differentiated update mechanisms at different spectral resolutions. The proposed method is evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark suite at 30 and 50 dimensions and the CEC2022 suite at 10 and 20 dimensions against eleven representative optimization algorithms. Convergence analysis, statistical distributions, population diversity, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Friedman mean-rank analysis, ablation experiments, and computational-cost analysis are conducted. The results show that MIFTO achieves favorable optimization accuracy and robustness on the majority of the investigated benchmark functions. MIFTO is further applied to robot path planning in 20 × 20, 40 × 40, and 60 × 60 static grid environments. The corresponding mean path lengths are 28.4494, 60.2801, and 107.5165, respectively, and MIFTO obtains the first Friedman rank in all three scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of restructuring the internal spectral search process of FTO and indicate the potential of MIFTO for numerical and constrained path-planning problems.

Article.Title: Circulating exosomal miR-34 and miR-122 as promising biomarkers of metabolic dysfunction and insulin resistance in type 2 diabetic patients coexisting with hypothyroidism
Article.Authors: Al-Khaleeli A.; Tabandeh M.; Borujeni M.; Mohammadtaghvaei N.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hypothyroidism frequently coexist; however, their combined impact on metabolic and hepatic dysfunction remains incompletely understood. Circulating exosomes and their miRNA cargo have emerged as potential molecular biomarkers reflecting disease associated metabolic alterations. This study aimed to isolate and characterize circulating exosomes and profile exosomal miR-34a and miR-122 in T2DM patients with clinical and subclinical hypothyroidism to evaluate their potential association with insulin resistance, metabolic dysfunction, and hepatic injury related alterations. A total of 143 participants were enrolled: healthy controls (n = 40), T2DM alone (n = 40), T2DM with subclinical hypothyroidism (SC-Hypo, n = 32), and T2DM with clinical hypothyroidism (C-Hypo, n = 31). Exosomes were isolated from serum and characterized by DLS, TEM, and Western blot for exosomal (CD9, CD81). Exosomal miR-34 and miR-122 were quantified by qRT-PCR. Biochemical parameters, insulin resistance markers and thyroid hormones were measured, and ROC analysis evaluated diagnostic performance. Isolated exosomes exhibited typical cup-shaped morphology (100–250 nm) and expressed CD9/CD81. Biochemical parameters (fasting glucose, insulin, TyG Index, HOMA-IR, GGT, AST, ALT, ALP) showed significant stepwise deterioration across groups. Exosomal miR-34 and miR-122 were significantly upregulated in all disease groups, with the highest levels in T2DM + C-Hypo patients. Notably, even SC-Hypo patients showed marked elevation compared to T2DM alone. ROC analysis revealed perfect diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 1.0) with 100% sensitivity and specificity for both miRNAs. Cutoff values for SC-Hypo vs. controls were 1.75 (miR-34) and 1.95 (miR-122); for C-Hypo vs. controls, cutoffs were 1.81 (miR-34) and 2.77 (miR-122). Circulating exosomes and their miRNA cargo—particularly miR-34 and miR-122—are progressively dysregulated in T2DM patients with hypothyroidism. Critically, even subclinical hypothyroidism contributes significantly to this pathological signature, with both miRNAs showing elevation beyond T2DM alone. The perfect diagnostic performance of exosomal miR-34 and miR-122 positions them as leading candidates for early detection and monitoring of metabolic dysfunctions in this high-risk population, highlighting the importance of recognizing subclinical hypothyroidism in T2DM management.

Article.Title: A deep learning framework for label-free prostate tissue classification using two-photon imaging
Article.Authors: Makkithaya K.; Rodrigues J.; Raju G.; Lewis M.; Chen M.; Yeh Y.; Tsay G.; Chang N.; Mazumder N.; Zhuo G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prostate cancer remains one of the most prevalent malignancies among men worldwide, and accurate differentiation between malignant and benign tissue continues to pose diagnostic challenges, particularly when relying solely on conventional histopathology. In this study, we present a label‑free, high‑resolution imaging and machine learning pipeline for prostate tissue classification using two‑photon microscopy and tissue microarray (TMA) samples. Two-photon fluorescence (TPF) images were analyzed from a quality-screened dataset comprising 295 images (146 normal and 149 tumor) representing 135 tissue sample groups (71 normal and 64 tumor). Three approaches were investigated: (a) handcrafted texture descriptors derived from gray-level co-occurrence matrices (GLCM) classified using logistic regression; (b) MobileNetV3-Small-based deep learning architectures comprising a Global Feature Network (GFN), Global–Local Feature Network (GLFN), and Global–Local Ensemble Network (GLEN); and (c) principal component analysis (PCA)-based variants of these deep learning architectures. Model performance was assessed using group-disjoint five-fold cross-validation. Sample-group-level analysis identified lower homogeneity, energy, and angular second moment in tumor tissues after Bonferroni correction for six feature comparisons. The GLCM-based classifier achieved an accuracy of 71.86% and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.766. In comparison, GFN, GLFN, and GLEN achieved accuracies of 85.42%, 82.71%, and 86.10%, respectively. GLEN demonstrated an AUC of approximately 0.914, with normal and tumor recall values of 84.25% and 87.92%, respectively. Incorporating PCA preserved the classification accuracy of GLEN at 86.10%, suggesting that dimensionality reduction can retain discriminative information within deep feature representations. Overall, the findings demonstrate the potential of combining label-free TPF microscopy with global-local deep learning representations for automated prostate tissue classification. Nevertheless, further evaluation using larger, independent cohorts and verified patient-level validation is necessary to establish generalizability and clinical applicability.

Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning identifies patients at risk for persistent influenza A nucleic-acid positivity
Article.Authors: Zhao H.; Jing R.; Xu J.; Li J.; Li X.; Xu X.; Ding Q.; Zhuang Z.; Yu Y.; Tang L.
Article.Abstract: A considerable proportion of patients with influenza A remain nucleic-acid positive after a standard course of antiviral therapy, but tools for identifying them at admission are lacking. We developed an interpretable machine-learning model for early risk prediction. This retrospective study included 432 hospitalised adults with laboratory-confirmed influenza A, randomly allocated by stratified random sampling on the outcome to a training cohort ( n = 346) and a validation cohort ( n = 86). Persistent positivity was defined as a positive respiratory nucleic-acid test within 72 h after completion of a standard course of antiviral therapy. Predictors were selected by elastic-net penalised logistic regression. Seven algorithms were evaluated using nested cross-validation with stratified ten-fold cross-validation repeated five times and stratified ten-fold randomised search for tuning. Discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis and SHAP-based interpretability were assessed. Persistent positivity occurred in 29.5% and 29.1% of the training and validation cohorts, respectively. XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination, with nested cross-validated ROC-AUC 0.793 (95% CI 0.748–0.835) and PR-AUC 0.600 (95% CI 0.530–0.676) in the training cohort, ROC-AUC 0.835 (95% CI 0.734–0.914) and PR-AUC 0.714 (95% CI 0.573–0.851) in the validation cohort. At a pre-specified decision threshold, validation sensitivity was 0.800, specificity 0.656 and negative predictive value 0.889. SHAP analysis identified C-reactive protein as the dominant predictor, followed by lymphocyte count, age, vomit, aspartate aminotransferase, urea, and kidney disease. The interpretable XGBoost model showed promising predictive performance and may support early risk stratification and targeted follow-up. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Early smoking-related lung function changes in biochemically verified current, former, and never smokers
Article.Authors: Spicuzza L.; Caratozzolo D.; Belsey J.; Nadir M.; John I.; Pennisi F.; Campagna D.; Anastasi E.; Geraci G.; Pluym N.; Sherer M.; Dass N.; Polosa R.
Article.Abstract: Conventional spirometry is relatively insensitive to early subclinical smoking-related lung injury. We therefore assessed a broad panel of lung function endpoints and their repeatability in biochemically verified smoking-status groups. Forced oscillation technique (FOT), spirometry and single-breath diffusing capacity (DLCO) were performed at baseline and after 7 ± 3 days in 170 healthy adults classified as current (55), former (60) or never smokers (55) using self-report, exhaled-CO, and a comprehensive biomarker-of-exposure panel. Repeatability was high for spirometry and good for FOT metrics. Standard spirometric indices and traditional FOT resistance/reactance measures did not differ between current and never smokers, but within-breath expiratory–inspiratory resistance differences were greater in current smokers, with significantly higher Δexp–insp R5 values in current smokers than in never smokers (median 0.57 vs. 0.23; p = 0.002) and former smokers (median 0.57 vs. 0.33; p = 0.006). DLCO% and KCO% were lower in current versus never smokers. A significant difference in KCO% was found between current and never smokers (median 94% vs. 106%; p = 0.0003) and between current and former smokers (94% vs. 102%; p = 0.02). Within-breath oscillometry indices and KCO% appear more sensitive than conventional spirometry for detecting early smoking-related functional changes supporting their use as repeatable endpoints in cessation/switching studies.

Article.Title: Residual vibration suppression in a flexible-joint surgical robot using identified modal parameters and input shaping
Article.Authors: Rajabi R.; Mirbagheri A.; Koochakianfard O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Residual vibrations in robotic manipulators used for minimally invasive surgery can degrade positioning accuracy and tool-tip stability. These effects are pronounced in telesurgical robots with flexible joints and harmonic drives, where rigid–flexible coupling excites oscillatory dynamics. Since mechanical redesign is constrained by sterilization, compactness, and regulatory requirements, vibration suppression methods without structural modification are highly desirable. This study presents input shaping as a feedforward command prefilter for suppressing residual vibrations in the Sina flex robotic telesurgery system. Experimentally identified dynamic parameters combined with manufacturer-provided transmission stiffness specifications are used to reconstruct configuration-dependent dynamics and extract dominant modal properties for input-shaper design. The designed filter is integrated into the motion command generation while preserving the existing feedback structure operating in Cyclic Synchronous Position (CSP) mode. Experiments on the first and second rotary joints demonstrate that shaped commands significantly reduce residual vibrations compared with unshaped profiles, achieving approximately 90% reduction in RMS vibration levels. Additional near-tip measurements confirm the reduction of distal tool vibrations. The proposed approach improves motion stability and reducing residual oscillations without structural modifications, providing a practical solution for high-precision robotic applications such as telesurgical systems.
Article.Topic: Dynamics and Control of Mechanical Systems

Article.Title: Optimized droop control-based load flow analysis for islanded AC microgrids with electric vehicle integration
Article.Authors: Meena G.; Mathur A.; Singh V.; Bukya M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microgrids have become a crucial element of modern power systems with increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and require an accurate load flow analysis (LFA) to determine the steady state operating conditions of Microgrid. In islanded configurations, traditional LFA methods are less effective due to the absence of a reference bus. In this type of network, the bus voltage, network frequency, and coupling between droop-controlled distributed generator (DG) introduce additional nonlinear characteristics that are not addressed by conventional LFA formulations. This paper presents an optimized droop control-based Modified Gauss–Seidel (MGS) method for LFA in AC islanded microgrids (IMGs) with integration of static electric vehicle (EV) load models in which voltage and frequency are treated as operating variables due to IMG operation. A bio-inspired optimization is employed to obtain suitable DG droop coefficients with the objective of network loss minimization and maintaining voltage and frequency in an acceptable range with improved DG power sharing. The proposed approach is evaluated on 6-bus and 33-bus AC IMG test networks under diverse static EV load scenarios and is compared with alternative optimization approaches. The optimized droop coefficient achieves active power loss reduction of 23.35%, 10.57%, and 18.97% for EV-1, EV-2, and EV-3 load models, respectively, for inductive DG output impedance mode in 6-bus network. For 33-bus network the loss reductions are 42.38%, 46.18%, and 47.39% correspondingly. In addition an average 2.28% and 1.80% voltage profile improvement are achieved for EV-1 load model for 6-bus and 33-bus test network with corresponding unoptimized scenarios. The results confirm that the proposed technique provides an efficient and flexible framework for adaptive steady state LFA and optimized operation of AC IMG with DG droop control and static EV load model integration.

Article.Title: Adaptive multi-paradigm intrusion detection with dynamic decision fusion for robust cybersecurity
Article.Authors: Kanimozhi R.; Jagan S.; Lalitha K.
Article.Abstract: Cyberattacks are becoming more sophisticated and complex, thereby putting outdated intrusion detection systems (IDSs) to the test, as they are based on a single-detector paradigm and static rule-based evaluation. To overcome these challenges, in this paper, we propose Adaptive Hybrid Intrusion Detection Framework (AHIDF), which combines the signature-based, machine learning-based and deep learning-based detectors in a single framework. A new Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Decision Fusion (ACWDF) mechanism is introduced in the framework, which dynamically weights the detector’s output based on the effectiveness of the detector in recent operations. Moreover, a new Operational Intrusion Detection Readiness Score (OIDRS) is proposed that is used to comprehensively assess detection capability, discriminative performance, false alarm behavior, latency, and the computational overhead. The experimental results showed high accuracy (0.89), precision (0.88), recall (0.86) and F1 score (0.87) in all the categories of cyberattacks and excellent discriminating performance in ROC analysis (AUC up to 0.92). The outcomes show that the proposed adaptive hybrid framework enhances detection robustness and operational readiness by adaptively integrating heterogeneous detection paradigms based on the adaptive decision fusion and deployment-oriented evaluation. The proposed work offers a realistic, scalable approach in today’s cybersecurity environment.

Article.Title: Tri-level hybrid electric bus scheduling under time-of-use tariffs for cost-effective public transportation
Article.Authors: M P.; S C.; D N.; J M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The deployment of electric buses requires coordinated fleet scheduling and charging management to maintain passenger services while controlling infrastructure and electricity costs. This study proposes a Tri-Level Hybrid Electric Bus Scheduling under Time-of-Use tariffs (TLH-EBS-TOU) framework that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for global exploration, Rule-Based Scoring Large Neighborhood Search (RBS-LNS) for schedule restructuring, and Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) for neighbourhood repair. A TOU-aware charging-time selection procedure coordinates charging expenditure with battery-energy requirements, compatible-charger availability, deadheading, and prescribed passenger departures. The framework is evaluated on a Madurai transportation network comprising 810 scheduled passenger trips per day and compared with standalone MILP, PSO, and RBS-LNS. The reported baseline solution uses 149 electric buses and 15 chargers, with an annualized total cost of ₹30.86 crore, representing a 4.85% reduction relative to standalone PSO. Bus capital, charger capital, electricity, and deadheading costs decrease by 5.77%, 4.81%, 3.54%, and 3.70%, respectively. Under the modelled conditions 48.00% of the required 37,885kWh per day charging capacity is allocated to the most economical time of day to charge. The results of these tests illustrate the possibilities of coordinated hybrid scheduling and tariff-aware charging for achieving operating economy while maintaining the prescribed passenger services.

Article.Title: Genomic analysis of Escherichia coli sourced from animals across clinical, farm and environmental settings in Tanzania
Article.Authors: Roberts T.; Kimera Z.; Mgaya F.; Campino S.; Matee M.; Clark T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pathogenic strains of Escherichia coli can cause a wide range of diseases, ranging from mild gastroenteritis to life-threatening illnesses such as haemolytic uremic syndrome and urinary tract infections. As E. coli is ubiquitous, found in humans, farmed animals, and the environment, it is important to conduct pathogen surveillance in a One Health context. In Tanzania, the rapid rise in demand for fish and meat for consumption, combined with the increased use of antibiotics in farming and aquaculture, has made this more pertinent. This study characterises 78 E. coli isolates taken from hospitalised patients ( n = 21/78, 26.9%), farms (poultry n = 26/78, 33.3%; pig n = 13/78, 16.7%), aquaculture ( n = 12/78, 15.4%) and the environment ( n = 6/78, 7.7%), with their DNA undergoing whole-genome sequencing (WGS) using an Illumina platform. A wide diversity of E. coli was captured, with 36 sequence types, including 5 novel ones, alongside 59 serotypes (including mixed O-types). All E. coli phylogroups were represented, with A ( n = 36/78, 46.2%) and B1 ( n = 16/78, 20.5%) being the most common. Ten of the isolates ( n = 10/78,12.8%) belonged to 3 pathotypes associated with human disease (DAEC, EAEC, EAEC/ETEC) and were found in humans and pigs. The DAEC pathotype ( n = 5/78, 6.4%) carried the broadest repertoire of genotypic virulence factors (23 VFs), and human isolates carried the most factors (median 11 vs 5 in other sources; Wilcoxon P < 0.001). Efflux pump-mediated resistance genes were near universal ( acrF : n = 76/78, 97.4%; mdtM : n = 73/78, 93.6%), and there was genotypic resistance to 13 classes of antibiotics. Many isolates encoded resistance genes to many commonly used antibiotic classes such as beta-lactams, quinolones and aminoglycosides. Concordance between genotypic and phenotypic resistance varied by antibiotic class from 37.2% (aminoglycosides) to 89.7% (phenicols), but both genotypic and phenotypic results showed that multi-drug resistance (resistance to 3 or more classes of antibiotics) was widespread (genotypically: n = 71/78, 91.0%; phenotypically : n = 67/78, 85.9%). Overall, this study reports the widespread nature of resistant E. coli in Tanzania, and the use of WGS in effective One Health pathogen surveillance.

Article.Title: Modeling associations between migratory movements and seasonal honey bee colony survival: a machine-learning approach with big data
Article.Authors: Coallier N.; Franco M.; Kuesel R.; Hopkins B.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates relationships between commercial beekeeping practices—particularly colony movement and recorded covariates—and honey bee colony survival. Using data on 362,884 colonies from 62 beekeepers over 4 years (2022–2026), we assessed how movement frequency and timing are associated with observed survival outcomes. Higher transportation frequency was associated with a lower probability of surviving beyond one season, while longer average intervals between moves were associated with higher predicted longevity. Because important drivers of survival (e.g., meteorological conditions, colony health, and floral resources) are not fully measured, these findings should be interpreted as predictive associations rather than causal effects. Finally, we compared three machine-learning survival models and an ensemble using C-index and Brier score, selected the best-performing approach for feature-importance and simulation analyses, and evaluated eight movement scenarios over three simulated beekeeping seasons. Our model-comparison results highlight the importance of appropriate data structuring for achieving optimal performance with censored outcomes.

Article.Title: Discrimination transfers but calibration does not across fundus cameras in diabetic retinopathy screening
Article.Authors: Tabibu S.; Abhyankar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep-learning screening for referable diabetic retinopathy (DR) increasingly runs on cameras it was not developed on. We asked whether a referable-DR classifier trained on tabletop fundus photographs (BRSET) keeps its calibration — the agreement between predicted probability and observed frequency — as well as its discrimination when applied without adaptation to handheld images (mBRSET) and an independent external dataset (APTOS 2019). Across two networks and five training runs, zero-shot discrimination stayed within 0.03–0.04 AUROC of networks trained on each target (AUROC 0.89–0.96). Calibration did not: on handheld images, expected calibration error (ECE) was 0.06–0.07 without recalibration and 0.10–0.11 with the source-fitted calibrator (0.009 in-domain), and a threshold giving 90% sensitivity on the source detected only 42–47% of referable handheld images. On the handheld target, prevalence matching attributed about four-fifths ( $$79\pm 10\%$$ ) of the calibration loss to its higher disease prevalence; on the external target, prevalence and other dataset differences partly offset each other. Prevalence correction without labels did not restore calibration, whereas Platt or isotonic recalibration with 100–200 labelled target images did (ECE 0.03–0.04). Half-precision models preserved discrimination and calibration; 8-bit integer quantization reduced zero-shot AUROC by 0.07–0.14. New cameras therefore require recalibration on local labels.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: referable diabetic retinopathy; classifier calibration; APTOS 2019; expected calibration error; Platt scaling

Article.Title: Integrated gut microbiome and plasma metabolomic profiling reveals distinct biological signatures of damjeok syndrome
Article.Authors: Yun K.; Lim Y.; Ahn Y.; Choi S.; Han K.; Lee H.; Ahn K.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Damjeok syndrome (DJS) is a chronic dyspeptic disorder in traditional Korean medicine characterized by persistent gastrointestinal and extra-gastrointestinal symptoms. However, its gut microbial and metabolic characteristics remain poorly understood. We analyzed the gut microbiome of 114 participants (50 healthy controls [HC] and 64 patients with DJS) using full-length 16 S rRNA gene sequencing. Plasma metabolomic profiling was performed in a matched subset of 90 participants (45 HC and 45 DJS), followed by microbiome–metabolome integration analysis. The DJS group exhibited a distinct gut microbial community structure and 33 key differential species, including depletion of Romboutsia_B ilealis , Blautia wexlerae , Bifidobacterium faecale , and Dorea longicatena , together with enrichment of Akkermansia muciniphila_D_776786 , Dysosmobacter welbionis , and Bacteroides spp. Functional prediction revealed reduced carbohydrate transport capacity and enrichment of secretion systems, nutrient transport, stress adaptation, and GABA biosynthesis modules. Plasma metabolomics identified 35 discriminatory metabolites, and integrative analysis demonstrated significant associations between predicted microbial functional modules and circulating metabolites. These findings indicate that DJS is associated with coordinated alterations in gut microbial composition, predicted microbial functions, and host metabolic profiles, providing potential microbial and metabolic signatures associated with DJS.

Article.Title: Electrospun PVA-PVP nanofibers blended with nitrofurazone and Ag nanoparticles as effective wound healing substitutes
Article.Authors: Alipour R.; Khorshidi A.; Shojaei A.; Mashayekhi F.; Moghaddam M.
Article.Abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol–polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVA/PVP) nanofibers blended with silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) and nitrofurazone (NFZ) were fabricated by electrospinning. Ag NPs were synthesized in situ by hydrothermal reduction of silver nitrate at loadings of 0.4, 0.75, and 1.5 wt% in the PVA solution. Ag NPs and NFZ were subsequently blended into PVA/PVP solutions and processed into nanofibrous mats by electrospinning. The resulting blended nanofibers displayed a homogeneous, linear morphology, with average fiber diameters decreasing from 157.7 nm (PVA/PVP) to 57.3 nm upon NFZ incorporation. Mechanical properties, water uptake, and weight-loss experiments were performed for each formulation. In vitro drug-release profiles were evaluated in phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.4). Biocompatibility of the nanofibrous mats as potential wound dressings was assessed by MTT assay on human skin fibroblasts (HSF-PI 18); cell viability remained above 78% for all compositions but decreased with increasing Ag content. Antibacterial activity was determined by the disc-diffusion method against Staphylococcus aureus , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and Escherichia coli . All Ag-containing mats produced inhibition zones against the three strains (6.3–10.7 mm), whereas the NFZ-only mat inhibited only S. aureus (6.3 mm); because Ag-only mats were not tested, the separate contributions of Ag NPs and NFZ could not be resolved. Finally, in vivo wound-healing efficacy was evaluated in New Zealand White rabbits. Nanofibers containing 1.5 wt% Ag NPs (AgNPs/PVA/PVP/NFZ) produced the most pronounced healing, achieving approximately 90% wound closure after 12 days compared with the PVA/PVP/NFZ control ( P < 0.05).

Article.Title: Predicting pathological upgrading of colorectal polyps after endoscopic submucosal dissection: development and validation of a machine learning model
Article.Authors: Gao F.; Chen J.; Liu L.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: To develop and validate a machine learning–based model for predicting pathological upgrading of colorectal polyps after endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), providing quantitative support for clinical decision-making. We retrospectively analyzed 561 patients with colorectal polyps who underwent ESD between January 2020 and December 2025. Clinical characteristics, laboratory data, and endoscopic features were collected. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection. Ten machine learning models (SVM, LR, KNN, DT, RF, LightGBM, GNB, XGBoost, GBT, and MLP) were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was applied for model interpretation. Among 561 patients, 100 (17.8%) experienced pathological upgrading. The dataset was randomly and stratified into training set (n = 392) and test set (n = 169) at a 7:3 ratio. The upgrading group showed larger polyp size, positive fecal occult blood (FOB), solitary (single) lesions, villous components, reddish surface, uneven morphology, and erosion. Among ten candidate machine-learning algorithms compared via repeated stratified nested cross-validation within the training set, logistic regression showed the best discrimination (cross-validated AUC = 0.795, 95% CI 0.667–0.927) and was selected as the final model; on the internal test set, it achieved an AUC of 0.799 (95% CI 0.701–0.879). Calibration and DCA demonstrated reasonable agreement and potential clinical utility in exploratory analyses. SHAP analysis identified villous component, FOB status, and mucosal erosion as the top three predictors contributing most to the model’s predictions. A logistic regression-based model showed promising discrimination for predicting pathological upgrading after ESD in internal validation, with acceptable calibration and potential clinical benefit. External validation is needed before this model can support individualized clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: Association of ​Simulation-Based Paediatric ​Basic Life support training with knowledge and skills among undergraduate nursing students: a quasi-experimental study
Article.Authors: VJ D.; Das S.; Choudhury J.; Panigrahi S.
Article.Abstract: Simulation-based education is increasingly used to support paediatric resuscitation learning among nursing students. This study examined whether participation in structured simulation-based Paediatric Basic Life Support (PBLS) training was associated with higher immediate post-test knowledge and psychomotor skill performance than conventional lecture-demonstration instruction. A quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test study with a non-equivalent control group was conducted among 168 third-year BSc Nursing students allocated according to two pre-existing academic cohorts (simulation, n = 84; lecture-demonstration, n = 84). Knowledge and psychomotor skills were assessed using an author-developed 20-item PBLS knowledge questionnaire and a 15-item Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) skill checklist. Each student in the simulation cohort participated in one 90-min structured simulation session; eight small-group sessions were conducted over four weeks to accommodate the cohort. The control cohort received one 90-min conventional lecture-demonstration session covering the same PBLS objectives and core content. Knowledge scores increased from 11.04 ± 3.73 to 15.68 ± 3.10 in the simulation cohort (P < 0.001), while skill scores increased from 8.05 ± 2.93 to 12.05 ± 1.98 (P < 0.001). After adjustment for baseline scores, the simulation cohort had higher immediate post-test knowledge (adjusted mean 15.33 vs. 11.37; adjusted mean difference 3.96, 95% CI 2.93–4.98; F (1,165) = 57.76, P < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.259) and skill scores (12.05 vs. 8.08; adjusted mean difference 3.98, 95% CI 3.42–4.53; F (1,165) = 199.17, P < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.547) than the control cohort. Participation in structured simulation-based PBLS training was associated with higher immediate post-test knowledge and psychomotor skill performance than conventional lecture-demonstration instruction in this sample. Because the study used two pre-existing cohorts, with baseline knowledge imbalance and unblinded assessors, residual cohort and observer effects cannot be excluded. The findings should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of causality, long-term retention, or transfer to clinical practice.

Article.Title: Sprouts as a source of phytosterols
Article.Authors: Zielińska-Dawidziak M.; Grygier A.; Biggi S.; Kmiecik D.; Grześ B.; Rudzińska M.
Article.Abstract: Plant sprouting, especially under abiotic stress conditions, has been suggested as a good method for increasing the content of anti-atherosclerotic compounds in natural food raw materials. The research presented aimed to compare changes in the profiles and contents of phytosterols and lipids in the seeds/grains and sprouts of six plants (wheat, barley, rapeseed, camelina, soybean, and lupine). Crude fat content decreased in seven-day-old sprouts of legumes and oilseeds, but phytosterol concentrations increased in all oils. The highest phytosterol content, expressed as the sum of phytosterols per gram of oil, was observed in control lupine sprouts (30.8 mg/g of oil). In rapeseed sprouts, MUFAs were the predominant fraction of fatty acids, while in the other materials, PUFAs had the largest share of the oil. Sprouting improved lipid quality indices. Considering the fat content of the sprouts and their phytosterol concentration, four-day-old rapeseed sprouts appear to be the most promising source of phytosterols among the sprouts studied. During this period, the phytosterol content increased by 150%.

Article.Title: Exploratory GlycA-lipid metabolic profiles and long-term cardiovascular and mortality associations in inflammatory bowel disease: an observational UK Biobank study
Article.Authors: Yuan Y.; Wang R.; Liu P.; Li H.; Feng Y.; Wang D.; An H.; Ye M.; Gan H.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with systemic metabolic perturbations and cardiovascular burden. We used UK Biobank proton nuclear magnetic resonance data to identify exploratory metabolic profiles and evaluate associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality. CatBoost-SHAP feature ranking followed by standardized-feature K-means clustering identified three arbitrary, dataset-specific labels: MQ (relatively lower GlycA and less overall perturbation), IM (an intermediate multivariable pattern), and IC (higher GlycA with some lower lipid measures). In polygenic-risk-score-adjusted outcome models using non-IBD controls as the reference, IC was associated with composite CVD in ulcerative colitis (UC; HR 1.57, 95% CI 1.27–1.95; 85/348 events/participants) and Crohn’s disease (CD; 1.60, 1.14–2.25; 33/149), heart failure (UC 2.26, 1.71–2.98; 50/396; CD 3.24, 2.21–4.77; 26/169), and death (UC 1.45, 1.18–1.79; 87/400; CD 2.40, 1.85–3.10; 58/173). Internal split-sample ARI was 0.919 for UC and 0.754 for CD. However, cluster separation was modest and method-dependent, feature-selection stability was limited, and incremental discrimination changes were small. These single-cohort observational findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality, external validity, or clinical utility.

Article.Title: SPL: stable pseudo-label learning for domain adaptive object detection
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Zhang J.; Zhang W.; Yu Z.; Hao X.
Article.Abstract: Domain-adaptive object detection uses labelled source images and unlabelled target images to address distribution shift. We introduce stable pseudo-label learning (SPL), an incremental extension of the JMT-YOLO Mean Teacher framework that couples adaptive filtering with dynamic assignment. Distribution-aware adaptive thresholding (DAAT) applies Otsu’s between-group variance criterion to a 100-bin histogram of teacher confidence scores and smooths the resulting threshold over iterations. Dynamic pseudo-label assignment (DPLA) restricts candidates by pseudo-box centres, combines classification, overlap and centre-distance costs, and uses IoU-based dynamic positive counts with minimum-cost conflict resolution. SPL obtained 48.6% and 58.4% mAP@0.5 on Pascal VOC \(\rightarrow\) Clipart1k and Cityscapes \(\rightarrow\) Foggy Cityscapes, respectively, and 62.8% Car AP@0.5 on KITTI \(\rightarrow\) Cityscapes. The corresponding gains over JMT-YOLO were 1.7, 1.1 and 1.8 percentage points. Component ablations support an incremental detection benefit in the evaluated framework. The evaluation covers style, weather and camera shifts within JMT-YOLO, with target-validation-informed model selection.

Article.Title: Operations risk management for aircraft engines maintenance, repair, and overhaul
Article.Authors: Alzammam Y.; Akkad K.; Mehboob H.
Article.Abstract: In the business of military maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO), it is necessary to embark on a risk management process to alleviate difficulties such as business productivity, lack of oversight, wasted resources, disjointed strategy, financial instability, ineffective planning and decision-making, and poor departmental integration. Risk management using Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and a discrete event simulation scheme were investigated in this paper. A bow-tie method was used to collect data from 19 departments. FMEA was used to identify the riskiest departments. 263 risks were identified, and improvements were made using technical data through discrete event simulations of the treatment options. The departments used for simulation were production, material resource planning, procurement, component repair center, facility and maintenance, and quality control. The simulation results enhanced the risk management process, demonstrating less processing and waiting time to benefit the stakeholders of the MRO organization. The combination of both the FMEA and discrete event simulation provides a structured framework for risk mitigation and improvement for MRO facilities.

Article.Title: Formal modeling and verification of parachain candidate validation and inclusion in relay chain polkadot
Article.Authors: Rashid M.; Qazi A.; Khan L.; Khan M.; Aljubayri I.
Article.Abstract: Polkadot is a next-generation blockchain platform that achieves scalability and interoperability through a heterogeneous multi-chain architecture, where multiple parachains operate concurrently under a shared security model. A fundamental component of this architecture is the candidate backing and inclusion mechanism, which governs the validation, verification, and incorporation of parachain blocks into the relay chain. This process involves coordinated interactions among collators, validators, parachains, and the relay chain, and proceeds through multiple stages, including candidate generation, validation, backing, availability checking, approval voting, and finalization. Subtle inconsistencies or design flaws within these stages may compromise system correctness, potentially resulting in invalid block inclusion or data unavailability. Consequently, rigorous formal verification is essential to ensure system reliability and robustness. Existing research predominantly emphasizes architectural design and empirical evaluation, with limited attention to formal verification of the candidate lifecycle. To address this gap, this study develops a comprehensive behavioral model using Promela, capturing key system interactions and concurrency aspects. Critical safety and liveness properties, including integrity, fairness, and fault tolerance, are formally specified in Linear Temporal Logic and verified using the SPIN model checker. The verification results confirm system correctness while highlighting state-space complexity and scalability considerations.

Article.Title: Identifying potential combinatorial mechanism between paclitaxel and Almonertinib in lung cancer through multi-omics integration
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Lv J.; Wang Q.; Pei S.; Feng T.; Piao H.; Chen D.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Combination therapy using epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) and cytotoxic chemotherapy is a promising strategy to overcome resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the complicated molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach to dissect the molecular responses to the third-generation EGFR-TKI Almonertinib (Alm) and paclitaxel (PTX) and their combination in EGFR-mutant NSCLC cells. Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling revealed that the combination therapy elicits an unique molecular signature distinct from either monotherapy alone. We identified a specific gene cluster (C8) that was suppressed only by the drug combination, and mainly enriched in cell cycle, DNA replication and mitochondrial function. The downregulation of these processes was validated in H1975 cells, and key genes (e.g., XRCC2 , SKA3 , TOMM40 ) also exhibited prognostic relevance. Meanwhile, metabolomic analysis uncovered a combination-specific blockade of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, evidenced by L-Carnitine depletion and accumulation of Hexanoyl-L-Carnitine and Oleoyl-L-Carnitine. This work demonstrates the potential combination interaction of Alm and PTX, converging on the suppression of cell cycle and the induction of carnitine metabolism blockage. Our findings provide a profound mechanistic rationale for this combination therapy.

Article.Title: LLM-enhanced semantic–collaborative fusion for next POI recommendation
Article.Authors: An H.; Jiang Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Next point-of-interest (​POI) recommendation is an important task in location-based social networks and intelligent mobility services. Existing sequential and graph-based models mainly rely on discrete IDs and structured propagation, limiting their ability to capture activity semantics and immediate mobility intentions behind check-in behaviors. Although large language models (LLMs) have strong semantic understanding capabilities, they may suffer from task mismatch and hallucination issues when directly applied to recommendation scenarios. To address these limitations, LSCF-POI is proposed as an LLM-enhanced semantic–collaborative fusion framework for next POI recommendation. Specifically, a trajectory prompting module is designed to convert structured check-in records into natural language narratives containing visit order, spatiotemporal constraints, and POI category transitions, enabling an LLM to infer users’ fine-grained dynamic mobility intentions through semantic reasoning. Meanwhile, LightGCN is adopted to extract macro-level collaborative preferences from the global user–POI interaction graph. Finally, an adaptive attention mechanism is introduced to align unstructured semantic reasoning with structured collaborative topology in a unified latent space. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that LSCF-POI consistently outperforms competitive baselines. These results demonstrate the complementary value of integrating micro-level semantic intentions with macro-level collaborative awareness for next POI recommendation.

Article.Title: Improving secure communication in the cloud through blockchain-based decentralized distributed chain link framework
Article.Authors: Jose Reena K.; Tamilselvi P.
Article.Abstract: Cloud Computing (CC) enables the storage and access of large datasets via the internet, reducing management costs associated with them. The expansion of cloud technology has raised concerns about data security and necessitated innovative approaches to protecting sensitive details. Traditional methods are frequently inadequate to mitigate the risks associated with compromised encryption keys and centralized key storage. Additionally, security mechanisms, such as encryption and authentication schemes, often fail to provide comprehensive protection against cloud-based threats. It presents significant challenges in maintaining data integrity and regulatory compliance in modern cloud systems. To alleviate these challenges, this article proposes a Blockchain-based Decentralized Distributed Chain Link (BD2CL) technique for secure sharing of sensitive information in the cloud. It starts with the proposed Dynamic Circular Shift Advanced Encryption Standard (DCSAES), which introduces block-dependent pre- and post-encryption circular shifts to AES blocks. The resulting ciphertext blocks are then secured with Elliptic Curve Public Key (ECPK) mechanism with individually generated session keys for securing the block-level keys. The protected blocks are then added to the BD2CL network and are subsequently decentralized-transmitted in the network after being authenticated by nodes, detecting the malicious-lines and verifying the chain-links by consensus. The Data Integrity Verification Scheme (DIVS) ensures that the received blocks are valid by using hash comparison, Merkle-root validation, digital-signature validation, and confidence-based integrity evaluation at the receiver. Only data successfully verified are delivered to the end user, and failed verification results in revalidation of the chain link it affects. The experimental result attains the high security performance of 93.71%, throughput of 405 TPS, and integrity verification accuracy of 94.73%. The security performance is better than the strongest baseline with BADS-ABE achieving 92.04%, 1.67% points above the strongest baseline. Overall, the BD2CL improves secure transaction performance, leading to lower latency and more security.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: data integrity verification; blockchain; Merkle trees; cloud data security; digital signatures; session key management; secure data sharing

Article.Title: Architecture of a virtual simulation teaching platform designed for college students' innovation and entrepreneurship training and its empirical study
Article.Authors: Chen T.; Liu J.; Yin G.; Xuan X.
Article.Abstract: Innovation and entrepreneurship education requires experiential and adaptive learning environments, but evidence is often limited by weak theoretical integration, incomplete intervention reporting, and non-randomized designs. This study evaluated a theory-informed virtual simulation platform for entrepreneurial learning while explicitly accounting for allocation, instructional exposure, measurement quality, and clustering. A two-arm quasi-experimental study included 480 students from 12 intact classes. Baseline assessment preceded non-random classroom allocation to the virtual simulation platform (six classes; n = 240) or conventional training (six classes; n = 240); students did not self-select. Two instructors taught both conditions using common objectives, schedules, and assessment tasks over eight weeks. Multi-item measures underwent reliability and confirmatory factor analysis, performance tasks were scored by blinded independent raters, and primary analyses used covariate-adjusted ANCOVA with classroom-, instructor-, exposure-, missing-data-, and alternative-composite sensitivity analyses. Baseline characteristics were comparable, although post-allocation attendance, active learning time, assignment completion, and participation were higher in the platform condition. Platform assignment was associated with a 6.96-point higher composite learning score (95% CI: 6.34–7.57, p < 0.001); the estimate remained 5.38 points (95% CI: 4.69–6.07) after exploratory adjustment for observed instructional exposure. Classroom-clustered and instructor-adjusted models were consistent. Engagement was the only significant specific indirect pathway, but it explained only 5.41% of the total association. Scale reliability, construct validity, and inter-rater reliability were acceptable to strong. The findings provide supportive, but not definitive causal, evidence that a structured virtual simulation environment is associated with better entrepreneurial learning, engagement, and acceptability. The magnitude of benefit should be interpreted alongside exposure differences, possible novelty and Hawthorne effects, assessment alignment, classroom clustering, and the single-institution context.

Article.Title: 2-Terminal refresh-free memory for high-density and low power consumption during data retention
Article.Authors: Shin H.; Kim Y.; Park J.; Kim K.; Oh K.; Park J.; Baek C.
Article.Abstract: We propose a 2-termi​nal refresh-free memory suitable for 1T-DRAM applications. This memory cell is composed of a multilayer nanowire including silicon (Si), silicon–germanium (SiGe) storage regions and a silicon buffer layer and the nanowire is surrounded by a polysilicon layer. A 2-terminal structure enables high-density implementation. The valence-band offset at the Si/SiGe heterojunction suppresses hole diffusion in the SiGe storage region, thereby improving hole retention and consequently exhibiting distinct retention characteristics in Si, SiGe storage regions. The polysilicon layer reduces electron inflow, thereby inducing holes to accumulate locally in the SiGe storage region rather than the Si storage region. This forms energy barrier from electrons in Si/SiGe hetero structure, reducing impact ionization while retaining the state “1”. The polysilicon layer with a Si/SiGe hetero structure enables to form a holding region that can retain data at low power consumption even when using only two electrodes, providing a low standby current of 4.5 pA when retaining state “1” and a wide holding margin with a gradual current slope of 220 mV/dec. This device achieves a memory operation speed within 10 ns. In particular, the buffer layer suppresses excessive hole generation, thereby improving the speed of write “0” operation.

Article.Title: APH-Net: a multi-task uncertainty-weighted neural architecture for subgroup-level pediatric health surveillance modeling
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Kang J.; He Q.
Article.Abstract: Aggregated public health tables contain repeated demographic and temporal estimates, but random record-level splits can overstate predictive performance when the same subgroup definitions occur in both training and test data. This study evaluates APH-Net, a condition-conditioned multi-task neural architecture, using a CDC surveillance table with 1,203 condition-stratum-period cells across eight health conditions, 25 marginal subgroup strata, and seven reporting windows. The primary evaluation withheld five complete subgroup strata (197 cells), while model selection used only the remaining 1,006 cells. XGBoost achieved the strongest primary regression performance (MAE = 1.272, RMSE = 1.699, R² = 0.862; 95% CI 0.823–0.887 for R²), followed by APH-Net (R² = 0.853) and Random Forest (R² = 0.838). For the auxiliary above-training-median classification task, XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC = 0.775 and macro-F1 = 0.626, whereas APH-Net achieved ROC-AUC = 0.627. Repeated subgroup holdouts and a non-overlapping temporal test produced lower and more variable performance than random-split estimates. APH-Net ablation showed task-dependent value: classification discrimination improved over a single-head MLP, while regression did not. The findings support subgroup-level surveillance modeling but not individual clinical risk prediction.

Article.Title: Autonomous adaptive motor control with neuron firing pattern and muscle growth
Article.Authors: Ogawa S.; Ishiwaka Y.
Article.Abstract: Various models for developing motion control methods using neuromuscular models have been proposed in many fields, such as biophysics, medicine, robotics, computer graphics, computer vision, and so on. This article proposes an autonomous adaptive model, Firing Pattern Controller and Muscle Growth (FPCMG), whose foundation is an implementation of the growth of muscle fiber used in tandem with the firing patterns of the neurons controlling it. The FPCMG model then consists of a motoneuron controller model with interneuron firing patterns and a muscle fiber model in which both slow- and fast-twitch fibers develop with a reinforcement learning rule with delayed reward. It is applied to a simple musculoskeletal model to demonstrate its validity. It simulates an isometric contraction using one joint and two muscles. The system learns different firing patterns depending on muscular strength, and adapts to achieve the target contraction.

Article.Title: Agreement among large language models does not track medical truth in health claim verification
Article.Authors: Artemenko E.; Koltsova O.; Nikolenko S.; Surkov A.; Probst A.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as tools to verify online health information. A common assumption from the self-consistency and ensemble literature is that agreement across models signals reliability. But it remains untested whether inter-model consensus tracks medical truth. We evaluated 10 LLMs spanning frontier, Russian-specific and medical-specialized families on RuHealth, a corpus of 108 short health claims (40 true, 40 false, 28 disputed) validated through multi-stage physician review. Each claim was classified as true , false , or disputed , in both Russian and a validated English translation, across decoding temperatures and 3 stochastic runs ( \({\sim }\) 90,000 judgements). Frontier models were most accurate (macro-F1 64–70) but no model was reliable: “disputed” was assigned to 59.8% of judgements versus a 26% true base rate, while false claims were systematically missed. Majority voting did not help. Three frontier models were unanimous on 90 of 108 claims, yet 31% of those unanimous verdicts were wrong, and 26 of 28 assigned “disputed” to claims that were actually true (14) or false (12). Thus, in this setting on health claims, agreement among contemporary LLMs is not evidence of medical correctness; this effect, which we term consensus mirage , proves to be robust to prompt wording and language.

Article.Title: The pancreatic cancer secretome activates the STAT3 signaling in pancreatic stellate cells to drive the secretion of muscle atrophy-inducing factors
Article.Authors: Yamakawa T.; Najjar L.; Zhang G.; Itakura K.
Article.Abstract: The pancreatic tumor microenvironment, a major component of pancreatic tumors, plays important roles in tumor progression, metastasis, and chemotherapy resistance. In patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, unintentional weight loss by muscle and/or adipose tissue atrophy, called cancer cachexia, is frequently observed. Although it is well established that cancer cells secrete muscle atrophy-inducing factors (MAIF), we investigated whether cancer cells also produce factors to facilitate the secretion of MAIF from microenvironmental cells. To test this possibility, pancreatic stellate cells were treated with conditioned medium from various pancreatic cancer cells (CCM). We revealed that CCM consistently activated STAT3 to secrete MAIF from stellate cells and that the secretion was not observed when CCM from brefeldin A (BFA)-treated cancer cells was added. These results suggest that conventionally secreted factors from cancer cells are responsible for the secretion of MAIF from stellate cells. On the other hand, BFA did not inhibit the secretion of MAIF from either pancreatic cancer cells or stimulated stellate cells. We therefore propose that not only conventionally, but also unconventionally secreted factors contribute to muscle atrophy.

Article.Title: Temporal and spatial trends in cystic fibrosis birth incidence over 50 years in Brittany, France
Article.Authors: Derrien J.; L’Hostis C.; Audrézet M.; Ramel S.; Belleguic C.; Deneuville E.; Arnouat B.; Férec C.; Scotet V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The clinical landscape of cystic fibrosis (CF), one of the most common rare genetic diseases, has evolved considerably over time due to major advances in disease care and management, the widespread implementation of newborn screening (NBS) and the recent emergence of highly effective CFTR modulator therapies. In Brittany (western France), where CF is particularly common, the establishment of a registry tracking all people with CF (pwCF) born since the 1970s, as well as the early implementation of NBS for CF in 1989, offers the opportunity to accurately monitor long-term trends in birth incidence. This study aimed to examine temporal and spatial trends in CF birth incidence in Brittany over 50 years. This study focused on pwCF born in Brittany between 1975 and 2024 ( n = 599). Patients born before 1989 were recorded by combining data sources, whereas others were identified from the NBS programme for CF. Temporal and spatial trends in incidence rates were modelled using Poisson regression and summarised as the average percent change between periods or departments. In Brittany, the birth incidence of CF decreased significantly by 50.1% between the 1975-84 and 2015-24 decades (1/2,175 vs. 1/4,361, p < 0.001), with a clear breakpoint observed from the 1990s. The west-to-east gradient previously observed in Brittany appears to have strengthened over the study period. During the last decade (2015-24), western Brittany exhibited a birth incidence rate 84.9% higher than that of eastern Brittany (1/3,120 vs. 1/5,769, p = 0.035). No upward trend has yet been observed since the expansion of access to elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) therapy in France. This study reports a significant decline in the birth incidence of CF in Brittany over the past 50 years, with a clear breakpoint coinciding with the availability of prenatal diagnosis. The analyses also highlight the strengthening of spatial disparities, with a higher incidence in western Brittany, a peninsula with lower population mixing. Ongoing monitoring remains essential to assess the potential effect of the recent advent of CFTR modulator therapies.
