Article.Title: Assessment of power quality improvement in microgrid using ReliefF-based feature selection and LSTM recurrent neural network
Article.Authors: Palanisamy D.; Govindasamy S.
Article.Abstract: The nonlinear loads, distributed generation and intermittency of renewable energy (RE) are serious issues in modern microgrids and result in a degradation of power quality. This study presents a data-driven framework, ReliefF–LSTM, for power-quality disturbance classification and power-quality improvement assessment, which is a MATLAB/Simulink-simulated IEEE 33-bus microgrid. ReliefF is used to select the power-quality features that are relevant and the LSTM is used to classify the temporal patterns into seven power quality disturbances. This forecasted disturbance class is passed to a subsequent compensation section which is tested with total harmonic distortion (THD), power factor and voltage deviation. Electric measurements such as voltage, current, frequency, power factor, active power and harmonic components are then measured and processed, followed by signal conditioning and multi-domain feature extraction. The algorithm ReliefF selects the most relevant and non-redundant features of the power quality indicators, and the selected features are grouped in temporal sequences. The power-quality disturbance conditions are then specifically learned and numerically predicted using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network, which is not directly used to generate the control signals. The ReliefF–LSTM model is formulated exclusively as a sequence-to-label classifier that identifies seven power-quality operating conditions. It does not predict continuous electrical values or directly generate control signals. The predicted disturbance class is subsequently provided to a separate power-electronic compensation stage, whose effectiveness is evaluated using THD, power factor, and voltage-regulation measurements. The experimental comparative analysis is made with eight benchmark techniques such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), RNN, GRU, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, BiLSTM, TLBO-ANN, and GJO-SAPF. Based on the predicted power-quality conditions, following disturbance classification, the separately implemented DSTATCOM reduced THD from 14.7% to 3.1%, corresponding to a 78.91% reduction, improved the power factor from 0.78 to 0.94, and reduced the maximum bus-voltage deviation from 0.082 to 0.032 p.u., corresponding to a 60.98% reduction. The outcomes of these results have confirmed the accuracy of the proposed framework in terms of temporal disturbance prediction, and the power quality enhancement and intelligent microgrid management following that prediction.

Article.Title: Development and external validation of deep learning models for spontaneous preterm birth prediction from mid-trimester cervical ultrasound
Article.Authors: Chanian R.; Mishra D.; Jain R.; Sharma N.; Khurana A.; Tripathi R.; Jain A.; N/A N/A.; Bhatnagar S.; Bal V.; Das B.; Dash M.; Desiraju B.; Kshetrapal P.; Misra S.; Natchu U.; Rath S.; Sachdeva K.; Sharma D.; Singh A.; Sopory S.; Thiruvengadam R.; Wadhwa N.; Maitra A.; Majumder P.
Article.Abstract: Preterm birth is the leading cause of neonatal death. Despite sustained efforts to identify high-risk women in the mid-trimester, accurate prediction remains difficult. Quantitative cervical ultrasound texture has been proposed as a predictor of spontaneous preterm birth. However, earlier models were developed in small single-centre samples and were not externally validated. We developed image-texture (Local Binary Patterns with a Random Forest), deep-learning (Vision Transformer), clinical-variable, and multimodal models to predict spontaneous preterm birth on the prospective GARBH-Ini cohort. We then externally validated our best models on an independent cohort scanned on a different ultrasound machine. Our best overall model reached an internal-test area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.71 (95% CI 0.59, 0.83), but performed modestly at 0.52 (95% CI 0.38, 0.67) externally. The deep-learning and multimodal models did not perform better. Discrimination appeared higher in a clinically high-risk subgroup at the 34-week threshold. These estimates were imprecise because of few cases and are hypothesis generating which need to be confirmed in future studies. Among the several likely reasons for the modest external performance is the heterogeneity of preterm birth. Predicting distinct preterm-birth subtypes separately, and integrating additional biomarkers and data domains, might improve model performance.

Article.Title: Efficient infrared radiation calibration method for wide dynamic range infrared radiation measurement systems
Article.Authors: Gu M.; Peng X.; Li S.; Ren Q.; Zhou J.
Article.Abstract: To overcome the limitation of long calibration time of traditional infrared radiation calibration methods, the paper presents the efficient calibration method for wide dynamic range infrared radiation measurement systems. First, by analyzing the energy transfer mechanism in systems incorporating variable optical attenuator and adjustable integration time settings, we develop the comprehensive system response model that accounts for the effects of both optical attenuator and integration time, incorporating nonlinear corrections in both dimensions. The model is designed to be universally applicable and can be seamlessly integrated with the inner-outer calibration concept, enabling full calibration method coverage—from collimator-blackbody and close-range extended source to inner-outer calibration—within a unified efficient framework. Consequently, the efficient calibration algorithm is derived based on the model, utilizing nonlinear optimization for parameter estimation. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method boosts calibration efficiency multiple times relative to traditional approaches Furthermore, compared to Yang’s fast calibration method, the approach does not require strict linearity in the attenuation and integration time dimensions, making it applicable to a broader range of infrared radiometric systems.

Article.Title: Multishell diffusion MRI models have limited sensitivity to ketamine-induced microstructural changes in the mouse brain
Article.Authors: Ewbank S.; Hart A.; Gopal D.; Azadian M.; St. Laurent R.; Rodriguez C.; McNab J.; Airan R.
Article.Abstract: Gray matter neuronal morphology is relevant to psychiatric diseases and pharmacotherapies. For instance, ketamine rapidly induces dendritic remodeling and spinogenesis which are required for its therapeutic effects in psychiatric disorders. A noninvasive biomarker of this phenomenon could aid in treatment response monitoring, patient stratification, or drug development. In principle, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) is sensitive to microstructure and could provide the desired approach. Here, we used three multishell dMRI-based models (diffusion tensor, neurite orientation dispersion and density, and diffusion kurtosis) in vivo to interrogate ketamine-induced microstructural changes in wild type mice and in the SAPAP3 knockout mouse model of compulsive behavior. Although histological analyses confirmed ketamine-induced increases in cortical synapse markers, we observed no corresponding changes in dMRI metrics. In Monte Carlo simulations of diffusion in scenes solely containing realistic dendrites, dMRI was sensitive to small morphological changes across gradient amplitudes only in noiseless conditions. In contrast, the same dMRI acquisitions resolved baseline microstructural differences between sexes and between SAPAP3 knockout and wild type mice, supporting the sensitivity of the method as implemented. Our findings suggest that the in vivo dMRI acquisition and modeling approaches used here lack sensitivity to detect the subtle dendritic morphology changes induced by ketamine.

Article.Title: Pre-synthesis theoretical study of acetophenone and indole adsorption on fullerene nanocage derivatives for their removal and separation from wastewater
Article.Authors: Almohana A.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluates pristine C60 and its B- and Si-substituted derivatives (BC59 and SiC59), as theoretically proposed platforms for adsorbing acetophenone (ACF) and indole (IDO) in wastewater and for studying their adsorption-induced electronic and optical responses. We performed calculations using the B97D and ωB97X-D functionals. We examined structural stability through cohesive-energy and vibrational analyses, and characterized adsorption using optimized geometries, BSSE-corrected adsorption energies, estimated recovery times, frontier-orbital descriptors, dipole moments, a dimensionless gap-based electronic-response descriptor proxy, TD-DFT spectra, NBO, QTAIM, ELF, and LOL analyses. Pristine C 60 interacted weakly with both analytes, yielding corrected adsorption energies of approximately −6.6 to −7.1 kcal.mol −1 and predominantly closed-shell, noncovalent contacts. Substitution with B or Si considerably strengthened the predicted adsorption by creating localized electron-accepting sites. At the ωB97X-D level, adsorption energies reached −19.80 and −26.22 kcal.mol −1 for BC59@IDO and SiC 59 @IDO and −22.23 and −34.64 kcal.mol −1 for BC 59 @ACF and SiC59@ACF, respectively. NBO and QTAIM results together indicated localized, strongly polarized N···B/Si and O···B/Si contacts, with partial shared-electron contributions according to the QTAIM energy–density criteria. Adsorption also produced pronounced frontier-orbital changes, with dimensionless gap-based response values (Rg) reaching + 4.139 for BC59@IDO at the ωB97X-D level and + 6.788 for SiC59@ACF at the B97D level. BC59@ACF was additionally predicted to have a visible-region absorption maximum at 605.44 nm. Overall, SiC59 gave the strongest predicted adsorption and the largest B97D gap-based response for ACF, whereas BC59 offered a potentially more balanced adsorption-recovery response. These results provide a pre-synthesis basis for future experimental evaluation of the proposed fullerene-based platforms.

Article.Title: Parental anxiety mediates the association between child behavioral problems and parenting stress among parents of children and adolescents with allergic rhinitis
Article.Authors: Fangli L.; Xiaojia W.; Li W.; Yunyan X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a common allergic disease among children and adolescents. Parenting stress is closely related to the health of children with AR and the psychological well-being of their parents. However, how children’s behavioral problems and parental anxiety jointly affect parenting stress remains unclear. A cross-sectional design with convenience sampling was used to recruit 230 parents of children and adolescents with AR aged ≤ 18 years (mean age 9.93 ± 3.00 years). The Conners’ Parent Symptom Questionnaire, Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, and Simplified Parenting Stress Index were used for assessment. Structural equation modeling was performed using AMOS 26.0, with the bias-corrected bootstrap method (5000 resamples) to test mediation effects. Descriptive statistics were computed using SPSS 26.0. The hypothesized mediation structural equation model demonstrated acceptable fit (χ 2 /df = 1.684, CFI = 0.973, TLI = 0.962, RMSEA = 0.055, SRMR = 0.041). Child behavioral problems were directly associated with parenting stress (β = 0.650, 95% CI [0.520, 0.766]) and indirectly associated through parental anxiety (β = 0.086, 95% CI [0.042, 0.149]), indicating partial mediation. The model explained 59.0% of the variance in parenting stress. Child behavioral problems related to AR showed both direct and indirect associations with parenting stress via parental anxiety. These findings suggest that interventions addressing both children’s behavioral concerns and caregivers’ psychological well-being may help reduce parenting stress and enhance family coping capacity.

Article.Title: The influence of tropical weather events on movement patterns of nesting green and loggerhead sea turtles
Article.Authors: Iafrate J.; Holloway-Adkins K.; Provancha J.; Ahr B.; Reyier E.; Greene J.; Oliveira K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones alter marine habitats and influence the behavior of many marine organisms. Sea turtles may be particularly impacted because they rely on both terrestrial and aquatic environments, migrating to and from nesting beaches during the peak of the Atlantic hurricane season. Along southeast Florida (USA), green ( Chelonia mydas ) and loggerhead ( Caretta caretta ) sea turtles nest in globally significant numbers from May through October, overlapping the most active months of tropical cyclone occurrence. We investigated movement responses of green and loggerhead turtles to two tropical cyclones during and following the nesting season using acoustic and satellite telemetry. Bayesian state-space models were fitted to satellite telemetry data to characterize movement paths and behavioral responses, while acoustic telemetry was used to quantify local residency. Key findings revealed greater displacement and highly directed movements for individual green turtles in association with the onset or passing of storm events, including directed offshore movements and long-distance travel, whereas loggerheads exhibited more localized behavioral responses. Environmental variables, particularly wave height and water temperature, were strongly associated with turtle movement speed, depth use, and distance from shore. As tropical cyclones are projected to increase in frequency and intensity under climate change, this study provides insight into potential energetic and behavioral consequences.

Article.Title: The relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust among college students: a serial mediation model
Article.Authors: Zhao H.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to explore the relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust among college students, as well as the chain mediating roles of social support and psychological resilience. A convenience sampling method was employed to survey 504 college students from selected universities in Liaoning Province. Data were collected using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, the Interpersonal Trust Scale, the Perceived Social Support Scale, and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. (1) Physical exercise was positively correlated with interpersonal trust among college students. (2) Physical exercise was positively correlated with social support; social support was positively correlated with both psychological resilience and interpersonal trust; and psychological resilience was also positively correlated with interpersonal trust. (3) Social support and psychological resilience mediated the relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust, with three specific indirect pathways identified: physical exercise → social support → interpersonal trust; physical exercise → psychological resilience → interpersonal trust; and physical exercise → social support → psychological resilience → interpersonal trust. (1) Physical exercise is positively associated with interpersonal trust among college students. (2) Both social support and psychological resilience serve as independent mediators, as well as chain mediators, in the relationship between physical exercise and interpersonal trust. Given the cross-sectional design of this study, these mediating pathways should be interpreted as statistical association patterns rather than as evidence of causal mechanisms.

Article.Title: Adaptive visual perception and navigation framework for safe indoor mobility of visually impaired users
Article.Authors: Nagaraju T.; Murugeswari R.
Article.Abstract: Indoor mobility for visually impaired people is an essential problem due to dynamic obstacles and inadequate real-time detection systems. Existing solutions have been found lacking in terms of robustness and adaptability. The current research develops a robust adaptive visual perception and navigation system based on obstacle detection and indoor navigation in real time. The system consists of You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLOv11) algorithm for obstacle detection, Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement (MSFE) for better representation of smaller and distant obstacles, a pixel-wise replacement approach through Kernel Density Estimation (Ps-KDE) for pre-processing with illumination variation, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for adaptive decisions in navigation, and Adaptive Coyote-Badger Optimization (ACBO) for learning. The developed indoor high-resolution dataset consists of 23 obstacle classes and was used to train and evaluate the proposed algorithm; the NYU Depth v2 and SUN RGB-D datasets were also utilized for validation. This model has been able to generate 97.52% Mean Average Precision (mAP) and 96.67% Mean Average Recall (mAR) in the customized dataset with an average frame per second of 55.6 FPS, which makes it suitable for mobile applications. For the scale evaluation, distance estimation, camera position, ablation, and real-life tests are carried out to further evaluate each component as well as the entire framework. A mobile application for providing navigation guidance through text to speech has been implemented. This framework shows its effectiveness under different indoor scenarios without depth sensing.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: YOLOv11; multi-scale feature enhancement; kernel density estimation; obstacle detection; deep reinforcement learning; indoor mobility; illumination variation; visually impaired navigation; adaptive navigation

Article.Title: Postoperative pain after endodontic retreatment using different integrated electronic apex locator working length control modes
Article.Authors: Uyanık H.; Maraş E.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of different simultaneous working length control modes of an integrated electronic apex locator (EAL) system on postoperative pain following retreatment compared with working length determination using a conventional EAL. This prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled clinical trial included 144 patients undergoing nonsurgical retreatment of mandibular premolars, of whom 126 were included in the final analysis. Patients were randomly allocated to 4 groups: conventional EAL (control; Root ZX Mini) and three integrated EAL modes (apical reverse, apical slow down, and apical stop). Postoperative pain intensity was recorded at seven predefined time points: 6 and 12 h and days 1, 2, 3, 5, and 7 after treatment, using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). A significant main effect of group was observed ( p = 0.006). Averaged across assessment points, NRS scores were higher in the conventional EAL group than in the apical reverse group ( p = 0.010). Other pairwise group differences were not statistically significant ( p > 0.05). A significant main effect of time was also observed ( p < 0.001), whereas the group × time interaction was not significant ( p = 0.077). Procedure time was significantly longer in the conventional EAL group ( p < 0.001). In univariate analyses, longer procedure time was associated with higher odds of postoperative pain at all evaluated time points ( p < 0.05). The apical reverse mode was associated with lower overall postoperative NRS scores than conventional working length determination, while all three integrated EAL modes were associated with shorter procedure times. No statistically significant difference in pain trajectories was detected among the groups.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: endodontic retreatment; postoperative pain; mandibular premolars; electronic apex locators; procedure time

Article.Title: Shock impedance mismatch and transmission loss in fiber–metal laminates: a computational and experimental study
Article.Authors: Pai A.; Rodriguez-Millan M.; Satish S.; Nayak S.; Jaideep J.; Hegde S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The shielding performance of multi-layered sandwich structures is influenced by the shock impedance mismatch at material interfaces. In this study, an integrated computational, analytical, and experimental framework was developed to evaluate the acoustic transmission loss (TL) of fiber–metal laminates (FMLs) incorporating fabric-reinforced polymer core plies. A dimensionless shock-impedance formulation based on the Buckingham- $$\pi $$ theorem was employed to examine the influence of material properties, including Poisson’s ratio, on three-dimensional elastic wave propagation and aid in material selection. A mesoscale representative volume element (RVE) approach was used to derive the effective orthotropic properties of aramid-, basalt-, and Zylon-reinforced plies, which were subsequently incorporated into a macroscale finite-element (FE) harmonic-acoustics framework to evaluate TL over the 63–1300,Hz frequency range. In parallel, a multi-layer analytical formulation was developed to estimate insertion loss and the corresponding frequency-dependent TL response. The empirical parameters of the analytical model were calibrated using a single baseline configuration and subsequently applied to six additional stacking sequences, for which the mean TL difference from the corresponding FE predictions remained below $$3.06\%$$ . Impedance-tube measurements of the baseline Al–Ba–Ba–Ba–Ba–Al configuration provided an experimental benchmark for comparison with the analytical and numerical predictions. Among the configurations investigated, the all-aramid sequence exhibited the highest mean numerical TL, while aramid–basalt and Zylon–basalt hybridization increased the mean TL relative to the all-basalt configuration. The experimental measurements exhibited a stronger frequency-dependent reduction in TL than the idealized analytical and FE predictions, highlighting the influence of physical and boundary effects not completely captured in the computational models. Overall, the proposed multi-scale framework provides an efficient approach for evaluating material combinations and stacking sequences, facilitating the preliminary design and comparative assessment of FMLs for low-to-mid-frequency shock shielding applications.

Article.Title: Surveillance for zoonotic viruses in human population at the human-animal interface in North Sulawesi, Indonesia
Article.Authors: Wiyatno A.; Kusumaningrum T.; Dewantari A.; Latinne A.; Kowel C.; Gaghiwu L.; Bernadus J.; Rey B.; Rambitan M.; Jaya U.; Ma’roef C.; Myint K.; Olival K.; Pamungkas J.; Safari D.
Article.Abstract: For the past decades, novel, emerging and re-emerging zoonotic diseases have been identified with the potential to cause pandemics. Our study aims at detecting viruses that circulate in people who have close contact with animals including wildlife, poultry and companion animals in North Sulawesi, Indonesia to better characterize viruses and zoonotic disease transmission. This study was conducted at one hospital and one primary health center in the Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi, Indonesia from November 2017 to December 2018. We enrolled syndromic patients exhibiting symptoms of respiratory illness (including severe acute respiratory illness), or fever of unknown origin. Questionnaires and biological specimens, including respiratory and blood-derived samples, were collected. Specimens were then tested using consensus PCR followed by sequencing for nine viral families/genera with pandemic potential or endemic significance. A total of 217 patients were enrolled, of whom 63 (29%) tested positive for at least one of the viral families screened. The detected viruses included Influenza virus (n = 21, 9.6%), Flavivirus (n = 15, 6.9%), Pneumovirus (n = 14, 6.4%), Enteroviruses (n = 10, 4.6%), Paramyxovirus (n = 2, 0.9%) and Coronavirus (n = 1, 0.5%). None of the filovirus, hantavirus, or henipavirus detected in this study. 32% and 22% of patients with positive viral detection had contact with rodents and bats, respectively, primarily through the preparation or cooking of wild meat. Our study provides proof-of-concept for integrating zoonotic virus screening among symptomatic patients with assessments of human-animal contact within a clinical setting.

Article.Title: A dual artificial neural network core PRNG on FPGA driven by a novel 4D hyperchaotic system with hidden attractor
Article.Authors: Tuna M.; Vaidyanathan S.; Alçın M.; Koyuncu İ.; Saleh M.; Benkouider K.; Ibrahim S.; Almaymuni A.; Makhtar M.; Sambas A.
Article.Abstract: This paper introduces a hardware-implemented pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) driven by a constructed Novel 4D Hyperchaotic System with Hidden Attractors (N4DHSHA). The dynamical properties of the oscillator are rigorously investigated through Lyapunov exponent spectra, bifurcation diagrams, basins of attraction, and the 0–1 test for chaos, revealing a Maximal Lyapunov Exponent (MLE) of 4.4662 alongside robust multistability. Furthermore, the model demonstrates linear topological controllability via DC offset boosting and amplitude scaling. To resolve the challenge of digitizing delicate equilibrium-free attractors, we propose a dual Artificial Neural Network (ANN) core architecture consisting of a Predictor layer activated by a Log-Sigmoid function and a Refiner layer activated by a Hyperbolic Tangent Sigmoid function. The proposed generator is implemented on a Xilinx Virtex-6 FPGA utilizing the 32-bit IEEE-754 floating-point standard. By harvesting 18-bit Least Significant Bit slices per clock cycle, the system achieves a real-time throughput of 139.714 Mbps at a 139.714 MHz operating frequency. Post-synthesis evaluations indicate highly optimized hardware footprint metrics, consuming 63.69% of available slice registers and 3.13% of DSP48E1 slices. The statistical verification shows that the generated bitstreams pass all 16 sub-tests of the NIST SP 800 − 22 test suite with P-values exceeding 0.01, proving that the dual-core neural architecture successfully preserves hyperchaotic complexity to deliver an entropy source for secure communications and image encryption.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: pseudorandom number generators; hidden attractors; multistability; hyperchaotic systems; FPGA implementation; Lyapunov exponents

Article.Title: A dual-modal fiducial marker with single-view x-ray pose recoverability for MR-guided surgical navigation
Article.Authors: Xu G.; Li X.; Xiong W.; Yin Z.; Yang Y.; Wang X.; Zhong D.; Liu H.; Xie Y.; Chen K.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In orthopedic surgery, accurate intraoperative localization of implants and instruments is essential. Traditional surgical navigation markers rely on a fixed external reference frame, but in mixed reality (MR) surgical navigation the tracking camera moves with the surgeon’s head, making conventional markers unsuitable. This study proposes that markers for MR navigation must satisfy three design constraints: omnidirectional recognizability, X-ray recognizability, and dual-modal compatibility. Based on these constraints, we designed a marker consisting of a central cube and four cylindrical axes with unequal diameters, and proved analytically that its six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) pose can be determined from a single X-ray image. A pose estimation algorithm combining geometric optimization and deep learning-based feature extraction was used to validate dual-modal pose estimation, in which the marker pose is estimated independently from a single X-ray or optical image. On 100 X-ray and 194 optical images, the X-ray recognition error was 1.58° ± 1.26° (coronal plane) and 1.90° ± 1.50° (sagittal plane), with 94% of samples achieving a composite angular error below 5°; the optical recognition success rate was 90.2%, with an overall angular error of 1.52° ± 0.98°. Error distributions were symmetric and zero-centered (signed means within ± 0.02°); X-ray pose estimation remained solvable even at extreme sagittal tilt (up to ~ 40°), while rare optical failures (2.3%) could be reliably detected. These results provide preliminary evidence of dual-modal marker pose estimation from single-view X-ray and optical images; further validation is required before clinical translation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: deep feature extraction; MR-guided surgery; 6D pose estimation; geometry optimization; optical tracking

Article.Title: SQCDL-WIoT: a scalable quantum convolutional deep learning framework with wearable IoT integration for breast cancer screening
Article.Authors: Ramudu K.; Saturi S.; Ramadevi B.; Radha N.; Katamreddi H.; George A.; Pandey S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep learning techniques have greatly improved the ability to perform automatic diagnosis of breast cancer through use of computers; however, existing techniques are generally complex and costly, do not well incorporate multiple data modalities, and cannot be deployed clinically in real time. This paper proposes SQCDL-WIoT, which is a scalable, wearable-based internet of things (IoT)-enabled quantum convolutional deep learning (C-DL) framework capable of multi-class breast cancer screening. The proposed method includes two VQCs with five qubits each that can be embedded into a ResNet-50 back bone. In addition to being able to process images from histopathology and wearable-based bio sensor signals as input, the method also enables the incorporation of both wearable based bio sensor signal processing (i.e., wearable-IoT) and clinical variables via the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism. Thus, this proposed method is capable of hybrid quantum-classical training. Using stratified k-folds cross-validation (where k = 5) on the BreaKHis dataset and zero-shot transfer learning on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, SQCDL-WIoT demonstrated the highest accuracy (98.14%) with the highest sensitivity (macro-sensitivity = 97.63%), specificity (macro-specificity = 98.87%), and area under curve (AUC = 0.9891) when compared to all other baseline methods at 40x magnification on BreaKHis. Additionally, SQCDL-WIoT demonstrated 93.41% accuracy on the CBIS-DDSM dataset via zero shot learning, indicating good cross-domain generalization. Finally, the wearable IoT sub-system demonstrated a mean real-time edge-inference latency of 378 ± 12 milliseconds on an ARM Cortex-A72 processor, meeting the defined clinical threshold for response of < 400 milliseconds. The results of ablation studies indicated that both quantum convolution and SE attention contributed to complementary and synergetic increases in performance compared to classical ResNet-50 baseline models. Overall, the collective results presented here indicate that the proposed hybrid quantum-classical DL framework combined with wearable-based IoT sensing may represent a viable solution to scalable and intelligent breast cancer screening.

Article.Title: Bioactive properties of Rhinacanthus nasutus (L.) Kurz and Andrographis paniculata (Burm.f.) nees: inhibition of oral pathogenic bacteria and inflammatory responses
Article.Authors: Suriyaprom S.; Cheepchirasuk N.; Intachaisri V.; Tragoolpua Y.
Article.Abstract: Rhinacanthus nasutus (L.) Kurz and Andrographis paniculata (Burm.f.) Nees (Acanthaceae) are medicinal plants widely used in traditional Asian medicine for the treatment of infections and inflammatory disorders. This study aimed to characterize the metabolite profiles of their ethanolic extracts and evaluate their antioxidant, antibacterial, antibiofilm, anti-adhesion, and anti-inflammatory activities against oral pathogenic bacteria. HPLC analysis identified rutin and chrysin in R. nasutus , and chlorogenic acid and quercetin in A. paniculata . LC–QTOF–MS profiling further revealed distinct metabolite compositions, with tentatively identified naphthoquinones (lapachol, α- and β-lapachone) and coumarins (umbelliferone and dihydrocoumarin) predominating in R. nasutus , whereas diterpenoids (neoandrographolide) and flavonoid glycosides were characteristic of A. paniculata . R. nasutus exhibited higher total phenolic and flavonoid contents and stronger ABTS radical scavenging activity, while A. paniculata showed greater DPPH radical scavenging capacity. Both extracts demonstrated antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans , Streptococcus pyogenes , Staphylococcus aureus , and Klebsiella pneumoniae , with MIC values ranging from 15.63 to 250 mg/mL. In addition, the extracts significantly inhibited S. mutans biofilm formation, reduced bacterial adhesion and invasion into HSC-4 oral epithelial cells, and downregulated gtfD and gbp gene expression. Scanning electron microscopy revealed structural alterations in treated bacterial cells. Furthermore, both extracts significantly suppressed nitric oxide production in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. In particular, A. paniculata markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of iNOS , COX-2 , IL-6 , IL-1β , and TNF-α . These findings highlight the distinct in vitro bioactivities of R. nasutus and A. paniculata and provide an information for further investigation of their potential applications in oral infections and inflammation-associated conditions.

Article.Title: Climate variability and forest fire dynamics in Himachal Pradesh, India
Article.Authors: Mehta P.; Baweja P.; Goroshi S.; Dadial P.
Article.Abstract: Forest fires are recognized as a major threat to a significant global challenge for ecosystem stability. In the recent past the state experienced rise in forest fire events. Therefore, the present study provides an overview of forest fire events in Himachal Pradesh, along with its relationship between climatic attributes. The fire events mostly occur during summer and monsoon season. Therefore, the fire data was collected for said seasons from Fire information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) portal from 2004 to 2024. The findings reveal an increase in forest fire events from 132 in 2004 to 1358 in 2024. The Solan district reported the highest number of forest fire events of 274 in both the seasons in 2024. Therefore, Solan district was selected for exploring the relationship between fire incidents and climatic attributes. The change point detection and Mann–Kendall test have been applied for trend analysis. The results analyzed significant rising trend for maximum and mean temperatures for August and September while diurnal temperature showed significant increasing trend for April month. The summer series of temperature showed significant change point around (1997) and confirmed the homogeneity at 95% confidence level. The Angstrom index (AI) and Fuel moisture index (FMI) were also computed for the prediction of forest fire incidents. The indicators proved effective for monitoring fire incidents the AI values below 2.0 and FMI values below 15.0 in 2024 were associated with maximum number of fire incidents. The correlation analysis indicated a positive correlation between fire events, potential evapotranspiration and mean temperature ( P ≤ 0.01 and ≤ 0.05). In addition to Principal component analysis (PCA), two components (PCI and II) contributed about 63.8% and 64.9% of variability during summer and monsoon season and indicated that potential evapotranspiration, mean and diurnal temperatures have highest positive loading with forest fire incidents. The study underscores the increasing role of climate in forest fire incidents and emphasizes the need for extensive ground-level studies for effective forest fire management. Enhancing region-specific knowledge, understanding fuel types and their characteristics, and recording high-resolution hourly climatic data to analyze fire-related indices at a micro level.

Article.Title: Equity and socioeconomic determinants of integrating inpatient hospice and palliative care into primary health care: a spatiotemporal ecological study in China, 2019–2023
Article.Authors: Ye Z.; Tang Y.; Zhu L.; Fan Y.; Liu L.; Tang Z.; Zhang H.; Xu Y.; He J.; Jing L.
Article.Abstract: Equitably integrating hospice and palliative care (HPC) into primary health care (PHC) systems remains challenging in rapidly aging settings with regional disparities. This spatiotemporal ecological study assessed all institutions providing PHC-based inpatient HPC within a pioneering PHC system in China from 2019 to 2023. Annual development scores were calculated using a localized comprehensive evaluation framework. We mapped service expansion and district-level development gradients using kernel density estimation and natural breaks classification, quantified spatial equity using Dagum Gini decomposition, characterized local clustering and trajectories using Exploratory Spatiotemporal Data Analysis, and evaluated district-level socioeconomic associations using OLS, GWR, and GTWR models. The number of institutions increased from 94 to 163, whereas the citywide median development score increased modestly from 443.54 to 462.10. Citywide equity improved, but localized heterogeneity, catch-up dispersion in the outer suburbs, and path-dependent spatial structures persisted. GWR performed best, indicating spatially heterogeneous socioeconomic associations. These findings suggest that policy-driven expansion improved service availability but did not fully resolve capacity constraints or local disparities. Equitable integration requires spatially responsive strategies that combine continued expansion with workforce investment, targeted funding, basic resource provision, and essential medicine access.

Article.Title: Atlas-guided attribution ranking reveals anatomy-dependent localization gaps in C2 fracture classifiers
Article.Authors: Hu Z.; Lin H.; Rohringer T.; Jegatheeswaran V.; Khan Z.; Emami A.; Colak E.; Lozano C.; Wilson J.; Witiw C.; Sejdić E.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Binary C2 fracture classifiers can identify whether a fracture is present but do not show which part of C2 is fractured. We evaluated a framework that combines detailed C2-specific multi-atlas anatomy with classifier attribution maps to produce regional rankings, without requiring additional model training. Three CT examinations from the RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine Challenge were manually annotated into 16 C2 subregions and used as anatomical atlases. Deformable registration transferred these labels to individual patients. The resulting anatomical maps were combined with Grad-CAM maps from two existing classifiers and their ensemble using Peak-Guided Iterative Region Proposal. Primary localization analysis included 97 examinations classified as positive by at least one classifier; secondary detection-to-localization analysis included all 101 confirmed C2 fracture cases. Three-atlas leave-one-out evaluation of label propagation yielded macro-Dice scores of 0.88 for five anatomical groups and 0.77 for 16 subregions, with weaker agreement for small articular facets. Ensemble mean per-case F1@3 was 0.66 and 0.54, respectively. Ensemble detection-to-localization micro-Recall@3 was 0.83, compared with 0.86 among the 97 detector-positive cases. Odontoid and body–lateral mass–superior articular facet complex fractures were retrieved most reliably; transverse-process, posterior-arch, and pars-inferior-facet retrieval was reduced or variable. This framework converts patient-level fracture predictions into structured anatomical rankings and reveals region-specific weaknesses that are not apparent from patient-level detection performance. These findings suggest opportunities for targeted dataset enrichment and future model refinement.

Article.Title: Predicting compressive strength of concrete using machine learning
Article.Authors: Alzaidi M.; Rasheed A.; Aldehani R.; Alhaji F.; Baqer S.; Mokadam K.; El-Zahab S.; Uysal F.; Ghanem H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Concrete compressive strength is verified by destructive testing after curing, which limits how quickly candidate mixtures can be screened. This study evaluates whether mixture proportions and curing age support accurate, interpretable preliminary estimates, and how much the reported accuracy depends on the evaluation protocol. Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting were compared on the UCI Concrete Compressive Strength dataset (1,030 observations, 428 mixtures). A strength-stratified 80/20 split gave 824 training and 206 held-out observations; hyperparameters were selected by five-fold cross-validation within the training partition and the held-out set was used once. Gradient Boosting performed best ( $$R^2=0.940$$ , RMSE = 4.07​ MPa, MAE = 2.70 MPa), followed by Random Forest ( $$R^2=0.926$$ ) and Support Vector Regression ( $$R^2=0.887$$ ). Because most mixtures are tested at several ages, random splits estimate generalisation to new observations of known mixtures; mixture-grouped cross-validation, which targets new mixtures, lowered the Gradient Boosting score from 0.933 to 0.862 with the ranking preserved. SHAP attributions ranked age, cement, water, and slag as the leading predictors, consistent with established concrete technology but not read as causal evidence. The framework supports preliminary mixture screening with laboratory verification; external validation remains necessary.

Article.Title: Explainable multi-modal transformer framework for electric vehicle charging demand forecasting
Article.Authors: Us Salehin M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of EV charging demand is fundamental to grid stability, real-time pricing, and charging station management, but few prediction methods are able to utilize more than just historical demand, and are able to reveal why a particular forecast was made. In this paper we develop and experimentally investigate an explainable multi-modal forecasting approach to hourly EV charging demand, which fuses charging session data, weather information, grid prices, and grid operating information (voltage, frequency, transformer load) with station occupancy and traffic signal status. Using 15,304 charging session records from 55 charging stations between January 2019 and July 2020, we construct a 13,680-hour multi-modal data panel including calendar features, lags, and rolling statistics. We evaluate five forecasting architectures, including linear regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, a Long Short-Term Memory network, and our proposed attention-based Transformer network with a learned temporal pooling mechanism to interpret attention. XGBoost and Random Forest are the two strongest models overall and slightly outperform each other on different metrics: XGBoost achieves the lowest RMSE and highest R² (RMSE = 5.63 kWh, R² = 0.980), while Random Forest achieves a marginally lower MAE and MAPE (MAE = 1.67 kWh, MAPE = 7.39%, versus XGBoost’s MAE = 1.72 kWh, MAPE = 8.36%); a paired significance test shows this MAE difference is not statistically significant, so the two tree ensembles are best described as practically comparable, with XGBoost’s edge concentrated in the largest-error hours. Both substantially outperform our attention-based Transformer network (RMSE = 27.98 kWh, R² = 0.513) and LSTM network (RMSE = 30.02 kWh, R² = 0.440) at current data scale; in contrast, the attention weights from the transformer provide an intuitive explanation on which past hours are the most influential ones in forecasting the current charging demand. SHAP value analysis of the best model identifies the recent past charging demand, transformer loading, and the hour of the day as the most significant predictors, and ablation tests confirm a 4–6% increase in RMSE from the removal of grid and calendar data, whereas a negligible impact is observed from the removal of station occupancy/traffic features. All differences in forecasting performance across various architectures are confirmed by Diebold-Mariano tests to be statistically significant, and a sensitivity analysis to model hyperparameters reveals that the Transformer’s performance is largely independent of the exact model parameter count over a 6.5x range, indicating data volume rather than model complexity is currently the bottleneck. Further analysis of forecasting errors demonstrates that both the best tree-based model and the Transformer fail at the same sudden morning weekday charging demand surges. An alternative variant of the Transformer network using modality-attention fusion (learning weights for each input feature category in a data-dependent way rather than simple concatenation) slightly but significantly reduces the mean absolute error (but not the RMSE) compared to the non-modality-attention approach and offers learned modality weights that confirm the relative importance ordering from the ablation study. We conclude that for aggregated single-station charging demand forecasting, tree-based models with SHAP are both the most accurate and explainable, whereas attention-based models provide a promising approach for integrated feature explanation with greater scalability potential as multi-year and multi-station data become available. We discuss the implications for smart-grid operation and a road map for widespread spatial deployment of our model.

Article.Title: Developmental effects of unilateral deafness are ear-independent and persist despite longstanding cochlear implant use
Article.Authors: Bartels H.; van Wieringen A.; Wouters J.; Gao H.; Reszetnik G.; Negandhi J.; Cushing S.; Gordon K.
Article.Abstract: Developmental challenges of early childhood unilateral deafness (UD) could be ear-dependent, affecting outcomes of cochlear implantation (CI). This cross-sectional cohort study assessed auditory and cognitive abilities in 57 children with early-onset UD (median [IQR] age, 10.0 [8.2–12.9] years), grouped by affected ear and CI-use, compared with age-matched children with normal hearing. Measures included spectral and temporal discrimination, speech-in-noise perception, spatial release from masking, music processing, and working memory, assessed in free-field in the best-aided condition. In CI users, a subset of measures was additionally tested with the CI switched off. Additionally, self-reported CI-benefit and daily device use were collected. While cognitive performance was similar across groups, children with UD tended to perform more poorly on complex auditory tasks ( P = .06). Outcomes were unrelated to the side of deafness or CI treatment. Among CI users, device use improved speech-in-noise perception ( P = .02) and self-reported hearing ( P < .001), but reduced spectral processing ( P = .03). Additionally, CI users scored significantly lower than untreated children on music processing ( P = .02) and daily device use declined with experience in children with contralateral normal hearing ( P < .01). Results indicate that complex auditory deficits are ear-independent and may persist despite CI use, with spectral limitations potentially contributing to difficulties integrating electric and normal-hearing input.

Article.Title: Construction of urdu paraphrase types corpus (UPTC‑23) to detect fourteen urdu paraphrase types using multilingual BERT and distilBERT
Article.Authors: Shahzad F.; Valsalan P.; Hashmi A.; Amentie M.
Article.Abstract: This study addresses the limited availability of linguistic resources for fine-grained Urdu paraphrase types identification by developing a manually annotated corpus and evaluating multilingual transformer models for a fourteen-class sentence-level classification task. A new Urdu Paraphrase Types Corpus (UPTC-23) was constructed comprising five thousand sentence pairs, manually annotated into fourteen Urdu paraphrase types based on the linguistically motivated typology. Sentence pairs compiled from the COUNTER corpus, online Urdu news articles, and manually curated linguistic examples to ensure comprehensive coverage of all fourteen Urdu paraphrase types. The resulting sentence pairs are subsequently subjected to manual preprocessing, quality verification, and annotation using predefined annotation guidelines. To evaluate the proposed corpus, multilingual BERT and DistilBERT models fine-tuned on the annotated dataset were used to identify the Urdu paraphrase type of each Urdu sentence pair by classifying it into one of the fourteen predefined Urdu paraphrase types. Experimental results demonstrate that the multilingual BERT-base-cased achieved the best performance, obtaining 92.97% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 92%, while the multilingual DistilBERT-base-cased model achieved 91.87% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 92%. Unlike existing Urdu paraphrase resources, which primarily support paraphrase identification or semantic textual similarity tasks, UPTC-23 provides fine-grained annotations of fourteen Urdu paraphrase types to support automatic Urdu paraphrase types identification. The proposed corpus constitutes a valuable linguistic resource for Urdu natural language processing and provides empirical evidence of the effectiveness of multilingual transformer models for fine-grained paraphrase types identification in low-resource languages. Although the current corpus comprises annotated sentence pairs collected from the COUNTER corpus, online Urdu news articles, and manually curated examples, future work will extend the corpus to include additional textual domains and larger datasets for broader coverage of Urdu paraphrase types identification phenomena.

Article.Title: Efficiency of photocatalytic ozonation process in the presence of CoFe₂O₄/ZnTiO₃/Ag nanocomposite for the removal of bisphenol a from aqueous solutions
Article.Authors: Hatami O.; Dehghani R.; Sobhani-Nasab A.; Yazdani A.; Rahmani H.
Article.Abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting compound, persists in aquatic environments and resists conventional wastewater treatment, posing ecological and human health risks. In this study, a magnetic CoFe₂O₄/ZnTiO₃/Ag ternary nanocomposite was prepared by co-precipitation and calcination and tested as a heterogeneous catalyst for BPA removal by photocatalytic ozonation (6 W UV-C lamp, 0.2 g/h ozone) in a model aqueous system. XRD showed reflections of a spinel phase and metallic silver together with weak reflections attributed to ilmenite-type ZnTiO₃; however, the iron-rich EDX composition and an XRD pattern of the calcined core that includes reflections consistent with hematite show that the material is not phase-pure. Batch experiments (one run per condition) varied initial BPA concentration (10–50 mg/L), catalyst dosage (0.25–0.75 g/L), pH (4–10) and reaction time (up to 240 min). Under the best conditions tested (pH 7, 0.5 g/L catalyst, 10 mg/L BPA), BPA removal reached 91.30% and COD removal 82.5% after 240 min. Under the same conditions, removal was 76.09% for UV-C/O₃, 70.65% for O₃ alone, 9.78% for UV-C alone and 1.09% for the catalyst alone. The catalyst with UV-C but without ozone removed 85.87%, and the catalyst with ozone but without light removed 80.43%, so the composite acted both as a photocatalyst and as an ozonation catalyst. A 400 W metal halide lamp used as a simulated-sunlight source gave no improvement over the catalyst/O₃ system (80.65% versus 80.43%). The apparent rate constant of the three-component process was about 1.8 times the sum of those of the single processes but only about 1.25 times that of the best two-component process (catalyst/UV-C). Removal fell from 91.30% to 47.83% over seven reuse cycles, while the catalyst was easily recovered with a magnet. The proposed mechanism and degradation pathway are hypotheses based on the literature and on tentatively identified intermediates and were not tested directly. The results suggest that the system is a promising option for BPA removal in model water; regeneration, metal leaching, toxicity of the treated water and performance in real wastewater remain to be studied.

Article.Title: Molecular identification and spatial distribution of cutaneous leishmaniasis cases in Markazi Province, central Iran, using ITS1 PCR RFLP and GIS
Article.Authors: Yousefi B.; Gholamrezaei M.; Eslami G.; Hanafi-Bojd A.; Vakili M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) remains a considerable public health concern in Iran. This study aimed to characterize Leishmania spp. among available diagnostic specimens and describe the spatial distribution of cases reported in the Markazi Province during 2021–2022. In this cross-sectional study, all 210 microscopically confirmed CL cases were analyzed using a total census sampling method. A subset of 42 cases with available diagnostic smears was evaluated by internal transcribed spacer 1-polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (ITS1-PCR-RFLP) for species identification, followed by sequencing of four representative amplicons. Spatial distribution of the 42 molecularly characterized cases was mapped using a Geographic Information System (GIS; ArcGIS 10) based on recorded coordinates. Among all 210 cases, CL was more frequent in males (57.1%) with the highest proportion in the 40–49-year age group (20.5%). Lesions were predominantly ulcerative with exudate and localized to the extremities. All 42 molecularly analyzed samples were identified as Leishmania major , though this convenient subset may not fully represent the overall species composition across the entire province. Phylogenetic analysis confirmed that the sequenced isolates clustered within the L. major clade. GIS-based descriptive mapping indicated that analyzed cases were localized primarily in Saveh and Mahallat counties. These findings provide an updated baseline for CL in Markazi Province; however, systematic molecular surveys and vector-reservoir investigations are needed to fully delineate species distribution and transmission dynamics across all counties.

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of bacterial diversity in small water bodies of the Eastern Pamir mountains using amplicon-based and metagenomic approaches
Article.Authors: Łach Ł.; Rudak A.; Karnkowska A.; Karlicki M.; Hollender M.; Smacchia V.; Suska-Malawska M.; Kwiatowski J.; Hisoriev H.; Jasser I.
Article.Abstract: Microbial diversity in remote extreme environments remains poorly understood. We investigated sediment microbial communities in small water bodies of the Eastern Pamir cold desert using V3–V4 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomics, to assess taxonomic and functional diversity. Amplicon data showed high Pseudomonadota abundance and taxa overlooked in the 2019 analysis, including Vampirovibrionaceae. Reanalysis of the amplicon data increased taxonomic assessment from 54% to 93% without changes in the number of unique sequences. Comparison of amplicon and metagenome-derived 16S profiles revealed limited overlap: only 15% of metagenomic V3–V4 sequences were detected in amplicons. Fourteen of 37 phyla were exclusive to ASVs, whereas three (of 20) to MAGs. Metagenomics recovered 86 MAGs spanning 26 classes, predominantly from Bacteroidota. Sulfur oxidation and sulfate reduction pathways occurred mainly in Pseudomonadota. Phototrophic potential was identified in 25 MAGs, largely Bacteroidota and established phototrophic lineages; most possessed complete nitrogen-fixation pathways. Eight genera detected with all methods belonged to halophilic or halotolerant lineages. These findings highlight salinity as an important driver of bacterial community composition in Eastern Pamir benthic communities and identify differences between methods. Integrating amplicon sequencing and metagenomics provides complementary insights into microbial diversity and metabolic potential in remote extreme environments.

Article.Title: Evaluation of occupational exposure to benzene, human health risk, and associated factors among gasoline station workers in South Wollo Zone, Northeast Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Keleb A.; Ademas A.; Abebe M.; Berihun G.; Wolde E.; Teshome D.; Bezie A.
Article.Abstract: Even though benzene exposure is an internationally established occupational and public health issue, there is limited empirical evidence on the scope, health risks, and predictors among gasoline station workers in Ethiopia, particularly in South Wollo Zone. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate benzene exposure, health risks, and associated factors among gasoline station workers in the South Wollo Zone, Ethiopia, addressing a critical evidence gap. A cross-sectional exposure assessment was conducted among 61 gas fueling workers and 61 administrative staff as controls. Participants were selected by simple random sampling. Breathing zone benzene concentrations were measured with RAD130S personal passive sampler. Occupation-related data were gathered through face-to-face interviews and observations. The data were checked for completeness, recorded, and exported to SPSS version 25.0 for cleaning and analysis. In the multivariable analysis, variables with a p < 0.05 were considered significantly associated with non-cancer risk levels. The overall airborne benzene concentration inworkers’ breathing zones ranged from 0.032 to 4.160 mg/m³ with a mean of 0.608 mg/m³. Gas fueling workers had higher levels, ranging from 0.064 to 4.160 mg/m³, and administrative staff ranged from 0.032 to 2.560 mg/m³ (0.01–0.80 ppm) with a mean of 0.377 mg/m³. On the other hand, excess lifetime cancer risk among gas fueling workers ranged from 5.17 × 10 − 6 to 3.02 × 10 − 4 , whereas among admin staff, it ranged from 2.58 × 10 − 6 to 2.07 × 10 − 4 . Being a gas-fueling worker (AOR = 3.92, 95% CI: 1.48–10.37), not using personal protective equipment (AOR = 2.71, 95% CI: 1.08–6.78), and not receiving job training (AOR = 2.69, 95% CI: 1.05–6.78) were statistically significant with unacceptable non-cancer risk. More than three-quarters of gas station workers are exposed to benzene levels above occupational limits, posing cancer and non-cancer risks. Gas-fueling workers have a 50% higher lifetime cancer risk compared to admin staff. Providing PPE, improving ventilation systems, and enhancing safety training by employers, proper utilization of PPE, and adopting positive behavior among workers can significantly reduce gasoline exposure and minimize associated health risks.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of overall survival after lung SBRT using clinical, dosimetric, and radiomics features: a multicenter study
Article.Authors: Invernizzi C.; Benveniste P.; El Ayachy R.; Leroy T.; Blanchard N.; Schipman B.; Debelleix C.; Chamois J.; Pointreau Y.; Bibault J.
Article.Abstract: Radiomics combined with clinical and dosimetric data may improve outcome prediction after lung stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This study aimed to develop machine-learning models to predict overall survival (OS) after lung SBRT for primary and metastatic lung tumours using planning-CT-derived features. Clinical and dosimetric data were retrospectively collected from six centres. Radiomic features were extracted using double tumour segmentation and filtered for reproducibility (intraclass correlation ≥ 0.80). From 181 lesions in 158 patients, 180 features (124 radiomic, 45 clinical, 11 dosimetric) were aggregated to the patient level. OS was modelled as a time-to-event outcome using random survival forests, per tumour origin and pooled with tumour origin as a covariate; features were selected by LASSO within cross-validation folds and interpreted with SHAP. The pooled model achieved a concordance index of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54–0.71) with time-dependent AUC of 0.69, 0.62 and 0.52 at 1, 2 and 3 years; a temporal split preserved this (0.61) whereas leave-one-centre-out validation gave a pooled concordance index of 0.57 (95% CI 0.48–0.65). Adding dosimetric and radiomic features to a clinical model increased discrimination (ΔC + 0.12, 95% CI 0.001–0.244). Recurrence- and metastasis-free survival, examined as secondary endpoints, were near chance. These leakage-free, censoring-appropriate models provide an honest, hypothesis-generating benchmark for OS prediction after lung SBRT, most informative at one year, that will require external validation.

Article.Title: Effects of exogenous melatonin on growth, physiological traits, mineral element concentrations, and essential oil percentage of peppermint (Mentha piperita L.) under cadmium stress
Article.Authors: Shamsabadi V.; Moradi M.; Mirzaei S.; Roosta H.
Article.Abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination poses a serious threat to the growth, yield, and quality of medicinal plants. This study investigated the potential of exogenous melatonin (MT) to mitigate Cd-induced damage in peppermint ( Mentha piperita L.). A factorial experiment based on a completely randomized design was conducted with three cadmium chloride (CdCl 2 ) treatments (0, 75, and 150 mg L⁻ 1 CdCl 2 ) and three MT levels (0, 75, and 150 µM), with three replications. Cadmium chloride (CdCl 2 ) was supplied through the irrigation water, whereas melatonin was applied foliarly. Results showed that increasing Cd stress progressively reduced shoot dry weight (27.64–46.64%), essential oil percentage (20.32–36.36%), plant height (31.70–43.16%), chlorophyll a (9.89–15.06%), chlorophyll b (6.39–11.04%), total chlorophyll (8.62–13.57%), carotenoids (20.23–32.14%), SPAD index (7.34–13.31%), water use efficiency (26.45–44.59%), and leaf iron (17.68–55.49%) and zinc concentrations, while increasing leaf Cd concentration .However, MT application at 75 and 150 µM significantly alleviated these negative effects, increasing shoot dry weight (67.98–96.84%), essential oil percentage (60.78–85.29%), plant height (40.18–63.69%), photosynthetic pigment levels, SPAD index (9.86–14.79%), water use efficiency (67.73–99.21%), and leaf Fe, Zn, and K concentrations, while reducing leaf Na and Cd concentrations. The Cd × MT interaction was significant for shoot dry weight, essential oil percentage, plant height, SPAD index, water use efficiency, and leaf concentrations of Fe, Zn, Na, and Cd. In contrast, chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, total chlorophyll, carotenoids, and leaf K concentration were affected by the main effects of Cd and MT, with no significant interaction. Under the highest CdCl 2 concentration (150 mg L⁻ 1 ), foliar application of 150 µM MT increased shoot dry weight and essential oil percentage by 115.20% and 111.43%, respectively, compared with the corresponding treatment without MT. These findings indicate that exogenous melatonin improved several growth, physiological, and mineral-related traits of peppermint under the Cd exposure conditions tested.

Article.Title: Explainable texture fusion for pediatric pneumonia classification using chest radiographs
Article.Authors: Kantasa P.; Yana B.; Praphasawat R.; Wongrach K.; Palamee T.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluates a two-branch deep–texture fusion framework for pediatric pneumonia classification from chest radiographs. EfficientNet-B0 encodes the raw image, while ResNet-18 encodes three gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) maps: contrast, dissimilarity, and entropy. Squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention jointly recalibrates the concatenated embeddings before classification. The contribution is this integration strategy and its evaluation, rather than a new backbone, descriptor, or attention operator. The 5,856-image dataset was repartitioned into 4,099 training, 877 validation, and 880 test images, using identical assignments for all configurations. SE fusion achieved accuracy of 0.9818, F1-score of 0.9875, AUROC of 0.9958, and Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.9539. Its accuracy exceeded raw EfficientNet-B0 by five correct predictions and ungated fusion by six. Other configurations achieved higher sensitivity or specificity. The mean normalized texture gate was 0.0759, but this gate summary is not a measure of causal importance; the benefit over simpler auxiliary features remains untested. Attribution and perturbation analyses are model audits, without radiologist-validated localization. The study uses one image-level split, with no external or repeated cross-validation, and patient independence cannot be verified. The results support further investigation on this benchmark but do not establish clinical generalizability or deployment suitability.

Article.Title: Growth and physiological responses of Populus nigra L. to salinity stress following inoculation with indigenous arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi
Article.Authors: Salehi A.; Matinizadeh M.; Nouri E.
Article.Abstract: Populus nigra L. is an economically important tree species whose growth and physiological performance can be adversely affected by salinity. Given that mycorrhizal fungi can provide external assistance to plants under adverse environmental conditions, this study aimed to evaluate the salt tolerance of one-year-old P. nigra “62/154” plants following inoculation with indigenous arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF). We conducted a greenhouse experiment using a randomized complete block design involving two factors: (1) mycorrhizal status (inoculated with native AMF or not) and (2) salinity stress (0, 50, 100, 150, and 200 mM NaCl). Subsequently, morphological, biochemical, and physiological responses of the poplar plants were measured. Our results showed a marked decrease in survival, growth, biomass, leaf relative water content (RWC), and nitrogen (N), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) concentrations of plant tissues with increasing salinity stress. In contrast, salt stress increased antioxidant activities and the concentrations of sodium (Na), chloride (Cl), phosphorus (P), and micronutrients in plant tissues. AMF-inoculated (AMF+) plants showed improved growth, biomass, leaf RWC, and some macronutrient concentrations at low to moderate salinity (0–100 mM NaCl), and enhanced some antioxidant activities at 0 and 50 mM NaCl. AMF reduced shoot sodium and chloride concentrations only at 100 mM NaCl, while the positive effects of AMF on micronutrient concentrations persisted at higher salinity levels. The reductions in survival, growth and biomass, together with changes in physiological traits, nutrient balance, and shoot accumulation of proline, sodium, and chloride, indicate that P. nigra “62/154” is sensitive to salinity. These findings highlight the importance of managing soil salinity to maintain the optimal performance of this poplar clone. Moreover, the observed benefits of inoculation with indigenous AMF indicate their potential to contribute to salinity tolerance under low to moderate salinity. Further long-term field studies are needed to determine whether these effects persist under prolonged salinity stress and variable field conditions.

Article.Title: Exploring surplus resource theory and the role of dietary energy in the expression of play behaviour in pigs
Article.Authors: Hewett E.; Houdijk J.; Lewis C.; Doeschl-Wilson A.; Turner S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Surplus Resource Theory proposes that play behaviour is expressed more abundantly in juveniles that have access to necessary resources. We propose that sufficient dietary energy is likely to be a requirement for play and therefore hypothesise that pigs on an energy-deficient diet will show reduced play. A total of 128 mixed sex pigs of 28 days old, were randomly allocated across two diets: control (CE) or low energy (LE). Pigs were given access to a play arena, for 20 min, 4 times over 10 days and on alternative occasions, before entering the arena, offered a sucrose supplement. We hypothesised the provision of sucrose would increase play, particularly for pigs on the LE diet. Dietary treatment and play session interacted on social object ( P = 0.025), solo locomotor ( P < 0.001) and social locomotor play ( P < 0.001). Dietary treatment and pen mate average sugar intake interacted on social object ( P = 0.019) and social locomotor play ( P < 0.001). The interaction between dietary treatment and pen mate average sugar intake ( P = 0.002) affected total play. Overall, the CE diet appeared to extend the developmental period of heightened engagement in social play. Our findings suggest that diet quality in weaned pigs may impact specific aspects of play behaviour with potential benefits for animal welfare.

Article.Title: Murine splenic CD45 + erythroid cells display a transcriptomic signature of antigen-presenting cells
Article.Authors: Nazarov K.; Alrhmoun S.; Perik-Zavodskaia O.; Perik-Zavodskii R.; Vasilev E.; Shevchenko J.; Sennikov S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract CD45-positive erythroid cells represent a distinct erythroid population described in mice and humans, but their molecular characteristics in the adult spleen remain incompletely defined. Here, we characterize the immune-associated molecular features of murine splenic CD45-positive erythroid cells using complementary cytometric, transcriptomic, spatial, and epigenetic approaches. Flow cytometry resolved CD45-positive and CD45-negative Ter119-positive erythroid cells and showed that a coordinated panel of immunoregulatory molecules—Galectin-3, Galectin-9, CXCR4, PD-L1 and the cytokines MCP-1 and TGF-β1—was expressed by the CD45-positive fraction but was largely absent from CD45-negative erythroid cells, identifying this immune phenotype as a specific feature of CD45-positive erythroid cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed immune-associated transcriptional programs in CD45-positive erythroid cells, including MHC class II antigen presentation, antimicrobial, and immunoregulatory genes. The MHC class II-associated module expression reached levels comparable to those observed in monocytes, while computational analysis predicted potential MHC-II-associated communication with T-cell populations. Spatial transcriptomics localized CD45-positive erythroid cells predominantly to the splenic red pulp. Independent NanoString profiling confirmed these immune-associated programs across Ter119-positive splenic erythroid cells, while epigenetic profiling provided complementary regulatory context. Under hematopoietic stress and within tumors, CD45-positive erythroid cells displayed context-dependent changes in immune-associated phenotypes. Together, these findings show a reproducible immune-associated APC-like gene signature of murine splenic CD45-positive erythroid cells.

Article.Title: Nrf2 inhibition overcomes regorafenib resistance in well-differentiated sorafenib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma cells
Article.Authors: Kahraman E.; Kiriş H.; İnci T.; Şanlı U.; Göker E.
Article.Abstract: Sorafenib is one of the most effective agent used in the systemic treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, patients often develop resistance to sorafenib over time, thereby limiting its therapeutic efficacy. Potential efficacy of combined treatment of regorafenib with Nrf2 inhibitors in sorafenib-resistant HCC cells remains unclear. Therefore, in this study, we investigated whether inhibition of the Nrf2 pathway could enhance the anticancer activity of regorafenib in sorafenib-resistant HCC cell lines. In HuH-7 SorRes cells, IC 50 values following regorafenib treatment were 4.9-fold and 2-fold higher at 48 and 72 h, respectively, compared to parental HuH-7 cells. Similar resistance patterns were observed in Mahlavu SorRes cells. Western blot analysis revealed upregulation of Nrf2 expression in HuH-7 SorRes cells. Suppression of the Nrf2 pathway in HuH-7 SorRes cells resulted in a significant reduction in cell viability and ERK1/2 phosphorylation, along with increased cleaved caspase-3 expression, elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species levels, and decreased cell migration. Furthermore, in 3D tumor spheroid models, regorafenib significantly inhibited spheroid growth in HuH-7 SorRes cells under Nrf2-suppressed conditions. In conclusion, our study demonstrated that HCC cells which developed resistance to sorafenib also exhibited resistance to regorafenib, and this resistance could be overcome by inhibition of the Nrf2 signaling pathway.

Article.Title: A bidirectional strong tracking filter for nonlinear state estimation with multiplicative model uncertainty
Article.Authors: Li W.; Wen C.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Navigation and maneuvering target tracking are fundamental to autonomous systems such as unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles, intelligent robots, aircraft guidance systems, and radar surveillance systems, with the core task of achieving accurate and reliable estimation of key states including position, velocity, acceleration, and attitude. Under high-speed maneuvers, complex environments, and multisensor fusion conditions, nonlinearities, model uncertainties, and time-varying environmental disturbances may degrade the estimation accuracy of the conventional Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and even cause filter divergence. Although the Strong Tracking Filter (STF) exhibits strong adaptability to model mismatch, it mainly compensates for prediction errors by adjusting the predicted error covariance matrix, without directly addressing uncertainties in the state-transition model. Consequently, its estimation performance remains limited in complex dynamic environments. To address these issues, this paper uses weighted least squares (WLS) to identify an equivalent multiplicative state-transition uncertainty factor and directly compensate the prediction model. The compensation targets model mismatch that can be approximated by scalar scaling of the nominal state-transition term. Furthermore, by integrating state-model information with the statistical characteristics of uncertain factors, an information-augmented state prediction method and a corresponding error covariance calculation method are proposed. By directly compensating the state prediction model, the proposed method aims to improve the consistency and accuracy of state prediction and covariance propagation under maneuvering conditions and external disturbances. On this basis, a novel strong tracking filter is developed within the EKF–STF framework by integrating WLS-based identification of multiplicative state-transition uncertainty, state prediction compensation, and covariance-associated information enhancement. The conventional one-way inflation mechanism of the STF is extended to a bidirectional adjustment mechanism capable of both inflation and contraction, enabling the filter to adapt to variations in model uncertainties. This allows the filter to balance tracking adaptability under maneuvering conditions with estimation accuracy under steady-state conditions. Finally, a conditional covariance analysis characterizes the ESTF-1–STF comparison under the stated assumptions. Numerical simulations show improved estimation accuracy for ESTF-1 relative to the selected STF and EKF baselines in the tested scenarios, with ESTF-0 included as an oracle reference.

Article.Title: Blood-based fibrosis scores align with liver stiffness measured by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography in type 2 diabetes
Article.Authors: Marie Č.; Karolin S.; Moustafa E.; Michal K.; Adam U.; Jan P.; Iva H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at high risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This exploratory cross-sectional analysis examined associations of 18 liver scores, bioimpedance-derived body composition, and three exploratory circulating biomarkers with two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE), shear-wave dispersion (SWD), and attenuation imaging (ATI) in 40 adults with T2DM and suspected liver involvement. Spearman and age- and sex-adjusted partial Spearman correlations were evaluated with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and 10,000-resample bootstrap confidence intervals. Fourteen fibrosis-oriented scores correlated with 2D-SWE after outcome-specific FDR correction; thirteen remained significant across 54 score-ultrasound comparisons. The largest positive coefficient was observed for DiabetesLiver (ρ = 0.527; 95% CI 0.257–0.726), followed by the Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4; ρ = 0.516; 95% CI 0.224–0.730). Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) and LiverRisk correlations were 0.444 (0.153–0.674) and 0.408 (0.076–0.669); broader q ≤ 0.030. ATI correlated with three metabolically weighted scores. No body-composition association survived the broader 75-test correction. No score-SWD or biomarker-ultrasound association met q < 0.05; limited power warrants caution. Moderate associations with liver stiffness do not establish diagnostic equivalence. Findings are consistent with guideline-recommended two-step risk stratification for advanced liver fibrosis in MASLD: FIB-4 followed, when indicated, by liver stiffness measurement or ELF.

Article.Title: Synchronization independent three-dimensional localization of LEO satellites using passive distributed ground antennas and staged dimensionality reduction
Article.Authors: Khorshidi M.; Samimi H.; Orvatinia M.; Karimzadeh Baee R.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a novel synchronization-free method for three-dimensional (3D) positioning of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites using a network of distributed passive ground antennas. By combining improved relative Received Signal Strength (RSS) measurements with Apollonius circle geometry, the proposed method leverages a multi-stage dimensionality reduction technique to enhance the precision of target estimation in multi-receiver systems. The initial stage estimates the projection of the satellite’s position onto the two-dimensional (2D) XY plane through an improved relative RSS algorithm. In the second stage, the satellite altitude is estimated by minimizing a cost function formulated from the Rician channel amplitude model. A multi-snapshot averaging strategy is utilized to mitigate Rician fading and additive noise, reducing the amplitude estimation variance by a factor of N through the coherent averaging of N independent snapshots. Theoretical results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 3D positioning median accuracy of approximately 31.41 km and a 3D angular error of 6.55 degree over 200 Monte Carlo trials with randomly distributed satellite positions spanning altitudes from 100 to 500 km. The robustness and sensitivity of the proposed algorithm are further evaluated under variations in receiver height, SNR, receiver antenna gain, shadowing and Rician channel parameters. Notably, these performance levels are attained without the need for inter-receiver synchronization, complex hardware, complex computational burden or prior knowledge of satellite ephemeris.
