Article.Title: Phytonutrient, phytochemical, bioactivity, and genetic fidelity profiling of meta-Topolin-derived plants of an underutilised medicinal herb Solanum virginianum L
Article.Authors: Biswas D.; Mukherjee S.; Ghosh B.
Article.Abstract: The rising trends in pathogen multidrug-resistance, malnutrition, and population growth have become globally concerning issues. These may be addressed by harnessing the nutritional and ethnomedicinal potential of underexploited wild plants like Solanum virginianum . This study has focused on profiling several nutritional and medicinal bioactive components and characterize bioactivities of S. virginianum to evaluate its promising prospects, and develop a sustainable mass production system for the plant. Initial LC-MS/MS screening of the methanolic leaf-crude-extract of the plant has shown the presence of 17 distinct pharmacologically important phenolic, flavonoid, saponin, and alkaloid compounds. Maximum shoot multiplication (42.10 ± 0.06) and root numbers (15.10 ± 0.15) were observed in MS + 0.2 mg/l thiadiazuron + 0.2 mg/l meta- Topolin and ½ MS + 1.0 mg/l indole-3-butyric acid media. The regenerated plants were proven to be genetically similar with mother plant using inter-simple sequence repeat (ISSR) and start-codon targeted (SCoT) markers. The regenerants were also found to be similar to or slightly better than the mother plants in terms of soluble proteins, amino acids (glycine, phenylalanine, threonine, valine), vitamin B and C, steroidal alkaloids (khasianine, solamargine, solasodine, solanine, solasonine), and 14 different phenolic acids (caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid) and flavonoids (luteolin, myricetin). The regenerated and source plants also showed comparable antioxidant activity (DPPH, ABTS, FRAP) and antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogens. This study provides a comprehensive account of the nutritional and medicinal prospects of S. virginianum , along with a reproducible micropropagation protocol. These information can be helpful in future investigations related to possible commercial exploitation of the plant in the pharmaceutical or food industries.

Article.Title: Fracture propagation analysis of limited-entry perforation in horizontal multi-cluster fracturing considering thermal effects
Article.Authors: Jiang H.; Xiao J.; Jiang W.; Yang L.; Ren L.; Deng C.; Tang D.; Zou L.; Zhao Z.
Article.Abstract: The long-stage multi-cluster fracturing process is widely applied in the development of deep shale reservoirs, but it also faces the challenge of non-equilibrium propagation of multiple fractures. The mechanism of the temperature disturbance caused by the injection of low-temperature fracturing fluid into deep high-temperature formations and the resulting thermal effect on the competitive extension of multi-cluster fractures has not yet been clarified. To reveal the influence of thermal effect on the competitive propagation of multi-cluster fractures, based on the finite volume method and displacement discontinuity method, a numerical model for non-planar fracture propagation in multi-stage multi-cluster fracturing considering thermal effect was established. The simulation and analysis of the limited-entry perforation fracturing under the action of thermal effects was carried out. The perforation numbers were optimized under different geological conditions. The results show that the thermal effect intensifies the non-equilibrium extension of multi-cluster fractures. When the formation temperature increases from 60 ℃ to 180 ℃, the dimensionless length variation coefficient L cv increases from 0.28 to 0.61, and the standard deviation of the transient inflow ratio Q sd increases from 6.82%. to 12.29%; Maintaining the perforation friction at 3.3 MPa ~ 7.5 MPa can eliminate to a certain extent the non-equilibrium propagation caused by the given heterogeneous ground stress, stress shadow between fractures and thermal effects; The optimal number of perforations decreases with the increase of Young’s modulus and increases with the increase of pumping rate. Increasing the pumping rate can relatively weaken the negative impact of thermal effects on the balanced inlet of each cluster. The study shows that thermal effects have an important impact on fracture propagation when the underground temperature is higher than 90 °C. The research results can provide a more comprehensive reference for deep shale fracturing design.

Article.Title: Compound environmental events in Washington coastal waters from high-resolution downscaled projections
Article.Authors: Kristiansen T.; Sydeman W.; Thayer J.; Thompson S.; García-Reyes M.; Schumacker J.; Koval G.
Article.Abstract: Coastal temperate upwelling ecosystems face increasingly frequent and persistent environmental extremes including warming, deoxygenation, and acidification, yet integrated regional assessments of future change remain limited. Here we apply high-resolution statistically downscaled CMIP6 projections (SSP2-4.5, 2017–2060) to Washington coastal waters, combining threshold-based detection to characterize individual and compound event dynamics including ocean warming (surface/bottom marine heatwaves (SHW/BHW)), deoxygenation (hypoxia), and ocean acidification (OA). We further introduce a dual-baseline framework that contrasts a fixed (historical) reference against a shifting (rolling) reference to separate long-term warming from genuine extreme short-term variability, and we quantify the time of emergence (ToE) of chronic exposure regimes (≥ 50% annual exposure sustained for three consecutive years) along with cascade lift (the conditional probability of one event type following another above its unconditional baseline). Surface waters warm at 0.032 °C yr − 1 , 67% faster than bottom waters (0.019 °C yr − 1 ), accumulating to projected increases of ~ 1.4 °C (surface) and ~ 0.8–1.2 °C (bottom) by 2060 under SSP2-4.5. Hypoxia and acidification are already chronic at baseline, with bottom oxygen declining at − 0.0034 − 1 decade -1 and pH at − 0.0011 units yr − 1 , reaching an estimated pH of ~ 7.7 by 2060. Under the fixed baseline, OA is the first chronic regime to emerge (median ToE ≈ 2028), followed by SHW (~ 2029), BHW (~ 2037) and hypoxia (~ 2038); under the shifting baseline, SHW and BHW never reach the chronic threshold over most of the domain, isolating OA and hypoxia as the persistent long-term signals. The coastal waters exhibit pervasive compound-event exposure, with 58.8% of the area experiencing high to extreme combined event exposure. Cascade-lift analysis confirms that bottom warming significantly increases the probability of subsequent hypoxia (lift ≈ 1.5–1.7 around 2025–2030), whereas acidification operates largely independently. These findings illustrate a transition from episodic to chronic compound-event regimes and underscore the need for spatially explicit frameworks to inform adaptive management in temperate upwelling systems globally.

Article.Title: An eco-friendly glucose-based dust suppressant for heavy-duty haul roads in open-pit coal mines during high-temperature seasons
Article.Authors: Lu X.; Yang F.; Zhang W.; Wu L.; Wu Z.; Shao H.; Li R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dust from heavy-duty haul roads in open-pit coal mines poses a serious environmental challenge, particularly under high-temperature summer conditions. In this study, an eco-friendly dust suppressant was developed based on physicochemical characterization of three representative dust types (coal, loess, and rock-soil) from the Haerwusu Mine. Wettability and chemical analyses revealed that coal dust exhibited the poorest wettability, whereas loess and rock-soil dusts exhibited superior wetting behavior. A formulation comprising industrial-grade glucose as the base material, SDBS as the surfactant, and glycerol/NaCl as moisture-regulating agents was optimized via single-component and orthogonal experiments. The optimal composition was determined as 30% glucose, 0.05% SDBS, 2% glycerol, and 2% NaCl. Molecular dynamics simulations elucidated the adsorption configurations and wetting mechanisms of the suppressant on quartz and coal surfaces. Field validation under actual summer conditions demonstrated that a single suppressant application at 1 L/m 2 maintained a noticeable dust suppression effect for approximately 5 h at temperatures up to 54 °C under normal truck operations during this field test, and the effect could last up to three days when combined with reduced routine watering. This work presents a sustainable, cost-effective, and operationally viable strategy for dust mitigation on haul roads in open-pit coal mines during high-temperature seasons.

Article.Title: Anterior vertebral height as an exploratory predictor for acute adjacent vertebral fracture after single-level high-viscosity cement vertebroplasty in women
Article.Authors: Liu P.; Liao H.; Lin H.; Yao Y.; Wang S.; Hsiung W.; Liu C.; Chou P.
Article.Abstract: Adjacent vertebral fracture (AVF) is a common complication following vertebroplasty (VP), particularly during the early postoperative period. We retrospectively reviewed 100 female patients (24 AVF events) who underwent single-level high-viscosity cement VP to identify candidate predictors of acute AVF within 2 months. Twenty-four baseline and operative variables were evaluated using forward logistic regression. Lower hip dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry T-score, absence of preoperative anti-osteoporosis medication, lower preoperative anterior vertebral height (AVH), and higher cement volume were independently associated with AVF. The association between AVH and AVF was replicated in an independent cohort of 45 female patients (15 AVF events) from another medical institution. The areas under curve for AVH were 0.681 (95% CI, 0.545–0.817) and 0.849 (95% CI, 0.722–0.976) in the discovery and replication cohorts, respectively. An exploratory, data-derived AVH cutoff of 1.17 cm, determined by maximizing Youden’s J index, yielded negative predictive values of 85.7% and 91.7% in the discovery and replication cohorts. AVH demonstrated discrimination comparable to two previously published scoring systems. These findings suggest that preoperative AVH may serve as a simple radiographic predictor for identifying female patients at increased risk of acute AVF after VP, but further validation is warranted given the limited sample size.

Article.Title: Genome-wide identification and deciphering the role of Ca2+-ATPase genes towards low pH stress tolerance in rice
Article.Authors: Singh G.; Pandey D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Calcium (Ca 2+ ) serves as an important secondary messenger in plant stress responses, which is largely mediated by calcium-transporting ATPase. These ATPases function in calcium homeostasis and activate distinct signalling networks necessary for plant adaptation to various stresses. Present study aims to identify and characterize Ca 2+ - ATPase genes and their comprehensive role in stress signalling mechanisms under low pH stress in contrasting rice landraces. Utilizing previous published low pH stress-impacted rice transcriptome data, bioinformatics, and computational approaches were applied to decipher the characteristics, regulatory mechanism and signalling role of Ca 2+ - ATPase genes in response to low pH stress in rice. Further, reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction was performed to see the Ca 2+ - ATPase genes expression in contrasting rice landraces under low pH stress. Result revealed that Ca 2+ - ATPase genes contain cation-transporting domains and calmodulin-binding domains involved in calcium regulation and signaling and shows evolutionary conservation and functional specialization across different plant species. Importantly, Ca 2+ ATPase8 and Ca 2+ ATPase9 showed strong syntenic relationships with Elaeis guineensis (XP_010922239), while Ca 2+ ATPase1 exhibited high alignment with Oryza sativa japonica (NP_001384944). STRING-based interaction mapping of 13 Ca 2+ -ATPase genes revealed strong functional associations, indicating their coordinated roles in calcium homeostasis and signaling pathways. The predicted localization of Ca 2+ -ATPases suggests their presence predominantly in plasma membranes and Golgi apparatus, reinforcing their role in membrane-bound calcium transport. Structural modeling and binding pocket site prediction provided reliable 3D structures, identifying potential ligand-binding sites crucial for ATPase function. The predicted secondary structure of Ca 2+ -ATPases contributed to protein stability assessment, supporting their functional integrity. Expression profiling of Ca 2+ ATPases genes like LOC_Os03g10640, Ca 2+ ATPase3, LOC_Os05g02940 and LOC_Os08g40530 showed varying expression pattern in contrasting rice landraces under low pH stress. Result infer that low pH stress indued influx of Ca 2+ causes binding of CaM-Ca 2+ to N-TRD activating Ca 2+ ATPase, and differential expression of Q10QA3, CaATPase3, ACA9 and ACA5 lead to transport Ca 2+ from cytosol to outside of plasma membrane maintaining homeostasis in the cell.

Article.Title: Sleep disturbance mediates the effects of nighttime infant feeding and husband's companionship on postpartum depression
Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Yu L.; Tao M.; Jiang R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postpartum depression is a serious condition affecting mothers, infants, and their families. This study investigates factors associated with postpartum depression and their interrelationships, with a focus on the mediating role of sleep disturbance. This cross-sectional study included 663 postpartum women who completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Logistic regression was used to explore factors associated with postpartum depression and sleep disturbance, and mediation analysis was performed to explore the interrelationships among these factors. In this study, 11.8% of postpartum women had an EPDS score ≥ 13. Factors associated with postpartum depression included previous emotional problems, discordant relationships with family members and husband, higher nighttime infant feeding frequency, poor dietary satisfaction, and less Husband's companionship time. After adjusting for confounders, sleep disturbance was found to mediate the association between nighttime infant feeding frequency and postpartum depression (11.3% of the total effect) and between Husband's companionship time and postpartum depression (8.0% of the total effect). This study clarifies the factors associated with postpartum depression and their interrelationships, including the direct and indirect associations of nighttime infant feeding frequency and Husband's companionship time with postpartum depression through the mediation of sleep disturbance.

Article.Title: Association of valgus knee alignment with hallux valgus in individuals with knee osteoarthritis in the population based ROAD study
Article.Authors: Kuhara R.; Matsumoto T.; Adachi S.; Takeda R.; Iidaka T.; Horii C.; Oka H.; Muraki S.; Hashizume H.; Yamada H.; Yoshida M.; Nakamura K.; Tanaka S.; Yoshimura N.
Article.Abstract: Hallux valgus (HV) and hallux rigidus (HR) are common forefoot deformities, but their relationships with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and coronal knee alignment remain incompletely understood. This study examined associations between knee alignment, KOA, and the prevalence of HV and HR in a population-based cohort. Data were obtained from the fifth survey of the Research on Osteoarthritis/Osteoporosis Against Disability (ROAD) cohort in Japan. After exclusions, 3,582 knees and feet were analyzed. Knee alignment was classified into varus, neutral, and valgus groups using sex-specific femorotibial angle thresholds derived from knees without osteoarthritis. KOA was defined as Kellgren–Lawrence grade 3–4. HV and HR were assessed on foot radiographs. Generalized estimating equations accounted for clustering of bilateral limbs. HV prevalence was 29.4% and HR prevalence was 7.7%. In the whole cohort, HV was associated with neither KOA nor alignment. In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis among women with KOA, valgus versus neutral alignment was associated with HV in an adjusted analysis (adjusted OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.22–6.78; P = 0.011; global alignment P = 0.013), although the formal alignment × KOA interaction was not significant (P = 0.079). HR was not independently associated with KOA or knee alignment after multivariable adjustment. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a possible association between valgus knee alignment and HV among women with KOA, although the overall alignment × KOA interaction was not statistically significant. This finding should therefore be interpreted cautiously. HR was not independently associated with knee alignment.

Article.Title: Modeling and NSFD discretization of HIV dynamics under Crowley–Martin incidence
Article.Authors: Naser M.; Sweilam N.; Elsakout D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, we consider an in-host HIV infection model which takes into account logistic growth for CD4 $$^+$$ T cells, the recovery rate of infected cells, and Crowley–Martin form of two-sided saturated incidence function. The main novelty of the proposed model lies in extending a classical logistic HIV framework by introducing the Crowley–Martin incidence mechanism, which captures mutual interference and saturation effects between healthy cells and free virions, thereby providing a more realistic description of infection dynamics at high population densities. In addition, a nonstandard finite difference NSFD scheme is developed to preserve the essential qualitative properties of the continuous model. First, we show that all solutions of the model are positive and bounded and calculate the basic reproduction number $$R_0$$ using the next-generation matrix technique. It follows from our analysis that the disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if $$R_0 < 1$$ and globally asymptotically stable under an additional sufficient condition, while the existence of at least one biologically interpretable endemic equilibrium and its local stability occurs if $$R_0> 1$$ . The existence of an endemic equilibrium is described by a quartic polynomial whose constant term changes sign at $$R_0=1$$ . In order to preserve biologically relevant properties of the continuous problem in the discrete-time case, we propose a semi-implicit NSFD scheme that is designed to preserve the qualitative behavior of the continuous model.

Article.Title: Privacy and security preservation of bitcoin digital currency transactions on mixing services using enhanced heuristic-aided optimal weighted features and hybrid deep learning network
Article.Authors: Ezhilmathi S.; Samy S D.
Article.Abstract: Bitcoin (BTC) is a Peer-to-Peer (P2P) digital currency that facilitates transactions using pseudonymous identities. Mixing services improve the anonymity of transactions but are misused for illicit activities such as money laundering, raising security concerns in the BTC ecosystem. This research implements a hybridized deep learning approach for privacy preservation in BTC transactions. The required data are gathered from Elliptic Dataset and Ethereum Fraud Detection dataset, and these datasets are used for evaluation. The features are extracted from these datasets, followed by weighted attribute selection. The optimal feature selection and fine-tuning of the weights are implemented using the Improved Current Mussel Time-based Eurasian Oystercatcher Optimizer (ICMT-EOO) algorithm. The weighted attributes are classified using a Faster Regions-based Convolutional Neural Network with Dilated Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (FRCNN-DBi-LSTM). Experimental evaluation is performed using existing classifiers and optimization algorithms to demonstrate the efficiency of the approach. The proposed method achieves an accuracy of 95.2%, an F1-score of 92.98%, a recall of 95.21%, and a precision of 90.84%, respectively. The results confirm that the developed model achieves improved performance and enhanced security compared to existing methods.

Article.Title: Spectral moment embedding: a matrix-moment generalisation of characteristic response analysis for covariance-based signal classification
Article.Authors: Lahiri J.; Panwar S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Covariance descriptors summarise cross-channel dependence in biosignal and machinery classification, but compact eigenvector summaries can map distinct covariance matrices to identical features. We define Spectral Moment Embedding (SME), a sign-invariant matrix-moment representation that preserves covariance information targeted by Characteristic Response Analysis (CRA) and its Positive-Orthant Characteristic Response (POCR), while avoiding non-injectivity from positive-orthant eigenvector summation. SME regularises each epoch covariance, forms $${\varvec{C}},{\varvec{C}}^2,\ldots ,{\varvec{C}}^p$$ by dense multiplication, and applies diagonal, upper-triangular half-vectorisation, or row-sum projections; a sub-window trajectory variant tests non-stationary trials. Five public datasets were evaluated under strict subject- or recording-grouped cross-validation against CRA/POCR, covariance, Riemannian, polynomial, and spectral baselines. SME exceeded POCR on Sleep-EDF staging ( $$64.5\%$$ vs. $$44.2\%$$ ), MIT-BIH arrhythmia ( $$37.7\%$$ vs. $$19.2\%$$ ), CWRU bearing faults ( $$84.1\%$$ vs. $$45.5\%$$ ), and UCI HAR ( $$80.5\%$$ vs. $$62.0\%$$ ). Motor imagery was negative: static SME reached $$30.2\%$$ against POCR at $$31.9\%$$ , and trajectory-SME fell to $$25.6\%$$ . In sleep staging, multitaper PSD led globally ( $$71.9\%$$ ), whereas SME retained a narrow N3 F1 advantage (0.806 vs. 0.782). Timing followed $$\mathcal {O}(N^3p)$$ scaling and was three-to-five times faster than POCR at $$N=128$$ . SME is therefore a general covariance-moment algorithm, strongest when stable cross-channel covariance carries class information.

Article.Title: A novel integrated RSM-spherical fuzzy AHP-fuzzy MARCOS approach for drilling optimisation and enhanced strength in the sustainable fabrication of magnesium alloys via stir casting using bio-waste materials
Article.Authors: Sivam S.; Umasekar V.; Lazar P.; Kesavan S.; Sathishkumar P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of lightweight and sustainable metal matrix composites has become increasingly important for advanced engineering applications requiring high strength-to-weight ratios and improved functional performance. This study presents the fabrication of a sustainable Magnesium (Mg) hybrid composite incorporating marine bio-waste-derived reinforcements, namely fish bone ash (FBA) and seashell ash (SSA), along with Boron Carbide (B₄C), Silicon Carbide (SiC), Graphite, and Zinc (Zn) using a stir casting technique. The developed composite was investigated through microstructural characterization, mechanical evaluation, wear assessment, corrosion analysis, and optimization of drilling performance. The incorporation of FBA and SSA promoted reinforcement-induced strengthening through improved particle–matrix interactions, grain refinement, and enhanced load-bearing capacity. At the same time, B₄C and SiC contributed to improved hardness and wear resistance. The drilling performance of the developed Mg hybrid composite was optimized using a hybrid framework integrating Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Spherical Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (SF-AHP), and Fuzzy Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to Compromise Solution (Fuzzy MARCOS). The proposed optimization approach simultaneously considered multiple machining responses, including thrust force, torque, surface roughness, and hole diameter accuracy, thereby enabling the identification of optimal drilling conditions under conflicting performance requirements. Statistical analysis confirmed the adequacy of the developed predictive models, while confirmation experiments demonstrated good agreement between predicted and experimental responses. This study provides an integrated strategy combining marine bio-waste valorization, sustainable magnesium composite development, and uncertainty-based machining optimization. The findings advance environmentally conscious lightweight materials and provide a practical framework for improving the manufacturing efficiency of sustainable Mg-based hybrid composites.

Article.Title: Nonlinear fractional oscillatory dynamics in memory-dependent Stuart–Landau networks: wave propagation and pattern formation
Article.Authors: Almatroud O.; Damag F.; Albosaily S.; Ennaceur M.; Alameri A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This work investigates nonlinear fractional oscillatory dynamics governed by memory-dependent Stuart-Landau oscillator networks (SLNM) formulated through the Erdelyi-Kober (EK) fractional operator. To obtain analytical-computational solutions, the homotopy recursive iterative method (HRIM) is developed. The proposed framework combines recursive homotopy constructions with fractional-order recursive series expansions, generating accurate approximations for the nonlinear dynamics of considered network system. An operator-theoretic formulation is established in suitable Banach spaces and sufficient conditions for existence, uniqueness, convergence and Hyers-Ulam stability are derived. These results provide mathematical foundation required for the validity and reliability of the proposed methodology. The developed framework is subsequently applied to EK fractional SLNM to investigate oscillatory structures, memory-dependent wave propagation and pattern formation processes. The influence of fractional-order parameter on the network dynamics is examined through several computational experiments. Furthermore, comparative analysis with homotopy perturbation method (HPM) is performed, while residual error analysis is employed to assess accuracy of the obtained approximations. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed HRIM yields accurate solutions with rapid convergence and effectively captures essential dynamical characteristics of memory-dependent fractional oscillatory networks. Consequently, developed approach provides an efficient mathematical and computational framework for studying nonlinear fractional network systems involving memory effects and complex oscillatory behavior.

Article.Title: Cholesterol efflux capacity as an indicator of HDL dysfunction across the metabolic syndrome spectrum in a South Indian cohort
Article.Authors: Sherly. A A.; Mysore Srikantiah R.; Rohatgi A.; Parashiva G.; Hegde A.; Maruthiyodan S.; Harish S.; Shirali A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background:To evaluate high density lipoprotein(HDL) functionality using cholesterol efflux capacity(CEC) across control, pre-metabolic syndrome(PreMetS) and metabolic syndrome(MetS) groups in a South Indian cohort and determine its association with metabolic parameters and disease severity. Methods:This cross-sectional study included 88 adults [Control (n = 38; age 32.9 ± 6.20 years; M:F 19:19), Pre-MetS (n = 24; age 36.5 ± 3.50 years; M:F 15:9), MetS (n = 26; age 46.6 ± 5.68 years; M:F 17:9)] classified using modified NCEP ATP III criteria. Anthropometric (BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure) and biochemical parameters (fasting glucose, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, ApoA1, insulin, HOMA-IR) were assessed using standardised protocols. HDL functionality was measured via BODIPY-cholesterol efflux in PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophages. Multiple linear regression and Spearman correlations were performed (p < 0.05). Results:Progressive intergroup differences were observed in waist circumference, BMI, fasting glucose, insulin, triglycerides, and HOMA-IR (p < 0.001). ApoA1 declined proportionally across groups (231 vs 206 vs 187 ng/mL; ε 2 = 0.839, p < 0.001), representing the largest effect size in the dataset. Notably, CEC considerably reduced at the Pre-MetS stage and remained diminished with progressive metabolic deterioration, emphasizing early detection and intervention. CEC differed significantly across the metabolic spectrum (p < 0.001). Multiple linear regression identified triglycerides and insulin resistance as independent negative predictors of CEC, adjusting for HDL-C and ApoA1 (adjusted R 2 = 0.769). Conclusion:CEC is significantly diminished at the Pre-MetS stage and remains reduced with progressive metabolic deterioration. Triglyceride enrichment and insulin-mediated suppression of ApoA1 synthesis likely impair HDL remodelling and efflux capacity. These findings highlight CEC as an indicator of HDL dysfunction with implications for earlier cardiometabolic risk assessment in South Indian populations.

Article.Title: An integrated contact-aware cobot design for accurate UAV battery docking and battery swapping
Article.Authors: Robin L.; Remmi S.; Mariprasath T.; Zewdu M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This research introduces a integrated design and evaluation methodology for a lightweight, contact-aware cobot for autonomous battery swapping of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). It involves Denavit–Hartenberg kinematics, inverse kinematics, quintic trajectory generation, inverse dynamics, actuator torque sizing, structural verification, modal assessment, gripping-force estimation, connector-compression modeling, passive wrist compliance, docking-misalignment sensitivity, and a Battery-Swapping Cobot Performance Index (BS-CPI). The six-degree-of-freedoms manipulator was modeled under the following conditions: 3.5 kg of battery-gripper load and a working reach of 0.88 m. The nominal trajectory generated an estimated peak simulated torque of 24.97 Nm at the shoulder pitch joint, which was identified as the critical actuator location by conservative torque sizing with a required torque of 142.61 Nm and a rated torque of 220 Nm. The maximum link deflection was 0.177 mm and the minimum preliminary factor of safety was 56.97 from the structural evaluation. There was no force exceeding the safe limit of 45 N in the controlled insertion force for the contact-aware insertion model and connector compression was limited to 6 mm. Sensitivity analysis also indicated that the combination of lateral and yaw misalignment resulted in higher insertion forces and only caused the retries under extreme misalignment. The final performance index was 0.498, which showed a reasonable compromise between mass, torque demand, insertion safety, stiffness and cycle performance. The study provides a tabular computational conceptualization as a traceable pre-prototype basis for developing autonomous UAV battery-swapping stations that engage connectors in a safe manner, handle them repeatably, and have quantified tolerance to docking misalignment.

Article.Title: Influence of fatigue and sex on running ground reaction forces in runners with pronated feet
Article.Authors: Mirzanagh E.; Jafarnezhadgero A.; Mousavi S.; Safajou H.; Paquette M.
Article.Abstract: Pronated feet (PF) and fatigue are recognized factors that can alter kinetic variables during running. Women may be at a lower risk of sustaining running-related injuries compared with men, and injury types and anatomical sites tend to be different between sexs. One potential explanation for sex differences in injury rates may be attributed to distinct running patterns between men and women. This study aimed to determine the influence of fatigue and sex on ground reaction force (GRF) in runners with PF during running. Thirty well-trained runners (15 women and 15 males) completed three overground running trials at 3.3 m/s ± 5% before and after a standardized treadmill fatigue protocol while GRF were collected. Vertical, anterior–posterior, and medial–lateral GRF components, time-to-peak values, loading rate, and free moment were extracted from the stance phase. A mixed-model ANOVA (fatigue × sex) was used to assess the effects of fatigue and sex on all kinetic variables. The first vertical impact peak was higher in male compared to female runners after the fatigue protocol only ( p = 0.02). Several horizontal GRF variables were lower while vertical GRF variables were higher in male compared to female runners with pronated feet ( p < 0.05). Fatigue had limited effects on the measured GRF variables, with a significant reduction observed only in Fx HC . Several sex differences in GRF variables may contribute to the understanding of sex-related differences in running mechanics among runners with pronated feet and thus, sex should be considered when studying external loading while running in runners with pronated feet.

Article.Title: Spectrophotometric chemosensing of thioacetamide using toluidine blue as a metachromatic dye: a time-dependent study
Article.Authors: Nami F.; Bahavarnia F.; Hasanzadeh M.; Shadjou N.
Article.Abstract: Thioacetamide (TAA) is a significant organosulfur compound widely utilized in industrial applications such as rubber vulcanization and organic synthesis, while simultaneously serving as a potent hepatotoxin and carcinogen that poses substantial risks to human health. Effective monitoring of TAA is critical due to its tendency to induce severe oxidative stress and hepatic necrosis; however, conventional methods such as HPLC and GC-MS often suffer from high costs and complex sample preparation. In this study, an innovative, and time-dependent UV-Vis spectrophotometric-based chemosensor was developed for the precise quantification of TAA using a Toluidine Blue (TB) as optical probe. The proposed method exhibits a broad linear dynamic range of 0.6 to 80 µM with a lower limit of quantification of 0.6 µM. Reduction in Zp of TB (13.4 mV) to -0.918 mV for TB + TAA solution was confirmed complex formation and electrostatic interaction between TB (optical prob) and TAA (Target analyte). The selectivity of engineered opto-sensor was rigorously tested against various potential interfering species and the sensor demonstrated suitable specificity for the recognition of TAA. Furthermore, the practical utility of the sensor was successfully validated in human plasma samples, confirming its reliability in complex matrices. The stability of the analytical platform was also extensively characterized via intra-day and inter-day precision assessments yielding highly reproducible results. These findings establish the TB-based optosensor as an accurate and innovative, simple and accessible analytical tool for TAA monitoring.

Article.Title: Tunable chiral anomaly in electron magnetotransport in the Weyl semimetallic Pb$$_{1-x}$$Sn$$_{x}$$Te:Cr alloy
Article.Authors: Królicka A.; Łusakowska E.; Matusiak M.; Mirowska A.; Łusakowski A.; Story T.; Dybko K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We study magnetotransport properties of semiconductor substitutional alloy Pb $$_{1-x}$$ Sn $$_{x}$$ Te, known to exhibit Sn-content dependent properties of topological crystalline insulators with a semimetallic zero-gap state at a specific band inversion point. We experimentally verify the theoretically predicted role of chemical disorder in this multivalley electron system, which leads to sequential band inversions in various valleys and places the Fermi level close to the pairs of Weyl nodes, as identified in the density functional theory calculations. Doping with mixed-valence Cr resonant impurities enables exploitation of the unique properties of dopant resonant states, which provide an effective means of tuning carrier concentration. The combination of these two effects results in the pinning of the Fermi level in the vicinity of the nodal touching points across a wide range of composition. To address the above issues, we grow Bridgman bulk crystals of Pb $$_{1-x}$$ Sn $$_{x}$$ Te heavily doped with chromium and covering the full range of tin content (0 $$\le x \le$$ 1), i.e. spanning both the topological crystalline insulator and trivial electronic regimes. We observe the emergence of the three dimensional (3D) Weyl semimetal phase over a range of Sn compositions, namely for $$0.25< x < 0.45$$ . We provide magnetotransport evidence for this and verify the relationship between the magnitude of the experimentally determined Berry curvature and the electrical properties of these materials. Quantum transport regime observed in magnetoresistance is also independently confirmed by thermal conductivity measurements. For one of our samples we observe the striking phenomenon of the room-temperature re-entrance of the chiral anomaly, in addition to its occurrence in the 93–150 K temperature range. We also note a pronounced chiral anomaly-induced negative magnetoresistance, reaching up to 75 $$\%$$ . Consequently, the proposed approach creates favorable conditions for realizing the Weyl semimetal phase not just for one material with one specific composition, but in tunable complex IV-VI compounds.

Article.Title: Increased susceptibility of multi-drug resistant and wastewater-exposed bacteria to antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation
Article.Authors: Jones D.; Ahmed A.; Geheran A.; Green R.; Cooper J.; Cheng Q.; Skwor T.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a significant global health threat, necessitating urgent development of novel antimicrobial strategies. Antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation (aPDI), which damages multiple cellular targets simultaneously and therefore reduces the likelihood of resistance development, provides a promising approach. Here, we evaluate the antimicrobial efficacy of structurally modified TMPyP-based photosensitizers (PSs), focusing on the combined effects of metalation and long-chain alkylation against both reference and multidrug-resistant (MDR) ESKAPE pathogens as well as within wastewater matrices. Addition of a 14-carbon alkyl chain significantly improved the antimicrobial activity of a metalated PS, achieving substantial killing of Gram-positive and -negative species under low light dosing conditions. Although the alkylated and non-alkylated analogs exhibited similar singlet oxygen production, increased bacterial association of the alkylated PS suggests that improved cellular interaction drives the increased efficacy. Notably, Gram-negative MDR strains displayed equal or greater susceptibility to aPDI compared to non-resistant counterparts, highlighting the potential of this approach against resistant pathogens. Within wastewater matrices, a zinc-chelated analog (ZnC14) demonstrated effective treatment, significantly reducing both mock and indigenous microbial populations. These findings suggest that combining metalation with amphiphilic modifications enhances aPDI performance and may broaden its applicability as an alternative or complementary strategy against AMR in complex environmental systems.

Article.Title: Geochemical characteristics and origin of the oil residues in the fractured basement reservoir rocks in the Habban oilfield, Shabwah depression of Southeast Yemen
Article.Authors: Hatem B.; Hakimi M.; Mustapha K.; Kumar A.; Qadri S.; Kahal A.
Article.Abstract: Fractured basement rock, located in the Habban oilfield, Shabwah depression, is one of the major oil-bearing reservoir rocks made in recent years. However, the geochemical characteristics of the discovered oils from the fractured basement reservoir, origin of organic matter (OM), depositional environment conditions, thermal maturity, and oil-source rock correlation remain unclear. This study presents the first comprehensive geochemical investigation of the oil filling the micro fractures of the basement reservoir rock in the Habban oilfield, integrating biomarker characterization of the oils, molecular structural data of their oil-asphaltene and 1-D basin modeling analysis of oil generation and expulsion histories. The studied oil residues from the host fractured basement rock is characterized by high total organic carbon (TOC) and free hydrocarbon (S 1 ) values up to 2.75 wt% and 5.17 mg HC/g rock, respectively, resulting in high oil saturation index (OSI) values of more than 40 mg HC/ g TOC and up to 188 mg HC/ g TOC. The elevated OSI and S 1 values indicate that the oil residues in the host fractured basement rock are migrated from mature source rock. Integrated biomarker data from the saturated fraction of the oil residues suggest that these oil residues originated from marine source rock that deposited under suboxic to anoxic conditions, and containing mixed planktonic and bacterial organic matter, reflecting mainly Type II kerogen. This finding of Type II kerogen input into marine source rock is supported by the molecular structure (MS) characteristics of the corresponding oil-asphaltene fraction. The geochemical signatures of the oil residues and molecular structure of their asphaltene are consistent with the oil-source rocks of the Lam and Meem succession. However, the maturity-biomarker indicators of the examined oil residues provide evidences of mature source rock, reaching mainly peak mature of the oil-generative window. 1D basin modeling shows that the Meem source rock is more mature than Lam source rock, reaching late mature of oil-generation phase, with Easy %Ro values of up to 1.10. The extensive maturity level of the Meem source rock results in an extensive kerogen conversion ratio (TR) of up to 78%, and high oil holding capacity, promoting the development of high pressure and create micro-fracture pores within the Meem source rock. The basin model results also show that the significant amounts of generated oil have been expelled from the Meem source rock since Late Cretaceous to Late Oligocene, and then moved and migrated downward from the overlying Meem source rock into the underlying porous basement reservoir through micro-fracture network system, and also vertically migrated along faults upward to shallow sandstone reservoir of the Lam Member. These findings reduce exploration risk and highlight that the mature Meem source rock in deeper stratigraphic levels is regarded as a main source rock for most of oil exploration and production in the Shabwah depression.

Article.Title: Modeling the binding of fused pyrazole inhibitors to p38α MAP kinase using CorrEA-guided ensemble docking
Article.Authors: Castro-Cázares T.; Caballero J.
Article.Abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase p38α is an established therapeutic target implicated in inflammatory signaling and a variety of human diseases, including autoimmune disorders, cancer, and neurodegenerative conditions. Fused pyrazoles constitute an important family of ATP-competitive p38α inhibitors, displaying considerable structural diversity and a wide range of inhibitory activities. However, accurately describing inhibitor recognition remains challenging because the ATP-binding site of p38α is inherently flexible and cannot be fully represented by a single receptor conformation. Here, we constructed structural models for a series of 50 fused pyrazole inhibitors, comprising 1 H -pyrazolo[3,4- b ]pyridin-6(7 H )-one (PPO) and 1 H -pyrazolo[3,4- d ]pyridazine (PPz) derivatives, by combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, ensemble docking, and the CorrEA methodology. Representative receptor conformations extracted from MD trajectories were used in cross-docking calculations, and the experimental potencies of the series were then supplied to CorrEA as selection criteria to retain, for each inhibitor, a single receptor–ligand complex from among the available docking solutions. The resulting models were examined through ligand pose comparisons, interaction fingerprint analysis, and characterization of conformational changes within the binding site. The ensemble model successfully described all inhibitors while preserving the canonical interaction pattern of ATP-competitive protein kinase inhibitors, revealing that subtle rearrangements of multiple binding-site residues collectively account for the observed differences in inhibitory potency. These findings illustrate how explicit incorporation of receptor flexibility improves the structural interpretation of structure–activity relationships and provide a practical strategy for modeling ligand recognition in flexible protein targets.

Article.Title: High resolution multi-depth quantification of the retinal nerve fiber layer
Article.Authors: Callet C.; Bertrand M.; Guzman K.; Mecê P.; Rossi E.; Grieve K.
Article.Abstract: Thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layer, composed of axon bundles converging toward the optic nerve head, is a key biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring glaucoma and neurodegenerative diseases. High-resolution en face imaging of individual nerve fiber bundles offers morphological information beyond conventional optical coherence tomography, yet lacks automated analysis tools and normative data. Here, we develop image processing pipelines for automated quantification of bundle trajectory, tortuosity, orientation, and width, and establish a normative database from 18 healthy volunteers enrolled across three studies (n = 15, 11 and 11), imaged using adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy and full-field optical coherence tomography. Trajectory analysis revealed systematic deviations from existing mathematical models, leading us to propose two refined models. Bundles were on average 12% wider at shallower retinal depths and bundle width decreased significantly with age. These results and toolkit provide a foundation for high-resolution biomarker extraction in retinal investigations.

Article.Title: Development of PEBA-PEMA blend membranes for the pervaporation separation of 1-butanol from aqueous solutions
Article.Authors: Denganavar P.; Choudhari S.; Krishnegowda J.; Aditya D.; Nataraj S.; Sajjan A.
Article.Abstract: Using the Hansen’s solubility parameters (HSPs) approach, novel polyether block amide (PEBA)-polyethyl methacrylate (PEMA) polymer blend membranes were synthesized and applied for the pervaporation (PV) separation of 1-butanol. Blending with PEMA led to an increase in surface roughness and hydrophobicity. PV performance of the blend membranes for the recovery of 1-butanol from aqueous solution (20 g/L) at 40 °C showed an improvement in separation performance with the blending of PEMA; however, a higher blending ratio (≥ 8 wt%) significantly reduced PV performance due to phase separation. The membrane (PBPM-5) containing 5 wt% of PEMA achieved the best PV separation, yielding a flux of 0.19 kgm −2 h − 1 and a separation factor of 15.5, which is a 50% enhancement in flux and a twofold increase in the separation factor as compared to the pristine PEBA membrane. An increase in PV operation temperature and feed butanol content showed simultaneous enhancement in both the separation factor and flux for the PBPM-5 membrane. Separation of butanol from multicomponent mixture resulted in lower performance indicating the presence of strong coupling effect. This work shows the PV butanol separation capability of PEBA can be significantly enhanced through the judicious blending of small amount of PEMA polymer.

Article.Title: Vaccine responses to influenza viruses and SARS-CoV-2 under novel immunotherapies in myasthenia gravis and CIDP: a prospective observational study
Article.Authors: Lattau S.; Heiler F.; Glaubitz S.; Meyer S.; Dürrwald R.; Fitzner D.; Eisele M.; Zschüntzsch J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) require long-term immunotherapy, making effective vaccination essential for infection prophylaxis. As these immunotherapies increasingly involve novel agents such as FcRn antagonists and complement inhibitors, their influence on the vaccine response needs to be assessed. Therefore, we prospectively enrolled 23 patients with MG or CIDP receiving contemporary immunotherapies who were vaccinated against influenza viruses ( n = 21; Northern Hemisphere 2025/26) or SARS-CoV-2 ( n = 12). Sera collected before and at least two weeks after vaccination were assayed for antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 spike S1 subunit and three influenza strains. A response to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (≥ 2-fold increase in anti-S1 IgG) was observed in 9 of 12 patients (75%; median fold-change 2.6), and influenza seroprotection rates (haemagglutination inhibition [HAI] titer ≥ 1:40) rose for all three strains reaching 86% (A/H1N1), 76% (B/Victoria), and 67% (A/H3N2). The effect of individual medications on post-vaccination titers was assessed by analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for baseline titer and diagnosis. In these exploratory models, estimates were directionally higher under ravulizumab and lower under efgartigimod and mycophenolate; none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Patients receiving efgartigimod and mycophenolate concurrently had significantly lower absolute post-vaccination HAI titers for A/H1N1 (median 1:30 vs. 1:160; p = 0.0085) and A/H3N2 (median < 1:10 vs. 1:40; p = 0.022). These findings are consistent with lower baseline and circulating antibody levels and do not show a detectable difference in fold-change in this small exploratory cohort. Patients who failed to seroconvert to any strain were more frequently receiving FcRn antagonists, yet most retained seroprotection against at least one strain. Under FcRn antagonism, influenza titers did not parallel total serum IgG, with several patients seroconverting despite a concurrent decline in total IgG. In conclusion, most patients mounted a measurable humoral response to both vaccines despite contemporary immunotherapy.

Article.Title: Elucidation of chemical background enhances interpretation of novel oligonucleotide drug impurities by mass spectrometry
Article.Authors: Roussis S.; Bradley K.; Rentel C.
Article.Abstract: Sample introduction into a mass spectrometer (MS) is associated with the likelihood of introducing background chemicals, which may form adducts with the analyte of interest such as oligonucleotide therapeutic drugs, significantly interfering with the interpretation of the MS data. Here we examine the variables affecting the formation of adducts. We found that most of the chemical species forming adducts are present in the carrier stream as impurities. Adduct formation is affected by experimental parameters but also depends on the oligonucleotide sequence. We introduce a novel and practical approach to identify unknown oligonucleotide adducts which includes tandem MS (MS/MS) interpretation and comparison of the accurate mass difference between the parent oligo and adduct, with the masses of the impurities in the chemical background. We give exhaustive examples of the steps in the identification of 10 oligonucleotide adducts. Knowledge about the unwanted interactions of analytes of interest with extraneous chemical entities can increase the accuracy of MS-based interpretations and conclusions and is of interest to all areas of MS applications.

Article.Title: BIS-based model reference adaptive control of anesthesia depth under patient variability and time-varying delays
Article.Authors: Rahimi R.; Kamali M.; Shayegh F.; Baharlouei Z.
Article.Abstract: General anesthesia plays a critical role in modern surgical care, requiring accurate regulation of hypnotic and analgesic drug administration to maintain unconsciousness and analgesia. A major challenge in anesthesia control is the presence of significant inter-patient variability and physiological time-varying delays. Conventional control approaches often rely on manual tuning or patient-specific parameter identification, limiting their applicability in real clinical settings. This study proposes a Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) strategy for automated closed-loop regulation of anesthesia depth using propofol and remifentanil. The proposed framework incorporates a Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic model and compensates for nonlinear drug-response behavior through an inverse Hill-function approach. A key advantage of the proposed adaptive controller is its independence from patient-specific tuning and prior parameter identification, enabling real-time personalized anesthesia management without model recalibration. Simulation results on a heterogeneous virtual patient population demonstrate settling times of approximately 4–6 min during induction with minimal overshoot (< 5%). The Bispectral Index (BIS) was successfully maintained within the clinically acceptable range of 40–60, with an average value close to 50 and small deviations (± 2). Compared with previously reported anesthesia control strategies, the proposed MRAC approach achieves competitive tracking performance while maintaining stable tracking across heterogeneous virtual simulated patients and time-varying delays. These findings suggest that the proposed strategy provides a promising solution for robust and individualized closed-loop anesthesia management.

Article.Authors: Wu J.; Sun T.; Lin P.; Wang S.

The primary outcome was Day-7 renal recovery; secondary outcomes included Day-30 recovery, persistent AKI, acute kidney disease, and MAKE30. Stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weights from a multinomial propensity-score model were truncated at the 99.5th percentile. Among 6,289 patients, Early versus None showed no clear difference in Day-7 renal recovery (74.8 vs. 74.0%; risk difference, 0.77% points; 95% CI, −3.30 to 4.94). This finding remained compatible with the null in the propensity-score-refit bootstrap (95% CI, −3.59 to 5.18) and a 72-hour survivor-restricted analysis (risk difference, 0.27% points; 95% CI, −3.76 to 4.36). Secondary Early-versus-Late contrasts showed differences for some outcomes but were exploratory and statistically fragile given the small Late group, and they do not override the primary comparison, which showed no clear benefit or harm.

Second, per-defect principal component analysis separates a TEI-dominated crack family from an HSI/TNI-dominated high-intensity family; family-adaptive weighting increases between-defect-type separability (module-level Kruskal-Wallis H from 20.59 to 33.65), the gain persists in most held-out module splits and a ratio proxy assigns the family with leave-one-out accuracy 0.953. Third, a defect-specific residual irradiance correction (PV-FSI $$_{\text{IR}}$$ ), fitted on the 468 acquisitions meeting IEC TS 62446-3, removes the pooled irradiance drift ( H from 31.72 to 3.76). Referenced to nameplate power, PV-FSI shows no significant within-type association with $$P_{\text{mpp}}$$ ; it is therefore positioned as a thermal severity descriptor for inspection triage, complementing electrical characterization. Article.Title: An intelligent Adaptive Security Controller-based feature-aware BLAKE3-Bülban chaotic encryption framework for secure UAV image transmission
Article.Authors: Yogi B.; Sahid S.; Ghosh N.; Sharma L.; Roy S.; Jadwal P.
Article.Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) images are widely used in surveillance, border security, disaster monitoring, and military applications, where secure image transfer is crucial. This paper proposes an adaptive feature-aware image encryption framework to protect UAV images against unauthorised access and statistical attacks. The framework integrates image feature analysis, BLAKE3-based key derivation, and a three-dimensional Bülban chaotic system to generate feature-dependent chaotic sequences. An Adaptive Security Controller dynamically determines the block size, diffusion rounds, transient skip, and chaotic warm-up setting according to image characteristics and derived key values. The generated chaotic streams are used for adaptive block-wise permutation and multi-round forward-backwards diffusion to enhance confusion and diffusion. Experimental evaluation achieves an average encrypted-image entropy of 7.9993, NPCR of 99.6169%, and UACI of 33.4590%. The encrypted images also exhibit negligible linear correlation between adjacent pixels and are processed using a 256-bit master key. These results demonstrate favourable statistical characteristics under the evaluated experimental conditions. The proposed framework therefore provides a feature-aware encryption approach for UAV image transmission, while further implementation-level and application-specific validation is required.

Article.Title: Prevalence of positive depression screening among preoperative patients in Singapore
Article.Authors: Xu F.; Koh M.; Sim J.; Tan S.; Fong K.; Ching J.; Ng R.; Raghunathan K.; Dunworth S.; Abdullah H.; Ke Y.
Article.Abstract: Depression is under-recognised in surgical populations despite its association with adverse postoperative outcomes. Data from Southeast Asian perioperative settings remain limited. The primary outcome was prevalence of clinically significant depression (PHQ-9 ≥ 10). Prevalence was highest in patients aged 21–40 years (8.8%) and decreased with age, with no cases observed in those aged ≥ 71 years. Depression was more frequent in females than males, although differences were not statistically significant. Approximately one in 20 preoperative patients had clinically significant depressive symptoms, most without prior diagnosis. Routine mental health preoperative screening may have clinical value and represents an opportunity to identify at-risk individuals, particularly younger patients and females. Further studies should evaluate whether targeted perioperative interventions improve outcomes.

Article.Title: Association between mid-day meal program participation and composite index of anthropometric failure (CIAF) among school-going children in eastern India

The overall burden of malnutrition among school-aged children has often been neglected by standard measures such as stunting, wasting, and underweight. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of neck circumference (NC) to identify BMI-for-age Z-score (BAZ)-based thinness. All the anthropometric measurements were taken as per WHO standards. Nutritional status was assessed using Z-scores and CIAF classifications. We also described the spatial distribution of selected anthropometric failure indicators across the study area. The prevalence of CIAF in the study population was 44.94%, relatively higher in boys (47.99%). Children not receiving MDM had significantly higher odds of CIAF compared to those receiving MDM (aOR = 2.10, 95% CI 1.66–2.66, p < 0.001). Poor parental education, low family income, extended family type, and fast-food consumption were also significantly associated with CIAF. NC showed discriminatory ability for identifying thinness in the study population. Almost half of the school-aged children in this study experienced anthropometric failure. Participation in the MDM program was significantly associated with lower odds of anthropometric failure. Findings of this study highlight the burden of anthropometric failure among school-aged children and the association of nutritional status with MDM program participation. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the single-district study setting may limit generalizability. The NC cut-offs were derived and evaluated in the same study population and therefore require external validation before wider application.

Article.Title: A variety-aware retrieval-augmented generation framework for terminology support in Chinese medical interpreting
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Huang Y.; Ma R.; Cheung A.
Article.Abstract: Standard machine translation and large language models frequently treat Chinese medical terms as a single unified target, overlooking critical regional variation across Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. This study frames regional terminology assistance as a variety-aware selection problem in which terminology linked to a knowledge base (KB) remains distinguishable from provisional wording. VACMI-LLM is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that combines a concept-centred three-region medical KB, threshold-gated retrieval, and structured output with explicit KB-support labels. Evaluation used a constructed 700-expression retrieval stress set and a separate 300-case raw-query pipeline set. At an exploratory threshold of 0.90, the system achieved 95.2% Recall@3 for KB-supported expressions and returned no KB concept for 78.5% of KB-external expressions. In E2, reference-row accuracy for KB-supported expressions was similar between VACMI-LLM and ungated RAG, whereas KB-support labelling for external expressions was 96.4% versus 15.9%. Eight external professionals rated five fixed displays highly for terminology accuracy, regional appropriateness, and usefulness for interpreter preparation. These findings show how region-labelled knowledge and explicit support status can make terminology assistance more traceable under controlled conditions.

Article.Title: HPLC-based identification of bioactive flavonoids from Drimia indica (Roxb.) Jessop and their in silico and in vitro cytotoxic activities
Article.Authors: Shit V.; Dhakar M.; Kumar M.
Article.Abstract: Drimia indica (Roxb.) Jessop, a geophytic medicinal plant in the family Asparagaceae, has long been used in traditional medicine, yet its bioactive flavonoid constituents remain largely uncharacterised. In this study, we explored the pharmacological potential of flavonoids derived from Drimia indica through an integrated approach encompassing phytochemical isolation, computational modelling, and in vitro biological assays. Using silica gel column chromatography followed by high-performance liquid chromatography, we identified three major flavonoids: quercetin, myricetin, and naringenin, based on retention-time comparison with commercial standards. Providing HPLC-based evidence supporting the presence of myricetin and naringenin in this species. We evaluated the biological relevance of these flavonoids using the MCF-7 breast cancer cell line, with a focus on PI3Kα. Molecular docking and dynamics studies revealed strong and stable interactions between quercetin, myricetin, and naringenin and proteins involved in PI3Kα signalling. This study provides targeted evidence for the presence of myricetin and naringenin in D. indica through HPLC-based identification, along with their notable cytotoxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells, underscoring their anticancer potential and supporting the medicinal relevance and sustainable use of Drimia indica .

Article.Title: Testing the 3D QRNG by undoing
Article.Authors: Trejo J.; Calude C.; Stoica O.
Article.Abstract: We propose a method to test whether a photonic 3D QRNG operates according to the underlying theory by realizing the proposed measurement with the correct output probabilities and value-indefiniteness conditions, thereby generating strongly incomputable and maximally unpredictable sequences of random digits. The test relies on undoing the unitary evolution realized by the 3D QRNG. The test verifies the unitarity of the realized transformation, quantifies the magnitude of the residual noise, and detects those fabrication errors that are not common to the device and the undoing procedure; photon loss and dark counts are removed beforehand by heralding and are therefore outside its scope. By testing the validity of the implementation, the test can corroborate the theoretically proven features of the 3D QRNG, such as strong incomputability and unpredictability, or indicate how the implementation should be corrected, if necessary. The test can be easily incorporated into the QRNG and used as a means of experimental certification. The test module is fabricated identically to the QRNG.

Article.Title: Tunable mechanical properties of polymer-based surrogate materials for articular cartilage and vocal fold repair
Article.Authors: Faber J.; Schlicht S.; Kniesburges S.; Kaufmann A.; Bräuer L.; Liphardt A.; Bachl M.; Pogarell T.; May M.; Döllinger M.; Müller S.; Betsch M.; Perl M.; Drummer D.; Budday S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The macroscopic biomechanical characteristics of soft and ultrasoft tissues, such as articular cartilage and vocal folds, significantly determine their physiological function. Treatments of widespread tissue degradations due to osteoarthritis in the knee or vocal fold impairment remain an unresolved challenge. For the design of implants for tissue repair after injury or disease, the thorough understanding of the unique biomechanical properties of native tissues and potential substitute materials is essential. Based on large-strain mechanical testing methods combined with hyperelastic nonlinear continuum mechanics modeling and finite element simulations, we identify qualitative similarities between articular knee cartilage and vocal folds. Under compression, both tissue types show a strain-induced stiffening alongside hysteresis and conditioning. Based on synthetic metamaterials, we demonstrate that the replication of the complex mechanical properties, and thus the macroscopic mechanical functionality of the corresponding soft tissues, becomes possible. In accordance with native tissues, a pronounced nonlinear stress-strain behavior and stiffening is obtained, while hysteresis can be predominantly demonstrated for hybrid, polyolefin-hydrogel-based articular cartilage surrogates. We furthermore demonstrate the tunability of biomimetic stiffnesses of synthetic articular cartilage and vocal fold surrogates through tissue-specific process-material combinations. These involve complementary approaches based on adapting the density of load-bearing polyolefin networks in laser-sintered polypropylene-polyvinylpolypyrrolidone composites for cartilaginous properties, and the variation of the cross-linking density of synthetic silicone-based epithelium surrogates in ultrasoft vocal folds. These observations furthermore indicate the significance of viscous, hydrogel-based fractions for the biomimetic replication of hysteresis and relaxation. Our results therefore demonstrate the biomimetic similarity of soft tissues across a broad mechanical range alongside the feasibility of synthetic metamaterials in replicating essential passive biomechanical functions with great potential for future treatment options.

Article.Title: Fucoxanthin mitigates methyl cellosolve-induced testicular dysfunction in male rats: association with modulation of the JAK2–STAT3–SOCS1 signaling axis
Article.Authors: Aljarari R.; Abu-Almakarem A.; Aljarba N.; Saleh A.; Alalawy A.; AlRashidi A.; El-Said K.; El-Gowily A.; Abu-Khudir R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract 2-methoxyethanol (methyl cellosolve; MC)is an industrial solvent used in paints, coatings, dyes, and jet fuel anti-icing agents that has been associated with reproductive toxicity. Edible brown seaweeds contain fucoxanthin (FUC), a carotenoid with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and cytoprotective properties; however, its effects on MC-induced testicular dysfunction and the associated molecular changes require further characterization. This study investigated how FUC ameliorated MC-induced testicular injury in male rats. Molecular docking analysis was performed using AutoDock Vina 1.5. Forty male Sprague–Dawley rats were allocated to four groups: control, FUC control, MC, and FUC + MC. FUC was administered at 230 mg/kg body weight and MC at 100 mg/kg body weight for one month. MC exposure was associated with reduced body-weight gain, testicular and epididymal weights, sperm count, sperm motility, sperm viability, and circulating reproductive hormone levels. MC exposure was also associated with impaired testicular antioxidant defenses, increased oxidative stress and inflammatory markers, altered expression of JAK2, STAT3, and SOCS1, and histopathological abnormalities. FUC co-administration improved several reproductive and biochemical outcomes, reduced inflammatory and oxidative-stress markers, and modulated the JAK2/STAT3/SOCS1 pathway. Overall, the findings indicated that FUC attenuated MC-associated testicular dysfunction under the conditions examined.

Article.Title: A novel cast niobium alloy offering exceptional strength and creep resistance at ultrahigh temperatures
Article.Authors: Gaddam S.; Dryepondt S.; Bell S.; Nahin A.; Zhang M.; Chandran K.
Article.Abstract: A new precipitation-strengthened niobium (Nb) alloy, Nb-20 W-1Zr-0.13 C (wt%), was designed and made by plasma arc melting and casting. The as-cast alloy consisted of a compositionally modulated BCC matrix with metal carbides precipitated along grain boundaries, and fine precipitates in the grain interior. The alloy exhibited yield strength, tensile strength, and ductility values of 582 MPa, 687 MPa, and 1.5% elongation, respectively, along with a good fracture toughness (K Q ) of 13 MPa√m at room temperature. More importantly, the alloy’s tensile strengths at ultrahigh temperatures (414 MPa and 250 MPa at 1200 °C and 1400 °C, respectively) are exceptional, surpassing those of many historical Nb alloys. The present cast alloy was stronger by 57% and 36% at 1400 °C, compared to the additively manufactured C-103 and Nb-521 alloys, respectively. Remarkably, the strengths at ultrahigh temperatures are comparable to those of the Mo-based TZM alloy, which exhibits exceptional strength at such temperatures. Tensile creep data at 1200 °C show very low creep strain accumulation up to a stress of 150 MPa over a significant period of time (~ 100 h). The creep performance has been evaluated against selected historical Nb alloys and Ni-base superalloys. This study reveals the microstructural attributes that govern the alloy’s excellent mechanical properties at both low and high temperatures.

Article.Title: Regulating emotional experience in middle childhood using focused attention: a functional MRI investigation
Article.Authors: Bian Z.; Ju S.; Mull D.; Faibishenko J.; Zang Z.; Iwinski S.; Donovan S.; Bost K.; Dolcos F.; Dolcos S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prior research has primarily investigated later-stage emotion regulation (ER) strategies (e.g., reappraisal) in adults, but less is known about early-stage strategies such as focused attention (FA) in children. Here, we examined the neurobehavioral mechanisms of self-guided FA in middle childhood. Participants ( N = 21) were cued to focus either on the foreground (FG) or background (BG) of negative and neutral composite images and then rated their affective responses. First, focusing on the contextual details of negative pictures (BG Focus) decreased their emotional ratings to the level of neutral pictures. Second, this behavioral effect was associated with increased activity in dorsal control regions (e.g., frontal eye field, FEF) and in regions involved in processing spatial contextual information (e.g., parahippocampal place area), as well as with decreased activity in emotion processing regions (e.g., ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, vlPFC, and the amygdala). Third, exploratory brain–behavior correlations revealed a more nuanced picture pointing to individual differences in these effects. Consistent with a role in ER, there were negative associations with emotional ratings in the FEF (during the BG Focus) and the vlPFC (during the FG Focus). Together, these findings advance our understanding of ER in middle childhood and highlight the role of individual differences in using FA.

Article.Title: Design and characteristics improvement of GaN/Ga₂O₃ SACM-APDs featuring a p-type GaN multiplication layer for solar-blind single-photon detection
Article.Authors: Khoddami M.; Kaatuzian H.
Article.Abstract: In this paper, a separate absorption, charge, and multiplication avalanche photodiode (SACM-APD) based on a GaN/Ga₂O₃ heterostructure is designed and optimized for high-performance ultraviolet single-photon detection. First, we evaluate a conventional SACM architecture using an n − -type Gallium nitride (GaN) multiplication layer and a n + -type gallium oxide (Ga₂O₃) charge layer and an n − -type Ga₂O₃ absorption layer as a baseline. To improve carrier-multiplication dynamics and mitigate high-field heterojunction interface issues, we propose a novel structurally modified APD that integrates a p − -type GaN multiplication layer, an n + -type GaN charge layer, and an n − -type Ga₂O₃ absorption layer. In photodetectors exhibiting low quantum efficiency at zero bias, calculating the gain based on the zero-bias photocurrent often leads to overestimation artifacts. To prevent this error and provide a rigorous physical assessment, the avalanche gain in this study is calculated relative to the average unmultiplied photocurrent in the pre-avalanche region. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed structural modifications significantly enhance device performance. Compared to the conventional baseline, the proposed SACM-APD achieves a 93.7% enhancement in avalanche gain, increasing from 1.6 × 10 6 to 3.1 × 10 6 approximately, which corresponds to a multiplied responsivity of 1.603 × 10 6 A/W under 254 nm back-illumination. Furthermore, the operating breakdown voltage is favorably reduced from 55.55 V in the baseline to 52.77 V in the proposed structure. These findings highlight the robust potential of the proposed architecture for next-generation, high-gain single-photon avalanche detectors (SPADs).

Article.Title: Block-level urban socioeconomic characterization using satellite imagery and points of interest: the case of Lima, Peru
Article.Authors: Chia L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Identifying which observable urban features are associated with socioeconomic status matters for policy design, yet remains understudied at fine spatial scales. We develop an Urban Deprivation Index (UDI) for Metropolitan Lima, Peru, using the 102,368 census block records from the Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática (INEI). Our approach integrates Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR), VIIRS nighttime lights, and 40,826 Points of Interest (POIs) from OpenStreetMap. Using a Random Forest with 20 parsimonious variables, we obtain a Pearson correlation of $$r = 0.786 \pm 0.050$$ and a mean absolute error of 0.24 strata under spatial cross-validation (500 partitions, 50 districts). 88.8% of blocks fall within ±0.5 strata of the official classifications. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis reveals that only two variables, Green Accessibility and Urban Remoteness, dominate 79% of individual predictions. Removing them reduces performance by only 2.05%: the remaining 18 variables carry redundant information. Socioeconomic segregation in Lima is structured by environmental amenities and urban centrality.

Article.Title: Development of multihead cross-correlation attention fusion-based deep learning model for myocardial infarction detection using ECG signal and ESMOTE data balancing
Article.Authors: Gali A.; Das S.; Boda R.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular Diseases (CVDs) has become one of the leading causes of mortality in the world, with Myocardial Infarction (MI) being a serious cardiac disease that demands timely diagnosis to reduce fatality rates. ECG signals are largely used detecting MI because of their ability to capture the heart’s electrical activity and their non-invasive behavior. Nevertheless, the existing diagnostic models have some challenges such as data imbalance, noise artifacts and ineffective feature retrieval. These problems adversely impact the reliability and accuracy of the MI detection models. Nowadays, deep learning systems have proved enhanced potential in healthcare applications by allowing automatic feature learning and accurate classification. However, the effectiveness of these systems highly based on the quality of the signal pre-processing, effective feature extraction models and balanced datasets. To resolve these problems, a multi-head cross-correlation attention fusion-enabled deep learning model is proposed in this work for MI detection. At first, the essential ECG signals are collected from the benchmark database and given to a pre-processing stage to enhance the signal quality. Subsequently, the Enhanced Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (ESMOTE) model is adopted by improving the concept of the existing Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) technique for addressing the class-imbalance issue. Further, the balanced data is subjected to the feature extraction stage, where the significant features, such as wave features (F1), spectral features (F2) and deep features (F3) using the Spatial and Temporal Attention-based Sparse Autoencoder (STA-SA), are extracted. Finally, all these resultant features are fed into the Multihead Cross Correlation Attention Fusion-based Adaptive Feature-assisted Knowledge Distilled Temporal Convolution Network (MCCAF-AF-KDTCN), in which the three feature sets are fused by the Multihead Cross Correlation Attention Fusion (MCCAF), thus obtaining an adaptive feature. Then, the resultant adaptive fused feature is provided to the KDTCN model to achieve the classification outcome for MI disease. For further improvement, the hyperparameters of the KDTCN model are selected optimized with the help of Phase Transition-based Lyrebird Optimization (PTLO). The performance analysis is finally performed for the suggested model over traditional methods. The accuracy of the developed PTLO-MCCAF-AF-KDTCN is 95.78%, whereas the existing models, such as “Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit” (BiGRU), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and MCCAF-F-KDTCN, achieve 82.28%, 90.86%, 82.73% and 92.14% accuracy rates for the linear activation function. The results proved that the implemented MCCAF-AF-KDTCN is more effective for MI detection than the traditional approaches.

Article.Authors: Gül E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Terrain-resolved photovoltaic (PV) yield assessment needs an irradiance source whose direct component is retrieved rather than assumed, thermodynamic fields corrected for elevation and validated against ground stations, and an attribution layer explaining why yield departs from irradiance. These are rarely met together. Lapse-rate correction reduced ERA5-Land air-temperature root-mean-square deviation against 62 stations from 3.25 to 2.52 °C, a 22.5% improvement; dew point and wind were evaluated against 119 stations. For Türkiye over 2000–2025 the framework gives a climatological mean yield of 1805 kWh/kWp across 32,479 land cells, an inter-annual coefficient of variation of 3.3%, and provincial means from 1334 kWh/kWp on the eastern Black Sea coast to 1994 kWh/kWp in the southeast. In-plane irradiation matched PVGIS to within 2.1%. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attribution separates two regimes: irradiance sets the spatial pattern of yield, whereas air temperature governs the performance ratio, most strongly at elevation extremes.

Article.Title: Dietary diversity, nutritional status, and health-related quality of life among adults living with HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy in ilu Ababor Zone, South-West Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Gemechu E.; Lemma T.; Abate K.
Article.Abstract: Malnutrition, low dietary diversity, and reduced health-related quality of life remain common among people living with HIV/AIDS in Ethiopia, yet most previous studies have relied on body mass index alone, missing clinically significant muscle wasting. Factors independently associated with poor dietary diversity included low income, lack of formal education, detectable viral load, and CD4 count < 350 cells/µL. Combined undernutrition was the strongest negative predictor of health-related quality of life. Routine MUAC measurement should be integrated into ART clinics to identify individuals with isolated muscle wasting, and nutritional interventions should be prioritised for patients with uncontrolled viraemia and immunosuppression.
