Article.Title: Dynamic accommodative stress testing for early detection of anterior segment deformation patterns in subclinical keratoconus
Article.Authors: Başkan B.; Evcimen Y.
Article.Abstract: To investigate dynamic anterior segment alterations during accommodative effort in subclinical keratoconus (SKC) using combined Scheimpflug-Placido imaging and anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), and to establish a dynamic stress test for early ectasia detection. In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study, 180 participants (one eye each) were allocated to three age-matched groups: bilateral subclinical keratoconus (SKC, n = 60), very asymmetric ectasia with clinically unaffected fellow eyes (VAE-NT, n = 60) and healthy controls ( n = 60). Anterior segment imaging was performed under standardised mesopic conditions at accommodative stimuli of 0, 3 and 6 D delivered through a Badal optometer. Primary outcomes were the accommodation-induced changes in anterior chamber depth (ΔACD) and maximum keratometry (ΔKmax). Two composite indices, the Dynamic Ectasia Index (DEI) and the Corneal Thickness Redistribution Index (CTRI), were derived from the present dataset after data collection and were not prespecified. At 6 D, SKC eyes deformed more than controls in every primary outcome: ΔACD − 0.114 ± 0.021 mm versus − 0.069 ± 0.015 mm, and inferotemporal curvature change 1.76 ± 0.27 D versus 0.66 ± 0.17 D (both p < 0.001). DEI separated SKC from control eyes with 98.3% sensitivity and 96.7% specificity (AUC 0.995, 95% CI 0.989–1.000), and the bivariate DEI + CTRI rule with 96.7% and 98.3%. The Belin/Ambrósio D-index reached an AUC of 1.000, but because its thresholds defined group eligibility this separation is an artefact of the sampling frame and not a measure of performance. All estimates were derived and evaluated in the same dataset and are therefore optimistic. Accommodative stress testing reveals anterior segment deformation patterns that distinguish SKC eyes from healthy controls. DEI and CTRI provide an empirically derived screening framework and should be interpreted as screening composites rather than biomechanical parameters. External validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: ASIA: adaptive single-diffusion-stage inference acceleration for diffusion-based virtual try-on
Article.Authors: Mansour S.; Elemry E.; Osman A.; Abdelwahab R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Virtual try-on synthesises an image of a person wearing a chosen garment. Diffusion models give the most realistic results, but remain too slow for interactive use. The leading method, TPD, runs its diffusion network twice: a first pass predicts a pair-specific mask locating where the garment belongs, and a second pass renders the garment into that region. Each pass takes about 100 denoising steps, so one image needs roughly 200, half of them producing only a binary shape. This first stage does not justify a diffusion model. We propose Adaptive Single-Diffusion-Stage Inference Acceleration (ASIA), which replaces diffusion-based mask generation with a lightweight convolutional network. Using DensePose and the flat garment mask as structural priors, ASIA predicts the pair-specific mask in one forward pass, reducing that stage from seconds to milliseconds. Try-on then needs a single diffusion stage, whose input block alone is finetuned to the new mask distribution. On VITON-HD, inference falls from 15.4 to 7.5 seconds per image, a 2.05-fold speedup. Under a controlled reproduction of TPD, paired structural (SSIM) and perceptual (LPIPS) similarity both improve while the Fréchet Inception Distance rises slightly (9.04 against 8.78). Removing an entire diffusion stage thus trades a small FID increase for a large speedup and improved paired fidelity.

Article.Title: A privacy preserving federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification and severity estimation using indian field data
Article.Authors: Ram D.; Gyanchandani M.; Rasool A.; Kushwaha M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a privacy-aware federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification and severity estimation using heterogeneous field data collected across Indian agricultural regions. Conventional deep learning approaches rely on centralized data aggregation, which raises concerns related to data privacy, ownership, and scalability in distributed farming environments. To address these challenges, the proposed framework integrates a ResNet-18-based convolutional neural network enhanced with a Convolutional Block Attention Module for discriminative feature extraction, along with a model-contrastive federated learning strategy to mitigate client drift under non-independent and identically distributed data conditions. In addition to disease classification, a severity estimation module is incorporated using Otsu-based segmentation to quantify the proportion of infected leaf area, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of disease progression. The framework is evaluated across multiple federated settings with varying numbers of clients to analyse convergence, robustness, and scalability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 95.49% and a severity estimation accuracy of 94.57% in a five-client setup, while maintaining stable performance above 91% and 92%, respectively, even with increased client participation. High macro-averaged F1-scores and well-defined severity confusion matrices further validate the reliability of the model. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enabling scalable, privacy-aware, and severity-informed disease monitoring, making it suitable for real-world precision agriculture applications.

Article.Title: Spatial mapping of defensive toxins in the cutaneous glands of toad (Rhinella icterica) using optical coherence tomography and Raman microspectroscopy
Article.Authors: Ribeiro L.; Spencer P.; Mailho-Fontana P.; Moriscot A.; Chinait L.; Antoniazzi M.; Jared C.; Pimenta D.; Wetter N.; Freitas A.
Article.Abstract: The cutaneous glands of anurans play a central role in defense against predators, water balance, and physiological adaptation. In toads of the genus Rhinella , dorsal granular glands and parotoid macroglands produce and store chemically complex secretions that include alkaloids and bufadienolides. This study investigated the morphology of cutaneous gland types and the spatial distribution of gland-associated components in Rhinella icterica , emphasizing the localization of bufotenine (an alkaloid) and marinobufagin (a steroid), both previously investigated using desorption electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy imaging (DESI-MSI). Optical coherence tomography (OCT) was used to reconstruct parotoid and dorsal skin regions in male and female specimens, whereas optical microscopy and Raman microspectroscopy were applied to histological sections of the parotoid macroglands. Density functional theory (DFT), using the B3LYP/6-311++G** level of theory, supported the assignment of theoretical Raman modes for bufotenine, marinobufagin, and water. OCT showed that parotoid plugs could be detected and measured, although the deeper parotoid granular glands were beyond the effective imaging depth of the instrument. Dorsal granular glands were identifiable inside wart-like structures. Raman spectra of the extracted poison and the granular glands shared bands that were absent from mucous glands, particularly in the 1050–1200 cm \(^{-1}\) and 1450–1500 cm \(^{-1}\) regions. This supports the well-known hypothesis that granular glands are the main site of toxin production and storage in amphibians. Raman mapping further indicated that marinobufagin is preferentially concentrated near the connective tissue, whereas bufotenine was more abundant in the plug and inner granular-gland region. These results demonstrate that Raman microspectroscopy, supported by DFT and OCT-based morphology, is a promising approach for localizing defensive compounds in amphibian skin glands.

Article.Title: Freeze-drying-induced structural enhancement of graphene quantum dot–modified carboxymethyl cellulose beads for highly efficient cypermethrin removal
Article.Authors: Barzegarzadeh M.; Amini-Fazl M.
Article.Abstract: The influence of drying procedures on the pore structure and adsorption performance of graphene quantum dot-modified carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC/GQD) beads for cypermethrin removal has not been sufficiently elucidated. Therefore, hydrogel and cryogel forms of CMC/GQD beads were comparatively evaluated to clarify the effect of oven-drying and freeze-drying on cypermethrin adsorption from aqueous media. Freeze-drying preserved the interconnected porous structure and increased the specific surface area from 7.78 m 2 g -1 for the oven-dried hydrogel to 107.86 m 2 g -1 for the cryogel. Taguchi optimization identified an initial cypermethrin concentration of 90 mg L -1 , pH 6, an adsorbent dosage of 1 g L -1 , and a contact time of 120 min as the optimum conditions. Equilibrium analysis showed that the hydrogel and cryogel were better described by the Langmuir (R 2 = 0.9971) and Freundlich (R 2 = 0.9942) models, respectively, indicating predominantly monolayer adsorption on relatively uniform sites for the hydrogel and heterogeneous, multilayer adsorption for the cryogel. The Langmuir model yielded theoretical maximum adsorption capacities of 174.5 and 296.7 mg g -1 for the hydrogel and cryogel, respectively, while the experimentally determined maximum adsorption capacities were 65.4 and 276.12 mg g -1 , respectively. Kinetic analysis indicated that hydrogel adsorption followed the pseudo-second-order model, whereas cryogel adsorption was described by both pseudo-second-order kinetics and liquid-film diffusion. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed spontaneous and exothermic adsorption, with ΔH° = -86.09 kJ mol -1 and ΔS° = -230 J mol -1 K -1 . The cryogel achieved removal efficiencies of 98.7% in deionized water and 98.6% in simulated agricultural runoff. Moreover, using 0.1 M NaOH as the desorption agent, the cryogel maintained a removal efficiency above 75% for six consecutive cycles, although its efficiency decreased from 99.9% in the first cycle to 59.68% after eight cycles. These findings demonstrate that freeze-drying substantially improves the porous structure and adsorption capacity of CMC/GQD beads, providing a reusable adsorbent for cypermethrin-contaminated water.

Article.Title: A hypothesis-generating multi-resolution post-GWAS analysis of context-dependent regulatory signals in migraine
Article.Authors: Ding X.; Zhu Y.; Guo M.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genome-wide association studies have identified many migraine loci, but the effector genes and regulatory contexts remain uncertain. We meta-analysed summary statistics from FinnGen, UK Biobank and the Million Veteran Program (84,123 cases; 1,213,483 controls) using multiplicative random-effects inverse-variance weighting. We integrated gene-set and QTL enrichment, single-cell and bulk TWAS, PoPS, FOCUS, colocalization, and spatial and regulatory annotations. No MAGMA gene set or GTEx tissue survived false-discovery-rate correction. eQTL and sQTL enrichment was broad across tissues; coronary-artery sQTLs had the largest adjusted fold enrichment. Single-cell TWAS identified 39 genes. LRP1 was positively associated in effector-memory CD4 + T cells, whereas significant PTBP2, MRPS21 and TAGLN3 associations were negative across immune-cell models. PTBP2 had the broadest multi-method support; LRP1 was strongly prioritized but context dependent; MRPS21 was supported mainly by splicing colocalization; and TAGLN3 remained exploratory. These findings prioritize testable regulatory hypotheses but do not establish causal genes, tissues or mechanisms.

Article.Title: Impact of PTAA and MeO-2PACz hole transport layers on interfacial recombination in inverted perovskite solar cells
Article.Authors: Azamat o’g’li T.; Rustamovich A.; Oblakul o’g’li O.; Yuldashevich R.; Abdulkhamidovich A.
Article.Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) used as hole transport layers (HTLs) in inverted perovskite solar cells often outperform conventional HTLs based on conjugated polymers. To clarify the origin of this behaviour, we compare two widely used HTLs, the polymer PTAA and the SAM MeO-2PACz, in devices with an FA 0.9 Cs 0.1 PbI 3 absorber. MeO-2PACz-based devices achieve a substantially higher power conversion efficiency than their PTAA counterparts, mainly through a higher fill factor and open-circuit voltage. Steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence indicate more efficient hole extraction and reduced non-radiative recombination at the MeO-2PACz/perovskite interface. To identify the processes underlying these differences, bias- and illumination-dependent impedance spectra were analysed using the dual distribution of relaxation times (dual-DRT) method, which separates charge transfer, trap-assisted recombination and slow ionic relaxation by their timescales. At the MeO-2PACz interface, the recombination- and ion-related relaxation features are weaker and the transition to the recombination-dominated regime occurs at higher bias. This is consistent with interfacial defect passivation and reduced ionic polarization. These results show that the perovskite/SAM interface is better optimized for defect passivation than the perovskite/PTAA interface.

Article.Title: Sparrow Search Algorithm-optimized CNN–BiLSTM for lithium-ion battery capacity degradation prediction with SHAP-based interpretability
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Hassan M.; Ishak A.; As’arry A.; Okita T.; Ibrahim Ata K.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of lithium-ion battery capacity degradation is essential for battery health assessment and maintenance planning. This study presents an interpretable capacity prediction framework integrating a convolutional neural network (CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA)-based hyperparameter optimization, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Six health indicators derived from charging, discharging, and incremental-capacity profiles are used as model inputs. The CNN extracts local feature patterns, while the BiLSTM–LSTM–BiLSTM structure performs nonlinear feature processing. SSA optimizes the learning rate, regularization coefficient, and recurrent-layer hidden units, whereas SHAP quantifies the contributions of individual health indicators to the predicted capacity. The framework is evaluated on three experimentally aged 1.2 Ah lithium-ion batteries and the NASA B0005 dataset using chronological training, validation, and testing subsets. For the three experimental batteries, the reported RMSE values range from 0.003196 to 0.005025 Ah, with R² values between 0.922 and 0.989. On NASA B0005, the model achieves an RMSE of 0.0373 Ah and an R² of 0.8355. Under the adopted evaluation conditions, the proposed framework achieves lower prediction errors than four internal baseline models. SHAP analysis identifies the charging-current integral, time to minimum discharge voltage, and incremental-capacity peak as important contributors to the predicted capacity. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining capacity degradation prediction with model-specific feature interpretation to support battery health monitoring and condition-based maintenance decisions, while further cross-battery validation is required before practical deployment.

Article.Title: Performance optimization of evacuated tube solar air heater with twisted tape by using various machine learning methods
Article.Authors: Veerakumar A.; Ramkumar C.; Karthickmunisamy T.; Prasath S.; Sunilkumar R.; Terefe T.
Article.Abstract: The machine learning (ML) modelling techniques were evaluated for predicting the evacuated tube collector solar air heater with baffles and perforated twisted tape inserts (ETCSAHPTT) thermal performance. The experiments were run at flow of 100–500 kg/h, pitch ratios of 2, 2.5, and 3, and hole diameter ratios of 0.0714, 0.107, and 0.143. Output parameters such as temperature difference (TD), heat gain (HG) and thermal efficiency (TE) were taken into consideration. The five ML models (random forest (RF), multiple linear regression (MLP), support vector regression (SVR), multilayer perceptron (MLP) and gaussian process regression (GPR), ) were tested using 10-fold cross validation. The MLP model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy, with R 2 values of 0.9996, 0.9867, and 0.9952 for TD, HG, and TE, respectively. The flow rate was the most important parameter identified using partial dependence analysis. An increase in flow rate from 100 kg/h to 500 kg/h resulted in a reduction in TD from about 45-48 °C to 15-17 °C; an increase in HG from about 1450 W to above 1800 W; and an increase in TE from about 41-42% to above 55%. Increasing the pitch ratio and hole diameter ratio resulted in lower predicted thermal performance, whereas the pumping power requirement increased nonlinearly with the operating conditions. These quantification results show that the MLP model can accurately predict the thermal performance of the studied ETCSAH in the experimental operating range.

Article.Title: Tumor perfusion shows substantial temporal dynamics in super-resolution ultrasound measurements across 3-h intervals
Article.Authors: Raab A.; Baier J.; Porte C.; Lisson T.; Inczeffy P.; Mihyar R.; Schuppert A.; Girbig R.; Rix A.; Koletnik S.; Maurer J.; Dencks S.; Schmitz G.; Kiessling F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tumor perfusion is highly heterogeneous due to the abnormal structure and function of the tumor-associated vasculature. While spatial heterogeneity is well recognized, variability over short time intervals remains less well characterized. Here, motion model ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) was used to assess tumor microvascular parameters in two breast cancer xenograft models, MCF-7 (ER+/PR+) and BCSC1 (patient-derived triple-negative breast cancer model). Experiments were conducted in female BALB/cAnNRj-nu and NOD/SCID mice aged 6–8 weeks. ULM was performed using focused line-by-line nonlinear contrast imaging at a frame rate of 10 fps. Tumors were imaged longitudinally at identical positions over 9 h, with repeated acquisitions every 3 h following intravenous microbubble injections. Significant time effects were detected for mean track length and mean track-wise velocity range, while mean flow velocity and vessel tortuosity showed non-significant temporal trends. The remaining parameters showed no significant effects of time, tumor model, or interaction between time and model. Nevertheless, individual tumors showed substantial variability between measurement time points, most prominently in vessel coverage and distance to the closest track. These findings demonstrate that ULM-derived tumor perfusion parameters can vary substantially between measurements acquired at 3-h intervals and highlight the importance of temporal sampling when interpreting perfusion-sensitive imaging readouts.

Article.Title: Self-trust and locus of control under conditions of uncertainty among Ukrainian university students surveyed in 2020 and 2023
Article.Authors: Palamarchuk O.; Morska L.; Kolomiiets L.; Haba І.; Shulga H.
Article.Abstract: Ukrainian university students surveyed in 2020 ( n = 82) and 2023 ( n = 77) experienced distinct, overlapping forms of uncertainty. This repeated cross-sectional study compared self-trust and locus of control in two independent non-probability cohorts . Five open-ended questions, a self-trust assessment method, and the Level of Subjective Control questionnaire were used. Qualitative responses were analysed using content analysis. Quantitative analyses included the Mann–Whitney U test with Holm correction, Spearman correlation, and an additional approximate comparison of correlations based on Fisher’s z transformation. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for sex using regression models with HC3 robust standard errors. Self-trust was lower in the 2023 cohort ( U = 4034.0, p =.002, r ₍rb₎=0.278), and the difference remained statistically significant after adjustment for sex (B = − 3.449, p = .048). In 2023, overall internality and internality in the domains of failure, family, work, and interpersonal relationships domains were lower; after adjustment for sex, differences remained significant for six of the seven locus-of-control outcomes. A between-cohort difference in correlation strength was found only for the association between self-trust and interpersonal internality (ρ = 0.577 and 0.146; p Holm=0.011). The findings indicate selective between-cohort differences in self-trust and locus of control; however, the repeated cross-sectional design does not support causal interpretation.

Article.Title: Alterations in glymphatic system in patients with Sleep-related epilepsy: a study of PVS and DTI-ALPS index
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Wang D.; Xie F.; Jin H.; Feng X.; Ning X.; Hu D.; Xing W.
Article.Abstract: Sleep-related epilepsy (SRE) is a special type of epilepsy associated with arousal disorders. Glymphatic system function is related to sleep disturbances. However, whether the glymphatic system function is altered in patients with SRE remains unclear. This study is to explore the changes in glymphatic system function and its underlying neurobiological mechanisms. A total of 38 SRE patients and 40 healthy controls were prospectively enrolled. Diffusion tensor imaging along perivascular spaces (DTI-ALPS) index and perivascular space (PVS) volume fraction were measured to assess glymphatic function. We performed a partial correlation analysis to evaluate the correlations between glymphatic function indicators and clinical parameters. Patients with SRE had a higher DTI-ALPS index and lower white matter PVS volume fraction than controls ( P = 0.005, P = 0.002). The DTI-ALPS positively correlated with PADSS score ( r = 0.468; p = 0.004). Basal ganglia PVS volume fraction positively correlated with SAS score ( r = 0.465; p = 0.004). White matter PVS volume positively correlated with SAS score ( r = 0.486; p = 0.003) and negatively correlated with MoCA score ( r = − 0.330; p = 0.050). SRE patients may exhibit a compensatory enhancement of glymphatic function, which shows a certain degree of correlation with anxiety and neurocognitive function. The DTI-ALPS index and PVS volume fraction show potential as preliminary candidate neuroimaging markers requiring longitudinal, multicenter validation.

Article.Title: Impact of green hydrogen integration on the optimal sizing and cost of isolated PV–wind hybrid systems
Article.Authors: Abd Elaziz E.; Esmail M.; Ibrahim K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hybrid renewable energy systems, particularly wind–photovoltaic (PV) microgrids, are widely recognized as promising solutions for sustainable power generation. However, their economic performance is significantly affected by the high cost of energy storage elements, especially batteries, which are required to balance the intermittent nature of renewable sources. This challenge motivates the need for alternative strategies to mitigate the dependency on conventional storage systems. The main innovation of this work is the development of a unified techno-economic framework that comparatively evaluates the optimal sizing and techno-economic performance of five isolated PV–wind hybrid system configurations incorporating batteries, hydrogen production, fuel cells, and diesel backup under identical operating conditions. The framework further considers hydrogen as a revenue-generating energy carrier rather than solely an energy storage medium, enabling a comprehensive assessment of its impact on optimal system sizing and overall system cost. This paper proposes an effective approach to overcome the high cost associated with storage components by utilizing surplus renewable energy instead of relying solely on battery storage. During periods of excess generation-especially when wind and PV outputs coincide-the surplus energy is converted into hydrogen through electrolysis rather than being wasted. The produced hydrogen can be stored and later utilized via fuel cells or sold as a valuable energy carrier, thus improving the overall system economics without wasting the surplus renewable energy loss. Genetic Algorithm (GA) is employed to optimally size the system components under different operating scenarios. Five hybrid system configurations are optimized and comparatively analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that reducing reliance on battery storage while integrating hydrogen production significantly lowers the net present cost. A cost reduction of up to 78.5% is obtained under the considered assumptions, indicating the potential economic benefit of hydrogen integration.

Article.Title: Personality traits associated with attitudes toward end-of-life care among hospital nurses: a cross-sectional secondary analysis
Article.Authors: Fernández-Gutiérrez M.; Rodríguez-Barrios C.; Lubián-Fernández S.; Jiménez-Luque N.; Lubián-López S.; Benavente-Fernández I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract End-of-life care is frequently provided by hospital nurses outside specialist palliative care units. Although education and clinical experience have been linked to nurses’ attitudes toward caring for dying patients, the role of personality traits remains insufficiently understood. To examine the associations between work-related factors, Five-Factor Model personality dimensions, and attitudes toward end-of-life care among hospital nurses, accounting for relevant demographic, professional, and experiential characteristics. This single-centre cross-sectional secondary analysis included 303 registered nurses working in hospital where care of dying patients was provided. Attitudes were assessed using the Frommelt Attitudes Toward Care of the Dying Scale (FATCOD), and personality traits using the NEO Five-Factor Inventory. Associations with continuous FATCOD scores were examined using a theory-based multivariable linear regression model. The multivariable analysis included 297 participants. Higher Openness (B = 0.270, 95% CI 0.090 to 0.450; p = 0.003), Agreeableness (B = 0.362, 95% CI 0.085 to 0.639; p = 0.011), and Conscientiousness (B = 0.355, 95% CI 0.114 to 0.597; p = 0.004) were associated with higher FATCOD scores in the adjusted model. Compared with General Emergency, working in Critical Care was associated with a lower adjusted FATCOD score (B = − 3.444, 95% CI 6.378 to − 0.510; p = 0.022). Personality dimensions were associated with attitudes toward end-of-life care among hospital nurses. These cross-sectional findings support further investigation of how individual and work-related characteristics relate to end-of-life care attitudes but do not establish individual-level prediction or causality.

Article.Title: NeuroMemory-DiffNet: a reference-guided memory framework for brain tumor segmentation and classification
Article.Authors: Alagarsamy P.; Chandana B.; Hegde R.; Naveed Q.; Lasisi A.; Islam S.; Engida Yimer T.
Article.Abstract: The diagnosis of brain tumors is still difficult due to the diversity of tumor morphology, inter-individual anatomical differences and the limited interpretability of traditional deep learning models, despite the progress of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology. In order to overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a novel explainable framework named NeuroMemory-DiffNet (NMD-Net), which combines a Neuro-Anatomical Prior Memory (NAPM), Reference-Guided Difference Learning (RDL) and Healthy-Reference Reconstruction (HRR) to support anatomically guided brain tumor diagnosis. NMD-Net accesses a reference neuro-anatomical representation (NAR) derived from training, and uses RDL to estimate deviations between the observed MRI representation and the retrieved representation, which are related to the disease. The HRR branch is used to obtain a reference reconstruction and residual representation, highlighting the structural deviation toward the disease and minimising the impact of normal anatomical variation. To ensure structural coherence and facilitate strong feature learning and model level interpretability, an anatomical consistency constraint is added. The framework was tested on BraTS 2023 in the task of glioma segmentation and on the Figshare-based brain tumor dataset in the task of multi-class classification. NeuroMemory-DiffNet obtained an overall accuracy of 98.70%, a macro-averaged precision of 98.71%, a macro-averaged sensitivity of 98.70%, a macro-averaged specificity of 99.57% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 98.70% on the subject-independent test dataset for multi-class brain tumor classification. For tumor segmentation, the framework achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 96.31%, Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.62%, and Hausdorff Distance (HD95) of 2.29 mm and a false-positive rate (FPR) of 0.94%. Competitive performance to the benchmark level models evaluated in this work was achieved when compared with the evaluated models. The results show the benchmark level performance of NMD-Net for brain tumor classification and segmentation which also serve as model-level reference-guided explanations; however, they require further external and expert validation before making them clinically available.

Article.Title: Hydrological sensitivity and the reorganization of precipitation with temperature over the tibetan plateau
Article.Authors: Olowe J.; Cuo L.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how precipitation responds to temperature change is critical for interpreting hydroclimate risk over the Tibetan Plateau, a high-elevation water tower supplying major Asian river systems. While global-mean precipitation increases more slowly than Clausius–Clapeyron moisture scaling, regional responses can vary strongly with circulation and topography. We assess precipitation–temperature coupling over the Tibetan Plateau using two complementary approaches. First, we quantify Tibetan Plateau hydrological sensitivity (TPHS) from 14 CMIP6 models using idealized 1pctCO₂ and PiControl experiments (1850–1999), defined as the percentage change in precipitation per degree of warming. Second, we diagnose temperature-conditioned reorganization of daily precipitation occurrence using a quality-controlled 0.25° gridded observational dataset (1970–2019), evaluating precipitation intensity percentiles conditioned on temperature percentiles. The ensemble-mean TPHS is positive and seasonally varying: 3.6 ± 0.2% °C⁻¹ annually, with seasonal values of 2.6 ± 0.7 (winter), 4.9 ± 0.4 (spring), 3.6 ± 0.3 (summer), and 3.1 ± 0.5% °C⁻¹ (autumn). Observations show a systematic redistribution toward heavier daily intensities under warmer temperature regimes, most pronounced in spring and autumn. Together, these findings indicate that warming is associated with both an enhanced regional-mean precipitation response in CMIP6 models and a shift toward more frequent high-intensity precipitation in observations over the Tibetan Plateau.

Article.Title: Benzo[a]pyrene induces metabolic alterations and associated effects on cholesterol and vitamin D-related pathways in zebrafish embryos
Article.Authors: Ali M.; Ali F.; Berry J.; Matysik J.; Ewendt F.; Alia A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Benzo[ a ]pyrene (BaP), a highly toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon, is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen. Although BaP-induced carcinogenicity, oxidative stress, and developmental toxicity are well established, the mechanisms linking xenobiotic-induced stress responses to endocrine-metabolic dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we combined high-resolution magic angle spinning (HR-MAS) NMR-based metabolite profiling with targeted mRNA expression analysis to characterize BaP-induced toxicity in intact zebrafish embryos. BaP exposure caused developmental abnormalities, including reduced hatching success and survival rates, and induced widespread reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in multiple organs, including the liver and brain. HR-MAS NMR revealed metabolic reprogramming involving lipid, amino acid, and energy metabolism, with alterations associated with mitochondrial function. These changes were accompanied by altered expression of genes involved in xenobiotic detoxification, antioxidant defense, mitochondrial homeostasis, and neurodevelopmental regulation. Notably, altered expression of cyp2r1 and dhcr7 suggested changes in pathways related to cholesterol and vitamin D metabolism. Together these findings indicate that BaP exposure induces coordinated oxidative, transcriptional, and metabolic responses in developing zebrafish and provide a systems-level view of BaP toxicity. The observed alterations in cholesterol- and vitamin D-related pathways further suggest that endocrine-metabolic processes may contribute to the response to environmental toxicant exposure.

Article.Title: Effective regulatory relationships between genes differ from direct transcription factor-target interactions, and exhibit a distinct statistical signature
Article.Authors: Velázquez-Trejo D.; Islas-Ortíz J.; Rueda-Zarazúa B.; Hernández-Olvera A.; Olascoaga S.; Ramirez-Lugo L.; Gutiérrez H.
Article.Abstract: Gene expression patterns are determined by the interactions between thousands of transcriptional regulators and their target genes. However, mounting evidence of an apparent lack of causal and statistical association between transcription factors and their targets, raises the question of where the effective regulation of any particular gene lies. Using a simple computational gene regulatory network model together with human expression and perturbation data for 796 known transcription factors and their confirmed targets, we demonstrate a widespread and generalized lack of statistical and causal association between the activity of regulators and direct targets. We introduce the concept of effective regulators: genes that, upon experimental down-regulation, have the strongest impact on a given target. Effective regulators form a small set of genes that display a distinct statistical signature, and networks constructed from effective regulators exhibit greater clustering and connectivity than canonical TF-based networks. Our results show that, while at the transcriptome-level, actual effective regulatory relationships between genes do not coincide with direct transcription factor–target interactions and are, instead, diffusely distributed throughout the transcriptional network, they can potentially be identified based on their distinct statistical properties.

Article.Title: Fishers’ local ecological knowledge recovers information about the recent-past existence of a Caribbean coastal shark and ray nursery area
Article.Authors: Espinoza M.; Padilla-Saldívar J.; Bonfil R.
Article.Abstract: Elasmobranchs have declined sharply due to overfishing and habitat destruction. Nursery-areas are crucial for the recruitment and sustainability of elasmobranch populations; however, they have been scarcely studied globally and in Mexico. We used fishers’ Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) to investigate whether Bahía de la Ascensión was an elasmobranch nursery-area 30 + years-ago, and for which species. Shark nursery-areas are defined by three criteria that we evaluated using semi-structured interviews covering 90% of the target population (local fishers aged 40+). Several elasmobranchs met all criteria, supporting that this bay served as a communal elasmobranch nursery-area 30 + years-ago for Carcharhinus leucas , C. limbatus , Ginglymostoma cirratum , Negaprion brevirostris , Hypanus americanus and Styracura schmardae. Additionally, fishers reported changes in early-offspring elasmobranch abundance –including declines and increases– between our study-period and the present. This is the first study showing that LEK can be used to reconstruct the former existence of elasmobranch nursery-areas, highlighting its value to rescue past information in data-poor contexts, in support of conservation. This approach can and should be widely-applied for similar purposes. Our study is part of a trans-disciplinary project examining past-and-present elasmobranch nurseries in the Mexican Caribbean, providing a baseline to evaluate changes while preventing misinterpretation based solely on present-day data.

Article.Title: Danlou Tablets modulates the HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway, targeting ferroptosis and cholesterol synthesis to combat hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Pei Y.; Sun X.; Li B.; Xu J.; Wang Q.; Gao Y.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) involves abnormal cholesterol metabolism and evasion of ferroptosis. The HMGCR-mediated Mevalonate (MVA) pathway is a key regulatory hub in both processes. Given the efficacy of Danlou Tablets (DLT) in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and the inflammation-cancer transformation theory, this study investigates the potential inhibitory effects of DLT on HCC and its underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology was used to identify the shared targets among DLT, HCC, ferroptosis, and cholesterol synthesis. Bioinformatics analysis based on public databases was performed to explore the clinical significance of HMGCR in patients with HCC. In parallel, UPLC/ESI-Q TRAP-MS/MS was employed to identify the active components of DLT, and molecular docking was subsequently conducted to evaluate their binding affinity to HMGCR. Using Western Blot (WB) and transfection assays, we systematically validated the activation of the MVA pathway, alterations in cholesterol synthesis, and the occurrence of ferroptosis in both clinical HCC tissues and in vitro cell models. We aimed to establish whether DLT could regulate the HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway, which modulates cholesterol synthesis and ferroptosis, thereby potentially inhibiting HCC progression. UPLC/ESI-Q TRAP-MS/MS analysis identified 1,003 components in DLT. In DLT-containing serum, 87 components were upregulated and 22 were downregulated. Molecular docking revealed that eight components may exert therapeutic effects that are partly dependent on HMGCR. In clinical HCC tissues, WB and qRT-PCR assays demonstrated aberrant activation of the HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway, accompanied by accelerated cholesterol synthesis and suppressed ferroptosis. In vitro experiments, including flow cytometry, wound healing assay, and colony formation assays, confirmed that DLT significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation and migration. WB and qRT-PCR further showed that DLT inhibited cholesterol synthesis and promoted ferroptosis in HCC cells. Mechanistic studies using WB and transfection assays confirmed the critical role of the HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway in DLT-induced HCC inhibition. HMGCR overexpression reversed the DLT-induced inhibition of the MVA pathway in HCC cells, thereby restoring cholesterol synthesis and suppressing ferroptosis mediated by the MVA pathway. DLT may regulate the HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway, modulating cholesterol synthesis and ferroptosis in HCC cells and ultimately suppressing HCC development.

Article.Title: Eco-friendly geopolymer masonry units using ferrosilicon slag and Homra: experimental performance evaluation
Article.Authors: Ahmed M.; Yousef A.; Saleh M.; Ebid A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The escalating environmental concerns associated with traditional clay brick manufacturing necessitate the development of sustainable, low-carbon alternatives. This study investigates the novel utilization of Ferrosilicon slag (FS) and Homra as primary precursors for producing geopolymer masonry units. The research aims to evaluate the synergistic effects of varying Homra dosages (0 H:1 S, 2 H:1 S, and 3 H:1 S ratios) and sodium hydroxide molarities (6, 8, and 10 M) on the physical, mechanical, and thermal performance of the geopolymer matrix. A comprehensive experimental program was conducted, including assessments of apparent porosity, water absorption, bulk density, compressive strength, and thermal conductivity up to 28 days of curing, supplemented by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for microstructural characterization. The results reveal that incorporating Homra significantly enhances the densification of the geopolymer matrix. The 2 H:1 S formulation (66.7% Homra: 33.3% FS) activated at 10 M achieved optimal performance, yielding a 28-day compressive strength of approximately 9.2 MPa—a nearly 163% enhancement with respect to pure FS control—along with the lowest apparent porosity and water absorption. SEM and XRD analyses indicated the formation of a highly dense, amorphous N-A-S-H gel structure responsible for these improvements. Furthermore, all mixtures exhibited low thermal conductivity values (0.35–0.75 W/m·K), validating their suitability for insulation. The study concludes that the synergistic combination of FS and Homra offers a promising, eco-friendly approach for manufacturing high-performance masonry units, significantly contributing to waste valorization and circular economy principles in the construction industry.

Article.Title: Comparative network meta-analysis of immunotherapy and targeted agents for glioblastoma survival and response
Article.Authors: Shafi S.; Anwaar W.; Hamid A.; Yang J.; Sun M.
Article.Abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains a lethal malignancy. While immunotherapy has revolutionized oncology, its success in GBM has been inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) to quantify the comparative efficacy of immunotherapeutic and targeted agents against the Standard of Care (SoC). Following PRISMA-NMA guidelines, we searched PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov for randomized controlled trials. A Bayesian random-effects NMA was conducted using gemtc in R interfaced with JAGS . Heterogeneity was summarized using tau-squared, I-squared and Cochran's Q. Node-splitting was planned but was not estimable because the network geometry lacked comparisons informed by both direct and indirect evidence. Twenty-six randomized contrasts from 23 trials contributed to the overall survival (OS) network and 28 randomized contrasts from 24 trials to the progression-free survival (PFS) network, across 24 unique trials; because trials could contribute to more than one outcome network, these overlapping counts are not additive. Objective response rate (ORR) was too sparse for treatment ranking and was reported descriptively for two trials contributing five arms and three treatment–control contrasts. No investigational regimen showed a pooled OS or PFS advantage over harmonized control regimens, as all pooled relative-effect 95% credible intervals included 1.0, and rankings were sensitive to sparse network structure.

Article.Title: Assessment of interkingdom TIR domain interactions using a modular yeast tripartite split-GFP system
Article.Authors: Fernández-Vega A.; del Val E.; Coronas-Serna J.; Martín H.; Molina M.; Rodríguez-Escudero I.; Cid V.
Article.Abstract: Thanks to its genetic resourcefulness, Saccharomyces cerevisiae has been traditionally used as a model organism to detect and study protein-protein interactions. The recent development of synthetic biology toolkits brings an opportunity to expand such utilities. Here, we coupled the modular cloning (MoClo) system to the tripartite split-GFP strategy to systematically study protein interactions in particular cellular localizations. To provide proof-of-principle of this yeast-based tripartite split-GFP (ytpGFP), we challenged interactions of bacterial TIR domain-containing proteins ( Brucella BtpA and BtpB) between themselves, as well as against human TIR adaptors of the myddosome and triffosome innate immune signaling complexes. While fluorescence microscopy provided clues about which member of the interacting pair drives subcellular localization of the complex, interactions could be readily tracked and quantified by flow cytometry. The ytpGFP system detected known homotypic or heterotypic complexes and defined previously unknown interkingdom TIR-TIR interactions. Human MyD88, TIRAP, TRAM, and TRIF were capable of interacting with both BtpA and BtpB TIR domains with differing efficiency. Furthermore, our results suggest that the N-terminal non-TIR extensions of both BtpA and, especially, BtpB limit the ability of their TIR domains to interact. This strategy is a useful addition to other yeast-based tools to study protein complexes.

Article.Title: Comprehensive comparative genomics of camelids identifies positive selection, structural variants, and gene losses driving desert adaptation
Article.Authors: Kasimu H.; Han B.; Mohsin M.; Ahmad H.; Iqbal M.; Fouad D.; Ataya F.
Article.Abstract: Camelids have evolved remarkable physiological adaptations enabling survival in extreme desert environments, yet the genomic basis of these traits remains incompletely understood. We conducted a comparative genomic analysis across eleven mammalian species, including three Old World camels, four New World camels, two additional artiodactyls (pig, cattle), and two outgroups (human, mouse), to identify lineage-specific molecular signatures of adaptation. Using OrthoFinder, we constructed orthologous gene families and identified 11,861 single-copy orthologs across all species. We detected significant copy-number changes in cytochrome P450 gene families, with expansion of CYP2J and contraction of CYP4F in the camelid ancestor, suggesting a shift toward anti-inflammatory eicosanoid signaling. Branch-site analyses identified 47 high-confidence positively selected genes in Old World camels, including HACD3 , a fatty acid elongation enzyme harboring an ultraconserved substitution ( D270N ). Structural modeling and conservation analysis suggest that this substitution may hypothetically alter protein conformation, but this prediction awaits experimental validation. Tissue-specific RNA-seq analysis confirmed that HACD3 is expressed in camel kidney and liver, tissues central to lipid metabolism and water conservation. Systematic screening for inactivating mutations identified ten high-confidence pseudogenized genes, including CES3 , CPA3 , and PLA2G2F , enriched in lipid metabolism and epidermal pathways. The adaptive significance of these losses is currently hypothetical and inferred from homologous gene studies in mice and humans; because some of the cited genes are paralogs rather than orthologs, and because mouse and human phenotypes may not transfer to camels, these inferences are hypothesis-generating only and do not establish camel gene function. Experimental validation confirmed pseudogenization of TAS2R16, and cell-based calcium-signalling assays showed that the camel receptor fails to respond to salicin. This establishes loss of receptor function but not its adaptive significance; both dietary-breadth and neutral (relaxed-selection or drift) explanations remain compatible with the data. For CES3 , CPA3 , and PLA2G2F , functional consequences in camels remain unverified and require camel-specific experimental validation. Collectively, these results provide a comprehensive framework of gene family evolution, positive selection, and gene loss underlying desert adaptation in camelids, while highlighting that expression patterns are correlative only and do not demonstrate that the identified variants alter protein function or physiology.

Article.Title: Source apportionment, geochemical characterization, and inhalation health-risk assessment of PM2.5 in Tabriz and Urmia, northwestern Iran
Article.Authors: Rajabi M.; Souri B.
Article.Abstract: Desiccation of Lake Urmia may expose nearby cities to lakebed dust, but source-resolved evidence is lacking. The elemental composition of PM 2.5 (particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter < 2.5 μm) sampled weekly from March to December 2024 in the metropolitan areas of Tabriz (TBR) and Urmia (URM), northwestern Iran, were characterized through combining Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF), geochemical indices and United States Environmental Protection Agency health risk assessment (USEPA). PMF resolved seven factors per site. Lake Urmia lakebed dust was the largest source at TBR (32.20% of PM 2.5 ; Ti loading 85.80% of species sum) and the main geogenic source at URM (16.60%; Na/K/Mg-dominated), a contrast consistent with size-selective aeolian fractionation. Industrial/heavy oil combustion (29.80%) at TBR and traffic exhaust (22.00%) at URM led the anthropogenic contributions. EF and I geo showed extreme enrichment of Zn, Ba, and Ag at both cities, with Cd, Sb, and Mo additionally extremely enriched at URM. Contamination indices were higher at URM (PLI = 4.63; mCd = 63.83; IPI = 1080.60) than at TBR (PLI = 1.00; mCd = 33.42; IPI = 783.04), but these values mainly reflect the halite-evaporitic background of lakebed dust, a bias of crust-normalized indices shown here for a hypersaline terminal-lake setting, rather than literal pollution levels. Adult Incremental Lifetime Cancer Risk (ILCR) at TBR (1.43 × 10⁻⁶) fell within the USEPA tolerable range (1 × 10⁻⁶–1 × 10⁻⁴), and chromium, assumed fully Cr(VI) an upper bound, contributed 96.2% (TBR) and 87.7% (URM) of total ILCR; PMF attributed this chromium mainly to non-exhaust traffic emissions, whereas arsenic dominated the non-chromium fraction. MANOVA and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) indicated strong compositional divergence between the cities. Traffic control and industrial arsenic abatement are the most actionable regulatory targets.

Article.Title: Decision-focused learning for dynamic aggregation optimization of flexible resource clusters in active distribution networks
Article.Authors: An L.; Liu X.; Lu Y.; Xiang J.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Active distribution networks require flexible resources to respond at the right location and time while respecting device and feeder constraints. This study formulates decision-focused dynamic aggregation by connecting a graph-temporal representation of resource capability to cluster formation and network-constrained dispatch. The model distinguishes dispatch instructions from contracted delivery, links device controls to nodal power balances, and trains continuous dispatch decisions through a conditional convex optimization layer. Cluster assignments and discrete device modes are handled outside that layer. In the reported numerical comparison, the normalized regret index is 0.56 against a deterministic reference of 1.00; the corresponding voltage and under-delivery penalty indices are 0.18 and 0.15. The highest photovoltaic-penetration case reports curtailment of 8.7%, compared with 16.4% for deterministic aggregation and 13.5% for forecast-then-optimize scheduling. The numerical experiments demonstrate improved dispatch quality and renewable utilization in the studied operating cases. The framework aligns flexibility estimation with the device and feeder constraints that determine its operational value.

Article.Title: UltraSAM-based left ventricular analysis with local–global feature fusion for echocardiographic cardiac disease classification
Article.Authors: Alazeb A.; Basir F.; Najam S.; Alabdullah B.; Alonazi M.; Jalal A.; kim Y.; Kim K.; Shin J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases, particularly myocardial infarction (MI), remain a leading cause of global mortality, necessitating accurate and early diagnostic solutions beyond conventional operator-dependent echocardiographic analysis. The proposed hybrid deep learning framework in this study combines the region-specific and global representations for automatic cardiac disease classification from echocardiographic videos. It uses transformer-based UltraSAM to accurately segment the left-ventricular (LV) myocardium, and then extracts various features such as shape, texture (GLCM), motion (optical flow), and keypoint-based descriptors to characterize the myocardial structure and dynamics. Concurrently, a Swin Transformer is used to obtain the global spatial representations from complete echocardiographic frames. The heterogeneous attributes are fused and optimized by employing Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and temporal dependency is modeled by applying LSTM for robust classification. Experimental evaluation on the HMC-QU dataset achieves an accuracy of 94.7% with significant sensitivity (93%) and specificity (97%) for MI detection. In addition, the model has shown significant generalization capability on the CardiacNet dataset with an accuracy of 90.3% in binary classification (PAH, ASD), and 81.4% in multi-class classification( PAH, ASD, Non-PAH, Non-ASD). The results here confirm the efficiency of the proposed hybrid framework in capturing ventricular abnormalities at the local level and capturing the general structure of the heart for the reliable detection of cardiovascular disease.

Article.Title: Learning distribution-calibrated and prompt-robust quality representations for cross-prompt automated essay scoring inEnglish writing assessment
Article.Authors: Huan Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In English language teaching and writing assessment, cross-prompt automated essay scoring (AES) requires models trained on existingsource prompts to generalize to unseen prompts without relying on target-prompt responses. A central challenge is that prompts differ not only in rubric ranges but also in score distributions and optimization characteristics, so numerical score normalization alone may not provide transferable supervision. This study proposes DCR-AES, a source-only framework that combines prompt-relative empirical-distribution calibration, separation-filtered cross-prompt relative-quality learning, and prompt-level distributionally robust optimization. Human scores are mapped to mid-rank empirical cumulative distribution function (eCDF) positions estimated exclusively from source-prompt training data. These positions are interpreted as prompt-relative ordinal coordinates rather than absolute cross-prompt quality equivalents and are used to construct ranking constraints only when the calibrated separation is sufficiently large. Prompt-level robust optimization further adapts source-domain contributions according to persistent training loss while retaining a uniform contribution from all source prompts. Under strict leave-one-prompt-out evaluation on ASAP++, the five-run analysis yields a prompt-level QWK of 0.593 ± 0.004 (95% CI [0.588, 0.598]) and an attribute-level QWK of 0.590 ± 0.004. DCR-AES improves over PLAES by 0.0179 QWK across the eight held-out prompts (Wilcoxon p = 0.0078; rank-biserial effect size = 1.00), does not differ significantly from ProTACT, and remains below SICTS and stronger resource-enhanced systems in absolute QWK. Additional analyses show that calibration gains are positively associated with source-target score-distribution shift, while learned DRO weights correlate strongly with persistent training loss but not with static sample count or score-distribution descriptors. Article.Title: Positional encoding cross-attention ResNet50 framework for lung cancer classification across CT and histopathological imaging modalities
Article.Authors: Nivashini A.; Krishnamurthy M.
Article.Abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, primarily due to delayed diagnosis and limitations associated with manual interpretation of medical images. Deep learning approaches, particularly convolutional neural networks such as ResNet50, have demonstrated significant potential for automated medical image analysis. However, accurately capturing both low-level structural information and high-level semantic information within medical images remains a challenging task. This study proposes a Positional Encoding Cross-Attention ResNet50 framework that enhances feature representation learning through interactions between shallow structural features and deep semantic features extracted from different stages of the same backbone network. A two-dimensional positional encoding mechanism is incorporated to preserve spatial information, while a cross-attention module enables the model to selectively emphasize diagnostically relevant image regions. The proposed framework was independently evaluated on publicly available chest CT scan and histopathological image datasets for lung cancer classification. Experimental results demonstrate that the attention-enhanced architecture improves classification performance by effectively integrating structural and semantic information within each imaging modality. In addition, a separate rule-based clinical decision-support module provides indicative assessments of cancer stage, severity, and recovery range based on externally supplied clinical parameters. These outputs should be interpreted as decision-support estimates rather than validated prognostic predictions. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of intra-modality attention-guided feature learning for lung cancer image classification across multiple imaging modalities.

A structure-activity relationship analysis showed that several phenothiazine derivatives inhibited Poly(I:​C)-induced ICAM-1 expression in HUVEC. Article.Title: Genome-resolved metagenomic profiling of respiratory and blood microbiomes in Gambian children with pneumonia
Article.Authors: Khan D.; Espinoza J.; Tientcheu P.; Otchere I.; Mohammed N.; Worwui A.; Nicol M.; Kwambana-Adams B.; Antonio M.; Dupont C.
Article.Abstract: Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children, with bacterial pathogens being important aetiologic agents. However, most microbiome studies of childhood pneumonia use technologies with limited taxonomic resolution, and few have included lung aspirate or blood samples. In this study, we applied genome-resolved shotgun metagenomics to characterise the microbial communities and recover metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from the nasopharynx, nasopharynx/oropharynx, induced sputum, lung aspirate and blood of children with severe or very severe pneumonia in The Gambia. Our data show that Proteobacteria and Firmicutes were the most common phyla across the body sites, and this was largely driven by Streptococcus pneumoniae , Haemophilus influenzae/aegyptius and Moraxella catarrhalis. Blood and nasopharyngeal samples showed a mean species-level Jaccard similarity of 58%, which was greater than expected under random pairing of specimens (q = 0.046). We recovered 60 medium-quality MAGs, of which 35 met the criteria for high-quality MAGs including 11 S. pneumoniae genomes, 10 H. influenzae genomes and a Limosilactobacillus genome with less than 95% Average Nucleotide Identity to the closest species in the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB). We also showed that antimicrobial resistance genes in our MAGs were highly species-specific; more than 70% of the unique AMR genes detected (11/15) were found only within MAGs of a single bacterial species rather than shared across multiple species. Together, these findings demonstrate the value of shotgun metagenomics in resolving species-level detail across clinically relevant but understudied specimen types and provide a genomic resource to support future respiratory pathogen surveillance in low- and middle-income settings.

Article.Authors: Dhar A.; Dey S.; Ghosh S.; Sarkar S.; Ghosh A.; Bhowmik P.; Tunga C.; Bera M.; Tripathi S.; Mainuddin M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Agriculture in the Indian Sundarbans depends on surface water for irrigation, yet its quality is governed by complex geo-hydro-chemical processes. Farm ponds are the main source of dry-season irrigation in the Indian Sundarbans, yet their suitability has not been assessed at the pond scale at which irrigation decisions are made. We analysed 52 GPS-referenced pond-water samples collected at the pre-monsoon salinity peak (March 2025) in three villages: Rangabelia ( n = 16), Choto Mollakhali ( n = 18) and Satjelia ( n = 18) to ask whether salinity or sodicity limits use, whether hazards outside a composite index matter, and how much variation occurs within rather than between villages. Eight irrigation indices, hydrochemical diagrams, non-parametric tests, principal component analysis and cross-validated kriging were combined. Sodium hazard rose with it (EC–SAR r = 0.53): three samples reached class S2, 19 were doubtful or unsuitable on sodium percentage, and Kelley’s ratio exceeded unity in 24. The irrigation water quality index placed 28.8% of samples in the high or severe restriction classes. Magnesium hazard exceeded 50% in 88.5% of samples, and three ponds were strongly acidic (pH 2.89–4.29), hazards the index does not capture. Within-village spatial autocorrelation was weak, so pond-level screening is required.

Article.Title: A replayable intervention workflow for data-programmed Kuramoto networks in exploratory unconventional computing
Article.Authors: Oosawa C.
Article.Abstract: Data-driven Kuramoto representations are not new: coupled phase oscillators have previously been used to synchronize and extract structure from multivariate data. Here we address a different question: whether a fixed data-derived oscillator substrate can be interrogated reproducibly through controlled state interventions. Low-dimensional features are compiled into symmetric signed couplings, after which the couplings are frozen and the resulting dynamics are queried through a pause–inspect–edit–resume protocol. The contribution is therefore a replayable intervention workflow rather than a new synchronization theorem or clustering algorithm. A worked Iris example illustrates the protocol, while a small batch audit over five label-aware hard cases and matched same-class controls shows that recovery behavior is sample-specific and does not, in the present data, establish a general dynamical law linking hard-case status to slower relocking. Compact sensitivity checks further show that sign-preserving monotone coupling maps retain closely related pairwise phase organization, whereas shifting the attraction–repulsion threshold can change global order. These results support a cautious interpretation of iDra as a reproducible exploratory protocol built on a known oscillator substrate, with quantitative diagnostics and explicit limitations.

Impedance spectra showed a decrease in the resistive contribution with increasing temperature. The dielectric permittivity exhibited pronounced frequency dispersion and increased at low frequencies with temperature, reaching approximately 2500 at 560 K. These results provide a combined assessment of the optical, transport, and dielectric responses of the prepared BaTiO 3 ceramic over the investigated measurement ranges.

Article.Authors: Naveen K.; Mishra V.; Jayanthiladevi A.; Senthilkumar T.; varma K.; Allasi H.
Article.Abstract: The accurate prediction of thermophysical properties are required to design hybrid nanofluid based thermal systems. In this study, the thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity of TiO₂–CuO (50:50) hybrid nanofluid is studied experimentally in the temperature and volume concentration range of 30–60 °C and 0–0.5 vol%, respectively. From the experimental results, it was found that thermal conductivity was higher with increasing temperature and nanoparticle concentration up to 12.6% at highest concentration (0.5 vol%) and temperature (60 °C) when compared to the base fluid. At 30 °C, water exhibited a 20.41% higher specific heat capacity than nanofluid concentration of 0.5 vol%. The experimental data were then used for building Support Vector Regression (SVR) models for estimation of thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity. Three cross validation protocols were applied to evaluate model robustness and generalization abilities, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to explain the influence of input parameters on model outputs. The predictive performance of the developed SVR models was excellent under LOO and LOTO validation, with markedly reduced performance under LOPO (concentration-level) extrapolation, particularly for specific heat capacity. In general, the proposed SVR–SHAP model is an accurate, strong, and interpretable tool to predict the thermophysical properties of TiO₂–CuO/water hybrid nanofluid.

The prolong gastric residence time helps in reducing the frequency of administration and ensuring sustained control up to 24 h. The compression attributes were determined by Heckel analysis and USP 1062. A Quality by Design (QbD)- based risk assessment was performed to identify the Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) and critical variables. The high-risk score was determined for buoyancy parameters (floating lag time, total floating time, swelling index) and in vitro drug release at 1, 12, and 24 h, relative to HPMC K15M and Carbopol 971, as CMAs. The compression analysis revealed yield pressure of 161 MPa for tablet formation. A Central Composite Design (CCD) was used to generate the experimental design and design space via numerical optimization. The optimized formulation (F opt ) was characterized by buoyancy parameters, in vitro drug release, surface morphology, chemical interactions, and thermal stability by SEM, FTIR, and DSC, respectively. F opt released > 90% of the complex within 24 h and was found to be stable, with a shelf life of 16 months. In silico PBPK modeling using GastroPlus™ yielded PK parameters and bioavailability values comparable to the reported data. The controlled-release gastro-retentive floating tablets of (VAL-SAC) complex were formulated successfully using the combined effect of swelling and rate-controllable polymers.

Article.Title: Maternal perceptions and practices regarding traditional milk tooth extraction among children under five years in Khartoum State, Sudan: a multicenter cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Abdalla D.; Hamza H.; Ibrahim D.; Mohamed Z.; Altahir N.; Elageid R.; Suliman D.; Mohammed Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional healing practices are common in Sudan and Sub-Saharan Africa. Milk tooth extraction (MTE) refers to the manual removal of primary tooth buds, typically performed on children under five years of age. This practice is believed to have a therapeutic effect for symptoms such as diarrhea, vomiting, and cough. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MTE and to describe mothers’ perceptions of this practice. This cross-sectional study was conducted in seven teaching hospitals across Khartoum State. Mothers of children presenting to pediatric units were interviewed using a semi-structured questionnaire. The variables assessed included mothers’ perceptions of MTE, whether their child had undergone MTE, and a description of the procedure. A total of 385 mothers of children under five years participated in the study. The mean age of the participants was 34.96 years (SD ± 7.504), and the mean age of the children was 2.14 years (SD ± 1.350). Among the children, 174 (45.2%) were females and 211 (54.8%) were males. Approximately 154 mothers (40%) endorsed the practice of MTE. Reported reasons for performing MTE included family tradition (69.4%), diarrhea (56.1%), vomiting (46.5%), and fever (37.7%). The prevalence of MTE was 18.4% (70 out of 385 children). Factors significantly associated with this practice included maternal age, maternal education level, and rural origin. No major complications related to MTE were reported Most mothers did not report complications following MTE; however, fever, bleeding and other adverse events were reported. Milk tooth extraction (MTE) remains a common traditional practice acknowledged by Sudanese mothers. Awareness-raising initiatives regarding the risks of MTE should be implemented through health education campaigns in primary healthcare centers and hospitals, particularly targeting women of childbearing age and healthcare practitioners.

Article.Authors: Luo M.; Li Q.; Yuan C.; Ma R.; Ni Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence mechanism of water on rock slope stability under different water-content conditions, a high rock slope along a section of the Chongqing–Guizhou Expressway was selected as the engineering case. Initially, field samples were collected and sandstone specimens with varying water content were prepared. Uniaxial compression tests and shear property tests were conducted on natural structural planes within the rock mass to investigate the impact of water on both rock mass specimens and structural planes, while also deeply analyzing the mechanism by which water influences slope instability. Moreover, the slope excavation process under natural and saturated states was analyzed using the 3D-σ three-dimensional finite element numerical simulation software. Herein the stress and displacement variations of the slope during and after excavation were calculated and discussed for different water content states. The results of both physical experiments and numerical calculations demonstrated that: (1) In comparison to the natural state, there was a 23.88% decrease in compressive strength, a 12.34% decrease in elastic modulus, as well as a 21.2% increase in Poisson’s ratio. (2) The deformation of rock mass increases with a higher water content, while its shear strength decreases accordingly. When the rock masses reach a saturated state, there was an observed reduction in shear strength by 11.17%, cohesion decreases by 16.09%, and internal friction angle decreases by 10.02%. (3) The numerical simulation results showed that deformation and stress concentration were closely associated with the weak interlayer, while water saturation amplified the instability response by degrading the mechanical parameters of the slope materials. Compared with the natural condition, the saturated slope exhibited markedly greater shear stress and horizontal displacement during staged excavation. These findings provide a case-based reference for evaluating water-induced stability degradation of sandstone–mudstone interbedded highway rock slopes under comparable geological and hydrological conditions.

Article.Title: Carbon negative scheduling of direct air capture and hydrogen production in PV powered AI data centers under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Ye L.; Yang Z.; Liu Z.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure, exemplified by OpenAI’s data centers, has significantly intensified electricity demand and carbon emissions. To mitigate this environmental impact, this paper proposes a novel photovoltaic (PV)-powered microgrid system that integrates Direct Air Capture (DAC) and hydrogen production to simultaneously achieve carbon removal and renewable energy storage. Unlike conventional microgrid scheduling frameworks, this study develops a multi-objective Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) model that addresses uncertain renewable generation, fluctuating electricity prices, and volatile hydrogen and carbon credit markets. The optimization simultaneously minimizes total operational costs, maximizes CO \(_2\) capture efficiency, and ensures hydrogen production aligns with both storage targets and market conditions. The uncertainty modeling is handled by DRO, capturing worst-case deviations within an ambiguity set derived from historical data, ensuring operational resilience. Furthermore, the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) is employed to derive Pareto-optimal trade-offs, providing comprehensive decision support across financial, environmental, and technical dimensions. The proposed optimization framework is applied to a realistic case study modeled on OpenAI’s energy infrastructure. A 100 MW PV farm supplies renewable energy, supported by a 50 MWh battery system and a 60 MW electrolyzer for hydrogen production. The DAC system operates within a 3.5 MW baseline demand, scaling dynamically with surplus solar power. Historical data from NREL, CAISO, EU-ETS, and California hydrogen markets inform the realistic energy prices, carbon credits, and hydrogen values. The optimization is implemented using Pyomo, solved with Gurobi 10.0, and combined with NSGA-III via Platypus. Sensitivity analysis, including Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 trials, evaluates system resilience under varying solar irradiance, market price volatility, and operational uncertainties. The results demonstrate that PV generation directly governs DAC efficiency and hydrogen production scalability, with clear synchronization between high solar availability and optimal carbon capture performance. Pareto-optimal solutions reveal that increasing CO \(_2\) removal efficiency from 65% to 85% requires a 27% increase in operational costs, highlighting a trade-off between environmental and economic objectives. Furthermore, hydrogen storage utilization peaks at 85% when carbon credit prices surpass $90/ton, indicating strong market-driven operational shifts. Grid dependency reduces by 46% in scenarios prioritizing CO \(_2\) capture, underscoring the system’s ability to enhance renewable self-sufficiency.

Plateau intensity (A), replenishment rate constant (β), and A × β were measured, with segment-matched fluorescent-microsphere-derived MBF as the reference. Of 408 segments, 407 were analyzed. The adapted estimate preserved the basal-to-apical perfusion pattern but showed poor agreement with reference MBF (CCC = 0.080; RMSE = 3.479 mL·min⁻¹·g⁻¹). After adjustment for myocardial level, the adapted estimate did not improve model fit ( P = 0.328), whereas A × β remained associated with reference MBF ( P = 0.005). The final mixed-effects calibration equation was MBF = 2.863 + 0.176I_Basal − 0.906I_Apical + 0.012(A × β). Adding A × β to myocardial level alone changed leave-one-heart-out cross-validation RMSE from 0.510 to 0.508 mL·min⁻¹·g⁻¹ and CCC from 0.648 to 0.653. Predictive performance was driven predominantly by myocardial level, with A × β providing modest additional predictive information. This condition-specific proof-of-concept calibration under standardized constant-flow conditions requires validation in independent preparations and across broader perfusion conditions before wider application.

Article.Title: Nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous relationships between urban features and land surface temperature in a subtropical city
Article.Authors: Hu P.; Zhang M.; Chen B.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Prolonged hot seasons, intense solar radiation, hot and humid conditions, rapid urbanization, and intensive development exacerbate subtropical heat risks. NDBI showed relatively continuous areas of high local importance, whereas BSC and HBR areas were more dispersed; and (3) predictive contributions increased continuously for NDBI, initially increased then decreased for NTL, and declined overall for DEM, while BSC showed a non-monotonic response and HBR a nonlinear decline that levelled off. Joint contributions between NDBI and NTL, BSC, or HBR changed direction across paired-variable levels; DEM–POP and NTL–PD showed conditional dependence. These findings can inform sensitive-range identification, coordinated urban-feature configuration, and spatially differentiated interventions for block-level thermal environments in subtropical cities.

Article.Title: Numerical validation of a MOSFET-based control circuit for high-power intelligent reflecting surfaces for wireless power transfer applications
Article.Authors: Ichikawa G.; Omori E.; Nagata A.; Kumashiro A.; Kizaki K.; Saruwatari S.; Wakatsuchi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) have attracted considerable attention because of their ability to dynamically control electromagnetic wave propagation. While most existing IRSs have been developed for low-power communication and sensing applications, their extension to high-power wireless power transfer (WPT) environments remains largely unexplored, as the high induced currents can damage or saturate the sensitive control elements, disrupting their tuning functionality. Here, we propose a metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor-based (MOSFET-based) binary control circuit for IRSs operating at 2.4 GHz that can withstand input power levels of up to 1.250 W per unit cell (0.965–1.250 W depending on the design variant). The control circuit employs a back-to-back MOSFET switching topology with series and parallel capacitors to suppress impedance variations arising from device nonlinearity while maintaining a reflection phase difference of approximately 180 degrees between the ON and OFF states. A theoretical model based on transmission lines is developed and benchmarked against unit-cell full-wave/circuit co-simulations incorporating nonlinear SPICE device models. The dynamic range is evaluated with respect to both the rated current and the reflection phase difference, demonstrating stable operation up to 1.250 W for the best-case design. Supercell-level beam steering is further demonstrated through far-field simulations at six power levels spanning the entire dynamic range, confirming active control of the reflection angle via switching pattern reconfiguration. Although the present study is entirely numerical and experimental validation—including layout parasitics, biasing, and thermal management—remains as future work, these results provide a topology-level design foundation for extending IRSs to high-power WPT scenarios.

Article.Authors: Shukla J.; Singh R.; Maniraguha F.
Article.Abstract: The development of broadband dispersion systems for disc-loaded waveguides presents an essential requirement for high-power vacuum electronic systems and accelerator systems, yet current methods depend on precise tuning of specific geometric features. The calculation, truncation convergence and full-wave validation are demonstrated for both the operating TE 01 mode and the competing higher-order TE 02 mode, with modal-matching/CST agreement better than 1% across the entire passband. The design space of normalized geometric elements shows organized bandwidth distribution patterns which exist because of parametric domains that provide coherent control, not because of individual design settings. The combination of quantitative dispersion flatness metrics with statistical sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the system maintains its structural integrity when faced with geometric changes. Variance-based Sobol indices, reported with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, identify normalized periodicity as the dominant parameter (total-effect index 0.68 for bandwidth and 0.81 for curvature), while Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification shows that the optimized design retains 95% confidence-interval half-widths below 1.0% across the dispersion band under ± 2% fabrication tolerances; the distinction between output uncertainty (confidence-interval width) and parameter sensitivity (Sobol indices) is explicitly established. Finally, the transverse interaction impedance \({K}_{c}\) is evaluated from the modal fields and shown to remain within ± 8% of its 45 Ω mean value across the 58% passband of the optimized design, compared with ± 25% ripple in non-optimized designs, providing a direct quantitative bridge from the passive dispersion maps to gyro-TWT gain performance. The proposed framework enables engineers to predict and transfer the broadband optimization method to different periodic electromagnetic waveguide structures.
