Article.Title: Estimation of hydrate saturation through a joint elastic-electrical method
Article.Authors: Zhao R.; Wu M.; Zhang X.; Yuan H.
Article.Abstract: Natural gas hydrates are promising clean energy, yet accurate characterization of hydrate‑bearing sediments (HBS) is hindered by diverse hydrate morphologies and non‑uniqueness of single‑physics inversions. Conventional rock‑physics models separate elastic and electrical responses or assume ideal single‑mode hydrate occurrence, failing to reproduce microstructural evolution and physicochemical interactions in natural reservoirs. This work constructs a coupled elastic‑electrical rock‑physics framework for unconsolidated marine HBS. The Iso‑Frame model decomposes hydrate into cementing and pore‑filling fractions controlled by microstructural parameters f1 and f2 for elastic simulation. For electrical modeling, a saturation‑permeability‑resistivity workflow considering ion‑exclusion effects is established, yielding non-Archie-like electrical responses. Parameters f1 and f2 couple elastic stiffness and electrical current‑path descriptions via a joint objective function. Forward modeling identifies non‑monotonic resistivity variation against hydrate saturation. Joint inversion narrows ambiguous solution spaces of single‑physics methods. Validated by laboratory and logging datasets from Shenhu area Sites W11 and W17, this framework outperforms independent Vp and resistivity inversions, reducing cumulative absolute saturation errors by up to 62% and mitigating interpretation non‑uniqueness. This method unifies shared microstructural parameters across elastic and electrical physical fields and provides a robust, microstructure-constrained rock physical evaluation for complex marine hydrate reservoirs.

Article.Title: LeViT–ResNet hybrid AI model for transferable early detection and classification of liver cancer
Article.Authors: Deepa B.; Marimuthu C.
Article.Abstract: Accurate staging and classification of liver fibrosis from ultrasound images remains a complex challenge due to low contrast, noise artifacts, and heterogeneous tissue patterns. The staging of liver fibrosis is the main focus of this study. Ultrasound images are categorized into stages of fibrosis severity, and segmentation is only utilized to isolate liver regions related to fibrosis, not to identify or categorize tumors. This paper presents a novel, transferable AI framework that combines a Savitzky-Golay refinement filter, an Adaptive Seed Region Growing (ASRG) segmentation algorithm, and a hybrid LeViT–ResNet-based classifier. The feature extraction phase leverages contour-based shape descriptors to represent morphological complexity, while the classifier architecture integrates local (CNN-based) and global (Vision Transformer-based) cues using Residual Vision Transformer (ResViT) blocks. To fine-tune hyperparameters, the Sunflower Optimization Algorithm (SFO) is applied, ensuring robust convergence and optimal learning dynamics. Evaluation on a publicly available liver ultrasound dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models such as MultiPatch-ViTNet and MultiPatch-ViT-artificial neural network (ANN) in terms of accuracy, AUC, F1-Score, and class-wise discrimination, particularly for intermediate fibrosis stages. These results confirm the model’s potential for real-world deployment in non-invasive liver disease screening and diagnosis.

Article.Title: Deep learning for earthquake magnitude prediction using temporal fusion transformers
Article.Authors: Lodhi M.; Mahmood S.; Alsahfi T.; Almutawa A.; Ghanem S.; Eisa M.; Aboulola O.; Daud A.
Article.Abstract: Earthquakes cause severe casualties and economic losses worldwide, yet deterministic prediction of individual seismic events remains unfeasible. Consequently, modern seismology emphasizes probabilistic forecasting to quantify seismic hazard and uncertainty. While transformer architectures excel in complex time series modeling, their systematic application to natural tectonic earthquake magnitude forecasting remains limited. Here, we develop an enhanced Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) framework optimized via a quantile loss function to generate calibrated probabilistic forecasts of the next earthquake magnitude in a global catalog using historical seismicity, engineered temporal features, and spatial clustering. We also evaluate whether augmenting a small seismic catalog using a physically constrained Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) improves generalization on chronologically future events. Evaluated on held out real earthquakes using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and average quantile loss, our TFT model achieves a typical prediction error statistically comparable to the strongest recurrent attention baseline and significantly lower than a graph based baseline, while uniquely providing well calibrated 80% prediction intervals covering 85.0% of future events. Furthermore, our causal ablation demonstrates that synthetic TVAE augmentation does not improve forecast accuracy on unseen real events, establishing important practical boundaries for generative resampling in statistical seismology.

Article.Title: Habitat filtering and species-specific spillover of forest gastropods across forest-open fen boundaries
Article.Authors: Svobodová K.; Coufal R.; Horsáková V.; Horsák M.
Article.Abstract: Forest–open fen transitions represent sharp ecological boundaries for soil-dwelling fauna, but the extent to which forest species cross them depends on dispersal capacity, source habitat proximity, and environmental conditions. We examined forest gastropod occurrence along a forest–fen gradient to assess whether their presence in treeless calcareous fens is determined primarily by forest proximity or local habitat conditions. We integrated site-scale analysis of forest–fen transects in 17 Western Carpathian spring fens with a continental-scale analysis of 500 European calcareous fens. At the site-scale forest gastropod occurrence declined from forests towards open fens, peaking within fens at the fen-meadow margins with the deepest water table. Across European fens, higher water pH was consistently associated with greater abundance of forest species, whereas higher moisture levels had negative effects, indicating that a high water table acts as a strong environmental filter. Conversely, the influence of forest proximity was weaker and species-specific, showing a significant positive effect for only four out of 12 tested species. Spillover into open fens is constrained by species-specific responses to local environmental conditions rather than forest proximity alone. These findings highlight the importance of local habitat filtering in shaping cross-boundary occurrence of soil-dwelling fauna. In addition, they provide a framework for interpreting forest gastropod occurrences in Holocene tufa assemblages.

Article.Title: Resource-aware QAOA for autoclave batch scheduling in composite manufacturing using QUBO decomposition and parameter transfer
Article.Authors: Otaru A.; Barah O.; Bori I.; Zaid Z.; AlMuhaysh K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial quantum computing requires problem decompositions that respect near-term resource limits while preserving operational value. This study presents a hybrid classical-quantum workflow for autoclave batch scheduling in composite manufacturing, in which release-time and cure-family logic remain in a classical orchestration layer and each batch-selection decision is encoded as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem. Candidate pools of 4–10 jobs produce 8–14 logical-qubit QAOA subproblems after capacity-slack encoding. Depth-1 and depth-2 QAOA were evaluated using noiseless statevector simulation, with depth-2 parameters trained on four instances per problem size and transferred without re-optimization to six held-out instances per size. For transferred depth-2 QAOA, decoded feasible probability mass decreased from 0.956 at 8 qubits to 0.427 at 14 qubits, while optimal-subset probability decreased from 0.05283 to 0.00150. Comparison with an exact uniform-sampling null showed no consistent optimal-subset concentration advantage for transferred $$\text{p}=2$$ QAOA, despite exact best-of-4096 recovery across the held-out instances. The estimated sampling budget for a 95% probability of observing the optimum increased from approximately 55 to 2000 shots. In 15 end-to-end synthetic production scenarios containing 24–48 jobs, no statistically significant differences were detected between transferred QAOA and exact per-batch selection or simulated annealing for any reported schedule metric. Relative to greedy selection, transferred QAOA increased mean autoclave utilization by 2.70% points, corresponding to a 3.3% relative increase. This was the only nominally significant paired difference against greedy selection (unadjusted Wilcoxon $$\:p=0.029$$ ); other schedule metrics improved directionally but were not statistically significant. All results were obtained using noiseless statevector simulation and establish neither quantum advantage nor hardware-level speedup, but rather a testable quantum-classical integration pathway defined by decomposition, parameter reuse, sampling burden, and classical fallback.

Article.Title: Wavelet guided frequency-domain augmentation for robust time series forecasting
Article.Authors: Hasan M.; Huang X.; Li F.; Koch P.; Maass M.; Zhang Y.; Grzegorzek M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Time Series Forecasting (TSF) is essential across diverse domains, including finance, supply chain management, environmental monitoring, and healthcare, where reliable predictions support critical decision making. Despite recent progress in Deep Learning (DL) based forecasting, limited data availability and distributional variability often hinder model generalization. Data augmentation has emerged as an effective strategy to mitigate these challenges by increasing data diversity. Existing augmentation methods, such as frequency domain and wavelet based transformations, have shown effectiveness to some extent but struggle to maintain temporal coherence and consistency across varying prediction horizons. To address these limitations, this study proposes Wavelet-guided Frequency-based (WaveFreqAug), a novel hybrid augmentation method that integrates wavelet decomposition with adaptive frequency domain enhancement. The method operates on residual components to enrich spectral variability while preserving long-term temporal structures. Comprehensive experiments conducted on four benchmark datasets (ETTh1, ETTh2, ILI, and Weather) using six forecasting models demonstrate that WaveFreqAug outperforms both the unaugmented baseline, in which the same forecasting model is trained on the original data without any augmentation, and six State-of-the-Art (SOTA) augmentation methods applied to the same data, in the large majority of short- and long-term forecasting settings. These results highlight the robustness and generalizability of the proposed approach for improving deep learning based TSF.

Article.Title: Co-alignment and direct georeferencing can reduce ground-control effort in unoccupied aerial system monitoring of active rock glaciers
Article.Authors: Seier G.; Kaufmann V.; Wecht M.; Lappi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Monitoring rock-glacier velocity is important for understanding permafrost dynamics and associated impacts, but complex alpine terrain can limit dense ground control and repeated terrestrial surveys. We used unoccupied aerial system (UAS) mapping (2019–2022) at a rock glacier in the Austrian Alps to examine two georeferencing substitutions affecting mapping quality and horizontal displacement estimates. Nadir imagery from three UAS platforms was processed using structure-from-motion photogrammetry. Paired comparisons using identical imagery assessed integrated versus post-processed-kinematics-based direct georeferencing in 2020 and ground-control-based indirect georeferencing versus image-based co-alignment in 2021. Mapping quality was evaluated using bundle-adjustment residuals, independently surveyed check points where available, theoretical precision estimates, and stable-terrain discrepancies. Relative horizontal differences between alternative products were 0.06 ± 0.02 m in 2020 and 0.14 ± 0.05 m in 2021, compared with mean annual surface displacement of 1.8–2.4 m and maxima of ~ 4–6 m. Vertical discrepancies were larger and spatially structured, particularly near model margins. Under the tested conditions, direct georeferencing and reference-epoch co-alignment produced similar horizontal displacement estimates to their respective ground-control-supported alternatives. These approaches can reduce repeated ground-control and terrestrial-survey effort for highly active rock glaciers, provided that a robust reference model, stable surrounding terrain, suitable imaging conditions, and periodic independent validation are available.

Article.Title: Association of hypoglycemic agents with the risk of immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis in patients with type 2 diabetes
Article.Authors: Kobayashi Y.; Horii T.; Kubo Y.; Ando W.; Mihara K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are effective cancer therapies but can cause immune-related adverse events, including ICI-related pneumonitis (ICI-P), a potentially fatal complication. Whether baseline glucose-lowering therapy is associated with subsequent ICI-P in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a large-scale Japanese claims database (DeSC) from April 2014 to October 2023. Patients with T2D who were newly initiated on ICI-based chemotherapy were included, and glucose-lowering medication use was defined at ICI initiation. Associations with subsequent ICI-P were estimated using multivariable logistic regression. ICI-P was identified using International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision codes recorded after chest imaging; a sensitivity analysis used ICI-P requiring hospitalization. Among 21,738 eligible patients, 1,164 (5.4%) developed ICI-P. No glucose-lowering medication class used at ICI initiation was significantly associated with ICI-P in the primary analysis; for DPP-4 inhibitors, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) was 0.89 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75–1.05). Concomitant ICI use was associated with higher odds of ICI-P (OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.10–1.77), whereas older age was associated with lower odds (OR per 10 years, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.75–0.90). In the hospitalization-based sensitivity analysis, thiazolidinediones, SGLT2 inhibitors, glinides, and insulin were associated with higher odds of the outcome; these findings should be interpreted cautiously because this analysis included fewer events and multiple medication-class estimates. In this large real-world cohort, baseline use of glucose-lowering medications was not clearly associated with subsequent ICI-P in the primary analysis. These findings do not support a clear protective association between baseline glucose-lowering therapy and ICI-P and should be interpreted in light of residual confounding and outcome misclassification.

Article.Title: Gut microbiota and predicted estrobolome-related changes following multi-strain probiotic supplementation in primary dysmenorrhea
Article.Authors: Kiraman S.; Zakaria I.; Esther L.; Norfuad F.; Ghani N.; Ahmad H.
Article.Abstract: Exact cause of primary dysmenorrhoea is unknown but recent evidence uncovers a potential link between gut dysbiosis and benign gynaecological disorder via disruption of estrobolome. A randomized controlled trial to investigate the effects of multi-strain oral probiotics HEXBIO MCP BCMC on primary dysmenorrhoea has been conducted. This is a secondary analysis comparing the stool microbiome in women with primary dysmenorrhoea and those without (control), and the effects of treatment with probiotics versus placebo. Although microbial richness and evenness were comparable between groups (alpha diversity, p > 0.05), gut microbial community composition differed significantly (Bray–Curtis PERMANOVA, p = 0.015), characterised by reduced Bifidobacterium adolescentis and Blautia and enrichment of Faecalibacterium in dysmenorrhoea, alongside condition-specific core taxa. Post-intervention analysis revealed significant shifts in microbial community structure between pre- and post-treatment groups (PERMANOVA, F = 1.5768, R² = 0.11071, p = 0.022), with probiotic supplementation inducing more consistent and directed microbiome changes than placebo, without altering alpha diversity ( p > 0.05). Functional prediction showed no significant difference in overall β-glucuronidase pathway abundance ( p > 0.05). This discovery provides distinct gut microbiome patterns and predicted functional changes, although further functional validation is required.

Article.Title: Computationally efficient multi-step predictive control of airport electric towing vehicles using neural networks
Article.Authors: Chiboub M.; Majout B.; Alqarni Z.; Mosaad M.; Rhiat M.; Hirech K.; Bossoufi B.
Article.Abstract: The transition to low-carbon sustainability in airport operations requires the deployment of high-performance, safe electric tow tractors. In this study, an improved predictive control method for electric towing vehicles (ETV) based on multi-step finite control set model predictive control (MS-FCS-MPC) with neural network (NN) accelerated cost function approximation is presented. The ETV powertrain examined models of a MULAG Comet 4E tow tractor, integrating a battery-powered induction-motor drive, a power converter, and a fixed mechanical transmission, while considering longitudinal vehicle dynamics. To address the concurrent objectives of ETV, accurate speed tracking, torque control, and effective battery operation and protection under high fluctuating tow loads, a multi-step prediction horizon is developed. A broader horizon avoids shortsighted control operations and energy inefficiency; however, it significantly increases real-time computational complexity due to the combinatorial explosion of switching states. To mitigate this issue, an offline-trained NN is included in the predictive control loop to estimate the cost function. This avoids exhaustive analytical cost evaluation in the online control loop while retaining the multi-step predictive formulation and providing a measured reduction in real-time decision latency. The fallback mechanism recalculates the predicted cost of the control signal vector analytically when significant deviations occur, thereby providing the system with high robustness. The proposed framework is assessed in two challenging test cases: a step-speed transient response test and a realistic airport towing mission based on the Aero driving cycle with dynamic speed fluctuations, regenerative braking, and varying slopes. Extensive numerical simulations in MATLAB/Simulink, followed by real-time controller (RTC) hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing using a dSPACE DS1104 controller, highlight the efficacy of the proposed framework The results demonstrate a measured reduction in real-time decision latency from 49.8 µs to 42.5 µs, corresponding to approximately 14.66%, while maintaining the evaluated tracking and energy-performance characteristics. Therefore, this strategy ensures safe, energy-efficient, and fast operation for airport operations.

Article.Title: A threshold effect in the association between physical activity in late pregnancy and neonatal birth weight: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Ren S.; You X.; Zhao Q.; Jiang L.; Jin A.
Article.Abstract: This study prospectively analyzed the relationship between physical activity during pregnancy and neonatal birth weight in 337 singleton pregnant women in Shenzhen, China. The participants were enrolled from May to October 2023 at Shenzhen Second People’s Hospital, where they received routine prenatal and delivery services. Physical activity during pregnancy was assessed using the Pregnancy Physical Activity Questionnaire (PPAQ) at three time points: T1 at 14–27 gestational weeks, T2 at 28 weeks + 6 days to 32 weeks, and T3 from 33 weeks to delivery.After adjusting for confounding factors using generalized additive models (GAM) and smooth curve fitting, After adjustment for potential confounders, generalized additive modeling and two-piecewise linear regression identified a threshold effect in the association between physical activity at T2 and neonatal birth weight, with an inflection point at 218.22 MET-h·wk⁻¹. Below the inflection point, physical activity was not significantly associated with birth weight. Above the inflection point, each standard deviation increase in physical activity was associated with a 544.04-g increase in birth weight (β: 544.04, 95% CI: 184.77 to 903.32, P = 0.0032). These findings indicate a threshold effect in the association between physical activity in late pregnancy and neonatal birth weight and require validation in larger independent cohorts.

Article.Title: Endoscopic ultrasound image-based nomogram combining radiomics, deep learning, and clinical features for differentiating gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors from leiomyomas
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Dong Q.; Mo S.; Li Q.; Wang J.; Li L.; Liu X.; Lin C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurately differentiating between gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and leiomyomas before surgery holds great importance due to their divergent malignant potential; however, conventional endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) has inherent limitations, especially for lesions under 2 cm. In this retrospective study involving 408 patients (198 GISTs and 210 leiomyomas) with gastric submucosal tumors (< 2 cm), a novel deep learning-radiomics (DLR) signature was developed via feature-level early fusion, concatenating compressed deep features from a pre-trained MobileNet_v2 with handcrafted radiomics features, followed by joint feature selection. This DLR signature was integrated with independently identified clinical factors to construct a combined nomogram. The proposed combined nomogram exhibited better diagnostic performance, and the test AUC was 0.901 (95% CI 0.846–0.956), while accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were 0.846, 0.833, and 0.857, respectively, significantly outperforming the standalone radiomics (AUC = 0.822), deep transfer learning (DTL; AUC = 0.820), DLR (AUC = 0.860), and clinical (AUC = 0.724) signatures (DeLong test; all p < 0.05). The model showed excellent calibration and the greatest net clinical benefit among various threshold probabilities on decision curve analysis. This multimodal AI-driven nomogram provides a non-invasive tool for accurately differentiating gastric GISTs from leiomyomas in lesions smaller than 2 cm, with the ability to guide personalized management and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.

Article.Title: Risk of thrombosis associated with oral contraceptive pills use in Japan: a target trial emulation study
Article.Authors: Takeshita S.; Nishioka Y.; Morita E.; Myojin T.; Noda T.; Sugiyama T.; Imamura T.
Article.Abstract: The thrombosis risk associated with the latest oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) is unclear. Additionally, few studies have assessed thrombosis risk in Asian OCP users, despite wide variations in thrombosis incidence across ethnic groups. We emulated a target trial using DeSC database, an administrative claims database including monthly claims from medical institutions and pharmacies, health checkups data, and registry information in Japan from April 2014 to January 2023. Women who met both the inclusion and exclusion criteria and were not classified as OCP users served as controls. The participants were followed for one year. 59 thrombotic events (OCP group: 40; control: 19) occurred during the follow-up. The rate ratio (RR) of thrombosis among OCP users compared with control was 2.1 (95% confidence interval, 1.5–2.8). The RR among women using OCPs with 50 μg of ethinyl estradiol (EE) was 2.4 (1.5–3.3), and that among those using OCPs with EE < 50 μg was 1.8 (0.8–2.7). For users of 20 μg of EE, the RR was 1.0 (0–2.0) for norethisterone and 2.3 (0.6–4.1) for drospirenone in the three-year extended follow-up period. Our findings suggest a dose-dependent association between estrogen dose in OCPs and thrombosis onset, with a potentially higher risk for OCPs containing drospirenone in Japan. The thrombosis risk was generally higher among OCP users, both in the one-year and the three-year analyses.

Article.Title: Social network security risks and engineering systems based on artificial intelligence
Article.Authors: Kang D.; Qing L.; He C.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: In the research of artificial intelligence (AI) for social network security, in response to the difficulties in engineering implementation caused by the disconnection between models and systems and the lack of standards for risk assessment, this paper constructs a risk assessment framework and a modular scalable engineering system that integrates multidimensional standard indicators. The system decomposes social network security risks into four categories: data poisoning, model theft, adversarial attacks, and privacy breaches, formulated as a four-dimensional multi-label risk state whose dimensions are anchored to distinct security properties of the AI lifecycle, and maps them to quantifiable sub indicators through explicit functional mapping, with cross-dimension co-occurrence retained in the annotation and measured empirically. This article designs a streaming processing pipeline consisting of data access, feature extraction, risk inference, and response generation, and implements micro-batch event stream processing through Kafka. It integrates a federated learning mechanism based on Secure Aggregation, supports local model training and encryption parameter aggregation, and introduces a bias triggering strategy to reduce communication overhead, and composes a Gaussian perturbation step with the masked aggregation so that the released aggregate carries an explicit Rényi differential privacy bound. This article develops an automated response orchestration engine that interfaces with the platform’s security control plane and routes irreversible disposal actions to human operators under a versioned, reversible audit log. The experimental results demonstrate that in typical social platform scenarios, the proposed system attains accuracy with a mean of 0.91 to 0.94 and F1 score with a mean of 0.89 to 0.92, reflecting consistent cross scenario risk identification performance. Under a sustained input load of 20,000 events per second, the 99th percentile of the end-to-end latency measured from event ingestion to response acknowledgement is 310 ms and the sustainable throughput is 28,500 events per second. Under no privacy conditions, the success rate of member inference attacks is 18.2%, with an accuracy decrease of no more than 2.3%, indicating good model utility retention ability. The source code, the experiment configuration files, and a synthetic data generator reproducing the anonymized event schema are released at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22272217 .

Article.Title: High-resolution assessment and attribution of vegetation net primary productivity dynamics under changing socio-ecological conditions in the Zhengzhou Metropolitan Area, China
Article.Authors: Mu W.; Hu Q.; Lv J.; Ma W.; Zhu X.; Huang H.; Huang X.; Wan F.; Han Y.; Cao W.
Article.Abstract: Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) provides a measure of ecosystem carbon assimilation and vegetation responses to environmental changes. The relative roles of climatic variability and anthropogenic effects in regulating NPP dynamics remain unclear in rapidly urbanizing landscapes. This study investigated NPP dynamics and their drivers in the Zhengzhou Metropolitan Area (ZMA), China, during 2000–2020 using a 30-m resolution NPP dataset generated by integrating Landsat-MODIS spatiotemporal fusion and the CASA model. A scenario-based attribution framework was applied to quantify the relative contributions of climatic variability and anthropogenic effects across different socio-ecological phases. NPP showed a significant increasing trend during 2000–2020, whereas the periods before and after the early-2010s transition exhibited a weak negative tendency and a positive tendency, respectively, neither of which was statistically significant at the regional scale. Vegetation degradation was concentrated in urban expansion and agricultural areas, while recovery was mainly distributed across mountainous ecosystems, ecological corridors, and urban green spaces. Anthropogenic effects represented the largest relative contribution of NPP changes, increasing from 54.20% in Phase I to 61.63% in Phase II. Climatic variability remained a contributor, although its relative contribution decreased after 2010. These findings indicate that vegetation responses to urbanization depend strongly on development stages and ecological management strategies, highlighting the importance of integrating urban development with ecological restoration and adaptive land management.

Article.Title: Accelerated adjustable predefined‑time nonsingular sliding mode control for nonlinear systems
Article.Authors: Riaz S.; Saleem N.; Wu W.; Azhar A.; Daqqa I.
Article.Abstract: In this work, we have proposed a new accelerated adjustable predefined‑time (PDT) nonsingular sliding mode control approach for nonlinear systems (NLS). Based on the concept of adjustable predefined‑time stability (PTS), we have first established an accelerated inequality condition and given a complete theoretical proof to ensure the desired temporal convergence. This adjustable PTS accelerated lemma is then seamlessly integrated into a new accelerated sliding mode control architecture. Our approach ensures that the nonlinear system states exhibit accelerated predefined‑time convergence across both the reaching and sliding stages. The resulting controller not only preserves strong robustness against disturbances but also provides an explicit upper bound on the settling time that is independent of the initial conditions and is fixed solely by the user-specified time constants, while permitting the actual convergence time (CT) to be adjusted according to application requirements. In addition, the singularity associated with the derivative of the fractional-power sliding variable is avoided through a narrow boundary layer, which keeps the control effort bounded. The practicality and efficacy of the proposed technique are confirmed through rigorous simulation results on small and large NLS systems.

Article.Title: Incomplete nodal verification limits risk estimation for intermediate size rectal neuroendocrine tumors in SEER
Article.Authors: Meng G.; Xu H.; Cao D.
Article.Abstract: Management of 10–20 mm rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) remains uncertain. Registry analyses are vulnerable to verification bias because regional nodal status is selectively observed, particularly after local excision. We quantified the nodal-verification deficit and the resulting limits on nodal-risk inference in SEER. We analyzed adults with pathologically confirmed, non-distant, 10–20 mm rectal NETs in SEER 17 registries diagnosed during 2004–2023 who underwent strict local excision or radical resection. Surgery codes were harmonized across the 2023 coding transition. Node-evaluable status included exact examined-node counts and SEER special codes documenting aspiration, sampling, dissection, or node removal. The primary analysis reported verification rates, an NX = N0 lower estimate, complete-case estimates, Manski-type bounds, and illustrative fixed-risk scenarios. Descriptive survival analyses were restricted to 2004–2021. The primary cohort included 1,157 patients, of whom 1,008 underwent local excision and 149 radical resection. Ninety-four patients (8.1%) were node-evaluable: 13/1,008 (1.3%) after local excision and 81/149 (54.4%) after radical resection. Pathologically verified nodal positivity was present in 62 patients. Treating all unverified patients as N0 yielded a lower estimate of 5.4%, whereas the complete-case estimate was 62/94 (66.0%; 95% CI 55.9–74.7%). The conservative partial-identification interval was 5.4%-97.2%. Under purely illustrative assumptions that 5%, 7.5%, or 10% of unverified patients were node-positive, overall scenario prevalences were 10.0%, 12.2%, and 14.5%, respectively. The 2004–2021 survival cohort included 1,006 patients and 39 rectal NET-specific deaths. SEER empirically demonstrates a profound nodal-verification deficit after local excision. The lower bound obtained by coding NX as N0 and the high complete-case estimate answer different, highly selected questions and neither identifies population nodal risk. The principal contribution of this analysis is a quantified, citable demonstration of this structural limitation rather than a corrected surgical threshold.

Article.Title: Cell-bound biosurfactants from Limosilactobacillus fermentum ES49 and Lactobacillus johnsonii C101 show surface activity and antibiofilm properties
Article.Authors: Aragón A.; Jurado R.; Hernando N.; Jara J.; López-Montero I.; Fernández L.; Orgaz B.
Article.Abstract: Biosurfactants produced by lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are promising natural agents for controlling biofilms in food-contact surfaces. However, they remain poorly characterized. In this study, cell-free supernatants (CFS) and cell-bound fractions (CBF) obtained from 88 strains belonging to ten LAB species were screened for surface activity. Such activity was predominantly cell-associated, with CBF showing substantially greater reductions in surface tension (ST) than CFS. The most active strains, Limosilactobacillus fermentum ES49 and Lactobacillus johnsonii C101, yielded CBF with ST values of ~ 50 mN/m and exhibited critical micelle concentrations of 339 and 676 mg/L, respectively. Coating of glass surfaces with these CBF reduced biofilm formation by ~ 2 log₁₀ CFU/cm² for Listeria monocytogenes PS2 and ~ 3 log₁₀ CFU/cm² for Pseudomonas fluorescens B52, accompanied by a marked increase in damaged cell biovolume (~ 85%), as revealed by confocal laser scanning microscopy. Treatment of mature biofilms with CBF from these two LAB strains also decreased viability by ~ 1–2 log₁₀ CFU/cm² and increased the proportion of damaged cells (~ 50–70%). Chemical characterization of CBF by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry revealed complex mixtures of amphiphilic compounds enriched in long-chain (C18–C20) fatty acids, lipid amides, amino alcohols and monoacylglycerols. Overall, these findings demonstrate that LAB-derived biosurfactants combine effective interfacial activity with anti-adhesive and antibiofilm properties, providing new insights into their composition and supporting their potential as natural antibiofilm agents.

Article.Title: Autonomic maladaptation is associated with exertional dyspnoea and systemic inflammation in pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension: a hypothesis-generating pilot study
Article.Authors: Thomer J.; Wagner F.; Ratsimba S.; Reugels M.; Pradhan K.; Neupane B.; Gramlich M.; Kahles F.; Altiok E.; Marx N.; Hidalgo Pareja D.; Yousef S.; Martin C.; Michely A.; Daher A.; Aetou M.; Regmi B.; Giannoni A.; Dreher M.; Spiesshoefer J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The link between autonomic dysregulation and systemic inflammation has not been systematically investigated across pulmonary hypertension subtypes. Therefore, this hypothesis-generating pilot study investigated whether heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) at rest and during exertion are related to exertional dyspnoea, disease severity, and alterations in inflammatory cytokines in patients with pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension (PH). Patients diagnosed with pre-capillary PH (including pulmonary arterial hypertension [PAH] and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension [CTEPH]) by right heart catheterisation were recruited. Clinical disease severity was assessed, HR and HRV at rest and during inspiratory exercise were recorded, and a variety of inflammatory markers were measured using multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits. 33 patients with pre-capillary PH (age 68 years [IQR = 50–76], 22 female, body mass index [BMI] 26 kg/m 2 [IQR = 23–35]) and 16 age-, sex-, and BMI-matched healthy controls (age 62 years [IQR = 60–63], 7 female, BMI 26 kg/m 2 [IQR = 24–27]) were enrolled. All patients showed a decreased LF/HF ratio at rest and blunted HR response to exercise compared with matched controls ( P < 0.05 for PH vs. controls, P- ANOVA > 0.1 across PH subgroups). A lower LF/HF ratio was associated at the trend level with PH severity ( P -ANOVA = 0.07) and significantly with exertional dyspnoea ( P -ANOVA = 0.02). Alterations in sympathovagal balance were moderately to strongly correlated with levels of inflammatory cytokines (including tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interferon-gamma, interleukin [IL]-1 beta, IL-2, and IL-12p70). Autonomic maladaptation (and, as a hypothesis-generating sub-analysis of the present data, systemic inflammation) are key features and are related to both disease severity and exertional dyspnoea in pre-capillary PH, whether it is PAH or CTEPH. On a speculative, hence hypothesis-generating basis, this might be a potential target for therapeutic approaches. Article.Title: Machine learning classification of acute concussion using data obtained from neurological tests delivered through virtual reality
Article.Authors: Reneker J.; Gonzalez C.; Chambers D.; Pruett W.
Article.Abstract: Concussion is a traumatic brain injury with a subtle and divergent clinical presentation, which may account for why a gold standard for detection has yet to be found. This study describes the initial machine learning (ML) classification results of a project using virtual reality (VR) tests to detect concussion. Participants aged 18–40 with (cases = 29) and without (controls = 697) an acute concussion were enrolled. Self-reported and sensor-based data from the VR headset were collected. Altogether, 175 features were constructed from VR sensor-based data. Additionally, age, sex, varsity status, handedness, and year of education were used as independent features. Using two classifiers, logistic regression with an L1 penalty (LASSO) and a gradient boosting classifier (HGB), five models that vary in VR sensor, symptom, and participant characteristic features were developed. Quality metrics include area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and balanced accuracy. The full model showed the highest discriminability with average AUC of 0.86 for LASSO (95%CI 0.66–0.98) and 0.85 for HGB (95% CI 0.67–0.97). The average balanced accuracy for this model using LASSO was 0.77 (95% CI 0.56–0.91) and was 0.69 (95% CI 0.49–0.90) for HGB.

Article.Title: Dopamine- and serotonin-related grey matter atrophy in patients with Alzheimer’s disease and psychosis
Article.Authors: Manca R.; Pardiñas A.; Venneri A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polygenic risk scores for schizophrenia (SCZ-PRS) may represent risk factors for psychotic symptoms in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Since dopamine (DA) and serotonin (5HT) have been implicated in psychosis, this study investigated grey matter volume (GMV) loss associated with atlas-derived DA and 5HT distribution in AD-related psychosis and the relationship with a SCZ-PRS. Data of 98 patients with AD and psychosis (PT-PS) and 308 without psychosis (PT-NP), all amyloid-positive, were selected from the Alzheimer’s Diseases Neuroimaging Initiative. T1-weighted MRI scans were pre-processed with JuSpace to quantify the association between regional GMV and atlas-derived DA/5HT distributions. Generalised linear models were used to test the association between a SCZ-PRS and neurotransmitter-GMV correlation coefficients. PT-PS patients had smaller GMV than PT-NP in areas where 5HT1b receptor distribution is lower and D2 receptor and DA transporter distribution are higher. GMV alterations were primarily in medio-temporal areas, but the SCZ-PRS was not associated with GMV-neurotransmitter correlations. Although this study assessed neurotransmitter dysfunction indirectly via atlas-based estimates and findings are correlational, they offer insights complementary to previous evidence on the neurobiological underpinning of AD-related psychosis. Further investigations are needed to replicate these findings and to test the mechanistic involvement of neurotransmitters in AD-related psychosis.

Article.Title: Myroides odoratimimus clinical outcomes biofilm formation environmental surveillance and in vitro evaluation of novel antimicrobial agents
Article.Authors: Birgin H.; Zer Y.; Karabulut E.; Çalışkantürk G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Myroides species are emerging opportunistic Gram-negative pathogens increasingly associated with healthcare-associated infections and poor clinical outcomes. This study investigated the clinical characteristics, antimicrobial resistance, biofilm formation, and in vitro activity of ceftazidime/avibactam, cefiderocol, and aztreonam–ceftazidime/avibactam against clinical M. odoratimimus isolates. A total of 44 Myroides odoratimimus isolates recovered between January 2023 and April 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Identification was performed using the BD Phoenix M50 system and MALDI-TOF MS. Antimicrobial susceptibility was evaluated using the Phoenix system and disk diffusion, with colistin MICs determined by broth disk elution. Ceftazidime/avibactam and cefiderocol were tested by disk diffusion, and the results were reported descriptively because species-specific breakpoints are unavailable. Synergistic activity between aztreonam and ceftazidime–avibactam was evaluated in all isolates using both the disk replacement method and the double-disk synergy test, and biofilm formation was evaluated using the crystal violet microplate assay. All isolates yielded MIC values above the upper limits of the testing panel and no corresponding inhibition zones for the conventional antimicrobial agents evaluated; similarly, ceftazidime/avibactam and cefiderocol produced no inhibition zones against any isolate. Neither the disk replacement method nor the double-disk synergy test demonstrated synergistic activity in any isolate. Biofilm formation was detected in 22 isolates, including strong (15.9%), moderate (15.9%), and weak (18.2%) producers. Thirty-six patients were hospitalized in intensive care units (81.8%), and 38 had at least one documented underlying disease (86.4%). All-cause in-hospital mortality was 63.6% (28/44), with deaths occurring 3–61 days after M. odoratimimus isolation. The marked lack of measurable in vitro antimicrobial activity and frequent biofilm formation underscore the potential clinical relevance of M. odoratimimus in hospitalized patients and the need for increased clinical awareness and strengthened infection control measures.

Article.Title: Balancing loss of physical function in older Adults’ everyday lives with multimorbidity
Article.Authors: Østergaard K.; Skou S.; Bricca A.; Dideriksen M.; Høgsgaard D.; Simonÿ C.
Article.Abstract: Older adults living with multimorbidity often experience progressive loss of physical function, which affects autonomy, identity, and everyday participation. Despite increasing attention to multimorbidity, little is known about how older adults themselves experience functional decline following hospitalisation, and how person-centred interventions may support them. This study explores these lived experiences and examines whether a personalised exercise therapy and self-management programme helped participants live more active lives. We conducted individual semi-structured interviews with 20 older adults with multimorbidity enrolled in a Danish personalised exercise and self-management intervention trial. A phenomenological-hermeneutic framework adapted from Ricoeur guided data collection and analysis. Interpretation followed three analytic levels: naïve reading, structural analysis, and critical interpretation. Reporting adhered to COREQ. Four themes characterised participants’ experiences: (1) Balancing everyday life—independence and the need for help, reflected tensions between autonomy and increased reliance on relatives, often disrupting relational roles, (2) Adapting to a new everyday life—maintaining a sense of coherence, involved creative workarounds and temporal adjustments that enabled participants to maintain routines and coherence despite functional loss, (3) Uncertainties in everyday life—fear of falling, symptom unpredictability, and reduced social participation, contributing to withdrawal and insecurity, and (4) A sense of community among the MOBILIZE intervention participants - fostered motivation, belonging, and emotional support, reducing isolation and normalising functional limitations. Loss of physical function among older adults with multimorbidity seems to constitute an emotionally and existentially challenging process shaped by bodily, relational, and contextual constraints. The MOBILIZE personalised exercise and self-management intervention was experienced as supporting social connectedness, fostering agency, and helping them reorient everyday practices. Findings underscore the need for holistic, person-centred care models that integrate rehabilitation with emotional, relational, and existential dimensions of ageing with multimorbidity.

Article.Title: Variety-dependent cadmium safety thresholds for safe Pleurotus ostreatus cultivation on Cd-contaminated rice straw
Article.Authors: Qi H.; Chen L.; Deng M.; Wei D.; Liu A.; Xiao L.; Feng J.; Peng S.; Long S.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: The global threat of cadmium (Cd)-contaminated rice straw necessitates safe utilization strategies. Cd stress negatively affected mycelial growth in a dose-dependent manner. Substrate Cd safety thresholds for producing safe mushrooms were 1.282 mg/kg for 950 and 0.860 mg/kg for Zaoyou-12. Cd concentrations in the cultivation substrate ranged from 0.22 to 4.95 mg/kg, with no significant difference in fruiting morphology observed between the two P. ostreatus varieties. Zaoyou 12 exhibited greater sensitivity to cadmium stress: under high cadmium concentration (4.95 mg/kg), its biotransformation efficiency and yield decreased by 11.79% and 11.81%, respectively, compared with those under low concentration (0.22 mg/kg). In contrast, higher cadmium concentrations had no significant effect on the biotransformation efficiency or yield of P. ostreatus 950. This study provides a promising strategy for utilizing Cd-contaminated rice straw in safe edible mushroom cultivation.

Article.Title: A flexible language model-assisted electronic design automation framework
Article.Authors: Sestito C.; Kontou P.; Verma P.; Dixit A.; Keros A.; O’Boyle M.; Bouganis C.; Prodromakis T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming electronic design automation (EDA) by enhancing design stages such as schematic design, simulation, netlist synthesis, and place-and-route. Existing methods primarily focus these optimisations within isolated open-source EDA tools and often lack the flexibility to handle multiple domains, such as analogue, digital, and radio-frequency design. In contrast, modern systems require to interface with commercial EDA environments, adhere to tool-specific operation rules, and incorporate feedback from design outcomes while supporting diverse design flows. We propose a versatile framework that uses LLMs to generate files compatible with commercial EDA tools and optimise designs using power-performance-area reports. This is accomplished by guiding the LLMs with tool constraints and feedback from design outputs to meet tool requirements and user specifications. The framework is used to evaluate case studies on operational transconductance amplifiers, microstrip patch antennas, and FPGA circuits.

Article.Title: Generation of Quarter- and Hemi-embryos via blastomere isolation reduces mosaicism and reveals editing patterns in Cas9 RNP-edited bovine embryos
Article.Authors: Rahimi M.; Habermann H.; Haake L.; Albayrak E.; Brenig B.; Held-Hoelker E.; Benedetti C.; Hoelker M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mosaicism is a persistent limitation in CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing of preimplantation embryos. This study tested whether isolating blastomeres at the 2- or 4-cell stage reduces mosaicism in the resulting blastocysts and used the resulting variant patterns at the target region to analyze the duration of activity of Cas9-RNP complexes after electroporation. In vitro-produced bovine zygotes were Cas9-RNP-electroporated against the Tyrosinase (TYR) gene 10 h post insemination and individual blastomeres of cleaved embryos at the 2- or 4-cell stage were isolated to generate Hemi- and Quarter-embryos. While individual culture of embryos did not reduce blastocyst formation compared with group culture, blastocyst yield per source embryo was significantly higher in Hemi-embryos than in zona-free control (88.2 ± 29.0% vs. 51.1 ± 08.1%), whereas the blastocyst yield per source embryo of Quarter-embryos (68.2 ± 28.8%) did not differ significantly from any of the other four treatment groups. While editing efficiency was not affected by zona removal and splitting, mosaicism, however, was significantly reduced in Quarter- and Hemi-embryos versus intact embryos (21.4 ± 10.8% vs. 29.3 ± 31.2% vs. 59.8 ± 32.9%), respectively. Editing event evaluation demonstrated that approximately 66% of presumptive monoallelic edits, if these had been identified in the unsplit embryo, were actually mosaic. Finally, maximum allelic variant counts at the target region were consistent with Cas9-RNP activity persisting at least through S phase associated with the second cleavage division (corresponding approximately to the 4-cell stage) and becoming progressively restricted thereafter. These allelic patterns provide an indirect estimate of the temporal window of detectable Cas9-RNP activity during early embryonic cleavage. In conclusion, the results of the present study infer the temporal window of Cas9 activity during early embryo cleavages. Altogether, blastomere isolation markedly reduced rates of mosaicism offering attractive implications for optimizing genome-editing strategies in livestock breeding.

Article.Title: Glycolytic inhibitor 2-Deoxy-D-glucose protects against diabetes development in type 1 diabetes models
Article.Authors: Maruyama N.; Hayashi M.; Nishikawa M.; Kitada A.; Minamide C.; Yasuda H.
Article.Abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an organ-specific autoimmune disease caused by T cell-mediated pancreatic β-cell destruction. To evaluate the effects of 2-Deoxy-D-Glucose (2DG), a glycolytic inhibitor, on immune cells in autoimmune diabetes, 2DG was orally administered to two T1D mouse models. In a cyclophosphamide-induced T1D model in male non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice, oral 2DG treatment significantly suppressed autoimmune insulitis and diabetes. 2DG treatment showed a significant decrease in the frequencies of CD44 hi CD4 + T cells and CD11b + macrophages, and PD-1 expression level on B cells. Conversely, 2DG-treated mice showed a significant increase in the frequencies of Foxp3 + CD4 + regulatory T cells (Tregs) and PD-L1 + CD11b + macrophages. In addition, Integrin β7 expression level on CD8 + T cells was significantly reduced in 2DG-treated mice. Next, in female NOD mice, a spontaneous T1D model, oral 2DG treatment significantly suppressed autoimmune diabetes progression with a reduction of insulitis. The frequencies of CD11b + macrophages and CD11c + dendritic cells were significantly reduced in 2DG-treated mice. Notably, 2DG treatment significantly increased the frequency of Foxp3 + CD4 + Tregs in both splenocytes and PLN cells. These results suggest that 2DG may suppress autoimmunity and have therapeutic potential in T1D progression by affecting immune cells. In addition, reduced glucose uptake was demonstrated only in B cells, suggesting that metabolic regulation in B cells may contribute to the protective effects of 2DG.

Article.Title: Effects of local thermal non-equilibrium on parameter estimation from thermal single-well push-pull tests in fracture-matrix systems
Article.Authors: Zhang F.; Yu S.; Zhang Z.; Zhou D.; Tang M.; Hu H.; Ma C.; Wang Q.; Zhang T.; Wang S.; Luo X.; Tang H.
Article.Abstract: Thermal single-well push-pull (SWPP) tests are widely used to estimate parameters governing subsurface heat transport. However, most existing SWPP models rely on the local thermal equilibrium (LTE) assumption, which neglects temperature differences between the fluid and solid phases during heat transport. Here we develop a new thermal SWPP model for fracture-matrix systems that explicitly incorporates local thermal non-equilibrium (LTNE), wellbore fluid mixing and fracture-matrix heat exchange. Simulations show that the temperature difference between the fluid and solid phases increases as LTNE effects become stronger. This difference is positive during injection and early extraction, but becomes negative during the chasing phase and late extraction. When LTNE effects are strong, ignoring LTNE leads to a robust overestimation of thermal dispersivity during parameter estimation, whereas the porosity estimate is biased with an indefinite sign owing to the strong compensation between thermal dispersivity and porosity. In contrast, thermal breakthrough curves in the wellbore during injection and chasing are only weakly affected by LTNE. When fracture-matrix heat exchange is described using Newton’s law of cooling, increasing the heat transfer coefficient reduces the peak of the thermal breakthrough curve during extraction. In addition, once formulated consistently with the depth-averaged model, the classical averaged volumetric sink/source term corresponds to the perfect-contact limit of fracture-matrix heat exchange and therefore gives its upper bound, whereas the Newton’s-law-of-cooling formulation with a finite heat transfer coefficient yields weaker exchange. These results show that LTNE and fracture-matrix heat exchange should be explicitly considered to improve the physical realism and reliability of thermal SWPP interpretation in fracture-matrix geothermal systems. The model is verified against a semi-analytical solution and benchmarked against COMSOL Multiphysics under true LTNE conditions. The proposed model targets fractures filled with coarse sediments or breccia, such as fault zones, karstified channels and gravel-packed intervals; for typical EGS microfractures with millimeter-scale apertures and fine fillings, the LTNE effect is negligible and the LTE assumption is adequate.

Article.Title: Integrated transcriptomic identification of candidate genes associated with hypoxia- and lactylation-related transcriptional signatures in rheumatoid arthritis
Article.Authors: Duan J.; Liang R.; Zhang G.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease characterized by immune dysregulation. Both hypoxia and lactylation have been implicated in immunity and inflammation, but their underlying mechanisms in RA remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers associated with hypoxia- and lactylation-related features in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) through bioinformatic analyses and assessment of tissue protein expression. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in blood and synovial tissue samples. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was used to identify module genes associated with hypoxia and lactylation. Candidate genes (CGs) were identified from the intersection of DEGs and module genes. Machine learning algorithms and expression analysis were applied to screen candidate biomarkers. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was performed to explore pathways related to the candidate biomarkers. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to explore the expression of the candidate biomarkers across different cell populations in one peripheral-blood sample from a patient with RA. Finally, immunohistochemical staining was performed on synovial tissue to assess the protein expression levels of the identified candidate biomarkers. TIMM8B and ABLIM1 were identified as candidate biomarkers that shared pathways related to cell homeostasis and immunity, including oxidative phosphorylation and the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway. In this RA peripheral-blood sample, ABLIM1 was mainly detected in CD8 + T cells, whereas TIMM8B showed relatively high expression in plasma cells. Immunohistochemical results showed significantly increased TIMM8B protein in RA synovial tissue, and ABLIM1 protein also showed a relatively strong positive signal. This study identified candidate biomarkers associated with hypoxia- and lactylation-related transcriptional features in RA and suggested that they might be associated with RA-related immune dysregulation. These findings provide new clues for understanding RA-related molecular and immune features and a basis for subsequent mechanistic research and candidate-target evaluation.

Article.Title: Applying the urban transportation systems abstraction hierarchy as a tool for risk assessment
Article.Authors: Ashtiany M.; Harandi V.; Komendantova N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban transportation networks are highly vulnerable to earthquakes. However, existing risk assessment approaches, including index-based, graph-based, and system dynamics models, have limitations in capturing the interdependencies among physical, functional, social, governance, and environmental factors. This study applies the Urban Transportation System Abstraction Hierarchy (UTSAH), a graph-based framework comprising seven interconnected subsystems organized into five hierarchical levels. A hierarchical matrix-based formulation is used to trace the effects of local damage from Level 5 parameters through Level 4 components to Level 3 subsystems and calculate a Risk Index for each study zone. The framework further identifies and prioritizes mitigation interventions through graph-based analysis of the UTSAH network, providing decision-makers with a model-grounded and reproducible basis for risk reduction planning. The framework was applied to District 4 of Qom, Iran, under three traffic-time scenarios for a 475-year return-period earthquake. Results show that implementing a dedicated emergency transportation network could reduce the modeled Risk Index by 11.4%, while enhanced construction quality control and periodic inspections yield an approximately 5% reduction. The proposed framework supports urban transportation risk management by identifying high-risk zones, diagnosing key systemic weaknesses, and comparing the potential effectiveness of alternative seismic risk-reduction interventions.

Article.Title: Humification processes of biodegradation liquid products of Hongshaquan low-rank coal based on the dynamic changes of DOM
Article.Authors: Cao B.; Nussipov D.; Liu X.; Bai L.; Tastambek K.; Akimbekov N.; Zhou A.
Article.Abstract: Hongshaquan low-rank coal was biodegraded by Aquamicrobium terrae ( A. terrae ). Dynamic changes of dissolved organic matter (DOM), whose presence dominates biodegradation liquid products, were monitored by a combined technique of excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy-parallel factor analysis (EEM-PARAFAC) and two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2D-COS). EEM-PARAFAC results showed that the DOM included tryptophan-like (C1), humic acid-like (C2), fulvic acid-like (C3), and tyrosine-like (C4). 2D-COS results showed that from 1 d to 11 d of degradation, the variations of C1 and C4 preceded the changes of C3 (C1 + C4 → C3), which was attributed to the cleavage and recombination of aliphatic C-H and the generation of highly reactive C-O. From 11 d to 15 d, C2 exhibited later changes following C1, C4, and C3, the sequential variation pattern of DOM components followed the order of C1 + C4 → C3 → C2. Gel permeation chromatography (GPC) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) results suggested that the biodegradation of low-rank coal involved three sequential processes: dissolution, utilization, and possible recombination. This study reveals the humification mechanism of biodegradation liquid products of coal, providing a theoretical basis for targeted regulation of high-value degradation products.

Article.Title: The influence of AI chatbots’ human-like and technical characteristics on users’ perceived addictiveness
Article.Authors: Yuan J.; Shi H.; Li Y.; Zhao T.
Article.Abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative AI chatbots, their human-like and technical characteristics may enhance user experience while also increasing the risks of overdependence and potential addiction. However, how these two categories of characteristics jointly shape users’ perceived addictiveness remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, this study developed a model integrating perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, emotional attachment, functional dependence, and perceived addictiveness. Data were collected from 345 Chinese AI chatbot users through an online survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use all positively influenced trust, which in turn strengthened emotional attachment and functional dependence. Both emotional attachment and functional dependence increased perceived addictiveness, with emotional attachment exerting the stronger effect. Mediation analysis further indicated that chatbot characteristics indirectly influenced perceived addictiveness through two parallel pathways: trust–emotional attachment and trust–functional dependence. These findings reveal the emotional and functional mechanisms underlying perceived AI chatbot addictiveness, extend the S–O–R framework, and provide implications for responsible design, calibrated trust, and dependence-risk governance.

Article.Title: Resting plasma irisin shows lower levels in older adults independently of muscle mass and physical activity and is not associated with cognitive performance
Article.Authors: Novotny J.; Onyango I.; Forzani E.; Geda Y.; Stokin G.
Article.Abstract: Although exercise-induced irisin has been associated with improvements in cognitive and metabolic health, the determinants and functional relevance of resting plasma irisin (RPI) remain unclear. We investigated age-related differences in RPI and its association with cognitive performance in a population-based cross-sectional sample of 186 middle-aged (mean age 42.1 years; 48% female) and 178 older adults (mean age 71.5 years; 64% female). RPI was measured by ELISA and examined in relation to body composition (muscle mass, fat mass, and basal metabolic rate), habitual physical activity, and cognitive performance. Multivariable regression analyses demonstrated a significant inverse association between chronological age and RPI (β = − 4.57 pg/mL/year; [95% CI, − 5.90, − 3.24]), independent of sex, body composition, physical activity, and basal metabolic rate. No significant sex differences in RPI concentrations were observed within either age group. RPI was not associated with any cognitive outcome in either age group, even after adjustment for body composition and physical activity. These findings indicate that RPI is lower in older compared to middle-aged adults, independently of body composition and physical activity, and is not associated with cognitive performance. The cognitive benefits attributed to irisin in exercise and animal studies may therefore not extend to resting physiological concentrations, pointing to potentially distinct biological roles for exercise-induced and resting irisin during aging.

Article.Authors: M S.; G P.; Chakravarthi V.; Jaganathan V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The kinetic chain is a series of interconnected joints and segments that operate together to stabilize the body and facilitate the efficient transfer of energy across various regions. Although its importance in movement and performance is widely recognised, there remains a lack of empirical evidence to fully comprehend the effectiveness of kinetic chain training. This study investigated the effect of kinetic chain training on movement quality and power in recreational overhead athletes. A total of 28 individuals were recruited and randomised into two groups. The intervention group received a supervised kinetic chain training program for four weeks (3 sessions/week), while the control group continued their usual sports training. Measurements of movement quality, power, shoulder rotational range of motion, and myofascial stiffness were taken at baseline and post-training. No significant Group × Time effects were observed for left ( p = 0.952) or right ( p = 0.108) shoulder external rotation. Kinetic-chain training demonstrated significant Group × Time effects for movement quality, upper-body power, and bilateral shoulder internal rotation, but not external rotation, in recreational overhead athletes. Larger adequately powered trials are required to confirm these findings. This study was approved by the Kasturba Medical College Ethics Committee (IEC1:304/2024) and registered in the Clinical Trials Registry - India (CTRI/2024/10/074552) on 01/10/2024.

Article.Title: A biomarker catalog for inflammatory bowel disease medications
Article.Authors: Hart T.; West K.; Preto A.; Domingo-Fernández D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), which includes Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), is a multifaceted illness with diverse manifestations. Current treatment strategies are inadequate, with low response rates, secondary loss of response, and serious side effects. We aim at identifying transcriptomics and proteomics putative biomarkers for (i) disease severity, (ii) association with medication status, and (iii) putative response-associated signatures. We leveraged a large multiomics dataset (SPARC IBD) to compile a catalog of biomarkers for the three aforementioned comparisons. Data were stratified by IBD subtype (UC and CD) and tissue type; biomarker associations were identified using mixed-effects models to account for multiple medication groups, disease status (e.g., remission, active), and repeated sampling. Our catalog lists thousands of potential biomarkers: 9678 for disease severity, 299 associated with medication status, and 59 putative response-associated. These putative biomarkers, both known and novel, span multiple diagnoses, tissues, and medications. These therapy-associated signatures are hypothesis-generating. Longitudinal prospective validation is required before use to track treatment response or disease severity.

Article.Authors: Safdar S.; Bakhtiar M.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic diseases are increasingly associated with gut microbiome dysbiosis; however, integrated approaches combining taxonomic profiling, ecological interpretation, statistical testing, and explainable artificial intelligence remain limited. Disease samples showed marked taxonomic shifts, reduced alpha diversity, and clear Bray–Curtis separation from Normal and Obese groups. PERMANOVA confirmed significant community-level differences across all taxonomic ranks using Bray–Curtis distances. Differential abundance analysis revealed extensive disease-associated taxa, particularly at genus and species levels, with stronger separation in Normal vs. Disease and Obese vs. Disease comparisons than in Normal vs. Obese. Random Forest models showed strong classification performance for disease-related comparisons, with high ROC-AUC values, while Normal vs. Obese showed weaker discrimination. SHAP-based explainable AI highlighted candidate species-level biomarkers, including Anaerostipes hadrus , Anaerobutyricum hallii , Dorea longicatena , Faecalibacterium prausnitzii , Phocaeicola vulgatus , and Morganella morganii . Overall, this study demonstrates that integrating 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, statistical testing, machine learning, explainable AI, and network ecology to identify exploratory gut microbial signatures and candidate microbial markers associated with MetS that require independent validation.

Article.Authors: Son B.; Chung J.
Article.Abstract: As medical privacy regulations restrict the centralized aggregation of Electronic Health Records (EHRs), Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising alternative for training predictive models across distributed clinical sites. However, clinical deployment of Machine Learning (ML) models requires not only a high predictive performance but also clinical trustworthiness, which can be supported by eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). In this paper, explainability consistency, defined as the quantitative consistency of feature importance rankings between Centralized Learning (CL) and FL models, is systematically evaluated by analyzing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) feature importances using Spearman’s Rank Correlation Coefficient (SRCC). Using three benchmark EHR datasets (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU), explainability consistency in mortality prediction is evaluated across tree-based ensembles (LightGBM and XGBoost) utilizing cyclic boosting and TabPFN teachers with distilled XGBoost students. Experimental results demonstrate explainability consistency across nine architecture-matched comparisons, with SRCC values ranging from 0.6463 to 0.8374. Federated distilled students achieve Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) values of 0.8294 (MIMIC-III), 0.8402 (MIMIC-IV) and 0.8515 (eICU), close to centralized students. These findings provide a quantitative framework for evaluating explainability consistency alongside the predictive performance when comparing centralized and federated mortality prediction models.

Article.Title: Pan-cancer analysis and exploratory clinical evaluation reveal the prognostic and immunological relevance of MUC16/CA125
Article.Authors: Lin W.; Li W.; Guo G.; Lyu H.; Chen G.; Chen H.; Huang C.; Xue F.; Tian Y.
Article.Abstract: Mucin 16 ( MUC16 ), a transmembrane mucin carrying the antigenic epitopes detected clinically in serum as CA125, has been implicated in cancer progression, but its expression landscape, prognostic significance, and immunological associations remain incompletely characterized from a pan-cancer perspective. This study integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, single-cell transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, immune infiltration, and pharmacogenomic data to characterize MUC16 across cancer types, with clinical analyses using peripheral blood test data and tumor tissue immunohistochemistry staining. Pan-cancer analyses revealed cancer-type-specific MUC16 dysregulation and heterogeneous prognostic associations, while its mutations were most frequently observed in melanoma and NSCLC. Pathway analyses revealed associations between MUC16 expression and multiple oncogenic as well as immune-related pathways. Higher MUC16 expression was preferentially detected in malignant-cell populations, with inverse associations with several immune-cell populations, including CD8⁺ T cells. Correlation analyses identified TFAP2A , VTCN1 , and hsa-miR-21-5p as molecular factors associated with MUC16 expression. Clinical analyses further showed increased MUC16 protein expression in LUAD tissues and associations of serum CA125 levels with lower total lymphocyte and CD3⁺ T-cell counts. Computational drug analyses identified candidate compounds and pharmacogenomic associations for subsequent validation. Collectively, these findings support the prognostic and immunological relevance of MUC16 , warranting further experimental and clinical investigation.

Article.Title: Effect of pineapple peel meal supplementation on production performance and gut health in Sasso broilers
Article.Authors: Norlizayati R.; Chung E.; Zheng A.; Loh T.; Jesse F.
Article.Abstract: The effects of supplementing the Sasso broilers with dietary pineapple peel meal (PPM) on the growth performance, apparent ileal digestibility, intestinal histomorphology, cecal microflora, carcass characteristics, and meat quality were examined in this study. A completely randomized design was conducted using 240 day-old female Sasso broilers assigned to four treatments consisting of a basal diet without antibiotics (NC), a basal diet supplemented with oxytetracycline (PC), and basal diets supplemented with 1.5% (P1) or 3% (P2) PPM. Each treatment was conducted for 56 days with six replicates of 10 birds. Phytochemical screening detected alkaloids, flavonoids, saponins, tannins, and phenols in PPM, with alkaloids showing the highest reported content (1.99 ± 0.10%). Starter growth performance was improved with 6.3% increase in body weight gain and 3.9% reduction in feed conversion ratio when supplemented with 3% PPM ( P ≤ 0.032), while 1.5% PPM produced superior finisher performance with 7.8% increase body weight gain and 8.6% improve in feed conversion ratio ( P < 0.001). Broilers fed with 1.5% PPM inclusion also improved dry matter (+ 8.1%), crude protein (+ 11.7%), and ash (+ 25.5%) digestibility ( P ≤ 0.002), intestinal morphology ( P ≤ 0.019), and carcass traits ( P ≤ 0.021). Descriptively, 3% PPM showed lower coliform and standard plate counts than the negative control, while improving post-mortem muscle pH and reducing cooking loss ( P ≤ 0.010). Overall, 1.5% PPM showed the most consistent favorable responses across the statistically evaluated growth, digestibility, intestinal morphology, and carcass outcomes. Supplementation with 3% PPM was associated with higher starter-phase growth and favorable changes in selected meat-quality parameters. Differences in cecal microbial counts were descriptive and required further statistical validation. These findings support further investigation of PPM as a dietary feed additive in Sasso broilers while promoting the valorization of pineapple-processing by-products.

Article.Title: Speech, spectral cue and harmony perception in cochlear implant recipients with anatomy-based fitting: a prospective, randomized, multicenter trial
Article.Authors: Heuninck E.; Topsakal V.; Abari J.; Riss D.; Lüchtrath L.; Liepins R.; Brauer F.; Thurner T.; Auinger A.; Berwouts J.; Van Rompaey V.; Vanderveken O.; Lammers M.; Andries E.; Mertens G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anatomy-based fitting (ABF) aims to restore natural tonotopicity by pre-operatively selecting an electrode array for complete cochlear coverage and post-operatively adapting the frequency allocation of a cochlear implant (CI) to a patient’s individual cochlear anatomy. Fifty-six newly unilaterally implanted patients with a bilateral severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss were included at the University Hospital Brussels, the Antwerp University Hospital and the University Hospital Vienna. Thirty patients were fitted with ABF and 26 patients with a standard fitting. Patients had follow-up visits at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months and 6 months post-activation of the audioprocessor. No statistically significant effect of fitting was found for pure-tone audiometry ( p = 0.23), speech perception in quiet ( p = 0.66), speech perception in noise ( p = 0.42) and self-perceived auditory benefit ( p = 0.29). Patients fitted with ABF demonstrated a better perception of auditory cues in the spectral domain ( p < 0.001) at 3 and 6 months post-activation, and a more distinct pattern for pleasantness of harmonic intervals in comparison to patients with a standard frequency distribution at 3 months post-activation. A higher contrast in pleasantness of harmonic intervals may enhance music perception and appreciation. Article.Title: Spatial variability of GNSS –derived ionospheric total electron content over Ethiopia during 17–18 March 2015 geomagnetic storm
Article.Authors: Shiferaw Y.; Ali S.; Getahun E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ethiopia’s location within the equatorial ionization anomaly region renders its ionosphere highly vulnerable to storm-driven spatial ionospheric total electron content variability, although dense-network investigations of storm-time TEC response remain limited. This study assesses spatial variability of ionospheric total electron content over Ethiopia during the 17–18 March 2015 geomagnetic storm using GNSS -derived vTEC data from nine Ethiopia stations. The intense geomagnetic storm of 2015 were analyzed, the 17–18 March G4-class storm with Disturbance storm time (Dst) index − 234 nT. Concurrent Dst index, planetary Kp index and interplanetary magnetic field z component (IMF Bz) data were integrated with spatially continuous vertical total electron content (vTEC) map were done using ordinary kriging interpolation to characterize the storm-time ionospheric response over Ethiopia. A persistent east–west asymmetry was also identified with western and central sector such as Addis Ababa recording consistently higher vTEC than eastern sector such as Nazret (Adama) and with storm-time enhancements during the storm- time confined almost entirely to the 34–41°E sector within a specific local-time window, indicating that the longitudinal response is governed by local-time-dependent electrodynamic force rather than a spatially uniform disturbance. Positive ionospheric storm phases dominated the main and early recovery periods, while negative ionospheric storm phases emerged during later recovery intervals as disturbance dynamo-driven westward electric fields suppressed the equatorial electrojet (EEJ) and equatorial ionization anomaly (EIA). The leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) results quantitatively shows that the reliability of Kriging-derived TEC maps varies over time, with greater interpolation uncertainty during periods characterized by pronounced spatial TEC gradients.
