Data were collected using the Social Integration in Later Life Scale for social integration, Barthel Index for severity of physical disability, Perceived Social Support Scale for perceived social support, and Leyden Walking Instrument for perceived community walkability. Pearson correlations​ and multiple linear regression were performed. The mean SILLS total score was 53.66 ± 12.54. In the fully adjusted model (adjusted R² = 0.589), older age at the micro-level was negatively associated with social integration ( B = − 0.248, P < 0.001). At the meso-level, perceived social support was positively associated with social integration ( B = 0.438, P < 0.001), while perceived community walkability showed an overall association ( F (10, 488) = 7.282, P < 0.001), although this association was not statistically significant in a restricted sensitivity analysis ( n = 200, P = 0.119). At the macro-level, pension insurance enrollment was positively associated with social integration ( B = 3.727, P < 0.001). These findings may inform the development of multilevel interventions aimed at enhancing social integration and promoting health among older adults with physical disability.

Article.Title: Early identification of exercise-induced respiratory symptoms in competitive athletes: establishment and validation of a predictive model
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Wu X.; Hu Z.; Liu Y.; Zhang A.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Exercise-induced respiratory symptoms (EIRS) are common among athletes, but cultural factors may deter some athletes from reporting these. Thus, we have developed a predictive model to anticipate the occurrence of EIRS. A survey of athletes from five centers in Chongqing, China, was conducted from December 2021 to December 2022. Risk factors for EIRS were identified using univariate and multiple logistic regression analyses, and a predictive model was constructed. The model’s performance was assessed for discrimination and calibration, and its clinical utility was evaluated with Decision curve analysis (DCA). Model validation was done through 10-fold cross-validation. A total of 147 athletes were included in the analysis, resulting in the establishment of a predictive model consisting of five variables: “sex, type of sport, history of allergy, Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), allergic rhinitis” and visualized using a nomogram. Bootstrap ROC analysis showed good model discrimination (AUC, 0.806; 95% CI, 0.731–0.878). Calibration analysis further affirmed the accuracy of the model. 10-fold cross-validation suggested moderate internal predictive performance. DCA indicated its practical applicability. We developed and internally validated a nomogram-based predictive model incorporating five clinical variables to estimate the probability of EIRS in athletes. The model showed satisfactory discrimination and calibration, and Decision curve analysis supported its potential clinical utility. These findings warrant further external validation in larger and more diverse athlete populations before broader clinical application.

Article.Title: Long-read sequencing of the Amami rabbit mitochondrial genome reveals extensive tandem repeats in the D-loop region overlooked in previous assemblies
Article.Authors: Aoto S.; Shindo M.; Okamura K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Amami rabbit, Pentalagus furnessi , is an endangered species endemic to Japan, inhabiting only Amami-Oshima Island and Tokunoshima Island. Molecular phylogenetic analysis suggests that this species diverged before the separation of hares ( Lepus ) and rabbits ( Oryctolagus ), and it is considered a “living fossil” based on its morphological characteristics and evolutionary position. Despite its importance for population genetics and conservation, the complete mitochondrial genome structure had not been fully characterized. In this study, we performed whole-genome long-read sequencing using Oxford Nanopore Technology and determined the complete mitochondrial genome sequence prior to nuclear genome analysis. The total length of the Amami rabbit mitochondrial genome was 17,693 bp, approximately 1,000 bp longer than the previously reported sequence. This newly identified region corresponded to a tandem repeat region within the D-loop. The Amami rabbit D-loop region contains approximately 33 copies of an 8-base short tandem repeat and 7 copies of a 143-base long tandem repeat. We confirmed heteroplasmy in tandem repeat copy numbers, while no single-nucleotide heteroplasmy was detected. These tandem repeats in the D-loop region represent a characteristic feature of lagomorph mitochondrial genomes, and our findings suggest that D-loop lengths in lagomorphs, and possibly in other mammals, could be systematically underestimated in public databases, highlighting the need for long-read validation.

Article.Authors: Yan J.; Wang C.; Zhao J.; Qin J.; Shi R.; Ye W.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the effect of nanofiller dimensionality on the thermal stability of poly(m-phenylene isophthalamide) (PMIA) insulating films and the underlying mechanisms, zero-dimensional ZrO₂ nanoparticles and two-dimensional fluorinated graphene (FG) were selected as representative fillers. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed on neat PMIA, ZrO₂/PMIA, and FG/PMIA nanocomposites with different filler loadings. The glass transition temperature, mean square displacement (MSD), interfacial binding energy, and free volume fraction (FFV) were calculated to evaluate glass-transition behavior and its associations with molecular mobility, interfacial energetics, and free volume. The simulations predict higher Tg values for the investigated composite models than for neat PMIA, with filler-dependent differences in molecular mobility and packing. The glass transition temperature of neat PMIA was 539 K, which increased to 578 K for 1 wt% ZrO₂/PMIA and 593 K for 3 wt% FG/PMIA. The MSD results showed loading-dependent differences in PMIA atomic mobility, with the relative mobility of the composite models varying with temperature. The combined results suggest associations between filler–matrix interactions, molecular packing, and restricted PMIA motion. For the nominal 1 wt% ZrO₂/PMIA and 3 wt% FG/PMIA models, the reduced FFV values indicated a smaller fraction of geometric free space. The combined analysis of FFV, MSD, and Tg revealed filler- and loading-dependent relationships among structural packing, atomic mobility, and glass-transition behavior. These findings provide molecular-level insight into the glass-transition behavior of the modeled PMIA nanocomposites and identify candidate filler loadings for further investigation.

Article.Title: UGC driven generative 3D urban screens for urban interfaces
Article.Authors: Yuan Y.; Feng T.; Yu Z.
Article.Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence offers new possibilities for producing cultural content for urban public screens, yet systematic empirical research remains limited on how public digital expressions can be translated into locally grounded generative content and evaluated in real public spaces. Using Hubin Pedestrian Street in Hangzhou as a case study, this research develops a workflow integrating UGC corpus analysis, urban image and visual motif selection, generative visual production, corner screen based glasses free 3D presentation, and in situ evaluation. A corpus of 6708 deduplicated Weibo posts was used to identify tourism related urban images in Hangzhou. Structured prompts and a locally deployed Stable Diffusion workflow were then used to generate visual assets, which were further adapted into glasses free 3D content for the corner screen. Field evaluation included 100 post exposure questionnaires and 12 fixed camera behavioral observation sessions conducted over three consecutive weekdays. Participants reported generally positive evaluations of cultural representativeness, overall satisfaction, and visual comfort, and several post exposure perception dimensions were positively associated with sharing, recommendation, and revisit intentions. Stopping rates on the two screen on days were 17.4% and 16.1%, respectively, both significantly higher than the 3.5% observed on the screen off day (both p < 0.001), while no significant difference was found between the two screen on days. These findings indicate that the UGC driven generative workflow provides a traceable basis for urban cultural visual design and, in this study context, is associated with positive post exposure evaluations and higher public stopping proportions, offering a reproducible framework for generative urban screen design and in situ evaluation.

Article.Title: A height-aware design framework for single-tuned mass dampers in seismic steel buildings
Article.Authors: Shabib M.; Farag H.; Khalifa Y.; Zahran M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a height-aware engineering design framework for roof-mounted single-tuned mass dampers (STMDs) in multi-story steel buildings. Five three-dimensional steel models with 5, 10, 12, 15, and 20 stories were analyzed in ABAQUS/CAE under the Kobe and Loma Prieta earthquake records. A baseline assessment first applied the Sadek tuning procedure using a fixed 5% mass ratio to investigate the influence of building height. The resulting response trends were interpreted using natural periods, modal-mass participation, a higher-mode influence index, and a detuning indicator. The 12-story model yielded the largest baseline roof-displacement reductions, reaching 46.0% under Kobe and 21.0% under Loma Prieta, whereas the corresponding reductions for the 20-story model were 12.8% and 10.7%, respectively. A surrogate-based parametric design exploration was subsequently used to examine practical combinations of mass ratio, tuning ratio, and damping ratio within prescribed bounds. The surrogate exploration identified candidate parameter sets that substantially mitigated dynamic demands in low- and mid-rise structures; however, it failed to overcome the intrinsic modal-dispersion bottleneck in the 20-story frame. For that model, combining the STMD with shear walls or outer inverted-V bracing increased the roof-displacement reduction to 45.4–65.5%, depending on the earthquake record and lateral-resisting configuration. The proposed sequence height screening, parameter exploration, and hybrid-system assessment provide a structured design process for selecting the control strategy within the investigated building family. However, the control efficacy of standalone STMDs remains fundamentally limited in taller, flexible buildings due to higher-mode mass participation and nonlinear frequency detuning. The present findings are bound by the investigated prototype steel frames, uniform cross-sectional benchmark assumptions, fixed-base boundary conditions, and the selected ground motion records.

Article.Authors: Issayeva A.; Spychalski W.; Rysbayeva Z.; Antkowiak W.; Arystanova S.; Ospanova Z.; Łęska B.; Alpamyssova G.; Tleukeyeva A.; Issayev Y.; Pankiewicz R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract How substrate conditions relate to spontaneous plant colonisation of lignite waste dumps remains poorly resolved in seasonally dry environments. We compared vascular plant records with mineralogical and physicochemical measurements from two lignite waste dumps near Lenger, southern Kazakhstan. Vegetation was sparse and patchy. Asteraceae and Poaceae dominated the herbaceous component, while Capparis spinosa formed sparse shrub patches on waste B; no trees were recorded. Centaurea virgata subsp. squarrosa (= Centaurea pseudosquarrosa ) Agropyron cristatum and Elymus repens were among the most abundant taxa. Waste samples A, taken from beneath the plants, contained more silt than adjacent bare samples, but this pattern was not universal. Paired microsite contrasts varied in direction; these descriptive observations do not establish a general plant–substrate relationship or a temporal succession rate.

Article.Title: Unveiling the antitumor and chemo-sensitizing effects of ondansetron in the treatment of MCF-7 breast cancer cells
Article.Authors: Mashaly M.; Abd-Ellah M.; Hassan H.; Mokhlis H.; Shatat A.; Ashour A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer (BC) remains one of the global leading causes of cancer-related deaths among women. Resistance to chemotherapy and metastatic progression are key challenges. Serotonin (5-HT) and its receptor subtypes are implicated in tumor proliferation, but the oncogenic role of 5-HT3-Rs in BC is not well defined. The widely-used antiemetic, Ondansetron , is a selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, that is investigated in this study to explore the potential previously-unrecognized anticancer properties in MCF-7 human BC cells. To investigate the potential effect of Ondansetron , alone or in combination with Doxorubicin , in inhibiting proliferation, survival and migration of MCF-7 BC cells, and to explore some of the underlying molecular mechanisms. MCF-7 cells were treated with Ondansetron and/or Doxorubicin . Cell viability- (MTT), migration- (wound healing), and survival- (clonogenic) assays were conducted. The regulation of some downstream signaling pathways were analyzed by ELISA, Western blotting, or immunofluorescence to assess the modulations of migratory/metastatic (RAS/mTOR/SRC/FAK/MMP-2), survival/angiogenic (Cyclin D1/VEGF-A), and apoptotic ( Bcl-2/Cytochrome c/cleaved-caspase-7 ) biomarkers. Ondansetron significantly reduced cell viability and migration capability and markedly potentiated the cytotoxic effects of Doxorubicin . The combination regimen, downregulated key oncogenic signaling molecules ( RAS/mTOR/SRC/FAK/MMP-2/VEGF-A/Cyclin D1 ) with enhanced Cytochrome c / cleaved-caspase-7 activation, and suppressed the anti-apoptotic protein, Bcl-2. Pharmacological targeting of 5-HT/HTR3 with Ondansetron induces antitumor effects in MCF-7 BC cells by suppressing 5-HT3-mediated survival signaling and metastatic pathways, and increases MCF-7 cells sensitivity to chemotherapy. This study proposes using Ondansetron as a potential adjuvant to Doxorubicin -based treatment of BC, to improve efficacy and reduce toxicity of the chemotherapy.

Article.Authors: Tang D.; Xu Q.; Shao X.

The composite health score was assessed with the National Student Physical Health Standard (body morphology, body function, physical fitness); Chinese language achievement came from provincial standardized examinations; cross-lagged panel models examined bidirectional predictions. An fNIRS subsample (excellent, n = 20; qualified, n = 18) completed homophone and synonym tasks. Only physical fitness showed significant bidirectional associations with language scores (fitness→scores: β = 0.067, p < 0.001; scores→fitness: β = 0.142, p = 0.001); body morphology and body function did not. In fNIRS tasks, the excellent group showed higher accuracy and shorter reaction times in the homophone task (q < 0.05) but no significant L-IFG differences. The composite health score is prospectively associated with Chinese language achievement, driven by physical fitness, consistent with the executive function theory. The fNIRS findings are exploratory and not mechanistic evidence; mechanisms were not tested, and larger samples are needed.

Article.Title: A simplified fracture prediction approach for FDM-fabricated notched PLA components with cross-ply raster pattern: experimental verification by the semi-circular bend specimen data
Article.Authors: Sadeghi S.; Ayatollahi M.; Choupani N.; Torabi A.
Article.Abstract: Mode I translaminar fracture of the semi-circular bend (SCB) specimens containing U- and rounded V-notches (RV-notches) additively manufactured from Polylactic acid (PLA) is investigated. It is aimed to examine whether incorporating the limited tensile nonlinearity of the printed PLA through the equivalent material concept (EMC) can improve the fracture load prediction obtained within the virtual isotropic material concept (VIMC) framework. For this purpose, two modeling approaches, namely VIMC and VIMC-EMC, are applied in conjunction with the mean stress (MS) criterion, maximum tangential stress (MTS) criterion, averaged strain energy density (ASED) criterion, and cohesive zone model (CZM) applied via the extended finite element method (XFEM). The results show that the direct VIMC approach combined with MS criterion yields the best predictions with MAPE values less than 5%. The EMC correction has only a limited influence on MS and MTS criteria, while its effect on ASED criterion is also marginal. In contrast, VIMC-EMC approach improves the CZM-XFEM predictions, reducing MAPE value between 6 and 9%. Therefore, the EMC correction should not be regarded as universally beneficial for FDM-fabricated PLA, but should be evaluated according to the fracture criterion and material response. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations confirm a predominantly brittle fracture behavior for both notch geometries, although the U-notched specimens exhibit rougher fracture surfaces which are well consistent with their higher fracture loads experimentally acquired. Overall, VIMC-MS approach is shown to provide a simple, accurate, and computationally efficient route for predicting Mode I fracture loads of notched printed PLA components with a cross-ply [0/90] s raster pattern without requiring modeling the printed material layer-by-layer.

Article.Title: Self-stabilising QoS through autonomic scheduling of latency-critical traffic
Article.Authors: Ray R.; Pandey C.; Saurabh P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conventional queuing systems such as First-In-First-Out (FIFO) scheduling often experience unfair latency spikes and unbounded jitter. This makes them inefficient when handling bursty and heterogeneous traffic. As a result, maintaining fair and reliable Quality of Service (QoS) in mixed-traffic networks remains challenging. This work targets heterogeneous traffic (specifically mixed application classes: Video, VoIP, Chat, Browsing, File Transfer, and P2P sharing a single wired edge-router queue) rather than heterogeneous wireless access networks. Recent research has explored biological regulation mechanisms as inspiration for adaptive and robust resource management in complex systems. This paper formulates and evaluates a lightweight closed-loop QoS scheduler that converts application-level traffic semantics obtained from ML classification into local waiting-time-based priority adaptation, and systematically characterises the resulting latency, fairness, and stability trade-off under normal load, erroneous classification, multi-hop, and overloaded conditions. The MA-QoS dynamically adjusts packet priorities over time according to $$P_{\text {dynamic}} = P_{\text {base}} + (T_{\text {queue}} \times W_{\text {metabolic}})$$ , where $$P_{\text {base}}$$ encodes the application class’s latency sensitivity, $$T_{\text {queue}}$$ is the packet’s waiting time, and $$W_{\text {metabolic}}$$ is a tunable ageing rate; as a packet waits longer, its effective priority rises, preventing starvation while preserving class ordering under normal load. The model is evaluated using the CIC-VPN2016 dataset, which provides labelled network traffic traces covering application types such as Video, VoIP, File Transfer, and VPN-encrypted flows. Traffic flows are first classified using a Random Forest with 93% accuracy. Each flow is assigned a base priority by class, and a “metabolic” weight is used to boost its effective priority as it waits in the queue. In simulations with 10,000 Poisson arrival tasks, the MA-QoS queue reduces the median delay for video flows from 5.46 time units under FIFO to 0.52 time units, while also achieving consistently lower delay variance compared with RED and WFQ. Notably, MA-QoS also matches or exceeds a Deep Q-Network scheduler on latency-sensitive traffic while requiring no training; MA-QoS produces deterministic decisions for a fixed traffic trace, whereas the DQN’s run-to-run variance across independently trained models can exceed its mean delay. These improvements are obtained under identical load conditions: aggregate throughput and Jain’s fairness index are provably identical across all evaluated schedulers, achieved with modest additional computational overhead relative to FIFO. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed class-aware priority scheduler produces substantial latency and jitter reductions for high-priority traffic, while the metabolic ageing mechanism adds starvation protection when active, making MA-QoS a practical approach for QoS management in heterogeneous networks.

Article.Title: Decentralised health record management with blockchain: privacy and security in cloud-based systems
Article.Authors: Sree S.; Radhika D.; Veerabhadram V.; Sirisha S.; Jyoshna B.; Raghavender E.
Article.Abstract: The rise of Electronic Health Records (EHRs) has created a new challenge for healthcare organisations: how to manage, share and secure the growing amounts of health data. Conventional cloud-based EHR systems remain susceptible to centralised trust, limited auditability, and inflexible access-control mechanisms, and most existing blockchain-based systems don’t collectively support adaptive policy enforcement, privacy-preserving authentication, and anomaly-aware access validation. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the decentralised EHR management framework HealthBlockSecure, which combines permissioned blockchain infrastructure, encrypted off-chain storage, authentication with zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), decentralised identities, smart-contract-based policy enforcement, and the PrivAccessNet deep learning model. PrivAccessNet can provide context-aware access validation and anomaly detection based on request and policy attributes, and the external ZKP verification service can provide minimal-disclosure authentication without revealing sensitive identity information. Experimental evaluation with SyntheticMass and MIMIC-IV showed a mean access-violation prevention rate of 96.3% for five re-experiments and an audit-verification accuracy of 99.2%. It also identified all simulated tampering attempts using SHA-256 integrity verification. In general, HealthBlockSecure delivers an integrated solution for privacy-sensitive, auditable, and adaptive management of access to EHRs, with secure-access validation latency measured in the near-real-time range. The complete HealthBlockSecure implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/Sripada-RamaSree/HealthBlockSecure .

This study explores how health Streaming information access and self-awareness influence autonomous sports participation among Chinese university students from a psychosocial perspective, focusing on the mediating role of self-efficacy and the moderating effect of data trust. Based on user satisfaction theory and self-determination theory, this study constructs a theoretical framework integrating psychological and data trust dimensions. Data from 485 undergraduate and graduate students was collected through a questionnaire survey. Structural equation modeling analysis revealed that health Streaming information access does not directly predict autonomous sports participation, but self-efficacy fully mediates the relationship between the two; self-awareness positively promotes autonomous participation, while self-efficacy plays a partial mediating role. Furthermore, data trust significantly moderates the relationship between health Streaming information access and self-efficacy: the positive impact of information access on self-efficacy is stronger in the high-trust group. This study expands the application of user satisfaction and self-determination theories in the digital health context and provides practical insights for data security management of health Streaming platforms and the integration of sports education in universities.

Article.Title: Correlation between starch physicochemical properties and pellet feed quality under different starch sources for mechanistic understanding and prediction
Article.Authors: Peng F.; Huang L.; Xiang R.; Wu H.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Starch is the major energy source and natural binder in pelleted feed, and its botanical origin-dependent properties strongly affect feed processing quality. This study aimed to clarify how starch physicochemical properties govern pellet forming performance and to establish machine learning (ML)-based prediction models linking starch characteristics to pellet quality. Eight starch sources (wheat, common corn, waxy corn, potato, sweet potato, manioc, pea, and mung bean) were analyzed for chemical composition, granule morphology, gelatinization, rheological, and thermal properties. Amylose content ranged from 1.05% to 41.27%, and the amylopectin/amylose ratio varied from 0.94 to 74.90. Average particle sizes were 12.92–38.71 μm, and gelatinization temperatures ranged from 69.43 to 89.58 °C. Based on significant differences in gelatinization temperature (a critical processing-related index), four representative starches (wheat, common corn, manioc, and pea) were selected for pelleting trials. Within 10–20% starch addition, pellet density and hardness were 1.32–1.86 g/cm³ and 3.18–3.96 kg, respectively. Higher starch addition significantly increased pellet density and hardness. Low gelatinization temperature facilitated densification, while high amylose favored gel network formation. Five ML algorithms (GBDT, KNN, PLS, RF, and SVR) were evaluated. GBDT performed best for density (R² = 0.93), whereas PLS performed best for hardness (R² = 0.94) and powder content rate (R² = 0.98). SHAP analysis indicated that starch addition was the dominant factor, positively contributing to density and hardness but negatively to powder content rate. This work provides predictive tools for starch source selection and formula optimization in pelleted feed.

Article.Title: Evaluation of a tailored surgical site infection prevention bundle in instrumented spinal surgery using interrupted time series analysis
Article.Authors: Boni S.; Sartini M.; Cristina M.; Guastalli F.; Ricci F.; Del Puente F.; Blasi Vacca E.; Carbone A.; Viberti F.; Di Maio S.; Castriciano A.; Morelli P.; Adriano G.; Bruzzo M.; Pontali E.; N/A N/A.; Fabbri A.; Feasi M.; Ferrari L.; Giunciuglio P.; Internicola S.; Nelli M.; Pozzati M.; Santarsiero M.
Article.Abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are a major complication of instrumented spinal surgery, with incidence up to 16%. Although care bundles reduce SSIs across surgical specialties, prospective evidence in spinal surgery is limited. We conducted prospective surveillance (January 2023 – June 2025) in a tertiary care center. In June 2024 following structured operating room observations, we implemented a team-agreed five-component bundle covering skin preparation, hair removal, timely cefazolin prophylaxis, alcohol-based chlorhexidine antisepsis, and perioperative glycaemic control (<180 mg/dL) in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. Pre-bundle and post-bundle periods were compared. Primary outcome was SSI incidence assessed by interrupted time-series (ITS) analysis. Secondary outcomes included reoperations, re-hospitalizations, and healthcare costs savings. The pre-bundle period (18 months) included 203 surgeries, while the post-bundle phase (13 months) included 142 surgeries. SSI incidence decreased from 11.33% to 2.82%. (IRR 4.02; 95% CI 1.37–16.00; p=0.0065). ITS analysis estimated an immediate reduction of approximately 78% (​IRR 0.22, 95% CI 0.05–1.02), although the confidence interval included the null; uncertainty in the post-intervention trend precluded conclusions about durability.. Reoperations fell from 15 to 3 (70% reduction vs expected). Net estimated cost savings were €140,815. A tailored, team-developed SSI prevention bundle was associated with a large reduction in SSI incidence, reoperations, and healthcare costs in instrumented spinal surgery. Although the ITS estimate did not reach statistical significance, the magnitude of the observed reduction supports the potential clinical relevance of this approach.

Article.Title: AD2EF-Net: an adaptive dropout artificial neural network with behavior-aware feature engineering for version number attack detection in RPL-based IoT networks
Article.Authors: Alfriehat N.; Anbar M.; Aljaidi M.; Ahmad M.; Arafah M.; Alashhab Z.; Alshammari A.; Karuppayah S.
Article.Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) networks commonly employ the Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL), where Version Number (VN) attacks can trigger unnecessary global repairs and persistent routing instability. This paper presents AD2EF-Net, an ANN-based VN-attack detection framework that integrates SHAP-guided offline analysis, behavior-aware feature engineering, intersection-consensus feature selection, and a self-tuning adaptive-dropout mechanism. To avoid information leakage, the revised experimental protocol performs the stratified 60/20/20 train/validation/test split before training-dependent preprocessing; SMOTE, Min–Max scaling, and feature selection are fitted exclusively on the training partition and then applied unchanged to validation and held-out test data. Under this corrected protocol, the final evaluated AD2EF-Net pipeline achieved 90.49% accuracy, 84.54% precision, 98.19% recall, a 90.86% F1 score, and a 95.99% AUC on the held-out test set. A controlled ten-seed dropout ablation showed only small differences among no-dropout, fixed-rate, and adaptive configurations: adaptive dropout achieved 92.45 ± 0.21% accuracy, 92.49 ± 0.20% F1, and the highest mean AUC (97.36 ± 0.13%), while fixed rates produced slightly higher mean accuracy, F1, or recall in some cases. A separate feature-selection ablation showed that the intersection-consensus strategy is not the highest-performing selector on this dataset; Extra Trees top-16 achieved stronger predictive performance, whereas the intersection-consensus configurations are discussed as consensus-based design trade-offs rather than as the highest-performing feature-selection strategy. The revised results therefore support AD2EF-Net as a transparent, leak-free framework with high recall on the evaluated IRAD benchmark, while avoiding claims of universal superiority, generalizability, or deployment readiness.

Article.Title: Developing a deep learning–based model to predict simulated building performance using the spatial layout of residential apartments in Isfahan
Article.Authors: Ramezani M.; Zamani P.; Heydaripour O.; Saffari F.; Gorgabi M.
Article.Abstract: Spatial configuration is a primary determinant of residential building performance, yet evaluating trade-offs across design alternatives remains computationally intensive. This study introduces an integrated computational framework combining a Generative Spatial Layout (GSL) algorithm, Building Performance Simulation, and a hybrid multi-input Deep Learning (DL) model to rapidly predict multi-objective performance. Focusing on south-facing rectangular apartments in Isfahan, 27,000 distinct design configurations were generated and evaluated across six performance metrics: cooling demand, heating demand, useful daylight illuminance (UDI), embodied carbon, operational carbon, and embodied water. The dataset was partitioned into training (70%), validation (10%), and testing (20%) subsets to train the hybrid DL architecture, which integrates dense numerical layers and Transformer-based spatial sequence processing. The Mean Squared Error (MSE) value demonstrates the optimal performance of the study’s ML model, indicating high prediction accuracy. Moreover, the coefficients of determination (R 2 ) for all performance indicators range between 0.95 and 0.997, demonstrating strong predictive performance within the evaluated dataset. Analysis further reveals the significant influence of the dimensions, location, and number of Indoor Spaces, particularly the living room and Vertical Circulation Core, on energy and environmental performance. The hybrid DL approach proves effective for predicting residential building performance using multidimensional GSL datasets. Findings identify spatial optimization and strategic Vertical Circulation Core placement as critical factors for improving overall building efficiency.

Article.Title: StegoStack: a layered hybrid encoding fra​mework for secure and high-fidelity image steganography
Article.Authors: Tripathy A.; Kavitha C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Image steganography plays a critical role in secure digital communication by concealing sensitive information within multimedia content while maintaining visual imperceptibility. This paper presents StegoStack, a layered hybrid image steganography framework that integrates modern encoding techniques, historical cipher transformations, columnar transposition, and 2-bit RGB least significant bit embedding to enhance information security and concealment. Unlike conventional approaches that employ a limited set of encoding mechanisms, the proposed framework enables systematic evaluation and integration of diverse modern and historical encoding strategies within a unified architecture. A comprehensive experimental study involving 22 encoding methods was conducted across 6 real world application scenarios, including military communication, medical record transmission, digital watermarking, journalism, forensic evidence exchange, and gaming communication. The framework was evaluated using 17 performance metrics related to imperceptibility, payload efficiency, robustness, entropy, and computational performance. Resistance to automated detection was assessed using machine learning and deep learning steganalysis models on a dataset comprising 1,080 cover and stego images. Additional validation was performed through robustness analysis, ablation studies, scalability evaluation, and statistical significance testing. Experimental results demonstrate high visual fidelity, effective information concealment, and promising resistance against the evaluated steganalysis models. The findings further confirm the contribution of individual framework components and the scalability of the proposed approach across varying payload sizes. The proposed StegoStack framework provides a flexible and extensible solution for secure image steganography in diverse application domains.

Article.Title: Association between GLP-1 receptor agonist use and risk of repeat colonoscopy: a real-world cohort study with exploratory discontinuation analyses
Article.Authors: Sung K.; Hsieh P.; Wang Y.; Chen F.; Lai P.; Chang C.; Yeo Y.; Wu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for diabetes and obesity, their effects on gastrointestinal motility have raised concern about colonoscopy outcomes. We evaluated the association between GLP-1 RA use and repeat colonoscopy and performed exploratory analyses of pre-procedural discontinuation intervals. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. The analysis was restricted to adults aged 18–90 years with an index procedure between January 2021 and January 2025. Long-term GLP-1 RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with non-users on 44 covariates. The primary outcome was repeat colonoscopy within 12 months. Stratified analyses, exploratory analyses of discontinuation intervals from 0 to 8 weeks, and active-comparator analyses against dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor users were also performed. After propensity-score matching, 20,490 GLP-1 RA users were compared with 20,490 non-users. GLP-1 RA use was associated with a higher risk of repeat colonoscopy within 12 months (RR 1.50, 95% CI 1.39–1.61), with similar associations at 6 months (RR 1.61, 95% CI 1.48–1.75), 3 months (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.59–1.94), and 2 months (RR 1.86, 95% CI 1.66–2.08). In active-comparator analysis, the association persisted versus DPP-4 inhibitors (RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.21–1.63) and SGLT2 inhibitors (RR 1.26, 95% CI 1.15–1.38). Exploratory discontinuation estimates attenuated with longer intervals, but overlapping confidence intervals and decreasing stratum sizes did not identify a definitive discontinuation threshold. GLP-1 RA use was associated with a higher likelihood of repeat colonoscopy within one year in a contemporary, propensity-score-matched cohort, including in active-comparator analyses. Because repeat colonoscopy is a non-specific healthcare-utilization outcome and the discontinuation analyses were observational and exploratory, these findings do not establish inadequate bowel preparation as the mechanism or support a specific pre-procedural discontinuation interval. Prospective studies with directly measured bowel-preparation quality are needed.

Article.Title: Comparison of Bresenham and Siddon ray tracing algorithms for sparse view 3D reconstruction of simulated coronary vessel models
Article.Authors: Binesh A.; Szczypiński P.
Article.Abstract: Interventional C-arm imaging enables minimally invasive cardiac procedures while reducing radiation exposure through sparse-view acquisition. However, reconstruction of three-dimensional vascular morphology from a limited number of projections remains a severely ill-posed inverse problem, particularly in the presence of Poisson quantum noise. This study evaluates two ray-tracing models, Siddon’s (weighted) and Bresenham’s (binary), combined with the Simultaneous Iterative Reconstruction Technique (SIRT) and Total Variation regularization (SIRT+TV). Synthetic phantoms derived from patient-specific coronary geometries were reconstructed from nine simulated noisy cone-beam projections acquired at different angles. Reconstructed volumes were binarized using Otsu and IoU-maximized thresholds. Automatic Otsu thresholding was ineffective for Bresenham-based reconstructions due to severe reconstruction artifacts. Nevertheless, IoU-maximized thresholding yielded a mean Dice-Sørensen coefficient of 0.795, indicating preservation of relevant vascular information. Siddon-based reconstruction produced fewer artifacts and achieved superior performance, reaching a Dice-Sørensen coefficient of 0.860 with SIRT. No clear advantage of TV regularization over SIRT alone was observed. The results demonstrate that key aspects of vascular morphology can be recovered from sparse-view projections. However, the observed reconstruction errors indicate that substantial methodological improvements are required before practical application can be considered.

Article.Title: Automated histomorphometry of ablative fractional laser lesions enables a complete-field census of geometric heterogeneity
Article.Authors: Quadri S.; Marks H.; Wang-Evers M.; Manstein D.
Article.Abstract: Ablative fractional laser (AFL) treatments are evaluated histologically by measuring about ten selected lesions per sample, which cannot describe the whole field. We developed an automated framework that segments ablation, coagulation, viable tissue and background on horizontal nitroblue tetrazolium chloride (NBTC)-stained sections and measures every lesion. Six models (five architectures) were trained under a pre-specified protocol and tested on all 35 serial sections of a held-out punch. The final pipeline averages three architectures selected on validation data. On the held-out punch it reached Dice 0.932 for ablation and 0.911 for coagulation, detected 96.3% of lesions with 93.7% precision after a lesion filter (62.4% without), and measured ablation diameter with a mean bias of −0.1 \(\mu\) m. Accuracy decreased with depth (deepest band 0.858). These values come from a single punch that is an outlier in treatment density (pitch 2.1 times nominal); performance on specimens of typical density has not been confirmed. In expert annotations, a random 10-lesion sample estimated within-section size variability within ±20% in a median of 58% of draws, and selecting the 10 best-formed craters underestimated it in every section (median −63%). Complete-field measurement is therefore needed; as donor identity was not recorded, between-sample differences may reflect few donors.

Article.Title: Outcome-specific associations of whole-body and segmental body composition with physical fitness in Chinese youth
Article.Authors: Tian X.; Xiang M.; Zhang Z.; Huang L.; Zhang J.; Cao W.; Yang T.; Xu J.; Wang H.; Pan H.; Luo R.; Fang H.; Zheng Y.; Yang Z.; Zhao W.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Body composition is associated with physical fitness in youth, but task-specific relationships of absolute and relative muscle-related measures remain unclear. We analysed cross-sectional data from a national multicentre survey of Chinese children and adolescents aged approximately 6.9–18.0 years: 7,171 for handgrip strength, 7,667 for standing long jump, and 7,648 for the 50 m × 8 shuttle run. Twenty-four anthropometric and body-composition indicators were prioritized using site-grouped cross-validated XGBoost with held-out SHAP values. The highest-ranked indicator for each outcome was then examined using exploratory, post-selection restricted cubic spline models with cluster-robust inference conditional on the selected exposure. Skeletal muscle mass (SMM) ranked highest for handgrip strength, whereas skeletal muscle mass-to-weight ratio (SMMR) ranked highest for standing long jump and shuttle-run time. Complete-model pooled out-of-fold R² values were 0.793, 0.567, and 0.288, respectively. P90-versus-P50 contrasts were + 11.8 kg for handgrip, + 18.4 cm for jump, and − 8.27 s for shuttle-run time. Evidence of nonlinearity was strong for handgrip strength, modest for standing long jump, and absent for shuttle-run time. Predictive performance was substantially lower for shuttle-run time. These observational findings support outcome-specific associations but do not establish independent biological importance or causal effects.

Article.Title: Learning curve of distal radial access for coronary procedures: prospective, multicenter, observational study (IDEAL-BOX)
Article.Authors: Kim N.; Lee O.; Kwon Y.; Heo S.; Roh J.; Im E.; Cho D.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: While distal radial access (DRA) is increasingly used for coronary procedures, prospective data on its learning curve remain limited. We evaluated procedural outcomes in experienced and inexperienced operators. This prospective, multicenter, observational study enrolled 800 patients in whom DRA was attempted by four operators (two inexperienced and two experienced), each performing 200 cases. The primary endpoint was the trend in rates of successful coronary procedures without access-site crossover across four sequential 50-case blocks. Inexperienced operators showed a significant improvement across the case quartiles (83.0% in Q1 to 99.0% in Q4, P for trend < 0.001), whereas experienced operators maintained consistently high success rates (95.0% in Q1 to 93.0% in Q4, P for trend > 0.999). Although inexperienced operators showed a significantly lower success rate during Q1 compared to experienced operators (83.0% vs. 95.0%, P = 0.010), this inter-group difference was not significant in subsequent quartiles (Q2–Q4). No significant difference was observed in the overall procedural success rate without access-site crossover (observed, 92.5% [370/400] vs. 94.5% [378/400]; model-estimated, 94.9% vs. 95.5%, P = 0.714). The procedural success rate of inexperienced operators was lowest in the first 50 cases and did not differ significantly from that of experienced operators after 50 cases.

Article.Title: Usp14 knock down disrupts ubiquitin homeostasis unveiling the functional wiring of proteostatic, bioenergetic and DNA damage response modules
Article.Authors: Manola M.; Drakaki A.; Gianniou D.; Gumeni S.; Trougakos I.
Article.Abstract: Age-related physiological changes are primarily caused by the gradual accumulation of damaged biomolecules combined with the progressive deterioration of cellular stress responses, which then leads to systemic decline of organismal homeostasis. As cells are composed of complex protein 3D structures and machineries, organisms have developed quality control systems, namely the proteostasis network (PN), to limit loss of proteostasis, a major hallmark of aging. As part of the PN, deubiquitinase enzymes (DUBs) regulate cellular responses to proteotoxicity by controlling selective spatiotemporal protein turnover. DUBs reverse ubiquitin signaling and modulate, among other processes, ubiquitin homeostasis. In particular, Usp14 reversibly associates with the proteasome and regulates protein degradation at three distinct checkpoints, namely ubiquitin recognition, initiation of substrate translocation and ubiquitin recycling. Here, we investigated the in vivo molecular alterations that occur following Usp14 knockdown (KD) in Drosophila melanogaster . We found that Usp14 KD-mediated disruption of ubiquitin homeostasis results in graded proteostatic, mitostatic, and metabolic tissue adaptations. Interestingly, Usp14 KD also led to the accumulation of DNA damage, which activated DNA damage response mechanisms depending on the extent of Usp14 KD. These findings further highlight the Usp14’s pivotal role in modulating proteome and genome stability.

Article.Title: Motor imagery classification performance enhancement with EEG data augmentation via wasserstein generative adversarial networks
Article.Authors: Mann M.; Badoni R.; Sharma A.; Reddy C.; Stanimirović P.; Panwar D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Motor imagery electroencephalogram (MI-EEG) classification is often constrained by limited subject-specific training data. We investigated a data-augmentation framework combining continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalograms, a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP), and four-class convolutional neural network (CNN) classification. For each subject, trials were divided before preprocessing into $$80\%$$ training data and a $$20\%$$ held-out evaluation partition. The WGAN-GP was trained exclusively on training-partition scalograms, and generated samples were used only to augment CNN training. The framework was compared with Gaussian noise, rotation, shifting, SMOTE, VAE, vanilla GAN, and DCGAN augmentation. WGAN-GP achieved a mean held-out evaluation accuracy of $$75.68\%$$ , compared with $$29.69\%$$ for the real-only CNN, and attained the highest performance among the evaluated methods. Qualitative inspection, feature-space Fréchet distance, and downstream classification provided complementary evidence of synthetic-data quality and utility. Alpha- and Beta-band activity showed the strongest individual band-limited discriminability, while the complete CWT representation outperformed every isolated band. Statistical analyses showed consistent gains across subjects. These findings demonstrate the potential of WGAN-GP augmentation for improving data-limited within-subject MI-EEG classification and provide a foundation for future domain-adaptive and subject-invariant decoding methods.

Article.Title: Effects of extraction solvent and sample volume on metabolomic and lipidomic analyses of the human vitreous body
Article.Authors: Mortemousque G.; Simon C.; Dupuy C.; Lecolier N.; Lefèvre A.; Delaye J.; Oury A.; Monteiro J.; Ducloyer J.; Chicheri G.; Pisella P.; Ferguson A.; Colas Q.; Arsène S.; Emond P.; Nadal-Desbarats L.; Blasco H.; Khanna R.
Article.Abstract: Metabolomic and lipidomic profiling of the human vitreous body is challenged by limited sample availability and a lack of standardized procedures. The objective of this study was to assess the effects of extraction solvent and sample volume on the analytical coverage and repeatability of metabolomic and lipidomic profiling of a single pooled sample of human vitreous body using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS) and proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) spectroscopy. Vitreous samples were obtained from 19 adults undergoing primary vitrectomy for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, epiretinal membrane, or macular hole. All samples were homogenized into a single collective pool. Analytical performance was assessed by molecular coverage and reproducibility (coefficient of variation [CV] < 30%). With methanol extraction, 183–205 metabolites met the CV < 30% criterion across the tested volumes, including 205 metabolites at 25 µL (mean CV, 11.87%), whereas 139–178 metabolites met this criterion with acetonitrile. At low volumes (15–25 µL), 143–184 lipid species met the CV < 30% criteria with Folch extraction, with mean CVs of 16.12–16.21%; 204 lipid species met this criterion at 125 µL. Across native, filtered, and Folch-extracted vitreous preparations, 1H-NMR quantified up to 30 metabolites, with mean CVs of retained spectral buckets below 7%. Extraction solvent and sample volume influence analytical coverage and repeatability in human vitreous metabo-lipidomics, with methanol providing the highest metabolite coverage and the Folch method offering favorable lipid coverage while enabling complementary 1H-NMR analysis at low sample volumes.

Article.Authors: Kawa S.; Yoshida A.; Ueno Y.; Hashida R.; Shimozuru Y.; Ma X.; Wu X.; Watanabe T.; Ashihara N.; Nakamura A.; Oguchi T.; Ohta K.; Ota M.; Udagawa N.
Article.Abstract: Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a systemic condition characterized by elevated serum IgG4 and abundant IgG4-bearing plasma cell infiltration and is considered to have an autoimmune pathogenesis. Recombinant EII-Fru protein and its predicted a 21-amino acid epitope peptide that demonstrated specific IgG4 antibody elevation with IgG4-RD sera in ELISA. These findings suggest that EII-Fru from S. pyogenes may be a candidate target of the IgG4 antibody in IgG4-RD.

Linear discriminant analysis discriminated Florida and non-Florida morphotypes (100% resubstitution accuracy; 80–100% accuracy on small held-out random-forest test subsets), with synthlipsis width providing the strongest diagnostic character (AUC > 0.96). Based on concordant mitochondrial and nuclear evidence and geographically congruent morphological evidence, we revalidate Triatoma ambigua Neiva, 1911 stat. rev. as a distinct species within a newly defined T. sanguisuga complex and designate a neotype from the Instituto Oswaldo Cruz collection. Additional triatomine sampling in Florida and adjacent southeastern states is needed to characterize geographic boundaries. These findings have implications for Chagas disease vector surveillance in the southeastern United States.

Article.Title: Probabilistic energy management of renewable-based charging stations hub for urban electric public transportation fleets
Article.Authors: Hajizadeh M.; SeyedShenava S.; Shayeghi H.; Zare P.
Article.Abstract: Urban public transport electrification increasingly couples charging demand with variable renewable supply, creating operating conditions that deterministic station scheduling does not represent well. This work addresses that limitation through a probabilistic energy-management framework for a grid-connected charging station supplied by photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation. Solar irradiance and wind speed were represented by Beta and Weibull distributions, while fleet-side uncertainty was modeled through the initial state of charge and price-responsive charging or discharging behavior. Monte Carlo simulation generated stochastic realizations, and the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) determined 24-hour grid exchange and fleet power decisions subject to power-balance and operating constraints. The same scheduling problem was solved under deterministic and uncertainty-aware scenarios and benchmarked against four metaheuristic methods. Uncertainty raised the COA operating cost from 190.97 USD to 197.84 USD, indicating the economic effect of simultaneous supply- and demand-side variability. Even so, COA retained the lowest cost among the tested methods; under uncertainty, its cost was 15.70% below that obtained by particle swarm optimization. The stochastic results also preserved hourly power balance while capturing changes in renewable output and bidirectional fleet demand. The framework therefore provides a tractable basis for uncertainty-aware scheduling of renewable-supported public-transport charging stations and for assessing optimizer behavior under coupled generation and charging variability.

Article.Title: Structural and electronic properties of oxygen deficient HfO2-x thin films: from insulator to metal
Article.Authors: Goß K.; Gutsche A.; Bonino V.; Praxedes F.; Segura-Ruiz J.; Martínez-Criado G.; Dittmann R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hafnium oxide (HfO₂) and its oxygen-deficient variants (HfO₂₋ₓ) are key candidates for next-generation electronics, ranging from photonics and photocatalysis to both resistive and ferroelectric memories. Sub-stoichiometric HfO₂₋ₓ reduces the forming voltage in ReRAM devices and stabilizes the orthorhombic ferroelectric phase crucial for non-volatile FeRAM, yet a systematic understanding of its electronic evolution remains elusive. Here, we synthesize a complete series of HfO₂₋ₓ thin films spanning from stoichiometric oxide to pure metal and map their structural and electronic transformations. By combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, resistivity profiling, and Hf L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure, we reveal clear stoichiometry-driven trends in bonding, phase formation, and electronic structure, providing a definitive reference for tailoring HfO₂₋ₓ in advanced memory and photonic applications.

Article.Title: An experimental study on the neurological effects of hand-arm vibration: considering vibration frequency, ambient temperature, and wrist posture
Article.Authors: Aghazadeh S.; Aliabadi M.; Golmohammadi R.; Farhadian M.
Article.Abstract: Hand–arm vibration (HAV) is an occupational hazard associated with neurological and sensory disturbances. This study investigated the effects of vibration frequency, ambient temperature, and wrist posture on tactile sensory threshold and motor nerve conduction velocity (MNCV) following hand-transmitted vibration exposure. In this within-subject study, 25 construction workers completed 12 scenarios combining 10 m/s² acceleration, two vibration frequencies (31.5 and 63 Hz), two ambient temperatures (5 and 25 °C), and three wrist postures (neutral, flexion, and extension). Each scenario involved 30 min of exposure using a hand–arm vibration simulator. Median nerve MNCV was measured before and after exposure, and tactile sensory threshold was assessed using monofilament testing. Changes were analyzed using linear mixed models. All scenarios produced reduced MNCV and increased tactile threshold. The greatest MNCV reduction occurred at 31.5 Hz, 5 °C, and wrist flexion (− 2.780 ± 0.465 m/s), whereas the largest increase in tactile threshold occurred at 63 Hz, 5 °C, with wrist flexion or extension (0.533 ± 0.467 g). For tactile sensory threshold, significant main effects were observed for vibration frequency ( p < 0.001), ambient temperature ( p < 0.001), and wrist posture ( p = 0.010). For MNCV, significant main effects were also found for frequency, temperature, and wrist posture (all p < 0.001). No significant two-way or three-way interactions were observed for either outcome. Temperature had the largest effect on tactile threshold (ηp² = 0.307), while frequency had the largest effect on MNCV (ηp² = 0.606). These findings highlight the importance of vibration frequency, ambient temperature, and wrist posture in HAV risk assessment.

Article.Title: Performance-weighted ensemble learning for detecting patients with FTD and ALS from short reading tasks
Article.Authors: Ito Y.; Ohdake R.; Kato S.; Masuda M.; Suzuki M.; Watanabe H.; Sakuma T.; Ishibashi K.; Ogura A.; Hara K.; Shima S.; Mizutani Y.; Hashimoto M.; Katsuno M.; Ikeda M.; Sobue G.; Watanabe H.
Article.Abstract: We developed a novel machine learning model named performance-weighted ensemble learning (PWEL) to detect frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) using speech from word and sentence reading tasks. Overall, 197 participants (30 with FTD, 74 with ALS, and 93 healthy controls) were enrolled. The brief oral reading tasks consisted of 16 materials adapted from the Western Aphasia Battery and took 1 min to complete. For each task, 405 speech features (i.e., 384 acoustic, 17 linguistic, and 4 temporal) were extracted. Five-fold cross-validation highlighted acoustic features—especially Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients—as key discriminators of FTD and ALS from healthy controls. PWEL, which included under-bagging and adaptive task selection, achieved an area under the curve of 0.840, a sensitivity of 0.828, and an overall accuracy of 0.792. The sensitivity for FTD subtypes was 0.700–0.933, and that for ALS reached 0.812. Our proposed model surpassed both a simple ensemble learning model and task-wise classification in overall sensitivity, accuracy, and macro-F1. Its internal robustness was supported by consistent performance across stratified cross-validation folds and three recording sites. In conclusion, PWEL is practical, scalable, and making it a promising tool for detecting neurodegenerative disorders.

Article.Title: Explainable multi-agent task scheduling in vehicular edge computing using fuzzy logic and interpretable deep reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Lv Z.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: The swift expansion of latency-sensitive applications inside the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) necessitates that task scheduling exhibits both high efficiency and transparency, as well as interpretability. This research presents an explicable multi-agent framework that combines fuzzy logic with interpretable deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for intelligent job scheduling in vehicular edge computing contexts. Each agent (vehicle or edge node) assesses its local conditions—such as latency, workload, and energy status—using fuzzy logic, while the interpretable deep reinforcement learning model dynamically establishes optimal offloading and scheduling strategies. The proposed framework improves performance and explainability by utilizing explainable deep reinforcement learning architectures, including attention-based and decision-tree-embedded networks. Simulation outcomes under the evaluated simulation settings indicate that the model diminishes system latency and enhances task completion rates while preserving over 90% decision interpretability, providing a framework that demonstrates improved transparency and interpretability under the evaluated simulation settings.

Article.Title: SLIT3 promotes osteogenic differentiation in osteoarthritic subchondral bone
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Feng G.; Wang J.; Hu Z.; Yang Y.; Chen X.; Yan J.; Zhu G.; Ma L.; Jin Q.
Article.Abstract: Dysregulated osteogenic activity in subchondral bone is closely associated with osteoarthritis (OA) progression. Slit guidance ligand 3 (SLIT3) has been implicated in bone metabolism and OA-associated angiogenesis; however, its cellular distribution in OA subchondral bone and its role in osteogenic differentiation remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated microarray data from GSE51588 and single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE196678 to characterize SLIT3 expression in OA subchondral bone and validated the findings in human tibial plateau subchondral bone samples. The role of SLIT3 in osteogenic differentiation was examined using siRNA-mediated Slit3 silencing and recombinant SLIT3 treatment in MC3T3-E1 cells, while its in vivo relevance was evaluated in a destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) model using global Slit3 -knockout mice. SLIT3 expression was elevated in OA subchondral bone, was enriched in osteoblast-lineage cell clusters, and showed a progressive increase along the inferred osteogenic differentiation trajectory. In vitro, Slit3 knockdown suppressed osteogenic differentiation, whereas recombinant SLIT3 enhanced osteogenic differentiation. In vivo, global Slit3 deficiency was associated with reduced osteogenic marker expression in subchondral bone, accompanied by attenuated cartilage degeneration in the DMM model. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that SLIT3 promotes osteogenic differentiation in vitro and support a role for SLIT3 in OA-associated osteogenic alterations in subchondral bone.

Article.Title: The TOASHI multi-parameter habitability index provides a comprehensive metric for extrasolar worlds
Article.Authors: Ballester-Mauri J.; Espinós-Morató H.; Ilisie V.; Pérez-Pérez J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study introduces a planetary habitability index for exoplanets. Prior to defining the index, we analysed planetary and stellar factors that influence habitability. We reviewed existing indices and identified five sub-indices incorporating the most relevant parameters. Habitability is defined as a planet’s potential to support life, primarily determined by the presence of surface liquid water. Our index is a multiparametric score calculated as the geometric mean of several characteristics: the planet’s geophysical properties; its orbital parameters including orbital period, eccentricity, and the tidal effects; and stellar attributes, such as host star age, metallicity and incorporating a magnetic field criterion. We represent the continuous variables by an individual probability derived from a likelihood function that will be applied to the index. With respect to the parameters, the novelty of this index lies in calculating the tidal effect as a function of stellar age and in our approach to estimating stellar magnetism from the Alfvén surface. The planet’s position within its star’s habitable zone is also considered. Owing to current limitations in exoplanetary data, not all parameters are available for every confirmed exoplanet. We therefore computed the index for 588 exoplanets with complete datasets, out of NASA’s 5,867 confirmed at the moment of the study. The index ranges from 0 to 1, with Earth assigned a reference value of 1. Application of the index identified nine exoplanets with scores above 0, highlighting their potential habitability.

Article.Title: Bio-inspired mineralization of CO2 to nanoscaled hydrozincite mediated via Zea mays saccharata
Article.Authors: Masibi K.; Aligholami M.; Mohamed H.; Bucher R.; Matinise N.; Maaza M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The bio-inspired mineralization of CO 2 to single-phase Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 was demonstrated for the first time in this contribution utilising aqueous extracts of Zea mays saccharata (ZMS). The latter has been a successful chelating and capping agent. Under ambient circumstances (room temperature & atmospheric pressure), this novel method produced single-phase crystalline hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 with an average crystallite size of 38.5 nm. The UV–VIS–DRS, PL, FT-IR, XRD, and SEM–EDS studies sustained the potential of the bio-engineered nanoscaled Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 as a highly reflective material (Diffuse reflectance > 95%) and an effective blue luminescence (λ MaxEmission ≈ 457.3 nm). Electrochemical properties were investigated in 1 M NaOH electrolyte using cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). CV studies demonstrated a significant increase in current response with distinct Faradaic peaks at + 0.07 V, + 0.18 V, and − 0.16 V (vs. Ag|AgCl), confirming the inherent electrochemical activity and surface redox behaviour of the nanoparticles. This was further corroborated by EIS, which showed a substantial reduction in charge transfer resistance (R ct ) from 845.84 kΩ for the bare glassy carbon electrode (GCE) to 94.30 kΩ for the Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 modified GCE, indicating enhanced charge-transfer kinetics. These results demonstrate a bio-engineering route for synthesizing single-phase crystalline hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 nanoparticles with favorable opto-electrochemical properties, including enhanced electrochemical behaviour and charge transfer characteristics. Furthermore, the study demonstrates the feasibility of CO 2 mineralization to hydrozincite under ambient conditions.

Article.Title: Computationally designed multisubtype epigraph vaccine confers broad-spectrum protection against H1 and H3 swine influenza A viruses
Article.Authors: Madapong A.; Wiggins J.; Weaver E.
Article.Abstract: H1 and H3 subtype swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) threaten global agricultural economies and pose zoonotic risks, yet conventional vaccines provide limited protection against their vast antigenic diversity. Here, we developed a multisubtype vaccine utilizing adenoviral vectors expressing computationally designed H1 and H3 epigraph hemagglutinin (HA) immunogens. In mice, this All-in-One formulation elicited balanced humoral and cellular immunity and demonstrated neutralizing breadth against diverse IAV-S isolates compared to a commercially available vaccine. The multisubtype delivery system elicited concurrent immunity and protection against both H1 and H3 subtypes. The All-in-One vaccine conferred protection against heterologous H1 and H3 challenges and did not exacerbate clinical morbidity characteristic of mismatched vaccination. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of computationally optimized and multiplexed vaccines providing broad-spectrum protection against evolving influenza viruses without compromising safety.

Article.Title: LMTSDet: a lightweight Mamba-transformer detector with spatial-spectral fusion and feature calibration for real-time traffic sign detection
Article.Authors: Zhang G.; Feng L.; Bai L.; Zhao J.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Traffic sign detectors must preserve small-object detail and scene context under strict latency and memory constraints. We developed LMTSDet, an RT-DETR-based detector that uses the published MobileMamba backbone and three task-specific components. The Spatial-Spectral Fusion Module combines state-space spatial modeling with frequency-domain modulation, the Feature Calibration Module recalibrates directional spatial responses, and the Spatial Calibration Fusion Network aggregates calibrated multi-scale features. Structured channel pruning, knowledge distillation, and fine-tuning further reduce the deployment cost. On TT100K, LMTSDet achieves 92.8% mAP@0.5 with 12.1M parameters and 28.6 GFLOPs. The compressed model retains 91.5% mAP@0.5 and reaches 156 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT FP16. On GTSDB, direct transfer and target-domain fine-tuning yield 87.3% and 93.0% AP@0.5, respectively. These results indicate that LMTSDet provides a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off across the evaluated settings, although performance on adverse-weather and more diverse regional datasets remains to be established.

Article.Title: ACO based hybrid SM-BS control of DFIG: experimental demonstration of improved dynamic performance under variable wind
Article.Authors: Echiheb F.; El Youssfi N.; Alqunun K.; Albaker A.; Alshammari B.; Guesmi T.; Bossoufi B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs) are widely used in modern wind energy systems due to their capability to efficiently extract energy over a wide range of wind speeds while enabling independent control of active and reactive power. However, ensuring high-performance operation under variable wind conditions remains challenging for conventional control strategies, which often fail to guarantee robustness, dynamic stability, and accurate power tracking simultaneously. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid control strategy combining sliding mode control (SMC) and backstepping (BS) control, with optimal tuning achieved using the ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm. The proposed approach leverages the robustness of SMC and the smooth dynamic behavior of BS control, while reducing the chattering effect through optimized gain selection. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations under realistic wind speed variations. Results demonstrate improved active and reactive power tracking, enhanced energy capture, and better power quality injected into the grid. Furthermore, the feasibility of the proposed method is validated experimentally using a dSPACE DS1104 real-time platform, confirming its practical applicability.

Article.Title: Co-RoboPV: cooperative aerial robot system for photovoltaic power plant inspection based on reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Aghamohammadi A.; Esmailifar S.; Kolahi M.; Sizkouhi A.; Aghaei M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient inspection of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants can be significantly improved by employing a multi-aerial robot system. This article aims to develop an algorithm tailored to such a system for coverage path planning. Our approach involves determining the optimal number and types of aerial robots, designing a detailed flight plan, preparing the robots and their equipment, and analyzing the data collected from inspections. Autonomous operation is critical for enhancing efficiency and accuracy by eliminating direct human control of aerial robot flight. To this end, we utilize Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to train aerial robots to navigate and perform inspection tasks effectively. The proposed algorithm focuses on optimizing path coverage to ensure comprehensive inspections of PV plants. Our methodology includes training aerial robots with extensive data to navigate safely and efficiently across the PV field. Results indicate that the DRL-based algorithm significantly improves coverage and operational efficiency in the inspection process, demonstrating the potential of advanced learning techniques for enhancing multi-aerial robot systems.

Article.Title: Psychometric assessment of visual enclosure and walkability in intermediate urban spaces through virtual reality
Article.Authors: Belkacem M.; Abdelhakim H.; Nadia L.; Aya A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban environments are complex systems influenced by spatial, visual, and functional factors. Walkability assessments often depend on subjective opinions and symmetric distance-to-height ratios, assuming that streets are framed by similar surfaces on both sides. This study used immersive virtual reality (VR) to examine visual enclosure in intermediate spaces, while maintaining a consistent stimulus for all participants and a 360° experience. Fifty-nine panoramas, taken at twenty stations along a 1.5 km route in Batna, Algeria, were converted into achromatic line images. Each station was coded for boundary type and two signed asymmetry indices, geometric and material. Ninety-six architecture students completed a twenty-item questionnaire at each station; fifteen items formed five reliable sub-scales, and the medium was widely accepted (92.7%). Participants reported both enclosure (80%) and openness (96%), which seemed to coexist, but rated legibility poorly. In an ordinal mixed model, greater permeability asymmetry between the two boundaries was linked to less favorable ratings (OR = 0.597, 95% CI 0.393–0.906), while geometric indicators were not; 3.5% of the variance was between stations. These exploratory findings, from a single route and a student sample, suggest that boundary permeability may deserve attention alongside height in street design, and that immersive assessment provides a practical way to study how urban space is experienced.

Article.Title: Structural insights into bromodomain-containing complexes from Trypanosoma cruzi revealed by proximity labeling and stoichiometric space exploration
Article.Authors: Rodríguez Araya E.; Martínez Peralta G.; Alonso V.; Serra E.
Article.Abstract: Trypanosoma cruzi , the etiological agent of Chagas disease, remains a major health concern due to the limited efficacy and toxicity of current treatments. Bromodomain factors (BDFs), which recognize acetylated lysine residues, are key components of epigenetic regulatory machinery and represent promising therapeutic targets. Despite their importance, structural organization of bromodomain-containing complexes in trypanosomatids is poorly understood. In this study, we combined experimental and computational approaches to investigate the composition and stoichiometry of BDF-containing complexes in T. cruzi . Using TurboID-based proximity labeling, we mapped interaction networks for five BDFs (BDF3, BDF4, BDF5, BDF6 and BDF8) and identified two major complexes, CRKT and NuA4. To further resolve their architecture, we applied structure prediction methods that explore multiple stoichiometric configurations. Our analyses indicate that CRKT is organized into three modules with distinct interaction dynamics, whereas NuA4 comprises two modules. The CRKT core module displays a symmetric arrangement containing two copies of BDF3, BDF5, and BDF8. Its catalytic module contains three subunits including HAT2, while the BET module contains BDF4 and BDF1. In NuA4, the catalytic module resembles the yeast piccolo-NuA4 complex and includes HAT1, with the TINTIN module associating via BDF6. These findings provide structural insights into epigenetic complexes in trypanosomatids and support their potential as drug targets.

Article.Title: Aster-derived biogenic silver nanoparticles for multifaceted study on antioxidant, para-nitrophenol catalysis, cytotoxicity, and in silico molecular docking evaluation
Article.Authors: Thahir A.; Kandiah M.; Gunaratne B.; Perera O.
Article.Abstract: Advancements in nanotechnology have expanded its prospects as a promising avenue for addressing concerns over environmental remediation, sustainability, and industrial waste management through the development of metal-based nanoparticles. This study reports the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using four varieties of Aster flowers (white, pink, lavender, and violet) and their potential for antioxidants, catalytic, cytotoxic, and in silico molecular docking activities. The UV–Vis spectral analysis confirmed successful AgNP formation under optimal conditions of 90 °C for 30 min. Comprehensive characterization of A_Whi_AgNPs using scanning electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, X-ray diffraction, and energy-dispersive X-ray analysis confirmed crystalline face-centered cubic structures, spherical morphology and 61.0% Ag. Catalytic degradation of p-nitrophenol demonstrated concentration-dependent catalytic activity; complete degradation within 25 min for 10 µL of 4000 ppm AgNPs and instantaneous degradation with 50 µL, with A_Vio_AgNP achieving the highest rate constant ( k = 0.4346 min⁻ 1 ). The AgNPs showed high Artemia salina viability at 200 ppm and 800 ppm, whereas zebrafish embryo exposure revealed model- and exposure-time-dependent toxicity. In silico molecular docking studies revealed a stable interaction with the Ag 3 cluster and amino acid residues in the epidermal growth factor receptor (PDB: 1M17), yielding the highest binding energy (-1.24 kcal/mol). These findings indicate that Aster -derived AgNPs possess multifaceted properties and strong catalytic activity, with effective applicability in bioremediation and industrial wastewater treatment.

Article.Title: Polymetallic nodules provide a distinct habitat for abyssal meiofauna
Article.Authors: Diaz-Recio Lorenzo C.; Stratmann T.; de Wilt M.; Radhakrishnan R.; Macheriotou L.; Pape E.; Hoogerdijk L.; van den Hooven-Iza N.; Krüger J.; Kaspersmeier L.; Neuser M.; Klöckner M.; Lauth M.; Schaper M.; Patel T.; Gollner S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep-sea abyssal plains harbour extensive biodiversity, much of which remains undocumented. Polymetallic nodules in the abyssal plains of the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), Central Pacific, harbour diverse meiofaunal communities within their crevices, representing an understudied habitat. Given their high concentrations of nickel, copper, and cobalt, nodules are currently one of the primary targets for the extraction of deep-sea mineral resources. Here, we characterise the physical properties of polymetallic nodules, quantify their meiofaunal crevice communities, and compare them to those from the nearby sediments. We show that nodules contain internal cracks and microfossils, that their crevices harbour meiofaunal communities dominated by nematodes and copepods, and that faunal abundance increases significantly with nodule volume. Foraminifera were also a recurrent component of nodule-crevice assemblages. Nodule-crevice nematode and copepod abundances were equivalent to approximately 10% and 25%, respectively, of those recorded in nearby sediments across the two exploration contract areas in the eastern CCZ. Based on 18S rRNA data, nematode and copepod assemblages recovered from nodule crevices differed from those recovered from nearby sediments collected during the same expedition and within the same exploration contract areas. Our findings, therefore, demonstrate the presence of nodule-associated crevice fauna and the consequent risk of biodiversity loss associated with nodule removal through potential future commercial mining.

Article.Title: A novel fluorescent ocular tracer enables detection of TDP-43 pathology in ALS and related TDP-43 proteinopathies using retinal imaging
Article.Authors: Pilotte J.; Mandel Z.; Sharma S.; Khoury S.; Huang A.; Tafreshi A.; Vanderklish P.; Weinreb R.; Reiman E.; Frosch M.; Svendsen C.; Ly C.; Harris B.; Berry J.; Cudkowicz M.; Sarraf S.
Article.Abstract: Molecular biomarkers of neurodegenerative disease are positioned to facilitate earlier diagnosis and treatment, therapeutic development, and define disease heterogeneities that inform precision interventions. The retina, an optically accessible extension of the central nervous system, manifests biomarkers for many neurodegenerative diseases, providing an opportunity for simple, non-invasive detection. This study evaluates a new method to fluorescently label retinal deposits associated with TDP-43 pathology, a key biomarker of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE), using a prototype of a clinical-stage small molecule, AMDX-8050. In cadaveric ALS retinas, AMDX-8050 labeled cytoplasmic retinal deposits that co-localized with TDP-43 pathology and revealed a dense and spatially varied distribution of deposits resembling those observed in matched spinal cord and motor cortex cadaver tissues. Additionally, AMDX-8050 labeled deposits that co-localized with TDP-43 pathology in retinas from FTD-TDP-43 and LATE cadaver tissues. These results support the potential of a new class of retinal tracers with broad utility for the TDP-43 proteinopathies.
