Article.Title: Leisure-time sedentary behaviour and kidney function decline over 12 years in Australian adults with and without type 2 diabetes
Article.Authors: Dzakpasu F.; Kosaki K.; Owen N.; Brakenridge C.; Carver A.; Chadban S.; Chandrabose M.; Dempsey P.; Polkinghorne K.; Sethi P.; Wheeler M.; Dunstan D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A common leisure-time sedentary behaviour – television (TV)-viewing time – has been associated with kidney dysfunction; however, the longitudinal associations and moderating roles of type 2 diabetes remain underexplored. We examined relationships of 12-year declines in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR: kidney function) with changes in TV-viewing time (and explored potential joint associations with physical inactivity and gender differences) in adult Australians with and without type 2 diabetes. Australian Diabetes, Obesity and Lifestyle Study (AusDiab) data from 6220 baseline participants [mean (standard deviation): age = 50.7 (12.7) years; waist circumference = 90.3 (13.7) cm; 54.2% women] with five-year or 12-year follow-up data, or both, were analysed; eGFR, TV-viewing time, physical inactivity (<150 min/week self-reported physical activity), and glucose metabolism status (normal glucose metabolism, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes) were assessed at each observation time point. Multilevel modelling used age (centred at 50 years) as the time metric to estimate the rate of eGFR decline and the association with TV-viewing time, as well as the potential moderation by the presence of type 2 diabetes, physical inactivity, and gender, adjusting for potential sociodemographic and clinical confounders. Participants’ mean eGFR decreased, and mean TV-viewing time increased during the 12-year study period. Those with type 2 diabetes had lower eGFR and higher TV-viewing time at each time point compared to those without type 2 diabetes (prediabetes and normal glucose metabolism). At age 50, the mean eGFR was approximately 98 mL/min/1.73m 2 [Main: 97.6 (95% CI: 97.2 to 98.0); Sensitivity (analysis excluded those with chronic kidney disease at baseline, N = 5782): 98.0 (95% CI: 97.6 to 98.4)], which declined by about 0.80 mL/min/1.73m 2 /year [Main: -0.78 (95% CI: -0.80 to -0.77); Sensitivity: -0.79 (95% CI: -0.81 to -0.78)]. Increasing TV-viewing time was significantly associated with eGFR decline [Main: -0.022 (95% CI: -0.031 to -0.013); Sensitivity: -0.024 (95% CI: -0.033 to -0.015)] and was more pronounced in those with type 2 diabetes [Main: -0.037 (95% CI: -0.068 to -0.006); Sensitivity: -0.041 (95% CI: -0.073 to -0.009)]. The association was potentially stronger in those physically inactive at any given time compared to those physically active [Main: -0.015 (95% CI: -0.031 to 0.000), Sensitivity: -0.018 (95% CI: -0.034 to -0.001)], and was also stronger in women than in men [Main: -0.020 (95% CI: -0.039 to -0.002); Sensitivity: -0.029 (95% CI: -0.048 to -0.010)]. Among community-dwelling Australian adults, increasing TV-viewing time was associated with a greater rate of kidney function decline, which was heightened in the presence of type 2 diabetes. The relationship may also be stronger in those who were physically inactive and in women. These longitudinal relationships strengthen the evidence base for kidney health on the detrimental effects of excessive sedentary behaviour, particularly in those living with type 2 diabetes, those physically inactive, and in women. They further reinforce the clinical and public health importance of meeting recommended sedentary behaviour and physical activity guidelines.

Article.Title: A dynamically consistent NSFD scheme for an SIS epidemic model with vaccination and variable population
Article.Authors: Ahmed N.; Jawaz M.; Raza A.; Baleanu D.; Almutairi S.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates a sequential nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) approximation of an established SIS vaccination model with variable population. Disease-free and endemic stability are classified by the spectral abscissa in four parameter planes. The continuous model does not exhibit backward bifurcation, and the threshold \(\mathcal {R}_0=1\) separates disease elimination from the existence of a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium. The proposed sequential NSFD scheme preserves nonnegativity and the equilibrium set and reproduces the disease-free threshold exactly for every positive step size. First-order consistency and finite-time convergence are established, while discrete stability is examined through the spectral radius of the full discrete Jacobian. Numerical experiments near the threshold, with \(\mathcal {R}_0=0.99\) and \(\mathcal {R}_0=1.01\) , show the expected slow transients and the transition from decay to persistence. Comparisons with the forward Euler and fourth-order Runge-Kutta methods show that these standard explicit schemes may lose positivity or stability for larger step sizes, whereas the NSFD scheme retains the qualitative properties established analytically. These results provide a structure-preserving numerical treatment of the SIS vaccination model.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic profiling of chicken kidneys reveals host response to infection by the Iranian nephropathogenic IS/1494/06-like IBV
Article.Authors: Aghaiyan L.; Hosseini H.; Ziafati Kafi Z.; Fallah Mehrabadi M.; Ghalyanchilangeroudi A.
Article.Abstract: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) is a major avian coronavirus with nephropathogenic potential. The renal transcriptional response to Iranian IS/1494/06-like (Variant-2, GI-23) IBV remains insufficiently characterized. We conducted exploratory bulk RNA-seq using one pooled kidney-RNA library per condition, generated from 10 experimentally infected and 10 control specific-pathogen-free chickens to characterize antiviral and immune-associated expression patterns, renal metabolic and homeostatic pathways, and the viral RNA profile. Gene expression was analyzed exploratorily, and an alternative alignment-based workflow assessed computational consistency. The infected pooled library showed higher expression and enrichment of antiviral and immune-associated programs, including interferon signaling, cytokine and chemokine activity, antigen presentation, and complement-related pathways. In contrast, genes with negative expression changes were associated with lipid metabolism and membrane/vesicle-related annotations, with specific transport and TGF-β/SMAD findings remaining exploratory. Viral RNA mapping showed a 3′-biased, N-dominant read profile in the infected kidney library, with only a low-level viral-aligned read signal in the control library. Together, these findings identify candidate immune-associated and renal metabolic transcriptional patterns associated with IS/1494/06-like IBV infection. Without biological replication or independent experimental validation of RNA-seq expression findings, these observations remain hypothesis-generating and require targeted experimental confirmation in replicated studies.

Article.Title: Hybrid diffusion–DE-based 3D UAV deployment for joint coverage enhancement and energy efficiency in IoT networks
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Li S.; Xie C.; He Q.; Pan H.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted communication has become a key enabler for next-generation wireless networks, particularly in post-disaster recovery and remote-area connectivity. A major challenge lies in jointly maximizing the coverage of Internet of Things devices (IoTDEs) while minimizing the energy consumption of UAV base stations (UAV-BSs). To address this issue, we propose a novel hybrid 3D deployment algorithm, termed D3E, which achieves an effective balance between communication coverage and energy efficiency. First, a dynamic UAV coverage model is established by characterizing the relationship between flight altitude and coverage radius under realistic air-to-ground channel conditions. Building upon this model, we develop a hybrid optimization framework that integrates the global exploration capability of Differential Evolution (DE) with the generative sampling power of a diffusion model. The proposed D3E algorithm simultaneously optimizes UAV positions, transmit power, and energy consumption while ensuring the required communication quality for IoTDEs. Extensive simulations across multiple environments demonstrate that D3E significantly improves IoTDE coverage and achieves better energy–coverage trade-offs compared with existing deployment strategies, validating its effectiveness for UAV-assisted IoT communication networks.

Article.Title: Intermolecular coherent interference and topological modulation of electronic gaps in protein dimers
Article.Authors: Mousavi H.; Emami R.
Article.Abstract: We present a systematic tight-binding investigation of the electronic structure of interacting lattice protein models, focusing on how internal hydrogen-bond topology, intermolecular contact configuration, and temperature collectively govern intermolecular hybridization. Three distinct protein conformations with non-equivalent hydrogen-bond distributions are constructed to examine how graph-theoretic connectivity reshapes monomer Hamiltonians and modulates dimer spectral properties. The composite Hamiltonian is diagonalized to obtain the electronic spectrum, and the density of states is evaluated using the retarded Green’s function formalism. The results reveal that the HOMO-LUMO gap is governed by two complementary mechanisms. First, topology-dependent coherent coupling between multiple intermolecular contact points produces constructive or destructive interference among tunneling pathways, resulting in a systematic dependence of the gap on the number and configuration of contact points within the specific dimer configurations studied. Second, temperature induces a renormalization of the effective hopping amplitudes through thermally induced lattice fluctuations, thereby reducing the magnitude of intermolecular hybridization. While thermal effects reduce the absolute gap magnitudes, they preserve the relative hierarchy imposed by the static hydrogen-bond architecture. Moreover, gap ordering across homodimers and heterodimers is determined not by contact number alone, but by the compatibility of frontier-state amplitudes at the intermolecular interface. These findings illustrate, within the specific protein-dimer configurations investigated here, how coherent multi-channel interference, hydrogen-bond topology, and temperature-dependent electronic coupling jointly shape the low-energy electronic structure of biomolecular assemblies.

Article.Title: Improved Levenberg–Marquardt Algorithm for inverse kinematics of rock drilling manipulators
Article.Authors: Du Z.
Article.Abstract: The inverse kinematics of a non-Pieper seven-degree-of-freedom rock drilling manipulator has no analytical solution. Its configuration consists of five revolute joints and two prismatic joints, which cannot be solved by arm-angle parameterization, making numerical methods an inevitable choice. However, existing numerical methods still have deficiencies in joint limit constraint handling, redundancy utilization, and cold-start initial value selection, making it difficult to satisfy the requirements of rock drilling operations. This paper systematically investigates numerical solution methods for this problem. First, a D–H kinematic model is established, and its redundancy characteristics and solving difficulties are analyzed. Subsequently, the solution performances of the pseudoinverse method, the damped least squares method, and the Levenberg–Marquardt method are compared. The results show that the standard LM method achieves the best overall performance in terms of accuracy and convergence speed, but still has deficiencies in joint limit constraint handling and redundancy utilization. To address these issues, an improved LM algorithm is proposed that integrates an interior-point penalty function, null-space redundancy optimization, and a weighted multi-prior warm-start strategy into a unified framework. A logarithmic barrier function embeds joint limits into the optimization objective, ensuring that the iteration remains within the feasible region at all times. By projecting auxiliary objectives onto the Jacobian null space, the redundant degree of freedom is actively utilized to improve motion smoothness while maintaining end-effector accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduces the joint limit violation rate, improves trajectory tracking smoothness, and enhances the cold-start success rate while maintaining end-effector positioning accuracy. This study provides a feasible technical solution for inverse kinematics solving of non-Pieper redundant manipulators.

Article.Title: Generalizing the LoD transition space for continuous multi-scale representation using straight skeletons
Article.Authors: Gholami A.; Boguslawski P.; Meijers M.
Article.Abstract: Continuous multi-scale representation enables geographic features to evolve smoothly across Levels of Detail, avoiding abrupt transitions between independently generalized datasets. However, existing approaches provide limited support for complex transformations involving different geometric and topological configurations. This study generalizes the LoD Transition Space framework to represent continuous transformations between polygons, polylines, and points. The proposed approach uses straight-skeleton-based geometric primitives to construct continuous 2D + 1D transition volumes and decomposes complex transformations into localized LoD Transition Regions. The framework supports polygon-to-boundary-polyline, polyline-to-polyline, polygon-to-polygon, and N-to-M polygon transformations, including aggregation, merging, splitting, simplification, and collapsing. Horizontal slicing of the resulting 3D models generates intermediate representations at arbitrary LoD values. The implemented case studies show that the framework can represent a broad range of regular and irregular transformations under the supported input configurations; remaining disjoint, touching, and other exceptional relationships are explicitly treated as current limitations rather than as solved cases. The proposed 3D model provides a unified representation for continuous map generalization and supports the generation of consistent intermediate representations across scales.

Article.Title: Comparative performance of binary and ternary cementitious mixtures containing aluminum flue dust and steel dust
Article.Authors: Iqbal J.; Hong L.; Lal R.; Sikandar M.; Bashir M.; MAKOBERO B.; Khan M.; Basit A.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the effects of aluminum flue dust (AFD) and steel dust (SD) as partial cement-replacement materials on the fresh-state, mechanical, durability, and microstructural properties of cement pastes and mortars. To achieve this objective, binary and ternary mixtures were produced by incorporating 5–20 wt% of AFD and SD relative to cement in cement pastes and mortars. The results showed that AFD accelerated the setting time because of its high alumina content, whereas SD delayed hydration because of the iron oxide content in its composition. The incorporation of AFD and SD reduced drying shrinkage; at 400 days, the reductions relative to the control mortar (356 µε) were approximately 5.62% for AFD20, 11.52% for AFD10SD10, and 15.45% for SD20. However, increasing AFD and SD replacement also reduced compressive strength, flexural strength, and ultrasonic pulse velocity. Durability tests revealed enhanced resistance to chemical attack. After 180 days of exposure, SD20, AFD20, and AFD10SD10 exhibited approximately 2.8%, 16.7%, and 5.6% lower weight loss, respectively, in hydrochloric acid, and approximately 11.4%, 35.7%, and 24.3% lower weight loss, respectively, in sodium sulfate solution, compared with the control mortar. The improvement in chemical durability is attributed to the lower formation of calcium hydroxide, which is highly susceptible to leaching. These results indicate that AFD and SD may support waste recycling and the circular economy through partial cement replacement, reduced Portland cement demand, and diversion of industrial waste from disposal; however, environmental safety and life-cycle benefits require separate verification.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of dexmedetomidine, diazepam, and acepromazine as adjuvants to lidocaine in intravenous regional anaesthesia in goats
Article.Authors: Salem M.; Sharshar A.; Hassan M.; Alguzo A.
Article.Abstract: Intravenous regional anaesthesia (IVRA) is a safe, dependable, and economical method for regional anaesthesia for distal limb surgeries in ruminants. This study aimed to compare the effects of dexmedetomidine, diazepam, and acepromazine as an adjuvant to lidocaine in intravenous regional anaesthesia in goats. This study was conducted on 24 healthy male goats, in which IVRA of the distal hind limb was carried out. The animals were divided into four groups ( n = 6): lidocaine alone (Lido group), lidocaine–acepromazine (Lid/ACP), lidocaine–diazepam (Lid/DIZ), and lidocaine–dexmedetomidine (Lid/DEX). Physiological parameters (heart rate, respiratory rate, rectal temperature, peripheral oxygen saturation), biochemical parameters (glucose, lactic acid, cortisol, and IL-6), and sensory and motor block onset and duration were assessed at time 0 before tourniquet application, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 60 min during application of the tourniquet, and 5, 10, 20, 30 min after its removal. In comparison to the other groups, the Lido/DEX group had the longest duration of sensory (82.5 ± 1.1 min) and motor (83.9 ± 0.8 min) blockade, as well as the earliest onset of sensory (1.3 ± 0.1 min) and motor (1.4 ± 0.1 min) blockade. Additionally, during the procedure, dexmedetomidine offered better control over stress and inflammatory reactions. In conclusion, dexmedetomidine seems to be the best adjuvant to lidocaine for IVRA in goats, offering greater anesthetic quality, longer analgesia, and better management of inflammatory and stress reactions both during and after tourniquet application.

Article.Title: Experimental study on the shear strength and disintegration resistance of MICP-treated granite residual soil
Article.Authors: Liang J.; Qiao Y.; Zeng Z.; Pan G.; Li L.; Feng D.
Article.Abstract: To clarify the mechanisms by which microbial-induced calcite precipitation (MICP) stabilizes granite residual soil, this study investigates how clay content and treatment protocol affect its mechanical behavior and water stability. Soil samples formulated with distinct clay fractions were subjected to diverse MICP protocols and subsequently assessed through direct shear tests, disintegration experiments, and microscopic characterizations. The experimental outcomes indicate that bio-cementation effectively upgrades the overall structural integrity and hydro-durability of the matrices. Quantitatively, the biomineralization process yielded a dramatic 96.19% amplification in cohesion, alongside a 7.7% increment in the internal friction angle. Moreover, the evolution of shearing resistance displays a non-monotonic relationship with the clay fraction; as the fine-particle proportion increases, the shear strength initially diminishes—reaching a minimum at a 20% clay level—before escalating to its peak at a 40% clay content. In terms of disintegration resistance, while raw control specimens suffered total structural collapse within merely one minute of water immersion, the soils stabilized via a hybrid mixing and grouting MICP approach exhibited exceptional resilience with zero disintegration. Microscopic observations confirm that this integrated bio-treatment stimulates abundant calcium carbonate precipitation. These biogenic crystals fundamentally drive the macroscopic physical upgrades by occupying interstitial voids and firmly bridging adjacent soil aggregates. Moreover, the LFNMR (Low Field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance) test results demonstrate that MICP intervention efficiently diminishes the volume of both micro and total pores, promoting the understanding of MICP solidification mechanism from the calcium carbonate cementation at the macroscale to the pore structure at the microscale.

Article.Title: Radical prostatectomy outcomes in men aged 75 or older with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Zhou P.; Zhang Y.; Chen Z.; Zhang Z.; Feng X.; Ren Y.
Article.Abstract: We evaluated whether radical prostatectomy is safe and effective in elderly patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. We retrospectively analyzed 757 patients at four Chinese tertiary centers (2012–2022): 201 aged 75 or older, 556 younger. Elderly patients had longer operative time (165 vs. 155 min, p = 0.002), greater blood loss (350 vs. 280 mL, p < 0.001), and more Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher complications (8.0% vs. 3.8%, p = 0.018), but 30-day mortality was 0.5%. Pathological characteristics, including stage distribution, were broadly similar. At five years, biochemical recurrence-free survival was 72% vs. 79% (hazard ratio 1.32, p = 0.021), cancer-specific survival 94% vs. 95% (hazard ratio 1.45, p = 0.203), overall survival 88% vs. 96% (hazard ratio 2.18, p < 0.001), and metastasis-free survival 91% vs. 93% (hazard ratio 1.56, p = 0.028). Most deaths in elderly patients were non-cancer related (13 of 25). Propensity matching and weighting preserved effect directions, although evidence weakened in some adjusted analyses (weighted recurrence p = 0.053; competing-risk p = 0.062). A recurrence nomogram showed modest discrimination (C-index 0.63). Radical prostatectomy is feasible in carefully selected fit older patients, but age alone should not guide decisions; comorbidity and life expectancy must be considered.

Article.Title: Genome-wide diversity profiling and de-correlated composite selection mapping reveal the adaptive genomic landscape of Mithun (Bos frontalis)
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Vyas J.; Kumar I.; Nirwan A.; Nath S.; Illa S.; Yata V.; Mugaiahgari B.; Narapureddy B.; Ifelebuegu A.; Bukke S.
Article.Abstract: Mithun (Bos frontalis), also known as Gayal, is a culturally and economically important bovine of the Eastern Himalayan and Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot whose genomic diversity and adaptive architecture remain incompletely understood. We investigated genome-wide diversity, population structure and selection signatures using Illumina BovineSNP50 v1 genotypes initially available for 21 Mithun. Removal of duplicate or near-duplicate samples and stringent marker filtering retained 17 non-redundant individuals and 11,546 autosomal SNPs. Mean observed and expected heterozygosity were 0.1845 and 0.1823, respectively, while the mean minor allele frequency was 0.1190. PCA and ADMIXTURE indicated no strong discrete subdivision within Mithun, although one individual (GAYA14) showed a distinct admixed genomic profile in joint analyses with Gaur, Yak, indicine and taurine cattle. Primary selection analysis was therefore performed in 16 individuals and evaluated by sensitivity analyses. A de-correlated composite of multiple signals (DCMS) integrating |iHS|, rEHH, H12, Tajima’s D and nucleotide diversity identified four FDR-significant loci on chromosomes 3, 4, 19 and 25. Three loci remained significant when GAYA14 was included, while all four were retained under an alternative H12 window definition. Annotation of the four 1-Mb candidate regions identified 25 named protein-coding genes, including KCNA2, KCNA3, CHIA, CHI3L2, GRM8, ACE, KCNH6 and TANC2. Functional enrichment highlighted voltage-gated potassium-channel activity and chitin binding, and network analysis prioritized KCNA3, KCNA2, CD53, DENND2D, DCAF7, ACE, CHIA, CHI3L2, KCNH6 and TANC2 as candidate hub genes. The candidate regions overlapped 147 Animal QTLdb records representing 64 traits, with milk and meat/carcass categories most frequently represented. These findings provide a cautious genomic framework for understanding diversity and candidate adaptive loci in Mithun and for guiding future conservation and higher-resolution genomic studies.

Article.Title: Time adaptive clinical data driven cardiovascular disease detection using multi-objective features-based residual CapsNet with coordinate attention
Article.Authors: Amalraj J.; Kumaresan T.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, primarily caused by blockages in coronary arteries due to plaques or fatty deposits. Early identification and precise diagnosis are crucial for timely treatment, reducing disease severity, improving patient quality of life, and preventing complications. Objective: To develop an advanced, interpretable, and accurate CVD detection framework that addresses limitations in conventional methods related to feature representation and capturing complex relationships within the data. The model initiates with data cleaning to eliminate errors and inconsistencies, followed by Dynamic Gaussian Piecewise Normalization (DGPN) to handle heterogeneous and complex datasets, thereby improving feature representation. Multiobjective Weighted Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBM) extract salient features, with weights optimized via a Revised Fitness-Oriented Bobcat Optimization Algorithm (RFO-BOA) employing multi-objective functions. An Adaptive Residual Capsule Network enhanced with Coordinate Attention (ARCCA) is employed to identify complex spatial and hierarchical patterns, increasing detection accuracy. The parameters of ARCCA are finely tuned through RFO-BOA to further elevate performance. Extensive experiments conducted on two benchmark cardiovascular datasets demonstrate the robustness and efficacy of the proposed model. The RFO-BOA–ARCCA approach achieved significant accuracy improvements of approximately 15.94%, 2.56%, 8.12%, and 3.89% over traditional models, including ANN, LSTM, SVM, and CapsNet, respectively. The integrated framework combining advanced data preprocessing, multi-objective feature extraction, and an optimized capsule network effectively facilitates early and accurate CVD detection. This framework holds promise for real-time clinical applications, enabling improved patient outcomes.

Article.Title: Renewable-energy distribution network fault recognition via dynamic hypergraph diffusion residual learning
Article.Authors: Zhao R.; Lu J.; Guo W.; Li H.; Li Y.; Pan K.; Yu Q.
Article.Abstract: Fault identification in renewable-energy-integrated distribution networks is primarily challenged by two coupled issues: learning discriminative representations from dynamically reconfigured, high-order network topologies and maintaining robust classification under limited or imbalanced fault labels, measurement disturbances, and incomplete observations. To address these challenges, this study proposes a dynamic hypergraph diffusion prototype network, termed DHDP-Net. The framework consists of a dynamic hypergraph feature extraction module, a masked temporal diffusion encoding module, and a soft-threshold prototype identification module. The dynamic hypergraph module integrates physical connectivity with data-driven node correlations to capture high-order spatial dependencies among buses, feeders, and power-supply regions under topology variations. The masked temporal diffusion module combines masked reconstruction with a temporal transformer denoiser to learn normal temporal evolution patterns and extract fault-sensitive residuals from reconstruction deviations. Learnable soft thresholding suppresses weak residual responses caused by renewable energy fluctuations and measurement disturbances, while prototype matching constructs stable category representations in a discriminative metric space, improving fault identification when labeled samples are limited or unevenly distributed. Experiments on the IEEE 123-bus system and SMART-DS show that DHDP-Net achieves Macro F1 scores of 98.41 and 97.02%, respectively. Under degraded measurement conditions with a 30% measurement-missing ratio, the proposed model retains Macro F1 scores of 95.82 and 95.48%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 3.51 and 4.62 percentage points, respectively. Ablation, computational-efficiency, and parameter-sensitivity studies further verify the effectiveness of the proposed architecture. These results demonstrate that DHDP-Net provides a topology-aware and robust solution for fault identification under limited-label and degraded-measurement conditions.

Article.Title: Umbilical cord blood plasma-derived small extracellular vesicles attenuate the immune response as a novel therapy for type 1 diabetes
Article.Authors: Zhao L.; Sun J.; Yi S.; Lei Y.; Liu C.; Giordano F.; Xu N.; Wang H.; Hu W.; Yu H.
Article.Abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) from cord blood–derived stem cells exert therapeutic effects on both degenerative and autoimmune diseases. Cord blood plasma, a ‘by-product’ of mononuclear cell collection, has demonstrated its potential in the treatment of degenerative diseases. Notably, sEVs derived from cord blood plasma (CB-sEVs) play a therapeutic role in regulating tissue regeneration. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effect of CB-sEVs on type 1 diabetes (T1D). Our data showed that CB-sEVs reduced the incidence of diabetes onset in adoptive-transfer T1D mice, lowered blood glucose levels, and alleviated pancreatic beta-cell inflammation. Furthermore, CB-sEVs significantly inhibited human T cell proliferation following activation with anti-CD3/CD28 beads in vitro. Furthermore, we observed a proportionate decrease of effector T cells and central memory T cells, whereas the percentage of naïve T cells was significantly increased. Additionally, miRNA profiling of CB-sEVs revealed distinct miRNA signatures, providing insights into the active molecular components of CB-sEVs that may drive their therapeutic effects. These findings suggest that CB-sEVs represents a novel promising therapy for T1D.

Article.Title: Modulating glucose-stimulated insulin secretion by cell cycle synchronization of β-cells
Article.Authors: Pramanik T.; Verma P.; Firdos F.; Mittal A.
Article.Abstract: Cellular secretion is central to cell biology. With a well-established secretory assay, Mouse Insulinoma 6 cells serve as a model system for investigating glucose-stimulated-insulin-secretion (GSIS) by pancreatic β-cells. A recent report has shown that glucose specificity behind GSIS is attributable to direct binding of unphosphorylated intracellular glucose to Kinesin family member 11 (KIF11), which is also a cell cycle modulator at the G2/M phase. Hence, we investigated the effect of cell cycle synchronization at the G2/M phase on GSIS. We report that insulin secretion (ratio) was significantly higher for synchronized cells compared to non-synchronized cells, while the total cellular RNA, cellular protein and supernatant protein were similar. Interestingly, glucose interacted with the key residues in the allosteric pocket of KIF11, which are also the drug targets for KIF11 inhibition. Thus, glucose may act as a possible allosteric activator of KIF11, which open new avenues for investigations into the structure–function relationship of ‘glucose-KIF11.’

Article.Title: Waste valorization of seashells and expanded polystyrene in lightweight hybrid mortar for social housing
Article.Authors: Luka M.; Lima V.; de Arimatea Rocha E.; Rabbani E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The construction sector faces increasing demands to reduce its ecological footprint, particularly in social housing, where material cost-efficiency must be balanced with technical reliability. This research investigates a sand-free alternative aggregate matrix for wall-coating mortars by fully substituting natural quartz sand with waste expanded polystyrene (EPS) and crushed sururu seashells ( Mytella falcata ) on an absolute volume basis. Three experimental formulations were examined: a reference control, a 40% partial replacement (20% shells and 20% EPS), and a 100% complete replacement (50% shells and 50% EPS). Physical properties were assessed using modified geometric cold-saturation methods. Density decreased from 1752.6 kg/m 3 to 1421.6 kg/m 3 and 904.6 kg/m 3 across the formulations. Relative water absorption values shifted from 12.90% to 10.88% and 21.67%, while the absolute absorbed water mass decreased from 44.4 g to 38.6 g at full replacement. This indicates that the percentage increase is a mathematical artifact resulting from a 48.4% reduction in skeletal mass. The 14-day compressive strength declined from 12.60 MPa to 6.40 MPa and 1.85 MPa, yet remained within standard coating specifications. This approach aligns with UN SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). Overall, the findings indicate the preliminary feasibility of volume-based waste aggregate replacement, although further evaluation of long-term durability is required before standard field implementation.

Article.Title: Association of electrocardiographic P-wave parameters with pediatric vasovagal syncope: a case-control study
Article.Authors: Yan H.; Li F.; Wang Y.; Zhang J.; Liu P.; Luo X.; Cai H.; Zou R.; Wang C.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to explore the association between electrocardiographic P-wave parameters and pediatric vasovagal syncope (VVS). A retrospective study was performed including 128 children diagnosed with VVS and 78 age-matched healthy controls from June 2018 to October 2022 at The Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University. Resting 12-lead electrocardiography was conducted to obtain P-wave parameters. Compared with controls, children with VVS had significantly longer maximum P-wave duration (Pmax), P-wave dispersion (Pd) and corrected P-wave dispersion (Pcd), shorter minimum P-wave duration (Pmin) and corrected minimum P-wave duration (Pcmin), and a lower Macruz index (all P <0.05). Multivariate logistic regression showed that Pmax (OR = 1.22, 95%CI: 1.15, 1.31), Pmin (OR=0.80, 95%CI: 0.74, 0.86), Macruz index (OR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.21, 0.86), Pcmin (OR=0.96, 95%CI: 0.93, 0.99), and Pcd (OR=1.17, 95%CI: 1.11, 1.23) were independently associated with pediatric VVS (all P < 0.05). In conclusion, children with VVS demonstrate distinct P-wave abnormalities. P-wave parameters are associated with pediatric VVS, which merits further investigation for diagnostic utility.

Article.Title: A hybrid Lévy- and differential evolution-enhanced multi-objective particle swarm optimization framework for high-dimensional cancer classification using gene selection and sample seduction
Article.Authors: Althubiti S.; Khalaf M.; Alnaimat F.; Kumar R.; Ahmed H.; Singh R.; Singh N.
Article.Abstract: Feature redundancy, small sample size and noise in high dimensional microarray data pose serious challenge for cancer classification. To tackle these limitations, this work proposes a hybrid multi-objective optimization framework for simultaneous gene selection and sample refinement. The proposed method combines an improved particle swarm optimization strategy with fuzzy clustering to improve the relevance of features and the quality of the training data. We use a binary optimization scheme to find discriminative gene subsets and a continuous optimization scheme to select representative training samples. The two-stage strategy effective reduces the dimensionality and improves the classifier generalization. The model is evaluated using standard classification algorithms and ensemble techniques on several benchmark microarray cancer datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves significant improvements in terms of classification accuracy, stability and computational efficiency in comparison with the conventional methods. The feature selection combined with sample optimization allows robust performance on high dimensional and imbalanced datasets, illustrating the potential of the approach for reliable cancer diagnosis and predictive analytics.

Article.Title: Dust storms effects on surface-heat flux and sea surface temperature in the Red Sea
Article.Authors: Nukapothula S.; Papadopoulos V.; Dasari H.; Gandham H.; Kunchala R.; Hoteit I.; Abualnaja Y.
Article.Abstract: Extreme Dust Days (EDDs) are much more frequent in the southern part of the Red Sea (RS) compared to the northern part during the dust season (March–August) over the period 1980–2024. In this study, MERRA-2 surface heat-flux data and AVHRR SST observations are analyzed to investigate the influence of extreme dust events on surface heat fluxes and associated SST variability in the Red Sea. During this period, an increasing trend in EDD occurrence over the Red Sea is observed. The enhancement of dust during EDDs is associated with distinct wind patterns over both the southern Red Sea (SRS) and northern Red Sea (NRS), indicating that these wind patterns play a key role in transporting dust toward the Red Sea. Over the SRS, EDDs are associated with increase in longwave radiation (LW) about + 10 W m⁻², decrease in shortwave radiation (SW) about − 35 W m⁻², and in latent heat flux (LH; about − 12 W m⁻²), and an increase in sensible heat flux (SH; <2 W m⁻²). In the NRS, EDD-related anomalies also show an increase in LW (about + 10 W m⁻²) and a decrease in SW (about − 30 W m⁻²), accompanied by reductions in LH and SH fluxes of approximately − 20 W m⁻² and − 2 W m⁻², respectively. Consequently, SST anomalies during EDDs exhibit substantial cooling, with a decrease up to ~ 3 °C over the SRS region. In contrast, the SST response over the NRS is less pronounced, because of fewer and shorter-lived EDDs occurrences. These results highlight the influence of dust loading on the surface energy budget and SST variability in the Red Sea with potential implications for regional ocean dynamics and marine ecosystems, particularly under future scenarios of increasing dust activity.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial organization in rod and cone photoreceptors and intercellular mitochondrial material transfer in models of blinding disease
Article.Authors: Govers L.; Wögenstein G.; Merolla L.; Fottner A.; Taverna S.; Becirovic E.; Samardzija M.; Grimm C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Photoreceptors are among the most metabolically active neurons and rely on a highly specialized mitochondrial network to support phototransduction, outer segment renewal, calcium homeostasis, and synaptic transmission. Here, we established and used robust tools for visualizing and tracking mitochondrial populations in rod and cone photoreceptors of wildtype mice and four retinal degeneration models. Using a Cre-dependent mito-Dendra2 mouse line and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated cell type-specific mitochondrial reporters, we characterized the mitochondrial architecture of both photoreceptor types. Rods contained three major mitochondrial pools located in the inner segment, soma, and synaptic terminal. Cones displayed a more complex organization, including elongated mitochondria in the inner segment, a juxtanuclear mitochondrial cap, a characteristic rounded mitochondrion basal to the nucleus, and small mitochondria within pedicles. Application of these reporters to inherited retinal degeneration models with rod- or cone-specific mutations revealed photoreceptor-derived fluorescent material within Müller glial cells. The reporters also pointed to changes in the mitochondrial appearance and to spatial disorganization in affected photoreceptors, linking altered mitochondrial architecture to degeneration. These tools enable detailed visualization of rod- and cone-specific mitochondrial populations and may facilitate evaluation of mitochondria-targeted therapies for blinding retinal diseases.

Article.Title: Midlife telomere length is associated with perceived stress and chronic disease rather than lifestyle or physical function
Article.Authors: Skurvydas A.; Dadeliene R.; Aukstikalnis T.; Istomina N.; Strazdaite E.; Predkeliene A.; Baranauskiene N.; Obcarskas L.; Daublys D.; Domeika A.; Serapinas D.; Valanciene D.; Majauskiene D.
Article.Abstract: Telomere length is a widely used biomarker of biological aging, but its relationships with physiological function, lifestyle behaviors, and psychosocial factors during midlife remain unclear. In this cross-sectional study, 84 middle-aged adults (50.9 ± 7.4 years) underwent a comprehensive assessment, including telomere length measurement using high-throughput quantitative fluorescence in situ hybridization, together with detailed evaluations of neuromuscular performance, aerobic fitness, body composition, cardiometabolic biomarkers, lifestyle behaviors, and psychosocial factors. Multivariable linear regression models with heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors (HC3) were used to identify independent associations, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied to account for multiple testing. Telomere length was primarily associated with chronological age, while physiological traits—including neuromuscular performance, aerobic capacity, body composition, and cardiometabolic biomarkers—showed no consistent independent associations after adjustment. Similarly, lifestyle and demographic factors such as moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, sauna exposure, smoking, alcohol consumption, and education were not associated with telomere metrics. In contrast, higher perceived stress and the presence of chronic disease were independently associated with shorter median and short telomere length and remained significant after HC3 robust correction. Central adiposity showed only a nominal association with shorter telomeres that did not persist after robust correction. In midlife, telomere length was primarily associated with chronological age and showed no independent relationship with physiological performance, lifestyle behaviors, or cardiometabolic markers. Independent associations with perceived stress and chronic disease suggest that telomere dynamics may reflect cumulative psychosocial and health-related burden more strongly than current functional capacity.

Article.Title: Fast FDTD simulation and fabrication of holey-pillar hybrid millimeter size metalens
Article.Authors: Kim Y.; Moon J.; Pi J.; Oh J.; Hong S.; Lee J.; Hwang C.
Article.Abstract: The development of centimeter-scale metalenses is often constrained by the quadratic scaling of conventional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, where simulation time increases significantly with the aperture diameter. To address this computational challenge, we present an accelerated FDTD methodology that establishes a linear relationship between simulation time and aperture size for metalenses up to 1 cm in diameter. This approach reduces the simulation time for a 1 mm aperture to approximately 4 hours. The proposed method restricts full-wave simulations to a designated set of representative basis patches, subsequently leveraging the finite rotational symmetry of the remaining patches within identical annular zones through a fast Delaunay triangulation interpolation algorithm. The performance of this methodology is evaluated across various numerical apertures ( \(\text {NA} = 0.3, 0.6,\) and 0.9). For experimental validation, a millimeter-sized metalens with an \(\text {NA}\) of 0.3 was fabricated utilizing a hybrid holey-pillar silicon nitride ( \(\text {Si}_3\text {N}_4\) ) meta-atom structure. This hybrid design offers a practical advantage by reducing the height of the meta-atoms to 550 nm while maintaining full \(2\pi\) phase modulation, which is achieved through complementary phase retardations between the holey and pillar meta-atoms. The fabricated metalens exhibits reliable optical performance, demonstrating a Strehl ratio of 0.9, a veiling glare index (VGI) of \(3.8\%\) , and an \(\text {MTF}_{50\%}\) cutoff frequency of \(478~\text {cycles/mm}\) .

Article.Title: Low-frequency electrical stimulation reshapes functional connectivity in human-derived neuronal networks
Article.Authors: Zanini G.; Chiappalone M.; Della Mea L.; Martinoia S.; Parodi G.
Article.Abstract: In vitro neuronal models coupled to micro-electrode arrays provide a controlled platform to investigate how neuronal networks generate, organize, and adapt their activity. Electrical stimulation is a useful perturbative approach to modulate network behaviour and study activity-dependent mechanisms. However, the effects of repeated low-frequency stimulation on the dynamics and functional organization of human-derived neuronal networks remain poorly investigated and understood. We used human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neuronal networks cultured on high-density micro-electrode arrays. Networks were generated with a defined excitatory–inhibitory composition, combining 75% glutamatergic and 25% GABAergic ​neurons. Cultures were stimulated with biphasic electrical pulses delivered at 0.2 Hz from multiple stimulation sites. Spontaneous activity and functional connectivity were compared before and after stimulation. Network dynamics were assessed from firing and bursting features, while functional organization was evaluated using cross-correlation-based connectivity analysis and graph-theoretical metrics. Repeated low-frequency stimulation markedly reshaped spontaneous network activity. After stimulation, networks displayed more frequent but shorter network bursts, mainly due to a faster decay phase, together with increased asynchronous spiking activity. Stimulation also reduced inter-culture variability, suggesting convergence toward a more uniform activity pattern independently of the initial network state. Functional connectivity analysis revealed a broader but weaker network organization. The number of connected nodes increased, whereas node degree, connection strength, and global efficiency decreased, indicating a transition toward a more distributed and less centralized topology. This reconfiguration was accompanied by a reduction in pre-existing hubs and by the emergence of new highly influential nodes preferentially located near the stimulation sites. These findings show that low-frequency electrical stimulation can induce a structured and reproducible reorganization of both electrophysiological activity and functional connectivity in human-derived neuronal networks. This supports the use of micro-electrode array platforms to study stimulation-induced short-term plasticity in a human-relevant in vitro framework.

Article.Title: ALACRITY: a density-adaptive lightweight cryptographic protocol for secure v2x communication in vehicular ad hoc networks
Article.Authors: Ankarboina H.; Kumari J.; Bhardwaj A.; Singh A.; Kumar S.
Article.Abstract: Securing vehicle-to-everything communication requires cryptography light enough for real-time beaconing, and the vehicular networking literature has largely settled on elliptic-curve signatures as the lightweight choice over RSA. We show that this preference inverts under realistic operating conditions. Because a safety beacon is signed once but verified by every vehicle within radio range, verification rather than signing dominates the per-beacon cost, and RSA-2048 verifies twice as fast as ECDSA-P256 while signing an order of magnitude more slowly. The two cost functions therefore cross at a specific neighbour count. We develop ALACRITY, a lightweight protocol combining authenticated encryption, per-vehicle digital signatures, epoch-based group-key rotation and replay protection, and evaluate it across 225 independent simulation runs on a real urban road network. The crossover is observed between 7.2 and 15.3 in-range neighbours, consistent with a fitted value of 8.5. Traffic density in this region proves bistable: across 35 runs at the transition, none settled inside the crossover band; the network is either free-flowing or congested. Selecting the signature scheme from each vehicle’s local neighbour count reduces per-beacon cost by up to 19.5% where the two regimes coexist, a gain confirmed by direct multi-receiver measurement and robust to neighbour-count estimation error over a short window.

Article.Title: Modelling and analysis of modified Leslie-Gower predator-prey with prey counter attacking
Article.Authors: Lakshmi A.; Prasad K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although the phenomenon of adult prey attacking juvenile predators is well documented in several ecological systems, its influence on predator-prey dynamics remains poorly understood. Motivated by this ecological phenomenon, we propose and analyze a modified Leslie-Gower predator-prey model incorporating prey anti-predator behavior (role reversal) together with a Holling type IV functional response. The proposed model exhibits multiple coexistence equilibria and a variety of dynamical behaviors, including Transcritical, Hopf, saddle-node, and Bogdanov-Takens bifurcations, as well as homoclinic orbits. Sufficient conditions for the occurrence of these bifurcations are derived analytically and verified through numerical simulations. The results show that anti-predator behavior fundamentally changes the qualitative dynamics by promoting prey persistence, generating bistability, and including abrupt transitions between alternative coexistence states. Moreover, increasing the intensity of anti-predator behavior enlarges the parameter region in which prey populations dominate predator populations. These findings demonstrate that prey role reversal can substantially reshape predator-prey interactions and provide new theoretical insights into the ecological consequences of anti-predator behavior.

Article.Title: Optimization of approach traffic signal control scheduling for four-phase intersections
Article.Authors: Guo Z.; Alexander K.; Wang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an analytical intersection delay function for traffic signal control and network flow assignment. The proposed function incorporates queue length and green capacity, and provides an analytically tractable estimate of vehicle delay at signalized intersections. Based on Wardrop’s principles, a bilevel optimization model is developed in which the lower level determines equilibrium traffic flows for a given signal timing plan and the upper level optimizes the green splits under known travel demand. The framework is first derived for two-phase signal control and is then extended to a four-phase setting incorporating through movements and protected left-turn phases. The bilevel formulation with route choice is solved on a two-path network example. For the empirical part of the study, traffic data were collected at a four-phase signalized intersection in China; because demand is fixed per turning movement at an isolated intersection, the lower-level flow assignment is not a decision variable there and the problem reduces to a single-level nonlinear program. Under that formulation, the optimized green splits reduce the modelled total delay per cycle by 26.16% relative to the as-operated timing plan at the study site for one off-peak hour of measurement, and by 23.58% when a practical minimum displayed green of 15 s per phase is imposed.

Article.Title: Development of an explainable machine-learning-based predictive model for cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity using real-world data
Article.Authors: Kiyomoto K.; Ikemura K.; Okuda M.
Article.Abstract: Cisplatin (CDDP)-induced nephrotoxicity (CIN) is a major dose-limiting adverse effect. The early detection and precise prediction of CIN are essential for optimizing CDDP-based chemotherapy. In this single-center study, we developed novel machine learning-based predictive models for CIN using a large-scale clinical dataset incorporating demographic characteristics and time-series laboratory data. To address the limitations of previous studies, class imbalance was handled while preserving the full dataset, and the model performance was evaluated using an independent test dataset. Among the 1,705 enrolled patients, 551 (32%) experienced nephrotoxicity. Four models were constructed using random forest, support vector machine, logistic regression, and artificial neural network algorithms. The logistic regression model achieved the highest performance among the four constructed models with scores of 0.626 (F1.5), 0.791 (AUC-ROC), 0.702 (AUC-PR), 0.739 (accuracy), 0.645 (recall), and 0.188 (Brier score). Shapley additive explanation analysis demonstrated that baseline serum creatinine and serum creatinine levels on days 4–6 after CDDP administration were the key contributors to model predictions. In conclusion, we developed a machine learning-based model for predicting CIN using real-world clinical data. Following external validation, this model may have potential to support the early identification of patients susceptible to CIN.

Article.Authors: Dallash R.; Fikry I.; El-Kharbotly A.; Zamzam N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Two-Sided Assembly Line Balancing Problem (TSALBP) is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem. Although genetic algorithms (GAs) have been widely applied to TSALBP, many existing approaches suffer from premature convergence, limited scalability, and insufficient statistical validation. This paper proposes an Enhanced Genetic Algorithm (EGA) for TSALBP-1. The approach combines heuristic population initialization based on ranked positional weight and longest-path rules, adaptive crossover and mutation operators, earliest–latest station feasibility bounds, and a single-tier station assignment strategy. To improve workload distribution, a hybrid Tabu Search–Variable Neighborhood Search (TS/VNS) procedure is applied as a post-optimization stage. In addition, an AI-generated heuristic was developed, and its performance was compared with the proposed EGA and conventional algorithms. Performance was evaluated using solution-quality metrics and rigorous statistical analyses, including Friedman ranking, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Dolan–Moré performance profiles. Experimental results show that the EGA achieved an average gap of only 0.34% from the lower bound and achieved the highest overall ranking among all competing heuristics. Five independent runs across all 42 benchmark configurations showed low run-to-run variability, supporting the robustness of the proposed EGA. Besides, the proposed approach consistently outperformed the AI-generated heuristic, especially for medium- and large-scale benchmark instances. Finally, the TS/VNS post-optimization phase improved workload balance significantly, reducing idle-time variance by up to 99.7% in large-scale instances. The results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive hybrid framework provides an effective and scalable solution for TSALBP while achieving superior solution quality, robustness, and workload distribution. While hybrid initialization, adaptive operators, and TS/VNS refinement are individually established techniques, the novelty of this work lies in their coordinated integration within a TSALBP-specific framework, their controlled component-wise evaluation, and the rigorous statistical validation of the overall framework. The main contributions of this work are the development of an enhanced adaptive genetic algorithm with heuristic-based population initialization and dynamic search operators, together with a hybrid TS/VNS post-optimization framework for smoothing workload without increasing the number of stations. In addition, the proposed approach is comprehensively validated through rigorous statistical analyses and benchmarked against both state-of-the-art algorithms and an AI-generated heuristic to assess the potential of large language models for generating heuristic solution procedures for TSALBP.

Article.Title: Molecular characterization and relationships of hop stunt viroid (Hostuviroid impedihumuli) isolates infecting apple
Article.Authors: Amirnia F.; Gibbs A.; Hajizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: The hop stunt viroid has been isolated from several rosid angiosperms, including important stone and pome fruits. Nonetheless, despite the economic importance of apple ( Malus domestica ) and others of its hosts, the molecular diversity, evolutionary history, and global population structure of apple-infecting hop stunt viroid (HSVd-a) remain poorly understood. In this study, 137 apple leaf samples were collected from western and northwestern Iran and screened for HSVd by RT-PCR, revealing an infection rate of 54%. Twelve representative isolates were sequenced, yielding eight distinct HSVd-a variants with genome lengths of 297–298 nucleotides. Together with complete HSVd genomes retrieved from public databases, an alignment of 292 unique genomes was obtained. However, neither maximum likelihood nor neighbor-joining methods gave a resolved and statistically supported phylogeny of these genomic sequences, although both methods placed previously reported Iranian isolates at the root of the trees. Population genetic analyses, by contrast, revealed extensive gene flow between the population of all HSVd-a isolates, including those identified in this study and those reported previously, and HSVd populations from other hosts. Thus, selection by cloning and selection in different cultivated hosts seems more likely to account for the observed genomic differences of HSVd. This underscores the importance of multi-host dynamics in shaping the population structure of viroids, and the crucial value of international quarantine.

Article.Title: Integrated multi-omics prioritizes small-molecule candidates for the N-cadherin HAV site and reveals endpoint-level toxicity trade-offs
Article.Authors: Sisakht M.; Fallahi J.; Alamdari-Palang V.; Razban V.; Hassani M.; Hassani M.; Khajeh S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract N-cadherin (CDH2) is a central effector of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) that contributes to invasion, metastasis and therapy resistance. Although peptide and antibody approaches validate N-cadherin as a therapeutic target, small-molecule modulators of its adhesive interface remain limited. We aimed to prioritize candidate compounds that suppress EMT-associated transcriptional programs, show plausible binding at the N-cadherin HAV (His79-Ala80-Val81) hotspot, preserve the biomass objective in context-specific metabolic models, and minimize predicted endpoint-level toxicity liabilities. LINCS L1000 level-5 profiles were screened for concordant down-regulation of CDH2, SNAI1 and SNAI2, yielding 20 compounds across cell lines, doses and exposure times. Compounds were docked to the N-cadherin EC1 HAV pocket and compared with a spatially separated non-HAV EC1 control surface. Toxicity was evaluated using a multi-task DeepChem Graph Convolutional Network trained on Tox21 with a scaffold-based split. Predicted toxicity risk was summarized using max-risk, defined as the highest predicted positive-class probability across 12 endpoints. Context-specific metabolic effects were modeled with Human1 using E-Flux, pFBA and FVA, and summarized using Objective Preservation Ratio (OPR), Metabolic Impact Score (MIS), Targeted Pathway Selectivity (TPS), and Homeostasis Disruption Score (HDS). Evidence pillars were winsorized, normalized and integrated using a transparent weighted composite score. Docking energies ranged from − 8.1 to − 5.9 kcal mol –1 , and 19 of 20 compounds showed more favorable predicted binding at the HAV pocket than at the non-HAV control surface. The toxicity model achieved a micro-averaged ROC-AUC of 0.775 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.756 – 0.794) and PR-AUC of 0.335 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.298 – 0.374). Across modeled conditions, median OPR was 1.12, median TPS was 0.165, median MIS was 0.79, and HDS was uniformly low. Under the conservative max-risk-based integration, BRD.K09587429 ranked first (composite score 0.656). It showed concordant suppression of CDH2, SNAI1 and SNAI2, a HAV-site docking score of − 6.7 kcal mol –1 , OPR of 1.081, TPS of 0.184, and max-risk of 0.554 at SR-ARE. BRD.K04021425 ranked second and was retained as the alternative candidate, with the strongest docking score and the lowest endpoint-level max-risk. A 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation showed persistent computational occupancy of the HAV-site region, with His79 and Ala80 remaining within 0.4 nm of the ligand in 96.9% and 99.1% of frames, respectively, over the 20–100 ns interval. MM-PBSA analysis of 81 snapshots yielded a favorable end-state binding-energy estimate of − 24.58 ± 6.90 kcal mol – 1 , which remained consistent when analysis was restricted to the final 50 ns ( – 27.22 ± 5.68 kcal mol –1 ). This multi-omics framework prioritizes candidate N-cadherin/EMT modulators by jointly considering transcriptomic directionality, HAV-site docking, endpoint-resolved toxicity, and metabolic selectivity. BRD.K09587429 emerged as the highest-ranked discovery-stage candidate, with molecular dynamics showing persistent computational occupancy of the HAV-site region and MM-PBSA indicating a favorable model-dependent end-state energetic profile; however, direct binding, functional N-cadherin antagonism, molecular mechanism, and the predicted SR-ARE-associated liability require experimental validation. The framework distinguishes structural plausibility from safety and can be adapted to other protein-protein interfaces relevant to metastatic cancer biology.

Article.Title: Optimized niosomal nanocarriers for nisin encapsulation and prolonged antibacterial activity
Article.Authors: Alhashimi S.; Algburi A.; Niazmand R.
Article.Abstract: This study systematically optimized nisin-loaded niosomes prepared by thin-film hydration using Span 60 and Tween 80 (2:1 molar ratio) with cholesterol. Thirteen formulation conditions were screened using hydration pH, surfactant-to-cholesterol ratio (ST: Ch), and wall-to-core ratio as formulation variables. The optimized formulation (pH 7.4, ST: Ch 50:50, wall-to-core 3:1) showed an encapsulation efficiency of 67.7 ± 1.9%, loading capacity of 16.9 ± 0.9%, particle size of 383.3 nm, PDI of 0.283, and zeta potential of -8.6 ± 0.7 mV. FTIR analysis showed retention and changes in characteristic bands of nisin and the niosomal components, while DSC demonstrated changes in phase transition behavior after nisin incorporation. TEM and AFM showed predominantly spherical vesicles. In time-kill assays, the complete nisin-loaded niosomal formulation, tested as prepared, was compared with free nisin at equal nominal concentrations. Free nisin showed the lower MIC, its distinguishing feature was a prolonged antibacterial effect over 24–72 h, with an MBC of 50 µg mL⁻¹ versus 100 µg mL⁻¹ for Staphylococcus aureus and 200 µg mL⁻¹ versus > 200 µg mL⁻¹ for Escherichia coli. During 40 days of storage at 4 °C, particle size increased by 18.2% and EE decreased by 26.4% relative to day 1. These results demonstrate that nisin can be efficiently incorporated into niosomes under neutral hydration conditions and that the formulation maintains antibacterial activity over prolonged incubation, consistent with the rationale of encapsulation as a means of protecting nisin and extending its activity over time.

Article.Title: Association of sampling method and FFPE storage duration with comprehensive genomic profiling success in gastrointestinal tract cancers
Article.Authors: Iwata T.; Suzuki N.; Fujisawa G.; Miyakawa Y.; Tamada K.; Hayashi T.; Suzumori C.; Odawara N.; Hayakawa Y.; Sasaki K.; Yagi K.; Hasegawa K.; Watanabe K.; Shinozaki-Ushiku A.; Kage H.; Oda K.; Boku N.; Fujishiro M.
Article.Abstract: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) relies on high-quality formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue, but the association between storage duration and CGP success may differ according to sampling method. We retrospectively analyzed 273 FFPE samples submitted for CGP from patients with gastrointestinal tract cancers between July 2020 and March 2026. CGP success rates were 76.8% for endoscopic biopsy samples, 80.2% for primary surgery samples, and 84.2% for metastatic surgery samples. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic biopsy sampling and longer FFPE storage duration were independently associated with lower CGP success. A significant interaction between sampling method and storage duration indicated that the association of prolonged storage with CGP success differed according to sampling method. Predicted CGP success declined more rapidly in endoscopic biopsy samples. The estimated storage durations corresponding to a predicted success probability of 80% were 240 days for endoscopic biopsy samples, 868 days for primary surgery samples, and 891 days for metastatic surgery samples. These findings suggest that the suitability of archived FFPE tissue for CGP should be considered in relation to both storage duration and sampling method, and that earlier CGP submission may be particularly important for endoscopic biopsy samples.

Article.Title: IoT-based multi-sensor data fusion for freshwater ecosystem monitoring: a case study of Lake Tana, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Amssaya H.; Mekuria F.; Tegegne T.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigated an efficient real-time data collection mechanism for Lake Tana using sensor fusion and the Internet of Things (IoT). The rapid proliferation of invasive aquatic weeds in freshwater ecosystems necessitates robust long-term monitoring and efficient data acquisition techniques. Smart IoT-based sensor networks enable real-time acquisition of key aquatic parameters, such as pH, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and chlorophyll-a. This study presented an IoT-based sensor fusion framework for improving the accuracy and reliability of environmental monitoring. Sensor fusion algorithms, such as weighted, Kalman, extended Kalman, unscented Kalman, Bayesian, and Particle filter, are used to enhance the precision of the collected data. The experimental dataset consisted of 192 sensor observations collected over three months using multiple sensors deployed in Lake Tana. Experimental results demonstrated that the unscented Kalman sensor fusion significantly enhanced measurement accuracy and stability, achieving 81.46%, 84.10%, and 93.72% improvements over the no-fusion approach in reducing variance for TP, TN, and Chl-a, respectively. WF and PF achieved a 96.24% improvement in pH. These findings demonstrated that the sensor fusion approach effectively reduces measurement uncertainty and provides more reliable water parameter estimates, making it a promising solution for real-time IoT-enabled environmental monitoring applications.

Article.Title: Semi-bayesian learning optimization for low-power connecting networks in internet of things
Article.Authors: Alghuried A.; Alghuson M.; Abuhasel K.; Alotaibi A.
Article.Abstract: Energy-efficient (EE) optimization schemes have been widely used in massive Internet of Things (IoT) deployments to extend device lifetimes under strict quality-of-service (QoS)-assured requirements. EE-aware resource allocation over low-power connecting networks has been challenging beyond conventional requirements. Increasing energy demand, which remains constant during the paused allocation interval, worsens the performance of these networks. In this regard, the proposed work develops a Semi-Bayesian Learning Optimization (SBLO) framework to address the trade-off between energy demand and EE. The low-power connecting devices are evaluated for energy efficiency, with the required consumption and demand determined based on previous sessions. The key element used to distinguish data points is the residual energy taken as input when predicting for adjacent state transitions. The QoS is mostly long-lasting in the IoT area, as forecasted for admissible requests, quantified by connectivity and repair time. The states before and after allocation are EE, demanding from the state before allocation to the state after allocation. Then, a probabilistic demand model defines when to consider the next pause interval, replacement, or recharging. Intermediate-state learning is used to project new EE or demand for connecting requests in the next request. We evaluate the proposed optimization for energy utilization, energy demand, connectivity and service time while comparing to representative baselines through experiments.

Article.Title: Effects of ALK5 inhibition combined with bipolar irreversible electroporation on tumor response and fibrosis in prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Lee I.; Kim Y.; Won D.; Kim D.; Park W.; Lim B.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Irreversible electroporation (IRE) has emerged as a potential therapeutic option that selectively ablates cancer cells in the prostate while preserving normal tissue architecture and minimizing adverse effects. However, IRE-induced cell death triggers an inflammatory response that promotes collagen deposition, leading to fibrotic tissue remodeling. This study investigated the efficacy and safety of combination therapy using IRE and a transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) type I receptor kinase (ALK5) inhibitor in a human prostate cancer xenograft mouse model, with focus on whether ALK5 inhibitor could mitigate excessive fibrosis while preserving the anti-tumor effect of IRE. EW-7197, a specific ALK5 inhibitor, effectively suppressed cell proliferation and fibrogenesis in vitro. A total of 24 mice inoculated with DU145-Luc cells were enrolled. Tumor progression was monitored via in vivo imaging system, magnetic resonance imaging, and gross examination, and the anti-tumor and anti-fibrotic effects were assessed through histological analysis. The tumor suppression-related parameters in the IRE and IRE@EW-7197 groups were significantly lower than those in the control and EW-7197 groups (all p < 0.05). The IRE@EW-7197 group showed the greatest numerical reduction in tumor volume without statistical difference compared with the IRE group. Fibrosis-related markers were significantly suppressed in the EW-7197 and the IRE@EW-7197 groups. These findings suggest that ALK5 inhibition attenuated excessive fibrosis and modulated the inflammatory response without compromising the short-term anti-tumor efficacy of IRE. The combination therapy may represent a promising strategy to mitigate IRE-induced fibrosis in prostate cancer, although longer-term studies are needed to determine whether it confers additional oncologic benefit.

Article.Title: A hard illusion to break: the robustness of the Jastrow illusion across geometry, objects, and numerosity
Article.Authors: Santacà M.; Granziol U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Visual illusions are typically defined by specific geometric configurations, raising the question of how far their perceptual effects persist when those configurations are transformed or embedded in different representations. Here, we investigated the robustness of the Jastrow illusion across changes in geometry, object representation, and numerosity. Participants judged the relative size or numerosity of paired stimuli. In control trials, the two alternatives differed physically in area or numerosity, whereas in illusory trials they were physically identical and arranged according to the Jastrow illusion, in which the lower of two vertically displaced identical stimuli is typically perceived as larger. Illusion-consistent responding was observed across several geometric, object-based, and numerical configurations, although its prevalence varied considerably across stimulus types. Systematic manipulations of curvature and symmetry suggested that geometric properties modulated the probability of illusion-consistent responses without necessarily eliminating the bias. Likewise, the effects of removing internal details varied across object categories, with illusion-consistent responding remaining evident for birds and fish but not significantly exceeding chance for outline faces. However, these differences may partly reflect the distinct visual information preserved by each category’s external contours. Response times complemented the accuracy findings, showing that response-time differences between control and illusory trials also varied systematically with stimulus properties. Together, these findings suggest that illusion-consistent responding can persist across substantial transformations of the original configuration, while its occurrence and consistency depend on geometric and representational properties.

Article.Title: Neprilysin inhibition reduces microtubule detyrosination in cardiomyocytes through a cGMP-PRKG1-VASH1 axis
Article.Authors: Meyer-Jens M.; Sanyal C.; Pietsch N.; Ramirez-Rios S.; Herrera-Rivero M.; Krämer E.; Braren I.; Nikolaev V.; Frye M.; Könemann S.; Schlossarek S.; Moutin M.; Carrier L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microtubule detyrosination and re-tyrosination on the C-terminus of α-tubulin are mediated by the vasohibin (VASH)-small vasohibin-binding protein (SVBP) complex and tubulin tyrosine ligase (TTL), respectively. Elevated levels of detyrosinated α-tubulin (dTyr-tub) are observed in heart failure, and reducing this modification improves cardiac function, suggesting that heart failure therapies may modulate microtubule detyrosination. We investigated whether sacubitrilat and valsartan, the active components of the angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor LCZ696, influence dTyr-tub levels in endothelin-1 (ET1)-induced hypertrophy in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). While both sacubitrilat and valsartan prevented hypertrophy, only sacubitrilat prevented ET1-induced dTyr-tub accumulation. Sacubitrilat slightly increased cyclic guanosine 3′,5′-monophosphate (cGMP) levels and lowered dTyr-tub, whereas inhibition or knockdown of the cGMP-dependent protein kinase 1 (PRKG1) increased dTyr-tub. PRKG1 phosphorylated native VASH1 . Incubation of microtubules with the VASH1-SVBP complex containing wild-type VASH1, but not a VASH1 phosphomimic (VASH1-7E) increased detyrosination. Consistently, overexpression of VASH1-7E gave rise to lower dTyr-tub level than overexpression of a non-phosphorylatable form of VASH1 (VASH1-7A) in hiPSC-CMs deficient in VASH1. These findings identify a cGMP–PRKG1–VASH1 signaling axis that reduces microtubule detyrosination in cardiomyocytes.

Article.Title: Hybrid LED–LD underwater optical wireless communication system for long-range IoUT applications
Article.Authors: Zayed M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Underwater Optical Wireless Communication (UWOC) has emerged as a key enabling technology for high-speed Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) networks; however, its performance is severely constrained by wavelength-dependent absorption, scattering, turbulence, beam divergence, and strict alignment requirements in different water environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a robust hybrid optical transmission architecture that intelligently integrates light-emitting diode (LED) and laser diode (LD) sources to exploit their complementary characteristics. LEDs provide wide-beam coverage and reliable link establishment at short ranges, while LDs enable high-power, narrow-beam transmission for extended communication distances and high data rates. A comprehensive analytical UWOC channel model is developed incorporating water attenuation, turbulence-induced fading, pointing errors, geometric losses, and receiver noise, together with an adaptive SNR-based switching mechanism for dynamic source selection. The proposed hybrid LED–LD UWOC system is evaluated using received optical power, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), bit-error rate (BER) (analyzed versus distance, SNR, and transmitted power), achievable data rate (throughput), outage probability, coverage probability, link margin, energy efficiency (bits/J), spectral efficiency (bits/s/Hz), quality factor (Q), and eye-diagram–based signal quality assessment. Extensive simulations are conducted at blue (450 nm) and green (520 nm) wavelengths for multiple water types, including pure sea, clear ocean, coastal, and harbor conditions. Results demonstrate substantial performance gains of LD transmission over LED links. In pure seawater, LD communication distances exceed approximately 80–90 m, whereas LED links remain limited to roughly 15–20 m. In clear ocean conditions, LD links maintain ranges near 50 m compared with about 12–14 m for LEDs. Under a strict reliability constraint of BER ≤ 10⁻ ⁹ LD sources achieve successful transmission at significantly lower SNR requirements, reducing the needed SNR by roughly 8–9 dB relative to LEDs. Furthermore, at a 1 Gbps throughput threshold, LEDs support only short-range links around 10 m, while LD transmission extends beyond 60 m, confirming the strong suitability of laser-based propagation for long-distance high-capacity UWOC. The obtained results verify that the proposed hybrid LED–LD framework significantly enhances communication reliability, achievable range, and spectral efficiency across diverse underwater environments. This adaptive dual-source strategy provides a scalable and practical solution for next-generation high-speed underwater sensing, monitoring, and autonomous IoUT applications.

Article.Title: AKR1C3 induces resistance of hepatocellular carcinoma cells to sorafenib via modulating the ROS/SIRT1/BRD4/NFIC signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Chen S.; Li Z.; Hao Z.; Song Y.; Wang W.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate how AKR1C3 mediates resistance to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells. Bioinformatics analysis was employed to screen genes specifically expressed in sorafenib resistance HCC. Single‑cell transcriptomic profiling further dissected HCC cellular heterogeneity, revealing a proliferative cancer cell population with high migration/proliferation scores, a dedifferentiated state, complex communication networks centered on hepatocytes, and increased M2 macrophage/neutrophil infiltration. Western blotting, flow cytometry, and immunohistochemistry revealed that, compared to parental Huh7 cells, sorafenib‑resistant Huh7 cells showed significantly elevated AKR1C3, Nrf2, p‑SIRT1, SHP2, p‑PI3K, CyclinA1, MMP9, and HIF1α, and reduced P22, P47, BRD4, NFIC, and PTEN. Direct ROS measurement using DCFH-DA flow cytometry further confirmed that ROS levels were significantly reduced in sorafenib resistance cells. Flow cytometry demonstrated the role of AKR1C3 in normal hepatocytes (LO 2 ). Compared to parental Huh7 cells, sorafenib resistance Huh7 cells exhibited significantly elevated expression of AKR1C3, Nrf2, p-SIRT1, SHP2, p-PI3K, CyclinA1, MMP9, and HIF1α proteins, while expression levels of P22, P47, BRD4, NFIC, and PTEN were significantly reduced. Immunofluorescence showed enhanced relative fluorescence intensity of AKR1C3 and SHP2. Furthermore, AKR1C3 promoted the proliferation, migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of Huh7 cells by mediating the ROS/SIRT1/BRD4/NFIC signaling pathway, thereby conferring sorafenib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma cells.
