Article.Title: Empirical modeling of the equilibrium surface tension of nonionic flotation frothers using concentration and molecular descriptors
Article.Authors: Nazoori A.; Rezai B.; Abdollahzadeh A.
Article.Abstract: Equilibrium surface tension depends on frother concentration, molecular structure, and solution conditions. Eight nonionic flotation frothers were examined at 5–200 ppm in deionized water at 25 °C to develop an empirical correlation using concentration, the molecular weight to hydrophile–lipophile-balance ratio (MW/HLB), and an MIBC-derived correction. Calibration yielded R² = 0.9624 and RMSE = 1.0205 mN/m, reducing RMSE by 68.8% relative to a shared-parameter global Langmuir–Szyszkowski model. Internal concentration interpolation and leave one frother out cross-validation for the seven reference frothers yielded RMSE values of 1.1736 and 1.1484 mN/m, respectively. External evaluation using 18 observations for isobutanol, 4-methyl-1-pentanol, and 2-ethyl-1-hexanol without refitting yielded R² = 0.8934 and RMSE = 1.0006 mN/m, with compound-dependent accuracy. Structural comparisons revealed concentration-dependent branching effects and hydroxyl-position-associated differences between MIBC and 4-methyl-1-pentanol. Increasing temperature from 15 to 35 °C reduced surface tension by 2.1–3.2 mN/m for MIBC and DF-250. Adding 1.0 M NaCl reduced it by 3.4–11.7 mN/m for MIBC, while increasing pH from 7 to 12 reduced it by 5.0 mN/m for MIBC and 3.0 mN/m for DF-250. The correlation supports estimation within the evaluated concentration and molecular domain in deionized water at 25 °C, while supplementary experiments extend the characterization of frother behavior across different operating conditions.

Article.Title: Pantoea bangladeshensis sp. nov.; a new phytopathogen causing grain discolouration disease of rice in Bangladesh
Article.Authors: Goswami A.; Nayem M.; Jhan P.; Dutta S.; Hasan M.; Islam T.; Rahman A.; Bhattacharya P.; Rubel M.
Article.Abstract: Pantoea sp. (strains NSTU24ᵀ and NSTU24.1) is an emerging bacterial pathogen isolated from severe rice grain discolouration in Bangladesh. While initial 16 S rRNA sequencing indicated close phylogenetic relationships with species such as P. graminicola and P. phosphatilytica , definitive identification required comprehensive whole-genome sequencing. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize the genomic, phenotypic, and pathogenic features of these strains to determine their precise taxonomic identity and functional properties. Genomic analysis of the 4.35-Mb genome (56.13 mol% GC content) revealed exceptionally low Average Nucleotide Identity (≤ 92.51%) and digital DNA-DNA Hybridization (≤ 48.6%) values compared to its closest relatives, unequivocally establishing it as a distinct novel species. Rigorous in-vivo pathogenicity assays successfully fulfilled Koch’s postulates, confirming its causal role in the disease. Furthermore, comparative pan-genome profiling highlighted significant evolutionary divergence, identifying unique accessory gene clusters absent in related type strains. The new species also exhibits a distinctive functional repertoire; it harbors complete Type I and Type V secretion systems while completely lacking Type III and Type VI machineries, contrasting sharply with the strategies of closely related Pantoea species. Supported by integrated phenotypic, biochemical, and phylogenomic evidence, we formally propose Pantoea bangladeshensis as a novel taxon, underscoring the critical need for genomic surveillance of agricultural pathogens.

Article.Title: Line protection scheme for four-terminal flexible DC ring grids based on integrated characteristics of two-terminal transient currents
Article.Authors: Jin H.; Liu Y.; Wu Y.; Song J.
Article.Abstract: To address the difficulty of balancing selectivity and sensitivity in existing two-terminal transient protection for four-terminal VSC-HVDC ring networks with centralized current-limiting reactors—caused by the lack of physical boundaries and the multi-path propagation of traveling waves—a protection method based on integrated characteristics of two-terminal transient currents is proposed. Analysis based on the fault superimposed network reveals that internal faults exhibit consistent polarities of two-terminal components along with local energy dominance. In contrast, disturbed non-faulted lines display false co-directionality due to multi-path interference but lack energy superiority. The proposed method utilizes cosine similarity to characterize the direction for initial screening, and employs the local energy ratio, incorporating the energy of adjacent lines, to determine the attribution of the response energy for intensity verification. These two aspects form a coordinated criterion via a logical AND operation. Furthermore, fault pole selection is achieved using the transient energy ratio between the positive and negative poles. PSCAD/EMTDC simulations demonstrate that this method can reliably identify internal and external faults, block disturbed lines, effectively improve protection selectivity under the simulated conditions, and exhibit a certain degree of robustness against fault resistance and noise.

Article.Title: Non-invasive estimation of brachial pressure waveforms via oscillometric transfer function analysis using cardiovascular hardware simulator
Article.Authors: Hong J.; Lee B.; Jeong J.; Park Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cuff oscillations are dynamically distorted relative to arterial pressure. We investigated reconstruction of normalized brachial arterial pressure waveforms using a cardiovascular hardware simulator with six upper-arm phantom configurations. Transfer functions were identified from random excitation and evaluated on separate pulsatile recordings at 60–96 beats/min and nominal cuff pressures of 40, 100 and 160 mmHg. Eighteen individual transfer functions (ITFs) were estimated. Generalized transfer functions (GTFs) were constructed by equally weighted complex averaging; leave-one-phantom-configuration-out evaluation excluded the test configuration. On the same 72 conditions, ITF reconstruction yielded Pearson correlation r = 0.9865 ± 0.0102 and normalized root-mean-square error (nRMSE) = 0.0528 ± 0.0213, whereas held-out GTF yielded r = 0.9725 ± 0.0192 and nRMSE = 0.0713 ± 0.0235 (mean ± standard deviation). A phenomenological standard-linear-solid model fitted the complex responses with R 2 = 0.9628 ± 0.0161. Exploratory analysis of peak-height ratios identified residual reconstruction errors and sensitivity to peak-detection settings. These results support normalized waveform reconstruction in the tested simulator; they do not establish system linearity, absolute blood-pressure accuracy or clinical generalizability.

Article.Title: lncRNA PVT1 and STAT3 are coordinately upregulated in Behçet’s disease and associated with disease activity
Article.Authors: Safary A.; Ghassembaglou A.; Ghaderipour R.; Zarredar H.; Jafarpour M.; Akbarzadeh-Khiavi M.; Khabbazi A.
Article.Abstract: Behçet’s disease (BD) is an autoinflammatory disorder with dysregulated IL-6 and STAT3 expression. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are important epigenetic regulators of inflammatory pathways; however, their role in the pathogenesis of BD remains incompletely understood. We investigated whether three lncRNAs, LINC00460 , DILC , and PVT1 , are dysregulated in BD and associated with IL-6 and STAT3 transcript levels. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected from 40 BD patients (20 active, 20 inactive) and 20 healthy controls (HCs). Expression levels of IL-6 , STAT3 , LINC00460 , DILC , and PVT1 were measured by qRT-PCR. ROC curve analysis assessed the discriminatory performance of each transcript in distinguishing BD from HCs and active from inactive disease. STAT3 , IL-6 , and PVT1 were significantly overexpressed in BD patients versus HCs (all P = 0.001). STAT3 transcript expression was higher in active BD than inactive BD ( P = 0.006). ROC analysis demonstrated excellent separation between BD and HCs for STAT3 [AUC = 0.992], PVT1 [AUC = 0.988], and IL-6 [AUC = 0.927]. However, only STAT3 and PVT1 moderately distinguished active from inactive BD. No significant differences were observed for DILC or LINC00460 . PVT1 positively correlated with STAT3 in all BD patients ( r = 0.340, P = 0.031) and in active BD patients ( r = 0.688, P = 0.005), but not with IL-6 . PVT1 and STAT3 are significantly dysregulated in BD and associated with disease activity. The positive correlation between PVT1 and STAT3 suggests a potential transcriptional co-regulation. DILC and LINC00460 are not altered in BD, indicating they are unlikely to play a major role in peripheral blood immune dysregulation in this disease.

Article.Title: Deep learning screening for severe nasal cavity structural abnormalities using endoscopic imaging
Article.Authors: Hirano K.; Murakami K.; Takeda K.; Ukai K.; Chang Y.; Mukai N.
Article.Abstract: To develop and evaluate a deep learning–based decision-support model using nasal endoscopy videos to identify severe nasal cavity structural abnormality (S-NCSA), an image-based morphological category defined by a visible septum–inferior turbinate contact point, and to explore its potential for future triage applications in non-specialist settings. We retrospectively analyzed 628 nasal cavities from 317 patients; frames were assigned by board-certified otolaryngologists to the image-based morphological categories S-NCSA, nasal cavity structural abnormality (NCSA), or normal (NL), with S-NCSA defined by a visible septum-inferior-turbinate contact point. ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs)-Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG16), 50-layer residual network (ResNet50), 18-layer three-dimensional residual network (3DResNet18), and 34-layer residual network (ResNet34)-were fine-tuned and evaluated with patient-level stratified four-fold cross-validation. Two ResNet34 strategies were compared: an Average-Diagnosis Model, for which the case-level score was the mean logit difference across frames and a positive mean logit difference indicated S-NCSA; and a Severe-Priority Model, for which a case was classified as S-NCSA when at least one frame was predicted as S-NCSA. In the bilateral-nasal ResNet34 analysis, the Average-Diagnosis strategy achieved 85.5% accuracy (95% confidence interval [CI], 82.6–88.1), 66.2% sensitivity (57.8–73.9), and 90.6% specificity (87.8–93.2). The Severe-Priority strategy yielded 79.5% accuracy (76.3–82.7), 84.6% sensitivity (78.1–90.2), and 78.1% specificity (74.2–81.8), indicating a sensitivity–specificity trade-off. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted nasal endoscopy can flag S-NCSA morphology, defined by a visible septum–inferior turbinate contact point, as decision support rather than autonomous clinical diagnosis. Because symptom severity and functional nasal patency were not evaluated, these findings should not be interpreted as validation of clinically severe nasal obstruction. The potential role of the Severe-Priority strategy in primary-care triage requires prospective clinical evaluation, while the Average-Diagnosis strategy may support image-based morphological assessment in specialist settings.

Article.Title: Reliability-aware tone–segment learning for weakly supervised Southern Min automatic speech recognition
Article.Authors: Qiu Y.; Pan W.; Pan Q.; Yao P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Southern Min automatic speech recognition (ASR) is challenged by non-verbatim Mandarin subtitles, unreliable pseudo-transcripts, tone-related acoustic variation, and programme-dependent domain shift. We propose the Southern Min Reliability-Bridging Automatic Speech Recognition framework (MinBridge-ASR), organized around two core mechanisms: cross-scale reliability bridging and branch-selective tone–segment learning. The former combines speech-conditioned character-level refinement of weak subtitles with multi-cue utterance-level weighting of pseudo-transcripts while maintaining teacher–student consistency independently. The latter uses controlled pitch interventions to encourage complementary tone-related and segmental representations while restricting programme- and pseudo-speaker-adversarial learning to the segmental pathway. On MinSpeech, MinBridge-ASR achieved character error rates (CERs) of 17.21%, 22.96%, and 20.10% on the official, primary programme-disjoint, and human-verified evaluations, respectively. Across five programme-disjoint splits, it achieved a mean CER of 23.11 ± 0.44%. Direct lexical-tone evaluation showed that the tonal representation outperformed explicit fundamental-frequency (F0) fusion in tone-category and tonal-minimal-pair discrimination despite lower raw pitch recoverability. Progressive ablations and reliability calibration further supported the two core mechanisms. These results demonstrate improved weakly supervised Southern Min ASR under subtitle noise and programme variation.

Article.Title: Machine learning model using contrast-enhanced CT for predicting overall survival in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE plus targeted and immunotherapy: a multicenter study
Article.Authors: Ning S.; Chen Y.; Feng B.; Sun Z.; Qu Q.; Lv Y.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a machine learning model based on contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) for predicting the overall survival (OS) in unresectable HCC patients treated with TACE combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) plus molecular targeted therapies (MTTs). This study retrospectively reviewed 180 unresectable HCC patients who received TACE-ICIs-MTTs therapy from 4 medical centers. The study comprised of training cohort ( n = 93), internal validation cohort ( n = 39) and external validation cohort ( n = 48). A series of analyses and kinds of models were conducted to build a Radscore. Then, models were constructed using Radscore and clinical variables selected through multivariate Cox regression analysis, evaluated by the Harrell’s concordance index (C-index) and the area under the curve (AUC). The radiomics-clinical model was further assessed by decision curve and calibration curve analysis. The Radscore was derived from 6 features selected by the optimal model (Lasso Cox + RSF with the highest C-index of 0.777). HBV infection and vascular invasion are clinical independent predictors of OS. The radiomics-clinical model demonstrated favorable performance. It achieved C-index values of 0.893(0.859–0.927), 0.758 (0.657–0.86) and 0.74 (0.624–0.856) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In the external validation cohort, the AUCs achieved 0.731 (0.569–0.893), 0.7 (0.515–0.885), and 0.756 (0.569–0.943) for predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year outcomes, respectively. The machine learning model based on CECT exhibited favorable performance in predicting overall survival in unresectable HCC patients treated with TACE-ICIs-MTTs, showing potential to identify likely responders and guide treatment decision-making.

Article.Title: The impact of physical activity on chronic diseases: a meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Zhao X.; Mo Q.; Tian Y.; Gan C.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Chronic diseases represent a major global health challenge. While physical activity is advocated for prevention and management, the comparative efficacy of different exercise modalities and the influence of geographic context remain areas requiring definitive synthesis. This meta-analysis aimed to: (1) quantify the pooled effect of physical activity on key health indicators in people with, or at risk of, chronic disease; (2) compare the effectiveness of different exercise types; and (3) examine regional variation in outcomes. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines. Four electronic databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Embase) were searched from inception to December 2023, yielding 2,867 initial records. After screening, 93 effect sizes from 48 publications were included. All outcomes were continuous, and a single effect measure was used throughout: the standardized mean difference expressed as Hedges’s g, pooled with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) under a random-effects model estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML). Heterogeneity was quantified using Cochran’s Q, the I² statistic and τ². Subgroup analyses were performed for exercise modality, health indicator, geographic region and disease type, and differences between subgroups were tested using the Q statistic for between-group heterogeneity (Qb). The review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261357663). Across all 93 effect sizes the pooled estimate favoured physical activity (g = -0.68, 95% CI: -1.02 to -0.34; I² = 98.70%); because this overall value aggregates indicators whose desirable direction differs, the indicator-specific estimates below are the more informative results. Among exercise modalities, only aerobic exercise reached statistical significance (g = -0.54, 95% CI: -0.82 to -0.27); resistance exercise (g = -0.45, 95% CI: -1.96 to 1.06) and combined aerobic-plus-resistance exercise (g = -1.27, 95% CI: -2.64 to 0.09) had confidence intervals that included zero, and the three modalities did not differ significantly from one another (Qb(2) = 1.08, p = 0.58). Physical activity significantly improved systolic blood pressure (g = -1.26, 95% CI: -2.11 to -0.42), diastolic blood pressure (g = -0.99, 95% CI: -1.85 to -0.13), heart rate (g = -1.01, 95% CI: -1.73 to -0.30) and VO2max (g = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.18 to 2.17; for this outcome a positive value denotes improvement), but had no significant effect on BMI (g = -0.42, 95% CI: -0.88 to 0.04), physical health (g = -0.38, 95% CI: -1.14 to 0.38) or mental health (g = 0.06, 95% CI: -0.44 to 0.57). Total cholesterol was the only indicator to move significantly in an unfavourable direction (g = 2.95, 95% CI: 2.36 to 3.53), an estimate resting on a single effect size. Effects were significant for hypertension (g = -0.90, 95% CI: -1.43 to -0.37) and diabetes (g = -0.57, 95% CI: -1.07 to -0.07) but not for cardiovascular disease (g = -0.17, 95% CI: -0.39 to 0.04). The largest regional point estimate was observed in Asia (g = -1.19, 95% CI: -1.96 to -0.41), followed by North America and Europe among the regions reaching significance, although between-region differences were not statistically significant (Qb(5) = 8.32, p = 0.14). This meta-analysis indicates that physical activity improves several key health indicators in people with chronic disease, with the clearest benefits for blood pressure, heart rate and cardiorespiratory fitness, and for hypertension and diabetes specifically; no significant effect was found for body mass index, physical health, mental health, or for cardiovascular disease. Aerobic exercise was the only modality with a statistically significant pooled effect, but because the modalities did not differ significantly from one another, the superiority of any single modality cannot be established from these data, and the same applies to the regional comparison. Given the very high heterogeneity, these pooled estimates should be interpreted with caution. The findings nonetheless reinforce the importance of promoting physical activity and support the development of tailored, region-sensitive public health strategies alongside better-standardized primary trials in underrepresented regions.

Article.Title: Anomalous terrigenous input to the continental margin of tropical western South Atlantic at the Pleistocene-Holocene transition
Article.Authors: Leite J.; Bastos A.; da Silva Quaresma V.; de Almeida F.; Rodrigues A.; Neto A.; de Mello R.; Catunda M.; Mulitza S.; Chiessi C.
Article.Abstract: Continental slopes off southeastern Brazil preserve key records of terrigenous sediment transfer during the last deglaciation, yet the processes controlling these deposits remain poorly constrained. Here, we analyse four sediment cores to investigate the origin of a distinct terrigenous-rich layer (TM facies) identified across all records. Sedimentological, inorganic geochemical, and geochronological data were integrated to reconstruct the depositional history of this interval. The results show a marked increase in sedimentation rates and in ln(Fe/Ca), ln(Ti/Ca), and ln(Al/Si) ratios between ~ 13 and 8.0 cal ka BP, indicating increased input of fine terrigenous material. This interval is not observed elsewhere in the records, suggesting specific paleoenvironmental conditions during its formation. We interpret the TM facies as the result of remobilization of sediments previously stored on the outer continental shelf and transported downslope during late deglacial sea-level rise. Although precipitation increased in northeastern Brazil during Heinrich Stadial 1 and the Younger Dryas, paleoclimate records indicate no substantial increase over southeastern Brazil. Thus, enhanced fluvial discharge is unlikely to explain the observed pattern. Instead, progressive flooding of the Abrolhos Shelf reestablished shelf–slope connectivity, promoting sediment remobilization. The sedimentary response to this eustatic forcing was likely conditioned by the local geomorphological context, which favored sediment storage on the continental shelf during lowstands and subsequent shelf–slope connectivity during the last post-LGM marine transgression. These results indicate that eustatic forcing was the primary control on terrigenous deposition, with climate playing a secondary role.

Article.Title: RankCloak conceals the surface form of synthetic cryptographic artifacts in language model generated text
Article.Authors: Mantzaris A.
Article.Abstract: Cryptographic artifacts such as hashes, nonces, identifiers, and ciphertexts are conspicuous when transmitted in their usual textual forms. RankCloak conceals this recognizable form by encoding each synthetic artifact through language model token choices, producing cover text that does not directly display the artifact. We evaluated 480 public deterministic artifacts from eight classes with three open source model families and 18 English prompt templates. The decoder recovered every artifact across 6,480 primary trials when the original token sequence and shared generation configuration were preserved. Recovery from rendered cover text succeeded in 61.1 percent of the tested robustness sample, whereas the tested blockquote and trimming operation, paraphrasing, and decoding with another model failed. Stronger detection tests separated duplicate and near-duplicate material before training, withheld model families, included human written comparisons, and used probabilities from the generating model. Under these tests, encoded covers were often detectable. Restricting embedding to positions with several plausible next words reduced some detection signals but also reduced capacity and increased cover length. Detecting a possible encoding does not itself display or reconstruct the concealed artifact. RankCloak demonstrates concealment and recovery specifically for cryptographic artifacts under a shared configuration while exposing detectability and transmission limitations, but it does not establish the concealment of arbitrary natural-language messages.

Article.Title: Intervention against autodigestion enhances cardiovascular stability and trauma response in the elder
Article.Authors: dos Santos F.; Muller C.; Moreira N.; Li J.; Schmid-Schönbein G.; Kistler E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An important step to improve the quality of life in older adults is to reduce their heightened sensitivity to trauma challenges, such as elective surgery. Our recent evidence indicates that a mechanism behind aging and reduced quality of life involves the leakage of pancreatic digestive enzymes from the gastrointestinal tract into the bloodstream and peripheral organs. The leaked enzymes degrade plasma proteins, extracellular matrix proteins, and membrane receptors, leading to cell and organ dysfunctions typical for aging. Here, we hypothesize that blockade of leaked digestive enzymes improves the quality of life in the elderly and their response to trauma. A one-week oral treatment of old rats with a pancreatic digestive serine protease (trypsin) inhibitor, without significantly impairing normal digestion, decreases protease activity in the central circulation and benefits older individuals facing trauma. We find that this pretreatment stabilizes the cardiovascular system of aged rats, improves metabolic disturbances caused by hemorrhagic shock, and significantly enhances their response to shock. Systolic and mean arterial blood pressures are normalized, and the baroreflex, which is severely impaired in aged rats, is substantially improved by the pretreatment. The survival rate during central blood pressure reduction is significantly higher in old rats pretreated against trypsin activity. The evidence confirms our hypothesis that aging results from the uncontrolled activity of digestive enzymes outside the pancreas and intestine, and that blocking their activity improves the ability of aged rats to withstand cardiovascular challenges. The proposed intervention protocol against the degrative action of digestive enzymes is clinically applicable and testable.

Article.Title: Phosphate-treated siwak as a calcium phosphate–bearing bioactive material for fluoride-free oral care: physicochemical characterization and in vitro enamel microhardness recovery
Article.Authors: Yerou A.; Elmeguenni M.; Bouiadjra B.; Albedah A.
Article.Abstract: Phosphate-treated siwak ( Salvadora persica ) was developed as a calcium phosphate-bearing bioactive material and evaluated for its in vitro enamel remineralization potential when incorporated into a fluoride-free toothpaste. Siwak powder was phosphate-treated with phosphoric acid under controlled conditions and characterized by X-ray fluorescence (XRF), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM/EDS), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Fluoride-free laboratory toothpastes were formulated with phosphate-treated siwak or hydroxyapatite (HAp) as the active material. Twenty independent bovine teeth were allocated to four groups ( n = 5 per group). Surface Vickers microhardness was evaluated at the tooth level, with five indentations averaged per specimen, and analyzed using Welch’s one-way ANOVA followed by Games–Howell pairwise comparisons. Phosphate treatment produced Ca/P-bearing signatures by XRF/EDS together with phosphate-associated FTIR and XRD features. Mean surface microhardness was 265.93 ± 2.12 HV in sound enamel, 127.93 ± 5.93 HV in the post-demineralization reference group, 300.19 ± 5.08 HV after the 7-day phosphate-treated siwak protocol, and 295.25 ± 13.31 HV after the HAp protocol. Overall group differences were significant (Welch ANOVA: F(3, 7.71) = 813.21, p < 0.0001), while no statistically significant difference was detected between the two treatment groups ( p = 0.863). Enamel FTIR showed qualitative condition-associated differences in phosphate-region features. These findings support preliminary proof-of-concept evidence that phosphate-treated siwak can participate in a treatment protocol associated with enamel surface microhardness recovery. Because the post-demineralization reference was measured immediately whereas the treated groups underwent an additional 7-day period in artificial saliva, the microhardness comparisons represent the net effect of the complete treatment protocol rather than the isolated effect of the active toothpaste component.

Article.Title: AFODRLS: an autonomic fog framework for task offloading using deep reinforcement learning with adaptive scheduling
Article.Authors: Alturki S.; Ghoneim A.
Article.Abstract: Task offloading in fog computing is difficult because nodes are heterogeneous, workloads are non-stationary, and failures are frequent. Autonomic computing offers self-management through the MAPE-K loop but relies on static rules, and heuristic schedulers degrade under non-stationary or adversarial workloads. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is promising, yet studies usually evaluate one algorithm in isolation without statistical validation. We introduce AFODRLS , a framework that realizes all four MAPE-K self-* properties in one loop driving four interchangeable DRL agents (DQN, DDQN, SAC, PPO), with an Adaptive Meta-Controller that selects between heuristic and DRL scheduling and an Online Capacity Estimator that replaces fixed capacity scaling. On a seven-level complexity benchmark (1,465 simulation trials), advanced heuristics outperform DRL at levels 1–4; at level 5 the best DRL agents match the best advanced heuristic; and at levels 6–7 the DRL group outperforms the heuristic groups, with DDQN (level 6) and DDQN/PPO (level 7) exceeding the best heuristic with large effect sizes (Cohen’s \(d>4.5\) , \(p<0.001\) ). The trained policies also transfer zero-shot to two real-world traces (GoCJ and HPC2N), matching the strongest heuristic on success rate without retraining.

Article.Title: Physics–informed multimodal deep learning for real-time defect detection and process monitoring in solid-state additive manufacturing
Article.Authors: Kumar T.; Kichena P.; Rathore P.
Article.Abstract: Defect-free fabrication remains a major challenge in realizing industrial adoption of solid-state additive manufacturing (SSAM) due to thermomechanical interactions prone to cause defects during layer-by-layer fabrication, some of which are non-trivial to capture with conventional process monitoring. Signal-based models can be insensitive to subtle defect precursors, while image-based approaches offer fine morphological details but are generally limited to offline validation steps. This work proposes MCAT-Phys, a physics-informed multimodal deep learning framework that learns the joint distribution of acoustic emission, torque, and infrared signals with microstructural details from FESEM and optical microscopy to identify process-induced defects. Specifically, the framework was compared against (i) conventional unimodal baseline approaches such as CNN, ResNet, and U-Net; (ii) advanced unimodal models such as a Temporal Transformer for process signals, and SegFormer for microstructural images; and (iii) the proposed MCAT-Phys hybrid model. The framework’s robustness was statistically analyzed using five-fold cross-validation, confidence-interval analysis, and paired t-tests. MCAT-Phys achieved an accuracy of 94.2%, and F1-score of 0.88, an AUROC of 0.97, and an AUPRC of 0.96, outperforming the evaluated unimodal baselines. Error analysis further indicated an approximately 30% reduction in false negatives and a 40% improvement in crack-boundary continuity. These results illustrate that physics-informed cross-modal fusion over process dynamics, microstructural information, and process meta-data can be realized. In summary, MCAT-Phys provides a promising yet interpretable basis for SSAM defect monitoring but requires further validation across machines and material and processing conditions before industrial implementation.

Article.Title: Prediction of IgE-mediated allergic reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics using machine learning models
Article.Authors: Bahrami S.; Fallahpour M.; Fattahi A.; Nabavi M.; Bemanian M.; Arshi S.; Shokri S.; Raz N.; Tavakoli S.; Seyedsalehi S.; Kazemifard M.; Sharifinejad N.
Article.Abstract: IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics represent one of the most prevalent and potentially life-threatening forms of drug allergy, often involving cutaneous, respiratory, gastrointestinal, and cardiovascular manifestations, including hypotension and hemodynamic instability. Conventional diagnostic approaches such as clinical history assessment and in vivo and in vitro testing are limited by suboptimal sensitivity and specificity as well as restricted availability for many patients. Given these limitations, intelligent data-driven models show promise as complementary tools for supporting more rapid and accurate assessments of allergic risk. This study aimed to develop, train, and evaluate machine-learning models for predicting IgE-mediated allergic reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics and to design a clinical decision-support tool intended to assist physicians in this field. Clinical data were collected from patients referred to an allergy clinic in Iran and subsequently curated for analysis. A total of 322 patient records were evaluated using nine independent variables: age, gender, culprit drug group, time since last reaction, reaction repetition, reaction with another drug from the same class, time-to-onset of drug reactions, reaction severity, and history of other allergies. Multiple machine-learning algorithms were implemented to predict the final clinical diagnosis as the dependent outcome variable, which was established according to EAACI-based clinical assessment. Within the limitations of the balanced single-centre dataset, Random Forest achieved the highest composite mean score in internal cross-validation (0.912), with accuracy of 0.90, sensitivity of 0.90, specificity of 0.89, F-score of 0.90, and AUC of 0.97. In same-centre temporal validation, the Random Forest model was applied to the independent 80-patient dataset without retraining or retuning and achieved accuracy of 0.96, sensitivity of 0.95, specificity of 0.98, F-score of 0.96, AUC of 0.99, and a composite mean score of 0.97. These findings suggest that machine-learning models, particularly Random Forest, may serve as adjunctive tools for structured risk stratification of suspected IgE-mediated beta-lactam hypersensitivity in an allergy-clinic setting. However, this single-centre, balanced, retrospective study should be considered preliminary, and the developed software should be regarded as a research decision-support prototype rather than a tool ready for routine clinical implementation. Further prospective, multicentre validation and direct comparison with established clinical risk-stratification approaches are required before clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Pre-conceptional microbiome alterations in women with recurrent spontaneous abortion: a pilot study
Article.Authors: Dietz-Ziegler S.; Herbst A.; Ruehle J.; Müller J.; Schoppmeier U.; Wolff D.; Poets C.; Hauke J.; Okun J.; Henes M.; Gille C.; Köstlin-Gille N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) remains one of the greatest challenges in reproductive medicine. In many cases, the underlying cause cannot be identified. The gut microbiome plays a crucial role in maintaining health and contributing to disease development, and alterations in its composition have been linked to numerous chronic diseases. However, little is known about the role of the gut microbiome in the pathogenesis of miscarriage. In this study, we analyzed differences in the pre-conceptional microbiome composition of fifteen women with unexplained RSA and twenty-two healthy controls with at least one prior successful pregnancy and no history of miscarriage. Samples were collected​ in Germany between February 2021 and May 2023. Microbial taxonomic alpha and beta diversity as well as differential abundance of taxa were assessed by 16 s rRNA sequencing. Differential expression of serum acyl-carnitines and amino acids was assessed by tandem mass spectrometry. Women with RSA exhibited significantly reduced microbial alpha diversity, as assessed by the Shannon and Simpson indices, compared to controls. Beta diversity analysis revealed a continuous compositional shift between groups along the primary principal coordinate. At the phylum level, RSA was associated with a reduced relative abundance of Firmicutes and an increased abundance of Bacteroidota , resulting in a significantly lower Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio. Genus-level analysis suggested differences in relative abundances between RSA patients and controls, but none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Functional prediction suggested potential alterations in pathways related to lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis and amino acid degradation in RSA-associated microbiomes. Serum metabolomics revealed reduced tryptophan levels in RSA patients. Our findings suggest that specific pre-conceptional existing gut microbiome and serum metabolic alterations may be linked to the risk for RSA. Larger cohort studies and functional characterization of these changes are warranted to validate the translational potential of our results.

Article.Title: Prevalence and genetic variants of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in malaria-endemic communities along the Lake Victoria basin, Kenya
Article.Authors: Musyoka K.; Chan C.; Kagaya W.; Naruse T.; Kongere J.; Omondi P.; Kimura M.; Teramoto I.; Idris Z.; Ngara M.; Narahara C.; Michimuko-Nagahara Y.; Mizukami S.; Masumoto H.; Muto H.; Baba A.; Kanoi B.; Gitaka J.; Hirayama K.; Kaneko A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, a common X-linked disorder in malaria-endemic regions, can cause haemolysis following primaquine treatment. Primaquine is vital for eliminating P. vivax , P. ovale hypnozoites, and P. falciparum gametocytes. Despite increasing non- falciparum malaria and artemisinin-resistant P. falciparum in Sub-Saharan Africa, primaquine uptake remains limited due to safety concerns in G6PD-deficient individuals. We assessed G6PD deficiency prevalence and its association with Plasmodium infections among 1661 individuals from five communities around Lake Victoria in Homa Bay County, Kenya. G6PD activity was measured using the Dojindo G6PD Assay Kit-WST, with deficiency defined as < 30% of the adjusted male median activity. Selected samples were genotyped for G202A, A376G, A542T, G680T, and T968C. Associations with Plasmodium infection and clinical attributes were analysed using ordinal logistic regression. Overall G6PD deficiency prevalence was 6.8% ( n = 113): 9.0% (69/765) in males and 4.9% (44/896) in females. G6PD deficiency was primarily explained by the G202A variant (G6PD A-/Asahi). Of 104 G6PD-deficient individuals genotyped, 66 were hemizygous, 26 homozygous, and 7 heterozygous for G6PD A- or Asahi variants. Whole gene sequencing further revealed G6PD Sibari (A634G) in a deficient male. G6PD deficiency did not protect against Plasmodium infection, however microscopic infections were associated with living in communities with higher parasite prevalence, male sex, young age, severe anaemia, and bed net disuse.

Article.Title: A physics-informed graph attention enhanced CNN-GRU coupling model for fire spread path prediction in chemical industrial parks
Article.Authors: Lei Q.
Article.Abstract: Fire escalation in tank farms is a major process safety risk, but CFD simulation is too slow for emergency use and purely data driven models ignore the irregular layout and the physics of radiative escalation. This work proposes PI-GAT-CNN-GRU, a physics-informed graph attention enhanced CNN-GRU model that forecasts fire spread paths under a strictly causal protocol and decodes node probabilities into ordered cascade paths, with a stochastic decoding of concurrent escalation. Radiation edge weights with an explicit radiative fraction, flame tilt and shielding are injected into graph attention, a causal temporal convolution and a GRU are rolled out autoregressively with quantified error amplification, and a composite loss encodes effective distance attenuation, view factor consistency, wind weighting and cumulative thermal dose, complemented by energy conserving constraints. On 1152 FDS scenarios of a 32 tank park, PI-GAT-CNN-GRU reaches F1 = 0.6187, PR-AUC = 0.6521, MCC = 0.5966 and PHR@Top-3 = 0.6784, against 0.5561, 0.5813, 0.5296 and 0.5789 for the strongest baseline FSTGAT, and the physics loss reduces the violation rate of four physical relations from 25.5% to 12.2%, while scheduled sampling lowers the error amplification ratio from 3.42 to 1.84. F1 retention is at least 80.6% on three further parks without retraining, 87.2% when the 32 tank park is held out and 91.7% on held out procedurally generated layouts, and Kendall’s $$\tau_{b}$$ with the documented order of the 2019 Deer Park tank farm fire is 0.60. The 95% intervals of MC dropout and a deep ensemble cover 89.4% of the empirical ignition frequencies under FDS input perturbations, the forecast error is of the same order as the scatter of the FDS labels, and a 3600 s rollout takes 0.43 s.

Article.Title: Integrating metabolomics and proteomics uncovers core carbon metabolic dysregulation in Wilms’ tumor in children
Article.Authors: Sun M.; Zhang Y.; Zhang P.; Gao J.; Qin X.; Zhang M.; Zhang M.; Ren J.; Zhang X.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: The unclear etiology, insufficient molecular classification strategies, and lack of validated therapeutic targets pose a critical barrier to precision treatment for Wilms’ tumor (WT) in children. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate metabolic dysregulations in WT by integrating metabolomics and proteomics. Metabolomic analysis of plasma samples from 36 WT patients and 36 healthy controls revealed 14 differentially abundant metabolites, including 5 upregulated and 9 downregulated. Proteomic analysis of 7 WT tissues and matched adjacent noncancerous tissues identified 3,378 significantly differentially expressed proteins, of which 1,783 were upregulated and 1,595 were downregulated. Integrated multi-omics analysis further identified three aberrant pathways associated with core carbon metabolism dysregulation: the citric acid cycle, ascorbate and aldarate metabolism, and propanoate metabolism. Collectively, these preliminary findings suggest that dysregulated carbon metabolism is associated with WT pathogenesis.

Article.Title: Coupled-phase transmission and reflection design with Cramé–Rao bound guarantees for STAR-RIS-assisted integrated sensing and communication
Article.Authors: Nishad P.; Sahu A.; Thakur S.
Article.Abstract: A simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface serves users on both of its faces. The transmission and reflection coefficients of a passive lossless element cannot, however, be tuned independently. Existing integrated sensing and communication designs assume independent control and place the target on the reflective side, so the reported performance is an upper bound of unquantified tightness. This work develops a joint transmission and reflection design that retains the quadrature relation and places the target behind the surface. The coupled amplitude and phase constraints reduce to a single real orthogonality condition per element. That condition covers energy splitting and mode switching within one formulation. The nearest feasible point is obtained in closed form from the dominant eigenvector of a real symmetric two-by-two matrix, which holds feasibility to machine precision without a penalty schedule. The angle Cramé–Rao bound for a target observed through the transmissive surface is derived and proved equivalent to a two-by-two linear matrix inequality in the transmit covariance. The sensing guarantee therefore enters the beamforming program without relaxation. Users on opposite faces are paired into nonorthogonal clusters, and the optimal decoding order decomposes across clusters. Enforcing the quadrature relation costs \(14.8\%\) of sum rate at 128 elements under a bound of \(3\times 10^{-4}\) rad \(^{2}\) . That penalty falls to \(12.6\%\) at 256 elements and rises to \(28.0\%\) under the strictest bound tested. Full-space coverage improves by \(75.1\%\) over a reflect-only surface.

Article.Title: Preoperative prediction of lymphovascular invasion in breast cancer using multicenter DCE-MRI radiomics and clinical features
Article.Authors: Li H.; Zeng Y.; Xiao Q.; Wang W.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Lymphovascular invasion (LVI) is a key histopathological factor driving the metastatic process in invasive breast cancer; however, a definitive diagnosis is typically only possible postoperatively. Radiomics based on dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) has shown promise for the preoperative prediction of LVI. Nevertheless, existing studies are largely single-center, lack systematic comparisons of machine learning algorithms, and have insufficient external validation. This study developed and validated multicenter DCE-MRI radiomics models for preoperative LVI prediction, systematically compared ten machine learning algorithms, and quantified the incremental value of radiomics over clinical variables available before surgery. This retrospective multicenter study included 935 female patients with pathologically confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma from three institutions. All patients underwent preoperative 3.0 T DCE-MRI. After manual three-dimensional delineation of regions of interest on DCE-MRI images, 1,197 radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics after image resampling to 2 × 2 × 2 mm³ (B-spline interpolation), intensity normalization, and fixed-bin-width discretization. Feature selection (Mann-Whitney U test, Pearson correlation pruning with |r| > 0.9, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator [LASSO] regression) was confined to the training cohort. Ten classifiers were compared: logistic regression (LR), support vector machines (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), random forests (RF), Extremely Randomized Trees (ExtraTrees), XGBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and multi-layer perceptron (MLP). A primary clinical model was built using only variables available before surgery (age, histological grade, Ki-67, MRI axillary lymph node status, and MRI tumor size); a sensitivity clinical model additionally included postoperative sentinel lymph node (SLN) status. Combined clinical-radiomics models and a nomogram were constructed, and all probability thresholds were fixed at the value maximizing the Youden index in the training set. Performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with the DeLong test, calibration intercept and slope, Brier score, and decision curve analysis (DCA) in a training set, an internal validation set, and two independent external test sets. In the multivariable analysis, SLN status (odds ratio [OR] 5.743, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.693–8.931, p < 0.001) and MRI tumor size (OR 1.413, 95% CI: 1.186–1.684, p < 0.001) were independently associated with LVI; because SLN status is established intraoperatively or postoperatively, the primary clinical model used only the five preoperative variables. Among the ten radiomics algorithms, LR and MLP showed the most stable cross-center performance (LR: AUC 0.841, 0.716, 0.632, and 0.586 in the training, internal validation, test 1, and test 2 cohorts, respectively), whereas complex ensemble methods overfit (Gradient Boosting: 0.991 in training vs. 0.696 and 0.532 externally; XGBoost: 0.894 vs. 0.613 and 0.453). The preoperative combined model achieved AUCs of 0.856, 0.721, 0.665, and 0.603, respectively, significantly outperforming the preoperative clinical model in the training, validation, and test 2 cohorts (DeLong p < 0.001, p = 0.013, and p < 0.001) but not in test 1 ( p = 0.306), and significantly outperforming the radiomics model only in test 1 ( p = 0.026). The incremental value of radiomics was significant in the training cohort (integrated discrimination improvement p < 0.001) but not in the external cohorts. Calibration slopes of the combined model declined externally (0.49, 0.28, and 0.21), indicating that probability estimates require local recalibration. In this multicenter study, LR and MLP were the most robust radiomics classifiers for preoperative LVI prediction, whereas complex ensemble algorithms were prone to overfitting on external validation. The preoperative combined model improved discrimination and clinical net benefit over the clinical model internally, but its external incremental value was inconsistent and its calibration deteriorated in the external cohorts. A sensitivity analysis using postoperative SLN status showed higher absolute performance, underscoring that genuinely preoperative tools trade performance for applicability. These findings emphasize rigorous multicenter benchmarking, recalibration before local deployment, and honest reporting of external performance in radiomics research.

Article.Title: Culturable filamentous fungi isolated from apparently healthy Nile tilapia and targeted screening of aflatoxin biosynthesis-associated genes in representative Aspergillus isolates
Article.Authors: Kholife M.; El-diasty E.; Moawad A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Filamentous fungi are ubiquitous in aquatic and aquaculture environments and may be relevant to fish health and food safety. However, information on culturable filamentous fungi recoverable from apparently healthy Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) in Egyptian aquaculture systems remains limited. This study investigated the genus-level composition, organ-associated distribution, and morphological characteristics of culturable filamentous fungi recovered from apparently healthy O. niloticus collected from commercial fish farms in Kafrelsheikh Governorate, Egypt. Five representative isolates phenotypically assigned to Aspergillus were selected for targeted PCR screening of the aflatoxin biosynthesis-associated genes aflR and aflP ( omtA ). A total of 210 apparently healthy fish were sampled from 11 commercial farms. Fungal isolates recovered from the gills, mouth, liver, spleen, and kidney were cultured on the selected fungal media and preliminarily assigned using conventional macroscopic and microscopic characteristics. Genus-level diversity was assessed using ecological diversity indices. Fish-level fungal recovery and the distribution of recovered isolates among anatomical sites were analyzed separately to account for the possibility of multiple fungal recoveries from individual fish. A total of 129 culturable filamentous fungal isolates representing 11 genera were recovered. Penicillium and Aspergillus were the predominant genera, accounting for 47.29% and 33.33% of the recovered isolates, respectively. Genus-level diversity indices indicated an uneven distribution of isolates among the recovered genera. At the individual-fish level, 118 of the 210 fish showed at least one fungal recovery, corresponding to an overall recovery proportion of 56.2% (95% CI: 49.4–62.7%). The recovered isolates were distributed predominantly in the gills (58.14%) and mouth (27.13%), which together accounted for 85.27% of all the recovered isolates, whereas fewer isolates were recovered from the liver, spleen, or kidney. Among the five screened isolates, aflP ( omtA ) was detected in all five (5/5; 100%), whereas aflR was detected in four (4/5; 80%). These findings demonstrate the presence of selected aflatoxin biosynthesis-associated genetic markers among the screened isolates but do not constitute molecular confirmation of their species identity, expression of the aflatoxin biosynthetic pathway, or actual aflatoxin production. This study provides a culture-dependent baseline of filamentous fungal genera recovered from apparently healthy O. niloticus under applied sampling and culture conditions. Further investigations should incorporate molecular taxonomic confirmation and direct assessment of mycotoxin production.

Article.Title: Integrated intracellular and secretome proteomics reveal compartment-specific responses to plasma-treated water solutions combined with doxorubicin in hypopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Stornelli G.; Cassiani T.; Caponio V.; Bravo S.; Battaglia A.; Ruggieri A.; Sallese M.; Pena C.; Biamonte F.; Casiello M.; Sardella E.; Perrotti V.
Article.Abstract: Cold atmospheric Plasma-Treated Water Solutions (PTWS) carry reactive oxygen and nitrogen species and may enhance chemotherapy, but their effects on the tumour response remain unclear. We used SWATH-MS and DDA proteomics to characterise intracellular and secreted protein changes associated with Air (richer in nitrite) and oxygen (O₂) (richer in H 2 O 2 ) PTWS combined with doxorubicin (DOXO) in FaDu Head and Neck Cancer cells and HaCaT keratinocytes. This discovery-based study aimed to identify treatment-associated proteomic signatures rather than causal mediators. Proteomic responses were formulation-, cell- and compartment-dependent. In FaDu cells, more than 80% of the secreted proteins modified by PTWS + DOXO were not modified by DOXO alone. Air PTWS + DOXO increased extracellular HSP70, HSP10 and RAB11B, whereas O₂ PTWS + DOXO predominantly reduced secreted protein abundance, with 25 of 33 modified proteins decreased, including cathepsin D, HSP27 and moesin. Both PTWS formulations reduced extracellular PRDX6, while HaCaT cells showed fewer and mainly adaptive changes. Secretome changes were only partly reflected by intracellular proteomics, providing complementary information on the treatment response. Overall, PTWS did not simply amplify the response to DOXO but modified it in a formulation- and cell-dependent manner. The identified secretome signatures provide hypotheses for future functional studies and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of tumour-microenvironment remodelling.

Article.Title: Adaptive saliency-guided signal representation for robust brain tumor MRI classification
Article.Authors: Indrakumar K.; Ravikumar M.; Al-mohamadi M.; Karali S.; Thanoon M.; Alrushaid N.; Alhashmi A.; Darem A.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) analysis is often affected by acquisition noise, intensity inhomogeneity, and complex anatomical variations that complicate the extraction of discriminative signal patterns. Although deep learning methods have demonstrated strong performance in medical image analysis, many approaches treat images as visual patterns without explicitly modeling their underlying signal structure. This paper proposes an Adaptive Saliency-Guided Signal Representation (ASGSR) framework that explicitly models MRI data as structured spatial signals. The proposed framework formulates MRI classification as a task-conditioned signal-representation problem in which classification-derived spatial sensitivity determines the subsequent spatial transformation of the MRI signal. The resulting saliency-conditioned representation is subsequently characterized using multi-resolution and statistical operations before probabilistic classification. A Bayesian decision model is employed for classification with posterior-probability-based confidence estimation. Experimental evaluation on multiple publicly available brain MRI datasets demonstrates improved classification performance and robustness under the evaluated conditions compared with the selected convolutional and transformer-based baselines. The method achieves an average classification accuracy of 95.2% and an AUC of 0.97 across the evaluated datasets, while the derived spatial representation exhibits higher PSNR and SSIM under the defined representation-level evaluation protocol. These results indicate that the proposed signal-centric formulation can improve classification performance, robustness to the evaluated perturbations, and the spatial sensitivity representation of MRI inputs under the evaluated experimental conditions.

Article.Title: A Chinese silent speech recognition interface for wireless gesture control of a soft robotic palm
Article.Authors: Wu S.; Juang J.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: In this research, we proposed a Chinese silent speech recognition (SSR) system for fast-reacting and wireless control of a soft pneumatic palm with six gestures in noisy environments. Non-vocal commands containing four, three, and two Chinese characters and syllables are recognized by monitoring facial skin deformations caused by muscle contractions and relaxations via eight flexible crystalline silicon strain gauges. To support fast command recognition, an offline-trained model combining multichannel signal processing, feature extraction and selection, negative-sample training, and random forest classification was adopted. The final seven-class test yielded an accuracy of 93.1% and a macro-F1 score of 0.93. The average post-acquisition time for signal processing, wireless transmission, and palm actuation was approximately 2.7 s, which excludes the 2-s acquisition window. The proposed SSR interface can be extended to a segmented pneumatic palm for complex gesture control or for individual finger-segmented motions.

Article.Title: Rubric-anchored large language model feedback for academic argumentation revision
Article.Authors: Wei J.
Article.Abstract: Generative AI can provide rapid, detailed feedback for student writing, yet its organization may affect how students use feedback during short classroom revision windows. This study examined descriptive outcome and process patterns across rubric-anchored LLM feedback (RA), non-anchored LLM feedback (NA), and an active criteria-aligned self-revision comparison in a four-week intact-class quasi-experiment with 105 Chinese second-year Economics students (three classes, one per condition). Rubric-scored argumentation performance was summarized using covariate-adjusted posttest means, with a maximum possible score of 24. Descriptive adjusted means were highest under RA (14.64), followed by NA (14.21) and Control (14.05). The naive individual-level ANCOVA did not yield a statistically significant Condition term. Descriptive revision-activity summaries based on words added, words deleted, and net word change showed greater textual change under RA across both practice tasks on several indicators. In an exploratory subsample of 24 students, the proportion of suggestions targeting Claim, Evidence, Reasoning, or Counterargument that were adopted or partially adopted was descriptively higher under RA (75.0%) than NA (69.0%). Given the one-class-per-condition design and condition-specific prompts, these findings do not isolate a causal effect of rubric anchoring. Within the GPT-4o-based implementation examined here, rubric-aligned organization warrants further investigation as a design feature for time-limited classroom revision.

Article.Title: Identification of the SNHG14/hsa-miR-577/CLIC4 ceRNA axis reveals the association of CLIC4 with stromal activation and microenvironment remodeling in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Xiao R.; Jiang R.; Chen X.; Chen C.; Zhen Y.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a prevalent malignancy with complex molecular regulatory mechanisms. In this study, we analyzed transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and identified differentially expressed mRNAs, miRNAs, and lncRNAs. Based on this framework, SNHG14/hsa-miR-577/CLIC4 was identified as key competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) of interest for further investigation. Subsequent functional analyses suggested that CLIC4 was closely associated with tumor microenvironment remodeling and stromal activation-related biological processes. Gene set enrichment analyses (GSEA) revealed that increased CLIC4 expression was positively correlated with pathways and signatures associated with epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling, angiogenesis, and matrisome remodeling, thereby supporting its potential role in modulating the stromal characteristics of CRC. Moreover, ceRNA-based screening yielded potential upstream regulatory insights for CLIC4, establishing a foundational understanding of its post-transcriptional regulation in CRC. In summary, our findings underscore CLIC4 as a potential biomarker linked to stromal activation and microenvironmental remodeling in CRC, offering candidate regulatory insights for forthcoming mechanistic and translational investigations.

Article.Title: Genome-wide characterization of Plasmodium vivax infections in local travelers and non-travelers from the Peruvian Amazon
Article.Authors: Safarpour M.; Cabrera-Sosa L.; Kattenberg J.; Deyaert R.; Rosanas-Urgell A.; Vinetz J.; Van geertruyden J.; Gamboa D.; Delgado-Ratto C.
Article.Abstract: In areas progressing toward malaria elimination, distinguishing locally acquired from imported malaria infections is essential for targeted surveillance. We used whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to characterize Plasmodium vivax infections in individuals with reported local travel and non-travelers in three communities in the Peruvian Amazon: Libertad ( n = 24), Gamitanacocha ( n = 23), and Urco Miraño ( n = 9). Traveler-associated infections in Libertad showed higher genetic diversity than non-travelers (median = 0.375 vs. 0.153). Pairwise fixation index (F st ) showed low differentiation between Libertad and Gamitanacocha (F st =0.056), but higher differentiation between Urco Miraño and Libertad (F st =0.548) and Gamitanacocha (F st =0.773). PCA and DAPC showed clear clustering of Urco Miraño parasites, while Libertad and Gamitanacocha partially overlapped. Traveler-associated infections did not form distinct clusters and mostly remained connected to non-traveler infections. ADMIXTURE indicated greater heterogeneity among travelers, and IBD identified two unconnected traveler-associated infections overall. These findings support integrating genomic and epidemiological data to interpret mobility-associated malaria transmission.

Article.Title: Scoring consistency of teachers and artificial intelligence algorithms in written expression assessment: a comparative quantitative study
Article.Authors: Akçay A.; Köçeri K.; Tümen T.; Safalı S.
Article.Abstract: Written expression assessment at the secondary school level involves complex interactions among text genre, evaluator type, and student characteristics. The present study examined the degree of agreement, divergence, and patterning between scores produced by four large language model (LLM)-based algorithms, ChatGPT, Grok, Minimax, and Gemini, and those assigned by human teachers when rating texts composed by secondary school students. A total of 122 students (63 female, 59 male), aged approximately 11–14 years and enrolled in grades 6, 7, and 8 at a public secondary school in Turkey, participated in the study and composed their texts in Turkish. Each student produced one text in a randomly assigned genre: folktale, poetry, or biography. All raters, both human teachers and AI algorithms, evaluated the texts using an identical five-dimensional analytic rubric. Inter-rater agreement was quantified via Pearson correlations and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), while score differences across evaluator type, text genre, and gender were examined using mixed-design ANOVA with Bonferroni-adjusted paired-samples t-tests for pairwise comparisons and independent-samples t-tests. ChatGPT demonstrated the highest alignment with teacher scores ( r = .78, ICC = 0.78). In contrast, Minimax showed the weakest correspondence ( r = .71). Text genre did not exert a statistically significant main effect on scores (F(2, 119) = 0.81, p = .445, partial η 2 = 0.01); however, a statistically significant evaluator-by-genre interaction was detected (F(8, 476) = 3.77, p < .001, partial η 2 = 0.06), such that human teachers scored poetry markedly lower than the other genres. In contrast, AI systems did not show this pattern. Gender-related score differences were observed exclusively in teacher evaluations (d = 0.50), whereas no statistically significant gender differences were detected in any of the four AI algorithms’ scores (all p ≥ .198). These findings indicate that LLM-based algorithms hold promise as formative feedback tools particularly ChatGPT, whose scores aligned most closely with teacher judgments across dimensions and genres, making it best suited to generating rapid, low-stakes draft feedback that students and teachers can use to guide revision while also revealing algorithm-specific limitations, most notably Minimax’s weaker alignment with teacher scores, that preclude direct substitution for human judgment in high-stakes writing assessment.

Article.Title: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm with cat qubits
Article.Authors: Vikstål P.; García-Álvarez L.; Puri S.; Ferrini G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)–a prominent candidate for near-term quantum computing applications–is tailored to find approximate solutions to combinatorial optimization problems using shallow quantum circuits. In this work, we investigate implementations of QAOA based on cat qubits, where the logical states $$|0\rangle$$ and $$|1\rangle$$ are represented by coherent states of opposite amplitudes, $$|\alpha \rangle$$ and $$|-\alpha \rangle$$ . Within this encoding, the primary source of noise–photon loss–induces a bias toward Z -type errors. We focus specifically on an imlementation employing Kerr resonators. By numerically simulating the gate sequences required for QAOA on these nonlinear resonators, we analyze performance on Max-Cut problems and benchmark it against conventional qubits realized as ideal two-level systems subject to single-photon loss. Our findings indicate that the use of cat qubits leads to improved approximation ratios for random Max-Cut instances compared to standard qubit encodings.

Article.Title: Activities of daily living, accident history, and environmental ergonomic conditions in nursing home residents: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Fallah H.; Sheibani M.; Rezaeipandari H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of the ageing population underscores the increasing importance of safety and functional independence in long-term care settings. This study aimed to examine the association between activities of daily living (ADL), accident history, and environmental ergonomic conditions among older adults residing in nursing homes. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2024 among residents of all seven licensed nursing homes in Shiraz, Iran, under the supervision of the Welfare Organization (Behzisti). Of the 591 residents assessed for eligibility, 550 were included in the final analysis. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, a standardized activity of daily living (ADL) scale, and an ergonomic assessment checklist. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.0. The mean age of participants was 78.42 ± 5.63 years, and 66.7% were classified as ADL-dependent. ADL-dependent residents reported a higher frequency of accidents in unadjusted analyses; however, this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for demographic and functional characteristics. Among the variables included in the final regression model, mobility limitation and hearing limitation showed the strongest associations with accident history. Slipping was the most frequently reported type of accident, and the environmental assessment identified multiple ergonomic hazards, with slippery flooring being the most common. Mobility and hearing limitations were the strongest individual-level factors associated with accident history, whereas ADL dependence was not significantly associated with accident history after adjustment. Widespread environmental ergonomic deficiencies, particularly slippery flooring, may represent potentially modifiable targets for improving safety in nursing home settings.

Article.Title: Associations between nutritional indices and self-reported history of colorectal cancer in middle‑aged and older adults: a cross‑sectional study based on NHANES 1999–2020
Article.Authors: Fu Z.; Qin S.; Jiang H.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between nutritional indices (i.e., the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index [GNRI], Prognostic Nutritional Index [PNI], Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index [ALI], and the Controlling Nutritional Status [CONUT]) and a self-reported history of colorectal cancer (CRC) using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999–2020. Weighted multivariate logistic regression was employed to evaluate the associations of GNRI, PNI, ALI, and CONUT with a self-reported history of CRC. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to examine dose–response relationships. Subgroup analyses were performed to test for potential effect modifications. Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to balance baseline characteristics in sensitivity analyses, ensuring the robustness of the results. Among 25,169 eligible participants, 327 (1.3%) had a self-reported history of CRC. Weighted logistic regression revealed that PNI (OR = 0.957, 95% CI: 0.925–0.990) was negatively associated with a self-reported history of CRC, whereas CONUT was positively associated (OR = 1.274, 95% CI: 1.156–1.404). Both GNRI and PNI demonstrated nonlinear negative relationships ( P for nonlinear = 0.010 and 0.019, respectively). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential effect modifications by diabetes for GNRI and by sex for CONUT. The inverse association was seemingly stronger in diabetic participants, and the positive association was seemingly stronger in females. Sensitivity analyses after PSM confirmed the stability of these findings. GNRI, PNI, and CONUT were associated with a self-reported history of CRC in middle-aged and older adults, suggesting a link between systemic immunonutritional status and a self-reported history of CRC.

Article.Title: A new ensemble of metrics for quantifying free-throw shooting performance using NBA player-tracking data
Article.Authors: McGrath J.; Glazer A.; Bushong V.; Nguyen M.; Goldsberry K.
Article.Abstract: With the NBA’s adoption of in-game limb tracking in 2023, Sony’s Hawk-Eye system now captures high-resolution, 3D poses of players and the ball 60 times per second. Linking these data to key events opens a new era in NBA analytics. Here, we leverage a large dataset of 21,964 shot attempts from 72 NBA players to introduce a novel ensemble of metrics for evaluating free-throw shooting. Inspired by baseball analytics, we introduce command, which quantifies the quality of a free throw by measuring a shooter’s accuracy and precision near the basket’s bullseye. This metric recognizes that some makes (or misses) are better than others and captures a player’s ability to execute quality attempts consistently. We demonstrate that command provides more diagnostic information about shot execution than traditional make-or-miss statistics. In a within-season temporal holdout, early-season command predicted late-season shooting percentage at least as well as early-season shooting percentage itself. To identify what is associated with command, we define launch-based metrics assessing consistency in release velocity, angle, and 3D position. Players with greater touch, i.e., more consistent launch dynamics, exhibit stronger command as they can reliably control their shot trajectory. Finally, we develop a physics model to identify the range of launch conditions that result in a make and to determine which launch conditions are most robust to small perturbations. This framework reveals “safe” launch regions and identifies the specific launch parameters most associated with shooting inconsistency for individual players, providing a diagnostic framework that could inform future player development work.

Article.Title: Adapting the SWOT matrix as a territorial planning tool for urban flood management
Article.Authors: Rezende O.; de Magalhães P.; Gomes M.; Thomaz F.; Lemos M.; Miguez M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urbanization significantly alters watershed runoff, increasing peak flows, reducing base flows, and degrading river ecosystems. Without adequate control measures, urbanization increases flood vulnerability, heightening flood risks and damaging urban infrastructure. Recent academic and technical perspectives emphasize the importance of efficient stormwater management, advocating for a systemic approach to address urban flooding risks. However, setting goals for stormwater management planning remains challenging due to its inherent complexity and multidisciplinary nature. This study introduces a novel framework, inspired by the SWOT analysis, designed to comprehensively evaluate urban flood potential and identify integrated flood control measures that combine natural and built environments demands. Applied to the development of the Maricá Stormwater Management Plan (Brazil), the framework proved feasible for structuring a diagnosis of current and future conditions and for deriving 60 specific objectives, consolidated into six general objectives. Because it relies on information commonly available to municipalities, the framework has potential for adaptation to other contexts, although its effectiveness in reducing flood risk depends on the implementation of the proposed actions and remains to be evaluated.

Article.Title: Can internal load associate with adaptation? A comparison of 1v1 and 3v3 basketball training in physically inactive female college students
Article.Authors: Li L.; Wang Y.; Zhou H.; Chen J.; Matta Mello Portugal E.; Trybulski R.; Clemente F.
Article.Abstract: This study compared internal-load profiles between 1v1 and 3v3 basketball training and examined whether accumulated internal load was associated with changes in estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max) in physically inactive female college students. The longitudinal estimated VO₂max analysis included 63 randomized participants allocated to 1v1 basketball training, 3v3 basketball training, or a non-exercising control condition. Internal-load and dose-response analyses were restricted to the 42 exercisers because the control group had no training-load exposure. Participants in the exercise groups completed three supervised 60-min sessions per week for 8 weeks. Internal load was quantified using accumulated session-RPE (ΣsRPE) and mean peak heart rate (HRpeak), with CR10 expressed as the algebraic equivalent of ΣsRPE divided by the fixed total training duration. Compared with 3v3, 1v1 produced higher ΣsRPE (12,174 ± 203 vs. 11,351 ± 229 AU; mean difference, 823 AU; 95% CI, 688 to 958; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 3.80). Mean HRpeak was also higher in 1v1 than in 3v3 (178.33 ± 0.83 vs. 177.49 ± 0.50 bpm; mean difference, 0.83 bpm; 95% CI, 0.40 to 1.26; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 1.22), although the absolute difference was physiologically small. Estimated VO₂max increased in 1v1 by 1.97 mL kg −1 min −1 (95% CI, 1.40 to 2.55; p < 0.001) and in 3v3 by 2.45 mL kg −1 min −1 (95% CI, 1.60 to 3.31; p < 0.001), whereas the control group showed no clear change (0.07 mL kg −1 min −1 ; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.24; p = 0.348). The group difference in pre-to-post change was statistically clear (F(2,60) = 18.93, p < 0.001, η² = 0.387), with greater improvements in both exercise groups than in control and no clear difference between 1v1 and 3v3. Among exercisers, ΔVO₂max was not clearly associated with ΣsRPE ( r = -0.050, 95% CI, -0.348 to 0.258; p = 0.755) or mean HRpeak ( r = -0.130, 95% CI, -0.418 to 0.181; p = 0.411). Neither association met the prespecified two-sided α = 0.05 criterion, and both 95% confidence intervals included the null value ( r = 0). These findings indicate that both basketball formats improved estimated aerobic fitness compared with control, while 1v1 imposed greater global internal load than 3v3. In this sample, and using the available global load indices, no statistically clear dose–response association was detected. Registration: The study protocol was registered in the ISRCTN (24697262).

Article.Title: A two-stage cascade framework for traffic sign detection: reproduction and boundary analysis
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Xiang Z.; Huang H.; Li M.; Guo H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traffic sign detection in adverse conditions remains difficult because small, distant signs and degraded illumination act together. This paper reports a reduced-scale reproduction and boundary analysis of a cascade framework for traffic sign detection, comprising multi-dimensional preprocessing, a fast-screening / fine-recheck cascade, and a rule-based semantic gate. We characterise the framework by condition, showing where it works and where it fails. On TT100K (45 classes; 3016-image official test split), a YOLOv8n screening stage trained for 20 epochs reaches mAP@0.5 of 0.187 ± 0.005 over three seeds. Component ablations show that the full pipeline does not outperform a confidence-only cascade on clean data, and that preprocessing yields no measurable benefit in clean conditions. Cross-dataset evaluation on CCTSDB reveals monotonic degradation with sign size (recall 0.323 for XL, 0.002 for XS) and pronounced weakness at night and in rain; preprocessing improves F1 by 30% at night but is ineffective in rain and for small signs. A rule-based semantic gate modifies only 0.66% of detections and loses true positives in 29% of its changes. End-to-end latency on our hardware is 239 ms (median), dominated by CPU preprocessing, giving a single-stream capacity of 1.6 frames/s. We conclude that the cascade skeleton is implementable and that small-sign detection and preprocessing cost are the binding constraints.

Article.Title: Social status and status loss do not influence alcohol-related behaviors in rats
Article.Authors: Coppola A.; Verma A.; Augier G.; Holm L.; Augier E.; Heilig M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impoverished social conditions have been reported to shape the vulnerability to develop alcohol use disorder in humans. However, how social environments mediate their effects on addictive behaviors is not known. In this study, we established a rat model to investigate the role of social status in alcohol-related behaviors, using operant self-administration paradigms. We screened male ( n = 76) and female ( n = 88) Wistar rats for dominance-like behavior using the tube test. Then, we forced half of the “dominant” animals to lose their social status to their subordinates while leaving the remaining animals’ social status unchanged. Finally, we tested the effects of social status and social status loss on emotional behaviors, including anxiety-like behavior and social preference and on addiction-like behaviors, including motivation for alcohol self-administration and resistance to foot-shock punishment. Both male and female rats showed a stable winning phenotype in the tube test that was predicted by social preference in males but not in females. Despite finding robust sex differences, with males being more motivated to get alcohol than females and females being more resistant to punishment than males, neither social status nor social status loss affected any of the alcohol-related behaviors or emotional behaviors.
