Article.Title: β-cyclodextrin encapsulation of Heracleum persicum essential oil for improved stability, controlled release, and food-related biological applications
Article.Authors: Rahimian H.; Nikzad M.; Hamedi S.
Article.Abstract: Heracleum persicum essential oil (HPEO) exhibits antioxidant and antibacterial activities, but its application is limited by volatility, poor aqueous solubility, and low stability. To address these limitations, HPEO was encapsulated in β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) to form inclusion complexes (HPEO/βCD-ICs). Three HPEO/β-CD mass ratios (10:90, 15:85, and 20:80, w/w) were investigated to evaluate the effects of formulation composition on encapsulation performance and physicochemical characteristics. The resulting HPEO/βCD-ICs exhibited mean hydrodynamic diameters of 397 to 593 nm and polydispersity index values below 0.3. The 15:85 formulation was selected for further investigation based on its highest zeta potential (+ 58.3 ± 1.95 mV), together with an acceptable particle size and encapsulation efficiency. FT-IR spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and thermal analyses provided complementary evidence supporting inclusion-complex formation and changes in thermal stability following encapsulation. Encapsulation improved the preservation of antioxidant activity during 30 days of storage under light and dark conditions. Moreover, encapsulation reduced the minimum bactericidal concentrations against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus . HPEO release increased with temperature and relative humidity (RH), reaching 28.1% after 15 days at 40 °C and 75% RH. Release kinetics were generally well described by the Weibull model. Overall, β-CD inclusion complexation represents a promising approach to improving the storage stability and antibacterial performance of HPEO, supporting further investigation of its potential applications in food preservation and active packaging.

Article.Title: Effects of recycled PET aggregate size and replacement level on hot mix asphalt performance
Article.Authors: Mohammadi R.; Ameri M.; Karamroudi M.; Jarrahi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing accumulation of plastic waste has intensified the need for sustainable reuse strategies in construction materials. This study investigates the feasibility of using recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) from post‑consumer bottles as a partial replacement for natural aggregates in hot mix asphalt (HMA) using the dry mixing method, emphasizing the influence of particle size and replacement level on HMA performance. rPET particles with natural‑aggregate‑like physical characteristics were produced and sieved into standard size fractions to function as rPET aggregates. The adhesion behavior and mechanical properties of rPET aggregates were evaluated and compared with limestone aggregates used in this study under different temperature conditions. HMA performance was assessed through dynamic creep tests (flow number and permanent deformation) at 40 °C, and moisture susceptibility and indirect tensile fatigue tests at 25 °C. To investigate the effect of particle size, 10% of natural aggregates (by volume) were replaced with rPET aggregates in five size ranges from ≤ 0.3 to 19 mm, and the most effective range was used to determine the optimum replacement level. The results showed that at medium-to-high temperatures, rPET had better interfacial adhesion with bitumen than with limestone, and rPET aggregates performed better in the LAA and AIV tests. Optimal performance was achieved using 4.75–12.5 mm rPET aggregates, where 18% replacement increased creep resistance by 57% and reduced moisture susceptibility by 7%, while 16% replacement improved fatigue life by 295%. These findings demonstrate that rPET aggregates provide an environmentally sustainable alternative for enhancing HMA performance.

Article.Title: Joint latent class mixed model trajectories of estimated glomerular filtration rate related to mortality and physical activity in older adults
Article.Authors: Weinmayr G.; Braisch J.; Klenk J.; Denkinger M.; Dallmeier D.; Rothenbacher D.; Peter R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deterioration of renal function occurs with age, leading in many individuals to chronic kidney disease, considerable disability and premature mortality. The trajectories of kidney function decline and potential protective factors remain poorly understood, especially in older individuals. We therefore investigated eGFR-decline trajectories related to mortality as well as the influence of physical activity patterns on trajectory membership in a population-based cohort of older individuals. 1,506 community-dwelling adults aged $$\:\ge\:$$ 65 years were recruited in 2009 and followed up for up to three times. Trajectories of eGFR-decline and their relation with mortality were determined using joint latent class models. The association of physical activity (PA) and sedentary behavior (SB), determined by accelerometer measurements at baseline, with class-membership was studied with logistic regression. There were 2,812 observations on eGFR. We identified two trajectories, one starting with a lower mean baseline eGFR value and showing a stronger decline over time and higher mortality. In adjusted models, we found robust inverse associations of time spent in PA and total steps with being in this trajectory (Odds ratios with 95%-confidence intervals of 0.72 [0.60, 0.87] for 10 min and 0.73 [0.62, 0.86] for 1000 steps); SB was positively associated with this trajectory (2.51 [1.65, 3.81] for 100 min). PA was negatively and SB was positively associated with the worse trajectory. This may indicate that interventions for increasing PA may potentially be viable strategies to prevent impaired renal function and slow age-related functional decline in older individuals and should be investigated in future studies.

Article.Title: Burden and case mix of adolescent finger fractures and dislocations from selected ball and stick sports in US emergency departments
Article.Authors: Huang S.; Chen D.; Huang Y.; Guo M.; Shi Y.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Finger fractures and dislocations are common acute hand injuries in youth ball and stick sports, but updated national emergency department (ED) estimates by sport are limited. We analyzed public CPSC NEISS annual archived data for 2015–2025. The main cohort included adolescents aged 10–18 years with primary finger injuries, primary diagnosis of fracture or dislocation, and verified selected ball and stick sport product/activity codes in Product_1 or Product_2. National estimates used NEISS sample weights, with variances estimated by Taylor linearization using NEISS stratum and primary sampling unit variables. Estimates were flagged using CPSC instability criteria. A survey-weighted logistic model estimated the odds that a presenting injury was coded as a dislocation rather than a fracture; this is a conditional case-mix comparison among presenting patients, not an injury-risk estimate. Annual estimates were computed under each year's own sample design and regressed on treatment year, with the covariance between years estimated from hospitals reporting in both years. The cohort included 16,066 unweighted NEISS records, representing an estimated 441,441 ED visits nationally (95% CI 341,825–541,056). The largest weighted sport groups were football (166,972; 95% CI 126,984–206,959; 37.8%), basketball (154,526; 95% CI 119,596–189,455; 35.0%), and baseball/softball (40,297; 95% CI 30,159–50,434; 9.1%). Fractures accounted for 83.2% (95% CI 81.7–84.8) and dislocations for 16.8% (95% CI 15.3–18.4) of weighted visits. Annual weighted estimates were highest in 2015 (52,516; 95% CI 41,665–63,367) and lowest in 2020 (18,071; 95% CI 12,467–23,674) and declined by 2.7% per year across 2015–2025 under the primary specification (95% CI 0.5–4.9; p = 0.018); the increase in 2024 coincided with a redesign of the NEISS hospital sample. In the adjusted model, the odds of dislocation relative to fracture increased with age (16–18 vs 10–12 years: OR 4.86, 95% CI 3.94–5.99; p < 0.001). Selected ball and stick sports accounted for a substantial national ED burden of adolescent finger fractures and dislocations, with sport-specific differences in case mix. Among adolescents presenting with one of these two diagnoses, older age was associated with higher adjusted odds that the injury was a dislocation rather than a fracture, representing a difference in diagnostic case mix rather than a greater frequency or risk of dislocation. These findings support sport-aware prevention, early recognition of potentially unstable finger injuries, and cautious interpretation of small subgroup estimates.

Article.Title: SkinFusionNet: MobileNetV2 and vision transformer hybrid deep learning model with automated skin cancer classification
Article.Authors: Zeeshan H.; Iftikhar M.; Rehman A.; Bhatti S.; Jaffar A.; Muaad A.; Heyat M.
Article.Abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most widespread and potentially fatal diseases worldwide, with millions of new cases diagnosed every year. Detecting malignant skin lesions early and accurately is crucial for improving patient survival and can also help reduce the overall cost of treatment. Nevertheless, the conventional methods of diagnosing are usually time-consuming, subjective, and dependent on the skills of a clinician, thus not providing homogeneous results. In order to solve such shortcomings, this paper presents an original hybrid deep learning model, SkinFusionNet (SFN), as an automated skin lesion classifier based on dermoscopic images. The suggested SFN model is a synergetic integration of the advantages of MobileNetV2 and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures the ability to extract local features efficiently by using MobileNetV2 and the ability to learn long-range contextual dependencies by ViT. The manipulation of both fine-grained lesion textures and larger image structures by such integration results in the high diagnostic ability of SFN at a wide range of imaging settings. The model was trained and tested on the 2018 ISIC dataset which had been augmented and balanced to equalize malignant and benign samples at 3,000 and 3,000, respectively. With SFN, outstanding performance was observed with 95.44 per cent accuracy, 95.48 per cent precision, 95.44 per cent recall and a Dice score of 0.9544, which is high compared to current CNN based and hybrid models like ResNet, DenseNet and MobileNet variants. Grad-CAM visualizations were used to mark important areas of the images that had an impact on model predictions to increase clinical trust and interpretability to offer important information about the decision-making process. The findings have shown that SFN can be an effective, interpretable and high-performance framework used in the initial detection of skin cancer. It can be easily deployed in the real world due to its lightweight nature and good ability to generalize, especially in healthcare settings that have limited resources. The given strategy is an important move on the way to making explainable AI a part of dermatological diagnostics, which would make the process of skin cancer screening faster, more credible, and more accessible.

Article.Title: Tissue-specific distribution of toxic metals and dietary risk indicators in commercial marine fish from the Chabahar coast, Oman Sea
Article.Authors: Pakzad-Toochaei S.; Abyar H.
Article.Abstract: The accuracy of seafood safety evaluations in industrializing coastal ecosystems has been constrained by the lack of integrated and tissue-specific assessments. This study addresses this gap by tailoring a comprehensive, multi-indicator evaluation of heavy metal, selenium–mercury interactions, and associated human health risks in three commercially important marine fish species from the Chabahar coast in the Oman Sea. A total of 36 specimens were analyzed across muscle, liver, and kidney tissues, accompanied by Se: Hg molar ratio, selenium health benefit value (HBV Se ), and advanced risk metrics. Results revealed a highly significant tissue-dependent accumulation pattern, with liver and kidney indicating higher metal concentrations than muscle. The highest concentrations were observed in C. chanos , including Hg (0.175 mg kg⁻¹) in the kidney and Se (6.11 mg kg⁻¹) and As (4.69 mg kg⁻¹) in the liver, whereas the highest muscle Hg concentration was detected in S. putnamae (0.046 mg kg⁻¹). Selenium consistently exceeded Hg, resulting in high Se: Hg molar ratios (30.4–470) and positive HBV Se values (≤ 77.4 µmol kg⁻¹), indicating a potential mitigating interaction between Se and Hg. Human health risk assessment illustrated low non-carcinogenic risk, and the cumulative hazard index (0.159–0.270) remained below the safety threshold. For As, the carcinogenic risk value for C. chanos exceeded the upper reference value of 10 − 4 , when the cancer slope factor for inorganic As was applied to the estimated inorganic-As fraction (10% of total-As concentration). This study provided an integrated framework linking metal interactions, bioaccumulation, and health risk indices, presenting applicable insights for improved seafood safety regulation.

Article.Title: Validation of gene variants potentially related to orofacial clefts in the polish population
Article.Authors: Zawiślak A.; Woźniak K.; Kawala B.; Gupta S.; Znamirowska-Bajowska A.; Lubiński J.; Jakubowska A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Orofacial clefts (OFCs) are common congenital birth defects affecting the lip and palate, with an incidence of about 1 in 700 newborns globally. The severity of the cleft depends on the stage of fetal development at which the process was interrupted. These malformations impact essential functions leading to long-term health and social challenges. Approximately 50% of OFC cases occur as isolated, non-syndromic defects, influenced by genetic predispositions and environmental factors. This case–control study investigated associations between four SNPs—rs227731 ( NOG ), rs2166975 ( TGFA ), rs142167 ( NSF ), and rs2205181 ( TGFB3 )—and non-syndromic orofacial clefts in a Polish cohort comprising 209 cases and 418 controls. Cases were recruited from two orthodontic centers, and control DNA was obtained from archived neonatal umbilical cord blood. Associations were assessed using sex-stratified Mantel–Haenszel analyses and multiple logistic regression. In sex-stratified Mantel–Haenszel analyses, rs227731 AA was associated with lower odds of OFCs (OR = 0.59; 95% CI: 0.39–0.88; reported p = 0.005), and CC with higher odds (OR = 1.56; 95% CI: 1.02–2.39; reported p = 0.020). These findings were nominal. In the multiple logistic regression models for OFCs overall, neither genotype reached nominal significance. The rs227731 CC genotype showed a nominal association with unilateral cleft lip and palate in the regression analyses. The study identified nominally statistically significant associations between rs227731 at the NOG -associated locus and non-syndromic orofacial clefts in the Polish cohort, with findings differing by analytical model and cleft phenotype. However, these associations did not remain statistically significant after the conservative Bonferroni correction for the 210 association tests documented in the full statistical report. The findings therefore suggest a potential association that requires confirmation in an independent cohort and do not establish clinical predictive utility.

Article.Title: Detecting object-oriented code smells through social network analysis
Article.Authors: Maddeh M.
Article.Abstract: In software engineering, maintaining high code quality is essential for ensuring the software’s maintainability, scalability, and overall performance. A major obstacle to attaining high-quality software is the presence of code bad smells, which are indicators of potential weaknesses and design flaws within the code. This paper investigates the potential of Social Network Analysis (SNA) as a new method for identifying and examining code smells. By applying SNA techniques, we aim to provide a novel perspective on identifying and analyzing code smells, which are indicative of potential design flaws and vulnerabilities within software systems. Our methodology involves modeling software components and their interactions as a network, allowing us to apply SNA metrics to uncover hidden patterns and relationships. In this paper, we model four Java open-source projects (JUnit 5.10.2, Spring 6.1.4, Apache Commons BCEL 6.8.2, and Guava 33.0) as social networks. Using SNA metrics, we then formulate and identify code bad smells.

Article.Title: A compact integrated platform for real-time live-cell imaging and photodynamic therapy: design and experimental demonstration
Article.Authors: Seydi M.; Khoee S.; Shirvalilou S.; Sadeghi A.; Khoei S.
Article.Abstract: Real-time integration of live-cell imaging and photodynamic therapy (PDT) addresses a critical experimental gap between treatment delivery and longitudinal observation of cellular responses. We present a compact, incubator-compatible platform that integrates inverted bright-field microscopy, automated X–Y scanning, and a uniform 630-nm PDT illumination module within a single experimental workflow, allowing the same cell culture to undergo repeated imaging and PDT without transfer between separate incubation, treatment, and imaging setups. The optical module provides a 1.5 mm² field of view at 2.2 μm resolution. The integrated mechanical and electronic architecture enables automated scanning and repeatable acquisition of predefined imaging regions. To experimentally demonstrate the dual functionality of the platform, A375 melanoma cells treated with 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA, 10–500 µM) underwent fractionated PDT and longitudinal imaging over 72 h. Complementary MTT assays confirmed a time- and dose-dependent decline in viability, while longitudinal image analysis quantified treatment-associated changes in cell confluency and individual-cell morphology over time. In addition, ROI overlap analysis demonstrated substantially improved preservation of imaging regions compared with a conventional workflow involving repeated manual sample transfer. By integrating treatment delivery and long-term imaging within the incubator, the platform provides an experimental infrastructure for continuous observation of the same cell populations during prolonged PDT protocols and other time-dependent cell-based studies.

Article.Title: Mitigating semantic reconstruction bias and methodological contamination in dementia detection using attention-gated linguistic fusion
Article.Authors: Tirpude S.; Makhijani R.
Article.Abstract: Dementia and other cognitive impairments like Alzheimer's disease (AD) are major public health problems worldwide. Early detection is crucial for timely intervention and improved patient outcomes. Natural Language Processing (NLP) has shown significant potential for detecting dementia by identifying cognitive decline. However, existing approaches may lack clinical interpretability, which can reduce reliability. This study proposes an Attention-Gated Hybrid Network (AGH-Net) that integrates handcrafted linguistic biomarkers and contextual semantic representations from DeBERTa-v3 embeddings to improve the robustness of dementia classification. The Pitt Corpus dataset is used to evaluate the model with a participant-level validation strategy to reduce subject-level data leakage and ensure unbiased performance estimation. The proposed AGH-Net achieved 80.18% accuracy and a high clinical sensitivity of 83.87%. A shadow analysis quantifies a 4.44% performance inflation from data leakage, supporting the leakage-controlled result as a more reliable performance estimate. The model achieves transparency through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods. External evaluation on ADReSS-IS2020 and the Lu corpus further examined cross-corpus transfer, with performance varying across datasets. We further validate the classification results against ground-truth clinical Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. The analysis indicates that the LLM can reduce the patient's pathological speech characteristics by normalising linguistically informative errors. Because general-purpose LLMs prioritise semantic meaning over linguistic noise, they may suppress linguistic irregularities that contain clinically informative signals of dementia. These findings indicate that integrating linguistic features with contextual semantic representation provides a reliable, interpretable framework for non-invasive automated dementia screening.

Article.Title: Eggshell-derived CaO₂@MgO–Al₂O₃ composite for phosphate removal through adsorption and precipitation
Article.Authors: Sudibyo N/A.; Gunawan I.; Fajar M.; Sukma V.; Rinovian A.; Rakesh B.; Yuliansyah A.; Petrus H.; Larasati D.; Anwar D.; Sugeng N/A.; Sahlan M.; Wibowo Y.
Article.Abstract: The increasing discharge of phosphate-containing wastewater and the accumulation of calcium-rich household waste are two significant environmental challenges that require sustainable remediation strategies. This study demonstrates the feasibility of converting eggshell waste into a value-added phosphate-removal material, with potential application as a low-cost adsorbent for phosphate reduction in wastewater treatment systems. Discarded eggshell waste was utilized as a sustainable calcium precursor for composite preparation, converting an abundant household waste material into a functional adsorbent for environmental applications. MgO and Al₂O₃ were incorporated as complementary components to enhance phosphate removal through synergistic adsorption and precipitation mechanisms. FTIR, XRD, and FESEM-EDS analyses confirmed the material characteristics. The composite demonstrated effective phosphate removal under different initial concentrations (5, 10, and 20 mg/L) and temperatures (30, 40, and 50 °C). Sorption experiments indicated that the adsorption behavior followed the Temkin isotherm model (R² = 0.9916) and pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R² = 0.94628), suggesting strong adsorbent–phosphate interactions. Thermodynamic analysis indicated a spontaneous adsorption process (ΔG < 0), with ΔH = + 24.07 kJ/mol and ΔS = + 60.39 J/mol·K. This study shows that eggshell-derived calcium-based composites can provide a sustainable pathway to simultaneously reduce phosphate pollution and valorize household waste into value-added environmental materials.

Article.Title: Aquatic subsidies increase the resilience of riparian spider communities after pulse disturbance
Article.Authors: Recalde F.; Rezende F.; Seixas L.; Cosenza M.; Brescovit A.; Romero G.
Article.Abstract: Climatic events such as intense winds and rainfall act as strong pulse disturbances in many ecosystems. Although these disturbances can abruptly alter community structure and dynamics, recovery depends on community resilience, which may be enhanced by resource availability. Cross-ecosystem subsidies can increase prey availability for generalist predators, potentially buffering communities against the effects of disturbance. In this study, we tested whether aquatic subsidies (i.e., emergence of aquatic insects) enhance the resilience of spider communities following unpredictable climatic pulse disturbances. We conducted a field experiment in four Atlantic Rainforest streams, simulating pulse disturbances in riparian and inland plots. We surveyed vegetation-dwelling spiders one day before and four times after disturbance simulations to estimate changes in abundance and community resilience, while stable isotope analyses assessed the contribution of aquatic insects to spider diets. Riparian spiders consumed more aquatic insects than inland spiders, and spider abundance was 24% higher in riparian plots. Disturbance effects were also 43% stronger in riparian communities. Despite this stronger immediate impact, recovery models indicated greater resilience in riparian spider communities, highlighting the role of emergent aquatic insect subsidies in post-disturbance recovery. Our findings demonstrate that cross-ecosystem resource linkages can enhance the resilience of terrestrial predator communities to climatic pulse disturbance.

Article.Title: SSLD-DET: improving symbol detection in station signalling layout drawings with multi-scale feature fusion and advanced attention mechanisms
Article.Authors: Kuang W.; Hao Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate and efficient detection of signalling symbols in station signalling layout drawings (SSLDs) is essential for intelligent railway design, engineering review, and digital management. However, existing detection methods often struggle with densely distributed graphical elements, substantial scale variations, and high visual similarity among different signalling symbols, resulting in insufficient feature discrimination and limited robustness in complex drawing environments. To address these challenges, we propose SSLD-DET, an efficient detection framework for station signalling layout drawings. First, the Efficient Channel Interaction C2f (ECI-C2f) module enhances channel interaction and improves the discrimination of signalling symbols while suppressing redundant structural interference. Second, the Global Context Enhancement Module (GCEM) introduces joint channel-spatial attention to strengthen global contextual perception, enabling more accurate representation of visually similar graphical elements. Finally, an enhanced Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) is incorporated into the neck to improve multi-scale feature fusion through adaptive bidirectional information propagation. Experimental results on a self-constructed SSLD symbol dataset demonstrate that SSLD-DET achieves a precision of 90.6% and a mAP of 93.4%, outperforming the YOLOv26n baseline by 3.9% and 4.1%, respectively. These results indicate that SSLD-DET provides an accurate and efficient solution for automatic signalling symbol detection in complex railway engineering drawings.

Article.Title: Diagnostic probes reveal shortcuts induced by the benchmark protocol in vision-language model annotation pipelines for video-based self-harm detection
Article.Authors: Lee Y.; Jeong H.; Choi H.
Article.Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as annotators: a model captions clinical images or video, a classifier is trained on the captions, and the resulting benchmark score is read as evidence of clinical capability. We describe two diagnostic probes that test whether such a score depends on the target finding. Necessity deletes the most class-discriminative caption tokens; sufficiency classifies from content-agnostic surface-form statistics alone. On an acted self-harm video benchmark (5,183 clips; seven actors; leave-one-subject-out evaluation), four VLM pipelines with a clinically engineered prompt reached F1 0.784–0.944 under the benchmark protocol. Deleting the 40 most discriminative tokens retained 92–100% of F1, and eight surface-form statistics recovered 83–95%. Re-analysis showed that this surface-form signal arose mainly from the protocol, which trims boundary segments from normal clips only and, with our captioning order, changes the number and position of captioned frames, and the prompt template, by class. With label-independent frame selection, AUC fell from 0.89–​0.99 to 0.53–0.65, and three pipelines retained a modest signal above a permutation null. The probes thus flagged a score that rested largely on a protocol artifact. Benchmark scores of VLM-annotator pipelines should be checked in this way before they are given clinical weight.

Article.Title: Analytical investigation in the seismic response of segmental hollow core bridge piers
Article.Authors: Mesbah M.; Abdelrahman A.; Okail H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Segmental precast post-tensioned (SPPT) bridge piers are a promising alternative to conventional cast-in-place bridge substructures due to their rapid construction and enhanced seismic performance. In this system, the footing, column segments, and cap beam are prefabricated and assembled using unbonded post-tensioned (PT) strands extending continuously throughout the pier. The unbonded PT strands provide excellent self-centering capability, thereby reducing seismic damage and residual displacement. However, the system has limited hysteretic energy dissipation. To address this limitation, bonded mild steel energy-dissipating (ED) bars are installed across the segment joints. Additional unbonded lengths are provided to delay low-cycle fatigue damage and prevent premature fracture of the ED bars. Three-dimensional finite element models were developed and validated against experimental results reported in the literature. The validated models were then used to investigate the seismic behavior of SPPT bridge piers under cyclic loading. The studied parameters included the number of column segments, the initial stress, orientation, and ratio of PT strands, as well as the ratio and additional unbonded length of ED bars. The results provide design recommendations for improving the seismic performance of SPPT bridge piers.

Article.Title: The discovery and validation of genes associated with lactylation in papillary thyroid cancer
Article.Authors: Li P.; Chen R.; Zhang Z.; Guo X.; Chen J.; Liang K.
Article.Abstract: Thyroid cancer is the most common endocrine malignancy. Lactic acid and acidification of the tumor immune microenvironment are key processes promoting carcinogenesis. This study was to identify genes related to lactylation in papillary thyroid cancer (P​TC) and explore potential regulatory mechanisms. Lactylation-associated genes were identified by combining differential expression and regression analyses, and these genes were subsequently used to construct a risk model. Functional enrichment analysis, immune microenvironment profiling, and drug sensitivity assessment were then performed. In addition, lactylation-associated genes scores were evaluated at the single-cell level, and key cell populations were identified. Finally, the expression of lactylation-associated genes was assessed in clinical samples. After multiple rounds of selecting, MTTP, FOSB, and JUN were identified as candidate lactylation-associated genes. A risk model was then constructed to classify PTC patients into a high risk group (HRG) and a low risk group (LRG), with HRG patients showing poorer prognosis. The “primary immunodeficiency” signaling pathway was associated with HRG and LRG. Significant differences were observed in the infiltration levels of endothelial cells and neutrophils between the HRG and LRG. Erlotinib_1168 were predicted to be more sensitive in the LRG, whereas Camptothecin_1003 and Vinblastine_1004 were predicted to be more sensitive in the HRG. Finally, single-cell analysis identified six cell types, among which T/natural killer cells, myeloid cells, B cells, thyrocytes, and myeloid cells were prioritized as candidate key cells by AUCell scoring of lactate-related gene set and the three-gene prognostic signature for subsequent pseudotime analysis. Experimental results show that, compared to the control group, MTTP, FOSB, and JUN were downregulated in tumors. MTTP, FOSB, and JUN were identified as lactylation-associated genes in PTC, offering preliminary clues for further investigation of targeted therapies.

Article.Title: Satellite derived bathymetric retrieval through tree based learning within the shallow hypersaline environment of Lake Urmia
Article.Authors: Mojtahedi A.; Yaghin M.; Shirgir A.; Dadashzadeh M.; Gharehaghaji A.
Article.Abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetric (SDB) retrieval in shallow hypersaline waters is challenging because complex hydro-optical conditions and bottom heterogeneity can produce nonlinear spectral–depth relationships that limit conventional linear approaches. This study develops and systematically evaluates a comparative framework for SDB retrieval in Lake Urmia by integrating Landsat-8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) spectral predictors, the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based predictor transformation, and complementary regression architectures. Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and CatBoost regression were evaluated using in situ bathymetric observations under consistent predictor and holdout conditions. In the primary five-repetition assessment, CatBoost achieved the highest held-out performance, with \(\:{R}^{2}=0.928\) , RMSE = 9.11 cm, and CC = 0.959, followed by RF ( \(\:{R}^{2}=0.898\) , RMSE = 13.31 cm, CC = 0.947), DT ( \(\:{R}^{2}=0.852\) , RMSE = 17.84 cm, CC = 0.926), and MLR ( \(\:{R}^{2}=0.799\) , RMSE = 27.97 cm, CC = 0.870). An extended 20-repetition analysis produced closely consistent results, with CatBoost achieving \(\:{R}^{2}=0.927\pm\:0.012\) , RMSE = \(\:9.2\pm\:0.7\) cm, and CC = \(\:0.958\pm\:0.007\) . SVD-based predictor transformation improved testing performance across the evaluated models, although the magnitude of improvement varied with model architecture. The four-model spatial assessment further revealed differences in spatial continuity and depth gradients, with the CatBoost and RF retrievals exhibiting comparatively more coherent spatial patterns than MLR and DT. These findings demonstrate that predictor representation and learning architecture jointly influence SDB retrieval under the investigated hypersaline conditions. The framework provides a controlled and reproducible basis for evaluating complementary SDB modeling strategies while maintaining the interpretation of quantitative performance within the environmental and observational conditions of the investigated Lake Urmia scene.

Article.Title: An interpretable postoperative model predicts one-year healing after endodontic microsurgery with temporal validation and clinician benchmarking
Article.Authors: Feng S.; Zhang L.; Wang A.; Guan L.; Sun Q.; Jia G.; Zu Q.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Endodontic microsurgery is an important tooth-preserving treatment for periapical lesions, but accurate postoperative prognosis remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and temporally validate an interpretable model for one-year healing after endodontic microsurgery and to benchmark its discrimination against clinician estimates. The development cohort comprised 312 patients (273 healed and 39 failed) and was split into a training set ( n = 218; 191 healed and 27 failed) and an internal model-selection set ( n = 94; 82 healed and 12 failed). The temporal cohort comprised 108 patients (95 healed and 13 failed). Twenty-six candidate predictors were evaluated using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator and Boruta procedures within the training set, and six machine-learning models were compared. The final L2-penalized logistic regression model was interpreted using exact linear SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), exploratory predictor-effect profiles, and a separate post-hoc odds-ratio refit, and was benchmarked against probability estimates from five endodontic clinicians. Logistic regression achieved an out-of-fold training AUC of 0.812 (95% CI, 0.708–0.907), an internal model-selection AUC of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.761–0.949), and a temporal-validation AUC of 0.703 (95% CI, 0.530–0.867). The internal model-selection Brier score was 0.084 (95% CI, 0.044–0.129). Internal model-selection calibration intercept and slope were 0.80 (95% CI, − 0.36 to 1.91) and 0.60 (95% CI, 0.24 to 1.39); temporal estimates were 1.11 (95% CI, 0.32 to 2.05) and 0.54 (95% CI, 0.16 to 1.15). Buccal bone plate height and CBCT bone-loss volume were the dominant SHAP contributors. The paired clinician benchmark analysis yielded model and clinician AUCs of 0.696 and 0.771, respectively, with an AUC difference of − 0.075 (DeLong P = 0.186). This study presents an interpretable postoperative/perioperative prognostic model for one-year healing after endodontic microsurgery. Temporal performance was lower than the internal model-selection estimate, and the five-clinician benchmark provided a comparison with clinical estimates. Multicenter validation and development of a fully preoperative model are priorities for future work.

Article.Title: Closing the loop: deploying auto-generating digital twins for particle accelerators
Article.Authors: Brynes A.; King M.; Baker K.; Banerjee R.; Clarke R.; Dunning D.; Jones J.; Leputa M.; Pollard A.; Romanovschi M.; Shaw M.; Ziyan N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital twins provide a powerful means of interrogating complex physical systems and enhancing their performance across the full operational lifecycle. This article presents an auto-generating digital twin architecture for particle accelerators, where high system complexity and limited, costly beam time make digital twinning vital for improving performance and increasing throughput. A virtual control system mirrors the physical accelerator hardware, driving updates to a simulation model that returns results through virtual diagnostics. All of the accelerator lattice information is cascaded from a single ground source of truth, eliminating ambiguity between hardware and model representations. The modular, extensible design allows researchers to integrate their own simulation tools, machine-learning models, and lattice definitions while preserving structural coherence across the digital twin. This architecture has been demonstrated for three accelerator facilities—the CLARA electron beam facility, the ISIS neutron and muon source, and the proposed UK XFEL—establishing a foundation for a collaborative, community-driven effort toward a generic digital-twin solution for accelerator operation.

Article.Title: Design and analysis of an intelligent audit risk assessment system based on retrieval-augmented large language model
Article.Authors: Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Audit risk assessment remains a critical yet challenging task due to the increasing complexity of financial reporting environments and the limitations of conventional data-driven models in interpreting contextual information. Existing approaches mainly rely on structured financial indicators and often fail to incorporate domain-specific regulatory knowledge and narrative disclosures. This study develops an intelligent audit risk assessment framework integrating a retrieval-augmented large language model (RAG-LLM) with a Bayesian–logistic hybrid estimation mechanism. The proposed framework combines financial, governance, operational, and textual information with external audit standards, regulatory enforcement cases, and historical accounting irregularities to generate context-aware audit risk evaluations. The system was evaluated using an economically calibrated synthetic dataset containing 612 firm-year observations across 14 industries spanning fiscal years 2017–2024. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RAG–LLM Bayesian hybrid model achieves an out-of-sample AUC of 0.912, outperforming gradient boosting (0.754), random forest (0.723), and logistic regression (0.694). The model also achieves improved calibration performance with a Brier score of 0.088 and a misclassification rate of 6.7%. Further analysis indicates that LLM-derived reasoning constructs contribute 48.3% of the explanatory contribution, highlighting the value of contextualized narrative interpretation for identifying latent audit risk factors. Although the evaluation is based on synthetic data and requires future validation using real-world audit datasets, this study provides an explainable framework for integrating retrieval-enhanced reasoning with probabilistic audit analytics and contributes to the development of AI-assisted auditing systems.

Article.Title: Targeted somatosensory stimulation modulates facial nucleus glial responses and promotes functional recovery after facial nerve axotomy in rats
Article.Authors: Lee J.; Kang H.; Yeo S.; Kim Y.; Yoo M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peripheral facial nerve injury is accompanied by distal nerve degeneration and glial responses in the facial motor nucleus. This pilot preclinical study compared manual whisker-pad stimulation with mechanical vibrissal brushing after unilateral facial nerve axotomy in rats. Twenty-four rats were randomly assigned to Sham, Axotomy, Axotomy plus manual stimulation, or Axotomy plus mechanical stimulation groups ( n = 6 each), with three intact controls for Western blot. Stimulation was administered three times weekly for seven weeks. Functional recovery was assessed longitudinally; other outcomes were evaluated at eight weeks. Morphological and molecular analyses included three animals per group, and immunofluorescence analyses included six animals per group. Relative to untreated axotomy, manual stimulation was associated with improved facial motor scores, higher compound muscle action potential amplitude, lower electrophysiological degeneration, greater myelinated axon counts and myelin thickness, lower c-Jun, SMAD2 and TLR2 and higher phosphorylated AKT levels, lower Iba-1 and GFAP relative intensities, and higher ChAT-positive motor neuron counts. Although fewer outcomes reached statistical significance with mechanical stimulation, the two modalities did not differ significantly from each other on any measure. These exploratory findings require confirmation in adequately powered studies and establish neither modality superiority nor causality.

Article.Title: Antibacterial effects of cinnamon, eucalyptus, and green tea extracts vs. chlorhexidine and their impact on efflux pump activity in Streptococcus
Article.Authors: Hashemipour M.; Sadeghi E.; Tadjrobehkar O.; Sardou S.; Rezvaninejad R.; Rezvaninejad R.
Article.Abstract: Dental caries is a common oral health challenge, and using antimicrobial agents like chlorhexidine gluconate is one approach to managing its progression, although its long-term application is limited by various side effects. Given that plant-based solutions such as cinnamon, eucalyptus, and green tea extracts offer promising antimicrobial effects, this study examines their potential as natural alternatives for preventing and managing dental caries. This in vitro study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of cinnamon, eucalyptus, and green tea extracts against Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sanguinis , comparing them with chlorhexidine. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of each agent, with and without the efflux pump inhibitor omeprazole, was determined using broth dilution and well diffusion methods. Chlorhexidine showed MIC values of 4 µg/mL and 2 µg/mL for Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sanguinis , respectively. Plant extracts exhibited MIC values with cinnamon at 375 µg/mL and 187 µg/ml. Well diffusion tests revealed increased inhibition zones when the efflux pump inhibitor was added. The study showed that 0.2% chlorhexidine had the strongest antibacterial effects against Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sanguinis , followed by green tea and cinnamon extracts. Green tea may serve as an alternative to chlorhexidine, potentially combined with efflux pump inhibitors to reduce resistance and side effects.

Article.Title: Hierarchical modality reconstruction and transformer interaction with adaptive fusion for multimodal sentiment analysis with missing modalities
Article.Authors: Lu C.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to recognize human emotions by integrating information from multiple sources, such as text, audio, and visual modalities. In recent years, this task has faced two major challenges in real-world applications. First, uncertain modality missingness leads to incomplete input information. Second, insufficient cross-modal interaction limits the effectiveness of multimodal fusion. Existing methods often treat reconstructed modalities and available modalities equally and lack adequate mechanisms for cross-modal interaction, which makes them prone to reconstruction errors and weakens the quality of multimodal fusion. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework for multimodal sentiment analysis with missing modalities, named AMF-MMSA (Attention Mechanisms and Missingness-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities). Under the complete-modality setting, AMF-MMSA first employs a self-attention mechanism to enhance modality-specific feature representations. When modality missing occurs, based on the enhanced features, we further design a modality reconstruction module (MR) guided by inter-modal affective consistency, while considering both random single-modality missing and multi-modality missing scenarios. Subsequently, all modality features, including reconstructed ones, are fed into a Transformer interaction module (TIM) to enable sufficient cross-modal interaction. Finally, a missingness-aware fusion module (MAF) explicitly distinguishes available modalities from reconstructed modalities and adaptively down-weights potentially low-quality reconstructed modalities, thereby achieving more robust multimodal fusion. Experimental results on three public datasets, CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS, demonstrate that under missing-rate settings of 0.0-0.5, AMF-MMSA significantly outperforms existing baseline methods across all evaluation metrics.

Article.Title: Physics-informed domain adaptation for synthetic-to-real bearing fault diagnosis with healthy-only target data
Article.Authors: Biziarkin I.; Litvinov N.; Korkhov V.
Article.Abstract: Reliable bearing fault diagnosis is difficult when real fault data cannot be collected without risking machine damage. We study a synthetic-to-real setting in which training uses labelled synthetic faults and recordings known to represent healthy operation of the target machine, while no target-fault sample is available for training, adaptation, or model selection. We propose Healthy-Referenced Physics-informed Diagnosis (HRPD), a framework that subtracts each domain’s mean healthy envelope-order spectrum, retains a complementary log-magnitude channel, and combines a temporal convolutional encoder with a physics branch built from characteristic-order harmonics. A cosine-prototype classifier and healthy-class-restricted domain alignment use the available target information without observing target faults. Under a common-data protocol on four bearing benchmarks, HRPD ranks first on CWRU, MFPT, and Paderborn (balanced accuracy 0.643, 0.979, and 0.545) and second on XJTU-SY (0.638). The results also expose clear limitations: XJTU-SY inner-race damage is dominated by a shaft-synchronous component absent from the geometry-based source, and Paderborn operational wear remains difficult for every evaluated framework. These findings support healthy-only target data as a practical calibration resource while showing that transfer remains constrained by synthetic-source fidelity.

Article.Title: Assessing machine learning algorithms for prediction of soil infiltration behavior in semi-arid agricultural soils
Article.Authors: Razzaghi F.; Shirazi S.; Zare S.; Sepaskhah A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of soil infiltration characteristics is fundamental for irrigation design, hydrological modeling, and sustainable soil and water management. However, the nonlinear interactions among soil physical, hydraulic, and chemical properties make reliable prediction of cumulative infiltration (It) and basic infiltration rate (Ib) challenging using conventional statistical approaches. This study evaluated the predictive performance of artificial neural networks (ANNs), random forest (RF), and multiple linear regression (MLR) for estimating It and Ib under three input scenarios of soil properties comprising (i) physical properties, (ii) physical and hydraulic properties, and (iii) physical, hydraulic, and chemical properties. Soil samples were collected from the Bajgah Plain, Fars Province, Iran, and infiltration characteristics were measured using a double-ring infiltrometer. The machine-learning models were trained and tested, and their performance was assessed using different statistical indicators. Among the evaluated models, the double-hidden-layer ANN achieved the highest predictive accuracy (NRMSE = 0.03–0.06, and R 2 = 0.98–0.99) for It using first and second scenarios and for Ib (NRMSE = 0.04–0.06, and R 2 = 0.99) using the first and third scenarios. The RF model also provided highly accurate predictions (NRMSE = 0.045–0.047, and R 2 = 0.96–0.97 for It, and NRMSE = 0.008–0.009, and R 2 = 0.999 for Ib). In contrast, the MLR exhibited the lowest predictive capability (NRMSE = 0.58–0.60, and R 2 = 0.63-066 for It, and NRMSE = 0.77–0.87, and R 2 = 0.27–0.42 for Ib) because of its inability to represent the nonlinear relationships governing infiltration processes. Incorporating saturated hydraulic conductivity improved the prediction of both cumulative infiltration and basic infiltration rate. Including soil chemical properties provided only marginal additional improvements, indicating that infiltration in the studied soils was primarily controlled by physical and hydraulic characteristics. The results demonstrate the superiority of random forest models for simulating soil infiltration characteristics and highlight the importance of selecting appropriate predictor variables according to the target infiltration parameter. The proposed models provide efficient tools for estimating infiltration where direct field measurements are limited and offer valuable support for irrigation planning, hydrological simulations, and sustainable soil and water management.

Article.Title: TMEM45A promote triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) related depression via the AKT/mTOR signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Xie H.; Zou Z.; Jiang M.; Liu H.; Shu G.; Feng R.; Niu D.; Yao R.; Fang F.
Article.Abstract: Patients diagnosed with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) frequently experience depression, a comorbidity that substantially compromises quality of life and survival outcomes. This study aimed to characterize the functional role and underlying regulatory mechanisms of TMEM45A in triple-negative BC related depression (TN-BCRD). First, we validated the regulatory effects of TMEM45A in 4T1 cells. An in vitro TN-BCRD model was established using HT22 hippocampal neurons co-exposed to 4T1 cell-derived conditioned medium and corticosterone. The siRNA of TMEM45A was transfected into 4T1 cells to investigate the effect of tumor cell-expressed TMEM45A on the TN-BCRD phenotype and the AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. For in vivo validation, we established 4T1 tumor-bearing mice model and examined the effects of tumoral TMEM45A on tumor growth, depression-like phenotypes, and hippocampal AKT/mTOR signaling. TMEM45A is significantly overexpressed in TNBC tissues. Knockdown of TMEM45A induced apoptosis and inhibited migration and invasion in 4T1 cells, while it promoted proliferation and reduced apoptosis in HT22 cells. TMEM45A knockdown also attenuated the activity of AKT/mTOR signaling and reduced the secretion of pro-inflammatory factors in HT22 cells under BCRD conditions. In vivo mice experiments demonstrated that TMEM45A knockdown in 4T1 cells suppressed the tumor growth and rescued depression-like behaviors in tumor-bearing mice. TMEM45A serves as a key regulator of TN-BCRD, and its targeted inhibition may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for this condition.

Article.Title: Relationship between physical activity and aging perception with mediating role of resilience among community-dwelling older adults
Article.Authors: Hosseini F.; Rashvand F.; Hosseinkhani Z.; Motalebi S.
Article.Abstract: The global demographic shift toward an aging population highlights the need to identify modifiable factors that shape individuals’ perceptions of aging. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the relationship between physical activity and perception of aging, with the mediating role of resilience among older adults. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 on 378 community-dwelling older adults in Qazvin, Iran. Participants were selected using cluster sampling method. Data collection instruments included a demographic questionnaire, the Barker Aging Perception Questionnaire, the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), and the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ). Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25 for descriptive statistics and Mplus version 7.3 for structural equation modeling. Path analysis was used to examine the mediating role of resilience in the relationship between physical activity and perceptions of aging. The mean age of older participants was 69.69 ± 7.04 years. The majority were married (70.6%, n = 267) and retired (47.9%, n = 181). Mean scores indicated a moderate level of perceptions of aging (55.73 ± 6.47) and physical activity (1803.74 ± 1776.98 MET-min/week), and a high level of resilience (34.78 ± 6.93). Path analysis showed that physical activity was not directly associated with perceptions of aging (β = 0.04, p = 0.397), whereas its indirect association through resilience was statistically significant (β = 0.04, p = 0.005). The total association was not statistically significant (β = 0.08, p = 0.100). The findings indicate that resilience statistically mediates the association between physical activity and perceptions of aging among older adults. These results highlight resilience as a potential psychological mechanism through which physical activity may be associated with more positive perceptions of aging, offering valuable insights for interventions aimed at enhancing well-being in later life.

Article.Authors: Ghareeb E.; Mansour M.; Samy A.; AboulMagd A.; Balamon M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The quinoline scaffold is widely exploited in the design of new anticancer candidates. Among these compounds, two derivatives ( 4) and (11) showed potent anti-proliferative activity against MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells with IC₅₀ values of 4.91 and 8.25 µ M, respectively. The same two derivatives also showed significant activity against the HCT-116 colon cancer cell line with IC₅₀ values of 6.38 and 9.44 µ M, respectively. Mechanistic studies further showed that compound (4) potently inhibited EGFR WT (IC₅₀ = 0.084 µ M) and mutant EGFR forms, as well as HDAC-2 with IC 50 = 0.123 µ M. Additionally, western blot analysis of compound (4) revealed downregulation of pEGFR, pERK, and pAKT, while RT-qPCR analysis showed upregulation of BAX and caspase-3, -7, and − 9 and downregulation of BCL-2 at the mRNA level. Cell-cycle analysis showed that derivative (4) induced arrest at the G 1 /S boundary. Taken together, all these results, along with molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, supported the stable binding within the ATP-binding site of EGFR and the zinc-binding pocket of HDAC-2.

Article.Title: District-level trends in veterinary antimicrobial prescribing in a resource-limited setting: evidence from Mongar, Bhutan (2023–2026)
Article.Authors: Pokhrel N.; Cheda C.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing One Health problem, yet routine veterinary prescribing data from low- and middle-income countries are rarely analysed. We describe antimicrobial prescribing at the District Veterinary Hospital (DVH) Mongar and 16 Renewable Natural Resources Extension Centres in Bhutan, using 17,482 Veterinary Information System records from January 2023 to June 2026. We identified 1,063 antimicrobial prescriptions (6.1% of records); at visit level, 1,022 of 8,881 visits (11.5%) included one. There was no significant trend, even after adjusting for seasonality ( p = 0.987; adjusted p = 0.939). Tetracyclines (39.5%) and Penicillins (35.3%) together made up about 75% of prescriptions. Drug class differed by species (χ²=403.25, p < 0.001) and by facility type, including within Bovine cases (χ²=56.96, p < 0.001): DVH Mongar used more Penicillins, the extension centres more Sulphonamides and Aminoglycosides. Prescribing peaked from June to August ( p < 0.001). Laboratory tests were requested in only 2 records, so prescribing was essentially empirical. These findings suggest possible priorities for stewardship in this setting: reviewing how existing treatment guidelines are applied at extension centres, and planning drug stock and stewardship ahead of the monsoon.

Article.Title: Modulation of cell death and neurogenesis by early intervention with sodium butyrate and galantamine in a streptozotocin-induced Alzheimer’s rat model
Article.Authors: Anbarian F.; Asghariehahari M.; Chodari L.; Niknam Z.
Article.Abstract: Given the multifactorial nature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), early combination therapies targeting complementary pathways offer the most effective neuroprotection. This study investigated neuroprotective potential of sodium butyrate (NaB) combined with galantamine (Gal), focusing on cell survival and markers associated with hippocampal neurogenesis and structural maturation in a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced rat model of sporadic AD. Male Wistar rats received intracerebroventricular STZ injection to induce AD-like pathology and were treated orally with Gal (10 mg/kg), NaB (600 mg/kg), or their combination for 14 days. Spatial learning and memory were evaluated using the Morris Water Maze (MWM). Hippocampal Aβ deposition, cell death, and neurogenesis were assessed by immunofluorescence, TUNEL assay, and Western blot analyses. STZ administration induced significant cognitive impairment, increased hippocampal Aβ accumulation, elevated cell death markers, BAX/Bcl-2 ratio, and reduced neurogenesis-associated markers, doublecortin (DCX; marker of immature neurons), and βIII-tubulin (marker of early neuronal maturation). Both Gal and NaB monotherapies significantly improved behavioral and molecular outcomes compared with untreated STZ rats. Combined NaB + Gal treatment produced the most pronounced overall recovery, restoring cognitive performance to near-control levels, markedly reducing Aβ burden and cell death markers, and modulating markers associated with early neuronal structural maturation. While Gal alone showed the strongest increase in hippocampal DCX immunoreactivity, combination therapy significantly increased βIII-tubulin expression, suggesting a potential facilitation of early neuronal maturation. Conclusively, early co-intervention with NaB and Gal is associated with neuroprotection, enhanced neurogenesis, and cognitive function in STZ-induced AD rats. These findings support the potential of multi-target combination early strategies for AD treatment.

Article.Title: DTR-GAT-OPAL: Digital Twin reinforcement learning and graph attention-based openflow prediction for secure cross-cloud SDN resource orchestration
Article.Authors: Manikandan S.; Banu R.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent resource orchestration in large-scale distributed computing systems can be facilitated via Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-enabled cross-cloud infrastructures, which allow programmability, elasticity, and service-centric administration. OpenFlow prediction accuracy, resource utilization efficiency, and Quality of Service (QoS) stability are significantly reduced by network heterogeneity, dynamic traffic fluctuations, controller congestion, and sophisticated cyberattacks. Optimization and learning-based techniques mostly estimate traffic or balance loads without topology-aware intelligence, adaptive decision-making, or synchronized cyber-physical representations for robust cross-cloud orchestration. DTR-GAT-OPAL (Digital Twin and Graph Attention Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intelligent OpenFlow Prediction and Secure Cross-Cloud Resource Orchestration) addresses these existing limitations. The proposed framework includes a Digital Twin (DT) layer for real-time synchronization of cyber-physical states, a Graph Attention Network (GAT) for topology-aware learning of flow representations, and a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based reinforcement learning engine for adaptive controller and virtual machine orchestration. Likewise included are a federated trust-security module and an uncertainty-aware QoS reasoning method for robust decision support under dynamic workloads. The same multi-objective optimization strategy maximizes service reliability and orchestration robustness while minimizing control-plane instability, migration overhead, energy consumption, carbon intensity, and security vulnerability. DTR-GAT-OPAL outperforms state-of-the-art methods in heterogeneous CloudSim-SDN and Mininet environments in OpenFlow prediction accuracy (0.99%), controller response latency (31.4%), energy consumption (34.2%), migration overhead (32.8%), and security assurance (29.6%). These results prove DTR-GAT-OPAL can orchestrate scalable, robust, and intelligent cross-cloud SDN resources for next-generation distributed computing ecosystems.

Article.Title: Ancestral and contemporary genetic diversification of Toll-like receptor 2 in sympatric mustelid species from central Europe
Article.Authors: Tissaoui G.; Suchentrunk F.; Awadi A.; Smith S.; Weber A.; Tolesa Z.; Slimen H.
Article.Abstract: The leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain of Toll-like receptors (TLR) of the animal innate immune system recognises specific pathogen associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). It often exhibits elevated polymorphism driven by diversifying selection. We investigated variability and evolution of a 465bp fragment of the TLR2-LRR domain in six Mustelid species occurring sympatrically in eastern Austria. We specifically hypothesised higher diversity in the occasionally hybridising polecats, Mustela putorius , and steppe polecats, M. eversmannii , because of their potentially larger effective population size and possible trans-species polymorphism maintained by selection. However, among our studied species, polecats and steppe polecats exhibited the lowest allelic diversity, possibly reflecting their recent divergence. Observed heterozygosities were lower than expected heterozygosities across all studied species. Overall, five codon positions were identified as candidates for positive selection, with codon 149 supported by four independent methods, while two codons showed evidence of purifying selection. Structural modelling localized candidate positively selected sites in regions potentially relevant for function, including residues predicted to be involved in TLR1–TLR2 dimerization. Notably, several alleles were shared within and between Mustela and Martes , a pattern consistent with long-term ancestral polymorphism potentially maintained by pathogen-mediated selection. Overall, our results suggest that, for the studied species, the TLR2-LRR domain evolves under a dynamic interplay of purifying and diversifying selection, together with demographic processes.

Article.Title: Phosphate mining byproduct-derived PHI-type zeolite with intrinsic Mg2+ ions for enhanced Cd2+ removal from water
Article.Authors: Mghaimimi I.; Berrada M.; Ahmed A.; Delhali A.; Beniazza R.; Adil K.; Belmabkhout Y.; Assen A.
Article.Abstract: Synthesizing functional zeolites from industrial residues advances circular materials chemistry, but controlling framework composition is challenging. In this study, PHI-type zeolite was synthesized from a phosphate mining byproduct containing SiO 2 , Al 2 O 3 , CaO, MgO, and Fe 2 O 3 . The PHI zeolite retains waste-derived Mg within its cationic environment, setting it apart from PHI made from conventional precursors. Similar syntheses using conventional precursors, with/without MgO, yielded phase-pure PHI without MgO addition, whereas MgO introduced secondary impurities or competing zeolites. The influence of precursor-dependent cation chemistry on functional performance was studied using Cd 2+ adsorption as a model water-treatment application. The waste-derived PHI zeolite exhibited superior adsorption capacity compared with its commercial counterpart, highlighting the combined effects of intrinsically incorporated Mg 2+ and enhanced pore accessibility on Cd 2+ adsorption. Comprehensive characterization (XRD, FTIR, TGA, SEM-EDX, and N 2 sorption) elucidated the structural and textural properties underlying this enhanced behavior. Adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model, and equilibrium data fit the Langmuir isotherm, indicating chemisorption on homogeneous sites with a maximum uptake of 99.8 mg g −1 . The material shows excellent stability and recyclability, maintaining > 95% capacity after five cycles. These findings highlight industrial waste as more than a feedstock for zeolite synthesis, revealing its potential to shape composition and functional performance.

Article.Title: Molecular identification and antifungal susceptibility of otomycosis agents in Shiraz, Iran: predominance of Aspergillus tubingensis
Article.Authors: Yazdanpanah S.; Pirmoradi M.; Hashemi S.; Rouhi F.; Mehrabadi M.; Aminzadeh A.; Khadivi Z.; Hosseini J.; Motamedi M.; Zomorodian K.
Article.Abstract: Otomycosis is a common external auditory canal infection, frequently caused by Aspergillus and Candida species. Diagnostic limitations and species-dependent antifungal susceptibility contribute to recurrence and treatment challenges. This study aimed to determine species distribution and antifungal susceptibility patterns of otomycosis isolates in southern Iran. A cross-sectional study enrolled 104 patients with confirmed otomycosis (November 2018–March 2019). Molecular identification was performed by β-tubulin sequencing (molds) and ITS region sequencing (yeasts). Antifungal susceptibility testing against fluconazole, posaconazole, miconazole, terbinafine, amphotericin B, and nystatin followed CLSI microdilution methods (M38-Ed3 and M27-Ed4). Among 104 patients, 55% were female, and nearly half were aged 40–60 years. Itching (81.7%), inflammation (80%), and otorrhea (74%) were predominant symptoms. Cultures yielded 102 mold and 16 yeast isolates. Microscopic observation identified the A. niger complex as the predominant agents, while sequencing confirmed A. tubingensis (36.3%) and A. niger (28.4%) as the main species causing otomycosis. C. albicans and C. parapsilosis were the most frequent yeasts. Posaconazole and amphotericin B showed potent activity against most Aspergillus isolates, and 12 of the 16 Candida isolates (75%) remained fluconazole-susceptible. Molecular techniques significantly improved the accuracy of species identification of otomycosis agents, revealing a high frequency of A. tubingensis in this study population. Posaconazole and amphotericin B showed strong in vitro activity, while fluconazole showed limited efficacy against molds. Overall, continuous molecular surveillance is essential to guide optimal antifungal therapy and prevent resistance.

Article.Title: Rapid identification of antibody leads from selection outputs using oxford nanopore technology
Article.Authors: Spector L.; Perea-Schmittle K.; Trujillo A.; Pohl T.; Gonzalez K.; D’Angelo S.; Ferrara F.; Bradbury A.; Erasmus M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditionally, the identification of potential clones of interest from in vitro antibody selections is carried out using random colony picking and Sanger sequencing. In contrast, next-generation sequencing (NGS) provides a comprehensive overview of selection output diversity and dynamics, facilitating lead prioritization and machine learning. Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) has emerged as a promising intermediary between Sanger and deeper NGS approaches. ONT offers a lower cost and faster turnaround time relative to Sanger and other NGS platforms. In this paper, we describe our experimental and computational pipeline, RADiANT (Rapid Antibody Discovery Applied to Nanopore Technology), to process and deconvolve unique cloned VHH and scFv sequences from polyclonal yeast-display populations using ONT. For campaigns targeting 10–20 lead candidates, ONT provides deeper sampling than Sanger sequencing and higher reproducibility than Sanger in the recovery of top leads found using PacBio, with up to a 90% cost reduction and a fifteen-fold faster turnaround time.

Article.Title: Eligibility gap scoring across first-line targeted and immunotherapy trials and real-world cohorts in metastatic renal cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Sawai M.; Narita T.; Sekine Y.; Shinohara M.; Kawashima Y.; Sato H.; Numakura K.; Mikami J.; Fujita N.; Okamoto T.; Yamamoto H.; Narita S.; Sato S.; Habuchi T.; Ohyama C.; Hatakeyama S.
Article.Abstract: First-line treatment for metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) has shifted toward immune checkpoint inhibitor-based combinations, but pivotal trial populations may differ from patients treated in routine practice. We developed an eligibility gap (EG) score to visualize selected eligibility-related baseline characteristics across first-line mRCC studies. Phase III randomized controlled trials (RCTs), published real-world data (RWD) cohorts, and the original AGEHA-JPN cohort were analyzed. The EG score integrated median age, prior nephrectomy rate, and IMDC risk distribution on a 0–99.9 scale. Thirty-six datasets were included: 10 RCTs, 25 published RWD cohorts, and AGEHA-JPN. Median EG scores were higher in RCTs than RWD cohorts (74.0 vs 60.3; p < 0.001), mainly reflecting younger age and higher prior nephrectomy rates, whereas IMDC-domain scores were similar. Asian RWD cohorts had lower median scores than non-Asian RWD cohorts (50.7 vs 64.5). Sensitivity analyses using alternative domain and sample-size weighting preserved the RCT–RWD separation. The EG score provides a descriptive framework for contextualizing selected baseline differences between trial and real-world populations. However, it does not capture factors such as histology, comorbidity, or metastatic burden and is not a comprehensive measure of trial eligibility, generalizability, or prognosis.

Article.Title: Clinical application of deep neural networks in laser endomicroscopic molecular imaging for accurate assessment of lung nodules
Article.Authors: Azari F.; Kennedy G.; Conner A.; Chang A.; Chang A.; Nadeem B.; Din A.; Cloonan D.; Gruev V.; Delikatny E.; Kucharczuk J.; Azari S.; Singhal S.
Article.Abstract: Needle-based near-infrared confocal laser endomicroscopy (NIR-nCLE) enables intraoperative imaging of pafolacianine-labeled cells within pulmonary lesions, but interpretation requires operator experience. We evaluated a machine-learning pipeline for classifying NIR-nCLE recordings as benign or malignant using final histopathology as the reference standard. Fifty patients undergoing pafolacianine-guided resection were prospectively enrolled, and 248 lesions were sampled. An AlexNet-based convolutional neural network classified individual frames, with lesions classified as malignant when the proportion of frames predicted to be malignant was ≥ 0.02. Lesion-level performance was assessed by stratified five-fold cross-validation using 121 analyzable recordings available in the retained de-identified archive, comprising 70 malignant and 51 benign lesions and 23,589 frames. All frames from each lesion were confined to a single fold; patient-level partitioning was not possible because patient-to-recording links were unavailable. Sensitivity was 98.6% (95% CI 95–100%), specificity was 72.5% (60–84%), positive predictive value was 83.1%, negative predictive value was 97.4%, accuracy was 87.6% (81–93%), and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.97 (0.94–0.99). Logistic regression using mean fluorescence intensity alone achieved an AUROC of 0.97 (0.94–0.99) and an accuracy of 90.1%; a 100-unit feature-based neural network achieved an AUROC of 0.98 (0.95–1.00). In an internal exploratory intraoperative cohort of 10 additional patients, all nine malignant and 18 benign lesions were correctly classified before final pathological evaluation, yielding a sensitivity of 100% (95% CI 66.4–100%) and a specificity of 100% (81.5–100%). Automated classification of NIR-nCLE recordings demonstrated promising preliminary internal performance, with similar AUROC estimates for simpler fluorescence-based models. Independent external validation with patient-level separation is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Isthmin-1, meteorin-like, and neuregulin-4 as potential diagnostic novel biomarkers for colorectal cancer in Thi-Qar Governorate, Iraq
Article.Authors: Roomi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer complications and deaths globally. Unfortunately, we have limited tests for early diagnosis of the disease. Nevertheless, novel integrative metabolic and inflammatory markers, including Isthmin-1 (ISM1), Meteorin-like (Metrnl), Neuregulin-4 (NRG4), which have the ability to formulate novel diagnostic strategies and broaden the knowledge of CRC. In a case-control study of 180 individuals, three groups were assessed: patients with CRC, individuals with benign colorectal disease (BCD), and healthy controls (HC), with 60 individuals in each category. ELISA was performed to assess the levels of these markers in individuals’ blood. Statistical results showed clearly higher ISM1 levels in CRC patients (8.91 ± 2.14 ng/mL); BCD and HC showed 5.76 ± 1.63 ng/mL and 4.83 ± 1.41 ng/mL, respectively (p < 0.001). Metrnl values were lowered by 62.8 ± 15.7 pg/mL in CRC patients, versus 88.5 ± 19.4 pg/mL in BCD and 96.3 ± 20.1 pg/mL in HC (p < 0.001). NRG4 values were equally low in CRC patients, averaging 1.74 ± 0.52 ng/mL, although this was lower than in HC (p < 0.001). The ROC analysis was promising for the three markers, with AUC of 0.912 for ISM1, 0.895 for Metrnl, and 0.887 for NRG4. In addition, ISM1 was positively associated with tumor stage and tumor size (r = 0.61, 0.53), yet Metrnl and NRG4 had the opposite effect. This study demonstrates that elevated ISM1 levels, in conjunction with decreased Metrnl and NRG4 levels, are significantly associated with CRC and its severity. These biomarkers provide more accurate predictions, which may contribute to enhancing our understanding of early CRC detection and identifying risk factors.

Article.Title: In silico and in vitro studies suggest anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory potential of Turbinaria ornata and Turbinaria decurrens
Article.Authors: Limijadi E.; Tjandra K.; Syahputra R.; Permatasari H.; Tsopmo A.; Santini A.; Romano R.; De Luca L.; Nurkolis F.
Article.Abstract: Inflammation, immunomodulation, and oxidative stress are central factors in various diseases that affect humans. Marine seaweeds, renowned for their bioactive compounds, offer a promising avenue for the discovery of compounds targeting these pathways. Herein, we investigate the chemical composition and pharmacological potential of extracts from Turbinaria ornata and Turbinaria decurrens , abundant seaweeds in Indonesian waters. Through multidisciplinary approaches including metabolomic profiling, molecular docking, network pharmacology analysis, and cytotoxicity assessments, we identified candidate bioactive compounds with predicted anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activity and measurable cytotoxicity. Our findings reveal a diverse array of compounds, including alkanes, alcohols, cycloalkanes, sterols, phenols, and carotenoids, with potential health benefits. Network pharmacology analysis predicts genes and pathways associated with inflammatory diseases, underscoring the complexity of these pathways and potential targets for intervention. Molecular docking studies predict favorable interactions of compounds with key receptors implicated in inflammation and immunosuppression. CTD1 and CTD3 showed more favorable predicted binding affinities (lower docking ΔG values) than the reference compound S-ibuprofen for all investigated targets (TNF-α, EGFR, ESR1, Fyn, mTOR, and iNOS); docking scores do not, however, demonstrate receptor inhibition. The RAW264.7 cell line’s IC 50 results demonstrated the metabolites’ varying levels of toxicity; the greatest values were found on TOE and CTO3. Extracts and individual metabolites were associated with comparably lower levels of inflammation-related proteins (TNF-α, EGFR, ESR1, Fyn, mTOR, and iNOS) in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages at a single concentration, which is consistent with, but does not establish, modulation of the corresponding signaling pathways. These findings suggest the anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory potential of Turbinaria ornata and Turbinaria decurrens extracts and metabolites as candidates for further investigation, including dose–response, pathway-specific, and in vivo validation.

Article.Title: Elastic strain energy redistribution and ground control through large diameter borehole pressure relief in a coal roadway under intense mining disturbance
Article.Authors: Xu Z.; Li C.; Ma X.; Qiao F.; Cao Y.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: To inform the selection of borehole pressure relief parameters for coal roadways under intense mining disturbance, this study investigates the pressure relief zone, elastic strain energy redistribution, and ground control performance in the 50,502 haulage roadway at Nangou Coal Mine using elastoplastic analysis, FLAC3D simulations, and field monitoring. The results show that the extent of pressure relief is governed primarily by plastic zone evolution. It increases with borehole diameter, vertical stress, and the lateral stress coefficient, but decreases with cohesion and the internal friction angle. Borehole drilling reduces energy storage in the shallow coal and shifts the energy concentration deeper into the coal mass. Under the conditions investigated, the peak energy density at depth increases rapidly when the borehole diameter exceeds 240 mm, whereas the energy density at the original peak location decreases markedly when the borehole depth exceeds 12 m. Boreholes with a diameter of 180 mm, a depth of 20 m, and a spacing of 1 m, combined with graded support and truss support, reduce the maximum roof-to-floor and rib-to-rib convergence by 23.5% and 56.1%, respectively. These findings indicate that pressure relief and support design must jointly account for shallow pressure relief, energy concentration at depth, and the load-bearing requirements of the surrounding rock.
