Article.Title: Hepatic and intestinal metabolism, intestinal transport, and ABCB1 interaction of 6-prenylnaringenin
Article.Authors: Šadibolová M.; Huličiak M.; Raisová Stuchlíková L.; Horní M.; Prchal L.; Svobodová G.; Vokřálová Navrátilová M.; Novák M.; Vokřál I.; Čečka F.; Červený L.; Boušová I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract 6-prenylnaringenin (6-PN) has recently attracted attention for its chemopreventive, cytotoxic, and analgesic activities; however, information on its pharmacokinetic properties remains limited, making it difficult to interpret its biological effects. This study thus investigated the metabolism of 6-PN in humans, mice, and rats, as well as its intestinal transport and interaction with ABCB1 in humans. 6-PN (10 µM) was efficiently metabolized predominantly via phase II conjugation across all studied species. Overall, 13 phase I/II metabolites were detected, including novel sulfoglucuronide diconjugates not previously reported for structurally similar hop prenylflavonoids. Importantly, murine hepatic metabolism of 6-PN more closely resembled its human hepatic biotransformation profile, favoring murine over rat models in pharmacokinetics studied. Further, 6-PN showed appreciable transport in the absorptive AB direction, while the observed BA-over-AB asymmetry was not reduced by ABCB1/ABCG2 inhibition, although it modulated ABCB1 substrate transport in a model- and substrate-dependent manner. Overall, these data indicate that 6-PN can undergo transepithelial transport in the absorptive direction, whereas extensive phase II metabolism may substantially shape its bioavailability.

Article.Title: In Vivo T2 mapping for early treatment response assessment in esophageal cancer: a prospective study
Article.Authors: Song X.; Li X.; Li Y.; Yuan F.; Wang X.; Wang Y.; Ni L.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the feasibility and reproducibility of in vivo T2 mapping in esophageal cancer (EC) and explore its role in early treatment response assessment during nonsurgical multimodal therapy. This prospective study consecutively enrolled patients with pathologically confirmed EC who were undergoing nonsurgical multimodal therapy from February 2024 to February 2026. In vivo T2 mapping MRI was performed before treatment initiation and again prior to the second treatment cycle. Image quality and measurement reproducibility of T2 mapping were evaluated. Quantitative parameters, including pre- and post-treatment T2 values, absolute change (ΔT2), and percentage change (ΔT2%), were calculated. Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC)-derived parameters were also assessed as established diffusion-based quantitative imaging biomarkers for comparison and multiparametric analysis. Treatment response was assessed using predefined clinical response criteria, and patients were classified into responder and non-responder groups. Between-group differences in T2-derived parameters were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed to evaluate treatment response using clinical-adjusted and imaging-based models. Thirty-four patients were identified as responders (CR/good PR), and twenty-two as non-responders (IR/SD/PD) based on clinical response evaluation. T2 values decreased significantly after early treatment compared with baseline ( p < 0.05). The magnitudes of ΔT2 and ΔT2% were significantly greater in responders than in non-responders. No significant differences were observed in absolute T2 values between the two groups either before or after treatment. The area under the curve (AUC) was 0.738 for ΔT2 and 0.754 for ΔT2% in predicting treatment response. The optimal cutoff values for ΔT2 and ΔT2% were − 5.44 ms and − 6.52%, respectively. In the clinical-adjusted model, ΔT2% remained significantly associated with treatment response after adjustment for age, sex, tumor location, and American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) clinical stage. The imaging-based model showed a higher AUC than ΔADC alone (0.834 vs. 0.823), but the difference was not significant (DeLong test, p = 0.554). In vivo T2 mapping demonstrated good measurement reproducibility in EC. Both ΔT2 and ΔT2% were associated with treatment response, whereas the incremental value of combining ΔT2% with ΔADC requires further investigation.

Article.Title: Integrative meta-transcriptomics and machine learning reveal defence networks and regulatory hubs in response to tomato bacterial pathogens
Article.Authors: Bakhtari B.; Moghadam A.
Article.Abstract: Tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) is an economically important vegetable crop, however, its production is severely affected by bacterial pathogens, including Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. michiganensis ( Cmm ) and Pseudomonas syringae . Plant defence responses are regulated by complex hormonal networks, particularly salicylic acid and jasmonic acid, which activate partially overlapping and context-dependent signalling pathways. Although numerous transcriptomic studies have investigated hormone- and pathogen-associated responses, conserved transcriptional signatures underlying tomato defence remain incompletely understood. To address this, we performed an integrative meta-analysis of massive RNA-seq data using five complementary approaches (fixed-effects, random-effects, Rank Product, Stouffer’s Z-score, and Fisher’s method), identifying 178 upregulated and 177 downregulated consensus DEGs representing a core hormone-responsive signature. Functional enrichment analysis revealed extensive metabolic and regulatory reprogramming involving amino acid metabolism, lipid-associated processes, vesicle trafficking, redox regulation and defence-associated signalling pathways. Protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted highly connected genes, including P5CS ( Solyc08G000796 ) and glutathione reductase ( Solyc09G002031 ), which were associated with proline metabolism and redox homeostasis. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) combined with machine learning-based feature selection enabled the prioritization of integrative candidate genes, including a xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase ( Solyc09G000233 ) and other poorly characterized candidates. In addition, the Random Forest model independently prioritized several highly important features, including Solyc10G001545 , Solyc10G002708 , Solyc07G002639 , Solyc12G001296 which showed strong associations with defence-related transcriptional variation. Collectively, our findings suggest that tomato defence responses involve a complex regulatory landscape integrating metabolic adjustment, signaling processes, redox balance, and cell wall-associated responses. The combination of transcriptomic meta-analysis, network biology, and machine learning provides a framework for prioritizing candidate genes and generating hypotheses for future functional studies aimed at understanding tomato defence responses.

Article.Title: Dynamic spatiotemporal graph network with a temporal masked transformer for traffic flow forecasting
Article.Authors: Wu Z.; Liu X.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Accurate traffic flow forecasting requires a model to capture time-varying spatial correlations, nonlocal temporal dependencies, and recurring traffic patterns simultaneously. Existing spatiotemporal models often rely on fixed relational graphs or local temporal operators, which limits their ability to represent evolving dependencies in traffic networks. To address these limitations, we propose a Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Network with a Temporal Masked Transformer (DSGN-TMT). DSGN-TMT combines layer-specific independent blocks with cross-layer information-sharing blocks to learn complementary representations along the spatial, temporal, and feature dimensions. A time-aware dynamic graph constructor generates periodicity-conditioned spatial and temporal adjacency structures, while a temporal graph convolution module treats historical time slots as graph nodes to capture flexible temporal interactions. In addition, a Temporal Masked Transformer (TMT), a full-history contextual Transformer encoder with an optional masked-subsequence design, is integrated into the forecasting network and trained end-to-end using only forecasting loss; in both training and inference, the TMT processes the complete historical sequence without masking and produces context-aware temporal representations. Experiments on four PeMS benchmark datasets show that DSGN-TMT achieves the lowest MAE, RMSE, and MAPE among 23 comparison methods. Ablation results further demonstrate the complementary contributions of layer-specific learning, cross-layer sharing, dynamic graph construction, temporal graph convolution, and contextual temporal encoding. These results indicate that explicitly coordinating dynamic graph learning with contextual temporal representation is effective for traffic flow forecasting.

Article.Title: Finite-element analysis of recycled-fiber reinforced concrete segmental linings for shield tunnels across construction and service stages
Article.Authors: Waheed M.; Shahbaz A.; Jalal M.; Ullah S.; Abbasi N.; Shah Q.; Alabduljabbar H.; Ahmad F.; Ullah I.
Article.Abstract: Precast segmental linings for shield tunnels experience substantially different loading conditions during storage, tunnel boring machine (TBM) advancement, synchronized grouting, and long-term service. This study presents a comparative finite-element assessment of conventional reinforced-concrete segments (CRCS) and recycled-fiber reinforced-concrete segments (RFRCS) incorporating 0.3% by volume of recycled tire-derived steel fibers together with conventional reinforcing bars. A shield-tunnel lining with an internal diameter of 5.5 m, external diameter of 6.2 m, thickness of 0.35 m, and ring width of 1.2 m was analyzed using Abaqus. Three construction-stage conditions storage loading, TBM jack thrust, and synchronized grout pressure were investigated, while service-stage behavior was evaluated using homogeneous-ring and beam-spring representations. Displacement magnitude and maximum principal strain were used as the primary comparative response indicators, while von Mises stress and reaction force were reported as supplementary numerical outputs. Across all five numerical analyses, RFRCS consistently exhibited lower displacement and maximum principal strain than CRCS. The calculated relative displacement reductions ranged from 60.0% to 70.1%, while the corresponding reductions in maximum principal strain ranged from 55.6% to 63.2%. The reported peak von Mises stress and reaction-force responses remained approximately unchanged between the two systems. The finite-element procedure was benchmarked against full-scale tunnel-segment experiments, with displacement differences of approximately 4.5%, 11.0%, and 6.8%. These comparisons support the adopted procedure for global deformation and elastic response. The consistently lower displacement and maximum principal strain predicted for RFRCS across all five analyses indicate a numerical trend toward reduced deformation under both construction and service-stage loading within the adopted modelling assumptions. However, the validation does not extend to crack propagation, residual tensile behavior, fiber pull-out, or post-cracking response, which were not explicitly simulated.

Article.Title: Prospective evaluation of urinary cytology in the VI-RADS 3 grey zone: association with muscle invasion in bladder tumors
Article.Authors: Altun E.; Oğuz U.; Aslan S.; Tok B.; Bekci T.; Eğrioğlu E.; Tok D.; Demirelli E.; Öğreden E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract VI-RADS 3 lesions represent a diagnostic grey zone for predicting muscle invasion in bladder cancer. We aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative urinary cytology and pathological muscle invasion and to assess its diagnostic performance in patients with VI-RADS 3 bladder tumors. In this prospective single-center cohort study, patients who underwent TURBT between September 2023 and September 2025 were evaluated. Among 241 consecutive patients, 57 with preoperative VI-RADS 3 lesions and available urinary cytology were included. The primary outcome was pathological muscle invasion (≥ T2). Given the few events, analyses were unadjusted: Fisher’s exact test, absolute difference in proportions, odds ratio (OR), and sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Muscle-invasive disease was detected in 5/57 patients (8.8%). Urinary cytology was positive in 12/57 (21.1%) and negative in 45/57 (78.9%). The rate of positive cytology was significantly higher in patients with muscle-invasive disease compared to non–muscle-invasive cases (80.0% vs. 15.4%, p = 0.006). Muscle invasion occurred in 4/12 (33.3%) patients with positive and 1/45 (2.2%) with negative cytology (absolute difference 31.1% points, 95% CI 9.5–58.8% points). Sensitivity was 80.0% (95% CI 28.4–99.5), specificity 84.6% (71.9–93.1), PPV 33.3% (9.9–65.1) and NPV 97.8% (88.2–99.9). In this cohort, positive urinary cytology was associated with muscle invasion in VI-RADS 3 tumors. Whether cytology adds diagnostic value beyond mpMRI or improves clinical decision-making requires validation in larger multicenter studies.

Article.Title: Low-intensity resistance training with blood-flow restriction improves muscle function and activates amino acid and phospholipid metabolism in sarcopenia rat
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Wang Y.; Lou T.; Liao Y.; Xia Y.; Wang Z.; Zuo Z.; Zhou L.; Zheng Y.; Cheng W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sarcopenia is an age-related disease characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and strength, leading to functional decline and frailty. Although high-intensity resistance training effectively improves these disorders, it is often unsuitable for older or frail individuals. This study investigated whether low-intensity resistance training combined with blood-flow restriction improves muscle function, morphology, and metabolism in a rat model of sarcopenia induced by ovariectomy and dexamethasone. A total of 44 female rats were studied, including a normal control group (NC, n = 8) and four model-based groups: sarcopenia model (SM, n = 8), blood-flow restriction (BFR, n = 8), low-intensity resistance training (LI-RT, n = 10), and combined low-intensity resistance training with blood-flow restriction (LRB, n = 10). Metabolomic profiling based on combined criteria of VIP > 1.0, FDR q < 0.05, and fold change > 1.2 or < 0.83 identified 72, 102, and 119 differential metabolites in the NC vs. SM, SM vs. LRB, and NC vs. LRB comparisons, respectively, and revealed that treated rats exhibited a metabolic shift toward the healthy phenotype. After 8 weeks of intervention, functional assessments, histological analyses, and untargeted metabolomics were performed. LRB produced the greatest improvements in grip strength, rotarod performance, and muscle indices, and increased muscle-fiber size without changing fiber number, indicating hypertrophy. Metabolomic profiling further showed a shift toward a healthier metabolic phenotype, with changes in amino acid and phospholipid pathways, including arginine–proline, glycine–serine–threonine, and choline metabolism. These findings indicate that low-intensity resistance training combined with blood-flow restriction improves muscle strength and morphology in sarcopenia and may act through coordinated metabolic remodeling.

Article.Title: Common yoga protocol improves cognitive functions and neural connectivity: a randomized controlled fMRI study in healthy adults
Article.Authors: Chaturvedi S.; Rao P.; Rao R.; Rohatgi S.; Rachalwar V.; Shejwal B.; Vadiraja H.; Patwardhan B.
Article.Abstract: The UN’s International Day of Yoga promotes global participation through the 45-min Common Yoga Protocol (CYP), suitable for all age groups. This randomized controlled study in Pune, India recruited 139 non-alcoholic and nonsmoking healthy adults (18–55 years) to either a 45-day CYP intervention or waitlist control to study effect of CYP. Primary outcome was affect assessed using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS). Secondary outcomes included cognitive domains assessed using the Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST), Digit Span test, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and resting-state fMRI in a subgroup (n = 50) to assess changes in connectivity of large-scale brain networks. Data were analysed using Intention to Treat using ANCOVA with baseline value as a covariate. CYP practice significantly improved positive affect (∆ = 4, p < 0.001), reduced negative affect (∆ = − 3.4, p < 0.001), enhanced digit span scores (total ∆ = 1.1, p = 0.01; forward ∆ = 0.84, p < 0.001), and improved sleep quality (∆ = − 1.2, p < 0.001). Backward span gains were nonsignificant, and DSST showed no group differences. fMRI revealed altered connectivity in sensorimotor, cerebellar, language, salience, and dorsal attention networks favouring yoga. Forty five days CYP practice significantly improves affect, sleep quality, selected cognitive functions, and neural network connectivity in healthy adults; dorsal attention network changes corelate with positive affect.

Article.Title: Attention-free temporal modelling for efficient video violence detection
Article.Authors: Alshdadi A.; Nadeem M.; Alsubaei F.; Alsolami E.; Alharbey R.; Banjar A.; Atlam H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Video-based violence detection is a critical component of intelligent surveillance systems, particularly in smart environments where real-time responsiveness and computational efficiency are paramount. Conventional deep learning models often rely on attention mechanisms to capture temporal dependencies across video frames, but these approaches introduce significant computational overhead, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper investigates whether the multi-head attention component of an established spatiotemporal violence-detection architecture can be replaced with a lightweight 1D temporal convolution while retaining competitive classification performance and reducing computational complexity. The proposed architecture retains the 3D convolutional DenseNet-style backbone and downstream temporal and classification components, while substituting the attention-based temporal modelling stage with a compact Conv1D module. The experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate superior performance where the proposed model achieves 100% accuracy on Peliculas, 95.00% on Hockey, 95.50% on Violent Flow, and 93.50% on RLVD. Additionally, the proposed model reduces the total trainable parameter count by approximately 23% compared with the attention-based reference model, while the Conv1D temporal module itself requires approximately 2.67× fewer parameters than the multi-head attention module. The proposed model also converges faster during training and requires less inference time, making it ideal for real-time applications. The proposed model offers a scalable solution suitable for various applications like smart cities, transportation hubs, and public venues where rapid threat detection is essential. The proposed model also represents a significant step towards attention-free, efficient video violence detection for resource-limited environments.

Article.Title: MEFV variant spectrum and geographic distribution in 2,250 Palestinian familial Mediterranean fever test records over 20 years
Article.Authors: Salhi I.; Alzahayqa M.; Salah Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is highly prevalent among Palestinians, yet large molecular datasets from Palestine are scarce. We retrospectively analyzed all MEFV genetic tests performed at a Palestinian laboratory network between February 2006 and May 2026. Reports issued under successive platforms (PCR–restriction analysis, Sanger sequencing, and variant-specific panels screening up to 24 MEFV variants) were harmonized and classified as negative, monoallelic, or biallelic. Of 2,252 tests, 2,250 records were evaluable. The biallelic genotype detection rate (homozygous or two different variants) was 20.9% (471/2,250; 95% CI 19.3–22.7) and the monoallelic rate 27.1% (609/2,250); any MEFV variant was detected in 48.0%. Among 1,579 variant alleles, five variants accounted for 94.4%: V726A (33.1%), M694V (20.5%), E148Q (16.3%), M680I (13.7%), and M694I (10.8%). The spectrum was stable across three technological epochs despite panel expansion, indicating a population feature rather than an assay artifact. It was strongly geographically structured (city × variant p < 0.0001): M694V, the variant linked to severe disease, dominated in Hebron (43.4% of alleles) and Bethlehem (52.6%), whereas V726A dominated in Nablus (45.9%). Because E148Q is a low-penetrance variant of uncertain significance, we isolated its effect: 80 of 471 biallelic genotypes depended on E148Q, and excluding it lowered the biallelic rate to 17.4%; counting only variants classified as pathogenic in Infevers gave any-variant and biallelic rates of 38.4% and 16.5%. Because the archive contains no clinical data, these rates describe genetic findings in a referred testing population and are not measures of clinical diagnosis. The findings support a focused five-variant primary screening panel for Palestine, highlight the regional concentration of M694V, and underline the need for cautious interpretation of low-penetrance variants and of the substantial monoallelic tier.

Article.Title: Microstructural and mechanical properties of kaolin stabilized with cement, ground-granulated blast-furnace slag, and nano-silica
Article.Authors: Demir S.
Article.Abstract: This study presents the effect of different ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) contents (5, 10, 15, 20, and 30%) on constant cement and nano silica (NS) (7.5% and 1%, respectively)- treated kaolin. A laboratory testing program was conducted, including Atterberg limits, compaction, consolidation, unconfined compression (UCS), and California bearing ratio (CBR) tests, along with microstructural analyses using field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and X-Ray diffraction (XRD). The long-term mechanical response was investigated using 7-, 28-, and 365-day-cured specimens in UCS tests. The results of fresh-state specimens showed that the liquid and plastic limits of clean kaolin increased with the addition of GGBS. With the addition of 7.5% cement-1% NS and 30% GGBS, the liquid limit and optimum water content (w opt ) of clean kaolin increased by 25% and 39.33%, respectively. Void ratio, compressibility (C c ), and swelling (C s ) indices increased with cement, NS, and GGBS additions. Unconfined compressive strength (q u ) of clean kaolin increased with additives and curing days. At 7 days of curing, 7.5% cement and 1% NS additions improved the q u value of clean kaolin by 681.3%. The q u values of some specimens cured for 365-days showed an increase of over 100% compared to their 28-day-counterparts. Similarly, CBR values exhibited a significant increment with GGBS additions, reaching around 300% with 7.5% C-1% NS and 30% GGBS additions. FT-IR and XRD analysis of clean kaolin and treated materials showed a transition from a crystalline structure to an amorphous structure. FE-SEM analyses demonstrated the gel-like products within the soil matrix. Consequently, the microstructural tests suggested that the improvement occurring at the macro scale arises from micro-mechanical changes at the particle scale. This study, therefore, presents new insights into the bridge between micro and macro-observations and the long-term response of kaolin treated with reactive mineral additives, including GGBS, cement, and NS.

Article.Title: Compact convolutional neural networks for AI-based drone detection system
Article.Authors: Farkas G.; Fazekas G.; Karakai P.; Németh A.; Farkas G.
Article.Abstract: The increasing use of first-person-view drones in modern conflicts has created a demand for compact and reliable detection systems capable of operating in complex electromagnetic environments. These drones continuously transmit video signals through onboard video transmitters, generating radio-frequency emissions that can be exploited for early detection. This study investigates the use of lightweight convolutional neural networks for automated detection of drone signals captured by a software-defined radio-based electronic warfare framework. Samples are converted into rasterized time-domain images, providing a computationally efficient input representation suitable for embedded systems. Several custom model architectures were designed and benchmarked in terms of accuracy, model size, and inference performance using a dataset containing approximately 40,000 labeled images. In addition to offline testing, the models were integrated into a GNU Radio signal processing chain for real-time evaluation. Under the evaluated conditions, the compact models achieved high detection accuracy while maintaining small model size and low inference latency, supporting the feasibility of embedded radio-frequency monitoring.

Article.Title: Sustainable recycling of steel slag for the stabilization of dispersive soils; insights into dynamic response and erosion susceptibility
Article.Authors: Ahmed S.; Keskin I.; Vakili A.
Article.Abstract: Dispersive clays are highly susceptible to erosion and structural instability, yet the effectiveness of steel slag (SS) for simultaneously improving their strength, stiffness, and dispersive behavior remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the effectiveness of steel slag as a sustainable stabilizer for dispersive clay by evaluating its effects on mechanical strength, dynamic stiffness, erosion resistance, and dispersive behavior. Clay specimens were stabilized with 0–30% SS at 5% increments and cured for up to 56 days. UCS, bender element, disintegration, and pinhole tests were conducted to assess the engineering performance, while SEM–EDX, XRD, and XRF analyses were used to identify the underlying stabilization mechanisms. Reactions of steel slag with soils allowed to form cementitious hydration products such as calcium-silicate-hydrate (C-S-H) and ettringite, with availability of portlandite (Ca(OH) 2 ), together enhanced soil properties and promoted ion exchange producing denser soil matrix. The results demonstrated a clear dosage-dependent improvement in the engineering performance of dispersive clay. The highest UCS improvement, approximately 152%, was achieved with 25% SS after 56 days, indicating its superior strength performance and favorable balance between mechanical interlocking and chemical stabilization. Accordingly, 25% SS was identified as the optimum dosage, while the reduction in strength at 30% SS after 56 days of curing suggests that excessive slag content may adversely affect the soil matrix. Increasing steel slag content progressively enhanced the dynamic response, with the highest Vs observed at 30% SS after 56 days. A strong correlation between UCS and Vs was observed, with correlation coefficients ranging from r = 0.90–0.98 were observed across the investigated curing periods, demonstrating the potential of nondestructive bender element testing for predicting strength development and monitoring stabilization performance. In the disintegration test, 5% SS reduced mass losses from 100% to approximately 8% after 100 min, while steel slag contents of 15% and higher transformed the soil from highly dispersive (D1) to non-dispersive (ND1–ND2) after curing. In conclusion, the findings demonstrate that steel slag provides a cost-effective and sustainable approach for stabilizing dispersive soils, while reducing dependence on conventional stabilizers and enabling the beneficial reuse of industrial by-products in geotechnical engineering.

Article.Title: Adeno-associated virus capsid as a modular molecular scaffold for the presentation of protein domains
Article.Authors: Hsi-Bell J.; Mietzsch M.; Eddington C.; Jabbari K.; Zachary J.; Sawh-Gopal A.; Chipman P.; Bennett A.; McKenna R.
Article.Abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid engineering has been usually limited to the insertion, substitution, or modification of only a few amino acids within exposed surface loops, restricting the ability to introduce larger functional elements while maintaining capsid assembly and stability. To overcome these limitations, we developed a novel AAV5 capsid scaffold in which the wildtype icosahedral 3-fold protrusions were removed (AAV5 3f DEL), creating an icosahedral platform capable of accommodating larger modular protein assemblies. We validated this approach by integrating twenty trimeric gamma-carbonic anhydrases into the AAV5 3f DEL capsid surface, demonstrating that intact protein domains can be displayed while preserving capsid assembly (AAV5(γ-CA)). The AAV capsid scaffold (AAV5 3f DEL) and the modified capsid (AAV5(γ-CA)) structures were determined using cryo-electron microscopy to 3.2 and 3.8 Å resolution respectively. Furthermore, the AAV5(γ-CA) capsid was demonstrated to be thermostable, with a melting temperature of approximately 65 °C. This approach can be used to expand the AAV engineering platform repertoire and may provide new opportunities for functionalizing AAV based nanoparticles with receptor-binding proteins, catalytic enzymes, and antigenic domains. The ability to decorate AAV capsids with diverse trimeric proteins establishes a versatile framework for potentially developing next-generation gene delivery vectors, targeted therapeutic platforms, and vaccine technologies.

Article.Authors: Ouyang B.; Yang Z.; Chen Y.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: Watershed management requires evaluating ecological service supply alongside human demand, yet basin totals can conceal contrasting patterns in water provision, erosion control, and nutrient export. WY demand increased from 174.80 × 10 9 to 207.51 × 10 9 m 3 , and the SC-demand proxy from 1.0 × 10 9 to 1.2 × 10 9 tonnes. The strongest spatial associations were SC in L–L (q = 0.1423), NE in M–M (q = 0.1702), and WY in H–H (q = 0.3083). Construction-land, population, and GDP showed stronger q values in 2010–2020 than in 2000–2010. These findings support targeted water-use efficiency, erosion-control, and nutrient-load management across distinct basin regions.

Article.Title: Integrated fermentation, downstream processing, and formulation shape the performance of Bacillus thuringiensis-based biocontrol agents
Article.Authors: Nasreddine R.; Ayyildiz G.; Amangeldi Z.; Peralta C.; Caliskan Keçe A.; Kallassy Awad M.; Fillaudeau L.; Escriche B.; Stephan D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The performance of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)-based biopesticides depends not only on their insecticidal proteins but also on the manufacturing process, from fermentation through downstream formulation. However, these stages are often investigated independently, limiting understanding of how process design influences the properties and performance of the final product. This study develops and evaluates a spray-dried formulation of Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. kurstaki (Btk) strain Lip by characterizing the fermentation growth–sporulation trajectory using controlled physicochemical parameters and off-gas monitoring, relating these dynamics to spore and protein production, characterizing the resulting spray-dried formulation, and evaluating its laboratory bioefficacy, and stability .Btk Lip was produced by submerged fermentation on a wheat bran medium under controlled operating conditions and converted to a spray-dried formulation (Lip-F) designed to enhance application performance and resistance to sunlight degradation, and as a unformulated dried material (Lip-U) that will serve as a control and a baseline for following experiments. Across four fermentations (72 h/batch), off-gas and pO 2 profiles were reproducible and coincided with rapid sporulation (9.0–10.0 log 10 CFU/mL) and protein accumulation (1.4–1.5 mg/mL). Quality control showed preserved Cry profiles (130 and 60–65 kDa) and comparable Cry densitometry to Delfin ® (5.0 ± 1.0 vs. 4.1 ± 0.5 mg/g), with higher total protein in Lip-F (104 ± 15 vs. 61 ± 13 mg/g). Bioassays across pests showed efficacy comparable to Delfin ® , with higher potency against Ostrinia nubilalis (LC 50 ratio 2.3; p = 0.03). Sunlight exposure improved stability, Lip-F retained 30 ± 6% CFU vs. 1.85 ± 1.18% (Lip-U), preserved Cry integrity, and maintained Spodoptera frugiperda mortality (Odds Ratio 0.217 vs. 0.0386).

Article.Abstract: Saudi Arabic regional varieties remain underrepresented in automatic speech recognition (ASR) and dialect identification (DID). Simpler fusion configurations also matched or exceeded the full model’s mean performance, while multimodal inference increased latency by approximately 21%, excluding transcription generation. These findings support calibrated ASR hypothesis combination and demonstrate the importance of controlled component evaluation when assessing acoustic–textual fusion for Saudi regional DID.

Article.Title: Comparison of design alternatives for real-time urban flood prediction using field-measured flood-depth data
Article.Authors: Lee G.; Lee H.; Moon H.; Cho J.
Article.Abstract: Minute-level urban flood forecasting performance can vary with lead time, precipitation-input configuration, temporal readout, and forecast format. Using field-observed flood depths at Saebyeok Market in Busan and 1-min precipitation data from three nearby gauges, we compared design alternatives for real-time prediction using precipitation alone. The final test set contained four flood-producing events, and 90.0% of its targets were 0 cm. Among the grouped configurations, the lowest numerical mean absolute errors (MAEs) for 1-, 10-, 30-, and 60-min point forecasts were 1.07, 1.09, 1.39, and 1.80 cm, respectively; the corresponding lowest mean MAEs for horizon forecasts were 1.21, 1.28, 1.35, and 1.54 cm. In paired moving-block bootstrap analyses under Case 4, all 95% confidence intervals included zero, indicating uncertainty in the paired MAE differences. Event-scale hydrographs showed that the reproduction of peak magnitude and recession varied among events. These findings support the joint selection of precipitation inputs, temporal readout, forecast format, and lead time for target operations.

Article.Title: Exploratory multiomics analysis of biologic switching in perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease highlights oxidative phosphorylation-related pathways
Article.Authors: Fang X.; Wang X.; Wang Y.; Wu J.; Zhang Y.; Ding R.; Tang R.; Zhu W.; Huang Z.; Zhang D.; Liu C.; Li Y.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (pfCD) is a severe form of Crohn’s disease (CD) associated with a poor prognosis and frequent treatment failure. Although biologic switching is often regarded as a marker of therapeutic refractoriness, its clinical significance and molecular basis in pfCD remain poorly understood. In this retrospective study, 169 patients with pfCD were enrolled, including 124 in the discovery cohort and 45 in the validation cohort. Clinical and laboratory variables were analyzed to identify factors associated with disease status, and discriminative performance was evaluated using logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and nomogram modeling. Serum proteomic and metabolomic profiling was subsequently performed to characterize molecular changes associated with biologic switching, followed by integrated pathway enrichment analysis. Functional validation was conducted in LPS-stimulated intestinal epithelial cells overexpressing NDUFS3. Biologic switching was associated with disease status after adjustment for the clinical variables included in the multivariable logistic regression model. The model demonstrated good discriminative performance in the discovery cohort and excellent performance in the validation cohort. Exploratory multiomics analysis suggested potential differences in serum molecular profiles between patients with switched and fixed biologic regimens, involving pathways related to inflammatory responses, extracellular matrix regulation, lipid remodeling, and energy metabolism. Exploratory pathway analysis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation as a potential pathway of interest; however, the evidence remained limited because proteomic enrichment did not reach statistical significance after multiple-testing correction and metabolomic support was based on only one mapped metabolite. In vitro, NDUFS3 modulated mitochondrial respiration and inflammatory responses in LPS-stimulated intestinal epithelial cells. Together, these findings suggest that biologic switching is associated with observed disease status and potentially distinct serum molecular profiles in patients with pfCD. The exploratory molecular findings and in vitro functional results warrant further investigation but do not establish a direct mechanistic relationship between biologic switching, NDUFS3, and pfCD in patients.

Article.Title: Helicobacter pylori infection as a prognostic factor in gastric cancer: Impact of comorbidities on overall survival
Article.Authors: Ferreira Paes Landim Ramos A.; Christina de Oliveira Santos-Dutra H.; de Abreu M.; Monteiro da Trindade L.; Pimentel de Assumpção P.; Dias-Neto E.; José Fernández Coimbra F.; Cordeiro Felismino T.; Paula Curado M.; Santiago Barbosa M.

Article.Title: Rheological optimization of low-methylated pectin–xyloglucan–cellulose nanocrystal composites for 3D printing: stability and printability
Article.Authors: Bandyopadhyay S.; Chibrikov V.; Grygorczuk-Płaneta K.; Fila-Loranty K.; Veettil A.; Cybulska J.; Szewczuk-Karpisz K.; Zdunek A.
Article.Abstract: Extrusion-based 3D printing of biobased hydrogels depends on ink rheology, requiring strong shear-thinning for smooth flow and sufficient yield stress to maintain shape after deposition. Among the components, pectin has the strongest influence on rheology. Biobased inks with equal proportions of all three components (3% and 5%) show optimal printability. Compared to 3%, 5% formulations exhibit higher viscosity and yield stress, improving shape retention and pore definition. Ionic cross-linking affects geometry due to swelling, yet enhances mechanical strength. These findings highlight multicomponent plant polysaccharide inks as tunable, sustainable materials for extrusion-based additive manufacturing, mimicking natural PCW assembly.

Article.Title: Effect of synthesis temperature on the carbothermal reduction of silicon carbide from rice husk with copper additive
Article.Authors: Kien K.; Minh H.; Nhi N.; Duyen T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The synthesis of silicon carbide from rice husk typically requires temperatures above 1500 °C due to limitations in solid-state diffusion. For the as-synthesized products, three distinct kinetic regimes were identified: a gradual increase in SiC yield from 900 to 1100 °C (4.63% per 100 °C), a sharp acceleration between 1100 and 1200 °C (8.48% per 100 °C), and a plateau approaching saturation from 1200 to 1300 °C. This kinetic enhancement is fundamentally driven by the Cu catalyst, which promotes a transient liquid-phase-assisted growth mechanism via the formation of a low-temperature Si–Cu eutectic (~ 800 °C), thereby significantly accelerating atomic diffusion between the liquid and solid phases. Following HF purification, the overall SiC content increased rapidly—averaging ~ 14.85% per 100 °C across the 900–1200 °C range—before leveling off. Ultimately, an enhanced SiC content of 88.47% (ISO 21068-2:2024) was achieved at 1300 °C. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of predominantly cubic 3C-SiC, while FTIR spectra revealed characteristic Si–C vibration bands at 809 and 624 cm⁻¹. HF treatment effectively removed residual SiO₂ and Cu oxides, as evidenced by SEM/EDX analysis. Article.Title: “On–off-on” fluorescence sensing of ascorbic acid based on a Fe3+-modulated carbon quantum dots–rhodamine 6G dual-emission system: application to pharmaceutical quality control
Article.Authors: Fang S.; Ding R.; Ke J.; Zhu H.; Xiao J.; Liu T.; Zhao C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable methods for quantifying ascorbic acid (AA) in pharmaceutical formulations are essential for quality control. Article.Title: The effects of smartphone presence during a reading task: a psychophysiological study
Article.Authors: Guimarães J.; Kim R.; Ferreira V.; de Azevedo Neto R.; Sirius E.; Lacerda S.; Bazán P.; Kozasa E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated the psychophysiological effects of smartphone presence and WhatsApp notifications during a reading task, combining questionnaires, electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), and eye-tracking (ET). Furthermore, WhatsApp dependence scores correlated positively with anxiety, perceived stress, and general mental health indicators. These findings suggest that the salience of social media notifications—even without direct engagement—imposes a measurable cognitive and affective cost, impairing task performance and acutely increasing anxiety. Article.Title: Chronic circadian desynchrony disrupts stage-specific spermiogenesis and male fertility
Article.Authors: Becin A.; Lalosevic D.; Andric S.; Kostic T.
Article.Abstract: Circadian disruption is increasingly associated with male reproductive dysfunction, yet the developmental stages underlying this relationship remain poorly defined. Article.Title: Hybrid feedback fusion with multi‑head cross-attention for top‑N recommendation in E-learning systems
Article.Authors: Tairan N.; Namoun A.; Shah H.; Lasisi A.; Naveed Q.; Ali F.
Article.Abstract: Learner ratings in massive open online courses are sparse and, where they exist, overwhelmingly positive, while behavioural traces such as opening, replaying and returning to a resource are far more plentiful and are usually discarded. We set out to test whether fusing the two channels through cross-attention improves recommendation on the Mandarine Academy Recommender System (MARS) corpus. We report the model, and five results about measurement that we consider more consequential than the model. First, the hybrid construction leaks. Because 99.4% of held-out test resources also appear in the same learner’s implicit log, an unguarded frequency-recency-session signal returns the evaluation target to the model’s own input; at the originally submitted configuration, closing the leak with four explicit guards lowers our own HR@10 from 0.910 to 0.635 under the conventional sampled protocol and from 0.526 to 0.206 under full-catalogue ranking. Second, the tuning budget decides the comparison: giving every tunable model the same twelve-trial validation search raised nine of the ten learned baselines, by up to 0.077 in full-catalogue HR@10, and moved our model from fourth of thirteen to eighth of twelve. Third, the sampled protocol that dominates this literature, one positive against ninety-nine sampled negatives, orders models differently from full-catalogue ranking (Spearman 0.664, p = 0.018). Fourth, rating-prediction error carries no usable information about ranking quality here (Spearman − 0.077 against full-catalogue HR@10, p = 0.81), and a constant predictor returning the training-set mean rating achieves RMSE 3.320, lower than that of every model. Fifth, a silent column-name mismatch had left most of our own content-feature matrix empty while its shape remained correct; correcting it reversed two conclusions we had drawn. Under the guarded protocol, with random tie-breaking and Holm-corrected paired tests, Mult-VAE attains the best full-catalogue HR@10 at 0.269 ± 0.003 and HAH-Rec reaches 0.214 ± 0.004, separated from six of the seven models above it. Its ablation shows that content metadata, not the implicit channel, supplies what gain there is, and that cross-attention adds nothing measurable. Text representations of the resources match the curated metadata at best: TF-IDF matches it, a sentence encoder trained for paraphrase similarity approaches it, and averaged word vectors and a transformer encoder fine-tuned for syntax fall below popularity ranking as content-only models and cost HAH-Rec accuracy inside it. The attention weights are weakly correlated with the measured importance of the resources they weight. What survives for the architecture is narrow: its content tower recommends resources withheld from training entirely, where popularity ranking scores zero, though a pure content model on the same metadata does so at least as well. We release the guarded pipeline so that the leakage and tuning effects we describe can be checked for on other corpora.

Article.Authors: Metin Z.; Sarıteke Y.; Yücel S.; Arslan N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a common condition among women of reproductive age. This study aimed to examine the relationships between UPF consumption, adherence to the Mediterranean diet, mindful eating, and PMS severity in young adult women. This cross-sectional study assessed PMS severity using the Premenstrual Syndrome Scale (PMSS), UPF consumption using the Screening Questionnaire of Highly Processed Food Consumption (sQ-HPF), Mediterranean diet adherence using the Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS), and mindful eating using the Four-Facet Mindful Eating Scale (FFaMES). Internal Awareness ( r = 0.221, p < 0.001) and External Awareness ( r = 0.234, p < 0.001) showed positive bivariate correlations. Mediterranean diet adherence showed a weak inverse correlation with PMS severity ( r = − 0.091, p = 0.025). Article.Title: Authenticated RGB image encryption using switched inverse substitution and multiplex Cayley-graph diffusion
Article.Authors: Razaq A.; Mustafa H.; Khyzer S.; Mazhar S.; Alolaiyan H.
Article.Abstract: Due to the high correlation of RGB images in both spatial and channel domains, the encryption should have the characteristics of nonlinear confusion, spatial and cross-channel diffusion, exact reversibility and integrity protection. This paper proposes SGEM-RGB-24, an authenticated RGB image-encryption scheme in which each pixel is represented as an element of \({\mathbb{F}}_{{2}^{24}}\) . Each round combines position-dependent whitening, a key-dependent switched inverse substitution over \({\mathbb{F}}_{{2}^{24}}\) , MDS mixing of the colour coordinates and two-pass diffusion on a three-layer multiplex Cayley graph based on \(\text{P}\text{S}\text{L}(\text{2,7})\) . Independent material for each component is derived using HKDF-SHA-256 and AES-256-CTR under domain-separated contexts; HMAC-SHA-256 is used to authenticate the encrypted material, the nonce and image parameters before decryption. It is shown that each stage is invertible. For three medical images and three general colour images, all images were recovered exactly, the mean entropy value of the ciphertexts was 7.999955, the mean absolute adjacent-pixel correlation was 0.001336, and, after a one-bit plaintext change, the mean NPCR, UACI and bit avalanche were 99.609521%, 33.463188% and 49.999446%, respectively. All graphs met the specified spectral-gap condition and all tested modifications were rejected. The scheme is described as a research scheme, which needs more formal cryptanalysis before standardization.

Article.Authors: Mosca R.; Avanatti M.; Infantino M.; Ricciulli R.; Sardelli G.; Suman A.; Moschini R.; Cappiello M.; Del-Corso A.; Balestri F.; Signore G.

MIA PaCa-2 cells also showed reduced extracellular lactate production, while cellular energy charge remained unchanged in both models. Article.Abstract: Waterlogging is a major abiotic constraint on sugarcane ( Saccharum spp. hybrid) productivity in poorly drained, monsoon affected parts of north-western India. Genotype, treatment, and their interaction significantly affected all studied parameters ( P < 0.0001). Waterlogging reduced chlorophyll content, total soluble sugars, and total soluble protein by 22.6, 25.0, and 16.0%, respectively, while increasing total reducing sugars, proline, total phenol content, catalase activity, and SOD activity by 39.6, 64.0, 32.0, 97.0, and 87.0%, respectively. CoPb 18,213 showed comparatively high values for chlorophyll, total soluble sugars, proline, and total phenol content, whereas CoLk 19,017 showed comparatively low values for several pigment and metabolic parameters and CoPb 19,212 recorded comparatively low CAT and SOD activities. Correlation and principal component analyses showed that CAT and SOD activity ( r = 0.906, P < 0.001) were strong positively correlated with each other but only weak and non-significantly correlated with the other measured traits, indicating that these associations reflect patterns within the present dataset rather than confirmed physiological independence, coordinated regulation, or waterlogging tolerance mechanisms. When compared using each genotype’s percentage change from its own control, CoPb 18,213’s CoPb 18,213’s- Do not put commas in all the varieties/clones names. Write them as CoPb 18213 (without using comma) strongest relative responses were enzymatic antioxidant induction (CAT, SOD) and reducing-sugar accumulation rather than proline or chlorophyll retention. CoLk 19,017’s comparatively low pooled means, in turn, were concentrated mainly in chlorophyll retention rather than a uniformly weak response across traits. These findings indicate that sugarcane clones rely on distinct combinations of pigment, metabolic and antioxidant-enzyme responses to cope with waterlogging, a distinction relevant to future screening and breeding for waterlogging resilience.

Article.Title: NGU-Net: a modified U-Net with feature refinement block for accurate medical image segmentation
Article.Authors: Hassan E.; Ghadiri H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is essential for medical diagnosis and treatment planning, enabling automated and reliable analysis of complex imaging data. Despite the widespread use of U-Net and its variants, challenges remain, including internal covariate shifts and suboptimal feature extraction, which can limit performance on complex datasets. NGU-Net builds on the U-Net encoder–decoder and introduces a Feature Refinement Block (FRB) that keeps the two-convolution structure of the standard block. In each FRB, a 3 × 3 convolution with ReLU is followed by a second 3 × 3 convolution, batch normalization, and a final ReLU. This ordering stabilizes the internal feature distributions and training, with only a negligible increase in parameters. These modifications contribute to faster convergence during training and improved segmentation performance. Experimental results on brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) datasets demonstrate that NGU-Net outperforms the original U-Net and several of its variants, achieving higher accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed framework provides an effective architecture for brain tumor segmentation, demonstrating promising performance on The Cancer Genome Atlas Lower-Grade Glioma (TCGA-LGG) dataset that warrants further multi-center external validation.

Article.Title: Molecular adaptations and metabolic reprogramming of Priestia megaterium KW16 in response to fungal pathogen-derived filtrates
Article.Authors: Pinski A.; Nowak B.; Żur-Pińska J.; Beckmann M.; Mur L.; Hupert-Kocurek K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Priestia megaterium KW16 is an endophytic bacterium with broad-spectrum antifungal activity, but its molecular response to phytopathogens remains unknown. Here, we combined transcriptomics, metabolomics, RT-qPCR, and fatty acid profiling to characterise the response of KW16 to cell-free culture filtrates of pathogenic fungi: Colletotrichum dematium , Fusarium avenaceum , Rhizoctonia solani , and Sclerotinia sclerotiorum . KW16 inhibited the growth of all tested fungi, with the strongest effect observed against S. sclerotiorum (> 50%), followed by C. dematium, R. solani, and F. avenaceum . Transcriptomic analysis identified 2440 unique differentially expressed genes, with S. sclerotiorum inducing the largest response (1149 upregulated and 1058 downregulated genes). A conserved response across all treatments included repression of sporulation-associated genes and induction of genes involved in iron acquisition, acetate utilisation, stress adaptation, and cell wall remodelling. Our results demonstrated that exposure to fungal filtrates upregulated the genes encoding gas vesicle biosynthesis, competence-associated functions, and lasso peptide biosynthetic genes, particularly in response to S. sclerotiorum . The fungal-derived metabolites could serve as both nutritional resources and ecological signals, driving extensive physiological reprogramming in KW16 and revealing molecular mechanisms that may underlie its persistence and biocontrol activity in competitive plant-associated environments.

Article.Title: Thermodynamically constrained exclusive occupancy of p65 Cysteine 38 resolves the persulfidation–overoxidation competition in neuronal oxygen–glucose deprivation
Article.Authors: Singh D.; Juvvanapudi S.; Jabbar M.; Heera M.; Sree S.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ischemic injury is described through a therapeutic window whose molecular content has never been specified, and the candidate switch, the redox state of a reactive cysteine, is measured only as a population average over whole proteins. Modifications of one cysteine are alternative fates of a single sulfur atom, yet no kinetic representation treats them as competing occupants of one site. Cysteine 38 of the NF-κB p65 subunit is represented here as a point on a probability simplex whose six vertices are its chemically distinct states, evolving under a generator whose rate constants are produced from state free energies, edge barriers and cosubstrate free-energy changes, so that every cycle affinity depends on chemical potentials alone. The residue layer is coupled to the bioenergetic collapse of oxygen–glucose deprivation and to a bistable survival decision. Cycle affinities proved invariant to the state free energies to $$\:4\times\:{10}^{-15}RT$$ , and detailed balance was recovered exactly, with net cycle flux below $$\:{10}^{-18}{min}^{-1}$$ . Persulfide occupancy rose to 0.44 while oxygen was absent and collapsed on restoration, when sulfinate occupancy reached 0.33, identifying restoration rather than deprivation as the vulnerable interval. Only representations enforcing exclusive occupancy reproduced the reported reversal of the sulfide effect with concentration, raising survival from 0.53 to 0.57 before falling. The thermodynamic constraint removed exactly the six parameter directions the observations cannot constrain, improving identifiability from 9 of 22 directions to 11 of 16 without altering any trajectory. Results are computational; no experimental measurement is reported.

Article.Title: Critical comparison of storage strategies for oral metagenomics
Article.Authors: Rehner J.; Förster M.; Rupf S.; Becker S.; Keller A.; Molano L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The salivary microbiome is increasingly recognized as a diagnostic resource for oral and systemic health, offering a noninvasive alternative to stool sampling. However, pre-analytical factors, including collection and storage conditions, may influence microbial nucleic acid stability and sequencing results, particularly in resource-limited settings where immediate freezing is impractical. We evaluated ten storage conditions across 50 saliva samples collected using sterile Falcon tubes, ZymoBIOMICS DNA/RNA Shield tubes, and Oragene ® Discover kits. Samples were processed immediately, frozen at − 80 °C, or stored at room temperature or 30 °C for up to three days, and were analyzed by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Most core oral taxa were detected across conditions but their relative contribution showed method-dependent abundance. Sequencing yield and Shannon diversity did not differ significantly from fresh samples. In contrast, both preservation buffers reduced observed richness by 16–25% and shifted community composition. These shifts reflected a selective loss of Gram-negative taxa such as Neisseria and Porphyromonas , which fell from 59% to 6–15% of reads in every participant. Unpreserved storage for more than two days instead increased the proportion of Gram-negative and anaerobic bacteria. Notably, nucleic acid from the bacterium Klebsiella pneumoniae was detected only in Oragene ® Discover and sterile falcon samples stored at 30 °C. Overall, freezing or storage in sterile tubes for up to two days best preserved the fresh salivary profile, supporting saliva-based metagenomic studies in decentralized and resource-constrained environments.

Article.Title: Design of an ultra low voltage VDBA using bulk driven quasi floating gate techniques for high order biosignal processing
Article.Authors: Kumngern M.; Khateb F.; Kulej T.; Arbet D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents a high-performance ultra-low-voltage (ULV) voltage differencing buffered amplifier (VDBA) operating from a 0.5-V supply. Consisting of an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) followed by a voltage follower (VF), the proposed VDBA combines bulk-driven (BD) and bulk-driven quasi-floating-gate (BD-QFG) MOS techniques to overcome threshold-voltage limitations and enhance the performance of subthreshold circuits. Designed in the Cadence Virtuoso environment using the TSMC 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed VDBA consumes only 370 nW and occupies 0.022 mm 2 area. Its applicability is demonstrated through a fifth-order Butterworth low-pass filter for ECG signals, achieving an electronically tunable cutoff frequency from 73.65 to 557.8 Hz, 1.1% THD for a $$\:100{\text{}\text{mV}}_{\text{p-p}}$$ input signal, and a 44 dB dynamic range. Monte Carlo and PVT analyses confirm the robustness of the proposed design, while experimental implementation using the commercially available LM13700 further validates the proposed filtering approach.

Article.Title: Composition- and temperature-controlled architecture of pluronic F127–miltefosine mixed micelles
Article.Authors: Carriles J.; Aydillo C.; Smith G.; Nguewa P.; González-Gaitano G.; Dirany Z.
Article.Abstract: Polymeric micelles have been long used as nanocarriers to improve the solubility and delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs. However, the incorporation of amphiphilic drugs introduces an additional level of complexity, where the drug can contribute directly to the self-assembly process, giving rise to mixed micelles whose structure and properties are determined by the cooperative interactions of both components. Here, we investigate this concept using Pluronic ® F127, a thermoresponsive triblock copolymer, and miltefosine (MF), an amphiphilic drug currently used for the treatment of leishmaniasis. By combining small-angle neutron scattering with complementary light scattering, fluorescence, and NMR methods, we establish a quantitative structural description of F127-MF mixed micelles over a range of polymer-to-drug ratios. MF promotes the formation of mixed micelles by facilitating micellization at lower F127 concentrations and below its critical micellization temperature, while preferentially partitioning into the hydrophobic core. Through manipulation of the polymer-to-drug ratio, the properties of these mixed micelles can be tuned. At high F127 content, the mixed micelles closely resemble those of the pure surfactant, whereas increasing MF fraction induces a transition from polymer-rich to drug-rich aggregates characterized by changes in aggregation number, hydration, and internal organization. Overall, this work establishes an exhaustive characterization of F127–MF mixed micelles as a versatile and tunable colloidal system, providing valuable insights into the design of pharmaceutical formulations based on amphiphilic block copolymers as drug carriers.

Article.Title: Governance capacity determines food security resilience across Arab sub-regions (2016–2025)
Article.Authors: Abdelmagid S.; Abdelgadir H.; Qurtam A.; Ali A.; Elsayed A.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the evolution of food security across the Arab region from 2016 to 2025, addressing three research questions: trends in key food security indicators, differential impacts of major shocks across sub-regions, and conditions under which shocks become persistent versus transitory. Using triangulated data from AOAD, FAO, World Bank, GHI, and GFSI with panel regression (2016–2022, N = 98), we find that while the pan-Arab food gap increased from $34.5 billion to $43.3 billion, the aggregate trend masks a four-tier resilience hierarchy. Persian Gulf countries showed strong negative correlation between food prices and hunger (− 0.741), while conflict-affected regions showed very strong positive correlations (0.71–0.92). Panel regression shows a statistically significant positive association between SDG progress and food security outcomes (Fixed Effects β = 0.255, p = 0.001). The analysis indicates that governance capacity, not strategy availability, is the strongest predictor of resilience. A central contrast emerges between sub-regions. The Persian Gulf maintains undernourishment below 5% despite 94.6% import dependence, whereas the Maghreb, Mashreq, and Central regions face rates of 6–8%, 12–15%, and over 20% respectively. This shows that the same import dependence amplifies vulnerability when fiscal buffers are absent. We propose a differentiated implementation model where AOAD coordinates region-specific programs tailored to sub-regional capacities. Without targeted interventions addressing these gaps, regional food security will remain fragile, poorly governed, and deeply unequal.

Article.Title: Decoding the night: a machine learning approach to diagnose and predict the severity of obstructive sleep apnea through clinical parameters
Article.Authors: Özçelik N.; Bendeş E.; Özçelik A.; Şentürk Topaloğlu E.; Özyurt S.; Karadağ M.; Güçlü Ö.; Yıldız M.; Selimoğlu Şen H.; Yetkin N.; Baran B.; Öztürk Ö.; Erçelik M.; Türkmen Kaya H.; Sarıoğlu N.; Çolak M.; Akkoyunlu M.; Kansu A.; Kotan A.; Karakaş F.; Bülbül Y.; Doğru S.; Gümüş A.; Özçıbık Işık G.; Topaloğlu Ö.
Article.Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep-related disorder associated with cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities. Early diagnosis is essential; however, access to polysomnography is limited. Machine learning approaches may support clinical decision-making by predicting OSA using easily obtainable variables. This study aimed to develop an artificial neural network (ANN) model to predict the presence and severity of OSA. This multicenter study included adult patients who underwent diagnostic polysomnography at ten different sleep centers. Eighteen demographic and clinical parameters were used as input features, and four OSA severity categories served as output classes. The ANN architecture consisted of one hidden layer with 50 neurons (ReLU activation) and a Softmax output layer. The dataset was randomly divided into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. A total of 1,954 participants (70.2% male) were included. Polysomnography classified 39.2% of participants as severe OSA, 29.4% as mild OSA, 15.0% as moderate OSA, and 16.4% as non-OSA. The ANN model demonstrated good discriminative performance across OSA severity categories, with class-specific AUC values ranging from 0.89 to 0.96. These findings support the potential utility of ML-based tools for screening and early risk stratification, particularly in resource-limited settings.

Article.Title: Intracortical recordings in human lateral occipital complex support the biased-competition model of spatial attention
Article.Authors: Vanhoyland M.; Ramirez J.; Janssen P.; Theys T.
Article.Abstract: Spatial attention is fundamental for prioritizing relevant information in complex visual environments. Yet, the neural mechanisms underlying this process in humans remain elusive, given the spatiotemporal constraints of noninvasive functional imaging. Here we present multi-unit spiking activity from the human lateral occipital complex (LO) during a covert spatial visual attention task. Spatial attention strongly modulates neural activity when two competing stimuli fall within the receptive field, but not when only one of them does, supporting the biased-competition model of attention. This model suggests that spatial attention reduces interference between stimuli by favoring the attended one. We further found that, under competition, attended, task-relevant objects are selectively maintained. This is, to our knowledge, the first demonstration of the neural effects of spatial attention in human visual cortex at the level of multi-unit spiking activity, offering a more naturalistic view of human visual attention, as participants received no prior training, unlike electrophysiological studies in trained macaques. Our study bridges human neuroimaging and primate electrophysiology, providing insights into the neural basis of attention.

Article.Title: Lie group error state representation and analysis in earth-centred earth-fixed coordinate system
Article.Authors: Mingming L.; Jinlai L.; Ke Z.
Article.Abstract: To address navigation accuracy degradation caused by error accumulation in traditional Strapdown Inertial Navigation Systems (SINS), this paper systematically investigates error state representation and analysis methods for SINS in the earth-centered earth-fixed (ECEF) frame based on Lie group theory. The SINS mechanization in the ECEF frame was established, embedding attitude, speed, and position states into the extended special Euclidean group, and deriving both left-invariant and right-invariant error representations for non-group-affine and group-affine Lie group error models. By introducing auxiliary speed vectors, a SINS mechanization satisfying group-affine dynamic characteristics was constructed. Given the time-varying characteristics of measurement noise in SINS/DVL integrated navigation, the Sage-Husa Adaptive Kalman Filter (AKF) was employed for real-time estimation and adjustment of measurement noise. Five algorithms were compared through shipboard experiments: traditional error model (ESINS), non-group-affine left error model (LSE), non-group-affine right error model (RSE), group-affine left error model (LSEGA), and group-affine right error model (RSEGA). Experimental results showed that under small misalignment angles (e.g., [0.1° 0.1° 0.1°] and [1° 1° 1°]), RSEGA-AKF and RSE-AKF perform comparably to the other algorithms, with only marginal differences in yaw and position accuracy. Their distinct and measurable superiority is exclusively demonstrated under large misalignment angle scenarios. Under [0.1° 0.1° 0.1°] misalignment, yaw RMSE and MAE differ by only 1 × 10 −3 ◦10 −30 , while position RMSE and MAE differences are within 0.7 m and 0.5 m respectively, which are negligible for practical navigation. Under large misalignment angles ([10° 10° 10°] and [30° 30° 30°]), however, the advantages of RSEGA-AKF and RSE-AKF become prominent and clearly measurable: under [30° 30° 30°] misalignment, yaw RMSE and MAE are superior by up to 0.3° and 0.1° respectively, while position RMSE and MAE are reduced by up to 15 m.

Article.Title: NSFA AQE CenterOBB detects oriented SAR ships using frequency domain noise suppression and angle quality estimation
Article.Authors: Roohi S.; Akbarizadeh G.
Article.Abstract: Ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery underpins maritime surveillance, traffic monitoring, and safety-of-navigation applications, yet high-quality detection in real-world SAR remains difficult. Multiplicative speckle and sensor-dependent noise degrade contrast, sea clutter and strong land or shore backscatter confuse inshore scenes, and elongated ships need reliable orientation estimates that a horizontal bounding box simply cannot give. We present NSFA–AQE CenterOBB, an end-to-end, anchor-free, one-stage detector built to address these three problems within a single oriented-detection pipeline. Its backbone is lightweight and includes Noise Suppression and Feature Amplification (NSFA) blocks that modulate the spectrum of intermediate feature maps, designed to attenuate clutter while preserving ship-discriminative structure; a Sobel-derived edge enhancement module adds boundary cues intended to support localization under weak contrast. Building on a CenterNet-style objects-as-points formulation, a probabilistic angle head predicts both an orientation mean and an uncertainty estimate, trained with a periodic negative log-likelihood loss that respects the π-periodic symmetry of ship orientation. At inference, this uncertainty drives an Angle Quality Estimation (AQE) mechanism that recalibrates detection scores during decoding and oriented non-maximum suppression. A symmetric Kullback–Leibler divergence regularizer maps predicted and ground-truth oriented boxes onto two-dimensional Gaussians and enforces geometric consistency across center, size, and orientation. On SSDD + , the rotated-box relabeling of the SAR Ship Detection Dataset, the detector performs competitively across both offshore and challenging inshore scenes, and our cumulative ablation shows that adding a geometry-consistency term to the training objective gives the numerically largest single step in mean average precision (part of which offsets a preceding drop at the probabilistic-angle stage); a controlled comparison across four geometry-consistency loss formulations shows the symmetric KLD variant we adopt achieves the highest mAP50, although the differences among the geometry losses are within run-to-run variation, and it is not the best in mAP75 or angular accuracy. The predicted angle uncertainty is, however, only weakly informative at the evaluated checkpoint, so AQE does not improve AP in our controlled comparison.

Article.Title: Enhancing ultrasonic spot weldability of aluminum-copper alloy through surface modification techniques
Article.Authors: V. S.; Pattanaik A.; Satpathy M.; Debebe S.
Article.Abstract: Ultrasonic welding is a solid-state technique that is increasing​ly employed to join Li-ion battery interconnections in electric automobiles. Understanding the joint microstructure is essential for evaluating the performance and joint integrity. Surface modifications play a crucial role in affecting the friction and contact behavior at the joint interface. This investigation describes the effects of surface treatments and various welding energies on the ultrasonic weldability of aluminum/copper alloy joints using lubricated, normal, electrolytic, and emery-polished surfaces. The results demonstrated that lubricated surfaces facilitated improved plastic flow and mechanical interlocking, resulting in elevated tensile shear and T-peel failure loads of 642.37 N and 280.86 N, respectively, at a welding energy of 1950 J. The interface temperature of 420.66 °C was attained at this optimum weld energy. Microstructural analysis indicated that the lubricated surfaces exhibited a ductile fracture mode characterized by dimples, signifying mechanical interlocking and interface diffusion. Emery-polished surfaces exhibited the lowest mechanical performance. This decline is attributed to mixed-mode fracture, adhesive wear, and poor metallic bonding. Restricted interfacial sliding is considered responsible for the weakened bond. X-ray diffraction verified the existence of Al 2 Cu, Cu 5 Zn 8 , and Al 4 Cu 9 intermetallic compounds at the edge of the aluminum/copper alloy joints.

Article.Title: Feature guided prompting distorts synthetic fake news corpora without improving detection
Article.Authors: Wani S.; Zangana H.; Gulzar Y.; Alkanan M.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly applied for generating synthetic training data to address class imbalance problems in fake news detection. Existing approaches commonly apply multiple stylistic constraints in generation prompts to control the characteristics of generated samples and evaluate their overall compliance. However, the contribution of individual constraints to synthetic data augmentation performance remains unclear. This research investigates whether any single stylistic constraint is necessary or sufficient to improve LLM-based data augmentation effectiveness. A single-feature ablation analysis was conducted using an LLM-based augmentation pipeline with the GossipCop–PolitiFact headline dataset containing 23,196 samples and 15 stylistic constraints adopted from previous research. The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model was used as the primary generator across 26 prompt conditions. Phi-3.5-mini-instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B were used for cross-model validation on three key conditions (full, naive, F5-only). Three independently generated corpora, each containing 5,000 headlines, were produced for every condition and evaluated with six classical classifiers (30 seeds each), three fine-tuned transformers (3 seeds each), and one zero-shot LLM classifier. The results indicate that no individual stylistic constraint is necessary, as all 15 ablation settings achieved statistical equivalence under a two-one-sided equivalence test with δ = 0.02. Although three features (F1, F7, F9) produced statistically detectable changes after FDR (false discovery rate) correction, their magnitudes remained within the equivalence margin. Furthermore, the F5-only prompt achieved performance within δ = 0.02 of the full prompt across the three evaluated generator families. The maximum within-family F1 difference among the full, naive, and F5-only conditions was 0.0088. Although F5-only achieved numerically higher F1 scores than naive prompting, the differences remained below the predefined practical margin. In the Qwen experiments, the F6-only and F12-only prompts also matched the full prompt within δ = 0.02, as did the F6 + F4 condition (Δ = −0.0037). In the primary Random Forest evaluation, the Qwen full, naive, and F5-only conditions achieved lower fake F1 scores than the no-augmentation baseline of 0.6034. Random oversampling and class-weighted Random Forest achieved higher scores of 0.6324 and 0.6452, respectively. The findings indicate that the stylistic constraints may introduce distributional distortions rather than improve alignment with real fake-news characteristics. The full prompt increased question mark frequency by 5.3× and reduced ALL CAPS usage by 12.5×, while the F5-only prompt increased exclamation mark frequency by 15×. The direction of question-mark distortion is partly model-specific: Qwen and Phi over-comply (5.34× and 4.51×) while DeepSeek under-complies (0.66×), confirming that the misalignment is a joint property of the prompt and the generator. These findings indicate that synthetic data quality evaluation should consider feature-level distributional alignment rather than relying solely on aggregate prompt compliance, particularly within the scope of the English-language headline generation setting evaluated in this study.

Article.Title: TraCo-CLIP: transition-conditioned CLIP adaptation for static-bias-robust open-vocabulary video action recognition
Article.Authors: Zhuang J.; Zhang Y.; Bao F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adapting image–text pretrained models to video action recognition requires learning temporal information while preserving transferable visual–textual representations. However, global category-level supervision can favor class-correlated static cues over localized temporal evidence. We propose TraCo-CLIP, a transition-conditioned CLIP adaptation framework for static-bias-robust open-vocabulary video action recognition. A lightweight controller combines semantic change, frame-level ambiguity relative to the source action vocabulary, and their interaction to estimate transition-sensitive routing scores. Temporal non-maximum suppression with fallback selection and confidence-weighted local aggregation construct transition anchors. Two auxiliary objectives supervise the same anchors: transition-centered visual–textual alignment provides inter-class discrimination, while static counterfactual contrast compares transition-oriented and static textual descriptions within the same action category. Both objectives regularize the shared visual representation during training. We evaluate TraCo-CLIP under base-to-novel, cross-dataset, cross-domain open-vocabulary, and out-of-context static-bias protocols. On XOV-Action, the reported controlled comparisons improve $$\mathrm {AVG\text{- }A}$$ by $$2.61$$ and $$2.60$$ percentage points under K150 and K400 source training, respectively. On UCF101-SCUBA/SCUFO, SCUBA accuracy increases by $$8.3$$ points, SCUFO accuracy decreases by $$6.4$$ points, and contrasted accuracy increases by $$11.9$$ points. Controlled ablations and representation-level analyses support the usefulness of the auxiliary learning framework under the evaluated settings. The auxiliary components introduce computation and text-bank storage during training. They are removed for recognition inference, leaving the same deployed architecture and inference operations as the controlled baseline.

Article.Title: Descriptive comparison of fatigue performance in asphalt mixtures containing reclaimed asphalt pavement using combined activation treatments
Article.Authors: Ma W.; Chen S.; Fazli A.; Khairy Y.; Ghoniem R.
Article.Abstract: This study examined fatigue damage evolution in asphalt mixtures containing 48% Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement to determine how RAP material characteristics and combined activation treatments influence dry and moisture-conditioned fatigue performance. Three RAP materials, Urban Arterial, Highway Corridor, and Industrial Pavement, were each combined with Low, Medium, and High activation treatments that simultaneously varied rejuvenator dosage, mixing temperature, and compaction temperature, producing nine formulations. Dry specimens were tested at 400 and 500 microstrain, while freeze-thaw-conditioned specimens were tested at 500 microstrain. RAP characterization included binder content, penetration, softening point, viscosity, carbonyl index, sulfoxide index, and fine fraction. Performance evaluation included volumetric properties, Indirect Tensile Strength, Tensile Strength Ratio, Retained Modulus, fatigue life, dissipated energy, normalized stiffness damage, Fatigue Life Retention, and Normalized Fatigue Loss. The Medium treatment produced the highest fatigue life within each RAP material. HC_M achieved the highest N₅₀ values of 81,726 cycles at 400 microstrain, 28,451 cycles under dry conditions at 500 microstrain, and 22,983 cycles after freeze-thaw conditioning. HC_M also achieved a Tensile Strength Ratio of 90.1%, Retained Modulus of 87.5%, Fatigue Life Retention of 80.8%, and Normalized Fatigue Loss of 19.2%. Increasing strain from 400 to 500 microstrain reduced fatigue life by 65.2% to 70.3% across the tested formulations. These results indicate that moderate combined activation provided the most favorable balance of moisture resistance and fatigue durability among the tested 48% RAP mixtures.
