Article.Title: Prognostic role of 18FDG-PET/CT based biomarker, tumor grading and immunohistochemical markers in breast cancer survival
Article.Authors: Fatima N.; Zaman M.
Article.Abstract: To determine prognostic strength of 18 FDG PET/CT based glucose metabolism, tumor grading and immunohistochemical markers in breast cancer (BC) patients. The cohort study conducted at PET/CT Section of one of the tertiary care hospitals in Karachi, Pakistan. A total of 110 patients with advanced-stage breast cancer (predominantly stage II or higher) who underwent baseline 18 F-FDG PET/CT between April 2017 and July 2020 were included. Patients were followed for up to five years from date of baseline 18 FDG PET/CT, and metabolic progression-free survival (mPFS) was assessed using serial 18 FDG PET/CT findings. Tumor demographics (type, grading, staging) and immunohistochemistry (estrogen receptor ER, human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 HER2/Neu, progesterone receptor PR, Ki-67) were also recorded. Using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis, the significant predictors of complete metabolic response (CMR) based on binary outcome (CMR achieved and not achieved) were analyzed. Kaplan Meier’s survival plots were analyzed to measure mPFS against ROC derived cutoff values of significant predictors. The median age of study group was 57 years (25–86 years), significantly obese and 85% invasive ductal CA with 97% grade II-III on Bloom-Richardson classification and stage IV disease (74%). The significant association of maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and Ki-67 index were found in CMR on logistic regression while no significant association of patients’ age, BMI, tumor grading, ER, PR, HER-2/neu status were found in CMR in BC. SUVmax > 5.4 and Ki-67 > 30% were found to have significant association with failure to achieve CMR (AUC 0.729 and 0.759; p = 0.0002* and p = 0.0001* respectively). The mPFS was significantly shorter in patients with SUVmax > 5.4 (29 vs. 45 months; Logrank = 16.356; p = 0.0001*) and in patients with Ki-67 > 30% index (27 vs. 48 months; Logrank = 14.901; p = 0.0001*). Higher baseline SUVmax (> 5.4) and Ki-67 index (> 30%) on baseline 18 FDG were associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CMR and significantly shorter mPFS in breast cancer patients. Integration of metabolic and proliferative biomarkers may improve prognostic risk stratification, particularly in advanced breast cancer.

Article.Title: Efficient greybox fuzzing framework with tabu search
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Niu Z.; Xiao K.
Article.Abstract: Recently, fuzzing has emerged as a prominent technique for automatically detecting a wide range of security vulnerabilities in cybersecurity. Nevertheless, existing fuzzers remain limited in seed scheduling and energy allocation, as they typically rely on coarse-grained criteria or computationally intensive methods to evaluate seed quality. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive fuzzing framework, namely TabuFuzz, which aims to prioritize seeds with a higher likelihood of generating interesting variants through mutation and allocate more energy to that seed. Specifically, TabuFuzz utilizes a tabu search (TS) algorithm to model seed scheduling, enabling the precise selection of promising seeds. In addition, we design an adaptive energy allocation strategy that exploits fine-grained dynamic execution information, thereby enhancing overall fuzzing efficiency. We implement TabuFuzz on top of AFL and evaluate it on nine widely-used real-world programs. Across six independent 24-hour trials, TabuFuzz achieved higher observed path exploration and crash discovery than the evaluated baselines on most target programs, with improvements of 19.89% and 160.87% over AFL, respectively. Comparative analyses further show that TabuFuzz recorded higher numbers of paths and crashes than representative fuzzers such as FairFuzz, MOPT, EcoFuzz, and AFL + + under the reported experimental setup.

Article.Authors: Shunkeyev K.; Sagimbayeva S.; Kenzhebayeva A.; Ubaev Z.; Beketova G.; Zhumabayev D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A purification and growth process for alkali halide crystals (AHCs) is demonstrated using KCl: Li as a model system and employing an experimental crystal growth setup manufactured by Across International, USA. The process involves the following sequential stages: (i) deposition of a thin pyrolytic carbon coating (pyrolysis) onto the inner surface of a quartz ampoule in order to suppress the adhesion of molten alkali halide compounds (AHCs) to the ampoule walls; (ii) generation of a high vacuum (10 –6 Тоrr) inside the quartz reactor to purify the alkali halide raw materials from oxygen-containing impurities; (iii) establishment of an argon atmosphere (1.1–1.3 bar) and the quartz ampoule shielding as a technological approach for suppressing the evaporation of aggressive halogen vapors. Flame photometry, absorption spectroscopy, and luminescence spectroscopy analyses demonstrate that the KCl crystal matrix was purified from oxygen-containing impurities (OH) down to 0.2 ppm, divalent impurities (Me 2+ ) down to 0.1 − 0.3 ppm, and alkali-metal homolog cations (Li + , Na + ) down to 1–3 ppm. Unique capabilities of the facility were further realized in the growth of KCl single crystals doped with hygroscopic lithium ions. Enhanced scintillation and dosimetric properties of KCl: Li crystals were demonstrated.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation and numerical modeling of the behavior of sandwich panels with grooved PVC foam cores and CFRP/GFRP facings
Article.Authors: Aribi C.; Houari A.; Djellab A.; Chellil A.; Lecheb S.; Safi B.; Nekkaa B.; Amroune S.; Hakizimana E.
Article.Abstract: This work presents a thorough experimental and numerical investigation into the mechanical behavior of sandwich panels subjected to three/four-point bending, as well as flatwise and edgewise compression. The studied structure is designed for aerospace and marine applications, aiming to optimize the trade-off between weight and stiffness. The core consists of a 10 mm thick, grooved, closed-cell Airex C70.55 PVC foam. The skins are formed by three-layer laminates combining carbon fiber (CFRP) and glass fiber (GFRP) fabrics of various areal weights. The panels were manufactured using the vacuum resin infusion process with an epoxy matrix. Experimental results reveal that failure initiation consistently manifests as localized compressive wrinkling of the upper skin, which subsequently progresses into direct crushing beneath the load application points. These tests highlight the critical influence of the facing material and the orientation of the grooved core face relative to the loading direction. The sandwich panel with carbon skins (BMS 9 − 8 3 K-70) outperforms all glass fiber configurations, while the “Up” orientation (grooved face positioned in the upper zone) yields the highest flexural strength. This configuration increases the failure load and the apparent ultimate core shear stress by 24% to 38%, an effect attributed to the resin ribs formed in the grooves during infusion, which raise the local indentation resistance of the loaded face by about one order of magnitude. The experimental flexural stiffness ( \(\:{D}_{exp}\) ) also exceeds the classical sandwich-theory prediction based on the facing modulus ( \(\:{E}_{f}\) ). In parallel, a 3D implicit numerical model was developed in Abaqus. The Hashin progressive damage criterion was implemented to predict composite skin failure, while a Cohesive Zone Model (CZM) based on COH3D8 elements was used to model skin–core interface behavior and delamination. The resin-filled grooves are represented explicitly and the core is described by a hyperfoam model calibrated on compression tests. For the reference configuration (BMS 9 − 8 3 K-70 facings, “Up” orientation, three-point bending), the predicted load–displacement curve agrees with experimental data within 3% for the peak load and 6% for the initial stiffness, with predicted damage localizing at the observed transverse compressive failure of the upper skin.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation of undrained and drained shear behavior of fat clay stabilized with industrial sewage sludge ash and reinforced with PVA fibers
Article.Authors: Jalali J.; Noorzad R.; Ta’negonbadi B.
Article.Abstract: The mechanical properties of industrial sewage sludge ash (ISSA) stabilized and PVA fiber-reinforced fat clay were studied with special reference to the trade-off between strength improvement and brittleness enhancement by stabilization. The experimental program included a complete set of Atterberg limits, standard Proctor compaction, unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial, consolidated-drained direct shear tests, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP) analysis. In the study, the effects of ISSA content (0–15%), PVA fiber dosage (0-0.5%), curing period (14–42 days), and moisture condition were examined. The results show that the ISSA stabilization significantly improved the shear strength of the fat clay and also significantly increased its brittleness. Under a confining pressure of 400 kPa, the maximum deviatoric stress increased from 553 kPa for untreated clay to 1602 kPa for soil stabilized with 5% ISSA. Increasing the ISSA content to 10% resulted in only limited additional improvement. The PVA fiber reinforcement improved the post-peak strength, the deformation capacity, and the resistance to shear localization. Within the investigated range, 5% ISSA, 0.3% PVA fibers, and 42 days of curing provided the most balanced performance. SEM observations showed particle aggregation, structural modification, and stronger interaction between fibers and matrix. TCLP results showed that heavy-metal concentrations were below regulatory limits for the tested conditions. The results suggest that ISSA stabilization with PVA fiber reinforcement is a promising method to improve high-plasticity clay and to reduce the brittleness caused by cementitious stabilization.

Article.Title: Thermal transport and crystallisation in octadecane composites with porous framework coatings and graphene
Article.Authors: Albalawi H.; Mukhtar A.; Jafarov S.; Sotvoldiav D.; Abdullayev A.; Abduvokhidov A.; Yadav B.
Article.Abstract: Low thermal conductivity and leakage limit the use of organic phase change materials for latent heat storage. Confinement can also delay crystallisation. Polyurea capsules containing n-octadecane were coated with either zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) or Universitetet i Oslo-66 (UiO-66) and embedded in a polyurethane matrix containing graphene nanoplatelets. Modulated differential scanning calorimetry characterised heat-flow components, while fast scanning calorimetry examined cooling-rate dependence. At a graphene loading of 5 wt%, the ZIF-8-coated composite had an effective thermal conductivity of 0.78 ± 0.04 W m −1 K −1 at 25 °C and an onset-based supercooling of 1.2 ± 0.2 °C. Corresponding values for the UiO-66-coated composite were 0.72 ± 0.03 W m −1 K −1 and 2.4 ± 0.3 °C. Control composites containing only the coating or only the graphene reached 0.31 ± 0.02 and 0.44 ± 0.03 W m −1 K −1 , so neither component accounts for the transport of the complete formulation. The ZIF-8-coated composite retained 98.2 ± 1.1% of its initial melting enthalpy after 1000 cycles between 10 and 60 °C, losing 0.34 ± 0.08% of its mass and showing unchanged infrared and diffraction signatures. Values are means and standard deviations across three independently prepared batches. The two coatings differ in thickness, crystallite size, surface area and growth conditions, so the measurements compare complete formulations rather than isolating a topology-dependent nucleation mechanism. Discharge power at device scale remains untested.

Article.Title: Embedded sensing telemetry and a validated explicit finite element digital twin of pressurised uPVC pipe under low velocity impact
Article.Authors: Ahmed H.; Kibria G.; Raphi S.; Benta Bashar J.; Afroz M.
Article.Abstract: Polymeric pipelines are increasingly used for pressurized fluid transport, yet their behavior under accidental low-velocity impact, and the means to monitor it in service, remain underdeveloped relative to metallic systems. This study recasts a combined experimental and numerical investigation of clamped unplasticized poly(vinyl chloride) (uPVC) pipe as the first building block of a physics-based digital twin for polymeric utility pipelines. A drop-weight rig was instrumented with a purpose-built ESP32-S2 sensing unit, using infrared timing gates and a pressure transducer, that streams real impact telemetry: the hammer velocity and the transient internal pressure pulse. Five water-pressurized specimens, spanning 689.48 to 2068.43 kPa, were struck at mid-span by a 4 kg hammer at 5.56 m/s, and a high-fidelity ABAQUS/Explicit counterpart was synchronized against the measured response. As internal pressure rose, the peak contact force increased from 3527 to 4174 N, the permanent deformation fell from 15.1 to 7.0 mm, and the pressure pulse grew while the contact period shortened, all consistent with pressure-induced wall stiffening. The contact-force response was linear up to about 1379 kPa before plateauing at the onset of the burst-pressure regime. Experimental and numerical plastic-zone areas agreed to within 16.9%, a conservative over-prediction the twin corrects during synchronization. On this validated basis, a conceptual digital-twin framework is proposed, enabling real-time damage identification and predictive, surrogate-driven structural health monitoring of polymeric pipelines.

Article.Title: A systematic review and meta analysis of early exercise based cardiac rehabilitation in patients hospitalized with acute heart failure
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Luo Z.; Yang M.; Huang W.; Wang Y.; Yu P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (ExCR) has been increasingly investigated in patients hospitalized with acute heart failure (AHF), but its effects on functional recovery and whether these effects vary across selected study-level characteristics remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of ExCR initiated during hospitalization on functional capacity in patients with AHF and to explore potential differences according to rehabilitation delivery model, World Bank country income classification, and study-level mean age. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI were searched from inception to May 2026. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if they enrolled adults hospitalized with AHF, initiated a structured ExCR program during hospitalization, compared ExCR with usual care or no structured exercise intervention, and reported 6-minute walk distance (6MWD). The primary outcome was 6MWD, secondary outcomes included health-related quality of life (HRQoL), clinical events and safety. Random-effects models were used, and subgroup analyses were considered exploratory. Twelve independent randomized controlled trials were included. Early ExCR significantly improved 6MWD compared with control group (mean difference [MD] 54.44 m, 95% CI 35.62 to 73.26; I² = 60%). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed no statistically significant differences according to rehabilitation delivery model, World Bank country income classification, or study-level mean age. ExCR also showed potential benefits for disease-specific HRQoL, whereas evidence for HF-related readmission and all-cause mortality remained inconclusive. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the primary 6MWD finding, although the certainty of evidence was rated as low because of risk of bias and inconsistency. Early ExCR initiated during hospitalization may improve functional capacity in patients with AHF. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not identify significant effect modification by rehabilitation delivery model, World Bank country income classification, or study-level mean age. However, the exact magnitude of benefit should be interpreted cautiously, and larger, methodologically rigorous trials are needed to clarify optimal delivery strategies and long-term clinical effects.

Article.Title: Estimating dispersal, survival and population size of wild Aedes aegypti in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania using self-mark-release-recapture method
Article.Authors: Tenywa F.; Makame H.; Moore J.; Dogan O.; Mapipi H.; Smith T.; Chitnis N.; Moore S.; Felber L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aedes -borne arboviral diseases represent a major global public health challenge, with vector control remaining the primary preventive strategy because there are no available antivirals or universal vaccines for most of these infections. This study quantified dispersal, survival time and population size of Aedes aegypti using a mosquito mark-release-recapture (MMRR) approach to generate ecological parameters required for implementing a release-based approaches for Ae. aegypti control. Wild Ae. aegypti pupae were placed beneath a marking unit covered with fluorescent dust-coated cloth-grids. Marked mosquitoes were recaptured within a 250 m radius using BG-sentinel traps, Prokopack aspirators, resting buckets and gravid traps. The overall mean distance travelled (MDT) was 94.5 m (95% CI 83.4–105.7) and the maximum distance travelled was 156 m. The average life expectancy (ALE) was 13.5 days (95% CI 12.2–14.8), with an average probability of daily survival (PDS) of 0.93 (95% CI 0.92–0.94). Survival analysis showed that approximately 80% of male and female Ae. aegypti survived up to 10 days. The estimated population size was 1195 mosquitoes/ha. These findings demonstrate that Ae. aegypti exhibit limited dispersal and survive beyond dengue virus’ average extrinsic incubation period (EIP) of 7–12 days, providing ecological conditions conducive to sustain arboviral transmission. The results also provide critical parameters for optimizing release-based control strategies.

Article.Title: Outcomes of surgically treated type a aortic dissection with malperfusion syndrome: an asian multi-institutional cohort study
Article.Authors: Cheng T.; Chen S.; Hsieh S.; Hsieh M.; Lin C.; Chen D.; Tung Y.; Hsiao F.; Chu P.; Cheng Y.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated mortality in surgically treated type A aortic dissection with malperfusion (mTAAD), identified malperfusion types associated with 30-day mortality, and assessed whether its prognostic impact persists beyond the early postoperative period. We analyzed 1021 patients with TAAD undergoing open surgery in Asia (2002–2018), including 209 with and 812 without preoperative malperfusion. Outcomes were 30-day mortality, overall mortality from surgery, and overall mortality from discharge, assessed using logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Malperfusion was associated with higher 30-day mortality (28.7% vs. 15.8%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.93; 95% CI 1.32–2.84) and overall mortality from surgery (34.4% vs. 24.0%; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.36; 95% CI 1.01–1.83), but not mortality from discharge (aHR, 0.84; 95% CI 0.40–1.77). Among single-organ malperfusion, cerebral malperfusion was associated with 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.25; 95% CI 1.08–4.70). Compared with no malperfusion, 30-day mortality was higher with single-organ involvement (aOR, 1.86; 95% CI 1.23–2.86), but not significantly with two organs (aOR, 1.66; 95% CI 0.76–3.66). In surgically treated mTAAD, the prognostic impact of malperfusion is concentrated in the early postoperative period. Cerebral malperfusion is associated with high 30-day mortality, supporting its emphasis in preoperative risk stratification.

Article.Title: Effects of an intensive firefighter training program on a simulated fire-escape staircase climb
Article.Authors: Sanchis C.; Martí-Martí J.; Miñana J.; Navarro-Martínez D.; Zahonero J.; Monleón C.
Article.Abstract: We examined changes in weighted stair-climb performance, its physiological and neuromuscular correlates, and attentional function in firefighters and firefighter candidates across a four-week intensive training program. Eighteen participants (17 men, 1 woman) completed baseline testing and 16 training sessions combining strength, power and endurance work; 17 completed post-intervention physical testing. Assessments included a loaded fire-escape staircase climb, an incremental VO₂max test, a 30-s Wingate test, a two-load squat test, anthropometry and the ANTI-Vea attentional task. Changes were estimated with linear mixed models and effect sizes were expressed as Cohen’s d . Stair-climb time was 1.26 s lower after training ( d = − 0.88). Post-intervention stair-climb time was best explained by a composite Strength Score (β std = − 0.65) and a Wingate Score (β std = − 0.37; R ² = 0.86). High-load squat velocity and power, estimated 1RM and Wingate mean power were higher after training (all d ≥ 0.67), whereas VO₂max, ventilatory thresholds and body mass were unchanged. ANT-I mean reaction time was lower ( d z = − 0.59); executive and arousal vigilance did not change. In this single-group design, changes were consistent with neuromuscular and anaerobic rather than aerobic adaptation, and suggest that preparation for this test should emphasize strength at task-relevant loads and anaerobic endurance.

Article.Title: Application of spectral preprocessing and machine learning models for discriminating nitrogen levels in cucumber production
Article.Authors: Sabzi S.; Azadbakht M.; Vahedi Torshizi M.; Pourdarbani R.
Article.Abstract: Nitrogen is one of the most essential macronutrients for plant growth, and its improper management can reduce fertilizer use efficiency while causing significant economic and environmental consequences. In this study, a hyperspectral imaging–based machine learning framework was developed and evaluated to classify different nitrogen fertilizer levels in cucumber leaves (cv. Super Arshiya-F1). Nitrogen treatments consisted of 30%, 60%, and 90% additional nitrogen applied to a nutrient solution with a base concentration of 2 g L⁻¹. Seventy-two hours after treatment application, a total of 300 leaves were collected from the treated plants, and hyperspectral images were acquired in the spectral range of 400–1100 nm, producing 327 spectral bands for each sample. To enhance signal quality and examine the influence of spectral preprocessing on class separability, three preprocessing techniques—Savitzky–Golay filtering, Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC), and Gaussian normalization—were applied exclusively to the training dataset and subsequently transferred to the independent test set. Three machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Decision Tree (DT), were evaluated using a 75/25 training–testing split along with five-fold cross-validation for model optimization. The results demonstrated that SVM consistently achieved the highest classification performance across all scenarios. The best results were obtained without preprocessing and with Gaussian normalization, both reaching an overall accuracy of 94%, an F1-score of approximately 0.94, and a ROC–AUC exceeding 0.98. In contrast, LDA showed moderate performance, while DT yielded the lowest classification accuracy. These findings highlight the strong potential of integrating hyperspectral imaging with SVM for accurate discrimination of nitrogen levels and for supporting efficient nutrient management in crop production systems.

Article.Title: Profilin-regulated actin polymerization dynamics at high monomer concentrations
Article.Authors: Heydenreich L.; Funk J.; Bieling P.; Kierfeld J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Actin polymerization in the cytoskeleton drives crucial dynamical biological processes such as cell motility and morphogenesis. Recent experiments 1 show that binding to profilin plays a crucial role in controlling the maximal polymerization speed of F-actin at cellular actin concentrations. These experiments are successfully described by a four reaction kinetic model, which predicts a Michaelis-Menten-like saturation of growth speed at high profilin-actin concentrations. In this work, we further analyze the four reaction model in terms of master equations and using the concept of two polymerization cycles, a pure actin cycle and a profilin-actin cycle and propose further experimental setups to gain access to all kinetic rates of the model. We find that varying the profilin excess leads to a profilin-dependent Michaelis constant for the growth speed. For polymerization against an external force, we identify a unique stall force as an indicator of energetically balanced profilin-driven polymerization, i.e., for the absence of coupling to other chemical processes providing energy input. Calculating length diffusivity (or Fano factor) we show that actin growth becomes much more precise by profilin-regulation and almost reaches precision bounds set by thermodynamic uncertainty relations.

Article.Title: Maternal autophagy contributes to grain yield in maize
Article.Authors: Tang J.; Wan X.; Myers A.; Avin-Wittenberg T.; Vollbrecht E.; Bassham D.
Article.Abstract: Maize ( Zea mays ) is an important crop species that is cultivated worldwide, and increasing maize yield is one of the major goals of plant breeding. The subcellular degradation and recycling pathway known as autophagy is involved in many plant developmental processes including vegetative growth, reproductive development, seed development, and senescence. Here, we demonstrate that maize autophagy-defective atg10 mutants have delayed flowering and reduced kernel size, weight and number, leading to reduced grain yield. Reciprocal crosses between mutant and parental lines indicate that, in contrast to the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana , the maternal maize plant genotype is the major contributor to the kernel phenotype in atg10 mutants, rather than the seed genotype.

Article.Title: Expression patterns of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p in a murine model of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Farzamfar P.; Salehi Z.; Mashayekhi F.; Khodayari S.
Article.Abstract: SLC38A4 (SNAT4), a system A amino acid transporter, contributes to nutrient uptake and metabolic regulation, but its role in the progression of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is unclear. We examined the expression of Slc38a4 and its predicted regulatory miRNA, mmu-miR-6948-3p , in primary tumors, invasive mammary tumors, and lung metastases in a murine TNBC model. RNA-sequencing data (GSE150928) from primary mammary tumors and lung metastases were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by functional enrichment, protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and miRNA–mRNA target prediction. Eighteen female BALB/c mice implanted with 4T1 TNBC cells were grouped into those with primary mammary tumors and those with lung metastases. Expression of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p was measured by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT–PCR). Public human datasets (TCGA, MET500, DepMap) were also examined. In the RNA-seq data, Slc38a4 was upregulated in lung metastases relative to primary tumors (logFC = 3.93) and was assigned to a PPI cluster enriched for amino acid transport and vesicle trafficking. qRT–PCR confirmed higher Slc38a4 expression in lung metastases (6.23 ± 0.48 vs. 1.00 ± 0.08, P < 0.0001) and lower expression in invasive mammary tumors (0.51 ± 0.05 vs. 1.00 ± 0.08, P < 0.0001) than in primary tumors. Levels of mmu-miR-6948-3p did not differ significantly between groups. In human data, SLC38A4 mRNA was lower in breast tumors than in normal breast tissue, and DNA methylation showed no clear relationship with its expression. Slc38a4 expression depends on tissue context during TNBC progression, being lower in invasive mammary tumors and higher in lung metastases, and this pattern is not explained by changes in mmu-miR-6948-3p. Functional studies are needed to determine whether the increase in the lung drives colonization or is an adaptive response to it.

Article.Title: Investigating the intergenerational stress buffering effects of ethnic-racial identity in disaster-exposed parents and their children
Article.Authors: Knowles E.; Danzi B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Disasters are a significant source of stress for parents, and people of color (POC) are disproportionately negatively impacted. Identifying protective factors is a necessary step toward promoting resilience and recovery in POC. Ethnic-racial identity (ERI) may protect against psychological stress for disaster-exposed POC. The purpose of this study was to identify how families of color (FOC) were affected by a disaster and evaluate ERI as a protective factor for POC and their children. It was hypothesized that FOC would report greater distress compared to White families and that ERI would mitigate distress in FOC. Parents ( N = 218) exposed to a hurricane reported on their family’s hurricane experiences, ERI, and parent and child psychological functioning. FOC parents reported greater hurricane-realted distress compared to White parents. ERI did not diminish the association between hurricane adversity and distress in parents. FOC children experienced greater distress compared to White counterparts. Child and parent distress were positively associated with one another. ERI was found to buffer the relationship between parent distress and child distress, such that these symptoms were mitigated. These findings highlight the impact of disaster exposure on FOC and describe how ERI may diminish negative outcomes for these families.

Article.Title: Parent-metabolite PBPK model of methotrexate to inform pediatric extrapolation, transporter-mediated drug–drug interactions, and renal impairment
Article.Authors: Dette C.; Marok F.; Alberg V.; Dings C.; Selzer D.; Schwab M.; Kotnik B.; Dolžan V.; Yildiz D.; Bittenbring J.; Remke M.; Lehr T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Methotrexate (MTX) is widely used in treating chronic inflammatory diseases and in chemotherapy for both adult and pediatric patients. Its pharmacokinetics are complex, as MTX is a substrate of multiple transporters. Particularly during high-dose chemotherapeutic use, it is associated with severe toxicities including reversible kidney impairment and hematological toxicity. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling offers a mechanistic approach to predict drug pharmacokinetics and guide dosing, especially in pediatric applications where clinical data is limited. A whole-body parent-metabolite PBPK model of MTX and 7-hydroxymethotrexate was developed in PK-Sim ® (version 12.1) for intravenous and oral administration in adults and children. Model development used 42 MTX and 16 metabolite plasma concentration-time profiles and showed strong predictive performance, with 53/58 area under the plasma concentration-time curve and 38/39 maximum plasma concentration values within a 2-fold range of observed data. Pediatric extrapolation incorporating transporter ontogeny yielded adequate predictions. Drug-drug interaction simulations for five perpetrator drugs met established acceptance criteria, and renal impairment simulations revealed markedly increased exposure in the high-dose setting. The model will be made publicly available to support dose optimization across clinical scenarios.

Article.Title: Effects of maximum teleportation distance on wayfinding in virtual reality: the role of optical flow cues
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Instantaneous teleportation reduces simulator sickness risk by omitting continuous viewpoint motion but may impair spatial orientation. Previous research has generally examined maximum teleportation distance and optical-flow transitions separately, leaving their combined effects during wayfinding unclear. We conducted a 2 (teleportation type: no optical flow vs. brief optical flow) × 3 (maximum teleportation distance: 5, 15, and 25 m) mixed-design experiment with 60 participants who completed route-exploration and unguided-return tasks in a virtual urban environment. Wayfinding performance and experience were assessed using sketch maps, navigation measures, the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. Sketch-map scores were lower at 25 m than at 5 and 15 m. Navigation time was longer at 5 m than at 25 m, and mean navigation time per teleportation increased across the 5-, 15-, and 25-m conditions. No significant between-type differences or type × distance interactions were detected for sketch-map or navigation measures. Simulator sickness scores were low across conditions. The aligned rank transform analysis indicated effects of teleportation type, distance, and their interaction that were not consistently reproduced by other approaches, leaving insufficient evidence for a stable simulator-sickness effect. Interview responses suggested that shorter-distance teleportation facilitated environmental observation, whereas longer-distance teleportation was perceived as easier to operate. The 25 m condition combined shorter navigation time with lower sketch-map scores. Distance conditions were paired with fixed scene variants, and the fixed 0.3 s transition coupled displacement with translation speed. The possible trade-off between traversal efficiency and environmental learning therefore remains specific to the tested configurations.

Article.Title: Hormonal dynamics in contrasting bearing habits of mango grafted on different rootstocks
Article.Authors: Vittal H.; Sharma N.; Sharma R.; Pandey R.; Singh N.; Ali A.; Singh N.; Kumar R.; Dubey A.; Mishra G.; Nirgude M.; Lata S.; Dilip S.; Gaikwad K.
Article.Abstract: Mango productivity is heavily dependent on the physiological transition from vegetative to reproductive growth, yet the integrated role of rootstock-mediated hormonal crosstalk in regulating these reproductive traits remains poorly understood. This study evaluated hormonal profiles and reproductive traits in regular-bearing ‘Amrapali’ and alternate-bearing ‘Dashehari’ grafted onto four rootstocks. Eight scion–rootstock combinations were evaluated with three biological replicates each. Leaf and bud concentrations of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), gibberellic acid (GA 3 ), zeatin and abscisic acid (ABA) were quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography, alongside assessments of flowering traits. Hormonal concentrations exhibited scion × rootstock × tissue interactions, with Kurukkan-associated bud IAA exceeding leaf concentrations in Amrapali (10.37 versus 4.92 ng g⁻ 1 ) and Dashehari (9.93 versus 1.40 ng g⁻ 1 ). Bud GA₃ also exceeded leaf concentrations under Kurukkan in both cultivars, whereas ABA showed contrasting tissue distributions. Amrapali/Olour produced the highest total flower number (1,077.33 per panicle), whereas Amrapali/PAM-2 exhibited the greatest hermaphrodite flower number (372.67 per panicle) and proportion (38.78%). Exploratory correlations associated bud zeatin with male flower number in Amrapali (r = 0.963, P = 0.037) and bud ABA with panicle length in Dashehari (r = 0.962, P = 0.038). These findings indicate rootstock-associated hormonal and reproductive variation without establishing causal relationships.

Article.Title: Quantum-resistant blockchain-assisted federated secure cancer diagnosis framework using hierarchical window pattern cognition network
Article.Authors: Asmeen S.; Chenam V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is still a major cause of cancer mortality in women, and the development of efficient, reliable and explainable diagnostic systems capable of inter-hospital data sharing while maintaining privacy of data is essential. This study proposes a Hierarchical Window Pattern Cognition Network for breast cancer diagnosis using the Breast Histopathology Images (IDC Regular Patches) dataset. The workflow starts with data collection, then the Patient-Level Data Partitioning process by applying patient identifiers to avoid training-testing overlap. The framework uses CLAHE and data augmentation, image normalization and image resizing to enhance the image consistency. The network learns hierarchical histological and cellular morphological patterns by the modules: Global Histological Representation, Cellular Morphology Learning, Adaptive Tissue Fusion and Diagnostic Probability Estimation. A federated learning framework with five clients uses Federated Averaging (FedAvg) to aggregate models and share model updates securely. The security layer uses an AES-256-GCM encryption algorithm, a SHA3-512 hashing algorithm, and a mechanism simulating those of CRYSTALS-Kyber and CRYSTALS-Dilithium for cryptographic security. Record-integrity verification is supported by a local hash-chain audit log, and predictions of the model are explained with visual and feature-level explanations by using GradCAM + + and SHAP. The proposed centralized model achieved an accuracy of 94.23%, precision of 94.00%, recall of 94.47%, F1-score of 94.24%, and ROC-AUC of 0.9651. These findings highlight the promise of combining the histopathology classification, privacy-preserving federated learning, cryptographic protection, tamper-evident audit logging and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified diagnostic framework.

Article.Title: Electroencephalographic patterns of equine sleep: comparative description and neurophysiological implications of recumbent and standing sleep
Article.Authors: Oliveira T.; Basile R.; Souza B.; Vicentini Y.; Barbosa A.; Baccarin R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to describe and compare the electroencephalographic patterns of sleep in horses during recumbent and standing positions, identifying the cortical dynamics and spectral characteristics associated with each stage. Eight clinically healthy adult horses were monitored through polysomnographic EEG recordings, using a double-banana montage with subcutaneous needle electrodes. Sleep stages were classified according to spectral and morphological criteria analogous to human scoring standards, with one sleep cycle analyzed per horse. REM sleep was posture-dependent, with complete paradoxical patterns observed only in recumbent horses. In standing animals, a REM-like state was identified, marked by rapid eye movements but cortical hypoactivation and absence of muscle atonia. Quantitative analysis revealed that N1 and N2 accounted for approximately 90% of total sleep duration, while N3 and REM represented smaller fractions. Standing horses exhibited longer light sleep stages and a smaller proportion of N3 sleep. These findings demonstrate that equine sleep architecture is highly posture-dependent, and behavioral postures such as sternal or lateral recumbency cannot be reliably used as proxies for specific EEG sleep stages. The study provides a methodological framework to support future investigations and facilitate comparisons of equine sleep physiology across studies and species.

Article.Title: A Bayesian Functional Kriging framework for spatial interpolation of PM2.5 concentration profiles
Article.Authors: Baseer A.; Khalefa M.; Ismael W.; Hussain I.; Basheer A.
Article.Abstract: Air pollution, especially fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), is a major global public health problem, causing breathing difficulties, lung disease, heart problems, and premature death. Predicting PM 2.5 concentrations at unobserved locations is essential in environmental science, especially with sparse observational data. This study introduces a new Bayesian Functional Kriging (BFK) model to predict PM 2.5 concentration profiles across Pakistan’s most populous province, using MERRA-2 reanalysis data at 17 city locations across Punjab. The BFK framework combines three methodologies: Functional Data Analysis (FDA), where continuous temporal curves model discrete PM 2.5 concentration profiles through B-spline smoothing; Functional Kriging (FK), in which functional data are used for spatial prediction of curve-valued observations; and Bayesian hierarchical modeling using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for parameter estimation. Prior empirical distributions are assumed for all parameters of interest: mean, partial sill, nugget effect, and spatial range, while posterior estimates are derived via a hybrid Gibbs-Metropolis algorithm within Gibbs sampling. Cross-validation results show that BFK is significantly better than the FK method, with RMSE and MAE differences of 30.9% (from 16.88 µg/m 3 to 11.66 µg/m 3 ) and 29.9% (from 13.03 µg/m 3 to 9.14 µg/m 3 ), respectively. In addition, we used the proposed model to estimate temporal variation in PM 2.5 concentration at five locations not sampled during data collection: Vehari, Sialkot, Attock, Khanewal, and Okara. We found that pollution is much higher in the southern areas than in the northern ones. These findings underscore BFK’s utility as a statistically principled and practically effective tool for air quality monitoring and environmental policy.

Article.Title: Predictors of prolonged hospitalization among children admitted with severe pneumonia in Southeast Ethiopia: a retrospective follow-up study
Article.Authors: Redwan M.; Belete B.; Abdeta G.; Gebremeskel T.; Demissie A.
Article.Abstract: Severe pneumonia remains a primary driver of pediatric morbidity in Sub-Saharan Africa. Prolonged hospital stay (PHS) escalates healthcare expenditure and strains referral hospital resources. This study aimed to evaluate the proportion, clinical determinants, and overall performance of factors associated with PHS among hospitalized pediatric severe pneumonia cases in Southeast Ethiopia. A hospital-based retrospective follow-up study was conducted at Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital, analyzing 395 systematically sampled pediatric cases (aged 3 months to 14 years) admitted with severe pneumonia. Multivariable logistic regression was executed with model diagnostics, including Variance Inflation Factors (VIF), Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The proportion of prolonged hospital stay (> 7 days) was 42.0% (95% CI 37.2–46.8). In the multivariable model, independent factors associated included presence of comorbidities (Adjusted OR [aOR] = 4.02; 95% CI 2.42–6.67; p < 0.001), care-seeking delay > 48 h (aOR = 3.89; 95% CI 2.35–6.42; p < 0.001), history of previous pneumonia (aOR = 3.23; 95% CI 1.81–5.74; p < 0.001), partial vaccination status (aOR = 3.03; 95% CI 1.73–5.32; p < 0.001), and underlying malnutrition (aOR = 2.44; 95% CI 1.15–5.18; p = 0.021). The multivariable explanatory model demonstrated good discriminative performance (AUC = 0.804, 95% CI 0.759–0.848) and good model calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.612). Over four in ten pediatric severe pneumonia admissions experience prolonged hospitalization. Prompt care-seeking behavior, complete routine immunization, and nutritional interventions may reduce prolonged hospitalization and should be prioritized in similar referral settings.

Article.Title: Hidden baseline heterogeneity can mask treatment effects in randomized xenograft studies
Article.Authors: Gül N.; Hekim N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Randomization and standardized analytical workflows are central to preclinical oncology, yet they do not necessarily ensure biological comparability at baseline. Using a real-world xenograft efficacy dataset generated under standard CRO conditions, we show that biologically meaningful treatment effects can remain statistically undetected when baseline heterogeneity is not explicitly considered. Although treatment groups appeared balanced at study entry by conventional summaries, baseline tumour volume exhibited latent structure within the cohort. Pooled group-level analyses reported no significant treatment effect, whereas baseline-aware evaluation of tumour growth trajectories revealed a responder subpopulation whose signal was masked by aggregation. This discrepancy did not arise from deficiencies in experimental conduct or data quality, but from limitations of pooled inference in the presence of structured baseline variability. Extending this framework to publicly available xenograft datasets, we observed that baseline tumour volume heterogeneity is common under routine preclinical workflows and can similarly alter efficacy interpretation. Together, these findings indicate that baseline tumour burden represents a biologically consequential source of hidden heterogeneity and that baseline-aware analytical strategies can improve the sensitivity and interpretability of preclinical efficacy assessment without deviation from standard experimental practice.

Article.Title: Virus induced cochlear inflammation alters stria vascularis function and auditory development
Article.Authors: Smith M.; Hirose K.; Britt W.
Article.Abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is the most common viral infection acquired in utero and a leading cause of sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL). In previous studies utilizing a murine model of SNHL that follows congenital CMV infection (cCMV), virus-induced cochlear inflammation has been shown to result in SNHL that develops in the absence of histopathology in the sensory neuroepithelium but is associated with the dysregulation of a number of deafness related genes (DRG). In this study, virus-induced cochlear inflammation was shown to dysregulate the expression of multiple DRG that have been shown to contribute to ion and metabolite transport within stria vacularis (SV). In addition, cochlear inflammation in virus-infected mice resulted in the loss of barrier functions of the SV that have also been linked to SNHL. Decreased expression of these DRG in infected animals was associated with SNHL that was similar to that observed in genetically engineered murine models with deletion of these DRG. Together, these results argue that virus-induced inflammation can lead to dysregulation of host genes associated with barrier and ion transport function of the SV, thus providing further insight into potential mechanisms of SNHL that follow virus infections during early auditory development.

Article.Title: Spatial distribution patterns and quantitative analysis of traditional villages in the Qiantang River Basin using geographic detectors
Article.Authors: He Y.; Ding C.; Bai C.; Yan D.; Hu M.
Article.Abstract: The distribution pattern and agglomeration characteristics of traditional villages play a crucial role as historical and cultural assets in rural development, emphasizing the significance of regional cultural preservation and rural revitalization. This study examines 362 national traditional villages in the Qiantang River Basin (QRB) in Zhejiang to uncover their spatial settlement patterns and analyze the influencing factors. Employing spatial analysis methods such as the nearest neighbor index, geographical concentration index, and kernel density estimation, the study elucidates the spatial distribution of these villages. Utilizing the geographical detector model, it identifies key factors associated with their spatial distribution, quantitatively assessing their explanatory power and interaction patterns among natural, economic, and cultural dimensions. The study also suggests strategies for the protection and sustainable use of traditional villages in the QRB. The research findings reveal that traditional villages in the QRB exhibit a clustered distribution pattern, characterized by a spatial structure of “two cores and multiple clusters”. This agglomeration tendency is observed at the county level, with a distinct pattern of concentration in the southwestern mountainous regions and sparsity in the northeastern plains. Various factors such as slope, altitude, per capita disposable income, road network density, and the proportion of the primary industry play significant roles in shaping the spatial distribution of these traditional villages. A multifactor detection model demonstrates that the distribution pattern of traditional villages in the QRB is a result of the dynamic interplay between natural features and human influences. The impact of each factor varies across different stages, highlighting the complex nature of village distribution. This quantitative analysis assesses the varying degrees of influence exerted by the natural environment, socioeconomic conditions, and historical heritage on the distribution of traditional villages, addressing limitations of previous qualitative studies. This study not only enhances our understanding of the factors driving the distribution of traditional villages but also provides a scientific foundation for the strategic conservation of these villages in the QRB and the management of cultural heritage on a basin-wide scale.

Article.Title: Impaired spatial memory destabilization and updating in middle-aged male mice is reversed by muscarinic receptor stimulation
Article.Authors: Huff A.; Jardine K.; Kot O.; Kalisch B.; Winters B.
Article.Abstract: Reminder cues associated with earlier learning can destabilize memories, rendering them modifiable. Memory updating deficits may occur during aging, but these have not been thoroughly explored. Cholinergic dysfunction during aging could potentially contribute to these memory updating deficits, as among its many functions, acetylcholine is critical for memory destabilization. We hypothesized that mice would display memory destabilization and updating deficits with increasing age, and that pro-cholinergic manipulations could alleviate these deficits. In the current study, we show that in young (3-months), but not middle-aged (10–15-months), male C57 mice, object location memories readily destabilize. These middle-aged mice had a significant downregulation in expression of hippocampal vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT). Critically, mice at both ages could acquire and retain basic object-location memories. Moreover, pre-reactivation administration of an M1 muscarinic cholinergic receptor agonist appeared to promote memory destabilization in middle-aged mice, enabling memory updating. Finally, a brief period of enrichment yielded behavioural effects consistent with enhanced memory updating, and these were associated with elevated expression of hippocampal VAChT. This research expands our understanding of the critical involvement of cholinergic system changes in age-related cognitive deficits, highlighting an underappreciated role for cholinergic transmission in memory updating functions distinct from merely learning and remembering.

Article.Title: Crowding-induced phase transition in Oedaleus asiaticus as a developmental stage-gated, irreversible multi-gene switch
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Guo N.; Rostami E.; Gao H.; Liu M.; Li L.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: Solitary-phase Oedaleus asiaticus (Bei-Bienko) can switch to the far more destructive gregarious phase as population density rises, posing a serious threat to agriculture, animal husbandry and local economies. The current investigation assessed how developmental stages and population density impacted phase transitions and which genes served as key regulatory elements of this process. The results showed that the younger nymphs were, the higher proportion that shifted from solitary to gregarious phase, whereas adults never switched; a density of 60 insects produced the highest transition rate, whereas lower or higher densities resulted in fewer gregarious individuals. The gregarious locusts maintained their original physical characteristics when they were grown in solitary conditions. Transcriptome analysis showed that gregarious individuals exhibited strong gene expression increases which included the juvenile-hormone acid methyl-transferase gene ( JHAMT ) and the phenylalanine hydroxylase gene ( Hn ) and the DOPA decarboxylase gene ( DDC ) and a chemosensory protein gene ( CSP ). RNAi silencing of JHAMT , Hn , DDC or CSP resulted in a major decrease of phase transition occurrence while JHAMT , Hn and DDC knock-down caused partial albinism. The research demonstrates that population density functions as the key trigger for phase transition while gene interactions with their respective metabolites undergo central regulatory functions. Nonetheless, since the locusts used in this study were field-collected and reared for less than two generations, the results should be interpreted within the context of environmentally induced plasticity rather than genetically fixed phase differences.

Article.Title: Self supervised multi scale learning for WiFi CSI contactless human activity recognition with potential applications in health monitoring
Article.Authors: Xu H.; Yao D.; Liu W.; Li L.; Ma L.; Jiang C.
Article.Abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) provides a privacy-preserving and contactless sensing modality for human activity recognition, but practical CSI recognition remains challenged by limited labeled data, heterogeneous motion dynamics, and signal perturbations. This study proposes CSI-MSRNet, a self supervised representation-learning framework that combines CSI-aware contrastive augmentation with a lightweight temporal and subcarrier multi scale encoder. The encoder models motion evolution at multiple temporal receptive fields and complementary frequency-selective responses across OFDM subcarriers, while Efficient Multi-Scale Attention is used only as a lightweight feature-refinement component rather than as the primary methodological novelty. Self supervised pretraining is restricted to the training partition, after which the encoder is fine tuned with different proportions of labeled samples. Experiments were conducted on the public UT-HAR and NTU-Fi HAR benchmarks using the SenseFi data partitions. Main recognition and low-label experiments were repeated five times with random seeds 42–46, and low-label subsets were independently sampled by stratified class sampling in each run. CSI-MSRNet achieved 98.76 ± 0.18% accuracy on UT-HAR and 99.85 ± 0.21% on NTU-Fi HAR. With only 1% labeled data, the corresponding accuracies were 73.6 ± 2.4% and 77.8 ± 2.8%, respectively. Controlled synthetic tests further indicated improved tolerance to amplitude noise and random subcarrier loss. These results should be interpreted as benchmark-level behavioral recognition rather than evidence of subject-independent generalization, clinical monitoring effectiveness, or embedded-device deployment. The framework therefore provides a computationally lightweight approach with potential applications in smart-home and health-related behavioral sensing.

Article.Title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal a senescence-associated lipid-metabolic macrophage phenotype driving immunosuppression and poor prognosis in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Zhao B.; Liao Y.; Ye S.; Jiang N.; Lu W.; Chen Y.; Chen W.; Huang Y.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their functional heterogeneity remains poorly understood, especially regarding the interplay between cellular senescence and lipid metabolism. Using eight machine learning algorithms, a prognostic model based on SALM signatures was developed and internally evaluated via nested cross-validation in a combined TCGA–GSE39582 cohort. Spatial multiplex immunofluorescence and qPCR were employed for experimental validation. SALM macrophages exhibit elevated IL-10/STAT3 signaling, terminal differentiation, and a core gene module enriched in senescence and lipid metabolism pathways. They interact strongly with T cells via immunosuppressive ligands IL-10 and MIF. Spatial analysis confirmed p16 + CD68 + IL-10 + cell enrichment at the tumor front. The SALM-based prognostic model achieved high accuracy (AUC = 0.972), and a corresponding nomogram showed potential for personalized prognosis prediction. SALM macrophages drive immunosuppression in CRC through a senescence-lipid metabolism axis, serving as a novel prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Design and characterization of beta-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 to enhance luteolin solubility and anticancer efficacy: bioinformatic and biologic assessment
Article.Authors: Kharazmi F.; Homayouni Tabrizi M.; Jafarinia M.

This study developed a luteolin-loaded β-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8) nanocarrier intended to improve drug retention, pH-responsive release, and anticancer activity against colorectal cancer cells. ZIF-8 nanoparticles were synthesized by room-temperature precipitation, coated sequentially with β-cyclodextrin and chitosan, crosslinked using sodium tripolyphosphate, and loaded with luteolin by post-synthetic incubation. FTIR, dynamic light scattering, zeta-potential analysis, pH-dependent surface-charge measurements, and FESEM characterized the formulation. Encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were quantified spectrophotometrically; release was assessed by dialysis at pH 7.4, 6.5, and 5.5. HCT116 colorectal carcinoma and normal human dermal fibroblasts underwent MTT testing. Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, AO/EB microscopy, SOD activity, FRAP, and qRT-PCR for CASP3, SOD1, and IL6 evaluated cell-death and stress responses. The particles showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 228.95 ± 2.7 nm, a PDI of 0.139 ± 0.04, and a zeta potential of − 27.24 ± 0.32 mV, indicating a uniform nanoscale dispersion. Synthesis yield was 78.5 ± 3.2%. Measured luteolin retention increased with feed concentration, reaching 83.5 ± 1.44% encapsulation efficiency and 16.1 ± 1.53% loading capacity. Release was slower under physiological conditions and accelerated in acidic media, supporting pH-responsive behavior; model fitting was descriptive, with Higuchi favored at pH 7.4, Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 6.5, and the lowest AIC assigned to Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 5.5. In HCT116, free luteolin produced an IC 50 of 166.5 ± 12.3 µg/mL, whereas Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8 reduced the IC 50 to 45.96 ± 2.3 µg/mL (approximately 3.6-fold greater potency; p < 0.001). The formulation IC 50 in HDF cells was 128.7 ± 8.4 µg/mL, yielding an HCT116/HDF selectivity index of 2.8. At 66 µg/mL, total apoptosis reached 48.9 ± 2.9%, compared with 1.3 ± 0.3% in controls. FRAP antioxidant capacity decreased to 0.578 ± 0.015 versus 0.801 ± 0.022 in controls. CASP3 and SOD1 transcripts increased 4.98-fold and 4.10-fold, respectively, while IL6 peaked at 10.92-fold at the intermediate dose. The dual-coated nanocarrier enhanced luteolin potency and apoptosis-associated responses in HCT116, with selectivity relative to HDF cells. Docking and characterization findings are supportive, not proof of KRAS inhibition, tumor targeting, or in vivo efficacy; validation remains necessary.

Article.Title: Physical literacy and health-related quality of life: the serial mediating role of resilience and positive mental health
Article.Authors: Mumu S.; Reena I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical literacy (PL) is recognized as a multidimensional construct that supports physical activity and health. Beyond physical competence, PL includes motivation, confidence, knowledge, and understanding. However, the role of positive psychological resources in explaining the relationship between physical literacy and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among university students has received limited empirical attention. This study examined whether resilience and positive mental health (PMH) mediate the relationship between PL and physical and mental components of HRQoL. In this cross-sectional study,159 undergraduate and graduate students from a single university in Louisiana, US completed the perceived physical literacy instrument, adult resilience measure-revised, positive mental health scale, and short form 12 health survey online. PROCESS Model 6 was utilized to analyze the mediation model. Age and sex were added as covariates. PL is positively associated with resilience, PMH, and both physical and mental HRQoL. PMH significantly mediated the relationship between PL and mental HRQoL, and a significant serial indirect association through resilience and PMH was identified (B = 0.227, 95% bootstrap CI [0.109, 0.403]). In contrast, no significant indirect effects were observed for physical HRQoL. The final model explained 35.1% of the variance in mental HRQoL. These findings suggest that physical literacy is associated with mental HRQoL through a psychosocial pathway in which resilience supports positive mental health. Findings from this study can be utilized to inform policy that seeks to identify modifiable psychological and behavioral determinants of HRQoL and meaningfully enhance the university health promotion program to support health outcomes of students in higher education.

Article.Title: Experimental and finite element analysis of coupled electro-thermal responses of concrete-encased grounding electrodes under lightning impulses
Article.Authors: Sarker M.; Zubair H.; Algarni S.; Alqahtani T.; Khan A.
Article.Abstract: Grounding systems are critical for maintaining the safety and transient stability of high-voltage and smart-grid infrastructure subjected to lightning-current impulses. This study presents an integrated experimental and three-dimensional finite element method (FEM) investigation of conventional copper-bonded steel rod and concrete-encased grounding electrodes under standardized 8/20 µs impulse-current conditions. Laboratory experiments were conducted using an impulse-current generator with a maximum current capability of 1.5 kA, while a COMSOL Multiphysics model was developed and validated against the experimentally accessible current range and subsequently used to investigate higher-current conditions numerically. Three representative soil types of clay, sandy loam, and gravel were considered to evaluate transient impedance, ground potential rise (GPR), current-density distribution, soil-ionization behavior, and electro-thermal response. Experimentally, the concrete-encased configuration reduced impulse impedance by approximately 33–49% across the investigated soils. FEM analysis showed a reduction in peak current density from 69 to 43 A/m², corresponding to approximately 38%, together with a larger effective current-conduction region. Numerical predictions at higher current levels indicated delayed soil-ionization onset and lower temperature rise for the encased configuration compared with the conventional rod. These high-current results are identified as FEM predictions rather than direct experimental measurements because they exceed the 1.5 kA capability of the laboratory generator. The validated experimental numerical framework demonstrates the potential of conductive concrete encasement to improve impulse-current dispersion and reduce localized electrical and thermal stress in grounding electrodes. Further high-current experimental validation is required to confirm the predicted behavior beyond the laboratory test range.

Article.Title: Urinary metal exposure and type 2 diabetes mellitus: the potential mediating role of biological aging in older adults
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Chen F.; Ren H.; Zhang X.; Zhuo L.; Guo X.; Cui C.; Zhang P.; Zhang Y.; Zhang Y.; Ding L.; Lei L.
Article.Abstract: The global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasing, and environmental exposures may contribute to diabetes susceptibility. Metals are widespread environmental contaminants associated with metabolic disorders; however, the role of aging-related processes in this association remains unclear. A total of 843 participants were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of six metals (Pb, Zn, Mn, Cr, As, and Co) were measured, and phenotypic age was calculated based on nine biomarkers. Additionally, Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr were positively associated with phenotypic age, and each one-year increase in phenotypic age was associated with higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.391, 95% CI: 1.319–1.466). Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that phenotypic age may partially account for the associations between metal exposure and T2DM, with estimated mediation proportions of 10.9%–22.2%. Article.Title: Relationships between reproductive steroids, glandular microbiota, and volatile chemical signals in naturally cycling versus hormonally contracepted female lemurs
Article.Authors: Grebe N.; Boulet M.; Bornbusch S.; Greenwald L.; Dimac-Stohl K.; Grady J.; Drea C.
Article.Abstract: Olfactory communication directs socio-reproductive interaction in animals, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. These results highlight the importance of cyclical endocrine variation in female reproductive signaling and the overriding effects on VOC manufacture of a disturbed glandular microbiome during contraception.

Article.Authors: Jiang X.; Tsubata H.; Shimizu S.; Nozaki T.
Article.Abstract: Electrohydrodynamic (EHD) propulsion has garnered significant interest as a lightweight and silent thrust generation technology, owing to its lack of moving parts and low vibration characteristics. These results indicate an engineering trade-off between maximizing absolute thrust and maintaining thrust to power ratio of the configuration. Overall, the incorporation of sub unit structures is crucial in enhancing thrust output. The proposed design strategy provides a promising pathway for improving thrust performance in EHD propulsion systems and provides valuable insights for the development of higher thrust output EHD thrusters.

Erosive disease, combined therapy, and tsDMARD exposure emerged as associated factors across definitions, emphasizing early disease control and comprehensive management.

Healthcare managers scored significantly higher than physicians (median 0.60 vs. 0.50; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.045, post-hoc p = 0.0304), a difference consistent with a champion–skeptic dynamic and, alternatively, with role-specific referents for administrative efficiency. Article.Title: Evaluating the decomposition of agricultural legume species to estimate nutrient recycling in Mediterranean climates
Article.Authors: De Prato L.; Harrison R.; Scanlan C.; Howieson J.; Steel E.; Yates R.
Article.Abstract: Legumes enhance the sustainability of Mediterranean farming systems by increasing soil nutrient levels, improving soil water and carbon retention, and reducing reliance on synthetic fertilisers through biological nitrogen fixation. However, the environmental and biological complexity of residue decomposition necessitates a clear understanding of how different crop residues decompose in synchrony with the nutrient requirements of subsequent cereal or oilseed crops. To address this, litterbag experiments were conducted at two distinct agroecological zones within the Western Australian Wheatbelt (Kendenup: 730 mm rainfall, Brown Gravelly Chromosol; Konnongorring: 350 mm rainfall, Grey Chromosol sandy duplex). Decomposition rates were significantly higher at the high-rainfall Kendenup site, with all species showing 70–85% biomass loss by 60 weeks compared to 50–75% at Konnongorring, reflecting moisture as the primary driver of decomposition. Across both sites, T. aestivum exhibited the slowest decomposition and highest N immobilisation (final C:N ~ 35), followed by grain legumes L. angustifolius and V. faba (final C:N 30–40). Vetch species ( V. sativa, V. villosa ) and T. spumosum decomposed most rapidly, achieving final C:N ratios of 11–19. Novel ley legumes O. sativus and Trig. balansae displayed intermediate decomposition rates and achieved a C:N ratio of 25–35, potentially optimising N release synchrony with subsequent crop demand. These findings provide the first comparative assessment of second-generation ley legumes ( O. sativus , Trig. balansae ) alongside traditional pasture and grain legumes under field conditions in Mediterranean environments. Results demonstrate that novel pasture legumes provided sustained N release, potentially optimising nutrient synchrony with subsequent cereal crops better than either fast-decomposing traditional pastures or low N fixer grain legume residues. This species-specific decomposition information addresses a critical knowledge gap in managing N cycling in evolving Australian farming systems, where increases in N harvest index and changes to ley systems have altered N dynamics. This study demonstrates that, while edaphoclimatic conditions were strongly associated with residue decomposition in the Mediterranean environments of Western Australia, species selection substantially influenced the timing of N release. Novel ley legumes offer intermediate decomposition patterns that may better balance availability and consistency of N release compared to traditional legume options, with potential implications for managing nutrient synchrony, cereal biomass, and grain quality (protein and grain size) in evolving rotational systems.

These findings identify scopoletin and linoleic acid as predicted dual-target AChE/BACE1 candidates from W. somnifera , offering a computational foundation for their experimental validation as multitarget neuroprotective candidates against Alzheimer's disease.

Article.Title: Dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network for spatiotemporal correlation modeling of mine microseismic events and intelligent rockburst risk level reasoning
Article.Authors: An J.; Zhou J.; Li H.; Wang X.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: Deep mining releases accumulated strain energy violently, and microseismic arrays record the fracturing that precedes rockbursts. Graph neural networks have already been applied to seismic and microseismic tasks such as phase association, source characterisation and event forecasting; what those graphs share is a topology anchored to a fixed sensor array and a single edge semantics, so they cannot follow an event field that turns over as the working face advances. This paper proposes a dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network (DHGAT). Every event enters as a node that retains four feature channels — waveform, source parameter, spatial and temporal — and three edge types (spatial proximity, temporal sequence, feature similarity) are rebuilt inside a 48 h sliding window. Relation-specific multi-head attention aggregates neighbours separately for each edge type, a semantic-level layer learns how much each relation contributes, and a gated recurrent encoder tracks the evolving graph embedding before four risk grades are assigned: no risk, low, moderate and high. On a 24-month catalogue of 7956 events from one deep metal mine, DHGAT reached 91.9 ± 0.4% accuracy, 0.853 ± 0.008 macro-F1 and 0.887 ± 0.006 quadratic weighted Kappa over ten runs, ahead of the strongest static heterogeneous baseline (HAN, 89.2% and 0.788) and of every other baseline at p < 0.01; recall on high-risk events reached 80.0%. Relation weights migrate from spatially dominated during gradual stress build-up to temporally dominated in the final hours before failure, which mirrors the shift from distributed microcracking to localised coalescence, and a perturbation test confirms that the attention carries the discriminative signal. Inference costs 46 ms per window on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. All data come from one mine, so the reported thresholds require recalibration before transfer.

Article.Title: Network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of dioctyl terephthalate in systemic lupus erythematosus pathogenesis
Article.Authors: Fang T.; Long S.; Wang T.; Chen T.; Yang H.; Zhong F.
Article.Abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP) may serve as an environmental risk factor for multiple diseases. Here, we explore potential molecular associations between DOTP exposure and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and identify candidate targets and pathways that may underlie these associations. Integrated network toxicology and transcriptomics identified SLE-associated targets. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses revealed underlying mechanisms. Machine learning was used to prioritize candidate DOTP–SLE targets. CIBERSORT assessed target-immune cell infiltration relationships. Molecular docking evaluated DOTP-target binding affinities. We identified 39 DOTP-associated SLE targets. Enrichment analyses linked them to inflammatory cytokine production and immune activation. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) and machine learning prioritized six key targets (NFKB1, TLR4, CASP9, CDK5, DNMT1, PRKCD). Exploratory CIBERSORT analysis described associations with LM22-derived reference profiles, while ROC analysis characterized within-cohort discrimination and an exploratory nomogram summarized the combined candidate-gene pattern. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between DOTP and these key targets. Our research results suggest a potential link between DOTP exposure and SLE progression through specific genes and pathways, and molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between DOTP and the relevant SLE targets. The ROC and nomogram analyses provided supplementary within-cohort characterization of the prioritized candidate genes. This study provides mechanistic insights into DOTP-associated SLE and supports the development of targeted prevention strategies.

Article.Title: ChGBO_QRNN: chronological gooseneck barnacle-based quantum recurrent neural networks for intrusion detection in IoT-SDN
Article.Authors: Jyothi B.; Thaiyalnayaki S.
Article.Abstract: There has been significant growth in the number of heterogeneous components configured within the Internet of Things (IoT) to allow effective data communication. However, IoT components are resource-constrained, and there are no standardized security procedures for communication within IoT platforms. While various solutions have been developed to secure communication in the IoT ecosystem, the existing approaches are not always reliable enough to address cyber threats and unwanted intrusions originating from IoT endpoints. Thus, this research presents a Chronological Gooseneck Barnacle Optimization-based Quantum Recurrent Neural Network (ChGBO_QRNN) for intrusion detection in SDN-IoT. Here, the proposed system contains three phases, which include a sniffer, a detector, and a sensor phase. In the sniffer phase, the features are extracted from the packets, and the extracted features are utilized for intrusion detection. In the detector phase, intrusion detection is carried out by the Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks (QRNN), and ChGBO is employed for training. In the sensing phase, the boundary of the attack is checked. If any concept drift is detected, the identification of a new attack is done using the proposed ChGBO_QRNN. Furthermore, the ChGBO_QRNN has gained weighted Accuracy, weighted True Positive Rate (TPR), weighted True Negative Rate (TNR), weighted F1-score, and weighted precision as 91.868%, 90.134%, 92.894%, 92.072%, and 92.978%.

Article.Title: Redox driven inflammatory and senescence-associated changes in Channa striata exposed to insecticide Fipronil with ascorbic acid-mediated modulation
Article.Authors: Yadav S.; Dubey A.; Jain A.; Singh S.; Dwivedi S.; Dwivedi S.; Tiwari V.; Srivastava R.; Dubey I.; Kumar M.
Article.Abstract: Fipronil (FIP), a widely used second-generation phenylpyrazole insecticide, is known for its broad-spectrum and systemic activity. The present study evaluated the toxic effects of commercial FIP (80% WG) on the striped snakehead fish, Channa striata , following 15, 30, and 45 days of exposure, and assessed the protective role of ascorbic acid (AA). Fish were divided into six groups: control, AA control (50 mg L⁻ 1 ), 0.002 mg L⁻ 1 FIP, 0.002 mg L⁻ 1 FIP + AA, 0.004 mg L⁻ 1 FIP, and 0.004 mg L⁻ 1 FIP + AA. FIP exposure significantly ( p < 0.05 ) increased erythrocytic ROS levels and protein carbonyl content, while GST activity declined markedly. SOD and CAT activities exhibited biphasic responses during the exposure period. Significant ( p < 0.05 ) alterations were observed in senescence-associated gene expression profiles. Correlation and Principal Component Analysis revealed associations among oxidative stress markers, DNA damage response genes, inflammatory signaling, antioxidant defense, and senescence-associated gene expression. Co-exposure with AA partially alleviated oxidative stress and moderated gene expression changes, indicating its protective potential against FIP-induced toxicity.

Article.Title: Experimental study on corrosion mitigation and shear behavior of novel repairable rock bolts
Article.Authors: Hu W.; Qian S.; Lin Z.; Cai Z.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Based on the concept of repairable anchorage for post-damage performance recovery and corrosion protection in jointed rock masses, this study develops novel repairable structures in the form of rock bolts: the extrusion-crushing repairable (ECR) bolt and the hot-melt repairable (HMR) bolt. Chloride wet–dry cycling tests and double-shear tests were conducted on separate groups of double-jointed rock mass specimens to investigate their anticorrosion effectiveness and restoration capability. Preliminary results indicate that both repairable bolts can release repair materials after damage to partially restore sealing conditions, suppress corrosive ingress, and enhance shear resistance. Specifically, the ECR bolt demonstrated the potential for superior corrosion resistance, achieving higher peak shear load and greater external work to peak load under the tested conditions. This improvement may be associated with the infiltration and adhesion of the released polyurethane–ethyl acetate repair agent, which helps seal damaged regions and restore grout integrity over a wider area. In contrast, the HMR bolt provides localized sealing and partial reinforcement through thermally activated melting of EVA adhesive, leading to comparatively moderate enhancements in corrosion resistance and shear capacity. Observations of the failure characteristics further elucidated the reparative mechanisms and the differences in mechanical responses among the bolt systems. This work suggests that integrating repair functionality into rock bolting systems may provide a promising approach for mitigating damage and corrosion in rock engineering.
