Article.Title: Clinical and serological differences associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Sjögren’s disease: a real-world multicenter analysis
Article.Authors: Cafaro G.; Lepri G.; Colafrancesco S.; Dei B.; Peruzzi A.; Guiducci S.; Priori R.; Baldini C.; Quartuccio L.; Cipriani P.; Alunno A.; Berardicurti O.; Valentini I.; Gerli R.; Bartoloni E.; N/A N/A.; Baldini C.; Berardicurti O.; Cipriani P.; Priori R.; Quartuccio L.; Alunno A.; Atzeni F.; Bardelli M.; Colafrancesco S.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) is a common metabolic comorbidity in patients with Sjögren’s disease (SjD), but their clinical and serologic profile remain incompletely characterized. We retrospectively compared SjD patients with and without DM and explored factors associated with a history of cardiovascular (CV) events. Patients with DM were compared with individually age- and sex-matched non-diabetic comparators. Group comparisons used appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests. Associations with DM were examined using logistic regression adjusted for age and disease duration and, in sensitivity analyses accounting for the matched design, conditional logistic regression stratified by reconstructed matched sets. A clinically prespecified Firth logistic model fitted to the original observed data evaluated factors associated with a history of CV events. Among 245 patients (95% female; mean age 70 ± 12 years), 100 had DM. Compared with non-diabetic patients, those with DM had higher BMI and more hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia. Disease activity was similar but ESSDAI was available for only 54% of patients. After adjustment for age and disease duration, DM was associated with lower odds of anti-SSB/La positivity (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.25–0.88) and low C3 (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.10–0.76); estimates were similar in conditional analyses accounting for matched sets (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.25–0.91, and OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.09–0.80, respectively). Thirty-one patients had a history of CV events. In the primary Firth model (n = 239), age (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02–1.12; p = 0.005) and hypertension (OR 3.21, 95% CI 1.27–9.54; p = 0.012) were associated with CV history. Anti-SSB/La, smoking and current HCQ use were not significantly associated with CV history. Multiple-imputation results were consistent. Adjusted metformin analyses showed no statistically significant associations. Type 2 DM was associated with a clinical and serologic profile characterized by greater metabolic burden and lower prevalence of serological markers associated with B-cell activity. In the exploratory CV analysis, age and hypertension were associated with a history of CV events. These observational findings, in particular the serological associations, were identified at nominal significance without correction for multiple testing and require independent and prospective validation.

Article.Title: Comparing self-regulation, anxiety, and willingness to communicate across blended, face-to-face, and online instruction in female EFL learners
Article.Authors: Shi H.; Salimi V.; Izadpanah S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Technology-enhanced language instruction has expanded the range of instructional options available to EFL learners, yet evidence comparing blended, online, and face-to-face modes across multiple cognitive and affective outcomes remains limited, particularly among advanced EFL learners. This study compared self-regulated learning strategies (SRLSs), foreign language classroom anxiety (FLCA), and willingness to communicate (WTC) in English writing across these three instructional modes. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was conducted with 360 advanced female EFL learners in Iran (120 per group), selected through two-stage cluster sampling from language institutes. Learners participated in 10 instructional sessions delivered through blended, online, or face-to-face modes. Pre-test and post-test measures of SRLS, FLCA, and WTC were collected using self-report questionnaires. One-way ANCOVAs were conducted for each outcome, controlling for the corresponding pre-test score, followed by Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. After adjustment for baseline scores, statistically significant between-group differences were observed for SRLS, FLCA, and WTC. The blended group had higher adjusted SRLS scores than the online and face-to-face groups (partial η² = 0.411) and higher adjusted WTC scores in English writing (partial η² = 0.266), but lower adjusted FLCA scores than both comparison groups (partial η² = 0.136). No statistically significant differences were observed between the online and face-to-face groups for any outcome. These findings identify a consistent pattern of adjusted between-group differences associated with instructional mode among advanced female Iranian EFL learners. They do not establish comparative efficacy or causal superiority of blended instruction. Pending replication using randomized designs, objective measures, and more diverse samples, the findings may inform further investigation of blended instructional arrangements and the specific pedagogical features associated with learner outcomes.

Article.Title: Material-dependent structure of roughness representation in generative AI-based texture analysis
Article.Authors: Momiyama Y.; Ishizuka H.; Hiraki T.; Miki N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Generative image models can produce visually different expressions of surface roughness depending on material context, but the structure of these variations remains unclear. Here, we systematically examined roughness-related image features in textures generated for six material categories at ten prompt-defined roughness levels. Three prompting conditions were compared: a Quantitative Model, a Generic Linguistic Model using common roughness descriptors across materials, and a Material-Specific Linguistic Model using category-specific descriptions. Nine interpretable image features comprising eight luminance-distribution statistics and the FFT spectral centroid were analyzed. Feature–roughness correlations varied substantially across materials, indicating that no single feature within the examined feature set consistently captured roughness-related variation across all categories. Hierarchical clustering revealed significant associations between material category and cluster assignment for both linguistic models but not for the Quantitative Model, with the strongest associations observed for the Material-Specific Linguistic Model. Silhouette scores in the full nine-dimensional feature space were −0.065, −0.001, and 0.271 for the Quantitative, Generic Linguistic, and Material-Specific Linguistic Models, respectively, indicating clearer category-dependent organization with material-specific linguistic conditioning. These findings demonstrate that roughness-related image-feature organization in the examined generative model depends on both material context and linguistic prompting. This framework provides testable hypotheses for future comparison with physically characterized surfaces and human perceptual judgments.

Article.Title: Performance of five large language models (LLM) on infectious diseases related questions
Article.Authors: Maker J.; Kim M.; Guo X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As there i​s growing interest in utilizing large language models (LLMs) in healthcare education, there are still concerns about their accuracy. The primary study question is to evaluate the accuracy of five LLMs in answering infectious disease (ID) related questions. We compared five LLMs—ChatGPT-4.1, ChatGPT-4o-mini, Claude, Copilot, and Gemini—on 227 exam items from an infectious diseases (ID) course in a Doctor of Pharmacy program. Items were categorized by topic, Bloom’s taxonomy, and format. LLM accuracy across different categories was summarized using descriptive statistics. The Chi-Square test was used to compare results among the different LLMs. Agreement across responses from different LLMs was investigated via Cohen’s Kappa Coefficient. The overall accuracy across all models ranged from 89.4% to 91.2% with ChatGPT 4o-mini scoring highest and Claude and Copilot scoring lowest. LLMs had highest accuracy answering pharmacology questions (93.6%), followed by therapeutics (93.0%), PK/PD (91.1%), microbiology (87.5%), and medicinal chemistry (84%). Medicinal chemistry and microbiology performed significantly worse compared to therapeutics (p < 0.05). Questions categorized as Evaluate/Create performed significantly worse compared to Remember/Understand category (85.6% vs. 92.0%, p < 0.05). The accuracy of questions with a picture was significantly worse than those with no picture (69% vs 91%, respectively). Inter-model agreement was moderate (κ = 0.497–0.613). Contemporary LLMs show high accuracy on ID coursework, with weaknesses in chemistry/microbiology content, higher-order reasoning, and image interpretation; careful integration and guidance are warranted.

Article.Title: Dietary diversity score, alternative healthy eating index and odds of breast cancer
Article.Authors: Sadeghi O.; Sasanfar B.; Toorang F.; Yarigholi F.; Zendehdel K.
Article.Abstract: Previous studies have mainly focused on individual food groups and nutrients in relation to breast cancer and few studies have considered diet as a whole variable. The aim of this study was to examine the association of dietary diversity score (DDS) and alternative healthy eating index-2010 (AHEI-2010) with odds of breast cancer. In this case-control study, we enrolled 477 pathologically confirmed cases of breast cancer and 506 age-matched controls. Dietary assessment was done using a food frequency questionnaire. Dietary indices including DDS and AHEI-2010 were constructed according to standard methods. After controlling for potential confounders, we found a significant inverse association between DDS and odds of breast cancer; individuals in the highest tertile of DDS had 37% lower odds for having breast cancer compared with those in the lowest tertile (OR: 0.63, 95% CI: 0.42–0.95). Such a significant inverse association was also seen among post-menopausal women; such that after taking potential confounders into account, women in the top tertile of DDS score were 60% less likely to have breast cancer compared with those in the bottom tertile (OR: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19–0.83). With regard to AHEI, we found no significant association between AHEI score and odds of breast cancer either before or after controlling for potential confounders. This association remained non-significant either in pre-menopausal or post-menopausal women. We found that adherence to a diet with high diversity was associated with decreased odds of breast cancer. However, no significant association was observed between AHEI and breast cancer.

Article.Title: Multiscale damage evolution mechanisms and life-cycle performance prediction modeling of asphalt pavement for resilient infrastructure
Article.Authors: Ju D.; He P.
Article.Abstract: Asphalt pavements deteriorate under heavy loading, thermal extremes and freeze–thaw cycling, yet damage physics, life-cycle prediction and resilience assessment are still handled as separate problems. This study joins them. We define damage at the micro, meso and macro scales through a single effective-bearing-area variable, and we link the scales with viscoelastic-damage constitutive relations, a cohesive interfacial criterion and representative volume element homogenisation. Scale-separation limits are stated explicitly: a convergence study fixes the representative volume element at four times the nominal maximum aggregate size, and the homogenisation integral is restricted to meso damage below 0.4. Characterisation combines openly accessible condition, climate and traffic records with a laboratory programme of 216 independent specimens covering dynamic modulus, four-point bending fatigue, wheel tracking and interleaved freeze–thaw plus ultraviolet conditioning, supported by image-based mesostructural reconstruction that we validate against expert annotation and against a learned segmentation baseline. A hybrid model embeds the damage evolution equation and a monotonicity requirement in the training objective of a gated recurrent network with attention, and an adaptive weight keeps the data and physics gradients comparable. On a test partition isolated by section, by period and by region, the model reached a coefficient of determination of 0.91 ± 0.01 for rut depth and 0.87 ± 0.02 for cracking ratio over five seeds; the physical constraint raised extrapolation trend consistency from 0.79 to 0.93 and cut monotonicity violations from 11.6 to 0.3%, while keeping the empirical coverage of the nominal 90% interval at 89.4%. Cross-scale transfer was nonlinear in temperature for all three gradations tested, amplifying below freezing and above about 45 °C, although the magnitude was gradation-dependent and we do not claim generality beyond the materials examined. Maintenance strategies separated clearly across resistance, recovery and adaptation. Data, code and configuration files are provided with the paper so that the workflow can be rerun without licensed components.

Article.Title: Spinal analgesia during childbirth in Sweden: a nationwide survey of midwives´ perspectives
Article.Authors: Bjurström M.; Fahlbeck H.; Skalkidou A.; Asif S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pain is a central symptom during childbirth. Compared to epidural analgesia, labour spinal analgesia (LSA) has received little attention, and no study has previously examined midwives´ attitudes toward LSA. This nationwide, mixed-methods survey study explored Swedish midwives´ experiences, perceptions, and use of LSA during vaginal childbirth. A 16-item questionnaire was distributed to 1,756 midwives, of whom 943 (53.7%) responded; the largest proportion was from the Stockholm–Gotland region (67.7%). Most midwives with LSA experience perceived it as effective (96.0%). Experience (number of women assisted with LSA) was categorized as none (4%), low (34.6%, 1–9 women), moderate (38.5% 10–49 women), or high (22.9% ≥ 50 women). Common indications included multiparity, previous rapid labour, and difficult-to-manage pain; the most common limiting factor was concern that the analgesia would wear off before birth. In multivariable penalized logistic regression analysis, working in a university region was associated with lower odds of LSA experience (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.01–0.39). Reflexive thematic analysis of 791 free-text responses resulted in two themes: Effective pain relief within limits of progress and Critical timing as a clinical concern . Respondents expressed strong interest in education on LSA. Further research and interprofessional collaboration are warranted to clarify LSA´s role in obstetric analgesia.

Article.Title: Understanding barriers to clinical trial participation among U.S. women: a national survey study
Article.Authors: Fida D.; Rajasekera T.; Roy A.; Wilson J.; Petro G.; Wiley A.; Lederman R.; Spagnolo P.
Article.Abstract: Women—particularly those from racially and ethnically minoritized groups—remain underrepresented in clinical research, yet their perspectives on participation are not well characterized. We conducted a national cross-sectional online survey of 5,301 U.S. women aged 18–70 years to assess willingness to participate (WTP), experiences with clinical trials, and awareness of sex-based differences in relation to research engagement. Because participation is shaped by social and structural determinants, we examined racial differences alongside socioeconomic status, healthcare access, and self-reported health to delineate intersecting contributors to disparities. Among 4,987 respondents reporting race (77% White, 14% Black, 7% Asian, 2% Other), most expressed at least tentative interest in participating (23% “definitely”, 60% “maybe”), yet only 11% had ever been invited and 7% had enrolled. In adjusted models, WTP was lower among Black women (β=−0.4; P = 0.0003) than among White women, whereas higher educational attainment and multimorbidity predicted greater WTP. Preferred resources, motivators, and perceived barriers also differed by race, which may inform tailored engagement strategies. Finally, most respondents (88%) endorsed women’s inclusion and sex-specific reporting in clinical research, suggesting that emphasizing the sex-specific relevance of research merits evaluation as an engagement strategy. Our findings suggest that limited invitation, together with structural and informational barriers, may contribute to women’s low participation, and support the evaluation of trust-building, burden-reducing, and culturally responsive strategies centered on women’s needs and perspectives to improve equitable representation.

Article.Title: Hand-washing frequency, gastric histopathology, and depressive symptom burden in adults undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: a structural equation modeling study
Article.Authors: Owais M.; Aziz S.; Gul S.; Ijaz U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depressive symptoms are common among patients referred for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, but their relation to mucosal pathology is unclear. An abrupt shift in patient characteristics and histology grades during recruitment was identified and adjusted for. In the primary model (CFI = 0.971; RMSEA = 0.040), less frequent hand washing was associated with higher depressive symptom burden (β = 0.23, 95% CI 0.06–0.39) but not with gastric severity (β = −0.11, 95% CI − 0.25 to 0.03). Gastric severity was not associated with symptom burden (β = 0.14, 95% CI − 0.06 to 0.35), and the indirect effect through gastric severity was null. The hand-washing association persisted in all six sensitivity analyses, whereas an apparent hand-washing–pathology association appeared only without adjustment for recruitment period. Depressive symptom burden in these patients was unrelated to mucosal pathology but tracked reduced self-care, supporting symptom screening irrespective of endoscopic findings.

Article.Title: Assessment of moisture availability and dryness during the growing season in the almaty region
Article.Authors: Akshalov K.; Zhunissova M.; Baisholanov S.; Zhumabek B.; Baimukanova O.
Article.Abstract: The novelty of this study lies in the integrated assessment of moisture availability and dryness during the growing season in the Almaty region over 1990–2024 using SPI-6 and SPEI-6 indices combined with NDVI-based vegetation response, providing new insights into climate-driven agricultural vulnerability in Central Asia. Under recent climate variability, an analysis of moisture availability and aridity and their distributions during the growing season in the Almaty region was conducted based on long-term data (1990–2024) on temperature, precipitation, moisture coefficient, hydrothermal coefficient (HTC), standard precipitation index (SPI-6), standardized precipitation-evapotranspiration index (SPEI-6), and NDVI satellite observations. It was found that the region is characterized by high spatial and temporal variability of climatic parameters. The average long-term temperature deviation during the growing season was 1.2 °C (maximum 1.8 °C in Kegen), the greatest precipitation variability was recorded in Esik and on the Almaty Kamensky Plateau, and the least in arid areas (Aul 4, Bakanas). The humidity coefficient varies from 0.33 (severe aridity) to 2.0 (excessive humidity), with HTC indicating non-arid conditions in the mountains (≥ 0.8) and severe aridity in desert areas (≤ 0.4). The SPI-6 and SPEI-6 indices revealed an increase in the frequency and intensity of droughts, especially in flat areas, while the NDVI confirmed vegetation stress during dry periods. The region's climate variability is manifested in both a trend towards aridification and short-term phases of excessive moisture (2016), with 2021 being the driest year on record. The results confirm the high climatic vulnerability of the Almaty region and the need for adaptation measures in the agricultural sector.

Article.Title: Network-based SEIVQHR modelling with optimal mobility control and QUBO reformulation
Article.Authors: Ramesh R.; Kannan M.; Chandrasekran K.; Zhan L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human mobility between interconnected geographical regions can substantially influence the spatial transmission of infectious diseases, motivating epidemic-control strategies that account for both disease dynamics and regional interactions. In this study, we develop a network-based discrete-time SEIVQHR model comprising susceptible, exposed, infectious, vaccinated, quarantined, hospitalized, and recovered compartments, with inter-regional transmission represented through a normalized mobility matrix. The formulation incorporates vaccination, quarantine, hospitalization, and mobility-dependent infection within a unified metapopulation framework. A key feature of the model is the explicit representation of breakthrough infection among vaccinated individuals. Vaccine efficacy $$\epsilon $$ determines the residual susceptibility $$1-\epsilon $$ , and breakthrough infections enter the exposed compartment before progressing through the infectious pathway. We establish positivity, boundedness, and positive invariance of the discrete-time system under admissibility conditions involving the time step $$\Delta t$$ . The basic reproduction number $$R_0$$ is derived using a next-generation matrix formulation that accounts for both vaccination coverage and network connectivity. The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be locally asymptotically stable for $$R_0<1$$ and unstable for $$R_0>1$$ . We further formulate a finite-horizon optimal-control problem with binary regional mobility restrictions and continuous vaccination allocation subject to vaccine-supply constraints. For a prescribed vaccination trajectory, the binary mobility-control component is approximated locally by a quadratic objective and reformulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. The resulting QUBO is mapped to an equivalent Ising Hamiltonian, enabling solution using simulated annealing, greedy heuristics, or quantum-annealing platforms. The framework is calibrated using COVID-19 surveillance data from India for 2021, with selected epidemiological parameters fixed at literature-based values to reduce overfitting and maintain biological plausibility. Numerical experiments examine parameter sensitivity, reproduction-number behaviour, admissible parameter regions, QUBO construction, and solver performance. The results identify the transmission rate as the dominant sensitivity factor and demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed QUBO-based formulation for binary mobility-control optimization. Overall, the proposed framework provides a mathematically consistent decision-support methodology that connects network-based epidemic modelling, continuous vaccination allocation, binary mobility intervention, and QUBO/Ising optimization while retaining the nonlinear epidemic dynamics for validation of the resulting intervention strategies.

Article.Title: Deep-learning surrogate modeling for rapid design of high-sensitivity terahertz metasurface sensors
Article.Authors: Ahmadi E.; Mirshekari N.; Taghadosi M.; Mohammadi Pouyan S.; Askari M.
Article.Abstract: The design of terahertz metasurface sensors commonly relies on extensive full-wave electromagnetic simulations, making systematic exploration of high-dimensional design spaces computationally demanding. In this work, a deep-learning-assisted surrogate modeling framework is proposed to accelerate the design and optimization of refractive-index-sensitive metasurfaces. A dataset comprising 2048 distinct CST-simulated metasurface configurations was generated over the frequency range of 1.0–1.4 THz. With 1001 frequency points evaluated for each configuration, the pointwise regression dataset contains 2,050,048 input–output samples of the complex transmission response. A multilayer neural network was trained to predict the real and imaginary components of the transmission coefficient as a function of geometric parameters, operating frequency, and analyte refractive index. The trained surrogate achieved strong predictive performance on an independent test dataset, yielding a mean squared error of \(4.12\times 10^{-3}\) , a mean absolute error of \(4.27\times 10^{-2}\) , and a coefficient of determination of \(R^{2}=0.9792\) . The model accurately reproduced the spectral features governing resonance-based sensing and enabled rapid evaluation of candidate metasurface designs without repeated full-wave simulations. The surrogate model was subsequently employed to screen thousands of candidate geometries and identify promising sensing configurations. Selected candidates were validated through full-wave CST simulations, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed screening strategy. The best-performing design exhibited a refractive-index sensitivity of approximately \(0.2~\mathrm {THz/RIU}\) ( \(232~\mathrm {GHz/RIU}\) ), which is roughly 2.5 times higher than the baseline value of \(80~\mathrm {GHz/RIU}\) reported for closely related metasurface geometries. The observed resonance shifts and the agreement between surrogate predictions and CST results demonstrate the capability of the framework to guide the discovery of high-performance sensor designs. The results highlight the potential of surrogate-assisted electromagnetic design as an efficient and scalable alternative to conventional parameter-sweep-based optimization. The proposed framework substantially reduces computational cost while enabling systematic exploration of complex metasurface design spaces, providing a practical route toward data-driven development of terahertz sensing devices.

Article.Title: Beyond formal institutions: informal governance and farmer cooperation in a transition economy
Article.Authors: Skreli E.; Xhoxhi O.; Valentinov V.; Imami D.; Zhllima E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Friedrich Hayek distinguished the small-group logic of local norms, interpersonal trust, and reciprocity from the impersonal rules of the Great Society. In transition settings, however, these forms of governance may coexist rather than follow a simple sequence of replacement. Using a cross-sectional Albanian orchard farm survey, we estimate OLS models, bootstrapped product-of-coefficients paths, and an exploratory interaction to examine associations among local informal-rule enforcement, interpersonal trust, reciprocity, institutional trust, and willingness to cooperate. Stronger perceived local-rule enforcement is positively associated with interpersonal trust and willingness to cooperate; interpersonal trust is strongly associated with reciprocity, and reciprocity with willingness to cooperate. Institutional trust has no statistically significant direct association with willingness to cooperate in the fully specified model, although the local-rules/cooperation association is modestly stronger at higher levels of institutional trust. Indirect-path estimates are consistent with a sequence linking local rules, trust, reciprocity, and cooperation, but the cross-sectional design cannot establish temporal or causal ordering. The study therefore provides exploratory, single-setting evidence compatible with complementarity between informal and broader institutional governance.

Article.Title: Clinical classification of multiple sclerosis by machine learning
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Liu H.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that affects many adults and causes substantial neurological disability. Its clinical presentations are highly heterogeneous, and distinguishing clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing-remitting MS and progressive subtypes remains difficult, even though subtype determines treatment. Machine learning offers a way to address this difficulty: it identifies subtle patterns in high-dimensional biomedical data and has shown promise for MS classification from neuroimaging, whereas its performance on transcriptomic data has received less attention. To examine this question, we benchmarked three ensemble classifiers, AdaBoost, Random Forest and XGBoost, on 594 peripheral-blood mononuclear-cell transcriptomes from three public datasets, using a shared 6,033-gene matrix for four binary tasks: MS versus non-MS, CIS versus non-CIS, primary progressive versus relapsing-remitting MS, and secondary progressive versus relapsing-remitting MS. Models were evaluated on a 3:1 training/held-out split after standardization and two-component principal component analysis. All three classifiers achieved high held-out performance across the four tasks. These results indicate that ensemble machine learning can effectively classify MS and its clinical subtypes from blood transcriptomic profiles.

Article.Title: An intent aware framework for semantic edge intelligence in autonomous 6g UAV and vehicular networks
Article.Authors: Begum S.; Khan M.; Babu G.; Raghavi S.; Sakri S.
Article.Abstract: In autonomous communication between unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and vehicles in emerging sixth-generation (6G) networks, intelligent edge computing is essential for reliable decision-making under rapidly changing network conditions. This paper presents SEM-EDGE-X, a semantic edge intelligence framework integrating semantic feature extraction, Bayesian priority prediction, adaptive edge-to-cloud routing, semantic memory-assisted decision-making, dynamic resource management, adaptive cold-start semantic fusion, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) validation, dynamic trust refinement, and Digital Twin simulation. Performance is evaluated using Python and SUMO mobility modelling with the KITTI and UAVDT datasets under varying channel conditions and network densities, in terms of semantic accuracy, simulated communication latency, throughput, energy consumption, scalability, computational cost, and robustness. The results indicate a favourable trade-off among communication efficiency, energy consumption, and semantic performance, with 95.76% semantic accuracy (transmission fidelity under channel noise, not correctness against ground-truth labels), approximately 1.04 ms simulated communication latency (propagation, transmission, and queueing only), throughput above 25 Mbps, and energy consumption below 0.006 mJ. The separately measured software execution time of the pipeline is approximately 109.6 ms and is not included in the simulated latency.

Article.Title: Evaluating weakly supervised deep segmentation trained on radiometric pseudo labels for thermal fault screening in electrical substations
Article.Authors: Ekici S.; Uyar M.; Kabir M.
Article.Abstract: Fixed radiometric rules often supply training labels for infrared inspection of substations, where dense expert masks are rarely available. We examined what segmentation networks learn from such a rule and whether the result supports fault screening. On 193 calibrated FLIR frames, pixels exceeding the frame’s 30th-percentile temperature by more than \(16^{\,\circ }\) C served as pseudo labels for U-Net, DeepLabV3 and a compact attention-based network under five-fold cross-validation; outputs were assessed against held-out expert labels and independent field notes. With per-frame min–max input normalisation, agreement with the rule was low (Dice 0.34–0.44), and two networks ranked expert-positive frames below expert-negative ones (area under the curve 0.26 and 0.30). Supplying the temperature difference on a fixed physical scale raised agreement to Dice 0.78–0.81 and removed this inversion, whereas architecture had no significant effect. The pseudo labels encoded the extent of warm equipment rather than faults (labelled-area AUC 0.40), and the rule’s maximum temperature difference remained the best screening signal (0.75 against expert labels, 0.91 against field notes). A local thermal reference made labelled area informative (0.60–0.69). Network inputs should preserve the physical units in which supervision is defined, and radiometric pseudo labels benefit from local rather than frame-level references.

Article.Title: AI-driven HR service quality and organisational citizenship behaviour in the Indian IT sector: the mediating role of organisational commitment
Article.Authors: Priya K.; Muddhangala N.
Article.Abstract: In the modern world, the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resource Management (HRM) is changing the landscape of service delivery in Knowledge-Based Organisations (KBOs). While there is an increasing trend in investing in HR processes powered by AI, there is not enough empirical research exploring how perceived AI-HR service quality relates to employee behavioural outcome through psychological mechanisms, especially in the Indian information technology (IT) industry. The study uses Social Exchange Theory (SET) as its primary lens and non-measured, but secondary, lens is Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to analyse the impact of AI-based HR service quality on Organisational Citizenship Behaviour (OCB) which is in turn mediated by Organisational Commitment (OC) which is operationalised as a second-order reflective construct with three sub-constructs namely affective commitment, continuance commitment, and normative commitment. A survey of IT professionals drawn from major technology hubs across India was conducted and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrate that AI-driven HR service quality exerts a significant positive influence on organisational commitment, which in turn meaningfully predicts organisational citizenship behaviour. Furthermore, AI-driven HR service quality also directly influences citizenship behaviour, and organisational commitment partially mediates this relationship. Individual and organisational boundary conditions, including AI literacy, technology anxiety, organisational AI support, and job role complexity, were found to moderate key relationships in the model. Theoretical and practical implications for AI-HRM system design and IT workforce management are discussed.

Article.Title: A long-term memory variational GAN for high-quality music generation and its application in music education
Article.Authors: Han Y.; Cheng D.
Article.Abstract: Traditional music generation models suffer from error accumulation and degraded quality in long-sequence generation, limiting their potential applications in intelligent music education. This study proposes a Long-term Memory Variational Generative Adversarial Network (LM-VGAN) by integrating long short-term memory and gated feature selection modules. We constructed multiple baseline models, including VAEGAN for comparative experiments, and adopted both objective quantitative metrics and subjective auditory evaluation to assess model performance. Experimental results show that after 50 iterations, LM-VGAN achieves a scale consistency of 89.15, pitch range of 1055, and note quality of 0.391, which outperforms mainstream baseline models and approaches real music standards. In subjective evaluation, it scores 8.30 in pleasantness and 7.77 in naturalness. The proposed model effectively solves the long-term dependency problem of music sequences. It provides a reliable technical solution for content creation, personalized training, and innovative development in modern potential applications for music education.

Article.Title: A privacy aware lightweight edge intelligent framework for real-time lethal threat interception and risk assessment
Article.Authors: Saha H.; Banerjee U.; Ghosh A.; Mattar E.; Bhattacharya P.; Shieh C.
Article.Abstract: Real-time intelligent surveillance systems require a careful balance between predictive reliability, computational efficiency, energy consumption, inference latency, and privacy preservation. However, existing vision-based approaches often achieve high detection accuracy at the expense of computational complexity, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose a privacy-preserving, lightweight edge intelligence framework guided by a multi-objective architectural design methodology that jointly balances accuracy, computational efficiency, energy efficiency, real-time responsiveness, and on-device privacy.​ The proposed framework combines hybrid local-global representation learning with a lightweight multi-scale spatial attention mechanism to enhance the recognition of small and partially occluded lethal threats. A lightweight Temporal Threat Validation Module suppresses transient false alarms through temporal consistency analysis, while a context-aware Threat Assessment Network transforms validated detections into quantitative threat intelligence for priority-based decision-making. The complete pipeline executes locally on a Raspberry Pi 5 integrated with a Hailo-8L neural accelerator, transmitting only encrypted threat metadata to ensure low-latency, privacy-preserving operation.Experimental results demonstrate a Precision of 95.36%, Recall of 93.74%, an F1-score of 94.54%, and an mAP@0.5 of 96.58%. The proposed framework reduces localization error by 34.1%, decreases false alarms by 60.9%, and increases actionable alerts to 92.8% while sustaining 31.8 FPS, 31.4 ms inference latency, and an average power consumption of 9.1 W on the edge platform. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively unifies lightweight representation learning, temporal reasoning, contextual threat intelligence, and privacy-preserving edge computing, providing an energy-efficient and practically deployable solution for next-generation real-time intelligent public safety systems.

Article.Title: Design, implementation, and deployment of a machine vision-based dimension measurement system for steel slabs using deep neural networks
Article.Authors: Mazandarani M.; Akbarizadeh G.
Article.Abstract: Accurate measurement of steel slab dimensions is important for quality control and process monitoring in hot rolling. This study presents an automated machine vision system for measuring slab length, width, and thickness under real production conditions. The system combines a dual-camera imaging setup, controlled illumination, DeepLabV3 + semantic segmentation with an EfficientNet-B5 backbone, RANSAC-based boundary fitting, and a height-dependent calibration strategy for pixel-to-millimeter conversion. The software is integrated with the plant’s SQL-based network to compare measured dimensions with Product Data Information (PDI) and provide operator feedback. The system was evaluated on 65 previously unseen steel slabs that were independent of the 1,514 slabs used for network training and validation. Mean absolute errors were 2.56 mm, 1.84 mm, and 1.04 mm for length, width, and thickness, respectively, with corresponding RMSE values of 3.15 mm, 2.39 mm, and 1.35 mm. Using plant-specific tolerance bands of ± 5 mm, ± 3 mm, and ± 2 mm, within-tolerance agreement rates were 98.5%, 96.9%, and 95.4%. The complete measurement cycle takes approximately 4.2 s per slab and the system is currently deployed on a production line.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based PM2.5 estimation using NASA’s MERRA-2 and comparison of ML- and SHAP-based meteorological normalization in Thailand
Article.Authors: Aman N.; Torsri K.
Article.Abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) poses severe health risks in Thailand; however, sparse ground monitoring has left long-term trends poorly quantified. This study utilizes NASA’s MERRA-2 reanalysis to estimate historical PM 2.5 levels across Thailand through two approaches: an empirical formulation based on PM 2.5 chemical components (MERRA2_EF) and a machine-learning model (MERRA2_ML) utilizing the Light Gradient Boosting Machine algorithm. Validated against 58 reference air quality stations across Thailand (2012–2022), the MERRA2_ML model significantly outperforms the MERRA2_EF, increasing temporal correlation from 0.48 to 0.84, while reducing MAE from 14.99 to 8.64 µg m⁻³ and RMSE from 24.95 to 13.39 µg m⁻³. Similar improvements in model performance were also observed across the different regions of Thailand, with the MERRA2_ML estimates generally showing stronger temporal agreement and lower errors than the MERRA2_EF. MERRA2_ML substantially improved the representation of observed PM 2.5 variability across Thailand, accurately capturing diurnal peaks, dry-season enhancements, and interannual fluctuations, particularly in biomass-burning- and urban-influenced regions, compared with MERRA2_EF. Long-term analysis revealed significant increases in PM 2.5 across Thailand (1.97 µg m ⁻3 per decade) and most regions from 1981 to 2022, with MERRA2_ML showing consistently lower and more moderate trends than MERRA2_EF, highlighting substantial spatial heterogeneity in long-term PM 2.5 changes. By employing Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) for meteorological normalization, this study isolated emission-driven PM 2.5 variations. Overall, decreasing trends in emission-related PM 2.5 were observed across Thailand and several regions; however, statistical significance varied by region and method, and the non-significant national trends do not provide sufficient evidence to attribute the observed decline to a sustained nationwide reduction in emissions or policy interventions. These findings demonstrate that ML-enhanced reanalysis provides robust, spatially explicit data to support evidence-based public health decisions and air quality management throughout Southeast Asia.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation of blade-tip leakage flow control in a low-speed axial compressor using natural aspiration through casing wall slot
Article.Authors: Taghavi Zenouz R.; Ghashghaie Nejad P.
Article.Abstract: Mitigating rotor blade tip leakage flow in axial compressors is crucial for improving aerodynamic performance and extending the stable operating range. This study experimentally evaluates natural aspiration through a circumferential casing slot upstream of an isolated rotor blade row, with the configuration informed by previous numerical studies. The treatment passively admits ambient air without an external compressed-air supply. Experiments at 1600 rpm compared plain and treated casings using performance measurements, casing-wall static pressures, and single-wire hot-wire anemometry. Fourier-based spectral analysis was used to examine the measured flow unsteadiness. The performance curves indicated an approximately 1.2% increase in the pressure-rise coefficient. The reported operating points extended to an inlet-flow coefficient of 0.28 for the treated casing and 0.32 for the plain casing. Wall-pressure distributions and velocity spectra provided complementary information on the near-tip flow response, without independently establishing vortex weakening or a specific stall-inception mechanism. The admitted mass flow and overall efficiency were not quantified, limiting conclusions about rotor-throughflow-based stability improvement and efficiency. The results provide an experimental basis for evaluating passive air admission as a compressor casing treatment.

Article.Title: Computational evaluation of pongamol interactions with potential molecular targets of Blastocystis hominis
Article.Authors: Subramaniyan V.; Kumarasamy V.; Osman E.; Rajamanikam A.; Ashok C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pongamol, a bioactive substance that occurs naturally, shows promise as a treatment that targets several molecular pathways associated with Blastocystis hominis infection. Its binding affinity, pharmacokinetic behaviour, and protein-chemical interactions were examined in this work using molecular docking, ADMET profiling, and STITCH network analysis. Docking analysis predicted favorable binding of pongamol to eight selected protein targets, with the lowest docking scores observed for squalene epoxidase (− 9.7 kcal/mol), dihydrofolate reductase (− 8.9 kcal/mol), adenosine deaminase (− 8.6 kcal/mol), and thioredoxin reductase 1 (− 8.2 kcal/mol). These findings indicate that pongamol may interact with proteins involved in processes related to sterol metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and redox regulation. However, the docking results represent predicted binding interactions and do not establish enzymatic inhibition or biological efficacy. The ADMET analysis predicted high gastrointestinal absorption, blood–brain barrier permeability, and favorable drug-likeness, but also indicated inhibition of CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, and CYP3A4, as well as potential hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity concerns. These in silico results support further investigation of pongamol as a computationally prioritized multi-target candidate against Blastocystis hominis . However, experimental studies are required to determine whether pongamol truly inhibits these targets or exhibits antiparasitic activity.

Article.Title: Chromatin-associated miRNAs in PANC-1 cells: strong chromatin abundance of miR-21 and candidates with RNA–DNA triplex-forming potential
Article.Authors: Martin M.; Jalife C.; Méndez C.; Montecinos C.; Brown-Brown D.; Díaz-Tejeda F.; Caffi V.; Zavala K.; Kugler F.; Molina-González L.; Valenzuela-Nieto G.; Längst G.; Mardones G.; Munita R.; Opazo J.; Maldonado R.
Article.Abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are best known for their role in post-transcriptional gene regulation in the cytoplasm. However, a subset of miRNAs has been detected in the nucleus, suggesting additional regulatory functions. Here, we systematically characterize chromatin-associated small non-coding RNAs in the human pancreatic cancer cell line PANC-1. Using chromatin RNA immunoprecipitation coupled with small RNA sequencing, we show that the chromatin-associated small RNA population differs markedly from the bulk nuclear RNA pool and is strongly enriched in miRNAs. Among these, miR-21 represents the most abundant chromatin-associated species. In parallel, sequence analyses further revealed that a distinct subset of chromatin-associated miRNAs fulfills sequence requirements compatible with RNA–DNA triplex formation at genomic regulatory regions. Gel-shift assays demonstrate that Argonaute2 (Ago2) can interact with triple-helical structures in vitro, providing biochemical support for Ago2 recognition of such triplex substrates. Evolutionary analyses indicate that triplex-forming chromatin-associated miRNAs show a restricted phyletic distribution, with the full complement observed only in anthropoid primates, in contrast to the much broader conservation of non-triplex-forming miRNAs. Together, our results define a chromatin-associated miRNA landscape in PANC-1 cells, highlight miR-21 as the most abundant chromatin-associated miRNA, and identify candidate triplex-forming miRNAs and Ago2-triplex interactions that outline a testable hypothesis for an additional mode of miRNA-chromatin communication.

Article.Title: Cognitive impairment is associated with lower extremity function among community-dwelling older adults in Taiwan
Article.Authors: Liang I.; Lin L.; Tseng W.; Lin T.; Shen Y.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairment is associated with poorer physical function in older adults, yet its relationship with different dimensions of lower-extremity function remains underexplored in community-dwelling populations. This study examined associations between cognitive status and lower-extremity function among community-dwelling older adults in Taiwan. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 82 adults aged 60 years and older. Cognitive status was assessed using the Saint Louis University Mental Status Examination (SLUMS) together with physician assessment, with participants classified as having normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia. Lower-extremity function was evaluated using standardised measures of lower-body strength (30-second chair stand), flexibility (chair sit-and-reach), agility and dynamic balance (8-foot up-and-go), and postural stability (Biodex BioSway system). Significant differences in physical performance were observed across cognitive groups, with participants with dementia demonstrating poorer lower-body strength, flexibility, agility/dynamic balance, and selected measures of postural stability compared with those with normal cognition and MCI ( p < 0.05). Higher SLUMS scores, indicating better global cognitive performance, were associated with better lower-body strength and flexibility, faster 8-foot up-and-go performance, and better performance on several postural stability measures ( p < 0.05). These cross-sectional findings demonstrate associations between cognitive performance and multiple dimensions of lower-extremity function in community-dwelling older adults. Performance-based assessment of lower-extremity function alongside cognitive assessment may help characterise functional differences across levels of cognitive impairment, although longitudinal studies are required to determine whether these measures have value in predicting subsequent functional or cognitive decline.

Article.Title: LeXT-Net: A lead-adaptive hierarchical network for 3-lead to 12-lead ECG reconstruction
Article.Authors: Tekin R.; Tekin H.; Onat M.; Akkuş M.; Kaya Y.
Article.Abstract: Standard 12-lead electrocardiography provides spatial cardiac information that is not fully available from the small number of channels typically used in ambulatory and wearable monitoring, whereas acquisition of all 12 leads requires multiple electrodes and controlled anatomical placement. Estimating unobserved leads from reduced-lead recordings may therefore extend the information available from compact ECG systems. In this study, we propose LeXT-Net, a hierarchical lead-adaptive architecture for reconstructing 12-lead ECG signals from three-lead inputs. The model combines a shared temporal convolutional network backbone, lead-specific grouped temporal attention, independent U-Net decoding heads with different capacities for limb and precordial leads, and a composite objective incorporating waveform fidelity, Einthoven-Goldberger consistency, and precordial spatial regularization. Four predefined input configurations (EGV1, EGV2, EGV3, and QSI) were evaluated using all-lead (mAll), non-input (mOther), and independent-target (mInd) scopes. On PTB-XL, LeXT-Net achieved R 2 = 0.910, PCC = 0.952, SSIM = 0.840, RMSE = 0.041, and SNR = 27.48 dB under EGV3-mAll; under the stricter EGV3-mInd evaluation, R 2 = 0.786, PCC = 0.885, SSIM = 0.622, and SNR = 9.918 dB. Additional five-fold evaluations on the independent Chapman-Shaoxing and CPSC2018 databases yielded EGV3-mAll R 2 /PCC values of 0.887/0.939 and 0.912/0.953, respectively. These results indicate that LeXT-Net can reconstruct substantial signal-level information from three-lead inputs across multiple ECG databases, including targets that are neither directly observed nor algebraically derivable. The findings support further investigation of reduced-lead ECG reconstruction, while clinical equivalence to directly acquired 12-lead ECG and robustness to native wearable-device recordings remain to be established.

Article.Title: Health-promoting lifestyle profiles among ethnic minority adults with cardiometabolic conditions in Yunnan, China
Article.Authors: Yu H.; He X.; Li H.; Tian H.; Yang X.; Wen S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Health-promoting lifestyle is important for chronic cardiometabolic disease management, but its heterogeneity among ethnic minority adults remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 957 ethnic minority adults with hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia in Yunnan, China. Health-promoting lifestyle was assessed using the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile-II Revised. Latent profile analysis was conducted using six standardized dimension scores, and models with one to five profiles were compared under equal-volume, equal-shape diagonal (EEI) and varying-volume, varying-shape diagonal (VVI) covariance structures. Posterior-probability multiple-imputation logistic regression using 5,000 pseudo-class draws was used to examine factors associated with the higher health-promoting lifestyle profile while accounting for classification uncertainty. A two-profile EEI solution was retained as the most parsimonious model with adequate class sizes. The lower and higher health-promoting lifestyle profiles included 508 participants (53.08%) and 449 participants (46.92%), respectively. The profiles showed consistently lower and higher scores across all six dimensions. Classification separation was limited (entropy = 0.506), and 184 participants (19.23%) had a maximum posterior probability below 0.70. Modal profile assignment agreed with an empirical median split of the HPLP-II R total score in 95.61% of participants (Cohen’s κ = 0.912), and the continuous total score discriminated modal profile assignment with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.995. Supplementary psychometric analyses showed consistent subscale reliability and did not identify substantial measurement non-equivalence across the five major ethnic groups. After accounting for classification uncertainty, older age, meeting the study criteria for two cardiometabolic conditions, and PARS-3 physical activity level were associated with the higher profile; the estimate for three conditions was directionally similar but did not reach statistical significance. Ethnicity-related associations were attenuated after adjustment for geographic region and recruitment source with site-clustered standard errors and should be interpreted as context-dependent contrasts within the sampled sites, without implying independent ethnic effects. PARS-3 total score showed a modest positive correlation with the standardized HPLP-II R physical activity dimension score (Spearman’s ρ = 0.315, 95% CI: 0.258–0.372, P < 0.001). In a sensitivity analysis excluding the HPLP-II R physical activity dimension from the profile indicators, high PARS-3 physical activity remained associated with the higher profile, whereas the association for moderate physical activity was attenuated and no longer statistically significant. Median-split and continuous total-score analyses produced largely concordant association patterns. The selected profiles represented quantitatively ordered levels of health-promoting lifestyle and provided limited incremental information beyond the total score. Profile assignment should therefore be interpreted as an exploratory probabilistic indicator of overall lifestyle engagement.

Article.Title: Association of the dietary index for gut microbiota with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic syndrome: an NHANES-based study
Article.Authors: Sun J.; Chen Z.; Wu X.; He Z.; Bao T.; Zhao L.; Tong X.
Article.Abstract: Previous studies link the Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) to mortality in CKM syndrome, but its robustness and added prognostic value remain unclear. We included 13,286 adults (≥ 20 years) with CKM syndrome from NHANES 2007–2018. Kaplan–Meier curves, weighted Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses evaluated associations of DI-GM with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Weighted machine-learning analyses further compared DI-GM with the Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII), and assessed the relative prognostic contributions of its 14 components. During a median follow-up of 80 months, 1,207 all-cause deaths occurred, including 368 cardiovascular deaths. Each 1-SD increase in DI-GM was associated with 11% and 17% lower risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, respectively (HR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.83–0.95, P < 0.001; HR = 0.83, 95% CI 0.74–0.94, P = 0.003). RCS analyses showed linear inverse associations; significant interactions by age and CKM stage were observed for cardiovascular mortality; and sensitivity analyses supported robustness. DI-GM demonstrated prognostic discrimination comparable to established dietary indices. Component-level analyses revealed the contributions of specific dietary components. DI-GM offers a complementary gut microbiota-based perspective for prognosis and dietary management in CKM syndrome.

Article.Title: An efficient stiffness-based finite element thermo-mechanical modeling of elastically linked double curved non-prismatic beams
Article.Authors: Keshmiri A.; Rezaiee-Pajand M.; Masoodi A.
Article.Abstract: This study presents an efficient stiffness-based finite element formulation for the mechanical and thermo-mechanical analysis of double-curved beam systems coupled via a continuous elastic interlayer. Utilizing an explicit stiffness matrix developed by the authors, the formulation accurately incorporates axial, shear, and bending deformations and allowing both prismatic and non-prismatic geometries to be handled with high fidelity, while a systematic static condensation reduces the 12-DOF element into an equivalent 6-DOF model without loss of accuracy. A distributed system of translational and rotational springs models the interlayer, and the unit load approach extends the method to capture uniform and gradient temperature fields in both prismatic and non-prismatic configurations. Principal results from extensive numerical benchmarks demonstrate that the formulation achieves rapid convergence and high accuracy, exactly matching analytical limits at zero ( \(\:k=0\) ) and infinite ( \(\:k\to\:\infty\:\) ) interlayer stiffness. Major findings confirm that interlayer stiffness smoothly governs the coupled structural response, transitioning behavior between independent and fully composite action, and that the proposed approach predicts thermo-mechanical interactions with superior computational efficiency.

Article.Title: AI-powered capabilities are associated with green new product development through exploratory and exploitative pathways
Article.Authors: Zhou J.; Chen J.; Liu C.; Zhan R.; Cao J.; Liu T.; Zhong D.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the organizational pathways through which AI-powered capabilities are associated with green NPD in manufacturing firms. Specifically, it examines the dual mediating roles of green exploratory and green exploitative, and tests whether the mediating effect of exploration is stronger than that of exploitation in the AI‑green NPD link. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a dual-mediation framework in which green exploratory and green exploitative represent distinct organizational pathways through which firms may mobilize AI-related informational and analytical resources. Hypotheses are tested using survey data from 333 Chinese manufacturing firms across five high‑priority sectors. Hierarchical regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4; 5,000 resamples) are employed. – Both green exploratory and green exploitative significantly mediate the relationship between AI-powered capabilities and green NPD. Although the exploratory indirect effect is numerically larger, a direct bootstrap contrast shows that the difference between the two pathways is not statistically significant. The full model explains 54% of the variance in green NPD. This study contributes by distinguishing green exploration and exploitation as two separate organizational pathways linking AI-powered capabilities with green NPD. Rather than assuming that one pathway necessarily dominates the other, the findings show that both mechanisms are empirically relevant, while their relative indirect effects do not differ significantly. This dual-pathway perspective provides a more fine-grained account of how AI-related capabilities are associated with green innovation outcomes.

Article.Title: Multimodal infection control bed isolation system: towards safeguarding emergency rooms from future pandemics
Article.Authors: Baek C.; Kim Y.; Lee K.; Park S.; Lee S.; Choi D.; Lee J.; Shim J.; Cho M.; Lim M.; Jeon B.; Kim B.; Yoon D.; Kim Y.; Cho S.; Yeo M.; Shin S.; Zo H.; Kim K.; Kim S.
Article.Abstract: Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) exposed how emergency rooms (ERs) can be overwhelmed during a large-scale airborne outbreak, forcing closures and disrupting emergency care. In this proof-of-concept study, we developed and evaluated a prototype of a multimodal infection control bed isolation system (MICBIS) integrating physical isolation, air circulation with HEPA filtration, and automated UV-C disinfection, designed to help ERs remain operational during airborne-disease outbreaks. The initial design was guided by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations; a prototype was then installed and validated in a full-scale ER mock-up by dispersing the biological indicator (BI) Bacillus subtilis with a Collison nebulizer. In biological validation under steady-state, static conditions in an enclosed laboratory environment, no viable BI was recovered outside the integrated unit, both airborne and settled BI within the enclosure fell below the detection limit, and remaining BI on the internal surfaces was inactivated within 20 min by UV-C. Because the MICBIS was designed as a standalone unit requiring no modifications to the ER or its ventilation, we expect it can be deployed rapidly at an open ER bed. Following this feasibility study, additional validation of this system is required in a dynamic clinical environment.

Article.Authors: Chan M.; Fisal A.; Francis J.
Article.Abstract: This cross-sectional study assessed the interrelationship, prevalence and severity of xerostomia and hyposalivation, and their associated sociodemographic and clinical factors, in a clinic-based sample of medically complex older adults attending a university Special Care Dentistry clinic ( N = 50). Subjective xerostomia was reported by 84% of participants (42/50; 95% CI 70.9–92.8), whereas 26% (13/50; 95% CI 14.6–40.3) demonstrated hyposalivation, defined as an unstimulated whole saliva flow rate of ≤ 0.1 mL/min. Among participants without perceived dry mouth, 12.5% (1/8; 95% CI 0.3–52.7) exhibited objective salivary hypofunction; this estimate rests on a single participant and is correspondingly imprecise, but it suggests a possible risk of underdiagnosis when relying solely on symptoms. A significant negative correlation was observed between xerostomia severity and salivary flow (Spearman’s ρ = − 0.367, 95% CI − 0.59 to − 0.10, p = 0.009). On exact testing, no sociodemographic or clinical factor examined, including the number of medications taken, was significantly associated with xerostomia severity or hyposalivation. Systemic conditions and medications were recorded from clinical records, but category-level analyses were not undertaken because the underlying classifications could not be verified against a pre-specified coding scheme. These findings indicate that xerostomia and hyposalivation are related but non-equivalent conditions, supporting objective sialometry as a useful complementary tool alongside symptom assessment within a multidisciplinary care framework. Given the single-centre, clinic-based pilot sample, selection and referral biases limit the external generalisability of these exploratory findings, which require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts.

Article.Title: A cross sectional study on legumes intake in relation to hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype and triglyceride glucose index in Iranian adults
Article.Authors: Esfahani P.; Moradmand Z.; Shahdadian F.; Rouhani P.; Saneei P.
Article.Abstract: Despite the clinical importance of the hypertriglyceridemic waist (HTGW) phenotype as a practical predictive marker for cardiovascular disease and the prominence of the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index as a surrogate of insulin resistance, previous studies have not adequately addressed the relation between these outcomes with legumes intake. This cross-sectional study enrolled 528 Iranian adults (45.6% female) selected through a multistage cluster random-sampling approach. The HTGW phenotype was characterized by the simultaneous occurrence of elevated serum triglyceride concentrations and increased waist circumference. Fasting blood samples were collected to measure serum triglycerides and fasting blood glucose (FBG) concentrations. TyG index was calculated for each participant using fasting TG and FBG levels. Those in the highest tertile of legumes consumption had lower odds of HTGW phenotype in both crude (OR = 0.46; 95% CI 0.28–0.78) and fully adjusted model (OR = 0.33; 95% CI 0.17–0.61). In exploratory subgroup analyses, this association was evident in men and women as well as in subjects with overweight/obesity. Logistic regression revealed a graded pattern between each tertile increment of legumes intake and reduced odds of the HTGW phenotype. Moreover, more legumes intake was associated with better TyG index, even after adjustments for confounders. Higher intake of legumes was associated with decreased odds of HTGW phenotype and lower TyG scores among Iranian adults employed in school settings.

Article.Title: Safety assessment of a novel cold atmospheric pressure plasma multijet device for biomedical applications
Article.Authors: Ossowska A.; Zende R.; Bekeschus S.; Stancampiano A.; Robert E.; Emmert S.; Boeckmann L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cold atmospheric pressure plasma (CAP) is gaining attention in medicine for its antimicrobial and pro-proliferative effects in wound healing, and is emerging as a promising oncological therapy with high efficacy and minimal side effects. Current CAP technologies face distinct limitations on biological surfaces. Dielectric barrier discharge devices are difficult to apply to non-uniform surfaces due to variable electrode distance, while single-outlet plasma jets, though more suitable for irregular geometries, provide limited coverage and require prolonged treatment times. This study presents a safety assessment of a novel multijet CAP device, conducted in accordance with DIN SPEC 91315:2025-07. The helium-based system demonstrates consistent, treatment time-dependent surface coverage and low liquid evaporation, attributable to its low gas flow. Ex vivo, contactless temperature measurements showed that continuous manual treatment does not increase surface temperature beyond 40 °C. Electrical characterisation revealed a stable, controlled power profile modulated by input voltage and treatment distance. In vitro genotoxicity testing showed no chromosomal damage in HaCaT keratinocytes. Prolonged continuous exposure in confluent cultures caused minimal cytotoxicity, suggesting good tolerance up to three minutes at the 70% threshold. Overall, these findings demonstrate a safe, controllable plasma delivery platform for biological applications, supporting further development toward clinical translation.

Article.Title: Expert-derived influence structure and structural associations among resilience engineering indicators in an Iranian petrochemical complex: an integrated fuzzy DEMATEL–MMDE–SEM study
Article.Authors: Yeganeh R.; Ghasemi F.; Amiri A.; Shirali G.; Rashnoudi P.
Article.Abstract: Petrochemical operations are high-risk socio-technical systems in which resilience depends on monitoring, anticipating, responding, and learning. Yet interdependencies among resilience engineering indicators are rarely mapped and empirically evaluated by linking expert-derived influence structure with employee-based structural evidence. This study integrated fuzzy DEMATEL, MMDE, and covariance-based SEM to examine 12 resilience engineering indicators in an Iranian petrochemical complex. Judgments from 10 experts mapped the perceived influence network, while survey data from 343 employees evaluated the MMDE-retained relationships as prespecified structural associations. In the expert-derived DEMATEL network, management commitment, awareness, reporting culture, learning culture, teamwork, and buffering capacity occupied net-dispatching positions, whereas preparedness, flexibility, self-organization, redundancy, anticipation, and fault-tolerance occupied net-receiving positions. MMDE retained 10 of 132 candidate directed relationships for structural evaluation. The primary structural model yielded CFI = 0.959 and RMSEA = 0.027, and all 10 prespecified paths were positive and statistically significant. Awareness showed its strongest associations with self-organization and flexibility and showed significant model-based total associations with preparedness and fault-tolerance, including indirect associations through buffering capacity and flexibility. The findings characterize resilience in this petrochemical context as an interdependent configuration of informational, resource, and adaptive capabilities. Awareness and buffering capacity emerged as evidence-informed priorities, emphasizing operational information flow, usable resource margins, and preparedness for adaptive response rather than causally established interventions.

Article.Title: Graph convolutional network with dynamic gating LSTM improves corporate credit default prediction
Article.Authors: Li T.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Traditional corporate credit evaluation models often treat enterprises as isolated entities and rely on static financial data, making it difficult to capture dynamic risk evolution and inter-enterprise risk transmission. This study proposes a Graph-fused Multi-Modal Dynamic Gating Network (GMDG-Net) that integrates three information modalities: internal financial and market data, external online public opinion text, and an enterprise association graph constructed from equity pledge relationships. A graph convolutional network learns spatial risk transmission patterns from the association graph. A word vector model extracts sentiment features from public opinion text. A structural adaptive gating long short-term memory network dynamically fuses these multi-modal temporal features and adjusts contribution weights of different information sources in real time. Experiments using a corporate stock pledge default prediction dataset (2017–2022, 12,384 samples) show that GMDG-Net achieves an accuracy of 0.913 and F1-score of 0.851, significantly outperforming baseline models including support vector machine (0.842), standard LSTM (0.889), and graph convolutional network alone (0.872). Multi-modal feature fusion experiments confirm that adding public opinion features increases accuracy by 2.2%, and adding graph structural features further increases accuracy by 1.8%. The model maintains robust performance under imbalanced sample conditions (weighted F1-score 0.897). This framework provides financial institutions with a more accurate and forward-looking credit risk assessment tool.

Article.Title: Evolution of the vertical structure of heat waves in Europe at hourly resolution
Article.Authors: Plavcová E.; Lhotka O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We employ hourly temperature data at 19 pressure levels from the ERA5 reanalysis to investigate subdaily characteristics of four heat wave types, defined by their vertical cross-sections of temperature anomalies. Contrasting patterns between individual heat wave types in their subdaily development are shown for three European regions. The near-surface type is the only one associated with a gradual vertical build-up of positive temperature anomalies from the surface upwards. By contrast, the omnipresent heat wave type is characterised by a relatively rapid downward propagation of positive temperature anomalies from higher troposphere towards the surface. The downward propagation is less pronounced but still present for the remaining lower-tropospheric and higher-tropospheric heat wave types. We also analyse vertical stability in terms of lapse rates of potential temperature and show that the previously reported nighttime layers, characterised by lower lapse rates and decoupled from the surface, are typical for the near-surface heat wave type only. These layers are not present under the other heat wave types, even those associated also with positive near-surface temperature anomalies (lower-tropospheric and omnipresent). We conclude that the use of the data with high temporal and vertical resolution highlights different processes linked to individual heat wave types, pointing to a variety of heat wave drivers.

Article.Title: Generalizable full-spectrum learning for recalibration-free refractometry with reflection-mode tilted fiber Bragg gratings
Article.Authors: Uğurveren Y.; Chah K.; Han X.; Guo T.; Caucheteur C.
Article.Abstract: A tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG) is a powerful refractometric sensor, but its complex multimode spectrum demands rigorous demodulation and specialist expertise. Our convolutional learning pipeline converts these spectra directly into surrounding refractive index (SRI) estimates, making sophisticated TFBG sensors accessible to a much broader range of users. We evaluated an established preprocessing and convolutional learning pipeline on independently fabricated reflection-mode TFBG sensors at tilt angles of \(7^\circ \) and \(8^\circ \) , without calibrating or adapting the model to either independent test sensor. Four model-development sensors at each angle were used to establish the pipeline, and one independently fabricated test sensor at each angle was reserved for the final independent test. The pipeline used deterministic mode equalization, with its amplitude scale fixed from the training sensors, and five multiscale models based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in each training fold, using five random seeds. The results demonstrate spectral prediction across independent sensors and between the two measured tilt angles using a pipeline established entirely from the training sensors. Four additional sensors at \(6^\circ \) and \(9^\circ \) , angles absent from training, were also predicted without recalibration. These results provide a reproducible foundation for broader validation across additional fabrication batches of reflection-mode TFBG sensors.

Article.Authors: Asgari M.; Saber-Samandari S.; Haghdoost F.; Toghraie D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, numerous studies have investigated the use of polycaprolactone and eggshells in preparing bone tissue engineering scaffolds, owing to their outstanding load-bearing capacity and bone-regenerative activity. After characterizing the coated scaffolds, selected samples received a second coating layer via plasma treatment and electrospinning of a gelatin-hydroxyapatite solution. These surface modifications significantly reduced the contact angle and increased scaffold hydrophilicity. Additionally, MTT assays, bioactivity, and mechanical tests of the developed composite scaffold indicated excellent Cytocompatibility, high in vitro bioactivity, and favorable mechanical characteristics, attributed to the presence of gelatin, chitosan, hydroxyapatite, and polycaprolactone in its structure. Collectively, the developed scaffolds demonstrate osteoconductive, apatite-inducing, and pro-proliferative properties, positioning them as promising platforms for bone tissue engineering applications.

Article.Title: Dissecting content profiles and information quality of myocardial infarction related short videos: a cross-platform cross-sectional investigation
Article.Authors: Zhou M.; Jiang J.; Luo L.; Meng Z.
Article.Abstract: Short video platforms have become key channels for public health information. However, the quality of myocardial infarction (MI)‑related health content across major Chinese platforms remains poorly characterized. This study characterized the content features, informational credibility, and dissemination patterns of MI-related videos on major short video platforms in China. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted from December 14 to 19, 2025, on TikTok, Rednote, and WeChat. Approximately 200 videos were initially retrieved for each platform. Two reviewers independently assessed videos using JAMA criteria, Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN, and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT). Multivariable robust‑Poisson regression and sensitivity analysis excluding top 1% engagement outliers were applied to handle over-dispersed engagement outcomes. Data were analyzed using R and GraphPad Prism. After exclusion criteria were applied, a total of 485 videos were analyzed. TikTok videos had significantly higher raw observed engagement metrics (likes, comments, collections) than those on WeChat and Rednote (all P < 0.001). Multivariable regression confirmed most of these platform‑related engagement differences, although the apparent sharing advantage of TikTok disappeared after outlier exclusion in sensitivity analysis. Rednote had a higher proportion of videos by junior and intermediate physicians ( P < 0.001). MI‑related educational videos were geographically concentrated in economically‑developed provinces. TikTok videos scored higher on JAMA but lower on GQS and DISCERN compared to other platforms; Rednote scored higher on DISCERN than WeChat. No significant differences were found between physician seniority groups on JAMA, GQS, DISCERN, or PEMAT understandability. However, junior and intermediate physicians scored higher on PEMAT actionability than senior physicians. MI-related video content varies in quality and engagement, with educational resources concentrated in developed regions. Findings underscore the need for stronger content governance and greater involvement of medical professionals in creating actionable health education to enhance public MI awareness.
