Article.Title: Bacterial etiologies, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and multidrug resistance trends among patients with sterile body site infections in Northwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Assefa M.; Tigabie M.; Tesfa A.; Smineh F.; Worku T.; Shferaw Y.; Worku M.; Mesfin Y.; Girmay G.; Almagharbeh W.; Cherie N.
Article.Abstract: Sterile body site (SBS) bacterial infections are one of the most critical problems in hospital settings. The rise of antimicrobial resistance and empirical treatment of SBS infections without local up-to-date evidence have led to higher patient mortality, representing a research gap in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the bacterial distribution, their antimicrobial resistance patterns, multidrug resistance (MDR) trends, and associated factors in SBS infections at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized and Referral Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia. A retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among patients with SBS infection at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized and Referral Hospital. The Kobo data collection tool was used to extract laboratory records from September 2021 to May 2026 (five years) using a consecutive sampling technique. Sterile body fluid samples were collected and inoculated onto blood agar, chocolate agar, MacConkey agar, and mannitol salt agar plates. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the modified Kirby-Bauer disc-diffusion method. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26 software. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test assumptions, and logistic regression models were applied. Bivariate logistic regression results with a p-value < 0.25 were entered into multivariate analysis to control for potential confounding factors. To assess associations between dependent and independent variables, a p-value < 0.05 in multivariate analysis was considered statistically significant at the 95% confidence level. Study findings were presented using tables and charts. A total of 1,368 study participants were included in this study, consisting of 678 (49.6%) males and 690 (50.4%) females. The prevalence of culture-confirmed bacterial SBS infection was 5.48% (95% CI: 4.38%-6.83%), with 75 bacterial isolates identified. No mixed bacterial infections were detected in any patient. There was a high prevalence of Gram-negative bacteria (88.0%, n = 66), while 12.0% ( n = 9) were Gram-positive bacteria. E. coli (33.3%, n = 25) and K. pneumoniae (26.7%, n = 20) were the most predominant pathogens causing SBS infection. Gram-negative bacterial isolates demonstrated resistance to commonly used antibiotics such as ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and ampicillin. An overall prevalence of MDR was 17.3% (13/75), with K . pneumoniae (35%, n = 6), Non-Lactose Fermenting Gram-Negative Rods (28.6%, n = 2), and E. coli (16%, n = 4). Being male ( p = 0.011) and study years 2025/26 ( p < 0.001), 2024/25 ( p < 0.001), and 2023/24 ( p = 0.020) were significantly associated with bacterial SBS infection. In this study, Gram-negative bacteria were the most common cause of SBS infection, with MDR E. coli and K. pneumoniae being frequently identified isolates. Over the five-year trend, a higher MDR rate was observed in 2024/25 (46.2%), with K. pneumoniae exhibiting a high MDR rate in 2024/25 (71.4%); p = 0.03, and the prevalence of MDR E. coli peaked at 50% during 2022/23 and 2024/25 tracking periods. This study highlights the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance surveillance and molecular detection of resistance mechanisms.

Salmonella prevalence using invA and pagC in parallel was 63.3% with and 57.5% without pre-enrichment, respectively, while prevalence calculated in series was 28.3 and 17.5%, respectively. Gwet’s AC1 coefficients showed that Salmonella prevalence in series without pre-enrichment had the highest agreement with prevalence in culture at 82.5% (probabilistic benchmark interval: 60–80%). Our results indicate that this platform is an effective tool for the detection of Salmonella in cattle feces without the need for pre-enrichment.

Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Taha E.; Soliman S.

The first strategy employed UV–Vis spectroscopy combined with Partial Least Squares (PLS), Genetic Algorithm-PLS (GA-PLS), and Multivariate Curve Resolution–Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS), whereas the second employed first-derivative Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy using zero-crossing wavenumbers. Validation mixtures were designed using Latin Hypercube Sampling to provide systematic coverage of the investigated concentration space. First-derivative preprocessing was applied to enhance spectral resolution and minimize baseline effects. The UV–Vis spectra in the range of 222–263 nm and FTIR spectra in the range of 4000–400 cm⁻¹ were used for quantitative analysis. Among the investigated UV–Vis chemometric models, MCR-ALS provided the lowest root mean square errors of calibration and prediction, with RMSEC and RMSEP values of 0.0359 and 0.0329 for TBM and 0.0622 and 0.0375 for OLH, respectively. The developed models provided recoveries of approximately 100%, with precision expressed as RSD values below 2%. Application to the commercial formulation produced satisfactory recoveries ranging from 98% to 101% for both drugs using the developed techniques. Statistical comparison with the reference HPLC method showed no significant differences at the 95% confidence level. Overall, the complementary UV–Vis chemometric and ATR-FTIR approaches provided satisfactory quantitative performance for the simultaneous determination of TBM and OLH within the investigated analytical ranges.

Article.Title: Field-compatible tissue cryopreservation enables delayed endothelial cell culture
Article.Authors: Allen K.; Burns J.; Vázquez-Medina J.; den Heyer C.; Shero M.
Article.Abstract: Decades of biomedical research have developed robust tools in molecular and cell biology, including cell culture systems, for model vertebrate species. Logistical constraints associated with remote fieldwork limit the application of these techniques to non-model species. Traditionally, cell culture requires tissue collection from live or very recently deceased animals, followed by immediate sterile processing and cell isolation, but these requirements are often impractical in field settings. To address this limitation, we developed a field-compatible method to cryopreserve arterial tissue from pinnipeds for delayed endothelial cell isolation. Grey seal placentae were opportunistically collected, and arteries were preserved using benchtop blunt dissection and a portable ​​-80 °C freezer with a standard cell freezing medium. Samples were held in a portable ​-80 °C freezer for ~ 2 months before transfer to LN 2 vapor storage for ~ 1 month, followed by endothelial cell isolation. Cells isolated from cryopreserved arteries are phenotypically endothelial, proliferate in culture and are the first endothelial cell cultures derived from grey seals. Grey seal endothelial cells respire after culture expansion, and ATP production rates are ~ 1.5×​​ greater than those in freshly derived endothelial cell cultures from a related species, though the relative contributions of OXPHOS and glycolysis were comparable between cell preparations. This method is practical for field researchers and supports the generation of primary cell cultures weeks-to-months after initial tissue collection with minimal resources, strengthening the ability to investigate the cellular basis of physiological phenomena in the natural world.

Article.Title: miR-20a promotes cell proliferation and migration by targeting DLC1 in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Mao Y.; Xu R.; Lu H.; Zhou Y.; Bao L.; Zhong L.; Wang P.; Ren C.; Feng X.
Article.Abstract: The role of miR-20a in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and its relationship with the tumor suppressor DLC1 remain incompletely understood. DLC1 knockdown attenuated the inhibitory effects of miR-20a inhibition on colony formation and migration and counteracted associated protein changes. These findings support DLC1 as a functional mediator of miR-20a-associated malignant phenotypes in NPC and provide a rationale for further preclinical investigation of the miR-20a/DLC1 axis.

Article.Title: Quality characteristics of frozen horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) treated with starch–glycerol coatings containing plant extracts
Article.Authors: Gurdal A.; Caglak E.
Article.Abstract: Starch-based coatings are biodegradable food-contact materials, but their performance depends on plasticizer level, incorporated active compounds, and the food surface to which they are applied. This study developed starch-glycerol polysaccharide coating formulations containing aqueous extracts from persimmon fruit calyces, cherry laurel leaves, and bilberry/likapa leaves and evaluated their application to whole horse mackerel ( Trachurus trachurus ) during frozen storage at -20 ± 2 °C for 6 months. Extract-level antioxidant activity was determined by the DPPH assay and expressed as percentage inhibition and Trolox equivalent antioxidant capacity. Comparable starch-glycerol films containing the same plant extracts had previously been characterized by Gurdal and Caglak and were used here only as formulation-characterization background. During frozen storage, TVB-N values increased but remained below 35 mg/100 g in all groups. Lipid oxidation responses were formulation-dependent: the lowest final TBA values were observed in PA and PB, whereas BA and VC showed the highest final values. pH, water activity, color, texture, and microbial results varied among treatments and storage months without supporting a uniform concentration-dependent response. The findings suggest that selected starch-glycerol formulations containing plant extracts may help modulate lipid oxidation and quality changes in frozen horse mackerel. However, the absence of a plain starch-glycerol-coated fish control, coating-uptake measurements, compound-level extract characterization, and composite-film antioxidant testing limits direct attribution of the observed effects to specific bioactive mechanisms.

Article.Title: Storying digital well-being and quality of life in Ghanaian adult learners’ use of generative AI
Article.Authors: Adarkwah M.; Kayi E.; Oduro F.; Osei-Tutu A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in higher education; however, little is known about what its use means for adult learners’ digital well-being (DWB) and quality of life (QoL). This mixed-methods study, which leaned towards a qualitative design (qualitative dominant), investigated these issues among adult learners at a university in Ghana. The quantitative phase involved 212 randomly selected respondents, while six (6) participants were purposively selected for the qualitative phase. The survey findings showed that overall DWB was above the midpoint of the 7-point Likert scale (M = 4.58, SD = 0.76). The mental (M = 4.09, SD = 1.12), emotional (M = 4.51, SD = 1.29), and reverse-coded physical (M = 5.14, SD = 1.45) subscales indicated generally positive perceptions of digital well-being. However, item-level responses showed that a notable minority of participants still reported physical challenges, including disturbed sleep, changes in eating habits, physical discomfort, and reduced physical exercise associated with GenAI use. QoL was measured using a 3-point substantive scale, with two non-substantive response options excluded from scoring. The QoL mean (M = 2.06, SD = 0.94) indicated modest gains in safety, control, activity engagement, and time efficiency. A digital storytelling analysis of the participants’ experiences revealed that the adults held ambivalent views about GenAI, reflecting both appreciation for its efficiency and anxiety over its encroachment on human creativity and authenticity. The coping strategies adopted included developing a critical distance and self-awareness, re-engaging human connection and support networks, mindful regulation and intentional use, and transforming frustration into learning. It is recommended that adult educators prioritise the digital safety of adult learners.

Article.Title: NPSBZn fertilizer rate and variety effects on carrot yield, quality, and soil acidity in the central highlands of Ethiopia: a two-year field trial
Article.Authors: Manore D.; Watumo T.; Bosha A.
Article.Abstract: Carrot (Daucus carota L.) is a valuable vegetable crop in Ethiopia, yet national average yields remain low due to soil nutrient deficiencies, unbalanced fertilizer use, and limited access to improved varieties. Most existing research is single-season, which limits the robustness of fertilizer recommendations across varying climatic conditions. Additionally, the recently introduced blended NPSBZn fertilizer lacks crop- and site-specific recommendations. To address these gaps, a two-year (2020–2021) field experiment was conducted in the Hadiya Zone, central Ethiopia. Two carrot varieties (Nantes and Haramaya I) were subjected to seven NPSBZn rates (0 to 150 kg ha⁻¹) in a randomized complete block design with three replications. Across both years, Nantes consistently outperformed Haramaya I in stand count, mean root weight, marketable yield, total soluble solids (TSS), and β-carotene content, while Haramaya I produced longer but often cracked roots. Increasing NPSBZn rates from 0 to 150 kg ha⁻¹ steadily improved all yield and quality parameters, with no plateau observed at the highest rate. Marketable yield reached 38.5 t ha⁻¹ in Nantes at 150 kg ha⁻¹, with marginal returns exceeding 1200%. However, soil pH declined from 5.94 to 5.56, indicating progressive acidification likely due to nitrification of ammoniacal nitrogen from urea and NPSBZn fertilizers. We conclude that NPSBZn fertilization at 150 kg ha⁻¹ combined with the Nantes variety is economically viable and agronomically superior in the short term, but integrated soil management including liming or organic amendments is required to mitigate long-term acidification and sustain soil health.

Article.Title: PLVAP promoter knock-in iPS cells for tracking endothelial-like differentiation and angiogenic activity in ischemic models
Article.Authors: Zhe Z.; Han S.; Kim S.
Article.Abstract: Differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS) into endothelial cells is now technically feasible, but it remains difficult to follow, in a quantitative manner, when and how these cells acquire mature endothelial characteristics. In this study, we investigated whether inserting a reporter driven by the plasmalemma vesicle–associated protein (PLVAP) promoter into human iPS could be used to visualize endothelial-like differentiation and pro-angiogenic activity. We generated a PLVAP promoter reporter knock-in iPS line and directed these cells toward an endothelial lineage to obtain induced endothelial cells (iEC). Endothelial identity and function were examined by qRT-PCR, protein-level characterization, in vitro Matrigel tube formation assays, functional NO production assays, and an in vivo Matrigel plug assay. We further evaluated the therapeutic performance of iEC in a murine hindlimb ischemia (HLI) model. Protein-level characterization further confirmed that iEC express and exhibit a pharmacologically regulated, eNOS-dependent NO response to the antagonist L-NAME and the agonist VEGF-A. Matrigel plugs containing iEC showed markedly higher red blood cell infiltration than plugs containing undifferentiated iPS. In the HLI model, iEC transplantation improved perfusion recovery and reduced limb loss compared with iPS injection. Histology revealed increased capillary density and elevated angiogenic cytokine expression in iEC-treated muscles, and transplanted iEC displayed endothelial-like phenotypes within ischemic tissue, consistent with in vivo vascular incorporation. The PLVAP promoter knock-in reporter provides a platform to enrich and functionally evaluate iPSC-derived endothelial-like populations with strong angiogenic and regenerative activity. These findings suggest that a PLVAP promoter–driven reporter can be used to refine and functionally evaluate iPS-derived endothelial-like cell products with strong pro-angiogenic properties in ischemic models and to support the development of cell-based therapies for ischemic cardiovascular disease.

Article.Title: Sequence fidelity of large language models in trauma primary survey: a comparative in silico study of spontaneous xABCDE-consistent prioritisation
Article.Authors: Koç M.; Kaya H.; Güven F.; Köksal A.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for clinical decision support, but trauma care requires not only correct actions but also appropriate prioritisation. We assessed whether three LLMs spontaneously generated trauma-management actions in an xABCDE-consistent order and whether specialty-based system prompts affected prioritisation. Ten investigator-developed polytrauma cases were submitted to GPT-4.1-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Claude Haiku 4.5 under five prompt conditions. The prompt requested six brief clinical actions without mentioning xABCDE or any predefined trauma algorithm. This generated 150 unique model-case-persona queries, each repeated once. Sequence disorder occurred in at least one run in 109/150 queries (72.7%; 95% CI 65.0–79.2) and in both runs in 101/150 (67.3%), with high inter-run agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.873). At-least-one-run disorder occurred in 17/50 GPT-4.1-mini, 43/50 Gemini and 49/50 Claude queries. In both cases requiring immediate external haemorrhage control, no model placed haemorrhage control first in any condition or run. Persona-related advancement occurred in 3/90 eligible queries, whereas premature secondary-care recommendations occurred in 84/150. These findings suggest that sequence fidelity may provide a useful process-oriented safety measure when evaluating LLMs for sequence-dependent emergency-care tasks.

Article.Title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
Article.Authors: Kodukhov A.; Pastushenko V.; Pflitsch M.; Vinokur V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel. In this study, we demonstrate that additional quantum effects and techniques can improve the performance of quantum cryptography while maintaining everlasting security. In particular, we study the recently introduced loss control-based QKD approach, which relies on the physical properties of optical fiber channels associated with Rayleigh scattering and on continuous monitoring of channel integrity. We show that achieving everlasting and future-proof security requires an additional assumption concerning the completeness of the mathematical description of the devices and, consequently, of the eavesdropper’s ensemble. Furthermore, we introduce a security statement framework that combines physical assumptions about a cryptographic implementation with formal mathematical security proofs. Applying this framework to loss control-based QKD, we derive the eavesdropper’s ensemble for an arbitrary number of local attack points and define channel-dependent QKD as a new class of QKD protocols. Finally, we propose a general criterion for identifying quantum cryptographic solutions based on whether the physical mechanism underlying security disappears in the classical limit.

Article.Title: NCOA1 and PRPS1 as novel metabolism-related biomarkers in myocardial ischemia–reperfusion injury
Article.Authors: Liu T.; Kong J.; Huang Z.; Zhong Y.; Lu J.; Cao Y.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: Mitochondrial metabolism (MM) plays a critical role in myocardial ischemia–reperfusion injury (MIRI), yet reliable metabolism-related biomarkers for this condition remain largely unexplored. Here, we integrated transcriptomic datasets from public repositories with MM-related gene sets to identify candidate biomarkers in MIRI. Through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression profiling, and two machine learning algorithms (SVM-RFE and Boruta), we screened candidate genes and validated their expression in both independent GEO cohorts and clinical whole-blood samples via RT-qPCR. Two candidate biomarkers, NCOA1 and PRPS1 , were consistently identified and validated, showing opposing expression patterns in MIRI versus controls. Immune infiltration analysis revealed significant correlations between the estimated abundance of M0 macrophages and both candidate biomarkers, indicating an association between these molecular and immune-related features. Pathway enrichment analyses further identified associations with ribosomal function and nucleotide metabolism, providing potential directions for further mechanistic investigation. Notably, molecular docking yielded moderate docking scores for the predicted biomarker–drug pairs, including NCOA1–methylthioninium and PRPS1–thioguanine, warranting further experimental evaluation. Collectively, our findings identify NCOA1 and PRPS1 as candidate metabolism-related biomarkers selected through an MRG-based screening framework, which warrant further validation in larger independent cohorts and mechanistic studies.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence and green supply chain management in Chinese listed firms
Article.Authors: Jiang E.; Cheng Q.; Jiang H.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may support green supply chain management (GSCM) by improving information processing and organizational coordination. Using 30,571 Chinese A-share firm-year observations from 2016 to 2024, this study examines the relationship between AI-related disclosure and GSCM-related disclosure. The results reveal a significant positive association: firms with more intensive AI-related disclosure also exhibit higher levels of GSCM-related disclosure. This association persists across alternative measures, firm fixed effects and matched-sample regressions. A non-text proxy based on machinery and equipment value per employee provides additional sensitivity evidence. Exploratory analyses link AI-related disclosure to greater green patenting, stronger ESG performance, shorter implied asset-turnover period and higher total factor productivity, suggesting potential organizational explanations for the observed relationship. The association is also stronger among state-owned firms and firms in heavily polluting industries. These findings contribute firm-level evidence on the relationship between AI and GSCM and highlight the relevance of organizational performance dimensions.

Article.Title: Nitrate enrichment of larval habitats enhances physiological resilience and reduces insecticide susceptibility in Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) mosquito
Article.Authors: Bala E.; Ukubuiwe A.; Ukubuiwe C.; Ossamulu I.; Abubakar Z.; Olayemi I.
Article.Abstract: Although nitrate is one of the most common fertiliser-derived contaminants in mosquito habitats, its public-health implications for mosquito development and insecticide susceptibility remain poorly understood. This study examined how nitrate enrichment influences biological traits that directly affect vector proliferation and the effectiveness of insecticide-based control strategies. Larvae were reared across a gradient of nitrate concentrations (0–1024 mg/L) and monitored through emergence. Developmental outcomes (duration of immature stages, survivorship, larval growth rate), metabolic reserves (lipid, protein, glycogen, glucose), susceptibility to permethrin (0.75%), and detoxification enzyme activity (esterases, glutathione S-transferase) were estimated following standard procedures. High nitrate concentrations significantly prolonged larval and pupal development, while survivorship remained high (> 90%). Larval growth rate peaked at moderate enrichment (16 mg/L). All metabolic reserves increased with nitrate exposure, indicating improved physiological condition. Importantly, nitrate-reared mosquitoes exhibited substantially reduced susceptibility to permethrin and elevated detoxification enzyme activity. These findings highlight nitrate pollution as an overlooked environmental driver that can enhance mosquito robustness and reduce the efficacy of insecticide-based interventions. As nutrient runoff intensifies with agricultural expansion, integrating environmental nutrient management into vector-control planning may be essential for sustaining the impact of current dengue and arbovirus prevention strategies.

Article.Title: Hepatic transcriptome, intestinal microbiome, and metabolite profiles associated with MASLD, MASH, and fibrosis in patients undergoing bariatric surgery
Article.Authors: Ghorbani Y.; Schwenger K.; Teterina A.; Liu Y.; Lou W.; Comelli E.; Fischer S.; Jackson T.; Okrainec A.; Allard J.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is prevalent in obesity and can progress to steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, cirrhosis and liver failure. The intestinal microbiome (IM) and metabolites may play a role in MASLD severity but their potential relationships with the hepatic transcriptome are not clear. Patients with MASH had higher expression of genes related to immune system, inflammation, cancer and apoptosis, higher Blautia species and lower Faecalibacterium prausnitzii , Bacteroides dorei , and Coprococcus species. Patients with severe fibrosis had higher expression of extracellular matrix-related genes and higher Collinsella stercoris . Significant associations were identified between differentially expressed genes in the liver, mainly related to growth, proliferation, metabolism and immune system, and bacterial taxa, especially B. dorei and F. prausnitzii , and fecal/serum metabolites (e.g. primary bile acids and acylcarnitines). Our findings demonstrate that fecal bacterial taxa as well as serum and fecal metabolites are associated with hepatic transcriptome according to MASLD severity. However, when adjusted for covariates known to be associated with MASLD definition or severity, these associations did not remain significant. Nonetheless, these interactions may suggest potential pathways and treatment targets requiring further study.

Article.Title: The hidden impact of cage position on behavioral phenotyping and reproducibility
Article.Authors: Keidan L.; Sasonov L.; Pick C.; Bikovski L.
Article.Abstract: Cage position within an animal-room rack is among the most routine housing decisions, yet it shapes both ambient illumination and husbandry contact. We asked whether this alone, in naive, untreated mice, alters adult behavior. Male and female ICR mice were housed from birth to adulthood on the uppermost or lowermost rack shelf. Lower-shelf mice left the dark compartment of the light-dark box faster, the only difference surviving correction, and showed less risk-assessment behavior in the elevated plus maze in both cohorts. Spatial memory, locomotor activity, nociception and ultrasound-measured optic nerve diameter showed no detectable difference, despite 70 versus 20 lx in-cage illumination. Lower-shelf mice showed greater novel-object preference, but not once cage clustering was modeled. Here, we show that cage position is associated with altered exploratory behavior in animals given no experimental manipulation, potentially identifying a hidden confounder that counterbalancing can remove.

Article.Title: Test-retest reliability of resting-state functional connectivity: a methodological investigation with implications for aggression research
Article.Authors: Beser-Robles M.; Cerdá‑Alberich L.; Aparici F.; Sarrate‑Costa C.; Moya‑Albiol L.; Martí‑Bonmatí L.; Romero‑Martínez Á.
Article.Abstract: The temporal stability of resting-state functional MR connectivity (rsfMRc) is a fundamental methodological consideration for longitudinal neuroimaging research, yet systematic evaluations across clinically relevant time frames remain limited. This study examined test-retest reliability of rsfMRc over short-term (1 h) and medium-term (1 month) intervals in 34 healthy young adult males across three sessions. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and matrix-wide reliability metrics were calculated to evaluate temporal stability across major brain networks, and associations between stable connectivity patterns and aggression measures were examined. Overall reliability showed moderate values (mean ICC = 0.566) with significant network-specific variation. Salience Network regions, particularly the supramarginal gyrus, and lateral parietal regions of the Default Mode Network demonstrated the highest stability (ICC > 0.600). Matrix-wide analyses indicated high consistency in connectivity rankings (Kendall’s W = 0.798). Among the 23 most temporally stable regions, five connections showed systematic associations with reactive aggression across sessions; none survived FDR correction, consistent with the non-aggressive nature of the cohort. These findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in rsfMRc reliability across brain networks and measurement intervals, providing empirical guidance for researchers planning longitudinal connectivity studies. Network-specific considerations are critical in study design, and importantly, reliability estimates from this healthy homogeneous sample represent upper-bound values not directly transferable to clinical populations, where greater symptom heterogeneity and state fluctuations are expected to reduce temporal stability. Within these constraints, identifying stable connectivity patterns through reliability-informed frameworks provides a proof-of-concept for future individual-differences research, while regions with poor reliability require methodological optimization before serving as measurement targets.

Article.Title: DnaB mutants suppress DciA essentiality in Thermus thermophilus and uncover its role in recombination-dependent replication
Article.Authors: Gost M.; Failde-Soler M.; Silva de Sousa B.; Quiles S.; Herrero P.; Gómez-Campo C.; Carrasco B.; Blesa A.; Alonso J.; Mencía M.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial DNA replication is initiated by assembling two hexameric replicative DnaB helicases at the DnaA-unwound oriC region, a process that requires a cognate helicase loader, DciA, DnaC, or DnaI. DnaB M375I expression is necessary and sufficient to sustain replication in otherwise wild-type Δ dciA cells. In vitro, DciA interacts with DnaB and its mutant variants. DnaB efficiently unwinds 3’-forked DNA and this activity is restrained by DciA through inhibition of DnaB’s ATPase and helicase functions. Notably, the combined loss of the RRD and the recombination proteins RecO or RecR is lethal. Together, these results establish DciA as the replicative helicase loader in Deinococcota and reveal a functional link between DNA replication and homologous recombination.

Article.Authors: Jiang S.; Za’ba N.; Hussin T.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a capacity-equivalent framework for selecting circular, square, and rectangular deep cement mixing (DCM) columns for a soft-soil bridge foundation when pier load varies in service. Sixty-three three-dimensional ABAQUS cases covered replacement ratios from 0.30 to 0.50; selected circular and rectangular cases were then evaluated at five loads from 180 to 240 kN. The model used Mohr-Coulomb soil and linear-elastic DCM and cushion idealizations and was checked against a layered-summation solution and one field settlement measurement at 196 kN. The finite-element settlement differed by 3.4% from the analytical value and by 14.5% from the field measurement. At m = 0.30, circular, square, and rectangular configurations produced settlements of 25.44, 27.78, and 32.41 mm, respectively; the rectangular configuration used the least cement-treated soil (3.60 m³). Increasing m generally shortened the design-dependent column and reduced equivalent-stress demand but increased cement-treated volume, so settlement did not change monotonically. Range-averaged normalized settlement sensitivities were 0.454 and 1.109 for the circular and rectangular cases, while the corresponding equivalent-stress sensitivities were 0.877 and 0.638. The framework shows that capacity compliance, settlement, relative stress demand, material use, and load adaptability can favor different geometries. The findings remain site- and model-specific because groundwater, consolidation, nonlinear DCM behavior, and full mesh and boundary sensitivity studies were not included.

Article.Title: Exact nonlinear wave structures in the conformable time-fractional Vakhnenko equation via bilinear neural networks
Article.Authors: Zidan A.; Shafee A.; Sanaee H.; Iqbal N.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a conformable bilinear neural network framework for constructing exact nonlinear wave solutions of the conformable time-fractional Vakhnenko equation (CTFVE), a model of high-frequency wave motion in a relaxing medium in which the fractional order acts as a tunable time-scale parameter. By introducing a logarithmic dependent-variable transformation and a generalized Hirota bilinear operator compatible with the conformable fractional derivative, the governing fractional equation is recast in bilinear form. Several feedforward neural network structures with one and two hidden layers are then employed as structured ansätze for the bilinear auxiliary function, and the resulting algebraic systems are solved in closed form. This yields the integrable solution families of the Vakhnenko equation—the one-soliton, the two-soliton with its exact phase shift, the breather formed from a complex-conjugate soliton pair, and the cnoidal periodic wave—each verified symbolically against both the bilinear form and the original nonlinear equation. We show that the fractional order is physically equivalent to an algebraically time-varying relaxation rate of the medium, which makes the wave structures propagate with a power-law (decelerating for \(\epsilon <1\) ) speed while preserving their amplitude and width, and a numerical perturbation analysis confirms that the soliton is orbitally stable. Because the solutions are obtained in closed algebraic form, the method avoids the discretization and convergence errors of iterative schemes. The framework offers a flexible analytical route to coherent structures in fractional evolution equations and extends naturally to related nonlinear wave models.

Article.Title: DirectHF-DA integrates a lightweight network and multi-resolution STFT-RGB for edge-deployable cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhu C.; Yu K.; Zheng L.; Wu M.; Ruan C.; Tie J.
Article.Abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions is challenged by domain distribution shifts and the high computational cost of deep models on resource-constrained edge devices. To address these coupled challenges, this study proposes DirectHF-DA, a directional high-frequency domain-adaptive network for lightweight cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis. First, a compact multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform representation (MR-STFT-RGB) is constructed by deterministically organizing short-, medium-, and long-window STFT spectrograms into a standard three-channel tensor, enabling complementary transient, modulation, and harmonic information to be jointly processed by a single lightweight backbone. Next, a lightweight feature extractor, DirectHF-Net, is developed by integrating directional depthwise separable convolution (DDSConv), directional residual refinement and transition blocks (DRRB/DRTB), and a high-frequency enhancement block (HFEB), thereby preserving fault-sensitive directional textures and high-frequency impact features with low computational complexity. Joint maximum mean discrepancy (JMMD) is further introduced to align the joint distributions of the source and target domains, enabling effective adaptation to unlabeled target operating conditions. Experiments on 12 cross-domain transfer tasks using the CWRU and HUST bearing datasets achieve average diagnostic accuracies of \(99.70\pm 0.05\%\) and \(92.31\pm 1.02\%\) , respectively. DirectHF-DA contains only 1.6 M parameters, requires 0.22 GFLOPs, and has a model size of 6.22 MB. When deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super, the proposed model achieves real-time inference throughputs of 60.54 FPS and 61.71 FPS on the CWRU and HUST tasks, respectively. These results demonstrate that DirectHF-DA achieves a favorable balance among cross-domain diagnostic accuracy, computational efficiency, and real-time edge inference capability.

Article.Authors: Alsaidy M.; Tahmasebpoor M.; Ateeq A.
Article.Abstract: Activated carbon (AC) derived from a mixture of walnut and almond shells was prepared via phosphoric acid activation (ACA) and subsequently combined with ZIF-67 to fabricate a series of ACA/ZIF-67 composite adsorbents for removing dye contaminants from water. Comprehensive characterization (including FESEM, EDS, FTIR, XRD, and N 2 adsorption–desorption) confirmed the integration of ZIF-67 within the carbon matrix. The results demonstrated that the highest BET surface area (592.43 m 2 . g − 1 ) belongs to the ACA5/ZIF-67 composite with a hierarchical porous structure. The effects of operational parameters, including ACA/ZIF-67 ratio, pH (1–11), amount of adsorbent (0.1–2 g/L), time (5–60 min), initial dye concentration (10–100 mg/L), and operational temperature (25–45 °C), were systematically investigated. Under the optimum conditions of pH 7, temperature of 25 °C, and the amount of adsorbent 1.5 g/L, the ACA5/ZIF-67 composite achieved more than 98% removal of 10 mg/L MB within only 5 min. Equilibrium and kinetic data were satisfactorily well-fitted to the Langmuir isotherm (R² > 0.99) and the pseudo-second-order kinetic (R 2 = 0.9999) models, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of 35.95 mg/g. This adsorption behavior can be attributed to the combined effects of pore filling, electrostatic attraction, π–π interactions, and hydrogen bonding between dye molecules and the ACA5/ZIF-67 surface. Consequently, these outcomes highlight the potential of biomass-derived AC/ZIF-67 composites as favorable adsorbents for the simulated removal of dyes from aqueous solutions, subject to further assessment in real industrial effluents.

Article.Title: Deciphering salinity tolerance during germination in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L) through systematic phenotypic screening
Article.Authors: Teku T.; Mekonnen T.; Bayissa K.; Hora O.; Woldesemayat A.
Article.Abstract: Wheat is the major staple crop contributing about 20% of global calorie intake and ranks second to maize in worldwide production. It is vital to increase the production of wheat by about 70% by 2050 to feed world population. However, soil salinity is a critical constraint that impairs plant growth and development during germination stage. Therefore, identifying salt-tolerant bread wheat genotypes at germination stages is critical for mitigating yield losses. This study aimed to evaluate and identify wheat genotypes with superior germination performance under salinity stress. To achieve this objective, a comprehensive study was performed on 153 Ethiopian bread wheat genotypes obtained from Holeta agricultural research center. Seeds of each genotype were treated under four salinity levels for eight days. The results demonstrated that salinity stress had a significant effect on all measured 17 traits. Salinity markedly reduced growth parameters (SL, RL, SH, SFW, SDW, RFW and RDW), physiological traits (SRWC and RRWC), and germination indices (GP, GVI, SI), which showed strong correlations with salt tolerance. In contrast, mean germination time (MGT), time to 50% germination (T50), and shoot height reduction (SHR) increased under salinity stress. The substantial genotypic variation observed among the 153 Ethiopian bread wheat genotypes under salinity stress indicates the presence of valuable genetic diversity for salinity tolerance at the germination stage, providing promising resources for breeding salt-tolerant wheat cultivars.

Article.Title: Deep learning–based object detection for automated classification of ripe and unripe tomatoes in field conditions
Article.Authors: Hassanzadeh L.; Pourdarbani R.; Sabzi S.; Daliran O.; Molina-Martínez J.; García-Mateos G.; García-Berná A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate detection of tomatoes at different ripening stages from close-range remote sensing imagery acquired under real field conditions is a key enabler for yield estimation, harvest scheduling, and selective robotic picking in precision agriculture. However, achieving reliable performance is challenging due to occlusions, variable illumination, dense foliage, and the limited size of domain-specific datasets typically available to small farms and research teams. In this work, we present a controlled comparative study between two representative object detection paradigms, Faster R-CNN with a ResNet-50 FPN backbone (two-stage) and YOLO26s (single-stage), on a curated dataset of 367 high-resolution images acquired in a commercial cherry-tomato greenhouse under natural illumination, containing more than 8,900 manually annotated tomatoes across three classes: blossom, premature, and ripe. Both models were trained for 100 epochs under a controlled protocol sharing the same data, stratified 70/15/15 split complemented by 5-fold cross-validation, and evaluated using COCO-style AP/AR together with per-class precision–recall and ROC analyses. YOLO26s achieved a macro-average AP of 0.741 and ROC AUC of 0.954 on the held-out test split, substantially outperforming Faster R-CNN (macro AP 0.241; ROC AUC 0.836), particularly under stricter localization thresholds, and qualitative examples confirm that localization rather than classification is the main bottleneck of Faster R-CNN. These results provide actionable guidelines for deploying detectors on small agricultural remote sensing datasets in fixed monitoring stations and on ground or aerial autonomous platforms, where tighter bounding boxes and a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off are decisive for reliable operation.

Article.Title: Coupling between structural evolution and glass transition in supercooled water
Article.Authors: Kocherbitov V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water exhibits unique structural, thermodynamic, and dynamic anomalies, particularly in supercooled states where structural evolution between high- and low-density liquid environments occurs alongside kinetic arrest. Here we use molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P/2005 model of water with cooling and heating scan rates from 10 to 3000 K µs⁻¹ to investigate equilibrium and nonequilibrium behavior. Above ~ 220 K, properties are scan-rate independent, indicating equilibrium, while below this temperature kinetic effects dominate on the simulations time scale, reflecting glassy dynamics. In the liquid regime, the temperature dependence of viscosity reveals two relaxation mechanisms with distinct activation energies. The rapid slowing down of the lower-temperature mechanism leads to the onset of the glass transition. At the cooling and heating rates accessible to the present simulations, the glass transition occurs in the same temperature range as the heat-capacity maximum associated with the gradual structural evolution between high- and low-density liquid environments. By integrating a two-state thermodynamic model with the Tool–Narayanaswamy–Moynihan glass-transition framework, we separate equilibrium anomalies from kinetic glass-transition effects. This combined structural evolution – glass transition (SE-GT) approach provides a consistent description of water’s coupled thermodynamic and dynamic behavior across a broad temperature range.

Article.Title: A fuzzy DEMATEL–ISM framework for unpacking barriers to digital twin adoption in high-density crowd management
Article.Authors: Miski A.; Bafail O.
Article.Abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology promises to revolutionize the management of large gatherings by coupling physical assets with their virtual counterparts to enable real–time situational awareness. However, adoption in safety–critical crowd scenarios remains limited. This work introduces a hybrid framework combining fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (FDEMATEL) and Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) to systematically identify, interrelate, and prioritize the obstacles to DT deployment for hyper–dense events such as Hajj and Umrah. By embedding fuzzy logic, the method captures the vagueness and variability of expert assessments, while ISM organizes barriers into a hierarchical structure. Analysis of ten barriers (BR1–BR10) identifies the nascent stage of domain implementation (BR10) as the deepest root cause, occupying the base of the interpretive structural hierarchy and exhibiting the largest net causal effect. The shortage of specialized expertise (BR6) occupies the second hierarchical level, mediating between domain immaturity and the remaining barriers. Crowd dynamics and behavioral diversity, legacy system integration, and regulatory and governance frameworks are net causes in the DEMATEL sense but occupy the upper hierarchical level as members of a mutually reinforcing cluster. Infrastructure requirements and cost emerge as the most strongly dependent barriers, followed by resistance to change and privacy concerns. The findings invert the intervention priorities transferred from industrial digital twin deployment, where cost and infrastructure are treated as binding constraints, and provide a cause-and-effect roadmap for policymakers and technology providers.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence-driven computed tomography analysis of upper airway morphology in patients undergoing multilevel sleep surgery
Article.Authors: Moon S.; Ryu S.; Jeong Y.; Lee J.; Cho H.
Article.Abstract: Anatomical information for planning sleep surgery is limited. We conducted an exploratory analysis to quantify upper airway morphology before and after multilevel sleep surgery and to examine whether preoperative measurements were associated with surgical response. In this post hoc analysis of a prospective cohort, 25 adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea underwent expansion sphincter pharyngoplasty, tonsillectomy, and single-port transoral robotic tongue base resection, with nasal surgery when indicated. Preoperative and postoperative computed tomography scans were segmented using a previously developed deep-learning pipeline. Surgical response was defined a priori as a postoperative apnea–hypopnea index below 15 events/h. Eighteen patients (72.0%) met the definition of response. Segmentation agreed with manual ground truth (mean Dice coefficient 0.868 ± 0.034). Surgery was associated with significant change in 8 of 13 morphological parameters, including uvula area (+ 140.2 mm²; 95% CI 109.2–171.3) and uvula–tongue volume (+ 2270.5 mm³; 95% CI 1166.6–3374.3). No preoperative parameter distinguished responders from non-responders (all p > 0.05), and preoperative tongue–epiglottis volume showed no discrimination. No drug-induced sleep endoscopy finding differed by response status. Automated computed tomography analysis reliably quantified upper airway remodeling after multilevel sleep surgery, but no preoperative morphological parameter predicted surgical response. These exploratory findings require independent confirmation.

Article.Title: PrivLightScreen: a privacy-preserving lightweight multitask AI framework for operational millimeter-wave airport security screening
Article.Authors: Adil M.; Ullah S.; Sajid M.; Aburaed N.
Article.Abstract: Airport passenger security screening is both a public-safety control and a performance-critical node in the airport supply chain, yet most artificial-intelligence studies on millimeter-wave (MMW) screening optimize detection accuracy without explicitly modeling false alarms, queue delay, privacy risk, resilience, or deployment cost. This paper presents PrivLightScreen, a unified multitask framework for privacy-preserving concealed-object detection in MMW screening, together with an Operational Performance Evaluation Framework (OPEF) that translates inference-level measurements into checkpoint-level performance indicators. PrivLightScreen combines physics-informed adaptive preprocessing, zone-guided self-supervised contrastive pretraining, a lightweight multitask module with an inter-zone Zone Transformer detection head, a representation-level anatomical abstraction layer, and a four-tier knowledge-distillation hierarchy spanning server graphics processing units (GPUs) to embedded processors. On the public Transportation Security Administration (TSA) passenger screening dataset, evaluated with a subject-disjoint protocol, the full model achieves a zone-level F1-score of 0.978 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.974–0.982), a log-loss of 0.0498 (95% CI 0.0476–0.0521), and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.983 (95% CI 0.979–0.987), giving the best result among the compared baselines under this protocol. Auxiliary keypoint and segmentation performance is evaluated against weak labels derived from the TSA body-zone metadata and a quality-audited pseudo-mask pipeline, reaching a percentage of correct keypoints normalized by head size (PCKh@0.5) of 99.81 percent and a weak-mask mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 85.7 percent. The smallest distilled student retains 98.3 percent of teacher F1 with a 3.1 MB footprint and an $$8.0\pm 0.6$$ ms batch-size-one forward-pass latency on commodity embedded hardware. Under OPEF, this edge model is the only tested configuration to satisfy all deployment-readiness thresholds, reaching a modeled 353 passengers per hour per lane (95% interval 345–361), a mean resilience index of $$0.82\pm 0.03$$ across six stress conditions, and a design-time Privacy Compliance Score of 0.95. The results show that detection accuracy, operational throughput, resilience, privacy, and hardware efficiency can be evaluated jointly in a single deployable MMW-screening framework, while regulatory deployment still requires site-specific validation and formal certification.

Article.Title: Depression, anxiety, and stress among Polish optometrists: a cross-sectional study conducted two years after legal regulation of the profession
Article.Authors: Garaszczuk I.; Zielonka S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mental health among healthcare workers is a major concern, as depression, anxiety, and stress contribute to burnout, medical errors, and suicide risk. In Poland, optometrists combine healthcare responsibilities with commercial pressures related to optical retail. In 2023, optometry was formally regulated under the Polish Act on Certain Medical Professions, introducing legal protections as well as new professional obligations that may increase occupational stress. Despite international evidence of elevated psychological distress among optometrists, no prior studies have examined mental health in this professional group in Poland using validated clinical screening instruments. A cross-sectional online survey using the DASS-21 questionnaire was conducted among 276 practising Polish optometrists between August and November 2025. Demographic and professional data were collected, and open-ended responses on occupational stress and burnout were analysed using conventional content analysis. Moderate-to-severe symptoms were reported by 44.9% of respondents for depression, 42.4% for anxiety, and 41.6% for stress. Female gender and lower income were associated with higher DASS-21 scores. Key stressors included excessive workload, inadequate salary, commercial pressure, and lack of professional recognition. Polish optometrists reported levels of depression, anxiety, and stress that exceeds rates observed in the general Polish population and among optometrists in several other countries. Targeted mental health support and workplace reforms are urgently needed.

Article.Title: Monsoon rainfall prediction using a BiLSTM model with an attention mechanism: a case study of Odisha state
Article.Authors: Sahu B.; Panigrahi A.; Pati A.; Sahu S.
Article.Abstract: Effective water resource management and disaster mitigation require accurate rainfall prediction for planning purposes. Forecasting of rainfall is a difficult time series problem as it is highly non-linear and non-stationary, and dependent on season. This study suggests a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) with Transformer Architecture and Attention, as well as the ensemble based on meta-learning. This framework employs CNN layers to gather temporal local patterns, BiLSTM networks to shape sequential dependencies, and transformer blocks to embrace the self-attention mechanism to formulate long-range patterns. An attention mechanism is used to dynamically weigh relevant time steps to achieve higher accuracy and interpretability in predictions. Moreover, various forecasts from LSTM, CNN–BiLSTM–Attention, CNN–Transformer–Attention, and XGBoost are fused together using a Random Forest-based meta-learner for enhanced robustness and generalization in the ensemble model. The proposed method utilizes Monte Carlo dropout for uncertainty estimation, enhancing the trustworthiness of the aforementioned approach by providing confidence intervals. The model undergoes assessment through a variety of performance metrics such as RMSE, MAE, R², MAPE, and NRMSE. Experimental results show that the ensemble framework consistently outperforms individual models, achieving better predictive accuracy and greater stability than individual models for a variety of rainfall, including extremes. The proposed model combines attention-based interpretability, transformer-based global learning, and ensemble meta-learning for rainfall forecasting, which is robust and scalable.

Article.Title: Integrative multivariate analysis of Pisum sativum L. genotypes using agro-morphological traits under contrasting semi-arid highland agro-ecosystems
Article.Authors: Mareai M.; Zaid N.; Al-Omri T.
Article.Abstract: Understanding yield formation and environmental adaptation in pea ( Pisum sativum L.) is essential for improving productivity under semi-arid highland conditions. This study evaluated eleven pea genotypes using morphological characterization and multivariate analyses across contrasting Northern and Central Highland environments of Yemen. Qualitative and quantitative descriptors revealed clear phenotypic variation among genotypes and successfully distinguished improved cultivars from local landraces. Analysis of variance showed significant differences ( P ≤ 0.05) among genotypes for all measured traits, indicating substantial genetic variability. Grain yield ranged from 0.40 to 1.20 t ha⁻¹ in the Northern Highlands and from 0.50 to 1.80 t ha⁻¹ in the Central Highlands, with Yahsb and Amran consistently exhibiting superior performance across environments. Principal component analysis indicated that yield variation under favorable conditions was mainly associated with seed weight (SW) and number of pods per plant (NPP), whereas phenological traits contributed more strongly under Northern Highland conditions. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive associations of grain yield with seed weight, pod length, pod width, and number of pods per plant, although the magnitude of these relationships varied between environments. Path coefficient analysis showed that seed weight exerted the greatest direct effect on grain yield in the Central Highlands (0.703), while pod length had the strongest direct effect in the Northern Highlands (0.568). Hierarchical clustering and heatmap analyses consistently grouped Yahsb, Amran, YG50075, and YG50083 into a distinct cluster across both environments, reflecting their close phenotypic similarity and superior agronomic performance. These findings demonstrate that yield determination in pea is environment-dependent and highlight Yahsb and Amran as promising genotypes for breeding and cultivation in semi-arid highland agroecosystems.

Article.Title: Association of the TyHGB index with hyperuricemia in adults aged 65 years and older
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang Z.; Wu T.; Ma J.; Zhang R.; Yu Z.
Article.Abstract: The triglyceride high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose body index (TyHGB) is a newly proposed metabolic marker. Our objective is to investigate the association between TyHGB and hyperuricemia prevalence in the elderly population. Data were analysed from 5730 adults aged 65 years or older in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), with an external validation sample from Kunshan Jinxi People’s Hospital, China. Logistic and linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were employed to evaluate the associations between TyHGB and hyperuricemia. TyHGB levels were significantly higher in participants with hyperuricemia ( P < 0.001). After adjusting for covariates, TyHGB remained significantly associated with hyperuricemia (OR: 1.141, 95% CI: 1.105–1.178, P < 0.001) and with increased serum uric acid (SUA) levels (β: 4.798, 95% CI: 3.759–5.836, P < 0.001). RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear relationship. ROC analysis further demonstrated that TyHGB had better discriminatory ability compared to other metabolic measures. These associations were also confirmed in the external Kunshan Chinese elderly sample. TyHGB is significantly associated with hyperuricemia, suggesting its potential utility in evaluating the role of metabolic disorders in hyperuricemia.

Article.Title: Motor imagery EEG signal classification using SAGAN-based data augmentation and ResNet-18 for brain–computer interface applications
Article.Authors: Jaipriya D.; Sriharipriya K.
Article.Abstract: Electroencephalogram signals are an important basis for motor skill rehabilitation and motor control in brain–computer interface (BCI) research. However, the limited labelled EEG data may limit the development of effective motor imagery (MI) classifiers. To address this limitation, this study presents a data augmentation framework using an improved Synaptic Augmented Generative Adversarial Network (SA-GAN). The EEG signals of the BCI Competition IV-2a dataset were transformed into two-dimensional time–frequency representations from one-dimensional time-series signals using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). The resulting representations were augmented using SA-GAN to generate synthetic MI samples and used to train ResNet-18 under augmented and non-augmented conditions. The proposed SAGAN-ResNet18 framework achieved better classification performance than the considered GAN-based augmentation approaches for all the evaluated subjects. The results show that the generated samples can provide valuable extra training information and reduce the negative impact of limited training data in within-subject MI classification. The results show that the proposed augmentation strategy is effective for the conditions evaluated in the BCI Competition IV-2a experiment.

Article.Title: Sex and gender bias in the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Neufang S.; Akhrif A.; Beyan O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sex and gender-related bias in clinical machine learning (ML) may contribute to inequitable diagnostic predictions in neurodegenerative diseases, where demographic factors may confound disease-related patterns. We developed and evaluated sex-debiased ML models for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) classification and their effects on model performance, fairness and interpretability. We analyzed 757 individuals suffering either from mild cognitive impairment ( N = 600, 269 females) or AD ( N = 157, 68 females) from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative. Sex was defined as the protected attribute. Four supervised ML algorithms were used to train classifiers based on demographic, genetic, neuropsychological, and MRI-derived features. For bias mitigation, methods of the IBM AI Fairness 360 framework were used. Fairness and model performance were assessed before and after mitigation, with LIME and SHAP used to evaluate changes in feature attribution. Bias mitigation reduced sample bias with the statistical mean difference decreasing from − 0.017 to 0.004. Mitigating model bias, two models demonstrated favorable combinations of classification performance and fairness: Logistic regression with Disparate Impact Remover improved balanced accuracy from 85.16% to 88.08% while reducing e.g. the equalized odds difference (original = -0.036, debiased = -0.003) and yielded the highest number of previously misclassified patients who were subsequently correctly classified. LIME analyses showed altered feature attribution patterns after mitigation including greater contributions from gender-related variables. The model achieving the highest balanced accuracy (88.91%) while maintaining favorable fairness metrics used Adversarial Debiasing. Adversarial Debiasing mitigates by reducing the influence of the protected attribute on model decisions. SHAP identified the total scores of the Mini-Mental State Examination and Functional Assessment Questionnaire as the strongest predictors of AD, suggesting that clinically relevant disease-related features remained important after bias mitigation. These findings demonstrate that fairness-aware ML can reduce sex-related bias in AD classification without compromising classification performance. The complementary strengths of the two models highlight the value of tailoring bias-mitigation strategies to clinical objectives. Integrating explainability may facilitate the development and responsible deployment of more transparent and equitable AI systems for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis.

Article.Title: The elusive alien fauna of soil and leaf litter of Socorro Island, Revillagigedo Archipelago, México
Article.Authors: Matías-Ferrer N.; Rojas-Fernández P.; Fragoso C.; Morales-Góngora Y.; Domínguez-Meneses A.; Pérez-Hernández B.; Myers E.; Mulcahy D.; Martínez-Gómez J.
Article.Abstract: Global trade and migration have facilitated the arrival of alien species within new ecosystems. Alien species that become invasive constitute a major driver of biodiversity loss. On Socorro Island, alien species in the soil have not been sistematically searched where their arrival is possibly associated with introduced plant species and the movement of various goods. We searched for alien and invasive fauna in the soil and leaf litter of Socorro Island and compared their present distribution with historical records. We recorded for the first time four earthworm species, 10 new ant species, and a fossorial snake. Snakes and earthworms were detected in areas where alien tree species were introduced several decades ago, suggesting a parallel invasion. Native and alien ant species were found across all sampling sites; nonetheless, invasive ant species were found solely around the naval base, the area with the highest human disturbance. Alien and invasive species represent a threat to soil structure and composition, and interactions with other species could facilitate their spread and establishment. Our findings highlight the need for immediate conservation actions to avert damage to soil communities on Socorro Island.

Article.Title: Residential environment, physical activity, and cardiovascular health in urban adults
Article.Authors: Andrušaitytė S.; Vencloviene J.; Rapalavičius A.; Miškinytė A.; Dėdelė A.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality. This study examined the joint and interactive effects of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and residential environment infrastructure factor (REIF) on cardiovascular health indicators in an urban population. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 95 adults in Kaunas (Lithuania). Participants were categorized into MVPA tertiles. Cardiovascular outcomes included arterial pressure (aBP), including systolic (sBP) and diastolic blood pressure (dBP), pulse pressure (PP), daily heart rate (dHR), endurance coefficient (EC), adaptive potential (AP), and a composite health index (HI). Principal component analysis generated a composite behavioral–environmental–health index (AEH) explaining 71.3% of total variance. Structural equation modeling (SEM) assessed direct and interaction effects. Participants in the highest MVPA tertile exhibited significantly lower dHR, PP, and more favorable HI profiles compared with the lowest tertile. SEM demonstrated significant associations between MVPA and dHR and HI, as well as between REIF and dHR. A significant MVPA x REIF interaction was observed for dHR. The model explained up to 61% of variance in key cardiovascular outcomes. This study suggests that PA and REIF quality may be jointly associated with cardiovascular health.

Article.Title: Hydrogen exerts antioxidant and cytostatic effects on C2C12 myoblasts
Article.Authors: Ebara S.; Ogawa Y.; Kawada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oxidative stress plays a pivotal role in the progression of lifestyle-related diseases and thus its mitigation is essential for managing these conditions. Hydrogen gas (H 2 ) exhibits potent antioxidant properties and is thus a promising candidate for mitigating these diseases. Various pathologies, including lifestyle-related diseases, are known to impair skeletal muscle physiology and regeneration; however, the specific effects of H 2 on skeletal muscle remain largely unexplored. We developed a specialized cell culture system capable of maintaining a sealed H 2 environment. Using this device, we evaluated the antioxidant capacity of 2% H 2 and its effects on C2C12 cell proliferation. Furthermore, we investigated whether H 2 modulates cell alterations induced by high-glucose (HG) conditions. In C2C12 cells, H 2 significantly inhibited hydrogen peroxide-induced lipid peroxidation and attenuated HG-induced abnormalities in mitochondrial membrane potential. Under standard conditions, H 2 suppressed cell proliferation without altering mitochondrial membrane potential or inducing necrosis or apoptosis. Under HG conditions, cell proliferative capacity decreased, and cell death (necrosis/apoptosis) increased. Although H 2 prevented HG-induced mitochondrial membrane hyperpolarization, it failed to rescue cells from death. Notably, H 2 further suppressed cell proliferation under HG conditions compared with HG alone, without exacerbating cytotoxicity. These results suggest that H 2 possesses antioxidant and cytostatic properties in C2C12 cells without discernible cytotoxicity. This study offers fundamental insights into the therapeutic potential of H 2 for managing oxidative stress-related muscular pathologies.

Article.Title: Adsorption performance of chestnut cupule-derived carbon in olaparib removal from aquatic environments: kinetic, isotherm and thermodynamic evaluation
Article.Authors: Türk Baydir A.; Bulduk İ.
Article.Abstract: The occurrence of pharmaceutical contaminants in aquatic environments has become a critical environmental concern, necessitating effective and sustainable treatment technologies. This study investigates the adsorptive removal of olaparib (OLA), an anticancer pharmaceutical, from aqueous solutions using chestnut cupule-derived carbon (CCDC). Comprehensive characterization revealed that CCDC possesses a well-developed hierarchical porous structure with a specific surface area of 576.5 m²/g and a predominantly mesoporous character (75% of total surface area). Batch adsorption experiments were systematically conducted to evaluate the effects of adsorbent dosage, initial OLA concentration, solution pH, contact time, and temperature. Under optimized conditions (15 mg adsorbent/50 mL, pH 7, initial concentration ≤ 30 mg/L, 180 min), CCDC achieved up to 99.43% OLA removal. The adsorption process was remarkably robust against pH variations (2–12), maintaining removal efficiencies above 98%. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir isotherm model (R² = 0.998), indicating homogeneous monolayer adsorption with a maximum capacity of 176.85 mg/g. Kinetic modeling indicated that the pseudo-second-order (PSO) model (R 2 = 0.947) effectively represented the adsorption rate and rate-controlling step, closely predicting the experimental equilibrium capacity (q e, cal = 148.36 mg/g vs. q e, exp = 147.43 mg/g). Concurrently, the superior mathematical fit of the Elovich model (R 2 = 0.981) confirmed that the adsorption occurs predominantly on an energetically heterogeneous surface governed by chemisorption mechanisms with varying activation energies. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed the spontaneous (ΔG° = -9.86 to -9.72 kJ/mol) and exothermic (ΔH° = -12.73 kJ/mol) nature of the process. The negative entropy change (ΔS° = -0.00964 kJ/mol·K) indicated decreased randomness at the solid-liquid interface. This study demonstrates that KOH-modified chestnut cupule-derived carbon (CCDC) is a promising, cost-effective, and sustainable adsorbent for the remediation of olaparib from aquatic environments, while promoting agro-industrial waste valorization within a circular economy framework.

Article.Title: Mechanistic basis of proteolytic signalling of the SltB-SltA dual system mediating cation homeostasis and alkaline pH response in Aspergillus nidulans
Article.Authors: Requena E.; Picazo I.; Tomico-Cuenca I.; Espeso E.
Article.Abstract: Cation homeostasis and adaptation to alkaline pH in Aspergillus nidulans depend on the Slt pathway, comprising the transcription factor SltA and the signalling protease SltB. However, the molecular mechanisms controlling SltA activation and subcellular regulation remain poorly understood. We have identified the proteolytic and localisation determinants required for SltA function. Basal SltB levels are sufficient to initiate the proteolytic conversion of inactive SltA, supporting a model in which pathway activation starts independently of SltA-dependent transcriptional regulation. Mutational and domain analyses in SltA demonstrate that a conserved RSMA motif is required for cleavage by SltB to generate the transcriptionally active 32 kDa form, independently of the poorly conserved C-terminal region or zinc-finger domain. Proteolytic processing is required for SltA nuclear import and nucleolar accumulation, which relies on a functional nuclear localisation signal adjacent to the zinc-finger domain and is enhanced by residues within the C-terminal region. Zinc fingers differentially contribute to nucleolar targeting and nucleoplasmic retention. Structural predictions aided in demonstrating that correct SltB auto-activation and stability depend on an RSKV motif followed by a K/R-rich region. Together, these findings define the molecular basis of proteolytic mechanisms in Slt system, which is highly conserved in the fungal kingdom, and link SltA proteolytic activation to regulated nuclear/nucleolar localisation.

Article.Title: Eccentric vs. plyometric training for hamstring health in soccer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of injury prevention and athletic performance
Article.Authors: Sarraj A.; Allaw J.
Article.Abstract: Hamstring strain injuries are the most burdensome muscle injuries in soccer, yet eccentric and plyometric training are typically studied in isolation — the former for injury prevention, the latter for performance. We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials of eccentric, plyometric, or combined training versus control in soccer players aged 13 years or older, searching five databases and a structured academic corpus from inception to 2026 and reporting according to PRISMA 2020. Of 705 records, 54 trials were included. Hamstring-injury risk was pooled as a random-effects risk ratio, and performance outcomes as change-from-baseline standardized mean differences, with subgroup analyses by intervention type. Eccentric (Nordic hamstring) training reduced hamstring-injury incidence by approximately 70% (4 trials; risk ratio 0.29, 95% CI 0.17–0.48), whereas plyometric bounding did not. Training improved vertical jump (g = 0.70) and sprint (g = 0.75); however, in subgroup analysis eccentric training did not significantly improve sprint (g = 0.30; two trials, underpowered), while plyometric (g = 0.67) and combined (g = 1.02) programs did. Eccentric training increased eccentric knee-flexor strength (g = 0.82). These effects are complementary: eccentric training protects the hamstring and builds strength, plyometric training builds speed and power, and combining the two addresses both.

Article.Title: Polyphasic taxonomic description of Streptomyces balliae sp. nov. and Streptomyces schrempfiae sp. nov.
Article.Authors: Nouioui I.; Kirstein S.; Steinkirchinger I.; Körsgen P.; Neumann-Schaal M.; Spröer C.; Bunk B.; Mast Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Strains DSM 116793 T (JZT14 T = CECT 31213 T ) and DSM 118148 T (= KCTC 59415 T = unkn41448C T ), deposited in the DSMZ culture collection, were subjected to modern polyphasic taxonomic studies to determine their taxonomic positions. Strains DSM 116793 T and DSM 118148 T showed 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity values of 97.8% and 99.5% to the type strains of Streptomyces sulfonofaciens and Streptomyces bungoensis , respectively, supporting their assignment to the genus Streptomyces . Digital DNA–DNA hybridization (dDDH) and average nucleotide identity (ANI) values between the genomes of strains DSM 116793 T and DSM 118148 T and their closest phylogenetic relatives were below the accepted species delineation thresholds of 70% for DDH and 95–96.7% for ANI, respectively. Morphological and phenotypic characteristics distinguished the strains from their closest relatives. Based on these data, strains DSM 116793 T and DSM 118148 T represent two novel species, for which the names Streptomyces balliae sp. nov. and Streptomyces schrempfiae sp. nov. are proposed, respectively. Crude extracts of strains DSM 116793 T and DSM 118148 T exhibited antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria ( E. coli Δ tolC JW5503-1, P. vulgaris DSM 2140) and Gram-positive bacteria ( E. faecium DSM 20477 T and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus DSM 18827). Genome mining of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) associated with secondary metabolites revealed multiple clusters with low similarity to known BGCs, indicating the presence of biosynthetic potential that warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: Evaluating FoundationPose object registration accuracy for AR-guided industrial inspection
Article.Authors: Masuhr C.; Koch J.; Oels T.; Schüppstuhl T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Augmented Reality (AR) can enhance industrial processes like manual inspections by increasing safety and efficiency. This is achieved by superimposing virtual guidance directly onto the physical environment, such as visual highlights, step-by-step instructions, or animated tool paths. The accurate alignment of virtual guidance depends directly on the precise registration of real-world components. This study evaluates the 6D pose estimation accuracy of the FoundationPose framework for registering real-world, complex industrial components (e.g., fittings, flanges) from a single RGB-D image without object-specific retraining. In a controlled pre-deployment evaluation with a robot-positioned RGB-D camera, the measured accuracy meets the requirements derived for AR-assisted inspection, achieving median translational deviations between 0.5 mm and 2.8 mm and a median rotational error of approximately 1.9° for plane-symmetric components. While performance remained stable against partial occlusions and reflective surfaces, the results highlight that accuracy is limited by key challenges, including performance degradation with symmetric and texture-poor objects and the need for optimization for real-time mobile deployment. Despite these limitations, the baseline accuracy identified in this study indicates the potential of FoundationPose for industrial AR applications that demand precise alignment of virtual overlays, subject to validation on the target device.

Article.Title: Defining the progression of normal and non-progression humeral shaft fracture healing using the plasma proteome
Article.Authors: Gerstenfeld L.; Tornetta P.; Demissie S.; Nafisi N.; Vaishnav A.; Chung S.; Chaffee T.; Kim R.; Azario R.; Lowe J.; O’Toole R.; Weiss D.; Matusewski P.; Hanson G.; Patterson J.; Natoli R.; Castillo R.; N/A N/A.; N/A N/A.; Gerstenfeld L.; Tornetta P.; Demissie S.; Nafisi N.; Chung S.; Tornetta P.
Article.Abstract: Current diagnostic tools are neither informative nor concurrent with the early biological processes of fracture healing. The plasma proteome of non-operatively fixed, isolated, non-articular humeral fractures was assessed to determine whether plasma proteins could provide insight into these processes. Radiological, clinical, and patient-reported outcomes, along with blood samples, were collected from 31 patients: 24 who had healed and 7 who had not healed and were assessed as nonunion within 2 months of injury. The plasma levels of ~ 7000 proteins were determined using the SomaLogic Inc Aptamer platform. Using the first or last clinic visit as the reference, 118 of ~ 7000 proteins assayed showed differential expression (DE) with a log 2 fold change ≥ 1.3 and a false discovery rate (FDR) ≤ 0.05. DE proteins associated with endochondral bone development increased between the first and third months. In contrast, proteins associated with the acute-phase response, inflammation, and lipid storage decreased after the first month and remained diminished relative to their initial levels over a 6-month recall period. A time-point-to-point comparison between normal and non-progression healing groups for the first three recalls (up to two months post-fracture) identified 41 proteins with differential levels ( p ≤ 0.05); given the small non-progression healing sample size, these findings should be considered exploratory. These proteins included specific extracellular matrix and acute-phase proteins, all of which showed lower levels than in normal healers. These data suggest that the progression of endochondral bone formation can be placed in context to radiological and functional outcomes in human fracture healing with a potential for the development of candidate diagnostic markers for the early identification of patients that are failing to progress in healing.
