Article.Title: Numerical study on instability failure and energy release of composite coal and rock under dynamic disturbance load
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Zhou Y.; Miao Y.; Pan F.; Zhu C.; Zhou J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the instability failure and energy release of composite coal-rock structures under dynamic disturbance loads, a numerical model of a “roof-coal seam-floor” composite block was established using the UDEC simulation software. The model comprehensively considered key influencing factors including the inclination angle of the contact surface, dynamic disturbance load parameters, and horizontal stress levels, with a particular focus on the failure mechanisms, instability characteristics, and energy evolution of inclined coal-rock composites under dynamic disturbance loading. The results demonstrate that, in comparison to static loads, dynamic disturbance loads exacerbate internal damage within the coal-rock mass, increase overall energy dissipation, and accelerate the dissipation rate, thereby playing a decisive role in its failure. As the inclination angle of the contact surface increases, the model becomes increasingly prone to sliding instability along the contact surface, accompanied by an elevated instantaneous crack propagation speed and pronounced stress concentration. An increase in the dynamic load amplitude elevates the peak kinetic energy, peak potential energy, and horizontal displacement, consequently heightening the instantaneous instability risk of the model. Furthermore, as the horizontal stress intensifies, the overall horizontal displacement of the model tends to increase; when horizontal and vertical loads act in concert, the model is highly prone to generating ultra-low friction effects. The findings of this research are anticipated to provide theoretical underpinnings and engineering references for the prediction and prevention of rockburst in deep coal mines under similar geological conditions, offering significant guidance for formulating safe mining plans and effective disaster prevention and control measures.

Article.Title: Modeling and optimization of high-temperature degradation in fuze coil springs using response surface methodology
Article.Authors: Ali B.; Saleh B.; Zhang H.; Gu X.
Article.Abstract: Accelerated degradation testing (ADT) of safety-critical mechanical components like fuze coil springs remains challenging due to complex, nonlinear degradation mechanisms under thermal stress. This study presents a novel cubic-order Response Surface Methodology (RSM) framework to model and predict the simultaneous degradation of two key performance parameters, permanent deformation (compression set) and stress relaxation rate, under elevated temperature and time. A total of 18 experimental runs were conducted across 120–160 °C and 1–318 h, and statistically validated cubic models were developed with R² > 96% and adjusted R² > 92%. ANOVA and standardized-effect analysis showed that the degradation responses are governed predominantly by nonlinear exposure-time effects. For permanent deformation, the quadratic and cubic time terms were significant ( p = 0.0009 and p = 0.0134, respectively), while for stress loss the corresponding terms were also significant ( p = 0.0022 and p = 0.0149). In contrast, the linear time main effect was not significant for either response. Temperature and temperature–time interaction also contributed significantly to the degradation behavior. Independent confirmation tests demonstrated high predictive accuracy, with errors ≤ 8.8%. Multi-response desirability optimization identified an optimal condition of approximately 120.4 °C and 1.10 h for simultaneously minimizing permanent deformation and stress loss, with predicted responses of 8.14% and 13.82%, respectively. This work provides an empirical framework for characterizing nonlinear temperature–time effects on spring degradation and for predicting permanent deformation and stress loss within the experimentally investigated domain.

Article.Title: Agricultural reuse of immobilized white rot fungal consortium treated textile effluent for improved agronomic performance and nutritional quality of Vigna radiata
Article.Authors: Sahoo P.; Raut S.; Panda A.; Sahoo A.; Rout N.; Sen S.
Article.Abstract: Growing freshwater scarcity, with increasing discharge of wastewater from textile industries, have intensified the need for wastewater treatment and agricultural reuse. The current research assessed the reusability of biological treated synthetic textile effluent (STE), comprising anthraquinone (AQ) dyes, for irrigation of Vigna radiata . To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to report a chitosan immobilized white-rot fungal consortium (WRFC) comprising Trametes cubensis , Polyporus umbellatus , Leiotrametes flavida , and Pleurotus pulmonarius for the treatment of AQ dye-containing textile effluent using batch, continuous, and fed-batch bioreactor systems. The immobilized WRFC based fed-batch bioreactor showed the highest treatment efficiency with 99.06% decolorization, and significant reductions in chemical oxygen demand (COD) (75.04%), biological oxygen demand (BOD) (96.05%), nitrate (95.38%), lead (39.47%), and cadmium (50%). The suspended and immobilized WRFC treated effluent (IWTE) was reused for irrigation of V. radiata . Plants irrigated with IWTE exhibited superior growth performance, including maximum plant height, fresh biomass, pod yield, and enhanced photosynthetic pigments. Nutritional quality of mung grains was also improved, with higher protein (28.90 g/100 g), carbohydrate (55.54 g/100 g), and energy value (343.25 Kcal/100 g) compared to plants irrigated with untreated STE. Overall, immobilized WRFC based mycoremediation demonstrated an eco-friendly and sustainable approach for textile effluent remediation and safe agricultural reuse under water scarcity conditions.

Article.Title: Explainable multimodal learning analytics for model-based counterfactual decision support using literature-calibrated synthetic data
Article.Authors: Venugopal A.; Al Rawas F.; Al Minhali A.; Goyal D.; Dadhich A.
Article.Abstract: Predictive learning analytics can identify students who are at risk of failing, however, there is a lack of information to guide advisors on what they should do. This paper proposes an end-to-end synthetic framework using eight structured indicators of Learning Management System (LMS) and an aggregated VADER sentiment. The XGBoost pipeline model had accuracy of 80.7%, precision of 76.5%, recall of 90.3%, an F1 score of 0.828, and an ROC-AUC score of 0.905 at the fixed cut-point of 0.28; logistic regression had the best ROC-AUC score of 0.930. With sentiment removal, the accuracy of XGBoost dropped to 76.7% and the value of ROC-AUC to 0.875. The constrained greedy counterfactual search screened 149 XGBoost cases separately, dropped 80 cases (53.7\%) below the target of 0.40, and reduced the score by a mean of 33.3% points. Threshold crossing rate for logistic regression and random forest were 100.0% and 41.4% respectively with the same search, highlighting model dependence. A 27-configuration, training-only sensitivity analysis placed the fixed XGBoost configuration 12th by five-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC (0.929), compared with 0.933 for the best configuration. DiCE-random crossed the target for 74.5% of the same XGBoost-screened cases but required larger normalized changes and approximately four times the runtime of greedy search. These results characterize a reconstructed synthetic model and its search procedures; they do not establish educational validity, causal effectiveness, calibrated institutional risk, least-burden recourse, or deployment readiness.

Article.Title: A rapid silver nitrate histological staining technique for studying the osteocyte lacunocanalicular system
Article.Authors: Wu J.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: The osteocyte lacuno-canalicular system (LCS) is a fundamental bone structure that plays a critical role in maintaining skeletal health and systemic mineral homeostasis. However, investigations into the functional and morphological properties of the LCS have been hindered by the lack of a rapid and reliable histological staining method. Here, we introduce the Wu–Wang Silver Nitrate Staining Method, a high-temperature rapid technique that enables efficient visualization of the osteocyte LCS within 10 min. Using a 1 mol/L silver nitrate solution at 50 °C for 10 min, the method yields consistent LCS staining across bone specimens from diverse vertebrate species. Importantly, this approach addresses key limitations of the conventional Ploton silver staining method, including structural damage and insufficient LCS staining. Overall, this rapid staining method will facilitate fundamental research into osteocyte biology and LCS morphogenesis, whilst accelerating biomedical and translational investigations into the roles of osteocytes and their LCS in skeletal ageing, osteoarthritis, and related pathological conditions of significant clinical relevance.

Article.Title: MSwinALL-Net: a multi-stage Swin Transformer network for acute lymphoblastic leukemia classification
Article.Authors: Prahaladhan V.; Anbarasi L.; Neeraja R.; Narayanan S.; Induja R.; Raj B.
Article.Abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a form of blood cancer that requires timely and precise diagnosis for effective treatment. The conventional method relies on manual examination of blood smear images which is a slow and inconsistent process due to cellular diversity and the limited availability of trained professionals. A Swin Transformer based architecture named MSwinALL-Net is proposed to overcome these challenges by incorporating a multi-stage shifted-window mechanism to capture both fine-grained local and global contextual features for identifying subtle abnormalities in leukemia cells. GAN based augmentation was used to synthesize high quality blood smear images. The proposed model outperforms transfer learning approaches by achieving an accuracy of 98.74%, precision of 1.0, recall of 0.99, F1-score of 0.99 and an AUC of 1.0 showing its potential for reliable, automated ALL diagnosis. The model's robustness and generalization are further validated through 5-fold cross-validation on benchmark leukemia datasets where the model outperformed recent transformer based models like ConvNeXt-Tiny and EfficientNetV2 which exhibited unstable and near random performance. These results highlighted MSwinALL-Net's effectiveness and reliability for automated ALL diagnosis in clinical applications. Future enhancement could incorporate more advanced generative frameworks such as StyleGAN and CycleGAN to further enhance synthetic image quality along with explainable AI techniques for providing interpretability and clinical transparency in real-world deployment.

Article.Title: Semantic image retrieval using deep feature representation, LDA, and extreme gradient boosting
Article.Authors: Mehmood Z.; Iqbal A.; Bibi R.; Elmannai H.; Alwarafy A.; Algarni A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Content-based image retrieval (CBIR) remains challenging because of the semantic gap between low-level visual representations and high-level image concepts, redundancy in high-dimensional deep features, and limited discrimination among visually similar categories. This study proposes a classification-guided CBIR technique that integrates fine-tuned VGG-16 feature representation, supervised linear discriminant analysis (LDA), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and cosine-similarity ranking. A fine-tuned VGG-16 network extracts 4096-dimensional semantic representations from the FC2 layer, which are projected by LDA into a compact $$C - 1$$ -dimensional discriminative space learned exclusively from the training partition. XGBoost subsequently models nonlinear category boundaries and predicts the semantic category of each query, thereby restricting the candidate retrieval space. Final ranking is performed independently using cosine similarity between the LDA-transformed query and candidate feature vectors, and the Top-20 images are returned. The proposed technique was evaluated under a stratified 80:20 closed-set protocol on Corel-1 K, Corel-5 K, Corel-1500, and OTScene. The proposed technique achieved mAP@20 values of 96.40%, 85.00%, 93.72%, and 83.96%, respectively, while maintaining an average retrieval time of 0.34 s. Controlled ablation experiments demonstrated that the proposed technique consistently outperformed eight alternative configurations, with an exact binomial sign test confirming statistical significance ( $$p=0.0078$$ , two-sided). These results show that supervised discriminant compression, nonlinear category guidance, and normalized similarity ranking provide complementary benefits for accurate and computationally efficient retrieval in labeled image collections. The proposed framework therefore offers a reproducible and effective solution for classification-guided CBIR.

Article.Title: Molecular and in-silico characterization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp. isolated from clinical urine samples, Lahore, Pakistan
Article.Authors: Khan N.; Aamir M.; Amin A.; Saeed G.; Mujtaba G.
Article.Abstract: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci are a serious threat to public health because of their multidrug resistance and the limitations in the treatment options available. This study investigated clinical VRE isolates from Lahore, Pakistan, and characterized the vanA gene via in-silico approaches. In this study, urine specimens were collected and cultured on selective media. Morphological and biochemical observation, such as Gram staining and catalase, oxidase, and mannitol salt agar tests, were conducted. Antibiotic susceptibility testing was done via the Kirby-Bauer method. DNA was extracted and the PCR amplified the genomic DNA, vanA , and vanB genes. Protein sequences were obtained from NCBI and analyzed with ProtParam, PSIPRED, and AlphaFold3. olecular docking was carried out using AutoDock Vina, structural dynamics were evaluated with iMODS-based normal mode analysis, and immune simulation conducted with C-ImmSim. Seven clinical VRE isolates were characterized. All isolates showed elevated MICs to vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and chloramphenicol, meeting CLSI resistance criteria; gentamicin and azithromycin MICs were also elevated but are reported descriptively, as CLSI interpretive breakpoints for these agents against Enterococcus spp. are not established for routine susceptibility categorization. PCR provided evidence for the presence of the vanA gene (732 bp) in all of the isolates. Genomic DNA sequencing of two representative isolates (NK-01, NK-02) yielded partial vanA gene sequence, confirmed via BLASTN analysis against isolate-derived and reference vanA records; these sequences did not provide species-level discrimination, and species identification for all isolates remained at the genus level ( Enterococcus spp.). The VanA protein was relatively stable (aliphatic index 94.69) with a globular fold and showed moderate docking with Vancomycin (− 6.0 kcal/mol). Normal mode analysis showed the domains to be flexible due to low eigenvalues. Immune simulation demonstrated prediction for strong IgM and IgG responses, along with identification of promising B- and T-cell epitopes, though a separate immunogenicity assessment yielded conflicting predictions. The current study confirmed VanA-mediated resistance in multidrug-resistant Enterococcus spp. and gave structural and immunological insight into VanA. These findings support VanA as a potential target for further therapeutic investigation; given that surface exposure, secretion potential, conservation across isolates, and population coverage were not assessed, its vaccine potential remains preliminary and unconfirmed, and the necessity for continued surveillance and development of new inhibitors against VRE is emphasized.

Article.Title: Optimizing open space capacity under heritage constraints in the ancient city of Suzhou: a multi-scale recursive approach
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Yuan X.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Optimizing open spaces in historic urban areas presents a unique challenge: balancing macro-level planning objectives with the preservation of irreplaceable heritage. This study introduces a multi-scale recursive optimization framework that integrates assessment, prediction, and configuration to address these conflicts. Using the ancient city of Suzhou, China (a UNESCO World Heritage site), as a case study, we applied the framework at city, community, and plot scales. Comprehensive assessment identified critical challenges, including insufficient per capita open space, uneven spatial distribution, and pronounced quality–quantity mismatches. Recursive optimization refined initial macro-level capacity targets, derived from national standards, by incorporating micro-scale heritage constraints. A potential–constraint model quantified regeneration potential, while spatial-cultural rules, such as water proximity, directed capacity allocations along river corridors. The proposed framework achieves synergy between capacity enhancement and historic character preservation. By shifting spatial governance from static blueprinting to dynamic, multi-scale optimization, our findings provide transferable methodologies and actionable strategies to support sustainable regeneration in heritage cities facing conservation–development conflicts.

Article.Title: Chatbot rating scale (CHARS): Development and validation of a new tool for assessing the quality of health and social care chatbots
Article.Authors: Olufadewa I.; Olayori E.; Adesina M.; Ayanwale M.; Oladokun B.; Oladele R.; Ale O.; Olufadewa T.; Oduro M.
Article.Abstract: Chatbots are increasingly deployed in healthcare, yet there is a dearth of standardized tools for evaluating their quality. The objective of this study was to develop and validate a novel, multidimensional instrument, the Chatbot Rating Scale (CHARS), for assessing the comprehensive quality of health and social care chatbots. This study employed a sequential multi-method design to develop and validate the Chatbot Rating Scale (CHARS). Phase 1 involved a rapid and comprehensive literature review and a modified Delphi process to identify key domains of chatbot quality and generate scale items. Phase 2 comprised psychometric evaluation, including pilot testing, construct validity assessment, reliability analysis, and factor structure determination. Items were refined through three Delphi rounds involving 24 experts, including clinicians, psychometrists, information technology specialists, graduate students, and end users. Following pilot testing of 10 chatbots, 979 participants, including health professionals, researchers, mental health experts, and end users, used CHARS (5-point Likert scale) to evaluate 36 health and mental health chatbots. Factorial validity was assessed using parallel analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis, while internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha in R (version 4.4.2). The modified Delphi study resulted in a refined scale comprising 25 items distributed across five initial dimensions. Empirical analysis supported a three-factor structure, which was: (1) Design, (2) Interactive User Experience (personalization, engagement, and usability), and (3) Functionality, with excellent internal consistencies (Cronbach’s alpha) of 0.90, 0.88, and 0.90, respectively. The factor loadings and interrater correlation coefficient for all 25 items of CHARS were high with standardized loadings ranging from 0.79 to 0.87 for Factor 2 (Design, ICC = 0.88), 0.77 to 0.87 for Factor 1 (Interactive User Experience, ICC = 0.98), and from 0.83 to 0.87 for Factor 3 (Functionality, ICC = 0.90), which were all statistically significant (p < .001). All 25 Delphi-derived items were retained and redistributed across the three factors, preserving comprehensive coverage of chatbot quality dimensions. CHARS is a novel, psychometrically robust, user-centred instrument that consolidates key experiential and functional attributes into a concise three-dimensional model. Its development highlights the convergence of user perceptions around integrated experiential qualities, offering a practical and theoretically grounded tool for evaluating chatbots. Future research should test its generalizability across cultural and technological contexts and examine predictive validity for user engagement.

Article.Title: FIA-LLM: feedback conditioned learning state estimation with large language models
Article.Authors: Jin X.; Baki R.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intelligent tutoring systems predict student achievement with increasing accuracy, yet they do not model the feedback-conditioned learning states that sustain engagement and guide intervention. A central obstacle is scale: large educational datasets lack validated motivation annotations, while using large language models (LLMs) to infer such labels risks creating a self-referential supervision loop. We propose FIA-LLM, a dual-stream framework that jointly produces a learning-state surrogate grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), a next-item achievement prediction, an SDT dimension label, and a structured diagnostic explanation. FIA-LLM integrates three components. Confidence-Aware Robust Distillation (CARD) combines 2,000 human teacher annotations with LLM pseudo-labels validated against human judgments ( $$\textrm{ICC}=0.83$$ ), using confidence-weighted training to suppress noisy supervision. Feedback Intervention Attention (FIA), a multi-head feedback-as-Query cross-attention mechanism, fuses feedback proxies with behavioral histories. Joint Structured Decoding (JSD) produces four outputs from shared representations through a motivation-related surrogate head, an achievement head, an SDT dimension head, and a diagnostic generation module. On frozen human expert test sets, FIA-LLM reduces macro-average RMSE by 8.6% against the strongest baseline and improves macro-average AUC by 1.2 percentage points (paired across seeds, $$p<0.01$$ ). Gains persist under ASSISTments platform-derived hint/scaffold proxies, and human teacher blind review provides external evidence of diagnostic quality.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal distribution of microplastics in the Gansu section of the Yellow River and its influencing factors
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Bai Y.; Liu X.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: The Yellow River, the second-longest river in China, is a major channel for the transport of microplastics. In this study, we investigated the occurrence, spatiotemporal distribution, and influencing factors of microplastics in the main stem and major tributaries of the Gansu section of the Yellow River. The average annual microplastic concentrations in the surface water and sediments of the main stem of the Yellow River were relatively low at 1502.99 p m − 3 and 206.86 p kg − 1 , respectively. The chemical composition of microplastics in surface water and sediments comprised polyethylene terephthalate, polyvinyl chloride, polypropylene, polyethylene, and polyamide, with particle sizes generally below 1,000 μm. Fibers were more abundant in surface water, while fragments predominated in sediments. The spatial variation of microplastics in surface water was dominated by population density, while in sediments, this was primarily affected by population density and average annual flow. The temporal variation of microplastics in surface water was positively affected by monthly averages of flow and sediment concentration, while the temporal variation of microplastics in sediments was negatively influenced by the two factors. Riverine microplastics exhibited distinct spatial vertical distribution characteristics related to their physicochemical properties. In months with higher average monthly flow, the vertical distribution of microplastics in rivers was more uniform, whereas months with lower average flow exhibited more pronounced vertical variation. Our findings provide a reference for the impact of population density and river flow on the environmental behavior of microplastics in freshwater ecosystems.

Article.Title: Model-consistent iterated least-squares initialization for UKF-based AUV tracking under an isogradient sound speed profile
Article.Authors: Zhao H.; Pan J.; Fu B.; Wan H.; Xia Y.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) tracking is an important enabling technique for the Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT). However, depth-dependent acoustic propagation and inaccurate filter initialization can significantly degrade the transient performance of nonlinear AUV tracking. To address these issues, this paper develops a model-consistent iterated least-squares initialized unscented Kalman filter (ILS-UKF) method under an isogradient sound speed profile (SSP). In the initial localization stage, a curved-ray ILS estimator is used to obtain the initial AUV position and construct its measurement-informed local covariance from the weighted time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) information. Specifically, the pairwise TDoA construction eliminates the common AUV transmission time term and therefore does not require synchronization between the AUV clock and the sensor-network clock. In the continuous tracking stage, the resulting position-covariance pair is used to initialize the UKF, which employs the same curved-ray TDoA model for recursive motion-state estimation. A posterior Cramér–Rao lower bound (PCRLB) and computational-complexity analysis are further provided for performance assessment. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves lower transient tracking errors and faster convergence than the conventional UKF, and that the measurement-informed covariance contributes to improved transient tracking performance.

Article.Title: Mathematical modeling and statistical analysis for predicting success in intrauterine insemination, intracytoplasmic sperm injection, and frozen embryo transfer
Article.Authors: Hafezi S.; Soleimani N.; Ghasemabadi A.; Namakin K.; Ghamsary M.; Effati S.; Ghaheri A.
Article.Abstract: Infertility affects millions of couples worldwide, and assisted reproductive technologies (ART) such as intrauterine insemination (IUI), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and frozen embryo transfer (ET Freeze) are commonly used to treat it. However, the success rates of these methods vary considerably, and the factors that predict successful outcomes are not fully understood. Identifying these predictors is crucial for personalized treatment planning and improving clinical decision-making. This study aims to identify and compare the significant predictors of treatment success across three ART methods: IUI, ICSI, and ET Freeze. We also seek to develop statistical and mathematical models to evaluate the relationship between patient-related factors and pregnancy outcomes, and to assess which model provides the best fit for predicting treatment success. This retrospective cohort study was conducted at Royan Institute, Tehran, Iran, using data from 2011–2014. The unit of analysis was the ART treatment cycle. After data cleaning, 6240 cycles remained. The final ordinal logistic regression analyses included 4592 cycles with a known ordinal outcome (blighted ovum, abortion, or live birth). Repeated cycles from the same couple were accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEE) with couple ID as the clustering variable. Ordinal logistic regression was used to model the association between predictors and treatment outcome. Of the 6240 participants, 209 underwent IUI, 2598 underwent ICSI, and 1783 underwent ET Freeze. For IUI, significant predictors of reduced success were increasing age (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.87–1.00, p < 0.058), BMI \(\ge \) 30 kg/m \(^2\) (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.19–1.10, p \(=\) 0.076), and longer duration of infertility (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.86–1.02, p = 0.116). For ICSI, significant predictors included age (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.92–0.95, p < 0.001), BMI \(\ge \) 30 kg/m \(^2\) (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.95, p \(=\) 0.018), fertilization rate (OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.21–2.50, p \(=\) 0.003), number of mature oocytes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.41–3.83, p \(=\) 0.001), and number of grade A embryos (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.04–1.82, p \(=\) 0.025). For ET Freeze, age (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95–0.99, p \(=\) 0.002) and number of previous abortions (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.60–0.99, p \(=\) 0.037) were significant negative predictors of success. The predictors of treatment success differ significantly across the three ART methods. For IUI, BMI, duration of infertility, and age were the main predictors. For ICSI, a broader set of factors including BMI, age, number of embryos, fertilization rate, and PCOS were influential. For ET Freeze, only age and number of previous abortions were significant. These findings highlight the importance of patient-specific factors in ART outcomes and suggest that tailored treatment strategies based on individual predictors may improve success rates. The proposed statistical and mathematical models provide valuable tools for clinicians to better counsel patients and optimize treatment selection.

Article.Title: Ambient-cured GGBS geopolymer concrete modified with alccofine, silica fume, or nano-silica: experiments and machine learning
Article.Authors: Sharma N.; Verma R.; Jain N.; Khan R.; Tiwari V.; Seema S.; Samreen M.; Paruthi S.
Article.Abstract: Ambient-cured geopolymer concrete (GPC) offers a promising route toward lower-carbon infrastructure by utilizing industrial by-products while avoiding the thermal energy required for conventional heat curing. However, achieving mechanical and durability performance comparable to heat-cured GPC under ambient conditions remains a major challenge. This study investigates two multi-scale binder-modification routes for ambient-cured GGBS geopolymer concrete using Alccofine (AF) together with either silica fume (SF) or nano-silica (NS). AF was fixed at 10% of binder mass, while SF was investigated at 10–30% and NS at 1–3%. The experimental program first establishes 100% GGBS benchmark mixtures cured under ambient conditions and at 60 and 90 °C and subsequently evaluates the modified ambient-cured mixtures in terms of compressive, split tensile and flexural strengths, sorptivity, chemical resistance, freeze–thaw resistance and rapid chloride penetrability. The best-performing AF10SF20 mixture, containing 10% Alccofine and 20% silica fume, achieved compressive strengths of 51.8 and 66.0 MPa at 28 and 90 days, respectively, with corresponding 90-day split tensile and flexural strengths of 4.0 and 6.7 MPa. The mixture exhibited initial and secondary sorptivity values of 0.095 and 0.035 mm/min 0.5 , respectively, and showed strength losses of only 9.6%, 7.6%, 5.8% and 3.1% after exposure to H 2 SO 4 , HCl, Na 2 SO 4 and NaCl, respectively. After freeze–thaw exposure, the mass and strength losses were limited to 3.0% and 6.0%, while the rapid chloride penetrability was 1450 C. Notably, AF10SF20 exceeded the 90 °C-cured benchmark in several key performance indicators, including long-term compressive and flexural strength and resistance to transport and environmental deterioration. In parallel, machine-learning models were developed for compressive-strength prediction, with particle-swarm-optimization-assisted XGBoost providing the best reported predictive performance. Explainable artificial intelligence using SHAP, LIME, partial-dependence and individual-conditional-expectation analyses identified the major influencing mixture parameters and revealed nonlinear responses consistent with the experimentally observed best performed dosages. The findings demonstrate the potential of multiscale binder modification to reduce dependence on thermal curing under the investigated laboratory conditions, while further field-scale validation is required to establish its applicability under variable construction environments.

Article.Title: Endothelial markers are associated with disseminated intravascular coagulation progression and clinical outcomes in sepsis
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhao H.; Liu L.; Wang N.; Zhang C.; Guo S.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Progression of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) is associated with poor outcomes in sepsis. Given the central role of endothelial injury in sepsis-associated coagulopathy, we investigated the associations of endothelium-related markers with DIC progression and clinical prognosis. In this prospective study, serum heparan sulfate (HS), hyaluronic acid (HA), syndecan-1 (SDC-1), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) were measured in 324 septic patients. Participants were divided into DIC progression and non-progression groups based on a ≥1-point increase in the DIC score from days 1 to 4, and further stratified into survivors or non-survivors according to the 28-day all-cause mortality. DIC progression occurred in 33.02% of the cohort, and the 28-day all-cause mortality rate was 25.00%. All four biomarkers were significantly elevated in patients with DIC progression. After adjustment for platelet count, albumin, fibrinogen, and septic shock, multivariable logistic regression identified HA, SDC‑1, and Ang‑2 as independent risk factors for DIC progression. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) for predicting DIC progression were 0.607 (0.551–0.660) for HS (ng/mL), 0.599 (0.544–0.653) for HA (ng/mL), 0.735 (0.683–0.782) for SDC-1 (ng/mL), and 0.706 (0.653–0.755) for Ang-2 (ng/mL). Multivariable Cox regression demonstrated that SDC‑1 and Ang‑2 were independently associated with 28‑day mortality. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a U-shaped association between platelet count and DIC progression, with both low and high levels linked to adverse outcomes. In conclusion, endothelium‑related markers are associated with DIC progression and 28‑day mortality in patients with sepsis, indicating their potential value for clinical risk stratification, though prospective validation remains needed.

Article.Title: Design and performance evaluation of a sensor-based device for monitoring soil properties
Article.Authors: Badr M.; Abdel-Aal N.; Noor M.; Abdeen M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sensors used in precision agriculture can support rapid, non-destructive, and cost-effective soil assessment for field-based decision-making. This study developed and evaluated an affordable multi-parameter sensor fusion device ($134) for measuring soil properties under contrasting field conditions. Field experiments were conducted across four evaluated soil matrices (clay, clay loam, loam, and sand) and four depth profiles (15, 30, 45, and 60 cm), with five independent field profiles per matrix, yielding 80 depth-specific observations. To assess internal predictive performance, the dataset was partitioned at the field-profile level using a stratified 70:30 internal hold-out scheme. Fourteen field profiles (56 depth-specific observations) were used for calibration, while six separate field profiles (24 depth-specific observations) were reserved for internal validation. This procedure assessed prediction on previously unseen profiles within the investigated soil matrices and sampling zones; it did not constitute external validation. Profile-based mixed-effects analysis identified statistically significant differences associated with the evaluated soil matrices, sampling depths, and their interaction (P < 0.01) for nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and moisture content (MC). The calibration relationships showed coefficients of determination ranging from R 2 = 0.8594 to 0.9996, while the corresponding sensor–laboratory measurements showed positive Pearson correlations ranging from 0.652 to 1.000. At the 15 cm depth, the highest observed N, P, and K values occurred in clay, clay loam, and loam matrices (clay: 80.0, 29.0, and 383.3 mg kg −1 ; clay loam: 61.6, 21.0, and 300.0 mg kg −1 ; loam: 46.5, 14.5, and 136.3 mg kg −1 ), compared with the evaluated sandy profiles (19.5, 9.3, and 82.0 mg kg −1 ). Soil pH ranged from 6.4 to 7.2, and moisture content was higher at the 60 cm depth. Bland–Altman analysis indicated a mean difference of 0.130 mg kg −1 , with limits of agreement from − 0.001 to 0.261 mg kg −1 . The plot showed no clear visual trend in measurement differences across the evaluated range, supporting consistency of sensor–laboratory agreement within the investigated dataset. The proposed platform provides an affordable option for site-specific soil monitoring and rapid field screening under the investigated conditions.

Article.Title: Modified MIND diet and symptoms of depression, anxiety, stress, visceral adiposity and cardiometabolic indices among Iranian adults: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Moabedi M.; Sadeghi O.; Zeydi M.; Moein M.; Aliakbari M.; Rostamian R.; Bagherniya M.; Saneei P.
Article.Abstract: Previous literature regarding the association between adherence to the Mediterranean-DASH Diet Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress was inconsistent. Moreover, it was not explored whether metabolic indices such as visceral adiposity index (VAI) or cardiometabolic index (CMI) may act as indirect influencers in these relations. We aimed to answer these questions by performing this cross-sectional study among Iranian adults. A total of 1,236 participants (796 women) with a mean age of 42.31 yr were included. Adherence to a modified MIND score (14 components; wine omitted because alcohol intake is unlikely to be reported reliably in this setting; range 0–14) was assessed with a 130-item dish-based semi-quantitative food-frequency questionnaire (FFQ). VAI and CMI were calculated via standard formulas using anthropometric measures and biomarkers from 12-h fast blood samples. Symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress were evaluated via a validated Persian version of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21). Based on the fully-adjusted model, participants in the third tertile of MIND had lower odds of having depressive symptoms (OR T3 vs. T1 = 0.59; 95%CI: 0.42–0.83) and anxiety (OR T3 vs. T1 = 0.66; 95%CI: 0.47–0.92), compared to those in the first tertile. In exploratory sex-stratified analyses, the association with depressive symptoms was significant in women (OR T3 vs. T1 = 0.57; 95%CI: 0.38–0.85) but not in men, and the association with anxiety symptoms was significant in men (OR T3 vs. T1 = 0.43; 95%CI: 0.23–0.78) but not in women; however, there was no significant interaction by sex (P interaction > 0.05 for all three outcomes). There was a significant nonlinear association between MIND score and depression; a score of 4.7–7 (median) was associated with higher odds of having depressive symptoms, and a score between 7 and 10.3 was associated with lower odds of the symptoms (P nonlinearity = 0.036). Modified MIND was not associated with stress symptoms (P > 0.05), VAI or CMI, and VAI and CMI did not statistically account for the associations in exploratory mediation analyses. There was a significant inverse association between adherence to a modified MIND score and odds of depressive and anxiety symptoms. There was no association for stress, VAI, or CMI.

Article.Title: Phase aligned EEG source space features for distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from frontotemporal dementia
Article.Authors: Lin J.; Sheng J.; Gong Z.; Zhang R.; Sun Z.; Cheng Y.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) share similarities in cognitive deficits and behavioural changes, increasing the difficulty of their differential diagnosis. Electroencephalography (EEG), as a non-invasive, cost-effective and easy-to-use tool that reflects brain activity in real time, provides potential support for differentiating AD and FTD. We propose a source-space feature method based on EEG phase alignment, where dynamic time warping (DTW) enhances inter-trial phase synchrony in the θ, α, β, and γ bands, sLORETA extracts brain region energy features, and a random forest classifier performs classification. In a dataset comprising 36 AD cases, 23 FTD cases, and 29 CN, the classification accuracies for AD vs. FTD and FTD vs. CN reached 94.21% and 90.63%, respectively. Abnormalities in the AD group were primarily observed in the θ and γ bands, involving multiple cognition-related regions, whereas the FTD group exhibited β-band abnormalities predominantly affecting the parietal lobe and default mode network. These findings suggest that source-space features based on phase alignment can effectively distinguish the neural signatures of AD and FTD.

Article.Title: Performance assessment of an industrial F-class combined cycle power plant with an air-cooled condenser using energy and exergy analysis
Article.Authors: Motahar S.; Heidari M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Combined cycle power plants are among the most efficient technologies for large scale electricity generation. This study presents a comprehensive energy and exergy analysis of an F-class combined cycle power plant equipped with dual three-pressure heat recovery steam generators, supplementary firing, and an air-cooled condenser. A detailed thermodynamic model was developed and validated against the manufacturer’s design data before being used to evaluate the plant under both design and representative off-design operating conditions. Under the design condition, the plant achieved a net power output of 734.3 MW, a net thermal efficiency of 54.6%, and an overall exergy efficiency of 54.1%. The energy analysis identified the air-cooled condenser as the largest source of energy loss because of heat rejection, whereas the exergy analysis showed that the gas turbine was responsible for approximately 71% of the total plant exergy destruction, followed by the heat recovery steam generator (15%). The steam turbine and heat recovery steam generator exhibited exergy efficiencies of 82.0% and 81.2%, respectively. The influence of ambient temperature, inlet air evaporative cooling, and supplementary firing was also investigated under representative operating scenarios. High ambient temperatures significantly reduced the plant power output, while evaporative cooling effectively recovered part of the lost capacity with a smaller efficiency penalty than supplementary firing. The proposed methodology provides a practical framework for the thermodynamic assessment and performance improvement of large scale air-cooled combined cycle power plants operating under water scarce conditions.

Article.Title: Association between hemoglobin glycation index and mortality in critically ill patients with intracerebral hemorrhage: a cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Zhu H.; Wei W.; Yang Z.; Xiao Z.; Li M.; Xin W.; Xie G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) carries high mortality in the neurocritical care setting, and metabolic risk stratification remains challenging. Conventional glycemic markers, including acute glucose and HbA1c, may be influenced by stress hyperglycemia and altered erythrocyte dynamics in critical illness. The hemoglobin glycation index (HGI), defined as the discrepancy between measured HbA1c and glucose-predicted HbA1c, may capture glycation–glucose discordance, but its relevance in critically ill ICH patients remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 1,688 critically ill patients with ICH from the MIMIC-IV database. HGI was calculated as measured HbA1c minus predicted HbA1c derived from the first available baseline glucose measurement and categorized into quartiles. The main outcome was 365-day all-cause mortality after ICU admission. Associations between HGI and 365-day mortality were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. Dose–response relationships were examined with restricted cubic splines. Very low HGI was associated with higher mortality across multiple time horizons. In the fully adjusted model, compared with Q1, the adjusted hazard ratios for 7-day mortality were 0.41 (95% CI, 0.25–0.66), 0.60 (0.38–0.94), and 0.41 (0.25–0.66) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. Similar inverse associations were observed for 14-, 28-, 90-, and 365-day mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses showed an overall inverse association between HGI and mortality, with little evidence of strong nonlinearity. In critically ill patients with ICH, very low HGI was associated with increased mortality. This finding may reflect a high-risk hematologic–metabolic phenotype involving acute stress hyperglycemia and altered HbA1c interpretation rather than a direct protective effect of higher HGI. HGI may serve as an exploratory adjunct marker for risk stratification, but further validation with detailed glucose timing, erythrocyte-related factors, and transfusion data is warranted.

Article.Title: Strain-dependent internalization and persistence of Cutibacterium acnes differentially alter biofilm formation
Article.Authors: Rwayane K.; Ruffier d’Epenoux L.; Baud’huin M.; Corvec S.
Article.Abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is increasingly recognized as a major pathogen in orthopedic implant-associated infections, particularly in shoulder prostheses. Its ability to form biofilm and interact with bone cells may contribute to chronicity and diagnostic challenges. This study aimed to investigate the strain-dependent internalization and persistence of C. acnes within osteoblasts and their impact on biofilm formation and bone cell function. Seven C. acnes clinical strains were studied. Internalization assays were performed using murine osteoblastic cell lines modified for β1 integrin (OB β1 +/+ and OB β1 −/− ). Internalization and intracellular persistence, biofilm formation before and after internalization, bone mineralization (alizarin red staining), gene expression (RT-qPCR), and IL-6 secretion were evaluated. Internalization capacity varied significantly between strains, with low overall rates (<0.5%). β1 integrin appeared to contribute partially to bacterial entry (decrease internalization rate from 50 to 97% depending on the strain in β1 −/− cells). Most of the strains persisted intracellularly up to 4–10 days. Biofilm production was strain-dependent and modified after internalization. No significant effect on osteoblastic mineralization or gene expression were observed. IL-6 secretion showed minimal variation in our conditions. These findings confirm that C. acnes can be internalized and persist within osteoblasts, by using partially β1 integrin pathway, contributing to chronic implant infections. Internalization influences bacterial phenotype, biofilm production ability but does not significantly impair osteoblastic function in this model. The role of intracellular reservoirs and alternative entry pathways warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: State mindfulness during physical activity moderates cognitive fusion linking intolerance of uncertainty to bedtime procrastination in university students
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Yang Y.; Lai Y.; Yang Y.; Luo L.; Qin T.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Bedtime procrastination is a common nighttime behavioral problem among university students. Grounded in the psychological flexibility framework and the cognitive model of insomnia, this study examined the association between intolerance of uncertainty and bedtime procrastination among university students, with particular attention to the mediating role of cognitive fusion and the moderating role of state mindfulness during physical activity. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in February 2026 using cluster sampling among 1,912 university students. The Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12 (IUS-12), Cognitive Fusion Questionnaire (CFQ-7), State Mindfulness Scale for Physical Activity-2 Short Form (SMS-PA-2), and Bedtime Procrastination Scale (BPS) were used to assess the core variables. Descriptive statistics and confirmatory factor analysis were conducted in SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 26.0, and statistical mediation and moderation were estimated with the PROCESS macro (Models 4 and 14). Intolerance of uncertainty was significantly positively correlated with cognitive fusion and bedtime procrastination. Statistical mediation analysis yielded a significant indirect association involving cognitive fusion, while the direct association between intolerance of uncertainty and bedtime procrastination was non-significant after cognitive fusion was included in the model. State mindfulness during physical activity significantly moderated the positive association between cognitive fusion and bedtime procrastination. Simple slope analysis showed that the positive cognitive fusion–bedtime procrastination association was smaller at higher levels of state mindfulness during physical activity. Higher intolerance of uncertainty was associated with greater bedtime procrastination, with a significant statistical indirect association involving cognitive fusion. Higher state mindfulness during physical activity was associated with a smaller positive cognitive fusion–bedtime procrastination slope. These findings are cross-sectional and should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal mediation, causal buffering, or intervention effects.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence promotes urban green innovation in China with regional spillovers and asymmetric climate-risk thresholds
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Guo Y.; Niu Z.; Meng K.
Article.Abstract: We systematically examine the impact of artificial intelligence on urban green innovation in the context of climate risk. The results demonstrate that artificial intelligence substantially promotes green innovation, an effect primarily transmitted through expanded openness to trade and enhanced scientific-research investment, with the digital economy playing a positive moderating role. Spatial analysis reveals that artificial intelligence advances in one city generate significant positive spillovers that enhance the green innovation performance of neighboring cities. This spatial pattern exhibits pronounced regional heterogeneity: the western region displays significantly positive indirect effects, whereas the eastern and central regions are dominated by direct effects. Threshold effect analysis uncovers differentiated responses to physical climate risks: artificial intelligence’s benefits are weakened once extreme high-temperature days exceed the threshold but strengthened once extreme low-temperature days exceed their threshold, while extreme precipitation exerts no discernible threshold influence. Finally, higher transition risk is found to amplify the beneficial impact of artificial intelligence on green innovation.

Article.Title: Identification of esculin as a direct modulator of IGF1 in cervical cancer with integrated computational and experimental studies
Article.Authors: Wu J.; Wang N.; Gao W.; Song X.
Article.Abstract: Aberrant activation of the insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) signaling axis plays a central role in tumor proliferation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Although most therapeutic strategies have focused on inhibition of the IGF1 receptor (IGF1R), direct targeting of the IGF1 ligand remains largely underexplored. An integrated computational-experimental pipeline was employed to identify phytochemicals that directly modulate IGF1. In the computational phase, a library of 75 natural compounds was screened by molecular docking against model 11 of the NMR conformer of IGF1 (PDB ID: 1PMX), followed by ADMET profiling, PASS-based biological activity prediction, and 500-ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations complemented by essential dynamics, free-energy landscape (FEL), and MM-PBSA analyses. In the experimental phase, the top candidates were evaluated using in vitro cytotoxicity assays, ELISA-based IGF1 quantification, and fluorescence spectroscopy with Stern–Volmer analysis. Esculin and rotenone were identified as the top-ranked binders from docking analyses. ADMET profiling indicated more favorable pharmacokinetic and safety characteristics for esculin. PASS predictions supported anticancer and antimetastatic potential for both compounds. Long-timescale MD simulations indicated that esculin altered IGF1 conformational dynamics, as reflected by reduced backbone deviation, controlled residue flexibility, persistent hydrogen-bonding interactions, and confinement within a distinct thermodynamically favorable energy basin compared with apo IGF1 and the rotenone-bound complex; MM-PBSA re-scoring returned comparable total binding free energies for the two complexes. In vitro assays subsequently demonstrated a clear dose-dependent cytotoxic effect of esculin in HeLa cells, whereas rotenone showed minimal antiproliferative effects. Esculin significantly reduced intracellular IGF1 protein levels (p < 0.001) and directly interacted with recombinant IGF1, as indicated by fluorescence quenching. Esculin is identified as a promising natural IGF1-binding compound with modulatory potential, supported by consistent computational and experimental evidence. These findings highlight its potential as a lead compound for the development of IGF1-targeted anticancer therapies.

Article.Title: Moment-based estimation for the Zipf law
Article.Authors: Ma J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Zipf’s law appears across many disciplines, but real datasets typically provide only frequency counts, and empirical ranks derived from noisy samples can differ from the true ranks, biasing common estimators of the Zipf exponent. Approximate Bayesian computation (ABC) mitigates this bias but relies on repeated accept–reject simulation with potentially large runtime. We propose a moment-based estimator that infers the Zipf exponent from type–token statistics alone, avoiding rank matching and accept–reject sampling. The estimator matches an empirical type–token curve constructed from a single sample to the theoretical expected number of distinct types, reducing estimation to a one-dimensional optimization. In simulations spanning Zipf exponents 1.10–2.00 and sample sizes of 100, 1000, and 10,000, the mean squared error of both methods generally increases with the exponent; the moment-based estimator is most competitive at the smallest exponents, while ABC is more accurate over most of the grid. Averaged over the simulation grid, it is roughly three orders of magnitude faster than ABC in geometric mean runtime. Additional simulations reveal sensitivity to finite support, Zipf–Mandelbrot deviations, and short-range dependence.

Article.Title: Data-driven hierarchical adaptive protection scheme for recloser coordination in active distribution networks
Article.Authors: Yazdaninejadi A.
Article.Abstract: Recent advances in data-driven protection have created new opportunities for adaptive protection of active distribution networks (ADNs). However, for complex multi-feeder systems, training a single global model often results in high computational complexity, overlapping fault signatures among feeders, model confusion, and reduced prediction accuracy, particularly under varying fault resistance conditions. Therefore, this paper proposes a self-adaptive protection strategy for automatic recloser setting that overcomes these limitations through a hierarchical framework. Fault transmitters installed at feeder branches provide rapid hardware-based fault pre-localization, enabling the protection algorithm to identify the faulted feeder before any decision process is executed. Consequently, only a lightweight localized data-driven linear regression model trained with data from the corresponding protection zone is activated, significantly reducing the search space while improving estimation accuracy and computational efficiency. The localized model estimates the prospective fuse current under different fault conditions, including varying fault resistance levels, to adaptively adjust the recloser operating time according to the fuse clearing time. The proposed method is validated on the IEEE 33-bus testbed under various fault locations, distributed generation (DG) penetration levels, and fault resistances. Simulation results demonstrate accurate fuse current estimation under diverse operating conditions. In addition, the hierarchical protection framework significantly reduces the operating time of the recloser for permanent faults on both the main feeder and downstream feeders, where the recloser operates as the primary and backup protection device, respectively, while preserving the fuse-saving philosophy and reliable fuse–recloser coordination. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective solution for adaptive protection of modern ADNs.

Article.Title: Coupling calibrated aerial perception to adaptive UAV emergency logistics scheduling: a YOLOv8–reinforcement learning closed-loop proof of concept
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; He R.
Article.Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles can survey an affected area and deliver relief, but most scheduling studies assume that demand is already known. We examine what happens when demand must instead be inferred from imperfect aerial detection. The framework combines an empirically characterized YOLOv8-Nano observation model, a disaster-situation state map, and a confidence-aware PPO scheduler in a simulated re-observe–re-plan loop. The detector achieved mAP50 = 0.251 and an end-to-end CPU rate of approximately 22 frames per second. Its global ECE was 0.0104, whereas the people-group ECE increased to 0.192 at the operational confidence threshold. Across seven independent training seeds, confidence-awareness significantly increased the composite training reward (Wilcoxon p = 0.016), but delivery rate, coverage, and unmet demand did not differ from the confidence-blind controller, and average delay was longer under the confidence-aware policy. This reward difference is interpreted as a training diagnostic because the two controllers use different reward definitions. A single-replication 2 × 2 factorial analysis indicated that either component individually recorded higher delivery than the baseline, whereas their combination did not; this exploratory pattern has not been confirmed across multiple training seeds. Within the tested operating range, the coupled system remained below the perfect-information reference. An independent recall–FDR sweep indicated that delivery was more sensitive to false-discovery rate than to recall for the fixed policy evaluated. These findings are limited to a controlled simulation with temporally independent detection errors, a synthetic demand proxy derived from a non-disaster benchmark, and a two-dimensional grid. Under these conditions, perception strongly limits logistics performance, while the effect of confidence-awareness on relief outcomes remains unestablished.

Article.Title: Symptom management self efficacy relates to self perceived burden and IADL in lung cancer patients with treatment associated pneumonitis
Article.Authors: Zhi F.; Fu J.; Bai L.; Liu X.; Sun Y.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: To examine symptom management self-efficacy, self-perceived burden, and impairment in instrumental activities of daily living among patients with lung cancer who developed treatment-associated pneumonitis (TAP) after radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy, and to analyze the relationships among these factors. This cross-sectional study included 140 TAP patients from October 2024 to June 2025. Data were collected using the Self-Efficacy for Symptom Management Scale (SESMs), Self-Perceived Burden Scale (SPBS), and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale (IADL). Pearson correlation, group comparisons, and hierarchical regression were performed. Mean SESMs, SPBS, and IADL scores were (6.00 ± 0.38), (34.35 ± 5.00), and (21.04 ± 4.00), respectively. SESMs scores were negatively correlated with SPBS scores ( r =-0.663) and IADL scores ( r =-0.634) (both P < 0.001); SPBS scores were positively correlated with IADL scores ( r = 0.429, P < 0.001). After covariate adjustment, SESMs scores additionally explained 20.5% of the variance in SPBS scores (ΔR² = 0.205) and 17.5% of the variance in IADL scores (ΔR² = 0.175). SPBS and IADL scores jointly explained an additional 21.0% of the variance in SESMs score (ΔR² = 0.210). Among patients with TAP, those with higher symptom management self-efficacy had lower self-perceived burden and less impairment in instrumental activities of daily living.

Article.Title: An emergency decision support framework for flight-deck accidents: integrating dynamic adjudication, multi-agent cooperation, and hierarchical path planning
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Hou Y.; Wang K.; Wang B.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: The flight deck of a naval vessel is a high-risk operational environment in which a single initiating event can precipitate coupled hazard cascades encompassing concurrent fire propagation, progressive casualty deterioration, and damage-induced stability degradation. Conventional pre-plan-driven response approaches are architecturally ill-suited to such multi-hazard, temporally evolving scenarios, as they cannot adapt to stochastic hazard interactions in real time. This paper presents the Intelligent Emergency Decision-support Framework for Flight-deck Safety (IEDFS), a closed-loop architecture comprising three tightly coupled core modules: (1) a knowledge–data dual-driven dynamic reasoning engine that performs online fire propagation modelling, casualty condition state estimation, real-time confidence updating, and damage stability constraint evaluation; (2) an attention-enhanced multi-agent cooperative decision module in which the task-allocation problem is formalised as a Decentralised Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and solved via an Attention-QMIX network preserving heterogeneous agent role attributes; and (3) a hierarchical time-varying path planning module combining a temporally extended A* algorithm for global route generation with D* Lite for local dynamic replanning, enabling simultaneous hazard avoidance, stretcher-carry task scheduling, and inter-agent conflict resolution. At each decision cycle, the reasoning engine furnishes updated situational assessments to the decision module, whose cooperative policy outputs are consumed by the path planner—completing a feedback loop that sustains adaptive response under continuously evolving hazard states. Validation on the FDAS-Sim platform across five progressively escalating accident scenarios demonstrates that IEDFS improves the critical-casualty golden-hour treatment rate by 26.3% points, reduces fire containment time by 40.1%, decreases flight deck operational recovery time by 36.1%, and lowers the damage stability exceedance rate by 53.2% relative to the static rule based baseline (B1), computed from the scenario-averaged means over five scenarios and ten independent runs. Ablation studies confirm the independent contribution of each module and quantify the synergistic performance gain from system integration. These results position IEDFS as a viable methodological foundation for intelligent decision support and simulation-based proficiency training in flight deck emergency response, within the modelling fidelity of the FDAS-Sim platform.

Article.Title: An inconsistent scaling relationship between tail length and hindwing area among five species (and one subspecies) of European butterfly (Order: Lepidoptera)
Article.Authors: Broadbent J.; Nudds R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The function of butterfly hindwing tails, narrow protuberances on the hindwing’s trailing edge, is usually attributed to predator evasion (mimicking the head to divert attacks away from vital body parts), or an aerodynamic function. One way of investigating these alternative hypotheses is to determine how hindwing tail length ( L tail ) scales with body size (hindwing area, A hind ). If evolved to mimic a false head, or for aerodynamic performance, we would expect L tail to scale isometrically with A hind ( L tail ∝ A hind 1/2 ), indicating relative similar mimicry and aerodynamic effects across butterfly sizes. If the anti-predator stimulus was optimised for one signal size, we would expect no relationship between L tail and A hind . Accordingly, here, the scaling relationship between L tail and A hind was determined in six species ( Thecla betulae , Favonius quercus , Lampides boeticus , Iphiclides podalirius , Papilio machaon gorganus and Papilio machaon britannicus ) using measurements from museum specimens. No sex-specific differences in scaling patterns were found, suggesting sexual selection plays no role in driving L tail in the species investigated in this study. The scaling between L tail and A hind differed among species, and implied that in some species L tail is likely the result of size dependent trade-offs, possibly between anti-predator effectiveness and aerodynamic costs, which are, in turn, species specific.

Article.Title: Combined effects of silica nanoparticles and putrescine on postharvest quality and vase life of ‘Pilaster White’ cut stock (Matthiola incana)
Article.Authors: pourrashid K.; Jabbarzadeh Z.; Amiri J.
Article.Abstract: Matthiola incana (stock) is an economically important ornamental species with limited postharvest longevity, which is associated with oxidative damage and deterioration of cellular membranes. This study investigated the effects of preharvest foliar application of silica nanoparticles (SiNPs; 0, 50, 100, and 200 mg L⁻¹) and putrescine (Put; 0, 1.5, and 3 mM), applied individually and in combination, on the postharvest quality and vase life of ‘Pilaster White’ cut stock ( Matthiola incana ). The experiment was conducted under greenhouse conditions using a completely randomized factorial design with three replications. Postharvest assessments included relative fresh weight, relative solution uptake, petal relative water content, electrolyte leakage, malondialdehyde (MDA), total phenolic and flavonoid contents, phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL) and polyphenol oxidase (PPO) activities, antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, APX, GPX, and SOD), and vase life. The combined application of 50 or 100 mg L⁻¹ SiNPs with 1.5 mM Put produced the most favorable overall postharvest responses. These treatments improved water relations, as indicated by greater relative solution uptake and maintenance of petal relative water content, and reduced electrolyte leakage and MDA accumulation compared with the untreated control. They also increased the activities of antioxidant enzymes and PAL, enhanced total phenolic and flavonoid contents, and reduced PPO activity during the postharvest period. Vase life increased from 12.66 days in the untreated control to 25.33 and 25.66 days following the combined application of 50 and 100 mg L⁻¹ SiNPs with 1.5 mM Put, respectively. These physiological and biochemical responses were associated with improved postharvest quality and prolonged vase life. Overall, preharvest foliar application of SiNPs at 50–100 mg L⁻¹ in combination with 1.5 mM Put appears to be a promising approach for extending the vase life of cut stock flowers under the conditions tested.

Article.Title: Turkish adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the entrepreneurship scale for nursing students
Article.Authors: Şimşek D.; Demir M.; Turan G.
Article.Abstract: To adapt to changing healthcare conditions and develop innovative solutions, nurses need entrepreneurial skills. Assessing the entrepreneurship levels of nursing students is important for informing educational programs and supporting research in nursing education. Therefore, this study aimed to adapt the Entrepreneurship Scale for Nursing Students into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. This methodological study was conducted with 300 nursing students at a state university between October and December 2025. The 25-item Entrepreneurship Scale for Nursing Students was adapted into Turkish through forward translation, back translation, expert panel review, and pilot testing to ensure linguistic and cultural appropriateness. Content validity was evaluated by five experts, and item-level and scale-level content validity indices (I-CVI and S-CVI) were calculated. Construct validity was examined using the Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin (KMO) test, Bartlett’s test of sphericity, and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) of the original 25-item, four-factor model. Reliability was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha, McDonald’s omega, corrected item–total correlations, and test–retest analysis. The I-CVI values ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, and the S-CVI was 0.98. The KMO value was 0.945, and Bartlett’s test of sphericity was statistically significant (χ²=4000.349, p < 0.001). CFA indicated an acceptable fit of the original 25-item, four-factor model, with standardized factor loadings ranging from 0.430 to 0.770 (χ²/df = 2.88, RMSEA = 0.078, CFI = 0.97, TLI = 0.97, SRMR = 0.057, and RMR = 0.036). The total-scale Cronbach’s alpha coefficient was 0.943 and McDonald’s omega was 0.942, although the Risk Acceptance subscale showed comparatively lower internal consistency (α = 0.615, ω = 0.615). The test–retest ICC for the total scale was 0.972. Convergent and discriminant validity were not fully supported, as AVE values were below 0.50 and the Fornell–Larcker criterion was not fully satisfied. The Turkish version of the Entrepreneurship Scale for Nursing Students demonstrated promising psychometric properties and an acceptable fit to the original four-factor model in the present sample. However, the lower reliability of the Risk Acceptance subscale and limitations in convergent and discriminant validity warrant cautious interpretation. Further validation in larger, multicentre, and more diverse nursing student populations is recommended before broader application.

Article.Title: A moderated mediation model of depression and insomnia in adolescents
Article.Authors: Xiao T.; Peng H.; Liang Z.; Pan M.; Wang Y.; Wang B.; Xiao R.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between depression and insomnia among adolescents and to investigate the mediating role of short video addiction (SVA) and the moderating role of physical activity (PA) in this association. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 725 adolescents from Hunan and Sichuan provinces, China. Depression, insomnia, SVA, and PA were assessed using standardized measures. Descriptive statistics and correlation analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. The PROCESS macro for SPSS was used to test the mediating effect of SVA (Model 4) and the moderated mediation model involving PA (Model 7), with 5,000 bootstrap resamples used to estimate 95% confidence intervals. Depression was positively associated with both SVA and insomnia, whereas PA was negatively associated with depression and SVA. SVA partially mediated the association between depression and insomnia, with the indirect effect accounting for 6.94% of the total effect. PA significantly moderated the association between depression and SVA ( β = −0.095, SE = 0.044, t = − 2.169). Simple slope analysis further showed that the positive association between depression and SVA progressively weakened as PA levels increased, with conditional effects of β = 0.313 at one standard deviation below the mean, β = 0.269 at the mean, and β = 0.173 at one standard deviation above the mean. SVA may represent one behavioral pathway linking depressive symptoms with insomnia among adolescents, although its mediating effect was relatively modest. Higher levels of PA were associated with a weaker positive relationship between depression and SVA, suggesting a potential protective role of PA. From a practical perspective, these findings support the potential value of school-based mental health strategies that increase opportunities for regular PA through physical education, active recess, and extracurricular sports, while also providing guidance on reducing excessive short-video use, particularly before bedtime, and promoting healthy sleep habits. Given the cross-sectional design, these implications should be interpreted cautiously and further evaluated in longitudinal and intervention studies.

Article.Title: WSPI: a wavelet-structured popularity index for stable content ranking via trend–noise separation
Article.Authors: Pirahesh S.; Mohammad Khanli L.; Baradarani A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Data popularity estimation ranks items by their share of demand to guide caching. Scores built from raw counts in a short window move with transient spikes; a long window is stable but reacts late and is less accurate. Our main novelty is to score popularity from the trend that a wavelet transform extracts from each item’s demand, not from its raw counts. DWT+AF and DTCWT+AF weight this trend by recency, with the discrete and dual-tree complex wavelet transforms; WSPI multiplies the DTCWT trend by a bounded factor from the spread of energy over the scales. We compare these three training-free methods with six conventional baselines on YouTube, NYC Yellow Taxi (three granularities) and MovieLens (two), over 131,443 windows, with block-bootstrap confidence intervals. With the baselines at their default 7-slot window, a wavelet-based method has the highest ranking stability (RSI@10) in all six scenarios, and WSPI has 2.0–2.8 times lower rank displacement under injected spikes than the best conventional baseline in each scenario, excluding PFRF, whose NDCG@10 is below 0.6. With an equal 64-slot window, a moving average is more stable and WSPI more accurate. WSPI offers an accuracy–stability trade-off and reacts later than short-window baselines to genuine surges.

Article.Title: Photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting of exhaled-breath metabolites for non-invasive disease screening
Article.Authors: Tatavarti R.; Nadimpalli S.; Pachiyappan A.
Article.Abstract: Optical breath diagnostics normally require molecule-specific spectroscopy. We ask instead how much diagnostic structure survives in the least expensive optical readout available: a single fixed-wavelength diode laser and a dual-axis position-sensing photodiode, giving three channels — back-scattered intensity ( $$\:I$$ ) and two beam-position coordinates ( $$\:x,y$$ ). Seven calibration classes, comprising five disease-linked breath-metabolite mixtures (disease-linked surrogates) covering established gas concentration ranges (in ppb / ppm), a healthy-air surrogate and an ambient control, were injected at constant mass flow, into a sealed chamber and recorded at 25 kHz, later down sampled to 10 Hz for each run for easing the computational load, over nineteen runs. Detection of any injection is effectively certain within seconds: mean Mahalanobis distances from the ambient cluster are 176 to 447, against a within-cluster mean of 1.6. Concentration is recovered by cubic intensity–concentration calibrations across nine gas channels, with coefficients of determination from 0.966 to 0.997. All seven class centroids separate, and a trajectory-aware nearest-template rule assigns 73.7% of runs correctly on resubstitution. Under leave-one-run-out validation, however, accuracy falls to 52.6% against a chance level of 14.3%, and the beam-deflection channels are shown to be dominated by a common pressure-driven refractive-index gradient rather than by composition - an artefact of the design and architecture of the experiment which can be easily modified to improve accuracy. The three channel readout ( $$\:I,x,y$$ ), therefore establishes a validated lower bound for minimal optics, and quantifies precisely what separates that bound from classification-grade breath screening.

Article.Title: Molecular typing reveals sub-microscopic P. ovale and P. malariae infections associated with anemia among asymptomatic populations in the Sudano-Sahelian region of Chad
Article.Authors: Ngakia T.; Akawung P.; Barou Z.; Ndumu E.; Asongha M.; Fotso-Toguem Y.; Mugenzi L.; Shey R.; Amir A.; Wondji C.; Betehndoh E.; Nkemngo F.
Article.Abstract: Unravelling malaria parasite species composition is critical for malaria elimination, especially in the Sudano-Sahelian seasonal transmission geography. Here, we employed a suite of RDT, microscopy, and PCR on 601 blood samples collected between November 2024 and January 2025 in a community-based cross-sectional study to examine the local Plasmodium species and assess the associated clinical impact on hemoglobin level in a setting characterized by intensive deployment of malaria control interventions. The findings reveal an RDT, microscopy and PCR-positive malaria prevalence of 23.6% (142/601), 28.1% (169/601), and 57.6% (346/601), respectively. Among PCR-detected Plasmodium infections, P. falciparum mono-infection was most common [58.1% (201/346)]. Sub-patent non-falciparum mono-infections included P. malariae [2.6% (9/346)] and P. ovale species [2.0% (7/346)]. Multi-species infections occurred at varying frequency, including P. falciparum/P. malariae [11.3% (39/346)], P. falciparum/P. ovale [17.6% (61/346)], P. malariae/P. ovale [3.2% (11/346)], and P. falciparum / P. malariae / P. ovale [5.2% (18/346)]. Co-infections were predominant among the 6–15 years and > 40 years age groups [OR = 7.3 (95% CI 4.1–11.5), p = 0.004]. Hemoglobin concentration was significantly lower (Welch's independent-samples t-test: mean difference = − 2.29 g/dL; 95% CI − 2.51 to − 2.08; p < 0.001) among Plasmodium -infected individuals [n = 346; mean Hb = 9.58 ± 1.40 g/dL] compared with non-infected individuals [n = 255; mean Hb = 12.6 ± 1.29 g/dL]. Non-falciparum infections (comprising P. malariae and P. ovale mono-infections and P. malariae + P. ovale co-infections) were associated with moderate anemia [Hb level = 9.3 g/dL; OR = 3.4, (95% CI 1.6–7.2), p = 0.03]. Further molecular typing revealed the circulation of P. ovale curtisi (36/70; 51.4%) and P. ovale wallikeri (19/70; 27.1%) sibling subspecies, and sequence alignment of the merozoite surface protein-1 gene of nine local Chadian P. malariae isolates indicates probable low genetic diversity (π = 0.002, Hd = 0.72) and phylogenetic kinship with the Cameroon historical reference strain, suggesting geographical relatedness with potential implications on cross-border malaria control efforts. Cumulatively, our study underscores the silent circulation of non-falciparum species and provides evidence to the Chad National Malaria Control Programme for policy reforms on a comprehensive public health strategy that extends beyond P. falciparum to include all relevant malaria parasite species towards the elimination goal.
