Article.Title: Development of a clinical prediction model and risk score for extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing urinary tract infection in a tertiary-care outpatient setting
Article.Authors: Kliangchuai N.; Sornsenee P.
Article.Abstract: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organisms are common in outpatient urinary tract infections (UTIs). However, practical risk stratification tools for outpatient care are limited. In this retrospective cohort study, we included 993 culture-confirmed UTI episodes from 710 adults attending outpatient clinics at a tertiary-care hospital in Thailand between 2020 and 2024. Predictors of ESBL-producing UTI were identified using Firth’s penalized logistic regression and incorporated into a point-based clinical risk score. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. ESBL-producing UTI accounted for 34.4% of all UTIs. Bedridden status, underlying urinary tract disease, recent catheter exposure, prior ESBL-positive urine culture, recent systemic antibiotic exposure, current systemic corticosteroid therapy, and recent chemotherapy were independent predictors. The score demonstrated favorable apparent discrimination (AUROC 0.832, 95% patient-level bootstrap CI 0.801–0.862) and underwent patient-level bootstrap internal validation. At the cutoff score of ≥ 5, which provided the maximum Youden index in this study population, the sensitivity was 79.8%; specificity, 76.5%; positive predictive value, 64.1%; and negative predictive value, 87.8%. In summary, following external validation, the score may support empirical antibiotic selection and antimicrobial stewardship in similar tertiary-care outpatient populations.

Article.Title: Resolving hidden interface-trap capture times through stochastic current transients in multitrap nanoscale transistors
Article.Authors: Lee D.; Park J.; Han J.; Kim S.
Article.Abstract: Charge trapping at semiconductor–dielectric interfaces governs threshold-voltage instability, low-frequency noise, and stochastic variability in nanoscale transistors. In the intermediate multitrap regime, the drain-current transient is neither a defect-resolved signal from a single trap nor a fully averaged ensemble response, making the underlying trap kinetics difficult to infer directly. Here, a framework combining pulsed current–voltage measurement and self-consistent stochastic modeling is introduced for extracting statistical capture-time descriptors of interface-trap ensembles from sensing-phase drain-current transients. The approach analyzes repeated subthreshold transients using both the mean current and its cycle-to-cycle fluctuation, while explicitly incorporating trap-to-trap dispersion, sensing-bias-dependent capture kinetics, and electrostatic feedback induced by progressive trap filling. Simultaneous fitting across multiple sensing biases identifies a common model-constrained parameter pair within an assumed log-normal parameterization of the capture-time-constant distribution. Within the assumed model, this analysis distinguishes intrinsic trap-to-trap kinetic disorder from measurement-induced electrostatic renormalization, revealing that the measured transient is not a direct image of the intrinsic time-constant spectrum but a dynamically reshaped response governed by finite-ensemble stochasticity and channel electrostatics. The framework provides a physics-based route for extracting hidden multitrap kinetic descriptors from stochastic electronic transients in nanoscale devices.

Article.Title: Sterna migration optimization-based uncertainty-aware energy scheduling in hybrid solar and wind power systems using graph diffusion learning
Article.Authors: Karthick B.; Rao S.; Somasundaram P.; Manikandan G.
Article.Abstract: Operational uncertainty in hybrid networks that integrate solar Photovoltaic (PV) and wind power is considerable and primarily caused by the unpredictable changes in the generation of renewables and the demand for power, which has a negative impact on reliability, power quality, and cost-effectiveness alike. In this respect, the research work under discussion puts forward a comprehensive uncertainty reduction framework that integrates optimal energy scheduling with predictive modelling in order to efficiently control the nonlinear interactions of PV generation, wind power, load demand, and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The proposed framework, called StMA-DGDNN, integrates the Sterna Migration Algorithm and a Decoupled Graph Diffusion Neural Network. In this framework, StMA minimizes Total System Cost (TSC), Annual Energy Losses (AEL), Energy Not Supplied (ENS), and Voltage Deviation (VD), thus optimizing the hybrid PV-WT-BESS dispatch. On the other hand, DGDNN captures spatial-temporal dependencies through graph diffusion and attention mechanisms, and performs uncertainty-aware nodal prediction of PV power, wind power, and load demand. The suggested system has been put into practice and examined in the MATLAB/Simulink setting, and its efficacy was measured against the performance of several current optimization methods like Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks with Particle Swarm Optimization (DCGAN-PSO), Artificial Ecosystem-based Optimization with Opposition-Based Learning (AEO-OBL), Particle Swarm Optimization with Sine Cosine Optimization (PSO-SCO), Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA), and Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA). The comparative results demonstrate that the proposed StMA-DGDNN achieves the lowest TSC of $1,402,300, reduces AEL to 894.24 kWh, limits ENS to 4.21 MWh, and maintains VD at 0.2724 p.u., outperforming all benchmark methods. Statistical and ablation analyses further confirm the robustness of the approach and highlight that the synergistic integration of optimization and prediction is the key contributor to the observed performance improvements. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and reliable solution for uncertainty-aware operation of hybrid PV-WT power networks.

Article.Title: Biobased phytic acid as a multifunctional structural and electrochemical modifier for high-ionic-conductivity PEO–LiTFSI solid polymer electrolytes
Article.Authors: Singh P.; Polu A.; Aldosari S.; Aldbea F.; Rawat S.; Alheety M.; Srivastava M.; Savilov S.; Kumar D.; Mishra K.; Kareem A.; Johari R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, we showcase a multifunctional biobased phytic acid (PA) additive that is able to function effectively as both a structural and an electrochemical modifier for PEO 12 –LiTFSI solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). Structural characterization shows that 20 wt% of PA has led to near-complete suppression of the detectable PEO crystalline peaks, which is accompanied by improved mechanical flexibility and increased tensile strength. Electrochemical analysis reveals a more than 34-fold enhancement in ionic conductivity, which is 3.88 × 10 − 4 S cm⁻¹ at 25 °C, and a high ionic transference number of 0.984. Moreover, the electrolyte possesses a widened oxidative stability range of 4.61 V and also demonstrates stable redox behavior in SS/SPE/Li cells. Full-cell tests with the configuration of Li/SPE/LiFePO 4 show very good performance in terms of rate capability and capacity retention throughout the range of 0.1–2 C, and upon returning to the low C-rate, approximately 91% capacity recovery is achieved.

Article.Title: Self-efficacy mediates and sensation seeking moderates the association between water safety knowledge and high-risk swimming behaviors in preadolescents
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Xiang S.; Zhang H.; Xie C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Swimming-related hazards are sudden, unpredictable, and irreversible, and preadolescent children are particularly susceptible to irrational judgments and high-risk behaviors in aquatic environments. Grounded in the dual systems model and risk compensation theory, this study analyzed questionnaire data from 1573 preadolescent children with a mean age of 11.32 ± 0.49 years. Regression-based conditional process analysis and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were combined to clarify the linear associations and multifactorial configurational mechanisms underlying preadolescent children’s engagement in high-risk swimming behaviors. (1) Water safety knowledge was significantly and negatively associated with high-risk swimming behaviors after gender, age, and grade level were controlled. (2) Self-efficacy mediated this association competitively: the indirect association through self-efficacy was positive, opposite in sign to the negative direct association, yielding a competitive (inconsistent) mediation pattern. (3) Sensation seeking positively moderated the second stage of this mediation pathway. (4) In the fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, no single factor constituted a necessary condition for high-risk swimming behaviors; two configurations were associated with high-risk swimming behaviors and two with non-high-risk swimming behaviors. Water safety knowledge shows a “double-edged sword” pattern of associations with preadolescent children’s high-risk swimming behaviors: it is directly associated with lower levels of such behaviors but is also indirectly associated with higher risk-taking through swimming self-efficacy, and this indirect association is significantly stronger among individuals high in sensation seeking. These findings suggest that safety education based solely on knowledge dissemination is insufficient; differentiated interventions should be tailored to children’s self-efficacy and sensation-seeking levels.

Article.Title: Effect of ZnCl2 addition to sunflower husk’s hydrothermal carbonization process: hydrochar yield, fuel properties and methylene blue removal
Article.Authors: Valadkhani M.; Mozaffarian M.; Malool M.
Article.Abstract: The lack of optimal and environmentally friendly treatment of agricultural solid waste and textural wastewater are thought to be critical environmental issues. Processes such as adsorption, chemical oxidation, photocatalytic degradation, advanced oxidation, and electrochemical methods have been implemented to deals with these issues. An experimental design approach was employed in this study, to clarify the impact of ZnCl 2 addition during hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) of sunflower husk (SF) at various temperatures and reaction times. The impact of process parameters on hydrochar yield, high heating value (HHV) of HC and methylene blue adsorption capacity were studied. The maximum attained methylene blue adsorption capacities at optimum conditions were 278.4 and 195 mg/g for ZnCl 2 -assisted hydrochar (at 171 ℃ and 7.48 h) and no-ZnCl 2 -assisted hydrochar (at 169 ℃ and 7.78 h), respectively. Moreover, the mean adsorption capacity increased by 51% due to ZnCl 2 addition during the HTC process. At 220℃ and 7.5 h, about 60% and 36% improvement in HHV of HC compared to SF were attained in the presence and absence of ZnCl 2 addition, respectively. Moreover, ZnCl 2 addition caused a 7% increase in the mean HC’s HHV.

Article.Title: Ultra-micro electrodes support low-current amplitude discrimination in intracortical microstimulation
Article.Authors: Su E.; Retheesh V.; Kumaravelu K.; S. Sharma S.; Grill W.; Otto K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Restoring somatosensory feedback is essential for achieving natural, embodied control of prosthetic limbs. Intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) of the somatosensory cortex can provide artificial touch by activating cortical neurons directly. Here, we systematically investigate how electrode contact size influences amplitude discrimination performance during ICMS. Six rats were chronically implanted with custom multielectrode shanks in the somatosensory cortex. Over twelve weeks, behavioral just-noticeable differences (JNDs) were quantified across eight electrode diameters (5–50 µm) using an adaptive discrimination paradigm. Discrimination thresholds were significantly lower for 5 µm and 10 µm sites than for larger contacts because these electrodes operated at lower reference stimulation amplitudes within their established charge injection safety limits. Weber fractions remained stable across electrode sizes, demonstrating proportional scaling of perceptual sensitivity with stimulus intensity. We used a biophysically realistic modeling framework to identify the underlying neural correlates of ICMS-induced amplitude discrimination. Both the magnitude of neural responses (changes in the number of activated neurons and the total population spike count) and the population mean spike count contributed to perceptual discrimination. Together, these findings show that ultra-microelectrodes produce smaller absolute JNDs by enabling operation at lower currents, rather than by improving discrimination sensitivity at matched currents. Their preservation of Weber-like scaling within safe charge-injection limits may be advantageous for high-density sensory neuroprostheses.

Article.Title: Short-term clinical outcomes following crystallized phenol treatment for recurrent pilonidal sinus: a prospective uncontrolled cohort study
Article.Authors: Alvandipour M.; Sayyadi S.; Khandel F.; Yazdani-Charati J.
Article.Abstract: Crystallized phenol is used as a minimally invasive treatment for pilonidal sinus disease. Evidence describing short-term outcomes in patients with recurrent disease remains limited. This study describes wound healing, postoperative symptoms, and pain scores after crystallized phenol treatment in a small uncontrolled cohort. This prospective uncontrolled cohort included 31 patients with recurrent pilonidal sinus following previous surgery. All patients received crystallized phenol treatment. Complete healing was defined as closure of the sinus opening and cessation of discharge. Healing within four weeks was examined as an exploratory descriptive category because this threshold was not prespecified. Pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS) on the day after treatment and at weeks 1 and 2. No pretreatment VAS measurement or concurrent control group was available. Complete healing within four weeks was documented in 18/31 patients (58.1%); 11 (35.5%) healed after four weeks and 2 (6.5%) had no documented healing. Pruritus was reported by 28 patients (90.3%) and burning sensation by 9 (29.0%); no abscess or collection was documented during follow-up. Mean postoperative VAS scores were 3.81 ± 1.37 on the day after treatment, 1.13 ± 0.84 at week 1, and 0.84 ± 0.82 at week 2. These observations describe postoperative pain over time and do not establish a phenol-specific analgesic effect. This small uncontrolled cohort provides a descriptive account of short-term outcomes after crystallized phenol treatment for recurrent pilonidal sinus. The observed postoperative decline in VAS scores cannot be attributed specifically to phenol, and conclusions about comparative effectiveness and safety are limited by the lack of a control group and incomplete characterization of adverse events. Larger comparative studies with standardized outcome assessment and longer follow-up are needed. Trial registration Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT), IRCT20130826014483N13. Article.Title: Association between sinonasal anatomical variations, adenoid hypertrophy, and sagittal–vertical skeletal patterns: a retrospective CBCT study in growth period orthodontic patients
Article.Authors: Demir H.; Çetin B.; Ulusoy Mutluol E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sinonasal anatomical variations and adenoid hypertrophy may influence upper airway function and craniofacial development. This retrospective study evaluated their association with sagittal and vertical skeletal patterns in growing orthodontic patients using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). A total of 125 patients aged 9–15 years were included. Sagittal skeletal patterns were classified using the ANB angle, and vertical skeletal patterns were categorized as normal, hyperdivergent, or hypodivergent. Thirteen sinonasal anatomical variations and adenoid hypertrophy grades were assessed on CBCT images. Nasal septum deviation was the most prevalent anatomical variation (68%), followed by accessory maxillary ostium (54.4%) and middle concha bullosa (43.2%). Grade 2 adenoid hypertrophy was the most common finding (60.8%). No significant associations were identified between sinonasal anatomical variations, adenoid hypertrophy, and either sagittal or vertical skeletal patterns, including after adjustment for age and sex ( p > 0.05). These findings suggest that, although common in growing orthodontic patients, sinonasal anatomical variations and adenoid hypertrophy were not significantly associated with craniofacial skeletal patterns in this sample.

Article.Title: Intra-session repeatability, turning laterality, and turning patterns during the instrumented figure-of-eight walk test
Article.Authors: Prieur-Blanc N.; Trama S.; Mangini A.; Giraud D.; Bertin D.; Hays A.; Bensoussan L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The figure-of-eight walk test (F8W) is a key component of the functional assessment of curved gait. A new instrumented methodology (F8Wi), combining a lumbar inertial measurement unit (IMU) and Doppler radar, has demonstrated good test-retest repeatability over time. However, the intra-session repeatability has not yet been investigated. Moreover, the literature remains contradictory regarding differences between right and left turns. Therefore, this study had two objectives: to evaluate the intra-session repeatability of a F8Wi protocol and to compare differences in turning time and gait parameters according to turning laterality, trial number, and walking condition. Twenty-two participants completed a F8Wi test comprising four loops, including four left turns and four right turns. The test was performed under four conditions: shod at a comfortable (SC) and fast (SF) speed, and barefoot at a comfortable (BC) and fast (BF) speed. Several points of interest were identified with a Doppler radar and an inertial measurement unit (IMU): the start of speed deceleration (A), the start of body rotation (B), the peak angular acceleration (C), the end of body rotation (D), and the end of speed acceleration (E). The dependent variables were time intervals between AB, AD, AE, BD, and gait parameters measured during the turn defined by AE time: gait cadence, mean step and cycle time (left and right). The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), standard error of measurement (SEM), minimal detectable change (MDC 95% ), and coefficient of variation (CV) assessed repeatability. ANOVAs and post hoc analyses were conducted to examine the main effects and interactions of turn laterality (left vs. right), trial number (1–8), and condition. The F8Wi test demonstrated good intra-session repeatability (on average: ICC = 0.85 and CV = 16.5%). However, the first and final turns were less repeatable and differed significantly from the other turns ( p < 0.05). In contrast to the effect of walking condition, turn laterality had little influence. The F8Wi is a reliable functional assessment tool that needs to be explored in clinical assessment, particularly for evaluating turning asymmetries in timing and gait parameters. However, the first and final turns involve a distinct timing compared with the others. Walking conditions can also be adjusted to introduce different task constraints.

Article.Title: Effect of printing angulation on the fit of additively manufactured provisional three-unit fixed dental prostheses
Article.Authors: Arshad M.; Hasanzade M.; Almsaadi Z.; Mosaddad S.
Article.Abstract: Printing orientation may influence the fit of additively manufactured provisional fixed dental prostheses (FDPs). This in vitro study evaluated 108 three-unit FDPs fabricated with a liquid crystal display-based masked stereolithography printer at nine combinations of buccolingual (150°, 180°, 210°) and mesiodistal (0°, 15°, 45°) angulations, with 12 FDPs per combination. Regional means from 28 measurements per abutment underwent separate unequal-variance factorial analyses with Holm adjustment. Buccolingual effects were detected for all regions; mesiodistal effects were detected for all regions except the premolar axial gap. At 0° mesiodistal angulation, the marginal-gap difference between 150° and 180° buccolingual orientations was 624.38 μm (95% confidence interval 470.87–777.88) for premolars and 442.02 μm (323.73–560.31) for molars. The 180°/0° and 180°/15° combinations generally had lower marginal and occlusal means, but the smallest axial means occurred at 210°/0°. These findings describe the tested orientation and support configurations; they do not establish a universal optimum or clinical performance.

Article.Title: A novel cost-effective layout-aware quantum circuit synthesis of symmetric functions on triangular, square, and heavy-hex layouts
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Al-Bayaty A.; Perkowski M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The quantum layout and the mapping of logical to physical qubits are crucial in quantum circuit synthesis for a real quantum computer. In particular, circuits containing large n -bit Toffoli gates ( $$n>3$$ ), such as those derived from cost-expensive gate constructions and hard-to-decompose Exclusive-or Sum of Products (ESOP) expressions, have complications with effective mappings into contemporary quantum layouts, including square grid and heavy-hex layouts. These complications are primarily caused by the limited connectivity among the physical qubits in such layouts, leading to the addition of many SWAP gates. This paper presents several contributions to address these challenges for cost-effectively constructing circuits for totally, generalized, and conditionally symmetric functions. Firstly, we introduce a novel quantum circuit synthesis methodology for such functions based on Reed–Muller Lattices, leveraging Positive and Negative Davio expansions as intermediate representations. Secondly, we present the SWAT gate, a composite operation consisting of a 2-qubit SWAP gate followed by a 3-qubit Toffoli gate, designed to reduce mapping overhead. Thirdly, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on existing industrial quantum architectures by achieving cost-efficient mappings onto square grid and heavy-hex quantum layouts without introducing additional SWAP gates when using the SWAT gate. Finally, we introduce a speculative triangular layout and corresponding layout-aware circuit constructions, serving as a theoretical framework for evaluating synthesis efficiency under enhanced connectivity assumptions. Overall, our research, benchmarked against ESOP-based and BDD-based synthesis methods, demonstrates that Reed–Muller Lattices provide a powerful approach for the layout-aware quantum circuit synthesis of symmetric and related functions, with significant potential to reduce mapping overhead in near-term quantum architectures.

Article.Title: An edge memory-driven iterated search algorithm with bidirectional feedback for the capacitated vehicle routing problem
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Zhang J.; Huang X.; Guo J.
Article.Abstract: The fixed‑fleet Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) is a canonical NP‑hard combinatorial optimization problem in logistics distribution. Conventional metaheuristic algorithms fail to fully exploit structural information embedded within historical routes and lack effective search guidance, which readily results in premature convergence. To remedy these limitations, this paper proposes an Edge Memory‑Driven Iterative Search algorithm with Bidirectional Feedback (EMIS‑BF). A dynamic edge memory matrix embedded with decay and upper‑lower bound constraints is devised to quantify high‑quality edge patterns and alleviate search stagnation. To couple global population exploration and memory‑guided local intensification, a closed‑loop bidirectional feedback mechanism is constructed, where forward feedback disseminates elite route structures and backward feedback feeds local optimization improvements back into the memory matrix to enable cross‑stage information exchange. Furthermore, a two‑stage hybrid search framework is established that integrates 2‑opt, 3‑opt, insertion and destroy‑and‑repair neighborhood operators alongside a probabilistic inferior‑solution acceptance rule to strike a balance between global‑exploration breadth and local‑exploitation depth. Numerical experiments are carried out on 83 standard A/B/E/P benchmark instances, with more than ten representative metaheuristics employed as comparative baselines. EMIS‑BF matches published best‑known solutions (BKS) on 68 test instances. The Friedman test combined with post‑hoc Bonferroni–Dunn statistical analysis shows that EMIS‑BF achieves the second‑best average rank among the twelve algorithms ranked on Sets A, B and P. The proposed algorithm yields statistically significant performance improvements over six baseline methods, while no statistically distinguishable performance gaps are observed between EMIS‑BF and the top‑five competitive solvers. Multiple independent runs further verify its robust performance and stable convergence behavior. The edge‑memory and feedback strategies provide valuable design references for hybrid swarm‑intelligence and metaheuristic optimization algorithms.

Article.Title: Computational study and ranking of drugs for peyronie’s disease using QSPR and MCDM techniques
Article.Authors: Vasanth K.; Iyer R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peyronie’s disease, a connective tissue disease with fibrotic plaque formation of the penile tunica albuginea, is often associated with penile deformity, pain, and erectile dysfunction. Despite the availability of a number of therapy agents, a comprehensive comparative evaluation of selected therapeutic agents according to structural and physicochemical features is still limited. In this study, an integrated framework has been developed by integrating chemical graph theory, Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship (QSPR) modeling, and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques to analyze and rank twenty drugs used in the treatment of Peyronie’s disease. Five degree-based topological descriptors, the second Zagreb ( $$M_2$$ ), Atom Bond Connectivity (ABC), Geometric Arithmetic (GA), Sombor (SO) and Nirmala (NI) indices were computed based on the molecular graph representations of the selected drugs. Correlation analysis was performed between these descriptors and nine physicochemical properties. Further development and validation of Multiple Linear Regression models were performed using Leave-One-Out Cross Validation (LOOCV), Ridge Regression with nested LOOCV, and Y-randomization testing. Among the tested properties, molar refractivity (MR), polarizability (P), and molecular weight (MW) demonstrated the most consistent QSPR performance. The models yielded $$R^2$$ values of 0.9733, 0.9829, and 0.9768, respectively, with LOOCV $$Q^2$$ values of 0.9435, 0.9547, and 0.9500. Entropy and CRITIC techniques were employed to establish criterion weights for decision-making analysis, and then the hybrid weighting approach was used to amalgamate them. The medications studied were ranked using five MCDM methods, which are MARCOS, VIKOR, WASPAS, TOPSIS and EDAS, followed by Spearman rank-correlation analysis and consensus aggregation using average ranking and Borda count methods. The findings show a repeatable computational framework for comparing molecular compounds based on certain physical properties. The obtained rankings are based on physicochemical profile prioritizing and should not be taken as clinical efficacy or therapeutic superiority.

Article.Title: Ultrafine PVP-stabilized platinum nanoparticles for megavoltage X-ray radiosensitization of MCF-7 cells: synthesis, characterization, and free quercetin co-treatment
Article.Authors: Afshar S.; Meidanchi A.; Eynali S.; Ebadtkar R.; Khansari N.
Article.Abstract: Ultrafine polyvinylpyrrolidone-stabilized platinum nanoparticles (PVP-Pt NPs) were produced using a single-step hydrothermal route and investigated as candidate nanoradiosensitizers for megavoltage X-ray treatment of MCF-7 breast cancer cells. Their performance was examined both independently and during concurrent treatment with free quercetin (Que). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed approximately spherical Pt nanoparticles, while quantitative TEM image analysis yielded particle diameters of approximately 3–6 nm with a mean diameter of ~ 4.5 nm. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed a smooth and homogeneous surface without pronounced agglomeration or cracking, consistent with a stabilizing role of PVP in limiting particle coalescence. X-ray diffraction showed reflections consistent with crystalline face-centered cubic (FCC) platinum with the Fm-3 m space group. FTIR spectroscopy showed spectral features consistent with possible interactions between PVP functional groups and Pt species. The optical response was evaluated by UV–visible spectroscopy. The cytotoxic and radiation-associated effects of PVP-Pt NPs, free Que, and concurrent PVP-Pt + Que treatment were evaluated at concentrations of 0.1, 1, 10, and 100 µg/mL, with and without megavoltage X-ray irradiation at 2 and 4 Gy. Without irradiation, significant reductions in MTT-derived cell viability were observed for PVP-Pt and concurrent PVP-Pt + Que treatment at 10 and 100 µg/mL, whereas the overall effect of free Que concentration was not statistically significant. Among the investigated formulations, PVP-Pt NPs produced the greatest reduction in MCF-7 cell viability following irradiation. At 10 µg/mL mean MTT-derived cell viability was approximately 45.4% under 2 Gy and 38.6% under 4 Gy irradiation. These findings support further investigation of ultrafine PVP-Pt nanoparticles as candidate nanoradiosensitizers for enhancing radiation-associated cytotoxicity in MCF-7 breast cancer cells.

Article.Title: Prior guided multi view clustering characterizes smartphone use behavioral profiles from heterogeneous questionnaire data in adults aged 60 to 69 years
Article.Authors: Chen K.; Tang J.; Zhao H.; Xiao J.; Fan L.; Liu B.; Luo Y.
Article.Abstract: Questionnaire surveys often contain heterogeneous modules whose roles in behavioral profiling differ. This study evaluated a prior-guided multi-view clustering procedure using a community survey of smartphone use among 428 adults aged 60–69 years in Chongqing, China. The clustering inputs were organized into a 26-item smartphone-use behavior view, a demographic and sociological view, and a lifestyle and health-habit view; smartphone-use context variables were excluded from cluster construction and examined only after clustering. Candidate solutions with two to six clusters were examined using internal validity and repeated 80% subsampling. The two-cluster solution showed the strongest internal separation. The three-cluster solution had the highest mean subsampling ARI (0.940), retained three nontrivial groups, and was selected as the primary exploratory representation; the five-cluster solution showed similarly high stability but contained a small group of 35 respondents. The three profiles contained 219, 112, and 97 respondents. Conditional on the prespecified prior \(\varvec{\pi }=(0.70,0.15,0.15)^\top \) , the estimated view contribution weights were 0.8054, 0.1060, and 0.0886. Behavior-view-only spectral clustering was highly concordant with the full solution (ARI \(=0.908\) ; profile correlation \(=0.999\) ), showing that the behavior view supplied the core partition while the auxiliary views provided limited, explicitly constrained contextual refinement rather than a qualitatively different structure. Variables used in clustering are reported as profile characteristics rather than independent validation. Smartphone-use duration, timing, location, and function variables that were excluded from clustering showed exploratory post hoc associations with profile membership. The findings support transparent prior-guided integration of heterogeneous questionnaire modules while emphasizing dependence on the specified prior, the dominant behavioral view, data-quality decisions, and the exploratory nature of the profiles.

Article.Title: Record warmth in the Sea of Japan amplified the September 2024 Noto heavy rainfall associated with a mesoscale low-pressure disturbance
Article.Authors: Shimoda M.; Sugimoto S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In September 2024, record-breaking rainfall caused severe flooding and landslides in the Noto region, Japan, where recovery from the devastating Noto Peninsula earthquake was still ongoing. During this event, the Sea of Japan experienced record warmth, with monthly-mean sea surface temperature anomaly of + 2.9 °C. To quantify the impact of this anomalous ocean warming on the heavy rainfall, we conducted numerical sensitivity experiments using a regional atmospheric model in which only the sea surface temperature conditions in the Sea of Japan were replaced with those from each year between 1991 and 2020. Simulated rainfall over the Noto region was nearly twice as large under the observed 2024 SST conditions, indicating that the exceptionally warm ocean substantially amplified the event. The warming did not alter the occurrence or track of a mesoscale low-pressure disturbance along the autumn rain front, but the intensity of the disturbance systematically increased with SST and was accompanied by stronger southwesterly winds and moisture transport into the frontal zone. Ocea​nic analyses further showed a marked strengthening of the Tsushima Warm Current in 2024. These results highlight the importance of atmospheric responses to anomalously warm ocean conditions in amplifying extreme rainfall under anomalously warm ocean conditions and underscore the need to consider such processes in future risk assessments around Japan.

Article.Title: Study on limit passing conditions of one-trip open hole window cutting tool assembly
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Zhang W.; Yan C.; Lu T.
Article.Abstract: Aiming at common downhole problems of one-trip open-hole window milling sidetracking tools, including sticking, bending deformation, excessive stress and unstable friction, this paper systematically studies the runnability and drag-torque characteristics of the tool assembly based on a deep test well. Combined with wellbore structure and measured trajectory data, constraint criteria are proposed, and a geometric pass-through model and beam-column bending mechanical model are established. Bending modes are divided into rigid, clearance and deformation types to calculate the ultimate passing curvature and critical dogleg severity. A 3D soft-string model is adopted for full-well drag and torque calculation, and finite element simulation verifies tool strength at the sidetracking point. Results indicate favorable runnability of the tool assembly. The 6–1/2″ drill collar has a critical dogleg severity of 8.94°/30 m, higher than field maximum values. The 3° whipstock leaves adequate safety margin against stress concentration and plastic deformation. Peak drag and torque reach 48 kN and 13,200 N·m, with 1000–3500 m as the high-load interval. This work clarifies safe running limits and proves the technical feasibility, offering references for deep-well open-hole sidetracking.

Article.Title: Contemporaneous network analysis characterizes symptom-network topology and core symptoms in patients with a stoma after colorectal cancer surgery
Article.Authors: Guo C.; Sun H.; Sun F.; Ma Y.; Zhang X.; Wu J.; Song X.; Lu F.; Qiang W.; Wang X.; Lyu H.; Ma S.; Jin Y.
Article.Abstract: Symptoms co-occur after colorectal cancer stoma surgery, but their network roles remain unclear. This two-center cross-sectional study included 331 consecutively recruited patients. Exploratory factor analysis identified five symptom clusters: Psychological, Peristomal Skin, Energy Deficit, Digestive-Urinary System, and Pain. Apriori association-rule analysis identified weight loss, social impairment, and mucus discharge from the anus as sentinel symptoms within the Energy Deficit, Psychological, and Digestive-Urinary System clusters, respectively; these labels reflect cross-sectional association patterns rather than temporal ordering. In the EBICglasso network, decreased subjective well-being had the highest standardized Expected Influence ( z = 1.25) and standardized one-step Bridge Expected Influence ( z = 4.74). Complementary nodewise regression yielded R 2 = 0.634 for this symptom, and the correlation-stability coefficient for Expected Influence was 0.749. Multivariable models for the core and sentinel symptom scores explained 7.8%–23.9% of the variance, indicating modest explanatory performance. These pooled findings may inform symptom assessment but may differ across postoperative phases; the mucus-discharge finding is further limited by unrecorded anatomical eligibility. Longitudinal studies should test temporal ordering and predictive utility.

Article.Title: Plasmonic biosensors based on X-shaped resonators for cancer cell detection with machine learning-driven transmittance prediction
Article.Authors: Khani S.; Rahmanimanesh M.
Article.Abstract: The measurement of the refractive index (RI) of biological tissues plays a fundamental role in bio-optical sensing systems. In this work, 5 plasmonic biosensors are proposed based on metal–insulator–metal (MIM) waveguides coupled with 1 to 5 X-shaped resonators (XSRs). By increasing the number of coupled resonators, the sharpness of the photonic band gap (PBG) edges is significantly improved, resulting in a substantial enhancement of the figure of merit (FoM) from 5.82 to 80.76. The distinct spectral separation between the two PBG edges also ensures stable sensing behavior without overlapping under changes in analyte RI, enabling broadband sensing capability. The proposed biosensors are further evaluated for cancer cell detection, demonstrating high sensitivity and reliable performance. In addition, transmission responses are predicted using an Extreme Randomized Tree Regression model, which reduces computational time by nearly 90% compared with finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations. Overall, the combination of a simple structure, improved FoM, high sensitivity, and machine learning-based prediction highlights the potential of these biosensors for advanced biomedical sensing applications.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of short-read and full-length 16S rRNA sequencing for circulating microbiota profiling in cirrhosis
Article.Authors: Ren L.; Zhang J.; Xu X.; Chen L.; Yang X.; Matsubara J.; Tian Y.; Jin X.; Xu M.; Zhu C.; Zhang X.; Qi W.; Feng Z.
Article.Abstract: Although current next-generation 16S rRNA sequencing (NGS) offers high throughput and low cost, its short read length severely limits resolution at the species level, particularly for closely related taxa. However, full-length 16S rRNA sequencing (FL) methods such as PacBio SMRT generate ultra-long reads spanning the complete 16S rRNA gene, granting precise identification at the species levels, and, in selected cases, at the subspecies levels. The higher resolution of full-length 16S rRNA sequencing could be critical for studying circulating microbiota in diseases prone to spontaneous infections, such as cirrhosis. However, direct comparisons between the two approaches in the blood of cirrhotic patients are lacking. This study compares Illumina short-read and PacBio long-read sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene in 30 blood samples from patients undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) procedures. Blood samples from peripheral, hepatic, and portal veins were collected. Subsequently, V3-V4 (Illumina) and V1-V9 (PacBio) regions of the 16S rRNA gene were amplified and sequenced. Raw data were processed using QIIME2 software. Denoising and the generation of the amplicon sequence variants (ASV) table were performed using DADA2. Subsequent data visualization was carried out using R software (version 4.4.2). Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated higher resolution in detecting the circulating microbiome at the species level. Both methods showed robust detection sensitivity, largely unaffected by sequencing depth. Moreover, both α- and β-diversity metrics generated by these two methods demonstrated strong concordance across the three vascular compartments. We investigated the circulating microbiome in patients undergoing TIPS and demonstrated the complementary utility of short-read (V3-V4) and full-length 16S rRNA sequencing for circulating microbiota profiling. These results could lay the groundwork for developing circulating microbiota-based biomarkers and targeted therapies for cirrhotic patients.

Article.Title: Adaptive selection of MICE algorithm parameters for pulmonary function value prediction models
Article.Authors: Im S.; Gang Y.; Lee M.; Moon J.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence-based medical prediction models are often affected by incomplete longitudinal records. We evaluated an interpretable initialization rule with fixed iteration budgets in a random-forest chained imputation procedure for pulmonary-function forecasting. The source cohort comprised 596 patients and 2,112 visits. A controlled cohort of 367 patients and 396 eligible prediction windows was evaluated using patient-disjoint five-fold splits. PFT cells were masked under MCAR and observed-covariate-dependent MAR mechanisms at 5%, 10%, and 20%, and every imputer and scaler was fitted on training rows only. The adaptive configuration used fixed variable-level initialization assignments. A fold-wise sensitivity audit recalculated the rule statistics and CV threshold from training patients only; all five folds retained the same assignments, so the imputed inputs and reported downstream results were unchanged. Twelve imputation approaches were compared by direct masked-cell accuracy and downstream performance using a fixed latest LSTM model. Across 360 latest-LSTM runs, the lowest-RMSE method depended on the condition: mean-initialized MICE ranked first in four conditions, adaptive MICE in one, and LOCF in one. None of 66 paired comparisons against the variable-specific adaptive configuration remained significant after Holm correction. The adaptive procedure is therefore reproducible and interpretable but was not universally superior. Direct imputation fidelity and downstream predictive utility should be evaluated separately.

Article.Title: Sugarcane/wheat intercropping maximizes crop productivity and effect on soil physicochemical properties in Pakistan
Article.Authors: Khan F.; Khan J.; Shah G.; Khan N.
Article.Abstract: The performance of sole and intercropping systems in sugarcane cultivation determined productivity and physciochemical properties in Pakistan. A structured face-to-face interview schedule used to collect field information from 70 sugarcane growers and 210 soil samples in each of the three stages i.e. early (before fertilizer’s application), crop maturity and after harvesting by these growers for key soil fertility indicators, including soil texture, mineral nitrogen, organic matters (OM), total organic carbon (TOC), pH and electrical conductivity (EC). Walkey Black and AB-DTPA methods were applied for analysis of organic matter (OM), and total organic carbon (TOC), and mineral nitrogen. Findings showed that single cultivar CP-77400 recorded sugarcane average yield of 118 tha -1 in sole cropping and combined cultivars CP-77400 and Pona produced an average yield of 110.70 tha -1 in intercropping. Moreover, average mineral nitrogen was calculated at 16.35, 22.64 and 10.78 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 17.06, 22.34 and 10.32 Mgha -1 in intercropping. Average organic matter was calculated 35.2, 36.5 and 37.5 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 36.4, 38 and 38.7 Mgha -1 in intercropping. The total organic carbon (TOC) was calculated 20, 20.30 and 21.80 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 21.71, 23.27 and 22.41 Mgha -1 in intercropping. Although soil pH (7.91 to 8) remained within optimal ranges under both systems, EC (21.51 to 27.01) was higher in intercropping plots, indicating possible long-term salinity buildup. This research highlights the importance of crop-soil compatibility, varietal selection and cultivation method in optimizing sugarcane production. Policy recommendations include expanding access and utilization of recommended planting material and enhancing farmer training on sustainable soil and crop management.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of core exercises on knee pain and physical function in individuals diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis: A 12-week randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Thomas D.; Eapen C.; Hegde A.; Mane P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This assessor-blinded, single-center randomized controlled trial aimed to determine whether adding the Core Activation and Rehabilitation Exercises for Knee Osteoarthritis (CARE-KOA©) program to conventional knee-focused rehabilitation improves clinical and functional outcomes in adults with mild-to-moderate knee osteoarthritis (KOA). One hundred participants with Kellgren–Lawrence grade 1–3 were randomized to CARE-KOA© rehabilitation ( n = 51) or conventional knee-based rehabilitation ( n = 49) for 12 weeks. Pain, patient-reported outcomes, physical function tests, isometric knee strength, and core endurance were evaluated at baseline and at 4, 8, and 12 weeks. Baseline imbalances in VAS-Activity, KOOS-ADL, and Timed Up-and-Go (TUG) were addressed using analysis of covariance. CARE-KOA© produced greater improvements in activity-related pain, patient-reported outcomes, transitional physical function, and core endurance ( p < 0.05), whereas improvements in isometric knee muscle strength were comparable between groups. Adjusted between-group differences remained statistically significant for VAS-Activity (− 2.27 cm; 95% CI − 2.65 to − 1.88), KOOS-ADL (5.45 points; 95% CI 2.62 to 8.28), and TUG (− 5.49 s; 95% CI − 6.16 to − 4.81). These findings support the incorporation of structured core-stabilization training as an adjunct to conventional knee rehabilitation to improve clinical and functional outcomes in individuals with mild-to-moderate KOA. Article.Title: Transforming the concept of crown shyness into a measurable teaching model in the basic design studio
Article.Authors: Bogenç Yılmaz Ç.; Bekci B.; Uslu E.; Çufali Sağbazar A.; Genç E.
Article.Abstract: This study focuses on the methodological gap in the integration of nature-based concepts in basic design education and examines the phenomenon of crown shyness within the context of the conceptual–formal transformation process, addressing it as a structured teaching model supported by criteria-based evaluation parameters. Methodologically, the research adopts a two-phase iterative Design-Based Research (DBR) framework within the Basic Design studio to analyze collage studies and final student outputs. The research adopts a design-based methodology and analyzes collage studies conducted within the basic design studio as well as the student outputs produced through this process. The developed pedagogical model is grounded in a four-stage teaching framework encompassing conceptual analysis, perceptual decomposition, formal abstraction, and compositional organization. The analyses conducted on the examined cases suggest that the proposed teaching model has the potential to support participants’ conceptual awareness and spatial organization skills but also situates the process of formal production on a rational conceptual basis by distancing it from purely incidental aesthetic concerns. In addition, the evaluation matrix developed within the study contributes to making the design process pedagogically traceable and assessable through structured, criteria-based parameters that reduce subjective bias. As a result, the study proposes a systematic and applicable model for the integration of nature-based concepts into basic design pedagogy, thereby strengthening the relationship between conceptual thinking and formal production and establishing an original methodological framework for design education.

Article.Title: Assessing urban mobility in Peshawar using functional zoning and roadway conditions
Article.Authors: Shams H.; Qiu Y.; Abdrhman H.; Yousaf A.; Ullah H.; Plescan C.; Plescan E.; Taus D.
Article.Abstract: Traffic congestion in rapidly growing cities is often exacerbated by weak zoning controls, insufficient road capacity, poor pedestrian facilities, and inadequate intersection design. This study assesses urban mobility in Peshawar by integrating traffic counts, origin–destination (OD) surveys, pedestrian observations, parking surveys, and road-inventory data across six functional zones. A Composite Mobility Pressure Index (CMPI) was constructed from normalised trip generation, trip attraction, parking pressure, pedestrian pressure, and roadway-deficiency indicators and tested under alternative weighting scenarios. OD patterns indicate that Zones D, E, O2, and O4 account for 57.2% of total trip generation, while Zones A, D, E, and F account for 61.3% of trip attraction. Cars, motorcycles, and rickshaws together account for 78% of observed trips. Under equal weights, Zones F (0.718), E (0.705), A (0.663), and D (0.661) form the high-pressure tier; B and C remain the two lowest-pressure zones under all weighting scenarios. The integrated analysis distinguishes demand-led pressure in Zone D from curbside- and pedestrian-friction-led pressure in Zone F, a distinction no individual survey can provide. The findings support coordinated zoning reform, parking management, pedestrian improvements, public-transport integration, and targeted intersection redesign. The framework offers a transparent, reproducible approach for diagnosing mobility constraints in data-limited, rapidly urbanising cities.

Article.Authors: Vandana V.; Shaik F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an experimental investigation of zinc oxide (ZnO) nanofluids in a parabolic dish collector with a hemispherical cavity receiver under real outdoor solar conditions. ZnO concentrations of 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 vol% were tested in water and in ethylene glycol-water (EG: W) base fluids with volume ratios of 0:100, 10:90, 20:80 and 30:70, at flow rates of 1 to 5 LPM, giving 60 experimental conditions. Performance parameters (thermal efficiency, exergy efficiency, useful heat gain, heat loss, Nusselt number and pumping power) were evaluated from the measured data at each condition. They were then modeled by response surface methodology (RSM) as functions of ZnO concentration, EG ratio and flow rate, and optimized using the desirability approach with equal importance for all six responses. For the water-based fluid at 0.1 vol% ZnO, increasing the flow rate from 1 to 5 LPM raised the thermal efficiency from 25.5% to 39.6% and the Nusselt number about 3.2 times, while the heat loss fell by 28%. Increasing ZnO from 0.1 to 0.3 vol% raised the useful heat gain and thermal efficiency by about 7% at all flow rates and EG ratios. EG addition reduced the thermal and exergy efficiencies, by up to 17% and 25% (30:70 at 5 LPM), and increased pumping power by up to about 97%, whereas the 10:90 mixture performed close to water at low flow. Heat loss varied non-monotonically with EG content. Response surface models for six responses fitted well (R 2 = 96.07–98.39%, predicted R 2 ≥ 96.92%). Desirability optimization with equal importance gave the best operating condition within the tested range: water base fluid, 0.27 vol% ZnO and 5 LPM (D = 0.93), with predicted thermal efficiency 40.0%, exergy efficiency 15.9% and useful heat gain 778 W. Article.Authors: Elsayim R.; Alqahtani M.; Alhaji J.; Yehia H.; Alameen A.; ALdehaish H.; Mohammad K.; Alshalan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Managing Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remains challenging due to its resistance to β-lactam antibiotics and its capacity to form biofilms. This study employed carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) profiling, an independent hypothesis-generating molecular modeling analysis, and in vitro fermentation to evaluate Arabic gum (AG) and baobab (BB) as fermentable substrates for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Bifidobacterium longum . The consensus CAZyme profiling revealed the presence of 52 and 55 genes annotated as glycoside hydrolases (GH) in the reference genomes of L. plantarum and B. longum , respectively. In contrast, only 13 such genes were identified in the S. aureus genome. These findings correspond to 19, 25, and six distinct GH families, respectively. In the computational analysis, digalacturonic acid and D-glucuronic acid exhibited predicted docking scores of − 7.0 and − 6.8 kcal/mol against PBP2a, with MM/GBSA ΔGbind values of − 24.22 and − 4.53 kcal/mol, respectively, compared to − 47.27 kcal/mol for the co-crystallized reference ligand. During 300-ns molecular dynamics simulations, D-glucuronic acid maintained repeated predicted contacts with Lys597, Gly599, Thr600, His583, and Ser598, whereas digalacturonic acid demonstrated greater conformational mobility. These in silico findings represent predicted ligand–PBP2a interactions and do not demonstrate experimental PBP2a inhibition. Experimentally, substrate supplementation significantly affected probiotic OD₆₀₀, viable cell counts, and culture pH (all ANOVA, P ≤ 0.0004), with 2% AG producing the strongest overall growth and fermentation response. Selected AG pH-matched preparations reduced MRSA growth by approximately 47–100% ( P < 0.0001), while selected BB-derived preparations resulted in approximately 39–94% growth reduction. AG-derived CFS at 1% and 2% significantly reduced MRSA biofilm biomass, corresponding to calculated reductions of 65.94% and 71.70%, respectively (adjusted P = 0.0401 and 0.0135). Overall, AG, and to a lesser extent BB, supported probiotic growth and fermentation and generated CFS preparations with measurable effects on MRSA growth and biofilm biomass, while the computational PBP2a findings remain hypothesis-generating and require direct biochemical validation.

Article.Authors: Kadambari K.; Boomika S.; Kumar S.

Using MangoleafBD dataset (4000 leaf images) from Kaggle, containing both healthy and diseased samples across seven categories including Anthracnose, Bacterial Canker, Powdery Mildew, Sooty Mould, Cutting Weevil, Gall Midge, Die Back and healthy collected from multiple orchards in Bangladesh. Article.Title: Dual inhibition of BChE and Aβ42 aggregation by novel 2-phenylbenzofuran derivatives as a multitarget approach to Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Delogu G.; Begala M.; Novás M.; Matos M.; Caria P.; Frau D.; Sogos V.; Isola M.; Sanna C.; Tuberoso C.; Fais A.; Era B.; Floris S.; Pintus F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder involving multiple pathogenic mechanisms, requiring therapies targeting different pathways. In this study, five 2-phenylbenzofurans ( 8 – 12 ) were designed, synthesized via the Wittig reaction, and evaluated as potential multi-target agents for AD. All compounds selectively inhibited butyrylcholinesterase (BChE, IC 50 = 5.1–45.8 µM), with compounds 8 and 12 showing the highest activity, better than the reference compound. All compounds also exhibited significant antioxidant activity in the ABTS assay (EC 50 = 10.65–27.02 µM), with compound 12 displaying the highest antioxidant capacity, outperforming the reference standard. Both compounds act as mixed-type BChE inhibitors and were non-cytotoxic in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells at their active concentrations. Moreover, they significantly decreased intracellular reactive oxygen species levels induced by H 2 O 2 , with compound 12 demonstrating highest potency. Thioflavin-T assay proved that both compounds effectively interfere with Aβ42 aggregation, with compound 12 showing the strongest anti-amyloid activity. The biological findings were further supported by computational studies, with molecular docking providing insight into BChE binding and ADMET analysis predicting favourable pharmacokinetic properties. Preliminary telomere analyses further suggested protection against oxidative stress-induced chromosomal damage. Overall, compound 12 emerges as the most promising molecule for further optimization as a multitarget therapeutic agent for AD.

Article.Title: Adaptive confidence-aware deep authentication framework for secure industrial Internet of Things
Article.Authors: Kalyanakumar P.; Selvaraj K.
Article.Abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) deployments authenticate an increasing volume of heterogeneous device traffic under adversarial conditions, and single-stage classifiers—whether shallow or deep—tend to commit to a label at every operating point, including the ambiguous region where the decision boundary is least reliable. This behaviour inflates both the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) precisely where an authentication system can least afford it. This paper studies a specific, narrow instance of confidence-based selective classification—an idea dating at least to Chow’s rule and later formalised for deep networks by Geifman and El-Yaniv and surveyed by Hendrickx et al.—applied to IIoT flow authentication, evaluating a two-stage pipeline in which a feed-forward deep neural network (DNN) escalates only its most ambiguous predictions to a Random Forest (RF) arbiter rather than a human operator. Rather than thresholding every prediction at 0.5, the framework partitions the DNN’s output probability into a high-confidence accept region, a high-confidence reject region, and a bounded uncertainty band; only requests that fall in the uncertainty band are escalated to a secondary ensemble vote, and the system fails closed (denies) whenever the two stages disagree. The framework is evaluated on a stratified 180,583-record subset of the X-IIoTID dataset (59 engineered features after cleaning, encoding and constant-column removal), split 70/15/15 into train, validation and test partitions; this subsample, rather than the full dataset or an independent IIoT capture, is the scope of the evaluation reported here. The proposed DNN attains 98.82% test accuracy and an AUC of 0.9991 on the binary authentication task, and a companion softmax variant attains 98.64% accuracy across ten fine-grained attack categories. Against four classical baselines—logistic regression, decision tree, linear SVM and Random Forest—the DNN is competitive but not uniformly dominant on raw accuracy: the standalone Random Forest baseline reaches higher accuracy (99.60%), lower FAR (0.668%), and lower FRR (0.137%) than the full adaptive DNN+RF pipeline (99.15% accuracy, 1.070% FAR, 0.647% FRR) reported below. The case for the adaptive pipeline over simply deploying the standalone Random Forest therefore cannot rest on measured accuracy, FAR, or FRR alone. Escalating only the 0.95% of test requests that fall inside the uncertainty band reduces FRR from 1.064% to 0.647% and FAR from 1.305% to 1.070% relative to static 0.5-threshold decisioning, while overall accuracy improves from 98.82% to 99.15%. These results, obtained from a single train/test split and a single trained instance of each model—statistical significance across repeated seeds was not evaluated in this study—indicate that selective, confidence-gated escalation applied to an automated fallback is a measurable, if incremental, way to concentrate ensemble-arbitration cost on a small fraction of IIoT traffic while reducing FRR and FAR relative to static thresholding.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: false rejection rate; false acceptance rate; Industrial Internet of Things; deep neural network; device authentication

Article.Title: Respirable crystalline silica exposure in agate-stone workers in Khambhat, India: a human health risk assessment using a probabilistic approach
Article.Authors: Saini M.; Kulkarni N.; Balachandar R.; Kharkwal G.; Asodia R.; Vaghela K.; Nimavat D.; Tank N.; Sivaperumal P.; Rupani M.; Modi B.
Article.Abstract: Crystalline silica, a Group 1 carcinogen, is present in dust generated during cutting, polishing, chipping and drilling activities in cottage-scale agate units. This study quantified respirable crystalline silica (RCS) exposure amongst workers in such units in Gujarat, India, and assessed associated carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic health risks. Personal respirable dust samples of workers were collected across four distinct work areas and quantified for RCS. Associated health risks were evaluated using Monte Carlo–based probabilistic inhalation risk assessment model. The activity-specific arithmetic mean RCS concentrations ranged from 0.039 to 0.359 mg/m³, surpassing occupational exposure limits in all work areas. Average carcinogenic risk estimates exceeded the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) screening benchmark in all work areas, with cutting exhibiting the highest observed mean modelled cancer risk ( n = 13), although differences in RCS concentrations between activities were largely not statistically significant. The non-carcinogenic hazard quotients in the cutting and polishing areas exceeded safety thresholds. Simulated implementation of engineering controls and respirator use reduced 95th percentile upper-bound health risks by 78% and 62.5%, respectively; however, mean cancer and non-cancer risks in these areas still exceeded reference values. Sensitivity analysis revealed that RCS concentration exerted significant influence and accounted for 61% of variance in carcinogenic risk and 82% in non-carcinogenic risk. Findings of this study highlight the urgent need for implementing effective exposure control measures amongst this informal workforce.

Article.Title: Sustainable gasification-based biochar electrodes with post-synthetic nickel incorporation for advanced energy storage
Article.Authors: Prabhakar K.; Jaganathan V.; Kumaravelu T.; Dong C.; Peramanan A.; Sathishkumar P.
Article.Abstract: Advanced energy storage systems are only possible with the development of sustainable, high-performance electrode materials. The nickel-doped biochar used in the study was produced through a two-step process: first, the biomass was carbonized via a self-sustaining gasification process, followed by post-synthetic nickel addition. This allows controlled surface modification without altering the carbon skeleton generated during pyrolysis. A detailed physicochemical characterization by BET, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) shows that nickel species are mainly present on the carbon surface as Ni 2+ , and that the biochar is in a partially disordered graphitic state. The optimized electrode (NPU) exhibits better electrochemical performance, including a larger CV area, a longer discharge time, and a lower charge-transfer resistance. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals improved interfacial kinetics, and XAS shows a strong electronic interaction between the Ni species and the carbon surface. Symmetric supercapacitor devices built with NPU exhibit stable performance over a wide voltage range, good rate capability, and reversibility. This article highlights the efficiency of post-synthetic nickel incorporation as a general approach to augment the electrochemical characteristics of biochar, thereby enabling the design of sustainable, high-performance supercapacitor electrodes. This study highlights a viable pathway to developing low-cost, sustainable, and high-performance electrode materials, offering significant promise for large-scale commercialization in next-generation energy storage systems.

Article.Title: Characterization of sorghum lines for low-temperature tolerance and reproductive performance in the post-rainy season
Article.Authors: Gaddameedi A.; Phuke R.; Gorthy S.; Jayakumar J.; Bomma N.; Kishor P.; Dar M.; Kumar A.
Article.Abstract: Low night temperatures during the flowering stage in November–December significantly affect sorghum production in the semi-arid regions of India, particularly during critical growth phases. Temperature plays a critical role in sorghum flowering and grain yield, as low temperatures can delay flowering, reduce pollen viability, and result in poor seed set, ultimately lowering yield. To investigate this, a set of experiments was conducted at ICRISAT, India, to characterise 16 sorghum genotypes—including nine varieties and seven hybrid parental lines—under both controlled environment facilities and precision experimental field conditions, with three replications per genotype. The results indicated that the B line 296B and the R line ICSR 149 were the most susceptible to cold stress, while B lines 4111B, 104B, ICSB52, and 185B exhibited greater tolerance. Among the low temperature treatments, Treatment 2 (25 °C/5 °C) had the most adverse impact, recording the lowest values for pollen viability, PHI, and grain yield. Significant positive correlations were observed between grain yield and PHI (r = 0.74, p ≤ 0.01), underscoring PHI’s potential as a reliable phenotypic marker for cold tolerance. In field experiments, both genotype and date of sowing (DOS) significantly influenced all measured traits except plant height. Notably, the second sowing date (8th November) resulted in substantial reductions in mean PHI, panicle weight, and grain yield, further highlighting the adverse effects of low temperatures on sorghum performance. To evaluate cold tolerance, indices such as Stress Susceptibility Index (SSI), Stress Tolerance Index (STI), and Yield Stability Index (YSI) were applied. The collective integration of cold tolerance indices concludes Dagdi Solapur and Phule Anuradha are consistent performers across the stress tolerance Indices and should be candidates for the cold-tolerant breeding program. The B line 4111B could be a better replacement of the popular 296B line for cold-tolerant breeding.

Article.Title: Capacity-aware learned task dispatch for resource-constrained unmanned fleets under feasibility projection
Article.Authors: Zeng X.; Fu F.
Article.Abstract: Learned resource-constrained dispatch can emit simplex-valued allocation intent that a downstream hard feasibility layer then substantially rewrites. We propose SAC-Dirichlet with Lagrangian-inspired actor regularization (SDL): a Dirichlet simplex actor, dummy buffering, adaptive actor-side capacity-aware regularization, and independent strict execution-side capacity enforcement. Under the original evaluation protocol, in a 20-vehicle/60-task setting, SDL reduced predictive overload from 3.471 to 2.401 and projection intervention from 37.051 to 31.498 relative to the Dirichlet baseline (DIR); completion was 0.614 versus 0.609, and the paired completion interval crossed zero. Mechanism diagnostics, ablation, and a local two-factor sensitivity study separate dummy buffering, routing structure, and operating-point trade-offs. A fixed-density 40-vehicle/120-task evaluation extended the compatibility pattern (completion 0.615 versus 0.583). Direct assignment methods remained stronger when an explicit capacity-aligned assignment could be optimized directly. A separately trained masked evaluation did not establish a consistent mission-level advantage for SDL across CORE (0.857 versus 0.849) and PRESSURE (0.850 versus 0.856). Dummy usage remains higher under SDL. Absolute completion rates from the original and masked evaluations are reported separately because the protocols use different inactive-slot preprocessing and independently trained policies.

Article.Title: A tumor-associated K318N variant abolishes AGGF1 nuclear import by disrupting key nucleocytoplasmic transport motifs
Article.Authors: Xie W.; Li X.; He Y.; Si W.; Yu M.; Xu J.; Li Y.; Zhang L.; Chen J.; Shen J.; Tao T.; Zheng Y.; Wang Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aberrant nucleocytoplasmic transport is linked to tumorigenesis. AGGF1 exerts nuclear tumor-suppressing functions, yet how its nuclear import is regulated remains unclear. Through deletion mapping and point mutations, we identified three motifs (272–279, 317–328 and 509–519 aa) governing AGGF1 nucleocytoplasmic distribution. Knockdown of importin β1 and inhibition of importin α1 showed that the importin α1/β1 complex is the primary nuclear import receptor. GST pull-down assays revealed that 317–328 aa and 509–519 aa, but not 272–279 aa, are required for efficient binding to importin α1. None of the three motifs alone was sufficient to efficiently drive nuclear import, whereas the combined 272–328 aa region conferred robust nuclear import. The tumor-associated K318N variant, within 317–328 aa, is absent from gnomAD and causes profound, cell-type-independent cytoplasmic mislocalization that is not attributable to enhanced CRM1-mediated nuclear export or 14-3-3α/β-dependent cytoplasmic distribution. Consequently, K318N fails to bind nuclear p53, stabilize p53, or activate its transcription, impairing AGGF1 tumor-suppressing function. RNA-seq showed K318-dependent genes enriched in Rap1 signaling, cytoskeleton regulation, and cardiac muscle morphogenesis, suggesting a predominantly loss-of-function effect. These findings identify key motifs and the nuclear import receptor for AGGF1, and reveal how a single variant disrupts nuclear localization and p53 regulation, potentially contributing to tumorigenesis.

Article.Title: Association of imipenem/cilastatin with development of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients requiring carbapenem treatment
Article.Authors: Aomura D.; Groat T.; Lazaro A.; Malinoski D.; Stewart I.; Howard J.; Hutchens M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cilastatin is an inhibitor of drug metabolism in the kidney which is only available for human use in combination with imipenem, a carbapenem antibiotic, as imipenem/cilastatin (I/C). Animal studies demonstrate cilastatin protects against acute kidney injury (AKI) and clinical studies suggest I/C may reduce the risk of AKI. However, the effective dose of cilastatin in animal studies is higher than that approved with imipenem, and rigorous assessment of the effect of I/C on AKI in patients with high risk of AKI, such as those in the intensive care unit (ICU), is indicated. To address this issue, we conducted a retrospective cohort study using 3 large ICU databases, including Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III), MIMIC-IV, and the Amsterdam University Medical Center database (AUMC). Total 3932 patients were included and patients treated with I/C or non-cilastatin carbapenems (NCC) were compared using propensity score-based overlap weighting analysis. AKI development or progression was less commonly observed in I/C-treated patients than in NCC-treated patients in MIMIC-III (odds ratio [OR] and 95% confidence interval of I/C group: 0.52 [0.31–0.86]) while the outcome was similar between the groups in MIMIC-IV (OR: 1.22 [0.81–1.86]) and in AUMC (OR: 1.06 [0.76–1.47]). The outcome development was also similar between the groups with the overall analysis across all datasets by random effect model meta-analysis (OR: 0.90 [0.55–1.47]). In conclusion, I/C and other carbapenems do not differentially associate with AKI risks in ICU, and its putative effects may depend on patient characteristics and clinical settings.

Article.Title: A dual-stream Pyramid ViT–ConvFormer architecture leverages dynamic early stopping to classify diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Article.Authors: Tang G.; Lim C.; Hussain F.; Oung Q.; Yajid A.; Azmi S.
Article.Abstract: Molecular stratification of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) based on MYC rearrangement status (confirmed via fluorescence in situ hybridization) guides frontline therapeutic selection. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) effectively model global tissue context, lacking localized inductive biases extends training convergence. We developed PyConv, an asymmetrical hybrid architecture engineered for the three-class histopathological classification of MYC -rearranged ( \(MYC+\) ) DLBCL, non-rearranged ( \(MYC-\) ) DLBCL, and reactive lymph node ( RLN ). PyConv combines local ConvFormer blocks with global Pyramid ViT blocks via Multi-Head Cross-Attention (MHCA) fusion. We evaluated the network on a patient-stratified cohort of 180 whole-slide images (69,480 testing patches) against 12 baseline backbones at both patch and patient levels. PyConv achieved a patch classification accuracy and macro F1-score of 0.9962 [95% CI: 0.9884–0.9991 via patient-level clustered bootstrapping] and a macro AUROC of 0.9999. Patient-level probability pooling yielded 100% classification concordance on the held-out test cohort (18/18 patients), showing no statistically significant discriminative loss compared to top-performing baselines (e.g., ConvFormer, \(p = 0.9866\) ) while integrating global stromal context. PyConv converged by epoch 20, reducing training duration by 68.7% compared to pure Pyramid ViT. PyConv provides an accurate, computationally efficient benchmarking framework for automated lymphoma classification. Although high patient concordance demonstrates internal feasibility, the model serves as an exploratory proof of concept requiring multi-center and multi-scanner validation before clinical translation.

Article.Title: Effects of semi-rigid joint modelling on structural and material efficiency of steel grid floors and ribbed domes
Article.Authors: Jeleniewicz K.; Jaworski J.; Stefańska A.
Article.Abstract: The study presents the moment–rotation (M–φ) characteristics of semi-rigid I-profile joints made using header plates and flush end-plates. The analyzed joints were applied as representative connections in a steel grid system. The M–φ characteristics were determined using the Frye–Morris polynomial model for header plate joints and the Richard–Abbott formulation adapted by Chen and Kishi for flush end-plate joints, with joint resistance and initial stiffness established using analytical procedures. The approximate M–φ relationships were described using a three-segment model, enabling a simplified yet realistic representation of joint behaviour in engineering calculations. The resulting curves were adjusted to the calculated design moment resistance. These models were implemented in Autodesk Robot Structural Analysis Professional (ARSAP) and used in the global analysis of two structural types: a steel beam floor system and a ribbed dome. The study aimed to assess the impact of semi-rigid joints on the utilization of structural members compared to typical pinned and rigid joint models. The comparison included internal force distribution, member utilization under ultimate limit state conditions, serviceability performance, and steel section selection. For the floor structure, replacing pinned joints with flush end-plate connections reduced beam utilization by 11.5%. In the case of the ribbed dome, the demand-to-capacity ratio for the parallels was reduced by an average of 9.9%. These results indicate that accounting for joint semi-rigidity can significantly improve material efficiency and structural safety in design practice.

Article.Title: Knowledge, attitude, and perception of cardiac and pulmonary telerehabilitation among physiotherapists in India
Article.Authors: Modak M.; Singh V.; Krishnan K S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite well-established and tangible effects of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, patient uptake is lower in middle-and-low-income countries. Telerehabilitation provides an opportunity to reduce barriers, improve access and program adherence. In India, as the cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation model is comparatively new, it is important to assess knowledge, attitude, and perception among physiotherapists. A cross-sectional study was conducted among Indian physiotherapists via a validated 29-item questionnaire. Questions focused on demographics, work experience, educational qualification, Knowledge, Attitude, and Perception of telerehabilitation. 121 physiotherapists participated in the study; most of them were MPT-qualified, with 2–7 years of experience. Overall, 72.7% demonstrated essential understanding to implement a cardiopulmonary TR program, while only 34.7% were aware of standardised protocols. 56.2% believed they could implement it safely and effectively, and 63.6% were willing to include it in regular practice. 95.9% believed this model could make significant differences in the quality of life of patients, and 78.5% felt it to be as effective as centre-based rehabilitation program. 99.2% felt the need for training before implementation. Findings show that even though there is good amount of awareness, attitude, and positive perception regarding telerehabilitation among physiotherapists, its training and actual application in routine practice is still lacking.

Article.Title: The spatial lipidome of the human epidermis and epidermal models
Article.Authors: Zoratto S.; Schirato M.; Kremslehner C.; Bauer C.; Mildner M.; Kühtreiber H.; Freystätter C.; Tessier A.; Marcato F.; Gendronneau G.; André N.; Khalifa Y.; Gruber F.; Marchetti-Deschmann M.
Article.Abstract: The structure and barrier function of the human skin are closely linked to its lipid composition, especially in the epidermis, the outermost part in contact with the environment. The differentiation process of living epidermal keratinocytes into corneocytes, and the subsequent formation of the epidermal permeability barrier are accompanied by major changes in the lipids contained in and secreted by keratinocytes. Conventional lipidomic methods can characterize overall lipid composition but provide limited information on how lipid species are spatially organized within epidermal tissue. Here, we used high-resolution MALDI FTICR mass spectrometry imaging to study and compare the spatial lipidome in native human skin and a skin equivalent model with a fully stratified epidermis. Across both ionization polarities, we annotated 509 lipid-related m/z features; 452 were detected in native human skin and 214 in skin equivalents. 157 were detected in both native and reconstructed skin, corresponding to more than 70% overlap and indicating that the model reproduces a substantial lipid core relevant to further analyses. Native skin showed greater overall lipid diversity, consistent with its higher cellular and structural complexity. However, representative ion images showed similar distribution of phospholipids, barrier-associated lipids, and selected sphingolipid-related features across the stratum corneum and epidermis of both native and reconstructed skins. In particular, ceramide-, hexosylceramide-, ceramide phosphate-, and sphingomyelin-related signals followed comparable spatial ordering, with minor shifts in the skin equivalent that may reflect differences in epidermal differentiation. Heatmap-based clustering of annotated lipid-related m/z features further revealed specific lipid profiles by epidermal layers and could therefore be used as unbiased regions of interest (ROI) for further analysis. These data show that skin equivalent models replicate the major aspects of lipid composition and distribution in native human epidermis, providing a practical and biologically relevant model for spatial lipidomics methods and a deeper understanding of lipids’ contribution to the structure and function of the human epidermis.
