Article.Title: ARCANE: cross-campaign attacker re-identification via Beacon and canary-token telemetry—a sequential evidence-accumulation framework for longitudinal cyber attribution
Article.Authors: Weinberg A.
Article.Abstract: Current cyber-attribution approaches typically operate on a per-incident basis, leaving open the question of whether aggregating evidence across campaigns can meaningfully improve adversary identification. We investigate this question with attacker re-identification via cross-campaign attribution network (ARCANE), a framework that aggregates telemetry from tracking payloads (“Beacons”/canary tokens) embedded in documents, credentials, or source code across campaigns to build persistent adversary fingerprints, and combines new evidence with a single, principled application of Bayes’ rule per query campaign. The method performs one multiclass Bayesian update per query rather than a chain of per-actor updates, resets the prior for every query campaign, and only allows knowledge-base entries to be used as evidence after an explicit label-confirmation delay that models a realistic analyst-confirmation lag. We evaluate it with an actor-level bootstrap statistical protocol (rather than pairwise tests that would treat non-independent campaign pairs as independent), against two similarity-based baselines, with a feature-group ablation, a calibration analysis (Brier score, expected calibration error), an open-set pilot, and a simulator-sensitivity check. On a synthetic benchmark of eight simulated nation-state actors and 96 campaigns, within-actor fingerprint similarity is reliably higher than cross-actor similarity (actor-level bootstrap \(\Delta _S = 0.149\) , 95% CI [0.104, 0.176]), but ARCANE attains only \(32.9\%\) accuracy (91 evaluated campaigns)—significantly worse than a simple running-profile nearest-neighbour baseline ( \(62.8\%\) ; actor-cluster bootstrap \(p = 6.7\times 10^{-4}\) ) and statistically indistinguishable from a k -nearest-neighbour baseline ( \(55.8\%\) ; \(p = 0.073\) ). Accuracy is stable across two different evasion schedules (chi-square test on per-campaign outcomes, \(p > 0.65\) in both cases)—a finding we report as evasion-invariance under the two evasion models tested , not as a general property of adversary evasion. A feature-group ablation shows that the geospatial feature subgroup alone outperforms the full 24-dimensional fingerprint, indicating that naively concatenating heterogeneous feature groups under a single cosine similarity dilutes informative signal rather than combining it. We present these results as a rigorously qualified negative/mixed finding: cross-campaign aggregation, even implemented as a mathematically valid Bayesian update, does not automatically outperform simpler running-profile matching on this benchmark, and any claim of a general “structural” separability ceiling in real-world attribution is beyond what a single synthetic simulator can establish. We scope our conclusions accordingly and outline the specific experiments—additional baselines, real telemetry, open-set evaluation, metric learning—needed to test them further.

Article.Title: Transmission mechanism and identification of power pulsation signals in sucker rod pumping wells
Article.Authors: Hao Z.; Liao C.; Yu H.; Cheng F.; Zhang Z.; Li Y.; Jia D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional wellbore communication technologies for sucker-rod pumping wells suffer from severe signal attenuation and poor stability under deep-well and complex operating conditions. This study investigates the transmission mechanism and signal identification of power pulsation wireless communication. A three-dimensional full-scale fluid–structure coupling dynamic model incorporating the sucker rod, centering device, wellbore fluid, and tubing is established to characterize stress wave propagation from the downhole pump to the wellhead. The model reveals that the transmission channel exhibits typical high-impedance, low-pass characteristics, with fluid viscous damping, rod–tubing friction, and material damping governing signal attenuation, while low-frequency stress waves retain superior long-distance transmission capability. The model is validated using field-measured loading data, achieving prediction errors below 10% across the full operating condition range. Based on the validated model, a joint time- and frequency-domain identification algorithm is developed by combining characteristic spectral peak recognition with time-domain waveform verification, enabling detection of power pulsation signals under strong noise. The proposed model and identification method provide theoretical and technical support for wireless wellbore communication, downhole condition monitoring, and intelligent lifting systems, offering a reliable solution for real-time downhole information transmission in complex oilfield environments.

Donor-cluster bootstraps supported the six expression advantages and the brain Random Forest scGPT advantage, while the other brain intervals crossed zero. Under strict PBMC label scarcity, expression reached Macro F1 0.818–0.930 versus 0.779–0.881 for scGPT. Held-out-donor temperature scaling reduced mean expected calibration error from 0.0072 to 0.0057 but not in every pipeline. Class analyses identified lymphocyte-boundary errors in TNBC and PBMC and rare-class errors in brain. Performance was atlas- and classifier-dependent for this frozen-scGPT pipeline; official fine-tuning, newer checkpoints and cross-cohort transfer were not tested.

Article.Title: Fear of failure and mental well-being among collegiate athletes: cross-sectional serial mediation analysis of obsessive passion and exercise dependence tendencies
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Zhang J.; Song P.
Article.Abstract: Fear of failure is associated with lower mental well-being in athletes, but the motivational and behavioral pathways underlying this relationship remain unclear. This study examined obsessive passion for sport and exercise dependence tendencies as separate and serial mediators among 694 Chinese collegiate athletes. A cross-sectional survey was conducted, and PROCESS Model 6 was applied with 5000 bootstrap resamples. Analyses adjusted for gender, age group, year of study, sport type, and years of training. Fear of failure was negatively associated with mental well-being before (β = − 0.459) and after including both mediators (β = − 0.307; both p < 0.001). The total indirect effect was − 0.152 (95% confidence interval (CI) [− 0.194, − 0.113]). Significant specific indirect effects were observed through obsessive passion for sport (− 0.073, 95% CI [− 0.105, − 0.048]) and exercise dependence tendencies (− 0.045, 95% CI [− 0.067, − 0.028]). The serial indirect effect was also significant (− 0.034, 95% CI [− 0.051, − 0.022]). These findings indicate cross-sectional indirect associations consistent with the proposed model. They also highlight sport motivation and exercise regulation as areas for further research into collegiate athletes’ mental well-being.

Article.Title: Deep learning-based pediatric colorectal polyp classification: evaluation of training strategies, robustness, and generalization
Article.Authors: M G.; Rajalakshmi R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although automated analysis of colorectal polyps during colonoscopy has the potential to support clinical decision-making, pediatric colorectal polyp classification remains challenging because of limited annotated datasets and variability in endoscopic appearance. This study systematically evaluates a pediatric colorectal polyp classification framework employing a two-phase transfer learning strategy across multiple pretrained convolutional neural network architectures. Controlled ablation experiments were conducted on the CP-CHILD-A and CP-CHILD-B datasets using five independent random seeds. For ConvNeXt-Small, the two-phase protocol improved accuracy from $$98.88\% \pm 0.54\%$$ to $$99.77\% \pm 0.16\%$$ on CP-CHILD-A and from $$89.21\% \pm 4.23\%$$ to $$99.88\% \pm 0.27\%$$ on CP-CHILD-B compared with training from scratch. Duplicate and near-duplicate analyses followed by inference-only sensitivity evaluation showed minimal changes in performance. Cross-dataset evaluation demonstrated strong transfer between CP-CHILD-A and CP-CHILD-B, while external evaluation on Kvasir revealed substantial domain shift. Evaluation on the independent VIM-Polyp dataset showed high positive-case recall, although this dataset comprised an adult, positive-only cohort. Overall, the findings support the effectiveness of two-phase training within the evaluated CP-CHILD setting while highlighting the importance of dataset diversity, patient-level separation, and independent pediatric validation before clinical deployment.

Article.Title: DC-link voltage control of grid-iegrated solar photovoltaic system using hybrid enhanced atom search optimization
Article.Authors: Kathirvel P.; Kaliamoorthy M.
Article.Abstract: Atom Search Optimization (ASO) evolved from physics and it is a nature-inspired algorithm based on atomic and molecular dynamics principles. It models the movement and interaction forces of atoms and molecules, leveraging the power of the concepts like the Lennard–Jones (L-J) potential. The forces acting on molecules such as attractive, repulsive and forces caused by stretching or compressing were modelled to perform a guided navigation in the search space to find best feasible solution or global optimal value. In this research, ASO is applied to optimally design a optimal Proportional-Integral (PI) controller used in Grid-connected photovoltaic (GCPV) system. The optimal PI controller is essential for regulating the DC link voltage during grid connected operation. In order to improve the convergence characteristics of ASO, a novel approach called Hybrid enhanced ASO (HASO) is introduced. HASO incorporates a spider mechanism from Black Widow Optimization(BWO) to optimally handle atoms that moves outside the boundaries of the search space due to velocity updates. This spider guided optimal selection of atoms ensures the algorithm to obey the search space boundaries and also allows the optimization algorithm to search and explore new solutions and effiectively exploit new solutions with in search space. The proposed HASO algorithm is tested on a variety of unimodal and multimodal benchmark functions, including Sphere, Rosenbrock, Rastrigin, Griewank, Ackley, Schwefel, Zakharov, Levy, and more. As evidenced by the Simulation study outcomes, it is clearly found that HASO significantly improves the convergence speed and optimization efficiency compared to the conventional ASO. The improved algorithm effectively finds optimal solutions with reduced number of generations, showcasing its robustness for complex optimization tasks. HASO is further validated by designing PI controllers for a inverter. The proposed algorithm was tested for its performance under both steady-state and dynamic conditions, considering a range of irradiation levels and load variations in grid-connected PV systems. The controller gain values optimised using HASO delivers superior performance compared to conventional controllers reported in the literature, offering improved system stability and response and maintains the Total Harmonic Distortion < 5% in all the tested conditions. This study highlights the effectiveness of HASO in enhancing optimization performance such as advanced controller design for power electronics systems.

Article.Title: Dose- and strategy-dependent effects of anti-angiogenic therapy on tumor growth and microenvironment remodeling
Article.Authors: Ling R.; Wu Y.; Qian Y.; Yan Z.; Chu Y.; Zhu W.
Article.Abstract: To investigate how anti-angiogenic therapies influence tumor growth and tumor microenvironment remodeling in colorectal cancer, and to evaluate treatment-associated differences across dosages, therapeutic agents, and combination strategies. A murine colorectal cancer model established with MC38 cells was used to compare anti-angiogenic treatments across different doses, therapeutic agents, and combination regimens. Tumor growth was monitored, and microenvironmental changes were assessed using hematoxylin and eosin staining, reticulin staining, immunohistochemistry, and ELISA to characterize vascular, stromal, immune, and inflammatory alterations. All anti-angiogenic treatments inhibited tumor growth, with combination regimens showing greater efficacy than monotherapy. Fruquintinib exhibited a clear dose-dependent effect. Distinct treatment-associated remodeling patterns were observed, with bevacizumab associated with relatively organized vascular and stromal features, while the tested small-molecule TKIs were associated with more heterogeneous structural alterations. The low-dose combination strategy promoted coordinated vascular and immune microenvironment remodeling while maintaining antitumor activity. Anti-angiogenic treatments produced distinct tumor microenvironment remodeling patterns, with treatment-dependent changes in vascular and stromal organization. Optimizing dosing and combination strategies may help balance antitumor activity with coordinated microenvironmental remodeling. These findings provide a basis for further evaluation of anti-angiogenic strategies across additional colorectal cancer models.

Article.Title: Non-destructive evaluation of grout compactness in precast concrete beams using thermal imaging
Article.Authors: Balakumar N.; Santhi M.; Malathi G.
Article.Abstract: The reliability of grout in a precast concrete approach is vital for structural reliability, durability, and effective load transmission in precast concrete elements. Typical methods for evaluating grout flow monitoring and flow performance tend to be imposing, time-laborious, and inappropriate for real-time monitoring. In this research, the internal grout flow and its performance monitoring along the horizontal direction in precast elements were investigated using one of the non-destructive testing approaches, namely, the thermal image processing method. A cementitious grout of M 40 grade was used in the study. Its viscosity was estimated using the Marsh cone test and used as an apparent equivalent Newtonian viscosity in a first-order Hagen-Poiseuille estimate of grout flow behaviour. Concrete beams of size 500 mm × 120 mm × 100 mm were fabricated with horizontal ducts of diameter 25 mm diameter in the middle. The ducts were embedded with pipes of different materials such as steel, HDPE, and PVC. One of the ends of the duct was sealed, and the grout was injected from the other end. The real-time thermal images of grout flow during injection and after it had set were captured using FLIR E75 infrared thermal camera to evaluate the internal grout flow and the grout performance. The beams were heated for 45 min and then cooled for 90 min to assess the grout condition and to detect the location of voids, if any, in different zones (zone 1 -5 at an interval of 100 mm). The duct with PVC pipe exhibited better thermal visualization than steel and HDPE pipes, and zone-wise thermal analysis detected void contents of 0% in Zones 1, 2 and 5, 7.00% in Zone 3, and 24.67% in Zone 4 (average of three beams), demonstrating the method’s ability to localize internal voids under controlled laboratory conditions. The destructive sectioning of the PVC Zone 4 provided 17.5% voids which satisfactorily validated the thermal based assessment. These results indicate the potential of thermal imaging as a non-destructive assessment tool for grout compactness in precast construction.

Article.Title: Sun exposure and sun protection behaviors among Saudi adults: a national study of 11,491 participants
Article.Authors: Aleisa A.; AbuDujain N.; Almuhaideb Q.; Alanazi M.; Veldhuizen I.; Alharbi R.; Almijrad S.; Alshahrani M.; Alramadhan H.; Alsinan N.; Aldarwish G.; Farhat K.; Rabah D.; Arafa M.
Article.Abstract: We aimed to describe sun exposure and sun protection behaviors among adults in Saudi Arabia and identify the key demographic and health-related predictors of these behaviors. A cross-sectional nationwide study was conducted using the Arabic Sun Exposure and Protection Index (Ar-SEPI) in 11,491 adults. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the responses, and multivariable linear regression models were used to identify the predictors of sun exposure and protection behaviors. The mean score for sun exposure behavior (SEPI Part 1) was 7.74 (24.18% of the maximum), indicating moderate risky exposure, while the mean score for sun protection behavior (SEPI Part 2) was 7.42 (37.10%), reflecting suboptimal protective practices. Males exhibited significantly higher sun exposure (mean = 11.2 vs. 6.3) than females. Because SEPI Part 2 is reverse scored (a higher score indicates lower readiness to increase protection), males’ higher Part 2 scores (8.7 vs. 6.9) likewise indicate poorer protection readiness than females. Multivariable analysis showed that sex, age, education, and income significantly predicted sun exposure. Males and higher-income individuals reported riskier sun exposure, whereas females and more educated individuals reported better sun protection behaviors. Despite moderate awareness, sun protection behavior in Saudi Arabia remains suboptimal. Males, younger adults, and those with lower educational levels reported higher sun exposure and lower levels of protective behaviors. Future research should explore unmeasured factors such as occupational exposure, cultural norms, and environmental influences to improve intervention strategies.

Article.Title: Trehalose transport as a male-specific axis of energy metabolism and reproductive fitness in Anopheles stephensi
Article.Authors: Sankhala N.; Singh T.; Yadav P.; Saini V.; Rohilla P.; Srivastava V.; Sharma G.; Pradhan L.; Tyagi S.; Tevatiya S.; Sharma P.; Dixit R.
Article.Abstract: Anopheles stephensi is a major urban malaria vector whose expanding range intensifies the need for complementary control tools, several of which act by reducing male reproductive success. Male mosquitoes meet the entire energetic cost of swarming and mating from dietary sugar, which they store and circulate as trehalose, the principal fuel of insect flight. Two activities govern its availability: a trehalose transporter (TreT) that moves trehalose between the fat body, haemolymph, and peripheral tissues, and the enzyme trehalase (TreH) that hydrolyses it to usable glucose. Whether this transport-and-hydrolysis machinery is actively regulated across the swarm-to-mating sequence, and whether its regulation sets the limit on male reproductive output, has not been established. Here, we examine this in male An. stephensi using survival assays, stage-resolved expression profiling, and RNAi-mediated knockdown. On a trehalose diet, male longevity fell by roughly half relative to sucrose, reversing the male survival advantage seen on sucrose and indicating a male-specific metabolic vulnerability. Across the swarm–mating sequence, TreT and TreH expression was re-timed in the fat body and midgut, and circulating glucose was depleted at coupling while trehalose was held in reserve. Silencing TreT raised circulating trehalose yet reduced the eggs produced by mated females, and combined silencing of TreT and TreH reduced egg output by approximately one-third, consistent with the deficit arising from impaired delivery of trehalose to tissues rather than a shortage of circulating reserve. Together, these findings implicate trehalose transport as a male-specific link between flight and swarm energetics and reproductive output, and suggest male carbohydrate metabolism as a potential target for vector control.

Article.Title: GelMA/OKGM/tannic acid hydrogel with antioxidant and antibacterial properties for full-thickness wound healing
Article.Authors: Peng L.; Ren Q.; Xu J.; Ren D.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cutaneous wound healing is often impaired by prolonged oxidative stress and bacterial infection. However, conventional wound dressings are generally unable to adequately address these challenges owing to their limited biological functionality. Although hydrogel-based systems offer promising approaches to wound management, combining appropriate physicochemical properties with multiple biological functions remains challenging. In this study, a multifunctional photocrosslinked hydrogel consisting of gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), oxidized konjac glucomannan (OKGM), and tannic acid (TA) was developed. The GelMA/OKGM/TA hydrogel underwent rapid photocrosslinking and showed antioxidant and in vitro antibacterial activities. In a sterile full-thickness excisional wound model in rats, the GelMA/OKGM/TA hydrogel accelerated wound closure and improved histological features of tissue repair compared with the untreated control and GelMA-treated groups. Together, these results indicate that incorporating TA into a photocrosslinkable GelMA/OKGM hydrogel confers antioxidant and in vitro antibacterial properties and supports wound repair in a preclinical model. Nevertheless, further investigation in infected-wound models, together with comprehensive in vivo safety assessments, is needed to evaluate the hydrogel’s therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Land subsidence susceptibility linked to unsustainable agriculture and groundwater depletion in water-stressed regions
Article.Authors: Rafiei-Sardooi E.; Mohammadi A.; Azareh A.; Cushman S.; Wan H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Land subsidence is a growing hazard with far-reaching socioeconomic, environmental, and safety implications, especially in densely populated and water-stressed regions. In areas where groundwater is the primary water source, prolonged overextraction causes declines in water tables and destabilizes the ground, leading to widespread land deformation. We developed a multi-scale deep neural network model, an artificial intelligence technique that integrates environmental and anthropogenic predictors across predictor-specific spatial scales, to identify the key drivers of land subsidence in water-stressed landscapes. We used 631 confirmed subsidence presence points paired with 631 pseudo-absence points to train our model. For each point, we extracted a set of environmental variables, including elevation (DEM), slope, plan and profile curvature, NDVI, topographic wetness index, distance to river, population density, well density, geology, land use, and soil type. Our results show that agriculture within a 4,000 m radius is the strongest predictor of subsidence susceptibility, followed by well density at 2,000 m and Qft2 geology at 3,000 m. Susceptibility increases sharply with rangeland cover up to 20%, while the presence of rock outcrops in Inceptisols leads to a distinct rise in susceptibility. Areas with the highest predicted subsidence susceptibility align with regions of intensive agriculture in the western, northwestern, and northern parts of the study area. Moderate- susceptibility zones are associated with dense well infrastructure and sensitive geological formations, whereas lower overall predicted susceptibility characterizes many rangeland-dominated landscapes, reflecting the combined influence of all predictors rather than any single variable’s local contribution. These patterns highlight the urgent need for sustainable groundwater management policies, particularly in agricultural landscapes built on subsidence-prone geology, to prevent further environmental degradation and infrastructure vulnerability.

Article.Title: Dietary patterns derived by RRR and PCA in relation to insulin resistance and adiposity: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Norouziasl R.; Lesani A.; Shab-Bidar S.
Article.Abstract: Insulin resistance is a key contributor to metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. This study compares dietary patterns identified using reduced rank regression (RRR) and principal component analysis (PCA) in relation to insulin resistance and adiposity indices among Iranian adults. This cross-sectional study recruited 850 adults aged 20–59 from health centers in Tehran in 2020. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated 168-item semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (sq-FFQ). The triglyceride glucose (TyG) index and lipid accumulation product (LAP) were used as insulin resistance markers, while the body roundness index (BRI), visceral adiposity index (VAI), and body adiposity index (BAI) were used as adiposity indices. PCA-derived dietary patterns were labeled as “Healthy” and “Mixed,” while a single RRR-derived pattern was extracted. Logistic regression models estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) across tertiles of dietary patterns, adjusting for confounders. Participants had a mean age of 44.76 years and mean BMI of 27.77 kg/m². The RRR pattern, characterized by high intake of fruits, organ meat, eggs, sweets, nuts, and refined grains, was significantly associated with a lower OR for VAI (OR: 0.53, CI: 0.28–0.97, p-trend: 0.041). PCA-derived patterns were not significantly associated with insulin resistance biomarkers or adiposity indices. These findings highlight the potential of RRR in capturing dietary patterns in Iranian adults that may be relevant to metabolic health.

Article.Title: GOMPC: a gas-optimized multi-party computation framework for blockchain-based parametric crop insurance
Article.Authors: Priyadharshini G.; Jayashree P.
Article.Abstract: Parametric crop insurance has emerged as a transformative solution for improving agricultural risk management by enabling automated compensation based on predefined environmental indicators such as rainfall, temperature, and drought severity. The integration of blockchain technology into crop insurance systems further enhances transparency, trust, and decentralization while reducing reliance on intermediaries in claim settlement. However, existing parametric insurance approaches suffer from limitations, including high gas consumption in blockchain transactions, delayed settlements, privacy concerns in data sharing, and vulnerability to manipulation in centralized verification mechanisms. Additionally, traditional smart contract architectures often suffer from computational inefficiencies and higher operational costs, limiting scalability for large-scale agricultural applications. To address these challenges, this study proposes a gas-optimized multi-party computation-enabled smart contract framework (GOMPC-SCF) that integrates multi-party computation (MPC) with blockchain-based smart contracts for secure, low-cost, and automated settlement execution. The framework employs off-chain computation, gas-efficient consensus mechanisms, and secure oracle-based aggregation of environmental data to ensure privacy-preserving, tamper-resistant insurance validation. The proposed framework is applied to drought-based crop compensation systems for automated claim processing and rapid farmer reimbursement. Experimental findings demonstrate that GOMPC-SCF significantly reduces gas fees, improves settlement speed, enhances security and transparency, and increases trustworthiness in decentralized agricultural insurance ecosystems. It achieves 47,000 gas units, 24 s settlement time, 70 TPS throughput, 98.92% privacy preservation, 98% attack resistance, 98% claim settlement accuracy, 97.84% scalability efficiency, and 97.82% farmer satisfaction index under maximum evaluation conditions.

Article.Title: Semi-analytical, physics-informed and numerical solution of a nonlinear reaction–diffusion biofilm model for the biofiltration of ethyl acetate and toluene as single pollutants and in mixture
Article.Authors: Nair J.; Praveen T.
Article.Abstract: The biodegradation of volatile organic compounds inside a microbial biofilm is governed by the competition between diffusive transport and inhibited microbial consumption, yet the coupled ethyl-acetate–toluene–oxygen subsystem that controls this process has rarely been examined as a self-contained boundary-value problem. This study isolates the biofilm equations of a dynamic peat-biofilter model and analyses the steady-state, dimensionless reaction–diffusion balances of ethyl acetate, toluene and oxygen, incorporating Haldane self-inhibition of ethyl acetate, Monod kinetics for toluene, competitive cross-inhibition of toluene by ethyl acetate, and dual oxygen limitation of both substrates. The resulting coupled nonlinear system is solved by three independent routes: the semi-analytical Akbari–Ganji method (AGM), a physics-informed neural network (PINN), and a pdepe-based method-of-lines scheme adopted as the numerical benchmark. Mixture, ethyl-acetate-only and toluene-only configurations are each studied across five Thiele-modulus cases spanning reaction-controlled to strongly diffusion-limited regimes. A quantitative point-by-point error analysis shows that the PINN retains sub-0.15% relative error throughout, whereas the AGM is essentially exact at low modulus and deviates by up to about 2% in the film interior at high modulus. A normalized sensitivity analysis identifies oxygen diffusivity as the dominant control on biofilm effectiveness, followed by ethyl-acetate self-inhibition and competitive cross-inhibition. The results also expose a pronounced kinetic asymmetry in which cross-inhibition and shared oxygen demand shape the two substrate profiles in opposite directions.

Article.Title: Hepatitis B and C infections and risk of age related macular degeneration in a nationwide Korean cohort
Article.Authors: Choi K.; Roh H.; Park W.; Yi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evidence on viral hepatitis and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains limited, particularly from long-term prospective studies. We investigated whether hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are associated with the subsequent development of AMD in a nationwide Korean cohort. Using National Health Insurance Service data, we included 12,386,563 adults aged ≥ 40 years who underwent health examinations in 2009–2010 and were followed through 2023. HBV and HCV infections were identified using diagnostic codes. Incident AMD was classified as exudative using Rare Intractable Disease registration codes and as nonexudative using Korean Classification of Diseases codes. During follow-up, 388,652 participants developed incident AMD. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, HBV infection was associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05–1.32) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.60–1.76). HCV infection was also associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.27–1.86) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.27–1.57). Associations appeared stronger in women in sex-stratified analyses. HBV and HCV infections were associated with increased risks of both exudative and nonexudative AMD.

Article.Title: Preliminary evaluation of inductive current transformers applicability for accurate transformation of distorted current
Article.Authors: Kaczmarek M.; Wiak S.; Di Barba P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper the key idea is presented to assess the applicability of inductive current transformer for transformation of distorted current on the basis of the level of the secondary voltage distortion measured for supplied excitation current of its magnetic core in the no-load state. The RMS value of the main component of the excitation current is determined from measured values of current error and phase displacement in routine test performed in accordance with the standard IEC 61869-2 for transformation of sinusoidal current of a given RMS value with a particular load of the secondary winding. The essence of the accurate transformation of distorted current by the inductive current transformer is to ensure lowest possible self-generation of higher harmonics to its secondary current. This phenomenon is caused by the nonlinearity of the magnetization characteristic of the magnetic core. This method therefore allows the degree of that nonlinearity to be assessed indirectly. For the tested units the factor ranked the operating points in the same order as the self-distortion current error measured in the full distorted-current test whenever the compared values differed by more than 25%. The verification covers only the 3rd and 5th harmonics.

Article.Title: Assessment of round-trip and coulombic efficiency in lithium-ion batteries using a mathematical modeling approach under variable operating conditions
Article.Authors: Kumar D.; Rao K.; Kumar P.; Rao C.; Bankupalli P.; Guntreddi V.
Article.Abstract: Accurate quantification of Coulombic efficiency and degradation is essential for evaluating the long-term performance of lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles and stationary energy-storage systems. However, existing battery-aging studies predominantly emphasize capacity fade and impedance growth, while the coupled evolution of Coulombic efficiency, capacity retention, and round-trip performance under aging and thermal conditions is less systematically quantified. This study develops an analytical framework for evaluating Coulombic efficiency and round-trip performance as functions of battery age and operating temperature. The framework is experimentally validated using a 3.6-V, 3-Ah lithium-ion cell under controlled charge–discharge conditions. Battery behavior is evaluated over 1500 cycles and across a temperature range of 0–75 °C. The discharge capacity decreases from 2.704 to 1.783 Ah after 1500 cycles, corresponding to a capacity loss of approximately 34.1%, while Coulombic efficiency decreases from 90.1 to 59.43%. The proposed model is further evaluated against experimental measurements over the investigated temperature range, demonstrating close agreement. The results establish quantitative relationships between battery aging, thermal conditions, capacity retention, and Coulombic efficiency, providing a practical framework for battery-condition assessment and efficiency-aware battery-management strategies.

Article.Title: Spectrum of viral infections and asymptomatic viral shedding in a cohort of Indian children with inborn errors of immunity
Article.Authors: Mohanty M.; Taur P.; Gowri V.; Vengurlekar P.; Varose S.; Pandrowala A.; Iyengar V.; Chougule A.; Potdar V.; Choudhary M.; Yadav R.; Madkaikar M.; Desai M.
Article.Abstract: Inborn Errors of Immunity (IEI), result in heightened susceptibility to pathogens in general including viruses, yet data on viral burden and immune correlates in Indian paediatric population remain scarce. This study aimed to characterize the spectrum of viral infections in Indian children with IEI and evaluate the association between specific immune cell deficiencies and virus shedding, and the clinical outcomes. A cohort of 102 genetically confirmed IEI patients were systematically screened for viral infections. RT-PCR was performed on nasopharyngeal swabs, serum, and stool samples to detect active viral presence. Our findings revealed a strikingly high prevalence of viral infections (67%), predominantly involving Adenovirus (31%), Norovirus (24%), and Parvovirus B19 (21%) in the Indian cohort. Sixty three percent of the infected IEI patients were asymptomatic, among patients with intrinsic and innate immune defects as well as predominantly antibody deficiencies. Importantly, patients receiving intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) therapy were able to limit the viral shedding, suggesting a therapeutic benefit in mitigating viral burden. Our findings have relevance in terms of community transmission of viruses as well as infection control practices in IEI children in the hospital and can provide data that can inform the development of targeted surveillance systems, early diagnostic protocols, and effective treatment workflows.

Article.Title: Phenotypic diversity in sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (l.) Moench] landraces in Tigray, northern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Welderufael S.
Article.Abstract: Frequency distribution, Shannon–Weaver diversity index (H′), and multivariate methods were used to estimate the phenotypic diversity of 108 sorghum landraces growing in Tigray based on 13 qualitative traits, taking their districts of origin, geographical zones, and altitude classes into considerations. Results showed that the H′ computed for individual traits varied from 0.33 for grain form to 0.99 for grain plumpness with a mean of 0.83. The estimated H′ of each trait pooled over districts of origin, geographical zones, and alctitude classes were high with an overall mean of 0.71, 0.74, and 0.70, respectively. The H′ pooled over traits within the districts, geographical zones, and altitude classes were high with an overall mean of 0.71, 0.74, and 0.69, respectively. On the basis of district origin, the highest (0.84) and the lowest (0.46) H′ values were from Tahtay adyabo and Raya Azebo districts, respectively. When the geographical zones were considered, the highest (0.83) and the lowest (0.46) H′ values were recorded for the northwestern zone and southern zone, respectively. With respect to altitude classes, the highest (0.80) and lowest (0.68) H′ value were recorded for 1001 m.a.s.l and > 1600 m.a.s.l, respectively. Partitioning of the phenotypic diversity showed that 85%, 92%, and 89% of the variations were explained within districts of origin, geographical zones, and altitude classes, respectively, indicating that most diversity resides within these classification variables rather than between them. PCA identified inflorescence compactness and shape, grain covering, and awns at maturity as the most discriminating traits. The treasure of diversity suggests the potential for exploitation in sorghum improvement and conservation programs.

Article.Title: Exploring the user experience and improvement strategies of AI chatbots on China’s Meituan instant retail platform from the perspective of generation Z users
Article.Authors: Lu T.; Song J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is profoundly transforming traditional service models. In recent years, AI chatbots have gradually become a common smart service on instant retail platforms. However, existing research still lacks sufficient understanding of users’ actual experiences when using this type of AI service primarily based on intelligent interaction. This study focuses on the AI chatbots on Meituan’s instant retail platform, examines the experiences and conditions of Generation Z when using AI chatbots, and proposes strategies and recommendations for improving the user experience. The study examined the research questions by combining user interviews, the KANO model, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process. The main findings are as follows: Generation Z has the highest demand for the intelligent interaction experience provided by AI chatbots. At the same time, the degree of importance of needs such as personalized AI chatbot avatar, humanized AI interaction, AI personalized recommendations, and intelligent emotional perception interaction is relatively high. This indicates that Generation Z’s demands for AI chatbots have already expanded from simple needs such as consulting about products and orders to diversified online personalized consumption experiences. For example, inquiring about the usage rules of platform coupons, receiving intelligent recommendations based on personal dietary habits, and other diversified online lifestyles. Based on this, this study proposes experience enhancement strategies for optimizing the dialogue mechanism between users and AI chatbots, improving the anthropomorphic level of the interface dialogue mechanism, providing visualized presentation of intelligent service progress, and providing functional settings for user privacy protection. This study offers new insights into improving the user experience of AI chatbots on instant retail platforms.

Article.Title: A novel GAA variant reveals potential mechanisms of proteostasis disruption in late onset Pompe disease
Article.Authors: Moschetti M.; Vercelli L.; Venezia M.; Giacomarra M.; Vinci M.; Zora M.; Boschi S.; Urbano G.; Gadaleta G.; Zizzo C.; Colomba P.; Duro G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pompe disease (PD) is a rare neuromuscular disorder caused by variants in the GAA gene, leading to an acid alpha-glucosidase enzyme deficiency. An exploratory analysis for protein interactions was conducted through STRING platform to investigate the molecular consequences of lysosomal dysfunction in PD. However, despite the absence of clinically validated correlations between functional enrichment and the phenotype, the analysis facilitated the identification of a network of proteins involved in pivotal metabolic processes. In this study, we report a previously unreported heterozygous variant identified in a 55-year-old male patient presenting with symptoms suggestive of late-onset PD (LOPD). Based on clinical presentation and reduced enzyme activity, genetic testing identified the novel c.944G > A (p.Ser315Asn) mutation in exon 5, compound heterozygous with the known causative c.2560 C > T (p.Arg854Ter) mutation in exon 18. Various analytical procedures and a family segregation study determined the pathogenicity of this new variant. Absent from public databases, the variant has been classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG criteria. This approach is crucial for interpreting variants of uncertain significance and expanding the molecular understanding of PD. Incorporating exploratory use of computational tools clarifies the biological mechanisms underlying the disease, opening future prospects for better prognostic stratification and clinical management of complex neuromuscular cases.

Article.Title: Internal and external factors influencing total segment number and posterior segment regeneration of the earthworm model Eisenia andrei
Article.Authors: Tóth G.; Pollák E.; Pirger Z.; Fodor I.; Molnár L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Posterior segment regeneration in earthworms is a complex process shaped by intrinsic physiological state and environmental conditions, yet the decisive factors determining regenerative output remain incompletely understood. Using the earthworm model Eisenia andrei (Annelida: Clitellata: Lumbricidae), we investigated how body condition, nutritional status, sexual maturity, and degree of tissue loss influenced posterior segment regeneration through quantitative, morphological, histochemical, and ultrastructural analyses. Our findings revealed a tendency for final regenerative output to converge toward a baseline body plan, with most individuals approaching approximately 100 total segments after regeneration. Sexual maturity (clitellate state) did not influence the regenerative output, suggesting that clitellum-associated regulation of regeneration may be context-dependent or species-specific rather than universal across earthworms. In contrast, nutritional status had a pronounced effect: starved animals regenerated approximately 82% more segments than fed animals despite substantial body weight loss, revealing an unexpected association between nutrient restriction and increased regenerative output. Regenerated segments also differed morphologically between nutritional conditions, suggesting that tissue maturation and differentiation may proceed differently under starvation. Ultrastructural analyses revealed extensive muscle dedifferentiation and a heterogeneous regeneration blastema, including cells lacking detectable mitochondria. Consistent with these observations, lactate dehydrogenase activity was increased particularly in regenerating starved animals, providing preliminary evidence for enhanced glycolytic metabolism and raising the possibility that lactate-dependent processes play a role in regeneration. Together, these findings reveal a strong influence of nutritional state on segment regeneration and provide new insights into the physiological and cellular mechanisms underlying total segment number and posterior regeneration in E. andrei .

Article.Title: A giant eocene ischyromyid from Southeast Asia reveals the early evolution of rodent gigantism
Article.Authors: Chaimanee Y.; Marivaux L.; Millien V.; Yamee C.; Tian P.; Jaeger J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gigantism has evolved repeatedly in rodents, but the best-documented examples are predominantly known from Neogene caviomorphs of South America. Evidence for gigantism among early rodents is scarce, limiting our understanding of its evolutionary history. Here we describe Yakamys sirindhornae gen. et sp. nov., a giant ischyromyid from the late Eocene of the Krabi Basin, southern Thailand. The new taxon is represented by a lower second molar and an associated lower incisor that combine exceptionally large dimensions with a distinctive suite of dental characters, including a moderately high crown, a short, isolated anteroconid, an incomplete metalophulid II, a bifid entolophid, and the absence of a mesoconid and hypoconulid. Incisor enamel exhibits a pauciserial Hunter–Schreger band pattern consistent with Ischyromyidae enamel microstructure. Body mass estimates derived from seven allometric equations range from 21.4 to 47.3 kg, with a mean of 31.6 kg and a median of 28.6 kg. We use approximately 30 kg as a rounded summary of the central tendency of these estimates, while acknowledging the substantial uncertainty associated with dental allometry. This estimate indicates that Yakamys had a substantially greater body mass than previously described Paleogene ischyromyids. Its discovery provides evidence for exceptionally large body size in Eocene ischyromyids of Southeast Asia. It demonstrates that substantial body-size increases had occurred in an early rodent lineage by the late Eocene, well before the major diversification of giant Neogene caviomorphs in South America. This finding further highlights the importance of the Southeast Asian fossil record for understanding the early diversification and morphological evolution of rodents.

Article.Title: DrowsyFormer-Gen: classical baselines match a triple-stream transformer with diffusion augmentation for driver drowsiness detection
Article.Authors: Leonid T.; Londhe G.; Theivadas J.; Ponnan S.
Article.Abstract: Driver drowsiness detectors must be judged on minority-class sensitivity, calibration and alarm behaviour, not accuracy alone. DrowsyFormer-Gen combines physiological, vehicle and behavioural transformer streams with cross-modal fusion, an adaptive classification head and class-conditional diffusion augmentation. We re-implemented and evaluated it on shared causal windows and subject-disjoint folds against five classical baselines, using DMPS (225,000 samples; 15 drivers) and SC-DD (87,430 segments; 20 participants); DMPS drivers are a subset of SC-DD participants. Baselines received nested hyperparameter optimisation; thresholds were fixed on training data. Tuned logistic regression reached 99.747 ± 0.031% accuracy, 0.953 drowsy-class recall and expected calibration error 0.0008, ahead of every neural configuration. Each proposed component failed a controlled test: removing diffusion augmentation improved every metric, and class weighting alone reached 0.989 recall; zeroing the adaptive head’s reference halved calibration error while its refresh interval was inert; and the fusion ablation, over 25 runs, ranged from 0.000 to 1.000 recall at a fixed threshold despite stable ranking. A single sample reached 0.915 recall against 0.956 for the 32-sample window. We report a negative result, conditional on the supplied records being what the source publications describe.

Article.Title: Evaluation of state-of-the-art models for improving the diagnosis of mango tree diseases through supervised learning of symptom images in Burkina Faso
Article.Authors: Dianda Z.; Kaboré E.; Keita Z.; Zida I.; Kinda Z.; Benjamin L.; Sadouanouan M.; Wonni I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In Burkina Faso, the mango industry faces numerous phytosanitary constraints. This situation is exacerbated by producers’ lack of knowledge about diseases and their symptoms and the low uptake of control technologies. This study aims to develop a tool using artificial intelligence-based approaches for better integrated management of the main diseases affecting mango trees. Surveys conducted in 40 mango orchards yielded 11,001 images of the characteristic symptoms of three major diseases, including 4,527 for anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides , 3,038 for bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. mangiferaeindicae and 3,436 for dieback caused by Lasiodiplodia spp. The data underwent several preprocessing steps. To ensure a balance between disease classes, 3,000 images per class were selected, for a total of 9,000 images. The images were then annotated and used for training with the pre-trained YOLOv11 model. Following training, three models were formed : V2-3 M (MAP@50 = 50,3%; precision = 55,1%; recall = 49,1%; F1-score = 51,9%), V3-3 M (MAP@50 = 23%; precision = 56,8% ; recall = 26,7%; F1-score = 36,3%), and V4-3 M (MAP@50 = 46,8%; precision = 52%; recall = 45,3%; F1-score = 48,4%). The most effective model is the V2-3 M, as it combines 55,1% accuracy, 50,3% (MAP@50, 49,1% recall and F1-score = 51,9%). In order to improve diagnosis and phytosanitary management in orchards, it would be useful to integrate treatment recommendations into the model, then deploy it on a mobile application and promote it to producers. Future work will involve dataset expansion, comparative evaluation with alternative deep learning models, and cross-regional validation to improve model robustness and generalizability.

Article.Title: Spatial distribution and health risk assessment of airborne and soil-bound lead in an industrial zone
Article.Authors: Jahanbakhsh M.; Yari A.; Fouladi-Fard R.; Karimi B.; Rezaie A.; Fahiminia M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The emission of pollutants from human activities in industrial zones poses significant challenges to air quality and soil health, particularly in semi-arid environments. Utilizing 56 sampling stations and geostatistical modeling, this study conducted a comprehensive, multi-pathway assessment of lead (Pb) dynamics in the ambient air and surface soil of the Salafchegan Special Economic Zone (SSEZ) in Iran. The results revealed a marked disparity between atmospheric Pb levels (mean: 12.88 µg/m³) and concentrations in the soil (mean: 3.05 mg/kg). This discrepancy is attributed to the region’s high wind energy (DPt = 936), which causes the resuspension of deposited dust and limits Pb accumulation in surface soil, effectively retaining the metal in the atmospheric phase. Both Ordinary Kriging (OK) and Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) produced comparable prediction errors in cross-validation; however, OK was selected for final mapping because it provides a measure of prediction uncertainty (kriging variance) and accounts for spatial autocorrelation. The OK-based maps revealed significant heterogeneity (CV = 58.36%) and identified industrial hotspots. A probabilistic health risk assessment, conducted via Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations, indicated that the total non-carcinogenic risk remained below the permissible Hazard Index threshold (HI < 1); however, children consistently demonstrated greater vulnerability than adults to exposure to this pollutant. These results show that local climatic factors strongly influence the environmental fate of Pb, indicating the need for targeted air quality management and regular monitoring around industrial zones.

Article.Title: Amharic medical question answering system using AmhBERT
Article.Authors: Bogale B.; teferra S.; Belay G.; Tegegne T.
Article.Abstract: A medical question-answering (QA) system is a natural language processing (NLP) application designed to answer medical questions. Developing such systems for Amharic remains challenging because of the limited availability of medical language resources. To address this gap, this study presents Amharic medical question answering system based on Amharic adapted multilingual BERT. First, we prepared medical question answering dataset from freely accessible medical sources such as Ethiopian Health Institute (EHI). Following data collection, we extracted relevant context passages from the documents and used them to generate question-answer pairs. This process produced a collection of context-question-answer triples, each consisting of a health-related context, a question, and answer. The quality of the medical question–context–answer triples was evaluated by three medical experts from Tibebe Ghion Hospital, Bahir Dar University, with expertise in clinical nursing, general medical practice, and maternal and child health. The annotators use two criteria: question–context support and answer correctness. Pairwise Cohen’s kappa was used to assess inter-annotator agreement, with a mean score of 0.872 indicating a high level of agreement for question–context support. The dataset was evaluated using Amharic adapted multilingual BERT (mBERT) and four other transformer models. AmhBERT was obtained by continually pretraining multilingual BERT (mBERT) on 1.34 + million Amharic text sentence. Experimental results show that AmhBERT achieved the best performance over XLM-R, mBERT, BERT, and RoBERTa by substantial margins.

Article.Title: Urinary microbiota in patients with urolithiasis: a comparison of cohorts from Taiwan and South Korea
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Chang C.; Wu W.; Wu D.; Cho S.
Article.Abstract: Cohort-associated differences may influence the urinary microbiota of patients with urolithiasis. This study compared urinary microbial profiles between Taiwan and Korea patients. This cross-national comparative study included 72 patients with clinically confirmed urolithiasis, comprising 31 patients from Taiwan and 41 from South Korea. Bladder urine samples were collected by urethral catheterization before surgery and prophylactic antibiotic administration. Full-length 16S rRNA genes were amplified using the 27F and 1492R primers and sequenced using a third-generation long-read sequencing platform. Sequence denoising and amplicon sequence variant inference were performed using DADA2, followed by taxonomic annotation and phylogenetic analysis in QIIME2. Alpha diversity, beta diversity, and differential taxonomic abundance were compared between the two groups. No significant differences were observed in alpha diversity indices, including microbial richness, diversity, evenness, and phylogenetic diversity. However, Unadjusted Bray–Curtis PERMANOVA showed a statistically significant but small association between cohort membership and microbial composition, explaining approximately 1.81% of the variation (R 2 = 0.0181, P = 0.009). PERMDISP indicated unequal within-cohort dispersion for Bray–Curtis distances ( P = 0.001), warranting cautious interpretation of the PERMANOVA result. Exploratory differential abundance analyses suggested enrichment of Proteobacteria and sequences assigned to Shigella flexneri in the Taiwan cohort, and Gardnerella swidsinskii , Prevotellaceae, and Veillonella in the Korea cohort. Urinary microbial community composition differed between the Taiwan and Korea cohorts of patients with urolithiasis, whereas no statistically significant differences in alpha diversity were detected. These findings describe cohort-associated differences and do not establish their underlying causes or their role in urinary stone formation.

Article.Title: A double-arc visual analytics framework for exploring multidimensional air pollution–impact relationships
Article.Authors: Megavarnan G.; Venkatachalam K.
Article.Abstract: Air pollution is an acute environmental challenge to the sustainability and even human health, but traditional methods of visualization do not always succeed in clearly displaying the multidimensional relationship between the measured multidimensional pollutant and the resulting effects thereof. This paper proposes a Double-Arc Visualization (DAV) framework helping to combine the pollutant concentration variables and the environmental or health impact indicators into a dual-arc framework. The proposed scheme reduces visual clutter while preserving structural relationships through arc-based parallel coordinates expanded into a dual-polar display with curved connector encoding and optimized variable ordering. The framework facilitates co-examination of essential air pollutants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and CO and O₃) with the impact indicators of the Air Quality Index (AQI). Real-world air quality data demonstrate that classical evaluation shows relative linearity in rendering scalability, rendering performance with large volumes of data, and 22.4% reduction in visual clutter compared with traditional visualization methods. Another case study confirms in another instance that patterns of visual outcome of DAV is in accord with statistical analysis ( R = 0.89, p = 0.001). These findings make DAV viable and a sound visual analytics model to explore multidimensional environmental data and make decisions.

Article.Title: Combined effects of pre-harvest drought stress and drying temperature on rice milling quality using multivariate analysis and fuzzy clustering
Article.Authors: Djakhangirova G.; Baxtiyor D.; Shokouhifard M.; Rakhimov S.; Zokirov K.; Sharipova G.; Ibragimova N.; Alimova N.
Article.Abstract: Climate-driven drought events, together with post-harvest processing constraints, increasingly threaten rice milling quality, a critical determinant of market value, process efficiency, and food security. Although the individual effects of pre-harvest drought stress and post-harvest drying temperature have been reported, their combined impact on milling performance across rice genotypes has not been systematically evaluated from an engineering perspective. This study provides an integrated, genotype-level assessment showing that the interaction between drought stress and thermal drying induces genotype-specific trade-offs between drying efficiency and milling quality in a fluidized-bed drying system. Six rice genotypes were cultivated under normal and drought irrigation regimes over two growing seasons and subsequently dried at 40, 50, and 60 °C in a controlled fluidized-bed dryer. Important process and milling quality indicators, including milling yield (MY), broken rice percentage (BRP), crack percentage (CP), degree of milling, and drying time (DT), were quantified to evaluate system performance. Multivariate statistical analyses (ANOVA, correlation analysis, and PCA) were integrated with deep fuzzy clustering (DFC) to resolve complex response patterns and support decision-oriented evaluation. Drought stress reduced Optical DoM by ~ 12% and Mass‑based degree of milling (Mass DoM) by ~ 7%, and reduced MY by ~ 3% (up to ~ 4% in the most sensitive genotype), while increasing BRP by ~ 23% and CP by ~ 32%. Raising the drying temperature from 40 to 60 °C shortened DT by ~ 51% but progressively reduced milling quality; breakage (BRP) and cracking (CP) were highest at 50 °C, whereas Optical DoM and MY declined steadily with temperature, highlighting a critical process trade-off. DFC identified genotypes with more stable milling performance under combined stress, particularly those maintaining higher MY and a smaller increase in CP (though absolute CP varied). These findings provide an integrated framework for optimizing genotype selection and drying temperature, supporting more resilient rice processing systems.

Article.Title: Explainable cross-modal face photo-sketch similarity with region-wise attribution and multi-extractor fusion
Article.Authors: Kim G.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cross-modal face similarity analysis remains challenging due to substantial modality discrepancies and the limited interpretability of existing recognition models. Although recent heterogeneous face recognition approaches have improved similarity estimation accuracy, they provide little insight into which facial regions guide similarity judgments or how these cues vary across modalities. To address this limitation, we propose an explainability-driven framework that integrates multi-extractor feature aggregation with region-wise attribution. We also present the Regional Consistency Similarity (RCS) formulation which summarizes localized attribution patterns derived from structured spatial perturbation and region-level aggregation. Multiple complementary feature extractors are jointly employed to reduce model-specific biases and provide stable similarity estimates under modality variations, while an optional natural-language explanation module converts region-wise patterns into user-friendly descriptions. Experiments on four photo-sketch datasets (CUFS, CUFSF, Toonify-CUFSF, and WildSketch) show that the proposed framework produces stable and spatially coherent region-wise attribution maps across diverse sketch styles and abstraction levels. Rather than pursuing recognition-accuracy gains, the multi-extractor configuration is interpretability-focused and recognition-preserving: it maintains verification performance comparable to the strongest single extractor while strengthening the region-wise consistency signal and exposing identity-relevant regions.

Article.Title: Deformation influence of large cross-section quasi‑rectangular shield tunnel parallel crossing existing shield tunnel
Article.Authors: Nie B.; Ma S.; Ding Y.; Xu Q.; Zhang Y.; Yan M.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the influence of a large cross-section quasi-rectangular shield tunnel passing in parallel with existing shield tunnels, a three-dimensional numerical simulation was conducted using Plaxis 3D software, based on the typical geological conditions in Zhengzhou. The construction of a new single-tube double-track large cross-section quasi-rectangular shield tunnel passing in parallel with the existing Zhengzhou Metro Line 5 tunnels was simulated. The results indicate that the ground deformation induced by the quasi-rectangular shield tunneling exhibits a funnel-shaped settlement pattern above the tunnel and a U-shaped heave pattern below the tunnel. The maximum deformation of the existing tunnel occurs in the horizontal direction (X-direction), manifesting as an overall outward displacement of 8.636 mm, and the maximum total deformation of the existing tunnel is 8.660 mm. The recommended values for the chamber pressure, and tail void grouting pressure are 0.15 MPa, and 0.24–0.26 MPa, respectively. Shield shell friction should be minimized. In the simulation, 15 kN/m² is the lower bound. In practice, it can be reduced by foam, bentonite slurry, polymer conditioning, and anti-friction coatings.

Article.Title: Mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction cardiogenic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis of mortality and safety outcomes
Article.Authors: Rahhal A.; Alamami A.; Najim M.; Shehadeh M.; Abdelghani M.; Altermanini M.; Mahameed Z.; Arabi A.; Omar A.; Basir M.; Awaisu A.; Elewa H.
Article.Abstract: RegistrationMechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) devices in acute myocardial infarction (AMI)-induced cardiogenic shock remain of uncertain mortality benefit with increasing safety concerns. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of MCS compared to medical therapy in AMI-induced cardiogenic shock. Following PRISMA guidelines, four databases were searched for studies published in English up to January 12, 2025, that evaluated the clinical outcomes of MCS devices, including Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump (IABP), Impella, or Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO), compared to conventional therapy. Data were pooled using random-effect models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, while the secondary outcomes included major bleeding and vascular complications. Heterogeneity across studies was assessed using the Q test and I 2 , with I 2 > 50% indicating substantial heterogeneity. A total of 32 studies with 38 comparisons were included ( IABP : n = 27, 131553 participants; Impella : n = 6, 56588 participants; ECMO : n = 5, 63848 participants). MCS resulted in similar all-cause mortality across devices compared with conventional therapy [ IABP : OR = 1.00 (95% CI: 0.85–1.18, I 2 96.1%); Impella : OR = 1.01 (95% CI: 0.64–1.57, I 2 97.47%); ECMO : OR = 1.1 (95% CI: 0.73–1.66, I 2 95.32%), and was judged to have low and very low certainty of evidence from randomized controlled trial (RCT) and cohort studies, respectively. Major bleeding was significantly increased with all devices, while vascular complications were higher with Impella and ECMO. This comprehensive meta-analysis found that MCS devices were not associated with a statistically significant reduction in mortality compared with conventional therapy. However, MCS use was associated with increased major bleeding and vascular complication rates, particularly with Impella and ECMO use, warranting more research for the selective and evidence-based MCS use in this population. Given the low to very low certainty of the available evidence and considerable heterogeneity, these findings should be interpreted with caution and confirmed in RCTs. Registration The protocol of the systematic review and metaanalysis was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250622111).

Article.Title: ResNet-GA: genetic algorithm-driven optimization of ResNet for automated dental caries detection in medical imaging
Article.Authors: Chefrour A.; Zemmal N.; Namoun A.; Benzebouchi N.; Khedairia S.
Article.Abstract: Dental caries is one of the most prevalent oral diseases worldwide and remains a major public health concern because delayed or inaccurate diagnosis can lead to irreversible tooth destruction, pain, infection, and more invasive treatment. Early and reliable detection from dental images is therefore essential for improving preventive care and supporting clinical decision-making. However, manual interpretation of dental radiographs is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Although deep learning has shown strong potential for automated caries detection, its performance often depends on manually selected hyperparameters and may be affected by image variability, low contrast, artifacts, and class imbalance. To address these limitations, we propose ResNet-GA, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines deep convolutional feature learning with a genetic algorithm to automatically optimize selected convolutional configurations, particularly the number of filters and kernel sizes in three convolutional blocks. The proposed framework was evaluated on a publicly available dental caries dataset obtained from Kaggle, comprising caries and non-caries images. Images were resized, normalized, and divided into training and validation subsets, with class balancing applied to reduce bias toward the majority class. The genetic algorithm iteratively evolved candidate convolutional configurations using classification accuracy as the fitness criterion. The optimized model achieved high diagnostic performance, with a mean test accuracy of 87.89% ± 1.41% (macro precision 89.74% ± 0.95%, macro recall 80.38% ± 3.04%, macro F1-score 83.32% ± 2.58%) across five independent runs on an independent test set. These results indicate that evolutionary optimization of convolutional configurations can improve robustness and classification performance for automated dental caries detection. By reducing dependence on manual architectural tuning and improving diagnostic consistency, the proposed framework offers a promising computer-aided decision-support approach for dental image analysis.

Article.Title: Floquet modes in quasi-periodic temporal photonic crystals based on the Kolakoski sequence
Article.Authors: Ittepadan A.; Jaffar Ali G.; Kotov L.; Nayak C.
Article.Abstract: We present a theoretical framework for quasi-periodic temporal photonic crystals (PCs) based on four types of deterministic Kolakoski sequences. The proposed system consists of two temporally modulated dielectric responses, where the refractive index contrast generates a momentum gap in the frequency-momentum space. Unlike conventional temporal PCs, the deterministic aperiodic ordering of the Kolakoski sequence creates multiple momentum gaps and resonant states over the momentum space. Using the transfer matrix method, we systematically analyze the influence of the permittivity contrast and temporal layer duration contrast on the transmission characteristics in both lossless and lossy cases. Results show that aperiodic order enhance the momentum gaps due to the increased number of temporal layers and stronger Floquet modes. Increasing permittivity contrast increasing width in the momentum gaps, while varying layer durations, causes larger momentum shifts in the momentum spectrum in both systems. In the lossy regime, material loss slightly enhance the amplification without significantly altering the position of the momentum gaps. These findings highlight the potential of Kolakoski-based temporal PCs for ultrafast, dynamically tunable photonic devices.

Article.Title: Patient-anatomy-referenced multiscale modelling of median nerve conduction in carpal tunnel syndrome
Article.Authors: Munir G.; Haque M.; Shamim M.; Shams S.
Article.Abstract: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS) is a common compressive peripheral neuropathy causing focal conduction slowing and sensory dysfunction. Existing computational models are either mechanical or electrophysiological in isolation, precluding mechanistic understanding of nerve dysfunction across severity grades. We introduce a multiscale computational system built on a patient-anatomy-referenced median nerve pathway, rigidly registered and anatomically deformed against this patient’s own segmented bone and skin geometry, with the compression zone defined at 0–29.4 mm from the detected wrist point. A reduced-order conduction-velocity model, a FitzHugh–Nagumo (FHN) reaction–diffusion model and an unfitted McIntyre–Richardson–Grill (MRG) double-cable model were analysed on this pathway. The velocity and FHN models were calibrated to Kimura’s Normal and Mild data (zone velocities 57–59 and about 41 m/s) and predicted about 24 and 7 m/s for Moderate and Severe CTS. The MRG model predicted a normal velocity of 56.1 m/s without fitting and complete conduction block in Severe CTS, but under-predicted Mild and Moderate slowing (52.8 and 43.6 m/s). Convergence, sensitivity analysis and ten-run registration repeatability are reported, with registration limitations (16.0% of tube-surface points outside the skin) disclosed rather than assumed away. The framework is a research platform for peripheral neuropathy investigation, not a validated diagnostic tool.

Article.Title: An integrated in silico and in vitro approach to optimize Aspergillus niger xylanase using agricultural wastes for bioethanol production
Article.Authors: Ahmed S.; Amin S.; Abou-Taleb K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungi and agricultural waste have drawn more attention as a source of xylanase enzyme synthesis recently. In this study, fungal isolates able to produce xylanase were isolated from the soil sample. Within the 19 isolates, three exhibited the highest activity as determined by the Dinitro Salicylic Acid (DNS) method. These isolates were cultivated using various agricultural wastes as cheap carbon sources (xylan), including corn cob, maize straw, sugar cane bagasse, wheat straw, wheat bran, rice husk, and sawdust. Out of the three isolates, the most effective one (WA7) and three agricultural wastes (rice husk 167 U mL −1 , corn cob 159 U mL −1 , wheat bran 154 U mL −1 ) were chosen based on the highest xylanase activity. Using Design-Expert, the optimization of xylanase production occurred in two phases. The first step was screening the essential fermentation parameters affecting xylanase production using the Plackett–Burman design. For the second step in optimization using a definitive screening design, the most important factors for enzyme synthesis from the fungal isolate were further investigated. The maximum xylanase yield after optimization was 242 U mL −1 . Based on genotypic characterization, the fungal isolate was identified as Aspergillus niger 28S ribosomal rRNA. Xylanase enzyme was used in four different processes to produce ethanol on various substrates. The fourth simultaneous saccharification and fermentation technique, which used rice husk as an environmentally friendly waste, was shown to be the most effective, with ethanol yields reaching 40 g L −1 . Further, A. niger xylanase showed optimal molecular interaction and binding affinity toward xylan: −8.00 kcal/mol. Based on these results, A. niger xylanase showed a promising perspective for xylan hydrolysis to produce ethanol.

Article.Title: Transformer-based endoscopic polyp detection with structural reparameterization and dynamic upsampling
Article.Authors: Ren X.; Tang Y.; He Z.; Lu D.; Xie X.; Wang M.; Li Z.; Liang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate polyp detection is important for colorectal cancer prevention, while practical deployment requires reliable localization, manageable model complexity, and robust detection performance. This paper presents an improved RT-DETR-r18 detector for endoscopic polyp detection. The proposed C2f_RCB backbone construction embeds a UniRepLKNet-derived large-kernel reparameterization transformation within the C2f hierarchy, while the original DySample operator replaces the two nearest-neighbor upsampling layers in the top-down neck. A source-code audit shows that the K = 7 DilatedReparamBlock contains one 7 × 7 depthwise main branch and three auxiliary depthwise branches, namely 5 × 5 with dilation 1, 3 × 3 with dilation 2, and 3 × 3 with dilation 3. During deployment, these spatial branches are merged into an equivalent 7 × 7 depthwise convolution, and compatible normalization/affine terms are further folded into adjacent operators by the UniRepLKNetBlock deployment routine; SE, GELU, GRN normalization/scaling, channel projections, residual operations, and DySample remain explicit in the inference graph. Under the archived evaluation protocol, the complete model achieves 96.8% precision, 93.0% recall, 97.1% mAP@0.5, and 79.5% mAP@0.5:0.95, with 13.90 million parameters and 46.6 GFLOPs. These values were obtained from an expanded-file split later found to contain augmented variants of the same original samples across subsets and should therefore be regarded as preliminary until leakage-free retraining is completed. The current evidence supports a compact, localization-oriented trade-off, but not a standardized runtime advantage, clinical readiness, or leakage-free generalization.

Article.Title: China’s elite championship output during and after the COVID-19 disruption: competition opportunities and Olympic/Paralympic cycle structure, 2013–2025
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Gong S.; Xu Y.; Zhou S.
Article.Abstract: Annual world-champion counts indicate elite sporting output, but they are constrained by the international competition calendar. This study examined China’s non-disabled and para championship output from 2013 to 2025 in relation to competition availability and Olympic/Paralympic cycle structure. Official annual data on world-champion counts and world-record items were combined with an 11-series selected World Championship calendar and official cancellation, postponement, and event-opportunity records. Primary analyses described annual output and ratios relative to group-specific 2013–2019 means. A calendar-sensitivity proxy was calculated for 2021–2025, when selected-core availability was non-zero. Mean pre-pandemic output was 115.43 championships for non-disabled athletes and 231.43 for para athletes. In 2020, output ratios fell to 0.035 and 0.104, while selected-core calendar availability fell to 0. In 2021, availability was 0.636 and the sensitivity proxies were 0.912 and 0.747. Mean output ratios across 2023–2025 were 1.458 and 1.070, respectively; the 2025 ratios were 1.265 and 0.773. World-record items fell from 16 in 2019 to 1 in 2020 and reached 17 in 2025. These findings describe substantial disruption and heterogeneous subsequent output patterns but do not isolate a causal COVID-19 effect or directly measure organizational resilience. Competition opportunity and cycle position should therefore be considered when interpreting national elite-sport output.

Article.Title: Association of the planetary health diet index with overweight and obesity among patients with diabetes mellitus in a cross sectional study
Article.Authors: Moradi Baniasadi M.; Nasli-Esfahani E.; Khakbaz M.; Azadbakht L.
Article.Abstract: The Eat-Lancet diet, which encourages a shift towards plant-based foods and reduced intake of animal products, has been proposed as a solution to improve both human health and environmental sustainability. This study explores the association between Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) adherence and the risk of overweight or obesity in type 2 diabetes (T2D) residing in Tehran, aiming to determine whether this diet can serve as a dual-purpose strategy for managing weight and promoting planetary health. A total of 210 participants were recruited in this cross-sectional study. Dietary information was gathered via a validated 168-item food frequency questionnaire, and PHDI score was derived from 16 food groups. Anthropometric assessments were performed following standard procedures to identify overweight or obesity. Associations between PHDI and outcomes were examined using logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models. Study participants had a mean age of 62.15 ± 8.60 years, and 70% were female. PHDI was categorized into tertiles, with 33.3% of individuals in the highest tertile. In fully adjusted logistic models, high PHDI adherence was associated—though not significantly—with lower odds of overweight/obesity (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.42, 1.95) and obesity (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.37, 2.20) compared to low adherence. Additionally, we did not observe any non-linear association between PHDI and odds of overweight/obesity in T2D patients, after adjustments for potential confounders. Given the absence of a statistically significant link between PHDI and the likelihood of overweight or obesity, which may reflect insufficient statistical power, future studies incorporating larger cohorts and diverse populations are needed to assess the generalizability of these findings.
