Article.Title: An advanced power management approach for renewable energy-powered EV charging system with a high-gain extended step-up converter
Article.Authors: Priya N.; Prabaakaran K.
Article.Abstract: Increasing global use of Electric Vehicles necessitates high-efficiency, and durable charging infrastructure. Photovoltaic (PV)-powered EV Charging Stations are an environmentally friendly solution; nevertheless, their effectiveness is limited by PV intermittency, low voltage levels, dynamic load changes, and grid integration issues. To solve these issues, this research proposes a PV-integrated EV charging architecture which includes a Max Gain Extended Step-Up DC-DC converter and a Eurasian Oystercatcher Optimized Proportional-Integral (EOO-PI) control technique. The proposed converter is used to convert the low PV voltage to a higher voltage while minimizing device stress and ripple. The EOO-PI controller employed for fast dynamic response, superior voltage regulation, and increasing resilience under varying circumstances. A Bidirectional DC-DC converter connected to a battery for effective energy buffering, peak load assistance, and power sharing during PV intermittency and outages. Grid integration is accomplished using a three-phase Voltage Source Inverter with an LC filter, which allows smooth bidirectional active and reactive power flow. Furthermore, a PI-controlled inverter-fed Brushless DC motor implemented for steady speed regulation and low torque ripple across all operating conditions. MATLAB/Simulink simulation and hardware outcomes indicate stable DC-link regulation and uninterrupted EV charging with 98.1% efficiency and grid current Total Harmonic Distortion of 0.26% (R-phase), 0.21% (Y-phase), and 0.15% (B-phase) under dynamic operating conditions.

Article.Title: Simulation-based LuGre modelling and voltage-scheduled control of low-voltage stick-slip piezoelectric actuators
Article.Authors: Saxena S.; Barrow J.; Lawrence J.; Omadutt A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Piezoelectric stick-slip actuators are widely used in precision positioning applications, including astronomy, microscopy, and micro-manipulation systems. In this simulation-based study, a low-voltage stick-slip piezoelectric actuator is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink using the LuGre friction model to describe the dynamic friction behaviour at the contact interface. The actuator response is first evaluated in terms of voltage- and frequency-dependent step size and velocity, as these parameters are important for understanding the motion behaviour and designing an effective control strategy. A voltage scheduling scheme is then developed to adjust the driving voltage according to the position error, allowing coarse motion at larger errors and finer positioning near the target. The model is further extended to a three-actuator triangular configuration, where the user-level input is interpreted in terms of desired pitch and roll, and then converted into individual actuator displacement commands. In addition, a discrete move-measure-correct strategy is discussed as a reduced sensing-duty-cycle approach for applications where continuous displacement measurement may not be feasible. The proposed simulation framework demonstrates the feasibility of LuGre-based modelling and voltage-scheduled control for low-voltage stick-slip actuator positioning, and provides a basis for future experimental validation in scalable precision positioning systems.

Article.Title: Regional and severity-specific heterogeneity in meniscal pathology: associations with clinical etiology and patient characteristics
Article.Authors: Gu J.; Wang C.; Zhang Y.; Jiang T.; Zhang L.; Sun Y.; Gu Q.; Mi D.; Yang H.
Article.Abstract: Meniscal injuries vary by subregion, but whether etiology and lesion severity show distinct regional patterns remains unclear. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 979 patients with meniscal pathology. Lesions were classified into six subregions and graded 0–III according to the Stoller classification; etiology was categorized as high-energy, low-energy, or degenerative. Regression analyses assessed associations with etiology, age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). After Bonferroni correction, only medial anterior horn (MAH) and medial posterior horn (MPH) lesions were associated with etiology ( P < 0.001 and P = 0.002, respectively). In unadjusted analyses, degenerative etiology was associated with both MAH and MPH lesions, but this association remained significant only for MAH after adjustment ( OR = 1.875, P = 0.007). Older age ( OR = 1.034 per year, P < 0.001), male sex ( OR = 1.548, P = 0.011), and higher BMI ( OR = 1.060 per kg/m², P = 0.019) were independently associated with MPH lesions. For MAH severity, Grade I lesions were associated with degenerative etiology and higher BMI, whereas Grade III lesions were associated with older age and male sex. These findings demonstrate regional meniscal heterogeneity, with degenerative susceptibility and mechanical loading varying by lesion location and severity.

Article.Title: Standardising bioassays for passive spatial emanators against mosquito vectors
Article.Authors: Silva Martins W.; Hill T.; Lees R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing use of passive spatial emanators (SEs) for vector control has underscored the need for standardised laboratory methods for bioefficacy testing. Peet–Grady (PG) chamber assays are widely used to test volatile insecticides; however, key methodological parameters remain poorly characterised. Here, we investigated how airflow settings (fan speed and baffle setup), mosquito-holding cage design, and cage mesh structure influence mosquito responses to a transfluthrin (TF) passive emanator. Susceptible and pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes were exposed to TF, and effects were assessed using flight inhibition (FI) and 24-hour mortality as endpoints. The assay was highly reproducible, with 83% agreement in FI dynamics across replicate comparisons. Airflow settings were more strongly associated with FI than cage geometry or mesh structure, with 5.86- to 9.57-fold higher odds of FI without a baffle. In contrast, 24-hour mortality varied less across airflow settings, suggesting that FI may be a more sensitive assay endpoint. Time to FI thresholds was up to 4-fold shorter under the medium fan speed setting without a baffle than under the low fan speed setting with a baffle. Cage mesh structure influenced FI responses, with larger mesh apertures showing 10- to 20-fold higher odds of FI in certain configurations, whereas cage geometry had little effect, supporting the use of a higher-throughput dual-cage configuration. These findings highlight the importance of airflow setting, mosquito-holding cage design, and cage mesh structure in determining FI responses in PG-chamber assays and support their consideration when standardising passive spatial emanator bioassays.

Article.Title: Acute effects of unilateral and bilateral split-squat conditioning on change-of-direction performance in elite fencers
Article.Authors: Yildirim E.; Koç H.
Article.Abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the acute effects of unilateral and bilateral split-squat conditioning on change-of-direction (COD) performance in elite sabre fencers, with a particular focus on comparing dominant-leg, non-dominant-leg, and bilateral protocols and evaluating how the responses changed over time. Seventeen elite sabre fencers (13 males, 4 females; age range: 15–21 years; mean age: 17.29 ± 1.93 years) from a national Olympic preparation center participated in a within-subject randomized cross-over design. Participants performed three conditioning-activity protocols at 85% of estimated 1RM (dominant-leg, non-dominant-leg, and bilateral split squats) and a control condition. COD performance was recorded as time in seconds (s) using the 4-2-2-4 agility test at baseline and at 1, 3, 5, and 7 min post-conditioning activity. Lower time values indicated improved performance. COD time was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with condition, time, and the condition × time interaction as fixed effects and participant as a random intercept. Time was treated as a categorical factor. Secondary participant-level condition-versus-control differences in change from baseline were evaluated using one-sample t tests with Holm correction for 12 comparisons. COD performance changed significantly over time, F(4, 304) = 7.894, p < 0.001. However, neither the overall condition effect, F(3, 304) = 1.866, p = 0.135, nor the condition × time interaction, F(12, 304) = 0.828, p = 0.621, was statistically significant. None of the 12 condition-versus-control comparisons remained statistically significant after Holm correction. These results provide no evidence of differential temporal responses among conditions; they do not demonstrate that the protocols are equivalent. COD performance changed over repeated assessments, including during the control condition. The present data provide no evidence that dominant-leg, non-dominant-leg, or bilateral split-squat conditioning produced a temporal response that differed from the control condition. Because the study was not designed or powered to test equivalence, similarity among protocols cannot be inferred. Protocol-specific patterns in the descriptive means should therefore be interpreted as exploratory.

Article.Title: A radio-aware secure routing protocol for wireless sensor networks using predictive Markov filtering and bounded swarm optimization (RSMFSO)
Article.Authors: Jasim A.; Issa N.; Mukhlif F.; Noordin K.; Abdrabou A.; Azzuhri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are one of the key enabling technologies for applications that are energy-constrained and vulnerable to insider attacks in adversarial environments. Conventional protocols optimized for swarms will soon fire up so many multi-hop paths as to exhaust node energy prematurely and yield increasingly higher flat power losses via ongoing over-promotion of available resources ( $$\:{d}^{4}$$ ) that exceed free-space limits. At the same time, traditional clustering mechanisms are susceptible to selective forwarding and blackhole attacks of malicious nodes. In order to address these interdependent problems, RSMFSO, a trust-aware and radio-aware routing protocol, is proposed. RSMFSO localizes a W = 5-round rolling state profile (PMF) to track the 5-round history of rolling state profiles and preemptively isolates compromised nodes prior to topology formation and cluster head selection. Simultaneously, free-space ( $$\:{d}^{2}$$ ) transmission with scene-dependent physical radio constraints is enforced within an optimization engine on the same biological principles. An automated shunting circuit breaker also dynamically circumvents high-effort clustering in late-stage network decay to prevent control packet cascades and dead cascades of control packets. Extensive empirical simulations executed over standard (Scenario A: N = 100 nodes, $$\:{E}_{init}$$ = 0.5 J) and high-density deployments (Scenario B: N = 300 nodes, $$\:{E}_{init}$$ = 0.5 J) verify that RSMFSO substantially extends operational network lifetime compared to evaluated baselines, achieving up to Round 400 with a non-failure node count of approx. 100% across both scales. Scenario B: In this scenario, RSMFSO delays the first node death until Round 500 (298 active nodes) and maintains 98 active operational nodes at Round 1000, compared with LEACH, MMABC, and WIFNCP protocols. Non-parametric statistical evaluations via two-tailed Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests ( p < 0.05) and Friedman Mean Ranks (Rank 1.00) confirm that RSMFSO achieves statistically significant superiority over LEACH, MMABC, and WIFNCP across 30 independent Monte Carlo runs. With a less than 10% malicious node footprint, RSMFSO effectively mitigates the blackhole effect while maintaining high data throughput from the sensor field to the base station, making it ideal for mission-critical WSN deployments.

Article.Title: Less is more: minimal Kolmogorov–Arnold integration enhances efficiency, transparency, and explainability of vision transformers for sedimentary facies classification
Article.Authors: Koeshidayatullah A.
Article.Abstract: Automated petrographic image classification can accelerate sedimentary-facies analysis and support depositional interpretation and subsurface exploration. However, the multiscale textures and visual overlap of carbonate and siliciclastic facies remain challenging for conventional deep-learning models. Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) offer adaptive edge-wise nonlinear functions, but the optimal scope of their integration within pretrained vision transformers is unclear. We introduce KAN-DeiT and compare three integration strategies: replacing only the classification head, extending KAN to the feed-forward sublayers, and further extending it to the attention projections. As a proof of concept, head-only KAN-DeiT achieved 100% accuracy on a held-out eight-class carbonate microfacies test set. On a more ambiguous four-class mudstone dataset, the head-only KAN-DeiT model achieved 91.47% accuracy and a macro F1-score of 0.9139, outperforming the accuracy of pretrained ResNet-50 (82.95%), EfficientNet-B0 (85.27%), vanilla ViT (88.37%), and MLP-DeiT (89.92%). In contrast, Hybrid and Full KAN integration achieved only 67.44–73.64% and 65.04–65.89% accuracy, respectively, with the same overall pattern observed for RBF and B-spline parameterizations. Deeper integration increased parameter counts by up to 8.8-fold and substantially raised computational cost, whereas head-only integration added less than 0.1% parameters with unchanged GFLOPs and comparable inference latency. Attention rollout, Grad-CAM, and learned edge-function analyses indicated that the head-only model preserved the pretrained spatial representation while modifying how geologically relevant textures contributed to class decisions, although occasional responses to possible image artifacts were observed. These findings indicate that targeted KAN integration at the classification head offers a more accurate and efficient strategy than extensive transformer-wide substitution for data-constrained petrographic classification.

Article.Title: Deep learning for odontoid fractures: the critical role of patient-level partitioning and Grad-CAM assessment in model generalization
Article.Authors: Kıymaz Y.; Taşdemir Ş.; Gezer B.; Uyar Pınar K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Missed diagnoses of odontoid fractures on Computed Tomography (CT) scans can lead to severe morbidity. While Deep Learning (DL) shows promise, many studies report inflated performance metrics due to hidden data leakage (image-level splitting). To evaluate six Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures under a strict zero-leakage protocol for odontoid fracture detection, validating diagnostic reliability and anatomical focus using Explainable AI (XAI). A retrospective cohort of 540 cervical spine CT images from 96 patients was evaluated under a strict zero-leakage protocol. Data was partitioned at the patient level into three disjoint subsets: Training (60 patients, 326 images), Validation (16 patients, 92 images for early stopping), and an independent held-out Test set (20 patients, 122 images touched only once for final evaluation). Six CNN architectures were benchmarked. Statistical robustness was validated via patient-level bootstrapping ( N = 1000 iterations) with Holm-Bonferroni family-wise error rate correction, paired with Grad-CAM visual interpretability. On the untouched test cohort, DenseNet121, GoogLeNet, and ResNet18 achieved similar, leading discriminative performance with AUCs of 0.830 (95% CI: 0.718–0.933), 0.829 (95% CI: 0.714–0.929), and 0.829 (95% CI: 0.697–0.934), respectively, with DenseNet121 demonstrating a balanced diagnostic profile (Accuracy: 73.8%, Sensitivity: 73.0%, Specificity: 75.8%). In stark contrast, SqueezeNet 1.1 and VGG19 suffered complete collapse to majority-class prediction (Specificity: 0.0%) under the evaluated training configuration. Pairwise bootstrap hypothesis testing confirmed that DenseNet121 showed a borderline statistically significant difference over SqueezeNet 1.1 after multiple testing correction ( $$\:{p}_{\text{raw}}=0.0090$$ , Holm-adjusted $$\:p=0.0450$$ on $$\:n=20$$ patients), while differences among DenseNet121, GoogLeNet, and ResNet18 remained statistically non-significant ( $$\:{p}_{\text{adj}}=0.9840$$ ). Architectures incorporating deep feature reuse or residual connections exhibit robust generalization under strict patient-level isolation, whereas compact models and unregularized heavyweight architectures can struggle under small-sample constraints. Rigorous zero-leakage methodology and qualitative XAI assessment are essential prerequisites prior to clinical translation of spinal CAD models.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning estimates clinically significant prostate cancer risk in men with PSA 4–20 ng/mL
Article.Authors: Xie S.; Wang Q.; Wang X.; Jiang X.; Gao H.; Luo Y.; Fan L.; Li Q.; Wang H.; Cai X.; Zhou W.; Wu T.
Article.Abstract: Men with prostate-specific antigen (PSA) values of 4–20 ng/mL often have overlapping risks of benign disease, clinically insignificant prostate cancer, and clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). We retrospectively studied 859 men who underwent pathological evaluation; 76 had csPCa. Twelve prediction algorithms were assessed with 500 bootstrap resamples. In every resample, LASSO feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model fitting used only the bootstrap training sample, and performance was estimated from patient-level out-of-bag predictions. C5.0 had the highest AUROC point estimate (0.843, 95% CI 0.801–0.886), an AUPRC of 0.421, and a Brier score of 0.066. Calibration was broadly concordant at low-to-moderate predicted risks but uncertain in the sparse high-risk tail. At a 0.10 risk threshold, the model would avoid 544.8 biopsies per 1,000 men while missing 10.5 csPCa cases per 1,000. In an algorithm-matched comparison, the full C5.0 and clinical/PSA-only C5.0 models achieved AUROCs of 0.843 and 0.827, respectively (paired difference 0.0157, 95% CI − 0.0086 to 0.0395). The incremental benefit of additional blood-based predictors was therefore uncertain. C5.0 may support pre-biopsy triage, but multicenter external validation, recalibration assessment, and prospective impact studies are required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Analysis of stresses and displacements in two-layer inhomogeneous hollow cylinders using the complex potential method
Article.Authors: Youssri Y.; Abbasov Z.; Bouzettouta L.; Alhujaylan A.; Zennir K.
Article.Abstract: This study presents an exact analytical solution for the two-dimensional (2D) thermoelastic state of a long, two-layer hollow cylinder composed of inhomogeneous materials under mixed boundary conditions. By accounting for distinct thermoelastic properties and internal heat generation within layered structures, this research addresses a significant gap in the existing literature. The thermal field is determined by expressing the temperature function as a power series. Leveraging the classical and effective Kolosov–Muskhelishvili complex potential method, the thermoelastic problem is transformed into the complex domain. The inverse transformation back to the physical domain is performed analytically via exact Laurent series expansions, ensuring that a high degree of accuracy is fully preserved without any numerical approximation errors in the mapping process. To ensure high analytical precision, the particular solution for the resulting mixed boundary-value problem is sought in the form of a Laurent series of a complex variable. The surfaces of the layers are assumed to be either thermally insulated or maintained at zero temperature. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the internal stress field is significantly influenced by the intensity of the internal heat source. The derived formulas provide crucial insights into the distribution of thermal stresses and displacements in non-homogeneous layered structures. Given that these results pertain to complicated thermal loading conditions, they hold great significance for high-performance engineering applications. The scientific novelty lies in the first-ever implementation of the complex potential method to simultaneously account for material inhomogeneity and non-uniform heat sources acting at the contact interface of a 2D multilayered cylinder.

Article.Title: Associations among healthy lifestyle behaviors, healthy eating attitudes, picky eating, sustainable nutritional behaviors, and Mediterranean diet adherence: a path analysis
Article.Authors: Oruçoğlu B.; Onbaşı Ö.; Palamutoğlu M.
Article.Abstract: This study examined associations among healthy lifestyle behaviors, attitudes toward healthy eating, picky eating, sustainable nutritional behaviors, and Mediterranean diet (MD) adherence in a large adult sample. In this cross-sectional study, 1,631 adults aged 18 years and older in Türkiye completed validated self-report scales. Associations were tested using path analysis with observed composite scores. The primary model adjusted for gender, age, education, and income (entered as categorical, dummy-coded covariates) and used the healthy lifestyle behavior score with its nutrition component excluded to reduce construct overlap with sustainable nutritional behaviors. Indirect associations were evaluated with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples, and an alternative model reversing the sustainable nutrition–adherence path was also estimated. The final covariate-adjusted model showed good fit, χ²(2) = 1.575, p = 0.455, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.009, RMSEA = 0.000, 90% CI [0.000, 0.046], SRMR = 0.0022; because the model was close to saturated (df = 2), these indices indicate consistency with the data rather than strong confirmation of the hypothesized structure. Healthy lifestyle behaviors (β = 0.519), attitudes toward healthy eating (β = 0.196), and picky eating (β = 0.173) were positively associated with sustainable nutritional behaviors; sustainable nutritional behaviors showed a small positive association with MD adherence (β = 0.087), and attitudes toward healthy eating also showed an independent direct association with adherence (β = 0.176; all p < 0.001). Bias-corrected bootstrap indirect associations through sustainable nutritional behaviors were statistically significant but small (B = 0.003–0.005). The model explained approximately 46% of the variance in sustainable nutritional behaviors but only 8% of the variance in MD adherence. An alternative model reversing the sustainable nutrition–adherence path also fit the data well, and the small difference between models did not provide clear evidence regarding directional ordering, indicating that temporal ordering cannot be established from cross-sectional data. Healthy lifestyle behaviors, healthy eating attitudes, and picky eating were associated with sustainable nutritional behaviors, whereas associations with Mediterranean diet adherence were comparatively small. Given the cross-sectional design and the limited variance explained in adherence, the findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than as evidence of causal mediation or behavioral spillover.

Article.Title: Quality and engagement of rosacea-related short videos on Chinese platforms RedNote and TikTok: a cross-sectional analysis
Article.Authors: Han Y.; Li M.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rosacea is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease. This study aimed to evaluate the quality, characteristics, and user engagement of rosacea-related short videos on the Chinese platforms RedNote and TikTok, and to explore associations between engagement indicators and video quality. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted on Chinese-language rosacea-related videos retrieved from RedNote and TikTok on April 14, 2026. Video characteristics, user types, and engagement indicators (likes, favorites, comments, and shares) were recorded. Video quality was assessed using the modified development of a quality index for health information (mDISCERN), global quality score (GQS), and video information and quality index (VIQI). Spearman correlation analysis was performed to assess associations between engagement indicators and quality scores. A total of 366 videos were included (66 RedNote, 300 TikTok). TikTok had a higher proportion of videos uploaded by medical personnel and achieved higher mDISCERN, GQS and total VIQI scores than RedNote. Overall video quality on both platforms was medium to low. Large effect sizes in mDISCERN, GQS and total VIQI scores were observed between medical and non-medical uploaders. Four engagement indicators were strongly positively correlated with each other. Total VIQI score was strongly positively correlated with likes, favorites, shares, mDISCERN score, and GQS score, but moderately correlated with comments. Rosacea-related video quality on TikTok and RedNote was at a medium–low level. Medical uploaders produce higher-quality content, highlighting the need to promote evidence-based, professionally generated, and engaging rosacea content on short-video platforms.

Article.Title: Potential ecological risk from Cd and As in agricultural soils near wastewater sources and a landfill in the West Bank, Palestine
Article.Authors: Mlih R.; Hasan A.; Khaled L.; Bader H.; Najajrah M.; Qurie M.; Alfares H.; Ghanem M.; Bol R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acid-extractable concentrations of Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, As, Cd and Pb were measured by ICP-MS in 80 composite topsoil samples collected from five agricultural sites in the West Bank, Palestine, near wastewater sources or a landfill. Pollution indices calculated relative to continental-crust values differed among sites but are conditional on the partial extraction and selected background. Mean sample-level PLI classified ADJ (1.12), EQR (1.23) and DSN (1.33) as polluted. Cd had the highest I geo at ADJ (3.1), and Fe-normalized EF classified Cd at ADJ as extremely enriched. An Al-normalized sensitivity analysis preserved the principal Cd, As, Zn and Cr patterns but changed four of 35 site–metal EF classes. Mean RI was highest at ADJ (424.5; considerable screening risk), followed by DSN (150.7; at the low–moderate boundary); Cd contributed 93% and 73% of RI at these sites. A validated 5 × 4 self-organizing map produced four stable compositional clusters. Exploratory three-factor PMF identified Cr-rich soil-matrix, Cd–Zn-enriched mixed and Mn-dominant signatures, although residual over-dispersion, rotational ambiguity, weak reconstruction of Cu, Zn and Pb, and site dependence precluded quantitative source attribution. These screening results identify Cd, particularly at ADJ, as a priority for confirmatory monitoring. They do not establish total metal contents, bioavailability, food-chain exposure or unique pollution sources.

Article.Title: Metformin-loaded mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes modulate CD4+ T-cell subset frequencies in PBMCs from patients with RRMS in vitro
Article.Authors: Soltani Shirazi S.; Eskandari N.; Varshosaz J.; Fouladseresht H.; Asgari V.; Sullman M.; Adibi I.; Gharibi S.
Article.Abstract: Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) is marked by a profound imbalance within the CD​4+ T cell compartment, characterized by an increase in pro-inflammatory effector subsets and a concomitant reduction in regulatory T cells, which together sustain neuroinflammation and drive disease progression. Despite its promising immunomodulatory properties, the clinical translation of metformin for RRMS is limited by its rapid clearance and poor bioavailability. Exosomes secreted by mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) constitute a novel drug delivery system with intrinsic immunomodulatory properties and the capacity to enhance drug stability. This in vitro study evaluated the immunomodulatory effects of human adipose-derived MSC (hADMSC) exosomes loaded with metformin (Exo-Met) on the frequencies of CD4+ T cell subsets in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) isolated from patients with RRMS. PBMCs from patients with RRMS and healthy controls were treated with exosomes, metformin, Exo-Met, or IFN-β. Frequencies of IFN-γ​​+ CD4​​+ T, IL-17​​+ CD4+ T, and FoxP3​+ CD25+ CD4+ T cells were analyzed by flow cytometry at 24 and 72 h. At baseline, the frequencies of IFN-γ​+ CD4​+ T and IL-17+ CD4+ T cells were significantly higher in RRMS patients compared to healthy controls. Concomitantly, a lower frequency of FoxP3​+ CD25+ CD4​+ T cells was found in the patient group. Treatment with exosomes elicited a partial immunomodulatory effect on the frequencies of CD4+ T cell subsets. In contrast, metformin significantly reduced the frequency of IFN-γ​+ CD4+ T cells within 24 h and IL-17+ CD4+ T cells by 72 h, bringing both to levels comparable to those of healthy controls. Nevertheless, FoxP3​+ CD25+ CD4​+ T cell frequencies in the RRMS group remained significantly below healthy control levels even after 72 h. Compared with the single treatments, Exo-Met demonstrated enhanced, multifaceted immunomodulatory effects. It induced a rapid reduction of IL-17+ CD4+ T cells within 24 h and a significant decline in IFN-γ​+ CD4+ T cells by 72 h. Furthermore, Exo-Met rapidly enriched the FoxP3​+ CD25+ CD4+ T cells, bringing their frequencies toward levels comparable to healthy controls within 24 h. The results demonstrate that Exo-Met exerts a dual immunomodulatory effect in vitro in PBMCs from patients with RRMS, simultaneously reducing pathogenic pro-inflammatory CD4+ T cell subsets while promoting the regulatory subset, thereby representing a promising nanotherapeutic strategy that warrants further preclinical and clinical investigation.

Article.Title: Phase II randomized non-inferiority trial comparing the humoral immunogenicity of NDV-HXP-S and BNT162b2 vaccines in Brazil
Article.Authors: Peixoto de Miranda É.; de Sousa Moreira J.; Diaz R.; Brito C.; Borges M.; Leal F.; Russo L.; Boulos F.; dos Santos Almeida M.; da Rocha M.; Miyaji K.; França J.; de Lima M.; Ragiotto L.; Raghunandan R.; García-Sastre A.; Sun W.; Palese P.; Krammer F.; Silveira C.; Correia C.; Marmorato M.; Thomazella M.; Kallas E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) prompted an unprecedented global vaccine development response and accelerated regulatory pathways for clinical vaccine development. Despite the end of the public health emergency, sustained preparedness, including the availability of scalable and affordable vaccine platforms, remains essential. This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled and non-inferiority Phase II clinical trial, to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of a fifth-dose booster of NDV-HXP-S 10 µg, an egg-derived, inactivated COVID-19 vectored-vaccine virus using the Newcastle disease virus (NDV) expressing stabilized prefusion S protein from the Wuhan-Hu-1 strain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), versus BNT162b2 30 µg. Healthy participants aged 18–59 years ( n = 200) or ≥ 60 years ( n = 200) were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to receive a single intramuscular dose on Day 1. Primary immunogenicity endpoints (per-protocol) were the Day 29 geometric mean titer (GMT) ratio of the 50% neutralizing titer (NDV-HXP-S/BNT162b2) against SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1 and the difference in seroconversion proportions (≥ 4-fold rise if seropositive at baseline, or NT 50 > lower limit of quantification if seronegative). Non-inferiority margins were a point estimate ≥ 0.80 for GMT ratio, the lower bound of the one-tailed 97.5% confidence interval (CI) > 0.67 for GMT ratio, and a 97.5% CI lower bound > − 10% for seroconversion. Primary safety endpoints were vaccine-related solicited adverse events (AEs) through Day 7 and vaccine-related unsolicited AEs and serious adverse events (SAEs) through Day 28. Follow-up occurred for 12 and 6 months for safety and immunogenicity evaluation, respectively. Between February 28 and August 30, 2023, 389 eligible participants were included in the safety population. Of 389 participants, 263 (67.6%) were female, median age of 60.1 years (IQR, 40.8–65.4) and most were White, 218 (56.0%). Among the 311 (77.8%), the GMT ratio (NDV-HXP-S/BNT162b2) of neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 (Wuhan-Hu-1) was 0.50 (95% CI: 0.40‒0.60), measured on Day 29. The difference in seroconversion was − 36.7% (-45.3% to -28.0%). Vaccine-related solicited AEs occurred in 132 (67.3%) in NDV-HXP-S and 149 (77.2%) in BNT162b2 ( P = 0.032) within 7 days post-vaccination, while vaccine-related unsolicited AE occurred in 46 (23.5%) in NDV-HXP-S vs. 51 (26.4%) in BNT162b2 ( P = 0.558) within 28 days. There were no vaccine-related SAEs within 28 days post-vaccination. Inactivated NDV-HXP-S at 10 µg did not meet the criteria for non-inferiority in comparison to BNT162b2 at 30 µg in SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1 seroconversion and neutralization as a fifth-dose booster. Both vaccines were generally well tolerated during the observed follow-up. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier : NCT05354024 (Registration date: 2022-04-27).

Article.Title: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound combined with near-infrared as a biophysical modulator of macromolecular and protein homeostasis in sarcopenia
Article.Authors: Chang H.; Lee X.; Li C.; Liou J.
Article.Abstract: Sarcopenia is characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance, with preferential vulnerability of fast-twitch muscle fibers contributing to functional decline. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) and near-infrared photobiomodulation (NIR-PBMT) represent non-invasive biophysical approaches with potential to modulate skeletal muscle phenotype; however, their optimal stimulation parameters and effects on fast/slow muscle induction remain incompletely defined. In this study, C2C12 cells were used to optimize LIPUS and NIR stimulation conditions based on fast- and slow-twitch myosin heavy chain (MyHC) expression. LIPUS at ± 20 V and 2.5 MHz for 5 min produced the most favorable fast/slow MyHC response, while NIR irradiation at 740 nm for 35 s resulted in the highest fast/slow MyHC ratio among the tested optical conditions. These optimized parameters were subsequently evaluated in male Sprague–Dawley rats subjected to 14 days of hindlimb unloading (HU) to induce disuse-associated muscle atrophy, followed by 28 days of NIR, LIPUS, or combined NIR and LIPUS treatment. HU markedly impaired toe-lift capacity, spontaneous locomotor activity, and rotarod performance and reduced relative tibialis anterior muscle weight and the fast/slow MyHC ratio. Both NIR and LIPUS improved functional performance following HU, with LIPUS producing a particularly pronounced improvement in rotarod performance after 28 days of treatment. NIR produced the most prominent increase in the fast/slow MyHC protein ratio, particularly at day 14. Immunofluorescence analysis further demonstrated recovery of fast/slow muscle fiber distribution following NIR, LIPUS, and combined treatment, with ratios approaching control levels by day 28. In contrast, combined NIR and LIPUS treatment did not consistently provide greater functional benefits than either treatment alone, suggesting that independently optimized stimulation parameters may not produce additive effects when applied concurrently. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that parameter-optimized NIR and LIPUS can differentially modulate skeletal muscle function and fast/slow muscle characteristics following disuse-associated muscle atrophy, supporting their further investigation as complementary non-invasive strategies for conditions relevant to sarcopenia.

Article.Title: Comprehensive analysis of cellulosic bio waste Gmelina arborea bark particulates for its potential in bioactive composite materials
Article.Authors: Manikandaraja G.; Rathinavel S.; Mahakur V.; Santhosh A.
Article.Abstract: Plant-based filler materials are attractive for their biodegradability, sustainability, and suitability in developing biocomposites. In this study, unexplored biowaste Gmelina arborea bark particulates (GABP) were evaluated for their potential as a filler material in biocomposites. The compatibility of GABP was assessed through chemical, morphological, thermal, UV absorption, and bacterial resistance. The particulates were reduced to an average size of 1.09 μm by ball milling and consisted of 47.5% cellulose, 21.6% hemicellulose, and 24.2% lignin. Morphological analysis revealed irregular surfaces with pits can enhance interfacial adhesion in composite matrices. The thermogravimetric analysis demonstrated thermal stability up to 324 °C, while UV absorption indicated 87.5% UV-blocking efficiency. Additionally, GABP restricts significantly the Streptococcus pyogenes , Streptococcus oralis , Aeromonas hydrophila , and Escherichia coli pathogens at higher concentrations. These findings suggest that GABP is a sustainable filler material for biocomposites, particularly in biomedical and food packaging applications, where UV resistance, thermal stability, and antibacterial properties are essential.

Article.Title: A generalized model predictive fault-tolerant control strategy for hybrid multilevel converter under arbitrary open-circuit failures
Article.Authors: Fan Z.; Xing X.; Liu Y.; Zhang R.; Li Y.; Wang H.; Li X.; Blaabjerg F.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the fault-tolerant (FT) operation of the T-type converter using a cascaded H-bridge (T 2 C-HB) topology under open-circuit failures (OCF) occurring in any IGBT switch. The high number of switches in the hybrid multilevel converter (HMC) increases the possibility of switch faults. However, existing FT control methods for HMC primarily focus on local faults, making them ineffective in addressing global faults and thereby limiting overall system reliability. To achieve global FT control, this paper proposes an FT strategy based on model predictive control (FT-MPC), which consists of two stages. In the first stage, the optimal redundant voltage vector position is determined by employing an optimal current tracking strategy. In the second stage, an initialization function is introduced to integrate various types of OCF into a unified framework. By employing weighting factors within the selected redundant voltage vectors, the optimal switching states are determined. The proposed method effectively handles various types of OCF and is applicable to any HMC incorporating cascaded H-bridge modules. Simulation and experimental results validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

Article.Title: Spatial spillovers and causal configurations of the digital economy driving green manufacturing transformation in China
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Zhang T.; Shang M.
Article.Abstract: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored. Based on panel data from 31 provinces in China (2012–2023), this study constructs a dual-methodological framework integrating the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, transmission mechanisms, and causal recipes of this relationship. The empirical results reveal four key findings. First, green manufacturing transformation exhibits a steady upward trend but follows a distinct “East-High, West-Low” spatial gradient. Second, the digital economy exerts a significant positive impact on local green transformation and generates positive spatial spillovers to neighboring regions, though the spillover effect is weaker than the direct effect due to administrative barriers; technological innovation and environmental regulation are identified as two pivotal transmission channels. Third, a “Northeast Paradox” is observed: while the digital economy promotes green growth in most regions, it shows a significant negative interaction effect in the Northeast, attributed to the “lock-in effect” of rigid industrial structures. Fourth, fsQCA identifies four sufficient pathways leading to high green efficiency: “Digital-Talent Driven,” “Digital-Innovation Driven”, “Internal-Capability Driven”, and “Comprehensive Synergy”. Notably, a substitution effect exists between talent support and R&D intensity, offering flexible transformation strategies for resource-constrained regions. By moving beyond linear effect analysis, this study provides a multidimensional analytical roadmap to support the design of differentiated, context-sensitive green transformation policies.

Article.Authors: Friedmacher C.; Glushan A.; Wuenstel J.; Klaaßen-Mielke R.; Karimova K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In 2022, cardiovascular diseases accounted for 32.7% of all deaths in the EU, with associated costs of €282 billion annually. In Germany, coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of mortality and recent reductions in life expectancy gains have been attributed to excess CVD mortality. High rates of avoidable hospital admissions suggest shortcomings in ambulatory care. In 2004, Germany introduced the general practitioner-centred care (‘Hausarztzentrierte Versorgung” (HZV)) programme with the aim of strengthening primary care. This longitudinal observational cohort ( N = 125,758 in 2011, N = 169,101 in 2022) study based on German claims data describes the long-term effects of HZV on healthcare utilization and all-cause mortality for patients with CAD in observation period 2011–22. HZV participants had consistently lower odds of all-cause hospitalisation (OR 0.988, 95%CI, p < 0.001), CVD hospitalisation (OR 0.989, 95% CI, p < 0,001) and ambulatory care sensitive condition hospitalisation (OR 0.989, 95% CI, p < 0,001) in comparison to usual care. All-cause mortality reduced over the observation period and odds were significantly lower in the HZV group at the end of 2022 (OR 0.987, 95% CI, p < 0.001). These findings emphasise the role of structured, coordinated primary care in strengthening care for patients with CAD and support the broader implementation of GP-centred care models.

Article.Title: Proapoptotic RHG proteins and mitochondria are required for sensory dendrite pruning in Drosophila
Article.Authors: Mukherjee A.; Cheng R.; Sproston C.; Pop S.; Kondo S.; Williams D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Caspases are best known for their role in apoptosis, but they are also deployed sub-lethally during development, where they contribute to cell fate specification, migration and terminal differentiation. How neurons activate executioner caspases without dying remains unresolved. At the onset of Drosophila metamorphosis, neighbouring sensory neurons in the dorsal body wall adopt opposite fates: class III dendritic arborization (da) neurons die by apoptosis, while the class IV da neuron ddaC prunes its larval dendrites before regrowing an adult-specific arborization. Their proximity allows lethal and non-lethal caspase signalling to be compared side by side in an intact animal. Using SR4VH, a sensitive dual-colour executioner caspase probe, we show that caspase substrates are cleaved in ddaC within 20 min of puparium formation, well before the proximal dendrites are severed, and at consistently lower levels than in its dying neighbours. Single-cell H99 mutant clones reveal that the proapoptotic RHG proteins are cell-autonomously required for pruning. Although reaper, hid and grim are all transcribed in ddaC as remodelling begins, mutant combinations suggest that reaper and grim, rather than hid, cooperate to drive branch severing and clearance. In addition, disrupting mitochondrial function or transport depletes dendritic mitochondria, prevents caspase activation, and blocks both pruning in ddaC and apoptosis in neighbouring class III neurons. Taken together, our data show that Reaper and Grim are required cell-autonomously for pruning, and that mitochondria are required for both caspase activation and branch severing.

Article.Title: Bone transport induces CGRP release from sensory nerves to promote angiogenesis and heal diabetic foot wounds in rats
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Guo J.; Zhang J.; Xu Z.; Alimujiang A.; Ma C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a critical complication of diabetes, characterized by high recurrence rates, high disability rates, high mortality, and a significant socioeconomic burden. The tibial cortex transverse transport therapy, based on the tension-stress effect, has demonstrated significant efficacy in promoting the healing of DFUs; however, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Recent evidence show calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is important for tissue regeneration. However, its role in BT-mediated healing is still unknown. This study aimed to investigate whether and how sensory nerves participate in the process of BT-promoted DFU healing via the release of CGRP. A femoral BT model was established in diabetic rats, with concurrent creation of an ischemic and dorsal foot wound model on the ipsilateral hindlimb. Capsaicin was employed to ablate sensory nerves and block CGRP release. Animals were allocated into four groups: sham-operated group, external fixator group, BT group, and BT + capsaicin group. Wound healing rate, angiogenesis, and CGRP expression in the DRG and regenerated skin were assessed. Transcriptomic analysis was performed on healed skin tissue. In vitro, the effects of CGRP on tube formation ability, as well as on the expression of CD31, VEGFA, and FAK phosphorylation, were evaluated in HUVECs. The BT technique significantly promoted the healing of dorsal foot wounds in diabetic rats ( P < 0.05) and increased the count of newly formed blood vessels within the wounds ( P < 0.05). CGRP release from sensory nerve axons in the DRG and within the wounds was significantly increased ( P < 0.05). Following sensory nerve blockade by capsaicin, CGRP secretion decreased, and both angiogenesis and wound healing rates were significantly slowed ( P < 0.05). Transcriptome sequencing revealed that DEGs in the BT group were significantly enriched in the nervous system development and tube formation systems. In vitro experiments confirmed that CGRP promoted endothelial cell tube formation in a dose-dependent manner ( P < 0.05), upregulated the expression of angiogenesis-related proteins and genes such as CD31 and VEGFA, and promoted FAK phosphorylation ( P < 0.05). The bone transport technique promotes diabetic foot wound healing via a “nerve-vessel-regeneration” axis. CGRP secreted by sensory nerves mediates this process, potentially by enhancing angiogenesis through the CGRP-FAK-VEGF signaling axis.

Article.Title: A hybrid framework with uncertainty-aware cooperative fusion for robust spectrum sensing in beyond 5G cognitive radio networks
Article.Authors: Nanthaamornphong A.; Revathi V.; Kumar A.; Alohali M.; Masud M.; Saini A.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit–Long Short-Term Memory–Convolutional Neural Network (GRU–LSTM–CNN) deep learning framework designed to enhance Cooperative Spectrum Sensing (CSS) in Cognitive Radio (CR) networks. The proposed architecture combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for spatial–spectral feature extraction, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units for long-term temporal modeling, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layers for efficient short-term dependency learning. This integrated framework enables reliable detection of Primary User (PU) activity under challenging wireless environments. A reliability-aware fusion mechanism is incorporated, where each Secondary User (SU) transmits soft sensing reports containing PU-presence probability and predictive uncertainty. The key novelty is a sequential multiscale spatiotemporal representation in which CNN, LSTM, and GRU respectively learn localized spectral structure, long-term temporal dependencies, and short-term temporal variations, followed by uncertainty-aware reliability-weighted cooperative fusion. This mechanism allows the Fusion Center (FC) to assign adaptive reliability weights according to Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and confidence level. The system processes 256-QAM modulated Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signals transformed into time–frequency representations using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). For comparative purposes, an Orthogonal Time Space Modulation (OTSM) waveform is additionally used as a reference signaling scheme in the BER and PSD analyses (consistently denoted OTSM in Figs. 9, 10 and 11). The model is trained using a composite loss function combining Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE), Brier Score, and sparsity loss to improve detection accuracy, probability calibration, and communication efficiency. Simulation results over AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels show that the proposed GRU–LSTM–CNN framework achieves higher Probability of Detection (Pd), lower Probability of False Alarm, improved BER performance, and reduced Power Spectral Density (PSD) compared with conventional Energy Detection (ED), Matched Filter (MF), and existing deep learning models. The proposed model achieves Pd ≈ 1 at − 4 dB SNR and maintains strong robustness under 15–25% channel estimation error, confirming its suitability for next-generation CR and IoT communication systems.

Article.Title: USP54 regulates RIPK1 protein abundance via deubiquitination in acquired sorafenib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Sun C.; Huang Y.; Zou Y.; He Y.; Hua C.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ubiquitin-specific peptidase 54 (USP54) is a member of the deubiquitinating enzyme family and is involved in the regulation of protein deubiquitination. Deubiquitination plays a crucial role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but the relationship between USP54 and HCC remains unclear. This study demonstrates that USP54 is aberrantly overexpressed in hepatocellular carcinoma, with further elevated expression in sorafenib-resistant cell lines. USP54 knockdown significantly increased the sensitivity of HCC cells to sorafenib in vitro, while its potential to enhance sorafenib response in vivo was suggested by the reduced tumor growth observed during sorafenib treatment. In sorafenib-resistant cells, USP54 knockdown increased RIPK1 ubiquitination, supporting a role for USP54 in regulating RIPK1 deubiquitination. Moreover, RIPK1 knockdown attenuated sorafenib resistance even in USP54-overexpressing HCC cells. This indicates that USP54 may promote the deubiquitination of RIPK1, thereby stabilising RIPK1 and activating its downstream signalling pathways, thus facilitating sorafenib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma. These findings suggest an association between USP54 and the progression of HCC, as well as sorafenib resistance, thereby providing a potential novel target for addressing sorafenib resistance in HCC.

Article.Title: Subacute carbon monoxide exposure alters AgNOR number and area ratio in the cerebral cortex of rats
Article.Authors: Gencer T.; Ozbay S.; Dag S.; Ozsoy O.; Saritas A.; Kavalci C.; Kavalci G.; bedel C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We aimed to evaluate the effects of hypoxia induced by different levels of subacute carbon monoxide (CO) exposure on the total AgNOR area/total nuclear area (TAA/TNA) ratio and mean AgNOR number in rat cerebral cortical tissue. Eighteen Albino Wistar adult male rats were randomly divided into three groups (control as group A, 1000ppm and 3000ppm concentration of CO gas exposed as group B and C, respectively). CO gas was chronically given as 30 min a day during seven days. Statistically significant differences were found among the groups for both mean AgNOR number (χ2 = 12.051, p = 0.002) and TAA/TNA (χ2 = 12.316, p = 0.002), respectively. When the two groups are compared in terms of TAA/TNA ratio, statistically significant differences were detected between control and 1000ppm (Z = -2.882, p = 0.004), between control and 3000 ppm (Z = -2.882, p = 0.004) for TAA/TNA ratio. Statistically significant differences were found between control and 1000 ppm (Z = -2.882, p = 0.004), between control and 3000 ppm (Z = - 2.887, p = 0.004) for mean AgNOR number. It is important to determine new markers with high sensitivity and easy to apply in order to determine the effect of toxication in different organs and tissues (especially brain tissues) that are subacutely exposed to carbon monoxide intoxication. It seems that AgNOR may be used for this purpose.

Article.Title: Glucose–steatosis–fibrosis and glycemia–fibrosis scores in relation to mortality in NHANES 1999–2018
Article.Authors: Gu F.; Lin S.; Fu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glucose, hepatic steatosis, and fibrosis cluster across cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) stages, but the incremental contribution of steatosis to mortality stratification is uncertain. We analyzed 21,511 adults from NHANES 1999–2018 linked to mortality through 2019. Missing covariates were multiply imputed (m = 50), scores and modified operational CKM stages were passively rederived, and survey-weighted Cox models were pooled across imputations. During follow-up, 3,317 all-cause and 1,056 cardiovascular disease (CVD) deaths occurred. Each 1-point higher glucose–steatosis–fibrosis (GSF) score was associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.200, 95% CI 1.152–1.250) and CVD mortality (HR 1.273, 95% CI 1.197–1.355). However, steatosis was not independently associated with either outcome after conditioning on glycemia, fibrosis, and covariates. In the CKM common-complete internal benchmark, a simpler glycemia–fibrosis score performed at least as well as GSF for discrimination and Brier score. High versus low GSF corresponded to higher 10-year all-cause and CVD risks and shorter restricted mean survival. GSF therefore characterized population-level metabolic burden but did not demonstrate incremental predictive or clinical utility beyond glycemia and fibrosis.

Article.Title: RELAX: Reliability enhancement by limiting adverse eXertions
Article.Authors: Dhanakshirur R.; Selvam R.; Venkataramani R.; Murthy P.; Aladahalli C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate and well-calibrated confidence estimates are essential for the safe use of artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical imaging workflows, where overconfident errors can directly affect diagnostic decisions and patient outcomes. Conventional training objectives such as cross-entropy often encourage uniformly high confidence across all samples, leading to substantial miscalibration, particularly on rare pathologies, heterogeneous patient populations, and inherently ambiguous cases. Recent work addresses this by modifying loss functions to improve calibration, yet these approaches typically penalize errors equally across samples, including intrinsically difficult or noisy examples, which can contribute to suboptimal calibration. To address this limitation, we introduce the Perpetual Burden Score (PBS), a measure of sample difficulty derived from prediction instability observed during training. Building on PBS, we propose , a burden-aware optimization framework that down-weights chronically unstable (hard) samples during training, thereby reducing their influence on confidence formation. Across four medical imaging datasets spanning ophthalmology, histopathology, neuroimaging, and chest radiography, demonstrates overall improvements in calibration, while maintaining comparable diagnostic accuracy. For example, across 5 different architectural configurations on the ophthalmology dataset, on average, reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) by 2.38% and 11.72%, respectively, while the reduction in F1-score is observed at 0.86%. These findings suggest that incorporating prediction stability into the training process can improve the reliability of confidence estimates without additional inference-time cost. As an architecture-agnostic and lightweight framework, provides a practical approach for enhancing the trustworthiness of clinical AI systems.

Article.Title: Electromagneto-thermoelastic microelongated plate in the context of the dual phase lag model with gravity field
Article.Authors: Alarfaj K.
Article.Abstract: In this study, the electromagneto-thermoelastic behavior of a microelongated elastic plate subjected to gravitational effects is investigated within the framework of the dual-phase-lag (DPL) model. The governing equations are formulated based on the generalized theory of thermoelasticity with microelongation, incorporating the effects of an external electromagnetic field, gravity, and internal heat sources. The analysis is restricted to a two-dimensional configuration in the x–z plane, and the resulting coupled system is rendered dimensionless to facilitate numerical computation. By employing Lame’s potential method, the field equations are decoupled and solved using a normal mode technique. Analytical expressions for displacement components, temperature distribution, stress components, and microelongation are obtained. Numerical results are presented graphically to illustrate the influence of key physical parameters, including phase-lag times, gravity, electromagnetic field strength, wave number, and angular frequency. The results reveal that the dual-phase-lag effects and electromagnetic coupling significantly modify the propagation characteristics and attenuation behavior of thermoelastic waves, highlighting the importance of microstructural and multiphysics interactions in advanced elastic materials. These findings provide valuable insights for stress–strain analysis and the design of advanced engineering materials in thermoelastic applications.

Article.Title: Integrative animal model and pilot clinical study reveal the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of Modified Wumei Pill against intestinal inflammation
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Hu J.; Wang Z.; Shi L.; Shi R.; Liang C.; Yu Y.; Wang Y.; Lv C.; Lin Z.; Li Y.; Jiao Y.; Huang H.; Yang A.; Wang W.; Zhang H.; Liu Y.; Li J.; Mao T.
Article.Abstract: Modified Wumei Pill (MWP) is a Chinese herbal prescription that has shown significant efficacy in ulcerative colitis (UC) patients in our previous preliminary clinical observations. However, its molecular mechanism has not yet been elucidated. The in vivo efficacy of MWP was evaluated in a DSS-induced colitis mouse model. Network pharmacology was employed to determine the main bioactive compounds and key targets of MWP for the UC treatment, and the results were validated through in vitro naïve CD4 + T-cell differentiation experiments. Subsequently, a small sample, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy controlled trial was conducted to further clarify the therapeutic effect of MWP on UC, and relevant clinical samples, including serum and colon tissues, were used to further validate the mechanisms discovered in animal experiments. Our results showed that MWP markedly attenuated disease severity, colonic damage, and pro-inflammatory cytokines expression in DSS-induced colitis mice. Network pharmacology prediction indicated Th17 cell differentiation may represent a core pathway underlying MWP’s potential effects. This was confirmed by the results from flow cytometric analysis of lymphocyte phenotypes in the spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes showing a marked decrease in the percentage of Th17 cells in MWP-treated colitis mice. Mechanistically, the human-derived CD4 + T cell experiment showed that MWP suppressed Th17 differentiation, and this effect may be partially associated with glycolytic reprogramming. Our pilot clinical study further revealed the good clinical efficacy of MWP in treating patients with active UC, with a clinical response rate of 95.65%, remission rate of 52.17%, and endoscopic response rate of 95.65%, and mucosal healing rate of 43.48%. Furthermore, similar to the results of animal experiments, the levels of Th17 cell in PBMC and key glycolytic enzymes including Glut1, HK2, PKM2, and LDHA in UC patients were significantly reduced after 8 weeks of MWP treatment. In conclusion, orally administrated MWP alleviates intestinal inflammation and promotes mucosal healing, at least partially through inhibiting Th17 cell differentiation, and holds promise as a novel immune‐based therapy for UC treatment. This clinical trial is registered with http://www.chictr.org.cn , registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2200063465).

Article.Title: Experimental and numerical investigation of biomimetic Serpenoid geometry for deformation control and stiffness regulation in reinforced concrete frames
Article.Authors: Umashankar L.; Satyanarayanan K.; Parthasarathi N.
Article.Abstract: Biomimetic Serpenoid geometry is a curvature-based structural configuration inspired by the lateral undulation of snakes, in which continuous sinusoidal curvature enables deformation through geometric straightening and uncoiling. Such geometry provides a basis for developing structural elements that regulate deformation and load transfer through geometry-driven mechanisms. However, the application of Serpenoid geometry as an externally connected deformable component in reinforced concrete frames remains insufficiently investigated, particularly with respect to its influence on structural deformation, stiffness response, strain-energy behaviour, and load-transfer characteristics. The Serpenoid geometry was initially investigated at a winding angle of α = 30°, followed by a parametric finite-element investigation over the range of α = 5°–60°. A critical transition region was identified between α = 35° and 40°, and the α = 36° configuration was subsequently selected for frame-level investigation. The selected Serpenoid configuration was fabricated using Fe550D reinforcement and externally integrated with an M30 reinforced concrete frame having overall dimensions of 600 mm × 1090 mm. Numerical and experimental investigations were subsequently performed on conventional bare and Serpenoid-integrated RC frames. At a common numerical load of 20 kN, the vertical deformation and strain-energy responses of the two configurations differed by only 0.225% and 0.159%, respectively. Experimentally, at a common load level of 8 kN, the Serpenoid-integrated frame exhibited a 13.21% reduction in vertical deformation compared with the bare frame, while the experimentally calculated energy absorption was 5.51% lower. The Serpenoid-integrated frame also exhibited a 120.6% increase in horizontal deformation capacity, higher absolute secant stiffness over the investigated load range, and a more distributed crack-development pattern. The results indicate that the proposed Serpenoid configuration primarily contributes to deformation control, stiffness regulation, and increased lateral deformation capacity rather than an increase in global energy absorption within the investigated experimental loading range.

Article.Title: Early albumin infusion is associated with lower mortality in patients with sepsis and concurrent heart failure: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Chen A.; Gu L.; Zhang L.; Shi Y.; Liu Y.; Cai X.; Xie L.
Article.Abstract: We retrospectively examined the association between albumin administration during the first 24 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and all-cause mortality in patients with sepsis and concurrent heart failure (HF) using MIMIC-IV version 3.1. The cohort included 4063 adults, of whom 432 were in the early-albumin group and 3631 were in the control group. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality after ICU admission; secondary mortality endpoints were 90- and 365-day all-cause mortality. The primary analysis used multivariable Cox proportional-hazards models in the full cohort, with analyses in the fixed propensity-score-matched cohort providing supportive evidence. In the full cohort, early albumin administration was associated with lower all-cause mortality at 28 days (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55–​0.85; P < 0.001), 90 days (adjusted HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59–0.86; P < 0.001), and 365 days (adjusted HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59–0.82; P < 0.001). Directionally consistent associations were observed in the matched Cox models. Early albumin administration was not associated with lower documented volumes of major isotonic crystalloids (0.9% saline plus lactated Ringer’s) during the first 48 h after ICU admission. In this retrospective cohort, early albumin administration during the first 24 h after ICU admission was associated with lower 28-, 90-, and 365-day all-cause mortality, but not with lower documented major isotonic crystalloid administration. These findings are observational and do not establish causality.

Article.Title: Cryopreservation of human hair follicles for organ culture
Article.Authors: Hamano S.; Sun T.; Nishino M.; Kageyama T.; Nanmo A.; Seo J.; Fukuda J.
Article.Abstract: Extracted human hair follicles are critically useful specimens for various purposes, ranging from basic research, such as skin and hair follicle biology, to applications, including hair drug testing and cell sources for regenerative medicine. The ability to cryopreserve hair follicles enables their use in large quantities at any desired time. This study investigated the feasibility of human hair follicles after cryopreservation using two approaches: slow freezing and vitrification. Slow freezing resulted in severe cell death and loss of hair shaft elongation in subsequent organ culture. Vitrification resulted in less cell death than slow freezing and approximately 75% hair shaft elongation relative to fresh hair follicles. Interestingly, vitrification induced a transition of the hair cycle from the anagen to catagen phase, which is a typical undesirable change in patients with alopecia. This transition was partially suppressed by minoxidil treatment in organ culture. These results suggest that, under the conditions tested, the vitrification protocol (15% DMSO and 15% EG with rapid cooling in liquid nitrogen) preserves human hair follicles substantially better than the slow freezing protocol (10% DMSO with cooling at 1 °C/min), and vitrification may provide beneficial hair follicle samples for testing hair drugs to alleviate the transition to the catagen phase.

Article.Title: Investigate the varying ratios of different PCM types on uniform characteristics produced with polyester double-woven fabric
Article.Authors: Seddik K.; Ali M.; Abd El-Aziz M.; Yahia S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phase Change Materials (PCMs) offer promising thermoregulation for functional uniforms, but optimal integration strategies balancing performance and cost remain unclear. This study systematically investigates how PCM type and blending ratio affect polyester double-woven fabric properties for uniform applications. We manufactured 12 fabric samples varying: (1) PCM type (polyester-based vs. viscose-based), (2) blending ratios (25%, 50%, 75% PCM content), and (3) carrier yarn (microfiber vs. Renova®). Comprehensive characterization included mechanical testing (tensile strength, stiffness), thermal analysis (DSC, thermal conductivity), comfort evaluation (air/water permeability, moisture management), and protective performance (UPF, electrostatic charge). Statistical significance was validated via two-way ANOVA (95% confidence, P ≤ 0.05), including interaction effects, and multi-criteria radar chart optimization. Results demonstrate that viscose-based PCMs significantly outperformed polyester-based alternatives, achieving 33% higher thermal storage capacity (46.86 J/m 2 vs. 35.20 J/m 2 at 75:25 blending ratio), 65–100% reduction in electrostatic charge (viscose-based: 0–0.013 kV vs. polyester-based: 0.003–0.037 kV), and superior hydrophilic properties enhancing moisture management. Critically, the 50% PCM: 50% Polyester Microfiber blending ratio (with viscose-based PCM) emerged as the optimal composition, maximizing thermal regulation, while maintaining mechanical and achieving excellent UV protection (UPF > 50+). ANOVA confirmed statistically significant main effects for 12/14 parameters ( P ≤ 0.05) and revealed critical interaction effects (Weft Material Type × Blending Ratio) for mechanical, comfort, and protective properties, whereas thermal storage capacity responded independently to these factors. These findings provide actionable design guidelines for material-efficient production of high-performance uniform fabrics, demonstrating that strategic PCM selection and a 50% blending ratio can simultaneously enhance thermal comfort, reduce static-related safety hazards, and maintain protective functionality while optimizing the proportion of functional PCM yarns—directly addressing conflicting requirements in professional workwear applications across industrial, medical, and service sectors.

Article.Title: Risk-sensitive safe reinforcement learning for joint cyber insurance and cybersecurity investment planning in cyber-physical power systems
Article.Authors: Alhazmi M.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cyber insurance and cybersecurity investment are tightly coupled in smart grids because cyberattacks can produce physical outages, financial losses, regulatory exposure, and insurance claims through the same operating event. This study develops a risk-sensitive safe reinforcement learning framework for joint cyber insurance and defense investment planning in cyber-physical power systems. The formulation treats the utility as a sequential decision maker that observes physical grid states, cyber exposure, insurance contract status, posterior threat beliefs, and budget conditions, and then selects coverage, deductible, hardening, monitoring, redundancy, backup-control, and incident-response actions. The framework combines a constrained Markov decision process, conditional value-at-risk loss control, an optimal power flow (OPF) safety shield, and a Benders-style decomposition between long-term policy learning and short-term security correction. The mathematical presentation separates model-specific cyber-physical-insurance equations from standard reinforcement-learning components, so that the novel coupling among insurance, defense, physical feasibility, and tail-risk control remains explicit. A simulation benchmark on IEEE test systems evaluates expected cost, 95% CVaR, physical-security violations, shield corrections, policy sensitivity, and belief-update degradation. Under the extreme-threat case, the safe-RL policy reduces 95% CVaR from 130.63 MUSD under the no-insurance stress case to 68.21 MUSD, lowers total cost from 36.8 MUSD to 17.1 MUSD, and reduces total security violations to four events per 1000 evaluation episodes. Across five random seeds, the total-cost and tail-risk results remain stable, with a mean total cost of 17.16 MUSD and a mean extreme-threat CVaR of 68.34 MUSD. The results show that cyber insurance is most effective when premiums are priced from verified defense posture and coordinated with physical safety constraints rather than treated as a substitute for cybersecurity investment.

Article.Title: Evidence-grounded AI risk event representation for listed-company credit risk early warning: a multi-source RAG and reliability-gated fusion approach
Article.Authors: Cheng Y.
Article.Abstract: AI-related corporate narratives may describe substantively different events, including operational adoption, product commercialization, investment expansion, speculative promotion, implementation failure, and regulatory concern. These heterogeneous narratives may therefore have different predictive associations with future corporate credit risk. Existing text-enhanced models mainly rely on sentiment, keywords, or document-level embeddings, which may fail to distinguish substantive AI adoption from speculative disclosure, implementation failure, or regulatory concern. This study proposes an evidence-grounded AI risk event framework for listed-company credit risk prediction. The framework constructs firm-year evidence libraries from AI-related news, corporate announcements, annual-report management discussion and analysis, investor-interaction texts, financial indicators, and macroeconomic variables. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module retrieves firm-specific evidence, and a large language model (LLM) converts retrieved evidence into structured AI risk events. A temporal reliability-gated fusion network subsequently integrates financial fundamentals, macroeconomic conditions, event-level AI semantics, source availability, extraction confidence, and cross-source consistency. Using 31,320 firm-year observations of Chinese listed companies from 2008 to 2017, the proposed model achieves an RMSE of 4.665 natural distance-to-default units, an MAE of 2.919, an \(\:{R}^{2}\) of 0.423, a standard-deviation-normalized RMSE of 0.760, and a high-risk AUC of 0.791 under walk-forward validation. The incremental improvement over the strongest component-level comparator using the same RAG event vectors and an FT-Transformer is smaller than the improvement produced by event-level representation itself: the paired firm-block bootstrap yields a mean squared-loss difference of 0.81 with a 95% confidence interval of [0.03, 1.68] and \(\:p=0.044\) . Predictive discrimination is also heterogeneous with respect to evidence availability, with AUCs of 0.817 and 0.748 for held-out observations with and without a valid AI event, respectively. An independent evaluation of 240 firm-year evidence libraries containing 2,684 manually identified relevant passages yields a Precision@8 of 0.842, Recall@8 of 0.781, nDCG@8 of 0.861, and firm-year event recall of 0.836. Ablation, robustness, and parameter-sensitivity tests confirm the value of evidence retrieval, event-level representation, source consistency, temporal attention, and reliability gating. Later-period, alternative-taxonomy, source-removal, temporal-knowledge, and firm-block bootstrap analyses further support the stability of the findings. The results indicate that traceable event-level representations of AI-related texts provide incremental predictive information in the studied historical sample. Most of the observed gain relative to structured and conventional text representations is attributable to evidence-grounded event construction, whereas reliability-conditioned temporal fusion provides a smaller additional improvement. These findings represent predictive associations rather than causal effects of corporate AI narratives on credit risk.

Article.Title: Energy-efficient and QoS-aware clustering routing framework using improved sharpbelly fish optimization and adaptive regularized routing optimization for WSNs
Article.Authors: Banu D.; Sivamani C.; Rani S.; Suriyakrishnaan K.
Article.Abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) face persistent challenges in maintaining energy efficiency, balanced resource utilization, and reliable data transmission as network density increases. Existing clustering and routing approaches generally address these requirements independently, resulting in inadequate coordination among cluster-head selection, node grouping, routing, and cooperative resource allocation. To address this research gap, this study proposes an integrated Energy-Efficient and QoS-Aware Clustering Routing Framework that jointly optimizes these network operations. The framework employs the Improved Sharpbelly Fish Optimization Algorithm (ISFOA) for cluster-head selection by considering residual energy, node density, communication distance, and trust characteristics. Hyperbolic Fuzzy C-Means with Adaptive Weight-based Filtering (Hyper-FCM) is subsequently employed to establish robust and adaptive clusters while reducing the influence of uncertain or unreliable node information. The Adaptive Regularized Routing Optimization Algorithm (ARROA) determines energy-efficient multi-hop routes by balancing routing load, residual energy, and end-to-end delay. In addition, the Shapley-driven N-Agent Teamwork (SNAT) framework promotes cooperative resource utilization and balanced participation among sensor nodes. MATLAB-based simulations were conducted for network sizes ranging from 100 to 500 nodes. In the densely populated 500-node scenario, the proposed framework achieved 16.0 mJ energy consumption, 97.5% packet delivery ratio, and 0.915 Mbps throughput, demonstrating controlled performance degradation with increasing network density. The results indicate that the integrated optimization of clustering, routing, and cooperative decision-making improves energy utilization and QoS while supporting scalable and reliable WSN operation.

Article.Title: Integrating climate change into pattern-based modelling of agricultural and forest land dynamics in Romania
Article.Authors: Kucsicsa G.; Sima M.; Bîrsan M.; Urșanu E.; Bălteanu D.
Article.Abstract: Climate change is increasingly reshaping land-use/land-cover dynamics worldwide, yet the magnitude and spatial distribution of these changes remain insufficiently understood at the regional scale. This study assesses the potential impact of near-future climatic conditions on agricultural and forest lands in Romania, by integrating three climate projections, namely SSP1–2.6 , SSP3–7.0 , and SSP5–8.5 , into a spatially explicit land-use pattern-based modelling framework, i.e., CLUE-s model ( the Conversion of Land Use and its Effects at Small regional extent ). To isolate the climatic signal, non-climatic drivers were held constant across scenarios, while changes in temperature and precipitation were introduced as the only dynamic inputs. The results indicate a generally high persistence of agricultural and forest classes, suggesting limited overall spatial reorganization up to 2050. However, several agricultural and forest classes exhibit localized shifts and transition hotspots, particularly in mountain regions, indicating increased sensitivity to changing climatic conditions. Across scenarios, temperature appears to exert a more consistent influence than precipitation on the projected spatial redistribution of these land systems. These findings highlight the need for regionally adaptive land-management strategies to support climate-resilient agricultural and forestry sectors.
