Article.Title: The impact of the digital economy on agricultural green development and spatial spillover effects
Article.Authors: Yao S.; Wang L.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: The transition toward greener agricultural production increasingly depends on the effective integration of digital technologies into rural production and service systems. Using a balanced panel covering 30 provincial-level regions in China from 2013 to 2024, this study evaluates the relationship between digital-economy development and agricultural green development (AGD). The two multidimensional indices are calculated through the entropy-weighting method. The empirical analysis proceeds through province and year fixed effects, a mediation framework, threshold estimation, and a spatial Durbin specification. The results show that higher digital-economy development is associated with a significant improvement in AGD. Agricultural technology innovation constitutes a transmission channel and accounts for 12.67% of the estimated effect. The relationship is also conditional on rural human capital: after rural human capital crosses the estimated threshold, the positive association becomes noticeably stronger. Regional estimates reveal substantial heterogeneity, with the eastern provinces exhibiting a larger effect than the central and western regions. Spatial decomposition further indicates that the influence of digital development extends beyond provincial boundaries, and the estimated spillover effect is greater than the within-province direct effect. Taken together, the findings suggest that digital transformation in agriculture depends not only on technological infrastructure but also on local absorptive capacity and cross-regional linkages. The results therefore highlight the importance of strengthening rural human capital, agricultural technology diffusion, and interregional cooperation in the process of agricultural green transformation.

Article.Title: Distribution and development characteristics of loess seismic landslides induced by the 1622 M 7 earthquake in Northern Guyuan, Northwest China
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Zhang Z.; Li P.; Chang C.; Han X.; Lei Q.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Coseismic loess landslides induced by historical strong earthquakes represent the predominant seismogeological hazard across the Loess Plateau, and a thorough inventory of their distribution and kinematic behavior is fundamental to regional seismic hazard evaluation and to the mechanistic understanding of loess seismic disasters. Although well-studied events such as the 1654 Tianshui M 8 and 1920 Haiyuan M 8½ earthquakes have received systematic investigation, the coseismic loess landslides triggered by the 1622M 7 earthquake have long been confined to brief entries in historical catalogs, with no clear understanding of their spatial distribution, controlling factors, or kinematic characteristics. To address this gap, we combined high-resolution remote sensing interpretation with field verification to identify 322 coseismic loess landslides and compile the first comprehensive inventory for this event. We analyzed the relationships between landslide distribution and seismic intensity, fault distance, seismic wave propagation direction, and loess ridge orientation, and we summarized the topographic conditions and geometric parameters governing landslide development. The results show that: (1) Landslides mainly occur in seismic intensity zones VIII and IX and form a dense NNW-trending belt along the southern segment of the Yantongshan Fault, concentrated on the fault hanging wall with sliding directions nearly orthogonal to both fault strike and loess ridge orientation; their distribution is jointly controlled by ground-motion intensity, fault geometry, topography, and seismic wave propagation direction. (2) Source slopes exhibit a typical loess–mudstone dual structure with a three-segment vertical profile; landslides preferentially develop on loess slopes 30–50 m high with original angles of 20–30° and free-face angles of 40–50°. (3) Landslides are dominated by small-to-medium sizes and show typical peeling-type failure along the loess–mudstone interface, with landslide angles mostly 10–20° and weathered scarp angles of 24–30°. (4) The dominant runout distance is 30–60 m, and the equivalent friction coefficient (μ) follows a normal distribution peaking at 0.25–0.30, indicating moderate-to-low friction and medium-to-short runout behavior; μ displays significant negative power-law correlations with volume (V) and runout distance (LR), revealing that larger landslides have lower friction and longer travel distances. (5) The inventory confirms that the southern Yantongshan Fault is a Holocene active fault, and the coseismic rupture length estimated from landslide distribution is 40–50 km, yielding a magnitude consistent with historical records. These findings fill a major gap in the study of historical earthquake-induced loess landslides in southern Ningxia and provide important theoretical and practical value for improving the historical loess seismic landslide database of the Loess Plateau, assessing fault activity, and analyzing regional seismic hazard.

Article.Title: Contrast sensitivity, binocular function, and higher-order aberrations after conventional and topography-guided PRK following penetrating keratoplasty
Article.Authors: Kijonka M.; Nowińska A.; Wylęgała A.; Dugiełło B.; Walasz K.; Stec-Pachcińska M.; Wylęgała E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Residual refractive error and corneal optical irregularity may impair functional vision after penetrating keratoplasty (PK). We prospectively compared functional and optical outcomes after conventional photorefractive keratectomy (C-PRK) and topography-guided PRK (TG-PRK) in 42 eyes with previous PK. Twenty eyes underwent C-PRK and 22 underwent TG-PRK. At 12 months, contrast sensitivity increased in both groups, with a greater unadjusted improvement after TG-PRK (mean change, + 0.368 vs. +0.113 log CS; P = 0.006). Total higher-order aberration root mean square increased after C-PRK (+ 0.924 μm) and decreased after TG-PRK (− 0.389 μm; P < 0.001 for the between-group difference). Changes in higher-order aberrations were not significantly correlated with changes in contrast sensitivity in either group. In multivariable analysis adjusted for baseline contrast sensitivity, spherical equivalent, and anisometropia, treatment group was not independently associated with 12-month contrast sensitivity ( P = 0.060). Both procedures were associated with improvements in visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, whereas TG-PRK was additionally associated with a reduction in higher-order aberrations. The functional benefit of TG-PRK should be interpreted cautiously because treatment allocation was non-randomized and baseline refractive characteristics differed between groups.

Article.Title: Vehicle trajectory prediction with temporal–channel attention and GRU
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate vehicle trajectory prediction is crucial for autonomous driving systems, as it provides essential inputs for downstream tasks such as behavior planning and motion control. In complex traffic environments, a vehicle’s future motion depends not only on its own historical dynamics but also on interactions with surrounding vehicles, resulting in strong spatiotemporal dependencies. Although recent deep learning approaches have achieved promising performance, many existing methods focus primarily on modeling temporal sequences or spatial interactions, while insufficiently considering the heterogeneous importance of different feature channels in vehicle motion data. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a vehicle trajectory prediction framework that jointly models temporal dependencies and feature-channel relationships through a dual-attention architecture. Specifically, a temporal attention module is designed to capture long-range temporal dependencies in motion sequences, while a channel attention module learns adaptive importance weights for heterogeneous feature channels. A gated fusion mechanism is further introduced to integrate the complementary representations from the two branches. Based on the fused representation, a GRU-based decoder generates multi-step future trajectory predictions. The proposed model takes as input the motion history of a target vehicle and its six surrounding vehicle classes, and predicts trajectories over a 5 s prediction horizon using 3 s historical observations. Extensive experiments on the HighD and NGSIM datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms several representative baseline methods across different prediction horizons, achieving average RMSE values of 0.78 m and 1.36 m, respectively. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the temporal attention module, channel attention mechanism, and gated fusion strategy. Overall, the proposed approach provides an effective solution for capturing both temporal dynamics and feature interactions in vehicle motion data, enabling more accurate and robust trajectory prediction in complex traffic environments.

Article.Title: VISTA with subepithelial connective tissue autograft versus fascia lata allograft for multiple gingival recessions: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Hatab E.; Hazzaa H.; Elgendy E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The purpose of this study was to evaluate the clinical and aesthetic results of the use of vestibular incision subperiosteal tunnel access (VISTA) with subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG) and fascia lata allograft in the treatment of gingival recession in the Cairo RT1 classification. Twenty-six healthy patients with gingival recession were randomly allocated to two groups: Group I (VISTA + SCTG) and Group II (VISTA + double-layer FLA). The clinical measurements that were recorded at baseline, 3, and 6 months after treatment were gingival recession depth (GRD), gingival recession width (GRW), gingival thickness (GT), mean root coverage (MRC), and complete root coverage (CRC). Significant improvements were observed in all clinical parameters in both groups ( p < 0.05). Even though the FLA group achieved comparable results and experienced less patient distress, the SCTG group achieved a greater mean root coverage. In addition, the gingival thickness of the FLA group was greater than that of the SCTG group. Article.Title: Generative decision intelligence: leveraging large language models for autonomous multi-objective resource orchestration in dynamic cloud environments
Article.Authors: Vakilifard M.; Sahafi A.; Broumandnia A.
Article.Abstract: With the expansion of hyperscale datacenters, optimal resource allocation (RA) requires simultaneously balancing conflicting objectives: resource utilization, cloud service provider (CSP) net profit, customer satisfaction (QoS), scheduling latency, and load balancing across physical machines. Traditional meta-heuristics encounter superlinear computational bottlenecks under high workload volumes, while numerical machine learning models lack semantic awareness to interpret high-level Service Level Agreements (SLAs) or adapt to runtime workload shifts. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a Generative Decision Intelligence (GDI) framework based on a dual-layer neuro-symbolic architecture. The Strategic Reasoning Layer employs a Large Language Model (LLM) that translates natural-language SLAs and runtime telemetry into dynamic fuzzy logic boundaries and objective trade-off weights. These parameters configure the Tactical Execution Layer, which comprises high-speed machine learning models (Random Forest, Deep Neural Networks) and adaptive fuzzy inference systems that assign tasks in real time while tracking resource releases upon task completion. Extensive experiments on 1,000 physical machines processing 100,000 dynamic requests from Google Cluster Workload Traces show that GDI achieves a 97.1% request acceptance rate, 81.5% average infrastructure utilization, and reduces load standard deviation to 7.5. An ablation study demonstrates that LLM-guided rule distillation yields an independent 3.7% acceptance gain and 20.2% lower load variance over static expert rules. Model inference runs in O (1) time, yielding an overall per-request allocation complexity of O ( N ) across N physical machines.

Article.Title: Reachability judgments in upper-limb segmentary exclusion syndrome explore action-related aspects of peripersonal space
Article.Authors: Herbé P.; Birck M.; Touillet A.; Pierret J.; Jarrassé N.; Paysant J.; Ceyte H.
Article.Abstract: Peripersonal space (PPS) refers to the multisensory representation of the space surrounding the body and is shaped by motor experience and body representation. Upper limb segmentary exclusion syndrome (UL-SES) is characterized by persistent underuse of a limb segment without identifiable neurological lesion and is associated with altered body perception. We investigated action-related aspects of PPS in UL-SES using a previously validated reachability-judgment task. Fifteen participants with UL-SES and 30 healthy participants completed a task comparing perceived maximum reachable distance with objective maximum reachable distance. Body representation disturbances were assessed using the Bath CRPS Body Perception Disturbance Scale (BATH). Contrary to our hypothesis, Reachability judgments did not differ between the affected and unaffected sides in UL-SES participants, and no significant group difference was observed between UL-SES and healthy participants. In healthy participants, reachability overestimation was greater on the dominant than on the non-dominant side, whereas no dominance effect was observed in UL-SES participants. Higher BATH scores were associated with lower signed RJ-error, i.e. reduced overestimation of reachable space, on the affected side. These findings provide no evidence for major alterations in reachability judgments associated with limb exclusion, while suggesting that body representation influences the estimation of action possibilities in individuals with UL-SES.

Article.Title: Model-free observer-based voltage control of non-holonomic mobile robot using reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Khodamipour G.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a trajectory tracking control strategy for non-holonomic mobile robots with unavailable orientation angle measurements. An observer is developed to reconstruct the trigonometric terms required by the controller, while the Fourier-series-based reinforcement learning scheme performs online estimation of unknown nonlinear terms, and the controller compensates for bounded external disturbances. The nonlinear system is transformed into lower dimensional subsystems, and controller design is simplified using a virtual auxiliary error function. A dynamic model of the mobile robot driven by permanent-magnet DC motors is considered, where the controller generates the required motor voltage signals. By integrating reinforcement learning with Fourier-series expansion, a model-free control scheme is introduced that achieves accurate trajectory tracking with fewer tuning parameters and lower computational cost than the considered neural-network-based benchmark. The stability of the observer and controller is theoretically analyzed through separate Lyapunov-based analyses. Simulation results demonstrate improved tracking performance, smoother control signals, competitive control effort, and computational efficiency compared with neural-network-based and robust voltage controllers.

Article.Title: Predicting short-term mortality in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: an explainable machine learning model with a web-based prototype
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ren G.; Ou Y.; Guo X.; Li Z.; Tan X.; Chen H.; Song Y.; Dong L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) is associated with prognosis in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (S-AKI). However, its nonlinear relationship with mortality and its optimal integration into multivariable prediction models remain unclear. Machine learning (ML) methodologies, capable of capturing nonlinear relationships among variables, hold promise for enhancing the accuracy of short-term mortality risk prediction. This study included 773 critically ill S-AKI patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Key predictors were selected from 25 candidate variables using LASSO regression. A panel of candidate machine learning algorithms was evaluated for predicting 28-day all-cause mortality after LASSO-based feature selection; the final model was selected on test-set performance. Model performance was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow test, Brier score), and decision curve analysis (DCA). The final model was interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and deployed as a web-based prototype. The logistic regression model was selected as the final model and achieved the highest test-set AUC (0.765, 95% CI: 0.706–0.824) among all candidate algorithms, retaining nine predictors identified by LASSO regression. SHAP analysis identified SOFA_CRRT and serum creatinine as the most important predictors, with GNRI ranking seventh and showing a pronounced nonlinear association with mortality; risk increased sharply when GNRI was below 75, whereas a protective association was observed above 90. Decision curve analysis indicated net clinical benefit across a threshold probability range of 0.1 to 0.6. Calibration was suboptimal (Hosmer–Lemeshow test p = 0.004), which we acknowledge as a limitation. The model was deployed as a publicly accessible web-based prototype ( https://freergq.shinyapps.io/GNRISHAP_Model/ ) for research-use risk assessment. The interpretable model predicts 28-day mortality and identifies a GNRI threshold (< 75) associated with elevated risk. The web-based prototype supports research-use risk assessment; prospective external validation is required before any clinical application.

Article.Title: Demand aware optimization of hybrid energy storage systems for renewable electric vehicle charging stations under variable electricity demand
Article.Authors: Gamil M.; Masrur H.; Alobaidi A.; Senjyu T.; Elkholy M.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a demand-aware optimization framework for a renewable-powered electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) using a hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) comprising solar photovoltaic generation, wind power, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and hydrogen energy storage systems (HESS). The IbI Logics Optimization Algorithm (ILA) is employed to determine the optimal system configuration under varying charging demand conditions. To capture realistic charging behavior, three demand scenarios are developed considering variations in fleet size, charging intensity, and temporal clustering of EV arrivals. Although the peak demand remains nearly constant at 930 kW across all scenarios, annual electricity demand varies by 19.28% due to differences in demand distribution and vehicle penetration levels. Results reveal that temporal demand characteristics strongly influence storage allocation and system economics. Hydrogen storage capacity varies by 36.74% across scenarios, highlighting its role in long-duration energy balancing, whereas battery storage capacity changes by less than 9%. In contrast, battery discharge power varies by more than 40%, demonstrating its critical role in mitigating clustered charging peaks. Comparative evaluation over 30 independent runs against the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) demonstrates the consistently superior economic performance of ILA, achieving average reductions in mean NPC of approximately 4.66% relative to GA and 4.10% relative to PSO across the three demand scenarios.

Article.Title: Fibonacci quasiperiodic structures for enhanced polar magneto-optical Kerr response
Article.Authors: Naghizadeh N.; Fallahi V.; Fazli P.; Aghbolaghi R.
Article.Abstract: The polar magneto-optical Kerr effect (PMOKE) is a key mechanism for optical readout, but conventional materials respond only weakly. Magnetophotonic crystals enhance the PMOKE via interference-driven light confinement, yet Fibonacci designs remain largely unexplored in the polar geometry and insufficiently benchmarked against other orderings. Using a 4 \(\times\) 4 transfer-matrix formalism, we calculate the Kerr rotation, reflectance, and their product, the figure of merit (FOM), for one-dimensional Fibonacci magnetophotonic quasiperiodic structures of cobalt (Co) and silicon nitride (SiN) layers as functions of Co thickness, wavelength, generation order (up to the eighth), and incidence angle. Fibonacci ordering yields Kerr enhancement at specific Co thicknesses, attributed to interference-driven field localization within the Co layers, and the enhancement remains robust for incidence angles up to about \(20^\circ\) . With increasing generation order, the Kerr rotation decreases, but the reflectance rises proportionally more, so the FOM generally increases. A comparison of the 8th-generation structure with all 1287 possible arrangements of the same length and composition shows that the strongest responses come from sequences whose local ordering is closest to the Fibonacci pattern, indicating that the specific correlations of the Fibonacci sequence, rather than the loss of periodicity or the layer-type ratio alone, underlie the enhancement.

Article.Title: Impact of axial length correction on retinal and choroidal thickness by widefield optical coherence tomography
Article.Authors: Chiku Y.; Hirano T.; Tomihara R.; Ito S.; Mukawa S.; Nakayama S.; Hoshiyama K.; Murata T.
Article.Abstract: The effect of axial length (AL) correction on retinal and choroidal thickness measurements obtained with widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) was assessed, and we investigated whether this correction effect differed by measurement region (peripheral region vs. macula) and anatomical layer (retina vs. choroid). This retrospective observational cross-sectional study included 302 eyes from 151 participants without ocular disease. Correction-related changes in retinal and choroidal thickness and the interaction effects among AL, measurement region, and anatomical layer on these changes were assessed. Correction-related thickness changes increased significantly with longer AL. Significant interaction effects were observed between AL and measurement region and between AL and anatomical layer. Specifically, the correction effect was significantly greater in the peripheral region than in the macula, and AL-related correction effects were more pronounced in the retina than in the choroid. Results showed that AL correction had a significant and spatially heterogeneous effect on retinal and choroidal thickness measurements derived from widefield SS-OCT. The impact varied by measurement region and anatomical layer, with the largest correction-related effect observed in the peripheral retina. These findings support incorporating AL correction in widefield OCT analyses to reduce AL-dependent measurement bias and improve measurement comparability, particularly when evaluating peripheral regions.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial potential of Pleurotus ostreatus against bovine mastitis pathogens: an in vitro screening study
Article.Authors: Kalińska A.; Zapora E.; Kot M.; Perlińska-Teresiak M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mastitis is a common multifactorial disease in dairy herds, usually associated with infections caused by bacteria, fungi or pathogenic microalgae and commonly treated with antibiotics. Widespread antibiotic resistance has prompted researchers around the world to search for new alternatives to combat infections. For centuries, plants, herbs and other natural-origin antimicrobial agents have been used in medicine worldwide. Therefore, the aim of this preliminary in vitro screening study was to evaluate the antibacterial effects of 10 Pleurotus ostreatus preparations against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli isolated from bovine mastitis cases. The preparations obtained using different extraction and preparation methods were evaluated at concentrations of 10%, 5%, 2.5%, 1.25%, and 0.625% using an XTT-based bacterial viability assay. The effects varied substantially among bacterial strains, preparations and concentrations. B9 (derived from oil-press pomace after hot-water treatment and subsequent methanol maceration) and B10 (derived from slow-juicer pomace by methanol maceration) showed the most consistent overall reductions in bacterial viability across the tested conditions, whereas other preparations produced pronounced reductions only in selected pathogen–concentration combinations. The observed responses were preparation-, pathogen-, and concentration-dependent and did not follow a uniform concentration-response pattern. In contrast, some preparations and concentrations were associated with bacterial viability values similar to or higher than those of the control, indicating a non-linear concentration-response pattern. These preliminary findings identify promising P. ostreatus preparations for further chemical characterization and safety assessment and support their continued investigation as potential sources of naturally derived antimicrobial compounds. However, the present results do not demonstrate bactericidal activity or therapeutic efficacy in cattle, and further studies, including evaluation in bovine mammary cells and subsequent in vivo validation, are required before any potential veterinary application in bovine mastitis can be considered.

Article.Title: Family history of low back pain is associated with low back pain, lower quality of life, and lumbar MRI findings
Article.Authors: Hu H.; Yang D.; Cordes L.; Schönnagel L.; Mödl L.; Grittner U.; Huang R.; Dong C.; Yang F.; Reitmaier S.; Schmidt H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Associations of family history of low back pain (LBP) with clinical outcomes and lumbar degenerative magnetic resonance imaging findings remain uncertain. This cross-sectional secondary analysis used data from 811 Berlin Back Study participants. Associations with self-reported family history of LBP were examined using logistic and linear regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking, and alcohol consumption. LBP prevalence was 57.9% without and 72.6% with family history (adjusted OR 1.91, 95% CI 1.42, 2.57, p < 0.001). Family history was associated with lower Short Form-36 global scores (unweighted mean of eight domains; B − 3.52, 95% CI − 5.79, − 1.25, p = 0.002), higher cumulative intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) scores (scale range 5–25; B 0.53, 95% CI 0.13, 0.93, p = 0.009), and higher cumulative facet joint degeneration (FJD) scores (scale range 5–20; B 0.41, 95% CI 0.15, 0.68, p = 0.003). Of the 63 secondary comparisons, 19 remained below the 5% false discovery rate threshold, including the three associations above. Among participants with LBP, no clear associations were observed with mean pain intensity or Roland–Morris Disability Questionnaire scores. Reported family history was associated with higher LBP odds, lower quality of life, and modestly greater IDD and FJD.

Article.Title: Large-scale reception testing reveals initial metrological non-compliance in brand-new domestic water meters
Article.Authors: Albaina I.; Mayo J.; Bidaguren I.; Alegría N.; Peñalva I.
Article.Abstract: Reliable domestic water metering is essential for billing, demand assessment and water-balance analysis, yet the initial metrological performance of brand-new meters remains poorly documented. This study analysed a historical reception-control database of 1,922 brand-new domestic water meters tested under controlled laboratory conditions using an accredited gravimetric test bench. The samples included single-jet, volumetric and ultrasonic meters. A meter was classified as non-compliant when at least one measured error exceeded the applicable maximum permissible error at any tested flow rate. Overall, 207 m were non-compliant, corresponding to a non-compliance rate of 10.8%. Non-compliance differed strongly by technology, reaching 33.8% for single-jet meters, 8.7% for volumetric meters and 2.7% for ultrasonic meters. Error patterns also varied by anonymised manufacturer code and metrological ratio (R). Within volumetric meters, manufacturer-code non-compliance ranged from 3.1 to 30.6%, while non-compliant single-jet meters showed marked negative bias, highlighting supplier-specific and pre-installation under-registration risks. Extended testing was associated with improved diagnostic resolution in some groups, although its marginal detection benefit depended on sample composition and error location along the flow-rate range. These findings show that reception testing provides diagnostic information that cannot be inferred from certification or nominal specifications alone.

Article.Title: Reliability improvement in CNC manufacturing through lean six sigma DMAIC: an empirical study on mean time between failures
Article.Authors: Shashi Kiran G.; Shivakumar M.; Ramachandra C.; Rameshbabu K.; Sachidananda H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Unplanned equipment failures at CNC manufacturing facilities create production delays that are difficult to schedule around, and published Lean Six Sigma DMAIC studies of Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) rarely report variance reduction as an outcome in its own right, despite highly variable failure intervals being at least as disruptive to production planning as low average reliability. This study applies the DMAIC framework to MTBF at a Government Tool Room and Training Centre (GTTC) in Bengaluru, India, a public-sector precision manufacturing facility, using six months of maintenance work-order records (January–June 2025, 502 unplanned breakdown events). Because system-based failure tracking began at the start of this window with no prior failure history available, the first recorded failure for each of 52 machines could not be paired with a genuine previous failure and was excluded as a left-censored observation, yielding a final analysis dataset of 450 events with a median baseline MTBF of 402.34 h (mean 429.92 h; CV, calculated from the mean and standard deviation, = 65.2%, a level of dispersion that limits the practical use of any single figure for production scheduling). Non-parametric Mann-Whitney testing (required by confirmed non-normality, Anderson-Darling A-squared = 3.81, p < 0.005) identified three factors statistically associated with lower MTBF: incomplete daily operator maintenance (median gap 104.5 h, p < 0.001), preventive maintenance not completed on schedule (gap 99.3 h, p < 0.001), and delayed component replacement (gap 113.4 h, p < 0.001; observed in 66.9% of events). Interventions addressing each factor were piloted on CNC milling machines and extended to four further machine families. Median MTBF rose to 558.70 h (+ 38.9%; Mann-Whitney, p < 0.001), with CV falling from 65.2% to 6.3%. The improvement persisted over a subsequent four-month Control-phase observation ( n = 267): every individual month remained significantly better than baseline ( p < 1.3 × 10⁻⁷ in the weakest month), and the statistically appropriate one-sided regression test found no evidence of regression relative to the immediate post-improvement result ( p = 0.985), with the Control-phase median (564.03 h) in fact marginally exceeding it. This study’s principal contribution is methodological as much as empirical: it demonstrates that MTBF variance reduction, not only the mean or median shift, can be treated as a primary DMAIC outcome, and it reports a transparent left-censoring exclusion rule that other facilities beginning failure-tracking from a fixed start date can apply directly. Findings are presented from a single facility and are not claimed to be representative of a broader setting. As a before–after study with no concurrent control group, the results show an association with the interventions, not proof of causation, and four months of Control-phase data do not establish long-term stability.

Article.Title: Sustainable machining of monel 400 using hybrid cryogenic lubrication and multiobjective optimization
Article.Authors: Patel D.; Sivalingam S.; Singh J.; Jani S.; M. K. A.; Mann V.; Thykattusserry N.; Thatoi D.; Bhowmik A.; Tamene Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the machinability of Monel 400 under four machining environments: dry cutting, Minimum Quantity Lubrication (MQL), cryogenic liquid nitrogen (LN₂) cooling, and hybrid cryogenic–minimum quantity lubrication (Cryo-MQL). The effects of these environments on surface roughness, specific cutting energy (SCE), and machining cost were evaluated. Cryo-MQL demonstrated the most favorable overall machining performance by combining the cooling capability of LN₂ with the lubricating action of MQL. Compared with dry machining, Cryo-MQL reduced surface roughness, SCE, and total machining cost by 48%, 29.17%, and 10.64%, respectively. Relative to MQL and cryogenic machining, surface roughness decreased by 10.34% and 15.22%, while SCE decreased by 19.05% and 22.73%, respectively. Machining cost was also reduced by 7.89% and 8.30% compared with MQL and cryogenic machining, respectively. A multi-objective optimization framework integrating Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) identified a balanced set of machining parameters. Experimental validation yielded prediction errors of 4.61%, 3.06%, and 2.79% for surface roughness, SCE, and machining cost, respectively. These findings demonstrate the machining-performance and economic advantages of Cryo-MQL, including improved surface quality, process-level energy efficiency, and reduced direct machining cost. The use of biodegradable sunflower oil further supports resource-conscious manufacturing. However, the environmental burdens associated with LN₂ production, purification, storage, and delivery were not quantified. Therefore, reduced SCE does not establish a direct reduction in carbon emissions. Comprehensive life-cycle assessment and carbon-footprint analysis are required to determine the net environmental impact and establish any contribution to SDG 13, while the findings indicate potential relevance to SDG 9 and SDG 12.

Article.Title: From parents to children: how nature experiences are transmitted across generations
Article.Authors: Tamari M.; Soga M.
Article.Abstract: Children’s direct experiences of nature are increasingly recognised as important for promoting health and well-being and fostering pro-conservation attitudes and behaviours. Understanding why some children experience nature more frequently than others is therefore important. Although parents can play a major role in shaping children’s engagement with nature, the processes through which nature experiences persist across generations remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted an online questionnaire survey of 1000 families in the Tokyo metropolitan area, Japan, obtaining matched responses from fathers, mothers, and one child per household. Children whose parents reported more frequent childhood nature experiences engaged with nature more frequently. Parental childhood nature experience was also associated with parental nature connectedness and perceptions of the benefits and risks of nature experiences. Parental nature connectedness and facilitative behaviour were, in turn, positively associated with children’s nature experience, whereas perceived benefits and risks showed no direct associations. These findings suggest that nature experience can show continuity across generations, with parents’ childhood experiences potentially shaping how their children engage with nature through multiple psychological and behavioural pathways. Such intergenerational continuity may be an important process to consider in efforts to reverse the extinction of experience.

Article.Title: Comparative study of moxifloxacin removal using Ulva, layered double hydroxide, and their green hybrid nanocomposite supported by DFT mechanistic analysis
Article.Authors: Makled S.; Youssef E.; Shafei R.; Saad R.; Hou L.; Mahmoud R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The removal of pharmaceutical contaminants from water bodies has been a matter of concern in environmental studies. This comparative study investigated the adsorption of Moxifloxacin hydrochloride (MOX) on Magnesium-Zinc (-iron) layered double hydroxide (MZF/LDH) @ Ulva nanocomposites, MZF/LDH, and Ulva spp. macroalgae from water under various conditions, including different contact times, pH values, adsorbent dosages, MOX concentrations, and temperatures. The physicochemical parameters of the statistical monolayer model were used to understand the functional groups of MOX, the active site density of MZF/LDH@ Ulva , and the sorption capacity at saturation. The MZF/LDH@ Ulva nanocomposite, which is a promising covering material with a high maximum monolayer adsorption capacity (Q sat = 215.6 mg/g at 328 K), showed a spontaneous and endothermic process of adsorption during the removal of MOX molecules. The adsorbents were comprehensively characterized using spectroscopic, microscopic, crystallographic, thermal, elemental, and surface area analyses. The maximum adsorption occurred within 60 min at a pH of 9 with an adsorbent dosage of 9 mg/20 mL of moxifloxacin solution. The equilibrium adsorption isotherms were described by the Langmuir isotherm model, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 463.96 mg/g at 25 °C for the nanocomposite. MZF/LDH@ Ulva exhibited effective antibacterial and antifungal activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans , respectively, as demonstrated by minimum inhibitory concentrations (1.56 mg/mL and 6.26 mg/mL, respectively), accompanied by a reduction in optical density (OD 600 ), showing measurable inhibition of the growth of microbes at low concentrations. A quantum chemical method combining the PBE0 hybrid functional (Density Functional Theory) with the Conductor-like Polarizable Continuum Model (CPCM) to model solvent effects, complementary DFT/PBE0/CPCM (water) calculations provided molecular-level insights into the adsorption mechanism. Energy decomposition analysis revealed that electrostatic interactions dominate (46-% of total attraction), with measurable dispersion contributions (25–30%), suggesting the physisorption mechanism. The novelty of this work is based on the use of the MZF/LDH@ Ulva green macroalgae green method for pharmaceutical pollutants, which exhibit favorable adsorption kinetics and antimicrobial activity against bacterial and fungal pathogens, suggesting potential applicability in water treatment.

Article.Title: Emotion-modulated interaction regression predicts static facial blendshape scores
Article.Authors: Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Emotion-conditioned virtual avatars require a controllable bridge from affective cues to facial control parameters. This paper addresses static expression-parameter prediction: given a facial expression image and an emotion-class descriptor, the model estimates a 52-dimensional MediaPipe/ARKit-style blendshape-like vector. The 52-dimensional coefficients are automatic Face Landmarker estimates of ARKit-named scores from 2D images. Because training and evaluation share this extractor, the reported metrics measure agreement with those automatic scores. Predicted vectors remain candidate control profiles for a subsequent documented retargeting step. We propose EMIRA (Emotion-Modulated Interaction Regressor for Avatars), a lightweight class-conditioned interaction regressor that combines a 272-dimensional handcrafted image descriptor, emotion-class prototypes, and explicit class-conditioned interaction features. At inference time, we additionally evaluate a feature-shift fallback strategy that switches to an emotion prior when the feature-shift score exceeds a training-set quantile threshold, and we analyze its output-selection behavior under feature-shift diagnosis. The Yale Face Database is used as a small four-class feature-shift diagnostic. On an internal static-expression benchmark with 13,357 valid samples, EMIRA reduces RMSE by 14.07% over a rule baseline and by a modest 4.44% over image-only regression. Paired bootstrap comparisons over 2003 test samples show positive deltas against rule, image-only, early-fusion, and same-dimensional capacity-control baselines. A class-balanced diagnostic over five reliable emotion classes keeps a 4.31% RMSE gain over image-only regression. A per-blendshape mechanism diagnostic further shows that 83.90% of the positive per-dimension error reduction over image-only concentrates in mouth controls. These results support class-conditioned interaction on a given visual branch as a useful representation for static MediaPipe blendshape-score prediction rather than a broadly applicable fusion architecture, with the reported RMSE reductions measuring agreement with automatic MediaPipe scores rather than independently annotated animation quality.

Article.Title: High gain non-isolated switched inductor SEPIC converter for renewable energy applications
Article.Authors: G D.; Arunkumar C.; Sidharthan P.; Nethagani S.
Article.Abstract: High step-up DC–DC converters are required in renewable energy systems to efficiently interface low-voltage sources with high-voltage loads and DC microgrids. The conventional high gain converter suffers from high voltage stress of semiconductor devices, low efficiency and complex circuit architecture. A high gain non-isolated switched inductor single-ended primary-inductor converter (SI-SEPIC) for renewable energy applications is presented in this research. The suggested topology adopts the switched-inductor network to realize a much higher voltage conversion ratio. The converter retains the intrinsic benefits of standard SEPIC converter, such as non-inverted output voltage and wide working range, which make it suited for solar systems, and DC microgrids. The converter is analyzed in detail in terms of operating modes, steady state characteristics, derivation of voltage gain, design of components and performance evaluation. The proposed converter is experimentally validated with a laboratory prototype of 75 W. The experimental results support the validity of the proposed SI-SEPIC converter for renewable energy applications with steady operation; high voltage gain and high-power conversion efficiency. The proposed maximum power point tracking method achieved a tracking efficiency of up to 99.8% with a minimum tracking time of 1.8 s under the tested operating conditions.

Article.Title: Numerical reconstruction of acoustic parameters of ancient bone pipes using the Ffowcs Williams-Hawkings model
Article.Authors: Warzyńska U.; Siwulski T.; Tokarz D.
Article.Abstract: The article presents a method for simulating sound propagation in simple wind instruments, such as ancient bone pipes, demonstrated through a case study of an ancient bone pipe replica. Since original archaeological artifacts are preserved museum objects and cannot be subjected to invasive experimental testing, the methodology was tested using a physical replica under a representative operating condition. The research combines experimental measurements of sound pressure level of the bone aerophone replicas, with numerical Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations using the Ffowcs Williams-Hawkings (FW-H) acoustic model. This numerical approach facilitates the visualization of the velocity and pressure fields during sound production, allowing for the identification of primary airflow patterns and jet–edge interactions. The results demonstrate reasonable agreement between simulated and measured acoustic spectral trends, capturing the primary spectral peaks within acceptable engineering tolerances for highly irregular geometries. Consequently, the proposed simulation method provides a robust framework for evaluating the acoustic properties of archaeological aerophone exhibits.

Article.Title: Seroprevalence and clinical correlates of fascioliasis among patients with hepatobiliary diseases in Urmia in Northwest Iran
Article.Authors: Hasannejad M.; Mohammad Hosseiniazar M.; Aminpour A.; Jafari R.
Article.Abstract: Fascioliasis is an important hepatobiliary zoonotic infection in which freshwater snails are intermediate hosts and livestock are the main definitive hosts. Humans become infected incidentally by ingesting metacercariae on aquatic plants or in contaminated water. This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of fascioliasis among patients with liver diseases referred to Imam Khomeini Hospital, Urmia, from 29 October 2024 to 26 February 2025. In this cross-sectional study, 313 sera were collected from patients with liver diseases referred to Imam Khomeini Hospital, Urmia. All sera were tested​ by anti- Fasciola hepatica IgG ELISA kit, and demographic, behavioral, and clinical data were recorded and analyzed using SPSS software. Geographic distribution of seropositive cases was mapped using geographic information system (GIS) mapping. Of the 313 patients examined, four (1.3%) tested seropositive for Fasciola infection; three of the four had a history of biliary stone and three resided in rural areas. Because of the small number of seropositive cases, the analysis was descriptive and no formal tests of association were performed. A live adult Fasciola sp. was endoscopically retrieved from the common bile duct of one seropositive-eosinophilic patient confirming active infection in this patient during the chronic biliary phase. The seroprevalence of fascioliasis among liver-disease patients in Urmia was low (1.3%), but numerically higher than the 0.33% recently reported in a different population survey in the same province. Given the parasite’s chronic course, its capacity to mimic other hepatobiliary disorders, clinicians should maintain caution for sporadic cases.

Article.Authors: Morikura T.; Sakaguchi K.; Tanaka R.; Iwasaki K.; Shimizu T.
Article.Abstract: To advance the industrialization of cultured meat and regenerative medicine, scalable and efficient cell culture techniques are essential. In this study, we proposed a versatile image analysis-based cell counting method by using cellular autofluorescence without any parameter tuning. The proposed method estimates the number of cells by applying spatiotemporal averaging to the autofluorescence signals in the microscopic images. This technique, which harnesses the ubiquitous autofluorescence inherent in living cells, offers a cost-effective and practical solution applicable to a broad range of fields requiring high-throughput cell quantification.

Article.Authors: Mousavifard Z.; Turaev D.; Sabirov S.; Avezovna A.; Urozboev K.; Davoudi N.; Farshad A.

Article.Title: Fluorinated protic ionic liquids for clay swelling inhibition in water based drilling fluids
Article.Authors: Farag A.; Nazar M.; Murtaza M.; Fahmi M.; Abu-Al-Saud M.; Hussain S.; Kamal M.; Patil S.
Article.Abstract: Wellbore instability caused by clay hydration, swelling, and dispersion remains a major challenge in water-based drilling fluids. Moreover, the role of fluorinated protic ionic-liquid architecture in simultaneously regulating these processes remains insufficiently understood. The median particle diameter (D 50 ) increased from 2.33 to 6.10 μm, while the zeta potential shifted from − 32.1 to − 23.9 mV, indicating enhanced aggregation and reduced electrostatic stabilization. Complementary structural, morphological, and thermal analyses further supported FIL-clay interactions and suppressed hydration. Collectively, the results support a complementary inhibition mechanism in which electrostatic interactions and charge screening reduce interparticle repulsion and promote clay aggregation, while fluorinated hydrophobic shielding restricts water accessibility. These findings demonstrate the potential of molecularly tailored fluoro-based protic ionic liquids as effective shale inhibitors for water-based drilling fluids.

Article.Authors: Kurgonaitė M.; Paulauskaitė A.; Frercks B.; Kriščiūnas A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract DNA has emerged as a promising medium for long-term digital data storage because of its exceptional information density and durability. The framework systematically evaluates how different codebook construction strategies influence downstream decoding, candidate ambiguity, and final image reconstruction. Under simulated nanopore sequencing conditions, all constrained codebooks achieved high payload recovery (> 91%), but substantial differences were observed in their ability to preserve the correct payload among decoded candidate sequences. The codebook combining sequence-space discrimination, biochemical quality control, and structural compatibility produced the highest candidate-set quality and, when coupled with Random Forest-based reliability filtering, achieved the best image reconstruction performance, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 29.82 dB, a structural similarity index of 0.9309, and 80.19% exact pixel recovery. These findings demonstrate that payload recovery alone is insufficient to evaluate DNA storage performance, as downstream candidate ambiguity directly impacts the quality of reconstructed data. The proposed framework provides an end-to-end approach to investigating the relationship among codebook design, decoding robustness, and image reconstruction, thereby supporting the development of more reliable nanopore-based DNA data storage systems.

Article.Authors: Moinuddin S.; Murugan G.; Ponnarengan H.; Nagallapati V.; Khan M.; Faraz M.
Article.Abstract: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) has emerged as a promising technology for fabricating large-scale aluminium components; however, reliable process optimization remains challenging owing to the complex interactions among deposition parameters, thermal history, and mechanical performance. This study proposes an interpretable physics-guided machine learning framework for predictive modelling and multi-objective optimization of circular-path Cold Metal Transfer (CMT)-WAAM of ER5356 aluminium alloy. A Taguchi L27 experimental design with three centre-point replications was employed to investigate the effects of wire feed speed, travel speed, interpass temperature, and shielding gas flow rate on ultimate tensile strength, elongation, flexural strength, and hardness. Physics-guided descriptors representing deposition intensity, thermal accumulation, cooling severity, and shielding adequacy were integrated into a multi-output stacking regressor to embed manufacturing knowledge and provide a physically structured representation of the process variables. The optimized process window predicted an ultimate tensile strength of 295.20 MPa, 40.10% elongation, 397.80 MPa flexural strength, and 71.80 HV hardness. A single confirmatory experiment produced deviations below 5%, with composite desirability decreasing from 0.9989 to 0.9565. Fractographic analysis revealed ductile failure through microvoid coalescence and ligament stretching, providing additional microstructural support for the behaviour observed at the optimized condition. By integrating physics-guided feature engineering with interpretable multi-output learning, the proposed framework provides a data-efficient and data-efficient decision-support approach within the investigated WAAM process window tool for intelligent WAAM process optimization, offering a practical pathway toward AI-enabled, digitally integrated additive manufacturing.

Article.Title: Exhaustive treadmill run increases urinary excretion of albumin and creatinine but not cell-free DNA in average trained healthy men
Article.Authors: Stec-Martyna E.; Szymanski J.; Falkowski P.; Konecki T.; Galczynski S.; Kulczycka-Wojdala D.; Kopacz K.; Kopacz L.; Sarniak A.; Prymont-Przyminska A.; Włodarczyk A.; Nowak D.
Article.Abstract: Exercise induces a transient rise of NETotic cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in plasma. Various mechanisms may be responsible for temporary character of this phenomenon including cfDNA degradation by DNAse or uptake by vascular endothelium. We tested whether urinary excretion of cfDNA may contribute to its normalization in plasma after exercise. The study involved 15 average trained men (VO 2 max 45.5 ± 6.25 ml/kg x min) without urogenital pathology and had comparative and crossover design (exhaustive treadmill run, speed corresponding to 70% of VO 2 max, run distance 11.2 ± 4.7 km, run time 67 ± 19 min vs. 1.0 h rest). Exercise caused ~ 25-fold increase in plasma cfDNA just after bout that returned to baseline after 4 h. Within this time post-exercise urinary output of albumin (an indicator of exercise-induced damage to glomerular filtration membrane) and creatinine increased, while no significant changes in urinary cfDNA were noted. The urinary ratios of cfDNA to creatinine and to albumin decreased in post-exercise urine in comparison to resting arm of the exercise physiology study (4.8 ± 8.4 vs. 3.7 ± 5.7 ng/mg and 614.0 ± 586 vs. 324.7 ± 494.8 ng/mg, respectively, p < 0.05). These findings exclude cfDNA excretion with urine as the significant route of elimination of cfDNA released in response to exercise and suggest that it is not necessary to limit physical activity in urine donors for cfDNA analyses.

Article.Title: Gaussian Boson Sampling for efficient dense subgraph identification in omic-driven gene networks during anthropogenic methane emission
Article.Authors: Ho K.; Lai C.; Tan G.; Lee P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This work presents a Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) method to identify densely connected subgraphs from omics-derived gene networks. The method utilises the intrinsic sampling bias of GBS towards densely connected nodes, providing an efficient strategy for sampling dense subgraphs compared with classical methods. We applied GBS to sheep rumen gene pathway networks under low and high methane yield conditions. The networks were naturally grouped into high, moderate, and low abundance clusters without specifying the number of genes per cluster. These clusters were associated with biochemical functions of facultative anaerobes, which may support methanogenic activity by maintaining reducing conditions favourable for methanogens. Benchmarking against the classical Greedy Peel algorithm showed that GBS consistently identified identical densest subgraphs while requiring 5 to 10 times fewer subgraph evaluations. Moreover, GBS obtained more subgraphs with higher densities than uniform random sampling. These results showed that GBS can substantially reduce the number of subgraph evaluations required to identify biologically meaningful gene clusters. However, the present study was conducted using a classical simulator, and investigations using photonic hardware are needed to evaluate the full potential of GBS. Nevertheless, these findings support the future use of GBS for subgraph search in large multi-omic networks where dense modules exhibit functional significance.

Article.Title: A Gaussian quantum-inspired optimization framework for robust medical image watermarking
Article.Authors: Garg P.; Gautam M.; Singh D.; Maitrey S.; Genta A.
Article.Abstract: The rapid exchange of medical images through telemedicine and cloud-based healthcare systems has increased the need for secure transmission while preserving the diagnostic quality of medical data. Digital image watermarking provides an effective solution by ensuring data authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality without significantly affecting image quality. However, achieving an optimal balance between watermark imperceptibility and robustness remains a challenging task because the embedding strength must be carefully selected. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust medical image watermarking framework based on Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Hessenberg Decomposition (HD), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and a Gaussian Quantum-Behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (GQBPSO) algorithm for adaptive embedding factor optimization. The watermark is first secured using a scrambling strategy and then embedded into the singular values of the transformed host image. Unlike conventional optimization approaches, the proposed GQBPSO employs Gaussian-guided quantum-inspired particle updates to achieve a better balance between global exploration and local exploitation, enabling adaptive selection of the embedding strength for improved watermark quality. The proposed framework is evaluated on publicly available chest X-ray and diabetic retinopathy datasets under a comprehensive set of image processing, noise, filtering, and geometric attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed GQBPSO consistently outperforms QPSO and QDPSO in terms of imperceptibility while maintaining competitive robustness. The proposed method achieves a maximum PSNR of 50.166 dB and maintains high Normalized Correlation (NC) values under various attack conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective balance between image quality and watermark robustness, making it a promising solution for secure medical image storage and transmission in modern healthcare systems.

Article.Title: Physical activity, sedentary time, and anthropometric differences in Saudi children with cerebral palsy compared to typically developing peers: an activPAL-based study
Article.Authors: Alghadier M.; Almasoud N.; Alharthi D.; Alrshedi O.; Albesher R.; Alothman S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Children with cerebral palsy (CP) typically accumulate less physical activity (PA) and more sedentary time than typically developing (TD) peers, but evidence from Middle Eastern settings is limited. This study compared objectively measured PA, sedentary behavior, and anthropometric profiles between Saudi children with CP and TD peers. In a cross-sectional comparative study, school-aged children with CP (GMFCS I-II, n = 14) and age-matched TD peers ( n = 15) wore an activPAL inclinometer continuously for seven days. Anthropometric measures included height, weight, and BMI percentiles. activPAL outcomes comprised time spent sitting/lying, standing, and stepping; sit-to-stand transitions; sedentary bout characteristics; and reciprocal leg movement (RLM) epochs. Between-group differences were assessed using Mann-Whitney U tests; daily stepping time was the pre-specified primary outcome, and all remaining activPAL variables were treated as secondary exploratory outcomes. Associations between anthropometry and activity were examined using Spearman correlations. Complementary multiple linear regression models adjusted for BMI percentile were run as sensitivity analyses. Children with CP demonstrated significantly lower body weight (median [IQR]: 21.65 [18.25–29.90] vs. 33.00 [27.35–37.40], p = 0.02) and markedly lower BMI percentiles (6 [2–59.25] vs. 87 [70–96.95], p = 0.002). Compared with TD peers, the CP group accumulated 2.66 more hours/day sedentary (median 692.1 vs. 532.3 min; Δ = +159.8 min), spent 0.46 fewer hours/day upright when combining stepping and standing time (median 254.5 vs. 282.0 min; Δ = −27.5 min), accumulated 0.7% fewer daily steps (median 7582.4 vs. 7639.3), and performed 11.2% fewer sit-to-stand transitions (median 93.5 vs. 105.3). Sedentary behavior in children with CP also tended to be accumulated in longer bouts, with ~ 1.18 more hours/day spent in prolonged sedentary periods (≥ 30 min; median 296.39 vs. 225.37 min), although this between-group difference was not statistically significant ( p = 0.13). RLM epochs count (10 s–1 min) were ~ 1.9% lower in the CP group (median 5883 vs. 5995.33), but this difference was not statistically significant ( p = 0.29). Saudi children with CP exhibited distinct anthropometric profiles, with significantly lower body weight and BMI percentiles. While descriptive trends suggested greater sedentary accumulation, fewer sit-to-stand transitions, and reduced stepping time, these between-group differences did not reach statistical significance in the primary analyses. In complementary regression analyses, CP group was associated with fewer sit-to-stand transitions and fewer short-duration upright bouts after adjustment for BMI percentile. Given the small sample size and exploratory nature of secondary analyses, findings should be interpreted cautiously and require replication in larger samples. The activPAL provided clinically actionable metrics for rehabilitation planning, and these findings may inform intervention strategies aimed at interrupting prolonged sitting, increasing stepping opportunities, and integrating nutritional support with physical activity promotion.

Article.Title: In situ stress constrains and redirects crack propagation during ultra-deep hole blasting of thick and hard roofs in coal mines
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Chen D.; Zhao B.; Du Y.; Wang Y.; Gao W.; Guo Y.; Wu Z.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ultra-deep hole blasting in thick and hard roofs is typically conducted under in situ stress and without a blasting free surface. Determining the extent of blast-induced crack propagation is therefore essential for blasting parameter design and performance evaluation. At the 73 upper 11 working face of Baodian Coal Mine, this study combines theoretical analysis, LS-DYNA numerical simulations and field borehole imaging to investigate the effects of in situ stress on the extent, direction and number of blast-induced cracks. In situ stress has little influence on near-blasthole pressure and particle-velocity responses but primarily restricts intermediate- and far-field crack propagation through the normal compressive stress acting on crack surfaces. As equal biaxial confining pressure increases from 0 to 30 MPa, the maximum crack length decreases from 231 to 43 cm and the number of major cracks from 18 to 0, whereas peak pressure at the blasthole wall and particle velocity change by less than 1%. Under unequal biaxial confining pressure, the mean normal stress primarily suppresses crack extent, whereas the principal stress difference mainly governs the directional concentration of crack propagation; the number of major cracks reflects the combined influence of these two stress components. To address the preferential crack orientation and spatially non-uniform distribution induced by in situ stress, an inclined-offset borehole observation method is proposed to acquire crack information at different distances and orientations. Major cracks were observed up to approximately 2.40 m from the effective charge segment, whereas only isolated peripheral cracks were observed at approximately 2.80 m. These findings provide a basis for evaluating the effective blasting range and designing blasting parameters for thick and hard roofs.

Article.Title: Repurposing PEM electrolyzers as active power sinks to recover curtailed photovoltaic energy as green hydrogen in active distribution networks
Article.Authors: Elias Y.; Daowd M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-penetration photovoltaic (PV) generation in active distribution networks produces large volumes of curtailed surplus energy while stressing voltage and losses. A battery alone cannot absorb persistent midday surpluses beyond its finite capacity, and prior hydrogen–battery studies have over-attributed battery-protection benefits without a fair comparison. This paper tests whether a proton-exchange-membrane (PEM) electrolyzer operated as an active power sink can recover otherwise-curtailed PV energy into sellable green hydrogen. A stochastic two-stage co-optimization framework couples a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) for siting and sizing with a linear-programming (LP) dispatch on the IEEE 33-bus network, using measured Benban PV Geographical Information System (PVGIS) irradiance, EgyptERA tariffs, and K-means clustering into nine representative days. The proposed system reduces active power losses by 38.8% and produces 127,448 kg/yr of green hydrogen (displacing about 1,000 t CO₂/yr) by cutting daily curtailment from 44.77 to 27.16 MWh. Under a fair comparison with identical degradation-aware dispatch and an identical smart-inverter rating, the minimum voltage (0.9549 p.u.) and battery degradation cost ($20.76/day) match a battery-only system: voltage support comes from the shared IEEE 1547–2018 smart inverter, whereas the electrolyzer’s distinct value is bulk curtailment recovery. Direct hydrogen sales at $2.0/kg dominate re-electrification across a $0.83–$2.56/kg range, driving the fuel cell to its minimum rating (electrolyzer/fuel-cell ratio 18.52). On a full-cost basis (O&M, stack replacement, compression) the levelized cost of storage is $0.978/kWh and of hydrogen $2.78/kg; hydrogen revenue offsets about 72% of the hydrogen-subsystem cost, making the electrolyzer a substantially self-financing grid-support asset.

Article.Title: Repurposed smart tuna-fishing buoys provide real-time intelligence for marine conservation and ocean observation
Article.Authors: Lebrato M.; Gavira-O’Neill K.; Losada-Ros M.; Murie C.; Nhamussua N.; da Graça M.; Jije-Gonçalves M.; Kalashnikova E.; Bravo A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract End-of-use echosounder buoys developed for industrial tuna fishing offer a largely untapped opportunity to expand ocean monitoring using existing fisheries technology. Here we present a technology-transfer and pilot feasibility study testing whether repurposed smart-buoys can operate as short-term autonomous platforms for marine conservation monitoring and ocean observation. Through Satlink project ReCon, refurbished buoys were deployed in fixed-point and drifting configurations across one shelf technical test area, two coral reefs, and two seamount/pinnacle systems in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) region (Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique). Across fixed-point and drifting configurations, the exported dataset contained 393 time-stamped acoustic records and 1,281 depth-layer relative acoustic biomass/backscatter observations, with buoy position and acoustic data transmitted by satellite (via INMARSAT) to shore-based systems. Integration with the long-term BCSS Ocean Observatory time-series provided concurrent weather and oceanographic context across > 20 in-situ variables, while scuba-based megafauna surveys recorded 14–20 megafauna taxa per site as biological context for the acoustic records. The pilot time-series captured consistent diel structure, with 20–40% higher nocturnal relative acoustic biomass/backscatter values, alongside exploratory temporal co-occurrences with cooler bottom-water pulses, transient chlorophyll-a increases, and site-level differences in megafauna assemblage structure. While these short time-series cannot be used to infer ecological baselines, reef health, fishing impacts, environmental drivers, or absolute biological biomass, they demonstrate the capacity of repurposed smart-buoys to generate high-frequency acoustic and contextual ecological information in data-poor and remote marine regions. Our study establishes a practical pathway for integrating recovered fishing infrastructure into marine observatories, while highlighting the need for longer deployments, broader replication, quantitative habitat characterization, and independent biological calibration before robust ecological inference can be made.

Article.Title: A novel switched inductor–capacitor high-gain DC–DC converter: DSP-based PID and fuzzy control with detailed transient analysis for EV DC bus
Article.Authors: Nethaji G.; Kathirvelan J.
Article.Abstract: In electric vehicle (EV) systems, where low-voltage energy sources must effectively interface with high-voltage DC buses, high-gain DC–DC converters are crucial. A new switching inductor–capacitor-based high-gain boost converter that can step up a low input voltage of 30–600 V without using excessive duty cycles is presented in this work. The suggested design reduces voltage stress, switching losses, and input current ripple while achieving high conversion gain through the use of numerous energy transfer channels and voltage multiplier action. Both Proportional–Integral–Derivative (PID) and Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) strategies are implemented through a real-time digital control platform using the TMS320F28379D digital signal processor to guarantee superior voltage regulation and dynamic performance under varying line and load conditions. A rigorous transient and steady-state performance evaluation is carried out utilizing essential dynamic indices such as rise time, overshoot, undershoot, and slew rate—a feature typically missed in prior high-gain converter research. A DSP-based hardware prototype running at 50 kHz is used to experimentally test the MATLAB/Simulink model of the system. The converter successfully produces an output of 600 V at 0.45 A with a peak efficiency of 88.99%. Comparative findings show that the FLC outperforms the traditional PID controller in terms of robustness, undershoot, and reaction time. The feasibility, dependability, and efficacy of the suggested converter for high-voltage EV DC-link applications and renewable energy systems needing effective, high step-up power conversion are confirmed by the strong agreement between simulation and experimental findings.

Article.Title: Performance analysis of dual-IRS-assisted NOMA for underwater visible light communication in turbulent channels
Article.Authors: Sripathi P.; Miriyala M.; Veerapu G.; Kappala V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Underwater visible light communication (UVLC) has become a highly attractive solution for fast wireless underwater communications, given its high data transmission rates, low delay, and security associated with the physical layer. Nonetheless, it suffers from serious limitations resulting from absorption, scattering, and turbulence-induced fading. In this paper, we present a new dual IRS architecture for UVLC communication that utilizes Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) and Non-orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technology to enhance the reliability and spectral efficiency of the link. A unified channel model is developed, where both the direct and IRS-assisted paths are taken into account, including the impact of underwater absorption, scattering, and turbulence through the Exponential Generalized Gamma (EGG) distribution. Based on the proposed channel model, closed-form expressions for the cumulative distribution function (CDF) and probability density function (PDF) are derived in terms of the Meijer- G function. Furthermore, analytical expressions are developed for the outage probability and average bit error rate (ABER), while the ergodic capacity is evaluated to quantify the achievable spectral efficiency of the proposed system. An asymptotic outage analysis is also carried out to characterize the system behavior in the high-SNR regime. The proposed framework is evaluated under different underwater channel and system conditions, and the analytical results are validated through Monte Carlo simulations. The close agreement between the analytical and simulation results confirms the accuracy of the developed framework and demonstrates the performance benefits of the proposed dual-IRS-assisted NOMA-UVLC system.

Article.Title: Liquid crystal soft interfaces reveal molecular-level influences on microscopic flow characteristics
Article.Authors: Erdil C.; Bukusoglu E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding boundary interactions at fluidic interfaces is critical for advancing synthetic and natural functional interfaces. However, classical hydrodynamic frameworks often fail to capture flow characteristics induced by localized molecular and ionic structuring at these boundaries. We present a microfluidic experimental oil–water co-flow platform, utilizing either a thermotropic liquid crystal (LC) or an isotropic oil, designed to systematically isolate the interfacial molecular and ionic mechanisms governing dynamic transport. Specifically, we provide experimental evidence of how water structuring, electroviscous drag, and molecular director alignment dictate interfacial flow, which remain poorly understood in conventional microfluidic systems. Our findings reveal that the precise spatial LC director configuration and ionic structuring at the interface fundamentally alter boundary layer slip conditions and drag. By bridging the long-standing gap between microscopic molecular events and macroscopic fluid mechanics near interfaces, this work introduces a design paradigm for engineering next-generation microfluidic and nanofluidic technologies, smart functional interfaces, and complex biological or technological systems.

Article.Title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
Article.Authors: Koerner S.; Egloff B.; Osterholz S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

Article.Title: Spatial and seasonal variation in soil organic matter responses to landfill disturbance in the Hyrcanian Forests
Article.Authors: Kooch Y.; Haghverdi K.; Nouraei A.; Hajimirzaaghaee S.; Amiri M.; Shabani S.; Zarafshar M.
Article.Abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to anthropogenic pressures that threaten soil functioning and long-term ecosystem stability. Among these pressures, landfill-based waste disposal has emerged as a growing concern in developing regions, particularly where forest soils play a central role in organic matter turnover and nutrient retention. However, the responses of these systems to waste-derived inputs under contrasting climatic settings remain insufficiently constrained. In this study, we examine how municipal solid waste disposal alters soil organic matter characteristics, with emphasis on carbon (C)- and nitrogen (N)-related properties, across climatically distinct forest regions of northern Iran. In this regard, soil samples from landfill-impacted sites and nearby forest control sites across four seasons and three soil depths were obtained from four forested areas (i.e., Chalous, Noor, Shirgah, and Behshahr) arranged along a west–east climatic gradient with progressively lower precipitation and higher temperatures. The results revealed that control forest stands, particularly in Chalous and Noor, exhibited significantly higher macro- and micro-aggregate-associated C and N, as well as greater stocks of labile organic matter fractions in surface soils, compared with landfill-affected sites. These differences were most pronounced in the upper soil layers and during summer and fall. In contrast, landfill sites, especially in the warmer and drier regions of Shirgah and Behshahr, showed reduced C contents in free and occluded light fractions and in cold- and hot-water-soluble organic C and N, indicating changes in physical stabilization and nutrient retention. Particulate and dissolved organic C and N were generally higher in surface soils (0–10 cm) than in deeper soil layers, with relatively higher values observed in the Chalous and Noor forest stands. Overall, the findings indicate that unengineered landfill activities were associated with significant changes in soil C and N stabilization pathways in forest ecosystems, with greater differences observed under warmer and drier climatic conditions. These results highlight the role of climate in regulating soil vulnerability to waste-related disturbances and underscore the need for improved solid waste management strategies to protect soil functions and ecosystem sustainability in forested landscapes.

Article.Authors: Kim M.; Oh S.; Yook J.; Ahn J.; Han J.; Oh Y.; Jeon Y.; Jung H.; Choi J.; Cho J.; Park S.; Kim C.; Han S.; Lim J.
Article.Abstract: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) is characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, and tubular cell death, yet endogenous mechanisms regulating these processes remain incompletely understood. DICAM expression was significantly upregulated following cisplatin exposure in HK-2 cells. DICAM deficiency exacerbated renal dysfunction and tubular injury after cisplatin administration. DICAM deficiency increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and NOX4 expression, along with changes in selected MAPK signaling components. These findings were accompanied by increased inflammatory responses, macrophage infiltration, tubular apoptosis, and early profibrotic changes. DICAM deficiency also altered adhesion-related molecules, including increased integrin β1 and decreased occludin expression, suggesting impaired epithelial structural integrity. DICAM may act as an endogenous protective regulator against cisplatin-induced AKI by suppressing oxidative stress-mediated signaling and apoptosis. Further studies are needed to establish the underlying molecular mechanisms.

Article.Title: Effects of physical activity on nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease incidence and mortality
Article.Authors: Chung E.; Choi H.; Lee H.; Jung J.; Kim Y.; Kang Y.
Article.Abstract: Data on the effects of physical activity (PA) on nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease (NTM-PD) incidence and mortality are limited. This retrospective cohort study followed individuals in South Korea who underwent health examinations between 2009 and 2010 within the National Health Insurance Service-Health Screening Cohort. PA changes were assessed in participants with a follow-up examination within 4 years of the 2009–2010 baseline. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations between PA and NTM-PD incidence and mortality. Of 360,946 participants, 58.7% had insufficient PA. Compared to the sufficient PA group, this group was older and had a lower proportion of Charlson comorbidity index 0–1 scores. These findings suggest that PA is a modifiable factor associated with NTM-PD risk and all-cause mortality, supporting the potential benefit of promoting PA for the prevention and management of NTM-PD.
