Article.Title: Caffeic acid adaptation alters the antibacterial and anticancer activities of Lactobacillus reuteri cell-free supernatant
Article.Authors: Ghaffari P.; Bahojb Mahdavi S.; Mokhtarzadeh A.; Memar M.; Pourbagherian O.; Ataei G.; Pouladi N.; Eskandani M.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) as a malignancy that develops in the colon and the rectum, is considered one of the most serious health concerns worldwide, with high prevalence and mortality rates. Probiotics are beneficial bacteria commonly found in the gut and have recently attracted scientific attention, due to their potential to prevent or slow the progression of CRC. Probiotics can break down dietary bioactive compounds, such as polyphenols. These compounds may can promote probiotic characteristics, such as antibacterial and anticancer activities, while preventing disorders like cancer. This study aimed to assess the effects of caffeic acid treatment on Lactobacillus reuteri and to determine the impact of the cell-free supernatants obtained from caffeic acid-treated bacteria (CAF-CFS) on the inhibition of growth and proliferation of colorectal cancer cells (HCT-116) compared with the supernatant of untreated bacteria (CFS). This study aimed to determine the potential effect of caffeic acid treatment on the acid resistance and antibacterial properties of L. reuteri . To achieve this, various assays were conducted, including low pH tolerance, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), and antibiofilm formation assays. Additionally, to evaluate the effect of CAF-CFS on colorectal cancer cell viability, apoptosis induction, and migration suppression, MTT assay, Annexin V-FITC/PI staining, cell cycle, colony formation, and scratch (wound healing) assay were performed. Eventually, the expression levels of genes associated with these pathways were determined using the qRT-PCR technique. The acid tolerance assay results indicated that caffeic acid adapted bacteria exhibited elevated acid tolerance compared to the untreated bacteria. Furthermore, MIC and antibiofilm assays revealed that CFS from caffeic acid-adapted L. reuteri showed a significant antibacterial activity relative to the control. Plus, based on MTT assay results, the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of the supernatant from caffeic acid-treated bacteria was determined to be 95.25% (v/v). At 100% (v/v), CAF-CFS reduced cell viability to approximately 38%, compared with approximately 57% following treatment with CFS. Flow cytometry analysis revealed a significant increase in the apoptotic population in cells exposed to CAF-CFS compared to those treated with standard CFS. CFS treatment increased the hypodiploid sub-G1 population, a finding consistent with DNA fragmentation and apoptotic cell death. additionally, the migratory and colony-forming capacities of CAF-CFS-treated cells were significantly dropped compared to both CFS-treated and untreated groups. Finally, qRT-PCR findings demonstrated that HCT-116 cells treated with CAF-CFS exhibited upregulation of Bax and Caspase-3/9 genes, alongside downregulation of MMP3, MMP9, and Bcl-2 genes compared to cells treated with CFS from non-adapted bacteria. Collectively, these findings confirm that caffeic acid-adapted bacteria exert a more potent anticancer effect than the control group. This study showed that caffeic acid adaptation of L. reuteri enhanced the antibacterial properties of its cell-free supernatant and increased the anticancer activity of CAF-CFS against HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells compared with CFS derived from untreated bacteria.

Article.Title: Community-based implementation and feasibility of portable ophthalmic diagnostic devices: a quasi-experimental pre-post study in underserved areas
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Kim J.; Kim S.; Na K.; Lee S.; Jang W.; Cho K.
Article.Abstract: Portable ophthalmic diagnostic devices have emerged as promising tools to improve access to eye care in underserved communities; however, their agreement with conventional equipment and real-world implementation feasibility remain insufficiently evaluated. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic agreement of two portable ophthalmic devices and their real-world implementation feasibility in an underserved rural community. We conducted a two-phase study consisting of an in-hospital agreement study and a community-based implementation study. In the in-hospital phase, a smartphone-based portable slit lamp (TopSlit) and a handheld all-in-one imaging device (Reticapture) were compared with conventional stationary equipment in 72 patients with ocular diseases. Agreement was assessed using Cohen’s κ, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Spearman’s correlation. In the community-based phase, 124 residents aged ≥ 60 years from 10 underserved rural villages underwent baseline ophthalmic screening and a 6-month follow-up assessment. The primary endpoint was the 30-day hospital-visit completion rate among referred participants; secondary outcomes assessed implementation feasibility and participant acceptability, while longitudinal visual-acuity and patient-reported outcomes were exploratory. TopSlit and Reticapture showed moderate to almost perfect agreement with conventional reference equipment (κ = 0.535–0.944). Among 60 participants referred for further evaluation, the 30-day hospital-visit completion rate was 53.3% (32/60; 95% CI, 40.9–65.4%), exceeding the prespecified 40% feasibility threshold (exact p = 0.047). No upload/network or image-quality failures occurred during field implementation, and no additional image reacquisition or remote-grader requests for additional images were required. Participant satisfaction with the program was high (92.9%). These findings support the feasibility and acceptability of integrating portable ophthalmic devices into a community-based eye-care program in an underserved rural setting. The observed agreement with conventional reference equipment, operational performance, and linkage to follow-up care support further evaluation in larger, rigorously controlled studies. The study was approved by the Dankook University Hospital IRB (DKUH IRB 2022-10-016 (Date of Registration: 2022-10-13; Date of Approval: 2022-11-10) and DKUH IRB 2024-06-016 (Date of Registration: 2024-06-13; Date of Approval: 2024-08-02)). The study was registered at the Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), Republic of Korea ( https://cris.nih.go.kr ; KCT0012177).

Article.Title: Deconvoluting the influence of environmental forcings on chemical weathering rates using machine learning model
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Liu W.; Zhao M.; Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: Quantifying the contributions of silicate and carbonate weathering to global carbon dioxide sequestration is crucial for understanding Earth’s climate regulation mechanisms. In this study, we introduce a framework that integrates explainable machine learning with partial dependence analysis to understand the relationships between environmental forcings and chemical weathering rates. We trained machine learning models on a geochemical dataset from the Tibetan Plateau together with climatic and environmental factors, achieving a weathering model with high predictive ability (R 2 = 0.84–0.96). Furthermore, we separated direct environmental driving effects from indirect mediating effects through systemic partial dependence plots. The results indicate that runoff is the dominant controlling factor of both riverine dissolved SiO 2 and HCO 3 ⁻ flux. Warming promotes riverine HCO 3 ⁻ flux in the river, but its effect on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is bidirectional-first inhibiting, then promoting. Further, our analysis reveals that the effect of precipitation on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is mainly mediated indirectly by runoff. Our study establishes a framework for investigating chemical weathering, highlighting the potential of machine learning to advance predictive modeling and reveal complex interactions between environmental forcings and chemical weathering.

Article.Title: Vaginal microbiota composition, inflammation, and preterm birth vary by HIV status and ethnicity in a UK pregnancy cohort
Article.Authors: Watters E.; Quinlan R.; Smith A.; Ferguson H.; Chrysostomou D.; Marchesi J.; MacIntyre D.; Lee Y.; Campos M.; Storch M.; Bennett P.; Taylor G.; Short C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-diversity, Lactobacillus -dominated vaginal microbiota are associated with immune protection in pregnancy, whereas community state types (CST) III and IV have been linked to inflammation and preterm birth (PTB). Pregnant women living with HIV (PWLWH) in the UK experience higher PTB rates than pregnant women without HIV (PWWH). We previously identified an association between PTB and CSTs III and IV among PWLWH in the UK HIV PTB Network study, but the potential contribution of ethnicity was not examined. Here, we build on these findings through a secondary observational analysis comparing vaginal microbiota composition, inflammation, and PTB outcomes in an expanded cohort of self-identified Black and White PWLWH and PWWH. 105 women (57 Black PWLWH, 14 Black PWWH, 15 White PWLWH, and 19 White PWWH) provided vaginal samples at 20–21 (median) gestational weeks. Twelve women experienced PTB, 10 of whom were Black PWLWH (18.2%). White PWWH had the lowest Chao1 richness and composite genital inflammation (PC1). Associations of HIV status with both Chao1 (β = 39.17, 95% CI 18.65–59.68; p < 0.001) and PC1 (β = 3.80, 95% CI 1.39–6.21; p = 0.003) differed by ethnicity, with higher values observed in White PWLWH compared to White PWWH but little difference among Black women. CSTs III and IV were more prevalent in Black women and White PWLWH, whereas CST I was less frequent. Nearly half of Black PWLWH (49%) underwent a CST transition and were more likely to transition than other subgroups (aOR 2.53, 95% CI 1.02–6.52; p = 0.048). Most PTBs in Black PWLWH occurred in CSTs III or IV, and exploratory analyses suggested an association between CST III-IV transitions and higher odds of PTB (OR 7.75, 95% CI 1.57–42.75; p = 0.01). HIV-associated differences in vaginal microbiota richness and genital inflammation varied by ethnicity, with greater differences observed among White than Black women. Black PWLWH had the highest proportion of PTB, and we identified a potential association between CST III-IV transitions and PTB. The observed differences may reflect unmeasured social or structural factors, while the potential contribution of CST dynamics to PTB warrants investigation in larger cohorts.

Article.Title: Well-being and body-related insecurity are associated with cycling status in anabolic-androgenic steroid users
Article.Authors: Bjørnebekk A.; Kaźmierowska A.; Juel J.; Thorsby P.; Scarth M.
Article.Abstract: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with adverse psychological outcomes, yet little is known about how psychological functioning varies across on- and off-cycle phases within individuals. Adult male AAS users ( n = 19) and weightlifting controls (WLC; n = 25) completed biweekly assessments of well-being (WHO-5), psychological distress (HSCL-10), and ten AAS-related symptoms over 6 months. AAS observations were classified as on-cycle (≤ 21 days since last use) or off-cycle (> 21 days), with hormonal measures available in a subset. Exploratory analyses indicated several phase-related differences, with the most consistent findings showing greater body-related insecurity (“feeling small”) and lower well-being during off-cycle periods. These patterns were also supported by within-subject sensitivity analyses, although only 10 participants contributed observations from both phases. Higher anxiety scores were also found in both on- and off-cycle AAS observations than in WLC observations, with no statistically significant difference between cycle phases. Other findings included higher levels of paranoid thoughts and depressive symptoms during off-cycle periods, but these were less consistent across analyses. Little evidence was found for cycle-related changes in impulsivity, irritability, or short temper. These preliminary findings require replication in larger samples.

Article.Title: Primal–dual interior point strategy based parameter identification method for serial industrial robots
Article.Authors: Wan J.; Wu L.; Zhou Z.; He W.; Liu X.; Wang T.
Article.Abstract: To accurately identify robot dynamics parameters and improve control performance, this paper proposes a full-parameter identification method based on primal–dual interior-point optimization (FPI-PDIP). Firstly, linearization of the robot dynamics equation combined with QR decomposition is adopted to extract the minimal set of inertial parameters (MSIP). Physical feasibility constraints are constructed according to the intrinsic physical characteristics of inertial parameters, transforming the identification task into a constrained optimization problem solved via the primal–dual interior-point method to acquire physically feasible full dynamics parameters. Optimized Fourier-series excitation trajectories and second-order Butterworth filtering are adopted to guarantee high-quality measurement data. The performance of FPI-PDIP is verified through simulations on a 7-Degree-of-Freedom (7-DOF) manipulator and physical experiments on a SCARA robot. Compared with the conventional MSIP scheme, the mean root-mean-square-error (Mean RMSE) of joint torque estimation is reduced by 46.09% across four joints of the 7-DOF robot in simulation. For the two joints of the SCARA robot, the joint-averaged Mean RMSE decreases by 53.59% on identification trajectories and 40.85% on unseen validation trajectories. The results verify the high accuracy and favorable generalization performance of the proposed FPI-PDIP method for robot dynamics feedforward control.

Article.Title: Pangenome-based design of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Streptococcus pasteurianus with computational evaluation of TLR1–TLR2 interaction
Article.Authors: Aljohani W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Streptococcus pasteurianus is an emerging pathogen causing severe hospital and community-acquired infections. However, there is currently no vaccine, prompting the need for new vaccine strategies. Here, we used a systematic computational workflow combining pangenome analysis, subtractive proteomics, immunoinformatics and molecular dynamics to develop a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) targeting common antigenic epitopes among different strains of S. pasteurianus . Pangenome analysis of 11 strains identified 1,436 core gene clusters (34.2%) conserved within the 11 genomes analyzed. Subtractive proteomics analysis yielded three predicted candidate proteins, DisA, FtsX and FtsW, based on essentiality, limited human sequence similarity and predicted antigenicity; their native surface accessibility remains unconfirmed. Computational epitope prediction identified six cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), four helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and three linear B-cell (LBL) epitopes from these proteins with high antigenicity and immunogenicity. The 344-amino acid multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) design, comprising the Mycobacterium tuberculosis L7/L12 adjuvant and peptide linkers, exhibited enhanced stability and physicochemical characteristics. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations a putative interaction between the MEV and a TLR1–TLR2 ectodomain model derived from PDB 2Z7X; the contact-based predicted was 1.3 × 10⁻²⁴ M, and MM/PBSA binding free energies were − 32.15 and − 16.83 kcal/mol for Replicates 1 and 2, respectively, consistent with a favorable predicted interaction. These computational findings provide a structural basis for further experimental investigation of the proposed vaccine construct. Structural stability was assessed using two independent 100 ns molecular dynamics replicates (200 ns aggregate), and the energetics of the predicted complex were further evaluated using MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations. In silico population coverage analysis estimated 76.87% global population coverage across various geographical and ethnic groups. In silico immune analysis predicted humoral and cellular immune-response patterns, with increased IgG antibody response, prolonged cytokine secretion (IFN-γ and IL-2) and generation of memory cells. Optimized gene sequence and in silico cloning into the pET28a(+) vector provided a proposed construct for experimental expression testing in Escherichia coli. This in silico study presents a computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidate against S. pasteurianus that requires experimental evaluation before any conclusions about immunogenicity or protection.

Article.Title: Influence of charged micrometer-sized particles on the breakdown voltage of air gaps
Article.Authors: Töpper H.; Reding J.; Franck C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Micrometer-sized particles are ubiquitously present and can reduce the breakdown voltage of high-voltage gas insulations by several tens of percent. Despite this influence, a quantitative and mechanistic understanding of how particles determine both the probability and severity of a breakdown is missing. To address this, the breakdown voltage reduction caused by micrometer-sized dielectric $$\hbox {SnO}_{2}$$ particles in a uniform DC ambient air gap is measured and modeled. The experiments cover diameters ranging from $${1}$$ to $${170}\,\upmu \text {m}$$ . High-speed macro imaging reveals that the breakdown initiation coincides with a single charged particle approaching an electrode to within approximately $${20}$$ to $${110}\,\upmu \text {m}$$ . This occurs for positive and negative particle charges with magnitudes between 130 and 1170 fC. Across the diameters, the breakdown probability increases from 80 to 100%. The mean breakdown voltage reduction increases linearly with the particle diameter from approximately 5 to 28% at approximately $${-19.4} \,\hbox {V }{\upmu }\hbox {m}^{-1}$$ . Outliers are observed to double the breakdown voltage reduction. Increasing the particle number from one to higher quantities raises the likelihood of a breakdown but does not significantly change the worst-case breakdown voltages. Based on a weakest-link distribution scaling, the influence of higher particle quantities is shown to be predictable. Thereby, the system-specific critical particle diameter falls in the range between $${15}$$ and $${54}\,\upmu \text {m}$$ . The analytical field distortion calculations demonstrate that the charge dominates the magnitude and spatial extent of the field enhancement. Based on this, a developed streamer integral-based model accounting for the measured charge magnitude, polarity, and particle position during the initiation is evaluated to determine if it can reproduce the experiments. This shows that the particle chargemagnitude cannot be directly mapped to the breakdown voltage reduction without considering the particle-to-electrode distance during the breakdown initiation. Additionally, the significance of the spatial position of the charge on the particle surface is demonstrated based on assumed distributions. Collectively, this provides statistical and charge-resolved breakdown data within a mechanistic framework that can serve as a baseline for quantifying the potential influence of particles on gas insulation systems

Article.Title: Reinforcement learning enables autonomous microrobot navigation and intervention in simulated blood capillaries
Article.Authors: Drotleff J.; Hohenberger P.; Tovey S.; Lohrmann C.; Hoßbach J.; Nikolaou K.; Holm C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autonomous microrobots navigating biological vasculature could enable targeted drug delivery and thrombolysis, yet training control policies for physiologically complex environments remains an open challenge. Prior reinforcement learning (RL) studies of microrobotic navigation have largely used idealized geometries lacking realistic flow in confined branching, and dense cellular obstacles. Here, we develop a physically grounded, deliberately idealized two-dimensional capillary simulation, with resolved flow fields, explicit red blood cell dynamics, and schematic-derived branching geometry, training RL agents via an advection-dominated concentration field driven by physiological flow speeds. Mapping success across robot size and swimming speed, we show via zero-shot transfer that most training failures reflect optimization limits, not physical ones. A policy transferred from a more demanding condition succeeds far beyond where per-combination training converges. Its eventual collapse offers a tentative lower bound on what is physically achievable. Successful agents converge on Run-and-Rotate strategies. The transferred policy, a variant of this family, shows a distinctive profile, that we believe is responsible for its exceptional transfer success. Without retraining, these agents perform targeted blocking and unblocking of individual vessel branches, restoring red blood cell passage toward baseline levels and suggesting RL as a viable framework for microrobotic intervention in biological networks.

Article.Title: Condition-specific seasonal rhythms in pediatric emergencies
Article.Authors: Tachinardi P.; Witt R.; Wu G.; Paulose J.; Wong H.; Dribin T.; Mendonca E.; Smith D.; Hogenesch J.; Ruben M.
Article.Abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) see patients for nearly every kind of medical concern, prompting efforts to understand when and why people seek care. Total ED volume predictably varies by hour, day, and season, but such summaries can obscure how specific or co-occurring conditions drive demand. We analyzed 1.5 million pediatric ED and urgent care visits from 2010 to 2021 at a major children’s hospital in Ohio, a region with four distinct seasons. Most chief complaints (CCs, 80%) showed clear seasonal rhythms, though peak timing varied widely by condition. Psychiatric emergencies, identified as a national crisis by the American Academy of Pediatrics, had some of the largest seasonal swings, peaking in spring and fall. ICD-10 profiles revealed subgroups within CCs that differed in seasonal timing, suggesting diverse underlying drivers. Condition-specific weekly patterns also emerged, compounding seasonal effects and carrying implications for staffing and care. Psychiatric visits, for instance, were 70% higher in October than in June—but 220% higher on Mondays in October than on Saturdays in June, a pattern consistent over ten years. Parallel data from Brazil, with different environmental and social seasons, showed regional contrasts in ED use, including psychiatric cases. Seasonal influences on pediatric emergency care are common, condition-specific, and regionally variable, underscoring the need to account for them in health system planning and etiologic research.

Article.Title: Design and evaluation of pregnant women’s waiting area chairs using an integrated user-need-driven framework
Article.Authors: Li C.; Suhaily S.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Most existing waiting area chairs for pregnant women adopt the form of general public seating and fail to fully meet the special needs of pregnant women. To develop waiting chairs that better address pregnant women’s needs, this study applied an integrated user-need-centred design and evaluation framework. A user journey map was first used to identify key behavioural nodes, experience pain points, and latent needs of pregnant women during antenatal examination waiting. The Kano model was then applied to analyse 427 valid questionnaires and clarify the roles of different design attributes in shaping user satisfaction. On this basis, experts in relevant fields were invited to use the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to calculate the weights of demand indicators. Quality Function Deployment (QFD) was then used to translate user needs into actionable product technical characteristics. Subsequently, Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation (FCE) was used to compare three preliminary design schemes and select the scheme with the highest score for further refinement. A questionnaire developed with reference to QUEST was then used to compare participants’ perceptions of the selected scheme and existing waiting chairs. The results showed that “assisted rising support” had the highest weight in the AHP analysis, indicating that the design of pregnant women’s waiting area chairs should extend from static sitting comfort to body support and safety assistance throughout the process of sitting down, waiting, posture adjustment, and rising. The QFD analysis further indicated that assisted seat lifting, integrated lumbar and back support, anti-slip structure, and stable assembly were key technical characteristics. The user evaluation results showed that the proposed scheme received higher mean ratings for comfort, safety, practicality, and aesthetics than the sofa and metal waiting chairs. This study clarified the relative importance of pregnant women’s seating needs and the corresponding design priorities, and illustrated their application in the functional and structural design of the proposed scheme. The findings offer a reference for the design and improvement of seating in obstetric waiting areas.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of SOC estimation methods for lithium-ion batteries in industrial electric forklift applications: experimental and simulation-based study
Article.Authors: Doğan H.; Demirci O.; Taskın S.; Schaltz E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for the safe, efficient, and reliable operation of lithium-ion batteries in industrial electric forklifts. Although numerous SOC estimation methods have been investigated for electric vehicle (EV) applications, their comparative performance under realistic forklift duty cycles remains insufficiently studied. Industrial electric forklifts are characterized by repetitive start-stop operation, abrupt load variations associated with acceleration and lifting, regenerative braking, and limited rest periods, which pose significant challenges for accurate real-time SOC estimation. Therefore, this study presents a systematic experimental and simulation-based evaluation of SOC estimation techniques. Field tests were conducted on an industrial electric forklift equipped with a 51.2 V, 554 Ah lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and operated according to the VDI 2198 duty cycle. In parallel, MATLAB/Simulink models were developed using equivalent-circuit parameters identified through Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC) tests. Open Circuit Voltage (OCV) and Coulomb Counting (CC) were considered as baseline SOC estimation approaches, while Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), and Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (AEKF) were evaluated using dynamic current profiles. Although CC closely followed the reference SOC under controlled C5 test conditions, its practical applicability remains sensitive to initial SOC uncertainty, cumulative current measurement errors, and capacity variations. Among the evaluated model-based approaches, the UKF provided the closest agreement with the reference SOC under real-world forklift operation, achieving an MAE of 0.852%, an RMSE of 1.070%, and a MAPE of 1.719%. The findings demonstrate that nonlinear model-based SOC estimation methods, particularly the UKF, can provide consistent SOC tracking under the dynamic load conditions encountered in industrial forklift applications.

Article.Title: Isolation and characterization of a lytic bacteriophage from wastewater source targeting Escherichia coli isolated from meat specimens
Article.Authors: Asadi N.; Mirshahabi H.; Afshar D.
Article.Abstract: In the present study, a lytic bacteriophage specific to Escherichia coli was isolated from wastewater, and its activity against E. coli isolates obtained from raw meat was investigated. A total of 60 raw meat swab samples were collected from butcher shops in Zanjan Province, Iran. The presence of β-lactamase genes, including bla TEM, bla SHV, and blaCTX-M, was examined using multiplex PCR. Bacteriophage isolation was performed using E. coli ATCC 25,922 as the host strain. Of the 60 samples, 37 (61.7%) were positive for E. coli . The highest resistance rates were observed against tetracycline (59.5%), trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole (57.0%), and amoxicillin (57.0%). Among the resistance genes, blaTEM was the most frequently detected (27.0%), followed by bla CTX-M and bla SHV. The isolated bacteriophage had an icosahedral head and a short, non-contractile tail. The phage remained active at temperatures ranging from − 20 °C to 55 °C but was completely inactivated at 65 °C. The detection of β-lactamase genes and antibiotic resistance among E. coli isolates from raw meat indicates a potential public health risk. he isolated bacteriophage exhibited lytic activity against 54.1% of the E. coli isolates, indicating its preliminary potential as a biocontrol agent against antibiotic-resistant E. coli in meat products. However, further studies, including evaluations in food matrices, are required to assess its practical applicability.

Article.Title: Memory-enhanced artificial rabbits optimization for solving global optimization and feature selection
Article.Authors: Shi R.
Article.Abstract: Modern artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly challenged by high-dimensional and multimodal data streams, which exacerbate the curse of dimensionality and significantly increase the difficulty of feature selection. To address the limitations of the original Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) algorithm—such as insufficient population diversity, loss of high-quality historical solutions, inadequate local search accuracy, and susceptibility to premature convergence—this paper proposes a Memory-enhanced Artificial Rabbits Optimization (MARO) algorithm. The proposed method incorporates an individual memory archive mechanism, an adaptive differential evolution operator, and a directed local search strategy, thereby effectively balancing global exploration and local exploitation. Furthermore, MARO is integrated with the K-nearest neighbor (KNN) classifier to construct a wrapper-based feature selection framework, termed MARO-KNN. Experimental results on the CEC2017 benchmark functions under 30- and 100-dimensional settings show that MARO achieves Friedman mean ranks of 1.40 and 1.20, respectively, significantly outperforming eight mainstream optimization algorithms, including GWO, PSO, and the original ARO. In feature selection experiments conducted on 22 publicly available datasets of varying scales, MARO-KNN attains an average rank of 2.83 in classification accuracy and 2.67 in the number of selected features, both ranking first. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework not only achieves superior overall performance, but also realizes optimal feature dimensionality reduction. Overall, MARO exhibits clear advantages in convergence speed, solution accuracy, and stability, providing an efficient and robust approach for complex high-dimensional global optimization and feature selection tasks.

Article.Title: WUSCHEL emerges as a promising molecular marker of in vitro regeneration competence across diverse poinsettia cultivars
Article.Authors: Davoudi Pahnekolayi M.; Schmidt V.; Boehm R.; Sprink T.; Halbwirth H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In vitro regeneration of poinsettia ( Euphorbia pulcherrima ) is strongly genotype-dependent, limiting the efficiency and reproducibility of tissue culture and its biotechnological applications. This study investigated whether regeneration-associated transcription factor expression in stock plants correlates with subsequent regeneration competence across ten poinsettia cultivars. We evaluated EpWUS, EpWIND1 , EpSTM , and EpCYCD expression in stock plants and during direct organogenesis and somatic embryogenesis in relation to regenerated shoot number, shoot regeneration percentage, and developed shoot length. EpWUS showed the most consistent association with regeneration performance across the two regeneration systems. Cultivar-dependent differences in EpWUS expression were already evident in stock plants before regeneration was initiated, and cultivars with relatively high basal EpWUS expression generally exhibited stronger regeneration responses. The association between EpWUS expression and regeneration performance was further supported by correlation analyses across both regeneration systems. In contrast, the expression patterns of EpWIND1 , EpSTM , and EpCYCD showed less consistent relationships with regeneration efficiency. These findings support EpWUS as a candidate molecular marker associated with regeneration competence in poinsettia. However, independent validation and functional studies are required to establish its predictive utility and mechanistic role. The findings provide a basis for developing molecular approaches to improve genotype selection for poinsettia tissue culture and biotechnology.

Article.Authors: Elbanna A.; Nasser B.; Saraya M.; Eraky M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) shares computation, memory, sensing, and middleware resources with other robotic perception tasks. This study evaluates Cartographer and RTAB-Map in ROS 2 Humble/Gazebo using a TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi, both alone and while a separate YOLOv8n object-detection node runs concurrently on the CPU. Ten runs were analyzed per configuration (40 runs total). Independent Gazebo ground truth and TF-derived SLAM trajectories were converted to planar x-y-yaw TUM trajectories, associated within 20 ms, and evaluated using translation and yaw absolute pose error (APE) and 1 m relative pose error (RPE). Baseline translation APE RMSE was 0.030965 ± 0.007947 m for Cartographer and 0.014013 ± 0.003691 m for RTAB-Map; corresponding translation RPE RMSE was 0.017614 ± 0.002281 m and 0.006209 ± 0.001787 m. With concurrent YOLOv8n, translation APE RMSE was 0.031711 ± 0.007119 m and 0.017177 ± 0.007964 m, respectively. Combined monitored process CPU reached 670.491 ± 15.741% and 624.513 ± 12.703%, while Gazebo real-time factor remained near 1.0. Because the groups were independently teleoperated, baseline-to-YOLO differences are interpreted descriptively rather than causally. The workflow integrates repeated-run localization accuracy, orientation error, resource profiling, and motion characterization under documented simulation conditions.

Article.Title: Intra-operative differentiation of benign and malignant thyroid nodules using diffuse reflectance spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Chander N.; Ranjitkar R.; Gkouzionis I.; Giot M.; Nazarian S.; Moonim M.; Flora R.; Mukhopadhyay S.; Palazzo F.; Tolley N.; Darzi A.; Peters C.; Elson D.; Di Marco A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Thyroid nodules are common, yet distinguishing benign from malignant nodules is a challenge. With current diagnostics, 39–52% of nodules are characterised as indeterminate, often necessitating diagnostic surgery to achieve a histological diagnosis. Depending on outcome, this may represent over- or under-treatment. The aim of this study was to determine whether diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) can accurately differentiate benign from malignant thyroid nodules. In this prospective study, spectral data were collected intra-operatively from freshly resected ex vivo thyroid nodules using a handheld DRS probe; results were validated against histopathological analysis as the gold standard for comparison. Binary classification was performed using the extreme gradient boosting supervised machine learning classifier. Data were divided into training and testing sets with a stratified 5-fold cross-validation method, and model performance evaluated for key statistical features. Our study revealed that for nodules deemed benign or malignant on pre-operative imaging/cytology, DRS identified malignancy with a diagnostic accuracy of 87.9%, sensitivity of 88.3%, specificity of 87.4% and positive predictive value (PPV) for malignancy of 88.0%. In pre-operatively indeterminate nodules, the diagnostic accuracy was 89.0%, sensitivity 79.9%, specificity 93.3% and PPV 85.4%. These findings highlight the potential of DRS in assessing indeterminate thyroid nodules, where its performance exceeds that of current image-guided cytological analysis (where the PPV ranges from 17 to 68%). This study therefore provides justification for further work exploring modification of the DRS system for pre-operative use, in order to support decision-making for indeterminate nodules and reduce unnecessary surgery.

Article.Title: Association between cerebral microstructure and cognitive decline in patients with hypertension
Article.Authors: Hung T.; Chen V.; Chen H.; Hsu Y.; Tsai Y.; Chang Y.; Weng J.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension (HTN) represents an escalating global public health concern and is recognized as a major contributor to cognitive impairment. It has been identified as a significant risk factor for cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and dementia. Nevertheless, previous research has yielded inconsistent findings, and the specific relationships among various cognitive domains and alterations in gray matter volume remain insufficiently understood. The present study employs brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to investigate structural brain changes associated with the relationship between hypertension and cognitive impairment. A total of fifty-eight participants were recruited and categorized into two groups: patients with hypertension and a normotensive control (NC) group. All participants were subject to a brain MRI and cognitive questionnaires; CVVLT, DSS, TMT-A, TMT-B, CGUOFT, MMSE and MoCA were used to measure the cognitive state. Voxel-based morphometry and vertex-wise shape analyses were used to determine differences in the volume and shape of the brain for the HTN group and the NC group. Multiple regression was used to determine the association between gray matter volume and the results of the cognitive assessments, in terms of memory, executive function, and global cognitive function. The HTN group has a larger gray matter volume in the middle frontal gyrus, the precentral gyrus, the insula, the amygdala and the cingulate gyrus and the HTN group has a smaller gray matter volume in the fusiform gyrus. In terms of memory function, there is a positive correlation with the hippocampus, the parahippocampal gyrus, the inferior parietal lobule, the brainstem and the anterior cingulate. In terms of executive function, there is a positive correlation with the middle frontal gyrus, the inferior frontal gyrus and the insula and a negative correlation with the medial frontal gyrus, the cingulate gyrus and the hippocampus. In terms of global cognitive function, there is a positive correlation with the thalamus, the caudate, the lentiform nucleus, the precuneus, the insula and the superior frontal gyrus. These findings contribute to our understanding of the structural and cognitive alterations associated with hypertension and may inform future studies of cognitive interventions in patients with hypertension.

Article.Title: On the role of water and humidity in the dry strength of paper and fiber-fiber bonds
Article.Authors: Gaspar Simoes M.; Mautner A.; Hirn U.; Schennach R.
Article.Abstract: Paper strength is known to increase as water is removed, typically attributed to fiber stiffness. However, whether inter-fiber contact/bonding linked to capillary bridges (CapB) and Laplace pressure (LP) also contributes to this strength gain during drying remains unclear. Theoretically, paper strength should peak before CapB collapses during drying. This study aims to clarify the roles of fiber stiffness and CapB in paper strength. To that end, the mechanical properties of untreated, unsized paper made from bleached hardwood pulp with 17% PCC filler were tested across different temperatures and relative humidity (RH), extending to extreme dryness (0% RH, 120 °C). At 27 °C, strength, stiffness, and E-modulus rose as RH decreased to 10%, then apparently plateaued between 10% and 0% RH. Notably, even at 0% RH and 120 °C, the paper still absorbed some water. To explain the mechanisms behind these results, we evaluated several possible scenarios. Based on this analysis, a new hypothesis is proposed: increased paper strength during drying results from a combination of Laplace pressure and adhesion forces, driven by inter-fiber molecular contact/bonding area, together with fiber stiffness. However, the experiments could not confirm or rule out a contribution from capillary bridges to paper dry strength.

Article.Abstract: Deep learning (DL)–based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detection has emerged as a promising technique for future wireless communication systems. To address the prohibitive computational cost associated with collecting soft-information training labels, a computationally efficient recursive label generation method is employed. The proposed framework demonstrates strong generalization capability, as it is trained at a single signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and evaluated over a wide range of SNR values. In addition, its generalization capability and scalability are validated across various antenna configurations and modulation orders. Simulation results show that the proposed method significantly improves bit error rate (BER) performance, achieving near–maximum-likelihood (ML) performance for coded MIMO systems while maintaining excellent generalization performance.

Article.Authors: Liu J.; Ge Y.; Wu Z.
Article.Abstract: Incomplete wetland-park inventories can limit spatial assessments of urban blue–green infrastructure. Standard deviational ellipses characterized directional structure, nearest-neighbor analysis assessed departures from a specified complete-spatial-randomness reference, and GeoDetector examined spatial correspondence with river density, slope, road density, and population density. The primary subsets showed broadly east–west orientations and an 8.26-km difference between their mean centres. Article.Authors: Du X.; Zhang T.; Shu P.; Yuchi X.; Song J.; Jiang S.; Wu G.; Bian H.; Guo F.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the effects of pressure-relief mining of the protective seam at different burial depths on the mechanical behavior and damage of the proximate protected coal seam, unloading experiments were conducted on coal specimens under various initial confining pressures, simulating the synchronous unloading of axial stress and confining pressure. Moreover, increasing the initial confining pressure significantly enhances the maximum and cumulative AE ringing counts, and the growth rate accelerates progressively. Article.Abstract: Abstract Whistler-mode waves can be guided along the ambient magnetic field by field-aligned irregularities in plasma density, magnetic-field strength, or both. Article.Authors: Choi S.; Jang H.; Lee S.; Ku S.; Kang D.; Jo S.; Jung S.; Kim C.; Lee Y.; Han Y.; Jo Y.

Article.Authors: Morrell J.; Barriere P.; Gesbert A.; Reigner F.; Laskowski D.; Ntallaris T.; Deleuze S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stringent efforts are required to stem the development of antimicrobial resistance, especially by avoiding non-therapeutic applications of antibiotics. The conception rates were not statistically different, being 19/23 for controls with antibiotics and 18/23 for Equicoll samples without antibiotics ( p = 0.71). Article.Authors: Naghnaghia S.; Darwaze M.; Hanani A.

These findings suggest a substantial burden of PTSD among Palestinian healthcare trainees and physicians during conflict and indicate that cumulative exposure to stressors may be linked to increased vulnerability. The findings also point to a potential role for individual personality traits, particularly neuroticism, in relation to trauma-related symptoms. Interventions aimed at strengthening resilience and adaptive coping strategies may help mitigate the mental health impact in this population.

These findings suggest that systemic [ 177 Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 PTRT is safe and effective for brain metastases in FAP-expressing advanced lung cancer, achieving intracranial tumor regression, symptom relief, and improved quality of life, thereby offering a promising therapeutic option for this refractory population.

Moreover, GeoShapley revealed pronounced spatial effects and GEO–feature interactions, indicating that the magnitude and direction of driver contributions varied across spatial locations. Article.Authors: Hakimi M.; Hatem B.; Mustapha K.; Kumar A.; Naseem W.; Alqudah M.; Nurgaliev D.; Gardezi S.; Lashin A.
Article.Abstract: This study integrates multi-scale organic geochemical and elemental composition analyses, along with microscopic observations of organic-rich shale (ORS) sediments of the Late Jurassic Shuqra Formation (SF) in the Say’un–Masilah Basin (SMB), and was designed to appraise past climate and redox conditions and their impact on organic carbon accumulation and preservation. The presence of sulfide mineral (FeS) in framboidal pyrite form associated with OM is consistent with low-oxygenated conditions, as the sulphidation of iron forms it. However, the framboidal pyrite shows a range of sizes from more than 50 µ to less than 5µ, suggesting depositional conditions from oxic to anoxic (dysoxic). The biomarker markers provide evidence of mainly marine OM input, with low amounts of a terrigenous land plant during the deposition time of the Shuqra shale sediments. The dominance of marine-derived material is supported by the abundant occurrence of alginite macerals, particularly lamalginite and telalginite algae, as identified through reflected light microscopy. Additionally, paleoclimatic indicators indicate that warm and humid climates dominated during the accumulation period of the Shuqra shale sediments. These warm-water and humid climatic conditions promoted eutrophication, enhancing subaerial weathering and nutrient influx, which in turn increased marine primary productivity within the photic zone. As a result, the combination of bioproductivity and efficient preservation led to significant OM enrichment in the Shuqra shale facies throughout deposition.

Article.Authors: Toichi Y.; Okuda R.; Yoshimura K.; Yamamoto I.; Terakawa S.; Sakamoto K.

The other one, which does not exhibit $$k_{z}$$ dispersion and does not appear in the theoretical bulk band structure, was revealed to be a surface state from slab calculations. Article.Authors: Yu C.; Stewart R.; Chen J.

Our findings indicate that depressive symptoms independently increase the risk of chronic disease onset, especially multimorbidity and specific disease types, as well as the burden of healthcare costs, underscoring the importance of integrating mental health screening into primary care and chronic disease prevention strategies for community‑dwelling middle‑aged and older adults, including those with subclinical depressive symptoms who have not received a formal psychiatric diagnosis.

While Markov models have been extensively studied for several cache replacement policies, analytical models for frequency-based caching remain limited. This paper develops a Markov-chain framework for the Perfect Least Frequently Used (PLFU) caching algorithm. We show that, under a strictly ordered popularity distribution for a catalog of N objects and a cache of capacity n , empirical request frequencies eventually separate, reducing the relevant cache state space from \(\left( {\begin{array}{c}N\\ n\end{array}}\right) \) configurations to only \(N-n+1\) states. The resulting reduced Markov model admits a closed-form stationary distribution and enables direct computation of per-object and aggregate miss probabilities. We further characterize the transition to this reduced representation through finite-time ranking-recovery bounds, a persistent stabilization bound, and Monte Carlo estimates. The analytical results are evaluated using synthetic IRM workloads and chronological real-world request traces. Finally, a three-level PLFU cache hierarchy is considered to assess the applicability of the model beyond the single-cache request setting. Although the request streams at higher cache levels are cache-filtered and therefore do not generally satisfy the IRM assumption, the recursively applied model remains close to request-level simulations, with aggregate miss-probability differences below 0.5 percentage points in the considered experiments. The results provide an analytically tractable framework for estimating PLFU cache hit/miss behavior in the single-cache setting and indicate its potential as an approximation for the cache hierarchy considered here.

Article.Title: Read-reference voltage adaptation for 3D NAND flash memory via RBER-aware few-shot transfer learning
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Meng S.; Hu H.
Article.Abstract: Program/erase (P/E) cycling and retention drift alter the threshold-voltage distributions of 3D NAND flash, causing previously calibrated read-reference voltages to become mismatched to new operating conditions. To update read references when target measurements are limited, we propose a raw bit error rate (RBER)-aware few-shot transfer framework that adapts a Gaussian-parameter predictor from a single characterized source condition without requiring a pre-calibrated multi-condition voltage grid. The predictor is pretrained on source measurements and fine-tuned using a small set of target records, with mean squared error (MSE) as the parameter-training objective. Candidate checkpoints are selected using a restricted RBER metric over the measured programmed-state boundaries, aligning model selection with read-reference quality. Experiments on measurements collected from 3D NAND flash cover six target conditions and five random seeds, accounting for both training and validation measurements. With a total budget of two target wordlines, the proposed framework achieves an average reduction of 83.0% in the evaluated RBER relative to the evaluated training-from-scratch configuration (95% confidence interval 67.2–98.8%). In a paired experiment using 32 target training records and 13 validation wordlines, RBER-based checkpoint selection reduces RBER by 42.1% compared with MSE-based selection on the same fine-tuning trajectories (95% confidence interval 34.7–49.5%). Target-wordline interpolation achieves lower mean restricted RBER than the proposed framework in all 24 matched-budget comparisons. The checkpoint-selection benefit therefore concerns improvement within the learned framework, while direct interpolation provides higher accuracy under the tested budgets. By combining source-model reuse with RBER-based checkpoint selection, the proposed framework enables read-reference voltages to be adapted to changing P/E and retention conditions using limited target measurements.

Article.Title: Empathy and compassion are comparable between individuals with cervical spinal cord injury and controls, but their association with interoceptive sensibility differs
Article.Authors: Vergara A.; Blanco-Madariaga K.; Recart E.; Baquedano-Larraín C.; Martínez-Pernía D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The extent to which empathic and compassionate processes depend on bodily signaling remains a central and unresolved question in affective neuroscience. Although converging evidence suggests that empathy and compassion are shaped by bodily dynamics, it remains unclear how these processes are expressed when spinal body–brain signaling is extensively and chronically disrupted. We examined individuals with chronic cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI; n = 30) and healthy controls ( n = 27) to determine whether chronic disruption of spinal bodily signaling is associated with differences in self-reported empathic and compassionate dispositions and interoceptive sensibility, and whether the associations of interoceptive sensibility with empathy-related dimensions and compassion differ according to injury status. Participants completed the Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI), Compassion Scale, and MAIA-2, and Bayesian regression models adjusted for age, affective symptoms, alexithymia, and perceived social support. No credible group differences emerged in the total or subscale scores of the IRI, Compassion Scale, or MAIA-2. Bayes-factor comparisons for the total scores favored models without group effects for the IRI (BF₀₁ = 3.43), Compassion Scale (BF₀₁ = 2.42), and MAIA-2 (BF₀₁ = 2.66), although the evidence was weak to moderate. Despite these broadly comparable self-reported profiles, the association between interoceptive sensibility and compassion differed by injury status. Greater interoceptive sensibility was strongly associated with greater compassion in controls, whereas this association was credibly weaker in cSCI. Together, these findings indicate that chronic disruption of spinal bodily signaling is not necessarily accompanied by differences in self-reported empathic and compassionate dispositions, but may be associated with differences in how interoceptive sensibility relates to compassion.

Article.Title: Psychological correlates of compassion fatigue among pediatric healthcare professionals in Isfahan
Article.Authors: Pakdaman N.; Naghavi A.; Samiee F.; Kalhor F.
Article.Abstract: Paediatric healthcare professionals are exposed to chronic traumatic stressors that increase the risk of compassion fatigue (CF). Despite its impact on workforce stability, the relationship between CF, moral distress, and work engagement—specifically whether engagement serves as a protective factor—remains under-examined in Isfahan context (located in Iran). This study aimed to identify the predictors of CF among paediatric staff in Isfahan. A descriptive-correlational study was conducted with 123 healthcare staff recruited from three tertiary public hospitals in Isfahan, Iran, in 2023. Hospitals with paediatric wards were recruited using convenience sampling. Participants completed the Moral Distress Scale-Revised (MDS-R), Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9), DASS-21, the Persian version of the Compassion Fatigue scale, and a demographic questionnaire. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods, including Pearson correlations and stepwise multiple regression, using SPSS version 25. A total of 123 participants, including nurses, medical interns, and paediatric residents, were recruited using convenience sampling. Compassion fatigue was significantly positively correlated with moral distress (r = 0.193), depression (r = 0.254), anxiety (r = 0.285), and stress (r = 0.341). No significant correlation was found between CF and work engagement. Stepwise regression identified perceived stress as the sole significant predictor of CF, explaining 11.6% of the variance (β = 0.34, p < 0.001). Compassion fatigue among paediatric healthcare staff was associated with moral distress and psychological symptoms, with perceived stress emerging as the strongest predictor in the regression model. Work engagement was not significantly associated with CF in this sample. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal relationships. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that interventions addressing perceived stress and sources of moral distress may be relevant to efforts to reduce compassion fatigue among paediatric healthcare professionals.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic responses associated with heat resilience in beef cattle
Article.Authors: Rodriguez E.; Beard A.; Rojas C.; Zayas G.; Rafiq F.; Mateescu R.; Rezende F.
Article.Abstract: Heat stress is a major limitation to beef cattle production, particularly in subtropical and tropical regions where rising temperatures can negatively impact animal performance and health. This study investigated the transcriptomic basis of thermotolerance in Brangus beef cattle using integrated phenotypic and transcriptomic approaches. Cattle were classified as thermotolerant (T) or non-thermotolerant (N) based on core body temperature responses to changes in temperature-humidity index. Blood samples were collected under hot (day 1) and cool (day 2) environmental conditions, and RNA sequencing was performed to evaluate differential gene expression. The repeated-measures experimental design revealed differences in transcriptional responses between groups, with fewer differentially expressed genes between hot and cool conditions in thermotolerant than in non-thermotolerant animals. Several candidate genes had reported functions related to oxidative stress response, immune regulation, extracellular matrix organization, metabolism, and cellular homeostasis, indicating that the transcriptional differences associated with thermotolerance involved genes with diverse biological functions. Among the candidate genes identified, MFAP5 (log 2 FC = 2.26, P = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ in N1_N2; log 2 FC = − 1.94, P = 1.9 × 10⁻³ in T1_N1) and NOVA1 (log 2 FC = 2.25, P = 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ in N1_N2; log 2 FC = − 2.07, P = 3.5 × 10⁻⁴ in T1_N1) showed relatively large expression differences in both within- and between-thermotolerance-group contrasts. Overall, these findings provide further insight into the transcriptomic basis of heat resilience in beef cattle and identify candidate genes for further investigation and potential use in genetic strategies to improve thermotolerance.

Article.Title: A multi-objective UAV path planning model for power transmission tower inspection
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zhang L.; Tang J.; Dai Z.; Zhang R.
Article.Abstract: Although unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have been widely applied in transmission line inspections, flight path planning for the detailed inspection of individual transmission towers remains underexplored, particularly regarding 3D structural modeling, the coupling between image quality and path planning, and constraint handling. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a multi-objective UAV flight path planning model for detailed single-tower inspection. With the objectives of minimizing flight distance and maximizing image quality, the model adaptively adjusts the inspection radius and layer heights and carries out comprehensive inspection of the tower and the crossarm. Four multi-objective evolutionary algorithms were applied to solve the model. The results indicate that NSGA-III performs optimally, achieving full tower coverage and zero penalty. The comparative experiments against an equal-height coverage model and a random model show that the proposed model effectively alleviates the uneven coverage caused by fixed-layer deployment and the diminishing marginal benefit resulting from random point placement, while achieving full regional coverage and significantly reducing the path repetition rate. This study provides an efficient, safe, and high-precision mathematical planning paradigm for autonomous detailed UAV inspection of transmission towers.

Article.Title: Metabolomics-based central obesity identifies subtypes musculoskeletal disorders management
Article.Authors: Han Q.; Zhang Y.; Feng J.; Zhou B.; Yin C.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to identify novel metabolic subtypes of central obesity using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomics data and evaluate their prospective associations with the incidence of four classic musculoskeletal disorders including sarcopenia, intervertebral disc disease, osteoporosis, and rheumatoid arthritis. A total of 247,107 community-dwelling participants from the UK Biobank were included, with a median follow-up of 13.8 years. The Categorical Boosting (Catboost) algorithm was employed to select metabolic features with the highest discriminatory power for central obesity from 251 plasma NMR metabolites. Through Shapley value ranking, 13 key metabolites were identified. Subsequently, principal component analysis and K-means clustering were applied to construct obesity metabolic subtypes. Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to assess the associations between these subtypes and the risk of incident musculoskeletal diseases. Four stable metabolic subtypes of central obesity were identified. Subtype III was characterized by significantly elevated levels of glycoprotein acetyls, valine, and phospholipids/lipids in large HDL, whereas Subtype II exhibited markedly lower levels of albumin and glutamine. After multivariable adjustment, Subtypes II and III demonstrated significantly higher risks of developing sarcopenia (Hazard Ratio, HR = 1.43, 95% Confidence Interval(CI) 1.28–1.61) and intervertebral disc disease (HR = 1.31, 95%CI 1.19–1.45) compared to the non-obese population. No significant differences were observed among subtypes regarding the risk of osteoporosis or rheumatoid arthritis. Metabolomics-based classification of central obesity identifies heterogeneous subgroups with substantially divergent risks of musculoskeletal disorders. The hyperinflammatory-hypercatabolic metabolic phenotype represents an independent high-risk group for sarcopenia and intervertebral disc disease, providing a novel metabolic classification framework for precision prevention and management.

Article.Title: Entropic analysis of time series through kernel density estimation
Article.Authors: Myers A.; Kay B.; Alvarez I.; Hughes M.; Mackenzie C.; Marrero C.; Ellwein E.; Lentz E.
Article.Abstract: This work presents a novel framework for time series analysis using entropic measures based on the kernel density estimate (KDE) of a time series’ Takens’ embedding in two dimensions. Using this framework we introduce two distinct analytical tools: (1) a multi-scale KDE entropy metric, denoted as $$\Delta \text {KE}$$ , which quantifies the evolution of time series complexity across different delay time scales by measuring changes in entropy, and (2) a sliding baseline method that employs the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence to detect changes in time series structure through changes in KDEs. The $$\Delta \textrm{KE}$$ metric offers insights into the information content and “unfolding” properties of the time series ’Takens’ embedding well-suited to the analysis of dynamical systems, while the KL-divergence-based approach provides a noise and outlier robust measure for identifying time series change points well-suited to the detection of injected radio frequency (RF) signals in noisy backgrounds. We demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of these tools through a set of experiments across several science and technology domains. In the case of RF communications, we achieve accurate detection of injected signals under varying noise and interference conditions comparable with tools of the art and without the need for training. Secondly, we apply our methodology to electrocardiography (ECG) data, successfully identifying instances of ventricular fibrillation with high accuracy. Finally, we demonstrate the potential of our tools for identifying anomalous intermittent chaotic regimes within a signal in dynamical systems.

Article.Title: Structural properties and impedance spectroscopy of solid-state synthesized Sr2MnTiO6 perovskite ceramics for oxide electronic applications
Article.Authors: Khalil H.; Dhahri R.; Madani M.; Omri K.; Mnefgui S.; Albargi H.; Elkenany E.; Neri G.
Article.Abstract: Sr 2 MnTiO 6 (SMT) double-perovskite ceramics were synthesized by a conventional solid-state reaction route and investigated in terms of their structural, microstructural, and temperature-dependent electrical properties. X-ray diffraction analysis combined with Rietveld refinement indicates that the major phase is described by a tetragonal I4/m structure, accompanied by a minor secondary phase. The refined lattice parameters are a = b = 5.5147(5) Å and c = 7.8091(6) Å, with a unit-cell volume of 237.49(3) Å 3 . SEM observations reveal a relatively dense microstructure with well-developed grains and limited intergranular porosity. Temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy performed from 290 to 550 K shows a systematic shift of the Z″ relaxation response toward higher frequencies with increasing temperature, indicating thermally activated relaxation. The impedance response is associated with non-ideal relaxation behavior and contributions from electrically distinct regions of the ceramic. Arrhenius analysis of the relaxation time gives an activation energy of approximately 0.312 eV. The results indicate that the electrical response of SMT ceramics is strongly temperature-dependent and governed by thermally activated charge transport and relaxation processes. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of SMT as a functional oxide ceramic for temperature-dependent electronic and dielectric applications.

Article.Title: Hylocereus undatus peel extract and ZnO nanoparticles suppress cancer through apoptosis and Wnt/β-catenin inhibition
Article.Authors: Tawfik M.; Barakat L.; Elfeky H.; El-Zend M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer treatment faces the challenge of multidrug resistance and systemic cytotoxicity. This study explores the anticancer potential of Hylocereus undatus peel extracts and their biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). Total phenolics, flavonoids and GC–MS profiles of the extracts were determined. Then, ZnO NPs were synthesized by using aqueous and n-hexane extracts and characterized by FTIR, Zeta Potential, XRD, SEM, EDX, and TEM. Among all tested formulations, ZnO NPs-AE (derived from the aqueous extract) showed the strongest antitumor activity, both in cell culture (Caco‑2 and HepG2) and in the Ehrlich ascites carcinoma mouse model. In MTT assays, ZnO NPs-AE was highly cytotoxic to Caco‑2 and HepG2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 and 12.93 µg/mL, respectively) and performed on the same level as doxorubicin ( p < 0.05). It also showed a more favourable selectivity profile, being less toxic to normal colon fibroblasts (CCD‑18Co; IC₅₀ = 32.35 µg/mL) than to Caco‑2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 µg/mL), which was better than doxorubicin. Consistent with this, ZnO NPs-AE reduced the proportion of cells in G2/M phase (7.39% compared with 12.65% in untreated cells) and increased total apoptosis to 25.98% in Caco‑2 cells. Molecularly, it up-regulated caspase-3 (6.15-fold), down-regulated topoisomerase II (0.33-fold) and suppressed the Wnt/β catenin axis. Consistently, ELISA quantification of Axin2 and Cyclin D1 in Caco‑2 cells confirmed down‑regulation of these Wnt/β‑catenin targets in parallel with the decrease in β‑catenin protein. In vivo, ZnO NPs-AE (5 mg/kg) reduced EAC volume to 89.36%, normalized hepatic/renal biomarkers, improved lipid profiles, and alleviated oxidative stress by elevating GSH, CAT, and SOD levels, while reducing MDA, alongside histopathological improvements. Overall, ZnO NPs-AE represents a promising, well tolerated biogenic nanoplatform for targeted cancer therapy.

Article.Title: Attributing compound flood impact from tropical cyclone Idai in Mozambique to climate and population change
Article.Authors: Vertegaal D.; van den Hurk B.; Couasnon A.; Paprotny D.; Muis S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impacts of extreme weather events are a complex interplay of compounding climatic and socio-economic drivers. In this paper, we attribute the effect of climate and population change on the number of people exposed to flooding from tropical cyclone (TC) Idai, making landfall in Mozambique in 2019. We apply an extended storyline attribution framework based on a globally-applicable model chain to simulate compound flooding and exposed population as a proxy for impact under factual and counterfactual climate and population conditions. This enables impact attribution to both drivers, and disaggregation across flood depth categories and socio-economic groups. Under the selected storyline experiments, 84% of the exposed population is attributable to the combined effect of climate and population change since 1975, with population change alone accounting for 80% and climate change alone for 9%. Climate change increases flood extent and flood depth, whereas population change alters the number of people living in the flooded area. These drivers change the distribution of people exposed to flooding, leading to different attribution assessments per flood depth category. Our results indicate that the effect of climate change is not evenly distributed across socio-economic groups, which is masked when spatially aggregating the attribution assessment.

Article.Title: Friction surfacing of Al2O3 reinforced aluminium coatings on low carbon steel with microstructural and tribological characterization
Article.Authors: Sivalingam V.; Vellingiri S.; Babu G.; Thangavel N.; Naresh M.; Dennison M.; Sridhar V.; Raja Sekhar G.
Article.Abstract: Friction surfacing (FS) was employed to create Al–7.5 wt% Al 2 O 3 metal matrix composite coatings on low carbon steel (AISI 1018), enhancing surface performance by solid-state processing. Two parameter sets were examined to identify their effects on coating microstructure and tribology. SEM–EDS showed dense, defect-free coatings with uniform reinforcement particle distribution, good metallurgical bonding, and a narrow compositional transition across the coating–substrate interface. The higher rotational speed and axial load promoted greater material plasticization, resulting in improved coating continuity and consolidation. The EBSD investigation showed significant grain refinement from 12.6 μm in the consumable rod to 8.6 μm in the coating, indicating dynamic recrystallization during FS. Effective microstructural stabilization was confirmed by a considerable rise in high-angle grain boundary fraction. The combination of grain refinement, strain hardening, and dispersion strengthening by Al 2 O 3 particles significantly increased microhardness from 160 HV for the substrate to 250 HV for the coating. Dry sliding tribological investigations indicated significant weight loss, specific wear rate, and coefficient of friction reductions compared to the substrate. The improved coating reduced weight loss by 67.2% and specific wear rate by 71.8%. The better performance at higher energy settings shows how FS process parameters improve coating integrity, microstructural refinement, and tribology.

Article.Title: Randomized trial of pressure controlled versus volume controlled ventilation during robot assisted urological surgery in the clasp knife position
Article.Authors: Cai X.; Chen J.; Lin W.; Wen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The combination of CO₂ pneumoperitoneum and clasp-knife position imposes substantial respiratory and hemodynamic challenges in Da Vinci robot-assisted urological surgery. Although volume-controlled ventilation (VCV) and pressure-controlled ventilation (PCV) are widely used, their comparative effects under these specific surgical conditions remain unclear. We hypothesized that PCV could reduce peak inspiratory pressure (Ppeak) and improve dynamic lung compliance (Cdyn) without compromising hemodynamic stability. The trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06056401). We randomized 62 ASA I–II patients to VCV (n = 30) or PCV (n = 32). Study measurements were discontinued in two PCV patients after randomization because of intraoperative bleeding, leaving 60 participants for the following analyses. Ventilatory parameters, hemodynamic variables, and arterial blood gas values were recorded at five time points: T1 (15 min after induction), T2 (15 min after clasp-knife positioning), T3 (30 min after CO₂ pneumoperitoneum), T4 (60 min after CO₂ pneumoperitoneum), and T5 (15 min after pneumoperitoneum removal). Ppeak showed a significant ventilation mode × time interaction ( P < 0.001). Lower Ppeak was observed in the PCV group at T2–T5, with the largest differences during pneumoperitoneum at T3 and T4. Cdyn also showed a significant ventilation mode × time interaction ( P = 0.012), with higher values under PCV at several measurement points. No significant ventilation mode × time interactions were observed for the measured arterial blood gas variables. No significant ventilation mode × time interactions were observed for the principal hemodynamic variables. No severe postoperative complications occurred during the 72-hour follow-up. PCV and VCV showed different intraoperative respiratory-mechanical profiles, including lower Ppeak and different Cdyn trajectories under PCV. No differential arterial blood gas or hemodynamic trajectories were observed, and the clinical significance of these physiological differences remains uncertain.

Article.Title: Source-dependent structural and pH-responsive swelling properties of bentonite/cellulose/alginate hydrogel beads derived from agricultural biomass residues
Article.Authors: Lungmala N.; Jaitham U.; Boonthawee K.; Yadoung S.; Huynh Q.; Danmek K.; Chen X.; Chang K.; Hongsibsong S.
Article.Abstract: Agricultural biomass residues are abundant and renewable feedstocks for the development of cellulose-based functional biomaterials. However, direct comparisons of cellulose-rich fractions derived from multiple agricultural biomass sources within the same hydrogel formulation and under identical fabrication conditions remain limited. This study investigated the structural and swelling properties of bentonite/cellulose/alginate (BT/CL/ALG) hydrogel beads prepared from eight agricultural residues: coffee pulp, mango leaf, corn cob, corn leaf, corn husk, corn stalk, sugarcane leaf, and bagasse. The biomass residues were subjected to combined alkaline hydrogen peroxide (AHP) pretreatment to obtain cellulose-rich fractions, which were subsequently incorporated into a sodium alginate matrix with bentonite clay and crosslinked with Ca²⁺. The resulting materials were characterized by compositional analysis, FTIR, XRD, SEM, and TGA/DTG. AHP pretreatment resulted in substantial cellulose enrichment, with the highest cellulose contents observed in corn stalk (76.0%) and bagasse (70.4%). FTIR and XRD analyses indicated changes in the chemical structure and relative crystalline organization of the biomass following pretreatment, while SEM revealed source-dependent morphological changes. The resulting hydrogel beads exhibited differences in swelling behavior, with swelling capacities measured at 144 h ranging from 218.57% to 419.83% in deionized water. Under PBS conditions, all hydrogel beads exhibited pH-responsive swelling, with greater swelling at pH 9 than at pH 3. The highest swelling capacity was observed for the corn-leaf-derived hydrogel at pH 9 (2245.85%). Overall, the findings demonstrate that agricultural biomass residues can provide cellulose-rich feedstocks for the preparation of BT/CL/ALG hydrogel beads with source-dependent structural and swelling characteristics.

Molecular docking predicted favourable binding poses for quercetin with Fabp3 and Adipoq (− 8.8 and − 8.2 kcal/mol), without establishing direct binding. Quercetin also attenuated oxidative stress, inflammation, collagen deposition and cardiac dysfunction. These findings suggest coordinated Fabp3-, Adipoq-, AMPK- and PPARα-associated responses, warranting causal validation.

Article.Title: SADA: semantic-aware perturbation and dual-view alignment for privacy-preserving LLMs
Article.Authors: Meng B.; Xu X.; Liu B.; Chen X.; Liu L.; Xiao M.; Wang Q.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted widespread attention owing to their strong capabilities in text comprehension and generation. However, despite their popularity in cloud-based inference services, concerns have emerged regarding the potential leakage of sensitive user information. Existing context perturbation methods with differential privacy apply uniform noise to input tokens to mitigate such risks, facing the trade-off between privacy efficiency and generation quality. To narrow this gap, we propose semantic-aware perturbation and dual-view alignment (SADA) for privacy-preserving LLMs inference. SADA introduces two plug-in modules named the perturbation module and alignment module. In the perturbation module, we design ADRTEXT, a semantic-aware local differential privacy (LDP) mechanism that achieves differentiated protection through token-level sensitivity analysis. Then, a novel dual-view alignment strategy is introduced in the alignment module to bridge a randomized perturbed view with an entity-free semantic skeleton, optimizing the trade-off between LDP-induced noise and generation quality. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that SADA achieves effective privacy protection while maintaining a higher generation quality.

Article.Title: Role of BCL3 dysregulation and LPHN1 in the transition from chronic inflammation in severe asthma to lung cancer
Article.Authors: Bhamidimarri P.; Salameh L.; Elemam N.; Heialy S.; Hammash D.; Mohammed A.; Dakkak B.; Busamah G.; Chouaib S.; Harati R.; Hamid Q.; Hamoudi R.; Mahboub B.
Article.Abstract: Increased lung cancer risk in asthma patients has been reported, yet the molecular mechanism linking chronic airway inflammation to malignant transformation remains unclear. BCL3 is an atypical member of the Inhibitor of κB family. Transcriptomic studies have reported elevated BCL3 expression in both severe asthma and lung tumor tissues. This study aims to investigate whether BCL3 dysregulation contributes to the transition from chronic inflammation in severe asthma to malignant transformation in the lung. BCL3 was overexpressed or silenced in asthmatic bronchial epithelial cells and lung adenocarcinoma cells. Cell proliferation, apoptosis, and NF-κB activity were assessed. Transcriptomic profiling identified BCL3-regulated genes and pathways. BCL3 overexpression enhanced proliferation and reduced apoptosis in epithelial cells, while its silencing in lung cancer cells produced the opposite effect. BCL3 overexpression reduced NF-κB-responsive reporter activity, whereas BCL3 silencing increased it. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of GPCR signaling, receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, and immune response pathways. LPHN1, a GPCR, was the only transcript consistently associated with BCL3 across all models. LPHN1 has previously been reported as a prognostic biomarker in NSCLC and as a potential bronchodilator target in asthma. Together, these findings highlight BCL3 dysregulation as a potential contributor to altered epithelial proliferation and survival and identify LPHN1 as a BCL3-associated transcript, providing new insight into molecular changes that may accompany the transition from chronic airway inflammation to lung cancer.
