Article.Title: CO2 confinement by a novel molecular spring architecture via reactive molecular dynamics
Article.Authors: Celik F.; Yılmaz M.; Karabulut E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, we propose a novel framework with a hybrid molecular spring architecture based on a spiral/helical-type nanostructure supported by slab layers and bridged by organic linkers. Hierarchically, the framework consists of symmetrical nickel (Ni)-doped α-Al 2 O 3 slabs, a sulfur-rich helical cage, and multifunctional 2,5-dimercaptoterephthalic acid (DMBDC) organic linkers. Ni/α-Al 2 O 3 supported, DMBDC bridged and helical pillared framework (SL-HPF) contributed to dynamic structural stability, the synergistic role of interfacial coupling and molecular confinement through reactive force field (ReaxFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The CO 2 confinement performance of SL-HPF was analysed by atomic arrangements via MD trajectories, self-diffusion coefficient (D), radial distribution functions (RDF), gas viscosity measurements. To isolate the contribution of the helical cage, a control system was conducted on pure Ni/α-Al 2 O 3 slabs. The D and gas viscosity of CO 2 for only control system are 1.451 × 10 –7 m 2 s −1 and 0.0163 Js m −3 , respectively. In contrast, the SL-HPF exhibited an enhanced molecular trapping because CO 2 molecules systematically penetrated the helical cage due to strong confinement effects. For SL-HPF, D and local fluid viscosity of CO 2 were calculated as 1.812 × 10 –8 m 2 s −1 and 0.0347 Js m −3 , respectively. Structural localization was further validated by a highly dense S-C pair RDF correlation peak at 1.8 Å within the helical cage. These results demonstrate that the synergy between catalytic metal sites, elastic organic springs, and high-affinity sulfur vacancies in the helical cage can successfully immobilize gas molecules through molecular trapping rather than chemical bond disruption. This work presents a novel molecular spring design and hybrid framework for next-generation environmental remediation technologies.

Article.Title: Prolonged visual-motor dual-task effects on dynamic stability in children with ADHD subtypes
Article.Authors: Soltani S.; Ghadiri F.; Farahpour N.; Bahram A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Research on dynamic stability in children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) has predominantly relied on short-term laboratory paradigms, limiting understanding of how prolonged task demands affect gait stability. This study investigated the effects of prolonged visual-motor dual-task walking on gait stability across ADHD subtypes. Fifty-seven children (7–10 years) participated: 19 with the combined subtype (ADHD-C), 17 with the predominantly inattentive (ADHD-I), and 21 typically developing peers. Participants walked on a treadmill at self-selected speeds for three minutes under four visual conditions (no target, fixation, saccade, and smooth pursuit). Group-by-visual condition effects on Margin of Stability (MOS) and its coefficient of variation (CV) were analyzed via mixed-model ANOVA (α = 0.05). Typically developing children exhibited larger MOS and lower CV than both ADHD groups across most conditions. However, children with ADHD-C achieved stability levels comparable to typically developing children during fixation, whereas children with ADHD-I remained less stable across conditions. Smooth pursuit was associated with the lowest stability in both ADHD subtypes. Saccades and fixation conditions were associated with greater stability consistency, with saccades showing the lowest variability. Distinct patterns of stability were observed across ADHD subtypes and visual-task conditions. Prolonged visual-motor dual-task walking revealed subtype-specific patterns of gait stability in children with ADHD. These findings suggest that visual-task demands may differentially influence gait stability across ADHD subtypes and highlight the importance of considering visual-attentional demands when examining locomotor control in this population.

Article.Title: A two-step percoll gradient enables high-quality immune nuclei recovery from frozen melanoma for single-nucleus multiomics
Article.Authors: Li H.; Duan B.; Sunwoo J.; Chen C.; Jin Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Single-nucleus multiomic profiling of archived melanoma remains challenging due to melanin-associated debris and poor recovery of fragile immune nuclei. Here, we describe and validate a Two-Step Percoll (TSP) gradient method that enables efficient recovery of immune-cell nuclei from frozen human melanoma while supporting high-quality transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling. Unlike FACS-based workflows, TSP requires no specialized sorting equipment, avoids mechanical stress on fragile nuclei, and effectively removes melanin-associated debris using only a standard benchtop centrifuge. TSP supports recovery of diverse tumor, stromal, and immune populations and high-quality paired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq profiling from archived specimens. We validated the method across independent melanoma donors and show that it enables reproducible integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analysis from frozen clinical material. This simple, low-cost approach provides a practical workflow for single-nucleus multiomic profiling of frozen melanoma specimens.

Article.Title: Graph and low-rank based cluster-prototype matching for transductive zero-shot learning
Article.Authors: Cao M.; Han X.; Chen X.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) addresses the unseen class recognition problem by leveraging semantic information to transfer knowledge from seen classes to unseen classes. Most existing models rely on learning an embedding space where the classes of test samples according to sample-prototype similarities are determined. However, most approaches do not explore the underlying distribution structure of embedded samples. In addition, whether the mapping can precisely preserve the sub-manifolds of samples is not investigated. In order to solve these issues, we proposed a transductive model named Graph and Low-rank based Cluster-Prototype Matching (GLCPM) model to learn a low-rank mapping to simultaneously explore the distribution structure and keep the sub-manifolds of embedded samples. GLCPM aims to apply a teacher-student mode, where the embedding paradigm of the test semantic prototypes is guided by the training samples but keeps its own properties. Specifically, the learned visual embeddings of the test prototypes are encouraged to preserve the local intrinsic structure by constructing a graph. Meanwhile, the visual features of test samples are clustered, and then a matching constraint is adopted that the projected test prototypes align the clusters so as to further improve the generality of the mapping function. Finally, an ensemble classifier, which combines the cluster-prototype similarity with the sample-prototype similarity, determines the label of each test sample. Extensive experiments on five benchmark data sets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: teacher-student learning; ensemble classifiers; semantic prototypes

Article.Title: Decoupled regression rate and stability characteristics of carbon-black and aluminum-doped paraffin fuels for hybrid rocket engines
Article.Authors: Elkhshen M.; Hashish A.; Hassan A.; Ahmed M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hybrid rocket engines offer inherent safety and throttling by separating fuel and oxidizer, yet their wider use is hindered by low fuel regression rates and by combustion instabilities that frequently accompany performance-enhancing additives. This paper presents an experimental framework in which these two aspects are assessed separately on a single dataset. A campaign of 31 firings was conducted on paraffin-based fuels doped with carbon black (PC, 1 wt%), conventional micron-aluminum (PA, 14 wt%), and activated nano-aluminum (PAA, 14 wt%), all burned with gaseous oxygen. A covariate-adjusted equivalence analysis (ANCOVA with $$\log (G)$$ as covariate) over the tested flux range (31–71 kg/m $$^2\cdot$$ s) indicates that the three fuels are practically equivalent on average , with model-predicted mean differences inside a $$\pm 10\%$$ margin. This average equivalence is not uniform in flux: evaluated at a single representative flux of $$G = 45$$ kg/m $$^2\cdot$$ s, the fitted curve for PA lies about 13% above that for PC, just outside the same margin. In contrast to the regression-rate similarity, the pressure spectra separate the formulations, though less sharply than the regression data might suggest. Narrow-band modes are resolved in 28 of 30 usable records, and they fall into two tight clusters at $$224 \pm 17$$ Hz and $$414 \pm 16$$ Hz that recur in all three formulations at similar rates. Because the mode frequencies do not depend on what the fuel contains, they are attributed provisionally to the test hardware rather than to the additives. All mode amplitudes are small, between 0.04% and 0.98% of mean chamber pressure, and median total broadband fluctuation over 5–500 Hz is 0.84% (PC), 1.00% (PA) and 0.97% (PAA) — at least a factor of five below the 5% threshold adopted here for identifying combustion instability. No formulation is therefore unstable under the tested conditions, notwithstanding the presence of resolvable modes. The formulation effect on broadband level is modest: PAA exceeds PA in the 5–20 Hz band and PA exceeds PC in the 200–300 Hz band, with no other pair separating and no significant effect on the total level. Because no anti-aliasing filter is documented and only one pressure transducer was recorded, the quoted frequencies may be aliases of higher-frequency components and the mechanisms proposed below are interpretations rather than demonstrated mechanisms.

Article.Title: Predictors of delayed healing after anal fissure surgery: association of Helicobacter pylori infection and intestinal parasitic infestations with healing outcomes—an observational study
Article.Authors: Zakaria R.; Kotb K.; Orban Y.; Amin M.; Abo-alella H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anal fissure is a common surgical problem. Failure to improve after surgical intervention is mainly due to delayed or incomplete healing. This study aimed to identify factors associated with delayed or no healing after anal fissure surgeries in order to modify potentially preventable risk factors. This is a single-center prospective cohort study that included patients who underwent anal fissure surgery from August 2024 to November 2025. Patients were categorized into two groups based on healing status: normal healing and delayed healing. Data were collected from patients and the follow-up physician, and associations between demographic, clinical, surgical, and infectious factors and healing outcomes were examined using univariable and multivariable analyses. Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusting for diabetes and muscle tone were performed for the infection-related associations. From the analyzed data, the mean age of group I (normal healing) was 40.9 ± 12.4 years and that of group II (delayed healing) was 44.5 ± 12.6 years. Age, BMI (body mass index), number of fissures, type of surgery, energy source, Entamoeba infestation, Helicobacter pylori infection, and Giardia infestation differed significantly between the two groups ( P < 0.05). In unadjusted analyses, V–Y advancement flap, laser fissuroplasty, and lateral internal sphincterotomy were associated with significantly lower rates of delayed healing. After adjustment for age, BMI, and number of fissures, only laser fissuroplasty remained statistically significant. Entamoeba infestation, Helicobacter pylori infection, and Giardia infestation all remained significantly associated with delayed healing after adjustment for age, BMI, and number of fissures, and Entamoeba and H. pylori remained independently associated with delayed healing when included simultaneously in the multivariable model. Sensitivity analyses using Firth’s penalized likelihood logistic regression, and additional models further adjusting for diabetes and muscle tone, yielded consistent findings for all three infections. Delayed healing after anal fissure surgery was associated with older age, female sex, higher BMI, multiple fissures, and positive stool tests for Entamoeba histolytica , Helicobacter pylori, and Giardia, although the association with female sex was of borderline significance. These infection associations remained significant after adjustment for age, BMI, number of fissures, and, in sensitivity analyses, diabetes and muscle tone. V–Y advancement flap, laser fissuroplasty, and lateral internal sphincterotomy were associated with lower rates of delayed healing in unadjusted analyses; however, only laser fissuroplasty maintained statistical significance after multivariable adjustment.

Article.Title: Combined supplementation of L-carnitine and stevioside enhances performance, stress tolerance, immune competence, and molecular responses in Nile tilapia
Article.Authors: Sallam G.; Hamad A.; Abaza I.; Saad A.; Elmaghraby A.; Fahmy A.; Fayed W.; Gewaily M.; Shehata A.; El Basuini M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of dietary L-carnitine (500 mg/kg) and stevioside (450 mg/kg) on growth performance, physiological responses, stress tolerance, immunity, antioxidant status, and molecular regulation in Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ; initial weight 3.84 ± 0.12 g) over 90 days. Fish were fed a control diet or diets supplemented with L-carnitine, stevioside, or their combination. Two-way ANOVA showed significant main effects of both additives on growth performance, feed consumption, and feed conversion efficiency ( P < 0.05), with the combined diet producing the highest numerical responses. No significant interaction was detected for growth or feed utilization, indicating additive effects. Supplementation enhanced intestinal digestive enzyme activities, with significant interaction effects for protease activity ( P = 0.007), and improved intestinal and liver histological integrity, including a significant interaction for villus height ( P < 0.001). Serum biochemical profiles were improved, with significant interactions for total protein, glucose, post-hypoxia glucose, and total cholesterol ( P < 0.05). Antioxidant status was enhanced through increased SOD, CAT, and GPx activities and reduced lipid peroxidation, with additive effects. Supplementation also improved hypoxia tolerance and innate immune responses. A significant interaction was observed for hypoxia tolerance ( P = 0.007), whereas immune responses were predominantly additive. At the molecular level, dietary treatments modulated genes associated with growth, metabolism, immunity, and antioxidant defense. Significant L-carnitine × stevioside interactions were detected for IGF-1 , GLUT4 , IL-1β , IgH , IFN1-α , and CAT expression ( P < 0.05), while SOD and Gsr expression showed additive responses. Overall, L-carnitine and stevioside improved growth, physiological performance, stress resilience, immune competence, and antioxidant capacity in Nile tilapia. Their combination produced the greatest overall responses, with effects ranging from additive to interactive depending on the biological endpoint.

Article.Title: Data-model fusion-based dual-RBFNN adaptive backstepping control for constrained power tracking in PMSG wind energy conversion systems
Article.Authors: Fan J.; Zuo D.; Wu C.; Zhang L.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Power-operating-point tracking in permanent-magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) wind energy conversion systems is challenged by coupled mechanical/aerodynamic and electromagnetic uncertainties together with converter current and voltage limits. This study develops a data-model fusion-based dual radial-basis-function neural network (RBFNN) adaptive backstepping controller for below-rated operation. A dimensional turbine-PMSG model supplies wind-dependent references, while two channel-specific RBFNNs estimate lumped residual effects in the mechanical and q-axis voltage dynamics. The design combines constraint-aware adaptation, current and voltage limiters, and offline Harris hawks optimization of five gains. A complete closed-loop boundedness analysis gives explicit ultimate bounds and conditional damping margins for the adopted model. Five controller configurations (M0-M4) were compared using three optimizer seeds, five held-out simulation seeds, and nine parameter-drift and measurement-noise conditions. Under the main condition, M3 achieved a power root-mean-square error of 382.320 ± 28.187 kW, representing reductions of 28.07%, 16.13%, 18.20%, and 19.02% relative to M0, M1, M2, and M4, respectively. M3 also attained the lowest power error in all 45 seed-condition cells. The observer-assisted M4 yielded a slightly lower speed error than M3 (0.023193 ± 0.004554 versus 0.024266 ± 0.004714 p.u.). A source-derived adaptive sliding-mode comparator further supports the power-tracking benefit under matched implementation conditions. Here, ± denotes the sample standard deviation across five held-out seeds. These repeated simulations show that the proposed controller provides a consistent power-tracking advantage and balanced constrained performance within the modeled operating envelope.

Article.Title: Unified compliance-based correction for indirect tensile strength in Brazilian disc, ring, and modified seesaw tests
Article.Authors: Kumar P.; Walia B.
Article.Abstract: The indirect tensile strength values obtained from the Brazilian disc (BD), Brazilian ring (IR) and modified seesaw test (MST) are highly sensitive to specimen geometry, stress concentration and compliance of the loading system and are not readily comparable. This study suggests a unified compliance-based analytical framework for consistent evaluation of the indirect tensile strength for these three testing configurations. To validate the proposed framework, experimental tests were conducted on dark grey granite specimens, and finite element modelling was carried out under the same boundary and contact conditions. The results indicate that the Brazilian disc configuration gives the highest apparent tensile strength due to the stress concentration effect of the platens, while the Brazilian ring and modified seesaw test give lower tensile strength due to the reduced stress concentration. The measured tensile strength was decreased by up to 12.93% for the Brazilian disc and 9.60% for the modified seesaw test when compliance correction was applied, highlighting the need to consider loading-system compliance. In addition, the stiffness of the specimens was determined to be greater at lower inner-to-outer diameter ratios and less at higher ratios. The proposed framework offers a common analytical foundation for understanding indirect tensile strength for various specimen geometries and loading conditions. It enhances the reliability and consistency of tensile strength measurement and offers practical guidance for the design, comparison and standardization of indirect tensile testing methods for brittle geomaterials.

Article.Title: Bioactive potential of polysaccharides produced by lactic acid bacteria isolated from dairy products in Egypt
Article.Authors: Noureldein R.; Refaat A.; El-Dougdoug K.; Abou-Taleb K.; Amin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) have attracted considerable attention for their ability to produce exopolysaccharides (EPS) with potential health benefits. This study aimed to optimize EPS production by LAB isolates and evaluate their bioactivities. LAB isolates were screened under different culture conditions, and 20 promising isolates were selected for further study. EPS production increased on modified De Man-Rogosa-Sharpe (mMRS) medium at an initial pH of 6.8 and 37 °C. Dry polymer weight (DPW) and viscosity ranged from 1500 to 17500 mg/l, with K1 showing the highest DPW. CH3, P2, and P4 exhibited notable antioxidant and antibacterial activities. CH3 isolate produced EPS on sweet whey medium and showed anticancer activity against Caco-2 cells and antiviral activity against hepatitis A virus (HAV), with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC 50 ) of 5859.37 and 417 µg/ml, respectively. High performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) revealed the presence of monosaccharides in the EPS produced by the CH3 isolate on sweet whey medium, including glucose (40%), mannose (29%), fructose (17.3%), galactose (13%), and arabinose (0.7%). The CH3 isolate was identified as Levilactobacillus brevis with accession number QB001328, These findings highlight the potential of LAB-derived EPS for food and health applications.

Article.Title: Marinas act as persistent introduction hubs driving the decadal accumulation of non-indigenous fouling species in an oceanic island system
Article.Authors: Ramalhosa P.; Castro N.; Álvarez S.; Gestoso I.; Canning-Clode J.
Article.Abstract: Long–term monitoring of marine fouling assemblages and non‑indigenous species (NIS) has been historically scarce globally, particularly in island ecosystems, limiting the ability to distinguish transient detections from persistent populations. Using an 11–year monitoring dataset (2013–2025; 33 surveys, 131 sampling events) across four Madeira Archipelago marinas, we evaluated spatio-temporal patterns in biofouling assemblages. Across 71 recorded taxa, cumulative NIS richness increased steadily, ultimately accounting for nearly half (45–48%; 27–30 NIS per marina) of all recorded fouling species, reflecting major community transformation. Multivariate analyses identified marina identity as the primary driver structuring assemblages, maintaining distinct spatial signatures despite minimal thermal variation. Temporally, seasonal dynamics revealed a clear functional decoupling: mean observed richness per sampling event peaked during warmer periods, whereas cumulative multi-year species turnover was highest during cooler periods. This decoupling reflects seasonal thermal regimes, where summer warming creates windows that trigger reproductive pulses and space preemption by fast-growing colonial NIS, while cooler periods permit broader species turnover. Together, these findings confirm marinas as persistent introduction hubs, where repeated introductions, recruitment, and population persistence. Long–term, seasonally informed monitoring is therefore vital for early detection and marine biosecurity in island ecosystems.

Article.Title: Factors influencing plasma brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in adolescent sport participants
Article.Authors: Josafatow-García N.; Tabor J.; Penner L.; Galarneau J.; Fraser D.; Emery C.; Wellington C.; Debert C.
Article.Abstract: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is being explored as a biomarker for sport-related concussion (SRC). We aim to explore BDNF contextualized by demographic and sport-related factors in adolescent sport participants. This cross-sectional study nested in a multi-site Canadian cohort study recruits a sample of uninjured male ( n = 60, 15.79 ± 1.17 years) and female ( n = 60, 15.97 ± 1.36 years) adolescent sport participants. We investigate plasma BDNF concentrations considering sex (M/F), age (years), concussion history (yes/no), bodyweight (kgs), height (m), BMI, menstrual cycle phase (follicular/luteal), and classification of sport participation (non-contact/contact/collision). Plasma BDNF was significantly higher for males ( β = 0.176, 95% CI: 0.010, 0.342, p = 0.038). No association was found between plasma BDNF and concussion history ( β = – 0.149, 95% CI – 0.323, 0.025, p = 0.093). Age was positively associated with plasma BDNF in females ( β = 0.089, 95% CI 0.002, 0.176, p = 0.044). Contact sport participants had significantly lower BDNF compared to non-contact sports participants ( β = – 0.462, 95% CI – 0.830, – 0.093, p = 0.014). BDNF increased with height ( β = 0.011, 95% CI – 0.001, 0.021, p = 0.028), but not bodyweight ( β = 0.005, 95% CI – 0.001, 0.012, p = 0.119), BMI ( β = 0.006, 95% CI – 0.017, 0.029, p = 0.062), or menstrual cycle phase ( β = – 0.210, 95% CI – 0.470, 0.051, p = 0.114). Overall, BDNF in adolescent sport participants was higher for males, increased with height, increased with age in females only, and was lower in contact sports. Future studies should consider participant characteristics and sport participation type when evaluating plasma BDNF as a biomarker for sport-related concussion.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence readiness in healthcare and health professions education in conflict-affected Syria: an online cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Katrib M.; Jamileh E.; Saleh I.; Hmidoush A.; Zakkar M.; Antoun I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly relevant to healthcare delivery, clinical training, and health professions education. Evidence from conflict-affected settings remains limited, despite workforce shortages, disrupted training pathways, and constrained digital infrastructure. This study assessed AI knowledge, trust, willingness, and digital capability among Syrian adults and healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals), with emphasis on implications for AI literacy and professional education. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of Syrian adults from March 4th to May 31st 2026, using a 35-item questionnaire distributed via social media through convenience sampling. The survey assessed AI awareness, trust, willingness, perceived risks and benefits, barriers to healthcare and digital health use, and Digital Literacy. Healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals) completed additional items on clinical AI use and exposure to unsafe AI recommendations. Composite scores were calculated for AI Trust (3–15), AI Willingness (4–20), and Digital Literacy (2–10). Internal consistency was acceptable to excellent across scales (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.787–0.856). Among 829 participants, 353 (42.6%) were healthcare respondents (119 students and 234 qualified professionals). Mean AI Willingness, AI Trust, and Digital Literacy scores were 14.5 (SD 3.25), 11.0 (SD 2.34), and 6.67 (SD 1.80), respectively. In multivariable linear regression, AI Trust (β = 0.483) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.305) were the strongest predictors, followed by General AI Knowledge (β = 0.165). In sensitivity models excluding the Willingness item that loaded on Trust, Trust (β = 0.44 and 0.38) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.31 and 0.33) remained the strongest correlates. Educational use was the most accepted AI application (65.5%) and educational support was the leading perceived benefit (64.2%). Medical errors were the most frequently perceived risk (76.6%), while cost, unreliable internet access, and lack of Arabic-language content were major implementation barriers. In this online convenience sample, Trust and Digital Literacy were the strongest independent correlates of Willingness to use AI, followed by AI knowledge. The high acceptance of educational AI suggests a practical entry point for conflict-affected health systems. AI literacy should be integrated into undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing health professions education, with explicit training on critical appraisal, safe use, bias, privacy, local validation, and clinician oversight.

Article.Title: Comparative field assessment of nanobubble-assisted immersion versus injection vaccination against Streptococcus agalactiae serotypes Ia and III
Article.Authors: Vinh N.; Dong H.; Lan N.; Wongkaew J.; Das S.; Kolvankar V.; Chatchaiphan S.; Turner J.; Senapin S.; St-Hilaire S.; Salin K.; Rodkhum C.; Turner W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Streptococcosis caused by Streptococcus agalactiae is a major source of economic loss in intensive tilapia aquaculture. Although vaccination is effective, its adoption is constrained by cost and logistical challenges. We previously developed a low-cost bivalent killed vaccine (combined serotypes Ia and III) that provides strong protection when administered by injection; however, injectable vaccination remains impractical for many farmers. Nanobubble-assisted immersion priming followed by oral boosting has shown promise as an alternative vaccination strategy, but its effectiveness for controlling streptococcosis in tilapia has not yet been optimized. This study evaluated two nanobubble-assisted immersion priming-oral boosting strategies for the bivalent S. agalactiae vaccine under laboratory conditions and subsequently compared its performance using a conventional prime–boost injection regimen protocol in field settings. In laboratory trials, nanobubble-assisted groups (O2NB-CS)-Vac and [O3NB-(O2NB-CS)-Vac] exhibited enhanced innate immune responses (lysozyme, IL1β, TNFα, IL6, HSP70) and higher protection, expressed as relative percent survival (RPS, 55.56–63.16%) than the non-nanobubble immersion group (RPS, 16.67–36.84%). Given their comparable efficacy, both nanobubble-assisted immersion groups were advanced to a farm trial. In the field trial, nanobubble-assisted immersion priming-oral boosting induced only negligible antibody IgM responses against both serotypes, consistent with laboratory results. In contrast, injection vaccination elicited strong IgM responses to serotype Ia, particularly after boosting. Immersion groups showed elevated lysozyme activity at days 30 and 60, and significant upregulation of gene IL1β and CD8 up to day 30, whereas no comparable immune responses were observed in the injection group relative to the non-vaccinated control. Laboratory challenge testing of field-vaccinated fish at day 60 post vaccination yielded lower protection in immersion groups (RPS, 10.39–42.86%) compared with injection (RPS, 85.71%). Harvest survival and production outcomes favored injection; however, interpretation of production-scale trial is limited by natural co-infections, coupled with potential environmental and husbandry variations. Overall, the nanobubble-assisted immersion strategy produced measurable innate immune activation and moderate protection under laboratory conditions, but it was less effective than injection in the current study. Further optimization of oral formulation and booster schedules are required to improve the immersion-prime oral boost strategies.

Article.Title: Modified Mohr–Coulomb criterion and risk coefficient for mining-induced fault slip
Article.Authors: Ruiming S.; Hongwei W.
Article.Abstract: Fault slip is a critical factor triggering coal burst accidents and poses serious threats to mining safety. In this study, the Mohr–Coulomb criterion is modified by considering mining effects. A mechanical model of fault slip under mining disturbance is established. Physical simulation test is conducted based on the Qianqiu Coal Mine to reveal the overlying strata movement and fault stress evolution. Furthermore, FLAC 3D is employed to systematically investigate how lateral pressure coefficient and fault dip angle affect stress distribution on the fault. The results indicate that a steeper dip leads to higher residual normal stress, whereas the shear stress exhibits nonlinear characteristics with abrupt transitions from minimum to maximum values. High-dip faults are more prone to appear stress concentration. The increase of the lateral pressure coefficient leads to an overall rise in shear stress, while the zone of normal stress release shifts from the upper part of the fault to the lower part. On this basis, a fault slip risk coefficient R f is proposed for real-time assessment of slip hazard during the mining activities. The study shows that R f dynamically increases as the mining face advances. Faults dipping at 45° exhibit the highest risk coefficient in the early stage of mining. The most prominent risk occurs under the combined influence of large lateral pressure coefficient and high dip angle when the mining face approaches the fault. This study can provide a scientific basis for stability evaluation of mining-affected faults.

Article.Title: Phenotypic diversity and preliminary phytochemical screening of Iranian Datura populations: a descriptive baseline study under controlled greenhouse conditions
Article.Authors: Morovati Z.; Karimzadeh G.; Rashidi-Monfared S.; Abtahi M.
Article.Abstract: Medicinal plants belonging to the genus Datura are prized for their production of bioactive tropane alkaloids and other therapeutic compounds. Systematic genetic improvement of these species is hindered by a lack of fundamental genetic information. This study evaluated morphological, physiological, and phytochemical diversity in 23 natural populations of Datura stramonium L. and D. innoxia collected from across Iran. Seeds were cultivated under controlled greenhouse conditions in a completely randomized design with three replications during 2022. Nested ANOVA partitioning species and population-level effects revealed that species identity was significant for 3 of 18 traits (LL, LW, and SWT), while population-level differences within species were highly significant for all traits, accounting for up to 99.99% of phenotypic variance. Analysis of variance revealed highly significant differences among populations across all traits assessed. These findings demonstrate that Iranian Datura populations harbor substantial genetic diversity at the population level, independent of species identity. Plant height was the most variable morphological trait (GCV = 42.80%), yet phytochemical and physiological traits displayed the highest population-level repeatability (R² = 0.96–0.99) and high potential population differentiation index (PDI = 67–116%) at the population level assuming a selection intensity of 10%, with antioxidant activity and chlorophyll b emerging as the most responsive traits (116% and 113%, respectively). These estimates, derived under controlled greenhouse conditions, reflect population-level differentiation and repeatability of population means; they serve as preliminary indicators for identifying promising populations for further evaluation. However, validation in multi-environment trials with appropriate genetic designs is required before these estimates can guide breeding decisions. Multivariate analyses, including hierarchical clustering, principal components analysis, and canonical correlation analysis, effectively distinguished populations and unveiled distinct trait associations. Canonical correlation analysis revealed a strong association between preliminary phytochemical/physiological and agronomic trait sets, with chlorophyll SPAD serving as the key linking trait, and clearly separated D. innoxia (superior seed traits) from D. stramonium (higher phenolic content). Heatmap correlation analysis grouped traits into three clusters: seed and reproductive traits (strongly inter-correlated), leaf morphology with phenolics (weakly associated), and pigments with antioxidant capacity (strongly correlated). Four populations S2P3 (Kerman, Kerman), S2P9 (Amiriyeh, Isfahan), S2P14 (Amol, Mazandaran), and S1P3 (Razavi Khorasan) exhibited superior performance across multiple traits, representing promising candidates for Datura improvement and warranting further investigation through targeted phytochemical profiling to quantify specific bioactive compounds. These findings establish a descriptive baseline that prioritizes the population for further investigation.

Article.Title: Divergent epigenetic and transcriptional responses to bisphenol A and thalidomide in human pluripotent stem cells
Article.Authors: Otsuka S.; Qin X.; Ito T.; Nansai H.; Hashizume M.; Katsura M.; Kobayashi M.; Taguchi A.; Wada Y.; Kohro T.; Abe K.; Nakao Y.; Sone H.
Article.Abstract: Evaluating epigenetic toxicity during early development is important for understanding how chemical exposure may influence developmental trajectories. We compared the effects of bisphenol A (BPA) and thalidomide (TMD) on differentiation, gene expression, and enhancer-associated epigenetic states in human embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). TMD produced more fold-change-defined responsive genes than BPA and a larger set of genes shared across conditions, together with locus-specific H3K27ac changes near LEFTY2 , MT1X , and MT1H . These responses were associated with altered expression of lineage-related genes during subsequent differentiation. In contrast, BPA produced fewer responsive genes, with limited initial H3K27ac changes but altered lineage-associated gene expression during embryoid body differentiation. Notably, both chemicals were associated with changes in lineage markers, including HAND1 , FOXA2 , and SOX1 , although the patterns differed between the two cell lines and across developmental stages. These findings suggest that BPA and TMD elicit divergent epigenetic and transcriptional responses in human pluripotent stem cells and highlight the value of comparative pluripotent stem cell models and epigenomic analyses for understanding chemical effects during early developmental stages. They further raise the possibility that even subtle differences in cellular state at the time of exposure may influence subsequent responses to chemical perturbation.

Article.Title: Short-term interaction of Fe(II)–GMZ bentonite under hydro-thermo-mechanical conditions
Article.Authors: Zhang M.; Tian L.; Xie J.; Xu X.; Lu Z.
Article.Abstract: The interface reaction between the bentonite buffer barrier and the metal disposal canister is one of the key factors affecting the long-term safety of high-level radioactive waste geological disposal repository. To investigate the short-term interactions between Fe(II) corrosion products and Gaomiaozi(GMZ) bentonite under low-to-moderate temperature and confining pressure, GMZ bentonite is selected as the test material. An independently developed THCM reaction platform is used to conduct Fe(II)-bentonite contact reaction experiments under different Fe(II) concentrations, temperatures, confining pressures and solution conditions. The ion composition of the suspension after the reaction and the changes in the solid-phase mineral structure are analyzed by atomic absorption spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. The results showed that contact with Fe(II) caused a rapid redistribution of aqueous cations, including an increase in the Na⁺ concentration, which is consistent with cation exchange involving the montmorillonite. Increasing the reaction time and temperature affected the aqueous ion composition and the local hydration and bonding environments of the solid phase. However, the XRD and FTIR results don’t provide conclusive evidence for structural Fe incorporation or montmorillonite-to-illite transformation. These findings provide laboratory-scale information on the short-term interaction between Fe(II)-bearing solutions and GMZ bentonite powder, while further validation using highly compacted bentonite is required before extrapolation to repository buffer conditions.

Article.Title: Quad-directional frequency-aware state space modeling for low-light image enhancement
Article.Authors: Mothe S.; Srinivas K.
Article.Abstract: Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) is a fundamental inverse problem in computational photography characterised by spatially non-uniform underexposure, amplified photon shot noise, and inter-channel colour imbalance. State-of-the-art (SOTA) Transformer based methods achieve compelling global context modelling but impose quadratic self-attention complexity, precluding efficient deployment at high resolutions. We present QDFA-SSM, a novel end-to-end framework built entirely on selective State Space Models (SSMs). Three principled architectural components constitute our design. First, a Quad-Directional Visual Mamba Encoder (QD-VME) scans 2D feature maps along four spatial orientations horizontal forward/backward and vertical forward/backward recovering isotropic long-range illumination context at strictly $$\mathscr {O}(N)$$ complexity via hardware efficient parallel scanning. Second, a Frequency-Aware SSM Decoder (FA-SSMD) decomposes decoder features into low- and high-frequency spectral bands via 2D FFT, applying independent SSM chains to each band to separately optimise global luminance consistency and local texture fidelity, preventing cross-band interference. Third, a Spatially-Adaptive Illumination Modulator (SAIM) estimates pixel-wise enhancement weight maps conditioned on local Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) maps, concentrating correction capacity on severely underexposed regions without requiring additional supervision. Evaluated on the LOL-v1 benchmark, QDFA-SSM attains PSNR = 25.15 dB and SSIM = 0.863, which improves upon the strongest prior selective-SSM baselines MMamba-LLIE and LatentDark by $$+0.67$$ dB and $$+0.42$$ dB respectively, and upon the Retinex-guided Transformer baselines represented by Retinexformer and LLFormer. These gains are obtained with 1.340 M parameters and 32.105 GFLOPs at 41.53 FPS on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU. It may be noted that the proposed model is not the smallest or the fastest among the compared methods; rather, it is reported here as offering the most favourable balance between restoration accuracy and computational cost.

Article.Title: Numerical modeling of the effect of cross-sectional shape on the interaction between dip-slip faults and underground tunnels
Article.Authors: Ghavami S.; Delnavaz N.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the interaction between normal and reverse dip-slip faults and tunnels with circular, square, and horseshoe-shaped cross-sections using validated two-dimensional finite element models, with the tunnel axis assumed to be parallel to the fault strike. The effects of cross-sectional geometry, equivalent diameter (4 and 6 m), burial depth (7 and 10 m), and tunnel position relative to the free-field rupture path were evaluated under a fault dip angle of 60° and a fault throw of 4 m. The results showed that tunnel geometry and position substantially influenced rupture propagation, ground surface displacement, lining stress, and soil–lining separation. Under the investigated faulting conditions, reverse faulting produced a more critical structural response than normal faulting because of its compression-dominated loading regime; at a burial depth of 10 m, peak lining stresses under reverse faulting were approximately 3–7 times those under normal faulting. Circular tunnels exhibited the most stable response owing to their continuous curvature and more uniform load redistribution, whereas square tunnels were the most vulnerable because of stress concentrations at their corners and the lower flexural rigidity of their flat walls. Larger tunnel diameters and greater burial depths generally increased lining stresses and intensified rupture–tunnel interaction. Their influence on rigid-body rotation was mechanism-dependent, increasing under normal faulting but decreasing under reverse faulting. Reverse faulting also caused soil–lining separation in all examined configurations and relative tunnel positions. The findings highlight the importance of cross-sectional geometry in fault-resistant tunnel design and support the use of circular sections, localized reinforcement, ground improvement, and ductile lining systems in active fault zones.

Article.Title: Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging-based measures of arterial signal-enhancement in patients with peripheral artery disease
Article.Authors: Khagi B.; Belousova T.; Short C.; Taylor A.; Bismuth J.; Shah D.; Brunner G.
Article.Abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD), a form of atherosclerosis of the lower extremities (LE), affects both large vessels and the microcirculation. PAD is associated with intermittent claudication (IC) pain, reduced mobility, and an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) of 56 participants (36 PAD patients with IC and 20 matched controls) were acquired at the mid-calf position to quantitatively assess first-pass perfusion in major LE arteries. Arterial signal intensity curves (ASIC) were derived for the anterior tibialis, posterior tibialis, and the peroneal (PE) arteries, representing the respective arterial signal dynamics including local pre-contrast arrival times and peak signal intensities. Several measures were derived from the individual and envelope arterial (composite) measures, each representing signal enhancement (SE), time to peak enhancement (TP), slope of the signal enhancement, and the area under the curve (AUC). Our experimental findings show that higher SE, TP, and AUC were observed in matched controls compared with PAD patients during arterial signal enhancement, suggesting impaired arterial circulation in claudicants. Several arterial measures including TP, SE, and the AUC differed significantly between PAD patients with compared to those without concomitant diabetes, whereas established PAD markers such as the resting and exercise ankle-brachial index (ABI), exercise capacity as measured by treadmill peak walking time and claudication onset time, calf muscle area, and renal function did not. In other analyses involving both legs, PAD patients exhibited significant arterial hemodynamics asymmetry with reduced SE, TP, and AUC in the target leg as compared with the contralateral limb. Among PAD patients with concomitant diabetes, the asymmetry was more pronounced and showed that the maximum and median TP, maximum AUC, sum of AUCs, and envelope AUCs were significantly lower in the target leg compared with the contralateral side. Several of the proposed CE-MRI variables of arterial hemodynamics were significantly associated with key clinical markers of PAD. CE-MRI-derived measures of arterial hemodynamics differentiate PAD patients from matched controls and also identify claudicants with concomitant diabetes who are known to present with an elevated risk for adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The proposed imaging measures could be of interest in the study of PAD status and severity.

Article.Title: Fiber diameter measurement for electrospun fibrous mats using scanning electron microscopic images: a protocol toward standardized characterization
Article.Authors: Pirsalami S.; Mottaghifard Z.; Goetz A.
Article.Abstract: Fiber diameter is a key characteristic of electrospun fibrous mats. This study aims to take a step forward in developing a protocol for standardized measurement of fiber diameter using scanning electron microscope (SEM) images. Manual and Automatic measurement (AM) methods (General Image Fiber Tool: GIFT) are applied to SEM images at magnifications of 2 kx and 4 kx. Results suggest that measurement on a synthetic image composed of fibers with constant diameter in the range studied be reported as a reference for minimum measurement variability. Fiber Based Method (FBM) which considers one contribution from each fiber in a SEM image is introduced. It was found that the average, minimum and maximum fiber diameter could be different from results obtained by Conventional Method (CM) which considers all measurements on a SEM image. FBM is suggested to be a better representative of individual visible fibers and reduce the bias associated with unequal numbers of local measurements per fiber. In addition, bin size for fiber diameter histograms is suggested to be set between the pixel size of the image for AM or the average measurement variability for manual methods, and 20% of the span of fiber diameters. Furthermore, “Fiber Index” as a criterion for evaluation and reporting of fiber diameter along with average and standard deviation is introduced.

Article.Title: Q-learning-based energy-aware parent selection and adaptive Trickle control for RPL in smart city IoT networks
Article.Authors: Venkateswararao K.; Swarup Kumar J.; M. Modi T.; Kumar Bonthagorla P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Smart city applications such as garbage management, water management, traffic control, and streetlight automation demand adaptive, energy-efficient, and scalable communication protocols. RPL (Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks) is an extensively used routing protocol, especially for IoT-based networks that contain constrained nodes with limited energy, memory, and processing power. This work proposes an enhanced RPL-based routing algorithm that combines Q-learning-based energy-aware parent selection with heuristic adaptive Trickle interval control. The Q-learning component selects rank-valid parent nodes using link quality, residual energy, packet delivery, delay, and routing overhead, while a Q-value hysteresis threshold is used to limit unnecessary parent changes. The adaptive Trickle mechanism adjusts the routing-control interval according to short-term network conditions while retaining the standard Trickle suppression rule. The proposed algorithm was evaluated in the Cooja simulator for node densities ranging from 80 to 400 nodes, Tx/Rx ranges of 60–100 m, and Random Walk and Random Waypoint mobility models. The performance was compared with MRHOF, RPL*, and Q-RPL using PDR, latency, average power consumption, energy efficiency, routing overhead, parent switching rate, and end-to-end delay. At 400 nodes and a 60 m Tx/Rx range, the proposed algorithm improved PDR over Q-RPL by 4.2% under RWM and 4.3% under RWPM. Energy efficiency improved by 12.7% and 12.5%, while routing overhead was reduced by 23.5% and 21.4%, parent switching rate by 45.5% and 44.3%, and end-to-end delay by 15.3% and 15.1%, under RWM and RWPM, respectively. These results indicate that combining learned parent selection with adaptive Trickle control improves routing reliability, stability, and energy utilization in dynamic smart city IoT networks.

Article.Title: Relationship between serum soluble HLA-G levels and clinico- pathological characteristics of endometrial cancer
Article.Authors: Li E.; Hong Y.; Li C.; Liang H.; Chen Q.
Article.Abstract: This retrospective case-control study was performed to investigate the associations between serum soluble human leukocyte antigen-G (sHLA-G) concentrations and clinicopathological parameters in patients with endometrial cancer (EC). Between September 2022 and July 2025, EC patients who underwent hysteroscopy or surgical staging at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Kiang Wu Hospital were enrolled as the case group. Age-matched patients receiving hysteroscopy with pathologically confirmed benign endometrium during the same period served as the control group. Comprehensive clinical data and postoperative pathological reports of all EC patients were collected. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was utilized to quantify serum sHLA-G concentrations in all participants. Immunohistochemistry was performed to detect HLA-G expression in tumour tissues. Histological subtypes were stratified according to the 2023 FIGO endometrial cancer risk classification into non-aggressive and aggressive histological subtypes. Exploratory receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was conducted for the aggressive subgroup; these ROC-derived metrics are hypothesis-generating only and lack independent external validation. No statistically significant difference in serum sHLA-G levels was observed between 55 EC patients and 56 control subjects ( p > 0.05). Patients with aggressive histological subtypes exhibited significantly higher serum sHLA-G levels than those with non-aggressive histological subtypes ( P = 0.033; n = 6 in the aggressive subgroup). Among 53 patients with endometrioid carcinoma, sHLA-G concentrations did not differ significantly across tumor differentiation grades (G1, G2, G3, p > 0.05). In the subgroup of 36 patients receiving complete surgical staging, serum sHLA-G showed no correlation with myometrial invasion depth (< 1/2 vs. > 1/2 myometrium, p > 0.05). Similarly, sHLA-G levels were comparable between patients with versus without lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), and between patients with versus without lymph node metastasis (all p > 0.05). No significant association was observed between serum sHLA-G and tissue HLA-G immunohistochemical status. In conclusion, serum sHLA-G concentrations were not elevated in EC patients relative to individuals with benign endometrium. Within the endometrioid carcinoma subgroup, sHLA-G showed no significant correlation with tumor differentiation, LVSI or lymph node metastasis. An exploratory positive association was observed between higher serum sHLA-G and aggressive histological subtypes. This finding requires validation in larger independent cohorts and does not currently establish sHLA-G as a marker of tumour invasiveness or as a diagnostic or prognostic biomarker.

Article.Title: Development and internal validation of survival models for predicting a composite clinical endpoint using clinical variables and quantitative SPECT/CT imaging features
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; Zhao Y.; Wu Z.; Zhang X.; Wang Y.; Yang M.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Quantitative parameters derived from single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI) may provide prognostic information in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). This study aimed to develop and internally validate survival models for a composite clinical endpoint (CCE) comprising cardiovascular readmission, coronary revascularization, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and death by integrating clinical variables with quantitative SPECT-MPI parameters. A total of 1,674 patients with suspected or confirmed CAD who underwent resting gated SPECT-MPI were retrospectively included and randomly divided into a training set ( n = 1,171) and an internal validation set ( n = 503). Quantitative perfusion, left ventricular function, and phase parameters were extracted from SPECT-MPI images. Seven survival models were evaluated: Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH), LASSO Cox, single decision tree (RPart), random survival forest (RSF), gradient boosting machine (GBM), support vector machine (SVM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Clinical variables and quantitative imaging features were considered as candidate predictors. Feature selection and model development were performed using the training set, while the internal validation set was kept separate from model fitting and hyperparameter tuning. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), graphical calibration, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). For XGBoost-based risk stratification, a risk-score cut-off derived exclusively from the training set was applied unchanged to the internal validation set, and event-free survival was compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis. During a median follow-up of 36.6 months (interquartile range, 20.5-58.7 months), 662 patients (39.5%) experienced the CCE. The retained imaging features included phase entropy, total perfusion deficit (TPD), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Adding phase entropy to TPD and LVEF resulted in minimal improvement in validation-set discrimination (ΔC-index = 0.0009; 95% CI, − 0.0072 to 0.0090). RPart showed the highest 60-month AUC in the training set (0.825) but declined to 0.600 in the internal validation set, indicating substantial overfitting. In contrast, CoxPH, LASSO Cox, RSF, GBM, and XGBoost showed broadly comparable discrimination in the internal validation set, with 60-month AUCs ranging from 0.702 to 0.717 and C-indices from 0.662 to 0.674. XGBoost was subsequently used for exploratory risk stratification, rather than selected on the basis of superior discrimination. SVM showed weak and unstable discrimination, with a validation C-index of 0.508 (95% CI, 0.454-0.538) and a 60-month validation AUC of 0.483 (95% CI, 0.417-0.548). Graphical calibration showed general agreement between predicted and observed risks, although deviations were present for some models and time points. DCA showed positive net benefit for several models over portions of the evaluated threshold-probability range, without consistent dominance of a single model. The training-derived XGBoost risk-score cut-off separated patients into groups with significantly different event-free survival when applied unchanged to the internal validation set (log-rank P < 0.0001). Survival models integrating clinical variables with quantitative SPECT-MPI parameters provided moderate discrimination for the CCE. ML models did not demonstrate a clear discrimination advantage over CoxPH in the internal validation set, and RPart showed substantial overfitting. XGBoost was used for exploratory risk stratification, and the training-derived threshold separated patients into groups with different event-free survival when applied unchanged to the internal validation set; however, its discrimination was broadly comparable with that of several other models. These findings do not establish the superiority of a particular modeling approach. External validation using well-defined and independently adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes is required before clinical application.

Article.Title: Outcomes of transplanted organs from donors with cardiac arrest by hanging in a nationwide Japanese cohort
Article.Authors: Hagiwara M.; Yumoto T.; Ueda Y.; Tokioka K.; Hongo T.; Obara T.; Nojima T.; Tsukahara K.; Naito H.; Nakao A.
Article.Abstract: The suitability of organs from cardiac arrest by hanging (CAH) donors remains controversial because of concerns regarding hypoxic organ injury. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Japan Organ Transplant Network database to evaluate transplant outcomes and organ yield among donors with a history of cardiac arrest between 2010 and 2023. Donors were categorized into CAH and cardiac arrest by non-hanging (CANH) groups. The primary outcome was graft survival by organ type, and the secondary outcome was the number of organs procured. A total of 415 donation after brain death donors (113 CAH, 302 CANH) and 161 donation after circulatory death donors (36 CAH, 125 CANH) were included. Among selected transplanted grafts, graft survival did not differ significantly between the CAH and CANH groups across organ types, and no significant associations were observed after adjustment for donor and recipient characteristics. Although the crude number of organs procured was higher in the CAH group, CAH donor status was not independently associated with organ yield. These findings support consideration of appropriately selected organs from CAH donors.

Article.Title: Fractional-order chaos–driven multi-stage image encryption scheme with an FPGA realization
Article.Authors: Megalli Y.; Edward P.; Alexan W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of image-centric applications in cloud, IoT/edge, and wireless multimedia systems has intensified the need for encryption schemes that simultaneously deliver strong security and practical real-time implementations. This manuscript proposes a software-hardware co-design of a fractional-order chaos-driven, multiple-layer image encryption pipeline that merges multiple color images, converts them to a $$1\textrm{D}$$ bitstream, and applies consecutive XOR–substitution stages powered by independent fractional-order hyperchaotic generators: a $$5\textrm{D}$$ fractional-order memristive hyperchaotic system, an $$8\textrm{D}$$ fractional-order Chen hyperchaotic system, and a $$10\textrm{D}$$ fractional-order Chen hyperchaotic system, with dynamic S-boxes generated per layer. On standard $$256\times 256$$ test images (USC-SIPI), the scheme achieves near-ideal randomness and diffusion with average encrypted image entropy $$H_E=7.99855$$ , very low post-encryption adjacent-pixel correlations (near zero), and strong differential resistance with NPCR and UACI values very close to their ideal targets; encryption distortion metrics further indicate effective concealment (average PSNR $$=8.06821~\textrm{dB}$$ , MAE $$=82.3120$$ , MSE $$=10146.0$$ ), while decryption is lossless (SSIM $$=1$$ for all reported images). The generated S-boxes exhibit competitive cryptographic properties (NL $$=106$$ –110, SAC $$\approx 0.493$$ –0.505, BIC $$=104$$ –108, DAP $$=0.015625$$ ), the key-stream passes NIST SP 800–22 with all p -values $$>0.01$$ , and the estimated key space is $$2^{2604}$$ . Efficiency is demonstrated in software ( $$0.0482414~\textrm{s}$$ for $$256\times 256$$ ; $$1.33031~\textrm{s}$$ for $$1024\times 1024$$ ) and via an FPGA-oriented architecture on an Artix-7 (XC7A35T) achieving $$78.64~\textrm{Mbps}$$ throughput with $$0.021798~\textrm{s}$$ execution time and minimal resource utilization ( $$\sim 1\%$$ LUT, $$0\%$$ BRAM/DSP), supporting embedded real-time cryptography.

Article.Title: The indirect association of emotional intelligence with self-reported performance-related outcomes through psychological resilience in athletes
Article.Authors: Kan E.; Han M.; Yarayan Y.; Solmaz S.; Alkhamees N.; Al-Mhanna S.; Gilyana M.; Batrakoulis A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to examine the relationships between emotional intelligence and self-reported performance-related outcomes (psychological performance and subjective athletic performance satisfaction) in athletes, and to evaluate the indirect role of psychological resilience in these relationships. The research was conducted using a quantitative, cross-sectional design. A total of 403 national-team athletes aged between 18 and 38 years voluntarily participated. Data were collected through self-report measures of emotional intelligence, psychological resilience, psychological performance, and aggression, together with a visual analog scale assessing subjective athletic performance satisfaction. Direct and indirect associations were estimated using path analysis with observed composite scores. Statistical inference was based on 95% bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence intervals obtained from 10,000 resamples, with aggression included as an auxiliary covariate. Emotional intelligence was positively associated with psychological resilience (β = 0.586, 95% BCa CI [0.495, 0.670]), and psychological resilience was positively associated with psychological performance (β = 0.469, 95% BCa CI [0.368, 0.559]) and subjective athletic performance satisfaction (β = 0.170, 95% BCa CI [0.054, 0.286]). The adjusted direct associations of emotional intelligence with psychological performance (β = 0.013, 95% BCa CI [-0.093, 0.121]) and subjective athletic performance satisfaction (β = 0.117, 95% BCa CI [-0.004, 0.231]) were not supported because their confidence intervals included zero. Significant indirect associations through psychological resilience were observed for psychological performance (β = 0.275, 95% BCa CI [0.205, 0.354]) and subjective athletic performance satisfaction (β = 0.100, 95% BCa CI [0.032, 0.176]). After accounting for aggression as an auxiliary covariate, the findings indicate that psychological resilience is an important statistical pathway linking emotional intelligence with self-reported performance-related outcomes. Because the study was cross-sectional, the results should be interpreted as directional associations rather than causal effects. Because all outcomes were self-reported with satisfaction assessed by a single item and the psychological performance measure showing mixed confirmatory factor analysis fit these associations should be interpreted with caution.

Article.Title: A TCN-KANformer-MDN model for engine remaining useful life prediction
Article.Authors: Xu J.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life of aircraft engines is critical to the safety of aircraft operations. Targeting the two problems of modeling complex nonlinear degradation relationships and quantifying prediction uncertainty, this paper proposes a novel RUL prediction model that integrates a temporal convolutional network (TCN), KANformer, and a mixture density network (MDN). In the proposed framework, the TCN is first employed to extract multi-scale temporal dependency features from the degradation sequences. Subsequently, the KANformer is introduced to perform nonlinear transformations on the extracted features, leveraging its learnable basis functions to enhance the model’s capacity for characterizing complex degradation patterns. Finally, the MDN outputs a probability density distribution of the RUL, thereby enabling quantitative uncertainty quantification of the predictions. Experimental validation on the NASA C-MAPSS dataset demonstrates that, in comparison with benchmark methods such as Cau-DA-LSTM, the proposed TCN-KANformer-MDN model achieves approximately 10% improvement in both prediction accuracy and uncertainty quantification metrics, fully corroborating its effectiveness and robustness under complex operating conditions.

Article.Title: Case series of combined microabrasion, home bleaching and resin infiltration for moderate-to-severe dental fluorosis
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Yu Q.; Meng X.; Cao Y.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Fluorosis is a common dental condition with a high prevalence rate, significantly impacting both aesthetics and psychological health. Traditional treatment methods often show limited results and may carry certain side effects. This study aimed to investigate the short- and medium-term clinical efficacy of a combined treatment protocol including enamel microabrasion, at-home bleaching, and resin infiltration for the management of moderate to severe dental fluorosis. A total of 74 fluorosed teeth in five patients were included in this study and classified as moderate fluorosis ( n = 29) and severe fluorosis ( n = 45). All patients received a three-step sequential treatment protocol consisting of enamel microabrasion, at-home bleaching, and resin infiltration. Follow-up assessments were conducted after one week and three years of treatment. Treatment outcomes, tooth sensitivity, and patient satisfaction were evaluated using the visual analogue scale (VAS). Changes in tooth appearance were summarized within each patient, and exploratory patient-level comparisons between T1 and T2 were performed separately for moderate and severe fluorosis using two-sided exact Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. One week post-treatment, both moderate and severe fluorosed teeth exhibited notable improvements in both white spots and yellow stains. At three-year follow-up, only a slight decrease in aesthetic improvement was observed in a small number of teeth. Exploratory patient-level analyses detected no significant changes between the two time points in either severity group (all exact P ≥ 0.500). No discomfort or sensitivity was reported during microabrasion, resin infiltration or post-treatment. The combination of microabrasion, at-home bleaching, and resin infiltration offered a minimally invasive and effective approach for moderate-to-severe dental fluorosis, yielding high levels of patient satisfaction. Clinical follow-up over the medium-term demonstrated the stability and safety of this combined protocol.

Article.Title: Humic acid urea improved grain yield and farmer’s profits while mitigating the carbon footprint of wheat production
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Zhang S.; Li Y.; Xu M.; Wen Y.; Zhao B.; Yuan L.
Article.Abstract: Enhancing crop yield and reducing active nitrogen (N) loss are crucial for the efficient utilization of N fertilizer and the decrease of agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Humic acid urea (HAU), an efficient N fertilizer produced via in-situ incorporating small amounts of humic acid into urea production, has reached to 1 Tg of physical quantity of annual production in China for its efficiency enhanced via the comprehensive regulation on fertilizer-crop-soil systems. Therefore, we hypothesized that HAU would increase yield and reduce the carbon footprint relative to CU, and tested it in a winter wheat experiment at two N rates (225 and 180 kg ha⁻ 1 ) in the North China Plain. The results showed that the application of HAU resulted in a significantly higher grain yield by 7.0–23.3% than CU, and thus significantly increased farmer’s profits by 8.8–29.8%. HAU production resulted in more GHG emission than CU production by 6.9 kg CO 2 -eq Mg −1 ; however, the GHG emission from the field was significantly reduced (10.1–23.3%) by reducing gaseous N loss. In the whole life cycle, HAU resulted in lower GHG emissions (1.9–14.4%) in the winter wheat agroecosystem. HAU application also contributed to higher C fixation and ecosystem economic benefit. HAU at 180 kg ha −1 achieved a comparable yield and farmer’s profit with CU at 225 kg N ha −1 , while reduced GHG emission by 14.4%. Applicating HAU is an advantageous N management strategy for maintaining wheat yield with the lowest C footprint.

Article.Title: Bio-electrochemical swarm intelligence with quantum constrained graph learning for distributed battery optimization in urban microgrids
Article.Authors: Lande M.; Shrivastava D.; Gadge G.; Marghade D.; Gajghate S.; Dennison M.; Das S.; Noor M.; Shelare S.
Article.Abstract: The integration of distributed battery storage in urban microgrids is becoming increasingly common. Yet, most existing methods for optimizing urban microgrid operation are incapable of jointly representing battery physics, device-to-device relationships, and the temporal variability of intermittent renewable generation. Conventional swarm and deterministic methods also commonly rely on random initialization, homogeneous agent behavior, or post-hoc constraint handling. Therefore, this research proposes a unifying framework that integrates five key components into a single pipeline: (1) Bio-Electrochemical Swarm Field Initialization (BESFI); (2) Adaptive Multi-Species Co-Evolutionary Swarm Routing (AMSCESR); (3) a Spatio-Temporal Energy Diffusion Graph Transformer (STED-GT); (4) Quantum-Inspired Stability-Constrained Optimization (QISCO); and (5) a Digital Twin Reinforcement Validation Engine (DT-RVE). The novelty lies in the closed coupling of physics-aware initialization, role-diverse swarm search, relational graph learning, in-loop stability filtering, and digital-twin reinforcement validation rather than in any isolated module. On the reported 25-node urban microgrid testbed, the framework achieved 95.8% dispatch accuracy, 94.6% energy efficiency, ± 3.7% voltage deviation, ± 0.019 Hz frequency deviation, 10.6% capacity fade, and 2.3 s supervisory adaptation latency. These results indicate improved load balancing, grid stability, battery-life preservation, and adaptive operation within the evaluated simulation conditions.

Article.Title: Development of a three-stage randomized response model for sensitive surveys with a case study on drug consumption
Article.Authors: Bhavani C.; Danish F.
Article.Abstract: Randomized response methods are commonly used in sensitive surveys to reduce response bias and to protect respondent confidentiality. However, existing randomized response models cannot achieve high estimation efficiency without sacrificing privacy. In this paper we propose a new three-stage randomization model to estimate the population proportion of a sensitive characteristic. The proposed model adds an extra stage of response, which allows the response mechanism to be more flexible and improves the precision of estimation. Expressions for variance and percentage relative efficiency (PRE) are derived to study the theoretical properties of the proposed model. Its performance is compared with the Warner, Huang, and Govardhana and Sarjinder randomized response models under different values of the sensitive proportion and different sample sizes. The simulation studies conducted on a large scale and the real drug consumption survey show that the proposed model always has lower variance and higher PRE than the existing models. The empirical results indicate that the proposed three-stage randomized response model is a more efficient and reliable framework for sensitive surveys while preserving the privacy of the respondents.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of combined oral dutasteride 0.5 mg and minoxidil 2.5 mg versus dutasteride or minoxidil monotherapy in male androgenetic alopecia
Article.Authors: Babakhani S.; Kashani M.; Samadi A.; Zahedi A.; Firooz A.
Article.Abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the leading cause of hair loss in men, impacting nearly 80% throughout their lives and frequently associated with significant psychosocial burden. Current FDA-approved therapies, such as topical minoxidil and oral finasteride, face challenges related to adherence, scalp irritation, and concerns about sexual side effects. Dutasteride, a dual type I and II 5α-reductase inhibitor along with low-dose oral minoxidil (LDOM) has recently been recognized as a potential off-label systemic therapy. Although each agent has demonstrated effectiveness on its own, there is limited evidence on their combined application. This double-blind, randomized, three-arm clinical trial enrolled 45 men with mild-to-moderate AGA, who were randomly assigned to receive (1) dutasteride 0.5 mg + minoxidil 2.5 mg, (2) dutasteride 0.5 mg, or (3) minoxidil 2.5 mg daily for 6 months. Efficacy was evaluated using TrichoScan parameters (hair count, hair shaft diameter, terminal hair rate), standardized scalp photography, patient satisfaction, and Investigator Global Assessment (IGA). Safety was evaluated through monitoring for adverse event and conducting laboratory tests. Thirty-nine participants completed the study. At 6 months, adjusted mean hair counts were 181.8 in the combination group, 167.3 in the dutasteride monotherapy group, and 156.0 in the LDOM monotherapy group. However, ANCOVA did not demonstrate a statistically significant overall between-group difference in hair count (P = 0.055), and the difference between combination therapy and LDOM monotherapy was also not statistically significant (mean difference, 25.8 hairs; 95% CI, − 0.16 to 51.90; P = 0.052). Terminal hair rate differed significantly among the treatment groups (P = 0.01), with a higher adjusted mean value in the combination group than in the LDOM monotherapy group (70.3% vs. 63.5%; P = 0.01). Hair shaft diameter increased over time without a statistically significant between-group difference. IGA scores were higher in the combination group than in either monotherapy group (P < 0.001 for both comparisons). Patient satisfaction did not differ significantly among groups (P = 0.107). Two participants discontinued treatment because of adverse events, and no serious adverse events were reported. All three treatment regimens were associated with improvements in hair parameters over the 6-month treatment period. The combination group had numerically higher adjusted mean hair count and terminal hair rate, but the between-group difference in hair count did not reach statistical significance. Statistically significant between-group differences were observed for terminal hair rate and Investigator Global Assessment. Larger, adequately powered studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these findings are reproducible and to further evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of combination therapy.

Article.Title: Green synthesis of multifunctional silver nanoparticles using Ocimum tenuiflorum L. inflorescence extract for potential antimicrobial and photocatalytic applications
Article.Authors: Ghosh B.; Bose A.; Nayak S.
Article.Abstract: Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using plant-derived resources offers an alternative approach to conventional nanoparticle synthesis by utilizing naturally occurring phytoconstituents as reducing and stabilizing agents. In the present study, silver nanoparticles were synthesized using an aqueous inflorescence extract of Ocimum tenuiflorum L. (Tulsi) and systematically evaluated for their physicochemical characteristics and multifunctional properties. The synthesized Tulsi inflorescence-mediated AgNPs (TI-AgNPs) exhibited a characteristic surface plasmon resonance band at 428 nm, while TEM analysis showed nanoparticles within the 20–90 nm size range and XRD confirmed their crystalline nature. FTIR analysis indicated the involvement of hydroxyl, carbonyl, and other oxygen-containing functional groups in nanoparticle formation and stabilization. The TI-AgNPs demonstrated broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, with MIC values ranging from 8 to 64 µg/mL against the tested bacterial and fungal strains. DPPH assay showed concentration-dependent antioxidant activity, while the nanoparticles exhibited an IC₅₀ value of 634.71 µg/mL in HEK-293 cells. In addition, TI-AgNPs achieved 93.4% methylene blue removal within 60 min under sunlight irradiation. Overall, the findings demonstrate that O. tenuiflorum L inflorescence can serve as a plant-based source for the synthesis of multifunctional AgNPs with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and dye-removal properties, supporting their further investigation for potential biomedical and environmental applications.

Article.Title: Two year randomised trial of twice versus once daily 0.01% atropine for childhood myopia control with real world extension
Article.Authors: He M.; Zhang L.; Tang C.; Bi W.; Wang L.; Zhang S.; Zhang Z.; Du B.; Wei R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To assess the efficacy of 0.01% atropine eye drops in myopia control with different frequencies (nightly versus twice daily) over a two-year period. Children aged 6 to 13 years with a post-cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) between − 0.75 and − 6.00 D were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive 0.01% atropine either nightly (QD) or twice daily (BID) during Phase I (the first year). Participants were then given the option to continue into Phase II (the second year), a real-world extension phase without randomization. The primary endpoint was axial length (AL) change over two years; SER change was a key secondary endpoint. A two-year follow-up was completed for 20 and 28 participants in the QD and BID groups, respectively. Over two years, the adjusted increase in AL was 0.523 mm in the QD group and 0.372 mm in the BID group, with an adjusted between-group difference of − 0.132 mm (95% CI − 0.246 to − 0.019; P = 0.023). Adjusted SER progression was − 1.087 D in the QD group and − 0.447 D in the BID group, with an adjusted difference of 0.640 D (95% CI 0.351 to 0.930; P < 0.001). During Phase II, no significant between-group differences were found in AL or SER changes ( P = 0.916 and P = 0.247). Twice-daily 0.01% atropine was associated with slower myopia progression over two years, but no significant additional benefit was observed during the second year in this small real-world extension.
