Article.Title: A comprehensive study of the stellar cluster ADS 16795 using Gaia DR3 astrometric data
Article.Authors: Badawy W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Open clusters consist of stars that formed at nearly the same time, making them valuable laboratories for testing theories of star formation, stellar evolution, and dynamical processes within the Galactic disc. In this study, we present a detailed astrometric and photometric analysis of the candidate open cluster ADS16795 using Gaia DR3 data. We note that the physical nature of this system is debated in the literature, with some studies classifying it as a moving group or unbound trapezium system. We apply the Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) algorithm to the Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) astrometric dataset in order to identify probable cluster members and derive the cluster’s fundamental parameters, including its location, age, distance, mass function, and total mass. Applying a minimum membership probability threshold of $$P > 90\%$$ , the HDBSCAN algorithm identified 97 probable member stars. From the derived distance modulus ( $$6.68 \pm 0.05$$ mag) and reddening ( $$0.17 \pm 0.02$$ mag), we obtain a cluster distance of $$0.217 \pm 0.005$$ kpc and an age of $$\log (\textrm{age}) = 7.50 \pm 0.05$$ yr. By fitting PARSEC v1.2S stellar isochrones, we estimate a cluster age of approximately 31.6 Myr and a relaxation time of $$\sim 130$$ Myr. The slope of the present-day mass function ( $$\alpha = -2.65 \pm 0.271$$ ) is in good agreement with the classical Salpeter value. Given the cluster’s young age ( $$\sim 31.6$$ Myr) and low dynamical evolution parameter ( $$\tau = 0.25$$ ), indicating that it has completed only about 25% of its relaxation time, the present-day mass function is expected to closely approximate the initial mass function. The total mass of the detected member stars is estimated to be $$46.6 \pm 0.3 \, M_{\odot }$$ , based solely on the 97 identified probable members and without correction for incompleteness. Using the galpy Python package, we derive the cluster’s kinematics and Galactic orbital parameters from the subset of 17 (of the 97) stars with available Gaia DR3 radial velocity measurements, obtaining a mean radial velocity of $$-14.1\pm {1.2}$$ km s $$^{-1}$$ . In light of these results, we can now revisit the system’s classification: the low dynamical evolution parameter, the young age, and the unbound nature of the system’s trapezium core indicate that ADS16795 is better described as a young, dissolving stellar aggregate or unbound association rather than a gravitationally bound open cluster in the classical sense.

Article.Title: CXCL8 and CXCL12 genetic variants and serum protein levels in male patients with laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Nagele E.; Liutkevicius V.; Liutkeviciene R.; Vilkeviciute-Petraite A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) is a common respiratory malignancy with increasing incidence and a strong association with lifestyle and environmental risk factors. Currently, there are no reliable biomarkers for early detection or prognosis of LSCC. CXCL8 is a proinflammatory chemokine that promotes angiogenesis, tumor growth, and migration, and its genetic variants have been linked to increased cancer risk and poor outcomes. CXCL12 plays a critical role in tumor cell migration, invasion, metastasis, and angiogenesis through the CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling axis. This study aims to investigate the role of CXCL8 and CXCL12 genetic variants, as well as their protein levels, in male patients with LSCC. In all, 300 healthy male controls and 256 male LSCC patients took part in the study. The salting-out technique was used to extract deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). For genotyping ( CXCL12 rs1029153, rs1801157, rs2297630, and CXCL8 rs2227306), real-time polymerase chain reaction was used. Serum levels were measured by the ELISA method. IBM SPSS Statistics 30.0.0.0 was used to perform statistical analysis. CXCL8 serum levels were significantly higher in LSCC males than in controls (median (IQR): 14.47 (4.89) vs. 12.71 (4.20) pg/ml, p = 0.014). ROC curve analysis demonstrated a modest discriminative ability for CXCL8 (AUC = 0.660, 95% CI: 0.540–0.780, p = 0.009). At the optimal cut-off value of 12.170 pg/ml, selected to maximize sensitivity for screening purposes, serum CXCL8 yielded a sensitivity of 85.0% and a specificity of 42.5%. Although initial unadjusted analyses indicated nominal associations between CXCL12 rs1029153 and rs2297630 variants and advanced LSCC characteristics, none retained significance after Bonferroni adjustment, highlighting their purely exploratory nature. Serum CXCL8 levels were modestly higher in LSCC patients; however, given its limited discrimination (AUC = 0.660) and the absence of validation, serum CXCL8 does not possess clinical utility as a standalone screening or diagnostic biomarker for male LSCC but represents an exploratory finding reflecting tumor-associated inflammation. These findings warrant further investigation into larger independent cohorts and functional studies to determine their biological and clinical relevance.

Article.Authors: Choi U.; Cho H.; Sung Y.; Fukunaga M.; Shim S.; Jeong H.
Article.Abstract: Pediatric pituitary gland (PG) segmentation is challenging owing to anatomical variability and the limited availability of labeled datasets, which restricts the direct application of adult-trained deep learning models. A three-dimensional U-Net model pre-trained on 153 adult T1-weighted magnetic resonance images was adapted to a pediatric cohort of 61 children, using consensus ground truth established by majority agreement among three experts. The TL strategy incorporated dynamic region-of-interest (ROI) cropping derived from consensus centroids, ± 8-voxel spatial jitter, and extensive 20-fold data augmentation to improve model robustness. On an independent test set of 15 children evaluated with label-independent ROI placement, the TL model (Dice = 0.83 ± 0.23) significantly outperformed the adult-only model (Dice = 0.72 ± 0.22; P = 0.0002) in the evaluation that included one localization failure. Mean absolute relative volume error was 17.1% and the volume intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.48. Ablating the spatial-jitter component showed that it conferred robustness to ROI placement error rather than peak accuracy: with the ROI placed at the training-set mean centroid, the jitter-free variant fell to a Dice of 0.61 ± 0.38 whereas the full model reached 0.83 ± 0.23 ( P = 0.031). After adjusting for age at scan, the associations of gestational age and birth weight with PG volume were small (partial r = 0.17 and 0.18; 90% confidence interval [CI] − 0.02 to 0.36 and − 0.01 to 0.37), and equivalence testing excluded moderate-to-large residual effects (|partial r| ≥ 0.4; P = 0.021 and P = 0.025), a pattern more compatible with catch-up by school age, although small effects remain undetermined. These findings show that pediatric adaptation improves segmentation and suggest that moderate-to-large persistent perinatal associations with PG volume are unlikely in this cohort.

Article.Title: Alternative explanation for the effect of myo-Inositol trispyrophosphate on normal human erythrocytes: 31P NMR studies
Article.Authors: Kuchel P.; Yong K.; Mohanty B.; Luck I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract myo -Inositol trispyrophosphate (ITPP) is an allosteric effector of haemoglobin in vitro and has been proposed as a therapeutic agent for diseases associated with tissue hypoxia. Its surmised action on erythrocytes (red blood cells; RBCs) requires transmembrane passage and intracellular binding to haemoglobin; however, direct evidence, of the kind provided by 31 P NMR spectroscopy, for entry of ITPP into RBCs has been absent despite proposed clinical use of the compound. We tested transport by monitoring fresh human RBC suspensions exposed to ITPP using non-invasive 31 P NMR spectroscopy over several hours. No intracellular ITPP was detected within the sensitivity limits of the method (~ 30 µM), and no evidence of significant accumulation was observed. Neither was there evidence of its hydrolysis in haemolysates. We conclude that ITPP does not permeate the normal human RBC membrane in measurable quantities under the conditions examined (and realistic in vivo ones). Consequently, the reported effects of ITPP when added to suspensions of RBCs, on haemoglobin oxygenation are unlikely to result from direct intracellular interaction with haemoglobin and are more plausibly ascribed to indirect effects arising from perturbation of ionic equilibria (Donnan effects) that affect intracellular pH and membrane potential.

Article.Title: Thermochemical upgrading of cereal brans into pyrolytic chars for solid fuel applications
Article.Authors: Piersa P.; Szufa S.; Kazimierski P.; Piersa K.; Spławski O.; Janiszewska-Latterini D.; Hutsol O.; Hutsol T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing production of cereals in Europe generates large quantities of milling by-products, including cereal brans, whose valorisation is important in the context of circular bioeconomy and renewable energy production. Although brans are commonly used in food and feed chains, low-grade or surplus fractions may require alternative management pathways. This study evaluated the potential of selected cereal brans, namely spelt, oat, wheat, rye, barley, durum wheat, triticale and millet brans, as feed-stocks for the production of pyrolytic char intended for energy recovery. The brans were pyrolysed at 500 °C, and the resulting chars were assessed in terms of solid yield, ash content, higher heating value and energy-related indicators. The char yield ranged from 30.27 to 37.04%, depending on the feedstock. Pyrolysis increased the higher heating value from 16.58 to 22.80 MJ/kg in raw brans to 24.45–30.15 MJ/kg in the corresponding chars, confirming the effectiveness of carbonisation in improving the energy density of the solid product. However, ash content also increased markedly, from 3.69 to 7.36% in raw brans to 11.41–23.31% in the chars, indicating that mineral concentration is a key constraint for combustion-oriented applications. The integrated evaluation of heating value and ash load showed that oat, rye and durum wheat chars offered the most favourable balance between high energy content and relatively low ash burden. To conclude, cereal brans can be considered promising feedstocks for thermochemical upgrading into charcoal-like solid fuels, particularly when they are unsuitable for food or feed uses.

Article.Title: Staphylococcus aureus and MRSA colonization and antimicrobial susceptibility among neonates, mothers, and the NICU environment in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Gulilat W.; Abera R.; Abebe W.; Haile S.; Desta K.
Article.Abstract: Staphylococcus aureus , particularly methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), is a major cause of healthcare-associated infections and contributes substantially to the global burden of antimicrobial resistance. Neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are especially vulnerable because of their immature immune systems, frequent invasive procedures, and prolonged exposure to healthcare environments. Colonization with MRSA may precede invasive infection and facilitate transmission within NICUs. However, data describing MRSA colonization among neonates, their mothers, and the NICU environment remain limited in Ethiopia. To determine the prevalence of S. aureus and MRSA colonization and describe antimicrobial susceptibility patterns among neonates, their mothers, and environmental surfaces in the neonatal intensive care unit of Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2021 to January 2022 among 116 mother–newborn pairs admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital. In addition, 230 environmental samples were collected from frequently touched NICU surfaces. Nasal swabs were obtained from mothers and neonates using systematic random sampling. Staphylococcus aureus was identified using standard microbiological techniques, including culture on mannitol salt agar, catalase testing, tube coagulase testing, and β-haemolysis on blood agar. Methicillin resistance was determined using the cefoxitin (30 µg) disk diffusion method according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) 2020 guidelines. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby–Bauer disk diffusion method, while vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined using the E-test. Descriptive statistics were generated, and prevalence estimates were reported with 95% confidence intervals. Overall, 43/232 participants (18.5%; 95% CI 13.7–23.9) were colonized with S. aureus . Colonization was detected in 26/116 mothers (22.4%) and 17/116 neonates (14.7%). MRSA was detected in 6/232 participants (2.6%), including 4/116 mothers (3.4%) and 2/116 neonates (1.7%). Six mother-newborn pairs were colonized with S. aureus in both members of the pair, including one pair in which both mother and neonate were colonized with MRSA. Environmental contamination was low, with S. aureus isolated from 11/230 samples (4.8%) and MRSA from 1/230 samples (0.4%). All 54/54 (100%) S. aureus isolates were resistant to penicillin, whereas susceptibility remained high to clindamycin and erythromycin. All 7/7 (100%) MRSA isolates met the study definition of multidrug resistance, with resistance spanning at least three antimicrobial classes. Among all 54 S. aureus isolates, 47/54 (87.0%) had vancomycin MICs in the susceptible range, while 7/54 (13.0%) had MICs within the intermediate range. No isolates had vancomycin MICs in the resistant range. Although MRSA colonization was relatively uncommon, S. aureus colonization remained frequent among mothers and neonates admitted to the NICU. The observed maternal and neonatal colonization pattern highlights the importance of continued infection prevention and control measures, antimicrobial stewardship, and targeted surveillance of high-risk NICU populations to reduce the risk of subsequent neonatal infection and healthcare-associated spread.

Article.Title: Mental distress diverges by gender across the transition to first parenthood and is not consistently buffered by working from home
Article.Authors: Cui S.; Guo Y.; Chen L.; Yan Y.
Article.Abstract: This study asks whether working from home cushions mental distress across the transition to first parenthood in the United Kingdom. Drawing on nationally representative panel data from the UK (2010–2024), this study uses person fixed-effects event-study models to follow employed women and men who are observed childless before a child appears in the household and who are aged 18–45 at that transition. Post-transition distress trajectories differ by gender: fathers’ distress rises and remains higher, whereas employed mothers’ distress is lower at the interview when a child is first observed, a pattern that cannot be separated from selection into continued employment. Working from home before that interview does not jointly distinguish these trajectories. Among mothers who remain employed, contemporaneous working from home is associated with lower distress two even waves earlier and with a less favourable gap at later waves; that timing pattern is descriptive, and working from home after the birth can itself respond to care or distress. Neither the distress trajectories nor this remote-work pattern reappear around subsequent births among existing parents.

Article.Title: DIA proteomics identifies time-of-day-dependent hippocampal proteomic signatures associated with exercise timing in type 2 diabetic mice
Article.Authors: Wu J.; Hu H.; Yuan S.; Guo W.; Qiu L.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with neurological dysfunction, including alterations in emotional regulation, and exercise timing may influence physiological adaptation under metabolic stress. However, the molecular signatures associated with time-of-day-dependent exercise responses in the diabetic brain remain incompletely characterized. In this study, we investigated the effects of exercise timing on anxiety-like behaviors and hippocampal proteomic profiles in T2DM mice. Male C57BL/6J mice with T2DM were subjected to swimming exercise during either the early rest phase or early active phase (ZT15), followed by behavioral assessment and hippocampal proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry. ZT15 exercise was associated with improved anxiety-like behavioral outcomes compared with diabetic controls. DIA-based proteomic analysis identified distinct hippocampal protein signatures associated with different exercise timings. Functional enrichment analyses identified timing-associated enrichment patterns involving transcriptional regulation, inflammation-related responses, and cytoskeletal-associated processes. These findings suggest that exercise performed at different times of day is accompanied by distinct hippocampal molecular responses under diabetic conditions. The identified proteomic signatures provide candidate molecular context and directions for future mechanistic studies of time-dependent exercise responses in metabolic disorders.

Article.Title: Differences in shoulder range of motion among tennis athletes by age and sex
Article.Authors: Mu Z.; Li S.; Imai K.; Wang H.; Ma H.; Han Z.; Wang Q.; Yan H.; Hu J.; Cui M.; Zhou X.
Article.Abstract: Investigating shoulder range of motion (ROM) among junior tennis athletes may help in developing injury prevention programs; however, few studies have examined the shoulder function of Chinese tennis athletes. Therefore, this study compared the shoulder ROM among tennis athletes by age and sex. A convenience sample of 123 healthy tennis athletes (aged 918 years) was included and categorized into primary school (9–12 years), junior high school (13–15 years), and senior high school (16–18 years) groups. Shoulder abduction, internal rotation (IR), external rotation (ER), and total range of motion (TROM) were assessed using a digital goniometer. Between-group and between-side differences were analyzed using mixed-effects linear models, with other comparisons analyzed using parametric or non-parametric tests as appropriate; post hoc comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Significant effects of side were found for shoulder abduction, IR, and ER ROM ( P = 0.007, P = 0.007, and P = 0.004, respectively). The non-dominant side showed greater abduction and IR ROM, whereas the dominant side showed greater ER ROM (all P < 0.001). Significant age effects were observed for ER ROM ( P = 0.004) and TROM ( P = 0.007). ER was greater in the elementary school group than the junior high and high school groups (both P = 0.002), and in the junior high school than the high school ( P = 0.002). TROM was greater in the elementary and junior high school groups than in the high school group ( P = 0.003 and P = 0.017, respectively). A significant sex × age interaction was found for shoulder abduction ROM ( P = 0.042); in males, abduction ROM was greater in the elementary and junior high school groups than in the high school group ( P = 0.026 and P = 0.003, respectively). Chinese tennis players aged 9–18 years showed side-related differences in shoulder abduction, IR and ER, and age-related differences in ER and TROM, with a sex × age interaction for shoulder abduction observed mainly in males. These findings may provide descriptive data on shoulder ROM in healthy tennis athletes aged 9–18 years.

Article.Title: Farm practice typologies as a strategy for management-relevant land use and land cover mapping in the Great Lakes Region
Article.Authors: Paudel S.; Okoye P.; McManamay R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Great Lakes region (GLR) is dominated by agricultural land use, characterized by diverse land use and land cover (LULC), land management practices (LMPs), and, in turn, diverse land processes. Conventional LULC classification systems often rely on coarse categorizations, summarized into spatial units that are either unmeaningful to management or lack the fidelity to capture human-driven heterogeneity relevant to environmental outcomes. Furthermore, most LULC systems are temporal snapshots, agnostic to the spatial dependencies of temporal land-use transitions and fail to provide an inventory of the diversity of land use and management within regions. Hence, we developed a multi-year integrated typology framework by combining LULC class transitions (2008–2023) with trends in LMPs, to characterize these differences in the landscape, using inductively developed, threshold-based classification rules at the farm-parcel level.​ Our multi-year integrated typology combined LULC and LMP classes to yield a total of 135 unique land types for the GLR, capturing sufficient variation in agricultural management and landscape heterogeneity that is not reflected in conventional LULC products. Staple Crop Rotation – Tile Drained (StRot-TD) and Staple Crop Rotation – Conventional (StRot-Con) emerged as the dominant multi-year integrated typologies across the GLR. Across three threshold scenarios in sensitivity analysis, 84.27%, 99.01% and 83.43% of parcels retained LULC transition, LMPs trend and multi-year integrated typology classes respectively. The diversity of annual integrated typology increased over time due to the complexity of land use and management practices, even though it decreased for conventional LULC. To demonstrate the practicality of our approach, we used linear mixed-effects models, which compare the performance of our annual integrated typology relative to conventional LULC classifications in predicting water-quality parameters (phosphorus, nitrite, and Kjeldahl nitrogen) in streams draining agricultural watersheds. The annual integrated typology models achieved lower RMSE and higher R 2 than conventional LULC models in the validation for phosphorus, nitrite, and Kjeldahl nitrogen, supporting the predictive value of combining the management attributes in the case study. The framework offers a flexible, interpretable tool for landscape characterization, agricultural planning, conservation implementation, and informed decision-making, and is replicable across regions.

Article.Title: Research on the application framework of multi-agent technology-driven failure analysis for industrial products
Article.Authors: Lu X.; Gong Z.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate failure analysis in intelligent supercharging stations is critical for operational safety and efficiency. However, traditional methods suffer from poor cross-condition adaptability, limited few-shot learning capability, and insufficient cross-model generalization. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Failure Analysis Execution System (FAES), which synergistically integrates a Multimodal Workbench, an Intelligence Hub, and a modular agent cluster. The Multimodal Workbench fuses heterogeneous sensor data (voltage, current, temperature, acoustic) through a progressive three-level fusion strategy with cross-modal attention and Dempster-Shafer evidence theory. The Intelligence Hub formulates task allocation as a constrained optimization problem, which is relaxed to a differentiable softmax routing mechanism. This enables real-time, load-aware scheduling. A fine-tuned large language model (Qwen3-Omni) provides domain-adaptive diagnostic reasoning through closed-loop reinforcement learning from human feedback. Extensive experiments on real-world charging station data demonstrate that FAES achieves 83.2% diagnostic accuracy under few-shot cross-dataset transfer-a 15.8 percentage point improvement over training from scratch and reduces average response time by 42.9% (from 4.2 s to 2.4 s) via dynamic multi-agent scheduling. Ablation studies quantify the contribution of each component, while hallucination analysis confirms a low rate of just 0.4%. These results establish FAES as an explainable, generalizable solution for industrial fault diagnosis, filling a critical gap in the application of LLM-based multi-agent collaboration to charging station maintenance.

Article.Title: Path-aware data-driven computational mechanics for elastoplastic bedded rock
Article.Authors: Bao Y.; Ma Z.
Article.Abstract: Bedded rock exhibits pressure-dependent yielding, strong sensitivity to stress path, and pronounced anisotropy associated with bedding orientation, making it difficult to describe with conventional phenomenological plasticity models. Data-Driven Computational Mechanics (DDCM) provides a model-free alternative by replacing explicit constitutive laws with nearest-neighbor retrieval from a material-state database. However, two fundamental issues constrain its application to elastoplastic geomaterials. First, the conventional fixed-scale distance metric systematically favors elastic database entries in the post-yield regime, where accumulated plastic strains may exceed the elastic reference scale by one to two orders of magnitude. Second, because plastic response depends on loading history, stress proximity alone cannot reliably distinguish states with different paths, leading to physically inconsistent nearest-neighbor matches near the yield surface. We develop a unified path-aware DDCM framework to address these two issues without introducing an explicit yield criterion or flow rule. We adapt the strain reference locally at each node according to its current database assignment, removing the bias toward elastic entries in plastic regions. To account for loading-path effects, we include confining pressure as a surrogate history variable in both the database entries and query vectors. Before each nearest-neighbor search, a Mixture Density Network (MDN) conditioned on partial observations completes the query in a branch-aware manner, resolving the bimodal structure of the elastoplastic material manifold. The physical projection is formulated in terms of displacement, eliminating the kinematic compatibility constraint and improving convergence along strongly nonlinear loading paths. The framework is assessed against Mohr–Coulomb analytical solutions for a thick-walled cylindrical cavity at five bedding angles ( \(\:\beta\:\) = 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°). Stress-subspace retrieval recovers the discontinuous strain jump at the elastic-plastic interface directly without specifying an explicit jump condition. At \(\:\beta\:\) = 30°, increasing the training pressure range by 20% reduces the circumferential stress RMSE by 67%, indicating that database coverage, not database density, is the major limitation on solution accuracy. Increasing the database size from 500 to 48,000 state pairs shows little change in solution accuracy, while the computational cost increases only sublinearly with database size. These results, validated against analytical elastoplastic solutions across five bedding orientations, show the framework performs consistently when using separate orientation-specific databases with the same optimization algorithm. While this validation establishes algorithmic correctness in analytically tractable configurations, extending to experimental material data and cross-validating with alternative constitutive models remain important future steps to assess practical robustness under measurement noise and model-form uncertainty.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: data-driven computational mechanics; bedded rock; mixture density networks; nearest neighbor search; cylindrical cavity; anisotropy; confining pressure

Article.Title: Isolation and molecular identification of non-tuberculous mycobacteria from diseased farmed rainbow trout in western Iran
Article.Authors: Yazdanmanesh M.; Maleki A.; Saberi A.; Tadayon K.; Najafpour R.; Yazdani F.; Kazemian H.
Article.Abstract: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are important pathogens affecting marine, brackish, and freshwater fish and may persist in aquatic environments. Identification of NTM species is essential for understanding their epidemiology and implications for aquaculture. Moreover biofilm-forming capacity is also recognized as an important survival strategy that facilitates the long-term persistence of NTM in aquatic environments. This study aimed to isolate and identify NTM species from dead/diseased farmed rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ) using phenotypic and molecular methods and to evaluate their biofilm-forming capacity. A total of 123 dead/diseased fish samples were collected from different fish farming ponds. Following initial sample processing, samples were inoculated into two Lowenstein-Jensen media and were incubated at 25 °C and 37 °C for 8 weeks. The positive colonies were identified using conventional phenotypic tests and molecular identification using the hsp65 and rpoB genes. Biofilm-forming capacity was assessed using the crystal violet microtiter plate assay. Associations between NTM species, growth rate category, and clinical signs were evaluated using Fisher’s exact test. Out of 123 samples, 19 samples (15.45%) were positive for NTM. The identified species included M. fortuitum ( n = 9, 47.37%), followed by M. chelonae ( n = 5, 26.32%) and M. marinum ( n = 5, 26.32%). No statistically significant association was found between NTM species and clinical manifestations ( p = 0.090), whereas a statistically significant association was observed between growth rate category and clinical signs ( p = 0.01). All positive isolates were able to produce biofilm, with 15 (78.95%) isolates classified as strong biofilm producers and 4 (21.05%) isolates classified as moderate biofilm producers. In conclusion, this study indicates the presence of NTM in dead/diseased farmed rainbow trout, with M. fortuitum being the predominant species among the recovered isolates. The high biofilm-forming capacity of fish-associated NTM isolates may contribute to their persistence in aquatic environments. These findings highlight the necessity of regular monitoring and reliable identification of NTM in aquatic environments.

Article.Title: Rock damage mechanisms and reservoir protective drilling fluid optimisation for a sandstone block in Dagang Oilfield
Article.Authors: Xie H.; Zou L.; Wang L.; Li S.; Wang H.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The tight sandstone reservoir in a certain block of the Dagang Oilfield exhibits a dual-porosity structure, comprising nanoscale matrix pores (average diameter: 11.99 nm) and natural fractures (50–100 μm). A key challenge facing this formation is severe water sensitivity caused by a mixture of sodium feldspar and montmorillonite clays, which account for 56% of the total clay content. Characterisation of the reservoir indicated that water sensitivity is the primary damage mechanism, accounting for 72.3% of the damage rate. To mitigate this issue, a novel film-forming sealant, CMJ-01, was introduced to establish a composite sealing system that combines physical bridging with chemical film formation. The optimised drilling fluid, to which 1.0 wt% of CMJ-01 was added, demonstrated significantly improved performance: film efficiency (σ) increased from 23.5 to 70.1%, the equilibrium pressure difference (ΔP) reached 0.1034 MPa, and API filtrate loss was reduced to 1.0 mL. Furthermore, the system effectively sealed fractures ranging from 50 to 100 μm in width. Consequently, the permeability loss rate decreased from 61.8 to 35.7%, whilst the permeability recovery rate increased from 58.1 to 91.3%. The film-forming sealant CMJ-01 also demonstrated excellent acid degradability, facilitating efficient post-drilling clean-up. This study validated a synergistic dual-function strategy that simultaneously ensures wellbore stability and excellent reservoir protection in highly water-sensitive, naturally fractured tight reservoirs.

Article.Title: College graduates and higher income adults in Japan unmasked faster after the government relaxed its mask guidance
Article.Authors: Takaku R.; Shimazawa K.; Nakata T.
Article.Abstract: We aim to shed light on the society’s normalization process after a pandemic by documenting the process of unmasking in the aftermath of the COVID-19 crisis in Japan. For that purpose, we conducted a weekly or biweekly survey of masking wearing behaviors from Summer 2022 to Spring 2024. Japanese citizens had worn masks at a high rate until mid-March 2023—three years after the onset of the pandemic—when the Prime Minister announced that mask-wearing would become up to individuals. After the announcement, Japanese citizens gradually unmasked themselves. However, the process of unmasking was uneven; some segments of the population such as college graduates and higher-income adults unmasked themselves faster than others.

Article.Title: PRRX1 isoform PRRX1A promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression through the ANTXR1–PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling
Article.Authors: Wang F.; Liu Q.; Chen H.; Wen T.; Wu Y.; Hu Q.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, and effective molecular biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain limited. PRRX1 has been reported to participate in the malignant progression of various cancers, but its role, isoform specificity, and regulatory mechanism in HCC have not been fully elucidated. In this study, we investigated the role of PRRX1 in HCC by integrating bioinformatic analysis, clinical tissue validation, and in vitro functional experiments. This study demonstrated that PRRX1 was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and associated with poor prognosis. Functional enrichment and tumor microenvironment analyses indicated that PRRX1 was closely related to extracellular matrix remodeling, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and immunosuppression-related features. Functional experiments further demonstrated that PRRX1A, rather than PRRX1B, promoted HCC cell proliferation and migration. Mechanistically, PRRX1A upregulated ANTXR1 transcription expression, activated the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and promoted cell cycle progression. This study confirmed the prognostic value of PRRX1 in HCC and revealed PRRX1A as the main functional isoform driving HCC progression. The PRRX1A–ANTXR1–PI3K/AKT/mTOR regulatory axis may provide a new molecular basis for prognostic assessment and targeted intervention in HCC.

Article.Title: Comparative efficacy and safety of pharmacological interventions for postmenopausal osteoporosis: a network meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Zhuang J.; Liu B.; Yu G.; Jiang Y.; Zhang W.; Xu Y.; Chen G.
Article.Abstract: Characterized as a common chronic metabolic bone disease, postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) leads to fractures, functional impairment, and a higher risk of death in middle-aged and elderly women. Although various pharmacological interventions are available, their comparative efficacy and safety profiles remain uncertain. A comprehensive systematic search was performed across multiple electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from August 1995 to March 2026. We included published randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Outcomes included lumbar spine bone mineral density (LS-BMD), femoral neck BMD(FN-BMD), total hip BMD(TH-BMD), trochanter BMD(TRO-BMD), etc. The analysis included 41 studies with 3,9429 patients and 7 drug classes. Based on SUCRA rankings, calcitonin_minodronate achieved the highest rank for both LS-BMD (SUCRA = 91%) and FN-BMD (SUCRA = 87.7%). For TH-BMD, abaloparatide (SUCRA = 89.8%) ranked highest, while alendronate (SUCRA = 94.3%) occupied the top position for TRO-BMD. Regarding bone turnover markers, ibandronate (SUCRA = 9.6%) showed the highest rank for C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX), whereas teriparatide (SUCRA = 99.4%) ranked highest for N-propeptide of type I collagen(P1NP). In terms of safety outcomes, calcitonin(SUCRA = 9.1%) ranked lowest for serious adverse events. For fracture outcomes, abaloparatide ranked lowest for vertebral (SUCRA = 6.1%) and non-vertebral fractures (SUCRA = 12.8%), The magnitude of treatment effects is presented in the full league tables. Each drug class offered distinct advantages in PMOP treatment. Therapy should be individualized based on efficacy and safety profiles. This study supported personalized management strategies for postmenopausal osteoporosis. Registration of systematic reviews : CRD420251149474, PROSPERO.

Article.Title: Multi-objective optimization of hybrid semi-trailer powertrains based on data-driven matching and backward simulation
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Heavy-duty commercial vehicles, despite accounting for less than 10% of the total vehicle parc, contribute nearly one-third of the total carbon emissions in the automotive industry. The electrification of heavy-duty vehicles represents a critical pathway to achieving sustainable and green transportation. Hybrid semi-trailer tractors combine the range of diesel vehicles with the advantages of electrification; their powertrain serves as the physical foundation of the entire vehicle, and its parameter matching plays a fundamental role in optimizing the vehicle’s overall energy consumption. Conventional forward simulation approaches based on standardized driving cycles and fixed parameters inherently suffer from information loss and also incur high computational cost. To overcome these limitations, a data-driven framework integrating real operational data analysis and backward simulation is proposed. Real-world operational data are analyzed using a two-layer clustering method to directly extract representative wheel-side demand characteristics that reflect actual user behavior. A decoupled backward simulation model is then developed to efficiently evaluate powertrain configurations integrated with energy management strategies. Based on this framework, a multi-objective optimization model is formulated with the minimization of purchase cost and fuel consumption as the primary objectives, subject to dynamic performance constraints including acceleration, gradeability, and battery state-of-charge sustainability. The optimization problem is solved using the NSGA-II algorithm. Validation through simulation and on-road experiments demonstrates that the proposed method improves simulation accuracy from 94.40% to 98.10%. In road tests, the optimized vehicle reduces equivalent fuel consumption by 2.8% compared with the baseline while satisfying all dynamic performance requirements. The results confirm that the proposed framework provides an efficient and robust methodology for powertrain parameter optimization of hybrid commercial vehicles under real-world operating conditions.

Article.Title: The role of social media and generative-ai in self-directed learning among respiratory therapy interns: a qualitative study
Article.Authors: Alnakhly F.; Alshareef N.; Redwan B.
Article.Abstract: Social media and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) are increasingly integrated into healthcare education and have the potential to enhance self-directed learning (SDL). Although these technologies are widely used by healthcare students, little is known about how respiratory therapy interns use social media and GenAI to support their SDL during clinical training. This qualitative study adopted an interpretivist approach to explore respiratory therapy interns’ experiences of using social media and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to support self-directed learning (SDL). A total population sampling strategy was employed, whereby all 25 eligible respiratory therapy interns undertaking their internship at one Saudi hospital were invited to participate. Nineteen interns consented to participate and completed semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis. Four themes were identified. First, participants conceptualized SDL as an independent learning process in which they assumed responsibility for identifying learning needs and seeking knowledge using digital resources. Second, social media supported SDL by providing accessible educational content, facilitating peer learning and collaboration, identifying learning needs, and supporting examination preparation. Third, GenAI functioned as a personalized learning assistant by simplifying complex concepts, summarizing learning materials and generating practice questions. Finally, participants stressed the importance of responsible use of digital technologies by critically evaluating information, verifying content using trusted sources and recognizing challenges including misinformation, distraction, plagiarism concerns and overreliance on GenAI. Respiratory therapy interns have integrated social media and GenAI into their self-directed learning in both academic and clinical contexts. These technologies complement rather than replace traditional learning resources and may enhance learner autonomy when used critically and responsibly. Healthcare education programs should enable students to develop AI literacy and self-directed learning skills to optimize the educational benefits of emerging technologies while promoting effective use.

Article.Title: Multidimensional attitudes toward persons with disabilities in Saudi Arabia: dimensional differences, demographic correlates, and implications for human health
Article.Authors: Alqraini F.; Adow A.
Article.Abstract: Societal attitudes are environmental factors bearing on the health and participation of persons with disabilities, yet Arabic-language evidence is scarce. This cross-sectional study assessed affective, cognitive, and behavioral attitudes toward persons with disabilities, and their demographic correlates, among 548 Saudi adults with a culturally adapted Arabic version of the Multidimensional Attitudes Scale (refined 23-item scoring). The three-factor model showed acceptable reliability, absolute fit within common bounds but incremental fit below conventional benchmarks, and loadings and intercepts that did not differ detectably by gender; the psychometric evidence is preliminary and requires independent replication. Reported negativity was in the lower scale range but differed across dimensions (partial eta squared = 0.16): cognitive appraisals were highest and behavioral intentions lowest. Affect correlated negatively with cognitions only among respondents with prior contact, suggesting that the affective subscale indexes anticipated interaction discomfort rather than evaluative negativity. Women’s higher anticipated discomfort lost significance once contact was controlled. Prior contact was the strongest correlate (23.1% incremental variance in affect), associated with less discomfort (d = 1.35) but more negative cognitions (d = 0.36) and avoidance intentions (d = 0.80). These correlational findings support multidimensional assessment and cognition-targeted training and warrant longitudinal or experimental investigation of contact interventions.

Article.Title: The safety and efficacy of oral vitamin C administration on erythropoietin dosing requirements in end stage renal disease patients on regular hemodialysis
Article.Authors: El-banna M.; ElSaid T.; Elborolossy R.; El Wakeel L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract End-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis (HD) require EPO for anemia complication. Oxalate increases halts Vit C use. This study assessed the safety and efficacy of oral Vit C in reducing erythropoietin (EPO) requirements in patients with HD. This randomized, open-label trial included 60 ESRD patients on stable HD (≥ 90 days) with hemoglobin (Hgb) 9–11 g/dL, transferrin saturation (TSAT) < 30%, ferritin > 100 µg/L, and stable EPO dose for two months. Patients were randomly assigned to one of three groups: A, control-standard regimen; B, standard regimen plus 250 mg/day Vit C, and C, standard regimen plus 500 mg/day Vit C, all for three months. Monthly assessments included Hgb, serum iron (Fe), TSAT, total iron-binding capacity (TIBC), EPO dose, and serum oxalate. Safety was monitored through oxalate measurements. Vit C groups (B and C) demonstrated significant increases in Hgb, serum Fe, and TSAT, along with significant reductions in TIBC and EPO dose versus group (A), (P < 0.05). The percentage reduction in EPO doses at two and three months was comparable and significant in both the Vit C groups. Serum ferritin decreased over time in the Vit C groups and decreased in the control. Serum oxalate increased significantly in both Vit C groups, with higher levels observed in the 500 mg-group. Oral Vit C in ESRD patients on HD improved Fe use and lowered EPO needed short term. Both Vit C 250 mg and 500 mg were effective, but 500 mg increased oxalates more.

Article.Title: Engineering a poly(methyl methacrylate)–sodium mordenite hybrid composite for efficient adsorptive removal of indigo dye from aqueous media
Article.Authors: AbouElleef E.; Ibrahim M.; Diab M.; El-Sonbati A.; Bdeir H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A poly(methyl methacrylate)-modified sodium mordenite (PMMA–Na-MOR) composite was prepared by in situ polymerization and evaluated for indigo removal under controlled batch conditions. FTIR, SEM, XPS, XRD, zeta-potential, BET surface-area, and pore-size-distribution measurements were used to examine polymer-associated surface modification, framework retention, interfacial charge, and accessible porosity. Quantitative PMMA loading was not determined and is identified as a limitation. Dye uptake approached equilibrium within approximately 90 min and was favored under near-neutral to mildly alkaline conditions. Increasing temperature reduced adsorption, consistent with exothermic behavior. Among the tested equilibrium models, Sips provided the best fit in the original qₑ domain (R² = 0.999, RMSE = 0.128, χ² = 0.016), with a model-derived q max of 29.07 mg g⁻¹ and n S = 0.786; the Langmuir q max was 17.59 mg g⁻¹. Apparent thermodynamic analysis based on K d, app = qₑ/Cₑ yielded ΔH app = − 26.43 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS app = − 95.60 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Because K d, app is conditional and dimensional, the positive ΔG app values are not interpreted as standard-state Gibbs energies. Removal remained above 80% in the presence of each tested salt, while removal efficiency declined from 92.4% in cycle 1 to 76.8% in cycle 5. In one real-effluent sample, PMMA–Na-MOR reduced the measured indigo concentration from 50 to 10 mg L⁻¹ under the stated batch conditions. These results support preliminary batch performance, while quantitative polymer loading, replicate-based inferential statistics, polymer-leaching assessment, extended regeneration, and fixed-bed validation remain necessary.

Article.Title: Physical properties of terbium-incorporated nanosized Li0.4Zn0.4Fe2.2O4 spinel ferrites: a new perspective
Article.Authors: Ateia E.; Younes O.; Arman M.; Saeid Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the current study, we examined the impact of excess rare-earth Tb 3+ ions on the structural, morphological, magnetic, dielectric, and optical characteristics of non-stoichiometric Li 0.4 Zn 0.4 Tb x Fe 2.2 O 4 (where x = 0.0 and 0.025). X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirms that the samples were synthesized as cubic spinel nano ferrites. The crystallite sizes of the samples were calculated using the Scherrer and Williamson-Hall (W–H) models. The surface topography of nanoparticles was studied using the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis. The specific surface area increased from 33.42 m 2 /g for LZFO to 44.37 m 2 /g for LZTFO. The remanent magnetization of Tb 3+ incorporated into LZFO rose from 4.868 to 10.713 emu/g, reflecting an increase of 120%. This enhancement can be linked to the alteration interactions between the A and B sites, as well as to the significant magnetic moment and strong spin–orbit coupling induced by the Tb 3+ ions. Based on the enhancements in saturation magnetization (61.020–65.124 emu/g), anisotropy constant (2684–5436 Oe), and coercive field (42.707–80.106 Oe) of the nano ferrites, the samples are well suited for high-density recording media and electromagnets. The real dielectric constant, AC conductivity, and Cole–Cole diagram of the Tb 3+ incorporated sample were investigated. The optical energy gap for the samples was calculated using four different methods and was found to decrease following the incorporation of Tb 3+ . The Urbach energies of the synthesized samples were investigated, in addition to the refractive index and extinction coefficient. The Wemple-DiDomenico model was used to examine dispersion energies. Mulliken electronegativity theory was used to calculate the conduction and valence bands potentials.

Article.Title: Quality-aware cost minimization for multi-tier LLM routing in heterogeneous data centers
Article.Authors: Chadli K.; Botterweck G.; Saber T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of Large Language Model (LLM) inference workloads poses a significant challenge for cloud service providers by increasing operational costs through intensive computational demand. Traditional resource provisioning strategies typically assume homogeneous hardware and static service levels, failing to exploit the economic efficiencies available in heterogeneous data center environments. In this paper, we propose HARP (Heterogeneity-Aware Routing and Provisioning), a cost optimization framework that minimizes operational expenditure for LLM inference services. We introduce a multi-tier quality adaptation strategy that dynamically routes requests across heterogeneous GPU instance types, from legacy to state-of-the-art, under varying Quality of responses (QoR) constraints. We formalize the problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) that balances the trade-offs between hardware lease costs and throughput characteristics across GPU tiers. By decoupling strict hardware dependencies from service requirements, HARP allows for intelligent offloading of lower-tier requests to more cost-effective hardware without violating Service Level Objectives (SLOs). Under a throughput estimation model combining public benchmarks with theoretical memory bandwidth scaling estimates, simulations using workload traces and on-demand pricing profiles show up to $$\sim $$ 23% lower modeled operational cost than a QoR-cost greedy heuristic (QCGH) routing baseline, with double-digit average savings across the evaluated demand compositions. Our analysis further reveals that these gains are largest in the intermediate QoR regime and that the optimizer systematically matches request complexity to the most cost-effective GPU generation, retaining legacy hardware for lower-quality tiers while reserving premium instances for the most demanding requests, underscoring that economic efficiency stems from heterogeneous instance mixing rather than from uniformly provisioning the highest-capacity hardware.

Article.Title: Phoenix dactylifera L. (Arecaceae) seed as a source for insecticide candidates against the mosquito Culex pipiens L. (Diptera: Culicidae)
Article.Authors: Elhawary N.; El-Aasr M.; Soliman M.; Seif A.; Meshrif W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The intensive use of synthetic chemical insecticides to control mosquitoes has led to the emergence of insecticide resistance; consequently, eco-friendly botanical insecticides have been screened for use as alternatives to chemical insecticides. Only a limited number of reports are available regarding the production of green biopesticides from fruit seed waste. Hence, this study aims to determine the insecticidal activity of five fruit seed extracts against the Culex pipiens mosquito. Methanolic extracts of apricot ( Prunus armeniaca ) , plum ( Prunus domestica ) (Rosaceae), olive ( Olea europaea ) (Oleaceae), Egyptian doum ( Hyphaene thebaica ) , and date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera ) (Arecaceae) seeds were tested against Cx. pipiens third-instar larvae. The extract of the date P. dactylifera seeds was selected for phytochemical screening and fractionation. The fractions were tested against Cx. pipiens larvae; subsequently, the LC 50 values of the most effective fraction were determined against the third-instar larvae and adult females. The petroleum ether fraction 's LC 50 value was further tested against eggs and different larval instars. Later, this fraction was analyzed using LC‒ESI‒MS/MS. The results showed that P. dactylifera seed extract exhibited the highest mortality rate, followed by P. armeniaca and H. thebaica . The petroleum ether fraction caused higher mortality than the other fractions tested. The LC 50 values for the third-instar larvae and adult females were 43.7 and 4381.2 mg/L, respectively. The early instars were more susceptible than the later instars of Cx. pipiens . Gamma-linolenic acid and hinokitiol were identified as the major compounds, followed in abundance by apigenin, glycerol-2-phosphate, and dihydrocapsaicin. P. dactylifera seed extract demonstrated promising larvicidal activity, particularly in its petroleum ether fraction, highlighting its potential as a cost-effective and environmentally friendly candidate for mosquito control. However, its comparatively lower efficacy against adult mosquitoes indicates that further studies are needed to optimize its application and evaluate its practical use in integrated vector management.

Article.Title: Reducing uncertainty in fractured carbonate reservoir models throughmultiscale discrete fracture network integration and dynamic calibration
Article.Authors: Hassan M.; El-Ata A.; Badreldin H.; Sayed A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fractured carbonate reservoirs are highly heterogeneous, and their multiscale fracture systems make it difficult to reliably characterize fracture geometry and hydraulic properties. This study presents an integrated discrete fracture network (DFN) approach for a Carboniferous fractured carbonate reservoir in the Kappa Field. Seismic interpretation and curvature attributes were used to identify fracture-related structural features and constrain their spatial distribution at the field scale. These results were integrated with fracture orientations and occurrences identified from borehole image logs and core observations to constrain fracture geometry at the well scale. Dynamic well-test data were then incorporated through transmissivity (KH) calibration to constrain fracture aperture and permeability and to evaluate the hydraulic behavior of the modeled network. The integration of these datasets provides complementary constraints on fracture geometry and hydraulic properties across different observation scales. The resulting DFN model shows improved consistency with the observed reservoir pressure response and provides a more reliable representation of fracture connectivity and hydraulic communication. This study demonstrates that integrating seismic interpretation, curvature attributes, borehole image logs, core observations, and dynamic well-test data provides a robust basis for reducing uncertainty in DFN construction and developing fracture models for reservoir simulation and field development planning.

Article.Title: Response surface modelling, equilibrium and kinetic evaluation of tetracycline adsorption by acid- and base-treated Tetrapleura tetraptera adsorbents
Article.Authors: Al-Hazmi G.; Ilesanmi E.; Olanrele O.; Ilesanmi N.; El-Rayye A.; Alsuhaibani A.; Refat M.; Hassan R.
Article.Abstract: Tetracycline residues in aquatic environments remain a major concern because antibiotics are persistent, biologically active, and may contribute to antimicrobial resistance. This study prepared two modified adsorbents from Tetrapleura tetraptera fruit shells and evaluated their performance for tetracycline removal from aqueous solution. The powdered biomass was chemically modified with hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide to obtain acid-treated sample (ATS) and base-treated sample (BTS). The materials were characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while batch adsorption behaviour was evaluated using response surface methodology with pH, adsorbent dosage, initial tetracycline concentration, temperature, and contact time as process variables. The RSM analysis identified initial tetracycline concentration as the dominant factor controlling removal efficiency for both adsorbents, while pH and selected quadratic terms also contributed to the adsorption response. Although the quadratic models were statistically significant, model-diagnostic outputs indicated that the RSM predictions should be interpreted primarily as design-space estimates rather than absolute endpoint predictions. Therefore, the adsorption behaviour was further supported using equilibrium, kinetic, and material characterisation results. Isotherm modelling showed favourable adsorption based on Langmuir separation factors below unity. BTS displayed the higher Langmuir maximum adsorption capacity (37.89 mg/g) than ATS (29.03 mg/g), whereas ATS showed stronger Temkin agreement, indicating stronger adsorbate–adsorbent interaction effects. Kinetic analysis showed that ATS followed pseudo-second-order behaviour, while BTS showed strong intraparticle-diffusion contribution together with pseudo-second-order interaction. Overall, the findings demonstrate that acid- and base-treated Tetrapleura tetraptera shell adsorbents have potential for tetracycline removal, with ATS showing a stronger percentage-removal response and BTS showing a higher equilibrium adsorption capacity.

Article.Title: Parametric sensitivity assessment of slip flow and thermophoretic effects on a vertical stretching surface using response surface methodology
Article.Authors: Ramesh S.; Niranjan H.
Article.Abstract: The present study was devoted to the investigation of the effect of velocity slip and energy slip on the magnetohydrodynamic boundary layer flow with special emphasis on thermophoresis under steady flow conditions. The governing partial differential equations are converted to ordinary differential equations using the similarity transformations and then solved numerically by using the bvp4c solver of the MATLAB software. The effects of velocity slip, energy slip, thermophoresis and dipole parameter on velocity and temperature characteristics are systematically investigated. A sensitivity analysis is performed to determine the most influential parameters and to optimize the heat-transfer performance which is one of the novelties of the study. The results reveal that the velocity slip parameter increases from 0.7 to 1.9, significantly impacting the velocity and temperature profiles, which result in approximately 3.3% enhancement in Nusselt number and about 19.3% decline in skin friction. The energy slip parameter also has a significant effect on the temperature distribution and heat-transfer rate, demonstrating its important role in controlling thermal transport. The combined effects of velocity slip and energy slip indicate that velocity slip mainly alters the flow characteristics, while energy slip directly influences the thermal boundary layer and heat transfer. Furthermore, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) demonstrate superior predictive accuracy compared with Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Comparison with previously published results confirms the validity of the present model. Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriate control of velocity slip and energy slip, together with thermophoretic effects, can provide an effective approach for enhancing and controlling heat transfer in advanced thermal management systems.

Article.Title: Tissue-specific lipidomic alterations in aging rats
Article.Authors: Aisin S.; Sokolova D.; Grishina E.; Stekolshchikova E.; Senko D.; Efimova O.; Mitina A.; Rybnikova E.; Vetrovoy O.; Petrova D.; Khaitovich P.; Tkachev A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aging drives tissue-specific lipidome remodeling, but comprehensive multi-tissue lipidomic profiles in rodents remain scarce. Muscle showed the largest number of lipidomic changes, with PG and PE O- enrichment indicating mitochondrial dysfunction. Plasma showed alterations in phosphocholine LPC and PC O-, while liver displayed an unexpected decline in triglycerides, particularly shorter- and odd-chain species, consistent with reduced gut microbiota–derived fatty acids. Brain regions showed myelin-related changes: decreased MGDG O- in cerebellum and mixed SHexCer alterations in the frontal cortex. Our cross-tissue analyses revealed that aging trajectories clustered by tissue function rather than baseline composition, with muscle more closely resembling brain, and liver mirroring plasma alterations. While no individual lipid showed ubiquitous age-related changes across all tissues, we found consistent patterns at the lipid class level, particularly among solid tissues. Notably, PG showed the strongest coordinated age-related changes, highlighting mitochondrial lipid remodeling as a common aging feature. Our data supports tissue-specific lipid aging processes, as well as mitochondrial dysfunction patterns shared across multiple tissues.

Article.Title: QSAR-guided generative framework for the discovery of synthetically viable odorants
Article.Authors: Pearce T.; Ibrahim A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The discovery of novel odorant molecules is key for the fragrance and flavor industries, yet efficiently navigating the vast chemical space to identify structures with desirable olfactory properties remains a significant challenge. Generative artificial intelligence offers a promising approach for de novo molecular design but typically requires large sets of molecules to learn from. To address this problem, we present a framework combining a variational autoencoder (VAE) with a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) model to generate novel odorants from limited training sets of odor molecules. The self-supervised learning capabilities of the VAE allow it to learn SMILES grammar from the ChEMBL database, while its training objective is augmented with a loss term derived from an external QSAR model to structure the latent representation according to odor probability. While the VAE demonstrates high internal consistency in learning the QSAR supervision signal, validation against an external, unseen ground truth dataset (Unique Good Scents) confirms the model generates syntactically valid structures (100% validity achieved via rejection sampling) and 93.9% unique structures. The latent space is effectively structured by odor likelihood, evidenced by a Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD) of $$\approx$$ 6.96 between generated molecules and known odorants, compared to $$\approx$$ 21.6 for the ChEMBL baseline. An ablation of the property head shows that its contribution lies in the density of retrievable structures near an odorant seed — a 4.3-fold increase in distinct novel compounds per seed — rather than in the odor-likeness of any individual compound. Bemis-Murcko analysis shows 2,499 of 6,765 ring-containing candidates, spanning 1,429 distinct core frameworks, are absent from all training sets, while a further 294 molecules, spanning 57 frameworks, independently recover odorant cores found only in an external catalog withheld from training. Generated candidates display physicochemical properties consistent with ground-truth odorants (mean MW $$\sim$$ 159 Da, LogP $$\sim$$ 1.67) and predicted ADMET profiles comparable to those compounds. Furthermore, quantum-mechanical calculations (GFN2-xTB) verify thermodynamic stability with energy distributions matching known volatiles, and automated retrosynthesis identifies candidate synthesis routes yields valid routesfor 100% of candidates, averaging 2.89 steps from commercially available precursors. This integrated approach provides a novel and systematic methodology for applying generative AI to explore chemical space specifically for the discovery of new candidate odorant molecules.

Article.Title: Healthcare utilization and costs associated with structured oncological training therapy: a retrospective analysis in cancer patients
Article.Authors: Zimmermann L.; Fahl A.; Baumann F.; Man S.; Meyer C.; Hammling M.; Tewes M.; De Lazzari N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exercise is an essential component of supportive cancer care, improving physical function and quality of life. In Germany, oncological training therapy (OTT) provides a structured way to incorporate exercise into routine oncology care. This retrospective study examined the healthcare utilization of OTT, focusing on differences in healthcare utilization among active participants (T), interested non-participants (I), and a control group (C). Clinical and billing data from a health insurance company were analyzed. The control cohort was selected using predefined demographic, oncological, and regional criteria. The interested group included patients who enrolled but did not participate. The final study population comprised 289 patients: 39 OTT participants, 94 interested non-participants, and 156 controls. A total of 152 patients initially registered for OTT between 2015 and 2019. Outcomes covered inpatient treatment days, outpatient visits and one-year survival. Between-group comparisons were performed using Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn’s post hoc tests for continuous or ordinal outcomes and chi-square tests for categorical variables. Of the 152 registered patients, 58 (38.1%) attended at least one session, and 39 (67.2%) attended at least 12 of the 24 scheduled sessions. The training group had significantly more outpatient visits than the control group during the second observation period (t2; median: 13 vs. 7 visits; p = 0.0005), accompanied by higher outpatient costs (median: €639.29 vs. €267.89; p = 0.0006). The interested non-participant group had the highest comorbidity burden and significantly higher inpatient costs than the training group during the first observation period (t1; median: €5666.89 vs. €0; p < 0.0001). Although estimated one-year survival was numerically higher in the training group (94.9%) than in the control group (85.8%), no statistically significant difference in overall survival was observed (log-rank p = 0.945). This real-world analysis showed that participation in OTT was associated with higher outpatient healthcare utilization and costs, while no reduction in inpatient utilization was observed. Further prospective studies are needed to determine whether these utilization patterns translate into a clinical benefit.

Article.Title: Impact of interval between freeze-all retrieval and first frozen embryo transfer: a large retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Hsu I.; Chang Y.; Huang Y.; Hsieh Y.; Huang C.; Chen M.
Article.Abstract: The optimal timing of frozen embryo transfer (FET) following freeze-all cycles remains uncertain, with limited and conflicting evidence. This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether the interval between oocyte retrieval and the first FET influences pregnancy outcomes in 2,229 first FET cycles performed between 2003 and 2023. The primary outcome was live birth rate (LBR) across four inter-cycle intervals (≤30, 31–60, 61–90, and >90 days), while the secondary outcome was clinical pregnancy rate (CPR). Although CPR and LBR declined with longer intervals in unadjusted analyses (p = 0.002 and 0.015, respectively), these associations were no longer significant after adjustment for maternal age, FET protocol, number of oocytes retrieved, embryo quality, and embryo stage. Propensity score matching yielded consistent results. Subgroup analyses further demonstrated no significant association between FET timing and LBR among normal, hyper-, or poor responders, or between natural-cycle or hormone replacement therapy FET cycles. Neonatal outcomes, including gestational age, preterm birth rate, and birth weight were comparable among groups. These findings suggest that delaying the first FET after a freeze-all cycle does not significantly influence live birth or neonatal outcomes, supporting flexibility in scheduling embryo transfer.

Article.Title: Coalition-based energy management of grid-connected smart homes in the day-ahead electricity market
Article.Authors: Ghobadzadeh M.; Yarandi H.; Hajiaghapour-Moghimi M.
Article.Abstract: The increasing penetration of residential renewable energy resources (RESs), battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and flexible appliances enables the cooperative operation of smart homes. However, existing peer-to-peer (P2P) and coalition-based energy management approaches often rely on bi-level formulations, computationally complex market-clearing mechanisms, or game-theoretic approaches, which limit scalability under uncertainty. This paper proposes a scalable coalition-based Energy Management System (EMS) in which inter-household energy exchange capacity is explicitly introduced as a tunable control parameter. This mechanism regulates peer-assisted energy sharing, enabling a trade-off between expected cost reduction for the system and performance metrics such as the peak-to-average ratio (PAR). The problem is formulated as a single-level, two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework that optimizes scheduling under uncertainty in renewable generation, electricity prices, and demand, achieving coordinated operation without the computational burden of traditional structures. Simulation results for a four-household coalition demonstrate a 10.5% reduction in total electricity procurement cost relative to an independent no-exchange baseline, increasing to 14.9% during weekdays, mainly driven by the complementary consumption profiles of working and retired residents. A 20-household survey-based case study shows diminishing marginal benefits beyond moderate exchange capacities, indicating that unconstrained exchange between residents does not necessarily improve aggregate load-profile metrics. Finally, scalability tests with up to 200 households demonstrate the computational tractability of the proposed framework for large-scale residential deployment.

Article.Authors: Dai Y.; Ding Y.; Luo F.
Article.Abstract: The rapid development of high-speed railways (HSR) has reshaped land use and impacted corridor ecosystems, often reducing ecosystem service value (ESV) and increasing landscape ecological risk (LER). Ecological zoning is thus essential for diagnosing and planning ecosystems along HSR lines. Using the Hefei–Hangzhou HSR corridor as a case study, this research examines the spatiotemporal dynamics of ESV and LER from 2010 to 2020 by applying the value equivalence factor method and the landscape ecological risk index. Based on ESV-LER integration, differentiated ecological zones were established, and future scenarios (2025–2035) were simulated using the PLUS model. Key findings include: (1) Built-up areas expanded notably (+ 157.84 km 2 ), while farmland experienced the largest decline (− 130.24 km 2 ) during 2010–2020. (2) LER structure shifted from high- and medium–high-risk dominance toward medium-risk categories, with overall risk declining, whereas total ESV showed an initial rise followed by a net reduction of 286.59 million CNY (− 2.46%). (3) Ecological conservation and control zones formed the mainstay of zoning; the ecological protection zone decreased most significantly (− 10.98%), while the ecological improvement zone grew the fastest (+ 16.50%). (4) The ecological spatial distribution in the study area remains largely consistent with 2020 across 2025, 2030, and 2035, still dominated by ecological control zones—which show a slight decrease (− 9.54%)—and stable ecological conservation zones. By integrating LER and ESV, this study proposes a novel zoning framework to support ecological management in HSR corridors.

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of classical, metaheuristic, and AI-based controller design and tuning strategies for VSC applications
Article.Authors: Syal M.; Toosy F.; Ahmad A.
Article.Abstract: Stable DC-link voltage regulation is essential for reliable power transfer and secure operation of Voltage Source Converter (VSC)-based systems. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative assessment of classical, metaheuristic, and AI-based controller design and tuning strategies for DC-link voltage regulation in a Voltage Source Converter. A single VSC terminal of a multi-terminal DC (VSC–MTDC) system is modeled and simulated in MATLAB/Simulink to assess the performance of different controller design and tuning strategies. The evaluated approaches include Symmetrical Optimum (SO), Pole Placement (PP), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). Controller performance is evaluated using rise time, peak time, settling time, and percentage overshoot. The resulting controllers are subsequently evaluated in a four-terminal VSC–MTDC network using PSCAD/EMTDC under different operating conditions, including load changes, power-reference variations, reactive-power variations, operating-mode transitions, and regulating-terminal outage, to assess their dynamic performance under the specified operating conditions. The results show that the classical and metaheuristic approaches generally provide faster step responses, with ACO and PSO exhibiting the shortest settling times, while the AI-based LSTM and FLC controllers exhibit lower overshoot values but with comparatively longer settling times. The comparative results demonstrate distinct trade-offs between response speed and voltage-deviation characteristics among the evaluated control strategies.

Article.Title: Population-specific reference equations for fractional exhaled nitric oxide in healthy jordanian adults: a cross-sectional study using GAMLSS
Article.Authors: Al-Qerem W.; Alassi A.; Jarab A.; Al-Zayadneh E.; Al-Iede M.; Eberhardt J.; al-sa’di L.; Aloshebe G.; Sawaftah L.; Mimi Y.; Khdour M.
Article.Abstract: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a biomarker of type 2 airway inflammation used in asthma diagnosis and management. Clinical guidelines use fixed decision thresholds, whereas FeNO reference distributions vary with demographic and physiological characteristics. This study aimed to develop sex-specific reference equations and upper limits of normal (ULN) for healthy Jordanian adults using the Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS) framework. In a cross-sectional study, 906 healthy Jordanian adults (505 males, 401 females) were recruited from hospitals, pharmacies, and a university. Medical history, including asthma and atopy, was self-reported. Exclusions included current or former smoking, relevant respiratory disease, and corticosteroid or antihistamine use. FeNO was measured using a NObreath® analyzer per ATS/ERS standards. Reference equations were derived with GAMLSS. Sex-specific 95th-percentile quantile regressions provided calculator-ready formulas. Median FeNO was higher in males (17.6 ppb, IQR 13.7–22.2; p < 0.001) than females (12.0 ppb, IQR 9.0–17.0); the overall median was 15.0 ppb (IQR 11.4–20.6). The spline-based BCPEo model achieved likelihood-based pseudo-R 2 values of 0.167 (males) and 0.106 (females), outperforming the corresponding linear models. The proportion above the model-based ULN₉₅ was 5.9% in males and 4.7% in females. FeNO ≥50 ppb was rare (0.44% overall). Sex-specific FeNO reference models and upper limits of normal were derived for the sampled healthy Jordanian adults. These estimates provide a basis for evaluating local FeNO interpretation, but their external validity and diagnostic utility require assessment in independent healthy and clinical cohorts.

Article.Title: Green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles as sustainable bionanofertilizer for Corchorus olitorius growth and zinc biofortification
Article.Authors: Akinsipo Oyelaja O.; Kassim H.; Fabiyi O.; Ogundele A.; Silva H.; Orugun O.; Oladele O.
Article.Abstract: Zinc deficiency affects over 50% of agricultural soils globally and is a key constraint on crop yield and nutritional quality in tropical regions. Conventional zinc fertilizers such as ZnSO4 have limited nutrient use efficiency (< 5%) due to soil fixation and leaching. This paper examined the effectiveness of neem-mediated zinc oxide nanoparticles (NMZ) with neem leaf extract (NLe) as a sustainable bionanofertilizer for Corchorus olitorius plants (COp). Characteristic NMZ absorption peaks were verified with a UV-Visible spectrophotometer, and a crystal structure of hexagonal wurtzite with an average crystallite size of 16.8 nm was revealed by the X-ray diffraction analysis. Fourier Transform Infrared Spectra demonstrated the capping of phytochemicals in NLe. Dynamic Light Scattering results revealed progressive size reduction of highly monodisperse particles with a polydispersity index less than 0.3. Brunauer Emmet Teller analysis showed a relatively higher surface area of smaller particles. Results also revealed that the plant height of COp grew by 28% relative to the control, growing to 18.5 cm at week 7. Leaf count grew by 19%, and the chlorophyll content reached its peak of 31.8 ± 0.5 mg/g fresh weight (FW) of leaves. Soil analyses after harvests showed that NMZ treatments had maintained an optimal pH (6.15–6.26) and significantly enhanced the quantity of available zinc. Plant tissue analysis confirmed enhanced zinc uptake, with shoot zinc content reaching 0.032% in 0.05 M treated plants compared to 0.012% in controls. The results affirm that NMZ is a promising and sustainable complement to conventional zinc nutrition strategies, warranting further field-scale validation.
