Article.Title: Complete blood count–based risk stratification to support lung cancer screening in resource-limited settings: a retrospective cohort analysis
Article.Authors: Araújo D.; Rocha B.; da Silva Lima S.; Silva A.; Kohara M.; Ribeiro V.; Pintão M.; Pereira O.; de Morais Malvezzi J.; da Silva F.; de Souza P.
Article.Abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to late-stage diagnosis. Although low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces mortality, its large-scale implementation is constrained by cost, infrastructure demands, and unequal access, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. We developed and evaluated a deployable risk stratification model based on routine complete blood count (CBC) parameters to prioritize individuals for LDCT screening. In this retrospective study, 83,904 individuals aged ≥ 50 years who underwent chest CT or lung biopsy up to five years after a CBC collection were analyzed. The model was trained using Lung-RADS 4 CT findings and evaluated exclusively on biopsy-confirmed lung cancer cases in an independent test set, with low- and intermediate-risk CTs and negative biopsies serving as controls. Lung-RADS 4 denotes radiological suspicion of malignancy rather than confirmed cancer, and control status was radiological for all but 307 individuals with negative histology. Logistic regression with L2 regularization (ridge) was compared with gradient boosting, and feature selection retained red cell distribution width (RDW), neutrophil count, and mean corpuscular volume as predictors. The ridge model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.62 (95% CI, 0.58–0.66), comparable to LightGBM. Risk stratification demonstrated modest enrichment: the high-risk group (22.46% of the population) captured 37.32% of lung cancer cases (relative risk [RR] = 2.34), and combining high- and moderate-risk categories identified 59.33% of cancers while prioritizing 42.84% of individuals for imaging. At the high-risk threshold, the number needed to screen fell from approximately 120 to 72 examinations per cancer detected, and decision-curve analysis showed net benefit over the better of the screen-all and screen-none strategies between threshold probabilities of 0.68% and 1.07%. The model requires only three CBC parameters, with no imaging data, questionnaire, or smoking history. Prospective evaluation against current eligibility criteria is required before CBC-based prioritization can be recommended.

Article.Title: Integrated multi-scale assessment of particulate matter in coastal environments: long-term analysis, mobile monitoring, and spatial prediction techniques
Article.Authors: Dhiman R.; Yadav N.; Gupta A.; Ambekar A.; Thajudeen T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a multi-scale analysis of Particulate-Matter (PM) concentrations across the coastal region in India using long-term air quality datasets, mobile monitoring, and advanced spatial-interpolation techniques. Long-term observations (2016–2025) were analysed to examine interannual and seasonal variations in PM across the coastal region. Fine-scale spatial variability in urban microenvironments (February 2026) was investigated using an instrumented two-wheeler platform equipped with real-time aerosol and meteorological instruments, including DustTrak, an Optical-Particle-Sizer (OPS3330), and low-cost sensors deployed in different orientations. The spatial distribution and prediction of PM at both regional and microenvironmental scales were further evaluated using Inverse-Distance-Weighting (IDW), Ordinary-Kriging (OK), Gaussian-Process-Regression (GPR), and Tabular-Prior-data-Fitted-Network (TabPFN-V2) interpolation methods. Long-term analysis showed strong seasonal PM variability, with winter PM 2.5 peaks (~ 60 µg/m 3 ) and $$\:{\text{P}\text{M}}_{10}$$ maxima (~ 65 µg/m 3 ) associated with southwesterly winds. At the regional scale, OK and GPR showed superior PM 2.5 prediction performance, with the lowest RMSE values (2.5–2.6 µg/m 3 ) across the Indian coastal state of Goa. Mobile monitoring revealed PM 2.5 hotspots (> 200–400 µg/m 3 ) and elevated total number concentration near major traffic corridors, while microenvironmental interpolation showed that TabPFN generated smoother and more spatially coherent PM patterns with the lowest RMSE (~ 51 µg/m 3 ) compared to IDW, OK, and GPR. Sensor orientation analysis showed improved particle sampling and lower-bias for front-and right-facing sensors due to enhanced airflow exposure.

Article.Title: TiN/dielectric nanolaminates: effects of metamaterial engineering and disorder on the superconductive properties
Article.Authors: Smolyaninova V.; Pokhrel S.; Snarski T.; Lang A.; Wheeler V.; Prestigiacomo J.; Osofsky M.
Article.Abstract: A series of TiN thin films and TiN/TiO 2 and TiN/AlN nanolaminates were deposited using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) to study whether the previously demonstrated metamaterial approach to enhancing the superconductive properties of layered (i.e. hyperbolic meta-) materials is relevant to TiN. While none of the nanolaminate multilayers had superconducting transitions, T c , that exceeded the bulk value of TiN, there were enhancements compared to the T c ’s of very thin single layer films (thinner than 30 nm) of comparable thicknesses, which have reduced values due to the effects of disorder. Upon closer examination, it is apparent that the nanolaminate stacks do not behave like individual superconducting layers separated by dielectric layers, but rather as an anisotropic single layer which results in higher T c ’s than for single layer superconductors. We discuss the role of the metamaterial engineering approach for hyperbolic superconductors versus other possible mechanisms of T c enhancement and effects of disorder.

Article.Title: Reliability analysis of machine operators employed in thermal spraying technology in the context of human resource management using the extended TESEO and HEART
Article.Authors: Pałęga M.; Salwin M.; Kossobudzka-Górska A.; Chmielewski T.
Article.Abstract: This paper aims to develop a model for assessing the reliability of thermal spray machine operators using the Technica Empirica Stima Errori Operatori (TESEO) and Human Error Assessment and Reduction Technique (HEART), which have been expanded to include four additional factors. The results of this model support human resources management processes, particularly in competence development, training planning, and risk reduction. The paper characterizes the thermal spray machine operator’s workstation and presents the specific work environment, taking into account the technical and organizational conditions that influence the technological process. Occupational hazards were identified and risk assessed using the Risk Score method. A human reliability assessment model based on the HEART and TESEO was then developed. To increase the accuracy of the assessment under thermal spraying process conditions, the model was expanded to include four original factors: the stability of technological process parameters, the intensity of physical impacts, the variability of material and substrate properties, and the dynamics of control and operational decision-making. The results indicate that incorporating additional factors allows for a more comprehensive assessment of the probability of operator error, better reflecting the specific nature of the thermal spraying process. The developed model can serve as a tool to support activities in human resources management, especially in training planning, competence development, and occupational safety improvement.

Article.Title: Adaptive parameter-estimation-method selection and life-distribution optimization for censored aero-engine data
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Lin R.; Yang Y.; Luo R.; Cui Z.; Guan C.
Article.Abstract: In aero-engine reliability analysis, estimator selection for censored data and life-distribution choice often rely on empirical judgement. This paper proposes an engineering-oriented framework integrating standardized data preprocessing, multi-criteria distribution selection, and adaptive final parameter estimation for multi-source operational data. Heterogeneous records are mapped to complete, right-censored, left-censored, and interval-censored observations. Candidate distributions are fitted consistently by maximum likelihood and screened by a parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit test. AIC, BIC, and the probability-plot correlation coefficient (CC) are combined using entropy-derived weights, with a prespecified mechanism-based physical-consistency constraint. After selecting a distribution family, the final estimator is selected from a validated rule or a rule constructed and validated for the target scenario. The framework is illustrated using 15 failures and 51 right-censored observations from the PW4000-100 No. 3 bearing-compartment heat shield operated by China Southern Airlines. Within the examined Weibull simulation grid, the 25-cell adaptive lookup rule reduced average regret relative to always using MLE without increasing the maximum scenario-wise mean NMSE. Entropy-weight fusion performed comparably to AIC-only, BIC-only, and equal-weight scoring while avoiding manually specified criterion weights. The framework provides traceable statistical support for reliability assessment under explicitly stated censoring and model assumptions.

Article.Title: Overweight and obesity as predictors of work-related upper extremity disability among dentists in Arak, Iran: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Mansourirad Y.; Bayani M.; Gholami M.; Ghamari F.
Article.Abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) pose a significant occupational health challenge for dental professionals because of prolonged static postures and repetitive movements, but evidence on the association between body mass index (BMI) and upper-extremity disability among practicing dentists is limited and mixed. This study aimed to examine the association between BMI category and upper-extremity disability, measured with the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) questionnaire, among dentists in Arak, Iran. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 276 dentists recruited by convenience sampling from dental offices and clinics in Arak 2025–2026. Data were collected with a demographic and occupational questionnaire, the Extended Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ-E), and the DASH questionnaire. BMI was categorized according to World Health Organization criteria. The primary analysis was multiple linear regression of the continuous DASH score on BMI category; as a secondary, exploratory analysis, binary logistic regression estimated odds ratios for a study-defined DASH score above 20. Results are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Overweight and obesity were present in 36.6% and 19.2% of participants. During the previous 12 months, symptoms were most frequently reported in the shoulder (58.7%; 95% CI 52.8–64.3), wrist/hand (53.6%; 47.7–59.4), neck (47.8%; 42.0–53.7), and arm/elbow (37.7%; 32.2–43.5). A DASH score above 20 was present in 65.2% of participants (95% CI 59.4–70.6). In the secondary logistic model adjusted for sex, age, and years of professional experience, overweight (adjusted OR = 1.84, 95% CI 1.02–3.32) and obesity (adjusted OR = 2.98, 95% CI 1.42–6.25) were associated with higher odds of a DASH score above 20 than normal weight. In this sample of dentists, higher BMI categories were associated with higher odds of a study-defined DASH score above 20 after adjustment for selected demographic and occupational variables. Because the design is cross-sectional and the outcome threshold is not validated, causal conclusions cannot be drawn; prospective studies using DASH as a continuous outcome are needed.

Article.Title: Combined inflammatory, lipid-accumulation, and pulsatile hemodynamic burden and cardiovascular disease across adapted CKM stages: a CHARLS cohort study
Article.Authors: Ren Z.; Liu X.; Liu Y.; Xu Y.; Qiao J.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages summarize disease progression but may conceal variation in biological burden and cardiovascular risk. We investigated whether a composite of C-reactive protein (CRP), lipid accumulation product (LAP), and pulse pressure (PP) was associated with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) and absolute-risk gradients within adapted CKM stages. This prospective analysis included 7779 CHARLS participants aged 45 years or older without baseline CVD. CLP was calculated as the equal-weight sum of standardized ln(CRP + 1), ln(LAP), and PP. During a median follow-up of 9.0 years, 1911 CVD events occurred. Each 1-SD higher CLP was associated with higher CVD hazard after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio, 1.22; 95% confidence interval, 1.16–1.28); the hazard ratio for quartile 4 versus quartile 1 was 1.85 (1.60–2.13). Nine-year cumulative incidence increased from 13.9% to 27.8% across CLP quartiles and from 16.2% to 29.8% within adapted stage 2. Relative associations did not differ significantly across stages (P for interaction = 0.147). Results were robust in competing-risk, selection-weighted, and alternative event-time analyses. CLP captured continuous multidomain burden and identified substantial absolute-risk heterogeneity within adapted CKM stages. These findings support epidemiologic characterization and require external validation before clinical use.

Article.Title: Entropy-Guided Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Complementary Deep Ensemble for osteopenia and osteoporosis classification from knee radiographs
Article.Authors: Medhat S.; ElAraby W.; Saad M.; Saleh H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automated osteoporosis assessment from knee radiographs remains a challenging computer-aided diagnosis task due to subtle structural differences among normal, osteopenic, and osteoporotic bone patterns, together with the limited availability of transparent and reproducible evaluation frameworks based on publicly accessible datasets. Existing studies predominantly rely on standalone deep learning models or conventional ensemble methods that assume fixed classifier reliability and rarely incorporate predictive uncertainty into decision-level fusion. To address this limitation, this study proposes an Entropy-Guided Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Complementary Deep Ensemble (E-ACW Ensemble) for uncertainty-aware osteoporosis-related knee radiograph classification in both binary and multi-class settings. The proposed framework integrates standardized radiographic preprocessing, fold-specific data augmentation, complementary deep feature learning, and an entropy-guided adaptive fusion strategy. Predictive uncertainty is estimated using Shannon entropy to enable sample-specific confidence weighting during decision-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on publicly available knee radiograph datasets using a rigorous five-fold stratified cross-validation protocol. Comprehensive experimental evaluation, including comparative benchmarking, ablation studies, fold-wise stability analysis, statistical significance testing, and computational efficiency assessment, was conducted to validate predictive performance, robustness, and reproducibility. Among the investigated configurations, the proposed EfficientNetB0 + MobileNetV2 + E-ACW Ensemble achieved the best overall performance, reaching 99.2% accuracy and 99.1% F1-score for binary classification and 98.7% accuracy and 98.5% F1-score for multi-class classification while requiring substantially lower computational cost than the corresponding high-capacity ensemble. These findings demonstrate that entropy-guided adaptive confidence weighting provides an effective and computationally efficient decision-level fusion strategy for osteoporosis-related knee radiograph classification. The proposed E-ACW Ensemble establishes a reproducible framework that can be readily extended to future computer-aided musculoskeletal image analysis and uncertainty-aware medical imaging applications.

Article.Title: Thermonuclear reaction rate of the deuteron alpha capture reaction in cluster effective field theory
Article.Authors: Nazari F.; Radin M.; Arani M.
Article.Abstract: In this work, we calculate the thermonuclear reaction rate of the \(d(\alpha ,\gamma )^{6}\textrm{Li}\) radiative capture process within the framework of cluster effective field theory (CEFT). The deuteron and the alpha particle are treated as effective degrees of freedom, enabling a systematic description of the low-energy dynamics relevant to primordial nucleosynthesis. The capture cross section is calculated by including the E 1 and E 2 electromagnetic transition amplitudes, while Coulomb interactions are treated nonperturbatively. The thermonuclear reaction rate is then evaluated at next-to-leading order over the temperature range \(10^6 \textrm{K} \le T\le 10^{10} \textrm{K}\) relevant to astrophysical applications. The scattering sector low-energy constants were previously constrained by experimental \(d-\alpha \) phase shifts, while the electromagnetic low-energy constants \(L_{E1}^R\) and \(L_{E2}^R\) were constrained by the experimental astrophysical S-factor. These parameters are used in the present calculation without any further refitting. The resulting CEFT reaction rate is compared with previous theoretical calculations, the LUNA reaction rate, and the NACRE II reaction rate. The CEFT result follows the overall temperature dependence of the NACRE II rate over a substantial part of the considered temperature range, while showing a more pronounced deviation from the LUNA rate. The present calculation provides an additional consistency test of the previously constrained CEFT capture description at a temperature-dependent astrophysical observable and provides a useful CEFT based reaction rate input for studies of primordial \(^{6}\textrm{Li}\) production.

Article.Title: An efficient comparative beam-shell framework for assessing the vibration characteristics of corroded monopiles in soil–structure interaction
Article.Authors: Ghandehari M.; Masoodi A.; Seyedi Hosseininia E.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the global (GSV) and local (LSV) structural vibration behavior of hollow steel monopiles embedded in soil. The monopile is modeled as a beam in the global formulation and as a cylindrical shell in the local formulation, while the surrounding soil is represented using a two-parameter Winkler-shear foundation. The governing equations are derived using Hamilton’s principle and solved numerically through the generalized differential quadrature technique (GDQT). A comprehensive parametric study is conducted to evaluate the effects of pile length, wall thickness, axial compressive load, boundary conditions (BCs), site classification, soil stiffness distribution patterns, corrosion-induced thickness reduction, and foundation stiffness on the inherent vibration frequencies (IVFs) of the monopile system. The results indicate that IVFs increase with mode number and soil shear wave velocity, while they decrease with increasing pile length, compressive axial load, and reduced boundary restraint. End-bearing configurations exhibit significantly higher frequencies than floating configurations due to increased tip restraint and effective lateral stiffness. The influence of wall thickness is found to be mode-dependent, with the first mode showing frequency reduction associated with modal mass-stiffness redistribution effects. The study further demonstrates that non-uniform soil stiffness distributions with low near-surface stiffness reduce higher-mode frequencies even when the depth-averaged shear wave velocity remains constant. Corrosion effects are shown to depend strongly on damage location relative to modal curvature, leading in some cases to frequency increases due to localized mass reduction. Overall, the results demonstrate distinct vibration characteristics predicted by the beam and shell formulations and highlight the importance of selecting an appropriate formulation for evaluating the vibration behavior of hollow monopiles.

Article.Title: Quantum-inspired annealing-based semantic-aware optimization for sustainable cloud-edge intelligence
Article.Authors: Almutawa A.; Ibraheem A.; Almaghrabi S.; Alawad W.; Alkasimi A.; Abdallah A.; Darem A.; Alazzam M.
Article.Abstract: The swift development of artificial intelligence (AI) models within cloud-edge systems has intensified energy usage and created sustainability challenges, prompting concerns about sustainable AI. Recent studies have investigated quantum-inspired optimization and resource orchestration to improve efficiency; however, the majority of current approaches regard data samples and model updates as equally significant, overlooking their semantic impact on learning results. This research presents Semantic–Energy Aware Quantum-Inspired Adaptive Learning (SEA-QAL), an optimization methodology addressing semantic relevance, energy consumption, and predictive efficacy in distributed cloud–edge AI frameworks. In contrast to current energy-aware optimization techniques, SEA-QAL directly integrates semantic utility assessment with quadratic interaction-aware decision optimization via a closed-loop sustainability controller. The approach includes a semantic evaluation system that assesses update impact through gradient sensitivity, prediction uncertainty, and attention-driven representational signals. Semantic utility functions as an indicator of learning significance rather than a comprehensive measure of semantic meaning. These indicators are employed in energy cost modelling to develop a loss-energy-semantic Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) framework. The resultant choice problem is addressed with a quantum-inspired annealing method that combines probabilistic state transitions with tunneling-like exploration in a classical computing framework. The approach improves optimization by including semantic utility, reducing unnecessary computation and communication costs while maintaining the model’s generalization capabilities. Comprehensive experiments conducted in cloud-edge workload contexts, including perception-oriented, sensor-based, and IoT-edge evaluations, demonstrate improvements in sustainability indicators, such as reduced energy usage and communication overhead, while achieving comparable or enhanced prediction accuracy relative to benchmarks. Furthermore, the evaluation of scalability with augmented edge-node configurations demonstrates the effectiveness of SEA-QAL for medium-scale cloud-edge deployments.

Article.Title: Design and analysis of a novel compliant XY positioning stage using a tapered folded beam
Article.Authors: Banumurthy S.; Bharanidaran R.
Article.Abstract: Recent advances in precision engineering favor compliant mechanisms for micro/nano manipulation tasks. Compliant mechanisms transmit motion through the elastic deformation of their constituent members; hence, the stiffness of the slender structural elements that undergo this deformation is a key design parameter. In this article, an XY positioning stage is proposed in which different slender-member geometries are investigated theoretically, by the finite element method, and experimentally. Straight folded and tapered folded beams, with the number of folds as an additional design variable, are selected as the flexure structures. The stiffness constants of these folds are derived analytically, with the tapering angle and the number of folds treated as parameters. Strain energy and Castigliano’s theorem are employed to obtain the stiffness constant of each segment, which are then combined using the superposition method. Finite element analysis (FEA) is performed for all folded-beam types over a range of geometries and compared with the analytical results. Selected models are fabricated and tested experimentally to validate the analytical equation. The proposed model estimates the stiffness of the tapered folded beam to within 9% of the FEA and experimental results.

Article.Title: Improving flood-modeling accuracy with refined NRCS Curve Number and Lag Time estimation via remote sensing-based land cover classification correction
Article.Authors: Salar-Khorasani S.; Bozorg-Haddad O.; Loaiciga H.
Article.Abstract: Land use/cover change (LULC) is a major driver of hydrological alteration and flood risk, yet reliable estimation of Curve Number (CN) and Lag Time (T lag ) remains challenging in data-scarce regions where conventional empirical formulas often fail to capture local watershed conditions. This study develops an integrated framework for enhancing the empirical Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) equations through the combined use of remote sensing, hydrological modeling, and parametric error correction. The framework applies multitemporal satellite imagery, Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-driven classification, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)-based land degradation assessments, and geospatial manual delineation of high-runoff zones to characterize LULC shifts and associated hydrogeomorphic consequences. The Hydrologic Engineering Center–Hydrologic Modeling System (HEC-HMS) model was implemented to simulate rainfall-runoff processes and calibrated using a major flood-event hydrograph. The parameters were subsequently refined using observations from an extreme flood event. Results indicate that urbanization and deforestation were associated with changes in hydrological responses and measurable changes in watershed runoff characteristics and the estimated CN and T lag parameters over the study period. The proposed α-correction framework reduced CN estimates by 3.8–19% relative to conventional NRCS values and increased T lag estimates by 26.3–210.2%, reflecting an improved representation of local watershed conditions. For the 2019 calibration event, residual errors of 14.8% for peak discharge and 22.22% for runoff volume remained. The findings of this study underscore the necessity of dynamic parameterization in hydrological models because static frameworks fail to capture anthropogenic forcings on catchment resilience. This work highlights the integration of geospatial analytics and adaptive modeling for sustainable flood risk mitigation and land-use planning.

Article.Title: Arginine-functionalized magnetic Stachys schtschegleevii trichome-supported Cu(II) nanocomposite for the recyclable synthesis of γ-lactams
Article.Authors: Esmaeilpour R.; Asghari S.; Tajbakhsh M.
Article.Abstract: A plant-derived magnetic nanocomposite, Cu@Fe 3 O 4 - SSC -Arg, was prepared in three stages: (i) in situ co-precipitation of Fe 3 O 4 on the surface of Stachys schtschegleevii ( SSC ) trichomes; (ii) covalent functionalization of the magnetized trichomes with L-arginine to introduce carboxyl, primary amine, and guanidinium coordination sites; and (iii) immobilization of Cu (II) ions on the arginine-modified support. FT-IR, XRD, FE-SEM, TEM, VSM, ICP, EDS, elemental mapping, and TGA were used to investigate the structural and physicochemical features of each intermediate and the final material. ICP analysis indicated a Cu loading of 0.76 mmol.g − 1 , and TEM/FE-SEM gave average particle sizes of ≈ 27 and ≈ 31 nm, respectively. The catalytic activity of Cu@Fe 3 O 4 - SSC -Arg was evaluated in the three-component condensation of a series of substituted aromatic amines and aromatic aldehydes with ethyl pyruvate, delivering γ-lactam derivatives in 81–98% isolated yield in ethanol at room temperature within 20 min. The catalyst was magnetically recovered and reused for seven consecutive runs without significant loss of activity, and FT-IR, XRD, and FE-SEM confirmed its structural integrity after reaction. The combination of the plant-derived support, the arginine functionality, and the immobilized Cu (II) provides a recyclable catalytic platform for γ-lactam synthesis under mild conditions.

Article.Title: Assessing sectoral output impacts of climate change in Iran using a dynamic input-output model
Article.Authors: keshavarz A.; Farajzadeh Z.
Article.Abstract: Iran is expected to experience increasingly severe economic consequences from climate change, given that its annual precipitation is less than one-third of the global average. This study investigates the potential impacts of climate change on economic output across different sectors of the Iranian economy using a dynamic input-output (IO) modeling framework. The results indicate that climate change could reduce annual aggregate economic output growth from approximately 2.7% under a no climate change baseline to 1.6–2.0% across the simulated climate scenarios. The effects vary significantly among different sectors, with the output structure gradually shifting toward services and manufacturing, while agriculture and energy experience comparatively greater losses. In particular, agricultural activities are projected to experience a reduction of 1–2% in their annual growth rate from the current level of approximately 2.8%, whereas the growth of most non-agricultural activities is expected to decline by less than 1%. In order to improve the flexibility of the traditional IO framework in addressing climate-induced disruptions, a fuzzy optimization method is integrated to determine adjustments that reduce output losses associated with climate change. The optimization results suggest that output losses could be reduced by approximately 22% by the end of the simulation period, primarily through an expansion of the services sector. Moreover, a 10% rise in final demand is observed to exert relatively minor impacts on total output growth and the composition of sectors throughout the simulation period. Under the optimization framework; however, this increase in final demand could raise aggregate output by approximately 0.4% annually. Overall, the findings highlight the substantial and heterogeneous economic effects of climate change in Iran and demonstrate that flexible resource reallocation, particularly toward the services sector, can partially mitigate climate-induced output losses.

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving deep learning for automated ANB estimation from lateral cephalometric radiographs with an exploratory extension to Cobb angle assessment
Article.Authors: Kalkan E.; Budak I.; Taskin R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automated cephalometric analysis requires accurate landmark localization and reliable transformation of radiographic data into clinically interpretable measurements. This study developed and validated a privacy-preserving deep learning pipeline for automated detection of Sella, Nasion, A-point, and B-point landmarks and ANB angle estimation on radiographs. Specifically, lateral cephalometric radiographs were used for ANB landmark detection and estimation. In addition, anatomical reference points used for Cobb angle measurement in scoliosis assessment were defined to ensure consistency in auxiliary spinal evaluations. Initially, 1286 raw DICOM images underwent technical quality control, protected health information audit, anonymization, DICOM-to-PNG fidelity validation, and strict landmark quality control, yielding 1282 final images. Each image was evaluated by three orthodontists to establish the reference landmark standard. Ground-truth ANB angles were geometrically computed from the annotated landmarks after y-up coordinate conversion. A UNet-based heatmap regression model was trained for four-landmark localization and evaluated using stable 5-fold cross-validation and an independent locked test set. In cross-validation, the model achieved a mean radial error of 1.03 ± 0.45 mm, ANB mean absolute error of 0.97 ± 0.61°, and class accuracy of 86.85 ± 4.90%. On the locked test set, mean radial error was 0.76 mm, ANB mean absolute error was 0.57°, class accuracy was 92.68%, and SDR@2.0 mm was 96.34%. This audited pipeline provides a geometrically verified and de-identification-compliant framework for automated ANB estimation from radiographs. As an exploratory proof-of-concept extension, the shared architecture achieved a Cobb angle mean absolute error of 0.78° on a small locked test subset ( n = 36), suggesting potential for auxiliary spinal evaluation that warrants dedicated validation.

Article.Title: Advancing statistical inference through the truncated copoun distribution with engineering applications
Article.Authors: Sindhu T.; Shafiq A.; Khatib Y.; Abushal T.
Article.Abstract: This paper introduces the Truncated Copoun (TCpn) distribution, a novel and flexible two-parameter model defined on the unit interval for modeling bounded lifetime data. The proposed distribution accommodates a wide range of shapes, including U-shaped and J-shaped densities and hazard functions, providing greater flexibility than existing bounded models. Key statistical properties are derived in closed form, and model parameters are estimated via maximum likelihood. A Monte Carlo simulation study is conducted to evaluate the finite-sample performance of the estimators, demonstrating improved accuracy and consistency as sample size increases. The practical usefulness of the TCpn distribution is illustrated using two real datasets: Boeing 720 air-conditioning system failure times and polyester fiber tensile strength data. Comparative analysis based on AIC, BIC, CAIC, HQIC, and the Kolmogorov–Smirnov test shows that the TCpn model outperforms several competing distributions. Graphical assessments using P–P and Q–Q plots further confirm the adequacy of the proposed model.

Article.Title: Machine learning classification of prevalent cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults with circadian syndrome from CHARLS
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Xiong Y.; Meng X.; Lv T.; Zhu Q.
Article.Abstract: Circadian syndrome (CircS) integrates metabolic abnormalities with sleep and psychological disturbances and is increasingly linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, few studies have applied machine learning (ML) to characterize and identify prevalent CVD specifically in individuals with CircS. This cross-sectional study analyzed 4,091 middle-aged and older adults with CircS from the 2015 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). To eliminate data leakage, missing-data multiple imputation (MICE) was fitted strictly on the partitioned training set (70%, n = 2,863) and applied to the held-out testing set (30%, n = 1,228). Several ML algorithms—generalized linear model (GLM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), random forest (RF), deep learning (DL), and a stacked ensemble—were trained and hyperparameter-tuned with 5-fold cross-validation. Discrimination and calibration were rigorously evaluated using bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for AUC, Brier scores, calibration slope, calibration-in-the-large, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The unweighted prevalence of self-reported CVD in the analytic sample was 26.9% (1,101/4,091). In the independent testing set, the stacked ensemble achieved an AUC of 0.733 (95% CI: 0.703–0.764) and a Brier score of 0.176, which was comparable to RF (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.699–0.761; Brier = 0.179) and GLM (AUC = 0.728, 95% CI: 0.697–0.759; Brier = 0.176). The AUC differences between the ensemble and RF or GLM were numerically small. Quantitative calibration showed satisfactory agreement, with calibration slopes of 1.100 (95% CI: 0.938–1.286) for the ensemble and 0.960 (95% CI: 0.818–1.130) for GLM. Dyslipidemia, hypertension, kidney disease, and age were the leading variables contributing to CVD classification across models. DCA showed positive net benefit across threshold probabilities of 10%–70%. ML algorithms, including both transparent linear models and tree-based ensembles, demonstrated acceptable discriminative capacity and favorable calibration for identifying prevalent self-reported CVD among individuals with CircS. Simpler models such as RF and GLM showed comparable utility to complex ensembles, providing feasible tools for clinical risk stratification. Prospective studies are needed to assess whether these variables can identify individuals who subsequently develop CVD.

Article.Title: TD-MSEFormer: temporal dependency multi-scale expert former for IGBT remaining useful life prediction
Article.Authors: Ma Q.; Guo Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) is important for ensuring the reliability of power electronic systems. However, IGBT degradation sequences usually exhibit nonlinear evolution, mixed short-term and long-term dependencies, and stage-dependent degradation characteristics, which makes robust RUL prediction challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Temporal Dependency Multi-Scale Expert Former (TD-MSEFormer). Specifically, a Sequential Dependency Calibration Module (SDCM) is introduced to enhance degradation-related temporal dependency representation. A Multi-Scale Temporal Expert Block (MSTEB) is designed to capture degradation patterns at different temporal scales, while a Temporal Dual-Attention (TDA) block further refines local temporal interactions. Extensive experiments on NASA IGBT Aging Dataset demonstrate that the proposed TD-MSEFormer consistently outperforms other methods, achieving the best overall RUL prediction performance with superior accuracy, robust generalization, and stable degradation representation under complex nonlinear aging conditions.

Article.Title: Cardiometabolic risk factor burden, psychological symptoms, and immune cardiovascular symptom profiles in adults: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Nawsherwan N/A.; Naeem S.; Bashir M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immune-related and cardiovascular symptoms may co-occur with cardiometabolic and psychological risk factors, but their joint symptom structure remains unclear. This study examined correlates, latent phenotypes, and item-level networks of immune-related and cardiovascular symptom burden in adults. In this cross-sectional study of 524 participants, immune symptom burden (ISB), cardiovascular symptom burden (CSB), and total symptom burden were calculated from 12 symptom items. Reliability, factor structure, multivariable linear regression, cardiometabolic risk-factor categories, latent class analysis, and exploratory EBICglasso network analysis were evaluated. Participants were 42.2% male and 57.8% female, with mean age 51.16 ± 8.83 years and BMI 28.33 ± 2.91 kg/m². Mean ISB, CSB, and total symptom-burden scores were 4.09 ± 3.13, 4.42 ± 3.60, and 8.52 ± 5.62, respectively. The bifactor model showed the best fit (CFI = 0.995, RMSEA = 0.016), supporting a general symptom-burden construct with domain-specific structure. In adjusted models, ISB was independently associated with age, BMI, and depressive symptoms; CSB with BMI, insomnia severity, and depressive symptoms; and total symptom burden with age, BMI, insomnia severity, and depressive symptoms. Symptom burden increased descriptively across cardiometabolic risk-factor categories, although risk-factor count was not independently associated after adjustment. Latent class analysis supported a two-class solution, and exploratory networks identified fatigue-related symptoms as central cross-domain bridge symptoms. Immune-related and cardiovascular symptom burden clustered with adiposity, psychological symptoms, and distinct symptom phenotypes. These findings support integrated cardiometabolic and psychosocial assessment in public-health symptom surveillance.

Article.Title: Features influencing diagnostic yield of exome sequencing in the DECIPHERD rare diseases study in Chile
Article.Authors: Moreno G.; Rebolledo-Jaramillo B.; Böhme D.; Encina G.; Martin L.; Zavala M.; Espinosa F.; Hasbún M.; Poli M.; Faundes V.; Repetto G.
Article.Abstract: Most evidence on exome sequencing (ES) performance comes from high-income countries and patients of European ancestry. In Chile, limited access amplifies health disparities and highlights the need to identify patients most likely to benefit from ES. The DECIPHERD study performed ES in patients with rare diseases with multiple congenital anomalies (MCA), neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) and/or suspected inborn errors of immunity (IEI). We evaluated clinical features and global ancestry as predictors of an informative ES. Phase 2, reported here, included 67 participants; combined with the 100 participants previously reported from Phase 1 (total N = 167): 53.3% female, median age 7 years and a mean proportion of Native American ancestry, 0.540. In Phase 2, 23/67 (34.3%) had a categorical result (pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant concordant with phenotype) and 7/67 (10.4%) a candidate variant of uncertain significance. Across both phases, 54/167 (32.3%) had a categorical result; 58.1% of the identified variants had not been previously reported in ClinVar. NDD and/or MCA increased the probability of an informative ES, while previous non-informative NGS gene panel testing was associated with a decreased diagnostic probability. Ancestry was not associated with diagnostic rate. These results support evidence-based prioritization of patients where access to ES is limited.

Article.Title: Mechanism-guided generative chemistry yields distinct agonist-like and antagonist-like ligand populations for the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor
Article.Authors: Akinnusi P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Designing serotonin 5-HT2A receptor ligands with a specified functional direction is difficult because binding affinity, assay-derived mechanism labels, molecular properties and receptor conformation are only partially coupled. We developed a mechanism-guided generative chemistry workflow integrating curated ChEMBL data, scaffold-aware supervised learning, a recurrent SMILES prior, reinforcement learning, medicinal-chemistry prioritization, receptor-context docking, MM-GBSA rescoring and property-adjusted contact analysis. The dataset comprised 8,949 measurements and 6,252 compounds. A five-seed binding Ki ensemble achieved scaffold-test mean absolute error of 0.588 pChEMBL and R² of 0.607; non-generalizing functional EC50 models were excluded from the reward. Separate campaigns generated 500 valid unique agonist-like and 500 antagonist-like molecules. Antagonist-like candidates showed higher predicted affinity and mechanism-label confidence, whereas agonist-like candidates showed higher QED, greater internal diversity and lower training-set similarity. Matched frozen-prior sampling showed only modest policy-level shifts from the already HTR2A-focused prior, whereas the reward-retained candidate populations were strongly enriched for the campaign objectives. Native-ligand redocking reproduced four deposited poses with heavy-atom RMSD values of 0.357–1.082 Å. Under fully contact-neutral pose selection and the prespecified repeated-measures model, S242, L229 and L362 showed FDR-supported campaign-by-receptor-context interactions; S242 and L229 retained the directions observed with the original selector, whereas L362 emerged in the contact-neutral analysis. The study identifies distinct model-defined chemical regimes and links campaign-level property drift to receptor-contact topology; generated compounds remain computational hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

Article.Title: Development and psychometric validation of the barriers to AI integration in nursing education scale (BAI-NE): a multi-institutional study
Article.Authors: Mohamed M.; Mohamud Z.; Sorour M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This multi-institutional study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate the Barriers to AI Integration in Nursing Education Scale (BAI-NE). A methodological study with a mixed-methods exploratory design was conducted in two phases: scale development and content validation, followed by psychometric evaluation. The 15-item BAI-NE was developed based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and an extensive literature review. Content validity was assessed by a panel of ten experts. A convenience sample of 470 nurse educators from seven faculties of nursing participated in the study. The sample was randomly divided for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA; n = 235) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA; n = 235). EFA identified a four-factor structure explaining 42.7% of the total variance, comprising Technical and Infrastructure Barriers, Knowledge and Training Barriers, Ethical and Regulatory Barriers, and Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers. EFA factor loadings ranged from 0.566 to 0.738. CFA provided preliminary support for the proposed model, with good fit indices (χ²/df = 0.90, RMSEA = 0.00, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.015, SRMR = 0.043, GFI = 0.961); because χ² was lower than df and CFI and RMSEA were at their bounds, these values should be interpreted cautiously and replicated in independent samples. Standardized CFA loadings ranged from 0.54 to 0.82. Internal consistency was satisfactory, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.713 to 0.754 and McDonald’s omega values ranging from 0.715 to 0.754. Test–retest reliability over a two-week interval was excellent for all subscales (ICC = 0.85–0.92). Convergent validity was modest, with composite reliability values exceeding 0.70, while AVE values ranged from 0.426 to 0.451. Discriminant validity was supported using the Fornell-Larcker criterion and HTMT values < 0.85. Among the four subscales, Knowledge and Training Barriers received the highest mean score (M = 14.0, SD = 2.51), followed by Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers (M = 13.1, SD = 2.63), Technical and Infrastructure Barriers (M = 12.8, SD = 2.68), and Ethical and Regulatory Barriers (M = 9.1, SD = 2.10). The BAI-NE demonstrated preliminary evidence of satisfactory validity and reliability and provides a practical instrument for identifying barriers to AI integration in nursing education, informing faculty development initiatives, institutional planning, and future research. The BAI-NE is intended to be scored and interpreted at the subscale level only.

Article.Title: Awareness and factors associated with improved cookstove choice among end users in Kericho County, Rift Valley, Kenya
Article.Authors: Adekunle S.; Ejohwomu O.; Emekwuru N.; Abiodun O.; van Tongeren M.; Lea-Langton A.; Too E.; Mandila B.; Wamalwa P.; Tamainot-Telto Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The understanding of the user engagement, selection and adoption of Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in developing countries is important to deploy measures to sustain their use. As part of a project developing, deploying, and empowering communities in developing countries with ICS, this study screened the awareness and choice selection factors for end users selected for ICS adoption. This was achieved through a survey of 1200 households in Kericho County in the Rift Valley, Kenya. The results showed that, despite some awareness of ICS benefits, the traditional and semi-traditional stoves remain dominant (with about 70% in use against 30% of ICS) and are still adopted due to socio-cultural behaviour as well as low financial resources and settings. The study also revealed that 34.6% of end users use cookstoves for functions beyond their primary food preparation role, mainly for space heating, lighting and meat roasting. This is an important and hardly explored factor that should be considered in the design of ICS and the implementation of measures to improve ICS penetration in households in developing countries.

Article.Title: Metaheuristic driven MPPT intelligence for unified PV battery EV energy convergence
Article.Authors: M. S.; O. V. G.
Article.Abstract: This paper discusses the challenge of reliable maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in solar photovoltaic (PV) battery electric vehicle (EV) charging systems, which face rapidly changing irradiance and temperature. Unlike standard MPPT studies that focus only on standalone PV systems, this work examines MPPT performance within an integrated PV battery grid EV charging framework. It implements and evaluates three recent metaheuristic algorithms: Alibaba Forty Thieves (ABFT), Beluga Whale Optimization (BWO) and Cuckoo Search Optimization (CSO) under the same dynamic operating conditions. A detailed MATLAB/Simulink-based system model includes PV generation, DC–DC boost conversion, bidirectional energy flow, battery management and grid interaction. This model assesses convergence speed, steady-state oscillation, tracking efficiency and energy delivery stability. Simulation results show that the ABFT-based MPPT achieves faster convergence, fewer oscillations and higher energy extraction efficiency compared to BWO and CSO, particularly during sudden changes in irradiance and temperature. The findings suggest that ABFT is a strong MPPT strategy for practical EV charging applications. It offers better energy use, stable battery charging and improved grid interaction under real-world conditions. ABFT reached faster convergence, around 2 to 3 iterations. It also reduced steady-state oscillations and improved energy extraction efficiency when compared to BWO and CSO under the same dynamic conditions.

Article.Title: Infection with GI-19 lineage infectious bronchitis virus induces transient restructuring of the cecal microbiota with persistent predicted functional alteration in chickens
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Kim J.; Jang I.; Le H.; Kim H.; Park C.
Article.Abstract: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), an avian gammacoronavirus, primarily targets the respiratory tract but also replicates in gut-associated lymphoid tissues, including the cecal tonsils, where its temporal impact on the adjacent cecal microbiota remains unclear. Specific-pathogen-free chickens were challenged with a field-derived GI-19 K-IId strain, and the cecal microbiota was profiled at 3, 5, 7, 10, and 15 days post-infection (dpi) via 16 S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Viral RNA persisted in the cecal tonsils throughout the 15-day period. Alpha diversity was significantly lower in infected birds across the experimental period, with values lowest at 5 dpi and higher thereafter, although this temporal pattern was not statistically supported. Infected birds also exhibited an altered overall community structure with increased inter-individual variability. This structural disruption peaked at 5 dpi, characterized by a transient expansion of Lactobacillaceae and a concurrent depletion of Ruminococcaceae , with no taxonomic differences detected at later time points. PICRUSt2 inference of functional potential from 16 S rRNA gene data predicted enrichment of bile acid biosynthesis pathways and of a KEGG pathway annotated from Staphylococcus aureus surface and secreted proteins at 5 dpi; the latter remained enriched through 10 dpi, over the same interval in which community structure remained altered. Because these predictions are derive from taxonomic composition, they reflect underlying compositional shifts rather than provide independent evidence of altered microbial function. These findings provide a high-resolution temporal framework of IBV-associated changes in the cecal microbiota during the acute phase of infection at a site where the virus replicates persistently.

Article.Title: Improving explainability of attention-based deep learning models for thermal analysis systems
Article.Authors: Al-Shalabi M.; Shehab M.; Alazmi M.; Alshammari M.; Alrawashdeh R.; Mahdi M.
Article.Abstract: To improve the explainability and reliability of deep learning models for thermal monitoring and industrial fault diagnosis, an Entropy-Guided Attention Filtering (EGAF) framework is presented. Conventional explainability techniques often produce noisy, spatially inconsistent visual explanations, making them difficult to interpret from an engineering perspective, even though attention-based neural networks can achieve acceptable forecasting performance. The proposed framework is an explainability pipeline that integrates transformer attention components, spatial attention modules, entropy-guided filtering, and multi-layer attention aggregation to address this challenge. It can be used with various deep learning architectures, such as Vision Transformer (ViT), attention-based ResNet50, and ConvNeXtV2 with focal self-attention, to generate informative thermal attention maps for extraction and refinement. Experiments were run on CIFAR-10, ISIC 2019, and SST-2 benchmark datasets and compared to Grad-CAM, LIME, SHAP, guided backpropagation, and traditional attention visualization approaches. The EGAF framework showed the highest explainability, fidelity, and localization with the lowest DAUC (0.281), highest IAUC (0.824), IoU (0.801), and localization accuracy of 91.7%. Noise suppression of noisy activations and concentration of attention were further improved by entropy-guided filtering, leading to greater similarity in correspondence with the predefined reference target regions. Comparative and robustness analyses showed that the framework consistently provided stable, semantically meaningful explanations in complex thermal environments and under noisy conditions. These results demonstrate EGAF’s effectiveness in the attention localization, explanation fidelity, and noise suppression aspects in heterogeneous test datasets. While the results are encouraging for thermal imaging and industrial fault analysis, further validation using diverse industrial thermal images is required to ensure applicability in real-world scenarios. To sum up, the proposed EGAF framework provides a computation-effective and highly interpretable solution to enhance transparency and trustworthiness in thermal engineering applications with AI assistance.

Article.Title: Frequent psychological distress and mortality among adults with all tooth loss across health-risk profiles
Article.Authors: Mao S.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Health-risk profiles (HRPs) are associated with mortality among adults with all tooth loss (ATL). Frequent negative emotion (FNE), prevalent in various chronic diseases, may negatively affect health outcomes. This study aimed to explore the relationship between FNE and mortality among adults with ATL across different HRP groups. 571,938 adults (52,276 with ATL and 519,662 without ATL) from the National Health Interview Survey (1998–2018) were included, with mortality outcomes linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between ATL and FNE. Latent class analysis (LCA) was performed to identify descriptive HRPs using baseline health-risk indicators. The association between HRPs and FNE was also examined. The associations of FNE with all-cause and cause-specific mortality across HRP groups were explored. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted as an exploratory assessment of the discriminatory information provided by negative emotion frequency and HRPs for all-cause mortality. Population attributable fractions (PAFs) of FNE for all-cause mortality among adults with ATL were estimated. ATL was associated with a 45% higher likelihood of FNE. Age was positively associated with the negative emotion score before age 46 among adults with ATL. Compared with the low-risk HRP, the intermediate- and high-risk HRPs were associated with 49% and 118% higher likelihoods of FNE, respectively. FNE was associated with higher all-cause mortality across HRP groups during a median follow-up of 7 years. Cause-specific mortality patterns varied across HRP groups, with higher cancer mortality observed in the low-risk HRP + FNE group and higher cardiovascular and cancer mortality observed in the intermediate- and high-risk HRP + FNE groups. Exploratory discrimination and reclassification analyses showed only modest improvements after adding negative emotion frequency to the model, including HRPs, in relation to all-cause mortality. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and do not establish clinical prediction utility. Exploratory PAF estimates varied across age groups, with greater uncertainty among younger adults. Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results. Among US adults with ATL, intermediate- and high-risk HRPs were associated with a higher likelihood of FNE, and FNE was further associated with higher all-cause mortality. Cause-specific mortality patterns varied across HRP groups. Exploratory discrimination and reclassification analyses suggested that FNE provided only modest incremental information and did not establish clinical predictive utility.

Article.Title: Dependency-aware evolutionary search using population representation learning for large-scale many-objective optimisation
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Khan W.; Singh S.; Siddiqui S.; Joshi U.; Wanjale K.; Chauhan A.
Article.Abstract: Many-objective optimisation problems characterised by large decision spaces and complex objective interactions remain challenging for conventional evolutionary algorithms. Existing approaches primarily rely on predefined variation operators and dominance-based selection mechanisms, which often struggle to exploit latent structural relationships among candidate solutions. This study introduces a representation-guided evolutionary optimisation framework that learns population-level dependencies during the search process and incorporates the acquired knowledge into evolutionary variation and selection. The proposed framework employs a population encoding mechanism based on self-attention to capture global interactions among candidate solutions and generate latent representations describing the evolving search landscape. These representations are subsequently utilised to guide adaptive crossover, mutation, and diversity preservation strategies, enabling a more informed exploration–exploitation balance. Unlike conventional learning-assisted evolutionary algorithms that use machine learning models as external predictors, the proposed method integrates representation learning directly within the optimisation cycle. Experimental evaluation was conducted on selected configurations from the DTLZ, WFG, MaF, and CEC 2020 MMOP benchmark families, involving up to 20 objectives and 1000 decision variables. On the evaluated configurations, MOEA-T achieved improved mean convergence and diversity indicators compared with the considered Pareto-based, decomposition-based, reference-vector-based, and learning-assisted algorithms. These findings provide evidence of the potential effectiveness of representation-guided evolutionary search under the tested high-dimensional and many-objective conditions. However, they do not imply uniform superiority across every problem instance in the complete benchmark families. Additional ablation and scalability studies confirm the effectiveness of dependency-guided search and population representation learning in addressing the challenges associated with high-dimensional many-objective optimisation. The findings suggest that integrating population-level structural learning into evolutionary search provides a promising direction for next-generation large-scale optimisation frameworks.

Article.Title: Causal machine learning reveals heterogeneous effects of loss versus gain framing on retirement savings
Article.Authors: Bösch K.; Müller O.; Weinmann M.; Feuerriegel S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abstract: As Western countries face rapidly aging populations, insufficient retirement savings threaten individual financial security and the sustainability of social welfare systems. Behavioral interventions such as loss–gain message framing are often proposed as scalable solutions, yet evidence on their effectiveness is mixed, largely because little is known about when and for whom they work. We analyze heterogeneity in the effects of loss–gain framing on real-life, high-stakes retirement saving decisions. In a large-scale randomized field experiment ( $$N = 22{,}919$$ ) with a European retirement savings company, individuals were randomized to loss- or gain-framed reminders designed to increase participation (extensive margin) and savings amount (intensive margin). Using causal machine learning, we estimate heterogeneous treatment effects across socioeconomic characteristics and validate them in a second, independent experiment ( $$N = 18{,}288$$ ). In this validation experiment, for the 25% most responsive to loss framing, conversion is estimated to rise by 9.4 percentage points relative to gain framing, whereas for the 25% most responsive to gain framing it is expected to fall by 8.4 points. For savings amount, we estimate that loss framing raises contributions for 64% of contributors (by €737 on average) but backfires for the rest (by €615 on average). Overall, a personalized targeting policy based on causal machine learning is expected to increase participation by 51% (from 4.53% to 6.86%) and average savings by 18% (from €2,062 to €2,442 per converted customer) relative to uniform loss framing.

Article.Title: Modeling afforestation suitability in the Cross-Niger transition forest through remote sensing and analytical hierarchy process to advance global goals
Article.Authors: Enoh M.; Enoh E.; Chiemelu N.; Okereke C.
Article.Abstract: Afforestation is a crucial strategy for conserving biodiversity, mitigating climate change, and preventing land degradation to accomplish Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.2. It is the process of establishing forests in previously unforested areas. Accordingly, the study integrates remote sensing and the analytical hierarchy process (AHP) to identify optimal sites for afforestation suitability that support SDGs within the Cross Niger transition forest. It combined sustainable factors or criteria such as land use/land cover, erodibility, soil, rainfall, aspect, slope, elevation, distance to river, distance to road, NDVI, land surface temperature, drainage density, and human disturbance index to model afforestation suitability maps. AHP was employed to assign weights to these factors, for normalization and validation with the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The final afforestation suitability map was classified as very low (1501.503 km 2 ), low (5297.648 km 2 ), moderate (6971.094 km 2 ), high (5178.869 km 2 ), and very high (2640.442 km 2 ) afforestation suitability. The AUC-ROC value of 0.970 demonstrates that the model has excellent predictive accuracy for afforestation suitability. The study emphasizes the relevance of integrating remote sensing and AHP for well-informed decision-making for afforestation initiatives, thereby supporting global goals including SDG 15.2 within the study area.

Article.Title: Optimizing environmental sensing on public transport to cover broader demographics in Amsterdam
Article.Authors: Koljenšić P.; Venverloo T.; Vrijhoef R.; Duarte F.; Ratti C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban senrsing systems often have uneven spatial coverage, with sensors concentrated in few areas, reinforcing social and environmental inequalities. This study explores how public transport vehicles can serve as mobile environmental sensors not only to increase the spatial coverage of sensing strategies but also to create a fairer and adaptive monitoring system. Using Amsterdam as a case study, we combine GPS locations of public transit vehicle data with 100 × 100 m sociodemographic data to assess and optimize fair sensing coverage. Our method selects the minimum number of vehicles to balance demographic fairness, spatial reach, and temporal frequency. Results show that six vehicles operating during one day can ‘fairly’ represent 17.6% of residents within the applied direct-sensing range, compared with 0.2% for the six static PM₂.₅ sensors deployed in Amsterdam. By redistributing mobile sensors, cities can move from unequal monitoring toward an equitable, city-wide environmental sensing framework.

Article.Title: Heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia incidence in a Chinese cohort
Article.Authors: Fei Z.; Zhang Y.; Pan Y.; Jin X.; Li F.; Luo T.; Shi L.; Zeng J.
Article.Abstract: Heatwaves are increasingly frequent due to climate change, yet their association with respiratory sarcopenia remains underexplored. We aimed to examine the association between heatwave exposure and incident respiratory sarcopenia in a Chinese cohort, identify potentially susceptible subpopulations, and evaluate the robustness of the findings across alternative exposure definitions. In a prospective cohort study of Chinese adults from 2011 to 2015, heatwave exposure was assessed at the city level as the difference in heatwave frequency and days between 2011 and 2015 across 12 definitions (HW01-HW12). Participants free of respiratory sarcopenia at baseline were followed to identify incident cases. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for the association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, BMI, geographic region, and chronic lung disease status, and sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the results. Among 1984 participants, 15.7% developed respiratory sarcopenia by 2015. Greater heatwave frequency was associated with higher odds of respiratory sarcopenia in five definitions, and more heatwave days were associated with higher odds across eleven definitions. Associations appeared stronger among participants with BMI < 23 and those with chronic lung disease, while no clear effect modification was observed by age, sex, or region. Sensitivity analyses yielded broadly consistent results. Heatwave exposure was associated with higher odds of incident PEFR-based respiratory sarcopenia in Chinese adults, particularly among those with low BMI or chronic lung disease. These findings support further research on environmental heat exposure and respiratory muscle-related health, while limitations related to exposure misclassification, residual environmental confounding, and indirect outcome measurement should be considered.

Article.Title: Cervical cancer on-site mass-screening device utilizing multiple biomarkers in Swab samples for surveillance in the resource limited areas of India
Article.Authors: Chowdhary R.; Khurana U.; Halder A.; Dwarakanath S.; Kumar S.; Kaore S.; Jadhav A.; Goel S.; Kapoor N.; Lokhande S.; Rozatkar A.; Kumar A.; Mukherjee D.; Nagar N.; Purohit R.; Yadav M.; Patil V.; Ray S.; Kanwar J.
Article.Abstract: At the World Health Assembly in August 2020, a target was set to eradicate cervical cancer globally by 2030 (incidence < 4/100,000) with 90% vaccination coverage, 70% screening coverage, and 90% treatment coverage. India has a worrying prevalence of between 6 and 30 percent, due to HPV infections and low awareness in rural areas. HPV infections and cervical cancer disease development window period is anytime between 6 and 20 years. Thus mass screening of the population will play a very crucial role. KayaCervi, a lab-free, point-of-care mass screening device based on fluorescence EEM technology, consisting of a cartridge, a reader and a microchip was clinically validated in the study. Initially, ten biomarkers were compared using ELISA and Pap smear. Four (p16INK4a, Ki 67, HPV16, HPV18) were selected. Swab validation was performed with cohorts’ of 200 hospital patients and 800 healthy community females, benchmarked against LBC to optimize sensitivity and ensure high specificity. The community-based validation study was to evaluate the performance of the device as a mass-screening tool among apparently healthy women. In such settings, the majority of participants are disease-negative, and high specificity is essential to minimize false-positive results, unnecessary referrals, psychological distress, and healthcare costs. Sensitivity was measured during the standardization phase by screening participants and confirmed positive cases. Initial findings used biomarkers p16NK4A, Ki67, HPV16, and HPV18 to categorize women into high, moderate, and low risk. The design of the cartridge ensured efficient sample capture and quantification, integrating mechanisms to correct for various light wavelengths during analysis. In community-based evaluation (N = 801), the device demonstrated an overall agreement of 98.0% with the reference standard. Cohen's kappa coefficient was 0.545, indicating moderate agreement beyond chance. The device achieved 100% sensitivity, 98.0% specificity, 38.5% positive predictive value, 100% negative predictive value, and 98.0% overall accuracy and identified high percentage of infections in the apparently healthy women comparable to the liquid based cytology reading done for the relative cellular changes. This study validated KayaCervi, a portable, laboratory-independent point-of-care diagnostic device developed to address India's high burden of cervical cancer. The device integrates a fluorescence-based detection platform with a four-target biomarker panel comprising p16INK4a, Ki-67, HPV16, and HPV18, achieving a specificity of 86–90% in community-based rural screening. As a rapid, low-cost, and user-friendly screening tool, KayaCervi has the potential to democratize access to cervical cancer screening by overcoming barriers related to laboratory infrastructure, trained personnel, and patient follow-up. Further, it include the need for larger, prospective, multicenter studies involving geographically diverse populations, with the biomarker panel and diagnostic thresholds predefined before evaluation and with an appropriate independently established reference standard. Such studies will be essential to confirm the reproducibility, generalizability, diagnostic performance, clinical utility and implementation feasibility of KayaCervi before large-scale deployment. Its suitability for decentralized, large-scale population screening is particularly important given the prolonged natural history of cervical carcinogenesis, where persistent HPV infection may take 15–20 years to progress to invasive cancer, providing a critical window for early detection and timely intervention. This highlights the public health significance by emphasizing the long preclinical phase and the opportunity for early intervention.

Article.Title: Training-corpus overlap and evaluation protocol constrain measured gains in a fine-tuned clinical language model
Article.Authors: Agha A.; Anwar E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fine-tuned medical language models are frequently assessed using public question-answering benchmarks, which may overlap with their training data. We re-evaluated an 8.2-billion-parameter QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-8B under a fixed generative chain-of-thought harness and compared eight benchmarks against its 97,041-item fine-tuning corpus using 13-gram, exact-stem and longest-common-subsequence matching. Exact-stem overlap exceeded 70% for PubMedQA, MedQA and MMLU Professional Medicine, making those scores unsuitable for capability claims, while MedMCQA, evaluated on a held-out split, was effectively unflagged. On several overlapping benchmarks the unmodified parent checkpoint matched or exceeded the fine-tune, significantly so on MedQA. On the 1,838 MedXpertQA items not flagged by exact-stem matching, the fine-tune scored 20.8% against 15.6% for its parent, a paired gain of 5.2 percentage points (McNemar exact P = 7.9 × 10⁻⁷), against an originally reported 7.1. A bundled ablation, in which reasoning traces, sampling weights, curriculum staging, token exposure and output-format supervision differed simultaneously, preserved approximately 70% of the observed improvement. The remaining 1.6-point difference was not statistically significant ( P = 0.175) and cannot be attributed to any single component. The evaluation protocol and the overlap of the training corpus limit the scope of measurable outcomes in these benchmarks.

Article.Title: Identifiability assessment and physics-informed residual machine learning for calculated Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–X thermodynamics (X = Mo, Hf)
Article.Authors: Yasin M.; Yahya A.; Bulay-Og L.; Quimada N.; Albina D.; Bajuyo J.; Muhammad Y.; Assiimwe E.; Badruddin I.
Article.Abstract: Calculated alloy properties can produce misleading measures of machine-learning accuracy when the prediction target is generated by the same equation used as the model prior. This study examines that dependence in 140 Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–X records (X = Mo, Hf), reduced to 129 unique compositions. The tabulated mixing enthalpies agree with a fixed regular-solution prior to within rounding precision. With complete elemental-enrichment trajectories withheld in turn, the prior and a regularized residual learner both give an RMSE of 0.00285 kJ mol \(^{-1}\) ; the maximum learned correction on the candidate grid is \(1.18\times 10^{-6}\) kJ mol \(^{-1}\) . This agreement will be inherited from the analytical prior and will not be an independent physical validation or measurable improvement in accuracy of machine learning. In the other hand, the composition-only support vector regression changes from the RMSE of 0.0202 (shuffled validation) to 1.5687 kJ mol \(^{-1}\) (omitting a complete enrichment trajectory). The features of each pair are ranked with 12 for 15 in post hoc singular-value analysis. There are two null directions, one being the absence of the Mo–Hf interaction, and two others being sampled interaction. There are 3051 possible compositions of the grid, of which 3005 satisfy the empirical thermodynamic criteria, 126 satisfy both proposed geometric restrictions, and 36 satisfy both restrictions and the empirical thermodynamic criteria and form a resulting Pareto set. The global equal-weight compromise is Ti \(_{15}\) Zr \(_{15}\) Nb \(_{25}\) Ta \(_{15}\) Mo \(_{30}\) . The fact that the calculations were performed with fixed priors is reflected in the results of the sensitivity tests and in the 300 interior compositions separately produced, which indicate that the geometric restrictions do not guarantee the reliability of the calculations. Controlled synthetic tests distinguish a learnable smooth deviation from unpredictable point offsets. The contribution is a reproducible assessment of analytical dependence, validation design and coefficient identifiability in a deterministic dataset. Biomedical suitability is not evaluated.

Article.Title: Proteomics-identified serum ROBO4 and VCAM-1 enable robust diagnosis and prognosis-associated biomarkers in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Lin H.; Geng L.; Li M.; Zhang Z.; Wu X.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: Early diagnosis and prognosis assessment of colorectal cancer (CRC) require more effective biomarkers. Using data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics, we analyzed serum samples from CRC, colorectal adenoma, and healthy control groups, identifying 50 differentially expressed proteins including ROBO4 and VCAM-1. These candidate biomarkers were further validated by ELISA in an independent cohort of 300 participants (100 per group). Serum levels of ROBO4 and VCAM-1 were significantly elevated in CRC patients, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance (AUCs: 0.886 and 0.871, respectively) compared to conventional markers CA199 (AUC = 0.757) and CEA (AUC = 0.808). Both markers were significantly associated with clinical stage and lymph node metastasis. A nomogram integrating all four markers achieved excellent diagnostic ability (AUC = 0.969). Public database analysis confirmed that high expression of ROBO4 and VCAM-1 significantly correlated with poor overall survival. This study identifies and validates serum ROBO4 and VCAM-1 as promising diagnostic and prognosis-associated biomarkers for CRC through proteomic screening and large-scale cohort validation, supporting their potential utility for CRC detection and risk assessment.

Article.Title: Characterization of plasmodium SEY1, an essential dynamin-like GTPase and potential anti-malarial druggable target
Article.Authors: Carolino K.; Blauwkamp J.; Bottome A.; Ghidelli-Disse S.; De Souza M.; Harmon E.; DeRocher A.; Morano A.; Chen D.; Farringer M.; Farre J.; Lafuente-Monasterio M.; Wirth D.; Van Voorhis W.; Absalon S.; Gamo F.; Dvorin J.; Winzeler E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In some species, SEY1 is a predicted essential dynamin-like GTPase that is implicated in homotypic fusion of endoplasmic reticulum membranes. SEY1 family members are conserved among eukaryotic pathogens, but they show minimal similarity to human atlastins. Here, we characterize Plasmodium SEY1 proteins. Through conditional knockdown and epitope tagging studies in P. falciparum, we demonstrate that SEY1 is essential, localizes within the endoplasmic reticulum, and its disruption leads to defects in endoplasmic reticulum morphology. We show that P. vivax SEY1 can be recombinantly expressed as a soluble truncated isoform. This protein maintains its catalytic activity and ability to dimerize. It also possesses a moderate K d for GTP and is amenable to high throughput inhibition studies. Our data show that SEY1 is a new and attractive druggable and assayable target that is conserved across Plasmodium species.

Article.Title: Molecular mechanism of preoperative autologous blood donation and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution in improving blood-derived PBMCss in diabetic patients
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Tao H.; Xu J.; Wang J.; You L.; Wu M.; Zhang Y.; Guo J.
Article.Abstract: Type-2 diabetes (T2D) is prevalent and significantly impacts the people’s health. At present, there is no specific treatment to prevent the progression of T2D. Furthermore, the clear mechanism of T2D remains unknown. The present study aims to clarify the mechanism of preoperative autologous blood donation (PABD) and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution in improving blood-derived PBMCss in diabetic patients through regulating the ChREBP-HMGB1-Nrf2 pathway. The present study was conducted to clarify the molecular mechanism of T2D. The general data and blood specimens were obtained from T2D patients. Then, the apoptosis and viability were evaluated. Finally, western blot, flow cytometry assay, immunofluorescence assay, and CCK-8 assay were performed to determine the molecular mechanisms of PABD and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution in improving blood-derived PBMCss in diabetic patients through regulating the ChREBP-HMGB1-Nrf2 pathway. The present study revealed that PABD and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution improved T2D patients by downregulating the ChREBP-HMGB1-Nrf2 pathway. This potential target would be of value in alleviating T2D progression. Our findings suggest that dysregulation of the ChREBP–HMGB1–Nrf2 axis may be associated with diabetic pathophysiology, although the precise role of Nrf2 appears to be context-dependent.
