Article.Title: Effect of freezing rain-induced changes in dry deposition on particulate matter concentrations in Hubei, China
Article.Authors: Tian T.; Xia X.; Wang L.; Zhu B.; Zhu Z.; Zhang T.; Zhang M.; Huang Y.; Han W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) pollution is a critical aspect of urban air quality degradation, and vegetation mitigates atmospheric PM concentrations via dry deposition, offering a natural, sustainable, and cost-effective strategy for pollution mitigation. Based on multi-source satellite remote sensing products, this study quantified the dry deposition effect of PM 2.5 and PM 10 on vegetation using a mathematical model, and evaluated its spatial and temporal changes in the long-term series in Hubei province, especially the impact of dry deposition changes induced by the extreme freezing rain process in early 2024 on particulate matter pollution. The key findings are as follows: (1) Leaf Area Index (LAI) showed a significant negative correlation with PM 2.5 and PM 10 , and modeled dry deposition flux (DDF) showed consistent coherence with LAI, Land Surface Temperature (LST), Wind Speed (WS), and Precipitation (PRE) at the one-month scale; (2) The physical damage caused by the freezing rain substantially diminished the vegetation’s capacity for particulate matter deposition, with the reduction of the deposition effect of PM 10 being more pronounced than that of PM 2.5 ; (3) A decadal spatiotemporal analysis of dry deposition on vegetation indicated an overall trend toward improving air quality in Hubei and further revealed stronger spatial heterogeneity in the long-term trend of PM 2.5 dry-deposition reduction than that of PM 10 , partly reflecting differences in regional socioeconomic and industrial activity and background PM concentrations. This study advances a deeper understanding of the influence of extreme weather events on vegetation-driven dry deposition and provides scientific support for air quality management and strategic development aimed at strengthening urban ecosystem resilience.

Article.Authors: Khajeh-mehrizi R.; Ardakani S.; Alizadeh A.
Article.Abstract: The degradation of frying oils during thermal processing and storage poses a significant challenge to food quality. Acid value was significantly reduced in TK20 (0.056 ± 0.001% at month 6, P < 0.05), peroxide values were lower in TK20 (5.30 ± 0.05 meq O₂/kg) compared to the control (7.6 ± 0.11 meq O₂/kg) at month 6, and the Totox values were also reduced in TK20 (16.2 ± 0.00) relative to the control(19.7 ± 0.00), indicating effective inhibition of both primary and overall oxidation. Polar compound formation was inhibited dose-dependently, with TK20 remaining below the 10% safety threshold (9.2 ± 0.00% at month 6). These findings demonstrate that P. khinjuk oil serves as an effective natural stabilizer, increasing frying oil shelf life and safety, offering a sustainable alternative to synthetic antioxidants with potential health benefits.

Article.Title: A garment-integrated shape-changing actuator for facilitating dressing
Article.Authors: Nipatphonsakun K.; Hayashi I.; Watanabe T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dressing is a fundamental activity of daily living that becomes challenging for individuals with motor impairments, particularly when garment twisting, wrinkling, and limited armhole space hinder smooth limb insertion. This study presents a garment-integrated shape-changing actuator designed to increase localized stiffness, preserve garment structure, expand the armhole, and reduce friction between the fabric and skin. Flat-tube pneumatic actuators were embedded into a long-sleeved shirt to dynamically maintain garment geometry during dressing. Mechanical evaluations showed that actuator activation increased armhole resistance and reduced sleeve friction compared with the inactive condition. A user study involving 32 participants under normal and simulated hemiplegic conditions revealed a significant reduction in dressing time when dominant-arm impairment was simulated, alongside improved subjective ratings of dressing ease (p < 0.001). Although objective improvements were not observed for non-dominant impairment, participants consistently reported enhanced perceived ease. These findings suggest that actively maintaining garment shape can facilitate dressing motions and reduce interaction barriers between the wearer and clothing. By supporting user participation rather than replacing it, the proposed approach highlights the potential of garment-integrated soft actuators as an interaction-level assistive technology to support independent dressing while preserving residual functional abilities.

Article.Authors: Barzgar F.; Azmi H.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the implementation and evaluation of a water level control system using Arduino and MATLAB. The main objective is to analyze and compare the performance of different controllers in a real experimental setup. The dynamic behavior of the system is identified based on experimental data, and the system transfer function is approximated as a first-order model. The controller performance is then evaluated in real time through direct communication with the Arduino platform. In this study, manual control is completely eliminated, and MATLAB/Simulink fully undertakes the control task of the system. Furthermore, various types of potential sensor faults are systematically implemented, and their effects on system performance are analyzed. To improve the response of the classical PID controller, a Fuzzy-PID controller is employed. This improvement is particularly evident in reducing overshoot and shortening the disturbance-recovery time. In addition, the system response is examined under both disturbed and disturbance-free operating conditions.

Article.Title: Calcium oxalate crystals provide a supporting matrix for the leaf structure
Article.Authors: Brumfeld V.; Sui X.; Wagner H.; Shtein I.; Karimov T.; Feiguelman G.; Cohen M.; Klein T.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the structural role of calcium oxalate (CaOx) crystals within leaf tissues, proposing that they act as a mechanical supporting matrix for leaf structure. While CaOx is often studied for its metabolic or defensive roles, its contribution to the physical integrity of the leaf is less understood. Across plant species, CaOx crystals are preferentially positioned around the leaf veins, but their precise architecture is species- and developmental stage-dependent. We focus on leaves of the Mediterranean evergreen tree species carob ( Ceratonia siliqua L.), applying a combination of micro computed tomography (micro-CT) imaging and mechanical testing. We provide data showing that the presence of CaOx crystals increases leaf stiffness. Specifically, we demonstrate the link between CaOx crystals distribution and leaf stiffness across three approaches: (1) among different plant species. (2) Among plants grown with or without Ca. (3) among leaves of the same plant but at different ages. Our data shows that CaOx crystals are not merely metabolic byproducts but are designed to form a mineral-organic structure which specifically enhances the resistance of the midrib and secondary veins to buckling forces. We propose that CaOx acts as a tunable stiffening agent of leaves that plants can modulate based on nutrient availability.

Article.Abstract: Current cattle-face recognition pipelines in smart agriculture still suffer from accuracy gaps and model bloat. Article.Title: Diurnal variation of islet autoantibody titers in established type 1 diabetes suggests restricted-time sampling improves aab measurement and detection
Article.Authors: Beam C.; DiMeglio L.; Speake C.; Boest-Bjerg K.; Pearce O.; Almutairi B.; Evans-Molina C.; Wong F.; Long A.; Gillespie K.; Pearson J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diurnal islet autoantibody (Aab) variation in type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains poorly understood and could hinder efforts to develop, test and refine new therapies. We sought to describe the extent and pattern of diurnal variation in islet autoantibodies and, having found significant variation, translate to the clinical setting. We conducted two studies in human subjects with established T1D: (1) a prospective study (n = 10) of the range of islet autoantibody and immunoglobulin daily variation within humans and (2) an independent retrospective, cross-sectional study (n = 705) of the effect of time of sample collection on Aab titer and detection in clinical settings. We found that some individuals have wide Aab variations during the day and which can exceed expected levels of inter-assay variation. For some Aab, this variation followed a circadian pattern. We also found that, in clinical settings, time-restricted sampling can lead to increased IA-2A and ZnT8A detection within specific age-groups. We conclude that time-restriction can potentially improve the use of Radiobinding-measured Aabs as biomarkers for the development and monitoring of disease-modifying therapies and in developing islet transplantation strategies in established T1D. Article.Title: Disorientation as a marker of neurotrauma in an animal that uses shock waves as weapons
Article.Authors: Mierow T.; Harris K.; Speiser D.; Kingston A.
Article.Abstract: By snapping their claws, snapping shrimp create cavitation bubbles that release supersonic pressure waves when they collapse. Shock waves such as these are dangerous to animals because they can cause blast-induced neurotrauma by transferring kinetic energy to neural tissues. Previously, we discovered that helmet-like orbital hoods protect snapping shrimp from blast-induced neurotrauma by damping the shock waves they generate and use as weapons. To learn how effectively orbital hoods function, we need to be able to compare levels of blast-induced neurotrauma in snapping shrimp. In humans, spatial disorientation is a behavioral hallmark of blast-induced neurotrauma. Here, we develop methods for assessing spatial disorientation in snapping shrimp and ask if shrimp, like humans, demonstrate disorientation following shock wave exposure. To do so, we quantified aspects of the path trajectories taken by snapping shrimp during shelter-seeking including path tortuosity, fractal dimension, distance traveled, and speed. Shock wave exposure caused snapping shrimp without orbital hoods to travel longer, slower, and more tortuous paths compared to shrimp with unaltered orbital hoods. By quantifying shelter-seeking behavior, we show that exposure to shock waves causes spatial disorientation in snapping shrimp without orbital hoods, supporting our hypothesis that orbital hoods mitigate short-term behavioral consequences of blast-induced neurotrauma.

Article.Title: Document world models: a cognitive-inspired auxiliary training framework for document-level relation extraction
Article.Authors: Wei F.; Yang W.; Gu T.; Gu B.; Lv H.; Jia L.
Article.Abstract: Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) requires models to integrate relation evidence scattered across multiple sentences. Yet existing encoder-based methods perform relation classification in a single pass over a static final representation, causing long-range evidence to decay before it can inform the classification decision. Inspired by theories of incremental reading comprehension, we introduce the Document World Model (DocWM), a lightweight training-only auxiliary framework that encourages progressive entity-state maintenance and relation-belief stabilization in standard DocRE encoders. DocWM introduces two auxiliary training objectives. Entity State Tracking (ES) maintains an entity-specific recurrent hidden state, updated sentence by sentence and aligned with entity embeddings pooled from mentions up to each sentence to preserve early evidence. Relation Belief Dynamics (BD) supervises relation predictions at each reading step via a temporally weighted loss, guiding relation beliefs to stabilize progressively toward the correct label. Experiments on Re-DocRED and HacRED show consistent improvements over the compared baselines, most clearly on long-range cross-sentence relations.

Article.Title: Genetic diversity of the endangered saproxylic beetle Boros schneideri and preliminary insight into its associated bacterial and fungal communities
Article.Authors: Kaczmarczyk-Ziemba A.; Wagner G.; Pietrykowska-Tudruj E.; Staniec B.
Article.Abstract: Boros schneideri is a rare and endangered saproxylic beetle associated with old, dead trees. We investigated its genetic diversity in Western Polesie, Poland, and assessed larval microbiota and mycobiota. COI sequences were additionally compared with records from Poland, Finland, and Mongolia. Both mitochondrial and nuclear datasets revealed high haplotype diversity and moderate nucleotide diversity, while phylogenetic trees and haplotype networks showed shallow relationships without distinct, well-supported geographic lineages. Shared COI haplotypes occurred among geographically distant populations. Negative Tajima’s D and Fu’s Fs values, together with the diversity pattern, were consistent with a possible recent demographic expansion. No Wolbachia infection was detected. High-throughput sequencing targeting the bacterial 16 S rRNA V3–V4 region and fungal ITS1 revealed diverse bacterial communities in 11 larvae, dominated by Proteobacteria, particularly Burkholderiaceae and Yersiniaceae. Preliminary mycobiota profiling of one larva identified predominantly Ascomycota, including Ophiostoma , previously suggested as a potential food resource. Despite limited sampling, these findings provide a baseline for understanding the genetic and microbial diversity of B. schneideri and support integrating population genetics and microbiome research into future conservation studies.

Article.Title: Perfusion-guided virtual element analysis for biomechanical diagnosis of breast cysts and tumors
Article.Authors: Mohana R.; Chandru M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the most common cancers in the world. There is a pressing need for sophisticated diagnostic techniques that can identify anomalies in their earliest, benign stages. Although infrared thermography provides a non-invasive way to monitor surface temperature distributions, the lack of quantitative, parameter-based markers limits its clinical utility. The current study presents a framework that uses quantitative blood perfusion reference ranges as a non-invasive pre-screening diagnostic tool in order to overcome this limitation. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations of the model, such as the derivation of optimal convergence rates, error estimates in the $$L^2$$ -norm, and demonstrations of existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution, in order to guarantee the robustness of VEM. Our methodology incorporates the Pennes bioheat equation into the virtual element method to determine blood perfusion ranges from thermal profiles corresponding to healthy, cystic, and malignant tissues, in contrast to traditional approaches that assume constant perfusion. By methodically mapping these thermal signatures against the selected perfusion ranges, pathological zones are identified, offering a diagnostic approach comparable to the application of biochemical markers in clinical settings. By creating perfusion-based quantitative markers, this framework enhances thermo-graphic diagnostic potential and opens the door to better early identification and characterization of breast tissue abnormalities.

Article.Title: A Caputo fractional physics-informed neural network for Lorenz chaotic systems
Article.Authors: Baskar A.; Naveen S.
Article.Abstract: Fractional-order dynamical systems provide an effective mathematical framework for describing nonlinear processes with memory and hereditary effects. Although physics-informed neural networks have demonstrated promising performance for solving differential equations, their application to fractional-order chaotic dynamical systems remains relatively limited. In this study, a Caputo fractional physics-informed neural networks (FPINNs) framework is developed to approximate the fractional-order Lorenz system by incorporating the governing fractional differential equations into a multi-objective loss function. The reference solutions are generated using the Caputo Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector method to ensure an appropriate numerical treatment of the fractional derivative. The proposed framework is evaluated for several fractional orders over the considered simulation interval, and its predictive performance is assessed using quantitative error metrics, including mean squared error, mean absolute error, sum of squared errors, and the coefficient of determination. The numerical results demonstrate that the FPINN accurately reconstructs the fractional Lorenz trajectories while maintaining good agreement with the ABM reference solutions. Furthermore, the study investigates the influence of the fractional order on prediction accuracy and computational performance, providing a systematic numerical assessment of the proposed framework. The results indicate that FPINNs constitute an effective and data-efficient approach for approximating nonlinear fractional dynamical systems within the investigated computational setting.

Article.Authors: Ekrami Kakhki S.; Kheyroddin A.
Article.Abstract: The bond behavior of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) and steel rebars in advanced cementitious composites is governed by a complex interplay of rebar type, concrete matrix, confinement, embedment length, and geometric parameters, yet it remains insufficiently understood. Using a consistent flexural bond testing framework, the integrated effects of rebar diameter, embedment length, bottom concrete cover, transverse reinforcement, fiber type, and fiber content were assessed. Results show that bond strength and failure modes are strongly influenced by rebar diameter and embedment length, with FRP bars displaying distinct responses due to their linear-elastic behavior and surface characteristics. Bottom concrete cover, transverse reinforcement, and fiber-induced confinement critically enhance stress transfer and mitigate splitting failures. Steel and glass fibers significantly improve bond performance via crack bridging and confinement, whereas polypropylene fibers mainly reduce shrinkage-induced cracking. The findings advance understanding of size effects, stress redistribution, and confinement efficiency in SCC and FRC systems and provide a robust experimental basis for developing improved bond models and design guidelines for FRP-reinforced concrete structures.

Article.Title: TrustLite-FL: multi-statistic trust aggregation for robust federated learning in consumer IoT
Article.Authors: Hussain I.; Badar H.; Alhwikem F.
Article.Abstract: Federated learning (FL) trains shared models on consumer IoT devices without moving raw data off the device, but poisoning can compromise it. It scores client updates by entropy, magnitude and direction relative to the round, smooths those scores over time, clips update norms, and logs suspicious behavior for audit. Its aggregation and scoring scale linearly with clients and model parameters. We prove that update entropy is invariant to positive scaling and sign flips, so entropy alone cannot detect them. We evaluate it in simulation on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, benchmark proxies for consumer device data, with non-IID clients, five attacks plus a clean setting, 30% adversaries, seven baselines and three seeds. It has the highest mean accuracy, or matches it, in 9 of 15 attacked settings, and is within one percentage point of the best in 13. Ablation shows that the norm clip provides most of this robustness. The trust layer excludes every Gaussian noise adversary, excluding at most 2.9% of benign clients, but no sign flipping or ALIE adversary. Article.Title: Diagnosis of breast cancer with high accuracy via Petri net modeling of signaling pathways
Article.Authors: Khodaei S.; Sarvari M.; Sajadi E.; Asadzadeh F.; Ebrahimian H.; Rahgozar M.; Kavousi K.
Article.Abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, affecting millions of people each year. There are many different types of cancer, including breast cancer, colon cancer and endometrial cancer, each with its own unique characteristics and challenges. One of the most crucial aspects of cancer management is early detection. Detecting cancer at an early stage significantly increases the chances of successful treatment and survival. In recent years, much research has been conducted to accelerate the diagnosis and prediction of cancer, especially by examining the role of genes, their effectiveness, and especially the sequence of changes in their activities in relation to this disease. An important part of the results of these studies has been related to KEGG signaling pathways. Many studies have also been conducted to model these signaling pathways via Petri net tools, which have shown good capabilities in this field. This article reveals in part some of these capabilities observed in a recently developed tool that provides a means for diagnosing breast cancer by modeling the related signaling pathway via Petri nets. The proposed method provides high accuracy and precision (95–99%) on most related GEO datasets. Similar promising results have been reported in various cancers and will be published soon. With this method, blood samples, which are less expensive and easier to obtain for earlier detection, perform as well as tissue samples.

Article.Abstract: Abstract We present OocystMeter, a machine learning-based software developed to automate the segmentation of malaria oocysts from images of mosquito midguts stained with mercurochrome. Manual dissection, staining, mounting, and image acquisition by human scientists remain necessary. Article.Title: Eigenmodes of synthetic antiferromagnetic skyrmions
Article.Authors: Zulfiqar K.; Lang M.; Holt S.; Pathak S.; Bruckner F.; Fangohr H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigate the excitation modes of confined synthetic-antiferromagnetic (SAF) skyrmions using micromagnetic eigenvalue and ringdown simulations. We consider several geometries: single SAF skyrmions in square and rectangular confinement, unequal layer thicknesses, and strips containing multiple skyrmions. The antiferromagnetic coupling strongly modifies the low-frequency dynamics. The square geometry exhibits two nearly degenerate gyrotropic modes, where in each both layers have the same rotation sense. In rectangular geometries, we instead find nearly linear SAF skyrmion translation emerging from opposite gyration sense in the two layers. These translational modes become the characteristic low-frequency excitations of SAF skyrmion chains. For skyrmion chains, we identify collective translational and breathing modes with standing-wave-like spatial profiles. Beyond ferromagnetic-like breathing modes, the SAF geometry supports breathing oscillations in which the two layers oscillate out of phase. We further demonstrate signal propagation along extended SAF skyrmion chains with propagation velocities about 15% larger than in ferromagnetic skyrmion chains. These results provide a systematic description of the collective dynamics of SAF skyrmions arising from the interplay of geometric confinement, intralayer, and interlayer coupling.

Article.Authors: Ti Y.; Cheng R.; Wei S.; Huang W.; Yu C.
Article.Abstract: The limited energy capacity of sensor nodes remains a central constraint on the operational longevity of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs)-a challenge that is more critical in Rechargeable Wireless Sensor Networks (RWSNs), where sustaining long-term functionality depends on delaying the First Node Death (FND), a key point that often signals the beginning of network problems. While prior research has extensively explored heuristic algorithms coupled with energy-aware routing mechanisms to reduce transmission energy consumption and extend network lifetime, these methods typically require repeated iterations to converge. Such computational demands render them unsuitable for real-time applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a hybrid optimization framework that integrates Genetic Algorithms (GA) with Deep Learning (DL). This framework can run quickly to improve energy efficiency and extend network lifetime in RWSNs. The proposed approach builds upon an energy-aware clustering architecture that incorporates a lightweight version of the Residual Neural Network (ResNet) model. This clustering strategy promotes a more balanced distribution of energy consumption across the network, delaying early node failures caused by localized energy depletion. Based on this setup, we create an optimization scheme using a novel version of GA that helps the ResNet model-simplified for use on regular CPUs-learns an optimal CH selection policy. The GA component employs a custom fitness function designed to maximize the time to FND latency. The synergy between the clustering method and the GA-DL hybrid selection mechanism enables rapid and effective CH assignment without the iterative overhead typical of heuristic algorithms. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only reduces energy consumption and extends the time to FND but also achieves near real-time performance. This makes it a promising alternative to traditional heuristic-based approaches, particularly in latency-sensitive RWSN applications. Together, these contributions mark a significant step toward the development of scalable, efficient, and resilient RWSN architectures.

Activation energies ranging from 10 3 to 10 4 kJ mol –1 were obtained, indicating that substantial overheating or undercooling is required to achieve rapid thermochromic switching.

Article.Title: Spatial multi-omics identifies regional immunometabolic remodeling and macrophage PCK2-associated T-cell activation in lupus nephritis

Functional perturbation in vitro further indicated that macrophage PCK2 contributes to T-cell activation under inflammatory co-culture conditions. Article.Authors: Voloskov B.; Karpov I.; Em V.; Firsov D.; Simonov A.; Karamov R.; Qian G.; Bryukhanov I.; Fedorenko A.; Evlashin S.; Sergeichev I.

The energy-based approaches (Proposed Methods I and II) demonstrated linear correlations with relative ND stress reductions (R 2 = 0.75 and 0.71, respectively). Furthermore, by subtracting the empirical micro-yielding threshold from condition-specific macroscopic yield strengths, Proposed Method III captured the relative RS relaxation trend. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis supported the proposed mechanistic interpretation by showing localized geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation prior to bulk yielding. These findings show that the proposed mechanical methods can serve as accessible tools for evaluating stress mitigation strategies in additive manufacturing.

Article.Title: Reuse of ESR-irradiated tooth enamel for amino acid geochronology: assessing the impact of gamma irradiation
Article.Authors: Dickinson M.; Duval M.; Penkman K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hominin and faunal fossil collections are valuable scientific resources for investigating past populations, making it critically important to preserve these rare materials and prioritise minimally destructive methods. Electron spin resonance (ESR) dating of tooth enamel typically requires laboratory irradiation of powdered subsamples; however, the effects of this treatment on organic biomolecules, and therefore their potential reuse for amino acid geochronology (AAG), remain largely unknown. This study investigates the impact of gamma irradiation on amino acids within tooth enamel, and its implications for reuse of leftover ESR-dated enamel for AAG from two palaeolithic sites: Hortus, southern France and Belle-Roche, Belgium (maximum laboratory gamma dose of 1500 and 3000 Gy respectively). Our results show that laboratory irradiation induces negligible racemisation in selected amino acids, although significant correlations between dose and D/L values emerge at higher doses (> 1200 Gy). This demonstrates that while low-level gamma irradiation (e.g. <500 Gy) does not substantially compromise the chemical integrity of amino acids in enamel, higher doses may alter racemisation patterns, potentially affecting AAG interpretation. Consequently, this supports cautious reuse of irradiated ESR powders, preferably those exposed to low laboratory doses, enabling effective reuse of finite fossil tooth enamel resources.

Article.Title: Differential temporal dynamics of Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity following minibeam and conventional irradiation
Article.Authors: Bertho A.; Martinez Vicente P.; Fernandez Rodriguez A.; Juchaux M.; Gilbert C.; Moros M.; Prezado Y.
Article.Abstract: Minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) improves the therapeutic index by sparing normal tissues while maintaining tumour control, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. TOP-TCF luciferase reporter activity and cell viability were assessed following MBRT or conventional radiotherapy (CRT) in A431, RG2 and MDCK cell models. Dose- and time-dependent responses were evaluated at 24, 48 and 72 h post-irradiation. Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity showed delayed, dose-dependent and strongly cell-context-dependent responses. Across the three cell lines, MBRT generally produced lower reporter activity than CRT at later measured time points and/or higher doses. These differences were accompanied by distinct cytotoxicity profiles, with CRT generally inducing greater PI positivity than MBRT. MBRT and CRT were associated with different magnitudes and temporal profiles of Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity. Because the irradiation modalities also differed in dose rate and cytotoxicity, the present data do not establish that spatial dose heterogeneity itself caused these signalling differences. The findings provide an initial framework for further mechanistic and spatially resolved studies.

Article.Title: O-antigen deficiency in Porphyromonas gingivalis attenuates dendritic cell-driven Th1/Th17-associated CD4+ T-cell responses
Article.Authors: Pavez V.; Melgar-Rodríguez S.; Selman J.; González-Osuna L.; Díaz-Zúñiga J.; Cafferata E.; Carvajal P.; Bravo D.; Vernal R.
Article.Abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis is a keystone periodontal pathogen whose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) contributes to immune dysregulation during periodontitis. Dendritic cells (DCs) link microbial recognition to adaptive immunity; however, how P. gingivalis LPS shapes DC activation and subsequent CD4 + T-cell responses remains incompletely understood. This study examined responses of human monocyte-derived DCs (hMoDCs) and downstream autologous CD4 + T lymphocytes to P. gingivalis strains that differ in complete LPS expression. hMoDCs were stimulated with the wild-type W50 strain, the isogenic O-antigen-deficient ΔPG1051 mutant, the complemented cΔPG1051 strain, or left unstimulated. We evaluated hMoDC maturation, cytokine responses, and expression of IRF4, IRF8, NOTCH2, and BATF3 by flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. We then co-cultured stimulated hMoDCs with autologous CD4 + T lymphocytes to assess cytokine and RANKL responses by RT-qPCR and ELISA and lineage-associated transcription factor expression by RT-qPCR. All P. gingivalis strains induced comparable maturation of hMoDCs. In contrast, W50 induced robust expression of Th1- and Th17-polarizing cytokines and increased IRF4 and NOTCH2 expression. Notably, ΔPG1051 markedly attenuated these hMoDC responses, and cΔPG1051 restored them. Consistently, CD4 + T lymphocytes co-cultured with ΔPG1051-stimulated hMoDCs showed attenuated Th1- and Th17-type responses, with reduced mRNA expression of Th1- and Th17-related cytokines, T-bet, RORC2, and RANKL, and lower protein levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-17A, IL-23, and RANKL. In contrast, Th2- and Treg-associated cytokines and transcription factors remained largely unchanged. These findings demonstrate that intact P. gingivalis LPS is a major determinant of DC inflammatory programming and its downstream capacity to promote Th1- and Th17-associated CD4 + T-cell responses.

Article.Title: Hemostatic efficacy and safety of oxidized regenerated cellulose hemostatic material in a multi-organ bleeding porcine model
Article.Authors: Li G.; Li Z.; Deng K.; Qiu X.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Oxidized regenerated cellulose (ORC) is a widely used absorbable hemostatic agent, but comparative data on its efficacy across different bleeding scenarios remain limited. This study compared the hemostatic efficacy, tissue compatibility, and safety of a domestically produced absorbable ORC (StypCel™) with an imported counterpart (Surgicel ® Fibrillar™) in minipig models of Liver, Gastric wall, and Mesentery bleeding. Sixteen male Bama minipigs were randomly assigned to the Liver bleeding model ( n = 8) or the gastrointestinal model ( n = 8). Within each model, animals were further allocated to the StypCel™ group ( n = 4) or the Surgicel ® Fibrillar™ group ( n = 4), with three bleeding sites created per animal per organ. Bleeding models were established for each organ, and outcomes including 10‑s blood loss, time to hemostasis, intraoperative blood loss, hematology, liver and kidney function, coagulation parameters, and histological changes were assessed. Both materials exhibited three‑dimensional porous network structures, with StypCel™ showing significantly finer fibers (9.82 ± 0.93 μm vs. 20.59 ± 1.88 μm, P < 0.001). In the Liver, Gastric wall, and Mesentery bleeding models, no significant differences were observed between groups in time to hemostasis ( P = 0.8759, P = 0.1578, and P = 0.9632, respectively), intraoperative blood loss ( P = 0.0805, P = 0.7673, and P = 0.4678, respectively), or any hematological, biochemical, or coagulation parameters at all time points (all P > 0.05). Histological analysis revealed similar degradation and absorption profiles, with inflammation essentially resolved by week 4 in both groups. StypCel™ demonstrated hemostatic efficacy and safety comparable to those of Surgicel ® Fibrillar™ across multiple bleeding models, supporting its use as an effective alternative.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been prominent in our daily lives by means of mobile applications and web search engines. Students’ perceived performance of AES system has a significant influence on students’ confirmation. Furthermore, students’ confirmation of AES system positively affects individual innovativeness, reflective thinking and criticism of AES. And students’ individual innovativeness also positively influences students’ reflective thinking of AES. However, students’ individual innovativeness and reflective thinking of AES system doesn’t have a positive relationship with students’ criticism. This study not only reveals Chinese private university EFL students’ attitudes and experiences towards technological tools but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.

Article.Title: Time to uptake of long-term postpartum family planning and factors associated with it among Ethiopian mothers: A shared frailty survival analysis
Article.Authors: Kabtyimer A.; Jemil H.; Endalkachew A.; Mankelkl G.; Kassaw A.; Abeje E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-term postpartum family planning (LTPPFP) involves the use of long-acting contraceptive methods within one year after childbirth. Delayed initiation increases the risk of unintended and closely spaced pregnancies, leading to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. This study assessed the time to LTPPFP uptake and associated factors during the extended postpartum period among mothers in Ethiopia. A secondary analysis of data from the Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia Cohort II, 2021 to 2023 was performed. A total of 2,167 postpartum mothers were included using a multistage stratified sampling technique. Data management and analysis were conducted using Stata 17 and R. Multicollinearity was checked using the variance inflation factor, while the proportional hazards assumption was assessed using the global Schoenfeld residual test. Three shared frailty survival models (cluster-level, region-level, and nested frailty models) were fitted and compared. Adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were presented, and statistical significance was declared at p ≤ 0.05. During the one-year follow-up period, 396 women initiated LTPPFP. Among users, implants accounted for 94% of methods used, while female sterilization represented only 1%. The weighted prevalence of LTPPFP utilization was 14.8% (95% CI: 13.2–16.4). A total of 1,748.37 person-years were observed, yielding an incidence rate of 183.5 per 1,000 person-years. The cumulative survival probability for one year was 0.809. Earlier initiation of LTPPFP was significantly associated with having a plan to use family planning (AHR = 2.45; 95% CI: 1.58–3.81), previous family planning use (AHR = 1.90; 95% CI: 1.48–2.43), institutional delivery (AHR = 1.52; 95% CI: 1.03–2.26), postnatal care utilization (AHR = 1.63; 95% CI: 1.00–2.66), complications during delivery (AHR = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.02–1.60), and age at sexual debut > 18 years (AHR = 2.04; 95% CI: 1.20–3.46). LTPPFP initiation remains substantially delayed among postpartum mothers in Ethiopia. Key determinants of earlier uptake included prior family planning experience, service contact points (institutional delivery and postnatal care), and reproductive history characteristics. Strengthening integrated postpartum counseling during maternity care services is essential to facilitate timely LTPPFP adoption.

Article.Title: Systemic Inflammatory markers are associated with drug-resistant pediatric epilepsy in Ghanaian children
Article.Authors: Mante P.; Ntewusu J.; Danquah J.; Owusu G.; Dotse D.; Adomako N.
Article.Abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) in children is associated with significant morbidity, yet the contribution of systemic inflammation to its clinical expression remains incompletely defined, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This study investigated the relationship between systemic inflammatory markers, drug resistance and seizure severity in a paediatric cohort in Ghana. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 180 participants (60 DRE; 60 controlled epilepsy; 60 healthy controls) recruited from a tertiary hospital. Clinical data and peripheral blood samples were obtained at a single time point. DRE patients exhibited significantly elevated NLR, CCL11 and PGE₂ levels compared with controls. Although these markers were associated with NHS3 seizure-severity scores in pooled analyses, these relationships were substantially attenuated after accounting for DRE status. These findings demonstrate an association between selected systemic inflammatory markers and pediatric DRE and support further prospective evaluation of their clinical relevance.

Article.Title: Imaging shallow magma storage and fluid pathways beneath Aso volcano using ambient-noise tomography
Article.Authors: Tsuji T.; Chhun C.; Andajani R.; Ishikawa Y.; Nishizaka N.; Yano H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the high-resolution three-dimensional internal structure of the large caldera-type volcano Mt. Aso, we deployed a temporary seismometer network and applied ambient-noise surface-wave tomography. We resolve the shallow crustal structure with high spatial resolution and identify an ellipsoidal low S-wave velocity ( Vs ) anomaly at depths of 2.5–4.5 km beneath the Nakadake crater. The Vs within this zone is ~ 1.5 km/s, indicating a highly fractured and pressurized rock, which we interpret as a shallow magma storage zone. Considering the temperature conditions, supercritical fluids could transition to a gas phase beneath the storage zone, leading to volume expansion, fracture opening, and reduced Vs . Furthermore, combined with previously reported temporal variations in seismic velocity and geodetic modeling results, the low- Vs zone could behave as a pressure-sensitive fractured system, potentially connected to the overlying fluid-bearing pathway beneath Aso Volcano. Above the storage zone, we image a narrow, vertically elongated low- Vs structure interpreted as a hydrothermal conduit that likely transports the pressurized fluids to the surface crater and generates very long-period (VLP) tremors.

Article.Title: Network modeling of science teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in science curriculum development
Article.Authors: Ibrahem U.; Alrashood J.; Diab H.; Alrosa T.; Alkhabra Y.; Alotaibi S.; Moussa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study employs psychological network modeling to examine the interrelationships among science teachers’ perceptions of benefits, challenges, and attitudes toward integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools in science curriculum development. The estimated network revealed a dense structure. Centrality analyses indicated that curriculum content generation and innovative pedagogical tools were most central, while data processing challenges and algorithmic bias emerged as prominent structural barriers. Centrality metrics identify AI-facilitated curriculum design and innovative pedagogical tools as primary benefits, while challenges such as data processing limitations and algorithmic biases emerge as significant barriers. Teacher attitudes demonstrate ambivalence, characterized by resistance to automating administrative functions alongside guarded optimism for interactive and adaptive learning applications. These insights underscore the imperative to address technical constraints, ethical considerations, and the evolving professional identities of educators to ensure effective AI integration. The study contributes a nuanced, systemic understanding that informs the development of tailored AI tools and support frameworks, ultimately advancing transformative innovation in science education.

Article.Title: HCVSOA: hybrid corona virus–snake optimization for hyperparameter-tuned kinematic handwriting analysis in Parkinson’s disease detection
Article.Authors: Ayus I.; Azad C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Working with machine learning models is challenging due to various complex factors such as high-dimensional temporal dependencies, control complexity and poor subject-independent performance. Researchers have identified that the conventional optimization strategies often fail to explore these complex factors fully which limits model robustness and subject-independent performance. The study introduces hybrid heuristic optimization strategy namely, Hybrid Corona Virus-Snake Optimization Algorithm (HCVSOA) which combines the exploratory strengths of Corona Virus Optimization Algorithm (CVOA) with the adaptive exploitation of the Snake Optimization Algorithm (SOA). The HCVSOA framework is capable of tuning model parameters for machine learning models which facilitates more effective temporal feature extraction and structured feature representation for strengthening accurate class-based classification. Experiments are conducted on both handwriting dynamics datasets with meander and spiral patterns. The HCVSOA + Convolutional 1D Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit framework demonstrates superior performance over other considered optimization strategies which records an accuracy of 96.25% on meander New HandPD signals, 97.86% on spiral New HandPD signals and 99.903% on spiral UCI dataset. The observed improvements in performance metrics confirm a well-balanced trade-off between sensitivity and specificity. Further, Area under the Curve and radar analyses confirm enhanced discriminative capability which highlights the consistent advantage across architectures and datasets for hybrid optimization techniques. The proposed HCVSOA significantly improves model subject-independent predictive performance for kinematic handwriting analysis.

Article.Authors: Sridhar J.; Unnissa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blockchain technology has emerged as an innovative digital solution aimed at enhancing transparency, traceability, and trust within closed-loop supply chains, particularly in the domains of remanufacturing and recycling operations. In light of Blockchain investment costs, privacy concerns, information transparency, and competitive dynamics in recycling, a Stackelberg game framework is developed to analyze optimal pricing strategies, collection decisions, and overall profitability. The research investigates the impact of collection competition and Blockchain-related parameters on supply chain performance. Through numerical analysis and sensitivity assessments, the findings reveal that the adoption of Blockchain technology enhances acceptance rates for remanufactured products and influences channel decision-making, whereas intensified competition in collection efforts tends to diminish individual collection performance. The results indicate that the $$M-R$$ model exhibits superior economic performance, while the $$M-3P$$ model demonstrates greater recycling efficiency in the context of intense competition. This research contributes theoretical insights and practical guidance for the design of sustainable Closed-Loop Supply Chains through the strategic integration of blockchain technology and optimized recycling channel selection.

Article.Title: Control of source–migration–trap coupling on hydrocarbon accumulation in the Shahejie Formation, Qikou Sag, Bohai Bay Basin
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Liu W.; Fu G.; Liang M.; Zhang D.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of hydrocarbon accumulation in continental rift basins remains a major challenge in petroleum geoscience because the relative roles of hydrocarbon supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness are often poorly constrained. Focusing on the lower section of the first member of the Shahejie Formation (Es 1 L ), this study formulates a hierarchical control framework that synthesizes source supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness to elucidate the mechanisms of hydrocarbon accumulation. Integrating three-dimensional (3D) seismic, well logging, and geochemical data, this study delineates the distribution of effective source rocks, systematically characterizes vertical and lateral hydrocarbon migration pathways, and identifies the development locations of effective traps in the target interval combined with the evaluation of fault lateral sealing capacity to carry out coupled hydrocarbon accumulation analysis of source-migration-trap. A total of 18 migration pathways and 24 effective trap locations were identified. The hierarchical framework identifies source-rock expulsion intensity as the first-order control, defining the upper limit of hydrocarbon supply; migration-pathway architecture as the second-order control, regulating hydrocarbon focusing, dispersion, and charging efficiency; and trap effectiveness, particularly fault sealing capacity, as the third-order control, governing hydrocarbon preservation and final filling degree. The results indicate that hydrocarbons mainly accumulate in zones with optimal matching of source-migration-trap elements, characterized by sufficient hydrocarbon supply from source rocks, unobstructed migration pathways and effective trap conditions. Production-testing results from Well BS-4, located within one of the predicted favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones, provide field-based support for the proposed coupling framework. The proposed hierarchical source-migration-trap framework provides a process-based approach for evaluating favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones in lower-source upper-reservoir petroleum systems of mature faulted basins.

Article.Authors: Kubota A.; Shinohara Y.; Goto A.; Tajima A.
Article.Abstract: Social isolation (SI) during adolescence is associated with neurobiological alterations; however, its effect on the hippocampal epigenome and transcriptome remains unclear. RNA-seq identified 106 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including upregulated Fosl2 and Hdac9 and downregulated Fbxw7 , with enrichment of myelination-related pathways. Although global concordance between chromatin accessibility and transcriptional changes was limited, integrated analysis showed directional concordance between expression and nearby candidate accessibility changes for a subset of DEGs. Cell type analyses suggested that SI-downregulated transcriptional signatures were linked to excitatory neurons, whereas SI-upregulated signatures were enriched in non-neuronal populations, particularly oligodendrocytes. Deconvolution suggested higher estimated oligodendrocyte representation and lower estimated excitatory neuron representation in isolated mice. These findings suggest that adolescent SI is associated with significant transcriptomic remodeling and candidate chromatin accessibility changes within hippocampal CA1, accompanied by distinct neuronal- and glial-associated transcriptional signatures.

Article.Abstract: We monitored the mortality of the fan mussel Pinna nobilis (L.) in the Venice lagoon (North of Italy) during a period of one and half year (2023–2024) in two areas named Ottagono Alberoni (OA) and Coffa Val Grande (CV) reporting the disease condition for the period time 2024. Our results show a positive correlation between mortality rates and host size, with higher mortality affecting bigger/older individuals, although with local differences. CV pen shell population was characterized by smaller/younger individuals affected by milder viral infections and suffering lower mortality rates. Conversely, OA population presented larger individuals (adults) of P. nobilis affected by heavy viral infections that suffering a 100% mortality rate, leading to the extinction of that population by October 2024. Total Hemocyte Count (THC) was lower in OA (1.77 × 10 4 ±0.16 cell/ml) compared to CV (1.65 × 10 5 ±0.8 cells/ml) showing a negative correlation with viral load, connected with percentage of dead cells percentage, in turn correlated with animal size, suggesting that number of immune cells is regulated by the level of infection, and also age. Article.Title: The spirometric blind spot: oscillometry identifies a tobacco-dose-associated small-airway signal in community case-finding
Article.Authors: Kotsiou O.; Passalidis K.; Gouta E.; Perlepe G.; Barkas G.; Kirgou P.; Papagiannis D.; Fotiou M.; Diakomanoli K.; Albanou M.; Dimtsi V.; Liaros T.; Karanikola E.; Tsiatsiou X.; Feizoula E.; Gkouletza K.; Laki E.; Nari C.; Koukousa M.; Fanara C.; Litso A.; Plessa A.; Nikolaou A.; Liaskou P.; Rousi S.
Article.Abstract: Small-airway dysfunction (SAD) may precede fixed airflow obstruction, but the clinical meaning of increased oscillometric detection in community settings remains uncertain. In this cross-sectional study, we evaluated an oscillometry-defined SAD phenotype, its concordance with spirometric indices, and its association with cumulative tobacco exposure within an open-access community respiratory case-finding programme. Adults attending nine healthcare sites in Greece underwent structured questionnaire assessment, respiratory oscillometry and spirometry. Oscillometric SAD was defined as any abnormal R5–R19, X5, AX or Fres z-score, whereas spirometric SAD was defined as FEF₂₅–₇₅ <65% predicted. Complete acceptable oscillometric classification was available in 533/615 participants and complete acceptable spirometry in 504/615. Oscillometric SAD was present in 145/533 (27.2%), spirometric SAD in 71/504 (14.1%), and fixed-ratio airflow obstruction in 18/504 (3.6%). Among 468 participants with complete paired oscillometric and spirometric classifications, positive agreement was low (22.8%; Cohen’s κ = 0.055). Each additional 10 pack-years increased the adjusted odds of oscillometric SAD by 19% among ever-smokers (aOR 1.19, 95% CI 1.05–1.36; p = 0.007) and by 18% among ever-smokers with FEV₁/FVC ≥ 0.70 (aOR 1.18, 95% CI 1.03–1.36; p = 0.020). SAD was also observed in 15/56 participants with asthma (26.8%) and 57/191 never-smokers without a prior chronic respiratory diagnosis (29.8%). Oscillometry therefore identified a tobacco-dose-associated mechanical phenotype that was incompletely captured by spirometric criteria, but its substantial prevalence outside COPD limits disease-specific interpretation.

Article.Title: Physical exercise and interviewer-rated appearance: longitudinal evidence from the China family panel studies, 2010–2022
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical appearance is an important form of social capital, yet limited longitudinal evidence exists on whether it can be shaped by modifiable behaviors such as physical exercise. Using seven waves of data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) collected between 2010 and 2022, this study examines whether changes in exercise behavior are associated with changes in interviewer-rated physical appearance. We construct an unbalanced individual-level panel and estimate fixed-effects models to exploit within-person variation over time while accounting for time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity and survey-year effects. Physical appearance is measured using interviewer evaluations on a 1–7 scale, and physical exercise is primarily measured by weekly exercise frequency. The results show that exercise frequency is positively and significantly associated with appearance ratings: each additional exercise session per week corresponds to a modest increase in interviewer-rated appearance. This positive association remains stable across sequentially adjusted model specifications. However, when total weekly exercise duration is used as an alternative measure, the estimated coefficient is no longer statistically significant. The estimated association is somewhat larger among women than among men, although the gender difference is not statistically significant. In addition, lagged exercise frequency is not significantly associated with current appearance ratings, suggesting that the appearance-related benefits of exercise may be more immediate than persistent. This study contributes to the literature by improving identification relative to prior cross-sectional research through panel fixed-effects estimation and by using interviewer-rated appearance. The findings provide longitudinal evidence that physical exercise is associated with external appearance evaluations in a manner that is relevant to real-world social interactions.

Article.Title: High stimulation rate ABR reveals auditory brainstem conduction abnormalities in vestibular migraine
Article.Authors: Li C.; Huang Y.; Wang Y.; Yang S.; Yu W.; Pan Q.; Wang D.
Article.Abstract: To explore the application value of high-stimulation-rate auditory brainstem response (ABR) in evaluating auditory pathway conduction in vestibular migraine (VM) patients and to analyze its correlation with clinical symptoms. A prospective case-control study was conducted, including 56 VM patients (56ears) and 56 healthy controls (56 ears). All subjects underwent acoustic immittance testing, pure-tone audiometry, and ABR testing at low (11.1/s) and high (51.1/s) stimulation rates. The interpeak latency variance of wave I–V (ΔI-VIPL) between high and low stimulation rates was calculated, and ≥ 0.28 ms was defined as the abnormal threshold. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) were used to evaluate headache intensity and dizziness-related handicap, respectively. The correlations between these scores and ΔI-VIPL were also analyzed. At the low stimulation rate, no significant differences in ABR parameters were observed between the control and VM groups ( P > 0.05). At the high stimulation rate, the latencies of waves III and V, as well as the I–III, I–V and ΔI-VIPLs, were significantly prolonged in the VM group ( P < 0.05). The prevalence of abnormal ΔI-VIPL was 69.64% (39/56), which was significantly higher than that in the control group 12.50%(7/56), P < 0.05. ROC curve analysis for discriminating VM patients from healthy controls showed that the optimal cutoff value of ΔI-VIPL was 0.265 ms (AUC = 0.791, sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 87.5%, P < 0.05). Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples supported its stability (bootstrap median 0.265 ms, 95% PI 0.215–0.285 ms). Spearman correlation analysis demonstrated that ΔI-VIPL was significantly positively correlated with the total DHI score ( r s =0.623, P < 0.05) and VAS score ( r s =0.534, P < 0.05). High-stimulation rate auditory evoked potential (ABR) can effectively identify abnormal auditory brainstem pathways in VM patients. The ΔI-VIPL parameters show differences among different clinical subtypes, and are closely related to dizziness-related handicap and headache intensity; however, these associations are cross-sectional and should not be interpreted as causal or independently predictive.Therefore, ΔI-VIPL may serve as an auxiliary electrophysiological metric reflecting brainstem auditory conduction stress in VM patients, although further studies with disease controls are required to confirm its clinical utility.

Article.Title: Generative AI-assisted design problem exploration in interaction design: response disclosure, prompt initiative, and cost-sensitive prompting behavior
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Ibrahim F.; Wang Y.; Liu J.; Liu Y.; Zhao S.
Article.Abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in early-stage design exploration, yet experimental evidence is limited on how system-side response disclosure and user-side prompt initiative jointly shape the exploration of design problems that are not yet well defined. In a 2 × 2 within-subject experiment, 48 design students completed four interaction-design tasks involving unfamiliar user groups under one-time versus progressive response disclosure and low versus high prompt initiative, with the composition time of every submission logged. Progressive disclosure was associated with greater perceived understanding change, higher self-reported engagement and germane cognitive load, lower extraneous cognitive load, and more prompts. High prompt initiative showed the same pattern on these four self-reported measures but significantly fewer prompts, reversing the predicted direction; composition time accounted for 18% of the exploration window under high initiative and under 2% under low initiative. Both sets of main effects held after multiplicity correction and adjustment for task and period. An exploratory interaction for germane cognitive load did not survive correction. These findings extend a mixed-initiative view of AI-assisted exploration by identifying response structuring and question formulation as separable design levers. They also indicate that prompt frequency should be interpreted together with the cost of producing a submission.

Article.Title: Comparative benchmarking of the small and nano versions YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 for FDM 3D printing fault detection
Article.Authors: Hany H.; Elashry A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D printing is widely used in industrial and consumer applications, but printing failures are often detected only after substantial material and production time have been lost. This study presents a controlled benchmark of four lightweight YOLO object detectors, YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s, YOLOv11n, and YOLOv11s, for in-process FDM fault detection. All models were fine-tuned under identical conditions on 5793 annotated images covering six fault classes. Performance was evaluated on clean test images and under three types of synthetic camera degradation: Gaussian blur, directional motion blur, and additive Gaussian noise. Deployment-related metrics, including parameter count, GFLOPs, ONNX model size, GPU latency, and CPU inference latency, were also measured. On clean images, YOLOv8s achieved the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.7905, while YOLOv11n provided comparable nano-scale accuracy with 14% fewer parameters. Stringing remained the most difficult fault class, with AP@0.5 values of approximately 0.45–0.48. The robustness experiments showed that blur caused a gradual reduction in detection performance, while directional motion blur was more severe than Gaussian blur. Additive Gaussian noise produced the largest performance degradation. Across the extended degradation grid, YOLOv11n achieved the lowest Degradation Sensitivity Index (DSI) of 28.80%, and also provided the fastest CPU inference at 48.11 ms/image and the smallest model footprint at 10.61 MB. These results provide a practical benchmark for selecting lightweight YOLO models and designing robust FDM monitoring systems.

Article.Title: Phase-matched ion pre-acceleration by upstream magnetic dipole vortices in relativistic collisionless shocks
Article.Authors: Naseri N.; Turkakin H.; Shvets G.
Article.Abstract: Collisionless shocks are among the most efficient particle accelerators in the Universe, yet the physical mechanism responsible for energetic upstream seed ions remains poorly understood. Using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of unmagnetized relativistic electron-ion shocks, we investigate ion pre-acceleration by self-generated magnetic dipole vortices (MDVs) in the upstream region of the shock. We identify two distinct ion populations: one remains phase-matched with the moving MDV, undergoes considerable energization, and returns toward the shock, whereas the other escapes upstream after gaining only modest energy. We show that the magnetic component of the Lorentz force reduces the ion’s longitudinal velocity relative to the moving MDV, extending the interaction time and allowing the transverse electric field to perform sustained positive work. Decomposition of the electric field shows that both the motional electric field associated with the moving MDV and plasma-generated fields contribute to the observed ion energization. Repeated interactions with successive MDVs can increase ion energy before the particles return to the shock transition region. These results identify MDV-mediated upstream ion pre-acceleration as a candidate mechanism for producing energetic seed ions that may facilitate subsequent shock acceleration.

Article.Title: Interpretable prediction of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in critically ill patients with heart failure receiving early thromboprophylaxis
Article.Authors: Meng S.; Yu S.; Zhu X.; Zhou S.; Zhu S.; Yu Y.; Xie Y.; Huang Z.; Xiang M.; Ma H.
Article.Abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a concern among critically ill patients with heart failure receiving early thromboprophylaxis, yet individualized risk stratification in this population remains limited. We developed nine prediction models using 8,825 patients from MIMIC-IV and externally validated them in 5,425 eICU records. Fifteen predictors were identified through combined least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and Boruta feature selection. XGBoost achieved the highest observed discrimination, with ROC AUCs of 0.764 (95% CI, 0.723–0.805) internally and 0.731 (95% CI, 0.676–0.786) externally. SHAP analysis identified atrial tachycardia/fibrillation, respiratory failure, previous thromboembolism, antiplatelet therapy, and mechanical ventilation within 24 h as the leading contributors to model predictions. External validation highlighted the value of recalibration, with exploratory five-fold cross-fitted intercept recalibration improving overall calibration and predictive accuracy. Decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit at selected low-risk thresholds following recalibration. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of an interpretable prediction model based on routinely available clinical data, with potential for integration into ICU workflows to support individualized VTE risk stratification and targeted surveillance.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a multidimensional scale for heat-related health behavior across domains of everyday life
Article.Authors: Schmid-Ellinger J.; Bachner J.; Blaschke S.; Mess F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heat is an escalating global health risk, yet how populations adapt behaviorally remains poorly understood. We developed and psychometrically evaluated a novel instrument to assess heat-related health behavior (HRHB) across domains of everyday life and along a continuum from reactive to anticipatory responses in a large population-based sample in Germany ( N = 3,351). Factor analyses supported a multidimensional structure capturing both domain-specific (diet, housing, clothing, activity/change of location) and temporal adaptations. HRHB showed good reliability and moderate associations with heat-related health literacy and knowledge, indicating related but distinct constructs. Higher levels of reported behavior were associated with greater symptom burden, consistent with behavior being partly driven by experienced heat strain. HRHB explained additional variance in symptoms beyond sociodemographic and cognitive factors, supporting its incremental validity. These findings identify behavioral adaptation as a distinct and measurable dimension of population-level heat resilience, enabling improved identification of vulnerable groups and more targeted public health interventions.

Article.Title: Phytochemical profiling and computational analysis highlight anabsinthin as a potential ligand of coronavirus main protease
Article.Authors: Loukman S.; Hadad S.; Mesrar F.; Talha A.; Tachallait H.; Benmrid R.; Bouchmaa N.; Daoud R.; Fatimy R.; Benhida R.
Article.Abstract: Natural products remain an important source of diverse structures for antiviral drug development, but pinpointing and prioritizing bioactive metabolites from complex plant extracts remains challenging. We developed an integrated approach combining phytochemical analysis and computational methods to identify sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia absinthium L. as potential candidates for interaction with the conserved coronavirus main protease (Mpro/3CLpro), a crucial target for viral replication. Using a central composite design, we optimized ultrasound-assisted extraction, followed by GC–MS and LC–MS profiling to analyze solvent-dependent phytochemical profiles. Ethanol yielded the highest extraction efficiency and enabled the enrichment of constituents tentatively assigned to absinthin/anabsinthin-type dimeric sesquiterpene lactones, followed by chromatographic purification. These compounds were assessed through molecular docking, ADMET and toxicity predictions, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations with trajectory-based Prime MM-GBSA calculations. X77 served as the crystallographic non-covalent reference, and nirmatrelvir was examined only as an additional MD benchmark. Both lactones were predicted to fit within the Mpro active site, with anabsinthin showing a more favorable computational profile than absinthin. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the anabsinthin–Mpro complex displayed lower backbone deviations, reduced residue fluctuations, and persistent interactions with key residues, including Glu166 and Gln189. Prime MM-GBSA estimates also favored anabsinthin over absinthin, although the energetic difference relative to X77 was sensitive to the sampled trajectory window. In silico pharmacokinetic and toxicity predictions suggested generally favorable early drug-like characteristics without prominent predicted toxicity alerts. This integrated workflow combining extraction optimization, phytochemical profiling, purification, and computational assessment provides a rational strategy for prioritizing natural products for further investigation. Among the compounds examined in this study, anabsinthin emerged as the most promising A. absinthium -derived lactone candidate for subsequent experimental evaluation against Mpro. However, these computational predictions require confirmation through biochemical and cellular assays before direct Mpro inhibition or antiviral activity can be established.

Article.Title: Normative OCT-derived ocular measurements in rhesus macaques
Article.Authors: Lester J.; Barron Arrambide A.; Burgos-Rodriguez A.; Schwantes G.; Ede E.; Nepal P.; Fasih-Ahmad S.; Huynh L.; Zambrano R.; Lee T.; Kim B.; Schuman J.; N/A N/A.; Antón S.; Brent L.; Higham J.; Martinez M.; Melin A.; Montague M.; Platt M.; Sallet J.; Snyder-Mackler N.; Melin A.; Higham J.; Danias J.
Article.Abstract: To define normative OCT-derived measurements of the retina, optic nerve head (ONH) macrostructure, and lamina cribrosa (LC) microstructure in a large cohort of healthy, predominantly youngadult rhesus macaques, and to investigate their association with demographic traits and image quality. In vivo spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) scans of the macula, peripapillary retina, and ONH were obtained from 52 healthy animals (90 eyes). Macular and peripapillary scans were segmented to measure the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL), and total retinal thicknesses. ONH macrostructure and LC microstructure were quantified using software of our own design. Linear mixed-effects modeling was used to assess association between demographic features, image quality, and OCT-derived ocular measurements. Average macular GCIPL and peripapillary RNFL thicknesses were 80.6 ± 6.4 and 96.8 ± 8.9 µm, respectively. Average cup-to-disc ratio and cup depth were 0.46 ± 0.18 and 75.6 ± 50.3 µm, respectively. Average LC beam-to-pore-ratio was 2.06 ± 0.37. Significant associations existed between LC OCT quality and most LC microstructural parameters. We present robust normative ocular measurements of the healthy rhesus macaque eye and demonstrate LC microstructural measurements are sensitive to image quality, which should be considered in any future analysis of these parameters.

Article.Title: Industrial defect image generation via structured latent-space interpolation
Article.Authors: Cang Y.; Rong H.; Zou R.; Ma J.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial visual defect detection suffers from scarce defect samples, limiting generalization. We propose a novel image generation framework that synthesizes diverse and realistic defect images through three sequential innovations. First, we introduce UMAP-based dimensionality reduction to project VAE latent features onto a low-dimensional manifold while preserving local neighborhood structure, thereby enabling artifact-free sampling in the subsequent stage. Second, we design a PSO-optimized Gaussian mixture model to capture the sparse, multimodal distribution of defect features within this manifold, and sample new coordinates from high-likelihood regions to generate diverse yet realistic defect representations. Third, we employ a non-parametric radial basis function interpolator to map these sampled coordinates back to the original VAE latent space, preserving geometric continuity and restoring high-frequency defect details before decoding. Experiments on bearing-defect and public industrial datasets show that detectors trained with a synthetic-to-real ratio $$\le 1:3$$ achieve superior accuracy and robustness, validating each innovation’s effectiveness.
Article.Topic: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

Article.Title: Simulation-based implementation of the developed system dynamics model for sustainable urban water supply systems
Article.Authors: Hassan Z.; Rehan R.; Khan F.; Khan M.; Ali A.; Nasery M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water is an indispensable resource, underpinning not only domestic livelihoods, but also the social and economic fabric of nations. Climate change serves among the most formidable threats to the world’s freshwater reserves. Naturally, potable water serves as a finite and precious commodity, merely, 3% is fresh, 2% locked within glaciers and polar ice caps, leaving only 1% accessible for human use. As global water consumption increases at an average rate of 1% annually. Projections alarms need of adopting robust and advanced water management policies, as only 60% of the world’s required water supply will be available by 2030. This crisis is most acutely felt, in developing nations with rapid population growth and pervasive poverty compounds water scarcity. In Pakistan, groundwater serves as the cornerstone of the national domestic water supply infrastructure approximately, meeting 70% of drinking water demands nationwide. Moreover, the widening chasm between water demands and supply urgently required, innovative water management strategies. At present, in Pakistan, urban water supply planning, development, and maintenance remain heavily anchored in conventional engineering and demand-driven frameworks. This study develops the first tailored System Dynamics decision-support model for Peshawar’s urban water system, introducing a novel coupling of an age-band leakage formulation with proactive pipe replacement policies tailored for intermittent, groundwater-dependent utilities. At its foundation, lies meticulously on a constructed Causal Loop Diagram, serving as a comprehensive visual map. To capture, the intricate interdependencies in social, financial, and physical/technical sectors of urban water supply systems. The framework was operationalized and demonstrated on Tehsil Peshawar over a 50-year simulation horizon. Currently, the public water supply system in Peshawar, comprising of tube wells collectively discharging approximately 2 million gallons per hour. However, at baseline static conditions, the total water demand is 6.01 MGH with an estimated leakage rate of 1.703 MGH (28.3%). Crucially, comparing these requirements against the actual municipal abstraction capability of 2 million GPH reveals a 3-fold supply deficit. This structural gap highlights the disparity between standard design benchmarks (250 LPCD) and real-world supply capacities, demonstrating how operational intermittent supply acts as a forced rationing mechanism under current system constraints. Critically, energy costs constitute nearly 80% of total tube well operating expenses, positioning energy optimization as a linchpin of financial sustainability. The study advocates for solar-based energy alternatives, demand management interventions and proactive groundwater replenishment strategies as transformative interventions. This paper makes a compelling case of holistic and systems-thinking approaches, embracing full complexity of sustainable water governance, offering a replicable and scalable model for developing nations confronting analogous of water security challenges.

Article.Title: Predicting the number of infant deaths per woman in ethiopia using complementary count regression and machine learning approaches
Article.Authors: Aga M.; Dugasa S.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infant mortality remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding factors associated with cumulative infant deaths and improving their prediction may help identify populations with higher infant-death burdens. This study examined maternal-level counts of infant deaths ever experienced by women in Ethiopia using complementary count-regression and machine-learning approaches. Data from the 2019 Ethiopia Mini Demographic and Health Survey were analyzed among 5,846 women with complete birth histories. The outcome was the cumulative number of infant deaths experienced by each woman. Because the outcome is mechanically related to the number of births, the logarithm of the number of children ever born was incorporated as an exposure offset in the count-regression models and excluded from the machine-learning predictor set. Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP), and zero-inflated negative binomial models were compared using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. Poisson Random Forest, Extreme gradient boost (XGBoost)-Poisson, and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-Poisson models were evaluated using 70% training and 30% independent testing split, with five-fold cross-validation for hyper-parameter tuning. Predictive performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). The ZIP model provided the best fit among the evaluated count-regression models, with the lowest AIC (2503) and BIC (2544). In the count component, maternal age, household wealth, postnatal care, child vaccination status, maternal education, and place of delivery were statistically associated with the expected number of infant deaths. In the machine-learning analysis, XGBoost-Poisson achieved the best test-set predictive performance, with an MAE of 0.320 and RMSE of 0.570. Region had the largest relative predictive contribution (gain = 0.190), followed by marital status (0.167), maternal age (0.136), education level (0.125), and wealth index (0.117). These variable-importance measures represent predictive contribution and should not be interpreted as causal effects. Cumulative infant-death counts among women in Ethiopia were associated with demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and maternal and child healthcare characteristics. The ZIP model provided interpretable adjusted associations, whereas XGBoost-Poisson provided the best out-of-sample prediction among the evaluated machine-learning models. The findings support the value of combining inferential count regression with count-specific machine-learning methods while emphasizing that predictive importance does not establish causality. Continued attention to maternal education, socioeconomic disadvantage, postnatal care, immunization, and access to appropriate delivery care may help inform child-survival strategies in Ethiopia.
